name: Aliens: Fireteam Elite
detailed_description: EDITIONS INTO THE HIVE EDITION Venture into the hive and experience the Aliens: Fireteam Elite story! The Into the Hive Edition includes both the Standard Edition of the game and its Pathogen expansion, which adds a new campaign with three new missions on top of the twelve missions already included in the base game. THE ULTIMATE EDITION The Ultimate Edition of Aliens: Fireteam Elite is a must have for any aspiring Colonial Marine. Upgrading from the Standard Edition gets you the Pathogen expansion, complete with a new campaign, new weapons and more! Plus, the Ultimate Edition also includes the full suite of Endeavor Pass cosmetic DLCs and the Endeavor Veteran Pack. About the Game Play with up to two players or AI as you battle through four campaigns to explore the mystery of a new planet, LV-895. Discover what hides in the ruins and caves beneath in this third-person survival shooter set in the Aliens universe. Build your fireteam focusing on class composition, consumables, and weapons to take down Xenomorphs, beat Challenge Card runs, or play various game modes with friends. Blast through hordes of Xenomorphs, evade deadly Prowlers and Spitters, and set up defensive positions to stay alive long enough to get your fireteam to safety. Build your Marine the way you want. Level up in each of 7 unique classes or be a master of one. Choose your weapon – everything from magnums and SMGs to rocket launchers – and use over 130 unique perks to create the build of your choice. Level your character through 7 Class Kits, each with two unique abilities to use in combat and unlockable perks. Max out a variety of weapons, powering them up in stats the more you use them.

_childDocuments_.review: Before my review, a message to the developers:Given that this game is NOT meant to be played as a standard run-and-gun shooter but rather as a  it's astonishing that I have to rely on a limited set of emotes and a ping ability, all of which are usually ignored. Of course, those of us that have people to play with can use Discord, but how the hell are people who join the public queue supposed to be able to work together if we can't talk or at least text chat with each other?Having said that, I love this game.From a technical standpoint, it runs great. It launches and loads quickly, my framerate never dips, and it has never crashed on me even once. The graphics are well-polished and fantastic, especially on the space station in the first and last campaign sections, which has some amazing lighting and does a great job of capturing the aesthetics of James Cameron's Aliens with a little bit of Alien: Isolation mixed in. As a lifelong Aliens fan, that alone makes me happy to replay it.As far as gameplay, the controls are simple, the shooting mechanics are smooth, and killing things is  Each character class offers multiple ways to accommodate different playstyles. The game does do a rather poor job of explaining the perk board, but once you figure it out, you have near limitless class customization options. There is also a wide and diverse selection of weapons, which are also highly customizable.It could definitely use more content. I wouldn't say that the campaign is the shortest that I've played, but it isn't terribly long either. Most people don't want to replay the same 12 story missions (+3 in DLC) over and over, and that's basically what you'll be doing. The horde mode maps that are unlocked after completing the campaign are fun, but too simple in my opinion and leave much to be desired. Most people get bored pretty quick.One more thing (and this might just be me,) but I did not like the music.  That might not be a totally fair critique since I have no idea what the music sounds like after the 2nd or 3rd mission, which is where I had to mute it. But as someone who loves and appreciates good soundtracks in movies and video games, this score was just not good and too distracting to me. However, I am also a huge fan of James Horner's soundtrack from the original movie, so I might be setting the bar too high on this. There's also this annoying headshot sound effect, but you can turn that off in the audio options along with the music.As much as I love this game, I completely understand why some people hate it. If you've never been a fan of horde modes in shooters (CoD Zombies, Halo Firefight, Left 4 Dead, Killing Floor, Gears of Wars, etc.) or PvE games in general, then you probably won't like this. That's all it is.It's really difficult for me to give this game an overall rating. At it's core, it's a solid third-person shooter that just needs a little more variety in it's content to keep it fresh. But the lack of something as basic as the ability to type a message to your teammates can make public matchmaking an absolute nightmare. Casual gamers and Aliens fans will likely have a blast, but I would recommend playing in private matches with friends or AI teammates, because other players in the public queue will probably ruin the experience.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fun in how it captures the honest feel of marines pushing through cramped corridors trying to survive while anything and everything creeps and crawls in anticipation of ripping you apart. The SFX is spot on when it comes to the Pulse Rifles and Smartguns. The addition of modded weapons, skills, loadouts, and mission modifiers helps create enough of a fresh feeling when rerunning the same 4 mission blocks, but that's where this game stumbles decidedly.Yes, there are numerous difficulty settings that you can switch to in order to recapture that tense feeling of knowing you're gonna' die - just not sure when - as each encounter with a Xenomorph threatens to tip the scales from almost assured victory into the gaping maw of hopeless despair. However, you can only replay these same 12 missions again and again before the tense moments drip away into memorized speedrun patterns in order to maximize your weapon/loadout/skill grind. DLC's are announced and I'm willing to update this review to reflect those changes, but if the Devs simply release skins and hex-color palette additions, this game will go the way of the Aliens vs Predator re-up that came out in 2010. If you  add to the actual game i.e. more mission blocks in the realm of 5 - 10, maybe a few more skill modifiers or outright new skills to swap out with, perhaps a new weapon or 2 that really ramps up the damage to carry you through the insane difficulty...If you  do this, then you can watch this game fall out of relevance like every other attempt with the IP. -Tyger

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely love this game.I play a lot of games in this genre: the Left 4 Dead alikes. Most of the time I have a host of complaints with balancing, mechanics, pacing, etc. - especially when the game first releases. I can honestly say I've experienced none of those problems with this game. The fact that it runs as smoothly as it does without any of the previously mentioned problems being noticeable on day one is a feat in itself. Fans of the Alien franchise will get additional glee from this game as it not only nails the aesthetic, but builds on top of the lore with a surprising amount of story content. This extra lore can be safely ignored if you're not into that kind of thing, but it is very interesting to those who seek more depth to the universe. Plus, it's undeniably awesome to see those aliens start bursting from every vent, crawling on the ceiling and walls to get to you: as an Alien fan myself, I get chills at those apex moments.The only real complaint I might have is that the game currently features absolutely no form of team communication. No typing, no speaking, no nothing. That needs to be fixed ASAP and I have confidence that it will be with how well done everything else is.TLDR:Amazing game for fans of Alien and L4D type games alike. No team speak hurts, but doesn't interfere with the fun factor

_childDocuments_.review: *Edit, most of my frustration comes from how the game isn't optimized. thus why I want to refund it. But also, I want to give credit to the Devs of the game by a large mile, for being the first game creditted to the vast majority on the project, you are all fantastically talented and I hope this game is even better in a year.I wish I could refund this product, I even bought the pack so 70€+ is gone and wasted, but that goes to show how stupid a person like me can be with money when they have fun for the first few hours only for it to burn and sizzle immediately afterwards from a realization of the game.With that out of the way, here's a review and I hope it helps the devs, but for some reason I don't think they are going to change the way the game plays atm.Pros: - Fun for a few hours, decent horde-style shooter.- Some of the open maps (chapter 2) are beautiful and amazing, the art team deserves a bonus for that.- Sound design is great.- Xenomorphs.- (This is a half point only) the Cards before deplying on a mission have potential, they are interesting but needs refinement. A con to this while we're talking about cards is that they are lost no matter what, even if you lose or crash on the loadingscreen. (Cards should only be consumed on victory).Cons:- NO Drop-in gameplay, the base design on how the multiplayer works should not have left the devs office and I am surprised this was even acceptable. You only have 1 minute to find players to play with due to the game autostarting, there is no search feature to find others to play with. Cancelling the countdown resets everything and so you have an absolutely horrid time to find others.- 39.99€, should have been put up as a 19.99 game in Early Access, then released for its asking price for point 2 > - Game was obviously not tested, or tested by their intended long-term market.- Unoptimized as heck, jittery as heck, random stuttering on 2 vastly different systems.- The person behind the 'rpg/leveling' system needs to be replaced by someone who understands horde games AND meaningful progression.- Perks are boring- Progression is boring- Balance is incredibly all over the place, both for players and the enemies- Hidden Caches end up being completely worthless and boring after completing the game, even after having found about 5-10 of them.I wish I could write more but just like my enthusiasm and energy for this game; it's completely gone.-----The perks aren't meaningful, exciting, fun or interesting at all. They are miniscule additions and the balance for some are completely whack or makes them worse. Most aren't interesting, they add nothing to the feel or enjoyment and you wouldn't notice having a perk for a specific set due to it.Add on top of this that the leveling is an incredibly long and an extreme chore that doesn't add much to you or your power at large; and you really got a recipe for being the complete opposite in trying to entice and motivate someone to level up. >>> Games they should have researched: Deep Rock Galactic, Vermintide 2-----It's an Aliens game, sure, fighting one in melee should be problematic but Predators didn't seem to have this trouble in the games they were featured, and so you'd think a team of professional marines would know how to fight Aliens too; with this said literally everything in the game killed in up-close range hurts you in some way no matter what you do. Even the non-Xenomorph aliens. For a game wanting to promote run&gun, there is a hundred different things in the game that makes it extremely frustrating to play it due to how the game is built up (especially the balance). Puddles of acid left from a previous kill a friend did and you had to run through it, friendly fire due to camera angles, just so many frustrating and un-fun elements. >>> Games they should have researched: Serious Sam series, 3rd person games like Orcs Must Die in order to understand how to design small hallways and suicide/floorhazard enemies.-----I could write more, but I am so bored and tired out of my mind at this point so I can just point out other obvious points people have made in terms of balance. - Extreme and Insane are completely not worth the effort, unrewarding and has no real insentive other than frustrating you. The Recon class is an absolute minimum for ammo refilling your party, due to the extreme bullet-sponginess enemies have and the incredible tankiness Synths have for no reason. - Doc is worthless and replaced hard by Recon, you are going to get hit no matter what but the best defense is to kill the enemies before they even get to hit you at all. Doc can't output enough damage to make up for having a heal and an accuracy team-booster. Recon provides a smaller heal (which is of no consequence to a team of people who can actually aim), much higher personal damage and an amazing tool with actual interesting upgrades on top of this that additionally boosts damage for the team.- Technician is powerful and optimal for all difficulties, ESPECIALLY on Insane and is a fun class to play due to the ease-of-use, flow of abilities and how its class design makes complete sense with how powerful it is.- Gunner is hellishly boring and easily replaced by Demolisher; both classes have a damage boost to shooting targets, they both have exploding abilities, the difference is Rifle/Shotgun and Rifle/Heavygun (smartgun, rocketlauncher, flamer, etc). Gunner might be slightly more optimal at Insane if it wasn't for Demolisher Flamer doing the single highest DPS against boss/elite targets.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow.....I really want to recommend this game. I am fair, I will edit my review if something magically changes. But right now holy sh$t is there some things absolutely wrong with this game.... Lets break it down:Positives:- Do you feel like a colonial marine? Hell yeah you do, there are a sh!t load of guns and attachments to suit your play style. Granted, the attachments eventually mean sweet diddly squat and its more about levelling your gun and what bonuses you have attached to your class. ( more on this in negatives )- There is somewhat of a story involved, all 8hrs of the initial non DLC campaign. ( more on this in negatives )- Feels and plays like Left For Dead, but with aliens theme which make it awesome.( more on this in negatives )- Different classes do actually feel different and have about 2 shovels worth of depth to them to make them worth trying out, but dont feel bad if you just play as " Gunner " for 99% of the time. ( more on this in negatives )Negatives:- This game was released in 2021... its now 2024 and where the hell is the VOIP? We have crossover ability with console players YET no way to actually communicate and -> play a team game <- with them. So enjoy being frustrated when 3 people think they are being clever and activate all their abilities simultaneously, which then leaves you seriously F**ked on harder difficulties where there are multiple waves. This is actually some really basic BS that should have been incorporated into the game. There are indie developers out there that have VOIP yet Focus Entertainment seemed to forget about such a critical feature in their " Co-operative third person survival game ". How the hell do we -> co-operate <- with other players, through emotes? GTFO.- This game was released in 2021... its now 2024 and where the hell is the ability to choose what regional server we want to play on? You only know if the team player is a console player or a steam player, you have NFI where they are located and what kind of game you will have. You could be in Asia playing with a South American, but 10fps stuttering and lag jumps... with no way to kick the player out of your team mid game. Somehow, hosting the game on multiple servers to actually allow players to -> play with each other <- was also forgotten.- I guess mostly N/A players are having a good experience, anyone who lives anywhere else you can expect a good 5-10 minute wait time ( or longer ) depending on time of day. Also expect your connection to be garbage 50% of the time due to above listed issues..- Game is set up as a co-operative team player game, there is an ability to start a map with A.I team mates, but its not intuitive at all and anything outside normal difficulty you can forget about trying to do that, you will just die in the first 5 minutes. Yet listed features above severely push against the ability to match make and -> co-operate with other players <-. A single player mode with stronger A.I teammates would be greatly appreciated and make the game a little more immersive sometimes if you want to have that " crawling around in the dark with the xenomorphs " feel.- Vanilla campaign is way to short, 4 different map types with three stages each. There is a lot of homage paid to all of the franchise movies, but even on upper difficulties you can finish most maps in 30 minutes tops. so 4x90 minutes = 360 minutes or 6 hours of gameplay. ( look, you can farm the very last vanilla level for a bit longer if you really want ) There is ONE DLC campaign.. the game came out in 2021... I would say sales-wise the game has done pretty well considering theres at least 16,483 very positive reviews... are we not getting anymore content?- The class system in the game is great, it provides some diversity, however, some classes are just better than others. A group of gunners can finish the campaign pretty easily, so it doesnt really feel like " there is a need " to play other classes, outside of creating challenges for yourself. It would feel better if the class system actually was -> required <- to finish the game, in a " co-operative " shooter anyway. Lots of variety, not much actual balance or thought put into them.- There are a TON of guns in the game, all of them giving you a solid Aliens feel. The attachments however... leave a lot to be desired. Once you have your gun " setup ", theres not much need or reason to ever change those attachments ever again, prompting you to wonder why you have 3-4 attachments to choose from per slot, when out of those options only 2 are viable options and worth equipping. Again, Lots of variety, not much actual balance or thought put into them.- Finally, it plays a lot like left for dead. Which is great but also curses the game immensely -> if this aliens clone doesnt live up to or exceed the replayability of left for dead <-, which unfortunately in my opinion it does not. Due to how stale the weapons, attachments, and classes eventually become, it kills the urge to play the game sooner than it should for something that has so much potential.Overall, as a game itself based in the Aliens universe I give it a 7/10 buy on sale condition. You do feel like a colonial marine. For a few hours.For the actual co-operative game play and functions put into this game, it gets a solid holy sh$t 1/10 what the hell is going on with this three year old game. There was " a patch " in october 2023 but it goes no where to adding new features or fixing the " communication issues " ( the uh, absolute lack of ) that are required in a " co-operative " game.If the devs could put in VOIP that would go a looooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooong way to starting to fix this game and making it more popular again... a start.

_childDocuments_.review: It's pretty good.  Everyone else has already said most of what can be said about it, but personally I think that the devs have done well.  Think about it, how disappointed were we all after colonial marines?  How long has it been since we've had a good Aliens game? The pressure to make another Aliens game that  turn the gaming community into a pack of raging, frothing at the mouth ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ must've been huge.  And they did it.  They made a game that  awful, that  a disaster.  In fact, it's pretty good.It's a relatively simple shooter based on the Aliens movie and it's fun to play.  It isn't going to win game of the year, but it's fun enough to play and pass the time.  That's good enough.And, most importantly, I think the devs should get some kind of game studio of the year award for this one thing:  there's no tutorial.  No 'Welcome to basic training soldier!  Push X to switch to your side arm!  Now bring up your main weapon again!  Push forward to go forward!" ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, as if I've went decades of my life never having encountered something called a 'com-put-er-game'.  We've all  played shooters, we could figure them out with our eyes closed.  And this game allows you that.  It allows me to just load it up, select my gear, and go smoke loads of aliens and for that I am happy.Sale only purchase BTW.

_childDocuments_.review: Fancy Aliens franchise, especially into the action and lore of it? Then this is for you. I would compare this to Left 4 Dead style game play, where you must use teamwork to survive and further in this game, can't leave teammates behind. Really enjoy how the xenos can come from anywhere, spawn spots littered everywhere so it really can get overwhelming and their AI is good about making sure they don't just funnel down the same path. They will often separate and come from different angles, whether the level you are on, above, or below. The weapons feel great to use and progression is rewarding. Some missions when played multiple times will feel different due to changing/moving objectives and enemies, this helps it becoming too repetitive.  I think it's really worth checking out if you like scifi shooters and bug hunts.

_childDocuments_.review: If you have played  or , you will be right at home here. I like this game a lot because it has three things I really like which are a linear, mission-based storyline that doesn't waste your time with "open world" or "live service" BS, drop in, drop out coop, and repeatable missions which allow you to try out new builds without worry that you are using the wrong one and won't be able to complete the one you need.  Movement and combat are third-person shooter with cover and dodge rolling or to put it another way, it's basically  or a low-magic version of . Mission design is a run-through-the mission, then stop and fight the horde loop which will be familiar to people who play , ,  or my personal favorite it that genre, Fortunately there aren't any missions built around bad puzzles or painfully tedious objectives (such as collecting enough gas cans to fuel a battleship as in L4D). It's basically just combat. There are also other modes including horde and some kind of roguelike but I can't comment on those because I don't play them. It's basically just a series of missions with a hub area where you can talk to people between missions. (They don't open their mouths when they talk.) It's no  but it's fine for what it is. This is NOT a story-rich game. I finished the main campaign (not the DLC) twice within the 24 hours I have on-record and that was with repeating a lot missions to try different builds. This game is clearly intended to be something that you replay a lot like  or  though that isn't usually how I play games. (I usually finish coop games once and then maybe do them again with another person before moving on to the next one.)I'd much rather have a short game than a tedious "live-service" that deliberately wastes my time or an "open-world" game that has me doing random tasks and climbing radio towers. This game DOES offer daily bonuses fro various tasks and it has lots of emotes etc. to collect by playing the game (there is no cash shop beyond the DLC on the Steam page I'm glad to say) but I don't really care about that stuff.In a world where good online games with repeatable content like this exist, exploitative, microtransaction-infested, FOMO-driven trash like  (made by a company that is more than 1/3 owned by Tencent 腾讯 btw) should not. If you like games with repeatable content, you'd be better off getting this one than flirting with  and other exploitative scams. Here's hoping for lots of DLC and a sequel or similar game with more budget. (More facial animations and some cutscenes would be nice as would a game with more missions and a longer campaign.)Best!

_childDocuments_.review: Great game overall! I would score Aliens Fireteam Elite a good 8.5/10 stars. Pros:After completing the first 4 campaign acts, most of the score goes to the fact that the game is nicely polished as far as it goes with shooting and combat gameplay, the enemies in the game are actually competent, there's a great amount of challenge to be had in this game ( I would recommend starting out playing this game on Intense difficulty for people very familiar with shooter games) and it is immensely satisfying to see that Cold Iron worked on this game and gave it soul. The arsenal is diverse, the load out customization and perk system is designed good, consumables are useful, and there is much potential for this game for the future. I'm happy to see that the developers care to drop many updates and patches to the game as frequently as weekly updates and to add in more content (Phalanx class) and cosmetics makes this game worth playing, albeit the game needing some more objective types to include, plus I would seek to it that the developers add in more campaign missions and more horde mode maps, but I digress.Cons:As far to date in September 19, 2021, the game has it's own fair share of problems within it. Most notably is that you may or may not come across bugs in the game. At times, the enemies may spasm on the ground after you kill them and the game itself at times buffers slowly , especially during swarms of enemies attacking you and your team. HOWEVER, the biggest reason why this game misses out on a 9 score is because I personally experienced a game with other players where an enemy crawler was glitched/bugged/stuck on the roof during the Gift Of Fire : Boarding mission, in which it almost cost us the game because we couldn't advance to the next room until that last crawler was eliminated. That is a HUGE deal, it would be immensely dissatisfying if more of these instances occurred , but it only happened once and it resolved itself. Nevertheless, the game has it's drawbacks realistically speaking. Plus, I believe a more in depth customization of appearances for your own marine should be including some more options just for the best experiences as possible with that. The last con of this game is that it also needs a better matchmaking system. I think this game can benefit with players going online and finding other players more quickly since the game tends to match players up with the AI bot teammate (which I do not recommend playing with) that took us several searches to find enough players.All in all, if you are an Aliens fan, look no further and get this game, it will truly make you feel immersed in the Aliens world and it include some more info of what's going on with the Colonial Marines and Weyland Yutani plot in this game. For more casual fans, this game will give you what you need out of a shooter and I would say that it is worth the $40 dollars, especially when you play the intense difficulty and have some friends to play with it. My biggest tip to you is to play this game with other players, the AI companions still have some more polishing work left in them to be more so reliable playing solo.

_childDocuments_.review: Dumb fun, with authentic aesthetics, audio, and atmospherics, coupled with great gunplay and level design. Moment to moment gameplay experience is top notch, with some genuinely hairy set pieces to contend with.As a third-person shooter, it won't make the earth move, but if you're an Aliens fan - this is absolutely the best game the franchise has seen in an age.Loving it.Edit: campaign now complete, plenty of experience on higher difficulties, all the lore collected, etc.What are you people whining about? This game is amazing - all the best bits of the original Destiny 1 campaign and Mass Effect 3 multiplayer, minus the individual failings of either.Shines at higher difficulties. Captures the tension and frantic panic of the movies, perfectly.And surprisingly, the first and only time Prometheus and Alien Covenant haven't felt like vile franchise tag-ons - an unexpected bonus, lore-wise.Edit 2: post-Pathogen purchase. A nice little addition, although with the caveat of having purchased it while the DLC was on sale. The new missions are welcome, although the first couple won't set the world on fire. The final third of the second, and the finale mission, offer up some nice aesthetic touches. They also go somewhere that only Aliens: Infiltrator has, so far, in terms of the lore.A great addition to the game, but one best grabbed on sale if regional pricing doesn't swing in your favour.Looking forward to Weyland showing up in the next DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is being written about 3 days into playing the game and one day after finishing the story and I have to say I had a lot of hopes and high expectations for this game. It is safe to say... I was not let down nor was I displeased with the end result. From the tight corners to the open environments Aliens Fireteam blows the atmosphere out of the water and impresses with each chapter that goes by. The weapons feel powerful and well-made, they fit perfectly with every environment and I never found myself relying on any single weapon over another. Each kit (class) is well-rounded and have a plethora of ways to customize/optimize them to fit your play style. I absolutely love it.The enemy types and the variety is also impressive, with Xenomorphs that will travel along the ceiling and walls to reach their target, you will absolutely feel a need to adapt to every fight accordingly or lose a small chunk of health. During the later chapters you start seeing Weyland-Yutani synths that utilize firearms over melee however they don't stick around for long and eventually fade out to the xenomorphs altogether, something Aliens Colonial Marines failed to do right. You will never fight the same enemy for longer than what is really necessary and they will prioritize fighting each other before fighting you (unless you get directly involved of course).The progression system is completely fleshed out with the ability to level up your character, class, weapon and abilities themselves. My personal favorite is the Gunner with their ability to Overclock nearby ally's Rate of Fire and their Reload Speed for a limited time. The ability to increase the duration and recharge speed of Overclock is a total game changer where the Demolisher can modify their micro rockets to utilize napalm and spread a thick line of fire to damage anything to move through it.All-in-All I absolutely had a blast playing Aliens Fireteam and the ending made everything worth the struggle and the climb. I strongly recommend picking this up when you have the extra spending money or when it is on sale because either way it is worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: Aliens: Fireteam Elite is like diving headfirst into a chaotic, xenomorph-infested theme park—and I’m here for it! The co-op shooter nails the tension of Aliens while giving you non-stop, pulse-pounding action. You and two buddies (or bots if you're feeling brave) will face waves of xenos, from facehuggers to massive warrior aliens, in tight corridors that bring to mind the movie’s best moments.It’s fast-paced, brutal, and satisfying. The sound of your pulse rifle firing? It’s pure nostalgia. The classes add variety to the gameplay too—each with unique abilities, so you can mix things up depending on your style. But the real beauty here? The teamwork. You’ll need to strategize, cover each other, and manage resources to survive.On the downside, there’s no real story depth. It’s all about blasting through levels and surviving. And after a while, the missions can feel a bit repetitive—shoot, defend, survive, repeat. But if you’re into that cathartic alien-shooting vibe, it works!The game looks decent, plays smooth, and scratches that co-op shooter itch. Is it a masterpiece? Nah. Is it a good time with friends? Absolutely. So grab a pulse rifle, and let's hunt some xenos!

_childDocuments_.review: (AFE) is a game that far too many people wrote off and ditched too soon, not realizing what they were missing. It's easy to understand now too in hindsight after 31+ hours of play. So I thought I'd write a review in the hope that it helps bring some more fan(s) of the franchise to a game I think most will enjoy.It's easy to understand why so many people ditched the game and were disappointed because honestly I was too at launch. The aliens seemed like pushovers. The maps were very linear and very formulaic, moving from one big fight to another with some of the encounters feeling more like they were designed solely to tick boxes in a design document or just irritate players by forcing them to burn through ammunition (in particular the downright boring marching hordes of "poppers" in the third mission of the third campaign section).The amount of content seemed pretty weak too. Yes, there were four classes to play initially ("Demolisher", "Doc", "Gunner", and "Technician" if I remember correctly), but the loadout limitations were confusing, the firearm mechanics and stats were not intuitive (making it surprisingly hard to compare gear and know which was better), and frankly I owned virtually  the weapons, attachments, and perks I could buy within my first five or six hours of play. I felt like I'd paid *far* too much money for the relatively small amount of available kit.But here's the thing: I'd now venture a guess that what I had at the time was  I didn't realize there was a *fifth* class until I finished the campaign for the first time and gained access to the "Recon" class, which might actually be my favorite. There's something about the combination of his loadout choices along with the PUPS sensor and health/ammunition drone that really suits my play style. He's got a lot of fun options for perks too.And that's not even counting all the stuff that's been added post launch. We've had multiple new classes added (e.g., phalanx and lancer), new game modes, new weapons, new attachments, new perks, new challenge cards, and a whole bunch of new cosmetics. The developers have not been idle in the slightest, having added quite a bit along the way.But honestly, I'm not sure all of that stacks up to the hidden stuff that was apparently already there. It was only when I started playing the game on the "Intense" difficulty with a couple of friends that I began to realize just how much is hidden under the surface. I started getting weapons I'd never seen before, perks I couldn't buy, and all kinds of other stuff. Then seemingly out of the blue, the requisition store opened up with *dozens* of new weapons I'd never seen before either. I'm still not sure why that happened, but I'm guessing it had something to do with completing missions on the "Intense" difficulty level. I say that because a friend and I were working through the campaign together a second time on "Intense" and we both suddenly noticed what seemed like an almost completely new weapon inventory.We haven't even tried the other game modes yet, as we're too busy having fun on "Intense". I imagine we'll finish that soon enough and move on to "Extreme" to see what lurks behind that gate. If what we've seen so far is any guide, then I expect we'll be finding some truly interesting goodies.To be fair, the game is not without its faults. I can't believe the bloody developers  haven't fixed the audio-stops-working problem that happens to me all the time with the pulse (and a few other) rifles. And the campaign is indeed extremely linear and repetitive. But the AI and overall feel of the game is almost entirely different on "Intense" compared to standard. I can't help but think this is the difficulty the developers expected us to play. I can say this much: the aliens are no longer pushovers, that's for sure!In short, if you're a fan of the franchise and have a couple friends to play with, then I think the game is well worth the asking price. You just have to understand going in that it's not going to open up and show you everything right at the outset. But there's a  more there than meets the eye as you progress.

_childDocuments_.review: Aliens Fireteam Elite is FUN, and ultimately that's the most important thing. This isn't a big budget AAA production and if your expecting that you'll probably be disappointed. But if you keep your expectations in check you'll be blown away with just how much of a good time you'll have gunning down Xenomorphs, Synths and weirder things with other players. (And that is the best way to play this game. You can go Single Player but it's not nearly as fun if you even have one person with you) The challenge cards, skill system and weapon customization give the game a surprising amount of depth and some rather long legs for the title and I can see myself playing this game for quite a while if it's properly supported by the Devs going forward. If you want to play this game for the story your probably out of luck, the game does have a story and it's not terrible but it's all told through radio chatter, in-game collectible intel and talking with people in the games hub area but it's definitely not front and center. The game is surprisingly stable and while their have been a few minor glitches there's been nothing particularly game breaking and have been surprisingly infrequent. If you wanna play another big budget Alien Isolation then this isn't your game. If you wanna have a great time blowing up aliens with a Pulse Rifle or a Smartgun though then this game might be for you.

_childDocuments_.review: I waited until I finished the campaign to write this review. As a whole, this game is disappointing and certainly not worth the price they're asking.The major cons: There's too much emphasis on action, and it was repetitive. Get from Point A to Point B. At Point B defend the point from a horde. Move to next point. Hold off another horde. And so on. It was just horde defense. It's good when it's used sparingly and properly. How about building up the tension? In Colonial Marines, there were large stretches where there's no shooting, just set environment and character interaction. In Alien Isolation, there was tension because the Xeno was stalking you. It would appear at random times and would even trick you. Not so here, it's just shoot, shoot, shoot and Xeno missiles that bum rush your team. The AI is better than Colonial Marines. Now your AI buddies can target and destroy the Bugs. They don't stand there and get in the way like O'Neil in Colonial Marines. However, there were many cases where the AI froze, or were caught up on something. Especially at the end, the Queen just stood there after chasing up down a corridor. It allowed us to escape. I also had a problem when characters fell through the map.In the sets there are many black holes where they'll pop out of. It's too obvious and allows you to essentially spawn camp because the AI becomes predictable, and they come out of the hole in a line. Also, the cover mechanics remind me of Gears of War. I find this to be out of place for a Aliens game.Another severe handicap, and please correct me if I'm missing something, but in a game that requires teamwork-why do we not have the ability to text or verbally chat? It was frustrating not being able to form a plan with my buddies before a horde. In another scenario, my buddies found an escape route and I got turned around and went the wrong way. They couldn't tell me which way to go other than using that marker device that would disappear after a few seconds. It would be easier to just have someone in chat say, "Go to the gap in the railing, immediately turn right, and RUN!"The ending got me angry. You set the facility to self-destruct. You fight the hordes. You see the Queen and she chases you. Your team reaches the lift...and that's it. There's no cut scene. No explosion. You're just back in the hanger with the AI saying the station was destroyed. All of that and I don't even get to see the end of my work?!I'm getting a refund. All of that and I didn't get a fitting conclusion.

_childDocuments_.review: Matchmaking is done per level. There is no "global" matchmaking that lets you match any level you've cleared. _childDocuments_.review: There are problems with this game, but I do love it.It's clear that the team loves the alien universe - great care is given to the set design, audio design, and gameplay loop to feel extremely authentic and fun. All of the alien designs, even the ones unique to the game, feel real and genuine. That love really shines through in the story - barebones as it is, there are some great voice acting moments (Honikker in particular does excellent) and your characters, while mute, never feel "tacked on."There are some downsides - the difficulty is the "unfun" style of number changes, there really are some genuinely useless weapons, especially on those higher difficulties. On the "hard" difficulty though, the gameplay loop is enjoyable - a very fun, but not necessarily mindless romp. It reminds me a lot of Doom and Diablo - an overpowered player character that has some difficulties sometimes but you can overcome them with some thinking, strategy, and good reactions. If you love the Aliens universe and L4D style games you could do a LOT worse.

_childDocuments_.review: I completed this game in about 9 Hours which is quite fast for a $40 price tag; However, the class system is nice, the gameplay is fun (Kind of reminds me of L4D and Gears of War) and I think the story is interesting enough for people who like that kinda thing. But you can also play it as a mindless looter shooter in a way, the loot pretty much just consists of lore you can pick up around the map, and 'secret' loot boxes which give you cosmetics and an attachment most of the time. The enemy variety is decent enough but I would like to see more interesting enemies in the future, as most just run at you and melee you or grapple you. Something I'm really hoping they plan to do is make future content free and make their money off of cosmetic purchases and boosts. They have the potential to make this a game with seasonal rewards. Sort of like a battle pass. Even a battle pass would be fine. pay a small fee every season and earn exclusive rewards for that season the more they play and challenges/achievements. I hope content for this game is free in the future, as I was sorely disappointed this game was $40 for this much content. There is so much potential for this game, I just hope they capitalize on it.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a turbo nerd for the ALIENS franchise, so I'm a bit biased.This game is independently produced and is a great 3rd person shooter. There is plenty of plot explained with good voice acting, and you get the horde mode when you complete the campaign.The xenomorphs are really well designed and are implemented very well.There is a great diversity of enemies as well, each employing different techniques to try to get the fireteam.It is kind of a shame that the party is capped at 3 people, but that is what a fireteam is, three people max.Matchmaking isn't bad either, although sometimes you may have to leave lobby and reenter to find real players.There is no comms (other than emotes) so team up in discord or ventrillo.There are plenty of options for your character and weapons (weapon/character accessories, outfits, decals, "colorways", etc).
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Fireteam Elite

_childDocuments_.review: Aliens: Fireteam Elite does a good job of recreating the feeling of the Aliens movie. The graphic, effects, sounds, and atmosphere feel great. The main campaign is okay but is best played with other people; the AI bots they'll match you with are pretty dumb.The biggest gripe that I have with this game is that the replayability is pretty low. Once you've gone through the main campaign, there's very little motivation to go through at the higher difficulty levels.  Yes, there are some cosmetics you can earn and you can upgrade the skills of each of your character classes, but there isn't a clear goal to work towards.The player base is pretty low right now, so I can would only recommend someone pick up this game if it's on sale or there's a major change to the gameplay loop to make it more rewarding.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first Aliens game besides the old Capcom arcade 'beat 'em up 'Aliens vs Predator' that I really enjoyed.  It feels a lot like the second movie of the series 'Aliens' with a small squad taking out different varieties of aliens and accomplishing different tasks. You can play solo with two AI synthetics called 'Alpha' and 'Beta'. However, the game really shines the most when you have a squad of you and two buddies. The game has several different classes such as a gunner, medic, ammo replinisher, so you can ensure your team has a nice variety of tools. It has different difficulty levels that increase the damage the aliens do, environmental damage (such as acid spills), as well as friendly fire. A couple co-workers and I would play it on our break on the easier level and that was fine for us. I went on later to play through it again and the expansion with my son. Complaints: The only bugs I encountered was a game ending bug that would put an alien so far out of my reach that I could never shoot them. They wouldn't come out of the hole and I couldn't hit them either. I would have to restart the mission. Thankfully this only happened three times to me. My other complaint would be that the best gun in the game is one of the ones your start with - the smart gun. That gun is better than anything else you get later on and is even better on harder difficulties because of it's lack of friendly fire. This is a game that oozes the spirit of the Aliens franchise, with the awesome sound effects, and a great co-op experience even if you are unfamiliar with the series.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, I'm close to 50 hours, I've maxed 3 classes and a handful of weapons, and I figured I'd let you know how it's going. It's been awesome! It's super easy to pick up and jump in, and it's fast and fun to level everything in the game. There are daily and weekly objectives that offer rewards, and they are a great way to vary your game as you select corresponding classes and missions with different difficulties. You'll need to complete every level on every difficulty, it doesn't stack. It doesn't matter which class you choose, they can vary. Also, you get bots if you want to go private! They're pretty useful, but I'd check out the guides for more advanced models for anything insane. Everything is scripted so it's easy to repeat and remember where everything triggers. It's one thing to go running around like a duck and another to take a post and funnel everything into a choke, all with friendly fire. Feel free to repeat familiar levels to rack up the xp. I love joining a game and marking all the intel, I think they appreciate it. Includes crossplay which has been most of my matches, it's on PS right now. I wish there was an in-game buddies list where you could click on your party and add them to your friends, but you need a special code they have to generate and then you copy, it's a whole process... and there's not voice or chat, the best you can do are emotes. Also, in every match, you get the option to select a challenge card that modifies the mission, like what kind of enemies spawn, or their frequency, or if you get to use your abilities or not, or no side arm, or get a ton of headshots, making it easier or harder depending and offering large amounts of credits and/or xp or none at all! I like joining games with day 1 rookies and choosing no hud and watching them panic. I too got the feeling that this was pretty similar to WWZ, this is probably less involved but faster to level up. Get to work Marines!

_childDocuments_.review: I have a love-hate relationship with this game. I hate the reasons that I love it...The game itself is nothing special, imo. Go to place, shoot bugs. Go to another place, hold f, then shoot bugs. Fairly simple gameplay loop with nothing revolutionary. Still a step up from the last Aliens game though...What I love is, this game has a few tiny little features or polishes that make it really hard for me to not enjoy playing. For example, how many third-person games allow you to swap which should your camera is over AND adjusts your character model? GTA comes to mind, and I think GoW? It's an overlooked feature that in bloated games that have lots of other problems, you wouldn't really notice or miss it, but in a simple game like this one, it's something that shines and helps highlight the gameplay.Another feature that was added post launch that made me update my review and got me back into playing; Lifetime stats. I'm not a completionist (usually) but not enough games have a clean way to display what you have/haven't done in them. This game is 4 Chapters with 3 missions in each chapter (again very simple) so having stats for each level is nice when looking for unique ways to replay levels and get more out of the game.I think $30 is a fair price for this game; you'll get about ~6 hours out of the 4 main chapters on casual difficulty. The game opens up a bit more and you start to feel the "co-op" aspect of it in the Intense difficulty. If there's a sale and you have a friend to get this game with, I highly recommend picking it up and trying to finish the game in co-op on standard or intense.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is almost very good. It could have been very good. It may still be very good if they continue to add content, but i'm afraid with how quickly the initial limited content gets old, the sudden lack of player interest, and probably a steep drop off of income this may be yet another opportunity lost. It's really ashame that the history of Aliens games made has completely overlooked one of the very first ones made. Aliens Online was a game from the mid(ish) 90's that had been part of what was called Gamestorm. They had quite a few amazingly fun games . Air Warrior, A mage battle type game, a Gangsters strategy game, and a cult favorite to many including myself - Aliens Online. In that game you could play Alien or Marine and gather in the lobby and see what new ' hives' started filling with players and whom. Once the marines got into the hive an alien player could take over as the Queen. The players got to know each other very well and it created a tight community. It was rather cool and rather sad because it was one of many games that...the evil EA has erased from being able to play. ( Alpha Centauri - an amazing sci-fi strategy game being another). It's ashame  with how much effort  Cold Iron studios put into recreating the look , the feel, and the sounds of the Alien franchise yet the main framework of what brings people back to playing multiplayer games is ....other people. You can't even chat to others in this game. Let us play alien characters in a versus marine mode.  Let us chat in some sort of lobby and create an in game community. Make this franchise....great again !
