_childDocuments_.review: So far, so good. One thing I'd like to say up front, everyone compares it to Left 4 Dead, but really I think it's 10x more like Deep Rock Galactic. You have classes and customized load out that increase with perks from leveling up and playing the class... L4D had no such thing. About the only similarities are hordes of monsters and you have a pair of weapons. Also L4D all characters were identical, and weapons were picked up in the level. This seriously is more like DRG than L4D.The game play and atmosphere are perfect, the leveling system is a little simple and not hyper tweekable, which is good.The down sides... The menu layout. It seems all over the place (like exit is in the settings? Why?). Escape doesn't go back one menu level, but all the way out, and right click goes back one menu level... Wtf. That gets irritating very quickly.also, yes you can change the key bindings, but why oh why was [E] not made the interact button... [F] is... I pulse abilities trying to interact with objects or npc's CONSTANTLY. Again, yes you can change it, but I leave at the default because I assume the devs had a reason for it... Though in this case I've yet to figure out why.Also, three players? I know 4 is just as arbitrary, but it's so normal it really feels like wtf here. Also 4(5, soon 6) classes... But only 3 players? And random teams really make this worse for teamwork besides "we all have guns, just shoot!" Tactics.Overall I still recommend the game highly. If you play with friends on comes outside the game like discord, the random player downside is mitigated, but the 3 player limit still makes it rough if you have a normal group of players you normally play 4 player games with, someone has to sit out.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Fireteam Elite

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Games like World War Z or Left 4 Dead. This is for you.If you have any connection to the Alien Franchise, as soon as you hear the first Plasma Rifle shoot or the first Xeno scream in anguish as you burn him and his fellow Friends to ash, you won't stop smiling.I promise you this!For about 40€ this is an absolute must buy!Crossplay needs to be added though.Will keep the playerbase alive!
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Fireteam Elite

_childDocuments_.review: Just got done playing through the first act with with my 2 buddies on Discord and we all had a blast. I went into this with really low expectations after being let down by the Back4Blood beta, but I've been very impressed with how fun this game is. The graphics do leave a little to be desired, however they nailed the atmosphere. The lighting and feel of the environment are awesome and capture the essence of movies. The sound design is also amazing, of course the M41-A pulse rifle sounds cool. If you have two buddies that want to play a fun co-op shooter, this is actually a really cool game with some interesting upgrade mechanics.4.5/5 if you're with friends and not bots
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Fireteam Elite

_childDocuments_.review: A 3rd person shoot-em-up type game, work together with 2 other co-op players (for a total of a 3-man fireteam) to defend yourself against waves of aliens featured from the famous series as you traverse through the various campaign maps and objectives. Players looking for Left-4-Dead type games will find themselves at home here. Various classes allow you to drastically change your playstyle with unique abilities and weapon buffs.A large variety of weapons and consumables, including a default infinite ammo pistol.Insane attention was used for the graphics, map textures, and hilariously detailed challenge cards and emotes.If you do not have enough players, the AI teammates are next to useless except as tanks and the occasional grenade (hopefully, the new patch will adjust this).Players who join a room and leave shortly thereafter 'locks' in an AI teammate, forcing players to remake the lobby and waiting time (which can take some time on the higher difficulties)Any difficulty above standard becomes significantly unforgiving, with no answer to trolls or 'solo' type players who join, die, and leaveAll in all, it is a very stable type game with surprising episodes of fun and amusement mixed into the relatively small map pool and grind type gameplay, backgrounded with gorgeous details in graphics and sound (once again, have to point out the entertaining challenge cards and emotes).
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Fireteam Elite

_childDocuments_.review: A fun if very straightforward experience. Basically, the game should’ve been made a decade ago. As an alien fan it’s a visual stunner, just under Alien Isolation in terms of how it viscerally re-creates the alien's universe. It even incorporated elements from Prometheus in ways far better than expected.  And there's some impressive deep cuts here. The only thing missing the lack of PREDATOR boss fights.  A Co-op shooter is decent; if you're nostalgic for the combat loops of GEARS OF WAR or Mass Effect 3 this will be for you. It does not have as much replay-ability of the all-time greats like L4D, DRG or Vermintide. So, I would recommend getting it on sale.   Its major issues it a that you must finish the campaign to get the other modes; which is a wildly backwards way to approach a game like this and the lack of a lobby browser. The actual progression is fine (Better than B4B some others on the market right now) but the lack of quick play from the start was a bad idea.  Decent for what it is; get it on sale.  6.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Fireteam Elite

_childDocuments_.review: Perfectly enjoyable co-op shooter. It has progression, class variety, good class synergy and rewards teamwork. Grindy enough to provide plenty of playtime, developed and deep enough to make it worth your while. Best if played with at least one, ideally two buddies (squad size is only three).Not recommended if you don't have anyone to play this with, as public matchmaking seems pretty dead (which is undeserved).Also, if you're a fan of ALIEN(s) you won't get many of those particular vibes, as the colonial marines in this game are a bunch of Xenomorph-murdering godsters, that routinely decimate entire swarms of aliens. So, no horror, decent action though.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Fireteam Elite

_childDocuments_.review: For fans of the Aliens franchise this is pretty fun as it brings the story forward and has elements spanning the various parts of the franchise.The story is fairly short, but it makes up for it in the fact that has a lot of replayability in what classes you choose, their loadouts, the challenge runs, leveling your classes and your character up, and the challenge cards making it harder or easier based on what you want to do. This was a really fun game, and highly recommended to play with friends as it was not designed to play solo very well.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Fireteam Elite

_childDocuments_.review: Exactly what I wanted. Survival against overwhelming odds. Whether you've got the adrenaline to face them all head on with a fully loaded Smart Gun and yell "Lets Rock!!", or you're simply terrified as you face a horde of Xenomorphs with a half-loaded Pulse Rifle like Hicks. The sites, the sounds: all Alien. Love it, I'm having so much fun and can't wait to play more, especially with a squad! Try it for yourself, "only way to be sure.":)
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Fireteam Elite

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty similar to the World War Z game but in the Aliens universe. Only 4 Campaign missions right now and each has 3 parts to each mission but I assume the devs will add more content as the game ages. WWZ was the same way, limited content at launch and more stuff added later. can get a little grindy at times but ultimately a decent way to kill some time and get some frustration out on some Xenos. going to try to get some friends to play with me later, I imagine that is where the real fun is.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Fireteam Elite

_childDocuments_.review: This has to be one of the most fun shoot em up, horde style games I have played in a long time. The atmosphere is excellent, the audio is perfect, and the gun play and enemy variety are all enjoyable. Fighting off hordes of xenos feels badass, and learning tidbits of lore from the other characters as well as in game intel drops is fun for a fan of the universe. I am 75% done with the campaign and its been a blast the whole way through. I look forward to playing the horde mode that unlocks after the campaign and I truly look forward to what this game has to offer in the future. I would have been content paying $60 for this game, so I absolutely believe its worth the 40 dollars its listed at.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Fireteam Elite

_childDocuments_.review: The game is honestly not that bad. BIG IMPROVEMENT FROM COLONIAL MARINES. The aliens are a bit derpy sometimes getting clipped into the environment / stuck in mass bodies of themselves. But that can easily be looked passed since its very fixable. There are special alien units.  Tho i will say the most entertaining part of this game is blasting a clip into the aliens feet and watching them desperately trying to catch their momentum in mid sprint like a cat trying to sprint across hard wood floors. (ABSOLUTELY HYSTERICAL) The synth AI that replaces your normal team mates are down right DUMB (please fix this). The game is obviously better with friends but this definitely fills that much needed void of L4D (Left 4 dead) / WWZ (World war Z) hybrid mod I've always wanted. There is a decent talent tree but I am honestly not far enough to exactly say how bad or good it is. Yes in the beginning it's a bit unrealistic cause you are literally "SWIMMING THROUGH ACID BLOOD" but put on a few challenge cards and change the difficulty and you will get the adventure / challenge you've ultimately thirst for you gluttonous monster for punishment. (Dont you lie to me)
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Fireteam Elite

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game! As a coop survival and Aliens fan, this is epic. Very fun, intense and challenging, love the action, the gunplay, great lengthy maps, there are tons of enemies (and I mean tons! My fingers hurt from all the action!), customization, perks, classes, weapons and attachments. I also appreciate the RPG elements, leveling up your classes and weapons, customizing your build etc. If you love Aliens and coop survival action, you'll love this!
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Fireteam Elite

_childDocuments_.review: The good:- present day graphics quality- almost Alien atmosphere in its levels- satisfying level design- satisfying game play - no technical bugs, flawless game to play- cards are a very interesting feature for this game and a plus.- a lot of guns to toy with- interesting perks/ original setup idea- plenty of online gamers to team with for missions- levels of difficulty feature + the cards are a game changer, making you come back for more.- satisfying number of classes to choose fromThe bad:- boring repetitive in "Serious Sam" style game play- no story to feel a connection to Alien universe- stupid, uninspired dialogues , in what was suppose to be a base, with NPCs,  designed  to familiarize with the story elements.- poor network coding. This is such a problem that sometimes you believe that you are actually playing a "Host connection lost" simulator. And not an ordinary one, but a good one.- no facial animation in dialogues with NPCs which is embarrassing for a game in 2022.- consumable slots too tiny for the task in hand in this game- lack of DLCs despite the rich Aliens universe realm which exists.- lack of communication between developer and fan base which is a major MINUS.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Fireteam Elite

_childDocuments_.review: For starters, a good game. Interesting classes/mechanics. Diversification via class build and weapon choice and attachments.The NOT RECOMMENDED is for the constant connection issues, worsened even more by NO possibility for rejoining a disconnected game (not even between friends or premade group)It's not even lag, can have lag spikes and game keeps on going but instant DC with no stutter/lag beforehand Will have fun sometimes with friends, but will not farm whatsoever anymore (stopped at 3 maxed classes)
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Fireteam Elite

_childDocuments_.review: not done with it yet but the sound design and atmosphere are incredible, would recommend for that alone. the game is a bit buggy no pun intended and it does suffer from the all too common problem of always online with ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ servers. you cant play alone without still hosting a match and using the brain dead friendly AI. would not recommend at full price
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Fireteam Elite

_childDocuments_.review: This game was pleasantly surprising to me as it actually has some difficulty to it. I was looking at the IGN gameplay and it looked... relatively easy. However, launching the game revealed that the "standard" difficulty is almost the lowest difficulty you can choose from. Now...Let's go kill some aliens2 hours after initial reviewI feel it is extremely important to mention that this game is challenging, even on the normal difficulty. The bots that replace teammates are kind of a weak link so if you plan on playing this singleplayer, definitely queue for a public match
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Fireteam Elite

_childDocuments_.review: My impressions of the game are twofold. On the one hand a good quality shooter, a few classes with the ability to compose your own unique build from modules, a lot of different weapons, crowds of enemies running from all sides, and all this in co-op. On the other hand a small variety of these same enemies, a small number of maps with the same missions, with little variation in what room you will do under the task quickly bored. And there are no players in multiplayer, you have to buy the game with friends. Put a positive review only because I like games with an emphasis on grind and I had someone to play with. Get it at a discount with two friends and then you definitely won't regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Fireteam Elite

_childDocuments_.review: Putting aside the cool Alien aesthetic, the game feels really awkward and stale. The core gameplay and design of the levels do not inspire me to push on through the grind and higher difficulties. Why is every other room a boring holdout? Why, when ambushing enemies spawn out of vents or holes in the wall, do they do so one at a time? Why, in this horde shooter about xenomorphs, is there an entire subset of synth enemies that turn encounters into a cover shooter? And why, in this online coop game from the year of our lord 2021, can you not join a game in progress? And why does it have some of the worst AI ever put into a videogame?It's just weird and tedious and generally boring. I'd rather play World War Z.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Fireteam Elite

_childDocuments_.review: Not bad, not exceptionally good though either. The matchmaking system is rather poor in design if just looking for a quick match, and forces you to pick a map and difficulty before matching up with others, when really you just want to "go at it". Often, it is difficult to match up with real players and instead and given two AI players instead (not so great, but not the worst AI team mates either).The weapons, meh. Fun, but the mechanics are basically the same for all of them. Aim and shoot. I was just dying for that one weapon that ruled them all, but it's not there. Nothing I can charge up, nothing with a massive advantage and nothing that I can customize more heavily than a few attachments here and there.To me, max-level Technician, play all of the maps, maybe a Horde mode here and there, enjoy. The rest will unfortunately be rather predictable and repetitive in time. Doesn't mean it doesn't have replayability - it's just that you'll get rather tired of that even on increased difficulties rather quickly.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Fireteam Elite

_childDocuments_.review: Game is in its infant state, so will be looking for more content down the road. It feels like an old arcade game... (Terminator) maybe... the one kids played back in the 80s & 90s.You dont need much to beat the game. the perk packs are worthless, you dont need them. All in all its not what I expected. Looks nice, sure, But far to arcade like. needs more of that horror that we all love... more blood, more of that fear drive... Needs Boss Battles maybe...Need: The Predalin, The New Born, Crock Alien, Rino Alien, Arachnid Aliens, Scorpion Alien. Option to play as Predator...
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Fireteam Elite

_childDocuments_.review: Good game with interesting additions to the lore. Might get a bit repetitive (in terms of gameplay) over time. But if you want to spend 25-40 mins (average level duration) of your time (alone or with friends) shooting xenomorphs and synths – this is a good option. Get it during sale and enjoy your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Fireteam Elite

_childDocuments_.review: Played through the campaign.imagine a small studio with talent and finite budget , they put all the resources where they matter . the animations are smooth the sound is awesome the environments drip in ambience. aside some of the campaigns occur on promethian tile sets and are mostly excellent , there are a few WY camps and stuff that look rather mundane , but crawling through the steam filled oppressive confines of the alien hive is all i could of asked for .the heart beat pulse of the motion scanner and the m14a roars into life screams , pops , aliens dropping and a huge smile on my faceand then anything they absolutely didnt need is unceremonial dumped there is no lip syncing for eg.some things got missed that should of been in quick play, a decent comms system for your mm squad etc.there is progression , customisation and variation for repeat play . though i dont think it will hold me for l4d2 lengths of time (but then what has) given the quality of whats here and skill demonstrated staying this tightly focused i have no issue trusting in the devs future development and ongoing building on this a very solid and fun base.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Fireteam Elite

_childDocuments_.review: Did you really want to like Aliens: Colonial Marines but got turned off by the bugs and Gearboxes deceptive marketing?Do you like third person shooters, horde based point defense, the movie Aliens, or co-op action romps?If you answered yes to any of the above, this game is absolutely worth the purchase and, while it's not a masterpiece, will put a massive grin on the faces of you and two close friends. Heavily suggested and a hell of a time.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Fireteam Elite

_childDocuments_.review: "Aliens Left 4 Dead" with classes, gear level ups and customizable builds.The game doesn't bring anything new, it's basically made by an indie dev team and it may look and be a mediocre game, but it is still a fun game and could go for couple of hours if you want to try and finish the campaign in the hardest difficulty setting.The missions are around 15-25 minutes each on average. So the story mode would stack up from 3h to 5h depending if you rush or look for intel.If you have the opportunity to play with 2 other friends it's highly recommended, if you have no one and want company you'll be better off looking on their discord or trying matchmaking coinflip (takes a lot of time read below).If you wonder how the AI is.. he does work, he does kill. Decently actually, but he doesn't dodge Alien attacks and sometimes is shooting walls. It's decent since you can use him as bait as well.As for achievements (hunters) it will take a while, I would say around 100h? Depending on which you like/dislike the most, completing the game on the hardest difficulty and max leveling all weapons will take the longest.The combat rating from my perspective doesn't provide anything. It is merely a statistic showing you already unlocked perks and attachments which give like boosts, but it's not a day and night difference compared to games like Destiny where 20 power is enough to get one shotted by enemies.The only thing I have to complain is queueing for public lobbies, the moment you enter one a mission countdown starts right away. The thing is, if someone is already looking for the same mission and same difficulty you'll join them, but if no one is looking you enter a queue lobby alone where the countdown starts right away, it is only 60 seconds and it only searches for players for the first 40 seconds, the final 20sec it will fill the lobby with 1 or 2 AI. You have to leave queue and requeue again and again if you want to play with at least one player.Please add a ready up system you have 3 options:- Majority starts the countdown (2 out of 3)- If all 3 ready up start the game automatically- Having a "host" where he can only start when the other 2 are ready.Also add server browsing or at least let people choose more variables when searching, ONE MISSION ONE DIFFICULTY is not enough. You come to a point you just want to play anything for XP. This will also help with personal mission preferences.We are in 2021 and some games still miss these little QoL that make a huge diference.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Fireteam Elite

_childDocuments_.review: At 249 hours: I finally beat Insane mode. What a game, and a masterclass in difficulty design, class balance and synergy. The game, which was only expected to last 6-8 hours, has been my ONLY game for weeks, and the most challenging shooting content I have played. 10/10 recommend, and is truly an experience for skilled shooter players. At 14 hours in:Came in with low expectations, given the mixed reviews on social media. This game will likely be my staple horde shooter. Amazing pacing, good controls. Match making is pretty good on PC. I suspect higher difficulties might prove challenging, as the player base would be smaller, but all in all, this is really good, 30 minute missions, which are fast paced and fun.At 70+ hours in: This game is FANTASTIC for players looking for a challenge. At Extreme to Insane levels, this is some of the hardest FPS content out there. Rewards you as well for completing higher difficulties with Skins and Weapons. Intense is a good starting point for most veterans, extreme and insane will require a coordinated team, and feels very rewarding. Difficulty level match making is a must for the future, small add on, huge benefit to the player base the game may have accidentally catered for. Could be known as a top game for difficulty, if they cater to it.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Fireteam Elite

_childDocuments_.review: A well-executed horde shooter that will resonate particularly well with Aliens fanboys & fangirls!The devs really nailed the look and feel of the game, all the way down to the almost corny personality of the NPCs. The orchestral soundtrack also leans heavily on the score from the Aliens movie, which adds to the fan service. Gunplay and character movement feels super tight, and there is a large array of enemy types to deal with.The number of levels is relatively small, but with tons of customisation option across classes, weapons, perks, and challenge cards, there is a decent amount of replayability. I particularly liked how novel the perk system is - using a grid with certain shapes and sizes. The hardest difficulty levels offer a real challenge and require a good set of teammates (tip: use Discord to find good folk to play with).Would love to see a sequel, or at least some more DLC for this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Fireteam Elite

_childDocuments_.review: I spent a lot of time with this game on XBOX GamePass. I bought it when it was on sale. Compared to 2021-2022, I can say the game is a bit more stable.More details are needed compared to the movie, and they should make that gloominess feel a bit more. + Graphics and map designs + Sounds ± The character movement mechanism could be better. ± When you want to enter as co-op, you may encounter lag. It seems like there is a SYNC problem. + Pathogen maps are perfect.- There is a freeze when the in-game maps are loading (Damn guys, they haven’t been able to solve this problem for 2 years)Still, I enjoy playing. But this game definitely needs investment.If you want to watch => 2023 =>  2022 =>
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Fireteam Elite

_childDocuments_.review: Aliens: Fireteam Elite is a very enjoyable and interesting game, albeit with some flaws and a mostly dead player base.- Fair price- Fun and engaging game-play- Lots of action, you're always shooting something- HUGE variety of new and returning weapons, including the iconic Pulse Rifle and Smartgun- Deep character progression and customization- There is always something to unlock- Several classes, each with their own unique play styles, skills and perk sets- Main campaign is of decent length- You can play with friends (if you have any), up to 3 players in a lobby- Good voice acting, with occasional mild humor- Tons of replay-ability and post-game content- Nice fresh take on TPS for the series- Some challenge cards change up the game-play in an interesting way- Horde modes are fun and challenging- Esther is cute af- Friendly fire is enabled and forced at higher difficulty levels- Boring and predictable enemy behavior and movement (all follow the same path for some reason, not very Xeno-like)- Goofy soundtrack which doesn't fit the game at all- Laggy servers that sometimes spontaneously disconnect you- A few occasional stability issues, such as entering a new area causing the game to stutter for a second- No in-game communication other than pings (not even a text chat)- Dead/dying player base, it takes a while to find a match, and the post-game content is devoid of players- DLC campaign is way too short- No facial movements, characters talk without moving their mouths- AI teammates are utterly useless, and sometimes wander around aimlessly- FOMO limited-time events with insane requirements (Extreme+ difficulty on Horde? Really?)- Horror elements are severely lacking- Only one real boss fight, which is exclusive to the DLC
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Fireteam Elite

_childDocuments_.review: HUGE WASTE OF MONEY. They need to make it so SOLO PLAYERS can play and SUCCEED.When you have to play the 1st quest 15 times to level of your player so you can ACTUALLY finish the second quest (there are 3 to complete the first mission), then there is a problem with the game. You run out of ammo constantly the first few play-throughs and it took me till the 4th or 5th time to get passed the second quest...and they take about 30min per play-through. They all seem to end the same way, RUN AWAY at the very end to escape and make it to the end of the mission. The AI are AWFUL...they stand there and watch more often than not. So if you don't have 2 friends to play with, then it is all on you and you are basically playing it solo 75% of the time. I still can't beat the final quest in the 1st Mission (there are 3 quests to do). Everything is fine until you got to push the last button and then RUN back to the ship with 5 Alien BOSSES chasing you...which I always get caught and die. I have played it almost a dozen times with different soldier types and it doesn't matter, you aren't getting away or fighting off the final swarm. Even game channels have the PRO GAMER saying "and now RUN FOR IT...RUN RUN RUN. Ahhh...made it." That is total BS. 18hrs playing and I STILL CAN't FINISH the FIRST MISSION!
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Fireteam Elite

_childDocuments_.review: Solid game. Aliens make for a great change of scenery from the traditional zombie hordes, they can walk on the walls/ceilings which changes how you pick your spots to hold and makes you more reliant on your motion tracker for vision.The game isnt particularly long, maybe 8 hours for a first playthrough but the replayability comes from either unlocking and leveling everything or the card mutators.Basically at the start of each mission you can chose to use a card, these cards all offer various rewards from XP to help level faster, Money to unlock equipment, attachment drops for mission only equipment drops and while you are learning you might also want to use the cards that buff you to make things easier to help you get past something you are stuck on.But late game you'll be playing the cards that make things crazy. There are the basics like faster aliens, more aliens, aliens do more damage, tankier aliens, CC immune specials then we have interesting cards like like turn every regular runner into a prowler (equivalent of making all commons Hunters/Jockeys lol), infinitely respawning drone to chase you through a mission, only headshots do damage, aliens are invisible, hologram aliens, specials spawn in pairs etc.Trying to do these challenge cards on higher difficulties has easily added another 150hours of playtime for me and my group.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Fireteam Elite

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a missed opportunity. It could have been a great game if it had more game modes/content. It has a great atmosphere, does not have huge hardware requirements and it is fun, if you have a friend to play with, but alone it will not last long. The game died after 2 months, because the player base reduced to almost 2-300 from 14.000 people. You have higher chance to win the lottery than finding two players for a random mission.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Fireteam Elite

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a mindless shooter to relax to and shoot massive hordes of xenomorphs this will scratch that itch. It's light on story but has a good weapon, class, and skill customization that keeps you engaged for hours. No micro transactions as of this review, and everything can be bought with in game currency you can earn which is always a plus from me. Have not tried the DLC yet so cannot comment on that content.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Fireteam Elite

_childDocuments_.review: At least it's not alien colonial marines!...but in fairness, it's overall, kinda lackluster.It gave me the impression of the developer doing the minimum and set their goals low, so they would not step into the same ♥♥♥♥ storm, as Aliens: Colonial Marines.The bad:The graphics quality looks more like ego shooters of the 2010 to me. The faces are ugly and you have about 8 of them (2 for every ethnicity). No body type modifications, a few hair styles, three female voices, that all spout the same lines, the armor clips into the body at the front, when you stand after having moved and so on.Forget about trying to make a character that looks like someone from the franchise or yourself with so limited options, you can be happy if you manage to make a character, that you are okay with playing and don't find ugly. The mission design is kinda uninspired. Go there set up a defense, then activate a thing and fend of the hordes of aliens. At least they come from different angles but still... no collapses of ceilings or floors, no battle damage starting to mount through explosions, no fires spreading, just the usual exploding red barrels and aliens jumping out of fixed points. As I said... lackluster. Only 3 people allowed per mission (even left for dead 1 had 4), no drop in of players, after the mission started, if one disconnectes instead he will be replaced by a bad AI controlled android, who is not terrible, but also not good.3 people is especially grating, as there are a lot of couples, who want to play together in these times.The visual storytelling is also kinda lackluster. Just a few bodies lying around without really telling you a story of what happend besides they having been killed, as is the storytelling in general. If I play three missions in a row about rescuing a single scientist and I still am not able to feel any emotion towards him (good or bad) at the end of the mission because he is that bland, something went wrong. The positives:The difficulty is good even on normal I had fun. You don't just breath through without looking and I had fun using some consumables to get through the mission. (even if the aliens are more like the zombies of l4d though from their damage output, which I find not to my personal licking. I would have wished for less aliens, but it being more important to not get hit by them. Instead we have true hordes and an alienattack costs you a very small percantage of your health. I am sure on the highest difficulty levels they will make much more damage, but with there being about 150 aliens per mission and around 40+ attacking you on a horde defense point, that is not what I am personaly looking for in an Alien game, but that is more personal preferance.)The sound design is okay, the music is okay, the graphics are okay enough to play. The Ai works and aliens crawl on the ceilings and walls without getting stuck (yes, my expectations are that low). There are some different alien types for variety (even if they too are uninspired) acid aliens, that exploded into big acid explosions, when you destroy them or try to jump on you and explode, if you don't and warrior/brute/minor queen aliens bulletsponges, that try rip you off your feet and attack you a few more times, till they let go again, Maybe there will be more in later missions of the game, but so far, that is what I encountered.Summary:5 out of 10 if I had to add a number.If you are a fan of the movie alien 2, wait for it being on sale and hope, that there are still players enough, that will play this then. If you are not an alien fan, why did you even read a review this long? :-D Give it a pass.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Fireteam Elite

_childDocuments_.review: Needs a server/game browser and the ability to join ongoing games. Needs an in game chat ability and or voice comms.Without these few crucial options I'm afraid it may die a slow death on pc as it bleeds players from frustration over trying to find players to join without waiting endless amounts of time. Nonetheless it's a fun shooter with some upgrading and plenty of build/class options that really nails the Alien franchise feeling. With a bit more work to it's multiplayer aspects it has some real potential.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Fireteam Elite

_childDocuments_.review: The campaign for this game is short, the NPC's mouths don't move when they are talking, and most people seem to get bored with it fairly quickly. That being said, the game is enjoyable to play, and with the promise of new content on the way the $40 this game originally retailed for isn't bad considering that most new AAA games are $60 (or $70 if you're unlucky enough to be playing them on "next gen" consoles).

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately, I dont recommend this game in its current state.Lets sandwich it, the good:1. Aliens universe done very well, tons of fan service and somewhat interesting story.2. Great look, feel, and sound design.3. Multiple classes, weapons, skills, and so on with modifiable configurations.The bad:1. Its multiplayer but has no easy way to make a team which is required for higher difficulties. This includes no in game chat or lobby.2. Presently only has 20 to 30 hours of play if you really want to grind out each character and weapons.3. Lots of bugs, though they are being fixed regularly.4. A bit overpriced for what we actually got.5. Lacks a long term replay ability.The good again, because its a sandwich:1. Has a lot of potential to be great and is decent for the time being. Essentially built a strong base to expand on.2. Studios first game and seems responsive to players and active in addressing bugs/issues.3. Fan service, again. As someone that grew up with these movies (80s - 90s) its spectacular.4. Its a good time with friends.So while there are quite a few good things, overall the bad things weigh very heavily on the game. If you're a huge Aliens fan its a must have. If you're just a gamer with a casual interest in Aliens, find something a bit more worth it. I would keep up with updates though and look for progress, as I said there is a ton of potential here.

_childDocuments_.review: Good game. A lot like Left 4 Dead + CoD Zombies.The overall "formula" to the game is very predictable. There's 2 parts or sections for every level in the entire game. A section that you walk or run through and a section where you hold your ground for awhile. Think hallways vs. large rooms. That is the entire basis to this game. Every level is like that, including the DLC. That isn't saying that the levels are boring. The level designs are authentic to the Aliens universe and are quite interesting to look around in. Look close enough and you'll see a bunch of little easter eggs for Aliens fans.Weapons wise I will say I felt 0 need and had 0 interest in checking out literally any other weapons aside from the flamethrower and the default machine gun (the main one from the movies with the side ammo counter). I maxxed them out and used them the entire game. I also only ever used one class, Demolitions.I think the strongest point this game has to offer is it's array of enemies. You have a multitude of different Synths and Aliens to kill. They each are pretty unique and offer different challenges for facing each enemy type. I played on the standard difficulty the entire time and found points that were both difficult and other points that were easy.If you enjoy games like Left 4 Dead or CoD Zombies, you may like this game. It lacks the charm of the two aforementioned games, but at least on paper has far superior replayability in the form of different classes, attachments for weapons, cosmetics, and challenge cards which drastically alter how each mission is played.I would easily recommend this to anybody who is thinking about picking this game up. However I would strongly urge you to buy it on sale. If you do buy it on sale I can pretty much guarantee that you won't regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: Fireteam lacks atmosphere and gravitas while ultimately coming off as a tad lazy in it's execution. The menus work, the game-play works, but there is no vision behind it. It's just a generic TPS shooter cashing in on the brand. Get it on game-pass.I'm a huge Aliens fan, so I can forgive more than somebody whose less interested in the franchise. Alien Isolation set an insanely high bar. This game is not on the same level as that. Temper your expectations! That being said it's... not bad!It's just kind of bland and lacks a game-play hook and atmosphere that other games in it's genre do far better. It's a bit frustrating because there is so many avenues they could have gone down and for some reason they decided on a generic TPS shooter. Meanwhile games like GTFO, L4D, and Darktide play like a far better "Aliens experience" than this "branded" game.The voice acting is grating and repetitive and the game-play is far too simple to hold my attention for very long. I would have preferred an FPS Vermintide/L4D clone or a more polished/forgiving GTFO style puzzle shooter. This is basically an arcade game wrapped in a Gears of War skin. A bit too dumbed down for mass consumption... and seems to have failed to find a large audience because of it. At best I hope this will spur some more interest in developing games for the franchise... Would love to see Alien(s) Isolation. Would I recommend this game to other people? Not really. I barely played it and I'm a huge Aliens fan.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't recommend this game. It's dead and kept on life support. It lacks players and content. This could have been a great title, similar to the Warhammer Vermintide / Darktide franchise, but instead it's just a missed opportunity, in my opinion. The campaign is short, we completed it in about 5 - 6 hours. After that, the only thing we could do was repeating it at higher difficulty, but neither one of my friends felt like grinding the same content over and over again.I then tried a couple of times the matchmaking, but failed to find anyone except for a couple of guys who left the game after a few minutes, leaving me with the useless bots to die miserably.And that was it. I then uninstalled the game and moved on.Now don't get me wrong, as a fan of the Aliens franchise I totally loved the campaign and the fact it's directly tied to the Prometheus / Alien Covenant lore (both extremely underrated movies, in my opinion). I loved being able to visit the engineers ship, I loved the shooting and the sound effects of the marine rifle, just like in the movies. I had some good fun. And that's another reason I was even more let down when I couldn't get more.The maps are big but most of the space isn't even utilized, at least I wish this game was moddable, users would create tons of content. But I guess the tools aren't really available, so even the mods are really minimal. I would have liked to revisit the campaign with a 1st person perspective, but even that isn't possible at the moment.The only way I can recommend this is when heavily discounted and only if you can convince a couple of friends to play it together. Otherwise it absolutely isn't worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: Switching to Not Recommended after revisiting it as a solo player months after release, and a note to say you should only get this game if it's on sale and if you have two other friends to play with.Solo players beware: the matchmaking is terrible beyond Normal difficulty because the playerbase crumbled rapidly after launch and the AI teammates you get paired with if matchmaking fails are not smart enough to carry you through a Hard difficulty mission or greater.I'll note the big reason the playerbase crumbled was because they didn't have Quick Match until a month after launch (!), so there wasn't a way to find anyone to play with beyond using their Discord server.If you do get paired with other players, more often than not they are bored veterans who plow ahead without you and breeze through everything because the spawn points for the aliens are the same every time (oof). You might think "that's OK, I'm just here to grab colelctibles and enjoy the plot," but the game doesn't stop spawning aliens behind you in an effort to keep you together as a team, which is actually kinda cool as it adds to the intensity, but again ruins it for solo players who're trying to take their time.And you can't communicate to that bored veteran player that you're trying to take your time or that you're a newbie because there's no voice chat and no text chat whatsoever.Using their DIscord server helps mitigate that a little, but even then you're at the mercy of whatever timeslots work for the leftover playerbase.Gameplay-wise, honestly, it's fine. It's an intense wave shooter that rewards and encourages you to stick together and work as a team (which is all the more baffling as to why they didn't include text/voice chat; all you have is a ping). The loadout system is actually pretty unique and lets you get a little creative. And the voice actors give it their all. Other parts feel a bit unpolished and lazy in that the aliens do not react whatsoever to getting shot (as others have said, they are bullet sponges in the most literal sense), again the spawn points are the same every time, and if you take a moment to look at any of the human's faces on the brig, you'll see they are all talking over each other and really not doing much to occupy themselves.So again, only get this if it's on sale and if you have two other friends to play it with. If you are an Alien fanboy like me and gobble up Alien lore no matter how bad it is (looking at you, Covenant), it's kinda good for that too.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the better Alien games I've ever played, some technical problems, but those are being fixed as we speak, game is great, frankly. I recommend this game wholeheartedly for any Alien fan that enjoys multiplayer shooters in general, the game was made to be played with friends tho (Sure, you can use the "any game is better with friends" argument, but this one was designed around it, so it gets a pass imo), and by having at least one bud, you will have a blast, some levels feel repetitive, and some feel a bit too linear, voice acting could use some work, but for a team of 40+ people, this is really ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ impressive, I had barely any hopes for this game when it was announced 3 years ago, and now, I'd say this is one of the better Alien Franchise games we've ever gotten.While I could list a lost of pros, I'll list the cons first as they are more important imo.Cons with Spoilers -Non spoiler cons - -Alpha and Beta, the bots that fill in for players, aren't that smart, this is probably by design tho-The levels are a bit repetitive, this is not bad by itself, it just means the game could use a bit more variety-Story is okay at best-You'll need some third party communication software, like Discord or Steam's voice calls itself.-BugsNow for the Pros --Great gunplay-Good weapon variety-Good class and ability variety-Great Alien enemy variety-Good graphics-Great sound design-Great soundtrack-Fun Perk and Loadout system-New maps, classes, enemies, weapons, mods, cards and more will all be free! The only post launch content that will be paid will be cosmetics! Overall, if you are playing this game as it is intended (with buds or randoms), then you'll have a great time that is amplified by using Discord or Steam to communicate with your buds, great gameplay and a good addition to the Alien Franchise. TLDR - Good game, 8.0/10.0, or6.0/10.0 if you don't have friends and somehow wants a MP Coop game to be like a SP one, which frankly, that's on you.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great. It's got good graphics and visual design that really makes use of the license. I love the first 2 Alien movies. Films 3 and 4 are fine. The recent 2 are hot trash with abysmal writing and I hate them. They are pretty though. This game, in addition to nailing the aesthetic of the good Alien films, uses the visuals and a few of the concepts from the recent movies in a way that totally works for a game and almost gives me a better appreciation of those terrible movies. If nothing else their existence provides a few new enemy types and level motifs for this cool game. The level design is well done. It's combat functional and visually familiar to a fan of the films but I still found myself pausing every now and then to admire the scenery.The core gameplay is fantastic. Good combat and controls. It's not remaking the genre but it is competent and fun to play solo or with other players. It is better with multiplayer and I've still only played with randos but I've had good times with them. I know this will be great with friends that I can chat with on Discord. Yea there's no voice or even text chat. Other omissions and slight flaws: There's no lip-synced dialogue or cut-scenes beyond the opening of the game. Didn't bother me with what else is on offer here. The game runs very solid for me on a high-end card. There is a weird issue with controller input dropping out intermittently that honestly got pretty frustrating on one campaign. I also had sound effects loop infinitely on one occasion. One patch and those bugs will certainly go away. They couldn't kill the fun I was having.The sound design is really good in this game. The score is awesome. They don't just pull music from the movie but what is there doesn't sound cheap and fits nicely with the atmosphere of the Alien universe. It's very cinematic. The in-game sound is just what you'd want from an Aliens game. Sound cues aid nicely in combat. I started really digging the menu sound effects. It's all very crispy and fun to interact with.I'm about 3/4 of the way through the campaign and still have only used one class. There's some depth to building out your character abilities and perks and I look forward to replaying the campaigns and exploring all that. New campaigns would be great. There's a lot of fun to be had here and I hope they continue releasing content for this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is BETTER than ALIENS COLONIAL MARINES  imo BUT the game itself is just decent to play a shame that it was rushed out in some aspects for those eager for a coop game.Some crucial little things about this game need to be fixed before I can recommend it which can be done. The negatives outweigh the positives for this game at the moment for me and others which is frustrating because of glaring issues while playing mostly due to missing basic functionality. I put in 37 hours into the game and leveled up the classes and hopefully will come back to it in the future but overall it is less than that to beat the normal 4 campaigns consisting or 3 missions each.▬ No voice chat OR text chat - I ask myself Why, 2021 no VOIP or even TEXT chat in this game at all to communicate to each other on the hardest difficulties. This game isn't GTFO but you can't tell people what they are doing wrong in the higher difficulty before they die out. Yes, people can say DISCORD replaces voice chat but that's just an excuse, You can't even contact the person in text through game tell them in the game the discord to hop in so basically I should randomly go through the trouble to add someone on steam (which requires levels) to have them join voice chat as the alternative?▬ The way the matches are set up is really stupid, You can only join people who are starting the match but you'll have 60 seconds to do it, You have the search for people in the SAME CAMPAIGN, on the SAME MISSION, on the SAME DIFFICULTY, with CARDS ENABLED OR NOT so expect respamming this nonstop until you get a chance to get gather a party of players. the lobby already automatically does a count down as soon as the host sets it up it and if it reaches a 20 or so seconds too bad, the bots take over. During the game, you cannot join in between an already ongoing match so no QUICK MATCHUP or DROP-IN  PLAY. If a player in your party gets kicked off for internet reasons or leaves it'll be replaced by a bot who are horrible on a harder difficulty so you become screwed and have to restart the game or try to deal with it.▬ No crossplays adds the already gruesome matchmaking system makes it really hard to find any games, you'll have to spam over and over and over again praying that someone will join your campaign in the same ACT, with the same MISSION with CARDS ON OR NOT and DIFFICULTY LEVEL all factored in to find the game,so basically going over each one refreshing nonstop starting game, quitting, starting, quitting hoping that 2 more people will hit the same one on the same difficulty at the same moment with the same skill level you are looking for. ▬ The bots in this game are dumb and yes this issue applies to many games, this is a common problem. They are replaced with working Joes who does not benefit the team with any kits or powers instead they have do fire at the aliens and rez you when you are down so just minimum basic functions.▬ Running through the maps is just a grind to get the better equips and attachments sorta rewarding but at the same time there isn't anything that makes the run from getting boring after multiple grinds since the map itself never changes sometimes it sends you different Xeno you've seen 1 or 2 run back but nothing major  about the game switches up. Everything is a set pattern loop. You run through with obnoxious npcs shouting out ambushes and things ahead of time before it happens to the game, defend a postion with turrets until hordes attack you rinse repeat for every map until you grind out the guns, perks, and levels you want etc. This game lacks any sort of Real depth and replay value after beating it once or twice. Horde mode is only ONE MAP and that is the only other gameplay mode. After beating the game will you unlock the last 2 difficulties and recon class.The cards (aka mutations) that affects the gameplay are cool but the game itself will only allow one randomly picked from your group.▬ need Fov slider▬ need proper Ultrawide support▬ The only 3 good kits in this game are TECH, DEMO, and GUNNER. Doc drones need a buff because they can be recharged when the doc picks up medic kit so most docs run around confused why the drone is empty or other teamates pick up kits which hinders the doc recharge. Also the RECON kit has a certain ability to zero in on certain targets to lower defense but glitches out and aims on teamates causing them to take massive damage. Either its working as intended or its half assed class that was put in at the last moment.▬ Alien blood aesthetic effect on characters in this game is so downplayed, I felt like the marines just swim in it like it's water even though when they drip in the environment you can see the environmental damage but your character is sleeveless and muscles takes no damage no scar no burns. I would expect to see burn wounds on me.▬ One type of enemy in this game makes it become a generic third-person shooter like every other game, not a big fan of humanoid,I know devs created them to break the pacing but its bad pacing and just turns it into a almost gears of war like game. (personal preference con)✜ The atmosphere and the lighting for maps in this game is absolutely fantastic, I felt like I was on ships,  even hallways from the movies. They did the research correctly and translated it into the game really well. Pipes bursting in corridors, flickering lights, dark areas and familiar sceneries and structures you've seen in Alien related lore and movies.✜The music and sounds in this game are great enough to make me go rewatch Alien movies because they brought back memories but the sound of guns in 7.1 surround is awful, they sound like they were ripped straight from a VHS movie. It's authentic but very low at the same time. Some of the other guns sound fantastic. Needs to pitch it up a bit so it doesn't sound like iam listening through a cup tied to a string.✜Some of the weapons in this game feel so good to use, the rifles the shotguns you must try and the heavy weapons and smart gun is beautiful.✜ The perk system is fun to mess with once you unlock them and combine them into different kits and skills. This makes it unique in how you build out your kit. They are blocks you rotate on a grid to benefit each other out with your choice.Long story shortThese are real issues, but overall any game is good with friends even if it has its cons. With communication it would make it more fun especially when you can socialize and strategize to play, I would not recommend this game if you plan to play solo online because overall it's just not fun. With all the above cons adding up to the game it makes it a hindrance  to matchmake with other players. I am however was fortunate enough to meet and make friends in the past games to play this one. If these stuff get fixed in the future I will gladly turn this thumb upside down because I do think this is an enjoyable title with elements that makes jumping into it very frustating. Alien fans will have fun regardless, people with friends will have fun, but soloist will be left in the cold.I think most people don't get why this game is thumbed down by me due to being blinded bias Aliens loyalist fans or just in general lack any sort of insight and perception, this isn't about following a hate bandwagon trend, that the game is bad or anything else but more so little technical issues, depth of gameplay and  what isn't in the package that can render the game unenjoyable and frustrating for those who wants to jump in and have fun out there in the long run. If you don't own the game or fail to see these issues above then I honestly cannot help your observational skills. my friends had fun, talked, and even discussed what they liked and didn't enjoy about the gameSome gameplay on the hardest difficulty available until we unlock harder

_childDocuments_.review: Aliens: Fireteam Elite is somewhat of a sleeper hit that wasn't super hyped up and there were no early reviews whatsoever. Being a HUGE Alien/Aliens fan (movies, comics, some of the games) I knew I was going to pick this game up right away and just hope for the best. After 10 hours of playtime I am pretty blown away with how much fan service there is here! It's not a perfect game, but there is a lot of fun to be had, even if you aren't an Alien/Aliens fan (if you have a friend or 2 to play with).The game is setup to be played mostly with a team of three people that progress through different campaigns that are each divided into different sections. Think something like Left 4 Dead or the free Steam game Alien Swarm. If you were to combine both of these titles and then throw in a ton more customization options you basically have Aliens: Fireteam Elite, and that certainly isn't a bad thing. The game feels quite good in third person. Most of the weapons are an absolute treat to fire, especially with how great the sound design is.The sound design is what I noticed first. Oh man it is EASILY 10/10. From the beautiful symphony-orchestra music pulled straight from the original Alien movie, to the gun firing sound of the iconic M4A1 Pulse Rifle, everything is spot on. When you are in a big hectic gun battle and you are hearing tense music, guns blazing, and aliens screeching, you really feel like it's happening around you.The game also LOOKS very good. All of the different gun models and types of Xenomorphs look amazing. The real beauty here, though, are the levels and level design. I am blown away with how some of these environments look and feel. There were times where I would walk away from the main path to go have a better view of something in the distance. The way the levels are designed and actually laid out feels really good too; not just a simple rail shooter where you walk in a straight line, but complex environments that come to life beautifully around you. There is a good variety of different landscapes and enemies throughout all 4 campaigns too (each one feels very different from one another). Everything seems to be optimized well too. My friend is currently using my old PC which is pretty old at this point and he is able to run everything on max very smoothly at 1080p (970 and DDR3 ram). I am currently running a 2070 and have everything maxed on 2k without any issues at all.The enemy AI seems pretty smart and the special aliens do a good job of trying to make your life an absolute hell while the swarm chips away at your team's health. I can't say the same, currently, about the friendly AI though. You MUST have real people on your team, the computer AI is extremely dumb and almost a detriment to you. Hopefully that gets fixed soon because I know my one friend who also loves Aliens would like to do some 2s with me and we would have to take on an AI allie (unless we just invited a random which you can totally do too). That is my main complaint with the game right now, the friendly AI. I would love to be able to boot up a campaign and play on my own, even on a harder difficulty without having to worry about how bad my PC allies are. I know back in the day I was able to do the harder difficulties in Left 4 Dead with PC allies, so hopefully they get an AI patch at some point.Finally I just wanted to say the customization is great. The ability to change your loadout for each of the 5 different classes to your liking is really the cherry on top of an already damn fine cake. Unlocking a new weapon as you level up and bringing it into the campaign to try out for the first time is a real treat. Also having loads of harder difficulties to progress through and unlock will be a challenge and one that will likely require playing around with your perks and finding something that works for your team. Not to mention there are a lot of cosmetic options to fool around with and unlock too.I will say that I don't know how long running through these same campaigns will last and there isn't really a ton here otherwise. In Left 4 Dead you at least had the versus mode to add some content in. Hopefully new campaigns are added in or this may be considered a bit lite on content for some people. Especially if you get bored with the main gameplay loop. If no other content is added then $40 may be a bit steep for this.Overall though, this is a must have for Alien/Aliens fans, the developers have done a great job creating a new story (albeit light) while sticking to the original content that we all know and love. Even if you aren't a huge fan of the series, there is a fun game here to play if you like games like Left 4 Dead or Alien Swarm and you have a friend or two to play with! Check it out!Overall: 8/10For Aliens Fans: 8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Criticism that the game is a) not scary/not horror survival and b) simply a horde shooter are not inaccurate; however, Aliens Fireteam Elite never presented itself as anything other than what it delivers, Left 4 Dead-like, high-octane thrills set against the sites and sounds of the Aliens universe. I find criticisms that the narrative is bare bones, virtually nonexistent, and uninteresting less accurate. I enjoy the obvious references to the movies but really appreciate the smaller nods to some of the novels like Aliens Echo and the direct tie-in to the Aliens Fireteam Elite prequel novel, Infiltrator, which gives the full story of Dr. Hoenikker and the events of Pala Station, including the backstory of Hoenikker's relationship with Monica. None of this is required to enjoy the run-n'-gun nature of the game, but it really helps flesh out what some might consider a lackluster story.It's a bug hunt, plain and simple. Run down corridors--preferably with real-life companions--and exterminate xenos. Rinse and repeat. Your mileage will vary and is likely directly proportional to your love of the franchise and action-oriented spray-n'-pray shooters. Some accused the developers of having no love for the source material, but any true lack of polish (NPCs' mouths don't move, for example) or additional modes is more a consequence of time and budget rather than lack of care. No cross play is unfortunate, though. Hopefully, this is added later.The game runs smoothly; the graphs are very good with detailed environments and authentic feeling locations. It's like a best-of of great locales from across the franchise. I had no problems with match making, and if you find a crew you like running with, you can continue mission after mission together. There is no in-game voice chat, but other than trying to decide which mission to play next, it's not an issue. NPC voice over guides you through the levels, as do location beacons. I like the voice over during the missions. It helps give the illusion that the missions happen in real time, as Sargent Herrera back on the Endeavor keeps you apprised of changes to the mission, new objectives, and incoming threats.The game is straight-forward. It doesn't pretend to be anything other than what was advertised. It's great summer fun that can be digested ad nauseam until you have your fill and feel like your chest is gonna burst. Crank some metal, raise the horms \m/ and lock n' load.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR:Aliens: Fireteam Elite. 5/10"A fine game but really just lacking in content and reasons to engage with it.""Wait until it is on Sale. $20 is fair, $30 is generous, but this game is not worth $40""If specifically you want one set in the Alien Universe. It's a moderately enjoyable investment of 4 - 6 hours."Pro:Music & Sound Effects -The Music was the heavy lifter. Knocked it out of the park in keeping the music very immersive to the Alien Universe while also being enjoyable to listen to in multiple parts. Ambient Sounds and all.Sound effects of the weapons were on point, the Aliens...Their death screeches were correct but honestly I didn't hear any similarities in their hisses or other sounds.Pro & Cons:Enemy Variety -It is both because without going into any spoilers there are several "groups" you could refer to them as and each group has at least 4 enemy types. So you'll face around 12 different baddies. However, they missed a potential easy win by going further in their enemy types, having each one more iconic, or more drastic changes in behavior.  For the most part its just a health, & skin tweak with the other differences being mostly ignorable. Team AI -Should you load in without a team or if your team leaves or disconnects during the game they will be replaced by the Synths, Alpha & Beta.At face value this is a good thing, your run isn't immediately dead as you will get new "teammates" to help you out. As far as their AI goes, it isn't terrible they are fairly competent in standard scenarios and to prevent getting lost or stuck on something after you go a certain distance they teleport to you. However, if Alpha or Beta are put in a bad situation they simply can not handle. If the enemy gets within melee range of them, they will never fire on them, use abilities or their roll to get away, they will simply allow the enemy to chip at their health until they die or you help them. Additionally they can't make intelligent choices like clear a room and then get up their downed partner, if you go down, they both will try to get you up. But be staggered by enemies hitting them, thus never able to get you up until they are slowly chipped to death as well, losing your run.Story -Underneath the gameplay there is an interesting and thematic in universe story to Aliens: Fireteam Elite. However, the way it is presented is very disjointed and aggravating. There are multiple story beats that break immersion, remove you from the middle of a mission to force you back to the ship just so you have to listen to or skip through a random NPC on the ship tell you a tidbit of information. Before giving you the mission to return right back where you started as if you never left to begin with.Cons:No Voice or Text Chat -I am unsure if this is intended to be placed in further down the line. But for a purely online game that is dependent on teams of 3 to work together, to have no way to communicate is a gross oversight. It should not have been released until this was put in at a Minimum.Theme/Immersion -Outside of the music and sound effects. This doesn't feel like an Alien game, there isn't a thrill or sense of dread or horror (except the Very last Mission of the Last Chapter in the Story). In the Alien Universe there should always be a sense of foreboding, hairs on the back of your neck standing up, head constantly on a swivel. But the programming of the Aliens leaves a lot to be desired because they are very predictable and sometimes get caught up on themselves which forces them to make weird pathing. The Aliens never seem intelligent like the Aliens from the Films (or scarier yet, the novels) just your typical cannon fodder. A game that did this much better, and the developers should've taken inspiration from is Space Hulk: Deathwing (which by no means is a good game at all mind you) but it did have the correct atmosphere with the tyrannids and the constant sealing & breaking down of doors to create & manage your own pathway through the Hulk was very well implemented, you never knew where they would come from or what to expect.Covering System -It isn't perfectly implemented (almost every time I try to reload my Marine comes out of cover) and of the 3 "Groups" of enemies there is only one that taking cover can actually be useful. The rest of the enemy types just Rush you and scale cover so it is actually detrimental to hunker down.Lack of Content -Upon release this game only has 4 Chapters, 3 missions in each chapter and a Horde mode (which you can not play until you finish the entire storyline). Each mission takes roughly 20 minutes, and is fully scripted with no variety no matter how many times you play it. So one 4 hour story that never changes. Zero re-playability.Horde Mode -Honestly one of the weakest Horde modes of a game I have seen in a very long time, I would expect something of this level on the XBOX 360 or older. There is only ONE map, with only one location to hold out at, the spawn. Of the 3 Groups of enemies the developers could throw at you they Only throw group 1, the Aliens, and their variant types.Difficulty Scaling -Standard is the basic "I just want to get through the campaign" level where its just a matter of chugging away until you're done. Unlikely to wipe during the mission. However, you take one step up to Intense and its a Vastly different game. It throws only a few more enemies at you but the enemies don't become any more intelligent or faster. The primary reason they are more "difficult" is because every enemy especially those tankier variants become absolute bullet sponges. You will run out of ammunition every little skirmish. They also increase the enemies damage 10 fold which is a drastic step up for a single difficulty increase, and friendly fire becomes merciless (A teammate had his flamethrower touch me for a second and I lost my entire healthpool).Squad Size -The developers made it clear in their press talks that they wanted it to be teams of three. Why? There are 4 different Marine Classes, with a 5th unlocked after you complete the campaign (though there is no reason to play it again after that).So there will always be one class at a minimum that can not be brought in to the squad, and unlike some other games, when you are party leader you can't enforce group variety. Lots of the players until they unlock the fifth class Only play Tech and Demo, so if you want a varied team you have to be the oddman out or lose out on some utility.The Shop -There are two currencies, one for Cosmetics or challenge cards(ALL of the cosmetics are very small changes, or in their attempts to stay aligned with the theme of Marine, they just come out to be bland or generic. No fun to be had there).The other for consumables, weapons, and weapon attachments. Outside of three? weapons (the grenade launcher, the flamethrower, and Potentially the rocket launcher) there is no reason to ever buy a weapon. They are only slightly different to what you start out with and stat wise are inferior."Exploration" -This game is Way too Linear. There is zero incentive to explore, for the most part the doors or pathways are sealed so you can not explore even if you want to. If you do, either you get some intel which does nothing for you except give you a bit of in universe lore (though it should lead to Better upgrades or at least more from the shop since the shop never changes from start to finish). Or you have the Chance to find a Hidden Cache which actually IS useful and appreciated when found, however since most of the time you go down these pathways they just lead to dead ends, with no added threat or danger or intrigue when doing so, it just feels like you wasted your time "exploring" unless you Do find a Cache.All in all, a game that is fine for one afternoon but in its current state worth nothing more. It would seem the Face Huggers got to the developers because this game is feeling pretty empty.

_childDocuments_.review: Aliens: Fireteam Elite : By Triple F"Aliens: Fireteam Elite" takes players on a thrilling and chaotic journey through the terrifying universe of the Alien franchise. Developed by Cold Iron Studios, this game manages to capture the essence of the films while delivering an engaging cooperative shooter experience that will have you and your friends at the edge of your seats.From the moment you start up the game, it's clear that a lot of love and attention to detail went into creating the atmospheric and immersive environments. Whether you're exploring a derelict spaceship or crawling through dimly lit corridors on a distant planet, the graphics and sound design work in harmony to keep you in a state of constant unease. The eerie audio cues and sudden bursts of Xenomorph activity amplify the tension, making every encounter feel like a life-or-death struggle."Aliens: Fireteam Elite" offers a variety of classes, each with distinct abilities and equipment options. This diversity encourages strategic game-play as you and your teammates decide how to best complement each other's strengths. Communication is key, and the game truly shines when played cooperatively with friends or other players online. Working together to fend off waves of relentless Xenomorphs while managing limited resources is a true test of teamwork and coordination.The enemy AI is commendable, replicating the frenetic and unpredictable nature of the Xenomorphs. From agile Facehuggers that scuttle across walls to towering Praetorians that require concentrated fire, each encounter presents a fresh challenge. The game also introduces new enemy types that add layers to the game-play, ensuring that players are always kept on their toes.One of the highlights of "Aliens: Fireteam Elite" is the weapon customization system. With a plethora of attachments, skins, and modifications to unlock and choose from, you can fine-tune your arsenal to suit your play-style. Experimenting with different load-outs and finding the perfect combination that complements your class and strategy is an addictive aspect of the game that adds a layer of depth to the overall experience.While the game delivers a gripping cooperative experience, it does stumble slightly in the story department. The narrative, while not lacking in potential, sometimes feels like a missed opportunity to further immerse players in the rich lore of the Alien universe. Characters and plot points could have been more fleshed out to create a stronger emotional connection with the story.In summary, "Aliens: Fireteam Elite" successfully captures the essence of the Alien franchise by delivering heart-pounding action, tense atmosphere, and challenging cooperative game-play. It's a must-play for fans of the series and a worthy experience for those seeking an adrenaline-fueled co-op shooter. While the storytelling could have been more robust, the sheer thrill of battling Xenomorphs with friends easily makes this game a standout addition to the franchise's gaming adaptations.

I wouldn't compare it to L4D too much, as L4D was mainly shining as a PvP game, while this is PvE with a max of 3 players. Matchmaking sucks a lot of the time, so if you have actual friends who're not cheapskates it's a lot of fun, especially on higher difficulties! There's a progression and the upgrades feel rewardful. _childDocuments_.review: Other reviews cover what the game is like so I'll just touch on the biggest failing of this game. In an age where most modern games have pretty good network code from decades of experience, Fireteam Elite will bring you back to the days of 20th century in good ole multiplayer network frustration, in a game where the intended difficulties and experience revolves around multiplayer. There is no seeing ally ping in lobbies, no built-in VC, no disconnect recovery mechanism of any sort (a short packet loss = game is gone), or any modern multiplayer optimization or convenience for that matter.It's as if all the network optimization and experience gained in the past couple decades in the industry just never happened for these guys, either that or nothing was budgeted to the network code/optimization at all... for a heavily multiplayer experience focused game. It's such a waste on the good parts of the game.I would say that it's not worth picking up the game, though it's basically competently done for the most part, the network roulette aspect is just more frustration then it's worth even if you live in parts of the world with good internet infrastructure.

_childDocuments_.review: Aliens: Fireteam Elite is basically this:- You run down hallways, killing waves of xenomorphs, sometimes stopping to kill androids in Gears of War-esque shootouts.- There are a variety of aliens: spitters, warriors, drones, praetorians.- You will regularly have to stop to press buttons to start horde events.And you do this for 6-8 hours. It's worse than Remnant: From the Ashes, but it's still fun enough that I don't regret my purchase.I wouldn't buy this unless you have a friend or two willing to play with you, though.
