_childDocuments_.review: I decided to pre-order this game due to my love for the Alien franchise and for the game's more reasonable price of $40. So far it seems like Left 4 Dead with ayy lmaos: go from point A to point B, hold out from swarms of bugs or synths, and shoot stuff in your way, so it's not the most exciting imo, but it still suffices as a cool co-op game to play with friends. The lore seems good and explains things simply to the players to help them understand some interesting tidbits or why so and so happened and what was the outcome, stuff like that. Haven't really payed attention to the story though, this game is one of those space out and shoot stuff type of experiences for me, but I'm sure it's alright, but probably not the most expansive. It feels kinda weird movement-wise, the third person camera angle was an interesting decision although first person might've been a bit better for playing as the marines, and looking around seems kinda weird and too fast or too slow at times, but overall the game seems fun and has good potential for the future. The class system and weapons/attachments are what really stands out to me. Being able to communicate with your friends and have a squad of marines with different specializations and weapons with various attachments that enhance the style of how you play in certain roles is awesome. Speaking of specializations and weapons, in past games like Colonial Marines and Aliens vs Predator, weapons such as the smart gun and flamethrower were like special weapons where you had limited ammunition and had to discard when the ammo was gone, but in Fireteam Elite they are generic but still viable weapons that you can replenish and use throughout the entirety of a mission, just like a shotgun or pulse rifle, which I like. Enemy AI doesn't seem that smart, but some xenos here and there can get a good flank on you, and even the lowliest enemies still deal alright damage to you even on normal difficulty. The marine character customization isn't that fleshed out or all that great, but it's still alright for what the game is and you can have some decent looking marines: definitely more customization than in Aliens vs Predator, and from what I think, more expansive than Colonial Marines. The sound design is pretty good for the most part, with a notable exception of weapons sounding weaker than how they should, but the music and various ambient noises of the environment and from your tracker and other sources is nice to listen to. At the moment there is no drop-in drop-out co-op, and no crossplay to those who are interested, but possibly might be introduced in the future? Although I like the ability that you can play with friends, I do wish it was at least 4 player co-op, three for a game like this seems kinda weird and disappointing if you have more than 1 or 2 people you play with. Speaking of co-op, seeing a PvP element to this game could be awesome, especially if you were able to play as the xenos with a few different variants like the ones you fight in the story or survival modes. If not that, then maybe synths vs marines, where both teams could fight eachother and AI xenos with their own custom arsenals/equipment of their choice? I don't really know how it would be done exactly, but its just a thought.My final thoughts: The game isn't perfect, but I think the game can be fun, and I'll continue to play it and recommend it. Don't know how I feel about the price at the moment though. While $40 is more reasonable than $60, I personally think that the current level of content and how things are isn't worth the $40. I already bought the game and played past 2 hours, and I love Alien related stuff anyways, so I don't mind it too much at the same time. There's no in game voice or text chat that I've seen yet, so if you play with friends then you might wanna use Discord, or Skype, or a telegraph to relay information other than with the ping system. If you're not sure if you'd like it, I'd say look up more information about how it plays, get a good look at the equipment, enemies, and customization if you want, and if you're feeling it, take a dive and try it out!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a weird game to recommend. On one hand, it has issues that limit its replay-ability and is very flawed, on the other hand it's still a solid experience to have with friends, and is probably the best Aliens game we've gotten in a long time. The classes feel pretty good (except Doc), shooting xenos is really fun, the iconic weapons are solid and aren't oversahdowed by the new ones (which are also mostly good), and the sound design is perfect. The customization is decent, allowing you to change your armor, headgear, weapon paint, as well as the decal on your weapon. Though, it would be nice if you could apply multiple decals at once, as well as being able to put decals on armor. Makes no sense that you can't.All that being said, though, it's a very flawed experience. First and foremost, the mission structure is repetitive. Most missions are generally going from one room to another, and activating a button that summons a horde. While fighting these hordes is fun and engaging, there isn't much to shake up the mission structure. You are essentially doing horde mode in various locations, with the occasional new enemy type to fight off. These encounters are largely scripted as well, meaning each playthrough is basically going to be the same. I think what they should have done is made it possible for tougher enemies to randomly spawn in any situation, so you're always on your toes, and then also allow more downtime between crescendo events.The difficulty scaling is also bizarre. While standard is pretty easy if you know what you're doing (you will rarely be at risk of failing), Intense also feels a bit much at times. The main reason for this is health scaling. On top of making the xenos deadlier, enabling friendly fire, lowering your ammo count, downs, and revive timer; the xenos also have more health. While the standard fodder xenos feel fine, the specials feel a bit too overbearing, specifically the spitter and burster. The spitter shoots acid at you from afar, and the burster rushes you down like a runner, but explodes in pool of acid that stuns you. For whatever reason, these specials are incredibly hard to kill on intense, making the literal hordes of bursters they throw at you feel like a chore to kill. Spitters have the same problem. You'd hope that maintaining fire on them would at least keep them from spitting, but that's not really the case. There's a stumble chance on weapons, but even weapons with high stumble don't seem to do a great job of suppressing them. I'm fine with everything else intense does, it makes it harder and more fun, but the larger health values on those specials is way too dramatic, and it gets worth with even higher difficulties, which I honestly think are just a joke.Then there's the synths, and I'm talking about both your AI buddies and the enemies. Your AI buddies are fine on standard, but worthless on intense. While the game does warn you about that, it's annoying that Left 4 Dead and Vermintide show that AI don't have to be bad, but today it's treated like forbidden magic. They need to be improved. As far as the synth enemies go, they're also way too tanky on intense. While dealing with synths mixed in with xenos is actually really fun (they even fight each other and it reminds of fighting flood and covenant in Halo), there's sections solely dedicated to fighting synths, and it feels like a chore to go through, especially on intense.There's also weird gameplay jank here and there. For example, reloading feels awful. It has that annoying system where you have to watch the entire animation each time you reload, so if you cancel it before they fully pull back the slide or charging handle, you have to do the entire reload all over again. This gets frustrating when being attacked by xenos, as dodge rolling cancels your reload, so if you have a particularly dangerous enemy on your tail, you're never reloading fully unless you risk taking damage. They need to make it where dodge rolling doesn't cancel reloading, much like how you can dodge roll and switch weapons.That sounds like it's a miserable experience, but it's not. It's a solid game, I like it a lot, but keep in mind you will probably only love it if you're an aliens fan, and will probably be the only reason to keep playing it past the first playthrough. As long as you know what you're getting into, it's a good game, but you really have to go in with modest expectations.

_childDocuments_.review: If you've read any 2 reviews of this game you know what you're gonna get. It's straightforward, it's familiar & even though it doesn't exactly break the mold anywhere, that doesn't stop it from being just a thoroughly enjoyable ride from start to finish whether you play on your own with bots or with friends.Relatively short story campaign (about maybe 10 hours give or take) is offset by tons of unlockable cosmetics, weapons & weapon parts that you pick up throughout, adding to the replayability. Two additional unlockable difficulties for added challenge, plus the ability to add Challenge Card to add to or take away from that difficulty. Finally, my personal favorite, character customization. Make your own marine (which you can freely edit again at any time outside of missions). Find a plethora of cosmetic items from outfits, to hats to aviators. Level up all your favorite classes earning perks along the way that change up and improve your class abilities.  Add to that the ability to fully customize your weapons as well; paint jobs, decals & attachments all. I strongly recommend you don't just pass on this as just another Left 4 Dead clone. The game has a lot more to offer you whether or not you're even familiar with the Alien series. It may not exactly be the innovative game of its decade, but it doesn't have to be for you to still have fun.

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly think this game is greatly underrated.  It's very addictive and fun.   Difficultly levels allow for a casual shooter all the way to a strategic and planned operation to have a chance of success.  Lots of character classes to choose from and the ability to create your own builds to customize your game play.  Well balanced weapons and classes mean a lot of options are viable.  The only real complaint for this game is it can be buggy, but it does appear the developer listens to the player base and patches / fixes are released with regularity.   If you miss Mass Effect 3 online I've found this to be a great replacement!

_childDocuments_.review: Sure it has a few bugs and gameplay is a little on the shallow side, but this is a GREAT game if you are a fan of the Alien franchise. Tons of lore and fan service to be found, even references to other games and tabletop.Forget using AI teammates unless you are on the easiest difficulty. Playing with friends with voice chat is the way to go.Pros:* Great setting, lots of lore. True to source.* You can use smart gun as a MAIN weapon, right from the start!* Fun with friends.* Progression system is decent. Better than Back 4 Blood at least.* Each class is distinct and fun in their own way. Suits various playstyles.Cons:* A few bugs here and there (and not the kind you can just shoot)* Gameplay loop is a bit repetitive: Run down corridors, get ambushed, hold your ground, try not to run out of ammo until the next refill, fight a big swarm at the end.* "Special" aliens aren't very engaging. Just various kinds of bullet sponges.* AI teammates are pretty garbage. They literally track mobs through walls and just shoot even without line of sight.* No text chat? Seriously??Overall: Recommended if you are a fan of the series and have friends to play with. Otherwise skip until there's a decent sale.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun game with a short play time that can be easily divided up into segments. The shooting is solid, and the classes each feel unique. _childDocuments_.review: If you are coming to this game to play a co-op game vs hoards of enemies, you are probably better going to the masters of the genre mentioned at the end of the gameplay section. _childDocuments_.review: I started playing "Fireteam Elite" only with the greatest of trepidation. Games in the Aliens license are an extremely mixed bag, and after the extremely good "Aliens: Isolation", the franchise felt due for a stinker. In this, at least, I was disappointed.Unusually, I started this game by jumping right into multiplayer. Or perhaps not so unusually; it is, after all, a co-op shooter. But the game does have offline play (with bots), and my normal method is to first play the game solo. But circumstances made it so I had a fireteam of colleagues at hand, and so we all experienced the game fresh. I don't think, though, that had I played the game solo first that it would have greatly affected my impressions of the game.In terms of production values, "Fireteam" is more than satisfying. It recreates the dark, chonky space-tech of the first two movies and - while it's not quite as good as "Alien: Isolation"- it captures the feel of the franchise quite well. The audio is above average too; there's nothing really exceptional about it - although the music score is divisive amongst fans, I rather liked it - but it doesn't do anything wrong either.But the gameplay? It's... ehn. Mechanically, it's okay; the gunplay is good enough, and the various classes add some nice variety to the game. I preferred the Lancer, just because the SmartGun's auto-targeting let me lazily point-n-spray my bullets vaguely in the direction of the monsters and still get a reasonable number of kills (other classes require a bit more skill). But outside the combat, I felt the game was lacking.The pacing was off, for one. The aliens are a constant threat, which, okay, it's a co-op shooter so sure. But there's no downtime in the game, and the constant pressure can be exhausting. After two or three matches, I was ready to call it quits for the day. The gameplay actively discouraged me from wanting to play it! The missions themselves lacked variety and spectacle; as good looking and true-to-the-movies as the maps may have been, there's only so much darkened spaceship and shadowy alien hives I can take before I started getting bored. The mission mechanics are all the same too: go to open arena, push button, fight off a couple waves of enemies, repeat. But beyond that, there's just the grind. There's a huge number of weapons and cosmetics you can unlock (none of which require micro transactions, fortunately) but there's little real advantage to picking one over the other, and getting them all would require me replay the small handful of levels more times than the cosmetics were worth. I certainly had no desire to go through the games the ten or twelve times it would take to max out each class.  I'm sure some people find that sort of thing fun, but I was getting bored with the game before I finished my first run through its campaign.In the end, "Aliens: Fireteam Elite" was an okay game, but it lacked the depth to keep me invested in it for more than a few hours. The biggest fans of the franchise will probably love the game to death, but if all you want is a co-op game, there are better titles that will occupy you for a much longer time than this one. Sure, if you love "Aliens", get the game on sale. Otherwise, it's really hard to recommend it over anything else when the competition is so strong.

_childDocuments_.review: When I bought this game, I was expecting a fairly mindless shooter, one that I would get a few hours of enjoyment out of and then quickly grow bored of. Sure, it has the frantic pace you'd expect, and the near-nonstop onslaught of xenomorphs, but there's also a depth and skill level here that isn't immediately apparent. _childDocuments_.review: Probably the best co-op horde shooter I've played since the original Killing Floor, and this game absolutely wipes its ass with Back4Blood as far as releases this year go. Every class manages to feel unique and fun to play, although you'll probably quickly gravitate to a main class and only play the others for daily tasks. Needs more levels for sustained replayability, as there's very little motivation to replay the campaign once you beat it except to collect more weapons, which have an unreasonably low drop rate anyway, and has extremely limited in-game chat or communication outside of emotes, so you'll need an outside VOIP program like mumble or discord for serious play. Still, if you've got a weekend to spare and a couple friends willing to play with you, this is one of the better ways to spend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a simple man – I love the Alien series and I love horde shooters. Here we have a game that is exactly that - so yeah, I had to check it out.Unlike the last couple Alien games we got – both in first person – Fireteam Elite plays as a third-person shooter. The best comparison I can make is basically a combination of Gears of War and Left 4 Dead. You got the semi-clunky movement, but fun shooting of Gears and the horde-like gameplay style of Left 4 Dead.It has its hiccups, but at its core – the movement and shooting are solid. Dodging is responsive, the cover system actually works, and landing shots is never not satisfying. The headshot sound effect in particular definitely adds to this feeling – it really makes those shots feel rewarding especially when playing on a higher difficulty.I would highly recommend playing on the game’s “intense” difficulty right from the start as opposed to its default “standard” difficulty. I started with the latter, but was breezing through the game with two of my friends and it didn’t really have that sense of urgency you would expect from an Alien game. Bumping it up to intense and now ammo is way more of a concern, the big alien types actually feel challenging, and setting up turrets, mines, and other traps in preparation for the next fight are way more rewarding. It’s just an overall better experience and I wish I had started on that difficulty from the start.Also worth noting is that there exists a “challenge” system similar to the skulls from a Halo game. Whether that be having an alien constantly on the hunt for you, having only half of your maximum ammo, or just straight failing the mission if you take damage – some of them are pretty extreme, but the rewards do make them worth a shot.The game has some light RPG mechanics that have you leveling weapons and classes and the challenge cards allow you to earn more XP and currency every time you activate one. The RPG mechanics here are where the game gets its depth and variety from. You get a handful of different classes – each with their own specialization and abilities. The doc, for example, has a really nice AOE healing field, whereas the demolisher (my personal favorite) has shoulder-mounted missiles similar to Predator.Your weapon type also depends on what class you pick, but you can freely swap between them between missions and the game even encourages this because it is constantly giving you loot for all of the classes – regardless of which one you are playing. There’s a good amount of experimentation here and the variety offered by all of the different weapons, abilities, perks, and other upgrades are really what carry the experience here.Despite carrying the Aliens title and obviously borrowing a lot from the movies – this is not really a game you should go into expecting any sort of “good” story. It’s not bad, but just kinda “there” – like this optional thing added on just to link the different levels together. For example, while there is dialogue and full voice acting – NPCs lack facial animation, so you’re just hearing their words while looking at them. The Aliens theme obviously went more towards the setting and enemies, rather than storytelling – which I wouldn’t even consider to be a bad thing. It’s nice to just drop into a lobby with some friends and get to shooting some xenos.Graphically, the game looks just okay. Despite being released on PS5 and Xbox Series X, it is still a game you can tell was developed for the generation prior. Not to say that it looks bad – rather just basic. There’s also not much to say about the music. It’s not that memorable and honestly, it felt a bit too “cheerful” for how dark the setting was – I would be in a big firefight while some upbeat cantina theme is playing.I had to put down a few settings to get the game to run at 1440p on my 1070 Ti, but once I did it was smooth sailing fps-wise, hovering around 60-80 for most of it and rarely dipping below that. Still, I did run into the occasional model freaking out, frame stuttering when loading back into the hub world, and a grand total of one crash. I won’t say it’s the most polished game, but the technical issues I did run into were relatively minor and hopefully something a patch or two can clean up.Aliens: Fireteam Elite may be a bit clunky, but the core combat is some good stuff and the RPG mechanics on top of it give it a nice sense of depth. Fun and unique classes, cool enemy designs inspired by the movie, challenging levels – it’s a nice all-around horde shooter even if the story and graphics may be lacking. It’s not really a game I would recommend for solo players (at least, definitely not at full price), but I had a good time playing through it with a couple of friends and would recommend it if you have some to play through it with as well.Follow my  for more reviews + videos!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun game to play with some friends. The co-op campaign is diverse and there are plenty of weapons and other unlocks to work toward. However, after you beat the game once or twice, the replay value dwindles. This is a game that feels finished but lacking, almost like the creators had a lot more planned but had a limited timeframe to finish it in. Instead of releasing an unfinished mess, they released a finished, playable, and fun product but a product that makes you want more levels, more customization, and more stuff to do to keep you coming back.Consider Fireteam Elite if it's on sale and you want a game to co-op together with some friends, then expect to shelf it until a new map is released or content is released. As far as playing with pubs or bots... Q: "Did IQs just drop sharply while I was away?"A: "Yes"

_childDocuments_.review: PROS-Variety of Weapons-Some Character Customization (Clothes and Character)-Great Sound Design-Great Character/Xeno Design-Different Classes to play with-Challenge Cards that add a Challenge to a regular mission (Weapons sometimes jam) which gives you more XP/Better Rewards if beaten-Decent weapon customization-somewhat decent enemy variety with lots of Xeno types and some Synth types(was hoping for a predator but its not called AVP)CONS-Little replay Value unless you have friends or are doing challenges-only 2 modes (Campaign and Horde Mode)-Story was all over the place-forgettable characters (I dont remember any names since they dont show up at all during missions and only in the main lobby)-Radar ruins atmosphere since you know exactly where the aliens are coming from (Unless you see a bunch coming in all at once it actually makes you terrified) -No first person (Was hoping for a first person option to raise the tension)-No VC or Chat which kinda ruins the whole PVE experience since you cant communicate with your team unless you use the Ping mechanicSUMMARYGreat Arcade shooter to play with friends, don't expect a full story with fleshed out characters. This game is a simple third person Left For dead shooter with aliens and Robots. Would recommend buying this once its on sale unless you're a die hard Alien Fan.7/10Would definitely play again if DLC or more content is added. Especially a Predator enemy type or Predalien in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is **fun**. Very fun, actually. Depending on the direction of the updates, all it will probably take is a few content additions for me to flip this recommendation.UPDATE: THEY CHANGED THE PRICE SO I FLIPPED THE REVIEW!!!ORIGINAL: At its current pricepoint, I would  this game. If it were $10 cheaper? Hell yeah, go for it.Aliens: Fireteam Elite is a third-person horde shooter where a team of 3 (no less, empty player slots will be replaced with A.I.) go from room to room fighting off hordes of aliens. You'll get story bits through "intel," items that are hidden across each map. However, there is no indicator or stats screen that tells you how much intel you've collected or are missing.That is the gist of how far the gameplay goes. Four kits (classes) from the start, one unlockable: There is a "talent" tree that lets you customize the build of your chosen class. However, based on the way that that grid is designed, the only thing really unique about each class are their abilities. Most of the perks are interchangeable, and the only other difference is the availability of weapon types for each kit.There's a neat feature called "Challenge Cards" where you are given either a beneficial or detrimental effects for an entire mission. Detrimental effects usually come with an incentive, such as increased XP or money after completion.Trying to survive from room to room using the tools your chosen kit gives you  {subjectively} fun, and because of how the loot is designed on each map (hidden cache locations are randomized, not unique), replayability is 100% there.There are dailies, dubbed "Tactical Opportunities." A total of three opportunities are available at the start of each week: Two dailies and one weekly. If you've completed the weekly early on then you'll only get a nice little refresh of two opportunities per day.The campaign is fairly short. A friend and I knocked it out in maybe around 8-10 hours, and that's at a leisurely pace.As fun as it is going from map to map, grinding out these Xenomorphs and their variants--we'll get to variants in a bit--the game is lacking a lot in terms of .The map designs are very bland, there isn't much variety and by the time you make it to the final mission you'll realize and feel like most of these maps are reskins of one another.Aside from the regular Xenomorphs you're 360 no-scoping, you're presented with maybe around 4-5 "variants" and nothing more. By the time you've met , you've seen them all. There are no bosses to fight, just the same Xenomorphs on the same (but different!) maps.Aliens: Fireteam Elite is  fun. But it's not worth $39.99. Wait for a sale, or wait for the game to (hopefully) go in a positive development direction. Depending on the updates, maybe it'll be worth its current price.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, this is a fun little game. It's charming to play with friends and shout lines from aliens and 80s action films at each other. If you get it on sale I'll say that it's more than worth your time, short dlc included (also got on sale.).However, for it's full price point, it's a bit buggier than I'd expect. Some of the levels confuse the poor Xenos, leading them to get stuck on walls and such (funnily happens more often in alien hive areas because the walls are less flat). And honestly the game doesn't have much replay value or late game content. This is the thing that almost made me not recommend this game. The endless mode is kind of a joke, only using a third of the game's enemies, and going back to replay the campaign on higher difficulties quickly gets repetitive because there's no AI director or any such system in place. Example. You're walking down a hallway and some xenos spawn out of a vent. Three of them, one after another. If you replay the mission, those three xenos will spawn again, almost always in the exact same place. All health, ammo, and item pickups are always at the same locations, all horde fights happen at the same locations.It's fun the first time, with a couple of friends who are into it, and even replaying the missions on harder difficulties are nice for a bit. (Friendly fire adds a whole level of complexity and unlocks the hidden ability to stare reproachfully at your friends.) But unless you really, really fall in love with the content, you'll burn out fast.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played this on Xbox and bought it for the PC for modding. There's a lot of action but the scripting is kind of light. This is a game that really forces "da funny" by hammering a square peg into a round hole. During the intro, you get chastised for asking questions and everyone treats you like a dummy. The game play is fast and furious and you'll be managing your resources carefully. One of the best parts of the game is getting swarmed by a horde of aliens while you're standing next to an ammo container so you can just rock and roll to your heart's content then reload and repeat. I'm not into multiplayer so I'm more of a game tourist ... I like to walk around and look at the eye candy and take the story in while others want to run and gun and see how quick they can compete a level. There's a real feel here that every marine hates every other marine, there's no feeling of cohesiveness, all of that is lost in the whacking of the square peg to get "da funny" across, which fails miserably. I've gotten to the second chapter on the planet and just kind of ... quit ... on Xbox because I kept getting my ass kicked by some stupid OP combat androids. Hopefully, with the mods I've installed, I can finally get on with my tour of this Alien story and have some fun. At 53yo, I hate games where I run into some level and I play it 30 times and still can't get past it. I usually just hand it off to my 16yo daughter and ask her to finish it for me.Her: "But ... you grew up with Atari and NES! You're old school!"Me: "Yes, but this level is designed for someone who is 8 years old, who freebases Ritalin and who shotguns Red Bull. I can't do that because my heart would blow out of my chest like I'd Frenchkissed a facehugger the night before."Overall, so far, PC version, it's a smurfy game. There are very few well written Alien games and this is not one of them because it tries to take everything Alien and be everything Alien and it ends up being a mixed up bag of xenomorphic slaughter which is fun but it's not Masterpiece Theater by any stretch of the imagination. Fun? Yes!Intelligent? Meh.Game physics? Problems.Buy it? Yes, if you like Alien games ... and you have some Ritalin and Red Bull handy and a 10 year old who can get you through some of the insane levels so you can get back to being a war tourist and strolling through the eye candy.

_childDocuments_.review: After about 20 hours played, here's my review.PROS:- Good graphics- No Bugs- Interesting narrative campaign- Decent gun play (guns feel like they pack a punch)- Decent level design/environmental diversity (But like most of these games, hallway > open area > hallway, repeat.)- Innovative skill tree design- Innovative consumables systemCons:-Loot diversity is basically non-existent. I have maxxed my Technician and I am still using the starting Magnum and Shotgun because everything you unlock is worse. There are clearly some attachments that are meta and you just end up using those. - No crafting, no loot upgrade/ progression, etc.- No ranking/leader board for horde, no PvP, no "reason" to keep grinding horde mode outside of getting all the cosmetics.So there's a decent 10-15 hour narrative PvE experience here. If you play on Insane with a team of friends, I'm sure you can sink 40+ hours into it. I'm just not sure why you would at this point. I have maxxed the Technician, and there doesn't seem to be a reason outside of getting some new weapon attachments and being able to min/max the skill tree. I am still using the starting weapons at max level as everything else you can unlock feels considerably worse. The pump action shotgun > all others imo. The magnum pistol > all others imo. The real weak point of this game is the loot. They need a new loot system that either involves finding salvage and using the cannon "fabricators" to build loot with random rolls/rarities, etc. But right now I have a loadout set and I don't see any likelihood of changing that loadout and I'm only on my second day of playing. Seems really thin on content. Overall, good bones, high potential if they figure out an "end-game" or something to keep you coming back. As of now, there really isn't as far as I can see.

_childDocuments_.review: amazing game, great horde shooter, dont listen to the nay sayers about comms, ive almost done every campaign on INSANE (hardest difficulty) without communications. there is a ping system everyone uses and you just need above averge IQ to make   it work. in higher levels the players you match with are versed in the good holdout spots and will guide you so dont fret! just get in and blast some xenos!

_childDocuments_.review: Long review for those who like to know what they are getting into. A TL: DR is at the endIf you can get two friends together for some old-school slay-em all with lots of explosions against an onslaught of Xenomorphs, then this is the game for you. You can also play with random people on the internet, but that is a mixed bag. Can go ether direction from very pleasant to never again. Soloplay is also viable, but the NPC Androids will be only useful on the lower difficulties, as you want some actual thoughts in your teammates (or not, you do you - could actually work better than some random internet people).First the technical aspect of the game:It runs very smooth even in high intensity firefights with lots of different particle effects appearing. I have set the settings for the maximum in Graphics and had no stutter or glitched out textures in the game as of yet (complete campaign playthrough). No frame drops in the entire game and the multiplayer seems very stable. I played the game with my two brothers and we only had one drop once in 13 hours and around 15 to 17 maps. The menu is very clean and the audio is VERY close to the atmosphere from the franchise. From the sound of the guns to the atmospheric music, the alien sounds, the bursting steam vents and the concerning ping of the motion-detector, everything fits very well together. If you are a fan of the Aliens Universe as I have been my entire life you will enjoy the composition of all these elements together. The controls are very intuitive and if you`d like to change them to fit your personal key setting, you can do that easily for all buttons i could think of using in the game. The balancing for the difficulty is also well done. On the lower difficulties the game has some nice little features you can make use of like no friendly fire or outlining the black Xenomorphs against the sometimes quite dark backgrounds. But it doesn`t feel like you can walk through an endless horde with the trigger pulled and a smile on your face. Even on lower difficulty the enemies can take a hit and are keen to return the favor.It is very easy to find a class with a suitable play style or gear set in the present classes. At the moment there are 4 basic classes and a fifth one after completing the game once.Now too the game itself:Without spoiling the story of the game i can say it fits well into the established canon of the aliens universe. It plays after all the movies and in an to this date unknown location story-wise. In short you are colonial marines on border patrol who got a distress call and went to investigate. Your Fireteam will then be sent to different locations in different campaigns to fulfill a series of key objectives stretched over a mission arc of three missions each.Classes:The Fireteam will be made of three players or a player / two players and a bot. The Bot/s are fixed and can not be changed in any way or form as far as i know (never tried bots as i am playing this with my brothers).The player classes are very well balanced and have each a viable place in a team. You can choose between a gunner (your bread and butter grunt), a smartgun wielding demoltion expert (laughs in heavy weapons fire), a doc (heroes never die?) and a tech with his trusty turret (santas little helper). A fifth class will be unlocked, as already mentioned after completing the story once. The recon is eyes, ears and in this case ammo dropping savior (i got nothing). On the higher difficulties he is pretty much essential as he is ammo, health and visibility in one.Weapons:You get two weapons slots for each class as well as an sidearms peashooter to tickle the Xenomorphs with (at least it got unlimited ammunition). The slots are fixed and limit the guns you can bring to the mission. The gunner got his standart rifle slot and a close-quarter option for those narrow passages for example. The demolisher has a rifle slot and a heavy slot for his smartgun or similarly nice toys like a heavy-duty flamethrower. Melee is generally a bad idea against an enemy who was made to rib you to confetti and wear the rest of you as a hat.Abilities and passives:Every class has a unique passive ability and to active ones for use in missions. The gunner for example gets stacks of 2% damage increase on hit up to a total of 20% as his passive, a grenade for clearing those hard to dislodge Xeno-Infestations and the Overclock for the team to squeeze some extra fire rate out of those badboy pulse armaments. The skills can be enhanced with class or universal mutators / modifiers in a system similar to the resident evil suitcase inventory, You unlock more space by advancing your class level and can interlink the abilities with the modifiers (they can be rotated too).Gun-kata:The trusty gun at your side will also get some out of the endless slaying you will pursue. Guns have four levels each and get some bonus stats each time the gain a level. You can fit three attachments on every gun with different benefits and those can be fitted on multiple guns at the same time.Cosmetics:The appearance of your characters is variable but not as extensive as in other games. On the plus side, you can change everything as much as you like, even after character creation. Want to play a mission as a though looking latino smartgunner, sure. Next mission you`d like to be the handsome blond daredevil gunner with his shotgun, easy. The guns also come in a lot of different color variations and can be fitted with decals for the personal touch. Skins and decals can be found in hidden caches in the level. Outfits for the characters are very sparse at the moment with only the dlc content and one other in game sold in the hub-shop.Maps and Cards:There is a wide range of different biomes where your bug hunting expertise will be put to the test. Without spoiling to much: You will go places kid. That`s what the marines promised you, didn`t they? You can play a challenge car anytime you start a mission (as long as you have any) to raise or lower the difficulties you will face in the missions. You should know that this may offer a better paycheck at the end of the mission or make you scrap your cash together to get that new shiny you want. No sidearms? That`s rough, here are some extra credits. Faulty detector, boy you are in for a treat! Flesh-packed human-sized, steroid-chugging Juggernauts, here is your teddy and a goldstar for my brave boy!Enemies:The Enemies can be split into three? groups: The "trash", the elites and the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ monsters.The "trash":Don`t be fooled the trash is still quite tough and if you can`t keep track of them ... they will get you.The elites:A wide variety of Xenomorphs will ruin your day or at least give it there best shot (think left for dead or Vermintide).The ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ monsters:The tougher big brothers / sisters? of the elites, if you don`t prioritize ending there life, the they will end yours ...On that note:On the higher difficulties the game seems to throw more elites and monsters at you. We actually found a variation of an elite that we hadn`t seen on the difficulty below at all.Story:The game has a very interesting story and you will be getting those Intel parts quickly (trust me). The NPCs in the hub feel real and diverse. There are a lot of references to the movies hidden in the game and anytime i found one it, it felt well placed and quite amusing.  Conclusion:In my Opinion a game that is well deserving of its price-tag (without all cosmetic dlc). They worked close to source material and atmosphere. The game they produced is well done and with little to nag on. A fun shooter in the Aliens Universe.TL; DR:A well done 3-person, third person team-based shooter. Campaigns: 4 with 3 missions each, at round-about 25 min - 40 min a mission. Variety in Classes and Styling-options are plenty. A game for casual solo playing people or the gritty, pay for inches in blood type, grind masochists.

_childDocuments_.review: Aliens: Fireteam Elite does everything right in my book, and by everything, I mean the gameplay. Here are a few examples:1. The floor is acid! - Xeno blood is acid, and acid hurts, so Cold Iron had the great idea of spawning temporary pools of acid under every Xeno corpse when they die, which brings an additional layer of spatial awareness to the game. Kill an enemy, get around the spot where it died to not take damage. If you're thinking right now ''But what about when you kill one in an hallway?'' here's example number two!2. Dark Souls, but it's Aliens! - Ok, I'm kidding. But, Cold Iron did take a little idea from the Souls series and used it quite effectively; the rolling. Rolling in DS makes you invincible for a frame or two, and the same is applicable in A:FE. So not only is it possible for the player to dodge an attack in a game where most enemies have claws and jaws, but it also gives them the opportunity to skip the damage given by a pool of acid by rolling over it. This makes the roll a core mechanic of the gameplay if one wants to navigate the battlefield with ease, and I absolutely love it. More movement in games is always good in my book, especially when developers demand it from their players.3. Mo' guns, mo' attachments - There aren't gazillions of guns, and each can only have 3 attachments on it. But. But...Builds. Whether you're playing as a Gunner, a Demolisher, a Doc or a Technician (I skipped two btw), you will unlock certain skills which encourage some different builds, meaning that in one mission you might be a close-quarter, high-spread-shotgun-toting Tech with a flamethrowing turret, and in another you might be a precision-specialised Grunt with a sniping double-barrel railgun. The attachments make this all the better, with various and vital stats that actually change the way you use your weapon, not just make it better.4. Variety is the spice of death - At first, the game feels short, and there seems to be very few levels, but that's until you realise that there is actually much more variety in the nine acts of A:FE than there is in all 27 World War Z Aftermath maps (A game I also love, but it didn't necessarily do great in that aspect). Each level introduces a new enemy or boss (With each Chapter introducing a new ''species'' or ''group'' of enemies), the level design is always fresh, which makes both the defending sections and the tense walks between objectives more engaging, and the randomly but seemingly calculated enemy and loot crate spawns add an incentive to look in every nook and cranny carefully, expecting the worse every time.5. Riley's no damsel in distress - Do you remember the times your head became a permanent anime pillow in L4D2 because of a Jockey? Pepperidge Farms remembers, and it sucked. The only thing you could do was spam the WASD keys in hope that you would somehow break the algorithm and free yourself. Of course, you could use the bash to parry, but if you failed, you had to wait for your friends to save your ass. Well the guys who've made A:FE thought that sucked too, so they used one of the worst mechanic ever created and brought it back to life by actually giving it an important role: once grabbed by a special enemy, a quick time event will pop in your window, and once you finish it, you're free! It's not an easy way out, though; the QTE can take a while so you definitely want your friends to shoot the enemy before it messes you up too much. BUT, if you're either playing with AI teammates, or simply dumb or high friends, this mechanic will save you a lot of frustration.6. Ok this one isn't about gameplay - That game FEELS like Cameron's 1986 masterpiece. The tense atmosphere, the color-shading, the design of the grunts, the rock n'roll attitude, the vulgar Spanish one-liners, the sounds, the fake jump scares, the music, everything feels purely ''Aliens''. Those guys sincerely loved the IP they worked on and it absolutely shows.So there it is. Great developers I'd never heard of kinda...finally innovated upon the L4D2 recipe, after 12 years. Definitely killed Back 4 Blood for me. And I do believe horde coop shooters are in good hands now if Cold Iron keeps up the good work and the people give them the praise and the money they undoubtedly deserve. I sincerely recommend the game, especially with a friend or two.

_childDocuments_.review: Pro's -Total left 4 dead vibe.. plus all the intensity you'd expect if you were thrust into the cast of an Aliens franchise.-Gameplay has a Gears of War vibe, is responsive an a target rich environment while managing ammo conservation will have you clenching at times to stay on your toes an protect your teammates while they're doing the same. Threats are superbly done with the movements being hard to pin down at times and can often mislead you to think you've capped a threat when they're simply staggered for a moment. - The sound ambience, combat an threats are superbly done. The music is perfect an the visual atmosphere can feel a touch claustrophobic in more than a few situations.- An absolute blast with friends or competent randoms.The Cons - missing in game VOIP and no chat input function. These two features missing are HUGE, mainly in terms of allowing players to communicate early on. Even having just a simple chat function would be a big help here, as it would allow players to simply offer up a 3rd party solution for VOIP with ease.- Limited missions. As each of the campaigns only offer up 3 missions per arc, an the final I believe has 4. So there's currently 10 missions? The layouts of the mission maps themselves are relatively static, with hidden caches being moved around and the swarm triggers being a little random. This game could benefit more if the mission maps were less linear, an or procedurally generated.- No animated lip sync of voice overs during NPC interactions. A bit of a let down for those expecting an animated voice over. I mean it is 2021 an has sort of become a standard in current gaming, but for old school gamers it shouldn't matter to much.-Minor graphical glitches in swarm sequences can occasionally render threats glitching with terrain, usually brief and clears up, but can sometimes end up with a bad result as the threat can't be hit during that glitch window.End result. I enjoyed it, an Yes it's far better than an earlier title Aliens Colonial Marines.Worth the full price? If your a fanboy of the franchise an want to give back in full to the devs to generate the incentive to push out more content.As it is. It still needs more content for consideration at the current price point, especially so with the lack of VOIP or chat. Otherwise I'd say it's a fair buy on a 20-25% off sale. Just my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: Shallow and practically empty.The SEARCHING FOR FIRETEAM screen has a short music loop which tries to convey tension, but you have to wait so long to get a teammate that it gets annoyingly repetitive. I went over the 2 hour refund window while waiting the best part of an hour (during peak time) to find a teammate, and when a teammate finally arrived (and the game gave us a bot to fill the 3rd slot) the game then crashed on loading. I wish I had stopped and got a refund. Having passed the 2 hour mark, I tried to get some sense of value for money by waiting for teammates and attempting to complete the game, but it was mostly just waiting, or getting stuck due to artificial difficulty. It's possible to start a mission with bots by making a private lobby, but this isn't obvious, the bots are pretty useless, and players won't be able to drop in.For the little time I had a teammate, there was little to no teamwork involved. I didn't hear any mic chat, and couldn't find a button for text chat. The scale of the game feels limited with only two teammates. The weapons don't feel like they suit any particular role, range, or circumstance. The pulse rifle fire rate feels wrong, and has no grenade launcher. Weapon switch and reload animations, and sounds are poor. The game didn't need hitmarkers; there's a big red X that appears when you kill an Alien, was it worth throwing away immersion for that? Many maps feel boringly modular. Bizarrely your hitpoints are counted at 1,500 which didn't give me a sense of vulnerability like having it counted by 100 would.Sometimes there's a bunch of mines in your path, which adds nothing to the gameplay. It's just tedious switching to your pistol that has unlimited ammo to shoot all the mines. A lot of the game feels like that - stuff being added even if it doesn't contribute positively to gameplay. Some enemies are bullet sponges, which doesn't make the gameplay feel skill-based, and isn't fun considering the lack of ammunition. The difficulty ramps up ridiculously as you get swarmed by bullet sponge enemies that deal high damage (and some have ranged attacks, but there's no button to crouch, so taking cover is janky). To beat the bullet sponges you would have to grind earlier missions to make your character slightly more powerful (or wait ages hoping to get a powerful teammate).There's kit perks, core perks, modifiers, , abilities, cards, attachments, intel, rep, requisition, weapon upgrade traits,  (fear of missing out?) Ontop of XP, ranks, and consumables. There's popups for challenge cards as soon as you launch the game, and some perks can be rotated to fit into a confusing inventory system that increases , different from the primary inventory menu. Did it all have to be this complicated, as opposed to polishing core gameplay?The higher FPS options are either 120 or unlocked, which wastes electricity when you consider it has a 3D menu, and you wait so long to get matched with teammates. For some reason there's also a 2D menu (reached from ESC), and weirdly it all moves as you move the cursor. The cosmetics for changing outfits didn't show a preview of the character on my client, and they look ridiculous. One player looked like they were wearing Valentines Day gift wrapping rather than camouflage. The water droplets and fires are low framerate effects, and many effects flicker. There's no ripple effect when shooting water. The game suffers microstutters. There's no ambient motion tracker ping, and the tracker fails to pick up a lot of motion. The voicelines are poor. There's a damage increase HUD element that comes up and felt pointless. Private matches can't be paused.The theme of flame and explosive weapons in the wider lore were chaotic ones that were deployed as a desperate last resort. Here they're thrown straight into combat. A character claims that humans never encountered a tool-using civilization. Did the devs not even watch the Aliens movie? They mention a species called the Arcturians, and encounter a massive alien ship at the start. What I assume was supposed to be a plot twist doesn't even feel like a spoiler because  when Between missions you're supposed to listen to NPCs waffle on, meanwhile I'm worried that my teammates are waiting for me to join the next mission. Couldn't the devs have layered the story into the gameplay like in AVP2? The characters are edgy and forgettable with no range of personality. There's no sense of camaraderie between the enlisted, and officers have no command presence. One officer that spends the entire game just standing in one spot shouts at you  There's no humour in the voiceline, so it doesn't come across with any hint of sarcasm. In the film the leaders were more 3-dimensional, either inexperienced but authoritative, or bossy but still had a hint of charisma.The story butchers Aliens was largely about the Aliens - the development here should have looked for creative ways to show their ruthlessness and the intelligence of these emotionless creatures to contrast the moral flaws in society. Yet the aliens are left so stupid in this game that they can literally get stuck while trying to move towards you. They don't work together, they just get spammed, but the ship crew complements are so low in the lore that it doesn't make sense to be killing thousands of Aliens. Where are they all coming from? I didn't see anything that justified the scale of their numbers. The development should have added quality to the encounters with them, then they wouldn't even need to spam them. The Aliens in AVP (1999) were more tangible and had weight to them - when you shot them they'd lose limbs and menacingly still crawl and swiped at you, and bled far more dangerous acid in concentrations, not just splashed like momentary stains.This feels like a cash-grab, where the only effort was put into graphics to make it look good in a trailer to get pre-orders (made obvious by the pre-order bonus system). You can't just jam some NPCs into a series of corridors and call it a sci-fi story. AVP (1999) had a lot of this nonsense beat 22 years earlier. It sounded better, had better Aliens, had NPC mouth movement, and GameSpy enabled you to see every lobby so you could immediately jump into a multiplayer match. As much as I liked Aliens and drew my nickname from it, I didn't find the gameplay enjoyable in this instalment to even want to complete it. The difficulty ramps up to the point where you'd need to grind previous missions to upgrade a character to survive later missions. I'd rather watch a film.There's so little teamwork involved that I wouldn't recommend it to my friends, which is ironic because it's a Left 4 Dead clone that should have been all about trying to flesh out satisfying teamwork. This game is not worth £34.99, and the pricetag only acts as a paywall to the players it needs as teammates. Unimaginative cash-grabs like this are the reason that Aliens games never got anywhere near as popular as Halo. There was no effort in places where it mattered. I can only imagine a sense of value for money if it was heavily discounted, but honestly you could just skip this one.

_childDocuments_.review: A solid, if somewhat simple, co-op shooter.It lacks any in-game voice, which is a mixed blessing whether playing with friends or internet randos, and the lack of voice comms means coordinating efforts can be tough.The difference in challenge and fun between difficultly levels is significant -- get to "INTENSE" as soon as you can, as that is where the game shines.It can be a bit grindy, between leveling classes and weapons. The classes themselves offer good variety, with none that seem overpowered and only a few that seem marginally useful. The skills system allows for substantial customization and complexity and is cleverly implemented. The guns themselves are also quite varied, allowing nearly each weapon type to cover a full spectrum from pistol to shotgun to rifle to sniper. All are reasonably balanced, with some notable areas -- heavy weapons seem ineffective and not worth it for higher difficulty levels, and the flamethrowers are good ways to both obscure your own vision and kill your teammates. The weapon attachment system is strong, and so is the customization. The game would have greatly benefited from more unpredictability -- random layouts, more random wave spawns, etc -- and perhaps fewer, more focused guns. The color palette is also fairly uniform, which is on-brand for the universe, but gets a little monotonous after repeated plays.Easily worth the purchase price, particularly if you have a few friends you can get on board.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a solid co-op game that has so many features I've wanted to see in other games where you find yourself fighting hordes of alien bugs and robots (you know which one I'm talking about in particular). The class system is solid, with a surprising amount of depth in the builds as you unlock more equipment and spaces for the interesting inventory-management-style perk trees, the weapons are highly diverse and have decent customization, the abilities are fun and punchy for the most part, the gunplay feels quite solid, the cover system isn't bad but doesn't force you to use it, the difficulty levels are well-balanced and easy to understand, and there are plenty of enemy types.I wish there were more players like there used to be, but hopefully a positive review will go towards extending the game's lifespan. It's fun, the co-op is good, and it's easy to quickly get into and make progress in. Highly recommend if you have friends to play with.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be honest. The Aliens property has always been a slightly messy thing to handle. I know the Xenomorphs have gotten their fair share of love with the AVP games but outside of those we never had a proper take on "Aliens". Yes we had Colonial Marines and at the time of writing this review I still haven't played it but to say the least the criticism that game drew may be enough to keep me away. And yes we got the spectacular Alien: Isolation but that's more "Alien" than "Aliens" as in it's more atmospheric horror.  But Fireteam Elite is a perfect example of a property getting some well deserved love because this game is not only a very competent hoard shooter with excellent mechanics but it's a MASSIVE love letter to the fans. It pays homage to everything related to Aliens and I mean EVERYTHING going as far as giving some love to Prometheus. Cold Iron Studios outdid themselves and I look forward to whatever else they bring from the Aliens license.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, the atmosphere is amazing feels like you're actually in the alien universe and the sounds are really pleasing but be warned the game gets very loud, I had to turn it down a few times as I couldn't hear my friend speak. Now I don't know about the matchmaking issues due to me only playing with a friend but I'd recommend the game if you have friends to play with or you enjoy playing this type of game by yourself as the AI teammates are actually pretty decent, they're not amazing but they're reliable in my experience.We've started going through it on a harder difficulty which has made it very interesting as some of the special aliens are now a real challenge to fight like the Warrior or Praetorian.The game has the main campaign and once you beat that it unlocks another two modes which are Horde mode and Point Defence.Horde mode you defend a point from Aliens but each wave adds more aliens and more special ones like Warriors, every ten waves the game gives you a bunch of stuff and asks if you wanna continue or leave. (I'd recommend preparing with consumables before hand as it gets hard fast, wave 4 sent a Praetorian after us which are the hardest aside from the Queen)Point Defence I haven't played yet but you have to defend some engineers from the Aliens and there's three points you defendThe Campaign overall is pretty fun but repeats itself at certain points but there's around 4 Episodes each has 3 chapters in them, there's around 5 difficulties which add things like less damage or increased health for the aliens, what was nice to see is different alien types I've only seen in other games or comics like the Spitters so that adds a nice mix, there are other things in this game I've only seen in the movies but I ain't gonna spoil that.There's also a few classes to choose from I think there's around 6 classes but you unlock 1 or 2 when you beat the game first time, all have different weapons they use but some also share weapons like the Pulse Rifle or Shotgun, each class has abilities too, they have two main ones and a passive one, there's perks too for each class that either alter or improve your abilities as well as a levelling system for each class and your own rankJust lemme know if there's anything you wanna know that I haven't mentioned or want something explaining better.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the few games these days that actually has some quality and purpose put into it, thoroughly reminds me of an early 2010's game (in a good way) that has direction and is finished on launch.The gameplay is a mix of Gears of War and Alien Swarm, which doesn't sound fun but totally is. It has a max (at the time of writing this) of 3-player co-op, but I'd be surprised if they didn't change that someday somehow.There is a large amount of variety in weapons, abilities, cosmetics and upgrades, so it never feels like you're just playing without progress.This game follows my rule of the "Hidden-Gem" theory I came up with, which is that games that receive little to no hype and have very poor advertising, usually come out to be some of the best games- while those that receive a lot of it, usually are banking on people riding a bandwagon and advertising to make money, and not the actual game. If you want a fun horde shooter that is challenging, well-made and has a ALIENS theme to it, this is what you want.

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard not to recommend for an Aliens fan. This current all time low sale price of $20 for the base and pathogen expansion feels perfect. $30 isn't terrible for the base, but $15 for Pathogen is a bit much, so definitely catch that on sale if you miss this one.The story is surprisingly good, again if you're into Aliens. Voice work is great. How the campaign actually unfolds a story is great and akin to L4D or Vermintide 2, but you actually have to play it in order, so it's coherent.The game itself has some jank and strange decisions, but it gets the important bits right.The 7 different classes (kits) all feel good and distinct with different roles for a fireteam. The customization within kits is also plentiful to cater to your tastes with the perk and modifier grid system.Gunplay is good. Smart guns feels fantastic and powerful on a horde like you'd think from the movies. Tons of weapons and attachments to choose from, both bought from a store and found/unlocked.There are consumable items like mines, turrets, and force fields that you can use to entrench positions.After you play the campaign, you unlock alternate game modes consisting of several different maps with different spice like xeno horde waves, so you don't only have the option of repeating the campaign endlessly. Downsides: No in-game communication like text or voice chat, just emotes and a non-contextual ping, truly a strange choice for a modern game. Low player count, but there is crossplay with Xbox and PS, so its not ridiculous to matchmake, especially on the later difficulties and post-campaign gamemodes (the discord is pretty active as well). Peer to peer with no ping display, so bad hosts can lag, drop, and burn a run since there's no reconnecting (or mid-run join either).I've not stuck with many a horde shooter before due to boredom of some variety (too repetitive, poor combat, bad/no progression, etc.) but AFE has a satisfying loop that outweighs the downsides in my book. It really feels like playing as a colonial marine a la Aliens, and who (again, of aliens fans) wouldn't enjoy that?

_childDocuments_.review: *Warning Possible Spoilers*Look, this game is OK at best. It's nothing spectacular but it's not terrible either. Shooting the Aliens is fun, I love their animations and the sounds they make. Some of the HUD displays are a bit questionable, for example when you kill a Alien a giant X pops up above their head and on certain difficulty settings the aliens will be lit up Red when you're ADS'd. I immediately turned these off as I felt they ruined the "Immersion" of the game. I use the term Immersion loosely as it's NOTHING like you'd get from Alien Isolation, Trust me. The Music isn't that great, it feels like someone tried to knock off the soundtrack of the Alien Franchise and did a terrible job, It's Very forgettable. There's this weird sound that the game makes when you Critical hit an Enemy I can't describe the sound via text but at first it didn't bother me. However after 10 hours of Grinding and constantly head-shotting things repeatedly this sound really starts to Grate on you. I did see in a Q&A that they will be looking to add a setting that will allow you to disable that though.The Story is rather short, 4 Acts and each Act has 3 Missions. They're... Okay. They honestly remind me of Left 4 Dead's Story Structure and Gameplay. Go here > Turn this on > Fight a Horde > Repeat. Some times different types of Enemy's such as Xeno Warriors will come out of no where and hunt you down, they're pretty cool and do add to the Enemy Variety. However the Story Missions are no where near as interesting as Left 4 Dead. Remember how L4D/L4D2 had the Director Mechanic that made the Missions different EVERY TIME you played it. Don't expect that here, EVERY Enemy placement is the exact same, they always come out the exact same holes with the exact same numbers of enemies. After you've played a Mission 3-4 times you learn how the level plays inside and out and it becomes EXTREMELY Repetitive, and while we're on the subject of the AI. They're not ground breaking in anyway, the AI are extremely repetitive and after playing and paying enough attention you'll see the AI do the exact same thing over and over, kind of like a conger line. 1 Alien will come out of a vent, run to a wall, jump on said wall, walk towards you then you'll most likely shoot it, but while the Xeno is walking along the wall 4 other Xenos are coming to do the EXACT same movement. I honestly would've preferred the Xeno's AI to be much more random in that they should be smarter and able to surprise you. But what makes it worse is you have a "Power Level" you need to grind these missions for so you're able to play the next Act's or the Previous Act's on a Harder Difficulty. Grinding this Power Level on 4 different Classes gets VERY old VERY fast. Think of the Power Level as the Light Level from Destiny 2, exact same concept except a Skill tree(different on all 4 classes) and weapon attachments are what raise your Power Level.Speaking of Destiny 2, I remember when I played that game one of the First things I did after repeating a Mission was Turning off the CRINGEY AF Dialogue. This Game is the exact same, the Dialogue is f*cking HORRIBLE in some Sections. Thank god they added a Dialogue Volume Slider on Release. 2 Things they didn't include on release however are -1. No Voice Chat or In-Game Chat box. Good luck telling new players how to play the game, when you're grinding and you activate a rare Challenge Card(which boosts XP and Credits), if the people in your lobby have no clue wtf they're doing you might end up wasting that Challenge Card because you can't Communicate with them. Seriously, it's 2021, In-Game Communication should be a STANDARD addition.2. No Cross-play? Yeah Cross-play isn't as much of a Expectation as Voice chat, but come on, a small horde game like this where it would be fun to mess around with friends. It should've had it! A lot of people keep saying they're having issues finding players while matchmaking, I have had this a few times but it's so few and far inbetween the times it does work that it hasn't really bothered me. If you don't find a player or 2 and there's 30 seconds left, just leave the Queue and Search again. Look, I'm a HUGE fan of the Alien Franchise. I collect Figures etc of this beautiful universe. Alien Isolation is one of the best games I've ever played. I just Can't recommend this game at it's full price (£35). It's just not Worth it. I'd say it's worth £25 at best. I'd say wait for a price drop if you know you definitely want this game. By the time you get it cheaper they may have sorted out a few kinks the game has and added more content. Don't get me wrong, It's not a flop like Colonial Marines, no way. It's just not the Aliens Game I was hoping for after all these years, it's just a pretty weak attempt in my honest opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: I do recommend this game but only barely for about 5-10 eu price range. _childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of A L () E N S, you'll appreciate this game. If you enjoy games like WWZ, Left 4 Dead, or Zombie Army Trilogy, then you'll definitely enjoy this game. Over all a solid AA horde shooter that feels authentic to the films in a way that adds lore and supports continuity of the Alien cannon. Decent story that ties in with existing lore. Authentic sound design from the films. Some NPCs are annoying and unnecessary. _childDocuments_.review: It's better than I expected. I have liked the Alien franchise since I was a child. Most of the games have been pretty bland. This one has been more fun than I anticipated. The weapons, settings and sounds are all pretty spot on for an Aliens universe. The loot system and challenges add more time to the game and it's enjoyable to figure out the weapons, though some are less useful than others.  Most people that like the Aliens movies or comics will find things to enjoy in this game. I think AFE is among the best of the franchises games, but it still has room to improve. I think this game is on the right track, but I would also love to see a full action RPG Aliens game.

_childDocuments_.review: Certainly, it's not like the games and movies are all flawless productions and there are quite a few stinkers among them but even so I still love the Alien (and Predator...) Universe. Aliens Fireteam Elite is a co-op shooter, a bit like games like Left4Dead but in 3rd person. It never reaches that quality of gameplay though and suffers from the same problems a lot of modern games have (Back4Blood for example). Don't get me wrong, the game is fun at times and it really feels like an Alien game but almost every run plays out the same. As far as I can tell most aliens usually spawn in the same way everytime, there hardly is any surprise at all. In most missions you just run around shooting aliens until you get to a point which you have to defend waves of aliens. Tactically it does not matter that much how you defend, at least not like in L4D was the case. It's nice you can play with  different classes, which all have different weapons and special attacks etc. There is some variety between (special) aliens. If you are familiar with L4D, you probably notice some similarities. There is for example an alien which spits acid, an alien which explodes, an alien which pounces you and an alien which could be seen as some kind of tank....In the end, the main thing why you would keep playing is the loot you get. There are quite a few cool looking weapons and other perks, you can level up your classes until you reach to a point in which you can level up like COD prestige levels....So it is a game you COULD spend a lot of time with but the question is if you SHOULD. Overall I do have fun with the game but I doubt a lot of people would play this game hundreds of hours.

_childDocuments_.review: Normally I don't leave reviews, but bloody hell this game is fun, and tense enough to make you pucker up the first time you play a mission. _childDocuments_.review: (Suggestions from one game developer to another)This is a great game! It really captures the essence of the Aliens movie with excellent level design and fun co-op. Single-player is good too although it's missing a few features related to the Alpha and Beta synths that cold make it great - I'll list below.A few things we would like to see added in future updates to knock this one out of the park:1) Ability to customize Alpha and Beta's (Synth) Load outs. A progression system for them would add depth too.2) Ability to give orders to the Alpha and Beta synths.3) Randomize where the xeno spawn a bit more. Especially in smaller corridors. When one comes out of a vent I know theirs always going to be 2-3 more from that same spot. I don't even have to look anywhere else. Just wait for them to line up. It breaks immersion when it's so predictable. 4) Add some basic animations to the Human AI in the base to move their mouths and hands a bit when they speak. Currently it just feels a bit incomplete in this regard.And that's about it. Cold Iron really nailed the rest of it. I'd love to see more DLC in the future so keep the content coming.  And thanks for this game.-Touchstone Bros.

_childDocuments_.review: as a first release from a small developer company, its awesome good work but still... not worth 40 bucks. if you plan to play this in single player or if you hope for good matches with other random guys => stay away from this!there are some fundamental things missing for such a coop-based game which should be a minimum feature. without any kind of ingame communication (no chat, no voice com), random players just hope they get matched with some other guys that can read other's minds. IF you get matched with real players at all! often times you wait in queue just to get matched with bots anywayz. in a few weeks, when the first hype about this game is over and less people will be online, it will get even harder to get matched i guess. PROS:- SOUNDS: awesome sound effects; feels like in the original movie- CHALLENGE: good challenge for players that like to be on the edge of being overwhelmed by the enemy- SLAUGHTERING: shoot everything and paint your surroundings with flesh and bones of your enemies- PLAYER UPGRADES: nice wide choice of combinations of weapons and upgrades to customize your playstyle for each mission- STABILITY: game runs fluently without crashes even on a mediocre PC and still looks good- CONS:- COOP-INTERACTION: no ingame communication with your random team mates!?! you need your own voice chat up and running to be effective on the upper difficulties- AUTOSAVE: no saved checkpoints during missions. if you (or your bots) f*ck up and die just short before the end, you'll have to do the whole mission again right from the start- STORY: short story that leaves you with a kinda "meh" feeling- PLAYER'S PROGRESSION: if you dont play with your friends on harder difficulties with your own voice chat running for faster xp grind, you need to grind through the "meh-story" in singleplayer mode like at least twentytwelvehundred times to level up your characters and gear to the max => missing motivation- GAMEPLAY: bots are helpful in the two lowest difficulties but with friendly fire activated in the harder ones, they mess up everything by runnig into your own line of fire every single time- MATCHMAKING: too few players online to get matched according to your own progress. you need your own friends to go sure you'll have a pleasent experience with the coop mode. - UPDATE POLICY: the "FOR FREE" marketing with the upcoming updates is just out of place imho. its like buying a new car for full price but you'll get the windshield "FOR FREE" in about three months! oh, and you'll also get the backseats in another 3 months - also "FOR FREE"! yayyy, what a deal, right?!- PRICING: 40 bucks is too much for this first release imho. for half the price it would be just plain awesome and players would understand that some things are just missing in a first release game. for full price though, customers can expect wayyy more content right off the start (and not in three/six/nine months)!sad to say i claimed refund for this release. maybe i get back to it when its on sale or something. but still have no hopes that this game will be relevant in 6 months from now.

_childDocuments_.review: A decent squad shooter with a very short campaign. Acquiring new weapons and skill perks keeps you in the game a bit longer, if they didn't have different weapons to try and upgrade the whole experience would last probably less than 5-10 hours for a full play-through. Even still I'm at the last chapter of the campaign at 10 hours of game-time and I've replayed 2 full chapters. I'll likely play until I max out my favorite class gear sets but I can't help but feel there was some lost potential with all that there is in the aliens franchise. I hope this is sort of a first installment in terms of the campaign and we'll get to play more or go back to some classic areas from the movies and play through those. Also the fact you don't really get any boss fights like the queen alien or the thing from Alien resurrection, again just feels like a lot was left on the table that the could have done here.Graphics - 9/10 - beautiful locations that look authentic, however there is a lot of repetition in the mapsSound - 7/10 - Soundtrack sounds sort of like the epic alien/aliens score but like someone playing it on a midi keyboard. But I do love the classic movie buurrt of the pulse rifles.Controls - 5/10 - the character responsiveness and controls feel clunky and slow. I did just finish playing through Outriders which had fantastic responsiveness so could also be bias from that.Mechanics - 5/10 - Basics are there and it's not horrible with a team but nothing different or even above average to the experience. Left 4 Dead probably had more to offer and it's 10 years old or something.Story - 5/10 - as I said it is super short. Essentially two locations. Story line has been done a million times over they could have come up with a little more here, although they did at least try to provide a little more with the collectible logs you can find and read.Value - 5/10 - it's overpriced currently, probably worth 2/3 or half in my opinionIf you really love aliens it's not a bad game to experience for about 10 hours with friends. The squad mechanics are nothing ground breaking, movie authentic locals are fun to see, characters are pretty simple but make sense given the lore/movies, don't expect too much and you wont' be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: I think this is a great game and accomplishes what it sets out to do.  It has intense moments which require coordination with other players to really maximize your abilities.  Problem is, you can't coordinate with other players within the game with the exception of emotes and pings.  Yes, you can communicate through discord, but through public matchmaking you run into the issue.  I hope they will eventually add some type of communication feature to the game.Controls are good, graphics are good, replay value is so-so (really dependent on finding other people to play with at the harder levels), and the class/weapon customization is great.
