_childDocuments_.review: What is Aliens:Fireteam Elite?Its basicly a PvE hordeshooter. You and 2 Friends or AI partners run from point A to point B and shoot aliens while doing so. Reaching Point B you allways have to defend against a Horde of Enemies for a certain amount of time or amount of Enemies. After doing so, you continue this gameplay loop until the level end is reached. While that sounds somewhat very basic and dull, I found it actually very enjoyable. The Game is filled to the brim with Fanservice and little details I absolutely loved.I am a Kid of the 90´s. Ellen Ripley was a strong Female main protagonist way before all that woke nonsense. The Movie Aliens is one of my most beloved movies of all time. And for people like me, who absolutely adore the Franchise this is a real gift.The Sound of the Pulse Rifle, the Smartgun, the way the aliens claw around them while you blast them to pieces. I absolutely Love it! And all the little details show, how much the developer cared for this game. While doing your missions, you allways got your Operator connected. "Herrera" a latin american though women and a Scientist that you rescue early on. The Dialogues between those two are often just awesome and very memoreable. Also Randomized somewhat, so that you dont hear the same voicelines everytime. That alone showed me, how much this is Fanservice. I wont go into detail here to much for the sake of Spoilers.To keep you entertained while playing, every mission has a hidden cache somewhere so there is a Ton of weapons, decals, colours, emotes and all that stuff to collect for you. There is also a Levelsystem in place with perks and different combinations of those to fiddle around with.I Bought this game discounted, even tho I actually love it, but I dont think its worth 40€. Mostly because im a cheap guy and know the next steam sale will come. 20€ Is money well spent on this. I did have alot of Fun and intent to keep playing this from time to time.The Game sounds and Looks amazing. The DLCs are mostly cosmetic in Nature, except for the Pathogen one. I do not own it yet, since it only offers a single new campaign with a playtime of rougly 1 hours. Maybe I´ll grab it once its on sale for 5€.TL;DR:If you´re a Diehard alien fan, buy it. If you´re looking for solid Coop fun. Buy it. Thanks for Reading.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm old and can't consistently play with friends because of life stuff, so bought primarily for single-player. That was a mistake. They won't complete objectives, they won't use equipment, they constantly get injured, and their combat AI is awful. Take cover > don't see enemies unless they're literally next to them > leave cover > finally see enemies > take cover again > try to shoot > too late, enemy is too close > leave cover > take damage and rely on the human player to save them. Repeat infinitely until dead. Because the game is balanced for 3 players, even the lowest difficulty is a chore. You have to do absolutely everything and spend more time babying the bots.You can't even pause out of frustration, the game keeps going as if it were online, so you just die.This really shouldn't list SP as a feature. If you're interested because it does, don't waste your time.

_childDocuments_.review: After completing the campaign and spending time with some classes I neglected in the process, as an Aliens fan I think this game is almost everything I would ask for.  The combat is fun and frenetic. The visuals and sounds are true to the iconic ambiance, and the Tetris-like perk system is appreciated over a simple skill tree where you just assign points. The story works as a serviceable backdrop and is probably better than anything the movies have done since Alien 3. I read a lot of negative or luke-warm reviews, and am not sure what many people were wanting or expecting from this game. It might be 9-10 hours to complete the campaign if you blitz through it with blinders, but with challenge cards, horde mode, and added difficulties there is ample reason for me to revisit to level up classes, unlock some cosmetics and find more hidden intels. I'm excited for future content, and will be looking out for new games from this developer. Well done and thank you for a fun Aliens game! The only bugs I've encountered so far were on the opposite end of the pulse rifle, although I don't know why anyone would leave the default swaying when using the menus. Well worth the $40 in my opinion, and also, no action movie has more amazing quotes. "Get on the ready line, marine!"

_childDocuments_.review: Long into short - fine licensed coop-horde-shooter-game. Seen one, probably seen 'em all, but FTE is a fine catch if you spot it on sale. Closer to an indie game than the triple-A powerhouse that Isolation was, though.When FTE launched, I got it to see how much I'd hate it before I refunded it.Don't get me wrong - it'd be an understatement to call me obsessed with the franchise.I'm the kind of guy who has 3D modeled the Pulse Rifle alone more than one hundred times for the better part of a decade. I spent seven years submerged in a world of Colonial Marines as the go-to-do-all modeler-art-guy for a community that today is still over nine hundred strong. I have spent countless hours more-or-less larping the force composition and platoon-level organization of the US Colonial Marines and nitpicking over the most inane ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ regarding the measurements of the Sulaco, the scale of the UD-4L Cheyenne dropship, and squad-level composition. My fixation on Colonial Marines and 3D modeling is probably what sent my brother to the marines and what has me working in gamedev myself.Alien and Aliens alike are both things I respect immensely, and I consider to be major parts of my life and what shaped me into the person I am today. Unfortunately, that makes me a fan of a franchise that is, if we count the AvP films, two good movies out of eight, perpetually screwed over by something or other. Alien 3 could have made the franchise as big as Star Wars, and instead it literally killed it off. Resurrection was a meatpuppet mockery, Prometheus was pretentious, Covenant was a mediocre compromise - I could go on for actual hours nonstop explaining exactly why I detest and loathe every misstep these films make, to speak nothing of the games.I didn't want FTE to fail, but the way Gearbox bungled ACM in 2013 basically killed the shooter half of the franchise and left me jaded.Suffice to say, however, that I've come out feeling pleased with the game.FTE is the Colonial Marine shooter that I've wanted for the last decade or two.Cooperative horde action against swarms of Xenomorphs. Smartguns, pulse rifles, shotguns, incinerators - back 'em with a healthy dose of rockets, grenades, and robot sentries, and you come out with hundreds of dead bugs. Kick the door with three-man-coop, and you'll find acid-edged action waiting - especially if you decide to run the game on Intense like you ought to. You will be killing literal hundreds of Aliens on every level, and if you think it detracts from the horror, you wouldn't be wrong.But you also shouldn't expect the man-seeking hyperdeath phallus that is the xeno to be immortal. Exoskeletons and acid blood are all fine and dandy until 10 millimeters of high-explosive armor-piercing come knocking at a dozen rounds a second. ALIENS has always been the action counterpart to the survival-horror of ALIEN. Not that there isn't a horror to the combat - when the big swarms start to roll in and you get overwhelmed, when the specials start pouncing in - you either find a way to put them down, or they put  down and tear out your throats. While making specials sponge damage doesn't feel like the best approach to difficulty, that doesn't make the drone rushing at you from behind any less of a threat, or the warrior wading through your fire any less a problem.If you wanted a cooperative ALIENS shooter, then this is exactly what you wanted. It's enjoyable, relieving, and everything that ACM isn't - which, generally, is good. I can't think of anything I genuinely hate about FTE, and I think it deserves recognition for what it got right, and Cold Iron deserves recognition for getting FTE out.I was skeptical, even critical pre-release, wary of how the game was years overdue and how slowly it seemed to pull together - I'd seen ancient alpha and beta screenshots long ago, sensed conspicuous absence from what seemed like obvious launch & announce windows. It felt, in ways, like ACM happening  - it almost took as long to put together, after all. ACM gestated from 2007 to 2013; FTE from at least 2016 to '21. Six years against five. When news finally did start filtering out, I didn't follow it very closely - but I know that I was wary.I know at first I didn't like what I was seeing. A pulse rifle with rails? Attachments? Without the grenade launcher? Phasing out the old armor, the old helmet, injecting LED-lined tech and doodads all around?It felt like Cold Iron wasn't giving the art style the kind of respect and understanding that Creative Assembly had with Isolation. Isolation's seven years old and still stands as the peak replication of the lo-fi sci-fi aesthetic ALIEN had. The Colonial Marine and Synth armor designs were perhaps the things I would criticize most harshly. Of the Synths, they feel cartoonish - they try to apply Working Joes in a combat role, and what results is something I feel like I should be seeing in my XCOM runs instead of an Alien game. They aren't uncanny or discomforting - just toyetic nuisances with guns. In design, AvP 2010's Synths were fare more interesting, far more discomforting in how they had practically skinless faces. ACM, abominable as it is, had some more interesting designs when it came to the PMC armor - helmets in particular that were similar to the M10, yet more advanced, more armored - things that seemed built on the old PASGT, mating characteristics of the M10 to aspects of the WY dogcatchers. The result was something that felt very much like an interesting counterpart to Colonial Marine kit.FTE's approach to the combat helmet, by comparison, is to basically take a modern FAST or ACH, and - that's kind of it. Instead of taking characteristics of modern kit and applying them in unconventional forms - which is what the classic marine body armor did - they just took the modern kit wholesale, with maybe some minor alterations here and there. Gone is the head mounted camera, gone is the integrated headset, shaved down if even present is the classic lobster-tail neckguard - and you can forget about that iconic forehead strikeplate. Just a modern combat helmet, I guess.This said, FTE's art design is something I accepted and grew to like - the helmet's design being bland is perhaps the worst thing I can say about the game. It's a precise nitpick, and I can readily say that I'd take their weapons over any of ACM's any day. Part of me finds the M41A2 sacrilege for removing the grenade launcher, going down to 60 rounds per mag - but another part of me can accept it, understand why it was done. It helps that it's a far more interesting design than ACM's awful M41A MK2.Art-wise, good stuff by folks like Bryan Flynn, who did design work for id on the last couple DooM games, and great melodies from Austin Wintory. Much respect in his tracks for Goldsmith in particular, and the environments I adore. The story might not be told in the most engaging way, but the writing and lore seems to come from a creative place that pleases a lorenut like myself. While these aren't the designs my 1995 Colonial Marine Tech Manual spoke of, they're an evolution that the writing sells, and it weaves together a more cohesive picture of the expanded universe a few decades after the films. Far as I can tell, it builds on what the recent tabletop roleplaying game established, too.ACM made me feel nothing but disdain & contempt. A hate that ran to the fiber of my very being for everything from art design to sound design, to story & characters, balance, gameplay, the very act of trying to close the game because it keeps relaunching - vitriol for such a careless waste of what could've been a good, fun time.I was ready to hate FTE, to crawl in, nitpick, & refund it. I'd been wary of live-service BS and cash-grab plastic trash. I was ready to rip it apart for the slightest thing.I can't express how glad I am that I had a good, fun time with an ALIEN shooter again.

_childDocuments_.review: It's fundamentals are solid, the core game-play loop is just fun. It's not super polished, but compensates with a bunch of great surprises. For instance, none of the characters have speaking animations, but there is a ton of lore you can opt into hearing, and the VO is unfailingly well written and acted.  Excellent artistic design, with large and detailed set pieces that make you just stop do admire them (Which says a lot given how often ambushes occur). Another one of it's surprising charms: You can just, fire your weapons and abilities in the hub world. Because you deserve to try out the weapon/class you just equipped, or see how the mods you just installed change the feel. Despite it's RPG elements (each weapon levels, as do the 6 classes) the game never feels easy and the difficulty scales seemingly to infinity. Even if you haven't seen the movies, it's just a fun game, and if you are a fan of the movies, you'll appreciate the art direction and all the little in universe lore dumps (Like the detailed poster about voting in the elections, wall panels straight out of the Ridley Scott movie, the loader mech in the back of the hub, the list goes on.)

_childDocuments_.review: Half-finished eye candy, third-person only, can't jump, can't crouch, no sprint only light jog, the highlights are you can do a fancy jump over -some- waist-high objects, and also somehow do a shoulder roll with a bunch of heavy solid gear on your back... But otherwise the player has the kind of environmental mobility you might expect to find in a mobile game, if that.Perks and the stat modifiers of weapon attachments make no sense i.e. are 'magical' (e.g. a magazine option will somehow increase your max carried ammo and also temp-buff your RoF with a hit or partially refill the magazine on-kill, it is absolutely full of nonsense like this), all enemies are slow as hell, show no tactics as every situation is either a shooting gallery, bottleneck or '♥♥♥♥ you' type of scenario.The main enemies are Runners, with Drones and Warriors being 'heavies' (you can even also button-mash to wrestle some of these things off of you as if you were just play-fighting with a large dog...), also ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Left 4 Dead-type enemies like exploders and loogie-hockers, as well as gross, dumb, pasty ♥♥♥♥ expanded on from the not-canon Prometheus offshoot lore. This game is not 'Aliens', it plays like an Aliens-skinned Left 4 Dead with a bunch of other 'Funzo' ♥♥♥♥ packed in, do not be fooled, it is absolute trash.There are also numerous bits of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ fluff that not-so-subtly cater to contemporary North American 'social sensitivities' and 'social uprising'-type cringe, various other aspects also cater to this (see my full review linked to below).No select fire for any weapons, no alternate fire for any weapons, no alternate ammo options (no shotgun slugs etc.) except for consumable items that indiscriminately add incendiary or electroshock effects to -any- weapon...There is literally only one gun from the Aliens movie and it's not even a service weapon; the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Hicks shotgun; the rest are watered-down or repurposed variants, and a veritable flood of slick-looking ergonomic burst-fire crap, as well as other made-up gap-fillers and needlessly obscure weapons from the lore (i.e. Kramer assault rifle, and they didn't even get that right). One of the new weapons even uses the same name as the M39 submachine gun from ACM, but has been completely redesigned with no reason given.They didn't even try to add any of the many preexisting weapons introduced in previous games or other media, probably because a lot of them have select fire, alternate fire modes and ammunition options, which these ♥♥♥♥♥ seem to be ignorant of. By the way you are also not playing as the USCM, you are playing as the 'UACM', oh and the Colonel looks like an aged, lesbian Miley Cyrus.DO NOT BUY ALIENS: FIRETEAM ELITE; as last but not least; the 'pulse rifle' does not have a grenade launcher and the magazine only holds 60 rounds... _childDocuments_.review: Expectations for this game seem high among players, and there's nothing wrong with that (especially for $40). I'm only a few hours into the game, but I am enjoying the gameplay and Aliens universe immersion.  The 3rd person style of play reminds me of The Division/Wildlands more than Deep Rock Galactic, but it is probably a good choice over 1st person view since you are in cramped quarters with a lot of close action might be better observed from a distance.  If you are on the fence, you may want to see how the developers follow up with additional content in the months to come.  Frankly, I'd MUCH rather be patient for some content/customization than have some greedy, soulless AAA developer milking me for money at every turn and lousing up the franchise in general.  So at this point I see my $40 going towards not just the current game, but the game over time.  Hope the investment pays off!

_childDocuments_.review: I couldn't help but feel let down by Aliens: Fireteam Elite. While the premise of battling against vicious xenomorphs had the potential for an epic experience, the execution fell short, much like a Space Marine without his faith.First and foremost, the gameplay mechanics failed to capture the intensity and tactical depth that I had hoped for. The combat felt repetitive and lacked the strategic elements that are characteristic of relentless assaults. I yearned for the satisfying melee engagements that define our chapter, but instead, I was forced into monotonous gunfights that grew tiresome all too quickly.Additionally, the overall level design left much to be desired. The environments lacked the atmosphere and immersion that would have made the alien-infested locales truly terrifying. I found myself unenthused as I fought through uninspired corridors and generic industrial settings, longing for the grim and foreboding landscapes of my beloved Aliens universe.Furthermore, the AI companions, or lack thereof, proved to be a major setback. In the absence of any meaningful companions, I was left with mindless and unresponsive squadmates. It felt like fighting alongside dull servitors, devoid of the camaraderie and synergy that should have been the hallmark of an elite fighting force.Finally, the story, or lack thereof, was a major disappointment. Aliens: Fireteam Elite delivered a forgettable and unremarkable plot, devoid of any emotional investment or memorable moments.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd like to preface my review with saying that this is not a BAD game, it's just very mid, which is the problem with video games today. Aliens: Fireteam Elite is a generic horde shooter with a coat of "Aliens" paint smeared on top. The campaign was an absolute snooze-fest, so much so that it took me almost 2 years to finally force myself to finish it, in an attempt to give this game a fair shake. I think I can honestly say that I skipped past every single piece of dialogue possible, so I could get back to shooting aliens as quickly as possible. The gameplay is meh; shooting aliens feels ok, but the progression (which comes in the form of perks that modify class skills, and some pretty lackluster weapon attachments) barely hooked me at all. Once you finish the campaign you unlock 3 variations of horde mode. All 3 of them are trash, and I can tell they were just tacked on just so the devs could say there was some kind of "endgame." All 3 variations utilize recycled scenes from some of the campaign maps, and you just hold out until you die, that's it. No fortifications, no roguelike progression, nothing. Just shoot until you die. How very f-ing boring and disappointing.And to add on to all of this, I saw from another steam review that pre-release, the devs stated that none of the post launch content would cost money except for cosmetic items, only to go back and quietly edit any posts or marketing materials that displayed that statement before announcing the Pathogen DLC. It's not like Pathogen is anything to write home about (just like the base game lol) but what kind of anti consumer ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ is that?

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be honest, I didn't have high expectations, seeing as there has been a long history of slapping good movie franchises on crappy games for a buck... but I gotta say, this game is a solid and immensely fun FPS that would be a blast even without the Aliens flavoring.The character class choices are varied and meaningful while giving all of them a place to shine, as well as being able to freely switch between missions. There are a ton of weapons to choose from, allowing a huge choice in damage type, engagement range, accuracy, clip, and many more options, and each has 3 scope/muzzle/etc. slots to further customize. Likewise, abilities and weapon skills can be modified, with each character getting a certain number of modifier slots that can be filled by a wide selection.There are 12 maps to play on (3 more in the DLC) that are split between space station and various cave-like areas. To add even more variety, most have at least one point where there's more than one possible path or goal, which the game randomly chooses each time the map is loaded. In addition, spawns are moderately randomized, which all in all gives a varied experience each play.The story is good enough that I kept playing to see what was going to happen, and mixes in Prometheus lore, giving it a new flavor over the previous Aliens games. (Predator is not featured... yet?)The game has a decent amount of character customization for a FPS, allowing the usual changes over a few base faces. In the base game, each class has 2 base armors choices, 1 more purchasable, and a bunch more earnable through leveling. There a few cosmetic-adding DLCs, but otherwise the game avoids micro-transactions, which is massively refreshing.TLDR; Good game, buy!* *See edit.Edit: I'm going to have to revise my review a little bit. The multiplayer aspect is utter ♥♥♥♥, and trying to find people to play with, or not get dropped once you do is bordering on impossible. If you're not okay playing single-player, seriously consider avoiding this game. Playing by yourself is fun, but unless you enjoy mindless grinding, you'll go through the content in a pretty quick time. By all accounts of the forums, the company that made this game has basically abandoned it. I revise my rating to "Wonderful game but too short, buy on sale."

_childDocuments_.review: This game takes the idea of co-op and applies the Alien world to it.  I thought this would be a decent shooter as I love the Alien universe. The game is probably not the best alien shoot em up co-op (I'd say that would be Halo or Gears of War) but taking something I love, in the Alien universe, and taking parts from something else that was a masterpiece (Alien: Isolation), makes this worth $40.

_childDocuments_.review: I can see how people enjoy this game and are loving it. Following the reviews, a friend and myself decided to try the game. We played through the first two scenarios on standard difficulty. The game crashed on my friend's end the first time we played and we had to restart the mission from the beginning (we were only half way through). We never felt it as much of a challenge, and just sat around killing waves of mobs. There was never much of a danger or threat. I understand there are harder difficulties and challenges which can make it more challenging. Variety of enemies. Yes, there is a variety, but the pace and how easy a lot of them fell, did not really make any difference between them. Plus, my mate had a tendency just to run through and past most mobs getting to the next point quickly. There was never a time he got punished for straying from the group.Group  of 3, not bad, but more could also be great. However, the biggest problem with it is no comms. No chat, no voice, we can only ping. This is not an issue if you have a pre-made group of 3 on Discord or other communication service, but if you are solo or needing to search for an extra person, there is no real way to communicate with them.Lastly, with optimisation, it lacked the depth of settings to change graphics (or we could just not find it). We could change some, but was more on/off for certain items. The game ran okay, but expected better performance based on the textures and lighting present within the game (did not feel as if it was a 2021 game).It may seem as if I have bashed the game, but this is the problems and issues we encountered. Overall, we just were not hooked on it. However, it is not a bad game by any means. With a few updates and at a lower price point, I would be able to recommend it. However, in the current state and price, not so much.  This is by no means to avoid, I'm really on the fence with this one. Cannot say not to get it because it is bad, nor can I say to get it now because it is amazing. It is...alright.

_childDocuments_.review: Some reviewers hated this game, but this is the best Aliens game released in a while. I love re-playing it, yes, there aren't many maps but you're not supposed to play this game for hours on end, play a map or two and take a break! It's ideal for that.Pros: -Huuuuuuge variety of weapons. For an Aliens game that is. Superb loot. -Sound design. Some people will HATE that the weapons sound is ripped directly from the movies. Personally I love it, shotgun sounds clearly show that developers were capable of making meaty good sounds, but either had to or chose to go with the original pulse rifle sound. In my opinion, that was a good decision. -Difficulty. This game is quite difficult after unlocking all difficulties, you have to min-max your loadout. It adds to replayability. -Enemy variety. Let's be honest what did you expect of enemy variety in a game based on Alien's franchise? No spoilers, I'll just say you will be positively suprised. -Challenge card system. This is quite interesting, it can terribly affect how you will play the map, conserve ammo or even affect the spawnrates of enemies, additional loot etc. Very fun addition. -B-story. Story is very simple, clearly budget cuts were made on it, but it's good enough. I do enjoy the banther and to be honest characters do speak like they're from aliens universe, that's all I needed. Who knows, maybe in the future they'll be allowed to expand the story?Cons: -Map variety. It's just not great. For a start yes it's good and they're expertly crafted! I love them personally but I just want more, even as DLC. -Arena style gameplay. It's very typical for all maps, sometimes the objective is a bit different but for the most part it's the same: go to room, kill waves, go to next room, do the same. There could be some more variety, but then again it's a shooter. For example, there could be sitiations where your fireteam is overwhemled by aliens because one person specifically has to cut the door through, while teammates cover you. That would add tension, sadly it's not here really. -Bulletsponges at higher difficulty. Guess I am complaning game is too hard, or I haven't properly equipped myself for it, but on higher difficulties enemies are horrible bulletsponges, especially the special aliens. You also get less max ammo so the effect doubles, so its sometimes really hard to push through. -Bot AI. It's awful, Gets in your way, bad target prioritization. In general the AI bots suck. Instead of nerfing them on higher diffs, you should buff them. I understand it's meant to be played with people online, but why gatekeep your playerbase who has enough of MP games for a day?I love this game, but like I said, you have to play it sporadically. I play it 1-2 times every day, do the dalies maybe a fun mission, grind something out and done. I am never disappointed. It's a must have for aliens fans. I really hope they'll make some good DLC maps and in general do more with the game, the developers clearly 100% have the capability to make a great game, but the budget did not allow them to.This game is a blast every time.

I asked my Son for help and he hosted a game for me to join. I loved it as it was the best time I had spent with my Son since my wife had died. This game has ever since brought my son and I closer again and now we actually spend time together outside the house as well. This game reminded me that there's fun to be had in everything, and it has brought both me and my Son many happy memories.

_childDocuments_.review: If you really love Alien franchise, especially Aliens, then it's a must buy. _childDocuments_.review: I've never seen a more faithful, authentic and esthetically pleasing Aliens adaption.Or movie adaption in general.Highly recommended for fans of the Aliens franchise but also as a scifi multiplayer game in general!It's the type of game where you play the same levels repeatedly, which probably isn't everyone's cup of tea. They did add some variation though, like different audio comments or loot boxes that spawns at a random location.Regarding the RPG aspect, the level cap is quite low, but there are several "kits" (classes). You level the same character in every kit you want and can switch to a different kit in between missions. At level up, you get additional perks of which you can equip only a certain amount. You can also level up your weapons and attach modifications.I enjoyed this system a lot, my only dislike being, that there aren't more kits and a higher level cap (and more missions as well of course!)All in all, I'd say skill and knowledge of the missions and strategies is much more important that your level in this game. There are also auto aim features however, which you don't have to use of course, but it seems to bother some people.I've only started playing this recently, but had no trouble finding people to play with online, even though the "Quick Play" mode is only unlocked after beating the game once.

_childDocuments_.review: YO FIRST OF ALL why does the music in the game sound like Mrs. Doubtfire is baking a cake? Flutes and oboes teeedeeleeteedeee.... Yet the radio in the ship is intense electo soundtrack? every single "thumbs up" I see below has less than 8 hours of playtime. Lol? That's because the game isn't even that long (most of my playtime was from just AFKing with it minimized)how can you release a game like this and not have any compelling endgame? The "horde mode" is slow until suddenly it's impossible. there is no "just put me in a game" so you have to manually pick which boring mission you have to slog through again to "level up." And then the artificial difficulty bumps are really more about the friendly damage than anything else, never mind that there's no real point to doing them. Gearscore is so arbitrary in this the hardest 2 difficulties don't even list a gearscore. Cool?I dunno, I wish I wrote down the time it took to complete each mission because all the endgame is, besides doing tacked on "2 dailies" and "1 weekly" is picking a mission and doing it again, meaning the most efficient mission is the only one you'd bother doing.the game doesn't even have a real ending, you do the last mission and instead of some cutscene it just puts you back on your ship to read text?Whoever thought it was a compelling game to have one character literally filling the other characters screens with fire (literally the entire screen becomes yellow if someone flamethrows through you) is a real genius. That's exactly who this game was made for, someone with $40 to blow (more for "cosmetic seasons?" lol) with some strong childhood nostalgia, who plays one mission a week in between uploading pictures of their RGB battlestation to reddit.

_childDocuments_.review: Hooo boy here we go. ( Game plays well, especially with friends, but the content is NOT worth the asking price )Now for the more serious review, for what it's worth to people.Positive overview.I like the game's setting, the maps and environments are well designed for the most part. I like the gunplay and the mechanics of each different class, the cover system works well and the customisation for guns is pretty nice and thorough for there only being 3 attachment slots per weapon.That's really about it.Negative overview.I don't like the mind-numbingly repetitive nature of it.4 'campaigns' that are 3 levels each isn't really that much content. Takes about an hour to do each campaign fully, if that.I get the plans to release new seasons and such for free, but the new class they just added is nearly useless compared to all of the others.Its got that Deep Rock Galactic system of various items and cosmetics relying sheerly on you finding randomly spawning caches in each level. Fun. Not.The daily challenges and weekly challenges ask you to do mundane tasks for little reward. Also, if you care that much about spoilers, I've seen daily challenges that literally spoiled half the things I hadn't seen up to a certain point.Levelling up is painfully boring unless you use challenge cards, which surprise surprise, are bought from RNG packs at the requisition store. And a lot of the cards are just annoying instead of being interesting challenges.As much as I appreciate that they randomised certain elements of the missions to stop things being completely stale, I still get bored playing said same missions more than once.There's more I can moan about, but honestly I'll just start getting nitpicky. I'll leave it there.I would happily recommend the game if it was about £20 (about $30) in it's current state. Even personally getting it for £10 cheaper from a key site I feel like it was still too much for what you get. I'll only be playing it more after this review date just for the sake of actually making up the hours for the price.Perhaps if you just like/love Alien as a franchise, you won't mind. But to a more casual fan, I don't see the price matching the appeal.

_childDocuments_.review: Aliens: Fireteam Elite is another 3 player: co-op game in the long line of co-op games; but this time set in the James Cameron Aliens universe; you can customize your own Colonial Marine and pick up to 4 classes each one carrying the iconic Aliens weapons that you know and love; having their own stats and abilities, etc.You are a part of a Fireteam squad sent to a remote location in deep space on a mission for Weyland-Yutani; fight alongside your friends as you battle through dangerous locations filled to the brink of Xenomorphs... You just might pull off quotes every now and then from the movieThis is a must buy with friends; the intensity, the hilarity; and in addition the additions of Horde mode, the challenge cards that can affect a mission, the dailies; there is a lot of fun to be had in this gameHowever, the BIGGEST concern is replay value; maybe after completing the game once and going through Horde mode is fun; but at some point it can get boring; no there is no PvP mode in this game, or a Haley's Hope DLC (not yet at least). There is a pre-order bonus where you can be Vasquez but not the other marines. The graphic look is dated, but the set pieces are amazing; really gives off the vibes very nicely as well as sound design for the guns and aliens. The only negative i can say is that - do not play this solo because the bots are just oof; and there is no 4 player lobby... Overall, for the price point of $39.99 again it's worth it ONLY if you have a squad; otherwise wait for deep sale or find people within the community.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't feel like reading the whole thing? Down at the bottom is the conclusion and score given to the game! :)Have you ever played a game that makes you feel good, like a sense of satisfaction? Well, that is what Aliens Fire Team Elite does! It features builds that make you want to play the game more as you unlock new awesome weapons and gear that are pretty neat. For example, you can get a Gatling gun with the auto-aim or an expansive shockwave that fries the aliens as they come closer to you. The aliens come from everywhere, appearing from ceilings, corners, and doors to ambush you daily. You must always keep your guard up as they can move fast and re-enter the ventilation system for a surprise attack later. They come in huge numbers, and it is fun to eliminate as many of them as possible before they breach your defenses and reach you.The game is well-balanced, there are enough resources to resupply once you start running out of ammo, and it keeps you going at all times. However, sometimes the game is too generous, which takes some of the tension away as you can keep refilling your ammo or get a lot of medkits. It is a relatively easy title to get into and play, but if you underestimate the aliens, you can lose, especially on higher-difficulty missions.  I played as the newest class, the Lancer, and had a great time, packing up an auto aim-gattling gun with an electric shotgun that melted the aliens away. There are several classes to fit your playstyle: doctors to heal allies, gunners to destroy enemies with a rain of bullets, and even tanks that can take a beating and deploy riot shields. What I didn't like about the game is that the cover system is out of place; since you kill the aliens too fast or they reach you, it is not ideal to stay in one spot. Most enemies are also melee, meaning that instead of staying in cover shooting, you would rather keep moving to get good angles to shoot the enemies from as they appear from multiple spots.The game was tested with an RTX 2060, 36 GB of ram, Intel Core i7-11700K - Core i7 11th Gen Rocket Lake 8-Core 3.6 GHz LGA 1200. I ran it at max settings and got a constant 72FPS at all times. In terms of graphics, the game looks fantastic, and there are animations such as aliens losing their heads and then slowly falling into the floor. The level design is excellent as the fidelity is top-notch; the environments look like they come from movies such as the Original Aliens or the Prometheus films. It nails the franchise's look and is loyal to the series. Now when it comes to sound, it could be a lot better. The guns have no impact; shooting them is like shooting air, and no weight is put into their sound or animations. It is a shame because you want to keep upgrading them, yet in the sound department, they fall so flat for a game of this budget. The alien's noise is also a miss as they are generic and don't instigate a sense of terror or presence in the player when listening to them coming; the standard enemy sounds a bit off for an alien.The voice actors are okay and passable, but the story is not the forte of Fireteam Elite, and it comes off as a bit crude. You will likely skip some dialogue lines as you lose interest in what the characters are saying.The best part of the game is that it is a fun short game; going into the missions and executing the aliens as you advance your build is rewarding. It feels euphoric when you see that red X mark on aliens the moment they die to your bullets, and it makes you want that improvement on how to dispatch them better. In addition, your weapons can be customized in various ways, making the progression system a blast as you add attachments and modifiers that can alter how your abilities behave!The game also understands that there are good aspects to making the game a short experience. It doesn't feature any grease filler nonsense or waste your time; instead, it puts you right into the action and doesn't overstay its welcome, as the title is a direct experience. The campaign is 7 to 10 hours long, which is the perfect length for this type of game. When it comes to replayability, Fireteam Elite has a lot to offer when it comes to content; it can easily last you 25 hours or more if you desire. The issue is how much of it you can stomach, as the game gets repetitive after the campaign's initial 7 to 10 hours. If you try to play more after that, you may be bored of the title or sick of the game as you keep playing it. After beating the story mode, you unlock new modes and difficulties that can keep your interest if you want to extend your time with the title.I recommend Aliens: Fireteam Elite, especially on a sale. If you want a lot of fun for a few hours, it is a solid title with enjoyable gameplay and progression. The expansion pack is not worth it as by the time you clear the story, you will probably be done with the game, and while it does add some extra modes, such as hardcore mode, the base game is a delightful experience that lasts the right amount of time. 8/10  GREATIf you enjoy and find the review helpful, please follow my curator StarsDeck!

_childDocuments_.review: Aliens : Fireteam Elite. Recommended. 3.5 out of 5 Stars.I enjoyed Aliens : Fireteam Elite, even though there really isn't an online gaming population. I enjoyed the DLC add-ons too. The Main Story offered about 8 hours of game-play. The DLC Story adds another 2 hours. Difficulty levels really don't change the campaign run time, but having better characters on subsequent runs does.Pros : Good story for Main and DLC. Challenging swarms as Difficulty increases. Good graphics. Re-playability in different modes. The game is fast-paced and the "Special" enemies can be tough. There is a decent mod base for A:FE (though none are being updated).Cons : Base Fire-Team bots are ugly generic "synthetics" with poor scripting (but they will draw enemy aggro). There is _no_ online gaming population (you'll wait in queue forever unless you pre-arrange a group, or enable Crossplay). Crossplay players are problematic (they can lag out games, AFK w/o consequence and kill your mission, some use exploits as there is no Crossplay VAC check). Opposition (Alien/Synth) bot pathing (routing) and spawn points are basic and fixed with very low randomization (spawn sizes and damage differentials only increase with Difficulty).I play non-mmo games for the Story first with no mods. If I like the game and game mechanics, I'll continue playing for accolades, pve/pvp, friends and experiment with mods. I bought the game on sale and believe I got my money's worth out of the title. I would suggest you consider following the same strategy if you're a fan of the Alien-verse, or have thought about trying Aliens : Fireteam Elite.

_childDocuments_.review: Not sure what the 'reviewers' are losing their cookies over. This is a great Co-Op shooter. For $40 it's got a least 10 solid hours of playability. It is pretty basic, which is part of what makes it fun. You don't have to invest hours of time just to understand the mechanics, do extended youtube research of how certain missions are completed or any of that. You just create your marine, pick a class and dive in. My only issues are, the weapon selection isn't small exactly, but it seems to me, so far, your starting weapons are the best your class gets, everything else is a weaker variation. This does get a bit drag because you want to try new things, but everything does less damage and eats more ammo, and higher difficulty levels continuously lower your ammo supply, so damage per shot is important. However I BELIEVE you can 'find' weapons in the game which aren't available for purchase. So far though nothing beats starting weapons. The 2nd thing is in the 13 hours I've been playing this, 1 time, just 1, my team cleared a room and the mission didn't trigger. Meaning the doors wouldn't open to let us proceed, meaning we had to quit and leave entirely. This is a real bummer. All the complaining about AI and everything, this wasn't intended to be a horror game, this is a bughunt. You're here to lay waste to the enemy en mass. It's a solid shooter with some interesting twists. Every mission though does seem to dwindle down to "go here, hold position against enemy waves, go here, do it again, go here and do it one more time for a big finale", literally every mission is the same recipe. The final mission mixes it up slightly by having you have to activate a thing and survive a short wave 3 times and then survive a big wave and then run like hell for the exit. You get a lot of 'gear' in the game, land mines, auto-turrets, etc. It feels like the auto-turrets are the only meaningful item in the bunch, landmines are a waste against smaller enemies and do relatively no damage to bigger enemies, I'm sure if enemies came in 'groups' and not single aliens running one after enough this might be more meaningful. Slowdown traps only last for 90 seconds which really shouldn't start until the first time an enemy enters into the area of the trap since the first 30 seconds of a holdout objective enemies tend to get wasted before reaching you. It's a good romp though, basic as it is, its a fun shooter. There's a few quirks but as is the norm these days I'm sure most of them will be patched out over the coming months.

_childDocuments_.review: What an excellent little co-op game! I feel like this caught not only the public but also the developers themselves off-guard. Having played through all of the campaign content and a few rounds of horde mode, I can quite comfortably say that the developers planned for more progression than they provided content for. Not to say that the content is in any way lacking - the campaign is constantly throwing new environments and challenges at you, but it seems to run dry well before the progression system tops out. This facilitates the need to replay the game at higher difficulties to get the most out of it. In hindsight, the 'Intense' difficulty (which proclaims to be the 'true way' to play the game) feels the most balanced for me and my friends, being a veteran of both Left 4 Dead and first person shooters in general.If you're looking for a game to fill a void somewhere between Left 4 Dead, Gears of War and Killing Floor, this game sits very comfortably betwixt those titles. It offers the rhythm and campaign progression of Left 4 Dead, the switch-up to cover-based shooter mechanics when the synths arrive, a la Gears of War, and the horde mode has very much the feeling of a more confined map in Killing Floor. The third-person perspective is very unobtrusive, and that's coming from a dyed-in-the-wool FPS gamer. If all of that sounds like your bag, I'd highly recommend this title. One can only hope that the developers and publisher recognise what an excellent - indeed surprising - Aliens franchise game they have on their hands, and support it with more campaigns!
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Fireteam Elite

_childDocuments_.review: It's a far better game than I expected. It is at it's core an online co-op experience first with a big focus on action. It plays well, it has many cool gameplay elements like the strategic placement of equipment to battle upcoming waves of xenos and the abilities of each class. Overall it is a good experience and feels like an Alien game. It lacks content though. It needs more maps, more weapons, more classes, more campaigns. If they keep updating and adding the content this game will be really really great at some point in the future. If you're an Aliens fan like me you will enjoy everything about this game... maybe wait for a sale though to really get the best value.

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun Left4Dead style cooperative gameplay with a surprising amount of weapon and class customization. I can't stress enough that the game is best enjoyed on Intense difficulty or higher with 2 other friends. If you don't have friends you get stuck with braindead AI that will almost always die and fail the mission for you. It's a shame that you have to have them along if you want to play Solo but with 2 other friends this game is a blast. Just having finished the first campaign and starting the second the game delivers very frenetic action and takes a lot of positive elements from the Aliens film and incorporates them into the game. Between $40 for this or $60 for Back4Blood just based on the beta, I would wager this is more worth the money as I am already having much more fun with this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely repetitive shooter with no real compelling story to speak of. You will basically go through the exact same gameplay loop of... Go into a mission, encounter a swarm, defeat the swarm, move into an area with an ammo crate +2 health packs, swarm happens again, move onto the next area, swarm happens again, move onto the next area, swarm happens again. Each of these missions are about 45 minutes to an hour long, and if you die, there are NO checkpoints. You must restart from the very beginning. The sound effects in this game are a huge disappointment as well. Guns dont sound like guns at all, I have no idea what to even compare them to, maybe dirty farts? When shooting the aliens it definitely looks like the guns arent having any impact at all, so perhaps we are shooting hot turd gas at them? It also seems to have a bit of a MMO grind to it, where as you get basically no amount of credits for completing the mission, so much so, that you will be forced to do a mission about a dozen times, in order to unlock any upgrades

_childDocuments_.review: hile Aliens: Fireteam Elite is far from being a movie tie-in, its overwhelming dedication to the cult classic from 1986 probably deserves its separate preface and recommendation. While being indifferent to James Cameron's action masterpiece does not make the purchase pointless, lack of affinity for ALIENS does make this game considerably less recommendable in the current market, but thankfully in terms of fan service, it is at worst- a guilty pleasure, at best- a genuinely good treat.   n its time, and with boundaries of the genre, Aliens vs. Predator 2 still ought to be considered a better title, nonetheless when it comes to attention to detail, dedication, and care about the proper translation of the source material, A:FE has moments where it firmly surpasses what the entire AvP series achieved. From flavor text and descriptions of items, atmospheric lighting, environmental design, sound design and music, to writing and the tone of the entire thing- from start to finish it is a proper homage to the fantasy of being a USMC grunt.Cold Iron Studios did really solid work here, especially considering this is their debut title! The game balances well on a thin line between respect for the IP and creative liberties involved in making a game of this type, and at no point it feels that team lost the will to make good on the opportunity given to them.That being said, excitement about the familiar setting, easter eggs and other member berries only get you so far and the game should be evaluated predominantly on how it plays, and... it's really not bad! Ultimately on most fronts, it's kinda a mixed bag, but with the aforementioned affinity for the ALIENS and some indulgence, it ends up being a enjoyable, pleasant enough experience.    o, what is under the hood? Well, a very basic AI companions with zero customizability and borderline nonexistent control over them during missions, that become very insufficient for difficulty levels above medium.A lot of repetitiveness with barely any additional layers of randomness spicing up replaying campaigns. And even during the first playthrough, the vast majority of activities are a variation of defending against waves of enemies, sometimes interrupted by pressing a button here and there.And hey- it is the name of the game (genre) but there's artistry in hiding turning gears, distracting players from the barebone formula of progression through linear levels, and fighting off swarm enemies. More of that could be forgiven some years ago, but now enough of them passed since Left 4 Dead, to realistically expect a bit more from the core gameplay loop.It's certainly an issue when taking into account the actual length and construction of the story content, divided into 4 campaigns (chapters) with three missions each, with an additional campaign in Pathogen DLC. All missions are extremely linear, with a handful of extra dead-end corridors and rooms here and there and with scripted set pieces and basic outbursts of enemies along the way. Honestly, the most notable alterations are NPC dialogue lines and responses, that in a few spots in each mission are picked at random.And this aspect, especially for people playing solo and not using A:FE as a community vehicle to chat with friends, is the weakest pillar of this game.But probably doesn't deserve equal amount criticism- it doesn't feel like devs ran out of time and money and cut the content short. Quality and polish are there from start to finish without any noticeable drops. That's just what could've been achieved with the resources they had to work with.   n practice, in the long run, the gameplay is carried by the setting and a few layers of progression and customization- just like in the Killing Floor series, players can play as one of seven classes sharing two out of four weapon groups: pistols, CQW, rifles, and heavy weapons, having a backup pistol, and a couple of special abilities, that can substantially be altered and modified with the perk customization system (fully unlocked after leveling a class to lvl8). The actual perks and modifiers are granted while leveling, as rewards for completing missions, and are found inside special caches (one per mission run), alongside consumables, skins, or emotes. A similar source of player income and gear are challenges that come in two types- daily and weekly quests set automatically by the game, and challenges from cards, that can be used during a mission deployment (one per player, using them and deploying destroys the copy of that challenge card), and can be bought in the armory on spaceship Endeavor (player hub) or found in said special caches. Challenge cards offer varying rewards of XP and currency, sometimes none and just provide advantages for those who are struggling. In practice- very simple and rather flexible system.Plus on top of that- there's player profile leveling, granting cosmetic items every 10 levels of prestige, up to lvl100. Overall not a bad depth considering the amount of actual story/mission content and that, gathering and leveling stuff, is mostly the actual endgame in this genre.   eedless to say, when evaluating A:FE as a product- not a lot of complaints can be directed toward technical performance. After numerous updates, the game is very stable and runs smoothly and reliably from start to finish. The scope and size of the whole thing is rather limited, but never presented deceptively, and in the end, it is overall definitely a case of 'sum bigger than its parts'.Even with disinterest for the license, Fireteam Elite still might end up a recommendation as long as one knows the limitations of the scope and size of this game. Yes, there are more potent horde shooter or narrative coop experiences, but it is a neat package, that can exist as a pallet cleanser between jumping into heavier games, or as a companion to those. There's very little in terms of systemic or mechanical overhead, which positions this game in a very nice spot where it can permanently sit on a hard drive for occasional dips, without a need to relearn complex systems and familiarize yourself with the flow again. As long as you have friends to play with or the player base remains workable, of course.   or ALIENS fans- it's a no-brainer. Even with a developed allergy to this genre, the entire game can be completed solo on lower difficulties, without the need for an additional human player. On its own, for at least one playthrough, it's more than serviceable, and from start to finish mired in love for the second installment in the Alien cinematic saga.Do not expect the ability to experience and checkbox everything this game has to offer while playing solo. In the end, the point of playing it becomes sharing the experience with other people while attempting to complete missions on the highest difficulties (and to be fair-split between the story campaign and a few additional modes, cool variations of horde point defense), leveling your player profile and weapons, and completing your perk selection, armaments, and a wide array of cosmetics. And no amount of your persistency can power through basic and lacking AI companions...   f that's not an attractive perspective- just grab it on deep sale and expect to breeze through it and say goodbye after a few hours.Otherwise- prepare for countless combat drops and a massive mountain of Xenos to climb onto.Well, and a hell of a lot of cornbread from which you'll find no respite.

_childDocuments_.review: I had initially given this game a positive review, I was having a blast, but the frustrations are wearing on me to the point I don't really want to play anymore. This game is a few minor fixes away from being amazing, but unfortunately they dropped the ball on a couple very basic aspects of any multiplayer game.I have two major issues.1. No native chat support of any kind2. Horrible matchmakingThe lack of chat was annoying, but it became unbearable as I started leveling my "doc" or medic class. The mechanics of the medic station are terrible to begin with, particularly with refilling it, but adding a team you can't communicate with and doesn't have detailed knowledge of how the station works makes the class completely broken and unplayable.There's a lot of other times when the lack of chat is noticeable, like before encounters or between rounds. It'd be nice to say "I want to play another, but give me 3 minutes to update my loadout", as opposed to everyone guessing how long we have before teammates start dropping. Or "don't start it yet, I want to put down mines" before an encounter.My issue with the matchmaking is the small windows you have and how quickly you have to react. I wish I could just search for players and not have bots populate after 40 seconds. Not have players drop at the last second and then I waste a good challenge card. Not have 1 player join, then get a bot and have to exit and join back hoping the other player will do the same thing just you can have a shot at a 3rd teammate.Honestly, just give me the option to disable bots and let the matchmaking search for players without all this extra effort and I'll flip my review back to positive. How hard can that be?Update: They fixed the issues I was complaining about, flipping review to positive. Still needs chat support.

_childDocuments_.review: 100/10 would recommend this to anyone who loves the Alien franchise.Audio is 10/10Gameplay is 10/10There is quite a good bunch of content so far, although it would be awesome if there is future plans to bring much more into it. I thoroughly enjoyed every chapter and the surrounding waves of Xeno's.My only issue(did have two but the other slowly dwindled away, which was the 3p limit) would probably be the fact you cannot give orders to the bots to say "hold down a position" or what not, like I understand it may add more "distractions" but there have been a few good times especially when doing intense and over and your bots just gracefully wonder right in front of you like a ballerina trying to get centre stage... _childDocuments_.review: I went in skeptical and bracing myself for a really low quality horde shooter with an Alien art job. Instead we got a fairly solid horde shooter with a great Alien art job.I was pleasantly surprised by what we got. It is not a horror game, but even on Standard difficulty there are frequently moments that fully encapsulate the GAME OVER MAN feel. There is a surprising amount of variety to the enemies and they throw new things at you often enough that you'll be guessing what horror is next throughout your first play through.Weapons feel punchy and satisfying and handle well. If you played and enjoyed Outriders (other than its bullet sponge enemies) or Mass Effect multiplayer, you'll feel right at home. There's a cover system as well, it's perfectly serviceable and I never found myself fighting with it.There's a tetris-style skill build system and a good amount of variety to loadouts, weapons, and attachments. It feels profoundly satisfying to toss off a salvo of micro-rockets from a shoulder launcher to wipe out an incoming horde of bursters and then wheel around with my smartgun to cut down a dozen xenos coming through the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ walls.The story is a serviceable homage to many facets of the Alien IP and while the in-mission storytelling is focused mostly on heat-of-the-moment objective stuff, there is a lot of fun background lore to flesh out the universe for those who enjoy that.Just finished a play through of all four episodes (3 missions per episode) on standard and while I was fully expecting to drop the game after I'd cleared the story, I'm excited to check out harder difficulties and the newly unlocked horde mode with my group tomorrow.

_childDocuments_.review: Cons: -12 maps, many of them visually similar-Just a basic horde mode and some consumable cards to add variety.Neutral:  -Just enough enemy variety to not get boring.  -The game is a little buggy, but they are clearly taking patching it seriously.  -The AI helpers are competent enough that soloing on normal difficulty isn't a chore.Pros: -Solid game mechanics.  The shooting feels good, the ability cooldowns encourage you to play aggressively.  -Weapons, for the most part, have their own niches and there are very few 'dead' weapons-Classes seem balanced enough.  Some abilities are more useful than others, but every class has something to offer.-The perk system gives a reason to level every class, and allows for some fun in making builds.-With season 1, we're seeing what they're adding, and it seems like it'll be a solid feed of new toys to play with.-Honestly, the writing and voice acting is a big bonus.  It's enough to keep you engaged, and the character dialogue is actually pretty fun.Bottom line: At 40 bucks, its a decent value proposition for the game you get, and a solid yes if you're looking for a 3rd person shooter that has fun co-op.  A definite must grab if on a steam sale, and If they add a second campaign with more map variety, it's a slam dunk yes at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Buy on sale. The game is good, but with how little content it  has it's more $20 worth of fun than it is $40 worth.Aside from being a faithful take on the Aliens experience, Aliens: Fireteam Elite is simply a good game. Is it a shot for shot adaptation of its source material? Certainly not, but I definitely felt like I was in at least some version of an Aliens world through and through. Its loot and combat only improve with time without asking players to mindlessly grind just to keep progressing. The obvious push towards co-op, as opposed to single-player, may be a bummer to some, but even those who venture into Xenomorph swarms on their own will have plenty to look forward to.Pros-------- Stays faithful to the Alien source material- Completely nails the aesthetic of Aliens- Intense combat action- Well-balanced classes- Multiple difficulties to suit all playersCons-------- Requires a full team of humans for the best experience- Enemy AI pathing is glaringly simplistic- Environments are lacking that 'Aliens have been here' look- Three players and five classes. Would have been better with a fourth player.- More mindless shooter than HorrorUltimately, Aliens: Fireteam Elite is more hit than miss. Although it does little to advance the survival shooter genre forward, Cold Iron Studio has done a great job of combining the familiar source material with fun, action-packed combat. The few flaws are merely a minor distraction and don’t mean game over, man!

You'd know each map by heart very quickly. ( I happen to like mindless grinding so that's why I have so many hours in this) -Very small playerbase so it's difficult to get a team-Some guns are worthless and certain ones like the rocket launcher and flamethrower are difficult to play with at the high levels since you can easily kill a teammate. - leveling up to a certain point just becomes pointless. -Weird glitches can cause you to fail the mission. - Certain cards to enhance the mission are actually awful and make the mission unplayable. Some positives are:-Great to play with your friends (even though it was short) -Cards can add sometimes interesting/challenging scenarios -Music and sound effects can be very nice, the guns are satisfying to shoot and weird for the most part.

_childDocuments_.review: I was really excited for this. I love Alien & Aliens, and after the disappointment that was Colonial Marines, anything would have been good. But sadly, this is a really shallow, boring game.I played through all 4 campaigns with one friend in 8 hours, and nearly got every gun, skin and costume. Neither of us are fans of repetition or when a game leans on repetition to pad out gameplay. We never replayed a single level and never died once even while using the challenge cards our deluxe copies gave the two of us. We would've replayed levels on difficulties above default/normal but all of the levels are flat and boring with scattered waist-high cover and re-skinned enemies (a la Destiny and its garbage). You don't even get to fight the queen at the end. The finale mission is a complete waste of your time as you can just abuse the hell out of the portable turrets your can bring into the mission with you. And if you want a story to compel you to keep playing, there isn't one. Due to the crap writing and mediocre voice acting (and lack of lipsync entirely), I literally skipped all of the text. The in-campaign dialogue is atrocious, often reaching Borderlands 2 (not BL3 thank Christ) levels of bad. Similar to the gameplay "loop," the cast repeats the same five callouts and event announcements over and over that I nearly quit just because they were so obnoxious.The game is designed like a grindy live-service title minus the teeth-grinding hallmarks of such. The levels are bland and all blur together but there really isn't anything to grind for because it is so easy to buy the best items at the start. There's the usual "all your equipped gear = your power level" like every other GAAS, except it's almost meaningless as is goes up naturally without that grind.This game isn't worth $40, let alone $60 for the deluxe. It is a $10 game with a $60 coat of paint meaninglessly splashed over it. There just isn't enough content to justify playing this for more than 8 hours, probably less if I didn't have to skip the paragraphs of worthless dialogue. Then they have the balls to release a $15 "expansion" with only one 3 mission campaign featuring the same re-skinned enemies and barely any new equipment that actually changes the way the game is played.Thank god I bought the deluxe on sale for like $25 because you shouldn't pay any more than that for the hollow experience you get.Edit: It blows my mind that people have put more than 10 hours into this (somebody put 1,000+ into this).

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of the series... Do yourself a favor and just hit that "Buy" button right now. This is an amazing experience for any Aliens fan in my opinion. To that last point I just want to say that I feel there are two types of authentic Xeno-experiences... The first being the spooky, being-stalked aspect that Aliens Isolation does so well. The other type of experience is hordes of Aliens coming at you in endless waves trying to overrun you that creates its own form of high-tension, high-intensity atmosphere. This game is definitely the latter.Honestly my favorite part of this game is the level design. You'll feel 100% like you're inside of an Aliens movie. Every set-piece is creepy and gorgeous. The last few levels when you're inside of the hive are my favorite. The aesthetic is just so true to the franchise. Bless you H R Geiger.For everyone else; this is a horde shooter with loot aplenty. There's 5 classes and more coming soon. Each class has their own perk trees and abilities. The varying playstyles are actually quite diverse. For example you can play a Technician and be a god-amongst-men during the hold-out segments with your turret but you can also play a Demolisher for the classic Smartgun (auto-targeting LMG) experience or just blow $@#% up constantly with rockets and grenades. The difficulty curve here is actually quite refreshing. It's pretty easy on the normal difficulties but it amps up quickly while giving you the equipment to handle the higher difficulties. I also appreciated the difference between fighting Synthetics with guns and playing more for cover as opposed to fighting Aliens that are constantly trying to get in your face. There's special types of each enemy combatant that switch it all up too. It's a really nice, fun mix of combat.Now to the Naysayers that never think anything is good enough...Yes, each mission basically plays the same way every time. It never bothered me in Left 4 Dead and it doesn't bother me here. What this game does well is gives you Challenge Cards if you want to add a little fun into the mix. You can make the hordes larger, you can make your guns have halved fire rate but doubled damage, you can make more exploders spawn, etc etc. Basically the replay-ability of this game lies within the challenge cards.I don't really get the minor consensus that this is a "dead game," honestly I've never had an issue finding co-op partners for the various missions. Personally I think this game has a pretty good shelf-life ahead of it. The first DLC Expansion was actually really nice.I personally think  but I'd understand if you bought it on sale too.If you're planning on playing it Solo I heartily recommend playing this game with the Modded AI. They're not going to be very good on the higher difficulties.So if you have no friends to play with then wait for a Sale. If you have a couple of Aliens nerds in your circle; this game will tickle all of your fancies.

_childDocuments_.review: After only 14hrs played, I can say the game is simply beautiful. IT'S ALIENS, MAN! I haven't been happy with the gaming scene lately, but this arrived just in time. If you love the Alien lore, you'll love this game for its aesthetics. Even the conversations with the characters are well written.I'm playing on a 9700k/2070S/64Gb RAM. The game is maxed out, at 1440p, and I have no issues with it, at all. I even turned on V-sync since I'm on a 60Hz monitor, and I'm not feeling any input lag. I only had one crash to desktop during a mission load.Whoever made the music for the game, absolutely nailed it. The way it creates the atmosphere in all the perfect spots during the missions is beautiful. I haven't felt like this in a long time.Sound engineering is, as well, on point. I can precisely tell where the enemy is coming from 100% of the time. No vagueness, no mushy audio, everything is clean, smooth and crispy.Linear levels (4 campaigns, 3 missions in each + Horde mode (enemies in waves)), 5 difficulties. Standard 3-player, over-the-shoulder 3rd person shooter, with a wide variety of weapons and customization, a kit (perk) system, specialty items and some cosmetics. If you're playing solo, you'll have bots with you that aren't actually dumb, as AI usually is. The weapons are 1:1 from the movies. The looks, the handling, the sounds... Beautiful!Communication:No voice or text chat, so it's hard to coordinate with randoms. However, on the other hand, it's nice to have a quiet and immersive time, instead of hearing someone's keyboard clacking, or kids screaming in the background, or just the general toxicity of people when a voice chat is a thing. Text chat would be a tough one, as the game only gives you the opportunity to relax for a few seconds, so chatting with others would be very challenging.Matchmaking:Even though there are around 13k players online, it's difficult to find players for anything above the Standard difficulty. It seems that the game is taking too many variables into account when matchmaking, so a Quickplay option would be a nice addition to have.Camera:There needs to be an option for FOV or just a camera distance from the player, because, for me, it's too close to the character, hiding most of the screen. An addition of a 1st person camera might also be a good idea.Overall, I recommend the game. It's too much fun! More stuff will be added in the near future, so it might even get better. No MTX, thank you! However, there might be some cosmetic DLCs.

_childDocuments_.review: Whilst this game is by no means perfect, it has compelled me to write a review for those sitting on a fence about it.  Like a lot of you, I was sitting on the fence contemplating whether I should jump in or wait for a sale before committing.  My friend who was adamant I join was kind enough to send me a copy. He knew I was very selective about my games.  Since then, I have thanked him many times.  Gosh, this game is exciting and the RPG lite elements of upgrading your guns and gear has got me hooked.  The main game is a 3 person squad horde shooter. This is where the Devs have got it right.  They put all their available resources into making the main game enjoyable.  It feels to me that the AI is programmed to overun your defensive position.  Every engagement feels exciting and hard fought.  If you don't have a friend to play with, you will be accompanied by two Ai's that are decent.  You don't feel that you're carrying them that much at lower difficulty settings and the game can be completed with them as your wingmen.  You just have to pull your weight a bit more.This Game feels refreshing and gives you excitement that you may not have felt since LFD1-2.  I would give it a 9/10 for pure horde shooting.  Now it's not perfect, there are still random bugs here and there but I've only ran into them once in my 9hrs of playtime. There was a valve in act 1 stage 2 that was stuck at 100% and didn't move so I had to exit stage and re-q.  Other than that it's been plain sailing.  If you're looking for a horde shooter, this is the sleeper hit you've never heard of.  B4B or WWZ has nothing on this game.  Now if the devs could add more content such as guns and modes as well as iron out the bugs, I don't think this game will be a game that will tide you over till bf2042, rather a game you will play for as long as LFD1-2.  Well done and keep up the good work DEVS! It's close to perfect, but we need more variety!

2202. A mysterious distress call reroutes your Marine Assault Unit to LV-895 in the outer colonies, where deadly Xenomorph legions, hidden corporate secrets, and ancient alien ruins await your arrival. Set in the iconic Alien universe, Aliens: Fireteam is a cooperative third-person survival shooter that drops your fireteam of hardened marines into a desperate fight to contain the Xenomorph threat. Face off against waves of terrifying Xenomorph and Weyland-Yutani Synthetic foes alongside two players or AI teammates, as you and your fireteam desperately fight your way through four unique campaigns that introduce new storylines to the Alien universe. Create and customize your own Colonial Marine, choosing from an extensive variety of classes, weapons, gear and perks, battling overwhelming odds in this heart-pounding survival shooter experience.

THE ULTIMATE HUNT
Play a pivotal role in the epic events that occur 23 years after the original Alien trilogy as a Colonial Marine stationed aboard the USS Endeavor, battling terrifying Xenomorph threats.

SURVIVE THE HIVE
Face overwhelming odds against over 20 enemy types, including 11 different Xenomorphs along the evolutionary scale from Facehuggers to Praetorians, each designed with their own intelligence to ambush, outsmart and eviscerate vulnerable marines.

CUSTOMIZE YOUR FIRETEAM
Choose from five unique classes - Gunner, Demolisher, Technician, Doc and Recon - each with their own special abilities and character perks. Utilize an extensive arsenal of 30+ weapons and 70+ mods/attachments in your effort to eradicate the Alien threat.
