_childDocuments_.review: Sorry, I had a need for Speedy Gonzales, if you get my drift.Enough with the jokes though. Let's talk Horizon 5.First things first, if you enjoyed Forza Horizon 4 you will enjoy this title as well.Horizon 5 is easily the best racing game available on PC at the moment but it has its issues and it has a lot of them. Some are minor and some are pretty huge.I had my review ready when the game was released. I hold off posting this review because I wanted to give developers some time to fix some of the stuff. Nothing has been done so far. In fact, the number of issues has grown. It's absurd.  A full list of cross-platform and PC-only issues is at the end of the review. The list is HUGE. EDIT: The list is so big Steam says my review is 13, 264 characters too long so I will post a list of Steam related issues only.I got in four days early and put around 40+ hours into the game in four days. Now, a week later, I have only 67 hours of playtime. Why?Connectivity issues. I had this in my "early access" period as well but it wasn't as bad and I thought it would be addressed and fixed by the time the game was released. I was wrong. It has gotten so bad I have not been able to play online AT ALL. As soon as I start up the game I get disconnected. I might be able to stay connected for five seconds maximum and it has been like that for the past 7 days at least. It has been frustrating.EDIT: It has now been 17 days since I was able to connect to ForzaLife (online). I've tried around 10 different fixes, the game has patched itself 2-3 times and each time they have claimed to fix the connectivity issue but it's all just lies. Nothing works. Beware!Why am I giving this game a positive review? Because it's still fun to play solo and it has hundreds of hours of singleplayer content in it. Just be warned: As of now singleplayer might be the only thing you are able to do and that includes not being able to do seasonal objectives and unlocking cars in those seasons.Alright. That's out of the way so let's get to what I originally wrote about Forza Horizon 5:If you're new to the Forza franchise then Horizon is the more arcade-y spin-off of Forza Motorsport. Motorsport is a proper sim-cade/sim racer depending on how you want to play it.Horizon is an open-world arcade racer where you can do whatever you want and progress however you want. Now when I say it's an arcade racer, it is, but it's also important to knowthat you can turn off all the assists, turn on realistic damage, set the AI to the impossible difficulty, and enjoy a more sim-like experience.The Horizon series offers you everything you would want in a racing game: Car tuning, upgrading, and customization, a huge open-world map with different areas to free roam in, all kinds of different race types from drag and street racing to off-road dirt racing and user-made custom tracks. Oh, I should also mention there are quite a few different radio stations available to almost every kind of taste... Almost. The rock radio station is a bit lacking and plays more pop/pop-rock songs than actual rock tracks but it's still pretty decent.Car selection is bigger than ever as well. Forza Horizon 5 launched with 534 different cars with many more on the way. Yes, it's true Horizon 4 had over 700 cars in the end but that's with all the expansions and updates. Let me remind you that Forza Horizon 4 launched with just over 400-450 cars so give Horizon 5 a little bit more time and we will eventually have even more vehicles available than in the predecessor.Now let's talk about the online portion of the game a little bit.Forza Horizon 5 is a great singleplayer game with tons of content but there is also a huge load of co-op and multiplayer content on offer.Every race you see on your world map can be played in an online co-op with your friends but you can simply queue for player vs AI co-op races as well.On the competitive side we have the "Eliminator" which is a battle royale with cars, your usual casual and ranked street, dirt, and other races, and a playground in which two teams of players compete against each other in zombie modes, capture the flag and a few other modes.The open-world map also has "arcade" events in which players either have to drift or do other kinds of stunts to rack up scores together and earn Forzathon Points. Forzathon Points  can be spent on cars in an online Forzathon Shop. The shop is currently unavaible.Now talking of online, I actually have a couple of issues with it. Actually, one issue to be perfectly honest. You can choose to roam your map in solo mode or online mode, in which you see other players drive around and join the open-world arcade events that appear on the map from time to time. Now the issue with this is that I've had quite a lot of problems.The first 5 hours were hell for me. I got disconnected several times in a minute. In ONE MINUTE! The issue is not on my side. My internet connection is solid. It has gotten better but I'm still experiencing connectivity issues so beware of that.That's my only issue so far. Other than that the game is great. The performance? Absolutely brilliant? The game runs at a solid 100 frames per second with every setting maxed out and at 1440p. RTX 2080 super, i9-10900K, 32GB RAM, and with this hardware getting 100 fps at 1440p with every setting on extreme/ultra I can't complain. Runs better than I expected and the game is a real eye candy.I have experienced some graphical glitches here and there but nothing serious so they have not bothered me at all.Definitely worth the full price! Next season will have the DeLorean as one of the seasonal awards so hop on board, get driving, and enjoy the festival with crazy cars, crazier people, and even crazier stunts!STEAM Related Issues     Players may be experiencing performance degradation after extended time playing due to memory issues    There are flickering water reflections on low spec PC with AMD graphics card    Car dials have a "white-ish" texture and are blurred when car is moving on AMD card with integrated Radeon graphics    PC - While using 'Alt+Enter' combination the Title still reads 'Enter' button as an input    Upon changing hardware the game doesn't ask you if you want to re-run the graphics setup.    Clicking buttons with the mouse can trigger the wrong action    Capturing the video using Xbox Game Bar with Scaled display in Windows result in partially black recording    PC - UMA video memory is not supported    At first launch in game resolution does not match the Windows resolution    Game window is partially obscured when launching in full screen mode    Turning off screen effects in the menu does not turn off chromatic aberration    PC - Chromatic aberration get very extreme with ultra wide resolutions    PC - User is not messaged to download media pack on Windows N version (windows 10 and 11)    Tabbing out during launch will cause window to open cut off in bottom right of screen    Steam - Mouse Cursor is stuck on screen at all times    Some car elements have missing transparency on PC with AMD GPU    DRS on PC can cause GTAO depth issues at high resolution    Texture rendering issues on PC for terrain and vegetation when using Resolution Scaling On    Players my get an e:1047-0 Invalid Save error message    Players my get an e:1045-0 Invalid Save error message    Horizontal stripes on road when SSAO is enabled    Graphics artifacts on screen edge at 3440x1440 resolution (Ultrawide)

Compared to Horizon 4 (stopped playing after horizon 5 launch and had almost full car collection not counting FE), the grind was not that very scary, you could just do anything and still manage to get millions without noticing it. For this title, right now skill points are limited to 10 while (if I remember correctly) forza 4 didn't had this limitation, rewards become definitely smaller (rewards are a joke right now) and drivavatars are so overpowered that it's impossible to drive normally and you have no other choice but ram to them and just slide with walls to pass them and hopefully finish first. Maybe it needs some time for drivavatars to learn tracks and so on, but it really makes them look unnatural when they are unmovable and have unlimited grip and acceleration that makes you frustrated. I haven't tried multiplayer that much but I heard that there exists cheaters (at least I haven't met one). And at least for me I don't see any point anymore to play further this game. It become just logging in for Forzathon event, get points to receive event featured cars and wait another week for another event, just like other gatcha game...Talking about graphics, it looks really gorgeous... if you watch a youtube video of someone playing this game on console. I'm using GTX 1080 and I tried so many solutions, but it still looks very crappy, Draw distance are very noticeable that it's just pain to look at it and overall I don't really see anything special. Forza 4 on the other hand looks better than this on my machine, so I'm guessing this is a issue with PC release because I'm not the only one with these kind of "features".Overall, I would not recommend this game for now, better buy forza 4 on sale (if they didn't nuke progression like they did for forza 5). I can't see a really good future for this game with these kind of changes, so my suggestion for developers would be fix their priorities, fix graphical bugs, fix AI, make game more enjoyable and worth your time so we could have a reason to play it every day (no heavy grind please).

_childDocuments_.review: Playground Game's beloved arcade-styled open world celebration of cars and insufferable festival dialogue written by middle aged people desperately trying to find the pulse of youth culture is back, trading the damp back roads of the UK for the volcanic mountains, swamps and deserts of Mexico. Forza Horizon 5 has taken everything Playground Games learned over the continuous development of Forza Horizon 4 and has remixed the flow of the game, in some ways for the better while in others the game falters.  Playground Games has eschewed fans demands for a Horizon game set in Japan, instead crafting an open world inspired by the varied terrain of Mexico. This game world is larger and more varied than  Forza Horizon 4's, offering the long stretches of highway, twisty mountain passes, long straight drag strips and plenty of water, mud and sand for players to plow through. It's richly detailed and gorgeous, which makes hunting down the fast travel and experience granting collectibles less of a chore than it may seem like on paper. In somewhat of a departure from previous Horizon games, there isn't really a traditional major metro urban area in the game, instead the game features a small city with labyrinthine streets and tunnels which is an interesting change and allows for some really interesting more technical races. Progression in Forza Horizon 5 is a remix of previous games, allowing players to ultimately construct multiple horizon outposts that represent each style of racing present in the game (road races, street races, offroad races, cross country races and PR Stunts) and within each outpost there are a handful of unlockable activities. In order to unlock these outposts and their activities, players must obtain accolades. Accolades are available for almost any activity in the game: online races, creating liveries and tunes, taking photos, free roam driving and of course winning races. No matter how you choose to spend your time in Horizon, you will make forward progress which allows any type of player to see the entirety of the main game. Unfortunately this is a two edged sword, the game doens't really feel like it builds to much of anything. Unlocking everything means entering the hall of fame and unlocking a new series of accolades as well as Trial challenges. If you are one of those players that wishes Horizon would force you to start with a clapped out hooptie and climb the economic ladder, your prayers haven't been answered here. Horizon 5 throws cars and credits at it's players constantly, but with so much content, completionists will appreciate this fact.The driving in FH5 feels much the same as previous games and that is fine by me. Each car feels distinct based on it's drivetrain layout: mid engine cars handle differently than front engine cars, front wheel drive cars tend to understeer, all wheel drive cars launch incredibly and hold traction well in a variety of terrain but understeer, rear wheel drive cars are prone to spinning if proper care isn't exercised. It's the perfect balance of realism and arcade, whereas cars Need for Speed and The Crew feel roughly the same with some cars simply being faster than others, you will fall in love with specific cars in Forza Horizon basewd on the way they compliment your strengths and weaknesses behind the wheel. The faint tinge of realism also makes the game world more compelling to navigate. The rest of FH5's online robust offerings fall prey to the same headaches as they always have: cooperative modes as plagued by drivers who don't understand that they are on a team and will ram you, playground games are usually spoiled by half of one team dropping out as soon as they feel they won't win, etc. The Eliminator modes returns, it was a late addition to FH4 and is a car based battle royale which is interesting but I don't feel terribly compelled to endure the long match making times in order to continually play it.With over 700 cars (the team at Playground Games is continually adding more), a wide variety of races and challenges, custom livery design, custom tuning and plenty of online modes, Forza Horizon 5 is a very strong package that remixes the elements of previous games in a way that is largely a step forward and keeps the experience fresh. There is simply no substitute for Horizon. It's imperfect, a little cheesy at times and is not breaking new ground, but for a fan like me, it hasn't grown stale either... If you love cars and can't be bothered with the technical demands of sim racers, you can't do any better than Forza Horizon 5.

_childDocuments_.review: Actually there is not much to say about Forza Horizon. Hands down it is the best arcade racing  game present. Playground Games did not risk to spoil the formula which brought success and cash to them in previous titles and without any serious rivals forcing them towards greater innovation they only added some new features to it . But this does not stop giving gamers the itch to play "one more race" in each playthrough.Here in FH5 you will be in Mexico which has a bigger and more colorful map with stunning vistas compared to FH4's "a bit too sterile" Britain . It is so huge and and there are overwhelming things to do, so many that the finish line of one race is likely quite close to the starting gate of another.  The map is positively littered with icons  -more than any Assassin's Creed game:)-  so filter will be your friend. -But still I can't help myself thinking Japan would be a better choice instead:)- Overall compared to FH4 the game looks better, sounds better. Apart from seasons now there are day/night changes, weather activites like sandstorms/tropical rain. You will not get bored easily since there will always be a lot of things to accomplish and game will steadily reward you for that forever.Keep in mind that this is an arcade racing game, it does not require a steep learning curve how to drive. If you want to exprerience a more serious racing sim you may go for Assetto Corsa or Project Cars instead. Yet still with lots of cars to unlock, nice setting and custimization options, fun activities and endless action FH5 is an open world racing dream for every player.Whether you are a racing fan or not you will like this game.Enjoy your ride..

_childDocuments_.review: When I had 43.7 hours in the game:For the first time I was playing it, it felt like a Forza Horizon 4 but on another island. I love Forza games, and it was very disappointing to see this, but I just kept playing.. I needed to realise that this game was WAY MORE than I thought! This game is one of the best.The game has a story line which is a bit weird and not the best, but this is a racing game. It doesn't need a good story, because you make your own stories and memories in the game.It is very fun with friends and it is one of the best games to play if there is only 2-3 friends available.The game's story had a rough beginning (specially on Steam), but don't make false assumptions.. just like how I did..When I had 498 hours in the game:It is exactly a Forza Horizon 4 copy! The same cars, sounds, everything.. The Premium Edition is a joke as you need to buy 4+ DLCs to actually get everything, which bumps the price above £100! Especially that it was advertised as "It includes ALL DLCs"None of the cars are/feel "special" as every car is easy to get. You get a Regera if you complete EVERY accolade in the game, you can also get the Regera from the shop.. The map doesn't feel that it is almost 3 times larger. And also it doesn't really make sense, a desert next to a rain forest.. The developers removed Ranked, so Online races feel like bumper car. And also cheaters are way bigger problem than I thought.In Horizon 4 Trials were a challenge and most of the time only competent players did it.. In Horizon 5 almost every new player does it. So if you don't have at lest 3 decent racer friends prepare to do it several times to finally complete it.. Why is there no restriction on Trials to only allow players join who has won against Unbeatable difficulty? Just buy Forza Horizon 4.. It is cheaper, better and looks almost the same as this..At this point I am really convinced that Forza Horizon is going to go down on the path of F1 games.. just the same game every year with somewhat improved graphics.. If they are not going to listen to the community, I am not going to buy the next Forza game.. even if I loved playing/was a huge fan of the Forza series..

_childDocuments_.review: This is a review for the Hot Wheels DLC, which I recently finished.I was so excited to experience a Hot Wheels DLC after missing out on FH3, but this DLC is just not good.I've seen a lot of people complain that the DLC is bad because it's just full throttle all the time, but I actually think that's one of its strengths. Hot Wheels is meant to be all about super high speeds and gravity defying layouts. The real problem is that Hot Wheels Park has absolutely terrible flow. It seems like absolutely zero thought was put into the layout of the map. Honestly, did the devs even playtest this DLC? Off the top of my head, here are some examples of track sections with bad design:> Sideways track (non-magnetic) that is too banked, so gravity pulls you towards the guard rail and you lose all your speed> Braking zones over a crest where there is low grip, so you crash into the guard rail and lose even more speed than is necessary> Uphill / almost vertical acceleration zones, where you take ages to build speed while the AI powers on and easily overtakes you> The half-pipe, which has absolutely no grip when you are not on the racing line, making it extremely boring to drive through> Extremely inconsistent physics on magnetic track, resulting in unpredictable car handling and acceleration> Sharp turns or heavy braking zones placed right after blind sections of track (like a loop) which are impossible to foresee so you just slam into the barrier (but the AI is programmed to take it perfectly)> The fact that you can't complete loops in most low cars because the force pushing you into the track is so great that the bottom of your car literally clips through the floor, losing you speedAnother problem with the DLC is the Hot Wheels Academy which is supposed to be the main attraction. Who on earth thought it would be a good idea to lock you out of using FAST CARS in HOT WHEELS and force you to use crappy slow cars that can barely go up a ramp? Not only does this make progression annoying, but it also just breaks the game. Even after becoming a Hot Wheels legend and unlocking X-class cars, certain maxed out cars (e.g. FE Sesto, BTTB) are UNUSABLE in Hot Wheels Park because their hidden PI rating is too high and the game thinks your Academy Rating is too low so it forces you to change car...Another big letdown with this DLC is the track builder. The opening race is - sadly - the best part of the DLC, because it takes you around the whole map and they even spend all this time explaining all the cool new track pieces (which is unfortunately plagued with cringe Forza dialogue). For some reason, however, they don't let you use ANY of these in Eventlab??? All you can do is place orange track, crossroads, and boosters... No Air Track, no Ice Track, no Water Flume, no Magnet Track, no Halfpipe. Oh yeah on the topic of massive disappointments, I should also mention that the Hot Wheels Goliath is garbage. It's meant to be the flagship race of the DLC but instead of taking you through the cool parts of the map it's just a mindless cruise around the perimeter with a few loops thrown in here and there. The weekly A-class event around the Ice Cauldron was more fun than the Goliath, which is saying a lot considering how often these weekly events are mind-numbingly boring.To top it all off, the racing is awful. The pre-made races are extremely short and like usual in Forza, you start right at the back. This makes it impossible to win at higher AI difficulties because there's isn't enough time to overtake everyone unless you ram into them early on. In addition to this, the track is narrow and the guardrail on both sides prevents you from dipping your wheels into the dirt to try and get past as is possible in the base game. Add to this the myriad of track layout issues I mentioned earlier and you get a recipe for disaster.Epic fail.

But suffice it to say, Forza Horizon 5 is hands down the most entertaining game I've ever played. So, if you're looking for a good time and a chance to flex your virtual driving muscles, this game is definitely for you.

So I won't write a review, I'll write a comparison for someone like I used to be, someone who played older Forzas and is hesitating whether to buy this new installment...Closest comparison to make is of course Forza Horizon 4, which I played for more than 400 hours through gamepass.MAP: Mexico is way bigger, or feels like it but also feels empty... so many deaf spots on the map. Scotland was way better map in my opinion.GRAPHICS: Nothing really changed, FH was always perfect and 5th game is no different. I love graphics on both game, FH5 is slightly improved of course.GAMEPLAY: Horizon seasons.. what is there to say.. both games has different systems, both games works well.. I can say I like FH5 seasons more because of requirements but I wish there were more of them.. specific country and level contains still many many cars. I gotta lift up new and new seasons, new cars, new rewards every month.Overall: FH5 is better in many ways, but you won't enjoy it if you won't get used to constantly crashing on driftwood in jungles or miles of empty deserts with no real use... UK in FH4 was way more charming.

_childDocuments_.review: It truly saddens me that I have to leave this negative of a review on a game that had so much potential. I've been a fan of the Forza titles since Motorsport 2 and I feel like their early titles just nailed it on the head. (Especially Forza Motorsport 4) I'll start with the positive. Visually the game is unbeatable. The graphics of the cars, map and visual effects are amazing. The lighting, reflections and car details really were emphasized in this game. The driving is also pretty damn nice. It feels very natural and the cars don't feel too heavy or light on the road. The credit system in the game is quite nice as it does reward you and allows you to either grind out races to earn money and level up or you can simply drive around and enjoy the amazing map that is offered. The overall car collection is nice as they do have a massive selection. Now for the downside! While the selection of cars is massive, the fact that obtaining some cars is completely based on chance or completing too many challenges that are temporary. This is absolutely ridiculous. One used to be able to grind out races or simply pay for certain special car but now it leaving it up to chance or an insane point system that requires so much grinding for little chance or opportunity to obtain certain cars. It is infuriating how damn greedy and pointless this system is. It's so discouraging and its made me give up on this game. I've put so much time but there is never a point where you have all the cars you'd like. Its excessive. I wouldn't recommend buying this unless you get it on sale or simply have too much time on your hands. The devs need to do better. Maybe follow the old formula that Motorsport 4 had. The festivals are fun and bring life to the game but the making cars nearly impossible to obtain just ruins it for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Hands down, the best driving game I've played in my history so far.And my experience dates back to 1990's with Top Gear 2 as my first game.This game offers so much, but I will talk about my main source of interest: Online racing.Short version - AMAZING.:: Online play ::The driving experience this "simcade" offers, is unmatched by any other driving game. It is so much fun trying to do the "perfect" corner, and it always shows. You win or lose on literally every curve you get good or bad. Somewhere you shave half a second or more, and on other places you lose.. it all depends on you, and your opponent racers of course.Some people love clean racing (myself included), but some like to give a little bumps, and it's all part of the game.This game also got "high-speed collision prediction" which makes you ghost through someone who crashed or who wants to ram you when speeding. Which is IMHO brilliant mechanic!Also, ghosting 10s from starting grid is genius as well, and lets you make your position through the grid without problems of raming (deliberate or non deliberate).So far i've driven 16 cars (out of roughly 700 or even more that this game offers), and in A800 class, racing seems quite balanced, and I havent noticed ANY "meta" car, and only minor differences which are really neglectable and can be ironed out by good tuning.. Really every car i've driven is viable, and it's all about your skill to detect that "apex" of the curve, and react accordingly.STRONG recommendation, and a very VERY solid gaming experience for me. Not just driving experience, but GAMING experience in all! It's recommended for all the competitive gamers, and those that wish to have fun.:: Graphics and photo mode::Another aspect that this game simply out shines EVERY other game by a kilometer! (im using metric system)When you take a "screenshot" you can set up your shot in a very professional manner, and even change the time of the day, and weather while doing so! I cant stress enough how good of a feature this is! Even though game itself is breath taking beautiful, it is very OPTIMIZED and will run without any problems even on my system (nVidia 1070 / ryzen 5 2600)Those are my 2 cents.I hope you enjoyed and agreed to most of my review.Cheers, see you on road racing!

_childDocuments_.review: 8.9 hours, not including my offline playtime. I'm able to play it on Extreme setting with Raytracing on High (highest) settings with above 75 FPS average on 1080p (usually sitting in between 70-99 FPS) on my RTX 3060. _childDocuments_.review: FH5 is a really great game. But I can't recommend it, because for me it's horizon 4 with a new map.I think the game mostly improved in the areas where it was already good, and became only worse in it's weak spots.So at this moment I believe that it makes more sense to buy horizon 4 with discount.Pros:Basically all the pros of horizon 4, so I keep it short.+ Graphics is great.+ Car sounds are good. Soundtrack is okay.+ Plenty of cars.+ Flexible tuning.+ Large map.Cons:- No feeling of progression at all. Game just throws at you the best cars in first 20 hours of gameplay. You can open almost everything from a wheelspins without do a single race. In a race game.- AI. Maybe it was the same in Horizon 4, but in this game it looks so fake. Many times I have a situation when I overtake all the drivatars, and they just form a train and ride like this (one after another on exactly the same line) till the finish. So they don't even try to imitate the real race and competition. And yes, they don't care about the game physics. If race has a jumps or water in it, drivatars have a huge advantage, because the terrain doesn't affect their cars.- "YoU'rE a SuPeRsTaR!!!111". It is way too much this time. All these radio announcements sound so unnatural, you are praised for absolutely everything. They don't reward, they just cause facepalms.- Stories are mostly meaningless and dialogs are weird. In one of the stories there is a phrase like "Why people don't like sandstorms?! They're so fun!". I mean there should be a line somewhere in being so optimistic and positive, right? Horizon has so great potential for a proper singleplayer campaign, but it's just a waste of time now.- Constant interruptions. New adventure! New wheelspin! New level after a race! Dancing before the race (WHY?)! Dancing after a race (WHY?)!- I can't say much about the online, because it constantly disconnects me, I was able to complete only a few races. And I still can't find an option to find a race in a specific class. It's so frustrating. Why I can't choose a race type and a car class so I can drive my favourite car in online race?

Freedom is nice but let's be a little real here, a supercar that is 1" off the ground is never gonna go over dirt roads and go launching off mountains. _childDocuments_.review: FH5 is both amazing and right on the mark, as well as an outstanding swing and a miss for me. What i mean by this is the game play and map are amazing, the visuals are Great and the overall fun factor and amount of content for the game is outstanding. With this being said the Musical choices, Understanding of Car Culture and certain aspects of the open world miss the mark entirely. The positives outweigh the negatives here by a large margin however the negatives are annoying enough to be spoken about first and foremostCON; #1 the soundtrack;though music is subjective i feel that the entire soundtrack in this game is literally the worst licensed soundtrack in a game possibly ever. its full of generic bass, screatcing, "Goingingingnging" and other obnoxious music made up entirely of compilations of sounds that should not be used to make the music of a car game. Gone are the days of the GOD teir soundtracks of old midnight clubs and Need For Speeds. and even worse it has no way to turn off all in game music :( CON; #2 Car People;I cant talk for the games accuracy with the Mexican Culture but i can for the car culture.... WRONG.... I would count myself as an intermediate car enthusiast, i work on my own car a bit, ive been to lots of car meets and one or two track days and this game does not at all in the slightest get any of the street racing or legal racing or enthusiast culture or lingo even close to correct. THIS IS FINE how ever in their attempts to reflect real car culture it comes across cringe. CON; #3 - The big oneFORZATHON LIVE NEEDS TO BE DELETED. it pops up infront of you out of nowhere and takes you out of gameplay and you cant opt out. it pops up literally on the most popular roads on the map and you cannot avoid it so you have to do different events. it pops up everywhere and if your car so much as skimms the bubble of it the game forces you to participate in the event and it is the worst aspect of this game by far. there is also other issues with the monthly events such as championships not allowing you to compete in single races that month if those are championship racesIf you can deal with the above issues i would highly recommend this game as it is one of the best arcade driving experiences youll have; Even at 99.95NZD this is an absolute must have even though itll make you deaf, cringe and pull your hair out.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just a very good repeat of all the other forza games, 90% same cars, same short boring stories(no offense lol) and above average graphics. I liked forza horizon 4 alot, as the seasons where so beautiful, and the online experience racing on the highway or meeting friends was way easier. Alot of people would disagree with me on this but i wish forza horizon 5 had a smaller map..... Its harder to meet players on the open world experience than previous games.. And the online mini games are the same.They promised more customization with cars... But i didn't see a difference from FH4 for the most part in that category, but the cars do sound better, like WAY better. You know im a big fan of realism, and to be honest i really don't enjoy the map... The developers did a awesome job of highlighting the forest and desert areas(offroad), but the city and street life in nonexistent.... In forza horizon 4 there was more variety, you could fit in perfectly with a lambo in a upper class area of the city or drive a old beater in a rural road. Now its like im driving a 2 million dollar lambo through little village dirt roads to go to my little beach loft lmao like doesnt feel realistic. The developers only focused on the off road aspect of the game taking 80% of the map with mostly rural roads, then leave a little village for the streetlife and street races. If your a big fan of offroading and offroad races then you would probably like this.. But if your like me and like some need for speed action, or some nice city to rip up in a lambo... Then this game isnt for you. Theres alot of politics in this game too.... People getting banned for livery or the wrong stickers on their car, but cheaters not getting banned. The developers are slow to addressing issues with online cheating, but quick to ban anyone using "hate speech" and doing grey area petty things. I dont really care about these issues personally, but these issues seem to be getting worse with each game.Get this game on a sale, and try it out.... or theres always forza horizon 4 :)

_childDocuments_.review: Before I'll jump into ripping it apart, let me get the good things about FH5 (in contrast to FH4) out of the way first:- You can now tune any car for any type of race. This expands possibilities and diversifies car selection for all types of races but did you ever want to bring a typical track car for a rally or offroad race and perform better than dedicated cars?- The game uses improved driving physics and feedback. The throttle and brake triggers now vibrates whenever you're at the brink of losing grip or locking up brakes. It makes FWD and RWD cars much more pleasant to drive and viable too (also thanks to improved driving model).- This one seems opinionated but rallying and cross country seems much better than it was in FH4, at least for me. - Still no microtransactions.That's pretty much it.Forza Horizon franchise is not a game that focuses solely on racing. It's a CAR GAME first and foremost and that's what killing it, not necessarily due to said focus but rather due to the game engine it's running on. Stemming from Forza Motorsport franchise, the Horizon games don't feel as arcadey as many other games in the genre, which in turn it could have been a very solid open-world racing experience IF IT HAD FOCUS (on racing preferably). However, the brilliant folks at PGG believed it'd be a better idea to push the game as this kiddie bullsh*it "do whatever you want" car game.FH5 has no true focus. Every mode it features is very bare bones. No mode is sophisticated to keep you invested for long. The only thing keeping me going is the core gameplay, tuning and Festival Playlist, being pretty much the only thing that motivates you to play as partaking in these events rewards you with newly added/returning cars. Starting my experience with FH4 at its near end of support stage, I was really hoping for so much more. Sadly, the game is outright a regression and here are my personal reasons for it:- Worst AI yet- Trials no longer use Unbeatable difficulty AI- There are no longer Trials in DLC maps. Instead, there are Horizon Tours which are absolute garbage.- DLC maps now feature only 1 (albeit unique each time) Seasonal Championship. FH4 had 3 unique for each season though unchanging.- Inability to host lobby races also greatly reduced my will to play and reason to tune for potentially more exotic class-car category combinations set by other players or myself.- Heavy gameplay imbalance due to mostly power-focused track design forcing to use powerbuilds is generally unappealing to me. Love using them but would hate to use only them...- DLC worlds are much worse. Hotwheels is a snoozefest and once completed there's no reason coming back, unless you love driving on highways. The Badlands is a bit better though...- Updates focus mostly on bullsh*it like expanded photomode, longer night times, sh*tty tie-ins like with Extreme E, Donut Media (and any update that adds Story-focused activities that are extremely boring). How about adding new modes, like Custom Championships, hm?- Stellantis unintentionally made FH5 an even worse experience without its brands present but it appears those brands will return on August 17th?- Further proving the kiddie approach with its DLCs (LEGO, Hotwheels). Even Barbie had to invade the game and it's exactly what all those automotive fans wanted, right? No data bloating has ever taken place and I'm Extremely, Eh... sure of it.So, yeah. From my POV, while FH4 co-exists, the supposed newer entry in FH franchise, this one sucks real hard.

_childDocuments_.review: Originally bought FH5 because my 10 year old son wanted it. He played it for a while he convinced me to give it a try after learning that my real life daily drive was in the game (Fiesta ST). Since then, I've totally fallen in love with the game. We currently have 227 hours and I (dad) probably have more of those than he does. It's been a great father/son bonding activity. Part of what keeps it fun is that the developers are continually adding fresh new content to keep the game from getting dull. There's always something new to do. Possibly best of all, as an open world you can play the game any way you'd like. Like street races in supercars? Like off roading on ATVs? Like painting cars and designing custom looks? Just want to chill and go for a casual drive cross country? Like the challenge of PvP or prefer to keep it strictly offline with AI? It's totally up to you. The only critiques I have are minor and are likely the result of it being a console port. We live in an era where things are regularly released with game-breaking bugs in the knowledge that the public will pay the developer to do their beta testing for them. If interface annoyances are the worst thing to complain about in a title, that's probably a good thing!The FH5 user interface and keyboard shortcuts are all over the place and make zero sense. Some menus you have to randomly hit some special key to continue and no mouse click will do it. One time it might be "push 7 to confirm" then another time it's the enter key or the space bar. Sometimes you can mouse click the confirmation, other times not. There's no consistency. To start the game you have to tell it 3 separate times that you're really sure you want to play the game. First, run it in steam. Once that loads you get a splash screen where you tell it yeah I really want to start now. Then it does more loading until yet another splash where you have to hit continue for it to finish loading into the actual game. I've customized the buttons on our steering wheel. I have to go into settings and manually change it from default Logitech binding group to my "custom 1" binding group EVERY SINGLE GAME. All of these are minor annoyances that you get used to eventually. I'm 44 now and have enjoyed PC gaming since the Commodore 64. I have fond memories of Half-Life coming out as a new game. Now my sons are both in love with Black Mesa and reliving a game franchise I enjoyed long before they were born. Point is, I've been around a while and played a lot of PC games.That said, I'd put Forza Horizon 5 is the top 5 games I've ever played.  Highly recommended for any gamer from casual to hardcore.

_childDocuments_.review: Forza Horizon 5 is not a leap over the previous Horizon game, but considering that Horizon 4 was already an excellent game, it doesn't need to be. It takes nearly everything that worked about Horizon 4 and introduces a much larger, more varied, and overall better world to explore and some semblance of structure to its "campaign" progression. The racing is as good as it's ever been, the new Horizon Stories have some fun conceits, and the expeditions, while small in number and easily finished off in the opening hours of the game, do sometimes slow down in ways the game doesn't usually foster. It does carry over some UI issues from 4, however, and as of the time of writng, there are many issues regarding servers and performance.Still, this is an excellent game that I'm confident will keep me coming back for the next few years.

_childDocuments_.review: Forza Horizon 5 is an impressive racing game that offers a stunning open-world environment, with an impressive level of detail and realism. The graphics are top-notch, and the vast map provides players with endless exploration opportunities. The car roster is diverse, and the customization options are extensive, allowing players to make their vehicles truly unique. Additionally, the game's multiplayer mode is enjoyable and allows for seamless co-op play. However, the game can feel overwhelming for new players, and the handling of some of the vehicles can be challenging to master. Overall, Forza Horizon 5 is an excellent addition to the series and a must-play for any racing game enthusiast.

_childDocuments_.review: The game has a small map. It should take at least an hour to go from one end to the other, but the map should be detailed and diverse as well as large. More than half of the map is empty. Instead of flat, empty lands, map should be designed with lands connected to the city or couple cities together. Diverse roads and enjoyable views makes gameplay so much fun, Horizon series has always came close to achieving it. I play the game for Its open world but it feels empty and lifeless, there isn't much to explore. It should give you the feeling of a road trip, that's the point of open world. Think about a long coast drive by the ocean... You nailed it with the Forza Horizon 5 but on a very small scale. There should be a lot more, diverse and licensed customization options for vehicles (bodykits, wheels etc.). Color corrections should definitely be made in the graphics, although the game looks very good in general, the awful image that occurs due to the wrong use of colors at some scenes makes me sick. There's definitely something off with the graphics. It's not right to compare two different titles but GT7 is one of the best looking out of the market. Vehicle models need to be updated URGENTLY. S15 Silvia, E30 M3 and R34 Skyline looks horrible for example because they're recycled. Driving mechanics are good but so static, they can be improved. Adding 900 degree steering animation in first person is a MUST. There should be an option to change weather, season and time in singleplayer mode. There must be an option or tool in game that allows players to make cinematics (DOF effects etc.). The game currently has that option as "replay" but it cannot answer the request. There should be more npc's all around the map to give that living world feeling but not the dumb ones like playing the same animation 1000 times. Increasing the number of usable houses would also be very cool. Other than that it is a great game.Edit: FIX THE ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ANTI-ALIASING, color banding and popping sun already it's been years

_childDocuments_.review: The game itself is fine. The FIFA of the racing series.The story is as cheesy and the multiplayer is as good (or bad, depending on how you look at it) as the previous games.With the story complete, the only replayable bits are largely through the weekly forzathon events, or multiplayer (casual or ranked) if you like being forced into the "meta" lineup to retain any competitiveness. Multiplayer is not fun for me outside of the weekly co-op trial, where the custom vehicle restrictions keep the casual fun (if you don't get bodied by your own teammates), or cruising with your friends doing photo shoots with the nice scenery and the massive selection of cars. The DLCs are okay - whether or not the top Premium Ultra Complete Whale Shark™ edition should include all of the DLCs is another can of worms.I've kept a neutral stance on this game until recently, and the reason why I'm writing this review is because I was temp-banned (5 days) for "Running cheat software on client alongside game." I don't cheat.From what I gather, beginning roughly in July 2023, a problem developed with the anti-cheat flagging false positives for players and that the dev team is working to fix this issue. This itself is fine, but support will not explicitly tell you what programs are being false-flagged within the anti-cheat, which prevent legitimate users from playing the game without being banned. They obstruct this information because "it would allow cheaters to bypass the anti-cheat." Regardless of whether or not I agree with this take, this means that legitimate players are unable to minimize the risk of being false-flagged by closing the non-exploitative yet false-flagged programs. Every time a user runs this game, they will be gambling with the anti-cheat because they will not know if their background program (discord, spotify, etc) will get them banned.I placed a ticket thru the support site but have heard nothing. Even as my ban passes I won't play further because I feel like I'm walking on thin ice around the game's anti-cheat. Nobody should need to sandbox their game to play it to the fullest extent.TLDR - Game itself is OK but can't play game because hypersensitive anti-cheat, support won't tell players what false-flagged them because "security through obscurity" which causes more bans.Update: It is claimed that the anti-cheat will intentionally flag mod managers for other games (i.e. Vortex or Mod Organizer), with the consensus that "If you mod games at all and the mod tools are present at all on your computer, you deserve to be banned." Why is this okay? People got angry when Rockstar threatened legal action against OpenIV. But Forza's anti-cheat overstepping boundaries, flagging software that has NOTHING to do with the game to ban a user is considered okay because "modders are bad and you should feel bad."I'm done. Thanks PG, and thanks T10.

_childDocuments_.review: Im, not one to normally write reviews for games but after being prompted to write one by steam and generally enjoying playing Horizon 5, I thought to myself I may as well do it.Without waffling on too much this game has brought back my love for the Horizon franchise. I didn't like Horizon 4, being a person who lives in the UK there isn't anywhere where you can open up your car to be best of its ability (And it certainly felt like this in Horizon 4) Sure it's great when you want to bash some country roads but every time you accelerated you felt like you were just getting ready for the next corner. Don't get me wrong Horizon 4 was great but it just felt like it was missing a lot in my personal opinion.Anyway, im here to talk about Horizon 5.Without mentioning too much about the obvious improvement of the engine sounds as well as most engine mods making a noticeable difference to the audio of the cars, I have been taken back to my childhood.This is the first time I have played a Forza Horizon that reminds me of that festival feeling of Horizon 2 which is something I didn't realise how much I had missed until loading up this game.I cannot say much about the performance issues that people have been reporting because since buying this game I have been impressed with how well the game runs, im not sure whether this is down to my pc specs or what but I have had 0 issues.The scenery of this game is seriously insane. The obvious graphical improvements and the level of detail that has been added show the effort the devs have put in this time around.To conclude this review, after owning this game for a few days now I can say this is the Horizon we all needed, being a petrol head and car enthusiast myself this is the Horizon I missed and if this is the standard we are expecting for future games, god im excited!Enjoy exploring folks!

_childDocuments_.review: is a game that has actually surprised me on how much fun it is. This is my first  game, so if you are here expecting me to talk about if  is better or whatnot you won’t be getting that here. I should also mention that if you are someone who plays a lot of  or  and you think you can play this game just fine too, you can’t. It will give you a feel on how to play it, however, don’t go expecting to be a pro.  is an actual racing game with real-world driving mechanics, and it will give you this feeling right when you start playing. has you tasked with joining an event as a celebrity racer called  and you will be going in this series of events in each outpost area. You can have standard racing, offroad racing, cross country racing, street racing, and more. Each race will require you to go through checkpoints to stay in the race, failure to do so will result in you going back to get that checkpoint. However, to prevent this from happening, you can engage a rewind feature that places yourself back near the checkpoint. I should note that missing checkpoints or using the rewind feature online, will screw you over big time, so I recommend successfully going through all of them in the race. is a very big place. You can drive through a dense jungle, a desert filled with cacti, through towns, nice shorelines, and traverse a volcanic caldera. Then there is the , think of it as a battle royal mode, where you and another racer battle in a head-to-head race. Horizon Arcade will make you go to these Arcade markers against other racers in challenges and minigames.!!My favorite race has to be  - it’s a giant race where you drive all across  and I picture it being a giant drive around the country.There are at least 526 cars for you to collect and you can either unlock them, buy them with the CR you get (the game's currency), or buy the DLC ones. You can customize the cars to your heart's content with a variety of colors, engines, horns, or skins. Go and get that nice cool sports car of your dreams and put an anime skin on it, or not, your creativity is your freedom.You can even change the appearance of your character, which to has a lot of options for you to choose from. There are only two voice options and I wish there were a few more to give you that freedom of choice for your character. The cosmetic options are very nice, and you can change the appearance at your house at any timeFurthermore, there are houses that you can buy, which will give you access to a new location for you to customize your cars or character in. However, you can’t explore them or even go inside the house so there is not really a point in buying them in my eyes.FH5 has a lot of nice things but it has a few issues with its gameplay that are noteworthy. My first problem is the fast travel locations; these will fast travel you to an area of the map that you want to go to. My issue with these things is that I just never found them useful as I just wanted to drive around to that area. Why fast travel when I can just drive to and through the jungle in my !! Of course, this is just my personal opinion and if you like doing that, then use them to your heart's content.Another issue I had was when it came to the  events, these are marked by pink circles and when you enter, you will need to wait a bit before the game starts. However, there are rare chances where you will go through a circle and will be thrown into the game with no intention of playing it. I wish they showed you the timers on when the game starts on both the mini-map and the actual map.There is also some downloadable content for you to acquire and these DLC’s can either be something that you can enjoy or a complete waste of money, depending on how you view it. Some of them give you extra cars while others are completely pointless, if you are someone who is a huge car person, then I suppose getting the DLC’s that have cars may be worth it.The  DLC might not be worth the price as it just reveals the locations of the fast travel locations and XP signs, where you can just use  and save your money, but it may hit the mark for those looking for quality of life DLCs. I also hear that  does not work at all currently, so I would pass on this one until you see confirmation that the issue has been resolved. has to be one of the most beautiful games that I have ever played. It shows us a rich  landscape and is really eye-catching. I especially love the night scenery when going through the towns, it just feels so nice to drive through. No other game has topped how great these graphics are and it shows that the devs have worked hard on making the game look the way it is.I tested the game on an NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1060 3GB, AMD Ryzen 5 1500X Quad-Core Processor 3.50, and 16 GB of RAM. You will need a good computer to run this game unless you want your old one to start smoking but I don’t think that’s a smart idea.I have also experienced some crashes when the game started which was rare or when I checked the ranked leader boards. I do hope they fix this issue with a patch someday down the road.The soundtrack consists of actual real-world music and has a decent selection of songs, like  by . That one has to be one of the best songs in this whole game, in my opinion, a straight-up banger. My only issue with the music is that there was no rock station but oh well.    is a fun racing game that offers lots to do, see, and explore. Regardless of if you are new to the series or coming from , I do recommend this game. There is plenty of content to be enjoyed throughout the game and with how big the game is there will always be stuff to do, even into the post-game. It has really beautiful visuals that will catch your eyes and plenty of cars to use or try out.However, I can't recommend  at full price. While I did say there are lots to do, it's not exactly the content that I would pay 79.99 CDN for. There are other games you can buy like ,  (plus it has DLC's that are worth the price), or you can buy food. The game is fun, and you will get some enjoyment out of it, just wait for a sale before buying.

_childDocuments_.review: Later edit: don't bother with the game, it's not worth it and fixes seem to make game worse instead of better. Wait 1 year, maybe it will have solved most of the issues. The game, in it's current state, is about a 7/8 out of 10. It's basically Horizon 4 with improvements to the graphical engine and physics engine. The new location is great, the biomes are outstanding and you have much more freedom than you had in Horizon 4. You don't have to go through a 4-6h tutorial that doesn't allow you to play with friends. After a few introductory races, you can start playing with friends, which brings us to the bad.. connectivity issues. The game right now is plagued by connectivity issues, random disconnects from the servers, alert error messages that don't display anything, friends not being able to play races due to those disconnects.. it's pretty bad, but solvable. There are also issues with memory leaks (which lead to poor performance or crahes), random and not so random crashes (like when changing parts on your car or bodykits multiple times) and texture quality issues when playing the game a bit longer. The other problem in the game is AI, which is infuriating sometimes. If you played Horizon 4 on Unbeatable or Pro difficulty, expect a shock. AI is just cheating, right in front of your eyes, with cars being on rails on higher difficulties, which cheapens your experience. Get ready to play on Highly Skilled difficulty for a time, if you want to win races :).With all being said, i still recommend the game, i enjoy it and i expect that these problems are solved in maybe.. 3 months tops?

_childDocuments_.review: Forza Horizon 5 is yet another step up for the series and arguably the best racing game ever made. Offering a host of content across a fantastic representation of Mexico, its varied terrain and scenery, there's so much to explore and race. A massive roster of cars will perform all of these, each feeling different from the others, with a variety of upgrade and tuning options almost matching those of simulation titles. Although there are a few minor bugs here and there, they are almost so small that they hardly deserve a mention. All in all, it's impossible not to recommend this for anybody, regardless of them being a fan of racing games or not, as this is that good.Pros:1. Fascinating gameplay.2. A huge amount of content that is constantly increasing with each new update.3. Beautifully detailed, fully explorable open world in a vibrant and colorful Mexican setting.4. Good car physics (of course, given that this is an arcade game), which makes the behavior of almost every car unique.5. Realistic weather conditions that directly affect the gameplay.6. Excellent soundtrack, perfectly complementing what is happening on the screen.Minuses:1. Minor technical issues.

_childDocuments_.review: I would give it a 4.5/5 (steadily increasing since launch).I had some initial trouble with crashing repeatedly in the intro, but I eventually figured out it was a piece of recording software running in the background that I had forgotten about. After that I lost my progress because I was not linked to my Xbox account during a session. Its alright, but not as good as it could be. I had set my expectations to fh3 levels, but this is closer to the previous game in terms of play time and story. At first I disliked the lack of classic cars, especially European classics. after playing a bit and having saved some credits, I took a look in the shop to be greeted by no Alfa Romeos, Fiats, Lancias, and very few older porches or British roadsters. They supplemented this largely with new models alongside truly enormous amounts of american muscle cars to bump up the total, and I was not not a huge fan. (They added back some alpha romeos, fiats, lancias, etc in an update a while back. However you CANT BUY THEM as most are only avaliable as exclusives that you have the privilege to grind for over the next four weeks). They also removed the handy "upgrade heroes" tab, which I found extremely pointless. Now its harder to tell which cars have or do not have body kits and major visual upgrades, despite this being featured prominently in forza's promotional content. there are still a fair few bugs, since launch and up until the time of writing. you can still spawn inside buildings in the eliminator, for example.At the end of the day, its still a pretty good formula. And the recent synth update has restored a LOT of my faith in the game.

_childDocuments_.review: It's beautiful, relaxing, and fun to drive around, but beyond that, what's the point? Progression in this game is essentially non-existent... I've only played 7 hours and I have a 999X car and have placed first in every single race I've done. I know I can turn up the difficulty, but that just seems artificial... There's zero excitement associated with winning (Maybe because of the rewind component? I'm a fan of the concept, but it just makes the game too easy). Also agree on the "Notification Overload" point. There are like 75 different menus with 1000 different sub-menus, and it's not really clear what any of them do and/or if any of them are important. I'm not sure what I expected, but I used to love racing games. The whole open-world concept is cool, but it feels like they just dropped the ball on the progression component. Maybe I'm too old for these sorts of games.

_childDocuments_.review: Forza Horizon has never looked better! The biggest and most detailed map they've created to date with some of the most breathtaking visuals you could have in a game period. The cars look and sound fantastic and are an absolute joy to drive. The game's library of cars is extremely large with over 500 to choose from! I'm sure your dream/favourite cars are there. The story is also really fun and the most interactive one they've made so far with separate Festivals each unlocking their own types of races.The only thing that I'm even remotely unsatisfied with would be the technical side of the game. There are a handful of bugs (Which I'm sure will be flattened out in the near future) but the one thing I think they've messed up with, would be the way they've handled the online free roam. Your friends/convoy will disappear quite frequently so if you drive around with friends or like to drift with friends and other people this tends to break the flow.That being said, this game is an visual masterpiece with a humongous map to explore, has plenty of activities for you to take on and will have you driving around in Mexico smiling all the way. I highly recommend this game to everyone!!

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, so while I said that this is my review, its more of a comparison to FH4 and my experiences with it.Anyway, here we go~So, at the time of me writing this, the game's been out for a week over a month (since I have the premium edition) and I've sank 300h into this. Not that I didn't expect I would since I loved FH4 so much. Overall, the game feels like an improvement compared to FH4 in almost every way. The map is much larger and has a lot more variety compared to the map of Horizon UK. The overall feel of the game, looking the past the connection and stability issues, has been a lovely experience and I am definitely going to play the game till the end of its lifespan. The UI feels a lot cleaner and has less unnecessary elements to it, though I feel they missed out on a few things I'd love to have had that were in FH4. I find it harder to join friends compared to FH4, where it would show a friends name over a icon in the main page of the pause menu. Looking at players you follow for customization is more troublesome (and tuner ranks and such dont seem to work right now) since you gotta be in the festival for it, whereas in FH4 you could look at them anywhere. I also do tend to prefer the old cars tab of FH4, where it had smaller icons for your cars, thus being able to fit more in one screen, although I don't hate this new one at all. On the other hand though, I do like the new car collection thing where you get rewards for having collected cars and are able to quickly buy them through the collection. My issue with it, though, is that it nor the horizon promo do not show the base PI values for each car at the very least, (which makes things troubling if you're like me and end up tuning most if not all of your cars and when you need to have something for some championship, you can't just look at base PI values somewhere to get a better idea for what to build on but honestly, its fine, I can live without it). I do feel like Horizon Super 7 is misplaced. Poor thing is hidden in the creative hub where nobody will look for it (which is a shame cuz it was such a great fun idea to add on to FH4).The soundtrack is... While I think there's a ton of great tracks, I don't think its as good as the one that FH4 had but thats purely my opinion of it and Its not really that big a deal.Gameplay feel has improved. I don't know if its just me but while the physics may be a little wacky, cars seem to feel a good bit more responsive (even a bit too responsive at times... looking at you, Sesto FE, but hey, its an arcade racer lol).For example, they've managed to make RWD and FWD drivetrains a lot better. They do not feel super inferior to AWD anymore in my opinion.Its a little easier to find yourself alone in eliminator than it is in FH4 due to the size of the map which is understandable but its generally a very good time all the same.Horizon tours is one of my favourite things to be added into the game as they allow you to basically play Trials (with reduced difficulty) continuously with different car types and races. My only real issue with is that it currently needs more variety. The cards themselves are great but there should really be more than 1 set of races for each of them. Even with 3 different sets of races would be great for each card because it ends up being kinda boring that while you do still end up having fun driving S1 cross country with anything goes, its always the same 3 races. Speaking of which, freeroam rush (horrible gamemode) has been integrated into the tour which, while I hated it as a racetype in FH4 (bc its so luck based), I'm loving it with the tour. Its real fun to drive from one race to the next one. Perhaps they could make it so that in the future, ignoring big races like goliath and such, each card is just randomized (starts from a random race, then just looks whats the closes next one of the same type up close and has you drive to that one and goes on till you've done 3 races for the tour). Race design overall feels great imo. The way most of the races are designed feels fun. We no longer have dirt races where only 7% of the race is dirt! Hooray! The cross country and dirt races especially are some of the most fun races in the game, with the ones up the volcano being some of my favourites. PR stunts feel pretty good, although I find some of the drift zones a little... eh, compared to the ones in FH4, which is a shame bc a lot of my time in FH4 was spent on drift zones but there's lot to love here. They're all good fun. I love the addition of accolades and trailblazers (finally) to FH5. Those were some of the peak stuff from FH4's DLCs that I felt shoulda been a part of the game in the first place. Accolades give you a ton of stuff to chase for in the game. Even if you dont much care for the accolade score, I personally find it very satisfying to see those accolade completed things pop up on the screen (not to mention that a lot of them have great names, I love that!)Festival playlist, while being generally more or less the same, offering much of the same things as it previously did, now has a new progress system, counting points instead of percentage for progress and showing you how much each activity nets you progress. On top of that though, there's new stuff like the treasure hunts (no million credit drops like in fortune island though... C'mon PG, you can afford to give players more than just like 50k for that... even 100k would go a long way), the horizon open challenges and the eliminator challenges, which are a welcome addition, not to mention that there'll be player created eventlabs stuff starting from S3, which is gonna be exciting as well as showcase remixes and featured story chapters in the future seemingly.Events lab is awesome! The addition of Events lab gives course-creating and building up custom races a tons of new options. The addition of props is pretty much expected, but the budget for the lab seems pretty crazy from my own experiences with it. You can add like a fences and stuff and still be nowhere near the limit. Not to mention that beyond the props, there are the race rules that you can mess with to make effects for the race or even completely new rules as we've seen in the festival playlist a few times already. Its really exciting what can be done about it but my one complaint about is that you can't edit a track once its been finished once. Huge bummer if you end up testdriving the track and find out that you forgot something or that you placed something wrong.  Customization has its ups and downs. The loss of Rocket Bunny has left a good few cars without the bodykits that were so memorable on prior titles (RIP RCF and that WANG lol), but on the other hand, there's a bunch of new bodykits to love, like the KRC and TPC ones for the '92 RX-7. Outside of bodykits and such, basically all of the cars that were ported over from FH4 had their PI values adjusted and the PI system seems to work differently in some ways in general. The addition of more tire compound choices is especially something I am very grateful as it allows for a whole lot more customization (Driving hypercars in S1 is dummy fun, especially cross country!). In terms of livery customization though, while the livery customizer has certainly improved from FH4, I can't reaaaally forgive that they hyped up the new editor to be similar to like photoshop and such only for it to nab some basic elements from editors of the kind, though it is understandable to some effect.The carlist as of right now has plenty of great cars. basically most of the interesting ones from FH4 (Where's I.D. R tho?) and a whole lot more interesting ones coming. I for one am real excited to drive that XJ220S TWR. I ended up hitting the maximum limit for a review. Had a lot more to say but guess not lol. Too bad.Anyway, great game! love it!

_childDocuments_.review: Full disclosure: I'm not a racing guy. I'm not a car guy, even. My extent of car knowledge begins and ends at "vroom-vroom go that way."But that's all you need to know for this game. I can tune the holy bejeezus out of a million sliders that mean absolutely nothing to me, or I can just equip a premade setting by someone who does and suddenly the vroom-vrooms are *better*. Not sure when to brake or start a turn? Easy, there's a friendly line. Follow the line, make less vroom-vrooms when it's red, everything's gravy. Don't have the reaction time to follow the line? You can slow the game down until it's at a pace where you can. Incredible.You can be as serious as you want with it. Me, I'm taking my van that's dolled up to look like the Mystery Machine and ramping it off a volcano.

The attention to detail in this game is truly remarkable.Another key feature of Forza Horizon 5 is its vast open world. The game is set in an expansive map that spans multiple environments, including lush forests, sandy deserts, and vibrant cities. This allows for a diverse and engaging gameplay experience, with plenty of opportunities for exploration and discovery.In terms of gameplay, Forza Horizon 5 offers a wide range of cars to choose from, each with its own unique handling and performance characteristics. The driving mechanics are smooth and responsive, and the game offers a range of difficulty levels to suit both casual and hardcore gamers.One of the standout features of Forza Horizon 5 is its online multiplayer mode, which allows players to compete with each other in a variety of different race types and challenges. _childDocuments_.review: Forza Horizon 5 is a great game, but just expect not too many changes. Also the physics of driving seems to have been redone and is much better and more accurate; especially RWD vehicles.P.S. I'm a big Mustang fan and im really sad that the 2020 GT 500 STILL has some inaccuracies with its model; the biggest one to me is the fact it's using the 2015-2017 Mustang tail lights when in reality it uses the 2018 - present tail lights, I know it may seem small, but it always bothers me. Another thing is the gauge cluster is incorrect as it doesn't have the Shelby speedo, instead it once again has a Mustang GT speedo. Again SUPER minor, but really annoying if you are like me and appreciate these cars like art.

_childDocuments_.review: It's absolutely mind boggling that this game has been out for almost a year and still has so many issues. The online in this is so broken that I just don't even bother trying to play with friends anymore since they haven't fixed bugs that have been breaking the entire experience since day 1. The only thing this has going for it is that it has a lot of cars, but most of them are just not interesting. You're gonna find a lot of super cars and variations of the same thing, and not many real life attainable tuners or sleeper hits. That might not be a big deal for some, but the novelty wore off really quick and everything just started to feel the same to me. I like Porsche but I don't need 30+ of them, and especially not when the other manufacturer selections are so sparse that you end up in situations where you're looking for something new and fun, and your choices are picking between 3 Acuras or a single (1) Datsun.  I also distinctly remember them advertising this game as having a better street scene than 4 and having a focus on cars from actual Mexican car culture which is just a straight up lie. There's 1 story line mission where you can unlock a beetle and that is the extent of that gimmick they marketed this game on. The characters are so terrible that I turned off dialogue so I would not have to hear them, and the story its self is just completely unneeded in my opinion. If you like time trials this game has almost none. The event creator is super bare bones and unfun to use. You can't invite people to your convoy through the game its self anymore, you have to use the xbox app instead which is just completely worthless. As far as I'm aware the only new races they've added since launch are from the hotwheels expansion which costs 20 dollars on top of this already unfinished 60 dollar game. The performance is terrible even on lower settings and anything under high looks like a late 360 game. Everything about it just feels soulless. This games biggest crime is being the only choice of open world racing game at the moment. Really hope something replaces it soon.

_childDocuments_.review: Always was a fan of the Horizon series, but this was my first ever Horizon game as I didn't have a console or a computer capable of running it (sad intel HD noises). Built a moderate level PC and after playing it, have to say it meets all my expectations, really enjoying my time with it. Gonna split this review up into the good and bad.-> Beautiful map, extremely varying environment from region to region and there's something for everyone. From off-road racing, to grip racing, to drifting on side roads.-> Great optimization, runs at 1080p high@60fps, with a GTX 1650 GDDR6 LP so thumbs up for that.-> Even at high, the game looks gorgeous, and the weather effects look, and sound great.-> Great selection of cars, got around 200 in-game, and they all feel relatively unique from one another.-> Progression is light, you're given loads of cars through wheelspins and accolades (in-game achievements), so you can save up your credits to buy something you really like. The game doesn't force you to do anything, you can play it at your own pace and do what you like doing.-> The handling model is arcade, but fun to play with on keyboard & mouse (keeping only ABS on).-> Servers still do cause issues, but they have improved massively since launch so I wouldn't worry about it.-> Multiplayer is a mess, I've only played it casually and there are clean racers but most people cannot drive without ramming you into oblivion or using your car to slow down for a corner (wondering if the changes to Horizon 4's multiplayer made it into Horizon 5)-> There are a few texture glitches, especially when the road is wet, but I'm not sure if it's only because the game is running at high.-> If you're looking to no life this game to get high scores for various activities (not my thing, but just wanted to mention), like setting fastest times, highest speeds, longest jumps, there are a few exploits currently ruining the leaderboards. -> Clothing, emotes and horns in wheelspins, I feel like the lifestyle aspect of the game should be separate from the racing/car aspect of the game.Overall, an all rounded game, that is enjoyable to play solo, and would be for multiplayer if they tweaked it so that people don't wall ride or ram into you. It's great to unwind and explore the map with your favourite cars and take in the sights. There's quite a bit a content, and there's going to be more on the way of course.Also wanted to mention that I got the premium edition, can't really say if it's worth it or not yet as the expansions aren't out yet, and won't be for a while I guess. But they haven't disappointed in the past, so if you're think about getting the premium edition, I'd give it a soft recommendation. But, if it's on sale definitely get the premium edition.
