_childDocuments_.review: I feel a bit mixed about this game, I'll pretense it by saying that I love this game, its fun and feels great to play - and was my introduction to the Forza series... However, something always felt off, and now that i've played some of the prior games, I feel like I know what it is. (I'll be comparing it to the previous title mostly as its the only one you can still buy on steam - idk for how much longer though)Graphics - One of the first things you'll notice is the graphics, they are impressive - if you have a machine capable of running it at max settings... Theres been no care into the lower visual settings, and that shows greatly on my system, I have a 1000 series GPU, Forza Horizon 4 looks GORGEOUS on it, and runs extremely well on the max settings, the cars & weather look stunning & every season is distinctly different in terms of colour balance. Whereas in this game, anything lower than High looks like a game fresh out the Xbox 360 era with just more polygons. Cars look almost like stickers on the screen, and weather effects look awful & can be really distracting while you're trying not to be wrecked by the AI.Forza Horizon 5 on Medium Quality... Looks worse than Forza Horizon 4 on Medium Quality (and runs a lot worse), and I dont believe there is an excuse for thatStory - if you could even call it that is uninteresting, completely uninspired & an absolute pain to get through. The dialogue is not entertaining at all, and often times just feels depressing to sit through. I dont even know how they managed to screw up the welsh drifty boi's dialogue, but it just wasn't as memorable as his appearance in FH4. Theres a distinct lack of interesting stories to do, and it feels like a very missed opportunity to showcase the unique environment of Mexico & its culture around cars. The Vocho story is a great example of what they couldve done, but instead that is the only story that focuses on Mexican car culture. FH4 has lots of memorable characters, each story felt distinct & THE BUSINESSES, OH MY GOD THE BUSINESSES - those are fun. This game does NOT have businesses, which were where a fair bit of my FH4 fun came from, an odd choice - and thats kinda what describes a lot of this games decisions... Odd.Car Selection - Great, but theres yet another odd choice in how its handled. Both Fiat/Abarth & Alfa Romeo are still missing even though it has been almost a year since the game has released, and despite massive amounts of asking from the community. Theres a distinct lack of unique American cars, brands like Saturn or Scion (both defunct im aware) are missing, theres a serious lack of saloons or other Consumer "i can get this" cars, Theres only 2 Cadillacs, 3 Pontiacs, 1 Oldsmobile (its a cool one, but still), and very few cars that would actually be common in Mexico... BUT there are ~60 Fords & ~50 Porsches, so it seems like they had their priorities straight when trying to add cars to this game :/. They also seriously like to add cars from previous Forza games & pass them off as "new additions" - I dont mind there being cars from previous games, but stop trying to gaslight us on the Forza Monthly streams into thinking they are new to the series. - We want cars we haven't driven before, not ones we've driven hundreds of times. And REALLY like adding supercars or sports cars, which I understand the appeal - but seriously I want my sleeper cars back, makes more sense to have them especially with an apparently "better" street scene in this game. Theres also a severe lack of appearance customisations, most cars have 1 spoiler option, and 90% have no options for bodykits, or really anything that most people would want to change. Its not too big a deal, but it'd be nice to have some more customisation options.Online & Bugs - OH BOY I have a lot to say about this. Theres been a day one bug, that continues to wreak havoc on our convoy sessions, that has recieved no fix or even acknowledgement by the devs. & that is the random freezing that happens occasionally when you rewind. In single player, this isnt much of an issue. However in multiplayer, especially if it happens when you accidentally hit rewind, it can seriously kill the mood of everyone in the convoy, and make even the most passive person ragequit. Fix the damn bug already. The online experience is awful, you cant join your friends convoy ingame anymore like you could in FH4, you now have to use the "Xbox Game Bar" otherwise you cant play with your friends, its once again an odd choice considering they already had the framework to join other's games in FH4. Its also a massive middle finger to anyone who runs this on linux through proton, since they can no longer join their friends games as its now OS locked.The biggest annoyance personally has been something that they absolutely refuse to fix, and thats the lack of balance between the cars. If you've ever driven the boneshaker (or most of the cars added by the Hot Wheels DLC now) you'll be aware of how absurdly overpowered they are, if you encounter a Boneshaker in A Class open, you will not be fighting for 1st place, you'll be fighting for 2nd because the boneshaker has finished the race 20 seconds before anyone else did. I want to love this game more, but the lack of care the developers have to actually rescore the cars to match what their actual performance is, its genuinely awful. Its worse knowing that these cars have been known to be broken since day 1, and there has been literally nothing done by the devs to actually fix them. So you'll always encounter them in Open or Tour.I want to say this game is good, I really do, I love playing it, and I love being in the game racing. But I feel like this game could be a LOT better with next to no effort from the development team. They could fix the unbalanced cars and instantly make the game 100x more fun to play online. They could remove cheated leaderboard scores & make getting the highest score mean something. They could actually add unique cars to the region, or listen to their damn community, but they won't. This feels like a "safe profit" game. A game manhandled by some execs into losing its soul just so it could be an easy game to profit from. It feels corporate, its not the same horizon you had as a child/teen on your xbox 360, and its not the same game as the previous title. Its a soulless husk of a game within a series that was at one point the greatest open world racing experience. I'm still going to play it, its one of the only open-world racing games & I dont exactly have a choice to fill that niche. I want this game to be the best it can be, but it really feels like i've joined just as the ship was going down. _childDocuments_.review: Honestly, the physics and mechanics are perfect. Unfortunately, this game is such a failure in most every other aspect. There is no competitive mode, (so no end game) and the multiplayer mode there IS, has like one meta car in each class that's 100x better then everything else, making it impossible to be competitive unless you use the unrealistic cheesy builds. (hot wheels cars etc) This wouldn't be such a big deal, since the majority of the experience is singleplayer, HOWEVER, the single player experience while plentiful, is a joke aswell. You can complete every single race in the game (aside from showcases and side events) with literally one car. You could complete the whole game by only using one car if you really wanted to. The game lacks any variety in vehicle usage in events. The game should force you to use different classes/types per certain events to make it interesting and give you a sense of progression but unfortunately, it does not. I am so disappointed since this could be an AMAZING game, the car selection is there, a great map, good physics and exceptional tuning, but the tuning is useless when you can just pick your difficulty and experience and are never once forced to go outside of your comfort zone. Aside from multiplayer where tuning can be very useful, it doesn't really matter if you dial in your car since the only tune you actually want to use can just be downloaded and put on to the few OP meta cars. I never played Horizon 1 due to not having an Xbox, but it sounds like that game had a very good progression system and variety. Why do games go backwards and not forwards? it boggles my mind...Racing games have taken a fall from grace and to be honest, its very depressing. Forza Horizon 5 offers an amazing sandbox but aside from that, it doesn't do a whole lot else which is honestly too bad. Really wanted to enjoy this game but can't see myself continuing to play it with no end goal or meaningful progression to move towards.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not sure who this review is really for. I don't play modern racing games yet I grew up with racing games like Need for Speed Underground 2, Midnight Club 3, Burnout 3, Burnout Paradise and even Mario Kart. Yet for some reason the Forza Horizon franchise (since Forza Horizon 2) has always called out to me and I have been playing it quite seriously since Forza Horizon 3; Unbeatable Drivatars, all assists off, manual w/ clutch, no rewind. The long and short of this review is that Forza Horizon 5 is a fantastic game and there's really no reason not to recommend it to anyone who doesn't already have an interest in Forza or racing games in general, but regardless, let's start off with the good points.The graphics and general detail have improved; one simple addition here is tyre smoke that adds a satisfying feel to drifting, and even racing in general. The UI has been cleaned up nicely and in general it feels like there is a lot less clutter on screen and in the menus. If you can't see it in front of you, it likely isn't important. Mexico is a wonderful setting for the franchise and hearing that Playground Games actually worked with a team in Mexico to avoid things like cultural appropriation really makes me feel that they did their best to make sure the game was treated with authenticity.All the features that were added into Forza Horizon 4 post release have been baked into 5 in a way that feels natural yet exciting. Features like the Festival Playlist and Eliminator return in 5 with renewed vigour and in general Forza Horizon 5 absolutely loads you with things to do while simultaneously showing you there is no rush to do them. Anything you do will likely result in XP or earning some sort of accolade, and this feels pretty good. This is also an improvement on the more linear aspect of previous entries. You're still required to attain X amount of accolade points to progress, but how you acquire those points (story missions, road racing, dirt, cross country, PR stunts, etc.) is entirely up to you, as is the reward you unlock for completing these. It gives a sense of freedom that the Forza Horizon series has always been about.The story missions are perhaps the best the franchise has ever seen, mixing Mexican culture, photography, racing, PR stunts. The story in Forza Horizon 5 won't blow you away but I appreciate that there is at least some continuity from previous entries with characters like Jaimin reappearing for the street scene (which has surprisingly engaging story missions tied to it). Having our avatars now fully voice acted is a nice touch too, and I especially enjoyed the quips about our protagonist being eerily silent back in the UK.Other significant improvements have been made to engine sounds, with most cars sounding a lot more unique than Forza Horizon 4 and general handling of cars. More than ever it now feels like you have to pick your car carefully for each track rather than using a "one tune fits all" approach.So why does something feel...off about this release? Despite my love for the franchise, why is this the least excited I have ever felt about Forza Horizon? Well, one might say the devil is in the details, and the lack of nuance and polish in some areas has left the game feeling less like Forza Horizon 5 and more like Forza Horizon 4.5. These points are aimed towards the more hardcore audience and I wouldn't actually expect the majority of people to feel affected by these.Let's start with the Drivatar AI, which frankly is the worst it's ever been. In the post game of Forza Horizon 3, I changed my difficulty settings to Unbeatable Drivatars, manual w/ clutch, assists off and never looked back. It was tough at first but eventually I got to a point where with the right car, clean driving, good downshifting and proper throttle control, I was able to beat Unbeatable Drivatars by a narrow margin. This continued in Forza Horizon 4, although I noticed instances where the Drivtars would "cheat". In Forza Horizon 5 I still beat Unbeatable Drivatars the majority of the time but it just isn't fun anymore. I understand the game will always have rubber banding to keep Drivatars competitive and I don't mind this, but some races are frankly unwinnable without ramming the Drivatar in front of you and playing dirty. More than ever Drivatars seem unaffected by weather conditions or even corners, which they'll often take without dropping speed or losing any grip.A common argument I hear from people is "well they're called Unbeatable for a reason!" Perhaps, then Playground Games should consider changing the name to something else, like "Extreme" or "Insane" because there are accolades and achievements for beating Unbeatable Drivatars and having them cheat to keep them Unbeatable just is not fun.Secondly, the music is disappointing. While this point is undoubtedly subjective, I've seen multiple reviews expressing the same sentiment. Forza Horizon 2, 3 and even 4 had outstanding soundtracks. I'll always keep coming back to Horizon XS but I found I could enjoy music from every station. 5 has slim pickings and I often find myself switching off the radio entirely.Unfortunately, the most significant point in all of this is the buggy state of the game. We've got it all here. Crashes to desktop, graphical glitches appearing as lines in the road, lack of detail in foliage, tearing on terrain, stuttering entering in and out of events, a horrible overexposed sky box which frequently takes away from the beauty of the game by overexposing brightness and blinding you. I know no game is perfect but visuals are a big part of Forza Horizon and all of these take away from what should be a mouthwateringly gorgeous game. Furthermore, if you care about being competitive there is literally no point trying to set any kind of time on any leaderboard because they're all been taken over by cheaters. It seems no matter how much this is reported to Playground Games, the issue still persists. This segues into my final point. The competitivity of Horizon feels like it's died with this franchise. In Forza Horizon 3 you could choose whatever kind or racing you liked, be that road, dirt, cross country, street. In Forza Horizon 4 this was inexplicably removed instead cycling between the 4 types at random with the dreaded "freeroam rush" mode which had you charging across the UK taking whichever route you liked to a destination. However, at least you still had a ranked system which allowed for more serious racing.This has now been removed.It seems that, instead of building upon the ranked system in place, or even implementing a system that prioritises clean racing above all, encouraging players not to shunt each other into walls, Playground Games sought it fit to just remove the system entirely. As a competitive player, there is now zero reason to play online, and even less of a reason to attempt to race properly when there are no consequences for driving badly. This, coupled with the fact that smaller features like launch control and gears grinding when you don't shift properly really makes me feel like they want this to be a purely casual game, whereas previous entries felt like there was something for everyone.Overall, I still love Forza Horizon 5 and this game is an easy recommendation, yet I can't shake the fact that this is the least exciting and least polished entry in the franchise and many decisions have been made that don't feel healthy for the franchise as a whole. Perhaps it's time I finally look toward a proper sim racer but I would still like Forza Horizon to flourish competitively.

_childDocuments_.review: While I have always been a big fan of racing games in general due to my love of cars, I really have not touched a game since Forza Horizon 2/3. I switched to PC a bit ago but just never got a controller for racing game's, that is until now.For some reason the release of Forza Horizon 5 sparked my interest so I got a controller and bought the game. Since buying it I have not gone a full day without playing it at least once. While games like this aren't played for their story, Forza 5 in my opinion did a good job of trying to make the player feel a bit more involved by having your in game character actually talk and interact with others. While its not a focal point of any racing orientated game, I think it should be recognized and appreciated.Now, down to the game itself.... IT IS SO DAMN GOOD!!!First of all, the amount of effort that went into making the game look and sound as good as it does it just remarkable. I am so happy that it was not only nominated for multiple categories in the Game Awards but indeed won best audio design, innovation in accessibility, AND best sports/racing game. In general I feel like at these big award shows racing and sports game's kind of get swept under by bigger releases and story driven games but I am so happy to see them succeed this year! The game runs so smoothly on my PC and while there have been issues with online connectivity and online racing, I have seen nothing but progress since it was addressed to the developers. The wide range of cars, trucks, buggies, SUVs, hatchbacks, and many other models to choose from and customize is endless. Making money also is not a hair pulling ordeal so you are always able to make new cars and get creative. The customization is quite in depth, but I do think there are some things that would be nice if added, and I honestly think that slowly stuff will be added. While it may be added via DLC I do not know but nonetheless it will be cool to see what they do.And finally, the feeling of driving in this game tops any I have experienced before. The added tire smoke, the sounds of the different engines that you can swap, the turbo spools and whistles, they are all done just so well. Normally when I would play Forza game's I would always just max out the power in any car, but with this release I find myself building different cars for different purposes. Some cars I max out and just try to make it as fast as possible, but others I lessen the power and make a fun little cruising car for the beautiful cities located throughout this GIANT map. And of course I cant forget to mention drifting and how amazing that feels on controller. I can only imagine how great it must be with a wheel setup, and like I mentioned before, the added tire smoke is so satisfying when drifting. The possibilities are literally endless and I cant help but always make a new car every time I open the game up.I highly recommend this game to anyone that is either debating it or looking for a open world racing/driving game because Forza Horizon 5 knocks it right out of the park!!

_childDocuments_.review: I love FH4. Poured hundreds of hours into that game. Tuning, Racing, Drifting, Off-roading. I'd come on and complete every weekly competition to get the cars. It was amazing. This feels like a complete reversal of what FH4 was and still is. It honestly feels like a complete downgrade except newer cars, better sounds and graphics. That is where the only positives for this game are.To start off with, you are physically forced to do off-road and cross country races to progress. You can't just ignore them if you don't like them, you have to do it. Another thing, when you complete the acolade stage, you are forced to pick an acolade and goto where that is (a showcase race or new event area).Back in FH4, I honestly didn't mind the off-road and cross country races. They are not my favourite what so ever, but I did have fun with them when I did them. Not this game, what so ever. The tracks are complete ass, sharp corners then immediate jumps. Jumps that are so large, no matter what you do, your car bogs down however the AI is just fine. And to top it off with these races, the AI are absolutely insane with them. They can race around cross country races as if they are an F1 car on a race track! They don't worry about grip, traction, balance NOTHING; all while you are wrestling with your car to get around the corners and not go off the course. You do all this effort just for the AI to slam their break, turn in and pass you as if you are standing still. This isn't to do with difficulty, I play the entire game on expert/pro, yet when it comes to cross-country (due to the race being apart of the forzathon playlists to get a new car), the difficulty is Highly Skilled (around 1-2 difficulty notches down) and it feels like I am playing unbeatable drivatars (the top difficulty level). I have had to retry, rewind and redo each race numerous times. It just completely sucks the fun out of it.I mention all of this to not even cross onto the fact that this was all to unlock a 911 GT3RS, A FACTORY MADE TRACK RACING CAR. Why the hell should you do cross-country races for a car that is purely for track use! It' s completely irrelevant. All this does is force me to play races that I don't like and have tried my hardest to avoid just so I can unlock a car that is better for the races I DO LIKE.That was just the actual races and physics! I haven't even gone on about the numerous bugs, irritations and down-right rage-quitting issues!I will keep this one short as it is already long as it is.First: the on-screen narrator. No matter what I do, within Windows, within the game, the onscreen narrator will always start speaking whats on screen for the entire menu until you get into the game. There is no way to stop this, believe me, I have tried. It makes me immediately want to shut down the game, because the voice and the fact that it won't shut up is highly aggravating.Next: Force feedback on the wheel. It is a luck of the draw whether it decides to work or not. You can boot up the game, load in and wait all that time just to realise you can' t feel what the car is doing because the FFB doesn't exist (bearing in mind without it, the car feels like a weightless feather on ice). All of this leads to you restarting the game, multiple times, until it finally starts to work again. And as soon as you tab-out, there is a high likely-hood that the FFB will stop working again.After that: The constant resetting of my wheel setup. I don't have a clutch pedal, but I like using the clutch so I can drift. So to do so, I bind it to one of the buttons on my wheel, meaning I have to use a custom wheel profile. This is completely okay, I did that in FH4 and it was never an issue. The issue is that FH5 resets it back to default, every. damn. time. Every time I open the game, I have to go back into settings and set the mapping to Customer Wheel Controller #1. Finally: Something that is still not fixed, however not too bad, the fact that there are still graphical issues within the game. That being the glitching road textures. You could just be driving normally and then all of a sudden you pass through a stretch of road that is filled with rainbow colours. Not the car, not the grass, just the road. You could reboot the game, go back to the exact road and it will be gone. This isn't an issue with my graphics card or installation as i have checked both of these, however it is still jarring and does break any immersion or enjoyment.This is all just to say that with the numerous amount of bugs, I spend most of my time restarting, rebooting and remapping FH5 so that I can play it. This just leads to me not actually wanting to play the game anymore. It is the reason I have not played it as much as I have wanted to do. The hassle and faff just outweighs the fun that could be had.

_childDocuments_.review: You're a British man/woman that goes to Mexico to race in the Horizon Festival, and become the very best like no one ever was. Along the way you learn about the powers of friendship and "family" through cringeworthy dialogue that includes stories about Papa Fernandos V O C H O, and you being a superstar (even though you haven't won a race yet and you drive like you're under the influence of something because you've managed to hit every single tree in Mexico). After nearly winning several high octane races, some of which are illegal street races with heavily modified Japanese cars covered in big booba anime waifus, or highly destructive offroad races in big pickup trucks that make you feel less British and more 'Merican (Yee haw, pickups and 4x4's go BRRRRRR) you are rewarded with an endless supply of random Lamborghinis and Ferraris like you've just been visited by MrBeast himself. You are also forced to abandon the use of Mexican Pesos, and embrace the Horizon Festivals cryptocurrency of Credits and Forzathon Points that can only be spent on more cars, modifications for the cars, and tacky clothing for yourself.Eventually, after you've devoted several months to this never ending festival you begin to lose your mind as you realize all hope of returning to the UK to see your wife and children is gone as the hosts of the Horizon Festival are keeping you in Mexico against your will to race for the rest of your life to keep the value of credits and forzathon points blockchain up in the green. You then come face to face with the mastermind of the event himself, Papa Fernando, and his V O C H O in a 1v1 winner take all race for your freedom along the mountainside. In an Initial D F&F Tokyo Drift fashion you and Papa Fernando race to the finish with you winning it by a second. As you leave everything fades to white and you wake up realizing it was all a dream, and you're still in the UK fresh from having conquered the Horizon Festival from FH4. And then.... you're told to pack your things... you're headed to Mexico...Great game btw 10/10 would drift in a V O C H O again.

_childDocuments_.review: Back when I was a kid, I held two standards for racing games- one, it has to have as many cars as possible. Cars good, more cars better. Two, it has to have the free roam mode. I longed for freedom outside the tracks. I would add the modded cars to games to the point of engine's limit and when the eventual crash occurred, I'd lose all interest and it took several weeks for me to regain passion for that game.For greedy kids like me, Forza Horizon will feel like a heavenly experience from the dreams. Incorrect models? Limited customization options? Younger me wouldn't care about such stuff. I played the first Horizon from the playable stand that was installed in knockoff K-mart here in Korea and that marked my first contact with Forza Horizon series. I played maybe two or three races(no free roam was available, I suppose that was a demo version) and while I enjoyed the game, there was no way for me to play that game outside that supermarket because I didn't have X360. After a while the supermarket changed the game to Lego Batman and the game faded from my memory.I had to wait till 2016 when Horizon 3 released with PC as one of its supported platforms. And the feeling of playing Horizon in its intended way was, simply magical. Boasting vast beautiful open world with hundreds of cars available, I think I played the game for one straight week using all my available free time. I was hooked. Before that point I had distanced myself from the racing genre because I was tired of console exclusives and rehashes, but Horizon 3 rekindled that passion inside me from years ago.Then the Horizon 4 came, with one DLC outside of the car pass and strengthened FOMO mechanics in the form of festival playlist. I still played it. I even bought it and played it twice when it had a Steam release later. After few years, we got a Horizon 5. And with my honeymoon period with the franchise long over, I've finally thrown away my tinted glasses and started to see its ever increasing faults. Car pass comes with so many packs not included in it. Usually there's like, car pass one, car pass two scheme to sell people two season passes. But not this game. You need to spend the whole price, no bundle discount provided.The level of FOMO hit a record high with more aggressive festival playlist forcing you to choose different cars, and literal checklist of ingame feats. You will feel the absurdness of it early game. You broke 10 destructive objects? Here's a medal! You got 10 cars? Here's another! Unwanted notifications everytime, you'll need to get used to that.Product placements are excessive and fill the majority of the already short story parts. Like, okay. It's cool to hear the specifications of Ford Mustang Mach-E from the guy who engineered it. Whatever. But I'd like to hear that outside the game, from some Discovery Channel show after 11pm, lie down half asleep.Expansions are boring. Rally expansion is just mid. No historical group A B 4 stuff, just some lame rivalry between local teams you couldn't care about less. Compare this with Fortune Island back in FH4 with its treasure hunt theme and 10 million reward. Yeah. And we already had a Hotwheels expansion back in FH3. Sure, they added this new weird gyro bar mechanic but I can only wonder who thought adding this scale thing in the middle of the screen all the time is a good idea.So do I think Horizon 5 lost its magic? No, but that magic is waning fast, following a constant downward slope. I want to think they're still trying, somewhat. They're constantly adding new cars with updates(with FOMO goals... But it's better than nothing). And the basic principle, recipe of the game still remain strong.To new players to the franchise, Forza Horizon 5 can still feel amazing with the freedom this game offers. But for how long? I can't be sure about the answer. I still recommend this game because there's barely any competitors in its genre that can really compete with this game. The Crew is a typical Ubisoft slop manufacture that can't even be played after some time and I doubt Solar Crown would succeed, sadly. So I give this flawed game a halfhearted thumbs up and few tired handclaps, like most critics and award presenters did.

You can continuously get game pass for 1$ a month if you cancel your subscription before renewing it.If you and your friends can all get forza for 1$ on game pass, it's a really fun game to play with them. I find it most fun to do private races with either slow, or moderately fast cars. I've personally found most S1+ class cars are too quick to even keep on the road, unless you like braking more than accelerating. I've found super slow cars like the 1926 Bugatti Type 35, and the 2010  Ford Crown Victoria are both super fun slow cars to race with. They're so slow you need to practice carrying as much speed around corners as possible. I feel it's a very fun change of pace from the hypercars you will see people driving normally. But if you don't like slow cars, I've found the 1988 Lamborghini Countache strikes a happy medium between fast and slow cars. It's moderately fast, and it has good handling. although it can sometimes suffer from understeer. It's honestly a blast to race it with your friends. I personally don't like the online racing with randoms. I feel it's nearly impossible to consistently do well unless you conform to the meta. Ontop of that, I've just found it's super sweaty and not super fun.TL;DR conclusion:it's a fun game to play with friends on xbone gaypass, but not worth it for full or sale price.

_childDocuments_.review: The Mercedes-Benz W123 is a range of executive cars produced by German manufacturer Mercedes-Benz from November 1975 to January 1986. The W123 models surpassed their predecessor, the Mercedes-Benz W114, as the most successful Mercedes, selling 2.7 million units before production ended in the autumn of 1985 for the saloon/sedan versions and January 1986 for coupés and estates/station wagons.[4]Following a slow production build-up during the first year, customers who placed their orders faced a lengthy waiting period of nine to twelve months. A black market emerged for the customers who were willing to pay more for immediate delivery. The slightly used W123 commanded about 5,000 Deutsche Mark premium over its original sale price.[5]Like its predecessors, the W123 gained the reputation of being well built and reliable. Many taxi companies chose the W123, and they were a common sight in Germany. Reaching 500,000 or 1,000,000 km with only minor mechanical issues was common with W123s used as taxicabs.[citation needed] Once the W123 reached the end of its service life, they were often shipped to Africa and third world countries where they were highly esteemed for their ability to travel on rough roads and to not require frequent maintenance.[6]W123 production ended in January 1986 with 63 final T-models rolling out. The most popular single models were the 240 D (455,000 built), the 230 E (442,000 built), and the 200 D (378,000 built).

_childDocuments_.review: Would've been a decent game if they didn't pander to 12 years old with ADHD on cocaine so hard. The game has a lot to like about it: great graphics, great sound, very wide collection of cars that all feel quite different, driving is satisfying and the map is big and has a bit of everything. However, it's absolutely ruined for me because the game constantly throws things at me I don't want and can't turn off:The game hijacks control and opens the map when I get some unlocks.The game automatically starts challenges when I drive through areas where they're set up. This also removes collision with other cars (you can just drive through them), changes my destination on the GPS and triggers various visual effects, sounds and cringey dialogues, completely breaking immersion.The game constantly reminds me I'm not playing in online mode. And that this or that game mode exists. And that I can send cars to people. And all kinds of other useless crap I don't care about. These are just a few things off the top of my head. If I were to jump in the game and drive around for 10 minutes Im sure I could find more. I get that the game is supposed to be an arcade and not a driving simulation, but there's no reason in not letting the player opting out of being constantly accosted with things he doesn't care about.This isn't even getting into the awful writing pertaining any line of dialogue, scripted event, cutscene and story point. Everything that happens in this game tells you how amazing of a driver and person you, the player are. You can hardly find an interaction with a character that doesn't at least mention how you're the best driver in the world. Whenever you turn on the radio you're gonna find some "news" about how you're such a legends. All the cutscenes and scripted events are so grand in scale and hype that they remove any sense of realism or immersion you might have had left. Hell, there are even scripted races where you're slightly behind the entire race then make a miraculous recovery and get in the first place meters away from the finish line, no matter how good or bad you were driving. And it's not an isolated event, it happens over and over and over again, as if the player is too stupid to realize what's happening.For the same reason, I suspect, the progression in this game is messed up. You get your first supercar as soon as you start the game. Within a few hours of playing the game you already have more supercars than a billionaire obsessed with them and everyone refers to you as the best driver in the world.The annoying part is that they had a good game at some point in development. But then they created a bunch of content that seemingly came out of a chinese mobile game and shoved it down the players throat. It blows my mind that over a year after the release they still didn't give us the option to turn all of it off. The game, as it is now has enough good to keep me coming back once in a while to drive around a bit, but I always close it with a bitter taste in my mouth because of all the extra ♥♥♥♥ I can't turn off and embarrassed that I spent time and money on a game designed to make children feel good about themselves.

_childDocuments_.review: Forza Horizon 5, is all about cars, your character's life revolves around cars, racing, and gaining a reputation. If you have played the previous, Forza Horizon 3 & 4. You know what's up ;) But for those of you who are stepping first hand into Forza, here's a bit about it:You are a well known racer, known for being able to drive really well, and gain a reputation. You can collect cars of a variety of brands, from Super cars, Rally cars, and even your Every day sort of cars. But with these cars you can customise them to your liking! You can design your own vinyl logos/designs, give it a new paint job, and even on the mechanical side of things, 'mod' your car to improve certain performances. Then, there's the fun part, Racing! Forza Horizon 5 is based in Mexico, where you can explore a wide range races, street races, dirt races, rally, etc. But then there's the Open World part. The world is stunning! Based on real sights seen in Mexico, with stunning details, graphics, sounds, and a whole open world to explore. You can play solo, or with friends, challenge your friends to races, or just mess around and drive Super Cars off the side of a Mountain... Whatever floats your boat really. In Short, I recommend this game to those who are interested in cars, racing, or just having a blast with some friends. And for those previous Forza Horizon players, if you don't have this game yet, What Are You Doing? ;) Hope this helped.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a simple man. I like to drift through every single turn and I never,  touch the brakes. I enjoy the Need for Speeds and the Burnouts, and as such I never got on with any Forzas, or anything that even remotely approaches what could be called a simulator.Horizon 5 is the exception. I'm not sure why. I hated the previous entry like I hate every other sim type racer. Like its predecessor, Horizon 5 has a multitude of settings you can tweak to get your ideal experience, but while I never got a good feeling out of 4, the fifth is one kick ass game. It helps that this is also one of the best looking car games. Performance is great, with everything maxed (except for ray tracing) my 6800xt averages around 100 FPS. Most importantly of all, the game is so much fun. It just throws everything at you all at once all the time. So much cool ♥♥♥♥ going on I can barely decide what to do, but whatever I end up doing is consistently thrilling. I can appreciate that. The sheer variety and quantity of awesome driving based activities here is mind boggling.For anyone thinking of a purchase, do it. I first played it on game pass, so that could be a decent way to try it without committing too much money. If you're looking at all the separate purchases and editions / DLCs and whatnot, you can very safely ignore all that and just get the base edition. It's already got way too much ♥♥♥♥, and you won't feel like you miss out on anything.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a pretty fun game all things considered, the main problem I experience is really bad pop-in, even after doing things to help improve it. The ultra settings for textures and world geometry are bugged, after playing for about 30 minutes you'll get rainbow textures or foliage will have a missingno-esque texture. The game runs fine, it looks fantastic when everything works properly. The racing feels like a forza game, if you played 4, it's basically the same game new area. The reason for not recommending the game is because of the issues that haven't been fixed since the game came out. Looking for solutions or other people experiencing these bugs and you'll see it all the way back to when it launched. It breaks the immersion and sometimes ruins the game. If you have ray tracing on there's a chance the game will crash while in the garage because of a bad texture. The courses that they release for the timed events are cool enough, however, they have a lot of issues, they tend to be these long and winding tracks that go up into the air and do tight turns and what not, it's cool in concept, but it feels like it was put together by an amateur because there are huge seems in the tracks where you'll hit it and you'll lose all speed and can't make the turn requiring you to rewind and hope you don't lose too much speed. That's not the only issue though, it seems there are a lot of graphical issues with these tracks too, causing huge pieces of geometry to disappear, for example, I did one that was really cool, but the mountain was disappearing at certain angles and it looked really bad. The base game races are quite fun though. If they can get better seasonal track design and fix the graphical issues, I think that it would be worth the $60, but as of right now, get it one sale for cheaper, or just wait until you see an update to the bugs.I should mention my specs before people call them out for the game being poorly optimized.RTX 3070 OCI9-10850K32gb 3200Mhz raminstalled on an SSD, 1tb, only about 200gb of storage used. windows 11 installed on NVmeand most importantly, have a nice day :)

_childDocuments_.review: Lifeless and lazy, is what I'd have to call this game.I tried really hard to get used to it and enjoy it, but at the end of the road, there really isn't any content in this game. I found myself constantly saying "Need for Speed did it better" at every corner of the game despite NFS not being particularly  groundbreaking either. The UI in FH5 is terrible - it's slow, doesn't make much sense and there's dozens of redundant prompts that get in the way every 5 minutes. Your party leader might queue you up for a race, but you're so deep in UIs that by the time you can back out of all the menus the 10 second (yeah, only 10) timer to accept the event runs out, and you get kicked from the party and everyone has to exit and re-party up again.The sound design of the cars is lifeless. Cars are tinny and there's little to no bass in any of them. To call it 'award-winning' is a joke. And don't get me started on the balancing. This is one of the most unbalanced, or stupidly balanced games I've ever played. Sure, the game gives you over 600 cars to choose from, but only about 10 of them are actually competitive, while the rest might have the same rating as another player's car but only have half the top speed, or slide out uncontrollably on near-straights.There are a very limited amount of race courses in this game, with the devs opting to allow the community to foster their own tracks and have them curated on front pages and in weekly challenges. The problem is people make awful tracks. I just want tracks that flow and have readable/sensible corners, with walls or props that indicate a clear direction. Instead, you get these wonky tracks with no walls or indication whatsoever to where you need to turn, so you spend the entire race staring at your GPS/minimap in the bottom corner of the screen rather than on the road.The story is pretty lacklustre as well, not to mention how 'happy' everything is. Everyone's way too cheerful and the dialogue is cringe. I'd rather not have the story at all to be honest. But it doesn't last long and after a handful of 'races' with random challenges you're on your own to just do whatever. There's no drive to do anything. Now, the game has some good parts to it as well. I very much prefer its physics over Need for Speed, and it's kinda pretty. But that's about it to be honest.I've played this game mainly as a social outlet to play with a couple of friends, and that's really what this game is. It's a social experience with racing, rather than a racing game with friends. But it even contradicts itself in that, as your interactivity with other players is very limited. To remove toxicity, there's no open chat, only a very limited chat system where you get 4 context-sensitive chat messages you can send, but you have to WIN them in lootboxes this game calls 'wheelspins'. You can't send cars or money to your friends without buying them with premium currency - speaking of which, I don't think you can even buy the 'premium' currency. They look like they're special, but you just get them from doing a bunch of dumb challenges.Buy it on sale if you have a bunch of friends who would be happy to join you, or if you're a car fanatic or just want to drive around for a while. But if you're looking for a serious racing game to play, this is 100% not it. Get any Need for Speed if you want basically everything mentioned in this review done significantly better minus the physics, or buy Assetto Corsa if you desire the physics and an open playground.

_childDocuments_.review: Forza Horizon 5  is a racing game. But its heart isn’t really about just racing at all. For my money, this spin-off series has built its reputation and quality around different foundations. It’s a series about culture. It’s about the mood, the tone, the feel.Part of all that is how each vehicle literally feels as it cruises around its open world map, but a bigger part of it is that nebulous, difficult-to-describe thing the game activates within you. Many things activate this bit of the brain, like over-the-top set-pieces and silly motoring stunts - but an enormous chunk of it is about one thing: the game’s world. I love this game! The best game with cars!

_childDocuments_.review: Actually really good, gave me the long-lost vibe of Test Drive Unlimited 1 that I had when I played it as a child. There's no real payment walls that would block you from making progress in the campaign and races. By being smart and using the cars you already received, and trust me, the game kind of spams you with the cars received from doing in-game achievements or finishing race challenges, you can usually just buy and use one of the tuning setups already made by the community to just keep on racking on money for other cars you want. The HOONIGAN Ford Escort that the game gives you for free as a tribute to Ken Block, when tuned, can help you with racking up a lot of skill points in free-roam and track races, performing drifts 24/7. I assume however that money still becomes a challenge during late-game for masochists wishing to 100% games, since finishing your car collection with "rare" cars that cost a fortune might be a pain to do without submitting yourself to the great evil of micropayments that was laid down by the game industry. But still, the feeling of the world in FH5 is full of life and joy, especially with all the radio broadcasters giving comments on new events and your progress in the campaign. Me likey.

_childDocuments_.review: Short disclaimer: It's not a bad game, but there is no middle option between "recommend" and "not recommend" for me to choose and I wanna at least give new people a bit of insight, before they buy it. Now, I have played this game probably for the longest time out of all the forza horizon installments. however, to me it still feels like a mixed bag. heres why:1. It just feels like Forza Horizon 4. The previous games all had different improvements over the game before. FH2 added a bigger open world, FH3 added better car customization and even bigger open world, FH4 added seasons that change the world in a quite unique way, but what big and impactful feature got added with FH5? Offroad tires on every car? Local weather events that rarely happens? While it does have some smaller QoL additions, overall FH5 just seems like a sequel or spin-off to FH4 and not a new installment of the main series.2. The carpark honestly feels pretty empty, despite being massive, if not bigger than the previous games. Some manufacturers are missing, like Lancia or Abarth, or sometimes just some stand alone cars, like the 1966 Chevrolet Nova. But on the other hand, we got a bunch of super cars that all look similar and arent very unique. So you essentially end up with a carpark that is bloated with generic vehicles and doesnt have many that stand out. While this is mostly a personal gripe, someone else might disagree with, it still gets quite boring when you add new cars to the game, you have either already seen in other games or are just an expensive trim of an existing car with a better engine. Speaking of adding cars...3. the new cars that get added with seasonal events. Once again, probably just a personal gripe, but it might still be orth mentioning. Every week, the developers add new cars to the game. HOWEVER...for the last few months those cars were a bit of a let down. You got stuff like an AMC Javelin...which was available in previous games. Then you got a Cadillac Limousine...which was also in previous games. Theres also the Rimac Nevera...which is just a Rimac Concept Two that drives differently. But hey, theres also the Cadillac CT5-V...and the CT4-V in the same season...which look similar...You get the point. The recent series rewards are kinda bland. Although it does look better with the current series (May 11th, 2023), so who knows what the future brings. HOWEVER, its also important to remember that all the problems with the carpark and the series rewards could very well just be licensing issues. the reason, why there is no lancia or fiat isnt, because the developers got bored of it, but because the license ran out. But I dont have behind the scenes information, so thats just an assumption. 4. The Map. Ima be honest, Im not a big fan of the map. Does it look good? Yes. Does it feel good? ehhh...As big as the map is, it honestly feels pretty empty overall. There arent that many memorable places, apart from a few towns and maybe a few natural formations. Another problem I have with the map is how small of an impact seasons actually make. In Forza Horizon 4, theres actually a decently sized difference between seasons with winter being all snowy, fall with the red leaves and wet streets. But in FH5? You could show me an ingame screenshot of the environment and I couldnt tell you which season it might be, even if you held me at gunpoint. Maybe the focus with the seasons was more the localized events, like sandstorms or heavy rain, but I feel like those barely happen. and even then...they are localized. you wont notice them, if you are on the opposite side of the map. 5. I have heard from some people that the game also has some issues with the DLCs, multiplayer lobbies, performance and some other things, but those are mostly things that I havent experienced yet or arent big issues for me. If you wanna know more about those, probably better to watch some videos about them or read some articles or something. I cant give much input there.With that being said, why should you get FH5 then, if it has so many issues? Well...those gripes are honestly just things that I PERSONALLY have issues with (and some other people as well). And it still has some nice QoL and can get you some hours for the price. If you dont care about the mentioned issues and you want more of FH4, or, if you just wanna dip your toes into the franchise, then you might enjoy the game. Otherwise you might wanna save your money for something else, or buy FH4 instead. TLDR: The game has issues, no doubt. The map feels pretty bland, the carpark feels empty and the series rewards feel boring, overall a pretty stale experience, once you reach endgame and start to run out of things you can do. Do I still recommend it, despite those issues? ehhh....Its essentially more of Forza Horizon 4. If you enjoyed that one, maybe buy Forza Horizon 5, when its 50% or more off, otherwise just stick to FH4 instead.

_childDocuments_.review: Forza Horizon 5 looks great, has a lot of content and lets you roam a big, varied map.And is ruined by the absolute shameful, unforgivable AI (or lack thereof).See, the drivatars you race against are a complete lie. There is no AI, there is no intelligence. Non-human cars do not obey the same physic as you do. They follow the racing line at a preset speed (which depends on the difficulty setting), as if they were on rails, no matter what car they're in.Only once you are very close to them does physic start to influence them, at which point they completely forget how to drive and usually brake, even if in a straigh road.So, your only chance to win (at higher difficulty level) is to take the lead very early, usually in the first few corners, by dive-bombing and ramming. Failing that, once the lead car get a couple of seconds in front of you (you always start a race mid-pack, so you're always at a disadvantage), you can forget about catching up. Just restart the race and ram harder...Oh, and obviously they cheat, they accelerate much faster than you, and in the off chance you get a significant lead, they rubberband back to you at insane speeds.Of course, you can lower the difficulty, at which point the game becomes a walk in the park. Not fun either.It is such a shame, because Forza Horizon 5 is a fun car game, but a terrible racing game...Edit : And to add insult to injury, the game is full of bugs (some small, some progression-breaking, all annoying), some of them having existed for months, and the devs don't seem to give a flying **** about it...

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game with a huge selection of cars and upgrades. Overall it is a beautiful looking game with a few minor issues with wheels clipping through fenders or the occasional light pole floating two feet above the ground. Driving physics is not meant to be a simulation but does provide a learning curve. The auction house has never been a viable system since there appears to be little to no effort to deter cheaters.Which brings me to one of my complaints, any of the online racing is almost assuredly a waste of time. Just about every race I've been in seems to either have a level 25 999 player (which would take over a thousand years to achieve without cheating) or level 2 player racing some low end car that ends up magically going around hairpin turns at full speed and winning by 30 seconds or more. If you don't have any interest in winning the online races, the only other caveat is the Eliminator, which is just arbitrary chance. Skill is meaningless; you just need to have the right car drop randomly next to you. This could be one of the all-time great racing games if Microsoft would actually do something about the rampant cheating and also eliminate the Eliminator.

There are hundreds of cars that they want you to spend extra money on.  There are areas on the map that look like new race events, but are, in reality, unskippable ads for DLC.  There are constant crappy voice over interruptions telling you to do things that jump on top of each other, repeat and glitch, and create an annoying distraction from what you want to do with this game in the first place which is just race.  The constant clingy need to prove that they're respecting Mexican culture while in reality just appropriating is insulting and patronizing.  They've taken what could have been a fun, open world racing experience and ruined it with constant interruptions, none of which can be skipped!  It makes the game a chore to play.

The pro :- Nice visuals- Enjoyable driving experience when alone on the roads- Love the designing tool (compared to The crew 2)- Love to be able to fine tune my car to my preference.The Cons- Grindy as hell- Nerf after nerf of the various ways to earn money- Some of the challenges are painfull, especially when having to compete against cheating AI.All in all, when played with friends (and the game keep in sync) it's nice and fun. Enough that I got 300 hours sunk into the game. So why the thumbs down ? Here is why :I did a 6 months break from the game, and decided I just wanted to take one of my car for a spin 2 days ago.I had the game using 100GB on my hard drive for the last 6 months, got the updates and all. But when I started it, reached the login to my Microsoft Xbox account, and then started the game, I got the nasty surprise to be presented with the Driver creation option and not being sent in my previous game.So here I am, 300 hours down the drain and having lost every singles of my achievements.After a bit of searching, I found out it's a common issue both on PC and console. A lot of players get corrupted save or error codes. In my situation I got nothing of such, no warning, no error code, just a complete reset of the user data save file.Now, after contacting the support I have to replay the Tutorial and reach the point that let a player go online. The very part I hate in every game who Gate the access to your friends through "Tutorials" and other mandatory things before you can join your friends online and can enjoy playing with them.Hate to have to do it a first time, or every single time a game decide you lost your datas (GTA 5, Dying Light, Forza Horizon 4 and 5). So, having lost everything, and not even sure I can get the rewards for the various Skins I made for a lot of car and shared online, I can't in good faith put anything else than a thumb down.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to preface by saying FH5 is the best arcade racing game on the market right now. If you want a solid racing game, pick it up. However, I can't necessarily recommend it as I think it's objectively a bad game and misses the mark on what makes a good racing game. It's missing things that I want so badly as a car guy but the devs just haven't implemented them in any entry. The things it nails, it REALLY nails, but the things it misses are deal breakers for me. The Good:- Great looking game- Handling physics feel incredibly good. Semi-realistic but still approachable- Massive selection of cars- Good campaign progression- Play it how you want to play it vibe. The Bad:- worlds most boring open world. It's so empty and so lifeless. The roads are incredibly boring to drive on. It's mind boggling to me that they have like two or three total windy mountain roads. This is the worst offender for me. It's incredibly small compared to other game's open worlds in 2024. I did not like The Crew 2 for many reasons but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that game's open world is so cool and interesting. Might not look the best but it had DETAIL. - Car building is lackluster. I feel like the only place you can truly make a car yours is the vinyl editor. There are less body kit selections then NFS games 10 years ago. Not to mention no way to tune exhaust sound, no way to truly dial in ride height and camber, etc. Building out a car should feel like I can make it truly my own and nothing like anyone else. But we all end up with the same cars due to the incredibly small selection of options.- Wheel spins. Loot boxes ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ suck. I paid $70 for this game have some crazy challenges to unlock crazy cars please. I don't want to hit wheel spins just to get a car I want since I can't buy it from auto show. ♥♥♥♥ is lame. - None of the races are all that interesting. Like there are no actual racetracks on the map, there's no large environment changes to make it feel like I'm going on a journey, and even Goliath does not feel like a long race. My favorite part of the crew is going on these 45 min long journeys through the map racing against other people. Would love to have that in forza! TLDR races feel like they are a means to an end vs an actual end.Anyways please just make a good racing game the bar is so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ low for car guys

_childDocuments_.review: I have almost 1000 hours in Forza Horizon 4. Half of it with controller and the other with a G29 Sim Racing Wheel. So obviously I love that game. But after that much time you need a different experience and that is where Forza Horizon 5 falls short. Because Forza Horizon 5 IS Forza Horizon 4. It’s the same game. Im playing the same game again. The differences are like a FIFA game. Now for a Forza Horizon that doesn’t have to be necessarily a bad thing. Forza Horizon 4 was after all an almost 10/10 game. The only things that it had to improve was its sense of speed, proper spots for dirt rally on the map a GOOD CITY maybe some better mountains for more offroad fun, Hill and Downhill races. It also had a lot off small things like the shifting stile being a difficulty setting (very annoying with a wheel) and its rater suboptimal class system. But Forza 5 changes none of that.Actual significant changes Pros:Better sense of speed thangs to ssdMore realistic car feel (better weight feel)Better Force Feedback (Sim Wheels)Much better car soundsCons:Terrible and uncreative map when compared to Forza 4No seriously it ruins the gameA lot less cars than Forza 4 (for now at least)More bugs than cyberpunk (mostly coop related)Conclusion: When you play with a controller just play Forza Horizon 4. The Force Feedback doesn’t affect you and the weight feel doesn’t do all that much. The map is worth it. When you play with a wheel and you can’t get enough off Forza or never played 4 before than the Force Feedback might be worth it or you just play assetto corsa.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't play racing games that much, but this one is different. I played a bit of Forza Horizon 4, but this one really nails the formula. There is so much customization, so many events, and it has some amazing cars. Progression is great and makes you feel rewarded no matter what you do. It is a game I can recommend easily simply because it gives you dopamine no matter what you choose to do. Forza Horizon 5 is a game that just wants you to have fun, no matter what you do, and I can easily say it nails that mission. From the Horizon Events that have you racing literal airplanes, just down to the XP signs and exploration, Horizon 5 just gives you happy juice no matter what. And its community has made some absolutely jaw-dropping car designs and vinyls that you can download and enjoy on your favorite cars. The amount of cars is staggering also, and the game is extremely generous when handing them out. By the first hour, you will have amassed some beautiful cars and that is just the beginning. There is much to unlock.The design editor is also extremely robust and friendly. There are many tools to get your car looking the way you want. Even if you aren't good at creating vinyl groups, you can download pre-made ones from the community and put them on any car you want. It is truly amazing just how much content there is in just customizing your cars appearance, and that doesn't even cover the absolute maddeningly detailed tuning system. Plus, if you do want to customize your car, it is extremely easy to understand and use, but an extraordinarily powerful tool if you master it.Finally the graphics. There is not much to say other than this game is the definition of paradise on earth. So many beautiful locations to explore. From mystic waterfalls, down to arid desert regions, to beautiful beaches, and deep into lush, rainy jungles. Forza Horizon 5 is a game that will make you step on the brakes and just marvel at its beauty, which is only enhanced by some impressive rain and dust storms.As for performance, for me performance has been buttery smooth. However, your mileage may vary based on reviews I have read, but to me this game is extremely well optimized and can maintain a smooth 60FPS easily without issues on the absolute highest graphics settings, RTX enabled. Never once have I encountered frame drops or chugging, nor have I crashed once. For a game as large as this, with this many cars and detailed environments, it is almost magical how this game can run so smooth. The developers at Playground Games are absolute wizard when it comes to optimization. My only gripe with this game comes down to monitization. As you can see on the Steam page, there is a VIP pass, a season pass, and a car pass. The Forza series is known for having some pretty bad monitization, but this isn't really an issue here in my opinion. I bought just the regular edition of Forza Horizon 5, and so far, there has been no reason to buy the car pass or VIP pass. All of the cars you get with the Car Pass can be obtained in the game pretty easily without hours of grinding. Leveling up is also extremely fair and you will be getting a new car probably every 40 minutes to an hour. There's also no way to purchase Wheelspins with real money, which is always a plus. This game may have monitization, but considering how much content is there, and the fact they don't let you purchase Wheelspins with real money is a massive win to me. Even if you aren't a racing game fan, I still recommend you check it out. You may be surprised just how approachable this game is and how addictive it can be. There is so much accessibility for everyone, and it is nice to have a game that just rewards you for doing stuff you want to do.  You will never struggle with what to do because everything you do in this game is rewarding, satisfying and fun. It is a game I am glad I paid $60 for and have no buyer's remorse, unlike with a lot of other games that came out this mouth.Give Forza Horizon 5 a go, and enjoy the absolute happiness this game will give you. And just remember, if you are not sure what to do, just hit the accelerator. You'll find your way to something truly satisfying on the horizon.

_childDocuments_.review: Forza Horizon 5 delivers an exhilarating experience that surpasses its predecessors in almost every aspect. Set against the stunning backdrop of Mexico, this open-world racing game offers a vast and diverse landscape to explore. From lush jungles to arid deserts, the attention to detail in recreating Mexico's varied terrain is truly impressive.The game boasts an extensive roster of cars, ranging from classic favorites to modern supercars, each meticulously rendered with lifelike detail. Whether you're tearing through city streets or conquering rugged off-road trails, the handling and physics feel incredibly realistic, providing a satisfying driving experience.One of the standout features of Forza Horizon 5 is its dynamic weather and day-night cycle, which not only adds visual variety but also introduces new challenges to races. Navigating through a sudden rainstorm or racing under the stars adds an extra layer of excitement and unpredictability to each event.The Horizon Festival returns bigger and better than ever, offering a plethora of events and activities to keep players engaged for hours on end. Whether it's competing in traditional races, tackling stunt challenges, or customizing your dream car, there's no shortage of content to explore.The online multiplayer component of Forza Horizon 5 is seamless and addictive, allowing players to connect with friends or compete against others in a variety of multiplayer modes. The addition of the Horizon Arcade, a collection of mini-games scattered throughout the world, adds even more opportunities for social interaction and friendly competition.Visually, Forza Horizon 5 is a masterpiece, with breathtaking scenery and meticulously detailed car models that showcase the power of next-generation gaming hardware. Combined with a dynamic soundtrack that perfectly complements the on-screen action, the game delivers an immersive audio-visual experience like no other.In conclusion, Forza Horizon 5 raises the bar for open-world racing games with its stunning visuals, diverse gameplay, and immersive world-building. Whether you're a casual racing fan or a hardcore enthusiast, this game offers something for everyone and is undoubtedly a must-play title for any gaming enthusiast.So expensive but the graphic so beautiful like a natural in realize, better forza horizon 4Recomended to play 4.5/5

_childDocuments_.review: Forza Horizon 5 is a great game! I purchased this game a while back as I had already bought and enjoyed Forza Horizon 4, and thought I would try it out on steam as well. It did not disappoint. I will go over what I felt was good and bad about this game below.First, lets start with the bad. In my opinion, the graphics are better on Forza Horizon 4 as I feel like there is less detail in the cars now. I also felt the map to be more crowded and found myself using the filter more often than I would in FH4, but maybe that was just because of more game content. Also, there was a limit introduced to the auction house that limits the amount of cars you can list every 24 hours. Next, it takes a lot of races to grind for money unless you find a money glitch or sell cars at the auction house, however that is a given with Forza games.That was the worst part of the review. Everything else, gameplay-wise, was better executed. I liked the story-line much more than the previous version, as I though that the vibrant Mexican culture introduced into this version was very interested. I liked that it tied into Mexico's history of cars. I liked the selection of cars available, and felt it was much different to FH4 in a good way. I also liked the landscape in this game, such as the active volcano (was one of my favourite spots in the game). Finally, this drives the same way North American roads would drive, and coming from Canada this makes the game feel much more immersive.Overall, I would recommend the game, especially if it's the first in your Forza series. If you have tried FH4, it might not make sense for another game, however if you have extra steam credits, or you completed the old game, I'd still recommend it over other games! Happy Racing!

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best racing games out there for people who prefer fun over realism. The game manages to have accurate weight carry, cars, driving, and more while still managing to let go 1000+ feet on a jump. With monthly series to do so you can get rare cars, public events, and a a large variety in races you're bound to find something you enjoy. There's a car for everyone and a track along side it. Are there some parts that could use improvement? Yes. Could there be more wheel compatibility? Yes. But it still manages to capture you, especially if you're new to the series.----Pros----- Re-playable races- Lots of roads to explore- Multiple car upgrades to make them useful anywhere- Amazing graphics, even low settings can be good enough for some people- Multiple languages, helped me learn French- Many brands and cars in them, alongside collabs and pop culture things- Community interactive- You feel fine without the DLCs---Cons---- Lack luster map if you're coming from Forza Horizon 4, drove most people away from the game- Feels like it's mostly rally focused, so other types of racing aren't as big- Low wheel compatibility, only a select few tend to read without any hassle- No trading feature, so trying to get a rare car from a friend is you just hoping you buy it first in the Auction House------- Before You Buy -------- Play this game if you like cars, if you're someone who's more technical about them or want something more realistic go for something like iRacing or Assesto Corsa.- Play it with a wheel if you can, and turn on manual shifting.- You can get almost any wheel to work, but you may need a 3rd party client to get it to read.- Turn on manual shifting. It's faster. And there is no denying that.- Never bought one map expansion or major DLC yet at ~350 hours of play time. Nor have I had an intense want for one.- Turn on your favorite song or call with your favorite friends, you'll have a blast.- DO THE SERIES WHEN YOU START PLAYING. I didn't understand what they were and missed out on some great cars.- If you need to buy a car from the auto show, you'll find it cheaper on the Auction House most likely.- If you want a limited time car that you missed, join the Official Forza Discord and ask around for it. But have some money at hand.

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels hollow and meaningless. There's no progression. You don't feel like you're achieving anything. You're not overcoming challenges. The game just feeds everything to you right from the start and only a few hours in I felt like I'd already seen it all. You know when you do a cheat code to unlock everything and turn on god mode, and it's cool for a little while but then you realise there's nothing left to do and it's actually not that fun? Forza Horizon 5 feels like that right from the start. You start with a tricked out Corvette and a sick rally car. About every thirty minutes the in game lottery will give you a new car and about half of them are also top class cars. Right from the start. There's six classes (D, C, B, A, S1, S2) and you START with S1 and A cars. The bottom three classes are basically meaningless unless you... want to do slow races, or something? There's no progression up from slow to fast, you just start at fast.Not that it matters! Almost all the races let you enter with any car and will pick matching opponents for you. There's no need to get faster cars to play the harder events and progress that way. No, you just show up in WHATEVER, and then just participating gets you 75% of the possible progression points ("accolade points") that event has. Winning gets you the other 25%, which feels insignificant and is entirely unnecessary to actually progress, so why bother?The open map challenges are much the same. Three levels of difficulty to achieve - and you start equipped to very easily get two stars on all of them.The game becomes a very bland grind of driving around the map to do unchallenging and unsatisfying activities just to tick them off the list. It's so dull.It's a real shame, because it does look gorgeous and the car controls actually feel great, but that's not enough by itself. I'd rather go play NFS Heat, which is also gorgeous and plays great but ALSO has meaningful big-picture gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: Forza Horizon 5 is a good game when playing by yourself, however it becomes a great game when you have a group of friends to play with and you introduce fun ideas for possible freemode challenges and builds. The issue with FH5's solo play is that in the end of the day it is still a Horizon game where once you have done every race and own every car there isn't a great deal of content left. Sure there is the weekly festival events where you will do races and PR stunts to get wheelspins and cars, but in the end it starts to feel repetitive. The real fun in FH5 in my opinion is when it is played with friends, preferably in a voice call, where as a group you can just ignore any 'challenges' set by Playground Games and begin to set your own challenges. In one instance me and a group of 3 others set out to ourselves to use certain car types within a certain performance index while leaving the cars stock and then perform challenges such as a sound test to see who's car sounds the best followed by events such as a hill climb sprint, drag race, top speed test and then finished with a breaking test to see whose car would score highest. There was no prize, only entertainment value for having fun in different cars as a group. In the end I would recommend this game, as for the first 50-100 hours the game can be played solo with a plentiful amount of content to entertain yourself quite fruitfully. However if you wish to play this game for the long term, I would only recommend it to those who have a friendship group that also play.
