_childDocuments_.review: Maybe it's just me but what on earth is this game?!? I would've rather payed 60€ for Far Cry 6 than 70€ for this extraordinary boring game. To be fair I got this in the August sale for only 30€ and actually payed full price for Far Cry 6, the game with almost the worst story and missions ever. Still I got 200 hours of playtime there because it was fun, fun that started right after the first cut scene. Oh and Far Cry 6 also featured a tutorial and essential stuff like that.But with this game? Nooo you get a loading screen with the controller key binds being shown, then a super quick introduction of half the necessary features, then you're on your own. After the introduction (I can't name it tutorial because  it didn't teach me enough basics) I could drive forward, backward, left, right and most importantly I could change the camera view.  As someone who has never played a proper racing game before this is very frustrating, I don't know how to drift, how to make a U turn nor how to do any other of these tricks that you buy a racing game for. In non racing games the controls of a car are obviously very simplified but they work well and they're easy to get into. Not the case here. Anyway lets get more to the game itself, where should i start... okay the intro, which is epic!!! It makes the game feel super fun and the slomo in the air reassures you that this purchase was worth it. At first all you do is drive on normal roads where you don't have to drift or slow down to get around the corners. The graphics are astoundingly well, 4k is easily playable with the RTX 30 series and the frame rate is top. Animations feel smooth and you don't lose any performance at all while in the dust. The introduction and story hits like the song Running up that Hill from Kate Bush after it appeared in the Netflix series Stranger Things. The whole game itself seemed amazing at first. Now the part where it starts to get weird is actually still within the intro, after your first few drops onto the road you start to think "well really cool game and all but when does this constant we drop you here onto the map and now there, next stop is this weird temple and oh prepare for your next drop onto yet another road". This part of the intro gives you a feeling of being controlled rather than controlling what happens in the game. After being dropped around the map the main story characters start to make jokes that are supposed to be jokes ig, I couldn't really figure out if they were jokes or not because they were unfunny as hell. Unfunny characters can be ignored, if you don't like the story just rush it and so on. Now you're probably thinking okay this guy just straight up hates this game for no reason and i wouldn't hate you if you think that. I thought that too which is why I kept up playing  to get a better expression until the point where I really just forced myself to like this game. In the intro you've been dropped onto roads at a few interesting locations, however once you get to drive around freely you realize that you've been dropped at a few interesting locations, which are in fact the only few interesting locations. The rest of the map is full of nonsense roads that spread out in the desert, it's boring. And the few races I played weren't something exciting. Let me tell you the main thing that just pisses me off. If a game literally blends in an advertisement that's built like the I Phone 15 ad  then you really start to wonder "wtf I paid for this, other people who payed full price will also get this ad". The ad is built to make the VIP thingy look like something that you could actually want as a consumer while adding less thing to the game than the "new" and "revolutionary" I phone 15. The fact that this is even possible is mind blowing but can be explained by the fact that the VIP subscription only adds weekly wheelspins, cars were already in the game before and instant unlocking a house that already existed is not new either.Not to mention the fact that this happened within 30 minutes of playtime, that is pretty outrageous if you ask me. I mean if this VIP subscription actually added something besides new cars then yeah maybe that is a cool thing for hardcore racing lovers. All you get is some VIP cars which will allegedly "boost" your game, weekly wheel spins and access to the player house, which if you already grinded your way through the game can be unlocked without this extra 20€ purchase. So in case you already bought the house, you are left with your 3 Forza Edition cars and weekly wheel spins. I'm not bothered by the fact that this exists at all, I'm bothered by the fact that this VIP stuff is actively being advertised in a game I payed for. Also tbh, why would anyone pay for a game and then buy VIP as a way to boost their progress, don't you want to get lots of hours of playtime in a game you literally payed for? But that's just my thinking. Overall if you know how to drive in Forza games and like a vast boring map then you shouldn't pay any attention to my review, this is just a first impression from somebody who isn't into racing games but always wanted to try one out. From a graphics standpoint this game far exceeded my expectations, from a gameplay perspective it has fallen behind. I would have further checked this game out if I didn't want my 30€ to go to waste because i wasn't enjoying it. I'm allowing comments so people with more than just first impressions can correct false things or impressions I have made

_childDocuments_.review: Forza Horizon 5 takes the exhilarating racing series to new heights, delivering an unforgettable open-world experience that's bound to leave players in awe. The game's breathtaking Mexico setting serves as the perfect backdrop for a diverse range of environments and challenges, from sprawling cities to serene countryside and everything in between. The attention to detail is truly remarkable, with stunning visuals that showcase the beauty of the landscape and the meticulously crafted cars.The gameplay is as thrilling as ever, offering a seamless blend of arcade-style racing and realistic physics. Whether you're tearing through the desert in a high-performance sports car or off-roading through dense jungles, the controls feel responsive and satisfying. The variety of events and activities available keeps the game feeling fresh, from traditional races to creative showcases and engaging stunt challenges.The social aspect of Forza Horizon 5 is a standout feature. The shared open world allows players to seamlessly interact with others, whether it's through cooperative challenges, competitive races, or simply exploring together. The Horizon Arcade mode, in particular, offers a playful and dynamic way to enjoy multiplayer mayhem.Customization options are extensive, allowing players to personalize their cars and avatar with a wide array of options. The progression system strikes a good balance between rewarding exploration and skillful driving, offering a sense of achievement without feeling overly grindy.While Forza Horizon 5 excels in many areas, it's not without minor drawbacks. Some players may find certain events or challenges repetitive after extended playtime, and occasional technical glitches can momentarily disrupt the immersive experience.In the end, Forza Horizon 5 is a triumphant addition to the series, delivering a visually stunning, action-packed, and socially engaging racing experience that's a must-play for fans of the genre. With its vast and vibrant world, diverse range of vehicles, and captivating gameplay, it's a game that's sure to keep players hooked for hours on end.

_childDocuments_.review: The game itself is insane, probably the one arcade racing game to play if you are into racing games. I do say arcade racer but its not like NFS or The Crew which are hardcore arcade racers. This is somewhat in between arcade and sim but can be more arcadey if you want.There's a wide variety of cars to choose from so no one is left out (although could use more SUVs). Very in-depth tuning and a lot of performance upgrades for most cars. This time some performance upgrades affect the sound of the car as well.Visually, the game is insane...if it works on maxed out settings. I have a 3070 and still cannot get it to work at 60FPS maxed out at 1440P (even 40FPS is not very stable) but it looks so much better on Xbox sadly which is a weaker system. Hopefully they optimize it.I usually don't care about the single player of games like this where multiplayer is an option and in FH5 as well, I don't care about the single player. They tried for a story or dialogue but its just cringey and would be better off with just one person telling everything to us rather than having multiple characters repeating the same dialogues over and over again. But hey its a racing game with multiplayer so for me that's not a downside.The online is well, its great when it works. The leaderboards are filled with hackers so have fun trying to get a legit score on there. But playground games cannot let people use most of the custom designs because its a kids game and ban the creators indefinitely. Mind you that on kid accounts for Xbox, most of the online content is disabled unless parents enable it. Considering how big tunes, liveries and tracks are in this game its really detrimental for the community. The devs are just on a power trip on banning people.Even after the patch the performance is horrible for the game (I've reset my PC so that is not at fault here). FH4 ran much much better and looked better too (since I cannot play above the high preset very well). The roads randomly turn into rainbow and black boxes. The foliage is just TV static and tons of bugs like suddenly stopping the car and falling out of the map.TL;DR: One of the best if not the best open-world racing games but can go downhill real fast if the devs don't patch the major issues like hacking, online disconnects and performance. All they do right now is ban people randomly for sharing a spongebob like livery. I wish I could give a neutral rating on Steam but for now a negative will have to do.

_childDocuments_.review: While this game does have strengths over its predecessor (handling fixes and engine noises primarily) it feels like it falls down in every other respect. Chief among which is that the world is so soulless and boring compared to the map of 4s. It feels shockingly empty and bland whereas it felt like every area in 4 was unique and recognisable. In regular Forza fashion, you get bombarded in this game with things to do without any of it actually feeling appealing to the player. Because of this, the sense of progression is even more belittled than even 4 was. I've already given up with this game and while I may come back to play more of it in the future, I don't see myself ever getting anywhere near the amount of playtime here than I got out of 4. It's a shame 4 is being delisted soon, because it remains a superior game.

_childDocuments_.review: First time getting back into the Horizon series since the first game back in 2012 and I am really enjoying this! The visuals are great, there's a ton of cars to choose from, lots to explore and different kinds of activities and races to do! Playing with friends is also easy to connect and fun. _childDocuments_.review: Is Forza Horizon 5 a fun game? Yes. Is it possibly the best arcade racing game on the PC right now? Probably yes. Hundreds of cars, a really fun map, tuning and a lot of challenges - what's not to love?Well, the technical aspect, that's what. Playing with others is either totally painless and fun or a nightmare. Some of the challenges are terribly designed. Sometimes the game crashes, sometimes it registers button presses while the controller sits on my lap. While some things have been patched, most haven't and that is, for such a big game studio, simply unacceptable, especially because Horizon 3 and 4 had some of the same issues so they should've fixed them a LONG time ago.I don't regret buying or playing the game but sometimes it feels like it's been created by a much smaller developer and that just sucks.EDIT: After both of the DLCs got released, I have to say I'm freaking disappointed. Even more technical issues, very limited content (especially the rallye dlc, damn)...it's such a mess that I'd honestly recommend you to only buy them on sale, anything else is just a waste. Horizon 5 is still an amazing game but as a huge fan I just feel like the developers try their hardest to make me regret my affections.

_childDocuments_.name: Forza Horizon 5

_childDocuments_.review: Hm, yeah, solid entry in the Horizon series like usual. As per usual, good map, good physics, good graphics, runs well, nothing too broken, more than enough content, ... - I think you know these games by now.The downside of it is just that it gets generic real fast. There is nothing special compared to the previous games, there is rarely something special between races itself and the open world activities are also always the same. They also kept the stupid story missions from Horizon 4 which I hated.Combined with providing a lot of hours worth of content, it becomes draining to complete everything. I can't say I'm excited to start playing, neither am I excited for the next game in the series (however I'm probably still going to play it at some point). They need to switch something up; the "make money and followers (rep)" strategy is just so old by now. You also get pretty high-end cars real fast, so making money to grind to better cars is also a useless/missing motivation, making races even more repetitive. Ugh.So yeah, it's definitely a good game, albeit being repetitive. If it's your first time you'll probably enjoy it a lot, if you have played the previous games probably not so much.Definitely only buy it on sale, take your time and don't dedicate yourself to 100% completing it.It by the way also runs beautifully on Linux, which surprised me a little since this is a Microsoft game after all.

_childDocuments_.review: My first expectations of the game were based largely on the previous game in the series, not anyone but the iconic Forza Horizon 4. Unlike most people, I was expecting exactly a game that was quite similar to the previous one with very slight improvements, and it lived up to those slight expectations. My first impressions when I got into the game were kind of mixed. I certainly saw the improved graphics and I really liked how much fresher the game itself was based in Mexico. FH4, which was based in England, was quite "colder"I'm pretty happy with the gameplay itself. Whether I want to play singleplayer or multiplayer I know I can have fun playing either mode. I want to pay more attention to the multiplayer, however. I spent quite a few hours in it and had quite a few good moments, but like everything else there were some downsides. I've run into hackers in a few sessions, but I've seen people complain about their far more frequent occurrence. I've personally seen hackers quite rarely, but it's not like they don't exist. I've also seen quite a few modded max level accounts and so on, which is pretty ugly and unprofessional for a game of this level.That aside the multiplayer is a wonderful place with room for everyone. Want pure races of various kinds? There's Horizon Open for you. Prefer to drift? There is a special place where all drifting competitions are organized. Or maybe you fell in love with the battle royale modе that was added in FH4? Well, it's here too, so I guess there's something for everyone to enjoy. The game currently has 97 achievements. You can do quite a few of them by going through the game's story, as well as through the Hot Wheels DLC. The ones you won't get by going through the singleplayer are pretty fun and show different details of the game that you might not notice unless you're focused on getting those exact achievements, but I really think it's worth the try to be completed.Aside from the intro to the game, you'll be able to alter your difficulty settings at any time in Forza Horizon 5. It pretty much depends on you. You can either make the game very easy for you or very hard. I suggest starting with the lower difficulties and gradually working your way up. I know you'll see yourself taking more money as you raise the difficulty, but you'll make a lot of money anyway just by playing and forget about watching your credits. Ignore them and you won't know when you have so much money that you don't know how you can even spend.The graphics are very beautiful. So beautiful that they make you feel warm inside while looking at them. And that big open world that you can roam around and explore... The graphics are so good that a lot of players like to just set up cruises with each others, drive slowly and enjoy. What can I say about Photo mode... I'll let the pictures speak for me.The Soundtrack of Forza Horizon 5 features over 100 songs available through six radio stations, each with a different genre and host. However i prefer to listen to my playlists on Spotify but some people prefer the in-game music and it ok so i don't mind it. I had no problems at all.Game tested on:The game isn't that new anymore and it gets discounted often, so I think it's best to wait for a discount and when you see it get it right away. The game is truly unique and worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: Note: This is coming from a long time GT fan and his first "Forza Horizon" video game. The review isn't one sided; the reason why I don't recommend it in its current state is because the cons outweights the pros. I might change this in the future if the cons are fixed. I've got to say that the RWD, FWD and AWD in this game just feels right. Understeering and oversteering are factors for all type of drivetrains which in some games aren't entirely existant. The only downside to physics is that jumping for thousand of feet in the air doesn't kill the car's suspension or better yet, doesn't bring your driver to the hospital! Lots of customization for both liveries and tuning. I was very happy to see that parts for the car like engines and drivetrains can be completely changed. This also changes the sound the car makes which is a nice addition. As for livery, I am aware that players are getting banned for some really stupid reasons. So be very aware of what liveries you share! Super7, eventlabs, etc. Community made content is what makes both a game good and bad. In this case, I'd say it's average for this game. Some of the community content are garbage and have thousands of likes. I mean, as an example, Super7 probably have hundreds of cards which hold the same jumps, highway runs and let's not forget go down that one huge mountain WITHOUT CHEATING! But yes, I'll leave this as a pro for now because I still enjoy it overall. Probably one of the best thing out there when it works. Playing with friends is what makes a game better if not best. It's sad to see that the servers have been struggling a lot and sometimes if not most of the time one of your friends will drop out due to something stupid like the servers not responding. To save up some ressources, I've decided to play the game in High settings. The game looks gorgeous! With photo mode you can take pictures that looks very semi-realistic. You could show it to a co-worker or a friend and they would totally believe it's your car! The game servers are struggling a lot. I still don't understand why a high budget game can't learn from others and actually put a bit more money into the servers. Some people claims it's bad netcoding which I entirely would believe. But not being able to play online pretty much breaks most of the features of the game which also includes playing with friends. I've been mostly playing on Highly Skilled as I felt like it was the somewhat less BS difficulty. And I mean less because the rubber banding in this game is way too obvious. The rubber banding is also only one sided. You make a mistake and you will not be able to catch up the AI. This can be clearly seen in single lap races when you have the best lap but end up coming in second place with an AI that has 3 seconds of lap time behind you. I do admit racing can't do AI right, even Gran Turismo has AI flaws. This is also one of the worse things I've seen in a game. Playing with randoms. It wouldn't be bad if you didn't need to do any of those, but the game forces you to do those races in order to win prices in a weekly "seasonal" event. Even in team races, the Forza community will still fight for first place. Some will push you, others will ram you out of the checkpoints. It's a bit of a frustrating experience so to say. Rarely you will get players who race "clean" but this is probably most likely due to the AI of the game forcing you to constantly play aggressively. I'm sure there isn't entirely a solution to this problem, but at least if there was a better collision detector it would probably at least make this less of a con. This game feels like a beta of an alpha version of a game. Things are VERY, VERY game breaking. Horizon Super7 cards crashing your game. The game teleporting you to areas you are not even suppose to be in. The game constantly pausing itself to show you progress while you're in the middle of something. Some car have non-working spoilers which is funny. This is just to name a few things I've gotten through in the 60 hours of gameplay I have.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great follow-up to Forza Horizon 4, Mexico is a big map, with a lot of sidetracks to discover, mountains to climb and weather conditions to test your driving skills in. A lot of the same cars make a come-back from FH4, but that doesn't make it repetitive. For sure, more (new) cars are needed, but overall with stunning visuals (if you can activate Ray-tracing) an excellent soundtrack, and the same good-old gameplay that made FH4 so adictive, Forza Horizon 5 is an easy recommendation for any casual arcade drivers, or anyone that want a close to life driving experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm late to the game but the game is great, has great car variety, fun races, more than forgiving difficulties and penalties, an amazing and welcoming community, and fun and cool ways to get cars and credits. The Auction house can get pretty cutthroat and appears to have a bot problem, but the wheel spin system at least makes up for it. Most of your money comes from wheel spins which you get on level ups, and there is a variety of races and activities where you can get them. Some cars are locked behind events and passes but are at least obtainable through Auction house and for quite the penny. Overall, I give this game a 8.5/10 for being a fun and amazing racing game and being better than NFS. I would definitely recommend this game to friends and relatives. Great for PC too. Multiplayer joining needs some work tho as well as proper crossplay.

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty fun "Adventure" themed open world racing game. It does a few things quite well in order to crack through to me, someone dealing w/ ADHD. In my experience, most open ended / open world games occupy one of two extremes: Completely directionless play (Minecraft Creative mode) and "The ubisoft tower" of completing one simple objective and having hundreds of chores immediately unlocked on your map. This game sits somewhere in between those, though its exact position oscillates as you play, and can be influenced by what you're doing.You start the game doing something cool immediately, and get to sample a few different kinds of cars and styles of racing right out of the gate. The game doesn't shy away from showing you how large its map is, but it intelligently hides most of the content that's on offer. Unlocking more is based on choices you make as you pursue the threadbare, albeit competent story the game has. It has an almost MMO-oriented pacing in regard to how you pursue content and unlock more to do. Different styles of races and environments have their own "quest givers" and "quests" to complete, which will unlock races that offer progression towards the next narrative beat, and a handful of side races that you can do for fun or rewards. If you ever feel stuck on what to do, the game contains an AI companion of sorts that you can call upon any time to guide you to an objective, loosely based on the kind of progression you've asked it to guide you to.I've played 60 something hours, dabbling in all of the race varieties I've come across, including setting foot into each major DLC. Nowhere near a "done" state with the game. I do think it becomes a bit less ADHD-accessible when you approach the end game, as the game gradually cares less about hiding what's available. The content distribution and volume is likely to have something you'll really enjoy, and you can really focus down on 1-2 styles of play and still have a ton to do.The only drawback with that play style is the reward mechanisms the game has, when combined with how many cars and other kinds of rewards there are. You might find yourself satisfied with circuit and street based racing, but if you want to unlock certain cars, certain emotes, and complete the story, you're going to have to engage with cross-country and off-road races, too.Not a bad game to play solo or with friends. Competitive types will likely end up disappointed, there isn't a ranked mode and the Horizon Open consisting of random races with random players takes away some of the satisfaction. Time trials exist for every course (whether they're official in-game courses or community made), though a significant portion of the top spots on the leaderboard are occupied by cheaters. Those that trail behind them have completely mastered the art of breaking the tuning system outside of its semi-realistic responses to your adjustments, extracting more performance from cars than they otherwise could, and they drive those cars exceptionally well. If you choose to compete here, you'll probably need to feel satisfied with placing in the top 5% or top 1% of times, or only comparing yourself to your friends.At the end of the day, this game has a ton to do, but the quality of any one thing it does is diminished. Not as much as you think, since this is the 5th Horizon game, built upon the legacy of the motorsports series that came before it, but other titles that specialize in one or two areas are going to be more satisfying to players seeking specific kinds of experiences (arcade/"fun" oriented physics, simulation-based physics, competitive racing in multiple formats, more concise track lists for the community to compete on and benchmark their performance with, etc.). Worth mentioning that there's an absurd amount of accessibility options to accommodate most disabilities and a dial your own difficulty system that will allow for just about everyone to play regardless of ability.

_childDocuments_.review: --PROLOGUE--I Started the franchise with Horizon 3 back in 2017. I had to choose 3 since I didn't (and still don't) actually own a Xbox. I saw it as an amazing sandbox racer unfortunately plagued by major instability and same-y type event customization. And to be honest, going into this installment I had expected to find more of the same.I couldn't have been more wrong.--PROS--The representation of Mexico for this game is, to put simply, fantastic. Lush jungles and beautiful coastlines in the south, with rugged forests and mountains up north, Filled in with deserts and plains in the middle, not to mention one of the best urban areas in any Horizon game to date.The base lineup of cars this time around is excellent in terms of both variety and performance, comprising of everyday sedans and classic muscle cars to racing trucks and Warthogs, even full-on Formula Drift cars, with the best hypercars reserved for the wealthiest and best of drivers. Each vehicle you choose can be customized extensively for performance and looks.I'm also glad to see character customization continues to expand in new and unique ways. Do wish more hairstyles and racesuits would be added though (Stig suit when).Online multiplayer no longer requires Xbox Live on the Steam version, meaning all the best Horizon races are available to play free from day one, as well as custom gamemodes such as Survivor, Flag Rush, Eliminator, and more. Online also allows access to thousands of custom blueprints and races, which in some cases completely transform the enviroment into a different place entirely. You can also build your own blueprints and race events as well.There also seems to be very few bugs and no crashes, a vast improvement compared to FH3.--CONS--It is EXPENSIVE to even get into the game, getting to $45 - $50 on sale at BEST, even during the giant Winter Sale, which is when I purchased it.The AI does seem unstable at times, with difficulty increases suddenly finding your majorly upgraded vehicle left behind by miles. I personally recommend starting at Highly Skilled to counter this, only moving up to Expert if you feel comfortable or when prompted.Personally, my only big complaint is that having certain cars locked to online events and challenges does create problems when trying for a complete collection, especially when these events are time limited.I also have concerns that lower end computers may struggle to run this at a decent framerate, but can be remedied by lowering graphics settings appropriately.--SUMMARY--There's simply no other arcade racer out there that competes with the level of detail and control that Forza Horizon 5 provides. With it's extensive personalization and vehicle lineup, not to mention a massive open world rivaling those of the best RPGs, this game definitely wins top trumps for pure size and ambition. It's a wonderful achievement that will surely go down as one the best racing games ever created.It might even be there already.

_childDocuments_.review: For the record: I bought the Ultimate Edition. I have all prior games with all prior expansions/DLC for Forza Horizon, and almost everything going all the way back to Forza 2 on that side. I am massive, massive Forza fan and it's likely someone playing one of these for the first time may not even be able to associate some of these as issues, what with the game industry just generally being as unacceptably bankrupt with product launch and post-game support as it has been lately. I want to make it abundantly clear before the rest of this kicks off: I believe they can fix or at least remedy most if not all of the problems with this game... given a few months' time and a lot of elbow grease, though there may potentially be some things they just cannot patch out as issues- namely the current iteration of the driveatar system, or complete lack thereof, and what they appear to have replaced 16 years of Turn 10's work with.Because I'm going to be so harsh on it after this, let me point out some serious positives to this game first. Amazing world design overall, up there if not outright matching that of Forza Horizon 3 while adding the wrinkles of seasons from Forza Horizon 4. Graphically masterpiece-tier. The raytracing reflections on the car running on my 1080 make the cars look closer to what they did in Forza 7- like cars rather than overglossy plastic. I couldn't bring myself to play with it off, even with the performance hiccups it might be bringing- it was too integral to the feel of the game. Fantastically executed. The world, too, feels like a living, breathing place. Sandstorms will kick up in the dry season (in weird places, mind, and sadly do not affect physics or handling that much). Most of the map transforms into a slick during the wet season, and the mists that swirl in the swamp can and will give way to random bouts of fog. This game, for all its faults, is still without question a technical triumph on what they've put together (don't conflate this with smooth performance, more on that later). I recommend going to see Digital Foundry's video on optimized settings for FH5. I was able to get it to run at 50-60 on a GTX 1080 with those, for what metric that may be worth (I also run a setup with four 1080P monitors and it was running on one of those, so take that with a slight grain of salt).This game has also now beaten the desire straight out of me to play it until they fix some of the more glaring issues. Between the patch on the 3rd of December, and what immediately seems like they've completely dropped the work Turn 10 has done on the driveatar system to have a unique selling point... They have instead replaced the built up AI behavior, and just made what you're racing against based on replays which I can only assume they intend to use machine learning on (which on all difficulties are sped up). It's intensely annoying to race against, and takes me out of the experience so often.Graphically the game is a marvel... but you're going to drop well below 60 regularly even on a GTX 1080 because they omitted some very essential optimization features, not least of which is the intensive and GPU consuming process of cloud generation. There are no options for that, it thinks my monitor runs at 59 hertz and does not give me an option to force 60 for proper VSync to function, and on top of that, as Digtal Foundry has noted in their optimized settings guide, the VSync option provided will give you a fairly decent-sized performance hit regardless of system, and you're better off just turning on VSync in your graphic's card's control panel. The result is a game that cannot run smoothly even above natural refresh rate and literally required the game ready drivers or better to not be a total performance mess (bizarre thing I'm not sure how many have run into: at one point I had 3-5 crashes an hour, I was never able to track down a reason, it just... stopped at one point during my last week with the game). Give it, at minimum, a few months, I'd argue. Right now it's not the refined experience you expect if you've played a prior entry (even from the relatively jank launches this side franchise has had compared to the main Forza's titles), and doesn't even have many of the options and features of the prior entry that were there at launch. Whether you can look past these issues or not... do your research a little, because unfortunately, a text review cannot exemplify most of the problems this game has very aptly, nor are you guaranteed to have anywhere near the same experience as I did. As always, your mileage will vary.And thus, the condition of this thing smarts, and it smarts hard. It smarts that higher difficulties literally play out like sped up replays that have been spliced together. It smarts that the AI gets a massive head start and rubber bands like there was no conception of time in the game. It smarts that the AI completely ignores the laws of physics you must obey in accordance to these replays, breaking my immersion in the only way I have to engage with it much while I have no patience for the netcode. It smarts that there's so much good... hindered by so many issues. To the devs: Please fix, I'll wait. When you're charging $100 for the full product ahead of time, your fans deserve better than what you have delivered, and we have come to expect far better than what you have delivered on PC already from the past two games. Do us a solid and bring back the driveatar system, if it's even possible. It was a far better solution than this... thing... you've hackneyed together to replace it.

_childDocuments_.review: Positive Note:* Content Rich - Hundreds of quality cars to drive.* Amazing Map - Miles of road with a few towns to drive around in, deserts to roam around in, and jungle to traverse through.* Great Physics Model - Love the way everything has an action movie feel to it. This is by no means a simulator but finds a way to give the impression that your playing one. Things can get pretty competitive however, if your into that. * Stunning Races - Hundreds of races to participate in whether your in single-player or multi-player. You have the choice to run a competitive race or a fun race and there is match making that supports both.* Great Community - The people in the community mostly want to have fun when playing and when I encounter a bad social interaction I can leave and join another match quickly, indulge their bad behavior and turn it into something else, or just simply switch to offline mode.* Controller Support - Does not require Steam Input to play! Has full controller support built in and supports most controllers right out of the box. Just make sure in the game properties from your steam library (not steam's actual settings) you uncheck Steam Input to get full controller support just through this game specifically and nothing else.* My favorite thing to do when I get bored is to play with the auction house. This is just one way to make money and it's quite fun to do so. One could just successfully play through the game by using the auction house just by itself. It is allot of work and time however but possible.* I seem to keep coming back to this game time after time. The replay value is out of this world! So many things to do and ways to play. Multi-player or single-player you’ll have something unique to do or participate in. Negative Note:* Releases old content from previous titles as new content for current title. Holds said content back and filters through the game until it’s been a year now since release and we still don’t have all the original content that would have come with it.* Reuses old content for new DLC releases that the customer pays double the price for. The 2nd dlc thankfully Doesn’t do that.* Optimization is kind of subjective here. I used to think it didn’t run well on my pc because of that. After lowering the settings more it works flawlessly. I have a great graphics card but my cpu and ram will need an upgrade before I can reach full potential. Unfortunately most games don’t have alternate content and/or rendering methods that allow for lower end cpu usage. * Paid DLC is a controversial topic of interest. The game itself cost $59.99 and the highest edition at $99.99. You get both expansions and whatever DLC was available at the time up to when the expansions released. After that you have to purchase the newer DLCs. I purchased premium in full the year it came out. Now about two years later, I purchased the remaining DLC. This is very subjective. All in all, if you have disposable income and want to spend it on this hobby great. If not, there are so many other timeless games and mods you can play that are free or it’s something you already own. Golf, basketball, shooting and shooting ranges, hiking, boating, and etc all have their expenses. It’s just the cost of anything and especially nowadays when it’s not only the developers that need to make money. Choices and forks in the road.

_childDocuments_.review: Fans of the genre will be completely satisfied with the thrilling and engaging racing experience that Forza Horizon 5 offers. This most recent game in the renowned Forza Horizon series transports players on an incredible journey through a colorful and varied open-world setting, making it a must-play for both racing fans and casual gamers.Forza Horizon 5 has an unmatched selection of nearly 500 painstakingly recreated vehicles, from vintage classics to contemporary supercars, which truly sets it apart from its competitors. Every player may select their ideal vehicle and take it out on the open roads thanks to the meticulous attention to detail in the car models, their handling, and the enormous variety available.The gaming mechanics are easy to understand and smooth, finding the ideal balance between enjoyment and realism. Forza Horizon 5 features a variety of difficulty settings and driving aids to accommodate players of all experience levels, whether they are seasoned racing veterans or newcomers to the game. Additionally, the game has a dynamic AI engine that adjusts to your play, making the entire experience tough and interesting.The multiplayer aspect of the game is one of its distinguishing elements. Players can participate in thrilling cooperative and competitive events in the shared open environment that is seamlessly incorporated into Forza Horizon 5's gameplay. The multiplayer component of this wonderful game adds still another level of excitement and interpersonal engagement, whether players are competing against friends in races or working together to complete cooperative tasks.When it comes to fostering a sense of adventure and freedom, Forza Horizon 5 excels. The enormous open world is brimming with things to do, things to see, and secrets just waiting to be found. There's always something fresh and exciting to experience, whether you're tearing across the countryside in a cross-country race, competing in pulse-pounding street races, or taking on exhilarating daredevil challenges.Forza Horizon 5 is a masterpiece in the racing genre, to sum up. It provides racing game enthusiasts with a memorable adventure thanks to its stunning aesthetics, wide selection of cars, approachable gameplay, and interesting multiplayer features.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR: Game is alright, just go buy horizon 4 instead.This is one of those games that desperately needs a middle of the road rating option, because at it's core it is still a fantastic racing game we've come to know and love in the games of the forza series. The driving is tight and responsive, not floating too far off either end of the sim-cade tightrope and striking an excellent balance with how the cars feel in weight and grip. (Most of) The tracks are engaging and a blast to rip through in a majority of cars and performance classes and the open world is varied enough in surface and style to always have somewhere else to go or a new style to try. The cars, even with so few actually new inclusions are still well detailed and the sound improvement over Horizon 4 is tenfold.Yet in good faith I cannot recommend this game to anyone, despite singing it's praises above.The core of the game while still indisputably Horizon is hollow and of little extra substance than Horizon 4. Campaign? Even more unengaging than the previous entry. Chocked full of style and cultural references without having any point or driving force, no escalation in car type or class and a story so forgettable it retroactively makes 4's look better by comparison. It's basically a sandbox and while everything is done well or at the least passably there's just no incentive to experience anything but what they railroad you in to with regards to the story.Online? Still absolutely plagued by the previous entry's problems, some even exacerbated throughout this entry.Load times have been made somehow even longer even on ssd, and chances are half your lobby is gone by the time the race actually loads. The convoy system constantly breaks and splits your party or makes them invisible or a plethora of other issues that weren't even present in FH4. The world system somehow feels even emptier even with the same amount of players, none are to be found roaming or racing along the highway or doing much of anything really, might as well be playing horizon solo. The racing? Again plagued by the issues of it's predecessor. The lead ai on higher difficulties getting rubber banding from p1 all the way to the finish and lower difficulties being absolutely pointless if you have access to any way of steering your car at all. As for online racing it's basically flipping a coin on if your opponents have functioning brake keys, constantly using cars in front and walls to take corners instead, which I can't even blame them for as there's piss all incentive to race cleanly or for anything but 1st. While the collision detection system has been improved from fh4, ghosting players much more frequently it doesn't do anything to mitigate the issue as at the next corner without any repercussion your opponent can just attempt to barrel into you or a wall with minimal issue, even in team races.Cars are again being drip fed through content which for the most part isn't a bad thing, but there's so few new additions you're basically playing to get cars that they removed from fh4 for no discernible reason half the time. The customization has been improved and although still meager is better than previous offerings. The paint and vinyl system is still fantastic and the community always has excellent designs on offer (as long as they don't get banned for being funny or having any ethnic iconography).Open world activities and timed lap rivals are infested with cheaters, any seasonal car is hoarded and sold for max price on the auction house making it unobtainable for the average player without some decent luck or a massive time investment to grind out the money. Event Lab while plagued by low effort content also has some amazing tracks and ideas by the community and is by far the best way to enjoy this sandbox racing experience.It pains me to have to be so harsh on the game but with such little innovation and constant issues there's not much of a reason to pick it over horizon 4 unless you've already played that one and even then this just feels like an expansion of that game.There's a great game core here, there really is but it's mired in a box without a soul. Just go buy fh4 instead, because this game is much of the same with even less charm.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT 19/11/21: I've repurchased the game following the "hotfix" that was put out recently (nothing was immediate or hot about it, it was more of a patch), and my opinions of the game are now neutral, and I wish it was possible to leave a neutral review on Steam. I will leave this as a negative review for the time being, as I assume people looking through negative reviews are doing so to look for any sort of critique for a game, so here's my experiences after the hotfix dropped.One positive thing that I can say is that game crashes and being disconnected from online are much less frequent, making it actually possible to play in a convoy with your friends now However, other players will still disappear randomly even if they are in your convoy. This extends to even the Eliminator, I won a game of it without seeing a single other person despite the fact I wasn't going out of my way to try and hide. Racing online with your friends seems to also work a little better, although I encountered a hilarious one-off bug with one of my mates being desynced and falling out of the sky on a flat road right in front of me. That isn't to say that I haven't had a few disconnects though, and I've only had one game crash. If you want to do massive skill chains to get accolades for them, you're still better off doing it offline as if you get disconnected half-way, people are still losing all of their points for no reason but at least your car won't be stopped dead in the process.Something else that has come up that wasn't present at the time of my original review is that there are a  of cheaters now. On rival's leaderboards, on the accolades hall of fame, and even in online races. FH4 had it's fair share of cheaters in rival time trials and online too, but it's even more blatant in this game with far more people doing it, with people having very visible speed hacks in races and rivals laptimes of under a tenth of a second. The top 100 to 200 times are all cheaters depending on how many people have done it, and as for the monthly rivals, this extends beyond the top 500 all being cheated times. It's not a huge problem as this isn't meant to be a competitive game (ranked online modes have been removed), but I still like doing hotlaps from time to time and seeing how fast I can go. Wheel support, at least for me is hit and miss. I still often have to unplug and replug my wheel several times to get force feedback but obviously this won't be a concern if you exclusively play this game with a controller. Custom control profiles still aren't being remembered.The last thing I have to say for now that isn't necessarily a bug or exploit is that I hate what they've done with Horizon Arcade (the new Forzathon Live). There's no notification of when they start anymore, because there will be multiple Arcades per hour, instead of having one every hour on the hour like in the last game. Not only that, but there will also be two completely separate Arcades lasting 10 minutes each rather than one lasting 15 in FH4. Combine that with the goals being ridiculously high, it's almost impossible to get it done for the festival playlist unless there's a large group of players all taking part. However, that's not likely to happen outside of asking a lot of friends to join you because there's no notification for them. This is a serious oversight on the developers, as I've seen more people doing Forzathon Live in FH4 on a consistent basis, even if there wasn't anything super valuable in the Forzathon Shop.All things considered, would I recommend this game now based on how the average player would play the game and what they would care about most? Yes, especially if you have friends to play it with, and I've changed this review to a positive one to reflect that even though my views on this game are still neutral. The average player probably doesn't really care about setting the fastest times in rivals, or the cheaters online, or wheel support because they would be spending most of their time playing with friends most likely, or customising cars, or going through the campaign events and a few custom events too.  I anticipate the developers will address other important issues that haven't been fixed yet in the future but if you're reading this and debating on whether or not to buy the game, here's my verdict:- If you're more casual about things and intend to primarily play with friends, I would recommend FH5- If you are going to play mostly or entirely on controller, I would also recommend FH5.- If you're going to be playing mostly alone, I'm not sure. For a game that has had over 10 million people play it, FH5 sure does feel empty on the online side of things with servers not showing that many players.- If you're the kind of player who likes to do some competitive racing or hotlaps, don't bother. I don't think they will add a proper anti-cheat system and remove illegitimate laptimes or scores anytime soon.- If you're going to be playing this with a wheel, I would also say don't bother. It's seriously frustrating to unplug and replug my wheel several times in several USB slots until the FFB decides that it wants to work and then having to set my custom control profile again every time I launch the gameI'll update this review one more time after another update inevitably comes out to fix more problems and change my recommendation accordingly.________________________________________________________FH5 has a solid foundation to be a good game, but right now I can't recommend it. Too many problems with not enough urgency behind fixing them which has caused me to refund it. When it works, it works very well. The suspension and tyre model physics are improved from FH4, force feedback on wheels is better once adjusted (especially off road). But instead of fixing any of the actual problems that players are experiencing, they'd rather fix the bloody treasure map of all things.There are stability issues, issues with multiplayer (namely convoys and horizon life) not working, custom controls and preferences not being remembered and having to be set every time you start, wheel support being hit and miss (a feature the devs specifically said they have improved) with me having to unplug and replug my wheel to get FFB to work. Also, taking part in Horizon Arcade (the new Forzathon Live) will cause your game to crash if you weren't there at the very start, and they decided to reduce it down to 10 minutes (from 15) for some reason.I will pick this game up once the issues have been addressed but for the time being you need to vote with your money if things will ever change with broken game releases. Don't buy this game if you haven't already, wait for the devs to fix it.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - Don't buy it on Steam full price, do not buy it from Microsoft, but instead probably on Xbox or PS5 instead as it has better error support.  Also this game often has trouble running/connecting at all when in multiplayer too.This game does not seem very optimized when you play it with higher hardware installed, or as it would seem.  Many RAM dumps and memory leakage, many frame stutters, many times does the ground not render.  It happens a lot one day, and then none another.  It's hard to explain, but it happens.  It makes racing actually infuriating when it does happen, especially at harder difficulties.In terms of gameplay, all of the sounds are 110% better for every car, every engine, and every tire squeal in particular.  The weekly PR stunt challenges are car-restricted like the weekly race championships were in the last game, and that frankly sucks.  All of the cars feel they have a "specific purpose", like for example most retro sports cars feel like they aren't supposed to be tuned for S1 and higher when they clearly can be anyways.  It's hard to explain, but the cars' handling makes it feel like they aren't supposed to surpass some kind of specific driving use.A lot of my friends don't seem to have the same issues that I had at first with actually running the game, so I think it might just not pair well with high-spec PCs even if that shouldn't be a problem.  Even more friends who play the game all come to the same consensus that I have, being that despite all issues it has it's worth buying and playing.  It has a lot of errors that need permanent fixes, especially with the display drivers and Nvidia tech such as ray tracing.  A couple of times it thought I wasn't signed in and needed to be, preventing me from playing outright for a couple minutes.  Countless times it crashes to desktop because of a Windows 0xc0000005 error that no one on the internet knows the answer to but I recognize it to be a bad install that Steam can't really reverse, so the answer is to reinstall a 100 GB game.  The crashes from in-game render issues that are the result of the game and not one's own hardware wouldn't be so bad if the game didn't take 5 minutes to boot from main menu to actually playing the game.This game is buggy and takes forever to boot, and while the cars they add later on are nice, I tend to avoid playing Cross Country races as the new tire physics make everything feel like an ice rink on the grass (especially as it rains) and it's not like a fun skid around.  Meanwhile when it rains and you race on the road, it feels great and very fun.  Also on higher difficulties it just feels like the bots are cheating and they have infinite acceleration and handling, but the moment you pass them it feels like they have a timer where they give up for the next 30 seconds or something.  Easy to lose to high end bots that feel like they're just hard for the sake of it meanwhile snowballing them is easy.  I drove Unbeatable difficulty races all the time in FH4 and in FH5 it just feels like a chore in comparison to a fun challenge.Over all, I'd say get it on sale just in case, but this certainly isn't worth more than $50 with how partially-functional the Steam version is.  A 70-75 out of 100 of a game because I still want to play it, but sometimes when playing and when any time there is an update the game just won't let me enjoy it the way I did Forza Horizon 4.

_childDocuments_.review: Updated review of Forza Horizon 5. After playing this game for over 1,900 hours, plus having played Forza Horizon 4, I give Horizon 5 an overall rating of 7/10. Here's a list of the pros and cons of FH5. PROS:- Largest list of cars to this day, with more to come with each month's update.- More custom wheels. Hoping to see more down the road because there's always room for more.- Amazing photo mode that lets you even adjust the time of day and weather for the perfect shot.- Improved driving physics compared to the previous Horizon game. Makes rear-wheel drive and front-wheel drive cars more manageable and quite competitive.- Test Track added so you can test your car, upgrade, and tune as you drive along. Neat. - Better graphical fidelity. CONS:- No sense of progression. The starter cars you're given, you don't even have to choose because you just get all three anyway. Plus, the game gifts you supercars from the start. So, where's the fun of earning credits to buy a glamorous car when it's just gifted to you by the developers? - Large map but it feels very empty. The large desert space, rain forest, and countryside have no depth to them. It's just flat. - No true four seasons like in FH4. All seasons feel the same. Just the spirit of Mexico I guess...- Car sounds could be better. They did improve some car sounds from FH4 to FH5, but at the same time, they butchered many other cars (most notable are the V12s from Ferrari and Aston Martin).- Horizon Stories are nothing more than cringe or a snoozefest. - Got rid of Super7 High Stakes from FH4. They could've added that to make Super7 more active. Instead, it's just wasted.- Got rid of Ranked online racing for whatever reason. - Still no penalty system for dirty driving behavior in online racing. Again, another reason for Ranked racing to exist is to separate the randoms from people with skill. Yeah, it's not guaranteed but Grand Turismo does a better job implementing a clean driving record. - No Horizon Backstage Passes added to the game. So there's no other way to obtain missed exclusive cars without having to try your luck at the Auction House. - Our Horizon Superstar can SPEAK. I much prefer a silent protagonist, otherwise you'll be hearing some awfully bad voice acting. - Lackluster car customization, especially for bumpers and rear wings. All you have for most of the cars are the same generic 'Forza wing'. I wish they added aftermarket wings for more cars.- Terrible AI that rubberband races like crazy. Higher difficulties on certain races will be near impossible to finish 1st. If you don't overtake them early in the race, you're more than likely to not catch up. - Music choice for the in-game radio stations are ok. Why bother adding songs if you're censoring the lyrics to them? Just don't even add them to begin with.

_childDocuments_.review: Forza Horizon 5 is a deep and nuanced car nirvana for revheads and auto geeks to endlessly collect, tinker, and experiment. It’s also an extremely accessible buffet of racing spectacle open to everyone, from Deluxe Edition diehards to Game Pass nomads – no matter their driving skill or mechanical knowledge. It’s an occasionally goofy but always earnest Valentine to Mexico’s world-famous culture, and a romantic ode to the magic of road-tripping through postcard-perfect vacation vistas. It’s a long haul, MMO-inspired racer that’s exploding with more races, activities, and event types than can comfortably fit on some parts of the map – and yet it still always feels relaxed rather than daunting. It never locks you into something you don’t want to do and steadily rewards you for however you choose to play it. It looks beautiful, it sounds magnificent, and it is glorious to play. Yes, Forza Horizon 5 is a lot of things. Above all, however, it is the result of a racing studio at the peak of its craft and the best open-world racing game I’ve ever played.MASTERPIECE 10/10Forza Horizon 5 is the result of a racing studio at the peak of its craft and the best open-world racing game available.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy this game and its stupendously large vehicle list, but playing the game on a racing rig is horribly unforgiving, frustrating, and downright enjoyable 90% of the time. The game, especially its physics (or lack-thereof ) is clearly build for game-pads and controllers. There is no incentive to use a rig, especially in multiplayer, both competitively and casually. Countering under and (especially) over-steer with a wheel is close to impossible without extremely fine-tuned settings and understanding of your wheel's dead-zones, (which I just find to be far too much in game)I spent well into double-digit hours tuning my drift setup, never feeling truly comfortable or confident just for Single player!Your mileage certainly may vary and I might just be terrible at understanding what the game wants from me. However, I feel like pure Sim-racing games such as AssettoCC or F1 are so much more forgiving when using a rig, and much easier to fine tune. (which you'd think would be the opposite?!?!)    On a rig, this game is not user-friendly enough to get a thumbs up from me. On a controller It's good and even excellent at times. However, it's controller bias ruins the experience for anyone who's invested in a rig.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, heres goes nothin! Thats the feeling this game gives you. You get in and think youre gonna be good immediately, then BAM! You did a PVP race against some dude that goes from 0 to 300mph in the time it takes for the sound of a fart to hit your ears. Personal experience has been amazing, however. This game has way more to offer than i originally thought. Dont want to race all day? Cool, go free-roam and practice your driving stlyle.OH! You wanna collect cars? Go for it! Over time (not that long) the server will send you a notification to go on a treasure hunt for Old Barn Finds, where you have a mechanic thatll repair the old find in to like new.Sure, theres other ways to get vehicles, but who cares about NPC races when you have a huge open world to practice on?OH! You DO care about NPC races and vehicles you unlock from them? Thats perfect then! Every town offers tons of races with new ones popping up daily, from Pre-loaded courses, to player created. The possibilities are near endless. The tuning of vehicles in this game is extraordinary, to say the least. You want your jeep to float like a boat when hitting tight corners? Go for it! You want your VW Bug to have a v10 Diesel, because **** you and your supercar? Go for it! You can fine tune every aspect of your ride to make it feel and react just as you want. You want to make a Shelby drift like a Dom Torreto? Go for it! Oh wait, you dont know how... right.. WELL YOURE IN LUCK! THERES TONS OF YOUTUBE VIDEOS! NOW!!!!... For the bad.... If you wanna drive insanely fast with amazing graphics.. you better hope you have a beefy system and harddrive. Otherwise, just chill, enjoy the tight corners this game has to offer, and just forget about life for awhile. Would i return this game even though i accidentally put 32hours in to it in the last 12 hours? Na... its too good of a game. Esspecially if youre looking for something with 0 stress and a great community.Good Luck, Gamers! Now.... ima go practice drifting and hope i dont slide off a mountain

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely amazing game!  But they need to fix some pretty glaring bugs, such as the game randomly crashing the moment that I load into a race. Doesn't happen all the time, but happens way too often.Update: most bugs have been fixed and the game is way better for it. I now really only wish that they would add more one-off versions of cars like the Senna and P1. We really should get the GTR versions of those as well as the super rare versions of other cars that are already in the game. I also hope they work on some of the engine sounds, some of them are clearly computer generated and definitely not recorded from a real car. Although most stock exhaust systems do appear to be real recordings of the real car. One last thing, and I know it may not apply to a large portion of the player-base, but it does effect me, PLEASE for the love of god make it so that the game works with the RPM lights on my Logitech G923 wheel! I'm really just nit-picking at this point, but it really is a great game and if these things got fixed, it would be that much closer to perfection! I really do stand behind this game and think that anyone considering it should try it!

_childDocuments_.review: Alright. This is going to be a weird one.I am in love with this game and was in love with Forza Horizon 4 as well. This is one of my favourites and I can spend 10 hours a day easily just enjoying the music and driving around, drifting, racing, doing showcases, etc.The good:- Music. This is the ONLY game that I enjoy while listening to the in game radio. It is beautiful, the radio feels live, changes according to your progress and the song collection is one of the best. I even ended up saving the Spotify playlist. The audio transitioning is amazing, one of the best I have seen.- It knows how to create the perfect environment, the perfect vibe for you to enjoy it. This is one of those games in which you will spend hours just roaming around, vibing with the music. The game feels like a party all the time.- Unlike all the other games where you "start from the bottom" and achieve something, here you don't. You already are a superstar, the main attraction of the event and the one everybody cheers for.- It doesn't need any grind for you to unlock stuff, you get plenty very easily, even for multiplayer. Oh and the multiplayer, there is so much to do there. You can go co-op or play PvP and I have tried both, if you got friends it is hella fun.Now the bad part. The game is HORRIBLE for PC users. As good of a game Forza Horizon 4 was in this department, this doesn't even come close. - Random FPS drops to single digit are pretty common.- Any time the podium shows up, there will be stutters during the car showcase, every single time.- The game always freezes after a couple of hours of playtime and has to be force closed.- If you are able to play for a long duration or just stay in the menu AFK for a few hours and come back, the game will start to run terribly. The FPS will keep fluctuating between 25-60 every few seconds until you restart the game.I have a decent build and able to run most of the games maxed out on 1080p and still reach 80+ FPS. Even Battlefield 2042 gave me less issues regarding FPS and I was able to enjoy that, but this just seems such a bad one. I never buy games for the full price, especially AAA titles that aren't solely multiplayer and wait for a couple of years.I still highly recommend it though, so much worth the full price. I can easily see myself putting in a few hundred hours before the next one comes out.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start this review by saying that I am a car enthusiast who spent a fair amount of time grinding ranked racing in FH4 with a group of friends. Most of my time in FH5 is spent racing online or grinding rivals.Pros: handling model is great, graphics are stunning, and the map design is generally pretty good. Also Hot Wheels is pretty fun.But besides the pros listed above, this is yet another soulless cookie-cutter open-world racer. The map looks great yet feels empty and lifeless. The 'missions' are purely a waste of time. Characters are forgettable if not annoying at times. The car list is largely unchanged from previous Forza titles; the cars themselves lack detailed modeling and animating, and blatant errors somehow make their way past QA, such as mirrored textures or leftover placeholder textures. Online racing is lackluster and the ranked mode from FH4 has been removed for no reason.Overall, this may be a fine racing game for someone who doesn't particularly care about cars or the genre. However, it is a disappointing one for car enthusiasts and long-time Forza players with many core issues that are hard to address with their monthly updates.
_childDocuments_.name: Forza Horizon 5

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the least amount of soul out of any Horizon games. Of course they improved a lot of things and there is some neat QoL present now, but the overall map still feels very barren, the Story was the least interesting and there have been so many bugs and issues that took ages to fix, some still aren't fixed, like some cars having their engine sounds swapped with entirely different cars and it keeps happening over and over again. They also went extra hard on the microtransactions this time around, which is really noticeable because everything you can buy ingame, you will easily get. The entire game seems to be designed to give you as many cars and money as quickly as possible. The true gems are then locked behind time limited seasonal rewards and microtransactions. I also love that i paid so much money for the premium edition which originally included all upcoming car packs, but at some point they just decided to release even more car packs that are not part of it. You don't even get a discount or something as a "VIP" player. The expansions were also rather lackluster so far and they still could not figure out a solution to all the rammers in multiplayer, despite having great ideas like with the collision detector, but unfortunately its just not enough. Outside of the seasonal objectives or PvP, there simply isn't a whole lot to do. Nothing to grind for either, because you get everything so easily already with minimal effort. You need like 10 or 15 hours for all the story races and then you are just left with some challenges and short sidestories, in a barren world with (if you are lucky) 4-8 other players spread across the whole map and absolutely no way to communicate with any of them. The map is simply not interesting enough to really motivate you to drive around, and its a big let down compared to previous titles. Visual tuning is also very limited to only few cars and their moderation system went overzealous on the liveries, banning people for even the most harmless things while leaving racial slurs, swastikas & co up for months. The sound design is basic. Sure we got a lot of different sounds but none of them sound great, just good at best. Still hate how every rotary car just sounds like a vacuum cleaner. But hey, the graphics are pretty and thats what most people have as their #1 priority, even though some cars have worse car models than in previous games. ¯\_(ツ)_/¯

_childDocuments_.name: Forza Horizon 5

_childDocuments_.review: Yet another AAA title that appears to have been done in 1 month with half their team. Like all they do is copy / paste the last game they copy / pasted, that was a copy / paste of the game before that but apparently everyone just ran out of f***s to give real quick.Beautiful new map in places, pretty bland and "FH1" feeling at times.The skys look neat with all their real sky photos with real sunrise and sunsets when you're not moving, but once you are it looks flat and fake so arguably a step backSounds are meaty, but everything just has rasp turned up to 11/10 once you modify it.Meaty shift sounds.Brainless banter over co-op races is about the only "original" thing to do.It runs well, even at 3440x1440 on high preset on a GTX 1060They got rid of the stupid championship races, that you had to do on every single event to fully complete them. Now you can do each one 1 time, get the win and completion. Rather than do it once for event completion, then do a championship off the same event and have to do 3 more races to get full completion.No one. Not a single soul so far in my ~100 hours, has ever gone into / competed in the Horizon Arcade stuff.It's quick to drop in / drop out if you want to play something for a little bit with no hassles.Lighting is real nice. The foliage looks a little PS2 at times, but when you crank the settings up for photos and such, it can look amazing.The playground games are good if you have friends to chat with at the same time. And IF the servers don't just freeze half the cars so invisible ghosts are going around.When I finally figured out the davinci code to make my T300 work. It was pretty fun to drive cars I like around with an H pattern. Even if they corner a bit too well at high speed. Ripping an E60 M5 or an SRT-10 Viper with a wheel and shifter was great.Your character talks in such a condescending way it makes the voice and cut scenes almost comical. Like they give as much of a f*** about what's going on as the devs did making it.It's actually hard to think of stuff now :|Felt like they had 1 month to make it with most the assets from the previous games.A number of cars just half-assedly done. Suspension at 0,0,0 under the cars, lights work on 1 side and not the other, gauges spin backwards, the Delorean was listed as a Citroen, brake calipers poking out through wheels, some wheels with borked vertices so it looks like you have vanta black boudica spiked wheels.Cars have no weight some times, so if you get hit you either get yeeted, or just slip past who ever hit you and they get yeeted. If you're real lucky the ghosting might kick in and save you.Somehow the usual clunky Forza driving dynamics feel even more clunky.You know how something like a popular FPS game is pretty fluid, CoD, CS GO, etc etc, but then you try Arma and it's so clunky like your character cant remember how to move. Thats the driving in this. At speed it's normal Forza, but mid speed their speed sensitive steering values take out what feels like 50% of your steering input so you can't make 90 degree turns without slowing way down, or cutting them. The cars are not close to understeering, they just don't turn. This might also be due to me being used to being able to steer in as much as I'd like from sims.Seemingly for most the cars, if you brake anywhere other than going straight you tend to go into a 4 wheel slide, which tend to have to slow down to stop. Once you break traction, it seems to want to keep sliding, and usually the rear end kicks out like some half implemented tap to drift mode. Being used to trail braking in sims, this to me feels real weird, so I'm trying to get used to that.Servers even after the "Fixes" are useless, constant disconnects, every minute or so everyone just disappears, traffic just disappears, some times you just get reset in place like you've hopped a server, losing speed and usually skill chainSame messy UI with unrelated pictures on the tiles, for what the tiles actually take you to.Pretty boring really, If you played FH1, it's the SAME game, which is the same as FH2, and FH3 and FH4. Copy Paste the base and give it a new map.The story seems to be following 1 family where every story mission is just helping them do some task while they usually just self doubt their decisions while you talk them up, like you're telling a child that even though they made a mess, it's easy to clean up to stop them from crying.Every time you unlock a new adventure thing, it stops you and takes you in to the damn menu so you either have to pick a new thing, or exit it.Everyone's always ghosted in free mode unless you're in a convoy, so you may as well just be in solo mode because there's virtually 0 interaction with 99% of people. Very, very rarely do you get people that hang around and drive with you, even drifters are like a 70/30 split to just ignore you and do their own thing now.I'd have refunded it just from the boring cliche intro if it hadn't been such a broken mess it put me over the 2hr refund limit and I had a couple friends to play it with once I got into online .. 2hrs of trash to even do the first 15 mins of the game ..Drivatars are cracked out more than the previously cracked out drivatars of previous games. FH4 it wasn't too difficult in my opinion to get wins on unbeatable so long as you didn't miss a braking point, or crash into a car. Now, expert difficulty is a 50/50 of either, you win by like 5+ seconds even if you crash, or 1 drivatar just hoons off 5+ seconds ahead of you for no reason while everyone else matches your speed.FFB with my T300 didn't work at all, except for the centering spring setting. I had to load the T300 preset, drive for a second, pull the power plug while "parked" in game, reconnect the power plug once the wheel finally disconnected, go in an re-load and re-bind my controls and then it worked.And shockingly, it's not too bad actually. Not great, but unlike whatever they set up for FH4 you can actually drive well with a wheel, and even on sim steering (Which iirc T10 said was completely broken in FH4) it's totally fine.Class racing is still broken. Don't build a logical "real world" A or B class, just build it to RWD or FWD, with the best speed, handling and acceleration stats you can. I built up and tuned probably 50 cars now for A and B, and my stock FD RX7 with a massive wing and basically no other mods is the one of the best cars I've come across. If you take a low class car and build it up with good mods, you seem to just end up with either a car with good speed but nothing else, or good handling and nothing else etc regardless of what it's stats say.Soften the rear to minimise everything rwd wanting to drift.If you're jaded with AAA games being dumpster fires, don't bother at full price, don't be sucked in by the same crappy "buy now to get this exclusive trash you wont even use anyway" cash grab sales. I downloaded the Witcher 3 while I played this and I'm way more keen to finally try that, than fire this up when everyone's offline.

_childDocuments_.review: I keep on playing this game because I want it to be good, but I am sorry to say it's not.I can't for the life of me understand what they have been working on for 3 years. The basic formula is great, and the driving is fun, but the game feels like a DLC for forza horizon 4. They didn't improve on anything except the map and weather effects.Online freeroam is actually worse than before. If you are looking for a world full of life, with other players around you doing their own thing, look elsewhere. The few times when there's players around me, it's 3-4 of them max.The hourly forzathons were reworked, and now, instead of having the whole lobby rushing to do it, you're stuck doing them on your own.The team has put absolutely zero effort on making the UI more user friendly. Filtering is basic, and the filters aren't ordered properly. Menus and car classifications oftentimes make little sense. In online play there's no way to decide on what kinda race you want to race, and many more things that could have been addressed with this new installment.The team seems to be lazy, and doesn't take the time to address the players (except the sad excuse for a Q&A once a month on stream). The big events (christmas gifting and world cup) are just pretend. The outcome is predetermined and the bar progresses as the season does. In the patches up to now, they've focused more on removing fun aspects of the game, instead of actual bugs and cheaters. All leaderboards are riddled with very very obvious cheated values. Removing them wouldn't even require much effort on PG's part. Wheelspins were nerfed to all hell, and my VIP (that I paid extra for) has been rendered completely pointless.There's many more issues and many more promises they haven't even tried to keep. As of now, I can not recommend the game for the price. Get yourself FH4 on sale and have a blast with a better populated world until FH5 drops in price.I regret pre-purchasing the ultimate edition, total waste of 100€.Edit. The only reason I keep on logging in is the weekly playlist and my fear of missing out on something. I still hope for a better game in the future. I paid for the expansions, so I'll keep on logging in until then. The DLC's could be good, but as of now I am not optimistic.
