_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Buy Forza Horizon 4.This game was a huge letdown. I loved FH4, the environment, the cars, the details, ran well, and the communal feeling.They set this game in a literal desert: it is desolate place with a handful of people in one place. The map is actually TOO big that you feel isolated, and the few people that are in the server are either in the main festival or all spread about. Then on top of that, Forzathon is just empty. It was so empty on launch, that they patched it so that less people contributed more points. Compare this to FH4 where almost 75% of server will show up and have a grand ol' time, and then scatters off back to what they were doing when they were done. You have none of that here, and the only interaction I have is with Horizon Adventure lobbies and the Trial as per season requirement for cars I wanted.The game also runs so much worse than FH4. I don't know any technicalities, but FH4 runs like smooth butter on my 2070 MAX-Q, but will dip below 30 FPS when it is not an average ~40 FPS all around. This despite the fact the games look mostly the same anyways. Again, not my area of expertise, but potato computers that could run FH4 can't run FH5 is what my experience entails. I mean Christ, they still have not addressed the optimization issues and I wonder if they just gave up on it. I quit mainly on the fact that the more updates the game got, the more unstable the game seemed to get, to the point that I was having awful desync issues and teleporting around. Not to mention the fact that convoys in this game are so hard to get working half the time. To say that there are a bunch of technical issues in this game is an understatement and the biggest turn off for me that led to me uninstalling it.The story is also just garbage. You are an instant superstar that everyone must know about every waking moment. The characters are hollow smiles that never, EVER not happy. Their dialogue is so bland and cringy. FH4 mostly left you alone to rise to stardom and never really smothers you in bland NPC interaction besides stories, which were fun if not challenging. FH4 just lets you race and leaves the story aspect as something optional. FH5 just smothers you in never-not-chipper NPCs that are so lifeless and hollow that it gets annoying real fast. This is personal opinion of course, but I feel racing games just don't fit story lines very well: just let me race and build my career without all the fluff thank you.Hot Wheels DLC was the only real fun I had so far, as it was much more interesting and fun than the entirety of Mexico. On that note, as of the time I am writing this review, there has been very little new content. Donut Media DLC dropped after I uninstalled the game, so I cannot form an opinion on that, but from the content I saw on it, it is more or less just copy paste of FH4 assets like they are somehow brand new and designed to keep me engaged in the game.That sums up this game pretty well: a hollow, un-optimized, version of FH4 that adds only a few new things and little else. You can call it Forza Horizon 4.5 for all I care.I will wait for FH6 to be in Japan, but I will never buy the Premium edition ever again unless it was worth it, like in FH4.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a typical Horizon game, and that's the problem. Yet another big, entirely empty map with nothing but dirt and rocks to look at. is it an improvement over FH4? yes. However I'd still prefer the FH4 map over Mexico. Car catalog is fresh, plenty of new additions with returning favorites. Turn 10 took a page from Need for Speed and added some crazy body kit options and some new rims that weren't in FH4. that being said, why on Earth, after 5 installments in the Horizon series, can I not adjust the wheel depth? _childDocuments_.review: Currently playing with:CPU: Ryzen 3800XGPU: XFX RX 580 8GBRAM: 16 GBActually pretty fun but has some issues. This is my first intro besides a little bit of gameplay from Horizon 3, and my review will be limited to the premium edition as that's what I got and other players who only have the base game may have a different experience. That being said, my other friends don't have the premium and don't feel like they are missing out on much so do with that what you will, obviously the big bonus of premium is the future content/expansions being bundled and discounted rather than having to purchase them separately.Pros:Great variety and customizationGreat graphics and optimizationFun to play online with friends and take part in eventsLots of things to doThe way they are doing seasons seems interesting, but also wish that they could be longer than 3-4 days each for the small ones.The rewind feature works incredibly well, especially online. I'm honestly amazed at how they were able to implement it so seamlessly, and it adds a lot to the game and helps tone down frustration if you are trying to complete specific objectives in free roam as well. That being said, the only time I've ever had the game crash (2 at this time) have both been related to me rewinding and the game freezes and crashes shortly afterward. Haven't been able to notice anything in particular that might have set it off.Meh:Lots of small details in the game when you are playing, but also weirdly enough a lack of them, hopefully some features will get implemented later like skipping cutscenes, and other UI decisions that will probably be suggested by the Horizon community.I'm sure there's more stuff but I'll probably add stuff in as I play more.Cons:Story is forced and it's literally torture having to watch unskippable cutscenes with terrible acting and lines. Wish we could skip all the animations that are in the game like the barn finds as well.Other story events are annoying where you are racing some AI like in the showcase events where they look like they are rubberbanding all over the place. The first showcase event with the motorcycles has it bad, and the bikes literally look like they are floating on the ground while they are driving, there's no actual substance to their movements if that makes any sense.Online definitely has issues, constant DC's, being forced to go into free roam from whatever menu you are in just to reconnect, players in your convoy disappearing in front of you or on the map, etc. Also weirdly enough your car stopping anytime you get DC's, which is super frustrating for those who get DC'd often. By that time a restart usually ends up resolving it though.Some parts of online, especially Arcade are frustrating mostly because of a lack of players, there isn't much incentive to play them, which makes it all the more harder if you are trying to do any seasonal or whatever objective and there is literally no one at each point. Maybe a queuing feature could mitigate that? Alternatively just play with friends but they aren't always available.The XBOX live integration leaves something to be desired, sometimes it just won't connect to online even though in game I am online and can play with friends. It's easiest to just join a friend by sending them an invite through in game instead of the XBOX overlay, or them specifically joining you outright.All in all though I'd say the game has been worth it so far, and I look forward to the improvements they'll make and whatever else will happen down the line.

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't a huge racing game fan but Forza 5 has me sold. It's imo a great mix of more arcade chill driving while still having realistic aspects. It looks great and it's just fun to play, there's an open world where you gradually unlock more events and you're never pressured to do thing X asap, you can pretty much play it in any order you like (+ load times for events are pretty fast, you can just drive nonstop around the world map and unlock stuff as you go). The car painter is great and it's basically a weeb's wet dream. Unlocking more cars and stuff is fast, and you don't have to grind long to get the cars you like apart from the more monster class ones. There's a variety of different driving styles for offroad as well. It's also well optimized and my laptop can even handle it at 4K Extreme settings at 60 FPS. Creating your own driver is also pretty fun, especially when you get to call him/her whatever you want, plus the story events add a nice touch imo.I would recommend staying away from the Xbox game pass version though, because it didn't recognize my PS4 controller and it also had a permanently disappearing mouse cursor, Steam version has been working way better for me. And I would definitely recommend playing this on a controller either way, or even a wheel if you have one.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like cars? Do you like destruction? Do you like racing people, whether they be friend or stranger? Do you like to win? Do you like the feeling of being the fastest in the land?If your answer was yes to any of these questions I can highly recommend this game to you.The game has insane visuals, I'd personally say a solid 9/10/. The detail put into the cars and map are extraordinary. The map is incredible, ranging from soft white beaches to a literal volcano. The voice acting is very good, not amazing, but then again this is a racing game. My only real complaint is in cut scenes the body and mouth movement is awkward to say the least. But as I've said before, this is a racing game, you're not hear to be immersed in an amazing story and acting, you're hear to drive like there is no tomorrow.The other complaints I have are minor, pausing the game and stopping your car each time you are able to unlock a new festival site, a strange visual glitch on one side of the volcano (might be just me but the terrain flashes from black and white to full colour again), the bugs you'll encounter along the way (though most of them are rather hilarious and have laughed me through some tough races) and the strange difficulty scaling (on higher difficulties the top 2 or 3 cars rubber band away from you making it next to impossible for you to catch up).I implore you to purchase this game if you have the money, and I hope to see you in my next race! Happy racing (or drifting, whatever your style is ;) )

name: The Jackbox Party Pack 8
detailed_description: About The Jackbox Party Pack 8 The eighth installment of the beloved Jackbox Party Pack franchise is here! Five hilarious new games will energize your next game night, holiday party, happy hour, or video call. No extra controllers needed - players use their phones or tablets to play along! Got a bigger group? Play with up to 10 players and up to 10,000 audience members. The Jackbox Party Pack 8 is currently in English only. This game does not support online matchmaking but can still be enjoyed remotely using livestreaming services or video conferencing tools. About Each Game Drawful Animate (3 -10 players) - It’s alive! The guessing game with terrible drawings and hilariously wrong answers makes a dynamic return. In this revamped title, players create looping, two-frame animations based on weird and random titles. . The Wheel of Enormous Proportions (2-8 players) - Trivia has never been so large! A fantastic, mystical wheel challenges you with a variety of trivia prompts. Winners are awarded slices of the Wheel’s face with a chance to win big with each nail-biting spin. In the end, one player will have their most burning question answered by the great Wheel. . Job Job (3-10 players) - Use other people’s words to create unique and funny answers to classic job interview questions. Go head to head to see who scores the job! . The Poll Mine (2-10 players) - A survey game that’s all about YOU! Split into teams and see who can escape from the witch’s lair! Players individually rank their choices to a difficult question, then must guess how the group answered as a whole. How well do you know your friends?! . Weapons Drawn (4-8 players) - A social deduction game where everyone is both a murderer and a detective. Players doodle all the clues, hiding a letter from their name in the weapon drawings. Can you solve murders while trying to get away with your own? . How to Play Remotely Players use any web-enabled device (like a smartphone or tablet) to join the game and play along. When playing with remote players, you can use a video conferencing tool like Zoom, Steam Broadcast, Google Hangouts, Discord, and more to connect with others! Just share your screen while on a call and make sure you look for prompts to share audio.

_childDocuments_.review: I own all the packs, played every game several times, yada yada.The TL;DR is that this is another great entry but it might not be worth the retail of $30.Translating animation into an accessible party game is an interesting approach for sure; Unfortunately it's executed sloppily. Drawful Animate has difficulty justifying the animation angle that's been introduced. The obvious strength of animation is conveying actions or sequences that would otherwise be difficult using a single frame; The problem is many of the prompts in Animate don't contain verbs/actions that would make good use of the 2nd frame, and instead are mostly prompts you could easily do with a single picture. It results in a lesser Drawful that takes twice as long. It would appear this is already the most controversial entry in Party Pack 8; Not just online, but even among the multiple friend groups I've tried the game with. This is a trivia game with a very heavy RNG slant. I had one group that thoroughly enjoyed it, and another that were actively agitated since most of the game is focused on the wheel opposed to the trivia itself. I personally enjoy it and it's arguably the most well-paced game on here, but if you don't like luck based games or trivia, this likely won't click with you. A Quiplash-esque game that works way better than you may expect. You type in a response to a question asked on your device; Then other players need to rearrange the words in your response to answer a completely different question. The limitations of what you have to work with result in broken, scattered-minded answers that end-up feeling a lot less  than Quiplash, but it's also why the game works so well. This plays a lot like  where the players are split into 2 teams, and need to guess the top answers out of everything presented. Trying to talk to your partners about what everyone voted for without giving away too much to the other team makes for a deceptively strategic experience. It's a very socially driven game and always leads to good discussions. The element of  that basically act as lives is a great idea and the entire progression of the game feels fully realized. Feels like you could probably speed this one up and slip in another round, but otherwise, Poll Mine might be the best in Pack 8. This is easily the most complicated drawing game ) and might even be one of the most complicated Party Pack games ever; I'd argue even more so than Push The Button despite that game involving much more strategy. Players play the role as both detectives, and murderers. You draw murder weapons, choose an accomplice to murder, and figure out who drew what weapons. Between trying to hide calling cards in your own art, and discussing with other players who did what, there's a lot going on here; It'll take a game or two before you get a full grasp on it. Props to Weapons Drawn for being the most conceptually creative game here, but transitions between rounds go on for far too long and overall it's a fairly slow game. Between all of the Jack Box social deduction games  this is the weakest we've seen. This is the first Jackbox with 2 drawing games which makes this a less varied pack than 7; And considering those 2 games are some of the weaker drawing entries we've seen  it's hard to justify that decision. Regardless; Party Pack 8 takes a lot of risks, and a lot of those risks definitely pay off. I can easily see myself coming back to this one a lot for Job Job and Poll Mine alone; But if you're not a huge Jackbox buff and want to know which game to start with, packs 3 and 7 will provide much more bang for your buck.
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Party Pack 8

_childDocuments_.review: I played through the games with some buddies and here's my short rundown of each game:Drawful Animation: Basically Drawful but with Animations added on top. I do prefer classic drawful over this, but there's nothing wrong with it. It just doesn't add much except for longer wait times.The Wheel of Enormous Proportions: Trivia game directed towards players from the USA. My squad is not from the US which means we didn't have time to enjoy it quite as much as we would've otherwise. Other than that it's just very RNG-driven, so don't expect to get a win just because you know everything.Job Job: This was the game we enjoyed the most. Make sure your entire squad answers in english and you'll have a real fun time playing this. Recommended for 6+ players though.Poll Mine: Definitely a game you need to be at least 6 people to enjoy. It's all about guessing (as a team) what everyone's opinion regarding some topic is.Weapons Drawn: Great concept, but very confusing all around. The rules are clear, but going through the entire gameplay ends up being confusing. How many mini-rounds are there in each round? What decides which weapon is next to your profile? Who's who during the voting section? Really need a more clear description on this one, but maybe it'll get clearer once I've played the game a few times more.

_childDocuments_.review: Party games require two key elements to live up to the expectations of the genre. First, they have to be easily accessible as the minimum number of players to get the game functioning is higher than in most genres. Second, they have to be easy to pick up so that players can hop in and get right to the fun with the least amount of initial investment possible. Jackbox tends to succeed in this regard with most of the games in its collection even if they are a mixed bag at times. The eighth entry in the series carries on the trend with a handful of games that are likely to entertain and disappoint in equal measure. I was lucky enough to have several good friends along for the ride and I’ve decided to rank the contents of this pack from the least impressive to most impressive experiences on offer.The Wheel of Enormous Proportions is most easily defined as a combination of trivia and Wheel of Fortune. A multiple-choice question is posed to the group with well over a dozen answers. Many of these choices are correct and the player who selects the most correct and least incorrect among them is awarded the most points. The highest-scoring player receives a slice to put onto the wheel that is visited after every trio of questions. When the trivia action moves to the wheel, each player places their collected slices onto it and a lucky player gives it a spin. Whoever’s space it lands on receives a hefty batch of points with a few surprise landings on it to spice things up as well.Every game is going to be subjectively judged and opinions may vary, though this was the game that the group unanimously decided was the worst in the pack. Trivia is hit-or-miss for me in general and I tend to get bored of it quickly, though it was a perfect storm of issues that lost me on this one. A short time restricted the amount of time that choices could be made and left a couple of the players who were playing on their phones frustrated as those using a browser had a serious advantage. I can certainly get on board with timed trivia, but time trivia that requires you to scroll on a smartphone while simply being point and click in a browser was rough. The wheel itself, the real gimmick of Wheel of Enormous Proportions, didn’t add much to the excitement either and there was a collective groan at one point when a near-win resulted in an entire additional round thrown on. This one’s likely to be a hard pass for me in the future unless someone else gets an urge to play and asks me to join in.Weapons Drawn is a unique enough game, though where it bogs down is its complexity. Jackbox tends to pull in groups of players who are seeking out something quick, comedic, and casual to play with their friends but this one doesn’t fit as closely as the others as it has an initial learning curve that ends up slowing down the play session for an experience that, quite bluntly put, isn’t worth it even once everyone has it down. Each player is both a murderer and a detective who is tasked with drawing a murder weapon from a prompt. The catch is that a letter from your name is used as your calling card, something that links a murder to you, and you have to hide it as well as you can inside of your drawing. Depending on the letter this can be a particularly arduous task or extremely easy (I’m looking at you ‘I’). Players will then name their own guest they’re bringing to the party and the group will have to figure out who killed each others’ guests by judging the pictures that show up.Although I wouldn’t say that Weapons Drawn was a bad experience, it wasn’t a thrilling one. It was less casual than the others in the pack and even after the investment required to learn it was behind us, we felt that we were mostly done with it before we’d even reached the end of our first run. If a murder mystery party game is what you’re looking for, I would highly suggest looking elsewhere at plenty of other places that do it better.Although my opinions have been a bit harsh, The Poll Mine comes in at number three and acts as the turning point. Each player is assigned to one of two teams that were named by the players themselves and takes off on an adventure where each location tasks them with answering a question in the form of a ranked poll. Teams then guess where the different answers ended up in the ranking in order to acquire the most torches with correct answers.This one was a hit with most of the group and I could definitely see jumping back into it in the future. It’s a good time guessing how your friends voted in the ranking and the variety of questions keeps it fresh. There’s a strong interpersonal element that wasn’t in the previous two entries that made this one stand out as a fun experience that has you continually guessing how the rest of the players lined up their choices in a particularly subjective poll.The silver trophy goes to Drawful Animate. In this one, players receive a secret text prompt and have to draw it before the game begins. However, these pieces of art have a unique twist to them in that you’re drawing two frames that become an animation to be viewed by the group. These are revealed one at a time and the non-artist players submit their own fake prompts in an attempt to trick the others into voting for theirs instead of the right one. Points are awarded both for guessing the correct prompt and for having others vote for the false one that was added to the mix.This was the game that felt the most like what I expected from Jackbox. It was fun and full of hilarious results hand-crafted by the personalities within the group. There was plenty of room for individuality and it was used to its full potential. I’m already getting the urge to play this one again and I would say that most of the conversations that have taken place since we ran through this pack have revolved around Drawful Animate.The standout game this time around is the job interview “simulation” Job Job. Players compete as candidates for a position by answering a variety of icebreaker questions in their own words. Once these answers are submitted, they’re chopped up into their individual words and thrown together into one large batch. They are then distributed amongst the players so that they may answer new questions using only these words. They can be placed in any order, though players no longer have the ability to type in their own at this point. Points are awarded both by having your own words picked to create the new answers or by having your Frankstein-monster of a sentence voted as a better fit than the other player’s that it’s lined up against.Job Job was a pleasant surprise as it checked all of the boxes for what I wanted out of a Jackbox game while also being something new. Everyone got a kick out of the sentence restructuring and guessing which players certain words in the jumble had come from. It was a tough call between Drawful Animate and Job Job for the top spot, but Job Job pulled off the win due to its uniqueness.The Jackbox Party Pack 8 lives up to its legacy with a few strong entries that are great additions to the collection overall. It’s likely to offer hours of fun for just about any group of players who are looking for a hilarious, personalized party game experience. That said, I would recommend waiting for a sale as it’s not the cheapest party game out there and there’s at least one entry that gets old before you’ve even finished your first game of it.

_childDocuments_.review: When it comes to Jackbox Party Packs, this is my favorite so far -- maybe the only one in which I actually like all the games.I love the Drawful games, and to animate things makes it even more hilarious than it used to be. There is also a fantastic Friend Mode.The cool thing about The Wheel is that you do not answer regular questions. You tap all the right answers, or you have to type out a word. The fun part too is that there is an element of luck, which keeps the game interesting for all players.The word game of the pack Job Job might be the weakest one. You create new sentences with words from other players, which is a hit or miss. The setting of a boring office seems to be somehow off-putting as well. Still fun though.The Poll Mine is the game everyone wants to keep playing. It is like Family Feud, but your group answered the questions. Technically, you can play it with two people, but it does not really make sense. I would say four is the minimum.And Weapons Drawn. A hybrid between writing, drawing and guessing. Amazing. First, you have to come up with a name for a character, but people will guess if you typed in the name, so it cannot be something obvious. Then you have to hide a letter in a drawing. Then you have to find out who the other drawings belong to,  basically. It is a really cool game.Keep in mind that you play with one smartphone / tablet or web browser per person. If you want to play with your friends online, you can use Steam Remote Play or Discord. It is still fun.

_childDocuments_.review: This pack is worth it just for Job Job. It's my favorite Jackbox game of all time. However, here's a review of all the games:Dawful Animate - This is just drawful, but slightly more complicated. You can draw two panels instead of one and it switches back and forth between them. It's probably best you only play it with people who have played the original drawful. In my opinion, simpler is better here. Just play Drawful.I was excited to play The Wheel of Enormous Proportions. Unfortunately, it feels much more luck based than it should be for a trivia game. Pretty much all the points awarded at the end seem to just come from spinning the wheel, and actually getting the trivia right is just fluff in the middle.Job Job is the best. You write answers to prompts, but that's really just giving people words for the next part. You have to answer questions using the word salad you get from the mixture of other people's answers. It always makes people laugh.I enjoy poll mine. First, it asks you a question and you're supposed to rank the answers given to you from 1st to last. Then, you and your team (everyone is split into two teams), all collaborate together to determine things like "What's the most popular answer?" In later rounds, you'll have to pick things like "What's the least popular answer?" It's actually pretty interesting.Weapons Drawn is not fun. It feels like there's way too much going on and even by the end of the game, everyone doesn't fully understand what's happening. Essentially, you're supposed to kill people and then draw a murder weapon based on a prompt, but you have to hide a letter that's in your name somewhere in the drawing. That premise by itself is only okay at best, so they tried to add a bunch of other guessing stuff in there that's just a little too confusing and the whole thing falls really flat. If I were to rank all the Jackbox games from every pack so far, this one might be dead last.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall: save your money and maybe just pick up some older Jackbox Party Packs. It's pretty evident that they're scraping the bottom of the barrel on new games.Pros to Party Pack 8:• Drawful animated is a fun twist on regular drawful.• Job Job is a fun, new game, that is pretty unique to any previous games.Cons to Party Pack 8:• Wheel of Enormous Proportions is a regular trivia game that just doesn't live up to Trivia Murder Party.• The Poll Mine requires a large minimum number of players. Probably 8 to be worth playing.• Weapons drawn just devolves into everyone drawing squiggles to try and hide things in the picture. • None of the good games really justify buying this Party Pack. There are either better games or similar games on previous packs. Even Job Job, while fun, doesn't have enough going on to warrant the purchase of this pack.

_childDocuments_.review: Very enjoyable.The 5 games listed in my order of preference:1: Job Job - I am *aching* because I've been laughing so much at that. It could well be my new favourite Jackbox game. Imagine quiplash with a 'fridge poetry' twist.2: Drawful Animate - I was worried that the animation aspect would make the game more difficult compared to previous versions of the game, but it doesn't; it's well explained and easy to follow. It takes the best bits from the previous Drawful games and tweaks it to make it even better.3: The Wheel of Enormous Proportions - I'm not normally a fan of the trivia games, but this worked very well; it doesn't show everyone else exactly what you got wrong so you don't have to get embarrassed 🙂4: The Poll Mine - Was a bit difficult to follow at first, but has an interesting premise. It would have definitely benefited from playing the game in person though rather than online because it encourages discussion.And, unfortunately...5: Weapons Drawn - actually terrible. Dull, convoluted and drawn out. Supposed to be a game of deduction, but it had a clumsy premise and lasted far too long. About halfway through I was wanting it to finish. I don't think I'll be playing that one again. As with the Party Pack 7, this one has an option to filter US-centric content, so if you're not from the USA, you don't get prompts and questions which only Americans will understand. This helped with Quiplash 3 in party pack 7, and is another reason why Drawful Animate is an improvement over the previous two. Verdict? Get it. 'Job Job' and 'Drawful Animate' are amazing. 'The Wheel of Enormous Proportions' is enjoyable even if trivia games aren't necessarily your thing, and 'The Poll Mine' is interesting; I'll definitely be trying it when playing it with people in real life! Just pretend 'Weapons Drawn' doesn't exist.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR 2 or 3 good games, the rest is meh. the good ones are worth playing but not at this price, hence the thumbs down. if it ever gets the price reduced to like 15 bucks i'll thumbs it up.I have played every jackbox game a million times, i streamed this with ~70 people to get everyone's opinions of the games. here they are:Drawful: Good game, but its just drawful again, the animation doesn't add that much 4/5Job Job: everyone types in answers to prompts, then you have to answer another round of questions using only words from the answers people just typed. if you think broken english is funny you will like this. highly dependent on the people playing to provide a good word bank. 4/5Poll Mine: try to guess how your friends would rank lists of obscure objects. its ok, not great but not awful. 3/5Wheel of Enormous Proportions: not good. its just a standard jackbox trivia game but after every 3 questions you have to go spend a few minutes spinning a wheel that's complete RNG to see who gets extra points. no reason to play this when you have any other jackbox trivia game as they are all way better. this one is a waste of time. 0/5Weapons Drawn: maybe the most high concept jackbox game to date. the game picks a letter from your name and you have to hide that letter inside of your drawing. its an interesting idea and has a lot of fun strategy in the drawings, but it suffers from the classic jackbox blunder of going on for way too long. if they cut the game time in half it would be better. 3.5/5overall its a standard jackbox release, 1 or two solid games and the rest is mediocre. i'd wait til its on sale or on gamepass. P.S. Please make a sequel to Mad Verse City next time

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the best party pack to date. Almost every game is solid and fun (except Wheel of Enormous Proportions). Drawful animate is a welcome update to a classic, Poll mine is a fun reimagining of Family Feud, Job Job takes what works about Joke Boat and makes it easier to be funny (I recommend extending timers), and weapons drawn was a lot less complicated than I thought (so it worked just fine via Discord). The only stinker in this group is Wheel... because the host is annoying and painfully drags everything out. Anyone who has played these party packs knows that there is usually only one or two good games per pack... This pack has 4 solid games and some appreciated menu tweaks to make running games easier.

So good. Cannot overstate.The Poll Mine: Maybe with bigger groups, didn't work for mine.Weapons drawn: Fun concept that I looked forward to playing but was too difficult to wrap ones head around so my group decided after one play that they don't care for it. Make sure everyone knows what's going on because it doesn't work when half the group is confused.Worth it for Job Job alone, but honestly it's the only game from this pack we even play.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr: By far my second favorite Party Pack with my most favorite game of the entire Jackbox Party Pack series. Despite its pacing problems, with interesting concepts and loads of chaos and fun, this Pack really has sold me and I really recommend buying it for these games alone.The Jackbox Party Pack 8 might as well be my second-favorite Party Pack in the series. It really boils down to how each game has been an enjoyable experience, even if one of them is literally Mario Party Trivia but I'll get to him soon.First, may I present the best Jackbox game of all time: . "WHAAAAT?! Even better than Quiplash?" Yes, hear me out. While Quiplash has been the series that introduced me to Jackbox and I have held the series of games in my heart, a lot of things that Job Job does compared to Quiplash hits harder. First, the way you input response isn't just typing words to use against others. You are instead using words that were written by other players during the first part the icebreakers. While this can be a make or break for some, it's way easier to create a response to the interview question than say Quiplash. Quiplash is awesome, yes, but there are prompts that are difficult to shallow and find a funny response that the other players will like. With Job Job, broken words pulled from the players (and from the question itself too, even your own name!) can make the funniest responses no matter how poorly written it is. Tho the game does drag long given the circumstances of getting your response, it doesn't really matter. Plus waiting is so enjoyable thanks to M. Bubbles being the best water-cooler out there doing some funny stuff that only they can do. And the motivation posters, the art style of Owen Watson, the amazing soundtrack, 10 players, and the WordArt! And by far one of the best credit songs ever written. While I do like to play Quiplash every once in a while, Job Job is a phenomenal game. I honestly really hope that we can eventually enter our own questions (UGC) similar to Quiplash and Drawful, but maybe for a sequel? Or if Jackbox updates their own games. Either one can come. Anyways M. Bubz rules! is yet another outstanding entry in the Drawful series. Unlike the other two entries, this time you're drawing two frames of animation. Onion skinning is available to help out make your animation a reality. The prompts in Drawful: Animate especially have nailed how people typically write their titles. Typos, weird punctuation, it really feels like they nailed their game here, and it blends so nicely with everyone else's prompt. My only problem is again time, but with the new capacity of 10 players, some quality of life changes (like the game auto-submitting your animation even if you don't finish on time), and the host being cheeky as always, this is a fun Drawful experience, and I can't recommend enough. is an interesting concept. Split into two teams, you are asked a survey question and have to rank the options (three in round 1, four in round 2, five in round 3). Afterwards, the fun can begin. In round 1, you have to find the top three answers. In round 2, you have to find the fourth, third, and second most selected answers and try not to select the most-selected one. And then round 3 is to find the options from bottom to top. Now, there are some things to consider in this game. Firstly, it is within your best interests not to reveal too much of what you answered, because the other team can take advantage of what you said to try to get the correct answer. Secondly, this game isn't fun with less players. Having only four people split evenly with two player cannot give enough answer survey responses to fill in. It'll make the final round harder to do. Finally, this game is actually pretty chill. Regardless of my issue with player counts, this game has a relaxing mood, from visuals to soundtrack. And I cannot commend the artists who went out of their way to make a unique artstyle for this game. Now while I think some of the survey questions can be questionable at best, it does allow us to have a meaningful discussion on what people voted for and why. So while I have some problems, this game is cool at best. has a very interesting and amazing concept. Every player is a detective, but also a murderer, and it's your goal to solve and commit crims. But everyone cannot just kill without a weapon, drawn by the player. These weapons require that the player hides a calling card, a letter from their name. If you are playing this, I recommend you try to rename yourself to something that cannot easily be traced right back to you. Letters like P, R, or J can be extremely difficult to hide. Moreso, having a letter like Y in your name can make it easy for a murderer to kill your accomplice, which you name in secret after your two weapons are drawn. Once some murders are committed, the investigation (and social deduction) can begin. Important notes, the murderer cannot be the person who brought the victim, nor any other individuals whose first weapon they have dropped shares similar weapons to the object that killed the accomplice. If you are successful at finding the murder, you get points, but select wrongly, and you get nothing. After another round with you drawing two more weapons and another accomplice, the final round, Cold Cases, is a lightning round of all the unsolved cases. As the detective, it is in your best interests to find the murderer on time, but as the murderer, it is also in your best interest to deflect everyone to earn points. Once everything is tallied up, the winner is declared. If all of this sounded too complicated to you, that's because it is. There is a lot to unpack with Weapons Drawn, but I don't think it's a bad experience. It's fun when you get to murder people, but there have been cases when one player will leave the game without having the opportunity to kill anyone, which happened to me once. Not only that, but it can be easy to cheese just by drawing some mumbo jumbo. Despite these issues, this game is really enjoyable to play. Mostly I give it props for the amazing soundtrack by Elise Wattman, who started her career with this game. The investigation discussion is fun, the accomplices names can be funny at times, and while I feel some stuff can be done better, this was a solid game.This leaves  in last place for this Pack, but I also don't think this one bad. This is moreso a trivia game mixed with Mario Party. You can only win once you hit 20,000 points and spin your name on the Winner Wheel, but you'll have more chances by answering trivia questions right, most being multiple-choice. I feel like a multiple-choice trivia has been long overdue in Jackbox. The concept of mixing it with chance, that is also interesting, if not chaotic at best. The Power Slice in particular can get messy, from point swaps to slice stealing, and so much more. This is a trivia game I wouldn't go to the most though, but this game can be a fun experience. My only real complaint is that the Winner Wheel stuff drags this game far too long. Hmm...I'd say this Pack's biggest problems that's dragging this from being my favorite is pacing. With Job Job and Drawful: Animate, I can excuse because a lot has to be done in those games, but I cannot excuse this for The Wheel and perhaps Weapons Drawn, for better or worse. The latter took almost 45 minutes with extended timers. Personally, if you don't mind doing a game for that long, you can keep extended timers on, but if you want to play any other game in this Pack, it'd be significantly longer than before. Other than that, this is a solid pack, and I cannot recommend Pack 8 enough for Job Job and the others. If you want to score the job, animate weird prompts, play Family Feud in a cave, solve and commit murders, or play Mario Party, this is the to-go Pack for you!
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Party Pack 8

_childDocuments_.review: For context, I own all of the Jackbox packs from 3-7 (as they are all of the good ones), and I wanted to get this pack as it looked as solid as the ones from before.Weapons Drawn looked like an interesting murder mystery, with Job Job and Drawful Animate looking like good ones for laughs.However, as I soon to find out, this pack wasn't as good as I was led to believe.Honestly, a pretty solid one. The problem however arose when the prompts given were incredibly obscure things, leaving many people to draw random things like an Among Us guy, leaving the answer to be extremely clear and obvious, ruining the game. This problem could just be with the concept of Drawful itself, however when you do get a non-obscure prompt, it can be a fun time. However, when you do get a non-obscure prompt, it can be explained and drawn usually in one frame, with use of a second pretty much useless. The only good you get out of the 'Animate' part of this one is through the images you draw for your characters, which says a lot.2.5/5On the surface, a normal trivia game, but once you dig deeper, it is quite bad. Like Trivia Murder Party, the questions are fairly obscure, however, this game isn't 'who can search on google the quickest', because even if you get every question right, this game is completely chance based. That's right, and the points system is even more messed up when it comes to the part where points can be split, and instead of it being done evenly, the majority of the points go to the person with lesser points, making both players have a similar amount of points, making the game even less fun.2/5This game is pretty solid, but nothing legendary by any means. It tries to imitate much better games like Survive the Internet or Quiplash, and it does it well enough in that regard. Many say this one is the best, but I think it's tied with Poll Mine, which I'll talk about next.4/5Poll Mine honestly is a pretty okay game, which I did enjoy. The only flaw with this one is the fact that usually during Jackbox you're in a room or voice call with the rest of the other players, meaning the other team can hear you discussing, and if you were to move room or voice call, then the other team will be unable to see what the other team had picked, giving them a disadvantage.This means when a team says that either the answer is A or B, and when you pick one of them and get it wrong, it leaves the other team able to pick the the other option, making them win in the end.This could be completely intentional by the developers, and it probably is, but for me it just does ruin the experience, however it is still a fun game.3.5/5Weapons Drawn was actually the game I was most interested in. The concept of everyone being both a Detective and Murderer was interesting, to say the least, but unfortunately the game was ruined for a number of reasons.First of all, the game was too complicated, at least according to my friends. I understood the game, but my friends said that they had no clue what they were doing the entire time. And in a sense, it's true. The drawing game where you had to guess the killer via a letter from their name would've been fine on it's own, but on top of that it was added with accomplices and guessing who is partnered with the accomplices, which is completely unnecessary and unlinked to the core concept of the game.Secondly, since players can see other players votes, people will usually just follow the herd and vote whoever is being voted by someone else. At times, it is completely unclear whether or not you're supposed to discuss and point out who the killer is, as if you do, once again, other players will herd the person and get the points alongside you, but even if you don't tell anything, other players will assume you know what you're doing, and vote alongside you, once again getting points with you.Third, it is strange that the letters the game pick's out of your name isn't specifically the first or last one, but instead it's a random one from your name, at least that is what it seems to be. The game no longer is about skill (like the wheel), but it's about who has the most convenient name, who has the longest name, and if RNG is on their side.Fourth, once you catch a killer, they continue to play the game. Though I guess it's wise to be against throwing out a player mid-game for losing, however, isn't that the entire point of a murder mystery?1/5Jackbox 8 is the weakest pack out of the one's that I currently own (3-7), and though I can tell they tried hard with these games, they just aren't the best, especially with the price being a lot higher than the other ones. Jackbox 3 and 4 still stand as the greatest entries at such a lower price, but this game has only two fairly good ones, with 4 of them being flawed in some way, and Weapons Drawn being so flawed I had to write 6 paragraphs to explain that fact.With the current price, Jackbox 8 isn't worth it. It's fun for a single session, but it gets pretty old fast. Definitely get Jackbox 3-7 first, then wait for this one to go on discount once the next couple ones come out, because, don't get me wrong, this is still a brilliant party game, but just not the most strong one.
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Party Pack 8

_childDocuments_.review: Party Pack 8 demonstrates that the Jackbox team only gets better and better each and every year. Just like the pack preceding it, Party Pack 8 is chock-full of substantial and entertaining games, each one pretty considerably wonderful.Job Job is one of the best games that has ever been released in a Party Pack. One of the few that my group has been able to consistently return to night after night, play for literal hours at a time, and continue to want to play. The highlight of this pack, far and away. Make sure you fill your icebreakers near the character limit; the game is much more fun with more words to work with!I really enjoyed Poll Mine personally; it's like a much more personal take on Guesspionage (one of my personal favorites from Party Pack 3). The group is surveyed in various categories, and you need to guess what aggregate ranking certain choices got in the whole group; depending on the friends you play with, this can be an absolute treat.Drawful: Animate is more of the same from the Drawful series, but that's never a bad thing; given drawful was going on half-a-decade without a new iteration (!!!) it was a welcome return of a series classic. The animation gimmick is lovely and the prompts are updated to be even more closer-to-the-pulse-of-modern-internet-slang, so sometimes we've been fooled by prompts being close enough to things my friends actually say that it was indistinguishable from someone aiming to get the likes award. Really fun, as drawful tends to be!Weapons Drawn is a heavy time investment, but absolutely warrants the time spent by providing pretty hilarious gameplay. Some people get really creative with hiding their weapons! It's impressive how many ways you can hide a cursive "t". Sort of a better take on Push the Button, and I'm a big fan of it for being a better deductive reasoning game (though PtB has its upsides, too.)The Wheel of Enormous Proportions is... well, my group isn't a fan. It seems like it's trying to be Trivia Murder Party (zany trivia with consequences for getting questions wrong, but getting a question wrong isn't the end of the game), but while the killing floors in TMP are interactive and interesting, the wheel spins really leave the fate of this game up to RNG - this makes it unrewarding to be good at the trivia (bad rng can equalize the playing field to an unreasonable degree) while also being boring to those not skillful at trivia (sure, you're not out of the game, but hoping on wheel spins to get back into the game is about as interesting as if every death in TMP was decided by the loser wheel. Yawn!) Ultimately, probably the lowest point of the pack - not a terrible game, just not Jackbox's greatest trivia showing. Ultimately, Party Pack 8 is one of my personal favorites in the storied series of party packs - a high recommendation from me!
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Party Pack 8

_childDocuments_.review: I own all of the Jackbox Party Packs up to date, and I can definitely say this pack has already climbed its way up my ranks. If you want my short, sweet recommendation for this party pack overall, it'll be at the very bottom of my review. Games-wise, I will explain Weapons Drawn last because it's got quite a bit of significance to me and it's a lot to take in.I'll try to keep the other games simple:Drawful except you draw a second frame to make an animation. I've seen some people mention the extended amount of time, or that some prompts are difficult to execute via drawing two panels. Yes, I will admit, some of the new prompts are very "What the hell?," but it adds to the funny factor as you grapple with how to draw it. Longer wait times was never an issue for my friend group. Drawful Animate is a great game that offered a lot of amusement.Jackbox definitely took a step in a different direction with this game, (in a good way). It's a trivia game that could be compared to the difficulty of the Trivia Murder Parties where almost no one knows many of the answers, but you're able to select numerous answers so you have a better fighting chance. Depending on how well you do in the rounds, you obtain "slices" to put into the wheel to earn jackpots to get you that sweet victory. Here's the catch though, the RNG for the wheel is horrendous. I personally did not mind it, as it spiced up the game and kept it going as everyone was neck-and-neck by that point in the match. This may turn some people away from the game, however, because you may be in first for a good chunk of the game and get the title ripped away from you at the very end. If you dislike poor RNG and/or somewhat random winners, I'd suggest you stray away from this game.I'd say this game was the most humorous out of all that are offered in this pack. You basically make anagrams out of a pool of words from the other player's responses at the beginning of the game. Fortunately for me, my friends had very.. Interesting responses to say the least and it provided good content for our answers, lmao. Definitely give this game a shot when you try the pack.I heard someone say this is like "Family Feud," and they are definitely right. Each round has a different twist, however. For example: You cannot pick the #1 answer, or you must answer which is the lowest score and move your way on up to the #1 answer. It's a clever and sneaky little game trying to deduce what the answers may be without letting the enemy team get too much insight on what your team picked for their answers. I also highly recommend this game, but I can see some people being turned away from it because of debate purposes. It's worth giving a shot, though!Lastly,Jackbox took a giant leap with this game, and honestly, I loved it. It's a very fleshed out game, and to be honest, it is probably the MOST complex game that Jackbox has ever created. Although I loved the game, I must also admit that it is very difficult to understand, and you will have to play it several times to get a decent grasp on how things run in it. In all honesty, I think part of the confusion drawn from this game comes from the players, too. This game gets quite complicated because you as the player are both a detective, and a murderer. Everyone brings a guest of their own to the party, and you must name your guest that you have brought. Once all the guests are presented, everyone must start guessing which player they think brought who (the guests). If you guess correctly, you murder the guest and get a murder point. That seems simple enough, until you have to start finding out who was behind the murders. Everyone had to draw murder weapons at the beginning of the game, disguising a letter the game assigned to them based off of the nickname they joined the game with. In order to throw people off, you are suggested to try and incorporate other letters so that yours isn't obvious.  The game becomes very complex because of the clever ways everyone tries to incorporate their letter into their weapon, and working around it to seem like it was someone else. It isn't all the players' fault for the complexity, however. Jackbox, after all, allowed for this to take place, and they even suggest it. Although yes, I thoroughly enjoyed Weapons Drawn, I cannot deny that I was scratching my head most of the duration of the game.Game mechanics and gameplay itself aside, the art, music, and ambience were phenomenal.Would I recommend Weapons Drawn? Absolutely, yes. However, keep in mind that this game requires a lot more thinking  and deduction than all of Jackbox's other games, (with the exception of Push the Buttton).Weapons Drawn Tl;dr:Frustrating to figure out and complicated as hell, but definitely fun and worth it as it pushes you to think creatively and cleverly. Great job on this one, Jackbox. You've outdone yourselves.

_childDocuments_.review: In short...I am going to not tentatively not recommend this one. Not enough in the box.................................................................................................................................................◽Drawful Animate: Pretty good as an opener and as a way to get people into Jack Box if they have never played before, but really only good as that. Has been replaced by more interesting drawing games. Still decent and plays up to 10 players which is super rare in jack box packs so for that reason alone it might get played more. The original plays a lot snappier, animating is satisfying and can definitely raise a laugh or two, just not sure it actually benefits the game.◽Job Job: First play was very fun, reminds me of the board game funemployed a bit. Okay alternative to Quiplash, not sure if it will have legs in the long run though. I feel like there is no reason to ignore the question and just pass on the "best" words possible in future plays. Need to play more to see. Plus side, also plays with 10.◽The Poll Mine: Only fun at high player counts. A lot of waiting between turns. But decent. The first time I played this with 4 I did not enjoy it. Another one that plays with 10, which could make it more interesting as the player count rises - we played the second time round with 7 and I enjoyed it a lot more. Still a bit  on slow side. The song bops though.◽Weapons Drawn: Far far far far to long for what it is. Also nothing to stop people just drawing squiggles in future plays I'd say. Did I mention its sooo slow. Would probably never play again even if I think its an okay idea.... in theory. Rating: It's a dud.◽Wheel of Enormous Proportions: Standard Quiz game, but the twist is just not fun. No Minigames just random chance and not the cool kind of random chance. Murder Mystery Quiz is ten times better. I will never play this over that. The second straight dud of the pack.Conclusion... Overall i would not recommend this one as your first party pack. If Job Job and the Poll Mine hold up maybe I will change my rating. _childDocuments_.review: update: we tried poll mine out and at least for us it is an A or B tier gameI love jackbox and the party packs but this one just didn't stick the landing like the others. This review mostly tells how my friends and I felt after playing some of the games.Drawful: Nothing has really changed from the other Drawful games other than the fact that your paintings are combined into one 2 frame animation. My friends were not very happy about the fact you could draw in only 3 colors and nothing else.Wheel: Wheel started out promising and the trivia was alright but once we realized that this game is basically just RNG + trivia it quickly lost its hype and we ultimately never completed it. _childDocuments_.review: This pack adds tons of wonderful new games! There wasn't any game that my friends and I didn't have a good laugh playing together. Here was everybody's overall consensus on the five new games:Drawful AnimateI personally am not a fan of Drawful AT ALL but Drawful Animate has changed my mind. Seeing everybody's animations and answers was incredibly hilarious. There's just a new layer with it that makes the humor out of control. Being able to control the speed of the two frame animation is such a wonderful tool, honestly. Made some of them much funnier. My roommate graduated college for animation and she won this game and screamed "MY DEGREE FINALLY PAID OFF!" which made everybody cry laughing.The Wheel of Enormous ProportionsIt's a new trivia game where you don't die if you get it wrong, you just get angry because you're bad at trivia and can't get any points. Honestly, this game felt a little unbalanced cause the people who actually knew things did do better BUT the wheel does help balance that issue. The first person to reach 20,000 points was second to last most the rounds, she just received a lot of points from getting spun on. Asking the wheel questions was kinda clunky though cause it seems like it just answer yes or no questions and nobody but myself asked a yes/no question. Makes winning feel a little empty if you don't know that in advance. Would have preferred to know. Overall still a fun game but I'd rather play Trivia Murder Party.Job JobSix out of six players said this game was their favorite. For good reason! Write in games are so great. It's what Dictionarium strived to be but never quite became. You write out answers to prompts, get them shredded and scrambled between players, and then answer interview questions with them. PLUS YOU CAN BUY T-SHIRTS WITH THE ANSWERS! We only played one game and I want half the answers as t-shirts in my closet. The prompts for writing and piecing together are great too. The game even lets you grab words from anywhere on the screen which is SO HELPFUL OH MY LORD. Definitely a game I'm throwing into my normal Jackbox rotation. Though maybe I like this game because I won. LolThe Poll MinesIt's fun. Pretty simple. Everybody gets polled on questions and you gotta find the most popular answers. It's Family Feud essentially. But sometimes you try to find the middle answers or the  least popular. Little twists. I was excited for it the most when everything was announced but not quite as exciting as I hoped. Fell a little flat on the group but it was still plenty of fun and I would play it again.Weapons DrawnMy second favorite game, though not everybody in my party enjoyed it. Especially because I won by a landslide (nobody solved any of my murders) and a bug made it so our sixth person could not draw weapons. I feel like I can't give it a solid review until I've had a more fair playthrough of it but I think this game is great so far. Wonderful concept. Somebody murdered Jesus and we did not rest until we found His killer. Which was my roommate. We still argued about it in the morning. My boyfriend made his first accomplice our boss and I don't know how nobody immediately assumed I killed her.Overall, it was a good party pack. Will play all of these games again, some more than others. Cannot wait for party pack nine! <3

_childDocuments_.review: This is my favourite Jackbox Party Pack yet. As always, there is a variety of games fit for all types of people. In fact, my group's favourite was The Poll Mine - a survey based/'how well do you know your friends' style game.We don't hate any of the games in the pack; it is the only pack that has no drawbacks for us.If these games seem like something you would enjoy, Jackbox Party Pack 8 is definitely worth the money!

_childDocuments_.review: So let's have a little talk about the new jackbox party pack!In this pack we have 4 brand new games and 1 returning one.We have:-Drawful: Animate (Return)-The Wheel of Enormous Proportions-Job Job-The Poll Mine-Weapons DrawnLet's start with Drawful:In drawful animate you get a secret prompt that you will have to draw/animate (a 2 frame animation). Once you have done that everyone will make a fake answer to make it look like that is the right answer to your animation while they will try to find the right answer hidden between all the other peoples fake answers.-This is an alright game because its a returning game but it can still be fun. The prompts can be really weird or the most obvious thing ever but youll always have something to draw. Most of the time you'll look at your prompt and think how in gods name you will draw this but hey, thats the fun of it!Next up Job Job:In Job Job you will fill in ice breaker question and you can answer these how ever you like (this makes for the best words to use and that makes it even more fun). After these breakers have been answered you will get "classic" job interview question that you will have to answer with the words other people have used/made for you. Most funny answer, voted by the rest of the players, wins that round!-This game is pretty relaxing and funny too. The amount of creativity you can put in your answers is all up to you and a little help by the other players. I really recommend you dont take the filling in of the ice breakers questions seriously because the weird sentences you get to make with the weirdest words is absolutely amazing.Up nexto it's The Poll Mine:In The Poll Mine you will get a category like: What is the best ice cream flavor?, Which tree would you be? or If you have to shop somewhere for the rest of your life where would you shop? (and thousands of others). When you get this category you will get a pre-set list of 8 answers and depending on the round you have to choose your 1st best answer, then 2nd, 3rd, etc. After everyone choose their answers they will compete in teams to try and find the best answers based on what everyone else also choose.-This is a good and pretty competitive game i have to say. Most of the time you will be really surprised by what your fellow friends have put in as their favorite ice cream flavor. And the way some teams will scream at eachother is hilarious.Aaaaand next is Weapons Drawn:In Weapons Drawn you are detectives who will also try to commits some murders for extra points. At the start you will try to make two murder weapons that have one of the letters in your name hidden in it as your calling card. After you have drawn these weapons you will name an accomplice you brought with you to the party. After that is finally all set and done you will try to commit some murder by guessing which other player brought one of the accomplices. After that you will try to find out which person commited which murder but looking for clues in the weapons.-Ive got to be completely honest with you, this game is not very great. The setup takes way longer then you might expect and the initial payoff isnt very not either. Ive played a round or two and i still dont quite understand what im doing. If this game wasnt as complicated and had less setup it might have been a little more fun but that wont really happen.Last and never least its THE WHEEL OF ENORMOUS PROPORTIONS:In The Wheel you first get to ask a burning question you always wanted answered and if you win the game you get this burning question answered too! After asking you will have to answer trivia questions to gain points and slices to put on the wheel for spinning. After 3 trivia questions have been asked you get to use the slices you have earned on the wheel to get even more points. This will keep happing until a player with 20.000 points lands with the winners wheel on a winning slice.-This game is fun, not trivia murder party fun but still fun. Most of these trivia question arent actually that hard and most of the times if you just guess you will still get enough right to get enough points.In summary this is another good pack with always some games that arent great but still a little fun.Now for some scores:Drawful: Animate - 6/10 - Fun but still the same.Job Job - 8.5/10 - Always fun and always fair, never any dull answer.The Poll Mine - 8.5/10 - Again surprisingly good, the competitive side makes it even more fun.Weapons Drawn - 6/10 - Could be simpeler.The Wheel of Enormous Proportions - 6.5/10 - Simpel but sometimes feels like its rigged (talking about you jasper).Over all score: 7/10.-Some good, some a little less good-

_childDocuments_.review: as of yet only played two of the games, but I'll review them anyway since I think those two alone would be worth picking up this box.weapons drawn combines both drawing and a little bit of word-based answers (with naming the guests) which makes it a fun way to gauge how people's humor works and make fun visual gags and references too.job job is definitely a stand-out star. it combines a lot of concepts from previous jackbox games into a really simple but great formula: (literally) twisting your friends' words into beautiful barely comprehensible word salad. it seems like a combination of joke boat and survive the internet, but the added addition of constructing your answer word-by-word adds a fantastically hilarious dimension of jank.[I'll add more to this review as I play the other games, but, again, I think these two games are already worth the pick up.]edit for poll mine:also a good game, but i feel it might lack replay value. it's a good way to judge if you know your friends and how they might rank things (of course when the category came to "best body part" it was inevitable we all voted "ass", so...) and it's a neat if somewhat overcomplicated competitive game if you like to split the room that way.

_childDocuments_.review: Job Job is easily solidified as S++ tier already, and easily the best game in the party packs since Tee-KO (and may even surpass it). I'm only giving this pack a positive rating because Job Job will  carry the game to having a decent dollar-to-hours-played ratio (as long as you can play with a decent number of people). It may not be terribly enjoyable with only 4 people, but with 6+ it shines. Maxing it out with 10 people (with a few in the audience) would probably be where the game shines the most (in that regard, it's a lot like Quiplash). 9/10Poll Mine is decent. There's not much more to say about it. It's easily a solid B tier or may fit in the lower A tier. There's enough there to have a good time - but it's likely one that will vary a lot depending on the group you play it with. Seems like it'd work excellently as a streamed game, though. 7/10Weapons Drawn feels like one of those games that would benefit from being in-person. As is the case with most of the recent party packs, this is the "meaty" game of the five. There isn't really enough talking or humour for it to be a fun time remote/over Discord. My group didn't particularly enjoy it the first time around, but I'm reserving my judgement on it. 5/10Drawful Animate doesn't really offer enough over Drawful for it to be worthwhile. If you're drawing with a finger on a 6-inch phone screen or with a mouse, it's just not possible to be precise enough to get your point across. Everything ends up sort of cramped, and a lot of the prompts hardly warrant the animated aspect of it. If you really enjoy Drawful, you'll probably enjoy this, but you should also probably just play Drawful instead. 4.5/10The Wheel of Enormous Proportions is pretty much just a more bland version of Trivia Murder Party. If you're a trivia fiend and have played all the other trivia games in the pack to death, you'll most likely enjoy it. Other than that, probably just play TMP. 3.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Party Pack 8

_childDocuments_.review: My initial review of Jackbox 8 was absolutely glowing, I gave it a 9/10, and said it was the best one so far. I have no idea what I was on at the time, but I'm redoing this review as I think it completely missed the mark.Jackbox 8 is fine, but it marks the end of the "golden age" of Jackbox, which I would define as 4-7. "Fine" is the key word I'd use to describe everything on show here, none of the games really stand out, but none of them are really terrible either. Weapons Drawn has a cool aesthetic, but it's the least interesting art game the team has ever produced. You get a letter, and you have to draw a weapon around that letter to make it hard to tell which letter you're hiding. It's a fine idea, but the restrictions make it almost impossible, the best way to win is to make fake red herring letters, and it just leads to everyone kind of bullshitting the game instead of actually playing it. Poll Mine is fun once or twice, but you need to have a big group of people that you know decently well, otherwise its a lot of shots in the dark, or there's not enough of you to make it interesting, and you can guess everything. Job Job is just rearranging letters to write something shocking, its the standard "play it once the first time you open the pack and never again" game. Drawful Animate is fun, but Drawful has always paled in comparison to Jackbox's cooler art games like Champ'd Up or TKO, and I find if your group doesn't have a lot of artists that people struggle a lot with the animation mechanic, simple as it is. Finally, The Wheel of Enormous Proportions is just another trivia game, but with some RNG to make sure the winner stays in the lead. Just a really weak collection of games, it's not one we ever really go back to, its just ok at best. 5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: I think this is a pretty solid follow up in the jackbox series, I cant lie after the triumph that was Party Pack 7 and how good that pack was it left a lot to be desired, and while I feel this pack did deliver on a few things, I cant help but feel underwhelmed especially after this was the followup to Party Pack 7.DRAWFUL ANIMATE: This is a pretty nice addition to the drawful series and its a VERY cute gimmick that I have a lot of fun with, it changes things up so it feels like a new game, but not enough that it doesn't feel like drawful which I love! The animations you make can feel smooth and satisfying to watch, I will say I think drawful 2 is still the best one, but this one does NOT disappoint, the only criticism I have is that if you are playing with the max of 10 people, be prepared for a LONG game, as when I played with 10 people it took from 30-40 minutes. THE WHEEL OF ENORMOUS PROPORTIONS:I think the obvious problem for a lot of people is the fact that this game is ALL RNG, meaning that you don't have to be good at trivia to win, you just have to be lucky.  FOR ME, this doesn't bother me, but if you hate luck games then this is a skip, but if it doesn't this is a game for you.  This is probably jackbox's best game on a trivia standpoint alone, the trivia is diverse, it encompasses a lot of different elements and is all around a very fun time, the trivia isn't niche, its about everything meaning you can get a category on something you're very experienced in.   The gimmick of getting to ask the wheel something if you win is also very cute, if you don't mind the RNG in this game i'd recommend it.JOB JOB:It's an alternative to quiplash, and while I hear a lot of praise for this game, i'll say I do not have that same praise everybody has for this game.  The positives are sometimes you can make VERY funny answers, so much so that this can top quiplash at times in funniness.  I will also say visually, this is way more visually pleasing then ALL the quiplash games, also I love the water cooler host.  My issue is actually my main issue, the word bank, now I get why its there and it sometimes it is VERY funny, however sometimes ill get stuff in my word bank that just doesn't make sense, or just doesn't make a sentence funny, and it can become very frustrating,POLL MINE:I love the family fued vibe this game gives off and the arguments that ensue over where to place a torch becomes very fun to do.  I like how the categories aren't anything very niche, like TV shows so that everybody can rate and place things in an order that they believe in.  I also like how you only know HALF of the peoples opinions, meaning that you have to try and guess what the other side likes so it makes it more difficult to try and guess and doesn't make it all cookie cutter.  The only con is if you are playing in the same room as everybody and its a small room, you might be able to hear the other team talking taking away that aspect of guessing what the other team rated everything.WEAPONS DRAWN: Unfortunately I can't say much about this one as i've opened it once and haven't touched it since.  It is way to complex and their are to many elements that makes it easy to understand for a first timer, and when I played for the first time I just found myself being confused.  Whats even more disappointing is that a murder mystery jackbox game sounded so fun, but the fact it turned into a drawing game that makes little sense is disappointingRATINGS:1. POLL MINE (9/10)2. DRAWFUL ANIMATE (7.5/10)3. JOB JOB (6.5/10)4. THE WHEEL OF ENORMOUS PROPORTIONS (6/10)5. WEAPONS DRAWN (3/10)

_childDocuments_.review: I'm usually a huge fan of Jackbox packs, but, this time, my friends and I all agreed that this game didn't live up to our expectations. For me, Jackbox is at its best when it gives its players freedom - the freedom to be funny, creative, or silly. The only game we all truly enjoyed was Job Job, but that alone is never going to be worth $26. It felt like the Wheel of Epic Proportions, Poll Mines, and Weapons Drawn were completely different from Jackbox's usual wheelbox  for creating fun, original ideas. It's not bad to try something new of course, but the games were not fun to play with friends. Nothing my friends and I did could have ever made the games more fun because the games were so heavily structured. It seems like Jackbox forgot that most of their best games provide their players the chance to make their friends laugh or get creative. This pack felt much more serious to me, and I would not recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: 5/6 Great Jackbox games. My personal order from worst to best is Drawful: Animate, Wheel of Enormous Proportions, Poll Mine, Job Job, and Weapons Drawn. You could switch them around (except for Drawful). Drawful sucks and I don't know why they made it again. Wheel of Enormous Proportions is fun like Trivia Murder Party. Unlike Trivia Murder Party, however, there is so much chance to this game. You could get 20k right away and lose to spinning a skull space 4 times only for your friend to get an easy shot at it that's nearly impossible to miss. Poll Mine is interesting because it is a team based game, something you usually do not see in many Jackbox games. The way it shifts from the objectives of the certain stages where you have to find the most or least voted answers is great. Job Job is improved Quiplash. By having to make something creative out of what you are given is amazing. This prevents people from having nothing for the prompt and just putting something random. Having all these choices limits you but also allows you to see what your answer is better. Weapons Drawn is the perfect Jackbox Game. One of my favorite Jackbox Games was Push the Button, and to see an improved social deception Jackbox game is great. This game is so much fun. From hiding your calling card, to searching for others calling cards, to naming your accomplices and guessing who's who, to just the narrator. This game is Jackbox perfection. This game alone makes 8 my favorite pack. This pack is 100% worth the purchase. Just don't play Drawful: Animate.

_childDocuments_.review: Another solid collection of thoroughly entertaining party games.Drawful Animated is a great twist on the original. Drawing games aren't usually our preference, but I think having two frames to communicate your absurd prompt is more forgiving and fun than just having one.Wheel of Enormous Proportions was a bit of a letdown. Trivia games aren't particularly interactive and the self-aware emphasis on randomness in this game means things are even more out of control (and not really in a fun-chaotic way). Most of the group's commentary was simply a reaction to whether they had won or lost that question or wheel spin.Job Job is my personal favorite. There's a nice, collaborative feeling to creating weird material for others to use. Everyone can usually come up with a response that's clever or at least comedically incoherent. It's just more of that classic Jackbox vote-on-the-silliness shenanigans in a surprising new format.The Poll Mine is probably the best 'group-discussion' Jackbox game yet. Even in a smaller group, deducing the popularity of various subjects as a team leads to good-natured discussions and arguments. Coming to grips with the reasoning behind others' thoughts for picking answers can be enlightening. Or, it can be a good chance to make fun of somebody and potentially make a fuss whenever the results surprise you.Weapons Drawn is the least intuitive game in the pack. It takes a while to explain and there's a lot of narration during play. The base concept of hiding a letter in a drawing wasn't as intriguing as many drawing games' premises are. The whodunit detective discussion aspect wasn't particularly entertaining either.
