_childDocuments_.review: Another good pack! This has entered my group's rotation regularly since release. Game by game:Everyone likes JobJob, which is easy to play and has ridiculous results. Downside is that the UI is not clear enough about there being multiple responses in the early rounds, so it always takes new players by surprise.Weapons Drawn is a lot of fun, and it's nice that it has several different things going on. Some people in my group really like Drawful Animate, but it has a lot of quiet, hands-down drawing time compared to Drawful.The Poll Mine seemed interesting at first, but because it relies on rankings made from a small number of votes, the later picks mostly end up feeling random. Figuring out what other people picked in a ranking also doesn't feel as interesting as expected, partly because the things you're ranking are often too weird.The wheel game is awful! The trivia part is OK, but the wheel part is slow, the player UI for the spin is confusing, and the way the leader randomly wins or doesn't win based on the wheel is extremely unsatisfying and makes the trivia feel pointless. In my group people jokingly suggest the wheel game just to get groans.

_childDocuments_.review: Jackbox 8 is the latest one I bought, and it is GREAT. I’m telling you, it’s way better than everyone claimed. The games are fun, and even the ones people are hating on are great. My friends and I are having fun with it. I know it’s a very unpopular opinion, but I would be bold enough to say it is at least as good as Jackbox 6, if not better. Maybe the best Jackbox pack there is even.THE WHEEL OF ENORMOUS PROPORTIONS is the weakest game in this pack, but it ain’t bad. It’s a good and innovative trivia game. The questions and their unique types are really great. And the wheel? Maybe it’s just us because I am from Central Europe and grew up watching a TV game show "Kolotoč" (basically my country’s version of the US game show Wheel of Fortune) but I LOVE IT. The wheel is funny, and its implementation gives some random factor of luck which spices things up. Overall, it’s really good. (6/10)Everyone will kill me now, but the second weakest for me is probably JOB JOB. It’s good and funny. The idea and visuals are great. But to me, it got really repetitive quickly. It may definitely grow on me, but I don’t think it’s the best game of this pack atm, not even close to it. It is kinda generic, and the rest of the games in this pack are way more innovative than just shuffling some words around. (7/10)The next one is probably DRAWFUL ANIMATE. This game grew on my friend group. The extremely random animations, often in terrible quality as we aren’t artistic at all, make it so funny. It’s basically like Fibbage but drawn. It’s very simple, but sometimes the simple games are the best. (8/10)It’s hard to decide between the last two games about my absolute favorite. But I guess that THE POLL MINE is a bit weaker. In a group of at least 6, it’s an absolutely awesome game. Everyone I played with likes the chaos between the teams when they try to communicate what option to pick without spoiling too much to the enemy team. It’s a more chill game, but things can get heated real quick when you don’t wanna make mistakes while losing. Overall, a freaking great game. (9,5/10)The best game in this pack is for me WEAPONS DRAWN. This game was the main reason why I bought this pack myself. All of my friends like this game, and I think the idea, the visuals, music, everything about this game… it’s just too good. Yes, it is very complicated. And I mean VERY. I always spend several minutes explaining the new players' rules before we start and then have to repeat multiple things as they forget the first time they play. But once everyone knows what to do after one playthrough, it’s just… perfect. Simply a perfect party game. The drawing creative weapons, murdering accomplices, solving the murders of others… it’s just super detailed and well-made. Whoever made this game – good job. It deserves the number one spot. (10/10)Overall:The average of game scores is 8,1.I really love this pack, and so do my friends. On average better than the 6th pack. But Jackbox 6 has better top 2 games than pack 8. The Internet really lies about it, because people are hating on many games that we actually love so so much. I absolutely recommend this pack. The games are very unique and creative, so not everyone will like all of them, but I am sure everyone will find some they will love.

_childDocuments_.review: I own all the other packs and I think I can comfortably say that this is either the 2nd or 3rd best one (best obviously being 3, second place maybe going to 7).Disclaimer: Haven't gotten around to playing Weapons Drawn just yet, if I remember that I wrote this later on I'll update it for that game. Anyways, about the other 4...Also I like making tier lists so I'll give each game an approximate tier list ranking.Drawful Animate:I think this one doesn't get quite enough credit. While it seems like the only main new gimmick of this game compared to its previous versions is the whole "animation" thing (which still allows for some funnier artwork imo), it has a second much more subtle change as well. The prompts.Normally in the "lie detection" games (Drawfuls and Fibbages) it's very easy to identify certain wrong answers due to spelling, grammar, or punctuation use. Drawful Animate throws that all out the window with some of the weirdest prompts I've ever seen. The game even gave me a prompt that was deliberately spelled wrong! This means the game is a lot more "how well do you know your friends' brains" and a lot less "did you do well in high school english class."However if you already own an older drawful and didn't notice/care for this trend while playing, you may be better off sticking to it instead.RANK: Low A tierWheel of Enormous Proportions:While it's certainly not as good as the Trivia Murder Party games, this one is still alright. The format of the questions switches up often enough to keep things from getting too stale. The wheel spinning does seem to be a bit more of the focus though, which may not be your cup of tea if you prefer competitive trivia. The delay between questions is also longer than in TMP, but is still quicker than YDKJ.If you want hardcore trivia, this probably isn't for you. But if you enjoy getting screwed over sometimes and screaming at your friends at the top of your lungs, then this game is a good choice. RANK: Mid B tierJob Job:Holy crap this game is just so good. I would say it's better than all 3 Quiplashes and maybe even good enough to take the crown from Surviving the Internet as the best Jackbox game overall. The game is similar to Quiplash in that you're coming up with comedic responses to prompts and pairing off against each other, but the main difference is that your friends get to do the heavy lifting by providing you with lots of words to pick from based on a personal response prompt (like in STI). This results in absolutely hilarious answers that look like they were written by a serial killer. The game also has a few easter eggs and lots of references for those who like that kind of thing.The verdict's in folks. Job Job is an absolutely incredible game that represents a new gold standard for the Jackbox series.RANK: S+Poll Mine: Currently my least favourite game (haven't played Weapons Drawn yet though). It isn't bad though, just not nearly as good as the others. The concept of a team based escape game is fun and creative (I think this is actually the first Team vs Team Jackbox game, which is surprising), but it has a couple things holding it back. 1. The 3 rounds (as far as I can tell) are always the same. You'll always be trying to find the exact same positions in the poll each game you play. This is the same reason I slightly prefer Quiplash 2 over the other 2 games; the final round is not the same style each time. 2. You have to rank too many things in the later rounds. I think that 3 is excellent number to stay at for the whole game. 4 is alright sometimes, but by 5 I find that people approach "impartial" territory with the rankings.Despite its flaws though, this game is still pretty fun, and the teams thing gives it some uniqueness.RANK: Low BOverall, pack 8 is a solid entry in the series. It's possibly worth getting for Job Job alone, but the other games do pull their weight as well. (I doubt my thoughts on WD will change this point much lol)

_childDocuments_.review: Best Jackbox yet. GAMES RANKED BEST TO WORST*Job Job: The 'write funny stuff' and make your friends laugh game of this game. This is the best one. Like all joke games, this will be benefited by a funnier friend group, although I think the fridge magnet mechanic of picking words makes it easier to think of funny things than some of the other games. We laughed really, really hard at this one though and it's novel.*The Poll Mine: Family feud style game with also some team vs team 'Codenames' type mechanics. Simple enough concept but opens itself up to surprising depth of strategy and interesting discussions. We replayed this one a couple times as well because we loved it.*Drawful Animate: Like the title says, this is your classic Drawful with a fun but not super game-changing twist. The animation aspect is pretty intuitive, you now do two panels. If your group likes Drawful this is absolutely worth playing, it's solid.*Weapons Drawn: I think with a few more grounds this might edge above Drawful, though there's a lot to learn the first time playing this and I think it could have been slightly more streamlined. It's kind of a mafia/werewolf type (social deduction) game with drawings. The core conceit of hiding letters in drawings is good, though and leads to some interesting results.*The Wheel of Enormous Proportions: Easily the weakest game by a mile. It's essentially a plain trivia game with a drawn out randomised wheel mechanic. I appreciate mixing up the theme from Trivia Murder Party with something more upbeat, but there's nothing really special about this one. It's still 'fine enough' but I don't think most players would be drawn to play this like some of the others.Overall, despite the Wheel being a bit weaker than the other games, all the others are extremely good and this is a very fine offering from Jackbox.

_childDocuments_.review: I sadly have to say that this is most likely the worst one of the series yet and definitely wasn't worth the amount of money. It's cute and caused a few giggles but that's about it. It's just Drawful but with a second image to turn your drawing to life.  This game was probably our least favorite. Not only do you ask a question that will most likely never be answered but you also get trivia questions with multiple-choice answers. Just pick all of them and you're good to go because most of them are probably correct. Not to mention that the questions asked are so ridiculously hard or so weird that it doesn't make any sense.  This game was one of the more fun ones. You get to fill in questions and your friends have to build answers with the words given to them. It was quite fun at first and we had a good laugh but that laugh didn't last long and the game soon became boring. After a while it almost feels frustrating to try and build sentences. Sadly we didn't enjoy this one either. It's a luck based team-game in which you and your friends have to rank your answers to a question. The teams then have to guess the results and figure out where the answer would be on a scale from 1 to 8. The results can be hard to guess as some friends (especially mine) tend to be trolls and just put in the most ridiculous answers that would make the least sense from a sensible perspective. This title didn't suit our group of friends at all. It felt longwinded and just really wasn't fun. You have to hide a letter in your name inside of a drawing of a weapon and then kill other player's accomplices with said weapon. Once you do that, people vote on whose murder gets investigated and then you have to compare the images and names. Then you vote on who you think is a killer and once you've done that, you will not learn if you received points or not. Too much for a game that's supposed to be a fun title for a fun night.Extremely disappointing. I'll stick to , ,  and .

_childDocuments_.review: Truly outstanding so far. I was worried about one or two of them, but they're all good fun.The soundtrack is consistently good. Job Job and Drawful Animate seem to be the weaker ones on that front, but they've got some scattered bangers themselves. The murdering song in Weapons Drawn has a cool owl, and the credits song is soothing. Wheel of EP is in general electrifying. Poll Mine is all-around good listening outside of the game, and the past couple of weeks I've listened to it while drawing and studying.Having two drawing games is a bit different, but they do focus on different things. Drawful Animate is, as Drawful always is, a celebration of bad drawings with tools and prompts designed to make even accomplished artists fumble. There's a "friends mode" that I need to give a shot and will update the review to mention. Weapons Drawn, however, is about cleverly hiding something in your drawing - but being aware that people can catch on to how you hide things, and also your style. There's always been a "haha, I know who drew that!" when someone draws in a distinct style on a tablet, and now there's a game with even more focus on hiding that.Poll Mine... Amazingly works with two players. With more players, it has a rare element of team games where you have to communicate with your team, but have to avoid creating a situation where you've helped the other team by giving something away. Is the other team banking on nobody picking something you placed at #1? Steal their thoughts and improve them. With an audience, the game changes yet again.Wheel of Enormous Proportions replaces the "you never feel like you're losing" that Trivia Murder Party has with some elements of pure randomness, which is somehow enjoyable. So far, however, I've felt that the answering style of most rounds discourages me from selecting answers and hoping most were incorrect. Maybe I haven't played enough, or maybe it will become the weaker game for me.Job Job is enjoyable. This might end up being the "it depends on who you play it" with of the pack, but any group should work well together just by being enthusiastic about it and giving the other players some good material. It reminds me of learning a foreign language or talking to someone who's learning English, which always results in some weird sentences that really show that language is a tool for communication. So, Job Job is a nice recreation of that "oh no, how do I say this thing with a limited vocabulary" feeling, without any fear of actual consequences. Seriously, though, I've seen people suddenly get really good at English in VRChat just because they repeated the words someone else said without caring if they looked foolish, and I don't know how to express the similarity I'm seeing with that and Job Job.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I think this pack is a little bit weaker than the last few but definitely not the worst and is still worth it in my opinion. Ill rank these games from my favorite to least favorite. However I might rank some games higher than I like them since how I rank them is my opinion, and then the ranking is what I think of it as whole for everyone.Starting off is Job Job. This one was really tough since personally I don't think this is that great of a game actually, for me and my group we are really a bunch of bozos and we seem to have a really hard time finding the right words to accurately answer the prompt in a funny way. However this is in no way a bad game at all, this game is really fun but I think it just takes the right group. The way I see this game is that it is just basically Quiplash when you choose the words from other peoples answers from the icebreaker question. So good game, but Quiplash is just better. This one is a low A tier for me.Next up is Weapons Drawn. This might be one of my favorite "not funny" Jackbox games of all time meaning that the purpose of it is not to be funny but something else. Basically in this game you are given a letter from your name and you have to fit that letter into a drawing that you make of a predetermined weapon, you do this two times and then one of those that you drew will be the weapon that you dropped for the rest of the game (used for people to compare murder weapons to to see if the letters match). Then you come up with a name for a guest and then when it comes to the murdering part, you pick a guest and guess who brought them, if you get it right you kill them successfully. Finally you see the weapon that a person was killed with and try to match that weapon with the weapon that all of the people dropped at the beginning of the game revealing whether they were the murderer or not. Overall this is probably one of the most complicated jackbox games of all times and because of that I think you really need the right group of people and you 100% need the time to learn it which might take a few games that could last very long. Luckly for me, I had the perfect group of people and after we took the time to learn how to play, we had a blast playing this game. For me this is S tier but objectively this is probably a solid low B or high C.Coming up next is Poll Mines. This game I think will be great for any group of people. Its not too long, its a great bit of fun since you have to work in teams of two. And is great for teamwork and strategizing with friends. Not to much to add, you basically get a prompt and have to rank the answers which creates a general ranking for each answer, than the teams take turns discussing what order the answers are in based on the round. Ex: "Rank top 3" "Rank worst to best" or "Rank 2, 3, and 4". Overall this game is great but can get boring if played too much so I would say an objective rating of 8/10 or around a solid mid B.Drawful Animate is next and while we had a lot of fun with this one, the other ones were just better for our group personally. This game is like any other game of drawful but you instead have to make two slides that loop to make a small animation with your prompt. You can also double up for when you are almost 100% sure you have the right answer. This game for us was like maybe a 6/10 but I think objectively this is definetly top 2 with Job JoB coming in with an A.Last and also least is The Wheel Of Enormous Proportions. This was not only the worst one for our group but also objectively this one just kinda falls short. I wont go too much into this one but basically its a trivia game thats not just multiple choice thats also mixed with complete RNG with spinning a wheel deciding who gets points. depending on how you look at it, it can either seem like a good concept with horrible execution or horrible concept with a great execution. I have to give it at least a little bit of credit since it does have a great visual design and has a pretty solid narrator. This one is a not-so-solid 5/10 or D tier both subjectively and objectively for me.Overall, this pack is pretty good but definitely not as good as the as previous games, (especially after pack 7 which in my opinion was the best pack by a long run.) Overall a B tier game. Definitely worth it if you have other packs, but if its your first pack i would go with pack 7 or maybe 6 depending on what you want.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm mixed on this Pack.Job Job: the best game in the pack IMO. Great mix of humor, creative wordplay, and making fun of your friends.Poll Mine: Probably the second best game. It constantly had me on the edge of my seat with each question, and it was also a neat way to see what everyone's opinions were. Very unique art style too.The Wheel of Enormous Proportions: Pretty solid triva game with a suprisingly good sense of humor. Definiately a game that heavily relies on chance for you to win, but I think it only enhances the experience, because you can still play skillfully or win through dumb luck. I think people don't give this one credit because "wah, the worst player can win by complete luck", but we already have jackbox triva games where one nerd dominates the ENTIRE time because they just know more. This is a very different kind of trivia game, and I think that's ok.Drawful animate: very torn on this one. I don't think this should be considered an upgrade to the past drawful games, it's more like a side-grade. The game lasts much longer, but in exhchange everyone's drawings could be more understandable and/or entertaining. Weapons drawn: Unless you're REALLY concentrating on the game, skip this one. It's clear that there's a lot of great ideas and fun art in this game, but it is just way to confusing to pick up and play.*as a general, not-specific-to-one-game comment, this pack introduced written tutorials shown on each players phone during the lobby and intro video of each game. I don't have much to say about this change, other than it's welcome.

_childDocuments_.review: I could go into more detail as to why I think this is one of the frustrating entries in the series, but you really should not get this pack unless you have more than 4 people to play it with.Technically you can play 80% of the games with 3 players, but games like Poll Mine were clearly not designed for small crowds even if only 2 people are needed to play it.Quick Game by Game review:Drawful Animate is hurt by the fact that you can't erase anything and that the actual drawing experience was a lot better in the previous Jackbox pack's drawing game Champ'd UpWheel of Enormous Proportions: This game had the potential to be the next Trivia Murder Party and could have carried the pack by itself with a better balance between luck and rewarding the contestants who actually know the answers to the trivia questions. The trivia portion of the game is as solid as any entry Jackbox has put out, but starting every player off with two slices to put on the wheel was a mistake. I don't know why Jackbox hasn't put out a patch to at least give players the option to make it less luck based.Job Job: I loved it, but the group I played it with did not.Poll Mine: This game is good. It's better with a larger group (as are most Jackbox games). However, in this case it's especially important based on the game mechanicsWeapons Drawn: STEEP learning curve. If you can get past that, then I think this game has the most potential as it combines a lot of the elements that make Jackbox games fun into a single game. My group got bored and wanted to go back to Trivia Murder Party after 3 games of it and we've never gone back.In conclusion: There are stronger Jackbox packs out there (especially 6 and 7) and most of them are a lot cheaper as well. Also, I'd highly recommend skipping this pack entirely if the group of people you're going to be playing it with is 4 or fewer.

_childDocuments_.review: I always instantly buy every single Jackbox Game as soon as they come out because I absolutely love these types of games. I play em with friends, family, and on my streams with viewers which you should totally check out btw. And the newest game, Jackbox Party Pack 8 is another fantastic entry in the franchise. It has a great mix of drawing, quiz taking, joke making, and social deception.And so I want to go over each game in this pack and tell you what I like or don't like from each game. The first game is Drawful Animate. This is pretty much just drawful but with an added gimmick of all your drawings having two frames that it rotates between to make it look like your pictures are animated. Your tasked with a prompt that you have to draw and everyone then has to guess what the original drawing was. I think this is my new favorite version of drawful simply because the animations do make it a little bit more fun but I wish there were more options like an undo button or different brush sizes as the drawing can be a bit limited.The next game in the pack is the wheel of enormous proportions. It is one of my new favorite trivia games in all of jackbox. It is a completely absurd and very RNG heavy quiz game but if you're not taking the game seriously it's one of the most fun jackbox games I've ever played. And the first thing everyone is tasked to do is to write a question in life that they would love to have answered. Then it's just a normal sort of trivia game except you're choosing which answers are correct in a big list of possible answers most of the time. And you're constantly being awarded these point slot things and whoever wins the last question gets an advantage in the next round. You're then shown this giant wheel and everyone can place their point slots on various different sections of the wheel. Players then take turns spinning the wheel and whoever it lands on gets points. There's also some crazy random rng stuff that can happen like switching two players point totals completely and other things like that. And that's what I love about this game. It is balls to the wall and as long as you're not taking it seriously it is the most hilarious thing on the planet. And whenever you get to 20,000 points you're allowed to spin a wheel that will potentially just allow you to win the game instantly. And you play until someone gets to 20,000 points and spins to instantly win. And then that player does one final spin on the question that they were asking at the beginning of the game to make for some hilarious moments! And like I said earlier this is one of my new favorite quiz games in jackbox. If you play it fully acknowledging that RNG is going to happen and you can't get annoyed by that it is so much fun.And because you can get answers partially right it feels like you're always making progress even if in normal trivia games you would just lose a lot of questions in a row. Easily one of my new all-time favorites in all of jackbox. The next game in the pack is Job Job. And it’s kind of like quiplash except it’s themed around multiple players going through a job interview and having to answer interview questions. Every player is tasked with answering a question you might typically find on a job interview and then the game scrambles all the words used in those answers together and has each player use those words to create funny answers to random prompts and everyone votes on whose answer was better.It is pretty unique but honestly after the first couple of times playing this game, I think I still prefer Quiplash for the type of funny answer game this is. Nothing wrong with it, I just don’t think it has the most replayability ever.The next game is Poll Mine and this one is actually pretty freaking cool. It splits all the players into two different teams and then it constantly gives every player polls like what's your favorite piece in the chex mix or other random topics. Each team then takes turn trying to guess what the top answers are, or bottom answers are, all depending on what the game asks you to do. It gives me big family feud vibes and honestly I dont think there was a jackbox game like this before so I think it fills a huge role in jackbox. I still haven’t played this game with people in real life, I’ve only played it on stream so I still haven't experienced it fully as I think a big part of it is reading the room and kind of trying to predict what your friends will respond to.This is easily one of my favorites in the pack and I think it will be a classic that I revisit over and over.And the last game in the pack is Weapons Drawn. It’s the main social deception game in the pack and it tries to do something unique from other social deception games including previous ones they’ve made. Instead of having most people be innocent and having some traitors in this game everyone is both a murderer and a detective. Everyone has a letter that is in their username they have to hide in drawings they make. You then have to try killing each others guests and guessing who killed who by examining everyone's drawings and trying to find those hidden letters.This is a game, like a lot of other social deception jackbox games, that are a bit more involved and I was a little confused at first but I think if I play it more, especially with people in real life it will grow on me. The one thing I really like about this game compared to other jackbox social deception games is that theres not a huge pressure to try and hide your the traitor or killer. The game is more point based as everyone is a murderer and a detective so I think its better for playing with more casual groups that might not like full on social deception games like push the button. And so overall I like every game in the pack but if I had to order them from my most favorite to least favorite I’d say it would be first the Wheel of Enormous Proportions, then Poll Mine, then Drawful Animate, then Weapons Drawn & Job Job.I think this is a fantastic addition to the Jackbox library and proves to me at least like each other game in the franchise that the developers are still able to keep producing amazing games in the franchise even after 8 years straight of releasing games yearly.If you are as big of a Jackbox fan as I am then this is a must buy!And if you love these types of games as much as me then follow my   for more reviews and videos about them!

_childDocuments_.review: The Jackbox party pack 8 is one of the worst packs in the series. I do not understand the positive reviews for it - I can only assume that the individuals rating this game have stayed isolated since the beginning of COVID and have not actually played it in a group setting.To start with, the wheel of enormous proportions is quite possibly the worst game ever made in the Jackbox franchise. It single handedly has killed the vibe of every group I have played it with. It has the potential to be a great trivia game, but ruins it with unnecessary randomness and spinning that does not seem to end. To summarise, the repetitive nature of the game absolute kills any fun it could possibly bring to a group of players.Drawful Animate is likely the best game in the pack, however also falls quite flat. It is a shell of other popular multiplayer "animate" games, but was fun about once. Poll Mine is not the worst mini-game, however it just doesn't have the spark that many of the previous packs bring to the series. With limited chances to be creative, have any spontaneity, the game becomes rather boring quickly. Weapons Drawn had a lot of potential, however a person in our group quickly realised a small visual flaw in the images that could be used to basically break the game mechanics completely no matter how well you disguised the image. This possibly may be caused from our large screen play area, but once the secret gets out, the game basically becomes unplayable. This leaves Job Job, which suffers from the same issues that Poll Mine does. We left the game with a few lackluster chuckles at best, but nothing that would come close to the hilarity that the other packs would have brought.Overall, I do NOT recommend that anyone purchase this pack, even for collection value unless you can get it on sale for ten dollars or less. Even at ten dollars, I'm not sure if I would recommend. I would sooner pick up packs 5, 6, and 7 as you will get much more playtime and value out of it for less money.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who owns every party pack but 7, I think this is the best release since party pack 4. However party pack 8 seems to be a refreshing break from other previous packs. Drawful animate is the only sequel game in recent years that actually seems justified and the rest are originals of rather sound quality. These originals seem more complex and require more learning than previous packs, but they are a lot of fun when you learn the ropes. Weapons drawn, Job Job, and wheel of enormous proportions are all decent games, but the one that takes the cake here is poll mine. It is different in the fact that it is a survey game essentially instead of a traditional trivia game, which I believe is a good new direction for the series. Poll Mine will be more fun among tighter knit groups of people, but me and my friends replayed that game 4 times after our first run through because it was just so novel to us.In summary, this pack I feel is an improvement on recent entries in the series. My recommendation is that if you already have 2, 3, and 4, this is the next one you should get.

_childDocuments_.review: We are now on the eighth iteration and seeing as how 7 was easily one of the best, this one had a lot to live up to.Drawful Animate has some good ideas – create a simple two-frame animation and pit it against a bunch of possible answers – but the underlying “animate” mechanic just falls flat. A lot of the time, the phrase given can be demonstrated in just one drawing, no animation required.That and a lot of the prompts are just boring or use super obscure language that even I needed to google to make sure I knew what I was drawing. It can be fun at times with the right group, but honestly, you’re probably better off just playing Gartic Phone, which has a much better animation game mode. This one just felt like Drawful with an unnecessary extra step – a waste of a game for a new Party Pack.You’re basically tasked with solving trivia and spinning a wheel in hopes that your score can get up to 20k. Problem here is that both the trivia and wheel spinning are just straight RNG. It does not even matter if you know the trivia or not, a lot of the time you can simply put in whatever answers and get enough points to spin the wheel and even if you are not spinning it yourself – another player is spinning it with the chance of getting you points.And once you do get to that 20k points, you’re given ANOTHER wheel to spin to determine the winner amongst ALL players with 20k points. The game is effectively RNG layered on top of more RNG and the trivia stuff feels underutilized as a result. It was really disappointing as a fan of trivia games and even though I do like myself some RNG, this one just doesn’t cut it.As if to balance out the two duds so far, Job Job comes out of nowhere and cements itself as not only the best game of the pack, but one of the best games in ANY Jackbox Party Pack. The game revolves around answering questions about a potential job and using other players’ own words to compose entirely new sentences. The result is often chaotic, deadpan, or just straight-up hilarious. Depending on the group, the prompts can bring out some really interesting answers to work with and the fact that you can pull words from the questions themselves is a cool bonus too.It’s simple concepts like these that Jackbox Party Packs really excel at and it’s perhaps the most accessible in the pack too, anybody can hop in and understand what to do without needing a big tutorial beforehand. It is for this game alone that I will likely keep the Party Pack installed for.This one is a step up in complexity, but it’s got a really neat concept. You play in teams and your goal is basically to guess the group consensus on certain questions and rank the different answers provided.The team focus adds this entire new layer to the gme, as you want to discuss with your team what the right answer may be, but doing so in a way that doesn’t give enough info away to the other team to use if your team gets it wrong – as the other team picks up right where you left off. It’s a neat tug-of-war concept that’s only aided by its absolutely absurd prompts, like “what is a smell you only want to sniff once and never again”. Easily the second-best game in the pack.On one hand, the concept is really neat. You have to draw “weapons” but must include a letter from your name so that when you kill a target, other players can attempt to deduce who the murderer was. On the other hand though, that is just one aspect of this game and there are a couple other layers that elevate it beyond the simplicity one would usually expect from a Party Pack title.In a way, this kinda defeats the spirit of the series, as it is not one you can just pop open during a party without expecting at least a few players to be confused and ruin the gameplay for the others. Once you get over that hurdle, it can be fun, but it takes a bit to get there and it doesn’t help that games last a long time. I’d place it as my third favorite in the pack, but I can’t say it’s one I’ll be returning to much.Party Pack 8 is a bit of a letdown following the release of the excellent Party Pack 7. The overall pack is less consistent, has only one real standout, and is perhaps the weakest in the series yet (I have played from 4 onwards). Job Job may have carried it a bit, but that is likely the only game in the pack that will be getting plays from my group in the future, even if Poll Mine and Weapons Drawn aren’t all that bad.Follow my  for more reviews + videos!

Jackbox, time to employ some different game designers for some new ideas.

_childDocuments_.review: The Jackbox Party Pack 8 is a comedic jackpot, a virtual amusement park of hilarity that'll turn your living room into a carnival of laughter. It's a treasure trove of mini-games that will create unforgettable moments during your game nights."Job Job" is a game where you'll have to think on your feet and craft absurd job applications for the weirdest professions. It's like a job fair in a parallel universe where the hiring managers have a great sense of humor, and your creativity is your strongest asset."The Poll Mine" is a quirky game of completing surveys and predicting your friends' answers. It's like entering a world where your friends' opinions are more entertaining than the questions themselves, and the revelations will leave you in stitches."The Wheel of Enormous Proportions" will put your knowledge and luck to the test. It's like a trivia game where the wheel of fate adds a wild twist to each question, and the unpredictability of the game will keep you on your toes."Drawful: Animate" takes the classic doodling game to the next level. You'll be creating animated drawings, and your friends will have to guess what's happening in your artistic masterpiece. It's like charades with animation, and the hilarity will reach new heights."Job Job" is a quirky game where you'll be drawing the most absurd inventions and pitching them to your friends. It's like Shark Tank meets an art class gone haywire, and the creativity will be off the charts.As with previous packs, all you need is a smartphone or tablet to join the fun, making it accessible for everyone. It's the ultimate level playing field where everyone can be a creative job applicant, a survey expert, a trivia master, an animator, and an inventive artist.The Jackbox Party Pack 8 will reveal just how inventive and zany your friends can be, which can be both hilarious and slightly alarming. You'll question your friendships, laugh uncontrollably, and wonder if you've stumbled upon a group of comedic prodigies.So, if you're ready for a night of creativity, quirky surveys, unpredictable trivia, animated doodles, and inventive pitches, The Jackbox Party Pack 8 is your golden ticket to comedic paradise. Rally your crew, embrace the absurdity, and get ready for an unforgettable evening of digital hilarity.

_childDocuments_.review: Growing up there was never a shortage of toilet paper. My family always stocked up like aspiring preppers on canned food and toilet paper. I had always assumed that a prepper sort of mentality was why my mother did it. Because we always had 300+ rolls of toilet paper at any given time. Well the years passed, I moved away, and Facebook became a thing. What a wonderful place to connect with friends and family to then hear too much about their lives... And my mother was no exception. The virus hit and everyone began panic buying things, especially toilet paper. My mother posts a status about how she was happy that there was no need to panic buy since she already had over 500 rolls thanks to her toilet paper fetish... I assumed that my mother, a very religious woman in her late 50's, didn't know the proper definition of the word "fetish" and was getting herself into an embarrassing mix-up. So I commented that I think she might be using the wrong word... And that's when she replied "DON'T KINK SHAME ME!" Sometimes it's better to just let things be and to not ask questions.Sometimes it's better to ask questions, like during this game. Jackbox 8 is a great social game to not play with family but with friends. Great conversations and a fun time for all involved, as long as they aren't related.

_childDocuments_.review: The games contained in the Jackbox suites (at least a lot of them) are 5-star hilarious fun and I do recommend the games themselves, but the suite's are a huge pain to navigate through. If I wanted to play Poll Mine, you have to A) know which pack of the 8 that game is a part of, start up that suite, wait for the super loud jackbox intro, then click to start, then select the game, then join and play instead of just being able to open the game directly. Then if you wanted to play a different Jackbox game, you have to, again, know which pack it's in and go through that whole process again. It's a major pain, it truly is. And the developers don't seem inclined to introduce any means of launching a game directly unless you pay $10-20 for each game individually. Out of the 8 suites of 5-6 games each, there's 10-12 of them that I enjoy playing. I wish I had just bought them individually instead of the packs at this point. I suggest watching the games being played on youtube and purchasing them as a one-off instead of these suites. The savings for the suite don't make up for having to go through and notate what packs have what games in a word doc that you always have to have with you.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is probably the best game to play with friends, in-person or on a voice call. Playing a new Drawful game took me way back to when I played Drawful 2 years ago with some friends and we had a blast. The wheel of enormous proportions is amazing, because you do have an advantage if you have trivia knowledge, but you still have a fighting chance if you don't. Job Job is just fun on the bun. It takes Quiplash's round structure and head to head competition, but adds it's own little flair to it. Poll mine is a fun one, but for an enjoyable experience, if you are going to livestream, play with friends over a voice/video call, instead of turning on streamer mode or letting people in as actual players. It's just a bit confusing without some sort of private chat to try and answer each question. Weapons Drawn is really fun as well, but it is extremely complex and I would NOT recommend it to someone who is new to Jackbox. _childDocuments_.review: I've been playing the Jackbox games since Pack 1. These packs are great. They are clever, fun, creative and the fact that we can hang out with family and just use our phones to play these games is intuitive. It's easy to set up and it's a blast. Party Pack 8 is not that fun. All the games on this pack are convoluted, complicated, and not simple at all. My family likes simple, easy to understand games. Trivia like Fibbage, opinion questions like Quiplash. These games are not that easy and really complicated.Back when I took Game Development class in college, my professor always said: "KISS, keep it simple, stupid". These games aren't that simple, and we find ourselves quitting during a game just to play an older pack. Here's my suggestions for future packs:1. KEEP THEM SIMPLE2. How about some word themed games? Boggle? Scrabble? Wordle? Give us something that involves scoring points to letters on a screen. 3. Stick to the formula that isn't broken. Give us variations of fibbage, quiplash, trivia murder party, etc that twist the rules a little bit. Be more innovative with the GAMES you already programmed. Make those more fun and exciting. 4. Keep it simple, please. If you are new to the party packs, go for Party Pack 2. That one was amazing and gives you Quiplash AND Fibbage. If you are a Jackbox Fan, I recommend watching gameplay of these games on twitch or youtube BEFORE considering purchasing the game. Thanks for reading my review!

_childDocuments_.review: The Jackbox Party Pack 8 is a pretty odd but great party pack. It offers some great games that you can play with your friends. This party pack is also the first pack to have the current UI that applies to Jackbox 8 and above along with more optimization features such as captions or automatically skipping tutorials. Some of the games include a sequel with a cool twist, a game about twisting other peoples words, trivia, etc. This review goes more into depth of each game.Drawful Animate: Drawful Animate (or Drawful 3) is basically a charades game where you draw a scenario and other people have to create a lie on the drawing and guess which one is the correct prompt. To summarize that, its basically Fibbage but with drawings. The twist with this game is that you can animate your drawings with 2 frames. I think this is a very fun twist to Drawful and makes it feel more fun to play including the fact that you can animate your own profile whenever you join a game of Drawful Animate. This game is pretty chill to play in general but has some flaws when it comes to playing it such as there being no redo button for your drawings which can cause a really big mess to your drawing. I do wish this game had more optimization when it came to drawing as it would be a relief without having the stress of messing up my drawing. Besides those problems, I do think this is a solid game where I would play it more than once or twice. The Wheel Of Enormous Proportions: The Wheel Of Enormous Proportions is a trivia game where everyone is competing in trivia questions in order to win the prize of a long desired question they have wanted. Everyone starts off with two slices and each question you get correct earns you more slices, including a final question that offers a power slice that gives the player who has it a lot of points once the power slice is landed on in the wheel. After the trivia, everyone takes a spin at the wheel to get either points for themselves or someone else OR a power slice. Once you get 20,000 points, you're able to spin the winner wheel. If it lands on your slice, you win the game. If it lands on a slice with a skeleton symbol on it, the game goes on. This required a lot of explanation but I feel like this game is both good but also does have a lot of flaws in the game as trivia with RNG can cause problems and in general I feel like this concept does not work out. I do LOVE the design and the host of this game but the RNG aspect of this game feels really tedious and in general is a game that feels like it could be at least somewhat reworked on. Trivia games can be fun as long as it is done right and a good example of that is something like Trivia Murder Party 2 from Jackbox 6. In general, I do think this game HAS potential and I feel like it can at least be somewhat fun but the RNG aspect can sometimes ruin that fun. Job Job: Job Job is a game where you and other people are in an 'interview" where you have to write sentences relating to the question and then mixing the words up to make a funny sentence. It is a little confusing on how to explain Job Job but playing is a BLAST. This is definitely one of the best games not only in this pack but in the entire Jackbox series. This has to be my favorite writing game because of the things that can just happen in this game. Not to mention the iconic style of this game including the host M. Bubbles which is an AMAZING host. This game also has a whole BUNCH of easter eggs from previous Jackbox games which makes this game a great experience. I don't really have much flaws with this game as me and my friends LOVE playing this game.  Definitely my favorite out of the 5.The Poll Mine: The Poll Mine is a game where you're split into 2 teams and the objective is to escape by answering 8 options to see if you get a correct door which earns you a torch or get it wrong which loses you a torch. This game isn't really in my interest and just seems really boring to me in general. It is a little confusing for me to understand and sometimes me and my friends get lost on what to even do in this game. I think this game had a lot of opportunity especially with how unique the design for this game is and the whole theme. Out of every game in this pack, I would say it is the most boring game in my opinion and could have been definitely been worked on to make it feel more interesting and actually fun to play. Weapons Drawn: This game will be the most complicated to explain. Weapons Drawn is a drawing game where you and 7 other people are both detectives and murderers. As a murderer, you draw two weapons which hides one letter of your name. Your objective is to hide this letter which will help you later on. Once everyone is done, everyone then makes an accomplice which is a mystery and should not be told to everyone. The accomplices are introduced and a minute later the lights go off. During that time, you are able to kill accomplices if you are able to guess who's accomplice it is. Now this is where the detective part comes in. Your objective as a detective is to figure out who killed the accomplice and if people guess the correct murderer, they earn points. At the end of the game, there are rewards for who did the best of each category which then shows the winner of the game. This game is really hard to explain and takes the longest amount of time to play. This game is really confusing but also is very fun to play especially when everyone accuses each other. I think the mix of a detective type game and a drawing game is a very interesting combo but it is confusing to understand until you play the game more or your further in the round. I would not recommend this game as a first pick when your playing the pack but it is a very fun game once you get the game and how it works. To conclude this review, this party pack is still one of my favorites and is recommended for you to play with friends if your new to Jackbox including Jackbox 7. I really do love this party pack as a whole with its style and everything and in general is a blast to play.

_childDocuments_.review: This party pack contains possibly one of the greatest jackbox games of all time, but definitely isn't as well rounded as some of the other party packs. Job Job is just incredible, and if you/your friend group don't mind just playing that one good game you like, this will probably be an amazing party pack. On the other hand, if you prefer more variety, you may be disappointed.Weapons Drawn just.... isn't that fun. Being a half drawing, half deception game sounds cool in theory, but the execution makes neither side of it feel particularly rewarding.Drawful Animate is... pretty much exactly what you'd expect. If you/your friend group like Drawful, you'll like this, and the twist definitely adds a lot. As someone who never really likes the drawing games, I can't give much more of a review than that, other than it hurts my eyes to see two vastly different images flashing back and forth sometimes.The Wheel of Enormous Proportions really didn't interest me or my friend group at all. Granted, the trivia based games have never really interested us, they seem more intended for a group who doesn't play a ton of games, but even compared to the other trivia games, it's mechanics sometimes seem kinda confusing and arbitrary.Lastly, Poll Mine, the biggest surprise of this pack for me. The strategy of trying to figure out what the order of rankings people gave without giving up too much information from you and the rest of your team is really interesting, and it makes this fun little semi-deception based game if you want it to be that. But it's also is just a fun little game about discussing silly topics that doesn't need to be taken seriously at all either. The Jackbox Party Pack 8 is quite good, and if it seems like you'd enjoy it, you probably would. Though it always can't hurt to look up some gameplay of the various games to see how they play out and if they look fun.

As a result, the bundle gets a thumbs up, but only just passable.

_childDocuments_.review: The best games on in this pack are JobJob and Drawful Animate. Both are inviting and easily hilarious without feeling forced. If the Wheel of Enormous Proportions The constraints on JobJob naturally brings out the fun of poor grammar and chopped up answers. It gives the players plenty of space to be clever without having to think that hard.  10/10Drawful Animate is taking Drawful to another level.  10/10My biggest disappointment is Wheel of Enormous Proportions. The trivia component of the games is better than Trivia Murder Party (if it was this alone, I'd give this game 10/10)- but the stupid wheel ruins what, otherwise would've been, an excellent game. Trivia players like to be rewarded for knowledge, but the completely random wheel takes away all feelings of control and completely sours the whole game. So overall, 5/10Poll Mine is best with more players and remote play. With fewer players, or players in the same room, it loses a lot its magic. After 1 or 2 plays, it gets boring and doesn't have the spark to keep the play interesting. Overall, it's ok 5/10.Weapons Drawn is a more complex of the Jackbox games. In every one of my play experiences, there will be at least 2 or more people who still don't get the rules even after the first play- this speaks to the rules explanation and complexity of the game for something designed to be light and should be easily picked up by even kids. 3/10

_childDocuments_.review: However, this is more of an 'additional' pack. I probably wouldn't recommend this as a first pack, but rather one to add variety if you already have a couple. Drawful is a great base to start from, and this is good because of it. I would struggle to say its better than Drawful though. Thankfullly it doesn't have to be better, and getting another flavor of drawful is welcome. If you have a drawing loving group this can be fantastic. Fantastic, it allows you to be creative and gives you something to be creative with. A very well designed game that is easily the stand out for many people, myself included. Its fun supplying your friends with words that they can take in unexpected directions. Not great in small groups. Just kinda alright overall. I wouldn't say its bad, but I keep forgetting it. Is quite fun, but also quite long. This one is experimental and fun but also can easily be a play once and don't return. I love the idea they had going here, but its doesn't have big staying power. Its a trivia game, and a welcome addition to the Jackbox collection. It does give you so many options it can be difficult but it also lets well versed players perform better as guessing isn't as good. Trivia games are great additions to Jackbox as you don't have to use the creative side of your brain which is a great change of pace or good if you are entertaining a group that isn't all that creative. Trivia Murder Party 2 (pack 6) is probably still better but something fresh is nice.

_childDocuments_.review: Talk about an entry I did not predict correctly, and I mean that in a good way.The resident trivia game, Wheel of Enormous Proportions, can be funny in how frustrating it is to see victory left partially to random chance, although it hasn't changed the usual line about how Jackbox's trivia games aren't for everyone.Drawful Animate is fine, but not quite as immediately pick-up-and-play as the original Drawful games.Weapons Drawn is strangely a game that feels complex while being played, but just going with the flow still resulted in fun times all round.The Poll Mine did run the risk of dragging on a bit, but it was still interesting to see the results of the answers, and I'd like to see more Jackbox games use teams of players in the future. But what makes this game is Job Job - the cursed gibberish-generating sleeper hit of the package. Many a guttural laugh was had at everything that my friends were able to cobble together from the various assorted ramblings we typed.

It's the team game that quickly reminds me with Family Feud, except all of us aren't family. 8/10- Weapons Drawn is also a bit complicated detective game, which honestly requires two or three times playing before I can get it. 7/10- Drawful Animate... nah, I'm not a good drawer. 5/10

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to talk about Drawful Animate, as that is the reason I bought this pack.It is just plain awful. The prompts either make no sense or are so specific that everyone can guess what the original prompt is. There is also a huge problem with American centric words being used all the time despite the fact I turned the American stuff off in the menu. As many of you know, once you get a word like gas (instead of petrol) or diaper (instead of nappy) in the prompt, everyone will know that was the official one because we don't use those words. When it happens, its easy points for the person who got it, but also feels like a waste of time for the person drawing because you know the other players will get it no matter what. Really, really lazy work on the developers here.Some spoilers I guess, to show how bad the prompts are."Welcome holiday horse in2 your home" What?"Medical grade egg nog" American word so it was easily guessed."My cat just got veneers" Veneers are an American thing again."Decorative gasoline wedding fountain". American word, easily guessed."Goblin wearing a diaper" American word, easily guessed."Lightning bug changing a light bulb" Lightning bugs are an American thing, so this answer was easily guessed.There was also prompts with dreidels and menorah, which none of us knew anything about so those drawings went well.This was all from only 2 games as well, so roughly 1/3 of the game was a failure to us.
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Party Pack 8

_childDocuments_.review: While I personally love all the games in this pack, they're all an acquired taste more than an instant love.Drawful Animate is a fun time that everyone I've played with enjoys, but it's purposefully clunky drawing portion means that you end up playing this one entirely for the absurdity of it, rather than to try and make detailed abominations. The Wheel of Enormous Proportions is a toss-up between players: either you think it's one of the best trivia games so for, or you hate the RNG of it with a passion. It's bullsh*t, but the bullsh*t is where most of the fun is. This game is what I'd call the "dust collector" of the pack just because of how divided opinions on it are.Job Job tends to be most peoples favorite, but it requires everyone to be funny in order for it to work. It also has the Talking Points issue of where it fundamentally doesn't work as a competitive game, but is incredibly fun to play casually. Whether or not you enjoy this one depends on the group you're playing with.Poll Mine is an interesting idea with various ways of playing it (the best IMO being everyone in a room, but not physically split into teams). Great for a competitive/cooperative showdown, but could easily wear out unless you really enjoy the game play of it.Weapons Drawn is probably my favorite Jackbox game of all time, but it's also the black sheep of the pack (and arguably, of all the packs). It's the most complicated jackbox game by far, and requires a good knowledge on what to do in order to fully be able to enjoy it. It feels less like a "jackbox game", and more like a full social deduction/strategy game. The issue there is that if your just casually going through the pack, a high-strategy and deduction game isn't really gonn be what you're looking for. Weapons Drawn is a game that takes time to learn, time that other jackbox games don't ask of you. Overall: not as good of a pack as 7 (which was basically the perfect pack), and definitely not the best starter pack (that would be #3), but still one worthy of being picked up if any of the games seem appealing to you. You'll either love 'em or hate 'em.

_childDocuments_.review: Part 8 of 8 for my review of every Jackbox Party Pack that has been released on Steam as of August 19th, 2022.Jackbox Party Pack 8, It is a lot of fun all things considered, a really strong pack that has been released.Drawful Animate, just like Drawful from JPP1 you are drawing something, and as the name would suggest it is animated, so it is a lot more fun to guess what the prompt is (Min 3, Max 10, Suggested 10)Job Job, Probably the weakest title in this pack, You are making mostly funny answers to job interview questions, its just like quiplash. (Min 3, Max 10, Suggested any amount)The Poll Mine. Everyone in the game gets surveyed about their preferences, then split into 2 teams and trying to figure out what took what slot, it is a lot of fun and encourages paying attention to the other side. (Min 2, Max 10, Suggested 4 or more in even intervals)Weapons Drawn, Another art game, but this one is very different from Drawful, your goal is to murder other peoples guests at a dinner party, and hide your murder weapon, but the catch is that somewhere in your murder weapon is a letter of your name. So like my user name "Snivy Films" I would have to hide an "i" in my weapon somewhere. It is a lot of fun, but it takes a while to get through. (Min 4, Max 8, Suggested any amount)The Wheel of Enormous Proportions, Its trivia. It is a lot of fun, and at the end of the game who ever is winning gets to have their question answered by the wheel. I would rank this higher than You Dont Know Jack but under Trivia Murder Party, but fun all around. (Min 2 Max 8, Suggested any amount)Jackbox Party Pack 8 is a pretty good pack over all, a lot of fun to be had, it is worth it at this price.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall concensus: Probably one of the better packs. Cap was raised to 10 players, 2 of the games are BANGERS, 2 are playable, only 1 is completely godawfulDrawful Animate: Pass, just play another Drawful if you have it. Rarely, if ever, does a 2 frame animation allow more expression than just a single image. Call us a bunch of uncreative idiots, but no one ever did anything animated and just redrew the first frame again, making it double the effort (and time) for every round with no payoff. And Drawful still has really basic drawing controls compared to other drawing games from previous packs like Champ'd Up and TKO.Wheel of Enormous Proportions: Pass. Slightly more trivia and significantly less getting uncontrollably screwed over compared to Murder Trivia Party, but that's not saying much. Yet I would still rather play Trivia Murder Party, because the trivia in Wheel is mostly selecting the answers from lists ("select every member of Monty Python" or "every form of poetry"), and lists are pretty lame because barely will you know every answer and are barely penalized for getting wrong answers. Plus the minigames in Murder Party are a lot more engaging, quick, and have a chance for frantic collaborating with your group, while Wheel is just... spinning a completely random wheel with no input from the audience, so sometimes Wheel can feel *more* random and inconsequential than Murder Party.Weapons Drawn: PASS. For one, it's just so LONG, I think the only game we played took a half hour, while most other games in this pack don't pass the ten minute mark per game. Well, it felt like a half hour to us. So it's an extra long commitment, and... well, the concept isn't bad, but it's just so easy to cheese. People can choose to ignore the drawing prompt and hide their clue in a sea of scribbles, and there's no actual way to punish them, and in fact they get rewarded for this because you can't deduce who made the drawing. And even if you have a group of friends who decide to follow the prompts and not be ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, the point system is really scattered, and nobody was ever certain they were winning or in dead last until the very end of the game. It's a social deduction game where it's too easy to not follow the rules and win, and a win felt random and undeserved. Also the drawing system is still extremely limited, and the magnifying glass during the investigation phase controls like the X button in a popup advertisement. Horrendous.Job Job: A must have. Every game has been a riot, and the prompts are all solid with no "how the hell am I supposed to answer this?" questions like in Quiplash. Probably a top 5 Jackbox game for everyone I've played it with, maybe even our #1.Poll Mine: Ranges from the most fun you'll have, to mid at best. Some polls I swear we were seconds away from drawing blood and spent the entire debate time shouting, because a team member chaotically admits to putting a stupid answer as the #1 on their poll, completely throwing out the presumed ranking and potentially spiraling your team out of control. A fantastic time. Other times the prompt is just so awful you are unenthusiastically forced to guess your way out, which leads to a lot of wrong answers and a lot of "sure, I don't really care, we all just put random stuff down so who would have guessed?" from the whole group. And I swear, every time I have introduced a new person to this game, one of the prompts is something like "Rank all players in this current game on who is most likely to ______" which is just awkward because they're excluded from inside jokes and never picked. The bad games are bad, but the good games are SO GOOD. If this game had a way to select what prompts are played each round, this game would be #1 GOAT Jackbox game. And having players voting for the top option isn't even a wild suggestion, THE WHOLE GAME IS ABOUT CHOOSING YOUR TOP OPTION FROM A LIST.

_childDocuments_.review: My friends and I love all the Jackbox games, this one being no exception, but this one does have some problems worth mentioning that stuck out to us right away that I feel like should be mentioned.Pole Mine is a fun game in concept but without a lot of players and/or an audience the end results end up skewed and sometimes feel entirely wrong. Weapons Drawn is your fun murder mystery of the pack, with one key flaw that can make the game very difficult to play. This one can be entirely derailed if your players only draw letters and scribbles to hide the letter. By doing this it can be very difficult to play.Job Job is just plain fun, end of story. If you loved games Blather Around and Quiplash, this game is the prodigy child of the two and I couldn't love a game more. My only problem with it is that you are able to click on your name to add it to the answer, but it doesn't let you choose an individual word from your name, instead the entire name gets put in. I went into Drawful Animate expecting it to be the worst one, no questions asked. It is only another remade game with barely any change right? Wrong, so very wrong. By simply adding a second frame to give your drawing life, it changes the entire game, making it an incredibly fun game to play. They even added shortened words and slang to make it harder to guess which one was written by the game. My only complaint with this one is that you can't put down the same answer as another player. If you do it gives you a prompt telling you it is too close to either the answer or what another person wrote. One of my favorite things in these kinds of games are the end of round screen coming up and seeing two people wrote the same obscure lie, so it is really sad that it is no longer a thing.Last and most certainly least is The Wheel of Enormous Proportions. Jackbox has always been king when it came down to trivia games. For example, the Trivia Murder Parties. With TMP, you got both real and the occasional goofy trivia question with a fun penalty game to do if you got it wrong, all with the theme of a murder hotel. Wheel of Enormous Proportions is not that, not clever, not too funny, not well themed, not fun. You are given select all that apply questions that give you the ability to put your name on the wheel. As of now I have no plans of returning to the Wheel, but to my knowledge there isn't any mini-games or special quirks either. After putting your name on the Wheel at certain tiles you have people spin arbitrarily for random amounts of points, then rinse and repeat until someone wins with a certain amount. When you win, you get your question put against the Jackbox team's version of a larger word count magic 8 ball. Without a doubt in my mind this game is the least fun of the pack and its lack of fun gimmicks or any good mechanics make it easier to decide what to play when the list of games is whittled down by one.While these complaints exist, they are currently the only real complaints I have. This pack is nowhere near being the best pack but is far from the worst. Worth the money spent and I will be playing again (except for Wheel of Enormous Proportions, all my homies hate Wheel of Enormous Proportions).

Animation is fun in my opinion, and I find it more fun than original drawful just because the simple animations.Job, Job: Great game when you play it with people who get it. Even the dumbest ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ can become great with the right Frankenstein of words.Wheel of Enormous Proportions: I think the complaints about this game just come from people who don't like trivia lol. I actually really enjoyed the different format for some questions where you can get partial credit. There is a luck aspect to winning, so if you get upset that your superior trivia knowledge didn't save you, I guess you also might not like it. Poll Mine: It's cute. _childDocuments_.review: Great addition to the Jackbox collection.Drawful Animate: A wonderful followup to Drawful 2. The animating is easy and fun. I like how the prompt writing style has changed, so the correct answers blend in better with your friends' silly guesses. But... why is there STILL no undo button? How come Patently Stupid and Champed Up have an undo button, but still not Drawful? Job Job: Decently fun. You have to answer job interview questions, but you can only use words that another player wrote. It can get hilarious. It works better if you have very silly friends who write long, silly answers for the beginning prompt.Poll Mine: I haven't played this one very much because it's not popular with my friend group. Everyone on your team makes their own tier list for a certain category, and then the answers are averaged out. You need to work with your team to figure out what landed as number ten, number nine, etc. It can be very frustrating and sometimes doesn't make much sense. If everyone picked an item to be their number four, why is it NOT number four?Weapons Drawn: I don't like this one very much. You need to hide a letter from your name in a drawing of a "weapon." Then the other players look at the drawing, try to find the letter, and guess whose name it came from. The problem is that it aaaall hinges on players' names. If one of your friends names themselves "AEIOU," it's going to be hard to guess the murderer even if you find the letter.Wheel of Enormous Proportions: A new take on a trivia game. My friends who dislike Trivia Murder Party and You Don't Know Jack looove this game. It's a lot easier to guess right answers (you can often pick multiple options). There's also a randomness element to winning (spinning the wheel and getting points), which means that you can know none of the answers but still potentially win. Up to you if this sounds like a pro or a con.

Weapons Drawn seems to have a pretty steep learning curve, however. Overall, a good pack to have.

_childDocuments_.review: Gamers and animation geeks will like Drawful Animate which has you trace animations and other players guess them. However, as a total non-gamer, I like games with elements of trivia and luck like Wheel of Enormous Proportions & Poll Mine best. In Wheel oEP you answer trivia by picking all the possible right answers, so you can guess if you don't know something, then depending on the better you do you'll get more pegs to add to the wheel which you can earn points (its kind of like the Press Your Luck gameshow now that I think of it). The other winner for me is Poll Mine, which 2 teams of 1 or more work with other teammates to decide the most popular answer from what you all just selected. It is more fun with larger groups than small, but I've enjoyed it every time. I enjoy the hokey graphics and basic games best... when they get too complicated (like Weapons Drawn, which nobody seems to understand who has played it with me) it loses me as a party game. This is my favorite edition since Jackbox 3 which had my previous fav games of Guesspionage & Trivia Murder Party. I get that Quiplash is the most popular game Jackbox has made since there is 3 of them already (and don't get me wrong I like that game fine), but these other games that are less about coming up with written in answers is easier to play with a wider range of people. So, thanks for including both types of games in every pack.

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic Party Pack that meshes really well with my friend group. Even the trivia game has been able to get laughter from my ESL friends, and that's a pretty high bar to hit.Drawful is funny for the artistically creative, but is still overshadowed by TKO or Champ'd Up, but it's almost unfair to compare it with these two, as they are absolutely amazing and some of my favorite Jackbox game ever.The Wheel is a great trivia game, where some questions will have you scratch your head in confusion or laughter, and then spinning the wheel is a nailbiter when anyone could benefit from your spin, even your WORST enemy! DAMNIT ALEX!Job Job is a fantastic twist on Quiplash that helps people who are less apt in creative writing and joke-spinning by letting them use words that are already selected for them by other players who might be better writers or jokers. This gives everyone a fair chance to write stupid jokes and gets some amazing laughs. Fantastic.The Poll Mine is how you lose friendship or question those two weird people in your friend group who go against the grain. Simply enough, you split all the players in two teams before the start, and then the game throws you prompts that requires you to select certain options in order of Best to Worst. It sends that poll to every player. Then it asks you, which ones are the best? Which one is the worst? Which ones are in the middle? And it lets players debate and argue which is which. Then you realise some of your friends really like licking pool cues, and they messed the entire order you thought would be normal. Great laughs, lose some friends. Make more.The Murder Art game is the sleeper of this one. One I thought would be more of a gimmick or that most people wouldn't want to sit down and play has been one of the best gem in this pack. Every player is a detective and a murderer - and one of the letter in their name HAS to be in every murder weapon drawing. They then need to dissimulate  or lead astray other players so as to not be identified. Pair that up with every player giving names to the potential victims and you get plenty of laughs and frustration as you realize who dun it and who dun get it! Fantastic.It's an amazing party back, just, amazing. Well worth the asking price!

_childDocuments_.review: I will start with my general opinion of the pack and then do a short review of each game within the pack.This is probably one of the best JPP games if not the best so far. My friends and I are still a bit unsure about "Weapons Drawn", but all the others are really enjoyable. And even "Weapons Drawn" still has a good idea behind it, it's just a lot more convoluted for newer players, so we'll be giving it a bit more of a shot in the future but even the only game we don't love, we can still see that it has potential. If you've played Drawful before, you probably have a good idea what to expect here. You basically draw the basic drawing and follow it with a separate frame. I think it could benefit from other gamemodes, perhaps things like "3 frames" gamemodes and whatnot. But it's good fun. This is a pretty weird one. You have to answer very random questions, then use the words everyone in the group have used for those answers to make up your answer for the next questions, it can make for some pretty funny answers. This is really just a trivia game but in teams. It can be pretty chaotic when people are opinionated but that's what makes it funny. I wouldn't suggest this one unless you have at least 6 players, though. It's surprisingly entertaining, though. As I stated previously; this game is quite convoluted and takes a lot of learning to understand it. But it definitely has potential, and it has multiple steps that can be pretty funny. But it feels a bit weird and will often end up with people trying to speak over each other to make their points/trying to fool others. It's a bit messier than the other games in the pack but I could definitely see this going somewhere in the future. This was probably the biggest surprise. Pretty much none of us in my friend group are into gambling/RNG. So going into a "Spin the Wheel" type of game, we didn't expect too much. But this is essentially just a big trivia game with some pretty chaotic aspects. I think this turned out to be the best-made one in the pack. : Each game is at the very least "Decent". If you like JPP games normally, it shouldn't be any different this time around.If people like ratings, my overall rating for this one would be around 8.5 or 9/10
