_childDocuments_.review: As far as the party packs go, pack 8 is solid. It certainly has its hits and misses, but overall I think it's a great addition to the series and worth buying if you like these sorts of party games! Below are my thoughts so far on the individual games:~Drawful Animate~-Hit or Miss: Hit!If you don't like drawing games, this will be a miss, but surprisingly I think it's the best Drawful game so far. I've never been too into the other Drawful games compared to some of Jackbox's other drawing games (Tee-KO, Champ'd Up, Bidiots) and I figured this one would be a more tedious version of the other two because of the animation component. Surprisingly, the two-frame animation doesn't feel tedious and the ability to have two frames makes drawing the weird prompts feel more manageable and more fun! Plus, as more accurate drawings often lead to more accurate false responses, it's often more challenging to guess the prompt. Overall, while it isn't may favourite drawing game, I think it makes Drawful more fun and more worth throwing in during games night!~Wheel of Enormous Proportions~-Hit or Miss: MissI've never been huge a fan of most of Jackbox's trivia games (although I've had fun with Lie Swatter and Trivia Murder Party) but I don't really feel this game adds much to a trivia game formula except for more randomness to who wins. The questions are reasonable but the game has a lot of uncomfortable dialogue with the wheel and weird lottery system to choose a winner which to me feel random and unnecessary. The "asking a question to the wheel" gimmick is kinda neat, but feels like a tacked-on gimmick rather than an important part of the game. Overall it's a fine trivia game, but besides gimmicks that just add time between answering questions, I don't think it adds anything particularly meaningful that makes it more worth playing than Jackbox's better trivia games.~The Poll Mine~Hit or Miss: Hit?This game can be quite a bit of fun with a good, larger group, but its point system is a bit odd and it's better in person than online. I think it's worth trying out to see whether or not it vibes well with your group, but it definitely feels most like a "worth playing every once in a few times" game rather than a big hit. That said, it's still good, but I'm not quite sure how to place it.~Job Job~Hit or Miss: Hit!!!This is easily the best game in the pack in my opinion. It's easy to pick up, fun, quirky and not too serious. Of all the games here, it seems like the easiest to play multiple rounds of in succession like a Quiplash, Fibbage or Survive the Internet. Definitely worth a try!~Weapons Drawn~Hit or Miss: HitOf all games in this pack, this is the longest and most complicated. It has the potential to be a lot of fun, but you need people who are willing to take the effort to get into it. Because of its drawing components, it also may not be a hit with everyone. That said, it is a solid murder mystery game best played with people who know each other. There is lots of room for creativity with the weapons, difficult sleuthing with the weapons, and social, bluffing aspects. Importantly, each part of the game feels important to the overall experience. Overall, this game is fun and well-put together, but requires the right group to be enjoyed to its fullest.

_childDocuments_.review: I think this might be the best pack for streaming. Each of the five games is so wildly different from the other and has a completely different form of fun. Drawful Animate is a tried and true classic that has been updated to be better than ever. Job Job is remarkably quick witted at times, and senseless fun at others. Poll Mine is an interesting team building exercise with the option to have everyone work to battle the audience. The Wheel Of Enormous Proportions is a Mario Party like trivia game with some of the tensest final rounds I've played in party games. Then there's Weapons Drawn, a very slow paced thinking game where everyone essentially designs puzzles and atempts to solve one another's before their own is solved.

Still, I think it's a worthy addition and if you have people craving for more Jackbox, they won't be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: OVERALLI have boxes 4-8 and can't recommend this pack. Job Job is the only game in it that my friends and I really enjoyed, and I certainly wouldn't buy the whole pack just for that one game.JOB JOBEasily the best game of the pack and probably the only one really worth playing. It allows for a lot of creativity so you can get some crazy and funny responses.WHEEL OF ENORMOUS PROPORTIONSThis game has interesting trivia questions and the select-multiple-answers style distinguishes it from other trivia games. However, you spend half of the game just watching the wheel spin, which is slow and boring. And there is way too much randomness in who wins, so winning doesn't feel meaningful. In fact, it seems like being in the lead early actually puts you at a disadvantage due to the rules and spinning mechanics.POLL MINEThis was my least favorite of the pack. It was boring and came down to random guessing over and over. The concept sounds fun and I think it would work better with fewer doors. But our prompt was to guess 8 answers in order of least popular to most popular and it was just a guessing game for 10 minutes.DRAWFUL: ANIMATEThis game is alright but if you already have the normal Drawful from another pack then you don't need it. The animating doesn't really add anything. You just draw two pictures now instead of one.WEAPONS DRAWNAgain, the concept was interesting, but it just didn't really resonate with us. We played one round then went back to playing something else.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't find myself writing reviews for games very often... but I just had to state that this may be in strong contention as the BEST Jackbox Party Pack to date. I own 3-6 + 8, though I have played 7 and the first two games in the series. Every game is incredibly fun, and there isn't an odd man out like most of the others. Most of the packs include 3 solid party games, 1 average game, and 1 "dud" that either isn't as fun, has a poor mechanic, or is just not something my group would ever like to play, but in JBPP 8 I found fun in all five games almost equally - putting it in my favorites list along 3 + 5.
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Party Pack 8

_childDocuments_.review: Overall: Probably the best pack since 3, all of the games in it are solid and there's a really good range of game types.  I would highly recommend this one if you are just looking to purchase a single pack.Weapons Drawn: A really clever combination of Social Deduction and Art games, where you have to hide a provided letter in multiple drawings and try and figure out the letters of other players to catch them in murders.  Definitely the most complicated of the pack, but fun once you learn it.  This one could use some balancing, though:  I had a game with the letter N, which is really diverse in all of the forms the game lets you use (lowercase vs. uppercase, cursive vs. normal).  I was carried really hard by my letter and no one guessed me for any murder.  Maybe if we could use shapes instead (or a smaller letter pool), that may balance the game more effectively.Poll Mine: Probably better for streamers who can get a huge range of answers from their chat, but still really fun with a small group!  You get into teams and try to determine the top answers for a given question.  The team aspect is really interesting since you have to be careful what all you tell your team, at the risk of the other team getting valuable clues for their turn.Drawful Animate: Basically Drawful 3, and Drawful was already one of the top Jackbox games.  The animation part doesn't completely change the game; it just adds new options to the original gameplay, which is nice.  The game's prompts really surprised us, since they're much more natural (ex. mispellings, bad grammar, abbreviations).  I kinda wish there was an option to turn mispellings off, but it's not a bad thing and makes the game a lot more interesting in some cases (and gives people a chance if they accidentally misspell something). The Wheel of Enormous Proportions:  A really chill trivia game, and a great way to start a Jackbox session with friends.  The questions can be pretty tough and interesting, and the wheel provides a good amount of luck for those who can't seem to get the questions right (aka me).  This one probably has the best art and vibes, a really good calm game to play.Job Job:  The standout title of this pack, it's a blast.  You have to answer random questions, then take the words from everyone's responses and use them to answer job interview questions.  The potential for people's answers is huge, and my friend group was laughing like crazy at the sentences we could create.  It's a pretty simple idea, but it goes a long way without any extra gimmicks needed.

_childDocuments_.review: Jackbox 8. My my my. There are quite a lot of good games to be found here, but I do still think that it's probably a step down from the last pack (although to be fair, pack 7 was damn near perfect, and whatever followed it was unlikely to be able to compare to it). Compared to all the packs, I would rank them as follows: 1<2<3<6<5<8<4<7.Looking at the individual games, we have Job Job, the funny game in the pack, Weapons Drawn, the unique drawing game in the pack which was mixed with some social deduction, Wheel of Enormous Proportions, the trivia game of the pack, Drawful 2, the remake game of the pack mixed with drawing, and Poll Mine, the unique game of the pack. I will give each of these games their own individual mini-reviews, as well as score them out of 10 rather than 5, because I'm feeling a bit like Fantano.Drawful Animate: This game is kind of a dud if I'm being honest, which is weird because it shouldn't be; it's a remake. Drawful Animate is basically Drawful, but you are allowed to draw one extra frame, to make your pictures "animated" (you probably could've guessed that lmao). This game blows, because there are already better versions of this game that exist. If you like the long slow and tedious task of animating drawings, play Gartic Phone. It's free and it's online, so you can play that with your friends. And if you enjoy the fast-paced gameplay of Drawful, just buy Drawful 2. It's relatively cheap, and maybe a few of you guys might already own it, as it was given out for free last year. This game is outclassed by other existing games, and because of that, it's not a super memorable game to play, compared to those other party games. For that, I would give it a 3/10.Wheel of Enormous Proportions: The trivia game of the pack. This game works pretty well as a trivia game, as the questions perfectly balance on the line of being not well known enough to be easy, but not obscure enough to be hard. However, the trivia is not the point of the game. The trivia serves as a way to score points on the wheel. The wheel is admittedly kind of divisive. I personally enjoy rng-based gameplay, so it's something that I personally enjoy, however, if you are a person who wants to win after getting the most points out of everyone, do note that this is not guaranteed, and you're probably better off playing You Don't Know Jack or Trivia Murder Party 1 or 2 off of the other packs. Overall, from my personal party, we would probably rate it a 8/10, but if you personally don't like rng, it's probably not going to be any higher than a 5/10 for you.Job Job: This game is proof that broken english is funny. Basically, all you do is answer weird interview questions, then use other people's responses to answer other questions. It's basically quiplash but the words are not your own. Now I know that me describing it makes it sound very frustrating, but you're gonna have to trust me on this. This game is objectively one of the most fun games off of the pack. 9.5/10Poll Mine: This game is basically Family Feud. It's a fun game, but if I'm being totally honest, my friends and I didn't get much out of this game. I think that maybe if it's played with a large audience and a lot of people, then you might be able to get the feeling that people were actually interviewed, and were polled. But with only 5 people, it's pretty easy to just gang up as a team, and tell everyone to pick the same option for number one, which can lead to it being shockingly easy to guess which is what. I think this game could be an 8/10 with an audience, but as it is with only 5 people, it's a 4/10 for me.Weapons Drawn: Man, people really don't like this game huh. I understand where their criticism is coming from, as there are quite a lot of unnecessary elements in this game, that are pretty much detrimental to understanding the game. That being said, my party of 5 actually did understand what was going on here, and because of that, we were able to have a lot of fun with this. The accomplice system can lead to some funnies, because you can name you accomplice whatever you want them to be, meaning that you can name your accomplice John F. Kennedy, then someone will assassinate him. But I think the biggest flaw is that the letters that are meant to serve as clues can very easily be scribbled over, making it shockingly impossible to guess who the murderer is. This game is very fun, if you know what you're doing, but explaining it to people who don't is probably going to be a challenge (which is why I abstained from doing so lmao). As it is though, I think this game is a 7/10.Overall, averaging out the scores, this pack would be a 6.5/10 from my party, or a 5.9/10 if you're a third party. It's worth the buy, but do note that there are a few experimental games here that you may or may not like.
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Party Pack 8

_childDocuments_.review: This is the slowest party pack for sure! As more and more games are created, simplicity is becoming a thing of the past. With games like Weapons Drawn and Wheel of Enormous Proportions taking a hot second to get the hang of, Poll Mine being simple but still long and even Job Job and Drawful animate being longer versions or other similar games. Despite this I think Party Pack 8 provides great games! Job Job is a Jam Jam, Drawful is better than ever! Weapons takes a round to figure out, but it's great. A great Pack, not quite as good as 7 but still great
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Party Pack 8

_childDocuments_.review: I like to do first impression reviews of new Jackbox packs, so here goes.Drawful Animate: Based on one game, I'd say it's the weakest in the pack. The animation factor doesn't really add that much, so it's still a very basic drawing guessing game. The prompts are also very obscure and can lead to multiple people guessing very similar things. Pretty mediocre game, especially compared to Champ'd Up from the last pack which knocked it out of the park.The Wheel of Enormous Proportions: I love a good trivia game (Trivia Murder Party 2 is my all-time favourite Jackbox game), but sadly this isn't it. The trivia itself is solid and includes some different formats of question which is cool, and the overall presentation is really enjoyable. Unfortunately, the game itself ends up being more about luck than general knowledge, so you can feel cheated by the RNG gods.Job Job: Now we're getting into the good stuff. This is definitely one of the best Jackbox games yet and arguably the one that generates the most laughs. It's hard to fault it, really!The Poll Mine: Right up there with Job Job in my opinion. The teamwork aspect is great and probably works better than in any previous team-based Jackbox game. I also like that it's based on the opinions of your fellow players rather than random surveys which allows you to gauge your choices based on your knowledge of your friends (and sometimes makes you despair at their choices).Weapons Drawn: I think of all the games in this pack, this is the one I like the most conceptually. The idea of trying to conceal a letter within your art is great, then the deception and deduction added on top is fantastic. In my opinion, though, the game itself doesn't quite live up to the expectations the concept creates. Once you know who has what letter, it's too easy to figure out who each killer is, especially if the artist has a distinctive style. On top of that, the cold cases can make the game drag towards the end.Overall, I'd say 8 is a step down from 7, which itself was a step down from 6 (the best pack in my opinion). The only games I can see becoming staples for my group are Job Job and Poll Mine. Drawful Animate especially seems like a game someone would want to play once, then abandon it in favour of better drawing games like Champ'd Up and Tee K.O.Still recommended, though!
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Party Pack 8

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game the day it came out, and wow. Wow wow wow. I had a LOT of fun playing it with my friends (Group of 6). I'll try and write a summary of each game and how much I enjoyed it.Drawful Animate: Same ideas as past drawfuls, you just draw two frames this time. You can adjust the speed it flashes between the two, as well as having an onion skin available so you can see the previous frame.Personal thoughts: I enjoyed it, as did my friends. I will say though that this is, imo, one of the weaker games, as its essentially the same as the last two drawfuls. However, it's not bad, although I did find the prompts to be a bit specific and a tad bit harder to draw (then again, thats part of the fun, lol.)Wheel of Enormous Proportions: What's a jackbox game without the trivia? Unlike past trivia games, there is more than one correct answer, and the more correct ones you click out of the dozen or so options, the more "slices" you get, that you then place on a wheel and spin for points.Thoughts: I enjoyed it, but it wasn't everyone in my party's cup of tea. It is very RNG based, which led to someone who only got a handful of questions right end up winning anyways, while other people were getting more answers correct. I did love the quirky style of it though, and the whole "answering the burning question" for the winner at the end. Once again, not everyone's thing, but I did enjoy it.Job Job: You write down answers to word prompts, and everyone else gets your sentences and has to scramble them up to get new sentences.Thoughts: Probably my favorite game out of the pack so far. My friends and I laughed our asses off the whole time over our dumb prompts. I also think it's cool how you can use any words on your screen and not just the sentences. Definitely one of the stronger ones out of the pack.Poll Mine: Rate a group of objects, and guess what the most popular/least popular is (depending on the round)Thoughts: I love the characters you get to choose from, and the game itself is also pretty entertaining. My friends and I enjoyed going against each other as teams and talking it out. All in all solid.Weapons Drawn: I have played this one yet ;-; I'll update my review when I do it.All in all, very good party pack, definitely worth the money if you've got a group of buddies to do it with.
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Party Pack 8

_childDocuments_.review: I've quite a bit of every game now and I can say this is a pretty solid pack! Usually there's two games that don't really click that well with my group but we played through each game multiple times and we had plenty of laughs so far in our four hours of gameplay.Drawful Animate: 3/5This is an average one to me personally but my group had a total blast with this. Who knew the animations could create such funny and tear inducing moments - this is our go too when we kind of just want to mess around with each other.The Wheel of Enormous Proportions: 4/5My group isn't much into trivia and the murder mysteries in the past jack box games never really stuck with us. We would play them, but they were nowhere near our favorite. This one however has been a huge hit with my group - everyone is always wanting to play this one every few rounds of other games. It has a fun little tidbit where it asks you to ask a question that you have been wanting to know the answer to and if you win you get your question answered. This has led to some very hilarious moments and lots of laughs.Job Job: 5/5This is probably the best game in the pack. You answer questions (really try to fill them out the best you can, every word helps!) and players then have to use your words to formulate a new sentence. This can get really funny and can create some very interesting sentences. "I destroy God" was one of my players 'perks for the job and it was tear-inducing.Poll Mine: 4/5Poll mine is so fun, a nice change of pace out of all the other games. In this one you have to rank different options and then determine what people picked for #1, #2, #3 -- this really creates an interesting dynamic as you're trying to figure out what your party would want in their guest bathroom or what they think may be the most needed items to bring on a plane with them.Weapons Drawn: 2/5I've only played this one once so far and this is probably our least favorite. In this game you have to hide a letter from your name in your murder weapons while at the same time trying to solve the murders of the other players. It is very complicated at least on our first playthrough and it took quite a bit of time too. I'm sure it will grow on us as most of these games do but from a first impression it was definitely the biggest let down because it was the game we were the most excited for.
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Party Pack 8

_childDocuments_.review: Recommend yes BUT as with all jackbox it really depends on your group. Some games are great some are... not good almost at all. Also 2 drawing games.Drawful Animate 4/5 - Its drawful! But also harder. The prompts seem anywhere from absolute nonsense to "I can't believe it was actually that simple." If you like drawing games or drawful definite win. 4/5 because prompts can be a little off, and making animations that are clear is much harder for some people than a single drawing.Wheel 2/5 - Ehhhhh. Mixed on this one. The trivia is interesting enough (until you get 5 obscure celebrity questions in a row). But then you just waste a bunch of time on the wheel spinning to actually get the points to win. And winning reaaally doesn't matter in this game cause its 90% RNG but it still feels flawed. 2/5 because the trivia can be fun and get the group discussing/laughing.Job Job 4.5/5 - My favorite game in the pack, but also very group dependent. Word of advice is definitely to exaggerate your word choice so other people can make really silly prompts. The sillier and more adaptable your group the better. Solid game no doubt. 4.5/5 with good icebreaker responsesPoll Mine 1/5 - This one is either decent, or absolutely awful depending on your prompts. Its a game that kinda plays into group psychology of what you think everyone else ranked the answers, and it is fun deducing that and working on that with your team. But when you get prompts about country songs or ludicrous weapons to bring into a castle, ALL of that psychology goes down the drain and everyone just gets frustrated answering questions wrong over and over. Very weird, not good game IMO. 1/5 Play it once or twice and move on probably.Weapons Drawn 4/5 - Social deduction drawing game. A bit of a more serious game as you try to hide a letter from your name in all of your drawings. You also try to match accomplices to the players, and is overall a good time as you try your best to be sneaky with your drawings and accomplices. It just feels good to play even if you don't win or get a lot of laughs out of it. 4/5 because cleverly hiding drawings and figuring it out feels greatOverall decent pack, but there's definitely a mixed bag of good and bad in here.

_childDocuments_.review: The newest Jackbox Party Pack is bound to bring a fun time to any gathering. If you've played any games from any of the other party packs, then you'll know that your phone/pc is the controller, and that only the host needs the game. The games in this pack range from okay to really good. But what games end up as the fan favorite of your gathering depends on who you're playing with. However, there have been two quality of life changes that are worth noting in my opinion.1. Pressing escape brings up a menu that allows you to exit back to the game, to the pack's main menu, and to exit to desktop.2. The games "Drawful: Animate" "Job Job" and "Weapons Drawn" have an option to disable timers. At the time of writing, I haven't been able to test this, but for those who don't want timers on these games, it is a nice option.Now with the quality of life changes noted, I think it's time to look at the games in the pack.1. DRAWFUL: ANIMATEEasily the weakest game of the pack, in my opinion. The two-frame animations add alot to the Drawful experience, easily making Drawful: Animate the definitive Drawful experience, but the lack of an undo button or eraser in drawing makes Drawful Animate a game I'm less likely to pick over games like Gartic Phone or Skribblio. Despite this, Drawful: Animate can easily bring the laughs and is a good supporting addition to the pack.2. THE WHEEL OF ENORMOUS PROPORTIONSThis is the pack's trivia game. However, the Wheel of Enormous Proportions (which I'm gonna call "the Wheel" from now on) takes the trivia game and makes it radically different from the other trivia games in the other packs. Instead of choosing between three or four choices in games like Fibbage or Trivia Murder Party, most questions will have at least ten possible answers that you're probably not gonna get completely correct. Some questions will require you to match pairs, and some questions will need you to guess what the wheel is thinking of. In all other Jackbox trivia games, answering correctly will net you points, but in the Wheel, you also need luck to win the game. First to 20,000 points and land on a winning spot  on the winner's wheel will net you the win. The Wheel gives a good time for all, especially since the large amount of potential answers means that everyone will likely have to guess each question, meaning that nearly anyone could get a slice on the wheel.3. JOB JOBEasily my personal favorite game from the pack. The premise of Job Job is simple: You're answering common job interview questions by using some of the words said by the other players, which can lead to cursed quotes depending on what everyone else said. Job Job without context sounds incredibly boring (I mean who wants to answer job interview questions for fun?) but one of the Jackbox Party Packs' specialties, in my opinion is making games with boring premises into chaotic messes with good execution. Also this game uses Microsoft Office's Word Art. Need I say anything else?4. POLL MINEPoll Mine tasks tasks two teams of players with escaping a cave or dungeon by making both teams do three poll-related challenges where everyone needs to answer a poll and then both teams try to figure out what options were chosen in a few specific positions by everyone in order to gain or lose torches. The first two challenges have no real consequences if you lose all of your torches, but if one team loses all torches in the last challenge and the other team gets the next poll position right, the team that answered that question right wins. Poll Mine is a fun game that encourages you to know everyone in the room better than everyone knows you in order to win.5. WEAPONS DRAWNWeapons Drawn feels similar to Among Us but if everyone was both an Impostor and a Crewmate at the same time. In Weapons Drawn, you hide one of your in-game name's' letters in a drawing of a random item the game gives you (like a can opener or a book). You use your drawn weapons to murder one of two "guests" that another player named.  Then the game becomes a typical Among Us emergency meeting after the murders happen while the murderer is decided. Weapons Drawn is a more interesting take on the Social Deduction game due to everyone being both a murderer and detective and can lead to some intense arguments seen in many Among Us games, just don't put extended timers on if you don't want the game to take forever.Overall, the most recent Jackbox Party Pack is a hit like always and is bound to make any gathering more fun.
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Party Pack 8

_childDocuments_.review: Party Pack 8 is similar to other packs in that there are one to two games worth playing along with some real duds.  Job Job: Job Job was probably the game my group enjoyed most, players answer "interview" questions with the individual words that other plays answer unrelated prompts with, so it could be difficult if the person who provided you with the prompts really phoned it in.  Has a very Quiplash/Survive the Internet slant.Poll Mine: This is a "family feud" type game, where the group votes on questions and are split into two teams to guess how each answer was ranked.  A nice slant, was you aren't always after the most popular answer, but sometimes the second or fifth.  Weapons Drawn: Is a fun social deception game, but is much much too long.  There is a "hurry" button like in Push the Button, but even with everyone spamming that, the game is a bit of slog.  Cool premise though.Wheel of Enormous Proportions: This might be the worst game in the whole Jackbox catalog.  The game is about 90% RNG from the wheel and 10% trivia. Our group did not have fun with this one at all.Drawful Animate:  I was looking forward to this one the most, because our group loves the drawing games, but it left us a little disappointed.  The actual drawing tools are VERY simple, only a few colors to work with, no options to change the brush thickness, no eraser/undo button, and the prompts can be VERY abstract making conveying your prompt difficult with the limited tools.  A GREAT feature I'm shocked that isn't in the game is the ability to "copy" your first drawing to the second frame for animation purposes.  At present, the game shows you an outline only and you have to re-draw it a second time.
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Party Pack 8

_childDocuments_.review: Very solid pack, though falls short of pack 7 imo.-Job Job is definitely the standout of the pack, it's a unique take on the usual Quiplash style of game which is very fun to play though sometimes you get absolutely shafted by other people giving you an awful word bank. 9/10-Weapons Drawn was one I was looking forward to, and it lived up to the expectations pretty well. Though it is a bit confusing and drags on quite a bit, I can imagine it goes on for a long time with 8 people. 8/10-The Poll Mine is a solid game, but doesn't work as well over discord as it would in person I think. Also, the first 2 rounds seem to be pretty irrelevant in the overall ending of the game as the final round changes everything so much. 7/10-Drawful Animate is pretty much exactly the same as the other Drawfuls except you draw twice as much. The animation doesn't really seem to add much to the gameplay, and the prompts are often so obscure that it's obvious which is real 80% of the time. 6.5/10-The Wheel of Enormous Proportions isn't the best trivia game they've made, but its definitely not the worst. A lot of the trivia is so obscure that not only is the wheel rng, but so is guessing the answers. Can drag on a fair bit depending on rng, (took 5 spins of the spinner wheel for the game to be over in our session) 5.5/10Overall, pretty good pack. Just not really games that you want to do more than once in a session except maybe Job Job. 7/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Party Pack 8

_childDocuments_.review: So i Pre Purchased this pack expecting more Jackbox... well i mean that is what i got, but what I wasn't expecting was just the amount of quality these games all had. This has to be the most quality Party Pack out of the five that i played (The others being 4, 5, 6, and 7) Not a single game was really a meh for me. I can see myself coming back to all of these games.Drawful... only with ANIMATION! Yeah its that simple, its drawful but with 2 frame animations instead of flat pictures. You get a prompt and you have to make a small moving picture based on that prompt. Once everyone finishes drawing, then everyone else has to then make a fake prompt to try and fool the other players and then guess what the real prompt for the drawing was. Good stuff Yeah. It's simple, doesn't go on for too long, and the small animation you get really brings a nice spice up to a familiar game.A trivia game with a healthy dose of mario party-esque randomness.  You answer questions to get wedges and after three rounds of questions you put them on the titular wheel and spin to get points. The catch is the real moneymaker, the wheel spinning, is completely random. You can be doing REALLY well in the question and have a bunch of wedges on the board but the wheel could potentially not land on them at all. It's complete random chance and chaos, making this a trivia game where you can suck at trivia but STILL come out on top if your luck is good enough. Really chaotic and I had a blast playing this with friendsThe standout game for Party Pack 8 in my opinion anyway. This one had almost nonstop laughter between my friends while we were playing. You start each round by answering prompts with sentences (5 words or more), then those sentences get sent to other players where they have to answer questions using on the words said in those sentences. (Or just from the question and writing prompt haha) This game leads to some random a hell (and very likely nonsensical) responses from every player. I don't know what else to say about this one, it was just pure joy to play. This game splits you into two teams and then for each round will give everyone a survey to answer honestly. Once everyone answers the game then will ask each team (one at a time) to pick a door each represented by a choice from the survey. The goal is to guess which choice came in a certain position depending on what the game asked of you (Example: 1st 2nd, 3rd or 2nd 3rd and 4th) Its a nice team effort that leads to some really intense moments as once you hit the final level your points (Tallied by torches) get taken away for every one you get wrong. The game is another standout of the pack and was a lot of fun to play. Okay this is the only one that didn't 100% jive with the rest of my team though I wouldn't say its a downright stinker or 'meh' game. You take the role of a murderer/detective and have to draw a murder weapon to murder someone with... the weapon must contain a pre-drawn letter from your own name as a calling card, so the catch is to incorporate the letter into the drawing discreetly. But you also have to guess who murdered someone else and try to figure out THEIR calling card, making this a game of trying to figure out symbols and who drew what. It takes a bit and the rules for winning weren't 100% concise if im honest. But I still had fun trying to figure out who dun-it being a fan of games like Ace Attorney and such.------------So overall just about all of these games were fun to play, and I can see myself replaying all of these at some point... at least compared to most of the other party packs. I'd recommend Party Pack 8 to anyone looking for a good time with friends, or anyone who is just a fan of Jackbox in general. Then again you've probably already picked the game up if you're either of those.
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Party Pack 8

_childDocuments_.review: I played this for three hours last night with six other friends. I can say that Job Job alone paid for itself with how much laughter and fun we had with it!Drawful Animate is okay but does take a long time to get going. I suppose technically the animation thing is optional, but it does literally double the time. Good if you have artistic friends like I did!The Wheel is a solid trivia game. Not as fun as Murder Trivia but it is still interesting with the wheel spinning bit. The more you win in trivia, the more likely you'll get your slice of the wheel spun on. Ironically better with fewer people since that keeps the game going longer.JOB JOB -- this thing is one of the most fun Jackbox games ever. You write essay prompts, then have to answer prompts made up of random cut out words for everyone else's previous prompts. You can even take words out of the instructions or anywhere else on the page! Literally cried laughing. Will be doing that one for a long time!Poll Mine -- hot garbage, not gonna lie. It's designed to where everyone has a tier list and you guess which rankings the majority gave. These prompts can be very solid or very lame -- we had "best activities at summer camp" and literally none of us ever went. It also goes on way too long. Definitely the weakest one.Weapons Drawn -- Unique and creative. Honestly better than Drawful because it gives you a mandatory letter of your name to hide into the drawing, and people have to guess who the killer was based on the image, looking for said letter. This letter can be in any case, cursive or script, and can even look poorly drawn so that it's hard to find! Get points for killing guests and having the guest you brought hard to kill!All in all this pack isn't as good as, say, Jackbox Party Pack 6, but Job Job and Weapons Drawn alone make it in my personal top 3. Just be aware that this one takes up a lot more creativity and time than most other packs, so depending on what you prefer or how timetables with friends are, this may be a pass.
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Party Pack 8

_childDocuments_.review: great pack. the games are all pretty solid and can fit for different groups. also love the quality of life changes. in older packs each game had its own settings page and none of those carried between games. in this pack there is one settings page for all games that you can access from all the games.

_childDocuments_.review: It's really fun just like all other jackbox games as long as you have good company.me and my friends found that the US content filter didn't have any effect Wheel of Enormous Proportions, we're are all english and we had loads of questions about US geography and TV shows that aren't widely known in the UK. The game itself was really good but we had a really hard time knowing anything about the subjects. this has never been a problem before in other jackbox packs so we were surprised. just be warned before purchasing
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Party Pack 8

_childDocuments_.review: The Jackbox Party Pack 8 is definitely a Party Pack that delivers a few really fun games but a couple I'm not the biggest fan of ultimately. Still a solid pack overall!Drawful is back in the form of Drawful Animate and this was definitely a cool concept on paper as you draw and make animations and there is a bit of novelty in that. Along with the new Friend Mode. However, the excessive length especially with the player count turned up to 10 really drags things out more than they should. I'm also not a fan of the weirder prompts and deliberate typos. I still think Drawful 2 is a much better, and more efficiently paced game.Job Job is one of my favorites in this pack and even though it does have a lengthy pace as well, the premise of twisting words is still very funny and fun. I always encourage people to use the full character limit and not think too hard on the prompts so everyone has something to work with and it's definitely a game that has plenty of charm.The Poll Mine is a survey-based game, but unlike Guesspionage, the surveys are based on all the player responses including the audience. Which makes things feel funny and fresh each time to see how everyone answers and make judgments with how they are ranked.The Wheel of Enormous Proportions is a funny new take on both the trivia genre and has the concept of a Magic 8 Ball (though it definitely has more question logic than that) and has the novelty of how you don't even need to be the best at trivia to win it. It helps but it does come down to spins and how you also acquire points that way to get to the Winner Wheel. There are plenty of fun twists and turns with this one. Another go-to of mine.Weapons Drawn is a game I did like initially but compared to Jackbox's other social deception games, it doesn't really compare. It can get very easy to spot player's letters in their drawings when you've played the game enough and just isn't as exciting as a social deception game should be imo. I like being able to have an alibi in these games too but once you play this enough and people can spot your letter immediately, there's really not a chance to defend yourself and try to form an alibi. Therefore, it does become a case of just finding the letter and matching it with the player. Which again, doesn't make the game exciting enough for me personally. But I do still like the bold concept, the music, and vibes.
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Party Pack 8

_childDocuments_.review: After playing all the games with my friends on one of their streams, I can say that game overall is very good. All of the games don't seem like a drag, and they are all fun. My only problem in this pack is that the games seem very long, like Weapons Draw. Other than that I would totally get this game for some laughs.
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Party Pack 8

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has enjoyed all packs, especially pack 7, I was looking forward to see if this game would deliver to the same heights as the previous packs. I'll be going over the games in a (somewhat) simplistic manor, as who cares for reading anyway.[Games were played in a discord server with below max players. That does heavily change things at least in my opinion.]Drawful Animate: The original drawful is good, and this one is too. The only real difference between this and regular drawful is the fact you can animate your drawings. Something that kind of upset those I played with was the fact that the baseline prompts given were a tad too specific. If you wanted to do the even slightest of joke prompt, it stuck out like a sore thumb. Still a decent game, just need to adapt to the prompts.Wheel of Enormous Proportions: I really like trivia games for some reason, even if I absolutely suck at trivia. Something that was neat about this game was the fact that it seemed like it was a child of You Don't Know Jack and Trivia Murder Party. A ton of shared aspects combined that made this game uniquely fun. Would've liked to have maybe played more than one time, but the rest of those playing did not seem to enjoy the game as much as I did.Job Job: Voted probably best game out of the pack between me and those I played with. You fill out the prompts the game gives you and then afterwords you must use words from other players' responses to create the ultimate funnypost response to another prompt. Profanity filter needs to be turned off for maximum enjoyment. Poll Mine: Again, another game that probably needs maximum players as possible for most fun. The players are split into two teams to try to further the amount of torches (points) each team gets. Answering random polls, people will need to vote on the most voted answers for torches, and eventually vice versa. Does this for a round or two and that pretty much wraps up the game. Game isn't the greatest but it isn't bad either.Weapons Drawn: Those I played with felt mixed about the game including myself. The premise is easy once you complete a game, but for the first game it just seemed confusing on what you're supposed to do. Mixing a pre-generated letter from your name, you must combine it with a drawing of yours to avert suspicious from you throughout the game. You need to successfully murder to even be classified as a murderer (duh?), but once you do people need to make context clues from your drawings to see if they can put two and two together. It's the same premise for 2-3 rounds or so. Points in this game were won solely on the fact if A. you committed a murder, B. Solved a murder, or C. fooled players. Maybe once we revisit the game we'll enjoy it more, but for now it was just okay. Overall, the pack to me isn't as good as pack 7. I'll just say it now. In my honest opinion you do need maximum players for all games to really settle into it. There's still plenty of fun to be had either way with all of the games in their own way.

_childDocuments_.review: Best party pack yet!! Every single game was really enjoyable and amazing! This has never happened in any other pack where I have really really enjoyed every single game! Also they have really upped their animation, settings (can change for all games - not individually), menu and so much more! I am so proud and amazed! Such a great game!

_childDocuments_.review:
The eighth installment of the beloved Jackbox Party Pack franchise is here! Five hilarious new games will energize your next game night, holiday party, happy hour, or video call. No extra controllers needed - players use their phones or tablets to play along! Got a bigger group? Play with up to 10 players and up to 10,000 audience members. The Jackbox Party Pack 8 is currently in English only. This game does not support online matchmaking but can still be enjoyed remotely using livestreaming services or video conferencing tools.

 

About Each Game

Drawful Animate (3 -10 players) - It’s alive! The guessing game with terrible drawings and hilariously wrong answers makes a dynamic return. In this revamped title, players create looping, two-frame animations based on weird and random titles.

Job Job (3-10 players) - Use other people’s words to create unique and funny answers to classic job interview questions. Go head to head to see who scores the job!

The Poll Mine (2-10 players) - A survey game that’s all about YOU! Split into teams and see who can escape from the witch’s lair! Players individually rank their choices to a difficult question, then must guess how the group answered as a whole. How well do you know your friends?!

Weapons Drawn (4-8 players) - A social deduction game where everyone is both a murderer and a detective. Players doodle all the clues, hiding a letter from their name in the weapon drawings. Can you solve murders while trying to get away with your own?

The Wheel of Enormous Proportions (4-8 players) - Trivia has never been so large! A fantastic, mystical wheel challenges you with a variety of trivia prompts. Winners are awarded slices of the Wheel’s face with a chance to win big with each nail-biting spin. In the end, one player will have their most burning question answered by the great Wheel.

name: Castlevania Advance Collection
detailed_description: Count Dracula is once more back from the dead... Join the fight against Evil in the Castlevania Advance Collection, a compilation of timeless action-exploration masterpieces! In addition to the three legendary Castlevania games that were first released in the early 2000s, this collection also includes Castlevania: Dracula X and some never-before-seen sketches and artwork from the games! All four games are enhanced with newly added modern features such as Rewind, Save/Load and Replay, making this the best way possible to experience these classics or discover them for the first time! This collection also boasts a handy Encyclopedia, a Music Player with all soundtracks and you can even change the ROM Region to play all games in different versions. Featured Games Castlevania: Circle of the Moon The story follows Nathan Graves, a vampire hunter apprentice who enters Dracula's Castle along with his Master in order to prevent the dreaded return of the Count. Combine action and attribute cards to create over 80 unique spell effects, ranging from fire whips to ice blizzards, with the 'Dual Set-up System'. Castlevania: Harmony of Dissonance Play as Juste Belmont, the grandson of legendary Vampire Hunter Simon Belmont! This title introduced a lot of new features to the franchise, such as 'Boss Rush' mode and the 'Spell Fusion' system that lets players combine Sub-Weapons with Spell Books to cast devastating spells. Castlevania: Aria of Sorrow Soma Cruz, a young high school exchange student in Japan, is somehow involved in the eternal cycle of reincarnation of the Dark Lord himself. What role does Soma play in all of this? Will he be able to return to his own world? Aria of Sorrow also introduced a brand new attack system called 'Tactical Souls', that lets Soma Cruz capture the souls of slain monsters to acquire their abilities. (100+ abilities in total!) Aria of Sorrow also has a ton of New Game+ content. Castlevania: Dracula X Castlevania: Dracula X is a reimagination of the cult action game Castlevania: Rondo of Blood and has been acclaimed as one of the most challenging Castlevania titles ever created. The Dark Lord Count Dracula rises again from the dead to revive the forces of darkness and to annihilate this corrupted world and create a new one. You are Richter Belmont, heir of the Belmont family, and you set out for Dracula's Castle to defeat its evil master. Fight your way through Dracula's Castle and defeat the toughest enemies with the new special attack 'Item Crash'! Brand New Features for an Improved Experience! Gallery Browse through scans of the original package designs and discover incredible artwork never shown to the public before. ROM Region Selection You can choose between the Japanese, American, and European versions for each game. Encyclopedia Learn more about all three games thanks to their dedicated encyclopedia. Detailed information on enemies, the 'DSS' system, the 'Tactical Soul' system and the 'Spell Fusion' system will help you truly master each game's unique combat system! Music Player Listen to any of four complete soundtracks any time you want. You can even create your own playlists! New 'Quality of Life' Features Save/Load You can now quickly save and reload at any point in the game. Even right before that deadly attack from Dracula himself. Rewind You can now rewind the state of the game for a few seconds for a second chance. It is almost like being resurrected... Replay You can record and replay your runs. This is great for creating new tactics, speed runs and streaming.

He eventually spilled coffee on the cartridge, but with this collection I finally finished the game!My total run time: 21.5 years.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite the thumbs down,  is a collection of good to great  games. The three main attractions are from the second half of the series, -inspired action RPGs where you explore Dracula's castle:So why am I dogging on this collection?I got a GBA the day it launched, back in 2001. Yep, I'm old enough that I think Gretchen Whitmer is hot.  was a launch game, the launch game I came home with. It was awesome -- but it was ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥  to see. You see, the original GBA's screen wasn't lit. At all. So if developers didn't account for that, and released a game with dark colors, best of luck. Reviews of the game were positive, but nearly everyone complained about this.Developers, Konami in particular, figured this out over time. By the time  came out in 2002, Konami knew what to do. The colors were absolutely blown out and gaudy, but on a non-lit GBA screen this was actually perfect. You could see it! Nintendo eventually released a front-lit model, the GBA SP, and so developers tended to split the difference later in the GBA's life cycle.  came out a few months after the GBA SP, and it occupies this middle ground. It's brighter than , but not as bright as .20 years later, you have to be careful presenting these games on modern displays. And that's the problem with this collection: Konami weren't careful presenting these games on modern displays. By contrast, I think Nintendo did a really good job with their Nintendo Switch Online GBA emulator, for three reasons: has none of this. In particular, it has no color correction. So ironically, despite what reviews at the time said about it being too dark,  might be the one GBA game in this collection that doesn't raise an eyebrow.  looks ; every inch of Dracula's castle is oversaturated and garish. The blue lines they added around your character to make him easier to see on a real, non-lit GBA screen are particularly egregious now.  fares better, but is still clearly a few notches too colorful.It's a shame, because otherwise, this is a pretty decent collection. There's lots of bonus content like scans of the original manuals and box art, enhanced audio, save states, and rewinding. It even includes a copy of the SNES , which I guess Konami just forgot about when they made . Like the earlier entries in that other collection, SNES  is not one bit  inspired. It's a tough as nails level-by-level action platformer. It's not great, and it gets a really bad reputation for being a watered down version of the magnificent Japan-only, TurboGrafx-only . But I find it a bit underrated. If you've worn out  and are craving a little more "Classicvania" style action, well, I guess I'd say check out the  games... but if you don't have those, SNES  is an OK way to pass an hour.Really, my only other complaint regards the new "gadgets" they added. Each GBA game has an optional gadget that helps you find collectibles. The gadgets for  and  are fairly useless, but the one for  should have been a game changer. Remember how I complained about not knowing which enemies dropped cards? The gadget tells you. If you fight an enemy that could drop a card, you'll get a message telling you. Unfortunately, these messages block a good chunk of the gameplay screen, and . D'oh. So what should have been a godsend turns out to be an annoyance. I say turn it off, go old school, and print out a list of card drops from GameFAQs. (I swear, I'm only in my mid-30s!)That's the sort of misstep I can forgive. The awful presentation, though, I just can't. Fan-made emulators have been doing this right for decades, so I find it inexcusable to charge for a collection of GBA games with no color correction. Doubly so when across the GBA's whole library,  is widely considered one of the worst oversaturation "offenders", said in quotes because it made sense to do at the time. It's a bummer, because like I said, the worst of the three GBA  games is still pretty decent, and the best of the three GBA  games is a universally recognized banger. But I can't tell you to go pay $20 for this fundamentally flawed collection when you'd have a much better experience emulating them and turning on a filter.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an odd collection when it comes to the title of this game. Castlevania Advance Collection. One would think this would just be the Gameboy Advance titles. And they would be wrong. While this collection does indeed include the 3 Castlevania titles from the Gameboy Advance, it also includes 1 entry from the SNES Castlevanias in the form of Dracula X. It makes me wonder why they did not just call this Castlevania Anniversary Collection Volume 2. It's definitely not a knock on this collection, but rather just a curious observation. In any case, yes, you get all 3 original GBA CV titles. There actually was a 4th GBA Castlevania, but it was just a port of the original Castlevania, which is not included in this collection mainly because it also available in the 1st Castlevania collection. And there was not really any difference between the GBA and NES versions, other than apparently a save system being added, and oddly, the end credits being removed from the GBA version. The 3 GBA titles are a nice package for fans of the mostly non linear Metroidvania side of the Castlevania series. The Metroidvania formula is intact in all 3 titles. Start in a section of the map, and progress forward while finding some linearity at first. However upon picking up certain powerups, the linearity starts to fade away and the game now becomes more open ended. Powerups can range from your typical tropes of allowing for wall jumps, double jumps, floating, increased strength to move large objects and more. Each game has a variety of these to collect to allow you to progress and explore more of the maps. You also get some RPG elements in each game that range from equippable gear that can alter stats, and also leveling up for different effects. Dracula X is the only title in this collection that is not a Metroidvania, and is instead more akin to Classicvania. This means progression is instead far more linear, and based on levels rather than 1 massive map that you explore. It is also a remake or re-imagining of the classic TG-16 title: Rondo of Blood. Because of it's more straightforward linear approach grounded in Classicvania roots, this will also be the hardest title of the bunch to tackle. And for some, that is not entirely a bad thing. All of the games, including Dracula X feature a bevy of monsters to fight ranging from skeletons, floating heads, zombies, werewolves, knights, and other bizarre creatures. You fight with either whips or swords mostly depending on which game, but can also use alternative weapons such throwing daggers, holy water, and more. There are also plenty of boss fights in each game! As for which game is the best? Well, there's no right or wrong answer here, as everyone's opinions will differ. What matters though is that each game will have stuff to offer most fans of the Castlevania series. The collection includes a couple of QOL features to make things a bit easier, such as being able to save anywhere in the game, as well as a nifty rewind feature. Other included features are things like saveable replays, a music player, artwork, and different region versions for all 4 games. You can also resize the games from pixel perfect, standard and full screen. Full screen does stretch the game a little keep in mind. Standard imo is the best way to play this. There's not much left to say. This is a solid collection, and while it may have half the titles of the 1st collection, I think it more than makes up for it with quality titles all around.

_childDocuments_.review: Developed by Kobe studios, CotM was the first Castlevania title to sell more than 1mill copies worldwide and was nominated for GOTY awards.In CotM you play as Nathan Graves, an apprentice vampire hunter trying to save his master from the resurrected Dracula. It's very much not a game driven forward by storytelling and instead it wants you to focus entirely on its exploration, combat and unique RPG system. The gameplay is simple and solid, with leveling up, exploring the castle and mastering abilities. The castle layout is one of the best in the whole series as it was a big priority of the studio. Sadly that same level of attention is missing in some key areas. The biggest problem is the movement. for some reason they chose to have Nathan walk incredibly slow which makes vertical platforming tricky some times. What made it more frustrating was the decision to have two movement speeds as the first upgrade you find is the dash boots with the ability to run by double tapping left or right. Having this activated on a double press is just criminally tedious and you get sick of it pretty quickly. Kobe have managed to get the hard part right by creating a world that's inviting to explore and a new RPG system called Dual setup system or DSS as it's known in-game. What is DSS? Through killing certain enemies you can find magical cards associated with either attributes or actions. The idea is that you link them in pairs to produce different spells that Nathan can cast using his MP with about a hundred combinations to experiment. Circle of the Moon has a reputation as a damn hard game and while a lot of that is because of the game's control issues it's also thanks to some choices of the developers as there is no shop to buy potions or better gear so you rely entirely on drops from enemies to gain resources.The bosses are a real step up in difficulty from previous titles. Many bosses have multiple forms or surprise attacks and if you head in without the correct DSS cards, fights like Death, Drama Leg and Hue will take you a long time to beat. Finally that Dracula fight... just nightmare.Harmony was the first Castlevania title I played and though many consider it a weak game i enjoyed every minute of it. Igarashi's story and gameplay concepts, Takeda's direction and programming and of course the character designs of Ayami Kojima, an amazing artist. The game is set in the aftermath of Castlevania 2 and you play as Juste Belmont which brings back the iconic Belmont Whip. The story is simple yet captivating. You find your childhood friend Maxim injured with no recollection of what happened to him. The only thing he does know is that their friend Lydie has been kidnapped and taken to a nearby castle so the 2 set out to rescue her but get separated. After some exploration you encounter Death who claims that the castle is not being manifested by the forces of Dracula. The mystery of who is in control of the castle is the core story of the entire game and frankly I think it's a great premise when the majority of the experience involves exploration. Now, as it is an Iga game, it means we actually get a plot worth experiencing. Harmony's gameplay and visuals are built on huge changes which make it unlike anything else in the franchise. Movement feels responsive and precise which in turn makes engaging combat fun. As the focus is now so heavily on action, the RPG system that saved CotM have now been stripped and in its place is a mechanic that's much more the traditional style of Castlevania gameplay. Hidden in various locations around the castle are Elemental spell books that change the properties of whatever sub weapon Juste is carrying.Now, on the downside I think the idea that the game takes place across two separate spaces requiring teleportation between them, even though on paper sounds really interesting, it's easily the worst thing about HoD. The 2 castles are completely identical in terms of layout and it can make the exploration extremely repetitive. Yes the enemies are different in each castle but that's not really enough of a change. The only place that the 2 castle system feels like it's working is in the narrative and forms the foundation of the mystery plot.I won't spoil the story but I'm going to praise how well woven into the Dual castle the plot becomes.In both castles the game ends in the same room but you get a different ending depending on if you are in Caslte A or B. It's the classic "good" or "bad" ending.But wait, there is a third secret ending, something that Igarashi loves to do in every game of his. The third one of course is the "perfect" ending.For the next title Igarashi and his team wanted to do something different. They decided to make a game that retained the core fundamentals of CotM and HoD but challenged all the other established tropes that the series had come to rely on. With Aria of Sorrow the intention was to serve up something like nothing else in the franchise.There was a huge change in the game's aesthetics and setting where Igarashi decided to take a bold step outside the series comfort zone. Instead of a gothic medieval setting Aria was gonna take place in the near future. The year is 2035 and we find ourselves in Japan as a transfer student called Soma Cruz on our way to watch the solar eclipse with our friend Mina. But as the moon moves in front of the sun we catch a glimpse of a castle floating in the sky.For me Aria of Sorrow has an amazing story, captivating, unique and with great characters so I will try not to include any more information of the plot.The gameplay formula changes once again and dramatically improves the combat and exploration.Instead of the classic Vampire killer Whip, Soma attacks by wielding a variety of weapons that are found throughout the castle and there's clearly been a big effort into upping the differences between them.From fast-paced rapiers and slower claymors, to elemental swords, spears, axes and even guns.That same degree of choice also governs Aria's main gameplay mechanic, the Tactical Soul system which is a reworked version of DSS into something much more interesting and deeply tied to the plot. The ability to absorb souls that Soma possesses is called the power of Dominance and by defeating enemies you can gain a range of different abilities which are equipped to 3 unique slots. There are 55 souls to find all with their own animations, strengths and weaknesses which adds a huge amount of depth to combat. Another area of real success is how Aria improves both balance and difficulty. The first couple of bosses may seem as an easy feat, but as the game progresses, you encounter bosses like Headhunter, the infamous Death fight and Graham.2 different endings as well here and a classic Iga secret ending that is top quality.  Aria of Sorrow is considered the greatest Castlevania title and Koji Igarashi's final masterpiece for the franchise.

_childDocuments_.review: I was extremely excited about this collection when it was announced, especially since it was the first time some of the entries like Aria of Sorrow would be properly available on PC. Sadly, it's one of the most barebones collections I've played in terms of quality of life features, marred by technical issues.The Good:-Great collection of classic games-Some nice features such as rewinding and quick saving/loading-Small additions such as an enemy encyclopedia and a feature that notifies you if you have received an enemies soul in Aria of SorrowThe Bad:-Extremely barebones settings. No resolution settings (simply pixel perfect, full, or an in-between), no brightness settings, not even a built in full-screen feature (you need to press Alt+Enter to do so)- The "high quality" audio feature simply muffles the sound effects and music to remove some of the higher pitches the GBA's audio quality produced. While it takes the edge off some of the peaked sounds, it also makes the soundtrack and sound effects muddled, with some tones outright inaudible.-Pretty terrible implementation of settings within the game, where many (such as the high quality audio) require a full game restart.-At least in my experience playing Aria of Sorrow, attempting to utilize the quick save feature had a 50% chance of crashing the game to desktop, in which I lost significant amounts of progress.-The Soul Gadget, a feature that notifies you if you had previously received an enemy's soul, places a large grey text box on the side middle of your screen every time you hit an enemy. This means hitting multiple enemies leads to one half of your screen being marred by boxes that don't even match the in-game UI.-Control options are extremely limited, in which (at least for Aria of Sorrow) you cannot map anything to the back two triggers. It makes little sense as to why you can't change what these triggers do or switch their feature (opening the emulation menu) to the front two triggers or even another button entirely.Altogether, it's an extremely simple port of fantastic games onto the PC. While I appreciate it being here for preservation, nearly all of the attempts to provide quality of life features are inconvenient at best, damaging to the game experience at worst. If patches are able to fix these issues, such as the crashing, as well as add in more basic PC features (resolution options, brightness, more control options) then this could be a great way to explore this generation of the series. Until then, this is only worth your time if you genuinely have no other means of playing these games.

_childDocuments_.review: I was disappointed with the state of the Castlevania Anniversary Collection PC port, it lacked basic features and even had bugs that made it feel shoddy.The Advance Collection proves to be a different experience. While imperfect, it needs be said that this is a pretty good port of the GBA's Castlevania games, along with the SNES' less appreciated "Castlevania Dracula X" as bonus. This fixes most issues the previous collection has and introduces some new QOL features such as rewind and 'gadgets' which prove very helpful for the in-game content that requires grinding. When you press 'Esc', you get a prompt which asks if you wish to leave the game, a feature which was somehow absent in the last collection. When you press 'F1', you get a fairly robust selection of options, which help with customising how the game displays and give options like replay, save states, and button bindings. Though if playing on keyboard, you are still unable to rebind your keys, which makes play slightly awkward. Given the default bindings list 'Z' as jump, 'A' as display map and 'Q' as evade, you may find yourself opening the map by accident instead of dodging your enemy's attack, which feels uncomfortable to work with. So controller is highly recommended here, not that it wasn't before since this is Castlevania, but it has better bindings which can also be altered.As for the games, they are as fun to play as ever. Though three of them were originally designed for a handheld games console and playing them on PC with a larger, vibrant screen and better audio changes how these feel on replay. I was given opportunity to reconsider how I view these games on my replay.Known for being hard to play due to the original GBA's lack of a backlight, the colour and style are evident now.The  are the staple gimmick of CotM, they offer stat buffs, give the whip elemental based attacks, or change the whip to a completely different weapon like a sword or a hammer. The issue is these cards have low drop rates, and it isn't explicitly clear what card combinations do what, this doesn't lend itself too well for what is essentially a ~8 hour long campaign. So unless you grind for cards, you will hardly see them on your first run. Speaking of grinding, the Advance Collection features a gadget that tells you if an enemy has dropped a card, paired with the rewind feature, you can save some time when trying to 100% your card collection. Though those drop rates are still a hassle regardless.Rewarding to replay. The colours are garish but a definite graphical improvement from CotM. The music isn't as hi-quality as the other 2 GBA games, but some songs are catchy and feel fitting in producing atmosphere. There are 2 areas in which this game is excels; character movement & magic.The dash and slide make it fun to navigate the castle.The magic is streamlined and fun to use. Just activate a spell book and its' effects will differ depending on the book and sub weapon you have equipped.You play as a Belmont, the only one to headline a metroidvania style Castlevania. Naturally you also hold the whip, though there's a twist; attachable tips. Most just improve damage but they do offer a minor cosmetic change, a fun one-off detail.HoD has some minor cutscenes for certain events which give the game a slight 'cinematic' flair.This game is less tedious to 100%. The main collectables are furniture, found lying in different areas of the map (and have a room on the map dedicated to displaying them all), which means no annoying RNG mechanics required to get them, merely map exploration. There's also a gadget which now shows you what items you have on a particular section of the map.HoD doesn't differ as drastically in quality as much as people want to pretend it does.Considered the best of the GBA games.Where CotM lacks graphically, and HoD lacks in soundtrack, AoS excels in both. The central gimmick, souls, is engaging. it replaces sub weapons and instead you gain the 'souls' of your enemies which allow the use of their abilities (or they're just stat buffs in certain cases). The souls encourage the player to try different play styles and builds.The inventory management of AoS is great, with items and spells being categorised appropriately, navigation is a breeze, your last used souls are at the top of the list. The story is something I enjoy as a fan, first and foremost. Some of it is fan service. Though the inclusion of certain characters makes it feel like a celebration of the series, even if it is cheesy.My main problem with the game rests in the souls' drop rates. The mechanic I previously praised as great features a problem, pitiful drop rates. The grind to get all souls can slightly stain the experience as the issue here is arguably worse than in CotM; there was only so many cards to grind for there. You can speed up the process by grinding for the 'Soul Eater ring'. This item costs a ludicrous price, but you'll find some valuable items through map exploration that you can sell off to get you there quicker. The gadget that keeps track of enemy souls obtained and the rewind included are helpful in mitigating some of the annoyance but it still takes a while.AoS also features a hard mode which is worth playing as it includes new items, higher drop rates for souls and provides a more challenging experience. This mode alleviates most problems of normal mode and elevates Aria of Sorrow as one of the best of the series.Perhaps an odd addition, but it's probably the closest game stylistically to the GBA games that still wasn't ported yet.Known for high difficulty, although that's frankly overblown. Enemies have telegraphed attacks which are easy to learn. The real challenge lies in the somewhat stiff jump, low invincibility frames and large hitboxes. The game has an alt ending depending on the actions you take. DX feels closer to the originals than Rondo of Blood does. DX is designed to better utilise the player's skillset, with the backflip, ability to jump off stairs, crouch preventing knockback and item crash's invinciblity frames being crucial skills to know to get through. Familiarise yourself with enemy proximity, character movement, don't rush; there's no time limit, and make use of the password system/ save states and you will find a fun game here.Underrated Classicvania. Experienced Castlevania players should give this one a shot. Expect a game that will help you learn and grow the more you play.A worthwhile collection, and this port (read emulator with collection of roms) feels like it actually had some effort put into it when compared to the previous. This collection features 4 quality titles, with Aria of Sorrow being a notable series highlight.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic collection, had a lot of fun. I hope in the future we'll get another collection or separate games with all the missing games from the series. Being someone who never had any of the original consoles, and also not being very good with emulators, I really appreciated this one.Looking at each game separately:Circle of the moon. Very fun game with unique mechanics. The sheer amount of DSS combinations are overwhelming in a good way, makes you pick and choose different combinations and strategies for specific areas/bosses, unleashing your creativity. Speaking of bosses, out of all the games in this collection, circle of the moon has my favorite boss fights. Among all the positives, there are some negatives. The worst part of the game is probably the grindiness. In order to beat the game, you'll have to either be absolutely cracked OR farm and grind like there is no tomorrow. The game is designed in a way that makes you grind for levels, equipment, healing and mana items. At times, this can get very tedious and repetitive. Harmony of dissonance. I enjoyed this game. Many have criticized the idea with 2 castles, but personally I enjoyed it, as it gave a unique exploration experience. "Enjoyed" might actually be an understatement, I bloody loved this mechanic. Puzzles are simple, yet feel very rewarding. Puzzles that use both castles? Even betterNegatives? 1. Was not very impressed with spell book mechanic, infinitely inferior to DSS and soul system. 2. This game is just TOO easy, no matter how you look at it. I completed 70% of the game by the time I died for the first time. Regular enemies are too weak, bosses are too weak, everything is just too simple. Bosses don't give that feeling of "oh I'll have to think this one through" or "I'm stuck aren't I". You meet them, you beat them, you forget them. Aria of sorrow. This one was just amazing.  Collecting souls was fun, having unique dialogues with characters was fun, exploration was fun, bosses were fun. I loved the gameplay, and I loved how they gave more personality to both main character and all the side characters. Even to the merchant! Many consider this game to be the best in this collection, and I can totally see whyNegatives: Every possible problem you encounter can be solved with enough Mana and Hp items. Like literally. And they're not even hard to obtain in this game.Dracula x. Hated by all, loved by me. Don't get me wrong, I understand why people hate it. This game is hard, and it is hard in a very ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ way. At times it feels like that game is just making fun of you, laughing from your sufferings. Enemy algorithm is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, level design is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, bottomless pits are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, hitboxes are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Which is what makes this game so great. I spent 8 straight hours on the last boss and every single crevice of my body was sweating by the end of it. It's a beautiful game, try itNegatives: every ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ positive is actually a negative and every negative is actually positive

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, listen.Let's not kid ourselves: The only thing Konami did here was the GBA Roms into one bundle. It has the same music, gameplay, lag, limitations and everything in between they had before. Absolutely no change whatsoeverWhat does this mean? If you LOVE the GBA Castlevanias like I do and it's been a lifetime since you've played it put your money in here. Is easy, convenient and the nostalgia rush is going to be glorious. Plain and simple.Don't come looking for remastered graphics, music or gameplay. This is your childhood game as a whole with both the good and the bad.
