_childDocuments_.review: The first thing you should be aware of in regards to this collection is that it lacks a settings/options menu of any kind. There are no screen resolution settings, no volume sliders, etc. The game defaults to 1920x1080 windowed mode, you can go fullscreen with alt+enter or by using a third party program like Lossless Scaling. If you want to adjust the game volume, you will have to do so through your overall windows volume or by tweaking the game volume in Volume Mixer.Additionally, there is no option to rebind the keyboard keys, only swap around what the pre-chosen keys do. As such, the collection is best played with a controller. I have never experienced any input delay, and although some people have reported audio related problems such as stuttering, audio not playing, buzzing sounds, etc. I have not encountered any such problem.Those are the downsides, so if any of that sounds like a reason you wouldn't want to buy this, there you have it. The positives are up next.The collection is running through emulation with a really convenient emulation wrapper that displays helpful information such as whether or not you've collected an enemy type's soul when you attack them in Aria of Sorrow. You can create and load save states, and there's also a rewind option which can be toggled on and off. The wrapper also comes with an encyclopedia for each game, acting as a sort of game manual with various helpful information tidbits.The modding community has figured out how to swap out the roms in this collection with romhacks or even different games entirely, though do keep in mind this could potentially cause achievements to unlock that shouldn't.Overall, this is a really fun collection of games and I have no regrets adding them to my collection.
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Advance Collection

_childDocuments_.review: I'm just happy to see Castlevania games on steam, even if this is essentially a glorified emulator without the ability to speedup or use romhacks. There are some bonus features. One feature is the ability to rewind time...but I find that cheap so I removed the bind. Another feature is that each game has some unique feature to help with completion and keep track of things. However...these are LACKING and clog the screen up. I don't need to know if the enemy I'm killing has a soul/card I need every time I hit him. It really isn't helpful.  It works well enough, but the fact you can't modify the sound in the app is lazy. While some people were having issues with getting a controller to work, I personally ran into no issues with my PS5 controller. The games themselves are great. Rondo is a more classic Castlevania, but still a really great game. I wish it was the PSN version that had SOTN as well. SOTN deserves to be on Steam. 8/10 Harmony of Dissonance - This really is the Castlevania of the SOTN/GBA/DS Castlevanias. I feel like this game is good, and I always liked it as a kid. However, I'd say it's the least unique of them all. The spell combinations are fairly interesting, but compared to the other two GBA games in this bundle...lack depth.  I'd say its aged the worst because of that. 7.5/10 Circle of the Moon - One of the more underrated Castlevania games. While the movement feels very different, it sort of grows on you. I will admit, constantly double tapping to run feels sluggish. The DSS system, where you combine cards to create unique spells is fairly interesting.  Sadly a lot of the options aren't worth using. The game also lacks unique weapons. You will be using a whip + subweapons + whatever spell the whole game. 8.5/10Aria of the Sorrow - Honestly, my 2nd favorite Metroidvania game. The only one I'd place higher is Order of Occlesia, which I hope gets a port in the future. It's a fantastic game, and honestly the best entry point in the Metroidvania era of Castlevania games. For a GBA game, the graphics have aged fairly well and the controls feel smooth and responsive. The soul system is a fantastic way of making every enemy killed feel potentially awarding. Each enemy has a unique soul which gives you a random spell, summon, or equipable passive benefit. This in addition to their normal loot tables of weapons, items, and armor.  10/10Overwall, I'd say buy this if you love the Metroidvania genre and want to play these games on Steam. Emulation is strictly better, but I like achievement hunting and these games were a huge part of my childhood. I mostly bought this in hopes that the DS games and SOTN get ported as well. If money's tight, just use an emulator.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a mixed set of games but overall I'd recommend the Advance Collection.Circle of the Moon : IMO, this one has aged really poorly but I know that's a hot take. The physics feel all wrong and the overall design just didn't really jive with me. The idea for the card system is unique but I don't see myself ever recommending Circle of the Moon to someone unless I know they love the old Castlevania movement. Harmony of Dissonance : It's fine? It's overall gamefeel is much closer to Symphony of the Night but that's not to say I think it's flawless. It's a perfectly fine Castlevania, I just prefer the systems in other games over it. It's way too easy to get an item needed to progress and not realize it, because it's just a regular piece of equipment in your inventory and not a relic. Aria of Sorrow: The one to actually get this package for, IMO. Aria of Sorrow has aged the best out of the bunch and feels like a follow up to SotN's mechanics. Collecting and using souls is fun, the movement is all right, we've got weapon variety with overhead swings, side swings, poking weapons, gun, all the fan favorites. The soundtrack is great, but held back by the GBA's hardware but overall it is THE one to play out of this set.Dracula X: I mean, I'm glad it got re-released but it's nothing special? It's not Rondo of Blood but it's another classic styled Castlevania, so if you wanted that instead of a metroidvania well it's here.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh Castlevania how long we know each other. Its like first game I ever played will never forget and always cherish you no matter what. We had some ups and downs but you will always be my Halloween spirit. We are back, slowly but creeping from a grave Konami. We can experience four new old titles from the past. This time more interesting metrovania style gameplay. While I can appreciate all of them but this will focus about Castlevania: Harmony of Dissocance. You play as Juste Belmont, one of most known family in this universe. Its up to you to face evil schemes from Death himself and her plans to return more evil spirit to this world. This time gameplay focus mainly inside huge castle location. One of the most beautiful games from castlevania collections and more innovative. First time you beat a giant Bat it will show you that this is only the begining of your long journey. Collecting hearts, upgrading your gear and returning to visited places just to reach higher level of secrets and unexplored rooms. The game doesn’t hold your hand and throws you at the center of evil dark. You will have your diary and map that somewhat guides your where you need to be. It shows you what enemies you faced, describe their weakneses and lets you combined more powerful weapons with some magic tricks. Super happy to know that this game is not on part of “crushing” or annoying difficulty like some other older titles. If you die that’s on you. Some of the bosses are harder than others but overall nothing can stop you if you have the right tools. Story is also one of the strongest in Castlevania library. Sometimes you will think that you are playing not one but two games at once, and the end if you will do everything 100% be prepared. Saving locations is on point and you can also use rewind option but you better not do that if you want to experience full potencial of this game. At the end with superb soundtrack and gameplay that will lead you all the way to the last door this one game could easily be sold as one because this from now on will stand in my top 2 best Castlevania games (until I will get to SOTN) of all times. Living a dream. We got superb Netflix Castlevania show and now second collection. Time will only tell…but I will always be waiting for more stories from this franchise.

_childDocuments_.review: Due to me being an odd individual who does reviews fresh from when they beat a game I will be doing this in multiple parts, 1 for each game specifically obviously lol dood.Castlevania circle of the moon: This was actually my first introduction to a metroidvania as a kid on the GBA, I was eager to see if I had nostalgia goggles on for this because I remembered loving it and honestly? I was happily surprised that it wasn't that, this is a good port of a great game with a stellar set of mechanics that can vary how you play the game, the DSS system allowed you to use various different abilities using your whip, sub weapons and even just insane magic in general, sometimes even passive abilities that basically made you invulnerable to different elements and such dood.It genuinely amazed me that they did so much with a GBA game for the time, even having a great amount of monster designs with unique attack patterns, as for what's new they added a card radar (back in the past you didn't know what monster had a card or not) the ability to save anywhere and the ability to rewind time a little, if you want this can kill the difficulty pretty much entirely but it's still a fun function for players who might need that extra hand dood. (that's part 1, see you for part 2 when I beat it!)Castlevania Harmony of Dissonance: Finally beat this one and honestly? I have a mixed opinion on it, was it a good game? yeah for sure but it feels this time around like they concentrated on the enemies and their mechanics over the players, granted Juste did have a myriad of spells of which you unlocked over time mostly powerful and with great visuals but it suffered for being linked with the sub weapons meaning you needed to find whatever sub weapon you wanted somewhere in the vast castle, on top of that unlike enemies who at times felt like mini bosses/martial arts masters at times you only really had your whip and it was fine if you were on the ground, the backdash afforded Juste some much needed distance but when it came to jumping attacks which you will be doing a loooot, it really made for a bad time, a massive lack of control often had you careening towards the enemy and we all know you get damaged just for touching them which is a big issue for aerial enemies and bosses dood.Overall though it wasn't too egregious, I had healing items aplenty if I needed to and the magic and subweapons were practically if not more powerful than the whip if used right, that said I feel the game this time around focused on the more classic stylised look of classic castlevania games which made for an amazing time travelling through the castle, granted it had to be for a certain reason I won't spoil for newbies like me to this game, all in all I think Circle of the moon so far was the more fun one to play but once you get into Dissonance it's no slouch, only major gripe was a huge lack of direction, my playtime is huge on this one if only because I spent a mass of time lost, in a bitter irony I actually did the right thing at the wrong place, go figure, minor gripe, the whip visuals for elements don't change like in CotM a dang shame, see you for the next one ya'all dood!Castlevania Aria of Sorrow: Finally got to this one and finished it, 100% no less and for good reason, Aria of sorrow is honestly the pinnacle of metroidvania games at the time, a large variety of enemy types, a myriad of skills, weapons and magic, some even passive to customise how you take on opponents, a new game plus, a new take on the typical style of castlevania games which I won't spoil for first timers to the series, particularly this game which actually got a second game on DS of which I played first dood.The game is truly packed with unique attacks and weapon visuals, a lot of which look outstanding and will even change how you fight in general, the backgrounds and areas often look outstanding, the moon early on was insane, this is a GBA game!? I felt and I played a lot of GBA games when I was younger, none of them felt as complete and full as Aria of sorrow in terms of content and gameplay options, my only problem with the game at most was drop rates, at times they could be a bit too much but even so they weren't entirely necessary outside of three particular things which the game hints at luckily, exploration is decently fun and you always have a reason to kill enemies outside of just levelling up and much like the other games I've played so far is a perfect port of a stellar game, one more game to go and I feel like I more than got my money's worth and then some just for these three games, see ya for the finale! right after I beat Julius mode dood *vampire killer plays*Castlevania X: Finally fully complete, so let's see, Castlevania X is...an odd one, not because it's not a metroidvania shockingly enough but because it feels like a step back while also being a step forward for castlevania classic style games, for starters you are slow as anything and I've played almost all the castlevania's including the very first when I'm saying that, you get a special backwards jump that is very limited in use outside of getting up certain ledges faster but no chain spin ability which honestly would have saved the pain against the vast myriad of enemies with very awkward hitboxes, it did have special moves with each sub weapon which was great though, enemies at times did waaay too much damage, some had attacks that at times felt impossible to dodge, it honestly felt like a game made with the era of limited lives and passwords for nostalgia's and fake difficulties sake dood.That said it wasn't a bad game by any means but suffice to say I took advantage of the rewind button a few times XD also it felt harder than the versions I've played such as the PSP versions and the more expanded versions, I'd complain saying why it wasn't those versions but well this is the "Advance" collection after all, a sly yet clever move, still now that I'm done I've got to say they've done an outstanding job with this collections, fantastic games, no issues with any of them, if they ever release the DS games somehow I will cry bloody tears of joy as it would complete my collection of personal games I would want from the castlevania series ^-^ thanks for reading and doubly thanks for those with the patience to wait for this piece by piece dood! <3

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great collection of three metroidvanias that would otherwise be lost to time, as well as one curiosity from the super nintendo era thrown in as a bonus. The emulation here is on point and all games benefit from quality of life features like save states, rewind functionality, and a dedicated encyclopedia of all monsters and items. There are even additional 'gadgets' that give you on the fly information on the sidebar, like what cards or souls a monster might be carrying or how many key items are in an area you've been exploring. As for the games themselves:Circle of the Moon - This game almost feels like a step back form Symphony of the Night. Though SOTN is regarded as a classic these days, it didn't sell very well on release and the devs may have been trying to nudge the series closer to it's roots with this one. There are no shops, money, or equipable weapons in this game other than the whip you start out with. Leveling and exploration are still present, but other than the typical exploration abilities the only loot to find are upgrades to magic, hearts, and life. Critical armor upgrades and healing items can for the most partonly be farmed from enemies and are subject to RNG, which can make things extremely grindy at times. This is also the hardest game of the bunch, with enemies soaking up ridiculous amounts of damage and hitting like a freight train, or filling the screen with difficult to avoid projectiles. This difficulty is balanced out with the magic card system, which allows you to combine pairs of cards to create up to 100 different spells. There's definitely a cool factor to this, but due to control limitations and inability to hotkey spells, this can also feel inelegant and cumbersome. Many of the spells are also redundant or underwhelming, providing only minor damage or stat buffs that aren't very worthwhile. The rewind function is the real MVP here, and I would have been hard pressed without it. A good game overall, but may not be exactly what your looking for from a metroidvania.Harmony of Dissonance - This game is much closer to SOTN in terms of systems. Items and equipment can now be found in the environment, shops are back (though a pain to find), and the overall difficulty has been scaled down, making this the easiest of the three. There is also an interesting spin on SOTN's 'two castles' twist, though it does mean you will effectively be exploring the same environments twice. The real standout feature of this one is oddly enough the dash, which is mapped to the shoulder buttons, one for each direction. If you're not rocketing through the castle by mashing the shoulder buttons, you're playing this one wrong. Movement is much more fluid and zippy compared to circle of the moon, and makes exploration in this one a lot more fun. Aria of sorrow - Of the three main games here, this is the one that's 'just right'. It's a little more difficult than Harmony of Dissonance, but not as brutal as Circle of the Moon. It's also the game that comes closest to matching symphony of the night on features, with equipable weapons returning and a shopkeeper who stays put in one place. The soul collection mechanic is also awesome, allowing you to equip a signature attack from each monster in the game as you acquire their soul. This game also has the best designed castle of the bunch. While the previous two castles often felt like generic labyrinths, this one has just enough detail to evoke the 'sense of place' that SOTN did so well. Overall the best game in the package, though it might be the shortest of the bunch.Overall this is an amazing value proposition even at full price, as you get three great games that will likely take around thirty hours combined to complete. The inclusion of Dracula X is just a nice little bonus as well. Thoroughly recommended.

Item Drops are also displayed as weaknesses etc. This is very useful for Circle of the Mooon since it doesn't have one ingameYou also get extra tabs which display Card Combos, Spell Book Combos or Soul Ability depending which game is on  are also a unique feature which helps you out tracking down specific things: - Circle of the Moon: Display info which Monster holds a Card as Item Drop - Harmony of Dissonance: Display for each Area Relics (Blue ?) or/and Room Items (Red ?) - Aria of Sorrow: Display for each Monster if Soul was collected or notI will list now my opinion on each game (+ / - / o)The Game itself doesn't stray too far and offers an experience akin to Symphony of the NightIt features the Card System where you can collect over 20 cards which you can combine and get powerful abilitiesMP is needed to use Card Abilities which differ from each combo. You can still though collect and use sub-weaponsOne thing that you will notice is, that the numbers for stats, health, attack etc. are very high (Max. Cap is 9999)Such high numbers are never seen againAfter completing the game you can play the game again with a different class (Default is Vampirekiller)You can play as a Mage, Thief, Fighter and Shooter with varying stats to enable different playstyles-Good BGM which mixes old and new tracks-Over 100 possible card combinations-Challenging Enemies and Bosses-Battle Arena to test your Skills (Reward at the End)-Replayability with different classes-After defeating certain Bosses, new Enemies spawn in old areas-Lots of Secret Rooms to find-Continue on Game Over Screen to return back in _childDocuments_.review: A better than emulation release. Really impressed by the features that Konami (of all the developers) put on this. From the rewind feature to the save states, to the resolution options, to the achievements to the tips on what monsters drop what and if you've gotten it. They even got rid of alot of the bitcrush GBA sound font on the soundtracks! It's an all around great release that will likely play amazing on Steam Deck which is why I got it, if I don't beat it by then. I am a huge advanced Castlevania fan and felt they did not get enough love and was extremely impressed that Konami, whom I thought forgot the franchise, did such a solid job on this. Seriously, the features and add-ons on this make Nintendo's Super Mario "remaster" release look like babies. If you have never played Aria of Sorrow but enjoyed SotN, grab this ASAP. Easily on par if not better imo than SotN and a lot of people missed on it due to the limited release and minimal press for it. CotM & HoD are extremely solid entries as well and playing them in order of release is well worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: (DISCLAIMER - I don't rate the Dracula X game thrown into this collection, since I haven't played it)Don't be fooled by the fact that these are "mere Gameboy Advance" games, or that they were released before 2005. These are the best Castlevania games you can officially play on PC to date. To keep this review short and informative: all three games are classic Metroidvanias, with open-world design. Great exploration, amazing music, unbeatable atmosphere and ever-evolving movement and combat are found throughout these gems. Every next game is even better than the previous one. My personal rating would be:Circle of the Moon - 8/10Harmony of Dissonance - 9/10Aria of Sorrow - 10/10The last one is a true classic. On par with legendary Symphony of the Night. If you'd want to play only Aria, it's still worth its price, in my humble opinion. To describe the whole collection by modern standards, it would be something like... 2D Anime Bloodborne with more of a fantasy twist? I don't know. Just try it. Let yourself sink into these games, as they are truly brilliant.The PC port is somehow flawed, it always starts in windowed mode - you can press ALT+ENTER to switch to fullscreen. Besides that, the whole package is really good, with clean menus, customizable controls, awesome rewind option, quick saves, in-game encyclopedia etc.Final rating:9/10 - bloody amazing!

_childDocuments_.review: The Gameboy Advance original Castlevania games (all three of which are included in this collection) were, along with Symphony of the Night for PS1 and the DS Castlevania games, some of my favorite video games of all time. When the Castlevania Anniversary Collection was released, I had hoped that we might eventually get the GBA and DS games along with Symphony of the Night and Rondo of Blood released on current-gen multi-platform. We didn't quite get that. Symphony of the Night and Rondo of Blood were both released in the Castlevania Requiem collection exclusive to PS4, but not multi-platform. We did get the GBA games with the bonus of Dracula X (an SNES port of the Turbografx-CD game Rondo of Blood). I was so excited that day one I bought the collection for Switch and a week later, upon getting paid again, I bought it for Steam, too! Aria of Sorrow alone is worth the asking price. If it wasn't for the small map I'd probably rank Aria of Sorrow above Symphony of the Night, making it my favorite video game of all time. I absolutely love the soul drop system that works in addition to the standard rare item drops. Circle of the Moon is a lot better playing on a modern console because you don't have to deal with the ultra-dark screen the original GBA had before the SP was released. The card system was a unique magic system that changed stuff up without changing too much from what was great with Symphony of the Night.Harmony of Dissonance I had kinda a weird experience with. Every time I'd play it I'd start and a good deal of the game played but get totally lost. I finally ended up finishing it after being lost for hours searching for something I missed after 3-4 play-through attempts. I really liked the magic system in this one. It was interesting how they paired magic books with sub-weapons to create different attacks. I was disappointed that you only had the whip as your main weapon, though.Dracula X was the weakest of this collection. It was a watered down version of Rondo of Blood. _childDocuments_.review: Three classic Metroidvania games, games that helped give the genre that title, as well as a bonus game left from the previous set.  I consider this set a must-have.  This generation of 2D Castlevania was my favorite, and I have torn through these games several times.Circle of the Moon:  In my opinion, the weakest of the three GBA games in this set.  The Metroidvania that Iga was not involved in.  The play style almost feels like more of a traditional Castlevania game that they wedged the exploration and RPG leveling aspects in.  At least it has significantly better movement than previous Castlevania games were known for.  The DSS system is interesting, but I think the most flawed of the systems.  There's really no telling what the cards drop from, though figuring out what the combinations do is easy.  One "type" card will always have the same "type", and one "element" card will always have the same "element".  You can extrapolate from there.  Sometimes it's a simple matter of putting one on, and then going out and playing for a minute or so until it triggers, either from walking, taking damage, collecting a heart, etc.  Other times you have to know to use the "item smash" spell combination, the half-circle from down to up and attack.  This set's including of the helper, which pops up on screen if you attack an enemy that holds a card, can be very handy.  It can also be very annoying as it blocks part of the screen.  I do think it's neat that even commercial games have started adding memory checks to the emulators to allow extra features like this.Harmony of Dissonance: I think this is the most underrated of the three GBA games.  It's very well done, a whole lot of fun to play, and a good mix of classic Castlevania (your protagonist uses the Vampire Killer whip), and the open castle exploration.  The helper system in this one is especially useful, as it keeps track of special items in various areas, and lets you know how many are left to collect.  It is unobtrusive, doesn't get into the screen itself, and can help reduce the amount of time spent item hunting come late game.  The game is not without its flaws.  Leveling is problematic as the game has a two-fold system to make levels take longer, first making them cost more exp but secondly by having enemies GIVE less exp based on your level to them.  I dislike double dipping like that.Aria of Sorrow: A widely regarded fan favorite, this one adds the soul collection mechanic, later replicated in function in Bloodstained: Ritual of the Night.  Once more the helper system splashes the information onto the screen, covering some of the game field.  This is another game that knocks it out of the park, though if I'm being truthful I may lean closer to Harmony as being my favorite of the three.  But only by a small margin.  There's a lot to do in this game, and the soul mechanic means each playthrough can be different, depending on what souls you pick up.  Unless you just sit there and grind ones you want or need.All three of those games include post-game content, usually in the form of different character runs.  And all three will certainly satisfy your metroidvania itch.  Which leaves us with the last game.Dracula X.  The SNES remake of Rondo of Blood.  This one feels more like it's been thrown in because they forgot to add it last time.  Or they really felt that they needed more than the GBA games.  It plays more like a traditional Castlevania, with some sluggish controls.  And it certainly has a feeling of cheapness to it.  Especially the final boss, which is fought over an instant death pit.  Something I highly dislike (it leads to slow, boring boss fights).  This one does have a challenge as well in trying to get the good ending by rescuing the pair, if you can find them.  Honestly, the game's not bad, just out of place here.As for the set itself, it includes a gallery, music player, information on the creatures for the GBA games so you can see their stats, drops, etc.  It does not, sadly, have a way to desaturate the colors in Harmony and Aria, which are overly bright to compensate for the GBA's lack of screen lighting.  A minor nitpick in an otherwise remarkable set.

_childDocuments_.review: One of my all time favorites and also the hardest metroidvania, especially if you don't abuse the well known DSS glitch. It even has an optional challenge area that disables using magic. The game is very re-playable, with four additional modes to unlock which are different character builds for Nathan:  starts with every DSS card, but makes the whip weak.  makes the whip very strong, but using magic is not allowed.  has an exclusive homing dagger and makes sub weapons strong, but the whip and magic are weak.  boosts the luck stat extremely high (even at level 1 your luck is higher than level 99 of other modes) and items that normally have low drop rates are easily found, however all other stats are very low.One of the easiest games in the series, not far behind Symphony of the Night. It does have a hard mode, but the game has to be finished once to unlock it. I've beaten this game many times and I still sometimes forget where to go. Using the Konami code to play as Simon Belmont in Boss Rush mode was my favorite part of the entire game. A very solid game, I don't really have any real issues with it. Even if you are going for 100% souls to get the Chaos Ring, it's really not that bad of a grind. This game has a NewGame+ feature and cool hard mode exclusive items to find for your second play through. Boss Rush mode also lets you earn unique items for your save file based on how good your time is.It resembles Rondo of Blood in a few ways, but it's really a completely different game. It's much harder too. If you are the kind of person that loves to do whip only runs, this game is out for your blood. The Dracula fight is brutal without using the axe. Be sure to play the uncensored Japanese version or you will explode into jizz when you die.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not going to beg for [X] game from the series, but Konami... please know we're in LOVE with the 2D Castlevanias! Anyone reading the review, please buy the game so Konami has some push towards releasing another (possible) Castlevania collection sooner. Thank you!Back to the actual review, this collection is a MUST HAVE for anyone who loves "search action" games (metroidvanias). The collection being comprised of Circle of the Moon, Harmony of Dissonance, Aria of Sorrow, and Dracula X. I know Aria of Sorrow was considered to be one of the most well known of the Castlevania games right next to Symphony of the Night, and I can attest to it.Circle of the Moon plays a lot like the original Castlevania formula until you continue unlocking abilities, and the bosses are relatively difficult. If you want a challenge, this one is the one to go for. This game was a launch title for the Game Boy Advance originally. The art style looks nice, but it isn't as detailed as much as the other games. The music is INCREDIBLE, though. Not a ton of plot, but there is a small story to follow along.Harmony of Dissonance is probably the "easiest" of the games. Bosses have weak patterns, your movement and attacks are quite mobile, and you can find yourself becoming OP in no time at all. The soundtrack is pretty crunchy, and the level layout isn't as "linear" as one might hope for, but if you make it past that... the game can be worth a play. The visuals are STUNNING, and I dare say they put too much money into the visuals that some of the other areas fell behind. However, there's lots of items and places to look around. It feels like a collectathon for items compared to the previous game.Aria of Sorrow is a fan favorite. Visuals? Great. Soundtrack? Amazing. Gameplay feel? 10/10. Bosses? Difficult. There's so much to tackle in the game, and the level design encourages you to do SO MUCH without holding your hand at all. The thing that I find super rewarding is the fact that EVERY enemy drops an equippable soul that you use to power yourself up, and that means you have access to equipment and boosts almost CONSTANTLY... yet every runthrough is different because you aren't going to get drops off the same monster at the same point. I'd say this collection is worth it for this game ALONE because of how good it is.Dracula X is a game I don't have too much experience on, but it's allegedly one of the most difficult of the Castlevanias. It is a port of Rondo of Blood, but a "downgraded" one. It's still a good game regardless of how it plays, I'm sure. I just haven't gotten to that one yet.As for this collection in general, the save states are incredibly useful when I want to save before a boss and didn't get to the save room, and just in general. The rewind function is a hit or miss for me because it can help, but I don't want to cheese a fight or avoid a death that I was due in the game. The art gallery is incredible because of how much unreleased and unseen art there is in it, and the music player has EVERY soundtrack from the games. It's been such a nice treat to use these. SO, thank you for putting these in.All I can say is get the game. This is the only way Konami will offer Symphony of the Night or the DS titles or other titles not before seen. And play it so you can enjoy the game thoroughly. That is all. <3

_childDocuments_.review: An overall great collection of Castlevania games. Excellent gameplay, graphics and music across the board on most of the 4 games included. These games all play pretty much exactly how they played on their hardware of origin. Here is my personal ranking on all of them (best to worst):1. Circle of the Moon- Amazing game, one of my all-time favourite Castlevania titles. I really enjoyed the exploration, the card system, the boss battles, and the difficulty spikes (I like my games hard). It  had huge replayability and a lot of secrets. 2. Aria of Sorrow- The majority of people regard this as the best of the GBA Castlevania games, and I wouldn't fault them for it, but I personally prefer CotM. Still an amazing title, though.3. Harmony of Dissonance- The majority of people consider this to be the dark horse of the GBA games, and they're not wrong. Still a very good game, imo.4. Dracula X- It's good. Far from the best Castlevania game, nothing special, but a decent game.My biggest gripe is the inability to rebind the keyboard controls, which are average (using some of the magic items in CotM feels really awkward on the keyboard, the game controls much more fluently on the GBA/DS). I recommend playing this on a gamepad for maximum enjoyment.

_childDocuments_.review: These are excellent games at a great price. However, there are no resolution options, and the game only runs at 1080p. No game is worth your money without a resolution option. You can full screen the game (with alt-enter), but it simply stretches 1080p to your display resolution. Out of the box, there are some annoying configuration settings:- A and B are bound backwards by default, likely because A and B are flipped on a GBA in comparison to an Xbox controller.- X and Y are bound to pause and select. Much more useful to rebind those to an extra attack / jump button for a more comfortable layout and so you don't accidentally pause all of the time.- Hi bitrate audio is a neat idea to soften the distorted GBA sound, but it sounds muddy and muffled. You'll want to turn it off.- There's a terribly annoying "gadget" overlay whenever you attack an enemy. Turn that off! Missing features:- GBA color simulation.- GBA LCD shader with pixel borders. I wouldn't use it myself but it's an easy addition similar to the CRT shader in the anniversary collection.- And of course, any kind of graphics/display settings of any kind. What year is it??I want to support games like these on steam, and I hope we get more collections in the same vein (SOTN, Rondo of Blood, DS games anyone?). However, this collection isn't worth your money yet. Play these games on retroarch with proper resolution support, better input lag, faster UI, and all of the shader options you could ever dream of.

_childDocuments_.review: NOTE: This game was received for free as a birthday gift.The Advance Collection is a pretty good way to play the GBAvanias and Dracula X (if you want to for some reason) without much fussing around. There's a few minor quirks that you might have to get used to, but it's nothing really serious. However, there is one thing that you should absolutely do before you pull the trigger on this...GET A DAMN CONTROLLER. SERIOUSLY DEAR GOD THE KEYBOARD LAYOUT IS GARBO and you can't change it. It's pure evil, I cleared Aria like that and I felt my existence drain away every second.The music player, gallery and little thumbnails for the games in the main menu are also neat. Savestates, rewinding and additional options for the games while playing are a great touch, and states are very cool for keeping order of my saves, too. Very nice feature.High quality audio will benefit practically all of the games, though I've noticed that Harmony seems to sometimes sound better without it. That soundtrack is more of an acquired taste, anyway, so I wouldn't be surprised if you tried to kill the sound in some way, anyway. One thing to note is that you can't change audio outputs in the middle of playing, you have to switch and restart the game. That's like a w/e to me, as I have an interface connected to my lappy all the time, anyway, but it's worth noting.This will run on practically anything from the last 12 years so long as you have enough RAM and a modern version of Windows. It now runs on the Steam Deck too - that's a really great combo for playing on the move.Overall, I really recommend the Advance Collection, but it might be worth it to wait for a sale if this is your first foray into Castlevania.

_childDocuments_.review: 4 Classic games for a good price bundle. Enough info already to justify your purchase; anyway i'll give my thoughts on all 4 games.Dracula X: true classic Castlevania before it went "Metroidvania" style. Hard. Not the hardest platform i've ever played, but rewind feature surely saved me lots of frustration here. Not much to say, it wouldn't shine as a game nowadays, but surely the franchise wouldn't be the same without these grandfathers of the genre.Circle of the Moon: probably my favourite. I've played it a TON back in the days on the GBA. Dark and gritty scenarios, impressive bosses and a neat card system. Difficulty, in my opinion, is perfectly balanced as it slowly ramps up the more zones you access. I can't really find any letdown by this game, as i think it nails down every single aspect. Also memorable tunes which i still think about after 15ish years. (I guess there is a reason if the cover art is the chosen one for the bundle isn't it?).Harmony of Dissonance: what a joke. Super vibrant and colorful headache inducing scenarios, obnoxious and random tunes, melting-cheese butterfried cheese boss mechanics and stupid difficulty overall. Took me something around 3 hours to finish it blind and 1 hour in Maxim mode. This game is like the Meme of Castlevania. I had fun playing it because of how ridiculous it was.Aria of Sorrow: now, fans overall are saying this is the best title in the GBA era, however lots of things imho are just frustrating. Difficulty spikes are all over the place going from one "lategame" zone where you'd gouge your eyes out to another zone which seems like a walk in the park. Overall forgettable tunes, a weapon system which, imho, is just annoying and a soul system which is a cheap copy of CotM with less interesting interactions.I wouldn't put this to the top of Castlevania titles for sure, but certainly more enjoyable, challenging and fun than HoD.Overall the bundle is very worth the price, even without discounts, as all titles are enjoyable in their own way. Recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Circle of the Moon is very challenging and can feel kind of unfair at times, but that helps make the magic system in that game worth using. You won't get very many cards (used in the magic system) through normal play, so you may have to grind for them. There is a handy tooltip included to help you identify which enemies drop cards, which you can turn off if you choose. Has a few additional modes after beating the game for replayability. Harmony of Dissonance allows you to instantly dash in either direction which makes the game feel smoother at first, but the attack animation is a little clunkier than Circle of the Moon. The map design is also much worse. There is an alternate but mostly identical version of the castle that you constantly have to swap back and forth between and the portals to switch castles are pretty far apart, requiring a lot of tedious back and forth. There is a tooltip that keeps track of important items in each area, which helps with the tedium. Aria of Sorrow is the best game here and makes the whole collection worth the price. The map is well designed and allows for a smooth flow of progress while also heavily rewarding exploration. The soul system is basic but fun, allowing you to customize your gameplay through a whole range of special abilities. An optional tool tip keeps track of which enemies have dropped their souls already. Completing the true ending of the game unlocks special modes for replayability. Dracula X is a typical platformer where you simply beat the levels. There are some secrets, such as a few alternate versions of levels and a true ending that requires you to find and free your girlfriend and her sister, but other than that it's a pretty linear game. You have no control over your momentum in the air, and there are many places where you can fall and die if you don't make the perfect jump, so it can take a lot of practice.TLDR; It's worth it for Aria of Sorrow. PS: It has rewind so if it's too hard you can just cheat.

_childDocuments_.review: Castlevania Advance Collection follows up on 2019's Anniversary Collection by focusing primarily on the series' three Game Boy Advance entries. These three games all followed up on the standard set by Castlevania: Symphony of the Night (still conspicuously not on Steam) in their emphasis on large, nonlinear worlds and RPG elements.Castlevania: Circle of the Moon was Konami's such attempt and one of the few made without the involvement of Koji Igarashi. As such, this game is something of a mixed bag. While it is a fun game to explore, it's severely let down by unforgiving random drops for gear, healing items, and even the game's unique DSS cards, with no other way to get them besides grinding. As such, the last few hours of the game are a slog that are alleviated somewhat by this compilation's rewind and save state functions. Not helping matters is that it's clunkier to control than its two immediate successors.Castlevania: Harmony of Sorrow improves upon the controls and introduces a unique modular magic system, as well as the always-fun trope of dimension hopping between two different versions of the same level. Unfortunately, this one is let down by a much lousier castle layout than the other two.Castlevania: Aria of Sorrow is the clear highlight of the collection, improving substantially upon Harmony's castle while also incorporating a very large selection of weapons and spells to employ. It can be a bit grindy, but not nearly as much as Circle of the Moon.Castlevania: Dracula X is a treated as a bonus to sweeten the collection and is as such an outlier, a loose SNES adaptation of Rondo of Blood (also not on Steam). It follows the traditional linear Castlevania style as opposed to the more Metroidvania layout of the rest of the collection, and it does so adequately, even if the difficulty can be a bit much at times.

_childDocuments_.review: Finally a reasonable way to officially have these cult-classic games in your collection, other than purchasing damn expensive cartridges. The collection additionally comes with the UI overlay that consists really helpful QOL features like in-build encyclopedia and save states and unpublished concept arts. The only nitpicky drawback is the games were ported 1:1 with all their well-known glitches.As for the games themselves, to put in short: is like a mid point between the classical (linear) and metroid inspired Castlevania games with a more vertical emphasised and coherent castle design than the later games. It features also more arcade oriented melee combat (no crits, backward dashes) and robust magic system based on combining the randomly dropped attribute cards to create an unique effect, even giving this installment sort of the jRPG vibes. Using them is crucial for staying alive since it's the most difficult position out of the bunch. Speaking of that aspect the game has on of the most memorable foes in the series due to their fantastic and still holding up design and artstyle. Especially when it comes to the bosses. comes with noticeable changes where the most significant is related to the castle itself. Now it consists of two identical, accessible via special portals, layouts differed by themes, bestiary and items. The layouts are interconnect environmentally: one cell change affects its alternate castle version. This "zig-zaging" works pretty well but it would shine brighter if it weren't for the rather bloated level design. The improved movement makes traversing through the castles smoother though. The magic system have been much simplified and arcade-ized since you cast the specified spells by using each sub-weapon coupled with different magic tomes findable throughout the game at the fixed places. This system is fun to use, yet some spells are way too overpowered. Sadly you rather won't have any need to fully utilise them against the odds because even without them the game will rarely cause any difficulty and that's only if you play on the secret hardmode difficulty. improves upon the rest games from the pack especially when it comes to the graphics and animations. From this side it's impressively close in quality to SotN. The same goes for the design of the castle, although there are some stages that are unintuitive to navigate through. Also the story is more developed and interesting than before. The old trusty sub-weapons and spells have been integrated into the ability souls dropped randomly from the fallen foes which adds more variety to this aspect but also significantly increases the need for the monotonous grind since each type of enemy drops a different soul.Attempts have been made here to balance the difficulty (items carrying limit to 9, no crits and slow dash) but still no significant progress in relation to HoD in this matter has been made.Nevertheless, despite the above flaws, it is undeniable that all of the above games are timeless and very playable. Exploring the castle, clearing it of bosses, finding secret items and leveling up player characters is still a lot of fun. And that's all considering the fact that the games are almost 20 years old.

_childDocuments_.review: Let's go game by game, shall we?Circle of the Moon: 6/10. The DSS system is interesting, but some of the cards' drop rates are frustratingly low. If it'll tell you anything - I enjoyed AoS' soul grind more than grinding for these cards. Speaking of grinding - leveling up takes a ridiculous amount of time late game. If you want to do the Battle Arena area you'll have to grind a LOT before you stop falling on your face halfway through (minotaur room, I'm looking at you...). The bosses are alright, so is the map design, but the movement could use some improvement. Pretty decent overall.Harmony of Dissonance: 8/10. Love the idea of two castles. It gets a bit confusing at times (especially if you're rushing for some of the achievements) but it greatly expands the game and gives room for some pretty interesting puzzles. The movement is far better than in the previous game. Lots of cool bosses to fight and the magic system is pretty fun too.Aria of Sorrow: 10/10. My favourite. I've loved it since I first played it a few years back. I 100% it every time. The controls are smooth, there's a lot of weapon variation and the soul system gives a lot of room for personalizing your playstyle. The story gets a bit ridiculous at times (castle? in an eclipse??) but Arikado's here, so I'll take it.Rondo of Blood: ?/10. Didn't really play it that much, only enough to get the achievements, so I'm not gonna speak on it.

_childDocuments_.review: As per my usual thing, I'm reviewing this game after hundo'ing it...sort of. Since the game is actually multiple games together, I'm reviewing it in parts.Part 1 - Harmony of Dissonance.Say what you will about its garish colors, it's still a good game to play. I'm sure there's plenty of people (who are better with words than me) who will defend its honor, so I got nothing else to say about it beside "good game, play if you like Metroidvanias". I got the cheevos (which entails doing almost everything except completing the encyclopedia and map) quite quickly in around 11 hours, but that's probably because I played the game to death as a kid. (Seriously, my DS Lite ate both my carts. D: ) Emulation-wise, I could find no significant faults, which is a relief considering the current market trend of basically churning out shovelware-grade emulations of old games (which deserve excellent, properly done emulations) and pretending the emulation isn't being done abysmally. So, 'well done' to the company that made this port, you did a good job, as far as I can tell.Part 2 - Aria of SorrowFirst, let me just say that getting 100% Souls SUCKS. It's not the worst grind I've ever done, and honestly it's not hard. But it really clashes with the pacing of the game. The drop rate, even with the Souleater Ring, is awful. I made sure not to start farming until I had pretty much beaten the game already, gotten the Claimh and a bunch of other stuff (and the Souleater Ring, obviously), and it still took 4 hours. I would have beat the game in about 5-6 hours-ish except for the soul farming. Ugh. Anyway, beating the game once unlocks Julius Mode, which I beat handily in about 50 minutes despite not really even knowing if I beat this mode as a kid. I mention this because I am genuinely confused how fewer people have beaten Julius Mode than have collected 100% souls in this game. Just, how? It's not a question of skill, because save states and rewind are both available in this game. (Unless you just don't want to use those, which is fair since the original didn't have those.) Anyway, having played this game way too much as a kid (why there's no Warps in the Chaotic Real is question that still echoes in my brain) I can honestly say that this port of Aria is perfectly fine AFAIK.Part 3 - Circle of MoonI've never played this one up until now. I will be brief. It's not the best Metroidvania. It's not the worst either. But you can really tell it was early stuff, genre-wise. The secrets are all largely just HP/MP/Heart Ups. Getting a 100% map clear isn't really needed to beat the game and honestly doesn't feel as rewarding as it does in other games. The magic system is really interesting, but ultimately hampered by the horrendous drop rate, the out of the way placement of where to get the cards, and so on. The movement feels weird at first (especially if you're used to Harmony and Aria), especially the gravity (ESPECIALLY if you're used to Harmony and Aria), but after a while of playing it it honestly felt pretty natural and almost fluid. The double tap to dash wasn't even a problem, though your millage may vary depending on your controller. (My Xbox 360 controller died a long time before starting this Collection. I was using a Stadia controller because I got it for free and I'm too cheap to buy a different controller. It's doing alright so far. Still haven't actually played any stadia games tho. :P I'll get to them, maybe.) But I would still recommend playing Circle of Moon if you want to experience History. The multiple modes of play (reg, magician, fighter, thief) do spice things up, but honestly not enough for me to go for the full 100% of the actual game (for now, at least. I'll give this game a rest and get back to it eventually). I'm settling with giving it a respectful 100% cheevos tho, because it wasn't that bad...especially when Magician mode unlocked the "Collect all Cards" cheevo. (Not really sure if that's a bug or not, but considering it means no farming for the last 2 cards, I'm fine with it.) But I really have to ask: WHY and HOW is beating Magician Mode THE Rarest cheevo for this game collection???Edit: Almost forgot, my recorded time played in Circle of the Moon came to a total of 13 hours, 54 minutes, 56 seconds. That time is  inaccurate as it doesn't include Save State and Rewind shenanigans, which I did use because it was more fun for me to do so. Those features work well, and even helped grind for cards.Part 4 - Dracula XFull disclosure: this is not my kind of game. This is not a Metroidvania. It's more akin to something you'd play in an arcade. Now, my mental abilities and time restrictions are just not up for a "proper" playthrough of this. My reaction speed and reflexes aren't good enough. So, why did I play this anyway? First, for the 100%, natch. But also to study it. I hundo games these days to truly study how the games were designed. And to show them a bit of respect by seeing what they can do. But I also wanted to see what so many speedrunners I've watched have to put up with, control-wise, because there's a huge difference between watching someone play a game and actually playing it yourself. I'd often wanted to know what they were dealing with, and my gosh was I glad I did. The movement, jumping, and even stairclimbing is just...I'm struggling to find a better word than "clunky". It's smooth but also weighty and very full of inertia. Very committal, but you still have a slight amount of air control but with some limited windows to perform it, I guess? And there's so many pits to fall into! If I'd had had to play this normally, with no rewind or save states, I would just not have done it because even I had been on my A-game I'd still not really have enjoyed this kind of game. And probably still not have finished it. But I did play it, and since I had rewind and such, I wanted to see if you can get the Best Ending without getting hit. Judging by Steam's playtimer, it took about 1.6 hours to do that. The game itself looks good, with good art and music. But yeah, not exactly a game that's going to thrill Metroidvania lovers. Unless you also like old-school action platformers. A bit of an odd choice to include the game in with the three metroidvanias, but the inclusion of save states and a rewind feature means even frequently distracted players experiencing health-related reflex and speed issues can at least experience what this game has to offer. Maybe I'll come back and try this "for realzies" when life isn't...well, if you're reading this around the time it was written, you know what it might be.Part 5 - The Bundle ItselfNot skipping ahead, not yet. Just putting this here before I forget: I watched the credits. You should also watch the credits, because there's a nice little mini-game play movie of the 4 main heroes and it honestly is what  washing the taste of "reused assets cash grab" outta my mouth. This collection was already doing a good job at doing that already, by the way, but I'll reserve full judgement until I've finished 100%'ing it. As for the mini-movie, it's not some big production, but it is honestly better made than most similar mini-movie things I've seen in game end credits.

_childDocuments_.review: With this one, I can finally say I completed Circle of the Moon and Dracula X. I had played the four games in emulators, but only finished two.Dracula X - Not gonna lie, I like Dracula X, even with its downsides. Maybe it's 'cause of nostalgia, for playing it over and over on an emulator when I was a teen? Either way, I'm happy for playing it, no matter if it's frustrating at times and that Dracula's fight is total ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ (rewind really carried me there; there's a reaso as to why I never completed DX before, and that fight's the reason)Castlevania: Circle of the Moon - This game sucks. People take a dump on Harmony of Dissonance a lot, but at least that game's fun; Circle of the Moon is not. Every problem that the Game Boy Castlevania Games had is in here, but expanded on and you actually need to grind a lot (or pray for RNG) to even complete the game.Castevania: Harmony of Dissonance - They tried to make a Symphony of the Night in all aspects, but on the GBA. Didn't work on some things, like trying to make everything as big as SotN and not having space for music, or not nothing that we have a second castle on SotN solely for padding (though the reason for the two castles and the constant back and forth is more interesting, though). However, even with all that, Harmony of Dissonance is fun, is slick, and delivers what you want from a post-Symphony of the Night Castlevania. Also, bit of a rant, if the only thing you have to complain about this game is the music and that breaks the camel's back for you, you seriously need a better way to evaluate what's good or what's bad >_>Castlevania: Aria of Sorrow - Aria was and still is quite fun. It rivalizes as a GBA favorite for me, though I think this one takes the cake most of times. The thing with getting the right souls, or even all souls are kinda "meh" (Curse of Darkness and Order of Ecclesia made power-collecting way better), but the small grind is needed only if you want the true ending, and getting all souls really doesn't grant you much (aside from the achievement that wasn't there on the GBA version), so it's not really a big problem. If you want to hit a GBA Castlevania game, this one's the most recommended, and with reason

_childDocuments_.review: Very mixed collection of games, I'll talk about them from the worst game to the best.I hate this game. It's one of the worst games I have ever beaten. Almost everything is awful within it. Starting with the graphics, the game looks dull and even though it has some variety between the environments you'll see a lot of same looking ones. The level design is atrocious, a lot of primitive and lazy layouts, but the worst of all - plenty of copy-pasted layouts, it often look all the same, if not for the map I would often get lost. The progression of your character is almost non-existing. There are dozens and dozens of health/mana/heart upgrades you can find and yet they are so little in power that you barely feel a difference, but the worst of all is that as you make progress game reoccupies old areas with stronger enemies, so you always feel weak and underpowered. The leveling up requires way too much grinding and the game throws so many enemies at you that most of the time I just jumped over them and ignored them. Seriously, there are so many enemies in some rooms and they barely give any XP, killing them would be a waste of time and even if I always killed everyone in my path, I'd still always be underleveled, because of how little XP enemies give and how little leveling up powers me up. The main gameplay is extremely monotomous, the most fun part is looking for secrets. There was one section in the game which I thought was great, the one with harmful blood water. I made it through the whole area and it was awesome, it was the only place in the game which felt both challenging and fair. And yet, I soon realised that I wasn't even supposed to go there yet as in other place you find an item which makes harmful blood water into safe regular water which makes the best part of the game which I played through by accident officially non-existent and vast majority of players probably did not even experience it the way I did. So this game really, has almost nothing good to offer. Now, the magic system. You get a great variety of magical powers, but most of them are too weak and almost useless... What really sucks is that the whole game is RNG based, meaning that the cards you need for magic powers drop extremely rarely and you probably only experience about 1/3 of all the powers the game has to offer. Another thing, the only way to get equipment is from enemies, but again, the drop rate for those items is pathetic, and even if you get some equipment it is pretty poor anyway. Even some of the better equipment in this game is pretty bad and doesn't make much of a difference if you have it or not. One time use items are even worse, they drop so rarely and they are miserable. For example, health potions heal you only 20 HP, but by mid game your health is already over 600 HP and enemies deal about 50-70 damage per single hit and you only get about 15 of those potions through the entire game... And the game also throws enemies that can poison or curse you, those effects stay for quite some time and antidotes are just as rare... Also, you can easily break the game, if you are lucky to have the right cards, you can make some (if not all) bosses effortlessly easy, it proves how broken and crappy this game is. Lastly, the controls are terrible, sometimes the game does not register my imputs, and each action is hard-locked animation, meaning that if you are in the middle of doing it, you can't cancel it or replace with another action which makes the game even harder and more tedious and annoying to play. Like, after you whip, there is still some time till you can do another action, like crouching or jumping and often the inability to perform another action ends in you taking a hit. And speaking of hits... If you take a hit, you are pushed back a long way, half the time you either get thrown into a hole or a trap or into the previous area again, meaning that the enemies you were fighting before all have respawned and have full health again... Fundamentally this game is garbage through and through.2/10Unlike COTM this game looks gorgeous, nice variety in the environments and really nice sprite work. What sucks is that this game is unbelievably cheap when it comes to difficulty. This game is insane at how much crap it pulls on you. They did all the annoying techniques to make this game as unbearable as they could and yet in each level they managed to introduce you to new rage-inducing stuff. You also move very slow in this game. But the biggest travesty is the final boss... Out of all the video games I have ever played in my life, this was the worst boss battle I have ever experienced. The first phase is extremely slow and long, the final boss slowly teleports to random spots and often you don't make it in time to hit him, and while he attacks you in easily avoidable projectiles you have a very slim time lapse to him and I swear, 75% of the time the game does not register my hits on him even though it should. The boss was practically invincible most of the fight and it was easy yet, so long, tiresome and boring. Then the phase two is complete opposite, I can hit the boss whenever I want, but he attacks in such a high pace and very difficult to avoid attacks that you pretty much never get the moment to perform an attack. Other than the preposterous difficulty, the game isn't completely terrible in itself, but it is pretty bad because of it.4/10At first it was wonderful. But after you beat half of it, you get the reveal that the game is double in size and it is in a way copy-pasted, but altered. It felt like such a drag, but at least the alterations were major enough to make it feel quite fresh again. The game has a huge problem of massive backtracking which is somewhat tedious. But everything else is lovely. Visually, this is the best Castlevania game I have seen so far, beautiful vivid colours, massive variety in environments. Magic is fun, controls are smooth. The game is surprisingly easy, the easiest Castlevania game I have played, wouldn't be surprised if it is the easiest in the whole franchise, often it is too easy to take advantage of it and there isn't a hard mode to choose from, at least when I started the game. But I'd much rather have it too easy than unfair, so I'm not complaining.7/10It is strong in every aspect. Everything where COTM fails, this game excels. Music, level design, graphics, combat, controls. Everything about this game rocks. My only complaint is that the drop rate for souls is way too low, or at least they should have made Soul Eater Ring to make odds for soul chance 25%-100% since the ring is extremely expensive. Anyway, I was completely addicted to this game till I completed it.8/107/10

_childDocuments_.review: In case you don't know the GBA games are similar to SOTN. If you are new to the castlevania series it's a good way to get into them as they resemble what we today know as metroidvanias, being that style of game after SOTN they are long. It's going to take a lot of hours to complete them. The last game Dracula X is SNES port of Rondo of Blood not the same game. It's an okay game overall Rondo is a better game. But Dracula X still has it's charm. I've enjoyed it but the main buy are the 3 Metroidvania games and they are perfect.These games are must buy just the best way to experience the games. Even offer improvements over the original hardware in advance games. With the cards being clearly seen and encyclopedia amongst other stuff. It makes tracking cards easier. The games run smoother compared to emulators out there as well. You can also play mods if you follow the guides people have put on the discussion page. A must buy and lets hope that M2 makes more. Considering how cheap these games are you may as well buy them. They offer the best emulation and a better emulation experience you can't get elsewhere. Also available with steamdeck support. Buy it and support M2 and Konami bringing us more of these games. Because we still have lots of castlevania games. Many that are really hard to get a hold of. DS games, Japan SOTN version, Rondo of Blood, PSP version, Castlevania Chronicles, even the PS2 and N64 3D games. It would be good to see them all on steam.

_childDocuments_.review: I was never that big on the arcadie platforming classic versions of castlevania. I loved the theme and lore but was never big on the games them selves. Then came Symphony of the Night, thought it be a game I wouldnt care for but gave it a chance. I was blown away how amazing it was as I always enjoyed the Metroid games and I compared it to that. Obviously I wasnt the only one cause metroidvania was coined up. Going forward I eventually got a GBA and had played all three of these games. I loved the Card system of circle of the moon but overall thought it was symphony of the night LITE. Honestly thought the same for Harmony of Dissonance. Still enjoyed those games very much. Aria of Sorrow however was a interesting twist on the metroidvania and really enjoyed collecting souls. My GBA version however glitched up and my save files wiped and was a sad day for me. Eventually I played the Ones on DS as well and loved those too. Only one I hadnt played was Portriat of Ruin and Never beat Order of Ecclesia.That being said I decided to pick up both this title and dominous collection. I played through all three of the GBA games and although my opinion hasn't changed, I loved all of them. I also loved that it also had savestate feature which made playing them again more enjoyable for me.I may go back to try to 100% Achievement this. But for now I plan to move on to the Dominous.

_childDocuments_.review: I purchased this for Circle of the Moon, its a nostalgia trip and really enjoyably so.For the DSS System if you have one card on both sides of the board, set them for use and exit the menu, press the activation key for it and before the animation finishes enter the menu again and change the cards to whatever you want (even cards you don't have) and you can use those cards effects. _childDocuments_.review: Man, can I just say I love Castlevania? There's a special kind of charm the metroidvanias in particular bring and it helps that there's some good humor in them as well! Juste Belmont is my favorite Belmont just because of how funny he is! The man wanders into Dracula's castle, finds an empty room, and decides to decorate and fully furnish it before besting Dracula, knowing full well the castle will be destroyed afterward.Juste Belmont does what no one else has: best Dracula in combat AND Feng Shui. What a guy! Be sure to give Harmony of Dissonance a spin! My man Juste needs more love!If you're looking to give Castlevania a shot, this collection is an absolute must-have! Start with Aria of Sorrow and branch out from there! Aria's a top contender for one of the best Metroidvanias in this series as well as proving time and time again to be a fantastic game for both veterans and newcomers. Circle of The Moon is a sort of branch between Classicvania and Metroidvania, and Harmony of Dissonance is basically a remix of Symphony of the Night with the most versatile and funniest Belmont in the series. Have fun, everyone, and don't forget to hit Alt and Enter to activate full screen upon bootup.

_childDocuments_.review: Like the previous Castlevania Collection, this PC port does not have any menu or resolution options. You need to press Alt+Enter to go fullscreen and Alt+F4 to exit the game, which is lame. You also can't adjust the volume of the menu music, which may drive you nuts if you're not in a specific game. Still, it is definitely an improvement over the last collection with the ability to rewind, the menus are much nicer, and you can remap the controls right away. The art they include is awesome, with full scans of the original instruction booklets from multiple regions, really cool. They kind of squandered the opportunity for the Encyclopedia to be unlocked through playing the games, and instead it tells you everything you could want to know about the game you're playing right away, including enemy drops and game unlocks. Very spoiler filled if you haven't played these before. It would have been cool to work towards completing the Encyclopedia instead of it showing everything the game has to offer before you even start playing. The music player is really basic but still a great addition.Still, they could have charged more than $20 for this, it's honestly a steal.Konami, please release the Xbox 360 version of SotN with Robert Belgrade voicing Alucard and a port of Castlevania HD on Steam.

But as many have said, Aria of Sorrow is worth the price tag alone. Get this.P.S.Oh yeah, and there is Dracula X. Game is dogwater.

It's a solid collection and the rewind function is awesome.I personally love playing Aria of Sorrow from the smooth animations to the excellent background art, the music is excellent,  and tactical souls was fun. You will have hours of fun either as a new game or new game +. The only thing I didn't like is the soul drop rate, which can be mitigated with a special ring.I surprisingly liked Harmony of Dissonance; like the vibrant yet almost hallucinogenic visuals (it's like Dracula slipped something in that wine), love playing around with the magic system, dashing around is a huge convenient especially for backtracking. The music was weak but let it slide since they admit they didn't have enough time, but if you want to spin it in a different view you could say it matches the dissonance from the title. Overall a good time.I had mixed feelings about Circle of the Moon because of the low drop rates (both cards and items), movement and jumping felt like walking through a muddy swamp, and some of the enemies and bosses can be unforgiving so those cards are a must. But the music was good, the duel set-up system was interesting to play around, the background and sprites are nice to look at.At first I was disappointed that it wasn't Rondo of Blood, but overtime grew to like Dracula X (or Vampire's Kiss).
