_childDocuments_.review: Circle of the Moon gets a bad rap in the Castlevania community, I don’t think this is warranted in the least. COTM is easily one of my favorite’s in the franchise. It may appear simpler than its contemporaries but it just gives it a more classic Castlevania feel with a lighter RPG side. It looks visually great and has high difficulty.The graphics in COTM are a contentious point with this game, I understand why some people might not be fond of them as they are behind its immediate predecessor and its successors. However, viewed as an evolution or merging of the NES/SNES Castlevania art style, I think they look absolutely beautiful.Character design is also on point, all the enemies look fantastic.So musically COTM’s soundtrack is mostly remixes of older Castlevania soundtracks, ; I’m reviewing it as is, in a vacuum.The soundtrack for this game ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ SLAPS, it is easily my favourite castlevania soundtrack several of the tracks are forever engraved into my skullsponge and I hear the on repeat all the time. Some standouts to me are “A Vision of Dark Secrets”, “Awake”, Clockwork”, and “Dance of Illusions”. Though literally every track in the game hits, they did a phenomenal job with it. COTM has really tight feeling controls, everything feels completely grounded and fast and advanced movements and techniques are completely fluid. I have no idea what people are talking about when they say they don’t like them, I just don’t get it.The story of COTM is rather simple and unimportant to the greater lore of Castlevania (as it’s a Gaiden title) but that’s okay, I enjoyed it and liked the characters and plot that exists in the game. So COTM is rather difficult, I’ve seen it ranked in the top 5 Castlevania’s in difficulty on forums more than once. And yeah, it shows. COTM will kick your ass, enemies will ♥♥♥♥ you if you don’t figure out there patterns and almost every single boss will take a few tries at least. I think the most notable Boss would have to be the Twin Zombie Dragons. It's rather infamous and could easily crush an inexperienced casual player’s run. And for a while I felt that it was completely unfair; even after defeating it in previous playthroughs I still held this opinion, however this was the playthrough where I figured it out, there is a strategy involving dodging under the dragons strategically and learning the timing on their attacks. This turns the fight into both one of my favorite and most hated bosses in the franchise. It'll still kick your ass when you know what you're doing but now it doesn’t feel like a slaughter, it’s a battle. (this doesn’t count DSS cheese)COTM also has an enemy variety issue, late game enemies are often reskins of early game ones.The DSS cards were a good idea, they’re easy to understand and can be fun as hell to use; The problem comes when you get to the way they’re acquired, grinding. Oh my god how I hate grinding, the drop rates on some of these stupid ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cards are so low that you could unironically spend an hour killing the same enemy with bad luck.I really wanted to like this game but I struggled with it hard. It’s visually gorgeous as they wanted it to look more like a PSX title than a SNES one and the gameplay can be fun but the music is absolutely atrocious and it has the least challenging gameplay I’ve ever seen in a Castlevania title so far.To start with, the music. It’s horrible, I had to mute the game's audio within an hour of starting. It’s like all the funding got put into the visuals and then they had the intern do the soundtrack in an afternoon. I have nothing else to say.This is HOD’s strongest trait. It is an incredible graphical feat for the GBA and holds up flawlessly. I love the look of every area in the game and some of the graphical effects they pulled off are awesome. However I have one big issue that’s staring you in the face for the entire game, The main character has a permanent non-removable highlight around him that is entirely visually grating. It actually looks like someone scribbled on the screen with a crayola magic marker and I hate everything about it.Story in HOD is actually pretty decent. They have an intriguing plot line related to the fact that Dracula was never supposed to resurrect at this time and some other mysteries that I won't spoil. All in all I’m a big fan of it.So the controls in Harmony of Dissonance are a little bit more loose and floaty this time around, I’m not sure what it is but it’s almost like there’s low gravity at times, though it’s not too bad. There are also additions like sliding in either direction instead of just backwards that I wish were in every title and it can make combat feel really good.However Combat itself feels completely pointless, I died 2 times in the entire game, 2 ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ TIMES. I didn’t even know what I was doing and I still ended up annihilating every single boss and enemy in the entire game because for some reason, in there course correction from COTM’s DSS cards they overcorrected so hard that magic became the single most overpowered thing in the entire game. It’s a really cool implementation and I like it, I just wish that it was nerfed into oblivion. The absence of any sort of challenge makes this game into an absolute chore.AOS is easily the best of the GBA trilogy, It has the perfect blend of the challenge and controls from COTM with the visuals and graphics of HOD, and on top of that it has one of the more interesting stories in the Castlevania franchise (in my opinion)They did a fantastic job on the soundtrack this time around, almost every single song in the game is fantastic with a couple that are just ok, none of the tracks are remotely close to the crap fire that is HOD’s soundtrack though. They nailed the controls in AOS, everything feels completely responsive and smooth. Soma also has a good feeling of gravity to him unlike in HOD, however they removed the left/right dodging and went back to the SOTN system which is a shame, I really enjoyed being able to dodge instantly in any direction in HOD. The gameplay is a lot of fun as well, they returned to the weapon selection system from SOTN and found a balance to make magic fun to use while not annihilating the game’s difficulty. However once again the way you get spells is though grinding, luckily It doesn’t seem nearly as necessary in this game as no bosses really need spells to be defeated; except for 3 specific souls you need to get the true ending, I am not a fan of this but it’s better than the DSS cards.I had some notes about bosses/enemies and whatnot but I’m gonna hit the steam review character limit so whatever.Wow they really hit the ball out of the park here. The game is set in the modern day and we get a whole load of lore and information, I don’t really want to discuss much about the story as to not spoil things however. (expect a returning fan favorite character though))Seemingly using HOD as a graphics base AOS looks just as incredible as ever, I really don’t have much to say that I didn’t for HOD but notably they removed the stupid ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ crayola outline from the main character and it improves the visual experience a lot for me.

_childDocuments_.review: The only game here I've played before buying this collection is Aria of Sorrow. Aria is fantastic game, probably the best successor to Symphony of the Night. It's beautiful and fun and while it's not my favorite in the series (Nintendo DS Collection when please, Konami), it's a solid 15-20 hour game with lots to do. If you've never played a Castlevania game and you start with Aria, you will absolutely not be disappointed. I'm not going to waste a lot of ink recounting praise for the game: it really is quite excellent.Whether Aria alone justifies the full $20 price of the collection is....eh. Depends. I wavered on this for a while. Aria is good, but I'd never played Harmony of Dissonance or Circle of the Moon before and I heard not-so-great things. I decided that since Konami has decided the future of one of my favorite game series' lies in pachinko machines and gacha games, having two new games to play in the series -- regardless of how good they were/weren't -- was better than have no new games to play. Circle of the Moon was....surprisingly entertaining. A lot more than some of the discussions I've read about it implied. It's a strange hybrid of classic Castlevania (your character is slow, jumps are slow with little control once in the air, you have no dodge, and you basically have to really focus on movement and positioning and aiming) and more modern Metroidvania style (an interlocked castle to explore, secrets to find, progressively feeling powered up). There are some notable downsides though, but the new features in the Advance collection do a fair job of reducing some of the worst parts of its cruft. The core gameplay component - the magic cards that you can combine to get different effects like boosting your stats, healing, gaining elemental attacks - are really fun and varied *but* they drop from random enemies throughout the game and if you have no knowledge of them, it's very easy to go through the entire game without ever encountering more than a couple and so your game experience is going to be way different from someone who knows what they are and which enemies drop them and is willing to farm enemies for a bit to get them to drop. The Collection version of the  game both tells you what enemies drop them (and whether or not you have the card already) as well as provides an encyclopedia for what the different combos do. The game is also a little on the harder side compared to Aria and SOTN, but in some ways it feels a bit too much of the "old school unfair" hard rather than a meaningful challenge. But the game comes with save state and rewind functions to utilize if you're feeling the challenge is a bit too much. All-in-all, I had a good time with Circle of the Moon. Enough to clear it a couple of times both on the initial run and then the unlockable alternate play modes that give you different stats and handicaps. The later parts of the castle kind of suck (lookin at you Underground Waterway) and there's very few warp zones and save spots, but I enjoyed it a lot more than I expected to. I imagine the negative reception among series fans is from older kids who played it on their GBA without strategy guides and didn't fully interact with the card system.As a bonus, the soundtrack kind of slapped. Harmony of Dissonance is a different discussion entirely. I'm still working my way through this one but it's a bit more of a mixed bag. Juste feels incredible to control - compared to Nathan from COTN - Juste's back AND forward dashes make him feel like a zippy little gremlin and the fights take advantage of the speed by making you do fun hit and run gameplay. But overall the game is fairly easy (I've beaten most bosses in a single try has they have fairly obvious attack patterns, tells, and escapes), the magic system is fairly overpowered (I've tried not to use it to preserve some element of the challenge), and the castle is deeply repetitive and boring with lots of backtracking and lots of long hallways. The game has some incredible looking special effects and sprite work (for a GBA game) but because of that, there wasn't much space on the original cartridge for music so the game makes use of chiptunes rather than actual sampled music. Some of them are quite catchy, but sadly very repetitive and I've found I've started to mute the game lately if I spend a long time in an area. One common area of complaint is with the visuals and the color choices and you know? They don't make a great first impression, especially if you're used to the usual design aesthetics of Castlevania games. But in retrospect, after playing Harmony for a while and then going to play Aria of Sorrow, I found myself missing the vivid hues and unique color choices. I don't always think it works in some areas of the game, but overall the aesthetic grew on me. It felt unique, makes the game stand out compared to its siblings, like Castlevania through a vaporwave fever dream filter. There are ways to mod it for a more subdued, "normal" Castlevania color palette (check the game's guides for a good tutorial) but the visuals grew on me and they might grow on you too.Overall, it's not a *terrible* game and it is memorable. It certainly stands out both in visuals and with some of its gameplay decisions (like having almost no secrets and hidden rooms), but it is disappointingly easy and navigating the cramped, repetitive castle gets old quickly. Play it if it interests or you want to see the badass granddad from Castlevania: Nocturne in his prime, otherwise it's totally skippable. There is a 4th game, Dracula X. It's....okay. Fairly solid old-style Castlevania platformer. I just wish Konami put Rondo of Blood (for a long time, a Japanese-only game) instead as there's still no way for PC players to play it (legit) and honestly, Rondo is much better than its erstwhile remake. If you're a longtime fan of the series, you probably have ROMs of these games already so whether or not its worth it will be up to things like achievements or the extra features. If you're a newcomer, maybe drawn in by the Netflix show, this is an okay deal. $20 for a great game, a fairly solid game, an okay game, and a meh game isn't really that bad of a deal in the long run.

_childDocuments_.review: Cream of the crop here with 3 fantastic titles each taking heavy influence from the fantastic Castlevania: Symphony of the Night. Oh and also Dracula X thrown in for a taste of a more classic Castlevania experience (why not include Rondo of Blood instead of this version? They have a port on Playstation 4 now ... but oh well.)Not counting Dracula X, you still get 3 amazing games here all presented with welcome quality of life changes such as in game trackers, a built in save state system, and a "rewind" feature. Yes the rewind can be used to trivialize the games, but I would encourage players to use it mostly to help combat with some of the more grindy aspects of the game (looking for certain item drops or cards I think is a fair use of it). If you are new to the series I would recommend starting with Harmony or Aria before Circle of the Moon as they are easier experiences overall. Beyond that there is not much else to say. This is prime Castlevania and anyone that has enjoyed other Metroidvania style games will get more than their value here.PS: Konami please release the DS Castlevania titles as well in another collection. Maybe include Rondo of Blood with that to make up for Dracula X here. Also why not just release Smthony of the Night as well on Steam? Yeah I know there are a million ways to play it, but it would be nice to have nearly every Castlevania game in the series in one spot with achievements and quality of life features. Oh, and maybe do a 3d collection? Include the 64 games and the PS2 games on it? Please Please...Achievements: For the most part they are quite merciful here and there are only a few grindy ones. Use a guide, but for the most part almost everything is unmissable which allows you to enjoy each experience at your own pace. Dracula X achievements can easily be done in one short playthrough as well so you don't have to linger on that game too long if you don't want to.
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Advance Collection

_childDocuments_.review: There are approximately zero BAD Castlevania games on either the GBA or the NDS. They are all gems of various qualities.Aria of Sorrow in particular is one of the finest games ever created.  It took everything that made SotN the classic that it is.. and improved upon every aspect of it and added the amazing Tactical Soul System as the cherry on top.  It's a little too soon to judge this specific port, but the mere fact that the GBA titles are no longer locked away on dead hardware where only retro collectors and emulation fans could access them is a huge, huge win in my book.  Konami finally took a breather from pachinko machines long enough to finally give us this collection, so I'll happily fork out my $20 and encourage everyone else to do the same....cuz we NEED Konami to give us the NDS titles next!
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Advance Collection

_childDocuments_.review: A decent-enough port of three GBA games and one single SNES game that nobody really asked for.Circle of the Moon, Harmony of Dissonance, and Aria of Sorrow are three excellent Castlevania games that all deserve a playthrough if you enjoy the Castlevania formula. They feel much larger than you might expect a GBA game to feel, and although each one really only takes about ten hours to get through, they are all fun and great games to spend some time on.

_childDocuments_.review: Good emulation for good games. Ratings are on a GBA scale.CotM is a heavy 9/10 The story is fun, the bosses are hard, and the mechanic is unique and engaging. This was my first GBA game when I first bought the console as a kid so I have a bit of a soft spot for it, but its still a fantastic game.HoD is a decent 6/10There's nothing really special about Harmony. The art style can be really grating, the music isn't great/memorable, and nothing about it really stands out for me.AoS is a light 8/10Aria is pretty much what people point to when they want to talk about the GBA or Symphony-esque Castlevania games, and there's good reason for that. The story has good depth, the environments are varied and don't get too stale, and the bosses are well done. I don't think I like it as much as CotM because I feel they didn't do it justice until the DS sequel, but its still very worth playing.EDIT I have played "the ROM they threw in with it" and it has to be one of the hardest sidescrollers I've ever put myself through. Took me an entire day to finish.

_childDocuments_.review: A good Castlevania collection. It includes all the gameboy advance games plus Dracula X from the SNES. The graphics aren't so good for today standards, but the gameplay and the music are excellent. Dracula X plays like a classic Castlevania, while the gameboy advance ones play like Metroidvanias. _childDocuments_.review: There's nothing wrong with the games themselves, aside from Harmony of Dissonance's notorious attempt to make the game elements readable on the original unlit GBA screen. They run well and play well. Aria of Sorrow alone is worth the price of entry. As a nice touch, all of the QoL features (such as rewind) can be disabled.I was a bit surprised that they included a classic Castlevania game in what would otherwise be a collection of Metroidvanias. But, as they only made three GBA Castlevania games, it was certainly a nice surprise to get something extra.As for the launcher/emulator, I have only some minor complaints:The game doesn't start in fullscreen and the only way to switch it to fullscreen is to hit alt+enter.There's no option on the main menu to quit the game, and you can't quit using a controller. You need to hit the esc key.The games don't default to pixel perfect mode, you have to set that yourself. Per game. The ability to set the default mode for all games would have be nice.The one SNES game doesn't have an NTSC filter available.The optional background image doesn't fill the entire screen in pixel perfect mode, leaving you with slivers of the black bars the image was supposed to cover up.All in all, I'd give this an 8/10. Higher if Konami fixes these issues.
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Advance Collection

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know why there isn't a full screen option.  The other Castlevania collection has the same problem.  Aside from this one thing, it's great.  Some all time classics that have been expensive for quite a while.  Aria of Sorrow in particular is excellent, and Circle of the Moon is the weird stepchild that you love despite its flaws.
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Advance Collection

_childDocuments_.review: M2 continues to deliver the very best in these classics reissues, providing numerous ways to play, resources, updates, and loads of goodies for series fans. DO NOT SLEEP ON THE GB ADVANCE ENTRIES IN THIS SERIES. An added highlight is this looks crisper and cleaner than emulating the gba, making it even more worth the price. Branching off as the weirder and sometimes more interesting and even arguably better younger brothers of Symphony of the Night - these are a sometimes forgotten or unviewed highlight in Castlevania and Metroid-vania's at large.

_childDocuments_.review: You can't go wrong with old Castlevanias. Actually I never played Aria of Sorrow and this was the one I started playing when I bought the Advance collection. This game is incredible. Finished it quickly but what a fun game!Circle of the Moon was still one of my favourite Castlevania "metroidvania" style but I don't know how I kept my sanity back in the day I was younger, since the game forcing you to double tap a direction to run is freaking annoying. You'll mess it up badly many times because of this.Harmony of Dissonance is also a really cool game but I'm keeping this one for the last of the three.You also have Dracula X which is a cool classic vania game and somehow hard as hell in some levels (hello stupid cave level and its boss!).But overall, this is Castlevania so it's good! :)
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Advance Collection

_childDocuments_.review: First off, let me start by saying that I absolutely love these games. All of them. The games themselves are not bad and finding physical copies of them is getting tougher. Purchasing this collection will give you a concise way to play all of these games. You should definitely know that you are getting emulators, and not the best ones at that. I didn't have any issues with Harmony of Dissonance, however I had issues with saves in Aria of Sorrow. I would save but then come back to my game and the last save that I made just never seemed to have saved. I struggled with hit detection in Dracula X and that was extremely frustrating. A lot of people pine for this collection to have Rondo of Blood and Symphony of the Night. _childDocuments_.review: Circle of the moon is not a masterpiece. There are flaws. The cards should be guaranteed, perhaps after bosses--perhaps in secret rooms. They should not be tied to .0000000000000000002 drop rates or whatever.If it weren't for that, it would be the stand out. Critically was well received at the time of release,  yet slowly fell from favor due to the issues with drop rate for important items, difficulty, a change in development studio and director (often entries in series that switch dev teams are attacked by dumb nerds despite being inventive, so this criticism is to be expected, but irrelivant), and technical issues with the GBA's ability to showcase dark environments. The last issue isn't important anymore on modern screens and what's left is one of the more beautiful castlevania games. Excellent music. Combat that is both technically simple and engaging. A fusion of the old school NES + SNES castlevania games and the modern metroidvania format--your protagonist is *slow* at first (eventually you can run.) His whip has a delay on it, like in the beloved Castlevania IV. It's the best of all of them, will take you the longest to complete, and gives you exactly what you're looking for in a game about a whip-wielding vampire slayer.Aria of sorrow is fun, but so easy, and very short. Harmony of Dissonance was always forgettable to me when I played it on an emulator, but I do remember it was also incredibly easy. These are not bad games. I do enjoy them thoroughly. They're just not my favorite.Highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: I got Circle of the Moon about 20 years ago, along with a shiny new Gameboy Advance, and in 2022, I'm playing Circle of the Moon again on a Steam Deck. You also get Dracula X, but we don't talk about that game.  All in all, only get this if you are like me, strangely nostalgic for life 20 years ago and able to get it through retrogaming.  there are certainly better games in this genre nowadays, from Hollow Knight to Bloodstained, but for the nostalgia kick, and the quality of life improvements, there's nothing better than this.  Tight gameplay, awesome music, memorable challenges, all in this package, but the biggest reason to buy this? Nostalgia.

_childDocuments_.review: This package include some of the best GBA games and true representatives of the Igavania genre.The jewel in the crown is , which is arguably a better game than , although it may not have the same impact and defining status as the PSOne classic. Nevertheless,  alone justifies the time and money invested in this collection, as it is one of the top 5 GBA games. However, If time permits, I recommend playing the other two games from the GBA trilogy before diving into Aria to fully appreciate the genre's refinement over time.Aria presents a captivating story set in a futuristic setting, complete with intriguing plot twists. Moreover, the gameplay introduces a unique soul system mechanic, wherein Soma can absorb the souls of defeated enemies, granting him a diverse range of new skills and abilitiesIn terms of settings, choose the pixel-perfect option in the display settings for the best fidelity. This option enhances the visual experience and ensures that the game is faithfully represented. Unfortunately, language options are only available in the European version of , allowing players to choose between English, French, or German at the start of the game. The other games are only English or Japanese.While this collection is praiseworthy, I must express my disappointment with the absence of the three DS games and the inclusion of , which is essentially a downgraded SNES port of . Including the DS games would have made this collection a true Igavania collection, and a much more valuable package. However, I understand the value of that inclusion as a preservation effort, since it's a game not available in the Anniversary Collection. Here's hoping Konami release a DS collection in the future, perhaps including  (that weird remake of the first game of the franchise) as a side game.Overall, this collection serves as an excellent entry point for those new to the metroidvania genre, and it offers enough content to keep players engaged and entertained. PS.  is available on every PlayStation platform and every Xbox since the 360, as well as Android and iOS. It's not ideal, but it is widely available on modern platforms to play officially. I would love a Steam/Switch port of the Requiem bundle, but it is not hard to legitimately play Symphony. PPS. Play  if you love  and . It is a prime example of a modern Igavania game.

_childDocuments_.review: If you always wanted to play the GBA Castlevanias, this is certainly a convenient way to do it. This collection contains 4 games along with some extras, and features that everyone expects nowadays (save states, etc.) Here's a quick rundown of what you get:Castlevania Circle of the Moon, despite being retconned for a few years back in the day, is a very significant game as the first portable IGAvania, as well as the game which helped sell the GBA in the first place. Think of it as Symphony of the Night in Richter mode, only more difficult. For that reason alone I almost prefer it to the admittedly very easy playstation classic. Also, unlike the GBA original, you don't have to be on the surface of the sun to see what you are doing; the original version was WAY too dark, but perfectly playable here. The soundtrack is also a technical marvel. The story sucks, but plot never mattered much in Castlevania anyway.If Circle of the Moon is a more difficult Richter mode, then Harmony of Dissonance is a more tedious take on Alucard. Similar to playing as Dracula's son back in the day, this game is laughably easy, only they have removed alot of the save points, which just makes things more annoying, and created a new spin on the 2 castle gimmick which serves no real purpose. The music also takes a hit; while well composed, the instrumentation can be grating on the ear. Still not a bad game mind you.Aria of Sorrow is the true classic of the collection: this is the first post SOTN game to successfully step out of that game's shadow. Also, unlike its inferior sequel it isn't tethered to using a stylus or other console-specific gimmicks. This is likely to be the game you spend the most time on of the three. Castlevania Dracula X is a neat extra that depending on the region is either considered an inferior port or sequel to Rondo of Blood. It is quite stiff and unforgiving to be sure, but still a competent old-school castlevania game. Overall, it's hard to complain about what you're getting here, but whether some old gameboy games are worth the price is up to you.

_childDocuments_.review: Thankfully, when Konami stopped making proper (aka 2D) Castlevania games for consoles, they kept right on making them for handhelds. Any Castlevania fan owes it to themselves to play these games.  Hopefully, this release will be popular enough to see a DS-games Castlevania release in the future.  This collection is not perfect.  The lack of full key and controller rebinding is inexcusable.  The QoL features are nice when they work, which is only sometimes.  But it plays right, the games feel right.  It makes the Steam Deck feel like a giant GBA.  Compared to how badly some other ports have been botched, this collection is very acceptable.

_childDocuments_.review: The Castlevania Advance Collection is a roller coaster of great highs and steep lows. As a fan of the series since 2015, I've grown to love and hate some of the games offered here, and what we have makes the complete package a mixed bag. For a more concise analysis, I'll be discussing the games individually from what I think are best to worst.Aria of Sorrow is one of my favorite games of all time and the sole reason why I bought this collection. The graphics are perfect balance of pleasing spritework and smooth animations and the soundtrack is great for GBA standards. While not as complex as Symphony of the Night, AoS is a perfect jumping point for new players as well as veterans with its tight controls, plethora of customization through the soul system, and a learning curve for advanced techniques. It doesn't matter if I'm playing casually, going for 100%, trying the randomizer or roguelike, or breaking the game via the speed run route, I could play this game a billion times and never get bored. Easy 10/10 and a must-play for anyone interested in the genre.Circle of the Moon is one of those rare games I don't know how to feel about. In short, CotM is great when you're playing the game in any fashion that is not the intended experience. Trying to play this game as originally designed is frustrating because of the steep difficulty spike about halfway through on top of there being no equipment for you to find outside of enemy drops. Armor, accessories, healing items, and DSS cards are all tied to the abysmally low enemy drop rate, and with the game's high difficulty, a first-time player is expected to grind away for hours just to stand a chance in the next area. But here's the kicker, when you're breaking the rules, the game somehow becomes infinitely more enjoyable. When I'm trying out the randomizer, using the DSS glitch, or making Nathan the embodiment of nuclear radiation, I'm genuinely having a great time. In my next playthrough, I'd love to learn how do some out-of-bounds tricks because breaking CotM has been one of the most fascinating experiences I've had in a video game. I'll be damned if try to play this game legitimately again, but at least I have a reason to come back time and time again. The graphics check out for a GBA launch title and the music is probably the best in the trilogy. 6/10 if you're playing the intended way and 8.5/10 if you're using glitches or other tools.Harmony of Dissonance use to be my least favorite game in the franchise. It still ranks very low on my Castlevania totem pole, but my most recent playthrough helped me appreciate what HoD was going for. I use to hate the Spell Fusion system because you had to pause the game to change spell books, but when I learned that you can switch elements by holding up and one of the shoulder buttons and switch to your subweapon by holding down and pressing both shoulder buttons (the game does not tell you this), combat became much more engaging. Boss fights benefited the most from this trick as I was constantly swapping spells like I was switching styles on a Devil May Cry game, even though HoD are laughably easy. It sucks that you can only hold one subweapon at a time, but I didn't mind experimenting with everything even though the cross was the best choice in every scenario. If I'm going back to this game, I'd like to give the boss rush a whirl now that I know I can swap spells on the fly. The presentation is by far the weakest of the trilogy in both graphics and music. I'm aware of HoD's development history and why the music sounds weaker that CotM, but AoS struck a great balance with graphics and music whereas this game's focus was the graphics. Speaking of, that didn't age well either. Most of the environments are very pixelated and most of the animations (especially on Juste and Maxim) look unfinished. I believe the Advance Collection dulled the brightness in a few rooms to make the game easier on the eyes, but the clown vomit final boss room was certainly not one of them. The copious amounts of backtracking and vague means of progression are also a knock against the game, not helping that there are two castles and you swap between both constantly. 5/10 but I'm at least satisfied learning that combat was better than I remember.Dracula X is the worst Castlevania game I've played. Even as a bonus, this inclusion feels like a joke. The level design is brutal, often unfair and the obtuse steps you need to take for the best ending are ridiculous. The final fight against Dracula is without a doubt the worst in the franchise, who in their right mind thought putting bottomless pits in the arena was a good idea? You have to take your time and lame him out with the axe, there is literally no good alternative. It's ironic to me that Dracula X, I least favorite classicvania, is suppose to be an SNES conversion of Rondo of Blood, my favorite classicvania. They are not the same game, far from it, but elements I enjoy in Dracula X are done better in Rondo. For example, the presentation: Dracula X looks and sounds great for SNES standards and the conversion is nothing short of masterful, but Rondo of Blood (in my opinion) has the better aesthetics and soundtrack. There's nothing here for me to enjoy that hasn't been done in a much, MUCH better game. 3/10 go play Rondo of Blood.As a whole, I think the Advance collection is worth your time despite some of its weaker parts. I may not like Harmony of Dissonance, but I know several people who do and you could be one of them too. I'm just saying as someone who loves the peaks of this franchise, the Advance Collection is a decent buy, although I wish the DS games were included to balance out the overall quality.

_childDocuments_.review: A great collection of titles in which Castlevania transitioned from an action platformer to the gameplay style which helped to jointly coin the term "Metroidvania". In addition, unlike the previous Castlevania collection, this release features several helpful enhancements, such as a rewind feature and, most crucially for me, visual aids showing collectables that have yet to be picked up, massively streamlining 100% completion, while still letting the player discover the items' locations on their own. One word of advice: leave Aria of Sorrow for last if you're playing all of these for the first time, you'll thank me later.

_childDocuments_.review: I kind of have a love hate relationship with these games. They have fair share of frustrations, but it's really in relation to them being made after Super Castlevania 4 when they decided to get rid of the 8 direction attack with the whip. It just seems like a downgrade rendering you helpless to deal with the unfair challenges. I cheated to beat Dracula x because of how unfair it was. Dracula X makes Rondo of Blood look more forgiving and I beat that game despite how hard it was. What I also found kind of disappointing with this second game collection was it didn't include Rondo of Blood or Symphony of the Night since they were both very popular Castlevania titles, but those are just nitpicks. The replay value isn't as high as other games, but they're classic so I'm a little easy on it. However most of my criticism is aimed primarily towards Dracula X. Harmony of Dissonance and Aria of Sorrow on the other hand are amazing to play. I still have to play more of Circle of the Moon (played it didn't like it).  If you're looking to bring back old memories or looking for a classic horror side-scroller to play during the Halloween season this is the game collection for you.

_childDocuments_.review: While not as robust of a collection as the Anniversary Collection, the Castlevania Advance Collection is more about quality over quantity.  Three super solid games (Four if you have nostalgia for Dracula X/Vampire's Kiss).  There are also more modern features included besides the addition of save states (which we now have 10 of, instead of the previous 1).  Konami added the rewind feature which is a great for new players looking to learn the games as well as players looking to get into speedrunning any of the four games in the bundle.  Circle of the Moon:  For a launch GBA game, this one holds up really well.  The cool thing about this game is you can treat as either a Metroidvania or a Classicvania game as most of the extra exploring in this leads to items like HP/MP/Heart Maxes.  The only complaint I would have about this game is how low the card drop rate can be, but there is an infamous glitch to get around that.Harmony of Dissonance:  Am I the only one that finds it weird that this is the only Metroidvania entry in series that has a Belmont as the main character?  Sure Richter is playing in games like SotN and Portrait of Ruin.  There's also Julius Mode in Aria/Dawn of Sorrow, but those are unlockable modes.  Either way, this one has a cool twist to it.  You explore two castles that have the same layout, but have different items in locations and the narrative has a cool way of explaining it.  Aria of Sorrow:  To me, this is the pinnacle of the Metroidvania CV games.  Everything they started in SotN is fleshed out here.  Also really cool plot revelations too.  I want to keep it short because this game is the main selling point of the collection.Dracula X:  While I appreciate Konami throwing us an extra game in here, I don't get why this game was included.  I've never been a fan of DracX or Rondo of Blood.  I find them extremely boring since my introduction to playing Richter was in SotN and all the gameplay options he has there are not present in his previous games.  Combine that with no nostalgia for either game and I'm left feeling unimpressed.  If you played either game as a kid, I'm sure you'll find some fun in them.I truly hope Konami does a few more Castlevania Collections.  I hope a DS collection (Dawn of Sorrow, Portrait of Ruin, & Order of Ecclesia) is in the works as well as a 3D-Vania bundle (CV64, Legacy of Darkness, Lament of Innocence, Curse of Darkness).  But the big one is definitely a Rondo of Blood and Symphony of the Night bundle.  They've already released them as the Requiem bundle on PS4 (and SotN can still be purchased on XBLA for Xbox users), so let's hope they do the same for PC.  Lastly, I want to say that Castlevania: The Adventure Rebirth needs to included in one of these bundles as it was (to my knowledge) the last Classicvania game was produced and it's really solid.  Even if Konami did a Rebirth bundle w/ Gradius, Contra, and Castlevania Rebirths, I'd be down to clown with that.

_childDocuments_.review: Due to Konami's actions of late, I didn't plan on buying this, but seeing it suddenly pop up, seeing some games I missed playing, I couldn't say no. No where near as good as Rondo of Blood which this is a port of. However the major saving grace for this title is the new features of rewinding game play, and game saving. So many of the bad port decisions no longer have to aggravate you as much as they did in the past, and it becomes a much easier to complete game in just a couple of hours. I just wish this was the full original game's experience, and I don't know why it's here as it never got a GB Advance release like the others did. Would make more sense to get Rondo on here as it at least had a recent hand held release (though also not for Advance).

_childDocuments_.review: Advance collections features the gameboy advances castlevania plus Dracula X aka vampire kiss from the snes.I've done both circle of the moon and Dracula X before on their original release buying this collection so my main focus was to get to play Harrmoy of Dissonance and Aria Of sorrow.from what I understand and remember Dracula X is a reimmagination of Rondo of blood but for the snes with a similar soundtrack and monster design yet a very different level design and boss fight , it"s a pretty hard and with it's only big flaw is having a ridiculously hard final boss fight on which the second phase has hole you can fall in and die instantly.Circle of the moon is fun but it's not very memorable beyond it's magic system and it's look meh , even for a gameboy advance game.Harmony of dissonance has a fast paced gameplay great control but has a castle which can be frustrating to navigate and the game tend to be easy once you've figure out it's very easy to stack an insane ammount of healing items because the game allow you to hold 99 items of each type and grinding money just require a bit of patience in order to buy both 99 potions and 99 high potions from the wandering merchant.Aria of Sorrow is the best game in this compilation , it's visually look great despite the low resolution thanks to it's well done sprites artwork using the gameboy advance color palette to it's best , the difficulty is also much more balanced then harmony of dissonance since you just can't pack an insane ammount of healing items. it's also got a decent map where you can figure out where to go without getting lost , yet the castle itself is still large and will take you hours to fully explore , especially if you're aiming for the "true ending".

_childDocuments_.review: Going to break down my review for each game and then give an overview of the collection as a whole.---Castlevania: Circle of the MoonThe overall feel and gameplay is solid. The core gimmick is the DSS "card" system where you take 1 of 10 action cards and 1 of 10 element cards and combine them to get unique abilities / effects. It is a bit much and could have been streamlined down to maybe 6-7 and 6-7, as a lot of the combinations are silly and/or completely useless or outshone by other choices. Still, it is fun and allows for exploration and some interesting discoveries for such an old game.The level design is average and while you do have to backtrack a bit it isn't that bad and overall it is fairly straightforward, especially if you use a color coded map guide.The main problems of the game are the sheer difficulty and punishing nature of some enemies / bosses, with attacks that are nearly impossible to dodge or deal with. Luckily, that is largely mitigated with the collection's "rewind" ability, but it is still frustrating at times. An even bigger problem is the weird drop rate and somewhat walling of advancement behind leveling up or farming. You can technically beat the game at low level, no items, with no cards, but realistically you need to farm some enemies to get XP / drops / cards to have an OK time progressing. It really locks you behind farming enemies for drops or XP for a while, which was probably done to pad out gameplay length, but in modern designs just feel like a slog at times. The "rewind" system does help where you can kill an enemy, check for a drop, and instantly rewind to just before you kill it to "re-roll" the drops over and over (just make an attack in between to advance the in-game RNG counter). Still clunky and time consuming, but makes it at least manageable. Finally, some enemy designs are just boring and/or frustrating. The end boss (Dracula, surprise surprise) is very boring and straight forward, while some bosses like Zombie Dragon have just weird attack patterns and a ton of health that makes it a slog.All things said the game isn't bad, but isn't great, and definitely shows its age.Rating: 6/10---Castlevania: Harmony of DissonanceFor nearly every step forward over Circle of the Moon, it takes a step sideways and a step back. The feel is very "floaty" and a bit unresponsive. Instead of being able to see the enemy name, the damage you're dealing, and other basic UI things, you have to unlock them -- which isn't a big deal as you can get them in the first 30-45 minutes, but it just seems odd. The core gimmick in this game is the "sub weapon + elemental spell book combo system" which feels worse than the DSS system from Circle of the Moon. While the DSS system was bloated and this a bit more streamlined, it relies on certain sub-weapons and means you can't easily change or adapt, you have to backtrack and find the sub-weapon to activate the ability you actually want. Ugh.Difficulty wise the game is much more forgiving and feels more fair (sometimes too much so), although bosses are somewhat even more bland at times which makes the whole thing a lateral move, or even slightly back, instead of something better.The biggest problems though, outside of the floaty feel and more "zoomed in" perspective (both which gives less overall control), is the level design which is pretty horrendous. You're backtracking often with little idea on where to go and sections are blocked off until you reach certain new powers without much rhyme or reason. It is VERY frustrating to have to backtrack huge amounts and check every place you haven't explored yet on the off chance you can now explore it with your new power up (as it isn't labeled what you need and where even if you're seen it)... which often isn't the correct one so you're just backtracking even more. The premise of "two maps that are the same but different" is neat, but it is just really poorly executed here. Really, really bad level design choices all around.Rating: 5/10---Castlevania: Aria of SorrowCircle of the Moon walked and Harmony of Dissonance crawled so Aria of Sorrow could run. While not as good as the DS titles to follow (Dawn of Sorrow / Portrait of Ruin / Order of Ecclesia), this is a solid game with a lot of great stuff held back by a few really odd and bad decisions. Controls are much smoother and tighter, and the camera view is zoomed out enough so you can actually appreciate the levels while dodging enemies and more. General movement is much more reigned in -- there's only a back dash and you only get a good movement speed ability ultra late into the game -- which feels more limiting.The concept of "every enemy has a soul you can absorb to get a special power" is super neat, but most abilities are meh, and the drop rate for some are INCREDIBLY low. While not a big deal for someone casually playing, it is very frustrating when trying to 100% the soul collection. Even with the "Soul Eater'' ring (which increases the odds of getting souls at the cost of 300k gold, or like an hour or so of farming gold), it only makes it barely acceptable. If the default drop rate matched having a Soul Eater ring and the Soul Eater ring gave even more it would be okay, but the sheer amount of farming one has to do significantly hurts the game. However, you can use the “Rewind” system here to reduce the farming, but even then it is a bit brutal (again, remember to attack the air in between resets to advance the RNG counter).Weapons are better and generally more varied, but some are just leagues above others, which makes a lot of the decisions not really meaningful. Finally, while the general flow and difficulty is good, some bosses are fun and others just boring. The variance between enemy design leaves a sour taste. A good experience, but overall not the best it could be, but the best for this collection.Rating: 7/10---Castlevania: Dracula XEw. This review is getting long enough so just skip this game. It has some good music at times and the backflip is cool, I guess?Rating: 2/10---Castlevania Advance CollectionThe collection itself is decent and the improvements / additions are generally very positive, but the individual games have ups and downs. The ability to "rewind" time dramatically helps with antiquated difficulty, level progression, and drop rates. Without that option the whole collection would have been significantly worse. It also allows for saving anywhere, an in-game encyclopedia of drops / monsters / other things, and some other tiny add-ons. Definitely a good improvement that helps smooth over the rough edges.Overall, the collection is okay and is a nice trip down memory lane, but just be warned on what you're getting for better or worse. Recommend it, but probably wait until it is on sale, unless you really want to experience nostalgia head on.Rating: 6.75/10P.S. One can only hope they come out with a "Castlevania DS Collection" where they really learned from the GBA games and made some decent titles.

_childDocuments_.review: The tldr for this review is strong The Castlevania Advance Collection comes with the three GBA Castlevania games - Circle Of The Moon, Harmony of Dissonance and Aria of Sorrow - as well the SNES Dracula X as a bonus.  The "Collection" itself acts as an emulator of the original games ( including all regional releases of CoTM, HoD, AoS, DX ) allowing for some quality of life additions like save states, pause/rewinds, and additional glossaries and trackers for collectables. There are also separate galleries for artworks and music for all titles included.Each of the games included behave exactly the way the originals did. All glitches and tricks remain intact along with a few new ones introduced by the nature of the Collection's emulator. The only downside for speedrunners is that the Collection's reset function may be a little slower in execution, but at least you can now say you legitimately own these titles while you continue to grind out runs on previously accepted emulators. Win Win.As for the actual quality of the games in this collection: While Harmony of Dissonance is often considered to be the weakest game of this batch, it still stands very strong against a lot of other indie Metroidvania titles out there. Remember that is one game in a bundle of four for the price you would have paid for that one indie Metroidvania that might not even be that good. Again - and to close this review -  I have to stress, the  is strong with this one!

_childDocuments_.review: Beware as my opinions seem to be unpopular. This compilation was my first time playing Castlevania in any form so don't expect me to compare Dracula X to Rondo of Blood or Symphony of the Night to the others. When it comes to the collection as a whole - I can't really say much more than that it has all of the basic stuff that you'd expect from it. You can do save-states, you can re-wind, you also have an access to stuff like concept art and music player. From this point onward I'm just going to say what do I think about the separate titles. Circle of the Moon: I know that this is the first of the GBA games but spritework looks really cheap at times. Besides that Nathan controls in a really clumsy way. You're slow as molasses and if you want to whip in mid-air after jumping - you have to swipe your finger in a weird way rather than just pressing jump and then attack. Also holy water is stationary for some mysterious reason. At first I kept dying to literally everything as I had some serious trouble figuring out all of the stuff that kinda went unexplained but that you can also access since the beginning. After that struggle the game seems to be moderately difficult. Harmony of Dissonance: Looks better than Circle of the Moon, controls better than Circle of the Moon and you gain abilities slowly allowing you to get used to the game in a much less painful way. Spellbook system lets you access more numerous and more useful special abilities than in case of its predecessor. (At least at the beginning.) One issue that you could have with this game is that it's really easy. I've played it the most from Metroidvanias and beaten several bosses dying only once. Not even to a boss. Aria of Sorrow: I've barely touched this one but I'm unlikely to. Why? Well - I know that Castlevenia games aren't played for the story but you can't expect me to take seriously a game in which a castle from Romania randomly materializes in Japan and main protagonist is a supermodel high-schooler that randomly gained the power to absorb souls. Outside of story being plain ridiculus - classic sub-weapons are now replaced by abilities absorbed from monsters that feel less polished to say at least. Whip seems to be replaced by a sword and it makes combat feel much clunkier for me. Outside of that game seems to look and play roughly the same as Harmony of Dissonance. Dracula X: Completely different from the aforementioned titles. Dracula X is not a Metroidvania but a classic-style Castlevania game. I know that it's supposed to be an "Inferior Port" of Rondo of Blood but since I've never played that game - I can't tell. Dracula X looks amazing and music that it offers is amazing as well. Easily the most difficult game of the bunch but also short and linear one; things get serious from stage 3 onward and enemy and pitfall placement progressively get more and more annoying. Nothing impossible though. Except for the final fight perhaps. Oddly enough I've played this game the most from the entire collection.

_childDocuments_.review: Castlevania Advance Collection is a solid collection of great games, and Dracula X. Other than certain scenes with flashing or flickering lights being blurred to make it seem more like a transparency effect instead, I didn't notice many changes to the games themselves. The collection is quite nice, offering a gallery, music player and regional variants of every game on it. The additional saves, replays, rewind, and game-specific encyclopedias are all excellent additions as well, though it still feels like it's missing a few things, like the ability to reverse search through items/cards/souls rather than only going one way.The settings for the collection itself are rather austere, in that there are none, pretty much. There are no resolution options, the only way to fullscreen the game is to use Alt+Enter, and you have to do it every single time you launch the collection. There's also no Esc key equivalent on the controller to close the collection directly from the game selection screen, requiring launching a game and selecting End Game with the shoulder buttons held instead. You are also unable to customize bindings on keyboard controls. It's also the type of game to freeze completely if Steam becomes unresponsive for whatever reason it usually chooses to do so.Might as well also bring up some quick thoughts about the games themselves.Would recommend, absolutely. Although I'm dissing Dracula X, it's still very nice to have it in a collection, and like I said, the three other games are all great titles. So great, in fact, that I only intended to revisit Circle of the Moon for now, only to end up playing all of them back-to-back, still wanting more. Lastly, the scene that plays on the collection's credits is adorable.

_childDocuments_.review: Hello Im Skill Incarnate and Welcome to My Games Review Series.My reviews cover indie games that i have bought, had gifted to me and have been provided by developers for review. In This Episode I check out The Castlevania Advance Collection. This collection contains all of the Castlevania games released for the Gameboy AdvanceThe collection allows you to enjoy all the classic Castlevania games restored in loving detail along with several new modern features.This includes all the regional versions of the game, a music player, replay system and the ability to save/load games.This is a fantastic way to enjoy some of the Castlevania series with some great improvements and the collection is great value for money.Please note: All opinions in this video are my own. Game was provided by the developer for review purposes================================================Castlevania Advance Collection Review: Skill Incarnates Gaming Channel: Skill Incarnates Gaming Channel on Bitchute: Skill Incarnates Gaming Channel on Twitch: Skill Incarnates Gaming Channel on Odysee: Twitter: Facebook: Email Enquiries: Castlevania Advance Collection on Steam: ================================================ABOUT THIS GAMECount Dracula is once more back from the dead...Join the fight against Evil in the Castlevania Advance Collection, a compilation of timeless action-exploration masterpieces!In addition to the three legendary Castlevania games that were first released in the early 2000s, this collection also includes Castlevania: Dracula X and some never-before-seen sketches and artwork from the games!All four games are enhanced with newly added modern features such as Rewind, Save/Load and Replay, making this the best way possible to experience these classics or discover them for the first time! This collection also boasts a handy Encyclopedia, a Music Player with all soundtracks and you can even change the ROM Region to play all games in different versions.Featured GamesCastlevania: Circle of the MoonThe story follows Nathan Graves, a vampire hunter apprentice who enters Dracula's Castle along with his Master in order to prevent the dreaded return of the Count. Combine action and attribute cards to create over 80 unique spell effects, ranging from fire whips to ice blizzards, with the 'Dual Set-up System'.Castlevania: Harmony of DissonancePlay as Juste Belmont, the grandson of legendary Vampire Hunter Simon Belmont! This title introduced a lot of new features to the franchise, such as 'Boss Rush' mode and the 'Spell Fusion' system that lets players combine Sub-Weapons with Spell Books to cast devastating spells.Castlevania: Aria of SorrowSoma Cruz, a young high school exchange student in Japan, is somehow involved in the eternal cycle of reincarnation of the Dark Lord himself. _childDocuments_.review: If you're not me and you love Castlevania, you'll probably love this. As for myself, I'd rather hold onto my GBA carts and just emulate the games.There's no options to manipulate the color space to address the over saturated colors, most GBA games color templates were tuned around the GBA screen with it's limited color reproduction and lack of a backlight, meaning Dracula's big spooky castle ends up looking very bright, with light grayish washed out shades of many colors that should be darker with very saturated sprites.Most modern GBA emulators let you tweak the color space to address the fact that you're now playing the games on a monitor/TV capable of many times greater color reproduction and fancy back/side lighting or self lit light emitting diodes.This version doesn't.It's barebones, it works, there's a few extras, it includes two 7/10 castlevanias and two 8/10 castlevania. It's great, it's just not for me and may turn off those who remember these games looking a little different on their non backlit atomic purple gameboy advance screen.

_childDocuments_.review: This game provides hours and hours of enjoyment.  If you like games like Metroid, Hollow Knight, Axiom Verge, etc., then this collection will be right up your alley. In addition to having a faithful emulation of the original games, the extra features are very helpful.  The rewind feature really helps deal with the difficulty, which might be too much for some players - it's not super-difficult, but it can get up there for some bosses and areas.  Being able to rewind and save or load at virtually any point, in addition to the encyclopedia, makes these old games much more manageable.  There are also options to remap controls, which can be useful for battle strategists and speed-runners.  The GBA Castlevania games also have a lot of replay value.  The card drops and spirit drops ensure that the game is never the same twice.  In addition, unlocking new weapons and grinding is actually pretty fun.  The gothic, horror atmosphere of each game provides a nice atmosphere for tackling baddies and maxing out each character. I'm not a big fan of Dracula X - it's not bad, but not in the top 50 percent of my favorite Castlevania games.  Some do enjoy it, but it's more straightforward than the other three in this collection.  I think it's cool that they included it.  As for the rest, the Advance games range from good to great.  Each game has plenty of surprises, weird bosses, cool level themes, scary enemies, and lots and lots of cool weapons and random drops that will keep many players coming back (including myself of couse).  There's so much here it's hard not to recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: The Castlevania Advance Collection is a must buy for 4 solid reasons but before I get into that, one thing must be said: I highly recommend using a Pro Gaming Controller from  for these games, it is what I've been using and the experience has been immaculate. Alright, here is my list of reasons why this is a must buy...1) This collection contains Castlevania: Aria of Sorrow. AOS is an S tier Castlevania game in which you play as Soma Cruz, a teenager living in the year of 2035 who has the ability to absorb souls and use the various powers/abilities they grant. With dozens of weapons and souls at your disposal the strategies available to you are nearly endless. There are many interesting areas to explore and the bosses are fun to fight. The music is awesome. The story is great. There are 3 endings, the good ending, the neutral ending, and the bad ending. Additionally, you get to play as Julius Belmont once you've beaten the game if you type in JULIUS when you're creating a new game in another save file. There is also hard mode which I plan to experience at some point, not to mention all the AOS mods that are out there. AOS is easily my favorite Castlevania game. I'd recommend buying Castlevania Advance Collection based on this alone.2) This collection contains Castlevania: Harmony of Dissonance. HOD is what I'd call an A tier Castlevania game, it's not as memorable as AOS but it's great nonetheless. The animation really stands out in this game, there are a lot of appealing backgrounds for the areas you get to explore and the blue afterimages that come with playing as Juste Belmont is super cool. The music is pretty good although some of it sounds a bit bland depending on the area. The fact that HOD has 2 Castles, Castle A and Castle B, also sets it apart from other Castlevania games. I've been told that navigating these maps can be confusing but I didn't struggle with that. This game also has a good story with a twist that I was not expecting the first time I played through it. It's refreshing to see how creative the developers were with the stories regarding both AOS and HOD. After you've beaten HOD as Juste Belmont (any one of the endings will do) entering MAXIM in an empty save slot will allow you to play in Maxim Mode. 3) Castlevania: Circle of the Moon is also among the games in this collection. I do not have much to say other than it's a B tier Castlevania game in my humble opinion. It's a good game, I would recommend playing it.4) Many retro fans along with those of us who grew up enjoying these games would love to have this collection. It gives a sense of nostalgia that I personally enjoy, it reminds me of a part of my life when I had so much less to worry about and I'm sure others will be able to relate. With that being said, I was never really a fan of Castlevania: Dracula X. Buying this collection means you'll be able to play DX and to be fair it's not terrible but if you're like me I wouldn't have high expectations for it. Still, you're getting 4 games for $20 and at least 3 of them are good so even if you ignore DX you'd be getting 3 good games for about $6.66. It was certainly worth it to me.That's all I got.

_childDocuments_.review: Terrific collection of games for $20!Circle of the Moon is a great blend of classic Castlevania with the Metroidvania style that Symphony popularized and all further released aped. It seems to have received a lukewarm reception at release, but people have come around on it and realized it packed quite a punch. For my part, I think it is the best of the three GBA games. It had a great castle, good level of challenge, fun bosses, you always had a good idea of where to go and what to do, and there was great pacing to it all. Just a really solid entry.Harmony of Dissonance is the weakest of the three GBA games. This was my first time playing it and while I ultimately enjoyed myself enough to finish it, I didn't think it was a very good game. It wasn't bad per se, but I found myself annoyed a lot with how easily lost you become all the time in it due to cryptic design. The castle doesn't flow all that well. You backtrack absolute tons in the game. And on top of that the game is a cakewalk. There's virtually no challenge to it at all. It simply isn't a very satisfying experience.Aria of Sorrow is basically Harmony of Dissonance 1.5. It takes what HoD did poorly and does it better. It's the most beautiful of the three games with truly great pixel work. The castle design is good and everything is generally pretty clear. There's ample teleports and save rooms that are placed pretty well. There was not much in the way of backtracking. But once again, the game is trivial in its challenge. You can literally stand in one spot fighting most of the bosses and tank them while attacking. The game just isn't challenging enough. I understand difficulty is a balancing act, but both Harmony and Aria failed to achieve a satisfying challenge.Still, I got tons of enjoyment out of the three games. And there's still Dracula X to beat, but most of us are probably here for GBA games. I found Circle of the Moon to be the most satisfying to play. And I hope one day we'll get a Castlevania that embraces more of its roots like CotM did.

_childDocuments_.review: The games included (except for Dracula X) are all simply incredible, especially Aria of Sorrow which holds up as one of the best Castlevania games out there. Each game has their own special charm and identity through memorable characters, music, and game mechanics that defines each game. The primary reason to get this game is simply because once you start playing, you simply cannot stop playing due to how addicting the exploration is.All of the games are expertly crafted in how you navigate and explore through Dracula's castle with each game having their own special mechanics such as the DSS mechanic in Circle of the Moon and the Soul mechanic from Aria of Sorrow which leads to tons of experimentation and freedom on which combinations to go for.I'd also like to praise how memorable the game's music is which is especially impressive considering the GBA didn't have a great soundchip. I would also like to add that Awake and Castle corridor are peak tracks!If you are interested in Castlevania but don't know where to start, you should consider starting with this collection as it is a solid beginning to get familiarised with the Castlevania series.

_childDocuments_.review: Hey, this Aria of Sorrow port comes with 3 other games!For real though, this is a good collection for those who want to play 2000's era castlevanias.they work, its all good. no big glitches. Setting the game to fullscreen borderless is kind of a pain in the ass however.Each game has save states, rewind, and a collectible track unique to each game to help completionists out there.how do these games play?Circle of the moon:Its rough, easily the worst in the bundle, and probably my least favorite. (I haven't played every castlevania, so take that for what you will.)Its grindy, backtracking feels unclear, the card fusing system is necessary yet put heavily into the backburner, combat feels tankier than it needs to be, and certain areas in the game aren't fun to play. One of which has red water everywhere. while touching it, you lose 5HP a second. on top of everything else attacking you.4/10Harmony of Dissonance:feels like a natural, yet experimental follow up to symphony of the night. pretends circle of the moon didn't happen, collectibles are much great, even if items earned aren't necessary to win. walking speed can feel a little slow however. you're able to forward and back dash as much as you want with the bumpers, however this quickly turns into mashing your bumpers for the entirety of the game. theres no run button. otherwise, what feels off is backtracking. there's teleporters everywhere, in some areas certain ones will only take you to others, meanwhile as you play, some areas will be blocked off after going through the first time. meaning unless you have an elephants memory, you're easily going to get lost simply from not being able to remember only ONE teleporter will take you to the one spot on the map you need in order to progress.8/10Aria of sorrow:Arguably the best 2D castlevania period. Everything symphony of the night did, but expanded on. Back tracking doesn't feel obtuse for majority of the experience. combat is fleshed out and realized. walking from point A to B isn't reliant on mashing a dash button, and not to mention one of the prettiest pixelated castlvania games there is.I wanna call the game flawless, however I can't ignore late game messing up in one spot. Every enemy in the game has an ability you can earn. for whatever reason 3 very specific ones are needed in order to progress to the endgame. There's no real reason this happens, story says nothing about why they're essential. they just are. You get a couple of hints, but it still irks me. In the room where you get the third one of the trio, you need the previous 2 in order to traverse the room. in there, tiny sprites the kinda resemble the monsters needed are shown on the wall.Whats more, 4 books are able to be found throughout the castle telling you what to do cryptically. however, 3/4 require extra digging to find.Ultimately it feels like a way to stretch out play time, because if you already know what you need, the game feels way shorter than first expected. If you don't have them, the game abruptly ends after one boss. it doesn't make sense.theres fun secrets to be found, but if you just want to play it once and move on, you may lose interest quick.9/10Dracula X:...yeah thats dracula X. if you've played any pre-SOTN castlvanias, its that. Its fine, but doesn't excite me personally.8/10 overall, the bundle works and the games inside are mostly worth it.8/10TLDR, circle of the moon sucks but otherwise these games are good.

_childDocuments_.review: This is everything I'd hoped it would be; the GBA Castlevania series was something I played for hours on end when I was on a 6 month recovery period. _childDocuments_.review: I love the Castlevania franchise so much that I even have SotN on Android. Hence, when I could get this, I jumped on it given how fun the other Castlevania games have been. However, since installing and playing, I can not recommend this game and here's why:Pros:♦ Game filesize is relatively small♦ Multiple Classic Castlevania games in oneCons:♦ Game resolution is incorrect by default (Game launches with it spread across both my monitors, instead of using my main monitor and fitting to the native resolution)♦ No main menu options or settings menu (Have to select which Castlevania game from the main menu first before able to access any options or settings menu)♦ Game is ported poorly and designed solely for Xbox Controller♦ Keyboard users can't see controls easily as all the key prompts are in Xbox Controller Input and it's hard to even find which button opens the menu to see the controls♦ Can't remap keyboard controls. I tried everything to try to remap keyboard controls and could only remap controller despite not having a controller plugged in♦ Forced to use arrow keys to move and WASD or numpad does not work for movement (This is annoying for players used to WASD or numpad or have a preferred keyboard setup) ♦ Seems like the port to PC is just a poorly made version of an emulator. An actual emulator console would have been much better than thisOverall, there are more cons than pros and I can not recommend this unless you own a controller (Which I do not) and want to play your PC game solely with a controller. If you do use a controller than this may work for you and be a fun game. But, since I am 100% keyboard orientated, I can not recommend this until the port is less clunky and keyboard keys can be remapped.

_childDocuments_.review: After getting into modern indie metroidvania's (like Hollow Knight, Momodora etc) decided to check out what helped start the gaming genre with the previous 'Castlevania Anniversary Collection' but refunded it because it was too arcade like and clunky (didn't mind the graphics as am a fan of pixel and old 8bit styles).Figured I'd try this collection (as could always refund it) but really enjoyed playing through some of the games so far. (50% Harmony of Dissonance and 80% Aria of Sorrow). Graphics are great and interesting monster design (health absorbing Dryads and women fused with spiders and much more). Exploration is rewarded with unique weapons/abilities and interesting levels to explore.Gameplay is quite fluid and easy to grasp though bosses are sometimes a little simplistic and clunky but still requires timing and precision. So far no issues with the games I played like bugs or crashes. Soundtrack for all games are available to listen to in the collections menu (but also can be found in your steam folder)......and the price is decent for what you get so I would recommend to anyone who enjoys this style of gaming.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a direct port with rewinding as an enhancement (i.e. don't expect gorgeous graphics). I have only played Aria of Sorrow so far and the port feels very low effort.The lighting effects in the save rooms feel like they will give me a seizure (The GBA version pulled off some graphical trickery with its hardware to make a cool flickering-light effect and this didn't translate well in the emulator used for this collection). Any play-testing would have caught this within 5 minutes of play which means they likely knew about it and just didn't care to fix it.Also, it is annoying to not be able to use my controller's d-pad to control movement and this means that I often register an (unintended) UP data input which causes me to cast a spell instead of attacking physically. Other than this, the controls feel close to playing this game on a GBA SP (not exact, but close).Lastly, there are no graphical options. My xbox controller  with this game. I'm unsure if it was a patch or simply the controller being turned off and on. This is the first game I've experienced this specific issue with this controller (only d-pad inputs not working).Also, the save room graphical issues are apparent in other terrains (ex: ice cavern section). Someone with more knowledge of GBA emulation could name the specifics of what went wrong with the emulation here (some kind of filter not being utilized correctly I'd guess).I emulated Aria of Sorrow a few years ago on a SNES Classic and it looked and played better than this game version (Controls felt extremely close to playing this on a GBA SP).I will say though that the rewind function was helpful for doing Julius mode and actually does rewind back a generous / respectable amount of time. The added gadget frame was nice for the soul collecting achievement but was generally annoying otherwise (you can turn it off in the L2 menu). I think this could be solved with improved UI integration of the gadget.

_childDocuments_.review: Circle of the Moon:Great plot, great power-up progression and good bosses (that are actually moderately/very difficult). Soundtrack is memorable. On the bad side, several bosses can be cheesed easily without using the rewind mechanic due to safe spots in boss rooms. No idea why HP potions even drop in this game because they are so rare and so useless you'll forget they exist. DSS is interesting but card drop rates are low and several cards are deep in late game areas, meaning you'll likely finish the game with less than half of them, even with a little bit of farming. Harmony of Dissonance:Two castle mechanic is somewhat interesting but the actual layout of the castle paired with few warp spots makes for way too much backtracking. You'll likely get stuck several times having no idea where to go next (more so than in the other games). Also the difficulty in this game is downright insulting. "Bosses" are punching bags that swing in your general direction maybe once every 15 seconds. New enemy I've never seen before? Dies in 2 hits, no idea what their moves are, don't care. Your character is so overpowered it's not even funny. No boss mechanics will pose any challenge because you can just use spells that deal damage while your character is invulnerable for a good 10-15 seconds at a time. Music is okay, but less memorable than in CotM. Also sadly there are no breakable walls. Aria of Sorrow:Plot and characters feels a bit goofy compared to the previous two, but our main character now has the ability to equip different types of melee weapons. The soul system is an interesting way to handle different types of active/passive abilities. Sadly, while boss difficulty has improved slightly from HoD, too many of them (especially early-mid game) are pushovers. The first time I reached the credits was a bit of a "that's it?" moment. Overall (I didn't play Dracula X yet):Well worth a play-through for fans of the franchise or genre, though somewhat lacking in challenges.
