_childDocuments_.review: Don't get me wrong, I love Aria of Sorrow as much as any huge Castlevania fan...But the other three games in the collection range from meh to excrutiating pain. You're essentially only paying for Aria unless you're masochistic, so get this on sale like I did. Even on sale and with some free Paypal vouchers I got I still kinda regret paying for this.Circle of the Moon in special has the WORST castle layout in the entire series, no kidding. It's so vertical and tiresome to navigate, filled with dead ends that you need to come back to without knowing if it's the pathway to a new area or just an HP\MP\Heart upgrade, and many more issues. The whole DSS system is flat out horrible and requires an ungodly amount of grinding and patience. Not even the fact that rewinding reduces the grind time makes it tolerable. Thank god they only require you to beat each game twice for the achievements, because Circle of the Moon has like 5 extra modes and each sounds more miserable than the last.Harmony of Dissonance is better in many ways, but the navigation still can get confusing sometimes, especially after the mid-way point where you discover there's two layers to the castle.Dracula X is not as bad as either of these, but it gets really painful in the second half. At least it lasts only a few hours if you're not that bad or use rewind a lot.Aria of Sorrow is an amazing game, but even it can't singlehandedly save a collection where all other games are just chores to play at best. Just play it somewhere else and call it a day, honestly.

_childDocuments_.review: After Konomi surprised itself with the success of its underfunded instant classic and game of the year Castlevania: Symphony of the night, it quickly cloned the formula on a vastly lesser platform, giving us three games with middling main characters, poor graphics, and vastly lesser music. Gone is the smooth movement and regal air of SotN, but the Gameboy Advanced tried its best. What it delivered in these three games good given their constraints. However, they are hard to play on the PC, where your screen resolution had better be blowing away what the GBA could deliver. Admire them for their place in history, and enjoy them for what they are. Just recognize that they are products for a lesser machine. Try not to hold that against them.

_childDocuments_.review: the 2020s just keep getting weirder - pandemic, climate change, and now Konami are making smart business decisions?  I guess they got tired of driving away their top talent and milking PESSo what we got here is a pretty straight up port of the Gameboy Advance castlevanias, with Dracula X thrown on for a bonus.  There's a few modern features such as a beastiary, save anywhere, rewind (ala Prince of Persia) and an art gallery.  While it would have been nice to have remixed sound (especially rerecorded music, like they did with the Final Fantasy pixel releases) and a bit of a spit-shine on the visuals, these are incredibly true to their original releases and dripping with nostalgia.  Best of all, you don't need to fiddle around with Roms to play them.  One slight caveat though - you can't turn off the music in any of these, and being gameboy advance ports, the music ain't really that great.  Therefore, if like me you'd rather blast through these with some bombastic power metal in the background (oooh give me some Powerwolf for flavour's sake) then it sucks for you (and me).Circle of the Moon - even with the bestiary, still can't get into this one.  The controls are clunky, movement is awkward, and the visuals don't seem to have aged well at all IMHOHarmony of Dissonance - if you can get past the garish colour scheme (that looks like something ♥♥♥♥ out of 90s MTV) and the awful compressed lo fi music Harmony is a proper good time.  The way magic combines with your sub weapon is awesome!Aria of Sorrow - defo the best in this collection and on of the best 2D Castlevanias.  Worth the price for this alone, although a bit on the short side.  The system of capturing enemy souls and using them as magic attacks is super fun.Dracula X - Kind of a weird inclusion being as not a Gameboy Advance title and a "classic" Castlevania (i.e. levels, no rpg mechanics), its still a nice addition and well worth a play.3 outa 4 ain't too bad if you ask me. Although its pretty bare bones, the low price and the chance to finally play these without either ROMS or spending a fortune on Ebay to track down a gameboy advance and a cartridge, this is a solid choice.  NOW FFS KONAMI GIVE US A DECENT STEAM VERSION OF SYMPHONY OF THE NIGHT!  AND HOW ABOUT SOME OF THE DS CASTLEVANIAS?

_childDocuments_.review: The games that put the 'vania' in metroidvania. While not as graphically and audibly as good as the masterpiece Symphony of the Night, these GBA titles are still very much worth your time for the gameplay. Many would even consider Aria of Sorrow as a strong contender for the best game in the franchise, and honestly it's easy to see why. I've always enjoyed the fast paced action of Harmony, as well as the challenging fights of Circle of the Moon, and having Dracula X in this collection as well is a nice bonus.I've sunk many hours into these games over the years on handheld devices, but being able to play them in this format on Steam with some nice QoL features added by Konami makes this collection worth the price.If you have never played a Castlevania game before and are looking to get into the series, then this is the perfect place to start, or if you're someone who has simply never had the chance to play these games in the series before, then don't miss out any longer.

_childDocuments_.review: The Castlevania Advance Collection brings together three games with unique takes on the Castlevania formula, each contributing something memorable while often struggling with various design pitfalls. Here’s a breakdown of each title in the collection:Castlevania: Circle of the MoonCircle of the Moon introduces the Dual Set-Up System (DSS), an intriguing mechanic that allows players to combine primary and secondary cards to create different abilities. While conceptually rich, the cards’ random drop rates make the experience frustrating; grinding enemies to complete your DSS collection feels more like an obstacle than an engaging feature. Luckily, the collection notifies players when an enemy holds a card drop, but it doesn’t fully alleviate the tedium of grinding.The core gameplay follows the Castlevania template, with players leveling up as they battle familiar enemies. However, movement is notably slow, and the double-tap dash required for running quickly becomes a thumb-sore and feels like poor design. Why not just make the default speed faster? Additionally, the story is unremarkable, and its unskippable cutscenes compound the sense of drudgery. Ultimately, Circle of the Moon has enough drawbacks to make its final levels an unappealing grind, and the pacing suffers so much that I can't see myself finishing it.Castlevania: Harmony of DissonanceHarmony of Dissonance starts strong with snappy, responsive movement; players can dash with the L and R buttons, making dodging and general navigation a joy. However, issues become apparent as the game progresses. Harmony has two overlapping castles, which means frequent backtracking between nearly identical maps with different backdrops. The lack of clear signposting often leaves players lost, and some critical items are so well hidden that a guide feels necessary to progress.Difficulty is all over the place, with some enemies barely dealing damage while others pose a significant threat. Bosses can be repetitive, with some appearing multiple times, although most are easy to dispatch. I enjoyed Harmony enough to finish it but would only recommend it with reservations; it’s not a game I’d revisit. The story, like Circle of the Moon, is poorly localized and unskippable, dragging the experience down further. The music, surprisingly subpar given the game’s title, suffers from low sound quality likely due to the limitations of its original hardware.Castlevania: Aria of SorrowAria of Sorrow is the standout entry in this collection and a fan favorite for good reason. The game’s movement feels fluid, allowing for jump direction changes and animation-canceling, which gives players precise control in combat. Souls, which are special abilities dropped by enemies, provide a wealth of offensive options. The sheer variety of souls lets players experiment and customize their approach, though this can sometimes tip the balance, making the game feel easier than intended.New weapon types also add depth to combat, with different attack styles that let players tailor their experience. The level design and music are highlights, with areas thoughtfully laid out and enemies distinctively placed to bring personality to each environment. Bosses are visually and mechanically interesting, giving players challenging but fair fights. The story, while better written than in Harmony, is still marred by unskippable dialogue and unimpressive localization.Aria of Sorrow is the clear reason to buy this collection and a defining title in the series. It’s easy to recommend, offering a great balance of challenging gameplay and smart design, though fans looking for a flawless experience may find the other games in this collection less compelling.Castlevania: Dracula XCastlevania: Dracula X is a watered down port of the Rondo of Blood with most of the fun stripped away and mean enemy placement.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a review for Aria of Sorrow (AoS). I haven't played any of the other games in this collection.I bought this collection after I read that AoS was worth playing. I've now seen the game through to the end and I honestly think that I wasted my time.AoS is a mediocre metroidvania at best. Little stands out as being particularly good or interesting. The most novel feature is a mechanic that allows you to absorb the souls of enemies that you kill, granting you new abilities. This adds a bit of variety into the combat at least, however outside of combat there is little opportunity to use these abilities. There's a few exceptions; boss souls sometimes confer mobility enhancements that allow you to proceed to different areas of the castle. These aren't always implemented well. For example, there are two separate souls that you can get for water mobility which are required for progression; one which allows you to walk on water, another which allows you to sink deeper into water. However, you have to equip/unequip these souls as and when you need them. The soul which lets you sink deeper into water doesnt let you swim upwards any further than your basic jump permits; to rise back to the surface you need to go into your inventory and unequip the soul. This is rather irritating because there's quite a lot of water to traverse in the game. The confusing thing is that they could have just made this one of the separate non-soul based abilities that you get (double-jump being an example of an early non-soul based ability), and have implemented a mechanic where you tap a button to wade through water (like you see in 2d Mario). Instead, you have to constantly go into your inventory and locate the soul among half a dozen others as and when you need it. Another problem you'll often encounter in AoS is a difficulty in distinguishing between background and foreground detail. A lot of the time it's hard to tell what is a platform and what isn't.The next point is somewhat subjective, but I think that most people will agree that the music in this game is particularly annoying. Somehow it manages to be quite good and quite horrible, simultaneously. You'll know what I mean if you hear it.Level design is entirely mediocre for a metroidvania.Enemy designs are quite fun, and one of the stronger aspects of the game. However, in keeping with the general tone of the game, they're often painfully irritating. Enemies are usually either too big, meaning they're difficult to circumvent (this is a metroidvania, remember, where backtracking is essential and enemies respawn), or too fast (meaning they're difficult to hit). Ultimately, then, we have a rather mediocre metroidvania here, which verges on being bad due to the persistent nature of its negative elements.I would recommend the following instead of AoS:Hollow KnightBloodstained: Ritual of the NightSalt and SanctuaryOri and the Blind ForestOri and the Will o the WispsBlasphemousCastlevania: Symphony of the NightSuper Metroid

_childDocuments_.review: The Castlevania Advance Collection is a good package for fans of Castlevania or anyone curious about classic Metroidvania-style games. It gives you four games and some nice extras like artworks and soundtracks, all for a reasonable price. However, while the collection is a great deal for the content, the quality of the games inside is very differentDracula X (Vampire’s Kiss)This is the weakest game in the collection, and it’s not hard to see why. Dracula X is just a bad port of Rondo of Blood for the SNES, but without the quality of the original. It’s a classic Castlevania with linear stages, but the difficulty is brutal, especially in the later levels. Compared to the other games in the collection, it feels outdated and clunky.Circle of the MoonThe soundtrack here is excellent, and the game has a lot of replayability with different modes. But it’s also very punishing. The movement feels stiff, and healing is rare, especially in the early game, where you can go long stretches with monster infested corridors without save points.One of the biggest issues is the DSS card system. It’s a cool idea because it lets you combine cards for special abilities and create interesting (and sometimes useless) combos. But the game does poor job explaining how it works, and the drop rate for cards is abyssmal. Most of my playtime was spent killing the same enemies over and over just to get a new card. At least in this version, you can see which enemies might drop a card, which helps a bit.Harmony of DissonanceThis one is a mixed bag. For a metroidvania it feels very open, almost too open from the start. You often don’t know where to go, which means a lot of wandering and backtracking. Many times, I walked into a new area, spent several minutes exploring, only to find a dead end or some useless collectible.The save points are sparse and far from boss rooms, which makes dying more punishing. Enemies deal high contact damage, and Juste (the main character) feels very vulnerable, like you’re supposed to avoid fighting. But then you also have to grind to deal with tough enemies and bosses.The bosses are not very creative, often having just 2-3 attacks but way too much health. The music is also disappointing, with most of it sounding like noise rather than proper tunes. And visually, the game’s bright contrasts and over-animated backgrounds can strain your eyes. Aria of SorrowThis is easily the highlight of the collection and one of the best Castlevania games ever made. The Tactical Soul System is fantastic, letting you collect abilities from enemies and customize how you play. It builds on everything Symphony of the Night did and might even be better.The difficulty is well-balanced, making it fun for both new and experienced players. It has a great soundtrack, and the new game plus mode, along with the extra Julius mode, adds even more replayability. If you get this collection for just one game, Aria of Sorrow makes the whole thing worth it.If you are a fan of Castlevania or Metroidvania games, this collection is still worth it for the amount of content and the chance to experience some classic titles. Just be ready for some highs and lows.Recommended at discount.

_childDocuments_.review: Castlevania Advance Collection is a really good collection of the original Game Boy Advance games and a great follow-up to the first Anniversary Collection, okay then now since I only have a limited amount of space I'll talk about the games as a whole while giving little bits about each game, but first the story.In times when people crave chaos and destruction, when they desire darkness and power their cries are answered by one being, one creature that will give them what they want and that creature is Count Dracula. But many vampire hunters like the Belmont Clan have vowed to find a way to destroy the vampire king once and for all, perhaps in the future they will succeed, but if they do a new lord might rise up to take up the mantle of Count Dracula and usher in a new age of darkness.Okay let’s get into the likes, the gameplay is very good this collection contains most of the metroidvania games that were released on the Game Boy Advance, circle of the moon, harmony of dissonance and aria of sorrows, it also has Dracula X but unfortunately not the Rondo of Blood one. Anyway each of the three metroidvania games boils down to fight monsters and get power ups to advance further but there are some things that help the games stand out, dissonance has you pick up little power ups that can give your sub weapons extra powers, circle of the moon has these cards that can give your whip different attributes like fire or ice or allows you to perform summoning and finally aria of sorrows allows you to kill enemies and absorb their spirits allowing you unique attacks, stat boosts and even being able to transform, a lot like symphony of the night.Also like symphony of the night is the fact that you can pick up different items such as clothes and accessories that can enhanced certain stats of your character. Dracula X is the only one that stands out because it's made in the traditional style of the original Castlevania games.The stories are good each one is simple and not too complicated, you have to kill Dracula but they do add a little more depth to each of the games, probably the best one would be Aria of Sorrows as it feels like a combination of both circle of the moon and harmony of dissonance taking the best elements from both of those games and combining it. The graphics are good each one has a nice use of colors, designs and over all feel especially for enemies and backgrounds, each part of the castle is quite detailed and helps it to stand out and makes you want to just stop and look at it. The levels are good each one is quite distinct and different with some pretty great details to look at, it just makes you want to explore everything and see all the cool background details and scenery.The enemies and bosses are all excellent each enemy and boss has a very good designs, we have your traditional skeletons and zombies, while we have more unique enemies like electric skeletons, petrifying bulls and zombie soldiers and those are the common enemies, the bosses are quite memorable with interesting and sometimes very creepy designs from Legion to certain second forms of bosses. The music is quite good with plenty of great tracks to listen too, also the bonus stuff is really good, from getting to listen to all the music from each of the games and seeing all the concept art, I particularly enjoyed the rewind feature as it helped me getting achievements a bit easier.Okay let’s get into the dislikes, while most of the games are good I have to say that Dracula X sucks, it's probably the worst game in this collection not only does it have stupid enemy placements, the final boss Dracula is such a pain in the ass mostly because of his stage basically it's a platform stage you have to jump from platform to platform while avoiding his attacks and because of the knockback feature if he hits you once you could fall down a pit, also his first form is such a pain in the ass because you have to hit his head and sometimes it doesn't work.Now circle of the moon has cards that like I said give you certain attributes and the way to get these cards is you have to kill a certain enemy, problem is some of the enemies can be pretty stingy with giving those cards also the last two cards can only be found on these two living armor enemies that are only located in the battle area, which is complete bunk if it wasn't for the rewind ability then I wouldn't have been able to get those two.The same problem happens in aria of sorrows we're certain enemies just won't give up their soul no matter how many times you kill them, also apparently the luck status is kind of broken so it makes having to get the souls in aria of sorrows even more challenging.There is a patch you can download but I feel like Konami really should have fixed that themselves, also this is a bit of a complaint/dislike I'm wondering why they didn't have Symphony of the Night in this collection as to my knowledge it was the first metroidvania that started the whole genre. So I'm wondering why that game was not included in this collection, also why wasn't Rondo of Blood the superior version of Dracula X and its remake we're not included in this collection as well, hopefully a future collection that will address that.Alright then now with that done Castlevania Advance Collection is a really good collection of the original Game Boy Advance games and a great follow-up to the first Anniversary Collection, it has very good gameplay, good graphics and excellent enemies and bosses. Now I definitely recommend this game if you liked the first Anniversary Collection or if you have nostalgia for these games then I definitely, definitely recommend getting this collection.

_childDocuments_.review: ATTOTR I’ve only played Aria of Sorrow, so can’t tell you how the rest of them are, but based off my experience on that game, the ports of the game seem pretty good. Wish there were some filters available but that’;s something you can set up yourself easily enough. Gonna be brief as the story in Aria of Sorrow is brief in itself. Basically you play as Soma Cruz, a high school student studying abroad in Japan in 2035 (huh...we’re just shy of 10 years from that year, huh.) He goes to see a Solar Eclipse with his friend, Mina Hakuba. They both get sucked into the eclipse, and find themselves in Dracula’s Castle, it’s whereabouts being unknown after 36 years since his previous defeat. The two are then set upon by a group of monsters. Another man by Arikado rushes to their aid, but Soma is able to defeat one of them by himself. He learns that he has “the power of dominance”, a power that enables him to use the abilities of their various monstrous foes that litter the castle. With his new found power, Soma adventures through the castle searching for an escape, and to find the answers to why he gained this weird power. Jumping off from Symphony of the night, you definitely know what to expect. 2D side scroll RPG action. Look for powers to access more parts of the castle, and then get BEYOND overpowered overtime. First played this game in 2011 so I do remember it fondly. It’s a bit basic nowadays but I still enjoyed my play through. Critiques I can offer is that the game is quite stingy with the teleport and saves, so you will have to backtrack if you die, but the rewind feature makes it manageable. If you do what you’re supposed to an explore as much as you can, you should have no issues.As I play through the others, will update the review, though I’ll have to be even briefer than this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Circle of the Moon-When reminiscing on this game I remember it having awful physics and poorly polished and uninspired upgrades, and it still does. However, I do like the horribly bugged magic system that allows you to use every effect in the game from the beginning and kinda saves it (yeah, a back handed compliment). The other thing saving it is the music, this version of The Sinking Old Sanctuary is my favorite and an excellent choice to hear when backtracking through the central hub area. There's nothing really interesting or surprising going with the progression through the castle, but the interruptions are at a minimum and thus let you stay in the zone longer. The bosses can be a problem with how much they ratchet up the difficulty towards the end and may affect how you perceive this game, the worst part being the last few ones have an unskippable cutscene beforehand. Ultimately, I'd say if you can put up with it's shortcomings and play on its terms, you can have a very comfy time with this one. Harmony of Dissonance-Don't know how people completely trash this game's OST when the Entrance theme kicks so much ass, among other select tracks. I'm assuming Harmony is the black sheep of this trilogy and I like this one quite a lot. It's biggest shortcoming is it's dense, confusing map, but I was eventually able to enjoy it a little bit by shifting my mindset. Movement/unlock upgrades are extremely sparse, but the games never cared about that for 100% completion. They only ever cared about finding rooms, and I think this game capitalizes on that progression more than any of the other metroidvanias. As long as you are filling out more map tiles, you are making progress. As a huge movement enjoyer, this one's got my favorite movement of the Igavanias. It has a high skill ceiling to master with strange but intuitive momentum that feels rewarding to flow through the zig zagging rooms quickly. I find the cast to be likable, the questionable translation charming and the use of colors and style of music gives the game a sort of dreamlike atmosphere. It's almost like stepping into Castlevania is like stepping into another dimension entirely. It felt like this series could've evolved into a different direction from the one we got and I wish there was another game that would dare take the positive aspects of this game and turn it into something uniquely good. Patches I've seen that improve Harmony are more focused on removing controversial aspects (muting the colors, de-chiptuning the music) and making it more like other Castlevanias, so I feel like I may be alone in saying "they're onto something here". Aria of Sorrow-You've probably heard about this game's reputation and I wouldn't be surprised if people told you to skip the others, and I wouldn't 100% hold back on it. To be contrarian, the two biggest flaws I felt are the movement feeling like a big downgrade from Harmony and the soul grinding, but the latter of which is entirely optional. Otherwise yeah, this game completely blows the others out of the water anyway. The graphics are on another level, it's insane going from Nathan's 3 frame dash to Juste's 5 frame jog to Soma's I dunno 20+ frame chad stride. The pacing and level design are fantastic and is probably the best designed castle among all Igavanias. The writing and characters are believable and likable, Soma's one of my favorite protagonists because I'd probably act the same way if I was in his shoes. The magic system makes the most sense and is the most engaging and tightly designed and considered and does so many clever and unique and inventive things all at the same time. The positives go on and on. It's a problem to spend hours running back and forth between rooms killing the same enemy over and over until the game says "yes", but the reason so many players end up doing it is because the souls constantly remain desirable with so many fun and weird abilities to acquire. I think after this point they just start copypasting this game's "just good enough to get by" movement and combat with minor variations, which is disappointing for a series that constantly reinvented itself all the way up to this point, but when I get to the Dominus collection I hope I end up proving myself wrong with Ecclasia at least. Dracula X-Rondo of Blood At Home has surprisingly good music for an SNES port of a CD based game. However, you can't play as Maria so it's an instant 0/10. Joking aside this game is really rough, cruel and mean spirited. I look back at Castlevania III and think about how it felt really hard and repetitive only to find out the Japanese version was actually designed pretty well and fair. This game kinda feels like that but for Rondo of Blood, but the changes continue to the stage design and backgrounds and the entire presentation is just lackluster and second rate. They do not think about what would be an interesting challenge for the player character, they just dump ♥♥♥♥ on top of you and call it a day. I didn't find out until recently that they did make a Rondo and Symphony compilation exclusive to PS4 and 5 which makes it feel like another petty exclusivity deal on Sony's part, and this game here is the result of them trying to compromise. They really shouldn't have bothered. Overall-The emulator features are much nicer this time around, allowing multiple save states, in game glossaries, and they even mark collectables like souls and cards in real time as you play. It feels kinda weird going from like 8-9 games down to only 3 and a half but when you start completing them, the denseness of the content of an action rpg compared to an arcade-like pure action game takes over and this is definitely the meatier experience. However, revisiting the GBA games can feel pretty spotty and dated by today's standards. They feel like formative games that set the groundwork for what people think of metroidvania today and by the time you get to Aria you might just say "oh, they finally got their ♥♥♥♥ together" if you're used to modern titles. Or not. There's a good chance your new favorite metroidvania is in here and you might have a hotter take than mine. I think there's always room for more fans of these games but they won't be AAA blockbuster quality, but that doesn't mean they can't be loads of fun either.

_childDocuments_.review: As a long-time fan of the Castlevania series, the Advance Collection is a dream come true! This compilation brings together three of the best Game Boy Advance titles: Castlevania: Circle of the Moon, Castlevania: Harmony of Dissonance, and Castlevania: Aria of Sorrow.Nostalgia Factor:Right from the start, I was hit with a wave of nostalgia. The pixel art is beautiful and the soundtracks are timeless. Each game captures that classic Castlevania atmosphere perfectly, and it's amazing to see how these titles have influenced the series as a whole.Gameplay:Each game offers its own unique mechanics and strengths. Circle of the Moon’s card system is innovative, Harmony of Dissonance has fantastic level design, and Aria of Sorrow’s souls system is incredibly addictive. The controls are tight, and the gameplay feels smooth and responsive – perfect for dodging enemies and executing those classic whip combos!Quality of Life Features:The inclusion of save states and rewind features makes revisiting these classics a breeze. I can jump back into a challenging part without frustration, which is a huge plus for both new players and veterans alike. The ability to play on the go with a handheld mode is another fantastic feature!Extras:I also appreciate the bonus materials, like art galleries and music tracks. It shows that a lot of love went into this collection, making it more than just a simple port.Overall, the Castlevania Advance Collection is a must-have for fans and newcomers alike. It perfectly captures the essence of what makes Castlevania so special and offers hours of thrilling gameplay. If you haven't picked it up yet, I highly recommend diving into this hauntingly beautiful world!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a collection of the 3 Castlevania Gameboy Advanced titles that came out between 2001 to 2003. It also includes Dracula X, a NES title, but that feels like an afterthought, and being from 1995 is significantly older, and clunkier, than the others. Overall the steam version adds little to the original titles, just some options like allowing you to map controls, and includes a single small quality of life feature in each game.There is a couple of design sensibilities that this era of Castlevania games share. They all have little, to no real story. Go to castle, fight monsters, kill some version of dracula. Aria of Sorrow has the most story and it is still very ignoreable. Women are lucky if they get a single character in these games, and are generally relegated to damsels in distress or dracula fan girls. The weirdness found in some of the later titles tends to be toned down, with most monsters fitting a horror theme or greek myth. Each game has its own "gimmick" to add to the normal formula that gives you a few new abilities/spells. The games take around 10 hours to beat, give or take. Your character has white hair.Circle of the Moon was basically the reason I bought this collection, as I have fond memories of it as my first Castlevania game. I believe it holds up surprisingly well. In my opinion, despite the first of the three, it looks the best. Obviously the Gameboy Advance had a much, much smaller screen, but as far as pixel art goes its pretty good. Also the soundtrack is one of my favorites. The map layout is good, with distinct areas but lots of inter-connectivity. The controls are a bit clunky by modern standards but not even necessarily in a bad way, its just more deliberate and slow. Unfortunately the DSS system of gaining abilities through cards kind of suck, as you get few cards most of the game, with relatively minor abilities and all the fun stuff is gated behind the end game challenges after which you really don't need them anymore. Consumables suck, and are basically useless except in large quantity but cannot be purchased anywhere. The alternate weapons basically suck as well, except the crucifix which feels OP (feels like a vestigial system from previous games). Overall I love Circle of the Moon, and its a lot of fun to play, but even I have to admit that a lot of the mechanics need refinement. Next, time wise, is Harmony of Dissonance. The main feature here is that there are two castles. This one is by far my least favorite. I believe the art is worse quality than the other two, and I actively dislike most of the music. Worst of all, I really hate the castle layout. While it is probably the biggest of the maps, it is poorly connected and it is often very unclear where to go next. You will often spend ten, even fifteen minutes, traveling across the entire castle to a place you think you might make progress, only to discover thats not the case. Most progress is hidden by almost nonsensical discoveries that are hidden in random spots. But the one thing I do like is the controls; while in most games you jump and attack at the same time to stay mobile in the air, this game does the opposite where jump attacking locks your momentum, so you instead use the new dodge buttons and stay on the floor when able. I really like this way of playing, it felt very different from the other games. Unfortunately it was not enough to salvage the experience for me with all the other negatives.Last is Aria of Sorrow, and it will likely be most people's favorite. It has by far the best gameplay (note, this is the only one of the three that got a direct sequel and the soul system also directly inspired Bloodstained ritual of the night) where each monster can potentially give you an ability. The game is technically the most impressive, with the most advanced art assets, and the music is the most varied. Overall I don't like the anime aesthetic as much as Circle of the Moon, but it is well made. The castle layout is also good and fun to traverse. The story and characters are a bit dumb and a bit too campy if you ask me, but that is clearly intentional. Most of my complaints basically boil down to preference. The end result is that I really liked this game and suspect most people will like it even more than that.Overall the Castlevania Advanced collection is perfect for someone like me, who has warm feelings towards one of the titles and gets an experience of both nostalgia and something new. While the games are definitely dated, and not a good place to start with the Metroidvania genre in 2023, they are still fun and, for me at least, are right at the point where they are not too old yet.

_childDocuments_.review: The Castlevania advanced collection is a joy for the hardcore fans, Circle of the moon is prob the hardest one I've played of the series due to lack of shops and getting health has never been more problematic to say the least, what makes up for is the inclusion of the DSS cards that lets you combine an action and attribute to create godly combos to decimate foes and bosses with. The last form for Dracula never looked so god and actually demonic like. Aria of Sorrow was also a joy being able to use the souls of different enemies, a shop system, and an engaging story line with alternative endings. Dracula X was pretty epic with the rock music mixed with refreshing new spin on old classics like vampire killer or nightmare from the first castlevania, the sub weapons and super abilities made the game very enjoyable with alternative storylines too.

_childDocuments_.review: First time player, so no nostalgy coming in.Had no technical problems I read about in other reviews. It's just an emulation, that's true. Really fun games. They may be a bit old, but not to the point that I would be annoyed.Sadly, there is also CotM and X. X is, afaiu a remake of the first Castlevania. And it is clunky as heck! You move absolutely slow and have to get over really hard jumps, without any of the exploring I like about Metroidvanias. No Sir!CotM is not as bad as that, but still feels arduous (you can definitely feel the fact that this game is older than HoD and AoS).So all in all: If you want to have an official emulation of HoD and AoS, I can recommend this. _childDocuments_.review: This is worth purchasing just for Aria of Sorrow. I’ve played most of the Castlevania franchise and AoS is basically tied with SoTN for me as the best in the series, and it is a Top-10 MetroidVania regardless of which you think is better. Its music and visuals are clearly inferior as a GBA game, which might be a holdup for some. However its level design and combat are much tighter than SOTN IMHO. If you’ve played Bloodstained, the soul steal mechanic comes from this game also but I think Aria is much better than Bloodstained...On top of that, you get the other 2 GBA CV games. I like Circle of the Moon more than most. The level design and backtracking are handled well and it is pretty challenging. You’re stuck with the whip though and the DSS system is terrible. Harmony of Dissonance is a great choice for those that love the inverted castle in SOTN. It’s a lot more open ended and requires you to scour the map pretty thoroughly. There’s a stupid amount of bosses like SOTN but they’re not balanced very well because of the openness. CotM and HoD are both fine and better than 90% of the Metroidvanias on steam but neither is a must-play like Aria.lastly, don’t even play Dracula X. _childDocuments_.review: Before I got this port, the only Castlevania games I'd ever played were Super Castlevania 4 (for the SNES) and Castlevania Symphony of the Night (for the Playstation 1).  I'd heard about the premise of Aria of Sorrow and I was eager to see it first-hand.  Thus, I bought the collection for that one game, and everything else was a bonus.In the order I played the games:[1] Aria of SorrowThis game was a lot of fun to play mechanically for the most part.  The emulator gadget to track collected souls was a little annoying, especially because the first enemy it shows up for has a tediously small drop rate.  Soul grinding never felt necessary to advance, though, and the game did a good job implying where I had to go next.  I did find getting the 100% soul collection frustrating, mostly because several of the souls were hidden in places I'd've never thought to revisit without a guide telling me to go there.The plot...Well, it's a really interesting premise, but they clearly cut corners when they were translating this game.  The dialogue was tacky and didn't really contribute anything of substance to the game itself.  Summaries of the plot come out with a stronger sense of intrigue then the actual run through the scenario.  I know that Symphony of the Night had tacky dialogue like this too, but given the time and the number of games between Symphony and Aria I had hoped this game would be more concise and interesting.  The dialogue is definitely the weakest point of this game, so if you're coming in blind hoping for a great story you may find yourself disappointed; read a synopsis of it instead.Again, in my opinion Aria was a lot of fun to play, but not so much fun to read.[2] Circle of the MoonI launched this game immediately after I finished Aria, made my way to the first save point, and then tabled it for a few weeks.  After the smooth gameplay of Aria's Soma Cruz, the slow-moving Nathan Graves with his three-frame walk animation perturbed me greatly.  I would have left the game on the shelf indefinitely, but hey, I paid for it, so on a boring weekend I decided to give it another try.  I'm very glad I did.That opening is a TERRIBLE way to start a game.  You have to crawl through maybe 20 squares worth of rooms before you get an item that lets you double-tap to run.  Once you have this item, the game is LEAPS AND BOUNDS better.  Nathan is an impressive vampire hunter and he's very easy to control once he can actually run.  Also, his maneuver of spinning the whip in place is way cooler than old Simon's hold attack lazily leaving the chain to hang.  The DSS was an interesting mechanic but never felt necessary (except for in the Arena section of the castle, but that's a matter of 100% completion, which comes with that expectation of grindage).The bosses were challenging and a little spongey, and there was a large difficulty spike after the one in the tower, but I never felt lost in the castle or overly frustrated by the difficulty.  Like Aria, there were some things to be found in places I would never have considered checking without a guide, so if that kind of gameplay irritates you it's something to keep in mind.  Overall I greatly enjoyed Circle of the Moon.[3] Harmony of DissonanceThis game started off giving me a very bad impression.  Juste Belmont is slow, looks like an Alucard wannabe, has agonizingly bad animations and a ridiculous jumping pose that you have to watch OVER AND OVER because it's a platforming game... and has this goofy blue aura that's supposed to indicate he's magic but really just makes him clash more with every other graphic in the game.  I get this kind of graphic design for an old Gameboy with no backlight (drawing attention to the player character with high contrast palettes is common for the era), but this left me wishing the collection had come with an option to overlay replacement graphics on the character and environment... a second emulation layer with modern graphics, feeding down to the same core game mechanics.  I've seen remasters do this before, especially those with proprietary emulation.I pushed past the ugly because I'd paid for the game and I wanted to at least give it a chance.  I'm glad I did.  Harmony of Dissonance actually has a really intriguing plot, which the game does a good job portraying with low-key dialogue (it's not cheesy like Aria of Sorrow).  It really gave me a good idea of how Dracula's resurrection actually comes to happen in the Castlevania series, and about the formation of the chaotic Castlevania itself.Speaking of the castle, Harmony of Dissonance has a pretty cool one.  There are several places in the game where you have free reign to wander wherever you want, which called back to my experiences with Symphony of the Night.  They inevitably bottle-necked as the castle is relatively small, but it was nice to have a choice which way to go.  There were some things the game could have communicated better, like how the iris portals worked (even not closing the door with that animation would have been enough to tell me I needed to press UP in front of this thing).  Some of the hint cards were pretty useless, too, which was frustrating because of how important the hidden items they point to turned out to be.  Overall, though, Harmony of Dissonance was a pretty good play, and if like me you missed it on the original hardware (and if you can look past the bad animation) you should have fun with it.[4] Dracula XOf the games in the collection, this one was closest to Castlevania 4, the Castlevania with which I've had the most experience.  It's a stage-based light combat platformer, so you can expect the tropes of that game genre to all be in play here.  Richter has absolutely NO aerial control when jumping, though; he establishes his velocity and direction as the jump starts and locks in like a projectile until he lands.  This can be incredibly frustrating because a missed jump usually means you fall into a pit and die.  Or you get hit by one of the many obnoxiously placed bats and medusa heads and fall into a pit and die.  Or you get hit by Dracula and fall into a pit and die.  There's a lot of pit death.  Thankfully the emulator this collection uses has a rewind feature, which I abused shamelessly to get through this particular game.  I played it because I paid for it in the collection, but I don't think I'd play it again.To summarize: Aria of Sorrow was fun but the dialogue was a let-down.  Circle of the Moon starts bad but gets good very quickly.  Harmony of Dissonance is ugly, but if you can look past that it is a very compelling story and castle to explore.  Dracula X demands frequent rewinding to be playable, and probably isn't worth much of your time.

As far as I can tell, this is the inferior Super Nintendo version and not the excellent PC-88 version of Rondo Of Blood, which has previously been rereleased on the Wii and PSP so I can't imagine its a rights issue. It's still great to have this piece of Castlevania history preserved, don't get me wrong, but I can't help but want more.Still, three great games and one underwhelming one. Worth it. _childDocuments_.review: 4 classic games in one. Let's take a look at each one. Except Rondo of blood since this version sucks.Circle of the Moon.Can be described as poor man's Symphony of the night. The second game to implement the metroidvania format, the most memorable thing about this game is it's brutal boss fight. I would've taken a lot more time without the help of the reverse time feature. It also distinguished it self from the other Castlevania game with it's Dual Set-up System or DSS. This system allows Nathan the protagonist to modify his whip attacks, cast powerful spells or improve his stats. The down side is to this system is it can feel a little bit grindy to collect all the needed cards needed to activate said skills. For the story, well the Castlevania lore with it's long history across countless titles is great. Individually though, they are pretty generic and this one is no exception. Someone is trying to resurrect Dracula, the castle has risen back and it's your job to stop it, although this time they threw in a little bit of conflict between rivals to mix things up. Overall it is a fun and brutal experience and a decent attempt at a SotN follow up.Harmony of Dissonance.The first thing that you will notice with this Castlevania entry is it's art style. It is loud, flamboyant, and vivid. Your character,  Juste Belmont wears a bright red coat and is outlined with a bright blue glow, the bats are outlined with red glowing red and the sky is bright purple. It can be a turnoff for some, and I personally find it distracting at first, but as soon as the monsters starts showing up I quickly changed my opinion. The monster design in this Castlevania is simply awesome, they are vivid, detailed and well animated. The hulking armored giants are my personal favorites. The combat is faster than Circle of the moon as you have a dedicated dash button to go left and right. Juste can also use Spell books that allows you to modify the effects of your subweapon. This obviously makes subweapons more important than other Castlevania entries. Harmony of dissonance is significantly easier than Circle of the Moon. The bosses in particular are not much of a challenge but they are more abundant this time around, and again they are all eye candies. My least favorite part of Harmony of dissonance is the level design. There are a lot of paths that will lead you in too deep only to find your self in a dead end since you don't have the right skill to continue yet causing you to backtrack. Circle of the moon usually have shortcuts that would lead you back to the entrance or other part of the castle to alleviate this, but sadly Harmony of Dissonance does not have this shortcuts. This, combined with the fact that you're gonna have to traverse two castle with almost the same layout, makes exploration extremely painful and I found myself not knowing where to go next without the aid of outside guide. The Story is surprisingly similar to Circle of the moon with the rivals plot point and a little bit of the classic damsel in distress thrown in. To summarize, despite the confusing layout of the Castle and painful exploration, it's wonderful art style, abundance of monsters and boss fights I still had a good time playing Harmony of Dissonance.Aria of Sorrows.This one's really. I mean that's really all I can say with Aria of Sorrows. It's art style might not be as memorable as Harmony of Dissonance but the game play is far superior to both CotM and HoD. The controls feels good and the protagonist Soma even has the same moonwalk type back dash as Alucard in SotN. I also think that it strikes a perfect balance between challenge and accessibility.
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Advance Collection

_childDocuments_.review: 3 solid metroidvanias and 1 very cruel action-platformer. I had never played a Castlevania game before this collection and I can say most of the games in here are very enjoyable even for a first-time-player. The games are solid, but the collection itself has some issues:-Can't change settings from the main menu.-Controller is the only viable way to play.-The only way to get fullscreen is to press Alt + Enter-The only way to close the game, besides forcing it to close with Alt + F4 or similar methods, is to start a game, enter the collection menu, and choosing end game while holding LB + RB on a controller.-The helper gadgets cover parts of the game screen whenever they pop up, but atleast they can be turned off in the collection menu.If you can tolerate the above issues there are some nice games to play.----Circle of the Moon---:Overall: 7/10+A good challenge+Great soundtrack+A few great bosses-A whole lot of fighting different colors of armor.-Very uneven difficulty-It's almost down to luck if you can dodge any attack that rains projectiles.-A few too many rooms contain the same enemy encounter copy-pasted several times with no variation.---Harmony of Dissonance---:Overall: 8/10+The most unique in the collection+The map is something of a navigational puzzle that is fun to solve+Dashing everywhere-A bit too easy to cheese with no limit on healing items and some magic combinations being extremely strong-Most bosses don't do much---Aria of Sorrow---:Overall: 9/10+Feels the most polished of the games in this collection+Great soundtrack+Great pixelart+Souls and getting to use weapons other than a whip gives you options-Felt a bit short.-Exploration rewards feel a bit underwhelming when it's only gear and consumables instead of also including health and MP upgrades like the previous two games---Dracula X---:Overall: 6/10+Very satisfying to conquer.+Great soundtrack-This game hates you and will do its best to kill you instantly as often as it can-No ingame saving. This is the only one in the collection I used savestates in-(Collection options) You can only get a full height 4:3/8:7 image with a CRT filter on it while the other games can do full height with no filter.

Etc.Only thing I wish it had was a borderless fullscreen option, luckily you can just hit "Alt +Enter" after the game launches or use the "-windowed -noborder" launch option on Steam or if you're on a good Linux distro that supports undecorating out of box it makes life easy. _childDocuments_.review: I mainly bought this collection for Aria of Sorrow, my favorite Castlevania game. I had previously fully completed it on the GBA, but I wanted to jump back in and do it again on PC. The collection is worth it for this game alone. The soul system adds a substantial amount of depth to the combat, and the castle itself is fun to explore and is bursting with personality. However, I think COTM and HOD are also incredible games worth your time. Also, you get Dracula X as an added bonus, a more traditional Castlevania from the Super Nintendo that acts as a fun distraction from the GBA entries. This collection is a really great showcase of some of the best the series has to offer, and there is plenty of content to keep you occupied for many hours, especially if you're a completionist.Thankfully, the games run how they are supposed to, and I appreciate the wealth of customization options like being able to change what buttons do, create save states, conveniently rewind without having to go into a menu, and the option of playing region specific versions of the games (which is great for speedrunners). Also, as is typical with these sort of collections, there's also an art gallery and sound test for those who want to appreciate the art and music (which is incredible btw).Overall, I highly recommend this collection. You won't be disappointed. Also, I think this goes without saying, but if you enjoy the Metroidvania genre in general, this is not a collection you should pass up by any means.Also, on a related note, I hope that Konami eventually gives us a collection of the DS games, especially with how expensive those games are nowadays on the secondhand market. I'd buy that collection in an heart beat! Also wouldn't hurt to throw in SOTN "wink wink".

_childDocuments_.review: I'm an absolute shill for the castlevania series as it's classic platforming and frustratingly fun difficulty at it's finest. I've played all of these games in the past on GBA but having a nice compact collection of honestly my favorite games in the series really makes it worth it to just experience the lesser known games in the series. Circle of the moon I'll say holds up pretty well even now but movement is a bit slow until you get a grasp of how to use the dash and realize certain spell card combinations are actually broken. It's a classic in my book as it's one of the first games I played on my GBA growing up and even now it gave me the hours of grinding rooms just to level up for bosses and that nice itch of exploration that you get with every igavania game. Harmony of Dissonance is honestly the weakest game on this collection for me. I mean it's actually pretty fun figuring out how the spell books work with sub items and btw the book subitem with ice spell is actually broken and fun to use against bosses to make things quite a bit easier especially in that dracula fight phase 2. I have nostalgia for the game so despite it being the weakest game on the collection I'll honestly say it's still a fun game to sit down and play but be ready because the castle map is confusing since it has the gimmick of there being two castles you'll switch between during parts of the game. Also if you're going for all the dracula parts they're not overly difficult to find but just be sure you go into the castle B entrance to the final boss because that is the only way you can trigger the true ending.Aria of Sorrow aka ABSOLUTE KINO aka ONE OF THE GREATEST VIDEO GAMES EVER CREATED!!! Okay just let me say first off messing around with the soul system and having different archtypes that will either give you attacks, summon familiars, or even in the case of things like Minotaur boost your attack power let's you really get creative on how you take on bosses and makes grinding rooms and enemies actually rewarding especially for the more rare souls. Usually I tend to go with Beam Skeleton, Buer, and MInotaur for later parts of the game but early on I'll say Winged Skeleton is actually a good soul to use for ranged attacks. Aria of Sorrow as a game holds up incredibly well even now since the grinding is honestly fair except on some of the more rare souls where I could spend 20 minutes just grinding for a soul while I had absolute crazy luck and got flame demon on my first try. DO keep in mind to get the true end you'll need to get and equip the Flame Demon, Giant Bat, and Succubus souls before entering the throne room. I could talk about this game for hours on end and tell you how amazing it really is but go play it for yourself and see the masterpiece IGA created.Dracula X is honestly alright. It's not the best game when Rondo of Blood exists. (Konami where is the steam port of Rondo/Symphony of the Night?) I don't have much to say about it since as I am writing this review I have only played the first stage of the game and tbh I just question why Rondo wasn't in this collection.An absolute solid collection of 3 great games and 1 kinda mid game but overall anything that has Aria of Sorrow gets an automatic 10/10 from me. Go experience the pure amazingness that is the GBA castlevania games!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Advance Collection

_childDocuments_.review: Played these for the first time thanks to the advance collection. Played through Aria of Sorrow and Harmony of Dissonance. They're both great in their own right. Aria of Sorrow has much more fluidity and much less confusion. Harmony of Dissonance's castle structure is difficult to follow and understand so be prepared to use a walkthrough in a few parts so you don't waste too much time.
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Advance Collection

_childDocuments_.review: Vania almost never disappoints. Price is worth it for Aria alone and while COTM, HOD and DracX have their problems they're also still great. Short description for each game.DracX-The only linear game here. No not as good as Rondo but overall a decent classicvania.COTM-Very barebones Search Action, to steal from the journos "the Dark Souls of Search Action". Most difficult game in the collection, interesting magic system by combining cards picked up, tons of different combos to experiment with.HOD- Feels like a 2D version of Lament of Innocence, utilizing that game's subweapon system. You equip spellbooks to combine with your held subweapon for some powerful results. Attacking while jumping makes for some weirdness but still an addictive Search Action with an underrated soundtrack (if you can get over compression)AOS-The best game in the collection, perhaps in the whole franchise. Controls incredibely, the main gimmick comes from gaining abilities from enemies, which you can then equip whenever you want. Each one is different and useful in different situations. You'll find yourself testing many different loadouts. It's the shortest and easiest of the Search Actions but it goes for quality over quantity. Pretty easy but Hard Mode is more than worth it once you complete the game. Also some incredible tunes and one of the best (if most ridiculous) stories in the franchise.

And the battle system is great.Arya of Sorrow is way shorter but as a whole, considering story, scenarios and progress (bsides battle) is a little better game. _childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Advance Collection

_childDocuments_.review: The GBA classics and then some - what more needs to be said?  Aria of Sorrow is perhaps the most legendary of the GBA titles as it takes what Symphony of the Night did and expands upon it further with weapon variety + the souls system that would be used by IGA once more in Bloodstained: Ritual of the Night.  Overall a very fun adventure and well worth the price tag alone.Circle of the Moon takes the classic gameplay of the whip-wielding Belmonts and mixes it with the IGAvania format which just feels *chef's kiss*, coupled with the DSS cards to collect and multiple 'classes' to play through the game as after the first playthrough.   Harmony of Dissonance is somewhat of the black sheep of the GBA titles, and yet it's got its charms and systems as well.Then there's Dracula X, essentially an SNES re-imagining of Rondo of Blood, one of the last pre-IGA era Castlevania titles.DS collection, Rondo, and SotN are sorely needed now, and please Konami don't forget the underrated gem that was Harmony of Despair.   My wallet is waiting.

_childDocuments_.review: Worth it for Circle of the Moon and Aria of Sorrow alone, at a reasonable price point. _childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Advance Collection

_childDocuments_.review: The years 2001, 2002, and 2003 were good years for the Gameboy Advance for a multitude of reasons, but the three Castlevania games that were released each year certainly testify to its greatness. When 2001 came about, the Gameboy Advance was launched, with Castlevania: Circle of the Moon as one of its launch games, and in spite of some of the game's clunky mechanics with the controls, it was a very popular game, and I recall playing it endlessly through all five modes. In 2002, Castlevania: Harmony of Dissonance hit the stores, and indeed polished up on the clunky controls, and though the music was slightly wonky at times, was still an amazing game with tons of replayability, having both "Maxim Mode", and a Boss Rush Mode. Apparently Circle of the Moon also wanted to make Hugh playable in a New Game + styled manner, but instead opted for the five different modes to play as Nathan Graves. Finally in 2003, we had Castlevania: Aria of Sorrow come out, which blew both preceding GBA games clear out of the water with it's awesome controls, awesome music, and sheer versatility with the "Souls" system, in which you could combine Bullet Souls, Guardian Souls, and Enchanted Souls to blitz through the game (and one very special combination of souls which allows you to access the true ending with a certain boss). Aria of Sorrow was a great way to conclude the overall evolution of the GBA Castlevania games, which in my personal opinion, outshined the PS2 Castlevania games.So should you buy this collection for Steam? Are you kidding me? Of course you should! Granted, some of the music which sounded great for it's day for the GBA's limited sound capabilities has not aged well for most modern PC's, but that's simply a punch you'll have to roll with (or just mute the music). It comes complete with an encyclopedic reference for each game, including all enemies, items, lore, and other fun stuff associated with each game, and if the price seems to steep for you folks, you can always wait to buy it on sale.10/10, would recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Advance Collection

_childDocuments_.review: Solid and definitive metroidvania games.An improvement on the previous Castlevania collection as there are now multiple save slots, the controller configuration appears to be fully customizable, and there are encyclopedias and gadgets to aid in treasure hunting. There are also more wallpapers. I'd still like to see more options for graphics filters. There's now a feature to make a playlist of tracks from the games.I somehow manage to keep pressing the rewind button, though maybe that's just my fault, and I couldn't find any option to exit the game from the title screen.
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Advance Collection

_childDocuments_.review: A decent collection of Castlevania titles, mostly in the Metroidvania style. There's a single Classicvania among them, and it's hard, so be prepared for that. Classicvania is wildly different from Metroidvania.Is the collection the best titles in the franchise? Not even close, but even the worst game in the franchise is pretty solid, for what it's worth.Circle of the Moon is a non-canon and kind of clunky entry in the Metroidvania style. Early GBA, and it feels like it, but it's still enjoyable.Harmony of Dissonance is good, though the character animations leave a little bit to be desired, for me. Aria of Sorrow is easily the best of the three Metroidvanias in this collection. Rock solid.Dracula X is the Classicvania, and it's great. The adventure of Richter Belmont is among the classic Belmont games.In the end, if you like Castlevania, this collection will give you many, many hours of enjoyable game time. If you don't, Aria may change your mind, grab it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Advance Collection

_childDocuments_.review: As this is a collection, I'll be reviewing the games individually of the ones I've playedCastlevania Circle of the moonCastlevania Circle of the Moon is a blend between Older Belmont style castlevania games mixed with the Metroidvania style introduced by Symphony of the Night, It's a solid time with it's rpg elements and exploration making it a solid time if you have it, it's difficult and enjoyable, it's got some weird mechanics like double tapping in a direction to run instead of just running normally but a lot of these minor things can slide cause they're so irrelevant with time, You play as a character named Nathan Graves and the game takes place outside the Castlevania Continuity.The music for Castlevania Circle of the Moon is very solid, some tracks just fit the area so well and make it a surprising pleasure you wouldn't expect from a handheld titleCastlevania Harmony of DissonanceCastlevania Harmony of Dissonance is a well hidden gem among the GBA library. The gameplay is incredibly enjoyable with a nice pacing to it, being the regular whip from the Classicvania games, it feels like they took some slight inspiration from the classicvanias while still making it a Post Symphony of the Night Quality game as a metroidvania. The colours are vibrant the areas are distinct and the bosses and magic system while can be considered simple and easy, are a joy to go through. But the Music is very forgettable, being a mix between the game being rushed out, and the GBA just not having good sound output. I would absolutely recommend this game as it's incredibly enjoyable to play especially if you're a fan of metroidvanias, there is a slight bit too much backtracking with no way of speeding up said backtracking till far later in the game. it's a solid 8/10 game that I would not mind experiencing again.Castlevania Aria of SorrowCastlevania Aria of Sorrow is a beautiful and absolutely brilliant game. it may be one of the very best in the castlevania series in everything except musicIn terms of gameplay, it is easily one of the best, with area designs and gameplay mechanics being unbelievably amazing for the Game Boy Advance, and the story being easy to follow yet also interesting and how it explains the Main Character's abilities is also very well done. I absolutely recommend this game as it may be one of the best in the series, if you have the ability to do so, play this gameI do not recommend Dracula X, that game is garbage.
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Advance Collection

_childDocuments_.review: While I prefer the DS entries in the series, the GBA titles are all solid entries in their own rights. Circle of the Moon feels a bit slow and stiff to play, but the DSS system allows for some pretty entertaining possibilities, and the alternate game modes you unlock by beating the game are interesting and add replayability to the game.Harmony of Dissonance gets a bad rap, but the increased speed and mobility are a breath of fresh air after the plodding movement of Circle of the Moon. I personally liked the two castles, as it felt like a bit of a throwback to SOTN, but I realize not everyone will appreciate the confusion it can cause while trying to navigate. Not much to say here, it's not amazing, but it's not bad either.Aria of Sorrow is the clear stand out title in this collection. The Tactical Soul System gives you an impressive amount of versatility in how you play, though there are certain set ups you'll find yourself having to switch back to pretty regularly. The story is the most enjoyable in this collection as well, and is continued in the DS follow-up Dawn of Sorrow, which I hope will be included in a future collection. Rondo of Blood is sort of a weird inclusion here. It's more in-line with the older, more linear Castlevanias, but it's still a good title, and this collection makes it more easily available (though it would be nice if it had been included with Symphony of the Night, as that game follows it up, and they've been bundled together in the past several times.)

_childDocuments_.review: Outstanding value. You can see I already put 60+ hours just into Circle of the moon by itself!Yes, there are ways to speedrun most Igavanias if you are really into that sort of sport but I believe doing that robs people of the "experience" of simply exploring many lovingly crafted areas each with their own decor,dark secrets,and haunted atmosphere. "That" and you are "rewarded" for being thorough,looking for secrets,acquiring items that aid you in overcoming environmental obstacles, and going toe to toe with some of the tougher monsters hidden away in the shadows.Though these games are old they hold up well to more recent offerings. To me COTM was every bit as enjoyable as BloodStained : Ritual Of The Night or the classic Symphony Of The Night despite a few imperfections. (Such as needlessly tedious grinding to get certain items or magic card drops) That says something considering COTM is often considered the "black sheep" of the gameboy advance trilogy. It was the one game Koji Igarashi didn't work on personally with his own team and yet the surprisingly great soundtrack,imaginative sprite-work,tried and true metroidvania styled progression,and card-pairing magic/ability system all make for a memorable authentic Castlevania outing.Chances are at least one game among Circle Of The Moon,Harmony Of Dissonance,or Aria Of Sorrow will tickle your fancy. Many fans consider Aria the best balanced strongest entry for good reason but Dissonance did make it's own improvements such as adding a merchant (Yes,finally you can buy certain items DIRECTLY without having to be at the mercy of random drops!) and making Juste Belmont move more gracefully than COTM's protagonist Nathan Graves. "Weaknesses" of Harmony Of Dissonance seem to be the more minimalist chip-tune esque soundtrack (Though it still has its' appreciators),repetitively themed bosses,oddly garish color palette, and that beat by beat its' story of two rival hunters is very similar to COTM's. (Only take out a father figure whilst adding a love interest)I would elaborate more on Aria's story but though it probably already is known to many I don't want to ruin it for those that have yet to experience it. Rest assured it's "very good" with a lot of original ideas centered around eternal love,past lives,reincarnation,and how Dracula's castle is a living sentient being and a "character" onto itself. (Soma can also steal abilities from the monsters he faces or enslave them to his will. He's like a moodier version of Pokemon's Ash Ketchum!)As for Vampire's Kiss/Dracula X? It is a very flawed snes port of Rondo Of Blood that does not allow the option to play as a young Maria Renard whom was originally Richter Belmont's partner. (Yes,the same Maria Renard from SOTN only in that game she's all grown up!) This is sad as Rondo was an important  prequel to SOTN and where Koji obviously got the most inspiration from. (It and CV 3: Dracula's curse. Later on he also used Bloodlines as a springboard when making Portrait Of Ruin.)"But" it manages to still be a fun old skool Castlevania experience that has a more unforgiving difficulty and more straight forward level design. It also looks gorgeous and sounds rocking despite being the inferior bastardized "remix". To me this is a definitive collection which offers multiple quality games that offer maximum immersion and maximum enjoyment at a minimalist price. Sharpen those stakes and salt those whips,hunters. We're going in! Pros+Good collection of all the Igavania games that debuted on the GB Advance including the multiple localised versions.+Easy interface.+Beautiful artwork by Ayami Kojima!+The ability to "quick save" anywhere or even "rewind" your progression. (Refer to the interface that also includes item descriptions,an extensive bestiary,and what creatures will drop what items.)+Potentially hundreds of hours of gameplay if you want to take in all the sights,slay all the baddies,and level up as well as outfit your protagonists to their maximum potential.+You can re-map the buttons if you so desire.+Every game has a truly marvelous collection of songs with some hitting the nostalgic sweet-spot more than others. Michiru Yamane is the most well known composer but the composers whom worked on COTM cranked out some brilliant ear-candy too!Cons-None I can think of though some have called this a "bad port job" whilst critiquing it. Perhaps they have had issues but the games perform slick as butter on my rig with no hiccups or crashes. Any "technical difficulties" I had were due to factors outside of me me running the CV Advance collection.-It was a strange decision to add Vampire's Kiss/Dracula X but not Rondo Of Blood.

_childDocuments_.review: When I got this, the wave of nostalgia hit hard. I grew up more on the MetroidVanias than the ClassicVanias and this is a nice lil collection.Aria and Harmony are still pretty good. While Aria is like my definitive MetroidVania from this era due to the variety it has, I feel that the balancing is way better in Harmony. Also I don't remember Aria having so few bosses while Harmony had so many but like I said, if you want variety, I suggest Aria. If you want something a lil more difficult, go for Harmony. Never finished Circle of the Moon since playing that game felt like your character had lead weights on him. Not as fun to control as the two previous games imo.As for the collection itself, I like a lot of the functionality such as reversing time but I wish the control mapping was better. Some special attacks are up + attack button but I wish there was an option to make that just one button akin to something like the CastleVania Dracula X Chronicles on the PSP where you could do that in the control settings of that game.Overall, still a fun time. It's also a nice time capsule of what MetroidVanias were like back then compared to now.
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Advance Collection

_childDocuments_.review: With companies like nintendo setting the example for how NOT to handle emulation and old titles it's great to see konami blowing it out of the water with a crisp release like this. Not only is it the original games ported to run in a modern environment, but they come with features you'd expect of running them in a third party emulator (save states, rewind, etc.) as a first-party developer AND they include widgets, art books and encyclopedias baked into the app that you can pull up at any time with a tap of a controller key. For instance in Aria of Sorrow when you kill an enemy there is a small popup that will tell you if you have that creatures soul or not as well as you being able to look for which monster drops something you're looking for in the encyclopedia. Should you not want the extra widgets or the higher quality music/graphics and are simply looking for a cleanly emulated experience you can do that as well with both hardware original sound and pixel-perfect options.Also this is one of the extremely rare cases where controller controls are so well done, even with the extended features, that I forgo playing this at my desk entirely. In my harsh and cynical opinion you cannot go wrong.
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Advance Collection

_childDocuments_.review: I ended up liking Harmony of Dissonance the most, great movement, cool character, fun spells and sub-weapons. The down side is that the game is on the easy side.The others offer more challenge, but not always in the fairest or most intriguing way. Circle of the Moon goes from hard to easy to hard. If you spend time grinding it out and getting all the spells and knickknacks the game probably gets a little easier. I had it rough toward the end stretch because I was under leveled; I just wanted to finish the game.When it came to Dawn of Sorrow, I'm the most disappointed. It was just irritating to play. Many screens of that game is: walking into a room and immediately being pestered by irritating enemies, they usually don't deal too much damage, but it's just ANNYYOING as hell; with no room what so ever to fight or maneuver it really got on my nerves. I screamed at my PC playing DoS, but that's me, and I'm a freak.Dracula X is not my kind of CV-game, I know about it, seen many speed runs on it and Rondo. Fine game, not my cup of tea.All in all, a very solid collection. Remember these are freaking GBA-games, and they still manage to evoke a strong sense of the Castlevania mid-year games. Great stuff, I'm hoping for the DS ones and the PS2 ones! I remember Order of Ecclesia kicking my ass and a struggled my way through on the 3DS, I want another go at it with a big screen and a real controller.
