Because it's 3d some of the hotspots don't line up completely all the time. And it's pretty short. Otherwise I definitely enjoyed every minute of this game. The mind palace is almost like Dr Strange seeing all possible outcomes. Choices do seem to matter. And the detective element is pretty cool. I just wish it were longer. _childDocuments_.review: Twin Mirror is a narrative driven adventure game about an ex-journalist Sam Higgs, who returns to a small town of Basswood after he finds out about the death of his close friend. Once in town, he soon discovers that his friend’s death might not be an accident, as it was ruled by the police, and sets on to investigate it with the help of his unique analytical abilities and his imaginary friend. Visually, Twin Mirror looks okay, except for the animation. It’s rather disappointing for a game that tries to be cinematic. One of the most interesting things in Twin Mirror is so-called “Mind Palace” - a visual reconstruction of the crime scene, as Sam tries to put the pieces of the puzzle together and figure out what really happened. Its visual design is really well done, even if investigations themselves are fairly simple. You don’t have much freedom in them. The game will only progress once you find all the clues you need to find and make all the correct guesses. You can’t miss something or make a wrong deduction. The game itself is really “on the rails”. There are only a handful of choices throughout the game and they don’t really do that much. The story is okay. It unfolds very fast. It took me about 8 hours to beat it, and I was taking my time and exploring as much as I could.  On top of that, some amount of time was eaten by sections where you go inside your mind to fight off a panic attack or do some introspection. There are some interesting ideas about mental health and problems with socializing, but they’re not properly explored, they’re just scratching the surface. Twin Mirror is a short distraction of a game with some interesting ideas that drown in its overall mediocrity. I mostly enjoyed it, but it was a rather forgettable experience.

_childDocuments_.review: If this game wasn't so short it may have been one of DONTNOD's better releases, instead we get characters with no real personalities and a plot that feels unfulfilled. _childDocuments_.name: Twin Mirror

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who often spend a lot of time living inside my own head, I really enjoyed the way that this game portrays the protagonist's inner world, and in particular I thought that the "mind palace" was really pretty.  (Having said that, I'm a bit of a sucker for shiny visuals; my wife, who occasionally looked over my shoulder, didn't care for them as much, though she agrees that the art design was very striking.)Another thing that I really liked that so many of the choices were difficult because they really made me think hard about what the likely consequences would be, and even in cases where one choice seemed to me to be the more "correct" choice I still found myself hesitating to make it because there were so many downsides associated with it as well.  This is in contrast to many games where the choices are less about trying to figure out what the optimal choice is in a given situation and more about deciding which "alignment" (good, bad, lawful, chaotic, etc.) you want to be (though many of the choices did come with an explicit or implicit choice of alignment).One important caveat, though: this game is not one that I would automatically recommend to everyone because it is a game for a very specific kind of taste.  In my opinion it is very good at being the kind of game it is trying to be, but you may or may not like the kind of game it is trying to be.
_childDocuments_.name: Twin Mirror

_childDocuments_.review: I have gone back and  forth in my head if this game is good or not. I don't think its a bad game in any means but when you compare this game to other games by the developers it falls short. There are some great mechanics which are interesting but there are other elements of the game that feel lack luster. For example, the character models....are honestly not the most appealing. The story is decent but can be boring at times, even the layout of the pause menu looks "Meh".  There is a huge plot point in the game that is not addressed until the ending and even then it is not clear what decision you should make. The game does have a really cool investigation feature which I think is neat but everything else just feel average. Maybe I am being unfair by comparing it to their other games. I dont think its a bad game but I did expect more.

I really enjoy games that are choice driven but the choices in this game didn't feel like they had much impact on the rest of the game. _childDocuments_.name: Twin Mirror

_childDocuments_.review: The title of the most unremarkable and mediocre game goes to... Twin Mirror! And its protagonist Sam, a middle aged white blonde guy from West Virginia. He's a reporter of some boring newspaper and recently went back to his hometown to visit the wake of his childhoodfriend. But actually he doesn't want to. Well, that pretty much sums it up. Sam has some kind of inner ego that talks to himself and is annoying as hell (and actually only suggest the opposite  of anything you can do, it doesn't really add any interesting choice in the game). Sam also likes to remember stuff from the past which plays out in cutscenes as "memento" - unfortunately you can't skip those scenes or anything in the game itself at all. I was very surprised about this uninspired game fron Don't Nod because I enjoyed their other games (Life is strange, Don't tell me why etc). Not all of them were brilliant but at least they were never boring and dull. The protagonist feels lifeless and dull, the other characters he meets look like made out of plastic and feel uninspired, too. The dialogues are, most of the time, pointless and forgettable. I really REALLY tried my best to play Sam as a complete ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ (and also tried to let him die, which I failed unfortunately) but the games narrative gave him way too much credit for everything. The choices one can make in the game are pretty unexciting and most of the time they don't change a lot (or the game just gives you the feeling to HAVE a choice at all) and even the most "major" decision feels so mundane (you can decide if you keep Sams ego called "him", or not). There are also some puzzles and minigames involved but they also feel very bland. If you get the clues in the investigations wrong you are just forced to watch another unskippable cutscene again and again - there's no consequences for getting things wrong. I can't recommend the game at ALL. Poorly written characters, uninspired story, boring graphics and lifeless animations of the characters emotions. The soundtrack is noneexistant and the only funny thing that happens is that you can play Pac Man in one of the first chapters. If you REALLY like to play an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ character - well, you can't even do that properly because in some scenes the game forces you to be "nice" and  caring towards other people. Anyway, don't spend money on this, please.
_childDocuments_.name: Twin Mirror

_childDocuments_.review: Twin Mirror is a narrative-driven psychological thriller developed by DONTNOD Entertainment, the creators of Life is Strange. Released on Steam, the game offers a single-player experience that focuses on story, character development, and decision-making. You play as Sam Higgs, a former investigative journalist who returns to his hometown for a friend’s funeral, only to become entangled in a mystery involving secrets, memories, and self-reflection.Twin Mirror reminds me a lot of “Fahrenheit” on PS2 which is also available on Steam.This game has a unique “Mind Palace” mechanic, where Sam processes memories and explores alternate possibilities to piece together clues. The story is very intriguing and character-focused, with a darker tone.Visually, Twin Mirror uses a detailed art style and atmospheric settings to heighten the sense of mystery, the game is suited for fans of narrative adventures who enjoy branching storylines with moral consequences like me.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, I recommend it for it being a cozy little story game if you have a day off.But why thumbs down? THE PRICE.30 Bucks for a game this short, shorter than LIS Saga and still more expensive. I dont get it.I was bored the first 3 hours and that was already halfway in. I didnt even get attached to other characters than Sam.Who is Sam? Who is HIM? What was going on in Sams childhood? Why wont we cover more of Annas and Sam unfinished relationship? Why was the Plot Twist so... short and abrupt when the story almost ended?It dragged out many moments where you had to find clues in an open area but kept it short on moments where it MATTERED.I LOVED the mind place, I loved every single bit about it.But who is Sam?It is a forgettable game.
_childDocuments_.name: Twin Mirror

_childDocuments_.review: It's a gorgeous game, like really really pretty. Basswood feels just as bleak as the story makes it to be. The atmosphere is nailed down perfectly. What I appreciate about this game though, is writing and by that I don't mean the story but the people of Basswood instead. Each person that is introduced in the story and setup is quite memorable, it has that small town feeling in the spades. The dialogues are well written, voice acting is fantastic. OST is pretty nice and used only in key areas. It's not overdone. I like the the overall package even if the story kind of does take a minor hit in third act, it's far from bad. It's actually a well written story. Definitely recommend giving it a try. The game is 6 hours long on average but it's good that it's not trying to be 12-15 hour long game unnecessarily. It's like a limited run series which really did a good job of keeping me hooked.  8.5/10 worth playing... on sale most likely if it's like 30-50% off?Oh and ♥♥♥♥ those people who say Sam Higgs got no personality. He's pretty awesome and his inner voice is very nice too.
_childDocuments_.name: Twin Mirror

_childDocuments_.review: The music and the athmosphere of this game is pretty nice, I really enjoy the dead-end little town vibe.I really enjoyed the visual aspect of the game, and the main character's struggle between being connected to other people vs preferring to live in his own mind are both relatable. However there are some story elements that I think are quite jarring. The game basically forces you to be nice with your ex-girlfriend for some weird inexplicable reason, and I think that's just cringe on a level I could barely put up with. You as a player didn't have a say in that relationship at all, you were basically forced into a doormat position and couldn't even pretend that you should have some level of dignity. The murder mystery plot of the game was not detailed enough either, elthough it was serviceable. All in all it was a good game, but I won't be playing it again, because there are no consequences and player-agency is very very lacking.

_childDocuments_.review: I can recommend this one, but let me be clear, only for like $9.99 or less.  It is NOT a $29.99 game......  Its a narrative driven story like most of Dontnod's stuff.  I enjoyed the detective/journalist aspect, and the idea of the mind palace was awesome, even started to get a little dark and creepy like that one part of Life is Strange, which was a bonus.  It's fun to creep around and investigate stuff.  But I will say.....   it was a little lackluster, borderline depressing at the end.  There are two main pathways to take in the game..... and let's just say no matter which one you pick, the upside is not enough to diminish the downside, so you're left feeling kinda bummed!  I wish it could've focused more on solving gruesome murders rather than dry dialogues trying to make your moody ex feel better.  Mild aggravations to be had as once again the main villain and his legmen are all whyte mayles!  No surprise coming from racist Dontnod.  But at least it wasn't laid on as thick this time.  Kinda.  Environments were fun and interesting and looked cool.  OMG though don't DARE walk out of the scene in the wrong direction, it will spin you around 180 degrees super slowly and give you motion sickness.  Man, make that more smooth!!!!Chief complaint 1: It was SUPER short.  SO so short.  Not worth the price tag, should be 10 bucks. Chief complaint 2: Just because the protagonist is a white male, don'tnod, you didn't have to make him the ugliest mofo main character known to man lol.  It's like playing as a stork.  Coulda' made him a big beautiful Nord.  Or even just average.

_childDocuments_.review: Twin Mirror Review by the Magnificent BastardAlright, listen up, you beautiful bastards... I’ve played some real garbage in my day, but Twin Mirror takes the cake, chokes on it, and vomits it back up. Allow me to break this one down for you.First off, the plot. Christ, what a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ mess. You start out thinking you’re about to dive into some gripping detective yarn, but no, it peters out faster than... well something that peters out rather quickly. Anticlimactic doesn’t even begin to cover it. It’s like gearing up for a car chase and ending up in bumper-to-bumper traffic. The story falls flat, no twist, no payoff. Just a lot of pointless buildup for a lousy payoff. Narrative blue-balls.Now let’s talk puzzles/mini-games/QTEs. You’d think they’d be a break from the snooze fest, but no, they’re a fresh hell of their own. Half the time you don’t know what the ♥♥♥♥ you’re actually supposed to be doing. Feels as if one is trying to read hieroglyphics with a hangover. There’s no real guidance, no useful clues, just a whole lot of frustration. I’ve had more fun watching paint dry.And the characters. Good God man! They drone on and on and on, like they’re getting paid by the word. Exposition is supposed to be engaging, but listening to these guys is like having your ears waterboarded. They never shut the ♥♥♥♥ up. Every line is a slog through a swamp of verbosity. It’s a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ chore to sit through their endless prattle.Then there’s the character models. Christ on a cracker, they’re the stuff of nightmares. Uncanny valley? More like uncanny bottomless pit. They look like something out of a botched wax museum. Eyes dead as a fish on Friday, faces stiffer than a corpse in January. I haven’t slept well since playing this, and it’s not because I’m haunted by the plot, it’s those ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ faces lurking in the shadows of my nightmares.The only glimmer of fun in this dreck is a chance to play Pac-Man at the bar. Yes, dear reader, you heard me right. The most fun you’ll have in this entire game is a few rounds of Pac-Man. And from there, it’s all downhill. It’s a sad state of affairs when a decades-old arcade game outshines your entire modern-day production.In short, Twin Mirror is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ disaster. Do yourself a favor and steer clear of this one. Life’s too short to waste on half-baked, anticlimactic, visually horrifying drivel. Now, if you’ll excuse me, I need a stiff drink to wash the taste of this turd out of my mouth...Bastard out.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't really have much to say about this game in all honesty.I really enjoy DONTNOD's games, and I feel like this one sort of just "happened"? I don't think I've seen anyone talk about this game as loudly as people usually talk about "a new LIS game coming out" and I kinda see why.I'll start off with saying it was fairly interesting. _childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games that really just deserves a giant "meh" rating. Read on if you want to know why I landed where I did on this review.If you're not familiar with DON'T NOD games, these are choose-your-own-adventure, story based tales. There's relatively little game play and they're more like virtual books. Some have some button pressing events but this one has very few truly interactive moments (and the couple that are in there are bad but more on that later). DON'T NOD stories are built around a personal power like time travel, telekinesis or emotion manipulation through your protagonist, who is often someone you really want to root for. They're also built around some realistic dilemmas with difficult decisions and powerful emotional moments. These moments can even challenge your real-life preconceptions of different perspectives of individuals.  When these elements work, as they did in Life is Strange, these games can be incredible tales hat will stick with you for a long time and provide you new real-world perspectives. When they're done poorly (LiS 2), they come across ham-handed, poorly-written, unnecessarily preachy which actually insults the intelligence of those who purchased the game. I'm skipping to the end a bit but this game really does neither and that's kind of a problem. The game's protagonist is Sam, who is returning to his small West VA hometown after two years to attend the funeral of his old best friend. He quickly learns that his old friend died under somewhat suspicious circumstances (sort of) and the story goes from there. If I said much more I'd get too far into the story elements and there's not a lot of story here at only 5 hours of game play.Twin Mirror involves your typical cast of characters but unlike some other games, there's really very little NPC character development. With perhaps the exception of one child NPC, everyone is pretty flat here. Your "power" is an ability to put the pieces of a situation (like a car accident) and logically think it through. Wow, the power of logic. How interesting. The only curve ball is you're doing this with the help of your made-up invisible friend....you know, the kind you had when you were 4 years old. Your invisible friend talks to you and makes suggestions. He's a bit more social and nicer than you are but all in all he's there to just to offer some form of conflict within the protagonist. The problems with this game are numerous. Since I don't feel like writing a review longer than the actual game, I'll list those out in bullet-point fashion:- It took me a paltry 4.9 hours to play the game and there's very little replayability. - Choices seem fairly dull and uninteresting,with relatively few ramifications besides perhaps 1 or 2. made right at the end of the game. - Sam isn't a particularly engaging protagonist. He's dispassionate about most everything and while he's not a bad guy, he's not an interesting guy. His internal conflict with his invisible buddy seems pretty forced and very obvious in its conclusion. - The story itself doesn't have many twists and turns. You're investigating a death and it's all quite basic. In reality, you find one clue, question one guy and you're off to the conclusion. There are other scenes in between but this is a straight road, headed right to the conclusion.- The only game-type elements were Sam using his special logic skill to solve mysteries - which I think you do 4 times throughout the game - and a couple of terrible interactions in Sam's mind with Sam's better invisible buddy. - Despite the setting (friends' death, coming back to your hometown) there are almost no emotional elements. There's nothing here tugging on your heartstrings or making you really think. On the plus side:- No bugs or technical issues- It's not preachy, blatantly racist or has any terribly contrived scenarios (looking at you, LiS2) - The graphics are okay- There's one character (Bug) who actually is kind of fun and well written. The game is almost worth it as she's one of the best pre-teen / young-teen characters I've seen in a game in quite a while. - The voice acting is okayI'm a pretty tough reviewer of games. I have limited time to play games so I want good reasons to play any particular title. This one simply doesn't offer enough for me. I got this on a Humble Bundle so it was a throw-in. If I paid anywhere close to full asking price I'd feel entirely ripped off. Even at 75% off, which is the Steam historical low price at the time of this review, I don't think it's really worth your money which is why I'm giving it a thumbs-down. There are just simply better games in this genre and this one is not compelling enough story to justify the purchase. But if you have it in your library like I did and want a diversion for an afternoon it's probably worth playing through this tale.

_childDocuments_.review: Twin Mirror is a fun, albeit short, story-based choose your own adventure game. It’s only about six hours long, so get it when it’s on sale.I thought the game was quite entertaining, and I love the idea of the protagonist having a mind palace and imaginary friend who helps him out. I think the biggest problem with the game is its length. I like that there’s not a lot of filler where nothing really happens, but at the same time, I still think the game could and should have been twice as long. It didn’t have much time to build up the world and characters, so you don’t feel that strong of a connection with them, and the story feels almost a bit rushed.Still, Twin Mirror is certainly enjoyable, and I did find myself immersed in the story. It’s not as ground-breaking and detailed as Life Is Strange by any means, and that game is still DONTNOD’s best work yet. Don’t expect it to live up to Life Is Strange. However, if you like the Life Is Strange games or similar games, like Telltale’s titles, I’d recommend spending an evening playing Twin Mirror in one go.The gameplay is simple, not offering much of a challenge or any real depth, which is more or less expected for a story-focused choose your own adventure game like this, but I did enjoy the parts of the game where you create a simulation to either plan what you’ll do or figure out what happened. It also plays into the mind-♥♥♥♥ aspects similar to what Life Is Strange did, with repeating sections set in an ethereal, surreal environment, but while I did find it cool, it’s not as cleverly punchy as it was in LIS.The environments in this game are beautiful, but the animations are just passable. Still, more or less the same as Life Is Strange when it comes to animations. Continuing the comparisons, Twin Mirror’s more linear, with physically smaller and less detailed sections, and not much backstory for the world or characters. You don’t fully immerse yourself into the world and the people within it like you did in LIS, and the characters here are far more static as well, whereas in LIS, they’d walk around and do various activities.In conclusion, Twin Mirror is good. It’s not great or fantastic, but it’s a fun way to spend an evening. I don’t see myself replaying it, though, but ultimately, if you’re a fan of this type of game, I think you’d enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: If there was a neutral recommendation for this, this would have taken the cake. This game isn't anything special. Story is fine but it could be polished with greater emphasis on the characters. Achievement hunting is okay too, as there's literally no other mode but the actual "scenes" or basically chapters, levels - whatever you want to call it (basically, it's similar to games like the 1st two A Plague Tale games, and Quantum Break, just to name a few) and you should be able to nab all achievements in under 4 playthroughs - but you can select a scene and start from there. The choices actually  because it will affect the different endings you get (there's an achievement for this, but you only need to get 4 - at least that was in my case).This is also a walking simulator, with a few collectibles that add depth to the universe of Twin Mirror and how it relates to the narrative. One thing I also hate is the fact that you cannot skip cutscenes when replaying the scenes to get the last achievements - most games should have it these days but I guess that's just my opinion. Controls are also simple, but the button to walk faster isn't really walking faster by any means - and this is probably attributed to the fact that the level design is just small for every scene.The best thing about this is its graphics. They are great and resembles the facial features pretty well. The price is also decent and goes on sale from time to time. If you want a short narrative experience that you can finish in under 8 hours or less, this game is worth buying.

_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed feelings about this game.It's generally a very compelling and interesting narrative, and you get sucked into the mystery pretty fast. You care about the characters and want to know the truth about this little town and the incidents clouding the main character's past. I like that you can choose whether to be more analytical, or whether to open yourself up to the community and build trust.But some of the choices become rather jarring. Some options turned out completely different from what I thought I was choosing. Normally when I play these kinds of games, I live and stand by my choices regardless of consequence, but I ended up reloading a lot of times in this one due to choosing things I didn't mean.One moment in particular had me very concerned. There's a section where you have to cause a distraction in order to sneak over to the outskirts unseen. And the main character keeps insisting that the "only way" to do that is to set the place on fire. He keeps stressing that he wished there'd only been some other way, that this was literally the only thing possible to get to that trailer and talk to the guy he looked for. Even when he brought someone who previously got to interview the residents of the area and surely some sort of accord could be made with her help (or even some other type of distraction) to get what they need, he's like "oh shucks, I'm so sorry, if only there was any other way but setting something on fire!"Needless to say, it took me out of the moment. I'd accept it if the game gave you the option to try something else, making it more of a morality choice, but the guy doesn't even bother.I still recommend trying it out since the price tag isn't too steep and it was enjoyable beyond that, but expect some of the choices to be a bit confusing.
_childDocuments_.name: Twin Mirror

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun, short little mystery story set in a small town where everybody knows each other. It's a tale as old as time, with some interesting elements like the main character almost having a split personality, an angel on his shoulder so to speak adding advice throughout that you can actively ignore, or listen to. It is a bit ho-hum throughout and it ends on a bit of a... can't call it a cliff hanger, but it was definitely dull and felt meaningless; Looking back it is realistic in a way how it all turned out, but wow making an ending as unexciting as real life is sometimes is... boo. At least the ending I got. 7/10*Slight Spoilers*The scene where you have to definitively choose between a logical way of thinking/being, and separating yourself from your "Mind Place" partner's emotional side was one of the most incredibly powerful and beautiful scenes I have ever seen in media. It perfectly encapsulated those moments in life where you know you have to change, you take a hardline approach and can never turn back to being who you were before. The music, visuals, and direction in that scene was incredible and emotional. Borderline psychedelic. I will never forget this game just for that scene alone.
_childDocuments_.name: Twin Mirror

_childDocuments_.review: This game is overall a fun experience, but it did feel like it was kind of edging me toward a greater climax that never actually arrived. My only real complaint is that the graphics were amazing, but the facial expressions were very stiff and the only emotion really displayed was by mouth. Story wise, I found it very compelling and interesting and omg why was the Double so hot ??But honestly, by the conclusion, it felt like an opening to a whole other act that never happened, so that was a bit disappointing. It kind of felt like an unfinished game/story in a way. I would not play it again, especially considering how the choices didn't actually seem to directly affect the outcome, but it was a fun ride for a first playthrough and I had a good time.So I think I'd give it like a 6/10 overall. Good times, good characters, but a lot of storylines that felt incomplete or not lived up to their full potential. The vibes were pretty consistent, though, when it comes to what you expect from Dontnod and their "small town everyone knows everyone" vibes, which is something I really appreciate and revel in.

_childDocuments_.review: Twin Mirror was actually a pretty fun game to play, despite it's issues. The actual look of the game, great, awesome, no complaints there. The game is stable, no bugs or anything. Story, interesting. Choices, also interesting although it varies, I didn't feel that it was really an issue. Basically there is a lot to like here. But, there is also a lot to not like here. First off, this game is short, only 5 hours to complete and I was afk sometimes so it might even be shorter or closer to 4 hours. For a game like this you would expect it to at least be 8 or 10-12 hours bare minimum, but it isn't so don't expect a long game by any means. Second, I feel like the cast of characters overall is a mixed bag. There are characters that I like, characters that I don't like, and characters that I like doing something bad, or vice versa, really everything in between. It just feels inconsistent. _childDocuments_.review: Although I didn't "hate" this game, it was not good enough in my honest opinion to recommend. The story was meh, so the thumbs down is based on whether I'd recommend someone to play it or not. The story started off as something that could have been interesting, but the objectives in the chapters seemed to drag on and the story itself could have been much better. I was chasing a possible killer, and once the game started getting interesting, it ended. All of a sudden everything was revealed without much buildup. There was no good plot twist, none of that feeling of pride when you figure something out, it was just a story with no buildup that ended abruptly and quickly. I have to say that most of the characters were just there, almost as placeholders. I didn't really seem to care about any of them and when I started to undertsnad or begin to relate with some of them, I beat the game. The puzzles themselves were not difficult at all, it felt more annoying than anything to solve just because of the way progression was laid out. The longest part was waiting to see a memory because you have to go to the mind palace, walk a bit, then see the memory etc. A memory that would have been fine with just a cutscene, is instead forcing you to visit the memory palace (gave me the same feeling of being forced out of the Animus for nothing, just for one character to speak a line and then me going back in).This game felt like it wanted to be a mix between Quantum Break, Detroit Become Human, and Heavy Rain, and yet it was subpar. The game honestly could have been 1000x better just by redoing some gameplay mechanics, fleshing out characters and story a bit more. I finished the game in almost 6hrs so it's not that long. If you are interested in this game I would highly suggest for you to wait until it's on sale. However, there are better story rich/choices matter games out there. Choices matter and story rich games are a lot of what I play and love, but this one just doesn't make the cut for me and doesn't have any replay value in my eyes. There really isn't much else you can do differently except for a couple of different endings which I don't feel it's worth replaying to see.

_childDocuments_.review: Twin Mirror feels like a playable book in which your main challenge will be to find out which parts of your psyche and mind are the most valuable to you...whilst also casually solving a mystery surrounding the death of your best friend in a small town. The story is intriguing and the characters have interesting stories - if you're willing to listen and investigate thoroughly. I believe part of the reason why many think they are not as "relatable" as the people in Life is Strange is likely the age. This time we're mostly dealing with adults and adult problems, instead of teenagers - which personally, I find refreshing. The small town feels like a place you might know and is visually well done.The character models are good, but have their flaws. The same can be said about the gameplay: good, but flawed. The interaction with objectives/clues you find just feels really clunky, and sometimes you need to wiggle around to make the right menu option even appear. In this game you'll make choices. Some people felt the choices were not free enough, but in most cases I think they were perfectly fine. If you like storydriven, short games with multiple choices and nice graphics, this is a good choice (despite of there being better ones out there as well). I'd recommend to pick it up on sale due to the short playtime it offers.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a bit of a mixed bag. It didn't make a good first impression, had two fatal errors and crashes to desktop in the first half an hour. Thankfully, once I verified the install files, it didn't happen again. I'm not a fan of Life is Strange, and this is a pretty different feel - it's more mature, interesting mechanics, lots of actual choices which affect your story.Not sure how I feel about them using schizophrenia as a tool for storytelling, it feels a bit disrespectful, especially with the fantastical way it's used. It makes for an interesting mechanic, but some people might be offended by it.All in all, a good game, I liked it. It's a little blah to be honest, the voice acting is fine but unremarkable. _childDocuments_.review: Imagine Tell Me Why, but with a generic, uninteresting main character whose powers are passive, and who has their adventure in a boring, grey, ugly town full of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ citizens, and that looks grey everywhere.That's basically Twin Mirror in a nutshell. There is a reason why nobody makes games set in West Virginia, Don't Nod. Nobody with actual empathy can relate or like these redneck side characters (aside from Bug). People complain about LIS's writing and stuff, but they really should watch gameplay of this game and see what actual bad and rushed writing actually is. LIS may have bad writing, but it's memorable and charming bad writing. Twin Mirror is bad, and dull, which is the worst thing you can make a game be: dull.Aside from the writing, the graphics are also a downgrade from Tell Me Why, which baffles me because they came out in the same year (perhaps the teams inside Don't Nod were different?), and while TMY looks gorgeous, TM looks boring and even low-poly at times with some objects. The gameplay also has some questionable choices. For example, you can't skip cutscenes, period. So if you mess up while figuring out those parts where you gotta figure out the correct sequence of events, too bad, you're gonna have to watch a whole cutscene. The character movement also feels stiff in the action scenes, so you may feel nervous not trying to hit the wrong door at the first sequence. Though I may find this Don't Nod's worst game among their narrative games, his relationship with his twin self is probably the most interesting part of this game. But really, there's too much mediocrity to actually spend money on this game.So I'd say, avoid this game, unless you're really, REALLY, like REALLY craving for more Don't Nod narrative games.

_childDocuments_.review: --------SPOILER ALERT------------ Twin Mirror is a captivating game that takes players on an enthralling journey through the troubled past of Basswood, West Virginia. The game's protagonist, Sam Higgs, is a former investigative journalist who returns to his hometown 2 years after writing an article which led to closing down of a mine that employed a lot of people to confront his demons and investigate the death of his best friend Nick.One of the standout features of Twin Mirror is Sam's expansive Mind Palace, which allows players to revisit his past, reconstruct events, and explore different scenarios. It's an innovative way to explore the character's psyche, and it adds a unique element to the gameplay. The Mind Palace is a reflection of Sam's state of mind, which means it can be both helpful and hindering as players navigate the game's challenges. It was pretty cool to use, albeit sometimes too simple.Another intriguing aspect of the game is Sam's Double (Him), which is the more social and empathic side of himself that nobody else can see. Players must navigate Sam's conflicted thoughts and feelings with their Double, making choices that will affect the course of the investigation and their relationships with the townsfolk.However, very few decisions players make in Twin Mirror alter the course of the investigation and their relationships with the other characters. IMPORTANT: The game's replayability is excellent, as players can make different choices on subsequent playthroughs, resulting in different outcomes (some don't even reveal the real bad guy)In conclusion, Twin Mirror is a pretty good DONT NOD game that offers an engrossing narrative, innovative gameplay mechanics, and a high degree of player agency.  I recommend buying on sale for anyone looking for a thrilling and immersive gaming experience, but if you haven't played Life is strange, try that out first :)

_childDocuments_.review: This was nice. Not the *strongest* game in DontNod's catalogue, but decent. I do have some complaints; Sam doesn't tend to move any faster than an unconcerned amble and he handles like a boat, some of the side characters (specifically the former miners) seemed more like caricatures than people, and the final choice seems not only forced, but entirely unnecessary. I'd also like to replay a scene *without* having to finish the entire game first. Overall, though, worth playing through to see all the endings, but definitely grab it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Twin Mirror is an interactive story type game, among the likes of Life is Strange, Tell Me Why and the Telltale games. The graphics are very decent, and the voice-acting is top notch, however its the story that keeps these types of games going.The story itself touches upon some very interesting points about the human psyche. Stuff like anxiety, staying true to yourself versus what others think, past regrets and how things could've been and talking to yourself are things that make the main character feel very relatable. At least, I thought so. The main plot however is a little less original. Without spoilers, it tells the story of Sam Riggs going back to his hometown Basswood because his best friend died, and then the plot thickens in an overly dramatic way as it turns into a "who dunnit" type of investigation.Overall I did like Twin Mirror better than Tell Me Why, but it is nowhere near the likes of Detroit: Become Human level of quality. The game also is on the short side (6 hours) but in a steam sale it might be worth it if you're into interactive drama stories.

_childDocuments_.review: The good- Awesome graphics with detailed models, realistic nature, high resolution textures and nice atmospheric lighting. It's so beautiful.- Great art direction. Its world is well designed with strong atmosphere and offers true vibes of a small provincial village somewhere at West Virginia.- Well built characters with unique personalities. It's always interesting to try to understand them or learn their personal story.- Well written dialogues that don't exaggerate showing the mentality of each character. They look realistic and at moments are very emotional. It gives you some interesting choices to make that will affect you although most of the time they don't really affect the route of the story.- Cool, convincing enough voice acting performances. Some are better than others but the protagonists sound very realistic.- Interesting story. It begins as a touching drama and evolves into a cliché crime thriller but there are some strong moments and manages to maintain your agony till the end.- There are some nice gameplay elements especially during the scenes that you try to form a plan or understand what has happened in a place. It's a little bit shallow of course and it gives you only few choices to make.- Great music that manages to enhance the atmosphere and fits perfectly to the overall vibes.The bad- The parts that you're inside Sam's memories or explore its phycological world are over the top and shallow as of their meaning. All these imposing scenes with illusions, mirrors, doors and labyrinths seem to be there only to impress the player without really contributing characters' or story's evolution. Also most mini games during these scenes are too simplistic and almost silly. It's like they didn't think much of them but they said "let's just put something visually impressive in this game". Sometimes the phycological state of a person is better shown through small daily actions or a casual conversation.- Animations could be better, but especially facial animations are weak. Faces have small variety of not convincing expressions and even talking seems not well synched with the voice. That's kind of a problem for a drama based on characters' emotions.- Some clunky control mechanics. You will find it hard to choose with your mouse the correct object (or white dot) and many times hitting the requested button on the keyboard is unresponsive.- Gameplay is decent but too linear and repetitive. You have a conversation, collect clues by just looking around then you go to the mind's place to figure out a solution and all over again.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game. Story is quite good. Not perfect, though.Firstly, not sure about the art-style. _childDocuments_.review: A really nice take on the Alan Wake / Sherlock Holmes style detective game!  Instead of physical combat or gunplay, you are left to use your words as tools and weapons - and I really did feel like my choices mattered throughout.It also uses one of the most visually and narratively brilliant versions of a Mind Palace I've experienced, putting you right into the abstract thought process of each deduction.  My ONE gripe is that sometimes the view/selection system when searching for clues can be a bit finnicky.  Not game-breaking, but definitely a little annoying when you are looking right at an object, it is highlighted, and you still turn around instead of selecting it.Definitely don't go into this one expecting shootouts, or QTE's or even a timer on your choices.  This is much more like a choose-your-own-adventure book in the best ways, and I really grew to care about the characters as I went along.If you want a 6 hour mystery game with a good narrative, some good humor, and don't mind taking things slowly, this is absolutely worth a play.

short_description: Take charge of a WW1 field hospital on the Western Front, and make all the decisions necessary to help the soldiers recover and to support the war effort. In this narrative management game, you are the last bastion of humanity.

_childDocuments_.review: The game exhibits many symptoms of various congenital diseases. Especially chronic form of unpolishness and life-threatening case of bug infestation. The main reason for developement of those symptoms is neglected prenatal care. The game also did not respond well to the subsequent brief emergency care from the developers.After 34 hours of gameplay the game fell into catatonic state and did not recover. The game was pronounced dead at 28th of January 2024 by the disappointed player. The post-mortem is eagerly awaited.All medical personel should be aware of high possibility of encountering following symptoms:PS: What broke the game for me? An ambulace got bugged or event did not trigger when it arrived and medics didn't come to retrieve wounded. And when the next ambulance came, it just stood in a queue waiting for the first one to leave. Since then I can not receive any new patients. _childDocuments_.name: War Hospital

_childDocuments_.review: No - too shallow overall.I want to like the game, because it is one of those that tries to showcase the horrors of WWI and the difficulties of managing a war hospital, but it falls flat on two counts;1. Once you understand how to triage things, the gameplay loop becomes boring.The devs did say they wanted to provoke the player's emotions via patient profiles (they're married, have kids, whatever) but the reality is when you're dealing with 5+ patients, and eventually 10+, you're not really going to pay attention to that sort of thing because it is completely irrelevant.The only statistics that matter are; 1. How difficult the operation will be, and 2. how many resources will we spend fixing this person up.If a patient arrives terminal? Send him to the palliative care department, he'll die on the way to surgery so why waste time?Patient is stable but the operation 100% going to fail? No point wasting time then is there? High risk operation with excessive resource demands? To the morgue with you.Low risk? Book him for surgery.It genuinely is that simple. When you have patients in excess of 5+, it just becomes a case of queuing the patients by how stable they are, and how tired the surgeon is.It can get dicey at times with the pressures of numbers of patients vs surgeons, but that's the point of triage, prioritising those you can save and unfortunately, discarding those who you can't.2. The management is just a case of escalating pressures mixed with resource drain.It is expensive to buy supplies, but creating them on site is mostly just refining one resource into another, and spending all day there with engineers staff.You have huge supply deliveries initially - enough to cap out your warehouse (why?) and then eventually you get nothing, except more patients brought in via train. So, as you can see, you need to prioritise building your base to produce supplies (for surgery, and food for feeding everyone), and this is alright, you do have to make choices here.Problem? You simply will never have any staff resources to spend to break any bottleneck, ergo half the upgrades are nearly pointless as you won't have any staff to work them. (I'm pretty sure this is a bug, because staff points were triggering through the tutorial phase, but on new games they no longer do.)That means you're unable to really set up chains of production because you'll never have the staff to do so. It also makes shift work pointless for most staff because you'll never have anyone available to rotate shifts with in the first place. You're better off manually resting staff than leaving them on 12 hour shifts, as they'll be off resting when emergencies happen. (Also, why would you shift work nurses in the operating theatre? That would mean you have a nurse working there during non-operating hours at times because doctors don't work to a shift, they work on a per patient and tiredness basis.)The result is a bit of dull gameplay loop - where you juggle supplies and ultimately, triage patients, but it's not really compelling because the progress is like a horse stuck in the mud, and endless grind of tedium. Rather than working towards optimising something, or breaking a bottleneck, it's just passing the time until you can get a staff member to even do anything with ~ for me, the balance is off. It's not even difficult, it's just... dull. And that's criminal in a video game.

_childDocuments_.review: I had high hopes but was unfortunately somewhat disappointed. I 'think' the Devs' hearts are in this game, so I'll just suggest a few things that could be better:-LOTS of repeat bios for soldiers. I get it, a lot of men are gonna have similar stories, but these are literally copy-pasted bios which causes the game to lose to diversity points. Additionally, many of the soldiers had female names- not something that would've been common or realistic back then. And I'm not talking about typical unisex names. One example was a male soldier named Emily. There's more. -*THE INJURIES*. I for one was expecting to read about/see specifics when it comes to injuries, but instead they just break it down by "Surgery, Trauma, and Chemical" injuries. There's no specifics for the injuries (call me sick, but I wanted to see/read some gritty details). It would add to the game immensely. If someone's flesh is melted off by gas, or the respiratory system is failing due to gas, or a bullet wound hit a specific area on  the body, I want to know about it. It'd be nice.I'll add more here as I come across them. I love the idea of this game but I think it could be so much greater with some additions. As of right now I can't recommend the game. If the Devs manage to improve some of these aspects, It could change my mind later.

_childDocuments_.review: I was really looking forward when War Hopistal was announced. The premise looked promising and there are not many games out there depicting horrors of war in the genre of base/resource/staff management. We could talk about This War of Mine and Frostpunk from which War Hospital takes many features and similarity is resembling, especially for the latter.The game is spread around 3 chapters and while the initial steps around your hospital seems interesting, after a while it becomes click/drag fest without any need to think. This is especially obvious in the last 3rd chapter. Not sure if I "broke" the game and found ideal setup, but I have breeze through the 3rd chapter on highest speed just assigning patients and clicking on simplifications/complications.War Hospital feels simply very rushed, where one would think that the authors were able to deliver somewhat nice game in first 2 chapters, but ran out of ideas for the third. I found myself often times wondering why they decided to do this and that. Some examples:- The Operating Ward does not have button for Assignments. Understandable for Doctors, but there are Nurses as well.- Scouting missions are nice, but often times the POI pops up out of nowhere without any notification so sometimes I was not able to finish few in time as I checked the map late. When you complete chapter everything resets, so you just missed out on some if you are not checking regurarly.- Do not understand Trucks and Depots, throughout entire game I ran into one depot in chapter 2. Not sure if I locked out of some due to Scouting mission decision or what, but I do no think this is a good design. There could be at least indication what are the rewards for completing the mission. (There are noted resources for some missions)- Missing option to drag multiple soldiers in Rehabilition Center to one slot. In chapter 3 I was dragging more than in Paint. It was crazy- No notification about VIPs in chapter 3 and no automatic assignment to correct slot in Rehab? guess a bug- The notifier sound about incoming patiens sometimes bugged out and was not working at all, only reload helped- Many features are not explained very well. For example, if I would assign more soldiers to the trenches, would it lead to less casualties?- While I think the graphics is fine for this type of game, the cutscenes of german attacks are simply joke and looks like someone filmed Toy Soldiers. I just skipped from third onwards. There could be more interesting variety added to this- No replay value at all. While I played Frostpunk scenarios many times to try to beat my last run, choose different options in Scouting missions, etc., here I do not feel I would ever come back. There is absolutely no reason to.- Not sure if the Medics assigned to ADS is just visual glitch, but they often chose completely different road where the wounded patients were- I do not understand why during the shift change, the workers leave their ubications right when their shift start. Their work starts at 08:00 but they come to the building at 08:30, leaving every single building unattended for 30 minutes. I always joked on this in my head like Nurses decide "Oh well, goodbye patients, my colleague will come in 30 minutes. I do hope you won't die here in CCS till she comes". Every building stops functioning for these 30 minutes twice a day for 12-h Shifts. My boss would fire me from work if I would apply this logic in real life. I stopped tracking this in 3rd chapter even when I had 8 hour shifts set for some building.- Storywise the 3rd chapter is complete lackluster. I was at least expecting some major attack or something at the end similar to Frostpunk final storm. But my hospital was like the best establishment around the place, where everyone was welcome and nobody would need to fear dying. The improvements were done in first 3rd of the final chapter, scouting missions same. There was absolutely no reason to play only to just see the end.- (EDIT) Adding one point for 3rd Chapter. The Main Mission is to survive. Great. Aside from this, the only "side quests" that popped up were to send soldiers to HQ. Repeatedly. Always. I was able to finish like 5 or 6 of these as I was healing everyone and sending over to HQ anyways to get resources. That is 24 soldiers per mission. You can do the math in regards of the drag fest. This was balanced a bit with scouting missions, which were by the way nice, but as I mentioned previously, these were done really fast and till the end there was nothing really to do aside of waiting it out.That is currently all I can think of while I am still processing the bitter end of the promising game that could be much better thing. Feels bit like Early Access and while I got 53 hours clocked, in reality it was much less as I am caregiving for baby and often I just let the game run in background. Maybe I would say 40 hours. In case this will be on sale, maybe get it just to try it out, but overall I would not recommend buying.

_childDocuments_.review: "War isn’t Hell. War is war, and Hell is Hell. And of the two, war is a lot worse." Dr. Hawkeye PierceI was excited about this game... for weeks and weeks. I watched MASH... and watched some old war movies... I talked to friends about it... I thought it would be fun! The first 10 patients that died, hit me hard. I wanted so badly to try to make everyone survive... a stupid endeavour. The first 30 patients that died, I felt numb. Tequila was my friend at that point... I had only managed to save 14. The first 49 patients that died was where morale had hit the floor and it was game over.I punished myself. I felt like I had failed them... and I did. My second play-through I did a lot better, I learned a lot from the first. You have to be a machine. Cold. Emotionless. Heartless. You have to run your staff to the very edge, but know when to give them rest, When to shift staff around different jobs to compensate for exhaustion, or negative feelings. You have to stay on top of upgrades, and other events, while balancing creation of resources like medicine or food... or else, it'll all fall down around you. The game is tough. It's a gut-punch every time you feel yourself losing patients... your patients are more than just lives... they're potential future security... they're potential resources... they're potential morale boosts. Losing one, costs. Losing ten... costs a lot. It's a difficult game, but... I think it's given me a greater appreciation of that job. It's something I could never do for real... and I shudder to think of the poor people who had to do it for real, or else it was the bullet or the rope. Massive respect to the men and woman who suffered and died for real in this kind of scenario. Massive respect to the dev's for capturing that harshness in it's rawest format.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a tough one to review but I'm going to take a crack at it. I'll start off by saying WW1-WW2 gameplay is usually first person, RTS, TBS, and fairly predictable. What I specifically like about this title is that it's taking a crack at WW1 from a different angle. The influences I smell on this one from my time played are This is the Police, 911 Operator, Papers Please, This War of Mine, and Frostpunk. The Difference is that the premise has the same level of intensity as those other titles but about battlefield triag.This come's with downsides that I think will make the game polarizing in many respects. The core gameplay surrounds you being a poor Major in the Army pushing paper to decide who gets what treatment, what employees work where, what requisition is called in, and who lives / who dies. This of course becomes more complicated because you're on the western front. Supplies are in incredibly short availability and for much of the game command will expect you to erect the Taj Mahal out of matchsticks and thread. It's a game that is utterly oppressive in how tough it has been so far, and damn near demands optimal play. Due to the random nature of the rolls that determine whether or not people live or die, this means you can do everything right and still lose on a certain level. That means optimal play will only carry you so far. Some people just die, and some people miraculously live despite all odds. There's something really human about that. I can understand why some people say the game is repetitive. This is not a spectacle game. This is a game about managing staff and doing paperwork to keep meters filled. If you can't on some level empathize or anthropomorphize your patients I can see how it wouldn't connect. It requires a fair bit of "getting into the setting" before I started to enjoy the work and interact with the game. As far as bugs go I've only had one, where the ui overlapped a little bit but it fixed after a few minutes. No crashes, no performance problems, no issues technical or otherwise. What I will say is that this is a game for a very specific kind of gamer. People who enjoy playing dour, oppressively difficult games that want you sweating the whole time and just barely scraping by. The stress this game generates probably isn't for everyone, nor is the paperwork style gameplay punctuated by auto-battle style fights at the front depending on who you assigned there. On a certain level I can understand the frustration of the other reviews. If you aren't the kind of person who played This War of Mine on Maximum difficulty and enjoyed it, this game is definitely going to rub you the wrong way with how far down your throat it likes to climb. Still, I'd recommend it if you can snag it at 20 bucks. It's a unique experience of the great war that we've never seen with a decent storyline, hindered somewhat by narrative gotchas that can spoil a run and randomness that can feel overly hard. However, I come from a medical family so I kinda came in knowing that some people die despite all the evidence to the contrary, and some people live through the impossible so it didn't really drag me down. I like the game for what it is, I don't know that I'd dump a zillion hours into it at a time just due to how gritty the setting is, and how bloody the subject matter is but I do like the game. I think my closest comparison is This is the Police. If you enjoyed that game you'll probably like this one. It's the only other game ive found that conjures that vibe of trying to do gold quality work with nothing in hand but a mountain of tin. It's not a bad game, it's just a game for a VERY specific audience that likes the taste of suffering laced with paperwork.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who was in the military as an Army Radiological Technologist/Specialist it was quite interesting to play this game.While some things are quite rudimentary and simplified, such as "Engineers" seem to cover everyone else that is not a doctor, nurse, or medic, it is somewhat accurate as to how a field hospital works.It is a sad fact in war that you cannot always help everyone. you have the hard choice of putting aside those who are expectant in order to treat those who you know you can save... If the expectant survive long enough to get through those who you know you can save, then you can try and help them too.While the vernacular is of a British field hospital back in World War I, it is still relatively accurate even today as to how a field hospital works. You have a casualty collection point where patients are triaged. Medics move patients around the hospital. Nurses do what they can to keep the patients alive, until they can make it into surgery, or sadly have to hold the hands of the dying...Instead of dealing in money, you work with requisition points that you acquire from saving patients. You're given the hard choice of sending people back to the front lines to help protect your hospital, send patients back to headquarters to acquire more acquisition points (I guess to show as proof that your hospital is doing its job and to sing your praises to the higher ups), or, to give your people a morale boost, send them back home.If you like simulations or city building or the like, this might be for you. If you are a medical professional, particularly in the military, I think you might be able to appreciate this game.The core of this game is not so much about the morality of fighting wars, or killing people, it is about piecing together the lives of those who were wounded. Every patient has a dossier, do you send that widower with three children back to the front lines, or do you send them home?Yes, the battle scenes aren't the most flashiest technology has to offer...Yes, the game has some flaws...But the bottom line is you are trying to save lives with sometimes limited resources.

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished this game, and I enjoyed it.  It's significantly flawed, however.  I would only recommend it if you're someone like me who would like something to tide them over until Frostpunk 2 and is willing to overlook some major issues.  The first obvious issue is bugs.  I junked my first playthrough due to one that made my food demands double for no reason.   The chapter system does help, because the transitions between chapters clears a lot of the bugs that pile up.  I finished Chapter 2 with 7 dead spaces in my rehab center (patients who did not show up anywhere but took up a slot), but thankfully moving to Chapter 3 cleared them. Another is a general lack of polish.  The patient biographies are a nice idea, but the mix of randomly distributed attributes makes little sense, to the point of immersion breaking.  For example, most soldiers with children are not married, but divorced, widowed, or separated from their spouses.  This just isn't at all realistic for the time period.  Similarly, the distribution of soldier names makes no sense.  Yes, the British empire used soldiers from all over, but most soldiers were drawn from the UK proper and would have names that reflect that.  I also find fault with some aspects of the gameplay.  The system for getting wounded soldiers from the trenches defending the hospital functions poorly.  Even if you max out everything related to it, you end up with a poorly-functioning system, and most critically your medic teams will not start sending soldiers from the Advanced Dressing Station to the hospital proper until all wounded in the trenches are recovered.  Sometimes you might need each team to recover as many as nine wounded to get everyone, and by that point many of the casualties are about to die.  It especially makes no sense once you've unlocked ambulances.  It takes only a few seconds for a medic team to load the ambulances, which then operate independently.  This annoyance aside, I'd say the game is actually fairly easy.  Most reviews seem to think the game is too hard.  If you've played a lot of Frostpunk (as I have), it isn't, at all.  The key is to build improvements that lower operation difficulty, which isn't too hard to do.  This means you lose fewer patients, which keeps morale up and gives you more resources.  It also lets you effectively treat patients who are in worse shape.  You should also uses nurses almost exclusively at the hospital, reserving the bare minimum to keep the rehab center going and ignoring the triage station entirely.  If you do this, almost every patient survives and you get a lot of simplifications, which speeds things up, saves a lot of materials, and boosts morale more.There are two other areas that would benefit from additional development.  One is the last act, which was not even half-baked and just became a repetitive slog, combined with a race to build unneeded improvements to complete achievements.  The other is the scout map.  It just isn't very important, and I think I unlocked three depots total the entire game, none in the third act.  All in all, this a decent game for a small developer.  It's maybe a little overpriced, and it pretty clearly wasn't made by people who speak English as a first language.  I will probably buy the DLC when I feel like playing it again because it's quite cheap.  I don't see much reason to play the main game again besides chasing achievements.

_childDocuments_.review: War Hospital is a primarily functional World War I management simulation game that struggles to establish a meaningful connection between players and their staff and patients. As you progress beyond the initial hours, the gameplay becomes bogged down by repetitive mechanics exacerbated by an inadequate user interface with insufficient tooltips and unclear instructions, accompanied by a host of frustrating bugs that compelled me to frequently reload older save files and restart entire chapters.Despite a promising start, the overall experience is marred by tedium and irritation. Its only redeeming quality lies in its exploration of a scenario rarely seen in the management genre. However, this alone does not warrant an immediate recommendation..

_childDocuments_.review: I do not recommend this game, and I don't know what Nacon was doing, promoting this game on strategy-focused channels like Pravus'. This game would be decent - if the game was about half of its current price, and it was marketed as just releasing into early access. I enjoy playing games from indie studios, and want to actively help and support them - but not like this. This is a cyberpunk-level dookie oopsie, with all the hallmarks of an unfinished game. Unfinished cutscenes and repetitive grindy gameplay with no frills. I kinda liked the story aspect, but it's rarely expanded on, and the numerous bugs, crashes (7 in 109 minutes) and technical issues make this game a slog. Nearing the end of the chapter, I was excited to think about the impact of my hospital being super successful, but no. It doesn't. The only reason to do the quests and VIPs is to acquire the staff permits. While this game overall would be fine if it was fifteen bucks, and transitioning from an open beta to an early access, sadly this is not the case. Brave Lamb Studio is already working on a new game, and in the news channel they themselves admit that they will take months between patches and updates. Oh, and they already have a six dollar Marie Curie DLC out. (though I did not buy that, so I can't judge it)

_childDocuments_.review: A very interesting simulator (?) of a field hospital. The mechanics are much deeper than they initially appear. Challenges varied and interesting. Graphics more than good for this type of game genre (on top of that, good optimisation makes the hardware requirements quite low). The video and audio layers create a very interesting, melancholic mood - appropriate for the subject matter the game deals with. First impression - very good. We can get to know the history of each patient, decide on priorities, make detailed decisions on selected medical procedures (choice A-B), during the rehabilitation period we decide on the further fate of the soldiers - we can send them back to the front, to headquarters or release them from service. Each of these decisions affects morale in the hospital, the favour of the headquarters and the chances of our side in the conflict at the front. Staff management is no less interesting - each staff member within a specialisation has certain preferences that should be taken into account when assigning them to tasks. Ultimately, we also take care of staff morale by, among other things, providing them with good working conditions, rest, etc. So far I have not encountered any bugs, but perhaps they will manifest themselves a little later. I hope I won't be disappointed in the rest of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: I've recently picked up the game again and played another 10 hours of it. It's a much better game than it was on launch with many of the bugs being ironed out. It still gets very micro intensive after attacks as you need to juggle who's dealing with what patient, which medics are going out to look for wounded in the trenches, which nurses are going to work and if you're ok with putting them on 12h shifts, engineers making resources so you don't run out. It's much more of a juggling act now and not so much a pause simulator.I still feel like corpse disposal needs tweaking as it seems like digging a grave takes far too long and you're likely not going to assign medics to that role mid crisis, leaving me with 30+ people to bury and my poor medics don't manage to do that even though I've 5 teams on a 24h shift dealing with that. The psych ward needs at least one more doctor slot as those are the longest procedures and you're capped at 3 doctors with all the upgrades. Not only that but the last upgrade for that building says it increases the procedure time. So we're looking at the ward that takes at least 6h and up to 12h to heal a patient with up to 3 doctors max and upgrades that increase the healing time.Overall it's a much better experience than on launch and it has become an easy recommend for people that like crisis management games like Frostpunk. I recommend this game with a very big BUT. I've played the first chapter and that's 5 hours long, it was enjoyable. Here's a list of positives and negatives to consider:This game is great but incredibly tedious.Imagine playing Frostpunk but you're constantly juggling your workers around. It's frantic and very fun but having to move 3 engineers to the rest area only to have to move 2 nurses to the rest area and have to assign your medics back to their assigned posts only to have to re assign your nurses to their posts while assigning the new patients that just arrived to their surgeons all this in the span of 5 second intervals gets really old really quickly. The game isn't fast yet a "day" in game feels like you've played an hour. I get that it's a war hospital in WW1 but people are suffering from exhaustion after working for seemingly 2 hours. This game needs one of two things: More resilient staff or a larger workforce with better/automated schedules. In Frostpunk you set schedules and people work those schedules. Meanwhile in this game, your Surgeons can work an entire day while an engineer or a nurse or a medic need to be cycled non stop.There's a leveling up system for your staff BUT you can only check their skills from the Personnel menu and you're never told how much experience they currently have (at least I didn't see it).There's building BUT you're never going to have more than 700 materials meaning that the higher tier stuff isn't worth getting.The game's quite buggy and has a few poorly thought out things. The triage center has a limit of 10 patients yet I've frequently gone over this number with no penalty. The graveyard crew got stuck and never buried anyone after the 42nd death, I ended the scenario with 100 deaths. Nothing I did fixed this. And there was no negative event due to it (thank god). The rehabilitation center has a limit of 10 patients, yet I've gone way over that number and again there's no issue.Morale goes up and down and seems to do nothing.You can randomly get patients that offer to join as staff yet if you don't have enough quarters you're set at a time limit to recruit them. This would be ok if your engineers weren't constantly crafting things or resting or if building materials were easy to come by in large numbers. Instead you have a random chance to get an immensely useful event, since getting new staff requires a very rare and limited resource, that can be completely wasted because you didn't build a very specific and expensive building that increases your staff slots.I've stopped playing because I somewhat dread how hard the later chapters may be. And the constant staff management is very draining.It's a good game. The devs need to tweak the numbers here and there and squash some very annoying bugs to make it fun. Get on a sale and definitely keep an eye on this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not meant for everyone, the game reminds me of This War of Mine, a game was not graphically pristine, but was made to just show the horrors of war, and drive the player into difficult decisions that if you immerse yourself into the story plot and each soldier, your heart would break. This is not Call of Duty game play, this is not God of War graphics, this is War Hospital with its own unique art style. If you are a strategist and enjoy management games like Two point hospital or Campus, or This War of Mine,  you will 100% enjoy this game. Give it a try, for 29.99 its a steal versus all the AAA games that charge you 69.99 for unfinished products. Thank you to the developers for creating a masterpiece. I have been streaming this today, in hope more people can find this work of art. Please do not listen to the criticisms and continue to make more games with meaning. My Twitch channel can be found at Warlord297 hope you enjoy the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game certainly is unique, but rough around the edges.It's management gameplay is the most similar to frostpunk, but still does a lot of things to stand on it's own.It's a balancing act of trying to save as many soldiers as possible through the various different methods and choices you have at your disposal, while deciding who you can't afford to save.It's all about trying to make the best out of a bad situation.The story is in the last stages of the first world war where you take the role of a new major arriving to the war hospital and you have to manage it throughout the game.It has a tendency to convey the message that "war is a terrible thing", but the way they do it, feels forced or don't fit.It's a nice message, but the delivery could have been way better.Not to mention, the game just sorta ends, the end cutscene even feels abruptly cut.Admittedly it does get quite repetitive in the long run, be it repeated events regarding what happends during operation, the dialogue told by the crew, flow of the gameplay and so on. You will see a lot of the same things over and over again.But thankfully it does have a speed up option so sections don't drag out for too long, plus there's always something to take care of, so you're never left without anything to do for long periods of time.However, eventually you'll have built everything so a lot of things feels just more or less like they work automatically.Despite the speed up, it's still a fairly long game and might be a bit slow for some people.in the early game it's a lot about balancing who you decide to save and who you can't manage to save with your doctors and ressources at your disposal, so you must leave them to die.at the end game it's more "hah hospital go brrr" and you're processing so many soldiers it's funny.perhaps there's some bigger message or meaning behing that you're essentially sending those soldiers to the trenches only to have them back at you again after the latest battle.Visually it looks nice and has a quite dreary and gritty look to the enviroment and objects.And the artwork is also quite nicely stylized and firts the graphics quite well.Voice acting is great and everyone conveys their character excellent.Music is Amazing and changes based on how you're doing and wheter or not an attack is imminent.It is quite buggy, sometimes the UI wouldn't quite respond to my actions, the tutorial boxes wouldn't disappear, the people were gliding across the place instead of walking, sometimes the radio operator would announce things that happened, other times she wouldn't.Notifications could be alot more noticeable, as a lot of times you're just hearing a bunch of noises that is played because of "something", but you hardly ever knew why the noise happened, eventually i just started ignoring the noises.It's far from a perfect game, but it set out to convey a part of war that's an important part, and it succeded in doing so.i had fun playing the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I was really looking forward to it. But after seven hours and a never ending (bug?) first chapter I can say: It is menu-clicker the game. you constantly are clicking the same menus over and over. and over. there is absolutely no automation whatsoever. Everytime a worker gets tired you have to switch him manually to rest. OR you could use (after developing) some totally inefficient shift-system, where two workers (which you don't have in abundance) are switching positions in 12 or even 8 hour shifts. which is total nonsense as every worker needs way less than 12 hours to regenerate. so you are wasting your precious work power. what the heck?And this is only the beginning of what makes no sense. The whole ui is made for hiding important information from the player. one example: every worker/surgeon/nurse etc. has positive and negative traits, which you don't see in the menu where you assign them their jobs. No, you have to switch into another menu, which is besides that totally useless, to see their traits. then you have to memorize their random names to be able to know in the first menu which trait belongs to whom. Just great!The same strange ui development philosophy goes through the whole game.Last but not least: I had little hope, that the combination of ressource management and moral decisions would work out well. And it doesn't. There are no moral decisions. You just go by what ressources you have and throw all other patient files into the bin immediatly. The dead are irrelevant as the little impact on your ingame moral-bar can easily be outweighed by releasing your cured patients from duty. it's like every saved man buys you a dead one. But no! Because depending on the "worth" of your cured soldier you get three (!) moral points by releasing them from duty. Man they must have been important.It's a pity. I'm not going further into bug-related details or the fact that the game seems to run worse the longer the session is.
