_childDocuments_.review: Just finished a playthrough. I see why people have compared it to Frostpunk, which is one of my favourite all time games. You have to manage a hospital in WW1, and there are many moving parts to juggle: 3 types of treatment wards, supplies and food production, recruitment and roster scheduling. They even throw in a bit of scouting around a mini map with scout teams. And of course underlying it all is a research tree which allows you to gradually get more efficient. There's a clever bit of balancing built in. You have cured a soldier, but you must then choose whether to send him back to the trenches to keep your defences up, or release him from the army to improve your morale, or send him to HQ to receive documents. Documents are needed to buy supplies, but also to research. Research requires engineers who are also needed to produce supplies. But to recruit more engineers you also need additional people, and additional people are a rare resource, which must also be used to recruit more doctors, nurses and medical teams (the guys who carry the casualties around), and even the scouts. Like I said, there are a lot of moving parts!Overall, I enjoyed it for 20 hours. Worth the cash for me.The Good- Very atmospheric, with only a few mis-steps on the English dialogue. - Requires planning and thought, particularly in the early stages. It can feel like one wrong decision will bring your whole hospital down.- There is a small skill upgrade available for each of your doctors/nurses/medics/engineers. As you don't get many of these key people, you can become quite invested in your staff.The Bad- The scouting side-missions around the minimap have the potential to be useful, but aren't particularly. They take a long time, the rewards are relatively small. You could ignore the whole scouting business if you wished.- Again on the minimap, you can invest research into trucks, which can be used to trundle to depots your scouts find on the map, bringing much-needed supplies. But these depots are very rare. In Chapter 3, I didn't find any. It felt like a bit of a waste of research time.- While you get to choose positive character traits for your staff as they get more experienced, you'll often find they've also obtained a negative character trait from somewhere, without warning. Not sure how or why, but there seems no way of stopping this!The Ugly:- The only major complaint I have is that this made my GPU roar throughout. I have an RTX 3060TI, which handles huge games like Hogwarts Legacy with no problem. But this game makes it operate at full capacity permanently, despite seeming to have very small graphics demands.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very niche game that some people will love and some people will hate.You are playing the role of a Field Hospital administrator in WW1. Your day consists of waking up, reading casualty reports, issuing orders to your exhausted crew, ignoring the cries of soldiers desperate to get priority treatment, and ordering medical supplies. Occasionally you'll get a crisis and you won't have enough people or supplies to handle it. It's extremely repetitive, slow-burn, and is downright unfair. I've seen a lot of people say it gets boring around 10 hours and it doesn't surprise me they feel that way. For me though, I'm 14 hours in and this game is amazing.There are bugs. I had some UI issues and occasionally trains would not follow the schedule the game gives you. I haven't had any game-breaking issues though. 14 hours in and I've only ever reloaded one save, and it's because I wanted to test something. (I was ordered to save a General and amputating one of his limb's failed the mission. Not sure if that's intended or an oversight but I wasn't surprised.)

_childDocuments_.review: This game has great potential.  It is alot of fun to play and has interesting mechanics.  You have to juggle many resources at the same time and, although it can get a bit tedious to micro manage these resources, it is interesting enough to keep my focus as I like management style games.  The concept of the game is cool also, running a war hospital during WW1 and trying to make sure you have enough personnel and supplies to keep the hospital operational.However, one thing I cannot get over is how often this game crashes.  Not only does it crash, but it also blue screens my computer and forces a reboot!  This is unacceptable for any released game.  I contacted Steam for a refund but was denied because I played the game for more than 2 hours.  I probably spent more than 2 hours just waiting for reboots!  That being said, since I was stuck with the game, I decided to keep playing it which is why I have so many hours on it.  I wish they would patch this game as I have read other reviews that seem to have the same issue.  If this game did not crash, it would be a definite recommend.  But with the amount of times it crashes, it is a thumbs down and a caution to those that do not yet own it.

_childDocuments_.review: So I guess I'll give this game a thumbs up simply because they do what they set out to do but that's not to say this game doesn't have any problems.It does.The fact that your personnel never take breaks on their own and will work till they die thus forcing you to micromanage and babysit every single one of them...is frustrating.The units getting stuck and the framerate dropping is frustrating showing the game is buggy.Once you give orders to your units (which takes a few seconds) you'll find yourself waiting for things to be completed (which takes several minutes) thus causing you to spend most of your time waiting rather than actually doing anything.And the cutscenes for the battles have far less quality than the rest of the game. Entirely different (not very good) art style and very low quality sound which is depressing because the idea of actually having and seeing trenches while you're mending the wounded is a cool idea.But despite those negatives the game DOES have some positives going for it. Interesting gameplay idea, some interesting gameplay components, good art style (not in battle) with good attention to detail. Decent voice acting and sound effects (not in battle) and overal a pretty decent attempt overall.I think I'd say this is a perfectly average game that needs some patches to iron some things out. But I don't believe it's worth 30 dollars. Wait for a discount. If you'd like a more in-depth look at the gameplay and it's pro's and cons please check out the video on my YouTube Channel (link below).Otherwise thanks so much for reading and I hope I managed to help some of you out there spend your money wisely.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR : I will consider buying this after there are more quality of life features implemented into this very pretty game with plenty of potential.Long Version :War Hospital is a very pretty, unpolished RTS about running a WW1 frontline hospital. Think of it as a WW1 hospital Tycoon game where you manage patients, staff of various professions, various supplies for feeding individuals, building, healing, and other intricate aspects of management of facilities in a WW1 setting. It does its best to place you in the gruesome reality of the time and managing difficult situations decisions such as war-time triage, sending men back to the gristmill, or giving them a home-bound pass to raise morale.There is a depth of gameplay here which sets it apart from other Great War games which appealed to me.BUT ...I refunded the game. Here is why: The game lacks many essential features are missing to make this a great experience. Any options at all, other than basic audio video options, such as customizable hotkeys, would be a great addition I can only hope they add quickly. Totalbiscuit (R.I.P.) would have a fit. right now.A slew of what are basic quality of life features nowadays would be key to make this a pleasant game. Hover-over tool tips, hotkeys, or a complete options menu are missing features I'd want to see in order to play this through to the end, or a very advanced point along the game.SO...Considering it was not cheap (not necessarily overpriced overall, very little is needed to make it worth $40 CAD), I am seriously looking to buy the game after the developer has had an opportunity to polish this into a more pleasant experience. I will be monitoring this game in the coming months as I really have a desire to play a more convenient version of what is already available.

_childDocuments_.review: The people review bombing this clearly didn't read the tin. This is an accurate and gritty representation of the worst war. Yes you are understaffed. Yes you are underprepared. Uninformed. Very little is, or will be, going your way. Save every life you can anyway!Now the UI could use some improvements, sure. Some parts of the game are intentionally designed a certain way, and certain parts need some TLC and updates to reach the vision the devs have. I'm not discounting any problems the game has, but the problems are not necessarily what these reviewers are claiming them to be.If you want an experience, as well as a competent strategy management simulation, this is for you. If you want a game that holds your hand and tells you everyone is going to be OKAY, that lets you save everybody while your doctors, nurses and medical staff have an easy and relaxed day.. maybe check out Two Point Hospital and other casual friendly hospital sims instead. TLDR: Its a fantastic game if this type of experience is what you're after!!

_childDocuments_.review: If it were in my power granted through Steam's system, I would rate this game a 6.5 or even a solid 7 out of 10. But due to the review system of this platform, I can only recommend [/i]against[/i] this game.It is not a bad game. Every basic system seemingly works. The few bugs I came across were too few and too far in between, or perhaps I either never noticed or never got far in the game to get some. Who knows.But my biggest gripe with this game is how you manage your Staff (Doctors, Surgeons, Nurses, Engineers, etc) is too exhausting than it should be. The system they were going for is fine at face value but when you start playing you realize that you need more personnel working in your facility than you were given. Nothing wrong with this except that hiring more Staff is next to impossible, and you hire more personnel through the spending of "Staff Permits." According to the Compendium (The in-game guidebook), you get permits over time and/or in-game events from HQ. In my 2.1hrs of playtime (And 3-4 games) I only had one event pop up but had to decline cause the objectives to complete were impossible at the time, but ever since I never had another event pop up again. But from what I can gather, the permits you get as a reward are lackluster. I was watching a streamer play this game and was lucky enough to get 2-3 events in his game. Each event rewarded him 1-2 permits each. This may not seem like a problem until you see that hiring more personnel requires spending at least 2 permits ea.Add onto the fact that personnel can get exhausted rather quickly and need to take a few in-game hours to rest because you have too few of them to split up the work, your progress will stagger quite a bit. I (And the streamer I was watching) were both able to get progress going again a few times when we were able to but the Staff system is what we both struggled on most of the time.Like I said, I wouldn't recommend against buying this game if you are thinking of getting it nor would I actually refund it (Too late for me anyway). This is actually a fun and enjoyable game to play, and I can definitely see myself having a lot more fun in the future. But if you come across the same problem I have managing the personnel is too much for you to refund it yourself, just keep an eye on your clock.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATED REVIEW (second Update) HAVING FINISHED THE GAME (70-80hrs approx)This is a well thought out and executed game, while it does have its problems and bugs that seem to be focused in and around the building that pull the wounded from the trenches and the medics and ambulences that are assigned there (MANY OF THESE BUGS FIXED AS OF UPDATE 1/2/24), also experienced a single crash that caused me to lose about 3 hours however this can be rectified by the user by saving often but I would also suggest an auto save feature should be added to the game until its stability can be more guaranteed (AUTOSAVE ADDED AS OF UPDATE 1/2/24), The game itself is quite challenging be more about resource management with what little you have. The currencies within game (that allow you to build improvements and hire staff) can be difficult to earn in particular the latter (chapters 1 and 2, the third chapter the resources can be quite generous depending on the players actions and choices) (the simple cure for this would be more non staff VIPs or even emergencies like in themehospital in chapters 1 and 2). In order to succeed in this game the player must quite often conform to a strict order in which to build stuff, this defeats the purpose of free play and frankly spoils the game a tad as you are also at the same time forced into a linear story line with the cataclysmic events becoming predictable (hence the strict order of building facilities becoming more apparent). The simple answer would have been a free play mode (no linear story with linear events) with completely randomised events as this in my experience would dramatically increase the repeatability of the game by introducing a more random element (currently the game is ended on being completed and personally i am very disappointed that this was the case as i still had much to build and complete). None the less this is a very good game and simple in its execution but difficult in its mastery (not for the short tempered) and i hope to see more development as time goes by as the game is not all it could be as of writing this. One more important note is that developers need to understand that while the pursuit of realism is commendable and I applaud it, the fact is its still game you want people to buy and have fun and game that makes you angry on a regular basis only tends to be fun for the select few people. In closing as a message to the devs (if you read this that is), please for all that is holy, please make this game open ended or at very least make it so you can restart using your current camp as the game feels incomplete even though it was finished and there is a severe lacking in repeatability and its a crying shame.

_childDocuments_.review: Update after finishing the first chapter The game starts quite slowly at first, but speeds up over time. We begin to run out of materials and doctors become exhausted. As a result, curing every patient is impossible, and in fact, a ratio of dead to saved better than 1:1 is a success. Every decision has its consequences. For example: after one of the VIPs was not sent to the front, the headquarters began to cut supplies for our hospital. For half a day I didn't have enough supplies to heal even one patient, which led to a significant drop in morale. I finally managed to get out of this situation, but it wasn't easy. Thanks to such aspects, the game is really engaging. Before I bought this game, I was afraid that it would be a worse copy of Frostpunk, but it is not. The game has its own unique mechanics that make it stand out. Of course, you can see some inspirations, but that's ok. Also, I did not encounter any game-breaking bugs or optimization problems, which is also a plus. The only thing I didn't like were the cutscenes (animations from the trenches during German attacks), which in my opinion (unfortunately) are quite weak. It's a shame they're not in the same art style as the rest of the gameplay, or the animations at the beginning of the chapters (which I like very much!).

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I would recommend this game, but with a few remarks:- You need to embrace the vibe and genre. If you look at it for the pure mechanics, it's not good enough. If you 'care' that people die, if you really put yourself in the position of wanting to save more then you probably can, it suddenly becomes much better. - Act one is very good and well balanced. However, act 2 becomes easier if you nail act 1 and act 3 is just too easy if you nail both of the acts before. I finished all upgrades beginning of act three, had most employees then too. I really did not need the 4th scout group... but had nothing to spend permits on.That being said I really did enjoy the game! I really wanted to do well, I was bubed out (a little) when someone died on the operating table and I really tried to cram 15 trauma patients with 2 doctors for way too long. Just to try and help them instead of giving up on them too soon.In act one, I never had the resources I needed for anything, it was a real scramble for every little bit of time worked from engineers, to choosing the correct upgrades. That really mattered and that was fun.Feedback to developers:- Make scouts more worthwhile, it's way too easy to just do everything (it seems) and I did not see any good reason for 4 groups. Sure it helped do them quicker, but then they sat back most of act 3 anyway. - Act 3 needs a real extra mechanic, not just extra attacks. Now you're just scaling up the same game-play loop. _childDocuments_.review: The latest update brought loads of improvements so I'm happy to change my review to positive. Especially the decrease recruitment costs made a huge difference to me.I played 10 hours yesterday after the update and it was a lot of fun!Original review below for reference---Really nice game, I liked a lot of it. The atmosphere is great, I also like the art style and atmospheric music, the hard choices to make.The fundamental game play loop can also be very fun and exciting.Unfortunately there are some problems that outweigh those positives for me personally.* The resource and especially the personnel shortage is way too heavy. Needs at least an extra surgeon and an extra nurse and/or cheaper personnel costs. The problem of downwards spiraling is very real: Low resources lead to more deaths lead to lower morale leads to even more deaths and even less resources.* A better failure state would be much nicer. Maybe you need to relocate your hospital or some other kind of punishment when you fail below a certain threshold in morale or troop power but a hard Game Over after hours and hours of play is just too punishing.* There's no auto save which makes that problem even worse. That would be a very welcome QoL feature but also not solve the underlying issue because a downward spiral once started seems to be quite unstoppable.* The tutorial is also quite lackluster and does only explain the surface mechanics,  which might contribute to this quite a lot.I get the Devs wanted to show the horror of triage and I think they succeed in that.But when a Game Over screen is the result then I honestly don't even care that much. If I have to see the consequences of my actions let me see them. A Game Over doesn't really show me anything other than "You wasted hours of your life. Start again if you want to waste some more"Most of those problems could be solved by patches, so maybe there will be some fine tuning down the line. I certainly hope so because in my opinion there's a strong foundation of a very good game.Right now it's not really that much after a couple of hours.P.S.: I wish I could give a neutral rating here, unfortunately I can't. _childDocuments_.review: A bit rough around the edges but still good fun, War Hospital is a decent management sim. The high points are the difficulty and how exceptional the 'domino effect' of making a bad choice early on can cascade into a loss hours later.But the game does have a lot of issues. It does not have an auto-save, for one. Which is... horrific. Sometimes the game will crash, as all games do, but if you do not have a dedicated save you are out several hours. You also cannot rebind your own keys. This is also a critical issue, considering the game relies on you making timed decisions, and you have to physically drag the mouse cursor over to the pause buttons to do it.The story is what I would consider standard, and the voice acting performances vary from great to ... well, I'm just glad they didn't use AI. The graphics are what you should expect for a game priced like this and from a studio this small. However, the cutscenes are repeated and poorly animated -- some PS2 games look better than this. I'm sorry, but I would rather have an in-game scene where I see explosion graphics on the game world than watch these cutscenes. They're mediocre.Failing the game and losing, and winning the scenario, are anticlimatic and have no proper game end screen. It's just a box that says you won or lost. This could be improved.So as you can see I have a lot of negatives about this game. They don't break the experience but they do remind you that the game is an indie game. With a few quality of life changes like keybinding, bugfixes, and a little balancing, I'd say this would be a great game to play over your weekend.

_childDocuments_.review: So this game is getting "down voted" due to it having a much broader reach then it probably should have.  Likely partially due to the price point being appealing and also some notable streamers/tubers that don't normally play strategy and simulation games.For much of the target audience (those who enjoy management games, niche simulators, dark/gritty yet grounded environments) this game is going to be very appealing.  It pokes into some interesting areas that other games haven't explored.  Games with war settings almost exclusively focus on the "combat" aspect, where as this game is having you focus on one of the vital "support" aspects.  Without Logistics (which this game demonstrates painfully to the player) and without Support Auxiliaries, your combat capabilities are close to meaningless.Comments about bugs are not without cause, but almost universally overblown.  Much of the assertions that they are "game-breaking" are more coming form those that "if the bug is overly annoying, it ruins my experience, thus breaking the game."  I haven't run into any that don't have easy work-a rounds.  Does that mean the dev team can ignore them?  Absolutely not!!  But if you are curious about a game recently released understanding it has some pesky mosquitoes, I wouldn't let that stop you.  Many of these are also attached to the tutorial, so my biggest piece of advice is after you feel you have a handle on the game, restart and shut the tutorial off.The game also breaks a lot of normal expectations, such as seeing "experience" bars on characters so you know when they are going to get a level.  They also don't have a quick way to reference what particular personnel are good at, other then the doctors, when you are trying to make assignments.  The first one does not bother me in the slightest.  This is a practical game that doesn't need to put "gamey" aspects into it.  Overworking a med team because they are "close to leveling" is something that would quite frankly remove you from the experience.  Having this hidden should stay apart of the base game.  The latter, however, needs to be addressed as soon as possible.  As a veteran who has had experience in crisis management, I can absolutely tell you I would put notes on "Tee cards" for particular assets when asked who was working where and how rested they were things they were best equipped or experienced to do.  This is almost precisely what you are looking at when making shift assignments, so it should information I don't need to look elsewhere to find.Finally, also leaning into that I am a veteran myself, it is far more indicative of the individual player as to how much or little you care about the "particulars" of those coming through your hospital past "in game stats".  It is more representative of how cold/callous the player is when they don't even pay attention to the fact that a Widower with 3 children whose brothers have all been killed has come through their station.  You best bet that guy is getting priority from me, and is getting sent home after he's fixed up, as there is no one left to care for his family and the potential families of his fallen brothers.  This information is what YOU make of it.  Stating "it had no impact on me" is stating just that.  Others of us play a game like this and do the proper role-play (actual role-play, not just "gamey" abusable systems of progressions) of what we think of these things and how we would actually proceed.  You may think that those who have already "spread their seed" should get back out there, and the young guys should be released to start a family.  You may go nuts on amputations to get as many through as possible.  You may refuse to amputate because you feel it's better to be dead then permanently maimed.  This is absolutely an impactful piece of the game if you allow it to be.  If everyone is nothing more then an NPC........everyone is just nothing more then an NPC.  The game won't be able to FORCE you to role-play.  You choose whether or not to do that

_childDocuments_.review: In short, for me the game  worth your time, but the price was a little too steep given the lack of polish and and the relative shortness of the game and lack of replayability. There were localisation issues, plenty of bugs, and a lot of minor QoL issues (no autosave, clunky UI, inability to allocate staff by clicking directly on the Surgical area) that I don't think are excusable even if this is an indy game.Not sure why Steam has clocked only two hours when I've completed the game, but there you go.I did enjoy this game, but I was hoping for a game with the depth of Frostpunk or something and it's not. I don't think it's worth the price point. It has a lot of bugs and a lot of its Quality of Life elements are missing. The localisation for English is also fairly poor, which is surprising because the voice actors are fluent in English and even they say things which are grammatically incorrect which is surprisingly jarring.Where it excels was in showing the overwhelming difficulty faced by medical services in the war. Having to manage exhausted staff, decide who to try and save and who to not treat was difficult and put you under pressure. This was similar to how Frostpunk made you take difficult decisions and prioritise certain elements over others. The medical side was great, the managing base supplies was less so.The scouting elements didn't work, I can see - again - inspiration was taken by the way Scouts work for Frostpunk, but the implementation isn't so good, and the stories are jarring and make no sense. A lot of them centre around Germans being behind the lines, up to and including artillery units. How? At the end of 1917, the Germans withdrew to the Hindenburg Line. Britain had some 3 - 4 million men under arms, dominating the fighting area.  They could locate something like 90% of all German batteries behind the German lines, so how these large formations are existing defies logic. The history for me doesn't work, but more than that the mechanics of it were unrewarding, clunky and got in the way of the main body of the game which should remain running a field hospital.I'll create a Steam Guide as this review is 5,545 characters too long....

_childDocuments_.review: I have family (surgeon and nurse) who served in a field hospital in WW1 and married after the war, so I felt drawn to this game for obvious reasons.  Gameplay: I didn't expect a lot in terms of gameplay loop, its not a complex simulation,  and the ethical conflict about choosing rank and status in the triage made the game work. However the resource management was crass, giving points and rewards for saving those who had higher rank/vip status, to the point where it is more beneficial to let low rank soldiers die or be arbitrarily amputated than have them return to the field.  Obviously this was not how triage worked during the war with conscripts, even if there was some aspect of preferential treatment.  I think a lot of potential nuance is lost here, but there are some events which help.I was disappointed with the events though, as they really could have been more unique and interesting.  I wont spoil them but there is a lot of filler content that takes you out of the moment by referencing present day issues like Covid-19 and memes against the French etc. The jokey tone of the dialogue and "scouting" sequence is jarring against the excellent gritty atmosphere of the graphics and audio, not to mention the seriousness of WW1 (which is acknowledged separately and deliberately through cut scenes).   I think this game could have benefited from a stronger direction -- either to be more serious and educational, or more gamy and arcade style.  Right now it tries to be both and achieves neither very well. I don't regret buying it but would not recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Looking at all these other comments my first add should be: I didn't discover any "major or gamebraking" bugs. In chapter 3 the fellow lady stopped commenting on my workers position etc. which was unfortunate, yet manageableStarted playing 3 days ago and was hooked by it. I like this genre and the game does some things really good, others are improvable or not good at all. What i liked about the game is, that it starts of really strong. At the start you'll struggle and search for the best way to handle your "hospital". I started over like 3-4 times, before i was satisfied. I like the art style and despite some other opinions, i think there has been put a lot of love into this game. Small cinematics at the start of a battle will repeat, yet i didn't expect new ones everytime, that's what the skip button is for. Storyline is decent, nothing too special, yet it's WW1 , so you should know what to expect. I like that your staff has to move to the place, before they count as working, same goes for your medics when transporting patients. I also liked the "grinding" part of it, where it felt like ages, until i got somwhere, yet i guess that is, what it should feel like. Like a struggle, although chapter 3 has been a bit too much. I had a good time playing this game, yet there's been some parts, which i would render "improvable".Morale:Morale is your main stat, you loose the game if morale hits 0. Unless you're careless or just ignored every upgrade under the healing tab you'll never hit 0 in my opinion. Chapter 2 comes in hard and can give you a surprise. Yet it did happen in WW1 and i totally forgot about it, so cudos to the developers. And as far as i could tell there's a hard drop, which drops you directly to 25%. I think that's stupid, still, you can get backup very easily. I think, there could've been done more interesting things, little sidequests etc. to make this more countStaff Preferences and Traits:Your Staff can have preferences and traits. For me, my Medics all lost their preferences over time (most likely bugged), and when choosing new traits, you can't really see what the preferences are and vice versa. It's too complicated to check in their vita and you should be able to see it directly, when choosing the person and especially on trait upgrades. e.g. Your nurse wants to work in the rehab centre and when unlocking a trait "works better in the OP", would have been nice to see if she likes it there.Scouts:Nice little story element, totally neglectable. You have to scrap all your staffpoints, so no use for them. I got my "tutorial" ones and only got all 4 when i was in chapter 3 and didn't know where to spend my money onChapter 3: Chapter 1 i really liked. Chapter 2 got me in the nuts, yet i got back up. Chapter 3 just tried to lull me into dizziness. Chapter 3 has been fullout boring. Nothing challenging, just throw out more battles and men. Can't remember yet it was something like 60 Deaths to 540 survived. I had over 300 requisition papers and just waited for the game to end. and it still took me like 4-5 hours to finish.Shift system: Never used it. Left everything on 24 hours and managed myself, since during shift changes, the posts can be unmanned.  Especially crucial in the Casualty Clearing Station. Patients will change their status immediatly.Food&Alcohol: Never had any issues, just bought all of it via train. Never had any engineers on prodcution. Researched it, cause i didn't know where to put the materials or requisition points into.All in All:I really enjoyed the game. I had minor bugs, had to reload twice (couldn't drag patients in the rehab folders), nothing too worrying. All other bugs didn't happen to me. Chapter 3 seemed the most "unstable" (voices not working) and most boring chapter. Could've been a strong ending, didn't, yet the way up to chapter 3 has been a good. 2/3 of a really nice game.Played 26 hours and liked most of them, I didn't need the last 3 hours of it though. I guess when you use the shift system and go on fastest speed you can beat it quicker. I stayed on second fastest, since i felt the need to manage my staff by hand.The game was 24€ and i got 26 hours of it. Hell, visting the cinema nowadays (including getting there + food and drinks) can be more expensive and you'll only get 2 -2,5 hours so i think that's a fair deal.If you like the setting and maybe the devs will polish the game some more, then it's a total recommended.Without it, it's sitting on the edge of recommended , yet i will put a recommended on it, since i got 2/3 of a really nice game.

_childDocuments_.review: So I recommend this game, but it does have quirks. The game follows actual procedures of a Causality Clearing Station in WW1. So another review states a lack of details about injuries. This is historically accurate, detailed reports were done at Hospitals, these stations were quite primitive. The game also has this bad habit of throwing a wrench at you at the worst possible time. Gas attacks? No one is injured by gas (usually only 1 in 30). Yet some random cutscene is going to ruin your day. WTF. There are optimization and UI bugs. Scouting aspect is weak and not fleshed out. Ability to send very ill soldiers to a hospital is absent. Levelling up staff is weird, ranks and medals for your own staff being absent is an epic fail. Even as a DLC, I might forgive this oversight. Needs work, but the basics are good.

_childDocuments_.review: War Hospital:~~~~~~~~~~It's 1918, your name is Major Henry Wells, and you have been drafted back to duty and sent to the Western Front to take over and manage a hospital near the trenches. It's a massive responsibility as you must keep the morale of your medical team and the soldiers up. You'll be pushed to the limit and must make many decisions daily. What is certain is that you will not be able to save everyone.  You will, however, have the difficult task of deciding who to send home and who to send back to the trenches. It is a tough job to manage a war hospital. Good luck, Sir!War Hospital is a management game with choice-matter elements developed by Brave Lamb Studio S.A. and published by Nacon on the 11th of January 2024 on the Steam platform. The game is also available on Xbox Series X and PlayStation 5.I was quite excited about the prospect of playing this game because of the subject: running a hospital towards the end of the First World War. But I had this persistent thought: how far could the developers take the subject? I was curious to see how much variation could be had in terms of gameplay, and how the strategic aspect would be implemented. I gave this game a good go - over 24 hours in total - and with this one, I am truly sitting on the fence!The game is laid out in two perspectives: the village where the hospital is based, and the trenches. You will have access to another aspect further down the track with the scouts, but it does not bring much to the gameplay. As you start the game, your field hospital will be pretty small. You'll have an operation room set up in the church, a train station, a casualty clearing station, a cemetery, a canteen, a staff lodging, a warehouse, a rehabilitation centre and an advanced dressing station in the trenches. The pharmacy and the scout tent will need to be built so you can start manufacturing medicine and send scouts on missions to gather goods. At the top of your screen is a daily timeline. This timeline will show when the German bombardment will occur and how strong your military contingents are in the trenches. One or more icons (two swords) will be placed on the timeline, and depending on the colour, it will tell you about your military strength against the next attacks. Red will be poor and blue strong, with several other colours in between. At the rehabilitation centre, you'll be making all the decisions regarding where to send the soldiers when they recover from their operations, and the time of recovery is different from one soldier to the next. The rehabilitation centre has a desk with three trays on it. One tray will send soldiers back to the trenches, another will send soldiers back to Headquarters by train, and the last tray will discharge soldiers who are unfit to return to the ranks; it's pretty hard to send a double-arm amputee to the frontline. All you have to do is choose which tray to place their medical sheet in. But before you get to choose where to send the recovered soldiers, you have to operate on them and try to save their lives. In a nutshell, this is why you have to do all three chapters of the game. The story is pretty good, and you have tasks to achieve all the way through to receive Staff Permits to boost your medical teams (doctors, nurses and stretcher teams) and bring in more engineers. You'll also receive Military Drafts for each soldier you send back to your Headquarters.The most important resources are the two I mentioned above (Staff Permits and Military Drafts). Still, you also need to ensure you have enough surgical, chemical and trauma medicine supplies. Engineers can manufacture the medical supplies at the pharmacy, and you can order some to be delivered on the next incoming train using Military Drafts. New personnel can be recruited at the train station if you have enough Staff Permits and space at the lodge where they can rest. They, too, will arrive via the next train. Engineers can also make food and alcohol, which you’ll need as resources. But their main task is to upgrade all your hospital buildings/tents (camp improvements). They are divided into four improvements: healing, housing, production and scouting. Again, you need Military Drafts to activate each upgrade. As the game progresses, regular events will occur, such as wounded soldiers coming in from the trenches and via trains.  You’ll also receive requests from Headquarters, and additional events, such as accepting civilians into your camp. That will boost morale, which is essential in this game because if morale reaches zero, it’s game over! But the downside of this example is that you'll need to have a good supply of food to accommodate the influx of civilians into your camp.When you reach the stage where you can build a scout, you can send a scout to explore the area near your hospital. In the tent, a map will be displayed with locations to visit. Depending on the distance from your camp to the destination, it will take a certain number of hours or days. When they reach the location, you'll be asked to choose between two options. Depending on your choice, you’ll either receive supplies or discover new locations on the map. There is not much addition regarding gameplay.The gameplay is pretty much clicking on every building to open the team rosters, and then managing your medical teams, stretcher teams, and engineer shifts over and over again, being careful to swap teams and engineers before they get exhausted. That's all you do! Even though there is a shift upgrade to help you manage your personnel, you are better off doing it by yourself. There are only two types of bombardment illustrations. It happens, and there is nothing else to do. You'll return to the hospital when it finishes and start triaging the wounded. It would have been nice to have a mini-game where you have to moved your soldiers to safe places within the trenches, but no, there was nothing of the sort. Positives:~~~~~~~ +	Nice graphics+	Courageous choice of subject for a game+	Interesting story+	Good interface and management system+	Good gamepedia+	Achievements Negatives:~~~~~~~~ -	Very repetitive -	Needed more variety, such as mini-games-	Scout implementation is poorly thought out-	Feels like more of a clicker game than anything else-	The price point is too high for what you get-	No trading cardsManage a war hospital on the edge of the Western Front in 1918. A courageous subject for a game that, unfortunately, lacks substance.6/10 Key provided by the developer/publisher for review purposes. Any opinions expressed are entirely my own!

_childDocuments_.review: I am going to spend a few words about this title since there are some negative reviews that I don't think are fair.As you can see I gave it a positive review because it's really entertaining and well done, it's not an easy game, it gives you challenges and decisions to make, it lets you play like if you were a first line manager of a military hospital that can choose to be "human" too. It is really accurate for the times it describes and at the end of this all, it is fun to play and it keeps evolving. Although I am happy of this purchase, there are a few things that I would like the devs to work on.First of all, regarding the units/squads, it's pretty hard to understand (except for surgeons or similar) the skill they unlocked and you gave them. Then when you have to put a squad to work, you must check their wishes (they want to work in a certain facility or they want a particular time schedule) well, it's nice as a feature, but It's not properly done, sometimes when they are in the housing facility they say:" I want to work at the graveyard" until you move them there and they change it in:" I don't want to work at the graveyard". (keep in mind that you gain morale from right placements).Another thing that is not working completely fine is when you have to collect resources in the scout map, you can assign trucks and everything but they get stuck in a loop or it will not even show you the timer for it. There are some other small bugs but they are not as invasive as the ones I mentioned earlier. In the end I would still recommend the game, you can get used to the bugs and work around them. Certainly giving a bad review to this game is not worth it, everything it's enjoyable and I can see the effort this small dev team is putting into it. I'll give it a 8/10. Well done.

_childDocuments_.review: An interesting game that shows a little bit of the brutality in war. The first chapter was hectic, and my hospital was probably more dangerous than the battlefield, with an near 3 to 1 ratio of deaths vs healed... You feel the helplessness with understaffed, exhausted and collapsing staff, and low supplies you simply cant save all, barley the few that is in a good condition when they come to the ccs.Later when you get upgrades and more staff into chapter 2, the odds are finally more even. The patients start to survuve more often, you manage to get more supplies, and the scouting missions starts giving its rewards. Still, not all patients survive, especially not in the waves after attacks, with many casualties. You have to make decicions on who gets a chance to survive, and those who don't trough triage. And meanwhile ypu have a nearby cementery with a memorial with all the names of the fallen to get a glimpse of wars brutality. All in all a good game. I enjoyed the gameplay, the mechanics where quite straightforward, with resources, tech-tree, morale and rested status, and dialogue and random avents that you have to respond to. A bit simple in terms of graphics, but that was not the main focus. I would not mind a sequel based in ww2 with more polished graphics and more combined gameplay like, like combat rescue missions in battle and more detailed injuries, treatments and decicions.The gameplay did what it was meant to do. To give a glimpse into the brutality of war, and the human toll.

I recommend this game now.I deleted all my saves from my Steam repository, started fresh with Chapter 1 and played all the way to Chapter 4. I went all the way to Chapter 3 before I encountered my first bug - a previously game breaking one where the Patient Card fails to load in the Rehab, making it possible to move the patient to Send to Trenches, Send to HQ, and Dismiss. The solution - just Save your game and reload the Save, problem solved. I encountered this bug maybe a handful of times from Chapter 3 onward. My fix also proves that the Game Save, Auto Saves, and loading those saves actually work (previously they did not which caused all sorts of issues). ADS Medic Teams and Trucks are no longer getting stuck permanently. No more "ghost" units in my Staffing. No more getting stuck on Emergency Operations. I only had a medic team get stuck when I was upgrading my CCS once, that sucked but wasn't game breaking or important when I lost that one patient (I would be yelling a lot more if it were a VIP patient). Morale is counted correctly, previously I had games where it never went up when it should have but did go down if something bad happened.Some feedback for the Devs:1) Add more Scout Missions to Chapter 4, and at least one or two Depots. By this point in the game we should be well invested in Warehouse Trucks and the Scouting Teams. I did not encounter a single Depot and over half of Chapter 4 my Scout Teams sat idle with nothing to do. My trucks sat idle the entire chapter.2) Chapter 4 overall just felt a lot less intense? I think I sat more idle this chapter than any previous just waiting for patients, I didn't feel pressure as my maxed out doctors just worked the queue. Consider adding a Horse Drawn Wagon that has a few wounded Civilians coming from the River (West, where the Scout Tent is located) once the evacs start happening. Maybe increase the frequency of the trains full of wounded? Add an event of a gas attack on a civilian village during the evacs? I had more raw production material than I knew what to do with, would be nice if there was something I could spend it on?3) Consider adding additional Research in Chapter 4 such as reducing the amount of rations consumed? Things like Therapeutic Hospital Vegetable & Herb Gardens, Therapeutic Hospital Chicken Keeping - to help. These therapies were also used in WW1 hospitals to great effect with Trauma & Amputee patient rehab.4) Add an endless mode.

_childDocuments_.review: If you know these types of games, you will know what is awesome about this one. A couple things get stuck here and there, but fixable with a save and reload. I am a big fan of games like This War of Mine, and this gives me those war time feels. I love the camera functions (but could use some fine tuning), the management is pretty well balanced, and the stories behind each soldier is a nice touch. There are challenging decisions that go against your core sometimes, but thats the realistic part of war. Triage is much different than you would expect and this game makes you think. If you're into these games, its a must have in your collection.

Gameplay is a bit stressful but very satisfying, and it ticks all the boxes for the "Make interesting decisions, suffer consequences" urge for me. I'm not sure where all the complaints about bugs are coming from, so far I've only observed one minor bug in a positive event that prevented it from having any effect, but that was about it. _childDocuments_.name: War Hospital

_childDocuments_.review: Good resource management game. This game too me 50 hours to complete and was addicting to play, once you actually start the game up its hard to stop playing.The game comes in 3 chapters around 10-15 hours each, for the first chapter, in my opinion was the best. The first chapter seemed the most difficult and at times i really struggled and stressed over what resources to make to save as many live as possible, i felt the stress of having no base resources for basic things and needed to really put thought into what I wanted my men to work on or if i could even use the resources to upgrade a certain area.Chapter 2 seen a new element be brought into the game with some choices you make really effecting the difficulty of the game, however the resource stress that i had with chapter 2 was gone, instead it turned into me literally putting men which gave less resources in the bin and i glided along.Chapter 3 in my opinion was the worst, i had unlocked everything i could by the first quarter of game play and resources were no longer a problem at all, the game got a bit boring and repetitive as all i did was wait as the clock ticked down for the game to end. All in all a good game, i would like to see this problem addressed in chapter 3 by maybe decreasing the train income and adding like 10-20 more perks to the tree, i feel as though it would be better if i couldn't just max everything out in one sitting of the game, all in all a good game and i recommend for the price.
_childDocuments_.name: War Hospital

_childDocuments_.review: The game is cool, but it has lots of bugs still. Also i got so freaked out when in chapter 2, I had over 90% of morale, 3 surgeons, 3 physicians and 3 traumas, 8 nurses, 8 team and 8 engineers, 196 healed, 54 dead and suddenly there is a scripted attack after which the game wants me to pick up 47 soldiers from the field. I in 2 minutes i get game over due to low morales. For real? That's ridiculous. My hospital is working like factory treating even sick civilians and all vips and because of the bug i cant go further to the next level. _childDocuments_.name: War Hospital

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Really enjoyed it but it's a bit short and sometimes too easy, really could have used two more chapters and game modes like endless. Get it on discount.Loved the setting of operating a field hospital in the Great War. Having to decide who does and does not get treatment cast a light on the difficulty for those working to heal the wounded at that time.  Somewhat difficult at the beginning added to this by creating situations when I had to deny treatment in order to save supplies. Scouts were a nice addition to create story elements during the core loop which kept things from getting stale.Chapter two gave a desperate struggle for me which I did like, unfortunately I don't think it would be difficult the second go around since I would know what to expect.  The final gauntlet in chapter three could have been more difficult. It felt extremely easy with everything built up which ruined any tension there could have been. Would have liked more of a struggle.The short length of the game is disappointing really makes it hard to give a full endorsement. The worst part is that I don't see much reason to replay it. Please add an endless mode., as well as another mode or two for the main storyline that amps up difficulty.  I want reasons to come back to this game, I really do. The concept and main loop work well to me. I would personally be willing to throw in a little more money for these things through dlc, provided they're bundled and not parsed out individually.All in all it's a good game, it just needs more.
_childDocuments_.name: War Hospital

_childDocuments_.review: The game, I daresay, is revolutionary. It takes the player into an up to now largely ignored part of warfare: the field hospitals behind the front lines. I wish there were more chapters as I found the choices I had to make quite difficult, and not many games can do that for me. I would encourage the dev team to develop a game that encompassed WWII, Vietnam, Korea, and even present day, as I feel that the well developed story here could lead to great things for the dev. I highly recommend this title.
_childDocuments_.name: War Hospital

_childDocuments_.review: War Hospital is a great game, to the point that I'm a bit shocked that I've already spent just under 18 hours with it. It is truly one of those games that are stimulating enough to make you loose track of time. It scratches the same itch as "Frostpunk" does, and while it does not fully live up to that game it highly recomended.There are bugs, as with most recent relases these days, but most of them can be solved with a simple "save and reload" which wont take that much of your time. The tuturial is dreadful however, even if it does not bug out so that you cannot continue it guides you to desisions that will actvivly make the beginning feel harder. My advice: Deactivate the in-game tutorial and read through the exellent compendium for a better time.
_childDocuments_.name: War Hospital

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good game, but understand that the game is about management and if you do it poorly, the game will be very hard on you. Now that being said, even if you excel in all areas, there are some game mechanics that work very poorly (e.g. Advance Dressing Station) and there isn't much you can do about it.Now regarding the bugs - yes there are a few, but not to the extent to make the game un-playable. Patches are rolling and they are solving several of them, regardless, you will encounter some. Just save, exit and relaunch the game, this cleared most of the issues I faced.And last, the theme, such an original idea, I dont know if there are other games that have a war hospital as a theme, but this was nicely done, very unique given that the majority of the games these times are just clones of each other.
_childDocuments_.name: War Hospital

_childDocuments_.review: War Hospital, like "This War of Mine" provides a unique perspective to war. Giving you opportunity (and responsibility) of deciding who is going to live or die. And makes you live with the consequences with the action you took, that being either a moral drop of your staff to outright being court martialed. If you like to spend your weekend stress-free and enjoy, this game is not for you. However if you want to immerse yourself with stressful life of a WWI Major that runs a hospital while being pressuıred into sending as many soldiers as possible to meat grinder, I can absolutely recommend this game.Also a side note, their Support works pretty efficent and friendly. Kudos for keeping me in the loop on the progress of solving first day bugs
_childDocuments_.name: War Hospital

_childDocuments_.review: Being a huge fan of Frost Punk, I have been looking for games in the same genre.Ran into a trailer for the game War Hospital, by pure luck.Thought it looked interesting, but the actual release was still far away.You never know when it comes to smaller studios. A lot of great concepts a announced, but never released or finished.This game set the right tone from the very start.Iike:The concept.The realism.The Visual design and artwork.The attention to small details.The stress level and increasing difficulty.There are a lot of things to do, and a number of ways to deal with them.Keep the British trenches manned, and decide which of the soldiers that you manage to save are fit to go back to the frontlines. Who is sent back to HQ for resource requisitions, and who gets to go home?I noticed that most of the negative reviews are referring to early bugs, that are mostly solved today.It is exciting to see how the best games often come from small, or mostly unknown developers.If you like Frost Punk, there is a good chance that you will enjoy this as well.I REALLY like this game, and hope for more content in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: War Hospital

_childDocuments_.review: Well, no clue why there are mixed feelings about this game. It is brilliant. I love the micromanagement and the storyline. First you start with a small team of medics and as the game progresses you end up having a real war on your hand. It really has that Frostpunk vibe, but in a more realistic setting. I waited for this one for a long while and i am not dissapointed at all. It has everything, the harsh reality of war, the casualties and the decisions you have to make for those who live or die.  It is all about "You can`t save everybody but save as many as you can".  I would like to see one thing though, and that is that i can name my savegames. It is a bit confusing now getting the right savegame if war messes it up.. For the rest i like to bow to the developers for such a interesting and deep game..
_childDocuments_.name: War Hospital

_childDocuments_.review: This product connects the enjoyment of a really well-designed strategy board game and havy atmosphere that reminds me of the "All Quiet on the Western Front" movie. I saw some comparisons to Frost Punk, but for me, those are two very different things. This game is not realy concentrated on the building of constructions, there is much more about moral choices and upgrades in specific fields. For me, War Hospital is much richer in those choices, and it is much more surprising in events, even though I can understand where the comparison is coming from with the timeline and ideas like sending expeditions. It is mor ol less like with chess and checkers, both on the same base but still very different. War Hospital is a real challenge for my brain. For now, I see many strategies that can probably do the job well, but while playing, I had many moments when I caught myself thinking why I chose these particular upgrades. I like the heroism of the game; it is not something like in "Saving Private Ryan" It is more grown-up kind of heroism. You are thrown into a dirty, gloomy period and place, and by organic achievements, you're trying to bring some light to it, even if you need to send back saved soldiers to the trenches straight from rehab to save the hospital and village. And as it might happen, you are not always appreciated for your actions. I thought that my first session would be just 2 or 3 hours of chill gaming, but it appears I spent over 8 with one stand, which has not happened in many years, and I am sure that I will come back to this title many more times
_childDocuments_.name: War Hospital

_childDocuments_.review: After some time I can finally say something about the game, as I was waiting for it for some time. Let me start from the bad things, because those will probably change your own playthrough the most: - The game is buggy. On desktop 4070Ti it constantly is dropping frames, not rendering things properly, and the popups are sometimes non-clickable. Nothing that a quick reset couldn't fix but it overall lowers the enjoyment.- Battles are just ugly. I do not know what got into the devs to put this poor looking 3d render there, but it is just unnecessary. - Some number values will not load properly. Rewards, penalties, morale boosts will come and go with seemingly random order. You still can play around it but it messes with long-term planningAnd now for a good parts- The concept is just awesome. You can feel the need to juggle with your staff, to straight up leave people because you need the manpower somewhere else. The resources are scarce but not unobtainable, people have problems but are not unmanagable. - Music is nice, same goes for dialogues. Of course it is to personal preferences at the end of the day, but for me it is good and fits the setting.- There is room for more. That sounds like a very poor review, but hear me out. This game do not exhaust the idea of war hospital, and in the playthrough you can see the areas on which it can expand. Mods, or DLCs, could make it better and, in my opinion, one of the better games in the genre. Overall, it is a nice game to play, but as of writing this review I would recommend waiting a bit for some fixes to arrive, and maybe some additional content.
_childDocuments_.name: War Hospital

_childDocuments_.review: I like games that are crisis management games.  And this game was that.  I also like how they handled an ever increasing level of difficulty.  Typical games get boring once you have build up enough resources where the crisis is no longer a problem (like the cold in frost punk, food in rimworld, or any resource in long dark. lol)I won't go to much into detail to avoid spoilers but basically this game asks you to make choices of what to do with your resources.  Because there will always be more people that need help.  At the end I had every single upgrade and every position filled and I still only managed to save 200 lives for every 100 dead..  So how much am I willing to spend to save one more life?  These are the questions this game will ask of you.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of bugs.  Bugs that I'm surprised made it to release.  Bugs that'll give you a Game Over, if not crash you.Also, the UX is really tedious, clicky, and clunky.  There aren't even any hotkeys.  You gotta click through tons of fiddly submenu's, but then you gotta double check some info first, and that's in a different menu so you click click click navigate back, okay now you got it, so lets go back again to do the thing you wanted to do.Related, there's 'unit cards' that you need to somehow differentiate between.  They all look the same, but if you check the correct sub-sub-menu, you'll see that THIS ONE will sabotage you if you don't remember exactly who they are, while you're shuffling them about, next to their other twins.   It's a back-referencing nightmare of "wait was it that guy, or that guy?" every time you need to re-assign a nearly-anonymous team.  And re-routing IS THE WHOLE GAME, so this UX issue is utterly withering.And did I mention there's a lot of pretty bad bugs?

_childDocuments_.review: Its a pretty good management game.  Clearly very inspired by Frostpunk.  The story kept me interested but not super engaged.  Where the game really shines is having to triage the patients based on your limited supply of doctors and supplies.  I'll say the difficulty scale is pretty weird.  There is a huge difficulty spike in Chapter 2 and then it never hits that again.  The final chapter is honestly pretty easy and anti-climactic.  People have mainly been giving this bad reviews based on bugs and frame drop issues in chapter 1.  I was able to fix the frame drop issues just by saving and reloading and I think they patched out the game breaking bugs pretty quickly.  The BIG problem this game has is lack of communication of features.  The main example is there is an audio notification when patients arrive but absolutely no visual indication which can lead to a terminal patient getting dropped off and dying without you realizing they are even in the CCS.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall the game is really fun and engaging and really puts you in the shoes of those who risked their lives to save the lives of others in one of the most brutal conflicts in world history. The events, VIP's, and scout locations do a great job at immersing you in the environment and often force you to make difficult moral decisions. The diversity of your staff and patients additionally do an amazing job of showing off the many different nationalities that made up the Entente forces.However, the game has some bugs that are indicative of it's recently released status but the dev team has been hard at work fixing them. My only other compliant is that the nationalities of the wounded seems to be off balance with most of the wounded sometimes being Indians over other nationalities. Which can break the immersion as while being a crucial part of the British Army they were not the majority of forces in Europe, but this is a minor aspect. Altogether, I would highly recommend this game to people who are interested in history, the field of medicine, or even just management games.
_childDocuments_.name: War Hospital

_childDocuments_.review: Quite enjoyable. Being extremely low on supplies and backed up with patient's while scraping by is stressful. The game is figuring out which staff to hire, skill trees to upgrade, and balancing the staffs' sleep to meet surges in patients. Only technical issue has been medics not going to work while using a 12 hour shift system. Once I noticed I reset their assignment and had no issues. People are complaining that the patient bios are meaningless and that triage becomes too easy. When that is exactly what real life is. Patients are strangers and their personal lives have no outcome on treatment, doubtful you would even know anything about them anyway in an emergent situation. Triage is meant to preserve the most life, you will not save everyone. The game tells you constantly you will not save everyone. People have a romantic view of what this game should be.

_childDocuments_.review: It is an OK game.  They really need to make the game have different difficulties.  I don't know if it is by design or just how it was planned, but there is a real shortage of staff at the beginning of the game that distracts from the game play.  I know you can't save everyone, but I would think you could be able to save more then 50% of the people who come to your hospital.  When you reach the middle of the game (I think), you have to amputate almost all of your patients and there are little rewards you gain; you are basally treading water.  I tried my hardest, but as how the game is balanced, you can only save about 50%.  I would like to be able you as the player being able to at least save 2/3s and being able to make more statistic decisions.  Not be forced to say, oh well, there is no way I could have saved half of your patients.  Also, like mentioned by a Youtuber, I think.  Be nice to heal some characters, to only come back to the hospital later.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most unique games I've ever played in terms of theme. The complex system of managing the hospital keeps the players occupied at all times, doesn't make us wait for even a single moment but involves us in making often multiple decisions at once. Combined with the constant reminder of limited resources we face an intense challenge that only a well-thought-out strategy can conquer. As a result we are given a fast-paced and engaging gameplay. The music, sound design and seamless graphics create a suspenseful, sometimes grim but not overly heavy atmosphere that further emphasizes what's at stake. So far I haven't encountered any major problems, just a few minor bugs.
_childDocuments_.name: War Hospital

_childDocuments_.review: This is the perfect game for me as some one who wants to be a medic.....that being said this game is not perfect. Lots of challenge and I'm having fun balancing triage and supplies. When you learn how to do things the game really steam-lines.  The most realistic military game I have played in a long time if ever..... you have to do everything you can with nothing, just like the real military.
_childDocuments_.name: War Hospital

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of WW1 and RTS Games Ive gone through my fair share of games like this and War Hospital has certainly met my expectations on a number of levels, has great potential and if you're a fan of the genre and the time period, then you certainly wont be disappointed (A few bugs aside)The game is split into 3 chapters of quite substantial length, between 6 and 8 hours each depending on what speed you play the game and experience. There are certain major story beats that occur in each chapter to throw your resources into disarray. The positives I found here is that I was able to just about able to manage the situation without any prior planning, unlike other RTS campaigns you will often have to restart a previous save and start stockpiling said resource to survive, I never found that here which I commend as the balance of struggling and having success in these games is a very fine line to treadThe core gameplay loop always feels like im just out of control which is what you want, it certainly takes influence from Frostpunk in that respect. The carrot on the stick is certainly there for new camp improvements so nothing feels out of reach eitherThere are certainly negatives in the way of bugs (No soft lock or game breaking ones as of yet) and other design choices that are worth noting;- Freight amounts increased by 1000 after chapter 1 on top of what ever I had before, however when save was reloaded, the extra amount I had disappeared so reverted to 1000 again- Minor clipping bugs for NCP's although these resolved themselves- Popups sometimes had different titles compared to the content- UI issues with text being too large on some objectives in the HUD (Dont go to Half Rations objective)- Some objectives appearing unnecessarily and then not clearing for ages. Staff the cemetery and CCS objectives which occurred when you swapped in new staff at the beginning of the game- Scouts dont appear to find much in the way of resources, a lot of Morale results but im yet to find a depot to send a truck to which feels quite bizarre to make it so scarceOverall I definitely recommend the game if you are a fan of the time period and similar simulations games, if you're willing to cater for the bugs
_childDocuments_.name: War Hospital

_childDocuments_.review: WW1 hospital simulator, Save as many as you can. throw soldiers into trenches to  keep your hospital safe or send them off to HQ for tickets to get more supplies or upgrade your base. sends scouts out to find resources( was my least favorite aspect as I had zero luck with them being much benefit. Game can have very intense moments of quick choices but once you understand the mechanics it becomes very manageable.   I personally thought it was a great game, but I am aware other people have experienced game breaking bugs, hopefully after it is patched that won't be an issue for some folks any more.  The Devs have been very receptive of the few bugs I encountered, so if you do pick it up and run it to bugs pop them off an email.
_childDocuments_.name: War Hospital

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Great Setting, Some Bugs, i encountered one game braking, UI is ok and its incredible unfair. Its great :)85/100The long review:Game Setting:WW1 is used not to often, combining this with not direct front line but instead with the suffering behind the lines of a war.I think that is a great setting and they achieve good immersion with the game.Bugs and Performance:The greatest critic from Reviews is the performance and the bugs. Now i don't mind bugs that much as long my game doesn't break or progress gets lost.These are some bugs i encountered:-Traits randomly changing.-People who want to talk to me or quest with timers disappearing before timer end.-Civilians who got an op don't leave rehab, but still count towards rehab limit.Performance wise i only encountered some problems in Chapter two. My guess would be that the civs who get into rehab break something because my performance problems only appeared with this bug.Gameplay:The generell Gameplay loop is great and there is a steep learning curve.You manage the hospital from logistics, production of consumables for op and food, improving and building new parts of the hospital.But the main argument of this game is to make the decisions, you never thought you would have to make. To you make more op consumables or do you build a xray machine to improve all future op´s but risk patients will die while you build it. There is almost no time where you have enough stuff you would need.UI:The UI is a two edged knife...One the one hand, it looks good, its build logically and finding stuff is easy.BUT only after you found the worst UI part. A big drop down list on the top left. And that is horrible IMO...My Critic:Some bugs need to be fixed...UI needs improvement in some areas: More information what some upgrades do in the improvements (what does my truck in the warehouse do???)The drop down on the top left needs some kind of change...I have some strange issue where i constantly need to press above all icons. I would guess that's because I have a 1440p Monitor?Fazit:All in all I would recommend this game. I get some "This War of Mine" vibes with it and i think they manage to capture the time, the tragedy and the suffering.It really gets you and you think about things in war that don't get too much notice.War is horrible and this game does a great job portraying it.85/10090/100 without bugsCheers

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good WW1 resource management sim. A lot like Frostpunk in terms of event popup options and how quickly resource and casualty issues can stack up. The Patient rank/biography profile was a bit misleading at first, their frontline combat point value is based on the 1-3 red chevrons; completely separate to whether they are a Private->Colonel.The tutorial isn't bad. Tip for new players:- Resources from the train aren't good value, much better to produce what you need. - Be very careful with VIPsWith all the quest-like events it also became beneficial to have a few post-rehab patients held in 'waiting 'before you pick where to send them off to.Couple bugs with overlapping event popups blocking each other but tabbing out and reloading the save did the trick.Overall 7/10 at release patch.

_childDocuments_.review: I had this game on my wishlist since it was announced. I was very excited seeing a game about WW1 that didn't have to do with any type of grand strategy, troop movements, or key battles. What I did get was an interesting resource, time and building management game. The "War within the War" so to speak, an army field hospital near the front lines of WW1. What I like about the game, the constant action. There is no lull in gameplay, you are constantly checking the CCS for new patients , making sure your staff is rested so they don't collapse and keep the production chain going. Discharge of the wounded , be it back to the frontlines to repel an attack, back to HQ for "building materials" or discharge from service for morale to keep you hospital open. Patient care is an interesting mini-game within the game. Not to give much away , but the severity and time an resources affect the surgeon in question, his abilities and his stamina. If you're a scheduler or love to use quickbooks, you'll love this part of the game. Supplies, depending on how well you've built your infrastructure, come by train. There's ways around but I'm not gonna spoil it too much. There are some issues with game play though, sometimes your staff will skill up and the game will freeze, when you set up schedules for your staff , depending on what time you start them at, will continue to work until they collapse because to the staff member , the shift doesn't end until the time comes. For some apparent reason, and maybe I'm missing something myself, the " truck garage" seems rather useless. Also, the train station, why can't it be upgraded to take more then one train ?The positives outweight the negatives in my opinion, the balance may be alittle off when it comes to difficulty , I do enjoy the tutorial taking the training wheels off right away, it gets the game going quicker. I do recommend this to you micromanagers out there. You'll be clicking every second !

_childDocuments_.review: For those who appreciate challenging strategic games, I highly recommend War Hospital. The intense atmosphere of the game truly captures the essence of fighting for real human lives, providing players with a unique and emotionally charged experience. The combination of strategic elements and the authenticity of the wartime setting creates a compelling and immersive gameplay. Whether you're a strategy game enthusiast or fascinated by historical eras, "War Hospital" is a must-try title that keeps you on your toes with its strategic challenges and authentically portrayed World War backdrop. It successfully blends intensity with a nice overall vibe, making it a standout recommendation for those seeking a gripping and historically resonant gaming experience.

Game does good job of creating bleak atmosphere, you are managing the hospital and dealing with the consequences from the frontlines operating (or not) on soldiers that were wounded in battle. What is interesting is that everything is focused on resource management having the effect where you have to manage your own sense of morality as maybe it is sometimes better to let some people go. On the other hand to keep operating you need soldiers on the front as well as protecting the hospital, so there is quite a bit of balancing you need to do to achive your goals while keeping in mind you are managing human lives.I can say from what I've seen so far that the game would be interesting for people interested in ww1 stuff as well as players enjoying management aspect of the game. Reduced all settings, but still ... Has some annoying bugs (like doctors not starting to operate for no apparent reason, despite being fresh and having enough material. I don't mind the triage thing and also the tough decisions and shortages... But this is no fun. Becomes a lot of micromanagement  and very repetitive. A real chore, indeed, more like hard work I should get paid for...^^ than pleasure while gaming. The story is a little shallow, so one doesn't really connect with the staff. Although I like they develop some helpful traits after a (long...) while. I made some small mistakes in the beginning... like for example ordering too many 3 bars soldiers back to the front instead of getting supplies for sending them back to HQ. Hardly can rectify this in the later game... So probably need a restart. Overall a very disappointing and frustrating experience... Also some annoying usability issues, for example no right click possible to close a window or exit a building. Also it seems that sometimes you click and nothing happens.... Plus, I am constantly being notified that personell is missing at the cemetery, but there is a team assigned. -.- But I hope for some updates and bugfixes, then it will be a great title. _childDocuments_.review: The game is not bad (at the core), but it is currently unplayable. From some point on there is a massive drop in FPS, then it's almost unplayable. For me it was in the third chapter, other times it's in the second, etc.Then also some parts of the game, like ADS, or the graveyard are relatively poorly designed and you can never handle the barrage of wounded (and also dead). I understand that the game is trying to simulate the brutality and suffering of WWI, but by the time I have all the upgrades and maxed out personnel, I find it a bit of a cop out. Other weird bugs are the drops in morale, for no apparent reason. There's no way to know exactly what happened and where. Similarly, the game has a problem (at least for me) with the fact that when I shut down the game with more base resources, it always loads with a maximum of 1000. Also, sending troops to the front is a bit half-baked, even if the army strength is at strong, the number of wounded is e.g. 40-60 after two attacks. The maximum number of medic teams (ADS) has no chance to handle the situation somehow.Traits take a long time to level, they have negligible effect.All in all, I have nothing against hard games, but they have to be fair, such as Last Train (also a WWI game), which is much better handled in terms of the game itself, optimization and all other aspects. However, War Hospital still has a long way to go, it's more on the early access level.
