_childDocuments_.review: Update: One week in and i'm just about to finish my second play-through. Some of the bugs have been patched but issues remain with pacing.  Act 2 is brutal and act 3 isn't really a challenge and noticeably missing voice acting (did they run out of time?)  .  There also needs to be more scenarios as there inst a whole lot of replay-ability once you have played though, once unlike front punk your choices don't have a chance for different outcomes each play though. Still issues will the shift system, for example operating theatres work best with max nurses but there is no way to assign max nurses to each shift (not enough slots) which leads to painful micromanagement dragging and dropping out staff when they are exhausted.  There is no benefit to using the shift system that I can see. The skill tree needs some work.  As a healthcare worker myself the illnesses/ treatments/ medical emergencies aren't accurate and are a bit repetitive, however I it scratches that triage itch. This game should have be release early access prior to full release to iron out these bugs. The game definitely still isn't finished. Review 14/1 Love this game! Super addictive, I played 10 hours of it the day I bought it.  A definite buy if your a fan of management games like frost punk, surviving the aftermath or this war of mine (like me!)  Some slight issues with units not doing what they should or graphics misbehaving, but that's easily fixed with closing and reopening the game. But for a game that came out only a few days ago should be expected and will hopefully be fixed in a patch.It feels like they ran out of money for the in came cut scenes with graphics looking like early 2000 games and not much in the way of story progression in those scenes (which is odd given the quality of the scenes on start up of the game).  If the devs are reading reviews, things I would love to see are the ability to zoom in on units and read more info, an improvement to the 12 hour shift system and some balancing/ re configuring  ( namely of how many units you can have deployed in areas to begin with, resource production rates, and the skill tree could do with some tweaking).All in all 7/10 game but could easily be 10/10 with the above tweaks and  a commitment from the devs to long term updates.

_childDocuments_.review: War Hospital is a resource management simulator with stressful, semi-randomized events that happen, ranging from enemy attacks to patient surgery complications. It feels bad when your other officers are suggesting you treat VIP patients first, forcing you to triage a patient into palliative care who would have survived if promptly treated.This game has a lot of elements that other colony sims have, resource management, painful sacrifices, questionable morality. However, there isn't really a "city building" aspect of the game, it's only upgrades and resource management. It also does NOT have a "sandbox" mode, and the overall story plays out on a calendar timeline on top of your screen, a lot like frostpunk... and although the global timeline events are set in stone, the individuals, their injuries, the severity, and complications are all random, giving the main storyline more replayability. Also, like many colony games, you cannot directly control units, but reassigning them a higher priority task will cause them immediately to switch to that task. There are also scouting teams, and a global map in the style of frostpunk that can uncover global events and provide you with reconnaissance about upcoming attacks.The games mechanics could do with a better tutorial, as not all of the mechanics are explained in great detail. That being said, once you understand them, they seem to flow together is a pretty nice way. My absolute biggest criticism about the game is the cut scene animations... they're really bad, like I can barely tell what's going on bad. As if these character models were being rendered on a PS1.... it's super weird because most the rest of the game is fairly pretty.I see a lot of complaints about the price and lack of content depth in the reviews, but I think the game is plenty deep for what it is. Buy this if you like frostpunk, IXION, the Pale Beyond, and The Last Train Home.  Just a reminder there's no actual city building in this "colony simulator". PS... Playing this game after the Last Train Home feels right, haha...

The year is 1917. You are major Henry Wells, a retired British combat medic, drafted back and thrown into the nightmare of World War I. Understaffed and undersupplied, you are the last bastion of hope for countless soldiers at the French Front.

Treat horrible war injuries as the commander of a field hospital. Build a facility to heal them while the artillery shells explode ear-splittingly close. Use real WW1 equipment and see how your tools and methods evolve. Your choices will make a lasting impact.

detailed_description: Born Of Bread - Baker Edition About the Game Beings from another age are causing havoc across the land! And with their mischief comes a great threat to everyone. The unlikeliest hero, a golem born of bread, will find himself and his newfound buddies in the middle of a drama that's thousands of years in the making. Together, they will visit incredible locals and meet fascinating characters. Although he may not look like much, Loaf might be the hero this land kneads . Play as a flour golem who possesses a never-ending childlike wonder and a set of odd abilities in this 2.5D adventure game! Team Up With Buddies! Loaf can't do it alone: Meet new friends during your adventure, each with their own abilities and personality. Use their unique skills to overcome threats and obstacles whether in fights or when exploring. Together, you’ll engage with varied NPCs, take on side-quests, and find treasures! A Quirky Battle System! Find equipable weapons and upgrades by exploring and completing quests. Each weapon and buddy attack has a button prompt associated with it that you'll need to successfully execute if you want to deal maximum damage! However, make sure you have the right weapon for the job since enemies can have a resistance and a weakness. While you fight, your dragon buddy Dub, who lets you save your progression while adventuring, will stream your fights to a fake audience with his little laptop! Gather more viewers and answer their demands to get rewards!

short_description: Get ready to go on a wacky and joyful turn-based RPG adventure! Play as Loaf, a freshly baked flour golem, and explore the different regions of a wonderful world ripe with mysteries with the help of a colorful cast of characters.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't really wanna bore anyone with a huge review, I think the game is best experienced by your own accord, but I will leave you with this.This is byfar the best Paper Mario inspired game thus far, I've played Bug Fables and The Outbound Ghost. Born of Bread has topped Bug Fables for me. The TTYD vibes are *all* there, but makes enough changes to form the game's own identity. If you like Paper Mario or Bug Fables, this is it chief.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game and at the start I actually did, unfortunately the further in you get the more frustrations pile on with annoying bugs and bland combat. The writing is pretty charming but that's just not enough for me. Maybe I'll still finish it and rethink my rating then but for now I'm just feeling really dejected and unsure of that.Also, I know that the Early Girl time challanges are entierly optional but dear god they're implemented in a way that makes me wanna tear my face off. The timers feel so tight it's like you can never make even a single mistake while running the track, and the fact that you have to always go through her rings means you can't make any meaningful shortcuts or figure out a better route, you just gotta deal with the ♥♥♥♥ the game throws at you and if you ever enter an encounter by accident you might as well just reset. The fact that the platforming in this game feels really bad and imprecise with the camera swinging wildly all around as you're trying to make improtant jumps definetely doesn't help. I am aware that this is very minor in the grand sheme of things but for me it was the straw that broke the camel's back as I failed the highlands race time and time again despite optimizing the ♥♥♥♥ out of it.Hopefully the annoying menu bugs can get patched quickly, but Im not sure how combat could be improved at this stage.Edit:I decided to give this game another shot and got softlocked in literally the first fight I encountered because the enemy's projectile despawned before I could guard against it. I guess it really just wasn't meant to be.Edit 2:I finally finished the game and was even lucky enough to 100% it (I say lucky because there's a good amount of bugs that can just randomly prevent you from completing certain objectives). Words cannot overstate how incredibly MAD I am that I have to keep this review rating as negative. The art is lovely, the story is lovely, the writing is lovely, the enviorment design is lovely, the combat could be more engaging but it does get slightly better the longer you play, but by god... the bugs...Some of them make the game near unpleabale though there is the silverlining of being able to fix most of them with a closing and opening the game again. Sometimes you have to re-try the same quest several times back to back because you get softlocked at the last line of dialogue, or the quest just doesn't register as completed and when you talk to the quest giver again they start the quest from scratch. When you get all the speed upgrades for sprinting there's a slight chance that while running your character will start stuttering in a jarring way. There's also another bug that will randomly delete boons from your equipped view while keeping their effects active leading to terrible confusion. Some boons are also bugged in a way where their effects don't stack, making any copies you get completely useless. I could literally go on and on but you get the idea, it's BAD. Practically every time I sat down to play the game I knew I'd encounter more of them, it got to the point that I started being genuinely surprised whenever stuff worked as intended.After experiencing the full story and everything the game had to offer, I really wish I could recomend it, but remembering all the frustration the bugs and small design decisions put me through... I just can't in good faith tell anyone else to put themselves through that. If this game ever gets patched to a point where the bugs are no longer a problem, 100% buy it, but until that day... maybe think about it twice before making a decision.Also, for whoever cares about my mini-rant about the timed challanges from Early Girl from the beginning of this review: They actually get way easier once you get the speed upgrades (which are received by beating every other of her challenges) so the first two (which were the only ones I experienced at the time of writing the first version of this review) were the only really frustrating ones.

_childDocuments_.review: I have never written a Steam review before, but I am popping that cherry today to address my disappointment with this game. Good things first though: Born of Bread is a game with beautiful visuals, and a lot of charm. The Paper Mario-esque aesthetic is done well, and when it works, the game is quite fun to play.Unfortunately, the game is held back by bugs and certain design choices which took away from my experience with the game. I have been looking forward to playing this game for a long time, which is why I am disappointed with the state that the game is in.Playing this game has been like having a really nice dream, but every time the immersion reaches its peak, you're shook awake. There is definitely much enjoyment to be found in Born of Bread, and the groundwork for a solid game has been laid, but without bugfixes, QoL updates and maybe a revision of certain design choices, TLDR;Pros:- Beautiful visuals, a truly gorgeous game- Charming atmosphere- Engaging story- Likable characters- Great musicCons:- A plethora of bugs that ruin the experience. After a certain point I stopped immersing myself in anticipation of the game suddenly glitching out on me again- Odd design choices in the menu and elsewhere- Combat is mostly uninspired and is trivialised by the Defend command- Blocking stops working at arbitrary times, making some outcomes outside your control.- Absence of common features in RPGs, such as enemy names and item storageNo one is particularly interested in hearing me ramble, but I have compiled a list below over bugs and features that served to hamper my overall experience with the game:

_childDocuments_.review: A charming and enjoyable RPG - heavily inspired by the original Paper Mario games - that is unfortunately inundated by bugs, lacking in polish, and contains a number of questionable battle mechanics.Overall, the game is still fun - and if you just want to scratch that Paper Mario itch, then it's likely still worth your time.However, with the current issues the game has, I don't feel like I can recommend it. The frequency at which I encountered these bugs are the main reason for this negative review.Here's a list of all the bugs I remember personally experiencing:Luckily,  these bugs are fixable by simply opening and closing the menu, or swapping to M&K, but often I have been forced to save and close the game. However, when one of the bugs is that you're unable to save... you can imagine how frustrating it can be to encounter them.As I mentioned, the game itself is enjoyable, and perhaps you'll be luckier than me and not encounter as many bugs. However, repeatedly having to find a save point and close the game just to get the menu to work... well, this slowly chips away at that enjoyment.I have also seen a number of comments mentioning that certain items are missing or specific achievements are unobtainable. This is annoying if you want to 100% the game, however, at least they don't directly impact your enjoyment while playing.Obviously, this point ties in heavily with the previous bugs listed - never have I seen a menu screen in a game be so unreliable before. However, there are also a number of basic or QoL features missing from the game. These are obviously minor grievances, but their absence just makes me feel like the developers haven't played it themselves.There are no keybindings to open specific menu screens. Opening the map would commonly be done with the Back/Select button on a controller, but this is missing.The D-Pad is entirely unused, but would have been convenient for quickly opening the weapons, consumables, boons, or party screens.There is no sorting of menu items and quick scrolling is only added to certain pages.Your weapons, consumables, and boons eventually become long lists, but with no way to sort them or jump to the bottom (where new items are automatically placed), so you have to hold down to scroll through them all.The only page with some form of quick scrolling is the quest log, however, pressing up only jumps to the bottom of the visible list of items - and then you have to continue to hold down to scroll through the rest of them.Finally, switching your partner in battle can only be done by Loaf - and it uses up your turn.While I am fine with it using up your turn to swap partners, the fact that this can only be done by Loaf means that you always have to waste his turn in order to switch out your partner. I don't think it would really affect the difficulty by simply allowing your partner to use their own turn to swap to someone else.The main issue with the battle system is the Defend command.Not only is it inconsistent in its usage, but it is also incredibly powerful and (if abused) ruins the balance of the game.Defend allows you to gain WP (used for casting powerful attacks) by successfully defending against enemy attacks.When you use the Defend command, it immediately becomes the enemy's turn and they attack the person defending.This means that, if you defend with Loaf, the enemy gets two turns.However, if you defend with your partner, the enemy only gets one turn - like normal.I can only assume this is done on purpose, because the Defend command is so strong.It allows you to continue using your most powerful attacks without needing to refill your WP with consumables. And not to mention the fact that later on you get a Boon that allows you to steal health from enemies whenever you successfully defend against their attacks.Ultimately, this leads to the next problem with the Defend command: the safest and most effective way to win a battle ( on the harder difficulty) is to attack with Loaf and have your partner repeatedly defend - allowing them to soak or blocks all of the damage, while also restoring your WP.This is a singleplayer game, so you can obviously play whichever way you want - and I definitely wouldn't blame you for ignoring a complaint about balance. However, knowing that there's an easy way to win every battle did slightly ruin the enjoyment for me personally.There are a couple of ways I can think of that this could be fixed:

_childDocuments_.review: Born of Bread is an adorable, quirky little RPG with a lot going for it and some very noticeable things working against it. I completed most everything in it, enjoyed my time with it but here and there I kept coming up against small annoyances or frustrations. Unfortunately what made them stand out was probably the great time I was having otherwis; so that when something popped up it'd be like taking a nice jog and then stubbing your toe before building back up to speed and whanging your knee on a chair.At the end of the day I would still recommend and heartily give this game a thumbs up but feel sorta bad that every piece of praise I write is going to come with a caveat.You play Loaf, a little boy baked into being by your baker dad, who soon after his birth has to travel the world trying to stop a gang of ruffians from a long dead empire from bringing it back with a powerful artifact. The writing in the game is quite good, specifically in the actual dialogue as well as the general chatter and voice. It's cute, it's very funny and the game does a good job giving even NPCs lots of dialogue and their unique voices. My only real complaints come in the general, as while the story itself is quite good, the pacing can sometimes leave certain moments feeling rushed, unearned or out of nowhere. It's not super egregious, but I will say that the story becomes about something else in the later parts which was actually quite strong and could have been very touching but the transition to it was a tad awkward. It's like...all the pieces were there, the game did A+B=C but if you sat with it too long it felt kinda sudden. I liked the end quite a lot and felt it was deserved but getting there had some stumbles.Gameplay is familiar to any turn based RPG fan of the Paper Mario series (early on). Similar to complaints above, it has all the parts, does a good job making things unique in it's own system like a focus on the weapons you can fit in a backpack, badges you can equip...but then cracks start showing. Your MC has an overwhelming number of options, and so do your sidekicks! Except...they only have 5 max slots and you can't switch the slots in battle. The battles mimic a streaming setup so that you can do well to earn back points to use abilities, but...they only ever ask you to use items so there's little variety. The combat is full of this, where it's quite enjoyable moment to moment but then you have to work around some choice or limitation that feels artificial or hurts gameflow.And I think that's my main complaint, to sum up and not harsh on each part of the game individually; the game has a lot of design decisions that feel very old-school or outdated in service to the game it's trying to evoke. I know a lot of games trying to bring back a long left behind style of game fall into this trap, but it's easy to see why. After all, when you romanticize a game from the past you often forgive it or let it glow warmly without remembering all the warts and flaws in favor of the nice feeling you get. Most noticeable is they gave an in game reason why you need to save in locations and there isn't a robust auto-save (and a character to go with it) but in practice it means that you are continually going to sacrifice gamefeel for a design choice that went away for a reason. Like fast travel when your dungeons and areas are expansive being limited to 5 general locations, like inventory space being so limited. The game constantly has outdated design decisions dragging down an otherwise well designed, fun and up to date game.Which makes me sound quite critical. And yes, there is a lot that could rub you wrong in this game. But there's a ton to love. Specifically the art style, aesthetic and world are gorgeously done and so fun and the music is fantastic without any draggers. The area design is strongly varied, the type matching makes you think in combat, sidequests have meaningful rewards and stories. I loved a lot of the characters, thought Loaf had a ton of personality for a silent protag and loved the antagonist group too.People will see a Mostly Positive or low Very Positive and fall into all or nothing thinking which I think is an enormous disservice to games like this that have their faults but have a lot of love put into it and a lot of love you can get out of it. We shouldn't write off ambitious but flawed games because they didn't reach the heights of games people have on their GOAT lists. It's unrealistic and unfair, and you will miss some truly enjoyable experiences if you only ever play the critically loved series.I would full heartedly suggest playing this game and would 100% buy any sequel from a tiny studio that learned a lot from this labor of love to go out there and do even better next time.

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately I think this bun needs to be in the oven a bit longer. While it is a Paper Mario inspired rpg and is a good game there are a few glitches and bugs that I have encountered that have forced me to exit the game and have lost about an hour of progress because of it. Jumping over a river and getting shot by an enemy projectile thus getting trapped under the water with no way of escaping, questlines not triggering when going to the appropriate area and talking to the proper person, enemies in the final area of the game attempting to attack and not being able to and softlocking the game. Additionally many of the quest rewards are very powerful one time consumables, that I don't want to use unless I am in a situation that I need them, however, there is no item storage, so despite the inventory upgrades, from completing quests, my inventory can only fit just over 5 items besides those special ones. Overworld abilities are all finicky and lackluster too, especially trying to swap your party members requiring opening the menu on one of the tabs that can be swapped to another menu, when some of those abilities are required in races. Then the battle system is very awkward with the defend action allowing the enemies to attack twice in a turn if used on your lead member, and swapping party members in battle taking a whole action of your leader. It's just very punishing without being difficult, so instead of strategizing within combat, it is mostly just a damage race. All of this is to say: I do like the game, but as a game setting out to be a modern day successor to Paper Mario in humor and writing, I will say it succeeds(the humorous tone and attempt at deep lore clash a bit), but in every other aspect it is just not as fun and has its own issues to worry about first

_childDocuments_.review: I just ended my first playthrough of Born of Bread.A few positives, negatives and thoughts:Positives: The games biggest upside is definitely the cast and atmosphere. This game oozes the personality and quirkiness paper-likes are known for and makes it its own. The music is always delightful and the areas are interesting while adhering to a somewhat traditional enviromental pattern imo. Also there is a dedicated run function you can even improve throughout the game.Negatives: The first thing I have to note about the game is its difficulty or rather: decided lack thereoff. Enemies aren't that strong, especially with the right badges. They drop imo way too much experience and your weapons are way too strong. I destroyed the final boss in 3 turns and I even tried my best to avoid enemies as much as I could from the end of chapter 2 onward though enemies are pretty quick and hard to dodge, especially when they are coming from the foreground or you fall into a pit (which respanws you at your last standing location aka where the enemy is that chased you).Furthermore I encountered quite a few situations where the game would just bug and I could hardly/not finish a fight/mission at all (the intended way) because I had high speed while starting the fight so my command wheel would be off the battle screen alongside my characters. Thankfully the game throws quite a lot of save spots at you so just save often. Currently it seems some achievements are also bugged, I hope this gets fixed. I spent a lot of time trying to 100% the game but I don't think I can do that at the moment. At the time of writing this I have 18 hours but I'm sure if you just want to experience the story you can do that in about 10-12. I really tried to do all the side content.So, it would seem my negatives column is much longer than my positives column. So why do I still recommend the game? Simply put, those negatives didn't bother me enough to hate the overall game and if you just want to go through the story first, you might find a decent challenge. My only gripe would be that the 25€ pricetag is a biiiiiit too step imo but I still enjoyed the game a ton.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a paper mario fan who enjoys the old games, but still likes where the series is going, this game is definitely for you! From the charming art style to the wonderfully written character-driven narrative, this game is truly a delight. It's not without its issues, but I think I can look past them for the most part, because this game had me smiling from ear to ear from start to finish!First off, this game is STUNNING! The vibrant, cheery colors and the bright lighting give the whole game this light-hearted adventure feel to it that makes me feel like I'm playing through an old children's novel! Then it gives way occasionally to a deep an ominous purple for the world's evil, which makes a fantastic contrast. And the character designs are just SO FUN! Everyone is amazingly unique with their own colors, species, and general mannerisms. You can even unlock custom color palettes for each of them!  Speaking of the characters, I'm happy to say each and every one of your main cast's character's stories are a delight to complete. Each character has their own side quest they want you to complete so that they can learn and grow, and also to unlock their ultimate abilities. I love the personalities of all of them too, especially Dub and Lint who are just nervous and adorable :) Each of them bounce off each other in fun ways that clearly shows a lot of attention was put into the dialogue. The story is a light-hearted adventure that will make you smile the whole way through! Though it is certainly a simple narrative, I think it works in the game's favor. It is clearly not meant to be taken super seriously, and constantly cracks jokes and puns that are both fun to listen to, and also not SO in your face as to be unfunny. It strikes a perfect balance that just makes you feel like a kid again :) And the MUSIC, oh MAN it's good. It changes style depending on what area you're in, so you get to experience a ton of stuff the composer is clearly very talented with. It's almost kind of a shame some of the battle tracks in particular don't stick around longer than they do, but I don't even count that as a downside because it means I just love the soundtrack to death enough to want to listen to it more, haha.  Finally, the battle system is a ton of fun too! It pulls in elements from both the older paper mario games (like partner turns and different weapons to use in your attacks), as well as some elements from the new-age paper mario games (like origami king's badge system), AND it even throws in some mechanics of its own (like a backpack-hero style inventory, and type-matchups for extra damage)! It is definitely an easy game, though I'm not convinced that's always a bad thing, especially since a hardmode option was added to the game during my playthrough.As stated before, the combat is pretty easy on normal mode, which is fine during a lot of normal enemy fights, but I did feel as though the bosses lacked oomph, and I was able to beat them in just a few turns. This is mainly due to the fact that your weapons deal A LOT of damage to bosses that just don't have enough health. Especially once you start unlocking new special attacks, because one of the ones you get pretty early on can deal upwards of 30 damage per turn if you have enough RP.  I have a feeling that the hard mode will be much more of a balanced challenge. I have yet to play it, so I may update this review later to accommodate.  Without spoiling the ending, I did find the end to be a bit too abrupt. I beat the final boss and then credits were rolling maybe 5 minutes later. I still like the ending, because I like the story that goes with it, but I do wish I got to spend some more time at the end of the game. That kind of ties into the fact that I think the whole game is just a little too short. I payed 25 dollars, which is not a bad price at all, but I'm kind of a dollar-per-hour kind of gamer, and it took me 17 hours to beat the game, which included main story progression as well as looking for secrets and completing most of the side quests. This final part of the cons is less of an actual complaint, and more of a caution to those of you who really hate bugs. I did encounter a few bugs, but all except 1 of them were just funny visual or auditory bugs that made me chuckle, so they really didn't bother me at all. The bug I got that softlocked me was in a spot that only set me back like 4 minutes, so it wasn't bad at all. I think some funny bugs can enhance the enjoyment of a game, but how others feel about that is purely up to the type of player. Born of Bread is definitely worth a purchase, whether you're looking for a new paper-inspired game to play, or just want a cute game with a fun story! It's a little rough around the edges, but if you're able to look past those things then I can guarantee you're going to have a blast!

_childDocuments_.review: Born of Bread follows a recipe that adds fun gameplay, sprinkles in endearing characters, and bakes in a great soundtrack, culminating in a tasty piece of gameplay. It's a delightful adventure that takes inspiration from the classic Paper Mario, set in a fantastic world full of wacky inhabitants and hilarious humor. The plot will take us from the streets of the kingdom to icy dark forests, as we chase after entities from another era that are wreaking havoc in the present day. I must admit that at first I wasn’t entirely convinced of the visuals of the game, but when I really paid attention to the promotional trailers, I thought "hold up, wait a minute”, and little by little it grew on me. That's why I'm going to start by mentioning the art, which is presented in a 2.5D that combines a cartoon style for the characters, details in menus and some additions to the environment, with objects and structures in 3D that at first I thought felt kinda weird, but resulted in a truly neat addition to the style of the game. The menus in particular are very charismatic, with doodles for the character cards that fit very well with the general aesthetic, and something that draws attention from the very main menu of the game. It is worth noting that here, in the settings, there are some colorblind accessibility options that, unfortunately, I have rarely seen in other games, and I really congratulate the devs for facilitating the gameplay to people with visual impairments. My respects!Hand in hand with the visuals goes the music, which left me totally hooked since the moment I turned on the game, and I kept listening to the main song for a while while I was tweaking the options. Not only the sound stands out there, since throughout the adventure we have an exquisite repertoire of songs, and several combat remixes suitable for each area of the game. Undoubtedly a super worked aspect, really hyped me.As for the story, Born of Bread will put us in the role of Loaf, a flour golem just out of the stove, and that gets pulled into the shenanigans of the villains pretty much instantly. Creatures from another time have come to the present looking to complete some kind of enigmatic ritual, and it will be our duty to stop them before they cause even more problems for the kingdom. This adventure will take us through various areas with their own thematic plots, from swampy forests to even the top of a mountain where a martial arts tournament is taking place!On our journey, we’ll befriend a cast of charming and unique characters, such as Yagi the martial artist goat, or Dub the little dragon. Dub, in particular, plays a crucial role, as he is in charge of saving our game, and I thought it was a nice touch to integrate this mechanic to a particular NPC. They are all great, and have their own subplots that deepen their personalities. But there are also more secondary and recurring individuals, such as Papa Baker, Loaf's father, who left me laughing constantly. It's worth noting that the villains have their own story alongside ours, and we get to witness some details from their point of view from time to time, which is a very nice addition.The gameplay, on the other hand, is very entertaining. We’ll be able to explore different maps from head to toe, with exploration skills that depend on our companions. Each member of the group has their own ability, such as digging mounds or lighting the way with a flashlight, which generates some variety. However, I must say that opening the menu to constantly switch between characters becomes a bit cumbersome, especially late into the game, and I think a dedicated button to switch between companions would have been really nice (unless there was one and I missed it).As we explore the world of Born of Bread we can find new weapons for Loaf, who can equip them in a Tetris-like inventory, giving us a nice variety as long as they fit; also, amulets or talismans that give us passive bonuses, such as improved health or the ability to run faster. There are also some small lizards that will be our collectables of the game, and also reward us with skill points, used to learn new attacks for our companions. This system integrates exploration with combat very well, I thought it was great!The combat is turn-based, where we can attack and defend ourselves with different elements, taking Loaf and a partner that we can change in the middle of the fight. So far nothing fancy. But! To spice it up, we’ll have active actions in the form of mini-games or quick-time events that vary depending on the weapon and attack, which rewards us with a very fun dynamic in combat. Some mini-games will make us keep our cursor in the center of a target, others will ask us to press a sequence of buttons, and so on. Defending ourselves does not require a mini-game, we simply press the interaction button at the right moment to receive less damage!In the middle of the battle we’ll have Will Points, which would be the “mana” of the game, and can be earned in several ways, either with objects or using our defense action correctly. But we can also acquire these points by carrying out requests made by our audience, such as attacking or using specials... because our fights will live on air, by the way. There will even be a stream chat, with people spamming emotes or behaving like typical internet trolls, and I really loved this aspect! It is worth noting that each emote is unique to the game, and some are based on the characters, which is a very cool extra detail. Born of Bread is a game very well cooked, with equal parts fun, humor and even some emotional moments, perhaps with combat that becomes a little easy as we level up and find powerful weapons, but entertaining all the same. It gives us a wonderful world, very cheerful and mysterious at the same time, with a story that develops well and has some twists that I loved, especially with a certain companion who joins in the final stretch! The characters are endearing, and always have something to add regarding some side mission, plus we can occasionally chat around a campfire while Dub recharges his laptop. It's a very beautiful title in all aspects, and I'm very glad I played it.

_childDocuments_.review: It's okay, but just doesn't do anything original and combat is tedious. It looks and sounds nice, and I love the designs of the main characters, but the game itself is lacking. All the enemies are the same, all of the main characters attacks are the same. There is an element system, but which attacks do damage to which enemies is arbitrary, and there isn't any strategy to battle other than that. There are plenty of NPC quests, but most of them boil down to running back and forth, and the questgivers are generally annoying. I also ran into several glitches, for example: if one ally runs out of HP and you switch to another ally, that ally will also be dead, despite their HP displaying as full. The game is not unplayable by any means, but in terms of gameplay depth it's several steps back from even the first Paper Mario.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish could I leave a positive review of this game without lying, but, sadly, that's not the case.The word that came to mind once I finished the game was: lacking. The combat lacked mechanical depth and proper exploration, RP was basically useless and at the end they double your hp if you did all partners quests. The Lore felt it was going somewhere but then you were at the sky and the games just ended. Jester, who was deemed the second protagonist, didn't really do much, his sessions were just waking simulators at best. The lack of a quick access to swich partners really slowed experience. The lack of mechanical polish was OBVIOUS with the great amount of bugs and oversight.What I love about this genre is that it proved it can stand up by itself without "mario" at the title. Sadly this game lacked so much on so many different areas, that It could not.

_childDocuments_.review: Four people made this. four. FOUR??? Not twenty????? And yes, I see they had a publisher and another team handled music, but still...this is a 5 course feast from an understaffed kitchen. For the ambition I can see in this project, I feel it's almost unfair of me to complain about any little issues or half-baked ideas. I'll give my feedback below, but please know that I give this game my highest regard regardless.- The writing is consistently charming. Characters have clear identities and motivations that are enhanced by excellent designs and emotes. Yagi's expressions are a joy to behold. Also, it is SO refreshing that your teammates aren't forgotten the moment their chapter is over (*cough* Paper Mario *cough*). They even have unique side-quests that alter the epilogue!- The aesthetic is so good. It's giving Cartoon Network. It's giving Disney Channel. Somebody on this team deserves to be picked up by a major studio.- The music. THE MUSIC. Nuff said.- Side quests, while simple, are pretty cute through their fun dialogue and tiny stories.- controls are good. Feels like it should. Loaf can Naruto run.- The combat is kind of bland. It's not bad...but something was missing. The majority of complaints I've seen were that it's too easy, but I don't think it's that simple. Paper Mario games aren't especially hard, but the combat has variety and unique elements that keeps the gameplay loop fresh. Yet in Born of Bread, even bosses are taken down with the same strategies as a regular encounter. That being said, I won't give it a con, because I never dreaded the combat. Attacks are quick and fun to watch and everything flows well. And I don't think it's fair to hold it up against a game refined by dozens if not hundreds of Nintendo Devs.- Puns. They're lovably used, but they tear down the unique character identities when nearly everyone uses them.- The story isn't going to blow you away. There's nothing groundbreaking in the plot (just like Paper Mario HEYOOOHHH!), but sometimes that's okay. It's just a fun little time with fun little guys, and you can't be mad at that.- The economy is a bit unbalanced. I kept expanding my wallet and collecting more clovers, but I never felt a need to spend them. There were very few purchases in the game that would have broken the bank, and not a single one that would have emptied me out (which is kind of the point of wallet upgrades). And you hardly need to buy anything since item drops are so plentiful. Although, it's always fun to break boxes and pick up stuff so it gets a neutral.- glitches. Softlocks. Small things that didn't particularly hinder my experience, but enough to say that this needed more time in the oven. And I'm so positive that this is an issue of publisher stakeholders demanding the game be released, because with the amount of passion that's on display, I can't imagine they wanted to release it like this. It becomes very obvious in the last chapter where things are super rushed and there's hints of things they wanted to include but couldn't (I'm looking at you, floating dragon city).- The final dungeon. This goes with my last point, you can tell they were rushed here. It's only two small rooms and one enemy type. They even started getting creative with partner ability puzzles, but it's over so quick that it doesn't leave the slightest impact.- Puzzles. The partners have so much potential for creative puzzle design and it's (almost) never utilized. Yagi can be a rock left behind for switches. Chloe has an arched projectile for hitting switches behind fences or through holes. Secret fourth character can aim shots for distant switches. Lint can....well he can dig, but I'm sure there's a way to make that interesting. Maybe he has to make a special dirt pattern, I dunno.All the above can be forgiven though, because, again...four people. And it does NOT spoil the experience. I had a great time!This entire game is such an inspiration to any indie developer trying to take on an ambitious project. Looking at this, it feels like anything is possible if you BELIEVE! I absolutely recommend this if you're looking for a fun little time that makes you feel good things. Loaf is just a little guy doing big adventures and I love him for it.

_childDocuments_.review: If I could sum up the entire experience of what I thought of this game, it would be someone offering you a raisin cookie when you thought it was a chocolate cookie. Looks nice and appetizing from the exterior, but once you take a bite, the flavors reveal themselves. Oh and the cookie was half baked too.+ From previous reviews and patch notes apparently the game was released in a buggy state. Thankfully, as of Build 3.2.4, I had not run into any game breaking bugs. + Aesthetically, the game is visually appealing! From the character designs to the view of the world, it’s pretty great!+ The music of the game is ok, nothing bad but at the same time not something I would listen to outside of the game itself.+ A nice touch is whenever you finish a side quest, that person may show up in the Audience.+ Plays well on the Steam Deck!++ The biggest positive I can give this game would be the campfire scenes. Specifically after you get the 3rd party member and onward. Seeing each of your party members interact with each other really makes me care for them! It’s a shame they only do this at the end of chapters.Unfortunately, with those positives, the Negatives heavily outweigh them.The Story of this game is rather weak. From the beginning of when the conflict stirs to the end of the game when it resolves, the whole journey felt underwhelming. To lay it out:Personal take, I feel like they could have made the story more entertaining. Early game spoiler notice! In Chapter 1 The combat system is what you would expect from the old style Paper Mario games. You can attack, use items, use special moves to deal more damage or support, etc. Born of Bread added an Audience/Streaming system to the gameplay. At random points of a fight, a viewer will come with a request that the player can choose to follow. Fulfilling their request nets the Team with additional WP. With how simple the combat system is, how can it be negative?When it is your opponent's turn, you have the opportunity to lessen their damage by 1 if you time your defense in line with their attack. What makes the Defend Action Card different from a regular defend action is as follows:The last two bullet points trivializes the entire battle system to a monotonous state. In addition, it makes the Audience system moot.Enemies deal too much damage and Loaf is low on health? Have your Partner defend.You want Loaf to use an attack but don't have the WP? Have your Partner defend.The enemy is charging up a powerful attack? You get the idea now.If it were harder to time like Super Guard in Paper Mario: The Thousand Year Door I can see it as a risk-reward type deal. However, that is not the case.Also if you are playing on Hard Mode like I did, you have to use this strategy. With the amount of enemies added, in addition to their buffed stats, simply having Loaf and their partner attack is not sustainable in the long term. Even with the 10 Items you can bring, they will burn out quick. The Hard Mode strategy is to attack with Loaf and defend with your partner. It's not fun.The game's tutorial teaches the player how to Attack, use WP/RP, and defend. What the tutorial did not bother to teach was the enemy weaknesses and resistances.Enemies will have moves that will deal more damage towards them or lessen the damage received depending on the move chosen. This was not known to me until I found a Boon saying enemies have weaknesses. If you wanted to know about this important mechanic, you would have to go out of your way to head to the Saver's Guild to read up on it. Make this part of a tutorial! Not something players have to go and read up on.I received this game as a gift from a Steam Friend and wanted to give it a shot. After playing, I was planning to stop after Chapter 2 and leave a short review because I didn’t like how the game was going. However, I wanted to give the game a fair chance, so I played Born of Bread through to the end. After the completion, I was still not satisfied with what I played and I do not see myself coming back to finish all the side quests.Personal recommendation, buy Bug Fables or the Remake of a Thousand Year Door. But if you really want to try this game out, I suggest waiting for a steep sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Gonna start this off by saying the game is good, but given that this game was clearly inspired by Paper Mario The Thousand Year Door i'm gonna draw a lot comparisons. This Game still has some interesting ideas and takes on Thousand Year Doors mechanics but personally I think they just end up being less good then what they're inspired by.  Starting off with how you gain weapons and passive bonuses: In Thousand Year door both of these thing as mostly tight to badges and you have the option to gain badge slots with every Level up. Meanwhile what Born of Bread does is split these two into their own categories which still each can possibly be enhanced with Level-ups, however getting a passive slot requires you to use 2 level ups to get 1 slot and upgrading your weapon rack requires the use of 3 level ups. These are also limited to a max amount so once you've gotten all the slots leveling will only let you up your base stats of HP, WP and RP. Which makes further level ups less interesting and also feels more limited then the Paper Mario Games.Then theres the combat itself which definetly has some depth but doesnt really feel as interesting as what it was inspired by. Enemies have an Elemental weakness similar to pokemon and are strong against 1 of 3 damage types, blunt, cutting or piercing. However you are given a badge that tells you the enemies weaknesses shortly after starting the game, so there's not really a need to guess and experiment what an enemy is weak to. Not like it matters much anyway since you can still go with any element anyway as long as you don't pick the damage type they're strong against. And even if you do that you biggest punishment is that you just deal very little or no damage. In the Paper Mario Games you would have burning enemies, enemies that have spikes on their heads or to their sides which stopped you from attacking with certain moves outright and punished you by dealing damage to you and breaking up your attack. This meant you had to overcome your enemies by using your badges and partners to the fullest which made combat feel like a little puzzle with each new enemy encounter. Granted once you knew what worked you'd straight go to use that but it made enemies feel more unique compared to here where every figth feels mostly the same.The Theater Stage Battles from the Paper Mario games where replaced by your fights essentially being twitch streams which you may find off putting tho I personally didnt mind since i just accepted that this is a more modern game for a more modern crowd and i thought it could still work just aswell as the stage battles. However they're just as lacking as my previous points. While you do get some commentary from your viewers they feel overall way less particepating then the play viewers from Paper Mario. Every now and then they will give you a small task and if you do what they want they will in turn give you WP. Which is all there is to it. Comperatively the Paper Mario play viewers would throw items, good and bad ones at you to help or hinder you and you could interupt them from doing any of those things if you pay attention. With this game having battle streams i was expecting stuff like viewers donating to either help you or screw with you like sending items view a delivery drone or donating to reverse your controls or something, given none of that happened i was actually let down a bit.Partners also feel less usefull since their out of combat abilites are sometimes awkward to use and can't be used to intiate Battles like in Paper Mario. neither are these abilites even represented in their actual Combat Moves. Theres not really any particular gimmick to the partners like in Paper Mario either where you'd have a character that is meant to be used at range or one that makes you invulnerable to avoid strong moves etc. What you get here is that each partner can use 3 elemtal damage types (given you leveled them as such), but for some reason allthough you allready have a low Partner count of only 4, 2 share psychic damage and one of those two also shares fire damage with another partner, while theres still elements that no partner uses??? Its a weird choice tho overall not even important since like mentioned earlier you can use almost any element on any enemy. Loaf the main character also doesnt have as many helpful out of combat moves as Mario does in Paper Mario. At best you'll find a crusher that'll make you flat and allow you to float in the air for a bit or a fire which lets you slam into breakable walls but those are rare and you barely get to use them. You'd think with the MC being made of bread they could have come up with a few more Bread based Abilities.My last bit of Negative Critic will be about how the game has some bits that make it feel unfinished/buggy. For example:-I had multiple ocassions where the game would randomly softlock both during and out of combat and i'd bet stuck unable to make any more inputs which left me with no choice but to atl+f4 and restart from my last save-Sometimes the Game decides that your Partner will go first in Combat, if this happens you better press the position switch button as fast as you can because if you don't then as soon as your Partner finished their move your turn will end without Loaf having done anything. For some reason Loaf can not go second ever so if your partner does a move first the game will assume you allready used both characters.-I had multiple, tho rare, instances where the Camera would bugg out and fixate on an area i'm not even in, essentially making me stumble through the dark since i was unable to see where my character is going.Now with all these Negatives out of the way I will say that the game also has some good ideas like for example being able to use skillpoints on your partners to unlock different variations of moves which i thought was neat. But if anything what kept me going was probably the writing. Tho Sometimes hamfisted with its puns i definetly liked the characters and how they interacted and reacted with/to the world. So I'd say I overall enjoyed the experience.TL;DR, I would say get it on Sale if you're unsure and for those who player Paper Mario Thousand Year Door, don't go into this game expecting something genre defining.

_childDocuments_.review: If this game is on sale, then I'd recommend it, otherwise, you should pick it up if combat doesn't matter much to you and you're really into a Paper Mario style gameplay. I really want to enjoy the game. I like the characters, the environment, the music, and its decent story, but it has some glaring issues. The UI is clunky and weird to navigate. Combat - This is where most of my complaint will be. The combat is boring and lack impact. It has this weird pokemon typing-like system which mostly boils down to using attacks the enemies aren't resistant to. It tries to have more depth with how defending work, but it fails since the enemies and bosses are wayyyyy too easy. The bosses lack mechanics and uses either basic attacks or buff themselves. Depending on the RNG, certain group of enemies could be more difficult. Overall, the balancing is awful in this game. Also, many partners use the same action-command sequences. For a Paper Mario game, the combat is definitely inferior compared to the first game.

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game through it entirety on the Steam Deck with no visual issues, at least none related to the game itself. There seems to be Keyboard and Mouse controls as well, but considering I played everything on a controller I may mention things that might be different on those controls that I'm not aware of.Pros:- The world building and environment is phenomenal. Everything from the 2D art inside a 3D environment is meshed together so wonderfully. It's able to do its own style while paying homage to Paper Mario's artstyle.- The main characters are likable and expressive, with none feeling too bland or too cheesy. As eccentric as some of them can be, they're also portrayed as down-to-earth as well, and don't go over the top with their personalities if it's unnecessary. You'll love the people you're meant to love, and hate those you're meant to hate.- The narrative as you progress the game pays light homage to a lot of other pop culture references (i.e. Pokemon, The Office, etc.), but retains enough of its own originality and personality that I never got tired to reading what everyone has too say, and even if the main plot is a little generic, the way the story is being told as the game progresses has never gotten boring for me, and I always look to see to what every NPC I encounter has to say. The dialogue in this game is genuinely entertaining to me.Cons:- The Combat System is my biggest gripe, which I'll go on for a bit. It's really un-intuitive. It's like a very watered down version of TTYD's combat system, where there's an audience that help restore certain resources if you do well enough, but usually in sparse amounts and they don't really make a difference. The timed hit system can be annoying at times, especially since there's no soft blows where if you mis-time a hit you'd at least do 1 damage. No, if you mess up you do nothing.- Early in the game you do have to deal with some resource management and strategy, especially since you only get to carry 5 items at a time in the beginning. But you can very easily stack up the game's main combat stat through level ups, which is Will Points (WP), until you have enough to waste since every stat is restored on level up. Believe me, about 97% of my level ups were on WP only since it was the only thing I ever needed. Oh yeah by the way, NONE of the enemies in the game have status resistances or immunity, including EVERY BOSS. Meaning as soon as you get something like Sleep, WHICH CAN STACK, every fight becomes trivialized provided you have enough resources for that fight duration. I never got to see the final boss attack me because I never let him.- The combat visuals are also very minimal. Aside from the very pretty background, the visual effects and expression of movements combat-wise are very bare-bone, and the camera is almost always at a fixed position other than zooming in a little for close range attacks (but only when you attack). Nearly every enemy has the same tell for when they attack, so you don't need to learn their attack patterns, save for a couple. There's also no Stylish moves or whatever, or if there was I never found it or needed it. Even the level up screen felt a little flat. Mixed:- The music. The music amazing everywhere EXCEPT during combat. I don't know why it always goes back to the combat, but the battle music, while there is a variety for each area, really doesn't feel as impactful and are very hit or miss for me. Even the boss fight music feels off, and the only reason I can think off is that it doesn't have that "Paper Mario pop" or intensity. Maybe it's the audio channel mixing, maybe it's the instrumentation, maybe I'm wrong and musically impaired, either way I'm not feeling it. - The UI/Menuing is kind of all over the place, and has a weird hierarchy for certain tabs in the menu. It's sort of the opposite of paper mario where all the equipment and item management is closer to the front and stuff like party status/arrangement and badges are closer to the middle-back. If there was a way to manually reorder the tabs myself I'd be fine. The UI could also serve to add more QoL improvements, stuff like a way to pop up the character status in the overworld, instead of having to jump into the pause menu every time.I think overall this game definitely has the narrative charm of Paper Mario, especially in a modern context. But there's a lot that could be improved in just the gameplay and combat. Personally, I still think Bug Fables did a better job in being faithful to the spirit of Paper Mario 64, while I'd say Born of Bread is like the middle ground between PM64 and TTYD. If you like Paper Mario, I do think Born of Bread does it justice done fair enough, especially for its content and price point.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright just finished going through this game as of version 3.1 and I have to say I definitely enjoyed this game! Of course while there are good things there is also some things I don't really like so I'll just list what I found enjoyable:The Good:Characters - I genuinely found each character interesting and funny at timesArt-style - I am a sucker for the Paper Mario aesthetic both the character designs and the world designs were genuinely one of my favorite things about this game.Music - The soundtrack is actually kinda a bop in my opinionSide-quests - A shock I know, but the side-quests in this game actually feels enjoyable and less overbearing and confusing for the most part. In some cases I actually found them better than Paper Mario side-questsPartners - I don't really have to say anymore but the implementation of this type of party system scratched that paper Mario itch for meStory - It is a really simple story and that is all that it needs to be. I won't say anymore so no spoilersSkins - No words are also kneaded (Puns also included in the "good")The Mixed:(Most of these opinions are likely due to current bugs not yet fixed)Battle-System - Really an in between good and mixed but I'll put it here for bug reasons, I find it difficult to calculate stats due to bugs not letting me see certain stat upgrades in the party skill menu and is only stuck on a certain party member's stat upgrade along with a bug where a certain red stone. I do like the combat however, but I do find specials kinda lacking and some other issues along side it.Achievements - As of right now some do not work due to bugs I believe, (for example there is a boon in the game that is just nowhere) so if your an achievement hunter or 100% completionist, waiting wouldn't be so bad, but hey don't let it stop you from enjoying the game.Items - Just felt like more could be done sadly no cooking in bread gameThe Bad:Bugs - There are a ton of bugs still. While it does add charm at times, if you do not save constantly it's really a hassleDifficulty - Honestly I played on hard mode and it was tough at times, however some of the combat mechanics still made it kinda easy, however I do not see this as a total negative as I think paper mario has similar issues so I don't really put it high into the rankingsOverall: Do I recommend this game? Yes, for Paper Mario/Bug Fables fans and need an itch scratched this is a great game to experience, but if you want to wait for any more updates and fixes I wouldn't blame you. However to the developers thanks for the fun game would love to see more of the Born of Bread world if ever possible.

_childDocuments_.review: Compelling game play, amazing music, wonderful art, fantastic story, and fulfilling secrets!As someone who 100% completed the game and achievements, I can vouch for the game if you are alright with:- Bugs (Save often)  - Timing-based RPG Combat that sometimes breaks (unavoidable damage)  - Some functionalities breaking like cosmetics and badges (boons)- Getting Potentially unhelpful items from sidequests or secret spots (cosmetics, nice but not incredible to have)Overall, worth it to play but not as worth it to 100%, although it is surprisingly easy, only needed around 20% guided help. But if you like a good story and a simple enough game with amazing music and great art, then I highly suggest this game!

_childDocuments_.review: I really wish i liked this game, but it cuts short in so many aspects. I'll try listing the pros and cons, because i do think the game does a lot of things right. Apologies in advance for possible bad grammar and spelling, english isn't my first language.The best thing i think this game does is it's characters. Everyone is very charming and sticks with you throughout the entire game, unlike others I've seen where some are forgotten after the chapter where they're introduced. Their personalities and gimmicks are very unique, and i think everyone can find a favorite from the group. I also love how Dub is your save point! Saving is an actual canonical thing in this game and its very neat.You also get to see the antagonist gang interact with eachother and develop along the way. Those were some of my favorite moments.Lastly, theres so many more minor yet still reoccuring characters that all have their own thing going on. Some obvious like Papa baker and Number One, but also more unexpected ones like Piper. It is probably impossible to play this game and not find a single character you enjoy.The music and art-style of this game are also phenominal. I was surprised multiple times by the soundtrack suddenly going crazy, in a good way! And every area is guaranteed to look gorgeous with it's own unique aesthetic in this wonderful 2D world.I also really like the menu. The weapon equip screen, the skill trees, the funny drawings for everyone and color palettes, even the way you unlock new skills. Its very unique and gives the game a lot of personality.And, this may not be completely relevant but i feel it is worth mentioning, this game was apparently made by a very small team. And even though i don't have a particularly positive sight on this game, i don't feel like I've wasted my money. I feel this studio has a lot of potential and will probably make great things in the future.Alright, now lets get to what probably most of you are reading for.I'd talk about the biggest issue first, but i feel like there is no one single biggest issue. Its a lot of small things that ultimately bring down the experience for me. I'll just list as many of them as i can in a random order.-The storyThis might just be me, but i didn't feel gripped by the main story at all. The stakes were so insanely low. At multiple points the enemy just walks away with one of the artifacts you need, and in stead of going after him or stopping him, the main characters just keep talking and are bummed out. The final chapter was also WAY too short to do all the buildup justice, it was like 2 rooms long? And by that point i had already gotten so strong that i could kill the final boss without a sweat.-Bugs, so many bugsI hard-locked so many times during this game that i had to keep count. For anyone unfamiliar, a soft-lock is a commonly used term in video games. It is when you get stuck somewhere and can't do anything but open the menu and restart the level/go back to the last save point. A hard lock is when you can't even open the menu. By the time i finished, i had encountered 8 hard-locks (Either my game froze when doing random things, or i got stuck in some kind of menu and no buttons did anything) and a lot of those lost me huge amounts of progress because i hadn't saved in a while or it was after a long cutscene. I also encountered a few softlocks, but those are excusable because it was a result of me messing around perhaps a bit too much.Thats not all. Theres many times where enemy animations worked incorrectly making me unable to time my block, or where suddenly the entire background in the overworld disappeared (happened mostly indoors).And perhaps the biggest bug is that when your buddy defends, the enemy will not attack after. And while defending, you take 0 damage in stead of just taking less damage while blocking regularly. So you can attack with loaf, and defend with whoever else you were playing with and as long as your timing is on point you would take 0 damage. I had to stop myself from using this to not make this pathetically easy game even easier, but it locked me out of defending with my ally which was very annoying.There are so many other things i encountered but i won't be listing them all, as that would be boring. Point is: This game is very broken.-CombatThe combat in this game is fine in the beginning, but it gets derailed very fast. Theres a lot of ally abilities or weapons that can instantly kill every regular enemy on the screen in the first turn. Meanwhile the enemies deal pretty much the same damage throughout the entire game, and the only issue is when a lot spawn at once and you can't kill them all instantly. Its way too easy!Why does Alfie get a skill that deals 3x3 damage, and then a damage up of one?! Thats 12 damage to every enemy on screen not counting crits! And if you do make skills that strong, at least start giving the enemies and bosses more health. From my counting the final boss had 80 health. Way too low!I have not gone down a single time. In fact, i have not had to use a single healing item ever.It also really doesn't help that you level up insanely fast. You only need 100 EXP to level up, and it stays at that for the entire game. I only healed through leveling, basically.Not once has this game properly challenged me. And as someone who enjoys turn based RPG's, that s a pretty big bummer.  So in short, the combat is pathetically easy and keeps getting easier as you move on. And there is no hard-mode.-A lot of little things.Theres no way to change your controls. Would have been nice, since it says that the "Open chat" button is spacebar, but spacebar is also the "Confirm action" button. So opening chat doesn't work on keyboard.For some quests, you get instructions from the quest-giver and then have to go do the quest. But if i'd stop playing before completing it, usually i didn't remember said instructions. A way to re-read them, or maybe having the npc's repeat them would have been nice.The puzzles... can i even call them puzzles? They're either super long fetch quests (chapter 3 in it's entirety is a fetch quest, especially annoying because of the instructions thing i mentioned earlier) or they're "Use this character's right click ability" with no other challenge to it. Right at the end, in the final dungeon, theres a singular section where you have to use Chloe's ability in a unique way. But after that is already the final boss, so its too little too late.I feel this game has so much potential! With just a couple tweaks and fixes it could be great! But right now it was kind of a bad experience, where the only thing keeping me going were the charming characters with mediocre dialogue.I'll end this review with a question: Has this game ever been playtested?In just my singular playthrough i found so many glitches, and the entire balancing of enemy and player strength was completely off. I feel like this could have been easily fixed if the devs asked some friends or family members to play through the entire game and tell them about issues they had.I hope with feedback from the community, that maybe there will be a patch or something that tweaks numbers and fixes most of these issues. For now though, i would not recommend buying born of bread.

_childDocuments_.review: After reading some reviews I started the game on the higher difficulty. Note: you are not able to change the difficulty midgame. You have to start over.The higher difficulty changes health of enemies and how many there are in one battle. That the main problem I encountered: often the battles would boil down to the same pattern of attacking with Loaf and defending with your partner. That got boring very fast.There is basically no incentive to use your special attack. You just don't need to because most of the time you have an attack which can finish of the enemies much faster.The setting, music, art and characters are really engaging but the gameplay loop is not.

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended MOSTLY because I personally enjoyed the game.I played 100% blind (no guides or info from searching) on Hard Mode, so anything that I could say might not be an issue on Normal. As of writing, I have yet to replay the game (except for the die from rat in the kitchen achievement). My only experience on Paper-Mario like games is only Thousand Year Door (GameCube). Loved the art-style and writing/plot, think my favorite character is Axel. : ) Loved exploring every little thing for the lizards and treasure, though most weapons were almost/completely useless (Meteorite Dagger). The buddy system was kind of bad, though. Personally didn't like the lack of skills the buddy characters can have, mostly being extremely underwhelming or detriment when used. Loaf always seem to be at a disadvantage if the Buddy never defends.- If Loaf defends, enemies will still attack after the Buddy does any move. - If Buddy gets swapped with Loaf at the start of battle, enemies will attack after the Buddy and it's back to normal turn-phase.- If swapping from Loaf to Buddy during battle, Loaf's turn is skipped. (I can see niche uses but not enough)- If Buddy attacks, Loaf gets punished from the damage.This was especially bad during the tournament area, where I encountered the Drums and Bells enemies doing a little too much damage despite blocking with Loaf. The only way to realistically get passed them is using the Fish Hammer (the only """good""" weapon I had at the time that could deal with the enemies, doing only 2 damage versus them IF hitting perfectly. With the bells having 10 health each, that was just 5 turns wasted. Loaf and Yagi was always at Defend duty just to get back some Will Points for me to do any damage without Loaf getting hurt. At the off-chance of being too low, Defend-ing was essentially the only option to allow me to use Loaf's only "healing" move through Reserve Points. Reserve Points and Skills are probably one of the most useless thing in the game, I never ever had to use it and only upgraded it once or twice to use the skills Papa Baker given to test it. It sucks that it has barely any uses or the fact that Buddies cannot use or have any Special moves. Annoying bugs that happened extremely often:- Inventory is uninteractable (ex: can't change equipment) until a screen transition happened- Some areas when the camera move won't load / wrong camera position - Cursor won't disappear when trying to cancel out using an item on a character- Softlocked during a fight after hitting an enemy that's still alive after being at 0 healthThe only bug I found funny was Chloe stealing all of Yagi's stat bonuses, making Yagi extremely useless for the later half of the game (5 DEF 60HP+ Chloe vs 0 DEF 35 HP Yagi). Had to fix the save so I can actually use Yagi. 8/10, I can excuse the glaring issues imo.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a tough one. Not tough enough to put a negative review, but the positive one comes with some severe caveats.First, it runs perfectly on the Deck, I got no problem on that side.As some people stated, it has some bugs, but I didn't get as much as reviews say here. It may be because of updates, it may be because of luck, but it was smooth sailing on that side of things.One thing that reviews don't really speak about and I got problems with is the camera. Damn is it bad. You can't see where you're going, so you fall, or you bump into enemies. Which turns into combat (without the initial free hit), which is mostly useless since the game is pretty easy, you don't really need to level up. Sure, you can flee, but you're wasting time at this point. Anyway, this would not be a problem if combat was really fun, but it's just kind of okay. Apart from enemy resistance, there is not a lot of strategy to be had here. Which would be fine, since it takes from Paper Mario, but it just got boring after a while. I was up for some cute and easy game but it takes so long to get to the interesting bits. If the game was half as long, I think I would have liked it more. More concise.At the end of the day, if you're looking for that Paper Mario itch, I would recommend Bug Tales more. If you've played that already... I Guess Born of Bread is an option? But wait for a sale, and if you're not liking what you see after a couple hours, be aware that it does not really improve upon the recipe.

_childDocuments_.review: So far I've been playing for 8 hours on release day (Thank god my college break began same day as this release) and I have to say the game is astounding.All the characters are full of personality, there are sidequests and worldbuilding aplenty (which you'd expect from this sort of game honestly, but it's still a plus to see it done so well), the amount of gamebreaking bugs I've ran into are 0, the amount of annoying bugs I've ran into are 1 (which doesn't effect gameplay in any majorly annoying way and it's already on their radar to fix), and the amount of nitpicks I have are incredibly minimal which is greatly surprising to me given the amount of depth in this game already.If you like Paper Mario or Bug Fables you will love this game.
