_childDocuments_.review: It greatly pains me not being able to recommend this game since it's a game I have had on my radar for quite a time and being very inspired by one of my favorites games (Paper Mario) made me very hyped for this game.Addressing the good first, the game is gorgeous, the art direction, the visuals, the mesh between the 2D characters and the 3D environments is fantastic. Areas are very well designed, with lot of details and nooks to explore, really I can't think of anything negative to say about it.The characters are charming and dialogues are pretty good. It has a very good kind of humor on tone of what you would expect from a game like this, there's a strong emphasis with puns and word play which I particularly love.Now, while personally I don't really look for difficulty in games I do get disinterested when games are way too easy and this is the case for Born of Bread normal difficulty mode. So I was very happy to hear a hard mode was added in a post-release patch.From what I can see Hard mode does what you would expect, enemies have more HP and damage, have additional resistances and battles tend to have more enemies, which is all good on paper. The one issue I believe ruins Hard mode was bumping the defense stat of every enemy in the game by one. With this change you struggle with every enemy in the game, making every battle encounter having the difficulty of a mini boss or a boss both in length and in difficulty. The issue is even more notorious when there are attacks that are completely worthless in Hard mode such as the third special attack "Whisk"  which deals 1 damage multiple time, but since the lowest defense of all enemies is 1 the attack do 0 damage.This is aggravated by the Battle System. I previously searched the discussion forum looking if these were bugs or actual features, and while I did find a post where the publisher claimed it was a bug, it was reported a year ago and it seems it hasn't been changed so I assume it is in fact, not a bug but a feature.My issues with the Battle System is that it goes its way to be very unintuitive, with weird rules regarding actions and turn orders that really do not make any sense. (This applies regardless of difficulties)In combat you first take action with the protagonist Loaf, then your partner, which is fine. When it gets weird is when there's an option to swap between Loaf and the partner but what this really does is just skip Loaf turn, after the partner's action, Loaf goes back to be in front and its the enemy turn, making swapping useless. The only way to have your partner receive attacks instead of Loaf is by using Defense, which by doing perfect timings you mitigate all damage, the thing is that Defense is only useful for the partner; defending with Loaf will make the enemies attack you before your partner's turn, effectively granting them an additional turn. Since defending with Loaf is useless, the partner alone is relegated to defense. While of course you can instead attack with the partner and receive damage, the partner should always defend in Hard Mode as otherwise Loaf will quickly be defeated by the increase in damage and number of the enemies.This in the end makes every battles take so much time; the additional defense point being the biggest aggressor. Battling quickly becomes frustrating as each enemy encounter is a long battle where you just hit the enemy with Loaf and defend with whatever partner you have. It is ironic though that bosses feel easier than normal enemy encounters since a boss would do 6 damage on his turn, while a normal battle you have four enemies doing 4 damage each (some enemies can attack twice too). I assume this is a much lesser issue in Normal mode, but since difficulty cannot be changed mid-game, I do not know.I will continue playing as I really like everything else about the game, but battling is slowly being a frustration point that's hard to ignore. I am not sure if developers are still working on this game (I know they're developing a new game at least). I would be more than happy to change this review to a positive if the battle system issues are addressed in some way.

_childDocuments_.review: Where do I even begin? So much to say, but I will try my best to keep it as brief as I can.I've been involved with Born of Bread since the Standalone Demo, and ever since then, I've been hooked. The characters, the music, the story, (although by that time it was it's own thing and was self-contained) just...everything.First and foremost, this is a Paper Mario inspired game like Bug Fables: The Everlasting Sapling, The Outbound Ghost, the upcoming game Escape From Ever After... This is most definitely a game that fits in the Paper-Verse community that has filled the void for the original Paper Mario formula. If that's the kind of game that you like, Born of Bread will fill that void and MORE in my opinion.In the game, you'll be able to level-up the main Character Loaf to increase Health Points, Will Points, (Flower Points like in the original Paper Mario games) & Resolve Points which allow you to use Special Moves and are back-up Will Points if you want to use them in that way also. As a Part 2 to your level-up, you'll also be able to increase your Backpack size which allows you to equip more weapons like in Resident Evil for example, along with your Boon capacity, with allows you to equip more Boons. Boons are like Badges in Paper Mario/Gear from other RPG's that add other abilities to your character.Each Chapter in the game gives you a Partner, (in this game these characters are referred to as buddies) and all of them have their own Skill Trees to unlock in order to customize their movesets.With a great story, great characters, an amazing soundtrack and being able to customize your build to how you want it, this is certainly an incredible experience. Not just because it's a great Paper Mario like game, but it also standing on it's own. Not just derivative, but also having it's own identity. Make sure you check this one out. It's the Yeast you could do. :)

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed the game, despite some of the jank that I experienced, which hopefully will be fixed with patches.Music, characters and visuals are all top-notch! Overworld exploration is really streamlined, especially with the speed-increasing upgrades you get later. Combat is very simplistic, but serviceable. I would've hoped more variety on the action commands on attacks (there's, like, only 4 or 5 variations, not counting the "Special Moves"), and for enemies to have a bigger variety of attacks to choose from, especially bosses.I would recommend if you want something charming and cute to play, and don't mind the more-or-less mindless combat! Heads up: it's on the easier side, especially if you've played the two first Paper Mario games or Bug Fables.Hoping for a sequel, and if that ever happens, for it to improve on what this game already does!

_childDocuments_.review: Born of Bread is a beautiful game that builds upon the Paper Mario style gameplay. Everything from the story, artwork, music, and gameplay are great to form an amazing package. All the little subsystems like the tetris backpack management, badge system, battle livestreaming, and unique level up system tie everything together and add a lot of flair to the game. _childDocuments_.review: Born of Bread, a whimsical RPG adventure available on Steam, introduces players to Loaf, an unlikely hero who is a flour golem with a perpetual childlike wonder. Set against the backdrop of havoc caused by beings from another age, the game weaves a story thousands of years in the making.The 2.5D adventure unfolds in a vibrant world brimming with mysteries. As players guide Loaf and his quirky buddies, they face off against menacing baddies through a turn-based combat system infused with a unique interactive twist. The game challenges players' reflexes, adding a layer of engagement to the traditional turn-based mechanics.In terms of presentation, Born of Bread stands out with its clear and colorful graphics, contributing to the whimsical atmosphere. The characters, each possessing odd abilities and distinct personalities, bring humour and joy to the narrative. The game is filled with delightful bread puns and a fun sense of humor, creating a charming experience.However, the 2.5D graphics pose challenges as characters and environmental elements may obstruct the main character, impacting visibility. Skipping dialogue could lead to missing crucial information for progression, emphasizing the importance of paying close attention. The in-game menu system, designed to be navigated with a mouse, doesn't work well with a gamepad and proves overly complicated, detracting from the overall user experience.Despite its enjoyable style reminiscent of the original Paper Mario, Born of Bread lacks originality, and the turn-based combat may feel tedious for players who prefer real-time fights. The inclusion of numerous pop culture references adds an extra layer of entertainment, complemented by a well-crafted in-game soundtrack.In conclusion, Born of Bread offers a cute and enjoyable experience with room for improvement. The game's strengths lie in its vibrant graphics, engaging characters, and a delightful blend of humour and pop culture references. However, issues with the 2.5D graphics and an overcomplicated menu system detract from the overall experience. While the turn-based combat may not resonate with all players, Born of Bread is still worth exploring for those seeking a lighthearted adventure.Born of Bread on PC (Steam) has the potential for growth and refinement, and with some adjustments, it could reach greater heights.Score: 7 out of 10Out on PC, Switch, PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series S/X.

_childDocuments_.review: This game disappointed me the longer I play, I haven't even beat it, and I'm dreading to play more of this boring game.The game has some good steps forwards to an extent, easy to follow plot, brief introductions, and establishes everything you need to know in the first hour or two, which starts leading to the issues. The fact that I have basically seen all the good of the game within the first hour or two, and all it can do, is really poor in my opinion(At the time I am about 4.8 hours, I will probably beat it because I don't want to waste money, and it's something to do.) This game is obviously inspired of paper mario games, but the only thing it took from it was the basics, and everything new/every "twist" they do is incredibly shallow. Let's start with the battles, which are in the same vain but so many issues. Your combat is turn based and all the enemies line up in a row from front to back, and all moves attack either front, any, or all, There seems to be no air enemies, no enemies with spikes/fire/cold/electricty, and the enemies feel all the same, with basicaly the same timing for attacks, and despite fighting what looks like a variety, they don't feel different at all, EVEN the bosses I have fought have next to nothing that makes them feel dangerous or unique, other than dealing more damage, or having a special attack or two. The same goes for your attacks, all the attack minigames to hit, are the same and give no real difference, we will compare to the inspiration, Paper mario N64. In paper mario mario had a simple jump command which was timing based, just like your first partner(didn't need a wheel or bars, just simple timing, that CHANGED with the size or shape of the enemy, and where they where on the battle) Kooper had a command similar to the hammer, a hold the stick and wait, but they where your first members, bombete had a hold and wait, parakary was timming based like marios and goombarios, but with a delay, bow was slaming the stick lefty repeadetley. Now back to BoB, Which your main character and first two partners, have the SAME basic attack, does the same damage, and hits the same enemies the same way, just dressed different. The special attacks also feel very bland with "oh this one hits all, but with this element(will get to that later) or causes various statuses(with low percentages) that don't really do much. Overall the combat feels like a chore, and you just choose whats strong and beat the battles. Also the little cheer system they introduce early on, which gives you an audience, and if you do well, you get more WP, and they want you to do special missions RARELY which are 70% of the time(Use an item you don't need to) which just makes the system feel useless.To move on to the next section, levelling, which is also bad, I have played this game up to level 10, and I have not felt a need to level anything other than your WP, and occasionly the RP(even thought I used RP skills twice) and sure you can increase your backpack size every 3 levels, or your badge ammount to equip every 2 levels(you have to stamp them every level, twice for badge, 3 times for backpack). Hp feels like what you have is enough, I have never taken more than 15 or so damage in a fight, and your partner NEVER gets hit even though they have 15 hp( I think one mini boss attacked everyone, but I blocked it and negated the damage)and you start with 20.Traversal, It just feels like the maps are alot of padding and with the camera being way to close, it SUCKS going towards the camera( MOST of the damage I have taken is from cliffs/ water I can't see) The puzzles are okay to bland, and the platforming feels slippery. You feel very slow going through area's, even with a dash, or you feel like you blaze through an area, cause Uh oh, it's tiny. and I know all your partners traversal abilties, cause it's obvious by the end of the first area, you get a character that can dig dirt mounts, which is just a glorfied "get rid of obstacle" and is bland and slow, the 2nd member is "This intangible thing is now tangible" and is ripped straight from Hat in time. the 3rd I presume is just burns things, and if there is a last, I don't care to learn. It doesn't help with the sidequests that require you to return to earlier area's for mudane things, so they all feel just bad.Items, They are all bad and half of them are the SAME item with no difference. You start with only 5 item slots, and go to 10 within the first 2 hours, There doesn't seem to be any use for them other than eatting, you can't even sell or STORE any(the only saving grace with the constant items, is they stay on the ground for seemingly forever till you leave the screen) Like I ran into like 5 different items that heal 3 rp, and they are all equaly useless. In other games if an item healed the same ammount, they usualy either had an additional bonus, was a cheaper version, or usualy, you could COMBINE them to do different things, which a game with a strong baking theme, I am suprised 4 hours in, and not one way to combine/ cook items.Designs, The npcs are incredibly lazy and look and feel all the same, like alot are just This model with different hair or accessory, but looks like the bare minimum was done to make them different, like it was just pasted onto their model with barely any care. The unique ones look fine, and the main characters have decent animations, but everyone else has the most simple animations that are 2 frame walk cycles. The backgrounds and area's are okay, they look relatively nice, but SO many invisible walls that are inconsistent.Backpack/ Skill system. When I saw the way you equip your main character with new abilties, I was intrested, but it's just putting blocks into a backpack, and organizing so they all fit, there is no depth to the system at all. Like an example I will use of one that is similar, Megaman Battle Network 6, It had a system for megaman to upgrade his stats by putting these coloured blocks into a grid, each powerup had a colour, brick style(bricked or non) and intresting shapes, generaly the stronger the powerup, the blocks where larger/more restirictive/odd shapes. You can increase the total size to make fitting in more blocks easier, but you had rules to follow, or you got constraints/debuffs. You had to juggle the pieces all fiting and ordered right, and not causing errors, or you could throw caution to the wind, and cram as much power as possible with little care, and have some big debuffs/ ailments to deal with. The system in BoB could of been more interesting, like certain elemental pieces next to other boosted/decreased the effect, or matching like pieces boosted power, but no, it's just bland. The skill system for your partners is equally bad. You collect lizards(or beating bosses/minibosses) and every two you give to a certain npc, you get 1 skill point(for ALL members, they share the points, so you have to focus on some to get their skills) and you have 4 tiers of skills, basic, advanced, expert and Final(I assume purchasing all the partners skills unlocks it) and you can swap out of 3 in each tier(except final) of what is in that slot, so you can only have 4 skills on each partner at a time(buying other skills is just for different choices) and they feel all bland, it's just best to buy the ones that hit the hard, and buy others if you have nothing better to do with the points.Elemental System, Gonna make this quick, it just feels overly complicated, but also 100% ignoreable, like there is like 7-8 elements, and they don't feel necessary up to so far.Overall, The game fails to take anything good from it's inspirations, and any twist or "interesting" thing they do is i shallow, the game isn't actively bad, it's 100% playable and simple to play and follow, but it's worse than bad games, cause it's SO boring, it looks like this game didn't only need more time in the oven, but a better Baker, cause it had all the ingredients to be good.

_childDocuments_.review: I've enjoyed this game but was left feeling meh about it both while playing and beating it. Born of Bread absolutely nails it in terms of both music and visuals. It also has lots of charm in its characters and dialogue. But that's sadly where my praising ends.- As mentioned the writing itself is very charming and filled with many many puns.- The story itself however is very simple and predictable. Characters goals and motives felt very one note. It's just lacking that main grip a RPG needs that makes the player really connect with it.- All the party members themselves also feel underdeveloped and their reasons for joining and sticking around felt unnatural and forced.- The combat is, fine I suppose. It's pretty standard paper mario combat without adding anything too substantial.- I find it charming they replaced Paper Mario TTYD's stage and audience system with a live broadcast and chat. But the game doesn't really do much with it and if it does, it's not well explained.- There's an unnecessarily complex and poorly explained elemental type system that feels arbitrary. There's a boon you get near the start of the game that displays enemies strengths and weaknesses. There's no reason to unequip these two so what's the point of having them?- Attack mini games and enemy attacks feel too similar and get repeated a lot. Because of the elemental type system both your attack types and enemy types hardly vary from each other. Making things feel very simple and plain.- Various oddities like rotating during combat consumes a turn. Enemies basically never attacking party members even though there's tons of boons to boost their HP. Etc.- And my biggest criticism about the combat. It's . I never once felt challenged even during the final boss fight.- Platforming really isn't ideal for this game despite its many efforts.- Maps themselves are too big. This game easily could've been downscaled. Big open areas with nothing much going on. (Especially in the main castle area.) Linear areas feel like a chore to traverse on repeated trips. Lots of areas feel too maze like and aren't well connected. (Especially with the entirety of chapter 3.)- Too many instances where the player runs at the camera. There's a reason in paper mario that the level design is heavily based on around walking left and right. Walking into the camera is a massive blind spot and there was countless times I've walked into enemies or off ledges because I can't see where I'm going.- The warioland like stage hazard abilities are underused. I remember the first demo being littered with them, giving a good sense of platforming and exploration but in the final game there's only 3 and they're hardly used.- Menu navigation is a nightmare. The main pause menu has so many tabs and pages to flip through you'll find yourself spamming triggers until you find where you wanted to go. (Also side note the pause menu DOESN'T PAUSE THE GAME.)- A lot of the quests (including main story) revolve around you running back and forth between areas and it gets stale very quickly.- During my first playthrough I'd encountered tons of soft-locking bugs and very easy to replicate sequence skips.

_childDocuments_.review: Simply put, I enjoyed this game a lot and I would certainly recommend buying it. However, it unfortunately didn't live up to some of my expectations. If you're looking for Bug Fables but it's bread instead of bugs, that's not really what this game is. Based on my save file's time it took me about 16 hours to beat this game. I did a lot of sidequests during that time as well, I'd estimate you could probably finish the entire game in around 8-10 hours if you only did the main quest (which I would personally consider to be kind of short). As of writing this review my save file's time is about 23 hours. I've completed all sidequests and found most optional collectibles. I would rate Born of Bread a 7/10. A really good game, even great at parts, but not quite what I was hoping for from a Paper Mario spiritual successor.That said, I'd like to give a bit more of a long-winded summary of my thoughts on this game. I'll try to avoid spoilers as much as possible, but my definition of spoilers might be different from yours, so consider yourself warned.Graphics & Music:The graphics and music are great. Nothing more to say about it.Writing & Story:I enjoyed the writing a lot. Most NPCs can be talked to multiple times for new dialogue, and I tried to talk to everyone I could. It's also quite funny from time to time, with frequent puns and witty remarks. I had a few good chuckles, and the humor never goes overboard in my opinion.The partners have a lot of personality. Each partner has a quest that rounds out his/her character arc, which is great. Unfortunately the partners don't interact with each other much outside of main story cutscenes. The overarching plot was fine, but nothing special. It's enough to keep the game moving, but sticks to the usual "find the magical mcguffins" trope pretty much all the way.The isolated plots for each of the chapters (or "parts" as I believe they are called in this game) are much better for the most part. I was pretty invested in the stories of the first several chapters, but the last ones kinda fell off for me as the overarching plot took over.Battles:Combat in this game is very, very easy in my opinion. I was constantly overflowing with items (which you can't store or sell, by the way), and the only times I got to low HP were because I was needlessly trying to save items. The audience and defending mechanics basically provide infinite Will Points (the equivalent of Flower Points from Paper Mario or Teamwork Points from Bug Fables), which is about as broken for game balance as it sounds. There are no difficulty options either. This is one of my main sources of disappointment with this game.The boon system is far simpler than badges in Paper Mario or medals in Bug Fables, which was also disappointing to me. All boons take up exactly one slot, with a max of just 8 slots. Increasing boon slots is separate from increasing HP and WP (and RP, which is unique to this game). I do like the weapon/backpack system quite a bit, or at least I like it more than the boon system.Exploration:The map is (with very few exceptions) entirely traversable on foot, rather than connected by magic pipes or whatever, which I love. Each area is unique, and I enjoyed exploring almost all of them. Overworld platforming in this game is pretty good for the most part. I was able to manage just fine with the limited directions offered by the WASD keys. I hope you don't get tired of battling enemies though, because they can be really tricky to avoid and there's no way to auto-defeat weak enemies. Controls:I played this game with keyboard and mouse controls because I don't own a controller. It feels to me like keyboard controls were an afterthought, because they use far too many buttons and overall just feel awkward. (EDIT: since writing this review, the keyboard control scheme has been updated to no longer require the mouse. I haven't played since then, but with that change the controls are probably fine now.)Everything Else:Many optional collectibles are hidden in rather devious spots. That would be fine with me, it can be really satisfying to find well hidden secrets on your own, if it weren't for the fact that there is no in-game hint system for locating missing collectibles. This was another major disappointment for me. I resorted to using a guide for a bunch of stuff at the end. 100%ing this game sucks, assuming you're using all Steam achievements as the guideline (there is no in-game completion tracker). I would personally stick with just beating the game and doing any optional stuff you find along the way, because I guarantee you aren't 100%ing this game without a guide.There's no postgame. If you reload your save after beating the game you get sent back to before you entered the final dungeon. This was also pretty disappointing to me, and I'm not really sure why it is this way.There are almost no tutorials, optional or not. It's a simple enough game that it mostly gets away with it, but there were a few parts where the lack of explanation frustrated me, including the following:1. There is no explanation for swapping partners, in or out of battle (swapping partners is required to beat the game)2. Partner skill trees are never explained (easy to figure out, but the explanation would still be appreciated)3. Boon and Backpack upgrades are not explained (also easy to figure out, but an explanation would have been appreciated)4. Loaf's first special is poorly explained5. Poor description for statuses like "Rage" (which is just defense down), and the status with the snail icon Lastly, this game is pretty buggy. I bought and started playing basically on release, so if you're reading this months or years from now you can probably ignore this paragraph. The devs have already patched several bugs, and I'm sure they're working hard on more bugfixes. In any case, I experienced a concerning amount of minor bugs throughout my playthrough.  Here's a list of what I remember (I'll be working on officially reporting as many of these as I can in the next few weeks if they haven't been reported already):1. Clipping under water by encountering an enemy as I fell in (I subsequently softlocked myself by walking off the edge of the map's collision and falling out of bounds) EDIT: this has been fixed, according to patch notes.2. Glitched blank battle cards sometimes appeared when trying to change the selected card3. Couldn't complete a sidequest in chapter 4 for a while because talking to the quest giver after completing all steps of the quest restarted the quest from the beginning. EDIT: This might be fixed now, not entirely sure4. Some sound effects stop playing when the game has been running for several hours5. Butterfly trees often just don't work on my brother's save file/computer (they work fine on mine)6. I lost a unique item by accidentally encountering an enemy while it was on the ground. EDIT: this has been fixed, according to patch notes.7. Battle options for swapping turn order and swapping partner remain in overworld if battle is won during the enemy's turn. Exiting another battle normally makes them go away. Attempting to use the options in the overworld can mess up the camera, but voiding out fixes it.

_childDocuments_.review: Born of Bread is a wonderful game that wears it's inspirations proudly on it's sleeve. For those who enjoy gameplay like the original Paper Mario Series and Bug Fables I would recommend this game since it fits almost perfectly in with the others. I am apprehensive about saying it fits with them due to what feels like the lack of polish the game has at nearly every turn. I did not experience any game breaking bugs in my play-through however I did find a significant amount of minor bugs/unintended interactions that ruined future companion reveals, removed all textures from a room, and made some treasure inaccessible intill a area reload.TL;DR If you want a paper mario experience and don't care about a couple bugs, then it's a good find.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't let what everyone else is saying about the bugs and the comparison to their fables sway you from trying this one out. I, much like many other fans of the genre, have played and loved Paper Mario and Bug Fables. This game takes a lot of inspo from both and it really shows.Pros:Art - both 2D and 3D, everything and everywhere in the game is beautifulMusic - SO MANY head bobber tracksCharm - the characters/villains and their dialogue and animations are super cuteCons:Difficulty - I played the game on HARD mode and the pacing was off. I still recommend playing it on this difficulty, although the midgame is definitely tougher than the late game IMO. If you're not careful, an ambush can take 80% of your health even with timed blocks depending on how many enemies populate the battle. In the late game, for some reason, the battles are constrained to populating only a single enemy and in this game, more enemies mean tougher fights.Combat - not the worst but definitely feels shallow compared to the games this one gets compared to. The badge system has some repetitive and uninspired design that can be better explored. Additionally, the input prompts are very similar to one another, even between characters. You will find yourself doing the same timing events between Loaf's many weapons, and his companions different moves. Speaking of, the companion's have their own skill trees but often don't feel very useful or impactful. In the harder difficulty, the "specials" hardly ever feel relevant. The defend mechanic can sometimes trivialize certain encounters, while also giving almost no incentive to block with Loaf but rather the companions only. The switch mechanics take up a turn and deciding who goes first almost feels negligible due to enemies attacking Loaf by default. IT CAN USE SOME POLISH BUT IT DOES NOT MAKE THIS GAME UNPLAYABLE, just some questionable design choices.Overall I had a great time playing through the story of this game. Their are still some bugs in the game but I never encountered anything that set me back or broke the game. Already the team behind it's development are hard at work patching these MINOR issues. The game is not the most challenging but that meshes well with the lighthearted nature of the game's narrative. Give this game a chance!

I guess you could say it was . . . UNDERBAKED!The fact that the devs have already added a feature to switch partners with the push of a button (THANK YOU!) and a hard mode tells me that they care about their game and want it to be the best it can be. _childDocuments_.review: Enjoyable Paper Mario like. It sways on the easy side, but it is enjoyable nonetheless. feels unique and interesting, although it could expand a bit more on the lore side of things sometimes. The game does a good try to have a vast explorable world. is really good, it has a different battle theme for each region, which makes the battles feel fresh through their washed-up mechanics. are fun since there is variety in moves and power, but you always end up using the strongest attacks possible instead of using strategy. Your partners suffer from this, since you'll always want to have the strongest ally out when battling. All enemies have the same type of attacks: either a dash, a projectile or a standing attack, so blocking always feels the same and is not rewarding. Enemies in general also deal very little damage and have low health, so bosses are a breeze. I haven't found a single enemy that attacks your partners, so having the main character in second position keeps him always safe from damage. are fun and charismatic. It's a shame your partners don't have much character growth besides a simple quest that not always explores the character's desires and aspirations, or does it poorly. Also there's A LOT of NPCs that don't offer anything when talking to them, not even a snarky line. And the game even encourages talking to them multiple times because they have 2 or 3 different lines, but it's a waste of time 90% of the time. NOBODY will give you anything besides a couple lines of dialogue and if they have a quest for you they will have an icon on top of their heads indicating so, so there's no purpose talking to them. is original and intertwines two different well written storylines. The script could use some polish, since trouble doesn't seem to go further than a couple lines of dialogue, a battle and a couple more lines of dialogue. There are few times where your actions seemed to have consequences in the world and everything else feels like you just go from A to B to advance the plot with no surprise or twist behind what you are doing. it is an enjoyable game where you can bury tens of hours if you like exploring every nook and cranny. Bug Fables is superior in everything this game does wrong, but it feels more like Paper Mario than Bug Fables does. With a little bit more polish this could have been on par with Bug Fables in terms of quality. It has good ideas and separates itself from being a Paper Mario clone, but lacks polish both in terms of mechanics and script. But it's a really good first try of a game from the developers. I have faith that they'll provide us with bigger and better games in the years to come.

_childDocuments_.review: It's...well, it's a good game. To start, I am having a blast playing this game. The art is very cute and the world we travel through is pretty and well crafted and aesthetically pleasing.  The humour is adorable and the characters are incredibly charming.  I very much recommend this game to buy.  BUT there are some things I would watch out for.I play via controller.  I think it plays better with a controller.  The battle sequences- I'm at just under 7 hours in, and I am not sure if the battle gets better or adjusts.  As of now as far as I've played, it is turned (which I love), but the cards become a bit repetitive, so not real brain power there. You pick a card, you hit or defend or use an item or a special move.  All that is fine, but it's missing that kind of skill-build that you would find in a turn based combat.  A part of me kinda wishes they just took the trading card idea and went all in to a deck builder. Also there doesn't seem to be a good battle balance in the game.  Like, I don't think this game should be super souls-like hard ever.  But the enemies and the battle play just seem too too easy, and the bosses I fought aren't like tactics kinda of bosses.  One was just repetitive until I finally whittled down its health which was slow as sin.  But I know there is more to come so I will edit if that changes.Sometimes the 2.5d nature of the terrain can be a bit difficult to navigate, but personally I don't think it's too distracting. Just takes a bit of getting used to.I did find that the quests were sometimes hard to figure out a direction to find it so I wander a bit to find it.  It you have patience to wander, that should be fine.So this is a game I do recommend. It's cute, it is fun, it has loads of charm. It has flaws to consider, but overall, a playable game.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the closest to a traditional Paper Mario game we've gotten so far. I've played all of the Paper Mario games plus Bug Fables, and I've seen a couple other heavily inspired games come out since, and I think this one is the most proud of its inspiration, and borrows the most ideas from The Thousand Year Door.That isn't to say there aren't any original ideas, but this feels the closest to what a new Paper Mario with the old formula in 2023 might look like. The graphics are by far the most stunning of any of the clones, and exceeds most of the actual Paper Mario games besides maybe Origami King. The dialogue is on point and consistently charming and funny. The music has several bangers already just 2 chapters into the game. The battle system is a bit basic, but still engaging enough to stay entertaining (And the stream live chat system to replace TTYD's audience mechanic is EXTREMELY clever. I almost always leave the chat on). The partner upgrades seem much more in depth than any game before it as well, having full skill trees rather than basic upgrades.Overall, very impressed. This game deserves a lot more attention. If you're a fan of the old Paper Mario and/or played and enjoyed Bug Fables, pick this one up too. It's excellent.

_childDocuments_.review: Born of Bread gets the Paperlike formula right. The world is bright and colorful, the characters are whimsical and wholesome, and the whole audiovisual presentation is warm and inviting. Once you start playing you notice the care that wasa put into its systems. Combat gets enhanced by quick action inputs that have just the right amount of timing to them, and they are varied enough to keep you engaged. Your protagonist Loaf will quickly amass a large arsenal of weaponry, and to ready them up for combat you will have to fit them into his backpack like you're rotating Tetris pieces on a grid. You can customize your experience further by choosing which stats to increase on level up, but also by choosing to expand either your backpack with weapons or your Boon slots. Boons offer a wide variety of helpful passive effects, like increasing the potency of healing items or getting more money from defeated enemies.Loaf isn't the only one who can be customized. All of your party members can have a move on four different tiers, but each tier has three different options to choose from and unlocking all the options within a tier will grant a permanent stat increase to them. To get the skill points to unlock them though, you have to be on the lookout for sleeping salamanders that you need to whack with your ladle. Exploration is greatly rewarded and encouraged not just this way, but with other hidden treasures, worldbuilding lore, and sidequests.95% of my playthrough was before Patch 3.0 and I ran into minor but obvious bugs and some more annoying ones, and I wasn't going to write a review one way or another. But reading through the patchnotes, I see that most (or maybe all) of my complaints have been addressed as well as many other issues I hadn't run into. As such I am confident that anybody picking this game up now or later will have a smooth and pleasant experience.My only remaining gripe is one of expectation. I knew that the game has 5 chapters, and the first four chapters were 3-4 hours on average depending on how much sidequesting I did, and I was expecting chapter 5 to also offer a full dungeon's worth of content. It doesn't. There's one big room, and then the final boss segment. It is generally a good sign of quality when a game leaves you wanting more and you don't want to quit, but here I felt like the game was missing a chapter's worth of content. So new players, be aware that unless more gets added in later updates, there's actually only four chapters and a very quick finale.

_childDocuments_.review: Born of Bread is utterly charming from start to finish. It impressed me how much character it had which allowed it to be more than "just a Paper Mario clone".I did run into a number of random bugs including a quest that would reset every time I tried to hand it in, sound effects stopped working, weird graphical bugs, and sometimes the controls getting funky. Nothing game breaking and all quickly fixed by quitting and reloading (the bugs seemed to happen after long chunks of play? Really weird). That being said I did play it on a Steam Deck so I can't say if it's a core issue with the game or Proton trying its best.Even with these little bugs though, the story, the characters, the engaging combat, the beautiful locations, and the silly side quests were all far too much fun for me to care about some silly little bugs!I rarely complete RPGs due to them demanding too much time, but this one is a perfect length with the whole story and a fair chunk of the side content taking me just shy of 18 hours total to beat. Perfect for people who long for a JRPG but don't have 80 hours to invest in a single game.Honestly one of my favourite games of the last few years. I hope we see more of Loaf and his buddies in the future :)

_childDocuments_.review: I was really looking forward to this game, and I thought the staff behind it used Tiktok and other social media well to hype up the game before release. However, for a game at release, I think it came out of the oven a little half-baked.Things I liked-The art style for this game has a lot of charm-Menus in battle were really easy to maneuverThings I think need work-I don't think the partners got enough time to develop their personalities strongly, especially Chloe and Yagi.-The game felt a bit rushed, pacing-wise, and is very linear without allowing much breathing room. Most of these areas were a straight line.-Quest system is very buggy...sometimes the game won't allow you to complete them until arbitrary points, and some that require the same NPC will easily glitch. Nothing has been game-breaking so far, but it could be handled better.-There are sometimes where the quests don't update with relevant information, and it's difficult to remember where you need to be going. The coffeeshop quest in particular I found by accident.-The menus out of battle felt really clunky. Having to go into a menu to swap between partners got old really fast.-Partner abilities outside of battle felt not signposted enough in their utility. Especially after  a certain point, the currency is just not worth collecting. Also, the platforming with partner abilities feels really klunky.-I liked the integration of skill trees for character moves, but the moves themselves felt not very special. The execution of them felt kinda klunky, and the rock-paper-scissors move types meant that for most of an area, only one party member would be worth using.This game clearly has potential, but I think this bun should have stayed in the oven a bit longer. It feels like DLC may be on the horizon, so I'll keep an eye out for that.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a bit of a lopsided recommend from me. If you're looking for a game that looks and plays like Paper Mario then this does mostly accomplish that. If you're looking for anything aside from 2D guys running around 3D maps and action commands for attacks, you might want to look elsewhere. I ramble for a bit, but the last paragraph is a TL;DR.I'm going to be talking about some aspects of the game, so I'm giving this a spoiler warning out of courtesy, but nothing story-wise is going to be in this first part. I will at some point though, so I'll give that a super spoiler warning when that happens.The game is a bit rough around the edges. Nothing too outright gamebreaking but a bit grating on the nerves. Sometimes sound effect animations would repeat and the only way to get rid of it was to change screens or reload. Transitioning to and from battle is going to be the bulk of your glitches. Sometimes you're still able to use party member's overworld abilities inside combat. Sometimes you'll exit combat and the little "Press A when it's green ring" will pop up out of nowhere.You get items that allow you to recolor your party members a few different ways. Sometimes they stick. Sometimes they don't. Sometimes they'll come undone when you pause the menu. Sometimes you'll change screens and you'll be using a color you don't even have yet.You level up absurdly fast, even if you're genociding everything you see. My inventory was consistently full of items because leveling up full heals you, and I was always leveling up before I even had to consider using an item. There's this cute system in place where foods have different attributes, so some party members will recover more if they eat a food they like, but this is largely unnecessary. Also, devs, if you read this, please let me push B to just instantly drop an item I picked up on accident instead of having to manually select it. And also let me store my golden foods somewhere which took up the bulk of my inventory by the end of the game.Okay, some story stuff now. Spoiler warning part 2.Although... There really isn't much to write home about here. I wasn't expecting the pinnacle of storytelling from this, but the game does not take itself very seriously even when a character is having a Big Moment:tm:. One character's big personal story quest is leaving behind an instrument that belonged to their mom. When you beat the game and talk to them in the big victory lap before the credits, they make it a point to comment that they wish they found it and they had it with them, even though the entire quest revolved around finding it and realizing they didn't actually need it. There's lots of stuff like this scattered throughout the game.As for the rest of the game, you get sent to different locales to find the PLOT ROCKS and get owned each time.The ending was also...Very very anticlimactic. I was a bit surprised when there was one last dialogue box and then the game just cut to the credits. Honestly, the entire ending sequence, final boss and all, was a bit underwhelming.Overall though, the game looks and sounds nice and manages to have some sparks of uniqueness even in relatively tried and true settings. The inside of the whale was probably my favorite area, both design wise and OST wise.TL;DR. If you are looking for a game that is similar to Paper Mario in the most basic sense, this is it. You will run into glitches, but thankfully they're on the "minor annoyance" side of things and not "oh cool I need to redo hours of game" side. If you're on the fence, you should be able to get a good vibe of the game within the two hour refund limit.

_childDocuments_.review: Just play Bug Fables instead this game costs more and has less (and worse) content.Less strategic, less in depth, side quests are WAY worse, combat is mindless, overworld exploration is boring.Music is beautiful, graphics are beautiful, but this game relies on it's beautiful art style, occasionally witty writing and awesome soundtrack way too much, because the actual "game" part of this game is straight up mindless garbage.Again, play Bug Fables instead, if you're looking for a fun turn based RPG based on Paper Mario. Already played Bug Fables? Well do it again, a replay is worth your time more than this game.I waited 4 years for this, and the game was even delayed by 4 months, and the end product was complete dogwater. The final chapter is literally 3 rooms long, and the final chapter enemies have 10HP, how did they mess up this badly.No shade to the developers personally, they're incredible and lovely people, but this is a criticism of the game, not the developers, and the game is not worth your time, or money.Also, some of the achievements are straight up broken. I had to SAM in Physiologus and Well-Traveled because they straight up can't trigger. Also a lot of times the game world straight up unloads right in front of you, particularly in chapter 3 inside the manor.This game is not finished. Wait a few months/years for balance changes, bug fixes, and overall improvements, but I feel like no matter how much they improve, they can't change that at it's core, this is a shallow and boring experience, that doesn't live up to it's inspiration, or it's competition.Not reccomended.Edit: It took them half a year to finally patch the game to be in a state where it's completable without cheats. That's actually really pathetic. I feel like if your game isn't even COMPLETABLE for HALF A YEAR it should NOT have been sold TO BEGIN WITH.I really hope this dev team learns from this and actually properly playtests their game in the future to ensure that they are at the very least complatable by the playerbase. The fact that it took half a year for even a single person to get the platinum trophy on console, and for the game to be 100%'able without the use of steam achievement manager is genuinely so depressing,

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to love Born of Bread. I feel terrible for giving an indie a poor review, but I just wasn't having fun playing it the more I went on.Below are my gripes but bear in mind that this is just one perspective from a jaded nobody with a massive backlog.----------------------- Runs on Steam Deck, though a 1280x800 resolution would have been nice.- Really cute art style, I like the way characters  jostle around when they talk.- There are bread facts on the loading screen!- On Steam Deck the loading times were short.- Music is excellent, very jovial and thematic. It sticks in your head and is a joy to listen to.- I personally didn't encounter any game breaking bugs or soft locks.- The battle system has a neat feature. The dragon Dub streams your fight to viewers and they leave comments Twitch style. Viewers can have requests and fulfilling them gets you extra WP.- If you like references to other media or games:  and I bet there's more I missed. ----------------------Skip over if irrelevant to you but if you're a disabled gamer you might want to consider a few things:- There are accessibility option to increase contrast, but nothing to adjust timings of attacks etc. They can be difficult if you have dyspraxia or mobility issues. There is a visual cue item that flashes when it's time to defend called Attack Sight that you get by - There's no auto sprint button, you need to press and hold a button to sprint.- Some actions like fleeing require button mashing. If QTEs are essential, an option to press and hold instead of button mashing for those actions would be a better accessibility feature.- At least two of Loaf's attacks that I found require you to move the left joystick back and forth very quickly. Not great for your controller or gamers with mobility issues.(In no particular order)----------------------- Pressing A to skip text means possibly skipping options in dialogue. I'd prefer an instant text option with a pause before choices in dialogue.- No auto save.- You have to scroll through the entire menu almost to get to quests or other sections.- The game keeps changing my party member after cutscenes when I have it set to Lint.- Born of Bread doesn't indicate when something is important or useful to interact with. I briefly got stuck in  but the game doesn't indicate this matters.Another example, there's this press thing in the mines that squishes Loaf into a smaller version. This lets him sneak under gaps and float over small distances. The first press mechanism I found didn't work. It was only when I found another press thing and tried it again that I realised it could do this. The press not working could be a glitch, but the game didn't tell me that it could be useful.- It can be unclear what type of item you've picked up until you check your inventory. E.g. I encountered the sleeping lizards before the game told me what they were. There's also no clear indicator of quest rewards. An NPC might say 'I'm giving you this' but if they don't, you'll have to check your inventory to see what the reward was.- No fast travel intially. This was really annoying and drags the pace down because you have to move around between areas so often. I found fast travel several hours in (I played very slowly) in - Unless I've missed something here, the map is useless. I can't view the different map segments within an area, only a big map of the large region I'm in. It can sometimes be tricky to figure out where you need to go. You need to remember which area links to which big region.- Inventory management is a pain, your item bag can only hold five items. As you get items battling enemies or finding them in the environment, you have to juggle them and choose which items to keep. Almost 8 hours in and I haven't found a way to increase the item bag size. It's pointless anyway because you can drop something to eat another item then pick up the item you dropped, because they don't disappear.- If you're moving in a particular direction and can't see what's coming up, you can fall into water or off ledges easily. It's especially funny when it happens to your party member, but they just reappear next to you with no damage. (You can disable environmental damage in the main menu for Loaf too.)- It's tricky for Loaf to land a hit on enemies before they attack you. As you need to get close to them to attack, this often means they get the jump on you first instead. If an enemy attacks you first, all of the enemies attack you. Whereas if you attack them first, only Loaf attacks once.- NPCs have a little scribble above their heads when they have a quest for you. But I found a quest giving NPC with no scribble.  gives you a quest to - Attacks that required specific button prompts didn't match up to my Switch style controller and there were no in game menu options to change it. These prompts worked fine on Steam Deck controls.- In some fights it doesn't seem to let you change your party member, but the game doesn't tell you this. So you can waste a turn trying to change characters and it'll just switch turns instead.----------------------Born of Bread started out strong with oodles of whimsy and cuteness but the more I played the more bored and frustrated I got. If you're desperate for a Paper Mario style game and don't mind the issues mentioned, get Born of Bread. If not then try Bug Fables or go back to Paper Mario, it still holds up!

_childDocuments_.review: My formal review of Born of Bread:Going into this game, I was ready to like it. The art looked good, it was inspired by Paper Mario (a thumbs up in my book), and it was 50% off at the time of purchasing. It appeared the stars aligned for me to enjoy this game. Unfortunately, for as much as I did enjoy the game, it has equally lead to frustration, bafflement, anger, and, at times, pure unalterable apathy. I attempted to 100% the game, but the game being bugged as it is lead me to stop even trying. Let me get the good that is consistent out of the way:The art is solid. All around. You will not find a bad piece of artwork whether it's 3d, 2d, or a mix. And that's it. The is the only positively consistent thing throughout the game. Everything else:The combat isn't bad, but it's easily abusable, and that makes it bad. Not to mention, on hard mode, they do a lot of damage that can - and will - outpace your health, and make you game over a bunch. Part 2 being the  worst offender for how much of a GRIND it was just to go back and forth to restock items and healing. Quests would activate when it's clearly a quest meant for AFTER the chapter/part was completed. Sometimes even picking up an item over the threshold would freeze the game if you happened to make an input at the same time. You will find bugs and issues you aren't even looking for. There are some quests where if you attempt to speed through the dialouge, the game freezes and doesn't let you progress, there are background characters that are somehow in two or MORE places at once! You will find hallways that disappear and you can see into the other rooms. The developers couldn't keep try of the background characters arc/dialouge, and these were just a few of the issues I found this isn't every single one. I was just playing the game casually! I wasn't trying to find these issues, but they still came up! Part 2 was particularly awful because that was the part where if you happened to game over when you were playing, and eat an item, it won't always register as having been used until you saved and game overed again. Then the item would be gone, but that's not the worst bit. See, I discovered that if you opened up the gates, and then died, the gates would pop back up again, so you have to unlock them again. And, in my case, if you were running low on items and health, managed to die, and attempted to go ALL the way back to get healing. You could not. I really hated the temple section, as a result. Even the ending wasn't spared from bugs because after you defeat the last boss of the game and start talking to the characters, whatever conversation you had with that character, whatever Loaf's reaction was to the dialouge, Loaf's face REMAINS that way until the next conversation. I couldn't even really enjoy the story, which was invested until between part 2 and 3, when (imo) I didn't really feel like there wasn't enough time spent with Jester and his gang to justify the beats the story was giving them, and was just apathetic towards the characters by the end of it, and had just wanted this game to be done and over with. For me, this was the worst part: I had collected all the Salamanders. Every single one. I even beat every quest save for the Main one, so I could get the blue gem. But even after I BEAT the main game, I still didn't get the blue gem. And I was just. Over it at this point.  I had wanted to 100% the game to say I experienced EVERY aspect of this game, but like. It would be an unhappy grind just to get to that point. And this game already sucked up enough of my time as it is, between the resets, the bugs, the combat, the fetch quests, and the story that didn't really wow me by the end of that. Which is really unfortunate, because I can see all the love and care and jokes that were put into it, but there's no refinement or polish here. The game was too ambitious for what these developers were hoping to achieve with it, especially if they can't keep track of their NPCs, especially six months after release of their title they are still fixing consistent and persistent problems that plague their game. TD;LR: Buyer beware: This game is on par with today's triple A standards.

_childDocuments_.review: Look, I enjoy(ed) Born of Bread. It's very charming--the story is lovely, the characters are charming, and the combat is engaging enough. But some of the bugs/choices are truly just unforgivable and make what is otherwise a delightful title to be a massive slog.  The game needs an autosave feature, something that I think would eliminate my major gripe with the games. I frequently forget to save and I so rarely have difficulty with the combat wherein I feel saving is majorly important unless quitting for the night. I've experienced two different instances where I've lost an hour's worth of game play due to a lack of autosave. The specific one I'd like to touch on, one that genuinely made me frustrated enough to put the game down, was upon visiting the City of Doors. An important note that I've seen is this: if you fall into a pit or water, the game tries to place you back onto the last spot of land you could safely stand on. This is all well and fine unless you, like me, are unlucky enough to fall onto a small arch just beneath the island. As you can guess, there was no way to escape--and my last save was an hour beforehand.  I would recommend Born of Bread to a friend, but I don't think I would recommend a friend without a cautious warning.EDIT: The developer has addressed the bugs I discussed previously, and I’m really excited to pick the game back up.

_childDocuments_.review: You can read my other reviews Video review: In a world where many of us, during our leisure hours, lean towards realistic graphics rather than a peculiar art style, titles like Born of Bread might easily slip under the radar. Drawing inspiration from Mario Paper, Born of Bread is characterized by its cheesy moments, filled with puns and dad jokes, accompanied by a unique art style featuring charismatic characters made of paper cutouts, all set in a world of adventures promising lengthy text narratives.The story unfolds as a group of supposed natural explorers stumbles upon an intriguing group of ruins during their adventures, inadvertently reviving a group of malevolent characters from a long-forgotten kingdom. Their mission: collect all the Sunstones to resurrect their master. This raises a serious problem for the world. If the group effectively manages to collect all the Sunstones, it will destroy the kingdom as its inhabitants know. Curiously, on the same day, the Queen requests her faithful cook to prepare a special recipe, resulting in the accidental creation of Loaf, the bread boy and unexpected hero. Still not recovered from the moment that he found out that he is a father, the cook is wrongly identified as the culprit behind the resurrection of evil spirits, after the attack on the queen’s castle. Loaf is thus in charge of cleaning up his father’s image and trying to stop this group’s plans that threaten to destroy the world.As Loaf embarks on his adventure, he gathers a group of friends, united either by similar goals or the desire for adventure, forming a charming but loosely-knit group dynamic. There is undoubtedly a lot to read between the lines of text, in some cases even too much. Set in a vibrant world, although at times empty of content, the exploration of this 2.5D environment adds an interesting dimension to the game.Combat takes the form of a simple turn-based experience. Some attacks require the use of the mana bar, others require the specific bar for the special attack, and even attacks that don’t consume any of the latter. Regardless of the skill chosen, there will always be a need to play a type of mini-game, which will consist of clicking the corresponding button at the right time, following the correct key combination, or even aiming correctly until the timer runs out. On a defensive level, it is also possible to click the defense button at the right time, to either avoid the enemy attack or suffer less damage. It’s a somewhat interesting point, which will change depending on the enemy you’re facing.At certain times it is common to resort to special attacks, even if the reason is to see something different in the character’s attack, causing the mana bar to reach 0. To fight this issue, is introduced the audience mechanic. The fight will be broadcast live to an audience. If the entertainment bar reaches green, you will recover mana points. Honestly, it’s a mechanic that initially seemed interesting but turned into something that I paid barely any attention to at all. Perhaps due to the lack of need to use special skills, due to the low difficulty level. The lack of a slider to help adjust this situation was one of the turns off of this title, which unfortunately makes combat moments superficial, without great strategies associated with combos or anything similar.Each character has a range of different attacks, which are unlocked with experience points. This is where the need for exploration comes in, as to obtain experience points the player have to necessary collect a type of salamander and exchange them for points, in specific shrines for this purpose. On the other hand, after winning each combat, a percentage of experience points is awarded, where upon reaching 100, the option to level up, in specific Loaf, will be presented, along with progression in points such as inventory space or buffs. Loaf will also have a backpack that allows him to transport his attack items. These items can be found scattered across the map, or purchased in specific stores and chosen by the player in an attempt to adapt to different types of enemies.Unfortunately, the controls were one of the negative points that made my experience in the world of Born of Bread annoying. The menus are clunky, sometimes the buttons get stuck, and even though there is no support for the PS5 controller when playing on PC, it is possible to do so. Despite all the problems associated with this choice. I faced problems opening doors and a bug where I couldn’t open the menu at all.Visually Born of Bread is an enriching experience, told through superficial lines of text between charismatic characters and combat that is too simple for its own good. Certainly, the problems presented can be changed in future patches, but the feeling that it should have remained in the “oven” a little longer is present.

_childDocuments_.review: Born of Bread. I'm sorry to say but this game does not do it for me at all. The combat system is honestly the worst thing I have seen since Paper Mario Sticker Star. Speaking of Paper Mario, it feels wrong to call this a Paper Mario inspired game. The vibes are all there but they are all wrong. The "audience" mechanic is so pointless, it takes MULTIPLE TURNS just to earn 1 WP. The combat is also insanely botched, swapping to partner? skips Loaf's turn and puts Loaf back in the front. What is even the point of swapping? Just get rid of it. Useless buttons. I see things constantly flickering. Lint's animation during battle for example, he disappears for a frame here or he clips into the ground for another. Anyways aside from the battle stuff. The story was so uninteresting and the jokes never landed with me. The only one that got me was the autosave joke which did get a chuckle from me. This game tries too hard to be funny which takes away from the story massively as everyone takes everything as a joke or is just 'grr me mad cus grr'. Yeah I have low hours but I just couldn't stand playing this for any longer than I did. Don't go relating it to paper Mario TTYD, you'll be disappointed just like me with this game.Edit 1: I feel like I judged the dialog too harshly. I wont be deleting everything I said as I don't want to let my honest opinions to go away. I will be playing some more of this at a later point and maybe if my opinions change I will update them.Also I forgot to add that the graphics are actually very fantastic, the world design is very good.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really enjoying it. It's only been out for a month, so I won't be too critical, but my two primary concerns are the bugs and the achievements. This game is FULL of bugs that need to be worked out, and two achievements are broken, possibly more depending on whether certain objectives are even present in the game. But considering how small the dev team is and how new the game, gotta cut them a lot of slack, and I know they are active with the community in addressing complaints and suggestions.Other than these gripes, this game is truly phenomenal. There's no way I would ever have logged over 100 hours in a game this buggy if it wasn't worth playing. Everything is fantastic - the atmosphere, the music, the towns and wilderness areas, the chapters and story, the characters, the art style, the puzzle aspects, the pop culture references, the little details in the background; it all really comes together to make an incredibly enjoyable experience. It's a hard recommend from me as long as the dev team keeps up with fixes and maintenance.

_childDocuments_.review: Now, I'll be honest: It's a bit of a unfair comparison to Paper Mario 64 and Paper Mario: TTYD but inspiration was clearly taken from both games and Moonsprout games' Bug Fables! So a comparison will be made nevertheless. So here is some comments from each chapter:Prologue - Does fine on it's own to explain the story and teach the basic overworld controls. That's about it...Chap 1 - Alright, could've used a bit of polish considering things kinda just... Happen. But all things considered, my favorite area in the game. I don' have much to respond with on chapter 1. It also does an ok job at teaching how to fight enemies.Chap 2 - Boring. Plain and simple. They hype it up to be this "Grand Tournament!" But it's just walk through these halls and fight a few enemies and solve some "Puzzles". It also had these "Master challenges." First was a game of jumping minigame which was alright, Second was a riddle "minigame" (The correct answer was always obvious.) And third was one of those follow the object under a cup minigames... Like what?! One of the enemy types in this area were also pretty tough all things considered. The Chapter boss was laughably easy though... I just swung a shish kabab at him 4 times and we won. :/Chap 3 - I HATED Clayton manor... It's a giant fetch quest while backtracking the whole dam area with major annoyances along the way... The enemies were also crazy strong! Their was multiple times I had to just Flee a battle to not risk going down... This is also the only area where I had a party member get KOed, But I'll admit that was due to poor action on my part. (I should've Fled/Healed instead of Defended.) They were also placed in areas that forced you to fight them if you weren't careful.  This area also had the most places I could have gotten stuck/softlocked, One of them was at a save point! Thankfully The game has checks when saving your game to teleport Loaf to the NPC. But, I shouldn't have even have discovered the game has this check in the first place...  And just like Chapter 2, The mini-boss and Chapter boss were major pushovers.Chap 4 - Chapter 4 was hectic. Alot happend, mainly just to tell story and stuff, but they never even give explanation. The layout of the level was just kinda... all-over? It was a linier path... But had issues... This area I also encountered a daming bug that put the player camera in first person of Loaf... That's horrid given this game is ment to be played with a third-person camera. The controls were also off because of it. So Left was back, Up was left, Right was forward, and Down was right... and since the camera was not ment for this. I couldn't rotate it...Chap 5 (Finale) - It was... Underwhelming. This was ment to be the big ***SHABANG!*** The thing you are building up to the ENTIRE adventure! But it was only 3 rooms long... Just like chapter 2 & 3, The enemies were strong, but given how this was the final area I was ok with it. But you also fight the mini-boss and Final Boss back-to-back without being given a chance to restore your Health/Will/Resolve, So you just go into the Final Boss weakend from the fight with the  mini-boss! At least Paper Mario 64 has the decency to heal you before the true final fight! And Bug Fables gives you a break between the Wasp King & Final Battle to prepare yourself and heal up! But it didn't even matter because the Final Boss went down like a wet napkin! He made the Everlasting King, (Bug Fables' Final Boss), Look easy! And the ELK was just attack and you win. I won by doing almost nothing but defending because I had a funny badge that made it to where If I defend correctly I perform a life steal on the attacker! It wasn't even intentional given how defending gives Will Points for free to use your damn weapons!And just before I you thought I was done, The game has other issuses, mainly during battle.-Some weapons are Overpowered and I used them constantly, some Underpowered and never worth using. -I had multiple instances where a enemy or ally would glitch out making it hard to defend/attack-It could have been the recordings I was taking, but the game had issues just playing it! It was a constant lag-a-thon. I even had the game freeze just entering a loading zone In Chapter 4!-This is more of a nitpick than anything, but While playing the game... all of the partners animations have less frames than Loaf's this is mostly noticeable with Loaf and Lint's running animations. But I noticed it every time.But who knows, maybe my review means nothing... Maybe what I said was some nonsense... But as stated above, I recorded most of my journey though this game and got many of the bugs, steamrolls, and trials on the recording...Personally, I've done some looking into the developer and publisher's perior games. And I'm gonna chuck this up to First-game-in-the-series itis. If another attempt at a PM style rpg was made, I feel it could do better... I won't stop anyone who wishes to play this game and see if they have better luck, but I cannot recommend Born of Bread.
_childDocuments_.name: Born of Bread

_childDocuments_.review: This game is like if the older Paper Marios (64, Thousand Year Door) were allowed to roam wild and free and frolic in the weird delight of imagination. The turn based combat is fun, the plot is adorable and genuinely interesting, the characters are easy to invest in, it's chock-full of references to all sorts of other properties... This game is overall a masterpiece and I'll be making my friends play it for sure!
_childDocuments_.name: Born of Bread

_childDocuments_.review: I played the demo back in June, and noted that the battle mechanics are particularily janky, mainly things that deal with both Loaf and the partner. The button that swaps their positions is actually just a button that skips Loaf's turn. The option that switches their positions also does this, but for some reason you can swap back to Loaf and keep his turn. Once it reaches the enemy's turn, they always attack Loaf UNLESS you pick the Defend option with your partner - which not only nullifies damage if you land guard commands while Defending, but also gives you FP. These issues alone might not be a problem, and if it took after Paper Mario 64's style it probably wouldnt be - but, like every Paper Mario-like, it clearly takes after TTYD's mechanics instead, just for them to be completely broken here.This game doesn't seem to have much identity to itself outside of that besides being wacky, so there's not much to this besides that. I am only like, 2 hours in though, so maybe it changes down the line. I'm kinda just along for the ride to see how stupidly jank this gets. Everyone likes a broken game every once in a while!That said, maybe don't give them your money on this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Born of Bread

_childDocuments_.review: POSITION REMAINS SAME: I CANNOT in good conscience recommend that people pay money for a game in this condition. Details below.-------------------------------After pushing ahead with this game, my thoughts remain unchanged. If I eventually finish it, it's going to have to be on the steam deck. On Steam Deck, parts of the UI - most notably, KEY DIALOGUE and your HP - regularly slide off the left side of the screen for some ridiculous reason. But it's at least playable, without dropping so many frames or hitching mid-combat and screwing up your attempts at each attack's minigame.And yet somehow, a game to run in buttery smooth mode on the deck, abjectly struggles to maintain decent frame rates on an i9 processor with an RTX 3080 at 4k, stuttering quite often during combat.Worse yet, the graphical modes don't seem to behave correctly. Content-wise, I WANT to like this game, but it's a downright chore to try to get it to behave to play it.As a response to the (INSULTING AND CONDESCENDING) note from the developer:====STEAM DECK ISSUES:====- Steam Deck setting is at the 1280x800 resolution. I have even tried setting it forced that way in the Steam Deck game properties (General->Game Resolution) directly! The cropping problem for the dialogue and UI remains unchanged. This very moment I'm in Chloe's dialogue and it's happened twice. The "Of" in "Of Course, the "C" in "Coldstock," and the "t" in "the house" are all currently cut off on my screen.- The cropping issue also persists whether the game is in Fullscreen, Borderless or Windowed on Steam Deck.====PC ISSUES====- On my PC, the drivers are the absolute latest NVidia Game Ready drivers.-- "Fullscreen" mode, unless you match the screen's native resolution? Enjoy the GIANT BLACK BORDERS on right and below.-- "Windowed" mode: halfway kinda viable, if you want to maximize it and put a white border on screen top, but you have to alt-tab out to get to interact with the top of screen.-- "Borderless" mode: just as bad as Fullscreen only actually worse, it managed to glitch into a "blind" mode showing me the black borders even with the screem "expanded." Had to flail around for 5 minutes to get it to windowed, reset to 4k, THEN go borderless to get a correct display.There is no way to get a simple "run the game in 1080p on my 4k screen" even for testing purposes.====EVEN WORSE AND MORE INCOMPETENT====The game seems to be saving its graphics settings to the same spot as the save file, and synchronizing them through Steam Cloud.So once I got it "set" on my PC, closed the game, and reopened on my Steam Deck: now my Steam Deck is trying to run in 4K Borderless.
