_childDocuments_.review: Im sorry to be making a bad review on such a great game, but near the end game, I accepted the quest "A ghastly request" and if you go in the wrong direction, the ghost will tell you. only problem is, he says that for EVERY DIRECTION. ive sat here for about 30 minutes trying to find a way around it then thought "maybe i just need a little more progress to unlock a path that he is wanting me to go down" BUT I SAVED WITH HIM FOLLOWING ME. until this bug gets fixed, im not willing to restart the game and go through aaaaall of it again, so for now if you see this, avoid that quest
_childDocuments_.name: Born of Bread

_childDocuments_.review: In my opinion, the Paper Mario series was never something that I enjoyed playing. I simply never considered it to be something that was really fantastic more, casual, slow paced and just boring all around.Born of Bread simply takes everything that was in those games and applies it in the same way that it was done in those games. The game play is stale, slow, and uninteresting; everything is the same, including the motions and the triggers; they could have at least added some kind of variety, right? Having conversations with non-player characters while slamming stuff with a frying pan and running around. Perhaps it makes an effort to be endearing and adorable, but it simply does not provide anything that is novel. This game will be a nice match for you if you feel like playing Paper Mario without actually playing Paper Mario, but there wasn't anything that was particularly exciting about this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Born of Bread

_childDocuments_.review: The timed combat system is stupid beyond all belief - the "wiggle the stick for 10 seconds" attack in particular.  Seriously?  Could have been great if they employed a different combat system.  I'd buy it again if they just reworked all of that.  So disappointing because it otherwise looks fantastic, menus are reasonable, etc.
_childDocuments_.name: Born of Bread

_childDocuments_.review: This game in one word, . It felt like they wanted the dragon ball z IP but couldn't get it. It's like paper mario but mario was a social media influencer instead of a plumber, or bread w/e. I'm under the belief that this game was made using only visual programming tools, with button presses bleeding through, instructions to press buttons at the correct time but they mean hold at the right time as quick presses often wont register, and the menus don't even pause the game. Just a tedious slog of a game that got far too much praise.
_childDocuments_.name: Born of Bread

_childDocuments_.review: The game is visually very nice, but that is about were all the upsides end imo.  The story is very basic and not all that fun.  But the biggest issue is a lot of the combat mechanic choices.  They just seem very annoying and frustrating instead of fun which is the main point of battling in a game like this.  Plus no ability to remap keys is just very unacceptable in 2023 for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Born of Bread

_childDocuments_.review: Yea I found BoB to be very disappointing, there's almost no care put into the battle system at all its basically impossible to die because of how easy it is to block. The art is inconsistent, no 2 characters look like they belong in the same world. There's nothing coherent about its setting or themeing. Your first weapon is a ladle you'd assume there's going to be a cooking them at least for your character but then you just get a sickle for chopping things. The writing has no charm at all there's no personality to any of its characters and its world being 3D with a lighting engine doesn't match the characters at all.So the combat is bland and has no innovation, the world is boring to look at and interact with and there's no reason to explore it because the rewards are useless and the discoveries soulless.
_childDocuments_.name: Born of Bread

_childDocuments_.review: If your looking for a game like Paper Mario, this is definitely one i recommend you play. It has a great story with a wide cast of characters, a unique art style which helps the world feel alive and fresh, and the combat feels right at home with how close it is to the Paper Mario mechanics.I sat for hours loving each and every character, sidequest, and story i unlocked as i kept playing this game, its a fun adventure im sure many people will enjoy!
_childDocuments_.name: Born of Bread

_childDocuments_.review: Tons of fun!! Obviously heavily inspired by the Paper Mario series, so if you love those, you'll have a great time with this. The fact that every single attack has action commands makes it sooooo much fun, and I'm glad we have more examples of it being implemented correctly because I would love to play more RPG's in this fashion.There are a few bugs with menu stuff, switching partners, etc. but it's not game breaking, nor does it really interrupt your ability to play this game to 100% completion. I don't expect it to be completely polished and without bugs, finding programmers and game devs to create a project with 0 bugs whatsoever would be way bigger news than "this game has a really clean finish". Had to address it because it's mentioned often in the reviews, however it's not a big deal. I hesitated to buy the game because of it, but I'm glad I ended up playing it despite it.My only real gripe is that the game can get super easy, and I totally forgot that special moves existed because you can run through the game without it. All of the sidequests require some form of backtracking, and you can end up over-leveling and no longer needing items or special moves at all. The difficulty makes it really accessible to younger or more casual players, which is great! But if there was a way to design the game such that you CANNOT forget about these aspects of the game, and it's challenging enough that you're forced to spend some RP on a regular basis, I think this game would be a 10/10. I'd give it an 8/10 though! - it's super charming- I love the characters- the story is well done- there are plenty of jokes and puns that make the dialogue worth reading- the sidequests are rewarding- the challenge of fitting the weapon blocks to keep everything in your backpack is super cool- The ability to increase your out-of-combat speed makes backtracking EASY instead of a hassle- The entire game was well thought out, well designed, with great artwork to boot
_childDocuments_.name: Born of Bread

_childDocuments_.review: This was a really enjoyable game!The gameplay is simple to learn and fun, the party members are a bunch of lovable dorks, and the story is a fun little ride. There are a few odd glitches but they were rare and not game breaking. I was hoping it would be a fun little Paper Mario-like game and it didn't disappoint. But it also stood on its own with the story and world. I can't wait to see what this team does next. I recommended this game to my buddies.
_childDocuments_.name: Born of Bread

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent in so many ways, but better suited for a younger audience. I followed this game's development as I just really loved Paper Mario TTYD and hoped this could scratch that itch. In terms of aesthetic, vibe, and writing the game absolutely nails this - far closer to TTYD than Bug Fables managed, with consistently witty, slightly whimsical writing, and fantastic characters. The story is pretty straightforward, but the fun of the characterisation and dialogue kept me going. The companions are engaging with well thought out in-world mechanical abilities, and the supporting world denizens have strong character and offer a lot of interesting side quests (mostly fetch quests but the writing still keeps it interesting).Onto the negative: unfortunately, the game is just very very easy. Mechanically everything is more or less pulled directly from TTYD (audience charging abilities, badges, timed blocks in combat, etc), and whilst this is not by itself a problem, the game doesn't really develop these ideas and is severely lacking in complexity. Throughout the entire main storyline I never came even close to dying in combat, and the in-game puzzles are basically limited to find and press a switch. I don't want to be too harsh as a lot of love has clearly been poured into the game, it has a lot of polish, and I don't begrudge my time playing, but this is just missing any sense of challenge throughout. For very young gamers this is probably perfect, and, again, I really did love the world and writing. Maybe let us actually fight our way through the Savers Guild next time.
_childDocuments_.name: Born of Bread

_childDocuments_.review: I can only commend the team behind this game. Some great care, effort and love for the genre has been poured into this.Everything from the Look, Designs, Soundtrack and Feel of the game is absolutely amazing.It made me so nostalgic for the times when I first played the Paper Mario series as a kid and was enthralled with the world - Born of Bread does the same for me today: Whacky Characters, great writing and a world thats so much fun to explore.The Combat is quick and snappy - and extends on the Turn Based / Action Based formular wonderfully with a damage type system - the action commands and a very clever Inventory System that keeps the game just complex enough to be enjoyable and deep - without going into more complex RPG territory.If you like the Paper Mario series - you will absolutely love this game.Thanks WildArts Games to deliver such a great experience <3
_childDocuments_.name: Born of Bread

_childDocuments_.review: Bug Fables filled the void of a lack of a traditional Paper Mario, and this game fills the void after that just as well. Beautiful visuals, impressive world-building, exploration and soundtrack, tons of side content, fun characters and comedy and a super engaging story. With a majority of the bugs in this game now being patched out it's a very enjoyable experience with only a few complaints being the Hard Mode being a little too reliant on defending for the first few chapters to get through it and a needless grind of the in-game currency near the end in order to purchase every unique collectable, as well as the final chapter being much shorter than I would have liked it to be. Would absolutely recommend to anyone looking for a wacky RPG adventure akin to the Paper Mario series.
_childDocuments_.name: Born of Bread

_childDocuments_.review: Born of bread is a pretty fun game inspired by Paper Mario (maybe borrowing a bit more from it than I think bug fables does which stands a little bit more on its own legs). Fun world and characters, colorful art, plenty of room for your team to become a very busted unit with a couple of different strategies. The actions you do in battle get repetitive since all partners basically share the same three kinds of action commands with one unique exception per each. The game is still quite jank and glitchy, the devs have been hard at work releasing patches to mitigate various bugs and softlocks (one of which i fell victim to when backtracking for the game's partner upgrade collectibles where a bee enemy attacked us and once battle started, it kept wiggling its butt at me in battle while my party was frozen in place forever with no way to get out without closing the program). At not even 12 euro during the current sale while I typed this review, I'd say it's worth it if you like paper mario and want something similar to that with some zoomer humor sprinkled throughout. Maybe "sprinkled" is sugarcoating it, more like baked into the whole experience. You'll probably feel the aftertaste.
_childDocuments_.name: Born of Bread

_childDocuments_.review: Given it has very many puns in it it's only right to make one myself.The game is good, it was fun (hard mode made early to midgame a challenge)But the finer details were just not done, you could say it still needed time in the oven (hehehe)There was for me no gamebreaking bugs but i stumbled into several.1: With speed upgrades you start to stutter when running as if collision happens with the floor, slowing you down and looks awful.2: If you die during combat and reload a save it sometimes just turns of sounds, have to restart to fix it.3: The final upgrades for completion don't work right and there should be a respec option as they affect stats.4: Map having collectibles tracked is really nice QoL but one of them didn't track, should be easy to fix though by uping the tracker by 1 for the location and tying a point to that weapon.5: Some battle commands are weird, can't switch partner during their turn (in paper-mario you could, and made it more a decision who does what), If you defend during your turn enemies act twice in a round, after your turn then again after partners turn.6: Most Boons (Badges) don't stack but you get several copies of some which is really weird.Though even with these problems the game is completable and fun enough, just needs some more polish and would happily look forward to a sequel, not many good paper mario style games around (Bug fables for one, and it's more well done than this one was so recommended if you like these types)Gametime heavily inflated, kept it on in the background quite a lot (due to health reasons can only play a little at a time) so probably ~20/30h is more right for 100%.
_childDocuments_.name: Born of Bread

_childDocuments_.review: Born of Bread is a RPG game that takes heavy inspiration from the Paper Mario series. This game has me with its colorful cast, cheesy puns, awesome music, and beautiful visuals. While the game may be very easy in my opinion, it does provide a bit of a challenge at times. I'd definitely recommend this game to anyone who's a Paper Mario fan or a fan of RPGs. Stay Toasty! (Literally)
_childDocuments_.name: Born of Bread

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game! I had an amazing time playing it!This will remind you of paper mario for sure, but despite that, the core mechanics, the arts, the MUSICS (the musics are truly amazing) makes for a very good and chill experience. _childDocuments_.review: Born of bread is a cute little game very reminiscent of paper mario. Lighthearted, doesn't waste time with endless grinding against enemies, and fun levels. There are some bugs, but during a normal playthrough I did not find anything game breaking. I hope the development team makes a sequel, this is one of the first games in a while that I not only finished, but finished within a few weeks of buying it - most games just end up in the ever-so-common steam library of nothingness.TLDR: Made me happy :)
_childDocuments_.name: Born of Bread

_childDocuments_.review: This is a cute game, a distinct art style, cute characters, and over all charming. I wish I could enjoy the game with no complaints, there are some bugs that make the game frustrating. From minor bugs I can ignore for the most part like dialogue getting sometimes stuck for a moment/or weird movement glitches. To ones that require a restart like sometimes when you drop a game in your inventory and the game has you try to 'use' the game that's no longer in your inventory so you're locked in the pick a character arrows and can't get out of it. Or more frustratingly a bug with a mechanic in another area that stops you from progressing in the area entirely Annoying and I can see fully how some people would stop playing out of these bugs (I do hope they are patched at some point especially if they are working on a follow up piece to this game, since having a bad experience w/ the first game due to bugs could hinder the next one)Over all I stuck through it because I did really like the other elements of the game a lot, but just one of those 'i would recommend but be mindful there are some bugs that I'm hoping get fixed to make the experience a lot better'.
_childDocuments_.name: Born of Bread

_childDocuments_.review: This game was really fun, it was full to the brim with style and I fell in love with the characters. Lint was my favorite from start to finish. The music was pretty good, albeit a bit repetitive when you are in the same area for an hour+. The battle mechanics do get a bit stale the more you play, but overall I still found them enjoyable.Now the only real issues I had with this game was a lack of polish in some bits. Both of my biggest concerns were in the llama heights, the butterfly trees felt incredibly wonky and Would I recommend this game? absolutely.Were there a few issues that took a bit away from the experience? yes.is it still worth your money? yes!9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Born of Bread

_childDocuments_.review: Very hesitant recommendation: Only get if you like exploration/collectingThe environments, platforming and collection aspect were top notch in this game. Music was really nice.Other than that, the game was pretty disappointing. Combat system was on one hand extremely fleshed out but also trivialized and overall none of the battles felt impactful or satisfying.
_childDocuments_.name: Born of Bread

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, this game is absolutely a good time. It's charming, fun, and pretty to look at. I found myself coming back to it often the moment I started and it became my "go to game" until completion. However, I do have a few problems that I feel I need to address. The game is a little too easy. That's not exactly a bad thing outright, but I found myself very underwhelmed at times when it came to certain battles that were made out to be important. The biggest one being the final boss (Which I will not speak more of). Though I did die on a few occasions, those deaths were usually caused by me not paying attention or because I had a lot of environmental damaged built up and went in on low hp. Fun and difficulty don't have to be connected and I myself am more of a causal and standard difficulty kind of guy, but it would be nice to have the option to increase the challenge.The physics in this game are straight janked, no beating around that. It was to the point where I was at a constant worry of accidentally soft locking myself by doing things I shouldn't be able to by jumping into a spot that, honestly, looks fine until you get there. It never happened and it was a mild worry, but with a game that encourages looking around, paying attention to small details in the over world, and almost constant platforming, you can hopefully understand where I'm coming from.I'm not trying to rip this game open and point out ever little flaw I came across because again, I had a good time with this one. People have their opinions and I'm expressing mine when I say, I recommend this. Just be ready for a handful of minor problems. It's not like it'll ruin the contagions and charming vibes.
_childDocuments_.name: Born of Bread

_childDocuments_.review: The art, dialog, and puns of this game are really greatBut this game should have been listed as Early Access, there are such a mix of really annoying systems and bugs that while you can complete this game from start to finish, there is a high level of annoyance the game gives:Item management: There is no sorting in the game, inventory is sorted based on when you received the item, making everything feel cluttered in the weapons panel and especially the boons menuBoon stacking broken: The game offers you multiple duplicates of the same boon sometimes 2 - 4 times and these do not stack, if the boons do not stack then they should not be duplicates, much less give me the ability to add them all to my pageThere is even a final boon that is unobtainable in the game if you make the mistake of not collecting the reward before it first, which is just weirdFriend Skills, broken:Some of the abilities in the game just do not work correctly as they are written, Yagi's final skill for example only hits one time dispite listing 2xPoor Balancing:Being able to perfectly block an attack stops being rewarding after a little progress in the game as it only ever seems to block one damageThat being said, most of the systems in the game feel too cluttered and unneeded, the specials you get, defensive items, healing items, for the most part feel completely unneeded, you level up so fast in the game that it becomes easier to rely on gaining a level for a full Heal over using any items or even using the rest spotsEven the final boss of the game was far too easy having nearly half my own HPAll in all I really do want to love this game, but I wish this wasn't sold to me as a complete game because if I had known how buggy it was I would have rather waiting to enjoy it
_childDocuments_.name: Born of Bread

_childDocuments_.review: As someone that grew up loving every second of Paper Mario and Paper Mario: The Thousand Year Door, this game was exceptional! A bit short, only clocking around 20 hours to complete it. The combat loop never got boring, and exploring all of the different areas with your partner characters was a treat (especially when you remembered seeing things earlier and coming back later to finally get the chest in the background).The game has a few bugs (and the achievements aren't accessible because of them,) but other than that I don't have any complaints about the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Born of Bread

_childDocuments_.review: It's not perfect; I do wish that some of the mechanics were explained better. But now that I'm getting into the meat of the game, I'm really enjoying the battle system, especially how you can defend to get back WP. And the story and characters are just so darn adorable; they're such a treat to interact with.
_childDocuments_.name: Born of Bread

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game, it was an absolute gem to find. Decent writing, great puns/dad jokes and a great cast of characters. Yes, it is similar to paper mario, they even play on that lovingly in achievements and in the game. My only complaint are the random bugs you'll run into (so SAVE OFTEN) and there are a few achievements that are busted and you cannot get them (completionists beware).EDIT: They have recently fixed a lot of the bugs and it is now possible to 100% the game. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Born of Bread

_childDocuments_.review: I deeply love Paper Mario and Paper Mario: TTYD. As a result, I had and still have really high hopes for this game. After playing playing for the first 30 minutes, Born of Bread has a distinct charm and potential to be Paper Mario's spiritual successor. However, first the bugs must be addressed. In the first 30 minutes, the bugs were enough to take me out of the game. Specifically, while moving the character's animation stutters when reaching collision as well as the camera stuttering. There was a moment where I could not choose what item to use but was locked into one specifically. There's so much evident love poured into this game, please fix these bugs and cross the finish line! I will resume my play in a few months and am hopeful that some of the bugs will be fixed!
_childDocuments_.name: Born of Bread

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely work for the style, game mechanics, and story that was chosen.  Nostalgic with the Paper Mario style.  Marvellous work the character personalities, emotes, and stories.  Enough to fit for general story play-through.  Good placement of fast-travel points, both teleport's and shortcuts.  Not crazy to complete 100%.  Might have bit too much running around for trying to get place to place, even with run button.  Warning for multitude of puns.  Found quaint and humorous, but warning for though of pun evasive positions.  Not ground breaking for the genre.  Interesting battle style, player has lots of verity and style to attack. Partners are distinct.  Not sure if bug or game, but player always takes the hit, so be ready.If turn based simple RPG is your jam, this loaf is ready, whether plain or toasted.If your searching for something more fast paced and challenging, you can leave in on the shelf.  It's still good.
_childDocuments_.name: Born of Bread

_childDocuments_.review: This RPG has successfully brought me back to the glory days of Paper Mario The Thousand Year Door! There are some minor mechanics I would change, but for the most part this game is great. Sucks that it only has 4 chapters. I feel like they could have made the game longer. Currently at the beginning of the 3rd chapter. I spent a lot of time backtracking to get those lizard soul things and I have 11 hours so, I assume I'll beat the game after 20 hours of gameplay. The comedy is very cheap but goofy like Paper Mario so I'll give it a pass.
_childDocuments_.name: Born of Bread

_childDocuments_.review: Loved every single second playing this game!Good:- Interesting characters with good and funny dialogues- Good Sidequests. It was fun to 100% them- Fun to explore the world to find weapons, boons and more- It really felt like a Paper Mario game which was my hope after getting a bit dissappointed by an ''insect RPG''- Banger soundtrackBad (Current Version 3.1):- there are many bugs which CAN happen if you get unlucky and can softlock yourself until you restart the game (spawning out of bounds over and over, game freezes in a specific battle)- Buggy achievements (if you're unlucky)- the game was overall way too easy, especially the bosses! i played on the hard mode which wasn't hard apparently :/Imo the 25€ are totally worth even tho it has some problems here and there. _childDocuments_.name: Born of Bread

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely loved this game:+ The OST was good or better- no bad tracks imo (and I'm picky!) ;+ Fun characters with consistent arcs throughout. + Backgrounds felt lived-in and had a story to tell.- A few minor bugs throughout but nothing too badOverall? _childDocuments_.name: Born of Bread

_childDocuments_.review: A charming and functional Paper Mario inspired RPG hindered by a lack of polish. As of this review, I often experienced performance issues such as stuttering, rooms not loading correctly, actions not triggering (laying in bed, talking to others, glitches when swapping partners after using abilities, saving the game, etc.), just to name a few. Even with those minor frustrations, if you love the old school Paper Mario RPGs, you'll probably love this too! I'm excited for the (probable) future games, I want to see how much more this franchise can expand.
_childDocuments_.name: Born of Bread

_childDocuments_.review: If you are looking for a faithful and well thought out Paper Mario clone, this is the one for you. others will tell you it's buggy, it's been patched. others will tell you it's not funny enough, they're wrong. _childDocuments_.review: The game is very nice and the characters are cute, I love what they do with the levels and the puzzles for each level, the diversity in level design really made me keep playing and seeing how far the game would take it.Huge recommendation to get this game just for the fun platforming, puzzles, and world building.The battles are your typical Paper mario style but with added flair where there are more resistances and weaknesses for the enemies, and you can get all the elements for the MC if you look around which is good.However the difficulty for the battles don't exactly increase much, the difficulty curve is much slower then your progression and once you have moves that can hit every enemy, its basically impossible to lose until the boss for that stage.Same goes for how to get perfect damage on your moves, There isnt many variations of buttons or mechanics to get perfect damage and the skill needed is minimal which can be nice especially if you just want to play it casually, but for people who played paper mario-like games like bug fables and want to test themselves, (and yeah I know they added a hard mode recently but still) I wish it was more difficult for some parts.One thing I really wish they added was more detailed hints for quests that are being progressed, because sometimes I was lost by what the quest wanted at times, and another thing is to let us know when we cant do a quest yet due to where we are in the story. I wont say why exactly due to spoilers but if you're a completionist, one or two quests will bug you cause you cant do them till later.also the bugs... self-explanatory...I know there is a lot more complaining on here then compliments, But I promise this game holds promise, it just has some rough edges, I love this game and the characters, and after a few updates can be perfect, and I  really do hope there comes a DLC for this game for some expanded lore or some post game content if possible.

_childDocuments_.review: Off the top let me be clear, this game is good, it's very enjoyable, but there are some issues as there are with any game, but the developers are working on those.First, the characters:You have  your main pc Loaf and 4 colorful and funny characters you will recruit, I won't spoil any of your allies, but I will at least talk about the player character Loaf: your player character silent, but kinda awesome in his own way, very versatile toolkit based on how the game works, so think most people will be able to find a playstyle that works for them. That said you do make dialogue choices, and he mimes much like a certain paper thin italian so you can often feel what he's feeling.Side characters, such as your pc's creator are all very enjoyable and honestly even the  jerk characters you can enjoy to a degree because of how hard they lean into it. Ther are characters that are references to certain characters from shows like pokemon you'll know them when you see them or hear them say something. Locations: Each of the four main locations are very atmosphereic from the woods you start in after the tutorial, an ancient monestary thats constantly being built higher and higher, to an old mansion with a quirky family living within, and he last main area has pirates so whats not to love.Quests: Your main and sub quests are normally fairly easy to follow, and give rewards ranging from cosmetic such as modifications for your battle indicators to make them look how you want them, to normal cosmetics for your heroes, weapons, or even just consumables. no matter what the quests are normally fairly enjoyable and easy enough. combat:  think  rock paper scissors with a bit of pokemon elemental stuff going on. there is a handy chart in game to show you what works on what, but there is also later a badge that will  just show you what enemies are weak to. but that only helps you as much as you having the right ally or right weapons equiped to loaf, I say right ally as at the time of writing there is no ability to switch your companions mid battle, least not that was obvious, and if you don't have attacks that are effective you can do little or in worst case scenarios no damage to enemies. so  work on upping the amount of weapons and varieties of blunt, slashing, and piercing damage you can do to ensure you have something for any opportunity.Leveling upStandard to a point, each level up you choose to up a stat, but you also put a stamp on one of the options, with a different amount needed for each to get your next big reward. There doesn't seem to be a level max, or at least I haven't hit it yet, but feels like you don't keep extra experience when you level.TLDR: Good game, get it,

_childDocuments_.review: I've spent a few good hours in this game, and am about halfway through. This review will be from where I'm at now in the game, and listing the pros and cons for my play time so far.Pros: -Combat is quite simple and complex at the same time. The actions in combat are samey, with many attacks having the same action command. While not an issue, it is interesting with the amount of weapons and characters in the game that there are only a few commands. The enemies also have resistances to certain elements, which is sometimes annoying. It does actually work into the games favor, due to their partner upgrade system; I'll go into that now.-Partners are quite fun. I've enjoyed the interactions with eachother, and the surroundings. The upgrade system for their abilities is quite interesting, and it requires exploration and close listening. Which in a game like this, is both amazing and frustrating. You have to collect Salamanders in the overworld and bring them to a "mysterious" figure that gives you skill points. It's fun to get the upgrades. However, your partners having their new skills have different WP Costs is quite significant.Cons:-Leveling is quite boring. You don't particularly need RP, due to Loaf being the only one to really use it. Your partners can use it if you run out of WP, but if you specifically level WP you won't have to worry about it.-The story feels quite bland? I don't have much to say at this point due to not being super far into the game, but The Maguffin is usually protected by one of the bad guys, and they still get the maguffin even if you win. It's understandable for the story, but it still feels like something could've been improved to make it more interesting. The 1st chapter boss has no real stakes, and the chapter 2 and 3 boss both ended up being uninteresting, with their attacks and "vibes". Points to the chapter 3 boss though for downing a party member. -Items are completely useless for competent players. The items heal too much given their place in the game, and you have to intentionally get hit to even really need to use them. The WP and RP items would be helpful, but you level up consistently enough that I only had to use them once, while quest grinding. Speaking of...-The quests have a lot of issues at the moment, and I've gotten stuck/softlocked on 2 of them. I hope a future patch fixes them(at the time of writing a patch is in the works), but I had to step away from the game due to inability to even play. After chapter 3 is completed, a lot of quests open up. Unfortunately, I GOT SOFTLOCKED. I am shocked this wasnt caught during testing, but the team on the game has done a great job with everything else, so I'll wait for the patch.-----------------------Verdict: I love this game. It's been genuinely fun to play through a fresh take on the Paper Mario style and gameplay is fun. Seeing their plans for the next update, it will add a lot of Qol and hopefully fix the bugs i've experienced. I'm very happy with the product, and hope to be able to play it more. Current Rating: 7/10.----------------Edit: 2/8/24Finished the game 5 minutes ago. Here to update my review to allow a new reader to get some more info. I genuinely love this game. The 4th chapter is quite fun, and without spoilers, is a fun take on the style of that type of area. The 5th chapter is kind of underwhelming, especially with the concept that the final room of enemies are worth 20EXP per enemy. Got me to my final levels I needed though, so its a blessing and curse. The credits had me laughing due to the post game photos, and the finale of the story was fun enough with the ending being satisfying. The game is a great game for beginners to the genre, due to the story and combat being simplistic, and it's easily accessible. Overall, after the bugs are fixed and the devs are satisfied with the game, I can easily recommend this to my friends.Final Rating: 9/10. Without the bugs, an easy 10/10 for this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Very artistic/stylish Paper Mario-like RPG. Great game for being made by a relatively small team. Story and gameplay doesn't stray far from the PM formula but generally succeeds when playing around with certain mechanics. If you're an avid PM fan then you can buy this at it's current state and price and you'll likely enjoy it despite its minor bugs and shortcomings. Otherwise, just wait until it to goes on sale and/or the devs have time to work through some bugs and it'll be well worth your purchase. With that being said, I'd say Born of Bread has earned itself being more than just being a "PM clone" and has a lot of things that make it stand out IMO:-  Obviously takes inspiration from PM, but doesn't feed in to the paper aesthetic as much as that or Bug Fables (also love the Bug Fables easteregg in there). It has it's own style and it's great.-  and their audio cues were a fun and easy way to encourage exploration.-  Parts of the map connect to eachother the more you explore.- - While I didn't care much for Dub as a character much as others may have, I think it's creative how he's used to tie in the game's save feature and the game's take on the audience system. -  As others have said, I feel like Jester and his team were more interesting characters a lot of the time. To get nitpicky, I would have liked more sections where you got to control Jester and/or his team and done things from their point of view. - : Most of them were alright. The time challenges were the most enjoyable. I noticed a few instances where quests would be blocked off from one another if you had to interact with an NPC for multiple quests. Sometimes the NPC I had to talk to wouldn't trigger the end of the quest causing me to be unable to finish it.-: I feel like I may have been an outlier in this area, because I personally didn't experience many bugs. When I did they weren't too bad and some were even enjoyable. I.e. being rewarded for accessing chests/areas I'm pretty sure you're not able to access yet.- : IMO it kinda gets annoying after a while. I'm sure others like it because it fills in for pretty meaningless decision-making dialogue options. It's subjective. -  I found myself only needing to use like 2-3 of Loaf's weapons, but it felt rewarding to solve the puzzles to fit in as many weapons as I could at once. -  It's nothing special. Just your generic, collect "X" artifacts and defeat "Y" bad guy. With how pretty the game and characters were, I would've wished it was longer to flesh out the characters and plot more, but it's not bad. I do feel like there wasn't enough suspense building up to the climax and the end seemed pretty underwhelming in my opinion.-  There were times I'd accidentally go through dialogue too quickly and then the NPC wouldn't repeat any important directions and the quest log wouldn't help. A big example of this is . -  A lot of the partner-skill puzzles felt too easy, which is fine. However, . And it was disheartening to see how puzzles only kind of started making you think outside the box toward the end .-  I realize now that you can turn this feature off, but it would've been nice if the game told the player that (especially after falling off the map 3 times in a row just while walking toward the camera). If felt like there were so many pointless fall areas.-  This game was just way too easy overall, I didn't die once throughout my whole playthrough and never got stuck on any of the intended puzzles. If the game was meant to be a laid back/stress free game, then that's fine. But, it would've been nice to have a better story and developed cast of characters if that was the intention.

_childDocuments_.review: If you loved Bug Fables and the original Paper Mario games, you will love this. Buy it.The world is a gorgeous mashup of 3D and 2D, and absolutely stuck the landing. Fun, airy, light-hearted feeling, just as it should be. _childDocuments_.review: A super cute little RPG.Born of Bread tells the story of an average loaf of bread that mysteriously comes to life in the royal baker's kitchen one fateful evening. At the same time a gang of mysterious n'er-do-wells escape their magical prison and attack the Queen's castle in search of ancient artifacts known as the 'Sunstones'.Jester (the leader of the aforementioned n'er-do-wells) ends up destroying the castle, causing Loaf and his "father" Papa Baker to be subsequently blamed for the coincidence. Loaf and friends are tasked with exploring the royal kingdom to stop Jester and (hopefully) avoid the wrath of the vengeful Queen.If you've played Paper Mario (in particular The Thousand Year Door) then you know what to expect. This game isn't super hard, and each different ability you use typically demands a different sort of minigame (such as timed button presses) to execute properly. There are perks you can equip to give you special abilities, called Boons, and a simplified stat system that only comprises of Hit Points and two types of Magic Points for utilizing abilities and attacks. There is a colorful cast of characters, all of which have more interesting designs and personalities than Loaf himself, although this is probably by design to let Loaf be a blank slate.The art direction and writing is very quirky and there are some references hidden away for those who are keen enough to find them (such as Xian and Xue having homages to both Android 17 & 18 AND Jesse and James from Team Rocket) but it never gets in the way of the story or takes you out of the setting.All in all the RPG mechanics are enjoyable but the true charm of the game is in the story, art, and character interactions. If you're okay with playing an easy game with a lot of soul, this is definitely one for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I really liked Born of Bread but it was fighting me the whole time. The visuals and music are great, I really enjoyed the game artistically the whole way through. There was obviously a lot of love and care put into this game and I loved the character designs.They introduced really interesting systems but they never really got expanded on. I liked the inventory management minigame of your item choices being little tetris blocks, but those choices are tied to the elements system. I was really excited about the elements, but theres an illusion of choice here due to some being outright bad and some being game breaking. All of these are little gripes though! It didn't stop me from enjoying myself! My main complaint here is the amount of glitches I ran into playing the game that took me completely out of the game and left me frustrated. I think I encountered a soft lock in each zone of the game! Sometimes just with individual enemy types that would use a move then get stuck. Partners doing weird things and being dead when I've healed them. Most of them got a laugh out of me but after a certain point the game was fighting my enjoyment.It's a good game! But I wouldn't recommend it to my paper mario enjoying friends currently.edit: 10/28/24Just booted it up to see if the update had fixed the bugs. I usually don't replay games but the devs commented so I thought I'd look. I loaded up my old save and the first encounter I did had the same soft lock where I watched an enemy do a funny little dance when he used an ability for 5 minutes before I alt+f4'd again. Literally the same enemy I reported to the devs last time. For reference it was the final zone and I'm on PC. If you can overlook the glitches its a fun game.

_childDocuments_.review: Born of Bread is fully Baked, but just a little bit burnt. Burnt Bread never hurt anybody, it's just slightly unpleasant. Let me explain.Born of Bread has pretty good combat in comparison to the Paper Mario games it's inspired from, but there's massive amounts of Power Creep. Loaf is your main character and he needs to equip items in his backpack and each item has a different type of elemental damage. All of your party members have different elemental attacks that are supposed to supplement for the attacks Loaf doesn't have. This game has 5 Chapters, and the combat suffices until about half way through the game where you can find a weapon that is so broken it makes combat a joke.Enemies can have anywhere from 4-10 health, but the weapon you find that I mentioned earlier does anywhere between 12-16 damage. Even enemies that have resistances to that type of damage still die instantly to it. Also, enemies give loads of EXP, so you'll be leveling up every few battles. You can upgrade HP, WP ( Attacking costs WP ) and RP ( Specials cost RP ). You ONLY ever want to upgrade RP unless you feel like you're taking too much damage. All attacks on Loaf and Co. cost Will Power to use, so you always want to be attacking as much as possible. Items are a plenty in this game so you'll most likely have an overflowing inventory. ( Starting at 5 items in your bag and throughout the game can be upgraded to 20 ).At the end of each chapter, you unlock a Special Move, and I only ever used these a handful of times. Specials cost RP and can do stuff like a big attack or buff defense, but I never needed these ever because even before I got my OP weapons I was already doing enough damage. Bosses in the game are cool, but still a let down with their HP. A mini boss I fought had 30 HP, several of the chapter bosses had 50 HP and the final boss had 80 HP. These are fine numbers, until you realize that You have OP weapons and you kill everything in an instant. The Final Boss WAS NOT RESISTED to the OP weapon you get that I mentioned earlier, so he went down in a manner of minutes with no phase 2.Also, party members have HP like Loaf does, but enemies only attack whoever is in front in the turn order. I only ever had enemies attack my party member 2 or 3 times because Loaf was always in the front doing the most damage at all times, mostly 1 or 2 shotting everything in our path. Teammate HP felt completely unnecessary.All of this to say that I still highly recommend this game if you don't mind the mid combat. The entire game was a blast to play start to finish. The story felt engaging to me and the cast of characters was excellent. All of your party members have great designs and motivations for being with Loaf and by the end you all feel like a big happy family. Even if you don't PLAY this game, the OST is incredible and worth a listen!This game is an indie project and I had several bugs throughout my adventure. Even some that were said to be patched out in 3.0 still happened to me. I had nothing game breaking or softlocking happen to me and the bugs didn't deter me from having a good time. I'm a Streamer/YouTuber and was given a free Steam Key for this game. I still spoke my mind on what I thought were flaws and was not payed in the slightest. I know there's going to be a physical Switch Version and I want to buy that for myself since I enjoy having physical games on my shelf and I want to help support the team! If you DID want to see my own playthrough for entertainment or as a guide for possible secrets you missed, check out my playlist: Born of Bread can be compared to other similar projects like Bug Fables, which I've also done an 100% playthrough of. Both have their strengths and weaknesses. Personally I prefer the world of Bug Fables over Born of Bread, but BORN OF BREAD IS NOT A BAD GAME, JUST A DIFFERENT GAME. I hope despite the issues with Born of Bread's combat, you still play the game for the charming story and characters this world has!

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start this review with the negatives, which in my opinion are pretty universal and understandable. This game is pretty buggy. _childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game, and recommend it even at full price like i paid for it, but I can't pretend it dropped off hard after the first 3 chapters. This is a strong Paper Mario inspired RPG that has wit, likeable characters, engaging mechanics, fun music, and all the usual gubbins that one would want in a game. I'm giving this a rec, but for those buying I'd ask you take note of the following:1. Glitches for days. This game has a horrible amount of glitches, most that seem to be based on memory and loading issues. Sidequest chains break and you often can't interact with interactibles or even save points (!) if the game has been running too long in some levels. Restarting often fixes these, but my heart broke after 2 hours in one dungeon and the first save i found wouldn't let me interact with it.2. Rushed latter half. They probably run out of money or time, but chapter 4 onwards is basically a single area then a dungeon each. Story beats and RPG talk for NPC also stops changing after this time. One character who is a boss basically has nothing to them but is treated as a climax at the beginning and near end with nothing inbetween. It's disappointing, but it's really obvious that this is where deadlines or cash started hitting and sadly the game ended up suffering for it.3. Easy to break. Investment in sidequests breaks the difficulty with powerful weapons (Looking at you ember halberd) that make even the final boss a joke. Try to avoid them if you don't want to shoot through the game.4. Attack minigames are very hit and miss. Paper Mario style RPG fans know about this and sadly the game can suffer, so you'll probably avoid certain moves to avoid games too easy to fail or that take too long.I'm hoping patches and DLC helps fix some of these teething issues, because we have the best PMRPG outside of Bug Fables here and that only makes its weaknesses hit harder. Really hoping the dev puts out some new content and hoping their next game builds on this!

_childDocuments_.review: Ever since playing through bug fables, I have been looking for another paper Mario inspired fan game to sink hours into, and unfortunately, Born of Bread does not deliver.  Pros: Amazing visual art style, characters are all very cuteInteresting battle system, I wish it wasn’t so easy though. Actually funny in some areas. A lot of really good ideas for mini games and fights. Cons: Bugs galore, I got soft locked twice before I stopped playing, one was due to making a gamer jump too early, being unable to get back, the second was to accepting 2 escort quests at the same time, blocking my travel to different rooms. Wayyy to easy, enemies and bosses deal almost no damage, and there isn’t a way to up the numbers either. While the idea of how you use special attacks is cool, you can’t just slap a resident evil 1 style minigame and have it instantly be good, it’s just a glorified badge system, speaking of which…Medals are forgettable, and you can’t equip a lot at a time. Also you can just skip a mandatory fight in chapter 2 by accepting a quest…And worst of all, the one problem that cannot be fixed, bad writing. Characters that have never heard of or seen the antagonists are quick to point out their whereabouts, because you know who they are, and the protagonist is silent. TLDR: It has a lot of potential, wait for a few more patches, unfortunately I just can’t recommend born of bread right now, at least, not as a hardcore gamer. If you enjoy more casual games then you might like it, but for now, just stick with bug fables.Edit: This review is dated, I will try it again, the devs of this game clearly care a lot about it, as they have been giving it consistent updates throughout the months

_childDocuments_.review: If you are looking for a chill RPG in the style of Paper Mario, you should buy this game. The graphics and soundtrack are generally better than in similar games. All of the partners have compelling personalities and individual quests that help you get to know them better. During dialogue, an inactive partner might pop out o chime in if they have something they want to say, so if there's someone you prefer to use, you'll still hear from the other characters. Additionally, the dialogue is quite funny, which fits the general vibe of the game.I have a couple of gripes; the menu can be a bit annoying to navigate, and overall the game is a bit easy. However, my understanding is the devs are considering adding a hard mode, which would address that issue. I also experienced a soft-lock once during my playthrough, and lost 10-15 minutes of progress.Edit: The hard mode update has come out, and definitely adds a bit more challenge. It has caused me to use the defend command much more, which in turn caused me to realize that defending blocks all damage if you time the block correctly.

_childDocuments_.review: Everything that bug fables promised to be and wasn't. A few weird audio bugs/glitches on my 3080, and chapter 2 is a bit of an unbalanced mess. When this game succeeds though, it gives that Paper mario vibe I've been looking for. I do dig it, and for whatever reasons games of this genre traditionally have terrible chapters 2s as far as balancing. Outside of that, I am having fun. It's not so much that I want to put bug fables down, as they just got a lot wrong with that game. Especially the 30 stage final boss for reasons of absolute nonsense. This got about 85% of it right for what they were going for.

_childDocuments_.review: First and foremost, if you are a Paper Mario fan, then you will most likely enjoy this game, and I recommend you try it. If you haven’t played paper, Mario, but you enjoy RPG with fun secrets to uncover, then I would still recommend it. HOWEVER I gotta be honest, it is far from perfect. I have encountered so many bugs. It’s kind of hilarious this year amount of them I ran into. Thankfully, the grand majority of them were not getting breaking. I did get soft locked once though. my tip is to save as often as possible to mitigate any possible hiccups.

_childDocuments_.review: I beat it and... it's so damn buggy. Don't bother going for 100%, it's currently impossible and my 20+ hour save is locked in that state forever. This game rides off of art really hard. Gameplay is super basic. Some thoughts:-It feels like his game was never playtested because just one casual playthrough would show you so many issues.-Menu is the real villain of this game. It just plain sucks. -You have so many attacks and weapons in this game yet all of them use one of 3 mechanics that are super basic and boring. They try to make it more complex by introducing like 10 types of dmg but it really doesn't matter.-There is 0 balance, and you'll end up fighting 1-2 enemies the entire game. Some enemies can combo you while others are so easy that I've never seen them attack once because I wiped them turn one. Usually, the easy ones give you more exp.-At times there's too much dialogue and characters exist in multiple places all at once (with the exact same dialogue they had 20 hours ago, while their version in a different place says something new, it's bizarre).-Some achievements are just straight up bugged, and I couldn't find any info online how to even get the blue blessing-Special skills are pretty pointless, I never bothered to use them or add lvl up points to them.If you like numbers:Art 10/10Music 8.5/10 (not the same as the sound design, on that one they dropped the ball, some things don't make a sound at all, but they should since they are required to progress, or things give you negative sound like you've dismissed something)Battle gameplay: 3/10Overworld gameplay 7/10Menu 0.5/10Story: 6/10 (pretty generic but the characters are fun)I invested 20+ hours into that game because I was trying to 100% it and didn't know it's still bugged. Multiple achievements are bugged. -3 for that because some bugs are so apparent that it genuinely feels like any playtesting would find them out. It's still positive because besides all that it's still an OK experience and will be pretty good once they fix everything. Addendum: I still struggle to see what Lint learned in his quest. The only thing to learn was that  Well, I guess that is still worth getting some compensation... Overall most of these lessons are pretty weak or backwards
_childDocuments_.name: Born of Bread

_childDocuments_.review: What a delightful game! Positives first: I loved the artstyle and music. You can tell the designers put a ton of love into designing all the characters and environments. The game simply looks gorgeous. Every character looks great, even random NPCs. It's just wonderful to see such attention to detail. The music was fantastic: There were so many times that I would just stand around a listen to the music before moving on to the next area. The composer deserves all the praise in the world. Combat is fun too, but it's way too easy most of the time. That's one of the things I found negative. Some challenge would be nice. Also, I found quite a few bugs, even in the 3.0 patch. I'm sure they will be fixed eventually though. Lastly, the ending part of the game seemed rushed, but it was still a fun game overall. Can't wait to see what they'll cook up next!
_childDocuments_.name: Born of Bread

_childDocuments_.review: Nothing impresses me more than an honest attempt made with heart. Born of Bread is a compelling and well designed homage to party based games like ff6 and the Paper Mario franchise. While it is obviously A love letter to TTYD, don't look over this little gem as a mere copy; with it's customization, unique locations/world building, and much more overtly humorous tone, it got me hooked as soon as I saw a friend playing it. - Pros - A fun, light hearted, romp through an interconnected world in the vein of Paper Mario Each char has a unique and interesting characterization. Characters and animations are smooth.All char's remain naritivly strong through the entire story. (especially lint) You are given plenty of time and reason to empathize with all sides in the conflict. You can pet everything (but if you bonk them, they answer in kind) - Cons - Bugs LOTS of bugsSome quests can be a little vague - sometimes you won't know if a quest bugged or if you're misunderstanding the quest prompt.The characters feel stilted in terms of power. When you get a new char, there's little reason to go back to A previous ally unless you're just looking for their unique personality.
_childDocuments_.name: Born of Bread

_childDocuments_.review: Born of Bread is a lovingly made game chasing the classic Paper Mario experience. There is so much to like about the presentation, music, humour and storytelling. Born of Bread also attempts to improve on the foundation laid by Paper Mario in it's own way.  The cracks start to show further into the game when a handful of later side-quests are uncompletable, issues with the menus, and combat not functioning the way it ought to.At time of writing developers have addressed the completion of some of the sidequests i observed a problem with, having bought the game on release I'm glad to see the game is going in the right direction.There is still more to be done for combat and menus, it's odd seeing a game with such polished presentation and production fall short with game logic.  My experience overall was still good but these issues drag it down from being a truly great and memorable game.In summary, if you cherished the first two Paper Mario games like many of us do, your still going to want to buy it, I'm happy with my purchase.If your coming into this game without nostalgia for Paper Mario I would hold off until there is more evidence of fixes, and even a discount.TL;DR Good game, Perhaps the most obvious bread pun is sadly the most fitting one, "Needs more time in the oven".
_childDocuments_.name: Born of Bread

_childDocuments_.review: I'm of 2 minds about it.... the humor and the art style and the world building are all great, it' s just a shame that the gameplay seems to be lagging behind. I wouldn't call it a bad game, but it is riddled with bugs, some that have since been patched out, but a lot of them are still in. Things like enemies always attacking Loaf, no matter if you switch to your partner making partner HP feel almost useless. Multiple side quests don't load properly or interfere with each other. There are 2 in royal town that required talking to Papa baker, yet even after completing the first one the dialogue for that same quest would play on a loop until I exited royal town and walked back in to finally be able to complete the other quests. There was one that required me to talk to 3 pirates and then go back to the quest giver to complete it, except talking to the original quest giver made the intro the quest play again, and it kept looping until again I exited the area and loaded it back in, I had many instances where my controller stopped registering in the menu and instead detected my mouse even though  my hands went nowhere near it. None of those are necessarily deal breakers, but it did make the experience a lot more frustrating than it needed to be. If you like paper Mario I would definitely recommend this as the inspiration is clear, but if you are just looking for the next RPG to play I would look at this one with a lot of caveats
_childDocuments_.name: Born of Bread

_childDocuments_.review: As a big fan of Paper Mario on the N64 and GC i was super happy to see another game that takes inspiration from it. I had a really good time with this game, it captures the humor of the Paper Mario games, the exploration felt great and it was fun to discover various pop culture references. While the game is not super challenging, the combat has some depths to it with strength and weaknesses. The story has a nice touch to it and while it uses certain tropes, it had a charming effect till the end. Like always, the journey is the reward. Only downside for me were quality of life things like the menus or rearranging stuff, but as far as i know, the devs are super attentive and already work on various balancing changes. If you want to see more about the game, i actually made a review about the game  so check it out if you are interested. Can definitely recommend the game and the price is more than just fair. Thank you for the great game guys!

_childDocuments_.review: Before I get into the nitty-gritty of my review, let me just state that although I recommend this game, I'm rating it a 7.5/10. The game is a lovely and fun experience, but give it some time so the devs can polish it some more.If you are looking for another Paper Mario spiritual successor, then this has hit the nail on the head (I personally have had Born of Bread on my wishlist for at LEAST 3 years now [I've lived in three separate apartments while waiting for this game!]). All that being said, I think Born of Bread needed a bit more time in the oven to get that 10 star rating from me personally. There is a LOT of heart put into this game, and it looks gorgeous, sounds gorgeous, but it unfortunately doesn't play gorgeous. I don't know if it was due to a publishing deal and a set release date for Holiday Q2023, but there are so many bugs and QoL features that are just... absent. On PC, there is no keybinding / controller binding. Before patch 3.0, I actually had to quit the game on multiple occasions because I couldn't swap my weapons around (thank you for fixing that). The devs are clearly hard at work fixing a lot of the problems that are present on launch which is much appreciated, I just want you, the reviewee(?) to know what you're getting into here.Regarding QoL, to swap between partners, you have to open the menu, navigate to the partner tab, then switch partner. Same goes for using your inventory items. Both of these problems could be solved with a hotkey button for items / partners, pulling up a smaller inventory UI list. The fast travel only unlocks around halfway through the game, so if you're trying to be completionist about quests then tough luck, have fun walking. Speaking of quests, it is a SLOG. The only saving grace for the quests is that the total amount for one area is marked once you get there. Otherwise, you will have to scour the entire area at multiple points during the story to try and find every quest. I did this, and the rewards ARE worth it, but since they're no guides at this point, it is a very time consuming process.I also want to make a quick comment about Chapter 3? 4? Bad memory, apologies. The winter cottage level. Let it be said that this is my favorite location in the entire game to explore, but the progression design? Not ideal. For it being a house, there are a lot of deadends and fetch quests that have you navigating the entire house back and forth multiple times. Sometimes hidden paths open up, and you're like "woah! maybe this will give me a shortcut!" but not quite. Anytime you need to get to the laundry room for instance, you have to go through 4 other rooms at LEAST to get there. It's just loop after loop, and it loses the wonder of being in a mysterious house with secret passages, you know? Another thing I want to mention is the map. The map is pretty useless imo -- yes, I can view major areas, where I am, and what smaller areas are there, but that's all it's used for. Some people in the forums have discussed fast travel through it, but I don't think that's necessary. It'd be great, yeah, but then you have to tie narrative into it. I wish that there would be more map markers however; something to show where I found a chest or a lizard guy. Or, maybe let the player place these markers themselves, so they can remember where they might need to backtrack to later?Okay these last two paragraphs don't really count as review, oops. I think the characters work very well for the setting and story the devs are trying to tell: I don't know if it was INTENTIONAL that they're kinda stereotypical and one-note, but the world is a fairy tale and that is exactly the vibe I would expect from a fairy tale. Performance is great (I have a crappy laptop and it still runs well). I play a lot of Paper Mario alikes and this gives me the closest vibes to it, though Bug Fables will always have a special place in my heart. The combat is fun yet formulaic, as is to be expected from a Paper Mario RPG alika; action commands do their thing, nothing new shakes up the formula there. Do well in the commands and your audience watching will reward you for it, flub and they'll leave your stream. Otherwise, it's just some added flavor.At the end of the day, this is a fantastic game but it just needs some time to simmer and rest. Personally I play it for a few days, give it a rest until there's a patch, and repeat the process. So, if you're a fan of Paper Mario games and can not WAIT to play another, then this is for you. If you have a bit of patience, I say wait for a few more months until the devs don't have to be dealing with some horrendous bugs.Thank you Born of Bread devs! I'm a game designer who's just about to graduate college and it's been a lovely experience playing your game, just needed to put it all out there for others to see as well :)

_childDocuments_.review: I never got to experience Paper Mario as a kid growing up, however, this definitely feels like an homage to that game! It has been truly a treat to play and stream--I do all sorts of silly voices for all the characters, which there are quite a lot. There are puns, though as one who fancies that sort of thing I don't mind it at all. The camera can be finicky at times, and there has been an occasional glitch out where I could see through a wall, but that is fine by me. The music is fitting for each of the different "bio-mes" or "areas". And the story is great thus far!All in all, I've been very happy with my purchase of this game! Kudos to the developers!

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the most 7/10 game I've ever played, that unfortunately is plagued by enough small (to occasional large) issues to make it a 6/10 at best.It does very well at overall presentation in most areas; things tend to look nice, and the setting and characters are largely original and creative. Combat is simple, which isn't a bad thing inherently, but it rarely challenges. The semi-borrowed audience system from TTYD is well implemented in an enjoyable way.Or at least that's what I would say if it all worked consistently. Throughout the game you're likely to come across enough small bugs that add up over time to sour parts of the experience. If you're too cavalier with your movement and button presses, you may accidentally shove yourself into a soft-lock situation. At some point in my playthrough I managed to somehow glitch the audience system to where they would hate if I did anything but a basic attack. At the very least I think I bugged it. There's seemingly no way to get information on the games systems (besides damage types, one of which I never even encountered an enemy who was weak to) beyond the basic information that's given upon first being introduced. The most egregious of bugs I encountered completely locked me out of completing at least 1 partner's main sidequest. By the end of the game I didn't bother to go and tie up any loose ends because I had no way of knowing the line between things I was missing or things the game broke without me noticing.Even still, aside from a few strange choices in presentation (general camera angle, often inconvenient text box position, lack of dynamic integration in many pieces of music and sound effects), the game underneath the bugs is still overall enjoyable.It's not wholly engaging enough as a story for me to recommend it to anyone but the people trying to fill a paper mario-shaped void in their library; but to those people, consider it a recommendation with an asterisk. If a good amount of the bugs every get fixed I'd recommend it fully in a heart beat. If those bugs do end up getting fixed though; This is probably the best paper mario like I've played so far.
_childDocuments_.name: Born of Bread

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun and quirky and enjoyable! Fans of Paper Mario will be right at home with Born of Bread, and I can very easily recommend it.. though considering I bought it while it was 10% off, I can't verify if it deserves the price it's going for nowadays, given a noticeable amount of bugs and technical issues, including a major side quest for one of your party members just bugging out at the end and you don't get to have his ultimate ability.They're not enough to ruin the game for me, but they are enough for me to say you should wait for a sale or for a patch to address these issues, whichever comes first.EDIT: As of yesterday, the 3.0 patch came out that fixed the issues I mentioned and alluded to. I can now safely recommend this game! Play it! It's cute.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm genuinely in love with this game so far! I'm pulled back to my teenage years, where I fell in love with RPGs because of Paper Mario TTYD. The combat system requires you to stay engaged, meaning that it's hard to get bored of it quickly. The world is fun to explore, and the game isn't afraid to let you make mistakes(i.e. falling into water when there are clearly "No swimming" signs haha)The game has made me laugh out loud a few times already, especially the loveable Dub. _childDocuments_.review: A delightful game full of charm, and a great take on Paper Mario's formula. The presentation is the most impressive thing here - the facial expressions on the characters are so...well, expressive! I love the wacky characters you recruit into your team, and the music is also a big highlight of my experience. Combat starts out really fun - I love the weapons' system, and action commands will always be a must for me when it comes to turn-based RPGs. Sadly, though, apart from enemy type weaknesses, there's not really much strategy involved when it comes to fights. You either stomp your opponent or they stomp you and you have to eat some food before attacking again. Not being able to swap your turn with your partner seems like a huge oversight, and I wish you weren't penalized for it. Overall I just wish there was a liiiiitle more strategy involved. Unfortunately, as I played a pre-release version of the game, there were a lot of bugs that interfered with my enjoyment of the game. But even despite this, I had a great time seeing a new take on the tried-and-true formula. For classic Paper Mario fans, I give Born of Bread my full recommendation  - don't pass on this one! Same goes for Bug Fables.You can check out my full review HERE:

_childDocuments_.review: I will say without a doubt, this is a fun game.  It's well written.  There ARE some very annoying bugs (like the cursor on a menu disappearing), however, I have no doubt in my mind the dev will fix them.  This is a game baked with love, just needs a little more QA time in the oven.  It's still playable and an 8/10 experience so far in this state.  My one gripe is that this game doesn't have gamecube controller friendly menus, so I had to rebind left bumper to a D pad button, which makes things a little odd.  They used gamecube controllers in the promo so I figured it'd be fine to use them, but just keep in mind you will have to rebind for it if you are using Delfinovin.Will update this when I beat the game for a more in depth review.

name: Killer Klowns from Outer Space: The Game
detailed_description: Digital Deluxe Content Digital Deluxe Content Includes: 2 Human Characters (Mike & Debbie) 2 Klown Skins (Fryzo & Sundaze) 1 Movie Klown Skin (Bibbo) Digital Soundtrack Digital Art Book About the Game Killer Klowns from Outer Space: The Game is an asymmetrical multiplayer horror based on the iconic ‘80s film. In the battle between Killer Klowns and citizens of Crescent Cove, team up and use your wits to harvest humans or save them from the alien invasion! Take on the role of the iconic Killer Klowns – cooperate in a team of three players, utilize unworldly abilities, hunt humans with zany weapons, and plan your alien invasion to harvest the population of Crescent Cove successfully. Fight back as a team of seven brave citizens of Crescent Cove – explore the city for valuable loot and weapons, avoid getting captured by Klowns, and try to survive the alien invasion. Crescent Cove is a sprawling arena for these unique multiplier fights between Klowns and humans – boasting various locations, and various tactical opportunities for both teams. Killer Klowns from Outer Space: The Game provides a unique approach to hide-and-seek gameplay, customization, PvPvE, and dynamic objectives leading to multiple match results. This game evolves the online horror formula in new ways.

_childDocuments_.review: Good:-This game is very faithful to the movie it is based on. Chances are if you liked the movie, you will enjoy this game. -Proximity chat makes for really funny encounters in game. -Aesthetic and art style stays true to the original Killer Klowns movie, and is nice to look at.-The maps are pretty cool and are also nice to look at.-Probably the first time I've seen an asym that is well balanced at launch, spare for a broken weapon or two on the Klown side.-This game rewards genuine teamwork on both teams; if you are used to DBD or F13, do not expect to easily take on multiple Humans at once as Klown. The humans can and will fight back.-It's a very casual and fun game, does not feel like a pure sweatfest, like what other asyms (ahem DBD) have become.Bad:-The objectives for either side are not communicated very well at all. The tutorial is just a series of images along with text. -There isn't much in terms of progression; you just unlock new cosmetics and characters, said characters not being very different from each other. Cosmetic options are also very limited.-What certain items or mechanics do isn't communicated well either.-Nearly a month after release it still has significant bugs.-A little pricey for what it is.This game is fun for what it is. But sadly the long term lifespan of this game doesn't look too good, from a combination of it being a game centered around a niche IP and Illfonic having a track record of mismanaging their games. Regardless, still very fun to play, would recommend before it dies in a year or two.

_childDocuments_.review: The Game is hell of fun and the ambience, graphics, colours and horror ambience is fantastic. I never thought the game would be that much amazing and beautiful. You nailed the art. Is to sun to ask for nerfs or buffs but:PLAYING AS A KLOWN: In my opinion I think is less frustrating playing as a Klown than as a survivor.  As a killer my only complain is when you play against 3 or 4 survivors at the same time. Is impossible to do anything. They play together you are done! You will die over and over. There should be a perk that when you are attacked by 2 or more survivors you should increase the movement speed to run away and take less damage or else is pointless . You will lose over and over. Also when you are being hitting by a bunch of survivores is very hard to run away. Sometimes I click run and the killer doesn´t run...PLAYING AS A SURVIVORPlaying as a survivor is very hard for me. The combat is very hard to me. I can´t control very well the hits. And running away is very hard when you are being hit constantly(SAME AS BEING KLOWN). You need to click run a lot of times to make the character really running.  Also my ping of 90 doesn´t help either. I think you guys should make better collisions and better combat interactions between the killer and the survivor. Sometimes is very hard to know what is going on. Another suggestions:- Make better interactions with doors(is very hard to close or open them when you are running from the klown or going after survivors. - You could add some dynamic weather(rain, storm, wind)- Maybe add a perk system (example: when you are chased by 2 or 3 clowns your movement speed increases so it doesn´t feel to much frustrating to play 1 vs 3 and make more "fair play")- Add more skins( this suggestion you already know) and I think you will add in the future- add more ambience sounds(birds, crickets and etc) to make more alive the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Killer Klowns from Outer Space is an interesting game, it borrows from ideas that have come from other titles in the genre. _childDocuments_.review: First of all - you have to watch the film. I didn't know it before and it's crazy!!! That movie made me really excited about the game. And anyone who knows the film also understands the game in a completely different way.The game itself takes a few rounds of play to get used to and to understand. Then it's just brilliant. Similar to F13, every round is different as every player plays differently. There are so many variations of what you can do and how - both solo and in a team.I think it's very good that you don't choose whether you play clown or human, everyone has to do both and it prevents people from only playing one and then complaining that one side is so much stronger than the other. It isn't!Also awesome if you're covered in cotton candy you can be freed for a while and if you die you can be revived. What's really good is that there are mini-games that you can play when you're dead to help the other survivors till you get revived or the round ends. So it's fun to stay in until the end.Overall a 10/10, the humor and the game structure are just great. Exits and items are always somewhere different - there is always something new and the game captivates me more with every round. Unlike TCM, there is no way to troll others. Trolling people only spoils the fun of the game and that's a very clever solution here. There is simply no way to troll. Very cleverly solved!In contrast to F13 and TCM, the game is playable in this early state - I've only had 1 bug in the 3 hours so far. The only thing that's a bit stupid is the menu where you customize your character. Could be better. But here it's a + again because you can completely customize the character - I think that's great.I'm excited to see how the updates turn out, so far I'm super happy with this game!!! The developers have definitely learned from old mistakes 👍

_childDocuments_.review: The only thing that makes this game unique is that it makes use of the killer klowns from outer space ip, literally the rest of the games aspects are undercooked, not well thought out and or outright horrible. _childDocuments_.review: This price alone is killing the game. Maximum $25 should not be more than that. _childDocuments_.review: In terms of graphics and visuals, the game is excellent.
