_childDocuments_.review: Honestly? It's pretty terrible. To get the worst out of the way first, yes, a lot of things that were talked about back when we were getting teaser streams isn't here, and a crucial element that sounded like it was in there, isn't here, and makes matches pretty hit or miss.The mechanic in question is the scrapped Loot Chance mechanic, replaced with RNG spawns, which... Let me put it this way: You can spawn next to an Escape with both items next to you, instantly leaving before anything can happen, or you can wander around the whole map FOR THE ENTIRE MATCH finding only Burgers, Weapons, and Tennis Balls. Had the Random Chance mechanic been in there, there probably would have been some degree of a Guaranteed Drop so that if there were less boxes left in the match, you might have gotten one of the escape items for the REMAINING escapes, but, alas. 5 security keycards and 1 gas can, not a spark plug or key in sight type beat, every damn time......immediately following that is the combat... Or should I say, Stun-and-kill or Run. This amazingly applies to both sides, but Humans definitely have it easier by way of having guns that actually deal health damage vs the Klown's Cottonizers that do 0 damage and have a HARSH regression timer and amount on their meter. Hell, the charges and swap-speed BS isn't even needed on most Klown weapons, Humans on their own can just break every single line of sight with their massive sprintbars, which has kinda led to the permanent meta: If human with Gun + Knife and/or Melee + sharp , get an airhorn as fast as possible and bully the Klown, otherwise just sprint the length of the entire map and tbag as the klowns literally cannot catch up with you and have to Klown Jump to get over there reliably. (Except no Klown does this, except me. There's a scoring event for it, it is MEANT to be a possibility, it's just... nobody does it.) If Klown, equip the Jawbreaker Flail once you unlock it and then use basically nothing else because the meta is to just klowntality everyone like this is a deathmatch, but not if you're alone because that'll get you killed, which leads us into the pointless mechanics......Next up's the minigames, Hand of Fate, and Revive Machine. It's still all useless even post revive-card-chance. Again, recall that even if you get revived, you need those Key Items to escape, and since everyone probably already used them, or they're in a single crate somewhere on the vast map, this really just ends up elongating the match and making people want to just do combat with the klowns instead of, you know, doing the objective of escaping. As a bonus negative, people typically die once and then leave instantly, not even bothering to stay and do minigames, which, as you might imagine, further foils the whole idea of reviving anyone at all.Oh right. People... and Proximity chat. Well. Imagine, if you will, DBD but people have voicechat always on. That's the experience here. You'll get yelled at, people will attract clowns over to you intentionally, you'll be cussed at for minor mistakes, people will even just get you false-reported on a whim. I've only been able to partially enjoy the game once it was turned the ♥♥♥♥ off. Oh, and they can stop matches from ever starting if they decide to just not ready up, so you can sit there for upwards of 20 minutes just because they refuse to press their ready button.Thus, in the end, we have the remains of a game that had completely different planned mechanics, scrapped into a game that rewards bullying on both sides, where everyone's as toxic as in DBD (Just Leave is also a meme in this one aswell) and, oh right. It costs $40.Hard pass.

_childDocuments_.review: Good game and has potential to be a decent party game, compared to TCM and F13th.Major issues -Spawning problems: Humans spawning too close to the clowns, making the game unfair and unbalanced.Rushed launch: The game was released prematurely, with many bugs that could have been addressed with a short delay.Skill check problems: Even when skill checks are executed correctly, they sometimes fail, alerting the clowns and disrupting the game.Overpowered Klowns: Some weapons and melee attacks of the clowns are too powerful, making the game unbalanced.No-clipping/glitching: There are too many to list, here are a small few - unable to pick up items as a human, noclipping under maps, hit registration is terrible at times.Suggestions for ImprovementImplement patches to address the critical bugs that affect gameplay. Focus on fixing spawning issues and skill check accuracy.Balancing:Re-balance the Klown weapons and melee attacks to ensure a fairer gameplay experience. Ensure no single weapon can overpower players too easily.Improved Spawning Mechanics:Adjust the spawning system to ensure humans and clowns spawn at appropriate distances, preventing unfair advantages.Player Engagement:Encourage more active gameplay from teammates by possibly adding incentives for cooperative actions and penalties for non-participation.Community Feedback:Engage with the player community to gather feedback and address the most critical issues. Regular updates and transparent communication can help rebuild trust. Currently, there is no platform to report bugs. Post-Launch Support:Provide robust post-launch support with frequent updates to address ongoing issues and improve the overall experience.Overall, this game has the potential to be a lot of fun, and I do enjoy it when I occasionally get a bug-free round. Despite the issues, I still give this game a thumbs up because Killer Klowns from Outer Space is an amazing film and a great addition to the asymmetrical horror genre. I recommend purchasing this game after the official release, so you can start playing when the game-breaking bugs have been fixed.

_childDocuments_.review: Killer Klowns from Outer Space: The Game is as wacky and crazy as the name sounds and just as wild and goofy to play. Killer Klowns is a fresh and exciting take on the asymmetrical horror experience. The over the top presentation of the game is excellent, the 1980's vibe is highlighted throughout the game and creates a rich and playful atmosphere. I recently watched the movie for the first time (great btw) in preparation for this review and I was happy to see the game draws heavily on the film. From the outfits to the props and even kill animations, all mimic the cult classic horror movie which adds even more nostalgia to the mix. The matches are wild and chaotic, there are plenty of laughs and thrills to be had, especially when playing with friends. The team composition is 3 Klowns and 7 Humans which provides plenty of opportunity for mayhem. Escaping as a human is challenging but not overly difficult. Playing as a Klown is a joy, but dont let their looks fool you. They are mean, powerful, and there is a variety of funky classes to choose from. All have crazy outer worldly abilities and weapons, like a popcorn gun or walking balloon dog for example, at your disposal to chase and hunt down the humans. I also appreciated the fact that the human team has a fighting chance when encountering a Klown compared to other games. Shotguns, pistols, and baseball bats, are some of the weapons you can use to pop a clowns nose and send them packing. Unlockable classes and abilities help replayability and there are a lot of cosmetics to collect. However after 25 hours I did feel a lack of variety and repetitiveness in the core gameplay. Some aspects like carrying a cocoon back to the ship and chasing humans felt more laboursome than I would of liked,  and escaping as a human felt easy at times. There are mini games you can play as a human when you are killed to help your teammates who are still alive to keep you engaged however it was not enough to keep me totally hooked and dying to come back to the game.The graphics and silly effects are pleasing to the eye with good lighting and character/environment detail. The Klowns look very detailed and creepy, a highlight of the game. There is a decent selection of maps all of which are fun to play on. The online community has dropped heavily since release, though you can still find matches fairly easily and you can also play custom matches with friends. Overall Killer Klowns is a crazy, exciting, and welcomed addition to the genre. A truly memorable game and one I enjoyed my time playing. It is hard not to smile while playing and definitely worth checking out for its price even though it can become repetitive after awhile.

_childDocuments_.review: The game just isn't it at the moment. I've played basically all of the asymmetrical horror games and Killer Klowns seems to be the worst of the bunch so far. It appears to have some of the worst balancing of all the asym horror games that I've played. It usually takes at least a couple of weeks for survivors/victims to start bullying the killers in these games, however, the Klowns are getting bullied right on the gate. The survivors can basically take the role of the killers and hunt down the Klowns in a group if they group up and choose to do so. I've experienced and seen the survivors hunting down the Klowns in groups on multiple different occasions. Once these asym games become killer bullying simulators they are always miserable to play for both sides and this game is presenting with that right out of the gate. Klown gameplay in general just isn’t very engaging if I am being honest. You are way too slow and don’t get  nearly enough stamina. The humans however get endless amounts of items to reset their stamina meter so Klown gameplay basically becomes this endless cat-and-mouse game. Fights are basically decided on the victim’s terms. If you end up catching up to a human it’s because they allowed you to because they want to try and fight you. Killer Klowns also doesn't allow you to choose which role you want to play. So if you want to be a killer only player that simply isn't in the cards.I am not a fan of this and this is a massive mistake in my opinion. People will just lobby dodge if they don't get the role they desire to play. I don't understand how this was overlooked as a problem. I've already seen multiple people leaving lobbies instantly and I presume it is because they didn't get the role they want.  Just allow me to choose which role I want to play. It works just fine in both Dead by Daylight and Texas Chainsaw Also, the game is just overpriced for the amount of polish it has. At least with Texas Chainsaw or Evil Dead, which were two asym horror games that also charged $40 right out the gate, they appeared to have high production value and polish to help warrant the cost of $40 to some degree. Killer Klowns on the other hand just looks very indy and cheap. There are endless amounts of wonky-looking and bugged animations. And if people managed to find Evil Dead and Texas Chainsaw that were much more polished out the gate overpriced, things certainly aren't going to bode well for Killer Klowns in that department.The game isn't the worst thing in the world by any means. It just doesn't seem to be worth the asking price of $40. Plenty of balancing needs to be done before I consider playing this game again. This is one of those wait and see types of games. Wait for a sale and see if they improve the balance later down the road. I'll be requesting a refund.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a bit of an asym vet, played everything from AvP to DBD. I like asym games, they are fun, promote interesting play styles, teamwork, and an ever evolving meta. They require good game knowledge, mechanical skill, and the ability to adapt on the fly. Killer Klowns falls a bit flat so far with some of these things, though it is early days yet.First, the maps are a bit all over the place. Their size and composition differ massively, and some maps have areas where the human is guaranteed to waste a lot of a Klown's time, some have areas where a human is nigh impossible to spot, some have huge dead zones where a human is liable to be run down in no time, and some have some seriously awkward collision in spots, like second floors some Klowns cannot access, or wonky hitboxes that block projectiles.In terms of mechanical skill, Klown weapons all handle very differently, and require their own approaches to master. The heavier hitters have been reigned in a bit (Bouncecaster and Popcorn Bazooka in particular) which bodes well for the longevity of the game, but nothing excepting perhaps the Laser Beamer feels totally useless. You're gonna have to mix and match your weapons with a plan in mind to get use out of them. The Klowns themselves need work, and a couple feel a bit redundant (Rudy and Chubby). But there's enough variety in the Klown tricks and weapons to eke out interesting builds. Humans are far more straightforward, with the archetype system not yet being functional (all humans default to the Athletic archetype as of now). All you gotta know as a human is save your sharp weapons for kills and cocoon escapes, guns are for when it gets a bit heated. Energy drinks are when you're in some trouble and need to leg it. Bricks are good for stuns. Turn on distractions to mess with Klowns. Use vaults to create distance and generate a stamina advantage. Maybe you wanna hide in a box. Maybe not.Klown game play is a mixed bag. Supposedly the early game is for Klowns to cocoon and late game is for them to execute humans, with endgame (the 15 minute mark) being the Klownpocalypse during which every remaining human who does not escape is killed. But cocooning despite a negligible CD reduction and the spawning of honestly rather useless minions feels like a risk early game, and pointless late game whenever the humans have access to sharp weapons. The most direct route a Klown can take, is to rush, execute, and camp the resurrection machine, which is not very fun. Klown lackeys and the CD reduction needs work to make it more worthwhile. EDIT: I almost forgot. If you hook 16 cocoons, you'll trigger an early Klownpocalypse. I forgot to mention it because this almost never happens during normal play. Human game play right now tends to favour particular escapes over other escapes. There are five possible escapes, and I've only seen the more difficult ones achieved a handful of times. The most common will be boat, and gate, as they're the easiest. I've managed to escape via boat in the first two minutes of a match due to the less than airtight escape item RNG. This isn't necessarily an advantage as Klowns learn this and patrol those areas most often. The RNG of this game and the fact humans right now aren't super coordinated means those more difficult escapes are going to seem nigh impossible in the endgame. One interesting thing is how when you escape or die, you can play mini games to help your teammates out.One big problem that affects both sides is the lack of a DC penalty, or a lobby cap after the game starts. Let's say little Bobby is not having a good time. He's got crap item RNG, and two Klowns have cornered him in a dead zone. Little Bob DCs. Oh no. So sad. This means the Klowns have wasted their time chasing Little Bob, only for Little Rob to come in immediately after. Little Rob, spawning in halfway through the match to take Bob's spot, finds all the items have been looted, all his teammates are dead, the map is full of Lackeys, and the Klowns have all the more attention to focus on him. Little Rob DCs. Cycle repeats. Fix that devs. Earlier the better.This game has a few other issues. As I stated earlier this game has missing features; human archetypes are not fully functional at the minute, challenges are hit and miss as to regards whether they're registered, there's a few bugs with weapon swapping, Klowns are missing one of their tricks (think like a perk or activated ability), lots of little things like that. None really annoy me too much personally.Now all that's out of the way I want to talk about what I like about this game. The first, as a Killer Klowns fan, is the aesthetic. It is spot on. They nailed it. Not only do they have the original composer for the score, but the Klowns themselves are wonderfully realised from their original movie incarnation. They radiate an inane blend of whimsicality and malice, so much more than the effects budget of the movie allowed. This game is replete with references to the movie, in the form of game play mechanics, sound and environmental design. The human and Klown customisation options are all references to the movie, and they've been painstakingly recreated. Even better, you can mix and match them, and no matter what you make it looks like it could fit in the background as an extra. Those aforementioned mini games are just super retro 80s arcade, from the music to the sound effects. Everything just fits. The aesthetic has been nailed.When this all comes together it's just great. I have not yet managed to get bored of the chase theme as my technicolor Klown advances on some hapless geek armed with nothing but a tennis ball and a stick. All the comedic sound effects that come with my punk sneaking up on a Klown, blasting him in the face. knifing him in the nose, and then insulting him as he disappears into a green flash. And whether I'm on the giving or receiving end of a Klowntality, it just somehow does not cease to amuse.Yeah this game has a lot of dumb issues. They've been good at addressing them thus far. As far as an asym goes, it definitely is one. And not only that, it's a Klown themed one. It scratches the 80s itch, and it's entertaining to play. If you like the sound of that, get it.

_childDocuments_.review: Hear me out. This game has it's fun moments but there's still a lot that needs improving on, whether playing as a survivor or as a clown. I've played a lot of Friday The 13th, Dead By Daylight and Texas Chainsaw Massacre. Killer Klowns takes bits and pieces from these but it doesn't seem to come together all that well. I'll put a few things that bothered me and cross my fingers that these get fixed or tweaked in the future. I love the graphics and how everything looks. From the environment to the characters but there's a lot of work that needs to be done.- As a survivor, you can easily escape within a few minutes. But then you're FORCED to spectate the rest of a match otherwise you don't gain anything, in which case you can't level up. - As a clown, you're so incredibly slow that survivors are able to outrun you with ease. Unless they stop to fight you by choice or you and the other clowns surround them, it's nothing but a footrace. - Another big issue, at least for me, is that you aren't able to choose whether or not you play as a clown or a survivor. It's randomized every match. I dislike that very much. Why you aren't given the ability to choose, I'll never understand. The game feels like one giant free for all if you're trying to escape. Everyone seems to be out for themselves. As a clown, it's pretty simple. Find a survivor and kill them. To be able to escape within 3 minutes of a match starting is ridiculous. There should be some measures put into place that make the match last longer. I really hope that these issues get tweaked. This game doesn't feel challenging at all. In one match, I spawned in an area where I was able to get an axe, and 2 spark plugs, along with a key. I made it out of the game in a good 3 minutes.

_childDocuments_.review: I found out about this game by chance and had no illusions about the quality of the game. I had a lot of doubts. The stream from the developers appeared very late and they said that this was a pre-alpha version. A very good excuse for all the problems. Does something look bad? Well, this is not the final version, you ungrateful monkey!The history of this company is also “interesting”. I personally played Friday 13th, Predator HG, Ghostbusters and now KKfOS. There were noticeable improvements in the games, but they all died pretty quickly. And don’t believe in fairy tales about the fact that F13 died due to problems with the license. It started dying much earlier. This is not about F13 now, so I won’t go into details. The point is that games from Ilfonic are cursed. They come out with a lot of problems (usually this is PvP balance/design problem) and die after about a year. As I already said. The stream from the developers appeared late, and when it did appear, it was a pre-alpha version. There were many unanswered questions.Valve recently updated its refund policy. Now you won’t be able to play as much as you want and return the game before the official release. Two hours is negligible for an ideal test. Fortunately for me, I can refund it. Now about the game itself.. The combat system is "janky".. You can't choose a side. It's random.. The tutorial is poor. A couple of images with a short description, but no page with controls, etc.. Speaking of controls. You can't change it.. With crossplay turned off, I had to wait a very long time for the match. As a result, I started the match alone (with bots).. There seems to be a connection problem. Initially I thought it was frame rate drops, but I had stable 60 fps. All that remains is the connection. Maybe it's Wi-Fi players. May be something else. Players with a ping of over 100 have already appeared.. It's not interesting to play as clowns. The maps are large. Experienced players don't make noise often. The exits are at different ends of the map and are not marked for clowns (?). The characters' voices are much quieter than the music. Marking the location of the clown/human (so that your partner can see him) is not possible. The audio in general (at least when playing with speakers) is not great. Trolling clowns in a team is not a very difficult task. Special thanks to the wonderful combat system. The victims here are not human.... The image is blurry. You can change it using the "Sharpness" option if you are using DLSS/FSR. I don't use FSR/DLSS.. Confused clown class system. The characteristics are slightly different. The arsenal is the same.. Bots are dumb. Don't expect to have a fun time. You might as well spit out of the window at your neighbors. Much more interesting activity.. Proximity (when you are close to another player) chat is shared between clown and human players. The story of F13 with degenerates and their mentally retarded dialogues repeats itself again.As expected (as I personally said earlier), players will gain experience during Advanced Access. Some have already gained enough. Just imagine, the developers provided streamers with access to the game even before us. The whole point of pre-order was early access to the game a week before the official release...In general, I advise everyone who is dissatisfied with the game to ask for a refund. The game is not interesting. Maybe someday, after major changes to the game's balance and design in general, it will become more attractive. Now I can't recommend it. Besides, there is something else to spend money on, and most importantly, time. New games will be released soon and the summer sale will begin. Of course, if you are a connoisseur of burgers and crap filmed on amateur cameras (not KK movie specifically), then yes, buy the game. Personally, I was more disappointed than I had planned.Bye.

_childDocuments_.review: If I could leave a neutral review I would. Where to start?At the time of this review the game has a few bugs that can ruin your matches. Getting stuck on some stairs as either side, getting thrown through the ground when in a cocoon. You currently can only quick-play or host a private match. So similar to Friday the 13th, it is randomly chosen who is human or klown. You also cannot keep your XP if you leave the match early. Got killed early, or escaped early? Well you have to watch the entire match to get your XP.I got this game to play with friends and it has been a hit or miss on half of our games. Sometimes it will divide our group of 3 between both sides. If you disband the party mid-game it will remove every player that was part of the party from the match. The voice chat is interesting. I can't tell if as a klown your voice chat is for the team or not. The human's voice chat is for everyone nearby, including klowns. So you know, taunting from humans insured.The starting kit for the klowns feels a bit weak. I understand why most klowns were running shotguns or so on when playing as a human against them. If a human is experienced, they can absolutely wipe the floor with you, finish the objective, and escape all in a few minutes. A group of 2 or more victims can easily kill a klown that isn't a tank if they are all armed. Not to mention, a hit on the nose from something throw or a charged attack can leave you repeatedly stunned back to back, easy to take down. Everytime you die as a klown you respawn almost a minute later, but it is easy to die back to back, just to be forced to watch your teammates.The human experience has certainly been something.  I've had klowns spawn right next to me and kill me before I could get a object. I've had important key-items for escaping spawn right near me, and then a tiny bit further the escape that needs said item. Of the two sides, the humans feel more forgiving in several ways. At least in the handful of lobbies I've played so far.I plan to play more of this game, try the different characters for both sides. Now is probably the best time to play before every player has maps, items, strategies and so on memorized. Despite the bugs and half of the matches being a bit of a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, I had fun overall and would recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: As of 6/8/24, until this game gets a few updates, it breaks my heart to have to definitely tell people to not spend 40 dollars on this experience. As a huge fan of the movie, as a huge fan of Friday The 13th, it's just not a satisfying experience to play yet. With devs who don't communicate outside of one place, a day one patch that fixed some things and broke a lot, a bit of a grind to unlock more than 80 percent of the game, and cosmetic dlc packs first day into the game even in it's current state, there's a lot to try to respect here.Pros:It's a very charming game. There's a lot of nice references to the movie, the klowns are designed perfectly, the atmosphere is great, the music is great, from an aesthetic stand point? It's designed fantastically.The horror elements are definitely here. There's a fun type of scare in being inside a building or in a bush and hearing the squeaks of clown shoes pass you by with alarming music. Human gameplay can be very satisfying. This is also going to followed up in on the con department, until then, it is worth mentioning that playing as a human feels strong. It feels absolutely fantastic. There are a lot of unlockables. You will more than likely have a good bit of content to unlock in this game as there is so many unlockables.Cons:Half the game is behind unlockables. There's no variety in klowns or humans until you're hours deep into the game. You could argue the most worth it klowns / weapons are hours in, which only those who played prior to the release have anyway. If you're playing as either of the two starting klowns and their weapons, it's not hard to make you look silly at all.Klowns are clunky, slow, and stupid. Especially the starter one you get. You will be outran, your abilities have a high cooldown, it is very much a chore depending on the map you're playing to succeed as clown.Humans have a ton of advantages and items galore. An item that gives you a ton of stamina to escape chase? Plenty. Weapons that can destroy you in seconds? Plenty. Weapons that for some reason have better hit reg than a ray gun? Plenty. Speaking of that, the default weapon you're given is a melee and a raygun. The cotton candy gun has the worst accuracy on the planet unless you're standing on top of the human at which point you may as well use the melee weapon.There's a lot of things missing from the trailers and hype up that we were told would be in at release. Some abilities missing. Some features missing. There's some things that haven't been given completely yet and it's sad to see it isn't here. And if it is here? It's behind twenty hours of playing the game before you can get it.Glitches are everywhere. Sometimes I can't speak to my team on voice chat. They can either hear me and I can't hear them, or the other way around. For awhile, cross platform partying didn't work. Challenges still don't work at times. Items can't be picked up or melted into the floor. Very fun stuff.I am rooting for this dev team, I am rooting for this game, I am rooting for Killer Klowns. As of right now, with the hours I have in, I can not recommend it. I can't recommend it for anyone who isn't willing to sink hours into the game, JUST to get weapons and characters to make the game feel even a slight bit more satisfying. I hope to revisit this review in the near future. Until then, I do not recommend spending 40 dollars on this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game needs an "Arcade Mode".Basically, both teams spawn in, and when either Human or Klown dies, they receive their score, and restart fresh (and can even select a different load out). When any player dies, they are put on a 45 second respawn timer, and respawn as normal. During this time, players can play minigames to spawn with certain items. Looted chests reset after 5 minutes from being looted.Exits can be used once, before they reset and require a key item to escape again. Clowns must hook or kill at least 5 players to "return to the mothership" (which counts as a victory, same as if a player "escaped".Each side has 3 lives. A victory is escaping for humans, a victory for Klowns is hooking/killing 5 humans. The match doesn't end; it's endless. When one player fulfills their objective or dies 3 times, the results screen plays out and they can move on to the next match, or stay in the same lobby. Auto-play will put them in a new lobby, on a new map, as either Klown or Human.The current system just doesn't really work for modern gaming standards. Players who die 3 minutes into a match don't want to wait 12 minutes for the match to end just to receive their experience. Other players just want to quickly get back into the action. Arcade mode would take off on this game super hard and make it extremely popular.

_childDocuments_.review: If Killer Klowns is already nostalgic for you, this is a no-brainer.This is a stellar asymmetrical horror title that feels like it carries less pressure than Dead by Daylight; but, it manages to maintain the same level of technical enjoyment. Granted, it's still early into its release and it isn't without its bugs, but the organic shenanigans and campy atmosphere make up for that, in my opinion. It carries the film charm into a cool little modern 3 vs. 7 formula that feels engaging and fun. Cross platform lobby play feels fluid and brings a variety of console cultures together. Killer Klowns is fun on it's own but is most definitely better with friends - and the proximity chat elevates that. Chances are if you're going in solo, you're bound to make some solid match buddies, if not longer term homies. You're bound to run into a little repetitiveness, a busted lobby, or a technical goof on occasion - but for what it is at the time of writing this, I'm content with the price tag. I'm really looking forward to seeing what additional content and gameplay tweaks IllFonic gets churning out for this goofy little banger. Lettem' slap a few patties on the Big Top Burger grill and cook.

_childDocuments_.review: DAY 1 PATCH UPDATE:It pains me to say this as I am a HUGE fan of the franchise and had a lot of hope with this game. But where it stands now even with the day 1 patch, I cannot in good conscience, recommend it unless it's on a steep discount. The game has A LOT of potential for the genre as long as Illfonic doesn't do their usual BS. Will update review accordingly and reasonably so, as this game progresses through patches.The game was fun, goofy and somewhat stable in the early access. The day 1 patch however, has ruined the game in many ways. The only two viable Klown weapons were nerfed into the ground. To counter this, a few fixes were made on the human side such as blunt objects no longer popping Klown noses (shouldn't have even been a thing in the first place).They also apparently changed key escape item spawn rates so that they aren't spawning near exits. But this is not true and probably broken as well atm as I find key items in the open next to objectives. All they had to do besides the nerfs to Klown weapons, was to also buff the other terrible Klown weapons. Which they did for two but it's barely noticeable. Klowns basically have no tools now and get jumped by Humans constantly. It has become a respawn timer simulator even when triple stacking Klown presence in a team fight.Other issues persist such as Klowns having super long animations without invincibility during said animation, so humans can just beat them up for free. Example: Klown Jump teleporting. Meanwhile Humans seem to be able to interact with escapes while being hit and stunned.The Trapper Klown class does not have traps of any kind and all mention of them in the game text, have been removed such as the challenges for it being changed to something else entirely. Because of the core class changes they made between builds when Illfonic took over, it is clear some of those classes were built around perks and upgrades that are now missing. An example would be the Tank class which is terrible and has no benefits to a Klown comp. The reasoning for removing the perks/upgrades is poor balancing. It makes sense in a way when you look at other games such as TCM or DBD. But I don't fully see it as the sole reason. I think what it is, is they don't want to put effort into fixing the game design flaws. Perks are good when balanced because it adds diversity.In my opinion, it's clear to me that Illfonic will continue doing Illfonic stuff when they release a terrible day 1 patch but take the time to add in paid cosmetics ON THE FIRST DAY OF FULL RELEASE. Some would argue that buying skins incentives them to make the game better, but this is not true and all you have to do is look at Predator Hunting Grounds or even another game/studio like TCM/Gun to understand that logic does not hold up.Outside of balancing, the game performs spotty now. I have a 3080 rig and it stutters heavily for some matches even on medium. I could play maxed out during early access week. It could just be server performance but idk for sure. The game also has a weird ghosting issue that happened even in early access. I know for a fact it is not my monitor or settings as I have no issues on any other games, and have also tested every setting combination possible. It doesn't ruin the game but it is still annoying nonetheless. It only happens on the menu btw. I have not seen it in matches yet.EARLY ACCESS REVIEW:The game is fun and goofy. Made by fans for fans. Surprisingly stable with minor bugs. Occasional server issues. HOWEVER with this being early access week, there are major issues I currently experience and see with this game long term. Will update review accordingly and reasonably so as this game progresses past early access.Without a preference queue in the early access, everyone is leaving Human lobbies to re-queue for Klowns. Getting Klowns is near impossible. I have played Humans at a 20-1 ratio if not worse which is absurd even for early access. This NEEDS to be fixed and will be fixed once a preference queue is added with the day one update. Sad that the preference queue was not here for early access.Another issue is the longevity for this game. There isn't a whole lot to grind for so once you max out (which is relatively easy and I have seen people day two already maxed out), the only other thing to grind for are the challenge booklets (cosmetic unlocks) which can also been done very quickly. Apparently this game was supposed to have a perk/upgrade system but was removed due to balancing issues? I get why cuz all you have to do is look at the disaster that became Texas Chainsaw Massacre with their meta. But come on, just balance as you go and don't let a meta rot the playerbase to death. At the bare minimum, some form of mastery challenges for, I guess, more cosmetics. That way people have incentive to keep playing beyond revisiting the occasional "fun" 6 months from now.There are balancing issues I have noticed but I think it is still too early to tell. My first thoughts being the fight or flight response this game has. It's not really cat and mouse, but more so run or fight. Fighting as Humans is infinitely better if you stay together but randos never do. As Klowns, it feels like the first two cotton candy rayguns are pretty garbage when I can just popcorn bazooka spam or beat them to death with a hammer if they challenge me 1v1. In my opinion, humans lose cotton candy from their bodies, way too quickly during chases. The higher the cocoon meter gets, it would make more sense to have it be stickier and harder to auto remove. I have seen Humans reset the entire meter back to zero within 2 seconds if they just take a sharp corner to break the raygun beam pathing. Not sure if this would be wise to change though when popcorn bazooka is as braindead no skill as it is now. Free infinite chasing into kill confirm weapon. Super easy to kite Human turn around melee engagements. On top of XP farm. Not sure why it gives so much XP but it does and EVERYONE is abusing it. Can't really afford to be picky though with balancing when it's still early access. Hopefully balancing actually happens.Overall, I still recommend this game. Whether or not it is worth the $40 price tag, is up to what you are seeking in a game. For me it was easy as I am a die-hard fan that wants to support the franchise and breathe more life into it. I give the early access a 8/10 as it is mostly stable and is a lot of fun. Just PLEASE do not let this flop and dry out.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly like 8/10, which is really good I'd say! The core mechanics and idea are great there's just a couple of major things that are missing or weird.1) Too few unlocks/levels/progress. I don't know if this game would benefit from or hurt from a Battle Pass style system but really i just mean if they double the basic unlocks/level stuff that would help a lot. Can sort of feel like a long wait to experiment then I imagine it sort of feels like it all came at once toward the end and poof its over haha.2) Balancing/Maps. There is some balancing to be done - I'm too new to pinpoint it exactly. But it's clear at least one or two things are off in some way. Bigger than that is the few maps and lack of variety in their objectives - you will play the same thing over and over. I'm still new enough im playing 'new' to me maps so it's yet to be a problem. But I can tell the maps can be mastered quick on both ends. Theoretically, I hope this leads to more technical gameplay in time as we all get less nooby. But more maps would still be good or alternating objectives/escapes, etc.This is a awesome start to an asymmetrical horror game with a great license. The core game play is solid as well as the age old idea of PvP but thrown into this unique and fun setting. It is certainly not perfect, the level and unlock system may seem a bit sparse and in the beginning slow. The maps are rather few and there seems to be some general human vs klown balance issues in a few small areas. But overall I've enjoyed my gameplay so far.For me this is a game you hop on for 2-3 hours a week in your free time when it's convenient and sounds fun. But when im in those conditions it's a great game! Perfect time waster at least as long as you are a fan of the license. Harder to judge if you are new to the IP.

_childDocuments_.review: The game DBD wishes it was. Takes all of the great elements from the survival horror genre and adds a fresh clown themed spin on it. Relatively balanced, good clowns are terrifying where as good survivors are annoying as f*ck. Skill checks have a bit of a learning curve but once you realize that the mouse icon indicates which click of the mouse you're suppose to do, it becomes much easier. It's much more than just 'hooking' survivors (as a killer), and running to a gate (as a survivor). Clowns can kill and remove players from the game in gimmicky and hilarious fashion, survivors can fight back and actually killed their terrorizers. Number of different escape possibilities, clown fatalities (funny as f+ck btw), and much more. All of these unique factors lead to each game playing out differently, a real breath of fresh air.Game needs more attention. I worry as time goes on it will start to bleed players. Hopefully with further updates, additions, and discounts, it will stay fresh and bring those undecided players in. The $40 price point is a pretty steep barrier of entry and will prevent hesitant customers from purchasing based solely on that. I understand licensing and I'm sure the creators of the original reference material are taking a big cut but $20 or, hell, even $30 would be a much fairer and realistic purchase price. Overall, great game that has a ton of replayability. I'm excited about what they plan on doing in the future. 'It' collab when?!?

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of the 1988 cult classic, I'm thrilled with how well this game captures the movie's unique atmosphere. _childDocuments_.review: Honestly this is the most fun Asymmetric Horror title that I've played and I don't even really play this genre of games very often but this one is actually a lot of fun. I can solo queue and still escape as a human no problem, and solo with a clown is pretty fun as well. If you have a small group of people that also play with you then it amplifies the fun. Overall I've really enjoyed this title despite it's need for some balancing but I believe this game will do well in the long run. Definitely worth the money in my opinion!Pros.-Playing solo is easy and actually a lot of fun.-The items all make sense, and are easy to use/understand.-The mechanics are simple enough to just pick up and play, but there's also some strategy involved.-The Humans can FIGHT BACK against the clowns, no more feeling powerless in tough situations.-The progression is fairly quick and you unlock new and fun things to play with quite often as well as completing challenges to unlock cosmetics.-PRIVATE LOBBIES WITH BOTS and you can farm challenges/gain XP as Klowns solo.-The wait between matches is very low and games are found very quickly and start very quickly even if people back out you can find games very quickly.Cons.-Some weapons for the clowns outweigh the others. Definitely needs some balancing updates (Bouncecaster/Popcorn Cannon)-In game chat quality is poor, use external chat software like Discord if you plan on playing with others.-A few major bugs currently that can softlock lobbies or break animations. (Day 1 patch will probably solve.)-Some challenges are currently broken/unable to be completed. (Again Day 1 patch coming soon.)-Currently Crossplay works, but cannot invite crossplay friends yet until June 4th, you have to que at the same time and hopefully find the same match.-You CANNOT select which role you want to play, it's always random and that makes some people dodge lobbies if they don't get the role they want to play.TLDROverall rating is 7/10 in it's current state, after Day 1 patch if major bugs are resolved then my rating will likely be an 8/10 at the least. Worth the buy!

_childDocuments_.review: Killer Klowns From Outer Space: The Game is an electrifying dive into the world of asymmetrical horror that will leave you on the edge of your seat! As a fan of the cult classic movie, I was thrilled to experience this interactive homage, and let me tell you, it does not disappoint.First off, let's talk about the gameplay. The asymmetrical setup adds a whole new layer of tension and excitement, as three players takes on the role of the menacing Killer Klowns while the rest desperately try to survive their onslaught. It's a thrilling cat-and-mouse game that keeps you guessing and strategizing every step of the way. And dare I say it, it surpasses Dead by Daylight by a longshot.Sure, there are a few minor tweaks needed here and there, but nothing that detracts from the overall enjoyment. With time, I'm confident these tiny issues will be patched up, making an already fantastic game even better.And can we talk about the nostalgia factor? As a die-hard fan of the original movie, seeing all my favorite characters and locales brought to life in stunning detail is an absolute treat. The developers clearly poured their hearts into capturing the essence of the film, and it shines through in every pixel.Now, while Friday the 13th: The Game still holds a special place in my heart, Killer Klowns From Outer Space: The Game is quickly climbing the ranks to claim its spot at the top. It's a pulse-pounding, scream-inducing masterpiece that delivers on all fronts. If you're a horror fan looking for your next obsession, look no further. This game is pure epicness wrapped in a colorful, clown-shaped bow.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy this game. As someone who plays an unhealthy amount of asymmetrical horror games, IllFonic has won me over. I've had quite a lot of laughs from the proximity chat alone.This game does great homage to the movie and I recommend it for old fans, as well as newcomers. Fans of Friday the 13th the Game would also love this, as it shares many traits from it. Running through the woods or city to find the escape, while a killer (3 in this case) tries to kill you, while also trying to avoid you from escaping. If you miss F13, this game definitely has that vibe.As of early access, there are many bugs that will hopefully be fixed when the game fully releases/soon. I hope this game stays alive for a long time. Asym horror game death is a sad thing and its way too common :( I will say that $40 is a bit pricey, but I have ZERO regrets for purchasing this game.Overall, I really do like this game. I recommend it to anyone who has any interest in playing.

_childDocuments_.review: I was very much so looking forward to this game for over a year, especially when i heard Game executive director Randy Greenback signed on. Still i was excited and was looking forward to essentially the quality and similar game play of Friday the 13th the Game as to an extent that is what the Bar for the game was Via Randy working on it. Now that it was released on Advanced Access i gotta say its Disappointing. The Games Pacing is down right non existent, Basic Options not even implemented such as Key Bindings, Tutorial doesn't explain HOW to play the game, Clowns can easily be killed either by being ganged up on or shot at, The UI is a cluttered mess, server tends to crash when game ends, Estimated wait timer doesn't properly estimate, There's no customizing variety right off the bat; everything has to be unlocked which isnt a bad thing just your extremely limited at the start, First 3 clown classes are pretty much the same over all, Klowntalitys just make you and your victim disappear for a mildly disappointing finisher (Nobody else will get to witness it), The Idea of Klown VC will have harsh distortion from the Human perspective isn't In the game, Humans can easily trap and gang up on Klowns, If you die or escape early you will have to wait a quite a while, Spectator mini-games feel out of place and unnecessary especially since it lets you stack the favor for the humans, Klown abilities really feels pointless to use for the most part since just running and killing works just the same, all 4 escapes being available at the same time ruins the pace, Klowns cant see Objectives; only when humans interact with them, Game overall lacks the serious vibe compared to Friday the 13th, No Offline mode yet there are Human AI's, Also if the game isnt populated AI's will be used as placeholders until more players join.All n All the main pro to this game which isn't even a good one to begin with is; If your lucky Your fellow players will provide the entertainment. Unlike DBD Killer Klowns is much less of a competitive horror multiplayer game and more of your great dumb funny gameplay. However that does not mean that there can not be some competitveness to be had. realistically this game shares more values with FT13TH than it does dbd, with the freedom of survivors having multiple escape options and weapons at there disposal to use to fight back the klowns. Which can be sometimes can overthrow the klowns on multiple occasions. However the klowns themselves can be a major threat in massive numbers. _childDocuments_.review: Don't be a Clown and purchase this title before it goes to the sale bin. NOT worth the $60, and most definitely not even worth the $39.99 base game. $20-25 seems about right for this product as it is, without the necessary tweaksThe Good, The Bad, The UGLY..The Good! - What I enjoyed so much about this game were the maps. The environmental maps are so visually and aesthetically pleasing. The inclusion of animations and detail that could have easily been left out such as moving carnival rides in the background add so much life, sense of realism. Character models and such are true to the film. Lighting and contrast values are spot on. Plenty of places to run and hide. Multiple escape route options available for the human side. Multiple weapon choices. Built in voice chat? BeautifulThe Bad - CANNOT choose how you play. Game will ASSIGN and DECIDE what's best for you, by selecting the Klown or Human side. I once counted, and was "assigned" the human side, 17 consecutive times, -17 -, while showcasing this game. Have aspirations to be a Klown or even a Human main? Nope. During that 17 streak, the game presented a graphic on the screen prior to each match giving me a serious false hope in RNG when it was "deciding" what side I would play by making me believe that there was a 50% coin flip chance when it had flickering graphics going back and forth between the words "Klown" and "Human", and ultimately always falling on the "Human" selection for that span. Terrible, terrible probability. The people who made this game have obviously never visited Vegas. If I hit Red 17 times in a row at the roulette table..The UGLY.. - For the humans, the objective requires you to either secure spark plugs and or gas cans/security cards in order to access any of the end game escape routes. To do this however, you need to search through chests, coolers, drawers, closets that are littered throughout the map. It takes sometimes 15-20+ searches just to maybe even yield ONE of the spark plugs needed. Cheeseburger, Cheeseburger, Popsicle, Cheeseburger, Popsicle, Popsicle, Cheeseburger, ENERGY CAN :O, Cheeseburger, Cheeseburger..and this is coming from a KILLER MAIN.. Chest Loot SimUGLY cont. - What should have been the most exciting thing about this title, the chases, the cat and mouse game, are actually the worst thing about this game. So very, very anti-climatic. Klowns are soooooo slooooooooooowwwwwwww By the time you even spot and catch up to a human, you always happen to be out of stamina, and all a human needs to do at that point is to pop an energy drink and smash the "W" key, and they're well on their way to Albuquerque. Base speed for the Klowns needs to go up. Way up. Get rid of the already present and lethargic slow base speed out of the game and create a new and even faster level of top speed that can be reached and achieved by utilizing perks or related itemsUGLY pt.3 - It's Texas Chainsaw Massacre all over again like others have already pointed out. Leeland anyone? There was a match where I actually witnessed all 3 Klowns being KILLED, -KILLED-, by the Humans, all within a span of less than 30 seconds. Humans were actually CHASING the Klowns afterward to hunt them down. Brutal. This is broken. So broken. I thought it was "Killer Humans from Outer Earth" for a moment or two XDDI don't intend to revisit this title in any serious capacity anytime soon less the proper and necessary tweaks be made

_childDocuments_.review: Admittedly, I haven't played too much of the game just yet. (Only sitting on about 6-8 matches at the time of writing this.) However, I thought I'd let my initial impressions out. F13 was a game I held near and dear to my heart because, despite the jank, it led to a couple lasting friendships and fond memories. That jank is present here and I welcome its embrace. This is not a review to slander other asymms, i.e. DbD or TCM. I've played my share of those games, enjoyed them, but still found myself yearning for Friday's style of unfiltered madness. It was a game that led to a lot of funny scenarios to the extent that I could never take winning or losing overly serious. I feel like this game matches its spirit so far within the community and I'm hoping it mostly remains that way. So far, I like the general improvements that are present here. Graphical presentation is not leaps and bounds better, but better. There are a variety of win conditions for both parties, "Klowns" and humans, alike that keep the game fresh; albeit, some of the game design is archaic and the tutorial is pretty poor at explaining game mechanics. Once more, as with Friday, Illfonic's labor of love to the original property shows in the game's aesthetics. They also implement minigames during downtime, which I found to be a fairly remarkable addition to hopefully stave off early player withdrawal. Unlockable customization feeds the hungry dress-up slut within me and I think also helps with player retention, knowing there is something to actively play to earn, including various skills, class types, and items. I mentioned archaic game design and this shows most notably in the UI. There are a million things assaulting your eyes onscreen at once, which is a fair step back from Friday. This is paired with intrusively loud sound design, as there are an assortment of noises, music and audio cues going off at once that often distract from moments of stealth. It's a fun, if not perfect, experience so far. Eagerly hoping it survives and improves.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to recommend this game, because I've been a fan of Killer Klowns for years, but I can't really do that with where the game is currently at. Here are some issues I have:1. The 4 Klown classes were originally advertised as each having their own unique set of weapons and abilities - however, due to balancing issues, they had to remove some of the classes' main abilities  (E.G; things like Trapper Rudy's baby Klown traps and Tank Chubby's sticky bash) and made it so every class can now use every weapon and ability. In my opinion, this has pretty much ruined the class system and eliminates the feeling of having a unique role in a Klown team. I was really looking forward to playing the trapper role and using the Klown-in-a-box traps, but that now class doesn't even exist anymore. I also feel that Chubby can hardly be called a "tank" after the changes; yes he can take a couple more hits than other Klowns, but his movement speed actually makes him more of a target than a threat to opportunistic groups of humans. He either needs more health, so he can actually tank damage, or he needs some kind of damaging/crowd control AOE to punish/deter groups of organised attacking humans - like he was supposed to have.2. Lackeys kinda suck. Any new human player will quickly learn that lackeys are very easy to avoid and even easier to kill - as it stands, they're barely a threat. One of their primary uses is to help Klowns transport cocoons to generators, but lackeys won't just pick up any cocoon they find in the world. Lackeys will only ever offer to carry a cocoon if you pick one up within a certain radius of them - in other words; if a lackey isn't close enough to see you picking up the cocoon, you have to drop/throw the cocoon closer to them, then pick it up back up so the lackey notices it and offers to transport it for you, then you have to drop it again so the lackey can pick it up... This gets very tedious after a while. Why can't they just see that you're holding a cocoon when you get near to them? When you fill up a generator by placing 4 cocoons in it, this should upgrade the lackeys from that generator - maybe making them faster?3. The invisible car is useless. When you activate the ability it takes so long for your Klown to actually get into the car and, when you do hit a human with it, it causes both the Klown and human to get stunned for the same length of time! It doesn't even damage the human? In the movie, Slim was able to ram a real car off the road with his invisible car - in this game, hitting a soft fleshy human causes the car to crash and throw the Klown to the ground. This ability definitely needs a rework, because it's currently just a worse version of the pizza box and isn't worth choosing. It would be cool if it was an insta-kill that flattened the human or took a chunk of health away, but has a very long cooldown so it's not too broken.4. Klown cosmetics are very disappointing. The choices feel very limited and the same assets are reused in areas - some of the hairstyles you unlock are the same between Klowns with little to no variation. There are also 5 cotton candy guns to unlock and two of them have the same exact design as two previous weapons; the Gigaray is just a puppet holding the Pentashot, and the Laser beamer is just a puppet holding the standard ray gun. Part of progressing through a game like this should be about unlocking cool NEW looking weapons and ways to customise your character - and this is Killer Klowns From Outer Space! There should be going all out and designing sorts of imaginative wacky weapons and cosmetics.5. I've watched the movie loads of times and I wish they stuck a bit closer to the origional designs. The models in the game just feel a bit... off? For example; one of Rudy's main defining features was his big upper lip/snout-like mouth and droopy zoinked-out face - you also couldn't really see his teeth. In this game, it's like they've went off-model to try and push the generic "creepy unsettling clown" look, and kinda lost the charm of the original designs by doing so. I mean, in the main screen and pizza Klownality, Chubby is missing his hair! The game has been out for months and they still haven't they fixed it - did they forget to add that part of his hairstyle in or what, because the hairstyle isn't like that in the character customisation options. I really would have expected to have a bit more attention to detail with the main characters of the movie/game. Ultimately, instead of adding an in-game store and trying to rake in money by selling us characters that should already be free to play in the game, they should be focusing on fixing the abilities that were supposed to be in the game and designing new maps/weapons/unlockable cosmetics. On top of that, they need to lower the current price, because there's not enough content in the game to justify asking for that much - this would also hopefully bring in some fresh players, which the game is definitely in need of. If they don't pull it back soon, this game is going to lose what's left of it's player base and be dead by the end of the year.P.S: I'm also really surprised that there isn't already a map that's the inside of the spaceship? Like, I was sure that that was something they showed off in the gameplay trailers?

_childDocuments_.review: Been such a fun and frustrating game to play but otherwise solid. Mechanics are easy to pick up from the get go and finding items can be quick or take all game to find such as escape items. There are more survivors (humans) than your typical survival horror games so room for error is less likely but there is a skill gap albeit it small depending on how well versed you are with the item randomization and knowledge of the how the maps work. Communication is pretty much key to your teams success whether you play humans or clowns because if you try to play solo, you will get ganged up by the opposing team or not doing the objective as a clown then you'll be dooming yourselves as humans have the upper hand in the early game. Also, whether you're dead or already escaped, playing the mini games are a unique twist that is completely optional but can be the deciding factor for the remaining players to find a means to escape or survive long enough for the last ditch escape via terenzi brothers. Overall the game is fairly balanced on both sides because you don't often see one sided matches unless you queue into a game with zero coordination which then you don't know who is carrying the crucial items until you run into them during the match or clowns who just want to be running around chasing people to kill. Is the game perfect / Stale? no, maybe? It's not been out long so updates will eventually come around. May not be everyone's cup of tea but definitely worth checking out if you're a fan of survival horror games or even the movie!

_childDocuments_.review: Works much like F13 or TCSM: there's a few different exits, with specific conditions that have to be met by the humans. Complete the conditions and a certain number of humans can escape through that exit. Klowns try to kill survivors. That's it.I kinda like it. Not as dead as it seems (crossplay baby!) but the flipside is there is an epidemic of leaving (no leaver penalty) and I can't even blame people because I too have fallen for it. The balance in this game is TERRIBLE.Speedrunning these matches is always a problem and that's why DBD has so much slowdown: can't kill survivors directly, objectives take a while, etc. None of that here. There's not really much counter to this game's equivalent of "slugging" except stockpiling knives (if you can find them) or getting one from a dead player. If you get two klowns on you, you're screwed and the game is over if they are any good. Conversely, humans can complete an objective ~within the first minute of a match~, literally before the klowns can reach it from spawn, and get away with 4+ people.On top of this, chases are generally uninteractive - sprint away from the Klown, sprint towards the Human - instead of the more interesting chases of DBD. Combat is more involved, but it's kinda janky.So naturally people leave. Because why play a match where you just watched half the opposing team get away 1 minute into a 15m match? Or where you die 30 seconds in and have to watch everyone else play and hope for the good luck of a respawn? Or where your teammates purposefully deny you an escape and call you slurs?I think it has promise but I can't recommend it. Too expensive and I'm already having a bad experience with toxic players and frustrating design.

For Klowns you have a variety of weapons to use and powers to help you hunt down the humans. I like the dynamics of the game. If you die as well then you can even help your team out by gifting them items by doing a minigame. The only thing negative I can really say about the game currently is that 1. The price on it seems a little too high for what you're getting basegame wise. I'd probably lower it to 20 bucks. 2. Some spawns feel absolutely horrible. Like sometimes as a human you will spawn next to a klown when you get into the game and just die because you're defenseless. That's really just a negative for the human sides. 3. There's some areas of the game where klowns can't get too. Not naming where but they have to either aim their guns to try and aim for a cotton candy cocoon which they will never be able to reach and the person just suffocates or they jump in between two windows and if you go into the house they'll just leave. The only other thing I could say currently is that some of the Klowns feel like they're missing something overall. Such as the Tank. Besides that, I still think this game is fun and hope it has a decent lifespan for players to play this game! _childDocuments_.review: As usual all the crybabies are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ in the forums and putting out negatives reviews with barely any input on whats so bad.After my first day I can say its a ton of fun.For the first day the servers held up amazingly imho,only one game we had a server crash and everybody was sent back to the lobby,some other people might have worse experience,but its day 1 people,ALL games have their servers on flames on release,theres nothing you can do about it,wait a week or so instead of complaining it'll be way smoother. - BugsI've only had one game breaking bug where I think because I interacted with a door as the Klown while holding a cocoon made me so I couldnt perform any action at all except checking lockers,so I had to quit out to the menu. Other than that and the aligment of the skillchecks being off I haven't experienced anything crazy that would ruin my games. Altough thats my personnal experience I've hear people having audio issues with or voip not working stuff like that,but no idea on that front since it hasnt happend to me.- Main Issues Personally my main issue is the ABSENCE OF CUSTOM KEYBINDS in the game,which I think in 2024 is crazy,but here we are. So far that I know theres no external way of editing them either and some keybind are pretty bad,crouch is on left Ctrl,and two abilities are on F and G respectivaly,which is easy to mess up,kind of annoying, I expect the dev to bring a fix to this so we can edit them out. There is no Exclusive Fullscreen either only windowed fullscreen,for me it hasnt been a problem even tho I never really play any game like that,but I know for some people with certain monitors/monitors setup it can take them back.- PerformanceMy Setup is new except my old ass 1060 6gb (still standing strong lol) and the game ran perfectly fine,no hiccups,no weird stutters,stable FPS all the way running everything on Epic. No complaints here.- BalanceOverall,without getting into particulars,I think both team definitely need balancing,as is usual with these types of game,theres always some OP stuff and tweaks needed. Contrary to what most people say its not really one sided,both sides can annihilate the other. I've had game as the Klown where we would, as randoms, without really much comms or organization, completely  own the survivors and some matches ending with 20k+ score. Other games where we would get completely rolled by the survivors,and Vice versa. Not as many people using mics as I expected,a few fun lobbies with most talking where the most fun for sure,but most of them you wouldnt hear much and people were getting by just fine,both as klown and survivor.Getting a bit more into specific I cant say whats OP on the killer side since I haven't unlocked everything,but its clear that the Popcorn bazooka is pretty much busted and need some tweaking. Abilities wise I think maybe the hipnotize could be a bit much when the killers work in tandem you're pretty much helpess and cant do much. On the survivor side, What comes to my mind is mainly the boat extract,quite superior and easier to achieve than the other ones,which all have some drawbacks (bridge collapse,bunker stay only open for 10/12 sec,portal has to be held open) but the boat doesnt really. You can just sit on the wheel waiting 10 minutes for other survivors to join (three total fit on the boat)and its usually one of the fastest to find since most maps have water only on one side of the map,so pretty easy to find it once you know your way around. There was also a game where all three survivor boarded the boat and where just sitting there on the dock,taunting us killers,since when they board it they're immune,or so they thought. after blasting them left and right and them just laughing it off I tought hold on the hipnotize ability pulls enemies towards you,could it work in this scenario? lo and behold one of the survivors got back on the dock and got pummeled by me and my teamate while the other two drove off scared ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cause they didnt expect that at all.Anyways,some matches can be a lot of fun regardless of the outcome when they drag on and get a bit on the longer side.Kill a bunch of surv,one guy clutches and revives almost the entire lobby,suddenly is new game +,other games as survivor I would be blessed by RNG and find all the key items I need to open X exit and be able to leave the map without barely doing anything or interacting with any  and out 3 minutes,and I think even tho theres always RNG involved and sometimes you need that ONE item you can't find even tho you crossed the entire map It could use some tweaking,to insure these short games where two poor bastard are left alone in the map barely at the beginning to fend for themselves. Which has happened more time than i'd like.To end it up,the game is a ton of fun,not at all as complicated as some people make it to be, if you played other assymetrical you'll be right at home. SOME OF YOU NEED TO READ THE TUTORIAL, cause i've seen and heard many complain about super basic things that are explained there,yes there are things that could be shown more clearly either with UI or others,but its not rocket science,just play and figure it out like everybody else.

_childDocuments_.review: Funny Klown game. Don't get your block knocked off. Very reminiscent of F13. It will scratch that itch for sure if you miss that game. There's some minor bugs, nothing game-breaking. I assume there will be a day-one patch. I'll update review to reflect that. 7/10 sound design9/10 gameplay loopProgression seems pretty fair;Some game features are blocked until full release, so only more to come! Post-official release edit: There was indeed a day one patch, it has fixed nearly every minor bug I had on mind at time of initial review. There is one that I can think of that is still needing fixing and that's some cotton guns not applying cotton candy on exits that have had the cotton candy completely removed. The previously assumed temporarily locked features are still in limbo it seems? Baby klowns are either scrapped or still not ready for release which is kind of disappointing. However I still recommend the game as it is a small thing for me. Game is still plenty fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Lets be honest here this game is basically friday the 13th but more jasons and same humans. Is it fun yes I enjoy the game and have been a fan of the movie. Is it worth 40$ that would be your choice i personally bought it and could see it maybe 25$ to 30$ range would attract more players into the game.ProsThere is plenty of games going on finding a match has never been a issueI see a decent balance in weapons especially humans in a melee battle you will win 9 times out of 10 as a humanThe leveling system is pretty good you level up almost every match if you are alive for about 5 to 8 minutesThe concept again the friday the 13th game. Which is enjoyable Being a klown and the special kills are all fun and have great tribute to the movieConsAs it is a new game you have bugs that need patched When you first start you go against pre release players who are already in their level 50s with the broken clown gunsclown guns could use some stat fixes for sureYou don't start with a weapon if they would add where u get loot boxes to get starting items the game would be 10 times betterThe spawns are broken as you can be a human and spawn right on top of a klown with no weapon and be dead in the first 2 minutesOverall the game will have a place in my heart so will the movie but with those given it is a brand new game so many things will have to be fixed and if you are wanting the game to play right now you will have to deal with the issues till they are fixed all that set aside I do recommend the game as if you are playing with friends its a hell of a time.

_childDocuments_.review: Not only is this game an absolute bore, it feels completely void of fun.  The tutorials are so lacking you actually have to waste time in the game trying to figure out what you're supposed to be doing.  You spend a large amount of time in the lobby's or in the death screen playing the very boring, and extremely repetitive mini-games that you don't actually get to play the full game.It feels like you're playing a mmo running quests most of the time because you're just going back and forth between point A to point B to point C.  You don't get to choose whether you're a Klown or a human, its completely "random" but as many noted when I was playing most times they find themselves playing humans than Klowns.It's laggy, it's buggy and many of the games I played you found yourself teamed up with bots or being dropped into a nearly complete game only to be killed once you've been spawned and now you're at those really repetitive mini-games they put in to burn time up.This game is ABSOLUTELY not worth the crazy amount of money they are asking for it.  Many people have said it feels a lot like the Friday the 13th game (never played it but know it wasn't great or well received).Oh, and they never implemented the "if you're a human when the actual players of Klowns are talking, you'll only hear the Klown language" that they advertised a lot.A lot of people have been, well they will patch issues on June 4th when the game officially releases.  If its this boring/lacking then it should have been postponed till it wasn't and not convince people to buy it early so they can use them as unofficial beta testers for it.  They had an extra year to get this game in a great place and they still flopped on that.If you're rich, burn your money away and buy it, but if you've been excited to get this game, wait till it goes on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm gonna start off by saying this game is like, 3.5/5, it's not a 'bad' game but it has a lot of room to improve balance wise, bug wise, etc. I don't want to give a negative review so early on, because that would feel unfair to a game that's just come out. I've had fun on the game.Some things that need to be added are:-Ability to make friends on the game, cross platform.-A proper tutorial to teach you how to play-ROLE QUEUE. This game could improve so much from Role Queue. Not everyone wants to play Klown, not everyone wants to play Survivor. Some want to play both.-We should be able to view Challenges in lobby so we know what we can do for each role.-Better skill checks, not necessarily with more buttons but definitely something seems off with timing.-The sound effects are a bit off, not easy to tell what direction what you're hearing something in.-Network issues-There's a weird effect after you've been cottonized that makes it so you can't hear and everything sounds muffled, even post mortem and post escape, and recently I've been getting issues with being able to do anything when cottonized effects have worn off.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is definitely enjoyable and even more so if you queue with a friend, but honestly the fact that klowns can just kill you after you get downed once seems like such an easy way to win for the klowns. I understand this game already gets a lot of dead by deadlight similarities, but I genuinely think klowns should have to hook a survivor at least once before you can get the choice to execute them, similar to how dbd has the whole mori stuff. Another thing that bugs me a little is the fact that you still make considerable amounts of noise by just walking. The only way to not make noise as a survivor is to crouch, which to me seems like a very slow way to play, even though you get a good amount of time to try to survive, especially because of how big most maps are and the amount of places where escape route items could be hiding.On the other hand, if you can hang around with your fellow survivors, most of these issues are easier to deal with, which is what I assume the developers intended, but there is only so much you can do once a klown gets the execution animation.

_childDocuments_.review: A Nostalgic Masterpiece: Killer Klowns From Outer Space: The GameKiller Klowns From Outer Space: The Game is a brilliant homage to the cult classic 1988 film, delivering a perfect blend of nostalgia and innovation that fans of the movie and newcomers alike will absolutely adore.From the moment you launch the game, it’s clear that the developers have poured their hearts into recreating the bizarre, colorful, and eerie world of the Killer Klowns. The graphics are superb, capturing the campy yet creepy essence of the original movie with remarkable fidelity. Every detail, from the Klowns' outlandish costumes to the eerie carnival environments, has been meticulously designed to immerse players in this quirky universe.Gameplay-wise, Killer Klowns From Outer Space: The Game offers a unique and engaging experience. The asymmetrical multiplayer format is a stroke of genius, pitting a team of humans against the formidable Klowns. Each Klown has its own unique abilities, mirroring their on-screen counterparts, which adds a strategic depth to the game. Whether you’re setting up diabolical traps or trying to escape the Klowns’ outlandish contraptions, every match is thrilling and unpredictable.The sound design deserves special mention. The iconic, chilling soundtrack from the movie has been brilliantly reimagined for the game, heightening the tension and adding to the overall atmosphere. Voice acting and sound effects are top-notch, further bringing the characters and environment to life.One of the game’s standout features is its attention to fan service. The developers have included numerous Easter eggs and references to the movie, which will delight long-time fans. However, even those unfamiliar with the film will find the game’s humor and style incredibly entertaining.The game also boasts impressive replay value. With multiple Klowns to master, various human characters to play, and a range of maps and modes, there’s always something new to explore and enjoy. The frequent updates and planned expansions ensure that the game will continue to evolve and offer fresh content.Killer Klowns From Outer Space: The Game is a triumph in the realm of movie-to-game adaptations. It captures the spirit of the original film while delivering a modern, engaging, and highly entertaining gaming experience. Whether you’re a die-hard fan of the movie or just looking for a fun and unique multiplayer game, Killer Klowns From Outer Space: The Game is a must-play. Prepare to be enthralled by the madness of the Klowns and the thrilling challenge of surviving their wacky, whimsical, and deadly invasion.
