_childDocuments_.review: This is game is pretty boring tbh. It's like a worse version of Friday the 13th.The maps are too large. You spend most of the match running around looting for supplies to escape. Victims can gang up and abuse Klowns. Victims can also crouch/walk the entire match to remain undetected from Klowns since they only see noise from running.Klowns are slow and weak. Lure is the only useful ability.Lastly, there are mixed info about whether or not you get XP after leaving a match. It seems that once you die or escape, you have to watch your teammates finish the match or else you won't get any XP. Other people are saying that you get it anyways even if you leave. I'm not sure, but the gameplay loop itself is boring.The map is way too large. Boring for Klowns and Victims tbh. Only fun to be had is to gang up on Klowns.If you're looking for an asymmetrical horror game, the best one gameplay wise is Texas Chainsaw Massacre. TCM has lobby issues and can be glitchy, but the gameplay loop is much more fun than Killer Klowns and the maps in TCM aren't overly large.

_childDocuments_.review: Hey guys, I have a decent amount of experience with asymetrical coop horror games, 1000+ hours in DBD and TCM. I played this game months ago at PAX East. While I say I recommend this game, it means I've had fun, but right now in its current stage (pre-release) there are definitely some changes that need to be made. I would have chosen a middle of the road rating if steam offered that. Lets start with the things that are good. Great size of the match being 3v7, good selection of maps, rewarding ranking unlocks, some player building mechanics. Character creation is relatively elaborate and allows you to make a unique character. The way you can kill the klowns is great. In-game chat is genius and a lot of fun. I love the mini games that you can play to have a part in the game even when you're dead. Custom games are nice. Melee combat is smooth and satisfying. Klown tricks are fun. The fact that it is random on if you are a human or klown is nice to you don't just get a sweaty killer. On the downside, the killer klowns are extremely overpowered. With just 15 hours of playing the game, they get weapons and tricks that give you no chance at surviving. It is luck based for humans on if you find anything to get you out of the map. People can be stingy and take exits from you. People who die with items often disrupt finding exits. Sometimes humans can wait in a bush till the end of the map with a soda and leave without searching for anything which defeats the purpose of the game. The baby klowns can be way too much with the area they cover and agro radius they have. The other thing is this game is in a pretty broken state, not the worst launch I've played, but I've experienced major server issues, I've lost out on 2 human survives because of a disconnection. My gun sometimes doesn't fire, most survivors miss all their shots, I don't think I've witnessed a real gun kill. I've been stuck in crouch before, I've been stuck facing one way. There's a lot, but this is at pre-release. My main concern is balancing the game. If I am a killer, it's just significantly easier to win, perhaps that will change on skill level.My verdict is this game has great potential, it just gets frustrating at times. It is fun and wacky and the aesthetic is fantastic. The vibes are immaculate. I love the team, attention to detail, and the collaboration between the films creators. This is a game that I would imagine is going to be a great game to get into. I can't wait to see the kind of support it gets. I like this game overall more than TCM, which gets very sweaty, where this feels like an arcade game. If you like co-op horror then you will like this game. It has charm. I only hesitate because it is kind of expensive and it has its issues.
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Klowns from Outer Space: The Game

_childDocuments_.review: I received the product as part of a donation to .I've watching the movie so many times. I've been in love with it since I was kid. I had really high expectations for the game, and boy were they met.The only bug I noticed was when I would try to throw a door to escape the clowns and it would move me outside the room with the door.I loved everything about this, and how consistent it is with the movie! _childDocuments_.review: I love it, but it needs changes. More variety would be amazing! Give classes more than just stat changes, like specific perks or abilities. this goes for humans and klowns. I definitely believe that it could take a few notes from DBD, though they are incredibly different. Like, a way to make humans stay in the match longer. Currently it feels a bit too much like RNG being the reason humans either leave immediately or take until klownpocalypse to escape, making that more consistent would be great, though I definitely would love to keep as many RNG aspects as possible. this is a casual game after all, and the more variety in games the better! DBD also allows you to choose roles, though I dont know if that would bode well for this game. There are times where I just want to play human, and the game gives me klown, which can be annoying. Overall though, due to current player counts and the amount of players required for a lobby I do not believe that this would work. It would take way too long to find a game without bots, which is frustrating, but its just how it is. Maybe one day? There's also a problem with postgame just being too damn boring. I feel like this could be fixed, though it may need a few sacrifices. Right now it sort of feels like an obligation to stay, as after escaping if you leave then your win doesnt count towards the "human victory", and you can't give items to other humans. On the other hand if you leave after dying, then you cannot be revived, and someone new can join the game who is instantly alive, making it harder for klowns to win. My ideas to fix this would be a few changes: firstly, remove backfill. This may help you find games faster but its just not fun for anyone. Secondly, let humans who left to count towards "human victory". Thirdly, allow humans to load into a new game after escaping while they still spectate, letting them give items to other humans before they find a new game.Another more experimental idea would be to put two resurrection machines on the map with only one use between them, in order to let players back in easier to the gameplay. You could also keep the one machine, but give it a certain amount of resurrections with multiple uses. for example, one resurrection machine that has seven charges. if two people are dead it will use two, and five will remain. it would prioritise humans who havent been resurrected yet. I do not truly know how these would affect the balancing though, so they might have to come with some nerfs.In conclusion, this game is really fun and really silly, but it still contains numerous problems that need change. It will lose players if not fixed, which would be a terrible fate. All of these changes are just my opinion though, and lots of them probably would not work as well as needed, but they are just ideas. Lets hope the devs steer this in the right direction!

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR = I am personally having fun and the game has a few cool differences to make it stand out from other games in the genre but I would only recommend to get this game  if you are big into Killer Klowns or the killer vs survivors/asymmetrical genre since games like this tend to have a short lifespan dependent on content drip fed to the game. So if you don't have a group of friends to play with it, or are addicted to this genre like me i wouldn't bother since $40 is a very steep price for this game, released with bugs and unbalanced classes and weapons early access players get to use on new players on release.Rest of review \/ \/ \/The game is similar in some ways to other games they have made mainly F13th but this is its own game with a lot of things to make it unique. The best thing i like about the game is the mini games after escaping or dying to get other players items to help survive or even keys needed to escape.Survivors can be fun fighting back especially hiding behind corners with fully charged melee hits. but it tends to be frustrating to play since the clowns have some overpowered and unbalanced weapons (brawler class bounce caster, and popcorn gun). most of which needs a level 50 character grinded out (about 15 hours). so if you are getting into this upon release you will be behind everyone else and need to grind against top tier players. This will only get worse as more players learn the meta. Also survivors walk super slow and if you want to make any progress you have to run giving your position away. sometimes when they find you they use max stamina builds and can just keep running at you with a popcorn gun until you are dead with little counter play.Klowns are fun to play with powerful weapons as said before, abilities and kill animations referencing the movie. The choice of getting a kill or hooking the survivors is good. killing them gives instant pressure but they drop there items and can be revived later. while cocooning can delete items from the match and not be revived as long as they stay alive inside (they can die sooner though), giving progress to the endgame with lackeys to help and another objective survivors need to doAnother possible problem is not being able to queue as either class and it being up for rng can be annoying and bad for the longevity of the game (but good for queue times for now)the only clown i don't like is the tank since he is so slow you will never be able to get a kill unless you are defending an objective or they try to attack you.The game does not seem polished and like a beta right now. i have not had a bug every round i played but i had them pretty frequently.-List of bugs i found so far. from most game breaking/altering to least>The skill checks are not properly represented and say you missed too early or too late even if you are in the zone and pressed right click or left click>items spawned on the ground are unable to be picked up sometimes, especially knives. this was the most common bug.>Stuck while a human burst out of a cocoon i was carrying as i put it on the machine, and was not able to klown jump because i was under the machine. not able to play rest of round.>Glitched by getting hit carrying gas, so i could not swap to other weapons and i died>Walls you can straight up walk through, the biggest one i found was the bathroom on the city map where there is a secret room connecting the male and female side survivors can hide in.>Stuck while falling endlessly on a rock as survivor>some windows won't let you slow and quite climb through as survivor>pizza ability on klowns made my guns invisible and not able to use until i klown jumped>lackeys only sometimes ask to carry cocoons for you and if they do they don't hook them>sometimes flairs look activated but are not>more to be added if i find any-These are maybe not bugs, but bad design choice.>Players that survive and then leave the game takes away that players escape, allowing new players to join the game and die not showing that progress that was made. i'm not sure if leaving after an escape gives you xp either.>maybe not bug, but when last players are hooked and there inventory is full not being able to receive a knife from spectators to escape, they can stay on the hook and waste everyone's time. It should just end the game.

_childDocuments_.review: ===TL;DR===--------------The game is currently miserable, but with a bucket load more polish it could be really good.===Is it fun?===-----------------No, not really. The game generally consists of wandering aimlessly, which is boring as all get out. There are concrete objectives to complete as both human and klown (yes, with a k), but it's usually pretty hard to actually know where to go. And for new players, the tutorials leave much to be desired. The game is wildly unbalanced. Klowns are not overpowered, but generally have more guidance than humans via noise notifications and minion alerts. This means that they are more likely to succeed. That's not even to mention the weapons the klowns have which make it that much harder to survive as humans (popcorn gun, bouncecaster).    Humans have ways to see their objectives from afar, but without a compass, it can be trying to navigate the maps. And even with a compass, you still have to locate "escape items," which are placed around the map randomly, and which can be stolen by humans on their way out of a match via an escape route. It is genuinely a trying experience to find these items once one or two of the escape routes have been used up.===Why do I recommend the game?==-----------------------------------------I need Dead by Daylight to have a competitor. I need it to have a competitor that lasts for as long as it does and which encourages it to become a better version of itself. And I need this game to become a better version of itself too, because my only recourse for assyms being DbD is an even more miserable experience than playing this game. I absolutely need this game to thrive for the sake of my sanity. For the love of god, please buy this game.

But I suspect that’s sort of the point; the latest movie license to get the asymmetrical-horror treatment feels like it’s aiming for a wider audience than just the slasher crowd.Games like  and the long-running  deliver plenty of scares, and some pretty intense violence. But  — still my favorite example of the asym-horror genre — has really always been about the laughs. Like , , or , the  film understands its audience is on board for a bit of silliness, and the game nails that aspect of the property. The  video game always had its share of problems, but it got you laughing even at the most competitive, do-or-die moments.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this movie, the game....not so much.  If you liked Friday the 13th game, then you will probably enjoy this. Pros: -Runs fairly smooth-wide variety of items-decent amount of cosmetic items even in early access-Nostalgia factor hits hard-No grab/one-hit ability that I've seen like Friday the 13th had.Cons:-seems to be P2P based servers and that results in vastly different experiences in latency game to game.  One game can be buttery smooth, the next is rubberbanding constantly.-The Klowns abilities can be attached to other klowns, essentially making certain klowns power houses and others obsolete once they are unlocked.-The hit registration is super busted and doesn't register nose shots properly.-Weapon upgrades for Klowns are straight upgrades and over time will create extremely powerful builds for those that have dumped hours upon hours into the game, and at the same time there is no upgrades to human characters at this time, strictly unlocking new classes (different stats but not varied enough to matter) and cosmetics. -No ability to choose between Klowns and Humans at this time.  It's randomized, which honestly may be a good thing for the longevity of the game and queue times but I don't like being forced into a role I don't want to play.-The matches get super repetitive quickly.-No controller layout of button rebinding options in the settings.-No way to adjust which audio input is being used within the game.  Forced to use system default.-Not really the developer's fault but a TON of impatient people that ready up and force a game to start prematurely before a lobby is filled, handicapping the humans more than they typically are.  -By extension of the above, bots that are loaded into your game are literal bots.  They have zero game sense and will either run towards a Klown that is firing at them or walk away slowly instead of sprinting.  There's plenty more but those are the major issues I've found.  Overall, if you are a fan of Friday the 13th you'll probably enjoy this game for a bit.  If you enjoy a "Balanced" asymmetrical game then you may enjoy this for a bit as well but odds are you'll find yourself refunding right before the 2 hour mark like I'm doing.  Game will probably grow and the balancing and issues may be corrected but in it's current state I wholeheartedly do not recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't remember the last time I had this much fun over an online multiplayer game upon release.This video game is not perfect, of course. The lack of a playable tutorial can make the game pretty difficult to access for newcomers, especially when playing as Humans. There are also a couple balancing issues once the game released, but luckily these are easy to remedy.Otherwise, this game has a lot of potential and I'm already having a lot of fun playing it. Both sides are fun to play, even matches I lose the matches feel very enjoyable. The customization options are also great - I wasn't expecting too much from a game like this but I enjoy customizing both my Klown and Human, and the reward system makes me eager to play more to unlock more options for them.This game perfectly captures the formula of the original movie, not just in plot but also in setting. The developers truly capture the atmosphere of Santa Cruz and the 80s, and it's apparent in this that they put a lot of research into creating this immersive experience for players.Upon release, Killer Klowns has a lot of potential and is very enjoyable. Of course, like with other live-service games, this may change in the future, but at the moment, it's off to a great start, and I'm interested in seeing how this game develops over time.

_childDocuments_.review: Its hard to recommend this game in its current state. Bugs are to be expected but it also needs a lot of quality of life improvements for it to be something I can recommend someone spend $40 for.- A lack of being able to choose your role greatly hurts the overall fun for many players. Some massively prefer one over the other and not having that option when the competition does (TCM and DBD) is something that I, and many others believe need to change.- A ping system for both sides, but, especially the Klowns is almost a must. Many people don't communicate over the mic and Klowns usually need coordination to catch smart Humans the vast majority of the time.- The grind to unlock the characters in a game you already payed $40 for is ridiculous. If you're gonna make them unlockable, you should get them no later than level 15.- Few minor bugs but a few game breaking ones that cause people to be stuck in place, has happened twice in my experience and I've seen it happen to many others- Lack of a real tutorial makes it very unappealing to brand new players and can cause it to be difficult for some people to fully grasp what they need to doThose were the major things I could think of. Might've missed more. I do want to make it clear that this game has its moments and the casual fun aspect is very much there. But it needs quite a bit of tweaking, fixes, and more content before I can confidently recommend anyone buy it for its full price of $40.

_childDocuments_.review: The devs did a fantastic job capturing what make Killer Klowns such a fun IP. The game feels like a cleaner F13, things just handle better and don't feel loose or as janky.Gameplay-wise its probably the most fun horror asym active right now, it feels a lot more like a party game. The progression is great and each match has felt unique due to the amount of escapes, kills, and loadouts.The mini-games are a really fun touch for players that have been eliminated and a great way to keep them participating in the outcome of the match.There are some pretty balancing issues at the moment but nothing that ruined matches or any of the fun. From my experience the players didn't seem to abuse any of the overpowered weapons. The most important factor here is, BOTH sides are FUN. The other asym games seem to have a huge divide between 'Killer' and 'Survivor', here I dont anticipate things getting that way as both sides are just as exciting and fun to play. Overall this is a lot of fun if you like these kinds of games, solo or with friends.

_childDocuments_.review: As a Klown:You can become one of the Klowns.You can put humans into cocoons and turn them into cotton candy.Your boots have a squeak to them when you walk or run.You are able to use the Klown's rayguns.Blunt weapons look like either actual weapons or toys.One of the Klowntalities is literally you becoming a tornado. Another one is a sword balloon.You can play as ALL of the Klowns from the original 1988 film.Getting all of the cocoons on the generators triggers the Klownpocalypse early.The special Klown abilities involve teleportation up to straight-up hypnotization.There can be up to 3 Klowns at once!You can put cotton candy on escape routes, making it harder for the humans to escape.Your goal(s) are simple: Either completely max out all of the generators, or kill all of the humans.As a human:You can literally shoot the Klowns in the nose, which kills them.You have free ability to parkour over objects.You can break free from cocoons by using a knife.You are the only normal person/people in the game.One human  can bring back another dead human to life at any time (it can only be used once).Your voice becomes muffled when you are inside a cocoon.Your goal is simple: escape the Klowns in the ice cream truck.As both:The game actually supports offline mode.There are several different maps inspired by the original film. Multiple of them.The maps have so much detail to them, including the circus, which contains actual rides like the Octo-Spider.The soundtrack is banging, like, legit.The game's release shows MGM cares about their old, forgotten gems.Online mode is just as chaotic as ever. Maybe even more.The only problems I have with the game:The controls are sometines clunky and the AI needs serious work in private lobbies.KOTY (Klown of the Year) contender right here

_childDocuments_.review: As an avid fan of the film, I love this game! Much funner than Friday the 13th in my opinion. Which I found was too heavily favored to Jason. He could find the survivors much easier and teleport around to the escapes without issue. In this game it’s much easier to get around as a human without being spotted and the Klowns don’t automatically know where the escapes are. Which makes the game feel a bit more fair and forgiving to casual players. The graphics are great. Particularly the detail in the Klowns. But Illfonic always nails the killers, so no shocker there. The humans could use a bit of work, but the customization is fairly nice. Hopefully they plan to give us plenty more options in the months to come to really craft something unique. So far I’m feeling the maps. They are very large and resemble scenes from the movie. They will take a bit of time to memorize and even then some of the machines randomly move around to keep things fresh. I wonder how crazy it would be if the entire map was procedurally generated? That way each play through would be chaotic and unpredictable. I guess that would bring its pros and cons but anything to keep the playing field even and to increase its longevity I say. I love seeing the circus tent space ship all lit up in the distance in some of the maps. It would definitely be a shame if we never get a map that incorporate the interiors of it at some point though. As well as other unique maps that weren’t even in the movie. The gameplay itself is pretty satisfying. Being able to kill the Klowns is a nice touch you don’t see in most of these types of games. The escape points are plentiful, each allowing three escapes and are pretty easy to learn after a few matches. It took my group 3 attempts to finally realize we couldn’t just run across the bridge lol.One of the most unique parts of this game outside the plethora of strange Klown oddities, is the mini games you can play when you die. These games give you items you can keep if you are to be revived as a human, or can be given to the remaining surviving humans to help them fend off the Klowns and/or to escape. Can’t say I ever seen this mechanic before and it’s greatly appreciated. I do think adding some perks to the humans could add to the depth and individuality. But at the same time I could see them just making the humans OP as the game is already fairly balanced without them. Though hunting for those in Friday the 13th was definitely an exciting journey. Minus the people abusing bugs to level quickly. I did experience one game breaking bug in my 5 hours or so of playing where I fell through the world after my cocooned body was dropped from a Klown that was attacked. I ended up dying when my life meter expired but that Klown went on to be completely broken and couldn’t do anything after. Looked like he was stilll holding the cocoon lol. The Klowns abilities are pretty sick. Each catered to their class and utilize elements from the movie which I really appreciate. Along with being able to upgrade their weapons which does help the Klowns eliminate more of the humans from my personal experience. Still nothing seems to be overpowered as the Klowns are slower and tend to run out of stamina quicker than the humans do. If I were to change anything with the Klowns, I would allow the user to zoom out a bit when they are using the jump ability. Right now its too zoomed in for how large the map is and it can he hard to quickly look around. I would also tweak how often Klownalities can be performed. This is one of the issues that plagued Friday the 13th. Some players love to spam instant kills and in my opinion it kinda kills the game. Maybe one per 30 seconds, or base it off how many cocoons you have successfully hung, as right now there’s not a ton of incentives to cocoon players. If you did give them a 30 second limit you should probably reduce the revive cooldown to 30 seconds as well to balance it out. But really basing it on the amount of cocoons I think is the best way. Maybe 1 kill per 30 seconds if you have 0-4 cocoons and then 2 per 30 if you have 5-9 or something along those lines. Also adding the ability for Klowns to use a straw on the human cocoons to get some kind of bonus would be pretty dope. Not only because its an iconic thing from the movie, but again it would entice more people to cocoon humans and not just instant kill them. The minions that spawn from hanging cocoons is a nice touch and also gives some incentives to hang more. But I feel like they could be a little more impactful somehow. Although they can attack players, and even help bring cocoons to the machines; I feel like more impactful functions could be added. One of the biggest issues I had with Friday the 13th, was people ghosting. You would get a group of friends and one of them would randomly be chosen as Jason and they would intentionally ignore all their friends and only go after the rest of the counselors. Or they would be told where those players were hiding, etc etc. It really killed the game in my opinion. This is why I wish there was a mode where the Klowns could all be bots or vice versa. Trained on thousands of matches with players of different skill levels to give you an accurate difficulty setting. But that is asking a lot I know. The reason I bring this up is because they really do need to add an option where your group cannot be split up though. Where it would just keep searching for a match if it can’t currently find one with enough open spaces on one of the two sides. Which is an issue that kept happening to my group of three and was annoying the heck out of us. Another thing that I think is gratefully needed is the ability to see your teammates names from far away distances. This goes for both the Klowns and the Humans. I get the game is supposed to be hard when it comes to really knowing where you are but many of times we kept trying to describe where we were to one of your teammates and we had a hard time finding one another. The flare works but anyone can throw one on the ground and cause your teammates to run to a random part of the map thinking that it was directing them to something important. Which happens a lot with strangers and trolls. Other than these things, I think the game is looking pretty solid. I’ve had a blast playing it so far. Hopefully we eventually see more things from the movie, like the popcorn snakes, and the giant parade float like cocoon vacuum the Klowns march down the street with. Also we must get Klownzilla to play a role somehow! The Terenzi brothers showing up in the ice cream truck is a nice touch though, despite me yet being able to witness it. Maybe more attention should be put on that event occuring, like a short cutscene to make people aware its occuring. Anyways, as the game stands right now on pre release. I’m giving it a solid 8/10. I really hope it will have some longevity unlike Friday the 13th and Texas Chainsaw Massacre. These types of games notoriously die off pretty fast, sadly. You gotta get in early to enjoy the experience. But if they keep updating it then people will keep playing it! Maybe it will even inspire the much requested sequel or tv show to finally be made!40 bucks is a bit steep for a game that will inevitably die. And 20 dollars for the small DLC pack is really a slap in the face. But for a true fan like myself, I think the potential here and the fun it provides is well worth the price of admission.

_childDocuments_.review: Previously did not recommend:Given the below previous review, and the a) inability to report bugs that b) completely broke the game down during a match, and made a character (in this case a Klown) unable to move or play further, it was a fair assessment of the game at that moment.That said, thanks to some helpful users that read the actual post and pointed out that there was a place to report things that had, after I went looking, opened up reporting options it's only fair to re-visit this review.Changed to recommended:Since the changes from late May, and playing the game more, I've yet to experience further major issues.  It seems issues of abuse and/or game-breaking bugs have been eliminated in the first few days of pre-release.  And while I fully admit I have been stomped on both sides of play, it doesn't make the game any less fun to lose.  The gameplay loop and options within are pretty balanced if you know how to play, and both sides have big advantages and disadvantages. You can easily turn a game in your favor by working together and communicating with your team, and leveraging all the options when you need them most.Pros:- Very fun Asymmetric killer variant- It doesn't take itself too seriously, much like the old cult classic movie- Fairly faithful reproduction of the film- Games can turnaround for either side at any point- There's always something to do, even if you escape or die as a Human.- With all the above, I've yet to have a 'boring' match.- Competitive, but just the right amount - you don't need to be a pro to win.- Generally good community to date.- Still more polished on release than most recent AAA titles.- Bring friends. Seriously. Much more fun. Buy friends if you need to.Cons:- Despite the utility of in-game proximity chat, the toxicity can be overwhelming from some.- Not using that in-game chat can kill an entire team, so turning it off is a sincere crutch.- Still buggy/glitchy at times, especially in matchmaking, but seemingly minor.- Concerns about Dev abandonment long term.Overall, they addressed my major concerns at the time of initial writing, and the game remains fun and engaging. While this won't be my everyday go to - simply because it's not my favorite style of game to play - it will be a regular game to play.  It'll be interesting to see if this ever gets less exciting or enjoyable over time.  For now, my group of friends and I have a great time when we're playing.=Previous Review=I watched the game in the 24 hour pre-pre-release and was hyped enough to buy it so I could play today.  I loved Killer Klowns as a kid.  I wanted to get in this game as soon as I could today and start enjoying it. Unfortunately, watching a group of friends play doesn't reveal the ugly grease paint that is players attempting to break the gaming experience for others.  There are multiple bugs left in the game that devs didn't think about too much, in which Humans can completely lock up Klowns and render them unplayable - either sit and spin, never moving, or exit a game.  It's pre-release, I get it, and not everyone thinks of corner cases.  But the compounding problem makes it worse: there is literally nowhere to report these things to be fixed.I've looked over websites, joined Discords, tried talking to mods... nowhere can you say "This problem occurs in this circumstance because of bad player etiquette combined with game bugs - please fix these."  Until these kinds of issues have a way to at LEAST report them, stay away.  You lose half your Klown arsenal, or the rest of your match, with any player that knows how and is willing to abuse the bugs that remain in the game.This review subject to change if and when game breaking issues are resolved.

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately Killer Clowns from Outer Space: The Game didn't appeal to me. As a big fan of Friday The 13th: The Game I thought this would be a good replacement. As a human you look for various items that will help you escape and there are various exit options similar to F13. During this you are chased by clowns and there is the possibility of being revived by your team. The maps are beautifully designed and have a pleasant atmosphere. However they feel so big that you never find what you need to escape. Killer Clowns doesn't stand out from the asymmetrical multiplayer genre at all and in my opinion the same mistake is made here as with F13. There is hardly any marketing or updates and then everything slowly falls apart. What a shocker.The game is also not beginner-friendly. You are getting thrown in the middle of a match and you don't know what to do first. The controls are clunky both for the human and the clown. Frustration is definitely inevitable here. The player base is as small as a speck of dust and who knows if the servers will even run for much longer. You can find lobbies quickly thanks to crossplay but half of the lobbies are filled with bots. The game costs almost €40 and DLCs worth €60 are offered - it's absolutely not worth it. They simply tried to develop a new Friday The 13th: The Game with another horror franchise and you really recognize a lot of things that were quickly adopted. But that somehow went wrong. You can only unlock a few cosmetics, weapons and new stats, but that's not satisfying in the long run. The game is neither fun nor do I see a future in this title.

_childDocuments_.review: Killer Klowns from Outer Space: The Game, is an asymmetrical multiplayer horror game that brings the cult classic 1988 film to life. Players can choose to be one of the three Killer Klowns aiming to harvest humans or join a team of seven humans striving to survive the extraterrestrial threat.Pros:Faithful Adaptation: The game captures the quirky essence of the original film, delivering a nostalgic experience for fans. Engaging Asymmetrical Gameplay: The 3v7 dynamic offers a fresh take on the genre, providing varied experiences for both Klowns and humans. Humorous Elements: The game incorporates comedic aspects, such as the Klowns' squeaky shoes and cartoonish boot prints, adding a lighthearted touch to the horror theme. Cons:Limited Content: With only a few maps and modes, the game may feel repetitive after extended play. Balancing Issues: Some players have reported that the Klowns can be overpowered, making it challenging for human players to survive. Technical Glitches: Occasional bugs and performance issues can disrupt the gaming experience. In conclusion, Killer Klowns offers a fun and nostalgic experience, especially for fans of the original film. However, its limited content and balancing issues may affect long-term engagement.Score: 4 out of 5 cotton candy cocoons—sweet and sticky, but not without a few tangles.

_childDocuments_.review: TerribleEdit: Okay I was fairly drunk when I wrote the original review.  But I want this game to succeed.  I had a lot of fun playing it with my friends after it first went live but eventually the myriad of bugs, lack of features, and slow progress in changing anything have made me entirely uninterested in playing it.  Features - The company released a roadmap a few months back and they promised a "exciting new gameplay feature" to come in September.  This ended up just being controls remapping.  There are dozens of cut features from the original anouncements and it feels disingenuous to call out control remapping as an exciting new feature when its something that should be standard.  Bugs/balancing - Hitboxes on various models are borked, balancing has been incredibly inconsistent, and attempts at fixing bugs often introduce new bugs or don't solve the actual issue.  For example, players would quit out right before dying for the first few months of the game.  This robs the Klown of a kill credit, allows the same person to rejoin, and for humans to cheese their way to a victory.  No humans escaped but 4 of them quit by the time the game ends?  Human victory!  This was eventually fixed (5 months after release) and the new version has allowed double the amount of people in matches.  Balancing gets one change, that later gets reverted back.  Or my favorite recent example - hit boxes have been incredibly buggy since the launch.  So they shortened the reach on some items... instead of fixing the hitbox.  What?  All in all, what I have seen them do in the 4-5 months this game has been around- add a micro transaction shop with a premium currency- eventually patch out the people quitting issue- add 1 map that I never got to play because it just never showed up in rotation for reason??  I played 30 games that first weekend it launched and never saw it.  Overall, I know this is a small studio, but it feels like the focus isn't in the right areas and the meaningful change necessary to improve it is going to take too long that I've given up.  Maybe in a years time, who knows.

_childDocuments_.review: I’ve been playing since pre-release and here are my thoughts:This game is a fun concept, cool design, graphics, and sound. However it is extremely unbalanced in these ways -1) No MMR, on your first day you can get grouped with level 50+ people. Given that Klowns get godly weapons at 50, this is very discouraging for new players.2) Much harder to learn human side. 3) There’s no separation of spawns. As a human who spawns in with nothing you can be right in front of a Klown that automatically spawns with weapons. 4) No noticeable imperviousness to damage when being released from a cocoon so you can immediately get downed again. This is an unfair advantage in favor of Klowns. 5) As Klown you need to work very closely with other Klowns if you’re going to be one of the classes like Tank. In general playing Klown feels like you need to work very closely together to secure kills or cocoons which isn’t possible often. 6) No pinging system for Klowns to help each other. 7) Interactions with objects like ground items or doors is very particular. You have to be faced directly at the door you’re trying to close and have the “e” button be on the exact right area to do what you need. 8) No key rebinding. So if you have a hard time reaching shift or control or E or whatever for whatever reason and would normally put things on your mouse you’re SOL.

_childDocuments_.review: DAY 1 PATCH UPDATE:It pains me to say this as I am a HUGE fan of the franchise and had a lot of hope with this game. But where it stands now even with the day 1 patch, I cannot in good conscience, recommend it unless it's on a steep discount. The game has A LOT of potential for the genre as long as Illfonic doesn't do their usual BS. Will update review accordingly and reasonably so, as this game progresses through patches.The game was fun, goofy and somewhat stable in the early access. The day 1 patch however, has ruined the game in many ways. The only two viable Klown weapons were nerfed into the ground. To counter this, a few fixes were made on the human side such as blunt objects no longer popping Klown noses (shouldn't have even been a thing in the first place).They also apparently changed key escape item spawn rates so that they aren't spawning near exits. But this is not true and probably broken as well atm as I find key items in the open next to objectives. All they had to do besides the nerfs to Klown weapons, was to also buff the other terrible Klown weapons. Which they did for two but it's barely noticeable. Klowns basically have no tools now and get jumped by Humans constantly. It has become a respawn timer simulator even when triple stacking Klown presence in a team fight.Other issues persist such as Klowns having super long animations without invincibility during said animation, so humans can just beat them up for free. Example: Klown Jump teleporting. Meanwhile Humans seem to be able to interact with escapes while being hit and stunned.The Trapper Klown class does not have traps of any kind and all mention of them in the game text, have been removed such as the challenges for it being changed to something else entirely. Because of the core class changes they made between builds when Illfonic took over, it is clear some of those classes were built around perks and upgrades that are now missing. An example would be the Tank class which is terrible and has no benefits to a Klown comp. The reasoning for removing the perks/upgrades is poor balancing. It makes sense in a way when you look at other games such as TCM or DBD. But I don't fully see it as the sole reason. I think what it is, is they don't want to put effort into fixing the game design flaws. Perks are good when balanced because it adds diversity.In my opinion, it's clear to me that Illfonic will continue doing Illfonic stuff when they release a terrible day 1 patch but take the time to add in paid cosmetics ON THE FIRST DAY OF FULL RELEASE. Some would argue that buying skins incentives them to make the game better, but this is not true and all you have to do is look at Predator Hunting Grounds or even another game/studio like TCM/Gun to understand that logic does not hold up.Outside of balancing, the game performs spotty now. I have a 3080 rig and it stutters heavily for some matches even on medium. I could play maxed out during early access week. It could just be server performance but idk for sure. The game also has a weird ghosting issue that happened even in early access. I know for a fact it is not my monitor or settings as I have no issues on any other games, and have also tested every setting combination possible. It doesn't ruin the game but it is still annoying nonetheless. It only happens on the menu btw. I have not seen it in matches yet.EARLY ACCESS REVIEW:The game is fun and goofy. Made by fans for fans. Surprisingly stable with minor bugs. Occasional server issues. HOWEVER with this being early access week, there are major issues I currently experience and see with this game long term. Will update review accordingly and reasonably so as this game progresses past early access.Without a preference queue in the early access, everyone is leaving Human lobbies to re-queue for Klowns. Getting Klowns is near impossible. I have played Humans at a 20-1 ratio if not worse which is absurd even for early access. This NEEDS to be fixed and will be fixed once a preference queue is added with the day one update. Sad that the preference queue was not here for early access.Another issue is the longevity for this game. There isn't a whole lot to grind for so once you max out (which is relatively easy and I have seen people day two already maxed out), the only other thing to grind for are the challenge booklets (cosmetic unlocks) which can also been done very quickly. Apparently this game was supposed to have a perk/upgrade system but was removed due to balancing issues? I get why cuz all you have to do is look at the disaster that became Texas Chainsaw Massacre with their meta. But come on, just balance as you go and don't let a meta rot the playerbase to death. At the bare minimum, some form of mastery challenges for, I guess, more cosmetics. That way people have incentive to keep playing beyond revisiting the occasional "fun" 6 months from now.There are balancing issues I have noticed but I think it is still too early to tell. My first thoughts being the fight or flight response this game has. It's not really cat and mouse, but more so run or fight. Fighting as Humans is infinitely better if you stay together but randos never do. As Klowns, it feels like the first two cotton candy rayguns are pretty garbage when I can just popcorn bazooka spam or beat them to death with a hammer if they challenge me 1v1. In my opinion, humans lose cotton candy from their bodies, way too quickly during chases. The higher the cocoon meter gets, it would make more sense to have it be stickier and harder to auto remove. I have seen Humans reset the entire meter back to zero within 2 seconds if they just take a sharp corner to break the raygun beam pathing. Not sure if this would be wise to change though when popcorn bazooka is as braindead no skill as it is now. Free infinite chasing into kill confirm weapon. Super easy to kite Human turn around melee engagements. On top of XP farm. Not sure why it gives so much XP but it does and EVERYONE is abusing it. Can't really afford to be picky though with balancing when it's still early access. Hopefully balancing actually happens.Overall, I still recommend this game. Whether or not it is worth the $40 price tag, is up to what you are seeking in a game. For me it was easy as I am a die-hard fan that wants to support the franchise and breathe more life into it. I give the early access a 8/10 as it is mostly stable and is a lot of fun. Just PLEASE do not let this flop and dry out.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game, but that's not to say this game is great. Currently, there are no punishments for people leaving mid-match, which can screw over either team. Also, sometimes the queue will drop you into a game already in progress, which can be unpleasant for the person queuing for the game. While the Klowns can be fun to play, some of the weapons seem to have a weird hitbox that doesn't always feel polished. The spawning system needs to be worked on, because there have been times where humans will spawn right next to a klown and be immediately killed/cocooned because of a lack of time to find weapons or evade the klowns. All those negatives don't mean there isn't a good game to play here. Being a human feels pretty well balanced, as even alone, an experienced human can run, hide, and fight a klown. In groups, humans can be extremely difficult to deal with, but a well coordinated group of klowns can still hold their own and fight the humans. The gameplay can be a lot of fun, with plenty of escape options, and a variety of tricks and weapons the Klowns can equip to take down humans.There are a few things I'd like to see in the game to further improve it:- Balanced spawns- Ability to change selected character loadout in the lobby (so you can balance the classes of humans and klowns in a game)- More refined weapon hitboxes for Klowns- In game trackers for challenges - Spawn with items (maybe each class gets a spawn item, like a branch or a burger or an energy drink)- Change the menu music option (I just want to hear the KKfOS theme song)- punishments for leaving the game mid-match- Refined party creation.I think right now this game is good, but it still feels like an early access game. If the devs can work on the current issues and come out with timely updates to balance the game and refine the experience, this game will be a must play. Right now, its still a fine game, but I wouldn't buy it if the issues stated in my or anyone else's reviews deters you.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a huge fan of DBD (6k hours across 2 platforms) and have dabbled in other asym games, but none of them really stuck for me the way Dead by Daylight has. Killer Klowns doesn't quite match up to DBD in my eyes, but that doesn't mean it isn't extremely fun. All things considered, it's a great new take on asymmetrical games, and it's the first one other than DBD that has really interested me and encouraged me to put in more than just a few hours.Here's my take on the game, including what I think is perfect as is and what should change: It's refreshing to be able to fight back as a human, something that you're scarcely able to do in DBD (of course, you have pallets on your side, but that's nothing compared to being able to whip out a shotgun). It's also great to be able to verbally communicate with teammates - and the Klowns, for that matter - via proxy chat. It can get toxic at times, but that's unfortunately inevitable in any game with voice chat. Thankfully it also allows for some really hilarious moments that Dead by Daylight doesn't owe itself to thanks to its eerier aesthetic. The ability to escape through multiple different routes is pretty great, too; this mechanic lends itself to some really fun plays, and usually encourages the humans to work together to maximize the number of escapes.(Usually. Until some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ decides to leave on the boat you provided the Gas for... Of course, this game has players who don't look out for their teammates just like all others.) Playing as Klown is also pretty fun, but it's a bit hard starting out, since leveling up allows you to unlock substantially better Klowns and weapons and you start out with a loadout that is just okay. Getting killed as Klown is frustrating, but it tends to happen a lot as you're finding your footing. Thankfully, you can respawn after a short while, and you have no limit to the number of times you can die. The Klown abilities are quite fun and are all useful, and add an element of strategy past just aiming with your Cotton Candy Raygun. I would like to see the Klowns have just a bit higher movement speed to make it easier to catch up to survivors; at early levels, using the Raygun while trying to catch up to humans can feel utterly defeating. However, the game does seek to balance this by making it a little easier to take down humans as a group of Klowns; the game really encourages teamwork and communication no matter which side you're on. Killer Klowns is definitely a game where you may feel a little out of your element in your first few matches, especially if you didn't play through the tutorial, but you'll catch on fast and find the grind pretty rewarding as you learn new strats and level up. I don't know that it has enough content at this point to warrant a $60 price tag, so I might skip the Digital Deluxe edition, but if you like Dead by Daylight, the base game is worth a try and will likely feel like a refreshing alternative to the DBD grind.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game, I love the movie, but there are some big inconsistencies with the game in terms of physics, hit-boxes and combat items. Weapons -Jawbreaker mace is incredibly powerful and only takes 3 extremely easy hits to down a player since it stuns and staggers Humans. Guns seem to be flimsy with the accuracy. Air-horns are buggy and sometimes won't work on Klowns.Klowns can sometimes be aiming at a player with a cotton candy gun and their aim tracks the player even around corners, I've experienced this a few times, I'm not sure if this a bug or is from cheaters but me & some friends have experienced this.Physics & Game Mechanics- Klowns can break a Human's game by stopping their interactions and Humans have to search or hide in something for it to fix.Fear mechanic is inconsistent and doesn't make sense and occurs randomly. The environment, particularly at Klown Camp and the other Forest map, vertical areas such as rock foundations and hills will bug out both sides and it takes WAY too long for a character to fall down or return to normal movement and Klowns can still hit humans where as Humans can't even try and shoot or swing a weapon because they're "falling" and can't do anything during this animation.The LOL Ability I don't know if this was nerfed or is bugged, but after using LOL the invincibility duration seems to be ineffective because not even after a second of activation, 1 gun shot or Sharp melee swing knocks a Klown down. This makes the ability incredibly useless in scenarios of player chasing or a Klown getting jumped by 2 or more Humans, which occurs VERY often, almost every match.Afterlife Arcade / Hands of Fate -A very interesting take on spectating games and a very helpful one at that...at least....most of the time.The minigames are very fun, easy to both understand a play, however.The reward system is very terrible.I have intentionally played horribly in certain games [Sequencer] and given players, Shotguns, Fire-pokers, Knives, Energy Drinks, and I've played with full intent to help & win [Simon Says], I can get 100% accuracy and hit the most sequences in the max allotted time, and I get, Tennis Balls, Baseballs, Flares, and Tree Branches, WHY ARE WE REWARDING THE EXACT OPPOSITE WAY IT SHOULD BE. Balls are the most useless items in this game and they're THE MOST FREQUENT REWARDS regardless of how well you did in the mini-games. Suggestion to fix the Hand of Fate; Card rewards shouldn't be a 'choose one of 3,' rather a reward upgrade system. Play a minigame, and how well you did, determines the level of reward your mystery item will be.Play sequencer, get an accuracy of 65%, your reward; 60% chance of common item [Wrenches, Flares, Baseballs, Tennis Balls, etc]25% rarer item [Metal Pipes, Baseball bats, or Stamina/Health item]10% Strong Item [Fire-pokers, Knives, Revolver, etc.] 5% chance for Escape Item [Key-card, Gate Key, Spark Plug, etc.]Klowns -Shorty [The Brawler] is by far the only Klown you should be using in this game, because he is the fastest Klown with the most Stamina and he is unbeatable with the Bounce-caster and Jawbreaker Mace. This makes the game incredibly unfair, and un-fun for Humans because even with an energy drink equipped, if Shorty is close enough in proximity, you're done for. Either; Shorty needs to be tweaked with the Stamina Management, or the Jawbreaker Mace and Bounce-caster need to receive nerfs, because this easy to unlock pairing, is a devastating combination.Resurrection Machine - The Resurrection Machine is probably one of the best features for Humans in this game, but that's not to say it's not really bad either. I find when I play Human, unless I'm playing with friends, NO ONE uses the Resurrection Machine. The Resurrection Machine also seems to have a bug where if a human died at least 10 seconds before the activation of the Resurrection Machine, this player will not re-spawn with the other Dead Humans.Speaking about the timing of the machine, why does it take almost a minute for the machine to activate? I don't think it should be a matter of timing, rather part assembling like you do with the exits, because as soon as a bunch of Humans are dead and the Machine notifies ALL players that it is now active, all Klowns have to do to make sure no one comes to use the machine, is camp. And that is SO BORING for both sides.Parts and Exits - While I appreciate there are 5 ways to escape the game, I think there should be some sort of change up with HOW you get those exits.- Parts - While finding Gas Cans, Spark Plugs and simply waiting for the Terenzi brothers isn't the biggest challenge in the world, I think that should change. I think there should be MULTIPLE Different part TYPES you need to repair exits. For example;I think for the exits, there should be more than just 1-2 parts required to repair and escape. The escapes should require the same amount of items, but add different types of repair items. Go in 1 game, and you reach the boat, you need Gas Can and a Spark Plug. Next game after you died or escaped, you go look for the boat again, you find the boat, you need Gas Can and a Boat Propeller. This would be a better way to shake things up and keep the methods of escape from going stale and leaving players just wanting to sit around and wait for the Truck while beating up Klowns.There's a few more things I'd love to talk about and possibly suggest, but I think I've gone too long already.Even after everything I've talked about, I still love this game, it's great, I'm still playing this more than DBD and TCM so you're doing something right LOL.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all gonna start with the pros, the game itself is very accurate to the movie, the map designs are nice, the cosmetics are great, The gameplay they are going for is very fun, but there are a few issues the devs need to address.Now for the bad:- The game has a horrible hacking situation, people are able to insta-down, insta-pickup, have unbreakable weapons, use speedhacks, get rid of cooldowns, and even prevent the bridge/tunnel from collapsing. It is incredibly easy to obtain the tools to do so, and people are even using these tools to target streamers and other folks that are either disabled,  LGBTQ+ or POC. - There are lots of balance changes that are needed. Currently several weapons on both sides are incredibly overpowered leaving either side very screwed when those weapons are in the right hands. Fortunately for Klowns some of these weapons are hard for the humans to find, but unfortunately for humans, a TRACKING gun is the strongest in the game. Klowns being able to perform a klowntality right away leaving the human in spectate mode for the entire match is a constant issue, and I would rather just quit and find a new lobby (It'd be great if I didn't get stuck in one with hackers though lol)- The BUGS and EXPLOITS. I don't know about you, but I absolutely LOVE it when I go to pick up a weapon and it gets stuck to the ground/table (not.) We had someone sneak through a wall into a bathroom where we couldn't reach them, and even kill me with a bat earlier. I'm glad I can't fall through the map in a cocoon anymore like before the day 1 patch, but I'd take that over my camera getting stuck in a weird angle after letting people out through the portal. Several humans have found a way to stunlock klowns in place where they cannot move, using their powers are next to useless, and using the Klown Jump doesn't help either, you just warp to another section of the map to stand there in the same spot unless some human who isn't in on it kills you.- The respawn timer. After a lot of thought, I just don't really like having to wait 45 seconds to respawn. The humans can do SO much in that amount of time that the game is able to end faster than you can respawn as Klown. I suggest trying 30 seconds instead of 45. The revival machine is in a fine and balanced state where it currently is though. A week ago my review would have been positive but now I just don't find the game as fun.

Compared to the previous games I'm finding it easier to play for longer sessions and don't feel tense or mad when playing as the rounds are quick and pretty high pace. Like Texas Chain saw, the proxy chat adds alot to the game, don't be surprised if Behaviour get an extremely original idea and add it into Dead by Daylight. Positives aside, meta gamers and sweats probably won't enjoy this one because it's "too casual", but that's for the better. Stick to DBD you freaks.While it has the odd bug and balancing issue here and there as the game leaves its first active week, the team seem both passionate to the game as well as the movie it's based on. I can only hope for the best in the games future, as I have really enjoyed the time I've spent playing it.

_childDocuments_.review: Sadly I cannot recommend this game right now, it is just far too buggy and somewhat unbalanced.Good: Proximity voice chat; more games need this. Light hearted, campy, atmosphere. Fun gameplay loop where-in both sides can fight the other. 3v7 means you can play with friends regardless of what team you are on. Able to play as Killer or Survivor when in a party, just like Dragon Ball Breakers before they shot themselves in the foot and removed crossteam queuing.Bad:Some of the killer weapons are notably stronger than others. The popcorn (shotgun) and bouncecaster (bouncing grenade launcher) are especially egregiously strong.Cannot change your keybinds. This isn't a big deal to me personally, but it is irksome.Killers (clowns) do not get a compass on their HUD for some dumb reason.Incredibly buggy (everything below).The latency mitigation (or lack there of) is troublesome to say the least. During skillchecks you will regularly miss a check despite being in the great or even just the good zone! Trying to aim for the center (regardless of good/great section) often doesn't even help to avoid this. Melee strikes will routinely just not apply damage despite being in the enemies face. I would say the same occurs with firearms, but frankly that could be me missing by a hair, so I'll chalk it up to that.Matchmaking has serious issues when you have a party of 4 or higher. After 4, you will routinely only get part of the team into a match. Leave, reform party, try again. Wash, rinse, repeat.Common interactions will softlock you. If a survivor happens to jump out of a cocoon while you are carrying them, at just the right time, you (killer) become permanently stuck for the rest of the game. If a survivor disconnects as you (killer) are beginning an execution, you will become permanently stuck. Being revived will sometimes just give you a 90% dark screen. You have to max your gamma slider out to temporarily work around it.Sound effects specifically have a tendency to cut out and just not come back. Music / Dialogue / VoIP are unaffected.Just insanely buggy, it's really sad because the game is fun.

_childDocuments_.review: DAY 1 PATCH UPDATE:It pains me to say this as I am a HUGE fan of the franchise and had a lot of hope with this game. But where it stands now even with the day 1 patch, I cannot in good conscience, recommend it unless it's on a steep discount. The game has A LOT of potential for the genre as long as Illfonic doesn't do their usual BS. Will update review accordingly and reasonably so, as this game progresses through patches.The game was fun, goofy and somewhat stable in the early access. The day 1 patch however, has ruined the game in many ways. The only two viable Klown weapons were nerfed into the ground. To counter this, a few fixes were made on the human side such as blunt objects no longer popping Klown noses (shouldn't have even been a thing in the first place). They also apparently changed key escape item spawn rates so that they aren't spawning near exits. But this is not true and probably broken as well atm as I find key items in the open next to objectives. All they had to do besides the nerfs to Klown weapons, was to also buff the other terrible Klown weapons. Which they did for two but it's barely noticeable. Klowns basically have no tools now and get jumped by Humans constantly. It has become a respawn timer simulator even when triple stacking Klown presence in a team fight.Other issues persist such as Klowns having super long animations without invincibility during said animation, so humans can just beat them up for free. Example: Klown Jump teleporting. Meanwhile Humans seem to be able to interact with escapes while being hit and stunned. The Trapper Klown class does not have traps of any kind and all mention of them in the game text, have been removed such as the challenges for it being changed to something else entirely. Because of the core class changes they made between builds when Illfonic took over, it is clear some of those classes were built around perks and upgrades that are now missing. An example would be the Tank class which is terrible and has no benefits to a Klown comp. The reasoning for removing the perks/upgrades is poor balancing. It makes sense in a way when you look at other games such as TCM or DBD. But I don't fully see it as the sole reason. I think what it is, is they don't want to put effort into fixing the game design flaws. Perks are good when balanced because it adds diversity. In my opinion, it's clear to me that Illfonic will continue doing Illfonic stuff when they release a terrible day 1 patch but take the time to add in paid cosmetics ON THE FIRST DAY OF FULL RELEASE. Some would argue that buying skins incentives them to make the game better, but this is not true and all you have to do is look at Predator Hunting Grounds or even another game/studio like TCM/Gun to understand that logic does not hold up. Outside of balancing, the game performs spotty now. I have a 3080 rig and it stutters heavily for some matches even on medium. I could play maxed out during early access week. It could just be server performance but idk for sure. The game also has a weird ghosting issue that happened even in early access. I know for a fact it is not my monitor or settings as I have no issues on any other games, and have also tested every setting combination possible. It doesn't ruin the game but it is still annoying nonetheless. It only happens on the menu btw. I have not seen it in matches yet.EARLY ACCESS REVIEW:The game is fun and goofy. Made by fans for fans. Surprisingly stable with minor bugs. Occasional server issues. HOWEVER with this being early access week, there are major issues I currently experience and see with this game long term. Will update review accordingly and reasonably so as this game progresses past early access.Without a preference queue in the early access, everyone is leaving Human lobbies to re-queue for Klowns. Getting Klowns is near impossible. I have played Humans at a 20-1 ratio if not worse which is absurd even for early access. This NEEDS to be fixed and will be fixed once a preference queue is added with the day one update. Sad that the preference queue was not here for early access.Another issue is the longevity for this game. There isn't a whole lot to grind for so once you max out (which is relatively easy and I have seen people day two already maxed out), the only other thing to grind for are the challenge booklets (cosmetic unlocks) which can also been done very quickly. Apparently this game was supposed to have a perk/upgrade system but was removed due to balancing issues? I get why cuz all you have to do is look at the disaster that became Texas Chainsaw Massacre with their meta. But come on, just balance as you go and don't let a meta rot the playerbase to death. At the bare minimum, some form of mastery challenges for, I guess, more cosmetics. That way people have incentive to keep playing beyond revisiting the occasional "fun" 6 months from now.There are balancing issues I have noticed but I think it is still too early to tell. My first thoughts being the fight or flight response this game has. It's not really cat and mouse, but more so run or fight. Fighting as Humans is infinitely better if you stay together but randos never do. As Klowns, it feels like the first two cotton candy rayguns are pretty garbage when I can just popcorn bazooka spam or beat them to death with a hammer if they challenge me 1v1. In my opinion, humans lose cotton candy from their bodies, way too quickly during chases. The higher the cocoon meter gets, it would make more sense to have it be stickier and harder to auto remove. I have seen Humans reset the entire meter back to zero within 2 seconds if they just take a sharp corner to break the raygun beam pathing. Not sure if this would be wise to change though when popcorn bazooka is as braindead no skill as it is now. Free infinite chasing into kill confirm weapon. Super easy to kite Human turn around melee engagements. On top of XP farm. Not sure why it gives so much XP but it does and EVERYONE is abusing it. Can't really afford to be picky though with balancing when it's still early access. Hopefully balancing actually happens.Overall, I still recommend this game. Whether or not it is worth the $40 price tag, is up to what you are seeking in a game. For me it was easy as I am a die-hard fan that wants to support the franchise and breathe more life into it. I give the early access a 8/10 as it is mostly stable and is a lot of fun. Just PLEASE do not let this flop and dry out.

Multi-player matchmaking allows players in the same party to be on opposite sides (both Klown and Human) in the same game. (Just today before writing this review I had 3 games in a row where humans and klowns were teaming and only killing the humans not in their party. For instance, I helped get the boat ready and we all got on, the person as the driver just sat there and waited for his klown buddies to jump to the boat and cocoon 2 of us off the boat).3.) Advanced Access isn't as advertised. This build feels like a beta, and is riddled with bugs (some game breaking), like if you crouch and open a microwave, your character might end up on top of the microwave and you can't move the entire match.)All in all, if you are like me and thought about buying the game because you are tired of the same old game loop of DbD, etc. at this point IT IS NOT IT. This game will only make you regret your purchase after the 2 hour refund deadline is crossed. It is fun at first until you actually realize the glaring issues. There will be a day 1 "patch" on the 4th... but unless the devs fix the 3 main things I listed above, the game will not last.

_childDocuments_.review: I look at this game like a fat kid looks at cake. All in all, it's an extremely fun, very well made game. _childDocuments_.review: Very fun game with good implementation of the asymmetric gameplay and incredible nostalgia factors.As the Predator, you are quick, agile yet strong and tough - but not invincible against good teamwork. The Predator has both beginner friendly easy-use weapons, tool, but also some high skill/high damage tools. There are weapons/tools to start/always stick with and stuff to master.As a Fireteam member (human), you stand no chance against the Predator in one-on-one fight - so you'll have to rely to your team. I personally always play with random teammates, and still manage to win. All you need is to get some basic things (Mudding up, using your ear, staying with your team) to become routines, then it'll be up to you and the team's overall abilities. From the start of the game, you'll have the itch to check the trees, listen to the noises - knowing that the Predator could be above you anytime from the start is thrilling.My biggest question was how good did the developers get the asymmetric-yet-authentic gameplay - IMO they nailed it! As the human team, you have options to get the job done - while all need some degree of teamwork, just like a real spec ops team. As the Predator, you are hunting, with the sole purpose of slaying your prey - using high-tech gadgets and/or with the good old wrist blades.The game also brings a very good amount of nostalgia factor, too. Musics, lines and a few cutscenes from the original Predator movie gives a nice plus for the experience. (And it also works backwards, when you rewatch the movie and notice these stuff in it.)All in all, if you like the Predator franchise and/or the asymmetric game style, this game will most likely be a good choice for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Predator: Hunting Grounds is an enjoyable and dynamic asymmetric 4v1 multiplayer game. I've been playing it for a year so far and while it has been a bit rough around the edges at times, the core gameplay is solid. If you enjoy Dead by Daylight or Friday the 13th you'll probably like this one. So far there are 5 maps and two modes, but each of the maps has different missions which cycle creating a varied experience. The Predator experience is in third person, with everything you'd expect from a Predator: heat vision, cloaking, an array of exotic weapons. The hit and run tactics, and wearing your prey down make for a thrilling hunt. As the Fireteam, you're part of a squad of four, with first-person gameplay. Completing a mission and dealing with hostile forces. Eventually the Predator will show up and things can go a number of different ways. If you're a fan of the franchise, Hunting Grounds has some great additions to the lore, with collectible tapes going through what has happened during this timeframe in the Predator Universe. This is also the first time we've seen Dutch back since the original film, voiced by Arnold himself. This game is by a smaller studio, so keep expectations in check, but they have said that a number of significant additions are being worked on. For a Predator fan like me, this captures the feel of the original film, with a gameplay experience that I continue to enjoy.Make sure to enable cross-play to help with the matchmaking wait times, but where this game really shines is when you go into private matches with four other friends and rotate as the Predator. Private matches get full XP as well.

_childDocuments_.review: Updated Review:Sadly, coming back to this game a couple of years later, it seems online is completely dead. Estimated wait time: 39s, Real wait time: 1m20s - then you get in a lobby, filled with bots and wait for players.. so yeah. I still recommend it, cuz its actually fun to play, but you should only buy it when its on sale for less than 10€.Old Review:This game is really awesome. A lot of people think its dead, because they just check the steam charts. But its crossplay, so you won't see all players via steam charts. After installing and playing the tutorial it took me like 40 seconds to get into a match, and that was not at a peak time. I've played now a couple matches and yes, sometimes it can happen that it gets you in a lobby and then you have to wait another 2-3 minutes to fill the lobby. But that happened only once out of 10 games to me. Usually lobby gets full pretty fast. (If i would have to compare, then i'm faster in the game then it takes to join a ranked match in R6 (for most of the time))As for the graphics, i agree the game is not very good optimized, but if you have a decent computer (i'm playing with a rx vega 56) you can still play with a pretty stable frame rate without having to turn down graphics to much. Its probably also possible to tweak the config files (Config files can be found in %localappdata%\SpaceFish\) manually but i haven't looked into that much right now as i'm totally fine with playing at 60fps.(more doesn't make sense anyway with a 60hz monitor.) For playing "hunt" game mode i'm having pretty stable 60fps, as for the fireteam vs fireteam mode  (don't know how its called right now) i did  noticed some fps drops and sometimes even stuttering. But that's also just simple math. It makes a difference if you play 5vs5 or 4vs1 - ofc it needs more performance with more players.I would recommend to get this game at sale, as its a good balance between value and price. If you liked asymmetric shooters like evolve 2 then you will probably love this game.As for the in-game loot boxes, this is only cosmetic stuff and you  will earn enough credits to purchase boxes by just playing matches (any you will get some boxes anyway for playing)So for all the haters out there, especially for those who've read some reviews like   - make your own opinion by playing it. Just test it and if you don't like it refund. Don't believe every ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ some wanna be experts have written, especially when they don't like the concept of asymmetric shooters at all. (Ofc it will take longer to find a match if you want to play predator. Simple math 4:1)  In the article linked above they complain about a lot of things which just shows that who ever wrote the article has little to no knowledge about asymmetric shooters or pc gameplay at all, so let me make some points clear:boring missions - Its not about the missions, its about staying alive while you do some tasks and hunt down the predator if possiblestupid ki -  i agree with that, ki is kinda stupid, but who cares in a pvp shooter about ki?unrealistic shooting - ehhh wait what? you complain about unrealistic shooting in a totally non realistic game? This ain't SWAT 4 dude.bad matchmaking - cant agree on that - sometimes you have a good team sometimes not. Sometimes predator knows what hes doing sometimes not. Also most players performance isn't constant across all matches.bad graphics - can't agree on that. Graphics a totally nice, an i'm not even playing on max graphics. _childDocuments_.review: Pretty fun! If you're an Aliens vs. Predator fan then you will love this game. I've been playing AvP type games on multiplayer since the first one back in '99. I always liked that one a lot because it was so easy to die. There was the newer ones but things just weren't as deadly and I thought they lacked a bit in that area, and then the player base was just non-existent for the past 10 years. So now that I just discovered this game, PlayStation and Epic Game players have been playing this game for a year and I've had no trouble match matching.As for the "deadliness" of the game, I mean it isn't like the old one but it can be pretty easy to die if you're by yourself as a human or if as a predator you just jump into the middle of a super aware and communicative fireteam.There are some really good high level preds out there, but it requires good planning, tactics, and skill to take them out. The bad part about this game is the smalll number of active players but luckily crossplay helps shorten the wait times, about 1 minute or less to play as a the fireteam but if you want to play as the predator it will take 4-5 minutes to find a match. As in many Playstation/Epic games titles you will come across the screaming child once in a while but there is a mute button. Wish this game had more players but at a discount I would say it's worth it for the Predator experience. have fun and don't forget to get to the choppa'.
