_childDocuments_.review: Having just gotten to level 100 in-game, I thought it was time to leave a review. I bought this game and a few of the premium packs around Christmas when it was on sale, I'd heard about it after pondering the ration of Alien games to Predator games and looking up if there were any Predator-based games. This was the main (and pretty much only non-AvP) game that showed up. Being more of an Alien fan than a Predator fan, I didn't expect to be enraptured by this game as much as I was! It's really helped me appreciate and enjoy the Predator franchise.For convenience's sake, I've split the review into two parts: part one will cover how it feels to a Predator fan, and part two will be general gameplay review. Feel free to skip the first part if you haven't seen or even don't wanna see the Predator movies and just wanna know what it's like as a game.**For Predator Fans**This is honestly arguably as good a love-letter to the original Predator as Alien: Isolation was a love letter to the original Alien. Much like the movie, the game revolves around a team of four players playing an elite fireteam on a mission deep in the Amazon rainforest. Honestly this game would be pretty fun if it was just this. However, there's a twist: they're being stalked by a fifth player: a Predator. It's very truthful to the source material, playing as a Fireteam really makes me feel like one of Dutch's men in the jungle. My only gripe might be there's not enough chance for the subtle horror and tension the second half of Predator had, but that's mostly because of what type of game this is. Honestly I don't really mind this at all and I can easily forget about it.As if that wasn't enough, there's even supplemental story! While the main game has little to no story (it's an asymmetrical shooter, not really much chance for it), there are audio logs you can find around the various maps to uncover more of it. My only gripe with the story is that the audio log format doesn't really work for the game, as you're only really able to find them as the fireteam and you're usually too busy trying not to die to worry about looking for them. Don't worry tho, as this only applies to the OWLF tapes, the Dutch and Isabelle tapes you unlock as you level up, which doesn't take THAT long. It only took me maybe 2-3 weeks worth of days played to get to level 100 and by that point all tapes were unlocked.**Part 2: Gameplay**As far as gameplay goes, it's REALLY fun. To address a big problem I see with asymmetrical shooters, it feels like a lot of the time you don't get to play "the big bad". As it's often up to a low random chance that you get selected to be "it", it's a long time before you get to be "it". However, this is NOT the case with Hunting Grounds. HG allows you to choose whether you are the Fireteam or the Predator every time! The only downside is it usually takes a couple minutes to find a Predator round, but I usually spend that time doing something else such as watching YouTube, opening field crates, or customizing my characters. On a bad day the waits can take over ten minutes, but I've found this is pretty rare, usually it takes no more than 5-6 minutes at worst.Either way, playing as either team is a blast. As the fireteam, you have to do certain missions while taking down (or avoiding) the predator. As you level up, you get better guns and tools to fight them, such as thermal smoke bombs or noisemakers. I personally prefer playing as the Predator but am always happy to play a round as the Fireteam if the wait times are too too long. ItAs the Predator, you have a LOT of tools at your disposal, as well as a lot of customizable tools and weapons. You also can unlock cosmetics and tools/weapons by opening field crates, which you get after matches. For both teams, cosmetics can also be unlocked with the in-game currency, or through field crates. Fortunately, Predators and the Fireteam do not have separate levels, so if you play a lot as one, you'll still get the level unlocks for the other. You could technically unlock all the Fireteam weapons playing exclusively as a Predator, or vice-versa. (Each Fireteam weapon has its own levels tho, which unlock upgrades like scopes and such.)It's a LITTLE tricky to get started in the early game, especially as the Predator, but not impossible. The tricks for each team are different.For fireteam:-STICK. TOGETHER. Honestly, the easiest way to die in this game is to get split up. I've beaten the Fireteam a lot, but the one thing most (if not all) the fireteams that have beaten me have in common is that they stayed together. Don't stick TOO close as you'll get bodied by an AOE attack, but stay within a few yards/meters of each other at all times.-Stay under cover as much as possible. The most difficult time for me as a Predator player is when the Fireteam goes inside buildings together. If you enter their building, it's easy for them all to shoot you and do major damage, especially when you have trouble finding your way out of the room they're in.-DO THE DANG MISSION. While you should never run away on your own to do a mission, your goal should be to finish it. If even one player finishes and escapes, it's considered a loss for the Predator. The quicker you can get it done, the less time the Predator has to kill you.For predator:-Really, it's just keep practicing and try to find out what your style is, then use tools, perks, etc. that compliment it. For example, I tend to prefer using melee attacks a lot, but also tend to forget to recharge my power. So, my perks buff my power and melee damage. I also tend to get decently hurt while dueling fireteam members, so I have a large bag to double my healing kits, in case I can't find any pigs.-Speaking of: kill pigs whenever possible. Pigs can heal you up quicker than medkits, are marked on the map when they die, and don't cost you anything to use. Having a few extra pigs around the map will really help you get out of a sticky situation.-If you're put into second wind (basically your last chance to run if your health is depleted), use your leaps to jump up cliffs. As the fireteam can't fly, it'll give them a harder time tracking you, giving you more time to heal and get back into action.There IS one more game-mode in the game called Clash, but I am not really qualified to comment on it as it usually has far to few players to play on it, so I won't say much on that.There's probably more I can say about playing the game, but that's really all I have to say for now. In short, I highly, highly, HIGHLY recommend this game to anyone who's a fan of asymmetrical shooters, even if you're not a Predator fan. It's one of the best asymmetrical games I've ever played, and it's really worth a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: Predator: Hunting Grounds is a 1 vs 4 game where a team of four special forces attempts to complete several military objectives in a hostile jungle environment before being picked up. The trouble is not the enemy mercenaries, its the predator hunting you throughout the mission. Its waiting for a slight mistake where you wonder just far enough away from the group to be hunted down, and the predator can get its trophy.Overall Predator: Hunting Grounds is a really good game. The graphics are pretty good, and its the best game from the franchise in a long time. Everything a fan of this series wants is present in this game, with more content promised to be on the way. Arnold Schwarzenegger is back to voice both a 1987 original movie character and a new 2025 older version of the character that has been scarred from years of tracking down predators around the world. There is even a pseudo-story that takes place sometime around the newest "The Predator" movie that is unlocked in-game through audio recordings that Arnold himself did. Players can also make their own character and customize them with a large variety of hats, glasses, clothes, and other accessories, or unlock other special characters. Human weapons consist of both older and newer weapons, like classics from Predator like the minigun, and newer modern weapons from Predators and The Predator. The predator class has the original movie skin, "City Hunter" from Predator 2, and other predator skins from the different movies like juvenile predators, some from the end of Predator 2 and the ones in Predators. Predators have different weapons and gear from the various movies, like the shoulder-cannon, disc, spear, net, and wrist blades. Special abilities including mimicing voices and the cloaking device to stalk prey in the trees are endless fun and essential to any good hunt.  Predator: Hunting Grounds has a great atmosphere, with dense jungle environments, mist, and the squeal of a pig in the distance just to scare you a little. A good predator player can make each match extremely intense and cinematic, with players firing their rifles into the jungle randomly as they are picked off. The game is only as balanced as the skill of the players, and many rounds end with an instantly defeated or instantly victorious predator, rather than an extraction or other ending. The game is very scary at times and a blast with a good team and experienced predator. The stock controls are weird, and graphics require some tweaking, but the game is worth its decent price. Many of the negative reviews call this game "dead", complaining of long wait times and inability to find servers to play on. I have never experienced an issue with finding a games within normal gaming hours, and cross-platform play allows for a constant pool of players from three different gaming services. While this may be a different negative for some because of the unbalanced pc vs console gameplay, it still allows for many players to be on at once.

_childDocuments_.review: Honest Opinion:This game is fun, but it has a lot of issues. For new players, it can feel like playing Russian roulette. There's no balancing—sometimes you’ll be matched with a group of level 1 players, and other times you’ll face opponents with many hours of experience.Match queue times are long, often taking 3-7 minutes depending on the time of day. If you're on a tight schedule, this can really add up. Those few minutes here and there quickly become 30-40 minutes of waiting instead of playing.The game is also filled with inconsistencies and bugs. For example, the shield only works about half the time, some perks are broken, and certain weapons are completely useless. It doesn’t capture the feel of a true Predator game—the mechanics and execution just don’t deliver. I refunded the game but gave it a second chance. While it’s playable, new players, even fans of Predator, might not enjoy it at all.Quick matches are too fast, and the AI is poorly programmed. This game would have been much better if it hadn’t followed the Dead by Daylight formula. A single-player game with co-op elements would have been more fitting. In the movies, the Predator carefully stalks its prey, but with the 15-minute timer and how fast the chopper can be called, rushing kills becomes the only real strategy.Overall, it’s not a good Predator game, and in my opinion, it’s not a great game in general.

_childDocuments_.review: Ehhh.It's just ehh, the game is nothing special, it's got plenty of flaws, but the premise is interesting, just not sure if it's $30 interesting.I honestly can't really say a lot about the game because there really isn't a lot of game to talk about. Two gamemodes, a traditional team deathmatch mode that isn't that great, and the main Hunt gamemode. A game of Hunt involves 5 players, a team of four soldiers, and a Predator. Each game the team of four get assigned a "random" set of objectives (They're all some form of go to location, pick up an item, wait for a timer to go down, pick up a second item, repeat all of that one more time, and then extract), meanwhile, the Predator has to do everything they can to stop the team of four using its tools, while NPC guerilla soldiers fight the soldiers (But oddly enough, not the predator).This is certainly an interesting premise, but it falls flat quickly. The predator's only means of dealing with the soldiers is through direct combat, whether that's shooting at them, or meleeing them. The predator cannot destroy terrain or create obstacles to split up the team, nor can the predator order the NPC guerilla soldiers to focus fire on a specific individual, and there is no way to disorient or confuse players.Of course, the predator gets plenty of free movement abilities to be able to better ambush players, and the game does actively try to encourage the predator player to pick off stragglers or alone players due to how the predator is balanced, being able to easily wipe the floor with an individual or two, but suffering against a team.This, however, becomes an issue because of those earlier mentioned objectives. no point does the team ever even have to consider splitting up, in fact, you can win basically every match as the soldiers just by sticking close to each other and not letting individuals rush off ahead or wander around cluelessly. The only time I've seen a predator win a match was due to one or two players either rushing off ahead and getting themselves (or the people they left behind) killed. Keep in mind, there is absolutely no reason to rush anywhere except besides finishing matches quickly. There are no timers, there are no player-specific objectives, there are no ways for the map to naturally split up the team at all, there is zero downside for the soldiers to just group up the entire match, meaning that, provided the team manages to stick together (which we've established to be very easy), the predator will have an incredibly difficult time in actually winning.Besides that, if you want to play a match as the predator, be prepared to wait. When I played, the predator queue was seven minutes. However, if you're just interested in playing as the soldiers, the queue for you is 25 seconds. In my opinion, the system just isn't that good. There is no good reason to allow players to specifically queue for whether they want to play as the predator or as a soldier.Now, aside from that, the game itself doesn't handle all that well? Like, the game looks nice, sure, but the gunplay, at least for the low-level weapons (You unlock weapons and equipment by leveling up), all feel super weak? Aside from damage output, which it seems the lower-level guns are far less effective than higher-level guns, the guns themselves have no oomph or feel to them, it feels like firing a slightly powered-up nerf gun more than anything else. The gunfire sounds weak, and the visual gun animations are kinda meh. In all honesty, the pistols felt better to shoot than anything else, but, well, you aren't exactly going to kill a predator using only pistols.The NPC guerilla fighters that attack the players might as well as be a joke. Their aim is poor, they deal tiny slivers of damage on a hit, and they don't exactly have any form of self-preservation, nor do they actually attempt any vaguely interesting attacks or ambushes. They'll run around a corner, stand out in the open, and shoot at you, refusing to take cover, peek corners, actually ambush the players, throw grenades, or do anything besides sit still, get shot, and miss most of their shots. Even with the starting rifle, the time to kill is maybe a second or two on the NPCs.The game really has a great premise, and if they touched up and balanced the game a bit better, I genuinely could recommend it, but at it's current state, it's just ruined by poor balance, weak overall design, and a lack of polish.

_childDocuments_.review: So this predominantly is an five player asymmetrical 1v4 shooter.This is the first game of it's style I have really played.It's been out on consoles and EGS for a year and just came to Steam in April for it's one year anniversary.There is a 4v4 mode as well but I haven't played it.Game play for the Fireteam (the Hunted) side is your typical modern day shooter FPS experience and feels solid.Gameplay for the Predator is third person with FPS aiming and is a little more complicated because of Predator specific mechanics.  Weapon and Gear swapping for the Predator feels more clunky and pretty much requires the gear wheel, which is annoying.  And you can't single press to use Gear items like the Fireteam.  All uses require a mouse click.  I think this is an intentional design choice to slow Predator players down or because of controls on consoles.  Not sure which as I have spent a LOT more time playing as the Fireteam.There is a level based system for unlocking more advanced weapons, gear, and perks,  This system is based on global levels and unlock both Predator and Fireteam kit as part of the same progression.  Leveling is pretty quick as you play.  For example I am already level 92 after 62 hours of play.There are cosmetic loot boxes which can be earned strictly through game play.  No cash required.There are unique DLC characters which allow for certain weapons to be unlocked early and have their own stat balancing.  They do cost cash but I cannot call any of these as pay-to-win as they feel pretty equal to the vanilla classes for the most part.There are some small glitchy bugs, which can be annoying.  However in my experience they are rare.As a fan of the Predator Action/Horror/Sci-Fi genre, I'm enjoying the game greatly.If you love the Predator franchise, jump in and have fun.If you're on the fence, wait for it to go on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: While Predator: Hunting Grounds may not be the best or well balanced game, it still is a lot of fun. I've enjoyed playing on both sides, the Predator, and the Fire-team. I've enjoyed the Predator the most. It's fun hunting down your prey and giving them a really hard time. Sure, the humans can whittle down your health with relative ease, but that's simply because you are rushing in. Predator takes strategy to play effectively. How I find myself playing is that I use my ranged weapons, the Yautja bow is my weapon of choice, and shoot at the humans from a distance. I then go in, finish them off with my combi-stick, and take the trophy. I also play the Berserker class, which fits my individual play-style. Hunting Grounds isn't without it's flaws though. The game has a bit of a long wait time for matches, especially for the Predator side, but, it's not a big deal, at least for me.  Some games take a long time to load, and get some players in. Hunting Grounds also has it's fair share of bugs and glitches. My Predator has found herself trying to jump onto a Predkour tree and instead of jumping on the tree, she'll spasm and rapidly turn from side to side, and fall down to the ground. Fire-team members have fallen into the ground, unable to be claimed. Lag spikes also pop up a bit here and there. The Predator also is underpowered. I feel that the health pool depletes way too fast. If there could  be maybe a fix, where the Predator has either more base health, or can take more hits, i.e., give the guns less damage, that'd be great! Texture popping is also an issue, but it's not so big that I am physically unable to play.Overall, my experience in the Hunting Grounds is relatively positive. I've met some nice people, and had some great matches. I feel that the game is a bit unfinished, if it could be reworked, polished and refined more, then it'd be an even more amazing game!

_childDocuments_.review: The game is technically and gameplay-wise okay. However, there is certainly room for improvement in terms of graphics, map selection, tactical possibilities on the maps and tactical gameplay in the team, overview, etc. The bigger problem with the game is that it is a full-price item in which I still have to painstakingly unlock everything (e.g. silly things like sights or weapon barrels, and that with every single weapon). Furthermore, the game is demotivating for beginners because the developer doesn't give you any instructions or training opportunities at all. There is only a small tutorial for the Predator, but none for the fire team. And there are no training opportunities to get an overview of everything on your own before you go into the online match and probably get hit in the head for several rounds. And the PvP compulsion in a full-price game is also the biggest problem. There are simply too few players, you often have to wait a long time for a match, especially if you want to play the Predator. That doesn't make any sense and that's why you can't recommend the game. If a small campaign (for the fire team and for the Predator) were included and single (or co-op) training missions and/or if the game were offered at a lower price or free to play, the game would be recommendable.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a die-hard PREDATOR fan and there truthfully is fun to be had in this game. That being said, I often go back and forth between having a genuine good time and being frustrated out of my mind; which isn't always a fault of the gameplay itself, but a fault of the numerous quirks that haven't yet been ironed out by the development team.It's hard to summarize just what irks me in a brief TLDR style, but .•  -  It's very bare-bones and awkwardly stiff. Automatic weapons have a delay on both firing and aiming down sights again if you let go of either of the mouse buttons, which feels horribly clunky when trying to hit the damned Predator when it's leaping circles around you. The FPS feel and movement controls could really use some polishing up so the game doesn't feel so ancient and the implementation of simple mechanics like vaulting or going prone could do a lot to achieve modernity. I played the Predator in the tutorial and a handful of public matches and that feels relatively solid, but there are some irritating things like repeatedly auto-jumping between the same two branches when trying to get down off a tree or being unable to shoulder swap the camera.•  -  I don't appreciate buying this game on PS4 and finding it can't even reach 30 FPS, to buy it again on Steam and find the PC version  gets constant dips into the 40 FPS range running on my RTX 3070 on High settings.•  - Simply put, the UI is  when playing as the Predator; whose button prompts only seem to display accurately on a controller or on the default control scheme. I nearly died trying to finish off a downed player the first time I played as the Predator because it falsely told me to press G and it just never performed the finishing move. Shortly thereafter, I got sniped out of the air and it told me to hold E to activate my self-destruct, but  didn't work so I just died kneeling on a tree branch I landed on where the other players couldn't even reach me. The ping button to tag the Predator's location has a cooldown after three pings and the marker will get stuck on leaves or vines; often catching foliage that is right in front of the Predator, or in some cases, leaves that are hanging behind your character's head. My loadouts often randomly get reset back to the default presets after completing matches. Sometimes mission objectives don't appear. There is no feedback when hovering over and/or clicking on certain things in the menus. You can't highlight players on the scoreboard during a match to view their profile or to report them. •  - In 75% of matches I play, we lose because one of my fellow Fireteam members goes down in a few melee strikes from the Predator, who then leaps into the trees and spams them with the plasma caster until they die. Then, they use the med-kit and  rest of the  before healing again. If that didn't occur, we lost because the Predator either used the bow or knew they could spam the leap button. Admittedly, I have yet to play as every class of Predator, but it seems to me there is  So they're 96% invisible and also constantly hulk-jumping incredibly long distances whenever they start taking damage. As much as I despise this, they have almost no chance of winning if they don't play like that against a competent team. It should be said though that the other 25% of matches are intense duels that seem perfectly balanced; maybe because either the Predator player isn't max-level or because my squad-mates actually are.•  -  and they have A LOT of health. They will get indefinitely stuck on the geography like rocks or stairs, stand completely still while you shoot them in the face, rapidly strafe side to side, aim at the Predator on the roof through the ceilings of buildings, aimbot you through foliage, or just refuse to shoot you. I really wish they had less health and balanced the difficulty by just spawning more of them so that you can go on action rampages like in the original film. The newly implemented AI Fireteam members have the same bot coding as the enemy soldiers, just turned to 11. They never split up and always seem to know where you are as the Predator in Private Matches. Alternatively, they will steal a lot of your kills when playing along-side them.•  -  if you want to win as Predator; or alternatively, be any help at all to your Fireteam squad-mates. I've spent dozens of hours grinding experience in Private Matches so I can be somewhat of a threat to the more aggressive Predator players.•  - Only one music track endlessly loops over and over in the menus. It would be fantastic if the developers implemented some of the alternate tracks that play during the matches or even better, included tracks from the film scores. I think the voice acting was performed by the developers themselves. It sounds out of place, way over-acted, and you'll hear the same handful of lines a dozen times per match. Here's something wacky, , meaning in one match I was able to track the Predator down every time he ran away because he was blasting music with his microphone on. This strange mechanic also lead to a particularly funny circumstance where a Predator player used his mic to announce to the entire Fireteam that he was friendly and helped us complete our objectives as long as we didn't shoot him. As funny as that was, a couple of matches later .There are a few things I actually really appreciate about this title, such as:•  -  on Cinematic settings. Love the little details like the way the sunlight pours in through the trees and illuminates the jungle fog. I only hope one day I can run it on my RTX card at a stable framerate.•  - Besides  in the game, I've genuinely enjoyed sitting down and eating lunch while listening to the audio logs he's recorded. Those tapes expand on what his character from the 1987 film has been up to since those boiling hot days in Central America. (It's befuddling that Mortal Kombat 11 couldn't get Arnie to voice the Terminator but this game got him to voice Dutch.)•  - The Yaujta in particular have an  and uh Predator stuff. _childDocuments_.review: I'll start off with the good. I find the game to be very fun and enjoyable when it works. The gameplay is good whether you are the Predator or the Fireteam. I think the Fireteam can have some good firepower on their side, so long as they come with proper loadouts, and the Predator is pretty balanced (or at least as much as an alien hunter with advanced weaponry and tech can be). Occasionally you do get the experienced Predator player who can jump in and absolutely wipe your squad, but it shouldn't happen too often. Playing as the Predator is fun too, although there's a bit of a learning curve at first, and you've got lots of different classes and tools to toy with. As long as your team sticks together and utilizes their loadouts, skills, and game mechanics properly, you should always be able to stand against the Predator. OH, and don't be dissuaded by people saying there are loot boxes. They are not...you get crates which contain skins and apparel after almost every match you play and you can buy things you want directly with in game currency which you also get very quickly. Not a pay to play scenario.Now all that being said, the bad...I mentioned the game is fun when it WORKS, however, it very often doesn't. In my experience, I'd say half the games I load up experience one or more of these issues-Game breaking bugs (jump in with no loadout/tools at all, enemies not appearing, mission not progressing)-Glitched teammates who can't fight or die-Matchmaking fails or takes incredibly long (especially in regards to the Predator wait times)It is much faster to load into Fireteam lobbies as there are more spots open and other players. Although many times you are in a pre-game lobby and it only gives you one other teammate and two AI Bot teammates, the bots being absolutely useless. When you do get human teammates, SOOOO many of them can be absolutely clueless and make it seem like they want to be disemboweled by the Predator (no real solution to stupid but I figured I'd mention it). Yet when I wait the 10-15 minute queue time to play as the Predator, it's like I'm going up against Seal Team 6 every time. I genuinely wish more people would play this game just so we have more bodies on Fireteam and less Predator wait times.To sum up, again I do really enjoy the game, but it certainly isn't without its faults. Faults that don't make the game unplayable, but are annoying enough to make people not want to continue playing. I hope the devs can continue to work on improving the game and fixing these kinds of issues, as I think it's a great representation of what it'd be like to go up against this awesome enemy.

_childDocuments_.review: I was expecting a multiplayer experience akin to Aliens vs Predator from 2010, or even some form of Dead by Daylight with guns. What I got instead was a lazy, shallow game that's trying to milk fans of the franchise for money. Not worth, even when it inevitably goes free-to-play to charge for loot boxes.The game is boring: either you get your objectives done as the Fireteam in about two minutes because the Predator is braindead, or you slaughter every single Fireteam member as the Predator in the first 10 seconds because he's just that strong. Balance has clearly been thrown out the window here. Good luck being the Predator though, as queue times for him can go for about 10 minutes. Fireteam queue times are as short as 30 seconds or less.The graphics settings on PC are very barebones and unoptimized, with textures not looking any different past the medium setting. Anti aliasing and post processing options are controlled by sliders, and offer barely any performance difference between the highest and lowest settings. Performance is fantastic as the Predator, but as soon as you step into the Fireteam's shoes, your FPS will dip for no reason even with all settings put to low. Forget the poor balancing, even the engine doesn't want the Fireteam to win.I'm still waiting for the day we'll be swept off our feet with a Concrete Jungle remake, but until then, just stick to AvP 2010 if you're a hardcore fan.

_childDocuments_.review: Half way through an objective, I noticed my teammates health bar dropping. He called for help over comms in a voice that betrayed a very recent bong hit. I found him just outside; he was 12 inches deep in a game of Punch-The-Sphincter with a very big dude who looked like a cross between Stevie Wonder and M.F. Doom. The 8 year old Mexican child playing the predator noticed me and screeched like Swiper was trying to snatch his backpack. Years of experience playing Mordhau (like the gullible idiot I am) came flooding back to me as this big crocodile-sounding behemoth lunged at me. I parried him 6 times while my other teammate replaced his vital organs with buckshot. We barely escaped the suicide blast.The next round I played, my fireteam was rapidly compromised and slain because the predator overheard my new team mate's abuelita vacuuming in the background over proximity chat.This game is great. You drag your mentally challenged fireteam through a string of objectives and try to evacuate before getting gored by the predator. There are PvE elements, but only nominally, the bots seem to be using airsoft guns and really only exist to distract you from and create sound cues for the predator player. Your greatest enemy will likely be the sheer incompetence displayed by the cross-platform console players.The game is out on PSN and will be released on Xbox soon, so, for the forseeable future, the player count should be acceptable. Loadouts, playstyles, and cosmetics are reasonably varied and aren't a giant pain to unlock. Overall, it's a great asymmetrical shooter title that's worth buying if only to experience the lowest depths of human stupidity.

_childDocuments_.review: Even though Predator: Hunting Grounds may not be the best game and may not be considered "Game of the Year," it is endlessly entertaining to play, stalking through the jungle as either a firefighter or a predator, unclear if you are the hunter or hunted is a rewarding experience, and the randomised missions keep things engaging, even without a cohesive and immersive story.While there are better games on the market, Predator: Hunting Grounds is just plain campy fun, and I always enjoy my time playing it, even if that time is swiftly ended by a maxed-out Predator who wipes an entire game of low-level players. A well-coordinated fireteam will always beat a skilled predator, no matter what their loadout or experience is. Final Verdict:Predator: Hunting Grounds will appeal to players who appreciate asymmetrical PVP titles. Keep in mind, however, that this is a fun game, not a competitive one. 8/10 ratings.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok. after about 27.5 hours of game play  and reaching level 80 on my character i figured it was time to review this game.  if you ever played AvP, Avp 2 , or Avp 2011, then this game will feel like 2/3rds of a game to you.  it's purely multiplayer .  with a team of 4 (humans) against 1 (predator) . so it sort of plays like  Friday the 13th and Dead by daylight , cept the predator can be killed. then there's clash mode where two teams of humans face off on objectives  and on member from each team can take over a "friendly predator". this mode feels closer to classic AVp action , minus the aliens.  that said i am finding the game enjoyable but of course i didn't get it till   reccently so i missed most the major bugs every one complained about early in it's life.  But on to the break down. The Good: Graphics- top notch i'm having to run most settings on high  to keep 60 fps @ 1440p  i can run it at 1080p on ultra  and get 60 fps but my TV is a 4k tv so 1080p looks kind of stair steppy on it  so i prefer to go higher res with less visual fidelity.  but even at my settings  the game looks gorgeous. Mission Game Play - the game play is quite fun and unlike the other games i compared it to above ( F13th , and DbD)  you can shoot back at your "killer" . which gives you almost a feeling like left 4 dead 2.   with the human team needing to complete objectives other than just "kill the predator"  it also feels like you are playing the first predator movie. Weapon variety - i find the weapon variety quite nice here. with many weapons for both the preds and the humans  it leaves room for many play styles.  Sound -  the music is taken right from the first movie so you really feel like you are in the predator universe.  all the gun sounds hit the right marks with a good balance of bass woofer use versus satilite speaker use.  i'm playing on a Klipsch 200 watt Promedia 2.1  speaker set  and it sounds amazing . makes me miss the klipsch 500 watt 5.1 system  i had back in 2003-4. but alas Klipsch discontinued the 5.1's and well more recently also discontinued the 2.1's  and exited PC audio in doing so.  but well suffice to say i'm sure the game sound kicks a** on most 2.1  or better systems.  The Meh:   un balanced weapons - Some weapons are trickier to use than others. the sniper rifle is nearly useless if the predator has already spotted you and down right hazerdous to the human player when the predator  is already in face slashing at you.  on the predator side of things the hand held plasma gun  it useless at any range  other than in the human's face , and at that distance you got way better attack options . also the shoulder cannon  doesn't have that lock on  that we all got so used to in the AvP series. but it's only a slight draw back as the cannon is so powerful  that a lock on would ahve made teh predators too OP for the humans. Cross play  - this one is sort of a good thing but can also be a negative which is why i have it in "the meh"  section.  it's plays cross play with console versions as well as epic store and steam store bought versions.  if that bothers you you can opt to turn off cross play  and just play with folks on PC. but that is where the good about it ends.  turn off cross play and you'll find game wait times get rediculous.  furthermore  most your games will wind up being against PS4/PS5 owners... The Bad Console gamers -  if you run with cross play on , you'll enjoy finding games quicker , but you will also have to put up with a younger , more immature crowd of gamers . hear me out. I don't mean to sound like a PC master race elitist.  of course many console gamers are mature and older gamers , but playing on or against console gamers you learn quickly that the gamer base is much broader and more varied in age and maturity  than if you were just playing on pc. you tend to run into more ass hats  in short.   thankfully they can be muted , but there nothing you can do about the shoddy team work you get from some of them. narrow map variety -  ok i get it,  it's predator , and the dev's were taking more influence from the first movie.  doesn't change the fact that all the maps get old fast , when they are all Jungle maps.  it would have been interesting to see some Predator 2  city inspired maps.  or even some artic maps  that take influence from  the AVP  movie.  just to mix it up a little.  Steep learning curve -  if you can't handle hard games  this one might not be for you.  jumping into an online only environment on any franchise  can be a pain , but this one requires you learn what to do and what not to do fast. so be ready for a bruising  early on as you learn the game. Conclusion :  The game is entertaining enough especially if you love the predator universe.  but lack luster map offerings  and a few other quirks hold it back  from being a must have game for every one. suffice to say the predator franchise needed this game, it does the franchise right , but still could have been better.  I give it a decent  7 out of 10.  not a bad game but it's an above average experience  and for the predator fan it is a must have.

_childDocuments_.review: It's like Friday the 13th the game, but with guns. There is a bit of a skill gap, but it doesn't take long to get the hang of combat and working as a team. Matches are decently balanced. Some matches the Fireteam destroys the Predator. Some games the Predator instantly destroys the Fireteam. Some games you accomplish all the objectives and Evac without even seeing a Predator. I like the way the game blends PVP with PVE. Missions don't feel out of place, and the NPCs attacking you at the same time you're fighting off a Predator makes for interesting combat. Mouse and key is the way to go, controller has no aim assist so it can be less accurate. Matchmaking is pretty quick during the day, (30 secs) but during the nighttime it can take several minutes to find a match. If you liked Friday the 13th the game, chances are you'll dig this too.

_childDocuments_.review: PROS:A lot of fun, especially as the predatorMany different yautja to choose from (provided you have all of the dlc)Good amount of customization options for both sides, I guess. A little more would be nice, thoughThe game is easy to learn after you play the tutorial or practice matchesThe graphics look a lot better now than it did during first launch in 2020Cool mockery voices for the yautja. My personal favorite is "Want some candy?"CONS:Not enough maps. There are maybe 5 or 6 and each map has a nighttime variant. Not to mention all of the maps are jungles. This game really needs more maps with different environments, possibly some of the areas we've seen in movies: ancient pyramid, arctic hunting ground, urban city or even the game preserve from Predators 2010Certain predators don't have their proper voices or don't have their correct equipment, such as Wolf. He doesn't have his shurikens, dual plasma casters, razor whip and laser mines. Super predators like Mr Black have the same voices as the rest of the male yautja, which doesn't make sense to me. Also, Mr Black's face doesn't look anything like his movie counterpart.The fireteam bots in private matches are insanely overpowered. They always know where you are and NEVER stop following you around the map, even if you're invisible. The fireteam bots don't use any tactics or skill, such as covering themselves in mud or using gadgets. They have extremely high health and deal ludicrous amounts of damage to you in seconds, so you literally have to batter and wallop the bots to bring them down, but you could get killed easily by taking that approach. Most of the time, your best option is to not get close and rely on ranged attacks, which is pathetic if your trying to roleplay as an honorable yautjaIn order to better balance the AI, you need to use custom match settings. But as a consequence, doing that will decrease your earned XP down to an abysmal rateAs for real multiplayer, not a lot of people are still playing this. The max these days is around a few hundred if you're luckyAt the end of the day, the game is fun and has cool features. But the lack of maps, real players, and the retarded "rambo" AI really take away from the potential that this game has. I really ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hope that the developers will continue to release patches and content updates in the near future. 7/10 for me

_childDocuments_.review: This game needs a good review.Basically you either bully humans or you bully a predatorThe gunplay is decent and playing as a predator is based because you can do funny thingsBully the predator by magdumping it with an assault rifle and an SMG and feel satisfied as it uses its self destruct and then kills you because you fail to defuse it in timeOh and you can play as Arnold SchwarzeneggerAs per request I shall expand my review. Outside of DLC (that I personally seemed to unlock just by buying the game) there is a distinct lack of micro-transactions, a big bonus in my eyes. While there are lootboxes, they provide purely cosmetic features and are very easy to acquire, and everything you can get in a lootbox you can buy with in-game currency.Matchmaking is set into two teams - Predator, and Fireteam, where you play as either the pred or the humans respectively. You get an EXP bonus for searching for both, and you can alternatively search for either one of the teams, meaning that you can pick what you want to play.The server stability seems to be good and there are a variety of settings for PC players, however the game does have some performance issues at the highest settings (Epic & Cinematic,) my RTX 2060 struggles to run at a solid 60FPS at epic settings, however it has not affected my ability to play the game, and that is my preference of using high graphical settings. I haven't seen any issues with net-code.As for replay value, you steadily unlock new weapons, items, and cosmetics all the way up to level 100+, levelling up is not too slow, but not too quick as to burn through everything you can acquire. The variety of perks, weapons, gears, and game play styles you can take offer a great deal of replay-ability.

Game is mostly predator based, not fireteam. For example, if predator didn't afk and did something in the game, he will get more xp than you, always. Not even perks, that give you more xp, plus xp bonus for playing as fireteam helps. If you completed the mission and killed the hunter, predator will get more xp. To win as fireteam you need to complete mission, but securing predators body is just a bonus. If you kill predator(which is not easy), but don't defuse the bomb - you lose. If you kill the predator at the start of the game and defuse the bomb - you lose, because predator will get more xp and even more if someone dies to a huge blast radius.Game can be quickly finished if hunter decides so, with out getting penalties. If hunter downs one of the humans he can finish him off instantly, suffering to small to no drawbacks for that.  Do it 4 times and game is finished. Predator gets tons of xp and you almost nothing. There is no punishment for hunter if they don't hunt, what is the name of the game.Cross platforming. The name says everything. 90% of the game will be with playstation players. If you play as human and hunter is PC player - you will lose, unless he is afk. Most of the time one of the players are afk and will be replaced with a bot, which is better than console player. Luckily, console players mostly obey orders, which gives you chances, but sometimes it's 1v1 against hunter. I haven't tried to turn off cross platforming, because the queue waiting time will be longer and I want to play and not wait. Small amount of maps and mission. Will get repetitive quickly. Day time, night time. Go there, kill, grab, go there.No more to say.♥♥♥♥ lobbies. No way to add friends. You can only mute or report a player, that's it. You can't contact the game support. I tried, only thing I found was playstation website and forum. I registered on forum, but I couldn't post anything, because I was a new profiles and new profiles can't do ♥♥♥♥ there. DLC's that add only skins. And maybe a better characters. I ahve only one - original Dutch. I am a fan on the first film. That's pretty sums up the game. I had 20 hours, when I wrote this review.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: After putting some more time in, I still think this is a good game but definitely some balancing issues between teams and Predators. Low level inexperienced Predators will get chewed up fairly quickly. Top level Predators are just hard as nails. A number of times I've heard the Predator within the first minute (spawned nearby or teleported??) and had them descend on the team seconds later. Often they just stand and soak up the damage as if it didn't matter. What concerns me here is I'm not sure if I'm seeing genuine gameplay or some kind of exploit. [/edit]General points:- Good to play on either side.- Fireteam gun-play feels good.- Character customisation is excellent- Low skill level wasn't a bar to fun - enjoyed it from the first mission.- Maps are about as varied as they can be considering the format and the tropical heat limitations- The game runs smooth on my system (Intel ARC / Ryzen 3700x)- In the matches I've played - only one issue (temporarily stuck on terrain - but managed to hop out). No bugs at all.- Predator gameplay is a whole other dimension.  It feels very close to the films. Chef's kiss.- Good VOIP system.- Crossplay helps keep the player numbers up.I don't know what the longevity will be like, but the format means you can drop in and have a round or two without it dominating your entire evening - whereas many games I have require too much dedication for those casual moments when you just want a quick blast. Probably the best Predator game I've played since the original AVP (which I played over a 56k modem).

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't gotten as much time in this one as I would like to have but what I've played hasn't been terrible.First off, I usually suck pretty hard at asymmetrical MP games. Mostly because I don't do well as the creature/monster/killer side. Of all of them, Evolve was my favorite of past ones in which I held my own on as the creature. As much as I'd love to be good as the Predator, he/she is tougher to control well. With different basic actions, a parkour system, a different perspective and several vision modes, it takes some practice to do well as. I've seen some kids out there bouncing around, in and out of cloak and shanking fireteams like a seasoned hunter and I've seen what people my level look like. You can be the Predator you know. I just can't.Next, the human fire team controls mostly like you expect although rebinding keys can prove a bit tricky. Completing a mission other than surviving a Predator attack is cool except sometimes your objective isn't totally clear until you've seen/heard all the basic premises. Most reviews that mention the bots miss my favorite feature of having one in your squad. If you die and don't get revived, you can spectate the surviving members of your team. If said member is a bot, you can take over control for another chance to "settle that score".If you're into the Predator lore and like MP shooters, you'll find plenty more good than bad here. If not, (then why are you even reading reviews this far down) then this one isn't going to make you a new fan. If you catch it on sale, most definitely pick it up.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE: Most Fireteams are using wall glitches, which results in you waiting them out. It's not fun, so it's made load times even longer. The devs aren't moderating at all, so it's basically a game of cheaters now. Do not waste your time or money.Old review:After playing this game more and playing a lot more as Predator I have developed a new opinion on this game, based mostly on the balancing and skillgap. I do not recommend this game anymore. Please see my original review below ** for more context.As a Predator, you are outmatched. Your controls and camera are very bad, and any experienced Fireteam can easily remove 3/4 of your healthbar within seconds of detecting your presence. This is because experienced Fireteams have access to better gear at no real cost. Late game, you can deck out your soldiers, while Predators' abilities have some effects on playstyle but they do not actually make you "better" like high-level Fireteam weapons do.So what you typically experience is getting bombarded by grenade launchers then immediately marked with gadgets, followed by grenade spam. Then you are hunted by two decked out soldiers (preventing you from healing) while the other two complete objectives. The two attacking soldiers are incredibly aggressive, because they know if they die they can be revived. So they aggressively pursue Predators with no sense of self preservation. The Predator can throw everything at them, but ultimately the human weapons are more lethal than Predator weapons. This is the major flaw in the game.By making high-level Fireteams too lethal, they have removed the entire cat-and-mouse from the game. As Predator, you then have a choice: die trying, or just snipe from a mile away. The kicker is, none of these tactics are fast enough to give you a chance at downing all soldiers (and revives) before they extract.Playing as Predator feels futile. You pray for noobs, because experienced players aren't at all threatened by Predators. Noobs at least offer an unpredictable experience.** My original review from Jun 23, 2021, where I recommended this game:I bought on a sale because I was hesitant. For $15, this is a steal.The game is simple. 2 modes: Clash and Hunt. Clash is basically Team Deathmatch. Hunt is a 1v4vE asymmetric showdown, and that's what I'll be talking about in this review.I started humble, and played as a soldier. You go on a mission in the jungle, take on some AI soldiers, do the objective, move to the next one, repeat a few times before you then call in the chopper to extract. While all of this is happening, the Predator is looking to kill you.Since the Predator has to actively scan to distinguish between AI and Players, you'll sometimes just catch a Predator on a branch, waiting for the fight to clear so he can hunt the squad that walks away. Other times you'll have a Predator try to hit you while you fight AI. And sometimes, he'll be killing the AI right there next to you because he never bothered to distinguish, and now he's going after everything he sees.This creates a lot of unique matches, depending on the people filling the roles. One of my first games, it played out just like the movie where people went down one by one to the Predator, but I'm not Arnold and I ended up dying to the Predator at the end.It seems balanced, as I've had my fair share of wins and losses. A great Predator can definitely take out a relaxed squad though. The key is to always have eachothers backs. One may die from an aggressive push from the Predator, but you can deal a lot of damage to the Pred in that time; and then you can even respawn dead teammates through an optional mission.I'm a big fan of asymmetric games. I even played and designed maps on Halo 3 for a Predator gametype that feels a lot like this. This game is fun. As Predator, queue times can be long and some Fireteams are way too easy. But when people are committed, it is fun and goes well -- you don't need to be "sweaty" or a "try-hard" to be decent either.

_childDocuments_.review: Bottom line for not recommended is because the predator is weak and at high level play fire team will win 100% of the time. The reasons are many but if the developers simply knew basic math they could have prevented half of the issues. To much power lies in the fire team or you could say the predator is to weak. You can't win a fight vs 4 fireteam EVER if its high level play. Developers should fix the balance. A fireteam that is experienced and knows how to play can literally hunt the predator all game. They have more DPS than the predator, they have 4 players vs 1 , if they die they can revive their team mates (the predator cannot revive its over), the fire team can find you so your cloaking ability is useless vs a good fire team. A lot of predator weapons have limited uses, your bear traps are few and the maps are big.... yet you cannot restock on bear traps and you also cannot simply pick up your used bear traps. I think allowing predators to pick them up after being used would be an improvement for the game because traps are easily spotted and destroyed as is by the fire team. The fireteam have everything on their side. All they have to do as a fire team is follow some simple rules.1. Stick together.2. Spot predator for team3, everyone engages predator at same time. If you  do this you should never lose as the fire team. Sure  you will need to get good at any game. But ultimately you should win as the fireteam if you play good.So when you  get to high level play the predator is the one being hunted and the game is no longer fun. (This is where I changed review to not recommended.)

_childDocuments_.review: +      great atmoshpere, start of every round (as fireteam) is hype, gameplay is pretty fun, a lot of weapons and equipment most of which seems viable, customisation is pretty good if you dont care about sculpting perfect faces-       the game has bugs and other issues and as far as i understand devs do nothing to fix it so yea, you got revived? you may experience a bug where you can crawl around at normal sprinting speed and still scream for help, you cant use your weapons and such and i have no clue how other players see you then but its not very fun        you may also experience what usually would be considered heavy lag (rubber banding, other players teleporting, etc) but all that while having stable 15-30 ping according to the game        there is no fireteam tutorial so good luck trying to learn how to difuse the predator mask when at most you've got 15sec and keybinds dont mention how to even operate the minigame (tried using 'w' and 's' to switch combination, tried the scrollwhell, both didnt work        another great bug is one situation when i joined a lobby to see that we had 5 fireteam players, usually its 4 fireteam members and 1 predator but this lobby had 5 fireteam dudes for some reason, waited till the game should have started, the 5th guy disappeared and got replaced by someone else as predator (completely different player if names are to be believed), then once the countdown finished we were just stuck there, looking at pre-game 'chose your spawn' screen until everyone left (which you could see in real time when a player disappears and gets replayed by a bot)Overall the game in terms of gameplay and presentation is great, gameplay is fun, graphics look good, atmoshpere is great, customisation is decentWhat is dragging the game down by a lot are the technical problems which at least in my experience where experience breakingThe queue times for fireteam are about 20-30 sec and 3-5min for predator, games can last from a few minutes up to ~15min, overall its worth a try IF its on sale or if you will keep an eye on your in-game time so you can refund the game if its a mess for you, for me it worked fine in the first 2h and now it gets buggier and buggier, I should have refunded the game when i had the chance.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a bit hard trying to decide where to start with this review, so I'll just start with the idea and execution.This game takes elements from a lot of popular multiplayer games, but they don't seem to compliment each other at all. I can see where they draw their inspiration from; L4D is the main inspiration and people LOVE competitive PvP anyway, so that's our hook. CS:GO has skins, so we'll just implement that to garner interest and indulge the players' vanity. Payday2 is fast-paced and because of that hooks new players quickly, but also gives experienced players lots of build options and ways to break the game, so why not try that to help with player retention. CoD has nice and tight gunplay and a simple to understand perk system, so it's easy to pick up and play. Cross-platform, the more the merrier so why not. Leveling and weapon unlocks are basically mandatory at this point in any multiplayer game so why the hell not. All of this on paper sounds really good, now let me tell you how it ACTUALLY works in practice.The copied CS:GO homework:The Predator is supposed to stalk you silently from treetops, and wants to remain invisible. The Marines have to roll around in mud to conceal themselves from the Predator's thermal vision. See where I'm going with this? Not only that, there is no trading and so that bit of motivation is also non-existent. Worst of all, there are DLC- only characters which are obviously unbalanced and leaning toward P2W. This is the kind of edge only the most well-established games can afford, since the players that are willing to put up with this BS are already too far in to care and vastly outnumber those who want nothing to do with it, making the latter's opinions irrelevant. You do not have that edge. If you wanted to use this for player motivation on a small and struggling game, you just blew your foot off with a plasma caster.Here are the main problems. They have implemented some sort of Quake Live- style cosmetics system where Exp earns you loot boxes, loot boxes earn you cosmetics, and if you REALLY want cosmetics you can buy them with RL money. In QL at least, (which I do not approve of at all), the cosmetics at least served a purpose of baiting you into buying lootboxes. Here there doesn't seem to be any "real" purpose behind the boxes, since you can't circumvent the grind and buy them directly. Maybe it did work like that once, but they ended up changing it since it wasn't working as intended, who knows.Point being, this system is now redundant any which way you look at it; it flies in the face of the fundamentals of the game. You can't satisfy my vanity because either I'm invisible or caked in mud, and because of that, you can't motivate me enough to care about looking good. Add to this that the only people that care to buy the P2W characters are barely out of their preteens, and you have a recipe for disaster. You are alienating any serious players who remember the source material, and motivating the people who will move on from this game in a month or two anyway for the next streamable Twitch hotness. The copied Payday2/L4D homework:PD2 has fast-paced PvE action, and it is quite challenging too. It takes skilled people and player co-ordination to get through the levels. Builds and perks help with this, and have a place and a purpose. Every level has a variety of approaches; you can go silent, loud, or whatever, what matters is clever class building and good aim. Not everyone is going to be on equal footing due to levels and unlocks, so difficulty levels helps with this. All the levels moving from the easiest to the hardest setting change the strategies in a fundamental way, and it takes a lot of experience from all 4 players to get through them. Now here is how P:HG handles it. You have 4 players and the "nemesis". The Marines have (several) side-objectives on a huge open map, and the Predator wants to kill the Marines and nothing else. Game ends if either the team or the nemesis die. There is a PvE aspect, but the AI is so simple/buggy that, apart from being useless enough to not be a challenge but just inconveniencing enough for them to be a threat to the Marines (not the Pred, though!) that it might as well not even be there. So what does this mean for gameplay?There are two game-modes, one objective based and the other a TDM mode. What usually ends up happening in the objective mode is that the Predator either remembers to use thermal vision to locate, and therefore slaughter the players, or doesn't and the Marines win. Either way, it is a lop-sided mess of a game mode which turns into a speedrun every match with no real challenge. The Marines get to their first objective, and if the Predator knows the map, he will jump straight to the objective and slaughter the team before they even get anything done. This is while the 4 players are alert and concentrating their full firepower on the assailant as he is ripping one of their spines out, after which he flees succesfully. OR, if you are an inexperienced Pred up against veteran Marines, their guns are already so powerful only one of them needs to plink a few rounds in your general direction before you are forced to flee or blow yourself up. What this tells us is that balance is ENTIRELY gun/level dependent and strategy, experience or skill does not matter in the slightest. What matters is how high in levels you are and how fast you can run. This should not be happening in a balanced game.This leads us to the next problem, which is the wide open map. L4D was able to predict this problem and made their maps linear and singleplayer-like. This ensured that the survivors dictated the flow of the game, while also giving the infected a powerful chance to strike. This was the point where the game could swing in either direction, all based on player skill. On top of that, it gave you a real challenge and a sense of progress since the map forced BOTH teams to work on the same problem at the same time. Linear maps also helped with getting players back into the game, since they would spawn close to you or somewhere where you were already going. This is not the case here; the survivor spawns directly on the other side of the map from where you are supposed to be; since you are most likely recovering from the Predator's onslaught, and since it is now EASIER for him to slaughter you, there is very little chance for you to ever get those players back. This puts a screeching halt to the flow of the game and gives the edge to the Pred. Not only that, there is very little any side can do to recover if up against full-level players at this point; if Pred ganked one or more of you in it's first assault, it's GG. If Marines are fully leveled, good luck trying to use strategy and skill to beat them. The so-called objective based mode without fail turns into a very unbalanced and short TDM brawl almost immediately. I am running out of space here so I will do a short critique on the perk system. Very similar to CoD, but the perks are so niche that their effects are either impercetible or useless. They do not add anything to strategy, and because of this there are no builds that affect the game in any way. There is no perceivable change to the flow of the game using the tools given. You have 3 slots, but an upper limit on perk "score": This means that you can't mix and match just any perks you want together, and will sometimes have to settle for only 2. Some perks even have a little disclaimer on them where they have no effect in certain game modes! Excuse me, WHAT?Reaching word limit but must rant. Great ideas poorly implemented, laughable balance, stale gameplay, asking price ludicrous for what feels like beta. Good lore, tight gunplay, they got Ahnold to voice the game. Want to like it, huge fan, but game stomps my balls. Please fix game, decide design direction, maybe slower paced. Go and eff yourself, give money back. My final message, goodby-

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing 1v4 asymmetrical game. Highly recommended. You can stalk the fireteam as a predator with a ton of abilities and take them out one by one while they complete missions throughout the jungle. A fireteam that works well together will easily wipe you out though, so you need to be careful how you approach them. But you've got plenty of time. Sit on a tree, leap from branch to branch, track them, see where they're going, set up a few traps, watch them get netted, swoop in for the kill. You can customize your kit and appearance as Predator or Fireteam. Lots of customization at that. You can create a glass cannon ranged Predator that stalks through the trees, a hulking melee berserker in full armor, or a true-to-film City Hunter Predator. You can even play as Arnold from the original movie or the sequels (separate DLC, $2 on sale).

_childDocuments_.review: Bought this the day of release on Steam. Played for about half an hour. Wasn't too impressed. I gave it a negative review.Around seven months later decided to give it another shot, a fair shot. Saw the Dutch & Predator DLC on sale real cheap, so I figured why not? So I got 3 of the Predator DLC and both Dutch DLC. So I started my journey as a Fireteam member. This was a little frustrating at first. I'd see people "mudding up" but it wasn't clearly explained in game. So instead of wasting valuable time I looked it up. (Look completely down at mud area, should see the interact pop up and press and hold  F, which is default until the meter fills. So unless you changed keybinds that will work) After this I wasn't almost instantly dying. Which upped the fun factor quite a bit for me. I edited the review to a neutral still keeping it negative.A concern I have seen in the community is whether the game is dead or not. This is crossplay between Playstation, Epic, and Steam. My queue times for Fireteam members has been usually between 20 second to 1 minute. Your lobby is filled with bots while finding players. I have had few games with bot players. In fact only one with me and 3 bots and I believethe Predator was AFK because I didn't see him for the entire match. DO NOT LET THE STEAM CHARTS FOOL YOU INTO THINKING THIS GAME IS DEAD. Because it is NOT. It is very much alive. Cross play continues to keep it that way.As Predator my queues have been no longer than 2 or 3 minutes. And that is really dependent on what time of day I play in NA. A complaint I see about the Predator's is "Predator is too OP, this game is unbalanced." Like what even the f*cc are you talking about? Did you watch ANY of the films? This is literally a hunting alien species that goes to other worlds to hunt their best warriors. In fact Dutch is the only survivor in the original film. The rest of his team was slaughtered by it. He figured out how it was hunting them all and developed a strategy against it and defeated it until it set off a self destruction device he barely escapes from. And even with all of that, the complaint isn't true. All 4 Fireteam members can easily kill a Predator. This complaint is probably from solo queue players that aren't using any sort of communication, not the emotes or the available voice chat in the game. Then get decimated, and cry that the Predator is too OP.The game is fairly balanced. Especially compared to most other 4v1 asymmetrical games. As stated all 4 Fireteam members can easily kill a Predator. If you're split up, then you're lambs to the slaughter. You need all 4 people to kill a Predator. You will not do it 1v1. And it should be that. Like I said it's an alien hunting species that hunts the planets strongest warriors. This species Yautja(Predators) actually hunts and kills the species of alien in the 1979 film "ALIENS" These aren't Toejam & Earl here. They're not here to get funky and high five you Fireteam members. They're vicious hunting warriors willing to die for the hunt. And they want your trophy. They are strong in game in 1v1 or 2v1, but 3v1 and 4v1 will present an issue for any Predator against competent Fireteams. They will have to retreat and try to heal. I feel a lot of the Predator complaints are either people not strategizing with the other members of their Fireteam, splitting up too far apart and not being able to help against an attack, or just being inexperienced in the game.The game is punishing to new players. But not in a sense where you're going to feel like you're beaten into submission. You kinda just pick up tips here and there or figure something out and you're like "Oh, okay. That will help in the future." My first couple of Fireteam matches I got flayed in what seemed like seconds, because I didn't know how to use the mud or didn't get that I can't be too far away from my team, and so on. The rest is just getting to know the maps and practice. My first Predator games weren't terrible, but I also didn't win. I killed 3 of the 4 on my first match, as I was ripping out the 3rd's trophy the fourth came over and finished me off, then escaped my blast radius. But it was still fun. The things I am unhappy about are the tutorial. You can only play Predator from what I have seen. (Could be wrong here) It's a fun little tutorial albeit annoying with the pop ups. I replayed it a couple of time, to get used to Predator. One time I jumped from a branch near a guy, when I landed it threw the Predator like 100 meters away into a crowd of enemies that unloaded the clip literally. In the options it does not show default layout for keyboard only controller. To see what the default key binds are for PC you actually have to edit them. I feel that's kind of lazy. Especially to release it on EPIC a year prior to it's Steam release and still not keyboard layout after 7 months of updates? That's kinda weak sauce. Not enough to ruin the game or anything but annoying AF.One major thing is most everything can be unlocked just from playing and earning in game currency. So if you wanted a DLC you can just play a lot and eventually just unlock what you wanted. And it takes way less grinding than in most games. Maybe like 10-20 matches and you should be able to obtain what you want to unlock, sometimes even less, it's dependent on the price and how well you do in each match.The unlock thing is a gift and a curse. It affords people to get the items and cosmetics they wish. But a lot of stuff is locked also behind a player level. And it's not difficult to level up player levels or anything. It's just more arduous. I.E. the Berserker Predator is unlocked at level 44. In almost 8 hours I'm level 19, so in order to play him I gotta put in a little work. But that's not even all that terrible, you gain a level every 1 or 2 matches depending on how well you did.I hated this game upon it's release. I wanted to see it burn in a dumpster fire. Over hours it's grown on me quite a bit. To where even the negatives are barely enough to keep me from playing it. If we were to compare it to the most popular 4v1 asymmetrical Dead by Daylight...this game is almost perfect in every respect and trumps it in fun, game play, the game actually working as intended, graphics, optimization, etc.For me most asymmetrical 4v1 games make me rage. As I mostly play solo queues in them. For some reason Predator: Hunting Grounds doesn't do that to me at all. Maybe it's because you can't really be selfish in this. If you get downed as a Fireteam member, you can be revived, and if a couple of people get killed and you can make it to a certain spot on the map you can revive the dead members as "back up". As Predator even if they manage to down you, it's so fulfilling to have the final "f*cc you!" with the self destruct device while you're laughing watching them sprint away in 18 seconds to not die also.I'm glad I came to my senses and gave this another try. It's been a really pleasant experience overall, even with the early frustrations.Overall: 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: (Man, why is there no Mixed option for reviews...)Predator: Hunting Grounds is a really good game. It has very nice maps, each of which are extremely detailed, and have decent AI and obstacles. The Humans are my favorite to play, and they have an insane amount of customization options, on top of a class system and weapon unlocks. Private Matches are some of the most fun you can have in this game, not saying that the multiplayer isn't, but Private matches are almost ALWAYS better than online matches.The Predator is fun too, as it lets you live out your fantasies of being a stalking Yautja waiting for the perfect moment to strike..... which almost never comes, as by the time you find the Humans they've completed half of their objectives and are moving to their next one. The pacing in this game FAR favors the Humans and "Hyper Aggressive" Predators, as most missions only take 15-20 minutes max, and it re-reinforces this by giving the Predator extremely High melee damage, encouraging them to rush in and not plan much at all, as the Humans will get 2-3 shotted by Melee from a Predator. Which severely brings down the maximum enjoyment of the game, as if you want to be slow and methodical for either side, you'll either have Speed-Running Humans, or a No-Think Melee Predator. If the missions were longer, and had more objectives, giving each side time to plan and not be rushed, and also decreasing the Melee Damage on Predators to at least a 4-5 Shot instead of 2-3, itwould be an even better game than it is. Overall i give it a 7.5/10. Def worth it if it's on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic, gem of a game which is only held back by developer transparency, or there lack of. One of the key issues to note is the recent removal of the Fireteam DLCs in which you could play as fan favourites Dutch 87, Dutch 2025, Isabelle and 'Beast mode' Dante. All of which came with their own unique abilities and weaponry. After 4 years on sale, they seemingly disappeared from all storefronts, platform wide. The explanation you ask? A mere reply under an unpinned comment "They were limited-time." (Taken from Illfonic's official socials) This is incredibly hard to believe but the issue is that Illfonic gave no warning prior to the DLCs being de-listed, causing many old and new players (Especially those on Xbox) to miss out completely, left in the dark wondering if they will ever return. There are threads upon threads of discussion surrounding this topic, with some players raising the question on a recent dev live-stream, where they refused to answer. It's clear that the community valued this aspect of the game and it would be nice to receive an official statement from the team as to why this content no longer exists but If I had to guess, it would be down to the recent ties with Sony being cut. Still, an explanation is needed.As for the game itself, it is incredibly fun if not a little unbalanced. Unless you are cracked or come across new players, your Predator will get completely demolished by the Fire-team, expect to lose. Graphics wise, it isn't the prettiest game on the market, but something has to said the Foliage and atmosphere, it's just like being inside the movies and at times seeing the Predator leap from tree to tree amongst a sunny backdrop is glorious.There is a ton to do here, with a plentiful selection of cosmetics to customise your Predator or Fire-team leader, as well as weapons and perks for both sides to level up and unlock. Building and outfitting your own ultimate Yautja is great, the possibilities are endless.The sound design has improved greatly since the relaunch, each Predator has its own distinct war cry and featured movie Predators sound just like they do on the big screen, Guns sound meaty and general walking through the jungle is tense, you can hear EVERYTHING.That being said The player count on Steam is a concern, It's a real shame because this game is truly a unique experience worthy of your time. It seems to be populated well on consoles which is a plus, with full cross-play finding a match is of no issue right now. I can find games most times under 30 seconds. But it would be nice to see those PC numbers rise.I'd highly recommend giving it a go, at least try it on sale. If you're a Predator fan this is the perfect game for you, if not, it's still an experience worth trying.Hopefully in the future the dev team can become more aware of their community that is keeping the game rolling instead of ignoring them.

_childDocuments_.review: Things to note with my review: It's solely based on the solo experience plus the fact that I got it on sale for about $7.50. PREDATOR has been my favorite thing of all things since I was a kid, and ever since Concrete Jungle I've been wanting a good game where I actually play as the Yautja. AVP 2010 was serviceable, but still not quite what I was looking for. This game's solo experience is pretty much the same thing: serviceable but not what I really want.You can play private matches with bots and play as either the Yautja or the fireteam, which is the only reason I finally bought this game because I don't do PVP at all. The downside here is, when playing as the Yatuja the fireteam AI is pretty stupid. They just run towards you rather than trying to complete mission objectives, making them fairly easy targets. What saves this, though, is the fact that there's also a number of enemy NPCs that you can hunt for extra XP, so the challenge becomes hunting as many NPCS plus the fireteam bots as you can before the timer runs out.Playing a private games as the fireteam is actually pretty fun, with the only downside being you won't fight a Yatuja. You just fight enemy NPCs and do various mission objectives.My favorite part is the customization. If I could get this level of customization in a single player PREDATOR game, It'd be a dream come true. You can customize armor, helmets, armor colors, skin tones, weapons, and much more.Overall, I'd give this game a 3/5. If you're like me and you have a no tolerance policy on PVP, you can still get some enjoyment out of this game, especially if you get it on sale.Also PLEASE FOR THE LOVE OF GOD ADD TRADING CARDS SO I CAN HAVE A DAMN PREDATOR EMOTICON ALREADY!
