_childDocuments_.review: OVERALL Rating: 6 / 10I have NOT played as Predator yet, so this is from a Fireteam perspective only. The music is awesome, the Data audio logs are interesting to listen to and that is something I almost NEVER do in a game, PEROID. I do like that as you play, you'll uncover more and learn more about the lore, which is fun in itself. Now, as for the gameplay. It most definitely feels like the Predator is powerful and I ABSOLUTELY love this fact. Despite that, out of the six matches I've had, I've "won" three, with one of the three, we managed to kill the Predator (most likely to a networking issue on the predator's part.The AI I'd give a 4 out of 10.. They are terribly basic, not that dangerous, more annoying if anything and sometimes breaks immersion just because of how stupid they are.The IN-GAME UI, I'd give a 5 out of 10. It feels dated, bulky and janky. They REALLY need to clean it up, adjust it and fix it. (If there's options to do this, I'll adjust this rating later)I do love that this game has objectives... so in that regard, it feels a bit more in-depth then say, Dead by Daylight.I do NOT like that some of the Locker Unlocks I got, remained LOCKED! That is a VERY bad bug to still have... and I was jipped out of two REALLY cool cosmetics.. The Gas Mask and the Avaitor sun glasses.. I have the points to buy them.. but I should have had them for free, via being unlocked.Most of the cosmetic DLC is okay. Not as interesting as I'd thought it'd be. But for $10, I'm cool with what I got, but I would love to see it improved... The game has a great foundation, just needs TWEAKS!Is this game worth more than $10 though? NO! Should you get it for $10 or less? YES!

_childDocuments_.review: Don't much like it, nein. The gameplay is at fault here, really, not the "authenticity" of the Predator-franchise.When you play as an SF-soldier, the movement feels too... It doesn't have the correct sounds or recoils. Also, enemy NPC soldiers are bullet tanks. They should be dead by one bullet to the head, you shouldn't have to spit 6 bullets in their face to kill them. Also, a customizable crosshair is missing. This huge-ass Xhair is just a gamekiller for me, in ANY game. I loathe it. The Predator gameplay is kinda clunky. I forget all the keybinds the second I'm done with a match, and I feel like the default binds are kinda weird. The AVP2010 Pred gameplay is MUCH better and more fluid. Otherwise, audio-tapes are always fun. Gives you a little dive into the Predator lore. Music is also good here. All in all, AVP2010 is a way better game to spend cash on if you want to get lost in some Predator action.

_childDocuments_.review: Mission for humans consist of fetch quest while youre shot at by bots.Meanwhile, the Predator gets to stalk you from the trees. The Predator can tank 4 sustained assualt rifles worth of damage whilst leaping around cloaked like a giant ♥♥♥♥♥♥ grasshopper. If by some miracle you are able to trouble him with your barrage of 4 military grade assault rifles shooting 800rpm into his face, with multiple reloads, well he can just hop up into the trees somewhere and heal. Meanwhile youre still expected to do fetch quests (with a timer no less) while ai bots shoot at you.Then the predator comes back fully healed to snipe you from the trees, hop around like a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ idiot while slashing with a combi stick, ripping downed players heads off so they cant respawn in 0.5 secs, and just generally having fun toying with the 4 human players.To add insult to injury, half the time your ADS just wont work. Annoying seeing as you get precious fleeting moments to shoot at the Predator while he's aiming a laser at you and hurling hot plasma (with splash dmg) at your face. If you manage to hit him, well he'll just use his inf stamina to leap somewhere else and do it again. Possibly throwing a bear trap at you so you can deal with that while he leaps around like the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ Easter Bunny.The playstyle breaks any and all immersion the game pretends to cultivate. The entire gimmick is "We made the first predator movie into a video game HAHA" complete with stupid callbacks like "get to the chopper" when your chore list is complete or, if by some miracle you manage to win as the fireteam, two players will clasp hands and do that little in the air arm-wrestle thing Dutch did with what-his-nuts CIA guy. Loadouts are sparse, perks are random and largely useless. The "Class system" for both sides feels rushed and not well thought out. The entire game reeks of a cash-grab looking to use the IP to make a quick buck, and in order to maximize profits, spend as little time and effort on the development of the game as possible without being outright vaporware.But hey, the predator looks cool, and you can have a RED mask!I love this franchise and to see it whored out like this so often is infuriating.Learn from Alien: Isolation, make a decent game first, worry about DLCs later. End Rant.

_childDocuments_.review: Predator Hunting Grounds is a asymmetric versus game with one team playing as a fireteam of four soldiers and the other as the titular predator both modes are fun however the fireteam mode is definitely better with friends or a squad of randoms that use voice chat. there are two main modes hunt which is the better of the two modes and clash which is a interesting diversion. Hunt mode consists of the fireteam completing objectives while being hunted by the predator and then extracting at low level play it can be a stop on either side by the game is fairly well balanced with tons of upgrades and customization on either side a good fireteam can get together and outright hunt the predator with good teamwork and great predator can catch out and separate players there is a good skill ceiling on both sides.Positives:Online Game is active at moment (30 seconds if queuing for fireteam or no preference and about 4 to 3 mins for a predator queue to find a quickplay game).  don't be fooled by the steam stats game on steam as a small but active community the bulk of the players are on play-station and epic and there is crossplay.matches are Quick and tense and there's great lore collectibles.low level of toxicity.massive amounts of customization both in load-out and appearance.Negatives:No PvE mode.AI soldiers very basic.

_childDocuments_.review: [NOTE 1: I personally main the fireteam, so my experience with the Predator is limited][NOTE 2: I personally don't play many pvp games but assymetry has always interested me][NOTE 3: This game uses [u]Easy Anti-Cheat[/u]. Some people might not like it so I'll say it here]Hey look guys, it's ! In 2021!What, don't know remember it?The Hidden is a mod for Half-Life and for the source engine.In that mod one player plays as 'the hidden' who is almost entirely invisible, only armed with a knife and molotovs.On the other side you have the I.R.I.S soldiers who are armed to the teeth, whose mission is to find the hidden player and take him out at all costs!Of course, if you let that 'hidden' player get close he will turn you into shishkebab. Bunch up together and you might get an molotov in your face instead.Oh wait, I'm not here to talk about The Hidden. Sorry 'bout that.Predator Hunting Grounds is also an assymetric pvp multiplayer game. Something like Evolve, or The Hidden as described above.In this game one player is the iconic Predator against a fireteam of four players.The biggest difference between The Hidden and this is that the fireteam actually has a mission to complete, the Predator is more like a side objective.Some games the fireteam and Predator don't even meet up! Depends on each party though.Also, compared to the dark corridors of The Hidden this takes places in the jungle which gives me some good ol' Crysis memories.I guess you could also see this game as Crysis vs Call Of Duty or something similar since you have one player with a huge advantage over normal meatbags... I mean soldiers.Easily the weakest part of the game though is that the fireteam faces some  soldiers on their way to their objectives.If the fireteam manages to kill the Predator (and cancel his self-destruct) the game will change into a horde mode challenge as enemy soldiers want to claim the Predator Corpse.And if the Predator takes out all fireteam members? Yeah, it is game over for them.I personally don't have too much of a problem that the Predator takes out a fireteam member in maybe 3-5 slashes.This is after all 'the' Predator's hunting grounds- not the friendly Predator's happy colourful playground with cushion castles!When you play the objective, damage other players (fireteam vs predator or vice versa) you recieve Veritanium (I don't know, alien cash?) which you spend on cosmetics and xp which unlocks classes, equipment, perks and weapons.Something quite nice is that the level between your fireteam character and predator characters is shared, so if you level up as fireteam your Predator will level up too.Matches can vary for about 5-10 and rarely 15 minutes, which is a good time span imo. Not to long, not too short.The developers also added a secondary game mode which places two fireteams against each other (4v4), and mid-match you can become the predator- increasing the odds against the other fireteam.I personally haven't tried is so far. But hey, for the bloodthirsty pvp crowd who want a sub-par Call of Duty clone you have that here.There is no PVE at all, and I fear if it would be added the playerbase will be split even further. If they could improve the ai and add an Predator ai the game could have some longevity.There are also some bugs that I have read about. Encountered at least one major so far, didn't hinder me but one player spawned in as an untextured unarmed fireteam member. Weird stuff.Although if there is one thing that irks me is that the fireteam has a big lack in the ammo department. There are some ammo crates placed about, supposedly. I have seen that ai enemies sometimes drop ammo, but it is RARE. There is at least one, but expensive, equipment option to bring more ammo.The Predator has always the option to fire ranged weapons thanks to it's plasma caster which is always recharging. The fireteam has no such luxury.And while I haven't played the Predator I think they should have some kind of (maybe not lore-friendly, stay with me) projectile weapon that is almost as hitscan as the fireteam weapons;Maybe the Predator could pick up human weapons and use them? Only for one clip maybe?There are dlc for this game which can maybe hurt balancing. Predator players can buy early access to a 'berserker' like predator with the viking or samurai for an example, therefor skipping having to learn to play the stalking game the Predator is all about.Fireteam players can buy early access to characters with their own stats, perks and also personal weapons. The Mercenary 87' and Hammerhead comes with grenade launchers attached!Note: When I say early access I mean early since those 'dlc' weapons unlock much much later after grinding. .Player counts for this game has always been low due to negative reviews which I believe are not entirely fair to the game. Angryjoe completely slaughtered this game in his review.Although for now thanks to cross play with PS4 the player counts has increased for the time being, since the game was included with PS+!Fireteam Tip 1: Bring one rapid fire weapon and a heavy hitter- whichever class you play as. The predator take a pounding!Fireteam Tip 2: You may want to silence your guns and mud up- that makes it harder for the predator to zero in on your position.Predator Tip 1: Keep yourself mobile! Don't stay on the ground for too long since fireteam member often have eyes forward- not upward! Predator Tip 2: You don't have to resort your valuable medkits to replenish health! There are pigs () running about the jungle. You can eat them for health!

_childDocuments_.review: Is this a great and fantastic award winning game? No, not by a long shot. Is it a fun way to spend some time in the Predator universe as a fire team member or the predator killing stuff? Heck yeah. I recommend if you're a fan of the Predator series. Tons of subtle and not so subtle Easter eggs pointing back to the movies.  Plenty of ways to customize your humans or predators through a easy to gain in game currency / level system with the option to get through their loot crate system. Some of the DLC do offer some early unlocks for weapons but nothing major. Game play is a simple PvPvE 4 fire team vs Predator and AI Stargazer dudes. Don't need to kill the predator to win but if you do ends the mission you're doing either leaving you to run out of the predators wrist bomb range or defuse and start a quick body protection mission for bonus XP.Balance depends on the people in the game. I've seen both sides OP in matches I would say slight advantage to the predator if they know what they're doing. Overall the game is fun if you enjoy this universe. Devs continue to release patches and have improved the game greatly since initial release where I played on Epic. Still some bugs and graphical things you notice out of place but don't detract from the game.

For the soldiers its more PvPvE than for the predator, which sounds good, but thats where most of the positives stop. The predator itself has some balancing issues, depending on which one you play making yourself either a mild annoyance to soldiers or an utter steamroller. It also suffers the fate of most asymetrical games where your experience is largely going to be determined by the playerbase you encounter and how many are playing around the time you decide to jump in; so your online experience may get varied millage. DLC is pretty pricey too for what each gives. With limited maps, far few than your choices in predators and soldier loadouts, missions may get dull on the soldier's end beyond looking out for space Tarzan jumping around in the trees.  This game I can only really recommend for die hard fans, as they get the visuals down pretty well and let you customize your predator and solider...provided you grind enough levels and unlocks ala Friday the 13th which I'm sure the devs recycled notes from.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, the night I bought it I put in eight hours as solely the predator. Amazing visuals, great sound design, the guns are all fairly well balanced, and not one hacker that I've seen thus far (it beats out most games these days for that last bit alone.) Just a fun game all around, but definitely needs more modes (perhaps a predator-heavy mode, maybe 2 on 2?) and has a few balance issues with some of the DLC, not quite pay-to-win, but almost (looking at you, ~terminator~ bionic predator.) You *can* play the game solo, private matches give XP (though not much) and the AI is in need of some work (when predator, they just run straight to you, no attempt at the mission or anything, just track you down asap. When humans, there just straight up is no predator AI to speak of.)I have no issues finding matches, only with the length of some of the matches because, for some reason, the players I've played against can just call the exfil chopper whenever they want. I may be missing something there, maybe I can call it too, but can't find info on how anywhere I've looked. A human based tutorial might help there, I guess.Overall though, as stated, great game. Couldn't be happier with it for the price, which was around 20-30 including all the DLC (minus the bionic predator, for obvious reasons) when I purchased it.

_childDocuments_.review: First time I ever left a review before, not sure why I felt like I wanted to this time. Maybe just because I was waiting for this to come out for a while? I don't know. All in all pretty cool game. I think they did pretty good job making it. I wasn't sure how they were going to manage making the predator feel as fluid as it ought to be in a 1st person shooter but it's ok. I realize the game is still pretty new and I haven't had much play time so far. Had good mission and had bad ones. Only one thing to complain about really and it's the reason I wrote this. Predator ranged weapons are crazy.Whether it's the bow, the spear thing, or the plasma caster, they really just mess you up pretty good. Which is needed for balancing but my complaint is that they can kill you. Not just down you. I've played a number of matches in a row where the predator just sat invisible in a tree and shot one member of the team to death, sometimes trapping them first sometimes not, then took off. And with the reinforcement taking a decent amount of time there really isn't a way to counter if the predator is competent. So they spot you, shoot one of you down, then to death, then jump away to recharge. And the speed they do this at will maybe allow you to mark them right before they run away. But worst case for the predator is really just taking a few hits then running off, healing, and coming back. Of course I'm still pretty new to the game. Maybe there is a counter to this, maybe better weapons will help. But I've seen this take out teams of noobs and experienced players alike. From people with miniguns and grenade launchers to just the basic starters so. I don't know maybe this is the predator meta and I've just been jumped in. Either way I'd suggest to the devs maybe make it so you can only be KILLED KILLED by the predator actually getting up close and doing a finisher, rather than being able to just snipe you down. That being said, I've been able to kill the predator before, though not when he's doing this strat, and have had my wins as well as losses. Just feel as though with this particular play-style there's kinda a wall there. Either way, still gonna play. It's fun, at least for now.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a tough one.Pros:-PC/PS4 crossplay works.-The Predator is reasonably well implemented and fun to play as, better than in just about any other game in the universe I've played.-You can play it single player.-Single player allows earning XP and progress and unlocks.-The visuals and sounds are good.-Rounds are constrained to 15 minutes, so it can be good for people who don't have a lot of time to play, and the time limit forces players to keep moving toward completing objectives.-Several maps to play on (game originally only launched with one, I read).Cons:-Crossplay is a major pain to set up.-There are still a lot of bugs in the game, and new bugs are still being added.-There is no AI Predator if you play solo as Fireteam, so it feels like a generic CoD knock-off you might call Shout of Obligation.-Pretty sure you can't play it offline, even in single player, because your progress is saved on the server, though your loadouts are not preserved between platforms/machines.-There are AI Fireteam bots if you play solo as the Predator but they stand in one spot the entire game.-The other random AIs scattered around the levels are pretty stupid and way easier to kill than the Fireteam.Still, as someone who doesn't want to deal with online toxicity, it's...okay.  I play it with someone else in my household and we manage to have a good amount of fun taking turns as Fireteam/Predator, but the amount of bugs that still exist (and new ones are introduced periodically) is really frustrating.  Like if you select DLC items as part of your loadout and another player doesn't have them, the game will reset your loadout to a couple of basic items when the match starts rather than warn you ahead of time there might be a problem/conflict.  Enemies will clip through objects like a vehicle or wall and get stuck inside, making them difficult or impossible to kill.  The rewards are all cosmetic stuff designed to maintain the grind and people buying lootboxes, which don't interest me at all.  You can unlock most things with gameplay, but it's going to take a really long time.All in all, it's unpolished at best and a complete mess at worst, but despite that, playing with friends can be fun, there are some choice moments now and then, and detonating as a defeated Predator and wiping out the Fireteam is a blast, pun intended.  If you dare to try it, get it on sale.  For the vast majority of people though, I really don't recommend the game.  I simply can't give a thumbs up to a game with so many glaring and mostly easily fixable problems that could make it great despite the handful of things it does really well.  If they actually fix and polish the worst issues, I might change my opinion, but you often only get one chance to make a first impression, developers.

_childDocuments_.review: The game shows promise in its game-play and foundation but is severely limited by its extremely low player-base and overwhelmingly poor performance, even with a very solid rig. I have not seen anyone able to comfortably run the game without utilizing mostly low graphical settings. Another issue that holds the game back, also retaining to performance, is the game's inability to determine your resolution. Your resolution will be set to 4k every time you launch the game, and will have to be manually changed using a work around (again, note that this does not save the setting upon restarting the game).To reiterate, I believe this game has potential, though I do not see PlayStation PC push to fix any of the issues with this port, as they have several other cash cows to maintain. As such, I would not recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: The short story:I'm not gonna lie. I've had fun playing this game, but this is a game made specifically for PvPvE and there is virtually no one playing it anymore, and of course as a result of this it has also lived out it's life (no more updates), and even IF you could find a group of people to enjoy it with the content is not all that extensive.The little longer story:This mostly appears as a product with very solid bones, throughout everything, but with very little game built around it. You either pick one of the 4 soldiers, or the predator. There is nothing groundbreaking about the soldiers, your typical 1st person shooter, and it works. The predator however is very interesting. A third person view where you can swing around in trees and really stalk and creep people out. Very nice!An important note is that you CAN play this by yourself. You pick the predator or one of the soldiers. The rest (or all of the fireteam if you play the predator) are bots. If you play the predator you must kill the entire fireteam and there are also NPCs which you can kill if you want. The fireteam must complete various objectives which revolve around killing the NPCs. IF you solo as the fireteam there will not be a predator. That requires a PLAYER. So be aware of this.The AI is horrible of course. Your teammates get in your way and pretty much do what they want. They are entirely capable of killing the NPCs, and on that note there is no difficulty slider, and the enemies just go at you if you are discovered.The setup is very good too IMHO, but I can't call it a story since there is no campaign, and it is otherwise only disseminated to the player(s) by finding various tapes that detail the "secret factions civil war". Two factions who know about the predator and hunt it for it's tech for their own purposes. Again they could have knitted together a little campaign or something it would have been great.Weapons and various cosmetics are very much locked behind leveling, and it is a  real grind. You also unlock a few more classes, both for predator and soldiers when leveling, so that also is not so great. But most of the predator classes, and a few of the soldier classes are entirely paywalled (like Arnie and Alice Braga - voiced by theirs truly to boot), so the game also gets significantly more expensive if you want the really good stuff, but their weapons can be unlocked by leveling at least (and just unlocks immediately if you buy the class).So a lot of good ideas, in fact I would say that Hunting Grounds could be a base for a truly exceptional game, but they just released the test copy. It is a lot of fun to swing around trees and stalk as a predator, but ultimately this is a multiplayer game, and there aren't all that many people playing it. I hope that the dev make a new predator game using these bones, and just make something truly exceptional.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good game. Not the best FPS by any means, as thats all it is when you play as FireTeam. Predator plays as a 3rd person experience with new gear and weapons than what you would've expected if you watched the movies. The wrist launcher and healing kit are the only things I really recognized. Obviously it's a 4v1vAi experience similar to Hunt, but FT has WAY more options available and the few that the Pred has are either OP or completely worthless. Obviously, skill is a major asset, as good players can win using the weakest pred and weakest weapon without perks, while a potato can fail even when using the broken options that are available. The FireTeam experience is honestly what I prefer to play, as you are encouraged to with a 30 second wait for FT and 8 min wait for Pred. But when I am the pred, i usually try and make sure the FT has fun. As you don't really get any rewards besides basic experience as pred, but FT can level up their weapons, get money, and even get the weekly objectives (something that pred normally can't help with). If you are planning on getting this game, keep a few things in mind:1) Illfonic had almost completely abandoned this game. The only content we have gotten is DLC. $6 DLC for a single predator (that is completely broken btw). 2) A LOT of players are toxic. Most will either leave the second they start to get in a bad situation or will be someone that sweats so hard you will drown.2a) EVERY WEAPON IS VIABLE!!! (I included this as 2a because of toxic players) if you ever talk with someone who has more than a dozen or so hours in this game they will most likely say that only 3 weapons are good (Sawz, Hammerhead, and 1011). And while these weapons are really good, ALL weapons can and will kill pred if you can aim and know how to track invisible monsters. Do not let some 300+ hour player tell you that you are an idiot for using a different assault rifle or an smg. This game has meme weapons that seem to be bad on purpose, but using them once will give you an idea of how bad they are. So you should learn what is good to use, what is fun to use, and what is bad to choose pretty quickly. 3) This game will get stale. If you are playing this alone, you will most likely drop it after 10-12 hours. Progression such as leveling weapons will only get you so far, so do not play this game just for the grind. Wait until this goes on sale for like $6 and then buy a copy for yourself, and a few of your friends. Get a group together or join one of the communities out there and play with people. Communication and friends make this game a good somewhat competitive game for you and your friends. The only reason I will continue to play this game is because I can easily spend 5+ hours at a time in privates or slapping potato preds with the boys and time goes by in a flash. All in all, a good buy. Don't fall for DLC scandals, the "Deluxe" version that comes with a few preds is enough to give you a wide range of pred options, and Dutch 87 is literally the strongest class for a varity of reasons. If you wait for it to go on sale, you can get both of those for less than $10. Which I highly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: This game at first seems like it would be a fun asymmetrical game that involves the Predator series. However after the 10 hours I currently have played i cannot recommend this game with the way it is.There are two ways to play this game either as a fireteam member who has to go into a zone do objectives and either escape or kill the predator. Then theres the predator where you have to hunt down and prevent and kill the fireteam members from doing their objectives. Sounds fun right? A game where your the hunted or the hunter, trying to escape from an immense force or hunting down humans. Well not quite. I managed to get 10 hours out of this game and think i've already done everything that can be done. Which for 30 dollars is a terrible deal. When it come to matchmaking, its completely up to rng whether you'll get good teammates or not. The game doesn't have any skill-based matchmaking currently and I think it's needed bad. New players should play with new players not the opposite. i feel bad curb stomping new predators because they went up against a high level fireteam and i dislike playing with new players because usually they don't know what they're doing and don't listen to others and end up dying somewhere or ditch us and leave the game. I don't think its the new players fault because they're new and are still trying to learn the ropes but they should be able to play with others their skill level. The game play gets extremely old very fast, Especially when you're playing as the fireteam. You just do the same objectives like "Get X number of items" and "Kill or Destroy X" and its not fun or enjoyable in any way. It's fun for like two matches but then it just gets old and repetitive. The gunplay is bad too. They're some weapons that are really good and everyone uses and some that just suck and are not worth using. Other than a model change there really is no gun variety.  None of the maps have that much variation and it feels like no effort was put into them. Each map has 2 big landmarks and the rest of the map is made up of jungle and random militia bases strewn about. The game has some positives like i think the game looks decent and matches the predator movies and the atmosphere is pretty good however the negatives outweigh the positives and i just don't think that this game isn't worth picking up at all even if it goes on sale because i don't think any amount of patches that add or fix anything can make this game enjoyable because the game at its heart is a bland asymmetrical shooter game based in the predator universe.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd spent a lotta time playing this game, and I don't understand the positive reviews, at all.First, just wanted to mention: the Devs (Illfonic) will just grab any license big-corps are willing to throw at them for a quick buck. Before all of this, they worked on Friday the 13th alongside Gun Interactive, which though Friday the 13th had legal issues down the line, a variety of issues that were known since even the Friday the 13th Beta were never addressed or fixed.Illfonic abandoned Predator: Hunting Grounds for their new Ghostbusters game, and their even newer "Killer Klowns from Outer Space", both of which you can guess they'll also abandon like Predator, once they've milked them and moved onto their next cash-grab IP - Killer Klowns even has the same class-system as Predator, as a means of easily monetizing it the same way.This is what Illfonic does, and in part as why I'm never buying an Illfonic game again - they're not a studio that's passionate nor dedicated to their games, and will drop it for a dollar, like Ghostbusters being Epic Store exclusive before immediately moving to Killer Klowns - they'd rather Epic's payout for quick money, rather than allow every platform to play, heavily Monetary-over-Player mentality.Moving onto my main points - Predator: Hunting Grounds, the game.-Can't earn new Predators/Survivors, you HAVE to buy them, and some are absolutely better than the Default/Free Predators/Survivors, to the degree you could argue it's Pay-2-Win.-Runs awful on modern hardware. Devs stopped even basic bug fixes & QoL development, choosing not to support DX12, which would've helped immensely.-Map variety is abysmal. Excluding the Night variants (same map, different lighting), there's 6 maps in total; 3 of which feel nearly identical.-2 Gametypes. Hunt (standard 1v4), or Clash (Control point TDM) - that's it, and Clash isn't remotely fun.-Grind to unlock cosmetics is absolutely insane - you will spend days, if not weeks, trying to earn enough tokens to buy ONE mask; or you can depend on RNG Loot-Crates to unlock it, which will very likely just give common-tier duplicates, which are worthless.-Extremely survivor-sided, especially when they know how to play (Sensor-Marker kill-squads) - they'll only lose if they're incompetent or new. -Predator needs to rely on Meta builds in order to effectively win; even then, there's no countering Meta-Survivor builds with competent players.-Survivor weapons are mostly the same, and those that aren't are either top-tier (so the same but better), or useless; leaving a very small relevant weapon/equipment pool. Still more effective than most of the Predators equipment, somehow.Overall, I can't recommend Predator: Hunting Grounds, even to hardcore Predator fans - The Devs abandoned it, it's extremely predatory in its monetization, and overall isn't very balanced nor fun, even with friends.

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game because my friends were playing it, and while overall I recommend it, I have some caveats I want to get into. It's a good game, but it has issues, and some might be deal-breaking for you, even if they weren't for me.PROS:-The game looks good, but more importantly the art style lends itself well to the gameplay. There's heat waves rising off of many surfaces, to convey just how hot the jungle is, but it also means that the Predator's distinct shimmer doesn't stand out the way it would if there wasn't so much heat distortion on the map to begin with. The dense foliage and massive trees lend themselves to the Predator's stealth nicely as well, but they also mean that a clever fireteam member can hide in the bushes covered in mud and get passed over by a Predator.-A healthy amount of gun customization and loadout customization means you can bring whatever it is you want to the fight, but usually not everything you want. No fireteam class feels particularly useless (though I like some much less than others), and for the most part, every Predator class is fun to play and useful as well (though the Valkyrie DLC Predator does absolutely nothing that another class doesn't do better, but that's really the only egregious example).-The game nails the aesthetic and tone of the first Predator film, down to Arnold Schwarzenegger himself voicing Dutch in a set of audio logs that directly follow the story of the first film (the narrative is genuinely compelling, if short). Even the voice of God in the sky (the game calls him Zeus) is a pretty fun character with a lot of that dumb, action movie charm.-At its best, the game is pretty well-balanced, with a coordinated fireteam typically beating an unskilled or careless Predator, and a skilled Predator picking apart uncoordinated or careless fireteams. It really feels like two different games, playing as the Predator being a stealthy, brutal, and high speed game of cat and mouse, where you alternate between being the cat and the mouse as you chase down fireteam members or run away while low on health. As a fireteam member, the game is a run and gun shooter with stealth and teamplay elements, which quickly becomes a fight for survival when the Predator shows up. The two sides play differently and they're both a lot of fun.CONS:-The game isn't well-optimized. My rig isn't exactly phenomenal, but it's one of the worst-running games on my PC, even on the lowest settings (which still look pretty good graphically, so I'd recommend lowering the settings anyway, even on a stronger rig). I would imagine no small part of it is all the destructible foliage the game is constantly rendering, combined with all the pretty heat effects and whatnot that I was praising earlier.-The game outright lies to you. More specifically, its UI does. I'm not just talking about UI prompts sometimes being wrong (though that is an issue), I'm talking about the awful statblocks it gives you for equipment. The game will tell you one class has less health than another even if they have the same health (Recon and Scout, for example). The game will tell you one weapon has a higher rate of fire than another when they're actually the same (the QR-4 and the G-ROW, for example). The game doesn't give you numbers, it gives you arbitrary bars that aren't even accurate. If you want accurate info on weapon stats, perks, specializations, or class stats, look on the wiki, as nothing in the game gives you those details accurately.-Remember when I said at its best the game plays well? Well, now we talk about how the game plays at its worst. At its worst, the Predator is hopeless against a competent, coordinated team, unless they resort to cheese. What kind of cheese, by chance? Plasma Caster spam. The Plasma Caster needs to have a refire time or a minimum charge time so you can't just spam it, because it genuinely ruins the gameplay experience to have a Predator simply spam the Plasma Caster into a room to finish off downed fireteam members or down standing ones. You see, the Predator usually has the advantage in combat unless they're against a very coordinated team, and that's fine. I expect coordination to be the only way to prevail in combat against the Predator, considering the fireteam doesn't even have to fight the Predator if they're quick enough and stealthy enough. The issue here isn't that the Predator is winning too many fights against uncoordinated fireteams, it's that it isn't fun to fight Plasma Caster spam, and it doesn't take skill to utilize. Sure, it sucks when you come across absolute gods of the game who somehow spot you even when you're standing still and are supposedly completely invisible, but I still feel confident I can win against those players if I use all of the tools at my disposal. As a fireteam member, I don't feel that same confidence fighting Plasma Caster spam.-This one is highly specific but I've lost games because of it, so it needs to be said. Stealth kills are not only unhelpful, but can be actively hindering to the Predator. There's a mechanic where you can stealth kill AI enemies or low health players from behind as the Predator, but it almost never comes up in a normal match. However, the prompt for it is the same prompt as melee attacking, either with or without a melee weapon equipped. Why is this a problem? Because there's been more than one occasion where I've been chewing through a team in melee with my Combistick only to somehow trigger a stealth kill prompt on an approaching AI enemy who is BEHIND ME, thus putting me in a lengthy animation that you cannot cancel, and causing the fireteam to force me into Second Wind when otherwise, I probably would have downed or killed most of the fireteam without them depleting my health bar. Stealth kills should only be capable of being triggered if your cloak is active, they shouldn't happen while you're actively engaging enemies. Whoever made that braindead call should be fired, flogged, or both.Overall, I still recommend the game. It's great fun, and the balance is, for the most part, pretty good. I usually feel like my losses and victories as the Predator were a result of my own skill and mistakes (except for when I get stuck in the stealth kill animation unwillingly). As a fireteam member, the wins are satisfying, and can sometimes be chalked up to personal skill, but are more often due to teamwork. Losses as the fireteam are usually because the Predator was skilled and we weren't nearly coordinated enough to deal with them. Very rarely do I feel the game is unfair, and that, I think, is promise for this game's future. Let's just hope they don't ♥♥♥♥ it up with overpowered DLC, eh?For real, most of the DLC are fine, but... Isabelle could probly use a nerf.

_childDocuments_.review: So what can I possibly say that hasn't been said before. First things first, I'm not a reviewer but I wanna share the experience I've collected so far within less than 2 hrs of gametime. So, I'm a big Alien and Predator fan. I think I even own all of the A(v)P games on Steam. But Hunting Grounds is one of the games I wouldn't even consider part of my collection. Because as bad as games such as Aliens: Colonial Marines might be, this game doesn't do the Predator franchise any justice. It suffers from many problems the Friday the 13th game already had like 4 years ago. (I ain't surprised, it's the same developer). Now I could go all about the Lore and Story of the Predator and what's wrong with it in HG, but imma keep it to the gameplay for now. I didn't know what to expect at first. I did watch some videos back then but playing it myself was a completely different experience. So lemme make this easy and start with the pros (It literally took me 5 minutes to think of anything positive regarding this game)- It's crossplay (So you can play with your pals over dem different platforms)- The map design is beautiful, but far from anything special compared to the current gen of games- Costumization (Outfits, Guns, Perks etc.) which adds a LITTLE variety or makes you OP asf- Is fun with friends if you wanna goof around in a private matchWow, 4 pros. It's the best I could come up with without exaggerating. On to the cons (My personal experience):- I get it, some People are new to this game. But why would you choose a pistol as your secondary? We're fighting a Hunter from outer Space here. Use a shotgun or SMG for best damage output.- Teammembers can't aim most of the time. Like, a good Predator is playing it carefully and hunts the Mercenaries one by one. But I've had so many situations where the Predator literally came bunny hopping towards us and basically killed most of us because every teammate was looking into another direction and NOT at the Predator. IF all 4 Mercenaries were to shoot such a careless Predator at once, he'd stood no chance (Happened once or twice in a good match). - Players that run off on their own. This game is a lot about teamplay, stick together and you might stand a chance against the Predator. Run off and you will basically end like the People in the movies and your team will suffer from your loss, especially when your mates are doing their best to get you back on your feet, just so you can run off again and collect them "goodies" for yourself. Rinse and repeat. - Now I don't know much about the META yet (if there even is one) but Bunny Hopping and spamming attack makes the Predator basically invincible. - Ping and Matchmaking. _childDocuments_.review: GRADE B+. This game does a great job of representing the IP. Everything from flying into the mission on the chopper to being stalked in the jungle by the predator feels exactly on point. And the game has a ton of unlockable cosmetics and weapons and skills to upgrade and level up. All things that make every game you play feel rewarding in some way. Predator: Hunting Grounds is a thrilling asymmetrical multiplayer game where you can play as either the iconic Predator or a squad of elite soldiers. The game is set in lush jungle maps, and the Predator must use its cloaking ability, deadly weapons, and cunning to hunt down the Fireteam. The Fireteam, on the other hand, must work together to complete objectives and extract from the map before they become the Predator's trophies.Predator: Hunting Grounds is a lot of fun, and it's a great way to experience the thrill of the movies from either side. Playing as the Predator feels powerful, as you stalk your prey from the shadows and pick them off one by one. Playing as the Fireteam is also tense and exciting, as you have to constantly be on your guard for the Predator's attacks and you stand the best chance working together. And you might disappear if you get separated from your team and wander alone to far in the jungle.Overall, Predator: Hunting Grounds is a great game that does excellent fan service to the IP. I would recommend it for a fun and challenging multiplayer experience. especially good, Of course, for fans of the Predator franchise

_childDocuments_.review: This has quickly become my current favorite game. Four human players are given a mission to complete, usually involving going somewhere and holding the interact key for a bit. It's Payday-Lite, with dumb as bricks AI. The real threat is that one player is a Predator, and that player wins if he stops you from completing the mission (by murdering all of the soldiers).Predators control extremely well. You can hold a button to get a targeted "leap", and most trees can be climbed up to begin very fluid running through the treeline. You automatically go from branch to branch, or you can jump to a branch in your field of view. As a result, a skilled Predator player is mobile and legitimately scary to be up against. Soldier gameplay is, as stated, fairly by the numbers, but doing it all while trying not to get murdered by a Predator elevates it. Queue timee have been quick. I've never waited more than a minute and a half, with times typically being more like 45 seconds. You can specify whether you want to be a human or a Predator, though the Predator queue is, as you may expect, much longer. I have been able to play Predator twice in my three hours playing with the preference set to neutral, so it's not impossible to get some surprise variety.There is a 4v4 mode that sounds like a domination style mode, however it never has enough players for a match. The one time I've seen it with a queue estimate, it was at 20 minutes. You play this for the main mode or you don't play it.

_childDocuments_.review: Playing as fireteam is like doing a group project at school. You're grouped with 3 other randos. Some of them will talk big on voice comms in the pre-game lobby, but ultimately they all suck and you'll end up doing all the work if you want to get out alive.Still, prepared to have your ego majorly stroked. Especially once you master the basic strategy of the game: move quietly/mudded between objectives, when the predator shows up—don't hide—shoot him until he is forced to heal, then work on the objective. Yes, your group members will consistently f*** up even this basic strategy. It's OK though. Online multiplayer is overwhelmingly full of PlayStation players. There's no auto-aim, so even a mediocre mouse+keyboard PC player will outperform like 90% of console players. You *will* be the action movie hero.I'd be remiss if I didn't mention the comically obvious bugs that the devs still haven't fixed. Like when you customize your weapon presets they don't save like half the time. Matchmaking on PC bugs semi-frequently (leaving the matchmaking and re-joining fixes it). Stuff like that.But, wow, if you like the Predator series, the gameplay design here is good. Really, really good. The way the fireteam needs to actively work on mission objectives is straight out of Predator 1. The way the Predator needs to really work to track the players, using heat signatures, footprints, sound, also out of Predator 1. The way the Predator heals is straight out of Predator 2. The ability for the fireteam to shoot off the Predator mask and deprive the Predator of tracking abilities is from Predator 1.  The ability for the fireteam to make the Predator bleed and track it that way is from Predator 1. The way the fireteam can use thermal evasion is from Predator 1 + 2. I could go on and on, like I haven't even touched on the weapons assortment. So many aspects from the movies are faithfully worked into the game as core gameplay mechanics.So, I like the AVP game series—very solid games. But if you're a Predator main, those games have nothing on the Predator experience in this game. For fans of the Predator movies (even the newer ones), you will not regret buying this game. Although maybe wait for it to go on sale cause it's probably not a game you're going to put 200 or 2000 hours into, owing to the lack of highly competitive multiplayer. As for people who didn't love the Predator movies? I don't know what's wrong with you.

_childDocuments_.review: So I'm mixed on this, I've put in just under an hour and I was interested in this for awhile. Picked it up on sale because I'd rather shell out 12$ over 30$ anyday being a cheapo and overall the game is okay. Nothing special but it does it's job right. There's definitely some pros and cons and some stuff in the middle.+Playing as the predator in terms of gadgets and movement is pretty fun overall, being able to use thermal vision and jump from tree to tree is pretty fluid+The sounds and overall graphics in terms of models and textures is pretty good+Being able to fight back as the fireteam with all the weaponry and gadgets at your disposal definitely feels good most of the time+There being ai forces in the map definitely makes this game different from other asymmetric games like it.+/-The mission pacing for each match can either be long and drawn out or end pretty quickly depending on the skill of the fireteam or the predator, this is neutral point to me because I couldn't really come down to a sweet spot with game length+/-Free Lootboxes from leveling up or finishing dailies feels kind of gross to me just because of what a bad taste they've left in my mouth in other games, not a huge deal since it's cosmetics but still bugs me-Night missions feels awful because even with nvg/thermal vision it feels like such a mess trying to find objectives or enemies-At the same time fights between ai, fireteams, and the predator can feel like a real cluster♥♥♥♥ at times, especially when you have objectives to guard a point and have to worry about not only the predator AND the ai at the same time-I get the self destruct thing is a thing predators do in movies but man is it annoying because it just becomes a frantic run gtfo moment unless you're fine with getting killed in the ensuing explosion, Almost every one of my matches ended this way unless the predator wiped us out-The overall playerbase is so small compared to other games even with crossplay, queueing up as fireteam is fast sure but if you want to play as predator? you're stuck waiting at a minimum between 3-5 minutes and sometimes even longer, longest queue I had was about 20 minutes. Not really sure how to fix this but it's def an issue.-Some of the fireteam classes being locked behind dlc feels gross to me, it's one thing when you make them cosmetics because it's whatever but the character classes themselves being paid dlc just doesn't sit right with me.Overall I'd really only recommend this either on sale or as something to play with friends for fireteam or as the predator if you're looking for a somewhat above average asymmetric game.

_childDocuments_.review: So I will be giving a positive review but I do have a major concern that coincides with this but I'll put up the positives first.- Good atmosphere, feels very much like the original Predator movie.- Good visuals that feels very much like the original Predator.- The Predator feels weighty and powerful, like a big monster.- The experience of a solid Predator VS the Fire Team very much feels like you're being hunted and fighting for survival amongst completing your objectives.- A good and varied set of customisation options for both sides in terms of both aesthetics and game play build options.Now for the negatives I have, which I'll point out my primary concern amongst as well.- Very little variation in terms of maps. You have a few set maps and we've not had any updates or additions of maps really whatsoever.This is the primary concern and negative I have with the game.- More or less an addition to the above, when we get DLC, even more so recently. The DLCs have all been simply more playable Predators, no updates to adding more maps, weapons or anything more meaningful. (Though we did however receive some balance updates as of April 2024, this is a positive.)- I'm unsure whether this is true, but this is speaking from my experience and the experience of a few friends who've played as the Predator, when you're playing against PC players, it can very much feel like they're cheating. I've had it where as a Predator, I'm simply unable to make distance or escape from the fire team. They just chase relentlessly and are able to somehow see me even if I'm invisible and not being pointed out as spotted. Keeping up with me even though I leap up cliff faces, jump into trees and make a wild path that should be essentially impossible for them to follow. This feels like somehow they might be using both wall hacks and movement hacks to keep up and constantly see me, I'm unsure whether this is true. _childDocuments_.review: This game should be amazing.  It really should.TLDR:  It's not.  Don't buy it.The graphics look several generations old, and that's on the epic settings level.  Crysis and Far Cry, yes, the originals, have far better looking flora than this game.  Graphics aren't everything, and if the gameplay is good enough it's easy to overlook sub-par graphics but in this case both fail to meet expectations.Movement is sluggish as both the fire team and the Predator.  Controls feel poor.  Aiming isn't too bad as the fire team, but it's pretty poor as the predator even after tweaking the controls.  None of the weapons feel like they have any oomph at all.  There's no impact, no weight to the combat at all, and in a game where you play as a frickin' predator that's a requirement.The cutscenes are mediocre, and I couldn't skip any of them.  Sometimes the sound just cuts out or doesn't exist for certain things, such as taking a trophy from a fire team member.  The sound just... stopped when the predator was taking the trophy.  I turned the music off so I can't comment on whether it's any good or not.One of the biggest issues is that I really didn't feel like a predator when playing as one.  They do have the abilities I'd expect programmed in.  You can leap, jump, climb, cloak, use a healing kit, and they've got a great number of weapons in the game but the gameplay?  It just feels off.  I don't feel like I'm a hulking predator at all.The fire team members feel a bit better, but something is still a bit off about the overall feel.Humans can also be bullet sponges and they really shouldn't be.  Some AI enemies took a *LOT* of shots to drop unless you hit them in the head a few times.  There's an option for head shots to be lethal, however some enemies have some pretty hardcore looking armour including ballistic helmets.  Since they had pretty heavy armour I didn't have a problem with some enemies needing two or three head hits to drop, however when you unload a 30 round mag into their legs and chest from short range and they keep coming as if nothing happened, well, I have a problem with that.Another issue is that apparently humans can parry the predator's melee attacks, which somehow stuns the predator and lets them get in a hit or two.  I've read that the predator can easily be killed this way.  Didn't experience that myself, but that seems wrong, unless the predator is seriously wounded already that just shouldn't happen.  They're so much stronger and tougher than a human, a full force swing from one that's healthy should blow right through a parry or block.  A human should stand no chance in melee unless the predator has already been significantly weakened.On that topic this is a game that would benefit from a more realistic wound system, limb damage, and permanent health reduction even after healing.  I could imagine slowly being worn down as the predator hunts the fire team, such as taking some damage after narrowly avoiding a shoulder cannon bolt that shatters a nearby tree because a few chunks of wood got stuck in my character's arm, having slightly weaker melee attacks, a slightly shaky aim, and slightly slower aim down site because of the injury.  Imagine taking a serious leg injury and being unable to run while the predator slowly creeps closer.  Every noise you hear, ever twig that cracks, would make you wonder if that's the last sound you're going to hear as you limp toward the extraction point.The same would be true of the predator, but it would take more damage to cause any debuffs or crippling effects.  It would also benefit from the ability to go prone, and lean around corners to really make use of cover - but you can't.My loadouts don't seem to save properly. I restarted a couple times and every time the loadout would default back to something else.  I read somewhere that this was on purpose, but I'd have a hard time believing that since there are numerous loadout slots that you can unlock so there's no good reason for them to revert every time.Speaking of unlocks... too many things are locked when you first start playing.  Way too many.  You need to give players a few more options early on so you don't feel like you're railroaded into one play style right out of the gate.Seems like they spent way too much time on the loot box cosmetics and not enough on gameplay, to be honest.  Every game seems to give you a few loot crates, each containing three cosmetic unlocks.  I did see some interesting looking cosmetics but after opening just a few I started getting repeats.  The repeats gave me 50 game currency per repeat, and I assume this changes with rarity - I only had low tier loot boxes - which was better than nothing.  You can unlock cosmetics with the in game currency which you do seem to earn at a decent rate, and there are usually a few challenges you can complete to get a pretty good chunk of them.Overall I liked the cosmetics and customization options, but too much of it needs to be unlocked and with the rather poor graphics I can't say the cosmetics matter as much as they could.The gameplay is poor at best, and the AI is almost completely brain dead, you can go loud and nearby enemies won't always react, or they seem to know exactly where you are even when hiding, in those cases they somehow GPS directly to you.  They need to take a look at some other, older games that had adaptive AI, like F.E.A.R., if they want this game to feel right.  In that game enemies would flank or change tactics, flush you out with grenades.  In this game they seem to stand still and wait to be shot, or they'll run right at you and then stand still waiting to be shot.  They don't seem to go for cover, they don't seem to use grenades to flush you out.  Nothing.  Maybe this is because the focus was on PVP, the 4 person team versus the predator, but the AI is just terrible and feels like a tacked-on afterthought.I really like the basic concept of a small fire team versus a predator while the fire team has a mission to accomplish and is harassed by the predator along the way so I had high hopes for this game.  Unfortunately it's a let down in almost every category and I've already refunded it.  I hope they either fix what's wrong, or another studio gives this a shot at doing this right in the next few years.

_childDocuments_.review: GET TO THE CHOPPER ...with your Fireteam of four -- as you are hunted by one ugly mother-****ing Predator!Arnold Schwarzenegger reprises his role as 'Dutch' Schaeffer -- furthering the continuity of the entire canon through an earned audio journal.  Jake Busey also stars, in an homage to his own father's late role in 'Predator 2' -- and is joined by Alice Braga, who carries her own character's narrative on from the events of 'Predators'.This love-letter to the machismo action franchise is a 4v1, objective-based hunter/hunted combat title. The human players perform objective-based assaults on NPC positions while surviving skirmishes with an alien antagonist.  Predator players track the party, and launch their assaults from the treetops.Fireteam members play in FPS mode, while the Predator gets a third-person perspective.  Various weapon unlocks/customization/cosmetics are earned through play.Bots are available when a lobby runs short -- and KIA players can take over (surviving) bot(s), making running a session with less people more tolerable.The game suffers slightly from the handicapping of mouse/kb that is necessary to give controller-users a fighting chance. This sacrifice allows for a massive playerbase through Crossplay -- w/ access to a pool of Playstation & Epic Store owners in addition to the PC.It probably won't offer a thousand hours of enjoyment like some other asymmetrical horror titles can, but it's a solid buy for your bucks.  In 173 hours of play time, I am sitting comfortably at level 183 -- and haven't even yet scratched the surface of the Predator-side of the Hunt!Overall, it's really great -- especially for fans of this franchise!If it bleeds, you should kill it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is honestly a blast. Playing as Predator is trickier than you'd think, but fun and rewarding. _childDocuments_.review: After playing it for several hours, and for the sale price of $15USD, I absolutely recommend this game if you are looking for a asymmetrical multiplayer shooter game. I have no problems finding games (this game is cross-play between playstation, steam, and epic). Thus, there is a good stable player base in this game. Playing as the fireteam you will find a game within a minute. Playing as Predator varies between 3-8min (so many people play predator).The overall gameplay of both sides is fun. Fireteam must do multiple objectives and then GET TO THE CHOPPA, or kill the predator, or "preserve" the body of the predator, plus a few other things. Fireteam requires teamwork, you will be picked off one by one if you don't work/stay together.  Predator must kill the fireteam. If you wind up getting killed, you can "nuke" the fireteam as a last ditch effort. There are some cool executions you can do as him as well. Both Fireteam and Predator has interesting classes to choose from (i.e. different perks, skills and weapons). Graphics look good. This game is "PvPvE" as there are AI enemy soliders. The AI is pretty dumb (I can compare the AI to the AI in the game WARFACE if any of you ever played that). They are more of a nuisance then a problem, so it's fun to shoot them dead. Though I do wish there were bit more of them. The developers have a roadmap every year which brings a new update (which includes new DLC of various kinds that bring either new map(s), weapons, characters etc. These updates happen EVERY MONTH (along with any bug fixes or whatnot). I hope though in the future the developers can bring more "theme" into new maps (as everything is jungle themed right now) and some more enemy soliders on the map. There is progression system for both sides.Overall, good game, interesting plays can be made, and some more cosmetics would be nice. Thumbs up by me. Overall, good game, good progression.

_childDocuments_.review: NO TIME TO BLEED!What can I say? I've now reached level 120 after over 50 hours of play time and I still keep coming back for a few rounds in the jungle because this game is still fun to play! Like so many licenced titles that are based on films, PREDATOR Hunting Grounds has its quirks, but you can tell that it's a game made by fans for fans.The game principle works so well that you can confidently overlook some weaknesses. One of these weaknesses is the NPC's AI. It is sometimes so miserable that opponents stand next to or in front of you and just don't shoot, or may run past you blindly. What's easy to overlook though, is that they don't actually represent a real threat (unless they spawn in huge numbers) and are more used to tell the Predator the position of the fireteam. They are just cannon fodder and deal relatively little damage, but generate the necessary noise through the alarm they can set off or just through firefights to get the Predator's attention. In terms of gameplay, the game shows its true strength. The Fireteam lands on the map and must complete various tasks while being chased by the Predator. Pretty simple, but that's exactly why it works so well.At first you might think the game is poorly balanced. Over time, however, you realize that this is not the case, but that it is actually crucial how well you understand and ultimately master the game. As a Fireteam you are forced to act as a team, since the Predator is far superior to the individual player. However, if you act as a unit and complete the tasks together and tactically clever, the Predator has a really bad time. And it is precisely at this point that gaming experience and skill decide who will leave the match as the winner. And that seems to me to be the reason why this game is so much fun, although in the end it is the same thing round after round, despite varying mission objectives on the few maps this game has to offer.There are rounds in which you, as a fireteam, manage to complete all mission objectives without ever seeing the Predator or even getting a scratch. In other rounds you will be literally obliterated within a very short time. Also in the role of the Predator you notice quite quickly whether or not you are dealing with a good team, since you also have matches in which you can easily take out all 4 members one by one. In other matches you realize quite quickly that a lot of tactics is going to be needed to succeed. Since your opponents also get better as you level up, the intensity of the game increases continuously.At the same time, the progression rate in which you level up and unlock new weapons and modifications is very high, which also keeps you motivated. And there is realy alot of content to unlock. The reward system is excellent, the cosmetics are just gorgeous and there is no pay to win either. This made me willing to buy some of the DLC happily. Another big plus is the cross-play functionality. As a result, there is still a large player base even after almost 2 years after release, as there are so many more Playstation gamers playing this game, and the waiting times for a new match are relatively short. This is where other developers can learn a lesson, because that's how you connect players and keep a game alive.All in all, one can say that fans really get their money's worth here. But also FPS players who are looking for a new challenge, will have their fair share of fun with this game. If you have trouble finding your way around the game at the beginning, just remember:"If it bleeds, you can kill it."

_childDocuments_.review: Def fun trip back into the original predator universe. For me it ran really janky on the highest setting (though my pc can handle well more than this), game runs fine on high getting a locked 60fps in game (not cut scenes), soo has room for optimization, esp in the loading into a round chopper cut scene.      I see many people saying the Predator is too easy, others too hard, well I have to say you just don't know how to either play as a predator, or have made a horrible build. Yes a good hunter (player) with a planned out build can be very tough and hard to kill, but a team built properly and working together can drop him working together, and knowing how to counter him (esp his/her melee's).     Playing as Predator is a real kick, esp when the fire team have no idea where you are. Throwing noise decoys and watching/hearing them freak out is so great.    The tapes of Dutch after the original incident you unlock are a nice touch, telling you what happened to him and what he has been up to.    My ONLY real gripe about the game honestly, I don't think the predator at any time should be able to see in normal vision, EVER. You should have to use I.R. as your main, and switch between the other modes that were available to them in their masks. A nice touch would be if you chose a pred. design without a mask (just rebreather) you have to see in all red, but that is just me being picky about the predator lore/tech.     That aside the game does have room for improvement but is really fun with a team who is working together. Hope to see more game modes and maps get added eventually. A urban map in South America or somewhere occupied by guerrillas would be interesting.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is a lot of fun with friends. Only gripe I have so far is that you can't cue with a group of your friends and have someone be the Predator. If you play with friends you can only cue as the squad of humans. If you want to play the game with your friends and have you or one of your friends be the Predator then you have to play the Clash game mode or you have to do a private match. Other than that the game is pretty fun. Good graphics, the gun play is enjoyable, and the overall mechanics of the game handle well. Also there are a lot of cosmetic customization items you can get for your human or Predator class. You get these cosmetic items by saving in game currency to buy field lockers or to buy the specific cosmetic item you want with the in game currency, earning field lockers by playing the game and leveling up or from weekly/daily challenges. You can get duplicates in the field lockers and if you do then you get in game currency equal to the duplicate item/s rarity which you can save to buy more field lockers or the specific cosmetic item you're wanting. Each field locker is 500 in game currency (Veritanium) and from my experience the game is very generous with the currency you earn from playing, leveling up, and completing daily/weekly challenges.  Also the levels of your human class and Predator class are shared so you don't have to level your human class to max then start over with the Predator class or vice versa which saves a lot time from grinding levels to unlock certain weapons, perks, and/or subclasses. I would recommend this game to people that are looking for a new game to play with friends and/or for people that want to experience hunting a squad of humans in the jungle as the Predator.

_childDocuments_.review: I was saddened by the abrupt halt in development for F13 due to legal reasons since Illfonic has show a strong love for 80s horror and when I heard that they would be at the helm of this game I was both intrigued but skeptical. Asymmetrical games have slowly become a mild hot commodity amongst video games and depending on the love and care the studio takes to improve the game it may either die off or live on. Thankfully I picked this game up at the right time thanks to a surge in players via Playstation crossplay and I'll be honest. I love but also kinda hate this game. As a fan of the Predator film series I was very pleased by Illfonic's excellent love and care of the source material going as far as including familiar faces from the films including humans and predators. But gameplay wise I feel like whenever you play as a human you're surely outmatched but then again I am terrible at playing as the predator so I really comes down to the mastery of that role. Playing as the human pretty much plays out like your typical modern fps which isn't a bad thing since I feel like the first person perspective heightens anxiety since you can't have a 360 degree view of your surroundings allowing you to easily get taken down by the predator.In a sort of fan service you can cover up with mud which makes it harder for the predator to detect you but dealing with that and human enemies does become a little much. I feel like if it played out like the first film where the human enemies are dispatched and THEN you deal with the looming threat of the predator it would better enhance match pacing instead of getting hit left, right, and center by numerous obstacles. And don't get me wrong it is a very fun experience when your team decides to work together but if you are dealt a terrible hand of players it can make the experience a little hard to swallow. I can definitely recommend it and hopefully F13 can come back soon thanks to the recent lawsuit result.

_childDocuments_.review: I still remember watching Predator for the first time when I was 12. I got home from school and I knew I'd be alone for at least two or three hours, so I went through my dad's case full of dvds. I knew what I was looking for, putting it into the player and watching it from start to finish. Predator is my favourite Arnold movie since and nothing has come close to over taking it out of all of Arnold's films. A few years ago when I saw the teaser for this game I was so hyped. Finally a game that's directly from the first and best movie. The soundtrack is perfect, the maps are great, the predator gameplay is okay. A lot of the elements from this game is taken from the movie, which I love.BUT. The game is a online multiplayer game only. No single player, no story, and no real connection to the movies other than tapes and recordings. The problem I have with this game was I hoping for something similar to Alien Isolation, if the alien before predator got a 10/10 game, then why can't Predator? It doesn't have to be a horror of course, just give us a action packed story where you choose to play human or predator. See how the story plays out from both sides. The fact its a multiplayer game Only really irritates me and by no means is a definitive game for the Predator. This game should have never even looked in the direction this game went, by the time I'm making this review its takes too long to find a match, which I can only assume that means not a lot of people play the game now. The customisation is nice but it somehow lacks variety, loadouts were honestly annoying as I had to constantly select the weapons I wanted over and over. However I did love seeing Arnold reprising his role as Dutch again, voicing his story after the events of the first movie by decades. Not to mention Isabelle after the third film. Hearing her story was Very interesting from where it left off after the movie. I enjoyed playing the game after the first hour or two, but after that I quickly got bored and wanted to play another game, the problem I have with games that are strictly multiplayer only is quality. Don't get me wrong this game does have it, but not to the standard a Predator game should have.Best part of this entire game was honestly the soundtrack and the references from the animations, other than that, I'm very disappointed with how a Predator game ended up like this.
