_childDocuments_.review: I’ve found myself enjoying my time spent with the game, and I think it has the potential to improve even more. I think if you’re in the market for something akin to Friday the 13th or Evolve, or just looking for a new competitive asymmetrical multiplayer experience, you could do a lot worse than Predator: Hunting Grounds. Just keep in mind that there are elements that feel a little rough, but barring that, it’s a pretty enjoyable shooter.There are of course some very big criticisms though. Easily the most annoying is that in order to find out how to play properly, you’ll really need to go online and watch some YouTube videos, because the game’s tutorial is terrible. Apart from a quick instructional, showing you how to use the Predator on a basic level, you’ll have to go into the extra’s menu to find some written tips on how to do other things. Neither go into the depth of what you can and cannot do in this game and it can be incredibly frustrating when the games user interface isn’t exactly helping you out either. A perfect example of this is when the Predator sets off his self-destruct, it wasn’t until someone defused ours that we even knew you could do this.Pros-------- Tense 4v1 showdowns- Progression hooks to keep you coming back- Fantastic audio and environments- Rewarding unlockables and customization- Movie soundtrack and other fun Predator tidbitsCons-------- Game seems to have a problem with Balance. It's not so great that the Predator can run in and kill all 4 squadmates with all of us shooting and it and it seems to have no effect.- Gameplay loop can get repetitive but because of how short the games can be I can accept it- Maps become stale after a while- Could use more strategic elements- Dumb human enemy AI- Match flow soon becomes repetitiveHunting Grounds is a decent multiplayer game with just enough content and ideas to make it worthwhile. It’s a huge improvement over Ifflonic’s last game, Dead Alliance, and one that’s definitely pumped up thanks to having a popular license to lean on and despite it's flaws it's worth checking out especially while it's on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Predator: Hunting Grounds

_childDocuments_.review: In general, I like the game and think it can be fun for Predator fans. There are not a lot of options as it is.Pros:-The Predator's movement in the trees is the best I have seen so far in a game.-The game does a good job at recreating the idea of the original movie in a game format.-The asymmetrical game mechanics work out pretty well. (I can feel overpowered or underpowered depending more on who I am playing with or against)Cons:-Sometimes, I think I spend more time waiting to play than playing.-Game lobbies are not persistent. (Once a match ends, it ends and you hunt for a new game.)-Forced 3rd Person for the Predator.-The Human AI is horrible and spawns out of nowhere. (Simply breaks immersion)-The Environment is not destructible. -Other than the training mission, you cannot play through the maps against bots only. (Looking at the AI, maybe that is a good thing.)+ It could be interesting to have a game mode of 4vs4 Predators or 2 Predators vs 8 Humans. Perhaps a town/city themed map
_childDocuments_.name: Predator: Hunting Grounds

_childDocuments_.review: This game is LARGELY a mixed bag, and could be excellent, or could be absolutely trash depending on what you look for.PROS:-Graphics are beautiful-Soundtrack is amazing and immersive-Diversity of maps, missions, gear and modificationsCONS:-Trash or nonexistent AI. (Human AI are downright awful, but they don't even have an AI for Predators, so a private game without a specific person playing as predator will result in that aspect of the game just never showing up.)-Balancing. Neither class is very immersive for the time-tested dynamic of Predator vs. Human. Melee for Predators is a JOKE. 6-7 hits WITH A SWORD just to down a person? You get gunned down in the time it takes you to land 3 hits, which necessitates a frog-hopping meta to survive and succeed, which is the EXACT braindead playstyle the developers said they wanted to avoid.-Frustrating idiosyncrasies: The predator has an energy supply that fuels the cloak, gadgets, deployables, whatever. You have to cease all energy usage for the energy to regenerate. Using thermal vision doesn't use energy. But YOU CANNOT regenerate energy while in thermal vision!-COMPLETELY LACKING a LITANY of Predator features we get in other, older games! There's no voice mimicry. There's no gecko-crawling. There's literally just the two vision modes (normal/thermal). The wristblades aren't customizable in appearance or function. There is no motion scanning. You can't even PICK PEOPLE UP. You can't even rip someone's spine out if they've died- for some reason you can only cut their head off at that point. YOU CAN'T EVEN STRING PEOPLE UPSIDE DOWN!-Completely embarrassing environment playability for the quality the maps are. The maps are beautiful. They're expansive, they are engaging to navigate and fight in. But you get CONSTANT reminders that you're in a rushed, insincerely developed game. You can come across a door that is VERY OBVIOUSLY poor quality wood. You can't melee it open (human OR predator), you can't use grenades, bullets, rocket launchers, or plasmacasters, NONE OF THEM. That flimsy wooden door is part of the building as a whole, and the structures cannot be harmed, so this flimsy door is stronger than anything else in the game. This makes sense???! NO.-The DEPTH of the human missions are laughable. They are essentially ALL just - Go here, hold or press E, kill AI, go here, find something, press or hold E and kill AI. That's it. It's bland busy work.-The structure of the gameplay as a whole, misses the mark in almost every aspect. 15 minutes is just too short for it to feel like an impactful, deep, complex and dynamic mission for humans to complete, and certainly is not enough time to stalk, analyze, and carefully plan your attacks as the predator. For example, the human missions (which can be used to circumvent fighting the predator for a victory) don't even necessitate the humans to split up, at ANY POINT! Even GTFO (a different videogame) has stages of mission progression where the squad of up to 4 people have to take different routes AWAY from the other group members to progress. It's a window of vulnerability, and a trial of hardship or luck. You're alone now, are you going to be attacked? Can you defend yourself? That risk is nonexistent in this game until you're the last person alive, and then you're probably just going to get killed, or the predator doesn't even know where you are.-The "Predkour" system they made for this game is the ONLY MOVEMENT SYSTEM the Predator gets. And it's doodoo. Climbable trees are highlighted in red. To climb into them you must walk close enough to get a button prompt, and pressing that button beings a lengthly climbing animation during which you are completely vulnerable and no other actions can be taken. From that point, it automatically takes you to the nearest branch level. Trees typically have 1-3 different levels of branch height. You are stuck to that linear branch, you can move left or right, jump to a different branch, or climb higher or lower in the tree through more, slow, limiting animations, Dismounting is clunky and delayed. You can't hang from the branches. You can't free climb to a specific position if it isn't on the top of the main branch standpoints. The tree doesn't move and creak under your weight. The branches can't be destroyed or damaged. The leaves don't shake and make noise. You can't "climb" literally anything else in the game, rocks, buildings, nothing. You can JUMP ON TOP OF THINGS, but that's literally it. Predators quickly realize the trees in this game are quite literally a waste of time, and they transition to spamming long-jump. So there is NO POINT IN THE GAME where you can stalk someone as the predator, and be upside down. You can't even be horizontal. You can't even go prone! -FIRETEAM HUMANS CANNOT BE ASSASSINATED FROM BEHIND UNLESS THEY ARE EXCEPTIONALLY WOUNDED. -There are literally no aspects of lore-related occurences in the game. Predators are HONORABLE when they hunt (Unless you're a Bad Blood, but then that should have it's own style of gameplay, right?) Well that has absolutely no implementation here. In fact, the developers DESIRE Predators to play this game from afar, only getting kills with ranged weapons. A maximum range plasmacaster or bow wielding predator wiping a team, that's the kind of stimulating, fun experience they wanted to create.-There's actually no system for tracking trophies! Sure you can customize which trophy you want your predator to wear as a decoration, but you have no collection or vault of trophies you've collected over a career of hunting. (For humans OR predators.)-Add in game developers who 1) Are intent on doing what THEY want to do, players be damned, 2) Don't care to listen about the state of game balance, and 3) Are intent on pumping out as much DLC as possible, whether it works properly, or not, and you have a game that is barely alive, and while it may persist, no one has ANY faith that this game will be polished into the giant gleaming DIAMOND that it COULD HAVE BEEN. That makes this game exceptionally sad to me. It really could have been something amazing.I had a heck of a fun time drinking in all the beauty this game had to offer, and grinding out customizations so my human loadouts and predator loadouts looked the way I wanted. Once I got to that point I found myself lacking any reason to pick up the game to continue playing. Predator Concrete Jungle (WHICH CAME OUT IN 2005) honestly has more immersive Predator gameplay.

Tried everything, changed the drive, reinstalled, verified file integ, nothing, it's a scam at this point.-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------20 hours in, level 70 and only played as predator I feel I have a grip on the gameplay at least on the predator side to give a review so here goes. I watched a few tutorials and some videos by BloodThirsty (Yes subbed, a great inspiration for learning the gameplay mechanics) to get a feel for it before diving in. I did the tutorial which only applies to playing as predator side of the game not the soldier (Fireteam) side of the game (which was a bit disappointing as personally I hate to be that player who really sucks and has no experience in a team), but let's be honest 99% of you will be buying it to be the predator :) The tutorial is basic, doesn't really tell you anything but I would say do it to get a feel for the controls, before the real challenge comes in. If you haven't bothered or cared (as in my situation) about playing or watching videos as a fireteam member then you are literally thrown into the deep end and it starts off really confusing... but you pick it up fast if you're willing to persevere.While learning there has been a few occasions where I thought I am doing something wrong, like the controls (specifically attacking) have become unresponsive for a short time (just a few seconds), I thought maybe some kind of stun however I was able to move around freely just my basic and heavy attack would not work, it was frustrating but this was probably 3 times in 20 hours so I can accept that (If it's something thats meant to happen in the game mechanics please let me know, as I said I'm still learning).After a few games I was just steaming into the fireteam all guts and glory and sometimes killing them all (This is down to my level, trust me this barely ever works as you start to level and play against experienced players). Eventually worked out what abilities, work best for me and that wearing them down from a distance the first half of the match is the key and not just trying to melee like a badass. Its sometimes a game of patience (unless you're playing a sweaty speedrun team, uggghhh lets move on and not even go into that). Now level 70 with 20 hours, I'm able to 4k 1/3 of my games, 2k 1/3 and I'll lose 1/3 but self destruct will kill the odd fireteam member (The self destruct part is fun in itself, sometimes a gamble but you'll see:))Loving the game, can't praise it enough, my average waiting time as predator is around 2 mins to get into a lobby, then a min or 2 to start match, so expect around 4-5 mins average as predator between game starts, but believe me when you get into it, theres time you will be frustrated, (not rust frustrated believe me LOL), but stick with it, it's totally worth it and rewarding when you get that feel for it.See you in the jungle.

Additionally, the game has some bugs, ranging from players loading into the game only to be permanently stuck in t-pose unable to do anything, to the lobby just completely crashing. Aside from those several issues, i thoroughly enjoy the game. The maps rotate well, the missions are randomized and i truly sometimes feel like I'm being hunted by the predator in the game. It is extremely fun to play with friends once the multiplayer issue is sorted out and its also cross-play. The weapons are relatively well balance, aside from a couple. The player community on steam is quite small, however I do usually enjoy the playstation players (even though they are heretic console players). One great feature this game does have is that the predator can hear the fireteam talking. I like this feature because, just like the movies, one can come to terms with the predator player and they will sometimes show you mercy, or in my case, you can sacrifice the one loud breathing, mic eating, console player to them in exchange for peace. Aside from all the issues, and what most people will say; "I've played games like this" or "I've watched the clips and I already know how this game is and it's trash", It is good fun and a really chill break from all the other games out there. So, while I'm more of a middle of the road opinion in this review, I have to put no. I cannot recommend this game in this state. Maybe someday we'll get that fabled remaster of Concrete Jungle. _childDocuments_.review: Underated byproduct of the Friday the 13th all vs one era. Fireteam is fun with a myriad of fun tools and guns, making it possible to be the most effective killing squad with friends, or the last man on the chopper out if solo. you do have to maintain some sense of teamwork to survive, and also deal with the cringey PS4 players who never seem to be enjoying themselves. The Predator is fun, and seeing as the last comparable iteration was 2013 AVP, it feels much funner and friendlier to play, with classic movie weapons and some we've only ever seen in comics. However, whereas matchmaking is normally 40s-1 minute, Predator matchmaking can range from 5 min to upwards of 30 min wait times. New content(mainly Predator) is added pretty frequently, so there's always a new invisible florida man to face down in the jungle.
_childDocuments_.name: Predator: Hunting Grounds

_childDocuments_.review: The main mode of play "Quick Match" is very buggy and half the time you have to leave and try again. The predators just get way more experience than the fire team members, sometimes even when they lose (even with the 30% bonus for choosing to queue with "no preference" selected), which does nothing to incentivize the people who don't actually ragequit when they don't get to be the big bad.Despite all that, it's generally a fun game to play. The weapons and utility items are enjoyable and the concept of the game is excellent.
_childDocuments_.name: Predator: Hunting Grounds

Plus nothing is cooler than blocking a predators attack with a knife while staring them in the face while ♥♥♥♥ talking.

Unless u got friend are playing with u if not really going to struggle to find player to help u out.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd say 5-10% of games the objective will bug and your only way of winning is by killing the predator. _childDocuments_.review: So I bought this on a whim and didnt know what to expect cause so many people said this game was deadI've only played 7.8 hours at the time of making this and I've reached level 36 and got into fireteam matches within 30 seconds to a minutePredator matches take like 3 or 4 minutes As for the game itself I'm not normally into shooters but I sorta more play this for the experience of shootin predatorsIf you like the movies you'll really love this game it's fantastic If you are looking for a really good shooter I'd say just move on cause this game definitely has its flawsBut if you like games like DBD and Friday the 13th you might like this it has that similar formula of team of people trying to survive a powerful monster except you can shoot that monster into dust really easily
_childDocuments_.name: Predator: Hunting Grounds

_childDocuments_.review: This game is genuinely very fun, especially if you have enough buddies to form a full premade fire team. However there are plenty of things that could use improvement. The lighting causes some mad framerate drops sometimes even on a great machine, for some reason 4k is not available. Overall the game is probably not very well optimalized especially during sudden and major lighting changes.There isn't much content at all, the main reason to keep playing is thankfully the fun factor, which I'm scared may diminish. Not very many customization options, main variety is in "shaders", which are re-colors, which some people may not care about at all. I am hoping we will get some new models, faces, hair, more gun customization. Extended mag, suppressor and 2 optics are not gonna get people excited about customizing.I understand that this is a jungle game, but all the maps end up feeling the exact same, there are not enough specific map features to immediately recognize a map, no matter whether there is an air strip on it or not. I wish there were more urban maps as well (City hunter), or throw in a desert, big lake with little islands, southern city with a big park in the centre, there are so many options other than forest.Also definitely a missed opportunity not having aliens. Would be interesting to see Predator vs 4 aliens, or Predalien vs a fireteam.I also understand the AI is just a fill to have some other feature there along with the PvP, but man is the AI ever brain dead, they run at you and gun, that's it. If you jump on top of a truck, they loose path to you and get confused. Also AI, even with a helmet on, shouldn't be able to survive 6 headshots. Gunplay is also mega arcade-y, even more than COD and that's pretty hard to do.Also there are some balance issues, smart play is often very hard and not very rewarding, many predators just choose Ghost Samurai with katana and hack and slash in the first 3 minutes and often end up being successful. On the other hand, if you have a Recon Spotter with Tracker perk on your team, you can easily turn the hunter into the hunted, that combination makes all the difference on a fireteam.In the end, this game is majorly entertaining, I have blast playing it, it just could have been so much more. I am very much hoping to see this game grow and get better. When you buy this, you will have lots of fun, but the initial excitement may diminish and you will constantly be pointing out with your friends what could have been improved, there are a LOT of missed opportunities. Could have been a 95/100, but probably stands as 65/100 at the moment.

_childDocuments_.review: Just wish they had put the effort into making a fun single player experience with a multiplayer option, rather than a multiplayer only game where most of the time you can't even play as the predator without waiting for a ridiculously long time to enter a lobby, only for the game to end five minutes in. At least the loot boxes are cosmetic only (as far as I can tell) and not pay to win. Get the folks who made Alien: Isolation to make a Predator game.

_childDocuments_.review: The cross-play with PS4, and it being free with PS Plus for Sep. 2021, makes finding matches fairly quick... if you're looking to be part of the fireteam. If you queue as the predator in the "Hunt" game mode, it could take anywhere from 3 to 5 minutes. There is another game mode called "Clash" which is also just as fun - but drastically different in dynamics.Take IllFonic's previous asymmetrical horror title - Friday the 13th: The Game, and balance it. Take 7 counselors and trade them in for 4 hardened spec ops soldiers. The Yautja is not as all-powerful as Jason Vorhees is to the high school camp counselors.You will hide in treetops, and pick off soldiers one by one more often than you will rush into a group of them. You can die as the Predator. It is not uncommon, if you are not careful.For any fan of the series, this is a game you should definitely play.

_childDocuments_.review: As a Predator fan... I love this game ! Beside games, I didn't expect  they asked Arnold and Alice Braga, Jake Busey for recording.... No matter the old faces[sound ] or the story telling, that really is a surprise.And............  THAT THEME MUSIC !!!I know they said there won't be 87's jungle hunter skin as DLC selling but there is no pre-order on STEAM.That skin of course means a lot to us [CLASSIC !, FIRST APPEARANCE SHOWED ON SCREEN!], I really hope STEAM can add this on.

_childDocuments_.review: Illfonic seems to think re releasing a 4 year old game with no apparent fixes to old issues such as audio bugs and CONSTANT game crashes was a good idea; There doesn't seem to have been any real effort on their part at this moment in time to actually improve upon there original attempt at what should be a an easy win considering a brilliant IP and a stagnant market of failures in asymmetrical 4v1 multiplayer horror survival games. In comparison, for the £35 i paid for this 4 year old hot mess I could purchase its main competitor DEAD BY DAYLIGHT as well as multiple DLC packages letting me play as ALIEN, CHUCKY AND HELLRAISER; When considering the price of both and the overall "replay-ability" which in this genre is arguably the most important area of the game design it should be a no brainer to let Illfonic use their camouflage to disappear deep into the jungle where they can either work hard to turn this game around or set of their Self destruct device laughing manically at managing to fool a community of fans into paying for this game more than once. .Unfortunately i can only see Predator Hunting grounds heading in the same direction as Illfonics previous momentous failure "Friday the 13th" without a lot of needed TLC. Illfonics goal appears to be, If they can bleed us for every penny they can kill us. 3 / 10 - The biggest bait since "WaNt SoMe CaNdY"
_childDocuments_.name: Predator: Hunting Grounds

_childDocuments_.review: Not a bad game at all. Graphics are cool, and being in the jungle is awesome. Would be nice to have more maps though.Some predator weapons are way too powerful and are ultimate cheese mode for easy wins which should have been fixed a while ago but have been let to fester. Also, some Predator can kill you in 1 or 2 hits in melee giving you absolutely no chance at defense. While it IS part of the movies, it's a bad experience for players. Allowing Predators to intentionally use the AI to trigger camp alarms before the FT even reaches that quest location to give them an even bigger disadvantage is also extremely shifty and should be addressed.FT weapons also need an adjustment, like some timers on explosives are way too long and worthless against the Predator because it's so fast and the timer is so stupidly long it renders frags almost worthless against it, but they'll butcher the AI. Bots are retarded and need a BIG update to make them at least semi capable, at the moment they're fodder for the Predator who kills them first so a player can't take over the bot when they drop and thus gives the FT an even bigger disadvantage.All in all, some small tweaks to weapon power and timers and you've got a solid game for fans of one of the best movie creatures ever created. Nothing like unloading a clip into a Predator who was a little over arrogant and asked if you wanted some candy before engaging. Plenty of room to customize every facet of your characters both Fireteam and Predator as you level up from clothes/armor style to color of weapons. if it's on sale, it's a safe buy.
_childDocuments_.name: Predator: Hunting Grounds

_childDocuments_.review: From the perspective of a Predator player...If you want to play as the Predator, prepare for either 5-15 minute wait times or play against the NPCs, who are quite worthless and not even worth "hunting". No I'm not exaggerating, they do almost nothing. There are bots, kind of, but as of the time of writing they've just been introduced and they do nothing unless there's another player on the fireteam. They literally won't move otherwise. The Predator really feels like the ones you saw in the movies. They travel in high places with superhuman abilities, are very tough, and very deadly. Thermal vision, cloak, plasma caster and a whole plethora of weapons make for some very interesting hunts.If you get a game going, it really shines. If the fireteam splits up, they become very easy prey. And on quickplay, they almost always split up. If they stick together, they stand a very good chance of winning. So why the not recommended? Because literally everyone wants to play as the predator, and who wouldn't? It's bloody awesome! BUT the developers made a critical mistake in thinking that there would be enough players who wanted to play fireteam at this price point that there would be enough players to make it work. Even with crossplay with EGS and PSN, it's not enough. The bots that were introduced have not helped, at all. I would be happy if I got to play 1v1 against the bots and a single human, but that doesn't seem to be happening either.So, as enjoyable as this game is, it's really hard to get a game going if you want to play the namesake, which is THE point for a lot of players. If you can get a friend or family member to play with, you can create a party and play each other. Sadly that's not an option for me at the moment either.If they remedy this wait time problem somehow, or you are a lot more patient than I am with an unpredictable estimated time that seems to increase every time it gets close to time, then I would absolutely change this to a recommended review. As I said, when it plays, it really shines.

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy "The Predator" this is about as close as you can get to feeling like you're in the original film.  The game doesn't have a ton of content, but it's fun to team up to fight the Predator with friends or to hunt them as the Predator.  Not the most polished game, but it is fun and for the most part works well at this point.  Definitely worth $15 in my opinion if you catch it on sale like I did.
_childDocuments_.name: Predator: Hunting Grounds

_childDocuments_.review: Every match plays out like the original 1987 film. When there is a good Predator teasing and hunting you the suspense is palpable. The shooting is a little clunky but has gotten better with patching. Game really shines when you have 5 friends in a private match all taking turns hunting each other. I do wish that when you hit the level cap that the XP you earn somehow counted for the in game currency. It would help with the replayabilty IMO. "If it bleeds... follow the blood trail, shoot off the biomask, kill the Predator, defuse the bomb, teabag, repeat."
_childDocuments_.name: Predator: Hunting Grounds

_childDocuments_.review: Ok so this game has some problems but it is also really awesome.First, the problems.Multiplayer is difficult to get right. Want a friend to join? Figure out how to create an Epic account, get your friend to do the same, get both of you to link your Epic accounts, friend each other on Epic, download the Epic launcher, restart the game and maybe your computer after you've done this, then send an invite after creating a party in game, and they'll accept it and then yay look at that you're playing the same game together, minus any other player.  Wow. What a friggin mission.  Want to invite others you've played in game and think are really worth playing again? Forget it. There isn't even a method to send them a message to come find you. Just forget it.  So you're stuck either playing one single friend (maybe more if you have them all online) or playing complete strangers.  Nothing in between.Now on to the positives, and yes, there are many.  You'll notice I gave the game a thumbs up. Fix the broken multiplayer stuff and this game is a real winner.The sound effects, graphics, game play, features, balance, everything about this game is just spot on. Really amazing.  Also it's a nice refreshing change that in one game you might be facing complete rookies, and in the next you might be versus an alpha predator who's been playing this game since 1852. You just never know what you're going to get. Very cool because sometimes you'll win, sometimes you'll get your ass handed to you on your own face.Overall this game is great, really great. Just fix that damn multiplayer stuff, seriously.
_childDocuments_.name: Predator: Hunting Grounds

_childDocuments_.review: Buy and play so there's more people and faster matchmaking times. If you like Asymmetrical 1v4 games, this is one of the best. Don't get made at a good predator, they've been doing it for a long time, and be understanding when you get destroyed as a level 1 predator vs level 100 mercenaries, give it a chance, its  a lot of fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Playing as the Predator is fun but the queue times for Predator are awful, its like 8-9 mins on average.The Fireteam have very quick queue times but playing the Fireteam can be very frustrating because the random teammates you get are generally terrible in my experience, always running off alone and dying. Overall this game is disappointing, I really hope the next predator game we get is a single player game.

_childDocuments_.review: Hunt or Be Hunted - Predator: Hunting Grounds is an immersive asymmetrical shooter set in remote areas around the world, where the Predator stalks the most challenging prey. Play as a member of an elite Fireteam and complete paramilitary operations before the Predator finds you. Or, play as the Predator to hunt the most worthy prey, choosing from your vast array of deadly alien tech to collect your trophies, one by one.

name: Isonzo
detailed_description: Charity DLC: Movember Handlebar Support the not-for-profit Movember Organization with the new Movember Handlebar DLC. Unlock the Handlebar Moustache and fit it on your upper lip to impress your peers! The Movember Handlebar DLC is available for purchase until January 2nd, 2025. Proceeds will be donated to the not-for-profit Movember Organization. PC Editions Overview About the Game World War One expands to the mountains of the Italian Front - beautiful but deadly in equal measure. Take part in key offensives of the Great War, from the Sixth Battle of the Isonzo to the Strafexpedition, and lead your team to victory among the scenic landscapes and peaks of Northern Italy. Isonzo is a realistic tactical multiplayer FPS crafted by BlackMill Games, known for their critically acclaimed authentic WW1 wargames such as Verdun and Tannenberg. Immerse yourself in faithful recreations of historical battles with intense 48-player matches, testing your tactical skills and mastery of Alpine warfare. Decide your path to victory: whether you’re leading the offensive with grenades or using mountain trails to flank enemy positions, you have options. Dive into combat or take a supporting role cutting barbed wire and crewing heavy machine guns and mortars. Thanks to a unique flare gun system, mark targets for artillery strikes or biplane flybys, before charging in to finish the job at close quarters with bayonets or trench clubs. Choose from six distinct classes and build your loadout from a selection of 50+ iconic WW1 weapons, along with historically accurate equipment and perks specific to each class. Play as a Marksman to pick off soldiers from afar, storm enemy lines with the Assault class, issue tactical orders as an Officer, and much more. After choosing a class, make it your own by picking from a large variety of role-appropriate uniforms, accessories and headgear. As a finishing touch, you can even pick your mustache from several famous wartime styles! From hillside fortresses to mountain trenches and city streets, fight through varied Alpine landscapes inspired by historical battles. Learn the lay of the land to maintain cover and surprise your enemies - or go a step further to shape a dynamic battlefield by placing sandbags, barbed wire and ammo crates. Trench periscopes and sniper shields offer even more tactical options, but beware of poisonous gas attacks and artillery barrages! Taking inspiration from the years-long struggle for control of the Alps during World War One, Isonzo brings the authenticity of the conflict to all players. Everything is recreated based on research and field trips, from sound effects, weapons and uniforms down to the houses, vineyards and trenches you’ll be fighting over. Choose your side and immerse yourself in History! Enlist for more First World War action with the other standalone titles in the WW1 Game Series: Tannenberg and Verdun. Experience trench warfare on the Western Front in Verdun, or maneuver for control of key sectors in Tannenberg on the Eastern Front. Choose from a range of squads from across the war, as they fight for control of the ever-changing frontlines.

The current system requires dedication to unlock all of the kits, the game play also feels a bit different than the previous games (not to my preference).

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game because it covers a part of history that's under reported on, a war at the turn of the century, the guns are awesome, and the environment is so good I might have to visit some of these places irl especially the mountains. Would be a fun game to play with friends. Wish more people played this underrated game.

_childDocuments_.review: Community is toxic and sweaty. It's almost impossible to get specials unless you sit camping the role the entire round waiting for Blind Elmer the Eyeless Marksman to have an aneurysm and headbang Alt-F4 so a sighted person can try it.The system for unlocking new weapons is a step back from previous games. Want to get new stuff to give you versatility to play the objective? Well, too bad. You get shoehorned into playing the game a certain way until you grind through the stupid challenges and play how you actually want.Have yet to figure out how spawns work. The teammate you choose to spawn on is in combat and unavailable, so it spawns you right next to him instead. When it does let you spawn on him, it plops you 120ft away on the side of an open hill.Officers are great or West Pointers, there is no in-between. I've seen games lost due to one guy's horrible smoke and gas drops and when they can't make good calls on support, the whole team suffers for it.Looks great, plays smooth, but the gameplay makes me wonder if the devs built a time machine back to 1995 when crack was popular and chic.Don't be like BlackMill. Crack is bad.
_childDocuments_.name: Isonzo

_childDocuments_.review: It's not ready yet;Hit scan weapons with no lead required regardless of distance.Lowest graphics setting gives users an extreme advantage is seeing enemies and basically removes most grass and bushes. Having the pretty graphics all set to ULTRA which is easy even on an old 1080ti results in you getting shot through trees and stuff that low setting users see right through.Maps are pretty tight, not the worst point but meh
_childDocuments_.name: Isonzo

_childDocuments_.review: Solid game overall, movement is decent, gunplay feels right and is responsive. Really only 2 gameplay loops, defender and attacker with a combined capture point and a rush-esq S&D point. Though the variety of maps and gameplay styles of the different classes  are where we find the gameplay variety. There are some glaring issues: Challenge completion is needed to unlock items and perks, many are fine early on and can encourage new players to play the objective and plan tactically; though later on they begin to get tedious, and force players to stick to certain tactics for many games and possibly avoid making the right decisions for the team simply because the challenges become more important than individual wins. Also, a fluctuating player base means you'll often find yourself playing with many bots. They can often have superhuman senses of perception and aimbot shooting, this needs to be updated and improved as it forces the player to almost abandon human tactics such as hiding in the dark or flanking from what would be out-of-sight to any human player.Despite this, the game is fun, addicting and scratches that tactical shooter/ Light mil-sim itchstrong 7/10 with a capacity for at least an 8.5 with the right improvements.
_childDocuments_.name: Isonzo

_childDocuments_.review: So far I've found this game to be fantastic, it has almost everything I wanted out of it. I really enjoyed the first two games in this series and this one definitely improves on almost every aspect of the old ones. Have to say I love the verticallity of the maps and the way they've redone classes. There's so much praise to give this game but I hate writing reviews so I'm not going to fit it all inSome of the cons tho, I wish you could enter games as a squad, I enjoy playing with friends so that was a nice feature they had before. Some minor glitches but that's to be expected and the devs are working out those problems quite quickly. If you're looking for a game where you can rambo your way across the map firing LMG's from standing like they're .22 plinkers and using obscure semi-auto rifles that were technically time period correct but only issued to like 6 guys in total then this is not the game for you. Go play BF1, don't waste your time and money. I don't want to see you in the chat complaining that you have to use the same rifle that everyone else is issued, you're not gonna get you special little prototype assault rifle.
_childDocuments_.name: Isonzo

_childDocuments_.review: I've been meaning to try a game from this series for a long time, since Verdun actually.Loving MilSim, I always wanted to try this out, and to be honest, I'm very disappointed.There are so many things wrong about this game that makes it just not fun.Although there's still plenty of good things about it : looks good, runs well etc, the base mechanics and map design arent good.From the spawn mechanics (that are horrendous) to the damage, it makes it plain not interesting on the long run.It is still quite enjoyable for a little bit but if I have to describe it : it's flat.Don't get me wrong, I was top of the scoreboard each game and I still didn't have fun. It's supposed to be a realistic game but you can spawn right in front of an enemy and get killed before even being able to move (fun right ?) or sometimes you'll spawn directly in the enemy flank, then pistols will one shot you at any distance but has a higher fire rate than any other weapon, and since this is WWI (first to shoot first to kill) it is plain stupid.There's no real "atmosphere" as well as being truly lost between arcade and simulation without mentioning the pure lack of any intuitive gameplay in order to play as a team.To be honest, I'm really disappointed by such a game, it is no mistake it fails to fill up its servers out of the free weekend.
_childDocuments_.name: Isonzo

_childDocuments_.review: A nice FPS shooter. Easy to get started, hard to master. Maps are beautiful and it feels good. Sound design is impressive. If you are coming for the Battlefield series you will miss some of the interaction with the enviroment, like shooting over cover when crouched or leaning behind cover. This would really add to the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Isonzo

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game. Gunplay similar to Hell Let Loose with some aspects of BF1's gameplay. Accurate load outs and mostly accurate sights on guns. Beautiful maps and vistas, though there could be a few more maps and gamemodes. Sound scape is pretty good though not as over the top as battlefield or CoD. Some peculiarities such as not being able to reload most rifles without firing all your shots and the enbloc's don't ping when you chamber the last shot. But all in all, 8/10, really enjoying the gameplay and setting
_childDocuments_.name: Isonzo

_childDocuments_.review: I bought and used to play this game on  since release  but was rewarded this game on PC. The game is, substantially, alright for an casual indie multiplayer game based on WW1, although it still has some minor flaws around the edges. While the  lack of playable game modes does take a bit from the potential this game can have, it has many details that can make it a memorable experience for some players. In terms of  videogames, players looking for games like this may find better examples elsewhere, varying from  However, for what it is and what it pulls off, it still stands pretty well as its own game in its current state, although there is still much room to grow.I would recommend this to people looking for a modern historical video game that feels similar in design to older titles like the original  without compromising on historical accuracy to the same extent as  (which is perhaps as accurate as Don Quixote writing his own rendition of 'All Quiet on the Western Front' after hearing it read by a random trench rat).

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels like a great upgrade to the original Verdun but all the same glitches and bugs exist if not a little more. I really want to enjoy this game but I keep seeing so many problems. Every match people fall through the map. You spawn on barbwire or can very easily be spawn camped. There's animation problems with reloading. Prone is a trap as it's glitchy and constantly has you stuck.  How would you like to reload your sidearm only for your character to very slowly and comfortably wait to fire it or cancel the reload all together? One pistol doesn't reload until your characters elbow straightens out (after the clip insert and slide pulled back.) If you move before that elbow it will reset to 0!Unfortunately on top of this theres a group (and notorious player) that has utilized every exploit in the game. It is required to use these in order to have a chance against them. They dominate any server they're on. You're likely to spend more time waiting to spawn than playing if you come across them. Expecting them to balance themselves out for fun is futile. There is no casual play as too many take the game seriously. The best part is the community, or rather some of it. As the game progresses it appears to become more toxic. Which is unfortunate because if it isnt the bugs, the guilds/ extreme imbalance issues, or the learning curve, it is the people that will be the final nail in Verdun's coffin.

_childDocuments_.review: Update: Trying out the game again after a lot of update, first thing you see is a message telling you they are going to collect data about you and there is no way to opt-out. Great, I need more company to collect informations about me.It's hard to recommend this game because even if the gunplay is really fun, there is too many things that make the experience really frustrating.If you want a WW1 for the experience and ambiance, then this game is probably right up your alley, but if you want to play this game also to have a good infantry FPS experience, then I wouldn't recommend it.The screenshake is probably what kills the game most for me. It's really a big screenshake effect and it happens whenever there is an explosion or something is shooting at you.Which brings me to the next point: the game is a huge explosion spam mess. There will be grenade, mortar, artillery, strafing run and mustard gas around you every second. I'm sure lots of people will find this immersive for a WW1 FPS, but to me it make it so hard to focus on the gameplay and it just makes it frustrating. Your screen will be shaking even more than if it was in a tumble drier and you'll die so many time instantly from an explosion.It's pretty bad as your are rushing to get to an objective, but as soon as the fight starts right on the objective, forget about it, it becomes a chaotic mess of explosion. I'm sure people will point out that it is probably an accurate depiction of WW1, but I'm playing a game to have fun, not to find the experience miserable like WW1 was.It would probably be easy for the devs to balance the ability cooldown, explosive ammo count and more to make the experience more enjoyable, but for now, it's a bit too much for me.I'll probably just stick to staying in the back with a sniper and stay away from all the screenshake explosion festival.Edit 2023-05-21: I tired the game again after a few patches were released and my initial review still stand. Gunplay is really fun, but the abilities really kills it for me. It just becomes a spam of nades, spotting flares (which show your live location to the enemy team), mustard gas, artillery and mortar.

_childDocuments_.review: Isonzo quickly drew me in by how well thought out it is. All you have as infantry is a rifle and a bayonet or grenade if you are lucky. _childDocuments_.review: Its a fun game and its an improvement over Verdun. The maps are quit awesome and love seeing not so well known battles playing out on screen. There are some minor bugs here and there ive noticed but it doesnt detract from the experience. There are always a number of servers full (though I havent checked during mornings on weekdays).Edit:So after playing some more hours Ive noticed some things about the game i dont really like and could be improved.1) Heavy machine guns are ass, dont use them as they are placed in specific spots and ur gonna get recked almost every time. I really think you should be able to place them down yourself as the engineer (maybe max 1 or 2) and be able to use it while prone.2) If you really want to use the sniper I hope you have a good PC because there is only 1 available per team so getting it can be dicey with a slower PC (or get lucky that the person who got it leaves)3) The challenges at later levels are kinda annoying and time consuming, which sucks because these are what unlocks some of the other weapons4) Overall I do enjoy the objectives in the game but I kinda prefer Verduns way of doing it as the overtime mechanic can be a bit annoying with these specific objectives. Even if you retake the objective you still need to push every single enemy off of it resulting in people running in and just tossing grenades constantly. 5) The spawning system in this game is horrible, you choose a spawn point and end up on the other side of the map. Or even worse you spawn right in-front of the enemy and get instakilled which just isnt fun. The defensive team is also constantly able to back cap your spawn and put up their own so you end up getting recked from behind a lot. (Which can be both fun and annoying)6) Lastly the use of gas in this game is pointless. You almost never get kills from using it (so its essentially used to smoke an area) and there is no real rush to put your mask on as you have plenty of time. I dont know if im remembering this correctly but the gas felt more brutal in Verdun than in this game. Which really breaks immersion for me since using gas seem kinda pointless. But here as the officer you can just take your mask off and whistle and put it back on afterwords)

_childDocuments_.review: Great game.    BIGGEST MOST FRUSTRATING COMPLAINT:devs have deincentivised team-play.  Nobody places grenade boxes or ammo boxes or gives ammo to LMG players.Why?Well as a rifleman or as any other class, you have PLENTY of ammo per life.  Riflemen spaw with 5-6 round mags and 95 rounds backup.  IF they spawed with 20 or 25 rounds backup they might bring ammo.  Same with other classes demanding ammo needs.  Instead, LMG role is left to hang themselves after 10 or 15 kills unless you force a rifleman in your squad to simp for you.  Either that or get lucky with a new player who has to do rifleman quests to level up.  Lowering the ammo reserves for all classes would make ammo carriers more valuable and give them more points for being a team player.  IDK - as it stands I hate wasting tickets as offense, or sacrificing a good position because I managed to kill enough people that I ran out of ammo as assualt ammo carrier.  OR give assualt an ammo pack instead of a grenade placement.  I'd use that all day every day.  But the only teamplay incentive there is that riflemen have the ammo I want, and I have the grenades riflemen want.  Not a win win when their perk is what... weapon sway?? are you kidding me?  who can't realize how dumb that is, hip fire is godlike as it stands for rifles so unless youre shooting at >100M with less than a second to aquire target who needs it?  and if you're aquiring your target in sub one second you don't need weapon sway reduction.  ffs.     This game has been out almost a full year and its flabberghasting that this core teamplay issue hasn't been addressed.EDIT:Your character will stop shooting, even if you were holding down the trigger, in order to place and pickup the weapons bipod.This has cost me several key positions.

_childDocuments_.review: 10 minutes into my first match I'm cowering in a shell hole, I've killed an Austrian soldier and I'm crouched next to his corpse. His last moments were spent moaning in unendurable agony, the entire screen is shaking thanks to an artillery barrage. As it fades I hear the unmistakable sound of advancing soldiers, to my right is a small hedge and I shift over into it. First one then another Austrian appears and I allow them to filter past me, two shots dispatch them just as allies appear. A friendly officer stops by me as I get the bandages to heal him, in the background other men appear building defences. Our counterattack gains weight and with a roar we charge, at least 2 men go down straightaway but we gain the next trench area. Before I know what is happening gas shells begin popping with a sinister hissing, I scramble my gas mask on and the sudden arrival of gas reduces the long range battle to a dreamy close quarters haze. I get ganged up on by 4 enemies and my time is short as a result. As I lay dying I take a moment, all i can think is what a bloody brilliant game. Brilliant, brilliant, brilliant.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played these games for a very long time. I have played Verdun since it launched on Console in 2016, and have played Tannenberg for a great while too. Isonzo, however, is an entirely different beast compared to any of the previous titles, in both good and bad ways. For starters, the sights and sounds of the game are grander than any title before it. The artillery gives you these massive plumes of debris, the music (while great in both previous titles) has had a massive overhaul and is hauntingly beautiful. The sights of the artillery call ins are also a massive improvement, giving you three colussal bombers to rain hell on your foes, or literally blanket  them in gas. The sounds of the environment have also taken a massive step forward, the sounds of cicadas chirping from the undergrowth, or the sound of mountain wind rushing by your head are two standouts. Despite all of these amazing things, I have two negatives. One, the game has moved to a smaller player pool, going from 32v32 to 24v24. While this isn't as noticeable as I had thought it would be before buying, it still makes attacking feel a lot less widespread than Verdun, giving each battle a smaller, more localized front. On top of that, my biggest gripe is that on launch their is only one game-mode. While that game-mode has a lot of maps and many many different locations, it still is just one game-mode, and can get repetitive quickly. In Tannenberg, there was at least two active game-modes that I could cycle between. In summary, the game will make you feel like you are there in the Italian alps, waging a senselessly violent war, but the biggest negative of Isonzo, is the fact that there is not enough of it, and we need more ways to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Isonzo

_childDocuments_.review: First off, I genuinely enjoy this game. It's probably one of the more fun shooters out right now, and the map design is top tier. Also a huge fan of the gun-play, feels good that people die when you shoot them.That being said, I recommend staying away simply because the devs. This game is absolutely /full/ of bugs. You can't go a game without one. I didn't think that was an issue though, games have it. Recently, the devs put out a blog thing talking about new game modes, new cosmetic DLC's and jerking themselves off about small details they got accurate because of reference pictures.Genuinely, I don't understand why all man-power isn't put towards the bug fixing and improving the base game mechanics. Some of the more outstanding and common issues; - Spawning at the beginning of the game, on the enemy side of the map. (You've got like 6 seconds to kill enemies before you're executed)- Spawning in general. I can't count the amount of times I've clicked to spawn at A, then for some reason, it spawns me at B instead.       - Spawning /inside/ barbed wire, on top of fire, or right on the edge of a cliff is common as well.- Guns randomly don't shoot. Idk if it's a jamming mechanic, there's no unjamming animation, you just have to keep clicking.- Infinite bleed glitch. Idk how it happens, but sometimes you just can't stop bleeding.- Invincibility glitch. I also don't know how this happens, but it's every few games someone just can't die- Spawning on the wrong team. I haven't seen it the last few days I've played, so maybe it's fixed, but there was a while there where you'd have people team killing you, cause they saw you as enemies. You'd have people in your squad on the enemy team you couldn't shoot. It is/was an awful lobby killer.- Class full. It's happened to me on marksman and assault, where I've been playing a class since the start, then suddenly/randomly, I'm unable to respawn as the class once I die. It'll say the class is at 5/4 capacity, and there's nothing you can do about it. You have to swap.- Out of Bounds. I said earlier that I love the map design, and it's true. they look great, they play great. But there's /so/ many places in some maps that look like they should be in bounds, but are out of bounds, and vice versa. Sometimes you can be out of bounds in the middle of the map, for seemingly no reason.- Not a bug, but something incredibly super annoying is playing as mortar. The giant point pins block your view from seeing scanned enemies. Ironically, the same happens with the "request vision" triangle they can place.- Prone. In the absolutely most stupid ways possible, you're unable to prone in the most random spots, despite realistically being easily able to. - The gas. Jesus christ the gas. It does nothing, you can't kill anyone but bots with it. Even then, you have to shoot them to stop them from putting on the mask and start bandaging instead. They nerfed being able to complete an Officer challenge out of the game. There's just no way to complete it.- Voice chat. Aaaaany time someone uses voice chat, it repeats 4/5 times. Super annoying.Honestly, there's so much to be working on that you don't need to be making DLC's, just pause it. Further to that point, why are you pumping out so many cosmetic DLC's to milk money from your remaining players? Make the game free to play if you want those microtransaction bucks.

_childDocuments_.review: Isonzo, the third installment in the WW1 series, combines everything great from Verdun and Tannenberg and creates a near perfect shooter experience. Nearly every aspect of the game, from graphics to progression is improved while adding new elements to perfect the recepie. Isonzo does not reinvent the wheel nor it is a grand upgrade from previous entries, but its more of a pinnacle of the series. The game offers a gritty, authentic and frantic WW1 mountain combat, thought this is not an easy game to get into. There are only minor bugs to dim the otherwise great experience. If you are familiar with the series or games like Red Orchestra or Insurgency than this game will also be familiar, however if you are looking for the Call of Duty/Battlefield experience, than this will be a disappointing game for you.For now, Isonzo is a very solid game and the best the series have to offer, with future updates (Germany will be added this November) it will be even better. See you on the Front lines soldier! >8/10

_childDocuments_.review: This game is by far the best WW1 game, scratch that, one of the best GAMES I have ever played. Call me biased because I'm Slovenian and I only play Austria-Hungary, but dismembering Italians with an icepick while also shouting the worst insults possible really is something worth experiencing. The map balance is sometimes really focused on the attackers, but a good defending team can defeat any attacker.TLDR; I love killing Italians.
_childDocuments_.name: Isonzo

_childDocuments_.review: Isonzo is the latest entry in the WW1 series, set at the Italian Front, and would typically be described as a “realism shooter”. It looks pretty good, even if it’s not AAA graphics. The scenery is quite stunning and a nice change to what we have seen before in this game series. We have very diverse locations that definitely breathe some fresh air into the series. The verticality of some maps is fun and demands new ways to approach attack and defence. The new game mode is similar to the Territories mode of the RO/RS series with the added twist of bomb planting & defusal. The core gameplay remains true to the WW1 series, though we have new role, loadout and progression systems. The NCOs are not roles anymore and have lost their call-in abilities which were given to two officer roles. The call-in system has changed dramatically as well. Other little changes like bandaging, rifle grenades and spotting complete the new WW1 experience.The game can actually be a lot of fun. In general, the new Offensive game mode works really well on the large maps and fighting for the objectives creates tense action. You now have much more flexibility with roles and loadouts compared to the previous titles though some of the loadout choices for certain roles leave you scratching your head. Rifles with scopes are limited to one per team, SMGs/LMGs to two. A welcome change compared to Verdun. The sniper limit has been criticised by some but  it is also very much in line with the limit in HLL where you have two snipers for double the number of players.Alas, the game has many issues. Here are a few of them:- Obstructive HUD markers that either don’t disappear when your sights point at them or the dead zone for them is too small.- A mediocre server browser that constantly changes the ranking of servers and can lead to you joining the wrong server (fix: static snapshots with a refresh button).- No dedicated anti-cheat- No party system.- Lack of tutorials.- A lot of involuntary and usually meaningless shouting that can give away your position to the enemy. It is particularly annoying if you try to infiltrate enemy positions.- Bad directional sound. Also hard to hear footsteps in this game.- Some loadout choices are limited. As a consequence, some players with slower loading and/or connection times will rarely if ever have the option to play with a certain loadout. This is particularly problematic in case of the lone sniper rifle.- No proximity chat.- In case of some choke points, progress of the attacking teams depends very much on at least one officer using the right call-ins at the right places. As there is no tutorial and no minimum level requirement for the officer role we frequently see teams getting stuck because of this. - Only 6 maps upon release. The roadmap promises additional maps for free. But you pay full-price now already.- A challenge system to unlock loadout choice.- The focus on small objective areas also means that most of the explosives as well as gas are directed at those areas. This often creates almost apocalyptic scenarios where the objective seems permanently engulfed in gas with incessant explosions. This might create a tense experience but is neither realistic nor does it make for good game play when the average time of survival on the objective is measured in single-digit seconds.- Little reward or stimulation to play the objective.- Instead of one officer who coordinates the attack or defence we have two officers spamming call-ins for little more than a good place on the scoreboard.The release is overshadowed by quite a few bugs. None of them severe enough to make the game unplayable. But they are a constant source of annoyance. Two weeks after release, few have been fixed. It is also incomprehensible why the game was unwittingly released  and why this still hasn’t been fixed. Judging from years of experience with the previous games bug fixes can take a very long time. And in case of the  we must assume that this will never be addressed as the problem is known since the days of Verdun. Another consequence of the deficient netcode is that playing with a ping >100ms isn’t exactly a joy.Other noteworthy bugs (by no means a comprehensive list):- Ubiquitous prone block- Getting stuck upon spawn, but also in other situationsMost so-called “realism shooters'' aren't actually that realistic. They just provide you with an  of realism which at the end is just another means of immersion. Even by the standards of realism FPS Isonzo falls short of the mark. Just like its predecessors Isonzo walks the thin line between realism and arcade but probably fails to truly satisfy either side’s player base. The game is an Italian-Front-themed immersion generator that creates a game experience based on distorted clichés. As such it is geared towards casual players who want an immersive experience that  more realistic than BF1. Fans of historical realism FPS will succumb to the novelty factor for a while. But in the end they will no doubt go back to HLL, Post Scriptum or maybe even Beyond the Wire. Those who want primarily skill-based gameplay might or might not thrive in Isonzo. It really depends on what you expect. If you like tighter maps like in Verdun or Day of Infamy you won’t be happy. The incessant nade and arty spam will also annoy those who expect a shooter instead of a PTSD simulator. If you like to hang back or sit on the flanks picking off opposing players, consistently avoiding the objectives at all cost, then this game is definitely for you. That behaviour might not always be beneficial to your team but judging by the scores you can obtain that way the game devs beg to differ. In fact, this is one of the major drawbacks of the game. It rewards and encourages playing styles that are detrimental to the success of your team and will in the long run lead to frustrations for those who play to win matches and not to be featured in the highlight tab at the end of a match.Verdun, despite its many shortcomings, has developed a unique identity between realism and arcade that neither camp was ever completely happy with but all were content to play. Between one-shot kills and arcade-like manoeuvering it was the casual players that were driven away by the punishing difficulty of the game. And while Isonzo seems to target the casual crowd more than previous games not much has changed in this regard. So what will happen once the novelty factor wears off? And will skill-based players favour a game where the spam of explosives is even more extreme than in Verdun? And will realism aficionados enjoy a game that plays a lot like the hardcore version of BF1 or that might be mistaken by some for COD: WW1? Isonzo is in search of an audience and because it tries to please them all it in the end pleases none. Matters are made worse by bugs and deficient feature implementations. Adding insult to injury the responsiveness of the developers has dramatically decreased. I remember that Jos once took  hours to talk with the competitive player base on Discord about prevalent issues in Verdun. No more of that now. Instead we have a significantly enlarged mod team that most of the time has nothing meaningful to say when it comes to legitimate complaints of the player base. Whether that bodes well for the future of this game I leave for you to decide. So with everything taken into consideration I cannot wholeheartedly recommend the game to anyone right now. Although the game at times can be a lot of fun, it just falls short of the mark. Hardly anybody I spoke to was overly enthusiastic about the game. I do believe that some will find long-term enjoyment in this game. But not enough to warrant a general recommendation, especially at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been following the progress of the game years before it was released and I can assure you that the wait is worth it. I read all the devlogs and patiently waits for the game, once It was released I immediately bought it and I instantly enjoyed. This is the sequel that we've all been waiting for. The overall gameplay of this game is pretty much a faster paced Hell Let Loose or if you mix Hell Let Loose with Red Orchestra 2 on a World War 1 setting. A Semi-Realistic First Person Shooter. If you've tried Verdun and Tannenberg before, Isonzo doesn't actually feel like it's a sequel. It feels like another whole different game. While there are still a few Verdun and Tannenberg Vibes in the game. What I liked about the game is that the game's Movement, Weapon Animation, and User Interface is much more smooth and polished compared to the previous two games. I always loved Verdun and Tannenberg since I first tried them when epic games gives away free copies of them a few years back. Verdun and Tannenberg does have clunky Weapon Animations and Movements if you're used to triple AAA titles but for an Indie game I absolutely loved it.   This game is actually pretty populated and I'm pretty happy of that. Compared to Verdun and Tannenberg that's basically dead by this point and most of the playerbase only skyrocketed when there's usually a sale or free weekend and I do hope that Isonzo's playerbase would stick around for long. The game also have bots like the previous two games and the bots are actually quite intellegent. They aren't that stupid and robotic compared to Verdun and Tannenberg which is great. If you're looking for a game that has bots because you have a pretty bad internet or if you just doesn't like playing with people then the game would be a great choice for you to try on. The game overall isn't very well optimized. I have an AMD RX 6400 which you could call a low or a medium spec Graphics Card. I was only able to get 60 fps when playing on the Lowest settings 1080p. If you have an older computer I don't recommend buying the game since I don't think it'll be a great gaming experience.Although if you have a computer that's pretty similar / better than mine then the game would surely run. I do still think that the game looks pretty nice even on the lowest settings.  If you're looking for World War 1 first person shooter or if you're a big fan of World War 1 in general then you should definitely hop on this game for it's an awesome World War 1 game. Overall I highly recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot recommend this game for a few reasons, most minor but they simply added up to a unenjoyable experience.The first thing that stood out to me was the sound design, all of the weapons sound weak at best, and many of the rifles sound like they share the same sound effect. Attacking with your bayonet doesn't even have a war cry or grunt, your character just lightly thrusts the rifle forward without even a charge up.Secondly, the movement just feels "off" with it being very very slow. The sprint is very short in duration and doesn't seem to give much of a speed boost at all, making running to cover impossible and bayonet charges a joke. There were multiple times I would get stuck on small ankle-height stones and ledges which would stop me in the middle of a fight. Aiming your rifle takes a very long time, which I understand is to avoid making the game too reflex heavy, but instead simply makes fighting at close range clunky at best. In general the whole movement felt very clunky and made the game very difficult to push or attack any objective. I was very let down at the lack of a bayonet charge attack. I didn't play every map, but the two that I did felt very binary, flipping between impossible to assault choke points or completely open fields with very little cover. Sometimes obvious routes to flank enemy snipers were only a few feet out of bounds, which just felt cheap. One map I played on had the enemy staring down at us from atop a mountain while an invisible wall prevented us from moving forward during the beginning of the match. I won't talk more about the maps because maybe the others were better.One of the biggest let downs for me was the equipment. Everything seems to be unlocked through levels or challenges, or challenges that are unlocked by leveling. While this wouldn't be a massive deal breaker, simple things like grenades for the assault class are locked behind level five. I played two matches fairly well and only got to barely level two. The variety of equipment also seemed to be lacking, there wasn't much to get excited for, as everything seemed to be a bolt action rifle of some kind. While I do appreciate this for historical accuracy, there just wasn't any interesting weapons or variety, the most variety I think I saw was a pistol for the officer class (which still one hit killed, so it was just a straight upgrade for close range fighting). I know there must be some way to have weapon variety while maintaining historical accuracy. Gunfights felt very awkward as well, there is no bullet drop or requirement to lead your shots. This made long range fights very easy as many people would simply sit on the edges of a map waiting for you to slowly sprint into their line of sight for a easy head shot. Another thing I found awkward was the machine gun nests and cannons spread around the map. Most of the time they are placed in very awkward spots making them a death sentence to get on, because you will be instantly shot from far away. The other thing that made them very awkward was limited ammo, which as far as I could tell, couldn't be refilled. I wish the rifleman or someone could place an ammo box nearby and maybe refill them over time. EDIT: A comment below says you can refill these guns as the rifleman, maybe I needed the rifleman ammo box that I didn't have unlocked at the time, so this was on me.The final thing that I disliked about the game was a lack of turning off "toggle crouch". I've always used "hold button to crouch" mode, and there was no setting to turn off the toggling mode as far as I could see. (Maybe I missed it to be honest.)In summary my time was spent slowly moving around the map, essentially being a target for pixel peeking snipers while I had no tools to flush enemies out of the trenches (even as assault). It felt more like the devs couldn't decide if they wanted an arcade-like experience set in world war one or a more tactical realistic experience and instead just took the worst of both options: extremely slow game play without any tactical options to make that slow game play worthwhile.I never played Verdun or Tannenberg, so I don't know how this lines up with the other two games in the series.

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game that deserves to be endorsed. Forget your Battlefields, this is the gritty reality of WW1. And it is damn entertaining! Besides that it shows you the horrors of real warfare, like gas and severing limbs (if you turn gore on). It feels muuuuch more authentic than BF1, with fully voiced soldiers speaking their language. The level design in the mountains is very interesting and you can directly influence it by building/destroying bridges and barbed wires.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is really good, the best WW1 game of the three but the only complaint i have is the AI. I know you guys have put a lot of work in the game but the AI sucks especially during the missions where you have to capture a objective and destroy a field gun or something like that. But only a a small amount of troops will go to the destroy objective. The most I've ever seen go to the destroy objective was 3-7, but this problem can be solved but is a lot harder because there not as many troops. But i found the way to solve this problem is if you set the bomb and then half the AI will come and the other half will stay at the capture point.

_childDocuments_.review: Good about this game: You can be a engineer and build obstacles and guns. When your teammates get wounded you can heal them and exchange bandages. Challenges are also good idea and progression of your soldier is also good.Bad about this game: Running, running and more running! You have capture enemy position and try to attack second one, then enemy is also in your doorstep waiting for you, and you get killed! Start again! Boring! Repeat and repeat! You are just try to shoot the enemy soldier and you think he get killed then, BUM, bullet penetrate your bullet! You can't be a sniper because you don't have any good place to hide! If you don't attack your teammates running circle and don't know what to do! Bot officers don't know how to use call-in phones! Enemy knows exactly all the time where you are and then they can shoot you at blind spot or through the obstacles. You have just do a hard work building obstacles, when you are engineer and then enemy running behind you and you get killed!
