_childDocuments_.review: The maps are absolutely gorgeous. Seriously, they're beautiful.The gunplay is awful.The movement is pretty clunky too.You'll see people running in circles around each other awkwardly trying to shoot each other because the gunplay is so bad. You'll regularly clearly shoot someone and it won't register. It's one of those games that just doesn't FEEL good to play. Can't recommend when there's other attack and defend games that FEEL better to play, like the Red Orchestra/Rising Storm series. The mechanics are all there for this game, but nothing can save a game with bad gunplay and movement.
_childDocuments_.name: Isonzo

_childDocuments_.review: Right out of the box, this is the most detailed and immersive WWI experience I have ever played. By far and away, in terms of graphics and SFX quality, the best game that they've yet made. Both gunplay and gameplay mechanics were enjoyable and customization of the soldiers was more than adequate. Sadly, as seen by the big red thumbs down, I cannot recommend this game due to one rather big flaw I've found. Out of all the games Blackmills has produced, this has been the buggiest and most troublesome game they've released just yet. I have never been disconnected from a custom match as often as I did with this game. In the most recent match that I've done with a friend, a custom match mind you, we had counted 14 separate disconnect in that 1 match at Piave. Yes, I've turned off my firewall and yes, I have checked my internet connection, constant 30-50 Mbps. At this point, I am convinced that the game doesn't want me to play it. A crying shame really, as in the sparse few moments of connectivity, I had never been so happy in playing a WWI shooters game.
_childDocuments_.name: Isonzo

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't expect to like this game but I think it is highly underrated. It is slight more casual than a game like Hell Let Loose but more realistic than Battlefield. I have liked all the maps so far and the game population is strong enough where you can always find a match. Most all guns are bolt action so don't expect gameplay like Battlefield 1. Matches can get very chaotic with officers who know how to properly call in artillery, bombers, and gas.
_childDocuments_.name: Isonzo

_childDocuments_.review: A game set on a unvisited front of the Great War by most media in general, Isonzo improves on its previous titles, Tannenberg and Verdun, offering a smoother, faster paced game with improved visuals.  So far the only negative aspect would be the limited faction choices, even with the potential implementation of the German faction it will still be a smaller rooster compared to its predecessors, though it is customization feature makes up for it a bit. Overall its quite fun and well worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Isonzo

_childDocuments_.review: Isonzo is a successful game.The shooter is particularly suitable for beginners because it is much more accessible than hardcore shooters like Hell Let Lose. Isonzo is particularly impressive because of its realistic setting and graphic implementation. Added to this is the overall good and at the same time simple game mechanic, which ensure a consistently exciting gaming experience. Each player class also has its right to exist and is well balanced.What unfortunately doesn`t work so well yet is spawning. Unfortunately, it often happens that you spawn in an open area or in a completely different location than the one you selected. This doesn`t ruin the game, but it`s still annoying. There are also a few little things that don`t have a significant impact on playing.Overall, Isonzo is a very good game that I can definitely recommend and can also be used as a game for in between.
_childDocuments_.name: Isonzo

_childDocuments_.review: It's special because it's WW1, but beyond that it seems like a pretty basic capture the flag style Versus only game. The battlefields are large and it's interesting, but I'm not sure I would but it even on sale. I got o play on a free weekend.What would make it worth buying at more than full price would be a Campaign mode with some checkpointed missions (not just a list of maps to win in order). I don't need a storyline with actors, just give me a WW1 COD1 style game and I'd shell out $50 for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Isonzo

_childDocuments_.review: Those who played Verdun will feel right at home with this one. The mechanics of the game are very responsive and the graphics are impressive for coming from such a small developer. The audio also does a great job at creating atmosphere. This is 100% a hardcore shooter, but I struggle to call it a "milsim". TTK is extremely quick as one would expect on a WW1 battlefield, with 1 bullet or stray artillery shell being enough to send you back to the respawn screen, but the pace of the game and lack of communication in public lobbies leads to a lot of mis coordination. I would play with a group of friends in discord if you're looking for a more tactical approach.The game really hammers down the aesthetic and feel of the Italian front in World War 1. You are't the war hero. You are't the lone soldier that's going to save the day. You're as fragile as every man around you, and it has to be appreciated that the devs are able to capture such a bleak yet enticing portrayal of early 1900's armed conflict. That is until you fire your rifle and realize the sound audio and feel of the weapons is beyond lack luster. It's definitely not enough to ruin the experience though.If you're a history nerd and enjoy authentic time period gameplay, buy the game. It's worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Isonzo

_childDocuments_.review: The WW1 Series strives tirelessly to recreate historical battles. It's cool to see some of these battles realized in a more authentic way than Battlefield 1 did. But you know what Battlefield 1 also had? Well designed mechanics and a ridiculous budget. Isonzo's gameplay loop just isn't as well refined; I don't like the healing mechanics in this game specifically, it makes something way more complicated than it was in the earlier entries like Verdun. Give it a go while it's free, but if you want a really fun historical shooter, I recommend picking up Hell Let Loose instead.
_childDocuments_.name: Isonzo

_childDocuments_.review: Good game. Slightly disappointed. Game is fun if your looking for something to turn on and play. Simple gameplay and the game feels balanced. For some reason thought there would be a campaign. That’s my fault.          The trailers for the game are a bit misleading as well. They show super smooth what looks like gameplay of your character cutting barbed wire in the trailer, but in game looks nothing like that. A lot of animations and character models look almost cartoonish or like that ww1 game toy soldiers or whatever it’s called from years ago.           To be blunt the game gets boring pretty quick. Not 100% sure why I feel that it gets boring. I find myself looking for reasons to like it more than actually enjoying it. 7.5/10 for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Isonzo

_childDocuments_.review: The combat is fast paced, it doesn't waste players' time with long walks. In addition, it lacks the unrealistic parkour and knee-sliding found in many modern FPS games. The synergy of class mechanics are unique and not overly complicated.The vibrant color palette enhances the scenery of the maps and gives the game a great look despite the ongoing battle. The game is well optimized and offers a multitude of user settings. Overall, Isonzo is a fantastic game and the team should be proud of what they have achieved. I can only hope for continued support and a loyal player base.
_childDocuments_.name: Isonzo

_childDocuments_.review: Very well made but if your looking for an extremely tactical game like squad or hell let loose don't get this. If your looking for an unrealistic game like COD then don't get this, but if your looking for a nice refreshing mix between the two then I suggest Isonzo. It's also more cheap then cod or squad.
_childDocuments_.name: Isonzo

_childDocuments_.review: TlDr; Good Game, must buy if you like Verdun or Tannenburg, but not missing out if you pass this up.After my first day playing I wasn't going to type any review for this because I have way to many hours in Tannenburg and I knew I was going to put the same into Isonzo before typing a review of my experiences, sadly I only have 16 hours and I've experienced and seen everything there is to the game.Surface level the game is awesome. Animations and character details is a huge upgrade from previous games. The mountains and landscapes look awesome. I've heard people claim that if Isonzo was a walking simulator they would still pay $30 for it.Once you start getting into the gameplay however, things get controversial. Every person you ask will tell you something different they hate about the gameplay.Oh I hate how I get instakilled from nowhereOh I hate how the guns aren't as cool as "x" gameOh I hate how everyone can't have a sniper scopeOh I hate how I spawned with a bullet inside of meOh I hate how the mountains are CT sidedThere's a lot to love and hate about the gameplay. Yes you will die a lot, but unlike games like hell let loose, you're back in the action in less then 10-15 seconds. However my biggest complaint I've seen no on talking about is that playing Isonzo today is nothing like playing Isonzo on day 1 release day. When the game released no one had ♥♥♥♥ unlocked. We were all basically throwing our bodies at the wall because it was better then shooting the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ starting rifles.Now its 3 days after release and everyone has machine guns and sniper scopes. Now the devs were smart and put team limits on certain weapons to keep the game feeling historical, but what ends up happening is some players just having way more power then others for no reason just because they can.The game is 24v24 but in reality it's a 6v6 and the other 36 players are just support npc's. The only 6 people on your team that matter and who's skill level will determine if you win the game or not are the 2 officers calling artillery, the 2 snipers with scopes, and the 2 guys with machine guns. Everyone else's only purposes in life is to spot enemies for these 6 people, build sandbags, and be cannon fodder.To sum up this review, unless you decide to put in the hours to unlock the right weapons or to learn how to be a good officer, then you're just a walking meat shield.
_childDocuments_.name: Isonzo

_childDocuments_.review: cool game, customization is pretty cool (idc if its not historically accurate I need the drip), plus it makes more sense for pretty much everyone to have rifles rather than mostly SMGs and MGs (though I do want tanks [crappy ones are ok] Bottom line, Isonzo is an awesome game that may take time to get used to, but totally worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Isonzo

_childDocuments_.review: Pour some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ wine and pop in the Pavarotti, it's Isonzin time. The game is kino and fun.Good things:-Authentic setting-Accessible and cinematic gameplaySeriously the game isn't that hard. If you're attacking take the destruction objective first and then worry about the capture point. It's not hard guys. The biggest problem with attacking is mountaineers not spotting and officers not using smoke since they think the best thing to do is save up for the carpet bombing strike or the mustard gas. Mustard gas becomes a smoke screen just by pressing 4 guys, don't do it. Just call in smoke. Carpet bombing, while effective is a huge wait when you could just call a strafing run on spotted enemies. Also if you have a dedicated mortarman who is being supported by mountaineer flares then the game goes to lmao mode with defenders getting rekt and angry. Which leads to the bad.-No tutorials for people who don't understand there's a reason for all these classes-Some of the progression challenges are aids. Not because they're hard, but mostly because they're time consuming unless you want to cheese them in singleplayer with bots. I will never forgive the devs for the "Capture 30 points as rifleman" challenge. (Protip just play Dolomiti as Italians and cap the two points. Repeat. For some reason the devs made the AHE bots go full ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ mode with an update and now they can't defend one of these points to save their life. It's the fastest way I've found to do it.)Also for anyone saying its not realistic for you to be able to run and gun as the assault class with their unique weapons:-The Madsen is still in use today and is sized more like an assault rifle. It can be fired from the shoulder looking down the sights.-The Villar Perosa is a submachine gun that was used to clear trenches.-The MG08/15 was designed to be fired on the move. (Granted in real life its bulk made this difficult but its a videogame, pretend your avatar is a real tough guy.)

_childDocuments_.review: I like this series, and I almost like this game, but like with all the others it's hard to recommend because, well, if you want to play PvP you might as well play BF1 because there are way more people playing it at any given time - I just looked and the first 100 servers in the list were at 64 players or close to it. Isonzo, right now, has one server with 12 people on it. Sometimes it has three servers with 40ish people on them. BF1 also doesn't require you to install three separate games you need to awkwardly switch between if you want to play on a different front. And if you want to play with bots, you're not much better off, because the bots haven't gotten much better since Verdun. They're allergic to actually defending objectives, especially as an attacker, where they'll set the bomb and then stroll away so the enemy team can easily defuse it. Defenders already have a huge advantage in this game especially with the wacky spawns so it makes playing solo pretty difficult, you need at least a friend or two to make any real headway. So the bots are mostly good at prefiring you but not much else. They're obsessed with buildables, leading to hilarious situations like trying to cross a bridge and the attacker bots bleeding tickets by rebuilding them every time half the defenders roll down the hill to destroy them. You can't even mess with the advanced options anymore without disabling progression, which sucks because this game's unlock system is pretty tedious. That alone is a huge step backwards from Verdun where we were happily blasting away at 128 bots which at least sorta makes up for their lack of intelligence. Also charging people 6.99 for winter skins to have proper camouflage on the single winter map is such insane garbage I don't even know what to say.

_childDocuments_.review: Isonzo is the third game in the WW1 series made by BlackMill Games, and I feel this is the best iteration of their craft. However, it is probably not for everyone. To begin it is a little more 'hardcore' than a typical shooter. Though I use hardcore a little loosely as it is still very arcade-y. Isonzo's team dynamic is that there are 6 classes to choose from, each with their own unique tools that they bring to the table, and sometimes weapons only they can use. Your average guy is going to have some kind of bolt-action rifle and things like machine guns are either built installations or only carried by 1 person on the entire team. And typically every single gun can 1 to 2 shot. So expect to die suddenly and without warning. Which for some can be pretty immersive!This game is extremely fun for a few things. The general feel of fighting on the Alps of the Italian front are incredible. While the game is not Triple A 'forget what reality even is', it's still something that makes you go 'wow this looks really pretty' despite the warfare that is actively going on. The gunplay is responsive and feels exactly as you'd expect. Rifles one shot in the body, the bolting is responsive. The sounds and sensations of the combat, putting on a gasmask during a gas attack. It's all incredibly fun. My only real complaints are somewhat few. The melee feels rather janky at times - though that has been a problem since the very first game 'Verdun' (Which I also recommend checking out!). A second is that the gameplay loop is unsurprisingly very defender focused (Which is realistic of course) though to the point of it being a little frustrating. Such as defenders being able to get behind attackers spawns, destroy their spawn points, and build their own. Which is fine if it was the engineer class but ANYONE can build a respawn point which can become frustrating to deal with.Surprisingly there are not very many bugs that I have come across, and the few that I have dealt with were patched out on the second day of the game coming out. I know, surprising that a game can be released in 2022 with little to no bugs!Isonzo, as of currently writing this review, only has 1 game mode across 11 maps. This can be a little stale admittedly, but it can still be entertaining with friends when you are holding the last objective or fighting your hardest to take it.If you enjoyed games like Hell Let Loose, Post Scriptum, and Battlefield 1 I believe you will enjoy this game quite a bit. If you are still unsure; however, pick the game up when it is on sale! Isonzo hits a great balance between being a great hardcore shooter and also being easy enough to pick up and play casually.

_childDocuments_.review: My second review to this game since the first one wasn't in any way useful, also the devs on the menu screen asked me. Now, this is the silliest theater of the great war that you could make a game about, considering the sides you can play as are the austro-hungarians and italy, back when that nation was still a kingdom, with all sorts of weird weapons, grenades and equipment gallore that either of those two sides used.The gunplay is far beyond mere serviceable, while it does sometimes feel like you can plant your iron-sights right on an opponents chest and miss those are rare occassions, generally the devs really tried to make every weapon correct in feel and gone above and beyond that with certain weapons, the prime example being the abomnation that is the villar perosa, an italian sub-light machine gun (legit what else would you call a twin-barrel smg-lmg hybrid?) Which required both hands on the rear grip to fire. Meaning that when the bipod is not deployed, only the right barrel fires, halving your ROF. In short ALL THE WEAPONS are done to this level of love and care.Saddly this is also kinda where the love and care stops, while the maps are often done to photorealistic standarts, as in, they take actual ♥♥♥♥♥♥ photographs to make them, this...unfortunately does not actually mesh well with the game, there are machine guns that litteraly stare into hills and are useless, machine guns with no cover that thus become sniper fodder, shooting galleries that you can't exactly align yourself with so you preventing you from actually aiming at the enemy fortifications, he still can see your body through it however, defeating the point of the the entire entrenchement as well as the worst point being the barbed wire, which on some maps can only be cut through at certain chokepoint, meaning that the defenders only need to watch over about 2-4 points on the map instead of the entire trench, making offesive play on these maps just a torture until those segments are over.Spawn points are another great failure, if not the SINGLE BIGGEST. For a dev team that has now been doing this exact style of game more than once, i cannot call it anything less than their placement and mechanics are utter, pure, incompetence.  The teams always have a set of constructible froward spawnpoints in the middle of the current map segment, however their layout baffles the mind. When you play the offensive side you will always first encounter your enemies forward spawn before your own, they are just further forward, so the idea is of course that you can first destroy your enemies spawn, and then just have to move a bit further to build your own, this, also become the gameplays biggest crux. And now this will become a big tangent.You see, the defenders have unlimited respawns where as the attacks are limited in theirs.So even after the defenders have lost their forward spawn, it can be quite easy to sneak around the assaulting offensive team and REBUILD their own lost forward spawn, thus allowing the DEFENSIVE TEAM to now spawn in BEHIND the offensive team, who often don't expect this, this can very easily lead to the offensive team to loose their forward spawns, thus now trapping their own men between TWO fronts of the defensive team. Again, the defenders already have unlimited respawns, this is a world war one game, the equipment already makes defence far easier than offense, yet this oversight that i by now see in almost EVERY MATCH, an oversight that forces the offensive team to keep men that are so desperately needed at the frontline in the back to prevent this and even then, there is another mechanic that makes me think the dev-teams intern programmed it in. Squad-spawns.You know how in certain games you can spawn in on your own squad? Yeah, now imagine a very forested map, and there is just that ONE guy you CAN'T find just not doing anything, only acting as a spawnpoint for his goons. Now the algorithm that determines WHERE on any given spawnpoint you spawn in is, to my current understanding pure eldritch craft beyond my comprehention, you sometimes select the forward spawnpoint and get placed almost at the rear spawnpoint, you sometimes spawn IN FRONT of your defences, right in the enemies sightlines, ON TOP OF ALREADY PRIMED GRENADES, at the edges of gasfields without your mask on, so you have to put it on leaving you defenceless and usually gunned down. Suffice to say, that THAT one guy acting as a spawn, his friends usualy won't spawn exactly where he is, so even if you have them pinned down, if you can't find HIM he will continiously act as a nuissance.This become worse due to another oversight, the fact that you can't ping! Well, YOU usually can't ping, the ability to spot is reserved to only a few chosen people, because apparently the devteam thought that a rifleman just does not have the ability to point his finger at a ridge and scream "MACHINE GUN!" I cannot stress how infuriating it is not being able to tell your own guys that there is a guy that just ran behind them with a shovel, only to round the corner, finaly shoot him but all your allies are dead. Chat is NOT a reliable way of getting important information out quickly, a simple short range PING feature would not even take over the spotters function, as he doesn't really ping but instead give out the EXACT location of enemies and can TRACK them for his entire team!To this comes the last legative point, the sound design....ugh...i the single negative point on the guns themselves, the reason?? Well let's make a hypothetical scenario, there is a dude 10 meters away from you, he shoots you but missed. Well, the bullet impacting the ground next to you is LOUDER to you than the shot he fired, this makes it very hard to tell FROM WHERE you got shot at, similar with the difference between shots and stabs hitting someone, they are very strangely quiter than shots hitting the ground. This is kinda infuriating with stabs as you can just run in behind your enemies and just chain bajonet them one after the other.However even despite these things the game can be a ton of fun and i can give nothing but appreciation for the fact that the game offered me to hold a minute of silence on armistice day, showing that despite our tendencies to turn that conflict into a silly show of weird weapons, the devs really do care about the sacrifices that were made during the great war. If you have read this far i thank you for your patience, i know this is an overlong review but i want to give ALL informations out as best possible, especially the negative ones, as i think if you can understand the issues that i have with them, and still think this can be for you, then you will definetly have fun at the battles of Isonzo!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really good game, hiding behind some blatant design flaws and annoying aspects.For one, the feel of the game is pretty good, its like a mix of BF1 and Hell let loose without the 12 year long respawn timers or really long distances between engagements in hell let loose.Shooting feels pretty good, when you land shots and people drop its satisfying, Its a very fun game, until its not.When its not, for one, is when you spawn and die 2 seconds later to artillery or bombers you have literally no way of knowing are inbound when you're about to spawn.Artillery is too common in fact, yes yes WWI and artillery are like cheese and crackers, but realism in this case isn't fun.There's also a very annoying flinch mechanic, if someone shoots near you, you flinch and your aim is thrown way off, which if someone is on an MG guarantees death, you have literally no chance. It also screws you if you end up in a 1v2 (or more) situation.There's also an annoying issue with the reloads, if you move the wrong way on the last 0.1 second of the reload animation, when you pull the trigger the next time, you'll start the reload animation instead of shooting. It literally just cancels it entirely. There's also been times where for no reason that I can figure out, it will just not push the bolt forward and you'll get a "bolt out of position" or some such message. This has gotten me killed a bunch of times.When you're on a bad team, its an even worse experience than battlefield, because you'll just die over and over without much hope unless you hide in your spawn. (Its very hard to take on multiple people alone when you die in 1 shot) If you can find a good spot you can sometimes just obliterate people though, I've gone 20-0 before just gunning people down from a hill side while spawn trapped lol.I want to keep playing this game, because when everything is going well, even dying is fun, but man, when things start to snowball and you start looking at the respawn screen more than actually playing, because the spawn system screws you and spawns you out in the open, and then the next one under a bomb, then the next one under an artillery strike and then the next one out in the open again.I like this game, but I also hate this game. Which I sometimes would still thumbs up, but I've reached this point in under 10 hours, and that's not ideal.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game recently so this might help anyone wondering. The game is still alive so far as you can see about 2 full servers usually. The visuals, sounds, effects, all of it is amazing. You really do feel immersed in the times and the game but outside making the game feel right, playing the game is a somewhat different storyThe places where it lacks is in the ability for teams to work together. Communication is basically nonexistent outside of officers blowing their whistles. There no conversations in the team so objectives are based on what is being swarmed the hardest. It really destroys this idea of organized armies going at each other and thats the single biggest killer of the game. NO TEAMWORK. Other issues include limited maps, large numbers of bugs that completely decide matches such as invisible players who can walk around destroying spawns, whole squads dying from nothing (and i do mean nothing) ,etc.Now i havent noticed much change since the release of Verdun but then again that was way back when so i might just not remember it well. I do think it would have been better for the main game to release with expansions and additions to the game over time. This would have done a few things such as decreasing the overall download size, kept everything from verdun to tannenberg to isonzo in neat package and most important of all KEPT THE COMMUNITY LARGE AND THRIVING rather than having it split every time a new game releases.Overall its a good game just lacks in key teambuilding areas and in content, particularly maps. 8/10 still an awesome game and you can tell the devs for all their faults care very much about the portrayal of the the front in a way that ONLY respects the men who fought and died in those mountains.EDIT 1: The defenders in this game honestly dont have any advantages, i dont know how else to put it and you would have to feel for it before understanding but a majority of attacks are won, it seems that even if the defenders have the high ground, fortifications (and in one map in particular) extra open space between objectives. Yet attackers can easily all snipe you no matter how far back or hidden you are. Being a defender then mostly consists of you runinng up and down a trench until the enemy reaches you because if you pop your head out some guy a hundred metres away in the low ground will stop going full sprint and focus and bang your down. theres really no point to the defences at all this game since attackers just easily get through wire and trench to reach the objectives. it seems they did the balancing wrong. They went with the idea that attackers should have a limited amount of troops but defenders have advantages only in theory since they do nothing to stop enemy advances. This should have been flipped where defenders and attackers have unlimited troops but defenders had a clear advanatge being in fortifications, as it stands mortars easily rip through trenches and the trenches themselves are a hindrance to defenders since they are so tall you barely have a view down. I honestly dont know how else to put it other than attackers have it too easy and the defenders only really have the endless men advanatage. The defender advanatge in manpower also doesnt mean jack when the with only 10 reinforcements left get to stack right back up to full on taking an objective. It basically leads to infinite troops for both sides in most matches. It feels more like battlefield than og verdun to mee

Speaking about bugs, this game has some, but to be honest you won't encounter most of them unless you really want to, plus most of the bugs and glitches are getting patched out relatively quickly so nothing special worth of mentioning.  Overall very good game and definitely worth of spending $15 or less(in case of steam sale around $12-13).Upd: Game drastically needed new players and recent sale plus free weekend did its job. _childDocuments_.review: If you are a fan of Hell Let Loose and Battlefield then this is a style of game for you. It is essentially a fast paced Hell Let Loose that has a smaller map and no vehicles. It has more of a arcade aspect like COD rather than a true realism aspect like HLL. I have very much enjoyed this game but there are some things that I wish would change.This ends up being like a Battlefield style game when it comes to communication. You can only voice chat with your squad when I think it would make this game 10x better to have proximity voice chat incorporated. The fun in games like Hell Let Loose is that immersed feeling of you and other squads pushing an objective and having that proximity chat to spice things up. The realism however can be compared to Hell Let Loose as the time to kill is very low. A single well placed shot with a rifle is almost always a guaranteed kill. There is a slight learning curve as you cannot just rush down no mans land whenever you want. There is minimal strategy needed in order to be successful as solo strategy doesn't win games and 80% of the time your team has no strategy (it is more like COD in that aspect). Just don't be surprised when there are blatant objectives to be accomplished and your team just sits there oblivious to what is going on.I have enjoyed this game so much though that this is the first time I have reviewed a game. Enjoy!Realism - 3/5Graphics - 4/5Fun - 5/5Strategy - 3/5

_childDocuments_.review: Here are the bullet points for those that don't want to read the full breakdown.1. The new progression system is incredibly slow and downright nigh-incompatible with limiting the number of players able to play each class.2. Can't change squad types anymore, each squad is the same for each faction. IE no more marines, alpenjaeger, anzacs etc3. All gameplay variance is locked behind class-based leveling and challenges, as all classes essentially are just rifleman for their first several levels of gameplay.4. New loadout limits are beyond unreasonable, only one marksman per team can have a scope on his rifle despite 4 rifleman being available for each team. That is, unless one team has some no-lifer that leveled to 20 on marksman and completed the challenged to get the second scoped rifle loadout.If you finally have come around to play Isonzo and you previously have played Tannenberg and Verdun I would not recommend this game. The maps are nice, the gunplay is well done, and the overall feel of the game is satisfying however...The progression system ruins the experience.   Like Verdun and Tannenberg this game has limits on how many people can play as each role in the game, sans rifleman. With the added class-based level progression and challenges you are forced to play one class continuously to experience any variance in gameplay whatsoever, as all classes are almost entirely the same until you put several levels into them and then perform tedious challenges in-match to unlock equipment for said class. This is where a glaring problem arises. THERE ARE LIMITS ON WHAT CLASSES YOU CAN PLAY AND LEVEL PROGRESSION IS INSANELY SLOW.     So, if say you want to level engineer or assault or marksman you have to get into a match that is already in progress, and if you're lucky you might get to play engineer or assault, (marksman is almost never available during in-progress matches) then play through the match, most likely without gaining any progress to the class you want to play, then HOPE you load in before the others as the next match starts so you can lock in the class you wish to play and progress in.    Oh, and on top of all of that there are now limits on loadouts as well. In previous titles there were limits on how many of one class could be played based on what types of squads were available, and each squad had a selection of roles you could play as, rifleman always being available across all squad types and factions. They have completely done away with this system entirely. Now there are just quotas on how many players can play which class, and no special squads whatsoever. The loadout limit mentioned before comes into play when you are lucky enough to play marksman. There are only 2 loadouts for marksman that allow for the use of a scope, the 1st is available at level one, however ONLY ONE PLAYER PER TEAM IN EACH MATCH CAN USE THAT LOADOUT WITH THE SCOPE. So if you aren't LEVEL 20 with your marksman and have unlocked the second scoped loudout for your class you're SOL, and just get to essentially play rifleman all game, the only benefit being that you can get marksman xp for that match, and continue the insanely long grind to try to get that sweet sweet level 20 loadout.      The game plays similarly to the other titles, but with the new progression system it feels like a weird kirkland brand battlefield with a verdun bumper sticker slapped on it.

_childDocuments_.review: This review really hurts to write, as I've been a fan of both Verdun and Tannenberg before this title. When I saw that visual updates would be made combined with an often overlooked front of the war, I was thrilled to play it. Sadly there are too many issues that prevented me from getting more enjoyment out of it.First off, the map design is not fun. Instead of having two teams taking turns defending or attacking trenches or fighting in an open and dynamic battlefield, the maps here from what I've played feel significantly more like a one-sided slog. For example, in one map you're made to scale a mountain to attack an Austrian position, which looks amazing in trailers, but in gameplay is agonizing to attack. From the matches I've played so far, they did not feel very balanced. Additionally, barbed wire can only be cut to walk through in specific designated areas, further narrowing options of approach, meaning the amount of time spent running around the map just to get to an objective or position will typically be longer than the time spent actually fighting.Second, combat to me feels less sharp than it did before. I can't put my finger on it, but movement, aiming, and shooting just feels more sluggish than before. This point is a lot less well defined than the others, and it could just be that I've not played games from this developer in a bit, but to me it just doesn't seem as tight.Third, the progression system. All of the weapons beyond what you start with are gated behind assignments where you're forced to achieve specific tasks, otherwise you CANNOT unlock new weapons. Rather than unlocking a new gun or similar for a class by just leveling up as in previous titles and playing organically, I'm forced to tick off a list in a box where until it's complete, I don't get new weapons. It makes it unnecessarily grindy for no good reason and did not need to be added to this franchise.Fourth, this game crashes. A lot. On release it was practically unplayable with constant failures to launch from steam, and even on day 2 I still ran into problems where the game would just randomly crash to a black screen. Maybe this will eventually get fixed, but coupled with the other problems I've mentioned before, it doesn't paint a great picture.Fifth, day one DLC. Sure, it's only cosmetic, but it's a dreadful precedent to set in a series from a smaller developer. In a gaming ecosystem where every AAA studio these days pumps out god knows how much microtransactions at us, we don't need these trends to start seeping into smaller games.It's honestly a shame, as I really wanted this game to be good, and before this I've never even attempted to refund a game I bought off steam. However, for the reasons mentioned above, I don't see myself enjoying this title the same way I enjoyed the last two, and I would tell people who've also played their previous titles to think twice and do their research before buying.

_childDocuments_.review: I own both Verdun and Tannenberg, and I have enjoyed both when I have the time away from wife and son to play. Being a WW1 history (some might say) fanatic, I was really looking forward to Isonzo, as the Italian/Austro-Hungarian front is too often ignored by the overwhelmingly British and French perspectives (the victors write history after all, even if it's riddled with propaganda). The PROS are that: the game looks absolutely beautiful, graphics have scaled up very well, it's less "clunky" feeling overall, has a very smooth play. Maps are... different, usually quite narrow in scope and linear in design; some may like this, others may miss the epic, wide open maps of the two former games. The CONS (in my own opinion): it is BRUTAL. Verdun and Tannenberg can be considered by some to be "unforgiving" but managable/reasonable in its realism/fun ratio. Isonzo does away with any kind of reasonableness and ups the brutality tenfold, to the point that, it is more a game of ultra WW1 realism, with its chaotic battlefields and wanton death from every and any angle, at all times, and less now a game that is a fun FPS based on WW1 campaigns... if that makes sense. I've only played 1.7 hours of it thus far (as of the writing of this review) and this difference is immediately obvious and quite glaring. I don't dislike the game, but I so far dislike playing it. I thought my many hours of Verdun and Tannenberg experience would prepare me for Isonzo, and no, it doesn't at all (other than perhaps basic controls and key bindings). Some will embrace this new torture device with gusto, and others, perhaps like myself, will look upon it with mild disappointment as we submit to the lash once more (and play anyway). Though I will say, it is comforting to see the devs so proactive, that's definitely a plus and appreciated. Since I only can submit a review that either recommends a game or doesn't, I guess I wouldn't recommend it in its current iteration? But honestly, I'm pretty neutral about it. My love of WW1 history makes this game a mandatory addition to my collection, but like I said earlier, some will find Isonzo's brutality fun, others won't as much.9/23/22 Edit: After playing it a bit more, it's no less brutal and unforgiving, and playing on Defense during an Offensive on certain maps can be quite the agonizing affair, I have grudgingly accepted this game as a masochistic delight. The level of frustration I feel playing Isonzo vs Verdun or Tannenberg is much greater, but that's only because if it isn't grenades up your butt, it's copious amounts of artillery instead. Yet as my lifeless body is flung across the map in pieces, I keep coming back for more. Yes, fine, I submit. Play the game. But you've been warned! Don't be surprised if after yelling obscenities, you get a text from your wife or S.O. in the other room scolding you for being a jackass. In seriousness though, the community is nice, competitive but also mature, and after every round (even if one side got squashed), there are plenty "GG"s to go around for everyone.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: In its current condition it's not worth the $30 price tag. 15 bucks seems reasonable for this game and wait to get the cosmetic DLC on sale (if you want some cooler uniforms). I got about 50 hours out of this game before I could no longer tolerate it. You can always play it for less than 2 hours and then refund if it doesn’t meet your tastes.Gameplay. You either play as an attacker or a defender. Attackers have a limited number of tickets to achieve one or more objectives before they lose the game. When the tickets run out the game ends even if the attackers have soldiers still on the battlefield. The only hope is to enter over time by contesting the objectives. Defenders have no incentive to play conservatively as they have unlimited lives.Interface/HUD. This needs a lot of polish. Your HUD is either visible or it isn’t. There isn’t any granular control or distance or visibility of friendly or enemy markers, fixed constructible objects (see below), objectives. A lot of the markers are intrusive, but can only be turned off if you disable your entire HUD.Class unlocks. You level up classes to unlock challenges to get access to weapons, other equipment, and perks. Not all of these are particularly rewarding despite being a real PITA to complete. Some higher level challenges provide access to mediocre perks or weapons that are inferior to ones you already have unlocked. The rifleman class is an ammo and medic support role and has some very slow-firing rifles (the engineer’s rifles seem to have a higher rate of fire than the rifleman).Sluggish mechanics. From maneuvering to aiming down the sights to reloading to donning your gas mask. Everything is painfully slow. Respawning can be fast, but only if an officer continuously blows their whistle to trigger instant spawn. Typically you will trudge along, die quickly, and respawn slowly.Melee. Kind of clumsy, but it works. However - no bayonet charges. Why?Friendly fire. Non-existent. You get penalized for shooting a friendly, but it doesn’t hurt or kill them. Grenades do not harm friendlies nor does artillery or air support. Infantry can advance into an area as big fat friendly artillery shells are raining down on them without effect.Spawn zones. Sometimes you will select a forward spawn or squadmate and you will be spawned far from the point you selected.  Other times it spawns you adjacent to your selection, but in the open and under fire. Today I had the pleasure of spawning under the map and plummeting to my death (and receiving a penalty for suicide).Fixed constructible objects. These are objects that are in predetermined positions around the map and make up most of what you can build. This includes mortars, machine guns, static barbed wire, spawn points, and radios. The fixed nature of these limits their utility.Dynamic constructible objects. Largely these fall under the engineer class. They are sandbags (two types), razor wire (two types), and snipe shields. Dynamic constructible objects cannot be built too close to each or any fixed constructible object. The building system is clunky at best and these objects can’t be placed into objective areas (the areas you would actually want to fortify and put down razor wire in). You also have a limit on the number of items you can build and they cannot be replaced unless the object is removed from the map (by an friendly or enemy).Machine guns. They are death traps. Most are in terrible positions with limited fields of fire and are exposed to rifle fire from a lot of different angles. Manning and leaving a machine gun is a slow process so if you happen to come under fire while manning one your character takes his sweet time leaving the machine gun. You can’t throw yourself to the ground or fire or reload the machine gun while crouched behind cover.Barbed wire. Static barbed wire can only be breached in certain spots despite the fact that classes carry wire cutters and engineers can permanently dynamite these spots. This means that large swaths of the map are impassable and create artificial fatal funnels. God help you if you catch your uniform on a small piece of barbed wire. Then your movement slows to a crawl.All said there is a lot of potential here, but sluggish gameplay and limited mechanics really kill the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Isonzo is a really good game with some minor bugs here and there that while they may hurt the immersion a little, don't hurt an otherwise amazing and really fun experience.I would classify this as a hardcore shooter akin to games like Red Orchestra, which means it may not be a game for everyone.Because this game is set in World War 1, most of the weapons are bolt action rifles, which makes the gameplay have a relatively slow pace (there is a fair amount of weapons that are better suited for high pace gameplay, like pistols, revolvers, grenades and of course - as this is World War 1 - melee weapons) and one that does not forgive mistakes made by the player, thus encouraging teamplay and sticking together with your squad.You can really tell the devs are passionate about their game and their product, despite the game not having a particularly large population (that being said, finding a server to play on is not an issue) they keep releasing new content and in my opinion seem to care about the historical setting and their game more than pursuing profit.The character customization is rather insignificant in the base game, that being said the DLC customization is not forced on the player and seems relatively fair priced for what you get (perception may differ depending on regional pricing).The only issues I have with the game are the really janky animations, I really hope that at some point this is addressed and they get a revamp because that is probably the only issue with this game that hurts my immersion.

_childDocuments_.review: -The game is set in an innovative era yet to be properly explored in videogames -Attention to historical details,despite some inaccuracies it stays mostly true to the depicted battlefield-Most weapons being  bolt-actions rewards skill in aiming/relying on teamwork in order to survive-Really good atmosphere at certain moments-Unbalanced spawn rates, defenders advantage isn't countered by longer respawn times (like in any other FPS ever),this leads to having to flush out twice the same people from the same point within 12 seconds.-Unbalanced maps, italian defense maps are wide fronts usually filled with forests and cover but no real obstacle, austrian defense maps are either funnels or barbed wire splitting the map in half with only access points,on open roads with no covers and 2 MGs overlooking at it from behind a ridge.-Grenade spam is one of the worst i've seen in any game, RO2 or HLL everyone gets 2 grenades but is not an issue since the cap area is a whole section of the map and not a tiny square inbetween trenches or a R6S demo with a huge marker on it.-An intrusive HUD that blocks vision and broken soldier stances, prone almost always gets you stuck in place, crouched is either too low or too high for the sandbags/walls to be of any use.-Slow movement with no uniform speed acceleration,a dive mechanic or a leaning one, add it to constant either too high or too low cover and you will have a whole map with virtually nowhere to go when fighting-The game requires you to die over and over through preset killzones but doesn't properly reward progressing the game by playing for the main objectives,making most people sit at the edges of the map taking potshots at eachother.-No friendly fire from artillery strikes or grenades,again as opposed to other "realistic shooters" where such weapons get used in a tactical way and require good timing and team coordination, in here they are just irritatingly dull,so it's not rare to have enemies charge you through 150mm shells with no consequences.Last but not least a dying playerbase that suffered a vertical freefall, the only game i ever witnessed going from 4200 players to 550 (at the time of writing this review) within 2 weeks from launch, effectively having a net 86% loss,which the plethora of mods and a few dedicated users on the forum will shrug off as something not concerning for the future of the title,so save yourself the money and get it only during Christmas sales or if it goes on Xbox gamepass.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me preface this with the fact that this is my personal opinion, and Im happy the devs brought so many new people to the series and have made a massively successful game. In my opinion Isonzo feels too much like a watered down BF1 and too much of a departure from Verdun. Sure, it looks nicer but I feel they removed what I feel are some of the core aspects that made Verdun fun. They removed the squad system which would determine what weapons you got to play with in exchange for what feels like and EVEN more limiting system. Things like, only 4 marksmen being allowed in a team instead of one in almost every squad, and ONLY ONE scoped rifle per team, or only 2 officers per team instead of ONE for every squad. They swapped a squad based system that ensured people were allowed to play what role they wanted regardless of external conditions, in exchange for an extremely restrictive team based system that SEVERELY limits those who have slower internet connections or long load times due to hardware issues. Wave defense mode is also missing from the game's roster. These decisions baffle me, because to me the squad system of the Verdun feels like what made it special compared to BF1. I don't want them to rework the entire game as there are people who probably really like the new system. But for those such as myself who don't care for it, I hope these issues are remedied with a new game mode, expanded options for custom games, or some other solution. If you are hoping for Verdun with updated graphics, this is not the game for you in its current state.

_childDocuments_.review: Could be a great game but left frustrated by many aspects:1) After levelling up each class and unlocking weapons or equipment you are required to perform "Challenges" to use the unlocks. These detract from the core gameplay loop and playing the objectives. They are not fun or rewarding in anyway to complete.2) The spawn system often places you in the sights of the enemy so you die instantly or spawn randomly behind the enemy line. There's also no way to skip looking at your dead body which after the 3rd time of dying on spawn gets irritating. The spawn time itself is also completely random some times you spawn instantly other times 20sec.3) Server's die off quickly leaving you playing against brain dead bots.4) Going prone and being blocked by terrain or map props frustrates.5) The maps are very linear with few avenues to flank, often games come down to officers "special" abilities clearing out enemy positions/objectives rather than any squad based teamwork.6) The sniper class is rather OP and there are too many snipers per map for a historically accurate game but probably draws in the $$$. 7) Reloading is frustrating when you accidentally interrupt the animation and have to restart it from scratch.8) The game modes where ones side is limited to defending get dull fast.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought Isonzo at release two days ago and already played 14 hours no stop between two evenings/nights. I'm playing together with other 4/5 friends and I'm having a blast so far. This is not Battlefield or Call of Duty, the pace is slower and somewhat the gameplay more realistic. The Offensive game mode is really good but attackers and defenders need to be organized, this is not the rush and shoot type of FPS, every action needs to be planned ahead and executed at a slower pace, together with your team in order to succeed. Keep that in mind and approach the game knowing that. If not, you'll be disappointed.The maps are not many (new ones are coming via free dlc) but all of them are REALLY big and well built and gorgeous from an artistic point of view. Each battle is long and hard fought, one game can last even 45-60 minutes and I already played some epic matches. All Isonzo locations are 1,5 hours from where I live and I visited all these places in real life and I must say...the developers did their research, not only from an historical point of view!! Graphics are good but I think the game still needs a little bit of optimization. Isonzo is not as "fluid" in player movement as other FPS games, it could feel clunky at first but I think this was a conscious decision by the developers.  I don't mind that, I think it is only a matter of time and practice for the normal fps player to adjust his sensitivity and way to play. I also really like the unlocks progression and I find the different classes interesting and each one with its role in battle. What else to say.....apart from the number of maps, a prone position that often blocks you from moving freely between obstacles and a bit of fps drops here and there in forest areas of a couple of maps, I must say I'm really satisfied with this game. I don't have many complaints, I'm still discovering Isonzo and some of its peculiarities. I hope more players will join the battle in the next few days and weeks, because this game deserves more love and the roadmap for future updates looks really interesting: 7 new maps, winter campaigns and a new faction, all for free! Not bad considering the crap we are asked to pay in these sad days of modern gaming! See you on the Italian front, I'll still be there for a lot of time indeed!

_childDocuments_.review: Out of the gate, this is a stunningly realistic war game. ts very satisfying to land kills, and theres ton of different ways to play the game itself through the 6 different classes. Rifleman (i always forget the name): Is generally the class that rushes into the frontlines and gets killed before they can see the target, however, you can also use ammo crates and strategically place them to get a boatload of passive xp gain, this is also the only class that can reload mortars,lmg's and cannons. Also you get a portable mininuke, to use rush an enemy, look down, jump and shoot :D.Officer: Generally fights very little, has an EXTREMELY high kdr because they are call-in focused, you get some massive call ins that can down 3-10 enemies from anywhere in the map. However, a really good officer constantly draws battle plans on the map to lead the army to victory.Engineer: Gets a super fast mortar reload time, along with super fast lmg reload time, is great for high kdr and XP, as you can build around 30 structures at once, and then continue to build your teams mortars, wires, and MG's, (i personally just fill one trench with 10 barbed wires and call it a day). As for the mortars, they are more precise versions of officer call ins, that hit less ground, but can still knock a solid 1-5 players if you are really focusing on the map. The MG's are super accurate, and can 1 shot, but you can't move while using them. Assault: Assault is actually pretty normal, there major strength is that they get multiple grenades, can get passive xp gain from placing grenade crates, and a lmg that is a really op "spray and pray" or camping weaponMountaineer:  Gives an unholy amount of passive xp gain from flare guns which spot about 10-25 enemies and give +5 per spot (+10 for kill on spotted enemy), an op melee, extremely powerful speed buffs, extremely powerful sniper buffs, and a periscope that can look overwalls and infinitely spot enemies once placed. This is a class that gets tons of passive XP, but generally will have a low kdr, and if you play aggressively, will be pretty nerve-wracking to play.Finally you have marksman, only 2 people get scope, and one of them HAS to be level 20. If you don't get scope, honestly, just use your pistol, the pistol is much better than your normal weapon accept for super long ranged combat, marksman while boasting a fairly high kdr, is kinda boring to play without the scope, as people who really want to snipe can use mountaineer instead.Players unlock weapons through levelups and missions, generally this is fairly good, accept when the missions are arbitrary, here are the missions i think could be improvedRifleman: help capture 30 points, This missions is stupid because even though it says "help" you actually need to be on the point the moment it gets captured as opposed to just being part of the group that helped capture it, which means you need to completely drop agression and just focus on hiding/camping.Officer: 50 gas kills, players RARELY die to gas, cus u can just put on a gas mask, so the only way to do this is with bots.Multiple classes: Grenade kills, post death kills dont count, which means the player needs to hide behind a wall to avoid getting shot by ANYONE while cooking/throwing the grenade, this goes against many of grenades best uses, in which it can be used to cover your flanks or be thrown onto important areas with many enemies at the players expense.Also despite the fact 2 classes have mortar quests, rifleman is never given a mortar reload mission, so only a small fraction of riflemen even know they can reload mortars........The only other major thing is that I honestly think bugle should get XP whenever someone gets a kill while buffed, as its one of the 3 strongest items in the game, (bugle boosts everyones speed).Other than those really specific issues, this is a really awesome game, and i highly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Based on the first few hours, Isonzo feels like a step back from Verdun and Tannenberg in most meaningful ways. The main issue I have is the game mode here doesn't work as well as in the previous games from M2H. Verdun had both teams taking turns attacking/defending, which meant generally over the course of a match the stronger team would be attacking (the tougher job) and the weaker team defending. Tannenberg was a more conquest style game mode, but it had the same principle of both teams attacking/defending in each game, and also gave you a bit more breathing room with bigger maps that allowed the rifles to shine. Izonso always has one team attacking/the other defending, and really attacking is just not much fun. The maps are narrow enough to have a lot of chokepoints that just turn into meatgrinders. I haven't encountered any of the kind of communication that allowed this kind of game mode to work in Tripwire's WW2/Vietnam shooters. Instead, the game rewards sitting back and camping as the attackers. Trying to push up just results in endless death to grenades, artillery, sub-machine guns, pistols and gas. There are a few cool moments, but mostly its just death and frustration. Small sample size, but most game's i've played, the defenders have won pretty easily. Often attackers will leave or switch teams because its kinda miserable. There have been some improvements to the visuals, and the maps are nicely detailed with interesting verticality. Audio needs work, and i've encountered some bugs like not being able to ADS. Overall, this has been a disappointment after Tannenberg which I quite enjoyed. I might play a bit more, but honestly I'll probably return to Hell Let Loose for my historical FPS fix.

_childDocuments_.review: My review on this game is very mixed, wish steam had an option for a review that is not positive nor negative. I've played both verdun and tannenberg and loved them both. I waited for this game since spring of last year. When this game finally came out I bought and played it. The first 2 hours were very fun in this game, but thats where it all started to go downhill. I see that the developers had inspiration from battlefield, but they copied it too much. The grind for anything new became as tedious and long as battlefield. And this game became less of teamwork and more of a sweatfest where everyone was grinding for a new gun. In the previous 2 games there was literally no grind, you can unlock everything withing your first couple of hours. I wish they implemented the same system for unlocking here.In the previous 2 games I enjoyed playing singleplayer for its immersion and a bit more relaxed gameplay. When I booted up singleplayer on this game it was not as fun. The bots looked a little less janky, but now their difficulty skyrocketed, on all difficulties the bots literally had aimbot and could 1 tap you in less then 1 second after you expose a pixel of your character. In both multiplayer and singleplayer the attacking team stand no chance and is basically condemned to loose after they capture 1-2 sectors. The defending team sometimes spawns right inside the objective(s), while the attackers spawn kilometres away, making any attempt at attack stop as soon the new wave spawns and grinds the attackers to the ground. The only way to win as offence if the defenders are EXTREMELY bad.The excruciating grind and the bad gameplay are the 2 major flaws in the state of the game as of this moment. _childDocuments_.review: This game takes a few nice steps forward in the Verdun series but too many steps back to have fun. To start, the classes and new weapons are always a plus. The unlocking is a bit weird at times with some being really easy like a mountaineer tagging enemies, while others are a lot harder like the marksman needing to get 2 kills in one breath 10 times. Some classes are just strictly better than other or should have been a off branch of others like combining marksman and mountaineer or having engineer be an off shoot of rifleman as the function the same without their special which is basically only for setup. The real issues though isn't the classes but rather the balancing of maps and AI. The main mode being the invasion being a mix of front line and maneuver that Tannenburg and Verdun had is great except for how it was implemented. The maps aren't really open and forces you down paths as attackers through trenches or certain cuts in  wire fences. This wouldn't be so bad if the machine guns weren't trained on theses areas.  To make things worse you can't flank without going out of bounds to be executed for doing so and straying from any path puts you in line of sight to be shot from all angles. In Tannenburg flanking was highly encouraged to break enemy lines, now it's either meat grinder or guaranteed death. This again wouldn't be so bad if there was balance in spawning. In the new mode offensive the attackers can unlock forward spawns that can be built and destroyed throughout play. Unfortunately many times rather than spawning at the spawn point it spawns you half way back between your safe zone and the actual spawn point allowing it to be easily overrun or you having to use your whole sprint stamina just to reach said spawn point. This basically negates the usefulness of the forward spawn since I still had to use all my stamina to get to the starting point to continue attacking.  To go with this many times when you spawn and it doesn't do that it puts you right next to barbed wire rather than the predesignated paths or in some cases I've spawned in the barbed wire and had to slowly die because of the spawn. The spawning continues getting worse as rather than bringing you the map to respawn with the next wave right away as you could in Tanneburg, you usually have to wait 10 seconds to see your death which causes you to miss the next respawn wave many times. It's constantly stacking unfun and unbalanced things against the attackers at all times and even gets worse as defenders often spawn right on objectives being attacked or 2 seconds away. This brings a whole other issue with balance.The spawning for defenders is a bit unfair as they have infinite lives and aren't punished for ding as much as attackers who lives drain as the game goes on. No with the aforementioned long spawn times this would seem easy to overcome but it's not as they usually spawn seconds away from objectives compared to attackers minute sprint. When attackers get into an objective given it's a fair fight maybe 3 people are left. Then 5 seconds later 10 defender are already there to wipe and reset with more than enough time to do so. This obviously isn't always the case but it's infuriating as a balanced game in skill level will easily go to defenders just due to spawns alone. Capturing objectives is another issue on its own.There are two types of objectives destroy which plants a bomb to be defended like Counter Strike, and control points which is pretty self explanatory of whoever has more people on it captures it. Neither of these are bad ideas but the capture rate is the real issue. To capture a control point it can take upward of 5 minutes to neutralize it then capture it which is without any enemies contesting it. This is a major issue as attackers waste tons of lives just having to wait and hope the cap before another 10 defenders wipe them and reset the timer. It's so bad that on 1 map in particular there is a singe objective to capture the top of the mountain. Even with forward spawns it take attackers almost 2 minutes to reach the control point meanwhile defenders spawn in or or literally 1 second away. I've played both attack and defense on this map and it's literally so broken with how easy the defender can throw the entire attacking team off the point while losing 3 times as many people doing so.  Overall the spawns need a major overhaul and change to be fun to play.Now the other issue the AI. As anyone who plays the game knows the player base is pretty small like less than 200 so it's not uncommon at all to see bots in the games. Honestly at times I prefer fighting them in order to learn new paths and weapons. The issue here is they break a lot of rules. Many instantly spawn after dying right back on the point to where I see I killed on in the killfeed only to die to him 1 second later while I'm capturing the control point. There's the very obvious aimbot that they have as I'll have one deadeye shoot me 100 meters out while they're sprinting towards me rifle at the hip only a flash from the hip. Other times it's so apparent where I've had one wound me with a pistol shoot and he hadn't even finished turning around to shoot so his gun was literally firing 180 degrees behind him. Bots cheating in games is a given but man it just enforces the issues of balance. Not to mention they don't coordinate at all and players can't control them or have them in their squad. This is my other major issue with the AI is that I can't play with them and play an officer to get benefits from the class. Bots can't be added to squads which sucks as they were automatically assigned to fill in in the other previous games.  This means officers can't do anything without human players. On top of that in the previous games you could spawn off of squad members not in combat, with bots not being allowed in squads you don't get that luxury but they do. Just adding issue to the spawning balance. Overall the game does take some nice steps in the right direction. It made a great new game mode, Better classes and weapons and unique gameplay to include mortars and construction of barricades. It makes all classes useful. But it took too many steps back by bringing back the Verdun spawnrates being too hard for attackers to actually capture and too long to capture points any ways (I mean why does a stick of TNT take 2 minutes for the fuse to blow.)  I think if they change the spawns to be more balanced by sending defenders further from objectives, lowering capture time needed or increasing capture rate much more when there's no enemies on the point, some AI adjustments and letting them be in players squads so they can coordinate with them it'd put this game above Tannenburg. If you want a good experience though I would go with Tannenburg it's not as detailed but at least you can spawn in an fight more on even ground than whatever was done here.

_childDocuments_.review: The progression is a bit slow and grind-y to unlock everything, and the rifle grenades can be a bit OP. But I like the gameplay overall. I would say that this is not for casual FPS players. This game is very unforgiving, which I could see frustrating people that come from any of your typical AAA FPS games. You've got to be in it more for the visuals and the history, or you just have to like games where getting shot in your pinky finger from 200m away is an instant death. Oh and hallelujah, no lootboxes or microtransactions. Although there is the paid cosmetic DLCs, you're really getting them for yourself to look at. Trust me, no one will be able to tell what you're wearing in-game - it's too fast-pace. As far as negatives go the game has a few bugs in its current build, but nothing game-breaking I have seen. Just maybe a bit of a killjoy when there is a "ghost" player that can still interact with objectives and buildings.

_childDocuments_.review: They don't know i'm here... Steady... Steady.... GAHHHHHHHH!He screamed, clearing out an entire trench with an ice pick. Magnifique.Verdun was one of my favourite games. I met friends who I still play games with very regularly to this day and it was because of Verdun. Tannenberg tried new things and in my opinion completely lost the thrill of the original. Bots walking casually toward you is... fun for a short time. But then it starts to just feel like any old horde game. Where it failed, Isonzo is a beautiful and triumphant return to Verdun style fun. The game mode now often requires you to hold 2 parts of a trench, 1 part often in a domination style capture point and another point is a point where you will need to plant a bomb that can be defused. Engineering works very nicely in this game which is very refreshing, even if your engineers foil your retreat by building barbed wire, trapping you to the enemy. 2 commanders work together to coordinate the rabble whilst also calling in support. One thing i think is excellent in this compared to verdun is the Smoke. Sure gas is still great particularlyon a point but if they have a perfect sniping advantage on you, wait it out and put down a huge blanket of smoke towards the objective. It really is effective and works a charm.The gunplay is outstanding but that's nothing new.The only things I'd consider would be, i did like in the event of a successful hold you can counter attack like in verdun but accept the new gamemode too, it is very fun. Maybe limit grenades just a little bit, explosions are already plentiful with mortars and 2 commanders calling in support strikes. Its fine in most areas but in some narrow parts of maps it feels like 10 nades land every 10 seconds which seems a bit much, And i'd like to see the engineer building fleshed out even further. All in all, if you like shooters, enjoy tactics and helping your team ( honestly, people who just spot enemies are the MVP in the game for me) this is well worth a try as it's reinvigorated my drive to play shooters. 10/10 would stab, gas and fieldcannon again

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked Tannenburg and Verdun. You'll enjoy this. Main differences are the game modes and classes and their limitations. Otherwise its still the same kind of game.Game mode for this iteration of the WW1 series is basically BF's breakthrough mode. One team defends points/objectives and the other team pushes (hopefully before their lives expire). There is an 'Overtime' component that seems janky/buggy. The attackers will be capturing during OT or the one objective (you have to blow up) will be on its countdown timer and the defence will just win.There's 5 classes. Officer - mostly support. Has call ins (recon, artillery, smoke, poisonous gas etc) and commands the team with their whistle.Rifleman - generic unit that drops ammo.Engineer - builds sandbags, fences, Heavy Machine guns etc.Assault - uses grenades and a flask to reduce suppressive fire.Sniper - self explanatory really. But only one of the guns has a scope and only one of the 4 snipers per team can use the scoped rifle.Progression for guns/gadgets isn't just a simple level up system. You level up to get to the point where you can then work on the objectives to unlock said gun. For example, to get the Rifle for the Officer class, you need to:Kill 100 enemies with Artillery Call-ins.Kill 100 enemies with Aviation/Aviator Call-ins.Only then will I get the rifle. Which can be tedious but you can scum these by just killing bots.Besides that? Its literally Tannenburg and Verdun. Would have been nice if they could merge the clients together so you can just launch one client and play any of the games you want.
_childDocuments_.name: Isonzo

_childDocuments_.review: If you really like Verdun or Tannenberg, you'll like this game a lot. It's essentially a modernized version of both into one game, with cleaner UI, better visuals and some adaptation and additions to gameplay.For me, it's just more of the same with some added polish. It's still quite stiff in the gun play, the maps are very narrow based and shoehorn into bottlenecks which just creates a repetitive gameplay experience. It doesn't have much dynamicism to the gameplay, though does have defensive deployables etc now to spice things up a bit.Progression isn't as quick as Tannenberg, so there is some longevity in that. The best things I can point out with the game is it's environmental design is a huge step up from previous titles, the environments are gorgeous. The other element is can appreciate is the historical authenticity.On top of this, stability seemed fine, 160+ FPS maxed out at 1440p resolution...then the crashes happened. In my play time I crashed 3 times.This game just isn't for me, it doesn't feel like it fits into an arcade or realism category, not even in-between the two..it's like it's trying to be too many things at once while not mastering any, while being quite a repetitive experience. I felt like I got to experience what the game had to offer in just a small amount of time.
_childDocuments_.name: Isonzo

_childDocuments_.review: Nice graphics, good gameplay, the hit detection is on point.Some of the best multiplayer maps (the love of details, you can feel the passion they put in) I ever experienced in my past years as a gamer.I tried the free to play weekend and bought the game yesterday - imo the only thing to complain is the lack of communication and/or proper squad playing like HLL used to (maybe there are admins out there who force you to, not sure yet). But that´s not BlackMills´ fault.If you are frustrated because you get fragged over and over re-think about your gaming style. This isn´t CoD; BF or CS2Think about the setting:WW1 Trench war.Take your time, calm, be good organized, get a good squad, play tactical if needed and faster only if you have to.I would say Isonzo is easy to play but hard to master.

_childDocuments_.review: Out of the three games released by Blackmill, this one is my favorite followed by Verdun. I had a great time with the game and as with every multiplayer game, it is always more fun with friends. A large chunk of people still play this game, and I live in the United States so there is always one server that is fully populated. When it gets late at night, I switch over to the EU server which also has one server that is full of players. The game is surprisingly stable for me even when the scoreboard tells me my ping is high because of the server change. All the weapons that I've used so far feel great besides the Steyr-Hahn 1912. I will admit it is a bit overpowered considering it can one-shot at close range if you hit a player on the upper torso area plus it has perfect accuracy even at long range. The damage drop-off is really the only thing that keeps it from being super OP. Still a fun gun though! The challenges to unlock the weapons as you level are honestly not too bad so far. I've so far only played rifleman and assault with me occasionally switching to the sniper class or the officer class if the need arises. The great thing about completing these challenges is that you can get these done even when you are playing in an offline server with bots! This is great as you can use this to complete the more annoying challenges so it is very nice that the devs allow for this. Everyone I've played with so far is pretty chill, and I have not encountered any cheaters yet. The only bad thing I can think of from my time playing besides playing with people who do not know how to do their job as an officer or people who spam the sniper class to be a sniper who then ends up doing absolutely the entire match is more content! I can't wait to see what Blackmill has coming for this game! I am just hoping it won't be like Tannenberg where it just died. The cosmetic DLCs for Isonzo are great. A lot of the outfits and accessories look really nice. I recommend picking up this game on a sale. It's a fun time but I feel like the price is a bit much considering you can get through the current content that Isonzo has pretty quickly.

_childDocuments_.review: I originally played this game on free weekend and bought it shortly after when it went on a big sale. I have loved this game in only the short time I've played it and the game is absolutely gorgeous and very immersive. The only real issues I have are with the DLC's but they are purely cosmetic which I appreciate and this game has no in game currency or battle pass to speak of, just the 90% of cosmetics being behind separate paywalls.
