_childDocuments_.review: I'm not much of a pvp fps player, but I love Isonzo. At the time of my review, I have played it for 275 hours.What I like:+ The setting (WW1 alpine front)+ Beautiful landscapes to die in+ Painfully immersive: You will die. A lot. Silently drop dead from a bullet across the map, get blown to pieces by artillery, pray you'll survive the bombing run when you see and hear the planes approaching, get your skull smashed in by a pickaxe, while your comrades are cursing the enemy in italian or austrian.+ Moustaches, moustaches, moustaches (character customization)+ Sometimes you get nerve wrecking showdowns in overtime (so much fun, even if you end up losing in the end)+ The different classes allow really diverse playstyles (my personal favourites are countersniping as mountaineer or suicidal sabotage trolling behind enemy lines as engineer)+ In the two previous games I got completely overwhelmed by squad and class selection - in Isonzo it is soooo much more intuitive+ Passionate developers+ paid DLC contain only cosmetics - everyone gets new weapons and new maps for free, so there's no "pay to win"What I don't like so much:- unnecessary grind for perk and weapon unlocks at the beginning (these challenges are easy enough to do in offline games against bots though - also, the starting perks and guns are perfectly viable, so they're not the reason you're fodder... ;) )- offline play against bots could be a lot better (but I still do a lot of it)

_childDocuments_.review: Positives-------------------------------------------------------------+ Visual improvement over Verdun and Tannenberg+ Combat brutality that adds tension to battles retained+ Guns feel great to shoot+ Overall Kinesthetics feel mostly solid+ Good progression system+ New Game mode (Offensive) is a nice change of pace to previous primary game mode styles from past titles.+ Destructibility, while limited, is fun to experience. + Abilities to build spawn points, health teammates, provide ammo to teammates, etc. are nice welcome additions that add to the variety. + Bots can be fairly accurate and more difficult to deal with at times.+ Being able to have bots in matches, in case no players are available, continues to be a godsend in an industry that has by now largely ignored the problem of low player count long term game sustainability. + Aesthetic customization is a nice bonus. + Maps well designed, and fairly scaled to give players breathing room to find numerous routes to objectives.Negatives---------------------------------------------------------------------------- Would have been nice if destructibility was more fleshed out.- Spawn points, both on objectives and teammates, can feel inconsistent and frustrating. - Some issues with getting stuck in terrain at times.- A few odd visual glitches, such as the horizon glitching out from time to time.- Some performance issues, especially when loading into some matches for the first time (momentary freezing). - Could have sworn there were some hit detection issues (ex. shot one enemy 10 feet away 4 times, no hit indication). - Wish there was more variety of game modes, similar to Verdun and Tannenberg. - Sometimes destroying or building objects hit detection's for activation feel too specific. Requiring you to be on roughly the exact right spot to initiate destruction or construction. - Wish standard battles had 64 players, similar to Verdun and Tannenberg, though that's a minor nitpick. - Frustrating to unlock weapon types, only to have the slot for the specific weapon type taken up, forcing players to use weapons for classes they otherwise don't want to use currently. - Minor nitpick, but too many cosmetic DLC's that should be unlockables in-game, in my opinion. Overall, still recommended, as much like Verdun and Tannenberg, there's no other FPS, especially WW1 FPS currently, that has this exact type of brutal but satisfying gameplay loop.

_childDocuments_.review: Misses the markI'm a longtime player of this series starting all the way with Verdun. Verdun was the chefs kiss, basically a sandbox where you could try to take an enemy position a thousand different ways. That's why the same maps were always fun, even when they didn't update those maps for years. All of the classes and different squad types had their niches but always had an impact on the game. Tannenberg had so much potential, but lack of a solid player base really doomed that one even though I really liked it for adding in the Russians and adding some really cool game play features. Then we get to Isonzo.There are several things I love about Isonzo, chief among them being the graphics. Fantastic upgrade compared to Verdun and Tannenberg. The environment and character models are great. The new classes, on paper, are really cool too. Also the character customization is fun and adds some uniqueness to the models. Furthermore this game adds such a unique setting that I don't think any other game has touched upon save BF1 (more on that later). That's about it though. This product isn't entertaining; quite the opposite, it's downright frustrating. And you can see that most players feel that way because the player count declines rapidly by the month. There are several issues I noticed in the game play. First, the bugs are just awful. Every 25 or so spawn ins, you'll just randomly fall through the floor and die. And it'll happen for a little before it corrects itself. There are several more. Hit boxes are totally out of wack, prone movement in this game is broken (which is a pretty important aspect in a realistic shooter) and I can barely hear other players because their mics cut out halfway through their message.Bugs are irritating in the game, but it's the game play decisions that really disappointed me. This game is desperately trying to model itself after Battlefield 1. From the movement of the weapons in the character's hands, the general interface, and the aesthetic of the game really make this seem like a low-budget version of it. It's really sad that the devs went down this route, because it just makes the product they worked hard on look cheap in comparison to the AAA titles. Another game play issue is the map design and spawns. They are god awful. Maps are centered around alley ways which just turn into kill zones and turns the games into slog fests. The maps designs limit creativeness and encourage teams to just slam fist there way into the objective through these kill zones. There is also little spawn protection. Its pretty common for a team to start slipping and then snowball into an utter rout because the other team has positioned themselves before the losing team's spawn, leading to cheap mass spawn kills and an easy defeat. Off map abilities in this game are out of control, to the point where on some maps its just a constant barrage of artillery, aircraft strafing runs, and gas. Combine this with the aforementioned spawn killings and you get the picture. The last of my grievances are the classes. On paper they are really cool, and I'm glad they finally decided to add engineers to build obstacles and supply stuff. But a lot of the classes feel useless. Engineers could be such a cool class, able to build traps and useful obstacles, but the game limits them to building certain things only in certain areas, to the point where most of the time the engineers are just using their rifles. Their is simply no incentive to play the rifleman class. The assault and mountaineer class are the best, along with the officer if you know what you're doing. The rest are just meh at best, and highly situational to the point where there's no real point in playing as them. Even for the useful classes like the assault, they have water bottles. Seriously? It increases stamina for a little. Of all the things they could have added, they choose stuff like that. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ lame. All of these factors on their own or even in pairs could be forgivable. The dev team isn't some crazy AAA studio that gets millions in funds. Nevertheless, these issues make me wonder if they properly tested their product. It's a damn shame.

_childDocuments_.review: This game hasn't been out for long, but i just can't keep my fingers off of it.All of the new gameplay mechanics they introduced in this game fit this game series perfectly.For all those who played Verdun and Tannenberg here's a quick list of em':- Fortification and MG/periscope building- ADS with light machine guns even if not prone with added recoil and sway (which makes the MG class more about skill and recoil management than about finding a blace to deploy that DANG BIPOD... oh yea and bipods will now deploy automatically if there is a surface beneath the gun model)- pistols and revolvers seem to do more damage but also have more realistic recoil and sway- officers now have flare guns to mark targets for artillery strikes, all kinds of different gases and smoke and plane/bombing runs which they can order in at dedicated einforcement/radio tables.- better leveling system. It now takes loner to level and you have to do certain challenes to unlock weapons/utility.- Spotters. there's a new class of Spotters, that can tag enemies with binoculars/periscopes which will then have an icon above their head for a short time and be easy to see and shoot.and much more little things too...I actually can't wait for this game to get updates, like the German faction and dedicated maps for them in the future. I hope this game doesn't die like Tannenberg did.To anyone who has played Verdun or Tannenberg, i can recommend this game if you're lookin for something new that still has the vibe and feel of Verdun.There is some bugs like spawning inside an object and being stuck in it and having to redeploy. however i'm sure those will et fixed soon enough.

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game and realistic, especially in terms of what equipment and weapons are available.  Weapons feel pretty good and the kills are satisfying.  Progression is fun and keeps me engaged, and the graphics aren't bad at all, either.  Sound is also pretty good for what it is.  There's a good bit of variety, too, as there are different nations to play as, and quite a few different maps. _childDocuments_.review: I want to recommend this game and see the improvements made from verdun and while isonzo is fun, its got quite a few issues. Full of bugs, glitches, and spawns that get you instantly killed. I like the map design overall and the inspiration they took from ww1 battlefields but objectives should be usable for defenders be it an ammo dump, command center, or cannon / heavy mortar. most of the time attacking or defending objectives has no real gameplay value besides that its the letter objective that you need to hold to win, not that its your teams ammo dump or some sort of equipment that helps you win. I like the bridges they put in the game cuz it adds map interaction to get to site and in certain cases blowing a bridge can change the nature of games by forcing attackers to cross rivers. I feel like making bomb sites usable would add more of this map interaction where objectives have value like we can no longer resupply or call things in there anymore if they blow it up.  Gunplay feels good but a ducking function on hmgs like in ro2 would have been a nice addition and gun sounds are a bit to poppy, Hell let loose i think is the best example of good sound design. Progression kinda annoying, wish they made it to where you progress towards cosmetics and only certain weapons like lmgs would be level based. things like icepick, daggers, grenade and ammo crates should be free to use by newcomers. The building aspects are decent but wish that they would make buildable zones for hmgs and cannons so static weapons could be setup alot more random and engies could build sites up more freely. add a vote kick system so we can remove cheaters and super sweaty players from games, add a territories/ campaign mode, add party system, and add a queue or auto join for servers that are full. Overall 7.5/10 pick it up for 5-10 bucks cause its authentic, intense, and fun but still needs alot of work to become the holy grail. P.S. add flamethrowers and more cannon spots

_childDocuments_.review: A WW1 simulator that keeps on giving! This game cures my nostalgia for the first COD game and the United Offensive expansion pack in a way.  The AI bots in single player mode are pretty good so if the online community ever slows down to a trickle it has good shelf life. I would liken the bots difficulty to the very hard setting on CS:GO. The class system is great because it allows me to be an engineer and construct defenses, mortars, and MG nests, which I really enjoy! I feel that this game could do with a tutorial for sure because the mechanics of each character class took me a while to get the hang of though it is beautiful that I can simply change class every time that I die in-game. You level up each class by performing tasks and getting kills like an RPG in this game. I do not own the previous two versions but it should be made known that you can quickly switch through all three games in the main menu which I found really cool. There is no ridiculous 3rd party game launcher like other games and for that I give them a huge round of applause!As far as Linux performance goes...The game does not run great. I run an i7 6700k/GTX970/16gb ram and I run it on low settings with a few extra sliders turned up. I feel like the game should be able to run on medium at least but it chugs un-playably hard. The native port fails at the map screen loading but proton performs better without crashing so it should be possible to run it on the steam deck. I feel like if the developers optimized linux gameplay (get a great on the deck rating) and finely tuned the AI and single player modes (gave us difficulty sliders and bot number control so I can stack my opponent unmercifully) that this game would have the ultimate shelf life and keep selling copies well into the foreseeable future.

_childDocuments_.review: this game is a hardcore battlefield 1 Italian campaign. imagine battlefield 1 and insurgency had a baby and it ONLY speaks Italian. a bit rough on the edges but it works. day 1 you had to open the .exe to run the game because the steam play button would hang. there is no kill cams, no tracers, no hitscan, and no lens flares. Sprinting makes you sprint at decent speed. you can jump and climb on the mountain terrain. the maps offer vertical combat compared to flat game play between invisible walls and buildings that make up 100% of the maps hell let loose has. every player can assist in gunning/destroying/healing. everyone can be a medic because applying a bandage is easy! and support classes can put more bullets in your pockets while you stay aiming at your target.You don't feel useless because your class is tied to one ability, instead classes offer bonuses you can choose like perks. since there are no tracers you don't see your bullet projectiles. and since its WWI you will be fighting close range. this makes many people think it's hitscan. bullets in this game are fast and they don't show travel time unless you are shooting 200-300+ meters away. that is when you need to lead them. i don't think many players realize that everyone is shooting huge WWI rifle cartridges and not 45cal like WWII.one negative reviewer said "Engineers troll all the time by building wire so you can't push on the map, making you stand still to cut it just to get shot." <- lol this is war son. also i'm stealing that idea.

_childDocuments_.review: Isonzo is a fun game in concept and has the basis to be another awesome entry to the WWI series, but needs more modes to be truly worth it.But there's one mode and its an attacking and defending mode a la Battlefield 1's operations mode (though it oddly plays more like Rush).  There are 6 gorgeous maps and the game looks good, but I really feel like Tannenberg had more replay value and more to offer.This game looks beautiful, and the Italian mountains you fight in are breathtaking to look at.  Uniforms are flamboyant and look great too! Effects like explosions are wonderful!Bolting, bayoneting, and many animations are, however, janky as hell and you'll notice.The sole gamemode is offensive- one side attacks, one side defends.  That is it.  That is the game.There is a lot of depth compared to BF1 operations or BFV/2042 breakthrough, but it suffers from being kind of repetitive if you want a break from this singular mode.  There is no TDM or FFA like in the previous WWI games, which was a nice distraction if you got bored with the main modes in those games.Offensive is far from bad- it plays pretty well from what I've seen, and there's a lot of depth because you can create your own strong points with barbed wire and sandbags, as well as there being smaller side objective points you can build and destroy.  This game mode plays as one side attacking a series of sectors, each of which of have 2 objectives to capture or destroy a la Battlefield's operations/breakthrough and Rush, respectively.  there is usually one of each.  Often there is a singular "destroy" objective and a singular "capture" objective, the former being to plant an explosive on something and let the timer run, and the latter being fighting over a small area of import on the map.  This latter bit is won or lost by having more or less soldiers in the area than your opponent.Isonzo is similar to Rush in Battlefield, as you will get 300 tickets (read- lives, and when its depleted the defenders win) for each assault against the next line of enemy defenses.  This makes it very frustrating when you attack and lose, as when your 300 tickets are up, the game just kinda ends even if you're on the first assault.As a defender, if you don't manage to get even just 1 kill, say 299/300 before the attackers successfully take the sector, the tickets reset to 300 and you have to get 300 more kills. I find this extremely frustrating because even playing well often means that my work is pretty much undone by the attackers completing their objective.BF1 solved all these issues by having 3 "battalions" of several hundred men you attacked with.  The attackers always had 3 chances to win, and the defenders kills would actually count towards the overall end of the match by whittling down the enemy force.  If a "battalion" was killed off, the attackers would get 2 more to use, but the tickets would not reset in between sectors.  So killing 100 men per sector meant that the battalion would probably last about 3 sectors. This system allowed for the defenders to not get overly frustrated by narrowly losing a point, as they could bloody the enemy's nose and make them pay for costly and reckless assaults. A little planning led to a lot of great moments as defenders being able to whittle down the enemy made the last sectors intense!In Isonzo, if you don't get 300 kills against the attackers and they take the point they just get more tickets and after a while you're just kinda bored.  The enemy can still charge you with reckless abandon, and your kills up to that point don't matter.Isonzo should adopt BF1 operations' system, imo, as it is very frustrating to fight off the attackers just to lose and have to do it all over again.  Attacking and losing outright also just isn't fun, and BF1's compromise would work well in this game.Now, the other big thing to recognize is that in Verdun and Tannenburg, there was a push and pull game-mode called frontlines, and then later a mode called maneuver. These modes allowed for both teams to attack and defend- maneuver played a little bit like a more structured conquest from Battlefield, and frontlines played like a big attack and counter attack, push pull type game mode.Both were fun, and both allowed for a lot more dynamic gameplay than just one side attacking and defending in Isonzo.  gamemodes like Isonzo's offensive (breakthrough/operations) are great, but they need other modes with more freedom to compliment them.  I find that Isonzo will get boring without more modes to play that allow for that more dynamic fighting like in the two previous WWI series games.So more modes, and then I can recommend this game!Gunplay is fun, but its also hitscan so whomever see's who first ends up winning the fight.  As a result, good "firefights" don't usually happen in this game unless you're grouped up with others.  The game does a good job to make you aim carefully, and there's some good realism thrown in for good measure, but a lot of the times this game seems more sensitive than Verdun or tannenberg and I feel that it's simply a little too easy to shoot and abuse the hitscan- especially at very long ranges since there is no appreciable bullet drop from what I can tell.That said, I still like it, but I really do prefer Tannenberg's gunplay, or the gunplay of games that use projectile systems.This game has a nice degree of realism, in of that the weapons are all authentic and kills are near always one shot and instant.  The hitscan is really my only complaint in this as of now, and suppression effects are well balanced.gas attacks and artillery are and feel lethal, and be prepared to deal with them often!There are like, 6-7 classes that have player limits on them, similar to games like insurgency or Hell Let Loose.  There can only be 2 officers, for instance, and only one or two players with a scoped weapon to keep things less camp-y.In a way, I like this system as the older system in the WWI games series involved you and your 4 man squad picking a sub faction on either the entente or central powers, be it storm troopers, american doughboys, or canadians.The old system locked you into one of 4 roles in a squad, and gave you 3 loadout options based on what you were expected to do in that role.  IE the machine gunner had a machine gun, the grenadier would have extra grenades, etc.In Isonzo this is gone, and you will find yourself simply making a loadout and picking what you want to do more so than you previously could.  This is good, in a way, but also it does take away from the intimacy of your squad in my opinion, and means that if a meta forms it's going to be far more easily followed by the player base. Personally I don't particularly mind what they did as it allows me to play how I want without switching squads.Squad spawning is a full feature in this game as well, for better or worse, rather than the old system where you could only spawn on your officer.on my rig, the game runs pretty damn smooth and I haven't encountered too many bugs or glitches.It's gross. There aren't that many uniforms in game but for around 15 bucks I think you can get a bunch of different uniforms and customization options for your character (which is new to the series btw you have preset faces but can change your uniform and some features about yourself)The guns in this game are almost all bolt action, and all are very authentic and look great! be prepared for this though- as this isn't the near fantasy realm of BF1. MG's are usually mounted and immovable, but mortars and artillery pieces add some nice flare and variety. personally I like whats here! There isn't much variety for basic primary weapons though, so just be aware of that going in.

_childDocuments_.review: ---{Graphics}---☐ You forget what reality is☑ Beautiful☐ Good☐ Decent☐ Bad☐ Don‘t look too long at it☐ Paint.exeWhile the texture quality itself would fall under simply "good", the part that made me select "Beautiful" instead is the great attention to detail and accuracy compared to the real location. Unlike Verdun, this game thrives from the huge variety of this front of ww1: From cold and grey bunker lines and muddy trenches to beautiful mountain scenery, cities, and blooming fields. The devs did a great job doing something many games seem to rather neglect: Making the artstyle and graphics aligning with the story, the worldbuilding, the experience they want to give to the player. ---{Gameplay}---☐ Very good☑ Good☐ It‘s just gameplay☐ Mehh☐ Starring at walls is better☐ Just don‘tIt is important to keep in mind that this is a realism game. It doesn't offer such a huge amount of weapons, perks and cosmetics like battlefield 1, but within the goal of making a realistic and historical accurate shooter, I'd say the game does the job pretty good. One aspect I really appreciate is the ability to host games and play with bots. Of course, playing PvP is a completely different experience. But having the oppertunity to test the waters and unlock items/perks in singleplayer is definitely a nice feature. Also, the bots have clearly been improved compared to their other games (Verdun, Tannenberg), which adds some replay-value even when played in singleplayer.---{Audio}---☐ Eargasm☐ Very good☑ Good☐ Not too bad☐ Bad☐ EarrapeNice music, authentic weapon sounds, and a lot of enviromental effects. Only negative point I have: No unique voicelines for the Germans, but rather recycled Verdun voicelines. ---{Audience}---☐ Kids☐ Teens☑ Adults☐ Human☑ LizardsAdults. Not saying there aren't teenagers also playing this game but generally speaking, I feel that the gameplay, speed and weapon handling will more likely appeal to adulds than teenagers (or even kids).---{PC Requirements}---☐ Check if you can run paint☐ Potato☑  Decent☐ Fast☐ Rich boiiiiii☐ Ask NASA if they have a spare computer---{Difficulity}---☐ Just press ‚A‘☐ Easy☐ Significant brain usage☐ Easy to learn / Hard to master☑ Difficult☐ Dark SoulsThe game has a rather realistic damage model, meaning you will die a lot and have little room for mistakes. Especially with bolt action rifles being the main weapon type, you do not only die fast but also can often not afford to miss shots. The good thing is: You have no restrictions how often you can spawn as individual. This is important, because otherwise you would have a hard time finding out about all kinds of chockepoints, nasty MG-emplacements or other kinds of death traps. Over time of course you will find these kind of things easy, and automatically know when to approach carefully and when where you can move rather swiftly without putting yourself in danger. But if you are new to the game expect it to be harder than most FPS shooters.---{Grind}---☐ Nothing to grind☐ Only if u care about leaderboards/ranks☐ Isnt necessary to progress☑ Average grind level☐ Too much grind☐ You‘ll need a second live for grindingUnlocking allows for more specialisations and additional weapons. Non of them are strictly needed or give you an insane advantage, but are nice because it allows you to customize your classes to your personal strategy. There are some challenges for various associated. Some of them can be a bit frustrating, but nothing impossible or too time consuming if you know how.---{Story}---☐ Story?☑ Text or Audio floating around☐ Average☐ Good☐ Lovely☐ It‘ll replace your lifeThere is no story as in a story mode, but rather am fairly accurate representation of the historical places during this time. Other than that there are some minor explanatios and references to the real "story" behind the battles, but that's it.---{Game Time}---☐ Long enough for a cup of coffee☐ Short☑ Average☐ Long☐ To infinity and beyondSo far (24h), I do really enjoy the game. I play it with a friend which definitely adds a lot more game time than if you'd play it alone. The game certainly lacks additional maps gamemmodes for now, but they do push out frequent updates still so this might improve in the future. I don't think it offers the same gameplay time as other, bigger shooters. But if you like the setting and have friends to play it with, it still has a decent amount of things to unlock and various strategies to play out until you run out of things to do.---{Price}---☐ It’s free!☑ Worth the price☐ If u have some spare money left☐ Not recommended☐ You could also just burn your money---{Bugs}---☐ Never heard of☑ Minor bugs☐ Can get annoying☐ ARK: Survival Evolved☐ The game itself is a big terrarium for bugsThe only minor annoying bug so far were disconnects and a bug during a certain unlock challenge. Other than that, I've only noticed purely cosmetical bugs so far. Overall, this game is definitely better than the average FPS game when it comes to bugs.

_childDocuments_.review: Though I have never played Verdun or Tannenberg, Isonzo is one of the best online first-person shooters I've played in years! Firstly, I am really enjoying the tactical and purposeful gameplay. Every class has a role and fulfilling that role rewards the wider team. In this regard, you win and lose as a team, unlike other mainstream franchises like Call of Duty (and Battlefield).Secondly, the game looks, sounds, and performs excellently. The Italian Alps is beautifully recreated, with trenches and bunkers lining the mountainside. Adding to these battles are Italian soldiers yelling commands, bullets whizzing by, and mortar fire in the distance, creating an intense auditory experience. Throughout my brief time playing, I have never had dropped connections, stuttering combat, or graphics failing to render. If I was being REALLY picky, I did have ONE issue with spawning into part of the built environment, but I am counting on the hotfixes to address that, especially as I do know others experienced a similar bug.Thirdly, you really get a sense that the developers cared about learning about the Battles of the Isonzo and prioritised historical accuracy. If you look through past Dev Blogs, you'll see this mindful attention to detail better reveal itself. Ultimately, the game does justice in showing the futility of these battles and does not glamorise the mass slaughter of these campaigns.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a low-budget, very old-fashioned  but adequately entertaining team shooter rendered fundamentally anti-fun by the total absence of communication or teamwork on 9/10 servers. You cannot select a server or easily connect with regulars. The voice communication is either entirely broken or so under-utilised by the player-base that in 16 hours I've never heard another player's voice.Pre-recorded voice communication via a radial menu is woefully underdeveloped, full of choices that have no use and missing almost anything anyone would ever have a reason to say.Gunplay is in the spirit of 2005-era historic war mods, with nearly pixel-perfect accuracy and snap-aim, making the use of machineguns or melee largely too dangerous to attempt, creating a historically inaccurate experience that's more like twitch-shooting.The maps are aesthetically appealing but extremely narrow and linear, and in most cases they've been overbalanced to the point of frustrating, permitting no creativity or tactical use of terrain. Invisible walls, execution borders and 'convenient' barriers, rocks and barbed wire abound. It feels like less like a battlefield and more like a roleplay creche for soldiers.All that said, the weapons are fairly satisfying, especially explosives like grenades, mortars and air strikes. The officer experience is entertaining. Handguns are punchy and feel nicely balanced, but rifles are just deathlasers with no weight, no heft, no sway, none of the real challenges of using a heavy bolt action long rifle in sustained warfare.It's... Not worth what it costs, for now, but if you have a group of friends and can overlook some of the issues above while communicating using third party software, you should find some entertainment here.

_childDocuments_.review: Isonzo is a bit of an oddity for me. I love the Italian front setting, the weapons are largely fair/historically accurate, and some of the scenery they used for the maps is really cool to see considering it's all done in Unity engine. What I don't like is the clunky feel to everything; movement, aiming, interacting with buildables (similar to Vedrun and Tannenberg). Sometimes there's just too many call ins/explosions and you will feel like you're participating in a meatgrinder. Coming from a background of Red Orchestra 2/Rising Storm 1&2, Insurgency, and games like Ground Branch/Ready or Not, I feel like the maps are a little choke pointy/cramped. Sometimes the only tactical option is to charge forward like zerglings. It's good - I'm a milsim/tactical shooter fan and this one keeps me coming back late night to play a round or two. When it clicks, it really clicks. You're diving in and out of trenches, trying to stay alive in the precarious stretches of wide open mountainous terrain while mortars are blowing up all around you. Those moments where you turn to check on your teammates only to watch them get blown to bits while you barely survived happen often with the brutality of combat. There's nothing cooler than committing to a bayonet charge because you don't have time to reload and it working. This scratches a BF1 itch for me and that's what I keep coming back to.Is it GOTY milsim? No - I'd like to see movement/interactions polished up more. Sometimes the clunkiness of moving around really takes me out of the immersion and fun. But, this game was clearly made with love for history and the WW1 setting. If you've played Verdun and Tannenberg, Isonzo is more polished but very familiar. For those who are coming in blind, you're going to die a lot before you find the groove. The community is on the small side but the playerbase is respectful and nice. If you want something on the brutal and crazy side, this is the game for yall.

_childDocuments_.review: If you've played any of the other games by this developer you'll recognise the elements of their previous games - claustrophobic trench warfare with mismatching and/or unsuitable equipment (Verdun), wide open maps with objectives (Tannenberg) and see them combined along with expanded squad roles into a game that is both innovative, and miles away from online live-service fps games and unlocks.You as a player do not matter, the game doesn’t pretend you are the fulcrum of the world you spawn into.  Unlocks exist, but only to add variety to gameplay not to motivate you to grind, the starter kit for each class it is as good as anything you will unlock later. Progress is through playing the game, rather than forcing platform engagement. You will die a lot, sometimes to agents unknown far across the map while you were focused on surviving the tiny hostile bubble around you, other times to whiffing a crucial blow, or by just being in the wrong place at the wrong time.The classes have a lot of nuance allowing for varied gameplay and playstyles, while the tuorials have been put into optional “challenges”, which also unlock different perks and equipment. You can, however just play the game and ignore the challenges, but personally speaking I found playing through them improved my core skills and introduced me to play styles I wouldn't otherwise have tried.

_childDocuments_.review: The game be pretty alright. Definitely an improvement over Verdun and Tannenberg. Movement is better: vaulting is now a thing and allows you to add some verticality to the gameplay (although this can be finicky at times).  Graphics are greatly improved compared to V/T. No more brown palette all over, landscape are gorgeous already from the main menu.You can now build support structures to both your and the team's benefit; you can heal yourself and your teammates (no more auto-regen crap).Six maps at launch, but they are plenty to have some fun (and there are three free expansions down the line for a total of 7 more maps incoming). They feel overall well balanced, without a clear bias towards defenders or attackers.The new class system is a lot of fun, although the challenges to level progress are definitely not everyone's cup of tea they work better than the no-effort leveling that V/T where.Isonzo is *very* reliant on teamplay, almost to its detriment. When the team acts together you will steamroll enemies, have great fun, and enjoy the game the way it was meant to be played. On the other hand, if you get with a team of campers you might as well die in frustration, as progress will be exacerbatingly difficult if you keep pushing for objectives, while your team stays in the rear doing overall nothing.Some bugs are still around, and can be VERY annoying to deal with, but the team is constantly pushing new fixes every other week, so the game experience is overall very positive.Netcode is definitely better, no more disconnections between matches or during a game for no particular reason.Will probably add some more hundred hours to it.

I haven't played a game as much in its early release like Isonzo, and its had me hooked from day one. 1. Great potential for awesome teamwork 2. Immersive gameplay3. Attentive Devs 4. Interesting cosmetics that aid the Devs but aren't necessary 5. Great variety of playstyles or ways to aid your team 6. Devastating call ins which will turn the tide if used properly 7. Historically accurate weapons and maps which look gorgeous8. Incredibly grandiose and sweeping soundtrack which makes overtime feel incredibly stressful. 9. Rewarding and varied gameplay10. Strong playerbase (I'm based on AU servers with 2-3 full servers every night) 1. Local voice chat to better coordinate squad tactics.2. Slightly more variety in gun sounds, more so to help in the tense trench battles to help discern between friend and foe (voice lines already help with this).4. Expanding the healing process into a pseudo medic class within the rifleman class, making an aid station deployable to full heal teammates as well as allowing faster movement speed from screaming teammate to screaming teammate. 5. Making smoke call ins more long lasting than XyXl Bromide gas, as smoke has a completely opaque appearance. Making bayonet animations more viable in close combat situations where aiming one's weapon is futile. 7. Grenade spam, which could be easily remedied by increasing the cooldown on grenade crates, or limiting the number of assault class players who can utilise grenades like scopes for marksman.8. _childDocuments_.review: Isonzo throws players into the gritty reality of World War I, blending immersive graphics with historical accuracy. While the single-player story might lack depth, the game truly shines in its multiplayer battles, i feel like it truly emphasizes strategic teamwork. Despite occasional server hiccups and minor glitches, "Isonzo" delivers an engaging experience for all types of players immersing players in the amazing landscapes of the Great War. Additionally, the game's fast time-to-kill, often resulting in one-tap kills, adds an extra layer of intensity to the battlefield.

_childDocuments_.review: Isonzo is the successful evolution of Verdun and Tannenberg. They took the good aspects of those two games and improved them with new mechanics and features, producing an enhanced WW1 FPS experience.The environment is stunning and the game immersion is almost unmatched by many other games. Beautiful locations get ravaged by artillery strikes, gas clouds and plane bombing runs, while soldiers push through the no man's land using whatever cover can be found. They will be lucky enough to reach the other side unharmed, before jumping down in the trenches to fight the enemy.The overall gameplay experience is superb, very casual but also very intense. It is very easy to die, but it is also ten times more rewarding managing to push and capture the enemy trench, possibly with the use of a well place smoke cover or artillery strike to clear out the enemy strongpoint and begin storming the enemy positions.The close quarter battles with single shot rifles, where one missed bullet could be the difference between keep fighting and going back to the repawn screen, are tense and challenging but also a lot of fun. The gunplay feels more on the casual side than realistic to me, but the weapons are all well balanced and there is no overall best weapon. A pistol will be very handy in a close quarter fight but almost useless at longer ranges, while a long-barreled rifle will be best when used to cover big distances but will feel very clunky in the trenches and will probalby get you killed if you find more than one enemy. Between these two extremes there are revolvers and shorter rifles and it's possible to choose the weapon that suits the situation best.The class system in this game is also well made, with each class having its unique features and synergies towards other classes, allowing a group of coordinated players to achieve better results in battle and possibly influencing the course of the match. The few classes and weapons that could result OP are restricted behind a very low number allowed per team and this makes them less relevant on the overall battle scene, giving a couple players the luxury to play with slightly more powerful toys WHEN USED CORRECTLY.The soldiers' voice lines are also outstanding, managing to perfectly capture the chaos of battle amongst screams of pain, warnings and encouragement in the soldiers' native laguanges, plus the soundtrack is incredibly epic, particularly when the battle is close to the end and the fight rages on a contested objective.This game is overall a very casual and relatively fast paced shooter (not COD level but not as slow as Squad nor Hell Let Loose) where it's guaranteed to die a lot. But the easy death is compensated by the fast spawn time leading to a continuous assault on the enemy position, which only helps replicate the assaults of WW1. Sometime after I respawn I just stop for some seconds and look at the overall battle happening, feeling amazed by how immersed I am and how realistic it looks like.This leads me to the last point that I want to praise: COSMETICS. These cosmetics are the most historically accurate I have ever seen in any recent World War game or FPS in general. The developers introduced extremely realistic, historical and even unusual but awesome uniforms, (just an example is the bycicle-carrying Bersagliere). They are blocked behind a paywall and I understand that, cosmetics monetization these days is the only viable option to support the development of further content, but every dollar/euro/pound/etc... spent on those uniforms will be well spent. This also allows us players to receive free dlcs in the future, going from 6 gorgeous and BIG maps to many more (hopefully even more beautiful).If I have to give this game a vote it would be a solid 8/10: unique, immersive and engaging, perfect for a quick game or a full offensive operation, spanning multiple maps and hours of gaming with some friends.

_childDocuments_.review: I found myself in stitches throughout my gameplay of [Game Title]. The chaos ensued from the very start, as even the most basic commands seemed to have a life of their own. Picture this:Me: excitedly attempting to unleash a hail of bullets with a machine gunGame: "Press 'E' to use Machine gun"Me: eagerly pressing 'E' ...and nothing. Not a single bullet.However, the amusement didn't end there because, as it turns out, mortality is a mere suggestion in this game. Let me walk you through the peculiarities that turned an ordinary World War shooter into an extraordinary comedy:I strolled casually across the battlefield, surrounded by the symphony of artillery fire and players scrambling in all directions. A peculiar observation caught my eye—everyone, friend or foe, seemed more invested in the ground than the actual battle. "Probably bots," I mused. Venturing closer to the frontline, I found myself thrust into a chaotic skirmish. Amidst the onslaught of enemies, I believed I had secured the perfect spot for a sneaky multikill. Little did I know, bullets were as effective as confetti at a warzone. Shooting turned out to be an exercise in futility, as my rounds seemed to be more interested in the sandy terrain than in dispatching Nazis.At one point, I found myself in a bizarre standoff, exchanging gunfire with an enemy who appeared impervious to bullets. To my surprise, even as five adversaries formed a firing squad, their aim remained steadfastly glued to the ground, shooting at an imaginary nemesis called "Sand."So, there you have it. In [Game Title], the ground is the true antagonist, and shooting at enemies is more likely to kick up dust clouds than to make any impact. It's a game where laughter reigns supreme, and the sand takes center stage as the unsuspecting villain of the battlefield.

_childDocuments_.review: These moments of nocturnal gaming leave an indelible impression. Eyes and ears are tensed to the maximum, the rustling approach of strange feet in the tall grass is an unutterably menacing thing. Your breath comes in shallow bursts; you have to force yourself to stifle any panting or wheezing. There is a little mechanical click as the safety-catch of your pistol is taken off; the sound cuts straight through your nerves. Your teeth are grinding on the fuse-pin of the hand-grenade. The encounter will be short and murderous. You tremble with two contradictory impulses: the heightened awareness of the huntsmen, and the terror of the quarry. You are a world to yourself, saturated with the appalling aura of the savage landscape of Isonzo. It's a fun game.

_childDocuments_.review: The game was fun, but has issues. Big ones. This is a tentative approval to buy the game, but I would suggest only if you can get it on sale, or have wide berth in your budget. Anti-cheat? Whats that. The more popular this game becomes, the more cheaters you are going to see, until you have BF problem where cheaters will clear lobies and the game will die. Emplaced Machineguns are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ useless. You stand stock straight up behind the things and do not attempt to take cover at all. This makes your head a perfect target for literally everyone. So dont use them, you say? Id love to, since they are so trash. However they are tied to tasks to unlock new weapons. Most everyone agrees that unless you are on the task, you dont use the things. Its just a way to get killed easier. This is quite the contridiction to history, where they were feared to face on the battlefield. Now they are just shunned to use.Pistols need to be nerfed. Sprinting through the trenches one shotting people constantly has basically turned the game into a game of WWI Quake. The servers are POTATOES. I keep getting a reported 22 ping, but constantly have sever connection, lag, or delay issues. Keep an eye on the right hand side of your screen, you may see these red icons pop for you, sometimes all map. Spawning: Sometimes spawning on flat ground is fine, especially when your team has pushed your opponent back a ways. However, if it happens to you while your enemy is close, its nearly an instant death as you are shot 2-3 seconds after you spawn in game. And if you spawn further back, the amount of time you would need to run to prevent a point capture is untenable. Mask Flashing: Whenever you mask up or off, the screen flashes three times. This is visually unpleasnt. I dont know if anyone else has this, but it happens every single time I use the item. So what do I like about the game?As much as this game is about corner camping, there is only one scope per map. This keeps some of the cheese to a minimum. Compared to something like Hell Let Loose, this is slightly faster paced. While sprinting through the trenches isnt completely realistic, there are a number of things it does much better. I can pass my allies in a trench, my allies do not block my line of advance. There is a dedicated role for spotting enemies, so you can assist your allies by marking assault groups or snipers. There is a sort of kill cam; Its black and white, and only gives you a general direction, but it allows you to either improve your future game play, or verify the authenticity of your death. Also, the Dev only has included cosmetic DLC (which would support further development of the game), and not included in P2W mechanics. I dont mind DLC like this, kudos to the Dev. This game is infested with hackers now that its gained some sort of popularity. Aimbot is both incessant and constant on both teams. It has become a contest of who cant aimbot the other faster. Without Anticheat, this game is a total write off now.

_childDocuments_.review: First, if you're coming to Isonzo from Verdun or Tannenberg, go to the settings and change the "toggle aim" to off and increase the aiming sensitivity... this will clear up some of the jankieness (not a real word, but accurate) and help you feel like less of a new boot.Second, if you don't have a decent pc, forget about it. Isonzo is very heavy on gpu's and had mine screaming for the first hour... fyi, scuttlebutt says the rtx 40-series is looking at release potentially around Sept. 20th, so I wouldn't be surprised to see more 30-series on the used market in the near future. Just in case you want to upgrade your rig.Those two things out of the way, I've legitimately enjoyed Isonzo for the 1.7 hours that I've played. I was really put off initially as I was expecting the game to handle more like the first two in their WW1 series, but the longer I played, the more I began to appreciate Isonzo's mechanics in their own right. Feel free to disagree with me, but this is my review.Isonzo's tiered unlock system was also initially annoying, but I did appreciate how it forced me to play in a more cautious and supportive way. I think there needs to be a little more balancing here, but in general, it tends to work well. I feel that the dev's could have focused a bit more on game play unlocks vs cosmetic unlocks, but I digress. Everyone's a critic and they can't please everybody.I personally find it refreshing to see games that reflect historical accuracy and realism with such vigor. Isonzo is not another COD knock-off where you can sprint at 30 mph, jump from a three story window onto a pile of rocks and keep on trucking like nothing happened. As a former combat infantryman and Purple Heart recipient, I can tell you that sprawling onto the side of a mountain to escape incoming fire from a height of even 4 feet is a sure way to ruin your day. Rocks are hard, your ribs aren't. Ask me how I know. You can't climb over everything and trenches are difficult to get out of at times... I feel that the character movement, weapon sway, and overall handling is one of the most true-to-life representations I've experienced to date.As with any game, it's going to take bit to get used too and I'll need several more hours to build experience, but here's the kicker: everyone is starting from a similar position.Overall 8/10*edit: grammer***UPDATE: RTX 4090 set for release 10/12/22**

It feels impossible to push.*The lack of weapon variety can be a bit rough when compared to say the amount of WW1 weapons in a Call of Duty game. It would be nicer if offense could get access to 1 or 2 more scoped weapons simply to help with entrenched machine gunners.Overall the game is an 8/10 and worth picking up at full retail price until whatever big shooter this year or next year hits you want to sink your teeth into. _childDocuments_.review: Isonzo: Third Time's The Charm.When I heard of this game being announced, I was very apprehensive. And not simply because it was a M2H game, but because M2H's games were getting a tad same-y. And I don't say that as a guy who picked up Verdun for cheap, I've been playing some variant of these games since all the way back in Pre-Alpha "Unity Browser" game stage. I roll deep. Verdun is good, chunky and while it has neat features has flaws like a wonky progression system, overall bad handling and gunplay and odd balance. Mostly because the MG-08/15 exists. Tannenberg was similar, although it had better-ish graphics and proper fixed machine guns it still suffered from floaty controls and died out quick as it good. So I expected Isonzo to be similar.Isonzo is the rare sequel that improves on every single flaw of the previous games, making the WWI era shooter standard Verdun have work and be fun while also more competitive with the competition. You now have things such as mortars, rifle grenades and buildables yoinked from Squad, and reasons to build them beyond base building. You also have a revised squad system that makes specific classes you can level up by XP rather than weird tokens you earn on level up, and challenges that unlock additional weapons and features. The gunplay is so reworked that I almost struggled to tell this was a Verdun game until I managed to lose my front sight while aiming.Some thing's don't change.Is it another WWI shooter from the guys who were the "First" to do WWI shooters? Yes. Yes it is. And deep down this game does play the same. But M2H and BlackMill have reworked Isonzo to such an extent that it's honestly hard to tell the two apart and it makes an average FPS with fun moments into a VERY fun FPS, beautiful to look at and somewhat fun to play. Mostly because I still suck at Verdun, but I'm having fun while I suck!

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10Generally a okay game with glaring flaws compared to Verdun and Tannenburg. Visual the game is stunning and an upgrade to the visuals of Verdun and Tannenburg. The flaws are many in my opinion that once you put a few hours into the game, and coming from other Blackmill games they will be very noticeable. Hit reg is a big one for me atleast. Bullets will not reg at point blank ranges sometimes but this could be a ping issue or just game engine. I remember Verdun and Tannenburg sometimes having this issue but not to the same extent. Explosives are generally very weak especially grenades, with most people completing grenade challenges on bot servers. Explosive call ins for officer's are okay but usually only wound players depending on placement. Gas is generally useless for inflicting deaths on the enemy team. Mostly used for cover, and causing confusion on objective points or combat areas. Not a huge fan of the offensive game mode. Heavily favors defense on most maps. Overall a generally good game, but with some flaws in it. I still have fun and would recommend this to WW1 enjoyers

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic WWI game. That sounds like a simple statement, but what I mean is:-Weapons are almost entirely bolt action rifles.-(Then someone whips out an LMG or ice pick, puts you down and you think "What the heck")-There was no tutorial or single player - you join a game and charge.-Although "straightforward" objectives, the trenches and terrain keep me disoriented-You die from 1-2 bullets-You're constantly getting shellshocked and suppressedIt's tough, unforgiving, and an all-around very World War One experience. It has also been a blast every time I've played, and while it quickly gets easier, it never gets "easier".

_childDocuments_.review: It's a casual milsim for people who don't really want to bother themselves with communication and co-op required in something like ArmA, Squad, or Hell let Loose. That would be a great thing and something I personally enjoy if the rest of the game wasn't also dumbed down to a point where long ass matches feel like a one-sided waste of time.First of all there's no auto-balance of any sort. If the teams are uneven, you can confidently predict that the match is going to be a stomp. Even more if one team has an officer who has enough brain cells to call in smokes, gas, and artillery. All of those things solely exist to erase FPS mechanics in favor of pressing "ok our time to win" button.The actual gunplay and movement don't do anything to salvage this garbage either. Everyone moves like a geriatric overdosed on sleeping pills. Forget any sort of movement in a fight or even using it for strategy, like repositioning between points or even recapturing a point. Guns feel good to shoot, but combat is just milsims dumbed down further than ever. Landing one shot with almost anything is an instant kill, and wounded allies can only be healed. There's no down-but-not-out mechanics or anything of sort.Much like Verdun was, and I'm sure their either fail of game is, Isonzo is mostly about a bunch of people standing 100 meters away from each other and clicking on people who can't see them. And when it's not, it's two elderly people shuffling left in right in hopes of being the one to land the first shot.The garbage unlock system doesn't help either. If you want to experience more than 5% of the content, you will have to grind this game over and over and over, often having to complete asinine challenge that at least partially rely on luck. These games always have diehard fans who don't play video games and will forgive any issues due to their weird worship of anything WW1 related, but other than them, you will be hard pressed to find someone who would consistently dedicate their time to such a dull and repetitive game.The latter is less of an assumption and more of a fact, as prior to recent free weekend + big update it was essentially a dead game with only a few active servers.If you want a more casual milsim type game, get Insurgency. If you want a proper milsim, get Squad or Hell let Loose. If you want a better WW1 game, get BF1. If you want a WW1 casual milsim then you're ♥♥♥♥ out of luck unless you can put up with sheer mediocrity.

_childDocuments_.review: An awesome game, definite improvement over the already amazingly fun Verdun and Tannenberg, it brings you into a action shooter that borders on the verge of being a "realism" style game. Set on the Austro-Hungarian-Italian Front of WWI you'll get to enjoy pleasant things like: artillery raining down on you and all of your friends, gas attacks causing you to suffocate to death, snipers that pop your head like a watermelon, and officers that force you to go "over the top" to charge headlong into a machine gun nest. Pros: Lots of fun. Gunplay is 8/10 and its easy to do really well, but it doesn't mean you don't have to work for it. When you have a good match, you'll feel accomplished. The devs put AI in the server so you don't have to worry about not being able to play if no-one is online. Easy to play with friends, you can run a squad together and cower in a foxhole while steel rains down on you from miles away!Cons: The AI is SUPER reactive. If they can see a hint of your body, they will shoot you. AI pathfinding is substandard, but it doesn't break the game luckily. Unlocking things for your class requires earning class XP and then completion of a challenge before you can use the item, it isn't a huge con though because finishing those challenges isn't extremely difficult until you hit level 20 in the class.Overall this game is a really enjoyable FPS that you can hop in to easily. With 20 hours in the game, I've already hit the 2,000 kill mark and hit level 70.

_childDocuments_.review: AVANTI SAVOIA!Great game, very funny. It makes you feel like a true soldier fighting for his life in a trench. It can be a little complex at first, though it's pretty easy to learn, and there are tons of videos on Youtube too. It has got a great balance between being a fun and memable game and an historically accurate ww1 experience: you won't be traumatized, but you'll definetly learn about the time period, and the game is very historically accurate: there are NO repeating weapons outside of pistols and few LMGs. This is actual ww1 warfare (only bolt action rifles for the most part), and realistic to this time period (much more than Battelfield 1, which is full of experimental weapons thatr weren't really used on the battelfield... pun). This creates a type of unique gameplay that can be loved or hated unfortunately, so it's best to ponder buying the game and to watch some gameplays first.Oh, and if you see a dude running around with an ice pick or that kills you with a flaregun in game, don't worry, it's just a mountaineer.Overall, the game has flaws, there's no denying that, but it's fun, accurate, educational, epic and memable, like all games should be.E per un italiano, è un must play per conoscere la storia di questo Paese, e la realtà storica di questo sanguinario periodo (escludendo i montanari di prima).I post this on the day when, 110 years ago, the war started for Russia, Serbia, Austro-Hungary, Germany, France and Britain, so its the perfect day to hop in and prepare the front for imminent war.And remember... AVANTI SAVOIA, VIVA L'ITALIA!

_childDocuments_.review: I have nearly 1400 hours in Verdun and Tannenberg (participated as tester for both Tannenberg and Isonzo). This game looks and feels very different from the previous titles, for sure. _childDocuments_.review: Great game, although I have the impression some battles are really unbalanced to one side (defenders, most of the time). The biggest problem tho, in my opinion, is that I have three different games (Verdun, Tannenberg and Isonzo) that should have been one, and every time I'm playing one of those I'm (obviously) not playing the others: the already not that big playerbase get divided and by result you have half-empty lobbys instead of full ones and this by itself may lead to some people stopping playing these games.I do recommend all three games, as there's no really other ones that delivers experiences like you get in WW1 Game Series, and those are already quite inexpensive games that are always on a sale so you can get it for even cheaper. _childDocuments_.review: From a Verdun / Tannenberg veteran perspective:Overall better game (out of M2H's ww1 series): YesFixed issue with netcode: NoAnticheat: No - as far as i know, but thanks for the issue above it's hard to recognize cheater vs player playing at lowest graphic settings or with high ping beceuse he's, for some reason, unable to sellect right server region for him...Fixed issues with bunny hops and movement exploits: kinda, tho it's more because of reworked battle mechanics where nomansland is much larger and the combat is more dynamic, becuase there's more complex battlefield - not like Verdun where there are trenches everywhere.Optimization: not great not terrible - just turn off tesselation and lod distance not greater than medium. Thiese will make you less competetive because tesselated terrain is not "real", so you can't see through where you'd normaly could, it's shootable through and invisible at greater distances for your enemies. And of course no need for maxing shadows and reflections.Other than that the game feels just more modern and bigger in terms of loadouts, bit of field structures building, i think the mechanics of objectives to destroy or capture while maitaining the battle lines is good - way better than Tannenberg where the issue of capture system was, that ennemy could capture parts of the map behind you. _childDocuments_.review: I love this game, it's great, but I do have some issues with it. the first one being that sometimes when I spawn, I spawn glitched into an object I cannot escape from and I end up having to re-spawn. I also have an issue with the toxic gas; if you get caught in the gas you only have a couple of seconds to put your mask on which is not enough time. I always end up dying before i can get it on. I am former military and we were taught that you have exactly 9 seconds to put on and clear your gas mask. Giving the player 9 seconds to put on their gas mask would be more realistic. And lastly, I think the stationary machine gun turrets should have more cover. There is almost no chance of surviving on the machine gun turrets because you immediately die; having just a little more cover for the turrets would make it a asset worth using. Other than that I think you all are great developers, and I enjoy your games. I also would  like to add that your company should really work on marketing. Your games tend to die out really fast and I believe its due to lack of good marketing. I'm talking about Facebook ads, YouTube ads, and just ads on other major platforms. That is an area you all are lacking in. I love this company and I love supporting it; I just want to see you all prosper. Keep up the good work.

_childDocuments_.review: Decent from a gameplay perspective, although I can see why it would be frustrating for some players. What I will comment on are two things: 1. the egregious amount of DLC already present for the game ($34 worth on LAUNCH), and 2. fears of the playerbase dying soon. Verdun and Tannenberg are highly rated WWI shooters, but they've been dead for a long time, and this game's price with its DLC and the devs' track record has me kind of nervous about investing time into this game. It's fun for the most part, I'd like to see it have some work done, and I hope it sustains a healthy playerbase longer than the last two games; because $30 for what could be something short-lived is steep. Going to give this a thumbs up for now, although my true rating is "on-the-fence." Gonna sit on this and see if it's worth keeping or refunding.Edit 9/27/22: Looks like the game's playerbase is already dying, which is exactly what I was afraid of and why I preemptively refunded this after all. Per Steamcharts, the playercount was peaking at about 3,500 every day for the first week, but is already at <1,600, averaging more towards 1,300 now. Decent game, mechanically, but not worth $30 if it's going to die within a couple months; I learned after Lawbreakers.

_childDocuments_.review: I think the balance is just right in Isonzo. It's fast paced with quick re-spawns, satisfying gun play and engaging action. There's also a lot of strategy involved, and a good amount of tension brought on by things like being pinned down or even when just reloading. Like when coming face to face with an opponent and you both somehow miss your first shots - Do you whip out your spade and risk going for the kill, try for the bayonet or power through those janky, tense few seconds while you both scramble for cover while reloading your bolt action rifles, wondering who will chamber and fire off their next round first. Class progression feels good, there are a nice amount of guns and extras to unlock without feeling overwhelmed with which class/path to play. You certainly don't feel dominated by high level players, it's a very skill orientated game and I can feel myself getting better every day. Don't get me wrong, sometimes I want to break stuff when I seem to get shot from every angle, or get flanked by enemy players, but the good times outweigh the bad. It's incredibly satisfying calling in a Mustard Gas strike and watching those kills rack up, or seeing an air or artillery strike decimate the enemy and push them back.I suppose my only real criticism, but I completely understand why it's in the game, is the class limitations per match. Having only two officers or one scoped sniper makes perfect sense, but in a game of 40-50 odd players I find myself cursing at low skill players who hog classes like Officer or Sniper, which can easily make or break a match.10/10 would run head first into a cloud of Phosgene Gas again, while pulling on my gas mask as i'm choking for air, firing off my pistol with my ears ringing from an artillery barrage.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm kind of disappointed with this oneLet's start with the pros. It looks absolutely amazing. The sky is bright and beautiful. The smoke effects from guns look great. The blood when you kill someone is a lot more realistic than the other two and makes it feel more gruesome, which fits the war setting. The new mechanics are neat. Mortars and field cannons are fun and building is an interesting touch. Classes are more customizable, which is also nice to see. Unfortunately, that's where it ends for me.This game has a lot of problems. I know a lot of people brush off this complaint, but you die WAY too much. Most of the time when someone says this people argue that it's to make the game more "realistic" so dying a lot is fine. However, I've played both Tannenberg and Verdun, the other games in the series. Those games are more realistic than this one but you die randomly way less. In Isonszo I constantly see teams get half of their players wiped out by artillery and plane bombs. As I said before, the game isn't even that realistic compared to the other two. It's much more arcadey. You can see indicators of where the enemy team is when they're behind walls. In Verdun and Tannenberg you had indicators on the map if you used a recon plane, but you always needed to use your eyes to know exactly where they were. The speed at which you construct things with engineer is unrealistic at best and impossible at worst, plus it's stuck in specific spots so it's not even that fun. Sure, these features are nice, but I don't get why they move in this arcadey direction and simultaneously make it so half of your team gets shredded by bombs every thirty seconds. It's both less realistic and less enjoyable than its predecessors.Overall, I wouldn't recommend this game to most people. If you want a gorgeous game set in this place and time, and you don't mind arcadeyness and dying way too much, I'd say go ahead and buy it. Otherwise, I'd avoid this one. If you want an open WW1 shooter, play Tannenberg. It may have less playerbase but at least you're not exploding every 6 seconds. If you want to play a realistic trench fighting game, then I don't know why you're here, play Verdun. I wanted to like this game really bad, but seeing how it compares to the other two games I just can't really recommend it to most people.

_childDocuments_.review: AVANTI SAVOIA!Patriotism aside, this is probably the most fun I've had playing a World War-era realistic shooter in a long time. Obviously there are some bugs, some of which can also be pretty annoying, mostly with the visuals or making you spawn inside a wall or chair, forcing you to redeploy. That said, the game only launched a few days ago, and so far the devs have put out a number of small updates and fixes, so hopefully these problems shouldn't last. What I personally have a problem with is a particular aspect of the gameplay experience: grenade spamming. The assault class can unlock a set of 3 grenades that are very effective at clearing out objectives and area denial, but because you can immediately respawn with all 3 grenades, taking an objective usually results in a game of "who can throw the most grenades" while officers block your vision thank to the smoke / gas barrages that they had called a few moments prior. IMO, some if not all officer callouts should have longer cooldowns. With that out of the way, I hope to see this game prosper and for the devs to add new content as they patch things up. I mean, if they're going to add a German faction for the battle of Caporetto, they should at least give the Italians some new weapons, and possibly a new MG/SMG, since the Villar Perosa is an extremely situational weapon due to its extremely high firerate but short range, unlike the Austrian Madsen MG, which can even be used at long ranges and packs a serious punch.I do recommend the game, but I'd suggest waiting for more patches to come out. It's very much worth it, even at full price, but there are problems that need to be solved, that's a thing for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: The Jewel of the WW1 series. An unforgiving tactical shooter set in the Italian Alps. The class system is well implemented and every troop type has unique equipment and play styles. From the humble rifleman all the way up to the officer coordinating assaults and support, everything feels useful and well thought out. Objective play is essential and the fighting over them is often at very short distances leading to some really intense moments that can be a lot of fun. The game has its fair share of bugs but they are being ironed out slowly and the game is frequently updated. The only major negative I can think of is that the game currently has a small player base. You will be playing with the same people in the same places a lot, many of them vets of the game, and that can be frustrating if you're new. The game does incorporate bots so every slot that isn't a player is replaced with a not totally incompetent bot which keeps the games feeling alive even when the player count is down. The bots also make it possible to create your own custom matches that still allow ranking up of the classes, reminiscent of Red Orchestra 2. The map pool is also fairly small right now, but there are multiple free expansions in the pipeline that will add new content and maps.It really is a great tactical shooter with a dev team that cares about making a good product. If historical shooters are at all up your ally drop a few dollars just to support these guys and the great games they will hopefully continue to make.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. It's a shame there is such a lack of ww1 games to play, but this is hands down one of the best right next to battlefield 1. It's surprisingly fast paced, despite the extremely fast kill time. The graphics are great, the voice acting is great, the combat is great, and the sound design is impeccable. However, I must say that it might take a while to get used to for people who say, try to play it like cod. If you run around in the open, you will get your head blown off very fast. Literally. The gore is pretty good too. If the game had controllable vehicle combat, it would be my favorite multiplayer shooter of all time, but that title goes to Battlefield 1.

_childDocuments_.review: A realistic immersive FPS that is very unforgiving but also equally rewarding. All of the weapons have the potential to kill you in a single hit. This means you need to be constantly paying close attention to your position on the battlefield and all of the likely areas where someone could flank you at any given time. The audiovisual design fits perfectly with this harsh gameplay since every weapon has a palpable sense of force and impact behind it. Firing your weapon feels like a big commitment which it should since you leave yourself dangerously open whenever you peak out of cover to shoot or throw a grenade. Matches are long drawn out affairs that can last for what feels like an eternity. However, that length is a positive rather than a negative since it gives each team ample time to mount comebacks if they are losing. Every game mode is balanced well from my experience and it is very rare that one team will dominate another team without a lot of resistance. Both teams always have to work hard to get the win.Overall, this game is a fantastic FPS that is very underrated. The punishing difficulty may take some getting used to but the core gameplay is extremely satisfying and riveting once you get the hang of it. I would reccomend this to any seasoned FPS player. Especially fans of the Battlefield series, which this game clearly takes a lot of inspiration from.

_childDocuments_.review: Strikes a good balance between realism and fun. Shooting someone with a full caliber rifle is almost always an instant kill. _childDocuments_.review: Game is fun, and a great concept. I enjoy the gritty gore content and succeeding in capturing a trench or a point is very satisfying. There is certainly a sense of distress and peril. But it still needs a lot of work. Starting the game with the bare minimal equipment and having to level up to even get a second gun option is a bit of a buzz kill. I would love to be able to customize my class a bit better, maybe give actual reason to carry around certain items, such as explosive charges. The marksman class is nothing more than a rifleman, and a scope needs to be available from the start. Sprinting in the game is near nonexistent. Your character runs for 5 seconds and is already out of breath, which doesn't read military soldier to me. Another issue i came across frequently, was the smallest insignificant objects making You unable to go prone, or unable to move or turn. I feel that a soldier should have no problems hitting the deck for sake of self preservation, despite a rock being next to his foot. The hackers are pretty common too, not in a way where everyone is hacking, but you can tell some people are using aimbots. Takes the fun out of it, when one guy has 107 kills and no deaths for example. But on a more positive note, the game is definitely fun. I'm a casual gamer and do not claim to be a good gamer in any sense. I'm average at best, and I just like to assist my team to victory the best i can. I do enjoy the ability to heal teammates and restock their ammo. It feels very real, and the visuals are beautiful. I do recommend buying this game at it's sale price, for you can easily get hours of game play and entertainment. Although, I wouldn't see myself playing this game very often or for long strides. Maybe just to satisfy my quench for a gore filled WWI experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Isonzo

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing Game, I loved Tannenberg and Verdun, and I have been waiting for this game for god knows how long. I will say, this game hits the damn mark, if you loved the other games, you would absolutely love this, they outdid themselves with not only the improved graphics, but the feel of the recoil of the gun and sound design in this game is absolutely astonishing. This game is beautifully made, the maps look absolutely amazing, the gun physics have definitely improved, and honestly, the atmosphere has always been amazing. If you want a great WW1 game, play this, as well as the others (Tannenberg, Verdun) as they are also amazing.

_childDocuments_.review: Really good fun, you can feel how the game has evolved from the games before. Animation and sounds are great and the maps are unique and diverse. I like the healing mechanic (injured -> bandage to almost full -> teammate heals all the way) that incentives teamplay.However, semi-automatic pistols seem to be a little inconsistent in the damage dealt and the airstrike call in for the commander feels a little overpowered and sometimes doesn't full kill enemies.The game has bots that can fill up empty player slots which is a very nice feature to have, and they feel semi-decent to fight against. On that note the player count does dwindle during certain hours of the day but there is usually a match or two ongoing.The game really captures the feel of WW1, be it the guns, the sound, the maps and how the game plays out, but most importantly it's got the style.8/10 would fight over a mountain instead of going around it.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're like me looking for Red Orchestra 2/Rising storm, this doesn't scratch the itch. That's the big takeaway.It's riddled with gripes that overall amount to making it downright frustrating, and missing the polish of something like RO2 did over a decade ago. Things like how choosing where to spawn borders on irrelevant when it will decide to spawn you on the opposite side of the map from where you selected. Not being able to toggle mounting ledges and forced to the moment you get close. Only the attacking side having spawn tickets. Overtime going on infinitely if the point is contested. Grenade kills for progression objectives not counting if you die before it detonates. Or my personal favorite, not being able to cancel reload animations. The absolute best is reloading 5/6 shots in your revolver,  and then canceling the reload animation and trying to fire. It doesn't fire, it starts reloading that last shot you never finished.On a positive note. The game is pretty, the devs do add new content to it and has a roadmap. Servers are still pretty active, unlike RO2/RS. There is fun to be had here, but every time I play it I always end up getting frustrated by the lack of polish. People say this is the most polished of the trilogy, and if that's the case, that's terrifying.
