_childDocuments_.review: Curious to try the new maps, I went back to Isonzo after having played it for some weeks after it was published.Great landscapes, and formidable cosmetics, but I am afraid Verdun was a much more successful attempt to recreate a WW1 battlefield.In Verdun you have 3 lines of trenches for each party, the mechanics are quite simple: if you conquer a line within a determined time, you keep the initiative and momentum, and stay on the offensive. You don't capture the enemy lines, you go on the defensive. No way you can wander around the battlefield attacking the enemy rear if you are supposed to defend. You stay in your trenches, and that's it. If it's WW1, it cannot be Rainbow 6 Siege, CoD, or Rust.  Battlefields are deep (to host 6 lines, 3 for each party), but not wide, and this gives you a sense of density that, again, seems to me better represent  WW1.In Isonzo one party is always on the offensive, you have more lines to conquer with a limit of 300 to your casualties, but the defender can move around the battlefield freely, like in a WW2 or a contemporary battlefield.Trying this game does make sense, especially if you can buy it during Steam sales, but since Tannenberg, it's not WW1 anymore.

I personally would like to see them add a more hardcore game mode where friendly fire is on for firearms, grenades, and call-ins, and the HUD is turned off with only prompts or very limited.My only issues with it currently are two very annoying bugs where you're stuck in hipfire mode with ADS zoom and movement speed penalty after using bandages, and spawning inside obstacles and terrain where sometimes you can't wiggle out at all. _childDocuments_.review: Highly enjoyable game. Strikes an excellent balance between the satisfying gameplay of realistic sim-like shooters ala classics like Red Orchestra 1/2/Rising Storm 1/2, Day of Defeat, Insurgency etc, and the accessibility, functionality and UI of a more mainstream title like Battlefield 1. It's a great leap forward in every sense from the developers previous titles, showing that they are a dedicated dev team that learn from their experience and push themselves to further reiterate and nail the formula. Graphics are impressive and I have to play on Low to Medium on my aging rig. A downside is the lack of dedicated server support/server browser. _childDocuments_.review: Great game overall. The gunplay feels much more like what you would actually have if you were a soldier in WW1 than games like Battlefield 1. The "one shot, one kill" mechanic of this game really means that you play more carefully, avoiding ennemy lines of sight while trying to get the first (and deadly) shot. There might not be as many guns as in other games, but the choice feels weightier due to the realistic limitations of each gun.My biggest gripe wiht the game are the often unpredictable and near-broken spawning locations. It happens too often that you spawn right behind or right in front of the ennemies, which can be frustrating. It's also too easy to spawn right in the middle of ennemy territory, which favours rushing objectives individually, making  the defense of your territory oftentimes absolutely pointless, as there's always a stealthy player slipping through the cracks and then spawning a whole platoon near the objective.
_childDocuments_.name: Isonzo

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I just don't understand it. I never have and I never will. These guys make these awesome WWI games, which admittedly, is a niche market.  They are so perfect. Brilliant attention to detail, historical accuracy, everything is awesome down to the slightest detail. But then you actually play. They implement the most ridiculous, slow, clunky, awkward gameplay.  I cannot emphasize "clunky" enough. It's just so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ridiculous. It boggles the mind. It's like they watched all those sketchy B&W clips of WWI and assumed everyone back then moved in this slow and clunky way because of some low-framerate B&W films. I struggle to understand their logic. So Verdun and Tannenberg at least were tolerable. You could get used to the movement, the reload speed, the mechanics, etc. For some reason, they decided to ramp Isonzo up on the clunkiness and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.  It's even slower than Verdun and Tannenberg. You're walking through molasses. The reload speed is insanely slow. But so are all movement, switching gear, building, manning weapons, etc.  I'm just going to assume their excuse is "Well, it's higher altitude, so you don't have as much stamina."  Or some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.  Doesn't fly. It's trash. If, at the very least, you could move, reload, build, man positions, etc., with the same speed as in Verdun/Tannenberg, it would be fine. Those previous titles' gameplay are still not great, but they are tolerable.  This is straight trash. So do with that what you will. I expected to have the same level of gameplay as Vdun/Tannenbrg. But that's not the case. It's a step down, gameplay-wise, and that is sad. Because this is their most beautiful game yet. The maps and level of detail are jaw dropping. It's an amazing, beautiful game. But when you start to move around in it, you feel like you're stuck knee-deep in ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ mud. That definitely knocks it down several notches.

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly, I wish I could give this a rating, not just a thumb's down, because I'd probably say my experience is mixed, but that's on steam's end.I'm a seasoned Verdun player, been playing since Verdun released, I have a ton of hours on Verdun and Tannenburg, both games are highly enjoyable and offer their own unique ways to play. I'm a huge fan of this series. Alas, Isonzo. Firstly I will start off with the positives: the overall aesthetic of the game is great. Scenery looks spectacular, I like the varieties of weapons (I assume late war stuff is coming later tho lol), and its also touched on a largely forgotten part of the war. I also really like the realistic and historical ways players can customize their individual soldiers, that is probably my favorite addition to the series so far, you should add that to the previous ones if you can. Negatives: its largely game play for me. I have way less fun in this game than I have in the previous two games. Granted its a new game with new features, but even Tannenberg I picked up pretty fast and got comfortable with it, basically a less static version of Verdun.  Isonzo on the other hand, I leave every match feeling more frustrated than satisfied than I do in the other two xpacs. The first thing I noticed is that aiming and shooting feel generally more clumsy and slower than in the other two games. For some reason in Isonzo, targets beyond 50 yards or so feel like much more difficult to take out unless you have a scope. In Verdun, one can get their kill with iron sights at 100 yards pretty easily. Sure there is weapon sway, but that can be mitigated by holding your breath. Doing this in Isonzo feels much less smooth. Even in more close range combat its worse, if you miss your first shot, you're dead. The reload and aim time is simply too slow. If you DO kill your target and his has a friend, you're dead. Most "squad" fights end up just being last man standing, one shot, one kill, one death. Next guy, rinse, repeat. It feels as if we're playing with muskets. After all this I can spawn on any of my teammates I want, or any of the spawn points. I may be the odd man out here, but I do not like the spawn point system in this game. In Verdun, if you wanted to "infiltrate" a side and spawn on any teammate, you had to chose the proper faction, or just spawn on your officer. Here not only can spawn points be captured, the enemy can build them right behind you, meaning AN ENTIRE TEAM can spawn while you're trying to take an objective. What I've seen in most matches is that fights now are entirely focused on holding or destroying SPAWN POINTS instead of the OBJECTIVE, which leads to 9 games out of 10 the attackers lose, because they essentially have extra objectives to hold behind them while simultaneously trying to attack 2 other objectives.  Also, the progression system: not a fan. The unlock system in Verdun was so much better. I had to grind for grenades for ASSAULT class? Even in Verdun the standard beginning loadout came with 1 grenade. Why did you change this? Also, the camera shake compounds all of this even worse. Officers can spam ordinance WAY too fast (compared to Verdun, where they arguably had MORE artillery in that theater) and 90% of the time I spend looking at my blurry screen, only to get sniped from the suburbs of Venice or God knows from where. While I do appreciate the positive aspects of it, the negatives vastly outweigh them and I'm probably go back to playing Verdun here before long. I really like the WW1 series, and I'm want them to succeed and continue making games, but for me personally, I can't in good faith recommend this game as it stands.

_childDocuments_.review: Phew, I played this game a little too much over the last few days and I enjoy it me even more than it's predecessors. First, the maps are fantastic: Up and down a mountain, then crossing a river, then attacking a church all in one map is just epic. I for one enjoy the general gameplay mechanics a lot, although the spawn system would profit from a bit of an overhaul. The gunplay feels good to me. And while at first I wasn't too sure about the sound design, now it feels just right; also I don't feel too shell-shocked after a couple of rounds (as I did in Verdun), that's a good thing I guess.There has been a discussion that some classes could be to powerful: At the moment I don't think the assault class with their machine guns is a problem. But I do think they have too much hand granades. I could do without scopes in the game, but this is remedied with the spotting system pretty well. However, while I enjoy the spotting a lot at the moment, you kinda start shooting below red dots. Idk if that's the best solution.I read a review asking for proximity VOIP, and I must say that I don't agree. I like the comparatively impersonal (and with it immersive) muliplayer experience it is now. I think the game is designed to work well without and it hits the sweet spot for me. Hearing only period correct voices around you is a huge part of the atmosphere and I trade some possible lost tactial potential for that.

_childDocuments_.review: It's taking me back to Battlefield 1. Much more polished than Verdun and Tannenburg - but does need a considerable amount of work. Fair few bugs but the Devs are really on the ball (still early days). What will make or break this game is more free content. More maps, weapons and even classes (no medic??). _childDocuments_.review: First off, I don't write reviews, ever.  Tried it on a free weekend and picked it up an hour later.  I've been searching for years for a game that felt like Battlefield 1942.  This is the one for me.  It's not your typical runner and gunner though.  Nor does it hold your hand when you're playing.  Much like WW1, you get tossed onto the battlefield without really knowing what to do and you will die very quickly and very often.  It's tough, but fun and rewarding when you finally get the hang of it and start racking up some kills\points with your preferred class.  Each member of your team has a job to do and if you don't perform your classes duties, you WILL fail at capturing any objective.  Totally worth the 10 bucks and I'd say worth the full price as well if they can keep up with new updates and getting players to return.
_childDocuments_.name: Isonzo

_childDocuments_.review: A nice sequel to Verdun with updated graphics, dynamic gameplay with diverse terrain. Can be challenging and also very exiting. Especially when both teams are making a desperate meat-grinding push for one objective.One of the most fun games to play and just immerse yourself in the carnage of WW1 on the Alpine Front.
_childDocuments_.name: Isonzo

_childDocuments_.review: Initial thoughts after a few hours of play. Firstly hit registration feels very good, feedback on connecting shots is at a good point. I LOVE that the game does not reveal the location of who kills you, just not way in which this game is not pandering to noob players who need their hand holding with everything. Map designs are astounding, they feel vibrant, cohesive, have good flow with fair restriction and the progression across the maps feels like it has a point and isn't just a random decision. The ability to coordinate properly without having to use voice is a fantastic move.As for classes, they are so well thought out. They all feel like they have a distinct function, with the officer class really shining in how it brings a new method of engagement to the table. Played late into the night on my first day and as the server stated to be populated by more bots as it got quiet I didn't feel that the game suffered too much at all. It was still a challenge and we still had a load of fun.So far, I am very impressed with this game and I highly recommend you try it out.
_childDocuments_.name: Isonzo

_childDocuments_.review: It's nothing much more from Tannenberg than a few more maps and teams uniforms. Therefore it shouldn't cost more than few euros. There is nothing new in graphic, or the game engine, the gameplay is also the same, and it's bad. You can die at the second you spawned, the controls are slow and does not give the real feeling of battle. But the leveling system makes the game a highly adictive and the time consuming grind.
_childDocuments_.name: Isonzo

_childDocuments_.review: This is the most underrated FPS out there. I am very surprised with how much different yet fun the gameplay in a WWI setting is. I do wish there was cross-play between PC and consoles. Some people have said it isn't available because the advantage to PC players. However, I play on PC with an xbox controller and haven't seen that much of an advantage. I consistently go positive in K/D ratio and this is with a full lobby of real players. I very much recommend this to anyone that is looking for a new and challenging FPS experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Isonzo

_childDocuments_.review: I've been looking forward to the release of this game for some time, and I can happily say this is one of the better early 20th century facial hair simulators on the market.There is a good variety to choose from, whether you want to rock the full beard and stache combo of George the Vth, the bushy moustache of Nietzsche or even that little weird stache popularised by that Austrian painter guy. The graphics are pretty decent so you'll be looking dapper no matter what you choose. In addition to the facial hair, you can also add a variety of classy and cool items such as pipes and glasses, and there are also a number of clothing and hats, though these are limited to military uniforms, for some reason.My main complaints though, has to be the inability to change hair colour, and the fact that we can't mix and match beards and moustaches. Several of the styles are also locked behind DLCs. The game is also locked into first-person mode, so you rarely get to enjoy the view of your classy visage.You also get to run around shooting people and calling in artillery, which is a cool addition to top it all off. This game mode needs some work though, all the classes are combat oriented with very little focus on the beards. A barber class that can bring in shears and oil, and construct grooming stations with mirrors in the trenches, is sorely needed.  All in all, it's a pretty neat game that really immerse you in the setting of the era with all its great facial hair. I'm definitely looking forward to see how it grows with further updates.
_childDocuments_.name: Isonzo

_childDocuments_.review: i just got it with no pre expectations and i was absolutley destroying people at the first 10 minutes of playing , its realy easy to play !! the simplicity of the authentic gameplay makes it more addicting / making we want to come back for more. for those looking for a easy to play ww1 sim this is defintly the one !  not only that the more you learn the maps and stragize the game goes incredibley deep in the core mechanics of the rush / control type gameplay  offering you various ways to flank  and outsmart the enemy bringing about crazy engagments , tons of flank routes , endless sniper holds , the list goes on and on .. my hats off to this studio/company, bravo good men
_childDocuments_.name: Isonzo

_childDocuments_.review: A fun historical shooter set on a seldom-depicted front of the Great War, Isonzo sits on an enjoyable middle ground between a hardcore experience (one will be killed in one hit very often in this game) and a more arcade-style offering (such as the mortars, team buffs from some equipment, and call-ins). The devs' passion for the setting shines through in the loving attention paid to the art style.If I had to offer any criticism, it would be that there are some PC-shooterisms in places, such as A/D spamming being an optimal and immersion-breaking way to win gunfights and heavy machine gun emplacements being akin to a flashing neon sign inviting an opponent to fatally click on one's head.Overall, it's an excellent shooter for the money for anyone interested in the setting/period which I would strongly recommend (not least because one of the loading screen tips politely asks for reviews from those enjoying the game).
_childDocuments_.name: Isonzo

_childDocuments_.review: While the aesthetic is nice to look at, I can't recommend this game.Do you want to play a game where the moment you spawn, the microsecond you show up and begin to move you get shot by some unseen blip halfway across the map? Good on you, you're dead and have to wait 20 seconds. Spawn again, surprise! You die. Wait another 20 seconds. Go back to your spawn and move forward for a few seconds and hey! A guy is in a cabin in your spawn area, spawn camping everyone. Back to waiting for 20 seconds!This game is punishing. You make the slightest error and try to hurry up to do ANYTHING and this game will punish you and make you waste the bulk of your time in that ever so familiar spawn zone. Also, seeing as it keeps losing its player-base, only the die hard fanatics are sticking around. And they sure as hell are not going to let you get used to the game. Because misery loves company, amiright?That's part of the game? So is watching paint dry yet I don't remember people paying to wait that out.I can't see jack all when I move, can't even see the slightest figure, but guess what? They can see you and that 20 second spawn timer is waiting for You!You want to increase your class levels and complete challenges? Best make your way to private games with all them bots where their movement is predictable and their aiming goes from delayed to instant laser pointed death. Not to mention nothing ever gets done because bots don't give a damn about the objective! Barely three on it at a time. So even more time wasted!And if you want to complete challenges and see what other weapons they have to offer, you'd better believe you will be spending way too much time bot farming.But hey, let's try the officer, the call orders have to be neat, right? Well guess what! Artillery will do nothing more than skin your enemies knees on a glancing blow but blow you to kingdom come if you're even entering the same timezone. Want to to shoot a rifle grenade? Guess what. You have two enemies between you and that impact zone and you will be the only one dying in that explosion.So, if you want to play camp and wait simulator, knock yourself out. For me: to hell with this game, I'm out. If I wanted to bash my head against a brick wall for 50+ hours I'd play a FromSoft game. Or DOTA.War is hell? Yes, war makes (sane) people not want to go through that again. Well congrats, BlackMill, you got that point across loud and clear. I want nothing to do with your games ever again.

_childDocuments_.review: The more I played this game, the more glaring issues and bugs I noticed and just felt overall disappointed with how it turned out. Coming from Tannenberg and hell even Verdun they're leagues above this game in terms of design and gameplay. Bad things I really noticed:-Extremely useful and essential gear is locked behind a very arcadey 'grind' system, where you have to level up to meet the requirements to then, do a challenge to unlock the specific item. Why not just have it like it was in Verdun/Tannenberg? where soldiers automatically came equipped depending on their role. -Officer is extremely strange/confusing to play, it also seems they've really gutted the officer in terms of actually commanding/giving orders. The *only* method you have for marking where you want artillery/gas or smoke/recon or any support is by a flare gun. The flare gun is interesting as a concept but its incredibly inaccurate and it seems like the support you do call in doesn't land anywhere near the marker. Binoculars are also useless, their only purpose is for spotting enemy soldiers, whereas in Tannenberg/Verdun you could mark attack points/support call ins/etc. Really dumb having to level up and grind just to find out the item you unlocked is limited to 1 thing only.-HORRENDOUS bots/AI performance. The aimbotting and inconsistency with the bots and AI in this game is actually terrible, from doing 180's and immediately headshotting you, to standing on top of you freaking out wondering whether to kiss or shoot you, the bots and AI are truly garbage in this game. -Reload speed of primary/secondary weapons feels *extremely* long, Animations are bad as well. Reloading a revolver or pistol takes ages and god forbid you run out of ammo in a trench or during an assault.-Bullets/rounds/damage not registering at all. Small calibre pistols are notorious. hitting enemies and *seeing* the red cloud, but no hit marker/damage at all. Rifles seem to wound enemies more than killing them, especially at distance which shouldn't be the case at all.-Bad spawns/Getting stuck in objects, spawned in a wagon and got stuck, frequently spawn into walls/floors or right next to enemies.-Bad/buggy sound design, bots make 0 noise approaching your position or when moving. *ALL* the rifles sound the exact same, same with revolvers/semi autos.-Build menu, cool concept but its implemented so, so poorly. Noticed particularly how long it takes to build objects in comparison to the time it takes to destroy them. You could spend 10-12 seconds building a spawn point, etc only for it to be destroyed in 1-2 seconds. These are just bad issues and bugs I noticed, this game needs some serious development before it can live up to its name. Hate to keep comparing to Tannenberg/Verdun but they really dropped the ball with this game which is a total shame as I was hyped for the third installment of these games. Hopefully they can fix alot of these issues but I fear by then the game will have died out as the playerbase is already dwindling only less than a week after release :/-

_childDocuments_.review: Really wanted to love this game, but I feel its lacking many things which made similar games great. I was looking for a 'Beyond the Wire' game-play experience, brutal combat, bayonet charges, chaotic matches and explosions which turn team mates and enemies into a red mist while their ragged corpses fly through the air.I feel this game does a lot right, but it just feels a little bland to me. _childDocuments_.review: A beautifully created game. I wasn't sure about how somebody could make a WW1 game that both leaves you with a sense of trench warfare yet is enjoyable as a FPS. The devs knocked it out of the park! It's easy to come to grips with, yet challenges the team. It can be frustrating at times, but enjoyable nonetheless. And the first time you go running through a smoke screen only to come across a dozen enemy...woah baby. This is the only time I've felt compelled to write a review for a game.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a 45 yo father, probably one of the oldest people playing this game. I am a single father to my Son, who is 14 now. My son got this game for Christmas in 2021 from his uncle, so we installed it on his computer and he started playing. By the end of the week he had 24 hours on this game. This was horrible for me, as it was already hard for me to find ways to spend time with my son, as he is always out with his friends or just watching YouTube. So i decided to make a Steam account and get this game to see if I could maybe play alongside him. I loaded into the game, picked my character and world and started playing but I was stuck on what you where supposed to do. I asked my Son for help and he hosted a game for me to join. I loved it as it was the best time I had spent with my Son since my wife had died. This game has ever since brought me and my son closer again and now we actually spend time together outside the house together as well. This game reminded me that there's fun to be had in everything, and it has brought both me and my Son many happy memories.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, this game is perfect like the 2 previously game, probably god-tier like for Verdun.The soundtrack, the sound, the scream, the chaos, the shake cam, the graphics, just perfect.Thank you for making this WW1 front.The Frontline mode actually reminds me of the good 'ole Battlefield 1 Grand Operations mode, just feels like the attacking side need extra chances to take the sectors.Hopefully that more old modes, especially the Squad Defense in Verdun will make a comeback.I had fun playing that, at least until the playbase getting low or/and hackers, trolls came like in Verdun, but for now I have fun playing it again, not since the Verdun days.Now, lets hope will there be historical events like in VerdunPS: Don't forget the gore, it was great in Verdun, now it's better, and more clear too

_childDocuments_.review: The game is not perfect, but it is very fun:Is a tactical FPS from the creators of Verdun and Tannenberg, still very accessible, full of action, no walking 10 minutes to the objective, i'd say realism in between Rising Storm and Battlefield.Compared to Verdun is, as expected, on a whole new technical level, but quite different in gameplay, with the trenches assault mode gone in favour of a "capture the points" mode; i think the changes make way for a more dynamic gameplay, and the vertical maps add to this factor. Choke points are essentials and the key to victory is bypassing or fortifying those.In this game you fight on the Italian mountains, and beside the aspects already considered you'll also have the beautiful sceneries, very well recreated and marvelous to look at.There is a class system with progression based on challenges that not everyone is liking, but i find it interesting and forces me to get comfortable with every mechanic of the game.Lovely soundtrack, very appropriate, nice voice acting, but the weapons, while sounding accurate, are a little on the weak side, more OOMPH would be appreciated.Devs are releasing small updates to refine an already good release, and there is already a roadmap with more campaigns to come.

_childDocuments_.review: the endings of matches are sometimes rather anti-climatic, rather than letting you fight to the bitter end, the game will just instantly end the match if the attackers run out of reinforcements or if the attackers capture everything, but other than that the game is absolutely amazing. seriously, the fights for the final point when it goes to overtime are the best part.

_childDocuments_.review: Already loving this game, great new mechanics such as building barbed wire, sandbags and machine gun posts. The terrain is really challenging to fight on and it's great to see a less well known theatre of the Great War. As you would expect with this franchise, the weapons and animations are fantastic.If you liked Verdun, you will enjoy this game, the graphics are great and it seems to run really well and has populated servers.
_childDocuments_.name: Isonzo

_childDocuments_.review: Mixed opinions on this game. Now i do like this game first and foremost, i've had hours of fun but it's very different from the developers other games. Now if i had i come straight from playing Battlefield and wanted something a bit more realistic, less machine guns and such, then this game would have been great, but i'm a longtime Verdun and Tannenberg player. It lacks the charm those previous games had. it's so much more fast past and seems to be pushing to be a major competitive shooter game rather than there previous titles. They've added things like microtransactions for cosmetic items and uniforms when in previous games you'd get them for free (Keep in mind the $40 price tag) it's ridiculous and it's obviously gonna piss off long time players who have for nearly 9 or 10 years been supporting them (Talk about the new trend of pissing off fanbases). Anyways, as long as they're bringing in cash they don't care, but this is at the end of the day my opinion, and i'm just pointing out a s.h.i.t.t.y trend in major and growing gaming compainies.Anyways aside from that rant, there is lots of good to the game. Everything from sounds, gunplay, graphics, animations have been improved, and even the AI has been significantly changed. Sometimes i couldn't tell between players and bots. Going back to the features. The older games were clunky and a bit derpy at times, i did like that, but it was clearly not the developers intention, these have all been improved so much. it's much smoother now and realistic. The maps are gorgeous and i love the countdown in the trenches after and before each battle, as well and the first charge. Builds so much more tension. The gore is not so good. it's like Call of Duty WW2. Just red!! that's it. Death does not look as horrific as it did in their previous games when you'd be laying in a packed trench suppressed by heavy machine gun fire laying on dosens of bloodied and mangled corpses. The death just lacks that feel that it used to. All in all i would recommend this game, but i just hope in the developers next game, which would likely be set in Gallipoli and the Ottoman Empire, It's not just a re-release of Battlefield 1 because we all know that is what this game series was not originally striving to be.
_childDocuments_.name: Isonzo

_childDocuments_.review: Major improvements on the previous two games in the franchise, and it has the potential to be one of the best 'realistic' shooters out there. The Rifle play is some of the best I've seen in any shooter before, and the balancing of special weapons (ie. Snipers, LMGs / HMGs) is superb. It is outstandingly realistic and accurate, with some of the most interesting and colourful maps in any WW1 Game. The only problems are: a lack of maps (just 6 at launch), fairly unbalanced maps (ie. about 1/2 the maps have dreadful choke points that are practically impossible to conquer) and - in my opinion - an infuriating multiplayer where you are constantly spawn killed by artillery / MGs, especially on servers with 25+ players. However, I would absolutely still recommend this game. Hopefully the Devs will continue the balancing and improvements, though even in the current state its loads of fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Isonzo

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, Arcadie enough to just jump on have fun and serious enough to learn and have a decent progression, perfect middle group WW1 shooter, very gory, epic charges, one drawback is depending on match it can be tough! getting wrecked a lot can happen and ruin experience but stick with it play a few more round and will have a good match. Graphics are good, sound is good and has depth. gunplay is slow but steady as in steady yourself before you shoot! slow down for shooting is a very important tip. very satisfying on kill.Lots to offer for price and a good fun break game for your friends.

_childDocuments_.review: A seemingly simple difference as a change in terrain, proves to be a striking contrast for what you may expect from a "WWI FPS" game. So long as you don't end up in a match with cheaters, which I haven't had a problem with thanks to many different and populous servers, it's quite a fun and engaging game that I would recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Isonzo suffers from many of the same problems in Verdun and Tannenberg, which is a huge shame. It also improves on those games in several areas.The menu is clunky and it lacks tooltips at key times. For example, there are challenges that give rewards but finding out why some aren’t working is harder than keeping mud off your duckboards. I’m in a game right now and have been given a challenge to kill 100 players while holding my breath—simple, right? Well no, because my tally isn’t being counted, I have no idea why, and try as I might, I can’t find a page that shows me this challenge. EDIT: I never found this particular challenge anywhere in my menu but I did find some of the others—literally hidden within unlabelled dots on the level progression ‘timeline’. Even the Quit Game button is hidden behind another button. Like, why? No user should have to ‘learn’ a menu just to access basic information or functions. Onto the actual game. Bots will shoot you through terrain, hip-fire you from miles away, shoot you while aiming elsewhere, spawn from seemingly impossible places and kill you cheaply. In contrast, some will stand around doing very little. Their animations as they climb over and into objects are sometimes clumsy and they can briefly teleport around making it hard to shoot them as they drop into a trench, for instance. The bots constantly repeat the same stock phrases and generally form a conveyor belt from their spawn points waiting to be killed or waiting to John Wick you. They use fixed machinegun emplacements and either don’t fire at enemies at all or fire ineffectively or simply bugger off in the middle of a fight. And there are many such minor, rather pointless annoyances that really shouldn’t exist. If you enter an animation for cutting barbed wire, setting up an MG, destroying an enemy resource—for instance—you cannot look around to watch for the enemy so you end up staring at the ground for ten seconds, hoping you don’t suddenly die. As the engineer class, setting up defences seems pointless as the enemy cuts through them in seconds. Mortar challenges are frustrating. Similar to Verdun, there is no resupplying of ammunition, other than through the rifleman class which is supposed to provide spare rounds to teammates—bot riflemen NEVER do this so unless you have some empathetic humans in your game you will not have many bullets to play with. You cannot fix and detach bayonets. Footstep audio is very badly done—one enemy nearby will sound like several, very close, and in all directions at once. This is awful when fighting in buildings. On the subject of sound, the screaming you hear does not emit from any casualty I can ever find and is simply an irritating part of the audio. Similarly, your character will receive a ‘snap’ from a near miss and flinch: this is all good immersion until you realise, like the screaming, it’s random. You cannot stop the animation playing when doing things like switching to loading rifle grenades. If you move in a certain way when reloading a clip into a rifle the rounds will literally vanish—another stupid aspect inherited from Verdun. The bandaging mechanism is really poor—an arterial wound must be bandaged, after which, hey, you’re absolutely fine.But there are good points, too. I hated the maps on Tannenberg but have enjoyed all of the maps I have played on this one. They are beautifully drawn with sweeping, mountainous vistas to take in while you dodge grenade fragments and shrieking colleagues. I love the weapon sounds, the ‘feeling’ you get from firing and the attention to detail. In fact, every weapon is great, though boringly few in number (the Italians really just have the Vetterli and the Carcano as their long arms). Other than the above, the sound design is quite good and the explosions and foley aren’t bad. The graphics are good enough, though very poorly optimised indeed, at least for my machine (which plays Baldur’s Gate 3 fine but cannot get a smooth FPS on this for some reason).This is all the same type of thing that tarnished the otherwise excellent Verdun and the lesser Tannenburg, and it’s a real shame the developers haven’t fixed those problems.So, like Verdun, I don’t recommend buying the game at full price: it is an acceptable shooter to pass the time if you can ignore the faults—but it is a massive missed opportunity. The devs were told all of these problems during the two previous games, and continue to be criticised for them on social media now, and it’s clear that Verdun could have been one of the greatest FPS franchise games of all time if it had been tidied up and then built upon, but they chose not to listen, which is a shame. The player-count for Isonzo has already dropped off sharply and, to be honest, I will dabble with this and then just go back to Verdun for my FPS hit.TL;DR: good for under £5, good for those with lower standards, fun at times, not the white whale.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is written on the 15. of September and as such represents the state of the game shortly after its launch.Overall I would recommend this game to WW1 enthusiasts that are looking for an authentic shooter set in one of the more overlooked fronts of the conflict. It strikes a good balance between a tactical and an arcade shooter, whilst offering the less commonly seen challenges of mountain warfare. I'd give it a solid 8 out of 10 and with the addition of more content, be it in the form of weapons, maps or game modes, I could see this game climb to a 9 out of 10.For those who are interested, below will be more detailed thoughts on this game:Isonzo has taken the concept of both Verdun and Tannenberg and successfully merged them together. The core of it being, that one team defends a series of sectors, with the other attacking them. Objectives in these sectors are either to take control of a key position or blowing up a marked objective within the zone. As one team advances with limited tickets, the defenders have infinite tickets available. On top of this, the defenders are given a short grace period after losing a sector, which they can use to construct defensive structures, such as barbed wire to block the attackers advance, machine gun emplacements as well as cover. While on certain positions either team is able to build light artillery, on some maps even field cannons, I have usually seen these being used more by the attacking team to support their efforts.Due to the nature of the games setting, this being alpine warfare, most maps incorporate verticality into their design. While it is a great idea, it comes with its own host of problems. On some maps the defending team is capable of firing into the attacking teams spawn at the first contested sector, which can be an issue as the attackers have a limit of 300 tickets per sector. Another issue for me is the variety of weapons. While the present rifles, represented through various patterns and iterations of them, are accurate to what would have been used in this theater of war, it would be great to see more variety in the available firearms. It is important to keep in mind though, that what could be added in the future is limited though, as the developers are striving to be as historically authentic as they can.Other wishes I personally would like to see come to the game would be the following:1. Having more maps and/or game modes would likely help the games longevity. As fun as the current "Offensives" mode is, it likely would be good to offer more options for players to change it up every so often.2.  Considering how it currently feels like a decent portion of the time in a match is spent being under artillery fire or aerial attacks, as well as the high frequency of gas attacks, it might be a good idea to increase the cool down timer officers have to use these abilities.3. The ability for Steyr M95 pattern rifles to eject a partially loaded block. While it is a lengthy process, it can be done on the real rifles by opening the bolt and pressing a button at the front of the handguard. This button releases the tension on the internal magazines spring and ejects the block out of the top. If this is also a feature on Carcano rifles, it would naturally be necessary to add this ability to them as well.

_childDocuments_.review: Today when I walked into my economics class I saw something I dread every time I close my eyes. Someone had brought their new gaming laptop to class to play Isonzo. The Forklift he used to bring it was still running idle at the back. I started sweating as I sat down and gazed over at the 700lb beast that was his laptop. He had already reinforced his desk with steel support beams and was in the process of finding an outlet for a power cable thicker than Amy Schumer’s thigh. I start shaking. I keep telling myself I’m going to be alright and that there’s nothing to worry about. He somehow finds a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ outlet. Tears are running down my cheeks as I send my last texts to my family saying I love them. The teacher starts the lecture, and the student turns his laptop on. The colored lights on his RGB Backlit keyboard flare to life like a nuclear flash, and a deep humming fills my ears and shakes my very soul. The entire city power grid goes dark. The classroom begins to shake as the massive fans begin to spin. In mere seconds my world has gone from vibrant life to a dark, earth-shattering void where my body is getting torn apart by the 150mph gale force winds and the 500-decibel groan of the cooling fans. As my body finally surrenders, I weep, as my school and my city go under. I hate gaming laptops, but like Isonzo.10/10 would play Hunt Battlefield, Battle Showdown.... again.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: Review was made based off of the free-play weekend around Armistice Day 2023So far, I believe this game to be the best authentic WW1 experience on the market. From what I've played, the gameplay feels rewarding and is overall well-balanced once you approach it from the right perspective. This is NOT Battlefield 1, so don't expect a heroic clutch last stand or any crazy  weapons or tactics. Approach this game as though it's real life; embrace defensive gameplay, move with your team, and always assume a sniper is ready to take off your head the moment you poke out of cover.I can recommend this game to anyone who holds a genuine interest in history, but not to anyone looking for either a milsim Squad-like or casual Battlefield-like. There will be unbalanced units, such as officers being able to wipe multiple riflemen with their handgun or an assault trooper running around with a Madsen LMG or rifle grenade launcher, and you will be stuck with poor loadouts for much of the early-game. Even regular grenades are locked behind several levels of grinding. Enjoy the setting and embrace PTSD, and you will enjoy your time with Isonzo! I could anticipate putting in 50 to 100 hours in total for any based WW1-setting enjoyer, but it's definitely not for everyone.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game, I have a lot of fun playing it, and you can play against all players, players and bots on both sides, or set up your own private "custom" game with just you against with bots on both sides.  If you are looking for a bot based match already out there find the "custom" games and select games with just 1-4 players in the game since the rest are bots so you have a challenge of facing a few players to win a battle but you still have bots to fight.I was a Rifleman in the US Marine Corps and a combat veteran of the Battle of Fallujah (hence my steam name) and I have a history and anthropology degree so I can tell which game are more realistic and not a cheesy FPS. The game play even with players are more about storming trenches and taking objectives rather than seeing players jumping up and down like in some MMO FPS which adds more realism to playing a WWI game.The customization though not highly detailed like an RPG is still really good which adds character and the uniforms are time period set but they are also dirty and not always fresh like they came straight from supply so it adds a personal and grizzly side to it.Plus the weapons are original to WWI (almost all bolt action rifles, revolvers, and pistols) so no steampunk or crackpot, history breaking submachine gun or assault rifle in other other "historical" period games. I saw online people hate bots but I love playing against them and they are still difficult and a challenge in a standard game PLUS if you do not add extra options playing against bots still gives you achievements and XP!!!!  So no more never ranking or getting anything because a handful of players horde everything.I would recommend turning the Gore setting to Ultra since it leaves the bodies on the battle field which make it more realistic to a battle as well, so the game is not "clean" and more attrition based. In any given battle in the game like 600 to 1,000 deaths can take place since the attackers have 300 lives at first then it goes back to 300 more lives if they reach the two objectives before and the defenders have unlimited respawn so charging in will not hurt your team.  Attackers try to take objectives usually one destroy an objective and one capture objective point while defenders try to kill all 300 before the attackers take the objects to prevent another 300 respawn. It is respawn points that need to eliminate so you don't have to kill every last player especially if a player is hiding somewhere you do not have to find them.The class system sometimes feels limited just because you cannot do everything in any class but it forces people to play their roles a lot.

_childDocuments_.review: Isonzo is a very immersive game set in one of the lessor known fronts of the First World War. If you've enjoyed Verdun and Tannenberg, you'll definitely love this game. If you've enjoyed Battlefield 1 there's a chance you'll enjoy this game though you will need a lot of patience for it as you will die a .  None the less its a great game I'd recommend to any fps player or someone who enjoys W.W. 1 history as the developers spent a lot of time making the game as historically accurate as possible while still making the experience enjoyable.10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Isonzo

_childDocuments_.review: Been waiting for this game since it was announced, Iv played a bit of tannenburg before but not alot, but my expectations for this game were high, and it delivered amazingly. The huge maps and intense battles are so much fun, and the unique classes are nice. Every time you get into a match you have different strategy each time, which makes the gameplay very immersive and replayable. And as someone who loves history, I love that everything is realistic, the gameplay, models, maps, everything. Would highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Isonzo

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying this; i expected worse after reading the negative reviews.Its the first game i bought from this Dev and the WW1 Series. Always found the Italian Conflict in the Alps one of the most interesting clashes in history of War, so naturally i was very excited to try this game out since its rather cheap (Reasonable Price for Early Access tho).I'll give you a quick pro's and cons list down here:+Gunplay not stiff+Maps are gorgeous and big, making matches go up to 30 mins+Sound design is excellent, explosions feel punchy and the ambient sound along with the music create a authentic atmosphere+Hitboxes and netcode are great as far as i noticed, no complaints+-My game crashed within 10 minutes in my first match-Graphics are okay, altough performance on stronger machines could be better imo (rarely hitting 100 fps)-Bots that fill up player slots have aimbot and are literally unkillable unless you snipe them from 100m-Had a bug where the entire server could not kill each other (maybe they simulated the Truce of 1916, i dunno)Keep in mind this review is from when the game is in its  stage, the devs are working hard and keep patching the game. There's not a whole lot of weapons to choose from but many things will get added along the way.
_childDocuments_.name: Isonzo

_childDocuments_.review: Actually fun.Except the times when you get stuck in a wall. Or a chair. Or a car. Or when you want to heal but it kinda doesn't, so you just bleed out.  Or when youre laying down and wanna move 1 inch to the right but the game says no, because theres a pebble the size of an orange.But other than that, yeah. Actually fun. Ggo get it, they will fix it eventually
_childDocuments_.name: Isonzo

_childDocuments_.review: As an avid Italian, I am constantly seeking titles which accurately represent my beautiful my homeland. I need not look any further than Isonzo.With its beautifully rendered graphics and immersive audio you truly feel teleported the beautiful alpine villages of my mother country. You can almost smell Mama Trampolini's  wafting through the air.But then, whats this? A thudding on the horizon? Gas shells land in the village, replacing the smell of sweet sweet spaghetti  with the foul stench of chemicals and the vomit of your dying comrades. Mama Trampolini is no where to be found.
_childDocuments_.name: Isonzo

_childDocuments_.review: While the game is decent, unfortunately it has many issue, the most glaring is that outside of free weekends the game is barely played by anyone. Another major issue is that you can't squad through steam with your friends, it seems it is an epic exclusive feature and steam only lets you join the match, the game can still put you into another squad or autobalance you into the enemy team. Movement is janky, fundamentally the system is good, it doesn't allow you to clip into objects while crawling, but it is implemented in a way that will simply not allow you to crawl up an incline or over small objects. Weapon handling is also bad, particularly the bipod kept ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ me over by auto deploying over everything, preventing firing.

_childDocuments_.review: Semi-hardcore, WW1 shooter. I liked the other games they've made, Verdun and Tannenberg, and this is a definite improvement with many QoL features you'd come to expect from higher production games.Like Rising Storm 2 but WW1, Holdfast but an FPS, Beyond the Wire with players, the hardcore mode sequel to Battlefield 1. Sense-shattering levels of violence.

_childDocuments_.review: it's blooming fantastic , optimisation is unreal for a game this beautiful, between-  130 - 160 - 200 fps throughout , everything on ultra, added tessalation , sharpness , all the added features basically , and with the 20 dead players still laying in the same trench with me that iv'e been sitting inn for like 10 mins , haha, the game play is super smooth , the sounds and immersion is incredible,  the pure intense moments of pushing and capturing enemy trench positions and then either falling back again or taking more ground from your enemies. love this experience , huge respect and love for this game and the developers. thankyou.

_childDocuments_.review: Classes are fun, maps are good. The quest objectives for the unlocks also make you wanting to jump back in. There are not many things at this moment imo that need balancing. If this game keeps getting content added, receive regular updates, and create a more efficient anti-cheat, this might quickly turn into my GOTY 2022.

_childDocuments_.review: I write this as I sit in a forward dugout somewhere in the Dolomites. The constant shelling is the only sound that fills the air, some of us even laugh when one of those shells hit a poor young kid from Northern Sicily. The Austrian's tried to push our lines but we held firm, but I feel as with every charge, I get the sense that some of my old school boy friends are no longer with us."Cigarette?" One lowly private says to me. I look at him, you can still see the youth in his eyes. He reminded me of me, before the war, before all this. I hear a faint whistle in the distance followed by the shouting of the men in forward trenches.As the crackle of machine guns start up, I look at the privates outstretched hand, seeing the cigarette he offered me. I smiled, took it out of his hand and lit it.
_childDocuments_.name: Isonzo

_childDocuments_.review: Played on the FTP weekend, lest we forget...However my mind has been made, I do not recommend getting this game at FULL price maybe for 15 bucks sure.PROSThe music is a nice touch, brings back the bf1 vibes.Historical accuracy and just details in general are sorta spectacular, fingerprints on the gun barrel, there are obviously some things that aren't 100% accurate after all it's a game. Good Map roster, and a decent amount of weapons to choose from.CONSIt does look a bit grainy at times, gunplay feels weak, there is no oomph to the rifles. Another thing is the developer has made 2 games in the past like isonzo, tannenburg and verdun, which are deader then this game due to no more support. That brings us to our next issue, there is only maybe 3 servers worth of people, the game is small. The unlocking mechanic for new weapons or items in general is pretty annoying especially when most of the roles are taken immediately so you will never be able to unlock it in a fair time. If you want to hop in to a ww1 game and have fun for maybe 20hrs tops then sure get this game, but even after a short time of playing it I got bored quickly, the progression is just too slow, and you can't blame that on skill issue because i was top 5 in the team with 30 kills, and yet I unlocked nothing.
_childDocuments_.name: Isonzo

_childDocuments_.review: A buggy mess, kept falling through the floor, the leveling up system and unlocking weapons has taken several steps back. It makes picking a class redundant for a majority of new players when only the Officer Class has a major difference in weaponry at the start of the game. Maps are too rocky and hilly (which I understand for the setting) but it makes it incredibly unfair and boring to play if you can just perch on the top of a mountain and one tap people. Play Verdun or Tannenberg instead.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who studied the history of this region's war for my Master's dissertation, and as a re-enactor and someone who cares deeply about WW1 representation, this is the game for everyone, its for everyone who was introduced to WW1 back in 2016 with another popular shooter as much as it is for the hardcore history buff. _childDocuments_.review: I was following this game's development for a year and i'm sad to say that this game is a disappointment that could have been so much better.The developers seem to care more about putting out cosmetic DLC than to put out actual gameplay content. The new expansion adding Germany is an utter disappointment to say the least. This game is an embarrassment to Verdun and Tannenburg. The biggest issue for me is the progression system. Verdun and Tannenburg had a career point system that let you choose what you wanted to unlock but Isonzo picked up the Call of Duty system and it ruins the immersion experience as you are trying to do the specific things needed to unlock a new weapon or tool. Please do not waste your money on this game.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the better and more authentic WW1 shooters out there.Weapons are heavily restricted to what were used in WW1, so you are not going to find like 20 guys running around with SMG spraying bullets everywhere.  Most weapons can kill you in 1 shoot.  Making gameplay more intense and slower at the same time.  In the game there are classes with each class having some specialized weapon or a set of skills.  None of the classes really dominate one over another, with each class needing the support of each other, but not to the point where solo play becomes impossible.  Certain weapons are locked behind a leveling system, but it is pretty easy to grind through.With the game being set on the Italian front, you get fight on beautiful mountain sides of Italy and Slovenia.  The mountains also give this game a lot of verticallity.  Which really helps emphasis the difficulty of mountain warfare at the time.One of the good things about this game, is that you can play it both online and offline.  If you don't want to deal with the competitiveness of PvP you can always make a private server and just fight bots. The bots are pretty good, but lack the ability to play some of the more complicated classes like an officer.  Plus the exp earned in PvE counts towards your level in PvP. The best part of the game with each new expansion no maps, weapons, or factions are locked behind a paywall.  The only thing they charge you are for cosmetic DLC.If you are really into time period FPS or looking for something different from you usually fast-paced modern shooters than I say this game is worth the buy.

_childDocuments_.review: Isonzo as it stands is another run of the mill shooter with hardly any improvements to show from its predecessor's that came before it. A barebones experience for the casual player is at best is what I would call this game.Pros: Map are done well for the most part, they play well in the mindset that these coming from an attacker's viewpoint a nightmare to assault. People who enjoy mostly playing defense will have an overall better experience. I sadly can only give this as my only pro as of writing this review....Cons: Just to keep it simple with a list I've written down.-Ingame VFX needs definite work.-Sound quality improvements much needed.-Gunplay is mediocre.-Challenge/Progression system needs being looked into to improve player experience. It feels more forced then welcoming.-Animations are slow and wonky.-Bugs galore.-Static gun placements or really lack of thereof.-Animations just don't seem to flow altogether.-Bugs..Tons of bugs.

_childDocuments_.review: Isonzo is a game about the Italian front of WW1. The weapons, uniforms, equipment, and maps in general are detailed with care, and the research that went into these aspects of the game are superb. It does require significantly stronger specs to run compared to previous games of the series, however that's due to the engine upgrades, as well as the bigger scale of the game itself. There are, of course, issues that were present on release, and are still present at the time of writing this review, however I'd like to clarify that  The devs have worked hard and are still working hard to fix all of the issues present, however there is something that's hindering them; Data collection. The devs need people to report bugs to them so they have more data to look through, since their patching work takes up all of their time, as well as work on their new expansion.Now, would I suggest purchasing this game at it's current state? If you have the money, specs, and are interested in the setting and are willing to help the devs fix bugs by reporting them, go ahead. If not, it's alright if you wait for a sale or for issues to be fixed.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been a veteran of the WW1 Game Series since the release of Verdun. After playing the game for about two weeks, I have to say that this is the best installment in the franchise yet. The Italian Front during WW1 was one of the most interesting fronts that is rarely talked about compared to the Western Front or even the Eastern Front at times. So I was very excited to see this would be our next front to experience.First, the historical accuracy of the game as a whole. This is by far the most strongest point of the game. Literally everything, the uniforms, the weapons, maps, etc., is nailed down pretty much perfectly, which is why I love this game series. I always appreciate it when developers pay attention to historical accuracy, especially when there is no sacrifice to fun game play. M2H and Blackmill have always done this since Verdun, and prove that you can have a historically accurate game about a certain period, while also being a fun game. As for the gameplay, they have improved it a lot since Tannenberg and Verdun. I think this new system of six classes with so many players for each class instead of multiple different squads of four players works much better. The way squads progressed in Verdun and Tannenberg just felt like a grind to get to certain styles of uniforms for the squad, requiring you to play for a long time before your squad level could get to said uniforms. Instead for Isonzo, You have your own personal account level as per usual, and each class has its own level progression. from this class progression, you get stuff such as new weapons, gadgets, and what you could call sub-classes(which are basically perks, as an example you can unlock sniper perk for the mountaineer class, which gives you 33% more zoom when you aim down sights). From the account level, you get certain character cosmetics unlocked, which I will get into soon. The new mode fits perfectly for the style of mountain warfare. Gameplay mechanics are pretty similar to Verdun and Tannenberg, but with some slightly better things that improve balancing, such as the ability for the only two officers for each team to be in charge of support abilities and orders, the ability for players to construct defenses(or offenses), only limiting one scoped rifle for the marksman for each team(along with limiting two handheld automatics for assault for each team too).Then we get to character customization. This was a fun move, as the customization goes far beyond from the very limited customization(if you could even call it that). If you really want to have fun with this, get all the DLC for the most customization. I know It's pricey, but to be fair the developers didn't have any DLC for the game series until now. The customization includes uniform style for each class, and from that you can customize faces, headgear, facial hair(the best part), and accessories(pipes, cigarettes, glasses, etc.) for each uniform style.I'd say the only negatives are bugs, which include the voice chat not working, and some other minor ones that don't effect my experience at least. I noticed some people complaining seriously hard about these bugs, but as I said earlier, they don't really affect gameplay that much. But either way, I'd imagine that these problems will eventually be fixed soon by developers, as it's only been two weeks since release.My conclusion, buy the game is you're a huge fan of the WW1 genre like me, or if you just need a new game to kill time. The bugs aren't that serious to me at least, but if you're one of these stuck up people when it comes to that, give it a few months if you truly think they'll bother you that much, But as for things I hope they add, I want to see more maps, weapons, customization, bug fixes, fixed voice chat. I would hope that they add the Germans too, as they did send some troops secretly to help the Austrians, among these Germans being a young Erwin Rommel. It would at least give some variety instead of being just Italians and Austro-Hungarians.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the FPS game for people who don't like jump/drop-shotting and people sliding over buildings to 360 no scope you from halfway across the map. The weapons hit like a truck, the gunfire is loud enough to deafen you, the mounted weapons are terrifying and the air support makes allies and enemies alike scatter for cover. The maps are varied and detailed, with thought out cover and choke points that always have one or two side-entries to keep you on your toes.Any free slot in the lobby is filled with a bot, which range from "Dumbly stand there while you shoot them" to "Terrifyingly headshot you as you come around the corner" to keep the game feeling chaotic and full even if you're playing solo for the practice. I couldn't recommend this game enough, especially at the price it is.

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome Game, Great addition to the WW1 Series. I Recommend all 3 games but this one brings a bunch of new things and elements to the WW1 Trench Fighting Genre. The bots, offline mode, and cosmetic DLCs without malicious micro transactions make this game a 5/5. You can level in offline against bots and you can use those levels in a online match. Getting it while its on sale is highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: With Hell Let Loose being my main WW2 shooter, Isonzo is now my WW1 shooter and a nice more casual alternative to Hell Let Loose. Casual in the sense of a kill feed, hitmarkers, much more linear and straightforward map design, quicker matches feeling like less of a commitment and less reliance on teammates. I like the guns, the maps, the mechanics and classes. Just a very solid shooter all around.

_childDocuments_.review: Isonzo is a superb tactical shooter that improves upon its predecessors in numerous ways. As always, it feels good and intuitive to control. But mastering the moment-to-moment action won’t lead to success unless you combine those skills with sound tactics—this is where the game truly shines. Isonzo introduces new items, new environments and much free-er load-out customisation, all of which contribute to its non-transitive complexity. The game facilitates team play, mainly through the ability to spawn on one’s squad members, and rewards—but does not force—cooperation. There’s various ways you can aid your team, which creates lots of niches for you to explore. This is encouraged by the environmental diversity you fight in. There’s only six maps at the moment, but their average size and the variety between sectors compensates for their modest number. They’re beautiful as well—too bad there’s little opportunity to admire the scenery mid-battle! The progression system is a tad bit slow though. It’s fine for unlocking weapon variants, some of which seem outright better than others judging by their stats alone—although the difference isn’t stark—but I have yet to unlock light machine guns and specialised melee weapons after close to 50 hours of playing each class equally much. That’s not right, actually: I have played the officer way more than anyone else. Leading and supporting your team via call-ins is a deeply fulfilling experience, and I swear a good officer makes all the difference. There were some notable bugs at launch, but aside from spawning half inside walls every now and again, and the infamous ghost soldier bug that lets people sabotage forward spawn posts and arm bombs while otherwise non-existent, it’s a polished experience. The community’s good too, and that’s invaluable to the overall experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Isonzo

_childDocuments_.review: Ferocious Alpine warfare will test your tactical skills in this authentic WW1 FPS. Battle among the scenic peaks, rugged valleys and idyllic towns of northern Italy. The Great War on the Italian Front is brought to life and elevated to unexpected heights.

name: Little Orpheus
detailed_description: The year is 1962 and NASA are trying to put a man on the moon. In a remote corner of Siberia, a Soviet cosmonaut is heading in the other direction. Comrade Ivan Ivanovich is dropped into an extinct volcano in his exploration capsule, Little Orpheus, to explore the center of the earth. He promptly vanishes. Three years later he emerges claiming to have saved the world. He has also lost the atomic bomb powering the Little Orpheus. He is taken to a top-secret bunker deep below the Ural mountains to be debriefed by the fearsome General Yurkovoi, a man so frightening even Stalin won’t buy him a drink. The General rolls up his sleeves, fixes Ivan with a steely glare and say “So... where have you been comrade? And where is my bomb?” And Ivan looks him right back in the eye and says “Well General, you might not believe what happened to me, but I’ll do my best. Because it happened like this...” Join our bold yet hapless hero as he explores lost civilizations, undersea kingdoms, prehistoric jungles and lands beyond imagination. Gasp as he battles the subhuman tribe of the Menkv and escapes the clutches of dreadful monsters! Cheer as he triumphs over impossible odds and brings socialism to the subterranean worlds! Little Orpheus is a technicolor side-scrolling adventure game inspired by classic movies like Flash Gordon, Sinbad and The Land that Time Forgot. The platforming and light puzzles solving of Little Orpheus are simple enough for casual players but rich enough for seasoned adventure fans. If you’re a fan of old school family blockbusters, want a rollercoaster story that’ll take you to the Earth’s core and beyond, or are just in some need of ideologically correct entertainment, join the most unlikely hero to hit PC and consoles on an adventure beyond belief. With stunning visuals, brilliant acting and a world-class score, Little Orpheus is a subterranean epic you’ll never forget. Comrades, to the center! Features A stunning, colorful world remastered for PC with hi-res textures, new moves and animations, enhanced graphics and lighting effects, and more. A gripping story full of humor and adventure by the award-winning masters at The Chinese Room, creators of Dear Esther and Everybody’s Gone to the Rapture. Award-winning vocal performances and a world-class music score by BAFTA-winning composer Jessica Curry and Jim Fowler, enhanced for PC in 5.1 surround sound. Includes the bonus 9th episode A Rush of Onion to the Head and the Lost Recordings Mode.                                                            A HERO WILL EMERGE!

Includes the bonus 9th episode A Rush of Onion to the Head and the Lost Recordings Mode.                                                            A HERO WILL EMERGE!
short_description: This definitive edition of the multiple-award-winning hit by master storytellers The Chinese Room is remastered for the big screen and includes all bonus content of the original. A HERO WILL EMERGE!

_childDocuments_.review: As a huge fan of LIMBO-like games, I was excited for Little Orpheus.  Alas, I was big let down.Pros:- Really nice art- Quality voice acting- Fun and engaging story (for most of the game)Cons:- Absolutely mindless gameplay. There's 1 puzzle in the entire game, and it's near the end of the bonus chapter.  Just full of run-right, slow chase sequences, and switches to pull for 3 hours.- This game does not respect player time.  Forces 2 playthroughs to 100%, and the 2nd playthrough is IDENTICAL to the first...  collectibles are all on main path, no secrets, no reason to force this second playthrough except to bloat playtime.- Cutscenes are unskippable (does not respect player time, especially on the 2nd play!!)- Controls aren't particularly responsive.  Changing directions is slow, no coyote time.  Could have been more fluid.- The ending to the story is a huge letdown; the entire plot turns out to be the McGuffin.  Give me some sort of resolution.- This isn't the game itself...  but one of the achievements has been broken for months, it got fixed for 3 days but the devs broke something else much worse in the process, and then reverted the build instead of fixing everything.  So you can't even 100% it.  All this with NO communication to the players; minimum on Discussions, no Announcements or Patch Notes.  I place these issues on the publisher over the developer, but they make the game look bad regardless.Overall, if you just want a cool game to look at and a (mostly) enjoyable story...  this game is decent enough.  But stay away if you want to 100% it and get all achievements, because the game doesn't care about your time.  And as of writing, one achievement is still broken, making 100% impossible.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Orpheus

_childDocuments_.review: I've seen people leaving unfair bad reviews for this game based on their gameplay expectations, I can't recommend it but this is not a bad review.The game is absolutely story driven and gameplay is super casual platforming, in my case it's a palate cleanser of sorts between more demanding games. I expected that having played Planet Alpha.Now, the reason I can't recommend LO as much as I enjoyed its lighthearted story and beautiful environments and soundscapes is because the story absolutely drops the ball at the end. It's like you are awaiting for something awesome to happen and instead you get the worst possible closing ever.I can deal with downers and stories that don't end like I wanted to as long as they have some impact. In a game where it's all there is to it... it just feels like wasted time, as much as you may have enjoyed the ride.So if this game appeals to you give it a try, as long as you are prepared for the meh ending you'll probably have a good time.

_childDocuments_.review: , a former Apple Arcade exclusive, finally makes its way over to PC with mixed results. While the game is visually striking and for the most part looks gorgeous, you can immediately see how its hampered by originally being an exclusive game to mobile devices as  provides very little platforming and puzzle solving challenge (the puzzles in particular are incredibly weak and don't require any brain power to solve). This was no doubt hampered by the original mobile device touch controls. With a wacky narrative that includes dinosaurs, flying mechanical fish, the innards of a whale,  goes out of its way to be quirky but with mixed results. While I enjoyed seeing what crazy scenario the game would throw me into next, sadly it fizzles out towards the end with a very anti-climatic ending that feels abrupt and doesn't give the story a satisfying conclusion . The game is also incredibly short featuring nine episodes that last 30 min each. Towards the end of the game (particularly episode 8), I experienced a lot of glitches and bugs which forced me to have to shut the game down and restart in order to resolve. Ultimately  ends up being a mixed bag and proves yet again that games can't skate along on good looks alone, their needs to be something of substance there to hook players, and sadly this is where  falls flat. Recommended but only when on a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah, totally agree with some other reviews here, Little Orpheus isn’t really a puzzle-platformer. No, after some levels it actually feels more like a walking simulator with loads of dialogs, extremely easy jump’n’run/hiding sections and an abundance of checkpoints. Also all levels pretty much play the same event-wise. But this isn’t a bad thing per se in my opinion. I mean, the highly retro-inspired, weird story, the awesome graphics (though with maybe too much chromatic aberration) and the humor are definitely its strengths. So I actually enjoyed a lot of the hours we (namely me and my wife) played. Yet after finishing it with 100% achievements, hmm, I’m not totally sure at which point it overstayed its welcome for me. Probably it was the necessity to replay EVERY level for achievements, because only AFTER you finished one, you could access the alternate version in which you could gather the orbs with the production designs. Truly boring, the levels were exactly the same, and especially as you couldn’t skip cutscenes or dialogs (and hearing all those again at some point got on our nerves). Seriously bad game design if you think about it. Add to this a somehow annoying and unnecessary end boss shmup fight with over-fickle controls in the bonus level. Nevertheless, I think playing the game once definitely yields a positive experience if you’re into hilarious and original stories, and aren’t expecting a challenge. But if you’re an achievement-hunter, better be sure what you’re getting into. Oh, and before I forget, some last advices. For 4K-TV users, you might have to use the borderless windowed mode, because fullscreen botches the screen size (at least happened to me). Also if you replay the bonus level for the orbs, Laika’s comments are suddenly translated (as kind of an easter egg), so you might want to listen to those again then for completion. And last but not least, better play this title bite-sized because of the general repetition of all game elements.

_childDocuments_.review: Little Orpheus’ landscapes may be colorful but its gameplay is a barren wasteland. As a platformer, it is boring and repetitive, with no memorable sequences across its four hour runtime. The story is more like a bad version of Groundhog Day, as a waffling comrade Ivan recounts his many adventures that lead nowhere in search of a nuclear device. Maybe Little Orpheus works better in bite-sized chunks that are easily forgotten between dreary commutes. Playing more than a few episodes at a time is akin to torture, and if Ivan had been forced to play his own game, he would have cut to the chase a lot sooner. If you are desperate for a colorful platformer, check out the Trine series or even Planet Alpha, because there is no pot of gold at the end of this rainbow.
