_childDocuments_.review: Berserk Boy is a wonderful Mega Man Zero/ZX clone with the gameplay gimmick borrowed from Luminous Avenger iX games where you have to dash into your enemies to tag them. However, I felt like this gimmick is underutilized in Berserk Boy since the stages barely have enough enemies to keep the combo flowing, but that’s like my personal wish while it’s quite obvious that the game isn’t designed around combo-ing onto enemies since the stages have different layouts that make use of different Berserk Orb abilities. There is, however, a way to keep the combo flowing and that is done by collecting energy orbs that are floating around that replenish your combo meter as well as your energy meter. On top of that, they add up to your score which determines your final rank at the end of the level. The energy meter depletes when you dash or use different Berserk Orb abilities and keeping it full is a crucial part of the gameplay. It fills back up if you wait around for like 2 seconds, though. Except for this energy meter, you have another meter called “Berserk Meter” that fills up when you hit enemies, then you can use it to unleash the ultimate attack of any Berserk Orb which is quite useful. As you progress through the game, you gain new forms through new Berserk Orbs you take from the bosses and each of them has their unique skill sets. You have to make use of their unique abilities to progress most of the time and that’s a good way of presenting their abilities to the player. You can also buy new skills for them from Quinn who is located in Resistance Base. The whole story revolves around these Berserk Orbs. There’s an antagonist who tries to harness their powers to attain his goals which usually come down to world domination and as you can easily guess, the story isn’t that mind-blowing. It comes down to a cliché story where you have to stop this guy from achieving his goal. The protagonist, Kei on the other hand has a special ability that can merge with Berserk Orbs without any force.  There’s also a talking bird called Fiore that helps you along the way who also plays a huge role at the end. There’s also a counterpart of Roll from Mega Man called Dizzie who dons the role of navigator but also comes down to help you with combat too when the moment calls for it. Kei is originally a teleporter who can teleport anywhere but chooses to navigate through the stages for gameplay purposes, of course.You can rescue other Resistance members you find in stages, collect Berserk Medals to unlock the ending and go for S ranks for achievements. The stages are usually long and make good use of Berserk Orb's abilities which is a good design in my humble opinion. You also get to unlock EX Stages after rescuing every Resistance member in each stage. I personally don’t have any problems with the game itself, but my only complaint is that the sprites are a bit big and some of them look off, but nothing that will take your joy away. The soundtrack is wonderful and iconic, I immediately fell in love with it. And if you’re wondering about whether it’s metroidvania or not, no. Most of the stages are linear, but some of them require you to take different paths. You could say that some of them are semi-metroidvania. The ending sequence was also blood-pumping with that new form and QTE stuff! A perfect Mega Man Zero/ZX clone with a great soundtrack and a wonderful level design with lots of forms to choose from! Some stages are semi-metroidvania, but most of them are linear. If you’re familiar with Luminous Avenger iX and Mega Man Zero/ZX games, Berserk Boy won’t disappoint!
_childDocuments_.name: Berserk Boy

_childDocuments_.review: This game is alright but it doesn't feel like a fully finished game. I feel like if they make a Berserk Boy 2 it will be really solid but this one just isn't it for me. The level designs range fun and interesting to just a boring slog. The Berserk Attacks feel weak, useless and not fun to use at all. I really only ever wanted to use the lightning suit as it felt fun to use and the rest of the suits while visually appealing felt way less fun to use.A few changes I would like to see if they make a part 2.1) Larger Screen view, I felt like I had to do too many blind falls that would result in me taking damage.2) Better Berserk Attacks, I saw no reason to use any of them as it felt like they did nothing to the bosses.3) More Currency, despite completing the game I felt like I never had enough money to buy most of the upgrades. Rescues and Badges should give a larger chunk of money.4) No more complete 3 stages and then the enemies invade the ship. The first time was interesting but every time it happened after that it was just annoying and felt like padding. Maybe if it served the plot and why we were going to each area or a reason to back track to levels to get parts after the ship is damaged of something would be alright but as it is now it is just bland and repetitive.5) Skip the cut scenes after the first viewing, I know I can press start to do this but why not just have it not play after you view it? I mean you could add it to a gallery mode or something to view them again later but it made me not go do any revisits or collectible hunting after completing a level which I normally would do.6) Give an option to turn off voice acting in the game. Lighting Justice is annoying to hear after the 10th time. Plus characters voice lines don't help much with boss fights or to enhance the talking segments.8) Boss battles need less of them popping up with the ground to damage me as they return to the screen. There were several times indicators would display which was nice but then there were times the boss would jump off screen them come back on the screen through the floor and damage me without anytime to react.7) Spike Chasers should have an arrow on them indicating which way they will go, most of them you pass through and they chase you but then you get to some and they fly right at you instead. Not super annoying after the first encounter mainly just me being nitpicking that choice.I feel like if you make a sequel to this game with some tweaks and improvements it will be an amazing game but right now this game for me is a 6/10. The visuals and lightning suit were so damn impressive but there are lots of things that marred my experience which makes me not recommend this to others.I also did complete the game but I will not be 100%ing the game as I feel no reason to do so.Do understand that this is jut my opinion and you are free to take it or leave it as you please.
_childDocuments_.name: Berserk Boy

_childDocuments_.review: You had me in the first half, but most of the latter content is genuinely painful to play through. This is due to a combination of issues that become increasingly apparent as you play, especially if you play on retro mode like me. Firstly, the bosses in this game aren't very good. Most of the bosses are just extremely easy and have repetitive choreography, with the exception of two that are only hard due to poor choreography mixed with very particular hit boxes. They weren't even the final boss, just bosses around the middle of the game, one of which was a sub boss rather than the main boss of the zone. Meanwhile, the fight with Genos was one of the easiest to beat in the game. So the difficulty definitely doesn't scale the way you'd expect it to. The same could be said for the level design, the difficulty is mostly easy but you'll randomly encounter a stage that's frustrating and just feels out of place from the last few levels you played. Speaking of the level design, it seems that levels in each zone tend to overcompensate for whatever power you last acquired. This wasn't too big a deal, up until the last 2 powers, which both made it very apparent this was an issue. When I have to switch from one power to another for just a very small segment, then come to a complete stop just to switch back to the one I was before, it really ruins the flow of the gameplay that was seen earlier in the game. Not only that, but the powers themselves are very mixed in terms of their abilities. The last 2 feel especially limited in comparison to the earlier ones, to the point where the only time they're worth using is when you're forced to use them (or when you just feel like flying past the BS in one of the oddly scaled levels I suppose). It's very disappointing to say the least, it doesn't really get much better than the first power. The second power is okay, but the hit box during attacking makes it very easy to take damage and the charged attack doesn't work consistently. The 3rd power would be a lot more useful if the ranged attack didn't change when you jump. The 4th is the worst for attacking and is only really useful for its flight, which only really comes in handy in levels built around it. The 5th is okay for attacking, but uses too much power to make it worth using over the first 3; it's really only essential when forced upon you. Another issue I had was with the checkpoint system. You're able to teleport between checkpoints when you're in a level, which can be very convenient for finding collectables. My issue is when you beat a level, the checkpoints aren't saved. So when you go back to a level with a new power looking to collect whatever you weren't able to before, you actually have to play through the entire level again. I eventually gave up on trying to collect everything right away because of this and just decided to play through normally and maybe go back to collect everything if I liked the game enough. Which I really tried to like this game, especially since a very close friend gifted it to me. I also really enjoy SAGE each year, so I was happy to see the game actually made it to release. I at least made it further than most players, stuck it out long enough to beat Genos but didn't feel motivated enough to finish collecting 50 medals to reach the true ending. Although I can't really recommend it myself, I hope the game is a decent enough success to help fund their next project!
_childDocuments_.name: Berserk Boy

_childDocuments_.review: There's just problems with the core gameplay, really. The power switching and range of powers each form gives you aren't quite as seamless as they'd need to be for the game to really shine. There's also just not...enough WEIRD stuff. Like your inspirations here are very obvious, both the X and Zero games put weird features in a lot of their levels that were unique, or outright strange. This needed that - and no, having the levels designed around using a set of powers doesn't count. Setting is...the setting needed more definition. It felt a bit like there was an attempt to steal Zero's setting and scope, but with none of the work done to establish the setting and circumstances. I mean, the base layout having that elevator is pretty clearly an homage, right? But it's hollow. There's really nothing to DO in the base, except for visit the only two rooms that have any significance. Moreover, why is what appears to be the only governing force called the Resistance? What are they resisting? Where did the things they're resisting come from? You need to establish these things. Even just an opening text scroll would help.The padding with the medals at the end was also pretty bad - especially since the medals do nothing else. It would have been better if the medals could be used to acquire special upgrades of some kind RIGHT from the start, motivating the player to want to collect them. The platforming is actually really good, and there's a really strong flow there with the electric power set. It's just that...a lot of the other elements of the game can't live up to that standard, and the electric power is the *first* one you get. I dunno. I think there were a few issues with this that kind of broke it, but it was really close to being a great game.
_childDocuments_.name: Berserk Boy

_childDocuments_.review: A fun throwback to the glory days of action platformers. When I first saw the trailer I was reminded of the Mega Man X series back on the SNES and, while it isn't exactly that, I wan't far off. You don't choose from eight different robots, but instead are thrust into a tale of a defensive force fighting against a dark force while a talking bird befriends you to put a stop to Genos and his quest to obtain the berzerk orbs at any cost possible. You unlock new powers (mostly elementals) upon finishing the boss of the act, which come into play in a metroidvania sense by backtracking to rescue more civilians caught in the crossfire. Sadly (at the time of writing this as maybe it exists later in the game) there are no hidden upgrades to find. Instead you collect resources and spend them at the lab to acquire new attacks, additional health, etc. While not bad, finding some of these in the stages or perhaps as rewards for getting that last hidden civilian that needs a boss power to reach would make getting stronger more rewarding.As of the time of writing, this title is an absolute blast. I put it down, I find myself coming right back not long after. I you dig retro 2D action platformers, this is a must.

_childDocuments_.review: Sadly...I really wanted to like this game. The demo was fun, but I did find the demo a bit lacking. Although I put that to the side thinking, "surely it's a demo, there'll be more to come." Then I got the game...and saw the demo was basically the first 2 levels. Was kind of annoying to play all this again, when it seemed like that data could've been saved/transferred over. As a big MMX/Zero/ZX fan, I found this game kinda boring. Slower movement, kinda one-dimensional combat (berserk base form being the best one for combat), and the bosses were pretty boring. I started straight on retro mode, and it wasn't a challenge at all. So I'm sure the other mode is much easier. The OST is great and fun to listen to. The art style, eh...not so much. It has the look and feel of a knock-off, like commissioned on deviantart or something. Not a big fan of any of the character designs. I gave it about 1.5 hours to see how far I'd get through, and that's about as far as I want to go. When you've played a game like Gravity Circuit and then come to this, it's pretty underwhelming. Could be a good game for someone getting into this genre, but not so much for seasoned veterans looking for a challenge. Hate to say I'll be refunding mine.

_childDocuments_.review: Stellar game.  Short, fun, and very well done.  Megaman X/Zero/Azure Gunvolt style game with self contained levels and a similar plot, for what little plot there is.  Most of your time is just spent playing, and that's a huge point in it's favor, and every part of said play is done very competently.  There's a lot of things to go back and search for and replay for 100% if that's your thing, and the potential for self-contained challenges and speedrunning is very, very high.If you enjoy the X/Gunvolt/Zero style platformers with some cool movement abilities and a very steady and enjoyable challenge, I'd wholeheartedly recommend picking it up, and if you're a platformer speedrunner, this game has a very serious amount of potential!My advice to the dev:Axe the resistance base defense missions.  They add nothing, they're tedious and boring, and the game is only better without their inclusion.  The story isn't strong enough to make them plot strong, and playing hide and seek in a big, annoying hub world sucks.  Frankly, I'd reconsider the hub world too...that really only works with a really strong plot.  Those things are hated by tons of gamers for a reason, and the X series just had stage select for the same reason.  We want to play, not hold walk.  The quick travel is a good bandaid...but it's a bandaid to a problem that doesn't need to exist, push to shove!Flame suit needs a total redo.  In a game where contact damage is your biggest source of pain and getting hit, a melee combo that launches you into your enemies is a big ol' no bueno.  Maybe give it a whip..?  I dunno, something.  But contact damage nerfs it into uselessness.  I used it once, got hit by contact damage, and went "whalp nope this thing is benched forever."  I wasn't wrong.Final level is both heavy on "wait" mechanics and sparse checkpoints.  This can be annoyingly frustrating.  In the future, I'd add more checkpoints in between portals, but more space between the portals as well if wait mechanics will be so prevalent.  It won't interrupt the flow of a casual this way, but the long, grueling ordeal test of knowledge it's meant to be will still be very present for the retro/hard players.Once you have the flying suit, the ninja suit is no longer relevant outside of combat.  Any room where the little bars appeared, I just went flight mode and flew through, only stopped by the kunai gates.  If the intent to fully force those zones, you'll need more common gates.  It also seems, a few times, that while designing challenges, you kinda forgot you gave us a flight power with 20+ seconds of flight.  While it's an amazing powerup...sometimes it can cheat the system.  Not a huge problem, but something to keep in the back of your mind, look over some of the later rooms and go "why wouldn't I fly through this room..?"
_childDocuments_.name: Berserk Boy

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked Mega Man Zero/ZX, then you'll like this game, and should buy it. Like the ZX games, there are multiple forms that you can swap between, and you can quickswap on the fly. Once you get all upgrades and get more comfortable swapping between forms the gameplay becomes fantastic. The music is also excellent, as Tee-Lopes was the composer for this game.While the gameplay is tight and the music amazing, there are a few negatives that I'd like you to be aware of. Biggest one is every interlude "stage" is just running around the base killing mobs.It even reuses the same dialogue. This happens after every set of stages so you're repeating this boring mission five times. What makes this suck super hard is that the interludes were some of the best parts of the zero games. Every MMZ fan remembers the "stop the missile" mission and how badass that was. Instead of epic memorable moments like that, you just get padding. That being said It also helped that MMZ had a clearly defined, powerful, antagonistic force so that things like "stop the missile!!" could fit narratively. This moves into my next point... Berserk boy unfortunately suffers from pretty unremarkable writing which to be fair, is still a problem most indie games face. I'm not saying it's bad, but it's pretty unmemorable. I didn't really like any of the human bosses, and honestly thought the main villain, Genos, was kind of a bum. It didn't help that the game has mediocre voice acting(sometimes cringe), and issues with boss characters having overlapping voice clips.Then on the level design front it's a little heavy on kill rooms which I dont mind too much since the forms are fun.Anyways I still heavily enjoyed the game since I love Mega Man and any games that are inspired by it. I'm just the type of reviewer that likes to focus on letting people know potential shortcomings rather than going in depth about what's done right. As I said earlier, if you enjoy Mega Man at all, you'll like or even love Berserk Boy.

_childDocuments_.review: To the point======================A solid Megaman X homage with more then a few stupid endgame descisions that keep it from being great.Good Stuff=====================- The core gameplay of the 'normal' suit, which is dashing and then doing a follow up projectile, it pretty great. It adds a wonderful element of speed to what is traditionally a more 'slow' genre. Once you unlock the double dash a lot opens up and the game becomes even more dynamic with its movement and keep the combat fresh.- The OST is fantastic and really captures the spirit of the games of the era incredibly well. There are more then a few fantastic tracks across the entire playtime. - Most of the critical suit functions, like the red suits ability to drill through stone, DON'T need you to shift back and activate automatically when you reach certain environmental triggers. This helps to lessen the mount of manual switching you need to do and is a great quality of life improvement.Bad Stuff======================- The other suits, outside of the need to use them for critical functions, never really seemed that necessary. From what I can tell the bosses don't have weaknesses in the traditional sense and the basic suits 'dash and shoot' mechanic worked fine on every boss so there was never a need to use them.- When you beat the game you get effectively nothing, no ending, no credits etc, just a maybe 15 second interaction with the bad guy claiming he'll be back.  In order to 'finish' the game you need to collect all Berserk Medals from each map, 5 in total. While it would be a cool idea for a 'true' ending the fact that you need it for even the basic ending makes the whole thing a tremendous chore. Compounded with the fact that...- ...there's no map in this game! It's nuts to think that a game that wants to do Megaman Zero style exploration in between missions can't even provide you with a stage map to make your life a little easier. The stages are fairly winding normally and I'm sure if you wanted to sit down with the idea of making one, it's probably not too difficult, but damn, who wants to do that?- Everyone in this story barely feels like a character. I know this is not a heavy story driven game but hell, I feel like each character had maybe a 1 paragraph introduction that they decided to drop right before launch because who the hell are all these forgettable people? - The EX stages, which you unlock when you rescue all the hostages in a stage, really have no reason to exist. There is zero incentive to do them and mostly, they appear to be time trials. It would be nice if you got absolutely anything for completing them.- The voice acting, which I'm fairly certain is made to sound bad on purpose (We must stop Docta WyWee!) kind of sounds like it was recorded through a seashell, even with the bad acting the lines themselves sound pretty brutal.

_childDocuments_.review: A Love Letter to Classics Like Mega Man Zero!Berserk Boy is a true gem for anyone who grew up playing titles like Mega Man and, especially, Mega Man Zero. From the very first moment, it’s impossible not to notice the influence of action-platformer games from the Game Boy Advance era. The pixel art style is stunning, with fluid animations and vibrant colors that bring the game’s world to life.  The gameplay is where Berserk Boy truly shines. The fast-paced action, unique transformations, and responsive controls made me feel like I was back in the golden days of retro gaming, but with a modern twist that keeps everything fresh and exciting. The boss fights are challenging, the level design is well-crafted, and the electrifying soundtrack takes the experience to the next level.If you’re a fan of platformers with intense action and a touch of nostalgia, Berserk Boy is a must-play. It’s the kind of game that not only respects its inspirations but perfects them in an incredible way. Highly recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: It’s as much of a Metroidvania as Mega Man X is. It’s more about isolated levels with extra pockets of areas for abilities you get later on or shortcuts rather than something completely new.Berserk Boy is a fantastic game that focuses on fun. Slightly inspired by Mega Man (and also made by fans of that series), it comes with its own set of ideas with a focus on hypermobility. While the story isn’t its Forte, it still manages to lay the loose groundwork for its lore. You can get a little bit more of a glimpse by talking to the NPCs within the base. This isn’t necessarily a bad thing, as the focus lies in the gameplay and helps in giving it a fast pace. Just don’t expect any character arcs, as the characters are more or less what they appear to be. The gameplay is quite different from its peers, as it tries to place a minimum number of limitations on the character. The Ability Gauge depletion is modest, and the regeneration is quite fast, especially because the blue gems not only give you money but also recover the gauge. This puts you in a position where you can GO BERSERK close to in perpetuity. The level design is made with the current progress in power in mind, which means there will be times where you have to switch forms. Mega Man “Buster Only” purists might frown a little bit at this, but it’s certainly not a dealbreaker.From what I’ve seen in Modern Mode, aka Easy Mode, with infinite lives and weaker enemies, the game can pose some challenges within the levels and boss fights, but none of that goes into unfair territory. It took me about 5h30m for a straight playthrough without going for the optional EX missions and keeping the collecting to the minimum of 50 Berserk Medals. On the other hand, Retro Mode comes with limited lives, and enemies have more endurance. The latter will force you to readjust your combat strategy because they will require you to hit them more. The Shield enemies that could be defeated immediately with a Berserk Thunder Drop (in the air down+jump) in Modern now require an additional attack. These small changes will make a big difference in the overall approach if you’re not going to dodge them.It also rewards exploration a little bit more because of the extra lives distributed throughout the levels, which obviously does not exist in the Modern Mode. The visuals and audio are excellent. A lot of work was put into the sprites and the animations, which gives it some additional oomph as each transformation comes with its own set. Even the enemies are no slouches, as they even get hit animations that help bring your attacks to life.On top of that, it comes with a strong soundtrack that manages to bring the spirit of the 16-bit era to the present. I guess this is no surprise when you have Tee Lopez’s hands on it. Personally, the music on the first stage left a strong impression. Is it close to Mega Man X’s? Only time will tell… It is quite catchy, though! Obviously, it’s not flawless. There are some inconsistencies with the markings of pitfalls, the rewards for exploration are rather inconsequential, and there’s some mandatory backtracking alâ Sonic Unleashed of collecting medals to access the final mission. Some would say that it lacks replayability, but then I’d have to take a look back at Mega Man X and ask the question: Do you need a reason to revisit a fun time? Berserk Boy is quite a labor of love and appreciation for those who paved the way before it. I guess the most remarkable quality about it is the lack of a reason not to revisit it. As in, there are some times where you want to go back to one or another game, but some specific part makes you say, “Nah, don’t have the nerves for that," like DMC4 Beyblades and Dice or Mega Man X4 Speeder Bikes. A quality that circles us back to Mega Man X, which doesn’t have this issue either. Yes, Berserk Boy does have two autoscroller/Shoot’em Up segments, but those are done in a flash. If you’ve watched some footage and played the demo, that’s exactly what you get. So if you like what you’ve seen or/and experienced, then there’s no doubt that it is a game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Berserk Boy

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game. I'm a big Mega Man fan, and I feel like I'm supposed to be the target audience for this as a Zero / ZX enjoyer, but it just has too many faults to it to be truly enjoyable, for me.Pros+Movement with forms is generally pretty good.+Some decent animations and sound design+Good main hero design.+Swapping power movesets on the fly is fast and feels good.Cons- Having to go back through levels to get stuff you missed is REQUIRED to beat the game. It's not optional. You cannot beat it without doing this. I was ready to praise this game for having linear levels instead of the messy interconnected ones in ZX, but BB found a new way to disappoint me by just having locked gates everywhere until you come back with more forms.- Levels blend together, lacking strong identity or memorability in a world. Not only that, but a lot of the tilesets look too similar. No part of the level design stands out as good or inspired in any way.-Speaking of re-used assets, some of the bosses are the worst part of this game. Waiting around to hit them while doing very little damage is such a pain.- The UI is messy. The level end screen in particular is jarringly bad and takes me out of the game every time I see it. Really could have used a revamp before release.- Collecting orbs to get upgrades doesn't feel good at all. They have a distinct lack of feedback, are far too numerous to truly matter, and the area where you get your upgrades is stuck in the HUB instead of in your pause menu. I feel like having customization options instead of straight upgrades would have worked in this game's favor instead.Unfortunately for Berserk Boy, Instead of learning from other games like the Zero series and Gunvolt and improving upon them, it just shallowly copies them and doesn't know how to do its own thing. It's not a bad start for a dev, using your inspirations to make your own game, but Berserk Boy really needed to be put through its paces before release, and it just screams unfinished and unfocused to me.5.5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer. I received this game for free.TL:DR - Berserk Boy is phenomenal. If you like 2D retro style platformers this is a must play! + Gameplay is really smooth and responsive especially on controller.+ Takes influence from classics like Megaman Zero and Sonic but adds it's own flare to it. Especially with some nice quality of life changes.+ There's a number of different forms available all with their own abilities and styles. Some are good for movement while others focus on packing a punch. + Retro mode for folks who want a bit of a classic challenge with a lives system and harder enemies (Big Kudos too for telling folks up front there's no achievements tied to that mode)+ The pixel artwork is gorgeous to look at. Really detailed and vibrant with each level adding more to it. + The SOUNDTRACK is epic! Tee Lopes knocks it out of the park again. Each set of levels has their own theme and variations on that theme within the levels themselves. Some retro style but not chiptune. It just rocks. ~ There's a moment in the game that I'm unsure about yet. Will update once I'm passed it and thought about it some more. ~ The story is there? Not bad, just nothing special. But I don't play these games for the story. The gameplay is where this game shines! No negatives so far!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an absolute TREAT for any platformer fans, or fans of good games in general. After playing through it on Switch and re-buying on Steam, I have some thoughts on why this game is amazing, and I'll get into a bit of them here!First, the movement. It's so snappy, fluid, and immensely satisfying to play - you can tell that a ton of work and iteration went into making it feel as good as possible. To me, the best mark of a good platformer is how good it feels just to move around, even when nothing is really happening. Berserk Boy absolutely aces this. By combining a bunch of different elements from similar fast-paced action platformers, Berserk Boy ends up feeling very unique, whilst not feeling any less exciting and dynamic than other games of this type.The music is absolutely fantastic, which should be no surprise if you're familiar with Tee Lopes' other work. Given the aesthetic of the game, you'd expect the music to be similar to Mega Man - which it definitely is at parts - but you quickly realise that Berserk Boy has a fascinating musical identity of its own. The most striking example of this is the track for the Abandoned Labyrinth stage, which has a funky four-on-the-floor rhythm with tons of varied percussion instrumentation -- choices that you may not expect from this kind of game. It ends up works perfectly, and just makes the game that much more of an engaging experience! The compositions themselves are absolutely solid as well, my personal favourite being Sky Fort stage. Aside from Tee, there were also additional arrangers on the project (Hunter Bridges, Jonny Atma, Andrew One, Anton Corazza) who absolutely nailed it as well. I didn't realise who did what until I checked the OST credits, the arrangements just work so well as Act 3 songs!The graphics in this game are absolutely GORGEOUS. I'm struggling to think of ant game off the top of my head that look as good as Berserk Boy. Despite the relatively high pixel resolution for this style, every single pixel feels intentional and important, and it all really lends itself well to the fact that Berserk Boy feels like a supremely polished labour of love in every aspect. The backgrounds are lush and incredible to look at (my favourite is Frozen Temple), the character animations are full of life, and oh my god, the attack VFX particle animations are just SPECTACULAR. The way everything blends together and flows is just so so satisfying to look at and experience, and is a huge contributor in how good the game feels to play. The level design is another place where this game really shines for me. With how chaotic and fast Kei's moveset is, I didn't really have a concept of how levels would even be approached in this game, but was pleasantly surprised with how everything is balanced. The difficulty curve is very fair, and the final levels are such an amazing challenge that are so good that they left me wanting even more of them! One aspect of this game has a huge positive effect on the level design that I did not expect at all at first. Despite Berserk Boy including the ability to take abilities from defeated bosses (that everyone is likely familiar with from Mega Man), the fact that you don't get to pick your own level order ends up completely transforming this mechanic. Since the game already knows which abilities you've picked up along the way, it can start throwing ability-conditional obstacles into levels as you play. Since you're constantly acquiring new abilities, this makes absolutely sure that each level feels fresh not only from the contents of the levels themselves, but from how it feels to control the game itself. These abilities also don't use up any extra energy, so you could theoretically do 90% of the levels with whatever ability you want -- this freedom is extremely refreshing and it's just so much fun!As a huuuge lifelong fan of platformers myself, I can say with full confidence that Berserk Boy is more than worth anyone's time. So much genuine heart was put into this game, and it shows through every corner. Please support this masterpiece!

_childDocuments_.review: Berserk Boy was a pretty good time with fun level design and an amazing soundtrack by Tee Lopes, though I do have a couple reservations with the game. The mini bosses and main bosses were decent fights, but I had issues with a couple of them. There’s this turtle mini boss in... I think the Sky Fort acts? It retreats into its shell to throw bombs and shoot lasers, and that phase lasted longer than I would have liked. I had a similar problem with Mine Buster. He curls into a ball and slams the ground a few times and is invincible while doing so, and he also disappears from the screen to send pillars your way. Again, a bit too much waiting around for my tastes...There are multiple forms you unlock as the game progresses, reminiscent of Mega Man ZX. They were all quite fun to use! Lightning Justice was a great all-around form with a useful dash for both platforming and combat. Flame Drill was fantastic in those rooms where you’re locked into a gauntlet of enemies, with the uppercut move in particular shredding through flying enemies. Ice Kunai’s kunai throw was a decent ranged option, but my favourite move was the dash that lets you move back and forth to continuously damage the enemy. Not the most efficient, but it was cool :)Soaring Wind was really good for platforming! Perhaps too good? There were times when the levels would call for Ice Kunai’s air dash chains or its ability to hang on to moving ledges but I was like ‘nah, imma fly over it’. I think some tweaks to the level design would ensure that Soaring Wind doesn’t completely steal the show in that regard. I didn’t find it the most useful in combat though, so maybe it’s fine the way it is? Mine Buster was my go-to form for combat once I unlocked it because its bombs were quite powerful, and very spammable when upgraded! Poor Genos didn’t stand a chance...Speaking of upgrades, I did notice that they can be a bit expensive. This can be a shame for people who want to go deeper into the game’s combat and what each form has to offer, but understandably can’t be arsed to grind. I was eventually able to unlock everything through my level revisits when backtracking for collectables, but it did take a while. Reducing the prices would do wonders here. On the topic of collectables, there was one design choice that struck me as odd. Saving each resistance member counts towards your completion total immediately, but this does not apply to the medals. You have to reach a checkpoint to cash in any that you collect. In other words, if you die with medals before reaching a checkpoint, you lose them and have to go back for them. This can be especially annoying in the later levels such as the Sky Fort acts.The incentive to saving the resistance members is unlocking the EX stages, which are fun tests of skill and speed. As for the medals, well, things used to be very muddy. Collecting a certain number of medals is required to actually beat the game, but before a patch earlier this month, I believe you needed 50 of these things... out of 75! There’s no indication beforehand that the medals served a purpose, so this unfortunately soured people’s experiences with the game...Now the required amount’s been reduced by a lot! That was great to learn because it shows that the devs do listen to player feedback. With that in mind, I’d be very excited for a sequel that irons out the flaws I mentioned in this review. But there’s still a good time to be had in Berserk Boy, enough for me to give the game a recommendation!

_childDocuments_.review: The best possible description I can think of for the game is "Mega Man ZX with some of the unfortunate fat trimmed". It's really interesting playing a Mega Man style platformer with a linear stage progression, as it lets the abilities you pick up along the way build on each other and the complexity of the level design can grow along with them. Berserk Boy manages to do this without making juggling all of your many abilities feel cumbersome. It's becoming a bit of a cliche for me to play a new game with a Tee Lopes soundtrack and think 'wow, this might be his strongest work yet!'. I did it with Shredder's Revenge. i did it with Penny's Big Breakaway. And, for a third time in as many years, I am doing it with Berserk Boy. Absolutely masterful production and melodies that have been stuck in my head nonstop when I'm not actively playing. There are some minor nitpicks, and if there were to be a sequel or future updates, I would hope to see them ironed out. - It would be nice to have a way to disable the transformation animation when you're changing forms with the right stick. I end up using the shoulder buttons to switch forms more often because it's faster. - I wouldn't hate a few more transformation pads for the ice form when you're just doing sections where you're grabbing onto poles. There are a few sections where one of the challenges is switching in midair to the water form after using a different ability and I would agree those should stay the same, but for regular platforming sections I think it would help keep the flow. - I agree with the folks who have said the upgrades are a bit too expensive. I would go even further as to say I don't think gating them behind a money grind really helps the experience for me at all. It would be cool to see some sort of arcade mode type experience where each form's abilities are fully available from the jump. Overall, it's been an excellent ride, and I am very pleased with the whole experience. Here's to much success for this game and whatever the team decides to do next.

_childDocuments_.review: Beserk Boy gets a big thumbs up from me. I've been playing though this game on Steam Deck and it seems like a match made in heaven.The current trend seems to be for every pixel art style 2D game to be a sprawling Metroidvania. This game has a more traditional level structure where you have to get from A to B with some branches to collect special pick-ups. These levels can be selected from the HQ hub and replayed when unlocked. You'll want to do this as you unlock new suits as you defeat the end of area bosses. This makes the game tighter and compact and makes it easier to pick-up for a quick play and to speed run levels.Each suit unlocked is distinct and has pros and cons in different situations and the controls are tight and responsive for each. I felt in control at all points and if I took damage or died, I felt like it was my mistake and not a control issue.My final comment would be the soundtrack. Tee Lopes is credited as the composer and the music lives up to his usual extremely high standards. I think good music can help elevate or detract from a game and this soundtrack definitely elevates it. If you've made it this far, it probably goes without saying but I'd highly recommend this game to most people. Especially if you enjoy platformers of old but with modern QOL features and enjoyed games like Megaman X and the original Sonic games.

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly - "Berserk Boy" is a breath of fresh air. Immediately upon opening the game and seeing the beautiful art and the vibrant colors of the starting screen, I knew I was in for an amazing time."Berserk Boy" follows the story of Kei and his companion Fiore on a mission to collect all the Berserk Orbs. From the jump, the first Berserk Orb you get allows you this fluidity in game play. The linearity of the game allows for some incredibly unique experiences and forces you to utilize all the tools in your tool kit. There are moments where the game becomes challenging, but never daunting.  The occasional voice acting is an added plus.I know many others, myself included, have been waiting for a game in this style and format for a long time. _childDocuments_.review: Game's definitely got those tight controls and combat that people are used to from the genre. BUT Berserk Boy deviates from, and, in ways, surpasses its inspirations with just how fast paced it makes that formula.Your bread and butter attack starting out is an 8-way dash that goes practically halfway across the screen. Good for practically everything, it gives you a very fluid, fast and reckless feel for whatever you do, as your attack, speed boost and dodge are all one and the same. I could go on about how that dash alone is amazing game design, but you'll of course be able to unlock more playstyles from the bosses you beat, opening up passages in previous levels, and offering even more ways to get around the screen.Overall, if you're into 2D action platformers, or just fast paced platformers in general, you should definitely consider picking this one up. You want reckless abandon? Go Berserk.
_childDocuments_.name: Berserk Boy

_childDocuments_.review: I’ve been following this for literally years and I’m so glad it’s finally come out. Props to the dev for their perseverance and talent! It’s clear that a lot of love went into this.Berserk Boy is a wild ride of a game — super tight platforming, stellar level design, gorgeous artwork, a Saturday-morning-cartoon story and an absolutely brilliant soundtrack. It’s a heady mix of Mega Man and Sonic, with a focus on speed and suit switches that keeps you thinking even as you’re moving at 100mph. It’s cool to get access to new parts of old levels (the ‘Metroidvania elements’ mentioned) as you unlock suits, and I can see speed runners tearing this apart in really interesting ways. Great for a splash of cartoony fun if you like platformers even a little bit.
_childDocuments_.name: Berserk Boy

_childDocuments_.review: I have been following this game for a very good long while, for 5 years almost and I have loved seeing the development of the game, seeing it go from a very basic layout to what it is today, this game has gone through leaps and bounds to get to the point where it is today and I must say it is an absolutely stellar and wonderful classic that I will be coming back to time and time again, the fact the I took the time to 100% this game says a lot since I have only 100% only a couple dozen or two games, this included.Let me get the few negatives I have out of the way. The game is not without its flaws, the bosses can be a little strange to fight too, I struggled a bit in them not exactly sure why, not sure if it was my fault or the game but later when you get the final power up they become a breeze. Speaking of said power up, the latter half of the game having a difficult time integrating the final power up into the game, however still fun to use and very useful to use in various other situations especially when going back to 100%ing the game, it helped sweep a LOT of the enemies very quickly and efficiently leading to more high speed action after the combat sections are done. Some of the deathzones are a little iffy, not all of the deathzones have the usual icon that shows that there is a bottomless pit and so trying to find secrets sometimes ended up in me just dying because I thought there might have been a secret and sometimes the death planes are a little higher than what was expected but those issues are very minor in the grand scheme.Now to the positives which there are a LOT of, the pixel art is SUPER magical, I have always been a huge fan of Zu's work with sprite art for so long. He has such a way with making effects pop out of the screen in a real flashy way, it is eye candy through and through, the layout of the levels are very cleverly designed in which you must use ALL of your power ups to get through most of the levels. None are left behind, They are all very smartly integrated in the game that truly makes the experience that much better. Every first level for each mission also emphasizes the new power up you get, using it as a pseudo tutorial level that really makes you understand the capabilities of every power up you get, and once you go to the next mission it is integrated into your move set with all the other powers and it feels magical. I love the fact for fast pace action that you automatically use the drill form when pointing towards a drillable wall, rather than needing to switch into it every time to use it. The high speed action in the game feels SUPER great, all of the levels which you can move fast in are just a huge dopamine rush of pure fun trying to get the highest combo possible, it feels intense and amazing, I can only imagine what this game will be like in the next year with speed runners picking up this game!Overall the game is an absolutely fun as hell time, Zu you made a masterpiece man and I am so happy for you :3 8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: This game is EXTREMELY rad. The Megaman X and Sonic the Hedgehog inspirations are plain to see, and this game executes on the best of both of them brilliantly. I especially want to commend the design of the lightning suit -- it's so rare for a control scheme to be this deeply satisfying AND intuitive! I just wish that every every suit felt as good to play. On the more positive end of the other suits, you have the fire and gale suits which, while not half as fun as the lightning suit, offer great utility and a much-appreciated change of pace. The fire suit's drilling mechanics really feel like you're exploring, and the the gale suit's flight is simple, sure, but also just innately fun!On the other hand, you have the ice and earth suits. The ice suit isn't necessarily bad, but it's finicky, and the first time a death bothered me, it was because of the ice suit's traversal. Worse, however, was the earth suit. I simply do not understand how it serves the momentum that makes this game so special. I do not feel like a Boy gone Berserk as I'm fluttering a scanner at "invisible" platforms or shooting a gun that is somehow the shortest range attack in a melee-focused game, you know?Beyond that, my "biggest" complaint is that base/hub felt too big for how much of it I used? I understand why it was that size, but I only ever used 20% of it, unless I had to hunt around it for enemies in those periodic attacks. This is definitely not a huge problem, but it kept coming up and I wanted to mention it.Final verdict -- 3/5, I like it! When it's doing what it's best at, it's phenomenal; when it's not, it's baffling. This is VERY worth playing if even just for the first two sectors alone!
_childDocuments_.name: Berserk Boy

_childDocuments_.review: With the references to Mega Man X and the pre-release imagery, I could see why a lot of people would expect a game along the Mega Man series line, but I'm here to say that's not entirely the case. Sure, there's definite influences in the presentation and some of the movement elements, but rest assured, Berserk Boy is more of a platformer more then anything. It's about moving through the levels with a brisk pace while using the tools in your arsenal wisely, and in that element, it succeeds. It starts to get reasonably good when you start getting more powers and have to choose between them, and finding the various resistance members can be fun for those collectahon players. It's got a heart filled presentation, with good design elements especially for the main character's forms, and it doesn't take itself too seriously.But be aware of the fact that if you're expecting a Mega Man X clone in any sort of way, you need to look elsewhere. The combat for the game is rather easy and repetitive, there isn't the positioning factor to take out enemies, you're sorta just a barrel of destruction rolling along with several of the powers. In addition, the bosses are probably the weakest part of the game: difficulty is not there and isn't the climax of levels that it really should be. There are parts of the game that are inconsistent that will have you scratching your head, sometimes it's something significant, but a lot of them are small things that add up. It makes sense for a new studio that may not have the pedigree of others to have some of the mistakes, but it's the fact that many of those mistakes are ok in other areas of the game similar to it, like there was a weird inconsistency that developed.Overall, while it wasn't what I was hoping for entirely, it's still a solid game in the platforming genre and worth your time: but isn't something you need to drop to play right away if you have other games you're focusing on. :

_childDocuments_.review: Electrifying Action That Sparks Pure JoyStep into a pixel-perfect adventure with "BERSERK BOY," a game that masterfully combines the heart-pounding excitement of a high-speed platformer with the intricate exploration of Metroidvania elements. From the moment you dive in, the vibrant and meticulous pixel art leaps off the screen, wrapping you in a world begging to be saved.The thrill of transformation takes center stage as you harness the elemental powers of Lightning, Fire, Ice, Air, and Earth. Each form feels distinct, not only adding visual flair but also offering unique abilities that change the way you navigate through the meticulously crafted levels. The controls are tight and responsive, essential for the lightning-fast action that will have you leaping, dashing, and going berserk in the best possible way.But what truly sets the atmosphere is the pulse-pounding soundtrack by Tee Lopes, whose work on Sonic Mania resonated with fans worldwide. The music fuels the frenzy, with beats that complement every jump, attack, and new discovery. It's a sonic experience that elevates the gameplay to a symphony of excitement."BERSERK BOY" isn't just a game; it's a retro-futuristic journey that honors its inspirations while forging a path all its own. Whether you're a seasoned platformer veteran or a newcomer looking to get your feet wet, this game welcomes all with open arms and an electric embrace. Go Berserk and be a part of the savior this planet needs!If you're craving a game that's equal parts nostalgic and innovative, with a side of electrifying gameplay, then "BERSERK BOY" is your ticket to an unforgettable experience.10/10 - Would go berserk again!

_childDocuments_.review: After 100% completion:It's a nice blast from the past. The game feels and plays like a platformer you would've been a fan of if you were a gamer in the 90's. The combat is fast and fun. The pixel art and animation is great. Combined with banger OST from Tee Lopes. A casual playthrough (you ignore the collectibles) is around 6-8 hours. Which may or may not seem short to you but this is the nature of these 90's platformers. It took me around 20 hours to collect everything, unlock the EX stages (time trial levels) and S rank all stages. I would say i got my money's worth.The negatives: Enemy variety is a tiny bit lacking to my taste. Especially the fact that the sub-bosses get reused is a bit lame. Some stages visuals (especially the later ones) also get a bit repetitive while the early game stages have more going on both in the background and in the foreground. Also while every form has it's uses for something some little balance tweaks would've helped. Most of the time you will use your starting form because it's just that good. While others will be pretty much utility only forms (looking at you Flame Drill and Soaring Wind altough i can understand why Soaring Wind is made to be weak in combat).TLDR: A great Megaman X style game with a bit of Sonic feeling. It deserves more attention and a sequel!

_childDocuments_.review: Berserk Boy is a fantastic game, it feels like a call back to the times of old Mega Man / Sonic whilst being very much it's own thing and rolling with it!I've only had time to play in small bursts so far but it works on Steam Deck flawlessly (so I'd imagine most other market handhelds will be fine too) and that's been my primary way of playing in-between life things, etcBig recommend to those looking for a great action game with fun transformations and lovable cast!
_childDocuments_.name: Berserk Boy

_childDocuments_.review: 𝗦𝗢𝗡𝗜𝗖 𝗠𝗔𝗡This game is amazing in every possible way. They perfectly merged the art style, boss stealing power-ups of Mega Man with game play of Sonic the Hedgehog and I never knew this merge would be as good as it is or that I needed it in my life!If you're a fan of either Sonic or Mega Man then this is a must buy. The game will roughly take you 5-8 hours to complete but it's enjoyable all the way through. I actually struggled to put the game down and go to bed because I wanted to finish it in a single play.Pros are literally everything this game offers. Graphics are retro in a good way (SNES Esq), the colors are vibrant, the details are on point, the characters are well done in terms of their looks/aesthetic, the soundtrack is well done with it being very Sonic-ish (go figure with Tee Lopes being the composer, which is awesome), the controls are smooth/responsive and the combat/power-ups are fun.The only honest critiques/cons I can give this game, which are inconsequential, is that the game with being only 5-8 hours for $20 is a little 'meh' but it's a fun ride that I personally think is worth it regardless and the writing for the game feels like some fanfic shenanigans. I had to read it aloud because I streamed it and some of the dialogue was a bit "cringe" and really makes you appreciate games like the original Mega Man series not having a bunch of dialogue. The story is good though overall and makes sense.I'd rate this bad boy a 9.5/10 and I WANT MORE!!!

_childDocuments_.review: The trailer shows cherry picked sections of interesting gameplay.The reality is the abilities of the suits are poorly explained and are weak or unsatisfying to use. In order to replicate the fast paced high intensity moments from the trailer you have to have sections memorized and be going through them after said memorization.The game does an exceptionally poor job of explaining your powers and move set to you and how it works. The tutorial you do get takes place before you get your first suit, so there's a massive disconnect between what you're being told and how it's meant to actually work.It looks great and has great music but the gameplay totally tanks this title. On top of that the few bosses I did fight where boring, and underwhelming. I suspect this is to compensate for the poor move set available to the player which is mostly all centered around traversal with combat being what feels like an after thought. Over all it feels like playing Mighty No.9 2.0I had to request a refund. Hopefully if you do decide to buy it, the game is more fun for you.

_childDocuments_.review: so this is a really tough no as I am a BIG fan of old school mega man games and this, in some aspects, gets really close. My biggest complaint is that the first form is incredible. Super fun and easy to use and strong. The rest kind suck. Like they have new abilities but a dash and seeking projectile is just too good. _childDocuments_.review: I had originally learned about this game casually on Twitter (and sometimes on Facebook) and while it looked amazing there, I was pensive. Why? A lot of good game ideas wander by before the people working on it either vanish or something dark crops up.Berserk Boy is one of the few that has come out and scratched the exact itch it looked like it would. Playing it is far smoother than the videos initially made it seem, the story is just the right side of SNES-era corn to be both amusing and genuinely engaging, and ye gods the flow. _childDocuments_.review: Really solid game. I could never get into Mega Man ZX or Advent due to various annoyances and getting lost in the map. This game takes the prototype ideas from those games and completing them. The game feels like a speed game with the amount of dashing you do (for both attack and movement) as well with the quickness you can switch movesets to perform flowing combos. The story is largely ignored, but familiar. The way that Gravity Circuit gave us an improved revival of the Mega Man Zero series, Berserk Boy gives us an improved revival of the Mega Man ZX and Advent games.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a great time start to finish. The gameplay is solid and has a nice variety. Don't expect much of a story though this isn't that type of game. This all about the gameplay baby. All of the powers feel good with what they do and how they flow. There might be some parts that feel a little awkward like a certain power's double jump ability but for the most part they feel good. Art style is fun too. I love the comic book like style and the poses are spot on. An artist myself its so fun and I love all the bright colors.Granted there is one Power that can negate certain sections where the game might want you to use a different ability but that doesn't matter as I appreciate the freedom in letting the player choose how to traverse a section. Its not too difficult but not too hard. The movement has a great flow which is good since there are extra EX levels that are time trials. Now for a few gripes though one has just been fixed. Originally you needed all 50 B Medals to unlock the Final Ending but that has been reduce to 20 so you'll naturally get them if you just look around a bit while playing.Minor gripe is Fire power not being resistance to fire. Please make that clear. When you have instant death flames glowing red and Fire Power is Red my brain thought "Oh use this power to resist fire damage"Then finding Resistance Members. I feel a map or something would really help that aspect or at least an indicator after finishing a level saying how many members are in each section as well as where the Resistance Doors are since I often forget where they were.Finally please reduce the price on upgrades. I understand wanting us to choose but actually maxing out everything would be a bit of a grind. That said the upgrades for the last power you get felt just right.Overall I'd say solid 8/10. It short but sweet. Gameplay is smooth. Bosses are fun. A few complaints but great game all around. Highly recommend. You don't have to worry about a time sink either you can plow through the main game in a day and its a good time.

_childDocuments_.review: After having just completed Berserk Boy at nearly 9 hours, I am pretty pleased with it overall. I think it caters towards a more casual audience than maybe the hardcore MMX games did but perhaps that was the right call? Levels are pretty straight forward, once you use one gimmick you will use it a thousand times making the levels themselves not overly unique aside from new background art. The Soaring Wind orb kind of breaks a lot of the game with making it so platforming isn't really necessary based on how the game tells you how to play when you can glide over most everything. Boss battles are a lot of fun and where the game arguably shines. I mostly stuck to the Ice Kunai power for them as the fast ranged fighter kept me alive most of the time but I can assume using the other orbs could lend themselves to neat outcomes too. There's a lot of good here and it seems like this is the first of hopefully many BB games. The price does feel a little steep, but considering I'd have paid the $30 or $35 for it to be on GBA where it feels like it would shine, this seems fine. It's a very polished game that cares about how accessible it is to various player types. I never got frustrated or wanted to rage quit. It was a fun and familiar ride with a lot of style.

_childDocuments_.review: General overview:Graphics, sound and gameplay are all great, I enjoyed most of my time with the game, however the icon collecting part at the end just to get to the last boss is tedious. As much as I liked this game, some of the forms feel a bit superfluous( I have no idea why you would want to change into your human form ), where I'd be flying past platforms thinking should I have been doing this in another form. I almost think it would have been better to have been locked into a form for the full level, with the ability to change between forms unlocked at the end of the game. Changing forms three time in rapid succession just to unlock doors simply isn't fun. At the end you will fight enemies that can only be killed with certain forms, not new enemies mind the same ones you've been fighting all game.I got bored quickly at the end of the game doing the token collection, which is required to fight the final boss. I'm not a fan of the metroidvania parts of the game especially being there is no map ( I've recently completed Bloodstained ROTN and Guacamelee), I feel this is something that could have been unlocked after first completion of the level.I wouldn't exactly call it metroidvania either as you are just replaying the level again, with all the cut screens, dialog and boss fights again.The 60% doors are pretty Bs as well, basically you can't rescue this fighter until you have rescued some other 2 fighters on the map first, it just forces back tracking and redoing parts you've done before.I feel this game would have been fine with less forms with some of the abilities being things that auto transform, see the tornado tunnel digger, this would have at least made selecting the right form easier using the d pad, i ended up switching to the stick for form changes.I found this game  easier than Gravity Circuit ( I played on modern mode), but I think gravity circuit felt a bit tighter, not having the issues with forms and the forced repetition of the levels, however the movement is way better here compared to using the grappling hook which didn't work well for me. Some of the recommendations for this game come after less than an hour and rate the game 10/10, I mean come on, you've spent more time writing the review than playing the game at that point. Can't argue with the price its fun and its fair with plenty of checkpoints, they have a retro option or a modern option with infinite lives, which suits me because my backlog is too big to be spending 50 hours on this game trying to master it. Despite my criticisms, I do recommend this game as I enjoyed playing it and would defo buy the sequel or any other platformer the dev puts out. I only mention my gripes in the hope that the sequel  irons them out.

_childDocuments_.review: I first knew of this game during the steam next fest earlier this year. Looked at a few games, saw this game's artstyle which I wasn't the biggest fan of since it looked a bit anime fanart-ish. However, as a sucker for good 2D gameplay with catchy tunes, I decided to give the demo a try. Plot was a bit anime tropy, but once I was in control, the game started to click and I decided to buy the full thing.The movement of the game is always something I enjoyed, always been fast and fluid which is perfect for people with zero patience like myself. Game never makes you sit there and wait for long, and I like that. There's always ways to move quickly in the levels and the game knows to keep its story in the background for fun moments here and there without fully interrupting gameplay which is the focus.  Granted as I am highly impatient, I gravitated towards forms that gave me more speed. Flame drill fell by the wayside since its air maneuverability is the lowest in the game, meanwhile Ice Kunai was my favorite due to the opportunities it provides for crazy shenanigans. When you land a dash with ice kunai, it gives you the opportunity to change direction and keep the dash going. If you are skilled enough to chain the dashes back and forth you can absolutely shred some enemies and boss fights (which might make it a tad broken in a fun way). Plus the drop dash gives the berserk meter more to do than sit there and be anti-boss fodder which I think is pretty interesting. It recontextualizes the game which makes approaching simple scenarios in the game a bit more varied and fun, raising the skill ceiling and satisfaction of mastery to the game. I wish the other forms had more crazy opportunities and "sauce" if you will. Maybe a speed or damage boost for chaining several enemies with lighting at once, lifting and throwing enemies with flame drill, hacking enemies with mine buster so they fight or get items for you, etc.You'd think some of the cool perks would be contained in the shop and to be fair some of it is, (double dash in lightning, drop dash for kunai. extra ammo for mine buster) but some moves I don't fully understand what they do exactly. For example I bought the second lightning justice (as I was gunning for all achievements) and was never sure what is exactly did. I'm sure the extra kicking animation does something, I'm just not sure what. Maybe clearer descriptions or more noticeable abilities/upgrades to offset this would be good? Level design I enjoyed. it is a tad boxy and repetitive sometimes (especially considering the game's desire to have the player replay some parts to progress), which I didn't find to be much of a detriment to my enjoyment, but maybe some would. Maybe having a few more level specific gimmicks or mechanics to make the levels stand out a bit from each other. Maybe the city stays the same since it's the tutorial area, but maybe the jungle has vines, to swing on, crazed animal life affected by berserk energy, a set-piece where part of the forest is set on fire, getting eaten and fighting your way out of a dinosaur, fighting through a snowstorm or outrunning a yeti, maybe less shades and more monstrous failed infusions with berserk energy, among other ideas to really make levels feel varied and pop out more. Kind of like how Sonic has a few new mechanics/set-pieces per zone to keep things varied (without compromising the precision focused fast-paced gameplay). Might be good for a sequel?Music is amazing. No complaints here. Different track variations for each stage, with all of them easy on the ears. Particularly loved the track for the ex stages. Speaking of stages, they are on the easier side, even if going for S-ranks (which mostly just require that you get most of the things in the level and don't die) so this game can fit into your schedule under the category of "I want to play a fast-fluid game with a great OST that doesn't cave my skull in".TLDR: You want a game that's fast, fluid (if a little repetitive) with a great OST? Here you go! Not perfect, but come on, the devs went through a lot to get this game to happen. Sure it has sime flaws, but this game comes from the heart and has genuine passion put into it. It'll be awesome to see that passion sharpened and evolved in future games. It's a fun time from a dev who deserves the money, give it a shot!

_childDocuments_.review: Flawed but satisfying-feeling title that seems to take inspiration from Mega Man ZX, of all games, but refines the multi-form approach to a sheen with a great focus on mobility and scoring, not unlike Azure Striker Gunvolt. The gameplay loop is crunchy and snappy, and the level design gets surprisingly challenging, asking you to swap between your forms on the fly and tear through enemies with efficiency. I love the act of going through the levels, and I think it's the real star of the show; the bosses, meanwhile, I'm saddened to say they were pretty uninteresting. Not poorly designed at all, just not particularly fun or memorable, visually or mechanically. For lack of a better word they feel more like an afterthought, and the levels are the main course. To me though, that's fine!The different forms feel well-balanced for the most part, though the linear design means not all levels equally incentivize using all the forms once you've gotten them all. I was hoping the EX levels with that in mind would basically be the regular levels but with more routes added, but they're closer to the bonus stages in stuff like Sonic Colors and Forces. Most of the levels have secret paths that require the use of a later power, but in the end the ones I've found aren't actually detours or alternate routes so much as secrets, meaning once you've obtained the secret they arent quite as appealing so even on replays some forms won't see a lot of use. Felt like a teensy bit of a let down, but the act of going through the levels is otherwise always a fun time.The actual spritework for the characters feels a little on the awkward side; some elements feel like they clash and some animations look a little uncanny (Dizzy's idle) or like they're unfinished, but the overall art direction and designs are nice and fun and gives off the feeling of a lost DS title. The saturday morning cartoon vibe is nailed perfectly here, Berserk Boy would genuinely make for a great looking show.Compared to other games though, I feel like for as tight as the core gameplay is there's a pretty notable unpolishedness in the presentation, ranging from small quirks to questionable decisions. These things aren't all horrible, but they do kind of add up to something that makes me feel like the developers didn't give it all enough thought. To quickly run over issues or quirks I've seen:- Kei's voice clips and attack callouts play so often that a Freedom Planet fan would blush, and in general at times feel too long for what you're actually doing. Expect to hear "LIGHTNING JUSTICE!" 5 times in a row while in a combat room- Retro mode includes a life system but perplexingly lives don't refill in between levels, not unlike a similar issue found in Mega Man Zero 1 (a little too much influence, huh?). This means if you finish a level with 1 life, you'll have to start the next level with 1 life unless you kill yourself first to get it all back at 3.- Volume of the voice clips that accompany the dialogue boxes is too low, and is often drowned out by the music- Some music seems to just straight up not loop properly; the boss theme has a distinct pause between the music stopping and starting again- Kei feels sensitive to touching things like walls; there's been several times where I hit springs and dash, but instead of flying straight he'll clip into something, destroying my momentum- The script overall is mostly fine, but there's some typos and strange words that give me the impression English may not be developer's first language- This is a lot more opinion-based but I think the combo counter drains way too fast; I feel like given the appeal of the gameplay, a skilled player should be rewarded with being able to keep their combo up through the entire level, which is virtually impossible as the counter drains while you're transitioning screens and zapping tagged enemies and there aren't enough orbs in between to keep it up. I feel like a more Gunvolt-style "you keep your combo up as long as you don't get hit" approach would work way better, or at least if the timer was greatly extended to make it so people still couldn't slack off, but were forgiven for not having the fine control to basically teleport from room to roomI think overall though there is an unfortunate feeling that even the game's core is a bit halfway baked. Outside of the inclusion of specific form gimmicks, the levels tend to be somewhat samey and blend together outside of visual themes and music. For as short as the game is I was hoping there would actually be more dialogue and writing to have more fun with the cast, but it's all almost too minimal feeling. The hub base is massive but there isn't remotely enough interesting going on to justify it outside of some weak transitional base defense segments that feel like padding. The aforementioned average bosses are especially disappointing because I feel like a game like this should have some truly exciting battles. There's a shop to buy skills for your forms but it doesn't feel like it adds anything outside of a loose progression system alongside the obvious. Your last form is introduced alongside a set of specific gimmicks that are completely trivialized by the form you get before it, making large chunks of the final levels irrelevant in terms of challenge. Berserk Boy is  a complete experience, but I can't help but feel like it only taps into about 50% of what it really could be and lacks total refinement of itself.As is, with those feelings aside, it's a fun little title that manages to get most of the right appeals from its inspirations and play in a unique and enjoyable way. While I hope the dev will look into the things I've mentioned, I think it's a worthy recommend, even if it isn't quite the big favorite I was really hoping it would be.

_childDocuments_.review: Berserk Boy heckin' slaps!Incredible modern take on a mish-mash of MegaMan X and Sonic with it's own spins that heavily sets it apart from it's inspiration.In summary, Berserk Boy is a high speed platformer all about dashing around, switching forms and combo-ing enemies. _childDocuments_.review: An absolute MUST-PLAY for Mega Man Zero & Mega Man X fans!I just rolled credits on Steam, one week after rolling credits on Switch, and I found I loved the game even MORE.Berserk Boy is what happens when you mix the platforming of Mega Man X with the up-close-and-personal combat of Mega Man Zero and the speed of Sonic (or other arcade-y Sega games).Note two things to fully enjoy this game:1. The controls are weird, but learn them. The game uses 3 primary buttons, one of which is often your initial attack AND your movement ability (air dash, etc.). It feels weird because you'll rely on the left and right of the 4 face buttons (Y and A on Switch, X and B on Xbox/Steam Deck) as well as the Left Trigger. It feels odd and takes getting used to. I think there is probably a better option or layout (and you can custom bind anything in the options), but these are placed where they are after years of testing and once I get in the groove after a few minutes in any play session, it doesn't bother me.2. The structure of the game is basically 3 stages per world, 7 worlds, each stage has a minor boss, each 3rd stage has a major boss that grants you a new ability. Levels usually take around 5 minutes, but many take 8-10 so definitely expect longer stages than Mega Man (another way the game is to the Zero series).In each stage, you can collect 5 hidden/secret coins, of which you'll usually find 2 on your initial playthrough, then there are 5-12 hidden resistance members to track down and 'rescue', so there's a lot in every level.Thing is, a lot of it is blocked off behind doors that require new abilities, and you won't be able to get anything in your first run.MY ADVICE FOR THE STRUCTURE OF THE GAME - Play one stage at a time all the way until you get the green ability (or the yellow one afterwards, which is the final ability), THEN start revisiting levels so you can find anything in one more run. You'll need the currency for ability upgrades, and you'll be finding new stuff every minute, so the replays feel fresh and just as fun as the first time - DON'T replay the same level over and over trying to find secrets, because that'll make things get stale pretty quick.All in all, Berserk Boy is topping my list for 2024 GOTY and I think it nailed the execution of delivering something that tickles our Nostalgia while also building something brad new.The game isn't too hard, the "modern" mode gives infinite retries while retaining currency you collected before dying, the music (by Tee Lopes - Sonic Mania, Shredder's Revenge) is incredible, and the painstaking detail is unrivaled in the indie space. This game is tight as heck and bug-free, with flawless performance on anything I could throw at it.I received this game for free on Switch to review, but then I got sick and couldn't review it...I loved the game so much that I bought it at full price on Steam to replay and found at the end of my second round, I feel even more fond of the game than I did after the first run-through.THIS is the kind of game you should buy. THIS is the new-but-familiar game that takes chances while delivering incredible presentation that we all want more of. No microtransactions, no mandatory updates, all the challenges are fair and fun, and it's all wrapped up in a package that will ALWAYS be fun.Go support this developer - Berserk Boy is a dream passion project by a single guy who clearly worked his butt off to make it happen, and gamers should support him for delivering exactly what was promised, if not more.
