_childDocuments_.review: Pros:Stylish visualsGreat movementSolid level designAmazing soundtrackCons:Difficulty (For some)After firing up the game for the first time and being greeted by a Toonami-esque cartoon intro, Myself and my cat were already bobbing our heads to the music and grinning at the character design. I could tell almost instantly that this was a game touching the right notes with the 90's/early 2000's pop culture inspiration.The first level serves as a tutorial of sorts and looks to introduce some of the colourful cast of characters. their dialog was fun, and i felt the pace of the game increasing at a fun rate climaxing in the reveal of the titular characters form. I really enjoyed this start as I am somebody who enjoys games, but does not profess to the best at them. This allowed me to get a good feel for the movement mechanics and some of the combat before thrusting me into the bulk of the action. The movement and combat are great, the 'Berserk Boy' form is reflective of his design, fast and unrelenting (hence the 'Berserk' i guess) as this form started to click it felt amazing to have the speed and power at my disposal. moving through the level at an increasing pace it felt great being able to tag enemies as i sped into them dealing damage and finishing them off with a lightning strike as i kept my momentum moving forward. The second form i have played with has a different.I have ran into some parts that are challenging and requires a certain level of platforming skill to be able to progress smoothly. With the difficulty setting of 'Modern' available this is offset slightly by having unlimited lives and generous checkpoints. Meaning for me it has caused me to take a step back from the fast pace i experienced in the earlier levels, and focus more on precision and understanding of the forms and movement available. This could be a negative for some as it has certain 'skill' checks to be able to 'Berserk' through the whole game. But with time and practise, the movement is fluid enough for it to be a 'skill issue' as apposed to being beaten by bad design. the visuals and soundtrack are where it really shines. It look amazing, the character design is fun and quirky with inspiration from a plethora of sources without it feeling too overt or obtuse. the levels and characters all fit within the world it is trying to portray and meshes well thematically with the level designs and backgrounds. The soundtrack is amazing, have found myself jamming to the music as i play and i feel this adds and extra dynamic to the game. the soundtracks helps to form a 'baseline' to whats going on on-screen and adding to the energy levels as you play, something i haven't experienced on a title since Adventure 2.From my experience this is a must-play for the genre and will be my go-to until i finish it.

_childDocuments_.review: Berserk Boy is the game where you are a boy, then you learn to go berserk. Going berserk allows you to defeat the baddies of the realm, kind of reminds me about a baddie I met at a mcdonalds in canada. That bird I forget the name of follows you throughout every level, but does not really help you in any way despite taking credit for everything at the end. This does not really matter though, as you can use your incredible movement and berserk orbs to chain together incredible tricks that will let you speed through the levels with ease. This incredible movement and smooth moment to moment gameplay motivates me, as I am able to pretend that I am running away from the stupid bird. Your epic berserk orbs do not only give you new movement options, but powerful moves, like the one the mcBaddie did in canada. These moves let you defeat powerful enemies while staying on the move, and prove invaluable when fighting bosses. The bosses are really fun to fight, except for that turtle, I cheesed that one, but I have been given explicit permission to do this by the creator of the game.All of this combined with the incredible soundtrack creates for a game worthy of being called Berserk Boy, and you should therefore buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: Full Review: ---G O  B E R S E R K !!!---Rather than feeling like a new Mega Man game, Berserk Boy feels like a love letter to 2D platforming in general with Mega Man as a blueprint for its structure. If you’re a fan of the genre, you’ll have an absolutely great time here as there is lots to love, Berserk Boy is a delight to control, the core gameplay loop is brilliant, with the game truly at its best when you are zooming through levels and firing yourself into the path of enemies ahead of you. It's fundamentally a very good 2D platform game, and feels like a lost relic of the Game Boy Advance.I can easily recommend Berserk Boy and if you want to support an independent developer who clearly does know what they are doing in a sea of big budget releases, there's great value and fun to be had here.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the SAGE23 demo and thought it looked cool, thought I would play the full game to see what more it had to offer before giving unfair criticism because I had assumptions that the game would basic, but that was pretty much how the whole game is.I thought the Berserk form would get a projectile or something as an upgrade to make its gameplay more varied but it really only has one function and I understand the whole game's level design is designed around it, but it got really boring by the 2nd zone. Ice Kunai is the form that should have been the default because it plays nearly identically but it has the projectiles. In fact, it is extremely overwhelming damage-wise. It can clear out some enemy filled rooms by standing in the corner and holding attack while bosses can die before their Berserk desperation move animation plays. It took me until going through some levels giving some final thoughts to realize that enemies have an elemental weakness system, I just saw no reason to utilize some abilities in combat other than Berserk Boy and Ice Kunai because they do plenty of damage already and maintain a high combo count. Meanwhile, Flame Drill just traverses through walls and the floor, if you didn't have to change into it to go under the low spike ceiling there would never be a use for it, its attacks are slow and overly commit to leave you vulnerable. Those drill wall sections really overstayed their welcome. Soaring Wind depletes almost all of the meter with its attack button that rotates around you so it's not fun to use in fights and there's an exploit anyway by rapidly swapping powers and dashing in midair that lets you collect things that it's supposed to be used for. Mine Buster has the same problem as Soaring Wind until you get the infinite ammo upgrade, deplete all resources doing its one attack and then either wait to recharge or swap abilities. Not every power is as highly tuned as Ice Kunai unfortunately, which I definitely used for 80% of the playthrough because it's really fun.Level design takes inspiration from Mega Man of course, all mostly designed around regular rotation through abilities and avoiding hazards. It's fun for the most part, briskly dashing through enemies and on the fly swapping to something else when you notice a different hazard or when the ability changer platform shows up. I have problems with it when exploring the zones to collect the Berserk Medals which you end up being required to have collected 50/65 to get to the final level. I see that every death pit is marked with skulls to indicate that you will obviously die and there's down there, but it's inconsistent and there are pits that do not have the skulls that you can still die. There is even a pit that has a ladder that goes all the way to down to death. It is an amateur design mistake. Also, switching abilities as soon as you touch that kill range (which is pretty high above the bottom of the screen imo) doesn't load back to checkpoint and you can't pause! Epic softlock! So I just have to learn from trial and error in those situations not to check 90% of pits unless there are energy coins pathing to another screen. You have to collect the medal and return to a checkpoint to have them saved to the totals which was really annoying. I really did not enjoy that few hours searching for medals.Aesthetics were good, mostly what pulled me into buying the game. I like most of the spritework. I would have liked to see more enemy varieties. Character portraits are inconsistent to the sprites and even cutscene art. Too many different artstyles for the same characters. Voice acting was okay, amateurish at times but not much to say about it because audio mixing was really bad and OST/SFX are way louder than the VAs and there's no sound options. Not all dialogue is voiced anyway, so whatever.Music is great. I don't have much to say about non-gameplay features, it's just solid.I like the game's style overall but I think it's too unpolished.
_childDocuments_.name: Berserk Boy

_childDocuments_.review: Man, what a cool experience! We've seen so many devs try to capture the spirit of the old Mega Man titles, especially the X series. But, really this is the first one to nail it. You can tell the devs are fans and they wanted to stay true to the feel, but really make their own game. It's fast, feels good and really fun. Totally worth the wait.
_childDocuments_.name: Berserk Boy

_childDocuments_.review: This one is a love letter for the oldschool gamers from the 16bit - 32 bit era of gaming. Don't sleep on this title. Music, art, controls, story and the energy of the thing... are ALL fantastic. Oh - and it of course suits the Steam Deck PERFECTLY!When I originally started this review, I was 30 minutes in. I'm now closer to 4.5 hours into the game and I can say that my first impressions were correct. If you love classic 16-32 bit era platformers - you're going to love this game.That's because Berserk Boy is taking the BEST of things like Dragonball, Gunstar Heroes, Megaman X, Megaman ZX, Pulseman, and maybe even a little bit of Sonic the Hedgehog and blending it together into one EPIC win. The powers are fun and creative. They're very versatile. It's not just a new elemental projectile that you get - you get a whole new motif with new control scheme attached. As of this writing I just got the air powers and I can say between the fire and ice powers and now air - not to mention your original electric/lightning powers - each skill set makes you play like a new character. This keeps things fresh and fun. It's also a nice mechanic that each level has troops you can save, sort of like SNK's Metal Slug series... once you get at least 60% of them in a level, it'll open up another section of the stage that's usually hidden... and once you get 100% you open up the EX level which in my experience are much harder and apparently offer some great rewards. I haven't actually finished one yet, because I decided to save it for after I have all the powers.Transitioning from power to power is done with a nice radial wheel selection interface. It's fairly seamless while still being purposeful. I actually prefer it to cycling through powers megaman style. The story is fun but about what I'd expect of this kind of game so far. If you're on the fence... stop it. Get the game and have some fun. This one is worth it and I can only hope they have success with this IP enough to make more games in the series in the years to come.
_childDocuments_.name: Berserk Boy

_childDocuments_.review: Berserk Boy is what happens if someone likes a particular game genre very much but can't decide what game in it is their favorite, so they take their favorite bits of each and mashes them together.The result is a fast paced, fluid platformer that offers collectibles and secrets for those that like to take their time as well as time and score mechanics for those aiming for a perfect run of a stage.The soundtrack is phenomenal, the visual presentation is incredibly charming and the story is...there i guess? Certainly not one of its stronger points.All in all, Berserk Boy is yet another Indie platformer highlight. Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Berserk Boy

_childDocuments_.review: I want to be clear that this is by no means a 'bad' game. It's a mostly-on-rails Sonic/Mega Man-like game with a few modern touches. I liked Sonic when I was quite young, but I wouldn't replay it now. I've never really gotten along with Mega Man.If you like those games, you will probably really like this game. It's certainly well made. I don't find it to be fun. I appear to be in the minority here- I didn't like Gravity Circuit either, which is also clearly a great game for some people.I played through the first few areas, and this didn't hook me. Metroidvania / 2D platformers are some of my very favorite games, but this particular niche is not for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Berserk Boy

_childDocuments_.review: I wen't through a phase these last two years of immediately buying "boy games" ...Monster Boy, Owl boy, Cat boy, Berserk Boy, Bat boy...etc. I don't know why that way of titling games just basically ensures a good time. Berserk Boy is absolutely in the top 3 of all the boy games I've played, and the only ones that I'd consider better are just based  on my own personal bias (monster boy btw). This is a Dev to keep on your watch list moving forward.
_childDocuments_.name: Berserk Boy

_childDocuments_.review: If you grew up about all things Megaman and DragonBall adjacent; raiding your school's yearly Scholastic Book Fair for all the slightly-off How To Draw Manga books and haphazardly tracing over them without a care for artistic fundamentals because it's all just so cool (netting you the esteemed "artist" status among your peers all the while), this is EXACTLY what you dreamed of creating with your surface-deep lorerip AU and too-familiar OCs galore.Berserk Boy is a perpetually 5th grade effort. I mean all this with utmost kindness and sincerity, but perhaps a bit of bite? I was that kid, one of many. That's why I'm drawn to this game and compelled to talk about it, that's also why I would only ever recommend this to others with that same formative fondness. Sates that one note without relent but....not much else? By design it doesn't quite get the full breadth of it's inspirations and hits a fair number of pitfalls, what I can mostly call awkward clunk at...well, most points whenever the game is not pushing you forward in a blitz of dash, rail, cannon, drill and homing actions. Keep it moving and it's fine, excels even. A downright blast, executed right. Stall out for combat or exploration and it can get dicey.  It might sound contentious, but BB is a bit simple in design and geometry. It's shallow. For what it is I don't think that's bad. It's rather concise, to-the-point and I do appreciate that. Serviceable low sci-fi anti-terror background and GET THE MACGUFFINS YOURE THE ONLY ONE WHO CAN SAVE US PLEASE OH GOD HELP US DELIVER SALVATION THE BADDIES ARE SO DARK AND EVIL AND MISGUIDED story that's at home among the morning Y2K kid's anime scene or at the very least familiar to Megaman fans. Completion comes easy and I'll never tire of revisiting old areas with new powers in games, even for simple purposes of civilian rescue and coin collecting to make your percentage numbers go up. You're not going to garner anything truly astounding in doing so, at least until later if you're committed. I'd say it's worth seeing through.From the onset of the opening animation and title screen, it's clear what you're getting into. The heroically soaring cheesy guitar lick buttrock is a natural deterrent. If it turns you off then it's a safe bet Berserk Boy isn't for you. Otherwise it's likely to give you a hit of something that you've let lie dormant in you for too long. That's what it did me.
_childDocuments_.name: Berserk Boy

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun and fresh take on the Megaman style of games. Easily the funnest one I've played in a long time.I can't wait to get all the different powers and see what more this game has to offer.The mission based structure is well done. The bosses are fun and the powers are cool.This game has a lot of nice quality features as well.The constant "LIGHTNING JUSTICE!" line starts to grate on you before even finishing the first stage.. They could have recorded variations of the line to randomly play and make it occasionally not say anything because we get it after so many times of hearing it.There's a few areas where you can jump to your death without knowing there is a death zone beneath and the walls won't let you jump against them or there is a time that you're locked out of other actions after exiting some states which feels bad. I'm pretty sure this is a cardinal design sin of this genre however its at least not too bad to get back where you were before.The car zone had some jankyness to it where the screen would keep going long after I should have died. At least I was able to quit and return to my last save point without redoing the entire mission.
_childDocuments_.name: Berserk Boy

_childDocuments_.review: You play as a guy who gets different powers that let you traverse the linear levels in a fast and stylish way. The game is a teeny tiny bit jank with some interactions, but the sense of speed and flow are very fun. If you play on the "Retro" difficulty, like I did, you will have a surprisingly fair and reasonable challenge that ramps up all the way through. If you think it looks fun, you should get it.Berserk Boy is a "retro throwback" platformer where you play as Kei, a member of "The Resistance". You need to stop the city from being over run by Dark Energy (immediately, wuh-megaman). You even get to rescue reploids... I mean resistance members. You'll see a lot of inspiration from the various Mega Man games and a few different franchises. You go from stage to stage, you fight a boss after a few and each major boss gives you a new power that adds mechanics to the next stages you need to overcome. You get a standard dash in any direction, some attacking moves and some other moves that interact with the environment in a specific way. There are lots of secrets to find and collect and even a "secret ending" if you are willing to look hard enough.Just to get this out of the way, I've seen a lot of people say "This is like X Franchise" but It's far more original than it seems. While you can see where the inspirations for this game comes from, it's very much its own thing. So if you are looking for something very similar to Mega Man, this is not that kind of game. I'd compare Berserk Boy more to "Rocket Knight Adventures" than Mega Man.I know this sounds like a backhanded complement, but Berserk Boy really nails the "homing attack into enemies with health bars" thing Sonic Heroes was going for, but dash doesn't home-in. It's actually very fun. The key difference is that the enemies in this game don't have bloated health pools. Some enemies require more of your attention than a dash. Towards the end of the game you will have a comical amount of options to dispose of different enemies.I played on the Retro difficulty and I have to say I was pleasantly surprised. The game is balanced well and feels punishing enough when you don't play carefully. It's nowhere near the difficulty of a Mega Man Zero game. Spikes don't instantly kill you for one thing. My favorite thing is that many of the levels do their best to cut down on constant power switching, which can get annoying when you have all of them. I know many people (who are bad at games) think lives are outdated, but having to do the level over again when you were reckless too many times is a fair enough in this case. Especially considering you can cruise through these levels once you know what you are doing.The only thing that sours this for me is the "You are invincible" option in main menu. Usually, these options are put in place for "accessibility reasons", but also are a sign of an unbalanced game. It is not needed for this game. I have a lot of nitpicks when it comes to specific levels, but they were not annoying enough that I wanted to turn that option on.Secrets have a negative I'll get back to, but they are well hidden, but also well telegraphed. You need to pay extra attention to find them, but you don't need do something obtuse to find most of them. It's what happens when you find some of them where I have the problem. But the placement of them is really good.Please note that music is different than the audio. I promise.The music is really well done and very catchy.If this review turns you off from buying the game, I would recommend the soundtrack by itself.I'm satisfied with the graphics so this is technically a positive. However the different "Art" types feels off. The art-style differences from the cut-scenes and the in-game pixel art scream "We hired different talented artists for these two things", which ok sure. But the cut-scene and promotional art have this "fake anime" aesthetic, and the pixel art has this "Every character is wider with chibi-esc proportion" look that feels inconsistent.The non-humanoid enemy design looks dope as **** though so I'm not really upset.I give it 3/7 Metal Slugs.There are a lot of them, or at least many behaviors that present themselves as bugs. Including:* Sometimes spikes kill me from full health instead of just doing damage.* Jumping off of walls has weird interactions when doing things like changing powers or dashing.* Corner detection (Wall, Floor) seems a bit wonky when as hitting a corner. It seems to try and auto jump me off the wall. if this is intended, it does not "feel good".The audio mixing is a disaster, there is no audio ducking when people speak in cut-scenes. Many voice lines peak (too loud when recorded). It's like everyone involved with the voices were sharing a blue yeti with the gain cranked all the way up. You can turn the voices off, but you should leave it on for the main villain. I keep seeing Berserk Boy is a "Mega Man" or a "Metroidvania" or a "Rogue Like". Berserk Boy is none of those things. Unlike Mega Man, you don't pick your stage. The stages are linear and you have to do them in order, so it's not rogue-like. There are hidden collectibles, but many stages require the final power to 100% them, so you will need to backtrack in order to get everything.I don't really like this, because, other than getting a higher score (and I guess getting the secret ending), you don't really get much out of re-doing the stages. It's trivial to get an S rank if you hit every enemy on your way and don't die once.I really hate how pervasive the patented "Inti Creates spikes below ladders you can't see until it's too late" has become in "Retro-Inspired Mega Man-esc" games. I liked the Mega Man Zero games, but this is one of those things that sucks about all of them. Berserk Boy has a ton of spikes you won't see off screen. Weather you are falling, doing a ground pound, or going down a ladder really fast, there will often be spikes where you are landing. This is garbage game design. Stop putting these in your games. There is nothing fun about being encouraged to go fast but also having to deal with  spikes when you ground pound to keep your speed going. You figured out instant death spikes were ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, but you still did this? Put the spikes where I can see them. You did ok with the enemy placements, why are spikes like this?There is nothing more frustrating than finding a secret, but you either don't have the last power in the game, or you are too early in the level to have found 60% of the resistance members in the stage. Backtracking specifically for these reasons suck a lot. Everybody said it was bad when Mega Man X 3 did this and I know you played that game, so how did you make the same mistake?I'm not going to spoil it, but getting 50 Medals and fighting the final boss was very disappointing. Your attacks are so slow, the fight is more meandering than it is "Epic", which is what I think they were trying to go for. Spark 2 final boss fight this is not.Overall, I liked my time with Berserk Boy. As good as it is, it could use a bit more time to polish the less good bits. The less good bits are at like 80% though, so there isn't much to complain about really. I would highly recommend Berserk Boy, short as it is.But I guess the real question is, "is this game as good at that song by Eminem?". Almost.
_childDocuments_.name: Berserk Boy

_childDocuments_.review: This game is excellent fun! Great soundtrack, awesome feeling with the powers at high speed, breakneck pace. It has a lot of variety to the levels and a ton of secrets. Looks great (especially the special effects) And just had a fun time all around with it. While the game seems to, on the surface, be a tribute to the GBA era Mega Man games, it doesn't really play like them; its very firmly its own thing and makes the most out of everything it introduces. The only thing I would say is that, while the bosses are all cool and not exactly easy, Berserk Boy himself moves around at such high speeds with so many powerful attacks that I feel almost sorry for them - definitely a case of "I'm not locked in a room with you, you're locked in a room with me" every time. Which is not exactly a major negative as it's still a ton of fun fighting them!A highly recommended game!

_childDocuments_.review: It has been a hot minute since a 2D platformer got me like Berserk Boy has. The demo had me jonesing for more, and getting to play the full game only further encouraged my excitement over this one. The combat and platforming are approachable to newcomers, yet challenging to old heads--especially through the game's "modern" and "retro" difficulty settings, which I found to be a very thoughtful addition. The soundtrack coaxes you on throughout, and the collectibles are rewarding. Don't sleep on this one!

_childDocuments_.review: Berserk Boy turned out to be a very pleasant surprise for me. I was already sold on its art-style, combat and music from the first trailer, but now that I have completed the main story, I can confidently say that I had A LOT OF FUN playing this game!Below is a list of the main "strengths" as well as "weaknesses" that I noticed during my playthrough of the game:The gameplay in Berserk Boy is very smooth/satisfying. From the very first level, once you get your first Berserk Orb (my favorite btw), the main character (Kei) feels very strong and the way he dashes in all directions while also using that dash to take out enemies (along with his other "shock" attack) is just very addictive and never gets old (other Berserk abilities are cool as well in their own way with very smart ways to utilize each of their abilities as you progress in the story). If you are looking for a "fast-paced 2D Platformer", then you are definitely at the right place!The level structure in this game in general is a mixture between 'Mega Man X-style" levels and 'Freedom Planet-style" level design (which is a VERY good thing). Overall, I enjoyed traversing through most levels in the game and I really liked that later levels encouraged you to use different Berserk abilities to navigate through them instead of just relying on 1-2 Berserk abilities (you could do that, but I kept circulating between different abilities, which also helped me better understand how each Berserk ability worked). The levels' length are "moderate" (not too short, but not too long either) and to me I found the duration of the levels to be "satisfying" overall.I mean what can I say? The main composer for this game is the one and only  so OF COURSE I was in for a treat and boy was I right about that! ALL tracks generally fit the level they play in and different tracks reminded me of different games from the past. One track ("The Adventure Begins") sounded like it could fit as a  Another theme ("Genos X-treme Theme") sounded like it could fit as a  while majority other themes felt like they could fit as Overall, the music in this game is a BLAST to listen to and is EASILY a The voice-acting in this game is.....  to be honest. Not all dialogue was voiced and even the ones that were voiced none of them were memorable to me (aside from a few line for the main character) and my biggest problem was that most of the voiced lines were  and most of the time  and so it was very difficult to listen to what the characters were saying to begin with (shockingly, there is  as well). Overall, the game probably would've been better-off not including any voiced lines at all (aside from the "Go Berserk!" line) in my opinion. After all, better "not baked at all" than "half-backed", right?Another weaknesses I noticed is that it didn't feel like the game had enough variety of monsters that would fit each of the different zones throughout the game. I kept seeing the same enemies over and over from the first stage till the last stage and very few new enemies were introduced in-between as I progressed in the story. It's not the biggest issue for me personally (since the gameplay itself is still fun), but I would've liked more new enemies that better blend-in with the different environment of each zone IMO.Additionally, "closed sections" (where you get trapped and have to defeat a number of enemies to advance) as well as the "enemies infiltrating the home base" were a  time and time again throughout the game. Although, for me, as long as I am enjoying the gameplay itself (i.e. moving fast, killing enemies quickly with different abilities), then repetitive enemies/sections become less of a issue for me personally (but it is still a "weakness" worth highlighting nonetheless).Shockingly, the game doesn't allow you to access the "Settings Menu" from the "Pause Menu" and the only way to do so is to  It's honestly a bit baffling how the developers didn't think about making the "Settings Menu" more easily accessible through the "Pause Menu" after loading your save file. This is especially important early on when you want to adjust the "volume/resolution/customize input" as you are getting used to the game, so every time I had to save at a checkpoint (thankfully there are lots of them) before going back to the title screen to access the settings menu to adjust those settings early on.Additionally, early on I faced some "screen tearing" issues while playing in "Full Screen" mode and since there wasn't an option to turn-on "V-Sync" (another shocking omission), I had to play the game in "Bordered Window" mode which seemed to fix the screen tearing problem for the most part, at least for me personally.Other aspects like story characters, story plot, grinding for shop upgrades were all "fine" by me and were neither a clear "strength" or "weakness" and so I didn't dedicate any section for them as I had "neutral feelings" towards those aspects for the most part.Overall, despite the few issues I had with the game as I mentioned above, I can confidently say that  The gameplay, music and boss battles (which are the top 3 most important aspects of any game for me personally) have been OUTSTANDING to experience and now I'm definitely looking forward to 100% it as well as doing a 2nd playthrough of it down the road. If you are 2D Platformer fan, then I  for you! Don't miss out!(P.S: I also for a hope for "Berserk Boy 2" sequel in the future that expands the gameplay further with new "Berserk Orb" abilities, while also polishing the game further to iron-out the few weaknesses that the first game had).

_childDocuments_.review: This game's gameplay flows SUPER well, and the soundtrack is an absolute **BANGER**My main gripes are the repetitiveness of the "enemy invades safe zone" sections as well as the overly spammy voice clips on some boss fights (namely Ice Kunai and the final boss)In general, I'd recommend this game to all fans of the Mega Man ZX games.
_childDocuments_.name: Berserk Boy

_childDocuments_.review: If this was 20ish years ago it would be a B+ third-party title--not bad but not in the same tier as first-party stuff. Presentation is excellent (aside from the less-than-professional voice acting) and the level design seems to have some higher thought put into it. However, once you've seen a mechanic or enemy, that's it. They never grow or become more difficult. For example, drill claw sections in the second and last world are interchangeable.With the different forms, another reviewer put it like this and it's worth repeating: every form somehow manages to be worse than the last. The lightning/first form is highly mobile and powerful and feels great--the others, not so much. The final form can delete enemies and bosses with the infinite ammo upgrade but it sucks to traverse with.Overall this is a tentative recommend. In olden terms, it would be worth a rent. It's okay or even decent but it has a lot of things keeping it from being truly great.
_childDocuments_.name: Berserk Boy

_childDocuments_.review: this game really has a lot of that Megaman Zero and Megaman ZX influence and it shows, from the resistance base and rescuing resistance members, form changing quick menu, and most of all fast-paced unrelenting action and platforming, this really takes me back to the GBA and DS days, I highly recommend this for those who were into the Zero and ZX games back in the day
_childDocuments_.name: Berserk Boy

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very nice game. Totally recommended if you like this genre.The stages are well done with nothing that can be considered unfair. There is also indications, barriers or automatic transformation points to know the intended way to beat a section of a level. The jumping sections are difficult enough to have a challenge but not enough to conseider them impossible. It also helps you to get to know and experiment with new powers, Each time you get a new power, the first stage has a written guide of what it can do, which is very very useful to fully master each form. It is not perfect. There is things like having to watch cutscenes of a level you already beat (you can skip them), or, to my opinion, some of the upgrades being completely unnecessary since with the right transformation you can beat a boss easily. Sut, overall it is a really nice a fun experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Berserk Boy

_childDocuments_.review: When a hero comes along in a world full of turmoil it is best to just roll with the punches and go Berserk. Berserk Boy is finally here and after all this time it did not disappoint. Welcome gamers to this review of Berserk Boy. Does this fill in that missing itch of a great mega man style platformer?The story as most might know starts with our new hero Kei who gets caught up in the nefarious dealings of an evil scientist. Until he gets his hands on an orb that gives Kei tremendous powers! I mean he has to start off somewhere when going through hordes of deadly robotic adversaries. With his flying talking companion Fiore and many others embark to help Kei with his journey. It is a crazy ride throwing this kid in the middle of a war, but the resistance needs an edge and Kei is it.Gameplay:Berserk Boy follows a great formula of going through different stages, each stage broken up into parts until Kei confronts that stage orb holder. Most gamers will know where this is going as you have your base abilities until you defeat a boss and absorb their power. As you utilize your powers each one with have mid-range, close-range, defense, and all with elemental abilities. All of Kei's orbs will be used in different scenarios that might be needed. When progressing through the stages, the player will start to see a pattern that some stages will require you to use all your abilities. There is backtracking as each stage will require one of the abilities to get to certain areas.I've only unlocked 4 abilities so far and just wanted to share my thoughts before I go even further. I am hooked. Each enemy brings on a new challenge and even the stages can be its own boss fight. It comes down to patience and after each stage you will be scored on your performance which you can use those points to buy upgrades for each ability. This is where the grind comes in as you will use that replay value to go back to previous missions and get a higher score on them and more points to buy the upgrades.Visuals:Kudos to the designer of Berserk Boy the levels, the characters and the sound design are all wonderful. Very Anime and makes me wish for figurine merch or an anime in the future. Music composed by Sonic Mania composer Tee Lopes is a plus and drives the action in the right direction.Final thought:Not going to spoil anything further and being that said Berserk Boy is on sale right now at $18 from $20 which is not bad. There is massive replay value to be had and even though it is a bit tough, there is something to learn from mistakes. Players will get better as they play along. Check it out for yourself. This beast gives Berserk Boy 5 out of 5 beastly paws. - Beast Out -
_childDocuments_.name: Berserk Boy

_childDocuments_.review: It's a dang good megamanlike.There's elements of Zero and Gunvolt scattered throughout the design, and it works. It works really well. Most of the game feels extremely fluid, with only a few rough patches where the game forces you into bland, meaningless fights in between stages.Broadly, in Berserk Boy you have a set of elemental forms you can switch through, each with different traversal tech, and the stages are designed to encourage certain forms for certain areas, but mostly they just let you freestyle.The plot is sparse, and it's lighthearted nonsense in the style of classic megaman, but it doesn't really need to take center stage when everything else is so good.Core movement feels great. This game has some of the best dashes in the genre. And levels branch a lot, encourage replays, and are crammed with optional content.To get the true end you need to do some amount of backtracking, and I don't really have that time right now, but if you like the satisfaction of 100%ing platformers you'll probably have a great time here.By a similar token, I suspect this is a fantastic speed game.Overall, if you like the sorts of things I've talked about here, pick this one up at full price. Gameplay-wise, I think it's the best of the modern megaman successors, and I'd love for this dev team to have the resources to make another one.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game on a whim because I follow indie game devs on twitter and this game looks absolutely PEAK. Then I bought it and it WAS PEAK. The gameplay takes a second but as sooooon as you understand what the devs were thinking you literally start gliding through stages like butter, it's insane how they managed to keep the same general control scheme between powers but still have them all feel entirely different.In a world of £70 games that are 200GB to download, you could have an insanely fun experience for just £15 and a little over a GB.
_childDocuments_.name: Berserk Boy

_childDocuments_.review: So far I've played the first stage and there's a lot to love. The pixel art is amazing and the music absolutely slaps! Platforming feels great, the dash and combat are great (even if I get hit a lot). The levels are full of slightly hidden areas and (I'm assuming) reasons to come back after you get more abilities. The levels have at least 2 types of collectibles, plus time and score based ranking so there's plenty to do for each level. It also worked flawlessly on my Deck with Proton 8.0-5 which is always nice
_childDocuments_.name: Berserk Boy

_childDocuments_.review: Real fun action platformer! The action is fast, the music is great, the multiple form switch fast and control well, the pixel art is great, it's fun time all around!My only minor gripe is the incentive to come back to previous level near the end, and the ennemies variety being low : there's actually more than enough for a full game, but you'll fight them over and over so it become noticeable, but it's no big deal. I also wish there were more bosses, but those present do a great job. And the flow of battle really make it up for it all, fitting well with a name like 'berserk boy', your first form playing like wario but way faster!Overall, a really fun game, not perfect, but what it do well it do really well, and i'll be curious about these developpers future game. _childDocuments_.name: Berserk Boy

_childDocuments_.review: I just played BerserkBoy, and it's AWESOME!! I love how satisfying the movement is, and the combos that you can perform! The pixelart style and the OST ROCK!!! It takes me back to the Megaman X era, but this game has its own original flow! I love it!! I can't wait to keep getting more abilities and see what else I discover in the story!

_childDocuments_.review: Berserk Boy has been a blast! The game oozes with personality and style, it seems like every inch of the game knows the theme it's going for and knocks it out of the park. I've been especially impressed with how smooth the movement feels and how well the levels flow! _childDocuments_.name: Berserk Boy

_childDocuments_.review: Oh no, I've GONE BERSERK and now I can't stop BERSERKING everywhere!This game is great, super tight controls, great pixels and animation, dope soundtrack, just the right side of challenging.If you would like to feel like a child again, playing rad platformers in your neighbours bedroom for hours before being shouted at to go and play outside, then this is the game for you!
_childDocuments_.name: Berserk Boy

_childDocuments_.review: I've been going BERSERK waiting for this game to come out!The game is a blast to play, with really great feeling movement controls.The enemy design and levels are really well designed too.Personally, I feel like the soundtrack would be better if the composer pronounced his last name correctly, but other than that, it's pretty listenable.Really really well made game!

name: DREDGE
detailed_description: OUT NOW: THE IRON RIG DLC The Iron Rig is the second official expansion for DREDGE - a cosmic horror fishing adventure with a sinister undercurrent. This content adds a new constructable destination with its own story, items and adversities that can be experienced at any stage in your playthrough About the Game Captain your fishing trawler to explore a collection of remote isles, and their surrounding depths, to see what lies below. Sell your catch to the locals and complete quests to learn more about each area’s troubled past. Outfit your boat with better equipment to trawl deep-sea trenches and navigate to far-off lands, but keep an eye on the time. You might not like what finds you in the dark... Explore the Islands & Discover their Secrets Starting from your new home in the remote archipelago, ‘The Marrows’, take to the water and scour the depths for curious collectables and over 125 deep sea denizens. Explore each area while completing quests and visiting neighbouring island regions – each with their own unique opportunities, inhabitants, and secrets. Dredge the Depths Someone wants you to dig up the past, but can you trust them and will it ever be enough? Beware the Fog Danger is everywhere, so watch for sharp rocks and shallow reefs, though the biggest threats of all lurk within the fog that cloaks the night-time seas... Game Features: Unravel a Mystery: Captain your fishing trawler across a collection of remote islands, each with its own inhabitants to meet, wildlife to discover, and stories to unearth. Dredge the Depths: Scour the sea for hidden treasures and complete quests to gain access to strange new abilities Study Your Craft: Research special equipment and upgrade your boat’s capabilities to gain access to rare fish and valuable deep-sea curios. Fish to Survive: Sell your discoveries to the locals to learn more about each area, and upgrade your boat to reach even more secluded locations. Fight the Unfathomable: Strengthen your mind and use your abilities to survive trips out on the water after dark.

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed this one, it has a dark undercurrent that draws you in and makes you wonder what the hell is going on. The fishing mechanic is solid if simple, You will do a lot of cruising around the islands doing tasks for all the people you meet, not all part of the main quest. As you progress you upgrade the boat and can catch more fish. There are some minor issues such as a couple of the people you meet have unresolved story lines, whats up with the lighthouse women? Also you will have more money than you need after a while as there is no real cash dump. Despite this it looks great plays great and is tense and spooky when you are out at night. I won't spoil the end but it is sinister, also don't neglect the robed figures you come across on little islands, they are hungry. I did the whole game with 95% of side quests in about 15 hrs.
_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.review: When I first saw the trailers for this game I was thinking to myself absolutely not, but I briefly tried the demo and something about the ominous vibe of the game constantly keeps my heart racing. No joke, when it gets dark, I will close my eyes and pray I'm steered towards town.I have extreme Thalassophobia (Cannot actually play Subnautica, any games with dark waters are so unbelievably terrifying for me) and this game definitely keeps me on the edge of that. The soundtrack is great and ominous. Catching a monstrosity and hearing the deranged music always gives me a little shiver. I am sure at some point something giant is going to move under my boat and I'll have to uninstall this game. But I love Eldritch horror and this game OOZES IT.
_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.review: It took me 17h to finish the game (~95% completion) and I can very much recommend it. Well rounded experience, mentally and mechanically engaging. A very solid package. Nothing sticks out. It has variety, chill and tense moments, cozy and unnerving atmosphere.Navigating the ship is fun, especially when you can make fast dockings. Controls in general are crips and well thought out and the whole interface just feels very good. Big props to all the UX people.You can see my biggest compaints here:- Dredging for trinkets feels a bit underwhelming after a while (time/effort vs. reward wise)- Grabbing all items from crab pots could be done with fewer clicks, like in other contexts ("sell all" / "repair all")That's ALL I have to nitpick about the game.Overall, it's very easy though, I literally only died one time (30 minutes in or so).Would hope for a hardcore mode where everything is much harder and you lose everything when you die lol.Honestly, that's the only way I would play this game again, because the replay value once you done everything is straight zero.Well worth the price when it's on sale for example. I absolutely couldn't stop playing until I was done.One could say, I was ... hooked B-)
_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.review: The most fun I've had playing a PC game in years. It's like Darkest Dungeon as a chill fishing simulator. It balances the calm vibes of a relaxing game like Stardew with, at times, genuinely ominous lovecraftian horror, interspersed with moments of intense stress. I don't really know how it achieves that balance, but it does. Dredge does an amazing job of providing challenge, while offering quality of life features and never being punishing. I never once wanted to quit and come back later because of something like an unfair loss or a frustrating mechanic. As much as I enjoy the game, I do have 3 complaints. (1) Playing on a keyboard & mouse feels awkward at times. It seems like the interface was set up with a controller in mind. Now and then, I found myself repeatedly pressing the wrong key/button, while the correct key/button felt counter-intuitive.(2) There were 2 points where I got stuck for a while, not because of the challenge, but because it wasn't clear how I was supposed to proceed, In one case, I thought that a specific upgrade material was supposed to be hard to find, and was looking for it all over the place, but eventually realized it was just for sale in some shops. The other time, I was unaware of an entire method of fishing that you need to get past part of the main storyline, and messed about for quite a while before realizing there was a simple solution. Generally, it works really well that Dredge teaches you mechanics through doing, and expects you to explore its mechanics yourself. But, I wouldn't have minded some explicit information nudging me in the right direction, in those cases. (3) The only thing that comes close to a major complaint is that there is minimal endgame challenge. There's a very decent amount of endgame *content.* I could still find a number of fish and chase some achievements. But with my boat heavily upgraded, that feels more like a grind than an interesting challenge. Basically, I love the game and want to keep playing it, but I'm not finding chasing down the last few fish species as interesting as what came before.
_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.review: Could not recommend this game enough. This hit all the right spots for me thematically and was surprisingly fun mechanically. This was such an enjoyable experience. Also, at the time of writing this the game is not classified as horror, but this game has left me legitimately terrified. And I'm not talking jump scares like most other games. The feeling of dread, panic and tenseness this game was able to inflict on me is remarkable. Fantastic work from the developers
_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.review: Hyper fixation controls my life. Not only did I 100% the achievements, I caught everything there is to catch (which isn't an achievement funnily enough, I believe it doesn't include abberrant forms of crustaceans) and made all the paints (also not an achievement but i just wanted to keep playing). Atmosphere was amazing, game mechanics were fun, stories (main and sides) are intriguing and I enjoyed my short time in this world very very much. 1000% recommend giving the game a try.
_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.review: Dredge is a great indie experience. It manages be both a relaxing fishing experience and an atmospheric journey all at the same time.Visually, it has a great art style, which I imagine was the first thing that drew people into it. The music is also very good, a perfect fit for the ocean aesthetic and really spooky when it needs to be.The gameplay is quite simplistic, but also very satisfying. It's minigames are not difficult by any means, but they're still better than most representations of fishing in other games out there. The map is not too big, meaning travel feels quite satisfying as opposed to annoying. There is also a decent amount of additional side activities to engage with should you wish to explore the world some more.Even without the side stuff however, there is still a solid amount of content on offer. Beating the game took me around nine hours in total. If not for getting stuck a couple times trying to figure out what to do next, this may have been shorter, so your time may vary slightly from person to person.Overall, Dredge is a quality indie game and a standout amongst the years lack of interesting or great releases so far. I would absolutely recommend it, no matter who you are.
_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.review: I can't help but feel that I've been plunged into a Lovecraft fishing simulator and I couldn't be happier. Dredge combines very smooth gameplay with a lovely art style which results in a calming but sometimes spooky fishing experience. Although I adore fishing and collecting - and getting scared by fishes, there is a gripping story that is told via notes found and scarce character dialogue (very dark souls style) which makes it all the more appealing to see through to the end:4.5 aberrant fish out of 5 🐟🐟🐟🦑
_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.review: Although at first the game seems fun... the monotony of rinse and repeat sinks in. The missions are as soulless as politicians. There is no dialog - all txt. Also I have noticed that after just few hrs the docking procedure is doing my heading. Get close, keep pressing f for 3 seconds and the boat will adjust, then you open the store... but first you need to click twice to skip the pointless monolog message... rinse and repeat... 10... 30... 60... 100 times. Just thinking about docking and opening the store makes me hate this game.
_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic slow albeit not very long game, quite relaxing with it's rare moments of jump scares and some stressful moments.There's not much to say about this game without spoiling it... You're a lil boat and you go fishing with easy and not frustrating mini-games (for once). The spot where you can fish are clearly visible with splash of water.The move through the lovecraftian story (and there are 2 different endings), you need to accomplish various goals and puzzles along with a few side quest.You will visit, in the full version + DLC, 6 islands, the DLC will make you revisit some of those. You will also need to collect crafting materials to improve your ship and be able to fish in different part of the world.At night, you will start to slowly lose your mind and this is where troubles begin so you will need to go back to a port and sleep if you can.And that's it, really... You will wander in this open world and the time you spend with the game depends of how you like to play. From start to finish while grinding a bit, I took about 27 hours (visited everything, did all quest, did all craft and research, got both endings) but if you want to 100% the game and find all game, you will most likely spend more time than this. (I found 163 fish out of 230 and did not judge worthy to find them all)It's a very good game which makes you wish a sequel will someday show up and we'll control a sub instead of a boat.Loved the story and every characters, the art style and the music were pretty good too.If you liked Sunless Sea, you'll love this (although it's not as big and heavy with story as Sunless Sea but it's the same kind of idea, minus fuel, crew and hunger management)
_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.review: I know people are saying its overpriced for what it is, but my niece and nephews went to the movies (Super Mario) and the tickets combined to $35 bucks for the family for an hour and a half of entertainment.Collectively, between the three of them and myself, we've got 16 hours out of Dredge at the time of this post.The younger two boys care little about plot or pacing, they just like to fish and get chased by monsters lol. But my oldest niece and I both loved the endings (there are two) and the "good" ending was our favorite. The story has a lot of surprising layers that by the end, you think back on and start unpeeling. it makes for a surprising and enjoyable narrative of love, tragedy, desperation, and- optionally- redemption.Or, you can play like the boys and still have fun lol.Fun game, and I hope any future updates include a variety of boats as options, and maybe some ways to kill more of the monsters that prowl the seas.
_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.review: Dredge is a fantastic and polished game that I highly recommend. The cartoonish art-style is really charming and adds to the overall experience. I experienced no crashes and there was no lag during my gameplay.The well thought and interesting dialogues in the game are a great addition to the immersive experience. The whole story of how you end up there is intriguing and keeps you invested in the game from the start.In terms of gameplay, the game is really polished and everything works really smoothly. I didn't experience any technical issues or bugs during my playthrough.Overall, Dredge is a well-crafted and engaging game that is definitely worth your time. If you're looking for a fun and spooky adventure game with a great story, interesting characters, and a polished gameplay experience, then this is the game for you!
_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.review: Dredge is a cozy fishing game that invites you to unwind in the tranquility of mucky waters. It's a digital retreat, offering a peaceful escape from the demands of everyday life. So, grab your fishing rod, sink into the soothing embrace of Dredge and let the gentle currents carry you away. 8/10, because sometimes the coziest adventures are found in the most unexpected places.
_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.review: I find the game very engaging, although I do wish there was a better "good" ending option...anyway, I have enjoyed it enough that I gifted it to my nephew so he could enjoy it as well! The graphics are lovely, the gameplay is intuitive, and the story line is intriguing with a nice twist. The tasks even make sense to the story and seems to flow with it and add to it, instead of feeling like busy work or grinding...I am currently working on 'From the Depth' achievement so...going for 100% completion - including the DLC The Pale Reach (which I already completed 100%)
_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.review: 6.5/10If you like Fishing-minigames you will likely like this one too.A game that satisfies you for the moment, but might not stay for much longer in memory.It's a decently good fishing game and the Horror factor certainly adds a good flavor. Now having finished after 17 hours and only missing 4 achievements i wished there was more. like... more everything.Map/World:The map feels rather incomplete, every Island-area isolated with only a few random islands scattered in-between, which may or may not have side quests. I wish there where more island masses that one could explore and maybe a few bigger side-story besides the main story to discover.  Especially once you have upgraded your hull and gotten a few better engines the map will feel very, VERY small.More Towns would have been nice or rather more interesting areas to dock. The wandering merchant was a nice discovery at first, but it saddened me somewhat to see that they would appear on every island-group instead of at least another town.Fishing:The fishing is divided into dredging and fishing, where dredging is active (eg. you have to do something or you never get the item) and fishing is passive (you don't necessarily have to do anything to get the item), being active while fishing merely speeds up the process, which takes less time of the day, or potentially let's you catch a trophy fish which sells for more. There are variations on the fishing minigame, however all of them are the same with a slightly different paint-job (that's just a reference, they are not differently colored). I wish fishing had been more interactive or at least had a bigger difference between the minigames/areas/fishcategories.Panic:Panic is this games Horror mechanic, if you stay out on sea at night, in certain areas or do certain actions, your panic increases. This is showcased by an eye in your HUD that turns from closed -> blue -> green -> yellow -> red/purple and also starts to move frantically the more panicked you become.Panic causes you to see things in the dark. Rocks may suddenly appear, Ghostly islands and Ships appear but turn out to be giant fish which will ram into you to cause hull dmg. Occasionally also some kind of creature boards your cargo to infest Fish. On that note... that is it.You very quickly learn how to handle panic and in my play-thru i ignored it all-together after i had acquired the 2nd hull upgrade. Infested fish actually did not seem to have any downside. In fact it seemed to be a positive which seemed... wrong, to clarify, fish has an age, the fresher the more you can sell it for and fish will eventually rot, making it worthless. infected fish however had the same price as (fresh*) fish and did not rot, alas you could just cruise the ocean without a care.I kinda wished for Panic to toy with the player more, maybe turning all (or some->many) fishing spots into "unknown" fishing-spots, letting you fish in a delirious trance and fishing veiled fish which would take inventory space. then once you go back you sell them but it could turn out that you actually had not fished anything in the first place but you just had thought you had. ofc. that would be more frustrating, but also would make you more aware of Panic. or maybe when you fished you have a higher chance for aberrations (maybe that's already a thing, but it did not feel like that for me)?maybe some harbours would just disappear entirely or maybe an entire island region would only be accessible at x panic. that would have been cool. Sadly at this point, Panic feels to me like nothing more then a gimmick.Research:nice overall. fairly good diversity, my biggest problem however would be the Engines.I frankly can't remember what the 5-6 slot engines speed was, but the Jet engine simply topped them all. for 3 reasons.1) It's Speed per slot is very high.2) You can research it right after the first engine.3) Should your hull break, it's unlikely that your entire speed goes out the window as you likely only run jet engines.imo. it's a too good engine, it's overall performance should be lowered. (either in speed or in time it takes to research)one thing i would have also liked to see is that once you have unlocked the upgrades, you would also have to gather more resources to actually buy them (besides money) as you very quickly can go thru the entire upgrade-tree and then never have a use for materials ever again. that would also somewhat reduce the acquisition speed of upgrades. i would however only add this for rods, net's and engines. Not for crap-pots or lights.Story:A big fetch quest that makes you do only thing only in each area, often tied to a side-quest issued by a person on said islands. again, wish there was a bit more too it.Fishes:overall good variations, Abyss and Hadal seem underutilised and i would have wished for more species and generally more Hadal areas.Most of the Aberrations where pretty dang cool. good variety again here.can only tell you however. finishing the Encyclopedia is a pain as you have to catch aberrations for Moonfish, Sunfish, and the sharks which are already rare. about 30% of my game time just streamed into those 6 fish.And that's it.My review. As i mentioned, overall a good game but it could use MORE in every department. but it will likely just stay in my mind as "That one Eldritch horror Fishing game".Which a few more changes and an update that might change into "The Eldritch horror Fishing game"
_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.review: One of the only games i have 100% in. It is so amazing both in gameplay and story. It is so relaxing, but still has intrigue and amotsphere which elevates it above games such as spiritfare and stardew vally for me. There is only 1 timed quest (the hooded figures) so long as you are aware of this the game makes very few demands of you and you can take it in your own time. it does not demand too much time of you either as you can see on my time playing it. It is my favorite game of 2023.
_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.review: I really really hate horror and it scares me a lot. 10/10 game i love it. the fishing mechanic is fun and so is the puzzle of how to store your catch, and the islands and boats are really cute even when its 2 am and theres something behind you thats catching up to you slowly but surely and nothing seems to stop its movement, not even the light of the buoys. you cant see past the fog and youre not sure if youll be safe even if you stay at a harbor. you cant check behind your or youll run into the cliffside. you dont know if its still behind you, but the music and the flashes of sick lights says its still there. really good game :]

_childDocuments_.review: DREDGE is a relaxing horror game. I am a quarter of the way through all the tech tree. I've finished a third of the Story line and finished 1 of the 5 islands, I've visited 3 though. The game is nerve racking and intense. The most this game should ever cost is $40 but its well below so that's good. _childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.review: A fun and simple game that I believe serves as an excellent starting point for those stepping into this genre, a "babies first" introduction to Eldritch Horror. By no means it that an insult, rather a recommendation to anyone who has not or rather not play(ed) an cosmic or eldritch horror style game. The fishing mechanic is fun and regularly mixes itself up, the story is short and simple, but keeps enough depth to enthrall our attention, and does not force anyone's hand or rush the player. The eldritch elements are still disturbing with a whimsical flare, the first time i fished up a mutant i was like "EW! ... but its kind cute tho". All the hidden Pursuits and puzzles were fun and offered decent rewards to help tide over the player until better equipment can be researched and purchased, they are also wickedly designed and i would love to set a real set sometime. and the story itself plays out right under your nose, though nothing is overtly said or concluded. you need to be smart enough to catch on. All in all I'd give it a 9/10, their were a couple of areas that never let up on the threats and that made fishing the encyclopedia to completion more than a little frustrating.
_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.review: In its current state, no I would not recommend the game. For multiple reasons:1. Pricing, you pay a quite high amount for ONLY 10-15 hours gameplay2. Replayability, there is NO replayability whatsoever, NONE. You finish the end quest and thats it, youre done with no reason to play again. I 100%ed it in one playthrough, you dont need to do a second.3. Content, there is really not much to do in the game. Its just a fetch quest over and over tbh, which isnt all that exciting. Like point 2, in endgame you dont do anything, youve probably maxed out your ship and equipment, theres no point doing anything afterwards because its all doneI would hardcore LOVE this game if there were endgame stuff. I was talking with friends about it being kinda lackluster even though I think the setting and atmosphere of the game is great. My ideas probably dont fit the creators intent for the game, but i think itd be really cool to have bigger game (as in creatures not videogame) that you could battle, maybe you can battle and catch the mother lava fish thing, or have some other large creature. Maybe you build a house or fish processing factory on an island. Yknow, stuff that'd make the game worth sinking more hours into, something to build up towards.Currently you complete the story and thats it, you never touch it again, because there is no game, only story. _childDocuments_.review: No spoilers here.I just finished my first playthrough and I absolutely love this game, to the point that I plan on replaying it to find secrets and side-stories that I missed. Cannot recommend this one enough, and it's fairly priced for the quality and length.Highlights:-Fishing doesn't get boring. The array of fish, environmental threats, fishing styles, and the strangeness of the night makes it great fun. You always wonder what new monstrous things you'll find. You always hope you'll stumble across that one part you're missing.-The crafting element is simple but very well-laid out. It's not overly hard to find what you need, and you get extra bits and valuables often enough that it's very rewarding to hunt for materials.-The missions and stories are mysterious and engaging, and each area has an awesome central theme and creatures unique to the environments.-The mysteries are just open-ended enough to let your mind make up scary stuff on its own. The human mind is incredible at concocting horrors beyond description, so the writers expertly leave a lot of room for your imagination to make the horror for them. The fog. The lights. The strange shapes. The wrecks. The cloaked figures. Your brain will make them much scarier than they are just because they are completely unknown and anything could happen. And the sheer variety of things that actually DO happen on-screen suggest that multitudes of much worse things could happen.-This game is out to kill you, but it's also very fair. If you lose things due to being damaged, you can always get them back. In fact, I only found a couple things that you can't recover or redo, and they did not harm the main story at all.Overall, this is a fantastic light horror and mystery game that I truly believe is perfect for all types of players, even those who don't like horror. There are no outright jumpscares and most of the horror element is at night, which can be avoided for a majority of the game. The only people I wouldn't recommend this to are those with a genuine phobia regarding the ocean, or those who don't enjoy fetch quest-style games. The majority of the gameplay is travel, nicely-done fishing minigames, and collecting items. It is very easy to play but takes some doing to master as you deal with harder navigation due to environmental dangers. And the ending goes wonderfully unexplained in a way that just makes your brain race. I wanted to write a Lovecraftian-inspired story immediately afterward.Worth picking up at full price to support these awesome devs!

It has the same fear as Sunless Sea (To some extent) but the tone and vibrance of Stardew Valley. It is probably the best Thalassophobic horror game (Deep Ocean Horror) since Subnautica. Words cannot convey how good this game is, and the quests and challenges are even better. My recommendation is this... _childDocuments_.review: "Dredge" is a small and simple game that combines various elements to create an immersive experience centered around the uncertainty and fear of the ocean. the exploration channels Outer Wilds vibes, where there is little direction and the limited but detailed world allows you to put the story together yourself as you play. With 30% exploration, 30% fishing mini-games, 30% inventory management, and 10% worrying about the dark, the game offers a unique twist on a casual collection game. The art is beautifully done, and the music and sound design enhance the atmospheric ambiance. While not particularly long or challenging, it's enjoyable to play and relax while catching fish. The game's cosmic horror theme leaves you with unanswered questions and intriguing mysteries about the world. It presents cosmic entities indirectly through mutated fish, distant shapes, and fragments from an ancient civilization. If you enjoy chill games and cosmic horror, "Dredge" is recommended. It's also worth 100%, as it showcases everything it has to offer without being overly difficult, and you can obtain both endings and all achievements in a single playthrough.The DLC was a nice fresh evening of content, and I recommend buying it to support the devs.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr -  Love this game so far! A unique adventure RPG with interesting gameplay mechanics and a unique visual style that both set it apart from many of the adventure games I've played! 100% recommend!I actually wishlisted Dredge BEFORE people started playing it on YouTube because it appeared in my discovery queue and I remember just seeing the screenshots and immediately falling in love with the art style of this game. It's simultaneously beautiful and unsettling in just the right kind of way! This game reminds me a little bit of a cartoon I used to watch back in the 2000's titled The Misadventures of Flapjack art direction wise, although that show was WAY more unsettling, and I gotta admit, I'm oddly into it!In terms of gameplay and story, I'd pretty much call this an adventure RPG, and I've only scratched the surface! The fishing and dredging minigames are both quite fun and I like them a lot! Overall, this game is already very unique from the other adventure games I've played in terms of how it's structured. I like the way the "inventory" takes the form of your ship and the fishing equipment, lighting, and engines take up space the same way items do, and the way certain items take up more space than others or fill space in awkward shapes creates this sort of limited feeling to the inventory, and this contributes to another thing I really like about this game, there's this constant need to run back to a town not only to unload your inventory but also to avoid getting stranded out at sea in the fog at night, and I know this is only in my mind, but I can't help but compare that to the rush to get back to administration before the generator runs out in Amnesia: The Bunker, it's definitely the same type of tension, anyway, and I gotta admit, I'm really into it! This is also the first game I've ever played where time only passes when you're moving or doing something, which is also quite cool! I'm also getting pretty invested in the story now. The world this game is set in seems a lot more H.P Lovecraft inspired than I was expecting and I find that really cool because most of the time Lovecraft inspired games tend to be horror games and it's refreshing in a way to see a game that isn't a horror game, at least not in the traditional sense, utilize Lovecraftian storytelling and world-building tropes the way this game does. Overall, I'm enjoying this game a lot so far, and I can't wait to see what else is in store.I AM playing this game on a controller, by the way. Steam says that Dredge is "mostly playable" on an X-box controller, but so far the controller support seems fully built in and functional, so if that's worrying you, then fear not!

_childDocuments_.review: No, I would not recommend 'Dredge'.I had to quit. Decided to call it. I was forcing myself to play the game in short bouts and each time was a mind numbing experience. The game is dull and boring. It quite simply misses the mark. Never got investing in the gameplay or story.I'd guess the 'mark' is that they intended this to be a scary horror game. It isn't. Not in the slightest. Too bright. To clear. Nothing is a threat or danger. The graphics lend themselves poorly to the theme of the game. Its all from the perspective of top down boat view. I get that its an indie title. I just kind of wish they could get a redo on this. The theme is good. New fisherman. Everything seems fine. It isn't fine. Weirdness ensues. Creepy vibes. Lovecraft influence. "Dredge" just misses the bullseye and by too much.I'd like to put forth a suggestion. Play "No One Lives Under the Lighthouse" in the Dread X Collection. Ignore the weird bug thing and just take in the aesthetic. Its gloomy. Its gritty. Its bleak and unsettling. And its low poly low res. That's kind of the vibe I think Dredge needed. If there is a supernatural fog blanketing a region, you shouldn't be able to see across the ocean. Even at night, you can see landmasses on the horizon. I would think you'd want that, "Uh oh its night and I'm lost in an evil fog playing tricks on my brain."I also think it would do a world of good if you had a character. I'm talking first person immersion that is impossible in top down isometric games. Imagine that whenever you travel, the game shifts to first person at the wheel of the ship. Fog setting in. Night looming. Weird noises scratching and taping at the hull. What was that? Stop and inspect. Walk around your little boat. Guess it was nothing. Head to town to sell fish.  The radio frequently shifting to static white noise. You give it a few slaps. There we go. People that eat the fish get sick. Start acting weird. Everyone that didn't blames you. Now you have to worry about the people and the monsters. Well done you goof! Geez ya boned that up quick!I can play modded Minecraft with shaders and my gpu fan is nice and quiet. This game makes it really ramp up and I'm not sure why.Lastly, it reminds me of something you might have played back in the Flash game website days. I couldn't shake the feeling that I'd done something like this before. I think I played a pirate game where you are in a similar island setting and selling goods to ports. Which is what you do in this game. Sid Meier's Pirates? I remember reading something about pirates from an npc in Dredge so maybe that was a wink to that pirate game?I feel bad for giving this a nasty mean RED thumbs down. In truth, its a very grey 'meh' game. I'm sure some people would enjoy it. So if you are reading this keep in mind... reviews have little value and personal experience will always top it. The game is fairly affordable and still being developed. I didn't like it. You might. Only one way to find out.
