_childDocuments_.review: It's definitely a good game, but it also has some major shortcomings that left me a little disappointed.Let's start with the good stuff and work our way down.The fishing minigames are phenomenal and the way that different fish have different shape as a component of inventory management makes for a truly exceptional mechanic.The lore descriptions on the aberrant fish are absolutely top tier Lovecraft horror. Just so good! I can vividly imagine some of them, such as the defaced skate. Great stuff!The graphics, music, and overall atmosphere are very solid as a package. Very clear art, sound, and style direction. Excellent work!The story is pretty okay. If you spend any time at all talking to obviously important NPCs, you can probably predict the entire story before you're 1/4 of the way through it, just like I did. If you look at my achievements, you can see I have only the secret ending. This was not difficult to find and I went through the game entirely blind.Let me give you a huge spoiler about literally every story in every game ever, especially indie titles:There is one NPC that handles all of your sales, upgrades, research, and resupply. They even sell the rare components for upgrades and her inventory refreshes. She also sells the unlockable "crafted" items and she's never very far away. This one-stop-shop makes every non-fishing mechanic feel cheap and simple. Why bother travelling anywhere when I can just farm crabs directly in front of the one NPC that can unlock everything.The horror elements are actually kind of weak. The game breaks the "don't show the monster" rule very early, and consistently exposes you to the monsters directly. There were certainly some surprises in this part of the game, but nothing iconic or memorable (except for one event that happened to me only one time that I don't want to spoil). The worst part is that during the day, everything is fine, but during the night, the entire world becomes saturated with hazards, so you're constantly exposed to what should be a mostly imaginary threat. It shouldn't be so obvious.Also, you're rarely required to go out at night, so you can totally ignore this part of the game most of the time. The game is at its best when you're trying to get home for the night, slowly navigating a treacherous waterway in the dark while being hounded by some imaginary threat. Sadly, this is extremely rare and is often overshadowed by silly monster antics and actual threats. If the map was better, this could have been a common occurrence, but this brings me to my final point.The map is dull. It's extremely uniform and evenly distributed, the fishing locations are hyper-delineated, the islands are super close together, every island is marked and every island has a point of interest, so there are zero reasons to explore anywhere that you cannot directly see, and in that regard, you can see everywhere from anywhere unless there is something in the way.I know the devs are planning a lot of updates that I will be eagerly watching, so here is my wishlist:And more than anything, I really wish the islands were a lot further apart and you were forced to face your fears and sail the open seas in the dark. Take away 90% of the "spooky" things in the dark because they're far too common and are mostly a nuisance, and then scale the map to be 400% further between destinations.Let me be clear, I loved the game. It was a great experience overall, but it did leave me longing for a lot more. The greatest strength of the game is the core fishing mechanic and the subtle horror of the mutated fish, and yet weirdly, that somehow takes a back seat to gimmicky threats in the dark and bizarre "boss" fish that I suppose are meant to scare you but mostly just act as a nuisance that prevent you from fishing.Anyway, if you like fishing games and driving a cute little boat, play the game. It's a really good game. It deserves the rating that is has been given.

_childDocuments_.review: The game I recently quickly fell in love with.Whilst on the surface it is a chill game about a fisherman that lost his memories and wants to make a living fishing to keep a small town fed, gradually the tone shifts towards something more supernatural and lovecraftian. This combination of genres in a game played out at sea goes hand in hand and during my playthrough I've encountered as many beautiful environmental scenes as well as many spooky and straight up scary moments. Although I wouldn't consider the game to be scary, it handles these tense moments very well.As I don't want to spoil too much I won't go into the details of that and would rather add that I loved the fishing and dredging mini-games as well as the inventory management. I was skeptical of the prospect of having to fish all game long as in many games it becomes very boring after a while, but for a game this length I found they had a really good variety of options. Standard fishing with a rod, automatic fishing by dragging a net through the sea and caging crabs in pots combined with the right amount of biomes and habitats made it a joy and not a chore to catch all of the fish!All in all it was a very nice game, reminding me of slime rancher and stardew valley, and if updated in the future I might give it a go again.

_childDocuments_.review: I usually don't write reviews, but this game is too good not to, especially with the release of the Cold Reach DLC and the planned release of another DLC next year which looks to be just as good if not better. First of all, the sound design of this game is truly amazing, and it's one of the few OSTs I actually listen to when not playing the game. Most of it is very relaxing, but in certain areas the soundtrack definitely amplifies the fear of the unknown and the lovecraftian vibes.Although the gameplay loop is somewhat simple: catch fish and dredge for parts to bring both back and earn money to upgrade your ship and get better equipment, it's also so much more than that. Each NPC you meet along the way has a unique voice and narrative (except for maybe the "figure(s) in [colour]") that make them stand out and make the world feel genuine.  The quests you get can be a challenge to complete, but they also are rewarding, either giving you something to progress the story or just to make your life easier (ie books, upgrade parts). Speaking of which, the story. The story, although seemingly simple, is one of the best stories that I have seen in a video game. Without spoiling anything, I would say that although the story's straightforward, you can pick up both background information and clues to the ending(s) throughout your playthrough which help you to understand the ending(s). If you're concerned about the replayablity of the game, I will say that it is still just as fun a second or third time around, especially if you're trying to get either fish or notes or books that you missed. It doesn't have the same impact as the first time when you're wondering what the story is, but it is still very fun. This isn't even mentioning the "Cold Reach" DLC, which adds another layer of worldbuilding and the fact that another DLC is supposed to come out next year. I definitely think the game is worth the $25 price tag, but if you're concerned about that then you can always wait for a sale, especially if you're planning on getting DLC(s) with it.

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't finished the  game yet, but making steady progress, doing quests, upgrading my ship and exploring the world. And I think it's safe to say that this is a beautiful little game. It is SO relaxing to cruise around and fish, and at first, that's what you do, exploring the area and enjoying the ambience. The artwork is quite beautiful and the soundtrack definitely adds to the atmosphere. The fishing is a rather simple mini game, so it's a pretty relaxing activity. However.. slowly but surely, some creepy undertones start to appear, and you'll see that not everything is so peaceful. I was intrigued by the "Lovecraftian" tag in the Steam store, and yes, it has some of that vibe to it, even though this is not any kind of an adaption of HPLs work. There is a lot to explore, there is some grinding to do in order to get upgrades for your ships, but it never feels TOO grindy. Just do some fishing while you work on finishing those quests, or put in a couple of days of fishing to have a relaxed time. I can't wait to see how it all plays out, and I have enjoyed those 7 hours quite a bit. If you're into mystery and adventure games, if you like fishing mini games, if you like relaxed games with some tension and suspense in there, give this one a try, it's a wonderful little game!

As you upgrade your ship, it becomes more of a sandbox/collectathon experience, which is not necessarily bad, but it is a bit of a weird transition. _childDocuments_.review: A compact adventure game that mix cosmic horror with fishing, a unique premise to say the least.Dredge is a pretty casual adventure game that has you fish for money, upgrade your boat and equipment, and solve problems that originate from the mysterious beasts of the sea. Most games include fishing minigames as comfortable and safe pastime, they're engaging in way that doesn't put sudden death in front of players, and can be done for as long as the player likes. Fishing in Dredge is rather different. Minigames to fish up creatures below can be fun, but nothing more than simple quick-time event, no reeling or fighting the increasingly stubborn fish. It almost feels like, a job, which it essentially is, since you're just a fisherman.What sets your character apart from other men at sea, is the fact that you're haunted by something - something deep in the ocean. It's your quest to explore about the archipelago to find pieces of the puzzle, and unlock the answer.  A lot of things around these lands and water are not as they seem. Trying to figure out the truth or even getting scared by the many horrifying elements is exciting all the way through.Unlike the strikes of horrors, progression in Dredge is smooth and thought out well. The simulation part of this game lets you fix up and upgrade your own ship. Managing storage spaces and picking which fishing equipment to install for each venture are engaging and immersive. Installing fishing net can catch fish passively over time, but it also takes up a lot of space and requires regular maintenance, for example.Apart from your pursuit of the truth, there are also side quests all over the many islands. Some ask for fish, some ask for rare and rotten fish. And since you have a functional transportation, delivery of packages or even people can spice up the fishy gameplay loop.A trophy catch of an indie game, give this a try if you're not scared of fishing.
_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.review: This is mostly a game of exploration. And fishing. The goal is to catch different kinds of fish in different regions. The problem is, as you'll learn, not all of these fish are "right". There's a sinister force in this water and you have to do your best to avoid it while you collect relics from four different areas, avoiding hazards and solving how to navigate dangerous waters. It's a fresh take on what would otherwise be a tedious game. Without it, the gameplay would fail. But I like the graphics, the atmosphere. _childDocuments_.review: While it is so far enjoyable and an 8/10 and you should get it, I do think it's worth noting that "Lovecraftian" is a bit of a stretch, given how it was marketed. The trailer (which is closer to what I would call lovecraftian) makes it seem like what is for the most part really a very light game seem like a heavy dose of forlorn existential dread, which it just isn't, not even close. If monsters and light magic elements are all it takes to make something lovecraftian, then it is I suppose. But tentacles alone do not a lovecraftian tale make. This is more of a saturday cartoon lovecraft than an adult version. Much of the game is bright, the music is mostly up beat or neutral, filled with people rather than isolation, and their tone is pretty cheery or comical. I would say if you're looking for the sort of vibe you get from reading lovecraft, sunless seas or skies is far closer.It's more diet-lovecraft.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not bad, it's just not worth 25€. There is some creative decision making and exploration lying around, but it's mostly about getting ordered to go from A to B to C and mindlessly checking things off a list. Off-the-rails content does not offer any relief from this tedium and instead will suddenly have you sail over half the map and back just to catch a single crab you happened to need. The game has its moments, but the core gameplay loop is too short. After some time, you will want to ignore the paranoia mechanic because it's up almost all the time; the penalty of reaching dawn without having rested isn't negligible however, such that half your time in the game is spent idly sailing back to the port from where you came. It's one of those games where progressing the story and playing the game are polar opposites.How to fix the game isn't obvious. However, a good start would be to remove bloat mechanics such as crab pots and nets and instead capitalize more on the core fishing mechanic available from the start. It was painful to see how little the game expanded on it over its course.

_childDocuments_.review: Platinum Review:Dredge is a brilliantly paradoxical Lovecraftian Fishing Simulator that I fell for hook, line, and sinker. It sows a feeling of being watched through its simple art style, haunting music and sound effects, and unsettling cast. It pays great attention to detail and is one of the few games that I read every single splashtext for every fish to be immersed in its creepiness. It tows the line of horror which is perfect for those who like the frightening atmosphere but don't appreciate jumpscares. The gameplay itself is enjoyable and scratches the achievement-hunter itch. Each of the five game areas have quests, upgrades, ports, NPCs, and a big encyclopedia of fish to catch include rare mutated variants. Many fishing simulators create a seemingly endless supply of fish and variants that do nothing to add content, and just suck away your time (I'm looking at you Sea of Thieves). This game nailed the perfect amount of variation to make it the main focus, but without making searching for the right fish a chore. The story is alright. It's not amazing, but has a nice twist and is certainly better than many triple-A games in recent years.The way the game builds the world through your traveling speed is fantastic. At first you can only barely venture out to the first few fishing holes only to scurry back when it gets dark. Through upgrading your ship you access better engines and gear and can venture out to distant islands. Before you were dock hopping to avoid the monsters that lurk in the night, at the end of the game you're flying around at 100 knots and it suits the size of the map perfectly. I have a lot of respect for the developers. They have done a lot to listen to the community and add QOL and desired features. When I first played there were some fun quests that, unknown to the player were timed, and were permanently unavailable if failed. This was disliked by much of the community, so the timed aspect was removed. I'm excited to see what Black Salt Games will come up with next.My favorite part of the game was the length. This is a game that respects your time. You can 100% the game in 20-25 hours, and can have a great time in 5-15 completing the main story and exploring the islands. I'm tired of forever games giving me a part-time job instead of a relaxing experience. Overall, definitely worth the money, and secures a spot on my top ten list for a unique experience that respects your time and ties a bow on a complete package.

_childDocuments_.review: What a great journey. As a Lovecraftian mythos fan I got to say I loved the various story element adaptation and the shape of this universe. Great atmosphere and story. There were quite a few subtle Lovecraftian twists I really appreciated.Gameplay is essentially fetching stuff, but all game mechanics and progression put into perspective - it got never dull or boring. You are never made to grind, but sometimes you got to try harder and overcome RNG. Journey was never tedious or feeling like wasting my time. Everything is placed with intent, if you are curious and explore a bit, you will find everything and you will experience everything the game has to offer without any help of guides. There is no unnecessary backtracking, multilayering zone locking behind progression or other 'smart' ways to recycle same content.I loved how game progress, how your character and vessel progress - things become kind of harder, but the upgrades you pick up makes you less careful and more in control of various high-risk situations.As I finished it 100% plus the DLC, my only complaint is that it could have had few more main pursuits and few more zones. Style is gorgeous, kudos to the people who worked on the art.All in all, if you love Lovecraft mythos, this one is a no brander, creators definitely did not do dirty on this one.

_childDocuments_.review: An incredibly atmospheric exploration game that alternates between relaxing and frantic. Dredge is very tightly designed with its gameplay loops, perfectly juxtaposing the calming nature of fishing, trawling, and piloting your boat with the incredibly tense moments of navigating in the fog with a full cargo or trying to escape unseen terrors of the deep. The fishing is simple but fun, the grid inventory system forces the players to manage their cargo and make careful decisions about what to take and what to discard, and navigation is smooth and effortless yet still has persistent threats that will reward caution and punish recklessness. It's a very absorbing experience thus far.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game today and have played for 3 straight hours before taking break for lunch and coming back for 2 more. The game play is a simple but addictive loop. Both work perfectly well (controller is fully supported) but the heavy focus on Resident Evil style inventory management make the mouse/keyboard a better fit in my opinion.I don't have a Steam Deck, but the dev says it's fully supported. I could see this being a perfect way to play the game at home or on the go. The game can be saved any time you're at a dock (maybe more, haven't tried a at-sea save) and the game can easily be played for 15 min on a train commute or for 5 hours like I have. Well done Black Salt Games and Team17... you have a hit on your hands in my eyes.

_childDocuments_.review: dredge is a good game. the atmosphere is spot on. its presentation is great, the artwork hits the spot, the music and sound design is well done. the fishing mini-games are fun. there's secrets to find, places to explore. dredge is a good game.but...i can't shake the feeling that it ultimately is a bit underwhelming. it all sort of falls apart at the end. it doesn't do enough with its premise. once your boat is fully upgraded, fishing becomes pointless because you don't need the money. once you've got decent engines on your boat, most of the danger goes away. the main plot, while "fine", feels underdeveloped. there's only about 5 fishing mini-games, and they don't really advance in complexity or mechanics. the secrets mostly just involve "go catch this fish for me". there just feels like a lot of lost opportunity here to do something amazing. i enjoyed my time with it, but...dredge is a good game. i just wish it had been a great game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an amazingly designed and polished game; I could not put it down until I finished it and figured out as many little secrets and optional quests as I could. In fact I'm still going back and trying to find a few that I missed. The art style is beautiful, the gaming mechanics are simple but enjoyable, and the plot quests and upgrade systems really push you along in your progress well. I wouldn't exactly call it a horror game, but it has plenty of spooky, lovecraftian atmosphere and some moments that make you say 'nope', and turn right back around. All in all, I really enjoyed the experience and would definitely recommend it to anyone that wants to experience something fun, addicting and unique.HOWEVER ---vague, minor spoilers; ye have been warned--- My only complaint is that the endings were pretty disappointing and unfulfilling. While there were a couple of endings to get depending on your choices in the end of the game, both of them were very simple and felt rushed. There was no final epic battle or long cut scene, just sort of a 'arrive at location, click button, the end'. The ideas behind the two endings were great, and I really wished they would have spent more time on them as it felt like they deserved more. I think they were supposed to be two emotional and impactful conclusions to an otherwise great game, but I'll admit when I got to it I just sat there and thought, "...Was that it?...".So yeah, other than the rushed endings, this game was very fun and I can't deny that I really enjoyed playing it the rest of them time. Was definitely worth the money (and so was the artbook!).

_childDocuments_.review: I am obssessed with this game. Since i got it I tried  limiting myself so I wouldn't finish it too fast but i couldn't help myself because it was SO adictive.They really NAILED the lovecraftian atmosphere, it's a major part of why i keep coming back to the game and replaying. The slow building of tension, especially at the beginning where you might be too afraid to get out very far from the initial island..The little pieces of dialogue that make you go????? in the middle of an otherwise normal conversation really make it.Second good point is the music, man, I never got bored of it, i even listen to it outside of the game when I'm drawing and want to get inspired. The soundtrack is gorgeous and features both really? soothing tunes? for when you're fishing during the day, and the shift to menacing with the sun setting is fantastically executed, that goes for the sound design too.The scares were good throughout, I liked the creatures, but past some point you get used to them, the abnormalities are way too fun to collect though, highly recommand the game just for those.The addictivre parts came from updating my ship, i just kept on teling myself "just one more fishing trip so i can get that new rod!" and then you're two headlamps and a motor deep-I was pleasantly surprised by the side quests you get, there aren't that many and they may not all be epic, but they do have some repercussions on the universe around you and some really made me feel for the characters. Most of all I was sad when it ended, I wish the game was longer, its perfectly paced and definitely not too short, but i wanted to stay in that universe for longer.Overall, this is a fantastic fishing game (unironically) and the horrors offer a very nice combo, the main story itself might not be too complex but it was still nice

_childDocuments_.review: Dredge is a masterwork of "beauty in the simplicity". The gameplay, art, music, and story all create a perfect environment to immerse yourself in. The story and gameplay in particular unfold in sync, beginning you in the shallows of the center of the map with limited range and room to grow as you gain the means to travel further and further out. You're given the feeling of being a very small fish in a very big ocean, and the ever-present sense of MANY things lurking deep beneath the surface for you to discover. Without a doubt this game has one of the best reveals I've ever seen, leaving you looking back to realize it was all staring you in the face right from the start.Likewise, the two DLCs make for excellent additions that mesh into and expand upon the world. The fact that the Pale Reach was an "apology" because the developers weren't able to release the DLC they WANTED to in a timely manner amazes me, because at no point does it ever feel like something that was just thrown together. It's a bit more self-contained than the newer one, but rewarding with the items you earn from it. The Iron Rig on the other hand is much more entwined with the rest of the map, the effects of the drilling being felt in every corner. I absolutely LOVED progressing with the events it set in motion, and you can earn many scientific tools to improve every aspect from fishing, to salvage, to even just how your boat controls. Also it's just really fun watching the rig get bigger and bigger as you help build it.I truly hope that the devs are encouraged by my words and others' to continue exploring the world that Dredge presents. What are the various giant beings we've encountered? Where did they come from? What is the Ironhaven Corporation? They don't even have to answer these questions, I'd be perfectly happy with another DLC that leaves me asking more because this game does a phenomenal job investing me so that I WANT TO KNOW. There are still large portions of the outer edges of the map to the West, East, and North that remain untouched, so there's plenty of room for something like the Pale Reach to appear from the mists or rise from the depths.
_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.review: Saying that I recommend this game is a VAST understatement. DREDGE is an amazing game that plays its part wonderfully and doesn't stretch itself out for too long. _childDocuments_.review: Thumbs middle review, but given the need to swing one way or the other, I go thumbs down.TL:DR - it's a really long fishing mini-game with exploration and some insanity/survival mechanics that mostly don't feature if you're playing even vaguely strategically - it's basically just time management the game. Chill and pleasant, but there's not much beyond that, and that's a weird descriptor for an ostensibly unsettling Lovecraftian tale. Buy it on sale with an expectation of a short ride.Play the first 90 mins of the game. Then make a decision if you want to do that for ~8 more hours. The gameplay/strategy really doesn't change much. Ever. There are a couple neat alterations to the formula, but they're incredibly basic and almost un-notable despite seeming major in context. On the positive side - the devs got the basics right. They kicked the ♥♥♥♥ out of the basics. Which is really good, because the basics are all you get. If they hadn't, no-one would play this for more than an hour because there's nothing else there.On the negative side - there is almost nothing to this game beyond a quite competent fishing mini-game, and some decent writing with a couple of dissatisfying and non-descriptive endings (and a bunch of sidelines that just have no real resolution, or quests that end in "and then everything was normal and you never talked about it"). A game that's meant to be creepy and unsettling is mostly just "oh, I caught a weird fish", or "oh, in this one specific area there's a weird mini-boss". It is incredibly easy to avoid the "panic" meter in almost all circumstances, so I genuinely mostly have no idea what that even did. Expect no creeping dread, and expect whatever spooky things you encounter to have absolutely no explanation. The lack of dread is pretty much the game's greatest failure. To play an ostensibly Lovecraftian game set on the ocean that provided almost no dread is a contradiction in promise vs delivery. Also a lot of story-lines end with half-assed resolutions at best. The game is 30 odd dollars. I spent 10 hours on it, and there is no reason for me to spend more. If 3$/hour is a satisfying cost/value proposition for you, then grab it. Just know that the game is less interesting as time passes. I know game production is expensive, and that the prices put on games these days are nuts relative to cost, but in terms of audience expectations I'd have to price this game around 15-20$. I will certainly never pick this game up for a second play.A final point - I genuinely don't understand why this game is receiving "Overwhelmingly Positive" reviews, many of which say it's a 9/10 game. It's 6/10 at best, and that's just because the fishing gameplay is competent, but the devs really nailed the basics re: feel and show.  The art is... questionable? Good, but only if you like this very modern "let's use the fact that all computer graphics are triangles as a style" played to the extreme for human models. The music is... there? It's functional and competent, but nothing about it is notable or memorable. The sound design is mostly solid, but nothing to write home about (though this is mostly just a feature of sound design - it's usually only bad or unnoticeable). The writing is good, but regularly without resolution (both narratively and rewardly). Overall the game is definitely at best a 6/10 - better than an average pass, but not by all that much.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. If you've played Sunless Seas before, it's a very similar vibe and setting, but with much lower stakes. _childDocuments_.review: Dredge is a game best described as "just enough." Just enough story, just enough fishing, just enough variety.Just enough pelagic nightmares and horrors of the deep.Dredge is a unique and well-put-together game about fishing, with some horror elements thrown into the mix. The story serves it's purpose as a driving factor, both for the plot and your curiosity. When the story falls short, the atmosphere and artstyle pick up the slack. There's enough variety in the different mechanics of the game that they don't get tedious. To some people, the game might be a little short for the price tag but I think it was "just enough" to hook my interest and reel me in.Playtime: 28.8 hours for two full 100% playthroughs.Update 1.1-1.3 Playtime: 2.0 additional hours for 100%.Pale Reach Playtime: 2.0 additional hours for 100% (with endgame ship and equipment). - While the story might be pretty simple, I really enjoyed the worldbuilding itself. It has great atmosphere, both during the day and the night, has charismatic characters, and encourages you to be curious about things. - One of the better minigames that I've seen. There's a few different styles and sizes that help to break up doing the same thing repeatedly. It's quick to pick up, and not too difficult, but rewards being good at it. I didn't get tired of it at all during my playthrough. Satisfyingly simple. - There's  (now 151, or 174 with Pale Reach) different fish in the game including aberrant variants. They're spread fairly even across the different zones.   - The game is a fishing game first, and horror game second. A few parallels I could draw are Sunless Sea, Subnautica, and Darkest Dungeon. It's the type of horror that's a result of worldbuilding and suspense than anything else, and I love that. -  added Passive Mode, for any faint-hearted players out there. It also added the ability to turn off the effects while using  which was much appreciated. - It's pretty bare-bones and straightforward. I did enjoy  and I think they did a very good job leading up to it. However, I still think it does a good enough job getting you interested and wanting to learn more. - It took me 15 hours to 100% achievement the game. This might be too short for some people. For me it's "just enough" as I said before. I ended up playing through it again with all the tips and tricks I picked up the first time around. Total playtime for two 100% playthroughs was 28.8 hours. Second time wasn't much faster, but I completed the four (previously) missable quests without failing some of them the second time around. - The way you upgrade your boat is pretty linear. I don't mind that so much, but I wish it was a little more customizable once you got an upgrade. I know the boat is set up the way it is so the TETRIS-style inventory isn't too easy, but it would be nice to have a little more choice over where things go. - Game doesn't require multiple playthroughs to get all achievements, even though  -  added the Photographer with a small quest to unlock photo mode. Personally not for me, but I know that a lot of other people would probably appreciate the feature. Likely best used with the Passive Mode previously mentioned. -  added the Painter with boat customization! There's now the option to change the color of your roof and your hull independently of each other, as well as add a flag or bunting. There's 8 possible paint colors, and 8 flags (including no flag). - They added map markers in . They're okay, and nice in a pinch, but they lack customization. Can't name them, so you still need to remember what they were for. Best used for a few things, instead of charting the whole map. In my opinion the icon on the map for them is also too huge to be usable. They're like, 10x the size of the crab pot marker. Bonus QoL is that you can see them using the telescope, I guess. -   -

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty outstanding game, albeit a bit short.Pros:- Great atmosphere. Music and art style are top notch.- Fun core gameplay loop. Catch fish, sell fish, upgrade boat, explore.- Story is well-written.Cons:- Game is short. If you play for long periods of time, you'll do everything in 3 sessions.- Low difficultly. This could be a pro or con, but I found the game needing a bit higher difficulty. I never had more than a single point of damage to my ship during the entire playthrough.- Simplistic "monster" mechanic for each zone. Each zone has a monster that will chase you or try to damage your boat. Most of them had the same behavior. I thought there could be a bit more differentiation here.At the end of the day this game is dope. I think it's worth the full price, even if it's a short game. Excited to see what sort of updates or DLCs this game will have over the next year.

_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.review: Dredge is a pretty good fishing games. If you're read the discussions, this is one of those games that isn't a "dollar per hour" unless you strive to 100% it. I'm not done with it, but others have described it as doing it over the weekend. You collect fish, you bring back fish to sell, find materials to upgrade your ship and research new ways to get fish/upgrade your boat.The artstyle is good and the setting is good. The inventory management is unique, and even though it isn't what attracted me to it, it's interesting. I was attracted because of the lovecraftian aspects, and it definitely sells that type of atmosphere. People being okay with the unknown while your character has to deal with anxiety and a HP bar in terms of how many hits your boat can take. Anxiety makes your boat get more, and the night is dangerous but profitable.I'm not someone who's scared by this game, but I prefer this type of horror over jumpscare. It's unnerving, meant to be creepy when you really think about it, but if you're just vibing you aren't really suddenly shocked. The hazards are more annoying than make me jump, but that's fine. The dialogue didn't even make me realize I was doing a majority of fetch quests. It's rather easy to get immersed and wonder what's actually going on.I'm someone that typically enjoys combat and RPG mechanics. This game was good enough to make me gravitate it despite it being somewhat of a puzzle solver, and having little control over fighting off the things attacking me. It's not completely suppressed, but this game isn't catering to me. More games where the devs make what they want instead of giving people hundreds of hours of empty content please.
_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.review: Fishing and salvaging are the main two activities you do in Dredge. By themselves they do not sound that fun or exciting but Dredge does. This is achieved by: making night a dangerous time to on the water trying to fish and salvage since that is when the really good stuff appears. Offering great visuals no matter where you are in the game. Good mini games when you are fishing or salvaging. Otherworldly horrors to avoid. Strange and mysterious people and beings to appease. A solid upgrade system for your ship, equipment, and engines. And probably a bit more that I am forgetting.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm torn on whether to recommend or not.  The core gameplay loop is superb, the mechanics are fun and well polished. The aesthetic is beautiful and fitting. And it manages to set a really good mood and tone. It draws you into its world masterfully and gets you in exactly the right frame of mind.  Then then it kind of does nothing with it. The gameplay and mechanics never stop being satisfying, but what's it all for? Its for a story that isn't finished. A story that is barely even there.When you play it you can see a dozen unfinished paths. A dozen ideas that got cut off before they could become anything. None of the side quests amount to anything. None of the characters change or do anything, but a lot of them look like they're about to. There's clear and apparent moments of conflict, or tragedy, or hope, that just suddenly stop. The next scene is missing, and the character just goes back to default behaviour. It's crushingly disappointing. Because I LOVED playing this game... I kept waiting for it to drop the story on me. For the "oh damn" moment when things go Lovecraft... but they don't. It doesn't ever do it. Because it's not finished.   If this game was finished properly, with quest-lines that build up and characters that change and a proper lovecraftian darkness, then it would likely be my game of the year. It would be worth $50 easy.   As it stands its still fun. It's still good... I still enjoyed it.But it's disappointing to see the potential thrown away.  I'd suggest waiting and hoping that they finish it in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.review: Good game, if you've ever seen that old game concept post floating around of a cosmic horror fishing game where a lot of the tone is carried on finding bizarre, mutated fish, this is about as close I can imagine we'll ever get to that. The art is very well done. DREDGE is not a particularly long or difficult game, but it is very fun to play just to chill and catch fish. Also don't buy the Blackstone Key DLC, you don't really need it. As a cosmic horror story it is not especially terrifying by any means (unless you have something like thalassophobia, I suppose.), but its tone still carries a lot of open-ended questions and mysteries that make you wonder about the world. It also avoids the pitfall of overly-long descriptions of the indescribable because your exposure to these cosmic entities is almost entirely through indirect means (the mutated fish, shapes in the distance, fragments from an ancient civilization, etc.) Also, the twist just before the game's conclusion is very well done.tl;dr if you like chill games and cosmic horror this game is for you.Should you 100% this game: Yes. Doing so will show you literally everything the game has to offer and is not especially difficult to do. Doing the final sequence does not lock or otherwise conclude your save file meaning you can get both endings in one file without having to make a backup.
_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.review: I do not have enough words to describe how incredibly this game captures the essence of a calm yet unnerving ambient. Mind you this might not be the game for everyone, as the core gameplay is in fact exploration and, well, fishing and dredging, which is actually super fun. But the story itself and how immersed you get are the true winners here.It does have Lovecraftian horror elements, yet the game itself is just beautiful for the eyes.Honestly, a must play. I really don't want to spoil it for you all.
_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.review: DREDGE is amazing. The fishing, boating, and inventory management mechanics are very engaging, and the gameplay loop is satisfying. Making money from selling fish to buy new equipment, and finding the resources needed to research new upgrades feels rewarding, as you can feel the impact of everything you unlock. The art style of the game and the music are also fantastic, along with all the ambient noise of the ocean making the game feel cozy and mysterious.I finished the game 100% in 15 hours, which may sound somewhat short, but it felt like the perfect length for this game. Any longer, and I feel like I may have gotten bored. I can definitely see myself revisiting this game in a couple of years to play it all again for fun. If you're on the fence about buying DREDGE, it's worth the experience.
_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.review: Dredge is cute and creepy, with a gameplay loop comprised of fishing during the day, selling/upgrading/resting at night. If you find yourself out on the open water when night falls, things can get a little strange. Blaring my fog horn and getting an answer from an unseen vessel makes me feel very uneasy, especially when I'm nowhere near the safety of the mainland and its lighthouse.This is definitely a keeper and worth a playthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.review: I dont normally review games, however, there are rare exceptions.Dredge starts out as normally as any game would and quickly throws you into a nighttime world of horror that your curiosity grabs at. It engages you in a story that you have no idea what it may bring next and encourages (and punishes) you for exploring the blue expanse. This game was fantastic. Simply outstanding
_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

Ultimately, it is "just" a fishing game with some Lovecraftian flair, but so far I have enjoyed it far more than I have games that come in at twice the price.
_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.review: I whole-heartedly* recommend this game (*with one caveat). Everything here is so well put together. It shows the quality of the game that my primary complaint is simply that there isn't enough of it (my only other complaint is that you can run out of convenient ways to get research parts after a while, which makes finishing your tech tree a grind). I managed to finish the game and get 100% of  the achievements in less than 18 hours, and I could have finished the main story in closer to 10. That makes the asking price of $32.50 CAD a little steep, and if you price your playtime to dollar ratio strictly I would recommend waiting for a sale.With the bad out of the way, all that is left is an amazing entry into the lovecraftian/eldrich/cosmic horror genre. Beautifully presented characters and fish, mysterious zones to explore, and a story with an ending that surprised me with how much it affected me.If you're even slightly interested in any part of this game, I think you owe it to yourself to buy and play this game.I also sincerely hope the devs consider doing another game like this, with even more to explore, catch, and discover.

_childDocuments_.review: A good game with decent mechanics. The Lovecraftian setting is easy to get into and just like the books, it's a slow and steady descent into madness. _childDocuments_.review: I’m someone who practically never plays horror games for one key reason, I hate the overreliance most horror games have with jumpscares. There is no such thing as an “earned jumpscare”, they’re all cheap ways to release tension and get a reaction from the player. In this sense, Dredge is very atypical in that as far as I know, there are no jumpscares whatsoever. Instead the horror comes from a creepy atmosphere and the fear of the unknown. While I don’t think the game is terrifying per se, the aberrations and effects of paranoia definitely had me on edge. Each new group of islands has a kind of big bad you have to learn about through interactions with NPC:s, observing the environment or the hard way. These factors create and sustain tension, and the relief comes from docking somewhere, rendering the boat safe.Beyond the horror, Dredge overall has one of the best atmospheres I have ever experienced in gaming. The art direction is amazing and perfectly complements the tone of the game. The music also works well making the game a very cohesive package and contributing to the atmosphere. As for the gameplay, it is definitely simple, but it doesn’t need to be complex as the main appeal is discovering what these places have to offer and exploring this amazing world that has been realized. You get pulled into this world and want to find out what that thing in the distance is and why things became so strange. The gameplay stays simple and engaging throughout which makes taking in the sights better as I never grew bored of the simple fishing and dredging micro games.All in all, Dredge is one of, if not the best Indie game released this year so far. The sense of discovery is immensely enjoyable throughout the entire playthrough, and I have tried to be vague because I think spoiling the contents of the game would be ruining an amazing experience. If you even slightly think Dredge looks interesting, I urge you to give it a shot and experience it for yourself.
_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game.  The horror isn't all that scary but there are a couple make-you-jump moments when some creature from the depths gobbles you up in the middle of the ocean at night.The game mechanics are easy to get into and the add-ons you receive as you complete quests enhance the game.I really hope there is DLC that adds quests/stories/locations/fish.

_childDocuments_.review: They combined the fishing and horror aspects quite well. Great gameplay and amazing atmosphere. My only gripes: 1) I wish research parts were more readily available; grinding for it in the end game wasn't as fun and 2) the ending was a bit abrupt; given the build-up throughout the game, it wasn't as satisfying as it could have been.Overall, a great game. And oh boy, was it worth it.At first the gameplay seems pretty relaxed, and the fishing aspect reminds a bit of games like animal crossing, but the atmosphere and the whole vibe of the game is a completely different one. You're asking yourself at all times: "what is happening?" "why are there sea monsters here?" or "WHAT THE ♥♥♥♥ IS THAT THING???"it's honestly one of my favourite indie games of 2023, if not one of my favourite singleplayer games of 2023 overall, and even though the story is not that long when you focus on the main quest like I did, it's 100% worth it, and I would definitely recommend this gem of a game to anyone who has some spare time and a few spare bucks to spend.

_childDocuments_.review: A (relatively) short game dripping with atmosphere, sitting in that perfect spot between compelling and unnerving. The gameplay loop is very satisfying, tasking you with fishing and dredging to make money and improve your ship not just to increase the value and variety of your haul, but also to resist the eldritch terrors that lurk a little too close to the surface for any comfort.Everything from the odd and suspect NPCs, to the aberrant fish you begin to catch, to the mystifying lore tangled up in your voyage serve to unsettle you just enough to provoke further exploration. In particular, I recommend playing the game blind to any guides or walkthroughs until you're truly stuck because the joy of discovery, paired with the immediate dread at the implications of that discovery, is a feeling not often found in many games these days.The DLC "The Pale Reach" is definitely worth the price to add 2-4 hours of extra adventure unrelated to the main plot, and especially provides you with rewards that add real value for completionists. The "Blackstone Key" DLC is considered only beneficial in the early game by many (it's basically a couple of helpful pieces of gear), but as it was a contractual obligation to create, it's therefore an optional "give the devs some more money to show thanks for a great game" button. A third DLC is on the horizon, and I'm awaiting it eagerly.

_childDocuments_.review: A simple but incredibly addicting game. The core gameplay loop is go fishing, upgrade your setup, and fish some more. All the while you’ll have tasks to complete along the way guiding you towards the end. The art and music is perfect for this kind of game. There’s a serenity and longing bathing the whole game and while it sells itself on its horror elements, it’s those quiet moments that stand out the most to me. Even without the eldritch horror aspects it would make for an incredible fishing sim. If you are into that kind of game then it’s a 100% buy. Easiest decision you could make. I only have a few minor complaints. The biggest one is that I wish it was a little harder (perhaps a difficulty setting so people can enjoy it as a relaxing fishing game too) so the horror has more emphasis later in the run. I’d also prefer if there was a build up to the fish becoming abominations as you become increasingly more corrupt. You can get a lot of the mutant variants early on and it leaves little reason to return to already explored islands. My final complaint (more of a recommendation) is to make things increasingly more dangerous as you find more trinkets and as you deplete the pools. The theme of the ocean trying to fight back is a cool one and should be explored more. Besides those minor complaints/suggestions, I’ve had a blast and it leaves me wanting more (in a good way). The best praise I can think of giving a game is that I can’t wait for the sequel already. Highly recommend buying the game. One of the best indie titles in a while. A sequel building on the core mechanics would be like TOTK following BOTW.

_childDocuments_.review: This game by no means deserves a negative review - it is great. I have played for less than 10 hours at the time of this review and have completed almost everything the game has to offer and I'm not interested in playing through the story again because the experience will be exactly the same.Something I think could improve the playtime issue is increasing the difficulty of making progress. In my opinion ship upgrades are too easily obtainable (they don't require enough materials and they are very cheap). I also think the ability to purchase research parts, explosives, and bait from the store makes the game too easy (introduce a crafting method).Hopefully in the future we will see the addition of more content, either through regular updates or DLC. I would love to see: New Fish, New Fishing Mechanics, New Ship Upgrades, New Regions, More Side Quests (Maybe even another main Questline), More Books, More NPC conversation.Gameplay: 9/10Price: 8/10Content: 8/10Game Length: 6/10Overall Rating: 7.75/10

_childDocuments_.review: Dredge is a fishing, exploration, and collection game that has a few puzzles and a lot of mysteries to unravel. This is the first game developed by Black Salt Games, and let me say, they knocked it out of the park. I loved reading all the individual aberrant descriptions for all the mutated fish and looking at the images. (Got me attacked by monster more than once.) Very creepy.Story: The story and the mood of the entire experience ushers forth a lingering foreboding. With every quest you complete, the world of Dredge seems to get a little darker and more unsettling. The Black Salt Team did an amazing job of developing the atmosphere and designing quests that support and perpetuate that feeling.The dialogue of the characters is believable, though a little limited. You may find a little extra story here and there if you catch up for a chat with the locals.Pacing: Relatively steady, aside from perhaps trying to catch mutant fish where you have little to no control over when they decide to jump into your nets. These times you may get lucky in ten minutes, or you could be at it for a while and cursing your choice to become a fisherman.There are boat upgrades that are available any time throughout the game. You can progress though those as quickly as you wish, if you can fulfill the requirements. There is a bit of fishing grinding, but toward end game, they give you a few more tools to help you get the last missing fish/fishy mutants so as that you’re not suffering for hours on end—unless that’s your jam. You do you. No judgment.Audio: The ambient noises of the ocean’s waves, the unsettling groans from the deep, the screams of the birds overhead, all of these are working in combination to bring this game to life. The sounds only support in creating the unsettling atmosphere and creating a more “tangible” environment. No voiced dialogue.Gameplay: The game itself is easy to pick up. The controls are limited to directionals, the interact button, and what special ability you want to have equipped and activate. Accessibility: there is a surprising amount of accessibility choices to help make the game playable for everyone. I do believe there are settings for colorblind capabilities. Ya love to see it! The game is played in third person, with little to no screen shakes, though there is the occasional screen shade darkening or becoming another color. The game is controller compatible and may even play smoother with a controller. I played with keyboard and mouse and found the experience to be a positive one.Conclusion: For a new game being $25 dollars isn’t unreasonable at all (especially when there are larger titles games charging three times that and delivering less of a satisfying experience). Dredge is doing all the things right for up-and-coming developers in the community. The game is unique with the graphics and music. The developers are taking pains to add such extensive accessibility options to keep the game as inclusive as possible is a huge win in my book. That’s what players should expect from all developers big and small going forward and Black Salt Games is riding that wave.The game is a lot of fun. I’d recommend this to anyone who’s looking for a good chill game, who likes collections games, or who really likes fishing and eerie eldritch feels emanating from the depths of the ocean.Bonus:Game has achievements? YesAre they tedious/impossible? NoWorth your time? I would say yes if you’re looking for that 100% type of deal. A few of the achievements are story based, but most are discovery.Storyline tip: There are two possible endings to this game.Quests tip: There are four quests that you can fail if you’re not ready for them. They’re started by people dressed in hooded robes out on secluded islands. Don’t talk to them unless you can use a variety of methods to get an assortment of fish. If you’re unsure: Wait.Liked the review? Looking for more? I'm a curator! Check me out:

_childDocuments_.review: When I think about this game, I mostly think about its wasted potential. DREDGE sort of feels half-finished, like it should be an early-access game. _childDocuments_.review: Games that can integrate story and gameplay together are some of my favorites for that reason. It’s why  is one of my top three favorite games of all time. It’s why I’m a big fan of , and for how much praise that game (rightfully) got, I still consider it to be a bit underappreciated. These are the games that I firmly believe are the peak of the medium.  does enough to scratch that particular itch for me, but it doesn’t quite hit it out of the park the same way some of the best have. The visual presentation of the game is top notch stuff. Its simple graphics aren’t going to demand a $7,500 machine to run, but they have the same benefit of a game like  in that it looks great now and it’ll look great in twenty years. Outside of just the general “it looks good” praise, the way everything is shown adds to ’s phenomenal atmosphere. When you start the game in a small, harmless town, the day brings you islands, cliffs, and ancient buildings in the far distance, telling you where you can go once you’re ready. With the game’s core being tied to its fishing and sense of exploration and discovery, I couldn’t wait to visit these places to see what new fish I could find and what new secrets I’d discover about the world I was in. While not strictly exploration focused like some other games,  is tightly designed around the reasonable world size it offers, and almost no space is wasted. The night takes the game’s cozy fishing simulator gameplay and adds a nice layer of unease to everything. At first, you’re essentially going around in a paddle boat trying to get as many fish as you can to get some money for needed upgrades, and you can largely avoid the night. But when you do have to venture out into the night, and you will have to, the Lovecraftian parts of the game come through in the form of monsters (or parts of them) attacking you. While this does fit under horror, I appreciate the developers’ restraint in how they handle it. In my entire run, I found one thing that I felt like was a legitimate jump scare, and that was when a massive tentacle suddenly burst out of the water to hit my ship. Even that wasn’t completely unexpected, as  does a pretty good job at letting you know when something is about to happen, but this instance didn’t have the same audio and visual feedback to let you know it was about to happen. Instead, most of the horror in it comes from the atmosphere and suspense the game builds. Weary residents of the town frequently warn you not to go out at night when you start the game, and they give the sense that something is just a little off, but they’re all just living with it. When you do go out at night, the open world becomes claustrophobic in feeling, but only changes slightly in practice. The dense fog around your ship makes it extremely difficult to see your immediate surroundings, which means you can hit a rock and damage your hull, which also takes out an inventory slot at random. Another aspect of nighttime is your panic, a stat that increases the negative effects of the night itself, will go up. Early on, you won’t have many means to keep your panic down on your own, which makes fishing at night the first real challenge of the game. One consequence of increased panic is rock formations spawning near you, which can make a familiar route suddenly get filled with damaging obstacles. Managing the day and night cycle while fishing and gathering resources for upgrades is the core gameplay loop. It might not blow anyone’s socks off, but as someone who really enjoys fishing, I loved exploring as much as I could during the day and inching my way out at night to find new species. For me, the fishing gameplay loop was solidified with the inventory management system on your boat, which is like ’s inventory management. But when you can finally craft enough upgrades for your ship to start making more dangerous journeys out in the archipelago, the threat of the night lessens substantially. I really enjoyed how the difficulty curve of the game was handled and how it ties in with the overall gameplay and story integration  offers. In the story, these are people who’ve been living with this horror hanging over them, making them all visibly tired, but they continue to live their lives and try to work through it. When you first get there, the night is this almost overwhelming presence that you just aren’t equipped to handle. But when you spend more time in this world and get accustomed to everything going on, you become more prepared to handle it. As your character settles into this nightmarish world, it all becomes easier to manage, in both the narrative and gameplay. That does mean that the game does become a tad easy as it progresses. The Night Angler that pursues you without rest at the start of the game becomes something that’s laughably easy to avoid with better ship lighting and better engines. Other panic-induced enemies or obstacles become just part of the job when you can essentially outrun and outmaneuver just about everything that can realistically cause a challenge. But to counter that, the game doesn’t take too long to beat. By the time the challenge really starts to feel like a walk in the park, the game’s story is probably ready to be wrapped up. I was able to 100% the game in about twelve hours of playtime, which a lot of was because of great luck with fishing. If you don’t want to catch every critter out there, finishing the bulk of the game shouldn’t take long at all. : The relevant plot stuff doesn’t really come at you until the very end as well. Through the entire game, you pick up messages in the water and vague clues/hints from some of the characters in the game. Generally, it’s pretty thin on the ground until you give every relic in the game over to the Collector. At that point, you have two options for an ending. The “bad” ending has the Collector join you on your boat (without him taking up any inventory spaces, which no other character or object did) and take you to a spot where a woman drowned. It isn’t outright revealed what the connection is between the woman and either the Fisherman or Collector in the dialogue shared between the characters, but it’s strongly implied there is a significant connection. The Collector throws all the relics into the ocean, where the woman is resurrected, but a colossal eldritch creature emerges from the water and destroys the starting town. The “good” ending has you talk to a couple of characters before proceeding with the collector. It’s revealed the Collector isn’t a real person, but an imaginary figure/reflection of the Fisherman himself. Instead of handing everything over to the Collector to throw into the water, the Fisherman throws the cursed book he dredged up into the water, where his vessel is eaten by a massive sea creature, but the night fog finally breaks, and the starting town has a peaceful night. It’s not there isn’t any indication of where the plot is going before this, but everything largely revolves around you helping other people with their own issues (often caused by this calamity) to get the relics that get you to the end of the game. If people appreciate a story that's a little more straightforward, ’s story might be a little off-putting with how suddenly it ramps up right at the end. This is a definite recommendation for me. I love fishing, I love the atmosphere, and I love the characters just trying to continue their lives with this almost-vague presence that looms over them, but doesn’t directly touch them. The gameplay loop might not be a world-beater, and the progression system might make people feel like the game gets too easy, but if you’re looking for a snack-sized game with a dense atmosphere,  might just be worth a buy.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't normally review games on Steam. In fact, I think this is my review writing debut. Be it through apathy or or laziness, I've just never been extraordinarily keen to post a review. However, my experience in Dredge has been so immaculate that I have to recommend it to as many people as possible. I want to stress that to this point, I have not finished the main game, and I'm nowhere near 100%ing the part that I have finished (which I wholeheartedly aim to do.) That being said, here are my main reasons why Dredge is one of the best games I have ever played.    1. The atmosphere and ambiance of this game are second to none in my opinion. A beautifully creepy soundtrack, mixed with drop-dead gorgeous visuals, and a Lovecraftian mystery that will both terrify and ensnare you, combine to create an experience that is transcendent of the genre and medium. The fear of the unknown and the innate desire to discover the secrets trapped therein that the atmosphere of this game creates is immaculate in its execution.     2. The gameplay in this title is simply brilliant, in that it is literally simple, but tight and engaging enough to hook you. The fishing aspect is very straightforward, as it does not require you to sit there for ages looking for a bite. You simply pull up to a spot and catch some fish. Add to that the intuitive UI and you have a core gameplay system that is simple enough not to frustrate you, but interesting enough to keep you playing. Exploration, another core gameplay loop, is excellent for many of the reasons listed above. However, it improves on the fishing with the added element of danger. While exploring there are numerous mysterious entities and creatures you can encounter, none of which I will spoil here. That brings me to my final words of praise for the gameplay, as well as my only real criticism thereof. As mentioned earlier, this game will make you fear the unknown and drive you to uncover its secrets. The progression in this game and the little hints you continually get from NPCs and the environment that things are not at all what they seem are top notch. However, there simply isn't enough of it. This is the only real complaint I have seen from others who have reviewed Dredge, and I must wholeheartedly agree. As of the time this was written, I have around 7 hours in game and I am about to start the quest for the final location, which isn't nearly as much time as I wanted to spend getting there. Since the game has captivated me so thoroughly, I almost find myself intentionally procrastinating because I don't want it to end. This is naturally a good problem to have, but it remains a problem nonetheless. That being said, the fact that I am purposefully slowing down right before the end of the game, illustrates just how absolutely enamored I am with this game. Despite its rather scant length, I glowingly recommend this game to anyone who is looking for a tight, beautiful, and well-crafted single player game to get totally ensnared by.    TLDR: This review is a bit lengthy, so I'll spare those who don't have the time or patience to put up with my long-winded twaddle. This game is second to none in it's atmosphere and ambiance, with fascinating and subtly terrifying gameplay that will keep you on the edge of your seat. It is a bit short for my taste, but don't let that dissuade you for a second. 10/10. Edit: I've finished the game, and the endings are the perfect encapsulation of what makes this game so special. Hauntingly beautiful imagery and music came together to put a perfect, and subtly horrific capstone on this absolute masterpiece of a game. I wish I could go back and experience them again. This game shook me to my core in all the right ways, so buy it. Now. It's easily the best single-player experience I've ever had. This game will leave you salivating for more. Be it more of the atmosphere, game play, subtle Lovecraftian terror, or the thrill of uncovering the sinister mystery, this game will leave you in withdrawal of all of it.

_childDocuments_.review: Call me Ishmael. Some years ago—never mind how long precisely—having little or no money in my purse, and nothing particular to interest me on shore, I thought I would sail about a little and see the watery part of the world. It is a way I have of driving off the spleen and regulating the circulation. Whenever I find myself growing grim about the mouth; whenever it is a damp, drizzly November in my soul; whenever I find myself involuntarily pausing before coffin warehouses, and bringing up the rear of every funeral I meet; and especially whenever my hypos get such an upper hand of me, that it requires a strong moral principle to prevent me from deliberately stepping into the street, and methodically knocking people’s hats off—then, I account it high time to get to sea as soon as I can. This is my substitute for pistol and ball. With a philosophical flourish Cato throws himself upon his sword; I quietly take to the ship. There is nothing surprising in this. If they but knew it, almost all men in their degree, some time or other, cherish very nearly the same feelings towards the ocean with me.

_childDocuments_.review: An incredible experience of a game and wonderful impression from Black Salt Games, the artstyle is very unique, capturing you in the world of dredge's mysterious NPCs and the dreadful, grotesque bodyhorror introduced with the abberated fish. The game created a nice incentive for me to finish my fish collection, alongside the questlines/pursuits, my biggest issue with the game is how the characters feel very one dimensional and not fleshed out, how some fish can be incredibly difficult to locate without use of guides/wikis (the sunfish, moonfish, their abberations and the abberated jellyfish) and how there isnt any need to actually go out into the sea at night due to how close the islands are to eachother, making the night threats and Panic meter irrelevant midgame. Overall the world built in Dredge feels really intriguing and makes you want to explore it, the soundtrack encapsulates you into the world with tense night fishing segments over a terrifying sea and peaceful, tranquil day segments over a blissful ocean. All in all, the game felt a little short and small compared to what it feels like it presents, but I enjoyed every bit of it. A solid 9/10 from me, I can't recommend it more to anyone looking for a fun, interesting experience, and here's to hoping the DLC is just as splendid as the basegame!!also funny fish gaming lmao

If you stay out in the dark for a long time you gain this stat and start seeing little red eyes... Is that all? The game might have explained it better and I just didn't catch it but anyway....Then there´s the gameplay... I'ts pretty much just a collection of mini games. Well packaged and all and I really like the tetris style inventory. But then there's the town mechanics and UI that really annoy me. The most used type of town has a fishmonger, dry dock, shipyard and these are just menus but to switch between them you have to exit and enter a new menu there is a short animation where the storekeeper says something before you can do anything. It's not a long animation but it sure does get annoying when you just want to play the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed DREDGE a lot. The game reinvigorated my curiosity towards eldritch storytelling. Once you understand the mechanics and upgrade your ship a bit the scary things become more of a curiosity than a danger. I found myself looking for trouble to experience the monsters instead of trying to avoid them. So it's actually a pretty cozy fishing game after all.The game does seem to have an option in the settings to turn off danger. I didn't try it but I love that we have the option.DREDGE is definitely more about the vibes and the journey than the destination. And that's not a bad thing at all.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is rad.At the time of posting this review, I've got 3 hours, but it is INTENSE. I'm just a simple little fisherman, but the things in the ocean want me dead- and those things are pretty nasty.I love the aesthetic of this game, and the gameplay is absolutely intriguing and grips you. I played all in one sitting nonstop, intent on my next goal, my next upgrade, trying to get better, to get faster, wondering if I was completely out of my depth (I was lol) and if I was where I should be (probably not). Lantern Fish Ghost Boat is probably the scariest thing I've ever experienced, lmao.I like the fact that this is a more chill horror game. Horror these days relies pretty heavily on the jumpscare factor, and while this game absolutely made my heart race and even almost made me scream because Ghost Boat McGee snuck up behind me somehow, I get a reprieve from the constant terror and feel comfortable to keep playing, versus getting nonstop scares that either wear me out completely, or eventually get old. The story is a nice slow burn that you take your time through, piecing it together as you come across it and learn about the world.It's one of those games where you want "just five more minutes" because you just need a LITTLE more to get the next upgrade, JUST A LITTLE MORE, lol- and then it's 3:00am.

_childDocuments_.review: A fairly unique take on a fishing game, though I'd describe it more as a time/resource/threat management game based around about 3-4 fishing mini-games that are more or less skill checks/QTEs. A lot of it is managing your inventory while under the threat of various monsters, as well as time management so you can avoid being out in the night where most things that want to drag you down to the depths will be. Of course there are various fish that can only be caught in the night, so at some point you will have to take that plunge. And naturally there are still threats present even during the day in most major areas which is part of the threat management; "do I have time to fish/dredge here before the big monster comes to take a bite?" and "I gotta sort this ♥♥♥♥ quick or the big monster is definitely gonna take a bite out of me."A major part of the game is the atmosphere. If you aren't the type to be immersed and focus solely on the gameplay Dredge ironically might not be deep enough for you. Boiling it down to its base a lot of the game just ends up being fetch quests to improve your boat and fishing equipment to become better at fetch quests. While it is by no means a walking simulator, there are clear threats and failure states, most of the game is "go to place to get something and bring it somewhere else." You are at best able to temporarily drive away the monsters, you won't be defeating anything. So actually getting invested in the world, talking to and learning about its characters, reading descriptions of the grotesque mutations taking place, finding bottles and monoliths to find out what is happening and may potentially happen in the future, is fairly important to your enjoyment. If you engage with the setting you'll find it drags you in really well with its various little touches.

_childDocuments_.review: I saw this game being featured by Steam and figured I'd give it a shot. Dredge is different from what I usually play and I tend to have a soft spot for indie dev studios. To put it bluntly, Dredge is the best indie game I have played in a long time. The Pros:- The storyline is good.  - The visuals are nothing short of gorgeous, especially during sunrise in the Marrows and at night in the Stellar Basin. - There are a ton of aquatic species to catch, along with their mutated counterparts. - Anyone can play this game regardless of skill level. - There are plenty of things to do and discover apart from doing the main quest.The Cons:- It's a relatively short experience. I have 14 hours logged into the game and have completed both endings. I wish there was more things to do and maybe that can be possible with future DLC.-While the storyline is good, it isn't as good as it can be. There are many moments that don't feel as fleshed out as they could be.   - If you damage your hull there is the possibility of losing an important item from your boat that you can't get back. You therefore have to reload a previous save to get your item back. This is just something I personally find annoying and it may not be a con for you. - There's side quests that involve you catching types of fish for hooded figures spread out across the map. These fish vary from shallow all the way to hadal levels of deepness. You need special fishing equipment for these catch types since not one fishing rig can do it all, and you have to research these rigs which takes time. Since these specific side quests are also timed, it doesn't help if you don't have the right equipment unlocked for the fish being demanded. If you take too long, you  miss out on getting a one time only special item. There's no way of figuring this out until after you've started the quest. Long story short, have all catch types unlocked before doing these hooded figure quests. - The endings felt a little rushed. They were still full of "wow" value, but there could have been more there. - I wish there was more Lovecraftian elements in this game than what you get. Overall, I recommend Dredge. It's a nice, neat fishing game with Lovecraftian horror thrown in. The endings throw you off-guard and there's a part in the storyline towards the end of the game that makes you sit back and say "holy sh*t". Hopefully the devs can add on to the game in the future with DLC because, like I said, it is a relatively short game. That, however, doesn't mean it isn't a pleasant experience. Ill say it again, it's the best indie game I have played in a long time.

_childDocuments_.review: This game somehow combined 2 things I am not usually a fan of in games, fishing and horror, to provide a very fun experience. The fishing doesn't get repetitive which I know I shouldn't be surprising considering the game's built around it, but the amount of games that I have played that have fishing as some boring side thing where you cast a rod out and wait for an indicator just to have a chance of getting 1 of 30 different fish from one spot all the while being required for 100% completion has entirely tainted my perspective on the mechanic in games, so something like this that makes it fun is a nice change of pace. The horror elements of the game are also great, as I like how it's not shoved in your face all the time and is there more to just add more weird or interesting elements to the base game of fishing and give a little excitement here and there. Anyways, if you're looking for a completely unique lovecraftian horror story, sorry you won't find it here. But if you're looking for a neat game about fishing with a little bit of horror action to go along side it, then you've found the right game.

_childDocuments_.review: Good game. Driving a boat around 5 different areas with own threats, own little stories, inhabitants, exploring fauna, beautiful surroundings, peaceful days and scary nights. The fishing mechanics is relaxing, collecting money and resources to upgrade the boat, trying various fishing tools, learning how to deal with dangers, experiencing mysteries, solving puzzles.And the bad would be UI, lack of hotkeys for skills, huge list of fishes without search, lack of way to know what aberrations you need, poor map markers, lack of way to find pool of fish you need for whatever, few puzzles are impossible to do without internet. The progression is not balanced, e.g. it's possible to upgrade board to max after like 15% of completing game story, side quests and achievements. Replayability is not here.Few things are annoying, like the need to lower trawl or sometimes disappearing light, which required to be turned on by opening menu, selecting skill, right clicking, opening menu and selecting back skill you need..But overall it was a nice casual experience, I enjoyed it! It gave me that nice feeling of exploring the unknown and progressing, which I like in games. It's short, but at same time long enough to not get bored.
