_childDocuments_.review: DREDGE is an enjoyable fishing game that uses Lovecraftian themes to give it a refreshing allure. The fishing aspects are simple, allowing players to enjoy at their own pace for 7-10 hours. Spend your time dragging nets, laying crab pots, exploring archipelagos, helping strangers, or catching big sharks. Rearrange the cargo and sell your catch to unlock boat upgrades that let you carry more or travel quicker. Fishing at night comes with a spooky atmosphere and a few new threats, but it is not scary or challenging enough to make the most of the darker themes influenced by Lovecraft. The simple catch-and-sell gameplay loop definitely makes DREDGE easy to play and a good option for fishing fans. If only there was more below the surface.
_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.review: DREDGE took the one mechanic that unifies nearly every great game, the fishing minigame, and turned it into a primary gameplay loop. Brilliant! The game has 4 main parts: the fishing itself, fish-based quests, a tetris-style inventory management system to take care of all your fish and equipment, and your boat upgrades. It's all wrapped up in a spooky eldritch-horror world. Everything works pretty well together. If you've ever enjoyed a fishing minigame, you'll probably enjoy DREDGE!The game is relatively short compared to some other titles I've enjoyed. A completion chalks in at about 11 hours, and getting 100% will take about 15. The game is highly bingable, as I got completely lost in the satisfying loop of fishing, selling, and upgrading, but probably doesn't have enormous replay value. Once you've caught all the fish, completed every quest, and purchased every upgrade, it doesn't feel like there's a whole lot left to do. I do wish there was some sort of post-game content, but DREDGE is still fine as a well-contained experience with a definitive end.

_childDocuments_.review: Dredge is a fun and engaging fishing game that takes you on a sometimes-nightmarish journey to catch fish in various locations. The game's simple yet effective mechanics make it easy to pick up and play. There are a variety of environments, each with its own unique fish species. The sound design is also top-notch, with ambient sounds and that enhance the game's overall immersion. That being said, the game does have some limitations. The fishing mechanics can become repetitive after a while and the game's progression system may leave some players wanting more of a challenge. That being said, Dredge is only $25 and contains at least 8 hours of gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has given me a bad case of what a good friend called 'fish derangement'. I started it less than two days ago and have already completed it (that is, I have caught every fish in the base game and seen both base game endings, I haven't touched the DLC yet because I have to sleep at SOME point). It speaks to how effective this game is that I became a single-minded fish-obsessed freak while playing a game where the main character is also a single-minded fish-obsessed freak. I finished it and then immediately bought it for two of my friends, that's how much I enjoyed it.Of particular note: I am severely thalassaphobic. I wanted this game specifically because I knew for me it would be scary, but fun scary like a roller coaster. It hit that spot just right and was a delightfully creepy experience, especially thanks to the stellar sound design. The art is gorgeous but simple and frankly the big, blocky shapes of the whales looming out of the water at me was way more frightening than a hyper-realistic monster would have been. If anything I was a little disappointed that there weren't more cetacean monsters, because that's the kind of thing I really find scary. The more 'alien' looking sealife was much less frightening. I will also say this is basically the only game with a fishing minigame to have got it right. The minigames are simple, fun, differ depending on what kind of fish you want to catch, and are not even required of you unless you want to reel the fish in faster. It's the only game besides maybe Animal Crossing where fishing is downright zen, which is good considering how much of the game is fishing. In summary I am so normal about this game I am a normal human being I am not a fish I promise

_childDocuments_.review: Everyone talks about the art-style in Dredge, and rightly so. It felt to me like stepping into a Graphic Novel. For anyone just starting this game, I would suggest exploration and side quests. The DLC also felt too short, especially The Pale Reach. I still very much enjoyed both, but The Pale Reach in particular didn’t have a significant enough ending, although still very enjoyable.I guess the main theme of this review is the game left me wanting more, which is no bad thing. I loved it.

_childDocuments_.review: Dredge is a uniquely fun and frightening game that exceeds expectations. Initially, I expected a simple fishing simulator, but it offers much more. During the day, you catch fish, explore areas, and engage with intriguing characters, all while enjoying satisfying upgrades for your gear. However, nightfall brings darkness and the threat of sea monsters, enhancing the game's cosmic horror vibe. The music, animations, and story create a captivating atmosphere. I highly recommend this game—it will not disappoint you! 10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm typically not the kind of person to write long reviews about the games I've played, only done it for a handful in the past, but for games, I've really, really enjoyed I would feel honored to write a review, not only to recommend it to others but also as a Thank you to the Dev Team <3.There is a reason this game has so many positive reviews, and they all are justified.So here are the hard facts:Sound Effects / Music:[x] Godly[] Very Nice[] Ok[] Meh[] HorribleNote: I'm a sucker for great sound design and this game certainly didn't let me down.Graphic:[] Reality is a Joke compared to this[x] Very nice[] Average[] Good enough[] BadNote: The art style is very sweet and you can feel that the devs were very passionate about itDifficulty:[] Dark Souls[] Hard[] Average[x] Easy[x] RelaxedNote: It is very relaxing, at night though if you don't watch out it can be a bit tricky.Story Length:[] Never going to finish this[] Very long[] Long[x] Average[x] ShortNote: I finished the story after ~12 hours but didn't do every sidequest. If you play the game more relaxed, it'd take you around 20.PC requirements:[] NASA[] Overkill[] High End[x] Medium[] ToasterNote: I have a decent Rig (Ryzen 7 3800x, 32Gb RAM, RTX2070) and I could easily play at 2540*1440 pretty much locked at 140 frames.Worth the Money:[x] No Brainer, you have to have it![] Good Value[] If it was on sale[] If you have nothing else to play, yes[] Just keep on scrollingNote: I bought it while it was on sale, but after I've played it I would have immediately bought it for full price!Activities:30% Exploring30% Fishing-Minigames20% Questing10% Inventory management10% Worrying about the darkTo sum up, Dredge is a very sweet indie-story-exploring-type-of game you won't regret buying. The Sound and graphics are charming, the story is a bit short but very nice, and the overall atmosphere is fantastic. If you are looking for a relaxing game to play after a long stressful day I can 100% recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game! I spent the entire weekend absorbed in it, so I finished the base game (excluding DLC) in two days. Fun to play, pretty art style, and the upgrade system has very noticeable and rewarding results over time. Manage your inventory space like RE4 and pick up little lore bits as you explore the ocean in search of new fish to catch and new towns to explore and sell your catch to. The surprising amount of thriller/horror elements in it keep it fresh and interesting throughout!
_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.review: True gem. Fun mechanics, inventory mgmt, beautiful and eerie music, nightamare fuel-looking fish and a fair price. When games are getting more and more expensive I think the latter seals the deal for me. 9/10 would get chased by , panic, and sail into rocks again.PS: Seriously, the fish are really nasty. Amazing art and style.
_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.review: Dredge balances the relaxation of fishing, curious exploration, tedium of fetch quests and anxiety of what lurks in the dark quite well.The game follows the survival structures well - spend your day (safe) time well gathering resources for upgrades, with the onset of mystery and anxiety/fear in the night. The day/night cycles seem somewhat quick, but considering the actual time it would take to travel & fish - it makes sense thematically. It's an overall fun game, frustrating at times (ie. stone that comes out of nowhere, tornado's that chase you, giant fish that always damage your primary engine lol), but also intriguing, mysterious and with some surprises along the way.As a gamer who highly enjoyed games like Subnautica - it didn't measure up - however, it wasn't trying to either. Dredge is certainly it's own thing - and I can say for my 6 hours of playtime that I've enjoyed it so far and it is close to worth the price to buy it. If you want to relax & fish, explore, see some unsettling things that will heighten your anxiety - give Dredge a whirl :)
_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.review: This a fun game. There's nothing crazy or surprising in it, but it's consistently fun the whole way through. Btw if you don't like horror games, don't worry. Dredge is like 98% fishing/exploration and 2% horror. Maybe even less than that. Even fishing at night isn't very scary as the dangers are all pretty easy to avoid. I would say Subnautica is like 25% horror for reference. The fish art is all pretty cool, especially the many many aberrations. It's always a fun bonus to pick one of those up.
_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted this game for my Steam Deck, ended up buying it for my ROG Ally, and ended up playing it most of the time on my desktop with 3090 FTW.Don't let it fool you, this humble little game is so relaxing, and addicting, you'll end up playing it instead of your fancy AAA titles time and time again.*EDIT* Enjoying it again on my Legion Go!
_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.review: Lovecraft, mystery, sea monsters, fishing, and beautiful art. I was gifted the game and played through every bit of it to reach 100% completion. I recommend Dredge for anyone looking for a fun game with reasonable challenges for achievement completion. The only bit of frustration I found was getting all aberrations as chance is involved and you'll need to revisit some spots over and over. Took me an hour to get my last aberration - a blood skin shark, but still enjoyed doing so.
_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.review: I love awful deep sea creatures, so I'm not sure why it took me so long to play a game which was clearly designed by people who could see something like a barreleye or a viperfish and go 'but what if it was even worse?'. Having said that, as someone who hasn't engaged with horror as a genre much I found this the perfect level of unsettling, just enough to keep me on my toes but not so much that I was afraid to explore. I was even motivated to completely fill out the encyclopaedia, aberrations and all, which is a rare feat in any game. In short: strongly recommended for anyone who wants to sail around and collect horrible fish for 10-20 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.review: This is an wonderful short/medium exploration game about fishing. And fishing by itself is kinda boring, so they add some lovecraft to make things more instresting. The primary focus isn't making a horror game about fishing, its about making a fishing game that is lovecraft flavored.The biggest flaw is its length. Every story note is pretty 1 beat, and doesn't go anywhere in depth. The narrative strength is pretty weak, and the game isn't long at all.
_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.review: Length-wise, I 100%ed within 25 hours without looking anything up; if you just want to do the story then it can feel slightly brief for the cost, with the first few hours being the most enjoyable. The final equipment upgrades (I recommend the biggest net asap) come a bit too late in the main path to be of too much use, but it's not too much of a grind to get everything if you want to - you just have to sleep a lot.It's more fishing minigame than horror, particularly around the half way point when it feels like you've seen all the visual effects and understand how they work. However, right at the end of my 25hrs I went out (sanity fully intact) to the borders of the map to try getting eaten and on the way a new large non-catchable finned creature spawned and swam past - not the dolphins or whale. I wish I hadn't had to wait that long to see it. I guess that's my gist of the game: some really neat things happen that I wish there were more of.
_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.review: Before you read my review, just one disclaimer: The game's horror vibe didn't click with me. The game satisfied a certain itch, but I would not recommend it.From my perspective the by far weakest part of the game. Starts out interesting, but round-about mid-game there's basically nothing to keep you . Most of the side-quests just end without any real revelation, even those that would have an interesting story.After completing the third (out of five) biomes, I mostly rushed the remaining part of the game to see its conclusion.I found this aspect particularly frustrating as the mystery setting starts out strong.There are only fetch-type quests, nothing else. Some side-quests have you guessing what you have to fetch.As written, it did not work for me. You quickly find out how to manage the horror, and at that point, it just falls over board to never return.I played the game entirely with a controller. Initially on the steam deck, but since the default button mapping isn't optimal and cannot be changed on the deck, I switched to PC.In the game, there are basically three relevant areas for the controls:As stated above the default button-mapping is rather bad, and cannot be changed on the steam-deck at the time of writing this review (as soon as you open the respective menu, the game starts to scroll down and won't stop; haven't seen this behavior on any other game on the steam deck, or my laptop with this game)I actually found the changing background tunes very good and fitting to the mood.The simplistic graphics fit to the overall tone and theme, and get the job done. Framerate is decent on the steam deck.Another weak spot. Progression comes in the form of grindable unlocks (ship improvements, research) and abilities unlocked through completion of the main story.The abilities are unremarkable and don't provide much to the gameplay.The grindable unlocks are - grindy. And poorly balanced. Several of the research unlocks can actually be only used when you have unlocked most of the ship improvements, especially the engines. Others are easily accessible nearly from the start and make the lower-level ones basically useless (trawl-nets, baskets)Maybe it would feel more natural if the unlocks were gated by the story progression?A weakly told story that could have been much more. A heavily repetitive main gameplay loop and a poorly designed progression system that relies on grinding.Why did I complete it with all endings? I don't really have an answer for that. Up until mid-game, the weaknesses are not that obvious. The game allows to be played in very short sessions which fits well to my private situation. If it weren't for the button remapping bug, it would be a good fit for commutes with the steam deck. Or if you don't mind the default mapping.
_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.review: It's everything that I want it to be: a solid fishing game with a decent variety of fishes to catch and well done horror elements. There is a drab creepiness that permeates the game without being obnoxious or overbearing.I really enjoy this game as something to do at the end of the day. It's relaxing with a world intriguing enough to never feel boring.
_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.review: I started off this game absolutely terrified to venture much beyond the starting area and ended the game just speeding around the open seas at night, daring the ocean terrors to come after me (and I have a pretty strong case of thalassophobia). This game is both relaxing and good at filling one with dread--quite the balanced mix. The fishing and filling out the fish encyclopedia is so much fun. I really enjoyed the variety of side quests. I loved this game and want more of it. I hope they develop a sequel! It would be an instant buy for me.
_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.review: The game is so good. Though it's totally different in genre, gameplay, and settings, it gives me Subnautica vibes. You get that same thrill—exploring, finding secrets, dodging monsters, and upgrading your gear—but here it's more story-focused. The gameplay is pretty chill and straightforward. Doesn't overstay its welcome, perfect length considering the gameplay variety. Plus, the art and designs? Awesome. Played it non-stop for a few days and finished it. Such a great experience.

I very highly recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: In summary Dredge is what all fishing games must aim for in the future. It’s designed beautifully. The developers have vowed to continue to develop Dredge with them releasing the first DLC A Pale Reach in November of 2023. So what are you waiting for? Come avoid some Lovecraftian horrors and come fish with me!It also runs perfectly well on the Steam Deck! Overall Rating: 9 – Outstanding!Full Review -

_childDocuments_.review: First off, I NEVER leave reviews for games. But this game was so extremely good that I had to. The artstyle, gameplay, flow, story, horror, sounds, EVERYTHING is insanely amazing and I can't stress that enough. I took my time with the story and explored/completed a lot of the side quests and that alone offered 12 hours of highly immersive gameplay throughout. Even after the main game, there are HOURS of enjoyable replayability for completionists like me. Dredge has easily become one of my favorite games of all time. I would highly recommend this game and I'm excited to see what else the developers produce in the future. Dredge is beyond more valuable than what it is priced at and worth every penny. Well done on this 10/10 masterpiece!

Or maybe the knowledge about the world makes it easier to go through it?Anyway: It feels like the last two areas just fly by, while the first three feel much more alive and cared for.It's still fun to play. _childDocuments_.review: It was fun at first, but it gets annoying after an hour or two. The time and space managment element is disappointing because days in this game are way too short and your ships is way too small so you have to plan everything (including things that you don't even know about) in advance. It would be alright if this game focused either on exploration or chill vibes but by encouraging both at the same time neither is fun.For example: crab pots. The game wants you to put them down somewhere on the map and return to them every once in a while to get crabs from them. Sadly, this gameplay element isn't fleshed out enough to have any depth so it gets annoying fast. It discourages adventures because you wont have any place left on your ship after one to pick anything up. If you decide to instead wait and do some mundane tasks close to them so that you can actually use them, the game punishes by being boring.The horror elements are weak. Just some ghost ships and ghost rocks. I got to the 4th area and didn't game over a single time. I even started to ignore the day and night cycle. The only scary part was when the game deleted my save and I lost all my progress.I hope the game gets better in the 5th area but I lost my motivation to keep playing in the 2nd one. The story seems basic, the gameplay doesn't change, the horror is non-existant. There is some charm in this game and I believe it is in some ways one of a kind. If you like thrilling games, this one will annoy you.If you like cosy games, this one might be for you.

_childDocuments_.review: I have to say, I'm shocked by how well reviewed this game is.TLDR:A very tedious and repetitive grindfest and series of fetch quests with a "sanity mechanic" that aim at making the process as needlessly time consuming as possible without adding anything else to the game (not even any real horror element).Don't get fooled into thinking this is a chill, relaxing or even spooky game where the focus is on your and your fishing adventures, because this isn't the case.----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------I'm actually sad about this game. I really wanted to like it, everything I saw about this game so far looked fun and interesting.What I expected from the glimpses I took from various streams, the steam page and the review was a chill fishing game where you explore the seas, live off your catches and have to deal with some spooky Lovecraftian shenanigans that would make fishing at night an interesting challenge.What I got instead was one of the most shallow experience I've ever had without any of these elements. It was instead of very by the book, almost MMO-like series of fetchquest and grinds without even an interesting gameplay to back it up.The navigation is uninspired. Weather, Wind, Waves, basically nothing matter in the slightest (I think, in some very rare occasion the wind may impact your deplacement? Maybe? The fact that I beat the game and I'm still not sure just hilight how unimpactful it is anyway).The fishing is uninteresting. A simple QTE with different variants that all could be boild down to "press the buttom when the green thing get in the target". I've honestly seen more engaging and impactful fishing minigames in other games where fishing is a very small side activity, but there it's the main activity. The overal story is very linear and basically a very long and uninspired chain of MMO quest style tasks, almost entirely made of fetch quests. Complete a couple of thos and you've cleared one of the 4 corners of the map.Complete all the 4 corners and you've completed the game.But all that could be handwaved if the game was actually fun and engaging... sadly its not.You just go in a straight line toward the next zone.Find the quest.Struggle a bit to understand exactly what you are supposed to do (or rather where exactly you are supposed to go), rince and repeat until it's done. At least one zone had a side quest (which was basically find the 3 fishing spots that glow yellow) and it gave me a reward that is pretty underwhelming.And all that with the god awful day/night timer that forces you to constantly run back and forth between the spot you are trying to clear and the nearest port, because if you don't regularly go there and hit the "sleep" button, you will be bombarded by various ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ until you die and have to restart from your last save.The game present itself as if it has some kind of lovecraftian survival element (I've even seen some hacks try to tag this game as "horror game", which is hilarious), where you have to manage your sanity like a ressource and some time have to push against the madness, but that's not the case, once you realize how basic the game is, it lose any hint of suspense of fear.Night come, you can't seen anything so you can't really keep fishing, and if you stay anyway your sanity drop. Once it's low random damaging entity, from giant fishes to heat seeking tornados will go after you constantly attacking you and making fishing basically impossible as you turn into a sitting duck while doing so, so you have to stop what you were doing, get to the nearest port and sleep, then go back where you left off and start again.You will basically spend 80% of your time going back and forth between your fishing spot and the port until you get some upgrades that will slowly make things better but that's pretty late in the game. Remove that and the game could probably be completed in 2 hours, and I'm not even joking.Once you get hit you will lose cargo space, which mean one of the fishes you already caught, or one of your gear (and if one of your engine got bit you'll have the joy of being slowed down to a crawl, which makes the process of getting back to the port even slower). And since damages can only be repaired in one specific port per zone, getting hit will ruin your day.Once you get to the port, you can repair any damage for basically no money and your sanity is fully replenished in seconds, without any other effect.I cleared 99% of the content, leaving only a handful of quest (the cultists asking me a very specific rare fish, which I honestly couldn't be bothered to play gatcha for, and a quest where I had to find a home for a random dog... no prompt ever showed up so here's that).The only reason why I stuck with the game till the end was first to be able to make that review, and second because I am the kind of autistic individual that can't let a progress bar unfilled, but god knows filling these bars was one of the most unrewarding experience I've ever had.The ship itself is just a giant ressource sink with basically no choices others than in what order you want to complete the grind.You can't chose a ship type, you can't really "make a build", it's all very linear. (Here's a protip for you, focus on the fishing gear first as its literally the only real "gear check" the game will throw at you. You will need a specific type of gear to fish into a specific region, so just max fishing gear, get the omni tools that let you fish everything and you are done).You quickly realize that basically none of what should be the core gameplay (exploring the sea and fishing stuff) matter. The money you'll get from fish is only useful to upgrade the boat and buy the couple of fishing pole required to fish in all zone, and the money isn't even the real roadblock here, it's the wood, metal and cloth you get from Dredring (roll credit), so you'll spend most of your early game desperately looking for these specific fishing spots between the rest of your fetch quests and... that's it.At some point I got hit by how painfully pointless everything is here. I could have a good time fishing because of the constant back and forth with the closest port because of the sanity mechanic, I couldn't really explore because of that mechanic once again, so the only thing I can really do is grind as fast as possible the couple of upgrade I could slap on my boat to make that process less painful and keep doing the fetch quests.The game try to pretend you have an impact on the growth of the world around you, like the starting town growing thanks to you, but it's all window dressing and fake. There is no comerce that would require you to go to specific regions to sell specific fishes at better prices. There is no economy, not other fishermen you could encounter at sea, nothing. You don't have any choices outside of a last second choice between Good Ending and Bad Ending (the bad ending has a pretty cool cinematic shot tbf) and that's it.I bought the game on a decent 45% discount and I still feel rippedoff. Not of my money, but of my time.I sunk 14h in it and and wish to get them back.I've had deeper and more engaging fishing boat experience in MMOs like FF14 or ArchAge.I've had more interesting lovercraftian sea exploration games like Sunless Sky.I've had better boat navigation game overall like Blackflag, Sea of Thief or even Zelda wind walker.And I've had better "chill, do busy work and fill the bar" games like Stardew Valley, Factorio or Grave Digger.This game is just worthless and I'm baffled by the fact that so many people seem to have enjoyed the experience.

_childDocuments_.review: BLUF: Too Short. Just my personal opinion, but i've always rated games by "a dollar an hour" approach. If you sell a game for 26 USD, I should be able to get around 26 hours of game play. With this game... unfortunately... you'll need to wait for it to be on sale.It kills me not to recommend this game, because its ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ AMAZING! Its a GREAT game. Literally the only issues I can think of with the game is that the hooded figure quests have a built in timer, that starts the moment you talk to a hooded figure. If you fail to complete the quest before the hidden timer expires, the hooded figure dies, and you lose the quest rewards forever. The game never tells you the timer exists.That one and only game related complaint is not enough to warrant a negative review. But the fact that I beat the game, got both endings, and got far enough into the game to have completed or near completed 95% of the content, in just 13 hours, makes it too short to be worth 26 USD.(For context, near completed example: A quest to find 4 specific fish. _childDocuments_.review: While I do recommend this game, I much preferred the first half of my play-through to the second.I felt like many of the mechanics, while not necessarily simple, weren't fully explored or as deep as I'd hoped. That's not inherently a bad thing, but the presentation of the game gave me the expectation that there'd be more to it. Once I figured out the handful of mechanics it was easy enough to effectively bypass any of the challenge and accidentally speed-run to the end. Each of the main objectives is deceptively simple to complete, and I'd frequently be more underwhelmed with the quick resolution than impressed with the circumstances that got me there in the first place.The art direction is gorgeous and consistent throughout, each region you visit feels unique and the characters you encounter are good fun for a bit. The magic of it all just ended quicker than I expected and the horror elements weren't what I was hoping they'd become.

_childDocuments_.review: Dredge is a captivating game that left me wanting more. The storytelling and atmosphere are excellent, drawing you into the game's world. The sea and boating mechanic are also superb, although I would have liked to experience more intense weather conditions. The madness mechanic is well-executed, with a sense of impending doom that adds to the tension of the game. The effect of rocks appearing as you descend into madness is particularly neat.I played the game twice in just three days, and for 25, it's fair at a dollar per hour. However, I felt that the fishing and dredging mechanics were a bit too simplistic, and I would have preferred something more like Graveyard Keeper. Despite the game offering a vast variety of fish and fish variants, all fishing feels the same. There's no real distinction between different baits or line snapping, and it lacks a more engaging mechanic that could make the fishing aspect more immersive. A sonar minigame for the nets would have been a nice addition, as the current system makes catching fishies  uninvolved.Overall, Dredge is a fantastic game that could have been even better with a more immersive fishing mechanic. Despite its flaws, the storytelling, atmosphere, and boating mechanics make it a game worth buying.
_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.review: I am amazed, I've watched this game as a part of a game showcase and I immediately got hooked. Lastly, the art style truly fits the game as it reflects the atmosphere, characters, and items in the surrounding environment.

_childDocuments_.review: Im giving this game a positive review because it simply deserves one. However, Im going to list some cons that I've run into during the game that detract from the experience more or less. I find that I'm more comfortable buying a game knowing it's negative tendencies more so than a bunch of people saying "itz gud". 1. The map is ill utilized. Essentially, there are 5 main "areas" in the game to fish around/ in and progress the story. These areas are right in the center of the game world map and the other 75% of the world map is completely empty ocean outside of this circle of hub islands. You cant fish, there's nothing to find and it seriously detracts from the exploration side of the game. They should have mixed around the hub islands and a bunch of sprawling isle locations throughout the entire map rather than having all of it outside the hub isles completely empty.2. Treasure is pretty damn useless. It doesnt sell for much and there is literally no incentive to collect it. Fish sell for far more and you can deliver fish to any of the five ports in the game, whereas treasure can only be delivered to a single trader in the starting region. 3. Unique ship parts are also terrible. Going through a lengthy quest which rewards you with an item that is objectively worse than the standard one you can buy at the shop is terrible design. There's only one or two unique parts in the entire game which are worth the trouble.4. This might not be a big deal for some, but for me it was annoying. There is no combat in the game whatsoever. "Its a fishing game, why would it need combat lol?" Because there's a plethora of aggressive fish and sea monsters throughout the game where your only option is to run away. I thought it was cool at first to be a small tugboat desperately trying to escape leviathans, but later on when the anxiety wears off its just a huge annoyance when you're simply trying to grab that one piece of wood or fish and to be constantly harassed by your mom. The game does give you a stun ability about halfway through, but it only lasts a few seconds.5. All of the quests are exactly the same. Deliver fish or cargo, that's it.6. The game has an interesting mechanic right at the very start. You owe a loan to the mayor for giving you an old boat. After paying the loan off within the first 15 minutes of playing, this is never brought up again as a mechanic. There are no other boats you can purchase and all equipment is paid in cash. I would've rather seen a boat improvement system which continues to put you in debt as you purchase better upgrades/ better boats during the game. It would create a much better incentive to fish more, whereas now the only time you "need" to fish are when quests demand it or you just want to buy that super cheap upgrade. Thats about all I can think of at the moment. I would definitely recommend this game if you're wanting something for the weekend. I'd personally give this game an 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: It's... not bad, but I think that the price and the overwhelmingly positive reviews make the game seem better than it actually is. The main gameplay loop is almost perfect. Catching fishes, upgrading your boat, all great. The mood, atmosphere is also great, nice art style, no bugs, well polished. You can find may secret spots, which I enjoyed a lot. The quests are nice, but they are a bit artifical. Basically there are 4 (5 if you count the starting area) "quest hubs", and you  can find and do all on one quest hub before moving to the next. They don't reference to each other, they don't send you from there to there, etc, it didn't feel like a real world, more like levels, or chapters. Especially as all of these areas has a very generic "travelling merchant" that can do basically everything so it is not even needed to go back to your base to upgrade your ship or anything. Most of your time you interact with this travelling merchant instead of the actual inhabitants of the area. I think simply changing the travelling merchant to a location-specific NPC would've helped. Fishing and dredging is fun, but you find a lot of unneeded stuff. Why would you dredge up some trinkets to sell them for 20$ when you can simply fish for better money. Overall the game economy is good, you never swim in money, but you also don't starve for it. The boat felt a little small, as some of the later fishes have rather large silhouettes, but it wasn't annoying, it just made the inventory tetris interesting. I finished the game in 8.5 hours, which, for 25 euro, isn't a lot, especially as it wasnt some super amazing 8 hours, but more like "i am kinda having fun" 8 hours. I don't feel that I should go back and get the good(ish) ending too, even though it wouldn't take a lot of time.I know my review sounds negative, don't get me wrong, the game is not bad, its just.... well, I expected some Sunless Sea vibes, and this is a bit simpler. But hey, at least I finished it, which is not true for SS :) Overall recommended, but I think the overall impression of the game is simply too good, and it just cannot deliver it perfectly.

_childDocuments_.review: this game is insanely good. i went into it thinking "this looks kinda cool," but it has quickly become my favorite game of the year thus far. the concept is so uniquely perfect - a seemingly basic fishing game elevated by a lovecraftian atmosphere, reminiscent of "The Shadow over Innsmouth." It's inherently simple but that is part of its charm. the music alone is worth the asking price - and the characters are interesting and well written. i cannot recommend this game enough. check it out.

_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. _childDocuments_.review: Oh boy, steam reviewers have really taken a down-slide over the years. After this game im completely giving up on having faith in "Overwhelmingly positive" reviews. Which is sad because these reviews used to be VERY reliable.Lets break this down...Graphics - 4Sounds - 3Story - 4Gameplay - 5Replayability - 2What we have here is a VERY SIMPLE fishing minigame which gets repetitive quite quickly, and is far too easy. Probably worth $5-10 dollars. There are no real skill requirements, you will never lose a fish or break a line. Time passes by stupidly fast, you catch around 8 fish then head back to base, rinse repeat, with each trip taking around 4mins. The inventory management part is more annoying than fun, with the various 'Tetris' shaped fish just being laid out on the deck, rather than being stored in iceboxes or containers, which doesnt really make sense.The horror night theme was very lacking, i expected to have to use your wisdom and knowledge of the waters to navigate back home in the darkness, but the fact is when night falls, the entire map changes, you cant see far it all, which seems cool, but the game trolls this by having rocks suddenly appear that were not there earlier which do not reward a player for "knowing the waters" like an experienced fisherman would.I feel this game would have benefited a lot if it had an actual storage place for the fish, and the fish caught each day were more around 30-50 each day, rather than 5-10. Also i think a game of this nature suffers a great deal by having a story, and follow the path system with the exact same map each game. I think a random map generator would have made things a ton more fun.TLDR, far too expensive for such a very very simple game.
_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.review: It's one of those games you wish you could forget and play again.But even aside from the story and mystery DREDGE is a very good game. The fishing mini games are very enjoyable, there's never any waiting for something to bite or similar annoyances. The atmosphere is very fitting. And fortunately for me, not as "horror" as some YouTube titles might have you believe. It's more along the lines of a psychological thriller.All in all i was VERY pleasantly surprised. If you are on the fence just buy it before you get spoiled. For me DREDGE certainly was one of the best games in recent history.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games your friend recommends and then you never play. You should listen to your friend. She's just trying to help you. She knows you've been having some troubles. You know ever since that thing that happened. You know the thing we don't talk about. I'm sorry I brought it up. It's just you've been looking very pale.Remember those days  down by the shore,  Your friends and you would go out on that rust-bucket fishing boat. We didn't do much fishing but we had a good time. Everyone would just drink. not too much but never too little.  Our laughter mingled with the soft whirl of fishing reels?  God I remember that thing you used to do, that was crazy.  Wild the things you can learn from books. We knew you were just foolin' around about the other stuff. Everybody likes to talk big about their catches. The sun would cast a golden glow over us,  and then quietly slip beneath the waves. The water was really dark that night, remember? I know we said nobody would ever find out, but are you sure? It's just that we don't talk since then. I'd still like to go out on the ocean but I think we would just drown in our memories of that night.You've just been so different. You should really see a doctor, you really don't look well. I just thought a fishing game would help. A first step, just a small one. Maybe the sound of the motor will remind you of the thrum of waves crashing against tht old boat of ours. The fish were always biting, it's just that we weren't listening. Don't worry about your game backlog, all those regrets. You just need to listen to the call of the ocean. I know it still calls to you, I hear it too.We were happy then. We can still go back, back to the way things were. She was right you know, about the recommendation. These indie games, their just a little outside the norm, a bit off the beaten path.  She was a true original,, she would have wanted this. We were all a little different, just some more than others. Don't wait for the sale. Haven't we all waited long enough waiting. Isn't that what you said? Life is for the living,, mostly.The time is nigh.

_childDocuments_.review: Look... you have a boat, you fish, fish are kinda weird. Hey, what's that? *FOG HORN* It's a black ship! He is hailing me, he want's to be friends. I'm taking damage, this boat is evil. What the hell are these tentacles? There's floating eyes? What is happening. I'm going to sleep this off.Oh cool, inventory Tetris mini-game. Oh, Pokemon at sea, gotta catch them all... at different depths. Black rocks do cool... and terrifying things. Hey, this game is pretty damned good. You should buy it, you'll enjoy it.
_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.review: This game ticked a lot of my personal boxes. Ocean adventures, collecting a vast array of fishes, inventory puzzle and an atmosphere of horror hanging over it all. Perhaps not the most helpful comparison, but it put me in mind of the sailing in The Legend of Zelda: Windwaker. This vast oceans with all these little places to discover. Safe to say that this game does a lot right and a hearty recommend from me. The few qualms I have with Dredge are mostly centered on the lack of stuff the game can reward you with in the latter half. I had the upgrade-tree finished roughly by the midway point, and then all the materials you find and the wealth you gather are useless. An endgame prey to hunt that requires three yachts duct-taped together wouldn't have gone amiss. Something so soak up all this capital I've been accumulating. Basically, the only issue I had with the game was that I wanted a reason to stay longer in the world, which could be considered just another compliment in disguise. If you enjoy exploration, collecting and the open seas, you'll enjoy this game!
_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.review: It's a rare moment that a game has such a concise and PREcise vision and executes on it so well. Dredge starts slowly, but deliberately and ramps you up in sync with the tension that comes naturally from wandering outside your starting tutorial haven. It immediately asks of you-- "what's out there?", and waits until the perfect moment to show you. Give it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.review: the core mechanics (fishing minigame + inventory management) fizzle out as there is no tension to the gameplay loop; there's no resources that really need much attention like sanity/hunger/required deliveries. this lack of tension turns into frustration given that days are incredibly short, and story quests range from 'rather compelling' to 'flat'. when i reached the section requiring dynamite, i realized my enjoyment had lapsed ..giving this a thumbs up because it was quite pleasant to begin, and i'm sure many will not take issue with the lack of tension to the gameplay loop and instead simply enjoy the story (there is a charming story here if it suits you).
_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.review: INCREDIBLE COZY SPOOKY FISHING GAME ITS SO GOOD NO SPOILS JUST PLAYAtmosphere and art style are amazing, beautifully marrying 2D painted characters with a low poly 3D world.The propeller even spins!Music and SFX are top notch, draws you in so well - shout out to the New Zealand wildlife you can hear at some points.The developers have found a fine balance between exploration, storytelling, and vibing on a boat.Play at your own pace for a comfy story experience, or devour the content like the old gods intended and let the panic set in. How you play is up to you and DREDGE will feel wonderful however you choose.10/10 puns, don't let this game pass you like a ship(?!) in the night.
_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.review: The story line is well thought out with clues that give it just enough mystery to keep you looking. Upgrading your boat is rewarding and well paced. I bought The Pale Reach DLC and have really enjoyed exploring the ice fields, and the story there as well. I hope they keep adding areas and more stories, or even expanding this universe.
_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.review: A beautifully crafted game! Gameplay is well balanced, gripping me early on with a simple, almost cozy loop... almost! The story coaxed me to probe ever deeper, at my own pace, and kept me engaged all of the way through. I picked up the DLC after a day of playing, but didn't engage with it until near the end of my playthrough which was a mistake. I think The Blackstone Key DLC should be dealt with earlier in your game, and the Pale Reach would also probably have been more of a challenge had I not already hit the end game, but it was still worthwhile.I suggest playing with gamepad for the added vibration cues to go with the lovely audio, but keep a mouse handy for inventory tetris!34 hours and I'm now just combing the seas as a completionist before finding out what the finale brings... I have no doubts it'll be good! Picked this game up on sale but I'd pay full price for it, it's a good'un.
_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a person that tends to overthink games and rush far too quickly into the game trying to get to the next "bit". This game has curtailed me of this sin. The game progresses fast enough as to not to be a chore but slow enough that you can absorb the atmosphere. And that's what this game has in spades. The atmosphere is right on point. Don't want to scare yourself; fish during the day, earn some money, upgrade your boat for the next catch. But...you will at some point need to push out of your comfort zone. There's a lot of trepidation in doing so but there might just be some serious rewards for doing so. I'm 5 hours in and feel like I've only just scratched the surface of what this game has to offer.

_childDocuments_.review: REVISED REVIEW @ 68 HOURS - A Request and an Edited ReviewRevised again at ~80+ hours to include some additional information recognizing some of the amazing access/inclusive options in settings, and expand the DLC idea(s). Thanks Devs, y'all are awesome.Short Version - It's a darn-good game that the whole family can enjoy with many options for "accessible Inclusion" (though I think there could be some more options made available) and many options for replay when you challenge yourself to complete the game in various ways. If I had to give it a number score I would put it at a 8-9 out of 10 .. they just got so many things "right" as the game has developed and expanded. The Blackstone Isle DLC (the only one avail as of 2023-06-29) is worth the price and adds to the enjoyment of the game.A REQUEST .. To the Devs .. please make a patch/add-on setting in your game settings that adds some strength to the boat hull .. be one of those games that is deliberately designed for folks with a different level of ability, be it congenital, traumatic, or geriatric .. there are FAR to few opportunities for a HUGE chunk of the world population to enjoy content like this .. that "brittle hull" destroys the game for anyone with visual impairments or physical challenges to their fine-motor skills .. even folks with Asperger's or other challenges find this to be a challenge that causes them to simply quit the game as they can't manage keeping the boat intact .. it's a pretty simple fix that opens up the game to young and elderly folks alike.EDITED REVIEW - VERY POSITIVE - since "EXTREMELY POSITIVE" is not an option .. lol .. A Brilliant Game .. (1) First off, it's "wholesome" enough that the whole family can play .. (2) It's a "Puzzle Challenger" with Static Tetris/Placement Puzzle, and a story line that unlocks with "Discovery Quests" throughout the game play and exploration.(3) Skill Challenges for fishing - Varied "timing" challenges for different species of fish/crabs - NOTE: that the speed of these challenges can be adjusted in the settings for those who have fine motor-skill or fast-response issues (huge shout out tot he Devs for including this setting).(4) Visual Impairment Settings are available in the settings - These also include motion/shake and chromatic settings. Again, THANK YOU DEVs for including these settings as well.(5) Game Atmosphere - It's a pretty tame "horror" experience with some decent "jump scares" and "run-for-your-life" moments .. and some of these/this can be adjusted in the game settings as well. Once again, a HUGE Thank You to the Devs for expanding the options to allow for a large audience.After my third run-through to 100% the game it is still fun and enjoyable .. I will be playing it again to challenge myself with some different builds (mission accomplished on play-through 4 and 5) .. at first I really felt the game was a "once-and-done" game, but after discovering there is a "hidden/secret" ending that takes a bit more time to unravel, I had to make that second run .. and then a third to 100% the game .. and depending on the DLC updates I will likely continue more runs and exploration of the the mechanics of the game and the story line .. and I am also enjoying challenging myself with min/max builds and trying to compress day-cycles (I hesitate to call them "speed runs") top accomplish game completion both in tasks and number of days.The game is one that I enjoy so much that I have shared it with my family and (so far) have purchased three copies of the game .. and a 4th is looming large .. lol ..I'll make a DLC/game-play request/suggestion as well .. maybe through a DLC like the Blackstone DLC you could add new items and an expansion for the hold to allow enough room for that new/revised equipment that covers ALL of the fishing/trawling "types"?? .. I would love to play a 100% play that used only "Aberrant Items" .. currently that is just not possible as you (the player) are required to research at least two items to acquire "Volcanic" access to complete the game, and you have to purchase the base net which is offered by/in the Shipwright sub-menu .. Currently, you can't place all of the "Aberrant Items" into the hull/provided spots at one time for a "current game" (as of 2023-06-22) .. though it's not "impossible" to manage, as a personal preference, I just don't enjoy the creation of "micro-management challenges" to extend game play. I would (personally) much prefer loading up my ship and heading out to sea to explore and enjoy the game .. there is enough "running around" to complete missions/side missions/tasks with out adding the extra layer of micro-management. Is there and chance at all for a "maximum hull" upgrade so players can min/max their builds to change things up to create different personal challenges (and hint: it would be really sweet/kewl/amazing to include specific challenges in the Steam Rewards. Can/Would you "fix" or "include" this/these PLEASE?

_childDocuments_.review: What sets DREDGE apart from traditional fishing games is its ominous atmosphere and mysterious narrative. The developers have expertly woven an underlying sense of unease into the tranquil fishing experience, gradually revealing the dark secrets hidden within the archipelago. The game's art style, haunting sound design, and subtle environmental storytelling combine to create a captivating and immersive world that keeps players engaged throughout their journey. DREDGE successfully merges the serene art of fishing with an engrossing narrative and a sense of foreboding. The game's fishing mechanics, upgrade system, and captivating atmosphere create an experience that goes beyond a simple fishing simulator. If you're looking for a single-player adventure that offers a unique blend of relaxation, mystery, and anxiety inducing extensional dread, then DREDGE is a catch worth reeling in.
_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.review: Dredge is an Adventure/Exploration game focused on fishing, with a sprinkle of lovecraftian horror elements. The consistent, yet nonrestrictive game play loop and the creative world/art keep you engaged throughout it's ~15-20 hour runtime. While the world gives you enough information to be intrigued, the plot and stories that are told through the game are not as prevalent. Dredge contains a solid game play loop of fishing for money and using the money for upgrades. Ship upgrades allow for more hull space, faster travel, and new categories of fish to capture. Developing strategies around upgrade paths was truly the hook of the game. Every upgrade feels immediately rewarding. The freedom in the upgrading and management of the game is also reflected in the world. While the game does provide you with set objectives, you are free to explore the world at your will. I had a lot of fun exploring "late game" areas early, and then returning later on, better equipped to manage it's unique challenges. Adopting horror elements into a fishing game seems out of place, but Dredge manages to pull it off. It invokes the fear of the unknown multiple times throughout the adventure, whether through it's mechanics or it's world. The art, in particular the creative design around the aberration fish designs was truly a treat. I find myself wanting to catch every species just to see the creative ideas the art team came up with. Dredge implements a day system where time passes as you are moving. Unfortunately, the mechanic of passing days did not come into play besides a day/night cycle and a few side-quests. I would have loved to see more quests and objectives utilize the day system in such a way that it forces you to make temporal decisions.
_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.review: Dredge is a phenomenal game about fishing, management and exploration, and it's one of the more recent titles that really showcases the passion of indie game development. The game features a brilliant artstyle and soundtrack which enhances the grim, dark and twisted nature of its world. Gameplay-wise, it's not very challenging, but it heavily rewards exploration. Along your travels you'll meet new characters, gain new abilities and upgrades for your boat, which keeps it interesting. Few games are without flaws, though. The first hours of the game are truly magical and very ominous, but when you start traveling to new areas, that feeling kind of disappears. The story and its characters could definitely have been explored more deeply. I was kind of disappointed at the ending since it feels fairly anticlimactic, all things considered.Overall, I whole-heartedly recommend Dredge, but I would love to see a sequel that has a more fleshed out story and perhaps is a little longer.

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful combination of fishing game and Lovecraft's eldritch horrors... without the bigotry. Fun to play! Could stand to benefit from marks on the map -- WHERE I'm supposed to go for different quests. (Update: those show up once one has discovered the locations.) Also: dredging is a difficult minigame (have a slight handicap), but fishing is fun! (Update: settings allow for help to those with handicaps, or who just want an easier minigame experience.)The two DLCs added their own unique eldritch horrors and wonderfully creepy moments, which were SO worthwhile. And I went through two different endings to the game, which were BOTH awesome, in different (and wholly Lovecraftian) ways!Finally, LOVE the soundtrack. Well written, and perfectly scores the eerie story. One of my fave games this year!

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a deeply addictive quality to it. The "arcade-y" aspect mixes with the horror element in a way I really didn't expect them to succeed in. Don't get me wrong, this game will likely not scare you. But it does do an excellent job of telling a quality story, being backed up by mostly fun, engaging, yet relaxing gameplay. Also, paying homage respectfully to its clear-cut Lovecraftian influences.It has a pretty satisfying "level up" system, the characters make you want to read every line of dialogue, the controls feel intuitive, as does most of the game (it's quite easy), there's a decent amount cool little things around the map for you to find and piece together, and both endings are a fitting conclusion to this little gem of an indie game. Also if you're into collecting there are a LOT of fish for you to find and log.There are only a few negative things I have to say about Dredge. Firstly, I feel like while there is a decent amount of side content here, the world could have been a bit more populated with quests and characters to find. Maybe I am spoiled by other games, I just feel another three or four quests would have been pretty much on the money.Secondly, the endgame can be a bit grindy, and then it feels like the game has run its course as far as upgrades go. At the end of my playthrough I was basically spending money on everything I could and it was genuinely hard to drop below 4k, boat fully upgraded, that's it. I know some people will look at that and say "it has to end somewhere" and you're right. But the feeling of grinding for money and then the payoff actually being less fun to play because the game is easy and it's easy to make a lot of money. Plus, there are really no new things for me to spend my cash on, and my boat was pretty much fully upgraded before the volcano. The early stages of the game, the struggle with what you have, that is the most fun part of the game in my opinion.Thirdly, while I do agree that it's completely optional content and not necessary, the DLC selling you access to the workshop which gives you two items that should be in the base game is kind of annoying. Without the DLC the workshop is still there, you just can't access it. In what I would consider an otherwise completely finished and full package experience, it feels like a strange decision to take some of the shine away from that accomplishment.Lastly, I just want there to be more of it. I can't wait to see what the devs do next. I got a decent amount of hours out of it for the price, and I am more than happy with the experience I had.I'm so glad this turned out well, a gem of 2023 for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: I played this for ~15 hours and completed till the end. It has a pretty good (if basic) story line and it is very well presented. And that is the key thing throughout - it is well presented. The graphics are simple, effective, and fit the mood. The UI is well presented (clear, uncluttered) and more or less intuitive (a couple of huh? moments which in hindsight were my own issue). Only real usability issue is the Encyclopedia - The left hand categories "toggle", but the right hand side does not. If I am looking for "a fish", I may not necessarily know anything about it except its name - A search would be useful hereThe "rod" progression screen could do with something to indicate that the second batch of rods can only be gained after the first 5 or 6 are completed). I did a little trawling and a bit of potting - screens looked ok.Some balancing is needed with regards to wrecks and scrap - Not enough wood. Would be good to see some offered by the merchants as it is quite scarce when on tier 4 hulls.Would also like to see some indicator on some side quests to indicate that these are time sensitive - Need to complete in a period of time else the pursuit ends (so can't complete them all). Best if these are left till later in the quest so the player knows where to find the fish needed to complete).Sounds work well, sets the tone and atmosphere.Completing the whole set of pursuits is an issue (due to the time limit on some of them - Unknown until you fail) and I am disinclined to start the game again to complete these.Only other minor gripe is that the day/night cycle is sometimes too short. Wake up at 6, sail to an island, dock, need to sleep till the next day...Would welcome a "passive sailing" mode where you can just sail around, fish, explore - not affect game play.Would recommend. Polished. Nice difficulty level. Lots to fish to find. Nice set of diverse biomes to explore.Shortish.

_childDocuments_.review: I ultimately vote to recommend this, but that recommendation comes with major caveats.The first is that I absolutely loathe the control scheme in this game.It's an inventory management nightmare (thematically appropriate, I guess).  My biggest beef is that basically every quest in the game has you giving items to characters, but there's no faster way to do it than having to drag everything from your ship to the character.  And stars help you if you have to dig through the storage tab instead.  There's a button to quickly move items from your cargo to your storage, or to quick sell, why can't there be a "Quick Turn In" button?  Huh?  Devs?  *crickets*Driving the boat also sucks with the default control setup.  You move forward and back with the left stick and also turn with the left stick.  Do yourself a favor: the first thing you ever do should be to go into the settings and change forward and back to the right/left triggers like a driving game.  You will thank yourself for this later.  If you don't, I guarantee you that you will run into something at least once because of the default controls and you will feel stark regret.The second caveat is that the gameplay loop never throws any curveballs at you.  It never evolves after the first hour of the game and it's the very definition of "ocean wide, puddle deep".  None of the fish are ever more difficult to catch than they are at the beginning, finding them never becomes more complex, storing them never becomes more complex, the quests themselves never become more complex - it's go here to this X on the map, pull up this thing and bring it back to me the entire game.  I'm not asking for the game to turn into Dark Souls in the third act or anything, but something a bit more challenging than My Little Cthulu would have been nice?  The game's atmosphere just didn't not outweigh how simple it all was for me, which is an absolute buzzkill in these games with 10 hours runtimes.So yes.  Fun, but simple.  And wears out its welcome by the end.  Great atmosphere, good art, good audio, frustrating controls.  Recommended, sort of.

_childDocuments_.review: A very compelling videogame but a pretty weak piece of weird horror fiction. If simple, satisfying mechanics and a moreish progression loop appeal to you, consider this a strong recommendation. If it's the "Lovecraftian" elements that caught your interest, . Weird fiction is a genre driven by hidden depths. Characters appear to be one way, but they're hiding disturbing backstories. Reality appears to work one way, but learning how it  works breaks your mind. In Dredge, everyone and everything is exactly as it seems on the surface. It takes the aesthetics of weird fiction--ancient cults, spooky 20th century technology, strange monsters--but delivers very little of the atmosphere, none of the existential dread and none of the mind-bending philosophy. It's weird horror without any of the actual horror.Put all that together and you get a sharp, compelling exploration/management game with a very disappointing shrug of a story. My recommendation: play while you listen to the audiobook for The Fisherman by John Langan, and just click through all the text in the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Fishing games are cosy games right? Not this one which starts off innocuously enough with you trying to pay back a loan to your wrecked boat by fishing and selling the catch to the local town. Simple matter, no? Though soon enough you learn that after dark weird things tend to happen that tests your very sanity to the point where eldritch Lovecraftian beings soon start bleeding into reality as you start losing your mind to the madness that is, the sea. There are similar games such as this before, the best case being Sunless Seas. The difference is that Dredge compresses the intricate and multilayered world of Fallen London and complex mechanics to a minimalist core, which doesn't diminish its charm, interesting game play and horror induced story line at all, yet makes it more approachable to a wider audience and easier to enjoy.Pros:+ Lovely low poly graphics fits into the world building, they dynamic changes from day and night not only enhances the environs but cranks up the horror factor as you struggle in the dark and fog battling horrors from another world.+ The main story line is straightforward but layered and conveys adequately a tale of mystery, horror and intrigue in which you slowly peel and understand with each completed task until the climax.+ A variety of biomes with their own terrain, ecology and challenges that provides enough variety of fishes, each requiring you figure out and install the appropriate gear and also technique to catch them.+ Innovative and impressive crafting system which isn't too complex but engaging enough to players. Several tiers of research, gear crafting and mini games makes for a real challenging, yet well scaled progression ssytem.+ The upgrade system for the boat is interesting to play with as well as gear and inventory management, kudos to the developers on this. A very unique limitations on how much gear you can install and juggling space to hold your catch, crafting gear and a whole host of other stuff.Cons- Some random RNG for catching crabs can make it frustrating and time consuming compared to the other tasks.- The story is lighter than most of the other esoteric genres out there, while its not as complex, it distills the essence of Lovecraftian and still brings it out to the gamer. It may seem lite to true Lovecraftian lovers but an easier entry point for those unfamiliar with it.- The DLCs while varied and adds to more game hours, isn't really worth the standalone price, buy it at a discount. They also feel a bit disjointed from the overall game at times.

_childDocuments_.review: God I love fishing and hate my wife.Grab a beer. Throw the headphones on. Forget about the wife. Catch some fish. Beautiful.I don't even know what fishing is, I just play this game to look at the pretty water and question life.This game will really remind you of that time you spent with your dad before he left to get a pack of cigarettes and never came back.You know how sometimes you're with the lads, then you tell them you're off to bed but you're actually playing that single-player game you're addicted to? This is that game.I stopped playing Sex with Hitler to play this.Like my wife’s boyfriend says, it’s not about the boat size, it's about the motion in the ocean!I loved Dredge SO MUCH! Beat it the first time and then immediately started a second game to look back on what I missed. I'm kind of a fan of fishing games already and a lover of Lovecraftian/eldritch horror inspired media so this was right up my alley. It’s not terribly scary but there is a great Lovecraftian mystery to uncover with some spooks here and there. It’s got a familiar gameplay loop: grind in order to upgrade your equipment so that you can grind more efficiently, so that you can improve your equipment even more so that… you get the point. This tried and true formula is executed perfectly in Dredge. The hook here is that the grind consists of fishing, to upgrade your boat. The catch is that things are not quite as they seem, especially at night. This game lures you in with it’s lore and simple mechanics, and before you know it, it has sunk it’s hooks into you. After capsizing and waking up on a tiny island, you start your adventure with a tin can of a tug boat that can barely make it across the bay. Your first fishing rod barely has the ability to catch fish in shallow water, but nearby oceanic fishing spots get you excited to start upgrading your gear. The fish that you catch have to fit in your initially limited cargo space and you have to make them fit in a grid reminiscent of the inventory system for Resident Evil 4 where you might have to move things around in a tetris like fashion. You quickly realize something isn’t right as you start catching corrupted and aberrant fish. Your friendly neighborhood fishmonger finds an item inside one of these fish which piques the interest of a local collector. This collector is the main driver of the story. He asks you to retrieve an item for each of the four islands on the map. He also gives you the ability to “dredge” up materials from the ocean floor that can be used to upgrade your ship. These ship upgrades are cleverly gated by a rare item that can be found at each of the islands so that your upgrades mostly mirror your progress in the game, but a gung ho explorer could speed up the process by buying these items instead.One of the standout features of this game is the exploration. There are four main islands outside your intro island and each is a treat to unravel. Each is thematically distinct from the last with minor puzzles that build upon the powers gained in the previous island. Throughout all of this, you are constantly trying to avoid the night, and the madness that comes along with it. Ghost ships, various eldritch monsters, and freaky natural phenomena all make the night a dangerous time for fishing. Amazing to have a game that feels so chill during day time but at night I can feel myself panicking to get back home! I had a great time exploring all the areas and uncovering secrets, there's this ever present sense of uneasiness that permeates the waters that you traverse, you can really feel the amount of love that was put into crafting the world and atmosphere in the game. I think it very beautifully captured the vastness of the ocean and that sinking feeling of coming up onto something and just having this nagging voice in the back of your mind saying "I shouldn't be here".My favorite part of this game is it brings back what most of these games either forget to add, or forget to keep. The game reeks of DREAD. It’s got this constant eerie feeling accompanying you, like the “stranger entering a little village” and the feeling that the locals are hiding something from you. Picture yourself encountering a man, who asks you to carry parcel to a nearby island. He warns that he is stalked by a great sea monster, whose mouth waits open beneath his vessel, and that's why he won't leave the small island he's moored at. You take the parcel, and fit it into your cargo. And sail towards the destination, over dark, deep water. Maybe it'll get you, maybe he's crazy. But you can't help but steer towards shallows and take the long way... You've been attacked by great tentacles on the sea before. And you know this game is willing to go there. That dread is there all the time. It's so well done. You just have to let yourself get into it. Listen to the waves, reel in the fish, and listen to the water as you reel. Time passes in that menu, and things WILL creep up on your boat. Dredge does a great job of keeping you tense like that. Even when you get into the grind of fishing. You get that "Everything is fine, I'll just hit two more spots and... well that was a new noise... time to head back. Yup let's get the heck out of here." I absolutely loved it, as well as the profound sense of discomfort it seems very able to give me consistently!Both endings are great and satisfying endings that tied a neat bow around the main story. That said, it does leave you wanting more, and would have benefited from being explored a little more. Despite some minor annoying design choices, and relying on a formula we’ve seen in countless other games, this is an addictive romp on the open sea, and the lovecraftian horror elements peppered in throughout help to spice things up and give this game its own identity. In the daytime when you're fishing and dredging it'll be a mostly zen experience, but going out and driving around in the darkness will have you sh*t your pants at times. It will be a short but lovely horror game, a unique and refreshing experience to play. I highly recommend it.10/10
_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.review: The concept of DREDGE is really good; a fishing game with elements of Lovecraftian horror. However, after playing through the main story and completing all pursuits, I can conclude that it unfortunately doesn't lean nearly enough into the Lovecraftian side of things. The way Lovecraftian horror manifests itself in this game most of the time is with aberrations, horrible mutated fish that you can catch. The shock of these aberrations wears off quickly. The first time you catch one you're like, "Oh my god, what the hell is that?" but by the time you get even a quarter into the story, your reaction changes to "Oh, another one. Time to sell it for a slightly higher price than a normal fish." To the game's credit, the aberrations are pretty creepy and well-designed, but unfortunately that creepiness factor only affects the fish's appearance and doesn't have an impact on gameplay in any significant way. The other way this game leans into Lovecraftian horror is with the Panic mechanic. Panic grows when you are out on the water at night for an extended period of time, especially if you haven't slept the previous night. It rises faster if you are attacked by any of the various enemies roaming around the map, which range from giant piranhas to demon stingrays to enormous sea serpents. Like with the aberrations, the wow factor wears off pretty quickly, and most of them are pretty easy to avoid, especially with an upgraded boat.Another bone to pick I have with this game is the story, which is perfectly serviceable, if inconsequential, right up until the end. I'm not going to spoil it here, but it ends very abruptly without any follow-up. The game also warns you when you reach the point of no return, which is completely pointless because the final mission takes less than five minutes, and after the credits roll it returns you to right before the mission.I've talked a lot about the Lovecraftian part of this game, but I haven't really talked about the fishing at all. You know, the main thing you do in DREDGE. I don't have a lot to say about it. The fishing mechanic is good, and the grid-based inventory system makes it so you have to lay out your haul in a creative way to fit all the fish on your boat. I haven't played any other fishing games though, so I don't have anything to compare it to.All this complaining in my review must make it sound like I hate DREDGE. I don't. It's a fine fishing game, if a middling Lovecraftian horror game. The concept of this game drew me in hook, line, and sinker, but the light Lovecraftian horror elements left me wanting more. As someone who's interested in Lovecraftian horror, I really wish this game had more for me. I'll still recommend it because the Lovecraftian horror elements aren't outright bad, just lightly sprinkled in. In DREDGE, Lovecraftian horror is the seasoning on top, when it should have been the main dish itself. Overall, DREDGE is a really good concept for a game held back by the developer's unwillingness to do any more than dip a toe in Lovecraftian horror, instead choosing to focus on the fishing aspect.
