_childDocuments_.review: Summary:A unique kind of fishing game: cosy and smoothing during the daytime, cosmic horror and stressful at night. It takes around 10 hours to complete the main quests, and double the amount to 100%. Despite enjoying this game myself, I only recommend it cautiously due to its multiple downsides. If you are not daunted by the price, the Complete Edition offers the best experience.Goodies:+ Well-polished and arguably feature-complete after more than one year's updates and two major DLCs.+ The different mechanics are all easy to pick up.+ Top-notch art and sound design and soundtrack.+ Amazing Lovecraftian atmosphere.+ Passive mode and other accessibility options.+ An captivating open world divided into 7 beautiful regions, each with a vastly distinct environment and types of fish (more than 200 kinds in the game!).+ Gratifying to go through 5 tiers of one's boat and to get faster, larger, and more versatile as one goes along.+ Very satisfying boat driving and water physics.Downsides:- Not much evolution in terms of gameplay or plots; you basically repeat the same kind of mini-games / fetch quests / farming throughout the whole game.- The upgrades of equipment are fairly incremental and utterly underwhelming. Furthermore, the items at the end of the tech tree are not necessarily the optimal ones, which takes away the pleasure of researching all upgrades.- Each tier of the ship has a fixed layout which indicates where you can install each of the four types of equipment (fishing rod, trawl net, light, and engine) and how many slots you have for each type of equipment. In other words, it is not really up to you to make the compromise between having more equipment installed (which makes you ship more powerful since stats from different equipment stack) and more cargo space.- For a game with so many collectibles, there is no in-game tracking system; one has to rely on online guides or maps.- Extremely fragmentary lore.- Flat NPC design: insipid character arcs which rarely intertwine (NPCs rarely have reactions to the events outside their quests).- Only possible to fast travel to the centre of the map. Even with the full-upgraded ship, it is a slog to travel between regions again and again, especially at night when visibility is highly reduced.- No manual save.- In the late game, you will have tons of money but almost nothing to buy. This is exacerbated in the second DLC, where craftable equipment requires raw materials that you cannot buy directly (only obtainable via dredging or farming).- - - Particularly highly priced, especially the two DLCs with a debatably small amount of content and boring story; the complete edition costs twice as much as most indie games.More details follow; you are also highly encouraged to visit , which has a dozen of one-minute-long videos showcasing various mechanics (e.g. fishing, inventory, time management) and main in-game regions.Gameplay structure:* A playthrough consists of finishing a set of main quests, which guide you to each main area of the open world. The quests (both main and side ones) are mostly independent and can be fulfilled out of order. They are mainly fetch quests: fetch/deliver me these fish or those objects from/to point X.* Fishing (by rod) and dredging are mainly based on several kinds of QTE mini-games; the principle is more or less the same: push the button when the moving dots are in the indicated zone to accelerate fishing.* Throughout the game, you drive a fish boat. Fish, material, trinkets, equipment, etc, all have a fixed form and occupy a certain number of slots; you need to fit them into the storage of your boat like playing Tetris.* Money and material earned from quests or selling fish are necessary for upgrading your boat (more space to hold more goods or larger equipment, better equipment for more types of fish, higher cruising speed, etc).* Fishing/dredging + selling + upgrading form the main gameplay loop.More about the fishing elements:* There is a day-night cycle; time advances when fishing, driving, or installing equipment. Some fish only spawn during the night.* There are also passive ways of fishing by using trawl nets and crab pots.* Fishing spots appear as bubbling water; each spot contains one kind of fish, which can be guessed from the silhouettes under the bubble. The spyglass allows determining the kind of fish in a bubble from far away, saving you the trouble of approaching.* The number of available fish in a spot is limited; once depleted, it takes some time for the spot to respawn.* The position of all the spots for each kind of fish is mostly fixed; you can consult an  to learn where to find the fish you are searching for.The particularities lie in its Lovecraftian horror setting, which manifests through more than the story arcs:* By design, your character is highly discouraged from staying out during the night because they have a sanity metre (called “panic” in the game). When the panic is high, you will see and experience all sorts of strange things: chromatic aberrations, optic illusions, fish infection, and most horribly, sea monsters, which will pursue and attack you. (Luckily, sea monster attack can be turned off in the passive mode.)* Each kind of fish has one of two eldritch variants (called “aberrations” in the game); these variants appear with a small probability each time you fish.

_childDocuments_.review: oddly relaxing and disturbing fishing gameif you enjoy stuff like Sunless Sea and Sunless Sky, where a large portion of the gameplay is you doing your mundane job while also uncovering the horror filled veil of the world around you and constantly getting bodied by something beyond your playable character's fragile mind can handlethen this one is highly recommended, especially if you have Steam deck, you can pop this game whenever you need to unwind without committing too much of your timepros:- the game is easy to pick up and get into- the core gameplay loop is relaxing - neat visual and art direction that fit the theme quite well for a simple low poly aesthetic with hand drawn NPC and fish illustration- decent fishing mini-game- fair amount of fish species to caught and collect for our guide book, each with their own unique biome and "odd" sub species- done the 'horror of the unknown' theme experience quite well, 3 hour of gameplay and i'm still stumbling upon new encounter quite oftencons:- the game is too easy with no real difficulty tweak- there are no real urgency for player to constantly fishing, the game doesn't demand you to aim for profit other than to buy upgrade, so you can easily bypass the need to fish most of the time and just scavenge for upgrade parts, and just fish when you need the money for said upgrade.- there are little to no meaningful punishment nor penalty for player decision, you don't need to manage your fuel or supplies when you go for a long fishing trip/run so you can easily fish for up to 3 days before the fish you caught start rotting, in game such as Sunless Sea/sky, you are demanded to plan your route and schedule before going for a run because the game need you to manage not only your storage for goods you meant to sell, but also the space for fuel and supplies for your journey, this mean player can decide whether they want to fill up their storage space for more goods and in turn more profit but with more potentially dangerous run because their low fuel and supply mean they could easily stranded if they choose a wrong route or if something unexpected happens, or they could fill the storage with more fuel and supplies for safer journey but low on profit. stuff like these can really add more complex player decision regarding how they want to tackle their mission and playstyle- similarly, in regard to our sanity when out in the world at night, there is no real danger or urgency to pay much attention to our sanity level, because player can just look at the already established map and search for nearest harbor/dock to sleep, and player don't even need to sleep that long to completely reset the sanity drain either, so player can easily just hop in for 3 hours and continue the night just fine. they could do so much more with the sanity drain and make it harder for player to recover right away, in that this could also effect how player proceed into the game and their decision making- i also just kinda wish the world map is tad bit bigger with more landmark or point of interest to explore and interact with (similar to Sunless Sky), maybe a future dlc could add some more areas

_childDocuments_.review: Dredge — 5.0This has its charm, particularly early on when the mystery is enticing and you feel the threat of madness from everything around you. I loved the first time I called over a ship only to be attacked by a spirit, or the unavoidable damage from certain projections. But eventually, you realize it’s all kind of the same, and the loop doesn’t evolve with enough of a challenge to do anything interesting. It’s fun, don’t get me wrong, but I would have loved for the gameplay to get increasingly complex — and for the madness mechanic to leave actual impact on my character. By the fourth island I literally stopped sleeping, because through books and boat speed I just wasn’t going mad anymore… with no repercussions. Odd. Enjoyed it, but felt it could be better, particularly when it comes to tying together themes with gameplay. More NPCs, more hallucinations, and more horror!

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, first things first, this is a really good game. Relaxing, chill, no stress, and a fun game loop. Honestly, it was on my Wishlist and I slept on it, and let it pass me by. After a years time and waiting, playing some more stressful type games, I was like, I need a break so here I am. The game is simple in nature. Its for me, more of a metrovania-lite style game. Its not as prescribed as a Metrovania because more or less nothing is sectioned off necessarily, but you cant catch or do certain things until later on in the game when you have money to buy things. Which of course comes from catching. There is a fun little upgrade system, nothing super crazy, just simple and nice. There are a few little biomes in the game which present their own little puzzles. Also tons of fish and alternate versions of them, with their own cycles (day or night) or require a special kind of gear to get. There is a story here, that I grazed. The art style was cool but I was in it for the gameplay. The world is large enough, it really suited the game well. Too big would have been a time waste and not worth it. The gameplay is boiled down to, catch fish, sell fish, upgrade boat, go get more fish. Generally the game is split up in, go fetch fish or do certain things with fish to keep you going. Its simple and rewarding. I personally would like to see a town building aspect in the next game. This was a great intro game but if there is a Dredge 2, lets build a town! For this game, a release all fish back to the sea would have been great rather than having to toss each one individually would have been welcome as well. There are a few dynamic events in the sea but they are kind of the same thing so having added a few more would have been nice, especially since the sound, the weather and everything just comes together so well. Seeing those gigantic monsters coming from the sea was epic. I think overall the game is great. Upgrading your boat, repairing your boat, the various biomes are just a really great treat, especially in this day of gaming. I think the addition of a few powers as you move along the game was a nice touch. Im glad the game stayed simple despite a few requests above. It could have been filled with fighting or racing but it was just a fishermen's story. After 100% in the game, I can say there is very little to dislike in the game.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not what you'd call challenging, but it does have a nice combination of fun, simple and relaxing gameplay with some Lovecraftian inspired spookiness. I say spookiness and not horror. This isn't Call of Cthulhu, but more like a cheerful Tim Burton animated movie. The fun part is simply having the freedom to go about and explore the world, discovering what lurks just beneath, while avoiding scary denizens of the deep. While your boat starts of kind of sluggish, making your vulnerable to the scary stuff that descends with the night, you can upgrade reasonably quickly to the point that the game actually becomes genuinely hard to put down.Haven't had any moments of frustration from it. It also runs like an absolute charm and I haven't encountered any bugs or glitches, which is always nice.At around 14 hours in I have my boat maxed out to its top tier and I still have one more region to fully explore, so it's probably not going to be the longest gaming experience - I'm guessing somewhere around 20 hours till completion time. That's about the same as The Last of Us pt. 1, except this runs a hell of a lot smoother.If nautically themed Burtonesque Lovecraftian lore (that won't drive you insane) floats your boat, then this is definitely worth wasting some hours on.

_childDocuments_.review: Before getting really into this I'd like to say that I had refused to watch any real gameplay for Dredge. I watched the trailer, and knew I would play this game, but wanted to be surprised by the game mechanics. That being said this game was pretty much on par for what I was looking for.DREDGE is overall a great game. The storyline follows the chemistry of most Eldritch Horror, there's an unknown, you should explore that unknown, and when the curtains close you feel like you have about the same amount of new questions to answers you've received. To be honest, the past year I've been dying to play a fishing game; not to say that this is a traditional fishing game though it scratched the itch. Mechanically the game runs well, even when driving your boat through a tight corner you can get the drift that would happen. Many times that was the downfall of escaping an unimaginable horror in the foggy nighttime air. I did have some issues; at points the game felt empty, as much as I like inventory management the engine placement didn't fill the bottom of the boat (my ocd trigger), in some places if your camera is too close to the land it pushes it in a weird direction (making driving into a rock or wall highly possible. this happened at the blackstone a few times).Lets talk about Dredging, since its the namesake. I very much enjoyed the minigame/majority of the game. Having master a pattern or just ingeneral learning it for the first time, It's truly wonderful. Though I assumed it would be more like parking and casting a rod or net, its fluid, and a great surprise. At this 15 hours of play time, I've completed the game with almost all achievements. I do personally think that the research parts are a pain to find or just buying them takes to long. But the achievements are all doable and realistically, its fair enough. I enjoyed spending the time to do a majority of them. And probably will 100% the game in the near future. For a game that was $25 on release, I'm pretty happy with it. I will say its closer to $20, I even spent $5 on dlc because I had assumed it was a side mission included. But alas, all I did was speed myself up toward the end. This game could have a road map planned, I'm not entirely sure. But, here are some thoughts. 1. New Game Plus (with a timer for speed runners)2. Free play mode (for people that want to enjoy the game without a sanity meter)3. Most side quests/missions (I had assumed there would be more transporting of people, more building and finding resources to upgrade the town, or other locations)4. One last overall hull upgrade (as increasing lights or having the room for more poles/nets would be sweet)5. Personally wondering why sections weren't closer to twisted strand (in regards to making the area safer, thus making the section easier to access. clearing part of the fog, getting rid of a majority if the lava fish, etc.)This game is a 8/10, will last you hours of exploration, and very much think it has extreme potential to be bigger and better!

_childDocuments_.review: Pros -  Awesome Visuals - Check, Amazing sound track - Check, Fishing - Check, Well thought out boat upgrades - Check, Amazing story - Check, Freaky Fish - Check, Always feeling like something is going to come out of the water and eat you whole - Double CheckCons -  I need more of this! In all seriousness I seriously love this game. When I first found it I was kind of hesitant but after a bit I decided to get it the day it came out (two days ago as of writing this) and I was not expecting to enjoy it as much as I have. I love the art style and the mystery surrounding the area. I rarely do side quests at all unless they are interesting. I went out of my way to find them as I didn't want the game to end. I finished my first play through in a little under 12 hours with the boat fully upgraded and every side quest done. Right after I finished I started over again. Though yes I could have just restarted from the last save to see the next ending I wanted to actually play through the whole thing again. There is only 1 other game I have ever done this with. _childDocuments_.review: Take hold of your own fishing ship, manage the catch, upgrade your boat and reveal interesting story through various missions.With minimal resources the game presents a fun and rewarding gameplay loop that is supported by slowly unwinding story that pushes you to go out "for just one more day"The day/night cycle is quite short, but it's by design - time is one of the resources you have to manage. And at the same time the game is mostly very relaxing - you can take your time, exploring at your own pace. Want to fish in the starting bay for a month? Sure go for it. Want to go out in the vast sea on your first day? Be my guest (only face the consequences)An easy recommendation to anyone who might consider this kind of game.

_childDocuments_.review: Dredge is a fun fishing game. You are a fisherman with a boat and you catch fish. You do this during the day because it becomes spooky spooky at night.The main gameplay loop is to drive your boat around, catch fish via the handful of fishing mini-games, look for trinkets and boat building material, sell the fish for money and upgrade your boat to catch bigger and more different fish. This sounds simple but it is super addicting.There is a simple storyline behind what you're doing and what is happening in the world but in order to truly understand the "why", you need to find and read bottled messages scattered throughout the world.10/10 fun game. Took me about ~10 hours to beat the game with a fully upgraded boat and most of the bottled messages.

_childDocuments_.review: Who knew an eldritch horror fishing game could be such a relaxing cozy adventure game. Dredge first captured me with its uniquely stylized art style, reeled me in with its amazingly haunted setting and kept me with its relaxing mechanics. By the time I was comfortable with the gameplay I was in a catch-em-all mindset with every abberated fish in the game. The story is straightforward but it awards you well when you've explored every single nook and cranny island/rock in the game.  Dredge renewed my interest in Eldritch/Lovecraftian stories that I even got into some horror audiodramas and even got the Lovecraft manga. The game is great for those who are busy or find themselves multitasking, I had to leave the game open for a while once, leaving my little boat floating in open waters yet the game didn't punish me for it, I didn't lose a single catch. Highly anticipating the next DLC as a day one purchase. I need more Dredge!

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10Carried by an extremely satisfying central gameplay loop, Dredge creates an intriguing world to explore and backs up its mechanics with strong visual design, especially environments and the monsters, and very good audio design and music. Definitely nails the Lovecraft/King vibes. I was probably more absorbed in upgrading my fishing boat than I was in the story, and I don't think it quite sticks the landing, but that's true of a lot of horror games for me. By the end I wasn't motivated enough to finish all the sidequests and fill out the encyclopedia after ~10 hours, so if you're not a completionist you might find it a bit thin on content for the price. But I really enjoyed my time with Dredge, and definitely recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.review: Peaceful fishing game with a heaping side of Lovecraft horror, Dredge does a great job combining peaceful and stressful elements into a single game without losing one or the other.The game itself isn't particularly long but feels fine for the amount of time you put into it. The fishing mechanic is simple so you won't be struggling to catch anything too badly, it also changes slightly depending on what fish you are going after for a bit of variety. The upgrading system is smooth and upgrading your ships hull changes the appearance of the ship which I really like and makes the upgrade system feel more impactful.The 3D environment looks great, combined with the day night cycle does so much for the games atmosphere, the ocean is a whole different place at night. The characters and fish on the other hand are instead stylized 2D sprites that look even better, the fish in particular each have a rarer corrupted "aberration" form each with a unique sprite. Each of the zones in the game have a unique look, mechanics, and story to them, Stellar Basin in particular is amazing.Overall Dredge is a great game with a great story and a fair price with an ambiance and atmosphere second to none. Don't forget just because you don't see anything on the open ocean doesn't mean something doesn't see you, try going out of bounds.
_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.review: Delightful and occasionally chilling.  I greatly enjoy setting sail and catching fish; my only complaint is that my "fishing simulation" experience is cut short each day, as the in-game time before sundown seems short.  But whoever thought up all the aberrant fish had a deliciously terrifying imagination.
_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.review: Well after 100%ing the game i still have an itch for more. I suffer heavily from burn out in games but after doing two playthroughs to ensure i totally understood the story and to go back to get everything i missed its safe to say i have a new favourite indie game. Theres easily 14-18 hours of game play to 100% this if thats your goal. To just enjoy it like myself 20+. Buy this game you wont be disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.review: Meticulously crafted, Lovecraft inspired ambience and universe that's honestly a delight to exploreSurprisingly calming and yet, unnerving day/night fishing gameplay loop that is extremely tight and really satisfying.All in all, Dredge is a very polished indie title full of heart, over-delivering on its asking price.
_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.review: I would not recommend it at the full $24.99 price-point.If you are looking for a casual game with an intuitive fishing mechanic, go for it. Just a warning, there's not much of a pull to replay the game once you've completed it once.I enjoyed playing the game up until a point. I felt like midway, I was simply playing for completion, too late to request a refund. I felt that there was no consequence for much of my playtime. I did not need the in-game currency or any of the upgrade items. The timed quest had no impact for me, the day and night cycles were inconsequential and I did not really see a reason why the number of days were tracked in the UI.The concept and the theme is neat, but I would recommend that there would be more of a focus on catching fish, better upgrade paths, a sense of urgency for the quests to be completed, or have the ability to interact with more of the world in order to feel more immersed in the horror and lovecraftian theme.
_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.review: 5 out of 10Start to finish it's about 10 hours. I had a few times where I needed to step away for a bit. The story isn't really all there, it's more of a discovery of a story by you rather than you being apart of the narrative. The entire game is just one big fetch quest. Go to "x," collect "y," bring back to "z." Once you've upgraded your boat the entire core game loop becomes irrelevant outside of needs for repairs.The game also suffers from the typical power creep mismanagement. You get these powers:1) teleport back to the creepy mansion by the starter area2) scare away small baddies3) instantly harvest a fishing nodeYou get power #3 right at the end of the game...why even have this ability when the game is over by the time you get it? This makes no sense. Same thing with abyssal fishing. You only need it for the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ quest for the researcher at the end of Stellar Basin and 1 fish in Devils Spine. Otherwise it's totally useless. Really, though, it's a big slap in the face for your time with Atrophy because you don't even need to get abyssal fishing, you just need Atrophy. You get them basically at the exact same time. This is bad design.Trawl nets are also largely a wasted mechanic as you only need them for 1 spot which is the researcher fetch quests at the Stellar Basin. The rate of accrual for the fish you collect is so slow that even with a maxed out net it's actually faster to just manually fish than to have this passive mechanic. Despite the game being named "Dredge" that's only a small portion of the game play. I know, I know...it has to do with the theme, it's a play on words, blah blah blah. This game could have been infinitely more terrifying if it was a copper hat diving suit FPS dredging and spear fishing game (free idea for someone, just give me a name drop in the credits). Don't need to be an actual shooter just diving down into the water with a limited oxygen supply a simple spear gun, some hooks, nets, and similar things with a goal of hunting sunken relics in ever increasingly creepy locales. I'm only giving this a thumbs down because there's no middle ground option. I can't justify the price tag to the playtime and constant fetching, plus driving a boat around in a dreary setting isn't all that engaging. If you're going to get this game, get it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: DREDGE

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed the game, especially the story. That's what kept me coming back.  The fishing gameplay loop was fun,  but it reached a point where I only fished if I had to for a quest or materials.The one down side for me was that the story was so nicely wrapped up, that I'm not feeling the need to get the expansion.It took about 15 hours to complete the base game (with three deaths all traceable directly to stupid mistakes I made).

_childDocuments_.review:
Dredge is a fishing adventure with a sinister undercurrent. Sell your catch, upgrade your vessel and dredge the depths for long-buried relics. Explore the stories of the strange locals and discover why some things are best left forgotten. 

Starting from your new home in a group of islands known as The Marrows, upgrade your engines and set sail for the neighboring regions - each with their own unique fish, personalities and secrets.
Dredge up forgotten treasures. Outsmart unremembered terrors.

Someone wants very badly to retrieve relics lost to the ocean floor. The work is lucrative, but can you trust them? What will they use the relics for? And will they ever be satisfied?

It's not just the sharp rocks and shallow reefs you need to watch out for - keep your eyes on the depths below and the sky above. The biggest threat to your safety might come from within.

name: SANABI
detailed_description: You, a legendary retired veteran, are called upon for one last operation: to ascend a mega-city ruled by a corrupt conglomerate. You were chosen for this mission because of your signature chain-hook prosthetic arm and the ability to maneuver and quickly defeat enemies. The mission: to hunt down a mysterious entity known as “SANABI” and uncover corporate secrets hidden deep within the city. An exhilarating platformer Your giant chain-hook prosthetic arm acts as both a method for quickly maneuvering around and also a way to swiftly take out your opponents. With your legendary skills, you are capable of using your prosthetic arm to jump over cliffs and skyscrapers, dash through bullets and traps and defeat powerful enemies. It's time for you to come back out of retirement for one last mission. A beautiful yet mysterious cyberpunk dystopia Mega-city “MAGO” is a high-tech city ruled by a corrupt conglomerate… at least, that’s what it was 24 hours ago. After a sudden blackout, all of its citizens mysteriously disappeared and the city was left in total chaos. It’s your mission to explore the depths of the city and uncover what happened. Mari, the hacker prodigy A brilliant hacker and drone rider you meet during your mission. Mari can open locked doors, reveal enemy weaknesses and uncover encrypted information. Mari is lovely and reliable, but maybe just a little too chatty. Who knows though, this girl might be the key to finding SANABI.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is good, and it's easy to recommend for the price, but it does have an off-putting issue.The story, the artstyle, the game mechanics, the world-building, and the soundtrack are all top notch. It does however get really tedious at times. It's clearly heavily inspired by Katana Zero, but where Katana Zero effortlessly succeeds in integrating an intriguing plotline with its fast-paced gameplay. This one fails; miserably at times. It felt like the cutscenes and gameplay were constantly interrupting each other, the second you get into the gameplay and are being thrown challenging enemies, you're interrupted by a cutscene twice as long, and when the story gets interesting, you're interrupted with the gameplay. At some point it was hard to enjoy the game cause there was this constant anticipation that the gameplay would come to a grinding halt with a dense cutscene.I played the speedrun after completing the campaign, and playing it felt leagues better than story mode, the gameplay felt more connected and fluid.The story is definitely worth experiencing but I don't think it warrants the awful gameplay to cutscene ratio. A lot of it could have been condensed, some of it could have been shown in collectables or records people who are interested could go out of their way to find, having cutscenes between longer sequences of gameplay, etc.It's good but it would've felt so much better had it put its fast-paced gameplay front and centre, and it seems they could've easily done that.
_childDocuments_.name: SANABI

_childDocuments_.review: Genuinely one of my favorite games of all time. The story really beats out any thoughts I have about the gameplay other than it being a fine platformer, but that isn't why you should play the game. A compelling and touching story that does some good work within the cyberpunk genre. I could not wait to replay it and within a week of playing it the first time I went back and played through it again.Weird translation stuff but only shows up a handful of time.I could not see how this game could be played on anything other than a mouse and keyboard since most of the platforming involves a lot of freehand aiming.
_childDocuments_.name: SANABI

_childDocuments_.review: ...Its main and its ONLY gimmick, which isn't a bad thing. The grappling hook is satisfying and mostly mechanically sound. The game will mostly push it to the limit with what they can throw at you considering it only revolves around one mechanic. Now... I say mostly because I don't think the game reaches that "last stage" feel for the final act of the game, instead you go through its entirety again but just a small ramp up in difficulty where it should have had an entirely new area. Kind of a cop-out.Some of the bosses were also a bit of a let down, almost all of them pale in comparison to the final boss.Those, however are but minor complaints because the game IS fun and will keep you invested in the story... mostly.The story is good, it starts out very strong and for the first act of the game comes off as, while cliche, a relatable revenge story that is serviceable, especially for this type of game but, of course, it comes with a plot twist.I don't have a problem with the twist per say, I just think it could have been done with more tact, the pacing is just off. The game drip feeds you information and then in the final act just expo dumps on you to the point where I almost didn't care anymore. You've got 10 minute long cutscenes with almost nothing happening for the entire game and then 30+ minutes of exposition in the end with so much technobabble I was tuning out. That's not to say the story is bad but when it is the focus like this and heavily praised in the reviews I expected something better. If you ignore that though, it's a very interesting story. The soundtrack of the game is also worthy of note. It helped elevate a lot of the encounters and comes with a couple of certifiable bangers I actually listen to in my off time. Overall, a great game with a couple of issues. It doesn't quite reach the peak of, say, Katana Zero but it stands on its own right just fine.My full playthrough of the game .

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: The art and animation alone are worth the price of admission in my opinion, but on top of those you get a fun action platformer alongside a well written story that has a few interesting of twists and turns.The platforming focuses on using a grappling hook with new abilities introduced at regular enough intervals to keep things from getting stale. Likewise, levels alternate between platforming and combat to keep things varied enough that nothing ever gets boring or same-y. As someone who rarely plays platformers, there were a few sections I struggled with but I was ultimately able to overcome. If you're someone who struggles with platformers but wants to give the game a try anyway, the Easy mode removes HP loss so you can experience it at your own pace. You'll still get to enjoy the feeling of completing platform heavy levels but won't have to worry about repeatedly hitting a game over screen or getting stuck in one of the combat sections. However, if you're someone who likes your platformers to have some extra bite, there's a difficulty that reduces you to a single HP. One mistake and you're done.The story may not be anything groundbreaking but it's executed so competently and paced so well that it really is an unexpected selling point of this game for me. The two main characters get some really well done character growth throughout the 8 to 10 hour experience and the side characters get enough screen time to be interesting but not so much that they feel overly used. The story knows when and how to pull at your heartstrings and the twists and turn of the narrative were just so very fun to see unfold.I cannot overstate how great the animation of this game is. Despite it's pixel graphic style, the characters are so expressive and able to use body language in a way I genuinely wasn't prepared for. On top of that, the animation pairs up very well with the controls and feedback to make your movement in the game feel fantastic.

_childDocuments_.review: I have to give this a very reluctant thumbs up.  This is a very good game, but it is certainly not a game that deserves an "Overwhelmingly Positive" tag.  Here's why:(1) The best part of this game is the story; there is little doubt about that. Though the story is very good, it is absolutely not original, as it is basically an exact copy of a couple very specific movies. Still, the story is worth getting through. I suggest you don't read anything about it and just go through it without any spoilers of any type, even the trailers.(2) The problem with this "game" is that there is too much emphasis on the story.  You will spend significantly more time watching cut scenes and reading dialogue than actually playing.  That sounds like an exaggeration, but it is 100% true. There is LESS TIME SPENT ON GAMEPLAY THAN ON CUT SCENES. (3) The game took some obvious inspiration from Bionic Commando.  Swinging around is fun, but that is basically all you do.  There is little combat here and it is as simplistic as you can possibly get while still calling this a game. (4) It way too easy. The challenge of the game is figuring out and becoming adept with the controls.  Once you do that, you fly through the game with ease. Some of the reviews compare this to Katana Zero, even saying that it is better than Katana Zero.  I don't think this game is playing in the same league as Katana Zero.  Katana Zero is a far superior game. This could have been a legitimate classic if there was more time spent on gameplay and less on cut scenes. This game is a B.  I am not suggesting that you should not play it, as it has its fun parts, but this is really more a movie than a video game.
_childDocuments_.name: SANABI

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. Writing is excellent, sounds, visuals etc are used in a sophisticated way to tell an interesting story. The plot twists aren't completely unexpected, but it's still nicely done.The environments and gameplay can at some points feel a little repetitive, but the story is the main purpose of this game, and it manages to carry you through.Great, emotional journey!
_childDocuments_.name: SANABI

_childDocuments_.review: The Overwhelmingly Positive rating is well deserved. Originally, I was getting the impression this was a mid platformer with some nice graphics, but the game manages to stay fresh with each new area introducing one or two new mechanics which are combined well with previous ones. I would say you can tell by the 2nd area or so if this game is for you. I won't focus much on the positives here are my negatives:- The early story is sloooow. Not a slog, just slow, with more than a couple walking segments. I can see this would put off a lot of people from otherwise fast paced game unfortunately, but it only happens near the beginning.- The mystery of the story takes a while to start resolving, but by the time it does start, you kind of already know what the answers are going to be. Not to say it's unoriginal, but the themes have been tread before. That being said, I really like how this game's story plays out. I was interested all the way through to figure out what is going on. Some minor things are confusing at the end, and I spotted more than 1 plot hole, but it's nothing major.- There is a gauntlet at the end. The game has frequent saves so it's not a gameplay problem, but you're running through areas you've already been to, which is always annoying to me. Thankfully it is a lot faster this time around. That reminds me,- Levels are quite long some times. I finished in 9.8 hrs, and I played in one day in one sitting (because I really wanted to see how story pans out) so probably closer to 7 hours. On one hand, there is a lot of gameplay here, but at the same time a lot of that gameplay is the same mechanic throughout a level. It's not that the character is slow or anything either, the levels just start to drag at some point, especially Chapter 3 levels.- The boss near the end is annoyingly hard. I don't even know if I want to come back and do Legendary because of how annoying that boss was to fight.Overall, I will say the mystery and theme carries this game more than the gameplay. The gameplay is nice but I can easily see how it can feel padded or samey and boring. Unlike Katana Zero, if the game starts easy for you, it ends feeling just as easy. But if this isn't a deal breaker for you, it's a good game. Just a really well put together game with a really good story.
_childDocuments_.name: SANABI

_childDocuments_.review: such story, such gameplay,Story beats are unpredictable at times and really executed well with theme and direction they were going. They were fresh, mysterious and intriguing. It reminded me a lot about why i love Katana Zero so much (aside from its soundtrack)Gameplay exceeded my expectations, was expecting a grappling hook game with the simplicity of the flash game "Spider-Man vs Batman" LOL. But just with the use of 2-3 mechanics related to it, the grappling mechanic can be a hard to master yet rewarding mechanic to learn. It stands on its own feet even when you're just traversing from one place to another, now couple that with level design, platformer elements and enemies you need to face and you get a really fast paced platformer with badass gamplay that i have never seen in other games. Sure you could "swing around" and "beat enemies" like that in games like Spiderman but it never calls for swings with such speed and precision. Plus, Spiderman is arguably a slower paced game since stealth (which means crawling around enemies then do some thinking and planning) , albeit small is part of the game, while this game has no such thing.wow i typed too much and ended up with a real review.

_childDocuments_.review: Wheeeee...STORYYYYYYY...whee...STORYYYYY...wheeee...STORYYYYYYYYYYYYYY. This describes the gameplay loop and why I was ANNOYED for the first two-thirds of the game. Then, in the last third of the game, the story balls started landing one after the other. Plus, the gameplay went from slick-but-unchallenging to just plain slick. It never got quite as hard as I wanted, but I also ended the game in awe and tears. So I might return and clean-up the last three achievements. If you go in, expect the first two thirds of the game to be underwhelming, but to have the best time in the last act.Narratively, Sanabi went from feeling super wrote to having one of the best bait-and-switch landings that I've found in memory. I still think the script could be pared-down by 25%, but then I don't know that I'd edit much at all from the deeply affecting conclusion.

One is the sort of whiplash you get with constant switching back and forth from gameplay and cutscenes. When you are having a lot of fun playing, the game stops you and has you experience a cutscene. When you are excited by story progression, a new mystery is brought up, and becomes a cliffhanger that is interrupted by gameplay.They don't want to info dump on you, but they kind of mess up the pace. A bunch of conversations investigate one idea and then for one reason or another, they have to drop the conversation and start running again. It takes time for the story to get good because the main character is deadpan rude and does not allow conversations to progress very far. There is a purpose for it in the story, but I can see how it would get on someone's nerves. Once the story begins dropping answers on you, it explodes into something amazing, and you wish you could just watch it like a movie. Shortly after, gameplay calls, and you will feel motivated to perform well and go wild only to still be stopped to interject small dialogue.Despite this, time is minimally wasted and it didn't hinder my enjoyment of the game. I highly recommend it,

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Great story with solid platforming mechanics akin to Celeste and Ori. If this interests you, play it.Honestly, this has solidified itself as one of my all-time favorite games. The mechanics alone are pretty fun, and swinging around at break-neck speed is exhilarating, especially when doing so skips over chunks of what the room "wanted" you to do. The level design often felt reminiscent of Celeste and Ori (Specifically, the Bash). What really sets it apart (for a lot of people, I think) is the story. It made me.... . I don't want to give too much, because I believe you should go in totally blind, but playing through the first half hour should determine whether you would be invested or not. It also entices a second play through, but I haven't done that yet. There are a  dialogue bits that are worded strangely and take a bit of deciphering, but this is really just a result of localization and doesn't affect the quality at all imo. Do be prepared for several long cutscene sections, however. While I loved the story, there were a few sections that felt like they talked a little  long, though I never felt it was useless information.The runtime is very solid: it took me 10 hours to complete, though I'm sure many beat it faster (I wouldn't say I'm unskilled, but usually I trail behind most people by a few hours in run time on shorter games). I believe I played under the veteran difficulty (basically, you can only heal up to half health between games) For $15, this is reasonable to me, and the quality makes it feel like pocket change.I would dare call Sanabi a masterpiece, aside from the occasional weird level choices (the red zones can chain damage, and if you get too far into it, it's almost impossible to get out before it chews through all your health) and a few initially fun concepts but poorly executed sections (looking at you, exploding ventilation shaft). In the end, I'd give it a solid 9/10. Overall, if you enjoy a good story, Celeste, and Ori's bash mechanics, this I believe is the game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: If a person frequents Steam enough, I'm sure they will come across a game every once in a while with a "overwhelmingly positive" review that just doesn't really click for them. For me, that was Sanabi. Now before I get into my problems with the game, I just want to state, I like Sanabi. I think it is a well made game and I can see what people saw in it. But for me, there were way too many frustrations and poor designs to make me REALLY like itLet's start with what I think is the worst part of the game, the recoil from taking damage. You have 4 hit points before you die, but in most cases you might as well just have one because the recoil is so bad that you get stuck in whatever is hurting you. In many areas there are these red squares you cannot enter, but if you happen to hit one from the bottom, the recoil will push you up, even deeper into the area that's hurting you. You basically get stun locked desperately trying to escape when it's not possible. The game is challenging but most of my deaths came from the recoil putting me in a spot I couldn't recover fromSecond annoyance is the bosses. Each once has multiple phases HOWEVER there is no checkpoint in between each phase. Therefor, you basically have to do each fight perfectly or you have to do the whole thing over and over and over again. Now this seems par the course for video game bosses but the problem is when you are fighting bosses with pits below you. A fall in a pit is an immediate game over, so you could still have a full health bar but one mistake and you start the whole fight over again. And the fights aren't even that engaging, it's just survive all the enemies attacks until you get the one opportunity to hit them. Bosses can work in fast paced platformers like this one, but in Sanabi they just don'tAnd finally, the narrative. While I overall think the story is the strongest point, and is full of twists and turns, the writing does this absolutely obnoxious thing where the character you are traveling with clearly knows more than they are letting on, and you get literally a dozen moments where you might learn something from them only for them to go "Nah nevermind." The game basically pulls you along with that until the very end where you get an info dump on why everything was happening the way it was. I will say though, once the story really gets going at the end, it is very well done, to the point where it brought a tear to my eye.I'll be 100% honest, while I liked Sanabi I only beat it out of pure spite. I wasn't really enjoying my time by  the end but I had made it too far to quit. In a sea of people praising the game, the best thing I can say is it's fun when it clicks but absolutely abysmal when it doesn't
_childDocuments_.name: SANABI

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely phenomenal.Movement with your grappling hook is incredibly satisfying.  You get into this lightning-fast, fluid groove where you practically dance around the battlefield, dashing from enemy to enemy to catch a platform and boost your swing to orbit around it and dash to a third enemy and Spider-Man your way at mach speed into the next room to do it all again.  There are some sticking points with the movement - sometimes literally, as there's a brief period where you cling to a wall you swing into and it can completely kill your momentum, and it requires some practice to avoid - but once you get the hang of it, you feel downright invincible.At least, until the difficulty curve gets steeper.  The second half gets increasingly brutal, and while you still retain full control and your failures feel fair throughout, SANABI's later challenges demand mastery of the mechanics it's teaching you.  There were a couple points where I was grinding the same section over and over, swearing at my monitor (if you know, you know), but that frustration was quickly forgotten when the story kicked back in and gave me some new questions to chew on and a new mechanic to play around with.Regarding the story, I won't say a word about it - I think it's best experienced with no prior knowledge.  That said, the game's cutscenes borrow a lot of cinematic flair to their great benefit.  Even with some lines of dialogue tripping over themselves a little due to awkward translation, SANABI at multiple points legitimately unsettled and shocked me thanks to the extra work it put into its direction and cinematography, and some visceral, powerful sound design to match.  It's also capable of being, like.  REALLY funny.  The writers at Wonder Potion know how to tell a good joke and they create just enough bathos both in cutscenes and in gameplay to keep an otherwise very bleak cyberpunk aesthetic from crushing your ability to care without cheapening its more harrowing moments.Basically, let your emotions sit a little closer to the surface while you play.  The subject matter overall is not for the faint of heart, but it's worth every second, and in my opinion those are seconds you need to slow down and savor to enjoy SANABI to the fullest.Getting to the end isn't what's important, after all.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd been looking for a new game to play for a while, and when I saw SANABI on the store page, its visuals and story setting immediately drew my attention. I had never heard of it before, but seeing the overwhelmingly positive review score, I decided to listen to what seemed to be the general consensus and go in blind. Now, after having finished the game, I absolutely agree with the sentiment. The story in this game is deep and emotional, and full of twists and turns. I can't, in good faith, say more than that, and if you have any interest at all in this game, go in completely blind. The gameplay revolves around your grappling hook arm, and features a lot of aerial movement. The game provides a decent challenge, and has incredibly fun and fluid movement that makes it feel good to go fast and pull off tricks, or just finish certain more difficult sections. The controls are responsive, and you can feel your momentum carry over in your movement without feeling too floaty. The combat in the game is an extension of the movement system, and fighting enemies furthers the momentum instead of bringing the gameplay to a halt. The pixel art is nothing short of beautiful, with several unique and cinematic locations and backgrounds. I will say, the English translation isn't perfect, and there are some lines that don't quite make sense and need to be read over more than once, but it was still very understandable and didn't really hamper my enjoyment of the story. I would absolutely recommend the game, especially if you like platformers, pixel art, and crying over said pixel art.

_childDocuments_.review: SANABI is not really my kind of game, gameplay wise. Between its elaborate movement mechanics and total lack of secrets, it's definitely a speed game at its heart. But I grew up with Mega Man rather than Captain Commando and I don't have the speedrunning kind of autism (more the challenge run kind of autism, lol). So being a very speed-centric game focused mostly on a grapple hook mechanic puts it a little bit out of my primary genre focus.I will say that, if you ARE the kind of person who immediately perks their ears at 'speedcentric grappling hook game,' you will probably love the gameplay. I don't think it's quite a Celeste equivalent, in terms of polish and inventiveness and variety. It doesn't mix it up as much, it doesn't explore 'grappling hook' the way Celeste explores 'air dashes,' its environments and mechanics aren't as varied. But it's close enough for me to compare it and you don't get much higher praise than that when it comes to 2D platformers. Moving around very simply feels fantastic, and that's both one of the hardest things, and the most important things, to check off on a game like this. I also played it almost at the same time as Nine Sols, a game which has become one of my top 5 games of all time, likely settling in somewhere around third, or maybe even second. That game, comparatively, is EXTREMELY my kind of game, gameplay-wise. Basically made for me. It's a rough comparison to be forced into.So it says a lot that SANABI very, very comfortably made it into my top 10, and may even make it into my top 5 the next time I really stop to think about it.It's pretty simple. The game is visually gorgeous, and it has an absolutely top-tier plot, narrative, and characters. I feel like I can't really say much more about it than that, except that it's very funny and also I cried a bunch and I'll remember it forever and, for other people like me, that's surely enough to sell it. If you're big on stories and narratives in games, you should play it. No deep analysis here, no dive into the real ups and downs, it's just a beautiful story that I'm so, so glad to have experienced, and if you like things that throw you around and yank at your heart-strings, you will probably also deeply enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: An honest review of SANABI - SANABI is undeniably captivating, weaving a tale of intense gameplay and immersive storytelling. Although, there are some setbacks to it. Gameplay and Visual Charm:SANABI's gameplay is a thrilling escapade, offering a challenging platformer that has its difficulty with a lot excitement. The 2D pixel art style, reminiscent of Celeste, adds a nostalgic touch, creating a visually compelling environment. The *initial* playthrough is a delightful rollercoaster, with engaging mechanics that set it apart from other games.Replay Value:While SANABI looks fun for another round, its charm begins to disappear upon replaying. The story really loses its charm, it's just not interesting after you know the ending, and the achievements, omg. The achievements that are left after completing the game are some of the hardest ones. Challenges and Achievements:SANABI introduces a commendable level of difficulty, reaching its zenith in the formidable Legend mode. However, the pursuit of achievements becomes a double-edged sword as the overwhelming challenge, particularly in beating the game on Legend mode, can deter even the most determined players. The lofty difficulty may alienate those seeking a more laid-back gaming experience, impacting the game's accessibility.Cutscene Overload:A notable drawback lies in SANABI's reliance on cutscenes, disrupting the harmony between storytelling and gameplay. The engaging storyline is occasionally overshadowed by an almost 50/50 split between cutscenes and interactive play. This imbalance, disrupts the game's rhythm and could potentially remove the amount of overall enjoyment. Time:It's really a short game, sadly. It's only got about 8 hours worth of gameplay, and like I said, it's about half cutscenes. I really loved this game, but it only being 8 hours really deterred me from it. If it were lengthier, I'd definitely rate it better than I will soon.Conclusion:SANABI stands as a commendable piece of indie gaming, offering an enthralling platformer with a narrative that initially captivates. However, the overabundance of cutscenes and the super difficult achievements in the latter part of the game pose hurdles to its long-term appeal. Nonetheless, for those seeking an adrenaline-pumping and challenging gaming experience, especially during the initial joyride, SANABI remains a solid choice. It IS worth the cost, 100%, 8/10 game.

_childDocuments_.review: If anyone is on the fence and happens to read this review, I am only 2.3hrs deep.I came here looking for a new experience, (small story). Some of which are Castlevania-like, souls like and didn't really speak to me. But this game.. wow, to make this short'n'sweet here we go.Immediately I noticed the... STORY. That's right, this has a really intriguing story, I am only 2+hrs deep and I'm thoroughly interested, the characters are well written and the pace for this game is really well handled.The story could be a bit much for some people, but slow down and enjoy the game, so much rushing in this world. _childDocuments_.review: Solid game from start to finish. The story-telling aspect is very well done and in spite of the gameplay loop, it is very heavy on that story. The pacing manages to hit a really sweet balance between character building and actual gameplay. The main characters are fleshed out very nicely. I'll be honest and say that some of the late-game plot pieces got me choked up. There's good use of tragedy and comedy with a cast of characters that are relatable.Graphically, I love a good pixel art game. The low-res nature of some games can get in the way of their ability to tell a story. This is very much not an issue with SANABI. Characters are animated beautifully and they are able to convey a lot, even without text cues.For a game that got so many things right, the soundtrack is even better. Every track fits the scene it belongs to. The mid-game boss chase is tense and unnerving. After all story revelations have been made, the end-game march to the finale has a sense of renewed purpose. A game's soundtrack can really make or break an experience, and SANABI's soundtrack absolutely completes its narrative arc. For an indie title with a relatively small gameplay loop, Sanabi has a good amount of run-time. Like I said, it's heavy on story, which means there are fairly lengthy dialog sessions. These sessions run the full spectrum of emotion. Many of the "planing" scenes are cute and bubbly with a matching tune and definitely put a lighter touch onto an another bleak story. SANABI is a gem of a game.

_childDocuments_.review: The core gameplay in Sanabi is pretty solid. Once you get the hang of it, the speed and momentum of the grappling hook makes for some fun movement. I particularly like how the combat and platforming mechanics are integrated with one another rather than using two awkwardly overlapping systems, allowing the game to throw enemies and platforming challenges at you simultaneously without it becoming a problem for controls. There are a few awkward aspects to the controls, mostly surrounding the charged attack you get later in the game (specifically how it halts mid-air momentum and can be awkward to aim at a angle) and the hookshot-like ability (where you can’t pull yourself to the end of the hook depending on the angle) but these problems are largely avoidable either through improved technical abilities or just avoiding putting yourself into a situation where they might occur. But the one issue I have that can’t be easily avoided is the lock-on for the grappling hook. Because of how fast you’re moving and how small some targets can be (mostly enemies), it's not really feasible to rely entirely on manual aiming. While the game gives the option to disable lock-on, I tried it for a while and found the problems with manual aiming were far more difficult to deal with than the alternative. Specifically, the lock-on can focus on some weird spots and I really don’t understand why. It seems to avoid corners and edges (where you would be able to make the best use of the grappling hook’s other mechanics) and instead latches onto spaces that are a significant gap away from the edge, often leading to your next jump falling short. Even worse, it can sometimes go in directions you absolutely don’t intend, particularly when you’re traveling quickly. There were many times where, following a jump, I would be propelled down a corridor with both a ceiling above me and floor beneath me. And while I always had my cursor towards the top of the screen, if I got just a little too close to the ground the lock-on would target the floor instead and ignore any corrections to my aim by moving the cursor.With such a fast-paced game, these issues can be a big drawback. You want to make sure players can instinctively trust that the game will do what you expect it to do so they can focus on executing more complex and difficult maneuvers rather than sticking to simple and easy options to avoid the risk that the game screws them over. And while the systems worked well enough that I found the lock-on better than the lack of it, it was still inconsistent enough that I don’t think I was ever able to make full use of the mechanics.The level design was another source of problems. While most of the challenges worked quite well, they often suffered from alternative options. Rather than a challenge the player would need to overcome to clear a specific room, relying on their abilities to get them there, most of the time rooms had two options for clearing them. You could do it the intended way by swinging around, rarely touching the ground, and just gliding from one end of the room to another. But rather than making that intended solution the only option, there were enough climbable walls that you could also just walk and climb to the end of the room without any actual obstacle. If I failed a jump or mistimed a swing, my punishment wouldn’t be death. Instead, it would either mean walking back to the start of the room to retry or just getting to the end of the room through the lamest and easiest method possible. While this gets better towards the end of the game, it really felt like the entire first half was making it as close to impossible as they could for players to actually face consequences for their failures. I don’t think I had a single death until the 3rd chapter because the game just never introduced mechanical consequences to failing before that point.It's not until the second half of Sanabi that it really starts to feel like the mechanics are being fully utilized. Time pressures force you to get through the rooms quickly and timing becomes much more dependent on the various platforms and obstacles in a room rather than the player’s own comfort. The challenge ramps up, the consequences for failure start to become serious, and the general art, music, and tone of the game all start to magnify the tension. And while it does take a dip toward the very end with a huge chunk of story content interrupting the gameplay (and the following section feeling more like a romp to show off your skills rather than a real challenge) it's still a satisfying experience overall.As for other aspects of Sanabi, I’m generally positive though I don’t place as much emphasis on them compared to the core gameplay in evaluating my overall feelings. The pixel art was nice and never felt confusing when it came to distinguishing between interactable and decorative elements. The music did a decent job of setting the tone of each area, but apart from the main theme none of the tracks actually stuck around in my head for long after they went away. The story is really the big thing here that elevates Sanabi beyond the gameplay alone. While certain portions could be a bit annoying (especially towards the end where a huge chunk of the plot all gets revealed at once, killing the pacing for that section) the overall picture was very well done. I like the characters involved, their interactions, and the hints throughout the earlier parts of the game did a good job of telegraphing what was happening without spelling it out so clearly that you could figure it out without really paying attention. I’ll admit that it had a bit of an emotional impact on me by the end and, while it certainly won’t be winning any awards, I do think the game would be noticeably weaker without the story binding everything together.I enjoyed Sanabi overall. I have my issues with its execution at times, but they’re more so the problems that reduce my enjoyment rather than increase my unenjoyment… if that phrasing makes sense. It certainly had the capacity to do great things as the latter areas show and even though the game only occasionally reached those heights it was a great time whenever it did. Sanabi is far from a perfect game, but it's still an easy recommendation overall. The core gameplay is fun, especially if you’re willing to challenge yourself even when the game gives you an easy out, and its other aspects are a net positive to the overall experience.

_childDocuments_.review: SANABI is a 2D action title developed by Wonder Potion under the NEOWIZ umbrella. You play as a retired general whose peaceful life changes forever on one fateful day. Armed with nothing but his expert skills in combat and his mechanical arm he seeks out the entity known as SANABI that hurt the one closest to him as he entangles himself in a grander and broader mystery that is looming over the horizon.SANABI's introduction is brilliant, the game is funny when it wants to, cute when it calls for it and gritty when necessary. It gives the player ample amount of questions that pile on one another, and as the story concludes it answers all of them in a heartbreakingly satisfying way. It's not the most unpredictable story ever created, but damn is it good and well written. And the gameplay accompanying it is as good as the story. On your journey to seek SANABI you'll meet Mari who'll tag along you throughout the entire game. Mari's bubbly and seemingly carefree persona contrasts beautifully with our jaded general. She's a great character, she's bubbly and funny but not to a degree where it takes away from SANABI's darker subject matters. She, like others written for the story are layered and believable and I got heavily invested in all of their personalities during my 10 or so hours of playtime. I cried profusely when everything unfolded as the devs pulled on my heartstrings.And what accompanies that story and characters is an equally banging and satisfying gameplay loop. SANABI is 2D action game that prioritizes movement. Your base kit is simple but hard to master; you have an ability to climb most walls, jump and your main attraction: the Grappling Arm. The arm works like most grappling hooks with an incredible weight and snappiness behind it. You grapple to certain surfaces and swing, how hard could that be? Well.. decently difficult actually since Wonder Potion have done a beautiful job with SANABI's level design. Granted, some of them do get a little.. same-y but considering the game that game doesn't overstay its welcome too badly it doesn't really take away from the overall experience.Combat is also revolving around your hookshot, and the combat encounters here are mostly just minor roadblocks that are fast to deal with. They're not bad, some of them, especially the bosses are a highlight but I was wishing for something just a little bit "meatier" if that makes any sense. That being said they're mostly designed for speedrunners in mind, since the game also comes with an in-built Speedrun mode for those who seek to optimize their routes to perfection.Music, spritework and overall presentation in SANABI are a joy as well; the game is (seemingly) based in a dystopian fictional version of Korea where a big corporation has taken over the normal, day-to-day citizen's lives. Backgrounds consist (but are not limited to) beautiful mountaintops with lushious greenery to neonlit corporate cityscapes. It's all there and it's accompanied by a great soundtrack that suits every environment beautifully. Characters are lively with so little pixels, so the devs put some extra effort into animating text boxes to bring out that extra bit of personality which goes a long way in making SANABI's world feel truly alive.I've praised to the Moon and back.. but SANABI isn't perfect, no game is. So what gives? For one, the level structure can be a bit unclear where it wants you to go at times, and some of the sections feel a bit more trial and error than others (like the Overseer chase sequence). Some text boxes had weird spacing issues between sentences and some of the translations were off by just a bit. Assisted aim needs more, in-depth way to customize it and what bugged me the most was that the main characters is just.. a bit of ♥♥♥♥ at times. Look, I understand why and I understand the weight of the story but it was overbearing, just by a little bit at points.Otherwise, SANABI is a true gem. A testament to game development and 2D indie games as a whole. It's getting a physical release soon and I cannot wait to pick it up. Please play this game because it deserves all the love that it's getting and then some. It's also priced incredibly well in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: I have 8 hours in game and I have just completed the game. I spent about 3 hours of it actually playing and 5 hours watching cutscenes, no joke. It spends too much time meandering on points that have already been made and just never ends. Gameplay is also broken up constantly by cutscenes. The game focuses too heavily on story and the gameplay suffers not only for having the story constantly interupt the gameplay, but also having the mechanics not be fully fleshed out as the game leans too heavy into the story. I wish there was a more creative way to killing enemies rather than just charging at them and one shotting them, as well as there being a lot of visual noise moving around the screen while this is one of the most complicated movement systems I've used. The best part about this game was the sprite and artwork, really well done. For a future game, please cut back on the story and flesh out the gameplay more. Why is this dumb little pixel art game doing this to me?"I thought, on first glance, this was just a cool 2d platformer with a fairly unique traversal gimmick and while that is definitely part of it, it really is only a part of it. The story though. I'm normally quite good at feeling out where a story will take me in games and not only did I not call this one, when it all wrapped up at the end it left me absolutely devastated.  I'm not even kidding when I say that once it was over I just sat in the dark contemplating it. I almost want to say that I wish the team behind this would do more like it but the more I think about it I hope they don't and that they just let this thing exist on it's own. I only wish more people knew about this and would give it a chance because they don't know what they're missing.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, I played it because it was tagged as similar to celeste/noita, but in fact it is more close to To the moon rather than the other, Over 11h played, I probably played 3 hours at best, the rest was dialogue/story etc, and because it was an action game, related to celeste/noita I was expecting more gameplay phases.Overall, it is good considering the price, I'll rate it around 6/10 or so.details below:Pros++ The movement of the character was quite good, even if it was hard to handle at the start.+ The music is overall ok; some tracks that I will definitely listen to while working; others that I already forgot; still, one or two good tracks is already a good feat. As long as the rest don't pull the game down, which is the case here.In the same way, the audio fx are good enough for me.+ The pixel art is good enough; it's more the pixel art's animation that I liked overall.+ You can skip dialogue if you want only game play, but because it was my first game through, I didn't skip anything in case there were more things than tutorials sometimes.+ The story overall is cool, a bit too slow, and I would have wanted more gameplay phases to do stuff with the hook.Neutral= the game is really easy, I'm playing hard and I didn't that much times despite not excelling at platformers (expect when I was trying to do a short cut or obviously committing into a bad idea to just try it out).= still, something that bothered me was that the character's hook is always on the foreplan, switching from the left to the right arm depending on the direction you are going on, it probably saves some sprites, but it just feels a bit weird, nothing much though.Cons (there is a lot, yet considering the price and the fact that in the end I was still able to enjoy it, etc.)gameplay:-- Level design is poor or cluncky at best, the camera doesn't always follow the character, and you end up in a fixed panel from which you have to go to the side of the screen to make transitions. well, good luck finding the transitions that kill you or not. Most of the time, jumping to the bottom of the screen kills you, but still, it is not constant, same for the sides, nothing is more frustrating than dying because you lack information on where to go. Most of the platforms are skippable because you can go too fast, which is cool, but you easily struggle to find the way when you need to transition to another screen.- you have to aim with the controller, I couldn't play with the keyboard because between each screen my input was lost (ie : i go right, I press D, the screen changes. If I don't dubbletap D i'm not moving at all)- related to play with the controller, I had a lot of issues with the Aim assist, that glues at every corner, sometimes hooks through the enemies or through the object I wanted to aim at, in the end I turned it off most of the time because failing something because of the bad aim assist was more frustrating than missing because I struggled to aim with my controller, especially on the last boss (It rather be my fault than being betrayed by the auto aim).- the reset button for the moving platform is always ahead of the said platform, so most of the time I end up snapping into the reset button instead of just grabbing the platform.To grab a moving platform that is moving away from you horizontally, you have to spam LT A because the character doesn't grab the side of the platform.- the respawn can be really slow some times, especially on the training where you need to score a timer, went up to around 10s on the boss that flashbangs your screen and burns your eyes (my spec is i9 13900/RTX 3090). By the way, fading to white should be illegal, even more when it happens that often. And more, on the boss that flashbangs your whole room, if you input too fast on a respawn, some input is not taken into account.story:- I expected smth like celeste, but it was celest with dialogue every 3 screens at best.- there is a lot of small talk (thanks to genshin I can't stand it anymore especially on the couple's first hours before I feel involved with the characters, I needed more gameplay to pace it better).- I tried to do funny tricks with the grappling, but because of the duration of dialogue I struggled to get back to controlling my character properly.- there is a lot of unnecessary explanation; the story voiced out everything when things were already clearly implied in the story or by the action of the character, it took me 11h to complete the game at 4hours in I already knew everything so it was a bit long to get to the last chapter just to confirm that I understood it well.(ie SPOILER :  ,  , )(ie nospoilers: at some point you get a ride and things are falling off and you can see that you go fast but the characters have to voice out everything : explanation why they are going so fast, that if they hit smth at that speed they die and that they have to dodge the things that are falling off / another example is when you encounter the second training area, the game will again explain that it is a training area despite the fact that you can see it.)Overall that issue could be solved if the small talk was integrated into the gameplay phase, with the characters talking to each other while you play.- sometimes instead of a panel on the screen that explain a new mechanic, the characters will do small talk to explain it when basically you could just experience the new mechanic yourself.- a lot of repetition in the dialogue with the character sometimes running in circles (ie, you got a brief that said the city has been wiped out of living beings and the characters will keep saying that the place is empty in cinematics, or will ask the other character to leave the "mission" when they agreed to go in together.) In comparison you got a dialogue at the beginning that comes back at the end that isn't repeated a single time till the end of the last boss and it has more impact than the dialogue that were repetitive.- the ref of elon/choi, I understand kameo is a thing but putting someone from the reality to a fantasy world just put me out of immersion and instead of diving into the story I just recall the reality, and i'm not playing a video games to read news or whatever.Overall, I would have probably less issues with the story If I knew it was close to "too the moon" I had more gameplay expectations.
