_childDocuments_.review: Well, SANABI is more like a mix of Katana ZERO and Celeste, but not nearly as good as either. It's not terrible, and this would be a "thumbs sideways" if Steam had such a thing. The concept and core mechanics are solid, but the execution leaves a lot to be desired.The main grapple hook mechanic takes a bit of getting used to, but once you have a feel for it zipping around feels pretty good. Your suite of tools gives you enough options from the start to make things interesting, and the upgrades you unlock open up new possibilities. Unfortunately, the mechanics are let down by mediocre level design and bad pacing. Levels introduce new ideas like moving platforms or danger zones but fail to evolve these in interesting ways and quickly become repetitive and stale. That, is when you even get to play at all. SANABI constantly pulls you out of the action for cutscenes, many of which are inane and unnecessary, and this choppiness makes the whole experience drag and prevents you from getting into a flow. Another annoyance is that when you die or fall into a pit, it takes a few seconds before you respawn. A big part of the reason dying a few dozen times in a challenging platforming sequence in Celeste doesn't feel so bad is that it gets you back into the action instantly. SANABI is nowhere near as difficult as Celeste, but on the occasional challenging segment where you do die or fall a few times in a row, the slow respawn adds unnecessary frustration.Spending so much time in cutscenes also makes you realize how bad SANABI's writing is. The story concept is interesting, if unlikely to surprise you. But the narrative is disjointed, with frequent references to characters, lore, and worldbuilding that are never explained and a plot that spends an inordinate amount of time chasing its tail. The dialogue in particular is rough. It sounds nothing like how people actually talk, and half the time SANABI can't seem to decide if it wants to be a thriller or a comedy. Though it's hard to say how much of the dialogue issues are due to bad writing versus how much should be attributed to a translation that was clearly written by someone whose English skills weren't up to the task.The art and music are the strongest components of SANABI. It's obvious the creators were heavily inspired by Katana ZERO, but insofar as SANABI is an imitation in this regard it's a very good one. The pixel art looks great throughout, with detailed and imaginative environments, and the music has good energy. It's exactly the backing you want for flying around on a grapple hook smashing robots.I liked SANABI just enough to finish it, and it might be worth picking up on sale if you like these types of games. But if you're expecting the next Katana ZERO, lower your expectations. A lot.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first Steam review I've ever written, and chances are it may be the only one. SANABI is my favorite game ever made-- from the stunning artwork to the funny noise the vending machines make when you save, I love every aspect of this game. It is very dialogue-heavy, which I *normally* hate in video games, but the dialogue and story are so good that by the end, I found myself speedrunning gameplay segments just to get to more lore, more story, more of these characters. But that gameplay, oh my goodness... the game isn't the most challenging, but the experience of running through the levels is unparalleled. You're almost never actually touching the ground; the number of movement options you get lets you fly from room to room like a madman, and it's beautiful. The artwork and animations are gorgeous. The little robot who walks you through the tutorial has more animations to it than the main characters of some games. To prove I am not a shill, I did find some of the bosses kind of obnoxious, but never to the point where I was ripping my hair out. I think if I played the game again I would do a lot better-- the movement system can be tricky to get a hold of at first, and the bosses really push your understanding of the game's systems. Please play this game, and remember to enjoy it-- getting to the end isn't what's important. 10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: The game's story goes from 0 to 100, really ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ fast, and and it's the highlight of the game, by far. Characters are interesting, and it does have some funny moments here and there for what I would describe overall as a pretty dark and dystopian atmosphere. The mystery that's going on isn't cut and dry, so you're kept guessing what's going on. The only "twist" that you could see coming from a mile away is essentially having to go through this game's version of the Mines of Moria. Only small nitpicks are that the game does have a few small typos here and there, and some world building gets left out. One example being when the main characters mention that the government says some research is banned and illegal, and I'm sitting here wondering, "Why is it illegal? Was there some event that led to it being made illegal?" But again, nitpicks.My only gripes are that the main mechanic of the grappling arm doesn't control very well in some places, the platforming can be really tight in some areas, and it makes it difficult to tell how you're supposed to progress through some areas, as in, "where am I supposed to go? I can't see anything on the screen to latch onto". For context, I'm playing with a controller here, so maybe it's less finicky with a keyboard and mouse? Additionally, there are times that it feels like the invincibility frames after getting hit are way too short, and I get that it's meant as a recovery mechanic, but when some random platform goes into a danger zone, you're knocked off, and some bullet randomly hits you and you get hit again by the danger zone...it gets kind of tiresome. I will say, I wish there was a type of general purpose dodge sometimes, that doesn't involve getting hit.Combat's pretty decent, the normal mooks aren't too much trouble and it's insanely fun to zip around the map killing enemies. That is, until this one enemy starts showing up partway through chapter 2, and turns some fights into less of a combat encounter, and more of a puzzle fight, and not in a good way. Having to maneuver enemies into certain positions gets really annoying, but outside of that section, that particular enemy did not reappear in chapter 3, which is the furthest you can go at the time of review.Boss fights on the other hand are much more entertaining, with a few small hiccups here and there for some fights. The only downside I can say is that there's no checkpoint system for any of them, so if you die at any point, you're starting at the beginning of the fight once again. It's a pro for some people, a con for others. It's not that bad for the first boss since it's not the longest boss fight in the world, but it becomes a pain for the second, especially considering how many times you need to knock them down, and the "process" to knock them down...Overall, the game's pretty entertaining for what's there, and I'm pretty invested into the story at this point, so I'm really interested to see where it goes.

_childDocuments_.review: A game I REALLY want to like but the more I think back on my time the more I feel like there is a huge wealth of missed potential.This game demands both speed and precision, however there are numerous pitfalls (metaphorically and VERY literally) that hinder the overall experience. This is almost exclusively because of level design. There is almost always an instant-death pit beneath you, meaning that one minuscule mistake will cause you to restart however you are encouraged to go as fast as you can due to the many timed puzzles and pursuant enemies driving your forward. You can become stunlocked and die with no way to recover and the sheer amount of information you need to be processing in the later levels is nothing short of insane. It's like you're expected to fail just so you can see what's coming up ahead. Once you know what you're meant to be dealing with the game becomes much easier to enjoy as you can actually plan your next moves. As a result I feel like this game would benefit strongly from a slow-down mechanic. Maybe it can be tied to certain actions you perform or simply a button toggle but if I could have had even a second to take a breath and assess my surroundings my frustrations would have almost completely vanished.The art in this game is beautiful, the music is fantastic and the characters are engaging (although the story does beat you over the head for way longer than it should about certain plot points). When the level design allows it you can really fly through the city and simply enjoy traversal. Heck, even the combat is fun for how sparse it is.However there is a specific boss "fight" that goes on for FAR too long. It was such a long encounter that there are multiple checkpoints IN the encounter itself, and the difficulty of what you're supposed to do isn't consistent. Some "cycles" are nigh-impossible to do in time without knowing what you're dealing with ahead of time while others are so easy you could do them in a wheelchair. And this sporadic difficulty is all over the game, there's no real sense of difficulty progression because the problem is often "you don't know what's ahead? Better die and figure it out on your second try". And then when you DO get ahead you have to repeat the process allllllll over again.I think the best way of summarising my feelings is this:Instead of "cyber Spider-man" I got "trial and error: the reckoning".There is a good game here, it just wasn't hitting the right notes for me. Too many issues were compounding on one another and the only thing keeping me engaged was the story and character interaction. Despite my frustrations I'd say there's more to enjoy than dislike here, even though it seems like I've done nothing but rant endlessly.

_childDocuments_.review: Movement feels amazing when you really get into it. The last section of the game, when you zip through the areas from all the other chapters and revisit their mechanics, is amazing to play through. The hardest difficulty is definitely the best way to play through the game, as it feels so rewarding to get through sections without taking a single hit. It also makes the combat sections, which are too forgiving on the normal difficulty, much more intense and satisfying to get through. The only time I got annoyed with this difficulty though, was in the final two boss fights. The pattern of attacks these enemies use is too random. When I finally beat them, I felt more that I had gotten lucky that they chose an easier sequence of moves rather than feeling that I had truly mastered them.The story is interesting, but it interrupts the flow of the game. There are so many cutscenes. While it is interesting to uncover the mysteries the game has created, there were many times where I was getting into the flow of the game just to be interrupted by a 1 or 2 minute cutscene of dialogue.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't really like this game. The story at first is really cute and then kinda heavy and interesting but it's also mostly very forced. The gameplay is "fast paced" but the story parts keep bringing the character to a halt and forcing you in a slow walk state, which breaks the flow of the game.Of course the artstyle and visuals are really good, but some things get reused in the worst possible way. Can't really describe it without getting into very early spoilers but the character interactions and personalities are reused between multiple characters and kinda removes some of the impact of what happened to the earlier character.As for the gameplay, it feels "wrong". At first you see the chain arm thing launch a claw with a satisfying sound and mechanical noise, expecting it to behave like a grappling hook. But nope, it becomes completely flaccid and acts like a swinging rope. Then the game teaches you that you can attach the arm chain to enemies and reel onto them, using the chain like what you would expect of a grappling hook from other games. So now you have this weird mix of two completely different behaviors depending on what the chain arm attaches onto and it's very jarring and disorienting. It makes it feel like you have little to no control over the character's movement. On top of that the chain arm has a weird auto aiming that isn't always aiming where you would expect so you have to correct for it, making it feel like you have to fight the controls.Talking of controls, at first I tried playing the game with my 8bitdo controller that is supposed to be recognised like an xbox controller, but no, the game didnt even understand there was a controller connected. Then I tried using the steam input thing to map keyboard and mouse to controller, but it made the chain arm aiming completely useless. So I tried playing with keyboard and mouse instead but it wasn't really nice either.Also back to gameplay, the momentum feels wrong. Depending on which direction I was pressing, sometimes the character would come to a complete stop after releasing from a super fast swing, but sometimes he would be launched into the expected trajectory. Gravity and momentum feel like they have no effect on the swing behavior, even tho it's supposed to be the main thing the player does. Sometimes when holding no directions the swinging worked fine in an expected manner but then pressing a key would break that natural movement. It's hard to explain but it just plainly felt wrong.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is like Katana Zero in that they are platformers that have dialogue. In every other respect this game is nothing at all like Katana Zero, and it's a shame I got my expectations so dialed in after every other Steam review made the comparison.Katana Zero had a gritty story that made you question reality at every turn, with a fairly peppy back-and-forth between text and gameplay. Sanabi prefers to instead bludgeon you with plot points, repeating the same handful of conversation set pieces over and over, swinging just as recklessly as your character between melodramatic and ham-fisted. Sanabi can't seem to decide whether it wants to be Katana Zero or The Messenger.The gameplay suffers a similar identity crisis. The bionic arm feels really good, and checkpoints are distributed reasonably; still some sections run on with a single theme for far too long, and after spending twenty minutes on a one-hit-kill boss encounter where death meant starting completely over, I was too mentally exhausted to care about avenging my daughter.The pixel animations and soundtrack are top-notch. Sanabi just needed a lot of trimming down elsewhere to be a compelling experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I will play this game again and do a more in-depth review, but here's my thoughts after my first playthrough:This game has gorgeous pixel art, satisfying movement, simple combat, and overall wasn't *too* hard (playing on normal difficulty.)It's a lot more story-heavy than you might expect walking in, which at times is great and at other times makes me wish I could just go back to using my grapple hook. It's almost a shame to put such a fun game mechanic in such a story-heavy game. There's a few moments of bad level design (some jumps that you need to make offscreen with little to no indicator that that's where you need to go) and the pacing really drags during the middle, but it has a rewarding ending so overall I'd say it's worth it. Whatever this studio does next I'll be checking out. TL;DR this game spend half of its time ruling and the other half of the time playing like a visual novel, and both parts work well in a vacuum but together they tend to clash. A solid pick for fans of the Ori series and Night in the Woods. If neither of those games do anything for you, you probably won't be too impressed.

_childDocuments_.review: I can confidently say SANABI is probably one of the best games I've ever played. TL;DR: Amazing game, play it now, thanks Wonder Potion for making something this good.Most games have movement systems that make either the combat OR the platforming engaging, leaving the other as boring filler that unnecessarily fills up the game. This game capitalizes on both, having some of the most fun combat AND platforming of any game I've ever played. How does it achieve this? The protagonist's signature chain arm and other movement abilities, beyond being cool as heck, give the player unrestricted freedom over exactly where they need to go, how fast they need to get there, whether they need invincibility frames when getting there, etc. Pretty much any mistake or screw-up in this game is entirely the player's fault, while every success is a result of the player's skill, and adds to the feeling of flow the game allows. There's no better feeling than being able to breeze through multiple checkpoints in a row without dying or falling out of the map. The game offers different difficulty options for different people based on the experience they want (ex: I would imagine someone wanting to experience the story alone would probably pick Easy, where your character doesn't take damage, while people who want a challenging experience may pick Veteran(hard) or Legend(one HP)), so players have some level of control over their experience.  As for the actual content in the game itself, the game is roughly 15 hours long with 5 levels. Each level has a different setting, platforming mechanics, BGM (this game has a really good soundtrack), and enemies. While different, all of these levels are fun and enable a player to achieve the flow state I was discussing earlier. The last level in particular is what I believe to be the best level I've ever played through in a video game in terms of mechanics, writing, and pure fun factor. Furthermore, there are a number of bosses spread throughout the game, all of which are fair, look pretty cool, and are a blast to fight. Visuals: well, you've seen the trailers. The game looks gorgeous, with a beautiful pixel-crafted world that encapsulates the futuristic city we all imagined in our heads. The game uses visuals well, never being too overbearing and never taking away from the gameplay while perfectly telling the story of the place you're in. Furthermore, animations are solid as well, making the protagonist look cool as the player platforms through these levels while ripping apart every enemy in sight. For the game's plot, I won't say anything except that it's really good. The plot centers around two characters, and their interactions throughout the game made me smile, laugh, and tear up at different points throughout the game. If you like a story with well written characters, play this game.It's a great game, and you should definitely play it, especially if you like action platformers like Katana ZERO.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best indie games I've ever played.SANABI is an unbelievable 2D action-platformer that will see you swinging and slashing your way in the foreground of a beautiful pixel cyberpunk backdrop. The gameplay is stellar and is well-paced in how it slowly ramps up the difficulty as levels progress, adding tougher enemies but also giving you new moves to add to your arsenal. Once you get the hang of how the hookblade works it's a ton of fun to swing about and very smooth feeling.As I'm sure you've seen with other reviews, the story is stellar. At the beginning of the game it can be a bit text heavy but don't let this put you off, after the first 30-60 minutes it's pretty much 85% gameplay, and you'll actually find yourself happily awaiting cutscenes to see the intriguing plot play out. And yes, you will cry at the end of your journey. Or maybe you won't, I don't know how emotional of a person you are.The campaign will run you around 8.5-10 hours depending on your skill level and what difficulty you pick. I played on normal but if you're used to playing 2D platformers I'd recommend the hard difficulty as the game is quite generous with giving health packs, and has frequent checkpoints.For the bones of €10 you cannot go wrong with this masterpiece.

_childDocuments_.review: If you have ever liked a single action platformer, or if you're the type to remember a game's story more than anything else about it, Rarely do I encounter a game so good and so artistic that I purchase it three times within a week of first hearing about it. (For those curious, I gifted it twice immediately after finishing it, and the 20% discount of the winter sale contributed to that decision.)The emotional hook is instant, and caries strong through the entire story. No other game has come close to the level of emotional impact SANABI can provide, and I hope I'm wrong when I say nothing will again. The gameplay starts a little later, but is very easy to pick up and becomes familiar and extremely satisfying in no time. Every single environment, every single character, is crafted to perfection and refined even further into a masterpiece. Just look at how many reviews are positive here, and ask yourself if so many people can be wrong about a game this good?To be clear: This game is NOT for everyone. There are people who will find it too easy, there are people who will find sections too difficult. There are people who will find the story too short, there are people who will take issue with the story slowing down a fast-paced platformer. There are people who will love this game as much as I do and people who will find a flaw to fixate on and let it ruin their enjoyment of it. At the end of the day, the issues some people may take do not stop this game from being a masterpiece, as no game can be all things to all people. But if from this description you think you may like the game, then you should absolutely give it a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: SANABI

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not sure if I can praise this game enough but I'll try. Sanabi is an incredible cyberpunk action platformer with tight controls and a rich story. Taking obvious influence from Katana Zero, the combat and controls in this game are easy to learn and fun to master. By the end of the story, you're blasting through each level and it feels so satisfying. I really appreciated the lack of rankings and collectibles to better focus on the incredible story. I truly did not anticipate the twists and turns this game brought, but even more-so how the story stayed easy to follow. I was never truly lost on what was going on in the story, any more than the games narrative was intentionally pacing itself for. The pixel art in this game is just gorgeous. Each area has a distinct art style separating it from the last and SEVERAL screenshot worthy stills presented by the story. The soundtrack is littered with the main theme which is always a treat to hear weaved into hard synth tracks all the way into the more somber tracks. There are also several moments of humor that were always in good taste and never skipped a beat to present them.This game truly is a 10/10 for me. It masters tight controls, great storytelling, beautiful visuals, & atmospheric music all into a very reasonable price for the length of the story (~12 hours). If you liked Katana Zero, Ruiner, Hotline Miami, you will love everything that Sanabi has to offer.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly one of the best platformers I have ever played (definitely one of the best I have played in years) and was really excited when the full release came out after playing early access last year, the pacing of the gameplay including great implication of puzzles elevate this game to the same level as other greats like celeste. Honestly recommend it to all my friends that love platformers. The caste of characters are all bubbly and have great dialogue and the art is katana zero level of good. For me its definitely a 9/10 and as the developers work on improving the game it will definitely reach 10/10. It is already a staple for me in the genre and in indie games in general so I will always sings it praises. so if you continue to read my review know that my critique for the game is from a place of love and I really recommend this game.However there are two problems that I hope the developers due read in my review that I hope they will address, one minor and one I think is pretty majorThe Minor problem is the lack of a break in certain sections, for example without going into spoilers, there is was a part in the game where you encounter three set pieces (major action parts/boss fights) that happen one after another. The player is unable to find a suitable moment to exit the game without feeling that if he quits now he would it would ruin the experience in some sort of way. What do I mean by this? Well after the set piece ends the player immediately enters a cut scene that he is unable to pause and save than safely exit, he would only be able to pause the game after he skips the cutscene (which why would you? the cut scenes are great) or allow it to play out. Now for most this might not be such a bad thing, it just means there is just a lot of exciting and cool events in the game that can make a player play for hours. However not every player is like that and most times after a major set piece especially after a boss fight would normally save and exit the game. So it is not to start the next part of the game. Now you can save and exit after the cutscene but I feel like if a player came back the next week to play the game he or she would forget the context of the major set piece he or she was playing in therefore slightly hindering the experience. What I propose is before a cutscene starts (one that leads to the next boss fight or event) after a major set piece that the player must first interact with Marie than does the event trigger therefore not hindering pacing plus allowing players that opportunity that they now feel safe to save and exit the game because unironically the part of the game that I'm talking about the player's character is extremely exhausted which was how I felt after the three set pieces in the row.The major one is using the controller. Since I have played the game mostly on the M&K I had no idea about how controller was like in the game until I had it plugged in the other night and decided to use it. There is a feature in the game the slows down time kinda like in katana zero (I had no idea this was even a feature) that allows the player to aim the grappling hook to where he wants to go. Now I didn't even once use it when I was M&K let alone I had even forgotten it was thing until I picked up the controller. Why is the ability triggered when ever you aim the grappling hook with the joystick? it should be a separate designated button, as it ruins all pacing in the game and makes it incredibly sluggish and frustrating as I was so use to just moving around super fast and making quick second decisions. I quickly unplugged my controller after that and continued to have fun on the M&K but please devs make it a separate button like in katana zero. allow controller users to decide if they are going to use the slow down ability or not than just forcing it on them.

_childDocuments_.review: SANABI is going to scratch that fast-paced platformer itch you've had for the past few months. You play as the retired army general on the path of vengeance. Attached to your shoulder is the Chain Arm - part weapon, part grappling hook that you use to not only swing around the dystopian cyberpunk streets of Mago city, set in Korea. The Chain Arm is also used to...*checks notes*...rip enemies apart in an instant.This is a one-hit kill platformer that makes you feel powerful when you pull off a sick move, and like an absolute loser when you whiff it. Speedrunners rejoice - this is the one you're looking for. There are various tools to traverse the environment, boosting through swings with your Chain Arm at the right moment will propel you to the next area in a single swift move. Memorizing the environment will make it even easier to chain your movement from zone to zone quickly.Which is a bit of a shame because...the environment is beautiful. Mago city is full of neon lights, industrial corridors, and beautifully-designed robots both friend and foe. The game gives massive Katana ZERO vibes, with the fast-paced nature of Super Meat Boy and similar wall-jumping platformers in the genre - all wrapped up in tasty cyberpunk vibes.There are some minor graphical issues in some of the cinematics, and there were TINY but noticible performance issues I while playing. But this review was made literally hours after the game's early access release so there's still time to tune these things up.I have a lot to play and experience in Sanabi so far, but if you're a fan of fast-paced platformers like Katana ZERO and Super Meat Boy then you're really going to like this one.
_childDocuments_.name: SANABI

_childDocuments_.review: I'll keep this review sorted into gameplay mechanics (movement and combat), story (narrative and plot) and art direction (visuals and music). Also keep in mind, I am writing this review after finishing the Early Access up until past the Factory. TL;DR at the bottom. ALSO: SPOILERS (DUH)!GameplayShort interjection for the level design on a pragmatic level: Just feels tight. I love the areas so far, the puzzles are a bit too easy I feel but these jumps man... they are creative. You can feel that someone on the dev team understands flow and movement not just in a general sense, but on a grander scale. Where and how to go from A to B. Levels blend into each other, the arenas are very well thought out (enemy spawning positions especially, speedrunners will have a field day), and while everything is neon and cyber and gritty, the change of pace with each level introducing a new mechanic or environmental asset is refreshing enough to make me not mind it. I don't need a jungle level or some volcano manor if the levels themselves are just... plain fun to play.MovementFeels bad to start with a wonky topic so early, because I know I love it, but I also know some people will find it a bit off. But let's get the elephant out of the room.The swinging, pulling and overall flow from level to level feels incredible - if you got used to it. Like, I finished the EA, immediately tried the speedrunning mode with my ackquired knowledge on how it works and it was ADDICTIVE. It feels like the old son-I mean Mach games. Fast, fluid, you feel like a demigod, and the early visuals with John Wi- I mean our protagonist feel validated by your own skill, the invincible cyber solder mode feels earned retrospectively. But oh boy, a wrong hook or a slow down in speed and all the Dopamine is just gone. It feels like hitting a brick wall. Not only losing momentum, but getting hit feels TERRIBLE. Like, they game is not even saying anything, it just blatantly and boldly shows you the result of your own failure. If you are bad at the game, you won't enjoy it, but if you "get" the momentum, it feels amazing. Getting better feels amazing. Side note: the stops hurt so bad, they made me want to get better. Which is a good thing.Combat Combat is very rudimentary, and I can fully understand it, since movement and speed are the main focus of the game. Using the enemies as speed boosts is very rewarding, albeit sometimes a bit to generous I think. Like, you can clip through all kinds of stuff since the hook has a semi-hard lock-on per default. It makes combat go by very fast, which is good, since I wanna swing, baby. Just as it needs to be. The nice thing about the very simple combat mechanic is what's done with these limitations - bosses feel unique, I like the difference in design mechanics wise. Creative solution for this self imposed limitation.StoryNarrativeMy dudes I'm sorry, linguistics is my degree and I gotta pluck at the bones. That doesn't mean I find it lacking. I think these neo-noir revenge stories are perfect to convey very intimate feelings, and Sanabi does it pretty well imo. Sure, it's not narratively complex; I mean, it's Cyber John Wick on Crack - but that's what I love about it, and how it should be done aswell. Simple story, make the best out of it. The father-daughter dynamic is a bit cheesy at first, but the comedic and darker interjections mellowed out the initial cringe, since this frame of a hurt soldier with a death wish gets ACTUALLY CHALLENGED by Mari. I was taken aback, I did not expect such a nuanced view on the trope.Apropos unexpected, I was NOT ready for the assassination of a child in the, like, first 5 Minutes of the game. That actually sold me, since it's a bold move. It was surprisingly effective in setting the tone and makes Hook's suicidal rampage feel more... believable? Especially after all these shenanigans with his daughter before the explosion. There's two main themes here - A classic father-daughter dynamic that's pretty on the nose, and what I call "a gentle death wish". That feeling of not "actively" actively wanting to die, but being okay if it happens rather abruptly. The nihilist's dilemma I guess? The former is I don't wanna say well developed, since I'd personally go more into challenging the roles of their dynamic (might happen in the future, who knows!), but it suffices for the plot. The latter feels a bit more nuanced, especially after a few "talk it out"-cutscenes I did not expect. I wish some of the implications weren't stated directly afterwards. The change of heart comes not as gradual as I had hoped, but it was still nice to see.There's of course the whole government corruption subtheme, but I felt it not uh... too important? Maybe because the focus is definitely on character exploration and development. PlotActually, there isn't much to say. Bad dude kills morally ambiguous dude's daughter, and Hook respecs into Retribution for DEUS VULT. Chasing Sanabi (who isn't revealed yet!) through an empty city feels just... immersive. I don't know, it's simple but effective. Reminds me a lot of Ray Bradbury's "The City" in his Painted Man Anthology. Dude kicks ass, I like. Art DirectionVisualsCome on, don't deny it, we all cliced on it because it was purple, blue and pixelated. That isn't to say it's bland, I think they did it right - give the people what they want and do it as best as you can. The sheer amount of time it must have taken to draw all the backgrounds is jaw dropping. The city feels BIG and VAST. The Tower of Babel feels HUGE. The backtracking after Hook killing some of Sanabi's goons gave me shivers. Reminded me of Zulf's pardon and penance in Bastion. These black glass windows in the factory where you just KNOW some big ass overpowered AI will suddenly come out of the dark feels impactful. In General, the hooking feels like your body has weight, there's a very nice sense of impact, force and gravity. They really want you to soak in the atmosphere and basically overload you with the sheer vastness and effort put into it. MusicIt bops hard. Gotta say it. I actually laughed out loud when there was this little scene with some game references and a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Thrash Metal track came on when Mari puts on the neon glasses. I actually found this game through the soundtrack and tried really hard to find it since I can't speak korean. I'd have bought the soundtrack if it was available (correct me if I'm wrong, maybe I missed it though).ConclusionSo far very enjoyable. Sadly rather short, but the gameplay is 95% pure tightness. There's some minor glitching I found while trying the speedrunning mode, but that's why it's EA. I love games that polish that first and continue with the story during the EA and Beta stages, since I feel that's what's many people judge on a first impression. If you like fast paced platforming that gradually gets harder and has some just NASTY level design (in a good way, there was one jump with a moving platform amplifying my swing that had me stop for a minute because I couldn't believe how TIGHT it was. I felt disgusted by myself, because the dopamine overload from playing this game well is overwhelming),you will absolutely love this game.TL;DR: Good ship, that's some good ship right there. MMMMmmmh, like chocolate sauce on vanilla pudding. Ship's got me HOOKED. Buy it. Do it for Mufin. 8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: So, I'm not quite done yet, but I felt the need to write a review for this one before I finish it up.This game is a beautifully paced tide of intensity, starting with a simple layer of movement, and then the mechanics start packing on and punching in to make the pace frantic, the combat hectic, and the overall result a pulse-boosting, emotionally captivating experience. Soundtrack is absolutely bonkers level of tasty synthwave/electronic goodness. EXTREMELY high quality. The pixel art and general spectacle of the game are fantastic. Writing somehow manages to balance grittiness and some level of comic relief without feeling forced or having any "Well THAT just happened" moments. The highs are high and might give you a chuckle, and the lows will hit ya right in the gut.Level design is generally great, with a few small sections that I found a little irritating, but were eventually passed with relative ease on the normal difficulty once I took a moment to step back and put on a momentary cap of thinking for five seconds and actually controlling my movement. Certain sections have a bit of a learning curve, so some levels will rack up the death counter, but if you really dig into the movement mechanics you mechanically feel like a dang superhero by the last few sections of the game. My best recommendation without spoiling anything is, when you are given the option to rerun the tutorial, do it a handful of times, mess around with the movement, get a feel for the speed and what directional inputs do while you're swinging. I ran the tutorial around 5 or 6 times because it's less than a minute long and I genuinely feel like it enriched my experience with the game.It's also consistently adding in new little mechanics to make sure that movement never goes stale and ensuring that they tie into that delicious, delicious worldbuilding.There are difficulty settings across the board from "You have infinite health and can only die in pits/instant kills, enjoy the story" to "A single fart from an enemy kills you". Also has a speedrun mode that you unlock, presumably after beating the game once. If I had to guess it's probably the levels and bosses in rapid sequence with cutscenes removed.Game is positively dank. As I said, not quite done yet but I'm really, REALLY enjoying it. Kind of hoping that the game hits me with a plot twist and like six more hours of game.If you like platformers, snag it, it's already relatively cheap.

_childDocuments_.review: Every Hello ends with a goodbye. Getting to the end isn't what's important: it's how you get there.Sanabi is a *beautiful* pixel art platformer with a phenomenal soundtrack. The grapple mechanic is smooth and very engaging to play around in, and even as someone who doesn't speedrun games i found myself craving to try and be faster and faster by mastering momentum and dashes and pulling myself to surfaces. There was only one part that I found to be rather grating or annoying, and its limited to one chapter specific platforming gimmick regarding large red areas you cannot enter. Otherwise, it was all fun, varied, and interesting. Combat isn't the most in depth thing but it doesn't need to be: it's good, and it works. There's a hundred comparisons to Katana Zero, and its well warranted. Even the game has a direct Easter Egg to Katana Zero. This in and of itself should tell you this is very high praise. The story is...it's very good. There are a few twists and turns that will flip everything on its head twice over, re-contextualizing all of the events you go through. Even knowing this, you won't be ready for it. It's a heartbreaking story of loss, and revenge, and the depths at which that blind hatred can truly consume you and effect the people around you. The people in the reviews aren't lying, it sucks you in and makes you cry. There's a minuscule amount of translation errors, which can make a few sentences confusing, but overall it's been localized quite well and they are still updating them. The game is very, very good. Easy recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: -takes a deep breath- okay, let's talk about Sanabi.Not sure how this game found itself on my wishlist, but I'm glad it did. I grabbed it on a small sale and saw a lot of the reviews praising this game and saying it is similar to Katana Zero, another great game I love. Upon finishing Sanabi, I have to say, this is one of the best 2D action games I have played. I feel like it is Katana Zero meets Celeste. Let's dig in.You play as a retired General who is spending time with his lovely daughter. While living the good life and using your awesome grapple hook arm, your daughter heads inside your home and sees a clock with the name "Sanabi" on it. Before the General can warn her, she dies in the explosion. Days have passed, the General now wants to hunt Sanabi for the death of his daughter. He takes on a mission to enter a city where are the humans have mysteriously vanished. All, but one. A woman has sent a distress signal from inside the city. Your mission is to figure out why all the humans have disappeared from the city and to get the woman out of there alive.Sanabi is a 2D action platformer. The controls are tight and very fun to get used to. As the General, you will be jumping and grappling onto walls, platforms, and more as you traverse the city to complete your mission. I felt like I was playing Celeste but with a grappling hook as the levels got more and more complex. Everything is very simple to master and as you progress, you will learn one to two more skills that enhance the gameplay.The pixel graphics are gorgeous as well as the music. I was bobbing my head to the great soundtrack as I was swinging across chasms and fighting enemies. The boss fights were very fun and memorable. However, gameplay aside, Sanabi's strongest asset was its story. While playing, I kept thinking I had the story down, and then curveball after curveball hit me until I got to the good ending (which was so EFFIN good!!!).However, this game does have its flaws. While the story is very strong and beautiful, it also hinders the game as well. You know how Metal Gear Solid is a great game but it has long cut scenes? Sanabi has that same issue as there will be times you will be sitting through long scenes in between gameplay that will just break the flow. While these scenes are skippable, you really need to watch them to fully immerse yourself into the story. Some of the later levels really hit you with a skill check and may take a while to beat. I also had a bug here and there where my jump button was also tied to my grapple button, but a quick reset on the controls fixed this issue whenever it occurred. There were times when I got stuck in walls or laser grids that got me some cheap deaths, but nothing game-breaking.Final verdict? This game has definitely planted itself into my top 10 games. I tried to keep my review short and sweet because I don't want to spoil anything, but I just have to say, the scenes leading up to the end of the game literally had me in tears. I legit sobbed at the end of the game and I am so grateful I played it to the very end. The characters were great, the story was amazing, and the gameplay and boss fights were top-notch. This was a perfect indie game and I highly HIGHLY recommend you play this masterpiece. The story will slow you down and there may be a bug here or there, but the overall experience was just perfect and I praise the developers for a wonderful journey. Thank you for reading.PS: "Getting to the End is not what's important......"

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game on a whim after seeing that it was on sale and hearing good things about it from a friend. At first, the concept of a grappling platformer game "hooked" me and I didn't think the story was all too intriguing, however, my opinion shifted very quickly at around the halfway point, with my two views on these two aspects swapping positions. While the core gameplay mechanics is quite solid and very satisfying to pull off, the story manages to lock in at around the 66% mark and pulls you in for a rollercoaster of emotions. I ended up crying as the credits started rolling, which is something that not many games, or even media, manage to make me do. This is achieved thanks to the wonderful soundtrack perfectly expressing all the feelings and emotions that I felt watching the end, and is overall one of the best aspects of the game. Easily a must-buy game, it's not too long, visually stunning pixel art, and every dollar poured into this game is easily worth it for the experience.

It has some good parts - very nice visuals and the gameplay is okay.But sadly, the developers are deranged and their derangement has compromised the artistry this otherwise would've had.It smuggles a "current year" ideological message that becomes apparent about 2 hours in. You reach a corporate space showing the villain - Elon Musk - and one of the characters makes a comment that "he's making life hard for many people." It's not some subtle parody or allegory, it's a picture of Elon Musk's likeness, and it immediately drags the game down into the same territory as that Alex Jones game, except that one is advertised honestly.Other negatives:- It barely lets you play. It's full of cutscenes and dialogue and forced walking sections, much of it quite painful to get through.- The entirety of the game loop consists of grappling hook usage.- The grappling hook, while okay, is frankly sloppier than grappling hooks in other games. There are some delays during which inputs are dropped rather than queued, and it feels a bit clunky for it.Update: I looked it up, and it appears at least 60% of the game is cutscenes/dialogue. That is obscene for this kind of game.

_childDocuments_.review: First, game is fire and makes its impression with the overall qualityNotes on visuals:> Pixel Graphics which aren't just scaled up squares. Depth of color gamut to provide more depth to the graphics. Moving text is arguable, but if you read with voice actors reading it out loud in your head, the moving and stressed font highlights it for me. Overlapping text boxes are intentional and mimic realistic interruption in speech. Well tracked parallax and detailed assets offer visual exploration. LOTS of clever use for graphical assets--background details become relevant in narrative.To add the opening is such a strong intro to the character and game, and the usage of a side scroller's panning camera to introduce offscreen elements is so clever. Even using simple lighting to obscure sections reminds me of advancements from Hotline Miami and Katana Zero. I was pleasantly surprised when I found this isn't Dennaton/Devolver. I really hope to see more Eastern indie games like this using western influences to mingle into our markets soon.Audio notes:> The music takes a step back compared to games like Katana Zero so you won't hear any really outstanding motifs just yet. Admittedly I have to replay the game to check if there is a running theme in their soundtrack. The sound effects are impacting and punchy. You can truly hear the weight and presence of the MC's footsteps--even though at times it's a bit much. Music was a huge focal point in games like these, but I think this works for this game as the narration wants to be at the front of your first play through.Gameplay notes> It's fun and momentum based. If this were under one of the bigger publishers that own Bionic Commando, I would totally say this can easily be canon as a sequel being in Korea. I often thought about a singular mechanic being your main mode of combat and this game does just that with mobility enhanced by the grappling mechanic. One fall back is the weird momentum changes using dash while grappling--I'm still figuring out if it's momentum based or directional influence using input. I would say the wall cling needs some QoL improvement by letting yourself launch with the [jump] command while sliding down against the wall. With the rest of the mobility mechanics feeling fluid, it felt slightly un-intuitive to let the stick/movement reset to neutral before ejecting off the wall. Controller mapping for the Chain retraction is also a bit weird having to skip a beat and risking pixel perfect input. Damage in the more forgiving settings is easily chained and is mitigated slightly with a recovery dash. I believe second or two of slowdown can help here as QoL change along with a slightly longer invulnerable state to allow players to recover more easily, this may be tricky in balance, so maybe this have to have either small changes or a rework.Narration Notes> Maybe it's because I'm part of a slightly older crowd, but what a gut punch in the intro. It felt very consistent and the characterization was not dry whatsoever in the English localization. I really don't mind the quirky Gen Z 2020 slang/memes because despite how cringe it may be to a lot of people............ that's really how a lot of us sound when we try to be ironic. Perhaps we just live in a society?Don't act like I don't see your classist undertones! Tell the writers I love and appreciate the usage of Cyberpunk tropes to highlight previous Korean critiques, (Parasite, All of Us Are Dead, etc) This aspect is told mainly through another lead character you'll meet in game framing around the MC's backstory. It feels a lot like modern day action movie writing curbed back to allow for that 80s gratuity. Obviously the graphic violence has been replaced with robots most likely due to censorship laws (that I have no idea about in Korea) It does drag in some places for a beat too long, but it's still filled with developments among the characters enough while adding context to some scenes and also disguising short tutorials. I think that latter point is an accomplishments the devs + writing teams should be proud of.My play time of 3 hours is a single run-through on normal difficulty all the way to the end of the available content as of this writing. There is a speed run mode available I have not yet used, but all in all, definitely a game worth keeping in your collection next to Hotline Miami and Katana Zero. I'll be watching out for the full development in due time because I would like to support more East Asian productions going west.

_childDocuments_.review: *Updated Review*I was expecting to play a fun platformer for about 5 hours. I was not expecting an emotional punch to the gut. I am very much not an owl, I'm crying my eyes out. The movement has improved, the gameplay feels tighter, the music is amazing and there is MORE of it. There is honestly so much to love here. This went from being a KZ inspired game to almost surpassing it in my eyes.The bugs are fixed, there is SO MUCH more content since I last played in 2022. Id say the only blemish on the game is the second level as its a little too restrictive with its movement. 9.5/10 questioning if anything is real.*Old Review*Though I've only played for around 2 hours, I've gone through the entire game. There is a good amount of content here for what it is and more to come. Clearly inspired by Katana Zero, this game focuses much harder on the movement aspect of these games to great effect. Highly recommend the pick up if you are looking for something similar. There are some complaints I have though, the main one being polish. While this game looks and plays great, there are some things that become apparent when you start playing. The settings don't reset when reloading the game. Some of the grammar in the dialog is messed up, probably an easy fix. Your grappling hook reel-in is tied to the up arrow, however if you put jump on the up arrow as I do in my platformers, it can cause some annoying movement, reeling in when you meant to jump and continue your momentum. Also speed-run mode, probably what will be the main draw for games like this, still displays cutscenes and dialog and can even bug out to the point of turning the screen completely black. This is early access though and I expect that these bugs and features will be ironed out for the final release.As for the rest of it? Movement is smooth and flowing when the level allows for it, you can get REALLY fast here. Some of the levels are worse than others, requiring you to stop and wait for something before continuing on. Mostly a personal gripe, I like flowing and continuous movement in my games. And the OST, it slaps. Where can I find this music, I need it.Overall: 7/10 Very solid platformer with a good story and crisp movement. Some things need tuning but when the game is released, I suspect this will be an 8-9/10. Easily worth the money.

_childDocuments_.review: People raved about this game so I gave it a go.It's not worth it, unless you're a speedrunner maybe. The main gameplay is using a grappling hook to move between platforms floating in midair, surrounded by a city that is somehow connected to the platforms. I have no idea how, since most of the platforms don't show any use outside where the player steps.The main gameplay loop is, for the first part of the game, OK. Midgame a whole bunch of obstacles increasingly bog this loop down and it becomes less fun. It's like they took the worst parts of super mario and stuffed them into the game. Pacing is unheard of, levels go on for a comical duration, and it's just the same puzzles over and over again. All of this makes it seem like the developers have become creatively bankrupt; as if these mechanics were the last thing they could possible find to add to this game.Combat exists but should have been left out as it again just drags the main experience down. It also completely stops momentum as you can't exit most combat areas before killing off every enemy, and they respawn. Just annoying tedium for no reason other than extending the duration of the levels it seems.Story is well below par, but has a weird twist just past the tutorial that I guess a lot of people latch onto. Forgettable otherwise.I wanted to say something nice about this game other than this, but I don't really have anything that would be justified. I'm not even through the game as I'm currently stuck at a boss that requires an ability that has been used perhaps once before, and that the developer seemingly doesn't care to tell me about again. Ultimately, this, combined with the bloat of mechanics that the game just seems to push onto the player, the experience is just less and less enjoyable as the game goes on.

_childDocuments_.review: Having just finished this game, I need to get all my thoughts out now before they leave me.Sanabi is an absolute gem of a game that EVEN more people should be talking about than there already are. From the beautiful pixel art to the jamming OST to the incredible story, this game was a treat from start to finish. I bought this game on a whim because "Oh wow, this pixel art looks great AND it's all about movement???" I was sold on that alone. But it turns out there was SO MUCH MORE to it than just that. As I got further and further into the story I realized how much it really captured my attention. There were points where I stopped playing to take a break only to hop right back on just because I felt like I needed to see more from the story. Also you can VERY EASILY tell how much you're improving as the game progresses. Learning the controls is incredibly simple and of course as you go through each level you improve, but the stark difference in skill that have towards the end compared to when you start is such a satisfying realization to have. The feeling of "Wow, that was me, I did that" is at an all time high with this game and the praise that I give it is not close to enough to what it actually deserves. 10/10 game

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely powerful and unique game. Gameplay wise it's a momuntum/grapple based platformer that feels like if you distilled down the good bits of the bionic commando reboot and made it retro. It functions extremely smoothly for the most part (there are a few bugs with controller that have you grappling onto the wrong side of thin vertical platforms and causing some problems) and is extremely high intensity and speed. The final run is probably one of the most purely *fun* things I've done in gaming for a while. Story/art wise, it's just a straight up masterpiece. I legitimately cried over it, and the Korean-sci-fi backgrounds are absolutely gorgeous. Great humour and characters, and one of the few times that I've seen a twist get extended and played with so masterfully. It's one of the few games I'd actually recommend playing twice, once on the normal mode for the story, where you take advantage of the health and just damage boost/move fast to play to that strength, and once on the legend difficulty, because the limitations there make it feel like an entirely different game.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: - after completing all the content currently in the game on normal difficulty, I can *heartily* recommend SANABI - even at full price! Solid action platformer with fluid movement, surprisingly engaging story (very much looking forward to future chapters), and some amazing art/music direction. Minimal cons, really just nitpicks. Buy this game! Pros:- Good Music - Great Art - Fluid Movement - some of the best of any platformer i've played - Interesting (enough) Combat - A story which was fine in the beginning, but really hooked me into the building story-arc by the time i reached the end - it left me wanting more in a good way. Lots to look forward to as more content is added to the game!!!- 2 good bossfights - inclusion of a speedrun mode is really nice, for those who want *everything* timed. and getting rid of cutscenes for future playthroughs- the protagonist has real motives and, despite his somewhat limited dialogue, acts like a fairly real person. written concisely i think would be a good term - the deuteragonist was a little annoying at first, but definitely grew on me- there was a really really cool moment towards the end of the currently playable content, i won't spoil it but i made me jump a little lol Cons: - 1 bad bossfight. middle child is always neglected, i guess? it's not really *offensively* bad, just not nearly as good as the other two. - Some of the stage gimmicks are too easy - the higher difficulties don't change the game enough, they just make you health progressively lower. in retrospect i could've even put the game on the highest difficulty (where you have 1 hp) and only really struggled with a handful of platforming sections, and one of the bosses in particular- there's only one save slot atm- this means in order to play the timed portions of the tutorial you need to erase current progress ( a way to access these in the main menu maybe?)- some of the signs and notes in cutscenes are untranslated from korean (as this is a brand new korean indie studio, i give them a lot of slack in this department, the english TL of the story is better than a lot of native-english game writing these days)- some of the audio settings are too loud by default, even with my system audio being pretty quiet, and some of the audio effects are disproportionately tuned (footsteps on a steel floor in a cutscene being louder than some of the gunshots right after). not a massive deal though, only broke my immersion once at the very beginning, and after i tuned audio sliders all was well.Overall i'd say the majority of my Cons are nitpicks, and i purposefully kept a lot of what i *couldve* praised in the Pros concise or absent so as to not spoil some of the great fun in this game. Very very much looking forward to what the team at WONDER POTION do with this project next!

_childDocuments_.review: Sanabi is a tight and engrossing experience comprised of an incredibly fast and fun gameplay based around a grappling hook as main movement mechanic, and an intriguing story that can tug at your heartstrings if you let your guard down. All of this delivered on a package full of nice sound design and amazing art in the form pixel art, having some impressively expressive characters for the amount of pixels they carry.All of this not having touched the hardest difficulty or the speedrunning mode unlocked after beating the game which would add more hours to the playtime, but even the first playthrough of the game is well worth it.The combat is either incredibly fluid or a tad clunky by the nature of the game and the enemies, but even having played at the veteran difficulty nothing felt too annoying or unfair, nothing that would blemish the experience enough to be worthy of comment. The only thing that was close is the design of the playable character, while cool looking and well animated it looks off in comparison to the rest of the game aesthetics, feels like one of the very first things ever designed and keep all the way through. While not too damming I often felt like it didn't belong in the game world for some reason, but I get it, it is a really cool design.And remember, getting to the End is not whats important.

_childDocuments_.review: SANABI, in under 12 hours, has become one of my favourite games.Within minutes, it thoroughly hooked me onto its story and its gameplay- both of which are wonderfully executed and ramp up over time. It's a blast to play, and breathtaking to look at; its beautiful art and animation never failed to enamour me no matter what I did or where I went. Music is also bangin'.Gameplay's just downright awesome, especially when you feel yourself improving at it and the mechanics. It's simple, solid, and fluid. And the story. Yes, it's the main focus, and there are definitely a  of cutscenes and dialogue, but the way it's done so genuinely, paired with the music and artwork, makes it all worth it and interesting... if you're willing to get into it. Getting to the end isn't what's important.All in all, top tier gem of a game. 10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok so I changed my mind.This game's biggest draw and most interesting mechanic is it's biggest weakness. It's style is fantastic, it's pixel art is brilliant and the backgrounds are stunning, there are some more detailed shorts which are beautiful and super impressive, a lot of the playable set pieces are super cool and inspired.The story only picked up for me right at the end even though there's a bit too many cut-scenes for my taste that're a bit too long, ultimately I think the story is told extremely well, there's a lot of on the nose foreshadowing but a lot of more gentler stuff, the game guides your thought process in a super interesting way, when I thought I was being clever it was because the game was slipping something else past me, by the time I got to the twist I'd already figured it out so I wasn't shocked but it was revealed expertly and impactfully, I appreciate how layered it was and how it was told to me. The ending is fantastic, they utilise the art brilliantly, there are some really artistic shots and everything is wrapped up neatly, concisely and emotionally. Unfortunately Sanabi's biggest failure is the gameplay.The chain claw is a cool idea, manoeuvring during free platform sections can be super fun but anytime there's an enemy involved it stalls and this is the most egregious in boss fights. You can't react to anything, you have no defensive options except for 'move' and generally that is restricted to arcs that cross the line of fire you're attempting to avoid anyway, the closest thing you have to a defensive option is something you can only do after you get hit, you move out the way a bit a maintain speed, but you still keep the damage you took meaning it's still all too easy for enemy rooms to combo you to death anyway, there is no simple way to move in a straight direction out of the way unless you take the time to aim, grapple and then input an extra button to pull yourself to the wall and it's detrimental to the game, later in the game you unlock a self-proclaimed 'air dash' which I thought would fulfil this role but it doesn't, you can only dash to objects that you've locked on to. This brings me to the next downfall, the enemy lock-on. It's inconsistent at best and restricts you from precise movement, it's impossible to grapple near an enemy without locking onto them, as that's how you attack, and this stings in boss fights where you have infrequent grapple points with enemies that counter your attack, if you want to grapple near them you'll automatically lock onto them and take unavoidable damage. The bosses themselves I also have a huge issue with, without any proper ways to react to oncoming damage, combined with just how long the boss fights last they start to feel like a slog that stands out from the rest of the game. I truly believe if there was some kind of skill based dedicated parry or dodge button that allowed you to directly interact with and reasonably avoid attacks the game would be far more enjoyable and fit much better the fast-paced category that it's clearly going for. The gameplay damages the game greatly but to some extent the cut-scenes that used to be unbearably long became a welcome reprieve and it was worth struggling from A to B to find out what happens next. This team is really promising, their storytelling is stellar and the art is stunning and I want to see more from them in the future

_childDocuments_.review: This is a suprisingly innovative game that has a pretty decent story it tells you through the 7-10 hours it will occupy you. The music is great, the sprites and animations look good and the atmosphere it tries to capture is also superb. The strong point is the story. You do get a sense where its headed a bit early on but nevertheless its quite captivating and surprisingly dark too. Its a shame the Ending went for more of an emotional explosion rather than delivering what the characters actually wanted. Its still satisfying and really well told for a game like this.The gameplay is very innovative as you swing around with your hook-arm using the momentum you gain to keep going faster and faster. I really recommend playing it with Mouse and Keyboard. The Controller works too but its not as precise. There are a few hiccups in the gameplay, where you just die in certain areas because of the way your character moves when he takes damage and sometimes there is so much going on its easy to spin out of control really fast, meaning you either die quickly or take a lot of damage. Luckily the game is very generous with its checkpoint system. If you parkour around and it goes well, its really fun. I am sure there are some people out there that try to master this and then the game is a sight to behold.Outside of a few hit glitches and some minor spelling mistakes the game runs flawlessly.Definitelly recommended, its a steal for this price.

_childDocuments_.review: I have already played this game through someone in the past, but bought it for my account because it's simply an underrated masterpiece. Sanabi has some of the most compelling, emotional, well thought out, and engaging story that I have ever played in a video game. Alongside the story, there is absolutely stunning pixel art that is followed by music that always sets the mood very well. Sanabi is a very story heavy game, which in turn can make the pacing of the game a bit weird at times, such as a few min of gameplay being followed by 5 min of dialog, but it shouldn't be a problem for those who get drawn in due to the engaging nature of the story. As a platforming game, the combat is fairly straight forward with fast-paced, fluid movement and also does a very fine job of making the player feel as if they are truly playing as the main character once they get the hang of the movement and the environment. I don't normally place games on such grand of a scale, but Sanabi touched me emotionally in a way that only a few games ever have. While no game is without its flaws, such as the pacing in areas and some translation errors here and there, I still believe the game is more than worth it. So yes, I HIGHLY recommend trying out this game for yourself.
_childDocuments_.name: SANABI

_childDocuments_.review: I went in expecting something similar to Katana Zero, but it's so much more than that. Saying Sanabi is a Katana Zero clone would be a huge disservice to this game. To me, both are exceptional gems.But before I continue to sing my praises to this game, what exactly is Sanabi?Well, in this action platformer game, you play as a retired veteran with a simple mission, which is to hunt an entity called "Sanabi". To do this, you will use your chain hook prosthetic arm to get around a city called Mago. This weapon can also be used to hook yourself to the enemies, destroying them in the process.This grappling hook mechanism means that you will spend most of your time in the air, going from one platform to another, from one enemy to another, from one boss to another. And when done right, it feels oh so good, especially because of the tight movement. Makes you feel unstoppable, and it gets the adrenaline pumping!I said "when done right", because at first, I struggled getting used to the grappling hook gameplay and gamepad controls. Because not only you can hook the enemy, you can boost yourself, slow down time, jump, and so much more. But overtime, I learned to get good and finally experienced that flow state.Surprisingly, even with this addicting gameplay formula, my favorite part of Sanabi is still the story. Without spoiling anything, you will be confused at first because of the mysteries surrounding Sanabi and Mago are pretty complicated, but once you connect the dots, it will be mind blowing. At least mine did, that's for sure. It makes me want to replay the whole game instantly to see all the hints I missed.Not only mind blowing, Sanabi's story has a lot of heart thanks to its characters. Mind you, Sanabi doesn't have too many characters, since you spend most of your time with a hacker girl named Mari, who's helping you find Sanabi, and her robot companion Mufin.While Mari might be too talkative to some, I found her character very charming, I really enjoyed her funny personality and antics, and I think the game definitely won't be the same without Mari.I was too invested in the story of Sanabi, the retired veteran, and Mari. By the end of the game, I was left sobbing my eyes out, heck, I instantly went to write a review, three years after I wrote my previous review.All of these positive points, combined with the epic soundtracks and the eye catching pixel art, makes the game a complete package worth checking out, even in full price. Scratch that, I insist YOU to try out this game if you love some fast paced action gameplay and heart tugging storytelling.With that being said, to Wonder Potion a.k.a the developers, I'll be looking forward to your future games! Doesn't matter if it will start as an Early Access product again, I WILL be there!

_childDocuments_.review: Up there with Blasphemous as the most gorgeous pixel art game I've ever played. My 1440p monitor tends to blow up pixel games when I play them full-screened, so it's pretty easy to spot imperfections or shoddy artwork, but Sanabi was routinely beautiful. The animations are slick as can be, and backgrounds are especially stunning. There was a surprising amount of lore for the setting, and the artwork really sells you on Mago City being a lived-in setting. The mood and atmosphere are all there.And that's just the aesthetics! The gameplay is smooth as butter too. At its core, Sanabi is really just  and is focused on making you feel like the cyborg equivalent of a Formula 1 driver. The platforming is the track and the grapple mechanics are your gas. It's kinetic and exhilarating while remaining intuitive enough to never feel overwhelming. You'll never catch yourself in a bad or unwinnable situation because the momentum from swinging around is such that you almost always pivot on the fly. The gimmicks introduced in each chapter always feel organic and never feel designed to frustrate you. The mechanics you get enhance your ability to sail through sections of the game without making things less difficult. I really can't complain about any of it.There's also an unexpected-yet-welcome emphasis on story in Sanabi. With a nearly 1:1 ratio between gameplay and cutscenes, you'll be spending just as much time with Mari and the General as you will swinging around. I know that sounds like an absurd amount of talking for such a fast-paced game, but I think it does wonders for making each segment of the game feel memorable by offering frequent breaks. Sanabi handles its plot like Metal Gear Solid, trying to get you engrossed in the setting and working it into every area, mechanic, and boss. The story's an integral part of the game's pacing, so it never feels superfluous or out-of-sync.However, i don't agree with all the praise that the story itself gets. Without spoiling anything, some of the twists are pretty silly, and the plot ties itself in knots trying to get some of them to work. The translation varies from scene-to-scene, ranging from surprisingly well-localized to extremely rough. Overall, though, it's a pretty great action movie experience. Just don't go in expecting some tour de force.If you have any interest in Sanabi's core concept, or if you like Katana Zero, I think it's an easy purchase. For 14.99 USD, you'll get all the grapple hook action you could possibly want, plus a cheesy action movie. To me, that's a pretty good deal.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, the game is fun but it has a lot of very un-fun things about it. Pros: Swinging around feels great most of the time and you feel very in-control of your movement. Nice, fun platforming in general, I just wish it was a little more difficult.Cons: I don't really care about the story, so for me it had WAAAAY too many cutscenes, unskippable dialog, and slow pointless RP walking when I just wanted to get back to swinging around. My other big issue is that some of the "puzzles" have a very tight window to complete (which isn't a big deal once you know what to do) but it can be frustrating when you have to replay them multiple times because there's no way for you to know what's coming next and if you fail, you have to start over. Just zooming out a bit would honestly help this so you have at least some amount of time to react and don't automatically fail a section multiple times because you didn't predict what the next hurdle was going to be.

_childDocuments_.review: The story at the beginning felt like a turnoff with the tacky dialogue and awkward plot setup- thinking that it doesn't run deep, but it soon picks up steam and becomes a lot bigger than it initially seems.Once the  unfolds, the game takes a completely different approach to telling the story. A lot of the details will then be left to interpretation, which can suck to those who are seeking for a more linear/straightforward storyline. Personally, it was very satisfying to piece it all together, though I can't tell if the experience will be just as good if you decide to ignore itThe end is indeed emotionally heavy, compared to how the game started; which is pretty evident from the amount of reviews of people having their eyes bawled out. It becomes an emotional roller coaster not just because of how it conducts its plot (twists), but also because of its contriving themes that are eventually revealedThe movement takes time to get used to (especially with how limited it is at the start), but I find the level design to be more on the lenient side. I was able to zip through most of the obstacles with ease, but that's because I've had a hand with platformers. Fortunately, there are accessibility options for the less skill-inclined or if you want a more casual experience.Admittedly, the combat is next-to-nothing in terms of depth, and I'd say that it's probebly the weakest aspect here. The game does not focus for it to be its own thing, and instead integrates it to be a part of movement. With that being said, the bosses still find a way to be interesting even if you aren't able to attack most of them directlyOverall, it's a great ride for what short playtime it offers compared to most games, and it's definitely an odd but welcome spinoff to Katana ZERO. I wonder what made them ditch the katana for a grapple hook though...

_childDocuments_.review: What I wanted out of this game was a fun, fast paced game with tight controls and some interesting puzzles based on physics and maintaining momentum. A decent story would be good too. What I got was a game with a good (not groundbreaking or anything) story and game play that in the final chapter I just turned down to easy because I didn't care any more and just wanted it to end. There are tons of other reviews praising the story, so I'll just give some quick thoughts on it. It was good, if not fairly predicable half way through the game. The developer put some foreshadowing in to give the player some "oh, that's why..." moments but they are a bit too plain. When the big twists hit, they're not really twists but more "called it" moments. The issue I had with the game is the part that I wanted to love the most. Swinging through the levels, trying to maintain your momentum and reach that next screen. Maybe I'm just aching for more Celeste, but this game doesn't have it. The physics aren't great. I would really have loved to have seen the chain hit a corner or wall and have it react properly. Perhaps I was asking too much here, which is fair. Which isn't too much of an expectation is the controls working properly. I lost count of the number of times I died because my chain got stuck on the other side of a wall and wouldn't release. At one point I dropped the controller and ran my hand back and forth on my keyboard. Nothing would let it release.The levels themselves are also uninspired. I doubt I could skip to a random youtube let's play and see a level and think "oh! I remember that one." They're all pretty much the same renditions of 3 or 4 tile sets with slightly varied positioning of platforms and hazards. Overall, if you want to experience the story I'd suggest watching a let's play or wait for a sale. If you played the demo/beta/whatever that was and thought "yeah, I'd like more of this thanks!" like I did, then understand you've basically played what the game has on offer.
