_childDocuments_.review: I saw when the Katana ZERO developer was gonna play a lot of different games akin to his own on stream, as to push more publicity. I had never heard of it, so when I saw it was going to be one of the games showcased I wanted to check it out beforehand....I'm very disappointed.I don't care about the story nor the characters; so when there's like a fricking 1,5 hour elongated never-ending exposition dump of every single character ever in the intro, then that's just a HUGE turn-off. I'm not given reason to like any of the characters, and I prematurely already don't care for them due to the sour taste in my mouth from its horrible pacing & storytelling; so at such point why should I? The only reason I should ever care about any of these characters is because my main-character would, but he doesn't even do that very much. He shrugs most characters off or don't care about them. ??????????It's like God of War 2018 Kratos all-over again, but at least here it didn't ruin a previously good character.And the cutscenes are WAYYYYYYYYYYY TOOOOOOOOO LOONG and WAYYYYY TOO MANY OF THEM. I swear it feels like 90% of my game time are just cutscenes or dialogue. I only learnt about the ability to skip cutscenes like half-way through. OK. But then you skip the cutscene, which then leads you into another cutscene, which leads you into the next cutscene, which then leads you into a new cutscene; which you can't skip for some reason??? And then you're loaded into even further dialogue for some reason, and then even more........... This is unacceptable.The tutorial for this game goes on and on and on and on and on and on and on and on. I can't believe I've only played this game for 4 hours, as the tutorial alone felt like 16 hours in total. It was abhorrent! Not a fan.You can't just give like 80 rooms or whatever just meant to tutor you in a row with bare-minimum pace shifts. It's just parkour, parkour, parkour, parkour, parkour, parkour, parkour... The combat alone only gets introduced like an hour in........... WHAT?! HOW?! This is embarrassing. I just don't understand whatsoever.And even the combat feels broken. It's so easy, and yet so mushy. Playing on 'Hard' was actually embarrassing.The entire combat system is just bad in execution. The slingshot grapple-hook arm is so wimpy, and I feel like I weigh as much as a feather, as I have no control of my movement if I'm hanging still. I can't rock myself back 'n' forth anymore, and when I do have momentum it feels really awkward. When I loosen my grip on platforms there goes a small second before my character actually does it, it's weird. It completely ruins my precision & timing.And when I'm a fast-paced, complex character that can fly all-over the room then ultimately why are my enemies robots that are locked still & unable to move? They pose no threat. It's like a battle between One Punch Man & a pebble; where's the excitement??The sprite work is somewhere between 'good' & 'awful'. There are times where the game looks good, I won't deny that. However it is immensely dumbed down by the sheer amount of times it does not. A lot of the times the background is extremely flat, stale, boring, empty, and lifeless.The art-style is really inconsistent. There are times where background/foreground items have a black outline, there are times when they don't. There are times when the animations are smooth, there are times when they aren't. There are times when the game is really bright, there are times where it's too dark. There are times where the game is too barren looking, there are times it's too flooded with busy details.It feels like 700 different people with truly unique & different art-styles & visions tried to work on the game, and all with poor management & quality control.It feels like the game wants to look like 60 different games at the same time.And I swear to god some of the animations are frame by frame copied straight from Katana ZERO.I'm shocked, I didn't know it could be this bad.It feels like it was made by fan of Katana ZERO & Celeste; but completely misunderstood or never even comprehended what made either of those aforementioned games 'good' or 'fun'. The inspirations are hefty.I'm completely staggered by how bad this all is.I like some of the music though.

His main weapon is the grappling hook that lets you move like spiderman, and the game takes this one mechanic and makes it feel like an arsenal of tools. Every boss fight genuinely feels unique, and the progression of unlockable abilities is actually very useful and makes you be and feel faster and more powerful.Art and Animation - 10/10Its some of the best pixel art I've ever seen and the best pixel art I've seen in a game. Just watch the trailer again-just look at the city billboard background spread at the start, look at how many different environments there are in the trailer and how they all feel like different environments, look at how realistic the falling down stairs part looks, just look at how fluid the combat looks and how monstrous those boss looking things are. That's what the whole game is like, its super impressive how natural the animation looks especially with how few pixels they have to work with on the characters.Music and sound - 11/10My ears exploded from peak. The music is absolutely incredible. Disclaimer: it is a different style and genre from the trailer music, but just as epic, and it harmonizes with the game setting perfectly. I will never find a single bad song in the soundtrack, and the boss themes are the best things ever. _childDocuments_.review: (Mild spoilers; no more than what's mentioned in the game's description)SANABI deserves a lot more recognition. I wouldn't have heard of this game at all if it weren't for a friend recommending it to me, and the game is definitely good enough to warrant a lot more popularity than it currently has.At first glance, SANABI offers very satisfying 2D platforming with lots of charming pixel art and an exhilarating soundtrack. Moving around in this game is very intuitive; rarely will you run into a situation where the controls don't react like you expect they would. As the game progresses, the various things you can do with your robot arm make navigating levels a lot of fun. The relatively short game has a surprising amount of variety to its obstacles and enemies: levels will switch things up in quite refreshing ways. What I liked the most were the bosses, all of which require quick thinking and creative maneuvering to beat.What the game description doesn't advertise very well is its highly engaging story. SANABI devotes quite a lot of time to dialogue, without breaking up the pace of the gameplay too much. By the end of the 8-10 hour experience, you'll come out knowing quite a lot about the world of SANABI and the characters that inhabit it. English-speaking players may encounter some awkward translation issues: the English version suffers from grammar and wording issues, making the game's dialogue read a tad stiff. Despite the language barrier however, SANABI's story shines through as a unique and compelling take on classic cyberpunk ideas.With a setting full of robot arms, mega-corporations, and flying droids, SANABI manages to tell a surprisingly personal story. Whereas a lot of cyberpunk settings tend to gravitate toward narratives about inequality and power, SANABI delivers, through its grizzled veteran protagonist, a heart-wrenchingly intimate story about guilt, loss, and the way our pasts can define who we are, against the backdrop of an oppressive, technocratic dystopia that threatens to destroy it all. Unfortunately, this framing means that significant questions about how the world at large functions are left unanswered, but the important emotional beats are good enough to overshadow some of these concerns. In my estimation, the ending probably contains the best writing in the game: the dénouement is genuinely quite touching.I don't play too many platformers, but I'd play a lot more of them if they all had as effective a story as this one. SANABI is a very good example of a small-scale indie game with very captivating gameplay that is dedicated to give the player a good story along with good gameplay, and anyone itching for a good story ought to give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: The screenshots make it look like this game is "Korean knockoff Katana Zero", and while the first 2 hours of gameplay feel like Katana Zero x Super Meatboy, the last 3 hours do EVERYTHING right. Gameplay gets insanely frantic. All abilities become totally overpowered once mastered, and enemies scale almost perfectly. Bossfights are heavy hitters, enemies are diverse and interesting, level design is great too. The plot has interesting twists that pull on your heartstrings as hard as Korean dramas always attempt. There is one incredibly corny dating-sim slide that totally ruins the peak, but, again, to be expected by Korean media. I did enjoy the story, mostly because the pixel art and graphics are insane. There is so much life in these 10 pixel wide characters, that the cutscenes turned into the highlight of the game for me.This game is genuinely great. Worth the 10, maybe even full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Most games are fake, and most reviews are fake as well. Sanabi is subversive, therefore it starts out fake, but at a certain point in the story it becomes real. Therefore I must attempt to write a review for this game, despite the fact that there exists no guarantee that a video game review finds its intended audience.To put it simply, the reason to play Sanabi isn't in the steam description and must be given indirectly. The story of Sanabi involves deep questions which cause it to be a good, authentic, and immersive video game:-What does it mean to be human?-What does it mean to see another as human?-How can you be sure that what you see is reality?-Do memories accurately depict reality?and ideas:-An unfeeling entity that possesses an automatic and unfocused drive to kill-The purpose of one's entire life depending on a single independent concept that, taken by itself, is meaningless-love-and so on and so onSanabi's story is subversive, much like Omori's, which is why the above text seems absurd compared to the summary given on the steam page. However, this is the nature of subversive stories. In short, play the game.

_childDocuments_.review: It's Celeste and Katana Zero's long lost sibling.In all seriousness, if you like either of those games you should play this. Even if you don't you should play this. The pixel art is gorgeous in places. The animation is fluid and expressive despite how small the sprites are. The music is *amazing*. And the story is also incredibly compelling. That's what really hoked me honestly, which is saying something given everything else. There are some translation issues with the script in places and the dialogue can go fast, but everything important in emphasized and clear. It handles the narrative in intelligent ways with a lot of visual story telling. Uses the medium well. And it really benefits from a second play-through, there's a lot of depth you can pick up.Oh, have I not talked about the gameplay? It's good. Really good. The grapple-hooking and hookshot speedy gameplay is smooth and clear and clean. You never feel uncontrolled and while it can get difficult it's always clear where you messed up. I'm not into speedrunning personally, but the game has a whole mode for that specifically. And it is one of the few games that made me want to play it start to finish right after beating it.Please buy this game and play it. The devs deserve our support.

_childDocuments_.review: AFTER 4 HOURS OF PLAYING:I'll recommend this because it clearly has a lot of love put into it from the mechanics to the pixel art and animations. But I'd be lying if I said the pacing didn't bother me. The story is decently intriguing to me, but nothing super interesting, so I am definitely not happy continuously having like 2-3 minutes of gameplay only to be met with 7-9 minutes of cutscenes where you can already tell what kind of conversation the characters will have and which I can't even sit back and watch but instead have to click through each and every time. Up until the point I'm at I found the story beats a bit predictable too, which doesn't help. Its not atrocious, but I really haven't found the story as amazing as other reviews have made it out to be. The gameplay on the other hand ... is really fun! But the gameplay sections are simply too short. And that really breaks my enjoyment of this. I'll see what the rest of the game has to offer.EDIT AFTER FINISHING: After finishing the game, I am more than happy to say that the game has completely clowned on me in its latter third. The story really picked up and definitely had my attention by the end of it all. I still stand by the opinion that the game suffers a bit from its pacing especially in its earlier parts, but once you get into the meat of the story, its great! Definitely something to look into if you like some good platforming and an intriguiging story,

_childDocuments_.review: (I played the full game now; I'm changing this review to positive and will write more details later. The rest of the message is the old review)-----(Keep in mind this review was written back in Early Access; I still need to revisit the game to give it a more fair rating and review)I can't, with a light conscience, recommend this game as it is right now, as much as I want to.Keep in mind that the game is in early access, and a lot of what I'll be saying might change for the better; this is exactly why I'm writing this review.First, let's start with the negatives:(-) The cutscenes and dialogues are too frequent, and break the pacing of the game quite a lot. There are dozens of very long cutscenes, many of which don't seem to be necessary.(-) The dialogues have several problems; even in the intro sequence, it's possible to spot moments where text boxes don't seem to match the context, or dialogues don't make sense, at least in English.(-) The translation is incorrect or inaccurate, which adds to the dialogue being bad.(-) The dialogue goes TOO FAST during action sequences. I think dialogue during action sequences is great, but having it be unreadable is just frustrating and not fun; I had to pause during my playthrough during these dialogues, when I cared about it.(-) The story is intriguing, which makes this all the more frustrating; you really want to take the game seriously, but these problems make it so that it's hard to.(-) The game doesn't really explain to you about clockwise and counter-clockwise movement with the dash. Although players will eventually figure it out, I think with the amount of tutorials, the game could have told me that as well.(-) There was some untranslated Korean text in a few cutscenes. It's understandable with the scenery, but I think it would do good just to have some subtitles, you know?(-) Some areas seem very empty or incomplete, bland, with nothing new. I think these would be a good opportunity for the game to put some of the exceeding dialogue, instead of cramming all of it into a million cutscenes. Namely, I can see the "plan" sequences working out during these more empty parts.(-) There were some opportunities lost with gameplay. I think this would be a perfect game to play with more momentum mechanics and bunny hopping. Making that easier and accessible for the player would be a good idea. Instead, touching the ground while attached to a hook just makes you lose all momentum. Also, retracting to your hook does not make you keep your speed when you cancel the retraction, and I think that's a big lost opportunity.(-) The parts with throwing the enemies into the laser just felt a lot more boring than the idea sounded like.(-) There are no secrets and no real hidden easter eggs or anything like that. At least none that I could find. I feel like this game would greatly benefit from having several collectibles and hidden areas, to explore everything you can do with the tech of the hook.( ? ) This might be just me, but I didn't understand health and checkpoints very well. I've finished the game in about 3 hours or so, on hard mode, and had about 2 or 3 deaths; but I thought I was supposed to die after 2 hits? It semeed like I had 4 health instead, despite playing on "hard", where I was supposed to die in 2 hits.Now let's talk about the good points:(+) The gameplay is fluid and satisfying; it's a character that is "fun to play as". The hook movement just works, and having a game based solely on that is a good plus.(+) The artstyle is beautiful; it reminds me of Katana Zero a lot. There is even a Katana Zero reference inside the game (time samurai, lmao)(+) Add this to having several animations for the characters. Characters have many different poses and expressions, and it seems like it never ends. Specially, Mari and the Daughter were really adorable during the cutscenes.(+) The screen transitions feel smooth! I like that a lot in the game.(+) It has a good sense of humor in the dialogue. I feel like some jokes drag on for too long, but in general, it's likeable and I did laugh a few times.(+) The music is good! Not phenomenal, but it was nice to listen to.(+) The story is intriguing, and it did make me a bit emotional. Although the beginning is so positive and wholesome, that you know exactly what's going to happen after.Overall, this game needs little to be an amazing game, but it's important to let devs know about the problems with it.As the game keeps getting updated, I'll keep playing it, and I'll update my review when I can and when I think the game is in a better state.If you want to try it out yourself to see what I'm talking about, and perhaps just feel that sick gameplay, I do recommend the game; I just can't tell anyone to try playing this game for a fun and enjoyable experience.

_childDocuments_.review: The immediate appeal of SANABI is the satisfying hook-swing platforming and combat, though an understated yet essential part is the rich choreography and sound design. The ability to read emotion through subtle looks, shifting feet and a hand landing on the railing, animated clearly with intent to be readable in this limited resolution, is a work of art in itself. The world feels much more immersive through the attention of detail in sound design and controller rumble - walking on metallic floors, a descending elevator coming to a stop, the shuffle of clothing as you turn around.There are some strange parts of the English translation that doesn't read as natural or clear as it could be, it'd be nice to have in-world text translated, and some platforming gaps and dangers could be better telegraphed (there are few too many examples where the player is expected to drop into what seems like void to make progress, without clear signs of where the next platform or wall may be).While some of the music does not have a distinct identity or catchy melody, there are some standout pieces of music that matches the tone and mood of the scene super well, especially when it's written for the cinematics choreography!The variety in the boss battles are very appreciated, though one of the early chapters feels like it goes on for too long and the scenery design can become dull with time.

A beautiful experience from start to end.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh christ. Y'know, this game was an odd experience for me. A lot of people compare this to Katana Zero, which just from the store page and the first few hours I can see. Katana Zero is absolutely right... but completely unfair nonetheless. Admittedly, the first half of the game felt a little funny -- it had the feeling of a game that was just the slightest bit... something. Something felt a little off. Not sure what it was, but I could feel it nonetheless. In most games, that feeling is a bad omen, usually stemming from iffy game design -- which always gets worse over the course of the game. An odd plot point here, an unclear cut from cutscene to gameplay there... it was completely benign at the time - again, I couldn't even put my finger on what it was - but I had seen many a promising game fall apart at the goal post.Not Sanabi.I'm obviously not saying anything about the ending. All I'm going to say is that the game got me. It got me GOOD. For all my subconscious and conscious gripes about nitpicky nothings... I got got HARDER than I've EVER gotten got in my l i f e.This game is a love letter to katana zero and so much more. It feels a little funny even calling it that to begin with. It has more than earned it's own identity -- it's own soul -- in my eyes. Please, toss a couple bucks the dev's way and let it do the same for you. You won't regret it.(p.s. if you think a cutscene has gotten stuck, try moving around. for all of it's beauty and tact, the game still does have it's eccentricities :p)

_childDocuments_.review: This was one of the greatest games I've ever played. Probably the most fluid and fun movement mechanics I've ever seen in a 2D platformer, amazing boss fights, incredible music, the pixel art is probably the best I've ever seen in a video game and the story is one of the most emotional and impactful I've ever experienced. Game was about 9 hours long for me on Hard difficulty and the quality stays high that whole time, there's no point where it drops off, which is insane given the quality of the animation in every scene. It has a ton of wit and charm, I genuinely love this game. All of that AND it has a grappling hook. Do yourself a favor and just buy the game as soon as you physically can

_childDocuments_.review: Sanabi is as satisfying to play as it looks, boldly making another case for the ol' question: "Does a grappling hook make every game better?". In the case of this cyberpunk platformer, the answer is yes. Drawing heavy visual and storytelling inspiration from the fantastic Katana: Zero, Sanabi is a story about transhumanism, capitalism, trauma, and family. While in some cases the anti-capitalist nature of the story comes off as ham-fisted especially as it conflicts with its seemingly pro-militarist narrative, the game is at all times tongue-in-cheek with it's delivery of this message (there is a painting of Elon Musk in one of the levels). Aside from thematic criticism, the writing in Sanabi is occasionally muddied by what is clearly haphazard translation from Korean to English, but this is a criticism specific to the English version and I can't speak for other versions of the game. Overall I thought the writing was very good, with good dramatic and comedic timing, so this is more of a nitpick than anything. I highly recommend this game for people looking for a fast-paced platformer with a good story, good art, and satisfying movement mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: Very good game. Bionic Commando + Katana Zero had a beautiful baby with major feels. There is one minor con for me though* Tons of chase sequences (game feels like you are running from something like 80% of the time). There is almost always a sense of urgency. You rarely get a moment to just take breather and enjoy the swinging mechanics. I suppose that's due to the linear nature of the game. You are always moving forward to the next goal.* Sometimes when I saved the game and came back to this another day I didnt know which direction to go. I'd often find myself going the wrong way but not sure how they could have addressed this one easily. Luckily, I of course found a walkthrough online and when I got lost- I'd reference it to figure out which way to go. I suppose another alternative would have been to not put the game down til I'm at a good stopping point (instead of the middle of the level).That's the only negatives I can think of. Ran great on both my Steam deck and home PC. I highly recommended this one

The first 3 chapters are unbearable considering that players who try the game should stick around if their first experience is good but in this case the game goes from horrible to somehow decent.The grapple is insufferable until you get a skill that improves it but having to wait for that seems crazy to me. _childDocuments_.review: Been awhile since I would highly recommend a game and I would say this would par with Katana Zero (KZ) ratingSo what makes this game really good? The story.  Hands down one of the best I've seen so far.What about the music? Imo, I  its good but it isnt as memorable, unlike KZ counterpart. Gameplay? Uhhh... it is smooth & has some sort of fighting mechanic but it isnt combat heavy like KZ.For me personally, what makes this game disappointing is the lack of bosses as well as too much level design swinging. I would prefer it to be more combat oriented ( more drones to fight ). It gets really REALLY tiring and boring when you have to swing so much in this game. I had to play this game over the span of 3 days because I dont have the patience to do the swinging. However for what is worth, as I said, the story is amazing. So how did I give this game a rating as equal as Katana Zero when there is only the story to be praise for?In terms of animation, both are good but I have to say Sanabi takes it. _childDocuments_.review: TLDR; Pixel GOTY 2023. If you love Pixel games, Rich Plot & amazing music? This is the game for you, especially with that mix of the Cyberpunk aesthetic.IF YOU LIKE THIS GAME, CHECK OUT EASTWARD. BEAUTIFUL PIXEL ART WITH EQUALLY AMAZING  STORY-LINE.I'm an incredibly avid pixel game fan, I'm not just speaking of classic Zelda, castlevania or Stardew. I'm a HUGE sucker for breathtaking pixel art visuals partnered with an amazing story.Honestly the only other game I can recommend that gives the same HUGE impact like this one has got to be Eastward.Ever since I played Eastward back in 2021, I was lost in the void constantly seeking and searching for a game that was honestly the exact same.Breathtaking visuals, banger music, fun mechanics, and very VERY rich storyline. But with the different amount of games (and trust me, I've searched EVERYWHERE), nothing came close to Eastward.Until now.I, very rarely, actually sit down and bulldoze through a game, sometimes I get burnt out and "take a break" for a couple of days and if I end up not wanting to play as much as I first started then I have the tendency to just drop the game until further notice, sometimes never touching it ever again.So the fact this game broke through my standard protocol and I would rush home from work to immediately play and beat it in 3 days since I bought it? My goodness.THAT'S how you KNOW it's a great game."Great" doesn't even COME CLOSE to how MAGNIFICENT this game is.2 years, I was searching for a game similar to one that had increases my standards in pixel gaming and was always disappointed or didn't have my itch scratched, but this one will have to take the spot in my heart.Now I'll be looking for a game that is similar to this one instead. The bar has increased and I'm so excited to see and play more games by Wonder Potion.This game provided such an amazing adventure with so many new and amazing concepts, I can't even begin to describe the PERFECT EXECUTION that this game provided. From the backstory, the hinting, to the plot twists and the end. It all pieced together so amazingly and ughhh I wish I could just forget the game and "WIPE THE DATA" from my memory so that I CAN EXPERIENCE IT AGAIN FOR THE FIRST TIME (sorry for my lame pun).Anyways, this game is  MUST PLAY, ABSOLUTELY. AND AGAIN, IF YOU LIKED THIS GAME, PLAY EASTWARD THANKS BYE.

_childDocuments_.review: So, first off, I imagine a great number of people have done a quick google search and seen Screen Rant's review? To start, disregard it (mostly). SR and GR are garbage companies that force their writers to pump out so much content it's either trash from the start or necessarily shallow.With that said, the second thing to keep in mind is that while this game is definitely inspired by the visual style and setting of Katana Zero...this is most DEFINITELY focused on different genres. I'll give SR credit for one line only, and that's that if you don't get hooked on the narrative of this game? This game is not for you.Sanabi is narrative first, platforming second, and combat a distant third (and in effect, just folded under platforming). In my experience the narrative is subtle, gripping, and very well done...but that's me. To be a little more descriptive without giving everything away...it's themed on family and guilt the most, with a fairly bittersweet ending. That's a pretty broad hook, but it's admittedly not a universal one. And you DO need to enjoy the story, because it definitely takes priority (ie, the action will be frequently interrupted for dialogue).Segueing to the next things...yeah. There are a lot of interruptions. At first most of them didn't seem relevant...but play through the game again knowing the twists, and it's easy to see how nearly every line of dialogue means something. After you complete the game once, I highly recommend playing though at least one more time to revisit all those big and small dialogue moments with new context. It's nice to see how deeply the endings reveals are hinted at and foreshadowed...and while there are a couple of twists you can probably see coming halfway through the game, there are others and the context of others that will probably genuinely take you by surprise.So what about the game that's getting interrupted? Well, it's a chain-shot plat-former with a heavy emphasis on circular arcs and fast movement. It's not the most complicated platformer I've ever played, but it's not a bad one either, and the focus on boosting movement along arcs controlled by the chain is fairly novel for a grappling-hook plat-former. And if you find you really like the game play after you are done with the story (or even before the story if you want partial spoilers I guess)? There's a Speed-Runner mode that removes all dialogue pauses. So replaying the game without the story is absolutely possible.On to my next topic...difficulty. I'll be frank. this game is built around harder difficulty. The check-points are plentiful and well-placed, you aren't going to be replaying more then a minute or two if you screw up. So unless you get stuck on a boss or particularly nasty section? I recommend playing on Veteran difficulty to start. All the mechanics have a decent introductory period, and as long as you aren't on legendary difficulty you can make multiple mistakes before dying (and check-points are both plentiful, and refill your health). Do yourself a favor, play on hard, and have fun getting good enough to zip through the game and around terrain at high speed.Finally, graphics and music. The game is gorgeous, and the back-grounds are highly detailed and beautiful (with two exceptions), and all of them are very distinct. The music is thematic and very good. Not quite the absolute best...but by no means shabby, and it definitely compliments both the game-play and the story (hint hint). As for those exceptions I mentioned? One is the shortest section of the game, a transition from the first chapter to the second. The other is the third major chapter of the game and honestly? You'll have other things to be worrying about then the background being pretty in that part.So what's my final review?Story: 10/10 Beautiful, memorable.Gameplay: 8/10 Not the most complex on it's own, but the game isn't long enough to overstay it's welcome and the mechanics are all tight and synergistic.Graphics: 10/10These are some of the BEST pixel graphics I've seen.Music: 8/10Great and well incorporated.Difficulty: 8*/10I'll be real, I liked it? But if your playing on anything but baby-journalist mode, expect at least a little challenge. And if you ARE playing on easy mode...I could definitely see the game play starting to be more of a slog as you go from sections you can't fail into harder ones where infinite pits WILL send you back. Plus, plat-forming is pretty much the second big pillar of the game. Remove the difficulty from that, and you take a lot of the enjoyment from success, skill to play better, and just adrenaline to enhance the plot beats.On the flip side...this is not the hardest of games. Even on legendary where one mistake is death, enemy and map patterns are all the same, and checkpoints are plentiful. This is NOT the Dark Souls of platforming.Finally...Replay-ability: 6/10 - 10/10Yeah...this is a narrative heavy game. Once you've played it through the first time, there's more to enjoy going back again to see all the little hints and character moments with new context. After THAT though? Yeah, there's not much to be had besides the speed-running scene. I'm torn on this front because there's a solid 'end-point' where pretty much all the little secrets, characterizations, and hints will have been revealed, and after that there's not much to the game besides a basic but well put-together plat-former. On the other-hand, it's a game that actually FINISHES, and it ties up nearly all of it's plot threads in the process (if you pay attention at least). Since playing through once takes around 5-8 hours, doubling that puts you at 10-16 hours game-play for maximum narrative experience. Since the game is only $15 USD, and it does go on sale and bundle with other games occasionally? I'd say it's absolutely worth it, and it'll probably be fun to play again after you put it down for a few months/years. But it isn't close to maximizing time-spent to hours played if that's what your looking for. Though if that is...try looking at rogue-likes, rpgs, and online games. Not story-focused platformers.

_childDocuments_.review: If you haven’t already, look at the other reviews. They’re probably far shorter than this review, more elegant, and, above all, far more humorous. But most of them share the same point:That this game is phenomenal, in so, so many ways, and one that you shouldn’t miss. The grapple hook is done extremely well here, and, with the other mechanics it introduces, makes you feel like a boss as you zip across the screen, killing enemies with crunchy sound effects and a badass soundtrack.The story starts off pretty simple, but, at least for me, it was quite engaging (hey, maybe I don’t have taste, I don’t know). But as it unravels, there are twists that completely table the turns and a satisfying ending that blows your socks off and leaves you hungry for more (yeah, it’s satisfying, but as soon as it ended, I was like “that’s it?”). I heard that the developers were making DLC, which I hope is true, and really hope is coming soon. The characters here are great too, and, throughout a game, you really do feel a connection to them. Mari serves as a great side character, adding humor to the game and strengthening its many serious moments. I do have a minor nitpick with this game, which is when you fall off a cliff or die. When you die, the music completely stops, it pauses for a few seconds, and then you start back at a checkpoint. It kills the flow of the game and I feel it would have been better if the game involved quicker deaths and allow you to get back into it faster (according to my memory, it did this for ONE BOSS FIGHT, and I frankly wish it did this for the whole game. I did do this on normal mode, and didn’t try it on legendary or other difficulties. The pause button also speeds things up a bit, although it still pause the music and you still have to wait).Regardless, this is just one small blemish on a masterfully crafted painting, and it beats out most 59.99 and now 69.99 games out there (for the sweet, sweet price of 14.99).So just get it.

_childDocuments_.review: SANABI is an absolute masterpiece of a game that deserves way more recognition than it currently has. I only discovered this game because of a massive sale from their publisher, and after scrolling through their games, I eventually found this hidden gem. I will try my best to cover the game, with all its strengths and weaknesses.PROS:Gameplay: SANABI's gameplay is amazing in so many ways. The game absolutely nails the platformer genre with the use of the grappling arm, giving the player very satisfying solutions to the levels they clear, all the while maintaining its simplicity. The game's combat emphasizes your mobility by making most combats quick and short. Because of this, the game drives you on to move as fast as you can, and experiment with all of your mobility options, all of which are IMMENSELY satisfying. I can say with confidence that once you get into the zone, the game reaches highs few others, especially those of this genre, can.Soundtrack: SANABI has an absolute banger of a soundtrack. The Synthwave OFT perfectly fits the very modern, cyberpunk aesthetic, and the songs fit each moment very well. The soundtrack of the game ranges from adrenaline-pumping, to relaxed, to emotional, and all of the songs of the game were great, especially those in the latter-half of the game. (Side note, the fact that the OST is not on Spotify IS A CRIME).Graphics: SANABI is an absolutely beautiful aesthetically, and there are so many things to appreciate about it. The characters all have memorable character designs, the enemies look unique and threatening, and all of the environments look absolutely stunning. Furthermore, some of the cutscenes are animated, and every time they utilized this, I'd get so hyped up. I'm having a hard time writing this section because of how much there is to appreciate, but seriously, this game is an absolute delight to look at.Story: SANABI at its core is more than a platformer, the game is trying to tell you a very deep and compelling story. The game is split around 40/60 between gameplay and cutscenes, and all of the cutscenes for the game are decently long. Furthermore, the game gives you cutscenes after around every 10 minutes of gameplay to give you a break. Some may not like this, but at its core, SANABI is a heavily story-based game. If you are not a fan of story-based games, I'd heavily question buying this game. Anyways, I can't say too much without getting into spoilers, but the emotional impact this game had on me was incredible. It's hard to even describe, but the way the game touched me and resonated with me is something few pieces of media have ever accomplished. The ending for this game was absolutely perfect. and the experience all the way through was a blast. I HEAVILY encourage you, if you are interested in buying this game, DO NOT LOOK ANYTHING UP, the story of this game is very interesting and heartfelt, and spoiling the game for yourself will only dampen your experience of this absolute gem of a game.CONS: I enjoyed SANABI very much, and I only have some small critiques. Don't let these dissuade you from buying the game, but they are something to note.Story: The one things I critique about the story is that several times, the game pulls a "sorry mario, your princess is in another" card multiple times, as the game's plot makes the characters  change their means of reaching the higher levels multiple times in a slightly annoying and uncreative way. I think the game could have done better in this regard.There was also a small section of the game which took you away from the normal gameplay and turned it into a sort of "minigame", where you had to dodge falling rocks. While the idea of it was cool, in practice, it was boring than much else.OVERALL: SANABI is a hidden masterpiece, with amazing story, graphics, gameplay, soundtrack, and level design. While the game is not perfect, the flaws of the game are SEVERELY hidden behind the brilliance of the game's strengths. It's honestly surprising that the game has not garnered more attention, as everything about it is truly amazing. If you have any interest at all in buying this game, PLEASE do so. The game was a satisfying ride all the way through, and the game has become indie game of this year after having played it.Thank you for reading this review, and thank you SANABI devs for working so hard to make this masterpiece, you all did an amazing job.

The game is NOT short, and the set pieces just get crazier and crazier as the story unfolds. The mysteries of the plot and characters grip you like a VISE. I was so engaged and NEEDED to know what happens next that I played the whole thing in one sitting (over 10 hours). And the ending is absolutely wonderful...But getting to the end isn't what's important, it's how you get there. And the gameplay that transports you through the game is probably some of the best 2D platforming I've ever experienced. It takes a bit to get to grips with how exactly the swinging behaves, but once you get the hang of it, it feels like you and the game are in perfect sync. It's a game that feels good from the start, but clearly has a lot of room for skill expression and growth. It was only near the end of my second playthrough that I truly felt like I mastered it. I HIGHLY recommend checking out the speedrun mode and see just how good you can get; you may just surprise yourself.The only real criticism I can give is that there's A LOT of dialogue, and it might wear you down if you're not interested in the story. The plot does tend to overexplain itself a little, so try to be patient. It's worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: (short version: maximum quality video game, buy it)I played this game in early access in the middle of 2022. Me playing any early access game is rare enough, there are apparently 29 games in my Steam library that were once in early access, only four of which being games I purchased myself during that time, and Sanabi was not one of those. A friend gifted it to me and simply said "you need to play this" and so I did. Version 1.0.11 already had me completely hooked, and I could tell right away that this was going to be an incredible game when it was finished. So, after getting to the end of the demo, I put it down and patiently waited. Eventually I forgot about it, because when it finally came out on November 8th of 2023, I didn't realize it happened until it was almost December, and by the time I got around to playing it properly, it had already seen several more patches... including the addition of a speedrun mode. That's how you know it's *really* a gem.A certain rule of thumb has existed in the back of my brain for many years now. "If the game has a grappling hook that isn't a quicktime event, it's probably an amazing game." Hasn't failed me yet. Well, not only does Sanabi *have* a grappling hook, the grappling hook is *the core of the gameplay*. A 2D platformer built entirely around swinging with a grappling hook and using enemies as single-use springboards is a game made specifically for me, but also a dangerous concept, since it relies *heavily* on the controls feeling consistent, predictable, and extremely good. The player needs to always simultaneously feel fully in control, and on the razor's edge of control. Not an easy balance to achieve.But thankfully, it's fully achieved here, even managing to never become frustrating because the incredible clarity of the controls makes it impossible to blame the game for a skill issue. Not that you'd be doing that very often anyway, however, because even when you're not playing well, flying around the map like Captain Korea still always looks and feels cool. The game only loses its footing for a moment in the later stages, because one of the cool setpieces feels really clunky compared to the rest of the game and overstays its welcome, but I find that easy to overlook since it only happens once. It's even easier to look past that hiccup when considering the sheer rush of dopamine the final chapter gives you, rushing through the game at full power feeling like a god. I'd be singing this game's praises even if it was *just* a platformer with nothing else of note to offer.But simply building the entire game around perfect controls wasn't enough. They had everything, and needed more.Sanabi is a visually breathtaking game that bleeds style no matter where you look, with another level of visual beauty added through the extremely expressive and stylish character animations, all well beyond any reasonable expectations for a team of this size - only five people, and starting out as college students no less - to produce. Sound design is also wonderfully chunky and crisp, adding a lot of weight to the already weighty visuals, and even notably improved since the early access build I originally played.The original soundtrack is beyond perfect for the game as well, fitting flawlessly into every scene and elevating the experience *greatly* while also being simply fantastic music on its own, to the point that I will probably be listening to this soundtrack outside of the game from time to time - as *music* to lose myself in, not just background sound - which is something I do so rarely with games that I didn't even have a top five until now; Jet Lancer, Hypnagogia: Boundless Dreams, Doom 2016, Iridion II, and now Sanabi... and it takes position 2 in that list.Games like this aren't expected to have much, if any, narrative either. Nobody would have complained if Sanabi didn't have a storyline, all it really needed was to say that a bad thing happened and you're going in to fix it. But of course, that wasn't enough for Wonder Potion. The story of Sanabi is more than simply present, it's compelling enough, interesting enough, and charming. It's not exactly revolutionary, but that doesn't matter, it's way better than it ever needed to be - much better than the disgraceful writing of some triple-A games that get showered with praise - and I thoroughly enjoyed it.As I played, I figured out most of the reveals before they came to pass, but from what I've seen online, a lot of people didn't, and even if you *do* see things coming like I did, getting to the end still makes the second playthrough feel pretty different, so I can't even say predictability is a caveat here. The only real caveat is that towards the end of the game (but not *at* the end, pretty much just in chapter 4), the translation quality dips, and it can be a little jarring, occasionally causing me to need to reread lines... but I can't get mad at that. Oddly, the focus on the story seems a little controversial, because The Gamers™ hate reading and cutscenes in 2D platformers, even when it's as good as this.Fortunately for them, they only have to deal with it once, because once you see the true ending of the game - continue the game if you went downstairs - speedrun mode is unlocked. No dialogue, no cutscenes, no boss fights, no loading screens, no fades to black, just a straightforward run through each chapter with nothing to distract you from the incredibly fun flow of swinging through levels quickly. Every time you complete a chapter in speedrun mode, the game kicks back to the title screen instead of back to the speedrun menu, which is unfortunate and annoying, but livable considering how fun it is to run through each chapter nonstop. I'll call it an enforced moment of respite. My first attempt ended up at a total time of 1:11:20, which felt pretty slow to me and did a very good job of showing me just how much I still have to learn, especially since I then found out the current record on  at that time was 25:58. I will definitely be coming back to this for a long time.The more I like a thing, the less I usually have to say about it. I've said as much as I can think of at this point, I don't know how to dig deeper into the details about *why* this game is so fantastic or what makes it feel so amazing to play. So just trust me bro. I'll close with this.Wonder Potion had everything they needed and chose to go *well* above and beyond for the sake of their vision. The result is something to be very proud of, and I applaud them. Sanabi is absolutely one of the best games I've played, and an all time favorite.

_childDocuments_.review: Slick and stylish platformer that can be difficult, but not hard enough to prevent you from reaching the end. There are a couple of small translation errors, but nothing bad enough to keep me from understanding what the text meant (mostly just a couple instances of awkward english). I wish levels reset a little faster and that there were some small checkpoint improvements, but these were mostly minor annoyances that did not come up often. Game ran great, no performance issues. Beautiful visuals, great pixel art and clever animation of the characters. Its crazy how emotive they can be. Also, some excellent cut-in visuals at key story moments. _childDocuments_.review: Sanabi is a 2D precision-action platformer with an emphasis on traversing the environments with your grappling hook arm. The game has a cyber punk/tech noir aesthetic as you traverse varied environments in the world of Mago City. If you have an appreciate for pixels, there's a lot to love here.The sounds and soundtrack in particular is awesome. It's full of dark synth wave bangers and a few emotional tracks as well. The OST is probably worth the pick up too.The story is excellent, and far exceeded my initial expectations. I enjoyed the cinematic storytelling and it never hurt the pacing of the action. If the beginning doesn't make you cry, the end just might.Overall, this is a rock solid pick up for any person who enjoys a good 2D platformer with a strong emphasis on swinging around. I love stuff like this, man.Swinging rules!Controls work really well by default, and I played from start to finish no problem on my Steam Deck.

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent 2d cyberpunk action adventure - with mechanics strongly reminiscent of the Ninja Rope from Worms.The level- and art design are impeccable, which in combination with an electrifying and surprisingly varied soundtrack gives you an uninterrupted feel of flow. _childDocuments_.review: I think it won't hurt to reiterate what is already present in almost all negative reviews of this game, namely the dialogues. I generally don't mind a substantial amount of text, however, in Sanabi, the dialogues are notably subpar and, oddly enough, longer than the gameplay itself. While I don't really like to make such comparisons, juxtaposing it with Katana ZERO - often associated with Sanabi - reveals significantly fewer dialogues, yet the same amount of information is conveyed. Furthermore, in Katana ZERO, you have the opportunity to actively engage in the story, with your decisions impacting plot details. Here, throughout the entire game, you have only one significant choice, and it's NOT a dialogue with a character. In other words, if I were to put it briefly, it feels like you're more of a spectator in a movie during the dialogue sections, where your participation is limited to repeatedly pressing the spacebar. It wasn't a significant issue, but considering the game's length, spending almost half of the total time on reading dialogues... let's be honest, that's at least not what you generally want and expect from such game, but this is already a more subjective opinion.Out of curiosity, during my second playthrough, I wondered how long it would take me to complete the first chapter without dialogues. The answer: around 20-30 minutes. How long does it actually take? Approximately one and a half to 2 hours. So, ponder that for a moment. MINOR SPOILERS ALERT:The one bright spot I'd genuinely tip my hat to is the gameplay. It turned out well, nevertheless was spoiled by the game's pace. Playing it the second time, already familiar with the game, was much more enjoyable than the first time. For me personally, the gameplay didn't seem particularly unique or exciting. I believe it could be due to the reasons mentioned earlier, and also that most features weren't thoroughly refined.What I would like to see more of are additional mechanics for speed of movement. Some momentum conservation or more thoughtful level design could enhance the experience. With such mechanics, the locations could've been much more diverse, opponents strategically placed rather than respawning, and the approaches to them could've been more inventive than simply circling a platform from below and sneaking up behind them.In conclusion, I essentially got what I wanted, but there is a feeling that the developers didn't polish the game to perfection, and it has obvious flaws. Some, or maybe even many, decisions seem strange. This makes me doubt about the quality of the game that, at first glance, seemed good.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm just going to make a bunch of quick fire points as to why you should absolutely get this gameFluid, action-packed gameplay. As if the fact you had a grappling hook to make traversing the engaging platforming sections in front of astonishing hyper detailed backgrounds wasn't badass enough, the way enemies become obstacles and movement puzzles in the best possible way just feels so good to play. The pixel art animation is ridiculously good, everything from the animations keeping up with the fast paced gameplay, to the character details and emotion shown through the basic in game character sprites keeps you invested and engaged through every minute whether it be the gameplay itself or the story based cutscenes. As for the story itself, I have no words. Just play the game and experience it for yourself. If any of the previous points sounded at all up your alley and you might be worried that the story side of the game might end up being a let down. I won't say anything about it, don't look at anything about it, just take my word for it. The story is incredible and you should absolutely experience it for yourself first. This game is a masterpiece and I hope you enjoy it as much as I did.

_childDocuments_.review: ...wow.I have just finished Sanabi. I heard good things about it - now I am the one preaching.Sanabi is a delightful mix of fast-paced grappling hook combat, futuristic music and well-rounded story in one, pixel graphic package.First thing you notice - despite being pixel based, everything is expressive and vibrant, on a level that some AAA studios don't reach. I was personally taken away by the cutscenes, well-directed and conveing a story that hooks you with a simple premise, but quickly devolves into intriguing mystery of the city where people just... vanished? While you will speculate an maybe even correctly predict some of the reveals, I can guarantee you won't be able to see the extent of the big picture the game paints before you.Combat is blazingly quick, stylish and rewarding - no health bars, no unnecessary HUD. The controls are intuitive and responsive both in fights as well as in platforming sections (tried keyboard only, but I can see it on controllers). I was worried that in later stages the action may be a bit hard to follow, but suprisingly you never feel lost, even when you character is a couple pixels on the vast arena.I greatly reccomend Sanabi. And while I am a bit sad that it ended so quickly, remember: Getting to the end is not that important. What's important is Ṡ̸̻͕̬̥̹̠̔͘͜a̷̡̛͕̩̙̰̗̻̼̩̖̬͇̳̯̐͊̇̅̀̀̀̇͆͌́̾͜͝͝ņ̷̢̢̠̮̟̺̬̖̺̘̋̿̈́̂͠͠a̸͕̯̰̺͙̅̊͛̌͂̾̾͆̆̒̀͘͠͝b̵̨̛̓̒̽̒͌͐̓̒͗̎͠i̶̡̜̦̺̯̼̦̲̰̫̅̿ͅ.

_childDocuments_.review: I think if this game was revisited it could seriously be a WAY killer game, but right now I am not liking a lot of what I just experienced playing this.The mechanics were really awful to the point that it put me off from the entire game's story (especially the shift lock-on, the entire factory section, immunity enemies and the general mechanic of just pushing ♥♥♥♥, the waiting 50 yrs to retry after falling/dying, constant flow interruptions).The game's story is also presented in a really annoying way where there is so much exposition dumping and 4356893689535 flashbacks in between gameplay that it ends up being more like a 70/30 cutscene/gameplay ordeal, and the storytelling structure that was went with was so much "tell dont show" that everything it was going for felt like it hit way less than it would've if it just let the game speak for itself instead of trying to invest so hard on the "plot twist" moment that ends up just being another exposition dump while doing some really basic platforming in contrast to if the game just let it speak for itself.ALSO WHY IS THE MOST BORING PART OF THE STORY THE MAJORITY OF THE GAME??? The plot twist and onward were way more interesting topics and ideas that could have been touched on, but instead they amass for like 25% of the game only or something??? The dialogue earlier in the game is also so bad (which is on purpose, but it doesn't really excuse it personally)I could not emotionally tune myself in to the ending because of how exhausting it was to sit through the game. If even playtesting was more rigorously done, I think even just that would at least had let me enjoy the ending more. Otherwise I was just like yea wow that's definitely the ending I expected.To me this game would have done much better if there was actually way more playtesting that was done before rollout, and if the general storytelling structure of the game was handled in a WAY different manner that didn't rely so much on cutting between the gameplay, and constantly spamming flashbacks and exposition dumps on your faceIdk that's mainly the impression and issues I got from this game, and they are so tremendous that I can't consider this game good, or something that should be recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Sanabi is bloody excellent and deserves to be a household name as recognizable as  and the other indie platformer greats.Some people say its just another game with a grappling hook, but no, this is THE game with a grappling hook. To explain why would require going into technical minutiae whose significance is difficult to appreciate (eg. camera is very zoomed out, there is slight auto-aim, hooking into a new object resets your momentum which prevents you from overshooting your own rope and rendering it slack, etc). All I will say is that the hooking mechanics are the smoothest they've ever been, allowing you to zip around levels with ease once you master them.The game does have combat, but if you're expecting the improvisational dances of , you will have to look somewhere else. The combat philosophy is closer to something like Sonic's where it's more meant to complement the platforming and add to that sense of speed than to be its own independent system. When you judge it for what it's actually trying to do, it's pretty fun, zipping around levels and arenas trying to kill all the enemies while making it to the exit as fast as possible.Except for the boss fights, cause these... are real fights! If you want battles that test your skills with both hook and fist, then this is where you'll get them. Each boss is a cinematic spectacle that will make you feel like a grapple ninja. The final two in particular are worth shouting out for how cool they are.So now that I'm done talking about gameplay, I have to find a way to talk about the story, cause that's actually a pretty big part of this game. The reason why this is so challenging is cause the story is good, SIGNALIS levels of good. By the time you reach the climax you will be heavily invested in these characters, but there are some criticisms to be made by how well it integrates into the rest of the game.The big problem is the impact on pacing. You'll be grappling around faster than the speed of sound, then you'll cross a level-transition barrier and everything crashes to a screeching halt as a cutscene begins. The cutscenes themselves can be pretty fun, but sometimes they can take a while. The bigger problem in my opinion is the gaps between cutscenes. They're too short, there's not enough gameplay between them meaning that you never get to avoid that feeling of being shunted out of your groove. It's the only noticeable flaw in an otherwise excellent game.Thank goodness the story is one worth telling then! I can't spoil anything, but despite what I mentioned in the previous paragraph, I still think it adds more to the game than it detracts. I simply suggest you have some patience during the beginning when the story is still taking its time to establish things. So those are my thoughts on Sanabi. Massively underrated game. I hope this review can convince at least one other person to play it. There's a reason why it has a 50% completion rate, and why 10% of people who complete it end up completing it a second time on the hardest difficulty.Also, game's got an epic soundtrack.

_childDocuments_.review: SANABI - 10/10"Getting to the end is not what's important"Never before has a game made this emotional, a truly phenomonal and heartwrenching experienceThe unique thing is that for a game presenting itself as a lightning quick action-platformer, it actually feels like the gameplay isn't the main focus. Despite that, it's still a lot of fun swinging around and grappling to enemies across a room who dared to think they could ever get a shot off on you.The real meat of the game is it's story and presentation. The game takes place in Mago City, emulative of south korean cyberpunk dystopia. As you make your way up the city to reach the top and achieve what you set out to do, the story slowly unfolded until it all comes crashing down and the truth is revealed. The main characters have a great dynamic that adds a lot to this.On top of that, the soundtrack is amazing and really compliments the rush of tearing your way through the city and the heavy story beats.SANABI is truly a masterpiece that deserves to be discussed and remembered, and it's a shame I only heard about it in passing conversations on the katana zero subreddit

_childDocuments_.review: I bought the game during early access, but wanted to wait until the campaign was fully fleshed out and finished. The waiting paid off and the release is truly a wonderfully executed, finished game.As great as the music, the art style and the combat is - I'm mostly happy that the developers stuck the landing on the campaign and delivered an amazing story that quite frankly is even better than Katana Zero's. It hit me in the feels like KZ didn't.A lot of comparisons with Katana Zero have been made - in a very positive sense ofc, but now having finished the game I can honestly say, that the comparisons should probably stop. Yes, the music and the art style is just as great, but apart from that Sanabi stands on its own. It has it's own unique gameplay, that is far closer to Celeste than Katana Zero. Traversing levels at 'high octane' speeds and killing enemies along the way has a very different feel compared to KZ. The boss fights are all unique and fun. The difficulty is even on Veteran mostly fair. There were one or two passages in Chapter 3 or 4 where the next checkpoint was a little bit too far away and you had to repeat 'a little bit' too much for my taste but otherwise it was a great experience. What is also interesting to note is, that the further you get in the campaign, the more abilities you unlock and the more fun (!) traversing levels actually becomes. I thought that was quite a feat, because usually the further you get in a game the more difficult and frustrating it simply gets - this is somewhat true for Sanabi as well, but trust me, you will have the best time in the game when you blast through the last chapter with all your abilities unlocked.  What a great finale and feeling, when you reach the ending!Uh yeah, so.... recommended! In fact..a tie for Game of the Year for me (with BG3 and Dave the diver)

_childDocuments_.review: I don't quite remember the last time any game wowed me like Sanabi did, but it's been a while. Every single thing I wrote before still holds true in the full version. Playtime is roughly doubled, there's more mechanics to the swingy gameplay, the banger ost (and sound design in general) has been expanded upon, the characters and story stayed true to themselves at all times... long story short, Sanabi has, in my opinion, turned out to be a near perfect game from start to finish. I will probably be thinking about this one a lot in the coming days. And I couldn't be any happier about that._____________________________________________________________________With a soundtrack that easily rivals Hotline Miami and a gritty neon-lit cyberpunk setting portrayed in beautifully crafted pixel visuals like these, you've already got me on the hook. Add lightning-fast swingy slashy gameplay and lots and lots of different mechanics and enemies to that in just the five hours I've played so far and I won't even fight while you reel me in. Seriously, though: Who's responsible for this absolute banger of a soundtrack and / or the positioning of the tracks within the game? Cuz they deserve a hecking medal!Even so, at this point I've not even touched the story / writing yet. At times wholesome, cute and funny, at others dark, serious and downright heartbreaking, and sometimes completely over the top with some sprinkled in references. And yet, it never feels forced because it seems to know exactly what it wants to do with its story. Also, Mari and General Ninja dad are incredibly cute together.Even if the game was fully finished in the five hours I've played, I would consider my buck fully banged. Even better that there's more to come in the future, of course. Some games manage to amaze you enough, that the golden rule of 1€ = at least 1 hour of game time simply does not apply. And to me, Sanabi is one of them.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could recommend this game, however after about 90 minutes of play I had to request a refund. Here are the issues I had that were enough for me to not want to finish playing:      - The core game play loop is not especially fun. I think speedrunners will love this game, but for more casual players it feels somewhat monotonous and uninteresting.      - Combat lacks depth      - Comparisons to Katana Zero are aesthetic and people should not expect a similar gameplay experience      - The story is mediocre at best if not downright cliche, and there are far too many cut scenes. The grizzled old veteran protagonist and central conflict of the narrative is incredibly tiresome and overdone. Maybe there's some big twist later in the game, but it simply becomes an absolute slog from the get-go. Honestly, it was the dialogue and story that made me stop altogether, and the undue time this is given in comparison to a somewhat stilted core gameplay loop. Maybe some future updates will improve the gameplay, but I cannot recommend this one.

_childDocuments_.review: I was sold on the grappling alone since it looked awesome but what I wasn't expecting was how story focused this game was.I'll be upfront and say that while the gameplay of SANABI is quite fun, I would not recommend this if you can't stand long/frequent cutscenes where control is taken away from you.If this doesn't turn you away, I will say that the story of SANABI is surprisingly great, for a roughly 7 - 10ish hour journey I was honestly quite surprised with how much I cared about the narrative by the end, despite me seeing some of the larger twists pretty early on.But since I can't really go into spoilers, I'll comment on the gameplay, SANABI is a game that I'd say all about movement.Manipulating swing arcs, momentum, moving platforms, the occasional bit of combat, a lot of it ain't necessarily unique and admittedly I feel the enemy variety and combat designs should've been a bit more dynamic and varied, but it's all pretty fun all the same.One place I think they did a really great job in though are the boss fights, arenas are pretty varied, no fight is the same and none of them outstayed their welcome, the setup for these fellas are also pretty well paced, really enjoyed these.The last thing I really need to comment on is the presentation and man this is some really good presentation.Music was quite enjoyable, everything's wonderfully animated, the art design is quite practical and never felt like it got in the way of gameplay, it's just a really pleasing game.It's not the biggest standout in its genre but it has enough going for it to make this an easy recommendation, cheers.

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of this review the game is not finished, so only part of the story is playable. With that said, what's available so far is incredibly fun. Core movement and combat mechanics strike a satisfying balance between simple and fluid, but also allowing for a high ceiling of mastery which makes me excited for a possible blossoming speedrun community. Story has been very interesting so far and I'm excited for more chapters to be released to see where the narrative goes. Overall art direction, music, sound design, and spritework are also stellar. For a studio just getting started, this makes me very excited to see what else they can do.At the time of this portion of the review, I can safely say this is one of the most unexpected masterpieces that I have ever experienced. Not only does the gameplay escalate in such a way that challenges the player up until the very end without feeling unfair, but while saying as little as possible, this game's writing and direction surprised me with how flawlessly they executed the story they wanted to tell. For a game that started out as a lesson on how terrible of a Spider-Man I would be, I came away from my first full playthrough feeling the same way as when I finished Ocarina of Time. Yes. The Legend of Zelda. I am fully confident in this comparison, and you will have to beat this game before you tell me I'm wrong. I am blown away by how much of a surprise hit this is, please play it I'm begging you.

_childDocuments_.review: Came across this game, saw the art and saw the Steam reviews saying this was like Katana Zero (a personal favorite).I do see why people make the comparison to Katana Zero but I wouldn't make it personally. It has a a lot more platforming, and the grappling is quite different (and good fun). Even the combat is quite different, although again fun.While the platforming and combat is fun, it didn't blow me away on its own. What did blow me away was the total package for an indie studio (from what I can tell) making their first game. The length, pacing, music, and presentation are all superb, and more than worth the $12 I paid.The pixel art is gorgeous, and the framing of so many scenes highlights the art even more. The music doesn't quite hit the heights of Katana Zero or Hotline Miami, but you get the pounding synth tracks for combat and then the slower and more quiet subtle tracks for the emotional moments. Really good stuff overall, and used in all the right places.The game is also well paced, no single combat/platforming section or story section felt too long, keeping everything moving. Each area in the game introduces new mechanics specific to that area that also keeps you engaged and having to learn new things. No area feels too long or drawn out. By the end you are zipping along and it does feel good. Without spoiling anything, the last chapter in the game pays off the progression in game mechanics throughout the game beautifully.  The game is just the right length I felt too to let the story properly play out and unfold without dragging or any extra fat.Getting to the story- a lot of praise in the Steam reviews, and it is good. You get enough to put most of the puzzle together before the end, so you'll have some idea where it's going, but the way it unfolds is compelling, and you won't be able to figure eveything out before the end. The story really pays off emotionally with a touching ending too.Writing and text delivery deserves kudos too, a lá Katana Zero, so much tone, flow, and personality is exuded in the way text bubbles are presented, the way they overlap, sound, changes to the font, etc. The delivery really helps get you invested in the characters, specifically the main two, but also the side characters. Even characters who get little screen time I found myself caring about. The writing and characters really elevate an already solid plot.To put a bow on it- all of these elements make for a game that's hard not to come away satisfied with. It just hits so many high notes on the presentation with the art, sound, story delivery, everything. The gameplay isn't super complex, but it is fast and fun, and it stays fresh, introducing new areas and mechanics at just the right pace.Spend $12, play this game. If you have a Steam Deck, great way to play.

_childDocuments_.review: PLAY IF:   - You enjoy 2D platformers similar to Katana Zero or (somewhat) the gameplay loop of Hotline Miami.   - You are willing to withstand occasional nonsense level design/bugs.    ---------------    This is quite possibly the most conflicted I have ever felt completing a video game. This game's highs are jubilant, featuring some of the most freeing movement in a 2D platformer and a story that subverts one's expectations in a way that feels earned and powerful rather than a cheap plot point like many lesser stories.Inversely, however, this game inspired such frustration within me that I had not previously thought possible, with the game's targeting system with the hook and the late-game charging move. (I am aware that there is a setting for aim-assist for the hook, but I had problems both with it on and off.) I also encountered several bugs, but according to the patch notes they seem to have been patched or at least acknowledged. This game was also originally written in Korean, as while it is very well localized, the translation itself features some minor errors and, more importantly, many vague sentences that make it unclear what exactly is happening.This game has undeniable faults, but I still recommend it to anyone who enjoys intense 2D platformers or, thanks to the game's many difficulty options, anyone who would be interested by a heartstrings-pulling story. I would also highly recommend playing on keyboard and mouse, as despite the unwieldy keybindings, you may edit them as you choose and aiming the hook is significantly more satisfying. ...Yeah, I think that about covers it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game isn't just a game, it's a movie. A beautiful one. Out the gate, this game has a eye-catching and vivid pixel graphic art style that pulls you in. It was the reason I bought this game, but it's much more than looks. SANABI might be the best metroidvania game I've ever played. The one downside that may turn away a lot of people is the fact that there is a crap ton of dialogue. I'd say 60% of the game of the game is just dialogue and cutscenes. However, these long periods of dialogue is how you connect to these few characters we learn to care for. As you click to the next sentence, it unveils this story revolving around revenge on a mysterious figure who the main character deems is called "Sanabi", and by the end of it all, you'll be crying in your seat as the ending pans out. Gameplay wise, the grappling mechanic is extremely fun to use and traverse the dazzling, atmospheric world of this dystopian, dead city which makes you feel alone. As the game progresses, you gain different mechanics to use for combat or platforming. SANABI isn't the hardest game to pick up, nor is it hard to master, but it is fun and exhilarating to fly through and pounce on enemies. SANABI is a top 5 game of 2023. It's short, it is unique, the story is moving, and it is worth every penny.

_childDocuments_.review: I cried man. I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cried. This was some of the good stuff. If you liked Katana Zero, SANABI is another incredible side scrolling, pixel art platformer with a mesmerizing story. The best part about the game itself is the final couple chapters when the player has the most freedom with their movement and the story is coming full circle. Grappling and swinging through stages at awesome speeds while listening to the incredible soundtrack is a blast, but there's probably just as much gameplay as story, which finds its essence in wholesome adoptive father-daughter interactions like with Zero and the little girl. At the same time that the narrative is great, I do have misgivings about certain aspects to it and how it relates to gameplay. Half way into the story the dialogue and plot progression get a little redundant, almost like it needed something--anything--in terms of dialogue about the story in spite of zero progress towards uncovering the mysteries of SANABI during the ensuing dialogue. The same questions and answers are repeated a few too many times. The gameplay during this segment is quite slow too--providing new mechanics but also restricting movement options and occasionally flashbanging the screen on top of it. And although the story is fantastic, there are a few cutscenes I would have liked to be able to skip during my second playthrough (I'd rather not cry again). SANABI is a really fun game but an even better story with very memorable characters and interactions as well as a unique world to present them in.

_childDocuments_.review: SANABI is another one in a long list of games that should finally teach me that "Overwhelmingly Positive" is a meaningless rating in a review aggregate system. Most negative reviews seem to mind the gameplay-to-story ratio or the quality of the story; for me, personally, these are the selling points. The story is certainly generic and hopelessly derivative, but it's executed well enough for its dramatic beats to hit. The characters aren't terribly original, but they do their jobs and the whole thing is helped by some great (if simplistic) sprite work and a banging soundtrack.My problem is the gameplay. I *detest* the controls in this, both in kb+m and gamepad. The physics are too wonky for the type of precision platforming the game requires from the mid-point onwards. Spider-Man-ning your way around the gigantic levels is fun at first, but from some point onwards, a swing will go wrong outside of your control or your hook won't latch where you want it to (especially on gamepad, which has the left stick tied to the hook direction for some ungodly reason) or you'll be dealing with enemies that lock on to you from all directions and you can't tell what's going on, because the sprites are small.SANABI feels more like an idea rather than a fully fleshed out game. Before the half-way point, the game loses its creative spark and struggles to come up with new challenges properly tailored to the mechanics. By the point they introduce the necessity to launch enemies into the massive "red zones" to defeat them, it becomes painfully obvious they're out of tricks. The idea of a physics platformer where your main means of traversal and combat is a grappling hook isn't bad and it dates all the way back to the '80s and Bionic Commando. But SANABI is undercooked and, as engaging as I find its simple story of revenge and surrogate parenthood as a means to cope with grief, I don't think it's the best example of its genre and I wouldn't recommend it when better options exist.
