_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games I have ever played. I came in to the game knowing that it was going to be emotional, but I did not expect to leave the game with sore eyes from crying so much. With that out of the way I have to say that the gameplay of the game is absolutely amazing and extremely fun. The movement of the game is very fleshed out and they constantly introduce new mechanics to keep yourself on your toes. The game is very fast paced and really makes you feel like you are the main character straight out of a superhero movie.The music of this game is very good, albeit kind of one dimensional. What I mean is that most of the music can really fall into one category, which is techno music that plays when you need to panic. This is not to say the music is bad, as it is very servicable and does a good job at setting the tone of the game. The music is simply not a genre that I am too interested in. Lastly, the story of this game is absolutely amazing. I have already mentioned at the start that this game is really emotional and got me to cry like a baby, which is not something that I can say very often (in fact only one other game has done this for me). However, I will say the story gets very confusing at times, as you are placed in the shoes of the main character who is also thrown into a mystery that they do not know the answers to. As a result, you are going to be left very confused for the majority of the game, until the very end where everything becomes clear. I do, however, believe that this works in the game's favor, as once you put the pieces together and notice the clues and hints from the start of the game your mind will be metaphorically and physically blown. Overall, I would give this game a 9.8/10 and an absolute wholehearted recommendation, and always remember: Getting all the way to the end is not what's important.
_childDocuments_.name: SANABI

_childDocuments_.review: SANABI is an incredible, story-driven action game, developed by WONDER POTION and published by NEOWIZ. It tells an amazing story, and while certain gameplay elements and moments can feel a little finnicky at times and the game features a few, annoying, unadressed bugs: such as the final boss having a tendency to bug out and become both inanimate and invincible, forcing you to restart the game, the story really sells it. Overall, there are a ton of cutscenes in this game, so if that's not your thing, I might suggest skipping it.In SANABI, you play as a retired, war veteran, with a massive claw arm prosthetic, who is sent on his last mission, seemingly a suicide mission, in search of the ever-elusive SANABI, a man, organization or thing that is tied to the death of your beloved daughter. Not all is as it seems...In summary, everything in SANABI is awesome or at least good enough to overlook the few flaws and moments of jank (particularly on the game's hardest difficulty, where the problems become the most pronounced). Outstanding soundtrack, a story that made me cry like nothing has in a long time, controls that are solid for the most part, a ton of awesome moments, and only a few annoying ones. You're really doing yourself a disservice, by not experiencing SANABI, at least once for the story (: most of the "jank" is only really pronounced enough to be noticeable on the game's highest "Legend" difficulty, where you die in one hit)
_childDocuments_.name: SANABI

_childDocuments_.review: This is by no means a bad game. It is very good actually, but i do not think it's good enough for the overwhelmingly positive rating that it has at the moment.I find it hard to pin down why, but this game felt like a chore to me. The platforming can get repetitive at times and the combat in general feels rather monotonous. The only things that save it for me are the bossfights and the presentation.As far as the story goes, it is pretty good, however, the dialogue . Other than that, the moments hit when they are supposed to hit, the music is wonderful, and the story is way better than I expected.Unfortunately these good things do not make up for the bad in my opinion. So i do not recommend it, but can recognize that it's a good game. It's just not for me.
_childDocuments_.name: SANABI

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible movement, good writing and a beautiful conclusion wraps together in a neat 7-8 hour package leading to a overwhelmingly nice experience. Fun, sad and mysterious, it really had everything i couldve asked for,,My two complaints were that the hardest difficulty was locked behind the ending, and since this game is so story focused, i felt a second play through wouldnt have hit the sameand The lack of a quick save/ save system beyond the usual progress ones was kinda annoying.Alas, beyond those two very miniature complaints, the game is perfect :3
_childDocuments_.name: SANABI

_childDocuments_.review: While I personally don't like action platformers, and frequently had to take a break, the story is amazing.Do note this game is only about 6-8hrs of playtime to complete the game but I think it is still worth the price for the experience, especially when it goes on sale.Now that I've played games like Library of Ruina, Lies of P, and Sanabi, I can confirm Korea is cooking with their games and GOATED stories.
_childDocuments_.name: SANABI

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a fantastic art style and starts strong. However, the "tell don't show" approach to its storytelling and the long, click-through dialogue scenes interrupt the game far too often and for far too long for me to enjoy it. The gameplay feels chaotic, but I imagine it would be great if time were invested in getting used to it. Mostly, I just wanted to switch it off due to the frustrating cutscenes, which is a shame because the story is quite compelling and has good humour. You can skip some cut scenes, but knowing the story is part of the game. It's more the format and how often they happen, considering the levels are so short.

_childDocuments_.review: im sitting in the credits as im writing this and man that was a ride....  as far as im concerned i loved the story 10/10 for me the gameplay theres an easy mode that makes it so the combat its almost impossible to die so if youre not in for the challenge you could play that ( which i did towards the end) honestly its such a good game with a great story
_childDocuments_.name: SANABI

_childDocuments_.review: Sanabi is a game that is frustratingly less than the sum of its parts.The good: the graphics are obviously great, the gameplay is mostly fun and satisfying, the story is long-winded but engaging.The bad: so what's the problem? The pacing is a huge obstacle. You get 3 minutes of gameplay, followed by 5 minutes of dialog. Back to 1 minute of gameplay, followed by 2 minutes of dialog. Back and forth, back and forth. The game barely lets you get into a rythm before it slams on the brakes and takes you out of the action. It's almost worse that the story is actually pretty good. If it were garbage, I could say "just skip past all the story bits and enjoy the gameplay", but I really feel like you'd be missing out if you did that (at least on your first playthrough).Long story short, I'm sure some very talented people put this game together, and I hope they get the chance to make more projects in the future; I just didn't really enjoy my time with this game
_childDocuments_.name: SANABI

_childDocuments_.review: AVOID | LACKING | MAYBE | WORTHWHILE |  | UNMISSABLESANABI is a fast-paced action-adventure platformer that has a strong narrative backing it. There was much more story than I was expecting, with probably 1/4 of the time playing being plot-driven/narrative-based. While I wish there was less story than this, that's mainly because of how the main gameplay works - as I said, it's fast-paced and the movement feels super smooth, so it can be a bit jarring to go from that to a discussion between characters. Ultimately, I think the devs delivered this juxtaposition as well as they could with an engaging storyline to boot. Aside from that, the only other thing I wish was different is that in some areas, hitting terrain that hurts you (primarily areas with red lasers), you can easily get stun-locked into dying. It's not a big deal given save points are frequent, but there were several times I hit a laser and knew I would have to wait for it to hit me three more times so I could die and start over instead of having the chance to reposition myself (which would be more skill-expressive, IMO) and carry on.SANABI has a little bit of everything going for it - action, adventure, platforming, combat, a relevant storyline, and a fantastic soundtrack to accompany it all. If you dig the look of the game and want something that simply feels great to play, I recommend this title.
_childDocuments_.name: SANABI

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR : A fantastic and very stylish game with a great story the pulls on the heartstrings, a sick soundtrack, and fun gameplay and with only very minor things that I wasn't a huge fan of!The Pros:+ Beautiful art/music/style+ Fantastic story + I personally enjoyed the switch between narrative and gameplay. I know others were not huge fans of the smaller gameplay chunks and then longer sections of reading, but it felt nice taking a break from the breakneck speed.The Ehh+/- The dialogue can be campy at times. I loved it and thought it made the game endearing, but others may not be as big of fansThe Cons:- Some levels can be tediously long, and as amazing as the art is, I got sick of being in the factory level because of how long it felt (Could easily be a me thing) - Some of the checkpoints for me were a bit odd. I am no platforming expert (I played on normal) but sometimes falling off to your death (or missing your swings) landed me in different spots. SOMETIMES it'll respawn you nearby with a bar of health missing, and other times it'll send you 3-4 screens back (despite having enough health to survive the fall) which would take the wind out of my sails especially if I had just completed a tough section. During a particular boss fight if you fall you automatically die and restart from the beginning of the multi-phase boss fight which can be mildly irritating.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an indie game from Korea.  It's based around a grappling hook, and it's everything you wished for in a 2D action platformer with that as the concept.  If that's not enough, it's got pixel art and music to rival Katana Zero.If I have to nitpick, I'd take issues with the cutscenes.  Not the story itself, which is honestly fairly good, but for a 2D platformer this game has way more cutscenes than its contemporaries.  This isn't always bad, as most of the unique sprite-work happens here (quite frequently too), but the storyteller in me says that about 1/3rd of the cutscenes could have been left out and we would have still had a good narrative.Is that nitpick enough to stop me from recommending it? Not at all, It's rare for any game to get grappling hooks right, let alone nail it on such a level that it will be the bar I measure every other grappling hook ever against.I recommend Sanabi.

_childDocuments_.review: Sanabi is set in a dystopian city, the way the city is portrayed is well executed with its pixel art style and direction, the music/OST further immerses the player by complimenting the environment with its appropriate score. _childDocuments_.name: SANABI

_childDocuments_.review: This was a very enjoyable experience, especially for early access. The controls feel smooth for the most part though there are some areas where the grappling felt stiff mostly when turning some corners. Combat felt awesome, dashing around from enemy to enemy felt satisfying and while simple there were some mechanics that can make things interesting. Being able to dash after being hit is a nice recovery option and I can't wait to see how speedrunners abuse this tactic. You can go really fast in this game and swinging around felt fun, though I hope to see a little more enemy variety in the full version. The final boss was definitely the biggest highlight of the game for me. All of the other bosses were great as well but I felt this one definitely will test your grappling skills the most.The story and characters were nicely written. The story goes from seemingly cheerful to dark pretty fast and early on. I like the concept of the world, with it being some sort of cyberpunk Korean setting with shadowy corporate conspiracies. The characters have enough charm to keep things from being overly mopey, and the game throws in cute references and doesn't take itself too seriously but manages to keep you invested in what's going on. The character designs were also good. One of my favorites was the Gun Head boss encountered at the beginning of the game. The look of the city is fantastic, though I wish there was a little more variety in terms of level aesthetic.As someone who is eager for the Katana Zero dlc I feel this game was able to scratch that itch while also being able to retain a distinct identity on its own. The comparisons were inevitable, and while it doesn't quite strike the same chords I feel that SANABI is on its way to becoming something great and I look forward to playing the finished version when it comes around.
_childDocuments_.name: SANABI

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a fan of the whole grappling hook games since I saw Bionic Commando in an arcade, and then zoomed through Fury of the Furries. Etc. This one is a really good addition to those games. That mechanic will always make a game fun, but in addition this game is visually gorgeous and has a gripping story.
_childDocuments_.name: SANABI

_childDocuments_.review: SANABI feels like two separate games slammed together, and the result turns out better than I ever would have expected.It's a fast-paced, high-flying grappling hook-based platformer. And it's also a poignant, gut-wrenching story about dying to get revenge and living with regret.Those two things don't sound like they really go together, and there was a point when I felt like they didn't. I almost quit the game because I was tired of it getting its own way. How many times is this game going to stop me in the middle of an intense grappling hook section to dump more talking heads in my lap?But I'm glad I stuck with because the payoff is more than worth it. The grappling hook goodness, the surprisingly gripping story, the gorgeous and emotive pixel art that makes the characters come alive more than a lot of AAA games, and one of the best video game soundtracks ever recorded -- this game has so much going for it. Highly, highly recommended
_childDocuments_.name: SANABI

_childDocuments_.review: Holy crap, I just finished the game and Im honestly amazed. Such a good story, such a good platformer. Honestly words cant even begin to describe how this made me feel. Literally a must play for everyone and anyone, I was in genuine ugly tears by the time I finished, one of the most hard hitting moments Ive experienced in a game, I just cant.
_childDocuments_.name: SANABI

_childDocuments_.review: I think there are two things you should know if you're thinking about playing this game:First, it has some of the best platforming/grappling controls I've ever seen, and does a fantastic job of pushing the player without punishing the player. Ideal.Second, the story at the start will seem very paint-by-numbers action hero fare - charmingly so, but still. Don't spoil yourself, but trust that the developers did that deliberately so that they could play with it later to create a very good story when all's said and done.

You, a legendary retired veteran, are called upon for one last operation: to ascend a mega-city ruled by a corrupt conglomerate. You were chosen for this mission because of your signature chain-hook prosthetic arm and the ability to maneuver and quickly defeat enemies. name: The Dark Pictures Anthology: The Devil in Me
detailed_description: A series of stand-alone branching cinematic horror games from the studio behind Until Dawn. Easy to pick-up and play in short sessions, alone or with friends. The Devil in Me is the fourth game in the series and the Season One finale. A group of documentary film makers receive a mysterious call inviting them to a modern-day replica of serial killer H.H. Holmes’ ‘Murder Castle’. It’s an opportunity that’s too good to pass up and could be just the thing they’re looking for to win some much-needed public interest. The hotel is the perfect set for their new episode, but things aren’t quite as they seem. The crew discover they’re being watched and even manipulated, and suddenly there’s much more at stake than just their ratings! Nothing is as it seems here, and the amenities are to die for! Explore every nook of the World’s Fair Hotel using the all-new season finale features including character inventory, tool-based puzzles, and expanded movement actions such as run, jump, and climb. Escape the torturous creations of an evil monster who is hellbent on becoming America’s deadliest serial killer & survive elaborate ‘killing rooms’ where your own death is by the killer’s design. Endure terrifying tests of loyalty – will you risk your own life for someone you care for? The two critically acclaimed multiplayer modes are back: share your story online with a friend or aim for safety in numbers through the offline 5-player pass-the-pad mode. Can you outsmart the killer and checkout all your cast? All playable characters can live or die in your version of the story. The Curator's Cut The Curator's cut features new scenes playable from the other characters' perspective with brand new choices and decisions to make. The Curator's cut is only available once you have completed the main story.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing most Suppermassive Games, (Men of Medan, House of Ashes, etc), TDPA: The Devil In Me, was an instant buy for me, and, being a fan of the series, I was instantly let down by it.First things first, the new gameplay features and mechanics, like jumping (I'll "jump" to this later), crawling and inventory, it's a nice welcome to a game that is more of a movie, than game. It now feels more like you're playing instead of watching and pressing QTE, á lá CD-i.Now, back to jumping.Did you know you can now jump? Don't worry, the game will let you know every 5 minutes, because all of the characters jump. And they jump a lot. See a section you cannot cross? You can jump. A section you can cross by simply walking over, you will jump. In truth, if you like hopping around like a rabbit in the wild, this game has you covered.Graphic wise this is one of the most polished games in the series. The mansion looks amazing and the character models as well. I did encounter some FPS drops here and there but nothing too noticeable.History wise, it's nothing to write Holmes about, especially considering the real life history it's based on. H.H. Holmes, or America's First Serial Killer, it's a gruesome tale and one that unfortunately cannot be taken lightly. But this game bounces safely when it shouldn't. Still, something to spend a weekend on, and move on to the next game on your list.You can check my first hour on YT:

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like horror games? Do you like true crime? Enjoy trying to kill off annoying young people in a video game? Then you may genuinely like this!Based loosely on the myth/story of H.H. Holmes, America's first "serial killer," and his Murder Castle Hotel, the game pits several young people in a documentary film crew with surviving a working replica of the eponymous hotel. Think: Moving walls, changing passageways, mazes, puzzles, devious traps, dark hallways and rooms, with a crazy, evil killer on your heels! I've played several of the games in this anthology and I (so far) like this one the most. Unfortunately, I'm a mess when it comes to QTE's, so I've already killed off 2 characters in my playthrough. I'm hopeful that I'll have a couple who survive. You may do better than me at this!The main cons to the game: 1. TOO DARK. You may need to adjust the lighting in the game to something lighter than you'd normally have it. Otherwise, it may be too dark to enjoy the beautiful environment and see things that are happening.2. Unlikable characters: Okay, I don't dislike them as much as the ones in "Until Dawn," but still... I assume it's part of the game mechanics to make characters that some players may enjoy getting rid of in interesting ways. 3. Can't go back and replay individuals scenes/parts if you screw up. You'd have to start all over and ugh...no. I guess that character stays dead then! 4. Crazy Eyes (Uncanny Valley)...if it bothers you greatly to see characters that are very realistic in every other aspect but the dead eyes, you may not want to play this as every character has those. It can be slightly unsettling, but maybe that's a good thing since it's a horror game?5. Jump Scares... Yes, there's quite a lot of them. If you hate jump scares, just stay away from this one.6. QTE's (Quick Time Events): If you suck at those, like I do, be prepared to have your characters die! However, despite these cons, it is still a great game and deserves accolades for story telling, mood and setting, environmental design, soundtrack... Just superb anyway! So, if you are looking at this game to determine if you'd like it, I recommend trying it out. This game comes from an award-winning anthology of games. You do not have to have played the others to play and enjoy this one!

_childDocuments_.review: I've played all Supermassive games and  totally disagree with many reviews and will explain why you should give this game a chance: - This game is MUCH better than other games from Dark Pictures Anthology- This game is not bugging anymore- Visuals became better, especially comparing to Man of Medan and The Quarry- Not braindead characters- Interesting story- Useful premonitions Origins: I was really frustrated and disappointed with last games from this studio. Until dawn was mindblowing at the moment with graphics, gameplay and story. As Man of Medan came out, it was WAY worse than Until dawn, especially with a story. So after House of Ashes I understood that games from this studio is ONLY for funny evenings with friends. It's like watching American Pie, no way I'd play these games alone for a plot or gameplay. Then The Quarry came out and it was disaster, worse graphics, stupidiest teenagers in the whole galaxy, characters motivation (like cop or hunters) just insane. It was like laugh and anger combined. So. I expected quite the same and ignored bad reviews when was buying this game just to stick to this tradition and have absurd pleasure.But surprisingly it is THE BEST game from Supermassive games at the momentPlot: unlike House of ashes'  or completely mystical The Quarry, or quite unrealistic Man of Medan,  this plot is interesting, and delivered well via flashbacks and recordings.There are not . It is real, and it's well arranged. Of course there are some exaggerated moments like Yet it's a bit charming devil features, there are some physical miracles IRL after all.Non-Braindead characters:  In previous games characters are so dumb your IQ lowers with each minute spent. In The Devil in me there are about 90% of character decisions you can at least explain for yourself. They may be not optimal or rational, yet they are realistic and mature most of the time. The Quarry had like completely brainless characters, despite of the age. Useful premonitions: Until dawn has best solution for future predictions. _childDocuments_.review: Okay... so I put this on off for a while because of the negative reviews flying around everywhere. However... with that being said. This is my second favorite entry into the "Dark Pictures Anthology" (my favorite still to this day is "Little Hope" because it feels so much like it was inspired heavily by "Silent Hill"). The story actually progresses very well with this one. The twists and turns through the story keep you enthralled. Not to mention having to make certain decisions to keep characters alive is a much more daunting task; because you'll think you're making the "right" choice in your gut... and then "BAM" someone dies. The QTEs in this one are unforgivable too. There's a certain scene in the game that's going to make you feel so relieved when the QTEs stop popping up on the screen for you (and you may have to shake out your wrist depending on the grip you've kept on your mouse/controller). Now this game may have been flawed upon it's initial release. I don't see any outlying flaws in it as of playing it now. There was only one graphical/voice over instance that made me laugh with how "goofy" it played out. Supermassive Games in my opinion has done a much better run with their "Dark Pictures Anthology" rather than the other games in this vein ("Until Dawn" is forever a gem because it was the first taste we got... but my God was I really expecting more out of "The Quarry"). I cannot wait for the second season to start... especially because it's in SPACE!!! But in all honesty I think "The Devil In Me" is getting an unfair chance in this because everyone was still left with a bad taste in their mouths from "The Quarry" earlier in 2022. I'd pay full price for any DPA game... but if you're still on the fence... I promise you if you buy it while it's on sale you'll enjoy the game so much that you'll also feel like you shouldn't have slept on it for so long... and maybe next time we'll all give Supermassive Games another fair shake when the next game comes out.

_childDocuments_.review: If there was a "Mixed" rating, I would give it for this entry. If there was a short way to describe this entry, I would describe it as "rushed". Still playable and can be enjoyed.(you can stop reading here because below I go into specifics, personal thoughts and possible spoilers) and foremost, I think the actors did a good job with their performance; especially the actress who plays Kate (Jessie Buckley) as she 100% poured her heart and soul into her role.  but sometimes they have dead expressions (pokerface) when they should DEFINITELY be having emotions and sometimes their line delivery sounds like they weren't given much room for retries., this game has an inventory system!!! Except, you don't really use it. I welcome new game mechanics and experimentation in games but this one didn't really make a difference. It's the same as it was in other games where you have items that need to be used, but now the game waits for you to select it from the inventory. There is a lot of room for creativity for the inventory system but I don't think they had the time to implement it properly.The game is 8 hours long when rushed compared to the previous games that were 4 hours long. That's good, but sadly there isn't much going on in-between that extra time. This game has, as far as I know, the LEAST dialog choices and interactions than any of the entries in Season 1. That's really bad, especially because the characters feel the most underdeveloped compared to previous games.They removed the cinematic letterboxes which looks worse imo and makes it visible that the game+UI are not designed without them. I hope they will at least have it as an option in the future.: other than the game not having lots of variations, suffering from plot armor and most choices not making much of a difference... this entry has unused potential and seems severely rushed. This story is the most interesting out of all Season 1 entries (true crime) and some of the way characters can die are really good.... but they could have (and should have) gone all out with traps and choices to end the season 1 on a bang. Despite the criticism, I still enjoyed and *somewhat* recommend the game. I think actors did a decent job, despite sometimes all of them being derpy, uncomfortable and underdeveloped. The story theme is great, the way they introduced the main cast was genius in my opinion. While you have some areas to freely explore, there are collectables around to make it more interesting so it's not too bad.

I've only played through the game once, for reference I had Kate dead but Jamie alive, and I could keep both Jamie and the dog alive. While obviously keeping everyone alive[Including the dog] will give you the best ending, I got a good ending while only having three of the characters in the cast alive. The game of course still has the sting of losing the characters you did, and I teared up when I saw Jamie pull out Erin's inhaler. _childDocuments_.review: Writing reviews after playing all four.All I can say is wow. Never before have I seen such a good game mangled by so many glitches. - Missing decision prompts, leading to characters dying.- Characters standing on each other's heads.- Head turned backwards after climbing down a ladder.- Reflective Lighting is botched in some areas, causing flashlights to simply not work well.- False/Misleading text (saying we failed QTEs, or saying we're one character when we're not).- Curator says everyone died in the previous game, when only one died, so it misreads save data from past games.- Movement and collision the worst in the series.Moreover, gameplay overall isn't great. Adds new mechanics simply for the sake of new mechanics, one of which (hide) is used exactly three times at the beginning, then never seen again, except for one time near the end. It's like they needed Hiding for one particular scene, so they introduced it as a brand new mechanic that just went underused. Collectibles need to be right next to you to see, as compared to House of Ashes, where they were very clear. This is understandable, since it takes place in a smaller environment. Loved the story. Really loved the story. Could have been the best in the series. But the bugs made it feel like I was helpless against not just the villain, but the developers. The game is designed to make you feel like you're in a forced loss situation, which does add to the theme... until it ACTUALLY forces you to lose. The devs were trying to tell a story where you narrowly escape unwinnable situations with your wits. Only it tells you nothing is going to work beforehand, so every death feels like a scripted loss that wasn't your fault, massively cheapening the impact. Overall, it's just sad to see that what could have been the best game in the series just drop to mid. Wonderful story, amazing ending, but the journey is paved with broken mechanics. Year after release, the devs have fixed nothing. Play it if you've played the others just to complete the series, and if you want a great story. Just be prepared for a buggy mess that gives you so little information, you're guaranteed to not get a perfect play-through first try.

_childDocuments_.review: I had high hopes for "The Devil in Me" as a fan of the developer's previous games, particularly since I enjoyed their previous release, "House of Ashes". However, the game was a major disappointment in every way.The 21:9 mode, which works flawlessly in all other games from the developers, doesn't work in "The Devil in Me". This, coupled with numerous visual bugs, makes it hard to get immersed in the story. It's often unclear whether certain events are supposed to be happening or if they are just a bug. This lack of clarity takes away from the horror experience that the game was supposed to deliver.The co-op mode, which was supposed to be a highlight of the game, is also a letdown due to numerous bugs and connection issues. It's impossible to enjoy the game with so many problems. The game's attempts to expand with new features feel unnecessary and frustrating. The game would have been better if the developers had focused on refining the core gameplay instead of adding unnecessary new features.The biggest disappointment is the lack of horror in "The Devil in Me". The title suggests a spooky and thrilling experience, but the game doesn't deliver on this promise. It fails to scare players in a way that captures their attention, and the absence of the horror element makes it hard to get invested in the story.Overall, "The Devil in Me" is a major letdown that falls short in every aspect. Its issues with the 21:9 mode, unnecessary new features, and missing horror element make it a frustrating and disappointing experience. If you're a fan of the developer's previous work, I would recommend avoiding this game at all costs.

_childDocuments_.review: As a big fan of the Dark Picture Anthology, I was incredibly disappointed by The Devil In Me. The story was fine. It's a little contrived and there's a lot of questionable decisions that seem to screw the player either way, but hey - you know that's what you're signing up for with this kind of game. The real issue is how many bugs there are. This game is broken to the point where I would say it should not be purchased or played. As aforementioned, I really enjoy these type of games, but after 2 hours of playing I was really not enjoying myself. I was playing co-op with a friend, and had to force myself to continue playing as it was one of the least fun experiences that I've had in video games for a long time. Some of the bugs that I encountered were:* The character lost the ability to interact with anything - This means that I was wandering around unable to progress the story, pick up clues, open doors, etc. Just wandering around in a room.* The camera got locked to a strange angle - I'm not sure how, but this happened several times. Trying to navigate a hotel and all the tight hallways and crowded rooms when the camera is fixed in a single direction and won't let you see what you're bumping into is misery.* The character's body became twisted - Their head would always face in one direction, permanently. So walking, turning, animations, etc, the character's head would be looking at the same point throughout, making it look like his head was rotated 180 degrees from his body.* The character's upper body vanished - For one of the chapters, the character had no upper body. Floating head and hands, but that was it.* Walking through stairs - At one point I was trying to navigate up a staircase, but the character would just keep walking through the stairs and out of the world, then snap back to the base of the stairs. This was incredibly frustrating.* Non logical jumps - There's a part of the game where you're in a room (Trying to avoid spoilers here), and I had my character leave the room and move to the complete opposite end of the hotel, a good 4 minute traversal. I guess I hadn't done something right, as a cutscene started and I was teleported back to that room and to my demise. I was furious, since I was long gone. * Unfair death - I lost a character early on because there was a "hold right trigger" event. I held right trigger, character 1 played the cutscene of pulling a switch, then character 2 was saved. The game then jumped back to character 1 failing to pull the switch and character 2 dying. There was no explanation of failure, just a cutscene of "you won" followed by a cutscene of "you lost". In a game where keeping the characters alive is the goal, I felt cheated and didn't want to continue playing. And of course, the game autosaves immediately as a character dies, so I couldn't even quickly exit and reload to try again.Bugs aside, the game suffers from other problems. The movement of the characters is both slow and very clumsy and jarring. You have very little fine control over what you're doing, which can often make traversing these crowded environments frustrating; however this isn't new to the series - the whole Dark Pictures Anthology suffers from this problem. I can overlook these navigation issues, but the bugs are dreadful.In short: I strongly recommend that you do not buy this game. If a patch comes out that solves these issues, then I may revisit my review; however since the credits of this game showed a trailer for the next series of games that are being made, my suspicion is that the developer will be putting their efforts into their new games instead of supporting what could have been a great send-off to the series.

_childDocuments_.review: Did I like the game? Yes? Is it as good as the ones before it? From the game-play standpoint no, I felt exhausted playing it instead of enjoying and feeling the seal-less flow of the story (that was my experience with the first three games).Proc:+ visuals as good as the first three games (if they improved anything I didn't notice, even though I've played them two weeks ago in reverse order(steam sorted them by alphabet and I didn't check))+ story is even better than Man of Medan and Little Hope (but not as great as house of ashes) that were already great IMO.- poor optimization, I had to turn down settings to high+RTlight to get stable 1080p60fps, otherwise there are noticeable dips in performance to high 30s (12400f+2070super).- the "inventory" system is annoying, I wish they didn't add it.- unnecessarily complicated gameplay elements (for example, multimeter does not display anything and you don't need it to solve the puzzle, but you need to bring it up anyway. And there are a lot of such unnecessary little things)- there are a lot of bugs, I remember cyberpunk at launch, it's about twice as bad. There are some game-breaking ones that I've spent some time to find a way around.  The worst one is when certain puzzles cannot be completed using controller (I am using dualsense) because it won't recognize the right stick.- invisible walls, previous games didn't have such problem while this one had a lot of them in the middle of the ground.- too much aimless walking. Like 10 times more than in the previous games- abundance of slow traversal segments while walking. Some of them are even hard to spot (there's no prompt or light (the one that highlights points of interest) on many of them) and I ended up soft blocked (spoiler: I couldn't find the passage in the secret-bar-basement). Did I notice that you have to walk a lot? slow segments makes it even worse.- bad camera angles and camera movement (gave me motion sickness/vertigo while playing. had to take a break every 0.5-1 hour)Why I don't recommend it? Mostly because of annoying walking, my motion sickness and game-breaking bugs (why did they released it untested? Shows how they value their fans), otherwise it is a fairly good "curated" movie and totally worth its price.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, where do I begin with this game. Its probably one of the worst games of this year. Supermassive for some reason decided to just shoot itself in the foot when it comes to how this game works. Personally I see a lot of complaints with the bugs in the game which I did experience a little with a friend, but it was not terrible for me. My complaints come with how the game works. The co op experience is horrible, many times as you are exploring areas and finding clues, if one player decides to move on to the next area it will instantly teleport you to the next area while you are in the middle of clues or puzzles. Its actually stupid. It probably skips 1/3 of the game just because you get cucked out of exploring areas and solving puzzles. I dont know why they did this but its unplayable. Next is the story, the story is so bad, it makes no effort to explain its self at all and through out the game you have no idea why you are even here, you are just trying to survive. The bad guy can have god like powers, and we are just suppose to accept it like its normal, and over all I was very confused on what was happening half the time because I got skipped into the next cutscene by the other player. The ending explains nothing and makes no sense. The main bad guy is like a god or something cause he can teleport everywhere, break and skip your decisions, even when they are right, and somehow teleport onto boats going 30 mph off shore and kill everyone. The gameplay was also horrible. I probably walked around for 30 mins of the game actually doing things and exploring, the other time was just watching cut scenes I had no control over. I have seen people praising it for its "new mechanics and gameplay" which im so confused by. How is pressing the A button to jump across a gap "new mechanics" Until dawn had these kind of things. If they really think walking across a log is new mechanics, then they are way far off of making good games. Another thing, the game basically forces you into these specific situations that a cut scene forces you into. The game felt way more linear then the other games with hardly any places to explore and look around, or maybe thats because I would get cucked out of each area because the other player was in a cut scene that made me teleport to a new area. Lastly the acting and animations. The acting in this game was ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ horrible. I dont know these actors but they are basically from a 4th grade play level of voice acting and sound like npcs in the background of a video game. The characters are all extremely basic and have no chemistry and are written as deep as a kitty pool, and they also fit (THE MESSAGE) of todays standard of characters if you know what I mean. The animations were so bad and none of them made eye contact with people, heads would spasm and tweak, mouths were uncanny and oddly creepy with how they moved. This game clearly had no inspiration for writing, gameplay, mechanics, story, or anything else. Also this game is so un scary. At least the other games had jump scares, this game has like nothing creepy. Most of the game you are just being chased by some dude witha axe in a cut scene. So the tension of a chase or something is just not there. The environment is pale and bland with no creepiness or spooky looks, it just looks boring. No monsters, no ghosts, no aliens, no creepy humans, just some dude with axe and mustache chasing you in a cut scene. This game is a solid 1/10

The Dark Pictures Anthology: House of Ashes is the best of the first season, but the others, including The Devil in Me, are just okay. If you are looking to pick up this style of game, go for House of Ashes or The Quarry (Until Dawn also, if you have a PlayStation). I like Supermassive Games and the style of games they make, but these smaller projects fall short of its tent-pole releases like The Quarry and Until Dawn. I wish they would focus on one high-end product released every three years instead of these B-quality titles every year.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a pleasant surprise! Certainly better than what I was expecting after reading the reviews. I only noticed 2 very specific bugs (a wall was invisible where there should've been a wall and a random QTE popped right after another then immediately failed itself) throughout an entire playthrough. All of the UI upgrades and the basic yet intuitive inventory system helped elevate this a little more than the other DPA games in feeling more "complete". The characters weren't super amazing but each had their own conflicts and surprisingly good development as the story progresses, especially towards the end. None of them were unlike-able and they all felt distinct from each other.I may just be extremely lucky with the game not glitching for me like most people are saying and with getting the better/happier endings. It really sounds like a shame so many are having problems getting this to work properly when only a smaller number of people happen to have rarely any problems. I wasn't expecting to type such a positive review as I was cautious with the purchase while anticipating many glitches to come. only to be treated to a very well functioning game (apart from those 2 moments though of course). I've yet to play with a friend though so the problems may arise there.Overall, this was a very fun experience for me! I would say buy it when it's on sale, especially if you enjoyed the other DPA games or any interactive horror game :)Edit: 3rd glitch I forgot to mention is not getting the achievement for completing the solo story. Simply selecting continue and skipping both credits and next game trailer made it work.Edit 2: Played with a friend. A few funny glitches happened to him and he crashed twice while nothing happened on my end. It didn't interrupt or ruin the experience for him though thankfully. I supposed I really am just one of the lucky ones to experience a working version of the game.Also I really feel the need to point out that... the Signature Quartet Version of the DPA theme song "O'Death" that plays in the end credits is genuinely one of the most beautiful things I've heard in a while :)

Crouch, shimmy, crawl, jump, rotate, lift, hop, pick lock on a dilapidated desk with a business card only to find a picture of a sunflower(wtf), C'MON! This isn't Assassin's creed, we can skip the parkour and cumbersome tasks.-Some of the choices that result in a character living/dying are arbitrary. There's one particular scene halfway through the game  that I am unable to logically reason as to why you would know the correct decision beforehand. Never in a previous game have I been unable to find where I went wrong after a poor decision, while several moments in this game have left me frustrated because the choices are up to chance.Still worth a play-through at full price imo, but I can't say I didn't get frustrated because of these issues (and a few minor bugs). 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: I want to preface that I have played all The Dark Pictures Anthology games at least twice before playing this one, so I have plenty of experience going into the fourth installment. Before playing, I was a little hesitant to play since House of Ashes was my least favorite, but after playing I was surprised at this game. The Devil in Me offers a unique game play experience that the previous titles do not have. As the game play style stays on track with previous titles in this series, this game finally allows the player to have a sense of exploration. While I was playing I felt that I had the ability to explore the world while having the opportunity to tailor the story to my choices. With the ability to explore and make choices that affect the other characters in their paths, it added a new unique layer of ethical choices. All positives aside, there are some negatives. There are some moments where I experienced stuttering and poorly timed loading screens during a crucial scene which took me out of the experience, but that is in now way a reason to not enjoy this game. Overall, if you are looking for a fun horror game experience that offers a fun story with a lot of twists and turns you will love it. You can play either solo or with a friend, but if you want the best experience, I would play solo since playing with a friend makes you miss specific cut scenes since you might not be controlling a specific character. Note to Developers (If Read): I hope you keep this same play style for future games because this one has made me excited for future entries of The Dark Pictures Anthology.

_childDocuments_.review: The story in this game is really, really good in my opinion but there are definitely some head scratching things about this game I noticed in my playthrough.I've played all of the games from this series on stream and it was a no brainer to pick this one up to stream upon release as well. I seen all the bug issues on twitter and YouTube so I decided to wait a couple days to see if they ironed out. Playing this multiplayer was definitely.... a headache. The mechanics felt super clunky, the QTE's sometimes didn't pop up due to lag and bugs loading in the textures, resources, etc. At times, your partner would teleport away from you and not be able to play because they were under or above the map frozen. One of the crewmates in my story died due to my QTE's and choices not popping up in certain scenarios, so that was annoying as h***.At times during QTE's my character would just freeze and it would take me out of my motion or from watching the monitors, or doing certain tasks. Your screen will lock randomly and you'll have to keep pausing/unpausing your game to fix it to allow free range of motion again. The bugs are definitely making this game egregious currently, but it is also still good and fun. It was honestly one of my favorite story games of the series next to "Little Hope". The atmosphere and situations you are put into definitely bring that "horror" aspect to it better than the others in this series. Sound score and scares are good as well. (I've also heard that most of these bugs only occur in multiplayer, not as often as solo. So i'll be playing again to test the experience out one more time.)I hope they address the bugs and clunky mechanics with a patch and fix soon because in my opinion that is the only thing holding it back; other than that this game is really good.

_childDocuments_.review: As a gripping addition to The Dark Pictures Anthology, "The Devil in Me" offers a thrilling and suspenseful narrative experience. The multiplayer aspect enhances the replay value, allowing friends to share in the suspense together. While some narrative choices may feel familiar to series veterans, the overall execution and engaging gameplay make "The Devil in Me" a solid installment in this anthology of interactive horror tales.

_childDocuments_.review: I give it a thumbs up but with heavy critique. I played it with a friend through the movie story using remote play, which worked fine despite some hiccups with the streaming. Overall I believe I would have rated the game 6/10. I do support the Dark Anthology games as they do make for an interesting game play with friends. Personally I wouldn't have played these games by myself in single-player.Straight to the point:Ignoring the introduction of the game and straight to the actual group you're playing - So we enter this area and mysterious things happen. You soon realise things aren't as they should be which should be expected from entering a murder hotel that this game is about.Starting with the negativeThe camera at times doesn't feel right, and sometimes it just seem way too close. The same can be said with pointing light at things and it just felt jerky. I can also say that it makes hard to find things when everything is dark literally 90% of the time and your groups items are real bad at illuminating. Also: What is the point with giving a super good flashlight near the end of the game when you don't need it? Troll us?Throughout the game, several times there are things that just doesn't make any sense at all example the big flashlight. In several scenes people don't react according to how they would in real life. Things that make no logical sense - like people not hearing sounds they would of heard in real life. People who ignore facts and information that was just put right in front of them. A superb example of this is in the end of the game which I must say felt rushed and open. There was no closure to a game that needs closure. There's no continuation to this game planned. If you don't mind spoilers you can read in more detail below.The positive about the game is that it had a nice atmosphere, despite feeling cramped. You understand the killer and the people more and more as you read through the documents and info put through the game. You understand his background, what he enjoys and why he enjoys doing what he does and so on. Overall the game feels like it manages to replicate something a disturbed person like that would enjoy. It is fun to play with friends, and I think the game is either a love and hate thing. This game would be better if you ignore all the stupid things that happen in the game. In addition - In all fairness, it would make more sense if the documentary crew stayed at least one day before they were exposed to his scheme to end them. That way he would have time to study them a bit more in his environment. But it is what it is.Gameplay 5/10Story 7/10Events: 5/10Characters 5/10Obstacles/puzzles/challenges 6/10Overall: 6/10Before buying I recommend buying the game if you are especially interested after making some research or if the game is on discount.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are easily irritated or (like most people nowadays) aggravated by technical hiccups, wait for a few patches - especially if you are playing in other languages than english. Once I had another bug, with voices being played through a filter as if they were on tape, but after a few minutes, it went back to normal. Facial animations are stiffer than in the first game, Men of Medan, even the ever enjoyable Curators, but if you don't meddle on these kind of things, the technical side is passable. The story in itself is not as good as House of Ashes, but it is a good slasher-story by itself, with some geniunely tense, sometimes even scary setpieces, there are little cheap jumpscares (even though there are some), the story has a nice flow with some pretty unexpected turns (some not as much) plus a great showdown (with a great title-song-rendition in the end), and the characters are mostly likeable. The english dub especially is great, with nuanced and fitting performances. If you like this kind of horror (Saw, Friday the 13th), can get over some technical issues and don't mind the price of admission, I'd say give it a go. If you have played other games in the franchise, you mostly know what you are getting. I had a fun time playing through the story and will definately do so again. _childDocuments_.review: The Devil in Me is one of the best ones in the series since Until Dawn. The story gets back to its rooms by stringing together several different mysteries and elements. Plus, the introduction of new mechanics (i.e. Mark's camera, balancing, inventory, etc.) made game play refreshing. Plus, I love that there is a difficulty setting. The atmosphere of this game is great. The spooky murder hotel genuinely scared me at several points. I believe this game has the best replay-ability out of the four. I'm actually excited to jump back in and see things I've missed and piece together the parts of the mystery I wasn't able to the first time.That doesn't mean the game doesn't have its cons. Some scenes are drawn out by repetitive puzzles (if I have to move one more crate to get up/down, I swear...) while others try to nudge you along the exploratory process with unhelpful dialogue like "We can't just stand around!" I'm not standing around, Brenda. I'm looking for dead people mouth coins! Additionally, the graphics tend to be glitchy, but that can mostly be adjusted in the settings to make it...less glitchy.Overall: 8/10. Would save the dog again.

(I'm looking at you, Little Hope)I can still say that I would recommend the entire series, each game for their own reasons.The best, in order.Man of Medan Devil In MeHouse of Ashes ties with Little Hope (Corny writing, not much scare after awhile. Sadly, Devil In Me fell into that same trap as the game went on.)Shock value can only work for so long until character decisions are just comical.Excited for Season 2. Will, probably, purchase all of them.As for the new comers that are unsure about any bits of the series, wait for a sale and expectt some interesting levels of disappointment.I hope we get a better understanding of how these stories have ended, cause there's a lot of confusion with very little insight.And, though this won't matter, I'm hoping for a longer span of time between games to allow more effort and consideration for story and character development.May update after replaying co-op. _childDocuments_.review: Update: Completed a solo player run. All I can say is, it is disappointing this game had so many bugs. For me this is a game I default to two player, so the fact that all the bugs seem to only be in two player makes me sad. With that said, this is probably my favorite story line released yet and one of the best in terms of fear factor. If this had released with no issues, it would be my favorite of the series.P.S. If you're reading this game devs, less heavy breathing please. It was the loudest and most constant audio to the point where it was funny, not scary.First Playthrough Review (More to be seen):Wow. This is the storyline I wanted from the last two entries. It is absolutely excellent. The jumpscares were actually scary and on the whole it did the aura of imminent danger well. I was actually scared on multiple occasions. That being said, the game suffered in other departments again. The facial rendering was uncanny valley in a way that it hasn't been in previous entries. The eyes would never looked *quite* where the focus should be from the other characters, The camera would get stuck at weird angles. This would force darker sequences from difficult to navigate, to outright blind. Additionally, there were multiple bugs that caused items to get stuck in the characters hands, through cut scenes. Cut scenes also seemed to be cut short. Entire visual elements were missing (tape recorders played audio, but I discovered video in single player). I got locked into a character getting killed, because I could not pick up the item I needed to escape, so it skipped an entire sequence and got a character killed when my partner got to the end of this component. Finally, and why this is maybe 2nd or 3rd in my favorites, it took OVER AN HOUR for my friend and I to exit the prologue. We disconnected over and over. We couldn't connect to the server. We couldn't connect  to each other. We didn't appear as in game. There are a number of issues that need to ironed out in the early days,I will be playing again...the story was that good.

_childDocuments_.review: Its a mixed review, since its the weakest entry out of the "Dark Pictures" Games. And because I liked the three prior games, I will give it a recommendation regardless. If you are not a fan of the prior games or this would be your first entry, do yourself a favor and try the others first.First of all - the things I actually liked: The cast, the voice-acting, some new gameplay elements (walking around with the microphone in the dark was kinda cool!) and that it takes a real-life serial killer as inspiration.Sadly, thats also one of its biggest flaws - since you do know who you are up against pretty early AND since there are NO supernatural things involved at all this time, I would rather say that this game is a thriller-movie, not a horror-movie.Yes, the previous game also are not THAT scary, but atleast there were some creative scares, a chilling atmosphere and the "fear of the unknown" - all that gets completely wiped away by setting up a standard killer. Three jumpscares got me, but thats about it. No horror at all here. And that's very disappointing. Also, I get why they chose this killer design and it makes sense, but there is nothing menacing about him at all. No creepy Michael Myers Stares from the distance, no evil spirit possessing the killer, nothing.TLDR: A few new and nice gameplay elements, a likeable and "realistic" cast get ultimately dumped on by a more grounded and "real" story with no supernatural elements and/or horror elements and I don't know if that is the right approach to the series.If you are looking for a scary experience, you might rather want to check the other 3 games out. This is more like a thriller than a horror-story.Regardless, I do hope there are many more seasons to come because I really like their games.

_childDocuments_.review: The Devil in Me is a great addition to the Dark Pictures anthology and a solid conclusion to Season 1. Supermassive Games have taken all that they have learnt from their previous titles and implemented it along with player feedback to reach a solid final product.-Advanced mobility (e.g. climbing, crawling etc.) -Inventory mechanic that allows each character to have a couple unique gameplay additions-Longer narrative than previous entries but not too long-The story was delivered well-The usual secrets and clues are solid as always-I have yet to encounter any bugs, frame issues, animation problems etc. (Solo story only so far, Shared story is often more buggy)-Characters aren't the most fleshed out of the series (they are still good though)-I can see the inventory items being on the border of feeling like a gimmick to some people-Seems like Curator's cut (or Shared story) required for achievements which is only available after at least a month of launch (or as pre-order bonus)-The 'highs' where not quite as high as previous games but the 'lows' weren't as lowOverall, I found The Devil in Me to be very enjoyable from start to finish and welcome all the new innovations Supermassive have put forward and commend that they have taken onboard player feedback in meaningful ways to improve the experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot in good conscience recommend this game. As a fan of the previous three installments, I had high hopes for this one, but it left me sorely disappointed. The abundance of glitches, especially when playing online, significantly hindered my enjoyment. It's disheartening when Quick Time Events (QTEs) are marred by technical issues, making it difficult to gauge success or failure.The level design proved to be a frustrating aspect of the game. There were numerous instances where I found myself confused, unsure of the intended path to progress. It's frustrating to discover that poorly designed climbing sections were the answer, bearing little resemblance to their intended purpose. It felt like wasted time and detracted from the overall experience.One aspect that left me particularly unimpressed was the excessive use of jumpscares. While jumpscares can be an effective tool in creating tension, their overuse in this game felt forced and predictable. It cheapened the fear factor and undermined any genuine sense of dread.Overall, this game failed to meet my expectations. The prevalence of glitches, confusing level design, and reliance on overused jumpscares left me feeling unsatisfied. I would caution others to think twice before investing in this title, as there are likely more enjoyable gaming options available.

_childDocuments_.review: By far the worst in the series. Now that claim and my recommendation do not go hand in hand but I'll explain why I feel this way. If you've been playing the dark pictures games and played the last 3, then, despite this one not holding up, there's no reason not to get it. I'm playing quite some time after launch so the bugs were mostly ironed out and overall the game worked as intended so if you're thinking about picking this up, I'd say do so.As for why this is the worst, it's simply because it had the most interesting ideas with a very sloppy execution. The characters are very one beat (apart from good ol' Charlie Lonnit!) and have very little to offer in terms of character and arcs (so much so that the has curator sit down to explain to you their individual arcs when you finish the game, or at least in my ending). The characters are also frustratingly obtuse making it impossible to enjoy this as a dark thriller/murder mystery and making it more of a comedy. There's also just a bunch of stuff that straight up isn't and can't be explained by the end of the story and it all just feels a bit messy.I also spent time watching YouTubers play through the game and this shows where it gets really sloppy. I was able to keep everyone alive and therefore I got the majority of scenes. However, if some characters die, instead of replacing scenes they just cut them and it often makes it seem as though the killer is practically teleporting. A good example of this is in Jacksepticeye's 4th video on the game at 26:27 through to 27:07.But, to give negative feedback along side positive feedback, it's worth noting that they really did try to do something new and it's definitely the right direction, it just needs some tweaking. The new camera system is SO MUCH better than the previous 3 games. It now feels like I'm actually playing a video game rather than watching an interactive movie. The inventory system is also a nice addition. However, it's made redundant in that who ever you're playing as will always have the tool they need to do the job in front of them. An example of this is Charlie's business card. He can use his card to open drawers that are locked... The only issue is that the drawers are only locked when you play as Charlie, so why bother? A suggestion I would make is have you stumble across these drawers as a character who can't open it and then have a chance for Charlie to walk through later on and if the player remembers, they can open the drawer.Overall I was displeased with the game but mainly because it was the most disappointing. It has so many good ideas that are ruined by the actual script itself. The bare-bones story is fine, its just ran through the mud with the ridiculous characters and almost comedic moments of stupidity. That said, I don't regret buying this game. I was also going to buy it and I was always going to play it to the end. It still has a lot of good stuff in here and I really hope they keep moving in this new game play direction and just improve upon what they started with this game. If you like the dark pictures games there will be plenty of moments in this game for you to enjoy (and also the little teaser for the next game really had my hyped).

_childDocuments_.review: The Devil in Me manages to build up an eerie atmosphere, and there were many times I was on edge and felt scared. The game has a very good foundation, based on H.H. Holmes, but the developers lost themselves in the making of the script. Many parts of the game is just complete garbage and completely illogical, with many plot holes. The game begins with a prologue where we get to play a newly married couple, checking in at H.H. Holmes hotel. This part is poorly written, with really bad voice actors having pillow fights before being murdered. It was very ridiculous and the worst I've seen when it comes to voice acting, script, and execution from Supermassive Games.We are then introduced to our 5 main characters who receive an invitation to a castle on an island where they can stay and spend the night while filming their documentary. What they don't know is that they have been tricked into becoming part of a killer's games. If some random person offered you a free vacation, would you believe it and go? Stupid. The characters are not very likeable and are very slow and stupid most of the time. The characters are very lifeless, the facial expressions are ugly and do not feel believable, and the dialogue is bad most of the time. There is a dog in this game, and it only has a few minutes of screen time. Still, you care way more about the dog than all of the characters combined.The funnest part of these games is when there are likable characters that you actually care about and want to see survive, and how the choices you make affect those characters, in a reasonable way. This was not the case with this game, and is the biggest reason why it is a worse game than its predecessors. Many of the decisions you make in this game lead to serious consequences that are completely impossible to figure out beforehand, and can lead to the sudden death of the characters. The outcome of the decisions you make or the outcome of the QTE's, whether you fail or not, are very uneven. Many times it doesn't matter which of the decisions you choose or how well you perform, because it still leads to the same outcome. Sometimes all you have to do is fail a single QTE or make a wrong decision, and your character dies. Other times you can get five Stay Calm moments in a row, and it doesn't matter if you complete 0/5 or 5/5, the result will still be the same. Then why even put that in that scene in the first place? I'm referring to a scene where Kate is being chased by the murderer on the rooftop and hides in a locker.Another stupid example is the suffocation chamber when you have to choose whether you want to save Kate or Erin. Me and my buddies thought the killer wants us to choose, so we let the time run out, and maybe both will survive. But no, it automatically killed Erin. The right choice is to pick "Kill Kate". If you choose to kill Kate, the door opens for Erin. Kate is suffocating in there and she then notices that there is a leak in the window so Mark can break it and save her. She notices this AFTER you have made your choice, and there are no clues as to how to save both, not even a Black Framed Picture. HOW are you supposed to know this? This was so idiotically written that we wanted to shut down the game.Charlie has a way of dying that is one of the dumbest ways ever in any of these games. You have to use your balance and walk across a board that is between a house and a cliff, and if you fail, you fall to your death, which happened to us and we found it really boring. It would have been better if he had just broken his ankle or something, which makes it harder for him to survive later, but not impossible. That would have been more exciting.In one of the endings, you manage to escape from the island with a boat. The killer tries to chop the boat with the axe just as you leave, but he fails. The boat drives out to sea at full speed and after a while, out of nowhere, the killer slams the axe on the side of the boat and climbs into the boat. If you manage to fight him off, you throw the anchor at him, the anchor gets stuck in his chest, the chain gets stuck in the engine, and he is pulled into the engine under the boat and there is a lot of blood in the water. We then learn that he survived. I have so many questions regarding this final scene. Where was he while the boat was speeding out to sea? It is a small boat, where there are not many places to hold on to, and since he was nowhere to be seen, he must have been under the boat. How does he manage to stay under the small boat for so long? And manage to get the axe with him as well? How can he swing the axe like that from under the boat to the edge on top of the boat? How did he survive after being shreded by the engine? Or, how could the engine shred him if the chain gets caught in the engine and slows it down or even make it stop? How could the boat continue to run after the chain got stuck in the engine? Where does the blood come from? Either the killer is pulled into the engine, blood comes out, he is shredded and dies, the engine is destroyed by his body and the chain, causing the boat to stop. Or, he gets pulled overboard, the chain somehow comes loose from the engine, he survives, and the boat continues to run at full speed. It can't be all these things at the same time. Just very illogical and stupid.In another ending, without going into the details of how to accomplish this, Mark and Kate manage to survive by escaping the island on the ferry. Just when the ferry is about to stop at the mainland, it starts to go back to the island where the killer is. The killer then stands there waiting for them, with a sniper rifle, and shoots them dead when the ferry approaches the island's coast. Sooo poorly written. Why didn't they just jump off the ferry when it was like two meters from the mainland? Nope, they stay on the ferry and go back to the island, just to die. And why not contact the police when Mark reach the mainland? So the ending was a real anticlimax, no matter which ending you get, because you also don't get to know who (or what) the killer is.Something else that was also very illogical was how the killer manages to control everything everywhere at the same time. For example, how he can close certain walls while hunting his victims? He is not in his control room at that time!Mark can take pictures of special objects/scenes whenever Mark is playable. When you aim the camera, and the reticle turns green, you know that you should take a photo of that object. But why? It has no impact whatsoever for the sake of the story, nor can you look at the pictures you've taken. There are 27 different occasions that Mark must photograph, but it is only for the sake of an achievement.The Devil in Me felt like a rushed ending to the first season, and it's far from their best game. A good idea and a good scary atmosphere that scared me many times, but the cons of the game are too great. The script was too poorly thought out and sloppily executed, the characters too dumb and unlikable, the decisions were mostly pointless and the deaths were unsatisfactory and stupid. Also too much platforming for this kind of game. Hard to say if I recommend this game or not. If you are not a super critic, and a fan of Supermassive Games and have some friends to play this couch Co-Op with, then yes I recommend you to play this game, at least once. Otherwise, probably best to stay away. 4/10.
