_childDocuments_.review: Inbento is a relaxing, wholesome gastronomic grid puzzle series. Players help a seemingly single parent Mama Cat make nutritious meals for child cat. I grew up in a food-based culture, so these home cooked meal puzzles evoke nostalgia. Epicureans will recognize some mouth watering tiles. For starter, there's salmon, radish, tamago (japanese folded eggs), spinach gomaae (Spinach Salad with Sesame Dressing), tomatoes and more. Each level has 9 puzzles laid out on 1 page. Each page unlocks a new puzzle mechanic, a new bento box theme, and a cute cat story cut scene unfolds between Mama Cat and her child. Low key, all chill no thrill, moderately to adequately challenging in later puzzles (does not inflict pain and suffering), kids friendly, no adrenaline rush, no heighten sense of accomplishment. Might make you hungry.Recommended for all ages puzzle lovers who wish to practice some multi-steps spacial awareness. Depending on the level, you can pick it up to unwind before sleep or something to do on the side.

_childDocuments_.review: After hours and hours, I gave in the temptation to look in a guide. The puzzles are extremely well-done. I got to give credits to the programmer who thought about and implemented them. In fact, to the entire team. Thank you inbento team for creating such a wholesome game.Asian tradition, family legacy, life cycle... A bildungsroman at its best. The story follows the journey of the Son (the orange cat) from babyhood to adulthood. He sees his Mother (the white cat) working on the perfect bento box, he learns this art from her and, when the right time arises, he will have to showcast his skills at work or... to pass this knowledge to his own child (the orange-brown cat).Would the Son be able to stand up to his family tradition? Help him arrange the perfect bento boxes. Let's see if you can beat these puzzles. It's not easy as they seem. PROS: - Cute and wholesome drawings;- Nice music;- Simple to complex puzzles;- Up to 14 levels, 9 puzzles each;- A hidden puzzle;- The money from this game goes to animal shelters!CONS:- Some puzzles are too complex (that's from my pov);- Nothing else.If you love cats and puzzles, this is a game for you!

_childDocuments_.review: is an adorable game about a mother cat assembling bento boxes for her kitten's lunches. The story is simple yet sweet. You play as a mother cat who learns new recipes to assemble bento boxes for her kitten’s lunch the next day. The premise of the game is pretty straight forward. You're given a recipe, an empty bento box and ingredients. The goal is to match the layout of the recipe. The further you level up the more complex it gets. There are over 100 levels to master and no time limit so you can relax and not feel rushed as the puzzles become more complex. It is also a game you can jump in and out of and not have to play all in one sitting. In fact it is best played in increments.  started off as a mobile game so at its core design that is obvious. However it does translate well to a PC game. It does support controllers but I played with a mouse. Visually the game is cute. Cute cats making cute food. I think the combination is an automatic win for most who love cat games. The art is a cartoon style with a pleasing colour palette. There are 14 levels (9 puzzles in each) with one bonus achievement to grab if you scroll to the end of the credits when you're done with all the levels. This game does get repetitive even though the mechanics change up every level. It is a game played in chucks to pass some time here and there. I recommend getting this one on sale.  🍱

_childDocuments_.review: is a short and moderately challenging puzzler that's well-designed and great to play a level or two as a distraction throughout your day. It's a bit short for the base price of $5, coming in at roughly 3-4 hours, but is a fun time for the duration that it lasts. Grab this on sale if you're a fan of puzzle games!
_childDocuments_.name: inbento

_childDocuments_.review: A very cute and relaxing bento puzzle ^^Like that the developers support their game even after a long time!Inspired by the art of Japanese bento-making, this game stands out with its minimalist design, calming aesthetic, and deeply satisfying puzzle mechanics. At its core, inbento combines elements of food preparation and spatial arrangement to create a unique puzzle experience that’s both relaxing and mentally engaging.
_childDocuments_.name: inbento

_childDocuments_.review: Cosy and casual puzzle game with cute cats.As shown in the trailer, your goal of each level is to match a pattern of bento using the gadgets given to you, which can be a motif of tiles, a transposition of tiles, etc.There are 14 Worlds, each with 9 levels.  Almost every World introduces a new gadget, so the puzzles barely feel repetitive. The difficult curve is also gentle, with a slight difficulty spike in World 10-12. Other than that, the game remains relaxing. It takes me around 5 hours to 100% the game.Finishing each World awards you some lovely 2D cutscenes with parallax. The captions of certain cutscenes are given as the names of achievements. Together, these cutscenes tell a heart-warming story of a cat mother raising and preparing bentos for her kid.The UI is simple and efficient; it has reset and undo buttons, as it should for a turn-based puzzle game. The art is cute, so is the background music.Conclusion: Recommended for all casual gamers or puzzle lovers. Perhaps you should also consider getting the Afterburn Puzzle Bundle; their games all share the same cosy vibe and cute art.
_childDocuments_.name: inbento

_childDocuments_.review: An adorable bento puzzle game that gets increasingly difficult the further you progress through the levels. Also, as you play the game you get a cute short story biased on the cats making the bentos. If you aren't sure about the price, the game goes down to about 2$ on sale, HOWEVER I think the price is fair in my opinion. For the Achievement Hunters out there, the achievements are "easy" to obtain as long as you complete the puzzles and the extra one at the end of the credits. If you do so happen to get stuck there are guides to each and every puzzle. P.S. This game has Steam Trading Cards if you are interested in that sort of thing.
_childDocuments_.name: inbento

_childDocuments_.review: Super cute, aesthetically pleasing, pleasantly challenging; in my view, inbento does not fail on any front. It's a brain-scratcher of a puzzle game, but never to the extent that you want to claw your face off in frustration.One of its biggest strengths is the myriad of movement mechanisms you must utilise to correctly rearrange your lunchbox. The gameplay feels innovative and fresh, and held my interest very well. As you advance, each 'world' introduces more of these puzzle-solving tools, and your bento boxes grow more complex. (Satisfyingly so.)My first play session stretched on for quite some time - a lot longer than originally intended. The game sucks you in and compels you to complete it. It's just very enjoyable. (And I don't think I've empathised with a fictional character as much as the ever-weary mama cat.) Additionally, the art is HECKIN' cute. Shout out to the artists for designing some of my favourite emoticons ever. 🥇I highly recommend this game to all cat lovers, puzzle lovers, and knackered parents alike!
_childDocuments_.name: inbento

_childDocuments_.review: Got boring about halfway through and completely forgot about it for almost a year. The keyboard controls are highly unresponsive, tested on multiple devices - very often registers only one key press out of five or more. Overall not really PC-worthy, it just feels like a mobile game that is good but not enough to justify a PC version. I also checked the mobile reviews and it is apparently behind a subscription paywall, giving another reason for a negative review.
_childDocuments_.name: inbento

_childDocuments_.review: Cute lil bento puzzle game with a wholesome lil visual novel after you beat a puzzle world (no real story just watching the cat grow up). the UI is kinda hard to get used to but the puzzles are unique and they introduce or combine different puzzle mechanics in each chapter so each chapter has its own unique feel. Small details like the change in food was chapters progress really paint a wholesome story of getting older and learning to take care of those who took care of you, and cherishing family tradition
_childDocuments_.name: inbento

_childDocuments_.review: This is game best described as 'gentle'. It's cute and generally just very feel good. I bought this to play when I want to do  but not quite sure what that something is. It's great when you've got a little bit of time before food is ready or when you want a break before a meeting starts etcThere's a heartwarming story within this puzzle game that is a nice motivator to keep going to get all of the level end screens. It's really well done in terms of meshing the art, the music, and the puzzle design, really great workOverall, highly recommend. There's lots of levels and sometimes the puzzles can be quite challenging - if you do get stuck I'd recommend giving it 10 minutes or so and then coming back another time and seeing if anything new jumps out at you
_childDocuments_.name: inbento

_childDocuments_.review: inbento is great, short puzzle game about creating bento boxes. By placing, moving, mirroring and adjusting you have to recreate a given bento box with the food that is either already in the box or part of your tools. This is a genius take on the puzzle genre and makes way for some really creative mechanics and puzzles that make your head hurt.This game is really creative and, besides the last two levels, always tries to add a new mechanic or function for you to work with in each passing chapter. That's right, chapter. Whilst progressing through the levels, inbento tells a short yet beautiful story about a young cat growing up with eating their mom's bento boxes for lunch, and eventually making their own as an adult. It's not too meaningful, but it doesn't have to be. The story is heartwarming and illustrated by beautiful artwork. And that's really about it. The game gets quite tough at the end but overall has a great length to it. I picked this game up for about a dollar and i can only recommend it. It's not too thrilling but perfect to take your mind off of things for a bit and relax. The only thing i somewhat disliked were the mediocre tutorials. which show you what you have to do using pointers, almost like a mobile game (just found out it actually is also on mobile). I think a more thorough tutorial would've been great. At one point i was stuck because i didn't know you can turn the squares once you had taken them out, because it was never explained to me. Anyhow, this game is worth it for such a cheap price, there is really nothing to complain.Final Score: 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: inbento

_childDocuments_.review: A soothing game about packing bento lunches. You follow the story of a mother cat and her child as you pack lunches through 14 chapters of 9 levels each. Confronted with tiles of food to place in specific patterns, you must determine the order and rotation of the tiles to form the pattern in the lunch box. You basically get a couple hours of relaxing gameplay for peanuts.My one criticism is that the music loops are a bit short, so you end up listening to the same loop over and over again per chapter, which can get somewhat repetitive. The visuals, however, are perfectly calming, and I found myself delighted by the little images that tell the story of the cats.4/5, with a star knocked off for the music irritating me a bit at one point. This is, however, a problem easily remedied by muting the music and playing your own tunes in the background.
_childDocuments_.name: inbento

_childDocuments_.review: While Railbound and Golf Peaks by the developer are interesting, well thought out puzzle games that require pure logic to work out, inbento sadly often feels like luck and guesswork. The presentation is super cute, the music is chill and the art style is a simple joy to look at, but the puzzle mechanics get frustrating quickly around the halfway mark of the game. That is because there are many mechanics that overlap each other. Your goal is to mimic the bento box in the top right of the screen, but, depending on the puzzle setup, ingredients can be moved, stacked on top of each other, removed and then put in, swapped - a lot of times in the same level.You can see where this is going - trial & error. After chapter 7, a lot of levels have 5 or 6 tiles that you either place or use to manipulate other tiles, so you have to think several steps ahead while trying out some random things, which becomes unfeasible at some point. The result is a stressful puzzle experience for the second half of the game, but a fun chill game for the first half. Sadly, I will have to give this a downvote, but it is still a cute puzzle game to play and the two followup games by Afterburn are a lot better and allow you more logical paths to the solution!
_childDocuments_.name: inbento

_childDocuments_.review: A simple puzzle game with a heartwarming story.There is a bento box to be made. There is a picture in your book how it should look like, but your pieces doesn't fit! You have to stack them over and use specials titles that can do tricks to achieve your goal.Inbento is easy at first, but the difficulty slowly and constantly increases, so the later levels are really challenging.Personally, I fell in love with this game.
_childDocuments_.name: inbento

_childDocuments_.review: Nice relaxing game. Have plenty of levels to clear but if one is frustrated to progress on, there's always that button to clear it all for you. But, it's not encouraging to do so. LOL~ All in all, it's a good game with a nice and simple story to tell in a cute picture by picture approach. The levels are decent, not too difficult but not too easy either. So, if you like solving puzzles, do give this game a try. It's soothing and can be played at your own pace. ( 7 / 10 )
_childDocuments_.name: inbento

_childDocuments_.review: Game is cute, fun and shortBut don't let the silly kitties fool you, some puzzles are pretty hard and will ask you to think out of the boxThe game could definitely use a hint system for some of the puzzles, but since it's so short (14 "worlds" and 9 levels for each) it's not like playing it without any hint was a chore, just yeah it's not rare to have 1 puzzle taking you a bit of time only for the 5 next ones to be easy.

_childDocuments_.review: When it comes to relaxing puzzle games, I usually mention LYNE as an example. Sure, that game does become utterly repetitive after some time due to exceedingly high number of levels, but it introduces one playstyle and sticks with it until the very end. While the puzzles do get more difficult and trial & error gets involved, the game never goes overly complex with its mechanics.The game in question here, inbento, does the exact opposite. Make no mistake, the game looks adorable with its story segments and starts as a very relaxing puzzle game, but unfortunately goes to the other end of the difficulty spectrum pretty fast. And I cannot bring myself to fault the game and its developers for this.I think the most defining feature of inbento is its presentation; especially when it comes to the story. The story in inbento is told through images in between each world, which tell the tale of a cat family through time, seemingly feeding mainly on bentos for some reason. And the artwork and the progression of the story is done very adorably. In fact, so adorable that you cannot shake this feeling that one of the main characters is definitely going to die, if the usual trend of storytelling in media is to be taken into account. Don't worry though, that's not gonna happen.That's the question I once asked myself as well.Bento is a single-portion take-out or home-packed meal, very common in eastern countries and especially Japan. It's basically various food such as rice, vegetables and meat packed together in one box (usually wood or metal... sometimes plastic), with these contents sometimes being arranged in a way to look like popular characters or a specific shape. So basically, you have the perfect setting for a puzzle/casual game here.However, inbento doesn't go into the design aspect of them and instead, focuses on arranging the contents next to each other to match a specific pattern. In each level, you are given a picture in the top right corner of the screen, and are tasked with using all of the tools and ingredients the game gives you to mimic that. In the first half of the game, it feels like it's going to be a short but relaxing experience, being challenging but not going overboard with it. But then...Unfortunately, inbento suddenly does a 180 after reaching the half-way point. The first 7-8 worlds are actually fine, with each of them focusing on usage of a specific mechanic to finish the levels with. But from that point onwards, the game runs out of new mechanic ideas until world 13 and starts to use most of them together. This creates a sharp difficulty spike in puzzle design and introduces the element of trial & error in the worst way possible; because all of the puzzles are are designed in a way that you would need a lot of experimentation, or the ability to visualize the results, to solve them.For reference, here's all of the mechanics this game introduces over time and expects you to use for puzzle solving. I'll spoiler them just in case:I think you can see how complex the puzzles can get when the game starts using a couple of these together at the same time, which it does. Couple this with the lack of any hints whatsoever, and you are left with a title that suddenly switches from an adorable and relaxing puzzle game to a frustrating brain-teaser right in the middle of it.And I don't know whether to blame the game and its developers for this or myself, as the store page describes the game as both a "brain-teaser" and a "chill" puzzle game; two words that don't go together! I guess it was my fault for not reading the main store description very well, but the devs should have known that the second half of the game is not chill, but brutally difficult.I wish Steam had a neutral option akin to the "Informational" tag in the curators, so I could have chosen that instead. But since I don't have that, I'm going to lean more towards the "Recommended" option. I really cannot fault a game for being brutally hard and aside from that, the game actually feels nice in other aspects. Just make sure you know what you're getting into before you buy this game.A short game (1~2 hrs) that starts off as an adorable yet relaxing puzzle game, then suddenly becomes a brutally hard brain-teaser from the half-way point and onward. Keep that in mind before buying.

_childDocuments_.review: A therapeutic puzzle game with Cats and Bento! I would say this game is worth the purchase if you're looking for a brain teasing-cuteness overload-sweet story game. Some puzzles can be trickier than others, so it takes time but it is enjoyable nonetheless. The soundtrack makes for a calm play time and the story telling makes for a heart warming experience. The trading cards and stickers are also an extra cute addition to your profile! 10/10 Bento points from me! ... now I want to eat.. hehe
_childDocuments_.name: inbento

_childDocuments_.review: a really lovely little puzzle game with cute theming and a cute story to go with it ♥I completed about 90% of the puzzles in inbento on mobile over a handful of hours before my attention was pulled to other things - I'm happy to be supporting the team by buying a second copy on PC for a couple dollars to finish up those last few levels and see the ending.
_childDocuments_.name: inbento

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very good puzzle game. You have to organize items in a grid box, with a fixed set of moves and pieces to add. It starts easy enough but introduces many mechanics and later puzzles are quite hard to figure out, but since there are about 4 different "moves" to make in each level, with some reasoning you can solve them, it never gets too hard to be frustrating. Totally recommended if you like casual puzzle games
_childDocuments_.name: inbento

_childDocuments_.review: On the whole, I liked Inbento and thought it to be a decent puzzle game.I really like how the game is presented. The pictures and the soft piano music are very charming. The colours and graphics are bright and pleasant.There are 14 stages with 9 levels each and new mechanics will be introduced as you progress. These include swapping pieces, taking pieces out to put in later, pushing pieces across, and copying pieces to another spot.Some levels I breezed through - either because they were easy or subconsciously I knew what to do once I started. Some levels I stumbled upon the answer after a while and thought myself lucky.Other levels I really struggled (hence my total hours). Levels 12-5, 13-9 and 14-9 just had me stumped.Admittedly, I had to look up the solution for these three. For 12-5 I was missing one obvious step and felt silly when I realised. But the other two... I just don't think I would have ever completed them by myself, as much as I tried.This is where the many mechanics put together had me at a blank. There were so many variables in the puzzle I didn't know where to begin. Did I have to take some pieces out first? Which piece do I push across, and when? I couldn't figure out the logic, sadly, and I kept arriving at the same incorrect endings despite trying to do different things.I think my brain doesn't do very well with these types of puzzles.Nonetheless, it was good to try and I recommend this game on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: inbento

_childDocuments_.review: This is difficult to review because for the first half of the game I was having such a good time, the comfy art and music made it so relaxing to just pick away at the puzzles. Then World 8 onwards hit and the difficulty spike jumped up to the point that it wasn't really enjoyable anymore and I had to keep tabbing out to look at a guide for hints on piece rotation or even entire puzzles. I feel like with how little you have to go off towards the end, some of these puzzles would be borderline impossible without hours of trial and error. Overall, not really very enjoyable.4/10
_childDocuments_.name: inbento

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun and charming game about solving puzzles putting food into bento boxes, with a little narrative about a cat family between the worlds levels. It was overall pretty fun, but being not much of a puzzle gamer myself, it may be hard to recommend to a casual puzzle fan and/or someone who hates having to look up solutions for puzzles. The game was pretty challenging and I found myself having to refer to a guide many times, the challenge really ramps up after the first couple of levels. People who enjoy the charming aesthetic and the game and like very challenging puzzlers, this would be a good fit for you, at full price, if you're not sure about the challenge definitely pick it up on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: inbento

_childDocuments_.review: It's cute, but it's not really what I would term "fun".I enjoy puzzles that can be reasoned through, like jigsaws and sudoku, quite greatly. I find them relaxing. Unfortunately, the type of puzzle being used here is actually quite stressful. The solution relies on the player thinking multiple steps ahead, and remembering what has already transpired. Attempting to go one step at a time does not avail the player to any hints as to whether or not their methods are correct, and is not helpful. As such, the player has to "know" some aspect of the solution to guess the correct answer, or be capable of visualizing all the moves going forward. It's not that it's impossible to solve, but that it's not intuitive to solve. Additionally, the function of each piece is marked by a symbol, and it's not always clear what will happen the first time it's used — there is no text in the game.Overall, I find it challenging in an unpleasant way, and would not recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: inbento

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very good game that does everything you want from a puzzler.The game starts with very easy puzzles, in fact the first 4 chapter are very easy and I think that was a good decision, you don't want to scare players right at the beginning.I wouldn't say this is a casual puzzler because it the latter there are some tricky levels. I would divide this game in 3 parts, first 4 chapters are like an intro, chapters 5 to 10 are medium difficulty and 11-14 are challenging but never frustrating. That being said I was stuck on some puzzles for longer periods, I even had to leave some puzzles and come back the next day (standard stuff if you play lot of puzzlers) .I am saying that because I didn't expect harder puzzles. When I saw this game I thought - Oh another puzzler with cats sticker slapped on it - . To my surprise and delight I found a game that has nice progression and harder puzzlers.It is a mobile game and it looks like one, it has some PC options but not enough if you ask me. The music is awful, I turned it off because it was so annoying.All in all a very good puzzler that does almost everything right. I recommend this game, easily worth the asking price.
_childDocuments_.name: inbento

_childDocuments_.review: Cute, simple little puzzle game. As all good puzzle games this one gets increasingly more complex as the game goes on. Inbento manages this increase in complexity really well, and at no points did I feel that the difficulty had jumped up, and I had no idea what was going on. However, at the same time the game kept me thinking and engaged.A beautiful, short, well priced puzzle game.
_childDocuments_.name: inbento

_childDocuments_.review: Inbento is a fun puzzle game where you create cute bento boxes by arranging different food pieces into patterns. The challenges gradually become more complex as you progress, keeping the gameplay engaging without being too difficult. The game’s story, though simple, adds a lot of emotional depth. You follow the journey of a mother cat caring for her kitten, with each puzzle representing a step in their bond as the kitten grows up. The game is a perfect mix of heartwarming storytelling and puzzle-solving, perfect for anyone who enjoys cozy puzzle games. -  – they add so much charm to the game!-  – making lunch for a baby cat adds an extra layer of sweetness to the gameplay-  – the story about growing up is subtle but touching-  – with no time limits or high pressure, it’s the perfect game for unwinding-  – the game’s art style is vibrant and visually appealing, especially the various food designs-  – straightforward mechanics make it accessible, but still fun-  – new puzzle mechanics keep things entertaining as you progress-  – the challenge level grows gently, making it feel just right as you play-  – the audio can get cluttered, affecting the relaxing mood-  – it’d be great to have some hints when you’re stuck on a tricky levelOverall, Inbento is a cozy and enjoyable puzzle game with a lot of appeal. Though the lack of hints and occasional sound issues can be a slight downside, the cute theme, beautiful graphics, and fun mechanics make it a great choice for anyone looking to unwind with a simple yet engaging game.
_childDocuments_.name: inbento

_childDocuments_.review: Very cute and relaxing game, the whole japanese aesthetic and cuisine is to my liking - but involve cats into it as well?! SIMPLY GENIUS! The levels difficulty started as simple and easy but got challenging soon enough - so to keep you squeeze your brain's gray cells for answers!10-10 would recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: inbento

_childDocuments_.review: One word: satisfyingThe gameplay, the music, the art style, the overall bento-aesthetics in which it's wrapped, everything. It's not beautiful from a technical standpoint but rather looking at it makes you feel an innate joy that can't be explained rationally, like coming home after a long day.It's real easy to pick up but gets progressively harder and sometimes even quite tough starting around World 10 (of 14). I'd say it's definitely worthy of your time if you like puzzle games, for this price it's an absolute steal.(Works perfectly under Linux, tested with Proton 6.3)
_childDocuments_.name: inbento

_childDocuments_.review: Deceptively simple in appearance, yet truly a challenge underneath the surface; be prepared for some real brain teasers as you progress in the levels! The game is an absolute STEAL for the cost, even if it's not on sale. You'll get loads of mileage out of it, not to mention the replayability is very high. Has a wholesome story told through cute illustrations at the start of every new chapter. The simple, yet vibrant graphics coupled with chill music makes this the perfect recipe to unwind to. Can't recommend it enough if you're a puzzle lover!
_childDocuments_.name: inbento

_childDocuments_.review: cannot believe that the food meant for cats in this game looks nicer than the food i make for myselfjokes aside pretty heartwarming game, mechanics are easy to learn, but still quite hard at some pointsgood game to play if youre ever up for a decently hard challenge linked to a wholesome story, though i will say its not that suitable if you wish to relax9/10, a smidge too expensive but does everything it says it does, and pretty bug free too at that
_childDocuments_.name: inbento

_childDocuments_.review: I like puzzle games, a lot, and when I first saw the gameplay of this, it looked way too easy for my taste. I wasn't going to, but then I bought it for 60 cents when it was on discount just to give it a try.Oh boy, how wrong I was. It looks easy at first but gets harder pretty quickly. There are over 120 levels and I really like the story aspect of the game with its cute artwork. Gained my interest and respect. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: inbento

_childDocuments_.review: Rotate, move and insert the ingredients correctly to complete the Japanese lunch box (bento). Soothing music, cute drawings, and a heartwarming story of a cat family involving the parenthood life and growth of the kitten to adulthood. Besides rotating and moving the ingredients, you can also copy the specific ingredients or swap various ingredients to match the required criteria to complete the bento.What a caring mama cat! How can she resist the temptation of the tuna while still neatly arranging the bento?
_childDocuments_.name: inbento

_childDocuments_.review: A challenging puzzle game.Simple, clear graphics. Easy-to-use interface (tip: you can rotate pieces as you drag them... hold with left mouse button and, while holding, rotate by tapping the right mouse button). The music was dull, but you can switch it off and put something better on in the background. There are windowed- and fullscreen-modes.There is a simple background story which is sort of cute. Sort of. There are Steam achievements (including one easy, but very-well-hidden one!).Overall the puzzles are fun to solve, but they get very difficult in the mid- to late- levels. Very difficult. If you are after tricky puzzles (or are a university major in Group Theory), then this is for you.It's a bit borderline whether to recommend it generally to everyone or not. But, according to the credits: ... so, okay.
_childDocuments_.name: inbento

_childDocuments_.review: Cute graphics and clever way to use food in bento lunch boxes as puzzle pieces. I really enjoy the small stories that are shown after solving some puzzles. The problems gradually get difficult but also teach well new techniques to solve these puzzles. Some problems are harder and I get stuck but then I leave them be for a while to solve other puzzles or do entirely something else until I get back and try again. Music also creates nice atmosphere and fits well to this game. From my perspective the UI is nice, clean and simple so it's easy to hop in and out to play this game!
_childDocuments_.name: inbento

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful, short-and-sweet game that is casual puzzling at its finest. The visuals are simple but pleasing and the puzzles are just the right amount of challenging that will let you feel smart when you solve them, but not so brutal that you're left banging your head trying to figure out a solution. There is also an adorable little story being told based entirely around cats, so that's a bonus!The game will take anywhere between an hour to a few hours to complete, depending on how good you are at deciphering the bento puzzles, but that is perfectly acceptable considering the very reasonable price point.
_childDocuments_.name: inbento

_childDocuments_.review: is a short, charming game where you arrange bento ingredients to solve a variety of cleverly designed puzzles. The minimalist but adorable sthetics pair well with the relaxing background music to create an encouraging and soothing gameplay experience. At first the puzzles do seem quite easy, but they progressively become more challenging and formidable as more and more mechanics are introduced. Overall, it's a lovely, bite-sized brain workout perfect for puzzle fans.
_childDocuments_.name: inbento

_childDocuments_.review: Inbento is a charming puzzle game where you craft bento meals by arranging food pieces into specific patterns. Don’t be fooled by its cute aesthetics, Inbento serves up puzzles that start out easy but quickly grow into real brain benders. Its minimalist design, paired with a heartwarming story about a cat family, cleverly mirrors the journey of growing up.10/10 for feeding both the mind and the heart!
_childDocuments_.name: inbento

_childDocuments_.review: In having a good understanding of simplicity and project scope, inbento succeeds in delivering a compact yet thoughtful puzzle experience. The story is told through wholesome single-slide illustrations involving cats and food. Heavy emphasis was placed on creating a  partnered with  for those who need it. The game is not very long, which works in its favor and is extremely easy to achieve full completion. There are some challenging levels towards the end that combine every previously learned mechanic, but if you find yourself struggling, the answers are readily available online and only takes seconds to input the solution.
_childDocuments_.name: inbento

_childDocuments_.review: Forgot to review this after I had finished the game a while ago, doing it now!I can tell you right now, . The visuals are adorable and gorgeous, very comfortable to look at. The story in-game is simple, still got attached to the characters. Even if it's a single image, their personality shows.Puzzles are actually quite challenging, yet still very fun and rewarding when you figure it out! There might be some replay value if you forgot about the puzzles after a couple of months and decide to install the game and do it again. There's no harm in it whatsoever.If you like puzzles and slice-of-life short stories packed into one, then this wholesome bento is for you. :]
_childDocuments_.name: inbento

_childDocuments_.review: What a cute little puzzle game! The puzzle consist of building a sushi box through various pieces and special blocks. I found most chapters would give you a couple tutorial puzzles for a new special block, then ramp up to hard puzzles. Until the last few levels, which were quite difficult and took a bit to think through.Accompanying all this is a super cute story about a cat family with a great relaxing soundtrack! Easily recommend this at it's affordable price point and was a nice little 4 hour experience.
_childDocuments_.name: inbento

_childDocuments_.review: Just like it says think inside the box!!! Very cute and relaxing bento box puzzles, totally worth buying and story is also growing by time we solve puzzles which is quite realistic and heartwarming photos of a wholesome cat family.Few levels are very time consuming which can be nice workout for brain.
_childDocuments_.name: inbento

_childDocuments_.review: 🏆 If you are looking for a game that combines puzzles and food to relax, I think this is not a good choice. If you want a challenge, it's not there yet.I recommend because I support the publisher.🎮 Worlds 1 to 7 introduce new mechanics to players. But the word world 8 is a mixture of the previous 7 worlds. A very confusing combination and some super difficult levels. It is no longer simply a matter of logical reasoning but instead of trying in vain over and over again.On the other hand, each world only has 9 levels, not 12 like Golf Peaks, and the story is unnecessarily drawn out.🎨 It's simple but still shows enough. But overall it's boring📖 This time it brought a rather interesting story.🎵 Because the level design is unnecessarily long, one music track will be used for two worlds. The sound effects are also not too impressive.
_childDocuments_.name: inbento

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this. It's cute and has a nice little story. The first half of the game is fun and relaxing and the puzzles are reasonable. The back half of this game has a lot of puzzles where the player is guessing and checking solutions several times until something works. There are just simply too many options in many of these puzzles for how the pieces can be moved and in what order to do so that unless you can think 5+ moves in advance, they will take a long time to solve. You can tell from the achievement percentages that about 88% of the players don't reach the end of the game and its pretty clear people lose interest in the back half of the game. Good concept, I think it just needs better execution.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an adorable little puzzle game about stacking food in a proper order to match the image.  It has an smooth learning curve, & the latter stages provide quite a challenge.  The visuals are nice & cute, a short story about a cat growing up through different stages of life. Some of the latter stages can have a bit too unfair of a curve in difficulty.  Like most puzzle games, the soundtrack is rather forgettable, & sadly, has little reason to come back after finishing it. As per usual, one simply needs to complete all the puzzles.  A fairly simple list, though the rising challenge of the puzzles will provide just that. Inbento is a brief, fun puzzle game that does a lot in it's final puzzles, but still comes across as a fair mindbender.  As with many of it's kind, don't expect it to light the world on fire.  But if you're looking for an enjoyable collection of puzzles with a charming little theme, this title is worth a look.

_childDocuments_.review: Inbento is a cozy, grid-based, puzzle game. Where you play as a single mother making bento lunches for her son. In each level, the game wants you to copy the recipe on the right with the tools at the bottom. Most of the levels are easy, simply teaching you the mechanics, as if you were the Orange Cat trying to understand his mother's skills. But same as when the Orange Cat grows up and gets thrust into the cruel world of adulthood, so will you get to experience the harder parts of the game that will test your game knowledge that you've accumulated over the course of the Orange Cat's life. Overall, I do recommend this game. It's a cute, fairly short game for a fairly short good time. And although I only found about 33% of all of the puzzles good. I still had my fun with it and had my money's worth.

_childDocuments_.review: 7.4/10. Bought on sale.It's a generally delightful puzzle game but a bit overrated due to aesthetics, polish, and the fact it has cats.There's a story progression where you unlock photos of a cat and its kitten throughout the years.The puzzles start out approachable and is presented in the form of organizing a bento box.The game introduces different mechanics up to world 8, and then starts combining them in all sorts of ways. This is where the difficulty ramps up, and honestly it starts feeling like a chore rather than a zen experience.A better soundtrack could've helped, but there's not much that can ease the frustration of later puzzles, where it feels like you're relying more on trial and error.

My favourite one is probably the colour blocking one, where the game will fill in all blocks with a certain colour/food when you place it down. After each chapter, there’s a nice cutscene that shows the life of our cute cat family and there’s even a hidden level at the very end of the game! It’s a very cozy puzzle game that is harder than it looks at first glance.If you'd like to watch all photos be displayed in one video, here you go:

_childDocuments_.review: I think Inbento is very relaxing and uplifting and I don't normally seek out puzzle games. The story is told through a series of cute and vibrant illustrations as you progress and is a quite simple affair but serves the purpose as far as theme - for each level you will arrange pieces within a bento box so that it matches the model you are given. Boxes may be different sizes, the pieces you have to work with may be various tetronimo type shapes, and there may be mandatory placement tiles that manipulate the pieces in other ways to make everything work. Inbento seems simple at first glance and during the beginning levels it is. However the difficulty will quickly increase and there were many that, for me, I had to go marinate on and come back to finish. I really like this as a short daily aperitif. The game does a good job tutorializing each new mechanic then offering a series of subsequent puzzles that implement that mechanic while slowly reintroducing previous mechanics. Each "difficult" puzzle I had to come back to felt painfully obvious once I solved it. WARNING TO STEAM DECK USERS: Although this plays very well on the deck, I did run into an issue where the achievements randomly stopped popping. I suspect it has something to do with proton but I couldn't get anything to work so who knows. I started Inbento up on my PC and re-did a few bento boxes on each level I already completed to get the trophies to trigger. I have a few more levels to go and am going to try REAL HARD to not look up any hints. I would love to play more puzzlers like this. Edit after making more progress: Getting into the later stages is making my brain twitch but oddly not every box is the same level of difficulty. I was bracing for vertical curve in difficulty but that's not necessarily the case. One will feel very difficult and the next I will solve almost immediately. Not complaining! I'm still enjoying this as a person who does not typically get too invested in puzzlers.
_childDocuments_.name: inbento

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely adorable puzzler! The game does a great job at teaching you how the different blocks operate without uttering a single word, and has a short story being told at the beginning of each chapter. There's no timer, so those who like to take their time can do so. I definitely had fun passing the time with this game and would recommend it to any puzzle lovers!
_childDocuments_.name: inbento

_childDocuments_.review: Despite my end conclusion, I actually found inbento to be a rather hard game to beat without guides in some instances. I may be no puzzle expert, but, on occasion, the puzzles felt weirdly overcomplicated for the limited range of actions you could do. Then again, that didn't stop me from enjoying the game. Afterburn have, once again, done a wonderful job at creating an enjoyable, albeit short puzzle game, which is why I would rate inbento an 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: The first 4 worlds of this game flew by me. I liked that there were new ways to solve the puzzles introduced at every level- swapping and switching and rotating the sushi bits is fun. I was also pleasantly surprised by how these concepts did slow me down and made the game ramp up in challenge until I feel like it's a very respectable puzzle game. _childDocuments_.review: A cute, charming puzzle game about cats making bento boxes for each other.The devs managed to make 127 total levels (126 + 1 hidden one at the end) out of a 3x3 grid & a handful of tools to swap the ingredients around - and that's quite impressive imo.I recommend this to anyone who's a fan of puzzle games and/or cats. It's a nice calming food organization simulator - and sometimes, that's just all ya need.
_childDocuments_.name: inbento

_childDocuments_.review: This review is specially made for those who like to get all the achievements in games.Minor spoilers ahead.Inbento is a 2D puzzle game about making Bento boxes. There are story images that represent a different stage of life of the cat protagonist, one for each of the 14 chapters. The levels have a box where several shapes (made with squares that represent pieces of food) have to fit while you recreate the pattern shown on the top right corner of the screen, and  there are 9 different ones per chapter.The graphics are minimalist: each type of food is simplified using simple patterns and just one or two colors, just like the rest of the work area. The cutscene images in the beginning of the chapters look cute and are cartoonish and stylized representations of the cats and the food they make. The music loops and gets repetitive, so after a while it’s better to turn it off and play some study/deep focus music on youtube. Each chapter adds a new mechanic, and they vary from move, rotating and copying squares to taking them out to place them later. The last puzzles in the last chapter in particular are very complex and took me some time to complete.  15 Achievement. Around 5 hours, without any help. Easy, with a few hard levels in the final chapter. Easy, just complete all the chapters and the bonus level that becomes available after SPOILER . inbento is a 2D puzzle game about recreating patterns inside bento boxes, using different shapes and tools to manipulate them. The graphics and interface are minimalist, but the simplified food squares look good and it’s satisfying to fill the boxes and create patterns.
_childDocuments_.name: inbento

_childDocuments_.review: This is an absolutely adorable tile swapping game. You are a momma cat packing her baby a bento. The art style is so charming and I love it. It's super cute.The music is also really nice and chill vibes. It falls into the background and adds to the game and never gets annoying to hear. As for the actual game play, again this is a tile swapping game. Your goal is to make all the pieces fit into the box. Different pieces of food don't do anything. They are more an indicator of where each piece goes as you are matching the box to the picture of the finished box. However the pieces will be different shapes and some will be locked in place. There are also pieces that are like arrows. So you may place something and there's one piece that needs to be slid over once, but if you have that arrow piece to place it on top of that piece and it will slide over.Things also layer. So it's not about fitting the pieces into the bento perfectly. It's about the picture matching at the end. You might place a 3 piece thing of rice and have a 2 piece of salmon that once you place it will cover up one of those pieces of rice, but all the pieces are in the places they need to be.So far it's not stupid hard but it does have a certain level of difficulty that keeps it engaging and fun for a nice and simple puzzler and never such a simple puzzle game that it's not fun.It is well worth the $5 price tag, but it does go on sale decently often so if you REALLY don't want to pay that $5 it will probably be on sale for like $2.50 at some point and it's 100000000% worth that price.If you live simple and cute puzzle games pick it up.
_childDocuments_.name: inbento

_childDocuments_.review: Nothing even remotely offensive and not a single end left untied, Inbento is a very clean, well-polished, and adorable game. It's a limited turn spatial reasoning puzzle with all the levels laid out around a vague but very wholesome storyline. If that sounds like something you would enjoy, you're in luck, because there's a lot of it! Over 100 levels of it for just a few dollars! I do find myself getting bored somewhat quickly while playing, but I dock no points for that because I feel like it has a lot to do with how much I get stuck. If you really love logical games and are quite good at them, I imagine you won't have that problem as much. The only thing I can really gripe about in relation to boredom is that I wish there was a few more songs, that would help prevent monotony. All in all, I'd say this is a nice experience! Pick it up if you want to play something which is both challenging and logical, but with simple gameplay that won't info overload you. Also pick it up if you just love cute kitty cats and want profile customization of them!
_childDocuments_.name: inbento

_childDocuments_.review: A cute puzzle game with a heartwarming story told in a very soft, line-less art style. I felt that Inbento balanced the difficulty curve very well, starting out simple and gradually increasing. Each new world would either add a new mechanic, or combine old ones in a new way to really twist your brain. A casual game, but one that gave me a sense of accomplishment after completing the more difficult puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: inbento

_childDocuments_.review: Absurdly charming puzzle game. A few of the levels took me surprisingly long, but the game is overall well on the easy side of the difficulty spectrum. If I were to complain about something, I'd wish for more background music tracks, hearing basically the same stuff for hours when there's little else in the soundscape could get annoying.
_childDocuments_.name: inbento

_childDocuments_.review: The purrfect cozy game to relax to! The puzzles in the beginning start out very easy and progressively get harder as you get further in the game. Once you hit the mid point of the game you start really having to think through the puzzles and do some trial an error to solve them; some of the puzzles can be quite tough too as I've had some I got stuck on for about 10 minutes. So far I am about 2/3rds through the game and have 2.3 hrs in it, for the price and the play time that you get out of this I would say it is well worth it to purchase! One thing I especially like and was not expecting was having a story to go with this game; at the beginning of every chapter you get to see the lives of these cats unfold. I definitely recommend at least trying out the game if you like puzzle games!
_childDocuments_.name: inbento

_childDocuments_.review: Charming little puzzle game that states what it is on the tin, very casual and nice to play when you just want to chill out, Interesting mechanics that alter as you progress and the artstyle is easy on the eyes.I would recommend turning music off if you plan on completing in one sitting as music is somewhat repetitive, but that's easily accessible in the main menu.  if this seems like a game you'd try I'd suggest giving it a whirl
_childDocuments_.name: inbento

_childDocuments_.review: Playing this game makes me hungry... Joke apart, this is a very cute puzzle game where we have to figure out how to arrange the different food elements of a bento box given a set of different allowed moves.The game has simple but well-thought mechanics but I personally found the game easier than the other two games from Afterburn.Between puzzles, various cute vignettes tells the story of a kitten growing up to become a cook.It's cute. Gameplay is fun and it has nice art. I enjoyed it.
_childDocuments_.name: inbento

_childDocuments_.review: Very cute puzzle game that I've managed to solve on my own for the most part, though I did have to look up a guide for 3 specific puzzles.  + Intuitive+ Teaches the mechanics through play and without words+ No pressure to solve things fast+ Easy undo and reset functions+ Great sound design+ Very cute graphics - Does not allow mouse controls for the menu, but does allow them while solving puzzles- No accessibility features- Occassionally there are puzzles where the first step is hard to guess with easy traps to fall into for incorrect moves, but your mileage may vary
_childDocuments_.name: inbento

_childDocuments_.review: If you like puzzle games and to relax this game is for you. There is no time pressure and every mistake can be undone. Just got at your own pace and solve each level. Some might seem straightforward at first but you will realize that an unexpected step makes everything easier. On top of that you get to see lovely drawings of cats, what else can you want?
_childDocuments_.name: inbento

name: Torn Away
detailed_description: Discord About the Game Torn Away is an interactive story about a girl torn away from home. Cross all of Germany and Poland to get to the homeland and help Asya reunite with her family. Along the way, you will find: Levels in the spirit of classic adventure games Remember, life was peaceful once, and brighter days still await you in the future. 'Touching' mini-games See the world through the eyes of a girl who was forced to grow up painfully quick. Platformer with stealth mechanics Hide from soldiers and overcome obstacles in the harshest of weathers. First-person cinematic levels Put yourself in Asya's shoes and face the danger. Will you be able to keep hope alive and return to your homeland? Features: Touching story inspired by the diaries of Soviet children about the hardships of wartime, told through the perspective of a little girl; An unfairly forgotten theme of the fate of 'Ostarbeiters' — people, who were forcibly deported from Eastern Europe to work in Nazi labor camps; Visual language assembled from elements of socialist realism and modern French animation; 3D levels stylized as 2D art; Original soundtrack inspired by the music of Hayao Miyazaki's movies, French New Wave cinema and experimental electronic music.

short_description: Torn Away is an award winning interactive story with a unique blend of adventure games, side-scrollers, and cinematic first-person levels. Help little Asya find her way home in the middle of war.

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game a masterpiece? No, but it is an amotional anti-war adventure that also plays well. We play Asya, a little girl in Stalingrad, who in August 1942 draws a picture for her mother, mends a torn glove and hopes to see her father, who has gone to war, again soon. Instead of her mother, however, only an artillery shell lands in the house where her small flat is located. Mother and daughter are fortunately unharmed, but are deported to Germany, where our mother is forced to do labour for the German war industry. The story then really begins in 1944, when our mother dies and we find ourselves on the run. Away from Germany, across Poland, back to the family still living in Russia. Asya has matured considerably and become more independent in the two years of imprisonment in Germany, but of course she is still a little girl who now has to make the long journey alone.On the one hand, the game is an adventure game in which objects have to be found, which are then used (often automatically) in the right place. Searching the environments reminded me a little of the Telltale Adventures. Another part of the game, however, plays like Limbo (or the new Planet of Lana). You move Asya from left to right across the screen, running, jumping, ducking and interacting with hotspots to avoid danger and solve little puzzles. In addition, there are various mini-games that always break up the action. Whether you have to repair a shoe, sew a tear in the fabric or fight your way through a winter storm, the difficulty level is usually set relatively low. The focus of the game is on storytelling, and it can be quite gripping. It's been a while since I've played through a game that portrayed the horrors of war in such an oppressive way. Fortunately, Asya is a very brave and optimistic child who talks to her dolls and thus fights her way through the terrible events.Torn Away is an anti-war game. Although the action is set during the Second World War, it is told exclusively from the perspective of the 10-year-old Russian girl, who notices very little of the war or world political events. Her small world is only about her family and the suffering caused by the war. It is about her absent father, who is fighting in a war somewhere, it is about her mother, who was taken to Germany as a forced labourer, and it is about her own survival in a foreign country. Cold, illness, hunger, fatigue, forced labour, darkness, loneliness, soldiers who immediately open fire, that is her world.An adventure game with relatively simple puzzles, combined with simple jump & run sequences and mini-games, but it tells a touching story. Experience the horrors of the Second World War from the point of view of a child deported to Germany with her mother, who flees alone back to her homeland in the last year of the war. Simple puzzles, easy to master action sequences, but a hard-hitting story that frightens and makes you think.

_childDocuments_.review: Hey there! You absolutely have to give "Torn Away" a shot. It's this incredible game that puts you in the shoes of a young girl during World War II. The story is so touching and genuine, and it really makes you feel a deep connection to her experiences. Plus, it sheds light on a part of history that isn't often explored in games.Visually, it's stunning. They've combined elements from different art styles to create this immersive and nostalgic world. And the music! It's like a blend of your favorite movie soundtracks, which adds a whole new level of emotion to the game.But what I love most about "Torn Away" is how it tugs at your heartstrings. As you guide the girl through her journey, you'll experience so many different emotions - hope, fear, determination. It's a game that really shows the strength of the human spirit and the power of family bonds.Trust me, you won't regret giving "Torn Away" a try. It's a unique and emotionally moving gaming experience that you'll remember for a long time.
_childDocuments_.name: Torn Away

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent game that will break your heart when you realize it is telling a story that happens to civilians all over the world, in all time periods. To sum it up... war is hell.You play as a young Russian girl (Aysa) who gets caught in the crossfire of WW2 as the Germans battle in Russia. Your life as a child is forever altered by the wartime experience and the developers did a great job of capturing the collateral damage of war. They made you feel as if you are in the middle of a conflict, even though the game has no graphic violence or bloody scenes. Torn Away is part point-and-click and part side-scroller. There are calm scenes with small tasks, stealth scenes that require observation and timing, and survival scenes that require evasion and speed. The penalty for failure is to restart the failed sequence. I was okay with the stealth scenes but the timed jumps and gunfire evasion took me quite a few tries to get through. Your progress is auto-saved on a fairly regular basis and at the end of each chapter. It is not saved on exit so you need to be careful if you are inclined to quit in the middle of a tough section.  Once you complete the game, you can return to any chapter to pick up missed achievements.There are no true puzzles. You perform some interesting tasks and, in some cases, figure out a path forward by manipulating the environment. There is only a handful of inventory items and they are easily used when needed. No 'try this' and 'try that.' The sound track is outstanding. Although the game recommends playing it with native-language voice-overs, I found it much nicer  to listen in English. The voice acting is excellent and Comrade Mitten is one of the best traveling companions around.I wish completionists the best of luck. There are no descriptions given for the achievements so I went to the web and tracked them down. Most are straight-forward, once you have a sense of what is required. 100% is not in the cards for me, as my only missing achievement involves completing an unknown section of the game with no deaths!My biggest challenge was the navigation with keyboard/mouse (hitting the E key to advance dialog and the WASD keys to move). I ended up using my controller for navigation and switching to the keyboard/mouse for manipulating objects. All in all, it is a lovely game that tells a story that will make you think. I will reflect on it as I am reading the news of current conflicts and wars.  I highly recommend this game with one caveat. If you have an aversion to stealth and evasion, you may want to skip this title. Although these are not the mainstay of the game, they play a significant role in its mechanics and can be a bit frustrating.

_childDocuments_.review: It takes skill, passion, and most of all humanity to successfully develop a game about the horrors of war. This War of Mine may be the most acclaimed anti-war game, a harrowing survival experience set in a war-torn fictional country. There is now a new entry in this subgenre of gaming, only this time it takes place in the very real Poland during World War II.Torn Away follows Asya, a ten-year-old who endures many traumas of war. From the bombardment of her city to scavenging for food in the woods, the 2D adventure runs the gamut of what many children lived through in the 1940s. In a way, the story is both excessive and too restrained: as this is aimed at a younger audience, elements like life in a labour camp or fighting in the trenches feel lightly sugarcoated, hinting at some of the violence but never explicitly tackling it (again, likely to avoid traumatizing younger players). At the same time, the narrative throws so many different disgraces on little Asya that it borders on ridiculous. If the goal was to use this character as a symbol of pure innocence becoming corrupted, the storytelling could have worked better if certain sections (like an extended sequence in the woods, running away from wolves and seeking shelter) were cut and others (mainly the labour camp) were extended.While that may seem like a big issue with Torn Away, it is a game that will work for pre-teens in learning about what happened from 1939 to 1945 in central Europe. The quality of voice acting for both Polish and German characters is impressive, as is the melodic and piano-heavy soundtrack. What makes the game feel truly special is its art style: while the levels are in 3D, everything is stylized as 2D art, making certain snapshots look straight out of a children’s book.

It tells us how terrible war is and how compassionate people can be in these conditions.There is no romanticization of these horrific events - only tragedy and pain. A game that makes you think about what humanity is doing, when it has long since been clear how disgusting, cruel, and inhumane any such conflict is. How many lives, how many people this beast devours...A story that will make even the toughest person shed a tear.A truly amazing game. .

_childDocuments_.review: My impressions video: Torn Away is a hard game to talk about without spoilers because basically every part of it is a spoiler. There's also not much in terms of "game" in here. This is more of an interactive story, but it has more going on than a typical walking simulator. You do have to take actions beyond just walking to advance the story, but nothing is particularly challenging, nor is there really any kind of failure state. I state this up front because some people are just not going to be into that, and that's fine if it's your preference. But as someone who has a very high standard for games of this type and has been very down on some other popular walking simulators, there is something special here and I think it's something to experience.Without spoiling anything, this is a game about the horrors of World War II, but it takes the perspective of a young Russian girl, a perspective on the war that's not often explored. This child goes through Hell multiple times over in an attempt to get back to where she thinks her family is. Along the way, she has a hand puppet imaginary friend, which is used as her subconscious and the rock by which she tries to keep her sanity against seemingly insurmountable odds. All the dialogue is fully voiced and it's in these conversations where much of the most poignant storytelling happens. The default and dev recommended voiceover language is Russian and while English is available, I don't recommend it as the English acting is pretty flat and not very convincing.Most of the time, things play from a side scrolling perspective, though there are some first-person sequences, plus some light puzzle solving, but nothing at all difficult. The art style is storybook-like, but also has this sort of bit crushed distortion effect around it, making it look almost like the art is struggling to hold itself together. I've never really seen this style before and it's quite memorable.The game is only about 3-4 hours long and unless you want to get all the achievements, there is no additional storytelling to be had by playing it more than once. But this isn't that kind of game. Again, if you're really averse to this kind of game, you might not dig this, but I found the story unique, moving and well told. I am glad I got to spend some time with it.

_childDocuments_.review: The atmosphere, music and game design are of a high standard, and I particularly appreciated the 2D to 3D transition.  The tale of a young girl searching for a way home moved me to tears. This game touched me deeply. I don't usually enjoy thrillers in games or movies and often give up halfway, but this one compelled me to continue. I would like to see more games like this one. Thank you to the developers for creating such a great game, I am confident that all the awards they have received are well-deserved.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a heartfelt and gripping experience that transports players to a time of great adversity. It's a testament to the resilience of the human spirit as Asya faces unimaginable challenges and danger while striving to reunite with her family. Torn Away not only provides a unique perspective on history but also instills a profound sense of empathy and connection with its well-crafted characters.
_childDocuments_.name: Torn Away

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to wait until a moment of clarity and inspiration to write this review. Torn Away deserves that. It's been almost two weeks since I saw the end credits and even now, I'm still waiting for the perfect words to describe this game. In a nutshell- Torn Away is a game that utilizes every feature possible to tell as great a story as it can. Visuals, sound, controls, variety, exploration, storytelling, voice-acting, all of it is marvelously realized and makes for an emotional experience. I was stricken by multiple moments across the span of this journey. There is a unique tone here, one that is quiet and purposeful and not melodramatic.For most people Torn Away could be anywhere from 6-7 hours long in order to reach the ending. Chapter select makes any completion clean up easy to accomplish. The one form of replay value is in the need to play this game with or around more people so they can share in the experience. It's just very touching.Some of the controls can be finicky. The very first section isn't as compelling or intense as the rest of the game. I could imagine some people stopping 30 minutes in or so and getting a kind of wrong impression of what is actually to come. But I would just like to close this review in saying that this game is easy to recommend, and I wouldn't really want to change much of anything about it. This is one in a very small number of games that brings something extraordinary into the world.

_childDocuments_.review: My great-aunt was just over 20 years old when the Germans took her to a labor camp. She was able to return home by walking across the country. It was an incredibly difficult path, full of dangers and hardships. She faced hunger, cold and fatigue, but none of these challenges compared to the fear she carried inside herself. Her soul was riddled with painful memories of the cruelty and loss she experienced in the camp. But despite all this, she did not tell anyone about her past. None of her loved ones and relatives knew what happened to her in those terrible days.My great-aunt was a woman with a huge heart. She didn't have her own family, but she found family in other people's children and grandchildren. She gave them all her love, care and support. My dad still remembers her care and tenderness with warmth. Her life was full of sacrifice and dedication, and she did everything she could to make the lives of others better.I want to thank the creators of the game for Asya’s story. This game evokes a lot of emotions and feelings in me. It shows that war is not only death and destruction, but also fear, loss, loneliness. It makes you think about how war affects people, their future and happiness. The game "Torn away" conveys all these emotions and feelings through the inner world of a child, and this makes it special and heartfelt.When I write about this, my eyes immediately fill with tears. There is no future when children suffer and die. But the game also reminds us of the importance of love, community and humanity. She shows that even in the most difficult times, it is important to remain hopeful and support each other. The game "Torn away" is a real work of art that will touch everyone who immerses itself in it.I want to congratulate the creators on their debut and wish them success. They put a lot of work, passion and love into this game and they deserve the highest praise. I am grateful to them for creating such a beautiful piece of art that draws attention to the problems of war and childhood tragedy.

_childDocuments_.review: Torn Away is a profound, moving and constantly compelling game about how the war devastates Anya, a young Russian girl. It moves from Stalingrad, to a German work camp, through the frozen wilderness, into a German town, train yards and the devastated Eastern front. It constantly switches between different genres: point-and-click adventure, platforming, 3D, stealth and also very moving cut scenes. The art style looks hand drawn and is similarly outstanding and very, very moving. I can't recommend this game highly enough. Very few narrative games have this much actual game play and move along this skilfully and powerfully. Torn Away is a small masterpiece and far, far better than most games I have played in the past year. If you are on the fence about picking up Torn Away, don't be. It is a great game.

_childDocuments_.review: Was it worth playing? Yes. Was it emotionally hard? Sure. Just a reminder of the price that people had to pay to overcome the biggest threat of the 20th century. Do I agree with all aspects of the story? Nope. Especially with the "Frau" part, being able to read through numerous historical evidences about the German Nazi society and the mood in it during the war. However – if you have 3-4 free hours, if you need to remind yourself how cruel life can be, if you would like to see the results of the fanatics – I can recommend the game. Not always you can see the The Great Patriotic War from the eyes of the child.

_childDocuments_.review: ✅A well told story✅Good narration voice acting✅Good art style✅Creative game world/playstyles➖Some frustrating platformer parts➖Autosaves are inconsistent, either 5 minutes or 30 minutes apartGame World: Torn Away (TA) takes place in the 1940s during World War II and is set primarily in the European countries of Germany, Poland, and Russia. The game has a host of unique perspectives that are not often found in games and I was pleasantly surprised to experience. You have a 2D walker/platformer, 2D movement on a 3D axis (like finding objects in the background/foreground), first-person parts, and a bunch of mini-games that are in the guise of chores. As for the setting itself, you end up traversing huge swaths of snowy countryside and forests, and some smaller camps/towns/rooms (the astute reader might realize the game takes place in the 1940s and I mentioned camps as a setting….uh oh!). Overall, I felt the game world was well done and offered a ton more variety than I was used to. Just when you get sick of one aspect of gameplay, you quickly shift to another for a bit. It is refreshing and most of all, creative. Narrative: TA tells the story of Asya, a Russian-born girl who was captured by German troops and is trying to return to her family in the Soviet Union. Throughout the course of the game, Asya experiences the horrors of war, something nobody, especially an innocent child, should be subject to. Immediately from the start Asya’s world is torn asunder and her life goes from a normal childhood into a constant fight for survival. I felt the plot of pretty much sadness personified. Asya is a walking Murphy’s Law and (almost) everything that can go wrong does indeed go wrong. Perhaps the saddest part is how TA keeps the narrative within the realm of possibility. Asya’s experience could have definitely happened to some random child during the events of WWII. It really makes you think about all the untold stories of those affected by tragedies not of their own doing. Ending spoiler thoughts: Length: This is a very short game. I was able to finish it completely in a little under 3.5 hours. Controls: You can play with KBM, but I found the controller to be better. Mechanics: TA doesn’t have much in mechanics, it's mostly a walking simulator with some puzzles. Mechanically the most you’ll need to do is do things like rotate a boot and brush it, or sew a mitten. Half the time is walking and doing timed-hiding encounters, while the other half is some pretty easy puzzles. This is a narrative focused game.Difficulty: A pretty easy game. The hardest parts are the dumb platforming bits. Quality: The quality is fairly unique and I found it deceptively good. Like it's obvious the game world is a pretty low polygon count, but the insanely creative art style masks this very nicely by applying a sort of cel-shaded look to the game. It’s not as heavy as Borderlands, more it looks kind of like a painting. Very well done. UI: The UI is simplistic and barebones, but for the type of game this is, you don’t need an extensive UI. In fact, I would have gone a step further and hid everything in the HUD. The game HUD has small elements like items Asya is holding, and her diary updates. The diary also has entries that share her thoughts as she progresses through her adventure. Performance: No issues with performance on my desktop PC. i9-13900KF | RTX 4090 | 64GB RAM | 1440p @ 240hz | installed on SSDSound Effects: The sound is well done. You have good environmental audio like war sounds. I also played in the original Russian/German voice acting, as it was recommended, so I obviously couldn’t understand anything, but the voices were well done. I could feel the endless support that Colonel Mittens always gave Asya just dripping through my speakers. Great narration. Music: The music is ok. There isn’t much in the game I could really remember, most of it is period pieces like classical USSR records from the 1940s. Overall, not memorable. None really. There might be some achievements to get and small decisions to make, but nothing that really affects the story. Torn Away is a good game to experience once, but it doesn’t have much staying power. After you play it, experience Asya’s (mis)adventure, there aren't a whole lot of reasons to ever revisit this, especially if you're a fan of not feeling depressed. I felt that every aspect of Torn Away is just good enough, but no part of it was excellent. The strongest part of Torn Away is its creativity when it comes to puzzle elements and world perspective. Aside from those, it just feels like a somber war story, of which there are many already, like This War of Mine. You can find my curator page here:

_childDocuments_.review: Torn Away is a poignant and emotionally resonant experience that left me deeply moved from start to finish. Without delving into spoilers, I can confidently say that this game offers a profound narrative that explores themes of loss, resilience, and the enduring power of hope.From the moment I stepped into the shoes of the protagonist, I was swept away by the game's immersive storytelling and richly crafted world. The attention to detail is remarkable, with every scene and character breathing life into the narrative. Torn Away manages to strike a delicate balance between heart-wrenching moments and tender moments of beauty, creating an experience that is as thought-provoking as it is emotionally impactful.Visually, Torn Away is stunning. The art direction is masterfully done, with striking imagery that evokes a sense of wonder and melancholy. Whether exploring lush landscapes or navigating through moments of introspection, the visual presentation enhances the emotional resonance of the story.Gameplay-wise, Torn Away offers a blend of exploration, puzzle-solving, and narrative choices that keep the experience engaging from start to finish. The puzzles are cleverly designed, offering just the right amount of challenge to keep players immersed in the experience without feeling overwhelmed.But what truly sets Torn Away apart is its ability to evoke genuine emotion. Through its well-written characters and thoughtfully crafted narrative arcs, the game invites players to reflect on their own experiences and connections to the story. It's a testament to the power of storytelling in gaming, showcasing the medium's potential to elicit empathy and understanding.In conclusion, Torn Away is a masterpiece of storytelling that deserves to be experienced by anyone who appreciates narrative-driven games. With its profound themes, breathtaking visuals, and engaging gameplay, it's an unforgettable journey that will stay with you long after the credits roll. Prepare to be moved, challenged, and ultimately, inspired by the experience that Torn Away has to offer.
_childDocuments_.name: Torn Away

_childDocuments_.review: Sadly, war is timeless, as many people today can still attest, and its casualties extend far beyond soldiers on the battlefield. "Torn Away" is the story of one of those innocent victims not standing idly by but taking action and letting her hope for a happy ending guide her through all kinds of hardship. Offering only casual adventure-style gameplay in between the more challenging puzzle-platforming sections, the game focuses on Asya’s travails, experiences a ten-year-old girl should never have to face. In doing so it certainly entertains, but it also makes you think, and especially makes you feel. This young protagonist is no action hero, certainly no superhero – not even an adult more equipped to handle these situations. In the four hours it took me to play, I forgot my privileged life and felt like I was there with her, increasingly dismayed each time her story encountered a new nasty surprise. The dark subject matter means it’s not “fun” in the traditional sense, but if you like the human side of war stories, be sure to bring the Kleenex because it’s you who won’t be able to tear yourself away.
