_childDocuments_.review: A sad and touching story about little girl trying to return back home to her family during WW2.A game is a 2,5D-platformer (with some 3D-sequences). Gameplay is simle, but there are interesting puzzles and mini-games. During my playthrough I encountered 2 bugs, not gamebreaking though and I think they'll be fixed soon. Game's length is just enough to tell the story and keep you from getting bored.Torn Away has a nice art style and sound design. Even though the plot itself is not very sophisticated, I followed Asya's story with interest and it was very heart-touching. It's not grim but sad. The developers also claim that they based game on real children's war diaries. The enviroment in game seems pretty realistic.If you've played Valliant Hearts, My Memory of Us I think you'll like this game. It's a good story about how war hurts everyone and especially the littlest one. And I think it's an important reminder in a time like ours.

_childDocuments_.review: There is hard to see and very emotional story about little girl, which gone through the War, parted with relatives, kidnapped and now – returning to Homeland. _childDocuments_.review: This is a very good game. It is made in the spirit of old adventure games and touches on a very unusual topic. _childDocuments_.review: It's not my type of game, but Torn Away has given me an unusual experience. I've never played such games before. The first level gives us a warm shiny day before bombs start to destroy Asya's home. At this moment the life of the little girl becomes harder..You'll be trying to survive in a cold forest (platforming levels are not so good, but it's okay), working in a labor camp, escaping from wolves and so on. The section with long walking around the fire was heartbreaking.It'll be long storytelling about my experience, what can I say It's a good start for perelesoq studio. The story of Torn Away tells us one of the most powerful messages: any war it's pain and disaster.

_childDocuments_.review:
Asya is ten years old. She wants to sail paper ships down the stream, play in the backyard with her friends all day and hurry home in the evening when Mom calls for dinner.

But Europe is engulfed in flames of World War II and millions of Soviet people are taken away for forced labor in Germany. Asya and her mother are among them. After several unbearable months in a labor camp, Asya manages to escape. Her only destination - home.

Torn Away is an interactive story with a unique blend of adventure games, side-scrollers, and cinematic first-person levels. Experience the tragedy of World War II through the eyes of a child and survive without losing your humanity.

Cross all of Germany and Poland to get to the homeland and help Asya reunite with her family.
_childDocuments_.name: Torn Away

name: Football Manager 2022
detailed_description: Football isn’t just about being the best and winning. It’s about overcoming the odds, realising your dreams, and earning your success. Fighting your way to the top and shocking the world or clawing your way back from the brink – these moments taste sweetest. Game Description There are 123 leading football leagues at your disposal. Have you got what it takes to spend big (or small) budgets wisely and guide your club to the top of the game? Build a world-class backroom team that can assist with everything from Recruitment to Player Development. Lean on their expertise as you navigate the everyday challenges faced in football management. Scour Football Manager’s world-leading database of more than 500,000 real players for undiscovered talent or build your squad from within, training your prospects to realise their ultimate potential. Play the beautiful game your way, creating a footballing identity on the tactics board that your players can buy into. It’s up to you to produce a system that delivers success time and again. Immerse yourself in our best-looking Matchday experience yet and watch your footballing vision come to life on the pitch. Make all the key decisions as you steer your team to glory. New for this season FIND YOUR WINNING EDGE Craft your own custom dashboard packed with powerful stats in the brand-new Data Hub. Utilise the same metrics and reporting methods that real clubs use to help you make smarter tactical and player development decisions to fuel your club’s success. ON-PITCH AUTHENTICITY See your stars showcase their skills in better detail than ever before thanks to our improved animation engine. A revamped pressing system and changes to player sharpness means that you can get after the opposition from the first whistle and benefit from a more authentic flow to the passages of play. TURN DEFENCE INTO ATTACK Implement one of the top tactical trends of the last few season with the new Wide Centre-Back role. Whether you’ve always favoured three-at-the-back or you see yourself as a natural innovator, you now possess even more tools to overwhelm the opposition as you chase those all-important victories. DEADLINE DAY DRAMA Feel the highs and lows of one of the most dramatic fixtures in the football calendar. Steal a march on your rivals to secure last-minute deals and work more closely with agents in our redesigned experience which replicates the unpredictability of the transfer window’s climax. COLLABORATE LIKE CHAMPIONS New, true-to-life staff meetings allow you and your backroom team to form a well-oiled machine. Combining weekly reports on Coaching, Recruitment, Player Development and Staffing delivers a level of improved support that will help propel your players to new heights. FURTHER ADDITIONS Craft your ideal managerial look with a redesigned manager creator, level up your transfer market performance with a suite of new scouting improvements and earn the bragging rights against your mates in the improved Fantasy Draft mode.

_childDocuments_.review: The new Data Hub is a useful feature for those who like to track data statistics for performances, the team, and individual players. Really helps you pinpoint where your team/players do well and where the weaknesses are. Also makes better use of your analysts. The match engine is marginally better but still seeing players just gliding on the pitch. The layout for the scouting centre and coach reports is an improvement, although the coach report is no longer showing how a player compares to others in that position like it used to. Estimated player valuations add a bit more realism, rather than having a set value there is now a range which will hopefully reduce the number of cases where a club tries to negotiate for £100m on a player valued at £20m (for example).

For instance if you want to check the shortlist you should go to the player search and find it...Also the game has a feeling of too much being a software more than a more exciting football game. Especially lack of a voice commentary, lack of stadium pics, player faces, more live media meetings etc. Maybe they will build that later on. I played Fifa 21 and it was there !

_childDocuments_.review: So, it's the same brilliant, in-depth football management simulation that I have mastered basically a decade ago already, with all the latest teams, rosters and stats updated for the 2022 season. I am happy to see there are some interesting online competitive modes for players to get involved in if you have the time to do so. It takes a well-groomed player about 20 hours to play a season so if you are a football fanatic there is plenty of replayability in this game as one game can keep you busy for 500 hours or more, and you can start with many clubs and play many careers and attempt a variety of challenges.Once you have mastered the under-lying mechanics of the game, for me now a decade later, I am excited to see what other innovations the game brings to the table in future editions, as I have looked at the game now and maybe the online competitions bring something new, but yes right now it does feel I'll be trying to accomplish something that I have accomplished already in terms of the solo career management gameplay experience....But make no mistake though, the newer changes to the gameplay are there and these changes are interesting for their reasons. I can see new players and veterans still enjoying this franchise for a very long time to come.Demo Review

_childDocuments_.review: I generally recommend the game if you want to risk your private life. It's negative because the review will get more attention and I have a few things to point out.If you are or will become an FM player you will be able to answer those questions:1. Your team is first in the league, you are well prepared, have maximum morale and will face the last team in the league on your territory. What will happen?a) Of course you will winb) It will be an even matchc) The worst team in the lague will stomp you 3-0.2. What does Offensive and Defensive mentality do?a) Offensive means you will shoot on goal more giving you more chances and Defensive means rival team will have more trouble scoring.b) The opposite.3. Can a player be mad at you of you praise his good performance?a) No, that can't be.b) Yes he can.4. Is it possible to have rival team scoring penalties against you 4 matches in a row?a) No, there's surely an option to tell players to be extremely careful.b) Yes there is such a possibility and it's not that rare.5. Is it possible to predict when enemy team will score?a) No, just like in real life, football can be unpredictable.b) Yes, you sometimes know when enemy team will score and you can do nothing about it.6. Is it a comming thing for the Goalkeeper to pass directly to the Striker, and the Striker to run alone at the goal to score?a) Probably extremely rare.b) Probably happens sometimes, especially when your defenders suck.c) It's a common way to lose goals and lose matches.Play FM and educate yourself! Then go back here and solve the quiz next time :)

_childDocuments_.review: Of all the "yearly refresh" licensed sports games, this is the one I mind paying for the least because SI is a good dev and each Football Manager release obviously involves a ton of work in scouting and player evaluation alone. Even as a consistent fan of the series, this year's release jumps out as a particularly good one. I'm not sure what it is, probably just a combination of polishing a bunch of things here and there while adding just enough new things to keep it interesting without being overwhelming. Recently, the community has found that the youth ratings of countries will barely change at all even if the country in question is obtaining ridiculous results. This is contrary to the announcement of the new feature made via tweet which reads:"A HUGE change for long-term saves as the quality of youth players coming through in different nations will now change depending on that nation's standing in the world of football."However recently Sports Interactive has announced on their forums that, regarding Youth Ratings:"A few areas that have been mentioned by some users as potential factors do not actually enter into these calculations, for example the national team ranking or financial status of clubs in the nation."So youth ratings do not actually change based on the nation's standing in the world of football. _childDocuments_.review: Sooo...I've been a long-time fan of the series, and the last version I played was FM20. No more adding image of your face to generate a (somewhat) believable model of your own face in 3D. There is no more timeline of past events below the game screen, so you could click any event and get an immediate reply of an in-game incident. This was a staple of all FM version I played since FM12...it was there from probably earlier versions. How tired are your players? Who the f** knows. No more % of their stamina, you now have a picture of a tiny heart so take a guess..maybe it's yellow, or orange, or red - take a pick. Default skin is terrible - with colour schemes all over the place. Fired-up player is purple for some reason, those that seem relaxed and convinced the win is coming are red. You just have a tiny icon to work with. No more setting up info screens that update automatically: opponent formation, player attitude, stats, etc. Ass-man suggestions?? Available only during periods between highlights, but NOT when you pause the match. Generally information is all over the place. It's harder than ever to keep track of your own players. There's SO MUCH information available now, new graphs etc, but all of it is so hard to get to grips with. _childDocuments_.review: Been playing FM for about 15 years and as always it is a great game and i'll always get several hundred hours out of the game as a minimum, but please for love of god like I have said every year for the last 5 update the UI & UX.The game itself is superb It is so cluttered, and the graphical parts of the game are more fitting of 2011, not 2021. The regen & manager faces are still awful (despite Miles wearing them as some sort of badge of honor - they look terrible) and the backgrounds on the stadiums just ruin any visual aspect of the game. There is a huge modding community (that SI continues to make life difficult for) that do a much better job than SI and they all do it for free anyway.As for the menus, they are 5 years out of date - there are several things you have to go through many menus to get too when 1 click would do a job. It is like it's only mini game inside the game just trying to rearrange the views. _childDocuments_.review: This game is a drug and I'll probably dump another 1000 hours into it because I'm a hopeless addict. But I'm not happy with the direction Football Manager has been going in with the past few versions.I recently fired up FM17 out of curiosity, and found the experience so much more streamlined. No more meetings that could have been emails. No more performance evaluations with the owners about whether I'd signed enough Portuguese players. No more forcing the latest updates from the Canadian Premier League down my throat by automatically going to the News and Around The World pages. Less staff members with vague titles whose jobs I don't understand. No more debriefings after meetings telling me "Actually players don't like being yelled at." FM17 ran faster, so less downtime waiting for the game to process. FM17 allowed me to focus on the core engagements of the game - trying to fit tactics to teams, finding and signing talent, developing players, and a reasonable amount of man management. FM22 is certainly more realistic. But that realism looks suspiciously like an actual job.There are aspects of FM22 that I missed. Dynamic youth rating is definitely an intriguing feature, even if its implementation is contentious (I think it was correctly implemented, but clearly some people disagree). The player valuation system and transfer market is much improved. I do like that player development is more variable, even if in the moment it's frustrating when the wonderkid I'd put all my hope in doesn't turn out. All these require a level of adaptability previous versions of FM just didn't ask of you. And while FM17's five year old database is a fun nostalgia trip, at some point I'll want to return to present day. I very well may return to FM22. Certainly nothing is a total deal breaker with it. But it's become clear that SI have built a bloated mess with a terrible UX and it's really tempered my enthusiasm for this franchise I've been playing for the last decade.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing football managing games since 1995 (Ultimate Soccer Manager, PC Fútbol, Championship Manager, Total Club Manager and many others). Since 2014 I've been pretty much settled with the FM franchise, I've been playing Football Manager 2015 for the past 7 years, and after giving FM2022 a shot I think I will simply continue playing FM2015 for another 5 years at least., with the same exact issues, and selling it for €55 season after season, even though it's been a while since they don't even have to pay for FIFA and UEFA licenses because someone will just mod them out for them.I believe the match engine hasn't improved a bit in 7 years, besides tiny adjustments in the animations. The training system is still quite annoying, so I just skipped it and delegated it to my coaches. The tactics are exactly the same as they were in 2014, with really minor changes, and they still have the same issues. They assume, for instance, tikitaka style must be played pushing the game through the center of the field, while in reality Barça and the Spanish team always used open wingers and really tried to make the field as wide as possible. Because of that, if you want to succeed in this game, you have to go for Italian catenaccio and counterattack or for a Premier League direct attacking style.. Sure, they have more options now, but that only means you waste more time reading the new questions and answers and picking the ones that you will be repeating forever from that moment on. Plus, you now have a second press conference after every match. .There are even several aspects where I find the game is worse than FM2015. , players have their demands and you must meet them or they will leave. Plus, their demands often make no sense. . Rookies ask for insane amounts of money or protagonism. One of my rookies, 17, refused to even discuss his new contract because I refused sending him on loan to a 2nd division team six months earlier, while he was playing regularly and won the triplet twice with my team. My team, by the way, is the richest and is at the top of the ranks in prestige. , just like the exhausting press conferences and so on, but there is really nothing pleasant in negotiations or discussions with players whatsoever.. Sure, it's a very good game, it was 10 years ago. But it's still the same now, almost exactly the same as it already was in 2011. How is it possible that this franchise keeps charging €55 for every single UI rewashing, and how is it possible that everyone keeps buying it year after year? That is simply beyond my understanding.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing Football Manager 2021 for near 800 hours, Football Manager 2022 is an extreme improvement in all, if not most of the problems I had with previous games. The match engine feels smooth, and the players feel so alive. The amount of lovely passing moves I've scored has been top notch. Besides this, players make inaccurate first touches, which helps gameplay massively. The game, when making a dedication to play more open type of football, feels awesome. Players get tired if playing a pressing style, which is much more realistic compared to previous years.Besides this, transfer valuations feel absolutely perfect in comparison to previous years. Last year, players would be extremely overpriced relative to what they were worth. Now, they are more realistic, with a more realistic overprice compared to before. Clubs will accept bids accordingly if they need the money. The transfer deadline day, despite being laughed upon when first announced, is a game changer. If you love harry redknapp, and want to do a bit of wheeling and dealing, the game allows you to do that. Players, much like in real life, become available on deadline day, and the transfer market feels less static, which is awesome.The Data Hub is well put together, and if you love those Tifo IRL scattergram videos, this place is perfect for that. It's lovely knowing all the different stats of the players, and it helps you make the proper tweaks to tactics if needed. The Data is easy to understand and is explained well, so anyone can understand it.All in all, Football Manager 2022 is a strong improvement in Football Management from the previous iteration, and the game continues to grow from strength to strength.

_childDocuments_.review: It's 2051. LOSC Lille are playing in the final of the Coupe de France, a competition they haven't won for 4 decades. 5 years ago, they were in Ligue 2. Yet here they are, in the final of a major competition after so long. It's tied, 0-0. The opposition, perennial title contenders Olympique Lyonnais, had dominated the match up until star midfielder Alexandru-Mihai got sent off in the 69th minute. Since then, it's been in deadlock, no side offering much offensively. LOSC striker Koutan gets a strike chalked off in the 84th for offside, and now it's in extra time. It passes quickly, no chances either side. That is, until the 119th minute of 120.Pierre Gicquel was born in Lille in 2033. For all his 17 years, he'd loved the club. His parents recalled the glory days of the club to him, culminating in title glory in 2021. His entire life, he'd dreamed of being the one to restore his club to greatness, to have the captain's armband while carrying the team to national, even worldwide, glory. From a young age, the staff at LOSC knew he was special, even being touted as the next Kylian Mbappe. Small, a mere 5'7, but incredibly agile, he started out as a striker but quickly found his place as a winger. He tore up every youth division he played in. Now, here he is, 17 and it's his first professional season for the club. Gicquel has played a big part in the team's first title challenge since 2021, but to start the cup final, he was on the bench.With the minutes winding down in extra time, LOSC's Dutch winger Ibrahim Jabbie was exhausted, and there was an obvious choice waiting in the wings. Gicquel stepped on the pitch, and if the weight of a city was on his shoulders, he didn't show it. It's the 119th minute. There's 1 minute of added time. It's the last attack of the game. Gicquel and right-back Balek are exchanging passes on the wing. Suddenly, a hole appears. Gicquel sees it, and swiftly dodges inside before the defenders can react. He cuts to the edge of the box. He's on his weaker left foot. He doesn't care. He's 25 yards out. He doesn't care. All he cares about is this city, this stadium, the one he grew up in the shadow of. The stadium whose visitors now all stare at him in awe. This club, the one he's been sitting in front of the TV, watching, supporting, following, for every day of his life. Pierre Gicquel strikes the ball. Everyone in the building knows where it's going. Top corner. Completely unsaveable.Gicquel became a LOSC legend that day. Everyone knows that someday he might grow up, he might leave, he might even force his way out. None of that matters. On one sunny day in May 2051, football was the winner, and Gicquel was its vessel. Perhaps it's just a game. But in that fateful moment, that game changed lives, and gave the world a story to be told for generations to come.

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I wanted to like this, unfortunately I cannot recommend this game in the current form. If you haven’t played some of the previous editions, go for it. If not, I would not touch this with a 10-foot pole. I found myself going back to FM21 save after playing just a few games. The match engine has improved graphically and also in terms how the players move. Apart from that, SI somehow managed to make the gameplay worse than in previous edition. Here’s why:1)	Your world-class strikers are completely useless: Can’t head a ball into the net from a yard out; miss easy one-on-ones with the GK; can’t put the ball into the net from a couple of yards out; take unnecessary touches when through on goal … The list is endless. These are same problems that people have been complaining about for years and somehow in this year’s edition, SI managed to make them even worse. 2)	Opposition goalkeepers are way too over-powered: It is really hard to score against most opposition goalkeepers, irrespective of the quality of your players or the GK. Even bang average GKs will pull out multiple out-of-this-world saves in the same game. 3)	Poor and unrealistic shot conversion: In most games, with a possession based tactic, you need on average 10+ shots on target to score 1 goal, wherein every opposition GK turns into an unbeatable GK.4)	Too many games with multiple shots hitting the post or crossbar. Too many games with multiple shots hitting the post when scoring is easier. My worst has been 4 shots hitting the post or crossbar in one game, while the GK makes 5 ridiculous saves on the other shots. 5)	Penalties: Is it a crunch game and you have been awarded a penalty? Do you have a chance to get a comfortable 2-0 lead with a penalty? Do you have a chance to go to top of the table if you score the penalty and win the game? 9 times out of 10, your best penalty taker will miss it. So far, I have had 9 penalties awarded to me in half a season, out of which 7 have been saved or have hit the post. My main penalty taker has a penalty attribute of 17 and composure of 15. These trends have been in the game for years, are entirely predictable, and make it seem as if the outcome of the game is pre-decided. 6)	Unbalanced games (getting FMed): Too many games ending in a draw where you score 1 goal from 15 shots in target while the opposition needs just 1. 7)	Poor implementation of pressing: Pressing seems to work sometimes, other times, it just stops. I have had many games where the opposition CB dribbles all the way to the half line and beyond and striker and IFs/IWs are camped out near the halfway line in spite of highest possible line of engagement. Save your self the headache, screaming, and ruined relationships, and go back to FM21 !!

_childDocuments_.review: I guess the only reason I'm giving this game a thumbs up is because despite everything it’s a very entertaining game to play. Honestly, it is not very different from the 2021 version (or any other version, for that matter) except it seems to be a lot easier for some reason. I'm at the end of the second season and I barely lost any games. I don't think any of the other Football Managers were ever that easy and I've been playing this game since it was called Championship Manager.Also, they seriously need to improve the dialogues and the players reactions to them. Some stuff just doesn't make sense at all. The pep talk before the match, for example, first off, I don’t think they changed it since God knows when. And the players react to them exact the same way every single time. I honestly only choose one option and all the players get extremely excited and motivated by it. What the heck?! And if they don’t, all you have to do is say you have faith in them. LOL it’s honestly hilarious! Then, the shouts during the matches. I honestly think they players’ reactions to the shouts are completely random.Still about the dialogues, the individual conversations are extremely limited. I always build a strong team and I like to rotate my squad a lot, so everyone plays and they’re always fit. When players get upset about not playing as much as they wanted to, there should be an option to talk about the squad rotation and try to convince the players of such. But you can only agree to the players demands or force them out of the team. This is just one example of how limited the dialogues are.The tactics are also very limited. You cannot really create what you want in there. I mean, don’t get me wrong, they really did an awesome job with the game mechanics and all, but you can’t create a specific play if you want to.Anyway, bottom line is, you don’t need to buy this game if you have the 2021, or possibly even the 2020 version. _childDocuments_.review: First, ignore the hundreds of hours of playing time; they're extremely misleading, because this is very close to a "browser game." When I used to play it, I used to leave it open in the background while browsing and stuff. I even used to forget it running and go to sleep! The Football Manager series has lots of pros, like some depth and tons of replayablility, but its cons are obnoxious enough to merit a downvote as far as I'm concerned. My biggest gripe with the series is that it is released every single year as a new game with a AAA price tag. Do the annual upgrades or additions justify a AAA price tag of a new game? Not even remotely. This, alone, is so low, obnoxious, unethical, lazy, and predatory that it deserves a hundred thousand downvotes.Other cons for the game include bad optimization or lack of responsiveness, regular loading times that definitely could've been eliminated or at least shortened with smarter code, outdated graphics, horrendous animations, and an obvious lack of user-friendliness in the UI design, like too many clicks to achieve things that could've been achieved with half the clicks if the developing company stops being greedy and hires competitive UI, UX, and user-friendly design experts to help design the interface and the whole game.The main reason for the ratings being generally positive on Steam is the addictive nature of the game for some players, which makes those poor addicts keep buying the game for full price annually instead of demanding these crumbs of improvements as DLCs or expansions. The second reason is the players who try the game for the first time and give it a thumbs up; those are justified in their rating sometimes, but I hope that they change their rating once they realize that there are zero expansions, and next year's release shows up with the predatory price tag that hits them in the face and wakes them up from the addictive stupor. Oh, but even then, it could be too late to raise awareness about this scheme, because the developer asks Steam to hide the older Football Manager games from searches and only show the current year's release with every new release. You know, just in case you had any suspicions about their predatory policies.If you are a diehard fan of soccer or football itself and its players, which is one of the main reasons you would play this game, then I don't think I can benefit you beyond what I wrote above plus adding that you may want to buy an older key for the cheapest price possible or try the game as part of a game pass to which you subscribe for [other] reasons. Football Manager 2022, for example, would allow you to experience everything worth experiencing in this series without paying the highest price for the current year's release. However, if you like these types of games generally, my strong advice instead is to try, put your money in, and play Cities: Skylines. It is an even deeper strategy game with [actual] graphics and from a much more ethical developer.

_childDocuments_.review: I was a sports management sim fan back in the 90s and I kept hearing that I was missing the best game of the genre. It was some soccer sim from England that was light years ahead of games like Front Office Football and Baseball Mogul. So I finally ordered Championship Manager '99 from Across the Pond and waited for snail mail to bring it to me. I got it and was introduced to a world of weird terms like putting in, knock and cracker. And then I proceeded to sink hundreds of hours into the game.So I'm a fan but I'm not one who buys the game every year. I buy it about every 5 years or so. I purchased 2017 and didn't put much time in it at all - it felt like a lot of filler - whereas I put in more than 500 hours into 2012. Well, the old desire to play another round started to sink in and after failed attempts to scratch the itch with a couple of poor basketball management games and some boring rounds of OOTP, I bit the bullet and bought FM 2022.All I can say is WOW. If 2017 didn't engage me because it felt like filler, 2022 grabs me by my lapels, drags me in and holds me down for hours and hours at a time. Now since I don't exactly know what's new, I'll talk about the features that have really engaged me.First, for those who don't know what this game is about, let me summarize it for you. You're the GM / Coach of a soccer (football) club somewhere in the world. It could be the MLS in the USA, a team in the minor Vanarama leagues in England or the coach of the Serbian National Team. You choose. And you'll deal with everything in running that team - tactics, training, contract negotiations, lineups, matches interacting with the press, unhappy players, the board of directors, statistical analysis, hiring a coaching staff and just about anything else you can imagine. It's frankly all too deep to get into because as soon as I try I'll exceed Steam's word count on reviews. It's that complex. It makes a good sports management sim like OOTP look like a mobile game. Now I've put thousands of hours into this series. So why does it strike a nerve for the first time in almost a decade for me? Because much of the stuff that was filler in 2017 has been fleshed out to actually mean something in 2022 and brand new features just enhance the experience.I love the look and feel UI and find that the tutorials to try to help a player get acquainted with these screens to be quite useful. The match engine looks better than ever. I remember playing it when there was no 3D version. This not only looks good but tends to be a bit less maddening in terms of showing a reasonable game experience. I don't watch the whole games - highlights only for me - but I appreciate the attempt to make it look good and play better. Tactics and training are deeper than ever and while the game still can be beaten with the killer tactics (I remember a 4-1-3-2 formation in 2012 would whoop most other clubs), the options to craft your own are amazingly deep. Same goes for training - you could spend hours/days in developing training schedules. Luckily for lazy players like me, you can also download both tactics and training schedules off the Steam Workshop. Much, much easier.Player and press interactions are better than ever, even if the press conferences kind of repeat themselves after a while. But the player interaction is far deeper and you'll get players pouting because they didn't play, or upset when the club is good and they feel they deserve a raise, or are upset because the team is playing poorly. In my limited experience, the higher the league you manage in the more likely you'll end up dealing with primadonnas that make your life challenging just when you think you have everything going smoothly.The transfer deadline feature is absolutely incredible and really feels like there's a countdown that day to trying to make your team better. I picked up a Serbian goaltender on the last hour to accompany my newly-acquired Serbian DL to make his transition easier to the club. Then my main goalie went down and my Serbian Connection propelled us to promotion. If i don't make that last second deal, we probably don't win the league. The amount of data is pretty overwhelming and the new visualizations make sense of it. Just being able to see better representations of our passing, shooting and other metrics is quite helpful. Scouting seems improved and just overall it's a far better experience. Are there issues? Not really. The game will drive you nuts - you'll have that stretch where you take 20+ shots on goal for 2-3 games in a row and somehow can't seem to get the ball in the net. And you'll have that match where your team comes out totally flat and for whatever reason and you lose a game you shouldn't have lost. Or you'll get hit with 2 of your stars asking for raises just at the point when your payroll is capped out and you can't do anything but watch your team go into an emotional tailspin. Case in point, I took over a larger club and ultimately led them to promotion. But I resigned after the season because the players drove me nuts and went back to coaching in a lower league where it's much easier to be a dictator.  Is this game for everyone? No. It's not an action game. It's going to take a while to learn how to play and more time on how to play it well. But is it worth it? Absolutely.As for the subject matter, it's not a big deal if you don't like soccer or don't understand it. You'll be too busy running your club to think about the sport itself. As for the terminology? You'll soon learn why a two footed challenge is bad but a screamer is good. Recommended, even at full price

_childDocuments_.review: *DisclaimerIf you played FM 21, this review is NOT for you*I played all the FM games except for FM 18-19 and FM 21. Fm 17 was a big no-no for me in terms of how similar it played out to the previous games and, I decided not to buy 18 and 19. I picked up FM 20 on epic for free just to check if there was any improvements or not, but it was totally similar again. So that's why I didn't buy FM 21. So when it comes to FM 22, I really couldn't hold myself and was missing the FM spirit a lot. I read a bunch of reviews on steam, so basically, everyone was saying it was a copy of FM 21. The catch was that I never played FM 21, so buying FM 22 would be a good experiment for me to see if they changed something from the previous games... And I tell you this;Fm 22 is a HUGE improvement to any other FM games I've played, especially FM 20. It might very well be a re-skin of FM 21, but then again, I have no idea about that game, so it's totally a must-have if you want to see some changes and improvements to layouts, 3d effects, some AI improvements on negotiations, matches and what-not. But keep in mind that it also seems like it's coming with a bunch of broken features as well. Gegenpress is simply broken, late-time scores are super frequent, the set-pieces are a big issue in terms of how easy you can score from a far-post, 16-17-year-old youngsters bug you a lot if you don't include them in the Europa/Champions league squads, meaningless press questions before Europe matches like what I do think about a certain manager from my league getting sacked etc. However, I really liked what they did with post-game match analysis, engaging staff and a less-stressful inbox. I recommend this game to everyone who hasn't played FM 21 but played the previous titles. It seems like this year they've learned a good lesson.

_childDocuments_.review: Do I like the game? Yes. Do I recommend buying this game or the next installment? No. Let me explain.I've played almost every version of this game, starting with the Championship Manager series. The game has changed so much over time, and for the most part the changes have been improvements. That having said, looking at recent years, a lot of changes have not been improvements and the focus is on the wrong things.I'm not going to beat around the bush. The graphics are bad for a 2022 game from a big developer. You can bring all the arguments to the table that you want, it doesn't change the fact that the graphics are simply not good. I, too, celebrated when the graphics changed from 2D to 3D and I thought it looked good at the time. Years later, and the graphics have not improved at all. Any other game, literally any other game in any series has improved their graphics, except Football Manager. You may argue that FM is not about the graphics and that its power lies in being an amazing "spreadsheet manager". However, years ago, they put all that effort into creating a 3D engine, so I would argue that SEGA does care about the graphics, but they put their energy elsewhere. Which brings me back to my original point; the focus is on the wrong things.I see new features and announcements of changes in the media interviews, more data, a deadline day feature, squad dynamics. Do these things really improve the game? Are they features that people keep using? That people keep coming back for? I've used the deadline day feature and don't see the appeal. I don't see how it makes the game better. More data? More dynamics? You can have all the data and statistics you want but you can still simply download a tactic from the internet and go an entire season unbeaten. With a downloaded tactic. One tactic that fits all. And no you don't have to pay attention to dynamics, or pay attention to training, or the data hub, or all the added statistics, just get a tactic from the web and you're good. Is it wrong when a downloaded tactic can do that? No. But it doesn't make sense to keep adding stuff and features around statistics, information, more buttons, etc. etc. when all you really need is a good tactic.Meanwhile, the game looks like it was made for the PS1. To put it into perspective; PES Club Manager had better graphics (unreal engine) and was just as enjoyable. It was all about managing your club, had plenty of tactic tweaking and statistics, but didn't go overboard with it. And the matches were fun to watch. It makes me sad to think a mobile game looked better than one of my favorite series of all time.This is why I don't recommend buying this game. And I won't be buying FM23. The game has plenty of features. The game has plenty of data and statistics. Let's focus on the graphics once again. Let's try to make the game look good. It doesn't need a yearly graphics update, but man, it's been 13 years since we first saw this 3D engine.

_childDocuments_.review: The FM22 match engine is a nightmare, a massive step backwards. It's just a crossing simulator at the moment. Central play is almost non-existent (although it's sexy to look at the few times it happens).If your wide player is wrong-footed he'll charge down to the goal line, turn 180 degrees and play it backwards. Every damn time. No cutting inside in this game!Marking is non-existent:  - Fullbacks never mark opposing wide men. They regularly run in to mark opposing players already being     marked in the 6-yard box, leaving the wide-men wide-open. - Cluster marking in the box.  - I often find my midfielders and wingers trying to defend the 6-yard box in crossing situations, while my    center backs are doing random stuff elsewhere. Also, you can forget about winning any rebounds. They say they remaked the pressing. Removed it is more like it. There's literally no high pressing in this match engine. Players just sometimes run to about 5 meters away from the opponent and starts jockeying.Goalkeepers are all over the place. They do more weird stuff than ever (although it might just be "wrong" animations playing), and glitch out regularly.This match engine needs A LOT of work before it becomes fun, to me. I much prefer the FM21 iteration. It just feels so rigged, and we're back to "opponents score in every highlight they have, whileyou need a metric ton to even get a shot on goal."

Whereas in FM20, it often times felt quite predictable what would occur throughout the match based on the stats and the highlights, and often times I'd find myself rather accurately predicting the outcome of each and every highlight; FM22 feels FAR more diverse in both the types of highlights you'll see, as well as being far less predictable in terms of what's going to happen in them. If you haven't played an FM game since FM20 or earlier, I'd definitely suggest picking up FM22, its still the same FM game we all love, but just much more refined and polished.

_childDocuments_.review: Football Manager is a stellar series of games and '22 is no different. There have been massive updates to the match engine and it's beginning to feel more and more realistic with each year. There are some problems with it though. The dynamics/player interactions system is completely screwed. Players will get angry at the littlest of things, and often you are walking a tight rope when interacting with your players. The transfer-list value is completely screwed, and your players will come to you if you offer them out for even the most minute discrepancies in value. Keeping your players happy while also winning is far more difficult than it should be. This area of the game is more like a dating sim than a football sim.In the same boat, the transfers this year seem like a complete toss up. It really feels like it's down to luck trying to either sell players for their value or get players for a fair value. Loans seem to be near impossible to secure without a senior affiliate. The staff meetings are completely useless. All they've done is taken what used to be a single email and put it in a long step-by-step meeting thing that takes far longer than it needs to. If you like to get really involved in the game, often times they will suggest things that aren't helpful or opposite to what you're trying to do (i.e. get a player to train a completely different skillset to what you need). The same goes for the transfer window meetings. I'd personally rather it just come up in the scouting email.For each thing I dislike about the game there's about 100 I love, so take these with a grain of salt. But this year the improvements outside of the match engine don't really feel like improvements at all.It's still definitely worth buying and a lot of fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Dabbled in FM13 back in the day, moved to FM21 last year and never really got my head wrapped around the insane playtime of the people playing it. Fast forward to FM22 and the loss of time is real. I don't consider myself an avid fan of the sport (or sports at all) but digging your heels in and really focusing on the inner workings of a football club has hooked me more than I thought it would. Every win feels like you put the work in and every loss hurts at an emotional level. Sure you can click through and hope you win, but the real meat is spending the time reading the reports, analyzing not only your team but your upcoming opponents, keeping your ear to the ground for club info around the league, and so much more. The addition of the data hub has allowed someone who isn't very knowledgeable of the sport to get a concise view of my strengths and shortcomings in a very easy to digest manner. I feel like my understanding of the game grows with every day that passes for my club. I am obviously ill-equipped to comment on the caliber of changes from previous iterations but much like yearly sports titles, if you are consistently buying these at every release you will have a much different view than I do when it comes to it's level of change and how well it's received. In short, for someone who isn't a die hard "fan" of football, this is great way to learn the game and the simulation level of interaction caters to the more OCD side of my personality. I'd encourage anyone with even a passing interest of sports management to take a look at FM22. Even if you aren't a sports nut, you'll find something to love here if you don't mind taking your time to learn how the majority of this game has little to do with what happens directly on the pitch. There is a whole world running between matches that includes finances, player personalities, building beneficial relationships, scouting, managing injuries, training, etc. that dictate how well you are able to perform as a club. While it is overwhelming for the newcomer, there are endless resources online to guide you to your next victory or emotionally shattering loss.

_childDocuments_.review: What do you expect here other than your annual fraud, where development incompetence, a database update and a slightly tinkered UI is priced 50-60€. Every year we get to hear how "this is the best game engine ever" and it is the same pathetic excuse of an engine that gets worse and more unrealistic with each update. Last year, for instance, the best plug & play formation had been a strikerless formation that cheated that "great engine" since enemy defenders are coded to go further up the pitch and match the attacking midfielders when there are no strikers.Also, in that "great engine" last year, a guy from the Chinese forums did a test with a 1 CA/PA team and won Premier League by prioritising only physical stats (primarily pace and acceleration) because they have significantly higher weighting in the game engine and the algorithm that auto-resolves a match. That very same test and other tests that followed proved that most stats from mental category (e.g. shooting) as well as some other stats from other categories (e.g. stamina) are completely useless and cosmetic only (except dribbling), in other words, whether that stat has value of 1 or 20, it is a placebo, doesn't yield any actual difference because its weight in the algorithm is so minuscule that doesn't affect anything at all. You don't believe it? Simply find the thread in fm-arena or reddit with a link to Chinese forums and use a translation tool to see for yourself. The test results are pretty consistent with fm-arena's test which demonstrates the superiority of physical stats, especially for pace and acceleration. And that's not a new thing, it has been pretty consistent since CM03/04 with the physical superiority of Norway's squad dominating everything back then.You think that these fraudulent developers who can't handle more than a database and UI update each year have bothered to fix this scum all of a sudden this year? You believe that increasing the pathing points of some basic animations so that players only move partially like robots and not entirely, that it magically fixed or changed the algorithm of how the game plays out? Think again. The game has been getting further and further away from simulating real football in any meaningful way. It's not a stretch to say that even Fifa 02 in the old PS1 console had slightly better engine, and by the way that is 20 years ago.I don't have a doubt that people will fall for this scum as it happens every year. If you are so keen on playing this scum of a game, then I would only say to you to at least search credible third party websites to get a steam key for 10€ or less, it doesn't warrant any more than that. Reviewed and refunded.

_childDocuments_.review: Expensive for a game that makes small changes each year.  I understand keeping things familiar.  I have a feeling people don't want a completely different game.  I DO think people want more detail and more simulation immersion. I doubt the developers read random reviews on Steam.  They are too busy rolling around in their money. But, I can always hope. And maybe it isn't the developers themselves.  Maybe it is just Sega, Creative Assembly, Relic Entertainment, and their greedy board members just all trying to squeeze every last cent.  I mean Creative Assembly is definitely run by some Scrooge McDuck type of individual so it isn't a surprise a successful game will be priced this way.  I will say, that if you are buying this for the first time...it is worth the investment.  If you have FM21...you are not getting anything different.  They can market it like they did, but you really aren't getting anything too exciting.I think the 2022 version of FM22 is like adding rubber mats to your new car.  2021 had some significant changes.  This one...not so much.  I bought it and played it for 30 minutes and got a refund.  The developers added a bunch of nonsense that nobody asked for.  I don't mind a meeting with the staff in the game.  But, make it more believable.  Have a room that has the correct number of staff in the meeting.  Have the room change based on the size of the club and their finances.  I also don't see why they can't have a few graphics of a practice.  Being able to visualize what is going on can help make sure you're not leaving someone out of some valuable training.My vision of what this game can be might not ever align with the developers.  But, I still don't feel like paying so much money every year for a game that is barely changing.  And on top of the lack of changes, this game is really only enjoyable after downloading Face packs and logo packs. I believe two things are true because of the Facepacks and logo packs. 1) The FM community work way harder than the developers to make this game more enjoyable. 2) This game would have its customer base cut in half if there was no facepacks and logo packs. There are games that have licensing rights and are still cheaper than this.  Granted, I do understand this game covers almost every club in the World.  FM22 on its own is one of my all time favorite games.  I have put a lot of hours into it.  This bad review isn't for the game as  a whole.  It is for the lack of changes from the previous years.  Not just last year.  I am over exaggerating a bit when I say this, but it is the same game back in 2010.

_childDocuments_.review: Some times it makes sense, other times it doesn't and you end up getting fed up with it. I would say it's a meh experience in frustration and heavily dependant on the RNG gods, but, still worth the money if you have the time for it as there is a lot of dead time in this game, looking for players, staff, etc. However, searching for players, building up the teams and seeing the progress is a very enjoyable part of this game. I do find it hard to play this game for long periods of time without needing a break from it though, as the RNG does become ridiculous at times and it's just too frustrating when you see things happening that just don't make any sense.Things this game gets right:- Management aspect is great- Looking for wonder-kids and bringing them up to become stars is great- It's an evolution from the last instalment in some aspects- Enjoyable managing a team from lower leagues to the topThings it gets wrong:- Full of bugs, which isn't something you usually see in FM- Players constantly offside (like 5 or 6) in free kicks and nothing you can do to fix it- Some stats seem to be wrong, like the passing % for example which is always in the 90s- The game has a thing for drawing games for whatever reason which lends to playing strong from minute one and end the game decisively in the first 30 minutes, otherwise, you'll probably draw even if you're dominating the match- You can upset your entire team by saying something completely trivial like "I think we can win the league"- Likewise, conversations with your players can be ridiculous with them getting angry and saying "I'm not going to let this go" just because you said "you've been playing well lately". Yeah that's a thing....- Menus are way over complicated and the information you would actually want readily available is behind several clicks a lot of the time- Press conferences... too frequent, the questions are stupid and repetitive, and it makes no sense how it changes relationships based on your answers at times- For some reason some times your team just goes to sleep (this is the RNG nonsense mentioned before). I watch the games because I like to tweak and react to the opponent. Some games no matter what you do or tell your team, they just ignore it and play sluggish like they couldn't care any less. Then the next game, back to destroying the opponent without making a single change. Makes no sense...- AI gets out of money troubles too easy, aka, cheats. Takes away the fun in managing the finances of your club responsibly- The match simulator sometimes decides to buff a single player before a match (conversely to putting your team to sleep) and that player will score 3 or 4 goals no matter who you are playing against.- Contract negotiations... how retarded is it that a player will demand a stupid wage and playing time, regardless of how big or small your team is, but they'll accept an offer from a smaller club for less money and less agreed play time? Worst AI ever in just about every interaction of the game...

_childDocuments_.review: As an avid FM player for the past seven editions, I am sad to say that this is by far the worst FM I've ever played. It feels like this is a buggy early beta build, not a fully released product. The match engine is the most unrealistic so far, with the only viable tactics in most situations being some form of pressing, short passing system even in lower leagues where this type of tactic shouldn't be possible. No matter what happens, even the worst teams in the league have completion percentages of 85% or higher, which if you know anything about football you'd recognize as being a bit absurd (maybe that would be normal for the best teams, but when the worst team in the sixth tier of English football is passing with 90% accuracy, you know something is wrong). Sometimes defenders decide to just wander off and are nowhere near the play. You can't play with anything other than a high defensive line, as crosses are way too effective this year. The transfer system is a bit of a mess, with players complaining about asking prices even when the interface says they should be happy with the asking price. I've had players throw a tantrum about their price being too high when a dozen teams were willing to meet it and the agent said it should be fine. Expected playing time vs accurate playing time is glitched, and sometimes the player who has started each of the dozen league games you've played so far will complain because the game thinks they're only being used as a squad player. Then there's features like "dynamic youth rating" which were misrepresented by SI (youth rating doesn't actually change except for very rare circumstances), who then give snappy responses when called out on it. SI's reaction as a whole to any criticism of the game or reports of bugs usually boil down to "not a bug, you just don't like our game being realistic", even when it's clearly an unrealistic bug, which is disappointing coming from a developer who is usually very good about interacting with the game's community. If SI would have re-released FM2018 with updated squads and called it FM2022 I would recommend it in a heartbeat, but I just can't recommend this game as is. If you really want to simulate last season, buy FM21 and download one of the third-party roster updates, but skip FM22 and hope that they do a better job with FM23.

_childDocuments_.review: FM is now FIFA. It's clear that SI are investing as little development into each edition as they can get away with. Comments elsewhere have suggested that the fair solution (for gamers) would be releasing a patch every season with an update of players rather than a whole new game. As can be seen, I've given plenty of hours to this edition so I think it's fair to say that these observations are based on a significant amount of experience with the game. 1) Transfers. With each edition, this gets more and more skewed in favour of the AI. You will rarely if ever sell a player for close to their valuation, yet any attempts to purchase an AI player for less will be rejected. The loan system is even worse, with negotiations only possible on your loanees, not on an AIs. 2) ME. The match engine hasn't improved and with every patch, something changes to ruin your previously developed tactic. There was a brief moment when FM22 came out that strikers finished one on ones, but that was clearly too realistic for SI so that was 'fixed'. Also good luck defending against the inevitable 30 yard effort from the opposition player who hasn't scored all season...3) Other: The game is riddled with annoying little flaws; the board scores are ridiculous, the inability to negotiate objectives is infuriating and a backwards step from previous versions... don't even get me started on the "dynamic youth rating"! In conclusion, I don't feel I can recommend this game anymore. I've had every edition since the switch to FM and it is without a doubt that there has been little actual improvement in the way the game plays. Yes, there's been "new features", though the usefulness of the analysis is dubious given the inevitability of some of the match engine gameplay. Unless FM23 offers a radical overhaul and massive improvement in the areas above, I think my time playing this game is over and that is one of the saddest realisations a gamer can have!

_childDocuments_.review: If you're happy to be frustrated to the point of destruction of your own person property, buy this game.For me, it is the worst FM by some distance. You can have a season whereby you win the lot, however, 2 games into the next season everyone has figured out how to play against you, and once you're stuck in this situation you need the IQ of Stephen Hawking to get out of it quickly.Being FM'd is all too common in this iteration too - yet when you try to raise faults and clear flaws on the FM forums, you're met with condescending responses from the a*selicking mods who will defend the game to the hilt - I know fine well they know of the fundamental flaws as I have been banned and warned for simply pointing out what I have found during hours of game time.It is absolutely scripted, again something they will deny. The game manufactures ways to include aspects they have programmed in. For example, playing the same team several times in a row following a "random" cup draw - it's strange how you're immediately asked about it by the media, in the horrendously tedious press conferences.I could go on and on and on but I'll leave it at that. This will be the last FM I buy, it's f*cking hideous.

_childDocuments_.review: I will now compile a FULL list of changes that SI does every. single. new. edition:-New transfers have been updated.-New UI elements, which no one asked for, which are horifically implemented and drastically reduce all QOL regarding the game. Their biggest UI additions include even MORE clicking to complete the SAME tasks as FM21! That's right, ladies and gentlemen, we have hidden very common UI elements like "request scouting report" behind ADDITIONAL MENUS! Now instead of scouting a player in two clicks, you can do it in four!-Four to five new in-engine scenarios which seem REALLY refreshing and cool upon first viewing! This is why the match engine ALWAYS feels "refreshed" and "updated" when you're first trying a new FM. Unfortunately, after the first 30 or so matches, you realize that this is all the game has to offer and these "new" scenarios quickly become as stale as the previous version-"Real life elements" like VAR! Do you ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hate VAR in real life? Now you can ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hate VAR in-game, too! SI realized that VAR was incredibly scripted AGAINST the player in the previous version, only being used to disallow goals! Well, fear not! Now it's the reverse! Every single goal where the linesman doesn't raise his flag gets to be VAR checked just to give the goal! So immersive!

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly didn't notice enough improvement from 2021. It essentially feels like the same game with minimal improvements and similar problems. It can still be fun when the AI isn't completely broken, which is far too often for my taste. You can only take so many instances of the AI goalies making superhuman saves while your skilled keeper just stands still as opponents put routine shots by him before you start to despise the game. The defensive AI needs a TON of work. I'm seeing Premiere League defensive backs passing back and forth in front of their goal before handing the ball to an opposing striker for an easy goal FAR too often. Some games your team will look like world beaters and the next they will literally be incapable of completing basic passes to each other. It is infuriating and tactics seem to have little to no bearing on your team's performance too frequently. At least add more media interactions so I'm not spewing forth the same canned responses we've been using for years now.It speaks to the lack of other quality sports sim games that I'm putting as much time into this one despite not liking it very much. Here's hoping they put more work into the next version.

_childDocuments_.review: Football manager (unlike over football games) gives you complete control over everything or you can delegate  some stuff to the game if you don't like doing, so there is so much customisation. This is not the case for other football games such as Fifa. The revamp of the online aspect of the game this year is tremendous, it has created a more user friendly way to play with your friends on the game.The main thing that i personally love about this game is anything can happen, you can take a team from the Vanarama National League (5th tier of England) to Champions League glory. _childDocuments_.review: "The closest thing to real football management"Yes, what you see here is a screenshot of top French striker Mbappe transferring to Liverpool  not even 1 year into the playthrough for 150k a week less than he was getting paid at PSG. You know, PSG, the top French team, which is the next best thing to Real Madrid (his dream club) which is the ONLY reason why he'd want to leave in the first place. This, along with tons of other completely immersion breaking events, is why I'm giving this game a negative review.You see, FM and I go way back. It's the reason why I'm on Steam in the first place, back when FM 2007 introduced me to it. You know what else FM 2007 had? Personalized player wishes and gripes, such as favoring a club they want to play for (which would make it easier to sign them) or vice versa, personnel they'd prefer to play with or vice versa, and so forth. In other words, players had a personality that matched their irl wishes. Something which has been removed from FM somewhere along the line. On FM 2007, Mbappe would've very likely only ever transferred to Real madrid, or at the very least for a huge amount of money + a huge contract. Not on a free transfer and with 150k a week less in wages.I stopped buying every FM since 2014 when it became clear that the developers were not making enough actual improvements to the game and even managed to achieve the opposite with the above example. I bought it again in 2017 and oh boy, was I done fast with that one. That one introduced the whole social media 'addition' and it was a complete and utter joke with how fans reacted to news about their club, along with a plethora of other ridiculous additions which only broke the immersion more. And here we are now, dipping my toes into the water once more after 5 years. Allan Saint Maximin and Houssem Aouar are the next superstars of football and with Newcastle's current situation, I had enough motivation to pick up FM once more by pairing them up and build a team around these 2 awesome players. Surely something had been improved regarding additions such as the social media example, right?....Nope.I'll walk you guys through the 'highlights' of my 1st season.  The very first thing I did was buying Aouar, obviously (make this happen irl Newcastle!!):The first thing you'll notice is the Fan reaction: B- rating. Now we all know Newcastle fans have...high expectations, but I reckon even if Mbappe joined them in this game they'd still rate it a B- with 1 comment stating "Ehh he ain't that good" by a Newcastle fan gaining a large amount of upvotes.Fastforward to transfer deadline day, I overhauled the squad by bringing in 8 players in total; and not just any players. High profile players, hugely improving the squad and already got em to gel together as well. This is what the fans had to say however:  "Could we find a way to get better up front" even though I signed Raphinha and Calvert-Lewin (who ended up becoming top scorer). The large majority voting for 3+ more signings. Another example was a comment with lots of upvotes stating "Sure, 'knee ligaments damage'..." upon a player's return from injury, while that injury happened in a match for all to see btw. Great, so you even got fans implying that these injuries are fake for no reason. Hilariously, the game got a few things right unintendedly which at least added comedic relief. Solskjaer got fired too shortly after....And that sums up my FM22 experience really; Fun, but for all the wrong reasons. Unintentional comedy can be found in almost every facet of the game, to the point that you question what on earth the developers have been doing in these past 5 years. Because my final verdict is: this game feels no different from the issues that 2017 had. They only made some functions harder to find by burying them in a convoluted mess of options or removed them entirely, left in the social media system which should absolutely be removed from the game instead if they refuse to improve it to the point of not being immersion breaking, players are still almost always graded half a current ability star lower than what all the scout reports of top stat scouts indicated after you sign them just like in FM2017, potential is never met in actual ability no matter how often you play them (stat growth and improving stats through training has been made worse than in earlier FM iterations), and the list goes on like that.Now I'm mighty tempted to list all of the easy-to-implement and obviously positive changes I'd like to see to FM but there's 1 problem with that: If SI do all of this for the next FM then what'll happen to the sales of FM24? And for that reason, even though I don't own the game I'm willing to bet that the indie game "Football, Tactics and Glory" would be the superior realistic FM game if they had the license rights since that's not tied to a yearly release which prevents devs from going all-out, making the best game they could possibly make. So instead we're stuck with this comedy product, and who knows for how long. 5 years hiatus doesn't seem to do the trick; gotta wonder if I'll even be alive by the time we get an actual realistic FM sim by this lot. But for now, I'd say the product description = nothing short of false advertising and advise everyone reading this to stick to older FM games...unless you really want to give Saint Maximin some love which he admittedly does deserve (most entertaining and  player along with Salah ever since the #1 legend JayJay Okocha). And yes, this is me going easy on SI; you can read other more mechanical issues in other highly upvoted negative reviews which I also agree with. The main point in mine is just how immersion breaking & unrealistic this game actually is and has been for years now. If this review gets enough exposure I'll consider opening comments and list some of my suggestions there which would take this franchise forward...if it wants to that is.P.S. Also Saint Maximin 10 long shots 11 finishing 16 speed stats in-game = LOL no (compared to other player stats & irl performance comparison).

_childDocuments_.review: I have been playing the Football Manager series for a couple of years now. It's been a really refreshing experience for someone who has dreamed of managing a football club for most of their life. Football Manager 2022 is a really detailed and complex football management simulator. You've got the chance to set up teams training session, make transfers, set up tactics, make adjustments while in a match etc. The game is very realistic in almost all aspects. You are not the "main man" of a football club. You have got to abide by the chairpersons set tasks. Player prices depend on player age, potential, current ability and financial status of the club they play for. The option to be able to delegate anything that you prefer not to do to your staff is an absolutely beautiful feature which helps enjoy only the parts of management that you want. I would definitely recommend the game to anyone with even a remote interest in football management.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the best FM to date. I am usually left disappointed when I buy a new FM because so little is added but this time a tonne of new features and QoL improvements have been implemented. The Data Hub is a brand new feature to FM that brings you incredibly deep analysis of your team, players, and tactics. It will help you figure out if your team is actually s#it or you're just unlucky. You will learn why and how your team is playing like they're playing and know of ways to improve it. The Data Hub statistics are all provided by SciSports - a genuine real life sports analytics company and provider of football data intelligence for real world football. The passing map will help you identify if certain roles selected are playing well together or not. There is so much more to the Data Hub you just have to check it out for yourself but its one of FM's best features to date. Learning it will make a huge difference to how you see your tactics. The match engine has been greatly improved but still not what it could or should be in 2022.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game.I got this game for the first time in four years, the last one I got was FM18. Perhaps the incremental changes don't look like much if you buy every edition, but for me, it was like buying a whole new game. Firstly, the game runs smoother than FM18 did on the same machine, which is a huge reflection of how well the processing works. I've played a season with Arsenal so far, and got top 4, but I liked the realism aspect so far. I started off badly, and until my tactics bedded in, I wasn't scoring much, and was losing games. I was in the relegation zone in October, and barely top half in December. With only one signing and no real change, I got top 4, with  some tactical tweaking (I'm pretty terrible at it, so it wasn't even a huge change) and just letting the team get used to each other and get used to the tactic.It's much harder to implement a pressing system, and so far, I might be wrong on this, but not pressing all the time is probably the way to go. Really enjoying it so far, and it's a challenge. The shouts system has been revamped, this may be older than this game, like I said, first one since FM18, but it's nice to see shouts have an impact in real time.My one gripe with this is the Dev Center. I don't like it really.

_childDocuments_.review: The new FM22 is a familiar experience. Coming from FM21, not much has changed except some layout changes, more focus on data (welcome change for some) and match engine tweaks. However, at its current state, I cannot recommend making the jump from the last years edition as there are major problems with the transfer and match engine systems. Lets start with transfers. Like last year, I started with Notts Co in the Vanaram national League (fifth tier of English football). While I understand that everyone in the league is keen to secure the signature of good players, I do not understand why the AI only tries to sign players as soon as I have approached them. A player can have no interested parties when I scout them but as soon as I make an offer, then Championship, League One clubs are suddenly all vying for the player's signature (which makes it impossible to sign them); regardless of how good that player is. Compared to FM21, the transfer market feels robotic and predictable as I have yet to make a transfer uncontested. The match engine has some major problems compared to FM21. The expected goals (XG) stat is completely broken. I play a 3-4-1-2 and I consistently hit 4-5 XG a game and barely score 1 or 2 goals while the opposing team have 0.4 XG and score at least 1 a game. I have no qualms with the fact that they score as it is typically clear cut chances. However, why are 1 v 1 rated as an event with lower XG compared to a long shot on target? Also, finishing in this year's edition does not matter as much as long shot. My striker with 14 finishing, 12 composure (Bare in mind this is a League Two) miss 9/10 chances (mostly 1 v 1s) while my youngster (8 finishing, 7 composure) can snipe the top corner as he has 10 long shot. It has gotten so bad that I have now removed the Advanced Forward role from my tactics and fully rely on Target Men with high Jumping Reach to score goals. Similarly, Paul Mullin, a former League Two top scorer with 32 goals to his name could only score 6 in Vanarama National League the following year despite my scouts telling me he is a League One/Championship talent. Don't get me wrong, I enjoy this game, perhaps a bit too much. But the issues that FM22 has makes this years edition a hollow copy of FM21. At its current state, I cannot recommend anyone, unless players from FM19 and earlier to purchase FM22.
