_childDocuments_.review: I played about an hour of this game, and had to draw the line due to very poor performance, low frame rates due to the DRM that's in this game, so refunded it, its not so much of a game breaker but im not paying for a game to have the quality of experience diminished due to some daft DRM, which I might add is well known for causing up to 50% less performance, Far Lone Sales, on the other hand, worked wonderfully for me, no performance issues what so ever... since I only played an hour in i cannot fully say much about the game, but once the devs remove the DRM I may revisit this release in the future and try it again.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: FAR: Lone Sails had been a balanced game. Between the interest-piquing puzzles, the micromanaging of your vehicle and the emotional amalgam of the post-apocalyptic scenery paired with the beautifully crafted soundtrack, it all formed a cohesive hole. Graphics were great too, bearing in mind that it ran on Unity.FAR: Changing Tides somehow missed this balance. Puzzles are okay-ish (although not on the level of the first game), micromanaging is way more tedious (more options to manage doesn't add more depth to the experience unfortunately), and the transitional periods are unnecessarily long (to cater for the soundtrack mostly - which is still brilliant). These parts which focus on travelling, the scenery and the music could have been easily cut down by 30% to achieve a more fluid gameplay. This way it's just a segmented go-stop jerk of the narrative (I found myself browsing my phone while waiting for these parts to end). Graphics are... maybe a downstep from FAR: Lone Sails. I expected more.And please support Ultrawide res. We're in 2022...
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: Very similar to the first one, but with a story nowhere near as compelling. You spend so much time micromanaging the ship that it becomes a chore. And it is very easy to get stuck, with no help from the devs on what to do next. Overall, not as much fun and a very poor successor. Refunding it.Oh yeah, and it got denuvo. So, screw that.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: (Edit: Turns out the game is between 6-7 hours long. This is good because it makes the game worth its asking price.)So I'm going to give this a thumbs up but only based on my small amount of playtime. If I had to base this on the last game it'd be negative because I didn't like the last one. But so far in this one its pretty alluring.The graphics are great, the music is amazing and the idea is great. But the majority of your time is spent sitting on a boat doing nothing but observing the scenary. The game is mostly thematic, its more of an experience than a game. You don't actually do a whole lot in the game itself. So if you're just looking for a thematic experience with hints of gameplay then this game is great for you.Overall I'm only giving it a positive review currently because the game has me curious enough to want to go further while also having great art and sound.If you want a more in depth look and feel of the game then please check out the video I posted on my Youtube channel (link below). But honestly, I just hope this game is longer than the last one and actually answers questions unlike the last one. Thanks for reading and I hope I helped some of you out there to spend your money wisely.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: FAR: Changing Tides trades the Wheels of it's predecessor for paddles and looses none of it's charm doing so.The aesthetics are still quite untouched by other games and so it's still a very fresh if albeit simple art-style that definitely struck a chord with me.This game is a beautiful journey that builds and surprises with every stop and if that's not enticing enough for you, i'll bait you with the promise that this game seamlessly connects with FAR: Lone Sails.It might seem short with a playtime of about 5-6 Hours but the pacing is on point and not one segment overstayed it's welcome.I would recommend this game heavily at a sale.At full price (19,99€ for me at the time of writing this) it's still a good grab especially if you played the first one and were longing for more.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

Each and every stair is placed in such a way that you will inevitably fall through it and end way at the bottom of some traversal bit quite often. In many places there are gaps that will do the same. Navigating the ship is a mess.I got to the chain puzzle and gave up. Do not care to finish this mess.

_childDocuments_.review: Far: Changing Tides is a melancholic, enigmatic masterpiece of desolation and destruction that takes place in a world only a few years into our future. The visuals are stunning and the water is so beautiful that it almost makes me look forward to our inevitable demise. The music is tranquil and gives us a fitting sense of despair as our character makes their way through the world presented. The game is a management style game that builds off the first beautifully with added mechanics such as new compartments, diving and new features that I won't spoil. As with the first game, running around in a panic trying to take care of the vessel is the best part of the game and never gets stale throughout game play. I can't really think of anything negative about the game, and as a person who is quickly losing interest in living, that says a lot. I recommend it if you like submarines.

_childDocuments_.review: Phenomenal. Never have I played a game as beautiful. Despite being a 2D linear adventure game, It makes the journey entirely your own. Never has a game given me so much with so little, including absolutely no dialogue or story text. I felt so many emotions playing this game and none directly told to me, none forced upon to me, none that felt the game's and no my own.It is a very simple game that is essentially a 2D interactive atmosphere and world. There is an underlying story to it all, but you are tasked to piece it together. I strongly suspect no two players would have gone through the same story in their head. There are light puzzle and resource management elements, extremely light. They are not at all a focus, and are even toned down from the first. The true game is the journey.Better than the first. A longer more personal journey and tale that was able to bring up much more out of me than the first. However this makes me strongly want to play the first to discover any ties they have. If you're into this kind of thing, or even just want to find out if you are I highly Recommend the Far series. Start with the first and then play into the second. Definitely worth the money

_childDocuments_.review: Far: Changing Tides, the sequel to the much-acclaimed 'Far: Lone Sails,' is an absolute triumph in every aspect. The game took me about five hours to complete, each moment more captivating than the last. It builds on the solid foundation laid by its predecessor and expands it in ways that are both ambitious and profoundly satisfying.The visual presentation is nothing short of spectacular. Every scene is a masterpiece, richly detailed and vibrant, enhancing the emotive, atmospheric storytelling that defines the FAR series. The transition from the lonely vistas of 'Lone Sails' to the expansive, dynamic environments of 'Changing Tides' is seamless yet impressively innovative.Gameplay in 'Changing Tides' is diverse and engaging. Not only do you manage and upgrade a versatile boat, but the game also introduces new elements such as a submersible and opportunities to explore on foot and even swim. Each mode of exploration offers its own set of puzzles and challenges, making the gameplay feel fresh and exciting throughout. The puzzles are thoughtfully designed, encouraging creativity and experimentation, and perfectly paced to keep you intrigued without ever feeling frustrating.'Far: Changing Tides' is an odyssey that beautifully captures the essence of adventure and the poignant solitude of its setting. This sequel not only meets the high expectations set by its predecessor but surpasses them, cementing the FAR series as a standout in the genre of atmospheric exploration games.I am left eagerly hoping for a third installment, as the journey through the breathtaking worlds of the FAR series has been an unforgettable experience. If you appreciate games that combine stunning visuals, innovative gameplay, and emotional depth, 'Far: Changing Tides' is not to be missed.

_childDocuments_.review: Another lesson in less-is-more.Very much like the previous game, Far: Changing Tides tasks you with maintaining a vessel across various landscapes and situations.  Collecting various upgrades along the way, your vessel's abilities change to keep you going through your journey.One thing I will say is this was a little light on set-pieces, I recall chugging along in the previous game while an explosion rocks the landscape and thunders boulders around me.  I can't really think of any in this outside of the completion of puzzles (of which there are a good few), not a problem exactly but I do like a bit of cinema in games like these.Mechanically it's very solid and enjoyable, but I can't help feeling something was missing, a bit of roller-coaster perhaps. _childDocuments_.review: I must admit, this is one of the best sequels I've played.From the trailers, I saw that now you'll have to control a fancy ship instead of a car, and the developers have carefully transferred the management of your companion  here, but they've also added several new mechanics that greatly enhance the gameplay.I'm not much of a lore enthusiast, but towards the end, I began to notice more and more details and events of this world. Apparently, this is how lore and its presentation should be, so that even a "slow thinker" like me could start to appreciate and become interested.Overall, the game has become even better: longer duration, more mechanics, more events, more locations, more art design, more puzzles. _childDocuments_.review: TL;DRFun short experience made with seemingly less love and an annoying layout of the vessel. Recommended if you like short unsusual games and when it's on sale. _childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent sequel to a fantastic game. While it improves on many of the aspects of the first game, it also comes with some new issues, which while a slight damper, don't ultimately mar the experience.In terms of improvements, the ship has more space for storage, which is a big issue in the first game. Additionally, there are more entries/exits and corridors to allow free movement within the ship, which is great. There's also a zoom-out key, which is MUCH needed, and fixed a frustrating issue with the first game where you had to constantly be running outside to see what was coming up.In terms of issues, there are a few sections which feel like they really drag on. While the scale increase of the second game is great (more gameplay!) there are also quite a lot of sections where I felt a bit bored. In the first game, the few areas where there was nothing happening and you just got to go forward and enjoy the scenery felt like a reprieve, and a well-earned rest and chance to enjoy the background. In this game, you're often looking at the same massive set piece for the entire time, which can be a bit slow.Additionally, while the improvements to the interior are noticeable, it has the same problem of putting passageways and buttons in locations where I find myself jumping into them or falling through holes while just trying to get around the ship. The zoom-out key is also unable to be re-bound (like all the keys) and must be held down to be used, which was a bit frustrating as there were many sections where I was just holding C the whole time, when it would've been better as a toggle.Ultimately the experience is still incredible, however. It makes me eager to see if there will be a continuation of the story in a third game, and makes me really want to see a roguelike/co-op experience with this kind of ship management at some point, from any developer. Really a fantastic game that you can't go wrong with, especially if you enjoyed the first one.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: The good- Gorgeous, minimal 3d visuals. Amazing, post apocalyptic world with many different places. Watching the colors and the lighting conditions change with the weather is great. Sea and underwater locations are nice too.- Solid, peculiar atmosphere that makes you feel alone and deserted.- Despite being a bit repetitive its gameplay is unique with some nice mechanics. It feels great to navigate the vessel and control its various parts and at some points the workload gets pretty heavy. It's nice that the vessel gets upgraded by time, acquiring some new tools.- The vessel and its mechanical parts are well designed. It feels like a machine that is alive, being in constant communication with the player.- Nice, fluid animations. Moving mechanical parts feels great. Protagonist's movement, running and swimming are very pleasant.- Responsive, effective controls. You perform various things with only a few commands.- Cool, convincing physics. How you catch or drop objects, how they float into water. Everything seems pretty natural.- Fantastic, calm music that enhances the feeling of survival and loneliness.- Good audio design especially for the moving mechanical parts. Environmental sounds are scattered but nice.- It's so relaxing and has some dreamy, surreal moments.The bad- The vessel evolves during only the first third of the game. After that controlling it becomes a little bit repetitive. Also, the navigation only sequences are too long and at some point they become boring.- Puzzles have some cool mechanics, but they're all pretty straight forward. There is no challenge and not much thought is required. They're only few puzzles too.- There is no story at all. You don't have any specific purpose and you don't know where you're going to. You do things just because they're there.- Collecting all these items for fuel ruins the flow of the journey. Stopping, swimming, carrying and all over again gets a bit annoying at some points.- Flat, uninteresting protagonist without a personality or backstory.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: This game doubles down on the fun quirks of "ship management" that the original game had and it definetly feels that it accomplished its potential, it didnt feel lackluster at all.The game is also longer than the first one, not by alot mind you, but definetly longer.For the puzzles, theres definetly alot more compared to the first game and... well they are quite straight forward and slightly more complex than the first game, but you wont be splitting no atoms with these brain ticklers thats for sure, and that's fine since as i said before its not really the foccus of the FAR series, so it doesnt come off as a shallow experience at all.(there was one part where i spent 10 minutes like a dummy stuck on a area because i was trying to dock on the wrong place, but thats on me for being silly brained, not on the game)The enviroments are quite interesting, exploring further into the wreckages of a past civilization than the first game ever did, you go inside buildings, shacks and more and it really helps into giving an insight of what once was a "thriving" society, exploring and looking around both under and above water is very fun and can be rewarding by finding "stashes" of fuel. The ambience in general is where i feel that this game kinda suffers with compared to the previous one. It may be due to it being alot more colorfull and full of natural life but i cant help but think that it didnt give the same sense of wonder and mistery that the first game had, nothing hit as hard as the bittersweet beauty of a ruined society of the first game, and it just kinda didnt really interest me like the first game did. this next part is very personal opinion (and also spoiler):Overall if you played the Far: Lone Sails and enjoyed it i'd recommend getting this one as well, its a solid experience, brings more to the table and gives "closure" to the series, with the only downside being that it doesnt hit as hard as the first one.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a worthy successor to its predecessor. Although I felt a bit more aimlessness here, and somehow the post-apocalyptic atmosphere wasn't as strong, the game's world and mechanics more than made up for these shortcomings.I enjoyed handling and repairing this makeshift ship-submarine vehicle, cobbled together from all sorts of odds and ends, just as much as the one in the previous game. I hope that both vehicles will be available in some physical form someday; I would gladly have them on my shelf.The ending of the story was simultaneously sad and touching.Overall, once again, the Okomotive development team has delivered a brilliant game to us. _childDocuments_.review: A great follow-up to Far: Lone Sails. This one is set on the sea instead of on land, so it has another dimension that you (and later your vehicle) can travel in. Along the way you gradually add whole new sections to your vehicle that make it do new and interesting things, introducing new mechanics and gameplay at a perfect pace that's frequent enough to keep things fresh, without being too frequent and feeling overwhelming.

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful graphics, beautiful music, beautiful story told without words, beautiful fictional world - all on an epic scale that makes you feel humbled to just... be there, seeing all the ages-old machinery moving and natural forces still working, as if no one ever really left.The best part is the gameplay - the game is not at all afraid to get you doing some COOL stuff - your ship is an ever-expanding list of buttons to press and things to check - much more complex than the uh... Okomotive? in Lone Sails! You are NEVER out of things to do - but the game leaves you moments to choose whether or not you want to do the regular loop or just... take it all in. And the game knows when to do either/or. During tense sections, you'd be running around the ship trying to patch things together while somehow keeping everything running - and in calm sections, you might choose to not angle the sail to 100% efficiency just so you get to sit back at the front of the ship and... relax.You never know what this game throws at you - giant waves, storms, crazy machinery, underwater cities, deep sea, giant waterfalls, INCREDIBLE icebergs (my favorite section personally), you get to FLY at some point?!This game is clearly made with SO MUCH love and I hope you give it a chance! It's 4-5 hours long, but let me ask you this -What's worth more?A game you will play for many hours and remember only a fraction?Or 4-5 hours of a game that is PACKED with memorable sections and you will look back at for maybe years.I know that FAR: Lone Sails had inspired me in my art projects immensely, and the game I'm currently working on is very inspired by idease FAR: Lone Sails did incredibly well! I actually have no idea how I waited this long to play this game, but I'm so SO glad I got to it. One of these games I knew would be absolutely incredible without even seeing a single detail about it - loved Lone Sails, love this too.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: This is the second episode of the Far series. Although it would work fine as a stand-alone, I would MASSIVELY recommend playing Far: Lone  Sails first. Again, it's not like this story is contingent upon that one.. but there are a couple moments that will be a lot more profound if you do. Ergo I'd massively recommend the first one first :-)So what is it? It's in the genre of Inside, Limbo, Stela, Gris etc in which you're a lone character in a beautiful world with no dialogue, picking up the story through context. In this particular world, you're a lone person on a journey - this time in the ocean, rather than on land.You are once again in a huge vehicle which you use for your journey. This time, I was a little afraid at first that they had dumbed the vehicle down, because it didn't have all the gadgets and systems that it did in the first one... but I stuck with it, and found out that instead of starting out with a mostly complete vehicle, in this one, you kinda build your boat along the way. A little farther in the game and you DO have all those rooms, systems, gadgets, etc. You will have to use these effectively to propel your boat, maintain it, repair it, and more.I don't like to give spoilers, so I'm going to hide part of my statement here. This vehicle is quite different than the first in surprisingly satisfying ways. Once again, my overall ratings for the overall gameplay are the same: the music isn't the best thing I've ever heard but very nice, sound effects very satisfying, gameplay EXTREMELY satisfying, storyline very interesting, graphics absolutely beautiful, and overall just a GEM among video games.The idea is simple. In your journey, you use your boat to go. You sail and sail, until you run into a roadblock. Once your path is blocked, you've got to go solve some puzzles and remove the roadblock. The puzzles are a nice balance between "so easy it seems like busy-work rather than a decent puzzle" and "so hard you ragequit every 30 minutes." They're not very challenging, but they're also not stupid. Each one is very unique and can be solved with some ease. Once you solve the riddle, your path is unblocked, and you may proceed.I've seen some reviews which suggest that the sailing is tedious, but I didn't find it this way at all. With the gorgeous background, the work of maintaining your vessel, and all that kind of stuff, I never found myself getting bored. Sure, it's not constant action and bullets flying everywhere, but it's beautiful and fun, so I have no complaints.I always try to say whether or not I'd pay full price... this one is a little more expensive than the first, but also a little longer and in some ways a little more complicated. It is still somewhat short.. although I logged 6.8 hours, I must confess that the day before I was on the go all day so at a certain point I paused the game and dozed off, so I recon I spent about 5.5-6 hours playing. Still... I do think the game is worth full price, given just how beautiful the world is and just how much I loved my vessel. I would recommend full price to anyone.Overall, this would be a FANTASTIC title to add to your library - though again, DO consider playing Lone Sails first. If you can get it on sale, this is an easy, easy buy. Absolutely stunning game.. and I am hoping and praying for a "next installment" :-)

_childDocuments_.review: "Far: Changing Tides" stands as a testament to how developers can take a solid foundation and elevate it to new heights. Building upon the unique and atmospheric world of its predecessor, "Far: Lone Sails," this sequel surpasses expectations in several key areas, delivering a gaming experience that addresses previous shortcomings with aplomb.One of the most noticeable improvements in "Changing Tides" is the size and functionality of your trusty machine. Unlike its predecessor, where the contraption felt a bit unwieldy and vulnerable, the new vessel in "Changing Tides" is not only bigger but also much easier to navigate. You also no longer need to constantly babysit every component, which alleviates much of the frustration from the first game. This change allows to focus more on exploration and puzzle-solving rather than micromanagement, making the gameplay smoother and more enjoyable. The gameplay in "Changing Tides" is where it truly shines. While "Lone Sails" had its moments of brilliance, the sequel introduces a much broader range of activities and challenges. The puzzles are more intricate and varied, demanding more creativity from players. The game keeps you engaged by constantly presenting new obstacles and opportunities, ensuring that boredom rarely sets in, although there are few moments where you're just supposed to just sail forward and soak the atmosphere. The silent, storytelling continues, with glimpses of a desolate world and its history unveiled through environmental cues and subtle changes in the surroundings. Visually, "Changing Tides" continues the series' tradition of beautiful, minimalist art design. The environments are breathtaking, and the contrast between the desolate, ruined world and the hopeful expanse of the sea is stunning. The audio design complements the atmosphere perfectly, enhancing the emotional impact of the journey.In conclusion, "Far: Changing Tides" is a worthy successor to "Far: Lone Sails." It manages to maintain the series' signature ambiance while evolving and expanding its gameplay and storytelling. It's a game that invites players to embark on a contemplative and mesmerizing journey across a beautifully crafted world. If you enjoyed the first installment, you'll find "Changing Tides" to be a delightful and immersive continuation of the series.Recommended, but maybe on sale

_childDocuments_.review: A solid if a little safe follow up to LONE SAILS. An acquired taste; but a good chill experience that feels particularly refreshing after a long binge of high-octane action shlock. Legible puzzles; Immaculate soundtrack and art style. Good technical performance.  As a minimalist exploration of loneliness and the twisted beauty of ecological collapse it works well for the most part. It can feel a bit too arty at points; but its pace is tight and if you are in the right head space it can feel emotionally absorbing in clever ways.  Would recommend it, but at a discount.  7.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: Its just fun to play. Beautiful scenery and very clever story book.However, I discovered a bug.At one of the floating towers, where the little man has to dive with the hook of the crane, he got lost when coming back up into the ship. I made a short clip and a screen photo in order to identify the location.Question: Where and to whom can I report the bug?Thank for input.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game but pick it up on sale. You can likely complete it under 5 hours.The story and puzzles are decent enough. My only criticism was the jumping mechanics felt frustrating. I don't know if it was the layout of the ship or i'm just getting old. But trying to grab ladders or jump between platforms was often frustratingly tedious to perform correctly the first try. They might be better with a controller.I also felt that "transit" between objectives was kinda dull and took too long. I don't recall it being so slow in the previous game. Maybe i just lacked the patience. But i often felt there wasn't a great deal to look at or do between objectives. Granted the title of the game implies that you need to cover vast distances. But honestly most of the transits were frustratingly long in my opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: this game, like its predecessor, is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ fantastic. I adore this game so much! something about it reminds me of old LBP levels in a wonderful wonderful. physically having to run around a vehicle, manually operate the controls and systems... there's such a wonderful connection you feel to the vessel that only this kind of gameplay can truly communicate. it's so tactile and pleasant. I really truly hope to see more games from this world. I think a third game would be a great place to maybe incorporate a 2 player couchplay experience. where one player is Lone and the other is (well the nomanclature would suggest this game's protagonist is named Changing) the protagonist of this game. and the combined powers of the okomotive and the vessel allow a new dimension of travel? all I really want to say is I'd play a franchise of these games for another 60 entries if you guys made them. and here's hoping this blossoms into a whole new genre of adventure games ( I was thinking we could call it vehicle management but perhaps it could be called FAR:like).the only thing I could complain about is how short this game is, but then again it's about 4X as long as Lone Sails.1000/10play it now
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: I'm giving this a positive review because I generally liked both Changing Tides and its predecessor Lone Sails and want their developers to keep making games in the future.However, I do have to say that Changing Tides did not improve too much on the first FAR's concept. Sure, there are different mechanics unlocked throughout the game, but I feel like there's a bunch of opportunities missed in the design of the game. There could have been more variety in the puzzles, less bugs, better core mechanics to the movement of the machine and its upkeep, and more interesting exploration aspects. All in all, it feels like the developers were afraid of expanding their game design in a meaningful way. Still, if you liked Far: Lone Sails, you will also enjoy Changing Tides.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: Whilst I prefer the first game (as it felt like it had a more solid personality in terms of the music and flow of the level narrative), I still hold this game in high regard as a beautifully crafted experience. I'd argue that the ratings for this game are accurate and that it is definitely worth a play. I look forward to seeing what Okomotive do next :)
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: Set sail against a backdrop of desolate landscapes as somber music comes and goes throughout your journey. Setting a despondent mood but a despondent mood that's enthralling. The magic however isn't here if you've played or at least since I played the first game. It was a fun game, and I enjoyed taking another journey. I would say play it for sure! If you haven't played the first. I think it would be alright to just play this one, or just play the first one. They're both good games. Sometimes this one feels a bit more drawn out unnecessarily it doesn't make it bad. It's just you need to be in the mood for it, and if you've played the first...it can be a bit like MOVE ON WITH IT! But nonetheless an experience I'm glad I got to partake in.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: I want more.It's so peaceful, so relaxing. It's not a hard game, it's the sort of thing you could mindlessly burn a few hours doing, losing track of time. The art is beautiful, the world is fascinating, the ship I absolutely love, to the point that I want to try building one in the real world, even if only as a toy or a model.I only have two complaints, the first being that there isn't MORE to the game, I would love some kind of endless mode, maybe a procedural generated event system that let's you sail on indefinitely on an endless ocean, clearing obstacles every so often and navigating various changes.And second, some level of customization for the ships colors or banners, something to personalize it ya know.I just love this game, I want MORE of this game.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed FAR: Lone Sails when I played it a while ago, but I don't really remember why. This was enjoyable, but not as enjoyable. I actually think this sequel is too long, potentially... It's still good, but I'd really recommend playing Lone Sails and leaving it there, unless you're REALLY aching for more.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: Finishing the game, I was a tad disappointed compared to the original. I give this advice so a third game, if made, can be improved.1. no danger. falls, swimming great depths (oxygen), sharks, threat of being stranded, threat of falling off the boat and losing the boat, real storms and waves that can cause harm. I even tried to jump into the material compactor to no avail. Feeding in material and running engine in full reverse to avoid a water fall. Outrunning a volcano like the original! Avoiding hail like the original. A real adventure requires danger.2. More interesting puzzles. I felt the puzzles were too easy.3. tedious recovering and carrying certain items. give me a backpack so I don't have to make so many trips.4. not enough back story.Positives: loved operating the ship and all the mechanisms. Loved the scenery and the art. Knowing Unity, I can understand how difficult it would be to make a game like this.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: Sadly not as good as the first one.It does almost nothing different and yet gets almost everything wrong.Controls feels less responsive, gameplay is slowed down and less impactful, music is less present, the game vastly outstays its welcome, and the achievements condescendingly congratulate the obvious at every turn.It's a shame, I really liked the first game and really wanted to like the sequel. The visuals were upgraded somewhat but then it ran like ♥♥♥♥ on every platform I tried it on.I originally bought it on switch where it performed so poorly I couldn't pull off basic jumps and I gave up.So many times playing this game things would fail to trigger properly and I'd get stuck for a while till I'd give up and look up a guide only to find out the thing I did was correct it just hadn't worked.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: i really enjoyed this game, the art style was beautiful, the music was good but i did like lone sails a little bit more, and the story was very good especially because everything that was in lone sail and in the beginning were eventually connected in the end, i even liked how the some things were left for interpretation in the end. however there were some things i found annoying gameplay wise, one example being the second sail making that noise when it closes over and over again and the fact that the sail would get damaged on things that weren't even near it. considering that the issues i had were minor ill give it an 9.8/10
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely recommend. It's the kind of game that leaves you speechless at the credits screen - just like the predecessor, FAR: Lone Sails.My only regret is playing this one (Changing Tides) first and Lone Sails second. I highly recommend playing Lone Sails first. The endings of both games have much more impact if played chronologically - that's how they were designed. But even if you don't, you will love both games. They're great.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: I wonderful, beautiful game with a story that gives you goosebumps. There's no traditional storytelling, except the one you will need to infer. I also highly recommend you play the first game "FAR lone sail" to get the full intended effect of these two games.Full recommend. It's a chill game with a bit of puzzle solving and a very likable artstyle that has its own endearing charm.Really looking forward to another such production. Not necessarily the same universe but the concept agrees with me very much.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a massive improvement over the first. It's 3 times as long gameplay wise, and they added a lot more to the ship you use. A true successor to the first. My next question is, if and when they make a third, will it be co-op? If so, I'd hope it to be optional, but I'm not opposed to it.SPOILERS AHEADStory wise, I like that it eventually ties in to the first game. Its bin a while since I played the first game and I had thought it was continuing where we left off, but seeing Lone at the end disproved that immediately. And it was awesome seeing the original ship again! Even if it was in shambles.Overall, I give this game a 9.5/10. One day I'd like to come back to this game franchise and play both of them in order so that I can judge the return value properly, then it'll be a 10/10. Maybe there'll be a third one in a few years time? Holding out hope!
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: Great sequel but it is essentially just a copy pasta of the previous game with zero improvements but a longer playtime.The color palette once again consist only of various shades of desaturated grey and brown. Everything is bland and boring, exactly the same as the first game. I can understand they went for the post-apo feel but they could at the very least add some lush green underwater vegetation or something.The music is once again missing in most parts of the game leaving you stuck with just the sound of waves, wind and your depression creeping in. Not a fan.But overall it was a nice journey and I really liked the ending. And even though you need to deal with denuvo ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ to launch the game, I would still recommend it when it's on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: Let's begin with a warning:   This game runs like TRASH on the Steam Deck! Someone at Okomotive or Frontier must have decided that a 20€ indie game urgently needs the worst possible copy protection ever, and it turns the game into a stutter fest on the Steam Deck even on low settings. SHAME >8(   Okay but now to the actual game.Far:Changing Tides, just as its predecessor, is breathing atmosphere. If you liked Lone Sails, you will probably love this game here as well. I know I did. A fantastic way of telling a story without a single spoken word. Beautiful graphics, sound and music add to the experience. However ,somehow I think Far:Lone Sails was a bit more challenging. For example, I was eager to collect most everything that I could use as fuel. I stuffed the belly of my ship with fuel, expecting to run out of it at some point. Just, this never happened. If fuel does not matter, then why even put it in the game? Just so that you are being motivated to use the sails every now and then? I wish the game were a bit more challenging and tense. Thankfully, some of the puzzles were somewhat interesting. I took my time to finish this (as I said, going for all the useless fuel stuff that I could find :P) and I was having a good time. It's mostly a slow and relaxing game. Very much to my likes.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10Far Changing Tides is a step-up from the first game and this time, you're going to really sail in the waters. Everything have been get better, gameplay, art design, audio and specially music. Like the last game, you need to take care of your machine to get through your journey. This will make you find a dependency to the machine, not strong like the first game but good enough. The only problem in this journey is that at the first half of the game after setting the sails, a lot of times spent just with relaxing and enjoying the view. But in the second half of the game, those are rare and this problem make the game unbalanced, because you miss those relaxing times. Except this problem, Far Changing Tides was one of my greatest second journeys I had.+:Entertaining gameplay that never get boringFantastic art design and music better than the first game and also cameraSailing on the waters make the gameplay different from Far Lone SailsGood graphic and visual Surprising ending-:The first half and the second half of the game are unbalanced
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: A good sequel to the previous game.Just one thing: The puzzles are more intricate and there are times where trial and error is involved that can lead to a bit of frustration as you figure out what to do.This is a personal thing and might not apply to everyone but trial and error is not a logical way of solving puzzles. Some people might find the first game too simplistic but at least it was without "try this then try that, rinse and repeat till something works."Besides that one small issue, this is as enjoyable as the first game.Highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely loved FAR: Lone Sails, and I'm happy to say that FAR: Changing Tides is not only as good as Lone Sails, but better. Lone Sails felt like a trial, it walked so Changing Tides could run. This game just takes everything the first game did, but better, and over a longer span of time, everything in it feels new and creative, it never gets dull or feels uninspired. The main difference is that in Lone Sails, the game starts complex and gets simpler as upgrades are added, whereas Changing Tides actually starts simple then gets more complex as upgrades are added. This is by no means a bad thing, I actually like this method more, because as you get used to The Vessel and how it operates, something else is introduced to keep the gameplay fresh and keep you moving. And, naturally, the soundtrack and atmosphere of this game are once again just as good if not better than Lone Sails. If you liked FAR: Lone Sails, you will absolutely love FAR: Changing Tides.I would like to end this review with a prediction: I think there will be another FAR game, it will take place mostly in the sky, and it will be a co-op game, where the players play as the main characters from each game.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: Don't watch any gameplay before playing, and don't expect action, suspense or your eye-hand skills put to any sort of test. This game is all about atmosphere and shear experience, and as such it is truly an amazing work of art.That includes the music, the sound effects, the graphics, the animations, the puzzles, and how they all blend together perfectly.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: I usually hate the 'little child in a scary world' 'pushing right to see more' walking simulator, but this one I do recommend, pending one question:Do you like ships?You see, this is not a 'little child in a scary world pushing right to see more' simulator, but a 'little child in a awesome SHIP RAISING STEAM FULL SAIL to see more' simulator. There are actually game play other than pushing D or being chased while pushing D. You manage a SHIP.That I can gladly pay 20 bucks to see. Gosh I LOVE me boat. I named it A.K.A.S. Sutherland, the prefix stand for a** kickingly awesome ship. I raised sail like the perfect topman then went straight to the boiler room, then stand proudly at the bow doing a best captain impression. At the end of the campaign I meet that little girl from the first game. She stood there besides her car, broken after the journey, waiting, and my lad just raising his head up high at the bow of his INTACT boat. Who needs a car when you have a boat, ain't I right?Hands aloft and bear away, stable ahead to Whitecap Bay!
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: Not quite as satisfyingly bleak as the first (but that might be a good thing to some), but far more engaging in terms of gameplay and the variety of mechanics. What is pulled off with the engine is actually quite impressive at times, and it's just fun to play.The art and music are fantastic, of course. Here's hoping for a third game someday.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: a worthy sequel! this time we get to go in the water. the game is a bit longer, but if we're being honest with ourselves, you're not here for a marathon of gameplay. you can bang this out in an afternoon and have a ton of fun with it. very cute overall, highly recommend playing FAR: Lone Sails first though
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: I knew it, I had a feeling the ending would connect to the first game.  As soon as I saw the fire in the background.  Another beautiful story, rich with landscape experiences and emotion.  The whole idea of silence, as I mean gameplay silence, for you the player to simply experience traveling the landscape and moving forward, keeping your vessel in tip-top shape, adjusting to the environment, and navigating puzzles to move your story forward - all beautifully-rendered in a simply amazing story.  I will call these games an escape, an escape form our harsh reality, to live in a world offered to the player to fix, fuel, and keep surviving until finding a peaceful ending to complete two beautiful games into one.  You will enjoy the anxiety of keeping your ship fixed and ready for the next challenge, the puzzle solving, and the traversing a world now in peril, but a world of solidarity and loneliness, and you will feel such loneliness throughout your struggles and traveling.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: What an amazing journey! Beautiful sites and just enough to do to keep your hands busy while ya watch em go by. Love the calming management of the engine and sail. Would highly recommend. Also, get the first game, Far: Lone Sails. Same advantages as this one. Both are unique enough to make the second interesting while also being similar enough to create the same emotions (serene, calm, beautiful, etc.).
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: It has the same charm as the first game (FAR: Lone Sails). This time you get to be a sailor! It starts off as a boat and later upgrades into a submarine. I like that there were more storage hooks. I wish the repair hose was kept because the repair comes as individual objects that disappear after getting used up. The music and scenes are still lovely. I thought that the energy booster was cumbersome to use. It was nice that the jumping platform was kept this time to power up the engine. The little details are cute (like the flower garden) as well as the water details (ripples and being underwater).
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: I've played both games and enjoyed both. Nevertheless I compared it to the first one and here's my conclusion:- The controls felt a bit more nimble and worked out in the first one- Widescreen support was dropped in this one (just two black bars on the sides, which is a bit of a shame for this type of game)- Some sceneries have some extremely bright spots, the overall color grading of the first one seemed a bit more balanced (my screen is color calibrated).With the minor bad things out of the way:+ The overall game mechanics are done well and I really fell in love with the machine. Being on a bigger vessel than on the first one is amazing and all the control options you have just add up to that.+ Stunning sceneries which are not repetitive+ Amazing passive storytelling+ Good connection to the first one+ Soundtrack & sounddesign+ Overall idea with being on a ship/submarine in a postapocalyptic world+ Longer playtime than the first one: I  recommend this game to anyone who enjoyed the first one. It is truly a masterpiece.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: The reviews here sound a bit harsh, to be honest. This game is amazing! its only misfortune is having to be compared with its predecessor, Lone Sails.It's longer, more complex and definitely more ambitious. But with all this extra baggage it lost that perfect pacing Lone Sails had. So this will often feel tedious and padded. Long stretches of nothing, followed by the most trivial type of puzzle of pushing boxes to reach a higher place.The decision to move to water was a very promising one! Specially underwater. So much potential for mystery and fear. However it went unexplored. My thalassophobia itch wasn't scratched.I actually felt a little disappointed a couple of times during the game where I thought it was the ending, but it wasn't.Damn, this is getting more negative the longer I write. It's good though! might not be as tight and solid as the other one, but it is further exploration of the concept. And that is a good thing.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: Just like the first game, this is very well made, and is fun and interesting without too much of a challenge.  Some small parts seemed drag on a little bit which I don't remember happening in the first game, but overall still worth the play.  Tells a neat little disaster story with no dialogue.  Mostly just learning the mechanics of the game is the fun part.------------------------------Control Scheme I Used:Gamepad, using both D-Pad and Analog Stick.  D-Pad on land typically, Analog when swimming.------------------------------Worth the current price (CDN$ 22.79)?  Hard to say, it's not a bad price really.  Definitely worth it on a sale.What I actually paid: $9.01        ------------------------------Completionist Review:DLC Achievements: No DLCRating: A little repetitive, but just a bit before annoying.Can be completed in one run: Potentially, but you likely wont'.Chapter Select: Yes, a couple achievements indicate which ones to replay.Did I need/use a guide?  Yes, but only for clarification on one achievement, it wasn't required.There are a long stretches of this game where you're just driving forward for a while that are drawn out a little longer than I'd like, but overall it's not a hard game to complete, and I had fun getting them all.  Somehow I had more fun on my 2nd run when I more understood the mechanics of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: A great Sequel to Far: Lone Sails. It is the same themes and idea, but just expanded (and also obviously a... water ship... instead of a land ship). Beautiful stark wordless storytelling returns, and is just as fun to manage your vessel as it putters along with you tinkering with it as you go with light puzzles along the way.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: FAR: Changing Tides is a breathtaking adventure game that immerses players in a beautifully rendered oceanic world full of wonder, mystery, and danger. As Toe and Glitch, players embark on a journey to explore this vast and intriguing world, solving puzzles and uncovering hidden secrets along the way.One of the strengths of FAR: Changing Tides is its attention to detail. The game world is expertly crafted with stunning visuals and immersive sound design, which creates a sense of awe and wonder as players explore the world. The gameplay is also well designed, with puzzles that are challenging but not frustratingly difficult, and the game's mechanics are intuitive and easy to learn.Another strength of FAR: Changing Tides is its storytelling. The game features a compelling narrative that is delivered through environmental storytelling. The story is emotionally resonant, with themes of loss, grief, and the power of human connection (or lack of). Players will find themselves deeply invested in their journey.Overall, FAR: Changing Tides is a remarkable achievement in game design. It is a well-crafted adventure/puzzle game that offers players a deeply immersive and emotional experience. It is a must-play for anyone who enjoys such games.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked FAR: Lone Sails, you will like this. The (under)water atmosphere is done really well, and the puzzles are easy but satisfying. Operating the ship feels great, even better than in FAR: Lone Sails. The storytelling is also wonderfully done. While you don't have to have played FAR: Lone Sails to enjoy this, if you're going to play both (and you should!), I would recommend playing them in order.It does drag on a bit longer than FAR: Lone Sails, perhaps a bit too long in places. But I certainly don't regret playing, and wholeheartedly recommend this game to fans of its predecessor.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: Ah the next installment in the Far series, and what a great one. Building off of the first games vehicle mechanics Changing Tides brings a whole new vessel with which to get attached to. Somewhat familiar in operation the new okomotive fleshes out the mechanics of the first game in a very interesting and fun way. The water aspects of the game truly added a depth that allowed much more contrast to color schemes compared to the first game, while still keeping the melancholy and desolate tone. The Graphics are upgraded from the first game while still maintaining the same feel and visually the vistas are expansive. The sound design and music were both wonderful, from waves to the score it was a pleasant ride the whole trip that makes you forget about the destination and enjoy the journey. I will say it is somewhat of a short game probably averaging about 3-6 hours to complete, depending on if you want to stop and take in the scenery. Truly recommend playing this great game if you are looking for a relaxing atmospheric sail. (but playing the first one first). Gameplay: 8Graphics: 7Sound: 9Length: ShortFeel: 9
