_childDocuments_.review: A bigger, better sequel to an already great game.i.e. cute puzzle adventure set in an atmospheric, beautiful world filled with puzzles that don't require a Ph.D yet manages to make you feel invested in the world.And that's just the first game ^_^The sequel is just... better PLUS it ties up a loose end from the first game.Best "experienced" immediately after completely enjoying the first game.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: So after completing Lone Sail, I had to purchase Changing Tide immediately. There is legitimately nothing wrong with this game, or its predecessor. My only complaint has and always will be a desire for more. Perhaps not an endless mode for this game, though Lone Sail would benefit greatly from an endurance mode.In my mind, I had named the vessel from Lone Sail "Papa" after the grave of the characters Father and the workshop of their home, I even named the giant version you pilot for a time "Grandpa"In this game, the ship is "Mama" or "Mother" from the portrait to Toe's mother and the plant you can take with you. The emotional connection I had to these vessels is unreal, and the ending of Changing Tide left me in Tears.Okomotive, I beg you. Continue this series, and allow me to give you more money.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: For the most part, this sequel is even better than the first game. This time you get to explore underwater ruins, which is pretty cool. As weird as it may sound, some of the best parts of the game are the ones that involve doing nothing but adjusting the mast on the boat. It's relaxing. My only problem was that controls and movement were a bit more awkward this time around. Jumping while grabbing things was very hit-or-miss.The ending was also very gratifying after playing both games.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:Graphics were great just like beforeMusic still sounds amazing although I definitely preferred the last games soundtracks moreThe ways of controlling the ship felt really good and easy to do once you learned how they operated and were pretty coolI was chilling the whole time during this game and it was pretty enjoyable glad they made a second one.Cons:Felt like there were some awkward pauses at timesMusic would build up nicely like the previous game but not often enough of as epic as the last game to meEarly in the game the create a moment that you're in danger and i really liked that, but as the game went on it never had that feeling again to me, wish they did that more since you have a repair toolThe ending was nice but the transition into it was a bit weird and sudden. Overall the game was fun! Grabbing it on sale is nicer too!
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: Such a charming game! I had an amazing time with this as it presented beautiful imagery, fun gameplay and a relaxing experience. The game keeps adding things to your vehicle to keep things fresh and the variety of environments you explore makes it extra fun. The ending was very clever. I'm glad that I dove into this gem.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: I would give this a 9/10, I loved it just as much as the original game, if not more so, the story telling in such an environmentally immersive way is truly enchanting. The only thing that keeps the 9 from reaching a 10 is that I was having trouble with the jumping mechanic. It was difficult sometimes to jump on a precise point or on a floating platform, especially with such quick movement speed. But besides that, If you enjoyed Lone Sails, then you'll definitely enjoy this one.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: Great music as well as sounds from the game. An interesting idea for the game. The appearance of the game and its mechanics are addictive from the first launch until the very end. It just happened that I played and bought the game on the last day of Easter. It was on discount. I took a chance and let me tell you that I wish it was longer, but every minute I spent in it was something extraordinary. Detachment from reality, nice views and great relaxation. A big round of applause for the developer and everyone involved. I am extremely curious and will certainly look into your future productions. This title won my heart. A game made with passion and heart. Congratulations again. Yours sincerely.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: This was a worthy successor to Far: Lone Sails.  In some ways it improved upon the original, and in others it didn't match up, but overall it was still a beautiful, relaxing game of exploration, learning about the world and about the meaning of searching for something.Around the middle or two thirds into the game it dragged on more than I would have liked, but I really enjoyed the ending.  The visuals were much more complex and detailed than the original, and remained beautiful, but in a way they looked less hand painted, and although the music was good, some areas could have used more music as they at times felt quiet, as if the game was telling me I should stop and do something, but there was nothing around.  The game mechanics are similar to the first one, and expanded upon - maybe a little too much - as you sometimes end up juggling more things than I would have liked.  The variety of locations and ways of traveling is great, but although this game is maybe 5-6 hours compared to 3-4 like the first one, some of it drags on and although it has some "wow" moments, they maybe didn't hit as hard as ones in the first game.  If this were a long movie, I would prefer trimming 30-60 min of it to make it a tight 3-4 hours instead of a stretched out 5-6.Overall, if the first game was a 5/5, this would be a 4/5.  Still great though not as impressive and spot on as the first one.  That being said, it's worth playing and I hope they make a third game.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: - As with its prequel, this game's art direction is excellent. Every frame is a photo, kinda like a Kubrick film. Seriously, just about any screenshot you take of the game will look fantastic. It's not graphically intensive, but it is very pretty- Traveling along presents you with several scenic environments for eye candy. For most of the game, you'll also have your cool steampunk ship to keep you company, which grows and changes as you find new parts to attach to it- Even though I only beat this game yesterday, I don't recall any of the music. I'll assume that means it was passable but certainly not memorable- The sparse sound design is appropriate for the ruinous post-apocalyptic seascapes you traverse. Most of what you hear is the machinery of your ship, crashing of the waves, and the whistling wind- Regardless of the size of the screen you're playing on, it can be easy to lose sight of your character when the view zooms out. There's fortunately a zoom-in function that helps smooth over this issue- If you played Far: Lone Sails, you're already well-prepared for this experience. Neither game in the franchise is story-heavy, but it still makes more sense to play the prequel first (otherwise the end of this game will make little sense)- The story mostly boils down to two words: Go right. Well, until the end of the game at least, which features a brief period of leftward travel- Like the prequel, very little is presented to you by way of explanation. There's just you, your ship, the way back, and the way forward. You don't know why you're going right or what's over there- Despite the game's linearity, the mysteriousness of it's objectives and the main character's motivations still lend it some sense of mystery. It somehow still feels like you're exploring even though you're only heading in a single direction- The overall tone is somber, lonely, and morose, yet peacefully so- The main gameplay loop is to manage your ship's sails and/or engine to keep it moving forward. Sailing is pretty easy, but running the engine is an exercise in multitasking. You'll be bouncing back and forth managing your stoking the fire, refilling fuel, handling boiler temperature, setting the gear, raising/lowering depth, and toggling overcharge while occasionally tending to repairs. Hell, even stopping the ship is a multi-step process (stop pumping bellows, change gear to neutral, turn on hose, put out fire). Believe me when I say that you'll be happy when you see wind and can raise the sails.- Some people may find this sort of micromanagment a little tedious, but there's enough puzzles sprinkled throughout to offer a change of pace. Puzzle design is difficult enough that the game managed to stump me for several minutes on a couple of occasions, but more careful observation got me out of both jams. Don't be afraid to test possibly wrong solutions- I'm never going to go back and get all of the achievements, frankly. Managing the engine was annoying enough at times that the thought of having to do it quickly is a non-starter- I started out on the Steam Deck, but switched to a bigger screen after only a few minutes. While "playable" is technically an accurate description, I don't think I'd recommend it- It ran perfectly on my slightly dated (2019) hardware- It's only a 5-7 hour experience (less if you're attempting to speedrun it), so the price tag seems a little steep. Probably best to wait for a sale- . I liked it a little bit less than its prequel, but only because the experience is so similar. You're just on water instead of land. That said, the core gameplay and visual style are both good, so it's worth picking up if you want a short, relaxing experience and the price is right
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ much, it is a beautiful sorrowful story told entirely by the environment as you travel aboard your ship. the ending made me cry because(no spoilers) it involves the first game too, I love these 2 games and this developer. if you have some free time you should 100% play FAR: Lone Sails first, and then play this game, I literally cannot recommend these enough, Okomotive knows how to make a beautiful story with 0 words spoken
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: I loved Far: Lone Sails and finally got round to buying the sequel - as before it's a charming game, part puzzle, part resource management, part platform. The graphics and music excellently complement the gameplay and the finale is very unexpected. There are places where it's not simple and working out what you have to do is less than straightforward but it's a brilliantly satisfying game
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: Take everything you love about the first game and replace it with an agonizing, tedious grind. Seems awesome at first but you quickly run into a dull wasteland of an annoying puzzler. All the relaxing exploratory joy of the first game is instead a frustrating platformer with annoyingly positioned buttons (much worse than first game which was already kinda wonky there). Even without comparing to the first, the game is littered with frustrations that remove the relaxing exploratory sensation this series had. Your sail can smash into all sorts of objects that aren't very clear, and even with the camera zoomed out you will never see obstacles coming in time to do anything.Ultimately, I wish I had just passed this one by and played something I actually enjoyed.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: forgot to write a review for this, what can i say? its absolutely amazing, well worth the money.its a relaxing experience taking you on a journey to see many interesting places while keeping to few but solid set of mechanics, and i'd take this any day over tons of unpolished features. 9/10, "i want more"
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely wonderful game. Very few games leave me sitting in contemplation during the end credits. The pacing is not as good as the first one in terms of puzzles and story, but it has much more depth in its mechanics which are pretty interesting. This game expands on the established world and mechanics of the first one, so it will be a way better experience if you've played Lone Sails first. Overall 9/10, a few annoyances with pacing and mechanics, but it keeps encouraging me to push forward to experience the next spectacle.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: This game is longer than Far:Lone Sails and has more depth to it when it comes to controlling the ship and the environments. I didn't feel connected to the protagonist as much as I did with the first game's protagonist. Controlling the ship is complex which made it more fun. Puzzles were amazing and smartly hidden.  This has great imagery like the first game. I never thought that I would get that ending when I started the game. If you are a person who has played the first game and loved it. This is a worthy sequel to it.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: Much like the first game, I enjoyed the diegetic design, and the world building. There is more to manage on the ship this time as new mechanics are introduced. In my opinion, this doesn't really take away from the world. Playing this game right after the first was certainly a great decision! I would definitely recommend this game. I got it on sale for $10
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: I've played both games and though I would overally suggest playing this game for the aesthetics and some interesting ideas with the boat, I want to add some remarks to the developers1. Somehow the controls are worse than the previous one. Not sure exactly what but the jumping is problematic and the ship layout makes it problematic. I think the controls are sometimes to sudden and I also don't agree with not automatically clinging to a ladder2. I think the in between scenes have grown disproportionally and make them boring. I understand the atmospheric part, but having to work either by sail or by furnace through the transition makes you stick but without any value since the surrounding changes very litle. Imagine you are under the water for which you have the option.3. I really liked the addition of the radar like device. 4. Some parts with the boat under water and you trying to manipulate the surrounding with the winge are very impressive. Well done.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game. Loved the first one and the sequal certainly doesnt disappoint.- Love the atmosphere and enviromental storytelling.- no HUD, no tutorial, just learn by doing- great mechanics and surprises with the vehicle, loved every bit of gameplay.- the music is awesome, kicks in dynamically and is always fitting.- I like that the puzzles are not that difficult. You almost always know what to do, yet enjoy doing the puzzles. Just seeing the little systems intertwine is awesome.I said it before on the first games review, would love to see a roguelike like this. It has a lot of potential as a survival game, but I also get, that the emotional story telling gets lost. Either way, absolutely recommend playing the FAR games and cant wait for a third one.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent line of games consisting of two parts! Amazing! There are no words to express delight! The first part of the game is much shorter, simpler and easier.The second one is much longer in terms of game time, plot events! Many thanks to the developers of this game! I would like to play the following parts in the future if such are in development! Many thanks for the ATMOSPHERE! Everything is as I like it!
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: Changing Tides is very similar to and somewhat different from Lone Sails at the same time.Sails to me was a great walking simulator with a fun walking mechanism. Tides is a more game-like game, it does feel like you are progressing forward in a game as you solve the current obstacle.Perhaps the biggest difference to me was how our 'relationship' with the machine _feels_ like. In Sails the machine was our home, our vehicle, our companion. In Tides it's a vehicle we are travelling with. In Sails we were Michael Knight and the machine was our KITT. In Tides we are Magnum and the machine is our Ferrari.I prefer Sails, but that doesn't mean Tides is worse, it's just slightly different. Sails set the bar very high, Tides doesn't reach that but it is very-very close. Both are brilliant games.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: The sequel was just as good if not better than game one. I loved every aspect of it and with you meeting lone at the end of the game it's just amazing. Even after I've played it a second time i nearly cry at the end. I hope there's a possibility of a third game, but if not than the end of both games was worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: I pretty much enjoyed Lone Sails. Very atmospheric, beautiful landscapes while listening to the great soundtrack. You were on the Okomotive, aka the steam machine trying to complete your journey. Here, Changing Tides takes another spin into this franchise which is now set on the water and into the water, with a new machine.I found this sequel to not be as good as the first game, where the puzzles weren't so irritating, tedious and lots of padding (pun intended). Here, you just have too many obstacles to slow you down and makes the game longer this way. The game mechanics were much simpler, easier and worked better on LS.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: I picked up this game because a YouTuber I follow, Thalasso Hobbyer, built the main vehicle. I really liked the gameplay loop in Far. Managing the ship was fun and running around, solving various problems as they came up with satisfying. The world of Far is intriguing and I wouldn’t mind returning to it.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: Some years ago, I fell in love with FAR: Lone sails. I was so pleased to know about this second release. I would strongly suggest to play it first.Can I call this a game? Better a journey towards hope, release and happiness, facing the unknown, the challenges of a uncertain voyage. During the journey, you will face amazing, breathtaking landscapes, involved in a wonderfull and soothing ambience provided by a splendid music score, speckled with challenging episodes, where your smartness is much needed.Definitely recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: Far: Changing Tides feal just like Far: Lone Sails.it is fun and epic.The only down side, compare to the first, is that the ship upgrade feal broken and out of place. Like if the game was rush out and cut the sceen where the steam engine get lowered from the train, to the ship. There a few things like that, in game. It break the game magic.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent sequel to an excellent, bite sized game. Relaxing, melancholic, and beautiful. If you liked FAR: Lone Sails, you'll love this title as well. It also feels like there's a lot more to do on the boat as well so traveling between places is more interesting than in the first title. The first was 10/10, this is 11/10 for me.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent sequel to an excellent, bite sized game. Relaxing, melancholic, and beautiful. If you liked FAR: Lone Sails, you'll love this title as well. It also feels like there's a lot more to do on the boat as well so traveling between places is more interesting than in the first title. The first was 10/10, this is 11/10 for me.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked the first, this is a worthy upgrade. Instead of traveling by land, you will spend most of time time on and under the sea. The locations are awe inspring, the puzzles, while simple, do their part in progression. Do not expect any big challenges in this game, it's more about the journey, the post-apocalyptic environment, the music and the joy of (linear) exploration.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: Great sequel to FAR: Lone Sails - if you've played the original, then you know roughly what to expect in terms of gameplay. Except this time, instead of a land-based vehicle, you're driving a sea-based one instead. As usual, the visuals are gorgeous and the gameplay sedate and satisfying. The puzzles are just the right amount of challenge, and the conclusion rounds off the game just nicely. My only minor complaint is that there are a couple of moments of sailing through open scenery without much happening - this isn't bad in itself, but such moments could have been shortened slightly. But I stress that this is a pretty minor gripe, and it's still a good sequel overall.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game! The story is amazing, I won't give any spoiler but my review remains basically the same as the one from the previous game, Far: Lone Sails.If you enjoy ainteresting mechanics, grimy artstyle and silent main characters that can still provide great story-telling, this game is for you!I do have a nitpick when compared to the last game in the series. I understand the need for making the sequel have something more in relation to the previous entires. However I htink in this case the mechanic was a bit too difficult and grindy. There are many moving parts to making the vehicle function, and sometimes it feels like you spen more time scaveging for resources than actually advanciing though the game.That being said, I really like that we don't need to repair as much in this entry, which is what bogged down a bit of the experience of the first one.All in all, this still is a great game and a must buy to anyone that enjoys indie games!
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: Another unknown Gem that follows up FAR "Lone Sails".FAR is proof that a simple video game can be art. I really liked the atmosphere and the soundtrack. Beautiful !In order to enjoy "Changing Tides" best, one should play the previous title first.The design is polished, the game mechanics are good, the story is nice. That is to my opinion a quality product well worth even the full price.We need more little games of that caliber.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: Fyi, I haven't played FAR: Lone Sails (had no idea that this is a sequel).This game is one of those that kinda take you for a ride without any explanation and you just gotta let it flow (heh). Graphics are very cute and soft, and paired with a beautiful soundtrack, they make for a very atmospheric experience. The puzzles are fairly easy and don't slow down the journey. Really enjoyed the mechanisms of the ship, would be cool to sail  with another player.Overall I recommend this game for people who like to relax and let the journey unravel, although this game is not very replayable, so keep that in mind.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: Much better yet more tedious. If you liked the firest FAR game then you'll likely feel the same way about Changing Tides. The great art style remains, and the new vehicle makes for a much better processes and routines type of mobility. I would say that this game improves on the original in nearly every single way with exception to the padding. It's been awhile so maybe it was the same with the first, but the sailing between puzzles feels so padded and drawn out, that a very large chunk of this alrealy short game is spent holding a lever while you sail while you move from left to right. It's been awhile since I played the first, but with this one I often found myself looking for other things to do IRL just to bide the time on the sea.  It's not overwhelming but once again it does make you thankul for this series' rather short playtime. Still highly recommend, especially if you were a fan on Lone Sails.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: Very chill exploration/resource management game. I wouldn't really categorize this game as a platformer since most of the game your in water but there's the occasional platforming. Charming art style and story! It's possible to get soft locked at around the half way point, but the checkpoints are frequent enough to where it's not too big of an issue and if you make sure to hoard every bit of fuel you should be fine. All in all a great game that should take around 6hrs if you take it slow. TLDR: Great game and story, fun to sail around and explore! Make sure to hoard the fuel hahaPS: This is a sequel so be sure to check out the first game! I did not know till half way through so i'll definitely be playing it!
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: I can't quiet put my finger on why, but this game didn't catch the same magic as the first. It just didn't have the same sense of wonder and adventure as the first. There were so neat settings, but I didn't feel like I got as much story as the first one. If you really enjoyed the first one, I'd recommend grabbing this one while it's on sale, but otherwise, I wouldn't recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: A nice 6 hour long experience / exploration / puzzle game that kept me awake for longer than was probably wise during a work week. No clue what the background story was about. Your only motivation is to keep on sailing further to the right either by sail or by steam engine, clear obstacles, open gates, find fuel, avoid storms, navigate tunnels and always curious what's going to come up next.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: A very nice sequel to FAR: Lone Sails.  Awesome:* New unique options for the vehicle, and driving feels much more engaging than the first game.* Visual style is wonderful.* Puzzles are diverse and satisfying, if a bit far between.Less Awesome:* The visual storytelling is weaker than in Lone Sails, and the overall story feels more empty.* It's possible to get stranded if you miss too many item caches.* Difficult to gauge the depth of items in the background, causing the sails to be damaged often.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic sequel to the original. The game is more ambitious in its scope and mechanics. From the new abilities that your craft has, to the new environments you can traverse, Changing Tides takes everything that was great about the first game and cranks it up a few notches.It also plays well on the Steam Deck, so this would be a great title to have installed when you're travelling.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: Put simply, this is a visual novel with some interactive puzzles.  If you like that sort of thing, this will scratch that itch.  Like many other reviewers, I agree that the average consumer would best buy this on a sale.  For those who liked Far: Lone Sails and want to support the Dev, buy it any time.It's a direct sequel to the Far: Lone Sails game and has a very familiar feel and style, albeit a longer game than their first.  If you haven't tried it please do.  Be prepared for a quite lonely feeling throughout and after as this is a recurring theme.All in all, expect about 6 hours of game play (nope, I did not finish) and enjoy a melancholy story with simple puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: This is a must play game if you enjoyed playing Inside/Limbo/Little Nightmare type games, but this game in my opinion emphasizes more on art and music. Very rarely does a game let you just take a break from the intensity where you as the player can get the chance to just sit and take in the beautiful environment and music as your vehicle pushes forward.This game is a MUST have if you appreciate left to right indie games, or if you really appreciate art.I have seen a few people say that it is repetitive with the whole fueling system but I think that by adding the moments where you are forced to stop and solve a puzzle outside of your vehicle helps keeps things fresh, plus I enjoyed fueling system where you have to be proactive in keeping your ship running.This game gives you a great sense of closure since it reveals more to what happened in the world of FAR, and the ending is perfect and brings it full circle. STRONGLY recommends if you enjoyed the previous game. PROS:- Very Beautiful game along with a great sound track that compliments atmosphere of the game.- Peaceful game some might even call it therapy- Bits and pieces of story to keep things interesting- A great game to experienceCONS:- short game (4 hours or so but I think it is a perfect length for the gameplay)- Some people might find it boringConclusion: I strongly recommend if you want a laid back experience as you take in and appreciate all of the art that it provides, and at the price at it is I say it is worth it. You have everything to gain and nothing to lose.10/10 (what else can you ask for in a game like this)
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: Hands down an amazing story. Its not easy to convey the life of a character with no dialogue, but Okomotive did a great job between both games and with a perfect end to both. I was worried Covid may have ended any future games, but you all pushed this game through and got it out there. Im sure there was more setbacks you all had to deal with then players realized so thank you.Looking forward to any more stories you guys create-
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: One of the first game I reviewed here was FAR: Lone Sails, and in that review I say that I was waiting for this game to come out.Well it did.It was amazing, they improved the graphics, the game mechanics and it al just works fine.It is challenging yet not too hard, they added another dimension (not only is a bit more 3d yet still on a 2d side platformer type), you can also go underwater at some point.It is just a great game, but for some reason even though there was a TWIST at the end, there was something that I felt in the first one that here is missing, I can't put my finger on it.The only real problem I could see is that it was too short, not because I love long ass games, but just because, as with the first one, I never wanted the journey to end.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: When I first bought this game I didn't think it would live up to the expectations of the original. I was wrong.This game is incredible in all the same ways as FAR: Lone sails. The soundtrack is golden, the art-style is gorgeous, and the game-play is fun. The game never really tells you what the story is, you have to figure it out from the environment. The game doesn't take very long to finish, though I personally felt I got my moneys worth. All and all, I wholeheartedly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful game, I enjoyed every single minute playing it, and it really does complete the joy of the first title "Far: Lone Sails" they are perfectly fit together, I had to go buy this one the next day after I completed "Far: Lone Sails", I just couldn't resist, the game is magical, and I really recommend this to anyone who played the first game, it's a 100% must have!
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: A more ambitious version of the first game. I don't see why you wouldn't play this if you enjoyed the first one. You should start with the first game, though.This game really reminded me of Inside. And in some ways I feel like it surpasses that. It plays with verticality and scale in ways that I haven't seen any other platformer do.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: A great experience, around 3-4 hours of gameplay, though mileage may vary. This is one of the few games that I knew I needed to buy as soon as I saw it. It didn't disappoint, from music, to art, to gameplay. Puzzles that are interesting but wonderfully intuitive. Managing a ship may not be easy, but it's worth it. Though I would recommend playing Lone Sails before Changing Tides, as this IS a sequel. All that being said, a solid 9/10, better than AAA titles.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: FAR: Changing Tides inherits from its predecessor while making further improvements. The shining points about the initial game were entirely carried over - Great soundtrack, plot, artstyle and atmosphere. At the same time, there are more variety and tools at your disposal and you'll have more things to worry about. I must add that the difficulties of the puzzles have also increased significantly in my opinion. It is not unusual for me to spend more than half an hour solving a single puzzle, while my playthrough of the initial game only took three hours in total. This is due to the variety of tools you have on your boat - There is little hints as of which tool you will need to use in order to solve the puzzle.Overall, I would highly recommend this game to anyone who has played the first game, or is down for some puzzle solving + atmosphere enjoying. Finally, I'd like to say that the ending embodies a big surprise yet it is very heart-warming. It makes me feels that all the time I spent on the puzzles with worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: It was a tough call not to recommend but I cannot see myself enjoying a replay.  The game looks great and is novel at times. There were a few glitches around scenery, ladders were particularly awkward, and for some reason the way a hatch opens gets reversed halfway through the game.  The puzzles were not at all intuitive and no explanation why doors close behind you other than to make it feel overly linear.  Last thought is that it needed more interaction with the game world, more to explore/find and a touch more story.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: I've been on Steam for quite some time - not once did I feel that I needed to leave a review. Until now. This game (and its predecessor) is one of the most beautiful gaming experiences I've had. The visual art and the general game direction are incredible. The ending was one of the best video game endings I've seen. A big thank you to the developers for creating this masterpiece. It may not be for everyone, but it certainly gets a 10/10 from me.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: What a great escape! like Limbo, in that you are a solitary figure interacting with environment and machinery to advance progress and work through puzzles, but unlike Limbo, you aren't perpetually dying and under attack by monsters. You can't die in the game, though falling great distances will stun you for awhile. The landscape is stark and grimly beautiful in a sepia-toned, post-apocalyptic way. Nice mechanical puzzles. Wonderful experience managing the ship in all it's myriad variations. Music was spare but enhanced the soundscape, which was dominated by wind and water sounds, for a rather soothing effect. I lost myself for a weekend immersed in this.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: As sequel to Far: Lone sails, Far: changing tides accomplishes its job by simply proposing the same gameplay of its predecessor. Perhaps not the boldest move but, nonetheless, the game provides a few hours of chill, relaxing puzzle game while navigating the remains of a ruined and yet beautiful world, just with a little of bit platforming.So, yes. A nice game, definitely worth to buy it if you enjoy after you played Far: Lone sails.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: Just as good as the first game, with a few new things going on such as going under water. Very relaxing game and less ship management in this one than the first game (IMO). Only complaint would be that there seem to be a number of times where nothing happens and you just move along at quite a slow pace. It's nice for a while, but can get a little bit boring. Other than that, a great game overall.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: A delightful almost-one-of-a-kind game, that expands upon the original (FAR:Lone Sail) by offering new mechanics, a new vehicle and a new environment (swapping sun-blasted desert for oceans). It's a considerably longer game than the original, and offers a little more in the way of complexity. It doesn't feel -quite- as polished (there were one or two clipping issues and/or a bit of background missing at one point), but this doesn't in any way detract from the experience. Can thoroughly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: This is a beautiful game, the art and music are wonderful. I feel like I'm missing out on something if I don't go and explore the world the developers created since they put so much time and thought into it. The puzzles are not very difficult, but provide an interesting interlude between the periods of travel aboard your ship.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: Improves on the already-excellent original. A puzzle game in which you play a small person navigating a water vehicle through a post-civilization seascape, overcoming obstacles and exploring.Fun to play with small children - although there is at some point a dessicated corpse of a failed explorer that you might have to explain. Not scary, not gory. Just, there. Still, recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: Impressive sequel, cannot believe they were able to make a more compelling and immersive game than the first game, Far: Lone Sails.One thing is certain, if you have Lone Sails, you must absolutely get Changing Tides. And if you get Changing Tides, you must get Lone Sails. The 2 games compliment and answer so many questions together.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: This is a nice game. It's not too long, has a relaxing soundtrack, the gameplay mechanics are pretty straight forward, and the artistic presentation is engaging. _childDocuments_.review: It always amazes me how human nature is so attuned to sociality that, with just an ounce of isolation, it will latch onto the first thing with characterization, even if it's inanimate. Okomotive creates that perfect feeling in this game. Your vehicle is reminiscent of Wilson from Castaway or the Companion Cube from Portal The game is somber and lonely and you micromanaging the ship both fills the world with something to do to distract from the endless wasteland and ruined civilization, and creates a symbiotic relationship between you two. That relationship is one of mutualism, where the ship transports and protects you while you maintain and guide it.I watched someone play Far: Lone Sails and loved the story so much I decided to pick up this one without spoiling anything and honestly I'm glad I did. I would highly recommend anyone to try this unique experience out. The game is a short and concise story (it took me less than 6 hours, though I know some do it in less) because the developers know what story they want to tell. That story is fascination. There's this momentum throughout the game, a steady movement right, forward in both distance in time. You don't have a destination, you just know you have to . I may be looking too much into it (I'm an artist, I can't not overanalyze) but it's very evocative of the human experience. We live in a state of loneliness with a final destination we cannot see. All we can do is build the relationships we can and just keep moving, hoping to arrive at a better place.However, I do have to say the game is not perfect. There are three main issues. Firstly, and least important, I felt like this game had far less worldbuilding than the first. Maybe it's because I just missed it. There are fascinating paintings and art I saw and this creates interesting questions, but the previous game had more literal information one could gleam about the history of the machines. I'll probably pick this game up for another playthough and try to see if I can interpret more next time. Second, the controls. the main buttons are wsad, e, c, v, and space. These are all used by the left hand so i often felt imbalanced while playing, like I wanted to do something with my right as well. When I only used my left hand I felt it difficult to maneuver in more complex situations. You also can't change the controls (which I heard they're planning to change, so that may be outdated by the time you read this). I found it more comfortable to use the arrow keys or numpad, which both also work as alternates. Third, and personally the most frustrating for me, is the camera. I felt like the camera was often in this awkward state of not close enough or too far. I have bad eyesight so the zoom-in option was actually pretty handy for seeing what I was doing. However, it wasn't toggleable so I would have to hold it down while trying to manipulate movement and interaction (this is one of those complex situations that is impossible to do with wsad. The zoom out is similar, not toggleable, but, in my opinion, even more useless. You barely zoom out larger than when you get on the top of the ship or when you (spoiler for one of the upgrades you get) . I actually found myself scrambling to avoid destroying my sail (and usually failing) because I couldn't see what was coming ahead. I found the best angle was on top of the ship, standing on the stern (absolutely beautiful angle) but I couldn't be there long because of the micromanaging. I just wish the zoom out feature would zoom further out or maybe rotate just a smidge to the right so you could see briefly up ahead.There are a few other minor things, some bugs and some confusing bits, but don't let my criticism dissuade you from getting this game. Those issues don't get in the way of the fantastic experience the game presents. I just hope those are some things the developers think of for a (hopeful) third installment.

_childDocuments_.review: FAR: Changing Tides, a casual puzzle platformer developed by Okomotive, is the sequel to the popular FAR: Lone Sails. Set in the same world, you play a child on a sea journey whose purpose gradually reveals itself.Most of the game’s controls and puzzles are straightforward and deducible by trial and error. Buttons or actionable items have a distinctive cyan colour and, later in the game, yellow lights direct the player’s focus. While movement feels unrestricted, most areas present only a few actual options to the player. Getting stuck is usually caused by insufficient exploration or wrong assumptions. “Breaking” a puzzle or losing required items is impossible.The puzzles’ goals are usually progression, usually travelling from left to right. However, sometimes solving puzzles improves your ship, such as adding an engine or a new mode of transport. Sometimes they hint more about the world, such as revealing a diorama or a painting.The game is short, containing about five to six hours of playtime. While that may dissuade some from its undiscounted price, the design of FAR: Changing Tides is economical and efficient. Mechanics are introduced, practised then the game moves on without overdoing them. Lengthening the game would not necessarily have made it better.As with the previous game, FAR: Changing Tides separates puzzle areas with long stretches of travel. Your ship’s controls are puzzles themselves, like tacking the sails against the wind or powering the engine. Once the controls are mastered, these travel stretches give you short breaks, temporarily immersing yourself in the world via the backgrounds and soundtrack. FAR: Changing Tides tells its story by implication and subtle reference. The flooded world drowned humanity’s cities and towns, but the strewn detritus shows the flood’s ferocity and suddenness. The unnamed protagonist encounters no living humans, only hints of their existence.FAR: Changing Tides continues the retrofuturistic “dieselpunk” feel of FAR: Lone Sails, putting 1930s through 50s aesthetics on advanced technology. Desaturated colours and dull, rendered plaster buildings are typical of that era and make the world feel bleak. The rusting carcasses of humanity’s leviathan mechanical creations dot the landscape. Some are almost organic, and you can hear a faint heartbeat when nearby.This desolation contrasts with the game’s naturalistic moments. Nature continues. The deer, birds and sea life are oblivious to your and humanity’s struggles. Glimpses of bioluminescent jellyfish or rays through your ship’s glass bottom or distant whales are wondrous moments.FAR: Changing Tides, as implied, is about the younger generation reacting to contemporary issues like climate change. The protagonist is a child, forced to undertake a journey to build a better life. He or she finds toys like wooden stags, music boxes and stuffed ducks but cannot play with them, forced to grow up early to confront older generations’ hubris.The protagonist demonstrates how the newer generation views the world. He or she does not blame technology – it is unclear in FAR: Changing Tides what caused the flood. Technology is something the new generation masters early and is vital to survival. The ship even looks like one a child might draw. The ending shows the new generation’s focus on each other and subversively ties it back to FAR: Lone Sails.However, FAR: Changing Tides could have appealed to our senses more. While the game’s engine has moved from predominantly 2D to wholely 3D – and shows it off at the end – most of the extensive backgrounds are simple and blandly textured. The developers are going for a stylized, cheap-to-develop aesthetic. However, desaturated does not mean uninteresting. The soundtrack adds emotion and context to otherwise empty moments but lacks memorable motifs or consistency.  The casual puzzle platform genre also has limits. Its puzzles are too simple for someone wanting a challenge. The storytelling is too subtle for those looking for clear themes. Experienced gamers enjoy these short diversions but the gaming landscape continues to expand and diversify beyond puzzle platformers.That said, FAR: Changing Tides is a worthy successor to FAR: Lone Sails, developing its novel vehicle operation mechanic enough to feel different but still comfortable. Those looking for a casual but not overly taxing game will enjoy it, especially if you fondly remember FAR: Lone Sails.

_childDocuments_.review: As a strong lover of the previous title, this sequel actually disappointed me. The gameplay felt quite cheap in many areas. Often times, in climactic situations, there was no music accompaniment, and I could not translate what emotion I was supposed to receive. There was less of a story intention in this title than the previous, it seems. I was also very confused with some elements, and the world felt too bland and open at times. In fact, most of the game felt quite bland.But the ending was unexpected, it certainly brought it home (no pun intended). And I do have to applaud Joel's music work once again. Beautiful, as always.I still wouldn't recommend this unfortunately. I felt too downplayed during this, and favored the previous title over this.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely breathtaking. The developers, yet again, outdid my expectations.  More of the same, with more of the good stuff. More streamlined vehicle management, fun new mechanics, and another awesome world to discover. Who knew how much story silence can tell. And how profound a shift in perspective can really  be.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: First of all - I like it! For the price I paid (it was on sale) I'm OK with the value for money. But at the same time I'm a bit disappointed. Lone Sails (the previous FAR game) simply was a better game. The difference is not huge, but in almost every aspect it's lacking that little extra that made Lone Sails so very special.The music is the most obvious difference for me, in Lone Sails it's a major part of the experience, in Changing Tides it's just music. Not at all bad, far from it, just not very special. Maybe it's just me, but I struggled all the time with controlling the vehicle. Missed jumps, pressing buttons by mistake and some things are too close to each others (when using the E key). For example cooling the engine was constantly a struggle because of the speed lever in the same place where you stand when sprinkling water. Extremely frustrating when in hurry between the places. Can't remember having such issues with Lone Sails.If you are considering this game, I would recommend you to try FAR: Lone Sails first.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: For games like it I can recommend Firewatch.The game itself is mostly a setpiece for the atmosphere which encompasses the world made by the developers at Okomotive. If you are ready for a contemplative journey from start till the end, remember to play the first one starting out, as the two stories are linked. Gameplay doesn't get repetitive over the 2-3 hours of gameplay, and while short i believe that games that are this expressive needs to be played through.The price is never easy to deal with, and as such i would recommend getting it when it drops under a 10-15 eur if you want your money's worth.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game, it's amazing, the atmosphere is great, the art style is so beautiful, the gameplay is magnificent, and the game is so relaxing that I can sleep easily if I leave the game still and lie on the side of the screen, and the story of the game is worthy of a movie, it is so exciting, i can't praise this game enough, thank you so much for making a second part of such a masterpiece, and if you make a third masterpiece, i WILL play it ^^
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: The only reason I got this game was due to a coupon from one of the badges and I have to say, it is gorgeous. The gameplay is nothing to complicated and you unfortunately do not get a back story. However this game ties in to the first one, wonderfully. The puzzles are not to complex and don't require to much thinking. Replayability wise, I probably will not play it again after just having finished it. The soundtrack is amazing and the artwork is great. Overall, if you like a game with some puzzles, relaxing and low-key, definitely pick up a copy if it is on sale!
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked Lone: Far Sails, you will love this game. It's eye candy all the way through with plenty to do and see on top of that. The boat is fun to maneuver and maintain, the environments are gorgeous, and the music is absolutely fantastic. I only regret that I can't keep playing it, but that isn't a bad thing in the slightest. A game this short but this engaging is a breath of fresh air.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: Bought and finished Far: Changing Tides today 4/5/2022I usually like games where the story is told through the environment and this was no exception. Short of a little bit of movement jank (the character has sharp controls but the jump is floaty up and quick down) I enjoyed my 6 hours with it and I think it makes a story of a planet in disaster well when melded with the story of the first game.Overall 7/10 would recommend to fans of the genre
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: The trouble with this sequel is the level of morbidity-factor. Who dropped you here? How many survivors are there? If you didn't drop accidentally, how far from a rebuilding civilisation have you come and why? The ending is a good compromise between what sort of civil functionality remains and what doesn't. However whereas the last game was in a wide open space encumbered by a hermit who you play, as related to a designer of the machines that used to travel the now dry vast open plains. In this game you begin as someone who has been 'dropped' into the opposite situation of a now waterlogged civilisation. Where you can tell many people may have died in this game the compensation of a more 'crazy' character tends to lead to the conclusion that there is some sort of characteristic and sinister hierarchy at play. It, it, it, it is not "supreme" in my opinion, must I add this for sanity's sake?!
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most amazing game you'll ever see. It takes you by the guts and tells you a story that will haunt you (in a good way). I can't even count the number of times when I was just too stuned, too amazed to think, to speak. If you're looking for some adventure, an escape for your normal life - this game is made for you. I dont think I can describe how good is this game ! Play it and play it again as you'll aways see, discover something new in it !A really good second game of the licence, Thank you for this amazing experience.My only bad comment is that commands are not ajustable (I had to change my azerty keyboard for the qwerty and the use of arrows isn't possible) and kind of quirky ? But the game isn't really strict and punitive. So it's okay !
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: So much to do and in such a great time span I think I may just be in heaven. The serenity the FAR series has given me is unrivaled to any other indie game and I would really hope to see a continuation of the series, realistic or not. Spoiler Alert: You should make a Final game in the series and make it Co-Op with both elements of travel combined, land and sea, with the two characters set out to find the answer to the apocalyptic problems.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing sequel that builds on much of what made the original great. The gameplay is fun and engaging like the first, with more to do and manage on your vehicle. All the different environments added a lot of beautiful variety as well. Like the first, I was engaged with the character and progress of the story, even though there is no dialogue/text really. The worldbuilding is incredible and the way they finished up the story was amazing as well.I would definitely recommend you play Far: Lone Sails before this one.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: Great little side-scrolling adventure with small puzzles to solve.  The art and music in this game is great and this is a big win for an indie studio.  The ship and scavenging to keep moving forward is a great concept that would port over well to AA and AAA games.  Would recommend this as a good and relaxed play through for anyone needing to de-stress.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed the first part and when I heard there was ganna be a DLC I was super excited. I finally got to play the game and all I can say is I am blown away. I would give this game a 10/10. I loved every moment from the art and scenery to the sound track and game play. I was lost for words and ecstatic when I came to the ending and my mind was blown. To the developers and team that made this game are one of a kind and really pulled this off. I really hope there will be a third instalment as you guys really know how to make a game and expand upon it and really make it something special. I am so grateful for the piece of art you have created and would support you in any other games you make.All in all, well done.Chiefs kiss
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game! I decided to purchase this game after watching someone play the first game FAR: Lone Sails. I wanted to give this one a try since I enjoyed watching the game-play of the first one. I'm really glad I did! The art style  and environment was absolutely stunning. Don't get me started on the soundtrack too. UGH! So good. Well done Okomotive! The puzzles were challenging but not super hard that it took away from the game, so that was nice. A lot of the times it was just me being stupid haha. The mechanics were also cool, so not many complains there. In addition, there were also times when I found myself saying, "WOAH." I repeat, great game. However, I highly suggest playing FAR: Lone Sails before this one if you haven't already. Story-wise and because it's also amazing. It's not imperative, but I still suggest it. FAR: Changing Tides is a great game if you want to sit back and chill while still feeling involved in the game. I will definitely be playing this game multiple times. Happy playing!
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: W O W!Great experience , no, a FASCINATING one - I loved the first one but this just took it to another level , then again and then at least one more time. It is a marvelous composition of detail and love. From every note in the music, to every bleak detail in the background. _childDocuments_.review: great game 10 outa ten the gameplay is great ship looks great i only wish there was a freeplay mode ya know like just traveling maybe random puzzles thrown in the games just so peaceful it needs one ya know mainly cuz i feel the game just goes so quick then i gotta do it over im on my second playthrough right now ya know i dont mind doing it over but just something to think about oh and if ya make a new one how about scrap collection and upgrading whatever vehicle you get ya know like a storage area where ya put the fuel in a box and when you press the button a hook slides out into the engine or ya know just a suggestion but like i said the game play was beautiful.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: A game that uses just the WASD keys, the E key, and the space bar seems somewhat simple, but this game, the second one in the series, is great fun.   There are no space lasers, or having to avoid squid men or anything else, it is just you sailing.  This is a game, parents can easily get for their kids and let them have fun with at their leisure.  The game took me about six hours to complete, but it was great fun.  I look forward to another one in the series.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: After completing this game in less than 6 hours, I can gladly recommend this game to everyone who likes athospheric/slow-paced games. This gem is a sister game of FAR: Lone Sails where you control (in both games) a vehicle while moving through a really nice world around you. By the way, I recommend playing FAR: Lone Sails first... (no spoilers!). I'm giving this an 8/10, and that's because on some occasions, it felt a little bit boring as you raise your sail and just watch your vehicle for a few minutes, but other than that, it was a super cool experience.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: My Score: 8/10Very lovely once again. Same mechanics for the most part, but I really enjoyed the sea-going affair, especially the storms! Just sailing and listening to the soundtrack was quite peaceful. Only glitched out once, but the auto save worked to reset not too far back. I think I actually enjoyed the graphics in Lone Sails a bit better, but it's been a while since I played that one. The only slightly annoying aspect was the amount of ladders and doors on the ship. Sometimes, I would jump across the hole in the floor and inadvertently grab a ladder when time was of the essence, but I learned to adjust. Overall, a very nice peaceful adventure!
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: I could not pull myself away until I reach the end.If I were to say there is a con, maybe a tad too much busy work to do while traveling, and didn't care for repairs being an expendable resource, but it wasn't so bad it hindered the game play. So, are they brother and sister, did I understand that correctly. Anyhow, I am curious now, where will they go now, what appears to be the last two people in that world. I guess "Far Stormy skies" will be the next logical move.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: While FAR: Lone Sails was never really my cup of tea, I did find myself oddly entertained by FAR: Changing Tides even though they are both, essentially, the same game. This change in heart is due, in no small part, to the change in visuals that created a world I wanted to look at and spend time within. However, it's still a "Far" title, and unless you can find peace and relaxation in having to constantly micromanage a ship that's falling apart, on fire or simply refusing to move, then maybe this isn't the game for you.PROS:	It looks really, really pretty	For the most part, the gameplay is pretty smooth, and the puzzle solutions are intuitiveCONS:	Micromanaging can very quickly become a chore	The puzzle sections often felt intrusive and brash instead of like a natural progressionRead my full review here:
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: Once again, Okomotive delivers a pretty and relaxing, almost meditative game. Changing Tides is an easy recommend for fans of Far: Lone Sails, but no-one else.When compared to its older sibling, this one is simply not as good, almost disappointingly so. There are some improvements in gameplay, player freedom and even length of the game. But at the same time, atmosphere, puzzle quality and overall enjoyment take a significant hit. One only needs to compare promo-screenshots from the Steam store page, those draw a very clear picture.In summary: Only play this if you love Lone Sails to pieces (like me). I can't recommend it to anyone else.

_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: Short and peaceful single player game. If you're into puzzles and maintenance mechanics, this game is perfect for you. There were a few bugs like the crank for the hook on the ship not pulling items and the water level not where its suppose to be after a certain incident. Overall, game is just beautiful to look at, the music is slow and peaceful and there isnt much of a story involved that will confuse you.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: I thought the first game, FAR: Lone Sails, was a great game. However I also thought that it ended a little too quickly and wasn't worth the full price. This game though improves on the first game in almost every aspect and I don't have anything bad to say about it. If you liked the first game you will probably like this as well but you can definitely enjoy this game even if you never played the first.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: In my opinion the art design the music and the overall variety of gameplay in this game is improved compared to the first one! I really loved it for the calm gameplay and atmosphere. The ship is a bit more complicated and the controls somewhat frustrating at times but after getting used to the new watering mechanic and the jump of the character it gets really fun travelling west! The music boxes are a lovely little detail :) I am excited to see upcoming games from Okomotive!
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: Up front I will say that I liked the ship controls on the original game better. It was more fluid and rhythmic. I can't count the number of times when I've added fuel when I didn't need to. Poor guy must also have a lot of bumps on his head from that stupid air lock. But other than that, the visuals and mood of this game remain top-notch. It still FEELS GOOD to play. Very uplifting. I don't remember getting as much metaphysical vibes than the first one, but in Changing Tides - that simple act of adjusting the sails to make the most of the wind drives a deep lesson home. Listen to that inner voice that tells you to keep going tirelessly. Magic can happen just when things seem like they will blow to bits. Wonderful and beautiful! I hope there's more in this series!
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed my time with FAR: Changing Times but I preferred FAR: Lone Sails. I think the previous game had more impressive visuals, better music and more impressive set pieces. Changing Tides also suffers by having the ship on auto-pilot for most of the game - hoist up the sails and just stand around as an endless, bleak scenery rolls by. For such a short game, I felt a bit cheated that most of it was spent either sitting in the ship doing nothing or running endlessly.Lone Sails had a lot more involvement as you struggled to keep the engine running while managing the other tasks. The puzzles seemed to have more variety. This new game just seems to have the same variety of pulling levers and using hooks to move obstacles. I did like the submarine capability of the new ship, but even that felt like it wasn't fully utilised in the game.6/10
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent sequel to FAR: Lone Sails. Captures the same essential feel and gameplay loop as the first game while keeping things very interesting. Almost perfectly polished too. Only bug I encountered was at the very end where I had been standing at the bow for the camera angle and the game walked me off the ship during the cinematic.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: OMG, this game is absolutely amazing, i just finished my first play through. The devs of these games are geniuses. I love it and I can't wait to see what happens next. If anyone is going to play this game I recommend you play the first game before this one, I don't want to spoil anything but lets just say things make more sence that way.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: A very endearing and whimsical adventure-puzzle game. The developers felt much more comfortable developing this as opposed to their previous title, letting it be and not rushing to let you experience all the cool stuff. Whereas previously they felt like they were trying to not overstay their welcome, this time they felt much more comfortable and competent both, being able to deliver a longer game that stayed exactly as long as it needed to.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: This is a well polished and bug free game. I played the previous FAR: Lone Sails and loved them both, not just for the sound/animation and story line but also the overall playability of your games. Compared to other games developers, okomotive games ROCK!!! and are stable and just work. I have an ultrawide screen 3840/1080 and no issues at all that I have had with other games. _childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: What a game and what a journey !8 hours to finish this game is pretty nice, I was expecting a much shorter experience even if many will take less time, there are things to do and discover. (and trying to get the achievements is also fun)The story delivers without a single word or single text whatsoever, you always know what is happening and where you are in the story.The gameplay is a succession of simple puzzles where you push buttons, levers and grab things off the ground.The game is always pretty easy but I wondered what I had to do a few times.The world is a beautiful grim dark painting, there isn't much life and even underwater is pretty dead outside of the puzzles, I wish there was a little more life down there (you see some here and there and it's always charming, I guess the emptyness of the ocean makes those encounters even more charming though)The instrumental music is slow and only plays when needed, it's beautiful if you love classical and relaxing music.Nothing to say about sound effects, they're precisely where they need to be and nothing needs to be added or removed while not exceptional either.All in all, a very good surprise, maybe a bit expensive at 20 bucks and without any replayability.If you're looking for a relaxing poetic game then this is the one !
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic little game. I will agree with some of the other reviews that it has more downtime than the first game, and not as many big memorable moments. The highs of this game were very high though, while the lows were at worst boring. It's still an awesome experience and I'm looking forward to see what they do next.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: This is one game I just can't recommend enough. It and its prequel are not full of action, next-gen graphics, good shooting sequences, rpg mechanics, fast paced racing scenes or open world gameplay.It's just you, travelling across a fascinating, melancholy waters in your ship, and your only imperative is to keep going. The only direction is forward (and depth, after a while). It has a little of FTL about it, in that you need to do a bit more than one person can comfortably handle to keep your vehicle going.It's a game defined as much by what it isn't as what it is. It's a contemplative, melancholy journey through a desolate landscape of oceans and hulking ruins, and it was a wonderful experience for me. I hope it will be the same for you. This game was roughly twice as long as the first game in the series, Lone Sails.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: Far: Changing Tides is an excellent sequel to Lone Sails with pleasing painted visuals and the vehicle-centric puzzles of its predecessor, but with more water than ever before. To avoid spoiling the experience, new mechanics and changed mechanics from Lone Sails, all I will say is this.I enjoyed it enough to play for longer than intended and finished in nearly a single sitting (barring letting the dogs out to "snowbathe" in the backyard) and to give it a review which I rarely do.The last thing I will say is that it provides a satisfying resolution and tie in with Lone Sails' ending. And I look forward to seeing if there is a sequel to Changing Tides, a prequel to Lone Sails or another storyline entirely that takes place in the same setting, assuming it isn't ending at a duology.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: A game that is equally as good as the sequel. Although there are some gripes I have with it, such as the fact that that it feels like there is too much "gameplay"One of the biggest complaints about the first game was the lack of gameplay, outside of maintaining the Okomotive and solving puzzles to progress, there were moments where the wind picked up and you could raise the sails and not have to worry about maintaining the Okomotive, it was here that the game truly shined. It would take the reins and let you experience its wondrous art-style and beautiful music, it was a truly relaxing experience. In this game however, while there are moments to raise the sail, you don't get a chance to relax and experience the scenery. Instead I found myself paying less attention to the scenery and instead more attention to the flagpole to make sure I was getting the maximum speed. I also feel like there were too many choices of moving forward. In the first game it would force you to use the Okomotive's engine, but also give you the choice to use the sail. In here, you're gonna be using the sail the majority of the time. I would've preferred it if I was forced to rely on the engine more often then the sail.Aside from that, this was a truly amazing sequel to a beloved game. I desperatly hope to see more from this studio and perhaps more from the FAR universe.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: FAR: Changing Tides does what it set out to do; it acts as a proper sequel to the first installment. If you loved FAR: Lone Sails, you're bound to enjoy this one. That statement is both a blessing and a curse as the game will feel very familiar, but never really expand on what it started years ago. You'll travel through a new environment, on a new steam-powered engine and solve some new puzzles. The only real deviation comes in the form of the new lore introduced. Beyond that, its much the same experience. I felt a bit disappointed when I noticed I could predict what was going to happen next, by simply recalling what happened in the first game. This made FAR: Changing Tides feel more like an alternate version of the original game, instead of something completely new. As a fan of the FAR world and its lore, I truly hope the next title expands on these ideas. Games that follow the same path as all of their predecessors, will inevitably grow stale. The world of FAR has a lot of potential and deserves the time and energy needed to grow.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a fantastic follow-up to what is easily one of my favorite indie games I have played. The soundtrack is just as amazing as the first and the art style has seen some nice touch-ups. The gameplay is much more relaxed in this game though there are some tense moments as well. While I might need a few playthroughs to really understand the full story, you should definitely play the first game before this one to get a more fulfilling experience. Barring some minor technical issues this game is an amazing sequel that deserves your time.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: An overall worthy successor to the first game. My sentiments mostly echo what has already been written and I feel the pros surely outweighs the cons. If I am to complain about something it is this; In the first game you had an upgrade which automatically picked up the fuel from the ground - an upgrade I still remember being super happy about. In this game there is no such thing so you have to pick up the fuel up one by one which is a bummer. BUT the option is there to use sails so  stop and pick up everything. Altough you will need the engine from time to time.  The game is beautiful and perfect for a casual gamer as myself. Nice and easy "puzzles". Really hoping they will do a third.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: FAR: Changing Tides is the sequel to FAR: Lone Sails and both games are excellent. Both games give you basic platformer controls, but you use them to operate various devices and mechanisms inside of a complex steampunk type vehicle. You can use the sail to propel the vehicle forward with wind (if wind is available) or use combustion to propel the vehicle forward with combustion (if there is fuel). You mainly just need to keep your vehicle moving, traveling ever onward across a forsaken land, toward destiny. Various challenges and hazards will present obstacles along the way. You can run out of wind, run out of fuel, have your path obstructed by large structures and debris, requiring you to do some on-foot puzzle solving to get your vehicle through or around. Storms will assail your vehicle and damage your sail and engine with lightning strikes. But in the moments where your ship is in great shape, the wind is blowing, and you're sailing calmly, the games are also incredibly peaceful.The games can be beaten in 4 to 10ish hours depending on how leisurely you take the journey, but it's honestly the perfectly length. You have a great adventure, but the games don't overstay their welcome or drag things out with a lot of repetition or filler.I would recommend picking up both! Very original and fun little games. I'll buy a third if they make it. No question.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: The experience was good but a little underwhelming. My biggest worry would be that they would add too many mechanics, and they did. The sail that made the first game so enjoyable, allowing for a little break with amazing music and visuals has been changed to make you do a very tedious mechanic that got really boring and frustrating after a while, these sections of open ocean had nothing visual to give most the time which ended up being the same. Yes your on a boat but the first game had so much variety in areas, things felt realistic in the world and in its setting, going through abandoned buildings, towns, factories. This games world felt a little confusing, opting for some pretty science fiction areas that felt pretty different from the rest of the world. I wish in the more underwater sections it would take us into more urban areas like a flooded city (which it had at the start of the game but never came back)Overall it was just okay and the ending was really worth it, but it didn't give me the same emotions or feelings as the first game.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: This is a beautiful and meditative game like the original Far: Lone Sails.  The puzzles are pretty simple with no way to fail them so just keep pushing buttons.  I liked the game but it wasn't as good as the original.  In the original there were long stretches of travel just listening to the beautiful music.  This one has music but there were also long stretches of travel with silence.  The additional mechanics of working the ship were a bit clunky but workable.  Overall I enjoyed the game.
_childDocuments_.name: FAR: Changing Tides

_childDocuments_.review: While FAR: Changing Tides didn't manage to further the intrigue the first installment produced, it managed to show exactly the world you'd expect after playing the first one. A solid follow up with an ever beautiful backdrop, fitting melancholic music and ever evolving ways to propel yourself to the right of your screen.
