_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game. Had it on my wishlist waiting for normal release, but it's just not good at all. First, it's incredibly annoying that as a caster, I'm totally gimped out the gate since I never got an offensive spell in the time I did play. The music is very repetitive and droll. It makes me want to fall asleep. The aesthetic of the world is unique at first but quickly becomes cumbersome and extremely confusing as everywhere you look is exactly the same. This isn't helped at all by not being given a map or compass. You can eventually buy a compass, but no map for quite some time.The UI is horribly designed for controller, which is what I played on. God forbid you try to navigate the controls menu with a controller... That is a nightmare. The inventory menu is sooo clunky and offers no consistent information to infer how to navigate it, meaning I was frequently swapping sub-tabs instead of main tabs or vice versa. Doing any kind of skill check was just a simple dice roll. That's just plain lazy. Also, not all locked doors can be opened with lockpicking, which makes ZERO sense. You can't kill any NPCs. If you want to be TES, you totally missed the mark on that. The leveling system is based on collectibles instead of using your skills, which is another big miss. This just forces you to explore instead of allowing you to explore naturally. This developer has no clue what made Elder Scrolls special.The introductory experience just didn't give me enough to trust that this game will grow into anything I will enjoy. It all feels a bit amateurish. I would wait for Tainted Grail's Skyrim-esque game to come out.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best game I've played all year, definitely the most invested I've been in an RPG since at least Baldur's Gate 3. Maybe further back. The world is really unique, each area feels distinct and interesting with its own problems. The missing child quest in the Clockwork Kingdom had me tearing up. _childDocuments_.review: I want to recommend this game but it's just too boring. The creators made a very interesting world and story but the gameplay is bad:-Combat is basically just hold left click for a power attack-Puzzles are: find the levers and be smart enough to flick them, roll a 6 sided die to lockpick a door, be strong enough to break the door, or be cool enough to convince somebody to open the door for you-Back track a bunch to farm resources to upgrade buildings-The rest of the game is running around and reading text boxesTalking to npcs is also pretty bad for a story driven game because they often don't react/have new things to say about changes in the world. _childDocuments_.review: I've had a honeymoon with this game, spending the first ten hours in complete ecstasy, what do you know I really like running around giant mushrooms. But soon the game's shortcomings started to get increasingly obvious, however never enough to put me off or make the whole deal unpleasant. So here is a modest review of this nice package.- Art direction is phenomenal. From NPCs clothing to the color of the sky, from the modest farm to the weirdest monster, everything is fresh and well thought, dodging every fantasy or SF trope to give life to a one-of-kind world. Whether you like the retro 3D style is a matter of personal taste but it does the job and delivers, bringing long lines of sight where mysteriously shaped landmarks loom in the distance. Quite beautiful all things considered.- Game systems are well thought of. All four of the stats are useful (even Might I regretted using as a dump stat) and have several purposes. The UI is slick and pleasant to use, magic is fun and has many wildly different spells, all useful. Shame you won't find most until mid to late game. The game is very much streamlined and keeps the same mechanisms until the end (more on that later), but sane design decisions allow difficulty to scale, the many items to stay relevant and the overall experience to be fun until the end.- There are many small but nice attentions, such as housing you can purchase and upgrade, giving you boons, or the NPCs having schedules or moving around the map.- Writing is good, though inconsistent. While the NPCs sometimes are quirky and talking with them vary between very fun and overdone, the whole lore is fresh and interesting and brings uncommon takes to the usual themes of Gods, death, science and the like. Many quests have several possible outcomes as well, and often there is no obvious good choice and the player will have to take side.- Music is ok. Each place has its own theme that loops quite fast, some of them I found nicer than others.- The map is vast, way larger than I thought at first, and is filled with various landmarks, towns, ruins, caves and secrets. Hallowshire has the most content, as the two later parts are smaller and emptier overall, although Ferropolis town is sprawling and makes up for the remaining of the land. The problem is that all this huge content will abide by the same limited interactions : finding ways to access it, looting it, maybe fighting mobs. Difficulty scales but novelty seldom appears, there is some nice hidden switch-hunting but after some times it becomes obvious it is more of the same. It is the beauty and mystery of the world that made me carry on, as well as the well-written main quest. On the plus side, the variety of fast travel options you slowly unlock is very nice and show the care with which the maps have been designed, and the player time and sanity respected.- The dev team has been very reactive after game release to fix the big bugs, but some smaller ones linger on. Nothing serious however.- Combat is serviceable at best, and it's a shame considering the various weapons, items and spells you can pit against the decent rooster of enemy. Fights will be too easy for most of the playthrough before spiking by the end, and they never be overly challenging nor fun. Parrying is useless when you can run around, and while all the ingredients are here for epic fights where you can buff yourself, summon minions, and strike with critical timing, in the end you'll simply move back and forth or simply over, sometimes blasting a spell when you want some variety. Easily the game biggest issue.- As a corollary the game is overall very easy. Its only challenge is finding your way in this huge alien world, which is well-made, but there's not much more to it.This game has a commendable quality in design, direction and technical matters. For a studio first game it is frankly impressive, and from the screenshots and limited information on which I bought it I wasn't expecting such scope, and, to be honest, such care. It is heartbreaking to see how close it comes to be an all-around marvel, as its combat system plagues it as much as its direction lifts it.This game has been compared to other video games, and while it does evoke the best qualities of some other famous RPG or FPS, in the end Dread Delusion is its own thing and should be considered as such. It is a crazy dive in an alien world, a place turned upside down but full of pragmatic and friendly characters, a realm of colours and wonders. It is for sightseeing amateurs, mushroom bunny-hoppers, fantasy philosophers, and indefatigable cartographers who value curiosity over challenge.I give it a friendly 4/5.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a decently fun retro like experience. But my complaints is that the game trys to be too retro. The game feels like it's from like 1998 in every way. I like the visual style and atmosphere, but enemies have extremely basic AI, combat is as basic as can be, and after a while the graphics start to become straining to me. The low resolution of things makes it hard to tell what I'm looking at and the lack of even a basic lighting system exacerbates that. I would've had fun with this game 15 years ago but in 2024 It's just hard to play. The game does have a lot going for it and I will recommend it only if it's on sale. $20 is a steep price for something like this, especially in this economy.Another note I want to add is lot's of people compare this game to dark souls. These people have clearly never played a dark souls game before. The gameplay has almost no similarities to dark souls. The only thing that is similar is the system for switching spells, weapons, and quick use items. So don't listen to these people.

_childDocuments_.review: Atmosphere, character designs, and story are all unlike anything I've played before. Quests feel thought-out and unique, with some offering difficult ethical choices that felt consequential to the worldbuilding.Combat isn't terribly deep, but functions well and it's possible to complete the game without fighting anything.Some minor bugs and stuttering when running quickly through zones, but nothing gamebreaking, and auto-saves are generous. I loved it for the retro-horror aesthetic alone, but the game itself is a solid, deeply written RPG about the the power and consequences of appealing to forces beyond our understanding.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Delusion

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:-Cohesive, comprehensive story-Unique Art style-Great World-building and Lore-Massive open world-Game *feels* good and responsive to play in most regards-Incredible, engaging quests and dialogue-Great music and sound designCons:-Straight up terrible combat-Not very many narrative choices-Not much gear-Exploration is kind of pointless because of a lack of unique loot-lack of skill trees and buildcraftingNeutral:-lack of landholding / convenience mechanics (no quest markers, no convenient fast travel etc.)-requires a lot of reading-Lock-picking is barred entirely behind RNG-Not many NPC's located in the open worldOverall a solid RPG. There's quite a few con's but really they're mostly just minor nitpicks that don't warrant a negative review of the game. If you can look past them, the world is amazing to explore, the story is captivating, and the art style alone makes it one of the most unique games I've experienced in a while. _childDocuments_.name: Dread Delusion

_childDocuments_.review: A streamlined and distilled vial of concentrated retro-rpg goodness. Don't take the word streamlined as a bad thing though, I haven't been this engaged by a game in a VERY long time. This little gem made me feel things that I thought I wouldn't be able to experience anymore, an addicting sense of childlike wonder and discovery from figuring out everything that this game has to offer by just wandering around and messing with stuff and exploring. The aesthetic is immaculate (though it strikes me as very 40k influenced that's no bad thing- and it's still VERY much doing it's own thing) and I think the majority of Morrowind comparisons are coming from that element of the game (the alien setting I mean, there's mushroom forests and floating jelly thingies), because it doesn't really go for many of the things Morrowind did outside of dropping you into a completely alien world blind, no significant gameplay similarities outside exploration.This game is an EASY recommend. It has problems, and you could nitpick the game to death sure- it's janky, and there's a bit of a content drought in the game, I can count the number of quests in the current game on my fingers and toes (it took me 8.3 hours to do everything in the game and I'm usually really slow when it comes to completion times in games), most dungeons are deceptively short and sparsely decorated, most npcs don't acknowledge any of the things you've done after you complete an area's content and move on, combat is clunky, the ore economy is all screwed up, ect ect. But none of that really matters, because this game is still offering something that I don't think another game on the store can give you right now. It absolutely has that X factor that makes an rpg an instant classic and my only *real* gripe is that this developer doesn't have millions of dollars and a massive dev team to help scale this up from a single Entrée to a 4 course feast. I just want more! Please buy it and support the team so they can keep things going.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Delusion

_childDocuments_.review: what an incredible game. Visually classic and thrust into a unique and living world. Teeming with classic RPG elements like platforming, exploration, and gear. An exciting and unique realm to explore, full of secrets, choices that fully transform the world, and little hand-holding, making the experience feel worthwhile and fullIts the best elements out of early Puzzle Platformers like Banjo Kazooie and Legend of Zelda, with the heart and soul of classic medieval fantasy RPG titlesperfection
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Delusion

_childDocuments_.review: The game feels incomplete, which is a shame because it had such high potential. Unfortunately, it falls short, likely due to the developers' overly ambitious goals. Dread Delusions boasts a charming ambiance and well-crafted world design, but it is lackluster in terms of gameplay. You can easily run through enemies like a train and avoid their predictable moves even at the lowest levels, with no real punishment for mistakes. This issue is so pronounced that you can use death as a means of travel without any repercussions.Despite the world's handsome design, it lacks content, creating a sense of emptiness likely stemming from poor gameplay design that fails to reward exploration. It's disappointing because I had high expectations for this game. As someone else aptly put it, you install Dread Delusions expecting an open-world version of Lunacid, but instead, you are met with a beautifully crafted yet empty world, devoid of engaging gameplay mechanics and burdened with unnecessary dialogues that feel as though they were written by a teenager.

_childDocuments_.review: Edited review after beating the gameAfter finishing the game my thoughts are still the same as before, mostly. Seeing the zones, while most exploration doesn't benefit you too much, is still neat. The quests available in the endless isle are the better ones of the entire game, not by much, but still better. Finally the airship exploration should have been expanded on. It along with the endless isle were the best parts of the game. Combat stays incredibly uninteresting the whole game unfortunately. This makes it so all combat stats are 100% pointless and you should be maxing out Lore and Persona for any magic locks or charm checks. I'm going to switch the review to positive overall, but just barely. Really make sure you know what you're getting into before scooping the game up.---Old Review below---I'm going to try this some more but as of right now the biggest issue is the gameplay is genuinely horrible.Combat is incredibly uninvolved and without any challenge. Other reviews talk about this but I thought, "Surely they're overreacting." They aren't. The combat in this game is significantly worse than running around half-life 1 with a crowbar. The art direction and world building is wonderful which is the only reason I've given the game a chance.The quests and their objectives are not good. This game has the exterior of the classic rpg's it's trying to imitate without any of the soul.You trying to explore? Your primary reward across this empty terrain is lockpicks and potions. Sometimes you find equipment you do not need because the enemies cannot even hurt you if you're paying the slightest attention.This is a walking simulator that inconveniences you with the most pointless combat you've ever experienced in a game.It's a shame I have to give this a negative.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fun if simplistic in its combat and rpg mechanics, some of them almost feel vestigial in nature, but the setting and characters are engaging.It's a title that wouldn't feel out of place in the N64 / PSX catalog, and it struck a nostalgic chord with me at times.But even if you're not someone who grew up with the fifth gen of consoles, you may find yourself enjoying this game on its premise alone; an alien world for you to explore and piece out its lore by roaming the land and speaking with its inhabitants, solving their problems along the way.Some side quests even offer you a few ethical dilemmas that may give you pause and think on the consequences of your choices.It's not very long and doesn't outstay its welcome, and zipping around with magic reminded me of Morrowind's magic exploits. Once your agility reaches a decent score traversal becomes a fun activity on its own right.Might be a bit too easy for some, but there's always the hard mode for people who want a tougher time. Beware some jank in the game's engine, as occasional stutters show up to annoy you (could be a consequence of the HUGE draw distance the game has, or just Unity issues).All in all, recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Was gutted to lose my save that i had a bit of progress on, but this is definitely well worth picking up. It's like a love letter to all the late 90's and early 00's adventure and rpg games. The graphics are very much like King's Field, and there have been quite a few times it made me think of a game i used to play called Excalibur 2555ad. Combat is pretty straightforward and was never really challenging through the parts i had completed (I was about to start the Clockwork Kingdom island), but it was serviceable and the game isn't packed with enemies, so it's not something thrust upon you constantly. The most fun part is actually exploring the world, which is really the main point (except for the story, of course) and normally rewards you for your efforts. Story was fairly decent as well, but you will have to be ok with reading a bit, which i know is like an anathema to people these days.Basically, if you can finish reading this review (see last sentence of previous paragraph) AND want a proper adventure game with an interesting world to explore then Dread Delusion is well worth the price of admission.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are into old school RPG/adventure games and don't require modern visuals, this game might be for you. To me Dread Delusion evoked memories of two of my favourite games: Majoras Mask for the melancholy, the looming dread and the strange art style, and Morrowind for the uniquely alien setting and the stat based skill progression towards slowly becoming a god (don't tell the Union...).I spent my first few hours with careful exploration, enjoying the setting, the surprisingly deep and effective world building and getting to grips with the mechanics. Fatigue had to be managed carefully to perform decently in combat and with skill checks, while also not moving at a snail's pace. I want to stress that this part was a fantastic experience that I enjoyed a lot, because now I will come to the negatives.Just like in Morrowind, it seems I've passed the breaking point of the game. After about 7 hours into the game, I can blast across the map at 60 mph without even losing stamina (which I'm not sure is intended). Overworld enemies cannot touch me because I run circles around them, and even if they land a hit, it barely does enough damage for me to feel threatened. I can also jump from any height without losing health, so traversing the map has changed from slow and careful exploration to speedy gonzales murdering everything and reaching any place on the map in under a minute.Just like in Morrowind, this is sadly where the game takes a steep dive for me. The journey up to this point was fantastic, but progression was way too fast. Agility seems to be too good of a stat, as it not only solves map traversal (movement speed), but also stamina management, and melee at the same time. So once you find the armor pieces that boost agility, you are basically set for the game. Just add whatever headpiece you need for the occasion. With only 5 base Guile, I was able to dump all remaining delusions into charm and lore to access the remaining gated content, leaving me with little to no weak spots. I once found a mine shaft door that couldn't be picked and only smashed at 7 might, which is the only content I have not been able to access with this build so far. Maybe there is more down the line.My suggestions for the devs: - Agility needs to be toned down a lot for the reasons explained above. Maybe tie stamina to might. Reduce the speed gain from agility. Make it apply only to forward and not lateral and backwards movement, so you can't kite enemies around as easily. Maybe also nerf the recovery rate. As I said above, me not losing any stamina from running might be a bug. If it's not, this probably needs to be toned down heavily.- Enemies should be much more lethal. This will make sneaking an actual strategic choice for non-combat characters. As it is now, you will want to kill most enemies because it becomes trivial fast and results in item drops. You will not die often in this game, which is a shame considering what happens when you die. So far I died twice (!) during my entire playthrough. Once by walking into a trap and once by running off an island. If I had been a bit more careful in these instances, I might never have met you know who. With more lethal enemies, progressing skills and items into might/attack/defense becomes more viable, which it currently isn't, because agility breaks the game.- Item drops need tweaking. Between items hidden in the overworld and enemy item drops, you accumulate too many health potions. I've sold about 100 by now and money does gate some elements of the game, so you don't want this mechanic to break too easily. You also don't need that many health pots because lethality is too low. Lockpicks are more complicated matter. They do drop very often in certain areas / from certain enemies, but you will also burn through your stack on a regular basis if you are not heavily invested into lockpicking. I'd say they are fine from what I can tell.All of that being said, this is a gem of a game that needs a bit of cutting and polishing to reach its full potential. The world is simple but intriguing with fantastic world building both visually and narratively. The game oozes atmosphere and the dialogues are reminiscent of old CRPGs. They vary from light hearted fun to serious drama and outright horror – think a light variant of Planescape Torment – with a fair share of puns, details and interconnections that make the setting surprisingly robust. The little time spent in this world had me relive some of the excitement only the very best games of their time have done in the past, something that modern games sadly fail to replicate. This game, with a bit more time, polish and content, can become a classic.Changes to this review will likely happen as I progress further into the game, so please feel free to check back. Comments and discussion are also welcome, of course :)

_childDocuments_.review: The aesthetic, worldbuilding and lore drew me in. The lack of meaningful combat bums me out.This is more King's Field than Morrowind, but really somewhere between the two, if we must compare - Dread Delusion absolutely does stand alone as uniquely its own game, but there are certainly some apparent inspirations or similarities.The combat being one such similarity, and where the game is most like King's Field. Enemy behavior is quite simple and mostly patterns of attack/retreat seem like they'll see you through any encounter. I wouldn't mind this, BUT, at least so far (about 7 hours), enemy encounters are almost exclusively 1v1 or 1v2. With this style of combat, that effectively neuters any challenge it could have posed.I actually quite like King's Field style combat, but what King's Field does differently (and, to my taste, better) is provide much more complex situations to navigate, with more enemies, with a broader variety of shapes, sizes and behaviors. Notably, in addition to being designed to challenge the player outright, meeting that challenge with the dated, sluggish control scheme of King's Field added further difficulty.Dread Delusion brings (welcome) modernization to the controls, but fails to evoke any tension in combat. You lose practically nothing when you die, as well, so the stakes are extremely minimal. I've seen other reviews mention there are no bosses, which is wildly disappointing.So, in this specific dimension, the game falls woefully short for me. However, I still intend to finish it, and I do - reluctantly - recommend it, if and only if fantastic story, worldbuilding and aesthetics can make up for a lack of meaningful combat and progression for you.As others have said, it's a lore game. And it's great at that. Don't let any articles and the like fool you into thinking you'll get the depth of a Morrowind, or the tense, slow, methodical grind of King's Field combat.

_childDocuments_.review: i'll preface my criticisms by saying this is the best-written game i've played that's come out this year. nothing is quite like it. the politics and philosophy are intriguing but subtle enough that i came to understand some parts of them later on when talking about storylines to others. if you really take your time to immerse yourself in the world, you will be rewarded greatly.that said, unfortunately, i can't imagine someone would have fun with this game unless they're willing to engage with it in this way - the combat and puzzles have little to offer in the ways of difficulty or creativity; because dread delusion wants you to be able to see as much of it as you want (which is not necessarily a bad thing), there are not many meaningful choices to be made outside of dialogue. how you build your character is of little consequence to the combat as you'll be equipped to deal with any threat the game throws at you regardless. consequently, the might skill is given a few doors here and there that must be broken down to give players investing in the stat something to do with it. access to different kinds of locked doors are in fact most often what investing in any skill will give you.as shallow as the gameplay and overall design may be, i find it hard not to enjoy this game when it has so much to offer in the areas it does excel in. i wonder if build choices might feel more meaningful if the dialogue options felt less so; you're given ample space as a player to roleplay even in the more railroaded parts of the story. even if your character MUST do something, you are allowed and encouraged to give them their own opinion about it. mainstream CRPGs might give you better distractions via sidequests and combat loops, but dread delusion is not a game you will even want to be distracted from.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Delusion

_childDocuments_.review: I simply couldn't get into this game outside of the story, people seem to enjoy it for different reasons. Personally, a lot of the music in this game isn't good enough to play on repeat for the next 100 tracks while you're exploring the biome you're presently in trying to find the next thing to progress the main story or being distracted by any number of long drawn out side quests and side locations you probably can't open yet because you don't have the stats for it, and there are a number of issues that have arisen as a result of their update, which changed everything from a seemingly seamless world to an instanced world, though this was before the launch of the game. Dread Delusion has a lot of potential, and the story is what propels you ahead, but as you understand the combat is mediocre, and the songs start to get stuck in your head with the humming and choire-like tones, it becomes very exhausting. I want to point out that the game visually is awesome, the music at first is alright, but to go on just Story and Visuals alone isn't enough for someone like myself, I need physical gameplay that isn't me running through every location with max guile (cause I'm silly) and ignoring every single fight because you don't get anything worth while, no exp, no loot outside of knives and potions, so you try to rush through, get the content pushed forward, but then you are in the wrong location, you have no stats (might or lore) to unlock the secret locations to get Delusion Points to level up more of your skills, which really aren't doing much for you. So you need to leave and come back some other time if you manage to find the clothing to boost your stat and find enough delusions to unlock that secret location, which won't have a lot there.I was enjoying the game until I wasn't, and I have put enough time in it that I felt compelled to continue on through the game to reach the end and complete the primary story, which was excellent, but I just couldn't pull myself to do so. If you enjoy games like Morrowind and other first-person instanced-open world RPGs, you might find something here, but my advice would be to look up a guide when you get lost to avoid the headache of the music, lack of combat, and overall gameplay outside of the story.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an adventure of exploration, tough decisions, and story telling. The grim world building and unique lore rich setting of this game was a wonderful surprise. Don't let the low fidelity graphics prevent you from diving into this great experience. Gods in this world are very physical, and their long reign has confined humanity by what magic is allowed, and all blessings seem to come at steep prices. Those prices often being sacrifices in one form or another. Humanity rebelled against the gods, and the union that emerged has become yet another authoritarian inescapable power structure. Some lament the days where gods made things easier. You will be given choices to intervene in the plans of people and gods, with several factions in play. These outcomes will shape your ending, and you will depart from this adventure leaving the people and places you got to know to the fates your have helped shape. This is a heavy exploration game, with many magic spells to find, simple puzzles to solve, secrets to discover, lore to collect, equipment to find, upgrades to craft, potions to make, relics to retrieve, homes to decorate, cosmic horror gods to encounter, towns to aid, and people to talk to. The combat is mostly avoidable, but satisfactory. This is a well written game that didn't have any huge flaws, but did have memorable moments. I am glad I found this game, and my first play though took 40 hours. The music is acceptable, but honestly could have stood out more. It is atmospheric and fits enough with the tone of the game. I only felt like one minor choice was really an illusion of choice that did the opposite of what I wanted. There were several choices where you pick between two outcomes where you still feel conflicted, but that is the charm of this game. They want to put you in a messed up world and play a round of "would you rather" as you are stuck between gods and those who would defy them. I feel like fans of cosmic horror and elder gods will enjoy the options provided. This story exists only in the small outer reaches of the setting they describe, and I do hope to play more in the broader world of the skyrealms in a future title. To do that though, I might need you to buy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played this RPG before its full release and have played it some now. Unfortunately a lot of the things that were wrong with this game before haven't been fixed and it lacks a lot of polish.Let's start with the bad. The audio in this game is really lacking. A lot of events, actions and interactions don't have any sound effects despite feeling like they should. A lot of sounds feel out of place (and I don't mean the ones that make it sound surreal but rather things like heavy metal doors opening when there's not a piece of metal in sight). The music - despite having some proper bangers - can really get annoying fast, as it repeats too often and too fast. And the little bits of voice acting the game has is okay at best.The gameplay is a huge mixed bag. The game is way too easy and there's no challenge at all. If you strafe and do your heavy attacks only you don't run out of stamina, you stun lock the enemy and during the rare moments that the enemy does attack you don't get hit, ending most every encounter in you not losing a shred of health. Combine that with the fact that there's absolutely no reason to fight 99% of times, no special loot, no experience points or anything. Once you get a certain spell you can just easily run past everything and that is what you'll be doing once you notice. Some things just don't work like you'd think they would. Sneaking while casting a magic projectile at the enemy will almost always lead to the projectile hitting the ground right in front of you for example.The exploration, which I enjoyed most, is also quite the mixed bag as many areas and a lot of progression is tied to a single skill check, meaning that if you wanna play a specific character you'll be forced to level everything anyways. The lack of options really breaks the roleplaying aspect of it. However I still enjoyed exploring once I got over the fact that I have to be an allrounder. Mapping the islands, finding secrets and leveling was still great fun. The aesthetics of the game in combination with the story and the lore make up for a lot of the games shortcomings as the dialogue, the books and other flavour text have all been written exceptionally well. Characters all ooze personality and feel unique, have a lot of cool things to say. And the artstyle is just straight up beautiful, especially if you've nostalgia for the PSX or N64 era. All of that together makes for fantastic world-building that (if you can ignore the bad things) still make the game worth the time it takes to play it.Still, as it is right now I don't fully recommend it. A lot of the things I ignored due to it being in Early Access are still here and now that it's reached its full release stage I don't think they're forgivable anymore. I will update my review in the future if the game gets polished and the bugs are getting ironed out as this game really does have a lot of potential.

_childDocuments_.review: Weirdly calming minimalist open-world RPG, making me think (as others have mentioned) of Morrowind on acid. Don't go in expecting a mind-blowing experience, but more of a slow-burn sombre melancholy. It's hard to explain exactly. I'm not done with the game yet, but this will definitely be one of those games that lingers in the back of my mind for a while after I put it down.The biggest negative is the combat being mostly easy and somewhat easy to cheese if you tryhard. I recommend just sort of running in there recklessly, you're probably not going to die.By far the greatest positive is just the overall feeling of the world. I love the wavy PS1-style graphics style. The music reminds me of many SNES/PS1 era RPGs. It really ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hits you in the feels, man.Highly recommend, just know it's not that long of a game and will likely be a one or two-shot experience at most unless you're a speedrunner. But that's fine, it's worth the cost and is exactly the type of game I want to see more of in this world of over-engineered and over-staffed games full of MTX ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.Also yes, you can buff your speed to a crazy amount and GO FAST.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed a playthrough of the game, while its clearly rough around the edges and clearly bit more than the development team could reasonably chew, it remains a very unique and enjoyable experience.I'd say that the Combat and the lack of more varied soundtrack hurts this game the most. The combat does its job but its nothing particularly spectacular, it exists and thats about it. The Story, sidequests and the worldbuilding are the best part of this game and frankly the reason to play it.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Delusion

_childDocuments_.review: This is a tough one to review. I think there is a great game here but it is definitely marred by poor design decisions that just frustrate more than anything else. Locking items or locations behind arbitrary checks for the Lore or Lockpick skills just feels like such an afterthought. It's made worse by the fact that performing an action (such as picking a lock) doesn't grant XP. I understand that you wanted the choice you make while levelling to feel important, but it wasn't a fun part of the game for me. The above point was my major criticism, but smaller things like the controls not being easy to discern on Steam Deck, the map not being zoomable, and the world just feeling static and lifeless all contributed to a less than great experience. Overall I think there's a fantastic game here that I might revisit once the devs put a bit more time into future updates.

_childDocuments_.review: Best game 2024. Early game is a lil basic but it gets good when ya make it to the Endless Realm with all the castle islands. It's 100% not a finished game but I've had more fun playing this than most 70 dollar titles from the past couple years. Exp system needs a change, I like picking up skulls for a big chunk but there needs to be another way to gain exp on a smaller scale (completing quests?) and the combat obviously needs the most work buttttt I really like the weapon and armor upgrade system. Maybe add durability to make Iron/Fine ore more valuable? Player movement is amazing tho. Feels like quake mixed with skyrim when you start schmoovin with bhops. _childDocuments_.review: Really wanted to get into this, since Morrowind got invoked a few times describing this game. And lo-fi graphics aren't always a bad thing, often it lets indie creators create a compelling game with modern mechanics that make a compelling gameplay loop.But aside from a strong theme, this game really plays like something a few generations previous to Morrowind, where just being 3-dimensional was a novelty in and of itself. I was born a little too late to enjoy a throwback to that era. To spell it out for others:*You can't really interact with the environment in a significant way, no book objects to pick up and sell, no NPC inventories to loot for better equipment, most of what you're looking at is bolted down and just for show.*NPCs/mobs can do written dialogue with Charisma checks, and can fight, seems like that's about it.*Lockpicking is a dice roll, again okay but considering the only other environmental interaction are switch presses, made me a bit underwhelmedThere's some pretty nice artwork/music for opening cut scenes but the gameplay music was a little too brassy, same as the overblown color palette with the rough poly modelsIt's really ambitious, I never want to discourage that. But for $20, there's just not enough going on. I would even consider buying a book written in the setting for that much, but soaking up the lore through an interface this dated wasn't for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Delusion

"I miss this game" after beating one...

_childDocuments_.review: I've fiddled around in this weird little world for a few hours and I've really enjoyed myself. It's very much early in development, and a lot definitely feels like placeholders for future content. What's here, though, is delightful and haunting, if a bit buggy. The jittering vertices, low polygon counts, strange creatures, and fun quest design have kept me fascinated by this game. It's a little bit more basic at the moment compared to some of its inspirations, but its systems are already beginning to be fleshed out. I think that this game could wind up being an all-time favorite of mine in the long run but it's still a bit early to tell. I'll keep poking around in the oneiric isles until they're done, admiring the strange islands lingering beneath the strange magenta light of the neuron star.

_childDocuments_.review: I had high hopes for dread delusion and while the game isn't bad it sure isnt the "Morrowind like RPG" everyone said it was. The looting system is similar to a platformer in a way where there's floating potions, coins and lockpicks. This threw me off as I was expecting a traditional RPG looting system and once again while this isn't bad it is sort of a deal breaker for me. Even the loot chests aren't traditionally lootable, they jiggle for a moment and fly open revealing the item inside. The aesthetic and lore of Dread Delusion is excellent, a ps1 style mixed with the other worldly vibes feels awesome but personally the lack of traditional RPG systems throws the whole experience off for me. WIll you like this game? who's to say, but don't go in expecting an RPG experience similar to Morrowind like many have said.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Delusion

_childDocuments_.review: Well I just finished this game and I am impressed. Dread Delusion in short is a Dark Fantasy open world RPG with some arguably some horror elements (though I didn't really get scared at all during it).As a small scale Indie game the world and story line is smaller and shorter than a game like Skyrim. But what is there very much justifies the price tag in my opinion. With a good mix of side-quests that involve you exploring and learning about the original and fascinating world Lovely Hellplace have created. With choices to be made about how you end it. Combat is simple (won't say its too simplistic as I lack sufficient experience with these types of games)All in all I really enjoyed myself.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Delusion

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished it for the first time in about 24h, and am already excited to do it again in a couple months, making new choices, supporting different factions, maybe not killing anything. Playing this was a pure delight and conveyed a certain explorative glee I have not felt in a long time =)Whenever I got a new progression based achievement I was in the .1% of players getting it, I was just so entranced that I had to press on after buying it. Except for the final encounter, real life gets in the way sometimes x)
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Delusion

_childDocuments_.review: im neutral on this one. one the one hand i encourage everyone to try this out and see if it fits.the art department on this one is strong and i love that.butit doesnt quite hit that open world elder scrolls jank. for one its not quite as open world as it maybe should be. for the other, you dont have a map for the first 2 or 3 hours. so i dont even know where to go for all of my quest.Duke asked me to get him some tea. when I got the tea, i went back for him but he was gone. i have no idea why he moved or where to but thats not how questgivers work.the most disturbing part about this is the Font tho. since theres basically No voice Acting (which is reasonable) you will read a lot. - a lot - but the font is hard to read. it looks cool, sure. but thats not what a font should do when it comes to dialogue and lore reading.why i however refunded it was, that the block in combat does not respond which makes combat not only risky but also boring. you just mash attacks and hope they die before you do.i expected more from a morrowind wannabe.however. this might not apply to you. so i do recommend at least Testing it out for yourself.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Delusion

_childDocuments_.review: Dread Delusion is a game that has some of my favorite RPG writing of all time and thankfully knows it's abilities in other fields. That is to say that the map and exploration is wonderful, the combat is nothing (which I would prefer to it trying to be something and failing. Outside of a complete genre change I see no way that this game would ever end up with astounding combat and it doesn't need it), the writing is impeccable, the music is great, and the art is excellent.Dread Delusion takes many fascinating routes with its quests. Most major quests turn into a philosophical debate about whatever topic may be at play: subservience that provides comfort, the ability to change oneself, the value that death brings to life, the game covers many interesting topics in its journey and honestly I can't name a weak execution among them.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Delusion

_childDocuments_.review: Game feels like Morrowind, just with simpler leveling and inventory. You level by collectibles so you don't feel like you're wasting XP by not killing things, just missing loot. Quest/World Structure is more like a KOTOR/Mass Effect instead of a true 'open world' so far. I kind of enjoy it better that way progression feels rewarding and it really helps with pacing and world building. Storytelling and world building is great. Combat is linear, but that's not the appeal of this game. Little buggy nothing too bad. This is a great game and hope the dev comes out with another building and expanding on this formula, perhaps with more advanced leveling/perks etc. If you're like me and love Elder scrolls, KOTOR, etc this game hits. Dont start at night when you have to work on the morning. 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Delusion

_childDocuments_.review: Dread Delusions strongest aspects are it's presentation and it's worldbuilding.I adore how alien the Oneiric Isles can feel, it's like Morrowind turned up to 11 with it's un-apologetic use of bold colours, bizarre creatures and environments; The game truly has an amazing aesthetic that I appreciated throughout my entire time with it.The worldbuilding is the second biggest aspect, I found myself paying attention to the lore of the events, factions, individual characters and even general concepts like cipher magic quite a bit, even found myself reading a few books surprisingly. It's all super interesting and if you're a lore nerd believe me you'll have a wonderful time with Dread Delusion.Unfortunately combat is not Dread Delusions' strong suit, I never found any enemy to be a threat to me. After a while you come to realize that almost every enemy is kinda just the same. Once I got around 30% of the way through the game I noticed this and from that point on all enemies lost their luster, was a shame really because the enemies look really cool, especially in later areas. Sadly they just have no teeth to back it up.Spellcasting is also not very good as it's very slow and infinitely less efficient then just hitting them in the face with a big sword. Overall if you can ignore the lacking combat Dread Delusion is a fantastic world that I would personally recommend as I enjoyed my time with it.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Delusion

_childDocuments_.review: Dread Delusion is an open world RPG brimming with strange places and dark perils. Carve your own path through the flying continents of a shattered land. Discover curious towns, unearth occult secrets, master powerful magic - and change the world through your choices.

name: My Friendly Neighborhood
detailed_description: Something is amiss with everyone's favorite Saturday morning puppet show! For years, the colorful cast of The Friendly Neighborhood delighted audiences across the globe with their cooky capers and educational adventures. However, as time went on and interest waned, the production studio found themselves out of money and closed their doors for good. Toy sales would dwindle, and birthday balloons and cakes would find new mascots. In time, the once household names would fade into increasingly niche fandoms. Until one night years later, the studio unexpectedly clicks back to life and starts broadcasting The Friendly Neighborhood. TV sets across the globe flicker for a moment before the familiar puppets return for a surprise encore! But this isn't your typical family-friendly holiday special... are those puppets eating each other!? Thinking the antenna on top of the main building has started broadcasting old episodes, the city sends Handyman Gordon to straighten things out. It doesn't take Gordon long to find that the typically friendly neighborhood has become a lot less welcoming. Stepping into his work boots, you'll have to fend off ferocious friends, solve a plethora of playtime puzzles turned perilous, and hopefully uncover the dastardly truth at the heart of this terrifying tale. If you're tired of games that rely on gore more than solid scares, then come on over to the streets of MFN! Featuring a mix of action and adventure, MFN is the perfect game for horror fans looking for something a bit different. Sure, there might not be any dismemberment or decapitations. But that just means the puppets don't stay down for good... Features A colorful cast of puppet friends turned adversaries (and maybe turned friends again!) Non-linear, survival horror gameplay. Make sure to check your map! Unique weapons like the Rolodexer. Do you know your ABCs? You better - it's your ammo. An array of puzzles in the vein of the survival horror greats. A multitude of diverse environments, from the 'BTS' Ray's Workshop to cardboard crayon halls A grid-based real-time inventory, 'cause that's just way better NOW FEATURING: Post game Neighborhorde mode!

_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: I am not a horror game player, but I figured a game with muppet-inspired characters would be a fine enough time for my antsy nature bout it to wear off as I played.It did indeed, and I was rewarded with a game that's fun to play, WONDERFUL to explore, and just a very genuinely heartful creation. Not only as a love-letter to Jim Henson and crew's projects; but the game itself and its story.A rare experience that can face you with some big, doofy thing in front of you; while a character gives outright poetic self-reflection.Definitely recommend it, especially if you like to take your own pace with a game and dig around all the rooms after you start to really settle in.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: More unsettling than scary, My Friendly Neighborhood feels like a great opportunity for those who typically shy away from the genre to experience a survival horror title.The narrative, delivered largely through discovered documents, draws you into a series of polished environments that become more interconnected and easier to traverse as you explore. The voice acting and ambiance are top notch and the game is respectful of its player's time. I look forward to checking out future titles from the Szymanskis.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; I had an amazing time streaming the game, while doing voice impressions of puppets. It's definitely worth the purchase, especially if you're a fan of RE gameplay, references to Sesame Street/The Muppets, and the comedic lines from the puppets and the duo of the Big Chungus MGS guy and Arlo.This game popped my Resident Evil cherry.Now that that's out of the way; I really enjoyed this game. I always liked The Muppets and Sesame Street growing up, so seeing the goofiness of this game via ManlyBadassHero & Vinny Vinesauce got me interested into the game. The gameplay felt smooth and fun to play, the humour was fantastic and the emotional moments were very touching. My only issues I had with the game were; 1) You can't reload your last save once you complete it. I don't know if that's a RE thing, considering I've only played the RE Revelations 3DS demo ages ago and like, a half hour of RE4, but I wanted to see the other choice without playing all over again. It's not THAT big of an issue, since the devs seems to be keeping it very faithful to a RE game, but it still would've been nice. 2) Not having an indicator for secret tapes. I know they're supposed to be "secret" for a reason, but the completion colour of the room messes with me. Thankfully, tapes collected are saved separately from your game's save, cuz my game crashed once or twice. 3) The last two areas felt rather short and I feel like they could've been combined into one. I loved the art style of the second to last area and the final area was getting interesting, but was as short as a jumpscare in an RPG Maker horror game. 4?) Maybe an option to have subtitles for the puppets, even if it does clutter the screen? It'd be kind of funny. Other than that I had an amazing time with the game. (Besides the couple of crashes, but the bugs I encountered were funny) I beat it in about 12 hours and spent the remaining 6.8 hours trying to speedrun to the truck and checking out free-cam mode. Shoutout to Cody for the ducks! My Friendly Neighbor (Being a Canadian, this is difficult for me to spell out) is super unique and charming and I can't wait to play it again to get the other endings. Norman is my favourite. Hopefully, the devs start a merch store (I don't see why they wouldn't), so I can get myself a Norman and rat plushie IN THE MAIL!P.S. I streamed the game :) (There was a lot of puppet voice impressions from me and I accidentally did an Elmo voice for the first time):

_childDocuments_.review: I gotta say this is a very unique game. The humor, the character design, (Which is obviously a love letter to Jim Henson's characters) I absolutely love the simplicity of the overall gaming experience. I'm gonna go through a 2nd play through because I absolutely love the hilarious dialogue and the life the characters bring to the game play. And if you are playing on the steam deck: FPS tops at 71 to 72 fps and overall clarity is there. I haven't made any adjustments to the settings on the Steam deck version as they are not required. Try it yourself. You will not be disappointed. It is a light-hearted horror experience that everyone should try. If you ever played RE7 or RE8 with light puzzles give it a shot. A lot of love was put into this gem.

_childDocuments_.review: While it’s not truly scary, there’s something to be said about how easily they made these goofy looking puppets feel like a threat. The controls are excellent, the soundtrack is top-notch, and it gets surprisingly tense!If you enjoy old school survival horror, that is to say: you don’t mind backtracking, then this game is something you should check out!A minor gripe I have is that it can be easy to overlook important/key items, but the map usually helps you avoid this by marking rooms incomplete until you’ve discovered everything.I do also wish it was a bit longer and a bit more truly scary. It comes close in the location you visit at the end.Regardless, this was an evening well spent!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a good example of how much gameplay can effect a users experience. The aesthetic the game is going for might not scare a lot of people (unless you have Pupaphobia), but the gameplay twists the artistic direction into a genuine nightmare. I found myself on trying to organize my items in my inventory, constantly keeping track of how much ammo or health-o-lax I had. Every encounter in this game is a question of "Would using a resource here be worth it?" The game genuinely got terrifying when I was low on my various resources and had to prepare for upcoming encounters. Also the voice direction in this game is phenomenal, I loved each character and the personality they brought to the game. Overall an amazing experience, 10/10 would recommend

_childDocuments_.review: I played through an entire run, and had a great time! Things I loved: -Combat: felt clunky, yet natural for wielding a rolodex and typewriter shotgun-Puzzles: a perfect blend. Not crazy obtuse, not insanely easy and over explained. Great environmental cues, and natural progression.-Theming: the art and theming were wonderfully on point, especially the classical art pieces featuring the characters. I loved that. Things I didn't love as much: -Pacing: the first two to three major stages felt well paced, but way way heftier than the last 2/5 of the game. -World building: needed some more of that. Would have loved to see the broadcast, and a better integration of the themes regarding  -Character building: the emotional beats, and especially the ending, didn't line up with the sparse character building over the course of the game imo. Some of the major character moments felt out of left field, and unearned. -I can't even say this one due to spoilers but The End Bit felt so rushed. There was next to no build up to it, it happened very very fast, and before i even got to revel in the dread of it all, I was in a boss battle and then shuffled out the door. Overall, I would definitely recommend this, as the things I didn't love as much are things that I can see promise of. For an indie title that started as a solo project, this game performs incredibly well and I would highly recommend it to any fans of Resident Evil or Sesame Street.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: its a fun game, bit annoying at times but once you get the hang of it theres a lot of enjoyable gameplay to be had, and does have some genuinely disturbing moments,  at first I was worried Id get stuck at some parts and this was due to the games difficulty, but I think learning what to do, where to go and how use things are a massive part of this games experience, if you fall you get back up, if you miss you just keep firing, if you remmeber what you need, you go back and get it.overall this game is a brilliant, possibly unintentional, homage to games we grew up with and still play today, the somber atmosphere and gameplay of resident evil, the styalised graphics and characters  that show you dont need a lot of details, and a story slowly unraveling as you play, urging you to keep going no matter how much harder it gets or how badly you want to throw the controler down and stop playing.but probably my biggest praise for this game? it doesnt discriminate between what it can be played on, you defintly need a modern computer but from what I can tell this is the first "new" game thats come out this year that I can play on my computer with no lag, no slowdown and no crashing, the resolution settings are perfect for playing this on older models and as said before, the simpler graphics and textures and ps2/xbox era character models make this a game anyone can play on any pc/laptop regardless of how old their grpahics card is.

_childDocuments_.review: If you want a genuinely good horror experience with much more below the surface that isn't a shallow jump scare riddled game like FNAF or Poppy Playtime, this game destroys them in storytelling, gameplay, and just being an overall good experience. It's as if the writers of Jim Henson's Creature Shop looked at Resident Evil Village and said "We could do that!" and made an unnerving experience that, while not too scary, unnerving with enough spooky curve balls to give you a jolt.Horror games with heart is a rarity, and this game absolutely has it. Very much worth the purchase, I loved this game

_childDocuments_.review: What an absolutely delightful game to play. If you are a fan of Bioshock and want a feel of crazy insane muppets chasing you and pounding you into the ground then this game is for you. The whimsical dialogue from the characters is funny and adds an interesting dynamic to the game. Although I was expecting this to be a horror game it doesn't quite hit that genre all that much in all honesty. It does have its suspenseful moments however from time to time. But this is more of an enjoyable and funny puzzler/shooter.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: First of all if you enjoy the original Resident Evil then I would say you should play this game, secondly this game also uses the inventory management that RE4 uses as well. Clearly a lot of inspiration from that franchise, but in the best way. The level design, characters, puzzles, and story are all fleshed out and terrific.  The game is a breath of fresh air when it comes to the Indie Horror scene.The Szymanski Family are all talented developers, so this was a no-brainer when I saw it go live. Play their games and you'll understand that they all take influence from the best parts of what make games fun, and crank it to eleven. Oh and for those worried about the length of the game (as if that matters), there are tons of secrets to find, cheats and game modes will also become accessible after your first completion. Some are game changers, and others are just for fun, either way a normal playthrough of searching for everything can last up to about 5-6 hours.I'd also like to note I purchased this Day 1 and the game never crashed nor did it give me any issues performance wise. Throughout my entire experience with My Friendly Neighborhood it was nothing short of a good time.I'm looking forward to making a video review on this one.Well done! I look forward to whatever you guys make next.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: This is just a brief little review to say that I really enjoyed this game! The idea of 'what if Resident Evil was on Sesame Street' premise is really quite cool, and the environment was an interesting one to explore. I do think that, perhaps, some of the puzzles & item discovery were a little too esoteric and some elements of the combat grew to be a touch tiresome towards the last hour or two, these would be minor criticisms in my mind. This is absolutely an experience worth taking the plunge on, even in a year that saw two fantastic remakes of excellent survival horror games in Dead Space and Resident Evil 4. A really neat, surprising package that I'm glad I experienced!

_childDocuments_.review: SPOILERS AHEAD.Genuinely, a great game. It's effectively a children's version of Resident Evil in terms of gameplay (puzzles, needing to find keys, a lot of backtracking, a few secrets to find, enemies respawn, inventory management, etc), but with the bonus that it's first-person and not third-person like the RE remakes (or third-person fixed camera like the originals).The puppets' voice lines get a bit repetitive but they're very well acted and felt a lot like the old Sesame Street and Muppets Show did when I was a kid. They have a habit of sometimes being a bit too on the nose with their "unnerving" phrases, and their constant shouting over each other, but it's fine. A bit more variation in types would've been nice to see.With the "boss" puppets, I liked that there's about 4 you can help. I helped all 4 on my first run through because I was trying to clear all the red zones from the map, and it inherently came with sorting all the problems. I can't remember their names properly, but I think there was Ray (a big monster in the sewer pipes that needed a boiler fixed), a big green frog thing that got sad watching the films in the theatre, a huge pink bird called Pearl that I gave back their eyes (I didn't realise they were hers to start with until I found paintings of her with them glasses on), and three annoying dogs that ate their food but 2 ran off somewhere else.The two real bosses were a bit flat, though (no pun intended with the first boss). First one was a giant wall-like puppet with eyes and a mouth spitting smaller puppets at you. It came completely out of nowhere and had no apparent connection with the show like all the others. Maybe some hint at an eldritch force involved? If there was, there was no other mention of what or why it was there.Second boss was again out of nowhere, just an amalgamation of the "unfriendly" puppets (which apparently just means the same puppets but instead of waiting until you catch their attention, they automatically chase you). I didn't even realise you could shoot it, when you first load after the phone call, you only have a torch and I didn't realise you could scroll back to your weapons, so I ended up kiting it around until the gate slowly opened. Again, a boss with no real explanation that I recall finding, no further references to it. Only those 2 weird bosses.The game itself loads really quickly, able to go from starting the game to getting into a save file within 10 seconds. The only real downside I could find was just how resource intensive it ended up. I had max graphics, and on my RX 7900 XT, I was getting 80 Celsius temps. I turned off Ambient Occlusion and it immediately dropped down to 65 Celsius. That could probably do with being worked on.All in all, it's a nice little game. It's very short (maybe 4 hours long?) but I ran through it four times for achievements. Grab it on a 75% off discount.

_childDocuments_.review: In general, I think this game does deserve a lot of the praise it has been getting, as it is definitely one of the most unique gaming experiences to come out this year. Especially, in terms of voice acting/character interactions, humor, art style, and the plethora of puzzles it encourages the player to solve. However, with that being said, I can't deny that this game has a few problems that can't be ignored. The first major problem being that it doesn't really do enough, except in one small section, to be considered a horror game. Specifically, the puppets are pretty much the same in every way except model design and they cant even be considered scary. They don't have unique attack patterns to diversify themselves, the voice lines while funny, can be a bit grating when there's more than one in a room repeating the same lines over and over again at the top of their lungs. So even if the player happened to have a fear of puppets, I'm pretty sure that fear factor wouldn't last long and they would get more annoyed than anything. The other major issue has to do with the melee is nearly impossible to use in this game. The puppets hit boxes are so broken, that half the time melee attacks would not register and there's also no option to block or dodge. However, for some reason the puppets could attack me from across the room.  So, it felt like if melee was the only option I had or if i wanted to conserve ammo, I was constantly being punished for playing the game.Overall, I don't love this game but I don't hate it either. This game has a lot of potential and could be amazing with some adjustments. Specifically, varying the attacks of each type of puppet and maybe toning down how much the puppets talk because when they are in the twitching in the dark and being quiet they are a little creepy. However, most of all, the game would already be ten times better if the melee attacks were usable and the puppets couldn't grab me from across the map.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: The theme of something innocent turned horror is nothing new these days, but it's still a well executed experience.The design in the levels and gameplay is very solid. Progression feels rewarding, with lots of reasons to revisit places, whether it's for puzzles or unlocking new things.It DOES feel like it peaked at the first studio stage area, but I still have other locations to visit, so it can still get better. Will update when I finish the game.Game isn't that intense in its horror, but it still gets you at times, and the amazing voice acting from the puppets help create a unique and unsettling atmosphere.There is VERY little searching for supplies, making you look at lots of things you THINK you can search or pick up items, but you can't.It can also be very unforgiving if you play poorly, because that saves, heals, and ammo are limited.If you're a fan of nostalgia turned into horror, and Resident Evil style survival horror, this is a really good design on both.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't let the mascot horror look fool you, this is actually a proper survival horror game in the style of Resident Evil. That means you need to conserve ammo, manage resources, and backtrack through areas to find any missed items or secrets. There's even a mechanic where the Puppets will get back up when you reload a room, similar to the RE1 Remake crimson heads, which can be prevented by taping the Puppets up just like burning bodies prevents crimson heads in RE1R. This makes you put a lot of thought into your routing when going back through areas, and rewards players who can effectively avoid enemies rather than engaging them in the first place.I didn't personally find it to be all that scary, but that doesn't bother me because the actual gameplay and exploration are so solid.My only possible criticism of the game is that it's a bit short. My first playthrough took 5-6 hours on Survival difficulty and doing almost every side objective. That said, this game shared another similarity with many Resident Evil games in that there's an end-of-game ranking and plenty of meta-unlockables to encourage repeat playthroughs and casual speedrunning. If you're the type to just finish a game and be done with it forever, though, then be aware a lot of the value here is in those repeat playthroughs.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: I have never written a review before but I felt compelled this time after finishing My Friendly Neighborhood. This game deserves all of the praise that it gets.The gameplay did not blow me away, but it is certainly enjoyable.The puzzles did not blow me away, but they are certainly enjoyable.The world and the underlying themes in the story did blow me away, however.The game looks beautiful and the developers clearly spent a lot of time putting attention to detail. I was honestly expecting some kind of half-baked Indie game when I got this, but I was legitimately impressed with how detailed and structured the environments are. The world is surprisingly large and without a walkthrough would take a LONG time to traverse properly. I really enjoyed stopping along the way to check each area and appreciate the little things that were added.The way the story comes together as you progress through the game has everything to do with whether you make it a point to find as many collectibles as you can. If you do, you will be rewarded with a much deeper experience than if you just run through shooting puppets. I found myself both surprised and extremely satisfied with the darker, visceral themes that come into view by the end of the game. I do not want to spoil anything, but after I was done I almost felt obligated to watch Sesame Street.If you like survival horror games, or just want a decent game experience that is worth the money, buy My Friendly Neighborhood. I very much hope for some form of a sequel in the future.Also, I will tell you right now,

_childDocuments_.review: It took me just about 6 hours of real playtime to play the game all the way through. I originally tried the demo version and decided it was amusing enough to give the full game a go- props to the devs for creating a demo version. Overall I would rate this game 3/5. It held my attention for the whole time, the puppets were both pretty funny and a bit spooky at times. The gameplay I would describe as a first person shooter survival horror game with a heavy theme of puzzle solving along the way. The different puzzles were reasonably difficult to solve, but not so much so that they became frustrating. By halfway through though, it did become fairly tedious to be circling back to places I'd already been several times when I had unlocked new content in the areas and there's no run option at all. There are candy bars that temporarily increase your speed, but with the amount of my inventory space taken up by weapons and items essential to the puzzles, I found them to be not worth the space to carry, particularly with their rather short timed speed boost. My bigger gripe with the game overall came down to the combat mechanics. I'm not a huge first person shooter gamer, but I've played my fair share. The close range physical combat was hit or miss. The enemy hitboxes are enormous but still I found inconsistency in how many swings/ placement and timing of swings to take down a puppet. This proved frustrating over time and it was never exactly clear to me if I was doing something wrong or not. The same goes for the ranged shooting - sometimes puppets would be taken down in two shots, other times 10. The lack of sights to tell you where you're aiming is fine, I can get used to that, but the unpredictable amount of shots it takes to move past puppets blocking paths just felt clunky overall. The game is designed in a way that its meant to be easily replayable with some additional 'cheats' or game modifiers that would change the gameplay up enough to spark some interest for some players. I will likely not be one of those players that runs this back for the foreseeable future. It was a fun playthrough and worth a chance if you see it on sale, but could be better.
