_childDocuments_.review: The concept of taking a beloved children's property and twisting it isn't anything new. But what I think makes My Friendly Neighborhood more appealing than games like FNAF and Bendy is the earnestness and love for what inspires it.You might be surprised that the combination of Sesame Street meets Resident Evil doesn't show a cynical nature for the entertainment industry it satirizes. From its inclusion of Arlo to its more tender moments with its original characters there is a clear respect that shows this was made by fans.While it's not the scariest game it also showcases strong elements of the horror genre. Its studio backlot setting contributes to this feeling by being just as much iconic as any mansion or castle. This especially when looking at its interconnected layout and a strong focus on puzzles.If any of this sounds appealing to you I implore you to give the neighborhood a visit.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I enjoyed the game to the extent where I wished it was a bit longer, but that's not to say it is short by any stretch of the imagination! It has a dark story, but it is not your average horror game. It relies on the audience having a predisposed fear of puppets and movements that cross the uncanny valley. There are a few genuinely solid moments of horror, in both and atmospheric sense, impending dread, and jump scares. The art style is bubbly and well composed and that was enough for me to be interested and boy was it worth the wait. Unsure of sequel potential, but this games quality alone was enough to merit praise! 9/10!
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: Finally got me some time to fully play through My Friendly Neighborhood and man was that an amazing experience! Very charming and the writing in these games never cease to give me a good chuckle.The gameplay's got that Resident Evil formula with the puzzle solving and back tracking, but it never got irritating with the plethora of shortcuts you unlock as you explore the studio. With multiple endings, difficulties, cheats and modes, you're bound to have a fun time playing through more than once.John Szymanski did a fantastic job with this game and I hope y'all will consider giving it a purchase. It was a wonderful time!
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: Love this game, really wish it got more attention over Security Breach: Ruin. This game was a god-dang delight the whole way through. Even after my first run, I went back and had fun with all the cheats they give (especially free cam, lots of hidden stuff outside the rooms). If you liked DHMIS or Welcome Home I recommend this one, especially if you liked the funny and silly parts of it.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, a fun experience. First time on Normal difficulty playthrough clocked in at 4 and a bit hours.I do enjoy the writing of the story and some of the lines from the enemies are fun but get real repetitive real quick. Puzzle variety and how they were presented was good, and I did like the way certain areas would be re-contextualised at later stages of the game.My biggest issue is the pistol/wrench damage and their inconsistency. I get it, not knowing how many shots or swings it's going to take does add to the tension but most of the time it felt egregious, any sense of fear turned to anger as I kept plinking away at regular enemies. 11 shots was the highest count I noticed for a regular enemy who if not taped, i'd be running into again later. Health economy felt fine, maybe even a tad too generous.I ended with a few key items I never used, looking forward to a second playthrough to see  what I missed.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of love and care went into this game and it does show. I believe the amount of time it took me to finish the game was a bit fast, but there was never much of a truly dull moment. The art style, the atmosphere, the voice acting, and the overall feel of the game was great. You do unlock several extras in the end to play with. Overall, I would recommend this game to anyone that loves the Resident Evil feel to games, as this is heavily inspired from them. For the average person, I would recommend it if it goes on a small sale.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: I really dont understand who this game is for. Its not funny enough for people to enjoy the type of humor this game is going for. I do see the vision, its like if Sesame Street became evil but the way information is provided left me feeling very lost most of the time. The map is confusing and not very fun to get around. I also noticed there isn't any music in the game so the silence from moving between room to room is very noticeable.I was also playing on the harder difficulty but it actually made the game more unfun. The puppets take too much ammo to kill and the melee is super unsatisfying and useless. I was always out of ammo or duct tape, meaning that my best option was to just run around until I died. Very frustrating and shallow experience
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: Its just a really well thought out game. Even though this game is newer, it makes me feel nostalgic like Portal does. I love playing this game and it genuinely makes me so happy. All characters are great, its fun with a little horror element to it, and is just a cool concept and world. There are a few glitches that sometimes makes it hard, or its easy to restart game completely, but I didnt mind doing it again or the glitches. So happy with this game though.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: Why i do not recommend this game:1.Who think having all the enemy NPC talking loudly all together in a single room is a good idea? Luckily, you could turn down their speaking volume. But why make them talk so much in the first place tho? This design is not scary nor humor. Just annoying feature. 2.Enemy hit-box is ridiculous. Sometimes you could hit them with your wrench, sometimes they get to you first. Melee is a joke in this game. You can only rely on luck when it comes to melee.3.Unnecessary door entering animation. They try so hard to imitate Resident Evil. When you enter a door, you go through a 3 seconds long door opening animation. It gets boring and repetitive.4.Plot is not engaging. Characters are plain and flat. Player has to progress for the sake of progress. There are nothing that keeps you going in this game.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: You'd think this game would fall under the mascot horror sub-genre and just be YouTube bait, but it surprisingly isn't. It's a genuine survival horror experience comparable to Resident Evil 7 and 8, except the horror is comedy instead.Plus it has the funny blue puppet guy who loves Paper Mario: The Thousand Year Door, so it's an immediate 10/10.Definitely worth playing, give it a shot!
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: When I first saw this game I thought it was another generic "mascot horror" title, but this game is far more than that. Real effort and heart went into this game, and its roots both as a RE2 style game and as a homage to both the Muppets and Sesame Street shine through at every step. Even the "guns" feel fun and friendly, using various office instruments to help the rogue puppets learn their ABCs.The level design is very strong. It's a decently sized map without feeling overwhelming, and as you explore the studio lot you come to learn which passages are the best to take in order to save on ammo or other resources, as much like RE2, these enemies can get back up.There's also a fun heart to this story. We get glimpses of the protagonist Gordon's backstory just so we can piece together how he came to be the gruff "get the job done" kind of guy he is. We also get to know some of the "boss puppets" better largely through context clues and better observations of their behavior.The puzzles in this game are simple but satisfying. Nothing too challenging came here or there, but by and large they were satisfying to learn and understand. Similarly this game does a decent job of letting you piece together where to go next without often directly telling you or marking some objective on your map.Overall this is a worthwhile experience, and truly not what I was expecting at all. A pleasant surprise to be sure.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely loved this game. I've never been someone to play on harder difficulties just because I get frustrated with the lack of resources. Even though I played on veteran and ran out of ammo several times, you can easily stun them with the wrench and work around it, wonderful game design in my book! The story was great and the game definitely has replay-ability. Highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: Foremost, I would say this is one of the best Indie games of the year. I do love how the story is written. The protagonist is trying to figure out himself. The backstory of My Friendly Neighborhood is sad and well-written. All of the characters are well-rounded. Lastly, I do like the Resident Evil aspects of the game: inventory, combat, and saving. I would definitely recommend this game to anyone interested in this genre.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing! The puzzles are a lot of fun and confusing, and the mechanics are so exciting to play around with! There's so much replay value, and while it's a little confusing on the first go around, it still feels rewarding to complete. Would definitely recommend to anyone who loves the mascot horror genre, and wants a little spin or variety in that category!
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: Fun, weird, funny, and has a good story to it! My only complaint is that in story mode, resources are so scarce and the fact you need tokens to save the game... (Like, what if the game crashes? Too bad for me...?) I feel like, there should be just a LITTLE more resource spawns, I checked so many drawers and felt like the devs just spent more time creating some 'prop' rather than a potential location that would give resources... Other than, that I love the game! Especially the NeighborHORDE mode!
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: This game is awesome! It's a different take on survival horror but all the gameplay elements are there to enjoy. I haven't finished it yet but I wanted to write this review for those who are playing on steam deck. There is a bug that causes tvs and theater screens to not play in game. To the point I'm in the game now it's only effected one part of the game but the rest is playable without it. So when you get a movie theater reel that says heist on it look it up on a walk through.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: I saw this game on my recommended on steam and thought it looked cool. But in all honesty I don't know where all these good reviews are coming from if there was a thumb side ways option I would pick that. The melee combat is just terrible makes the game not enjoyably but looking past that. The save mechanic is cool but with the lack of save stations throughout the game it just punishes the player for exploring. I really like the save mechanic but there needs to be more save stations because backtracking is just not fun, and the worst part about the game is how easy it is to get cornered. If the save stations weren't all miles away from each other maybe getting killed wouldn't discourage players from playing the game. I'll keep giving the game a chance maybe it improves later on but as of the first 30 min to hour of the game is just has so many small problems I just feel unmotivated to continue playing.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: when resident evil meets Mascot horrorOften now Mascot horror has been tainted by the likes of poppy playtime or garten of ban ban. These games feel more intent on selling you merchandise than providing a compelling story, or likable characters, or even well designed characters. I feel that this is in a sub-genre of anti-mascot horror games along the likes of bendy and the dark revival and baldi's basics and i am here for it. It doesn't bog you down with a non story and incomprehensible lore and gets right to the point. Part of my qualms with "Modern" mascot horror is that it feels like the monsters are designed to sell plushies, backpacks, NFT's etc, first and not being scary or unsettling. With poppy playtime it feels like they don't go far enough with the premises of the monsters, Huggy wuggy eats you, Mommy long legs doesn't look enough like a spider, but this game has a pretty simple premise for the characters, what if the sesame street muppets went mad. Being published by DreadXP comes with all of the pedigree it deserves, this is the same publishing studio that published Amanda the adventurer, Spookware and the DreadX collections which are all amazing horror experiences i recommend over something like banban or poppy playtime. I wish the developers luck as they further peruse their careers.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: It's Sesame Evil Resident Street, it's fantastic!Jokes aside, MFN is much more than I had expected. Just "more" everything. The story and characters are great, the levels are fun, the puzzles are interesting, the weapons feel incredible, it's a really great experience. Despite being fairly familiar with survival horror games like Resident Evil and scraping the game, I actually missed quite a few things, so it's designed for even the pros to have a hard time completing it in one run.PRO-TIP: if you're familiar with Resident Evil games, I would recommend going in on the hardest difficulty available. I played on Normal and was drowning in so much ammo and health, I had to start throwing some away to fit key items. Or you can use items way less sparingly, that also works.The story is genuinely sincere, even if very basic with simple morals. But that's the point and part of its inspirations, so who could fault the game for that? By being so sincere about it, it's hard to not feel its endearing moments touch you. Which may be an odd thing to say for a survival horror game, but MFN isn't a highly scary game. It got me tensed up a few times, absolutely, but don't come in this expecting a ton of scares, just vibes and tension.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: Don't be fooled, this is not a mascot horror game. This is just a really great resident evil 7 like.I especially recommend it if you need something to scratch that resident evil itch.Just please for the love of god, DON'T ever play on friendly mode. I'm not saying this because I think it's too easy, I'm saying it because the mode is bugged and if you grab any cheat tapes on it then you will be locked out of 100% on your game save and will be forced to delete your save file.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: Loved this game, was a joy to 100%. The artstyle and story (if you spend the time revealing it all) hit a lot harder than expected. The horror aspect wears off pretty quick due to how quirky the characters are. It's definitely worth playing through a 2nd time on a lot harder difficulty to get a real feel for the urgency of the game and how scare ammo can be. Don't leave a review on many games but this one stands out
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: A very fun game that reminds me of when games were good. This is no doubt a survival horror, while it might not be as scary as Resident Evil or Silent Hill, it definitely scratched that itch for me. It also has Bioshock-esque undertones too.I completed the game in around 6 hours but I still have secrets to unlock.I definitely recommend if you want a well-crafted horror game for an afternoon or two!
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: What an excellent indie horror game. Very much in the Resident Evil mould. The puppets essentially serve as roadblocks to solving the major puzzles in each area, but they are always hilarious and definitely creepy. Everything here from the story, to the voice acting and music, to the creativity with the weapons, and just the overall enjoyable gameplay deserve your attention and money. I look forward to seeing what these guys do next.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: This game kinda proves that survival horror actually works without horror.It's overall a competent survival horror game, however it's quite an overrated game.Simply because the game seems to try to be annoying as possible more often than not. Why?-after pretty much every door you get a loading screen (just like in RE1 I guess, but this is just a terrible idea in a modern game)-biggest problem is that every single enemy respawns after re-entering a room, unless you used a duct tape on a defeated enemy but those are super rare. So yeah, great idea having to refight enemies over and over again in a survival horror game where ressources are scarce. At the same time this basically means that you can cheese enemies by just making it to the next door while ignoring them, completly resetting them-every time an enemy damages you, your character gets thrown to the ground, again annoyingBesides that some words about the difficulty: I made my first run on Survival difficulty which is the 3rd out of 5 difficulties. It was pretty tough for a first playthrough but doable. Still I would recommend doing the first run on normal.But then the two highest difficulty are that hard that you basically need the ingame cheats to beat them, especially when you want to get S-rank on those.If you are big fan of the genre and don't mind those annoyances, you can grab it in a (big) sale.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: It's a surprisingly fun and competent survival horror game. You wouldn't expect something like that from a game where life sized puppets chase after you. The atmosphere is nice, the combat and puzzles are fun and the puppets are hilarious. Their constant and demented rambles might annoy some people, but I found it amusing.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: This is the game I am looking for when I'm on the watch for an indie game. They have built a pretty unique world one with this. The level design reminds me of the n64/ps2 era where is a small open world game, which is great and think more games should come back to. It seems pretty influenced from the original resident evil games in terms of combat mechanics and puzzles. This game is pretty puzzle heavy and they are the perfect level of difficulty in my opinion. I have completed one play through and there are a few puzzles and secrets left unsolved which I indent to play again to take another stab at. At the 30 dollar price point I feel like this game is worth it. I will be following these developers and look forward to a sequel or their next new game.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: It's finally good to see a "mascot horror" game where the mascot actually looks like something kids would like. If you showed a kid one of the neighbors, without the horror context, they'd probably love the hell out of them. Also, no jumpscares. Everything that spooks you happens naturally. Good game. Give it a try if you like survival horror or Jim Henson stuff.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: If you want to see some actual gameplay (or maybe the whole Let's Play), look no further: This game got most traditional elements from the original Resident Evil games and plays like a true survival horror game. Instead of zombies you fight the Muppet Show... or Sesame Street, or both. Which is something that one has to get used to.There's the limited inventory and item box, the maps you have to take from the walls, health items, weapons, puzzles and more. For Survival Horror fans I suggest picking the "survival" difficulty. The game isn't particularly hard (so far) and would probably be a little bit boring if it was easier. There's two more difficulties, but they are locked, probably until after you finished it.If there's some criticism to be had then I'd say that attacking in melee feels a little bit weird, since you have to do it from a little bit too far away (or else you get grabbed). And to be completely honest I do still prefer Zombies and Monsters to Sockpuppets, but that's me. I'm just weird like that.If you like Survival Horror games and don't mind fighting Ernie & Bert, I can recommend this game, and I'll update this review once I'm through.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: great game, better than most of the slog mascot-horror games that wanna be puzzles to solve instead of focusing on being a game first, not that its perfect i especially hate how short the last area was a hallway and a boss way too short, and the game is not scary at all, think resident evil style gameplay meet bioshock which is not a con by the way i liked it that way, it helps to reinforce the themes and story of the game, it almost feel like a deconstruction of the mascot-horror which i think was the intention, anyway i wholeheartedly recommend playing this game you wont regret it
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: MFN is an absolutely fantastic game for old and new fans of classic Resident Evil 1 style survival horror, can be played by the most jaded of RE fans or kids trying to get into horror at a young age but not wanting anything too scary, it's all there ripe for the picking My Friendly Neighborhood's one of the newest mascot horror-esque titles with survival horror deeply rooted in its genes, so I'd go as far as to say this belongs in a new subgenre; mascot survival horror - recognizable antagonists in a setting where your resources are limited and you have to pick your fights carefully all the while solving puzzles.[Premise]You play as Gordon O'Brian, a repairman for the Sprocket Palm repair company commissioned by the City Network Broadcasting Group to turn off the antenna at the vacant MFN studio, as it's begun broadcasting the titular children's show over regular programs. [Gameplay] You make your way through the many areas of the studio slowly getting to the antenna all the while avoiding the puppet characters who've become a bit starved for company over the many years since the show was cancelled and the premises were abandoned. You also encounter "boss" characters, who're more just environmental hazards. MFN plays a lot like RE7 and RE8 rolled into one with a bit of RE1. You play in first person with an attache case inventory system, being able to rotate and arrange key items, ammunition and recovery items within the available item spaces or deposit them in item boxes in save rooms. Save rooms have the classic typewriter save system where you need a currency to save your game, in this case save stations are like work punch cards where you insert coins as your currency. The difference being that you also can insert a coin in a heal station as well unlike in RE games. You have a few types of weapons throughout the game, most notable being the pistol-like tool you use, being fed rolodex letter cards as ammo. The game contains some interesting puzzles, some not seen before, some pretty in-line with what we've seen before, all the fun stuff. The puppets themselves don't patrol the areas they're stationed at and don't attack unless you approach them. A standout feature of the game is how full of personality the puppets themselves are. They have several minutes of interesting dialogue, all mostly warped versions of the lessons they'd be regurgitating to kids in the show itself, some being a bit questionable but funny. Only real disappointment I had with those was how every character essentially repeats those same lines with some lines being changed up to give it their own spin, but I guess they'd be doing that in the show anyway. They make a large part of the enjoyment factor of the game, including their goofy animations. The story doesn't have any big pitfalls or twists, but it's well paced and wrapped up nicely in a way that doesn't make it too cliche or generic for the genre. It provides a good message to its players that can be appreciated in reality as much as in its story.[Closing thoughts]Overall, I'd say this game is very much worth playing if you just want a good time and wanted to see what Sesame Street Resident Evil was like, and boy does it pull it off well. Easy 7/10. Story, gameplay, music and secrets are all solid and keep the game consistent in quality. You can buy at full price if you want, or wait for sale. I'd personally grab it at full to support the dev because if this is his debut title, I'm not sure how much higher we can go from here
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: I loved my time in the Neighbourhood. It's a very well designed Resident Evil-style game with a fresh presentation. The combat is punchy, and figuring out how all the levels interconnect is extremely satisfying. It may not be particularly scary (And I don't think that's really the point), but it is quite tense and rich in atmosphere. Playing this game is a no-brainier if you love the design philosophy and tropes of survival-horror.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: If you told me this wasn't a "children's show turned horror" shlock I'm used to seeing and instead an insanely enjoyable Resident Evil tribute: I wouldn't have believed you. Because I didn't. This game is a blast if you're a fan of the Resident Evil series. You will see references ABSOLUTELY EVERYWHERE! Anywhere from RE4 attache cases, to RE1 mansion hallway layouts, an ode to the RE7 save music, the RE1 bathtub zombie, consumables used for saves, and much, much more.It's a solid survival horror that's worth your time, but do know it's a 6-8 hour jaunt for $25 if you plan on just playing it once.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: This has been one of my favorite games of this year by far. The charm and nostalgia that this game brings me are wonderful. I grew up watching the Muppets and Sesame Street in the early 2000s and this game pulls on those strings very well. It's not super long but has lots of options for replay-ability. It very obviously takes a lot of inspiration from the resident evil series and while not a insanely scary game there were some jump scares and the tension was built very well.  I would recommend this game wholeheartedly.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent "Resident Evil Lite" that manages to capture nearly everything great about survival horror in a tight package. On top of that, it's got tons of secrets and extra content - and all this before we even talk about the unique setting that sets it apart. I highly recommend visiting the Friendly Neighborhood and making some new friends!
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: One of the top Survival Horror games coming out of DreadXP! I've been waiting for this game for a long time, and it did NOT disappoint! Chatty enemies, fun level designs, not too hard to get the good ending, but not too easy, either! LOTS of secrets to find, and it allows you to change ALL YOUR SETTINGS, BEFORE BOOTING THE GAME UP!
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: After hours of playing, I'm kind of torn on this one. It runs great and the graphics look good. The puppets say all kinds of crazy stuff that's fun starting out, but gets old/repetitive after a while. Why am I here doing all of these puzzles? First, I didn't know the entire game would be puzzles. That sucks, but I thought I was making a delivery. I wasn't captured. I just walked in and started solving puzzles. Why are there puzzles anyway? Where are all the people at? Would be more interesting if I went to make the delivery and noticed the puppets had taken everybody hostage. Then I had to rescue everybody. Anyway, I read a couple reviews that said this was too linear. You're in the same space but there is no set path. I have been everywhere wondering around trying to figure out what to do. It's a lot of slow running around to pad the runtime. I wish it was linear. It's weird to say this, but this game is too long for what it is. Should've been 3 hrs tops for $10. Probably be fun to speedrun.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: i have to actually admit i was skeptical about how this would turn out as a horror game but honestly after been playing 20 plus hours of this game and gotten to know the Muppet's and the objectives and puzzles as it being a Comedy clone of Resident Evil i have to say im honestly impressed and i can understand the Psychological horror in the game since....well...don't have a whole room with these muppet's and listen to what there all saying cuz its a Jumbled mess and...yeah it will drive you nuts if you got good headphones. I love the fact that some key muppet's here are special characters as well that serves as a side-quest to, that i adored the most cuz it was wholesome. Also damn fine way to make creative weapons who here now said that "Words don't hurt". I got nothing bad to say here this gets a thumbs up from me WELCOME TO THE NEIGHBORHOOD !!!!P.S: I can't imagine how the Voice actors must have laughed there heads off in between voice line shoots for the muppet's that would be fun to see XD
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: Genuinely a fantastic game.Reminds me of the old RE games with a dash of 7 to the mix. Like most RE games it is short once you understand the game but man I had far too much fun learning its puzzles and avoiding enemies to save up resources. Story was rather poignant for a game about puppets trying to hug you to death. Highly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: I picked up this game even though I'm usually not a fan of mascot horror, but WOW this is fantastic! The gameplay is rewarding and has that satisfying survival horror feel when finding health items or ammo. The graphics and audio are top notch. I encountered zero bugs while playing and, all in all, had a blast! If you like survival horror, you NEED to play this game. In addition, getting the true ending is actually feasible on a first playthough. Just be observant and take your time to explore each area. I managed to get the best ending without using guides or YouTube. I just played the game normally, taking the time to read the notes and being sure to pay attention to any environmental cues. I am really looking forward to the next game from this developer!
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: This was an experience I was never expecting and I absolutely loved it.Muppets/Sesame Street meets horror with game-play Resident Evil style.While I wouldn't truly say it is scary, the entire premise is just ludicrously creepy!Don't miss this one; it has the creep factor, it has the cute factor and it really has the amusing factor all rolled into one.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really quite good!  The campaign on Normal can be completed in about 3-4 hours, but the story is good, the characters loveable, and the message is wholesome.  It take the idea of Mascot Horror and helps you remember, they're still lovable mascots.  Graphics aren't at a AAA level, but to be honest, that's part of the charm.  I found myself laughing at some of the characters and their lines more then once, and it really left me with the impression that maybe the world needs to be a little more "Friendly".
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent new game, i love the art style, the play style, and nearly everything! the only thing that frustrates me is the inventory - which is, at least comparable to my limited knowledge, like resident evil-style inventory, which has always frustrated me lol. but its easy enough to work around, so just a minor thing!!! please play this game!
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: I was hoping to write a thumbs up review for the game as I am enjoying the concept, the humour, and design.Playing on normal difficulty, the combat is extremely frustrating, the longer you are in an area, and moving back and forth between rooms the more hits the enemies seem to take to knock downAttacks with the wrench seem to only connect 25% of the time, it's hard to tell what the correct distance to connect with an enemy in melee is.I feel the hit boxes could be tweaked a little to improve this somewhat.I don't mind the combat being a little clunky, as it is a survival horror, so you're supposed to have to think rather than run in and gun everything down.  Having to use duct tape to tie an enemy so they don't get back up whilst re entering rooms is a nice touch.But the number of hits needed to bring the "cannon fodder" down seems to vary wildly between 3 hits and 10. (Especially if you have already knocked them down once).Good luck if you are being pursued, the enemy attacks will interrupt yours every time, seems that if you are too close to an enemy you will miss every time you try to shoot or melee bash the bastards.I do feel there is a good amount of ammo hidden around, however i'm not that far into the game in an early area, and I'm running out because of how much is needed to put enemies down for the second or third time.Once again just a little tweak to the hit boxes for melee would be nice, to compensate for enemies becoming damage sponges.

_childDocuments_.review: Horror has long been my favourite genre, but most mascot horror leaves me cold; streamer-friendly reaction-bait rarely makes for an engaging experience without an audience to act up to. This game really subverted my expectations by having more in common with recent instalments of the Amnesia franchise - you manage dwindling resources to overcome obstacles while solving the puzzles that'll open the next area. The resources in question here aren't fuel and matches, but ammo and duct tape - and instead of holding off the antagonists with light, you do it by permanently spending resources to restrain them. This is interesting both mechanically (you have to consider who is worth spending the supplies on to disable) and atmospherically (restrained enemies stay where you left them, singing to themselves and talking to their echoes). The enemies, despite looking like the Muppets, are actually genuinely creepy and demented at times, continuously babbling to themselves or their long-lost audience about learning to count by swallowing their own hands and what it's like to live inside the TV. The first one I encountered hurled me across the room and then chased me yelling "LET'S BE EXCELLENT! LET'S BE EXCELLENT!", throwing me into a clumsy fleeing panic. The voice work really shines in these situations - the actors did a superb job. I would say that the character of the protagonist is a bit undercooked, with a traumatic backstory hinted at but not really explored; the various puppets have significantly more personality and notes scattered around the environment explain the decline of their show and the events around it. Fortunately, I cared so much about the situation around these defective Sesame Street lookalikes that my avatar's motivations weren't really important. If you're curious about what a horror game without any gore and offering solutions not exclusively centred around violence would look like, this is absolutely worth your time. The combat isn't the best, and there's a decent amount of backtracking involved, but that's a small price to pay for spending time in such a brilliant and creative setting with such a great script.

_childDocuments_.review: I got this as a gift from a friend who asked to watch me play it. I went into the game without watching any playthroughs or even watching trailers. I was told it was a spooky game with puppets and I just assumed mascot horror. While it is a little spooky in places, I'd hesitate to call it mascot horror because that conjures certain expectations. There are clear inspirations at work in the game's design. The theme is very much Sesame Street, the gameplay is extremely first person Resident Evil games. The theme lends itself to some creative environments and character designs that feel nostalgic but are a bit unsettling. You see a Sesame Street-like set, which feels familiar and friendly, but the off hours time of day, the aggressive puppets saying creepy lines, and the backstage off camera areas add a lot of uneasiness. Gameplay is fairly simple. You collect keys and things to solve puzzles, you pick up health and weapons, and you fight puppets. Enemies can be knocked out, but they awaken again if you leave the load zone and come back. The combat isn't that in depth, but it doesn't really need to be. The puzzles are fairly simple but may require some backtracking or thinking. The game's biggest strengths to me were its characters and story. I don't want to say too much for fear of spoiling it, but this isn't a "possessed puppets" or "eldritch horrors" kind of game. There are moments that genuinely tugged at my heartstrings, and I wasn't expecting that. It actually made me see the world of the game in a new light and kind of felt like it shifted the genre in some scenes.I've gotten two of the four endings and about half of the achievements, so I'm going to be doing at least another playthrough or two. I think my first playthrough was around eight hours, but I'm one of those people who likes to go slow and explore. Overall, a very good time.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished My Friendly Neighborhood and it was a truly bizarre, fun, and tense experience that wasn't what I thought it was gonna be. The Good:I think this game really works as a good intro to other survival horror games, and it deeply reminds me of many of my other favorite games (Psychonauts, Hypnospace Outlaw, and Resident Evil 1/2 principally). This game really feels like a Muppets adaptation of a resident evil/biohazard game, (complete with scary dogs and eye-centric bosses on the resi side, and the story revolving around a human protagonist/ the kind of energy that a classic Jim Henson production exudes).The Bad:I have some nitpicks, I wish that some areas were a bit brighter, puzzles a bit clearer (glares at the ), but really I just wish there was more game! I really was having a blast, and was slightly disappointed by how quickly it ended. I think the price is a bit too steep for the hour count (about six hours for me but you 100% can get a shorter time if not doing side objectives), but I suppose cheat tapes push back against that a bit. The Mascot Horror:I do think, at the end of the line, this is probably my favorite mascot horror game on the market. The current state of indie horror is something many people complain about, with some critisisms being made in ernest (poppy playtime NFTs having story elements locked behind them is actually abhorrent from a moral/art perspective) and others being made just because people don't understand what a game is going for. I think MFN has a very clear vision, and some people will not like it simply because it is not as graphic, directly violent, or serious as its contemporaries. I actually think this is a really good selling point and a look at 'responsible' mascot horror that know its audience might be on the younger side, without ever talking down to that audience. TLDR: MFN is a game I can imagine cool parents introducing to kids interested in horror, as the game can effortlessly balance clever scares with kooky humor and the strangest theme of hope and kindness in an unkind scenario.also im really tired so if this is illegible call my therapist: (866) 901-2739

_childDocuments_.review: My Friendly Neighborhood was my most anticipated game of 2023. Knowing John's previous work and the amazing work Dread XP have published in recent years I couldn't have asked for a better duo. After completing my first run of the game I'm delighted to say I can't wait to dive in for more. Puzzle design, safe rooms and much more feel so expertly plucked from the original Resident Evil games. Combined with a comically colorful aesthetic its almost impossible not to love My Friendly Neighborhood.Even though Dead Space, Dead Island 2 and Resident Evil 4 all released this year I'd still recommend My Friendly Neighborhood before any of them. I just can't escape how intriguing and inspired this whole concept is. On one small note, the QA team have done a fantastic job overall with the game. While I encountered a few moments where my frame rate dropped (mainly the main house in Stage 4), the general performance of My Friendly Neighborhood is stellar. I really hope the QA team get a well deserved pat on the back.Alongside this, John and Evan Szymanski have not only created a intriguing visual design for My Friendly Neighborhood but also accompanied it with an engaging and at times reflective narrative. Overall, please play this game. If you're worried about the survival-horror tag, rest assured this is arguably more spooky at times than it is outright horror (I mean that with the highest praise).

_childDocuments_.review: It's a very GAMEY video game. By that I mean, it has elements that like resident evil, where you can tie up the enemies with duct type, just how in RE 1 you could burn the bodies so they don't come back, or in RE 2 you can shoot a zombies legs off so you don't kill them to preserve ammo, and so on and on. Definitely recommend to any survival horror enjoyers, and cheers to the Szymanski brothers; they did an excellent job at this and I can't wait to see what else they've got in store!

_childDocuments_.review: Let me open by commenting on how wonderful this game is while combining genres that I would have never imagined put together. A Sesame Street x Resident Evil game is just the kind of passion project that I expect to come out of the indie game development scene. I had a blast going through it and it really unlocked a good sense of nostalgia in the back of my brain. I could even smell this game! Anyone who ever went to a children's museum growing up will know what I'm talking about. The musty air, with the scent of wax and paint. The feeling of public access plastic toys, and the spotlights that drags attention to the next curious object. It was like I was with my grandma again on a weekend after school. I cannot thank the dev team more for sending me back to those wonderful memories.Of course, this game isn't without its flaws and I would like to get into the more troublesome ones here.Since this game is a riff on the current Resident Evil formula a lot of the User Interface is the same, however with the implementation of some other gimmicks that the team has added to the controls, some sacrifices had to be made. This means if you are an avid Resident Evil fan you may find that many of the key binds are very different in this game by comparison. I recommend that a player change the controls at the start if they are confusing to remember. I tried about mid-way to change them and found that I had royally screwed myself over as now I was getting used to the old system but the new system I had created wasn't working either. There is also a bug with the control input screen. It refused to keep the changes that I made to my weapon switch buttons as it would always change one of them to the weapon spin action rather than keep it on weapon change when I left a room. I don't know if it is just with the button I was using or how far the bug extends but I hope that the devs read this and put it on a patch list. Otherwise, the controls are great. I'm also gonna use this time for a suggestion. The toolbox. You get the use of a second toolbox later on but if you go back to a previous save room you, of course, won't have access to items you store in it later on as there is only one toolbox in the room. It would have made more sense if there was a second drawer on the first toolbox and you could unlock with a key or something that opened it up later in the game. This way players could access both boxes anywhere and the team might have saved some time. Its long past the time to change it but I felt it could be something to implement if the team ever works on a similar game or sequel.I would recommend picking this up right away as it is worth the full price and has a good amount of replay-ability.

_childDocuments_.review: Started playing because I was drawn to the Resident Evil-style gameplay and it being on the DreadXP label but was legitimately shocked at just how great and fun this game was.  What seems on the surface to be a pretty lame 'mascot horror' premise for youtubers to scream at is actually (without getting into spoilers) a genuinely sharp, thoughtful, and melancholy rebuttal of the genre that really puts it well above the competition.  For a small team the presentation is incredibly good, with fantastic environment design, animation, and voice acting. The gameplay is a unique fusion of resident evils 1 and 7 and really nails the strengths of each, bringing back classic RE staples like limited saves and methods to permanently stop enemies respawning.  Felt compelled to review this as I'm sure many people will have written it off as blurring into a million other "what if kids show evil" games, but it really doesn't deserve that. Let's be excellent!

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic survival horror game, that knowingly leans into it's own comedic setting. You'll be exploring the studios and solving very familiar Resident Evil style puzzles, all whilst managing your supplies and planning when and where to engage enemies or even save the game.On the topic of enemies, most respawn when moving between rooms, but you can tape them up to keep them a non-threat on repeat visits. It's very similar to the crimson heads of the Resident Evil remake where you have to pick and choose your fights and plan the routes you'll be using often. I feel this game handles it better, as the enemies don't grow more powerful, but will still eat away at your supplies every time you go through them.Shares some similarities with games like Undertale in how  Will be revisiting the neighborhood again soon, there's so much to still discover and see, with many unlockable cheats and bonus modes to unlock.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: This game is different but entertaining in many ways.As far as the story goes, without too many spoilers, its a very nice little reflection on how things are in their type of business and those feelings behind itFor gameplay its nice taste of locations and puzzle gameplay that isnt too hard but has some really fun and overall well done secrets to fill in just about every space so nothing is truly blank or empty allowing for some great moments of "Oh so thats what that is for!"For overall replayability there are plenty of modes and funny modifiers that can make things more harder or goofy or maybe just a different experience all togetherId say definitely get this game if you love games like Resident Evil or Security Breach or any of those titles but are looking for something a little more stylized and goofy but evenly driven with a narrative to it that's a little wholesome and creepy at times.

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't like this game. I do, however, recognise that I did not like it for partially subjective reasons. What's more, even with the blatant caveats I'm about to elaborate on, I'd still say that this is a solid game. Just not exactly great. And your expectations should be set to reflect that if you want to have a good time with this one.Looks? Great! Sounds? Even better. How does it play? Smooth and fun, but only when it works and that last bit is the big problem for me (and, I expect, many others). It is clear that this is a labour of love with loads of polish and all of those extra bells and whistles that exist only with projects, for which the creators truly care. The problem with MFN (because I refuse to spell out this game's name one more time in full, but I'll get to why in a bit) is that said polish is practically applied only at a surface level.There are two core issues with this title: level design and puzzle design. The devs have taken a lot of the right queues when they were getting inspired for this one. I won't lie: I came here because I was told that I might like this game since I loved games like RE7 and 8. And while I can see why someone would say that, I must say that some bits were lost in translation.Okay then, what's the deal with level design? Well, it's simple, really: this game attempts to be a FPS metroidvania, just like the aforementioned greats, however it fails at one key component: satisfaction. Great metroidvanias work because they make you feel like you are exploring and figuring stuff out. Hence: backtracking is not an issue when you know what you are doing. And I never really felt like that with this game. More often than not, I felt like it was wasting my time. Don't get me wrong: the environments were lavish and inspired, but all of the mechanics therein entwined just don't make sense for this style of game. And I can't really continue talking about that without bringing in puzzle design into the mix. It's simple, really: you have to have one of those odd minds in order to enjoy this game's puzzles. To me? Torture. Every time I felt a puzzle coming up, I cringed and audibly signed. All of them were great ideas that weren't explained properly and I didn't enjoy a single one. The bad news? There's a lot of them. So where do these two clash? You get to do a puzzle that you probably won't like just so you can backtrack a long way, losing resources along the way due to one of the game's core mechanics, only to continue working on another puzzle that, let's face it, you're probably going to hate. All of this meant that I couldn't actually close my browser. This is why I said earlier that I refused to spell out the game's full name one more time. I mean, if you're going to make a game that needs a guide to be beaten, at least make it easy to spell, right?I constantly had to look things up, because nothing was properly explained. Obviously, this amounts to a huge UX issue that I'd wager is more universal than not. I think that this is a huge learning opportunity for the devs and one that they should pick up on, because -- I'll be honest -- when this game works, it's a blast. I hate games where I can't trust the narrative or design to guide me through the adventure. I hate having to break my session up to reference external media just to make it through. At the same time, I kept hoping that more cool stuff would happen, but all for naught: the story is, ultimately, quite lacklustre and even nonsensical at times. But it was cool. It was fluid and enjoyable when it worked. And the game's length is just perfect: all narrative-driven games should have their main campaigns take 5-6 hours to beat, that's just such a sweet spot. I appreciate the effort enough to recognise that while I hated a large chunk of all of this, there is a ton to love here. And I hope to see another, more polished game just like this from the same team. Hence: I'm not downvoting this. But I am highlighting some issues so that players like me can decide what's best for them.  Here's the takeaway: If you're here for another FPS metroidvania: you won't get that with MFN. If you're here for an exploration based action game: not much of that either. While MFN fails at some aspects, it does establish something else through which it manages to stand on it's own two feet. If you feel like you have some extra time to figure stuff out or you don't mind following guides: you might like this one.But I didn't. And I'm very happy I beat it, so I never have to play it again. But I will be keeping an eye out on what this dev team will be up to in the future.And for anyone like me, who is pondering weather to try it: you might. But you might end up watching most of it on YouTube anyway, so consider if you're hungry or not beforehand. Because I would've totally binged a vid if I knew what I was getting myself into.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game. For years ive been looking for a game that balances Game play, Story, Graphics, and Horror. And this is the game. I played the demo when i was looking for something to play and the demo was a great first experience for me and i recommend it if you want to try it for yourself. I wouldn't call this a horror game though. Its more like a survival shooter? its doesn't focus on just one thing. Theres puzzles that make you question your own intelligence, Theres combat encounters where you scramble together your little ammo and resources to fight off the incoming puppets.Theres going from room to room looking for every secret and duct tape. I almost never had to search up an answer to a puzzle i could solve, I would tinker around with it and look at it in a different perspective and then it would just CLICK. One puzzle that took me a lot of attempts was the Card game in the Offices against a Norman. The inventory system is amazing and you have to take into consideration what can and cant fit in your storage. So i find myself needing a quest item to take somewhere but dont have the space then i organize the items in it to see if it can fit now. Or when you find a toolbox to see what you want to take with you, i think about what is more important to keep or not. The layout of each room feels like it always serves a purpose for the gameplay and the lore, A room you finally unlock with a new key could contain a cheat disc or a loot stache to help you on your next encounter. The main locations are a 10/10! With each one introducing a new enemy or mechanic to help you. And you will find yourself going in between the same couple rooms and finding something new in one where you didnt see it before. Then by the end of the area you know the map like the back of your hand. You memorize what puppets are in which room and if they are taped up or not.Then even when you move on to the next area and want to revisit the ones before you see some enemies that appear there or a secret you can now unlock.The enemies are amazing to fight! You have your base normal enemies that walk slowly towards you and your mini puppets that jump off walls to attack you in a group and overwhelm you. And theres also special enemies who are only in 1 area and have their own way of attacking you, Like the gobbler who runs at you in a straight line trying to eat you, or Pearl who blindly walks around and could step on you, And Ray hides in pipes waiting for you to walk in front of it so he can hit you. Sometimes i would enter a room and see a "dead" puppet and then once i cleared the room it would jump alive and attack me. Its times like that where i am caught off guard and love that the devs are shaking up the game play with surprises like that.Now the Cons :(Ammo is so hard to find that i found myself with only a couple bullets and cant go through a room of enemies without sacrificing a couple health potions. I think that on the lower difficulty's there should also be more ammo along with the easier enemies.Settings. I feel like i could optimize my game more if i had more leeway to tinker around with my graphical settings, And i had this constant bug that resets my hz down to 60 every time i enter a room (my normal hz is 165) and its really annoying having to switch it back constantly.Thats it. A short list of cons but ones that break the gameplay. Everything else is perfect. Thank you developers for this game that hit a special place in my heart.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty damn good! It’s another game in the ever present “mascot horror” subgenre, but I think this game nails the somewhat creepy atmosphere without ever trying too hard to be scary. It plays with the ridiculous setting and never tries to make it something it’s not, and instead of focusing on trying to scare you it aims for making the puzzles and exploration fun which I think it succeeds at.My main issue is that the combat feels a bit wonky since your melee attack animation makes it hard to gauge your range, and a lack of a crosshair is never fun for shooting IMO (although maybe theres a crosshair option in the settings? I haven’t checked). However this complaint is minor as combat isn’t really a major component of the game, you just smack a guy a few times and are done - overall, I’m having fun.

_childDocuments_.review: My friendly neighborhood sent me back to my toddler days of running around with my favorite blanky while eating a banana. That feeling was fleeting, I quickly became overwhelmed with panic. I had to quickly find my ABC gun so I could stop the scary muppets from attacking me. My flashbacks of sesame street while playing the game was unnerving. I so badly wanted to feel safe with the familiar set that I grew up watching. Those feelings distracted me to the point that I didnt realize,  I was being hunted my a giant bird. I now have beef with every muppet in this game and I WILL prove to them and myself that I will SURVIVE!

_childDocuments_.review: When it comes to Resident Evil inspired games this game gets it so right,It takes a page out of the recent releases of 7 and 8 and then gives it a comedy spin.The writing, characters, game play and puzzles are so masterfully created I couldn't stop playing, and I even after beating the game I'm gonna keep playing until I have seen everything this title has to offerhonestly one of my favourite indie game released in a hot minute the only downside I can think of is the melee weapon is incredibly underpowered but other then that fantastic game, I highly recommend
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly feels like its made for people who don't play video games. Playing on the default hardest difficulty inundates you with health items and ammo in a game that already has 0 horror atmosphere to begin with due to its insistence on chatty sesame street enemies that shove you over at worst. Yes, I am aware that this was done to be in line with its theming concerning the morality of fiction, but the artistic elements are incredibly shallow in that sense and only serve to prevent the tension and dread that survival horror is meant to induce.In terms of raw gameplay the puzzles are incredibly simplistic and the combat is clipped-on. There are a handful of weapons that you use on a total of 4 actual enemies (Walking puppet, stationary mini-puppet, pipe guy, dog), but encounters are so basic its difficult to think of them as anything but a tape/ammo tax the couple of times you can't run past an enemy. The two bosses are defeated by throwing a grenade and running in a circle, which gets back to my original point. I can't think of a single actual "puzzle" come to think of it as they're all either direct directions given to you by the game or plopping down items on pedastals (I guess you had to flip the blocks to spell "neighbor" in the early game). I think I did two secret-ending related puzzles which, likewise, were just following directions but I cannot be bothered to go back and finish that ending.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: Ok alright I know the word "Mascot Horror" is thrown around alot these days, but I assure you this game is not thrown together for quick money. Actually interesting mechanics that call back to classic and modern survival horror from the likes of RE 1, 4, and the recent ones/remakes. Its not exactly trying too hard to be "scary" as there is more emphasis on fun, puzzles, and the stress of item/resource management and dealing with the threats that are currently in the room. There are some jumpscares and "certain things" that I would much rather have you find out yourself, but that's it in terms of pure horror. The story is also great, it makes you really care about everyone, the murderous puppets included. My only criticism is that I would've wanted more, like maybe one more "chapter", but I don't think wanting more is a bad thing because that just means the developers built a fantastic game. I don't do reviews often, but I want to emphasize how great this game is. For a handful of people working on it, this game turned out really good and I would like to see more. I doubt there will be any more to this universe (DLC, Sequel, etc.) but I'll be hyped for the next game if these guys decide to do more.I doubt its easy to implement, but I think it would be really cool if a workshop or map editor gets implemented at some point, you know something the community can use to make custom stuff. Even if its a basic map editor using pre-existing assets that would be cool.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: Haven't played it that long yet, but I love the premise. It is the reason why I have followed the development over twitter for so long. Even though I haven't gotten to play any resident evil game yet, the inspiration is clear and greatly executed.Even though I have seen some small issues like performance dipping in a huge room with a lot of props and enemies and once clipping through a wall when trying to fight an enemy after first getting the wrench, I wholeheartedly believe that these issues will get fixed soon, considering it is less than 24 hours after launch.Overall it is just a great concept and the execution seems really well done so far.So please do yourself a favor and check this one out if the premise seems even slightly interesting.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: I had so much fun with this game! I played through it normally once, did a glitchless handgun-only speedrun on survivor difficulty, and then got a little crazy and blasted my way through the hardest difficulty with the infinite ammo cheat code and some other silly stuff.Pros:- Very strong story- Rewarding gameplay loop of sneaking, fighting, looking for loot, deciding which enemies to permanently subdue, then deciding where to go next- Enemies are immensely satisfying to shoot. They ragdoll and sail through the air because they're puppets. Genius- Puzzle difficulty feels just right, with a good mix of easy, medium, and hard puzzles- Tons of secret bonus content to find and unlock- Production quality here is impressive. Beautiful art direction, full voice acting and nice animations- Runs very smoothly. I didn't encounter any stability or performance problems during my 3 full playthroughs of the gameCons:- Melee doesn't feel great. It's clearly intended only as a risky last resort, so I understand why it's designed like this, but it still feels difficult to predict your range and when you are about to get grabbed by an enemy- Game length is about six to eight hours for a first playthrough, depending on how much exploring you do. I actually feel like this is a good length for a story game but I hear a lot of people dislike games this short, so fair warning- Light on horror, despite its horror inspirations. Again, this isn't necessarily a bad thing but it will disappoint some peopleOverall rating: 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great. It's not the immersive sim or the horror game I expected when I saw the first trailer ages ago. It's a decent Resident Evil 1 homage with a surprisingly sincere story. I liked how the game consistently treats the puppets as sort-of people and doesn't really revel in violence against them as most games with enemies would (there's no stuffing coming out of them or limbs coming off). Really hope this is the start of a series, could use more of this.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: It's a Breath of Fresh Air for Survival Horror that Subverts & Deconstructs your typical "Mascot Horror" tropes; with their being a More Heartwarming & Wholesome message; And how this Plays like Resident Evi; with the Inventory Management, the Puzzles, deciding whether or not to tape the puppets to the floor with your limited tape, as well as how much of your limited amounts of ammo to use at any moment; and You can actually shoot the Puppets trying to hug you to death. . .It also shows us how Bleak the Timeline where Sesame Street's positive & moral & uplifting messages fell on deaf ears from an audience too jaded from this universe's version of the Vietnam War to even care; and Even Worse; it's a Universe where Mr. Rogers ACTUALLY became a General in the military; as such we never got that Wholesome Mr. Rogers' Neighborhood show in this even worse timeline[that's even worse earlier on than our own current timeline]I Also love how my Favorite Muppet Youtuber: Arlo voices one of the Characters; Ricky the Sock puppet!!
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game. To be perfectly honest, It's not scary in the slightest, but I don't think it's meant to be. It's more like a tongue-in-cheek horror survival game. The game mechanics are quite fun and it just oozes inspiration from Resident Evil games. You can also tell that the developers stayed within their capabilities and vision without overextending, which is something I always like to see in indie games.I would recommend this game for people who like horror survival mechanics like in the Resident Evil games and want to play something unique. That said, I would not recommend this to people who want a scary experience since it's more slightly creepy and you won't really get any unexpected frights.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: the concept, although very common, is fun, and the theme-ing is GREAT! but the game is just really lackluster. Decided to do survival difficulty cause I have played these RE style games many times, but it plops you in a world and gives you almost no clue to where to go, so you're just wandering til you get a weapon and/or key. As of today, first day of release, the hitboxes are BROKEN as sh!t. The enemies can grab you and throw you from 10 feet away but you have to be EXTREMELY close to melee them. And when you get the gun you get like absolutely no ammo, at least on survival, and there are very little resources. got to the part on the street set where the bird patrols, but it barely patrols. If it chases you it gives up instantly the second you turn a corner. At least make a threatening enemy. The only thing threatening about this game is how painfully boring and annoying it is. It's fun to make me run around enemies and avoid melee if im out of ammo, but its not fun when the enemies constantly respawn cause tape is rare, and they sit DIRECTLY in the way of anywhere you need to go. TL/DR: Cool theme and style, underwhelming gameplay though. Little resources and enemies constantly being annoying and blocking your path just adds a stale aroma over the style. I'd say wait for a better sale (something less than 20 dollars, or wait for more updates on balancing and hitbox fixes)edit:The dev replied to my neg review basically saying like get good play on normal. Like please sit down and quiet. You are talking to someone who has what is basically YEARS of experience in survival horror. Like I know when something is just "git gud" versus "buggy PoS". Clearly the devs do not. Like I know the low resources and high enemy count is just a simple get good moment, but broken game mechanics is not. I wish them no hate, cause the game looks great on the surface, but delving down and actually playing is just annoying and unfun. I would love if the devs made small changes to the puppet's visuals or audio, actually being able to tell you're doing damage to an enemy cause they either die after 4 shots or 10 shots, and the melee is just nonexistant cause you get grabbed and thrown back every time you get close. Theres no blocking, or dodging or anything of the sort that should make getting caught with no ammo and only a crappy pipe wrench be that devastating. Fix the hitboxes, and I will definitely consider spending 20 dollars on the game, but what its priced at right now is just too expensive for what it is. 4.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: Very similar structure and a clear homage to RE2, the likelihood in level design, puzzles, and backtracking is striking sometimes. decent combat with resource management involved. good voice acting, cute and heartwarming story. very little to no scary moments depending on your tolerance about this.however, it is VERY short. only recommended on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: Although is My Friendly Neighborhood a perfect fit for what we have dubbed the "Mascot Horror" Genre. It doesn't take the same missteps that have so many (including me) disappointed. It's not just a cashgrab, nor is it lacking in real passion for Survival Horror and Mascot Horror respectively. MFN not only delivers a charming, creative and funny game that is very unique. But it's also just a really great Resident Evil style Survival Horror game. All with a nicely crafted story that would be a good influence on the younger audience the game obviously is mildly created for. The back and forth between the happy go lucky inhabitants of the neighborhood and Gordon's hard, cold demeanor make for some really charming moments. Well done Szymanski's. Not only did you make a creative, fun and weird game, you showed everyone that this genre can be genuinely well made and have something interesting to say, even if it's more accessible to younger audiences. "Childrens Movies" shouldn't be dummed down just as much as games for younger audiences shouldn't be.  Also Arlo is a great voice actor in this. Puppet voice for a puppet character!
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: This was fun. Good voice acting. The puppets do get a bit repetitive, but thats unavoidable with common enemies imo. The amount of voice work for all the puppets is impressive for an indie game.Gameplay was fun. I appreciated the level design. Many areas are built around some major threat, and require different approaches to navigate.Not too difficult; started with the Survivor difficulty on my first playthrough and only died twice. I'm sure I could get 0 deaths on a second playthrough. If you're new to the genre, this might be a friendly (:p) entry point.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: Compared to the rest of recent "Mascot Horror" I believe this one stands out the most, and is my favorite recent indie game. The amount of passion and love is clear through the level design, the art of the characters and weapons, UI, etc. Not too much horror, but not lacking in scares, chases, and even sweet messages throughout the story. Fun gameplay, and not too difficult for people who don't play video games often. Everyone should definitely give it a try :)
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: you can tell the devs put a lot of thought and energy into this game! it is unique and charming (in an oddly funny way) despite being a "mascot game", would 100% be hyped for a sequel game with more story-driven or choice-based mechanics! can't get the chaos of the overlapping voice-lines out my head ahahah played through twice after accidentally deleting my save file in the park level (my skill issue though) ps. ricky is the best
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommend, if you like classic survival horror you'll like this.Dont be turned off by the 'mascot horror' aspects, its very much NOT a mascot horror game that relies on cheap jumpscares. Its essentially Resident evil but replace the horror with comedy. Apart from one or two moments the game isn't scary, but its not TRYING to be scary either. Gameplay wise its a stock-standard but very well crafted survival horror game. Semi-open map that opens up more as you progress, puzzle solving your way through the levels and trying to conserver your ammo. In typical survival horror style enemies dont stay down forever, and the resource needed to keep them down is scarce.That said difficulty wise its not too extreme, my first playthrough was on the hardest difficulty available to me (there's two more unlockable difficulties i think), and by the end of the game i was fully stocked with more ammo and healing items than i could use. Of course i imagine this'll change on the even higher difficulties.Replayability wise i'd say its pretty decent, apart from the unlockable difficulties there's achievement hunting and challenges, the game includes a speedrunner mode, there's unlockable cheats like infinite ammo or stronger enemies. I finished my playthrough in about 4 or 5 hours which is a good length for this kind of game. i'll come back in a few months and do another playthrough or hunt some achievements.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: Another Incredible title by the people at Dread XP. The environment you traverse and the characters you encounter will leave you uneasy and concerned when you hear what the puppets are saying. Inventory management, a variety of puzzles, and a riveting story keep you hooked throughout.I streamed this game immediately after it launched and I enjoyed every second of it.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: If you like the Resident Evil series *especially the last 2 new fps ones* you'll love this. It has a lot of soul and you can see the care the dev put into it, I may be only a little bit through but I'm absolutely loving the game! I would say its more off putting and creepy rather than straight horror though but again I'm not done with the story, I found this game watching Gmanlives and was pleasantly surprised it was made by the brother of another developer I like, good ass game!
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: Great puzzle game, but wish there was more horror elements. Maybe sneaking or distractions to help get around. Not sure if I just missed these features, but it seemed like the TVs around would be a cool way to move the puppets around. Bullets felt more like a needed thing rather than a last resort, could just be how the game was designed to be though.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: Who would have thought that a Resident Evil style game with the Muppets would be so much fun!!!The Story is pretty simple but does the job in pushing the game forwards. There are some notes that you can read that give more insight into the world and are actually quite interesting. The characters while there really only being two are pretty entertaining and bounce off one another really well.The setting of the studio is really well layed out and had a good variety of obstacles whether that be puzzles or even certain doors you have to enter. Each has its own feel to it and really adds to the world.Visually, i think that the devs went for the perfect look for this experience. Performance was solid throughout and I didn't run into any bugs or glitches. The Art Direction is spot on and really stands out from the crowd of games this one aligns with. The environments and enemies look so good and are a treat to try and fend off (or even help). The only weird thing is the proportions of the main characters hands as they look really odd, but apart from that the whole experience was great to look at. Sound and Audio are on point with the soundtrack (when there is any) matching the vibe such as the save room with the iconic calming music just like in RE titles. The Audio is also perfect with the way guns fire and even the voice lines of the enemies really standing out and making them feel like they've been ripped out of a tv show.In terms of gameplay, this is a solid survival horror game. Inventory management is on point and adds another level to the gameplay in a pseudo puzzle mini game. Guns and equipment feel great to use and are unique in their design as instead of firing bullets, it is in the form of letters. Enemies are entertaining and can be a challenge, however i will say that while there are some minor differences, it can be hard to see the variety that this game has to offer. There are even certain puppets that you can help out and in doing so will remove certain obstacles which is a really cool twist. While the game might be short when it comes to other run times in the survival horror franchise, there's so many game modes and cheats that players are able to mess around with and give this game endless replay ability.Overall, My Friendly Neighborhood was a delight to play and stands out as a quirky twist on the Resident Evil style of survival horror!
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: Having recently completed the game, and went through finding the secrets that I won't spill here. I can say that MFN is one of my favorite games of all time. It's goofy fun that still manages to get you to jump. It's tons of laughs that also make you reflect on your life a bit. Very fun game to play multiple times over, and the speed run addition really does add hours of replayability. Excited to see the routes people come up with and how they'll break the game. Which is also a mode in the game that leads to many easter eggs. Check outside some rooms when you unlock Free-Roam Mode. I do have some minor gripes such as the random damage/melee range being inconsistent can make some runs frustrating. Quick tip for those starting out. You can kite most enemies, and if they're doing a full flop after getting hit you have a small window of opportunity to run past them without getting grabbed. You can even get the Rolodex and make it to the door early if you figure out a way to speed up. Can't recommend this game enough even if you're just a one and done kind of player. This game will make you want to continue to play it for hours, days, who knows how long?
