_childDocuments_.review: The game is one of the best games that I've played this year, seemingly a critical response to the typical "mascot horror" genre. There's nothing groundbreaking about the game (with an inventory and difficulty system clearly inspired by Resident Evil), but that doesn't diminish its fun or quality. Ducky has done a fantastic job of creating an enjoyable and well-crafted experience without sacrificing integrity. The game can be somewhat short, but part of the charm is the game's repeatability and speedrun capabilities. Those who want a challenge in a unique environment can still find it. Although the designs and concepts might be catered towards a younger audience, I found that it was somewhat refreshing to actually have a straightforward story in a world of theory-crafting and YouTube obsessed lore. If you pay the price of admission, you won't be disappointed.**Mild Spoiler Warning**There are a few criticisms that I have, mainly regarding its difficulty and a few bugs here and there. On occasion, I found that the environments were too compact to avoid enemies (specifically, the dog in the elevator hallway). The final boss fight was somewhat disappointing due to the fact I could easily outpace the boss, and it didn't match the difficulty of the rest of the game. Furthermore, the introduction of the last area was a fantastic and different experience that barely lasted 5 minutes - I wanted it to last longer! There was a lot of atmosphere and excellent environment building that could've been added, and I feel as if it was underutilized. What was there was okay, but definitely the weakest aspect of the game. Most bugs are being fixed currently and weren't present in my playthroughs (except in Freecam mode, but I was technically breaking the game already). That being said, the true ending was excellent and story felt heartfelt and real in our contemporary society, and I really appreciated the story and message it was trying to send.I would recommend the game to anyone looking for fun experience in a quality game..
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: I really wish steam had a neutral review option because this game is great, but has too many flaws to the point where I wouldnt recommend it if you're not a fan of older resident evil games. I really like everything in this game with a small amount of exceptions, for one, the enemies health pools are so inconsistent, sometimes they die in 2 to 3 hits, and sometimes they're bullet sponges that can eat up an entire magazine, second, you have waaaay too low of a health pool for this kind of game, you die in 5 hits which might not sound like a lot, but if theres a room full of enemies that are bullet sponges it makes the early game absolute hell, I just got access to the shotgun and it makes it easier but ammo is so limited that i want to save it and not waste it on one enemy. My other problem is save stations and health restoring areas, I feel like these shouldnt be accessed via a limited resource, saving is crucial because of how much ammo you're going to waste on enemies and how often they'll hit you because theres barely any hitstun for them, and even then they can grab you whilst in hitstun. and being as theres a limited number of token it means you dont want to be saving multiple times in one area, but the gameplay contradicts that style of play because of how annoying the enemies are to kill and how often they respawn, even if you tape a few another will very quickly appear in its place. It's an incredibly fun game but needs more than a few balance patches before I'd give it more than like a 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: In short, this is an amazing achievement for a small indie team and it's exactly what you'd want out of a cross between a children's puppet show and survival horror. It has all the best features from the games that clearly inspired it - crazy puzzles, unsettling characters, interesting locations all tied up in a sort of metroidvania-esque semi-open world similar to games like Resident Evil 7.But it's way more than that. There's a lot of care and detail in here, from the risky decision of when to use your limited duct tape to permanently disable an enemy, to managing your inventory, to the disturbing and frankly hilarious script for the puppet's random mumblings and outbursts. I was also surprised by where the story ended up, and the game's optional content gave the world and its characters so much more depth than I expected (I HIGHLY recommend doing all the optional stuff to get the most enjoyment out of this game!).Gameplay wise, I'll be honest at first I felt like it was a little clunky, but that's because of my own expectations going in. Trust me, the more I played, the more it felt like everything in the game was intentional, that this was the game's intended vibe (and it's NOT a bad thing, it genuinely felt right). It's like a blend of nostalgia and modern survival horror and I loved every minute of it.I rarely replay games once I've reached the credits, but for all the fun and ridiculous unlockable content, I'm pretty sure I'll be coming back to this very, very soon.9.5/10, fully recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: Decent execution on the "Sesame Street/The Muppets meet Resident Evil" premise.  I'd say it's worth $20 or less if you plan to do one playthrough.  Pros:-Lots of Muppet references-Resident Evil 4/8 inventory system-The Ability to discard items that have no more use.-Lots of secretsCons:-Every normal puppet has a lot of the same voice lines, and they repeat them...a lot.-Not really as clever as the muppets (an incredibly high bar)-Not really gritty enough with the horror aspect in my opinion.  Except for one section, and one random puppet a little after you meet ray, they largely just chase and annoy you.  There's a handful of potential jumpscares, but the game is pretty tame overall.  I wish they'd leaned into the "human but not quite human" uncanny valley aspect of the puppets more, just to make it more creepy and unsettling.Overall I think it could have been better, but the puppets are more of a nuisance than scary or a threat.  Still worth a try if the premise grabs you, but set your expectations ahead of time.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just, simply, a good game. I played it, I finished it, and I enjoyed it. It didn't blow my mind, change my life, or make me sit down contemplating my experience for 3 days following the experience. I just simply enjoyed it.As stated many times before, there is a LOT of inspiration from classic Resident Evil in this game. Classic mechanics such as:-Saves requiring an item that is limited-An environment which has segments that is introduced piece-by-piece, then opening up and requiring some back tracking at the end-Occasional "Should I shoot them, or should I avoid them and save ammo" situations.-An eerie, almost oppressive, environment that never feels quite right as you explore-Inventory management, including boxes-More things I forgot to mention here.The game also takes a lot of inspiration from Sesame street with mechanics such as:-Talking puppets-(Attempts at) friendship-various creature-like characters with their own back-stories/occupations.-Phenomenal voice acting that captures the spirit of Sesame street.Combat is fairly straight forward and works well. The story is enjoyable enough to finish the game. The length is fine, I finished in just under 6 hours (I missed one or two things). There is replayability with cheats you can find in game to make things interesting and/or funny. There's various modes to play. There's also an unlockable "Very Hard" difficulty.The game focuses mostly on the puzzles. Again, this feels taken right from a classic Resident Evil game. Requiring some thought and occasionally some back tracking. The puzzles aren't too hard to solve. TL;DR - Overall I definitely recommend the game. Like I first said, it's simply a good fun game that you can enjoy in a night. If you want to get more out of it, there are options to get more out of it. If you're looking for a deep story and complex gameplay, or a difficult game, this won't be what you're looking for.

_childDocuments_.review: When I see a game labeled as “survival horror” I don’t expect it to be a classic survival horror and instead turn out to be a horror themed game of some random genre. So after playing the demo of My Friendly Neighborhood and seeing that it is shaping up to fit the classic survival horror genre pillars, I was pleasantly surprised. And while I wouldn’t name it among the truly good examples of the genre, it’s definitely a descent enough game to scratch that itch and it also has a bunch of cute ideas of its own.Being an example of said genre, you can expect this game to have places to explore in a somewhat metroidvania-ish level design and limited resources to manage while dealing with enemies. Exploring the locations is pretty fun since they are as varied as the setting of the game allowed them to be, while also presenting fun problems to solve and secrets to find. And to game’s credit, apart from a final point of no return, and a couple of permanent location changes, the game allows you to return to old areas with no restrictions and search for things you might’ve missed before or perform additional tasks that couldn’t have been completed the first time you were there.Resources on Normal mode, at least for someone who is well versed with the genre, are extremely plentiful and I’ve had more problems with managing the space for all the crap I had, then running out of things. But, in a way, that’s a me problem – I could select a harder difficulty from the beginning. That said, dealing with enemies in this game is… not great. It’s not terrible by any means, but the way enemies deal damage feels bad, avoiding them isn’t particularly fun and shooting them doesn’t feel good either. So I’m actually glad I didn’t play on a harder difficulty, because I feel that with this kind of combat design, more limited resources would have made my experience not more challenging, but more tedious instead.That said, the whole concept that enemies never “die” and are active again as soon as you enter the room they’re in via a loading transition, unless you tape them up, is pretty cute. However, the fact that you don’t know which doors lead to a loading screen and which do not is bad and can lead to situations where you think you’re opening a “normal” door to quickly check what’s inside and instead get transitioned to a different area, meaning that all enemies that were safely knocked out in that previous room you didn’t fully explore, will be active again when you return. The Silent Hill approach to maps, where you simply don’t see where you are until you find a map item, is also not great as it’s very easy to miss items in the room and without the RE-inspired “room cleared” marking on the map you might never know if you’ve missed something or not.Either way, My Friendly Neighborhood is a pretty nice and enjoyable game with a lot of charm. And it also has a bunch of interesting secrets, unlockables, a New Game Plus mode and other things that can motivate you play it more. It isn’t as memorable and fun as the FPS action adventure with horror theme In Sound Mind and it is also not on the same level of either quality or fun gameplay as Resident Evil 7 it’s most similar to. But it is about on par with Tormented Souls in “understanding what’s fun about the genre” and being a “good enough” example of it that’s worth checking out.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: My Friendly Neighborhood is a masterful mix of modern mascot horror and classic Resident Evil game design. It's full of great humour, odd characters, fun gunplay and some well designed maps and puzzles. The art style evokes the look of classic puppet shows like The Muppets and Sesame Street. It's a decent length too at around 5-6 hours on a first playthrough, and features a ton of secrets to unlock which add extra value to additional runs with new features like infinite ammo and speedrun mode. All in all MFN is well worth the asking price and one of the best horror games I've played this year.

_childDocuments_.review: Since the trailer dropped I had been looking forward to this game for a couple of weeks, I couldn't play it right away and when I saw the positive reception I was more then excited. The game met my expectations....as well as missed some of them. This will contain level spoilers and some story spoilers. So if you want to avoid that please skip my review. But TLDR: While I was dissapointed with some aspects I still had fun with the game! Please check it out! I'm not sure how to black out spoilers, sorry!First things first what I loved about the game: I loved the design, the puppets are simple but detailed enough that if you asked me ten years from now who Junebug was with a photo I'd tell you what she came from. They're charming designs which is hard to pull off considering the sudden surge of horror puppet media and while some of the clothing options were a liitttllee boring I could still recognize what game they're from. Second I loved the design of the studio, mostly, though it is a rather odd place considering this is supposed to be a TV studio but hey what are you gonna do with a game like this? Not suspend your belief? Naaah. I enjoyed the gameplay and like many others said it is like Bioshock is some ways which I don't think is ever a bad thing, but its not quite so good either. Neutral. Either way I liked how the weapons were designed and it was satisfying to shoot Norman in the head. The story was great I liked that we could have helped the puppets, I managed to get the TRUE ending and I'm happy how it ended. This game is full of creativity and I think it's worth it for anyone wanting to check it out. Now what I didn't like: The office portion is way too big. There is too much going on in that one building I often found myself getting lost, though I will admit I'm directionally incapable sometimes. However most of the rooms could have been downsized just a bit to make the long treks back a little less tedious. That's what I would call this section-tedious. I didn't mind having to go back and forward that's a very survival horror thing but when it gets to the point of being rather annoying it's a problem. I also noticed the one boss that covers the main entrance to the office...is way too easy to defeat! I used two bombs! Two! I was on normal it should not have been that easy, but maybe a more balance patch will come out.The wrench is also useless. No matter what I did I couldn't use it against a single puppet, I don't know if I was just bad at swinging it but I never landed a hit. All I got was a couple puppet hugs and damage for trying. And then the one thing I'm absolutely disappointed in (Don't hate me game devs! I promise I still love the game!) This game I personally would not call 'survival horror'. Mind you you're in a studio that is up and running (Though it shouldn't be honestly if the whole place is down but tomato tamato) you're going to have the lights on almost everywhere which isn't the issue. My issue is that throughout the entire first 3/4ths Of the game it's not scary whatsoever. Sure the puppets would pop up at times but they were usually very easy to get around or take down. It's hard to be scared of an enemy when I can quite literally run around them or just avoid their vision enough to get by. My six hour run time is mostly just running to and back for items and secrets. The puppets are a little messed up and while I did praise the design...they're a little too /clean/. There's no mold, no mud, no grime. You see this specifically in the end game boss which for what happened to them they look too uniform and clean to be anything but a walking bright colorful patch work that does nothing but jump at you. Where's the stuffing hanging out? The pulled apart stitches? The buttons hanging off the eyes?? Maybe mimicking human teeth with some roadkill teeth they pulled out? I absolutely loved the little jump scare of Junebug before the telephone rang, she was creepy! My biggest problem with the game is that the real horror aspect is at the endgame and very short depending on what weapon you have. The Unfriendly neighborhood should have been at least half of the game and not play such a small part. Personally I was expecting puppets to crawl on those cave walls without eyes so you'd have to walk and be quiet (Shut up no I'm not ripping off the lickers from RE2 ), I expected them to be more wild and out there. Maybe have the unfriendly hood get word of a handyman and they drag him down to try and force him to fix them only to terrify and scare him instead. This was a really missed opportunity and maybe if the devs make a sequel they could go more into the Unfriendly neighborhood and make things much more like a survival horror.  While there are aspects I am disappointed with the game was still fun and interesting to play, I liked it. I'm even planning to play it for videos. But it wasn't a 100% perfect game to me and that's fine, I still enjoyed it. It's fun and I like a lot of the ideas it has, especially with helping the puppets. I liked Gordon and his snappy attitude! It just didn't quite hit the mark. But if you're at all actually interested I would def say to give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: These folks hit it out of the park with this game. Is it a bit short, and is it a bit lacking in bosses? Yeah, admittedly. _childDocuments_.review: I really wish there were more proper survival horror games out there and My Friendly Neighborhood only makes me want it more. The game's a bit short and light on the content, it only has 5 weapons for example, but My Friendly Neighborhood has a silly concept and runs with it. The enemies and set pieces are all delightfully accurate to the PBS kids show feel and the game manages to squeeze quite a few fun environments, puzzles, and survival horror mechanics in.You'd think this game would be a throwaway FNAF rip-off, but it actually manages to stand out quite a bit by not relying on any gore, jumpscares, or convoluted plots. My Friendly Neighborhood winds up being genuinely sweet and endearing by not being all that scary and having a refreshingly simple plot about just being nice to each other in tough times. You'd think this would make it suck as a horror game and you'd be right, but MFN becomes something more unique and its own by doing so.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: Writing this review shortly after finishing the game and I have a lot of thoughts. My friendly neighbourhood is the type of horror game that i have been craving for years, something silly that doesn't take itself seriously. I'm tired of FNAF, Bendy, Poppy etc. These games that take "WHAT IF YOUR CHILDHOOD WAS SPOOOOOOOOOOOOKY" and made it predictably creepy. MFN does away with this by humanising the monsters and making them seem like weird little guys instead of evil creeps who just want to harm you.MFN has it's draw backs however, some puzzles feel pointless the maps aren't the best at times and the combat requires you to unlearn a lot.You're not a bioshock protagonist, you're Gordon, some guy, so using your wrench is best for thing slike stealth kills and not for a head on fight with a puppet.Overall i enjoyed my time with MFN and I plan to return to the neighbourhood with a quest to discover everything I missed.

_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: Finished Game Review:I was initially hoping for a darker game, but I have to admit that the lighter tone worked!  There is a lot of nostalgia for children's programming - especially Sesame Street and Mister Roger's Neighborhood - throughout MFN. The same can be said for the Resident Evil series. But that doesn't mean this is an actual children's game. There is enough snark and subverted expectation for adult players - though the Bendy games or Five Nights series are more direct horror. Overall a solid game!The main plot - besides surviving MFN - is figuring out what happened to your felt friends! They are real-ish, after all. There is a lot of charm, a few scares, and a bit of maudlin realization once the final act is over.  Themes include how adults and children process consumerism/monetization - and how adults and children can both learn from each other. You can choose to play friendly or not-so-friendly, and that adds to the plot as well. The puppet designs are delightful; their dialogue is hilarious and somewhat creepy and another subversion of children's TV archetypes. There is s good bit of world-building; I had fun exploring the MFN studio lot. Posters and notes have details that flesh out the story. It may be a trite storytelling technique, but the creators chose to put the right level of detail in these items so it works. The puzzles are entertaining and conceptualized. Gun play is serviceable but a little stiff. I would say this is more about the survival and discovery than the weapons. I will note that the weapons you do find are pretty creative. There is little to complain about IMO, though I wish there was more puppet dialogue. There is a good bit but more is always better. The MFN merchandise in the game was SO CUTE!Loved the game. I would happily buy a sequel or subsequent game from this developer. Original In-Play Review below...In-Play Review:Runs well. No bugs so far. Looks great! Fun to play! Puzzles are engaging. Player direction/support is balanced. Feels good not to be spoon-fed directions. Overall, a well-made game!  I am very impressed! And I want some MFN merch! Wish List:This is probably against the creator's concept - but I'd like to see puppets take some damage. I'd like to see a little bit of stuffing fly with shots or see damage to outfits, loose eye/eyes, etc..... It would be cool if there was an on/off toggle for something like that. More puppet dialogue! Love what is here; I just generally want more!Weapon-play could be refined a little; this is hard to describe but it feels a little...stiff, maybe? there is a reticle option, which helps.

_childDocuments_.review: Unique gamePros: One of the biggest strength is how huge the game's areas are. There's a ton of backtracking and figuring out where to go, but it may get repetitive for some to go from point A-B-A and generally the puzzles are simple enough. The challenge from the puzzles comes from how to get to them. The game has unique combat design in terms of survival horror aspect, enemies you down will respawn once you re-load back into the area via a door. This encourages players to think of ways to deal with enemies with the environment to save resources (pathing to avoid, taking down only a set of enemies, etc.) Generally new areas also have new enemy types. Cons: Unfortunately for me the game's biggest weakness was its balance. It is way too easy and the game gives you too many resources. There's 2 extra difficulties that are locked before beating the game, I can't comment on them - but on the hardest available difficulty at first, I was showered with resources. I beat the game with 0 deaths. This greatly discourages the combat engagement I mentioned above, especially if you get a secret minigun... As a result, most enemy types are unique, but don't feel threatening and eventually can feel like a shooter with puzzles. With too many health items, it seems you can take around 4 hits. After each hit, you get a bit of immunity - so you can exploit this to avoid hordes of enemies while sacrificing little. The snack bars also don't help with this.The wrench is exploitable. Some puzzles are a bit surreal, what I mean is; you need a "pen and paper" to do them and the game doesn't give you such thing.I wish there was a pursuer puppet (nemesis, Mr X)

_childDocuments_.review: This game is proof that Survival Horror doesn't necessarily need to be scary, but there are a very clear set of design principles Evan and John put on display here. Everything we love about classic Survival Horror is alive and well here in such a fun modern indie package. I love that this game and Signalis released within the same year as each other. Two vastly different experiences in terms of narrative, theme, tone, and presentation, but both prove that RE4 didn't kill classic Survival Horror... it's seed merely lay dormant in the dreams of the young. Shout out to Baseketball.I also love that a turd like The Callisto Protocol came out in between and reminded us once again, that indie developers got this one under control. AAA Survival Horror is mid at best. Sure Capcom has done a solid job across the handful of RE Engine releases, but nothing hits quite like this string of solid Indie Survival Horror titles. Daymare, Lamentum, Alisa, Tormented Souls, Dead Beacon, Signalis, and My Friendly Neighborhood are just the start and proof that the genre is in good hands, and with a laundry list of new indie titles on the horizon (Post Trauma, Heartworm, Ghost at Dawn, Conscript, Becrowned, Hollow Body, and many more), Survival Horror fans will never go hungry again.Please continue to support these amazing developers and their upcoming projects as they take their limited budgets and resources and run circles around the so called AAA industry as it burns to the ground.This game makes me ♥♥♥ buckets.Gang gang.Thank you Evan, John, and Company.The Boi
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not surprised by the quality of this game, the Szymanski brothers always release great games. It has a pretty unique idea and setting, and isn't just YouTuber bait. The game itself is actually good, it just has eye catching characters. The game isn't scary, it's a nice indie  experience without the horror . We have manual save points and save rooms, limited inventory space with item boxes in said rooms and strategies that are needed with enemy management in the form of permanently disabling enemy movements with duct tape. The game takes between 4-5 hours to beat, but that is not a discredit. Far too many horror games massively outstay their welcome as tension dies down over time, and the game will add padding in the form of fetch quests or unneeded backtracking  The game also features a lot of replay value in the form of unlockable modes, cheats and difficulties. There's also a bunch of secrets that don't seem to have answers found yet. The take away here is that if you appreciate good, well made, unique independent games, you should treat yourself to My Friendly Neighborhood.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game that suprised me in oh so many ways.I bought it under the assumption to play a horror-game.And it  creepy, don't get me wrong. And I  greeted by what appeared to be deranged murder-muppets.... that is really only the surface-layer.The story is intriguing. The different characters are not necassarily what they appear to be. The humor is spot on.This game is engaging, well thought out, more complex than it might seem at first glance, and cleary made with love.The voice-acting is top notch. The level design is full of small details that you might not see the first time or even first couple of times you play. The game-mechanics work as intended with no game-breaking bugs (or any bug... not any that I could think of at least, right now).The mix of shooter and puzzler works well, with little secrets everywhere.There are only two things I personally would criticize:One would be the price for the overall lenght and quality of the game. It is more on the shorter side (I have about 23hrs in this game and played it through for about 5 or 6 times with maybe 1-2hrs in freecam mode afterwards looking for secrets). And while the overall quality - story, character design, voice acting, sound design, level/world building - is really great, the graphics in and on themselves are... just okay.The other little grievance I have is while I do love the story and the direction it all took, in the end, it isn't really a horror game... and even creepy is something I would only call it occasionally. I'd wish for a DLC or something that took a certain part of the game (that I'm not going to spoiler here) and expands on that, either as a possibility to change the base game, as an additional/alternate story, or as a second part for this game.But, yeah, just a personal opinion.Overall, I would definitely recommend giving this game a shot. Either try the demo - which in my opinion isn't the best example for what the whole game is about -, wait for it to be on sale, or just take the plunge and buy it as is (you still have 2hrs to refund, afterall, in case you don't like it).

_childDocuments_.review: it took me way too long to finally play the full release for this jam and I just finished my first playthrough. It’s going to be one of my favorite games of the year.The premise was always a winner, and despite seeming like just another mascot horror I think My Friendly Neighborhood blows the rest out of the water. It’s so inventive in how it dresses up the standard  first person survival horror fare. The enemies are all homages to Sesame Street, the weapons all “teach” the enemies the alphabet, and if you’re going for a certain ending the story takes on a genuinely friendly tone.In terms of gameplay this is as solid as any Resident Evil with an equal focus on juking out enemies while solving puzzles, picking up keys and tools to open locked entrances and exits.If there are cons… one is that if you end up stuck in a puzzle you will be listening to the puppets talk nonstop. The dialogue is well acted and genuinely funny but this may drive you nuts when you’re trying to figure out what you are missing. Then again, maybe this is a feature not a bug.I finished this playthrough on Normal difficulty and there is so much more for me to do. I’ll be going back for more. _childDocuments_.review: My Friendly Neighborhood is a phenomenal game that released during a time where the majority of the games in it's genre were lazy, uninspired, and just downright awful. You could group this game into the genre of "mascot horror," but I'd say fitting it into the Survival Horror genre is a much better fit.You play as a technician named Gordon, who has been tasked with shutting down the antenna on top of the old MFN studios building after the long cancelled television program starts broadcasting on top of the news. When you get there, you are greeted by the many puppet characters within the studio who have developed some hostile tendencies. You have to fight your way through the studio and survive in order to get your job done.This game doesn't do a lot to make it unique gameplay-wise compared to other survival horror games, but rather takes existing formulas and applies them in really fun and creative ways. This game can best be compared to Resident Evil, only with Sesame Street-like puppet characters instead of zombies. The game has you manage resources, backtrack across all the locations in the game to progress, and fight through hordes of puppets. All of the weapons you are given are designed with a writing theme in mind instead of a usual handgun or combat knife like you'd see in Resident Evil. For instance, your main weapon is built similarly to a typewriter and fires letters at your enemies instead of bullets. All of the weapons fit this theme and adds to the overall charm of the game in my opinion.Speaking of charm, I'd say one of the most charming aspects of this game is the voice acting and dialogue. Every performance given from Gordon, to the recurring sock puppet character Ricky, to even the basic puppet characters you see throughout the game that don't stop talking for even a moment, were done spectacularly and help you feel connected to the characters and at times, humored by them.This game doesn't have any sort of super over-the-top dark or edgy theme to it, but rather a more heartwarming theme that becomes more and more apparent the more you play through the game. The puppets aren't alive because they're possessed or because they were the result of an experiment gone wrong, they're alive because they just.. are. To me there's beauty in that sort of simplicity.Overall, I went into this game expecting to play a pretty decent horror game that I'll play through and eventually forget about, but I walked out of it incredibly impressed by what this game had to offer and likely will be playing through this game again and again to find all the little secrets hidden throughout the game. I very much recommend this game to any fans of survival horror or mascot horror, or both.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: My Friendly Neighbourhood is an incredible game from top to bottom; the character design, the voicework, the 3D animation, the story. All beautiful. The only "issue" id say i had with the game is that i wish it was a bit longer, but i guess thats a good issue to have (probably). I would very much love a sequel/spinoffs to this game that can add to the city and history of MFNOverall grade: 8/10

_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: A very entertaining, humorous survival horror game. Not super long but there is a ton of repeatability and encourages players to look through every nook and cranny to find hidden items and such to make future playthroughs more entertaining. _childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: This game pitches itself as a survival horror taking from classic Resident Evil and wears that on it's sleeve with a quick turn button, ammo management, and even an FPS equivalent to the RNG damage of RE classic, but there's a deeper truth to the game. It's a message that can be found from the game's title, and it's clear why I love this game:It's about being a better, friendly neighbor, and after getting the ending I can say definitively that this game will stick with me, for being a bit of light in a world that's not all too friendly. I've been conditioned by horror games to expect only a dreary ending, or a secret twist of evil, but this game's stuffing, from what I've played, is exactly what it is, through and through, and I couldn't be happier.I should note that there IS horror in this game, but if you're expecting an Outlast you will be disappointed. It's a cutesty RE, and it's amazing for it.[Small tangent but if anything were to EVER get added it would be body awareness for our main character, Gordon, or even a sequel from the POV of a puppet. I love this world and how creative it is, and I can say with 100% certainty that I want more of it.]
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: Makes me think of some of the Resident Evil games, would recommend it to anyone who likes those kind of games and as an added bonus it comes with a touch of comedy cause some of the things the puppets say can be very funny. I will definitely be returning to this game some time in the future to play through it again9/10
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: This was a really enjoyable experience and I love survival horror games such as Resident Evil, Silent Hill, alone in the dark, others Etc, I liked it so much, that honestly I might add this to the list of survival horror games that I really liked. I mean, I like mascot horror occasionally too, but the thing is that most of the gameplay you're not actually fighting back. It reminds me of the old classic survival horror days, where the fear is mostly you losing progress, you running out of ammo, trying to conserve your ammo, making splitdecisions, and never knowing what's around the corner. This game didn't need to have any jump scares, and It didn't need to have any chase segments or anything. I honestly consider this, probably the peak of mascot horror. Yeah, there I said it. I say that because, again, it mixes survival horror and mascot horror without being a cheap cash grab, and it has a unique style to it. It's not the typical, "oh company goes bad, bad scientists, or they're like haunted animatronics" or whatever the hell mascot horror usually is, Whatever, you get the point. It also takes a very real world lesson, and a meaningful message, and it applies it to the game. There's my final thoughts on the game. I definitely enjoyed it.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly polished and extremely overlooked.My Friendly Neighborhood is an excellent game, inspired by Resident Evil and mascot horror games. It uses the right amount of both its' inspirations to craft an utterly fun and wacky experience. Obviously such a colorful game will probably not scare you like Outlast, Silent Hill or Resident Evil itself does, but it manages to slither some disturbing and charming creepy moments, matching the vibe of the characters and world around them.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: at its core, MFN is not a horror game. It is not scary, and it doesn't really try very hard to be. That's just the way I like it.I'm a hardcore horror fan and when I first played to the end, I felt a little disappointed by the game's lack of fear factor. But then it occurred to me that despite the fact that I was never afraid or unsettled, I had thoroughly enjoyed the game. I went back, got every achievement, saw every ending, found every secret. I did a couple speedruns. I made theories and fanart and wrote down scripts for post-game scenes I imagined. I filled a sketchbook with drawings of puppets and grumpy old handymen.At first, I'd been looking for a 'real' horror experience. I'd wanted to get my socks scared off, but what I found was a world that was so genuinely charming and lovable that, despite it barely holding the title as one, I think MFN is my favourite horror game. Not for the fear, but for the joy it brings me.I'll be finding out if I can make it on my own soon. In a couple months, I'll be finally moving out of my adoptive parents' house. If I can get through TAFE, and if I ever get into the game design course I'm going for, and if I can finally put my hyperactive energy to something, look out for a little Australian indie game that's clearly inspired by MFN.Cheers.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be honest, I kinda hated this game when I started playing it. But as it went on I figured out that I hate just didn't like the combat (especially the melee). Where the real fun of the game comes from is the puzzles and the easy story. So stick with the game for the first hour, if you don't like it by then the game's not for you.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: A solid indie horror game, that is, if you're the type to flee from any genuinely scary game. My Friendly Neighborhood creatively combines Muppets with survival horror mechanics, and pulls it off pretty well. While mascot horror games are fairly popular right now, MFN stands above with neat game mechanics like inventory management and the fact that dead children weren't stuffed into the damn mascots this time. There's plenty of entertainment, like being forced to drain a bathtub with a twitching puppet inside, or risking your life in a simple board game. Plus, the puppets' endless chatter is hilariously unsettling. There were a couple of glitches, like weapons being unable to hit smaller enemies from certain angles, but nothing severe. Personally, I wish the game was fleshed out a little more at times, but overall this game was a great experience.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: The puppet aesthetic is a lot of fun, but I was genuinely surprised by how tight the gameplay was on top of that. Feels like a love letter to Resident Evil in a lot of ways since you can only "kill" certain enemies, resource management is key, and exploration that rewards backtracking. The shooting itself is a bit generic and it would be nice if there were more puppets, but beyond that the theme is great, the levels are varied and fun to explore, and there's details and easter eggs crammed throughout that kept me charmed all game.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty cool game! It has a refreshing style and message as well as lovely characters and fun puzzles! It's nice that you can come back to things and that the game subverts the whole "children's media gone wrong" trope by having the question "why are these puppets alive?" be at the back of the player's mind for the entire game rather than control the plot. Highly recommend, it is a very entertaining and somewhat comforting replayable experience.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: A game that actually brought a tear to my eye when it was over.  I absolutely loved this game, bought it right when it came out, finished it and am on my third play through already. I am trying out the different difficulties and cheats...and having a great time!It's not scary...but that doesn't make it less of a thrilling game or diminish the survival horror aspect at all. Personally I died, a lot...all near the end because . The characters are often annoying to the point of relishing the idea of using the Novelist or Conclusion on them and laughing with glee while doing it.  They are also so endearing and you kind of fall in love with them (probably because they remind us of characters we grew up with).  I loved the fact that you made friends with some too - that aspect made the whole game so much more than a shoot 'em, kill 'em and move on to the next.You can tell the care that went into the game.  I encountered no bugs, no issues...absolutely the BEST soundtrack and a story line that tugged at your heart while making you manic at the same time.  I swear, if I hear that hacking cough of Liliana one more time I will scream...
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed playing through this, think of Resident Evil mixed with Sesame Street and that's what you get. _childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: It's an incredibly well made game, it has that Resident Evil vibe to it, especially when you get to the lobby of the second building it reminds me of the old Spencer mansion from the first game.  Only thing is it's a bit buggy and at least on my side of things some voice lines won't trigger, idk if there's a way to fix it or not.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, the game is really good. You have a grid based inventory, and every save station also has a way to heal to full health if you spend a coin, and a Toolbox, which acts as a  checkpoint inventory to store stuff in.Every enemy takes a few hits to down, but the game gives you plenty of magazines as you travel, I had about 5 stacks of them toward the end stored away. For each Major Enemy, usually one in each area, you could either avoid them or solve a puzzle to make them friendly towards you and get an achievement. There was a glitch that prevented you from getting one of the achievements, the Rolodexer only achievement, but it has been patched and I now have 100% of the achievements.It's a great game and feels like a love-letter or omage to the Resident Evil games.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good! A lighter-hearted RE8 style game with distinctly themed, interconnected areas with a dedicated boss in each. The theme and gameplay are what personally carried the game for me, as the lore/backstory while serviceable, weren't particularly strong IMO. Still though, definitely worth a play through, as it nails the fundamentals of the survival-horror formula, while providing a unique and clever spin. Also worth noting that there are multiple difficulties, unlockable cheats, and alternate modes that provide a decent amount of repeatability. If you're interested enough to read this review, I think you'll likely enjoy it and would recommend picking it up.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game, I really hope there is some DLC in the future. This game is clearly inspired by Bioshock, sesame street, and Res2. Honestly,  such a cool concept and fun gameplay.NOTE TO DEV'S: As a man with a....passion for puppetry, I greatly appreciate the effort you put into the overall floppiness of the characters. Most people think its about the texture or the stitching;  its really about the control, the power, the flop, the smile on their face as I inflict my will. Based on the amount of detail I can only assume you have the same passion as me.  Even though I have beaten this game, I know I will be back time and time again at 3 to 10 minute intervals; multiple times a day maybe less depending on my work schedule.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: I've had my eye on this game for a long time, and with good damn reason. This game has a *ton* of heart put into it, and it is the best entry to the "mascot horror" genre in a very, very long time. The one nitpick a lot of people have is the save system - hell, a lot of people drop it just because of that. However, if you can get used to it (and reach the first checkpoint), it's really not that bad. Just something you have to get used to. Resident Evil fans will be experienced with it.Apart from that, I genuinely can't think of anything truly wrong with the game. Compared to the likes of security breach and banban, it's a breath of fresh air. A game with not just a fun premise, but an actual message behind it, unlike the walking simulator, 5 chapter money hog of Poppy Playtime.Overall, I highly reccomend fans of survival horror in general to give this game a shot. You won't be disappointed. I rarely review on steam, and even I did for this, because I just had to say how happy I was that there was a mascot horror that wasn't a cashgrab sellout. Actual effort and replayability are in this game, and I can't express how much I appreciate it. My hat tips to you, developer.

_childDocuments_.review: Played through once on survival mode (one mode harder than standard). Had a lot of fun with this. Plays like an amalgamation of Resident Evil and BioShock. Scenery and character designs are interesting, the metroidvania aspect and the backtracking that came along with it was inoffensive, and the not-muppets themselves are genuinely entertaining to watch and listen to. The main character is an absolute cheesy cornball, but I'm a freak and enjoy that campy stuff so A+ there. Some people are commenting that ammo is scarce, but I had an overabundance if anything all throughout, between conserving, fleeing, and using the melee wrench. If anything I was tossing out ammunition and tape (an item that keeps enemies from respawning) out of my inventory to make room for other things. My biggest complaint is that the not-muppets' very long reach combined with a completely random super armor they seem to gain while being hit makes meleeing or close-range firing a very unreliable strategy. Any time you decide to melee one, it's a total roll of the dice whether or not you'll be grabbed and get your health chunked. Overall though this is a definite "buy". Very enjoyable 6-ish hours. Would love to see more of this, via DLC or sequel or whatever. 9 / 10

_childDocuments_.review: If you're an oldschool fan of Resident Evil and Silent Hill titles and the way they play, this game is for you. Don't read the rest of this review, just buy it.In terms of everything else though, this is an incredibly thoughtful game. Despite being clearly Survival Horror, it is far more focused on the "Survival" aspect than the "Horror" and makes for a great tool to ease people into the genre. For those that don't know, this was made by the Szymanski brothers who are known for games like Dusk and Iron Lung. If they wanted this to be a straight forward shooter, they could have made that. If they wanted this to be a straight horror game, they could have made that. But they didn't, they made My Friendly Neighborhood.Everything. Is. Deliberate. This was a creative work of passion that had something to say, and despite their past work the theme of this title largely revolves around the nature of consumer trends and what people have become accustomed to these days AKA overtly edgy and dark material. Despite the demos from a year or so ago, this game isn't just trying to be goofy and funny, the Sesame Street inspired aesthetic was a deliberate callback to the sunshine glossed TV shows from the 80's and 90's which have all since fallen by the wayside in favor of dark, gory, and grim TV shows that get churned out on a weekly basis. Ironically, a lot of these shows of times past were criticized at the time for the messages they were teaching children and for being too "sunshine and rainbows" without preparing kids for the brutal reality of the adult world.This game takes a step back and says pretty boldly that those good vibes those old shows presented not only had value, but that the market of dark material has grown too big and is simply a reflection of our own vices these days. People aren't making games and TV shows for fun anymore, it's all about following the market and playing it safe, which has ironically begun to revolve around the bleakest types of content imaginable. Not everything needs to be dark, sometimes you need someone that's going to tell you things are going to be alright, that life ISN'T so bad, and sometimes you need to stop taking yourself so seriously and just chill.I stress this all given the age of mass market mascot horror we live in.This game isn't trying to be that, it's unique; special even. I just hope it doesn't get forgotten.PS: The puppets never shut up. Don't forget to brush your teeth. Me? I prefer to brush mine with Worchestershire sauce.

_childDocuments_.review: Before I get into the meat of the review if you are someone just browsing reviews to see if you like the game or not here you go.TLDR: The game could have been good if it developed itself more, and while it starts strong it does not build upon itself on its story or game-play throughout the entire experience. If you read more, know there will be spoilers to the game and its experiences. You have been warned, read more at your own discretion.At the start of the game, the plot starts off strong with a specific goal: shut off the radio tower. You are introduced to the protagonist with little information which makes you feel like almost an empty shell for the player to fill. The direction and themeing of the game is a great hook, but sadly it is not enough to carry the entire experience. Once you encounter your first few enemies you get a basic melee weapon that is borderline useless, as all enemies do a grab attack that knocks you down onto the ground, and the range of the weapon is a few pixels larger than that range it feels. Getting the first gun helps, but enemies will endlessly respawn unless you use a very rare resource to lock down specific downed enemies. As well as enemies will endlessly respawn, but your amunition does not. I myself did not have issues with ammo within my playthrough, however that is because enemies will not follow you through doors and leaving and re-entering a room will reset their positions meaning that mechanic can be easily exploited. Combat in its enemies does not develop, and once you go through the first proper area you have seen most of the enemies the game feels it has to offer. And as you get stronger weapons through the game, but the enemies do not, you simply find tools to deal with nuisances rather than problems scaling with you. This game feels that it took a lot of inspiration from classic resident evil games, but not the best aspects of them. Walking around lost in an area until you find everything you need to progress is rough enough as is, but with enemies respawning constantly it means that you have to deal with dealing with the bullet sponges that they are. The pistol can take a few to almost a full clip to take out some enemies, which will simply respawn the second you leave the room. The shotgun will make any enemy fold, but it has rarer ammunition and again, unless you waste that rare resource to lock down an enemy they will just get back up. Going back and forth and shooting the same bland enemies with voice lines you have heard way too many times by the time you get to the 2nd area hampered my view upon the game.The story also does not develop itself more than the basic starting premise and a few notes around the game explaining "why" the show was canceled in the first place. That in which sums up as "it did not fit with the times anymore". A basic story that will not get better than that. As for the protagonist, he starts as an empty shell but has personality and references to "the war" which by the timeline of other notes in the game is in reference to Vietnam. But the game does not build upon him at all, other than a few references at times and that is it. Other notes are in the game, but telling your bare bones hollow story through way too many spread out notes is not how to do it. And while it is a "survival horror", the horror aspect is almost non existent. The only part that could be said to be even slightly scary is the very final area of the game which is only 2 rooms, with a final boss battle that I simply defeated by throwing 5 grenades at and a few shotgun blasts. A few areas are dark, but there isnt any horror, no dark past in the story, it is just a hollow experience that feels that it had a lot of heart put in it, but not much thought about the actual gameplay. I would be able to put it past that if this 5 hour game experience did not cost $30 at full price, which is WAY too much for this hollow experience. I wanted to recommend this game, but it has way too many flaws for me to recommend. It is a child friendly mascot horror experience in the lines I would expect from a Roblox game, not a $30 title.

_childDocuments_.review: Full video review: Condensed text version:Have you heard that My Friendly Neighborhood is like Resident Evil meets Sesame Street? Well, I sure did, probably too many times. Not that I'm gonna deny it's a pretty accurate description of the game. It's not a perfect game by any means, but it actually fully delivers on that proposal in a nicely-polished package.Indie horror games can sometimes get a bad rap for being full of shovelware, and mascot horror games amp that bad reputation up to 11. If you haven't heard the term "Mascot Horror" before, it's referring to a subset of indie horror games that usually share a few key qualities. You've got bright colors, ear-blasting jump scares, cutesy monsters, minimal gameplay, and a heavy focus on appealing to younger audiences. Not to say that all of these games are terrible, I mean I haven't played most of them myself, but it's undeniable that their success hinges mostly on marketing to children. We all know kids, they aren't exactly media critics. So a lot of these games are massive money printers, despite having some of the worst gameplay imaginable.But there's one big difference between My Friendly Neighborhood and the vast majority of the Mascot Horror genre - it's... actually good? You see, the game plays sort of like a certain survival horror series about Evil Residents that I won't mention for the rest of the review. If you've played classic survival horror games, almost everything you'd expect to see is present in My Friendly Neighborhood. We've got item boxes, inventory tetris, limited resources, branching paths, arbitrary puzzles, and tons of backtracking. Heck, they even took the classic zombie burning mechanic, in the form of taping up puppets that you've downed, so they don't get back up when you return to the room.I had a pretty good time exploring all corners of the map, slowly expanding and unlocking areas over time, and blasting some overly-chatty puppets along the way. Replicating old game mechanics is cool and all, and they're mostly executed pretty well. However, beyond nostalgia, it's clear why some of these mechanics fell out of favor over time. One issue I took with the design was how many loading screen doors there are around basically every corner. The loading screens aren't long, and the game runs very well, even in the larger, more open areas. Plus, there are doors that don't have loading screens attached, and it's not like they break the game or anything. But you never know if a door will trigger a loading screen until you actually interact with it. Many times I thought to myself, "I just wasted a bunch of ammo downing these enemies, do I really want to test this door and have that all go to waste?" So I can only assume the countless loading screen doors were added for two main reasons. The first being nostalgia, like many of the mechanics, but the more important of the two being that they force you to plan around enemy placements. However, even in a classic survival horror games I won't name, the zombies stay dead when you first kill them, until a much later point in the game. In My Friendly Neighborhood, if you're not planning to use your very limited tape on an enemy, it's almost always better to just run around them instead of engaging. There's no reason to waste resources on enemies that can be easily avoided and instantly respawn when you leave the room. I wouldn't even mind the doors that much if they weren't interrupting the game every 30 seconds or so, with the the random exception of some big areas that don't have them.While I'm listing off minor game design gripes, the puppets have a pretty wild grab range. It's clear that they don't want you to use the wrench much, but getting grabbed 10 feet away just feels wrong. However, don't let small issues like that take away from the big picture here. Overall I had a pretty good time playing through the 4-5 hour campaign on Survival mode.As you can probably tell by now, the visuals are solid throughout. It's not amazing or anything, but they executed pretty well on their desired style. There's a few highlights that stood out to me, like the retro sound stage and the art-deco office building, while some other areas like the garden felt a little more rushed.Like many horror games before it, My Friendly Neighborhood is decently front-loaded - in that the early levels are the most intricately designed and fun to experience. They definitely put a lot of effort in to the first few levels, but maybe they decided to expand the game a little more on the tail end of development. I don't fault them for this, but it does cause the game to lose a bit of steam in the back half, especially when one of the later chapters is basically just a backtracking world-tour.And while some parts of the game may vary over time, the voice acting remains consistently excellent throughout the whole runtime. I don't even know where to start with the voice acting here. I mean, it's possibly some of the best I've heard from any small-budget indie game.The constant chatter from the puppets is somehow annoying, humorous, and consistently memorable all at once. The sock puppet, who acts as a sort of guide, is very well-done. They provide not only comedy, but a range of unexpected emotions throughout the story. And of course I can't forget about the main character, who sounds exactly like Bob Hoskins from the 1993 Mario movie. All I could picture while playing this game was a gruff, grumpy Mario begrudgingly making his way through hordes of killer puppets just to do his job. You even do a little plumbing, so I'm really wondering if the old Mario movie was an inspiration here, at least in some small way. But really, all the voice acting is top-notch, so huge props to everyone who contributed to this.I could go on about the story, or the "boss" puppets, or the lessons behind the narrative, but I think I've already said enough. If you enjoy classic survival horror in an indie format, I think this game would be right up your alley. I'm definitely interested to see more from these developers in the future. But what I'm even more interested in seeing is how this impacts indie horror games in general. You'd have a hard time getting a Five Night's at Freddy's kid to play Silent Hill, but show them My Friendly Neighborhood and you could easily bridge that gap to other survival horror.
