My main interest is it was the DreadXP guys, and I generally like the stuff they publish/develop.What I did not expect was basically a sort of... first-person RE4, almost? Kind of. You're not running around helpless, which I think is a good thing. You've got at least a melee weapon and a ranged weapon. I'm not sure if you get more. You've got an RE4 tetris-style inventory (that you access in real-time, no pause!) and you're solving puzzles, putting emblems together, shooting baddies, that kind of thing.I'm still early on, so again, first impressions. But the controls even on a controller are super responsive and snappy, you've even got a dedicated 180 button. You're collecting keys with symbols to doors with those symbols, there's save rooms with save room music, all that good stuff.Game runs buttery smooth, and runs well even on a Steam Deck, no stutters either way. (The intro seemed to be a bit iffy on the Steam Deck as it wanted to skip the opening scene, but after using the latest GE Proton it's all normal) All menus and everything work as they should on a controller or a keyboard and mouse.Guess I have two minor complaints: Strafing is much slower than moving straight forward or back, I guess to make it harder to easily outmaneuver enemies, and most doors actually trigger a load screen. It's a super short one, like maybe 1 second on my SSD, so not a big deal, but worth noting, might be longer on a mechanical drive.No idea how long the game is, but I do like that on survival mode you have to use currency you find in-game to save. On normal it autosaves so either playstyle is covered. I'll probably update this once I have more time, I just wanted to signal that this seems to be a quality title and not just another "ooo the enemy chases you as you helplessly walk through hallways" kind of deal. Those can be fun but there's been far too many lately in my opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic Survival Horror game.Inspired by older titles such as the original Biohazard/Resident Evil and Silent Hill. Puzzles were challenging but doable with a bit of thinking, the combat was solid but with  a few hiccups like hit detection being wonky. First playthrough only took me about 4 hours but easily could be done is a little over an hour if you know what to do and where to go.I would 100% recommend this to horror fans. There is a demo if you want to give it a go first!
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: A refreshingly unique experience that's more comedy-horror than actual horror. I especially enjoyed the many environments to explore with a mixture of art deco and zany props.One complaint: I found normal difficulty to be too frustrating. Wrench combat simply doesn't work, so it's easy to run out of ammunition, especially when puzzles require backtracking through the same enemies again and again. Also, the need to ration save tokens means repeating lots of progress when dying. So I switched to easy mode, which worked fine but wasn't even slightly scary. I wish there were something in between. If the developers could just adjust the balance slightly, this game would be perfect.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: Let’s set the scene. the studio lot of the Friendly Neighborhood. Gordon. Repairman extraordinaire. A strange broadcast of the beloved children’s TV show, The Friendly Neighborhood has begun playing.Gordon is the quintessential repairman. He has an east coast accent that makes you believe he could truly fix anything?  Gruff and easily irritable?  Hairy arms?  Basically, the perfect person to clash against the ultra-bright and kooky set of The Friendly Neighborhood. After getting a work order from his boss, Gordon finds himself in the supposedly vacant studio lot with a supposedly easy task: stop the broadcast via the antennae on the roof.But of course, things are never that easy. After the studio stopped broadcasting, the puppets were left behind, and for a decade have been wandering the studio and surrounding areas, collecting dust and rapidly ascending into madness.When navigating through the studio, you can tell just how much dedication went into creating this lore-rich environment. Although they haven't broadcasted anything recently, you can get a sense of what the studio and life was like there from its design. I could spend hours just roaming through the different sets to just sit and absorb every little detail. One of the highlights of this title is the ramblings of the puppets. At first, the rants seem harmless, if not a bit strange. But as you sit there and  their stories get jumbled, they stop themselves before revealing darker and more twisted truths, or just something so  it makes you sit there staring at the kooky smiling faces as you try to process what they said. Although the picture and vision were clear for this game, there were a few things that made the broadcast a little staticky for me, mostly relating to quality-of-life aspects. Item and enemy ranges were tricky to dictate sometimes. Vital items were sometimes overlooked when not facing a specific item just right. Or getting taken down in a deadly bear-hug when stepping a little too far in when swinging a wrench or missing shots from the Rolodexer. The game is non-linear, which makes it fun for future playthroughs, but having the option of a 'goal' or 'task' reminder in the menu could help especially when entering new levels.  is a cast of fun and nerve-racking characters and environments. Whether you’re someone new to the horror genre or a bloodied veteran, you won’t be disappointed with so many (mostly) smiling faces around. It’s a sweet and nostalgic message, leaving you wanting to revisit those Saturday morning rituals.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a surprisingly good survival horror game, and just kind of great in general. It allows for wacky moments, throws some curveballs, ratchets up tension at points, weirdly (triumphantly) capitalizes on the cast of enemies and setting (no spoilers) and I actually even read all of the documents that I found as they started hinting at themes that played into the how and why of the plot. I had not heard anything about this game before seeing a stream of it being played, and I knew right away I wanted to play through it. I was not disappointed.TL;DR -- If you like the form of a survival horror (Resident Evil / Silent Hill / Evil Within) and can stand theming that isn't anime-bioweapon-horror or guilt-driven-supernatural-horror this is worth looking into. The creativity that My Friendly Neighborhood put on display throughout my first playthrough is something to be championed, and I look forward to playing through a few more times like any great survival horror game. Also, the paintings around the offices with the puppets inserted into famous works were incredibly entertaining, and deserve to be recognized!
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: extremely fun and enjoyable story. Horror game with puppets is a dream come true for me, from the first video I saw I knew this is my game. Ricky is one of the most lovable characters you will ever have by your side and while playing i felt really immersed in Gordon's story that I felt like I was becoming him. I grew so much arm hair just to be like my main man Gordon. My wife and i have already decided that our baby on the way is going to be Gordon.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: Had a lot of fun ! A game that recalls the classic resident evil style of survival horror. The game ain't particularly scary aside from a few scenes and some (very few) jump scares. But the gameplay really scratch that hitch of well design, inter-connected environment. I felt like each place was sufficiently uniquely presented to be able to hold where everything was in my head. The game starts linear but requires you to go around and backtrack a bunch which makes the usage of tapes pretty strategic ! I would recommend to play immediately in Survival, playing in Normal was too easy and I accumulated way too much resources I felt (could literally gun everything down).The main critic I'd have would be that there's not a lot of different puppet type, and the game doesn't create situations where they synergize enough to be interesting :( The game length is just enough for one of those nice "week-end" game. And in the tradition of RE-like there's plenty of cheats and unlocks once finished to replay a couple of time :)I highly recommend for fans of survival horror exploration games !
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: This game really moved me. I'm a survival horror game addict I love finding new and interesting survival horror games; this game surprised me with its child TV show muppets theme with no gore or blood, no demonic curses or dead ghosts of kids none of that overplayed sort of thing AND had amazing solid survival horror game FPS mechanics and fantastic map/level design. The level near the end and some parts of the game still creeped me out and scared me enough with the themes despite this game being for all ages. This is a amazing game, well designed gameplay, art, and story 9/10 imo. I was enjoying how good the survival horror mechanics are despite the cute themes only to find mid-way through the game how GOOD the story is. The main character Gordon was really well done. The other characters are charming but Gordon and his ability to cast aside his past to move forward to help the other characters thus helping his own inner darker feelings really moved me. Ricky is amazing as well The youtuber "Arlo" casted as Ricky was really well done and impressed me with how perfect he is at puppet characters. Ricky's writing was fantastic as well the lines he gives near the end of the game about how the city has turned rotten and the people need light was great when the broadcast gets shut off by Gordon. Ricky poking at Gordon for being a G.I and having killed innocent or defenseless people (you can tell the war represents Vietnam) was REALLY interesting. I felt bad for Gordon for probably getting drafted into that war and regretting it and the darkness that comes with realizing your government forced you to be a monster and how you'd question your own actions or the friends/squad-mates you lost for years all that mental hell. Gordon's new yorker older guy angry at the world while being a wage-slave negative mentality makes so much sense after that war backstory/context and made his kindness he gives to the puppets feel powerful. The words of the old CEO left behind on notes near the end of the game on how dark reality is and how "My Friendly Neighborhood" as a shows purpose was originally; really moved me. Its sad to think nobody wanted the cancellation and abandonment of the facilities/puppets but it had to happen due to the market/money constraints. Its sad the puppets need human connection themselves but couldn't get it anymore after the show failed and makes a TON of sense as to why they go so mad. The final area "Not friendly Neighborhood" where things actually get quite scary but its revealed the puppets down there decided to watch modern TV and see what their show is missing but it turned them awful and crazy was SO WELL DONE. Its actually scary to think the puppets are innocent and human entertainment could be so vile and evil that it imprints on them to turn bad themselves. Its a very interesting concept that makes you think like lots of parts of this story. Some nick-picks I might have is more actual boss fights than the wall of eyes or whatever that was; and the final boss in the not friendly neighborhood. The map/level design could have used way more enemies but keep in mind my playthrough was on survival horror mode which isn't even the hardest mode in the game. I hope for a sequel, maybe a VR mode for this game? If a sequel was ever done I'd suggest a longer play time/open world immersive sim gameplay more rather than how linear this game was. My play-through was 8 hours (I tried to do and experience everything hence how I got the perfect ending without even realizing it was that) but I hear complaints from other gamers tend to be that the short length. There is a lot of inspiration from RE4 in here and I'd like RE4's competent combat/enemy placements level design style here in this game too. I feel like you guys pulled a LOT of punches on the puppet enemy placements/level designs and didn't have to making the game easier than it should have been. (you could have pulled punches on the easier difficulty modes instead) I was expecting a final area with way more enemy swarms/waves attacking you with all your prepared and saved gear but it never happens. *I horded and saved a ton of ammo/nads/weapons but never got that huge battle* The final area is easy and you can avoid killing any puppets just eat candy and run the whole time. On my first play-through I got the good/perfect ending. THAT ending was the best conclusion and really has left me feeling like il never forget this game, il never forget the stuff Gordon said throughout this game to cheer the puppet bosses up; it was all really charming and soulful. Gordon's words in the end about feeling home really made me think and tear up; made me think about my own life and how dark things iv gone through lately bother me and its always great in fiction to see similar male characters fix their lives giving hope to themselves and the viewer. This is the first indie survival horror game iv played in so long where its hard to uninstall it when I beat it and I'm actually consider doing another play through on harder modes for fun. The purpose of MFN to be light in dark times for people... Its funny I hope the devs know or find out that this game is literally doing the exact same thing by being so soulful and charming in kinda dark times for both reality and the game industry.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely fantastic game that perfectly captures the spirit of Resident Evil while doing more than just giving it a "muppet coat of paint". All the weapons are cute and neat, and the secrets to be found are really fun! The way bosses work and are handled is also a neat idea that works well both for the RE and muppet inspired gameplay!
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: In terms of overall game play, I personally think the game was great! I loved the story, the characters, the goofy things said by the puppets, the weapons; I thought it was all great. Ray was my personal favorite of all the main people. He isn't mean; just... misunderstood. I loved the whole horror, puzzle solver type of game that was provided; but my only complaint is I just felt the game was a little bit... too short. I mean don't get me wrong, I loved everything about it, but personally speaking, I feel that a game that took me a little over 5 hours to complete, while going in blind, doesn't seem... very reasonable for... 30 dollars. I bought the game the day after it was released so I'm not complaining about getting a 10% discount, making it 26 dollars; and I know it was mainly developed by two brothers, which I think is quite impressive, I'm just not quite sure whether the full price of the game is... justifiable? That is just my opinion; I've played quite a few games that have a longer game play time for a lower price, but I personally think if it's going to be 30 dollars then there should be some extra content with it like a DLC as a bundle; then I could see it being more... reasonable. It is a great game overall; I just think the pricing could be a tiny bit better; I mean from personal experience, I'd usually expect an 8+ hour game time for at least $30; but that is just coming from my personal opinion. My idea of pricing shouldn't be taken to ruin your view of the game in any way though; nor do I intend it to. Pricing aside, just have fun with it. It won't hurt you in any way.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: this has quickly become one of my favorite games. I really loved how much it took from Resident Evil. the only issue I had was that I wish the last segment was a little longer. Love horror games and for the most part (especially once you learn the message of the game) this isn't really a horror game. speaking of which the ending is *chefs kiss* wonderful. all in all I give it a 9/10. I could tell I had hit gold when I beat it for the first time and hadn't gotten the best ending I immediately jumped right back in.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: The horror game for people who don't like horror games (but maybe like puppets).MFN has been an absolutely delightful experience. The puppets' chatter is just the funniest stuff to listen to - the only wish I had whilst playing is that there were more deranged voice lines from the incredible voice actors.wooshtershishter sauce
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely incredible game. Gameplay is as smooth as butter, the characters are all memorable and a treat to both the eyes and ears, and the level of replayability is incredible. There are very few games that can properly balance survival horror elements with comedy without sacrificing one of the two genres, but this game accomplishes that handily. My only piece of criticism is how difficult it can be to tell the range of both your melee attacks, and those of the Neighbors, but it hardly takes away from an otherwise impeccable experience. Well worth full price. Do yourself a favor and pick this one up, especially if you're a fan of Resident Evil.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: A charming antihorror game with a well-crafted world, a silky-smooth jazz score that I could never get enough of and a bit of wasted potential. While the game's fairly fun, it is relatively short, perhaps rationalizing the 20-something dollar price tag. The game seems to expect you to replay it multiple times to extract that value, so a solid choice for Acheivement-addicts. One of my many complaints is that different difficulties change little within the game, other than resource spawning, and a few of the sudden sparkles I saw in the game unexpectedly faded away.Please be aware, this game is not scary. You shoot puppets with a typewriter gun, and the demo was some of the most laughter-inducing gameplay I've had. Each section of the game has its own motiff and some areas intermingle in creative ways.Unfortunately, some of the content I enjoyed out of the demo failed to star in the rest of the game. The story is at different times an acid trip an homage to Sesame Street childhoods and a well-crafted suspense story. There are psychological horror moments, when you mutter to yourself "Wait, that wasn't there before."In conclusion: There are worse ways to spend $20, but I wouldn't put this on the top of my list. Expect about 8 hours of gameplay in a single playthrough at the base difficulty, with higher ones taking longer.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: This game Is one of the best horror games i have played in a good while. It has a great atmosphere and in my opinion has a very unique feel, and yes it can be whacky and comedic yet that doesn't diminish from the horror of the game and i feel like it only adds to it. It gives a unique spin on the gameplay we have all seen the kind that the resident evil games are known for. I have spent many hours in the game without realising it. and the puzzles only add to the game and on a few have had me stumped, i even feel like the jump scares in the game are evened out and have got me many time. I would say this is a definite pick up for any one looking to pick up a good horror game. The best way i could describe this game in as few words possible tho would be resident evil combined with sesame street. As a conclusion i would highly recommend this game for both people who are new or who are used to horror games alike, it will provide a great experience in my opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, straight up - the best game I've ever played. There's absolutely nothing to dislike about it, and I cannot for the life of me think of one criticism. I hope there are more in this series/style whether it be prequels or sequels, planned. What I also like is that you do not hurt/kill characters in the game and even have a chance to befriend/help some of them. It's just a beautiful game with a heartwarming story.Well done to all involved.Sincerely, a self-proclaimed kids TV historian.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: Tons of fun, full of charm, and it has secrets in every little corner!A rewarding experience for players who enjoy thoroughly exploring a game's map. I love the engaging environments and the strategic inventory and resource management. The characters are so charming and wonderful, you just have to meet them. I just finished my first playthrough, and I'm going back for my second, third, forth and many more!
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: I've been excited for this game ever since I played the demo! I believe other people have said the same but think of sesame street meets resident evil. The puppets are an all around laugh and can be a little annoying if not dealt with properly.  The choice of trying to sneak around them or using duct tape to take some weight off of your shoulders is definitely a nice touch. I haven't gotten too far into the game, but ive enjoyed every minute of it. I've only played it on my ROG ally but it has been an all around great experience with it on the go. It's a fun survival horror packed with some good laughs along the way. If you're a fan of the genre I'd highly recommend adding it to your collection!
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent nod to other survival horror titles! I couldn't help but make comparisons to Bioshock and Resident Evil while I'd been playing. It feels like they'd taken some of the best elements from a handful of games and spliced it all together to make something new of it. It can be suspenseful but never falls to an extreme level. It's a very light horror game. Unless you have some trauma involving muppets I'm sure you'll fair well with this title, however if you're like me prepare to get lost. Thankfully there's a map but you'll have to remember it's there.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: Finished the game earlier today and have nothing but nice things to say about it, super solid experience! The premise, the mechanics, the setting, the script, everything is on point. Something any game might struggle with, not just horror titles, is a sense of consistency, of identity- but MFN understands exactly what it wants to be and do, the experience it wants to give you. The devs clearly worked hard to make sure every element fit together to reach that goal.MFN wears its influences on its sleeve while maintaining its uniqueness. You can blaze forward and finish the game in a couple hours, or you can poke around and find things you might have otherwise missed. Exploring feels like what it should: a reward. The game is also incredibly heartfelt and funny, and I found myself becoming quite attached to all the puppets running around. (Gobblette has my heart.)Do yourself a favor and, when you have the chance, come visit the neighborhood!
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best Resident Evil-like game since forever. Puzzles are nice (never searched for clues once, everything is very clear for a veteran of a genre), gameplay is neatly balanced, gunplay is surprisingly fun for what it is (Dusk creators, no surprises here). Story is also quite poignant, really love the message.Also, great atmosphere, VO, art.This is surprisingly terrific game from a modest team. Bavo! Totally a must-buy for ANY puzzle or classic RE fan.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: As a horror game it isn't good but as a survival adventure game with off brand Muppets chasing after you its fantastic! The game offers a great balancing system and can be punishing if you aren't smart with the objects in your inventory. this game is a blast to play but if you want to be on the edge of your seat with fear this game is not it but if you want a game that demands exploration and respects your intelligence (and throws the occasional jump scare your way) I recommend picking this one up!
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: Had a very enjoyable first playthrough of this game. While a little lacking in scares for a horror title and having somewhat simple gameplay, My Friendly Neighborhood more than makes up for that with a rather interesting storyline and a cast of surprisingly memorable and even likable characters. The game is rather short and the plot is fairly straightforward but I don't believe that's to the game's detriment. Unfortunately, while playing through the game a second time on a higher difficulty without saving throughout the playthrough (something that the game incentives through it's post-game grading system), I encountered a bug when firing a weapon just as I tried to enter a door that caused the projectiles to block the doorway and left me stuck unable to enter the door and permanently stuck in the door-opening cutscene. As much as I would like to recommend this game, my experience was ruined by this. I'm not certain how common game-breaking bugs like this are and therefore, despite really enjoying my first run of the game I won't recommend it. Maybe temper your expectations before playing the game and don't expect the game to work perfectly to have a better time than I did.Edit: A developer on this game has since reached out to me and is in the process of trying to test on and eliminate this glitch. It seems to also he a highly specific circumstance that caused it. Just on the basis of having such a nice and genuinely helpful response to my previously negative review I've changed this to a recommendation. Developers like this are awesome and deserve all the support they can get. The game is very good, and just knowing that the Devs are actively looking into issues and are willing to reach out to their playerbase and assess feedback is absolutely wonderful. It definitely seems like issues just like this one will be addressed expeditiously so I really don't have much to complain about. If you're a fan of survival horror do yourself a favor and pick this game up, the game itself is great and the team behind it is even better.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: MFN is a throwback to classic survival horror (limited saves based on items, enemies that don't stop coming back unless you put them down for good, and key hunting especially), but with a muppety aesthetic that keeps the horror limited.If I had to pick any gripe I've had, the hardest difficulty, unfriendly, had almost no ammo item spawns (beyond a small handful where they were necessary for a critical puzzle), meaning that you have to rely on the wrench, which sucks due to the surprisingly long reach of the puppets, or the ammo you bring forward with NG+. The problem there is that the minigun is unlocked at the very end of the game, is fantastic, and has a deep enough ammo reserve that as long as you're somewhat conservative with your shots by not leaving it on full spray at every puppet, you'll get to the last room with ammo to spare. The 2 bosses in the game are also kind of week, with one being a "shoot it in the weakpoints until it dies" sort of deal and the other being a "just shoot it" type. Overall, if you want a weird but surprisingly heartfelt game with fun survival horror elements and a neat sort of twist on the concept of mascot horror, this is worth giving a chance.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: It's always a welcome surprise when a new Survival Horror instalment manages to juggle its horror with its humour and actually succeed with flying colours. The whole game is a treat and my only regret was not playing it on the hardest difficulty first to truly appreciate how scarce its resources could get.The story was a treat, though it did feel undercooked. It was easy to follow the narrative from start to end, but it felt like whatever themes the game was trying to explore just weren't tied well enough in with the gameplay itself. I think what the game needed to stick the landing with the story would've been a This feels like a game I could easily see myself coming back to, just for the gameplay alone. The controls in-particular just feel so smooth and enjoyable. Kudos to the people who fine-tuned it!
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: Genuinely excellent old school Resident Evil Homage full of love and care. Well Paced. Excellent Map Design. Killer Atmosphere.  Incredible ambient noise / OST.   I see some people complain about being given too many resources but I guess I'm a huge dumb ass cause I was always on the verge of running out of resources until the end game.  If I had to zonk the game for something I would say the climax is a little deflating.   Regardless of that hang up I would whole heartedly recommend this game to a fan of the old school survival horror genre or perhaps someone who is curious about this style of gameplay but is turned off by the ultra violence and gore as its a shining example of the genre done right.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot I wanna say about this game. First of all? It has been TOTALLY worth the wait. I followed its development on the creators Twitter. It is everything I hope it would be, and I am more than satisfied.This is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up Sesame Street nightmare. Only it's not. If you're looking for blood and guts and gore? You're not gonna get it here. The horror here is largely psychological. It's a head trip. Everything is so bright and colorful.... The environment feels too perfect. It is unnaturally perfect. It feels alien. It feels like you have stepped into a place that is wrong. It's a trap. It's a gauntlet. You are in for a fight and a challenge.There are puppets EVERYWHERE. They are bright and colorful and cartoony and weird and freaky AF. Tenacious as hell. And they are a THREAT. Don't underestimate them. They say some of the most demented s#!t. Treat yourself and let them run their lines BEFORE you start smacking them around. They're a wonderful combination of freaky as hell and hilarious. I mean, just some of the most messed up stuff. 10/10 dialogue and voice acting. And there IS voice acting! You're not a voiceless, emotionless, bland protagonist. You're a grumpy, crotchety old war veteran working as a handyman and you swing a mean wrench when you're not blasting puppets with the charmingly eccentric firearms.Smacking puppets down with the wrench is VERY satisfying.The story here is dark, haunting, twisted..... And it genuinely stabbed me in the feels by surprise. I'm not going to spoil it by going into details. But, damn. I was really not expecting it. There are scares and surprises and more scares. Freaky freakout surprises and twists. It's a darned good ride.The gameplay is challenging. Puzzles everywhere and a real-time inventory management system. (Yes, inspired by RE:4 blah blah get over it.) If you're looking for mechanics that are revolutionary and would change the industry? You're not going to find it here. But, they work, they're effective. Cleverly executed and satisfying. I DO love the Duct Tape mechanic.You can't jump. There is no jumping. Oh well. No real big deal there. I figure the main character is in his 70's. A 70 year old man ain't jumping for nothin, if he can avoid it. It makes sense.There isn't much in the way of stealth, but the puppets seem to be very nearsighted. Don't get too close and don't get seen and you'll have a bit of breathing room. But, there is absolutely NO avoiding them completely or for very long. You're in for a fight. They mean business.My review doesn't cover everything, largely because I'm actually trying NOT to spoil anything for everyone. But I really want to emphasize that there is an outstanding amount of POSITIVE here. The negative is absolutely negligible and doesn't matter in the grand scheme of things.This was 200% worth the wait, for me. I love the hell out of it. It is a STRONG first installment and I very much want a sequel. I very much hope there will be.This is getting a concrete 9/10 from me. Not my perfect game. But, damn it has been an experience not to be missed.Get it. Love it. This is something really genuinely very special. Most importantly? It is FUN. Get it.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: Originally, when I first looked at this game, I thought that this just a typical uninspiring mascot horror game made to monetize  ♥♥♥♥. But after I watched the YouTubers enjoy playing the game, I see some potential from this game and I decided to play the game.My Friendly Neighborhood is a like Resident Evil and Bioshock but with puppets inspired by Sesame Street or The Muppets. The game shows that the developers have put love and care to the game and breaks a lot of common mascot horror tropes.The story has a great massage that people should have faith and hope for the good despite leaving in the broken world of war, agony, and sadness, and it is up to them to become a beacon of hope to spread the light.The only bad thing about this game is the pricing, but with the cheats I have collected along with the new difficulties I unlocked, perhaps there is some replay-ability which I will try it later.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: Tight 7 hour experience, definitely quality over quantity, and very much worth your time. I would recommend playing on normal as the very beginning of the game is tough to teach you the mechanics of balancing encounters with health/saving. Ups the ante when you can't just heal and save through all problems. Great stuff overall!
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: I had an amazing fun time. Despite many inspirations from Resident Evil for mechanics, this game truly is something unique on it's own. More than that! I had an absolute blast. 10/10! However, my one and only tru complaint is that they had an opportunity with The Punctuation. The Punctuation should've exploded into characters such as . , ? ! ' ; :Other then that! AWESOME STUFF!
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: My Friendly Neighborhood takes what we love about games like the Resident Evil & Bioshock series and mixes it with a dash of Seasme Street to create something truly unique. MFN was a riot to play! No doubt about it, it's a fresh spin on an old classic. I truly loved the characters in this game, their aggressive personality was offset by the cute and cuddly appearance. The controls were easy enough to adapt to and the inventory management was crisp a la RE4. The story was well written and kept my attention making me want to grab ever little morsel and nod to the lore of this story! I wouldn't categorize this so much a blood curdling horror but there were a few jump scares and when low on ammo being chased by a puppy it sure to cause some stress.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: Did you ever ask yourself what if someone made a survival horror game similar to Resident Evil, but instead of zombies they were puppets, and instead of playing a young handsome Leon, you were an angry New York electrician? Me neither. That's what you get though and it works great. It's not a scary game, unless you have pupaphobia.The game offer challenge in puzzles, memorizing small things, and managing your supplies. You have a couple ways to deal with puppets. Knocking them down is temporary until you re-enter a room, but you have limited tape you can find that makes you decide which areas you want to just nullify the puppet threats and which you can just skirt by saving your tape for better areas.Voice acting is well done. From your grumpy electrician Gordan, to the rambling puppets. All who seems to mindlessly yammer on quoting their defunct children's show mashed in with some oddly creepy lines. The game has a couple choices you can make as well which adds to the replay value, also the cheats you can find on top of a couple different difficulties and modes.All in all the creators of this game did a great job story wise and in the game play. Hope to see more from them in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: GOTY so far! It feels fresh while hearkening back to games like Resident Evil and Bioshock. Though touted as a horror game, it could be better described as "eerie" than "scary". Much more of my time was spent laughing than quivering.The animation, writing, and voice acting is excellent. Maybe not the most challenging puzzles you'll ever encounter, but it's a well thought-out experience through and through.As an adult gamer with not a ton of time, this game is perfect - Finished it in a little over 5 hours, and missed plenty of stuff along the way. Might play it again!
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: A charming little survival horror game! Looks like your run of the mill mascot horror game but felt like an absolute ode to some of the core elements of some of those classic survival horror games. The puzzles were rather in-depth and you can tell the love and care that the creators had in making this. Resident evil but silly.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: What can I say? This game is charming, funny, a little peculiar thing.  The black humor is not forced, nothing here is forced. Unpretentious plot, sometimes funny, sometimes dark, tells about quite important issues. This is not another FNAF clone, or stories straight out of the increasingly boring and predictable "analog horror" trend. Some scenes are touching. I love how the main character can befriend or help certain characters he meets. In terms of gameplay, it reminded me more of System Shock Remake than Bioshock (I've encountered such comparisons). Also reminds me older Resident Evil titles. A lot more puzzles, inventory management here. I was concerned about the fact that saving the game requires the use of coins, which we find during the gameplay - but this one is so balanced and designed that, playing on the highest difficulty level available at the beginning, I never had a problem with making a save. I never had to replay a longer part of the game. Taking care of your inventory, deciding when to use duct tape and when to make a save, really keeps you hooked.The only thing I don't like is that the discard option in the inventory doesn't require any additional approval - the only major problem I found.A great game that I recommend to any person open to non-standard plot solutions, a somewhat surreal world, strangeness, humor and a certain dose of emotion.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game. It's been awhile since I had been immersed in a game world like this. Horror is subjective so me saying it didn't scare me doesn't mean it won't you, but I appreciated things not being over the top in terms of horror. I think this game is a perfect example of the horror survival formula being a fun and satisfying gameplay style that works when paired with a good theme. Can tell there are more secrets I missed, I want to go back and get different endings and figure out things I found but never solved.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: This was a fun little game. The puzzles were a little bit annoying at times and the combat left a lot to be desired, but overall it was a good time. I'll probably play it again in a few months. My only real complaint is that it feels somewhat expensive given that the game is probably only 4-6 hours long for most people.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: Fun and not to difficult. It was not a traditional horror game but I think that added to the charm. Glad the puppets weren't "possessed" like is common in indy horror games. The unlocks add a lot of fun too. Looking out of bounds with the free camera mode is so fun.I hope in a patch the devs will make it so shot ammo will despawn once it reaches a certain number of shots on the ground. The neighborhoard mode tanks on fps when i use the unlimited ammo and alternate ammunition cheats. And Gobblette makes the whole area shake in her neighborhoard map.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: Norman : How? Just get me out of here! That's right! Grab your dad's toolbox, take the hammer, and crack that TV screen right open. Go ahead! You have no idea how many friends are in here. Sure is lonely these days...I can only hope one thing .... make a sequel and alot of dlc's for this one, yes it is that good.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very very good. I highly recommend it. The whole atmosphere of the environments and the story are really good. The guns that you acquire are also great, fitting with the style of the game. The two things I dislike about this game are the fact that I feel that the base game is very short, which is why New Game+ content exists after beating the game. The other thing I didn't like was how towards the end of the game, there's a whole night scene with actually scary enemies and a decent boss fight, but I wish we had more levels in that dark style, because it was legitimately scary. Maybe hopefully they make a DLC where you go back and have to fight off those enemies, because they were underused in my opinion. Other than that, the game is great, and is a good 5 hours if you want to be a completionist or you know where you're going.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: This was a very fun game. It has a lot of replay value. There were things I missed and does not opened my first play through. Also, seeing there’s a achievement to get an S ranking on unfriendly mode is motivation and pure insanity. The art was also amazing. Some games I hate running back and forth to do tasks, this game was beautiful and muppets hiding around every corner that it wasn’t burning running around the map. _childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: Yes I received this product for free, but I have been a Patron of John Szymanski for years so I have actually paid for it, and would gladly pay full price for this game.Resident Evil has come to Sesame Street! I never thought shooting Ernie would be so much fun, but gosh darn-it (Excuse my language) it is a blast! The combat loop feels satisfying, the resource management fair and the puzzles are easy enough to not be frustrating but difficult enough to make you feel smart when you accomplish them,This game was made with love and enough time and effort was put into it to make it smooth and polished with no bugs (that I found). My only complaint is that the playground doesn't work, see-saws and the merry-go-round are frozen in place. Other then that 10/10!
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: [Works on Steam Deck]I've yet to finish this game, but honestly it may be the best game I've played in a good while - it's as if Resident Evil had a baby with Sesame Street in the best possible way.As a lifelong resident evil fan, seeing so many things that are call backs or references to the original games in this just makes me insanely happy, right down to the calming music in the saferooms. (There's way more but I won't spoil it for anyone else hoping to play!)I immediately fell in love with this game and all I have to say is... Uhhh... Can we get a merch drop asap please??9/10

_childDocuments_.review: This game is shockingly good. Mascot horror has been a defining genre last 10 years and has been building up. This is one of the biggest things to hit the mascot horror genre and I am shocked at the quality. This game is a bit more than mascot horror games, but worth investing in because you are helping some devs. Fun game to play and thought provoking.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: So as a child did you ever watch sesame street and think, hmmmm I sure hope those puppets never want to chase me down and murder me with there felt covered fists....welp living out your childhood fear is now a game mixed in with all the trauma of adult life. Yes you to can venture forth upon the nightmare fuelled fields of the puppet horror show of My not so friendly Neighbourhood and have a lot of fun doing it.  The game visually is amazing. It captures the essence of old school puppet shows like sesame street or the Muppets(even some mister rogers) meaning no matter your age you will get something out of this that you will identify with. Voices are spot on. Some reminded me of bert from sesame street, Grover from the Muppets etc. I do like how the main character is even voice acted. A lot of games skip that now thinking it helps with immersion but I feel it takes away from it. Game play wise I didnt run into any bugs until after I beat the game. You have the option of replaying and you can unlock special modes based on your play(this isnt a spoiler as the game makes this clear when you start) but it was one and it was distance between were I help the weapon and where enemy would appear on the map. Now admitedly I have not gone through the modes after beating the game yet I did try the ultra hard mode and if you keep with base settings I cant even imagine how you would pass as it triples the enemys but not the ammo soooooo good luck and stream or record it for proof. I am positive no one has beaten it on base settings yet. Now although you see I got this for free(thanks dreadxp you were my first dev support game means a lot), I stream and I am Very big into community trust and integrity so if the game had faults I would have wrote them out(constructively I believe in improvement not being a tool) but besides maybe getting a little lost once or twice I don't have any. The game is just so different and you can see how much love went into it.  So if this sounds appealing in the words of the evil muppets , its time to play the game, its time to turn out the lights, its time to meet the puppets in my friendly neighbourhood tonight.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: So it's overall good and I would recommend!BUT, it's less puzzle than I was expecting.  It's a LOT of walking from place to place working out what you've missed, and not as much puzzle as I had expected, so if you're expecting puzzles maybe dodge it unless you're obsessed/terrified of puppets like I am. A big part of it is thinking about where you need to go to get xyz item, for example.   Having said that, the general vibe and storyline is really good. The voice acting is incredible, and I also absolutely adore the Elmo characters (you'll know which ones I mean when you play it).  Like a lot of people have said it gets a bit weird when it starts talking about war which throws you off a bit because it absolutely doesn't fit with the storyline until that point but still, the overall premise remains.  I'd also say it's a liiiiiitle bit pricey for how long it plays.  When you complete it there's a bunch of options to play it again and do it better but really to me there's no incentive to do that because you already know what's coming.  Either way, despite the slightly pricey pricey pricetag, it's worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: MFN is by far one of the best indies to manage being faithful to the games that inspired it. The devs clearly cared a lot about this project and had a lot of fun making it. It doesn’t feel like all those other horror games with cute mascots that are trying to appeal to kids but are really not be for them, I feel like you could sit down with your kids and play this as it doesn’t really have anything scarier than the scariest scene out of a Disney movie in it. Would 100%recommend to anyone who likes RE games or even just puppets
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game, with lots of goofy lines. The art style is very fun and everything matches thematically in a way that's very satisfying. I've played through a couple of times now trying to get all the achievements, but also just enjoying the game play. I just wish the game was longer! Definitely play it, it's an experience.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, very lovely game. Very interesting aesthetic, a setting that isn't explored in this kind of game very often, solid level design, actually pretty fun writing. However, a few issues:1)Too much backtracking in  the later section, especially when they're pulling a few tricks to cut off some of your routes, feels tedious2) Its basically impossible to turn the field of view up to a significant degree without some issues in any part where the protagonist uses their hands3) There is no warning when you skip a cutscene. During one late game sequence, I tried to pause the game during a cutscene. No indication given, not at least requiring ESC to be held down to avoid an accident, it just skipped it without warning. To add insult to injury, the game autosaved over my save, so I couldn't even load it back up to go through it again, I had to check a youtube playthrough.4) Final section could have been expanded upon a bit, felt a bit shallow. Great music for that last encounter though.

_childDocuments_.review: can't seem to stop releasing games that capture player's attention. This time it's a game in the genre that everyone seemengly hates right now, not without a reason. With disappointments like  it can be hard to look at something like My Friendly Neighborhood and not get disgusted automatically. However , after you dive into it you'll realize that .Right from the get go game lets you understand that it's a . It's a perfect game for people that are overwhelmed by gore, darkness and tension in games like , that want to experience this genre, but couldn't. However  either because gameplay-wise it's excellent and deserve to be called "a survival horror kind of game". Despite its cartoonish nature the game is not a cakewalk, it's not going to test your reflexes or make you memorize enemy placements, but rather focus on minimizing resource spendings and your ability to strategize about which enemy to dispose of. In great survival horror fashion, you have . This game definitely was built with replayability in mind, its short runtime and whooping 5 difficulties along tons of unlockables confirms this.Narrative is surprisingly strong, and some unique interactions you can get with puppets can be touching at times. I definitely wasn't expecting such approach to this mascot horror theme and this made the experience like 10 times better, but I guess I should've known that DreadXP has something very cool prepared, they don't make bad games after all. Definitely worth the full price.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: My Friendly Neighborhood was theorized to be similar in the vane of what games were becoming after Five Nights at Freddy's. Well I'm proud to say that it does NOT fall into those tropes of possession, demons, or any other cliche that most mascot horror games take pages from in FNAF. I wish I could say why but that would lean into spoiler territory, so let's go over the basics of what I think of the game itself~The Good=~I love how the puzzles are handled, feels exactly how it was back in the old days of Resident Evil for the PS1. You need to actually memorize patterns, time things and pay attention to your surroundings!~The story is really good as it's setting feels like a completely different take on the horror genre and I'm happy it actually went in a new direction!~ Graphically decent on my end at least!~The secrets are well hidden and still require some brainpower and a lot of backtracking, but after solving them you feel like a genius! There's still even some secrets I missed! The VHS tape cheats you find are a joy to collect as well because they are hidden cheats and you feel accomplished when you either open a room to find them or even look down and see one below you in certain spaces where you didn't think to look!~Lorewise is pretty depressing and very relatable~ Won't say much more than that!~Voice acting is pretty swell! Especially coming from Ricky and Gordon! Arlo (The Youtuber Puppet get) was an interesting choice even tho I'm not a fan of his content, I still am glad he got to work on this!The Bad=~The combat is hit or miss for me. Whenever I try to strike with my wrench, I have no idea if it's going to hit the puppet or not. The length of hitting them is so off and weird. I feel like I need to get close to attack, but if I do, I get damaged! And no matter how many times I wack at them I cannot for the life of me tell when they will go down. There's no way to tell unless you hit other parts of their bodies at least through my experience.~The standard gun suffers the same problem. Sometimes when I hit a puppet, I have NO idea if my hits would take them down. It feels like I'm wasting ammo whenever I shoot them because there's no indication on where to shoot them or if it's working. And other times when I go out from a door, I see some handpuppets staring at me chattering. I try to shoot, but the letters just don't hit them unless I'm in a certain spot! Like it seems at rare times you try to hit them, but the letters seem to go somewhere else rather than hitting the annoying pests!=Item management is more of a mixed thing as it's a mechanic that was a staple in the original Resident Evil, but I've seen some times where a player discarded a key and it actually softlocked their game. Sometimes I was scared to throw away my shape keys as I felt they would be important to the story as well as extra stuff. Well thank God I did, but it still feels a bit off to people who aren't used to that mechanic...~Do NOT throw away your tokens. I made that mistake and I couldn't get back to the first boss to try again. Again, like the format they used from RE, but can still feel a bit jarring to people who haven't played them.Overall, the only weird glitches I've encountered is sometimes a voice clip of Gordon wouldn't play on really rare occasions and the puppets going into walls or ragdoll glitching like crazy when they are knocked out.But I still loved how this game performed, and with it being open ended with lots of places to explore and backtrack to, it's something that can be dabbled with for a short while as there are tons of secrets and extras you can find.As well as cheatcodes and the idea of speed running this game, it's actually a really good example on what the horror indie scene can do without relying on FNAF elements of the past!So happy I invested in this. Still needs some bug patching as well as more forgiving aspects regarding saving your game but I say keep up the good work!I give this game a 7.5/10! A good experience!
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: Unbelievably good, really resonated with me as a big fan of Resident Evil and Bioshock. I hope we get something similar to this but bigger from these devs!Update: Second playthrough done on Veteran difficulty, had even more fun since I was straddling the line of not having enough resources the WHOLE way through, best way to do it, shame it only unlocks after beating the game once. Also my single complaint in the game, the insta-telekinetic-grabs. I get melee isn't supposed to be strong but you should at least be able to avoid hits from enemies.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: I think this game is very fun. This is a semi horror humor experience with some puzzles along the way. It is a decent amount of time to beat the game but I will say the length of the game compared to its price is good. I like the creature designs and all the things involving the map design. Now as much as I can go on about how much I like the game let me tackle some of the negatives. There is some visual bugs with cut scenes that make your hands just float outwards during them but I am playing on day 1. This game is also not very descriptive with your objective leaving you puzzled and confused sometimes. The bird creature just seems to be their and from what I could tell not even a threat so its almost like a waste of a enemy. There isn't tons of crazy entities with the game only having mostly the puppets and then 1 unique one per zone making it seem bland for the characters. Although it is a shorter length game it still kinda sucks when it feels so barren. Last thing I have to complain about is the voice lines. I think they are very fun and creative to hear but after a while its the same old same old. It would be nice to have the roster expanded upon for the voices that the puppets make. Maybe even if they threw in some unique ones that are situational to whats going on around them. Even with those negatives I still think the game is really fun most of the time and I hope you people enjoy it to
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly cannot recommend this game enough. As someone who grew up on Sesame Street, it's both a horror and a delight to be thrown into this bizarro world of puppet shenanigans. The puppets stand in corners and talk to themselves (the audience) about things like the daily mail, the foods they eat, and how they're just really friendly. Even when you tape them up, they continue to talk about these things and it cracks me up. Beautiful story, beautiful playful graphics, and really fun gameplay.The only thing that really threw me off is trying to aim some of the weapons without a crosshair. I definitely wasted many letters (ammo) because I couldn't quite line things up from time to time. Thankfully, letters are fairly plentiful. Maybe a stamina bar could be added for when candy bars are consumed?
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: Really loved this game. It's a perfect blend of adventure, spooky, humor and puzzles. Your job is to shut down the mysterious broadcast and you have to go through various levels, when you will meet the puppets, who's job is to annoy you. But you can also help some of them, which can be rewarding in the end. The puzzles are nice and some one the them require a bit of thought. The only think I didn't like was the save system, which makes you find tokens in order to save, luckily there are just about enough of them in the world, but it can still get annoying. Overall it's an enjoyable exploration game above all.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: Small review considering I've been enjoying this game a lot actually. Sesame Street meets Resident Evil mechanics & game play feel! I really like how sizable the game is with the story and level design. A lot of back tracing but once you've gotten all maps, you can get an idea of the whole scope once you've did a few puzzles here & there. Very fun game that was made convenient to have many reruns: making it interesting with different modes it has with unlocking and beating the game's many difficulties. Really goofy at times as well with the AI having many lines of dialogue; talking about random stuff that a kids T.V. show would conjure up I guess but it's just humorous considering the setting. You will experience this a lot once you defeat the puppets lingering around the studio, and yeah. The tape mechanic of them being less of a barrier is nice to have for clearance around certain areas if available. Also has a feel of Bioshock with the weapons & the Healing Vigors remind of Infinite's Vigors you can get and grants you different abilities when found. Gun plays feels great, melee with the wrench can feel sometimes redundant due to how many times you have to slap a puppet. Along with just cheats, makes it sorta useless but then again. It does help with ammo scarcity when you're on higher difficulty so I guess there is an argument to be made for it not being totally useless.I definitely enjoyed so far my time with the Mini Gun you can find with a secret fuse puzzle but I won't say anymore about that. Overall the game is just really nice with it's narrative, being a good reminder with the concept and stand in of kid shows or even FNAF stuff. Gems like this can do something different and stand out, because of it's overall telling message.It definitely warped my expectations and I was genuinely surprised on how much I've come to enjoy My Friendly Neigborhood with my time spent finding all the clues and reading the lore of the game. just makes me glad something like this currently exist in a time where Mascot Horror imo is taking a predictable turn and lacking innovation so this was a well needed game for the community to dive into. And with all of the silly stuff aside though: It's a great game that wears it's influences on it's shoulder and the more you play it, you actually realize it uses those influences correctly. Making the experience feel pretty smooth from start to finish with it's game play.I do recommend this one with 100% approval. It's quirky, light-hearted, and charming at times. Not scary at all imo but then again. I am a horror junkie so it's hard to scare me nowadays with any game in this vein. But don't let that stop you from checking this out. You can find that this game is disturbing and horrifying in a different way other than visuals. At first glance: the neighborhood seems fine, til you visit the studio...  Check it out! Good price, definitely worth your time!
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: I've been following this game for a year now and I'm insanely happy with the final version. A puppet horror game is a great concept and all of the voices are spot on. My favorite ones so far are the tiny ones that sound like elmo. If anything needs an update I wish the map showed where the save stations are. Also what rooms you haven't been in yet had a different color.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: The story is a game that conveys a lot of thoughts as the game progresses. In fact, it asks so many philosophical questions that it seems to be a game that is closer to a work of art rather than a game.What's unfortunate about the convenience of gamers is that when you visit an area, if you don't find a "map" quickly, it becomes a tough exploration. Fortunately, the map structure is not that complicated, so you will get used to it quickly if you wander for about an hour.Level design has a lot of shortcuts, like "Dark Soul". This is also a considerable advantage if you adapt, but if you haven't found a "map" or if the map structure is unfamiliar, it acts as a disadvantage and becomes a complicated factor. (Please keep in mind that I'm at the level of being blind when I can't navigate well. I'm sure Everyone'll find way better than me. lol)Overall, i deeply hope it is such a great game that I think it would be good to win the Indie category at this year's Game Awards. It is safe to say that it is an art wearing a mask of game and a philosophical genre wearing a mask of horror genre.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: Just a short review:A genuinely and surprisingly enjoyable experience, albeit a little short. You play as a handyman tasked with finding out what's wrong at a local kids show studio, and the story unfolds. The story is nothing to write home about, but it is serviceable. I didn't find the game terribly unnerving, but I did enjoy its silly, wacky take on the genre.On the gameplay side of thing, you'll be playing in first person, exploring the environment, solving puzzles and picking up weapons/ammunition, akin to newer RE titles. Even as a non-hardcore-horror fan, I could see the passion behind the development of this game, and its paying homage to old-school horror titles like Resident Evil (i.e: inventory system and even the door opening animation is reminiscent of old RE games). All in all, a short and sweet play.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: My god!I have been awaiting this game ever since I saw the teaser and demo for it over a year ago and, my god, they delivered!!!This game is a survival "horror" game, with lots of comedy, quips, humor and fun!The game-play was lots of fun and always moving with a great pace, it never felt like there were any filler parts or any moments where the game-play was slow. It was always moving forward with great energy!At the end of my play-through, all I wanted to do was play through it more, try out the challenge achievements, and just enjoy the game more!Bravo to the game developers for delivering such an amazing game!High recommendation from me! Pick it up, you won't be disappointed!
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who is relatively new to the Survival Horror genre, having only really played games like the Resident Evil 2 Remake and Signalis, this was mechanically just as satisfying to play while putting up a dark comedy of, "What if Sesame Street was cancelled and the puppets just went a little bonkers?"My first playthrough was on Survival difficulty right off the bat and I completed it in one sitting around 7 1/2 hours and am currently going for all the achievements, it's that fun. Having a grouchy repairman relate to the puppets and actually learn lessons was a fantastic touch to the plot and reminds you of those morals you grew up learning from PBS shows.Just a great entry to the Survival Horror and even mascot horror genre without it being another FNAF or gorey-depressing-zombie-apocalypse game.5/5, Goblette deserves the best in life. They're right, you know-- it's hard to be friendly when cash is king.Game also seems to have an element of replayability through unlockable difficulties and cheats, which is nice to see. I'd say it was worth the $30, considering the above. My first playthrough took about 6 hours.[Initial Take]: Booted up the demo, saw the Szymanski name. Okay. Menus all looked... familiar; the sounds were familiar, too. Loaded into the game, saw the gun-- very familiar! Then I pressed tab: diagetic inventories! All the -bells went off and I bought it after playing through a little more of the demo.

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommend but one big caveat (originally had a negative review because of it but changed my review to positive in retrospect).THE GOOD:We finally have a game with the idea of a children's product going wrong that isn't jump scare cliche shock. It's a really well designed survival "horror" (it's not scary but I don't think it was meant to be) game, that isn't a walking simulator, with engaging voice acting and narrative.The art direction, level design, puzzles, great resource managing (with one big issue I discuss later), and gameplay are really engaging. You will feel like you have natural idea of where to go or backtrack to and make constant decisions to use your items/weapons or not. It also rewards exploration and critical thinking with one really cool unlock you get later if you pay attention.The levels are very creatively interconnected and no area over stays its welcome. I genuinely wished there was more, but I'm glad I felt that and not bored by the end.And the story is mature and bittersweet that is surprisingly optimistic for the genre. There's also no gore, it manages to be unsettling without any overtly shocking aspects.As well, the devs made it very user friendly with the settings menu being the first thing that opens before the game starts and it also runs very well at least on my rig (except for some instances I mention in the negative section.)I am genuinely impressed by how much better two guys designed their game than big studios often do. It was clearly made with passion and love, instead of opportunistic streamer fodder.There are a few moments that did get me by surprise and one "scary" section but overall it's more intriguing and thought provoking than fear inducing.THE BAD:My original review was negative due to the limited save system using an item you only get so much of, that can only be circumvented on easy mode (so you have to give up difficulty in a not particularly difficult game to get a basic QOL convinience) This is really aggravating and almost made me give up the game for a number of reasons.1. Game crashes. My game crashed 4 times at least on my 3080, and one time soft locked. Since I can't save more regularly I lost a lot of progress that I had to redo due to the general instability of PC gaming.2. It's very easy to accidentally waste save tokens. When the game loads it automatically starts you facing the save machine for some reason and if you forget and click the action button during the load or right after, immediately spends a token and saves. No confirmation window, no way to undo. So you can end up losing tokens really easily.3. I get it's a staple of the genre, but not everyone has hours to put in every session. Sometimes you can't keep playing or keep your PC running until the next time and if you have other things in your life can really make this game inaccessible to many people who would enjoy it.If the limited saves felt integral to the design I'd say then it's a niche product. But it really isn't. The game isn't hard enough on the highest initial difficulty you can chose to warrant it. I never really died due to anything but absent mindedness or impatience. The tension is great on its own without the gimmick.I wish they would give an option for unlimited saves without sacrificing difficulty or make it part of the unlockable difficulties you get after completion.TL/DR: Great game that is surprisingly unique and a great throwback to true survivor horror that deserves recognition and sales but really needs to have a more flexible save system.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh god yes.I remember playing the demo for this game in what feels like ages ago, and becoming completely captivated with its style of comedic horror. I added the game to my wishlist, and patiently waited for its release. Boy, was it worth the wait. I've been playing for 5 hours so far (ignore my Steam time, I play offline too), and I'm still totally enamored.I'm a huge fan of Resident Evil 7-style games, ones with inventory management and an overlapping world with distinctive zones and enemies. The developers of this game clearly know what they're doing; this world is brimming with creativity and stellar game design.As far as complaints go, I've only got one minor nitpick. The puppet characters in the game have a decent amount of dialogue that they splurge out constantly, and it's very funny and unsettling at the same time. I do wish, however, that the characters would have unique dialogue, rather than shared. Once I heard Norman and Junebug start speaking the same line simultaneously, and it's a little immersion breaking. I get the point of repetitious dialogue, and it makes for a very creepy childlike-horror vibe (similar to one you'd find in an episode of Doctor Who), but I would be overjoyed if more lines came in a future patch. That's asking for a lot, but you never know what could happen :)Please buy this game and support the developers. This has everything I want out of a survival horror experience, and I hope they continue to produce content on the same level of quality.

_childDocuments_.review: A deeply charming, fun and slightly unhinged game.Kind of like Resident Evil 7 meets Sesame Street.I wouldn't say its scary or particular challenging on survival difficulty. I ended up caring about Gordon and the Neighbourhood much more than I had thought. Probably helps that the audio/visual aspect of the game is very strong, in my opinion.There's also a lot of additional content after the campaign such as cheats, a horde mode, and additional/unlockable difficulty levels.Overall, I really strongly recommend this one.P.S. If there is a Szymanski involved, It's a good game.

_childDocuments_.review: This was my first RE type game and it was the best possible introduction I could have had to this game type. I was able to beat it on Normal (not friendly) and it was fun! Otherwise it would just be too easy! In the end I horded so much of everything that I had an excess at the end of the game!Really loved the options you had with the main puppets . _childDocuments_.review: I know exactly what you think. It might look like yet another "childrens thing but horror" kind of games that are super popular on youtube despite not having any meat to them. But this really isn't one of them!Instead of focusing on super complex lore and cheap scares my friendly neighborhood focuses heavily on the "survival" part of survival horor. That means a key aspect of the game is managing ammunition, healing items and what not. Sure the game might not be as scary as other titles in this genre, but maybe that might even be exactly what sells you on this game. If you were always intrigued by the gameplay of Resident Evil, Alone in the Dark and Signalis but always put off by the themes of those games, then my friendly neighborhood is exactly what you are looking for.  The one thing that holds my friendly neighborhood back is that it shows that this is an indie game. The graphics and voice acting are bit rough around the edges but it's far from being bad or game ruining. It just reminds you that you are not playing a state of the art AAAAA videogame from time to time. At the end of the day this game might not be groundbreaking but it's a game with a lot of charme that does exactly what it promises. Worth checking out even if you aren't too big into horror games or if you look for something to play with a 12 year old.

_childDocuments_.review: My Friendly Neighbourhood is classic survival horror without the horror (mostly).The plot is mostly told in a silly and irreverent tone but there is some seriousness in the main characters backstory, and personally I did feel pretty sad for the puppets. Don't trick yourself into thinking you're just playing a generic mascot horror game, if anything it feels like an anti-mascot horror. The game doesn't really try to make the neighbours scary. They are definitely something you want to stay away from, but more in a tactical conserve health sort of way. They are very rarely presented in a way that feels unnatural for a muppet-like character and it gives the game a refreshing tone that other games with similar aesthetics don't at all hit.All of that is great, but also the game is good! the resource management is really satisfying. Early on I thought it was giving me too much ammo, but when I realised the neighbours will get up as soon as you leave a room I started to see how the tactical use of ammo and tape with a bit of ducking-and-weaving could help make runs between item boxes and puzzles stressful (but in a fun way).It's also just a really nice game to look at. The aesthetic is very charming and making it a children's TV studio in an already heightened cartoon setting definitely lets it get away with the puzzles and different zones of the lot.Honestly shaping up to be my GOTY, but also Armoured Core 6 does come out in a couple of weeks...
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely amazing Resident Evil clone bustling with personality, smart and interesting puzzles, beautiful environments with a particular artstyle that isn't so much graphically insane but just nice to look at and easy on the eyes, and much much more. The enemies you face in this game, the insane Sesame Street-esque puppets, are both hilarious and also sometimes creepy with the things they say and trust me they are ALWAYS talking, sometimes to the point of making yourself go somewhat insane but that's kind of the point. The voice acting is extremely high quality almost AAA-level honestly, which makes for an extremely memorable experience.The game has many difficulty modes to choose from, the harder ones unlocking progressively as you beat the game with harder and harder difficulties, as well as TONS of very cool and sometimes downright hilarious modes and cheats the change that game in many ways and add a lot of extra replay-ability. The different areas are very intricately designed and function very well as Resident Evil/Silent Hill-esque survival horror areas and are very fun to explore and work through. I could say more but honestly you should definitely go into this game as blind as humanly possible, especially if you are in any way a fan of Resident Evil or really horror games in general you will appreciate it a lot more.TLDR: 9/10, absolutely amazing Resident Evil clone, lots of replayablity, lots of personality, top tier voice acting, get it now.

_childDocuments_.review: I personally think it's just ok, but you'll probably like it.Just ok, I don't usually score games but this is like a 6 or 7 out of 10. The first 3 hours are very good and the novelty of it carries it that far but the backtracking for story progression especially in the latter half is so painfully dull. I spent a lot of time holding the forward button. The gun play is good even if the gun options are very limited (3), Normal difficulty is perfect, the puzzles are good even if I think there are too many. I think most of my gripes could have been handled by making the garden and movie puzzles solutions in the same area the puzzles themselves are. The map is a bit confusing as well. It's about how all these little things compound on each other, especially when save tokens are involved. Saving and using the health machines consume consumable tokens and there is a finite amount. So by the end I have 3 tokens left and I explored nearly everything. So the backtracking with the limited saves made the situation of both all the worse. I don't think most people will have a problem with it. But personally come time for the 4th hour I was ready to be done with it. It's a good game, definitely above average. I'm probably the weird one here considering the rating everyone else gives but personally I really do think backtracking and the save system are not a good fit here.
