_childDocuments_.review: I just don't get it I suppose, prolly a boomer or something. I understand they're puppets and they don't need to take a breathe but the constant yammering just gave me a headache, it's like having 6 iPad kids word vomiting directly into your ear all at once. (This could be my fault, I could have missed a setting that reduced the frequency of voice lines to play not every fraction of a second.) I keep reading dev replies about how it's more of a puzzle/survival game than a horror game but honestly it didn't feel like either. The puzzles felt like monotonous fetch quests, not much to "solve", and heaven forbid you forget an item or don't have enough room as navigating the map is an arduous task. I feel like I would have enjoyed it more if there were less transitions to each area, every other door is a black loading screen, which only take milliseconds by the way, I will say the game is wonderfully optimized.As for the horror aspect, idk puppets just don't do it for me I guess, I never really felt a sense of tension or fear beyond a few cheap jumpscares. Though, there was one that I did quiet enjoy which I shall not spoil for anyone. While the visuals were amazing they just didn't add any horror element (which the game is tagged as so it's fair to criticize despite the developer claiming to not be horror focused.)To give the game credit where credit is due, it again, is optimized very well. The visuals are surprisingly great, it has this almost Bioshock-esque feel to the atmosphere and weaponry which I really truly liked. I also found a handful of the voice lines to be funny and a few of the voice actors were pretty good; in particular, Junebug (Natalie Roers) in regards to both.Back to dunking on the game though, the combat is inarguably bland, as is the "stealth" if you can call not standing in front of or too close to, an enemy stealth. The enemies kind of just meander towards you at a medial pace removing even more of the threat factor. It's kind of like when Michael Myers walks casually after his victims but in this version he just doesn't ever catch up. The enemies honestly just felt like a tedious speed bump in an already slow paced puzzle game.As for the "Lore" from what I saw it was, ehh, I'm a completionist so I was scouring every inch for all the notes, secrets, and little hidden dudes buried behind piles of rubble I could find but, wasn't too interesting to me, maybe because I didn't finish the game so I didn't piece it together at the end but what I did read just felt bland.Overall, I really wish I did enjoy it, I wanted to see the ending(s) I suspect there to be multiple endings from what I surmised. Between the tedium and sheer annoyance I unfortunately couldn't make it to the end. This is one of the times I wish Steam wasn't on a "Good" or "Bad" rating system because I feel I lean more towards "meh" than anything. You can tell the developers really care about this game, not just from the fact that they personally reply to most of the bad reviews, but just the way it looks, the way it runs, and the fact that everything in the game feels like it was looked over with a fine tooth comb twice to polish it out.Just my opinion though, obviously in the minority here as everyone and their mum loves it, just guess it wasn't for me.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: This is a pretty great game. The puppets add this unintentional accidental fear factor where they both undermine the fear, yet somehow that makes them all the creepier. Hearing someone be bright, optimistic, positive in tone while speaking about stomping their friends face in is pretty intimidating when just a minute ago he was singing in the stairwell. Though I should admit it has a few jumpscares, not many like, 3 at most and they aren't even that egregious, and I dunno if 1 counts since it was fully expected.The game also has a pretty decent background plot, one you get to piece together on your own through the various notes you find. Reporting the rise and fall of the MFN show itself, to the gritty documentation of war.My biggest complaints? Well to begin these aren't detractors from the game per say, just something I noted that struck a few questionable nerves. First inventory is a bit of hassle. While that's expected in a Resident Evil esque game to an extent, only having 1 tiny storage box to store things in doesn't make up for it. Sure you get a 2nd storage box later in the game, but it's only in like 2 to 3 locations and at that point the games 80% done and if you play like me you're pretty good at stockpiling things like a kleptomaniac gerbil and you begin to reach a 'what is the LEAST valuable thing I can afford to toss?' point.My biggest irritation is melee, while having melee can make or break a lot of survival aspects, it can be a nice rewarding method to conserve ammo. Not in this game. In this game the puppets have a longer reach than they look, longer than yours to hit them. So usually your only chance to hit them is right after they grab you, or when they get stuck on some corner, or when you abuse some longer reach jank. I found a good rhythm in shooting a puppet in the head, and if it did the flail back thing I could run up and smack it a few times. But it was rarely guaranteed to be a kill, if anything most of the time it injured me because of another subsequent problem. Inconsistent health.Enemies health in this game is all over the place. You can understand and gauge some of it. Junebug gets clapped pretty fast, the weird tiny hand puppets all go down in one hit, Lilliana didn't have a lot of health. The rest though? Could range from going down in 3 to sometimes 9 pistol shots, though you don't have to worry about the shotgun since that always was a pretty strong insta-knockout despite being a single shot. Towards the end of the game you get a minigun with only 1 clip of 999 rounds that naturally hits you in the gamer mindset of 'better save this for later, I might need it.' It feels nice to have but also kind of makes things a bit awkward in power dynamic.Sure the ammo isn't infinite, but by the time you GET the minigun you're near the end of the game and can afford to be a little careless at that point.The candy bars, they give you a speed boost for about 4 doors worth of loads I think? While that sounds like a lot, it kind of goes real fast the second you realize you double back through loading screens a lot. Sure as long as you have coins the hotel has infinite candy for you, and it stacks infinitely so you can run at mach 6 potentially if you eat enough, and make the boss fights a bit of a joke.The game starts to get really terrifying towards that tail end to, I really started to get into it at that point... The reality? That was maybe a 15 minute segment of horrors when you experienced the (REDACTED.) that get interrupted by a boss fight anyhow. Then the game just... Ends. It left me feeling, well, ironically it left me feeling a lot like a show I loved got abruptly cancelled mid-season.It's awkward, it felt like they were just starting to unpack the true horrors that no man should ever see box, only for you to walk out get offered a choice of ending, and then get the ending scene with your results. This is also pretty evident in the fact there were only 2 bosses in the game, which is fine enough but they kept introducing big enemies that I felt like were also meant to constantly harass us, only to be able to subdue or outright ignore them for a variety of methods.A game having an ending is fine, I paid full price for this and I felt like it was pretty well worth it. Especially if you just like playing on increased difficulties, or with cheats, or speedrunning. It fills that up very well.It's not a bad game, it has a lot of optional stuff and you can miss a lot of if you're careless, including the true ending which I had all the parts for but kind of forgot about because I wandered onto the 'no go back' point of the ending. Wasn't aware I did though, and I can't reload from back then to see the other ending since your game marks a file as donezo once you wrap it up. But yeah, the game has a lot of heart and passion put into it, but I do find myself wondering if it could've benefited from some more time in the oven. I abandoned my melee weapon in the name of inventory space entirely as well, since it was rarely as useful as just shooting something in the face repeatedly. I'd say it's worth the full price and I do find myself looking forward to what the devs do next.
_childDocuments_.name: My Friendly Neighborhood

_childDocuments_.review: I don't play horror games normally, but I was really interested in playing this one! It has this scary, unnerving atmosphere while still being very funny, and it was really satisfying to figure out all the puzzles, memorizing the map layout, and clearing every area of items. The mix of Sesame Street/Muppets/Resident Evil really works, and the gameplay works super smooth from grabbing items to going through doors. The Elmo voices were my favorite out of all the puppets!The game does allow for a lot of freedom when you go through the maps, but it also means that the game isn't completely linear. In the sense that, you are given multiple doors to go through when you enter an area, and you can go for a long time without finding the gun or the map if you went through a different door than the one presented directly in front of you. And there are key items that can lead to a slightly different ending, but it's not always obvious what you do with them. Or in my case, I knew what to do with them, but I couldn't figure out how the game wants me to activate them. So I ended up completing the ending without using these key items and feeling frustrated since I was waiting for some kind of direction. It's understandable that this is just the nature of the genre, but it's a hard pill to swallow essentially.Also there were times that I couldn't clear an area and it turns out there was a coin laying on the ground that needed to be collected. There weren't too many of those, but it also made it frustrating to clear areas when the more normalized places were already searched.Despite the frustrations, I love this game a lot! The puppets are very endearing, and I think that's one of the big reasons why I enjoyed this game even though I'm not so much a horror game player. The game's got a simple plot but woven with a lot of call-backs, nostalgia, and its own character. I wish there were more areas to explore, but the game has already given a lot more than I expected. I look forward to what else the developers make in the future!

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a beautiful breath of fresh air! An awesome horror game to sink time into and an interesting story at that. _childDocuments_.review:
Something is amiss with everyone's favorite Saturday morning puppet show! For years, the colorful cast of The Friendly Neighborhood delighted audiences across the globe with their cooky capers and educational adventures. However, as time went on and interest waned, the production studio found themselves out of money and closed their doors for good.

Toy sales would dwindle, and birthday balloons and cakes would find new mascots. In time, the once household names would fade into increasingly niche fandoms. Until one night years later, the studio unexpectedly clicks back to life and starts broadcasting The Friendly Neighborhood. TV sets across the globe flicker for a moment before the familiar puppets return for a surprise encore!

Play as Gordon, a repairman sent to get to the bottom of this disturbing dilemma. Fend off puppets and solve puzzles in this survival horror adventure.

detailed_description: Obsessed with occult rituals, you have finally obtained the last thing you need to summon the eldritch horror that has been haunting your dreams; a strange, bright-pink Necronomicon. You perform the only ritual that doesn’t appear to be insane ramblings, and inadvertently summon Ln’eta, a cute cthulhu-like girl. She agrees to a kiss, on the condition that you perform a few rituals from the book for her first. Looking back at the Necronomicon… all of the other pages suddenly make sense? Three chapters of laughs, screams, and tears, all in one thick package! Every decision you make will significantly affect gameplay and determine which ending you arrive at! Immersive re-imagining of the visual novel genre loaded with gameplay! 'Three' 'fully-voiced' 'dateable' 'girls' A stylish artistic/musical direction reminiscent of old-school anime and dating sims! No horror elements or danger whatsoever

_childDocuments_.review: When people talk about next gen they should be talking about games like this.The game is less than 1GB (as of right now) and runs smoothly all the time. The low poly artstyle along with the amazing color choices and shading makes the game look wonderful for what it is. Meanwhile you have games that are 50+GB and they look and run terribly because they went for realistic rather than going for a solid artstyle.The gameplay is also very pleasing and what makes it all come together. The summoning is somehow always enticing due to how much it benefits your quests for smooches. The combat section is also ever constant to provide you with challenge and the threat of failure; which will happen if you don't be careful. The game allows you to take your time by allowing you the luxury of choosing when you want to leave. There are also enough routes to avoid monotony. The book ritual system is very simple with handy text descriptions that aren't game breaking but just makes things easier.Overall a very fun game

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the perfect balance of meet-cute dating sim, chthonic horror (and yes, it can get horrifying), and comedy.  If you like visual novels and/or dating sims, this is a good send-up of those.  It's fully English voiced, which is nice.Fair warning, the true ending is much harder than the rest of the game.  It's like "story, story, story, BAM quicktime events!" It is short, but I think it's the right length for the humor and story.  Also, if you're looking for nudity, this is not your game.  It never gets more lewd than a smooch.

_childDocuments_.review: H.P. Lovecraft once said that fear of the unknown is the strongest fear of mankind, but what if you want to grab that unknown by the shoulders and plant a wet, sloppy smooch all over it's face? Well, this game basically tells you what happens. The game is literally what you would expect from it. You do dark rituals to summon eldritch horrors, you date them and try to win their smooches all for yourself. The writing in Sucker for Love is charming and funny throughout, but you still feel the pangs of fear once things start to go sideways. I think this is due to the time pressure from few of the scenes plus the more intense time pressure of the secret route, which is something you don't see in VNs that often. The gameplay involves talking to and performing rituals for your lovely lady horrors. The theme for these rituals change for each girl, as such it keeps the main mechanics of the game fresh even though you're still doing pretty much the same things. If you look past the thirsty meme reviews talking about how they want to bang that Cthussy and leave your expectations of cringe behind you, this game will un-ironically be amazing. The game parodies on dating sim games, human nature and Lovecraftian elements while also somehow doing all of them justice very well. The humour is also very funny and had me laughing out loud multiple times. And with the words of the protagonist: "3D women are fine, but fourth dimensional girls with non-euclidean geometry are smokin' hot! They've got curves I can literally get lost in." I leave you to choose for yourself: Are you ready to smooch those Lovecraftian Horrors? The answer is yes. obviously.and Aunty Nyan Nyan can step on me any day.
_childDocuments_.name: Sucker for Love: First Date

_childDocuments_.review: Forget the memes. Forget the lame "I got to kiss tentacle lady 10/10" reviews. Forget your expectations of cringe. THIS IS UNIRONICALLY A GOOD GAME. I generally think that overly ironic humor has been done to death and I usually pass on games like this by because I find their gimmicks to be boring, but this game was a pleasant surprise. It parodies dating sims, human nature, and Lovecraftian elements while also somehow doing them all justice? Oh, and it's laugh out loud funny. I'm not a weeb and I find a lot of anime tropes to be kind of obnoxious but the protagonist is shown to be extremely likable and fun. It also has a better understanding of what makes Lovecraftian elements good than any other videogame I know of and adds a lot of personality to otherwise faceless gods. It's pretty short but I would still highly recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: Gosh, where do I even start with this review? I have almost nothing but praise for this little gem of a title, but I want to try and articulate my praise as best I can. First and foremost, Sucker For Love is a horror/romantic comedy dating sim, serving at times as both a deconstruction and parody of a lot of by the numbers dating sims and visual novels, with an aesthetic heavily inspired by late 80s to early 90s anime and anime OVAs. The game's tone is quite unique, and in some respects I feel Sucker For Love is a dating sim game without peer in that regard. I've come across dozens of statements from people online, people normally adverse to this genre, who go on to say that Sucker For Love is both the best and only dating sim they've ever played or will play. The writing and voice acting for Sucker For Love is quite compelling, with AkaBaka's writing striking a good cadence between horror and comedy. It says a lot about the strength of AkaBaka's writing when neither of those elements undermine or compromise each other, and thus avoid weakening the impact of both. Oh, lest I forget, I must emphasize that this is in fact a Lovecraftian horror game. While Sucker For Love's horror is often mostly ambient in nature, it does have its share of slightly gory moments, and outside of that the ambiance alone can be quite nerve-racking too. As for the gore, it mostly pertains to facial mutilation and disfigurement, but it never escalates to anything more viscerally gory then that.As for the voice acting, every voiced character is well cast, with the likes of Michaela Laws, Kayli Mills, and Lani Mainella lending their considerable talent to the roles of L'neta, Estir and Nyanlathotep respectively. While all three voice actresses deliver cosmically stellar performances, a special shout out goes to Kayli Mills for her performance as Estir. And more specifically, her flawless read of AkaBaka's mostly ad-libbed lines of the King in Yellow, which were written in catalectic trochaic octameter to give the spoken lines a certain kind of flow. A flow which Kayli Mills grasps quite well.I think what surprises me the most about Sucker For Love is not just that it's a compelling narrative, but that it is mostly a passion project of just one person with a development cycle of roughly four months or less. There is no development 'team' for Sucker For Love, so to speak, though obviously Sucker For Love is still also a collaborative effort when it comes to quality assurance, voice acting and music. The fact that something this good came mostly from the mind of one person in such a short time frame is nothing short of astonishing, and it speaks volumes of the talent AkaBaka possesses. I must say, hats off to them, and from now on I am going to be on the lookout for any projects helmed by them.Now, as this review begins to reach its conclusion, some might be asking that after all my glowing praise, would I recommend this game? Absolutely. And I do mean I'd recommend this as a game, for while Sucker For Love has a lot of creative merit in terms of writing, art and music... Sucker For Love also has its merit as a game. For those familiar with dating sims, every dating sim has some sort of arbitrary metric for measuring the affection of the character you want to date, which you can 'raise' by performing certain actions or picking certain choices. Sucker For Love is no different, but in this case you raise the affection of your paramour by performing rituals for them. These rituals are essentially puzzles, and each puzzle has a different, unique solution. Most of these rituals are simple enough to perform, but there's a surprising amount of freedom in when you can perform some of them which can lead to all sorts of shenanigans.In any case, if you got ten dollars to spare and a free afternoon I urge you to give this game a chance. For all its focus on horror and comedy, there's a surprisingly strong emotional core to Sucker For Love. I think ultimately at its heart Sucker For Love is a game about discovering the humanity in the inhumane, being unashamed in your pursuit of those who are not conventionally attractive, and that yes a giant cat woman is fine too.
_childDocuments_.name: Sucker for Love: First Date

_childDocuments_.review: You know there’s someone out there that wishes they could date an eldritch horror. Well, luckily for them, and well anyone that likes dating sim visual novels with, let’s just say, interesting love interests, someone finally made a dating sim where you summon three different eldritch horrors. Though, it’s more to convince them to kiss you than to date you.In Sucker For Love: First Date, you play as a charming (enough) male character (he isn’t formally named, but he takes up any nickname he’s given) who has a peculiar fascination. Instead of being interested in 2D girls from anime or games, he’s been interested in eldritch beings ever since he had a dream about one named Ln’eta. When the game starts, we learn that he has been trying to summon an eldritch god for who knows how long and he has been unsuccessful. He seems to have the items needed to summon them, but he hasn’t been successful in getting a genuine Necronomicon. With today being the perfect day to try and summon Ln’eta, he hopes this Necronomicon will be the real deal this time, especially since this is the best chance he’ll get with the stars in position and he paid for overnight shipping. However, when the package comes, he finds that it isn’t what he asked for. For one, it’s not even his shipment as tracking says it’s going to run late (wow thanks, this is why I don’t pay for expedited delivery) and this Necronomicon is… pink and cute. Personally, I approve, but this isn’t what our main character paid for.Nonetheless, he decides to open the book and do the first ritual listed, or more accurately the only ritual written in a language he can understand which happens to be the first pages of this book. After completing the ritual, it actually summons Ln’eta (who is basically Cthulhu). It was genuine! Though, it’s less of a Necronomicon and more of a Survival Guide for dating Ln’eta which she tells you was made as a joke by Muu.Anyway, while this is a visual novel and you’ll of course be reading through everything, this does contain some gameplay. Throughout the game, you’ll mainly be performing various rituals. Before you start chanting, there are conditions you have to meet for it to be successful and it mainly depends on the ritual. Like turning off all the lights, lighting candles, putting on your ritual clothes, having the ceremonial knife in your hand, and so on. Once you do all that is needed, you can then chant by dragging your mouse across the phrase where your cursor will turn into a mouth, but you have to do it slowly. Once you complete the chant it will take affect immediately. Though, make sure you read everything as you can cause an early end.Apart from Ln’eta, there are two other eldritch horrors that you can smooch. After completing one of Ln’eta’s routes, Estir’s chapter is unlocked. Estir has her own book and while this does contain rituals, it also is based around performing a stage play. Though Ln’eta is also there and has her own route here. You can either go with either of them, or mix the rituals up together to get other endings as some rituals from Ln’eta’s book don’t blend well with Estir’s, and vice versa. The last chapter is with Nyanlathotep who only unlocks if you find three secrets (which two of them are pretty easy to find). Her’s is pretty unique not gonna lie, but it is pretty annoying to get one of her endings as it’s a sort of boss battle where you take in what’s happening around you and find the ritual you need to do and perform it promptly.While you don’t necessarily get to go on dates with the three eldritch horrors and mainly focus on doing these rituals, I did enjoy the humor here and how the characters were portrayed. Your main character, lusting over eldritch beings and all, pair pretty well with the love interests and does bring in some funny moments, especially when he makes them all flustered and/or confused that he just wants a kiss. Meanwhile, Ln’eta is pretty sweet and does somewhat come to care for you; Estir pretty much views you as lesser and mainly wants you to be her follower just to steal you from her sister (Ln’eta), but she does have some humourous scenes with her being theatrical (and her lines during the play are my favorite spoken lines); and Nyanlathotep isn’t exactly pleased with you getting with her nieces and is intimidating with her being too tall to normally stand in your room. They all are nice and entertaining to talk to, and I really did end up wishing that we got more scenes with them as I would have definitely wanted to know how the main character and these eldritch beings would have faired in a full blown dating sim.Though, there are some annoyances here still. While the checkpoint system is fine most of the time, as really you’ll need to go to the start of a section, it can get frusturating in Chapter 2 when you’re trying to get an ending that requires you to do rituals from both books and especially in Chapter 3. It can be even more annoying as some rituals cause an ending if you chant it too fast and in Chapter 3 you sometimes won’t know why you failed and you’ll need to start all the way over (while I’m sure it’s purposefully so you learn, I still got annoyed). And talking about chanting, I noticed that the speed you can do them in isn’t universal. Some do have some finnicky hit boxes, but I found that some phrases need you to read slowly while some will let you read it fast. Even for the same phrase. Which, as you can guess, can get annoying for rituals that auto bad end you when you read too fast or during Chapter 3 as it is time sensitive.While I did wish Sucker For Love: First Date could have been longer, and I experienced some frustrations, I overall enjoyed Sucker for Love: First Date. I did like the characters this featured, and come on what dating sim fan wouldn’t be interested in one where you date eldritch beings, I liked the humor, and I liked how this revolved around doing various rituals (even though the speed you have to chant annoyed me sometimes). Though, I might recommend waiting to pick this up on a discount, as while I still like Sucker For Love, I didn’t like it quite as much. There are three chapters, with each chapter dedicated to a love interest. There's replayability value for each chapter since it is a visual novel after all. However, the player cannot rewind the text to recall the dialogue if skipped too far. The options/menu is simple & straight-forward. _childDocuments_.review: TLDR: This game is a parody of anime dating simulator type games, which it executes perfectly. My playtime is basically the full length of the game, but there's plenty of replay value and I mean this is definitely a game that would be great to force your friends to play. You should definitely get it if it seems interesting to you at all. My Background: I played this game in the Dread X 2 Collection where the first date was available as a stand alone indie inclusion where I loved it. Honestly this was the best part of the Dread X 2 Collection so I immediately jumped when I found out that the full game had basically been released.Synopsis: This game features our main character who is obsessed with real life eldritch horrors coming across a book that lets him summon one. From there he attempts to woo it/her into kissing him which leads into a lot of "wacky mishaps". This game is basically a parody of other dating simulators and visual novel type games in the same sphere. One novel thing to note is the different chapters all focus on different mechanics which provide their own set of interesting ways to interact with the game itself. Story: It's the best part of the game. It's a parody so the story is just one long joke that hits every mark. There's also plenty of interesting twists and turns that keep players hooked.Gameplay: The idea of the gameplay is really interesting and something I enjoy. I do have to say that when you play it for a while, having to move your mouse across the screen SLOWLY to chant an encantation does get annoying after a while especially in chapter 2. _childDocuments_.review: I'm somewhat ambivalent about whether or not to recommend this game. I think this game existing is a net positive, so I think it deserves a "positive" review. On the other hand, the review is supposed to be a recommendation, and I'm not sure I can unconditionally recommend it. I wish I could give a more nuanced score than simply yes or no.First, the good.The voice acting is surprisingly good. I initially played it with the voices off because I usually find the voice acting in this sort of media to be pretty cringy, but actually I rather liked it.I thought some of the writing was fairly competent at conveying the enormity of the world-shattering events happening outside, even if I think it could have gone even further.The music creates a good ambiance, and one or two tracks actually stand out as fairly decent.And finally, the main reason why I'm giving a positive review: I'm hoping that this game is going to inspire a lot of great fanart like Helltaker did.Now, the bad.The game is very short. My five-hour play time is to 100% it. It only consists of four storylines. If you don't make any mistakes you could finish each in 10-20 minutes, depending on how fast you read. Getting all the endings will take longer because on some rituals the game turns merciless and forces you to start over from way back if you make a dumb mistake, like forgetting to turn on the lights.Being so short, there's no time to flesh out any of the characters. I suspect this is because they're fully voiced and this is obviously a budget title. Honestly, I think it would have been better to have lengthier storylines and skip the voice acting, if that's the case.The art style is rather er... amateurish, and some of the drawings look very sketchy, in the sense of being literally colored sketches. The art could use some extra polish and higher resolution images. On top of this, there really isn't that much art in the game. There's *maybe* 20 drawings in total, not counting the backgrounds.And finally what I think is the worst flaw: the bugs. Just casually playing the game, not even trying to break it, I ran into easily 5-10 bugs. For a game where a playthrough (from start to any normal ending) is so short, this is actually pretty impressive. Speaking as someone who writes software for a living, I can say there's basically three ways this can happen: a) there was no QA before release, b) there was QA, and the QA team missed these bugs because there were much, much more serious bugs (yikes!) distracting them, or c) there was QA and the developer already knew about these bugs at release, but he doesn't know how to fix them. I leave as an exercise to the reader which of these possibilities is the worst one.Even with these problems I'm giving it a positive review. Partly for what I said above, and partly because I paid for it about the same as what I'd pay for a bag of chocolate chip cookies. For that price, I think I can't complain.

_childDocuments_.review: Sucker for Love is a pretty simple dating sim, but what it lacks in depth it makes up in its aesthetics and writing. The 90s anime sheen infused into every aspect of the visuals ls well-considered and hits the perfect nostalgia spot, and paired with cute cosmic horrors, the game is just beautiful to look at. Personally, I would have preferred the girls to be a little more abstract, rather than being squeezed rather cleanly into sexy body types, but I can't really fault the direction taken instead - this is a game operating in multiple niches, so it needs to have something with broader appeal. I really enjoyed the tone of the narration and dialogue - the game takes itself just seriously enough to feel sincere, while still featuring a relentlessly horny protagonist and deeply funny character archetypes in the two main love interests. I had a lot of true laugh-out-loud moments playing through both of their routes, and there's even a smattering of that same tone in the otherwise much more serious final act, which I appreciated. What I was less fond of was how the game hard-pivots to a quick-twitch point-and-click action style for the final segment. It's an extremely jarring change of pace, and I had a ton of trouble keeping up with it, though this was probably a self-imposed Steam Deck handicap given the relative precision needed for the mouse-based challenges. It definitely left me feeling a little cold to finish the game, and it seems like the second game is a lot more of that, which is a little disappointing given how fun the dating-sim aspects of this one are.In short, though, Sucker for Love is a super fun, quick-hit dating sim, and it's definitely worth your time if any single aspect of it appeals to you. ln'eta best girl

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, one of the best meta roleplaying games I've played; and this perfectly filled my Mettaton-shaped hole in my heart, if you know what I mean.Although it may seem like a funny dating simulator on the surface, this game rang the same bells with me as Undertale did way back then. Beautiful hand-drawn anime art style, banger soundtrack (that jazz track in Darling's bedroom, oh my God!), unique twist on its genre with the premise (dating goddesses of eldritch/Lovecraftian horror), adequately delivered horror elements, charmful characters and meta game mechanics that really kicked me in the balls when I tried to 100% the game and made feel really bad for my actions (the game knows what actions you take and goes smirky about it, like Undertale).The game really did an Undertale-style knockback at me when .Sucker for Love is a very impressive roleplaying game on its own with lots to love about it, but fans of Undertale would appreciate the game the most. It's like one those anime games Alphys would play to geek herself out.This is the perfect game to get your meta RPG fix if you did not like Deltarune as much.My only complaint about the game is that I played through the endings I was interested in 3 hours. That's very short, this should have been an 8+-hour-long game.Besides that, this is a 9/10 masterpiece that dating sim and meta RPG fans, especially of the Undertale and Doki-Doki Literature Club variety, would likely regard as a modern classic.

_childDocuments_.review: Sucker for Love is a short, but delightful dating sim which balances elements of romance, cosmic horror, and comedy masterfully. Let's be clear at the start: This is a cosmic horror dating sim. It warns you at the start that there is blood, self-harm, and a lot of tentacles and they absolutely deliver on those warnings. If you are able to get beyond that, however, Sucker for Love is a delightful game which plays on both the tropes of the Dating Sim/Visual Novel while still having the dread and fear that comes with the Cosmic Horror genre. As if that isn't enough, it's also hilarious. I found the level of horror/gore/etc. to be tasteful, enough to stoke that sense of fear, but not so much that it made me want to stop. This commendable level of restraint also extends to the game being quite chaste, focused instead on the romance and themes of cosmic horror, rather than something more obscene.If I have any complaints, there are some times where the game can be a little buggy, and you cannot tell if something correctly triggered or not, which was a larger issue when dealing with the challenges in the third chapter. Given how short the game is, and how easy it is to load in a check point, this was not a huge issue for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Sucker For Love: First Date is something of an enhanced version of the original Sucker For Love made for the Dread X Collection 2 (which I've also reviewed in the past). Seeing as that was a highlight of that collection, I thought it worthwhile to play the expanded version of that initial game, and wanted to give my two cents on it. So, here we are.Sucker For Love: First Date plays as something of a point and click visual novel. You sit in the shoes of our protagonist, D (yes, that's his name), a man with a single minded goal: To smooch Eldritch beings. To do this, he gains access to a Necronomicon-esc tome that, while not looking like one, is actually a cult ritual book to summon Ln'eta, a waifu-ifed version of the great Cthulhu! In order to earn the smooch, D must complete various rituals, which the player does by flipping through the book, collecting the required items via a simple point and click interface, and then chant the rituals by dragging the mouse over the appropriate incantations slowly. It's certainly a unique mechanic for a dating sim.However, the game features a checkpoint system with a flowchart, and multiple different endings, both good and bad. This allows the you to see what would happen if D did something in a ritual wrong, or some other thing that causes him to die or go insane (I mean, we are talking about smooching Lovecraftian beings, so what's a little sanity for the promise of smooches?).Upon completing a date with Ln'eta, you unlock a second episode of sorts, where you can date Ln'eta again, OR you can choose to go after her eternal rival, Estir, a girl modelled after the King in Yellow themself, Hastur the Unspeakable. If you choose to go down Estir's path, the rituals shift into a recreation of the play "The King in Yellow," inspired by the story of the same name's use of said play, which is one of the primary sources of Hastur's lore. But Estir is offering TWO smooches for finishing it, so heck yeah we gotta do it! It's otherwise the same mechanically as the stuff with Ln'eta. Of course, you CAN try to go for both, but it likely won't end well for you.However, that's not all. If you manage to fulfil some special conditions in your pursuit of smooches, you can unlock the third episode, featuring Nyanlathotep, a waifu version of the Crawling Chaos, Nyarlathotep. However, in her case, you aren't in it for smooches this time. Instead, ol' Auntie Nyan Nyan (she likes this nickname for some reason) wants you to suffer for trying to consort with her nieces, or just going after the unspeakable horrors for smooches in general. This is a survival gauntlet, where you have to use the book to survive an onslaught of small rituals that, should you fail, will end you. It's a tense final challenge. In the end though, you give the ol'Clawing Chaos something to fear when she sleeps: D and his need for endless Eldritch Smooches!The game is quite funny, especially if you're a fan of both a massive weeb (which I very much am) and a fan of Lovecraft and associates works within the Cthulhu Mythos. There's tons of little jokes that fans of those things will get more out of than the average player, but I assume if you're interested in this game, you're a Lovecraft loving weeb like me, so you'll probably get a kick out of it. The writing is generally really good, and it's clear Akabaka has more than a basic knowledge of Lovecraftian Horror fiction, since, as previously stated, it has a lot of nods to the lore of the creatures that he waifu-ified.The game also has solid voice acting all around for the three lovely ladies you meet along the way. There are ONLY 3 voices, as D lacks a voice, but that's usually expected in these types of games. There is technically a voice reciting the unholy forbidden spells you use, but it's just a basic sound effect. The sound design outside of that is pretty basic. It does have a fun little anime ending theme inspired song in it, so that's pretty neat. The art direction is also really solid, capturing both cute and horror really well! I don't really have much to say beyond that in terms of anything beyond the writing though, given how short it is.It's not without it's issues though. There are a few instances of visual glitches, usually with how the text is displayed. I think there are one or two voice lines that also just may not play, which is a little sad, but it's not a total deal breaker. I didn't come across any game breaking bugs or anything, so it's really just a tiny bit of grime on an otherwise solid experience. I do think the price may come off as a touch steep for some, given that it's quite short, clocking in at a little under 3 and half hours for me, and I was aiming to 100% it. There's also a few missing quality of life features for these types of games, like being able to see a log of what characters said. The game is simple enough that a save system isn't really needed, especially with the checkpoints you get, but I'm mentioning that purely because some people want that in a dating sim/visual novel type game.Overall, I'm gonna give Sucker For Love, First Date a solid 4/5. I think I gave the Dread X Collection 2 original a higher score, but that was within the context of a greater collection of bite-sized games. As a stand alone title, I think it's better than the version from the collection, as it has more content, but I am left wanting more. At time of writing, the long awaited sequel, Sucker For Love: A Date To Die For, has just come out, and I did just finish it, so I'm going to be reviewing that game too.

As much "existential terror" as "terror of the giant space octopus so horrific that a single glance at its true form can shatter our sanity." It's not that something beyond our comprehension exists, but that it is so massive, ancient, and incomprehensible that it think of us as much as we think of the ants beneath our feet and delivers excruciating suffering and death as absentmindedly as breathing without an iota of malice.Reading spells in-game is a hassle, but it's the only real challenge the story offers, so I give it a pass. _childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I thought this game was going to be another one of those stupid meme games that you play for twenty minutes to laugh at and send stupid pictures to friends. And in a way, yes, it IS that, but it also plays itself incredibly straight at the same time despite the jokey nature of the game. I like it, it's not a very long game, but it manages to make a pretty solid impact and has a variety of fun ways to die if you're into collecting a bunch of bad ends.The character designs are nice, you can see the original basis of all of them with fairly unique spins on them. I particularly like what they did with Hastur because it's more subtle than the other two eldritch abominations, but also a clever take on the lore.I was surprised that even with the tone being overall lighthearted, the game is very good at twisting it into horror in just a moment, and a few of the scares actually got me. The ending is also fairly intense and can get kind of nerve-wracking, which I was not expecting from what I thought would just be a slightly glorified visual novel.I would say maaaaybe don't get this for full price just because it IS short, if you're strapped for cash. But I would definitely recommend it for anyone who's looking to have a fairly unique horror experience, or someone who just really, really likes Lovecraftian horror. This game knows what it's doing and does it well in its brief time.

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting concept, decent execution. With all the complexity of doing eldritch rituals, I expected the progression to be less linear.The mechanics are hit and miss. There were pretty frequent visual bugs with equipping items, especially in chapter 2. Perhaps the game engine wasn't being used as intended, or perhaps the dev team was inexperienced or rushed. Good job to whoever did the art though.I turned the voices off since they didn't add much, and while the dialogue was pretty clever most of the time, the game and story just didn't have much depth. I don't know how much getting voice actors cut into the budget, but my guess is the game could have been more fleshed out story-wise by not including it.The price point is also a bit high for how short the game is. It took me like 3 hours including the secret final boss fight, which is easily manageable if you read through the book a few times before starting it (kinda tedious; ending wasn't particularly rewarding either). Almost every ending felt rather abrupt and unsatisfying.Overall, this game just feels like a big missed opportunity that could have been much more. It tries to do cutesy romance, cool spellcasting, and eldritch horror, but nothing stands out as 'great'. It's all just 'there'.This is one of those games that make me wish steam let you choose a neutral option for reviews, because I do like the concept and I want to see it done on a larger scale. I'm gonna downvote to make this review easier to find since I have a differing opinion from the mindless cthussy echo chamber. 5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay so I'm going to put up my usual disclaimer. This comes from a guy that plays a LOT of horror games and doesn't typically like visual novels short of Doki Doki, Cooking Companions, and a couple others, this is easily one of my favorite horror games/visual novels/dating sims! If you want the TLDR; it's humor is spot on for me, it's goofy, it's also unnerving and puzzling at times. It really strikes a balance between everything. If you want some more spoiler free specifics, here goes! Pros:- The artstyle for this game is equally adorable and detailed. There's the obvious parts of it's beautifully drawn and animated, but there's also little details that I appreciated. Such as your cursor/hand casts a shadow whenever it's around a light source. There's little particles floating around in the air and it just kind of adds a dimension to the game when it could've easily just been the usual PNG background with characters and a dialogue box! - The spoops. Spoops don't get me very often. I can usually break them down and call them out play by play, but this game uses spoops sparingly and it pays off. There's always a bit of a creepy and horrifying atmosphere, but there's some truly scary moments. - Story. The story is definitely engaging enough to keep someone like me and my ADHD brain interested. There's enough of a hook to pull you in and the story starts branching out as you go on. Also the humor for this game had me laughing and giggling constantly. That's worth it's price tag right off the bat. Cons:- Visuals. I've experienced a few visual bugs that don't seem to affect gameplay, but it can be a little confusing as I wasn't sure if it was a problem or not.Really. That's it! If you're reading this at the end of the review, you're curious enough to really dig into what someone thinks of it and I'm telling you it's worth it's price tag for a fun horror visual novel. Highly recommend this one!

_childDocuments_.review: There's polish that needs to be done, but I really love and respect what's here so far. It's a fun, funny, and spooky indie title well worth its asking price. The third chapter especially is fantastic. I think my one word of warning is that the game has some annoying glitches in its second and third chapters, but considering this just released, I'm imagining the devs will fix it soon enough. It's nothing game breaking, but it had me worried the game was soft locked.In the second chapter, if you get a message asking you to take off the robe when you don't have it on, try the spell with the robe on, then take it off and try the spell again. This happens a few times, and it gets a little annoying when I'm just trying to get all the endings, but it was an easy fix.For the glitch that got me in the third chapter, I knew what I was supposed to do, but initially the game wasn't triggering what I needed to do to go down the branching path. It was only after I restarted the game and got out of full screen mode that it worked and I could get the final ending.That said, I'd happily buy this for a friend or two. I would recommend this if you're curious about it. It's good for if you want a new horror title, or you just think eldritch terrors are hot.

_childDocuments_.review: Sucker for Love:First Date is one of the better visual novel styled games I have played in the last few years.  The game is not that long only about two hours or so if you try for all endings, but I found the short length to be a pro instead of a con in this case. I feel the length of this title kept the humor from wearing out and overall helped set a good pace along with the chapter based gameplay.One thing that I particularly liked about Sucker for Love is that it really did not take itself seriously, the humor is right in your face from the start, but its also serious enough to not ruin the game with fan service style nonsense like you would see in a lot of other short anime, or adult visual novels. Overall I was really surprised when I tried this game a few years ago, it sat on my wish list a long time but it is definitely a quality purchase and I would not feel bad about paying full price it. I am looking forward to the second game and I can easily recommend Sucker For Love: First Date to anyone looking for a short Visual Novel, with a genre twist of comedy, horror, romance in respective order.

_childDocuments_.review: So I first found out about sucker for love when I watched a plathrough of the demo (?) which is now effectively the first chapter of the full game. The writing is solid, with plenty of self aware humor that you would expect of a game where you date elder gods, but also can occasionally pull on your heart strings as well as being downright unnerving if you think about it too much.And the VA's do an excellent job bringing the characters to life and putting the game a little above just a joke visual novel, especially in the recitation of the king in yellow's play which actually has some decent verse to it and is definitely sold by the voice over. There's a total of 10 endings across 3 chapters, with a few semi-endings that don't count towards your ending count but lead to a usually humorous scene including one where you get caught two timing, and the bulk of which are in the second chapter. Which is where trying to discover the different permutations will get each ending as well as some alternate scenes adds some light replay value.Then it culminates in hunting down three secret actions that will unlock the third chapter which depending on route is either the shortest, or the biggest departure from the rest of the game leading to a pretty interesting use of the game's limited mechanics and game space that adds a nice cherry on top.Simply put, if you think the concept of dating a hot cthulhu girl is enough to merit a ten dollar chuckle, you'll get more than your money's worth despite a short playtime. And never underestimate what humanity will subject itself and the entire world to in the name of smooches.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a work of unfiltered passion from the developer and it is a very funny and engaging spin on the visual novel and dating sim genre. Its cast of quirky characters are fully realized with amazing voice acting work and even the unvoiced protagonist feels like a unique character with memorable moments which is a refreshing change from the plain slates visual novel protagonists usually are. I'm not a reviewer so I can never do this game the justice it deserves but I'll tell you what I liked. If you suspend your disbelief to go along for the ride and get engaged with the characters then this game can deliver some emotional damage that leaves you asking for more. The VAs for this game really gave it their all on the delivery and they really can be the main appeal of this game and their characters cover a wide range of archetypes which all have their own appeal (Team Ln'eta lets goooo). One of chapter 2's endings left me genuinely devastated which was a welcome surprise because I'm not really a fan of visual novel games (watch part 6 of the VA's Michaela Laws' playthrough to cry like we did if you won't get the game and yes I watched this game play out multiple times).The replayability value is also pretty good with the usual multiple ending mechanic of the visual novel genre. After being introduced to this game from the youtuber Manlybadasshero's hours long videos a week ago I still wanted to experience it for myself despite watching literally the whole game get played out. I'm also glad I did because gathering some friends to show them my newest obsession and performing the protagonist's lines for their entertainment at 2 A.M. was one of the funnest experiences I've had in a LONG time. Like this game has genuinely been the object of some cosmic obsession of mine and I can't get enough of it. Like Helltaker, this game's short length does not work against it and its characters leave fans like me searching for more. Btw if you're as starving for more content as I am did you know there's a Q&A for this game which along with breaking down some development and lore questions also includes a canon script reading of an epilogue to this game? This game is also oozing style in the music department. From the trailer (watch it pls) to its beautiful cover of All I Have To Do Is Dream at the end of chapter 3 to even the casual background music, they all are so memorable and really do get the nostalgia for older anime going. Even the game's musical motiff that plays with most endings is such a joy to hear. Speaking of the very expensive cover for All I Have To Do Is Dream, I never knew I needed to hear this before in my life. It's an earworm that plays in my head before I sleep and its such a great farewell from the game as it basically encompasses the game's themes of dreams, reality, love and painful goodbyes. There's some small hiccups in the game still like some misspelled words or some moments not playing out right like two characters not acknowledging each other while being in the same room but these hiccups are all so minor and specific at this point they are a non-issue, especially considering how much the small team for this game got right. The only issue most people would notice is the unlock counter for chapter 3 not visually tracking unlocks properly between playthroughs but its still tracking correctly even if it says it isn't. If you read no other part of this review then understand that this indie game is a passion project which sincerely pays homage to 80s/90s anime, dating sims and lovecraftian mythos in a genuinely sweet and funny little adventure that may just leave you a sucker for love. And for the developers, keep doing what you're doing. The game is great and I would love to see more of your work. Sucker for Love has a lot of potential to blow up (advertise the merch louder) and from what I've heard about the next game's plot from the Q&A and comedic translations from the weird cosmic language in the survival guide, I'm along for the ride for whatever comes next. To the fans that already exist, we need more fanart and a bigger community man. I've spent more time writing this than doing my papers due soon lol.P.S. this game has merch like waifu posters and shirts on the DreadXP website. You're welcome weebs

_childDocuments_.review: Sucker For Love is a two player children’s game, the object of which is to pick up your treasure chest on the central island and sail back safely.Each player has a giant sailing ship as their main game piece. Each ship has a removable sail, two trigger-action side panels, and a huge spring-driven cannon. Players take turns moving forward along a prescribed track and shooting bean bags at their opponent’s ship. A hit on one of the side panels will force it to pop off and give the player a free shot at the other side; a hit forcing the sail off becalms the ship for a turn.To add to the pirate flavor, each player also has an eye patch. Wearing these will slightly affect depth perception and add a marginal bit of sport to the shooting.This game retailed for the somewhat impressive sum of $16 back in 1962. With its huge plastic ships (close to a foot long), giant vinyl play mat, and the eye patches, it may well stand as one of the more overproduced games of the early 1960s. Sucker For Love?

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing subversion of the visual novel format. The 90s anime artstyle is beautifully executed with its saturated colours and bright appealing character designs. The story balances 3 different love interests without compromising the stories or character of any of them, easter eggs and hidden details being incorporated into the gameplay to add to the mystery of discovering the unknowable. The game balances humour and horror stunningly well, with humour cutting the tension of the more eldritch elements, while the horror creates immersion and adds stakes, grounding in how it re-emerges to add paranoia to the lighthearted nature of the dating sim. It reminds me of Doki Doki literature club in it's subversion of the genre, but it manages to supercede it as the story is able to balance the weight of the horror throughout the story, instead of revealing it as an endpoint. It carries all of it's best elements and improves upon it, having more of what was so compelling to begin with, and having a final battle within the visual novel setup that manages to have real stakes and horror, working with the gameplay elements to make for an eldritch final girl moment. Amazing game, I reccomend it to everyone, I look forward to seeing more content from the franchise as they build from an incredibly strong foundation, with amazing characters and compelling worldbuilding and story.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite encountering some crashing and freezing issues, I had an absolute blast playing "Sucker for Love: First Date"! Each character is wonderfully designed, with distinct personalities that make every interaction memorable. The voice acting and dialogue add a lot of flavor, making it easy to get engrossed in this bizarre yet delightful world.Even though I faced some technical hiccups, they didn’t detract from the overall enjoyment. The developers seem committed to improving the game, and I’m confident these issues will be ironed out soon. The game's charm and creativity shine through, making it easy to forgive a few bugs here and there.If you’re looking for a dating sim that’s refreshingly different and aren’t afraid of a few eldritch horrors, "Sucker for Love: First Date" is definitely worth your time. I wholeheartedly recommend it to anyone seeking a fun, unique gaming experience!

_childDocuments_.review: +Solving ritualistic puzzles can lead to some humorous moments, especially when you deviate from the main path. +Some witty and cute narrative moments.+Unique occult setting.-Controls are primitive.-No achievements.-Some stereotypical anime tropes.As typical with most visual novels, the vast majority of Sucker for Love (SfL) is simply reading through the story. The part that is different from other VNs becomes the ritualistic puzzles you need to solve for the story. I thought it was a nice change of pace using various items like a knife, robe, candles, lights, and chalk symbols in a very specific manner to solve the puzzles. The controls were a bit primitive. You cannot even use WASD or arrow keys to move back and forth in your room. Otherwise, normal KB & M controls. The difficulty I found pretty easy for all but the final storyline where you have some fairly ambiguous puzzles thrown at you and no explanation for failure. Still, these can be brute forced. Typical anime-style graphics. There is no animations, just new drawings of the characters. Overall, pretty simplistic, probably able to run easily on a PS3. I found the musical score to be largely forgettable. The voice acting is decent enough, though your character isn’t voiced despite having no customization or choices. I found the world too simplistic, as there are literally only 3 zones, but perhaps that’s a given for such a short game. The story is also simplistic where  Still, SfL isn’t really trying to be profound, it’s just goofy fun. There is no NG+ to partake, nor achievements, so this really tanks the replay value. There are branching storylines,  With only one real path, the game will take you about 2-3 hours to complete. Overall, I enjoyed my time with Sucker for Love. The unique puzzle aspects were something I wish was built out more in a longer visual novel. But only if it’s on a deep sale. _childDocuments_.review: Visual Novel – Reading + "Speaking" (Hovering your mouse over text)Additionally: Timed sequence in 3rd chapter, where you need to "survive" About 4h Smooch/10  10/10First of all, I’m actually too much of a chicken to play the secret ending or secret route part myself because well, I was creeped out enough by the other two chapters…Another thing: DDLC was compared to this game in some reviews I saw and I want to kind of disagree with that comparison. To me DDLC had totally different vibes than this game and I actually found DDLC a lot creepier.Basically, this is a short novel with horror elements and some jump scares (for me at least). There are at least three romanceable options: Ln’eta and Estir and in the secret route Nyanlathotep. Your character works as a host and has a weird obsession regarding eldritch gods. Long story short, the character manages to summon one and makes a deal with the summoned Ln’eta. He has to perform various rituals to increase her affection and, if he succeeds, she will reward him with a , I mean “smooch”. Seems easy enough, right? Well, just play the game and see for yourself…Let’s talk a bit about the characters and the corresponding routes. Ln’eta is the protagonist of the first and of the second chapter. The first chapter is meant to be an introduction to the whole gameplay and setting: The novel feature of this game is that you need to hover your mouse over the words that are written in your Necronomicon to “speak” them and perform the corresponding ritual. Additionally, you will realize fairly quickly that this novel has indeed horror elements to it.Estir is one of the protagonists of the second chapter. The second chapter is actually a bit different than the first chapter. While in the first chapter you have a pretty much straightforward story line, where you do not have any choices and are basically only performing the rituals, the second chapter has multiple endings and choices. Additionally, there is a “penalty” for performing rituals wrongly. The third chapter is about Nyenlathotep and its focus are timed rituals. Basically, the first two chapters “prepare” you for the “boss battle” so to say. However, like I said, I did not play it myself, but watched a Let’s Play. It actually takes multiple trials to win there and it’s kind of both creepy and challenging.To summarize, I enjoyed playing (and watching) this game a lot. The idea that you “chant” spells by hovering with your mouse over them and you “fail” them, if you move your mouse too quickly, is cool and novel for a visual novel. Additionally, the story line and the characters were very interesting and enjoyable, so I had fun playing this game. I’d recommend it to everyone, who has a few hours to spare, enjoys a funnily written original story (with horror elements) that you shouldn’t take very seriously and wants to challenge themselves a bit.

_childDocuments_.review: Very cute (yet terrifying) visual novel with nice interactive elements. As the description suggests, you romance Eldritch gods, three of them to be exact. Each of them has their own book with various rituals to perform in order to win their affections, but the focus of each book is a little different. The first one is straightforward, simply following the instructions. The second involves "acting out a play" which requires paying attention to the stage directions and reciting the lines properly. The third is more time sensitive, needing to find the relevant page in the book based on what's happening and carrying out the ritual in time.There are three chapters, with two true endings in the first and last chapters, and 6 in the 2nd chapter. The checkpoint system makes it not too difficult to get each ending, but at the same time the game itself is extremely short (I got 100% in under 3 hours). At $10, this length would normally make me not recommend a game but... honestly, it's just so cute and charming I still enjoyed it. Each girl has a distinct personality, and even though you might not like them all, it's still entertaining . You also might learn something about Elder Gods from the game while you're at it!If you like monster girls, definitely a must buy, especially if you can pick it up on sale. However, if game length is important to you, you might want to wait for a steep discount.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to write a more comprehensive review than those I've seen promoted on this page, as those are your usual one-line memes.Slight gameplay spoilers, obviously. Don't read if you want to go in blind, but I personally wanted a bit of an explanation of what the game was like before I bought it.So, this is really quite a clever little dating sim, which has you enacting rituals to smooch the various cosmic horrors. The gameplay is your typical VN fare, shifting items in and out of your inventory and progressing through dialogue, but you also have a grimoire that has you read incantations to progress along the routes, which is a nice touch and I really like how you have to slowly drag your mouse across each incantation for you to cast it, you can't go too fast or else it doesn't work. There's only one location, the apartment itself, and the items don't really change between routes. You're also told what you're missing if you cast an incantation without everything set up properly, which is very helpful and appreciated.The writing is very fun and lovingly parodies both dating sims and cosmic horror. There's some surprisingly tender moments, mostly with Ln'eta (the Cthulhu-girl). The art is fantastic, too, very 90s anime, which is one of my personal favorite styles.The third act is a twist on the formula of the first two acts, and is very fun and engaging. I love how it played out, but I won't spoil that here.I think my only critique is I kept running into glitches and little bugs. Moving to different routes to get all the endings was a bit wonky, as some flags and triggers didn't match up quite right, and there's one instance where I flat out couldn't select a particular bookmark, despite having it unlocked. I also had a bookmark unlocked that I technically shouldn't have at that point in the game. There's some weirdness in selecting items covered by other ones, and you can't switch routes if you have your grimoire up. These can all be ironed out, though, and didn't detract from my experience.One other thing I wanted to mention: there's an instance of (implied) animal abuse in Act 1. I don't recall that being listed in the trigger warnings at the beginning of the game, but worthy of note nonetheless.All in all, I quite liked this despite an initial negative reaction upon first seeing it, and am definitely interested in seeing the sequels!(Estir best girl obv)

_childDocuments_.review: Genuinely the best dating sim game I've ever played. The way the different paths work is amazing, the plot doesn't take itself over-seriously but still tells a compelling story, and the game mechanics are genuinely incredibly fun. It's not often a visual novel style game like this has a gimmick that's so enjoyable. And the way that the concept of eldritch horror is discussed is incredibly interesting! The final (secret?) chapter ends on a note that feels incredibly triumphant, which isn't a theme found in cosmic horror. It was a surprise that left me feeling fantastic. _childDocuments_.review: Genuinely creative "horny" visions of probably some of the coolest concepts in literature and that sincerely needs commendation to Akabaka/ChromatoseDev.But what I appreciate most is the fact the user can determine the lengths of where the obsession goes. On the surface level, yeah there's some allusions to more risque stuff, but ultimately... your boy just wants a smooch. It is not overtly obscene, but it does not dance around any bushes, especially if you hop onto Twitter and see some of the fanart that the developer/artist retweets.There is particularly another game that uses puzzles and demon girls, but again, you (the character) do not do anything overt in the gameplay, but it is totally up to the user to determine the implications. Same concept but Sucker for Love defines itself among its brothers and sisters as a totally palatable satire and TECHNICALLY... this is Cthulhu cannon considering how the I.P. of Lovecraft is treated. So ENJOY the calamari, folks!It sounds weird to compliment on a game like that, but it does not stigmatize you and recognizes that some folks just want a FUN experience on their terms. 100% support that and I 100% enjoyed my time so far.Can not wait for another stream and would be happy to buy/support any dlc that may come.

_childDocuments_.review: Our lives and freedom is an illusion, or rather a big joke. We are not the beloved children of an universal God, but the slaves and playthings of Elders Gods ready to end our reality just by awaken from their slammer.Not in this reality thankfully. In this one an obsessed person wants to smooth a Rule 34 Cthulhu named Ln' eta by following the instructions of a pink survival guide, for starters. He is 100% focused on completing all the rituals and ready to doom his reality...what.Just because it is a parody visual novel of the Lovecraft's mythos and Anime of the 90s, doesn't mean that the horror theme of the game takes a back seat entirely. It is a successful mix of comedy and horror together.More specifically all the dialogues you hear from the talented voice actors that give life to our sexy elde-, I mean young Goddesses can be both hilarious and terrifying based on how you will please them.In the rituals you also need to perform, you won't be safe either. _childDocuments_.review: I played the game when the prototype was first showcased on the Dread Ex collection 2 and I definitely enjoyed it then. Then the full game came out and couldn't help but buy it to see how it had turned out. I was once again filled with all the laughs, charm, and intrigue of before and I had to eat my own words because this is a wonderful, multiple hour long, full game. It took everything it had in the Dread Ex collection, then improved and fleshed-out everything.  Sucker for love is a visual novel style, semi-horror game with a great sense of humor. It plays on a lot of tropes of the Lovecraftian genre and does it well. It had a couple good scares in it, but most of the time I was too preoccupied with the game, story, and laughs to be afraid. It has a couple hours of game, (roughly 3-6 hours) depending on if you are bad at the game like me, and if you decide to get all the endings and explore its secrets.         Chapter 3 of the game is actually what inspired me to write this review because it incorporates all aspects of humor, horror, and gameplay so seemlessly well. I thought it was a pretty good game before but after  chapter 3, I thought it was a great game.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a sucker for this game.I'll be honest, I bought it on a whim "to try"; with the reality that I'd likely just refund it - but once I started playing it, I wanted to see where it all went, and I'm glad I did.If you're into eldritch/cosmic horrors, the writing and way this game plays out from all aspects is very creative and unique (story, and mechanical); definitely something I appreciated. This isn't your typical Lovecraftian-trope romp that every game nowadays is; it's an inventive, yet respectful, take on the entities - without comprising any of the attributes or scale, that makes them such nightmares to behold.I did have one minor gripe: As a visual novel game with multiple endings, trying to unlock all of them can become a bit... maddening - charge forward and focus on playing and enjoying the game to its fullest; then go back and worry about the "what other ways could this have played out" - otherwise, you may become a it frustrated trying to sort out all of the exact routings required (once you've unlocked them though, you understand how/why it is the way it is).Overall: A very creative and respectful take on eldritch horrors - all without comprising what makes them, them. Unlocking ALL the endings isn't as clean as it should be, but, the game is still fantastic as a story.The art stylings, sound designs, and voice acting are all top-notch too. They really help round out the whole package, and get you invested into what's going on.

Her lines during the play in the second route are fantastic and I could listen to them on a loop for a while. And I absolutely love the third route. 2 story tall cat girls are the best.Basically, that eldrussy got me acting unwise and I'm loving every second of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Sucker for Love: First Date

_childDocuments_.review: Sucker for Love is an absolute gem. There is so much heart and soul in this game and I am genuinely at a loss for words about how much I enjoyed playing it. You get to woo elder gods and perform rituals all while experiencing all things eldritch and cute and it's a dream come true. The story is beautiful and funny and while the game has sexual innuendo, it isn't outright lewd. The music is amazing and the art is gorgeous. I played this game and recorded it for my channel and when I was done, I had a real moment of, "Oh it's over now..." with that pang of sadness that lets you know you just finished playing something special. Thank you so much to everyone who worked on this game and I cannot wait to see what you come out with next.Do yourself a favor and PLAY THIS GAME!
_childDocuments_.name: Sucker for Love: First Date

_childDocuments_.review: So adorable, much kawaii, and...I...I kinda want more.Update after beating game- Pros:- Will melt a cold heart and give hope in the cruel dark abyss.- Full Voice Acting- I love the endings, the good ones are just so good- No echii, just wholesome- You won't believe it but there's some interesting worldbuilding that makes me invested enough to write a review for the first time...ever.- Was...WAS THAT A GURREN LAGANN REFERENCE?!Cons:- Some weird bugs that should cause trouble/continuity errors but then either will or won't. - No echii, just wholesome- Want more big mommy catgirls- Short enough to complete in an evening.will leave you wanting MORE.So it may not be long, it may not be deep, but as a sucker for love (ha, title drop) at heart, this VN is amazing. _childDocuments_.review: Sucker for Love is a very well written and just overall charming visual novel. I bought it expecting a bit of weird fan service eldritch simping, but did not expect some really great lines and tugs at my heart strings. I love the characters, the atmosphere, the core mechanics, the general artstyle, the voice acting, and... just about everything in this game.For $10, this game is a steal. I would **love** to see more content, whether it be for free or paid DLC.I would love to see maybe some new additions of eldritch beings whether they be directly based off of the Cthulhu Mythos like Azathoth or Atlach-Nacha or just lightly inspired by some of the other beings. Maybe we could get a different setting other than the MC's apartment. Who knows what we'll get, but I'll happy to see what they come up with!To the Devs/Publishers: Thank you for making this into a full game and putting a new spin on Lovecraftian horror! _childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game, I originally watched someone play the prologue in the DreadX collection and decided to check out the full version. Cute visual novel with some horror elements in the style of Anime from the 80s with things like Urusei Yatsura and whatnot which I absolutely fell in love with. The characters are pretty simple but written very well and it had a really goofy story that got me invested enough to play it all the way through. It is definitely very short with you being able to beat it in around 3 and a half hours at most maybe and that is getting all endings. There are a few bugs that can sometimes make things confusing but I am sure those will end up getting patched out pretty soon, It would also be nice to potentially see achievements added at some point as well as the soundtrack being released because all of the songs in this game were honestly amazing and catchy and I found myself humming them throughout my day.  Anyways I loved this game and I honestly recommend it if you want a short silly little game to play and I am excited to see what comes next from the developer.
_childDocuments_.name: Sucker for Love: First Date

_childDocuments_.review: If you are remotely interested in this game, let me tell you that it's worth it. Each chapter adds just enough to make the experience feel new. It can occasionally be jarring, but in my opinion not nearly as disturbing as other prominent games near this genre.) The overall message is hopeful, maybe even silly. There were some decent puzzles too. My only issue is that there isn't more of it. However, it seems if the game does will Akabaka is considering the addition of new content or a sequel. I rate 9/10, great content you can't help but want more of with only a few minor gripes about the puzzle/route solutions.And remember - there are no curves like non-euclidean curves.
