_childDocuments_.review: To be brief, this visual novel is a fun, almost irreverent blast of romance and eldritch horror. The character's are all great and distinct from one another, and in their relatively short time on screen they become surprisingly well-developed. Gameplay is simple enough not to get in the way of the story, but varied and nice enough where it counts to feel like it can't get boring, which is great considering the core gameplay loop is what drives the plot forward.Lastly, actually  all the game has to offer is easy as summoning the elder gods with it checkpoint system, making, so your time is not going to be wasted too much. Only bad things I can take a stab at are the lack of a dialogue review system, and that I wish the protagonist could have actually had traditional dialogue picking options to interact with the girls more, possibly even unlocking new ending or events. Not BIG problems, but still worth pointing out. That, and that the inherent premise can be a bit alienating (heh), so those with little love for anime or less than serious adaptations of Lovecraft's works will find even more wanting with the game than I.Overall, if you have the money to spare and you like the idea of a semi-goofy, semi-scary romance visual novel, don't miss out on this gem. Especially when you can get it for a pittance and has all the charm in the cosmos on its side.

name: OXENFREE II: Lost Signals
detailed_description: Play the mind-bending original, OXENFREE About the Game TVs turn on and off. Planes lose radar. Radio stations can't broadcast through the static. In the small coastal town of Camena, unnaturally occurring electromagnetic waves are suddenly causing interference with electrical and radio equipment. Reluctantly, Riley Poverly returns to her hometown to investigate the mystery, but what she finds is more than she bargained for. OXENFREE II: Lost Signals is the mind-bending follow-up to the critically-acclaimed narrative adventure game OXENFREE from Night School Studio. Play it as a standalone story or dive deeper by playing the original – it's up to you. As you play, you'll shape every step of the story through your choices. How you choose to deal with the supernatural events at hand will forever alter the future. Your choices matter. Shape everything through your conversations and dialogue choices. Forge a deep friendship with an old acquaintance from high school or opt to ignore a lost fisherman in need. Your choices impact who Riley becomes, your relationships, and the story options available to you at every turn. Start chatter from anywhere. Use an all-new walkie talkie conversation system to chat with contacts and uncover useful insights about the mysteries of Camena. Ask for info, check in with the locals, or completely ignore them. It's your call to make. And, it has consequences. Stop Parentage. Five years ago on nearby Edwards Island, a few teenagers unwittingly opened a portal, creating a rift between realities and timelines. Now, members of a mysterious cult-like group called Parentage are deliberately trying to open a new portal to pull something out. Who are they? What do they want? Are they trying to contact ghosts? Tune in to the radio. Ghostly signals are piercing through the frequencies of Camena. Tap into the eerie sounds and static using OXENFREE's signature radio mechanic. You’ll communicate with the supernatural, manipulate the world, and travel to the past by tuning into time tears: unnatural fissures in the time-space continuum. Save everyone and everything. Your future was on the line in OXENFREE and those stakes are even higher in OXENFREE II. Explore, climb, and rappel across Camena’s beautifully treacherous landscape. Take risks and see where it takes you. It might be dangerous. But it could also save the future. Not only for Riley but for everyone.

Tune in to the radio. Ghostly signals are piercing through the frequencies of Camena. Tap into the eerie sounds and static using OXENFREE's signature radio mechanic. You’ll communicate with the supernatural, manipulate the world, and travel to the past by tuning into time tears: unnatural fissures in the time-space continuum. Save everyone and everything. Your future was on the line in OXENFREE and those stakes are even higher in OXENFREE II. Explore, climb, and rappel across Camena’s beautifully treacherous landscape. Take risks and see where it takes you. It might be dangerous. But it could also save the future. Not only for Riley but for everyone.
short_description: Five years after the events of OXENFREE, Riley returns to her hometown of Camena to investigate mysterious radio signals. What she finds is more than she bargained for.

_childDocuments_.review:
TVs turn on and off. Planes lose radar. Radio stations can't broadcast through the static. In the small coastal town of Camena, unnaturally occurring electromagnetic waves are suddenly causing interference with electrical and radio equipment. Reluctantly, Riley Poverly returns to her hometown to investigate the mystery, but what she finds is more than she bargained for.

OXENFREE II: Lost Signals is the mind-bending follow-up to the critically-acclaimed narrative adventure game OXENFREE from Night School Studio. Play it as a standalone story or dive deeper by playing the original - it's up to you.

As you play, you'll shape every step of the story through your choices. How you choose to deal with the supernatural events at hand will forever alter the future.
_childDocuments_.name: OXENFREE II: Lost Signals

name: Strange Horticulture
detailed_description: Find and identify new plants, pet your cat, speak to a coven, or join a cult. Use your growing collection to influence the story and unravel Undermere’s dark mysteries. Welcome to Undermere, a quaint town surrounded by hag-infested forests and rugged mountains. You are the Horticulturist, owner of local plant store Strange Horticulture. As a cast of colorful customers come by your shop, you are quickly thrust into an occult mystery stretching back hundreds of years. Explore the lands beyond your store to find new plants, but be careful! The dark woods and lakes are not always friendly to a simple herbalist. You might discover powers beyond your wildest dreams - or lose your mind completely. Use context clues to determine which places to visit, and which to avoid! Using your trusty encyclopedia and clues found on your explorations, you learn more about the strange plants you come across. By identifying each plant, you will be able to use their effects to influence the story -- from hypnotic hallucinogens to powerful poisons.

_childDocuments_.review: I was able to finish this in a day. I enjoyed it and sad how short it was. I think there is a missed opportunity for after completing the story, to just continue to play as a Horticulturist. I enjoyed identifying the plants and discovering things on the map. After the ending -  I'm glad I bought it on sale,
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome detective-style game where you identify plants by their characteristics, looks, and smells.  You meet different characters in your shop, follow clues and visit places on a map.  It's a bit like solving the puzzles in Obra Dinn, i.e. piecing the clues together.  It's not all that hard though, I wish it were a bit more complex.  Enjoying it a lot though, definite buy recommendation!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Cozy lovecraft plant detective vibes. The game is easier if you play it in as few sessions as possible, so that you can keep information fresh in your mind. It's very unique, and I'm happy I gave it a shot because I've never played anything like it before.The controller support isn't great; it just treats it like a mouse and a few keys. Works fine on a trackpad, though.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Plants, puzzles, maps, a vaguely creepy aesthetic?  Everything I could want!  This is super fun, and while it's short, I enjoyed it a great deal.  There are choices and different paths to go down, so there's replay value.  And collecting all the plants!  Highly recommend for anyone looking for a cozy, puzzle-ish game.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun puzzle game where you have to solve clues and cryptic notes to find strange plants and identify them without accidentally bringing harm to yourself or your customers. Recommended it to a friend who loves Nancy Drew--right up that kind of alley. Will appeal to fans of cozy cottagecore witchy gaming!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr: very pretty - designed to please the senses, but the 'exploration' tag is a cruel joke for a game that doesn't reward (some should as 'actively punishes') exploration, and the "gameplay loop" (if you can call it as such) is boring to the point where any desire to replay to go through the few different endings via the very few binary choice points is drained out of me. there are better games predating this, that it feels like SH leans very heavily on, which get less attention, and less praise for doing -the same thing- better. If it's a coincidence, so be it. But if the 'alchemy' isn't a simpler, reduced version of potion craft's, i'll be damned. pros; nice design (clearly a large proportion of the total effort went into it), some of the "card" puzzles were fun/esoteric.the purring cat sound is very cathartic.big list of cons;could be and should be so much more, a good 30-40% of playtime felt like faffing just trying to LOOK for more to do, outside of watering plants. maybe 10% petting the cat,no real incentive/reward for general exploration, as in something akin to Potion Craft (would recommend instead for a more gameplay focused experience with a similar idea; some parallels, is one of the many 'shopkeeper' games coming out over the last couple of years) combined with lacklustre map puzzle hints + the plant watering mechanic didn't really make for totally cohesive gameplay. It just didn't feel like there was a satisfying gameplay loop, given how repetitive your tasks are. I did play this before the update that had checkmarks for identified plants (which felt like a necessary feature, though I did just end up labelling everything anyway) but some of the UI detail felt a little unnecessary, as though features were intended and either never implemented, or because it was a good idea on paper. Things like the notes archive, and sorting, some of the tool snapping, and map navigation felt a bit clumsy etc. Expansion of things like the invisible ink lens for fun stuff/easter eggs/hints/secrets whatever would be good. The major story 'choice' points felt very binary, and are very few in nature, there's not a whole lot of deviation from the rails or fun things you can do with "wrong" plants. Given the earlier point about post-ending, the story does feel like it throws a lot at you towards the end, both in terms of the sheer number of plants you just seem to accumulate (and not use) and the fact the final few main events just seem to happen in quick succession after quite a lull.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: A short, chill puzzle game with a neat story.The gameplay revolves around collecting, identifying, and using plants for different purposes. In order to accomplish that, you end up finding/solving a variety of different puzzles, clues, and secrets. There is a really generous built-in hint system which will eventually spell out what to do if you keep asking enough on a certain task / section, so it's quite beginner friendly.The mystery and story is nothing mind-blowing, but I found it interesting and enjoyed it. There are various possible branches based on your actions / choices at certain points in the game which lead into a multitude of different possible endings.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I'm impressed. I'm quite a picky gamer myself, so of course i didn't expect Strange Horticulture to become one of my favorite games. I'm just  with the storytelling (short but well written), the vibes, the ambiance, and the songs/soundtracks that it came with. There's not much replay value once you've obtained all achievements and/or endings, though I would definitely get back into the game just to listen to the song and rain in the background (just like listening to an ambiance or ASMR).Considering its usual price, I wouldn't really say it's well-worth the money spent since I cleared this game with 100% achievement within 8.6 hours . However, I would definitely tell anyone to go for it once there's discount!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I HIGHLY RECOMMEND THE GAME BUT do NOT expect a mystery game. this is literally just a puzzle game. like thats it. the reason why i labeled this as "Not Recommended" is because i want more people know that this games genres was mislabeled. in mystery games you yourself, the player, discovers the story on your own. mystery games are basically just story-rich puzzle games but the puzzle is the story itself. however this game just feeds you the story. you do not solve the story for yourself.like, its a good game but i expected it to be a mystery, not a puzzle game but with a story going on in the background. i just wish the genres used to define this game was more correct because i was looking for more mystery games to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I think there are things to like and dislike about this game and, depending on your price tolerance, is fine to get for an afternoon/evening of entertainment.The good:- The game mechanic is pretty unique.      - You are trying to figure out which plants are which based on the descriptions and pictures you have in a book that you continuously add to.      - Each plant also has some effect that the consumer will experience.  Some of these are good, some are bad.- These two things combined mean you are trying to identify and then provide plants to customers.- The art style is, in my opinion, great.  The plants, the book with all of the notes of the plants, the world map, the different splash art for the areas and events you visit, all of that is amazing.  The one spot I will say the art isn't that great is the characters.  They aren't bad, but I felt that they are just very flat and lifeless when you compare them to all the other great art in the game.The neutral:- The story is interesting, but it feels very detached even when you get towards the end when you are supposed to have more involvement.  You are initially just hearing about what is going on from your customers, then you become more involved by providing solutions to the customer's needs that are tailored for what is happening, and then you get the ability to directly impact the story with your choices and even choose how the story ends.  It just never felt like I was involved beyond making some of the choices. I am more than willing to say that this is more of a 'I just didn't get invested into the story' thing than anything else, which is why I don't put it in either the good or bad sections.- The game mechanics and game concept were, for me, fundamentally interesting and fun.  I have some issues with the execution of some portions of the game mechanics, which I get into later, but at the core I think it is a solid concept.  It is very dialog driven and closer to a puzzle solving type game.  So if you aren't into that style of gameplay, then this lilely isn't the game for you.The bad:- You can't really give customer the 'wrong' plant.  There are times when you can choose to give the person a beneficial or detrimental plant, but you are still limited to giving them one of two options.  If you try to give the customer a plant that isn't one of the 'allowed' options, you gain some 'Dread' and a warning that you need to give the customer the 'correct' plant.- If you max out your Dread meter, usually 3 failed attempts, then you have to play a puzzle minigame and are then put back into the story where you were. The puzzles aren't hard and are just a waste of time.  They have no impact to the story and there is no other drawback other than you wasting time.- While identifying the plants is unique and relatively interesting for a while, storing the plants and trying to find the ones you need is more tedious than anything.  You can come up with your own label system to try to track them, but that only gets you so far.   One example is that there is a plant that can help the customer find gold.  However, when you have 50 plants, finding the one you know you have, but just don't know where it is, is more annoying than anything.- The game is pretty short.  I finished the story in about 5.5 hours, but I also took a break part way through, so lets call it 5 hours.  There also isn't a lot of replay value in my opinion as, outlined above, the storing of the plants becomes more tedious as you go.  You will also have the answers to all the puzzles the second time around, so the only 'new' thing is to see the different endings, but I don't feel it is worth 5 hours of my time to go back and see each of them.Overall, if you like the art style, the idea of being a 'plant detective' or botanist in a more fantasy world, and are ok with spending $2-3 per hour of entertainment, then this game is worth picking up.  If you have any issue with any of those above qualifiers, then I would pass.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game to play casually and work through puzzles. Well written stories and character development. Don't play the game with a guide, just go at it however you want and you'll be rewarded with the ending you want, along with the fates of the different characters based on your decisions. I'm on my third playthrough but I have a feeling I haven't seen them all yet, so will definitely play some more.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: This is a short, simple game but I had a lot of fun with it. The main puzzle is identifying plants with a guide that you have in order to fulfill (or not) various customer requests. You also receive a tarot card of sorts each day with a puzzle leading to new plants, and sometimes get letters with simple puzzles to find more plants. There is no time pressure and no real fail state (though some plant decisions lead to better endings than others) - if you make too many mistakes you just have to solve a little puzzle to get back in the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: It's 3 am after a few days of rabid playing and we're wishing there was more to this game, but it's been thoroughly played through.  The layout is not very complex at all, and the game play is very straightforward.  But you have to use deductive skills to figure out which plants are which, while you're lead through an absolutely wild story of adventure and intrigue and deception and horror and tragedy and more.  We're hoping there's another game like this coming!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I had this game in the back of my mind for a while but recently watched a stream with the developers. That really piqued my interest in the game, and I decided to buy it on sale. I am so glad I did. I love the mysterious, ominous vibe and the plants are so interesting! I highly recommend and will definitely be playing Strange Antiquities! DLC and more games, please! <3 :)
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Really calming and interesting - there's a wonderful sense of doing all these little tasks and trying to identify plants with the most obscure details while being on the edge of this creepy little mystery. The puzzles are fascinating - each one really needs a bit of thought. I wouldn't say the game is too difficult, but it's an absorbing time (approx 3.5 hours to get to one of the endings).Perfect for a rainy day :)
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing little sleuth game, identifying plants, exploring locations, deciphering clues/riddles, finding easter eggs and petting Hellebore who is the cutest kitty! Great little game to sit and relax to with a cup of tea. Found it really calming thanks to the playstyle, soundtrack and added kitty purrs. Add to that the decisions felt no pressure thanks in part to the factors mentioned which aided me through a high anxiety time. Overall great storyline and concept, high playability with little need for instruction or explanation of the mechanics. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Recently replayed this game and it still holds up as one of my favorite games of all time. The story in engaging and the vibes are witchy and cozy and creepy! This is the perfect rainy night or Halloween night game. Or sunny day, idc just play this game! The mechanics for identifying plants feels so good and specific, and I appreciate how "game over" isn't really that. I can't recommend it enough! AND with the devs working on a new game which might take place in the same world???, all the more reason to get in here!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Very immersive and enjoyable. The atmosphere of the gloomy but peaceful shop and somber but soothing music is very relaxing, and finding and identifying plants from the various vague clues is satisfying and the perfect amount of difficult to be challenging but not frustrating. I also get a lot of joy from just labelling and rearranging all my plants. I'm nearing the climax of the story now, and it is quite gripping, in a quiet, slow-paced way. I hope there is more to do in the game after the central story conflict is resolved, because I really like spending time in this world.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I binged this game in almost one sitting. I loved it so much and the concept of it was great. Organizing is so fun for me and so being able to label different plants as well as identify them was a DREAM. The plot is interesting, too, and keeps you invested. I'll be interested to play again and see all that I missed because i know I missed quite a bit. 10/10 - I highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: This is  fantastic little game that gave me a far different experience than I expected and I love it for that. My expectation had been that all the focus was going to be on just giving people various different plants for whatever ailments, but the game ended up being a lot more than that. I also didn't expect there to be any real story here. I expected it to mostly be a store management thing with a sprinkle of puzzles.So what did I get instead?In Strange Horticulture you are indeed managing a shop, once again handed to you from a dead relative (points for creativity in that it's an Uncle this time), where you are caring for plants and selling them for various medical and spiritual needs. Someone will come to your counter and they will request a specific plant or a plant with specific properties. You flip through your little book and find the entry then based on the clues given in the book via the description or physical apperance (sometimes it will be something you look at more closely to find  a plant that smells a certain way) and then give them the correct plant.You will gain new plants by exploring your map. I thought at first that I would just look around at random. Instead I was delighted to find that the puzzles aren't just which plant to give someone, but also finding plants. You will get letters from people that indicate a plant or book entry location. You will get puzzles at the start of each day as well. Were they hard puzzles? Not really. However, they were very clever so I still really enjoyed them. I used the hint button very rarely in the game and it was almost always in relation to the plants puzzles more than the map puzzles. When I did use the hint button it was usually because I looked through my entries and it would seem to me that I was either missing a plant or missing a book entry. So I would use the hint button just to see if it told me I HAD the plant and if I didn't than I knew there was something else I needed to figure out. I almost never used it to actually find the solution to a puzzle. So again... not difficult, but the cleverness of the puzzles made me smile.Again though I expected this to be primarily a shopkeeping game. Identify plants, give correct plants, rinse and repeat. However, you will very rarely use the same plant twice. For the most part you are identifying a plant for a single use. This is one of the reasons why I highly suggest that when you tag a plant that you put all of your plants that are identified to one side of your shop and put all the ones you haven't on the other side. That way when it comes to finding a plant you need you can focus solely on the plants you haven't identified first since the plant you need will almost always be a plant you haven't used before. Then if it's not one of those you can go hunt through the plants you have identified.Identifying the plants ultimately ends up being less of a matter of manning your shop and more of a vehicle by which the plot is moved forward. Sometimes a key moment will happen where a person will ask for a plant and you will be given the option of picking between two different plants. What you choose will branch out to a different story as there are multiple endings in this game. It seems there are 5 and I've found 3 of them (including the "bad" ending that it seems few have gone for). On the note of the endings by the way. Some of the endings are VERY obvious on how you get to them. You don't have to actually do a full play through of the game to get the various endings it seems. One of the endings I got was from playing all the way to the end, another I had to just go back to day 11 for and the other I think was like day 15. The key different choices I made were made on those days. So you can get various endings without playing all the way through if you are able to identify what likely changed the story as you do your first play through. The last two endings I haven't gotten are strictly because I will need to do a full play through to get them because I have no idea where I changed the story to not get them.Is the story good though? I would say yes. Did it blow me away? No. There IS a twist in the story that I didn't expect in regards to two characters. Otherwise I could see where the story would go for the most part. I still enjoyed it though. I really liked the way it was set up. However the game play at the end of the day is my favorite part of the game.I really enjoyed the loop of solving a couple map puzzles a day, identify a few new plants, and repeat.My ONLY issue with the game is that I wish you could put multiple tags on a plant. There are a few times when your clue is based on the "latin" name of the plant and it was kinda annoying to have to flip through the book to hunt down those names since they aren't in the index in the front of the book. It would have been nice to be able to tag a plant with it's normal name, a tag with a nickname the plant goes by, and then it's latin name. Or if the game had a second index that went by the latin names instead of the regular ones. I get that it's like this so you actually have to skim the book and "research" rather than just looking through the index, but it got a bit frustrating on somethings. Such as when I had to skim the entire book (and it was long at this point) to figure out which plant went by the nickname "Sweetbreath"I'm going to wrap this up though with the aesthetic of the game. I love everything about the design. The desk with the drawer makes me think of Papers, Please where you can have some stuff on your desk and tuck away others. I love the artwork of the plants, everything is pretty clear and easy to identify specific features, with some plants being juuuuuust similar enough to be confused. The character design, I don't know if this could be an inspiration, and animations of the characters reminds me of old flash videos like Childrin R Skary except colored instead of black, red, and white. It's just the vibe I got and it made me feel nostalgic. The only aesthetic design choice that I didn't appreciate was the text on letters and the maps. This is only because i have reading comprehension and sensory issues. So sometimes it was very hard to read the writing. I know it doesn't match the aesthetic of the game, but I wish there was an option to toggle off the cursive and "ye ole" fonts so that they are easier to read like the text in the book. They do give the option to zoom into the text because it can be small and I appreciate that accessability feature, but I was not able to find a font changer if there was one and I wish there were.  Frankly that was my biggest issue with the game and... maybe even my only one.So who should by this game and what are my overall thoughts? Overall thoughts is that this is a clever puzzle game with nice design and a decent story.This game is something I would recommend to people who like to catagorize and research things. People who like to sit down with a simple mystery and puzzle experience.I don't recommend this game for someone who is looking for something highly difficult. You will be disappointed. If you can appreciate the cleverness of a puzzle though. Those moments of "Ah! Well that's neat" and enjoy it despite it being easy then you'll probably like it. If you want something hard this isn't the game for you though.If you are looking for a LONG experience this game also isn't for you unless you, for some reason, find the game hard. My play time at this point is just shy of 9 hours and that was for one full play through and two partial play throughs that I was able to speed through at that point because I remembered most of the plants from the points I started at and on. I would say to get the last two endings I would probably need no more than 3 or 4 hours. So total play time is soooooomewhere in the realm of 12-14 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Strange Horticulture is a mysterious, compelling, and beautiful puzzle game unlike any that I've played before. The dreary, mysterious, Lovecraftian atmosphere is wonderfully translated within the first few seconds of starting the game, and it works in tandem with the sound design to enhance what is truly a superb story. The puzzles are exquisitely integrated into the story itself--they don't feel out of place, and are just difficult enough to provide a sense of accomplishment every time you complete one. This is a top notch, artful game that is well worth the play for anyone who is a fan of botany, mysteries, and gloomy "cozy" games. Plus, you can pet a cat.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game! It is incredibly satisfying to come up with your own organization system for plants. I love the graphics and the audio. The ambiance it creates is amazing and cozy in a dark way. I am on my third play through now and I love that you can get different outcomes based on your choices. Getting to pet Hellebore is also a huge bonus in my book.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: PROSThe Visual and Audiative Experience: The atmosphere, the art, the soundscape, the weather changes... simply gorgeous.Plot: I love it fact that someone made a game to act as a witchy plant dealerAlso, there's a cat.CONSShort: I played for 9 hours and reached one ending.Ending: The ending I reached felt at bit flat.NEUTRALTempo: Quite slow except the ending.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: One playthrough doesn't take very long, but it scratches the puzzle itch and has replayability because the characters have different endings depending on your choices. Bonus: at the end of each playthrough you have the option of cataloging the remaining unidentified plants to satisfy the completionist urge. I am amused by the different plot paths, especially when I realized there are options only available with a specific combination of choices. I'm on my 5th playthrough now and still discovering new choice trees. Highly recommend, especially when on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Nerding about weird plants - checkPetting the cat - checkExploring occult-themed story and puzzles - checkListening to the sound of rain while organizing your plants and bottles to a satisfying order - checkIn other words, a very chill and relaxing little game. I'm kinda sad there's not more but I enjoyed it while it lasted (got all the endings, identified all the plants).
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I thoroughly enjoyed this game. It wasn't what I had expected when going into it originally, but I'm ok with that. Honestly it was really hard to stop playing and not just chase every thread that I could find, but I also was getting so into figuring things out that I would miss things that were in front of my face and lead me to get frustratingly stuck at a few points. Easily I can forgive that since it was my own error that caused me to get stuck. I do, however wish, that the game was longer, or at least the post-game was longer. I wasn't too thrilled with the grind post credits, even so, it doesn't stop me from loving this game nor interfere with my plans on replaying it. Honestly I would love an update which would give more plants, not even for story use, just an after a fact, just to give customers more plants, and maybe some more potions as it's an underutilized feature. Really I just want more for this, even if nothing big is happening, or maybe a new mystery comes about, either way I'd be down.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: You have a plant shop with no catnip... why the hellebore not?All I would grow would be catnip and Hellebore would go bonkers!... that would've been cool to watch, whilst supping on an ice cold elixir.Like in real life, I'm rubbish at looking after plants.... so why didn't these plants die?... not even a wilt? - I didn't water them much/at all... after 16 days I would have had a forest of twigs sitting on the shelves!All in all, a decent experience, preferred the mini stories to the main, not difficult for my ageing brain, overall a quality game, good music, intrigue - is good - recommended to all.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Nice, pleasant game, that could be described as a mix between "Papers, please" and "Cultist Simulator", but without timers or the need to rush. Everything is very relaxed: you can even take a break watering plants or cuddling a cat! The only downside of the game is that it's quite easy, but if you want to spend 8 relaxing hours collecting and identifying weird plants you will not be disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game, a good 5-8 hour time sink! Some puzzles are ridiculously easy, some took me an hour to figure out. Definitely has some Potion Craft vibes. I really liked how the encyclopedia had depth to it, the world-building aspect felt super detailed. Going to play through again to achievement hunt very soon. One thing I think would improve the game would be to add more non-story based plant requests every day. It would make the game feel less rushed, because there would be breaks between story progression. It would also give more opportunities to use the plants which you might not label until the very end, when the librarian comes over to you. Overall, cool game and concept, can't wait to see what the developer makes in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Very cool concept, created by 2 very talented brothers, with a map based on the Lake District in the UK - which was a cool little touch. I don't want to spoil too much, but I will say;I didn't get this for a while due to how I thought it would play (the screenshots etc), it looked a little too complicated for my little pea brain, but it stuck in my mind and I'm glad it did. If you're on the fence too, just go ahead and buy it - it's not badly priced and I enjoyed the puzzles and identifying the plants etc. It was soothing but intriguing and labelling them all and putting them in alphabetical order was quite therapeutic to me.. I wish it was longer, but the only real way to achieve that is to have it not be story based, which would take away the charm of it so that's fair, I'm just greedy and enjoyed it a lot :P. Tiny tiiiny, barely complaint, is that I wish they switched the difficulty, puzzles being a lot easier so I'm not staring at the map as much, and harder to identify the plants/people not knowing what plants specifically on a more frequent basis and me having to work out what they want from their ailments. I also keep seeing this being compared to Papers Please and I see the comparison, there is definitely a cross over but just to note, there is NO time limit during the day, the day ends once you've served the maximum amount of customers, unlike in Papers Please. And I prefer this, I do not enjoy timed games, it makes me feel rushed. Very glad that that's not a thing here.

_childDocuments_.review: Loved this game! _childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Absolute delight! I finished one of numerous varied play-throughs in about ten hours. Don't let this put you off; if this was a book we'd call it 'un-put-downable'. My shortened play time is the result of heavy binge. GEMS:*The ambiance. This game has 3-4 screens, the main screen being your plant shop. In Help Will Come Tomorrow, this bored me something fierce. The charm here is that you can rearrange your plants, pet your sassy cat, and there are weather effects outside your greenhouse windows, with soothing rain and thunder sounds on occasion. Regular visitors and customers  break potential monotony. The color palette is 10/10 for beautiful and chill. *Working through each 'day' takes effort but is never a grind- something I struggled with in Graveyard Keeper where simple tasks involved tedium. Solving puzzles and identifying plants involves real deduction and you feel rewarded for your time. The game understands how to balance challenges so that you never lose that immersion.*Your desk! The drawer in your desk is organized with occult and deductive tools, slots for letters and clues, and LABELS. You can make labels for the plants you identify. I know this sounds 10/10 micromanager but the process is satisfying. Drag and drop organizes your items, no fuss required. The interface makes them available on the map and laboratory screens.*The art style. Along with the color palette and ambiance, the overall style has a wonderful hemlock-y Series of Unfortunate Events feel. The tarot card clues between levels add a bit of occult. The error meter is illustrated with a sick/dying plant, which leads me to...*The error meter. Occasionally you make mistakes in crafting elixirs and identifying plants (some are very similar). When your worrisome, sad dead-weeds meter fills, you've failed one too many times. Rather than force you to repeat the day or penalize you, the game offers one of several genuinely satisfying puzzles (solve the pattern/arrange the pieces). The secondary delight of this is that I didn't dread failing a task, making challenging portions fun and stress free. *Story telling. The dialogue of the characters who enter your shop, the letters from acquaintances out traveling the world, and the stories from people you travel to meet with are all short, punchy, and immersive. The use of language to convey a lot with a little while keeping it evocative is great. All of this contributes to a overarching plot that's tropey in the best sense.  *Pleasing soundscape! There is no talking but the sounds for discovering a plant or unlocking a page in your horticulture manual are as dopamine-inducing as Mario collecting coins or picking up stacks of things in Stardew Valley. The music is lovely and understated. And again, the sound effects are so atmospheric; thunder with lightning outside the window; rain tapping against the glass; a terrible hiss when you mis-mix an elixir. Your black kitty Hellebore! Which leads to...*Hellebore gets her own bullet-point. You can pet her, she reacts, and she purrs. Not a cat person but her little personality is great and her purring is warm and happy.*The travel system is fantastic and streamlined. Your world map is beautifully-drawn with some points and landmarks that never play into the game but add depth to your sense of the world. There's no point in going to the map unless you have a clue or letter involving travel, and once you solve the clue you know exactly where you're headed. There's no tedious wandering and feeling overwhelmed by the world at large. Plus, extra travel points from watering your plants! If you do wind up in the wrong spot, or fat-finger click outside your destination, watering offers a brilliant secondary means of recovering travel stamina. *Puzzles. Outside the penalty puzzles, main game puzzles are clever and satisfying. Some plants have actions that can be used in a number of ways. You feel extra smart when you sort out a plant's properties and overcome a challenge. *Coven of witches. 11/10This game was an absolute joy in every way. While I got what I consider the best of all 'good' endings I can't wait to try others just for the pleasure of playing again. And you'll discover an incentive that makes it worth playing for at least one of the 'evil' endings :p Happy horticulture, Hunter of Hunters
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: The potted Palliance sits upon the shelf, minty green leaves swaying below its dusky blue flowers. Behind it, the rain patters against the window, a comforting white noise to fill the peaceful little shop. I flip through the pages of my notebook, scribbling thoughts and theories onto scraps of papers, when out of the corner of my eye I see my sleepy black cat raise his head towards the front door. A customer comes in, shaking the rain from her jacket. She eyes the dusty shop, filled with hope-tinged skepticism, before requesting an herbal remedy to help quell the insomnia keeping her up late into the night.I tap a quill against my old desktop in thought, before pulling out an old crinkled map and spreading it out across my desk. I look across the mountains and rivers before swiftly departing in search of the plant to help this woman. I return soon after, in hand a bulbous plant crowned with a lovely cluster of blue flowers. I hand the Forest Camphry to my dear guest, whose eyes are now filled with confidence. She nods her head in thanks, and backs out into the storm.The shop is quiet once more. I scratch my cat on the head as I rearrange the planter with my favorite Ambrella, enjoying its sweet scent of honeyed strawberries filling the air. What a lovely day.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Reminds me a bit of the early days of gaming. It's a little inconvenient, it's not like anything else, the plot is a bit underbaked, there are features that exist only for tone, and replayability is low. It's also fun, it doesn't overstay its welcome, and oh how those features that exist only for tone distill things perfectly. It does feel like there is untapped potential in the mechanics introduced, but similarly, I suspect that if the money forces a DLC or sequel on the devs, the result will be something tighter and less enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Not much of an avid gamer but have been playing games for a couple of months now. This game has a pace so that beginner gamers like me adapt easily and can keep up. I had the opportunity to have a walkthrough of the game for a couple times and each time I could try something new such as for this turn lets put the labels in accordance to the type or maybe not at all. _childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a gemstone of a puzzle game that I enjoyed and still enjoy playing, so here are the pros and cons for this game:PROS:* Graphics are stunning; the plants look like those vintage stickers used in scrapbooking, which I actually love. The overall aesthetics remind me a little bit of the Edgar Allan Poe stories* This game has a DEMO, thank all gods for that (triple-A studios, have a seat and take notes, ty)* The story line is intriguing, mysterious and in some occasions, dark* There is a wide variety of collectible plants for all sorts of purposes* The puzzles are interesting and fun and you really need to pay attention to every clue, every letter, in order to solve the puzzles* You have a lot of tools to use in your exploring: mysterious artifacts, maps, your book of plants, microscope  etc* The exploring area is quite large for a puzzle game, so you will explore a lot* This game has !8! different endings, which again for a game like this is quite a lot and I love the re-playability aspect of this game* You can also brew elixirs based on the recipes you get from various quests* A lot of story characters to interact with* BONUS: a lovely black cat called Hellbore who loves scratches and purs CONS:*TOO DAMN SHORT*Maybe it would've been cool if we had a more diverse soundtrack to go with the different characters and quests that we are interacting with, but it's not a big deal.*Would've loved more customization options for the shopOverall, this is such a great and lovely single-player puzzle game and I definitely recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: i love this game!!! very cosy and fun with a dark twist. i have finished it twice now and im definitely planning on playing it again. Even when i thought that i knew what to expect, my second ending had a pretty big plottwist :o im very excited to see what other endings there are. definitely recommended if you want to play a relaxing but interesting puzzle game... and if you like plants :))
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I do not play a lot of games, but with this one, I was absolutely immersed. I completed it within a day because I was so engrossed in it.There is also a simplicity in exploring and labeling plants that make it almost relaxing. Even when I mixed things wrong, I didn't get frustrated. I just tried again.My only critique is that a lot of the "scavenger hunting" (lack of better description) were somewhat vague and I had to do a great deal of reading and sussing it out. It doesn't help that you only get a small amount of freedom due to our protagonist being a hermit so if you guessed wrong, it was watering plants until you were ready again or you do it sometime in the next day. Still, I had fun.  I'll definitely play it again in the short future when I forget a lot of things I did so it can be almost fresh and I can get immersed all over again instead of burning myself out.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Literally just buy it! Especially with fall right around the corner, this is spooky cozy vibe central right here! I absolutely love this game. _childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: More fun than I guessed it would be. I thought there wouldn't be enough action but it was really engaging in a "theater of the mind" kind of way. The game only took me 5 hours to 100%, so I hope they release additional storylines in the future. I wanted to give one character some comeuppance and never got the chance. No spoilers, but that character punched a dog and here I am with a shop full of poison! I would have liked a feature that allowed me to draw lines on the map to solve some puzzles. I would also have liked an index of locations. You click on map tiles to discover new plants; but usually only after that tile is activated by a clue. If you like Lovecraft, Myst, Agatha Christie, and kitties--give it a shot!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: A cute point-and-click puzzle game with a foreboding feel. It's a bit disappointing that it couldn't be based more off of real plants, but the magical element is probably what makes it more fun/tolerable, especially if you don't have a lot of plant knowledge like me.Using the microscope for examination, a book, and some key words through dialogue, you can identify plants to satisfy your customer's needs. Explore a grid-like map and solve more puzzles to unlock new plants/items/recipes. Use labels to tag your identified plants. You can be as descriptive or plain as you like. My only non-spoilery advice would be to only tag them as you identify them. If not, well, you'll probably find out why later on! Can't say I'd replay it again, but it definitely stands out and carries a lot of charm. Everything is alive with animations and you can even pet the cat!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Finished leisurely in 17 hours, completing the story and all plant identifications. It was probably paused while I did other stuff for some of that time so I can't vouch for the real, exact length of play.A fun game that has puzzles of varying difficulty. There is a hint button that will give 2-3 levels of hints, with the final hint basically solving the puzzle for you.There is a story which you largely interact with via conversations with customers. Occasionally you have an option between two different solutions, which has a minor impact on the story and can lead to alternate endings.There are a lot of plants to identify, though most of them are only needed once. It does feel satisfying collecting new pages for the book, identifying plants and labeling them, and organizing them on the shelves. The watering can doesn't seem to do anything; you don't need to care for your collection at all. The gameplay is limited, but the game ends before it gets boring. I did not explore the alternate endings, and it looks like you'd need to start over each time if you wanted to do so, which I don't. I'm not inclined to replay a puzzle game, since I already know all the solutions.I do recommend this game. I had fun playing it. But it is very short and has limited replayabliity.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favorite new games. You have to identify plants and fulfill requests, even adventure a little bit into the surrounding areas by solving puzzles that show you where to go. In some cases you must identify plants to help you progress. Make no mistake - this is a strictly an aim & click puzzle game with wonderful writing and graphics. And you really have to think for yourself. Multiple failures are "punished," but very fairly (just solve a puzzle and try again). It's unique and pretty wonderful, I think.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: You act as a background character throughout the game, handing out various plants with special properties to customers, whilst a bigger threat looms far away outside your shop.I love this game. It's calming, it's engaging, despite having no monetary system it feels very rewarding and it has good characters.A nice little touch to the game is that everything feels manual. You have to decipher clues as to where to find plants, search a map for the specific locations (Which was probably the longest part of the game for me), retrieve the plant and then try and figure out the name of it. Then you get to name the plant yourself using the labels, so you could even list the properties or nicknames of the plant if you wanted to.I realised there are different endings to the game as well so I'll likely be replaying it soon. I really enjoyed my first playthrough of this game and I hope it achieves an award in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: This game has quickly become an obsession. It's a great story-driven puzzle game about matching description to plants and solving map related puzzles. It's not the most challenging of games but it's fun and engaging. The mysteries that unfold are compelling and you are given just information to stay intrigued. Giving the wrong plant to a customer at a crucial moment could have dire consequences. It's a good game to play with someone else. My partner watched me play and helped me with some puzzles in a cozy autumn evening.If you like story heavy games with puzzles like Ace Attorney or Ghost Trick but with a slightly more somber tone, then you should get this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was fun to play! I finished in about 4 hours. I am a quick player though. You can set your own pace with this game, which I really like! _childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: It's about 4-5 hours to complete one playthrough, but there are multiple endings and some choices you can make that impact the outcome. The game mostly involves solving puzzles to identify locations on a map to search for new plants and determining what each plant is based on clues given. There's not much else going on. There's some good lore to read and the story is enjoyable, though sometimes you are presented with choices without really understanding the options or what could happen as a result. Overall, it was a chill, enjoyable experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Fun light puzzler that stood out as just different from many games I have seen on the market. Played it while I was ill one weekend. Enjoyed the plot, the map, the plants etc. It's a nice one for a rainy day, or if you want something that is going to stretch your brain without making you want to throw things at your laptop in frustration. One recommendation to the devs if they go down this route again - the sort of "find this plant by it's latin/nick-name" type book searching is OK once or twice, but less engaging than the more subtle puzzles of working out which plant is which. I definitely hope you make many more games! Love the Lake District theme as well. Good luck!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game. While I was stumped a couple of times, I really enjoyed the puzzles and the mysteries of the game. It made me think without being mind crushingly obscure. The quiet rain in the background and the aesthetic of the art created a really comfortable atmosphere that made me think of curling up near a fire on a cold day. Looking forward to going back and finishing the other endings.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: There's a great game in here. There really is. You can tell just how much time went into the information on the fictive plants, the world of Undermere, and the depth of the puzzles. I think a Breyer's Disk is one of the coolest mechanics I've seen in a game. Like, any game.Where the game falls flat for me is just how  it is to mess something up. Using just three wrong plants sends your character into psychological freefall. You have to solve an objectively tedious jigsaw-like puzzle to get another shot at it. If you misread a clue and go to the wrong location on your map, you have to wait for your Will to Explore to refill, slowly and painfully, watering your plants and stewing in your frustration until you can try another location.It feels a lot like Myst. Both in terms of the complexity of the puzzles, and the agony of bashing your head against them until you figure something out. A lot of times, this game just made me feel stupid. Which isn't what you want a game to do! Eventually I looked up a guide so I was able to enjoy my plants and engage with the story, instead of being annoyed with it.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the sweet, fuzzy, and slightly occult flower shop I never knew I wanted to inherit. The graphics are charming - FYI - if you find the font hard to read, there's a setting for that. (Thanks for thinking of that, devs.) The music is soothing without putting you to sleep, and I think my flower shop might actually play something similar near closing time.At first I thought that learning about the plants would be tedious but I find it rather fascinating - and the unexpected surprise of exploring the world adds a depth to these interesting stories. It's not hard to put clues together and there's something very satisfying to my "Strange Book of Plants" having fewer pages and more checkmarks. There's a weird satisfaction, for me, to simply rearranging the flowers neatly or organizing my labels by rows. It starts to feel like, well, my shop - where I know things are and people had better NOT mess with my organizing system. Part of the system, is of course, the odor experience.Gameplay wise, if you played "Papers, Please", the interface will feel familiar. So far (2 hours in) I haven't run into anything timed which is fantastic for me. If you're a bit lost in the beginning, try click-hold-drag. You'll figure it out, and there's tips along the way. There's a "hint" system on the right if you get stuck or start to feel the slight bit frustrated (don't let that happen, these are plants, stay chill). Sit back, enjoy the plants of your choice, and learn about your town's "interesting" mysteries with its plant-based remedies - at your own pace.Oh, and always pet Hellebore. Even if you don't like cats in real life, the purring is very satisfying.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I only recommend this game if you are willing to take your time to read and understand the dialogues and descriptions in this decelerated game. The soothing music creates a calm atmosphere and makes you take your time to listen to the purring of the cat and think about the different characters and their requests twice. A wonderful display of how creativity in Indi games can create something completely new and beautiful.In a world of prequels, sequels, remakes, remasters of the same franchises again and again, this is something fresh.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: As far as I remember (played around a year ago), I liked it but also did not. There's secrets to uncover in this world and multiple story endings. Plus, who doesn't love a cat!! Identifying the plants and caring for them was quite fun. At times, I needed to search on the internet for answers MULTIPLE times which to me means that a game has not made things clear for the player. Overall though, it's not a bad game. I would still recommend it, just remember you might find yourself stuck.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: A relaxing puzzler. There's no clock to beat or battles to fight so my heart-rate and cortisol-levels stayed low :-)I took my time and reached the end in 16-hours - so it is shortish but worth the low-$ I think since there are  several different endings --  replayable.  I missed naming quite a few of the plants so I'll give it another play-through in a few weeks (when I've forgotten some of the clues).
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game! I was eagerly anticipating it after the demo last year and it didn't let me down. Thoroughly enjoyed the ambiance (especially when it rained), puzzles were good without being impossible and the hints were pretty good, as well, for the ones I used. My biggest complaint is how short the game is. I could easily have played multiple storylines as the horticulturist. I will be playing it again, as well. I did find myself a little surprised at how sudden the ending seemed to come--I didn't think I was ready for it.There are a couple of things I would have preferred, as far as the mechanics of the game go--1. It would have been nice to be able to take notes in the game, especially to be able to keep track of what plants I've matched (or think I've matched) in the book.2. I would have liked more space for plants, etc.There are  a couple of other things I could be a little nitpicky about and some things I think would be great in a sequel, but overall it's an awesome game and I highly recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: If you love visual novels and/or puzzle games, you're going to love this game. It is so hard for me to put this game down, there are so many levels of puzzles to figure out in this game. I have not been bored yet. The story is beautifully crafted and watching the puzzle pieces fit together is very rewarding.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: This game seems too dependent on luck, it doesn't provide enough information from inspecting plants to make a proper educated guess, as the book describing the plants talks about entirely different things then the inspection does. I got a refund on a discounted price.. because i don't like guessing when it has consequences, it didn't feel thought out.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: So happy to see the @dukope style "doing a job but it's interesting" game design getting played around with, and running a plant shop in an occult land of mysteries is a great and surprising application of that.Can't say if it's leading anywhere satisfying quite yet, but having a great time with what I've played.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games that catches you by surprise. Finished the storyline in just under 5 hours, which puts it as a shorter game but that's perfect if, like me, you tend to never finish longer games. I love the cutesy little plants and organising them with labels. I love that it encourages completionism. Love the art style and the look-and-feel of the game. The font is a little hard to read but they offer an alternative! 100% recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: A nice chill game, albeit one with a mysterious story. You run a potion shop. People come in requiring remedies. When you start out all you have is a shelf with some plants and a tome to consult that gives you clues to what the plants may be and what they can be used for. A person comes in with an issue, you consult the tome and (hopefully) identify the correct plant and thus provide them with a remedy. As the game progresses, you need to explore your area (the UK's Lake District) to find more plants and expand your tome with more pages. The interface and mechanics are simple yet very engaging, but as you progress a local-mystery starts to present itself through the characters that visit your shop. This is what elevates it beyond a simple puzzle-solving game with a cute art-style. It is still a chill game at heart but with an extra edge by revolving around a central mystery. Very engaging, highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: This is the kind of game I generally don't like, but I loved this one specifically. The style and story more than made up for the gameplay, which sometimes dragged a bit -- especially once I had most of the plants and often had to scour my book for hints about the specific plant I was trying to ID at the time.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Nice little detective/puzzle game. I managed to finish the story and  in about 6 hours, so bear that in mind if playtime is a selling point for you. Nice atmosphere, nice story, good mechanics - I thought the puzzles were a bit easy at times but there were still some satisfying ones that require a bit of critical thinking. Worth the $20 price point if you like puzzle games.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: A definitive YES for this one.This is a game that doesn't look like fun at all from the outside. A game about plants? Are you nuts?However, inside of it is a great game that combines puzzles, exploration, investigation in a simple, smart and sometimes challenging way. Along with it is a competent story that unfolds as you progress, pushing you to properly investigate and catalog your plants as the climax gets closer and closerAlmost everything in this game works. Exploring the map with the clues is fun and really makes you think sometimes, reading about the plants is satisfactory and never gets old, sorting them out in your stand is relaxing and you can even water them if you want to be a good Horticulturist. Later on you get additional powers and skills that help you progress in different ways and the characters and text manage to unfold the story perfectlyOf course, there's some negatives in this: Some of the clues, plant descriptions and puzzles might feel like they make no sense (this might vary from person to person. I know I had some of those but I'm sure there are people that will say that all of them were fair), the overall UI feels cramped sometimes (specially the map, even if you have a magnifying glass) and there could be an error tracker somewhere in there (to avoid visiting the same place twice in the map, or trying the same plan twice)However the overall experience is fantastic. This is a game that knew what it wanted to be and manged to point all of its mechanics and resources towards that goal. It's unique, fun and satisfying to complete. Congratulations on the team for making it. It's worth every penny
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: It is a bit slow for my taste but I still appreciate the tone and setting very much. I also just really enjoy a good indie game. A single run of the game provided me 14/18 achievements and there are eight endings if you would like to replay the game. I can appreciate them building some replay value into this but I can't see myself going through what would be much of the same dialogue and plant categorization all over again.  It does get a bit tedious towards the end with  all the reading and referencing you have to do but that is all part of the intended experience. If you don't think you will be into a slower game requiring you to constantly reference your materials then I would pass but if you want something a bit different that involves some deduction give it a go.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: This is a pleasant, relaxing game that becomes gradually more challenging as you progress (though sometimes it can be a bit too samey). It's not an exciting, adventurous game, but it has a story and purpose that becomes clearer as you get into it and there are some quite challenging puzzles along the way.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting puzzle game! It actually reminds me a bit of Return of the Obra Dinn for some reason. I bought it right before the sale and don't regret spending the difference. Only issue is I wish there was more after the end like you having to help townsfolk with their issues once you have all the plants.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I'm guessing I'm about 1/3 or 1/2 of the way through the game (but could be way wrong) and am really enjoying it.  It does have the board game feel and it would be neat to see this turned into something like that.  How to make it competitive? Whoo... I did encounter a bug, but found the developers very willing to listen and are already working on a patch fix.  So will chill out and look forward to further play.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: A delightful game, well made and well designed. I encountered no bugs, no issues, and the only difficulties I had were of my own making. The game is designed for multiple endings, and the save/load game mechanics support that. Instead of having to waste time replaying identical content you already went through, you can pick up exactly where you want to.It's not too spooky, but there's still a sense of consequence to your decisions.I have no complaints. The only things I think could be improved would be if the lore and story was based on historical events, or the plant lore was a little deeper/real.  But those are not faults, just things that I think could make the game even better!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Cute and cozy little witchy plant collecting and identifying greenhouse, potion making apothecary game with a branching story interwoven in Strange Horticulture's daily commissions, allowing you to unravel the story on your own journey of exploration and discovery. There's a lot to uncover and minimal penalties for wrong guesses (the need to solve additional puzzles after 3 strikes) which leads to very laid-back gameplay. Best of all, you can pet resident black cat, Hellebore and, since there's no time limit, ignore the customers from Undermere and surrounding areas to spend hours just giving scritches. 6.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: A really lovely little plant-based puzzle game! Collect, sort and identify plants to help your clients with their requests, and maybe get wrapped up in trouble brewing in the background. It's a short game full of flavor, it'll probably take most people a few hours to beat but it's well worth a play and has multiple endings! I would absolutely recommend this game to pretty much anyone.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: This is a little gem of a game- soothing management and plant identification, interesting puzzles and an immersive storyline. If you want to live your best witch life in a rainy greenhouse while ominous customers pull you into interweaving macabre stories, you will find yourself at home. My best advice is to play it with an analog notebook and pencil on hand because many of the puzzles depend on remembering factoids or parsing out information from lots of details. This can feel even more immersive- I know it makes me want to create a tourism guide and doodle my theories while I am playing through the day.Although there's no twitch reflex parts, the learn-to-play-by-exploring by interacting with objects might take a minute or two to figure things out. There's some hints the build started as a mobile game. (to explore the map you accumulate "will to explore" by watering the plants, and there is both a coins system and a timer, but the amount of coins doesn't seem that significant as the time will build up just through play. Nonetheless, there's no pay-to-play and it doesn't interfere with the flow of the game. It apparently comes in other languages than english, so I am possibly going to check out if it has a french translation in my second play through. It's reading heavy, so it would make a good language learning tool too.TL:DRIt's cozy, aesthetically extremely charming, and balances the tongue in cheek with dark.  The puzzles are moderately difficult, but not impossible to solve on your own- it's great to see where the adventure games of my childhood evolved to. Scratch Hellbore behind the ears for me, will you?
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: A really enjoyable game that uses just enough brain power to be interesting but still relaxing. Identifying plants and building my shop full to the brim with plants is just delightful gameplay. It's not a long game, but I think that's completely appropriate. It's just the right length to tell a story, without lingering too long and feeling repetitive.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game on sale and it was worth every discounted cyber-penny. Although I finished the main ending/storyline within a day, it was extremely enjoyable. The sound design and art is great, it feels very cozy. If you like farm sims, puzzle games, and/or witchy stuff, this is for you. I'll probably go back for a second playthrough to murder that annoying ♥♥♥♥ from the start.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: This is a short puzzle game, not exceptionally difficult at any point and does not have time limits within in game days. The 6.7 hrs is from two full run throughs, with the second using no hints (achievement to do that) and a repeat of day 16 (to get two different endings, each an achievement). Art's nice, stylistically simple but each plant is identifiably unique, and I love that petting the cat is an achievement. Map can be unwieldly to navigate, the text is small and sometimes clues are a little too vague. I will likely play through the game to get each of the eight possible endings (3 give achievements , so I have 5 left to do).
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Strange Horticulture is a calming and quaint game which can be played with low effort and at a relaxing pace.  The characters feel interesting despite only having brief connections with them and you start to get an understanding of what the world is like through these small windows of interaction.  Story wise, I appreciate the game and the multiple endings.  This is effectively a puzzle game that hands you a lot of the tools to succeed.  You'll be figuring things out largely on your own but the game does hand hold a little bit.Art style and music are also a plus.  (Plus, you get to pet the cat.)  There are some plants that don't necessarily get used but I believe that's the developers intent to misdirect when trying to figure out what needs to be used.  The story wraps itself up well but the world feels expansive enough that there could be additional content.  The game only took me about 8 hours to fully complete (and that was with me stepping away from the computer to play with my own cat while the game was running sometimes).  Aesthetics, story, and atmosphere are strong points for the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: *SPOILER ALERT* An amazing story puzzle game that's the perfect combo of chills and mystery. Once I found out the game had 8 endings, I decided to keep playing untill I've done them all. I've now finished the game 4 different ways and it keeps pulling me back in for more. It's the chill game I've always wanted and now have finally found.No annoying timers, just you, doing your thing, solving puzzles, traveling around the map for special plants, serving customers, following the story and scratching your good kitty Hellebore :) Thank you for this beautiful game!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: My husband gifted me this game and honestly, I can't get enough of it. I'm learning so many new things with it. I mean, essentially we're looking through what's technically the Voynich manuscript, plus having items from Nicholas Culpeper. AND, it's also decently accurate with the Cumbria region of England, like this is jam packed with references and lore to such an extent that I'm just utterly astonished at how much effort was put into it. Plus the plants are gorgeous and the story is incredibly interesting and the fact your decision matters is also AMAZING. Just I love this game y'all.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: A deceptively engaging and entertaining puzzle game. This title excels at pitching you devilishly clever riddles that are ju~ust challenging enough to test your wits, but not so obtuse that you'll be spamming the Hint button. The story's not too shabby either, adding a much-needed (and appreciated) narrative through-line for a title that would otherwise grow dull before long.It's by no means flawless; You'll be listening to the same looping piano track throughout nearly your entire playthrough and the game will sometimes reorganize a few of your plants without telling you. Plus, I think the game would have benefited from some voice acting for the characters to break up the musical monotony.All of that said, these gripes are minor sticking points in the grand scheme. By no means do they ruin the experience. Most of your time will be filled with pensive chin-stroking followed by many, many "EUREKA!" moments. Strange Horticulture gets a big thumbs up from yours truly.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommend. I found the game mechanics of puzzle-solving and identifying plants to be fun and relaxing while remaining challenging enough to keep things interesting. The underlying story was also interesting to follow. After completing the story once I realize there are multiple endings possible, so now I'm excited for two new challenges: uncovering the other possible endings and attempting to 100% the plant catalog.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: A delightful puzzle game with a very melancholic atmosphere and soothing music. I adore the witchy vibes. Bonus points for the pettable cat.One complete playthrough took me almost 5 hours, and there seem to be multiple possible endings. I will try for a different one when I am next in need for some relaxing occult vibes.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: The story was interesting, and it was fun to work through the puzzles.I have only played through the story once, but if you do much of the same in another playthrough I fail to se how it won't become tedious and boring to rediscover everything. Even if you make different choices and get different endings.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Spooky and cozy, with some clever but not brain-breaking puzzles scattered throughout. Perfect on the Steam Deck where you feel like you're carrying around a cozy pocket apothecary. Some things feel off--watering plants feels arbitrary, and doesn't really do anything to enhance the immersiveness of running a weird plant shop--but that's more an are of "could have been more thought out" rather than "this is bad."Good game, especially for spooky season.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Strange Horticulture has gameplay reminiscent of something like Papers, Please, and the story of something like Sunless Sea - and while it doesn't really reach the lofty heights of either, it's still a charming little game worth running through.To summarise: you, mute business owner, run a mystical plant shop with initially very limited stock and a very sleepy cat, but a series of letters and customers - coupled with off-screen expeditions to semi-arbitrary map locations - slowly fills your catalog, which you have to identify using an incrementally-filling book. The game is strictly linear: each customer comes into the shop in the same order each day, and won't ever ask for a plant which you haven't already had the opportunity to find. This might mean brief, mild frustration as the book suggests you find a plant that you don't currently have, but this is quickly resolved by solving any of the honestly very easy clues that pile up on your desk.
