The core gameplay loop of collecting and identifying the plants never really challenges, but with no time pressure or efficiency target (unlike the aforementioned Papers, Please), it's quite pleasant to relax to.The plot is delivered almost entirely through scraps of paper, short monologues from customers, and the occasional day transition screen, and consists of a fairly boilerplate folk-y horror core event with some completely unrelated vignettes scattered around it. There is some minor freedom in choosing an ending (of which there are several - although this will mean playing the exact same game many times, which seems like far too much of a grind to bother with), as well as a small handful of choices about individuals, but none of these are particularly consequential. In honesty, I didn't find any of the characters relatable or even slightly memorable (I couldn't tell you any of their names); there was just not much to really get me emotionally invested in any of them, and I clicked through the final 'here's what happened to the characters' epilogue without more than passing interest.Being frank, I think the atmosphere of the game was the biggest missed opportunity. While it's nice and relaxing to have the same workbench and the same music loop played throughout - bar one or two moments - it did nothing to add to the sense of increasing urgency that is clearly supposed to be building. Similarly, the monologues from the customers didn't do well to add much intrigue to the story, or really much beyond exposition: everyone is honest to a fault, basically laying all their motives and allegiances out as soon as you meet them and never deviating from them (I had a semi-constant feeling in the back of my mind that I was likely to be betrayed or spied upon any minute now - but no, everyone did exactly what they said they would do, with no twists or surprises... which lead not to relief, but to disappointment). Even  didn't really manage to inspire anything apart from one piece of incidental art, right at the end of the game. I hate to compare to other indie games, but Sunless Sea - while very different mechanically - managed to inspire feelings of dread, awe, horror, and a sense of impending doom entirely through text in a way that Strange Horticulture simply pales in the face of.While Strange Horticulture might not live up to the high - and possibly unfair - standards set by a handful of truly exceptional indie titles, it's still good fun for the few hours it lasts: a very chill and low-stakes plant-em-up to wind down the evening. I can only hope that the sequel, Strange Antiquities, truly evolves the series to a much more inspiring level.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: interesting concept with not so interesting realisation. anyway, still fun and i am sorry it took me only 8 h to finish the game. the riddles were fine, recognising plants was not so funny, but still somehow working. the story was fine and dramatic, but it was not clear in any bifurcation point (you were given a chance to solve some situation by two diffrent plants) how it might, and if at all, change the course of the story. and, anything involving a cat is perfect :)
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: A relatively short game - I finished it in about four and a half hours, including some time spent with the game still running while doing something else - but definitely worth the price.However, this game is not an endless game. There's a story here, and you will finish it. There's no endless mode where you need to constantly fulfill requests and such, but that's okay. There's other games for that.A few of the clues were a little difficult, but all in all, I had a lot of fun playing this game.I did end up with a rather messy store at the end, but that's fine.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I'm about halfway through this game and can already tell it's going to be one of my favorites! The puzzles are challenging, but not frustrating.  It's the same type of story telling as papers please, but without the time crunch that makes papers please kinda' unplayable for me.  Would recommend to anyone who likes story driven puzzle games, with a slightly creepy overtone.  Or if you're a sucker for anything with plants and multiple different endings, like me.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: This game checked all my boxes: alluring story that isn't just given to you; puzzles galore for both the intrepid puzzle player and for beginners; multiple possible endings; character development; cool art style; great setting; amazing concept; no time limits.If you're a fan of puzzles or occult stories, this game is for you. Also if you're a fan of "Papers, Please" but don't like the frantic time aspect, this game is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: The game is about 7 hours to play - but every minute was enjoyable. Some of the puzzles were 'tough' to sort out, but the Hint mechanism would point you if you get stuck. I had a great time organizing and re-organizing my plants so they weren't crammed, were alphabetical, etc. The story line wasn't a huge shock, but it was still really well presented and I found myself not actually skipping through or glossing over any of the dialogue pieces.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Very enjoyable puzzle game with lovely graphics and a neat little storyline - I loved identifying all the mysterious plants and how there were various different ways to do so. It did feel like it was a little short, but that was mostly only a problem because I was enjoying myself so much. Still, a lovely way to wile away a few hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of mysteries and puzzles, I definitely recommend this one.  It does two of the things I love most in mystery games: it doesn't hold your hand from moment to moment (if you don't pay attention, that's on you), and it has an excellent hint system that points you in the right direction without giving it away.  Crushed through it in two evenings, and had to go on to finish identifying the rest of the plants in the world. (Not my norm)
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Great chill game with a cool mystery, easy to understand but challenging mechanics, and plenty of quirky characters and lore.  Finished in about 5 hours, taking my time and petting the cat as necessary.You have inherited a horticulture shop in a mysterious realm.  You have a book with some clues as to the names and natures of the plants you own now, but must interact with customers from the realm to learn more and expand your inventory.  Through these interactions, you learn of something... untoward going on in the woods.The game is parsed into days, totaling about two weeks in game, so you don't have to sit and finish it all at once like I did - you could do a day at a time.  However, even completing the full story all in one sitting, I didn't lose interest or find gameplay repetitive.  It's full of mini puzzles and riddles but there's no timer... like a cozy game meets and escape room.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Its a really well designed game that feels more like an investigation than a florist shop.a bit short for its price though. first run took me 4.5 hours.there's a few other endings, but it will be much faster after your first time.matching plants to descriptions is fun, but might lose its charm on repeated playthroughs, so replayability might not be that high.pick it up while on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: A fun game! As others have said, there is a TON of reading. And you can't really breeze through the content has you have to catch clues to help you choose the right plant, location, etc. I would recommend this game to anyone wanting to play a detective story or folks who really enjoy plants. FWIW: In case you get stuck,  is an awesome guide.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Everything, I mean EVERYTHING, about plant identification, keying, the use of microscopes, the order of identifying a species… is either wrong or unbelievably inaccurate. It feels like a 4yr-old stumbled into their parents’ lab and started playing the work game. Tbh this can drive ppl who've had professional training in this field crazy caz there’s no logic or reasonable systems, at all. It’s simply a puzzle game with random “botany descriptions” (if those mumbles and urban legend-like stuff can be referred to as descriptions). Me, who could identify and write down a plant’s Latin class name by NAKED EYE in under 30sec and do this 60 times in a row (yes, that's how they test the easiest part of plant identification irl), is now forced to read this “it has a sweet scent like strawberry dipped in honey” ♥♥♥♥ four times a day, caz obviously that’s the only thing the main character could perceive with a MICROSCOPE. Lmao. Nah.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a decent game, as many have mentioned before - you can pet the cat and hear it purr. I also loved the sound the pages of the book make. Fairly easy mechanic, pretty art style. Interesting storyline and as a bonus, several different endings based on your choices in the game. HOWEVER, if you're playing to get all the achievements, it gets extremely repetitive.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Superb game if you are looking for a casual thinking game. Getting clues to identify and acquire plants for your store and help people with their ailments and otherwise. Has a nice aura of mystery and the looming threat of dread if you aren't doing your job well. There is an overall storyline but also has little offshoot threads that are not mandatory but most certainly worth exploring. Really enjoy this game when I want some relaxing fun. Highly recommend!!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I am not a green thumb or a gardener by any stretch of the imagination. though I do like plants and flowers. This game hits the perfect sweet spot of stress-free and engrossing that makes you want to keep going to find one more plant, solve one more puzzle, or just read the excellently written descriptions. There is enough of a story that you want to keep going, but not so much of one that it distracts from a very meditative and relaxed experience. Papers Please style gameplay meets management-sim style addictiveness. Definitely strongly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like plants? Mysteries? Creepy English country folk?This game is an absolute delight. I love plants, and figuring out each plant's ID has been great fun, plus there's a compelling story with multiple branching paths. The art is... fine. I'm not a fan of the characters' artstyle, but it's better than some games I've played recently.This will probably be one of the few games I try to get all the achievements for.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: There's nothing really wrong with the game, but it's tagged as puzzle so I thought it would be a bit more challenging. The gameplay has two main components: matching the plants on your shelf to the ones in your book, or navigating a map using grid coordinates. It also only lasted 5 hours for me. So overall, despite its charms and atmosphere, I have to give it a thumbs down personally. Again, the core gameplay is not really solving puzzles, it's just matching the description of a plant in the book to the one on your shelf. There's really nothing to it.I would only recommend it to someone looking to relax with a super short and super casual game. If you know someone who isn't into gaming, this could be a good introduction for them.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: The game has its charm, but the puzzles were too easy and the flow got repetitive after a few hours of game time.  The soundtrack became to oppressive so I turned it off.  I bought the game due to the effusive praise for it but I don't personally see what all of the fuss is about.  It was a relaxing game, which is why I recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I would definitely recommend if you enjoy puzzles, navigating relationships/situations with no definite 'good' or 'bad', melancholy, and rather clever turns of phrase. ( I do wonder how some of it translates.) The decisions you make impact future situations ie - the plants you find, the order you find them, what you can identify and what you can offer your clients. I have completed one play through based on what I thought were obvious nudges towards the 'good guys!' And was pleasantly surprised to find it wasn't nearly so cut and dry as I lead myself to believe. I will be starting another play through shortly in an attempt to address my own wrongs from this play through, and am excited to navigate the consequences that will bring on its own.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Had me mesmerised from start to finish - starting, unfortunately, at 11PM. It's just difficult enough. I only had to Google for help once, and that was only because I forgot it has hints built-in. The story and characters are interesting, although some of them look so similar that I forget who they are. Identifying the plants is very satisfying; I only wish the elixir-making feature was introduced a little sooner, and that there were more of them. Worth the price.Cat-petting is a 10/10 tactile experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: While looking for plants from your shelf based on a vague description seems fun at first, it quickly grows old and becomes a tiresome chore. As your collection gets bigger and bigger, the time to search for something increases dramatically and the game slows down to a stall.What surprises me though, is that this game offers no tutorial on what to do and how the game works. You have to figure out everything by yourself. Which would be fine, if the game had at least some kind of foreshadowing hinting on what types of plants you will eventually need and when. Or if it gave you some tips on how to sort your collections. However, the only thing the devs gave you is a lame 3-colored tag system (and I still don't get the intended purpose of the other tag colors), coupled with a huge shelf that doesn't fit onto your screen. You have to bear through hours of painful superslow scrolling to get from one side of the plant shelf to the other.Basically, this game should not have been released in this state. Its gameplay loop idea is fresh and interesting, but the tools given to learn the mechanics and run the shop are ridiculously underdeveloped. Even the player choices are limited to just a handful of points in the story, where you are explicitly given the option to choose from two different plants. Talk about a waste of potential. Why just pick from two predescribed ones? Why only in those very rare circumstances? This is a huge letdown, the game could be so much more immersive if you could give your customers any plant you please and they would respond based on what they have received...If you thought the story would save this, then you'll be disappointed. I have not seen such a slow and bland narrative in a long while. How can you mess up the perfect setting filled with magical plants, potions and secret cults? Smh. I don't understand why does a 14€ game have only one ambient music track that loops for hours on end, just worsening the headache you get by mindless scrolling through your plant shelf. I turned the music off completely after 2 hours.BTW this 2D game runs like trash. I get about 18FPS on average through the SteamPlay on Linux @1080p with a recent Intel GPU. There is no fast-paced action here, so it's still playable, but it is annoying, making me hate this game even more.What a shame.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: You would never guess by the looks of it, but this game is a hidden gem. It contains a huge array of puzzles revolving around plants, their abilities, local map etc. I was honestly amazed about the variety given the limited mediums. The atmosphere is on point as well, one may feel immersed in the occult, yet calm occupation of a horticulturist. You communicate with strangers, help (or not) them via giving them correct plants and see the consequences of a few of your choices, this honestly does give a vibe of such a job.Do not expect much from the story, but it is on theme and well written. Ambient music with constant rain in the gloom city feels pretty charming to me.Overall, immensely pleasantly surprised!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Great witchy, little quaint shop vibes. Great artwork. Love the aesthetic and the chill at your pace gameplay / deduction puzzles. Mechanically/gameplay wise, it reminds me a lot of papers please (minus the timed element). Ie, people walk in and you get plants for them, you have a little desk and trays to store books, clues, maps, etc. I like how even the puzzles themselves go along with the game aesthetic. Very immersive.Easy recommend if you are looking for a casual, indie puzzle game and the artwork looks like your thing.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Great Point and Click adventure with a dashboard home center. Recommend at $10 sale price. Would be nice if it was Rogue-lite. While there are 8 endings they are based around a small set of choices. Many of the clues and puzzles in the game can be randomized to give the game more replay value. Would be nice to do more with the plants, breeding them, feeding them meaningully etc. A great start both in lore for a world as well as a game platform. Looking for more variations of this in the future from Bad Viking.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Strange Horticulture starts off really strong and then grows a bit weaker as the game progresses. I was instantly enamored with the plant identification and discovery puzzles, but as you collect more plants, it becomes clear that the space you have to store them isn't enough and your little greenhouse swiftly becomes a cluttered mess. Also, the whole cult/demonic entity story line takes itself a bit too seriously for what it is and how little background each character has. The core mechanics are really what make this game fun - I couldn't care less about the story or multiple endings.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: It feels weird to downvote a game with overwhelmingly positive reviews, but honestly, I'm just not seeing what everyone sees in this game. I find it boring and repetitive. There are two main things you do in this game: Identifying plants and Identifying places in the map. None of them feel particularly challeging, rewarding or fun. This game is like a simpler, easier and overall worse version of Papers Please. I'd give it a 4/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Love the aesthetic, rainy and spooky. It's a very chill game to play, good for after a long stressful day when I want to just relax. The quests themselves aren't too difficult. I enjoy using the clues to find new plants. I've only had one instance where there seemed to be a glitch in the "hints" and I had to Google which plant to use. Otherwise, I'm enjoying it. Like the witchy feel. Already bought it for two friends who also wanted to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: This game is charming, compelling, and incredibly clever, for such a simple gameplay loop. While it may look like something of a shop-owner sim, in reality it's actually a very well constructed detective game. It's strange to say that identifying plants could become addictively exciting, but the thrill of getting a new plant or description and having a bell go off in the back of your mind makes for a surprisingly engrossing play. The story is fairly well written and interesting enough, and though a playthrough might only last you a few hours, there is the promise of multiple endings, and a bit of postgame content to give it a bit more value. Honestly, I just want more. An awesome, relaxing, but engaging little game.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Short-ish 3-4 hour puzzle for the first ending.  Linear storyline with branches- multiple possible endings.Clues will lead you to where you need to go- no randomly hopping around the map. No RNG?You cannot die- failures eventually force you into a puzzle minigame.Continues after the end so you can get 100% completion on all the trick and false flag plants.There only seem to be four elixirs, and they're all tied to recipes you get, so don't try tossing random things into the potion kit because you find 3 plants that seem to do the same type of thing.You can pet the cat.  Try the demo.  If you like staring at the book and trying to figure out which plant is which then this is the game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Beyond relaxing. Started playing and the next thing I know it's 1am. A story that is slowly coming together through the interaction with your customers. Selecting, labelling and discovering your plants whilst giving your pet cat some love. Lot's of reading (which is great for a bookworm) to bring together the narrative. Highly recommend if you need a break from life and just want to chill and water your plants!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent idea carried by a strong central gameplay loop and wonderful art and design, but the lack of story and the repetition of performing the same two simple tasks over and over again for 10 or so hours soon wore thin. For me, the game either needed to be much much shorter or add more depth and interaction to it's narrative and gameplay in order to provide more variety.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: A clever puzzle game where you use fantastical plants to solve the problems that your customers have. The puzzle aspect of the game comes in many forms, including plant identification, map reading, riddle solving, and using each plant's unique effects to help or hurt your customers. The game has multiple different endings, which going into the game blind, i was pleasantly surprised by.Solid 9/10, i would give it a 10/10 for what it is, but I felt like although the music is nice, the majority of the game is one track.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Use context clues, drawings, and little puzzle mechanics to identify ~70 different plants and mushrooms; pet and startle your cat; rearrange your greenhouse, and watch a mystery unfold. Soothing, mysterious, cozy fun. Puzzles aren't very hard, but manage to still be satisfying. 4-5 hours of gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: My playthrough was very fun, but it was even more fun to replay for achievement hunting after finishing the game once. With all the info about plants and events in the game already known, it essentially became a challenge of how much I could remember while getting through the game as fast as possible multiple times.Very fun learning experience and very nice game, definitely worth its price.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: There is little to say about this strange game except that it is a little gem.A relaxing game but one that entices you to keep going until you discover all the mysteries it hides; the plot is the main part of the game to which a management part has been cleverly mixed, plus of course everything about the mystery to be discovered, so it is also an investigative title.Undoubtedly difficult title to understand and describe, but trust me it is worth every penny.+1 point for the presence of the black kitty who will always keep you company.DING!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: First playthrough took 5-6 hours. The second one (with a different ending) is now at 8. Atmosphere, Art, Gameplay are pretty interesting and refreshing. However, length is a bit short for me personally. The puzzle/detective aspects are either you get it (easy) or you dont (cryptic) side.  And having played various puzzle games like Talos Principle, The Witness, all the Zachtronic ones, most of the puzzles here are fairly straightforward. Except for one which i had to search up (which indicates bad puzzle design). For those other games that i mentioned, i never felt like i had to search anything up; those were more of type where eventually you will solve it so long as you keep at it.Overall this game is meh, and i would only get it on a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I sat down and started this game and played for several hours until I had completed it. It is so rare that I actually finish a game, even rarer that I do it in one session. The story unwraps in such an interesting way, the puzzles are right in that sweet spot of being challenging and making me think a bit, while not being impossible and so cryptic that I get frustrated and feel tempted to look at a walkthrough. Plus you get to collect cool plants.10/10, if there's ever a sequel I'll buy it immediately.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: As a cozy gamer and detective story lover this game is the combined joy of both! Strange horticultur not only has a unique and beautifull design but a catching storyline that keeps you on your toes. i loved witnessing how my decissions changed routes and outcomes while still having the tranquility of my plant garden and snuggly little hellebore. I cant wait for the next game of this franchise and am hooked to see more:)
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: A fun, enjoyable game for anyone who loves puzzle games. The bulk of the game involves identifying unknown plants for customers, managing research elements (your plant book, letters sent to you with requests, decoding hidden messages, and using tools in your desk drawer), and exploring the map. I enjoyed the story line and meeting familiar faces. I also appreciated the mystery element of who to trust and who to believe. Kudos to the creators: I had a lot of fun!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Super charming game with a unique art style. If you like plants and you like mysteries, this casual murder mystery game is for youuuu. Lots of cool features in the game as well! From inspecting clues to collecting plant species to traveling to other areas of the map to uncover the mysteries, there are so many fun elements to discover in Strange Horticulture. Definitely recommend!!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Fun although relatively short, I liked the intertwining character stories, diverse characters and atmosphere (will probably replay it later just to spend time arranging my plants while listening to the rain and thunder outside and occasionally petting my cat). Also like the instant travel, not realistic but I don't care, I like to think the shop door can just open anywhere. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Having played for six hours, I can say this game is a delightful mystery, with an atmosphere of ancient magic and supernatural allure. I enjoy collecting plants and the puzzles are challenging but doable. My only disappointment is that the plants aren't based on real plants, which would have been a bonus education. This game is unique and special, and I wish there were more like it.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: This game is simply amazing. The theme, the music, the fascinating plant descriptions. While I was starting it I was afraid it may get boring after some time but oh boi, was I wrong! The little riddles and puzzles are great and though they can be difficult, I feel no need to search the answers online, because cracking it is fun for me. I don't even know when the hours have passed. Beautiful design, taunting atmosphere - that's what I was looking for.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, a fun, dark, quirky puzzle game with elements of mystery. I had expected a bit more interactive content based upon the game descriptions, and you really should be able to interact more with your cat. Despite the puzzles, in many ways it feels like an old text-based RPG, but that isn't a bad thing as the story is compelling and the design of the game is generally quite good. Most of the dialogue is well-written, tehre were definitely a few passages that surprised me with humor along the way despite the dark nature of the story. While there are a few different ways the plot can divert, most of it is fairly guided. The majority of the puzzles center around identifying the various plants in the shop, those you've inherited with the shop or acquired along the way. Do yourself a favor and turn on the "auto-label" function in the settings. Labeling each plant is tedious otherwise. You can always change the labels later if you want to color code (3 color options) or add a note to it. It took me about 10 hours to complete my first playthrough, and some of that was just due to me taking time to explore the map (such as it is--you never really leave the shop) and organizing and rearranging my plants on the shelves. I'll be doing another playthrough soon to try to get a different ending. (I got ending #2.)
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Not sure how to classify the game. It has a dark mystery adventure aspect, where traditional puzzles are replaced by identifying plants and locations based on more or less obvious clues. To be honest, I noticed pretty early (at the two-hour mark, give or take) that my brain is too inept to be able to identify the stranger plants and clues, so I did resort to (very well-written) guides to help me out. I tried to do it on my own, but when I got stuck I looked at the guides to continue playing, as I wanted to find out what the story was about. In the end I got a sort-of good ending, although two characters did not survive. I will recommend this one, as it kept my attention for 4+ hours and was strangely relaxing to play the whole time.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Quite a fun little game. Nice mix of logic, puzzles, gardening, and an eldritch horror story line. My only complaint is the game is not very long. There is a need to replay the game multiple times to get the full story line, but there is a lot of repetition on run-throughs. Expect the first play to take 2-4 hours, then subsequent plays about an hour each. Overall it's a niche game. But if it's your niche, its a great game!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: A lovely game reminiscent of the old Myst games in terms of just the right amount of difficulty in solving the puzzles. While there are consequences for choices and mistakes, there's no time crunch to add to the pressure. The music is pleasant. The font is easy for me to read (dyslexia). Plus, there's a cat you can pet, so automatically makes it 100/10 Game of the Year in my opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Really nice experience, there are lots of plants and the process of discovering each one of them is really fun.Game is short, but the price is fair (Maybe grab the game while it's on sale like I did).* Pros: + Really fun puzzles.+ Flower art is really good, i loved almost every design.+ Name tags for your plants.* Cons: - The game doesn't give you much freedom when choosing which plant are you giving to your clients, the developers really missed the chance to give us the freedom to be good or evil.- No real choice until the ending.- You can only identify plants when you sell them to your clients. It really defeats the purpose of uncovering all of the plants.Game is good, very recomended.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I spent my entire Sunday playing this game. I just couldn't take my mind off it. The puzzles are delightful, the ambience is immersive, and identifying a new plant species always feels satisfying and rewarding. I've seen one ending, and gotten several achievements. I plan to go back and get them all.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely, chill game with a great vibe. The quiet and dark atmosphere reminded me of old shows like Dark Shadows. As an agriculture guy, the horticulture aspect was super cool to me; learning about all the different plants, their uses and structures was very enjoyable.Pacing was very consistent and the story/characters unfolded in ways that didn't feel rushed, incomplete or that they were scrambling to piece an ending together.Puzzles were clever, fun and made sense within the context of the story. I cannot stand puzzles that are complicated and obtuse just for the sake of being complicated and obtuse. This was not the case here, refreshingly. I'm a big fan of weird fiction, so I did enjoy the story. Coupled with the atmosphere, it all made for a great narrative driven clicker.Only annoyances/gripes were that the sound effect played when you discover new plants is crazy loud. I also wish it had a more diverse soundtrack and I would have loved to see the alchemy system build out a bit more. But, I don't really have much negative to say about the game. Loved this one!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: This game is sooo cozy! I enjoyed every minute of it.I really liked the design, creating a very cozy, and mystic atmosphere. I loved solving the puzzles, even though it sometimes took me a long time to find the solution.  If you get stuck, you always have the option to unlock other things. I will definitely play it again in the future because of the different endings. AND I recommend petting the cat (I felt like I was doing it every minute) It will calm you down, I promise :)
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Totally worth the purchase. It's a game that you'll be able to finish in about 10 hours or so if you're playing till the very end. I enjoyed myself so much and had a great time! The art style is fresh, the narrative keeps you invested. All around awesome game, plus multiple endings. I do wish there was maybe a way where we could have more freedom when suggesting other not so well-being plants to customers - dealing with dastardly consequences later, but hey we're running a business here so I get it.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: The plant puzzles were fun to figure out but the failure mechanics seemed out of place. You had to wait to explore outside again and if you failed at guessing a plant 3 times you'd have to "revive" yourself by doing one of two puzzles which didn't change in difficulty and just seemed to be a waste of time. I had fun but finished it way too quickly
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic Game. It would be nice if you could use all three tags, One for the name, one for the Alias, and one for the effects. Also the end near the five plants, I believe I solved all the clues but I was missing one plant completely I had to lookup. I don't want to give any spoilers. I also think it would be great after you identify the plants if your book inserted a complete picture of the plant as to what is actually looks like in your book to find them fast, possible picture on one side and a description on the other and if the book updated with new details of the plant you discovered. Would also be a plus to have your plant journey have a tab for elixirs. All in all it is a fantastic game and will definitely buy a sequel. Look forward to more stories lines.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I've just finished my first run through and I had a fantastic time. The detail of the plants, the relaxed pace and the atmospheric music created a wonderful experience. I look forward to coming back to try for a different ending later. Gave me strong Cultist Simulator vibes but a more linear experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I loved every single minute of this game. I was hooked from the first plant through to the last.The mechanics of reading clues, listening to what people tell you, taking notes, researching, and then making deductions from what you've learned, is engaging and soothing at the same time. It's a perfect balance of creepy and comforting and beautiful.I chose to actively linger and stretch out my first play-through, and managed to spend over 20 hours enjoying and exploring the world before wrapping up the story. I will definitely be playing again, to see what consequences arise from different choices and how that shifts the resolution.I would LOVE future stories for this world. It's a wonderful place to relax, enjoy and exercise your research muscles.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Really great ambiance, and I like the level of difficulty puzzling through which plants are which. The story is just enough to be intriguing without being overbearing. It's got some decent replay value from making different choices, and since I waited a year to play it again I forgot what all the plants were.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Both cozy and spooky, and requires some more serious problem-solving than just finding linear answers. While the themes do get a bit dark at times, nothing is explicit/graphic. I love the style of the horticulturist's shop, the map and its mechanics, and all the letters. I also love the devices and codes. I found out that there's around 8 endings too, so your choices do have an impact on the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: There is a kitty... AND you can pet it. 10/10. This is a great game. The artwork is pretty and the story is pretty cool. If you do not like to read dialogue, maybe this is not your game. BUT this is definitely a comfy type of game. Grab a drink and a snack and enjoy solving some puzzles to identify plants!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: this game is amazing if you love plants and identifying them, or if you just like a rich story. plenty of online help if you get stuck, or just want to focus on story rather than riddles and puzzles. wish there was a way to load a save to before you made and decisions story wise, just because collecting all those plants can be tedious. Great game! def recommend:)
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Loved this. It's a relatively quick game if you're just going through it once. It's very relaxing, but puzzling enough to work the brain. I loved the art style, the storyline, the soundtrack, everything. Choices matter in the game, so at some point I'm going to play it through again, more than once to get all the endings. Awesome little dark cozy game.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I got instantly hooked on this game- it took me a few days to get all possible endings. The art, sound and story create an enchanting atmosphere. The puzzles and gameplay are simple but fun and rewarding, and they feel like a part of the story. The game lets you take all the time you want, which is perfect if you enjoy labelling your plants or figuring out all the details. Absolutely would recommend! Don't forget to pet Hellebore after every customer :)
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: This charming game has a pettable cat...Do I need to say more? No, but I will because this game deserves it.Unbelievably beautiful visuals with a cozy vibe. This game makes me feel warm and fuzzy yet also intrigued and cautious. I can't fault it yet and perhaps the only fault that I find will be that one day it will end Wholesome is a good word for Strange Horticulture, at least as far in as I am.I have started a series of daily let's plays if you want to take a look(I am new to PC gaming, but not new to gaming and this is my brand new channel)
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: It's a nice, relaxing game with a dense, yet subtle atmosphere. The riddles are fun to solve and have a decent variety. They do get tedious every now and then to keep you on your toes. The story of Strange Horticulture is also very nice with lots of dark magic and crime solving, all while trying to keep up with your job of being a horticulturist! I liked this game a lot and definitely would recommend it to people who are looking for a slow-paced, relaxing game.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Too easy and too repetitive. I have seen this game described somewhat accurately as a mix of "Papers, Please" and "Return of the Obra Dinn". Compared to "Papers, Please", however, the plot and your decisions affecting it fail to pack the same kind of punch, and the easy puzzles are boring without Papers' time pressure. And compared to Obra Dinn, the labeling puzzle you're solving is easier / less interesting.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Damn I don't really write reviews all the time but this game deserves mine. Needless to say, it's an excellent game! I love the aesthetic and style of the game as it reminds me a lot about the Rusty Lake games that I played on mobile. The story is mysterious as well as the ambience the BGM provides and I live for mysteries! Even so, I do have some constructive feedback. 1. I wished that there was more space that we can keep and organise the plants. After I had collected all 77 plants and mushrooms, all of them were squished together on the shelves, making it a tad bit difficult to navigate and find the plant I need and to organise them properly. I suggest adding another layer of shelves so that it also corresponds with the number of label colours. 2. When we visit locations on the map, I felt like there was a lack in the change of scenery. All that was presented were descriptive texts of the location and a small illustration. Perhaps some small cutscenes or images of the location we visit that span the entire screen would help. 3. With over 50 plants on the shelves and needing to right-click to closely inspect them one by one made my eyes strain a little. Sadly, I have no suggestions on how to improve this, so maybe other players can chip in their opinions on this. Thanks for reading my review!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Saw a streamer play some of this and thought it looked interesting, put it on my wish list and got it as a gift. Its one of the most interesting and unique games I've played. I've really enjoyed the puzzles, haven't finished the game yet but look forward to playing it when I can. I would definitely recommend it! And i'll be on the look out for similar games.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: A very pleasant little puzzle/adventure game. The hint system works really well so I never had to go to a walk-through, but I still felt challenged along the way. I'm not sure I'd play it through again to get the other endings, but this was very enjoyable. I'd recommend selecting the auto-label option if playing on Steam Deck.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: It's ok? It didn't really click for me. I like plants, I like mysteries, and I like spoopy culty things. Identifying the plants based on the oblique descriptions and drawings was nice, but I just couldn't get into the story and the only times the puzzles stumped me were when I didn't read carefully.Let's be clear: it's a puzzle game with a plot, it's not a mystery game. A lot of the puzzles just happen to use text, so it might seem like a mystery game. However, you can completely ignore the plot and still solve the puzzles, and solving the puzzles doesn't result in you learning the plot.Also, for your own sake, don't touch the hint button.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: BEST GAME EVER!!!Art style = gorgeousMusic = subtle and slightly dark with an edge of mysteryMechanics = point and click, user friendlyStory = multiple endings, story changes based on player choicesReplayability = amazingly fun, I spent 2 days playing multiple endings and am going back for moreCharacter development = diverseDifficulty = challenging enough for a hint or two during first playthrough but never needed a guidePuzzles = varied from easy to mindboggling Negatives = First, would be more fun if players had to actually take care of the plants. You run a plant shop but the plants never need any maintenance. Second, the timer for traveling is rather pointless since you can water the same two plants over and over to speed up the cool down. Why bother with the mechanic? Third, one particular plant (Wandering Bue) moves each night and shuffles the plants it bypasses. Nothing wrong with that; it adds a quirky uniqueness to the shop. The issue is that plants all over the shop change location every day when the wandering bue was on the other side of the shop. I tested this many times and, yes, your plants randomly shift locations so why even bother with the wandering bue specifically? Finally, would have been more fun if weather played a bigger role in the appearance and identification of the various plants.I experienced no bugs, glitches or issues with this game. It is a beautiful game with wonderful story telling. I am addicted and eager to hunt down all the possible endings. Something I've only felt with a small handful of games. Ever. I love being able to label the tags however I choose. That was a genius mechanic to use as it gives players the freedom to organize the shop how they want. I highly recommend this game to those looking for challenging puzzles with an air of Lovecraft horror.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: A pleasant deductive reasoning game with a wonderful mix of straightforward puzzles and ones requiring lateral thinking, making for a nice combination of achievement and friction. The story provides suitable set dressing and intrigue, but ultimately feels more like an excellent proof of concept for narrative game design than something really immersive. Took 5.5 hours to see one ending, and I'm not going to go back to get the rest, but I enjoyed my time and can easily recommend. 3.5/5.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Strange Horticulture is a delightful little puzzle game of scant clues to find and identify plants in a dark fantasy-tinged Industrial Age England.Clean graphic and sound design, a selection of characters to interact with, and of course, a cat.My first play-through took about 8 hours - a few steps took some thinking, but there were only two where I was unhappy with the answer.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: This game was so interesting! From the story line to the characters... and of course the BEAUTIFUL artwork! Beyond impressed with the amount of thought that went in to each plant! I've written so many notes for this game it's unreal, but good! I love a game I can get so invested in that I just can't stop myself from taking notes! Highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: this is such a cool game. I've never left a review on a game but this one is just too awesome, I don't even know where to begin. the art and animations and natural textures are amazing, and it's so satisfying when you figure out a new clue. there are so many aspects to Strange Horticulture; the incredibly well-done map, the 70+ plants that were apparently all INVENTED FOR THIS GAME, the phenomenal story line and characters... i could honestly go on forever. if you can help it, don't use any guides--just go in blind and figure it out on your own. trust me, it'll be so worth it when you start to see the pieces come together and everything starts to unfold before your eyes. it's just suspenseful and spooky enough to pull you into the story, but not so much that it scares you. i haven't quite finished the game yet (i am a very slow player who forgets to turn off the game when i leave the computer) but i can't wait to watch the rest of this story unfold. apparently, there are multiple different endings too, which are influenced if you can spare like fifteen to twenty bucks (don't remember the price but it was somewhere around there) i would totally recommend purchasing this game, it's so well executed and the writing is really good. amazing job, devs!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying that I quite enjoyed Strange Horticulture for what it is.  It's just a shame that what it is is fairly insubstantial.  There's not a whole lot of game here, and that's a shame because the potential is there for a much deeper and more engaging experience.  Still, it's an interesting central game mechanic and it manages to tell a fairly interesting story via that.  Worth checking out.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: The story is excellent. The game is visually appealing. I love the label system and spent probably way more time organizing my plants than necessary but it was really relaxing and super satisfying once each shelf and tag were in just the right place. I changed my organization system around a couple of times finally landing on Lavendar tags for plants with consumable or topical properties, Rose tags for plants that should come with a warning as they have adverse effects, and finally Yellow tags for everything else. During one playthrough I had all of my plants arranged chromatically which was pleasing as well getting to play my own puzzle inside of this already wonderfully curated puzzle game. Plus Helleborn is easily the best shop cat in a game to date. I love his silly litter mannerisms and the glorious ASMR experience of his purrs when you give that good boy skritches.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: A delightful little game. I got it on sale in the Lunar New Year sale, but even at full price I'd be happy to recommend it. I completed (not 100%) the main story in a little over 4 hours, but that was in a single sitting. It was incredibly compelling, and the ambience and sounds were delightful and relaxing. Best cat purring simulator ever. The puzzles aren't terribly complex, one baffled me for a little while but beyond that they were just enough to give that dopamine rush of successful completion - Yes, I *am* a smart one, aren't I? Pet the cat, get more purrs. The story is interesting, and there are a couple of different endings. Your choices in the game do impact your endings, but from what I can tell they don't change the story too greatly. A bit more complex than "choose red, blue or green" but not exactly divergent either. I would love to see the game expanded with new stories/mysteries. The plant location and identification gameplay loop was really quite enjoyable and I'd like to do more of it with a different plot if possible.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely fantastic. The puzzle of identifying the right plants never felt impossible but often felt hard which is the hallmark of a good puzzle game. It gave me enough room to feel smart and accomplished without feeling like it held my hand. On top of the actual puzzle nature of the game the story is pretty interesting and deep despite the rather unorthodox story telling system it employs. Highly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I thoroughly enjoy puzzle games, so Strange Horticulture was definitely a fun and quick game to play through! It's fairly simple in nature as a majority of the time you're identifying plants based off of different descriptions in a little book while "traveling" around your map finding even more plants to add to your shop (you don't physically travel, instead a window pops up and describes the location you traveled to and if you found any plants), and yet I was still intrigued by the plot and the little puzzles scattered throughout. Fair warning: there is a large amount of reading involved in the game, so if you're not really looking to spend a few hours reading plant descriptions and dialogue, I don't think this game will be for you. Other than that, I highly recommend this!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: "I'm looking for a red plant with thorns."*Checks book* *Gives plant to person*"Thank you!"That's the game... that's it. Sure, it's got a few choices here and there, and sometimes you have to check a map as well as a book... but that's it.When I got the game, I thought there was going to be alchemy or something. You're literally the owner of a shop, and you give things away. No currency, no money management, nothing.I've been playing it with a friend, and he's just as bored as I am. In his playthrough, he made a mistake 3 times. If that happens, the game literally punishes you by making you put a jigsaw puzzle together again in order to proceed. It's not fun at all... it's punishment. That's all.I'm 3 hours in, and nothing has happened yet. No idea why it has so many positive reviews. I guess people like handing things to other people, getting nothing in return.I'll likely continue playing it to get the ending, but I'm not having fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: very easy to play game where the challenge comes with matching shapes and following simple clues towards POI's on a map to advance the plot. solving the mystery isn't so much a part of any esoteric mechanics as it is the tone of the game. i was wanting this to be brutally complicated but it is very far from that, it's no Cultist Simulator where i'm fully bewildered into contemplations between sign and meaning. still, it is a satisfying clicker and the lore imparted on the individual plants are charming and made collecting them alot of fun
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: The game is interesting. You identify plants to give customers to help them to overcome illnesses etc. The only issue is it quickly becomes boring. The whole drag and drop could be simplified to make grabbing objects easier. Hotkeys for the encyclopedia etc. There just isn't enough space on the shelf either and after 60 plants things get messy. I made a line of mine at the bottom and as I found new plants they just messed up the order. There also seems to be a bug which has meant the 6th elixer isn't showing. Maybe because their wasn't enough space on the bottom? Sadly I can't recommend. Address the issues and I will improve the score. 6/10
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: Game developers are consistently improving the game and keeping up with correcting any issues that arise. I have been thoroughly enjoying this game, the story, and most of all the puzzles.Previous (negative) review: I failed to complete an early puzzle, did not see the prompt to use a plant - and now am unable to progress in the game any further unless I completely restart.  .
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: A plant collecting game with a mystery side quest. I was interested in the story, but there doesn't seem to be much of one. The ending I got had no weight at all and made me uninterested in seeing any of the others. The characters have no personality and look like they came from one of those paper doll dress-up games. Love all the plants, though, they are very fun! Only a few are actually relevant to the story, though, which makes all the collecting and identifying feel pointless. The fact that the whole game takes place in the plant shop is also kinda boring. Thematically it makes sense, but, I can't help but feel like that was a very convenient choice of theme for the devs.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: If the theme/story interests you at all and you like puzzle games like papers please BUY THIS! The story is amazing and hooked me in immediately, I could not stop playing and stayed up till an ungodly hour my first play through. The puzzles are just hard enough to give you pause but nothing you can't figure out given some patience and a careful reading of clues or plant descriptions. While the main game play mechanic is very much like papers please there is no clock working against you which pared with the music/atmosphere makes for a very relaxing yet captivating game.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: The game takes a little while to figure out, but once you do, it's very enjoyable.  The puzzles are challenging, some harder than other, but not impossible.  I really enjoyed having to figure out which plant was which, and labeling them.  Very relaxing, you go at your own pace.  Highly recommend for anyone who enjoys relaxing puzzle games!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: If you love plants and supernatural mystery, this is the game is a must.  The whimsical and macabre are at the thematic forefront as you discern fantasy flora with the help of your trusty plant guide. You'll receive letters, clues, puzzles, and hidden messages to lead you to new places and plants. These plants can be used to help, hinder, and make elixirs for you and your clients. Your mission, to solve the mystery involving The Servant. Multiple endings await you based on your choices. I spent ten hours for first play through with a good amount of achievements. Moderate replay value; I still need to unlock the alternate endings.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I LOVED this game, this was just what I was in the mood for! The trouble is... this game was very short. It had a terrific plot that draws your character into it gradually and ends with one of 8 different endings based on your choices. My favorite part (besides Hellebore the cat) was cataloging the 77 different species of plants. Some of them do not provide very good clues, but even in a situation where it's "Game Over", you do not lose progress. You simply need to solve a puzzle and you return to where you were. As I said, it's a short but brilliant game! If only I could go on collecting/discovering new plants and elixirs and providing plants to people in a post-game option... Alas, I cannot. What I CAN do is highly recommend this game if you want to relax, enjoy a good story, and some intriguing puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed the game! It has a great balance of hard puzzles that make you think and easy ones to help you understand what is going on. Overall really well done. At times things can feel a bit tedious and some of the puzzles really require you to have read and remember everything a character told you, which can be annoying but isn't the end of the world in my book. 7/10!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: omg!! this game is so good?? i was looking for a game for HOURS before this one caught my eye, and im so glad it did! i was looking for a game on the cheaper side but still good.... this blew my mind! the story was good, it has many endings, AND a cat!! its amazing, ALSO its about plant owning! it has all of the best things and the art is really good<3 all this to say.. you should totally get it
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: If you are considering buying this game, do it now. It's worth buying even at full price. It is very rare that I write a review for a game, but I felt extremely compelled to do so even after only 5 hours of play time. The ambiance set by the music, background sounds, and art is perfect for a chill gaming experience. The mysteries unfolding in the story line keep you engaged and wanting to know more. And the game gives just enough challenge to solve the puzzles (map, plants, clues, etc.), and won't make you feel like you're going to pull your hair out -- especially if you're like me and can get easily frustrated if you feel like you're missing something. After 5 hours in, there are a few concerns I have: 1. Replay-ability. I'm not sure how much the game would change if you make different decisions on the plant requests that you DO have an option to fill for certain customers. (Apparently there are different endings. I guess it depends on how much of a completion-ist you are to do multiple play throughs. 2. There are no "saves." The game is continuous unless you want to start over. And that brings me back to concern #1. You cannot go back and see the outcomes if you had made a different choice. If you have a mind like a sieve as I sometimes do, you might not remember what you picked on the next play through to attempt a different outcome. :/   3. Inability to decline requests for customers/plot driven fulfilling of orders. Obviously, based on the story line, there are a few customer plant requests that I wouldn't want to fill. There is no avoidance or alternate choice on some of these. If you answer incorrectly, you bring on "A Rising Dread." That isn't necessarily bad, but you have no choice than to give your customer the plant they seek.  Overall, my concerns above are not outweighed by the pros:-Ambiance-CAT!!-Music-Mystery-Puzzles-PlantsBrew yourself a cup of tea or coffee. Kick back and get comfy. Solve mysteries. Find plants. Pet your cat. Avoid dread. BAM! Cozy game experience :)
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not a big player of "cozy" games, but I still found myself very relaxed and pottering about the house making tea while playing this. The rain sound effects drew me in way too well, and the puzzles were engaging enough to keep you playing but still simple enough to go through even while in post work zombie mode
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty fun. I finished the game and identified 56/77 plants during my playthrough to give a more realistic idea of how long this game is. It's a unique experience with a few annoyances that I'll go over which some may find frustrating:* You can't search in the book which is fine starting out, but once you have dozens and dozens of plants it makes finding them based on the description of their benefits/traits very annoying.* Plants once identified and tagged are not sorted automatically, and sometimes don't retain their sorted order on the shelf. Once you have dozens of plants you have to sort them in some order, I went with alphabetical to match the book but having to sort them yourself or when they lose their place randomly is a bit tiresome. I wish they auto sorted once labeled.Overall this was an enjoyable experience that was different from many games, it's still all puzzles and logic but the setting is unique enough to make this worth picking up on a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I love plants, cats, and the occult. this game might as well have been made for me! it is so easy to get lost in the world of undermere. thank you for this charming, intriguing, and super fun game -- I can't wait to discover all the endings. (ps: if Hellebore is based on a real cat somewhere within the dev team, please know that I am metaphysically scratching them behind the ears.)
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I love the game so far. To me it's very relaxing and I love being able to try to figure out what each plant is. Still learning how to figure out clues but it's a fun game overall. If you're looking for a relaxing game this would be one. I also love how many of the days in the game are rainy days, this is another thing I find relaxing. I 100% enjoy this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: A very relaxing point and click puzzle game. I played the demo and was pleasantly surprised so I bought the game upon release and I have really been enjoying it. It's not super easy but also not really difficult either. If you do fail your mind melts and you have to play a puzzle game to rebuild your mind again. Interesting concept for a game, different and worth the money if you like these types of games.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Strange Horticulture is a great game for those who like the idea of spooky yet cozy. In this game you own a plant shop and each plant has special abilities. I loved identifying plants and obtaining goals; however, I found some of the descriptors a bit too vague or they did not seem to match up with the actual plant itself. Overall, it was a fun game that made me really think with trying to solve the puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Starts off a little slow but eventually the story and puzzles get more interesting and challenging. I like the multiple endings but wish I didn't have to replay the whole thing to try a different one. Despite the map this is not much of an exploration game. You can "visit" places but it only tells you what's there on paper, there's no sprite or location to walk around.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: A short, relaxing, spooky puzzle game. While there are a few more traditional video-game style puzzles involving secret codes and manipulation of objects, the heart of the game is simply identifying plants. Clues to identification come primarily from a book which inconsistently describes physical attributes, smells, and uses of various plants. From this incomplete picture and the initially small but quickly growing collection of plants available to you, you'll have to wrangle out the correct plants to offer customers, mysterious troublemakers, and mystic rituals.The atmosphere and interface are largely lovely, however flipping through the plant guide without either the rapid page-flipping benefits of a physical book or the ability to search terms as in many digital resources got mildly irritating at times. If you don't keep up to date and identify as many plants as possible with each new piece of information, I could imagine this becoming extraordinarily annoying later in the game. As it was, there were a few identifications where I needed to remember which plant had a particular latin name or had a particular anecdote prrinted in the guide and I went past the page I needed repeatedly in several complete passes of the book--this wouldn't have happened if I could have searched the text of the book for a key term or two.With those issues noted, I had a lovely time. I didn't find it especially challenging, but I did have to roll up my sleeves and put in the work reading through things and carefully considering different options. The story is simple but rendered delightful and fresh by your unusual perspective on it as the main players feed you smatterings of information while they acquire your services for identifying or selling plants.Highly recommend the game. It does what it says on the tin, does it well, and its over before it gets old.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: A very relaxing puzzle game about figuring out what plants people ask for with no time limit so you can take as much time as you want to figure out each request. I think at time of writing I'm about halfway done the story of the game which has occult/spooky vibes to it which I am interested to see how it plays out. There are a few multiple choice plant answers you can give to some customers to either answer their request as asked or do the exact opposite of what they asked for (a woman wants to not see spooky dreams anymore, you can give her a plant to do so OR a plant that enhances such abilities for an example) which I believe impacts how those character's stories play out.There's also a map which is used to answer riddles given each day or by customers which helps you find other plants scattered around the world. The only gripe I really have with the game is a mechanic that you get near the middle of the story is supposed to do something with the map and another piece of equipment after you find a particular plant (I'm being vague for spoilers) but the device never seemed to work and I couldn't figure it out and had to resort to a guide to help me find the plants the map would've pointed me towards if the device worked. It's likely I just wasn't big brained enough to figure out the mechanic myself since clearly the guide person got it to work so take that gripe with a grain of salt, but I still wanted to write my experience.Also you can pet the cat in the game which on its own earns a recommendation from me.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: A small but well-formed game that punches above its weight and delivers on gameplay, story and immersion.+10 for cosy goth vibes.Gameplay: There's no rush in Strange Horticulture. Gameplay is meditative and calm, ideal for those who love taking their own time to explore, put things in order and decipher puzzles. It's not stressful but it certainly isn't boring. There's enough to keep you interested as you quietly collect and catalogue a growing treasury of highly peculiar plants. Oh, and you also solve an occult murder. So there's that. Sadly, the game is just a little on the short side (my first - very leisurely - playthrough took only about 6-7 hours) but still well worth a play.Story: The story unveils itself at its own pace. Like the gameplay, it's satisfying and there's no rush. The cast of characters progressively introduces new world-building elements, and at times your new friends reveal wholly unexpected twists to the story as you go along.Immersion: Sound plays a big role in making you feel like you're the somewhat suspect proprietor of a deeply unusual plant shop in a small and gloomy village - the steady, relaxing patter of raindrops on your glass shopfront; the ding of the brass bell on the counter when a customer enters; the atmospheric but unobtrusive background music. Art style and graphics are solid, although I would have loved for the game to lean a little more into its own cosy goth aesthetic visually.Overall rating: 7.5/10 - a lovely little game
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful little puzzle game. Absolutely adored everything about this little gem, the beautiful art style, the characters you meet along the way (and maybe get killed, who knows), and the music. Even the sound effects felt like they had actual weight and purpose behind them. Deciphering the clues to find new plants, items and book pages was never dull and always felt rewarding, and determining what plants to give to customers makes you feel proud every time you go it right. Even the game over mini game was enjoyable. My only critique is I wish the game lasted longer, but the time spent with it is incredibly enjoyable and charming
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game with many different options and ways to mess up, which adds to the fun. Haven't experienced all the endings yet so I'll have to replay again soon.Love all the different plants and the characters. At first I had trouble understanding that the plants would be identified as you use them and thought I'd have to remember which one was which, myself.So much fun though.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Finished first playthrough of the gameRoughly around 7h per playthrough and it seems you need maybe 2 or 3 to find all the contents / achievementsOverall a perfect game for a chill rainy weekend afternoon. If you are the type of gamers that enjoy fast pace action packed, adrenaline rush games, this might not be for you. The game is slow but relaxing, curious and a bit challenging with its puzzle. Becareful, some puzzles are quite cheeky. Some puzzles are a bit too slow in my opinion, but then again, it could be just part of the charm.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this on a whim, and I'm glad I did! I absolutely adore this game! I loved being able to organize and label the plants in the way that suited me best. The puzzles and clues were really clever and I loved solving them. And of course being able to pet Hellebore and listen to him purr was very soothing.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: This is a well-made, intriguing puzzle game that can easily win one over with its diverse strong points: either with the plant identification process, or the map-based plant hunt or the choice-driven branching narrative. If you happen to love botany too, this is a "take my money" case. The premise and the story was on the verge of real-surreal, which was a really nice choice, the game has a truly excellent map system in my books ^^ and also, hosts a selection of quite original game mechanics that I did not expect (like the health/death/re-spawn mechanic). The best part of the game imo are hands-down the riddles which at times were truly eXhilarating [to subtly give away my favourite one].  I also positively recommend the attention the designers paid to matters of accessibility, usability, player guidance and in-game feedback, with special mention to the robust save system that allows exploring the branches of the narrative without unnecessary repetitions. Plus, I couldn't find a single bug (although I tried)!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: This game was so fun. A perfect puzzle game with a fun little mystery story strung throughout. Each day you're given mini puzzles, you identify plants, listen to the customers and slowly piece everything together. This game was super atmospheric and has a great cosy vibe. I think it was a really good length too, highly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Very enjoyable game with carefully designed ambiance. It's quite immersive if you like puzzle games with a pinch of mystery. However, be ready to obscure puzzles and riddles but your mistakes and miscalculations are generally forgiven. Be sure not to rush and take it slow and easy. Some of the puzzles requires high concentration and quick thinking. 8/10 from me!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Both short and tedious.  You'd think that a short game wouldn't have time to get dull, but it does because you spend most your time leafing through a book to find the relevant page.  The good part: interesting plants, fair story, and the fact that the game has save-points such that you can easily go back to choose a different path/action without the need to start a new game.  Sadly, those points are not enough to make the game worth the effort to play it.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Strange Horticulture allows you to assist local community members (cultists) with tummy aches, night terrors and the occasional murder. As the current owner of a niche shop on the quiet side of town you obviously  have a shop cat and constant pestering regulars showing up to hang around your counter and bother you while you're trying to read a map. The puzzles are fun, The music is relaxing and the art is nice. Definitely has the "witchy cottagecore" vibe. My only gripe is that there isn't a New Game+ or a way to save your labeled plants and potions. Also you can pet the cat. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: It's Papers, Please, but with more plants and less communism.My sole complaint is that there is only one piece of music on repeat. It's a nice piece, but it got old after an hour and I ended up turning the music off. Add a couple more songs, please!I enjoyed the puzzle difficulty. Challenging enough to make me feel smart without being frustrating. It would be a nice wrinkle if you had the option of saying you don't have something in stock. That would make the identification process more interesting.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: The charm wears off really quick as they stop having you deduce details in plants and start guessing at locations on a map with extremely vague and unhelpful clues. Even with the hints outright giving you the answer to add further insult, I was still left trying to figure out how the answer matched the riddle.That says it all. The biggest puzzle was how did the clues in any way match the answer. That's the level of puzzle design here.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the first playthrough. It had just the right amount of intrigue for the story, and the mechanic of identifying plants was very great. Some plants felt too vague in their description though and I had to rely on guides for one or two plants in order to progress. As for replay value, I just can't get myself to be interested anymore. The quests feel repetitive a second time.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: An incredibly chill game to play that requires no real commitment. You can walk away whenever and it will not affect time passage in the game. Which I really appreciate. The game is reading plant descriptions, trying to match them with the plants you get/find and finding the correct plants for clients that come in. Through the clients that come in you discover what is happening in the town and some of the choices you make can alter how the game ends. The puzzles are simple enough, making them more fun and less frustrating to solve. All in all, I enjoyed this little game for what it is, enjoyed it enough to replay it to try get the different endings. My only point of critique is that when you use the plants in brewery they don't get put back where they were on the shelves, but somewhere on the right making you put them back manually.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely loved this game (as in, accidentally stayed up until the wee hours of the morning to finish it!).However.I have to admit, there were aspects I found frustrating among the good.Pros:-Very relaxing, slightly spooky atmosphere.-You can pet Hellebore! 15/10 feature, kitty even purrs and leans into snuggles. There's an achievement you can get for petting a cat, which is always excellent.-Visuals are beautiful!
