I loved watching the plants move, the color choices were *chef's kiss* and I got so immersed in paging through the encyclopedia that I could practically smell it.-Music was engaging but not distracting. It's calming with a hint of something spooky around the edges.-Solving the puzzles was easy, but not so easy as to become boring. There were a couple I got stumped on for a minute, but I didn't have to rely on the hint button to finish the game like I have in other "puzzle" games.Cons: -There's a LOT of plants you don't use. Among those, several are difficult to identify based on what's in the book. Some don't get identified until after the main storyline ends, meaning you end up with a bunch of plants that're crowding your shelves with no idea if you need them. One such plant is necessary for several puzzles. I found it slightly stressful to not know what plants were what or if i'd need to know.-The process of picking the right plant, especially when the customer or book is vague, can be frustrating. Labeling/organizing plants does help some, but it doesn't always fix things. -I work in retail IRL, and was not expecting to encounter the same frustrations of customers not knowing what they want. Or what it looks like. Or what it's called. But it does (insert vague thing that several items on the shelf do). Or that one dude who asks for the plant that might as well be named I Will Irritate Your Skin and then threatens a lawsuit over it irritating his skin. However, the game *does* give you the very satisfying option of giving him I Will Irritate Your Skin 2.0 for being a jerk, so that was nice.-Some encyclopedia entries are all but useless for identification. There are a couple plants I ruled out as being the one I needed because a very obvious feature wasn't mentioned, or the Closer Look gave me a vague answer that applied to several possible plants.Overall, I loved it. Most of my complaints are due to my being a perfectionist/having some pet peeves vis a vis customer interactions, and they didn't cause me enough frustration to really be an issue. I'd recommend this if you love weird plants, witchy aesthetics, weird little towns with dark secrets, and raining karma on the head of one Isidore Burbidge. The jerk.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game more than I thought I would. It's beautiful and somewhat intriguing, but much shorter than I thought it would be. I completed the story in under 6 hours, and there were fewer options to influence the story than I thought there would be. I might return to do a replay to try and get a different ending down the line, but I think the main gameplay of identifying plants and using clues to find it on a map would be pretty tedious to do over and over for different ending. Would still recommend picking this up for a cosy evening of gaming, but I'd wait until it was on sale
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Perfect cosy game. No high stakes or timers, good soundtrack plus the rain sounds for asmr lovers, clever puzzles that are very different so you don't get bored and aren't repetitive, multiple endings so you can play through a few times to try get them all, interesting characters, fun plants that you need to use the clues in the books to identify, and a cute cat. No major negatives, maybe could be longer but the multiple endings help with that so not a big issue. Well worth the price and well worth playing... I will be playing again a few times to get the other endings.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun puzzle game. It takes approx. 20 hours to finish. The story is okay, but it's not the sort of thing in which you'd get heavily invested, but that doesn't really matter because the game mechanics is very engaging and original. Exploring the different endings is fun, though. If you like puzzle games and want to try something a little different, then you won't be disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Nice little investigation game, where you influence the course of the investigation by aiding or impeding the progress of various clients. Guessing which plants are which is really entertaining, and the game succeeds very well without a tutorial. The difficulty curve is expertly managed. I loved this game, I wish they'd make it into some sort of series, maybe set in different countries with some of the same a quite a few new plants... I want more of this!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Cozy Game Deluxe - with a hint of mystery and darknessThe only complain I have is that it isn't longer. I could have played this for hours and hours. But I loved every minut of it.Normally I have a hard time if there is to much reading in a game, because I tend to lose focus. But for some reason, I had no plablem with the reading in this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful little relaxing game that any fan of plants or apothecary will enjoy. Mechanics are interesting enough to keep you occupied without being too complicated. I loved solving the clues and searching the map for new additions to my plant collection. Music and animation is fantastic as well. Overall, a lovely game -- clean and well-done. Highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: The story was interesting. The artwork is pretty. Relaxing and also makes you think. The only thing I didn't like was the instruction on how to use items farther into the game rather than in the beginning. However, that doesn't affect how incredibly fun this game is. Multiple endings too which allows more play ability!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed my time with this game. As someone who kills all kinds of plants without even trying, I really enjoyed being good at keeping and identifying plants. Plus, there was a cute little black cat that you got to pet and (accidentally) scare every time you rang your bell. It was a calming, but intriguing game! I had a great time!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: You can pet the cat :)In all seriousness though, I was quite surprised at this game! I went in not knowing a lot about it but it really got me into the autumn vibes. Very dark academia if you will. I eventually did look up a guide for some parts but the puzzles are definitely solvable in the game, partly because there's a hint button if you're stuck. It is relatively short, so if you can, buy it on sale. It took me about 9 hours to complete. Overall great game! :)
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. Yet another one in the genre of esoteric simulation games with a wonderful story and aesthetic. Reminds me of a calmer cultist sim or papers please. The main story is satisfying and well executed and the puzzles are engaging, keeping you on your toes. Only real downside is that its not longer than 16 days but i hope this game really blows up and that they might even expand on it in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun puzzle game. There are different mechanics to uncover secrets on a map as well as discovering plants and their use. These little tasks are not too hard yet still challenging at times.The story is mystical and interesting. There are even some desicions based on which you're able to get to different endings. With just a runtime of approximately 5-6 hours this makes you want to explore other endings as well.The graphics are great. Nothing fancy but still very detailed and fitting for a game like this. Music and the overall ambience sounds are great. They really create a mystical atmosphere.All in all, this is a great game if you're looking for a mystery puzzle with unique mechanics and an interesting story to it.Plus points for being able to pet the cat! 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed immersing myself in the captivating stories and puzzles. What truly sets this experience apart is the flexibility in problem-solving; discovering multiple approaches to overcoming challenges added depth to the gameplay.However, there were moments where certain puzzles proved to be quite hard to solve, leaving me to seek solutions online. Which after finding out the solution I am baffled why didn’t I think of it because it was so simple to solve. Beyond the puzzles, I found great delight in tending to the garden and unraveling the intricate stories of the community. The ability to empathize with characters and match them with suitable plants was a rewarding aspect of the game, providing a satisfaction of offering the correct plant to solve the problem.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Very relaxing, and still chalenging. Right now I'm stuck, but nevertheless I keep coming back and trying new things. There's a story and a mistery (or more than one), but you don't really know, at least at the beginning, how does that affects you. A beautiful game, with simple controlers (only point and click, with occasionally having to press shift).
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game. It is basically a fantasy herbarium + mystery game. The core gameplay was pretty nice and the little puzzles engaging. Even if you fail, it is forgiving with re-tries and hints. It was fun to discover all the strange plants - a perfect match for material collectors and plant nerds, which I am. I took me 5 hours for the first playthrough. I played in English, but I had to take a look at the italian translation: the plant names are very well translated and sound like real plants, nice job! Maybe I'll do a second playthrough in Italian and try to get a different ending. The English names were very nice too of course. My compliments to the writers for coming up with all names and descriptions.Some notes:- I would like if there was a "note taking" mechanism within the game outside of plant tags. _childDocuments_.review: In Strange Horticulture, you have just inherited your uncle's herbal store in Undermere, a foreboding early 19th-century-esque town. Your business: selling herbs and solving occult mysteries.The basic gameplay loop is extremely satisfying. You identify plants by referring to an ever-expanding guidebook (matching features of the plant to the guide's written/graphic descriptions), and provide them to your customers in return for more guidebook pages and plants. There are also letters and other clues to sleuth out, helping you explore the world map (which could be accurately described as a 'scratch and win' puzzle sheet). Overall, the puzzles were very well thought out, if a little on the easy side  I felt some of the more interesting/difficult concepts could have been better exploited, but perhaps the lack of repetition ensures that the game doesn't outlive its 4–⁠7 hour runtime. The writing is polished, but story-wise Strange Horticulture seems a bit of a lost opportunity. The plot is pretty uninspired Lovecraftian fare, and not only does your character, 'the Horticulturalist', have no personality whatsoever, it is not possible to craft your character over the course of the game. I had no good idea of what the world was like at game's end, and, weirdly, everything seemed very low stakes. The game's outcome is determined by a very small number of decisions, whose consequences are, in general, not at all predictable.Similarly, the plants are beautiful, but the drawings of your shop customers are pretty uninspired. A major gripe is that when a new plant is added to your collection, it pushes all your other plants out of order (I spent so much time rearranging everything!).All in all, I certainly recommend playing this if you're attracted by the theme and are an avid puzzle sleuther, but don't go into this looking for a particularly engaging world or story.- Use the yellow/purple/red tags to tag the plants straight away. Use one colour for guesses and switch it to another colour when the plant has been officially 'identified'.- There is no point randomly exploring the map when you aren't following up a clue. I spent maybe 40 unnecessary minutes of my playthrough doing this. All you get is a bit of uninspiring flavour text.- If you are an achievement hunter, I wouldn't feel bad looking up guides on making the correct decisions during your first playthrough (which I didn't do), as the plot is pretty predictable but the outcomes of your decisions aren't.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing and I'm not entirely sure why. The concept is so extremely simple, but the vibe and atmosphere make it so damn enjoyable. The music is super chill and sort of mysterious. The art style is simple, but fits perfectly. The presentation of the gameboard makes it feel like a shop, even though it's only a representation of one. The identification and puzzle solving, while not typically challenging, could be at times, and were always fun. My only complaint, sometimes the clues given are a bit off and could fit multiple plants, or one is a better fit but it matches another plant.The story was weird and interesting, and I was curious to see how it panned out. _childDocuments_.review: The game is beautiful and the gameplay loop was engaging but the story doesn't add up to much, there seems to be no real replay value and the puzzles often felt pretty tired to me. The game promises:"By identifying each plant, you will be able to use their effects to influence the story -- from hypnotic hallucinogens to powerful poisons."  While it's true that as part of the game you sell people these interesting and dangerous plants and it forms part of the story, you don't really feel like you're much a part of the story. The exploration all takes place within a few lines of prose when you click on the map, while you remain firmly planted in the shop. And do these decisions influence the story? I think maybe but only in a very binary sort of way that doesn't ever feel like it really makes a difference. I've seen other positive reviews compare this game to papers please, but in papers please choices really did echo further through the narrative, and choices were always made difficult and interesting by having to balance your material circumstances with trying to help or hinder people. In this game, you can choose to give the rich grumpy landowner a rash or not, but what difference does it really make in the end?The epilogue as well is such a disappointment that just quashes any sort of ongoing playability once you've completed the main story.I wish i could pick a mixed review rather than a thumb's down, the design and some parts of the gameplay are great, i was compelled to finish the game but then just left with a feeling of disappointment.

_childDocuments_.review: Strange Horticulture is a plant identification game with occult elements. You inherit a plant shop with several plants and a grimoire with enough information to identify some of them. Visitors to your shop request certain plants or describe desired effects, and you have to give them the correct plant. On rare occasions, you can choose between different paths by either helping or hindering a customer. Eventually you are drawn into an age-old conflict whose outcome will be determined by your decisions.I found the story intriguing, if a bit short and not very original. But it was well written, and I would actually have liked more writing in general. The descriptive scenes for the various endings were most definitely good and engaging reads, but very short. The customer monologues weren't bad either, but it would have been nice to actually have a conversation, which is not possible - your only available "response" is to give them a plant. A narrator might have helped, but there is none until the ending, not even inner monologue. What's nice though, is that the game has a multitude of possible endings (considerably more than the 3 very distinct ones that give achievements, though most of them are variants of these three), and the game even takes care to show how your decisions affected each of the major characters via an epilogue screen.Gameplay consists mostly of three parts: One is identifying plants with the information in your grimoire, one is handing out plants to your customers, and one is traveling across a map to obtain new plants and grimoire pages. On 2-5 occasions you'll brew elixirs simply by selecting 3 plants. You do not actually have to care for your plants, they do not grow or bloom and cannot wither. You also do not have to worry about "stock" - once you have obtained a plant, it will always remain available, giving it to a customer does not remove it from your store. In terms of gameplay, you are not actually running a store - you don't "manage" anything, you don't set prices, in fact money doesn't even exist. The "store" is just a story hook.To identify a plant, you compare information from the grimoire to the looks of a plant. You can also drag a plant on a microscope to get more information. Usually, each source of information - the grimoire, the microscope, and the plant's look - provides 3-6 pieces of information, of which most are irrelevant. You have to find a combination of plant and book page where some of the information matches and the rest is free of contradictions. Effectively you're playing a "plant detective", which I enjoyed quite a bit, but some things felt a little odd. For example, when I know that I'm looking for a plant with rough leaves, then I should be able to check the leaves of all the plants in my shop, right? They are standing right in front of me, I would just have to touch them. But only for a couple of plants does the game actually tell you how the leaves feel, and that information may ultimately be a red herring for that plant if it cannot be matched to anything. The game deliberately withholds information that the player should have no problem obtaining, which feels forced and breaks immersion a bit.Getting new plants and new book pages is mostly done by visiting locations on a fairly large map (33x17 squares). You usually get at least two small riddles per day, and each of these leads to a location with new plants. Unfortunately you can only find these plants after you have been given the riddle, visiting the locations beforehand only gives you some descriptive text. This makes exploration pointless, but solving the riddles is fun regardless. They are quite varied but mostly really easy, though some of them require serious out-of-the-box thinking. At some locations you have to use a plant to find anything, but there's never more than one such interaction at any given place.Customers will never ask you for plants that you do not have access to, though you may need to find them first on the map. The customers will also not leave until they have received their plant, it is not possible to send them away. If you give them incorrect plants, you'll accumulate "dread", and after 3-4 mistakes on a single day, you'll have to solve a small mosaic puzzle to continue with the game - in which the customer will still be there, still waiting for their plant. This means that whenever you cannot identify a given plant or solve a riddle to obtain it, you're stuck until you find it - which isn't a huge problem given how easy the tasks are, but isn't great game design either.The plants, their locations, the riddles, and the main customers are not randomized in any way. This is not an issue if you play through the game only once (which takes about 5 hours), but creates an undue amount of repetition if you play again to explore other endings. You'll have to find the exact same plants at the exact same locations solving the exact same riddles, and then identify them by the exact same means as before. This can easily feel like a chore, a "New Game+" mode with either more randomization or a big selection of pre-identified plants would have been very welcome. A replay only takes about 2 hours if you know what to do and skip over the conversations you already know, but that's still 2 hours full of repetition.About the graphics: this is where the game truly shines. There are 77 different plants in the game, and each and every one has been drawn with loving care. They are beautiful, distinct, and a joy to look at. All other graphics, including the NPCs. are rather abstract in comparison - which is not to say that they'd look bad, it's just clear that plants have been given more care. The plants are also beautifully animated as they sway in a gentle breeze, your cat has some nice animations as well, and the NPCs have some facial animations, which is all pretty decent for a two-person development team. The background music helps create a calm, relaxed atmosphere. Sound effects are sparse, but fitting when they appear. There is no voice acting, and I did not really miss it.The game provides very little in terms of usability features. There are two separate volume sliders and an option to switch the flowery in-game font to a plain one that's easier to read. No visual options exist apart from the fullscreen setting. Most of the game takes place on a single screen, and some elements (like the text of the customer monologues) are very tiny. You can, however, zoom everywhere at any time and scroll around while zoomed in, even when drag-and-dropping plants around. This feels a little clunky at times, but once you've gotten used to it, you'll be able to take a closer look at everything that needs one, even if your eyesight is as bad as mine. Unfortunately the game does not provide visual filters for color-blind players, which may make the identification of some plants difficult, but the colors are often mentioned in the descriptions that you get from the microscope.The game is exclusively played with the mouse, keyboard shortcuts do not exist. Manual saves are neither possible nor necessary, as the game autosaves after every action. It also keeps two saves per in-game day, for any number of playthroughs, until you delete them. This is nicely done and makes it easier to explore different paths through the story. I did not run into any bugs or stability issues, which is not a given considering that the game only has two developers and was released just a few days ago - two thumbs up for QA!Despite some questionable gameplay design decisions, I recommend Strange Horticulture for its unique setting, beautiful plants, relaxing atmosphere, meaningful choices, and well-written story parts. The main gameplay loop of identifying plants, serving customers, and solving riddles to find new plants works well at least for the first playthrough. The game is also fairly priced for the experience it provides.

_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: This is the perfect game for a low-key, restorative, and rainy-weekend. It's the kind of game you play while you enjoy a nice hot cup of tea while listening to the subtle spooky background music. So far I've gotten 2 out of the 8 possible endings (1 on PC and one on Nintendo Switch). If you like puzzles, mystery, and witches, Strange Horticulture will definitely scratch that itch.  Because this game has such a reasonable completion time, I'll definitely come back to it again for the other endings.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Strange Horticulture is a charming but very short puzzle game with a unique focus on identifying plants. As is common in mystery games, a relative has died and you have taken over their store. There you identify flora using descriptions you find in a big book o' plants.Unfortunately there is nothing more to offer. Identifying plants is entertaining initially, but quickly overstays its welcome. The same goes for the few other puzzle aspects, such as map exploration. Repetitive, monotonous, and ultimately boring.The game's story is disappointingly simple and lacks the depth a good mystery would need. To make things worse, it feels almost entirely disconnected from the gameplay. Barely any of the riddles/puzzles you're solving have anything to do with it, and many of them feel arbitrary: Decipher a secret message to travel to a location that holds a plant, which you then sell to anyone who asks for it in your store. Why the secrecy? Is it just busywork? I'm fine if the game wants to be just about solving puzzles and riddles, but this game clearly leans into its story. These (and other) kind of scenarios are very immersion breaking on a story that is already pretty poor. Similarly, you are forced to give customers what they ask for, even if you know it's not going to help them (or if it feels morally wrong to give them the plant), because otherwise you cannot proceed with the story. It's all very disconnected.Worst are the puzzles you lack all the pieces for. This happens every now and then, and there is no indication that you're missing pieces. You spend time searching to no avail and just proceed, until suddenly you get that piece you needed. Nothing is worse than trying to solve an incomplete puzzle not knowing it's incomplete. You're looking through the box for that one piece that  be in there, but you won't find it. It'll be mailed to you a few days later.Strange Horticulture feels like an amazing and unique game in the first hour you play it. You can see the potential, and can't wait for things to unfold. It's just that they never do, ultimately making this a disappointing and short game with repetitive and time-wasting mechanics.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I blasted through this game with all endings and achievements in a weekend and it was great fun. It's a short game for sure, but well worth your time. The puzzles have a nice balance: Not too challenging, but still make you feel rather smart when solving them. Much prefer original ideas like this that are focused and well executed to grindy games that drag on forever.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Easily a favorite game. It's short, but the story is strange and enticing. I personally enjoyed every step of the way. My ONLY complaint is that I was there was an "open-ended" ending that allowed you to continue playing as a horticulturalist and continue selling your plants and potions. All-in-all, it was a game I thoroughly enjoyed and it's DEFINITELY worth the money I paid for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I played the demo, and was eagerly awaiting the release of this game. For background, I've got a degree in landscape horticulture and one of my favorite things to do is memorize the latin names of plants and learn how to ID them. So it felt like this game was built for me.I love gathering clues about new plants, trying to match up plant names and vague descriptions in the journal with the look of a plant or how it smells or feels. I'm not typically the type to enjoy puzzle games, but the puzzles were not too difficult for me to figure out. A few times I've had to take a chance on a plant I wasn't sure of, though since there's no way to skip visitors to your shop, I at least knew the plant they were looking for had to be something I had (or had an unsolved clue for).I wish the journal would let me take notes on it directly, for example to mark off the ones I've successfully ID'd and make it easier to find plants in the journal that I haven't ID'd yet. Or to add just a little bit of text for me to jot down what color flowers something has if it doesn't say in the book already.Exploring locations in the map isn't really exploring, it's only there to go to places you already have clues for. Don't bother visiting random locations as I did hoping to stumble onto secrets. The one time that happened for me, it was because I happened upon a spot that a later clue would lead me to. But you won't need whatever you find there until after you get the clue to go there, so there's no point to getting it early. I wish there were hidden things to find on the map that would encourage me to explore places on my own.All in all, it took me less than 10 hours to 100% this game with the three endings there are achievements for (though I suspect there might be other endings from the various combinations of choices to make). Quite an enjoyable time. I would 100% recommend this game to any of my plant-loving colleagues, even if they're not usually the type to play video games.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed this game, the puzzles are moderately challenging, the stories are intriguing to follow and the plants are creative and fun to identify. It's a fairly immersive experience, you truly feel like a strange horticulturalist. That being said, as much as I enjoyed the game, I'd still give it a 4/5, as I found that I had the end-game answer well before I could access it, so I wish there had been a bit more of a challenge there. I also felt that identifying the last few plants after the game's conclusion was very weak. Having one customer rapid-fire ask for 10 plants in a row was pretty lame. I thought it would at least take an extra two or three days with more characters to chat with as a follow up to game's events, but it just seemed they threw in a simple solution for the extra plants they imagined but didn't have a use for.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: If you *really* want to buy this game, buy it at a heavy discount (>50%). It is an interesting concept with very little gameplay or story. You play the first "day" of the game, you've seen all the major gameplay for your remaining time.The "game" amounts to deducing what plant a person wants based on provided information. Only in the last half of the game do you get to do anything useful with said plants, and that is limited to three "concoctions".There is a story here, but it is marred by a sub-standard gameplay and forgetful characters. One person is an investigator, another is a cult member, another is a childhood friend (I think?). There is no development of relationships beyond the cult member interaction half way through the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I liked the artwork and the concept. On my first playthrough I found it very entertaining - I played again to get the final achievements and it was a bit confusing but that was mainly b/c so much time had passed since the first play.I found it interesting and enjoyed trying to  figure out which plants customers wanted.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: It's a quasi-Lovecraftian plant shop simulator, which I had no idea I wanted, but it turns out I do! I haven't played that far yet (I will update later), but I hope the story progresses in interesting ways, and that maybe the plant funconality might become more interactive and important in later stages. Currenlty the focus seems to be on collecting, identifying, and using each plant for a scripted encounter with a shop patron that doesn't mean much. From what I can tell, you're basically guaranteed to have any particular plant when it is asked for, and all you have to do is pick the right one and give to the customer. I would like to see more of a point to having each plant in the future. Still, definitely recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Fun, chill game with a good balance of story and puzzles (in general in the form of finding locations, identifying flowers and their uses). There are multiple endings, that are affected by some choices that you make in the game (sometimes you will have to choose what flower you wish to give to someone, this will impact the ending you get). I was having so much fun I completed it in two days. The game is on the short side, I could  have gone a bit longer, but I think at one point it might have suffered from it if it had been, so I am happy with it. Got it during the winter sale and it was well worth it!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly I liked it, I wish, as always, that there was a "neutral" option for Steam reviews. It was good, it was cute, it was easy for sure, but I paid $10 and it took me 5 hours to finish it and that's just... a pretty awful price per hour considering the gameplay. I love to and do support indie games all the time so only a few hours for $10 or $15 isn't always a dealbreaker for me but I don't think the game is good enough to warrant it. $10 for it was also 50% off, to think that this is normally $20 is borderline offensive tbh.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great if you enjoy solving some simple visual puzzles, discovering and identifying a wide arrray of magical plants, and interactions with characters that have an impact on the ending. _childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Maybe you like plants. Maybe you like puzzles. Maybe you just want a zen organizational front desk job listening to lo-fi. Whatever your drive, this short but sweet game is well priced for what it provides. Not a ton of replay value here, but I thoroughly enjoyed the time I spent. It was quickly addictive yet relaxing. Just the right amount of challenge after a long day at your real job.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I played it for 3 hours, during which I really tried to like it. I wanted to like it. I couldn't. The game relies on 3 things: providing plants to customers, unveling the "story" and exploring the map to find new plants. In my opinion, t fails at all 3. Managing the plants is repetitive and uninteresting and so are the customer requests. There was no other request during the time I played that was any different than reading some basic text referencing to the plant, looking for the plant in the encyclopedia and finding it in your collection. It became boring after the first hour and unbearable by the time I put the game down.The writing is mediocre at best and simply bad at worst. I didn't find the story compelling as well. It was like reading through a random semi-interesting newspaper article. Nothing pulled me in.The map design is also basic and nothing more than passable. You get points from watering flowers and you can spend them to click a point on the map to maybe find a new plant (or something else) based on some tip you got. The atmosphere in the game is pretty cool, I'll give it that. If you want a game you can space out to, it's fine. If you're looking for interesting mechanics, a story worth following or anything that will hook you in and keep you engaged - this ain't it.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I have never played anything like this. Strange Horticulture's soundtrack whisks you into a world of puzzles of varied difficulty, involves you in somewhat twisted plot through meeting random strangers in your plant shop, all the while you are trying to find the most wonderful plants scattered around a medieval map. Oh, and by the way: you are a cat owner now.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great! It's like playing a series of interlocked Escape Room puzzles, with clever twists on its mechanics and a well-paced story. There are also welcome low-fi-beats vibes from listening to the rain while labeling your plants in peace. While the game has multiple endings, you probably won't see them because solving the puzzles once is enough; it still offers an engaging ten or so hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I was attracted to play this game not by its name, but the innovative gameplay and the different choices possible during the play.The story is so exciting that I have played the game at least three times through to figure out and receive all Steam Achievements. I am not an "Achievement Hunter", but in some cases of really good games, I try to get them all. This game is one of them!If you like "Papers, please!" this game might be also for you! Give it a try!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: It is a careful not-recommendation. I'd suggest to buy it on deep sale. My playtime was about 7 hours (I forgot to close the game once).While this isn't a bad game, I think the game squandered the potential it has.The identification puzzles do grow complex but mostly by withholding the information such as smell and touch. There are some outside of the box puzzles but only a few.There are some sequel hooks but thankfully not in the main story. It is never explained why we get those dreams or those cards, so some world/story elements look arbitrary and random. Later two tools (the looking lenses and potions) are severely underused and more like tokens. Music is one-two tracks. Character portraits are uninspired. Too much time goes just to sort plant on shelves. Days are very patterned - you get 4-6 clients and can explore somewhat - and it is only about 16 days total. When somebody knows what they are doing the game can probably be played in hour. There are artificial blocks in exploration with mobile-like energy meter which is just slow enough to be annoying, and game puts 'invisible walls' so one cannot sequence break, so the exploration is mostly pointless unless one gets randomly lucky to click a square where there is no 'invisible story walls' but some sidecontent. Not a bad game, but certainly very flat one.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this gentle puzzle game. Solve clues to find what map coordinates to click on to find new kinds of plants and mushrooms, receive requests from townspeople for specific varieties or effects, and then use your horticulture guide (which is very light on details) to identify your findings and give them exactly what they want. Meanwhile a dangerous creature is threatening a local coven, and through a few choices you can decide which side you'd like to support. None of the puzzles are very difficult (I got stuck twice and should have paid more attention to the items I had gathered), but the game is paced well and has enough details to keep things interesting. If you like the idea of studying a notebook to find the flower that aids memory or the leaf that can be used as an antidote to certain poisons, this might be your kind of game.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: This game really puts the cult in horticulture.I loved this game.I found myself fully immersed in this world, it's characters, their beliefs and of course the plants.I managed to get all endings and achievements in under 17 hours, but I also played around a lot with how I organised the plants and tags - I didn't realise until my 3rd play-through that there is an option to auto-label plants that you have correctly identified. I did struggle with reading the revealed secret writing, but maybe that's just because of my screen.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game. The story is interesting and the gameplay is quite straightforward. Some of the puzzles are quite tricky but not enough to make you give up.I do have a few tips for playing the game to make life easier - minor spoilers follow!!1. The main tip I have is about labelling plants. There are labels in your inventory so you can label plants as they are identified, or note what you think they are (I used a different colour label for the ones that were not yet confirmed). There are 77 plants in the game as well as 6 elixirs... I was using a controller rather than a physical keyboard so it was very frustrating naming them all. BUT there is an option to enable auto-labelling in the game options. I really recommend enabling this option! Note that plants are auto-labelled once they have been used and therefore identified. Elixirs are also auto-labelled once they are used and not after brewing as you might expect.2. Endings. There are 8 different endings depending on decisions you make through the game, or rather 4 x 2. There are 4 paths; each path has an A or B outcome depending on the decision you make on day . It's worthwhile noting the decisions or checking one of the guides that are in the Community Hub if you decide to go for all 8 endings: IIRC there is one decision which doesn't impact the ending but does lead to an achievement and another decision which doesn't have any impact on endings or achievement but leads to 2 different dialogues.3. Every day there are multiple tasks which involve travelling to a location on a map. You are given clues to these locations and I recommend noting them down if you are planning on multiple runthroughs. The clues aren't that difficult, although a couple of them are a bit fiddly to figure out the exact square. But it will save you time if you don't need to figure them out on each runthrough.4. If you decide to go for all endings, you can reload days from the main menu (choose Load Game and then select the day). Again, I recommend checking the guides for which decisions impact the endings so you can plan which day to reload and play from, to find the most efficient way to all endings.(One last hint - )
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fabulous mystery game of puzzles and detective work that unfolds over 5-6 hours of game play.  It plays like an interactive board game, feeling a little like "Sherlock Holmes: Consulting Detective" but as an interesting horticulturalist.  Customers come in, describe an issue, and you use your book to figure it out.  This is for anyone that likes detective work, mysteries, reading, and board games.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was an in-between option.The core gameplay is simply too easy, elements are introduced only to be never used again. The few times I made a mistake are because plants had similar properties and only one was correct, a new type of cipher/puzzle came up and wasn't telegraphed (also, was never used again), and I never noticed the buttons inlaid on the table until the hint button told me about them. The map is way bigger than it needs to be, you'll only ever need to explore a few squares. You learn facts and properties about plants only to never use them again.You only ever make three elixirs, but that was the only part of the game that provided any challenge. This should've been the core gameplay.The story is pretty cookie-cutter and provides no real surprises.That being said, the production of the game is fantastic. The artwork, music, and sounds are all great.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I have poured a lot of time into this game and have still only found two of the many endings. This is a worthy investment if you enjoy games that don't provide instructions and leave you to discover the game at your own pace. I would definitely recommend keeping detailed notes on where and how you acquire each plant as well as what components go into each elixir. It'll make any additional playthroughs much easier and you won't need to reinvent the wheel.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: A very peaceful and beautiful game.  I binged the entire thing in one night, very gripping in a way. _childDocuments_.review: Man, I had such a good time for 4 hours.Toward the end, I found myself doing more "looking" than researching. I felt like I was spending 80% of my time looking for where my red flowers were in my collection, and then 20% of my time actually comparing them to find which one was right. When a customer comes in requesting a plant, and you have that plant, and you have it labeled properly, and it's in the book, and you've gotten the fanfare of the game telling you yes yes that is that plant... Why am I manually mousing over every single plant I've ever found to find the label to show me the right one? Why does the book not have a picture of the entire plant once I've discovered it? Why is there not a "quick find" or "snap to" in the book? I found it in the book, why to I also, separately, have to find it on the shelf, when I already know what it is?This wasn't a problem in the beginning of the game. It was so fun to learn and recognize the plants.But after several hours, when you're being rewarded for going somewhere with multiple plants, and the game doesn't auto-label the plant you just got correct, it becomes way too cumbersome. I ended up just finding a guide that had all the plants labeled (like the book should have done) so I could control+f the name of the plant I needed. I hate feeling like the only way for me to beat a game with the tags "relaxing, mystery, puzzle, nature" is making my own pivot table in excel about it.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I have to say I fall into a sort of strange niche when it comes to gaming. I really enjoy a relaxing game that is enjoyable even when you fail. This game completely hits that mark for me. While being able to collect plants and solve puzzles, which every time feels rewarding, I also found the story line and choices easy to follow. I have to admit, I was worried the first time I failed and was sent to the mini game to come back, but even then I have to applaud the relaxed nature the designers took to this game. For the first time it was an enjoyable mini game to play when almost all other games are either stressful ones or just a flat restart. The only possible thing I could say negatively about this game was the repetitive music however once I turned that off and turned on some chill lo fi music, this was a perfect 10/10 vibe and experience for this game.I totally recommend this game for a relaxing, refreshingly non-stressful game to play.

_childDocuments_.review: I really loved this game, but it comes with caveats. A large part, even most maybe, of the time it's great fun. You're identifying plants with decent information, picking the right one, or trying to work through relatively good clues. Now, sometimes this is not the case. For instance you have daily clue cards that must be identified to progress and while most are pretty good, some of them involve the kinds of leaps of logic that reminds me of 90s point & click adventure games. I enjoyed the story in these, but sucked at the puzzles. It's the same kind of feeling "how on earth did you expect me to know to do this". Other times you simply are not given enough information in the book you have to make inferences for the plants (it's also possible to not have a plant even though you have the description and bang your head against the wall" for instance one plant I was told "when it's ready to harvest it will be blue green" no it was not, not even close, it was orange, other times you are only given one characteristic but that's a characteristic several plants have, this is not a problem if you've already identified the plant through a quest, but you haven't always (this happened to me at the very end, two unidentified plants shared the same characteristic from the book). You also don't have enough space for the plants to work out any good system, there isn't enough to sort them in any way, they are automatically sorted wherever but you can't make a better one. If it at least autosorted the labeled ones it would be something. You have labels for the plants, but you can only have one label/plant so if there's some additional information you want to add, such as an effect that is required several times, or info about a plant needed to complete the game - you better remember that or you have to make the label bloated. Not sure what the point of the different labels is. The game has a hint system, with several levels, and a lot of the time it's helpful (good job there) but not always. I do recommend becoming comfortable with googling some things. All that said if you are ok with these things that do cause some frustration, I highly recommend the game. I had great fun.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game a lot. There are 8 (at least?) endings to get with various choices you make during the game, to either help or hinder the people visiting your flowershop. In between visits you can water your plants, rearrange them, identify them, solve clues and puzzles, explore a map and find even more plants. There's also a cat you can pet and various tools to use to help identify your flowers like a book, a map, a magnifying glass and a desk with drawers. The game is slightly dark, both in colors and in themes. There's been a murder on a ritual site and something is haunting the woods. Madness or salvation is waiting around the corner. Death is a choice.Edit: Still good.

_childDocuments_.review: The story of this game is very interesting and dark, yet the game still feels somewhat relaxing to play. Your decisions shape the overarching ending and the fates of each individual character, giving it great replay value. As you play through the game, you collect different plants and journal entries and need to figure out which plant matches to what journal entry to progress the story and serve your customers. The in-game mechanism for labeling plants is so nice and you can organize your collection however you like. There are clues that you receive each day that are not too difficult to puzzle out but are still satisfying upon completion. It is a relatively short game but I still wholeheartedly recommend it to any player that enjoys story-rich games where choices matter, as well as those who like organization and simple puzzles.also you can pet the cat :)

_childDocuments_.review: Strange Horticulture is an interesting low-key puzzle game with some story choices. The puzzles are pretty simple but require some research. Typically, a customer will come in requesting a plant, either by name or description. Then you look it up and figure out which of your plants fits the bill. (You can also  preemptively identify and label your plants). As the game progresses these challenges get somewhat more difficult due to vagaries of description or missing information, but never really "hard". There's also a hint button if you need it.At the beginning of each in-game day you will get a clue which leads you to a location on the map, and new plants to add to your collection. Studying the map was a fun way to mix it up. Occasionally when someone asks you for a plant, you can choose between two options with lasting impact on the story, leading to different endings or character deaths. This feature is well implemented and really helps sell the theme. The game doesn't have tons of replayability, but when you've finished the game you might want to reload from an earlier day and make different choices to see what happens, or unlock achievements.

_childDocuments_.review: +  premise.+ Cozy atmosphere.+ Gameplay loop is fairly satisfying.+ Fantastical plants are interesting and creative.+ Cat is pettable.+ Relaxed pacing.- Slightly underbaked. Characters and gameplay concepts like being able to make elixirs aren't thoroughly explored.- Not very many points for interaction.- Unengaging plot.- The option to be "evil" has no real in-game justification.- No way to bookmark pages in your plant guide, or mark which ones you've identified already* The clues you get to find points on the map are mostly cool and creative.* Moment to moment writing is solid.If you have ever wanted to be a witch in a potion shop, this is your game. Strange Horticulture comes the closest of any game I've seen to delivering on that (admittedly underexplored) concept. It's satisfying to work out your own colour-coded organizational system for all your strange wares, or match a new description of a plant you've found to one that's been lurking on your shelf. The hints you're given as to which plant might be what are perfectly balanced, so that while there are some that you see and instantly recognize from your readings, you'll still occasionally misidentify one. This makes makes it extra gratifying when you do have a guess confirmed.The written descriptions of the plants are memorable, and the descriptions of the places you explore are pleasantly atmospheric. The overarching plot is, sadly, not quite as good. It's a very generic sort of occult murder mystery where none of the main players have any real relation to you, aside from showing up at your shop to ask for things sometimes. The mystery simply goes from "there is a dangerous thing lurking" to "we've figured out where it came from," and "here's how to beat it." And then you do, and you go back to your shop, and that's that, I suppose.Or, well, technically there are multiple endings where you can take other paths, but unless you enjoy sowing chaos for the sake of it there isn't really much of a compelling reason to. There is, for instance, no indication of why your little herbologist lady would feel tempted to join the shallowly-developed cult that shows up, or aid them in murdering people, other than "yay, violence" or "these strange and obviously insane men seem cool to me."The choice branches are few and far between, and it can sometimes be unclear how what you do will affect the plot, which meant there were a few times I exited to check a walkthrough just to make sure I wasn't accidentally dooming anyone (and surprise, in one instance I would have). You change the storyline by choosing between plants to give someone, although usually there's only one option available. There was only one major instance where I wished I could give someone something different or refuse, notably, which was when Overall, though, I'd solidly recommend this if the concept is at all appealing to you. There's a simple delight in maintaining a magical garden shop and becoming an expert in fantastical flora, the writing's more than serviceable enough to pad out the moments between finding more cool plants, and the puzzles are clever without being frustrating.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun, one of the coolest and most interesting games I've ever played. It has that old hidden object game vibe to it but is definitely more fun and interesting. Riddles are hard enough to be interesting but not so difficult as to be unsolvable. There seem to be several endings with different variations of each, so it looks like there is some replayability. Full playthroughs are just long enough to feel complete without being so long that you don't want to do it again. The game has a unique charm and I am definitely glad I bought it.The only potential complaint I have would be that once you learn what the plants are, you know them for every subsequent game. However, I don't think it would be worth it to sacrifice the obviously carefully crafted book and art just to make procedurally generated plants.

Hellbore's surprised face when the bell is rung made me laugh several times. It was so genuinely catlike in mannerisms.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Help the most dead-eyed paper-people buy weird plants. Story is something about a cult resurrecting a plant demon. Its whatever, the real work here is in identifying the plants and solving some basic puzzles that only really trip you up because they're a grab-bag of various kinds of puzzles and not specific mechanics that are introduced and built upon. I thought there'd be more alchemy or medicine making here, but there's only 4 potions in the game. Really feels like someone had an idea for a game, started with the plant identification gimmick, had an idea to expand into more gameplay, but eventually ran out of time or budget and just started adding random riddles and puzzles to try and mix things up. Anyway, I played it as a more of a stress-relief and, in that sense, its not bad. Flipping through books and identifying plants was nice.As a game though, its pretty mediocre, and by the end of it the idea of identifying plants no one asked for seemed tedious and boring.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Fun, relaxing puzzler. I only had two instances where I just could not parse the clue and had to find a guide. The game is 99% great at giving you the right nudge but a couple times I just couldn't get on its wavelength. That's okay, still a really delightful time and something that feels unique and special. It's like if Cultist Simulator wanted to be chill instead of a plate-spinning exercise.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: It's a nice relaxing game about strange plants and got me to look up some plants that exist. For example: Dendrocnide moroides. The very fine, brittle hairs on the leafs are loaded with toxins and cover the entire plant; even the slightest touch will embed them in the skin for up to a year in  intents amount of pain.I enjoyed learning real plants that sound crazy to be possibly found in nature.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not into plants at all, but this game was more fun than I thought it was going to be. It has a pleasant loop of identifying plants based on their description then using clues to find new plants on your map. I often found myself losing track of time while playing. Also, the clever way it uses the map and those clues is quite interesting. The story is pretty decent as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I really loved the idea, but the story is so short and boring and you don't even use 1/3rd of the plants you find. For the price, 5 hours of gameplay with no replayability (the option is sort of there, but there is no point), I do not recommend this game to anyone. For the price there are so many other games out there to get. Very disappointed...
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I thoroughly liked this unique game! I finished it in two sittings. Unfortunately I encountered a repeating bug that happened at least 10 times, that the customers coming wouldn't leave after taking what they asked making the game stuck and not being able to even exit to menu/desktop. Killing the game I had to reply the part of the day that I was in (through load) and continue game would start a new game since the game was corrupt each time I killed it in that state.. hopefully this can be fixed.. apart from that I enjoyed the soothing experience of the rain falling and the purring cat. Definitely recommended
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Something about this game stretches something deep in me that I love, only complaint is I wish there was some type of 'arcade mode'. I understand its more of a story focused game which is probably why, but I want to keep playing the game without already knowing everything. Maybe if I could play a mode where I was actually running the shop and trying to identify plants brought in by customers and selling requested tonics/tinctures and plants. Petting the cat and the rain/nature sounds are the toppings to the cake, well done devs.Weirdly found a deep part in my heart despite low replay-ability, 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game. I loved the gameplay and the ambiance.The puzzles are simple for the most part, but often hit the sweet-spot where you still feel good for solving them.The one feature I would LOVE to have in this game is some kind of notebook or journal where you can take your own notes.It has an interesting feature: plants are not automatically labeled when you identify them. Instead, you can label them whenever you want, whatever you want. This is great for immersion, and honestly is just really satisfying to say "yes! I know what this is!" and go for the labels so you can write it down.Just...a great game. Feels good to play. Feels good to finish it. It'll probably feel good to replay, but I can't report on that yet.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game.  In real life gardening isn't my hobby, but no prior knowledge is needed (or in fact, even useful).  It's similar to "Papers Please" in format without any of the pressure.  There are no time constraints on serving customers and no real penalty for failed explorations - just wait a little while and try again.  The puzzles are intuitive and it moves along at your pace.  The only thing I can't figure out is how some people play the game through without earning the Cat Lover achievement.  Monsters!  Pet the kitty!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: The game is very athmospheric for sure, but the gameplay itself is lackluster. Due to the slow pace of the game and the very indirect way of interaction with the story, the story never really catches on. The game is linear up to the point where you basically have no freedom at all, and just have to do certain things, because the game gives you no other option.In the end, sifting through your plants and your plant book just becomes tedious. I looked up the final solution because I simply did not want to swift through 50 pages of plant descriptions to decipher the final plants. All in all - I'm happy that I'm finished and can now delete it from my hard drive. Good riddance.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Good game. It reminded me of "Papers, Please" in the game format, in that you have a series of customers you have to complete increasingly hard puzzles for. It's a well put-together game, the puzzles are tricky but solvable with a bit of thought, and it rewards organisation and careful scrutinising of the game environment. It's not a long game, about ten hours, but there's a Hint button to help if you get stuck (so you don't generally need to go looking for help on the internet) which helps encourage you to complete it, and there are enough variations in the plot to want to play it through a second time to see how things turn out if you make different choices. The game even auto-saves each day for you, so you don't necessarily have to go back to the beginning if you want to try doing something differently.Recommended if you fancy spending a few evenings solving puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely adored this game! The mystery wasn't super mysterious, and I found it fairly easy to pull the pieces together to figure out what was going on, but it was still intriguing and enjoyable. The puzzles were fun and it appealed to the part of me that always has a full pack in games from all the things I collect. I'll probably play through a few more times just to see the different endings. All in all, great game!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: i loved the game, i originally thought i wouldn't like it but once i started playing i couldn't stop, personally i wish the game ran longer. even though i wasn't paying much attention to the story line i could still figure out what was going on. i loved all the puzzle too, as someone who loves puzzles and often finds them really easy some of the puzzles where quite tricky and i enjoyed having to genuinely think about how to solve it. when i first looked at the game i read the reviews first as you do to see if the game was any good,, and i saw some people mentioning that they wish there was more room to store the plants. at fist i didn't understand what they meant but as the game progressed i started to understand,, however by the end of the game when i was sorting out all my plants for the last time of my first play through i ended up with 2 full shelf's empty! i think this game is a great game if you want to relax and wind down while also working your brain in a relaxing environment. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game based on the other reviews, however, sadly, it fell flat for me. Will list what I disliked about the game.My biggest gripe is the identifying plant system. You have a book with the list of plants, but when trying to identify them, it was really hard for me to compare the poor drawing to the actual plant and then having to examine the plant to try to match it to the description did not work for me 50% of the time and ended up looking them up since I didn't want to constantly fill up that dread meter for being wrong. There was also two instances where they used the scientific name and not the actual name- why? what was the point of that?Additionally the elixirs portion was very small, and very frustrating- match the drawing of the photo to make your potion- I had an equally hard time matching it up, its probably a me issue but its worth mentioning that these two issues combined really ruined the game play aspect for me since it was too hard. I enjoyed the storyline, but wasn't worth the headache I got. At least the achievements were easy, as long as you set it all up right during your playthroughs.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Finished this game in ~6 hours. Puzzle game that was suitably challenging and didn't get boring as new elements kept getting added. There were some puzzles that I managed to solve before the later hints came. Didn't realise that there were certain points where your decision would affect the ending, . so be careful to read the descriptions of the plants lmao. I loved identifying the plants and the tagging system, though I wish I had a better way to arrange all of them.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game. Great atmosphere paired with a multifaceted narrative and fun manageable puzzles. Extra points for the hint system to scoot you in the right direction if you're struggling with certain aspects. It's cozy, a little spooky, with a lot of  art. I don't replay very many games, but the  kept me coming back for more. And there wasn't a bug or glitch in sight. Huge kudos to the game devs. A seamless, wonderful experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Score: 8Great game.  Once you get the flow of what you are doing it was super relaxing.  The story took a while to understand what was going on with how you fit into everything.  The puzzles were just the right amount of challenging to make you feel like you had to think and sometimes come back to but not frustrating.  The game didn't outstay its welcome with its length either.  This game has nothing to do with farming and it would be cool if the sequel had some plant management instead of just identification based on some clues.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: found this game through a friend, and man i was not disappointed. let my gay little heart live out its best life being able to do plant identification, and the puzzles were really fun and engaging. music is really calming, and atmosphere is so soothing. the story had was very interesting, and some of the twists actually made me gasp out loud. Highly recommend
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderfully relaxing game. The puzzles aren't very complicated and failure is just a delay and possibly another simple puzzle to solve. The music is well done as is the sound design. The interface is a little fidgety sometimes, but mostly because you might be trying to look at several things at once to solve a puzzle. The world itself is intriguing and the story not overly complicated. Don't forget to pet the cat!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game, there is a wonderful atmosphere and style to this game. I loved the characters and the puzzles. Figuring out which plant is which was so much fun and I love finding/exploring areas on the map. I will say that there were some parts I had to look up in order to figure it out maybe that is my fault more than the games, so take that with a grain of salt. I also loved all of the many endings. _childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Cozy narrative-based puzzle game about plants. Really excellent and engaging worldbuilding. Both the characters and world feel exciting to interact with, but the real star is all the beautiful mushrooms, plants, and flowers you collect. It's a short game, very calm with interesting mechanics. Despite its simplicity, the game feels tactile, intriguing, and has some genuinely challenging mystery elements.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game so much, and I hope my review gets others to play it too!The game's mechanics are very straightforward. Each day you fulfil customer orders by identifying plants in your collection with the help of your Book of Plants. These customers also move the plot forward, and depending on how you respond you will have different storylines/endings (only 2 as far as I'm aware).You're also given other puzzles in the form of cards and letters in order to discover new plants to add to your collection and progress the story.I didn't realise how short it was; initially I thought it would be a kind of quasi-endless game where you continuously serve customers and grow your shop. However it's actually super linear, with up to 18 in-game days, and once you finish the story it's over.I also recommend enabling the setting to auto-label plants you identify - it started getting annoying manually labelling every plant I identified.You should definitely play this game if you want a no-stress game where you chill with cool plants in a cozy little shop and every now and then get threatened by the occult.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Very lovely, gripping game with intriguing plot. Simple mechanics, but far from repetitive or boring. Beautifully made, clever, requires attention to details. Different puzzles that make you think for some time, but nothing that is impossible to solve. Highly recommend.  Although, if you are not an English native speaker, it may be hard to solve some of the riddles due to specific language-related facts.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: A beautifully charming puzzle game, very relaxing and engaging. I like the simple beginnings that slowly lead into the overarching plot, but perhaps would have liked the beginning to last a little longer, and we could get more uses out of the plants that I hadn't touched by the end. The art is pretty, and spoiler: It's clear that a LOT of care went into both the designs and descriptions of each plant, especially considering that each plant must fit only one book entry and vice versa.I very much like that the cat can be patted. Love you, Hellebore.Tip: Keep your plants in alphabetical order starting early on, so you don't lose your place back and forth across the shelves like I did on my first playthrough.The Elderphinium ending was satisfying, but so was the Gilded Dendra ending, hehe.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: i'm not sure how to describe the game.Every day people come to your shop and ask you for a plant.You open a book, read the description, recognize the item and give it to the customer. It is so simple I didn't immediately realize it was the actual game and I kept trying to find what I was really supposed to do.You also get "puzzles" that represent absolutely no challenge whatsoever and that reward you with new plants.There is some kind of story and you can make choices about some actions that doesn't appear to matter much.All this isn't too interesting but if you want to spend time with your brain off, it's a way to do it.The one thing that I absolutely can't stand is the interface though.You accumulate the plants on shelves and the upper part of the screen scrolls left and right.But that scrolling happens automatically when your mouse gets close to the sides and often activates when you absolutely don't want it to.  It can become quite frustrating when you have accumulated a lot of things. It would be fine on a phone or a tablet I guess.Given the little interest I already had for the game, it was enough to make me stop playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Not my favourite game, I loved the concept but it was not for me. I did complete is, which really isn't saying much since it is a super quick game. I enjoy difficult puzzles and games, but this game was a bit chaotic in which, if you miss any step at all, there are not prompts telling you other wise and you can go all the way until the 16th day without realising that you missed something from day 2. One thing that is positive about this game is your brief interactions with the cat LOL
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game! It was fun to figure out what you needed for the clues without a lot of explanation and it was really satisfying when you finally got it! I will say that I didn't realize that when given an option of what plant to give somebody that it would alter the ending, which was really cool! This game doesn't hold your hand, but it wont leave you out to dry either. It has simple mechanics and it is easy to pick up and come back to. Would recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Puzzles with plants and a sprinkling of eldritch horror.  Highly recommend this game if you enjoy a puzzle game that doesn't wrack your brain.  The art is simple but charming, the atmosphere is unsettling and flows well with the narrative.  There are more decisions to be made than I initially realized, and there are quite a few potential outcomes to the story.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: The fact that the game manages to be as suspenseful as it is given that basically the only thing that moves is the shop cat (pet the cat, by the by, the purring noise is one of the most satisfying noises I've ever heard in a game) is truly impressive. The actual gameplay of identifying and correctly using plants is good fun, but it's the fact that the creators have managed to weave a mystery and story so well into simply having people come into a flower store that really elevates this little game. Short and sweet and well worth the time.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Really well put together game. Took me about 4 hours to solve, but it does have some replay value with multiple endings. Definitely draws you in. Music is good but a little repetitive, but the other sound design is absolutely fantastic and is extremely immersive. Best cat purr I've heard in a game, I repeatedly pet the cat just to get the dopamine hit.Good game.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: a very fun game. a good puzzle game that helps you not feel stressed because it doesn't ever have a time constraint. a lot like papers please in the best of ways. good out of the box thinking helps with the puzzles to not feel stale. i am very much looking forward to more games like this from this developer. good job overall
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I got instantly hooked on this game and I finished it in a few days. I loved the storyline and the mystery throughout. A relaxing yet stimulating game great for anyone who likes to put ideas together and use logic. Also, the graphics were beautiful. I was sad when the game ended because I would've loved another plotline!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: This is great puzzle game! I know it's great because I HATE puzzle games; but I liked this one! I even completed it! _childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: very interesting, but short: took me 7h to finish. Add probably another 5-7h if I were to finish the other two hidden achievements which require re-doing the game twice over. there are other endings available depending on a few game choices, I think 6 or 8 endings? I didn't bother getting them all. _childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the game and will replay, since there are multiple endings. I especially liked the puzzles, since some were really "out of the box" type of thinking. Not too straightfoward, but completely solvable if you just think a little. Lovely art style. I think fellow biologists will also appreciate the made up latin names, that (mostly) actually make sense ;) The space for plants does feel a little cramped, but this is just a personal prefference.Overall a great game with great ambience.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: As the proprietor of a botany shop, you and your sleepy cat Hellebore get to meet some very interesting locals. The story is intriguing and the puzzles are very satisfying. The magical herbs and plants are fun to identify and I  that there is an interactive map to explore.  This unique gem is one of my favourites this year!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I saw this game pop up in the store and decided to look into it. It seemed to have a really cool vibe to it and that is what initially drew me to getting it. The quests are pretty cool and the way they are designed it also really cool. I liked the puzzle aspect to it and I also liked the decisions you make can change up the ending.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Everything else aside, the illustration and art design of this game are simply sublime. The plants, characters, map, tools, and fonts...everything looks so perfectly drawn and amazing to look at. Bringing sound into the picture makes for a dark and sinister mood, albeit with just enough glimpses of dusty light. In the true spirit of dark academia, it fully captures the delicate balance between being lost in an obsession and keeping your humanity, highlighting the totality of the human experience with multiple endings. I really found this beautiful.Unlike many live action fictions of a similar genre, it rarely feels cheesy or over the top with its tropes. Maybe this wasn't so hard to achieve, given the super limited gameplay and interaction, which puts the spotlight on the powerful art even more so. It's hard to emphasize how much love and attention were given to plants in this game, both visually and descriptively.Somewhat surprisingly, identifying them and searching for secrets can get tiring, even for such a short game. You can and will get stuck or confused in clues and pages, especially with UI being kinda clunky. Many puzzles are not that easy and require some creative thinking and a lot of patience. Moreover, serving your customers when you want to unravel the larger plot can get boring at times, but you got to suck it up and do your job. It does make for quite rewarding short story in the end, but getting there might drag at times, relatively speaking, just like irl job.
