Don't get me wrong, the game is a lot more fun than not, with super engaging folk horror thriller waiting to be uncovered, but having more stuff to do would've been very welcome.I'd suggest playing this game late at night when you can escape from the pressing matters of everyday life and submerge yourself in this little world of mystery. At some point, you might find yourself resting your eyes on the plants in your home, appreciating how simple and familiar these creatures are, but at the same time wondrously strange.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I tried to like this. I was super keen going into it with so many positive reviews, but I really don't get it at all. You have a bunch of plants in front of you and a book with lots of vague descriptions. Someone asks for a plant and you have to match the plant with the description and then give it to them. That's it. I just expected so much more. Maybe there is once you get further in, but after almost 2 hours I was absolutely bored stiff. The music too is this slow dreary background music that was lulling me to sleep, and if you fail 3 times you then have to complete one of two frustrating puzzle minigames. I genuinely don't understand what's fun about this.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Such an original game. This is one of those where I knew partway in I was going to hate for it to end; I only wish I could play it for the first time again. The gameplay nails the feeling of running your own little plant shop, almost like an apothecary, and the narrative unfolds so organically. The puzzles hit the sweet spot for me of neither being too difficult but still making me feel cool for solving them. Also gorgeous visuals and a rainy-day, slightly spooky but not scary feel while playing. Try to avoid looking up anything before or during, if you can help it.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going back and forth on whether to recommend this, but in the end I'm going to say no mainly because of how short it was. I played through the whole game with no help, no looking things up, no hints, in a little more than 4 hours. I'm going to play through it a couple more times since I think I can probably do it in an hour or so to get the other ending achievements (another negative: there are 3 endings that give achievements, and there's no way to save and reload or anything to get them; you have to start over and replay this extremely linear game where you've already solved all the puzzles 3 times if you want them all, with all the plants you've identified reset. Really dumb), but I'm guessing I'll have 100%ed it in under 7 hours. And the gameplay in this is definitely not worth more than $2/hour to me. EDIT: Quick addition now that I'm done to note that it actually ended up taking me about an hour to play through it again for a second ending, and I was able to reload a save once I saw how to get the third ending achievement (but I think the two more complicated ones are locked off so that you'd have to play at least twice, but I'm not sure). So my total time to 100% it over two playthroughs was just under 6 hours. Not worth $10.50 for me for that. END EDITThe game itself is fine. That's it, fine. It's a bit dry and repetitive, but it also has a ton of atmosphere and it's satisfying watching your shelves fill up with named plants, so they even each other out a bit. The puzzles were pretty simple. It's mostly, "I need this plant that does this certain thing; do you have it?", then you looking in your book of plants until you see the plant that does that thing and then giving it to them. Except most of the time the actual plant you need to give to them is already told to you, so it's looking up that entry in the book and then figuring out which plant that is, which is very simple ("the plant has big waxy leafs," so you look at your plants, examine the couple with big leafs and give the person the one with the description that says "the leafs are waxy"). The other puzzles involve finding places on a map to "travel" to (in the form of a text description), which is a lot of scanning the map's tiny text for one name in the midst of many and then solving a simple puzzle.Anyway, I would have liked this game a lot more if there was more to it, like it being more involved to find out what plants a person is requesting or if you had more to do in your shop other than "ring bell, talk to customer, give customer plant, repeat about 50 times." Or if it had been cheaper; $5 or $7.50 maybe would have felt better than even the $10.50 I paid on sale. Again, the creepy, cozy, mysterious atmosphere is great, but there's just not that much else there. I would love that atmosphere in a game where you did a bit more, whether that was more management of the shop or actually going out and exploring places to find plants. In the end, I think this will be something I'll forget about a week after I finish it and never play again rather than something I'd remember fondly and then revisit every once in a while.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I'm obsessed. This game is fantastic. From the story to the puzzles and riddles this game checks all of my favorite boxes for what I like about games. Also, even going quickly this game is about 8 hours of game play. Not sure what everyone is saying about only 4 hours, might be for the demo. And depending on how you play, the number of days the game goes for can change and yes, there are multiple endings. Enjoy!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I knew within thirty seconds of looking at Strange Horticulture that I would love it and I was right. Bought it immediately and finished it in one go, about 5 hours. If you like games where you do a lot of reading, organizing, and figuring out little mysteries that aren't too difficult but ALSO don't hold your hand and make you feel like an idiot, then you will love this game.Atmosphere is lovely--grim in an aesthetic sort of way with melancholy music and a lot of beautiful plant art (and a kitty!). Gameplay consists of:- Matching plants up to encyclopedia entries in order to earn more plants and more encyclopedia entries- Organizing those plants physically and with labels so you can find them again- Using letters and other mysterious clues to locate places of interest to visit on the map, which earns you plants, entries, and plot progression. You get to drag items around physically to look at and interact with, which is always fun- Occasionally making binary choices to affect the plot and characters- Other miscellaneous puzzles I won't spoilIf those sound good to you on paper, play this game! They're all very well implemented.Accessibility/Quality of life features include- The option to replace the text with a more readable font- The option to enable automatic labeling when you give the correct plant to a customer- When you've used all the information a letter has to give you, it gets a checkmark, and you can stick it in the archive where it won't clutter up your desk- You can zoom in anywhere on your deskOne nitpicky QoL thing I wish would happen would be for the map to automatically get put away once you're done traveling if it was in the drawer when you hit the explore button, but for the most part I didn't have any complaints.The story didn't defy any of my expectations from the genre, but I wouldn't call that a negative. It's an occult mystery made cozy by trope familiarity and the safety of your greenhouse, dark enough to keep your attention but kept at enough of a remove (no real-time gameplay, all other people remain firmly on the other side of your counter, most events happen offscreen and are recounted to the horticulturalist after the fact) that it's more soothing than anything. There are a few different endings so I'll be replaying it at least one more time, and I highly recommend this game to anyone who is intrigued by the premise.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: If you like short games with little riddles it is for you but for sure get it when it is on sale. It is not what I thought it would be. Fun and cute but very short. Did not realize it would be so linear and was hoping it would be more in depth like Potion Craft. There is not much replay value as there are only 2 story line options. Puzzles were more like riddles and some of them were tedious but very easy to solve. If I had to give a rating I would give it a 2.5/5.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: It's pretty short, but it's a fun game. Don't expect a shop management simulation though; this is a puzzle and mistery game and "running" the horticulture doesn't involve making in-game money or anything like it. The player character is supposed to be almost like a secondary character (though your actions have influence enough to change the outcome of the plot, of course). I enjoyed cataloguing the plants and figuring out how to progress the story through the puzzles.The visuals are fine but could be a lot better, I think, especially when it comes to characters illustrations. One thing I really liked was the map layout.The bit about making elixirs seemed a little out of place, as if the developers had something bigger planned but in the end didn't move forward with it. It leaves you wanting for more interaction with the whole lab setup.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't a terrible game by any stretch, but I can't recommend it.In a sense, Strange Horticulture is somewhat similar to a game like Return of the Obra Dinn. The main gameplay loop is (initially, at least) identifying different types of plants using intentionally-vague descriptors (similar to RotOD's gameplay loop of identifying characters by dialogue and actions while their appearances were intentionally obfuscated). I didn't mind this, and felt that I was always given enough information to conclusively identify each plant. This wasn't revolutionary gameplay or a revolutionary idea, but it worked. I liked the pseudo-horror elements gradually working their way into conversations with the people visiting the store. The map of the area and the atmosphere of the rain falling against the shop's window were charming and relaxing and the experience was thoroughly enjoyable.Where it all became completely unenjoyable was when the game started to lean farther and farther into incredibly contrived "puzzles" that have all been done better in other games. At the start of every day, you're effectively just handed a very simple logic puzzle to do with a very flimsy narrative justification. Suddenly you're poring over a map that loses its charm as you're staring at it for minutes at a time trying to find where on the map a specific arrangement of landmarks is so you can click on the correct box and progress the plot. It's usually not even a big deal if you click on the wrong map square; your punishment for guessing wrong is having to click a watering can and water your plants for two minutes until you build up enough exploration meter to revisit the map and click on another square.The only time I felt challenged at this point was when the game required me to remember a conversation I had with a minor character hours prior to determine which map square I was supposed to click on. Some of the characters in-game have a dialogue log, but from what I could tell this specific character did not. Introducing a dialogue log for the player to interact with only to not add certain interactions to the log seems like an incredibly cheap way to lengthen a playthrough.A lot of reviews posted so far seem to be from people who haven't made it terribly far in the game. I would caution you against trusting these reviews wholesale because the focus of the game changes substantially as it progresses, and from my perspective it gets exponentially less enjoyable as it progresses.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the perfect mix between being a challenging puzzle game and a relaxing cozy experience. Perfect for fans of the Layton games who are desperate for something (slightly) similar to play. Just more plants and witches and less top hats and hint coins. The puzzeles made to complete during the game are the right amount of difficult. Even the identifying of the plants can be challenging but fulfilling(Bonus points for the pettable purring cat)
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: this game contain rich stories on it with 8 different endings. the puzzle itself is somehow decent, not too hard, but still requires thinking out of the box. for reaching different ending, we have to redo the whole game (which is monoton, and not recommended, just search wiki for the other ending after finishing the first ending). dev should enable the name of those unlocked plants for second etc run (or at least enabling that in option) so reaching other endings wont be that hard anymore.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: An incredibly satisfying game to play the atmosphere was able to convey so many different feelings with very little effort. I have a hundred amazing thins to say about this game. The plants were astounding. The colors and gentle movements they did while being so incredibly different from each other was so beautiful and reading all of their entries made me so happy I felt as if I was a Horticulturist. I love plants and being able to play a game that focused not only on the collection of plants but implemented them in their uses was so refreshing after playing dozens of games that only ever really focused on their collection. The characters while simplistic had a diversity much like the plants and it was fun piecing together how everyone fit in the town exactly and their roles in the bigger story.Overall this game is one of my new favorites and I will more than likely be putting more hours in to see the differences my choices can make. Replayability is so important in games and being able to do so brings me joy.Now that I've gushed about the game I do have some critiques. Most of these are minor and don't really impact the game in any significant way. First off being the cat. I adored the little cat sitting on the ledge and getting the pet 13 times achievement but outside of a players own sense of whimsy or being a completionist there isn't much of a draw to interact with the one creature that is interactable to us through every moment of the game. It would have been nice to see the cat take on a bit more of a role even if it was as a map clue. Still love Hellbore I just want more of the little fluffball.There are some minor issues with clicking on things and the wrong item on the desk popping up the amount of times I somehow managed to open the map while clicking other objects was a tad annoying but didn't detract from the gameplay in any significant way for me at least.  What did annoy me was the plants constantly moving themselves around. I like to keep things organized and the fact that the plants would swap their places was greatly annoying considering they go back to their place after examining or labeling them. Didn't make me want to stop playing but it certainly ruffled my feathers.Finally the end where you can identify the plants you didn't get to through the play through is both I think sweet but missing the mark of replayability. It made more sense to me that the different choices you make in different saves is what allows all of the unlocks. I haven't done a second round yet just finished the first so perhaps there isn't a need for every plant but if that's the case why have them there? either way it was a sweet gesture but doesn't really promote the need to replay the game because the collection need is already met.I look forward to playing this game again, and again, and again.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: If you're into the whole "dark academia"/occult science aesthetic but want something cozier than Cultist Sim, this is a good pick. Identifying, tagging, and sorting your weird plant collection as it steadily grows to take over your whole shop was inherently gratifying to me, which is a good thing because your customers' requests are never difficult or complex enough to give an external incentive to really knowing your shop. Much like VA-11 HALL-A, another "customer service puzzler", I came away wishing I had been challenged more when it came to interpreting and fulfilling requests, although the riddles buried in the mysterious letters and cards you receive were enjoyable and immersive substitutes.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I truly enjoyed my time with Strange Horticulture!I loved the way they incorporated the puzzles and all the supernatural aspects of it.I felt like Mr. Giles from Buffy the vampire slayer, except, instead of demon research I researched mystical plants! Totally recommend for anyone that are interested in the supernatural, witches and plants!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: This game was exactly my jam - using clues and maps to find and identify useful and mysterious plants, whilst remaining atmospheric and solitary. It reminded me a lot of 'Return of the Obra Dinn,' in a good way - having to rely on myself and my abilities to pick up on subtle hints and figure out things was really satisfying. A big recommend if you have some time to yourself and want to spend some time being focused.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely would recommend! I enjoyed the demo a lot so I added to my wishlist and bought it when it came out. I've played through three times but I want to see all the endings so I'm going to keep going. I liked that you can keep playing to identify all possible plants. My only very minor gripe is that I wish the map grid marked places you've already visited. otherwise very fun and engaging!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: 7 hours in and I feel like I've beaten most of the game. That's not a bad thing, there appears to be a bit more to go. Overall this is a puzzle and plant identification game. I found it fun and soothing with an engaging plot line. I don't have a lot of hopes for replay-ability here, but I am happy with the experience so far and looking forward to finishing off the rest game.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: This game is delightful. Simple, beautiful interface, fun and slightly challenging but not difficult (although I am thrilled that the hint system is there because I remember getting completely stuck in the demo at one point). I'm enjoying unlocking the different mysteries and clues and just having a lovely time. Highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Very chill herbalist-mystery game, one of its kind as far as I'm aware. The only thing I'm missing is the voice acting that was present in the trailer, it would have made the game more immersive. It is a semi-short game, but it doesn't feel too short. It was an enjoyable journey for me. Definitely recommend. If you think you would like this then don't second guess yourself, just grab it and play.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed this game and find it calming.  Label all your plants (you can have it done automatically or if you are like me diy it) and pet the cat!  The game is not fast paced and does not have a time limit to solve the puzzles, you do have a timer between map visits (which can be sped up via watering plants).  The story is creative and curious, with some dark unsolved things going on... (don't wanna spoil anything).  Will probably play through at least once or twice more to get all achievements but not sure where it will grow from there... all in all it was enjoyable and would suggest it for the reasons above~
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Strange Horticulture scratches the itch to roleplay as a side character during fantastical near-apocalypse to escape the reality of living through the real world's near-apocalypse ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Connecting bits and pieces of a larger story while carrying on in your own management/organization game is just the type of game I love. Classifying plants is a wonderful practical puzzle that a particular person like me can hyperfocus and build organizational systems on. The gameplay reminds me of favorites like Papers, Please and Death & Taxes-- except the tools each have their own place in the drawers which keeps the clutter away. Super fun and looking forward to replaying it as there are multiple endings
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I thoroughly enjoyed this game, it was a pleasant surprise. Calming, yet intriguing. Simple but engrossing premise with enough twists and turns to keep me engaged. A few of the clues took me a bit to workout, but they weren't too difficult. Really glad I picked this up. May replay again in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Okay Guys,So I actually bought this game because I enjoyed Papers Please and thought this maybe would be similar.It is relaxing but its more of a solving riddles type of games.In the game you are just a florist who has to identify certain plants to give to their customers and while doing that from now and then solving riddles or finding certain places on a map.I have to say the first day was kind of boring, because no one really tells you how the game is supposed to be.But it gets better and the riddles are all sovable once you get the gist of it.Soooooooooooo long story short:If you are in search of a relaxing game with a some riddles, go for it :D
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: This game is beautifully designed. Every detail is stunning, down to the little squares on the map. The atmosphere this game creates is wonderful. It is calming, despite the crazy events happening in the story! I hope maybe there will be an expansion or second game in the future. I love the mechanics of it, even if the story was completely different from this one. Can't wait to see what else the developers create in the future!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I had been hemming and hawing about this one for a bit, then saw it was on sale and grabbed it.  I am really glad I did.  It's just, well, as perfectly executed as it could be.I am one of those people who takes forever to get the hang of a user interface but this felt like I'd been playing for hours already.  There were a few puzzles that even after solving them I thought maybe could have been a bet better worded but that's true of all games,  Everything is seamless.  Just shove that plant on the shelf and the ones beside it shift to make room, no hassle.  Even the totally dreary rain fits the moodI do wish the descriptions were just a tad more complete, simply because I would not be able to describe a plant in real life and not mention the big red flower, but that's not against the game, just the gardener in me!Definitely a good rainy day game when I can't get into the real garden beds.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed the unique puzzles in Strange Horticulture. I also liked that there were choices I could make, but that there wasn't really a time limit so I could stop and think about which plants I needed. Finally, I was extremely excited that I could go back and identify all of the plants and fungi after beating the game; I can be kind of anal about things like that and it was appreciated! I'll have to go back some day to get the rest of the endings.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: A sweet puzzle game with an engaging narrative. You're in charge of a plant shop and need to use your encyclopedia to identify the plants that people request. As time goes on, you collect new plants and expand your encyclopedia.The customers give reasons for their need for particular plants and there's only a few different people who come back day after day so you become engaged in their lives and their stories.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: It's so boring! +- the basic idea is inventive, sweet and the story is not even bad- you can stroke the cat-- you either search for places on a map, plants on a shelf or plant descriptions in a book; I fell asleep before I realized how to influence the story - the puzzles (apart from searching for the right flower) make no sense and don't fit into the story- at a certain point you can't do anything but finish the game, whether you know the solution or not; I didn't so I tried out random solutions, which was even more boring- the music is repetitive and, well, I won't repeat it again. Buy it on discount, if you want to see an innovative setup, but don't expect too much.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting setting and great artwork. The "puzzles', however, are just making sure you have basic literacy skills. You simply read the entry on the plant and match it to the one on your shelf. As long as you go to the locations in letters and cards, you'll always have the correct plant. I played through five or six days and the formula never increased in difficulty or really changed. It just wasn't challenging enough for my personal taste. Story wasn't compelling enough for me to keep playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: This is a Yes BUT suggestion. As someone who works with plants I am disappointed with the lack of plant description/knowledge within the game, You are given a book with a vague drawing of a plant, some descriptions talk about the description but more often than not the description is something that you cannot check with the microscope or visually... Instead the description talks about uses of the plant. I would prefer a more accurate description of the physical appearance and uses. This could be achieved through missing pages, letter, library visits, clues around the map, and pages found within the shop. All of these suggestions are already in game features, but i would rather have more details/information than more plants. Aside from that, I was surprised by the short time frame of the game, i thought it would be a longer play through especially since the beginning you are told you inherit the shop from a dead relative. Otherwise I like the flow of the game, I just want more from it.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: It's a lot shorter than I'd expected. Finished it in 5 1/2 hours. It's delightful, relaxing, and i appreciate the magnifying glass for the sake of my posture haha. It seems replayable, with the randomness of cards and potential alternate endings, but I feel like there might not be enough variety for me to try it again, not for a while at least.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: There is a lot to like about this game, but sadly there just wasn't enough game for me to really enjoy it.My main points against it are that the gameplay is very linear (get a plant request, identify that plant, then wait for the next plant request, repeat - sometimes with a puzzle), and there are only a VERY small number of times that I was able to make any choices to influence the story. I would like to go back and see what the other endings are like, but I am not excited to do all the same puzzles again.I kept playing in the hopes that it would open up, but alas.Positive points - this game is gorgeous! the bits and bobs were fun to play with, and the world building was great. I just wish that it had a more engaging game to go along with it.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I have no hesitation in giving this game a positive review. I loved the aesthetic, and found the core gameplay (of matching flowers to descriptions, and deciphering clues to find new specimens) really rewarding. I was always excited to get to the next day so that I could find my next clue, and enjoyed learning more about the characters who came to the shop. I also liked how the game added more features as you went along, so that by the end you could brew potions, use a spyglass to find new places/words on the map, and so on. This was a really unique experience, and one I thoroughly enjoyed (even if I would have loved more coloured tags with which to categorise my flowers!) Any game where you get to open letters each day is right up my street!However, there was something that spoiled it for me, and that was the 'multiple endings' aspect. I didn't feel that this really integrated into the game: all it really meant was that you learned more about some characters than others (so some people who seemed really interesting at first would then never come to your shop again). I found that, when I reached the end screen, it suddenly told me that one of the characters was someone else's daughter, as if this was something I already knew (which I didn't), and this made me feel like the construct was a bit hollow because it had left these gaps in my knowledge. Also, the few choices you make are fairly arbitrary (whether to ignore an invitation or not, whether to kill someone or not), and don't seem to have huge story-based consequences, from what I've read about the endings I didn't try.I suppose, in essence, I wish the game had just stuck to the shop-elements (finding and naming plants, brewing potions) and expanded on those, and cut out the story element altogether. But perhaps it's unfair to judge it based on 'what I would have preferred', so I want to end by saying that I really really did enjoy my time with this game. While I didn't like the choice/multiple endings system, it was more of a background nuisance than anything that detracted from my experience. Strange Horticulture definitely deserves the 'overwhelmingly positive' aggregated rating that it currently has on Steam - I hope the developers make more gems like this in future!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: i thought i would love this game & i was right!! it feels so interesting & enjoyable, identifying plants like i do in real life, learning their names, etc etc. the lore clearly goes deep & every character has a little secret life you don't know much about; but you know enough to have an idea of what it is. &! hellebore! i lov him! i always make sure to pet him before ringing the bell so i don't frighten him. overall i recommend this game if you like flowers/plants and want to make it more 'fun'!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Really great game for a relaxing afternoon. My brain that likes classifying things is very happy. The art is amazing, I also liked the relaxing music. The puzzles are just the right amount of challenge but no too hard. Yu can pet the kitty! Very important. If you'd like to play a game that is like arranging files in a folder but with plot then search no longer!P.S. No idea where feedback shoud go, hope the developers look at these reviews: After completing the game for the first time there should appear a checkbox in the main menu, allowing for automatic plant labeling as they are added to the shelves in subsequent playthroughs. The game has a few different endings and it can get greatly reduce the time it takes to reach the end to check out different outcomes of the story
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game. What starts off as a fairly simple deduction game, finding flowers and identifying them, morphs into a thrilling story of the supernatural and a quest to navigate the 'best' path. I got ending #7 on my first go, so plenty of variety to be had. The art and puzzle design is terrific. My only wish is a variety in the music if we get a sequel. Other than that, a great job :)
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game - it was a nice relaxing point and click experience with beautiful art and an interesting story. Easy to walk away and come back to it, which is nice for me as a parent. I did have to look up one of the puzzles after getting stuck for a bit. Great job to the team for this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Very well crafted game. Finished it once in 7 hours straight. It has many endings I reckon and I really want to dive in again to make some different decisions to reach a different ending.This is basically a  puzzle game. You read letters, act upon clues and solve small puzzles to get the stuff you need. There is no "shop" management in this game, if that is what you want this is not the game for you. There is also no "growing plants" or harvesting game mechanics. It is more akin to wytchwood gameplay-wise if that makes it more clear.The story and writing of this game makes me compare it to cultist simulator, so if you are a fan of that game or stories like lonesome october by zelazny you should give this game a go!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: A charming puzzle game with just the right amount of menace, and set in an alternate South Eastern England. Great atmosphere, great music, beautifully simple character animation, lovely controls, and a legitimately unique "mythos." It does require a good deal of patience, attention to detail, and solid intuition, so YMMV; but I'm down for exactly that sort of combination, so I loved it. Its greatest weakness is that, despite having several significant choice-points and several different endings, the rest of the game doesn't really incentivize a second playthrough -- so its not terribly replayable. But I definitely feel that I got my money's worth and am hoping for an expansion or sequel!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: What a disappointment.It seems all you really do in this game is looking up plants in your book and trying to match the very vague descriptions to plants you own. Which I'm sure will only get more tedious the more book entries and plants you collect. Exploration also seems to just boil down to identifying more plants.I somehow expected more player agency or creativity. The bits of story I've seen also didn't seem very interesting.I admit I haven't seen much of the game as I stopped playing early to get a refund. But frankly, I already felt incredibly bored. Not even petting the cat was fun to me.And by the way, the controller basically just emulates a mouse and it feels super clunky and slow to use. I really dislike that this passes as "full controller support".Considering the "overwhelmingly positive" rating at the time of writing, I guess this game just isn't for me. I really don't understand what others see in it.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: A great game for autumn evenings. It has a great art style, a mystery, atmospherical soundtrack and presentation – and of course a plenty of odd plants to study. The gameplay is … “deliberate” is probably the right word for it. No action, but no mind-bending puzzles either, mainly a careful detective work, gradually uncovering the truth.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't played many puzzle games, but after immensely enjoying The Case of the Golden Idol I feel like I've been sucked into the genre. There were aspects of this game I enjoyed which allowed me to play it to completion. However, Strange Horticulture pales in comparison to the aforementioned game. The puzzles are all straight-forward enough that I only had to use the hint button once. I appreciate not feeling stuck or feeling like I need to look up a guide (or feeling stupid), but solving the puzzles became repetitive quickly. Identifying flowers gets old after 77 of them. Finding map locations is 5% riddle solving and 95% scanning the map itself for specific named locations. And, all the other puzzles simply involved flipping through the plant book again and again. All in all, the game really only consists of turning pages in a book and staring at a map. There is minimal thought required to solve the puzzles, and no satisfaction to go along with it. One aspect that survives the game comparison is the story. Great world building with an interesting cast of characters with clear and competing motives. Unfortunately, the story really only picks up at the end of this short game, so there really isn't any time to savour it. There are multiple endings, but I have no desire to explore any of them.The 6.5 hours it took me to complete this game don't feel wasted and I don't feel too bad about spending $8 CDN for it on sale. But, if you ask me to recommend this game, I wouldn't.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: What I expected: an escape room style puzzle game with plants and a dash of occult horror. What I got: a tame narrative focussed game where you continually have identify plants and locations by reading texts and solving really simple puzzles.It was an ok relaxing 5 hours. Also you can pet a cat. Won’t go for the 100% because I need to replay the whole game for it. Did identify all plants though!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Not everyone is going to like this game. But for those who like quirky little games with puzzles, cute cats, and a strange mysteries to solve, this is going to be your jam!I really enjoyed puzzling my way through the plants, creating a labeling system, and picking up little clues toward the larger mystery. Lovely ambiance as the ran patters in the background and Hellebore purrs on the counter.Played through the first time in about 6 hours, taking my time. Went back and got a few more endings and finished my achievement hunt in another 3 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Plant sorting and cat petting, need I say more?Probably.Starting I felt a bit disoriented and got some plants wrong and didn't really know what to do with the map, but this way I got to experience one of the coolest gameovers I've ever had in a game. After getting the hang of it I enjoy what time I spend with the game and went out of my way to 100% it which isn't hard by any means but that's also not the point. I wanted to see everything the game had to offer. Overall the game has an amazing atmosphere and a great haptic feel to it. The art style, sounds and story are charming and fit everything very well.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Assessing, Categorizing, Arrangin, and Utilizing – the game. This fed the same urge I had for ”Papers, Please”, without the dystopian undertone, with easy instructions and an old school touch to searching and finding the information needed to collect them all!With a cup of tea in hand I sat in my shop, quietly petting the cat as I tried to derive what enticing, mystical, and hopefully magical plant I had before me. Labelling it and finding its’ rightfull place amongst the rest of all the growing and living flora upon my shelf, this is how I spent my days, with the exceptions of helping the few, but intrguing, customers who came by my shop. Time well spent.The two creators of this game has done a great job, and I must say buying this game is money well spent. I’ve had a fantastic time, and will return for the alternate endings! (I need more games like this, desk-based games)
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: It's okay, the puzzles to find new plants are interesting but get a bit repetitive toward the end of the game, the multiple endings are appreciated but with no New Game+ it's a bit tedious to have to do the whole game entirely just for a slightly different ending.The game has one gimmick and it does that well but that's about it. It's still a solid game if you're looking for something original to play for a few hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: A+ for originality, art, and world building. A whole world comes alive even though the entire game is spent in a plant shop.C+ for gameplay. Most of the game consists of two kinds of easy, repetitive puzzles: plant identification and map clues. Progress is linear, with few decisions or opportunities to influence the world.Still, the story was suspenseful enough for me to complete the game, so my judgment is positive overall.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely little deduction game. Puzzles are just difficult enough to have you feel clever, and the penalties for failure are there to keep you from guessing randomly, but are not so frequent or tedious enough to be frustrating. World is featured but not overbearing, and characters are subtle enough to be interesting, but still noticeable. I completed the main story in 5 hours, but there appears to be a touch more content afterwards.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I finished this game in 2 days after non-stop playing. Within the first 10-ish minutes I was hooked and I knew I would be playing this game through the end. It was such a cozy yet spooky experience and I managed to drag 2 of my friends into it with me; and they both ADORED it! I love the mystery aspect and I really enjoyed finding out that you could make choices that would affect the ending of the game, that was a nice surprise. My only complaint would be that I never got to leave the shop, it was nice for simplicity sake but I would have liked the option to go out and explore or have a little more involved gameplay. Overall, still a 10/10 experience and I will absolutely be playing it again to see what other ending I can get!! New favorite replay game.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: This game is delightful, addictive and just beautiful. The only thing i regret is not having more plants to look for and identify nor clients to sell them to. If you haven't played it yet, DO, you wont regret it, it's worth every dime, every minute of your time and earn a place in your heart. Thank you.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend the game with the emphatic note that this game is primarily about following a story, not really about running a plant shop. The progression is very linear, if you don't have a plant for a customer you cannot turn them away as they are all part of the tale, you must solve the related puzzle to get the plant. Fortunately there are hints for that if you get really stuck, unfortunately that is not very satisfying.I really liked that you can label all your plants yourself based on what you read in your little book, but very sadly this is somewhat pointless as I've only encountered one or two occasions where you'll actually need a plant you've used before.Overall I have to say I was a bit disappointed by the game, because it wasn't really a game of simply running a quaint little plant shop on your own as I'd hoped. I can still recommend it though because it's a relaxing and beautiful game, you just have to adjust your expectations.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Love it!! Calming, relaxing and interesting! The soft music is so nice, and yet the dark mysteries that encourage you to figure it all out yourself is so cool. There are dark and strange things happening in this world and you only have cryptic clues, scraps of paper and a book about plants to understand whats really happening. Oh, and a map - be prepared to be seeing a lot of the map hahaha - it's very essential, and a lot of the puzzles to figure out that involve the map are soooo fun!You get to name each plant you come across with your choice of three different coloured tags if you want to keep things organised, which later on I would highly recommend! At the very least, name with red tags all the nasty ones xD Also you can pet the cat, 10/10 right there.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: From the more somber and tense atmosphere, to the various poisonous plants now under your wing, running the Strange Horticulture shoppe is full of riddles and puzzles. If you enjoy digging though old notes and using a magnifying glass and old mapp to find your way, I highly recommend this game. 10/10 would accidentally eat Storian again
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Spent roughly thirty minutes of my playtime holding my head and staring at my fungus shelf in consternation. Discovered the secret of the map about four hours in while streaming this for friends and the resultant collective jubilation and horror will stay with me for a long time. As an amateur slowly self-educating in botany and mycology, and as a narrative designer, I cannot recommend this game enough. I am fascinated by everything it's doing and I'm enchanted by the potential to apply this formula to other niche subjects. I have no doubt that this game will have an overt and fundamental influence on games I make going forward. I hope this style of mystery becomes a genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: A decent little puzzle game. It was good for a few hours of entertainment, but nothing special. I'd recommend picking it up on sale, and only if you can play with mouse and keyboard - Steam Deck feels very bad to play on because of the controls and the resolution.Some other thoughts:The plant identification is a fun concept; however, by the end, you have so many plants crammed on the shelves it becomes a bit tedious to find what you're looking for. Had I organized the shelves as I went, I wouldn't have had this problem, but I didn't do that, so it was chaos at the end.The story is nothing special. Vaguely interesting, but not really unique or compelling enough to keep me interested. The puzzles pick up that slack, however.A bit light on content. I think there's a great core concept here that could've been expanded on, specifically the map travel bits. Still, fun enough for a few hours of puzzles. I can't see myself replaying it, however.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Lots of fun! Sort of like Papers, Please in a magic plant shop. You identify plants and make decisions that affect which of the several endings you get. I enjoyed reading through the notes and plant identification book to solve puzzles; they were mostly pretty easy, but still enjoyable. On the shorter side, but well worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could leave a neutral review, but since the game has so many positive reviews I figure my negative one will be a drop in the bucket. Other insightful negative reviews have covered how I feel about this game, but I'll try to sum it up.The game is really cute, and I actually kind of like that the puzzles aren't super difficult, but I know this is a big con for a lot of folks. The concept is wonderful, and well executed in a lot of ways. I loved looking over the map, flipping through the plant book, using little tools to solve puzzles. I did not have the same issue some reviewers had of not discovering plot-important plants in time, and I had no roadblocks like that during my playthrough. I felt that pacing was pretty good overall. I finished one play through and reached one ending.However, here is a list of the sorts of issues I had with it that make me hesitant to give it a good review:-Sifting through the plants and the plant tags is just so tedious!-The plant identification book needs a clickable index and the plants to be sorted in it after identification. Like sections for mushrooms, daisy-like flowers, cluster flowers, etc. Like a real plant book. Searching through the entire book every time and scanning for a word or phrase to find a plant I already identified is unpleasant and irritating, and flipping through the pages is so slow! Them being only sorted alphabetically by their common name only is so unintuitive.-The game doesn't really seem to be worth replaying, especially due to how tedious it is and how bare bones the story is. I won't spoil anything major but it feels like there really can't be much interesting variation off of the one ending I achieved.-The main character has no traits, personality, or really anything. She isn't fleshed out at all!-The other characters are also really only people you meet in passing, it's really more like you are an outside observer only vaguely aware of more interesting goings on elsewhere, but the game acts like you are integral to it. -The plant identification and care are so basic and uninvolved. I had hoped for it to be more about tending to the plants in the greenhouse, growing and harvesting, and preparing them. I didn't expect a full alchemy simulator but something more plant focused at least.-The puzzles and plant requests seem at times to be intentionally vague to make the player fail. One of these might be fun, , and the name is misleading but the plants at times are so vaguely described in the book and upon identification, a lot of the quests are just throwing things at the wall and seeing what sticks.The concept is there, and the atmosphere is lovely. Maybe in a sequel with a bigger team and revised mechanics this game could really evolve into something special.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Such a fun and well made game! Fun puzzles, fun story and a cute cat! It was relaxing to play too and being able to identify all the plants after you finish the story adds that perfect touch. Also has replayability due to being able to achieve different endings! Works great on both PC and the Steam Deck!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Strange Horticulture is tight and sweet. It's puzzles have a rhythm that last long enough to be rewarding, but not tedious. After about 10 (casual) hours, it feels like I'm a stone's throw from the game's climax, and it looks like I'm set up to make some interesting choices with regard to the final outcome. I can't wait!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Since there's not an in between rating I'll go with thumbs up, but I don't think it deserves the rave reviews I was reading. It was good but not fantastic. It's pretty much a point and click with a little bit of puzzle guessing flowers from clues, but I found it a little boring and simple. However, the visuals are very nice, and the story is fun if a little lean. There are 8 endings, and the first run through was fun but as there are no achievements for all 8 endings.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game. It had challenging moments trying to identify where to go on the map or which plant was needed but not overly so where I was over it. The atmosphere was relaxing. I really enjoyed the gloomy music. The overall vibe of the game was very chill but grim which I found very pleasing. The characters and story were interesting. It could get a bit tedious but I like that sort of thing. If you enjoy researching and figuring things out, I think this is a great game for you. My only complaint, and it's minor, would be I would have liked it to last a bit longer and have some customers to attend to that weren't part of the main story. Oh and the cat is an adorable touch.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game! I hope that more updates allow for longer game play. I finished the game in about three days, which was longer than I'd expected. Also more characters and more in depth interaction? I didn't know what was going on until the end, and then I had to go back and re-read dialogue. A lot goes on at once. Slow it down a bit? Add more puzzles?
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked identifying and organizing my plants. The story was interesting, although a bit slow to start. I wish there were more choices you could make with the customers. The game could've been a bit more difficult. There were some good puzzles, but overall too easy. I would prefer if the game did not tell you which plant to use.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: A really fun and immersive game - especially if you fancy yourself a plant lover, witchy, and or a lover of the occult. It's an enticing world with puzzles to draw you out all over the map, wanting to identify everything in your collection, and on top of all of that there's also a mysterious murder spree going on in the background you find yourself in the middle of somehow.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: While it felt a bit repetitive in the beginning, I quickly learned how varied this game was. Tons of different puzzles using clues, unique equipment, map, and your trusty plant book. Not done yet, but the story elements have been fun to uncover.It can be a bit cumbersome to scroll left and right when viewing all of the plants, so make sure to label (or organize) them as you see fit.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I love the concept and the few hours of gameplay you get out of it, but overall it feels kind of unfinished. I would like more freedom to sort and categorize plants, making notes in your book to find stuff later instead of reading through all the descriptions for the fourth time because you didn't remember which plant had this specific other name. The ending was also disappointing, after the "bossfight" the librarian just asks you to identify all the last missing plants in a row, which wasn't a real challenge or rewarded in any way. I would recommend it anyway because everything else about the game made you feel exactly like what I imagined the job of a horticulturist of strange plants feels like.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Some have described the game as boring or repetitive - I found it incredibly soothing (and it does come to an end fairly quickly). If you're looking for WASD action, this isn't your cup of tea. But if you're looking to use your wits and click on a single interface was you sip from a relaxing brew, then get this game! I thoroughly enjoyed learning about these semi-fictitious plants and places, piecing together challenging but not mind-bending clues, and playing solo a few nights to complete the game. Very satisfying. Better than Netflix. Now I need a Hellebore plushie.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: This game!!!!! This was an amazing game! Loved every minute of it! I couldn't stop playing!! I wish it could go on and on. The thought behind this game was so well thought out! The set up of the desk and the drawers and the watering can and the whole darn thing was really very well planned and very well designed! The best game that I have played in a long time! congratulations to the two brothers who made it! Well done. I hope you will have a sequel of some kind! Bravo!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing, wonderful, spooky, and most importantly: taught me about horticulture! I had no idea that identifying plants was such a neat process. Plants have so many cool unique features! I swear, I'm not usually this into plants. But this game accomplishes everything it wanted to. It's got elements of exploration, story, puzzle, and even a bit of idle watering and alchemy. Amazing. Worth it!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Wife and I have been enjoying this game on this first night of playing it!  Puzzles are fun and gradually add difficulty as you progress (more logic and different ways of thinking about the same things) and the story has us drawn in... we're really curious how it will all connect at some point!  Really looking forward to seeing how this all plays out and if you want a fun and engaging, yet very "zen"-like puzzler look no further!  Charming writing and a soothing soundtrack (sounds effect are great as well and immersive) make this a must play for your casual chill puzzle solving adventures!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Liked:  Love games with puzzles, the story and characters were fun, building a collection of strange and unusual plants, and who doesn't love having a shop cat (other than that one guy in the game).  I liked the ability to add custom tags to plants with different colors so I could keep an eye on which ones I wasn't sure about and which ones I was pretty sure I had figured out.Wished there was more of: Brewable elixirs (I only found four on my first playthrough, not sure if there are more) and chances to use them and/or more chances to create remedies using plants that I had obtained.  Disliked: There was a pretty good variety of puzzles, but some of them got repetitive after the first time solving one like it.  After getting farther into the game and gathering a larger number of plants, I would have liked to have had a way to indicate in the journal which plants I had or hadn't "solved" yet so I could more easily flip through the book and find what I was looking for.Weird stuff: Sometimes after closing up shop some of my plants would rearrange themselves on the shelves.  I blame the shop cat.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Great, intuitive puzzle game based on plants. Only a couple mechanics that I had to take a second or third look at but I never felt like I had to find answers outside of the game or rely on a wiki to solve things. I enjoyed the ending I got and will likely replay to see the others at a later date. Music was zen, game was zen, easy recommendation for anyone looking for a story driven puzzle game to relax with.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: This game is basically just a bunch of chores. You identify plants, and once you have collected enough of them, it becomes work rather than a fun game. There is no mystery in the game, because every note you get spells everything out for you. You aren't investigating anything, there's barely any actual choice, and you spend a lot of time waiting to use items that you collected several days earlier only to be let down because the thing you thought was mysterious was dealt with easily by a note that explains exactly what is going on or what to do. There is a funny feature called hints, which essentially allows you to skip part of the work involved in identifying plants. This indicates to me that it was added to skip gameplay because the gameplay is not interesting enough to be bothered to deal with. There are multiple endings, but who would want to discover them? It's not as though the game is replayable, you have already identified (and presumably labelled) the majority of the plants in the game, having to find them again is just doing more chores rather than playing a game. The only thing good about this game is the flower art and the sound Hellebore makes when he purrs.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Finally, a game that fulfils my desire to be a tiny plant shop owner, detective and potential murderer. sat down to play for a few hours before bed and ended up binging the entire thing until past midnight. No regrets.  This is a beautifully crafted little game - there's an immense amount of satisfaction from getting a new plant or book entry and going "aha! I know which one that is!" and then affixing a little label and putting it up on the shelf.  Surprisingly good story and well-written characters.  My only complaints are that even near the end game some of the plant requests are a bit too easy and a few are repeated - I'd like to see more customers who are looking for a specific effect or only have a few physical traits to go off.  Having the non-story requests randomized would also help with the replayability.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I want to say I really and truly liked every bit of this game, but I didn't like all of it.  The one aspect that ruins it for me is how you have a Rising Dread meter that, if it gets maxed out, you get shunted out of the game play completely just to do a couple of puzzles just to get back to finding plants and "adventuring" (you don't leave the shop screen, you just get passage of if you found anything in the place you clicked on the map).If this took the Rising Dread meter out and kinda just told us if we didn't have the right plant/went to the wrong place, I would really love this game.  But, as my frustration with the fact that every two minutes I'm getting shunted out of the game play because I didn't pick the right plant, I get more and more disinterested in continuing to play this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I really, really enjoyed this game. Got through it all in one sitting, not because it's short but because I was so hecking entranced and needed to see it to the end. The puzzling was mostly great, though there were a couple I could not puzzle out myself. One included the map during the endgame and a really obtuse clue (in my opinion, maybe I'm dumb but holy moly was I frustrated haha).Otherwise though I would highly recommend this if you're a fan of puzzles and mysteries and puzzling out mysteries haha. It's a good'un. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely little puzzle game. The art is very pleasing and the gameplay is very relaxing. It's primarily researching and identifying your plants and solving riddles to unlock more information and plant types. Most of the puzzles aren't super difficult, but there are a few that can't be solved until you get more info later on, so it's best not to dwell too long on a puzzle in case you don't have all the pieces yet. (the coin and long meg particularly stumped me here)There are multiple endings having to do with a few key choices you make along the way, which gives it a bit of fun replay value, and replays go a lot quicker since the plants, customers, and events don't change beyond those key branching choice points.It's a short game (3-4 hours) but I got it on sale for $10 and I had a wonderful time with it, so I would say it's worth it if you're a puzzle/mystery game type.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: This is a decent game, and it would maybe be a neutral if not for all the deep occultism and cabinet filing tasks.If you love filing things and organizing things in what is essentially a filing cabinet next to an end table, this game might be for you. If you are really interested in learning about the facets of a fake religion based on plants, this game might be for you. Essentially, if you are a wacky librarian, this game might be for you.But if you aren't this target audience, the game is fine for about 5 hours. Might be worth the cost on sale. It's hard to put down and come back to because you're expected to catalog about 75 fictional plants according to their descriptions, medicinal properties, and latin name, but you don't have anywhere to write notes. If you put this game down, you'll need to reread the plant catalog before you get rolling again with the puzzles.However, the puzzles are fun. But they are kind of easy. The difficulty is in cataloging tons of plants in your memory.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Plants, pretty art, letters and clues. Make urself a warm drink (yes coffee, not tea) and a sweet snack, sit down, listen to the music and rainy days in the game and slowly discover new plants, help visitors, brew some elixirs and assist in a murder case. All from behind ur own cozy desk in the game.Took me about 6-ish hours to complete. Pretty sure u'll need to replay for all achievements. PS: there's hints if u get stuck and want them, but u can also play without (that's also an achievement).I'd love another game like this!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: This is an amazing, unique game. It's perfect if you're looking for an off-the-clock feel that lets you linger, investigate, and explore. The physicality of the game is very appealing - there's a real sense of place and presence in the desk drawers full of items, the letters, maps, and papers, the plants that you pick up and order and care for. The mystery narrative is interesting but not obtrusive; I've never felt forced to cut short my dipping into map locations or plant research or just examining objects and ideas by the events of the plot, which are just there when you want them, quietly waiting. It's a quiet game in a very good sense - a strong atmosphere, interesting notes on map locations, a real sense of place. The plants are beautifully drawn and the lore inventive, and the challenges in identification are well-planned. It calls for close attention to detail, but it's not capricious or punitive. I like that they use characteristics you'd look for in real plants - number of petals, shape and ordering of leaves, fine-grained detail in fungi gills - as points of reference in these imaginary inhabitants of your store. Overall, a very enjoyable solo game. Oh, one note, though - the Steam trading cards WILL give you identification spoilers!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: This game is simply lovely. I have been learning about herbal medicine for about 5 years now and have always wanted to have my own apothecary. This game really fills that niche for me in the meantime. It is so peaceful. The art is amazing, story is intriguing, and the puzzles are really fun and engaging. Oh, and you get to pet the kitty! Couldn't recommend it enough!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Who knew plant admin could be so fun? I was completely immersed in Strange Horticulture and was constantly looking forward to playing again. The creators have done a fantastic job at combining elements of mystery, fantasy and detective work and providing a rich and zen experience for players. I wish the game was longer, but acknowledge it's just because I want more.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: A sort of escape-room experience of following clues and riddles. Really really loved this game. I coincidentally bought a copy of Culpeper's Complete Herbal maybe a month before finding this game, and I've been really impressed by the depth of the occult narrative and plant identification. Just completed my first run-through after ~7 hours, but there are still more puzzles to go and multiple endings to try and get.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible game.You have inherited a horticulture shop from your uncle. You are a trainee botanist working and exploring amazing plants and their properties. Some are quite common while others even have supernatural effects. As a newbie you find yourself in the middle of an occult murder mystery trying to figure out how all of the dots connect.The game starts out slow and it's more of a shop simulator but it quickly picks up the pace and pulls you into a compelling story full of mystery that you will not get enough of. There's many interesting characters and trying to pinpoint their true motives is a thrill. There are also some choices to be made that can affect the outcomes of the storyline which is a nice little addition. The game has great puzzles, they are not too difficult but for some of them I found I had to think and work quite a bit to crack them. And with that came great satisfaction. The art of the game is fantastic and the atmosphere is good. I wish there would be a bit more variety when it comes to sound design. It seems like there is mostly one ambient track playing in the background and it gets a bit stale after a while. P.S. Don't forget to label your plants! 8,9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Almost a nostalgic feel to the game. Loved most of the clues, didn't have too much trouble. Got stuck a couple times but the hint system is just enough that it doesn't give you the exact answer so you can still figure it out mostly on your own. I do wish the descriptions of some of the plants would be a little more detailed when you inspect them, but still a good game.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Atmospheric, relaxed. light puzzler. Takes less then ten hours to finish, but that felt like just the right length and is fair for the price. Also three different endings, appearantly, though I don't think these change all that much. I recommend not dragging out one playtrough over several days, for although you *can* reread / reexamine everything it helps if the latest additions to your plant collection / plant book are still fresh in your mind.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: 4/5 - Delightful game with little replay valueLoved this game!Own a shop and collect around 80 unique plants! Lovely atmosphere, fun puzzles, and an interesting story!Only gripe is a lack of extended content. Most plants are used exactly once and then never touched again. A little disappointing to have a shop stocked with exotic flora and fauna, only to have every customer asking for one of the few remaining unidentified plants.I just want to sell plants!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually start a game and finish it before a year has gone by, but I binged Strange Horticulture in about a week. I love everything about it -- the art style, the UI, the plants and descriptions, the puzzles, the people, the emerging story. I feel like I'm keeping shop in Innsmouth, but you don't need to know anything about Lovecraft to enjoy the game. I'm looking forward to replaying and trying a few things I didn't the first time around.The developers made some great changes from the demo -- the auto-labelling is perfect -- but there's two more tweaks I would love. One is that the book would mark entries that you already own and have confirmed as correct. (My husband, a game dev, suggested that owned and labelled entries could turn into color instead of black and white.) The other is that when you receive new pages, the book marks those entries as new. Sometimes you get three or more pages and it can be  difficult to pick them out of the index.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game. I wish there was more of it but hopefully that's coming in the near future. It would also be nice to open it up to modding so we can add stories of our own, or download them from other people.I'm not going to write a full review because so many have already done so. Suffice to say, it's just as good as everyone says it is.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: at first i was sceptical, but the beautiful graphics and aesthetic of the game drew me in. i'm not usually one for puzzle games but this got very addicting very quickly and suddenly i was desperate to get every ending and learn all of the lore lol. can't wait for strange antiquities to be released!! :)
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: It's a short game so I'm glad I got it on sale. I liked it bc it wasn't too dark or too scary, the stakes weren't high. It's a very relaxing game, the puzzles aren't hard, it sometimes takes a little while to read through the text. It took me 6 hours to finish the main story and get one of the endings, I'll definitely go back to the game to discover the rest of the plants and try to get some of the other endings.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: A very fun game that requires wit, deductive reasoning, and a fondness for plants and organization. Not a game you can play all at once, so it will last a couple days of gameplay if you set aside a few hours. Multiple endings with character statuses are given, so you can play multiple times to get different results.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Such a charming little gem of a game!Everything from the subtle ambient music, to the dreary, rainy days: this is a masterpiece, and nothing quite comes close to it in terms of atmosphere. It's a highly immersive and quirky game, and I love that it has no problem just being itself.There is mystery in just the right amounts. Simple puzzles that require just the right amount of thought (nothing difficult at all). You'll be visited by very strange (and some times downright awful) patrons, seeking remedies for often very odd ailments and situations.So much to cover for such a little game!If you like story, if you like reading, if you like plants and if you like some dark, witchy stuff (as a bonus)...
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I don't really post reviews much but here's an attempt at one: I really like this game. The story is fun (because I always like a good witchy murder story), collecting the plants and figuring out what they are is very satisfying, and there's an adorable little cat almost always on screen. Idk, something about this game scratches an itch I didn't know I had. I definitely highly recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: A unique and surprisingly relaxing game about collecting plants, identifying them, giving the correct ones to customers, and solving the mysteries that come about around the region with your particular expertise. I would recommend this game if you're someone who likes a little mystery and solving puzzles. If you also like relaxing games, this one is probably a good one to try out. It has a nice art style, some witchy themes, and of course a shop cat for you to pet whenever you want. I've enjoyed it thoroughly thus far, though I don't suspect it's a super long game, and I plan to play it to completion.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Just a lovely game on every level. A little dark, but in a cozy, mysterious sort of way, with relaxing gameplay that satisfies in terms of both narrative and its puzzles. Delightfully DIY, though hints are available. I would absolutely love to see an expansion pack or DLC for this, it's a great idea that feels like it could continue from here.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: - Really organic-feeling gameplay/puzzle element- Interesting narrative about occult happenings and murders- Choices that actually impact outcomes- So many beautiful and detailed plants- Lovely art- A chill, magical game!I enjoyed this chill, witchy, magical, plant-filled game! (Ok, it feels a bit weird saying this was chill and magical when it actually gets quite dark, especially in some endings, but the gameplay is chill, and there's magical sort of stuff happening, so *shrug*)I loved how organic the gameplay felt. You can move items around on your desk. You can put things into the little side drawer. You can label plants and type out the labels yourself. To solve the puzzles, you actually have to read letters, look at the map and find locations, use tools, etc. Occasionally you have to find a plant, but the game doesn't tell you the name, just a quality of it, or a use for it, or a nickname, and you have to look through the entries in the identification book. (I'd actually have liked if the game worked this way more often, since most of the time, when it came to giving plants to customers, you were told the name of the plant you needed. That's a small gripe though, not an actual problem.)Speaking of which, there was so much detail and thought in all the plants, and that added a lot to the vibes and fun of the game. Each one has an entry in the identification book that explains what it can be used for, if it's dangerous, lore attached to it, or whatever is relevant.There's a narrative element too, a plotline about occult happenings and murders. You get to make a few decisions in the game that determine what ending you get. And what I loved about this was that 1) the choices felt like a natural part of the story and made sense as something your character could and would do (depending on what kinda person you wanna be), 2) the choices actually had an impact, and 3) the impact made sense (for the most part, though one character does act pretty differently for no apparent reason in some endings). I also like that you get not only an ending but a brief explanation of how things pan out for some of the important characters in the story.The art is lovely, especially all the plants! The plants are just so pretty. And there are so many of them, all unique! (I know I keep talking about the plants, but that's, like, the main thing of the game, so it'd be weird if they weren't really great.)The music is ambient and sort of sad. I think just one song throughout, except for near the very end to match the intensity of the story. Nice ambience though.It took me about 6.5 hours to finish my first playthrough. It took me 9 hours to get all the endings, with the help of a guide (so that I didn't have to solve puzzles and identify plants all over again) and you can also search online for advice on how to get all the endings with essentially one playthrough, using the auto-generated save points. I'm glad I did my first playthrough without looking at a guide though because I enjoyed seeing what ending I got and what consequences my choices had before I knew anything.Overall, I enjoyed the art, the puzzles, the choices, the story, and all the lovingly crafted plants in this chill little game.*Review can also be found on my blog (link in profile).*(May not include everything)- Not accessible for blind / visually impaired players and screen reader users.- Can choose sans-serif font.- Can choose auto-labeling for plants.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: It's a sweet game. I really like the visual style and the sounds, music is nice to listen to. It has that mysterious vibe. The story is interesting.But it is a bit short, I would wish there would be more clues to uncover, or more mysteries to solve. The buildup at the start is great, but the ending is very fast.Most of the puzzles are very easy to solve (at least they were for me), I personally would wish for harder puzzles and more clue following to the ending. Did expect a bit more.But otherwise it was enjoyable. Was it worth the amount payed for it? Perhaps. If it was a tad bit longer, then yes. I might replay it again in a year or two or three, but that's about it.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I LOVED this game! The clues and puzzles were sometimes difficult, but never too hard to where I'd get stuck and give up.
