It works your brain while also being super interactive and calming. Great replay-ability, there's several endings and outcomes which I love. Being able to write your own labels out is also fun for me since I love organising things. Overall, amazing storytelling, great atmosphere, replayable, makes you think. Lots of reading though so beware of that, sometimes in small or hard to read fonts!  8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I liked this game even more than I thought I would :) It strikes a great balance between charming, relaxing and dark. Plus, as everyone has noted, you can pet your cat, he purrs, and his little eyes follow your cursor! Adorable. The puzzles are not too difficult, although my autistic ass is bad at unravelling cryptic messages so I did a little cheating here and there. I loved finding new plants and figuring out what my customers needed. I also appreciated that if you get it wrong too many times the "punishment" system is super chill, although it would have been cool to have a couple more options to put your mind back together.I really wish you could keep playing simply as a shopkeeper once you've beat the game, instead of going through all the effort to find the plants and then just having to end everything. It would be so cool to keep being able to make elixirs and unravel what your customers need. I also found it hard to keep track of the different storylines and characters for some reason, so I just kind of randomly picked an ending when it was offered, lol. I'm going to play again and try to focus more on the storyline to see a different ending. Other than these very personal gripes, I loved this game and can't recommend it enough! Took me five hours to play through.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: From start to finish, I couldn't stop playing. I was sick home from work and planted myself like the beautiful plants on the shelves of my Strange Horticulture shop and settled in for 5 hours. It was fun and relaxing and such an enjoyable experience. ANY game that gives me plants, magic AND an adorable cat to pet? 10/10 I wish you could keep playing at the end in an open ended manner and help the people of the village and explore all of the fun little map, there were so many places I didn't get to go! Definitely going to play again and join the cult this time! Should be easier now that I know all the plants!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: A ton of style masking very little substance.The mechanic for identifying plants could have been more robust. The descriptions in the encyclopedia are vague, one time it said a plant was an irritant but examining the correct plant just said the leaves were coarse, whereas examining other plants did give descriptions that mentioned skin irritation.Fulfilling requests is similarly bare. Customers will come in, for the most part say exactly what they need, then if you've correctly identified the plant, they take it and it gets checked off as identified in the book. Take the first request in the game, for example. The customer is complaining about noises at night and wants to better hear what's going on. Instead of making the player go through the encyclopedia to find an appropriate plant, the game just lists the correct plant below the request and the player's only task is to look up the plant and identify which of the ones on the shelf is it. So that's two opposing problems, the game is vague when it needs to be specific and specific when it would be better vague.The game's third failing is the exploration. There is no point in searching at random or even checking out the landmarks. By the time you need to find a specific plant you'll have already received a message about its location and going there early won't help; indeed, the big exception to this rule is the abbey in the northwest of the map and going there early is a sequence break that won't make sense until you actually get the clue to go there.It's a shame because the story and atmosphere are pretty decent, but the gameplay doesn't realize its potential.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Good fun, great lore and fab puzzles! Quick to get through but super enjoyable! I do wish there were more mysteries to solve but thats also me being greedy.The fact that you can cuddle the cat? Incredible. Showstopping. Spectacular. Music was also great and I really liked those lil cards at the end of each day. Deffos would recommend for anyone that likes witchy things and puzzle games!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Strange Horticulture is a very interesting take on a puzzle game, and I really enjoyed playing it, very relaxing and soothing music. In this game you will have to both read and listen to customer’s descriptions of the plants that they are looking for, in order for you to identify them. The game has several different endings all depending on the choices you take throughout the game. A nice little detail that the mouse cursor is a leaf - also of course a big plus that you can pet the cat.If you like puzzle games I would definitely recommend Strange Horticulture!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: A very pleasant, fascinating and relaxing game! Being a biologist and loving detective games, I especially liked the game idea of exploring the map with clues/puzzles and finding plants that you identify using a book. It was not too hard to determine the plants, though sometimes the descriptions were a bit vague. It would have been nice to have the identified plants ticked off in the book, that way it would have been easier to keep track of the plants and entries. The story was charmingly intriguing and mysterious!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a beautiful and relaxing game!The puzzles aren't too hard but a little confusing at times so you really need to pay attention :D The world is fun to explore but some events will only trigger if you get the clue, so be careful! The art style is amazing and I loved everything about the story and the characters you get to know along the way. And there are 8 (or more???) story endings!!! I haven't explored all of them yet. So whenever you make a decision, it's possible to get another story line! So the replay value is really high.The only thing I have to complain about (a little) is the plant book: As the story progresses you get more entries and they also put a checkmark on plants you already identified. But it would be helpful to put pictures of the actual plant in the book for better and quicker identification because if you make an elixier you only need 3 plants to do it. Well, try to find them in your ever-expanding greenhouse! :D but that's complaining on a high level, it would be nice to have only. Like the self-labelling. On my first playthrough I played without it but on my next I enabled that feature and the story went smoother, I liked that. But on your first playthrough I would do it without it because then you get to know your plants better the more you work with them.All in all it's a big recommendation from me and I hope you pick this game up! :)If you know of games like this one, please feel free to comment to this! :)
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: A decent core puzzle mechanic surrounded by a decent story with great atmosphere. The puzzles aren't particularly difficult, time is limitless, and the difficulty doesn't really ramp up too much either. Some of the later identifications are overly vague and rely on you having already identified a different similar plant, and every time I needed to flip through every single page of the encyclopedia just to find the right latin name was annoying. These are pretty small complaints though, and the overall experience is quite pleasant.If you are looking for a chill, story based deduction game, then this is a solid choice, especially on sale. 7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: An interesting and slightly dark game. The clues for discovering the plants are better than in a lot of similar puzzle games, and the plot line is coherent and sensible; I never found myself looking up a help guide and thinking, "That makes no sense but OK." One quibble: there is at least one time-sensitive puzzle that changes the outcome of the game, but unlike the other time-sensitive puzzle, it doesn't suggest there's any deadline. So, if you don't solve the puzzle by a certain day, you never get to solve it. It would have been nice to know.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Strange Horticulture is brilliant enough if you just enjoy puzzle games. The puzzles are sometimes easy to work out, other times a bit more challenging. There are multiple paths/endings as an additional bonus. Furthermore, it's a puzzle game with multiple paths/endings, which is actually well scripted, leads you into a rich story line on the darker side of legend, has interesting quests and characters, AND it teaches you about plants. We enjoyed this quite a lot; but me?...I'm in mad love. Rec 10/10 Excellent! :) EDIT; because how dare a crazy cat person forget to mention your darling companion, Hellebore.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: This game turned out to be pretty interesting and cathartic. The story was perhaps so-so, but the mechanics were a good deal of fun. The game is well-designed and easy to master.Replay value is focused on alternate sets of achievements for those who want to get to 100%. But I think it would be neat to explore a bit more of the world and discover more plants, catalog them and enter data into a botanical register.That said, this was a fun game, and I enjoyed it.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I guess I am about half way through the game at this point but I love it already. Most of all it manages to evoke a sense of mystery that I only know from Sunless Sea, while the gameplay is entirely different. The atmosphere and presentation is also spot on. There are some UI annoyances, but it is nothing compared to the UI disaster that was a certain other game that tried to be mysterious.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely loved this game. Reminds me of Potion Craft strongly in vibes but is a totally different game. I love that there isn't money and that the only way to get new plants is to solve puzzles and progress through the game- it keeps me from feeling like I have to grind early to stock up. I like the "will to explore" mechanic since it punishes you for wrong guesses without being very harsh. The "rising dread" also feels like it prevents you from spamming random guesses without being too punishing, although I definitely did not understand the key puzzle and just guessed. It's definitely possible to solve this game on the first playthrough without hints although I did not. I'd recommend this to anyone who is interested pretty much. Pros:-good vibes-the core gameplay of identifying plants and their usage is fun-puzzles at just the right difficulty-feels well thought out and high qualityCons:-price is on the higher side, though still worth it even if not on sale (I am a bit of a penny pincher tho)-character problems: they feel flat and a bit forgettable. I wouldn't let this deter you unless you're looking for something where the characters are a major part of the game-Not much replayability, since once you know the plants it's not a challenge to reidentify them.Overall a solid 8/10, a nice time.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who likes to start playing and never finish a game, this one was different.The game was very engaging in a way that it kept me playing for the whole day and finished it in ONE sitting. (~8 hours)The puzzles are great and not too hard. If we ever find ourselves struggling, we can use hints.I like the story-line too, the flow was steady and it kept me interested throughout the play.Graphics are nice, and overall I think the game has been refined well before release because I didn't encounter any technical troubles in my 8 hour run.(+) Concept is new and interesting (Plants!)(+) There are several puzzle type so it doesn't feel redundant(+) You actually can spend a LOT of time in the game reading about the plants if you're not speeding through(+) For me, the game feels relaxing. You can just take things very slowly, pet the cat, water plants, and chill(-) No endless mode (You can't keep on playing after you finish story)
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I found this game by coincidence and was not conviced I would like it. BOY WAS I WRONG! I played through one of the multiple story paths in one 6-hour sitting. I will dream of plants. The style and sounddesign make it a very cozy experience. I enjoyed the riddles which are cleverly designed, and the times I was completely stumped there was a mostly spoilerfree solution avaialble in the guides. The hint button itself felt a little bit redundant, as it basically just tells you if you can progress without solving said riddle without providing help FOR the riddle. That was however the highest nitpick I could find. The characters are charming, the story is intriguing and your choices matter. Oh, and YOU CAN PET THE KITTY!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Surroundings were misterious all year round. From the early spring snowdrop making it's way through the white earth and ground covering violas, to the field mushrooms and golden red domes of leaves below and above my eyesight in autumn, coniferous spikey trees were still green and still unclimable.Insectariums were useless to me because i swore to myself that i would fill them up with wasps. Herbariums on the other hand... well let's say my familily was not exaclty pleased when i was constantly asking whats the name of THIS blade of grass even if it was the same plant that i picked 2 days before, or when i used early 20 century books for pressing flowers.  My values were skewed a bit. Time went on, forgot all about my little adventurous research. Made new ones with videogames and their codexes. I will note here the pleasant Witcher journals and codexes with all types of creatures, lore and ofc my favourite PLANTS! In this game potions and oils have great importance if you want to play on harder difficulties and it's half of the moving arch of the witchers. World of Warcraft also scrached my itch for collecting plants; my gm allowed me a guild tab that i was constantly supplying with herbs and high tier potions.   A detective, mystery, deduction, collection game that has a Herbarium! and living plants (wandering bue amirite). Besides the gruesome plot and the ordinary people that enter your little shop with ordinary ppls problems, some mundane others a bit straaange (yeah it's in the title), the appeal of the game loop is still deducting witch plant on the shelves is that on your catalogue. I played on release when you didn't have a automated check mark on the right ones so it was a treat flipping pages and confusing myself to exasperation of getting a order wrong.   The game is leveled by days. Days are mesured by suppling customers with plants they need. Plants don't have a quantity, only a type and are found in the world that you can access by a very beautiful and interesting map. The layout is remaniscent of papers please depicted by a desk with drawers where you can sort clues and tool like items. After a day you will get a clue that you will have to follow to uncover a new plant or event. The puzzles are clever and they never repeat. The customers needs are always different.  The plants, how they look (i wanted to write how they smell, but immediately snaped back and realized that the immersion of a animated drawing will not have the same effect for everybody) the attention to detail in a simplistic drawing and putting a minor difference in a plant to confuse the heck out of the player is the perfect gamedesign for deductions. The game does not hold your hand. You have to read (not a wall of text) and be attentive at the descriptions and clues in order to advance.   Forget about the hint button, never used it but maybe you will need it, i'm not sure how it works. Not going to spoil anything about the story, i will only say that is good enough and definitely mysterious. Another mechanic i didn't really care for is the fail system. I will not say anything about this either because it gave a sense of dread and panic similar to Until Dawn butterfly effect but miles away; I wish that maybe, maybe devs will implement such a thing in their next game because they nailed the sensation, but not there as a driving mechanic for it.  There is another system for activating traveling, again not great because you have to wait or complete tasks or water your plants. Tbh it is the weakest part, only there to drag minutes better spent examining clues or tagging plants.  There is no voiceacting and it really does not need it, it would have snapped you out of researching on a very bleak, rainy, dark piano background music.  Besides the customers, there are notable characters with diverse backgrounds and different stories, your choices matter for their ending as much as yours. Not anything convoluting but enough to make you play one more to see their stories outcomes.  It dabbles a bit in potion brewing, enough to spark your imagination but leaving you wanting more. I really smell a beautiful sequel or prequel because the lore matches it flawlessly. The lenght i feel is perfect, but i really hope that Bad Viking will continue with this genre and theme in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I liked this game a lot.Strange Horticulture gives you a job to do. It is up to you whether you want to play God and influence the lives of others. The primary mechanic of collecting and identifying plants and fungi is complex enough to make you feel like an expert, but simple enough to be fun, and the characters are generally clear-cut and interesting.It's like reading Agatha Christie, or watching a Hallmark movie. "I, an ordinary person with a useful skill have suddenly become a crucial part of an enormous conspiracy," if you see what I mean. It's fun; it's comedic; it has that self-centered quality about it while still being entirely original.Play this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I thoroughly enjoyed this game. From venturing out via the map and using clues in order to locate plants, to organizing and labeling everything in my Apothecary. This lil gem of a game was very pleasant for me. I enjoyed the music as well! I would routinely wake up in the morning, feed my cats, open my shutters, brew a coffee or tea and settle down at PC for an hour or so of this game. I have my own Apothecary in my house with my herbs and oils and I felt right at home. I hope for another game like this in the future!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10 game, logic puzzle based with fairly rigid storyline and only one real screen the entire time, but hit a sweet spot for difficulty/repetitiveness with the puzzles: really regret that there's not more of this game out. Judging by the sheer size and detail of the map, and that there were still many unused plants by the end of my run with very few plants used more than once, I imagine there is a great deal of room for continued expansion.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly comfy game for it being "dark". I play it almost solely to pet Hellebore, but it is nice to collect plants. it's not an open world where you can clock 200+ hours and still not complete the game.  You can replay and make different choices to have different outcomes, so there is replay-ability.  I enjoy the ambient sound, the graphic design and the story of the game, and it's a quick play-through in comparison to other puzzle/story games.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: It's a very interesting game and it does make you think. There is no time pressure which is absolutely wonderful  but you will definitely feel the little cogs in your brain twirling. Few things weren't clear which made me feel frustrated a few times, I admit that. However, the overall experience is very unique and satisfying. And I did finish the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: This was a GREAT 10 hour play (with another chill replay in my future.) I could have drawn it out a little longer but I got stuck on a few End Game puzzles and my patience got the better of me because I was THAT excited to see where the story was going!Fun Management Sim with some great head scratching puzzles in a world with mystical and mildly creepy overtones gave it a great balance of bewitchingly (dare I say) kind of cute, with the ever encroaching fear that something sinister is going on. Perfect for anyone that enjoys the idea of the day to day life of being a low key witch with a green thumb while facing the threat of the occult. Ya know. The usual.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyed this game and didn't want it to end. Though looking back I think it was the perfect length. The gameplay and puzzles are simple but still challenging to a reasonable degree - nothing that will get you stumped for an ungodly amount of time. I loved discovering all the new plants. The story and characters are interesting and mysterious, though I do wish the ending(s) had a bit more huzzah to them. Hellebore / 10
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Got it in the sale, took 8 hours to finish a single playthrough and get what I think is a standard ending.I expect that it would not take me much longer than that again to get the other endings as puzzles I took time to figure out on second runs I will know how to do already cutting down in time, For the sale price (£5.39) its fantastic value for money at full price unless the additional playthroughs add a lot more time than I would expect to figure out how to trigger their endings then I would say it’s 50/50 and really comes down to how much you love this style of game.The story while simple was engaging and the art style is pretty and works fantastic with the enviroments and style of gameplay. The descriptions in the book are really well done and it did not feel like a chore rooting through it to solve puzzles or identify the plants. most of the puzzles were simple to answer one or two had me pause for a moment because I forgot a clue from another page and went back for it.I enjoy puzzle games but would not say they are my go-to game so if your hoping for something to really test your problem solving its probability not going to be this game as I expect people who are really into puzzle games will find this very easy but the story and journey I would say still makes it a worthwhile game to play (more so at a sale price).
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I love plant/alchemy games like this and I love the occult/spooky vibes from it. Its fairly simple, people come in with household names (sometimes scientific names) for plants they need, or they come in with an issue and you find the relevant plant and hand it to them. In total there's roughly 8 endings, and some of the puzzles can leave you sitting there for a few seconds before you figure them out, but the thing I enjoy the most is the fact you can choose who to be with. Overall, if you want a spooky game that doesnt take too long to finish then totally get Strange Horticulture.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: If you like spot the difference and matching types of games, you might like this, but there isn't a lot of plot, and the riddles/puzzles are mainly just spot the difference. You have agency in follow-up playthroughs, but you don't get enough information in the first playthrough to guess at what all the results of your actions might be, and follow-up playthroughs to get different endings are repetitive drudgery. There aren't good tools to help with sorting or organization of your plants (just labels and the ability to drag the plants around), so you have to do all of that manually, and your desk can easily get cluttered. There's also no way to search for labeled locations on the map, so you're either trying to memorize the map or poring over it every time you have to find a new landmark.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: If you are interested in these cozy types of games this one is for you. I'd say it's a very interesting mix of Papers Please and Potion Craft. The characters and story help give a sense of progression to the gameplay. I wish it had expanded on some other mechanics more, such as the plants that have hidden details you need to discover, or the use of the plants' powers on other items you hold.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: This is a calm game. There are no time pressures to complete an interaction and your decisions have consequences. There are some nice gameplay choices, the ability to name plants or have it done automatically as you identify them. The chance to organise the plants in an order that works for you. The neatly compartmentalised storage draw. It all makes me feel happy to see a game well designed and with user comfort in mind.Bonus point to any creators who give me an animal a pet and an achievement for doing it. All the pats for Hellebore.😸 (I'm so disappointed in the over 50% of plavers who don't have that achievement btw)It won't be for everyone but I enjoyed it greatly.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: A fun, unique experiment.identification puzzles are one that's underutilized, and is this game's entire mechanic, so it was a breath of fresh air and potential that I enjoyed through and through; the dark undertones and mystery had me fully engaged, and I loved wracking my brain to figure out solutions that were literally staring at me.There are some aspects that aren't the most fleshed out; for example many plants are used a single time for a single puzzle, and there are very few times the game gives you choices of plants to use. It would have been interesting to see fewer, more complicated plants, with puzzles that worked more innately with you researching and discovering them. That said; the plants are wonderfully designed and drawn, you can pet the cat! a very chill game which is trying some new things; Which worked out in a fun result.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not your garden variety herbalism store management sim. There are dark overtones and cultish vibes to the story, which I absolutely love. The gameplay is similar to Papers Please. And you will have to read a lot. There is no voice-acting or narration. But the mystery of the town and the nearby areas will draw you in. I was hooked and played for 4 hours straight and still haven't finished the game. Absolutely loving it.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: fun little research/deduction game with good set dressing. plays like a less-dreary papers, please but lacks much of the weight that made that game excepitonal. that said, it's greater than the sum of its parts--the narrative isn't especially unique or memorable, the puzzles and deduction aren't difficult at all, but the whole package feels  and flows naturally at a good pace. game does a great job of pairing a dour soft-lovecraftian tone with moments of brightness and warmth. multiple endings based off choices made add replayability. can't deny that i got a sort of lizard-brain satisfaction from sorting and labeling all my plants. works well on steam deck with mouse control on the pads.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: What a great game! Never thought I would be so hooked by identifying plants, but here I am. I liked the story and going through puzzles was engaging even though they weren't that hard. One play through took me 5h+ but there are multiple endings, so there is a replayability option to hunt those. Totally recommend if you like relaxing game that involves some mystery solving. PS. You can pet a cat, so it's a 10/10 in my book!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: It's an enchanting and pleasant game that draws you in with a bewitching story set in an intriguing world accompanied by charming characters. There's puzzles to solve using various clues and secrets to discover. All the while, you're collecting new plants to help aid the citizens of Undermere in their various ailments and adventures. Overall, it's very relaxing like settling into a good book on a rainy night.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I´ve to admit... this is probably one of THE best games i´ve ever played.The first thing that gets one hooked is the basic but unique game idea of having your own plant store and having to organize so you don´t totally loose control over it.But not that this is everything. The attention to detail that went into this masterpiece is just overwhelming...just consider the details considering the art (e. g. the different characters or flowers) or the story telling. The fact that one simple decision can change the outcome of the story (and there are quite a bunch of different endings to this game) is genius.Only one thing that I would like to point is that the amount of puzzles one has to go through could be increased if I´m honest. For me it wasn´t enough to just have the wonderful and creative puzzles appearing only when messing up basic tasks during the story. It would be nice having more of those puzzles like searching the right key for the keyholes or something. Regardless the amount riddles like those leading towards finding new flowers.Actually, I have to admit that this masterpiece became one of my favorite games. Maybe even my most favorite one. Thank you for developing such a genius and entertaining game.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: This was an extremely enjoyable game that I will replay for achievements.The plants are unique, the story is compelling, the secrets are well thought out, and the decisions make your playthrough seem more personal. Honestly I wish the game had continued forever. I will be looking into other games from this team. You also can pet the cat. Very well done.TLDR: Dark, Compelling, Unique, Polished. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game - as a concept.It is ruined by an atrocious user interface.The game consist almost entirely of unnecessary clicking, draging and inventory managment.Plants you organise in your shelf become disorganized, because now plants just drop anywhere between already identified plants (which you then have to label yourself), and after you have reorganized and close the shop at the end of the day... for no reason some plants become swapped again, for no reason.The *riddles* often  consist only of sifting through loads of papers, which you have again, organize manually by hand. Or you have to remeber which of the 30+ plants and fungi has another trivial name.... and you have to click through pages and pages with terrible UI. Your main horticulture book? thats the only thing that somewhat organizes itself, adding new entries alphabetically, but you cant even browse pages with arrow keys. Oh, and the plant discriptions? sometimes they don´t even include any identifying characteristics. *FUN*.Instead of gameplay and riddles, you are given tidium and bad game design.The *Story* isn't even that bad... just very, very shallow.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: It is a cute game, but a little short.  I like the concept.  identifying the plants is challenging but not so hard that it is frustrating and unplayable.  Choices matter to some extent and there are alternate endings.  Overall a fun little game.  Unless more content comes out though, you could beat it and get all achievements in about 10-15 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: The idea is there but the execution just kills all sense of mystique, both from a narrative point of view and a puzzle point of view.Customer enters the store, and she requires a flower to achieve her desire purposes. The logical process for this would be to detect what the actual flower is that fulfils her purpose , and then find it by descriptors. Instead this game just flat out tells you what flower you're looking for by name, even though the customer doesn't know it, and presumably you can't possibly know it, unless your character is just an expert with librarian knowledge of plants, in which case, that doesn't make any sense because you'd just give her the plant, and also what would the point in the game be. Instead you are brought forward to the process of detecting what it looks like on your shelf. Why would you know exactly the name of the flower to find, but not know what it looks like.It doesn't make any sense whatsoever.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't know what to expect but it certainly wasn't this, and I am enthralled.I absolutely love the atmosphere of the game, the music, the character building, the storytelling.I love that your choices matter. And moreso for myself, I love that I recognise a lot of the names on the map and that there's even one place named that is a ten minute drive from me.Music: 5/5Storytelling: 5/5Characters: 4/5Plants: 5/5Puzzles: 5/5You are a horticulturist. You work in a humble plant shop that was left to you and you're getting to grips with the different plants that you have in your shop.Through pleasant and not so pleasant interactions with daily visitors, you will expand your knowledge and use of different plants that you currently own or will come to own through a unique way of exploring your map by way of orienteering at points.The game is not stressful, nor is it timed. You could spend the whole first day watering your plants (they never die) and exploring the map (though it would take a while lol), but through deduction and the use of some interesting items, you visit and revisit locations to discover more varieties to provide the people with what they desire.Slowly you find that something is not right with the town and become involved in something a lot deeper than the roots of your plants go.Your choices matter and there are several different endings that you can encounter. Do you choose to aid, abet, or alter the future?I 100% recommend. It's a charming, dark, mysterious tale and you find yourself getting wrapped up in the goings on in Undermere.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: A brilliant spooky puzzle game. Puzzles are challenging and get you using your problem solving skills without (in my opinion) being overly complicated. The art style is gorgeous, perfect to play on a rainy autumnal afternoon. And the music is very relaxing. Perfect for cozy gamers looking for a more dark academia, spooky autumnal vibe to their game.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Pixie Rating: While the game has a good story and puzzle aspects the length of time it took me to beat it without a guide makes it not worth the full 16-17 US dollars it's asking unless you wish to fully support the game devs. With 8 variable endings for those who like to see each of the endings. But for those who tries to go best ending first and leaves it untouch will find it lacking.   with the theme being base in the Occult it's fairly straight forward. the characters coming in gives you a window to the outside world, or hints to locations for plants or needed objects. the character's themselves reflect the world they live in. The story a cautionary tale of what happens should you try and mess with forces you don't fully understand.  With your trusty book and basic deduction skills all the puzzles don't require much thinking. Some, but not brain straining.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: If you've watched the series Grimm, then you know what I mean by saying that this is a Rosalee Simulator. or Spice and Tea Simulator.A very calming game of collecting plants, identifying them based on hints and helping clients with various ailments ranging from the physical to the paranormal. Sometimes you can also choose to either cure or hurt the clients. You'll get drawn into mysteries of the world around you through stories and quests.  There's no fighting or speed required. You always have time to think. A nice change of pace from running, shooting or racing against the clock.Definitely recommended for anyone seeking an almost meditative game with a hint of mystery.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: So cozy! I love collecting and identifying the plants and I found the map puzzles to be really fun. The story was kinda meh for me but I didn't really care. The game lends itself I think to the possibility of some fun DLC options so I hope they do that, or make a sequel that has more flushed out gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: This game was such an enjoyable experience. I've played through a couple of the endings and each path was just as fun to play as the others. The plants are all well-designed and unique, which I can imagine was hard to do considering how many there are. I also love having the option to pet Hellebore, which I do before I ring the bell every time to make sure he doesn't get startled. The only things I wish this game had were a screen to let you know which endings you had gotten so far and some kind of post-game hard mode that never told you the name of the plant you were looking for. I mostly wish that it was just a little bit longer, it's almost criminal to make a game this good so short! Overall, I highly recommend that anyone considering getting this game to go for it, you won't regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: An atmospheric interactive story / puzzle game, where you play the role of a plant-collector in an occult version of the Lake District. Although it is a linear game with only a handful of chances to affect the story, the game manages to disguise this and feel very open due to the game map -- you can visit any square and learn a bit more about the gameworld.The puzzles are engaging with a wide variety of puzzle-types, but the game holds your hand and it's very easy. I didn't need to use any hints and finished within a few hours. It's perhaps best to enjoy it as an interactive first-person story than a hardcore puzzle game.The overall narrative is engaging, but it needs a Part II to go into the backstory of the characters a bit further. Similarly, a lot of thought has gone into the individual plants and locations, but that richness is also underused -- once you have identified a plant or visited a location, there are only a few cases where you have to come back to it again to do something with it. (The short postgame in particular feels like a bit of a wasted opportunity.) There is definitely scope for a DLC / patch content to go deeper into the game lore, add additional side quests, develop the characters further etc.   so I am looking forward to that. Re-playability is a bit of a weak point as things currently stand: it's a linear game, so after completing the game with any ending (which takes about 4-5 hours), the main enjoyment is trying alternative choices and looking for other endings. You can restore saves at appropriate points to shortcut this, but this wipes your end-game save so be warned. However, if you start a new game, you then have to relabel all the plants again and repeat the same puzzles. So it's a shame that completing the game once doesn't unlock a variation on the main playthrough to make it more interesting to pursue the other endings.I'm not sure about the 'overwhelmingly positive' evaluation the game currently has, but it's 'very good' in my book, and I look forward to the devs filling out the game with more content, so I can come back and explore this world again every once in a while.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Bought this game on sale because I have wanted to play it for a while, and I am so glad I did. There aren't too many 'bad' things about it. I will complain that some of the clues you REALLY have to think outside of the box or guess a lot. Which isn't that big of a deal, it just got frustrating sometimes. I like that there isn't much of a timed aspect to this game (i don't like time limits). I have so far only finished one ending, but i am going to continue to play and see if I can't get the rest of the endings. This game is wildly different than a lot of others I have played. I loved the story line and the adventure aspect. Definitely recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Explore the woods. Uncover mysteries. Lightly poison a villager or two. A cozy plant shop simulator with clever puzzles, loads of ambiance, and a purr-fect cat companion. This is a lovely game to play with a friend or with a stream, helping you decide which plant to give a customer and what space to tick off on your map. My friend and I read all of the letters and lovely dialogue aloud, all the way up to the most excellent ending. It's fun and calming, even when the goings-on in Undermere are not.A very satisfying playthrough that will absolutely be reprised at some point to see where other choices would have taken us. Some lovely accessibility features as well. Highly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I got one ending so far and I am at 5 hours of playtime. The plot unwraps as the main character identifies more plants. I like the style of storytelling; however, it is rather tiring to play this game, probably because of all the readings and identifying, and for a moment it actually feels like a job. I might not have the energy to collect all the endings, but I got all the plants identified! Looking forward to Strange Antiques.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: If you want a less grindy Cultist Simulator or a similar experience to The Room, Strange Horticulture is right up your alley. Perfect for short or long sessions, no rush to complete the game and an amazing background theme that after a 4 hour session does not annoy in the slightest.10/10 for what it wants to be and what it delivers.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Fun and relaxing little game. Great art and music. The story was OK but was oddly paced and ended abruptly. Few minor gripes:- The botanical aspect did not feel well-researched. This was very disappointing since this is a game about plants. The plant descriptions were lacking in technical terms and even used incorrect terminology in some cases.- The desktop gets cluttered quickly, especially since the book and map are regularly used and cover almost the entire square. The drawer system would be more helpful if things would automatically go back to the drawer after being used.- It is difficult to organize the plants since new plants spawn in the center of the lower shelf and push any plants around them to the sides. Using the lower shelf for your identified plants is unavoidable after a certain point so I wish there was a better organization system for this.Enjoyed it overall.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: It is a very relaxed game. I purchased it so that my wife and I could sit and play it together. On that basis and the fact that the story is somewhat interesting (with a caveat), I would recommend it as a purchase. Some clues are obscure, perhaps a bit too obscure like the developer got too cute with a puzzle. The choices that you are faced with in the game don't seem very clear cut as to why you might choose one path over another. In fact, in some cases the choices don't seem to be choices at all and that you really only have one choice and doing anything else is just wrong. However, apparently, these are the moments that bring about the multiple endings. We did complete the game, but I can tell you at the end of it we both said, "meh, it isn't worth our time to go and see what the other endings might have brought."
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Just from the promotional images / videos, I wouldn't have expected to like Strange Horticulture, but once I tried its demo, I was won over nearly instantly. Strange Horticulture has a great sense of atmosphere, from its almost tactile-seeming gameplay and wonderful sound design (both the ambient sounds of the weather and the sound effects for picking up / putting away each item) to its gently spooky town inhabitants and mystery plot.The developers clearly put a lot of thought and effort into this game, and I really appreciate how even small details serve to flesh out the world, characters, or atmosphere (like how there seems to be no real "game over", just a series of ominous puzzles to solve, or how you can tell that one of the characters has been consuming a lot of Drathium just by looking at their character portrait - even before you read their bio or talk to them). I also really enjoyed the drip-feeding of the story and puzzles for each day, which gives the game a really nice, consistent pace, as well as the brilliant use of the map - using it for puzzles while also giving a sense of where characters / events are located. All in all, this was a great game and is highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game. It took me a while to get the hang of it, but once I did, I was hooked. I haven't gotten the whole way through it yet, so I don't know how difficult it gets from here. So far, I think that it is a great game to play. Remember to label the plants that you discover from the very beginning.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game. So many reviews have said that people wish for it to end sooner - I wish it went on for longer. The end of the story was quite abrupt and I wasn't expecting it as I got so caught up in helping people and identifying plants.Here are a few things I absolutely loved about the game:1) HELLBORE! 2) The cataloguing and sorting of plants is so much fun. The plants are beautifully made. The sketches are gorgeous and the descriptions satisfy my need for lore. Definitely the highlight of the game for me. 3) The puzzles to find new plants from letters and card clues are not so hard that they're impossible but slightly difficult so that when I do figure it out, I'm proud of myself. Great mechanic and perfect balance.4) Petting the kitty before ringing the bell so he doesn't get spooked. I did it every single time before I rang the bell haha.5) The story is actually quite enjoyable and getting to pick between different plants to give people changes the outcome. Love that.6) I was worried that it would come across as a shop management game but the lack of income to manage was very nice. Definitely sets this game apart from others.7) Yeah, the cat.8) The music and sound effects of rain and storm are supremely relaxing. Ambience/10. I really enjoyed sitting in a dark room and playing the game. Was completely immersed because of the sounds and was very relaxed the entire time.Things I didn't like:1) Potions are annoying.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: Played through my first ending live and I cannot express how much I adored this game!! A wonderful mix of frustratingly delightful puzzles and the smaller puzzles of identifying each plant. Also cat. Normally little gimmicks like "yes you can pet the cat" are a bit silly to me (since you should always be able to pet the cat ofc) but you've made the purrfect purr noise. No matter how frustrated I got when i misunderstood puzzles, I could always pet a cat.I played through the game without utilizing the hint feature except by accident once; and the puzzles are incredibly well done for sussing the entire game out without needing it. Even when I horribly misunderstood a puzzle, the game gives you plenty of leeway to backtrack and figure it out eventually.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fun to play for a while with many puzzles and relaxing rain. While it may get difficult at times, sticking with it and playing it out feels very rewarding. I personally enjoy the game and hope it also comes off just as appealing. May not be worth over $10, but all in all I am glad I made this purchase.
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review: What a cool little game! Mystery games are hard to come by and this one was short but satisfying. The game does a great job of introducing mechanics one at a time and giving you puzzles that feel good to solve. I thought it would all be plant identification (which is harder than I expected) but there's also secret messages, map navigation codes, and a story with multiple endings. Oh, and the sound design is great, it's very soothing and ASMR-esque, especially when it's raining. Such a nice time!
_childDocuments_.name: Strange Horticulture

_childDocuments_.review:
Welcome to Undermere, a quaint town surrounded by hag-infested forests and rugged mountains. You are the Horticulturist, owner of local plant store Strange Horticulture. As a cast of colorful customers come by your shop, you are quickly thrust into an occult mystery stretching back hundreds of years.

Strange Horticulture is an occult puzzle game in which you play as the proprietor of a local plant store. Find and identify new plants, pet your cat, speak to a coven, or join a cult. Use your collection of powerful plants to influence the story and unravel Undermere's dark mysteries.

_childDocuments_.review: PHILIPPINES MENTIONED!!jokes aside, i really love this game because its so much more than what it initially imposes. the game makes the player feel more involved with their actions and the world, and that extends even outside of the main gameplaythe story is so much more than the events that transpire. its about our relationships with people and learning to love and let gothe art is incredibly appealing and i find it really cutethe visuals and cinematography add so much to the overall immersion and helps a lot with driving the narrative and emotions in each sceneoverall really amazing game!

_childDocuments_.review: I don't even know where to begin.This isn't really a "game" per se, but more of an interactive visual novel. So there'll be a lot of reading and advancing dialogue. But believe me when I say that the emotional rollercoaster this narrative takes you on is on the same levels of Omori, Persona 3, and Your Name. (I know, weird comparisons, but trust me.)Also...after about 8-10 hours of gameplay, it will feel like you're done. But please, let the credits finish and keep going. You're not done yet. If you've ever played OneShot... It's kinda like that. Just trust me.Please. I beg you, play this work of art.A few small suggestions I have for the developers...Please find a way to get cloud saves to work. I switched from my steam deck to my PC partway through and struggled for hours to find where the save data was stored on the linux version to transfer to my PC. It'd also be nice to get this to run at a consistent 30fps on the steam deck. In several scenes it drops down to 20-25fps. While this isn't that big of a deal for the kind of game this is, it's still a bit jarring with the way the text is animated. I also had the game randomly crash a few times on steam deck. Didn't notice this issue on Windows.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, a big applause to the developers;  it’s clear they put their heart into this game.At first, it might seem like a very chill story with silly jokes here and there, but man, the way they unwrap the story—ho-ho, not gonna lie, it’s pretty unexpected and sentimental. My eyes were quite watery most of the time (maybe I’m just a bit sentimental, but anyhow…). But seriously, what I really like is the pixel art, which is really well done and noticeable during the characters' close-ups and when surfing in the in-game social media. Combined with the soundtrack and 3D environment, it makes the scenes feel alive throughout the story, giving the game its own unique identity. Lastly, the message they want to convey us is really nice and gives you something to think about. It’s definitely a game I’ll remember.So, if you enjoy visual novels with mini-games and interactive choices, and want to use up a new box of tissues, then this is your game.

_childDocuments_.review: It was the best purchase i have made. I regret not even a second that i have spent playing this game. _childDocuments_.review: (very, very light spoilers)I really, really wanted to enjoy this game. My favorite kind of games are interactive visual novel type games (Doki Doki, Danganronpa, Your Turn to Die, etc.) and going into this game, I was expecting something of very similar quality to these games because of the high praise that I had seen. To my pleasure, the demo seemed to give exactly that and more. The first thing you notice going into the game are that the visuals are absolutely stunning; a pleasing mixture between 2D and 3D pixel graphics which is done extremely well. The interaction: waking up Mark with the clock, putting the coins into the subway machine, texting, making the slides with Ryan. It was all amazing. The story up until the end of the demo was very intriguing. So, I bought the full game. The visuals are the only thing about what I mentioned prior that stayed consistent throughout the 20 hours of gameplay. For me, the game began to get very frustrating and boring as I continued playing. The main issue was the pseudoscience (Louise's "experiment") and the explanations of such that accompanied. It was very unconvincing and honestly very cringe worthy to me. The game seemed like it was trying to be somewhat horror/psychedelic, but it failed in the process. I would have MUCH rather the game been a light hearted slice-of-life than be entangled in some "science-y" nonsense which the game became 5 hours in. The attempt to make the story "deep" ruined all of the other aspects that had the potential to work well in the story. Cathy was almost developed fully. Almost. Mark's character seemed to get lost in the action (like, Mark's personality suddenly vanished and we were left with a very basic and uncompelling character). Kate was a pointless addition, Ridel was boring, and Louise needed to do more than just use big words to convince me that she was smart. The Mark and Nicole situation made no sense and was not justified. The final ending was silly. The entire game is basically just a story with very, very minimal gameplay (probably less than 30 minutes, total). I think I pressed my spacebar a total of 1,000,000 times throughout the game (idly, most of the time). I'll stop ranting, but really, the only good aspect of the game was Cathy. I'd've much rather preferred this game without all the multi-universal-willy-nilly and with full developments of the characters. I'm astonished that this game as received such positive feedback.(TLDR; Although visuals are superb, the game was boring with minimal gameplay, the writing was cringey, there is a messy mixture of plots (with a main plot that doesn't make sense) with severely undeveloped characters.)

_childDocuments_.review: I remember playing the demo of this game a couple of months ago and being really fascinated by the writing after I finished it. The team at Polychroma Games have created such well-written characters in a great story in a (for me) foreign and interesting setting, that I had to experience it all (for the first part) in a six-hour session that ended with me crying at 4 o'clock in the morning. Thinking about it, I probably cried more than once. If you are mildly interested in a wonderful and emotional story, Until Then will be a 20 hour long experience you won't get elsewhere.To that extent, I really don't want to make it a secret that this game is meant to be played more than once (it's not really New Game+ or anything like that, you'll have to see for yourself), and although I was happy with how this game ended the first time around, the last one really makes this game a whole. I hope this doesn't sound cringeworthy, but in a way you can compare it to EVA/End of EVA & Rebuild EVA. - You can get away with just one of them, but as a package it's the definitive and complete story.Play Until Then because,the world hasn't ended yet, right?

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game on a whim a few weeks ago, but sat on it because life became busy for me (ironic, I know). I should also mention I don't play new video games all too often, either getting bored or shooed away in the first couple hours or it sits in my library collecting dust. That was until I sat down and started playing Until Then and the moment I did, I couldn't put it down. It hit me on a level I never thought a video game ever could. And, of course, I bawled my eyes out at least 10 times.This game made me feel extremely nostalgic. Sure, I can reminisce on the past and all that, but to have me sobbing like a madman because of it... that's what makes this special to me. And to find myself crying from nostalgia, grief, joy or even laughter... this game does it masterfully. And the characters... wow. I absolutely adore all of them. Some I initially didn't resonate with, eventually grew on me with time (and hardship).While I personally didn't enjoy a handful of the mini game sections throughout the game, feeling they were clunky and/or half-baked, they added a charm to this game making it go beyond a typical visual novel experience. And the true ending may hit or miss with you, though I personally wouldn't call it a bad ending and felt satisfied with it.Overall, phenomenally written game that will resonate with anyone no matter the state of mind they find themselves in. Aside from a few minor gripes, this is still a phenomenal addition for visual narrative gaming. It is an experience that is unique, charming, soul-crushing (at times), and can even be life altering depending on who plays. Would absolutely recommend this game to everyone.

_childDocuments_.review: Mixed feelings on this one. For a game that involves waves a lot, it's funny that my opinion is also shaped like a wave: Low interest in the start, followed by a huge rise in quality in the middle, then crashing down to a fairly meh ending. ***VAGUE SPOILERS AHEAD***POSITIVES:-Despite some hiccups, the game is wonderfully written. Each character felt really unique and alive.-The art is really beautiful and has so much variety! It's a small touch but adding in lots of unique background assets and characters makes the world feel much more vibrant.-The music is good, never great but not intrusive either. Perfectly serviceable.-I love the texting feature, it's really nice to see the main character write something only to delete it, giving us a glimpse into what they really think.-Great sound design. Cities feel packed, classrooms feel chaotic. -Brilliant uses of the medium throughout. I was a bit disappointed at first, as it felt like this could have been a movie or a comic, but it uses the fact it's a game really well towards the middle. NEGATIVES:-Some visual glitches that required restarting the game. Only happened twice, but they were significant. -There are a bunch of mini-games sprinkled throughout the game. Some tie in nicely with what's happening, like playing carnival games or bike-racing with a friend. Most however feel way to random and just thrown in to make the game seem more interactive then it is. -There is a really strange design decision regarding the protagonist playing the piano. He practices throughout the game, but we only get to take part in a rhythm game of his song during the later stages of the game. It would have been much better to have us interact earlier, perhaps making the rhythm game harder when he is rusty and making it easier when he improves. Then, as he improves at the piano, we improve at the game. A perfect way to join gameplay and story. Instead, we just watch cutscenes of him practicing. -The game's story is unsatisfying. So many interesting plot points and mysteries are brought up, but only a few are resolved. Everything is rather ambiguous at the end which is fine in small doses but here it feels like they ran out of steam while writing the conclusion. I'd still recommend the game through, especially if you like character over plot and can ignore the threads that go nowhere. Maybe get it on sale though. 6/10

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 Buy this Filipino anime disguised as a video game.I'd normally give like a joking summary of the game, but I'd much rather you buy the game and play it for yourself so I'm going to copy paste the plot summaries of Your Lie in April, Anohana, and friggin Steins;Gate from their TVTropes pages before hitting you with the biggest spoiler joke of all timeso anyway SPOILERSKousei Arima used to be a Child Prodigy at piano. Winning many competitions and earning himself a name in the classical music world, he seemed to have a future that was bright, colorful and full of possibilities. However, after his mother Saki's death, his breakdown at a concert made him stop playing.Kousei, now in middle school, spends his days living in a monochrome world, having spent two years without playing piano but managing to live every day thanks to his friends, his cheerful neighbor Tsubaki and his best friend Watari.That is, until Tsubaki introduces him to Kaori Miyazono, a mysterious and beautiful classmate who plays the violin in a way he's never heard before, and that introduces colors into his world again.When a loved one dies — be it a friend, a classmate, a significant other, or a family member — it strikes a chord. Things change. Close friends drift apart. Some move on, and some stay firmly rooted in the past.The latter is what happens to Jinta "Jintan" Yadomi, a high school-aged Hikikomori. After the death of Meiko "Menma" Honma, Jintan and their four other friends — Naruko "Anaru" Anjo, Atsumu "Yukiatsu" Matsuyuki, Chiriko "Tsuruko" Tsurumi, and Tetsudo "Poppo" Hisakawa — begin to lose touch with each other and move on with their lives. Five years later, Menma's ghost pays him a visit, asking him to help her fulfill a wish. Just what that wish is, she doesn't completely remember, but getting the old gang back together is a start.Being a Mad Scientist is awesome. Converting your microwave so that you can send e-mails to the past? Awesome. Being stalked by a secret organization doing their own Time Travel experiments and dead-set on capturing or eliminating you? Not so awesome.Like many of his friends in the Akihabara district, Okabe Rintaro loves to tinker with different gadgets and inventions. However, he's taken this love so far as to declare himself a Mad Scientist who goes by the alias "Hououin Kyouma" and imagines himself fighting all manner of evil government conspiracies.One fateful morning — July 28, 2010, to be precise — he and his ditzy childhood friend Shiina Mayuri are attending a lecture when they discover the dead body of Makise Kurisu, a celebrated researcher. As they flee the scene, Okabe sends a frantic text message to his Playful Hacker buddy Hashida "Daru" Itaru... and suddenly everyone around Okabe blinks out of existence, only to reappear a moment later.Shortly thereafter, Okabe runs into a very-much-alive Kurisu, and Daru mentions a garbled text message he received one week earlier. Investigating further, the team of wannabe scientists discovers that by continuously modifying and upgrading their microwave, they've stumbled across the secret of Time Travel... or at least, the ability to send text messages back in time, which is a starting point, right?Unfortunately, they're not the only ones interested in time travel. A shadowy French research organization called "SERN" has been running their own time-travel experiments, and after they catch wind of what Okabe has discovered, they begin to close in, sending in their agents, the Rounders, to acquire the machine. Soon, Okabe finds himself truly living his chuuni fantasy, and it is far worse than he could have ever imagined — he must evade the Rounders and their unknown leader, FB, while fixing his grave mistakes and finding a way to save those he loves from a universe that seems intent on killing them, no matter what.Anyway now that that is out of the way, on to the spoiler cookies and message<3<3<3<3 MY MOTHER IS DEAD <3<3<3<3Edit: I made it through to the end of this experience.Still greatStill recommend itStop playing it after 10 hours just a warningIf you continue playing after 10 hours (or going back to previous moments because it's got that scene replay thing) you are going to be hyped up and depending on how you feel about Bait-and-switch, you'll probably either feel extremely satisfied or extremely let down like a fireworks finale ending on a fizzle instead of a bang you have got to be kidding me with that ending.

Very interesting and unpredictable story line, specially if you get all endings. And don't even get me started on the soundtrack, much like To The Moon it creates a deep connection between the characters and the songs they play, resulting in absolutely devastating dialogues without the need of any words.Would be a 10/10 for me if it wasn't for the ending sequence, I think that for the amount of suffering the story makes the player go through it would be more satisfying to have a playable, longer, more detailed and satisfying ending, specially regarding Nicole and Mark.An outstanding game overall, made me cry, made me relate... made me feel lots of things honestly. _childDocuments_.review: Never have I been hit with such a monumental narrative in which I was rendered helpless staring at the masterpiece I stumbled across.I saw the trailer for this game during the summer of 2024; saw the alternatively striking art style and thought, "This game looks fun," and thought nothing more about it as I shoved it in my wish list along with the rest of the games rotting there. An entire month after its release, and as my bored ass was scrolling through the Steam store, I find it again. And it was the best damn game I've played in my life.I don't usually play these "heavy narrative story games" or the "visual novel" archetype. When I look to play games, I tend to lean towards competition and multiplayer games with my friends. A single-player story game? That's completely left field for someone like me. That being said, I believe this game has the charm to entice anybody to give it a shot. Sit through the first hour, and I promise that you won't be able to turn back. Just trust me.The game is a bildungsroman where you, as the player, experience joy, heartbreak, and agony, but also hope like you've never experienced before. Time and time again I was hit with twists that wrung my heartstrings until there was nothing left to squeeze out. The friends you made along the way and the unique story telling made me feel like I've known them my entire life, like I grew up with them. This, along with the magnificent craftsmanship of the soundtrack, the colorful visuals, and the touching dialogue, made me feel immersed as if I were there myself, as Mark.The game focuses on the themes of trauma and guilt, mostly surrounding two main characters but affecting everyone around them as well. After all, each individual is a fleshed-out character with more than just two dimensions to their name (even though they are literally two-dimensional models 🙃). Guilt goes hand in hand with regret, but at the end of the day, some decisions we made in the past cannot be changed. But that's okay. I don't want to call it a "moral of the story" and render it down to a single phrase (because it just can't lol its so much more than that), but this is what causes personal growth. Humans were never meant to remain stagnant, but to grow and flourish from their pasts. The glorious thing about people is that they can share these experiences with each other and remember. Memories of the past were meant to serve us to become better people in the end. Memories, as bittersweet as they are, that serve us a mean slice of reality pie. If you've read your way here, I suggest you give this game a shot. I can't do the game justice—not as much as you playing the game yourself. For me, personally, I will genuinely never be able to play this game again because of how much it broke me. But until then...

_childDocuments_.review: This is what I mean whenever I say stuff like "Video games aren't just a genre, but a medium of art". A couple hours in and I'm already impressed by how much heart and soul was poured to this game. Until Then may have the visual novel tag, but it's nothing like the other VNs . Instead of clicking monotonously through text boxes and starting at blank stills on the screen, every moment is breathing with life, from the characters to the surrounding world; every text response feels deliberate and real, you feel immersed in a way that is only possible within video games. The pixel art is also masterfully drawn, like I said, it's definitely different and alot better than most VNs you can find out there.  All this and the character's aren't even voiced, I feel like watching "Robot Dreams" for the first time again, with how the themes are handled, how the world is crafted, how it invokes emotions that you never knew you had and how the characters are oozing with life and personality. It's definitely not your typical VN and just like Robot Dreams, is produced by an Indie studio. I can absolutely recommend this to people who aren't into video games and strongly recommend trying out the demo first. All in all, Until then deserves it's overwhelmingly positive rating and Polychroma Games should be proud of themselves for making games with such passion and love. Do yourself a favor and pick this game up.

_childDocuments_.review: ( full review with screenshots:  )It's pretty incredible that Until Then comes from a developer that has never released a game on Steam before and a publisher that many people have likely never heard of. It's far from the first amazing game I've played that got no pre-release fanfare and came from somewhere totally unexpected, but these sorts of games are supposed to fit a certain mold. They're usually only a few hours long and don't have the budget to do much more than what's absolutely necessary in terms of presentation. Until Then is as good as any of those games, yet it's also 20 hours long and packs an absolutely mind-boggling amount of detail into every scene. The result is something truly special. I'll get the one negative out of the way early: there are a lot of minigames here, and they range in quality from slightly quirky to nonsensical. This might have impacted my rating if the minigames had consequences, but as far as I know you can completely flub all of them and at most an NPC comments on how you did. Although I'm sure it would have been an even better experience if the minigames were more fleshed out, they didn't hurt the experience as is. It helps that nearly all of them have a story reason for happening, so you're getting dialogue alongside the gameplay instead of just playing a dumb flash-esque game to pad the runtime. Next, the art. It's hard to fully appreciate from the static screenshots on the game's store page. You can tell that it's great pixel art, but you can't see how much Polychroma was able to do with animation and dynamic camera angles. Even though most things are done with sprites, the characters and backgrounds are as expressive as most high-budget 3D games, which makes every scene feel that much more alive and allows for some excellent subtle storytelling. I've seen many games with unbelievably detailed pixel art backgrounds and static sprites, but none that come close to this when it's all put together. The dialogue systems are also impressive. These were apparently inspired by Oxenfree and Night in the Woods, which are two great games to learn from. It doesn't have the same depth of conversation trees that Oxenfree did, but it achieves a similar liveliness in its dialogues by varying the timing and presentation of your options and through great writing regardless of your choices. You'll also spend a lot of time talking to friends by text, where you'll often end up writing and deleting several messages before pressing send. It's a small touch that lets Polychroma show more of their character's personality while also making text conversations feel far more real. No one actually writes and sends the first message they think of every time, after all. Although this is ultimately a linear game, it also remembers a surprising number of the choices you make. You're not going to end up with different endings, but characters will call back to choices you made at important moments and sometimes even trivial things will have consequences. I was particularly entertained by receiving an angry message from a minor NPC whose picture I'd opted to share. It's a nice way of adding some player agency without needing to shoehorn in choices or endings that don't fit the characters. Of course, what you're really here for is the story. And look, even lower-scoring reviews of this game call the narrative a masterpiece. There's really no other word for it. It has a large cast, but everyone has a meaningful role, a unique personality, and their own believable motivations. The only games I can think of that realized their casts this fully are the Persona and Mass Effect series, but those had far more time to work with and were still full of less fleshed-out hangers on. I got truly invested in these characters and their problems, and that makes the story beats hit even harder. Still, probably the biggest compliment I can pay to the story is that I'd still be giving this a perfect score even if it had ended halfway through after the first time it shows credits. You get an absolute gem of a story only for the game to go "but wait, there's more!" and then get even better.
