_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Until Then is a 10/10 game that allowed me to reconnect with my thought-to-be-forever-lost Filipino identity. If you're Filipino, play the game. If you're not Filipino, PLAY THE GAME.I'm going through something of a cultural reawakening at the moment, and it's all because of this game.-----------------------------------------Until Then follows the story of Mark Borja, a teenager going to school in the Philippines as he navigates high school. Mark presents as lazy and unmotivated, for reasons revealed as the game progresses. He's joined by his childhood friends Cath (a pluviophile) and Ridel (an aspiring and apparently incredibly talented filmmaker) as well as a smattering of other interesting side characters. After a literal run-in with Nicole Lacsamana, a transfer student and refugee from a world-shattering event known as The Ruling, Mark's life changes and whether it's for better or for worse is something you'll have to discover yourself. Without getting into too much, both Mark and Nicole bond over what they've lost. Their connection is otherworldly, and I both loved and hated going through it.This game is many genres. It is romance, sci-fi, thriller, horror and mystery all at once. Its story takes you all over this fictional Philippines, circa 2014. Every character we meet has a role to play in the story and the ways they change as the game progresses feels organic, if a bit jarring in some cases.The art is spectacular, and there's a scene within the first 10 minutes of the game when you first meet Louise Ordunia where you'll wonder how in the hell they did that with pixel art. I highly recommend a play through.Playing through the game brought back visions of fireworks two feet away from my front door for New Years' 1995 (and 96. and 97. and 98. It's no wonder I need glasses and have hearing problems), the unbelievably steep wheelchair ramps in the hospital where my sister and I were being treated for dengue, running for my life from my batchmate's dad through the schoolyard after I accidentally tripped her into a massive mudpile, and the tears I forgot to cry when my parents told me our life in the Philippines was over.----------------------------------------Most people don't know that I struggle with my personal identity, because I don't often speak about it. I'm many things to many people; a son, a brother, a friend, (apparently) an inspiration, maybe even a nemesis or a missed chance to some. However, I don't really know what I am to myself.My family decided to move to the United States in 1999. We've been here ever since. In the time between getting on that plane as a 7 year old boy, forgetting the faces of my childhood friends, settling in America and trying to begin a new life, I lost a few things. I lost the life I thought I'd live forever, my faith in religion and, most crucially, my identity as a Filipino disappeared.My parents sped up mine and my sisters' fluency in English by only speaking to us in English as kids. I tried my best to keep Tagalog, but it didn't really work. I can still speak and understand a bit, however I'm a bit embarrassed to speak it when I'm around other Pinoys. My sisters don't speak a word, outside of familial honorifics (Nanay, Tatay, Kuya, Ate, etc).I was an awkward kid. Moving at such a formative age put me in a situation where I had to assimilate with the norm or be ostracized. "Alien" is simultaneously such a derogatory and appropriate word for immigrants. I wasn't able to return to my home, yet I belonged nowhere in this new and confusing world.Making friends was tough. I barely knew the language. I brought weird food to school for lunch. I got caught bringing cough medicine to school (I was afraid to take it myself so I asked my teacher to administer it and I got in trouble both with the school administration AND with my parents for getting in trouble in the first place). I wasn't familiar with societal norms and was expected by my peers to just know what music and TV was in.At times I felt like an animal in captivity, caged by my lack of understanding (of both the language and culture), being observed and ridiculed by a group who didn't know how painful it was to be on the outside. I WANTED to learn and become a part of their world, but it was probably too late.I did bond with a few people and that helped, but I mostly spent my time playing video games by myself. That knockoff Playstation 1 with 100 or so odd games was my best friend for most of childhood.I found food to be a comfort and a passion. My dad is an amazing chef, watching cooking shows and eating at restaurants (the few times we did) made me realize that food is a language everyone understood. So I decided to become fluent. When I was 10 years old, my identity began to mold into that of a chef. 20 years later, here I am.Sometimes I wonder what life was like for people who weren't sure of what they wanted to be as adults. I'm sure many of you can relate to the fleeting desires as children to be spaceship gunners, Power Rangers, iguana chiropractors or part of an official sandcastle demolition crew (seriously, what happens to sandcastles after you leave the beach?) I wonder when you decided on your path and what the catalyst was for that decision.In the 20 years between setting my career path in concrete and now, I never did reassemble my cultural identity. Fragments of it lay scattered about my personality, the gaps filled with anime, alt rock, awkward crushes and the fact I didn't learn how to ride a bike until I was 19. A few of you have heard me describe myself as "a white guy in a Filipino body." Sometimes I still feel that way.It wasn't until July 21, 2024 when I booted up this game for the first time that the pieces started fitting together again and I began to remember.-------------------------------------------------I was going through something painful when I began the story and it did help, if only to keep my mind off things. It began as a distraction for me, but towards the end it helped me sort through everything I'd lost and either make peace with it or clean up the jagged edges and add it to the stained glass mosaic of who I've become.Hi. My name loosely translates to "With the freedom and strength of an eagle, I fathom the depths." I am a chef, a son, a brother, a friend, an inspiration (apparently), a nemesis, a missed connection, an alien, a memory, a formerly aspiring iguana chiropractor and a Filipino. I also spent WAY too long writing this, and I bet half of it makes no sense. I live, love, mourn, celebrate, succeed, fail, and embrace my life with every fiber of my being.Most importantly, though. I'm trying my best. And I know you are, too. The lives we have now are the only ones we get. You'll never be able to do everything you set out to. The only thing you can do is experience as much as you can with the people you care about.I don't know why I spent so much time fretting over "finding myself." I realize now that who I am changes bit by bit with every passing day. I'm excited to meet tomorrow's me, and I know that 7 year old flying across the Pacific in my memories is too."Kung pwede akong gumising bukas at umpisa ulit, wala akong iiba.""If I could wake up tomorrow and start all over, I wouldn't change a thing."

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not sure how one even reviews a game like this. I suppose categories are the norm, but this one really needs a few custom-tailored categories because OH BOY is it ever unique.Do you like slice of life/literary fiction? If so, you can stop reading and play the demo right here. The story is an absolute masterpiece. It's got love, it's got friendship, it has problems everyone can relate to. It makes you wonder, leaves you doubting. It takes you on a rollercoaster ride properly, not just to happy-fun-rainbow-land or to grimdark-edgelord-world where it's all downhill for 20 hours straight. The story has twists and turns, the setting is unique but not unrealistic. I sure hope your excuse for still reading this review is "my internet connection is slow and the demo is not done downloading".Yes, these warrant their own chapter, because you will identify with one or more of them, the game will grab you by the collar and put you on the rollercoaster mentioned above. Every single one of them is well-written. If you think one of them is n-dimensional (where n is any number), I guarantee you're a dimension and several character traits short. No cliches to be found here.Gameplay of pure storytelling games is often deemed secondary at best. However, the devs of Until Then have added minigames, interaction with smartphone apps and simulated webbrowsing and various other tidbits that do so, so, SO much to add immersion that other games lack. None of it feels tacked on, all of it has a purpose, at no point did I feel that this should be a comic, movie or a book. Without the immersion (and consequences) that these interactive elements added, this just would not have been the same experience.The pixel art is lovely and a refreshing change from the samey stuff that "retro-inspired" games chuck at you. I love pixel art myself and even I'm sick of the same old tile-based top-down retro RPG style. Until Then not only has its own 2D style, it also has the best 2D-3D compositing I've seen so far, combining sprites with 3D environments and effects to make for breathtaking environments.If you like piano music, it's great. If you don't, sucks to be you.I draw the following conclusions:

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting visual blend of 2D sprites and 3D backgrounds, with some well composed shots, amazing lighting work and beautiful and fluid animation make this game an eye candy. It explores a lot of themes, some more than others, but there's enough of variety to get a personal touch and reach closer to majority of players in one way or another. Story leans towards much more grounded narrative and discussion of the topics present. It doesn't go with stereotypical catchphrases, nor you will find many memorable quotes. Much like the real world, some conversations are just that - a talk you must have and sometimes the most dull words get ingrained in your mind in an unexpected way. Grounded is the key word. This game plays crisis scenarios through the prism of the most common daily interactions, one of which is communicating through your phone and social media. This key feature turned out to be, personally, the most affecting form of narrative.Whether it's foreign to you or not, setting is not a random backdrop, featuring a lot of cultural aspects and symbolism it feels familiar in some ways, and equally relatable through your interactions with the world.This is one of the most lasting and least clunky indie game in the genre. Few, but strong dialogue options feel impactful. While minigames are generally mixed, they add variety. Same goes to little hidden objectives you can do throughout the game. It's optional, but a small notion that reminds you that it is, indeed, a game.This adventurous experience will last you 15-20 hours, depending on how fast you navigate the areas and read through dialogues.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a visual novel that's a long intricate exploration of dealing and moving past grief and loss with some very heightened stakes, and it's really touching in a lot of ways. Both in how it handles the above themes and how just straight up romantic it can get at times. It's all handled well and is quite the experience to play through. That being said I didn't find the story to be perfect, as it gets bogged down a little by the science fiction underpinnings they loosely incorporate and structure the game around, which can result in parts of the game feeling a little dragged out. Especially if you're familiar with these types of stories, you'll be able to predict a lot of the later story beats. But it's not a huge detractor at all. The game also looks really nice, I think the pixel art/3d blend done here works quite well. Occasionally I'd say they zoom in a bit too far on certain character's low res sprites, which ends up looking pretty goofy, but most the time it's done well. Some notably really nice work with the expressions of characters throughout, even the lowest res pixel sprites are extremely expressive in a natural way.And the stars of the show here really are the characters, they're all really likable and well-developed, and due to the structure of the storytelling you get to see them from all kinds of different perspectives. You really do end up wanting to save each and every one.The game is set in Indonesia after a large catastrophic series of natural disasters, and just like A Space for the Unbound (a game I'd say this game shares a lot of similarities with) it feels a bit like stepping into a time capsule. And just like in that game I found it very cool to experience that little very specific slice of culture. There's also something to be said about how just straight up cozy I found parts of this game, especially the early portions, a lot of scenes where the main character lies in bed at night browsing Facebook and DMing friends, lit only by the screen of his phone. This is probably just a result of me being around the same age as some of developers of this game but this is an experience I had a lot during that period as well and haven't really thought about since and all that just came rushing back. Try as you might nostalgia always gets you.So yeah, it's a good one. Easy recommend if you like a nice story/visual novel.

_childDocuments_.review: This work is... genuinely exceptional.This story depicts a path. A path which a lot of us are, were, will be on. A path many don't even realise they are on. This long and frustrating path called trauma.This path is confusing. We often think we have reached our poignant end with all those pesky loose ends tied up. And yet, there we are again, making the same mistakes, retreading the same stories. It feels like it gets worse every time. But is it really?This story caught me. Because I, myself, was stuck on this path. At a certain point I realised that this story is not just "relatable", it is me.Maybe I would have reached the end one day, found the answer myself. But it really means something that this work took me by the hand and showed me the ending that I needed to see. Showed me that all my work on myself was not for nothing.Every other statement others will make on this games quality in every other respect is true. It is probably the sole 'Interactive Fiction' game that manages to sit in a tier alongside Disco Elysium.But in terms of "effect on mental health" in a game. This game is, again, exceptional. It genuinely doubles as therapy.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay I just finished the game and wanted to share my thoughts about it.First, I had some hiccups when I booted up the game where the screen will be black and the game wouldn't load the next scene even when I hear the audio. I couldn't even change the resolution or even switch to full screen but as soon as I reached chapter 2, I encountered no more issues like that. I guess the issues occurred in the 1st chapter which covered the demo? I haven't played the demo since I want to wait for the full name but it might be the reason.Now, let's go with the game mechanics. This is an adventure visual novel where you get a number of interactions like the Social Media feed which I love and enjoyed since it pretty much resembles a typical Filipino social media feed (the typos, the memes, the roasting that happens). Sometimes you can like, comment and even click on news article and read the full article and no it's not just ONE article, you can read a number of articles! Talk about detail there. Not only that but there are also mini-games which kinda needed a bit more work since I had moment where I have no idea what I'm supposed to do.For the music, the music is amazing! I enjoyed it a lot! Would be nice if there's an OST that I could listen to because it's really good.Now let's really dive into the biggest factor for me: the story. I love seeing the references in Filipino culture given that I'm a Filipino myself and could relate. I could even hear Tagalog in the background and some texts in the game's background are in Tagalog. It would've been nice if I see more Taglish convos or heck, if the game has Tagalog as a selectable language. I think the banters in Tagalog will be livelier imo. Anyway, so the story resolves around the pain of losing a loved one and moving on from that grief. It's very relatable and if you're also living in the Philippines, you can also relate to the pain of having parents who work abroad. It's hard especially when you are so young when they had to go and work overseas so your family can survive and provide for your future (at the cost of not being around to see you grow up or not being around to celebrate special occasions together). The game did an amazing job in conveying those emotions through the lives of the characters. Each one of them have different ways of coping with pain, suffering, grief and I really love it. I couldn't help but cry in some parts of it because it hits home...A LOT.Overall, I'll give this game a 9/10. Aside for the tech issues and how the mini-game could use a bit more work, this is an overall solid adventure visual novel that I would highly recommend that you all experience. Oh and without spoiling anything, once you see the credits, DON'T STOP THERE. Continue and you'll see more the full picture that the games wants to tell you.Special thanks to the devs for such an amazing game and for giving me a key so I could play and stream it on my channel! It was a great honor and I've really enjoyed playing this from start to finish.

_childDocuments_.review: A month after finishing this game, I think I have gathered my thoughts enough to write a review.First of all: I highly recommend Until Then. From its characters and dialouge to the music and art style, the game does an excellent job at reeling you into its world. The cast each have distinct, loveable personalities, already existing bonds are presented well and new bonds are introduced nicely. It's a very neat atmosphere and very endearing.The game is mainly following the life of our protagonist Mark, done so by lots of reading that is periodically switched up by neat little mini games. The best comparison would probably be Night In The Woods. A majority of those mini games are rythm based, which ties into a huge chunk of the overall story. The story itself starts off slow, very slow even. Spoilers from here on out.We are introduced to the setting of a city in the Philippines, Mark's home town. Dealing with the aftermath of the  Ruling, a massive earthquake that destroyed several homes and lives, many families have evacuated to the city, among them a girl named Nicole, with whom Mark will form a complicated bond while both deal with their personal losses of loved ones. The overarching plot here is a strange occurence of people suddenly vanishing without a trace and memories being inconsistent. However, this train only starts its ride after starting your second playthrough, as the first one seems to be more dedicated to the characters and their relationships. This doesn't mean that the first playthrough has no significance however, as you, the player, will suddenly notice inconsistencies and changes between the two playthroughs very early on, which again, ties into the main plot. It's truly an interesting piece of writing that will reel you in further and further as you progress and more information is revealed. It builds everything up so nicely, things start escalating, the tension rises, so do the stakes. Everything is on the verge of falling apart completely, it kind of has already. And then, at the very end, it drops the ball. While everything ends up resolved, we never get a proper explanation as to why Mark and Nicole are the only ones truly aware of these inconsistencies and the threat looming over existence itself, why they are the ones that can somehow "fix" this situation (by literally holding eye contact???), or how the loved ones they've lost suddenly make an appearance as if they had something to do with all of it. I feel like it's implied the Ruling was also somehow connected on a higher level, but that isn't properly explained either, only that it gets worse the closer they get to fixing things. It may seem like nitpicking, and maybe it's supposed to be unanswered because it enters meta-physical levels, but I feel like that ending could have been better handled. Also, that final cutscene was a very rude spit in the face.The very end is my only complaint with the story however, the rest is fine. My other complaint is with the rythm mini games. Maybe my music-note-illiterate ass is simply too stupid for any rythmic feeling, but some of the mini games seem a bit inconsistent, mainly the coin game on the bus with is brutally precise timing and all of the piano arrow games, which in contrast have very lenient timings.Besides those points, the game is very great and you should play it.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't play visual novels, in fact, I don't know how I came across the demo for this game, but I'm so glad I did! Until Then has taken me on an emotional journey of self-discovery alongside the beautifully animated and written characters in a fascinating, and very real/relatable world. If you enjoyed the movie Your Name( and love to cry), this is the game for you! 💚 I'm about 5hrs in currently, and am bunkering down to finish what I started last night. Which is saying a lot, 'cause my backlog is almost around 450 games long on Steam alone!If you would pay to see a movie, you should pay to play this! 💚UPDATE: I just finished my second run and started my third. This game is life-changing. My soul is tired from the loss.. I don't want this to ever end, but I want it all to work out.. but I don't know if it can. I'm the kind of person who can't remember names, in life and especially in video games, but I feel like I remember EVERY character's entire family, history, tendencies, mannerisms, etc.. I feel like I'm going to need to convince my therapist to play this and like I need to study it and take notes on a full second run. It feels like I've lost friends, REAL friends, people I'm invested in. How did you do this?! 💚 💔 I'll comment below my final thoughts after completing this experience. So far my only criticism is that some of the mini-games are a bit janky, but I've definitely played worse.

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't quite as enthralled by this as the majority of reviews, although I would still recommend it overall, so if you're unsure my review might be of use.Until Then is at its strongest when it focuses on the experience of being a teenager navigating the world of instant messaging and social media. The multiple rewrites as you try and pin down the perfect response, the flurry of messages in a group chat as rumours spread, and walking the tightrope of flirting for the first time.That said, the script could definitely have used some tightening. A majority of scenes go on far too long, creating this pervasive sense of sluggishness in the narrative. There is a sci-fi side to this story, which takes a frustrating amount of time to be properly addressed, and lacks impact or originality when it does raise its head.Ten hours in I felt I understood most of what the game was trying to say, and yet the game took me 15-20 hours to finish.It's a good, not great, visual novel where your mileage may vary for lots of different reasons. Until Then undoubtedly has heart, endearing characters, and is the only game I've ever played set in the Philippines, which is definitely worth celebrating. It's just not without its flaws.

_childDocuments_.review: Until Then is a beautiful story about the struggles with friendship, family, and community, dealing with loss and abuse, and forgiving yourself. The game feels deeply rooted with the Filipino people and setting.I know it’s corny to say the game is making me think. But what this game is leaving me with is you’ll never fully understand somebody, but that’s part of understanding. All you can really do is try. The world hasn't ended yet.

_childDocuments_.review: Phenomenal Game!! First and foremost i just love the story, the music and of course the characters. As a Filipino person who plays the game, it's hitting every references here and there from local delicacies like fishballs, menudo, and of course the Lechon. To Buildings and everything the game has to offer like it brings back so memories when I was in highschool. i have learned a lot from the game, and it's been a while since the last time a game that really hit's deep in me that made my cry 9 TIMES!! And i think the storytelling relates to most of us Filipinos in a way that higher opportunity job is more important than the time you spent in your loved ones, and I think most of us Filipinos relate to this, mainly because we're so focused on a dream so longed that we forgot what's important to us.. and that is Time and Family. Mark Borja's story is so well written that I think most Filipinos working overseas are going to realize how deep the meaning of the game's story is, and I thank the developers for making it in the first place. Of course let's not forget about how well made the game's MUSIC!! it's if not by far one of the best music I've heard in a while ever since Life is Strange. Like no joke when the song hits, i just cried at every moment. Overall very phenomenal game and I hope the devs will continue to make games like these, and the only thing i don't like about the game is it's lack of voice acting, but it's not really an issue because i think the main point about silent characters is how the player's portray how they act and voice which makes the whole experience engaging and immersive. 10/10 Game and deserves GAME OF THE YEAR!!

_childDocuments_.review: 'Until Then' is truly a one-of-a-kind game. The intro, art style, narration, story, characters, music, dialogues, mini-games, and everything else were really impressive.After finishing the game, I felt like rain had washed over me. At first, I was caught off guard (especially because of the final scene) and soon felt the coldness of the rain. But then I was happy and content with how everything seemed to make sense. When it was finally over, it left me feeling a bit empty as well.Also, because of this game, I learned a few things related to the Philippines, such as: Tahanan means 'Destiny', Bagong means 'New', what Noche Buena is and how it is celebrated there, the fact that Gulaman is a Filipino drink, and as per Filipino myth, butterflies/moths are believed to be the souls of deceased loved ones who visit us. Well on a side note, it also pushed me into the rabbit hole of looking into double-slit experiments, quantum entanglement, quantum splitting, and such.Overall, this game has gifted me with a whirlwind of emotions and knowledge, while reminding me to hold close and look out for our loved ones, as well as not to hold onto things that are out of our control. Because to fully move forward, we need to cut loose all the ties from our past that are holding us back.I'm really glad I got to play this amazing and wonderful game. Kudos to the devs for creating such a masterpiece, that has truly left a spark. Looking forward to their next game.Totally recommends everyone to give it a shot. Side note: Just sit through the entire credit scene after the racing game, believe me it's only just the start.The world hasn't ended yet, so what are you guys still waiting for? Go and play this game rn.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm absolutely floored and conflicted at the same time. Been a while since a game made me feel so many different things, but I'll say that this is a game that everyone who's even remotely interested in narrative games should try for themselves -- so I'll surrender to cliché here and tell whoever is reading this to stop looking at reviews and just play the game. It's worth it.On one hand, the 'first act' is one of the best things I've ever played, hands down. I don't even know what to say to make it justice, I would just, again, urge everyone to play it and see for themselves. It's just an amazing display of writing and a cohesion of its themes that left me speechless at the end.On the other....I don't know how to feel about the story progression after that. I didn't dislike it and I respect how they stood true to its overarching themes up to the finale, but...I feel that maybe the story had already said so much in a brilliant way in its first act, that after that it strived to give a satisfying conclusion that never really reached the heights of those first few hours, especially since it was (understandably) more concerned with plot and getting somewhere instead of the laidback, slice of life-ish feel of the beginning. So I was left with an ending that gave me more or less what I expected of it, but still left me wanting.

_childDocuments_.review: I rarely leave a review on Steam but this game...is totally life-changing. I'm a sucker for emotionally damaging games; however, this one just broke me beyond fixing. Nothing could have prepared me enough for the story and the amount of tears wasted. I am literally wasted from crying so badly.This is a game about loss, grief, friendships, traumas, disasters, and dreams. If you're currently in dark places rn, PLEASE proceed with deep considerations and reach out for help.The game is beautiful in many instances:The story kicks off kinda slowly and many plots are placed as if the game is directionless; however, this is fully intentional. As the story goes on, everything becomes clearer and clearer, trust me, you have to see it to the end.Each character is unique and full of emotions. The flow of conversations is natural and not forced nor rushed.The total playtime is quite long, around 15-17hrs so please take a break whenever you need to. The minigames are enjoyable; however, some of them lack proper hints, making the experience quite unpleasant, but that should not be a concern. The art style and soundtracks are beautiful btw. The game broke me forever. It's hard to explain but as I was playing it, I couldn't help feeling related to what the characters were going through; in other words, the game really hit home. At some point, it really shows how fragile our lives really are and we could lose someone at any time without a warning. One of my favorite impactful aspects of the game is its ability to convey regret. No matter what we do or wish for, we would never know if what we did was enough or if there'd be anything else we could have done.... the game really got me thinking.Idk what else to say tbh. This is something you have to experience yourself and I believe my words are not enough to give this piece of art the recognition it deserves. However, to those out there who find themselves related to the story, and to those who are going through some dark times, I wish you all the peace you deserve. Although I don't know you, I believe you guys are the most beautiful people I've ever met and I hope you can have the strength to overcome...to live, and to be happy, again, and over again. I wholeheartedly believe in y'all.Please take care.
_childDocuments_.name: Until Then

_childDocuments_.review: If "5D Chess With Multiverse Time Travel" had a plot:This review focuses mostly on the ending of this work, where all elements discussed throughout the story are supposedly finely knit up in the end, what Until Then alas poorly accomplishes. Therefore, if one doesn't mind spoilers, it's recommended to read along shortly before buying it, or skip to the last two paragraphs.Overall the game would've been better without the Sci-Fi elements, but left just with a single route (maybe with multiple meaningful choices and endings, offering the player more agency, which is surprisingly lacking here) with all characters fleshed out better than this nonsensical multidimensional convoluted 5d chess. Less is sometimes (much) more, after all. Nonetheless, it still taught me many meaningful things throughout the journey, because of its themes of grief, friendship, passion, true love, trauma, forgiveness etc. (along the stunning graphics, albeit surprisingly silent for a story in part focused on music). In a sense, Life is Strange does all  that better though.Like suggested, the narrative follows like a kinetic visual novel, where your decisions don't affect the outcome not even in the short-term. Aside from some silly, pointless mini-games, you're just reading it, and one might as well do that through some walkthrough posted on YouTube.4/10. Let's discuss!

_childDocuments_.review: What a game this is! Okay, so I went into it expecting a mediocre visual novel with pixelated art, but this game is much more than that. I would dare call it a high-quality product; you can sense the attention to detail and care that went into creating it. It immediately got my attention, from the soundtrack, graphics, and art style to the characters and the fact that it simulates real-life social media to make it feel more relatable to our time. If you have ever played visual novels like Fate/Stay Night (Remastered version coming to Steam this year), Tsukihime, Witch on the Holy Night, Steins;Gate, and those types of games, you will like this one. I have no idea why, but personally, I like pixel art, and Katana Zero was probably one of the best games I finished last year (2023).I recommend this game to anyone who doesn't have brain rot and can appreciate good storytelling through TV, books, and video games. _childDocuments_.review: This game is such a wonderful experience from top to bottom! Your experience with the game greatly benefits from going into as blind as possible because you really don't know what direction it would even go. Each time I booted the game up I was fully prepare to immerse myself in it. The excellent pixel art really conveys so much about every character and every background character and the backgrounds were these beautiful 3D environments that just kept on giving. The game does something special with every other scene having it play a fully animated and cinematic scene, really emphasizing a characters emotion or showing a special moment between characters and those moments enriches the whole experience each time it happened. It is akin to getting a full FMV cut-scene in old JRPGs where it would change from the in-game graphics  to this beautifully produced CG cutscene. The story is so engaging, really going into some deep subjects about the connections you have with others and how tragedy can influence either take away, give, or enhance those connections. These characters are well written but most importantly FUN to be with! You get excited to see everyone the main characters sees because they all well designed, have distinguishable personalities, and again they are FUN characters. You definitely have a favorite. The game is a complete and wonderful experience that I feel will make anyone no matter how cynical or jaded feel something. I can not recommend this game enough. _childDocuments_.review: What a journeyWhat starts out as a teen slice-of-life interactive visual novel quickly devolves into a science-fiction roller coaster that, despite at times biting off more than it can chew, drew me in from the demo and never let go. It's like the game was tailored to my exact likes - piano, The Strokes, chess, pretty pixel art, Life is Strange-esque vibes... I thoroughly enjoyed it!I will admit that it's at times too sappy and the logic of the science fiction isn't consistent and by the third act becomes straight up confusing, but in suspending the science behind it and pretending that what the characters are talking about is sound, it's a really good story that above all else emphasizes friendship, accepting failure, learning how to understand one another, and facing the fact that you aren't in control over everything in your lifeSure the dialogue gets a little mushy at times, but if you knew how much I berated YA fiction, I was, on the whole, very much in tune with the dialogue. The characters were lovable (who wouldn't want a Nicole in their life?) and the story was tender. It takes a unique spin on time travel () and goes on for quite some time, much longer than I was anticipating for a game of this caliber. Feels were felt in every act and the ending was very bittersweetI highly encourage you to try out the demo and if you are even a little bit enticed to buy it without hesitation. What a lovely, lovely adventure

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games ive ever played. The Great: The visuals are fantastic and so emotionally driven. With great pixel and anime art. Some of the backgrounds in this game are so beautiful that i will remember them for the rest of my life. I love how the game transitions from anime to pixel and it really added alot of emotional impact on story moments. Game is also really well animated with every character having different animations which add alot to their personality and to the games artistic presentation. Music is amazing. As a classical music enjoyer their were alot of pieces that i recognised and that made alot of the scenes better. But theirs also a good amount of original music in this game that is mind blowing. One of the best OST's this year handsdown. The game is mostly a visual novel with interactive scenes. But there are some minigames that are inspired by other minigames in games. While they dont do alot for the game, they do a good job being "mini". I also really like how one of the minigames had tons of narrative put into it. Having the player play at certain scenes really added alot of emotional impact and immersion. Characters are fantastic. You will have tons and tons of experiences with them over the game. You will love them and hate them for tons of reasons. But at the end of the day you will understand as to why you feel this way. Characters are really good because the writers really understand how teenagers act and talk. I really enjoyed the great instagram social media stuff aswel as the really great story moments of texting. The writers understood how texting can be used as a great tool for dialogue and i loved how they explored it in the game. I really enjoy romance and there is a great romance in this game. I also really like the Bi and Gay representation in this game. A small warning for spoilers. But their is a paranormal part of the game. I usually dont enjoy when paranormal/scifi stuff is put in games like these. But they really pulled it off well. They integrate it almost perfectly into the story. Cause its not just paranormal stuff, it actually ties back to the characters. It feels really human, and natural, dispite it being very disturbing and weird at times. Also + points for making me ugly cry during the ending. The Meh:While i think that the story is excellent and almost perfect. Some parts of the games pacing is weird, expecally the middle part of the game. While i do feel like it reinforces what your going through and the mystery of the game, it does feel a bit too redundant. There are also some characters that i adore, that just needed a small amount of more exploration of their personal lives. Cause it feels like their a little to underdeveloped for some emotional moments to really hit. This is more of a nitpick since i dont think it actually ruined anything for me, but it might for others if they didnot really connect to some of the characters. Some of the sound mixing in this game is not good. Their are ambient sounds that are louder than things that should be at the forefront of the sound. This ruins some of the immersion in scenes.Controls are a bit weird. Some of the game requires you to press a certain key or button at certain times, but its theres no prompts so you consistently spam your controller or keyboard, losing the immersion of the scene. Overall, this is one of the best games ive ever experianced. I will remember it for the rest of my life. I adored the characters and the story enough to make me cry. I love the music and the beautiful art. While it has some slow moments and some bad design, i do think that those moments get heavly overshadowed by the amazing parts of the game. So its a 10/10 for me, i think any game that can i get me to cry and be this emotional over it deserves to be crowned as a 10.

_childDocuments_.review: To start off, I really wanted to like this game. The trailer entices you with a deep story that will leave an impact on you, and the art style is beautiful. The story however is disappointing to say the least. At its best, each character has a story to tell, one that's fleshed out and with themes that are relatable to many. At its worst the overall narrative does nothing to tie these characters together. They all mostly feel like separate things happening all at once, resulting in multiple climaxes in the story, presenting pretty bad pacing issues and even unresolved story arcs. . The character interactions are pretty fun though and discovering their backstories and motivations was a nice experience. Its just that there's nothing holding it all together so the story as a whole lacked cohesion. Even the whole science mystery plot needed a biiig suspension of disbelief to follow, and for the first run it barely even fit into the narrative. Gameplay wise its a pretty fun, fairly linear visual novel with some branching dialogue options that give different reactions from the characters. Overall though I don't think the options change the story in a meaningful way as things feel like they are set to happen. The social media aspect was pretty interesting as you discover world events by scrolling through your phone and texting your friends. The mini-games though felt gimmicky, and a bit out of place, like they were put there just to have mini-games in place. Overall its an ok experience. Not great, not terrible either. It has a fairly strong hook at the start to get you into it, despite the unlikable protagonist it still had me curious about the rest of the story. I only wish that the overall narrative was more cohesive because the characters were pretty well written. Its definitely a nice game to try if you want to, but its not the best I've seen, nor is it a story that would stick with me forever.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first time in my life for 25 years, bawled on a story of a game. We don't live a lavish life and we have bills to pay so he took the opportunity to work abroad to provide us livelihood. Luckily, my mom is a housewife so she's with us all the time but, I know being a housewife alone and raising 2 children is not an easy feat. Life ain't easy back then (even today) that's why I treasure all those moments we had and have, Be it good times, bad times and sad times, We live through all the hardships together. That sheet hits hard, man. Just like my mom always said that she'll support us to pursue our dreams, and like last month when she told me that her dream was for us to finish our education (totally a Filipino parent dream), both me and my younger brother and that's a huge achievement for her. I was truly happy when I heard that and now only my brother needs to finish his Uni and my mom's dream would totally be fulfilled.Overall, I thought this was only just a game about the life of a Filipino high school boy but, damn I was wrong. _childDocuments_.review: This review won’t contain spoilers.When I first saw the Steam page for this game, watched the trailer, and saw a few pictures, I thought it was going to be a high school story, something cute to make my day better.I was very wrong. There are many, many more things to this game. Many topics, many characters, many stories. And they all feel so real. I’ve never felt like I was watching human beings talking in a game before. I’ve never felt like I was watching people living their lives in a game before.If you are, yourself, someone who has been through life, through high school, through love, through friendship, through grief, through change, through pain—there will be at least one topic that will make your heart sink, that will bring tears to your face, that will make your skin shiver.I cried so many times that I just stopped counting at some point. I got angry, I got scared, and all the other times when my emotions weren’t playing with me, I had a huge smile on my face.I don’t know how else I can convince you to play this game, but I’ll tell you that in every life I may live, I’ll take the opportunity to play this game again.

_childDocuments_.review: It is inconceivable to write how this game is the most indicative piece of media surrounding everything we stand for individually and collectively. There are many ways you could praise this game as shown by many other reviews here. But, I want to offer a unique perspective on things to show how immaculate of an experience this was for me and many others if you are contemplating getting this game. I believe the more you have lost, the more you will gain from this game. My favorite game for 4 years up to this point was Celeste. It marked my determination in this world. Practically nothing could beat it. I've played so many games over the years indie and triple AAA. Oneshot, Hello Charlotte, Omori, Crosscode, Elden Ring, Library of Ruina, Night in the Woods, and so much more. I love video games so much and the ones that are most dear to me are the ones I resonate with and most importantly, change my life. Celeste changed so much about me I'm forever thankful for it for what it meant to me then and now.And just 8 ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hours into the game, it toppled Celeste as if it were a mere disposable pawn on the chess board. Less than half of the game. It's unreal how easily it did such a thing. I knew Celeste wouldn't stay there forever, but this game resonated with me so much you could convince me that future me developed it and sent it back to the past for me to play. I relate to, no, I am so many characters in this game. All the themes the developers wanted to showcase are fully fleshed out in a way I couldn't ever imagine, not even mentioning the very unique story structure I couldn't predict where we were heading next in the best way possible unlike most media nowadays I experience. I've always known people's favorite games will always be the ones that are most personal to them whether in the specific moment of life or resonating with oneself's past. But it isn't a hyperbole at all to say this might be the best game I will experience for the rest of my life for how it coincided perfectly with the current state of affairs I've gone through and will go through in the future. Hell! Maybe a candidate for the best video game ever created which is something I would've never considered for any game till this one. I eagerly wait for how this game will lead my future with how it's affected me. I cried so many times to this game than perhaps the latter half of my life. And I savored every second of it smiling underneath it all.Please buy this game if you have the slightest consideration for it. Whether it becomes your new favorite or not doesn't matter. But it will certainly make you cry. It will make you learn something anew about yourself. And that's okay.Until then, the world hasn't ended yet. We'll do this together.

_childDocuments_.review: A twisting narrative game that takes you on a journey through the lives of a group of Filipino teens navigating their complex trauma and grief. I adored the characters and their presence each carried with them, often times it felt like greeting an old friend when one entered a scene. I loved the art and the lighting used to bring the scenes together, the use of lighting and scenery to speak just as loud as the characters themselves.I am somewhat disgruntled by the ending, I will do my best to remain spoiler free. You see the narrative weave and can see things shaping out a certain way, you hear the message that the game is speaking to you and you feel your chest tighten because you know what is to come and how this story will end. And it does end and it does deliver on the message its giving you but not in the way you may have expected. You feel cheated. Everything you worked to fix, the trauma you waded through to get here and the effort you put forth feels hollow. It is not the perfect story book ending. Everyone ends up happy but there is still a missing puzzle piece. We can see it missing and we have to accept that if we keep looking for that last piece even though it is truly lost to the ephemeral then we will never be able to appreciate the picture we have made regardless of its imperfection. I wanted a different ending but this is the ending that needed to happen, and I have to accept that.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite this game only being released in a short amount of time, it actually helped me properly grieve over a friend.  have to say that this game actually helped me grieve. Spoilers ahead.Hi, I'm Ardit I'm 19 and live in the US. When I picked up this game I expected it to be just a simple romantic or heartfelt, slice of life game. But I did realize i was wrong. As I ventured throughout the game I felt like Cath was similar to someone I knew which she was. I had a friend her name was Finn. Me and Finn used to be close but as we grew up and moved away it became less physical but we still would obsess over eachother online. Our playful banters, subtle but heartwarming arguments. Much like Cath, Finn too had her own family troubles but she was very dismissive on it, would always same "same old" or "it's nothing new really I'm used to it" even a "don't worry about it" every now and then. One notable date was 2 days after my 19th birthday on December 5th, 2023 had I realized something was wrong. So I messaged them. It took a few days but I would message them memes, asking if they're okay. Until I saw on her Instagram account it stated "remembering" which is given to users that passed away. I didn't believe it at all until I asked one of her close relatives which they informed me she had taken her own life.I crumbled I couldn't believe the news because I couldn't believe that they would do that. So I chose to ignore it, chose to believe she was out there.But after playing this game, I saw myself in Mark. I saw how devastated he was losing Cath. And going through denial on his inability to change anything. After playing this game I for the first time in a year I was able to grieve Finn. Since I saw her fit Caths role so much. I grieved hard and I still am. I lost sleep, haven't ate well in over 5 days. Y'know people always say "they would want you to move on" and that I'm hurting myself but what people have trouble to understand is truly getting over on how it feels losing someone so unique, sweet and important. How they were your light, the only thing that could make anything joyous and all the sudden have it lost and taken away from you feels horrible. It's such an unfair feeling that you stop caring. It's like an odd mix of being selfless and selfish at the same time. I was stuck chasing after Finn and trying to deny the truth that I lost myself. In a way i never stopped blaming myself. I was saying the exact same words Mark was saying. "I wish I could've talked with you more" "I wish I was a better friend". But it was during the ending I felt like I was seeing words I wanted to be said to me. How I had to let go. How I had to stop punishing myself. Stop going back forever and to stop ripping my heart out because of something that was never in my control. The ending actually had me turn off my computer and take a walk to cry. I'm grateful for this game. Despite my favorite games Halo, and Cyberpunk along the list of other childhood games, this one tops everything. And it will officially hold a place in my heart. Thank you to the devs at PolyChroma studios.

_childDocuments_.review: someone mentioned here that the "endgame" was confusing, lackluster, and made no sense.in my opinion, i think it's very intentional, and as someone who was a stark hater of "Tails: Noir" or originally known as Backbone when i purchased it day 1 and played the 2020 demo, i can safely say that there is a strict difference between intentional conflictive story-writing and unintentional conflictive story-writing.spoilers aheadthere is a juvenile perspective to all of it, which creates that sort of supernatural feel towards it because the characters are still children, just barely 15, 14, or 16. they don't have experience with anything nor do they actually have answers for it, and refuse to seek help, believing it to be some sort of phenomenon within a world that has seemingly gone mad.these juvenile perspectives, thoughts, aspirations, ideas - they all create that sense of "something strange is going on here" when in reality it is all purely coincidental and its rather a demonstration of the idea of adolescent egocentrism that many psychologists have discussed. as teenagers they believe whatever that is out of the "norm" that occurs to them can really be a happenstance of maybe their life is interesting or special, when in reality as it was proven here: it isn't.the endgame is the culmination of these ideas the story presents. as us, Mark, reels and tries to recover whiplash from every discovery and theorem he gets from Louise that might be true, it's reality that crashes them back down to simple overthinking and child's imagination. it's in a strange position that we find ourselves when that very idea and obsession with it sort of causes the death of the most beloved best friend one could have. it's a selfish and evil thing to suggest that Mark's egocentrism that created his paranoia and overprotectiveness, fueling his hysteria and panic attacks that he's clearly experiencing throughout the story. however, this is the brisk deduction i've come to after just now finishing the game and piecing the pieces together without properly digesting it.in that short summary, the more we began focusing inwards to what we felt and thought, the more the world seemed to unravel around us and the less answers we found. they only got worse as the game progressed, only easing when we THOUGHT we had an answer or an idea, crashing into panic when that was debunked once again to disappoint. denial was a strong subject in this game, and we lived in denial for the entire game - even after attempting to deal with Mom's death and our grief after.the game demonstrated such confusion as more and more questions came abroad even after we thought we conquered our denial, our guilts, our fears. and this caused an even bigger reaction from Mark as the person who had his back all game was being threatened- in his mind, threatened- by a threat that never existed. when you thought you pieced it together after suffering, wouldn't you fall into a frenzy when it all came crashing down in front of you?it's a butterfly effect that ends in the death of Cathy, a character we've all come to enjoy and who had our backs throughout the entire story whether she needed to or not. after all, had we just wondered where she was, maybe tracked her down without feeling like she would die if we weren't there, our presence just in that moment had caused the very thing we sought to prevent. and it's in credit due to the motivation that we were somehow protectors against the supernatural, the inhumane, the unexplainable. we believed our brisk, irrational plans and reactions would somehow prevent these tragedies from occurring when it is in fact nature. and in this discovery of fighting against nature we are crashed back down to earth by watching our beloved best friend die to our irrationality as childrenin short, great game, amazing story writing, and it really captured the panic and uncomprehending reality that some of us can never "understand"and this game is only about understanding each other, each other's perspectives and how we present ourselves is not a reflection of how our life truly is behind closed doors. to move is to understand, clarity is understanding, and Mark finds his peace and his realization through this. he only ever seemed to be unable to stop running and panicking when he fought against it. now, as he matured and grew, he finally realized it. what he realized to himself, i am unsure, but i know what i understood and interpreted with the story and message it gave to me.goated game, one of the best stories ive ever had the pleasure to follow along with(the understanding just might be the motivation of life- that spark)

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game.It's a visual novel. The visuals and atmosphere are great. But what about the novel? The writing is just... not enough. The characters don't feel real enough, the friendships not convincing enough. Which sucks when the game is trying to make you care about said characters losing said friendships. So many background details and plot points are left unaddressed - for example, Mark leaving Cath at the fair. This is never directly addressed and we don't get to hear her feelings about it apart from her immediate reaction.These sorts of games usually shine at making you feel something. And I did feel very distressed about these kids' living situations, I'll give the game that. But nothing about the writing itself, about how those scenes played out, felt very impactful by itself. I was sad because it's a Sad Story TM, not because I felt like I really got to know these characters. (The opening is the worst example of this, because it happens before we even see the characters, so it just feels extremely cheap.)Also, this is more of a personal thing, but I'm getting tired of "dead girl/woman playing the piano inside a white void" as a Sad Motif TM. Still, it would've been fine if the music itself was good. Which, well....... art is subjective, but the supposedly emotional melody felt incredibly generic to me.Will update this review after I find the motivation to play the true ending.

_childDocuments_.review: I’m a curious gamer since the demo, tried it & wanting for more then my fellow enthusiasts 🇵🇭 in various sites in the internet like FB & YT have compared this to Space for the Unbound, an Indonesian indie masterpiece 🇮🇩 & I played that till the end. It was beautiful but also short but sweet. Until Then I was hoping it would be as good, finally this Philippine upcoming hidden gem 💎 has been released, Until Then! Pun intended. Like Mark, this is my crammed PowerPoint presentation report on Until Then by Polychroma Games on Steam (Very strong & memorable intro btw😂):Story 📖 ❤️: You are Mark Borja, a typical above average Filipino High School 🏫 that loves his friends as much as he loves his games 🎮. As dialogues progresses you encounter notable new characters that will play greater & switched roles later on (No spoiler). Overall it reminds me of my High School days in the Philippines albeit in the modern era with modern technologies like an actual smartphone for reading Facebook & each post’s comments, usual articles you scroll down to, & of course messaging your friends not to mention transportation like the LRT (In contrast to the 90s era of Space for the Unbound but still some things stay the same over the years like the Jeepney & Bus fairs, annual Carnival🎡 or Peryaan & of course the signature Dishes.) Like a Netflix series, it’s about the slow build up in the beginning therefore it’s a slow pace start that leads you to a much desired satisfying slow burn when you reach 2/3 of the game when everything will both make sense in a thematic level & wont make sense in a mystery kind of way but it will get clearer & clearer as you play the game more & more. I continued my progress from the early demo so I cut 2 hours of dialogue & mini games & I fear for the worst that it’s going to be a short game now thanks to that but luckily the devs have greatly extended the story!Update: I saw some reviews only playing the game for 4-6 hours so I think they only got the first non canon ending. If you beat the game once please please 🙏 hit continue after the credits rolled for the love of all gaming canon & satisfactory experience! You just gotta push through no matter how hard & emotionally provocative each scenes gets. The true canon ending is truly more worthier than the first one. “Nothing worthwhile comes easy”, “You can do this💪”, “The World hasn’t ended yet🌍!”Gameplay 🎮 💙: Straightforward dialogue interactive visual novel that tells the everyday life on Mark as he talks to his friends & classmates daily to reach new developments. In some scenes you select dialogues that’ll have some impact in some details later on (No spoilers). It’s subtle but effective true to its mystery genre. For the mini games it could be a bit better but like living there they couldn’t have interpreted more accuarately  since really everything there is really that simple from the fishball sticking to the annual fair games to the piano 🎹 mini game reminiscent of DDR or if you change the controls to left, down, A/X, B/Circle then DJ Max & even my surprise a Jeepney Fair Passing minigame! When I finish the demo way which is 1/3 of the first playthrough I distinctly remember commenting & wishing for multiple endings at Polychroma’s YouTube channel & they delivered , albeit in a linear fashion, but still very effective in presenting everything what the game has to offer with no stone unturned except those little details you missed & mini games that you have to get trophies 🏆 for.Music/Sound FX 🎼 🎹 🤍: The music is subtle but effective in creating moods in the scenes like Space for the Unbound. Added with Mark’s naturally calling for being a Pianist & we have a setlist of orchestral goodness. The background noise is so surreal like you’re really there🇵🇭 from the loud Jeepneys of Manila, Tricycles, Manong Taho shouting to attract customers, school atmosphere of students chatting & bells ringing (If my memory serves me right & not have lived in a Mandela Effect Alternate Universe Manila, Philippines) its so unreal hearing them in a 2.5 pixel art game!What to expect?🔎 🦋 💛: It has the same charms of Space for the Unbound mixed with Re: Zero theme for trying again & never giving up (which is funny cause I finished the game & got the Accept & Let Go achievement trophy😂) & set in the Pixelated Modern Manila, Philippines🇵🇭. Hope that helps visualizes the gist of it without spoiling. As for the juicy stuff it will come during 2/3 of the game. I won’t spoil it cause going in blind is the best way to go for full immersion in which the mystery of the story will unravel through your eyes little by little. Let’s just say “The more things change the more they stay the same” & vice versa. Like Space for the Unbound it’s all about healing❤️‍🩹 with your friends via the Power of Friendship & of course theres always bit of drama 🎭 which only amplifies the story & experience. It’s a must play for indie enthusiast, home sick Filipinos like me, a fan of interactive visual novels & mystery sci-fi stories in general. I love it. Mabuhay, Polychroma Games you’ve won my pixelated Red, Blue, White & Yellow heart❤️ 💙 🤍 💛 🎊 🥳  & remember: “Misunderstanding is the first step to Understanding” this surprising mystery of a hidden gem game! Thanks for reading.

_childDocuments_.review: Playing this game is like having testicular torsion but having the wildest things for CBT. You know playing it's going to be excruciating, but the game is masterful at getting you so emotionally invested that you cannot stop.Both the art design and music is beautiful, creating such an immersive experience. The story is one of the most wrenching yet marvel in interactive fiction, creating such an amazing character drama with a intriguing sci-fi mystery. The dialogue is witty with constant bickering, however heavier moments have such a realistic tone that makes these characters feel truly human. The game was very unique way of building its world, letting the player delve as deep as they want using the protagonists phone with the over world having some hints as well.I have a few qualms. Some of the mini-games presented were cute and fun, while some others felt like a chore you have to complete before getting back to the story. The ending to this game is quite unsatisfactory if you prefer stories with everything explained and relatively uncomplicated.Overall however, this is probably one of my favourite games to come out in a while. Seeing the dynamics between characters and witnessing their struggles was extremely compelling. The game excels at making you see into each characters personalities, struggles and motives. This game truly cannot be explained without playing it yourself. if you enjoy story games, do not pass this up.

_childDocuments_.review: Until Then is a touching narrative driven game with substance to match it's expressive style. There's something innately human about the characters, whether it be the animation, intricate sprite-work or the lovingly crafted and highly accurate portrayal of being in a whatsapp group chat at age 15 (Typos and all), and it's the first time a "coming of age" story has been able to resonate with me so strongly, with themes that are at times uncomfortably close to home.It confidently delivers stunning, often abstract visuals, yet exercises appropriate restraint with the more sombre or thoughtful scenes, often opting for a more diegetic ambience of the world around the characters. In terms of the interactive elements, I would say for the most part this game is an visual novel. There are decisions that can be made that can alter dialogue in an intrinsically pleasing way, but ultimately still follows a very linear path regardless. What interaction is there is a good fit for the narrative, and does offer some fun alternative chit-chat depending on your choices, but I would advise against going into this expecting a VLR/Somnium Files experience. If anything you could argue the game may have benefited a little from dropping some of the interaction that is there. While lovingly drawn and presented, each mini-game is rather simple and mechanically dull, and runs the risk of adding frustration to an otherwise seamless experience. I think in its current state, it may be worth introducing an auto-play for such events, because the effort to create them shouldn't be discarded, but could perhaps be made less distracting for those who get no enjoyment from them outside of the connected story beats. Thankfully these games are sparse, so it's only a small mark (hehe) on an otherwise well put together work.In summary I wholeheartedly recommend Until Then, and hope that anyone reading this considers giving it a go. The demo does a fantastic job of giving you a vertical slice of the overall experience, and will allow you to carry your progress forward if you choose to purchase the full game, so there's no reason not to try it out. Now excuse me while I go back to my cave until another game comes out that makes me want to bother to write something like this again (20 years maybe idk, I think I did a meme one about sonic last time, I would say I don't even remember doing it but that wont hold up in court).

_childDocuments_.review: "Until Then" is a unique game with a great price point (especially when on sale). There are some aspects I loved, but some I didn't. Story:The storyline is engaging. A bit all over the place, but engaging. I tend to miss obvious foreshadowing or plot points, and I had an idea of what was happening with many characters early on. So it was probably a bit predictable for most, but predictable isn't bad if the story is good.Social media/Texting:You have the option to browse through websites, engage (Like, comment, share) with posts, read articles, navigate profiles, and message people. The presentation of this is really well done, I appreciated how believable it was, like genuine conversation and comments that you would see on Facebook. Probably my favourite part of this game is how the news and social media is handled. You can spend as long as you'd like doom-scrolling and reading what the websites have available to you at that time (has different posts and comments available at each engagement with social media, however, all previous articles will be available to read in the future along with the new articles). When you share or like things, this is occasionally noticed by other characters (mostly in the earlier chapters). This is actually quite funny the first time because almost everyone has something to say about you sharing their posts (and some about liking their post). Gameplay:This game is leaning more towards a visual novel than an interactive game. It's fun to play and make choices, but as the game progresses, it feels like you have progressively less agency over your decisions in the game. Chapter 3 was mostly dialogue heavy and almost a bit annoying as a result. The game honestly did such a great job with the social media aspect and agency over own choices early on, that the removal of agency in elements such as who to talk to later on or how you spend your free time is more noticeable than if there wasn't any at all. Mini-Games???:The mini-games are cute in theory, but are played out like a BIG afterthought. Excluding piano, nothing is repeatable. It's done once and you move on and never engage with it again. I would almost prefer to not do them at all, considering there's no prep for these mini-games that appear (1) time aside from the piano, which I'm going to be honest, is a bit obnoxious. I practiced it because I enjoy rhythm games, but it's appearance was so late into the game that it felt redundant. Why is my character playing like ass the night before the audition, simply because I'm not used to the rhythm game? There should be build up with this game from easy songs all the way to the audition song throughout the game. Characters: Fun, enjoyable characters. They're not perfect in presentation and have a good range of emotions. Their stories are fairly transparent, especially the core three of Mark, Cathy, and Ridel. A lot of character specific story getting dropped on your lap near the end with little to no prior engagement with it is a little jarring. It still makes an impact even if you saw it coming, as you've likely grown to like these characters. That said, you don't get to really process these feelings you have around their own life because it's what feels like 5 minutes from the credits rolling (a bit hyperbole but it isn't very far from the end). I thought there would be more interaction with other classmates. Some classmates that are spoken about a lot rarely make an appearance.  Although this is an indie game, so I can't be too grumpy about the name dropping just to fill the classroom and realism of it being actually a high school learning environment. I really was hoping to engage with Jaggy more outside of his social media posts, though (and some others for fun value, but Jaggy could have had a whole story arc to himself).Now, my criticism is quite wordy, however, overall- this game is really good to pick up. Again, it's an indie developer with a great price, a good enough story, and lots of ways to feel immersed into the world. Especially if you poke around the social media and news. That aspect really made this game amazing for me and I wish more games would implement that layer of depth in more games with a modern setting. Because of that, I wished for more from it than I probably should have. I look forward to future titles. Overall rating:7 fish balls out of 10

Considering it's hard to come by a very pleasing yet emotionally damaging game. NOT TO MENTION, this being made by Filipino Game Developers in the Philippines in which work of art and act of creativity is often left in negligence, which sucks as Filipino artists are really talented in which ever since, I enjoy supporting them.So, how do I start off? This game emphasizes loss, grief, friendship, psychological trauma and natural disasters. There’s one important theme… But you’d have to play the game for yourself to see and find out about that one particular theme, as it is really impactful. I would say, just continue on playing till you’re satisfied with the conclusion.The story… I won’t spoil it, because playing it the first and last time will make your experience memorable as this game is full of emotions. One thing I REALLY LOVE are the characters. I’m a sucker for characters who have unique stories of their own, because that’s the backbone of their character development and how they’ll be impactful to the story, you just gonna add a bit spice of their struggles to make it really flavorful for the player to enjoy.. Or maybe to break them. Visually, I love 2.5 Perspective and I think 2.5D is an underrated perspective for most games. The use of pixelated style makes it intriguing to the right theme to what this game is going to be, and it's a go to choice for most indie developers and yet detailed. I’m happy seeing the typical Filipino places, such a jollibee, bayad center, DHL but more altered since of course. To avoid copyrights. :] The music, simple yet impactful and not too overcomplicated. Just right for a really impactful game. After all of that, how do I feel now? The story, the characters, the visuals and the music, they deliver hard and… It made me cry. This game literally broke me and was truly heartwarming at the same time as I cannot comprehend what I’m feeling after finishing the game in the first run, as I take that minute of break just to process everything. I think the word Regret is the strong suite to what this game is all about.Just enjoy the people that you love and cherish truly around you, because nothing can replace them.

You just have to experience it for yourself. If you struggle with anything in your life at this moment, I strongly recommend that you play Until Then. _childDocuments_.review: This game...well, I didn't think id like it because I'm not always a sucker for visual novel-type games. After all, it's a slow burn. and this game had a slow burn, but...I was curious to understand, read, and interact. I went in blind, not knowing the entire plot, and it was a little confusing at first, but I understood it, and there were parts that made me cry because it felt natural to me. it felt like a living diary of sorts. I understood how the main character felt, and the twist got to me, and I cried hard. The emotions were captured well, and the plot was long, but the endings made me want to do another play-through. I wasn't satisfied; it was bittersweet, inspirational, upsetting, and accurate. Only some things will go how you want them to, but it's a constant reminder that you're not alone; talk to people and connect. This may not be some people's tea, but that's okay. I enjoyed this game regardless, `the music is lovely, and the visuals can be a little bit rocky at times with the sprites, but despite that, the subtle changes in their faces does change the scenario.That got to me because I find it difficult to speak, and this game really brought it up. I knew I didn't feel alone in this feeling, so thank you for making and sharing this game and for giving me that closure I needed regarding emotions.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, it's so rare for me to get fully absorbed in a narrative-driven game like this. Usually, I'm the type to get bored and lose interest pretty quickly. But Until Then has been a total exception for me.It didn't grab me right from the start, but the game slowly and masterfully got me hooked, bit by bit. The engaging dialogue, the immersive mini-games, all the mysteriousness of the world - it all came together to make me feel absolutely immersed in this game.The characters all have such rich motivations, secrets, ups and downs. They all evolve and find their own paths in such a natural way. I want to express so much emotion about it, but it's so hard to put it all into words in a review like this.This is truly a masterpiece, and I can't recommend it enough. But you have to take your time with it, let yourself get pulled into the story. That's the only way to really feel the full impact of the ending.Hoho, Cathy, hope you finished your race.

_childDocuments_.review: I've never felt the need to write a long game review legitimately but, knowing how people are turned off by cultures they aren't familiar with (but they love the "Overwhelmingly Positive" tag at 500 reviews) and just how much i unexpectedly needed it and it emotionally gripped me I feel that everyone who experienced this start to finish should at least leave a positive review.(note my entire playthrough was done in the most emotional possible period of my life so far. i just got out of a very serious long term relationship and it has been very rough so it may be a bit biased and more of a review aimed at the developers)The story of Until Then is so amazing its appalling knowing that it came from a indie studio in the Philippines. Start to finish it heavily leans on the OST to push your feelings in certain directions and the OST never once lets a moment down (Where is the OST btw?? Some of those songs have made such an emotional impact on me I would love to be able to listen to them on streaming services). The way it tackles the themes of loss and acceptance over the three playthroughs and follows deep with Mark's inner thoughts and the way he learns to come to terms and understand his situation really helped me personally with the things I've been going through even if it wasn't the intended effect. I think everyone should know an experience like this is out there,, I can't think of a game with such relatable lines and dialogue for dealing with loss. Losing the person that taught you how to feel these ways and that it's acceptable to feel these ways as a human is one of the hardest things I think everyone will have to go through eventually; and learning that the world isn't over yet is vital when that happens. I'm glad I was able to find something so guiding and therapeutic in a time like this so thank you to the devs personally <3 Gameplay wise; I wasn't a HUGE fan of the minigames in the first playthrough (most of them felt very choppy and the rhythm game had random input delay) but overall, considering the story and music, the small gripes i have are VASTLY outshined by those positives. The overworld movement is fine, it's a 2D walking sidescroller there's really not much to ask for but the style of the bodies and the way they breathe took a bit of getting used to. The pixel art through the entire game is amazing and the little detail they catch in some scenes can give you goosebumps. It's easy to tell how much love went into the art. Overall going down as one of my favourite story games of all time, I just hope more people can know it exists. If it doesn't catch now I honestly see this coming back in a few years after some sort of video essay goes viral :p
