_childDocuments_.review: I have dabbled in some walking-sim and visual novel type games before but none have ever held my attention in the same way that  has this last week.Every once in a while I get a craving for a game that can make me cry, and when I stumbled across Until Then during the summer sale I bought it in blind faith:Like obviously this was the exact thing I was looking for. Having not read any reviews nor done any research before purchasing it I assumed it would be another 2-3 hour existential game like one of my favorites And while it delivered on the existential melancholia I was anticipating, at the 3 hour mark the story was still going strong... Then as I thought it was wrapping up around the 6 hour mark it took an unexpected detour and here I am 20 hours later regretting none of it.I hesitate to talk much about the game because I feel that it was such an amazing experience to go into blind and I don't really want to rob anyone of that. But it was such a beautiful story of friendship, loss, forgiveness and acceptance. I feel like I just walked out of the theater after a really good movie and I'm still awestruck even after taking the time to sit through the entire credits processing what I just experienced.I do have a bit of criticism. There were consistent audio and control issues that seemed to become more prevalent the longer a game session persisted. I circumvented these by just restarting the game every few chapters and it mostly ran smoothly, not to mention the devs already patched out one issue I was experiencing so I have faith the game will continue to become more stable in the coming weeks. I also thought that the conclusion could have tied up more lose ends in the mystery that prevails throughout the entire story, but ultimately it was a satisfying and masterful narrative experience. I wouldn't be surprised if I spent another 20 hours to ride this emotional roller coaster again one day.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has been sitting on the fence for me personally, as it has qualities that would both be very polarizing and very appealing.First let me talk about the actual game itself, in which I believe that there are a lot of kinks to this game. I genuinely lost track of how many times this game crashed or had some weird glitchy bug that wouldn't allow me to progress through the game, forcing me close and open the game which led me re-doing segments of the story more than once. Furthermore, the game itself would just close on its own out of nowhere, making me initially believe that the game was breaking the 4th wall (Which I later found out it definitely wasn't). While it wasn't infested with these problems, the fact that it occurred to me more than 10 times throughout my play-through was enough to be both disrupting and noticeable. There were also a lot of mini-games to play, but there really wasn't a proper explanation on how to play these games. I messed around and generally got the concept, however having at least some guidance or explanation would have been useful. And because of the kinks within the game, I sometimes couldn't tell if the game was purposely messing with me (Which it sometimes did) or was just genuinely a bug, making me watch other people play through the game to double check.As for the aesthetic of this game, it's absolutely beautiful. I enjoy pixelated art which expresses both personality and visual clarity, which this game absolutely nailed. The game's art is both unique and vibrant, catching the eyes of many people around me in real life. I cannot praise the art style enough, and honestly was the tipping point for me to recommend this game to others.Now as we talk about the story, something that I truly appreciate is how realistic some aspects of social life is shown. While I didn't have a high school experience directly in the Philippines, I was able to see a lot of things that drew parallels to my own experiences while showing unique aspects of Filipino life to me. These aspects made the game far more enjoyable for me, but I can see it being a personal gripe for others (As the pacing can be slow, but daily life can't be always be crazy imo). I am also a person who enjoys a lot more menial tasks being shown as it makes characters far more human in my eyes, though that is also a personal preference. As for the story itself, I think it's just fine. There are times where certain concepts are constantly pushed down your throat to emphasize how important it is, but I feel like if their execution was more subtle, it would have enhanced the story for me. I also feel like some of the endings didn't exactly make sense to me, leaving me with some unanswered questions. While I understood the thought process and how some endings occurred, some of these endings still felt very contradictory to me. I may have missed out on some details or possibly misunderstood, but I feel like some of these endings felt too forced, or shoe-horned in. Overall, this game truly feels indie to me, and I enjoyed the game quite a bit. While there are aspects that need to be refined (Optimization for this game and story endings [In my personal opinion]), I think it's still a fun and unique game that can be appreciated by a lot of other people.

_childDocuments_.review: I’m no stranger to slow-burn, slice-of-life games/ experiences, but let me just say that I am extremely disappointed with this game. Yes, the depiction of the Philippines is quite impressive and extremely accurate. I am a Filipino who grew up in the Philippines before moving to the States when I turned 20. Yeah, I did experience how it felt to walk to MRT stations, have to wear uniforms to school, buy street food, and haggle tricycle prices. My mom was also an overseas worker most of my life so I understand the pain of being separated from family. The first ‘Life is Strange’ is probably my favorite gaming experience among ‘Outer Wilds’ and ‘Firewatch’ and the reason I’m saying this is so that you, dear review reader, aren’t baffled by the score I’ll give this game and thing that this guy doesn’t know what he's talking about. Or it’s a justification I’ve been telling myself just to make my (kinda deep rooted) disdain for this game relatively valid. I’d like to say that I kinda do. There WILL BE SPOILERS for this review. Why did Mark’s dad not come home when his wife’s plane crashed? Why was the ruling so inconspicuously talked about despite being ‘the end of the world’? Why were the subplots so vague - Nicole’s issues with Jake, Louise’s apparent imposter syndrome and research about ‘quantum tsunami’s that occur when ripples through particles interact,’ Sofia’s grandmother, Mark and Nicole’s obvious PTSD, and Cathy’s familial tension. It felt like it was leading up to something big, an overarching plot that’d connect all the dots they laid out, but they didn't resolve anything in the end. The writing of the game itself felt off; the first few chapters were filled with trivial teen drama ♥♥♥♥ with sprinkles of supernatural flashbacks and the occasional intertwining of separate subplots. What I really don’t like is the way they all just try to explain everything through an exposition dump halfway through the fifth chapter about something the main character was hiding from the start of the game. It’s not that it felt too out-of-left-field, it was just I find it hard to believe. And Cathy was waiting by a bus stop shed, (I know Filipino trucks are ass at driving) but I find it hard to believe that it didn’t stop. And we never got any closure on Cathy’s issues with her families, just a slow-mo of her bruises and scars as she ran across the street on a stormy night? The final Louise “All in LeHeads” explanation really made me want to punch my monitor for some reason ngl. Then they had the audacity to do a time skip at the end and be like ‘everything went back to normal.’And I understand the limitations that come with being an indie up-and-coming studio, the main retro 8 bit aesthetic, slice-of-life genre campiness, and text based interface - no voice acting, minimal and simple gameplay. I agree and applaud the representation of Philippine culture, but it still doesn’t hide enough of the flaws that stood out to me. I also appreciate the subtle nods to other games and franchises like the Doki Doki one really had me laughing and led to me explaining the whole gist of that masterpiece. The conversation with Ridel was really heartfelt. I'm glad they gave him a chance to express himself after being relegated as ‘the friend who grew apart’ the whole film. And the MCU post credits slideshow of Cathy's perspective of the night. ***Chef's Kiss*** And the racing game ending taking inspiration from this reddit post was quite an ending garnish. []Don’t let my opinions stop you from enjoying the game and if the game’s message really hit home for you, I am so very happy that it did. I understand the message it was trying to send and know that it would resonate with a lot of people with similar contexts. Honestly maybe it’s me and my self-imposed overexposure to narratives like this - one to many John Green books, Paper Towns and Looking for Alaska, or Makoto Shinkai films, Your Name, Weathering With You and Suzume, or stories with butterflies as analogies like the Life is Strange series. Yeah, maybe it is me. Perhaps, I’m no longer the target audience. Baka 'di na ako yung YA. Hanggang A nalang ako. SHEESH.If anyone is having trouble at home, don't keep it to yourself. Someone is always out there for you. Let them know. You don't owe your parents anything.Nevertheless, I still highly recommend this experience for its exhibition of the childhood I grew up loving. Thanks for reading.

_childDocuments_.review: - Until Then is one of the best story games, If not the BEST story game I have ever played. Might not be the best game for fun. Especially since some of the Mini-games are difficult. But if your willing to experience a Tear-Jerking story, this game is honestly, the best game that could ever fit your needs. Especially when the same mini-games work to complement the same story, so well. If you have $20 to spend on a game, this one is definitely one to buy when you get a chance. So much so, that I would arguably wish to play this game for the first time again, just because of how much it touched me emotionally.                                                                I                                                               I                                                              VWhen I bought this game, I thought it was just another indie game with some unique story that would ultimately live rent free in my head for the next couple weeks, only to then be forgotten again. However, when I started the game up, and saw the interactive start with the alarm clock... I knew this game was going to be something special. Something, I wasn't going to expect from a small game like this. I took my time playing through the first ending, experiencing all what I thought the game had to offer. For me the story on the first go around, was... underwhelming, at least at first, and assuming you're reading my comment, and already played the game fully, you'd know, that the first "play through" wasn't the entire game. To my surprise, when I got the option to hit continue on the TV, I thought nothing of it. Only then to be placed right in front of what I can only call, the Pinnacle of the "Darkfiends" franchise. Slowly then, did I realize that there was more to do, albeit, from what I could tell, just a retreading of the game. But slowly and surely, there was more to offer, specifically, two more repeats of the same "five chapter cycle", that I was used to. Little did know I would ultimately dig so much deeper into the beautiful, complex, heartwarming, and bitter sweet story that continued from there. Throughout the game, there was many instances in which I really related to Mark, the Central Protagonist of the Story. The highs, the lows, and everything in between. I related to his struggles as a Musician in trying to get better at an instrument. I related to his struggles of communications and expressing his emotions. I related to his struggle to forgive himself and move on. As I personally have dealt with many scenarios, just like his, albeit less supernatural and probably more realistic and boring. But without a doubt I realized the and understood the Gem this game was. Now to actually get to the Review... Until Then is arguably one of the best story games out there, if not probably the best. The way the story was retold time and time again. Woven through out the entire course of the cohesive story. It was like experiencing the beauty of the Mona Lisa for the first time in history. Although that might be massive of a comparison. It goes to show how much this game has touched my heart, soul, and well being. From the importance on his self hatred, to the focus of love, forgiveness, and family, each part of the game felt, Personal... It felt like it was a Diary, someone's diary...Through it all, Until Then repeatedly made me think about what happens next. Who will be the next to disappear? Who will be the one to see failure and pain? Will Mark and Nicole finally fall in love again for the umpteenth time? And will Mark finally find peace, and happiness once again? It constantly made me think about what happens, about the characters, and how the final scene will play out, and boy, was I not prepared for it. Until Then as mentioned probably more times then it should have, made me feel for the characters and story. And admittedly, as person who doesn't really manage their emotions a whole lot, the story absolutely destroyed me. It made me cry... Which is not something that can be said for a whole lot of media, for that which I have consumed. But oh boy, did I cry puddles. It was honestly touching, and made me think a whole lot the night I finished it. But that only really happened, the Night I more specifically, finished the first cycle. Not expecting what was to come. Going into the second, and third cycle, I was a lot more emotionally vulnerable, I guess? And when I finally finished the Second cycle only to be shoved into the third cycle, I knew something was waiting for me at the finish line. Until Then is a game that isn't a game. It's one of those "games" that are a piece of art. A piece of history. A game that may not have profound significance to many, but to those many who have found significance, It means a whole lot to them. It may not have the most complex mini-games that you could grind for hours. And it may not be the GOTY for many, but as far as I am concerned, Until Then is a Piece of Art that encapsulates what it's like to be a Teen. Not only that, but to struggle with forgiveness, to struggle with Self-Love, to even struggle with Depression. For what it lacks in game play as a "Video Game", it makes up, tenfold! in the story it has to offer. Not only to those who may need to learn how to love themselves again, but to love others, and forgive them. As of writing this review, I have 17 hours of playtime, and a whole lot o emotions to unpack. As I move away, and accept the Ending of the game, and possibly wish or theorize how Mark and Nicole eventually find each other again or reconnect somehow at the Cafe during the last scene. I can't help but focus on the fact of letting go. Maybe not necessarily the one's you love like in Mark's case, after all the theme of Soulmates is constant throughout game, and I'd argue many people would support the possibility of them reconnecting somehow after the ending. But more so, I focus on the acceptance and letting go of hatred for oneself, for moving on from mistakes, and regrets, and enjoying and embracing life. As I said, I cried at the end of the first third, and I'd be remiss if I did not admit that I cried four times that, at the actually ending of the game. For a game to make a person, who admittedly doesn't cry a whole lot, to cry about 5 times, alone, when an emotional movie can really only make them cry about once, is a very profound thing, to be able to accomplish. At least for me. As much as I would love to spout for hours on end about Until Then, I must accept the impact it has had on my life, and finally move on from what is admittedly a very long and somewhat repetitive review. As mentioned earlier, I have to rate the game a 9/10, it is a Masterpiece of story telling, so much so that It dethroned all the story games I had in my listing, like Disco Elysium, RDR2, or even Fallout. It managed to make me feel like a fan boy of a game, that should have more praise than it has or probably even deserves. But nonetheless I am finally ending my review. And with that I say, if you haven't played it and read all this. I'm Sorry for spoiling it, but you were warned, and it's just that good. And to my fellow Steam users who have and wanted to see what someone like me wanted to say about it, Thank you for reading a heartfelt review, and If I could, I would wish that me and you could magically play this game for the first time again. And again, Thank You for reading!

_childDocuments_.review: Until Then has some of the most relatable and realistically written young characters. It's a game that will make you laugh, cringe, rage, and cry, as life never goes according to plan. All you're trying to do is learn to play the piano and live a normal life; if only life was that simple. Until Then is not what most people will play because it's a visual novel, aka no real gameplay. It has minigames that aren't really fun but are used to tell a story or build character, not just random. They are quick so you can get back to the good stuff, the characters you'll grow to love and hate to see what happens to them.I was so engaged in reading texts as it felt like responses from my own mind at times. A simple feature to type out your responses instead of just having it pop up; allows for the many mistakes of natural texting. You don't always send your first text, you edit it by pressing or holding a button to further engage you in the conversations and mysteries unfolding. I'm praising texting in a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ visual novel and all I'm really doing is holding a button and reading. I don't play visual novels because they are all weeb games, which I don't play. I wonder if it's these unknown hidden gems with normal stories that I need to look at? If you know of any, let me know. I'm looking at trying out A Space for the Unbound, but I need to emotionally recover first.The thing that made me even try this out was seeing its art style from the trailer and its mixture of 3D with 2D pixels. What I got was grounded writing that makes you feel a part of this world, this group of friends, and experience a life relatable in the mundane, even when it gets weird. The endings will slap you many times with the feels that only a few games have ever done. I am also a sucker for music in the way they handle it in this game. Fans of Sanbabi will get it

_childDocuments_.review: Am I biased towards this game as a Filipino? A bit. Did some of the themes of this story hit way close to home and give me more personal engagement and cause me to cry a lot? Absolutely. Despite that, though, this game is genuinely worth your time. A carefully crafted story about love, grieving, and the human condition, with some time-flavored mystery sprinkled throughout.Sometimes you can get lost in all the sci-fi quantum theory jargon, but I found myself very easily suspending my disbelief. There're moments where the emotional beats can come off as too much or almost unreal (which I personally feel is par for the course with YA fiction), but when this game times those moments perfectly with the right amount of feeling, it absolutely hits you. The minigames are short, but always managed to keep me engaged. I could go on and on about how much I love the music and the expressiveness behind some of these tracks, but all that really needs to be said is "piano good :)".The lack of understanding of Filipino culture and references that some players might have doesn't impede at all with the overall storytelling of the game, and you are very quickly sucked into the lives of these characters as you find beauty in the mundane. Highly recommend checking out the demo of this game at bare minimum.

_childDocuments_.review: 'Until Then' is an utterly beautiful,  slice of life / mystery visual novel covering the highschool experience of a handful of Philippine high schoolers.The characters might on the surface seem 1 dimensional, especially given they're literally missing their entire third dimension, but be real with yourself: You knew somebody like that in highschool. You knew the tomboy kid who came from a terrible home. You knew the top-of-the-class teachers-pet girl who you had zero chance with. You might've even been the borderline hopeless kid who had the ability to do something better but always did the bare minimum and probably just needed a little push to get there but the push never came. The characters feel real, at least to me anyway. Even the literal joke characters. Only a few people come across as cardboard cutouts and they only exist in a handful of scenes to advance the plot anyway. Also, in-case it's putting you off, you'd hardly know the game was set in the Philippines bar a handful of cultural / locale specific things like crosses and Jesus references being everywhere.As far as the overall experience is concerned, it was  flawless with only a handful of hiccups along the way (auto saving only sucks, pacing can be slow at times).  Btw, one last thing, "Howlongtobeat" is completely wrong on the playtime. (Extremely minor spoilers that you should look at regardless unless you wanna miss a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of content: ).- . If Steam overlay isn't opening, you aren't getting achievements. My drivers were only 3 or so months old at most and I got screwed out of every achievement except Cocoon (I realized too late what was going on and updated them). This has never happened prior in any other games.

_childDocuments_.review: ok first time leaving a review for a game, let's go :))im not really big on visual novels, as i have a bad case of ooga booga action brain (closest i ever got to VNs were Persona 3 and 5 () as well as Ace Attorney. a friend told me to check the demo for this game and i got hooked on the art style and creativity behind it, and .Things I liked:-. man. they really got me good with that demo. the vibrant colors and upbeat animations. id like to clarify that I didn't know anything about this game before playing the full and demo version. i did not expect this game to have such a hold on me. to say it was a roller coaster of emotions would not do it justice. i have more to say about the story in the spoiler section later on. if i already interested you enough to play the game, please do go play it and come back :3. otherwise feel free to keep reading.-. the main thing that got me waiting for this game's full release. its pretty. im aware that 2d pixel  style isnt new, but the creativity to use different styles for different parts/scenes, and mixing 2d elements with a 3d environment was amazing to me. dont really have anything else to say here other than game look pretty.-. minigames!!!!! i wouldnt necessarily say that theyre breaking grounds here with the minigames, but it made me say "oh thats cute" a couple of times. and i think thats a good thing. i suck at rhythm games though :b----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------Things I didn't like:-. i get it dont worry. its the first week that it's been out so there's bound to be a couple issues here and there, but im more concerned about the system requirements. im not a game developer nor do i claim to be, but i feel theres room to optimize this game to allow it to run smoother. i find it extremely baffling (for lack of a better word) that i need "at least a gtx 1650" for a visual novel. im lucky i can run the game but even i get the occasional crashes and fps lag. really hope they optimize this game so more people can play it, as i was starting to lose motivation when the game would start to lag.-. as mentioned before, i suck at rhythm games. and i didnt expect it to be a recurring game past the first time. i found it harder to immerse myself into the story whilst trying to hit the notes (skill issue yes i know) but at the very least there should be a feature to opt-out of it. same goes for other minigames. a skip button for other unnecessary minigames (looking at you jeep rhythm game)--------------------------------------------------------------Read if you think you finished chapter 5Read if can confidently say you finished chapter 5 and did not miss anything

_childDocuments_.review: "Until Then" is a game that truly surprised me with its depth and complexity. At first glance, it might seem like a straightforward narrative adventure, but as you dive deeper, you realize that the story is just beginning when you think it’s about to end.The interactive elements are wonderfully implemented, particularly the in-game texting and social media feed interactions. These features add a layer of immersion and realism that I thoroughly enjoyed. However, I found the QTE mini-games at critical plot points to be a bit frustrating. It would be great if players had the option to load right before these sequences to make related achievments less arduous.The storyline is dramatic and profound, evoking the emotional weight and complexity reminiscent of the movie "The Butterfly Effect." The decisions you make feel significant, and the ripple effects are both compelling and thought-provoking.Additionally, the game offers a rich depiction of Filipino culture, from the everyday life of students to the unique local modes of transport. This cultural immersion adds a unique charm to the game. The pixel art style and the soundtrack further enhance the immersive experience, drawing you into the vibrant and intricate world of "Until Then". However, while the graphics are charming, they could benefit from a bit more polish, although they fit the overall aesthetic of the game.Overall, "Until Then" is a beautifully crafted game that delves into the intricacies of memory, identity, and friendship within a captivating narrative. Highly recommended for those who appreciate a good story.

It's such a good story of events on a world-ending scale being told through the lens of two teenagers. Honestly, it's inspiring. It has such an incredible message of trying to move on. To grow out of old cycles. To be better. To DO better. To make up with your past, to never forget, but to continue moving forward. I can't even encapsulate how many themes, messages, and raw emotion that comes out of this game. If you're still, STILL scrolling through reviews, please, I beg you, go play it. It's a 10/10 from me. I'm optimistically waiting for the next game from Polychroma Games, but Until Then, it looks like I'm going to playing this game again, and again, and again.

_childDocuments_.review: Before I start I will say this review will not contain any spoilers whatsoever.When I say this game is a masterpiece, it truly is a one of a kind experience. When I first started playing I didn't think much of it, but the further I got into the story, the more emotions it got out of me.  Sorry.. Each scene has an impact and references to events that happen later on that you won't even notice the first time you play through.  The characters feel relatable in a sense that it makes you feel like you were in the story.  I can relate to some of the characters in certain aspects and that is definitely what drove me to liking this game even more than intended.  The art itself is amazing, especially when we are talking about close ups to each of the characters.  You can see the emotions of each character with such detail that it makes you feel what they do.  The music is some of the best music I have ever listened to.  I can say that it has pulled more than just a few strings in my heart.  It more like ripped my heart out and put in a new one, one that is actually filled with emotions.  One that understands in a sense.  When you combine all these elements, it makes what I would like to call peak writing.I have finished the story and will continue to enjoy it in it's entirety and I hope that everyone will enjoy it as much as me. _childDocuments_.review: This a great game.  If you are a fan of visual novels then I highly recommend Until Then.  I'm going to list out quick positives and negatives, but I strongly would recommend this game for anybody who loves stories that are both filled with happiness and sadness.Positives:- Story:  No going to spoil anything, but this is one of the best stories I have seen in a video game at least in the past year or so.  Nothing ground-breaking, but extremely well-executed for the most part.- Characters: In my opinion, the biggest strength this game has.  Seriously, most characters are just great!  I did not think any one character fell flat, but especially the main characters really do feel real (in their world).-  Ending:  I actually enjoyed all the possible endings (will not spoil them).  I personally felt the strongest attachment to the first ending, but the last ending is almost perfect for me.  My personal gripes:- The story is pretty straight-forward up to til the end.  I personally don't think is so complicated or convoluted, but it does get a bit out there.  I think it reels it back in a good amount.-  Some "missing" parts of the story: I do not want a story that handholds me throughout, but there are just some question marks from the story that I just felt did not land fully or were just either purposely or not a big hazy on.-  I suck at rhythm games, so the recitals were difficult haha.Overall, 9/10 - would recommend. Quick Spoiler for the last ending,  so do not read this unless you played the game, but I need to get it off my chest

_childDocuments_.review: a beautiful story about loss, grief and letting go of people and things. this was truly a rollercoaster of emotions that made me feel all sorts of stuff; fear, excitement, sadness, uncanniness, anger, loneliness and relief. at first i expected just around 10 hours of gameplay, but once i found out this game had several cycles, i was SHOCKED. the attention to details and amount of stuff changing every time you start a new cycle is just jaw dropping, i can see the developers really put their heart and soul in it. another thing i pay attention to is sound design, and trust me its AMAZING! it helps to really feel the mood of every scene. despite dialogues not being voiced, you can very well feel the tension or emotion of the words. i also really loved the mix of 3d surroundings and 2d models - definitely not something im used to (or ever seen before), and i must say it looks very well done, along with the shadows/lighting! next thing that i absolutely loved is character design. despite characters themselves ironically being two dimensional, the personality for each and every one of them is huge. the game easily makes you feel empathetic towards the main characters and understand every perspective of the story from different sides. im not filipino, but im sure natives can find a lot of correspondences and easter eggs. in conclusion - you will definitely love this game if you're into visual novels and story-rich psychological games (like omori, milk inside a bag of milk, needy girl overdose, etc). i ugly cried twice as a not so sensitive person. 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first steam review I have ever written for any of the 200+ games I've played but I felt so strongly about this game that I felt I had to say something. I was initially drawn to the game by it's combination of 2D and 3D assets and it's unique style but after playing the demo I was hooked in fully by it's plot. I wasn't too sure what to expect since I haven't really played visual novels before but if all of them where as interesting or as relatable as this then I might need to play more. This game deserves it's very positive score and in my opinion overwhelmingly positive and here's why.I loved every second of this story it was so incredibly well written and paced. The characters were relatable and funny, the dialog was realistic and compelling, and the ending oh man the ending nearly had me in tears. From the very beginning seeing Mark's struggles and how he goes through life without much care and how he gradually changes himself to Cathy seeing her friends changing and finding their direction in life. If it wasn't for other life obligations I would have probably finished it in one sitting that's how invested I was. The game is not without it's flaws some of the mini games were a little janky like the whack-a-mole hit box. The rhythm game sections didn't respond too well to the arrow keys the left and right arrows felt as if they were only reading every 3rd or 4th press and it wasn't until I found the DFJK keys that I was able to get consistency. I did also feel like some of the sections that had you walking around until something triggered like the clothing store were a little long but nothing deal breaking. Lastly while I love the story and think it's one of the best written games I've played in a long while the rain element (to avoid spoilers) felt like it was never resolved or really figured out to me and kind of took a back seat to everything else. If that was what was intended or if I missed something that would have answered it for me then that is perfectly fine.Overall as I've said before this game had me glued to the screen every step of the way and I found myself rooting for all of it's characters. The developments, plot twists, emotional moments, and the music all work amazingly well together and provide an experience that I am thoroughly inspired by. I could not ask for a better first review title and I am looking forward to seeing what other games Polychroma comes out with in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start off about why this game is amazing. The characters are well written and the world is immersive. Even though you can pick some dialogue / choices with Mark, the point-of-view character, at no point do you ever get the feeling that he's just a self-insert. The story of Until Then is a character driven plot all the way through, and sucks you into its world in the process. The art of the story is gorgeous, and the music beautiful to boot.As to my small gripes with the game.The story does feel like it steps on its toes a bit. It revolves around bouts of "deja vu" that the characters, especially Mark, experiences. These bouts of "deja vu" turn out to be , which is a very interesting premise, if not for the fact that the  around, not much actually changes to warrant the long time that you spend repeating mostly similar events. These  actually are the cause of the natural disasters that form the backbone of the game's world building, but the twist that  makes me take a step back like "yes, this is indeed a young adult story", in the same way that Bunny Girl Senpai attempts to explain a lot of its plot with arbitrarily related scientific concepts.Spoiler alert; it's bad to dumb a story down, but if you had to, then it would essentially be like  As a result of such a story, there is an open-ending concerning All in all, besides the gripes I had, I was still very much satisfied by the game and would recommend it those who want to immerse themselves in a great story.

_childDocuments_.review: Sometimes, we think that we've become numb to the things going on around us. We think that we've felt everything there is to feel, as if the emotions that once wracked our souls will never again move us. Flickers of buried sorrow and forgotten happiness remain ephemeral in the midst of our battered hearts, torn asunder by the whirlwind of life. And yet, numb as we may be, there come times when we find it -- a spark. It can be something profound, or even something utterly mundane. What matters is that it starts, cascades, and crashes. Before we even know it, we find ourselves overwhelmed with emotions, with feelings, with life. Until Then is a game about finding that spark. For me, the game itself is a spark. I had thought that there was nothing else left for me to feel. But the world hasn't ended just yet. And so long as it hasn't, so long as we're here and trying, even failing -- so long as it isn't over, there might be hope for us yet.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played a large list of Visual Novels over the years, some of which have emotionally crushed me, some of which have been quite well-written and have stayed with me to this day, but holy... I've never felt this conflicted with myself after playing through one of them. It's not depressing because it's sad... it's depressing because it's so overwhelmingly relatable. It's so real; it's so down to earth that it doesn't feel like a game or a visual novel, but rather like I'm staring at myself in a mirror with each and every one of the individuals you'll meet. I can't express how it moved me, because it's hard to put into words.Like, all I want to do now is expose this game to everyone and get as many people as possible to try it for themselves, more than any other game I've played. The music, the visual design and direction, the emotions, the struggles. I'd like to stress that if you've recently experienced some trauma in your life especially with friends, family and any other situations, it wouldn't be a good idea for you to sit down and play through it, since I don't want to bring you any more suffering and it might even go as far as to make things you're going through right now and harder to heal. The unfortunate thing is that I want so many other people to enjoy this game, but it's unlikely that they will because Visual Novels are typically deemed niche and undesirable to the average gamer. I'd want to stress that I am a general gamer. I participate in the majority of games that others do. I play Final Fantasy, Valorant, Apex, League of Legends, Action Roguelikes, Racing, and every other genre you can think of and I too prefer those other genres. I'm not very interested in Visual Novels because I have ADHD, which makes it difficult for me to focus when there isn't something to occupy my attention. This could refer to the music being played, the characters and their relationship, story & twists, or voice acting. There has to be something for me to be able to latch onto, yet Until Then drew me in without even having to try. I did not have an option. I was glued to my seat for all 19.6 hours, which is how long this experience lasted, not 9 like many reviewers have posted at. You are definitely getting your money's worth here. It's more than a reasonable fee for an experience you'll only have once in a lifetime. Even if you don't feel like playing this game at this very moment, just like the thousands of other games you have on your Steam Library, seriously. Please give it a chance, especially if you have friends that you know enjoy emotional experiences. I hope this developer succeeds with their creation so that we may see more stories from them.
_childDocuments_.name: Until Then

_childDocuments_.review: Before I really get into it, this is a good game. It has its flaws as a "game", but as a piece of pure storytelling and interactive media... I love it. This is probably the only serious review I've written so far. Please give at least the demo a chance if you're on the fence about it. The save data carries over, so no need to worry about that.WARNING: Mild spoilers ahead, but I don't say anything that you won't be able to pick up early through the game anyway.Okay, getting into it now. I want to talk about two things I love about this game.First off is the setting. The setting for me feels incredible. Despite having only moved to the Philippines for college, I feel like the devs did a good job in making the class experiences feel very universal. Cramming for presentations, buying materials for projects last minute (well, if you're an irresponsible student like Mark and I).Mark having OFW parents hit hard for me. Luckily I grew up with them around since I was born and raised abroad, but only when I was older did I really appreciate the hard work they put into it for a better life for their kids. When I moved to the PH for college, my dad stayed behind while my mom came with me to take care of me. Mark receiving bank transfers in AED was just such a surreal hit to home for me that the I was immediately enthralled. I could say more, but that would be breaching into more spoilery territory.Secondly, I'd like to talk about the characters. As a side note, I both half appreciate that all the dialogue is in English (with funny side comments/graffiti/logos in Filipino), but I somehow do wish there was an option for a Filipino text language, but I do understand that that's probably low on the list when it comes to requirements for publishers and all. Either way, I would still play it in English cause my Filipino is bad haha.Going to the point on characters, they all feel so incredibly human to me. The writers did a good job of really hitting home with interpersonal struggles and personal struggles that even I, as a mid 20s Filipino, feel today. Each of the characters have their own unique charms that just enchant you the more you get to know them. Even the side characters have a ton of love put into them. Again, I could go on but that would be spoiler territory.To wrap this up, this is the first time I felt compelled to write a review of any length. To see a game this moving made by a Filipino dev is truly inspiring. I hope to see more from them in the future. Until Then.

_childDocuments_.review: In many ways, the work of a critic is easy. We risk very little, yet enjoy a position over those who offer up their work and their selves to our judgment. We thrive on negative criticism, which is fun to write and to read. But the bitter truth we critics must face, is that in the grand scheme of things, the average piece of junk is probably more meaningful than our criticism designating it so. But there are times when a critic truly risks something, and that is in the discovery and defense of the new. The world is often unkind to new talent, new creations. The new needs friends. Last night, I experienced something new: an extraordinary game from a singularly unexpected source. To say that both the game and its maker have challenged my preconceptions about fine game development is a gross understatement. They have rocked me to my core. In the past, I have made no secret of my disdain for Polychroma Games' famous motto, "Anyone can develop." But I realize, only now do I truly understand what they meant. Not everyone can become a great artist; but a great artist can come from anywhere. It is difficult to imagine more humble origins than those of the genius now developing at Polychroma Games, who is, in this critic's opinion, nothing less than the finest game studio in The Philippines. I will be returning to Polychroma Games soon, hungry for more.

_childDocuments_.review: Until Then is a beautiful story about loss, acceptance, and healing.  I normally dont play these types of games but when i saw Overwhelmingly Positive I looked through the reviews and liked what i saw.  And i must say this game delivered, what i thought was going to be a surface level experience made me think introspectively like i never have before, and even managed to get a few tears out of me.  Something i will note is that this game takes roughly 20 hours to play, so if you do decide to pick it up and you find yourself done at the 10-15 hour mark (depending on how many times you just left the game running in the background) just know you absolutely are not done.  This game, as far as i can tell is an on rails narrative, so if you arent at that 20 hour mark you quite literally are not done with the full narrative aspect of the game.  Keep that in mind when you look at reviews with only like 10 hours on them.There are a few gripes i have however, the piano minigame is incredibly inconsistent, youll press a key on the exact same timing and sometimes itll miss, be great, or be perfect, sometimes when you press a key and theres a hold right after it the hold will jump up and youll miss it.  That and the minigame is quite infrequent, i wish it was used more often despite the quirks as the first time you are given it at a significant narrative moment.  Another complaint i have is that the background sounds are often too loud for the scene, the gym ac fans stick out in my mind, if you just put the SFX down to like 20 percent though it fixes it.This game is great though, give it a shot, and its only 20 bucks too, a steal for what it gives.And just a note if any of the devs read these, i really like the approach you took with the ending, its not the cliche i expected, and i think it perfectly matches the message of the game, yall knocked it out of the park.

_childDocuments_.review: This is going to go some places and get a little personal.When I was a teenager, I met a group of people from all over the world because we had a shared interest in a sci-fi manga. We talked about it, wrote about it, made our own fantastical stories. They had to do with other realities and other versions. Loss and love and friendship. Life and uncertainty. Humanity persevering in the face of impossible odds...and sometimes failing, but starting again. People doing the wrong thing wanting to fix the world, rebuilding and recovering. Destroying everything, unintentionally, because you love someone, and you want them to be happy.We wrote these stories for many years. Sometimes, someone would fall out of touch. Sometimes, that was me. We'd always reunite eventually. Sometimes it took years, but at the end, I kept reuniting with my friends from all over the world. We would write again, a little more wise, a little more grown, and we would catch up. We would make each other things for our birthdays and share our heartaches. We would play silly games and cry when things were rough. I was grateful to them in so many ways. I think they taught me about myself, and I hope I did a little in return. I admired the way they crafted stories, the way they'd create. How much I learned about places I had never been, about concepts I had never learned of. I treasured it.Nowadays, it's harder. We're all grown up. We haven't written together in some time, and more than that we've all been busy with our own lives. And last year, the last message I received from one of them was horribly distressing. "If I die," she said. "We're being bombed, so if I die," she said. I asked for her to check in, when she could. She hasn't.She was always so kind to me. We were around the same age, but she felt so much older. Whenever I was afraid or insecure, I felt I could go to her, and we would figure it out, together. She went through some rough times. When I drifted, I became afraid I'd never talk to her again. I was so relieved that was proven false.And now, here I am again. I barely spoke in our chat, in fear of her possibly last message being swallowed up by time. No one else did, either. I think, perhaps, we were all some level of scared of that. I may be presuming too much. I'd been afraid to reach out to any of them, on the chance they may have heard something horrible. I'd been afraid to message her, on the chance that I never get a response. I was afraid, stuck in the past, feeling pain whenever I thought of those happy times we had together growing up. Afraid that, after all the starting and stopping, it was over, because one of them was gone.I picked up this game on a whim. The sale was there, and I liked what I saw of the teaser trailer. I was stretching my funds, but I felt like I had to get it. And then, I started playing on a whim as well. I don't know when I realized this felt like something my friends and I would write together. I don't know when I started seeing parallels and connections, reflections of stories we told in our youth. I just know that, at my first time through Chapter 4, when I was ugly crying, I felt like I was writing with them again. For a brief moment, I wondered if someone I knew was a part of it.They aren't. I know that. But I've played at every chance I could, because I wanted to see the end of the story. Because it felt like, for one last time - whether it's because one of them is gone, because we've all grown too busy, because we've all grown up - I would get to write with all of my friends. Because I know they would love this story, and it felt like a way to be close to them.Before I finished the game, I messaged my friend who left what could be her last message in our chat. I haven't heard back. I don't know if I will. But I've wanted to, since I got that message. I was afraid. Far too afraid. But, Until Then helped me be not afraid. Because even if I never get a message back, at least I tried. At least I have hope that somehow, somewhere, she could know I'm thinking about her.I think this game has started to heal a deep scar in me. Or, at the very least, it's let me take a look at it and understand I can't keep being like I am. Stuck, waiting, in hibernation.Please forgive my meandering. If you have read this, a memoir and a eulogy for people you've never met wrapped in a review, thank you. And, if any of you are out there right now, reading this, I love you. Thank you for being a part of my life. Everything that happened mattered.That's what playing Until Then meant to me. Polychroma Games, thank you. I don't know if I've managed to express how grateful I am, but please: Thank you, from the very bottom of my heart.

_childDocuments_.review: (This review is spoiler-free. However, I do mention some of the themes discussed in the game and some of its gameplay aspects)."Until Then" is the best game I have played this year (in the last few years too tbh). I never write game reviews at all, but I really needed to write a review for this one as I have been thinking about this game for more than a month after completely finishing it. It's probably one of the most impactful media I have ever had contact with.It is an emotional visual novel which explores themes of grief, loneliness and connection, while immersing the player into Filipino culture. Even though the game focuses on the story of a few characters, it really feels like it represents a collective feeling of loss due to natural disasters and political incompetence (events that could definitely happen anywhere in the world, but unfortunately resonates very closely to Philippines reality). The game respectfully delves into these collective themes while telling a very personal story (that of Mark Borja). That said, you are probably gonna cry a lot playing this game.The game art style is just so interesting, it mixes 2D pixel art and 3D environments in such an impressive way. It is really effective in capturing the characters' feelings and creating an immersive environment full of little details and references to Filipino culture. The gameplay is very basic, it is mostly interacting with scenarios and characters, but there are some mini-games here and there that are effective in either building the relationships between different characters or developing Mark's character. Also, the dialogue in this game is so thoughtful, it all feels very natural and personal (and frequently very emotional). The game presents some dialogue choices, but they do not have a huge impact in the game story (this is not really a decision-based story game, like the Telltale ones, and I actually thinks that is very positive as it allows the game to have a more cohesive narrative and message), only making minor changes to specific dialogues. Another gameplay bit the game has is scrolling through social media, which gives more information about the universe of the game. There is a specific gameplay aspect of this game that I feel like it is very smart and well-executed, but I'm not touching on that because it would be a spoiler unfortunately :(.I love the soundtrack of this game. The soundtrack (by Kyle Patrick Naval) is composed of some classics like "Fur Elise", but also some amazing original songs (Memories and Time Is Tearing Us Apart are both amazing), which helps making the game even more emotional.I am really happy I got to play this game and, if you can't already tell, I strongly recommend it, specially if you like story-based games. Polychroma really made an amazing game and I can't wait to see what they do next :).The world hasn't ended yet.PS. I really wish the game was in Brazilian Portuguese, it would be awesome and I am sure the Brazilian community (myself included) would love it :).

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not even two hours into this game, having just finished Chapter 2 moments before starting to write this review, and I cannot express the fascination I have with this, and for one core reason: The Main Character.I've been a massive fan of story based games all my life, but nothing hit me nearly as hard as this. I think some personal circumstances definitely create a bias for me here, but I have never found a character as relatable as Mark (your character). I intimately know what it's like to lose your drive, your creativity, your effort, your desire to live an eventful life, and not be able to pinpoint why. The loss of ambition can cripple a person into behaving like Mark is, and as I have. Flunking classes, leaving everything to the last minute, not thinking about what they say, or not caring about what they're doing. _childDocuments_.review: Man. Where to begin. This is a long one, sorry.  TLDR; play this game.Let's start with what I didn't like as much. I loved the diversity of the mini-games. I think they really changed up the pace of the story when they appeared, and were a nice way to engage different gaming muscles besides reading, walking, and holding the space-bar. Unfortunately in my experience, some mini-games were laggy or didn't sync up to when I was pressing my keys. This happened the most in the jeepney, videoke, and piano mini-games (which I really wanted to get perfect on!) This could, however, be because I was running the game on my laptop instead of console or PC.The second thing I found less than ideal was the management of texting when multiple chats were active. This could be by design (to emphasize Mark's lack of control over the situation), but having new texts pop up over the arrow to go back and answer them was a little annoying. I didn't find clicking on the text brought me to that chat or anything, but maybe I was just missing something.Another small thing that irked me was the walking path. In a few places (the thrift store comes to mind), pressing an arrow key would cause Mark to move in the opposite direction, following his pre-laid walking path. It took a bit of time to figure out which way to go to get to where I wanted, especially around those aisles. Those three (minor) things aside: what a game.STORYAs you may have seen already from other reviews, this game has multiple sequential "rounds", each with a different ending. The story starts off fairly linear in Round 1, and becomes extremely nonlinear in Round 3. Not all three rounds have to be played, but if you play Round 2 I highly recommend not stopping and playing Round 3 as well.(Aside: Round 1 is an absolute masterclass in the horror of realization and repeated emotional sucker punches. I had to take a two-day break before continuing after that ending. So good.)The dialogue is witty and natural, the characters are charming, and the world building (news articles, social media, posters, background characters) is incredibly well done. I'm not much for romance, but I really enjoyed Mark and Nicole's relationship. I also really enjoyed being able to revisit places in a new light in the different rounds The story itself has its high moments filled with jokes and references, but also moments of raw and deep emotions. The writers did a great job of including the overall theme in many parts of the story, in all three rounds. The game also does an incredible job of both showing and telling, with Mark's feelings or perception of the environment reflected in the sound, scenery, or gameplay. I will say three things about the story. One, the choices you make do not greatly affect the outcome. There are little things that change, but they are minor. Two, Round 3 especially becomes very non-linear (so much so that I retroactively was questioning whether the ending of Round 2 has actually been the ending.) Three, it does use quite a bit of hand-wavy quantum physics ideas to explain to sci-fi/supernatural elements of the plot. I think these are all acceptable concessions though, and didn't take me out of the story much at all.I know some people have grievances with some of the endings, but I wholeheartedly loved them all! I will definitely be going back to replay some scenes to reabsorb details I might've missed on my first playthrough. AUDIO & VISUAL10/10, showstopping, incredible. The gameplay graphics, cutscenes, and scenes are all absolutely beautiful. Kudos to the entire art team for an amazing job. The visuals are originally what made me curious about Until Then, since I'm a big pixel art fan. The characters are all very expressive and have unique mannerisms, and I really liked their prom outfits. The rooms and buildings are well-built and detailed, and the lighting in some scenes is breathtaking. I remember going through scenes for the first time and thinking "oh, this sets the mood perfectly for what is happening." The diversity of angles and closeups was also great, but I'll talk more about that in regards to direction.Of course, can't forget audio. Sound design was also incredible, whether it was background music or environmental sound. I really feel like the music, or lack and contortion thereof, helped drive the emotional aspect of the story. Other people may have mentioned certain background audio taking them "out of the story", which is valid, but I personally didn't have that problem. It just made it seem more realistic to me lol. Special shout out to the dogs barking audio clip and ayooooo uncle. Anti-shout out (but still respect) to the audio manipulation of the carnival during Round 1 (it was super effective!)GAMEPLAYGameplay, gameplay, gameplay. Starting the game with the alarm clock? Genius. Streamlining texting with the space bar? Effective. Numbers for selection? Easy. Arrow key/WASD movement? Classic (though we never really did move Up/Down iirc)Until Then did an excellent job of making a visual novel interactive beyond pointing and clicking. It wasn't just endlessly pressing a key and reading text, and there was decent diversity in keyboard and mouse interactions used. I will admit that I wish there was more clarity on controls, specifically for mini-games. I think even a "trial mode", like how piano practice was a trial for the performance, would be helpful as well. I liked the interaction Mark could have with his phone via texting, email, and the web. The scrolling and following links made it feel a little fresher, despite communication following the same basic concepts as the rest of talking on the game. I also liked the one "quick-time" event there was, a kind of wish there had been more! Or even other small "quick" decisions that could've been made throughout the story.DIRECTIONThis. Now this one right here. Absolutely amazing. The camera work, the perspective choices, the timing of dialogue sections, the close-ups and zoom-outs. Outstanding. This, especially, is what makes Until Then stand out so much to me. I can list multiple scenes where the composition just blew me away with how much it contributed to the energy and emotion of the story.Until Then almost feels like a movie with the way it's directed. There are the in-between bits, sure; walking to the station, walking between classrooms, scrolling through social media. But then there are the scenes. Standing outside 7-11. The confrontation at Nicole's house (both of them.) Mark facing all those television screens. Louise at the door as the slidedeck is frantically being created.The direction of this game makes it really, really special. It has vision. It has purpose. It has, dare I use a Gen Z word, aura. The visionary, purposeful aura of this game has made it stand out so much to me this year, and has made it absolutely one of the best games I've been lucky enough to experience.--Playing this game has taught me a lot. It's taught me a lot about game design, about story design, and about scene direction. It's reminded me of lessons I already knew, about the human heart, hurt, and resilience. I'm looking forward to what Polychroma Games puts out next, and will definitely be staying tuned. If you have 20 hours and enough heart, attention, and money to spare, please play this game. It's worth it.I have to learn Godot now fr

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking into a visual novel like experience similar to "Oxenfree" in terms of interactivity (not genre), I recommend this game. This was a game I played shortly after playing Final Fantasy 16, so I also played this game during a difficult period in my life (one I am still going through). However, I let a month go by after getting the first ending as I started playing Baldur's Gate 3 a bit, and wanted a bit of time away from "Until Then" until I processed the first playthrough and was ready to go into the game again. I'm kind of glad I did, because I realize now that I actually hadn't completed the first playthrough - only the first ending of the game. It wasn't until I picked up the game again in September that I realized that you had to get through two endings before experiencing the true ending.You follow Mark, struggling with school and carrying a lot of grief that he has not accepted and moved on from (this is something you don't find out until you get closer to the first ending). But when he meets Nicole, a transfer student, he begins that journey of healing, along with helping Nicole start hers. It's a very strong, powerful narrative about grief, guilt, and moving on.The minigames you come across at times is cute, and the characters are all fun to learn about - Louise being my favorite. I hated Ridel in the beginning, but now have a soft spot for him since I played the 2nd timeline. I miss Sofia's involvement in the story, even though it was limited. And I'm glad that Cathy finally got seen, because this game was also about Mark's friendship with her. And I felt for Mark - for his pain, his depression, his desire to fix things.The music is also very beautiful. It's quite minimalist as the score mostly uses one instrument per cue, such as the piano or the guitar. Some cues have more instruments going on sometimes. but it's still very minimalist.I enjoyed this game a lot, and I definitely foresee myself replaying it down the line when I'm ready to - and possibly getting all the Steam achievements.

_childDocuments_.review: Upon first boot I noticed that this game is built using Godot.  It immediately brought me to a setting screen where I was allowed to change resolution, adjust sound levels, check controls, and even tweak video settings.  I left everything but the resolution at default settings and then proceeded with the game.  I did take heed from the developer to use Keyboard and mouse as they are still working on controller input issues.  I was greeted by a pleasant piano melody and pixelated rain along with a nice poem.   I noticed the animation in the opening was fluid, stylized, the silhouette was a nice touch I thought.   The opening Ends with the line “The World Haven’t Ended Yet” setting the mood for the game for me.     This brought me to the actual Main Menu where you can see a pretty nice bedroom with a worn closet, some well designed and nicely styled pixel graphics, an overturned laundry basket that was just slightly out of focus gave a sense of depth that you don’t really find in many pixel style games.  Seeing that the Start button is literally the clock’s Alarm sound made me laugh very hard, I have a feeling I’m going to enjoy this game very much.   When the Main character finally woke up in what I have to say is the most Human possible way, I searched the bedroom and clicked on everything I could find.  Which led to a cutscene of the Main Character playing the keyboard.  Once you’re done playing Piano you start flipping through your phone and check your Email. This is where we find out that Your name is Mark Borja.  Mark is a Game obsessed Student who would far rather be playing video games than doing his homework, which we soon find out is going to bite him in the butt pretty heavily.       Now that we have some introductions to the games out of the way, I would rather not give any spoilers for the rest of the game, so instead, Let’s get on with the RatingsGameplay: 3.5 out of 5 Gems.The gameplay of Until then is actually kind of odd, the controls feel fluid, but at the same time the graphics on the screen don’t always match what the controls are.  Since I did get notification from the developer that this is expected I won’t hold it against the game.  There is a lot of clickable easter eggs in the game that I found to be quite interesting, the bulletin board for instance you can “Strategically Transport Equipment to an Alternate Location” as The Fat Electrician would say, You can also get an achievement for liking your own post on the social media app in your phone.  The level of detail they put into it really astounded me.  Good marks.  Soundtrack: 4.5 out of 5 GemsThe soundtrack is almost perfect, The ambient noise brings you to the location,  You can tell whoever designed the game Lived in a place like this,  it is inspired by the Philippines and you can clearly see the influence.   The music is rich and warm, inviting to the ear and combined with the ambient sounds, it really adds a lot of depth to an already deep game.   I was highly impressed.  Graphics: 4.0 out of 5 GemsDespite this being a Pixel art game, the character models, the backgrounds, the props, the shadows, the lighting, the mixture of 2D and 3D to create a depth of field that almost feels like looking at a hologram, I was blown away at how intricately simplistic it is, the longer you look the more you realize just how complex it is.  Even in the first twenty seconds of the game, you can see several different techniques to add depth and dimension to the scene.  Truly Wonderful design I can’t speak highly enough about it.   Difficulty: Not ApplicableBeing a Visual Novel, there really isn’t a difficulty factor to speak of, but that doesn’t really hurt the game in any way, you’re experiencing a story, not really playing a game.  It’s like listening to an Audiobook, you get a massive information dump directly into your cortex and get a nice hit of that sweet, sweet dopamine in return.   Immersion: 5 out of 5 GemsThis game is built to immerse the player. Every second playing, I was captive to it. My alarm is the only thing that snapped me out of it, From the environment, the music, the background noise, I could almost smell the subway funk through my monitor.  There is an incredible amount of immersion in this game to be had.  Trust me when I say this, you will be in center stage of your own private screening of this play, and you will be on the edge of your seat while you do it.  Overall Rating:  4.25 out of 5 GemsUntil Then is amazing,  it takes the concept of a Visual Novel and turns it on it’s head and gives the entire Genre a good spanking,  The animation, the music, and the story that I experienced in just this first hour I would put against any visual novel on the market today and be confident that it would hold up, if not decimate all the competition.  I can flatly say now, everyone needs to grab a copy today because you will be missing out otherwise.   Final thoughts: So, the real question is, Is Until Then worth the Retail price of 19.99?   No, it’s worth more, Honestly, I believe that the developers should have went a minimum of 24.99 on this title and it would still sell handsomely.   I truly enjoyed every minute of playing this game and look forward to playing it more in the future, Between the complex characters, the beautiful music (even when Mark is practicing and misses a note it still sounds good and adds to further the immersion), and the highly interactive every part of the gameplay, you really can’t go wrong.  It’s a nearly perfect Visual Novel, the only bug I came across had to do with controls, and since those are known and being worked on, I absolutely will not hold that against the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is genuinely one of the greatest I've ever played. As for storytelling, the game is perfect. People say the dialogue is weird, but it's teen dialogue that is really really common around people my age, 18-22, and very much increases the realness of the game. Everything feels so real and connected, and the story just feels like a situation you can put yourself in. You get lost in the world and the way you learn about events going on feels so natural. The game is also LGBTQ+ friendly, so among all perfect scores, that adds a few more points, too. I've only completed one of a few endings, and to be honest, the ending felt on point with what you'd expect, but I also wish they went easier on the player cause I'm broken. Compared to Omori, this game is a close second to storytelling and absolute heartbreak, but also, with this games main story getting 12 hours out of me as opposed to Omori's 50 hours on one ending, I think it's obvious time was a big part in how Omori takes storytelling. (P.S. Omori is my example of a genuinely perfect game with a perfect story, so I always base my opinions on storytelling games based on how close they are to Omori). Visuals: The visuals are out of this world. I couldn't believe just how well they got the environment down, and how cinematic the game looks. It's like something straight out of a movie. Hell, I got popcorn mid playing so I could enjoy this game like I would a movie. There are times where you wish you weren't playing so you could pay attention to the visuals, and a big part of me wishes this was just a long movie I could watch.Smoothness: The game is very smooth and I play on a really, really bad computer. 1060 with a i5-3600k. I saw nothing go down in performance the whole game except for one minigame which was very lighting-centric. I only had to restart the game once because I couldn't hit escape and change a setting, but that was it. Characters: It feels like a real world. You see reoccuring characters that are just background characters but you see they have their own interesting stories. The main character is very likeable and makes the game very easy to play without stopping. I think people think the guy is annoying cause he makes mistakes you can't control, but it's not like you decide what the main character does, you decide his actions based on who he already is as a character that's existed before we play as him. In that way you feel sympathetic and learn to love him for all he is. The other main characters are amazing, too, and I wish you spent more time with them. Naturally doing so would only add time to the game and not much story, but I'd be willing to take that downside cause I see it as a plus. Conclusion: I think this game is absolutely worth the money, and I wouldn't be surprised if it gets talked about as much as Omori or Undertale because of how good it is. This game is a staple for any player wanting a visually stunning game, lovable characters, wholesome gameplay, and a storyline bound to make you cry and look at the world differently. I couldn't reccomend this game enough, which is why I got three of my friends to buy and play the game already. I really hope this game becomes a staple in the community. Thank you!

_childDocuments_.review: (Spoiler free review)I discovered this game relatively shortly before its release, looking for games similar to 'A Space for the Unbound', being my favorite one. I played the demo and instantly fell under its charm, so I impatiently awaited the game's release.On release day, I bought the game as soon as possible and continued with the story, and I have to say that I was absolutely not disappointed, what a great game. It was a totally magical experience, rich in so many ways, which warmed my heart as much as it broke it, and which I now consider to be ex-aequo with 'A Space for the Unbound' as my favorite games.The story and characters are extremely engaging, and it didn't take me long to become really attached to them. The characters are treated with such realism that some of them reminded me strongly of people I know. The storyline, which I won't go into in detail to avoid spoilers, is stunning and surprising, and there were many times when I had to force myself to stop the game so as not to finish it in one sleepless night, being so captivated by the plot.The game's best point, in my opinion, is its realism. I was surprised from the very first minutes of gameplay by the way this world is portrayed, extremely realistic thanks to the many simple, everyday elements of real life that are rarely properly represented in video games. A very simple example is the ticket machine in the subway station in the first few minutes of the game, a very simple element but one that allows you to jump straight into the daily life of the story. However, the element which really stood out for its realism the most was the mobile phone. The way messages, the "Facebook" timeline and web pages - which take a little while to load and display properly, for example - are handled is absolutely fantastic. The way the characters speak is also handled with great care, I really felt like I was talking to classmates with their own way of speaking, something not often well done in video games in my opinion, often giving the impression of older adults trying to express themselves like youngsters, which was absolutely not the case here.The graphics are magnificent, and I loved the half 2D, half 3D style, with a very realistic treatment of light that gave a lot of depth and liveliness to each of the daily locations (which, however, was quite hard on my GPU, I don't know if I was an isolated case or not, talking to other people I got the impression that this was the case but it's nevertheless something I'd like to note). I enjoyed this visual approach so much that I filled my PC with various screenshots of every scene and moment in the game. I don't know if this is planned for the future, but I'd love to acquire an artbook of this game, whether digital or physical, and I'd be delighted to open my wallet for such a purchase.The gameplay is nothing special, it's basically a visual novel with occasional gameplay moments, such as the piano rhythm game moments, but on the whole, there's no real gameplay, it's more like an interactive movie, but it really does not feel too much like it, as I believe it would very probably not work as a movie.The music is wonderful, perfectly conveying the emotions of the scenes, and I have to admit that on several occasions it made me cry, and the way the main OST of the game is inserted into the story is brilliant. I very much hope that all the game's ost will be officially released soon. Once again, this is something I'd happily open my wallet to acquire.The game provides a real life lesson, a superb moral that lets us really think about our past, present and future actions, what the right choices are in our lives, and what determines whether those choices are right or wrong. Opening our eyes to the world and the people around us. Thinking about ourself, but also about others, and how to balance that. The end of the game, the whole last chapter, absolutely broke me. My eyes were completely filled with tears (so much that it was difficult to read the dialogue) and I was absolutely speechless. When the credits rolled, I was absolutely drained (in a good way). What an incredible experience it was.One of the few games that has had a profound effect on me, and will continue to do so for the foreseeable future. 'Until Then' was absolutely masterful, thank you, thank you for this experience. I will treasure this game in my heart for a long, long time from now.I'm now going to take a short break from the game to reflect on what I've just experienced and then return to the game to complete it 100%.Beautiful, touching, gripping and with a superb life message. 10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: How do I even start? This is arguably my favorite game of all time, and I don't say that lightly. There turns out there are three separate main "playthroughs" that all tie together into a cohesive and undeniably beautiful story. _childDocuments_.review: Imagine waking up to the sound of a Filipino rooster yelling "TAHOOOOO!" and knowing your day might end with a time-bending existential crisis wrapped in pixel art so detailed it feels like a Makoto Shinkai painting mated with a nostalgic fever dream. - This metaphysical journey called "Until Then".First, you’re chilling as Mark Borja, a kid whose biggest worries SHOULD be flunking a class project or whether his friends notice his HAIRCUT. But OH NO, the devs said, "Let’s slap some sci-fi, emotional trauma, and a metric ton of philosophical ponderings on this bad boy." And before you know it, you're deep in the trenches of Mark's life, unraveling relationships more tangled than your earbuds on a Monday morning.Cathy. OH. MY. GOD. CATHY. She’s the heart of this game, a chaotic tomboy queen in pajamas and sweaters who will steal your heart and then emotionally crush you with her storyline. And the game KNOWS you love her. It’s like the devs built her out of pure serotonin and nostalgia, then dangled her in front of you like, "Don’t you DARE stop playing, or you’ll never know her FATE!"But wait- here comes Nicole, with her mysterious time-warping nonsense. Suddenly, you’re doing experiments that feel like they were ripped out of a pretentious sci-fi TED Talk. Double-slit experiments? Past lives? DUUUDEEE..... .The pacing? Like riding a jeepney in Metro Manila traffic: one second, you're cruising through heartfelt moments, and the next, you're stuck in a banana swamp of metaphors and monologues. But do I care? NO, because the soundtrack SLAPS! the visuals are STUNNING! and somehow, Polychroma Games convinced me to care about a fictional teenager’s texting habits.In short, Until Then is a fever dream, a love letter, and a slap to the face all rolled into one. It’s 20 hours of chaotic brilliance that will make you laugh, cry, and question why your life doesn’t have its own bestie Cathy. 14/10.I feel like I wrote this review many times but not sure...
