_childDocuments_.review: What can I say? I've been balancing on the fence with this one.I loved this game. But sometimes-I didn't. So, what is the issue? The game is first and foremost: gorgeous. I love the art style and the music (can) be really captivating and emotionally driven. For anyone who has experienced loss, for anyone who loves music (especially anyone who has played piano), and anyone who enjoys watching the internal struggles of teen-hood mixed with some sci-fi elements : this is for you. To avoid any highly potential spoilers, I will try to keep all my information/review as vague as possible. Whooo this was a ride. Let me just say there is a point in the game, that, if I never went to Reddit for answers, I would have never actually seen. I was quite confused and a little miffed, and wanted answers. Then I realized what I had to do, and, let's be real, they should have made it more obvious (if you know, you know). It may help with some early quitters on the game. Because, let me clear: the best part of this game is the middle chunk and BOY is it captivating. It's one of those moments where you just HAVE to keep going to know the ending. I love that feeling. But-you must be confused, why would I talk so highly about something and NOT recommend it? And I really (really!) wanted to recommend it. Especially because it's an indie game.A part of me still does. Because when it hits...man, it just hits. It had me crying and gasping and guessing till the very end. Actually, I'm STILL guessing at the end because there are some things that just didn't fully make sense to me. I'm not even talking about a one single relationship. I have questions about many things. Like his best friend. It left me confused and looking around going: did I miss something? I don't understand. There was a couple side plots that just never felt solidified very well. I wasn't the only one, come to find out a lot of people had the same questions after fully completing it.It felt like the game had so many strong points and everything that led up to the very end  Like it tried to smash everything together and when you pull out the cake it looks amazing on the outside, but it's still kind of uncooked on the inside. I still feel bad not recommending it, because this WAS a good game. But...there were too many things at (the real end) that made me go, "but I don't understand?" And while there were plenty of puzzle pieces that WERE put together and explained, not everything made sense in the end to me. Maybe that's the point. Maybe it's supposed to be left to interpretation. Anyway, love me some Cath and Ridel. The characters were all well done, the setting was gorgeous and terrifying at the same time, and I love how real all the interactions felt with everyone. The mini games were a hit or miss but they were alright. I wish I had some warning before throwing me into them sometimes though-I sat watching my screen waiting for my little race car to move for a solid minute until I realized I was supposed to actually drive the thing and not watch it, oops. (Additionally, while the piano was very pretty, I don't want to hear that song again after hearing it so many times).This is a good visual novel that could have been great. I think it needs to work on tying up the ending better, oh and can we please have a way to let the dialogue play without pushing the spacebar/a for each conversation? Sometimes I want to sit back with some popcorn and just enjoy the show. :p I'm not telling others NOT to give this a go. But it's hard for me to recommend it. I feel a little sad, it did make me cry a few times, but mostly because I felt that my favorite character never got a good explanation for her background. Again, it may just be me. Maybe it's not. Perhaps you should play it and decide for yourself. <3

name: Frogun
detailed_description: Become the best explorer in the land in this cute, charming retro themed adventure! Renata's parents are world-renown explorers, archeologists and inventors that travel all over the world uncovering the secrets of the past, bringing her with them in their expeditions. However, in their latest adventure, they decide to leave her at the base camp - the Beelzebub ruins are said to be too dangerous! For three whole days she waits, her pride hurt and bored out of her mind, until she realized: if they haven't returned yet, something must have happened to them! In a hurry she grabs her parents' last invention, the Frogun, and heads to the ruins to rescue them, and prove that she's as capable as them! Explore colorful levels full of crispy pixelated ruins, freezing snow caps, and scorching lava swamps in a modern representation of the lowpoly aesthetic From levers to buttons, lethal traps, and adorable enemies, there are countless ways to use your Frogun to navigate the world! Race Renata's rival and fight big bosses Find secret areas or shortcuts by mastering the grappling mechanics! How nimble are you? Collect emblems by fulfilling level challenges, and discover the stories of other adventurers through hidden diary notes Visit the hatter to trade your coins for hats, bestiary entries, game art, and more A posable photo mode to let you show off your creativity Unlockable 2-player duel arenas to challenge your friends!

_childDocuments_.review: + Main character design is great+ Some good enemy designs (visually)+ Environments can be appealing with nice vibrant colours+ Some cute idle animations+ Photo mode while basic is a nice addition- Slow movement feels bearable in the early stages but quickly becomes dull- Grapple is under-utilized, feels bad to use, unclear about when it will/will not work- Lots of visual enemy issues (slugs glitching out over terrain, bats blatantly teleporting back to their starting position after their attack etc)- Dangerously boring & uninspired level design (I can't think of one instance where I thought a set piece, obstacle or challenge was clever or engaging in any way)- Coins/pots/chests etc are scattered everywhere for seemingly no reason other than to keep you busy. This makes dying feel even worse as having to collect the over-abundance of coins was already tedious the first time round- Insane amount of waiting for moving platforms which are used far too often- Race stages making you do another loop of the stage is a drag & Jake being able to stun you is absolutely baffling, especially seeing as some races start and go straight into 1 tile thick sections- Bosses are dreadful, forcing you to wait out long, easy attack phases before you can get a hit in only to do it all over again (this has been solved in multiple 3D platformers in the past already & it's mind-boggling how bosses like this are still being designed in 2022. The game would be outright improved if they were just removed all together)- Forgettable OST. I can't remember a single song after 12 hours of playtime- Loads of unpleasant SFX, mostly when trying to imitate the Banjo-Kazooie style dialogue. Nearly all of them are genuinely uncomfortable to listen to- Showing expert time trials on the emblem explanation but not having them presented to you until the start of the bonus world is confusing & feels sloppy- The money situation is completely wack with required farming if you want to buy everything- Given the option to retry the final stage after defeating the boss on screen but forced into the long, unskippable final cutscene & credits anyway every single time- Final moment of gameplay before the climax of the story is the boss T-posing during his death animation - Far too long for how basic it isMy biggest gripe is how the game is clearly just not finished. It seems to be in the Early Access state while being presented as a finished game, which is a bit rich. Saying the game as a whole is rough around the edges would be an understatement but even with more polish there's no saving the dire state of the level design.

_childDocuments_.review: So I tried the update as promised and well.... not much is improved. The issues caused by high refresh are definitely fixed, props to that, but the other and main issue of my review is still very much present. They really tried to help fix it but it just doesn't work as it is, the main way they tried to fix the issue is "you can now shoot twice in the air before having to need to land to fire again" This would in theory fix the chain targeting over pits issue cause you get a second chance, it doesn't really in practice.The main issue is the time to correct your shot before its too late isn't even a full second, as you fall after a shot that fast, and most people are firing their first shot assuming they make it. So people miss their shot and then have to train their brain to let themselves fall an undefined amount of partial seconds to make their second chance line up. I deliberately did a few test runs of this intentionally missing my first shot just to test the reaction time needed and yes its possible, it always is, but its rather difficult in a game that's 100% chill and relaxing most other places. This game still suffers an identity crisis around the halfway mark of the game and I don't understand why it had to be this way. I think a really simple fix for this would just be widen the time frame of the sections where you have to use enemies to chain across pits, basically making the shot perform less "2D" in these parts because that's why this issue happens. The frog gun works way too much in a rigid 2D plane that if you're not exactly in those parameters, its going to miss. For 95% of the game this is a non issue, it only rears its ugly head around small targets ie enemies, and especially over instant death pits.Kind of a bait and switch. In general starts out a fun and fair platformer where there's only few challenging points.Around the halfway mark starts making you heavily rely on chaining hookshots with your gun over instant death pits, not even in the secret areas either, main path. The game's detection is very poor with this feature to make it required, coupled with the time to line up your next shot in the chain being often half a second. Every stage has a no deaths medal too which makes all of this a very frustrating experience around the halfway point. Honestly feels like nobody tested the game and asked "is this going to be fun?". Seen forums also mention that the detection gets even worse than usual with high refresh rate monitors, which only adds to the frustration. I do doubt even with a patch that the trickshotting will get much better and not just be an exercise in frustration.A shame, cause the first half of the game is pretty fun. I will be trying the 1.9 update when it comes out of beta and I hope they can sort this. But we'll see.

_childDocuments_.review: Frogun is a game that does plenty of things well. The soundtrack and art direction do convey an older game. Not sure if it's similar specifically to N64 games, since they seem to have a lower polygon count, but the feeling is there.The issues really start almost halfway into the game, where it wants you to do precision platforming with controls that aren't really made to be precise. There are some things that help a bit, like the ability to shoot twice while airborne, but it doesn't help a lot, and it slows down the game-play. The real problem of this is that a lot of these harder sections are farther away from checkpoints, so you will have to go through easier sections multiple times, making the game really tedious. This was done correctly in the beginning of the game, with the Obsidian Skulls; you have to out of your way for a challenge to get them, they are usually well hidden, and most of them are right next to checkpoints.I do think that the game brought me enough joy for the price that it has, but as a complete product, I do not recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Frogun is a game clearly inspired by the original Crash Bandicoot series, offering gameplay that focuses on either slow, methodical collectible gathering or fast-paced time trials. The protagonist, Renata, moves relatively slowly and has limited actions—she can jump and use her gun to defeat enemies or as a hookshot to traverse walls and other objects. However, the gun's performance is inconsistent. Vertically, the crosshair might indicate a target, but the hookshot fails if Renata is too high. Horizontally, the gun can latch onto distant mushrooms yet might miss nearby walls. The camera, while generally serviceable, struggles to keep up during chain hook sequences, making already difficult sections even more challenging. The triggers for the fail animation are positioned too high, especially over water. If you step off a platform, you die instantly. The game isn't really hard, but adjusting the position of these triggers would reduce much frustration. The bosses are easy and boring except last one having few very quick attacks with little time to respond. Visuals are very charming with great character and enviromental desings. Songs are few and servicable.Completing the game can feel like a giant slog. After mastering every level, you still need to spend 2-3 hours grinding one just to buy out the shop. Tying artwork unlocks to master rank time trial [which aren't needed for "Completionist" achievment] and making coins a limited, non-farmable resource and adjusting hat prices to match coin availability seems like such a basic idea that it's baffling why it wasn't implemented that way.I had two crashes and no major bugs. Despite my complaints, I would still recommend this to platformer enthusiasts, but maybe not to completionists.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR; The game looks pleasing, but lacks a lot of polish/refinement that ends up making it feel like a beta version more than an actual finished product. I want this game to be the best it can be, but the current version of it does not hold up.I want to start off with the fact that I LOVE the style that this game has. It's incredibly charming and appealing to look at and never gets dull. The aesthetics are on point throughout the whole game; the artists that worked on this deserve a world of praise.That's the only good thing I have to say about this game. Everything else about it is either lack-luster or completely flawed to the point of frustration and aggravation.Gameplay is decent at first, where the grappling mechanic is nice and fun to use with lack of threats and various objects/enemies to grab without seeming too tedious. Past the 2nd area, though, it becomes a lot like skiing: going downhill fast. The jumps and lack of control for aiming are a mixture for failure and make it difficult to find platforming enjoyable. The final areas are filled with more complex jumps/chain-grapples that end up making it incredibly easy to fall into the bottomless pit and having to restart AND recollect everything you already did.The grappling mechanic makes no sense what so ever. Sometimes you miss your shot, die, and end up at the beginning of the level right before the checkpoint OR you end up hitting a shot you didn't intend to, die, and end up at the beginning of the level right before the checkpoint. You can make the tiniest adjustment to your angle and end up WAY off. It's simply inconsistent and frustrating.The movement, especially at the later areas, become more and more apparent that free movement hinder more than help the player when trying to align shots and dodge obstacles/attacks (see: Beelzebub). Free movement mixed with obstacles that are fixed to a grid end up with hitboxes that are unfair when you are JUST BARELY within the range of it and you get hit for not making the MOST MINUTE of adjustments.Other minor gripes: There are plenty of sound effects that are grating/unpleasantly loud, some animations are jank and end up glitching, too many coins to collect without much of a reward doing so, and the Golden area being the same color as 1 coins makes it difficult to collect all the coins in some levels.All in all, I am disappointed more than anything. It looked as if it had so much possibility-- and it still somewhat does! -- but I can't recommend a game that is lacking proper play testing/refining. I would love for this game to get updates in the future that make it more easily accessible for more casual players to finish and just improve the gameplay as a whole.

_childDocuments_.review: Great Game. Has great visual style with plenty of variety in the level themes. Main character design is very fun and charming. Music is also quite good, although not amazing.Very traditional get to the end of the level but with heavy collectathon influence, to the point that collecting everything in the levels is the main fun of the game and not just getting to the end of the level despite not needing to do it to complete the game.Camera is quite good, but in later levels it requires you to switch between differents angles on the fly during the middle of jumps, which is tricky and awkward. But you can get the hang of it over time.the race levels are weak and not as good as the normal levels. They require you to repeat the same challenge twice since there is already a collectable that requires you to beat the level fast to get it. And trying to get them both at the same time means that when you start the level again to collect everything, you are force to first race that boy again anyway.And the bosses are easily the worst part of the game, they are very long fights with a lot of waiting around for easy attacks, even with the last two bosses that have actually hard to dodge moves, there is still a lot of waiting around. The further you go into the game the longer and worse they become. They can also be full of bull***t moments where you take damage when it's not your fault, and there is no extra health during the boss, so every damage matters. Combined with the later bosses that are so long and full of tricky moves that when you die it means you are gonna have to go through all that wating again. It is the definition of frustrating.

_childDocuments_.review: What starts out as a beautiful retro platformer devolves into an exercise in frustration by the later levels, I hate posting review like this as the game clearly has promise, but the grapple mechanic simply isn't responsive enough for some of the quick sucessions of grapples the later levels require of you. _childDocuments_.review: I think some of the negative reviews for this game are slightly over-dramatic. I had a really great time with the game and I nearly 100% completed it, minus some collectible grinding (which I'll address later). If you are the kind of person who enjoys a retro-style platforming game that pushes you to go for completion (think early Crash Bandicoot), you will like it. You can read the TLDR at the end if you want to skip the details.I'll start with the cons. I agree with everyone saying the controls need to be refined. They do. A lot of times the auto-aiming cross hairs will appear on a surface, but then your grapple simply won't attach. It happens pretty often and it can be frustrating how inaccurate the frogun is. In later stages the level design requires you to be precise with aiming and timing, and the grapple mechanics are not up to the task. You will have to die over and over again and hope you can get the perfect angle on a shot in one of your attempts. The other major negative I've seen a lot is the required grinding for achievements, which I also agree is pretty terrible. If you play the game normally trying to collect everything along the way, you will have enough coins to buy like 1/3 of the collectibles. That leaves you with more than 30,000 coins to get after the game is over. 100 coins per minute is about as fast as someone can reasonably farm them, so that means 30,000 / 100 = 300 minutes, or 5 hours of pure mindless grinding. That's being charitable with the time too, it could easily take longer and it feels needlessly disrespectful of people's time. BUT, you obviously don't need to go for 100%.With all of that said, here are the pros. The PS1 art style is great. If you like the look of it from the Steam page, you will enjoy it throughout the game. Every stage, the enemies, the overworld, it's all great to look at. The stages are also genuinely fun to run through. Be warned, they DO require you to do multiple plays of each one - one run for collecting everything, and maybe 1-2 more for a speed run and no-death run. However, I found that aspect to be enjoyable and there weren't many stages that overstayed their welcome. The game has a good amount of challenge so it's not just mindlessly collecting everything sitting in plain sight. I felt accomplished when finally beating tricky platforming sections after trying them multiple times. The poor controls are somewhat offset by the fact that there are no lives to lose, so you can keep retrying the same hard sections pretty rapidly. The majority of levels can be completed in under 2 minutes when you're not collecting everything, so the pacing is good. It really feels like a nostalgic '90s game that is a lot of fun to play.TLDR: The controls are fairly bad, but that is offset by not having a lives system and being able to retry difficult sections over and over quickly. You are also required to do multiple plays of each level to collect everything, but the game is fun enough to justify that. If you like old-school platforming and collectathon games, especially if you have nostalgia for them, you will have a good time with this game.

_childDocuments_.review: --Quickie recommend.Critisicms.Hope for a mechanics.--It's a super fun collect-a-thon platformer. With block based adventure levels. The main appeal of the game is trying to 100% levels, it's simple twist on chameleon twist, and progressing through it's adventure levels and smashing pots.The enemies/hazards, and especially bosses can be jank a lot of the time. Not interacting in the same way, not having tells on their animations. It really shouldn't be a problem if you take the dozens of health pickups in the optional chests. (which i didn't, owch)The graphic style is adorable and pleasant. Music either mid, or bangers. The level design is really good, even if the polish isn't. Has a fun optional battle mode (which needs more stuff to shoot at eachother!  If you like collecting, or platformers. You'd enjoy this game and forgive it's shortcomings... Except the grappling chains.1) The grabbling chains in the game is beyond frustrating and not polished. The main issue is when you look towards a target, a red cross-hair appears on it in the middle of it. You shoot, and your frogun tongue goes above or below it.  The cross-hair should accurately reflect where you will actually hit the target, or your tongue should have a bigger hitbox to grab those damn skulls.Most, if not all, casual players will get alienated with how hard the jank air grappling is. It really needs some TLC, because it's the only roadblock to this being a universal recommendation from me.The ability to shoot twice in the air definitely alleviates some of the stress. But it added in a infinite wall climb that you can use to cheese levels (I was able to skip the final race level using it, and a lot of other challenges).2) The patch to the coins/gems ruined a lot of the collect-a-thon appeal to me. I played the first half of the game pre-patch, and I was praising it's collect-a-thon aspect. Collecting coins and gems, and being worried about saving the progress at a checkpoint is exhilerating. Earlier levels aren't fun now that you can just deathwarp after you collect what you need :\It feels like a knee jerk reaction to the later levels, because there is very few check points, and a lot of death pits on them.  Please at least add a toggle so players can enjoy the original challenge. I definitely want to play that way when I revisit the game!3) Please show a difference between chests that gives you hearts, and chests that don't! I played through it all 3 hearts the whole time since I like a good challenge. I know other players who would think the same way. A simple graphic would help save players the time from saving and loading the game if the chest contains a heart.I'd hope to see a frogun 2 in the future! And definitely will play your next game dev! Some mechanics I dreamed of while playing:- It happens sometimes in this game, if you shoot the frogun at the top lip of a ledge, it pulls you over the top of the block. I really wished it was intentional, and easier to do. It would open up a lot of creativity on movement to be able to hit the top of blocks to leap frog up on top of them.- For being a game named Frogun, he has little uses. When you pick up enemies with your frogun, it would be awesome to shoot them to pick up coins.      o Flying enemies fly straight through the air.      o Grounded enemies roll until they fall of a block, or crash into enemy/wall     o Even something crazy, like spinning your analog with a enemy in your gun to spin them around your body. Like cappy in Mario Odyssey!- Bungee Jumping. It might hurt poor Frogun. But attaching to a special block, and plunging down into a pit to grab collectables.  In games like these, breaking up the gameplay loop is very refreshing, and gets you excited to to continue the adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun little PSX/N64 styled 3D platformer that feels like a mix between Crash Bandicoot, Ristar, and Captain Toad: Treasure Tracker. For the price of $7 on a Steam sale, this is pretty good. I really like the gameplay, it's pretty, picking up enemies and throwing them is pretty amusing. The game has a cute art direction.I do have a few things to note regarding technical issues with the game (Most severe first, with the more inconsequential stuff last), and then some minor qualms about the sound design.I could attempt to fix some of the technical issues by creating a BepInEx mod, but I can't say for certain if I can find exactly what needs to be fixed (without simply bruteforcing a hook that grabs onto a function that changes the game's resolution) thanks to the game using IL2CPP (essentially it compiles Mono/C# IL code to C++ machine code, and it obfuscates a ton of things), which makes it more difficult to mod.Onto the sound design, things sound relatively decent, but I personally don't feel like the level finish (or when you finish bosses) has enough of an emotional impact compared to the standard level music. In other words, it doesn't give enough of a rewarding feel to it.It's a pretty fun game so far, just make sure to follow my advice by enabling SteamInput and using Proton Experimental on Linux and the Steam Deck to avoid most of the issues.EDIT: I've put together a mod to add ultrawide support to the game, trying to minimize stuttering issues (right now it's a simple FixedUpdate value workaround), and a way to offset the camera distance and height, that can be found here:

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very nice game that is really let down by a few issuesFirst is the camera which is not good, and you can't fix it, you'd think the lock to 45° option would actually lock to 45° but no it's slightly floaty in a way that makes it not work like it should (if you move or are on a moving object the camera slightly "bends" away from the direction you are moving towards, it should be 100% rigid PS1 style (Alundra 2 does camera better than this and if you've played Alundra 2 you know that ain't a compliment) , then there's the whole load of issue with getting jumpscared by random geometry or stage effects that is very close to the camera but very far from what you actually care about, that could be fixed with a Art of Rally style solution where a small circle around you is always visible through any geometry.Second is the whole main mechanic (the frogun, which is a linear grapple hook more or less) deciding to be really jank at random times, most egregious example being the reticle sometimes being grey while you're in range, or being red and  on an object but once you fire actually missing that object entirely (and no it's not a case of the object or the character moving between me seeing the reticle and me pressing the fire button as I've seen it happen on entirely static situations as well)Autoaim is equally janky, sometimes deciding you're not actually aiming at the literal singular object in the vague direction you're pointing at but sometimes making you do a 180° turn away from where you're trying to point at because reasons.Not using autoaim is also not really an option as stick aim is too jittery and Dpad aim too rigid to handle what the game throws at you and while aim ode helps it doesn't work mid air.Third is the game goes from very easy (not a bad thing by itself) to very hard once it introduce grappling from walls to walls or object to object or even  walls to object that are over the void, walls and some enemies being especially bad as they do not give you any height on impact, anything with walls over void is ridiculously tight in execution and require Dpad usage more or less as autoaim doesn't help here, and the worst part is the hardest of such sections are the first ones, actually the whole difficulty curve is backwards as first you have objects and walls that give you no or little height on impact thus very tight timing to succeed then latter on you have objects that need you to either come from the side or top to avoid damage but are substantially more lenient in general in terms of execution and then you have enemies that give you ridiculous height and thus plenty of time to react and adjust or object that sometimes move but don't require being hit in a specific way also going from wall to wall over the void stops being a thing latter on as well despite being the hardest application of that mechanic.This single mechanic is by itself the biggest difficulty spike and most badly introduced mechanic, it's even funny that the tutorial section for that mechanic is something I used glitches on my first time through because that seemed way easier than dealing with the timing required.What that means for the game is that the difficulty is best described as easy overall but unfair and frustrating.Other than that it's mostly nitpicks like the expert time trials being too tight for their own good on a few levels but being ludicrously lenient on many others, it's hard to exactly understand how to deal with some enemies as some will be only vulnerable at some specific not necessarily obvious points or some will seem invulnerable until you figure out that you need to precisely shove an object in their face and nothing else, the "sticky enemies" bug where some enemies will attach to your hitbox if you come to close and by attach I mean they will damage you continuously until they decide to go away (the grasshopper enemy is especially bad about it), the final encounter of the second boss rush having some attacks that are completely ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and can hit you without any real possibility of reacting and finally the need to grind a fairly substantial amount of coins to unlock everything but lacking any fast or interesting ways to do so.IF you can power through the jank and frustration that comes with it it's actually a nice game, but I honestly don't think it's the majority of people that could, especially hen the game introduces itself in both looks and gameplay as being rather on the more casual side of things and when most failures don't really seem to be your fault (at least not entirely) but mostly a combo of camera and mixed signals from the game with a hint of bad difficulty curve.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun platformer game that's about as hard as you make it.Frogun, on the surface, is a beginner friendly platformer game that will let just about anyone complete it.  However, as the game progresses and you learn more about it, it becomes a tough as nails precision platformer that will have you pulling out your hair.First, if you're not a completionist, then this game is pretty breazy, but it does start to require more and more precision as you progress through the worlds.  The penultimate and ultimate worlds both require you to make some blind jumps and do some precisely timed jumps to make it through.  Thankfully, you have infinite lives and each level only takes less than 3 minutes, most taking less than 1 minute, so even the most frustrating levels won't have you losing too much time on them.Now, the one major exception to the relative ease of the game is the final boss.  The final boss has the most complicated move set of all the bosses and requires the most number of hits, and it is the most difficult boss to do damage to.  Between all these things, it took me about half an hour to finally beat him the first time, despite beating all the other bosses on my first or second attempt.Now, if you want to complete this game, be prepared for some serious frustrations and a huge time investment.  There are also several layers of completing the game, and each added layer is going to make your life worse.  First, each level has several items to collect to obtain "emblems".  These include: Collecting all coins in the level, collecting two special emeralds in a single run, collect a special section of the level to get obsidian, find the hidden notes, and complete the level under two different time constraints.So, most of the collectibles in the level are fun to find and get, but there are a few levels that require non-standard movement or searching to find/collect.  For the most part, this isn't that bad, but it's annoying to search for one missing item over and over again with now hints as to where they are in the level.Once you've collected everything in a level, you'll next need to complete the speed runs.  There are two speeds you'll need to beat to get all the emblems.  One is the shown level time, which is usually pretty easy to accomplish so long as you just run through the level ignoring all the collectibles.  The second is the expert time, and to achieve this time, you'll have to skip several portions of the level as well as performing perfecting elsewhere.  On the bright side, you time resets back to 0 automatically when you die and go back to the start, and it will reset to the time you hit a checkpoint when you return to them after dying.  On the down side, this reset happens AFTER you actually reset, so it looks like they don't reset.  All this means is that I ended up resetting the levels manually for a long time before I realized this was the case.In addition to these special emblems, there is also an extra world to complete after beating the main game.  These levels are just a set of more difficult levels, but the don't require anything special aside from time and effort.  That is, with the exception, of the final "Extreme" boss rush.  The extreme boss rush is brutally difficult and I don't really think it's worth the effort, but it's doable if you really want to do it.Now is the final piece of completion, that I haven't done, because it requires un-fun grinding after already completing everything in the game.  This final peice is purchasing every hat and gallery image in the game.  To make this happen, you're going to need 30K plus coins.  After completing the entire game, replaying levels several times to get all the emblems, and grinding a little afterwards, I only made about 15K coins and had tons of coins to go to get everything.  Honestly, I think the cost of everything should be significantly reduced after completing the game, or at least completing all the emblems, because it's just not fun to grind for these coins after already getting everything else in the game.With all that laid out, I only have one more thing to mention; Bugs.  This game does NOT have a tone of bugs, but the ones that exist are annoying.  One bug that is prevailent is the lack of animation cancelling.  Whenever you skip a cutscene (which you're likely going to do a lot of) Renata is stuck in her surprised animation when you retain control of her.  Luckily, you can still move with her, but it's a little weird to see her slide while reeling after every cutscene.  Second, During the thirds boss, the ice wizard, they have an attack with an associated sound that is unaffected by the volume settings.  So, unless you've left all the sound values at max, this sound is going to be extremely loud and come out of nowhere.  Third, and this is partly my fault, if you reset a level enough times, the timer will no longer start and you'll be unable to open the menu.  This can be fixed by dying, but it really shouldn't happen in the first place.Now, these last nit picks might just be me, but some of movement techniques that you'll use in the game have some issues.  The biggest and most recognizable one is the aiming reticle.  The reticle more often than not is lying to you.  The way it works is that you'll see a grey reticle if something is being pointed at but too far away, then it turns red if it's close enough to "tongue" and pointed at.  The issue is two-fold: the grey reticle is often wrong, as the tongue will hit things sooner than the reticle says it will. Next, and this is a much larger issue, when jumping, the reticle will almost always be wrong when it says that you're locked on.  This is a major issue as you need to jump and tongue items dozens of times to make it through the game, and sometimes you'll see the reticle hit the target you're expecting, only to shoot over the object or under it, killing you instantly.The last thing is Frogun has some advanced movement tech, and I found it to be incredibly inconsistent.  The main advanced tech is tonguing a platform above Renata and her jumping up the ledge.  However, I couldn't figure out what would allow her to climb up and what made her just fall off.  This really sucks, because you need to use this technique in a few levels to beat the expert times.  If this tech isn't intended, then it's be great to see some ghost data in levels to see how to beat the expert times without "cheating".  If it IS intended, then it'd be great to see some explanation on how to consistently make it happen.TL,DR:  This is a great game that's worth your time and effort, but I suggest ignoring the completionist emblems because they really aren't worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: The first half of the game is enjoyable. But later levels have some platforming that isn't really supported by the game's control. I'd say that the auto aim causes a lot of issues too.There are instances where you can see a platform beneath you but jumping onto it will cause you to die.I'm sure that this is an oversight but it feels weird when the game even has a speedrun mode, but shortcuts will kill you.It's not a terrible game, but I just wouldn't recommend it with the amount of other platformers exist.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game, and I feel terrible for leaving a negative review, but I can't really recommend it in good faith.The presentation is fantastic. The vibrant retro-inspired artstyle is lovely, Renata is an adorable protagonist, and it's got a fun upbeat soundtrack. The first 2/3 of the game was a delight. The frogun grappling mechanic works decently enough for the simpler levels. It was a relaxing and enjoyable experience, and the optional collectibles felt like they presented a fair challenge in this part of the game. Then the difficulty spike hits around the tar pit level, and the game begins bordering on masochistic. The player is introduced to chain-grappling, which might be the most inconsistent and awkward-feeling mechanic I've experienced in any platformer. Later levels start demanding pixel-perfect jumps, weaving between hazards with huge hitboxes, and chaining together multiple grapples over insta-death pits.This might have made for a good challenge, if the controls were more polished. But what killed the game for me was the checkpoint system. Checkpoints are few and far between, and only get more scarce the harder the levels get. Time and time again you'll find yourself having to redo lengthy sessions full of awkward chain-grapples. I gave up when reaching the final world, as the chain platforming and scarce checkpoints started making the game outright unenjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun and cute PS1 era inspired platformer. For the first few levels it seems very simple and i was thinking "Did i just buy a game meant for little kids?" but the levels quickly get a lot more complex.There's also an in-game store selling different hats to wear for no reason other than more hats is good.I like hats. Buy the frog hat.

_childDocuments_.review: This needed much more play-testing before release. The first part of this game is cute, but the hook shot mechanic the whole game is based on is completely broken. At first it was so inconsistent that it was only mildly annoying, but the moment they introduced chaining multiple hookshots together, I said "Are you kidding?" out loud. I get that this is a throwback to PS1 platformers, which had a lot of frustrations in their time, however, the big difference between Frog Gun and something like, say, Spyro the Dragon, is that Spyro is not only fundamentally fun to play as, but the controls are extremely tight and responsive. Frog Girl simply isn't either of those things.I often found Frog Girl hooking to places that don't even make sense. There is a soft lock on mechanic (similar to Shooting in Jak 2 & 3) where it will automatically lock on to the nearest "big" enemy, however, there is such a delay from when that happens that most the time you will either fall to your death before the soft lock, or your hookshot will shoot out into the aether or onto some wall in the background and you'll fall to your death anyway. I also found that this game was in desperate need of set camera angles, there are certain points in this game where hook shots only work if the camera is facing a certain way, "work" in the sense less regarding function, but more in "accuracy." In other words, the "soft lock" I referred to earlier only works should the thing you're targeting be on-screen. There are even bosses, Scorchy in particular, who actively go to where your camera isn't, in order to land some cheap hits.Additionally, the length of the grapple is inconsistent throughout the game, to the point where you can grapple on certain things if the hook is grayed out, and can't grapple on certain things if it's red (the viability of a grapple is color coded in-game, red means you're good-to-go, gray means you aren't)A final nitpick is I'm unsure what the hit-boxes for fire is in this game, the animation for the fire spewing totems tend to take up more than a block, and I found myself getting hit when i personally don't think I should have, and not hit when I think i should have.I'm unsure if I want to beat this game, currently I am at the first level AFTER the fourth boss (lava zone) and this level is honestly the straw that broke the camels back for me. I rarely leave reviews, games need to push me pretty far for that.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly quite frustrating, very hard to collect coins and such when you spend a minute or so doing so then fall off the edge and have to repeat that segment again... and again... and again. No checkpoints for bonus areas either, very few in levels in general. It would be nice if at least your collectibles were permanently collected or something. The checkpoints are fine if you just wanna blow through levels but if your the kinda player that likes clearing levels, be prepared for frustration.On the bright side so far with only a few hours in I've only needed to complete an objective or two to get the bonus items along the linear path between levels. Still very frustrating... gonna keep playing for as long as I can stand the game and probably will give up on clearing levels as its not fun.edit:  Bosses like this really should have health pickups or only give you them if you've died and failed a few times.

_childDocuments_.review: Frogun is a great little game until it isn’t. If you’re expecting a fast paced, fluid platformer like A Hat in Time I’d temper your expectations – it’s a slower, more methodical experience that’s closer to something like Captain Toad. Most of your time early on is going to be spend scouring the linear levels for collectables and dealing with some occasionally tricky but mostly pretty gentle platforming challenges. The controls can feel a little awkward, but earlier levels are built to accommodate them.About halfway through though those clunky controls just snap, and it honestly feels a little bit broken. The grappling mechanic was alright when you have safe platforms and time for you to line up the shot with the very finicky auto aim. Once it starts asking you to chain multiple grapples across bottomless pits you might as well flip a coin. Success feels entirely random, and there were levels where I died tens of times on the same string of platforms despite knowing exactly what I had to do.This is exacerbated by some mean checkpoints, and losing all your collectables when you die. And if you fall down a pit, you’re dead regardless of how much health you have left. Levels go from short and snappy to absolutely gruelling monsters.I was hesitant to post this review, as I do believe that this is a game that could be great with a few changes;•	Do something about the grapple. Whether this is making the auto aim a little less finicky, adding a touch of slowdown if you hold the aim button, increasing air time – I feel like there are a few ideas that could be implemented here•	Falling down a pit knocks off a pip of life, same as hitting an enemy. This would make the collection aspect of the game less miserable•	Drop in checkpoints near the optional purple skull sections. The dev has actually implemented this one, so they’re definitely listening!It’s a shame, as I absolutely love the look and feel of the game, and I really was having a lot of fun up until I wasn’t. I’m going to keep an eye on this one, and I’ll update this review if the kinks are ironed out.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: I love the visuals and the vibes of this game, unfortunately I think the controls really need some tuning up to make this enjoyable for me personally. I think the grapple gun as the main weapon is a great idea but is executed pretty poorly. The main issue is that we have 4 face buttons to work with, and yet there is only jump, aim and grapple as commands; whilst this sounds fine on paper, when you realise that grappling can either pull you towards something OR something towards you in a game that is a platformer so has numerous bottomless pits to navigate around it starts becoming an issue. The reticle also doesn't work about 20% of the time, coloured in grey (implying something is too far away to grapple) only to have Renata grapple it anyway, and vice versa. Aiming it is also FAR too sensitive making it quite annoying to control. I only got a few levels in but I can tell these issues are gonna become an absolute nightmare later on, so I'm gonna drop it here. Hoping the devs patch the controls up a little, but if not I hope they continue making games because I love the style this is going for.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: Frogun might be the cutest little adventure I've ever seen.When I initially bought Frogun, I thought it looked really sweet and cute and it'd be a fun little game to play for a bit. What I got was not only all of that, but I put quite a few hours into this 14 dollar game! Ultimately if you go through the game purely just to beat the levels it won't take you super long to get through it, but going through and trying to 100% every level by getting all the badges offered so much enjoyment that it was worth it every run.Each level has a set of badges, from speedrunning the level, to no deaths, to collecting all the coins, etc. and each one can be earned independently of the others so for me it really encouraged going for coins and collectibles on my first run through to get a feel for the level then to try and speedrun it with no deaths after achieving the other badges.The gameplay itself is actually really fun, it reminds me in some ways of Sonic Adventure 1 (My personal favorite platformer, which funny enough Renata does the games iconic pose). The game's level design absolutely encourages you to go bonkers with the "Frog gun" and utilize it to find ways to just break levels and skip whole sections. It's incredibly fun!Not to mention the art style is absolutely beautiful. There's so much personality oozing out of it and it was clear in every piece of art in this game that the artists had a big goofy smile on their face, and it absolutely infected me as well. My community on twitch absolutely adored this game and it will forever be a beloved little game for us <3Looking forward to Frogun Encore and more from this team!

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I'd love to recommend this and enjoy the game, I'm just getting frustrated with the controls. The main grapple mechanic is simply inconsistent and as you progress more and more into the game and the difficulty increases I find myself finding the game more and more of a chore to play as a result of these inconsistencies.Mix these inconsistencies with some of the later levels design choices/mechanics such as invisible blocks that only appear when you get near and the chaining grapples back to back makes going for any of the challenges really frustrating. Which honestly is half of these types of games. I'll probably still finish it because when the game actually manages to flow it feels really good. I just wish it didn't feel so indie and felt more polished.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: This is a brilliant game. It looks good. It feels good. It's challenging, but not unfair. I highly recommend you collect 100% of all the junk in the levels for what a brilliant challenge that is.There were lots of bugs, they were patched. There are some still left, I trust they'll be fixed.I have a few points left that I'd like to raise in an otherwise brilliant game.Firstly, I should note that the first half of the game is Easy and the second half is Hard. It doesn't feel like there's a middle ground. You just hit a wall where the game turns on, the training wheels come off, and you wake up. That difficulty eventually starts to fade away as you play more and get a Gamer Instinct for how far you can grapple etc, and start making more jumps based on that instinct rather than strictly sticking to what the UI is telling you at any one time.Secondly, in order to 100% the game, I seem to need to buy everything from the shop. This will definitely require I farm coins. I do not feel the desire to farm coins. The major fun of replaying the levels is to speedrun it, in which you do not pick up many coins, so I now need to strategise the best way to collect coins at speed in order to not artificially drag out the game. It's a real damper on the end-game "Do I want to get all achievements" moment. (I will do this but I'm writing this review first because a few hours of just collecting coins over and over will sour my mood on this)Additionally, one of the collectibles is not made clear until you beat the final boss. I would estimate that about 1/3rd of all the threads in the community on Steam are about people confused as to what this is; naturally some people want to complete all the objectives in a level in one go, but the game refuses to give you a hint about them. This also goes in hand with obscuring the time objective. It tells you on the level select what the time objective is, but absolutely nowhere in the level, so you simply have to rush and hope you beat it, without knowing how far off you are. It sort of means you're never really pressured by, say, a clock on screen that's telling you you're about to miss out, and you're just blindly trying to fly through it. I think the pause screen in general could contain that sort of collectible information (instead most of it is just on the UI as you play, though again with no idea about the objective)Also, some of the platforming with some of the objects feels a tiny bit janky. Especially the spiked skulls. Maybe I'm impatient and push forwards too much but I ended up bouncing off stuff and taking damage a lot when I didn't need to, and then having to make absurd grapple saves. I'm not really sure how you'd fix this. Some of them are perhaps simply too close together? I think some of the grappling occasionally comes across as unfair (I honestly believe that if the grappling was stuck to an 8-direction situation as if you were using a Gamecube c-stick, this game would play like an absolute dream) and you end up missing really easy grapples or chain grapples where you'd think you could just push in one direction the entire time (alas, no!)Respawning in Frogun also has two problems. Firstly: it takes too long. Animation takes a while, then there's a screen transition, then an entry animation. I like an instant reset. And if you die to a pit, you have to wait for that full respawn set to take place before you hit restart on the level in the pause screen. Why would you want to do that? Because if you die and are sent to the beginning of the level, and all your progress is reset, it still counts as a death. Ostensibly, it is a fresh start, you have no coins, no time on the clock, but it will not count for a deathless run. I'm not sure why! Should be an easy fix.Finally, the speedrun mode isn't my cup of tea. I was spoiled by the excellent speedrun mode in Neon White recently. A mode which chains levels together with no downtime, and an In-Gamer Timer that sticks to just gameplay. You exit a level, you move onto the next one with no move to any level select. This game operates differently. You can visit unlockable chests to get more health, so there's an argument to be made about keeping the world select in (especially for 100% modes) but the timer runs even during loading segments! You could achieve the exact same result just running a 3rd party timer separately. I honestly think it's a shame this game doesn't have something more thoughtful there, because the Individual Level speedrunning in this is great.Despite that enormous wall of text, this game offers a great challenge. It sounds wonderful. It looks absolutely sublime. It oozes charm in every corner. (Unrelated: that Can You Pet The Dog guy on twitter can ♥♥♥♥ off)Frogun should be praised for what a brilliant game it is. I know with the feedback from the community it is already being shaped to be so much better, and I trust it will truly shine very soon. I hope Molegato make some more small brilliant games that I can play in the future! ♥~

_childDocuments_.review: This is a charming looking game with not much staying power.  This can be observed in the achievements where more than half of players do not have the 'win a race' achievement, which is less than one hour into the game.  It's very much like an early playstation game where they couldn't figure out full 3D movement and were banking on visuals alone.Everything is a bit more fiddly and tedious than it needs to be.  The tongue attack/grappling hook is fully analog which instead of giving more control, just makes it easier to screw up.  There are un-tongue-able surfaces, but they are only used to prevent you from cheesing some levels (ie having fun) and are not used to prevent you from accidentally killing yourself in the early stages.  I almost think the game would play better without the titular frogun, as I dread using it.The layout of coins and collectibles does not lend itself to a smooth path through the level, you often have to backtrack awkwardly.  The race levels in particular - it's impossible to collect everything and win the race in one go, you have to ignore everything and win the race, then backtrack through the course to collect everything.  There are lots of coins in breakable pots and jumping on them is jittery because the camera tracks up with your character height, rather than the ground height.I quit about 2 hours in at the water strider boss 'kicky' along with 75% of all players, according to the achievement stats.  You know that boss design where you wait around for him to do a tedious attack pattern until he's stunned and drops an enemy and you have to throw the enemy at him then repeat that 3 times?  Yeah it's that.  We need some new ideas folks.If you're looking for fun 3D platformers, there is no shortage of them on steam:  Pseudoregalia, A Hat in Time, RiME, Spyro Reignited Trilogy, Grow Home/Grow Up, even Yooka-Laylee - these are all better experiences.

_childDocuments_.review: So far, I like this game, but there's a bit holding it back, but there's actually a pretty easy solution(s) to this that I'll say later.Good style, fun movement, cute character, funny dialog, and charming atmosphere do wonders for this game. My issues however is how tedious this game is with it's levels. To "100%" a level, you need to: Collect all coins, Green and Purple gems, notes, Not die, and finish under a par. Theoretically, these should only take you two times of playing a level to complete (a deathless speed run and a collectathon run), but in practice I've found this has taken me 3-4 times playing through ONE LEVEL to 100% it.Usually my levels look like this:1. A painfully tedious and slow collectathon run, if you die at ANY POINT you lose EVERYTHING since your last check point. So sometimes-2. [This was very common] If the challenge area (for purple gems) is too annoying to go back to and collect everything, i'll sometimes leave it for it's own separate run.3. An annoying deathless speedrun. If you die, you have to wait until you have control, pause the game, then go to reset. Sure this is like nothing but if you're awful like I am you're doing it over, and over, and over again. But sometimes-4. [This wasn't too common, but a bit annoying] I'd still be decently under par and died in a level around the last checkpoint so I'd go and try to complete it. So then I'd have to go do a slower deathless run.Good news is, I have two simple suggestions that will solve this:1. Have all non-coin items (or even JUST the Purple gem) persist after a death in the level.2. Offer the selection of a "speedrun mode" before entering a level where a death means a full reset of the level. I feel (the 100%) speedrunners would also like this feature.I did notice there's a speedrun mode option in the options, maybe I'll try that if it helps my second point, assuming its a toggle.

_childDocuments_.review: Frogun walks a fine line between puzzle and precision platformer to offer an extremely enjoyable blend of both. Has that classic "easy to learn, hard to master" kind of gameplay that seems simplistic at first but ramps up in difficulty at a nice pace without ever seeming unfair or cheep. Getting full completion on all of the levels is going to test even veterans of the genre and this game will not hold your hand in doing so. Only complaint is the grind at the end for coins to unlock all the hats/artwork and get every achievement which I would say isn't really worth it honestly.Easy recommendation for fans of 3D platformers. Looking forward to what this team does in the sequel!

_childDocuments_.review: A nice 3D platformer with some corners made of crumbly cheese.  It can scratch your collectathon itch for sure, but could have been better.  The visual design is all there -- very clean, cute, friendly.  The cartoony look of it drew me.  The controls are  there:  immediate character control and jumping are A-okay, with no need to fall back on the ol' double-jump for mid-air steering, which games sometimes do to make up for inadequate design in that regard; the tongue targeting, however, is fiddly, and just because you get a red reticle instead of a gray doesn't mean the tongue will actually .  The levels are likewise :  pretty fun to navigate for the most part, though the same-y-ness and dearth of novelty can mount towards boredom during extended play sessions.The bosses, now, are all "level" bosses and I think they're great!  You can only hit them at certain well-telegraphed intervals, so there's no room for hidden strategies to cheese them or rush them to their doom -- yet I loved the obstacles they threw at me.  The two boss rushes at the very end may have been the high point of the game for me.I think this idea, this look, this brand has a kernel of awesomeness in it, and I would like to see what it grows into.  More novelty!  Fix the tongue fiddliness!  Maybe a greater feeling of  to the movement!  Close the gap between "trivial to simply  the levels" and "extremely time-consuming to hundred-percent for adequate challenge"; for that reason I think I played a little longer than I  to and I still didn't get the last cheevo because it would have taken four-to-five hours of coin grinding just to unlock the artwork!

_childDocuments_.review: I can confidently say that this is the best experience I've had with a video game in several years, and I haven't even passed the 1-hour mark on total playtime yet. (You bet your britches I'm going right back into it, though!) I love how genuinely pure, straightforward, and lighthearted it is. So many great little touches, too. I love the selection of filters that you can put on top of the game, for example. Fantastic art direction, fantastic controls, fantastic character likability, and fantastic ways of making players rub two brain cells together without annoying them or insulting their intelligence.For me, another big reason this game succeeds so tremendously, especially where other games with a similar aesthetic and goal of nostalgia have failed, is the distinct lack of irony or sarcasm in its presentation: it's not "haunted", it's not "meta" or self-aware, and it doesn't have an unfittingly depressing hidden sob story that tries to examine the human psyche for the millionth time in indie gaming. This is just a fun game with a clever concept, plain and simple, and that's so refreshing.This is a brilliant video game made by brilliant people. It's the retro throwback game of my dreams, and it dared to fight my jadedness in gaming as a whole. Creators of other games that are trying to capture this kind of style and feeling should absolutely be using this game as inspiration, because this is an extremely rare example of how you make a game that celebrates the PS1/N64 generation of gaming correctly.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: Frogun is fantastic and exactly the game it appears to be; a good old collectathon throwback to the PSX/N64 era.The style and personality are what really sell it. Aside from being adorable, the rigid and structured level design shows how a few simple elements can be combined into engaging challenges. The pacing feels just about right as there are ample down moments where you get the joy of picking up tons of easy collectables interspersed with some tricky jumps, cycle-based action segments, and light puzzle solving. Renata herself controls quite well, she isn't slippery and the jumping feels nice and measured. There are a few issues with her wanting to flip about and the auto-aiming not always doing what you think it should which can create some frustration, but I find it easy to enjoy the game despite these slight annoyances. The developers have been responsive on the boards so far and it looks like they intend to address this. If they do, I think they'll really knock it out of the park and have a hidden gem on their hands, but even so this is an easy recommendation from me.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: While Frogun looked like Crash Bandicoot meets Umihara Kawase, it just lacked the depth and just ended up feeling boring and tedious.I spent most of my game time thinking "When will I get more abilities?" The "Frogun" grappling hook isn't anywhere near as fun or interesting to use as Kawase's lure, and it definitely isn't enough to carry this game. The Frogun lets you grapple and travel to nearby walls, and also attack enemies/grab items. Very similar to the hookshot from Ocarina of Time. However, in practice, it only travels in a horizontal straight line and I wasn't able to use it in any kind of creative or interesting ways. Also, lots of tricky platforming portions rely on making many grappling hook shots in quick succession, and this neither feels fun or challenging, just tedious and frustrating when you fail.This game is a great start, with colorful artwork and fun characters... but the gameplay falls completely flat, and I found myself losing interest as soon as the novelty of the graphics wore off.

_childDocuments_.review: Deceptively difficult game. Don't let the cute art style fool you, if you're going for all coins/all gems/all skulls you will die a lot. It's not Crash Bandicoot 4 level difficulty, just more difficult than I expected going into it. That being said, if just clearing all the levels is more your style, it shouldn't be too difficult for most people.  I had a blast with this game and I definitely recommend it to any 3D platformer fans.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wish I could recommend this game. It looks really good with It's low poly graphics, story isn't really big part of this game but the notes you collect through levels really tell a lot about the world you move in with bunch of cute characters. The levels or mechanics of the game aren't really the problem but the problem are in controls, the camera and some parts of the game like annoying races with Jake that I learnt how to skip thanks to Speedrunners and there are absurdly hard bosses in each world that may or may not be considered Dark Souls bosses which get even more frustrating to fight against progressing through the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: It's as simple as it gets, You go from point A to B and It's mostly focused on a platformer adventure game. There are collectables, the Frogun mechanic, creatures as enemies, and bosses in certain areas.Inside each level you'll be collecting coins and some other types of collectables. You can spend your coins in the shop, buying hats to use and some paintings to admire. A simple story about having to rescue your parents, there is nothing more unusual than that, throughout the game you'll met two more friendly characters. The story works well because the main purpose is for you to progress through the levels while being a classic fun adventure game. As you would've guessed the Frogun is the main mechanic in this game, it allows you to grab and throw things and it also let's you use it as a hook, for example: you can shoot at a wall with the Frogun and get pulled towards that direction. It's a nice mechanic. In every level you'll have collectables, most of the levels will have the following: A different number of coins for each level - useful to buy hats and paintings.1 note - It talks about the adventure itself or some character in the game.2 Gems -  Collectables which are neither easy nor hard to get.1 Obsidian Skull - located in a secret area in each level, those are usually more difficult to get. this is a nice feature that awards the player with an emblem on each level. There are 7 emblems counting with the notes. To get all the emblems you'll have to basically get everything in each level: all coins, gems, obsidian skulls, the notes, completing the level without dying, and you'll also have to speedrun it. There are two badges of speedrun, one to get a faster time and the other to a even faster one, I really like the emblems idea because it works really well. Not the easiest thing to 100%, most of the achievements are easily obtained by fully completing the game, there are some achievements that require a bit of grinding and some others that can be difficult for example, speedrunning the boss rush levels, but that's good because it serves as a better challenge for those that like it.The sounds and soundtracks are good on their own, but it gets even better when we combine them with the artwork in this game. All soundtracks are really well made and they do a good representation of the ambient that the player is located in. Some songs are better than others for my taste, I really like the songs from the swamp, the initial Ruins area, the race song, and the songs from the snow levels as well.I really like it. The textures, the characters, the enemies and the objects they all look nice, very pleasant to look at and It's one of the main things that made me enjoy my time in this game. The game is quite long so you'll be travelling through a lot of levels in different places, and each one of those areas will have a different design which makes this game worth it for its content.Overall: If you like 3D Platformer/Adventure games that have a lot of content, different levels with different areas and the option to get nice collectables, then I recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: A solid little collectathon platformer with a cute retro, low poly style.Once I realized you can 100% stages by, say, collecting all coins and collectibles on one playthrough while focusing on no deaths and beating par times on another, it created a very different feel where I can take a stage slow, look around for secrets and shortcuts on my first try before taking what I learned and just flying past everything to get the fastest time on my next try.Even without trying to get everything and just playing through the levels, there's plenty of content here for the price
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: I've just completed the first two worlds of this game but I'm already in love. It's a fun 3D platformer built on a simple premise; use your frogun to navigate obstacles while gathering treasure on your way to the end of the stage. It's a simple premise, but each and every level so far has built upon its foundation in fun and creative ways. I was surprised at how challenging the game becomes fairly early on, but the generally slower pace allows for anyone to enjoy it. You can pretty much customize the experience based on how much effort you want to put into it. It's great whether you want to explore every nook in cranny to find all the treasure, blast your way to end of the stage as quickly as possible, or even just survive each level at your own pace. Would recommend to any fan of platformers!
