_childDocuments_.review: This game gets a "yes and no" as far as recommendations are concerned.Do I like the game?  Yeah.  When the platforming works, it works really well.You might be considering it on the grounds that it was designed with older N64/PS1 platformers in mind.  I can attest that it fits into that crowd in more ways than one:  Much like its forebears, it has "The Jank".  That, and a camera that occasionally wants to fight you.Sometimes "The Jank" works really well in your favor; letting you skip 90% of a level and finishing within 20 seconds.  Most of the time:  You will take arbitrary damage because hitboxes are hard.  You will fall through seemingly solid floors and lose a ton of forward progress.  The frog tongue may not quite land where you need it to, and you'll get dropped back to the last checkpoint, or the death will force you to restart the whole level so you can appease the OCD part of your brain that demands completed emblems.This is my largest criticism, or "complaint", if you will.  With a solid platformer, a player has very little recourse but to blame their failures on the decisions they made, and the buttons they pressed.  Most of the time, that's applicable in Frogun; the entire first half of the game is an absolute joy, and I wholly endorse it.The "spooky" zone is where it goes off these rails.  You stop getting reproduce-able results for the same inputs, and that's not helped by having floating targets to grapple to in an empty abyss.  The developers gave Renata a shadow as quality of life for aiming your jumps.  That shadow is worth almost nothing for these sections.  (I should note:  It's entirely possible that this section of the game could be nicer to you if you're using a controller; I went through it with mouse and keyboard.  Maybe that's my problem.)Once you leave the spook zone, the level design becomes much more practical and finishes strong.  There are post-game levels for even more challenge if you're unsatisfied.  At the time of writing, I'm sitting at roughly 83% completion, and I think I've had enough.There is a lot to like about this game.  It has a lot of charm, the music has some surprising range to it, and the boss fights keep things interesting, (though the final boss reminds me a great deal of Banjo-Kazooie's, in that it takes entirely too long and perpetually sits on the border between obnoxious and absurd.  I will admit, it is an effective "final test" of everything the game has striven to teach you, but I will ALSO admit, I would not be sad to hear about some misfortune befalling the individual(s) who put that fight together:  Introducing spammed fast-moving projectiles you can't jump over as an 11th hour addition to game mechanics was kind of a jerk thing to do, final boss fight or no).Water under the bridge.  I hear there's a sequel in the works, I hope they use feedback to further tune the next installment of their series, and I earnestly hope it outperforms this title.So that's the caveat for the recommendation:  Platformers normally demand a significant amount of timing and coordination, but it's give and take with regard to being able to keep track of where you are in 3D space.  There are some levels where Frogun just kinda gives you a shrug and tells you to figure it out for yourself.  Then it delivers a swift kick to your junk, because you had .2 seconds to figure it out, and you didn't.So it depends on what you're into.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: Very cute game that I wasn't sure about mechanically at first, but grew to like it the more time I spent with it. The main grappling mechanic has some idiosyncrasies, like not allowing you to grapple a wall when you're at too sharp an angle with it even though the cursor seems to indicate it's fine, but I found myself having a lot of fun finding the fastest way through levels by exploiting shortcuts the titular Frogun allows for. Took me a bit to come around on it, but ultimately I had a good time.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: Frogun is a surprisingly good, 3D-platformer collect-a-thon type game.  The most noticeable aspect of the game is the visuals, which are quite nice and look better while playing than in screenshots.  It's very cute and a good use of low-poly art design.  There's a lot of vivid colors and a free swinging camera which allows you to see the scope of the levels pretty well and I like how all aspects of a level take place on the same gamespace.  This is something that's hard to describe, but for example, you can swing the camera around and see the obsidian skull sections of a level, which are separated from the main section of a level by falling into a hole, in the normal gamespace but a bit off in the distance.  It's a small thing, but I like it.Frogun is level-based and not semi-open world, thank god.  There's around 40 stages total and they tend to follow a biome theme.  I feel like there's actually a bit too many levels, as a lot of them kind of run together and it seems like there's too many dark themed levels for my taste.  Level of difficulty is quite easy for the first 2/3's of the game and then picks up a bit.  Part of that difficulty is due to the controls and their relations to game mechanics, which I'll touch on more below.Controls are fine.  You move (a bit slowly, but didn't bother me once I played more), jump and shoot your grappling gun and that's about it.  The big problem with the controls is that they don't play well with the more advanced aspects of the game, like trying to chain frogun grabs together because the aiming reticle lies at times whether you can grab onto something or not and the free camera control will definitely cause elevation issues, since you can only shoot the frogun horizontally and really need to be lined correctly to chain grabs consecutively, which is not a problem most of the game, but becomes a bit of a headache in the later third.  Checkpoints are plentiful but it's still a bit irritating to miss the same grab multiple times because of the lack of cohesion between the mechanics and camera.  Another thing that bothers me is you definitely slip off platforms too easily, there's need to be more margin of error here, as if you're the slightest bit off a platform, you're probably going to fall off.  You also can't fully rebind the controls, which is always annoying.The funnest, most challenging aspect of Frogun is speedrunning the levels.  Levels are short and can be beat quite quickly once you start looking for areas and angles you can grapple to bypass parts of levels.  The best example of this is one of the last levels, which is probably one of the longest in the game playing normally, but can be beat in about 30 seconds because you can use some grappling tech to skip around a locked door right at the start of the level.  This is one of my main complaints with the game though, as you don't really do much creative thinking on how to use the frogun unless you're trying to beat levels as fast as possible.   My main complaint about speedrunning the levels is how annoying chain-grabbing can be at times, the aforementioned platforms that are easy to slip off of and finally, your main speedrun pro-strat move, frogunning up to a ledge that's slightly above you is very hit-and-miss and doesn't feel like there's enough consistency to it.Also tied into this, there are two time trials for each level and the second one only unlocks your time goals after beating the game, though you can clear the expert time trial by getting the requisite time before that but you won't know what your time goal is.  There really should just be the expert time trials goal because the regular trial is too easy.There is very little story here.  You play a cute girl named Renata who is trying to save her parents with the help of her sentient Frogun.  There is very little dialogue or cutscenes, which I'm more than okay with.  It's nice to play a game where you just interact it with it in a pure gameplay manner.  Also, it's an indie game where there's no overt or subtle (or at least trying to be subltle) allusions to mental health or fouth-wall breaking.  Who knew such games existed?  It's just a cute game with minimal story aspects.  That is fine.In short, Frogun is a nice little 3D platformer with some fun speedrunning aspects.  I don't even really like this style of game (3D collect-a-thon) that much, but quite enjoyed it and it has been probably one of the more positive surprises I played this year.  It's definitely a bit too easy for the most part, but it's fun and nice to look at.  Also probably a good game for young kids due to its simplicity and visual style.  I am no longer a young kid but enjoyed it all the same.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to give this a conditional recommendation to general audiences and the 3D platformer curious, and a high recommendation to people who can see themselves putting up with a lot of jank and the more-than-occasional inscrutable death to explore some very clever level designs with a gorgeous aesthetic. The biggest problem is the camera. I admire that they let you use a fully free camera to hide secrets in a sort of Captain Toad fashion, but if I'm being honest, I really feel like a game like this would have benefited from a fixed camera. Each section has what feels like an intended camera angle where what to do is obvious & you can properly judge depth & line of sight on everything you need to hit to get from point A to point B. As it stands, figuring out this perfect camera angle takes some trial and error that I don't always have the patience or desire for. The Achievement completion percentage for the late-game boss I just beat is hovering around 12%, perhaps signaling that I am not the only one who feels this way.Despite this, it's a commendable effort for a relatively small team. I'm bought in to the studio's next efforts on good faith alone. They have an eye for design and display a sort of craftsmanship in the level design that can't be faked. If their next game(s) iron out some of the rough patches and continue to iterate on what they do well, this team's got a shot at the big time.

Loved my time with the game, but probably ruined the experience for myself a bit by trying to 100% every level once I got through it, which ended up burning me a bit out by the end. _childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely amazing! Ever since I tried the demo I've been waiting for this game to finally release.Don't be fooled by its cute design - Frogun is a challenging platformer that utilizes the Frogun - a sentient gun that shoots out its tongue - to leap you forward by tongue-ing and sticking to walls, platforms and several other objects. The Frogun can also be used to vault towards enemies or kill them.The levels offer several challenges in which you can gather several collectibles or try to go really fast as well as finishing stages without dying. Collecting things feels rewarding because it not only gives you achievement badges but also unlocks some sweet cosmetics for the main character, Renata. The game offers even more than those in exchange for collectibles, but ... *spoilers*!I personally love the style of the game, I love leaping around and trying to go faster each time. So if you like speedrunning - this game is perfect for it. One of the best things about this game is also that it's actually difficult, especially in the later stages! You want a challenge? You got it.Another positive is that the devs are really responsive and listening to their community. The first bout of fixes and adjustments is already on its way! Wow!I've been having a lot of fun with it and I cannot wait to sink more hours into this game and complete it 100%.

_childDocuments_.review: Version 1.8 (official release)The trailer makes the game look like an adorable and fun game, very chill, a child's play even.Problem is, it's only visually accurate. 2nd half of the game was spamming multiple ziplines while airborne and turning the camera. Sadly the game is poorly optimized. The characters range and height are left to guesswork and the camera is turned in random angles; so you keep repeatedly falling to instant death. The distinct lack of accessable save points for sometimes the entire "difficult" level and the penalty of losing 100% of the collection progress only exacerbates the issue. IT IS A LOT OF FRUSTRATION FOR NO REASON.ODDLY, there are many game breaking exploits, that feel like a required/intended feature, per level.Freezing time? We got you.Scaling unpassable walls? Sure thing.Ledge hopping to bypass the level? Of course.Skipping 25%-99% of every level with random mob/level border interaction? We got you covered!The game's difficulty balance, time requirement (aka content or 100% completion) and overall enjoyment are just all over the place. Same with the level designs. Most felt lackluster and the frustrating 2nd half of the game EXTREMELY REPETITIVE. Then suddenly the few extra levels are "mostly" well designed & "almost" fair.This also explains why speedruns are about an hour or two and full completion might average 30h+.Some of the "content" is just repeating the same coin grind FOR HOURS to unlock redundant pictures that you already see used in the game while playing it; in a more polished form, too. Didn't feel fun or rewarding to grind out what I already knew about... not sure why they aren't free and progression based... anyway...Similarly, the other collectable, the hats - by the time I could afford one, I was only spamming Jake levels.I wonder why Jake is a playable character, with own idles, but he doesn't have his in_game mechanics like extra range. Neither does the save point make a snake sound and icon. He can't use hats either...Why does any game that isn't a platformer have more actual platforming in their bosses than this game?The bosses are okay, but also. running in a circle and pressing jump every time is not very intuitive...Also, I swear that every boss has more solid ground tiles converged than average level combined.Can't there be some level variety that's not about falling 24/7? It cannot, instead have no tiles and go zipline!I made some screenshots in my steam of a few of the bugs, typos, oddities, completion... which won't matter.The devs certainly started a touch oblivous and optimistic, but are putting out patches rapidly to make the game actually accessable. RIGHT HERE; I'm rating the game as is, not as could be. NOT HOT.But after a few more patches, sure.Still, I can't say it was too memorable, not story, mood nor music. Just glitches, retry pain and camera RNG.

_childDocuments_.review: It's decent, but after playing it for a bit just wanted to make me rush to finish the game instead of wanting to play it more for completion.The game and level design is at conflict with each constantly. Is this a speed run game, is this a collect-a-thon?  You'll be replaying levels multiple times to beat conflicting goals you can't do at the same time. The controls and the camera are conflicting as well. Played with a controller. The targeting is finicky at times, where if you are just not at the perfect height or angle then you will end up falling to your death. Not dying is another goal in this game too for completion. Also, it's not clear at times if you will end up grappling toward things at times. There is some other nitpick issues with camera and graphic design too.And one last thing, but feel like the later levels might be visually harder to see for some people.

_childDocuments_.review: Cute fun N64/PS1 styled platformer. If you liked stuff like Mario 64 or Banjo you'll probably like this.It's pretty easy at first, but like other reviews point out it does get annoyingly harder. Not because the platforming itself is hard, but because of the detection on your Frogun which is pretty much just a hookshot and the main gimmick of the game. You'll have to chain shots later and missing just one could potentially lead to you dying. It's all doable, but if you're trying to collect all of the items in each level (which is like half the fun of the game), you're gonna be dying a lot later on. Like 90% of my deaths in this game are just from the Frogun being a little too slightly to the left or rightThere's also these "race" levels where to collect everything, you have to go through the level twice in one sitting. Feels a bit redundant. Probably shouldn't be any collectables in that type of level and just make it the race.I do still highly recommend it though. Cute visuals, fun gameplay overall, simple but likable characters, an alright OST, and a good amount of levels to go through. I would just make a recommendation to the dev to add better detection when aiming your frogun (ESPECIALLY when you're in the air), and maybe adding a lock-on in the air.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a delightful little game that I hope will get the love it deserves.  I've only played the first few levels or so but I can tell there's plenty to enjoy here.  Getting all of the collectibles in each level will take time but there's also an incredible amount of speedrun potential in this game.  Even within the first few levels I found lots of little skips you could take with the grapple so I can only imagine how optimized the game could become.  At $15 (or less) it's an easy recommendation that belongs in anyone's library that enjoys quirky platformers.

_childDocuments_.review: It's very very fun! I love the PS1 style graphics and there's also a bunch of graphic filter that you can use in the settings. Only minor complaint is sometimes the auto aim kinda not aiming at stuff you expect it's gonna aim but everything else feels pretty good.Renata and her frog gun is so adorable, and I just found out that the strawhat changes her hairstyle to a side ponytail which is super cute. I also love the fact that it has photo mode, I've been screenshotting a bunch lol.From what I've played so far it's very very fun, and I implore everyone to try this if you love retro style platformers.

_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: This is a surprisingly deep game that's probably going to be considered an overlooked classic one day. Don't let the trailers or the reviews fool you, this is more than just a throwback to the 5th console gen, it's a full-fledged successor that has a lot of fresh ideas that cast those older games in a new light. It's one of the first in the budding genre of "Hardcore 3D Platformers" like Blue Fire, playing more like Vexx on the PS2 rather than Mario or Banjo-Kazooie. The frogun takes some getting used to, but once you get the hang of it you can do a lot of crazy stuff with what seems like such a simple mechanic. It can be frustrating at times, but that's just part of the learning curve and probably only because there's no other game like this so you can't rely on muscle memory. If you stick with it you'll find that levels that once made you pull your hair out in anger will be a cakewalk upon returning later. Great game that unfortunately doesn't seem to be getting the credit it deserves.

_childDocuments_.review: I really WANT to like Frogun because it's cute and has a really good style. Great soundtrack too.But the stages just get SO FRUSTRATING as the game progresses. And not because of any unique level design or genuine difficulty, they get frustrating solely because the camera and the controls aren't cut out for what the devs had in mind. There's a stage called Running With Fear that has some jumping puzzles that I have never been able to beat. Ever. I banged my head against that stage for an hour. Then when I finally made it further than I ever did before, a skull platform vanished because of a bug and I died. That's it. I'm done. Maybe this game gets REALLY GREAT after that stage. I'll never know.

_childDocuments_.review: Game starts really strong as a collectathon with unique yet cluncky mechanics of having a gun that either pulls enemys or towards you or pulls you towards wall and objects and great aesthetic with graphics resembling old Mega Man Legends from the ps1. Unfortunatly however, at some point in the middle of the game, it becomes a precision platform where you will repeat the same jump over and over and over and over and over again because the controls are WAAAAAY to cluncky to make it work with the level design present in those later levels.I started trying to collect every single coin, note and gem in each level, as well as trying to do the deathless and speed run trials, but those latter levels are infuriating just to get through the first time, let alone doing a completionist run. At this point i'm not even sure if i'll even finish this game due to pure frustration where the game expects you to aim perfectly on 180 turns to hit jump plataforms where the slightest of analogict drift will make your character shoot to the void.I really like the visuals of this game and hope that those cluncky controls are ironed up in Encore or that at least the level design is more on par with how the game plays.TLDR: This game stops being fun after the first half

_childDocuments_.review: ( full review with screenshots:  )Frogun is a retro-style puzzle platformer where the central gimmick is your Yoshi-esque gun. Your gun can latch on to something at a distance and pull you towards it if the target is big or it towards you if the target is small. Small targets are then held and can be fired at something else. A lot of recent reviews have criticized the game for its controls, and I'm guessing they're mostly talking about the gun. Although it has a targeting reticle that always shows what you're aiming at and whether it's in range, the two targeting modes are either too slow or too imprecise, and the auto-targeting often aims at whatever is closest even if there's no reason to shoot that. Particularly in later levels when you need to shoot while moving, it's often more about being consistent in your setup that having any faith in being able to aim at anything. The good news is, you don't actually have to use the gun for anything important very often. I did everything except the expert time trial on nearly every level and was usually able to accomplish it with just the basic jump and maybe a few gun grabs onto large targets like walls. You have unlimited lives and dying even resets the timer to whatever it was at when you reached the last checkpoint, so there aren't really consequences for needing a few tries to learn the timing when you do need to make a more complicated jump using the gun. I won't deny that it can be very frustrating to fail a jump a few times in a row because the gun doesn't behave the way you'd expect it to, but it is at least consistent enough that it stops being a problem on most jumps after you get the timing down. The other source of negative reviews is likely the last two levels. Frogun has one race level in each world, and all of them other than the one in the penultimate level are basically trivial. This level is a perfect storm of complications that suddenly make it far and away the hardest platforming sequence in the game. The race actually has a fairly tight deadline this time, but loads of traps force you to stop and wait at every turn. There are gun jumps far from checkpoints that will be extra frustrating to learn, and one sequence at the very end felt impossible to do without pausing at each platform in the jump. Beating it the first time is bad enough, but then you need to do it without dying and in a very tight timeframe if you want all the medals. The final boss is an even bigger difficulty spike with one attack pattern that feels truly impossible to reliably dodge until you notice it's actually telegraphed by tiny little shadows a split second before. That was fine on my screen, but I can imagine those are essentially invisible on small screens or at low resolution. So I definitely don't begrudge anyone giving this a negative review, and I might have done the same if I hadn't noticed the secret to that boss pattern in time or if I'd been determined to get the expert time medals. Frogun can be extremely frustrating when it doesn't work. The good news is that it does work the great majority of the time, and the levels are a ton of fun to run through even using just your basic tools. Tracking down every coin and finding the secret items in each level both adds variety so that it's not always just a speed platformer and it changes worlds at just the right pace to stop you from getting tired of any one setting.

_childDocuments_.review: Scrimblo Blimblo, the Lovable Scrunko fans, rejoice !This new entry in the series is quite good. Simple, fun and cute well describe this game with an esthetic reminiscent of the N64/PSX era, where you use your frog gun to hook to walls or to fetch objects and monsters (so you can throw them away after). The voice of the tutorial frog is straight up taken from the Banjo Kazooie vibes.The steady, linear and fair difficulty curve of the game respect your time and your skills. With multiple challenges within the level, from collecting all the coins to finding the secrets. While you can't shmoove as you would in a Mario 64 - like game, the game respect your skills with its native speedrun challenges that rewards good routing and the finding of niche angles and jumps.I havent finished the game yet, but with 3-4 hours of playtime, it says that I am at 45% completion, which means that the game is relatively short, expecting 10 hours of playtime max total, but not so much when you see how unexpensive it is.Anyways its a recommend from me, low cost, low commitment, yet fun and expressive game.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: It's a pretty good game, with some annoyances especially towards the end of it.It's incredibly charming and cute. The basic gameplay is very tight and fun. When the game is at its best it's fun to zip through the levels. The game always stays fresh with new environments, enemies, obstacles and level elements. The bosses, with the exception of the last one, present a perfect amount of challenge (even though they turn into a bit of a waiting fest).The camera is mostly ok, but  it can get annoying on certain spots. It's funny that it even happens once or twice in the level map.As for the bad stuff:The game hands out health upgrades as a reward for various challenges, like completing 15 levels without dying and under a sctrict right time limit. I think it's a bad choice to place an upgrade that helps the player behind a test of skill, since those who will need the upgrade the most are less likely to be able to get it. Personally it wasn't difficult getting those, but it was tedious.The main "gimmick" of the game, the Frogun, is fun when used casually, but in the last few worlds the game requires a bit too much accuracy with it. I'm willing to bet that more than half of my deaths in the game are when I tried to use the Frogun and missed.Overall, I recommend getting it on a sale and to not try to 100% the game,
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: Frogun is a very cute stylistic platformer worth your time and money and gives you a solid amount of hours to play. There are also options to speedrun or 100% the game that reward you with cute art and hats.Most levels play smoothly and mechanics are easy to understand, learn and use. Every single character including enemies seem designed with purpose and love. The soundtrack is just as amazing as the game's design, also.Not every level is super smooth and easy to play, and I'd argue some of the later levels are definitely challenging. If the camera turns you off, and makes you dislike this one, I would also recommend looking into Frogun Encore, where the camera is fixed in angle. I'm still mad about the final boss, because it took me quite a while to beat and was very challenging to me, but I'm rather casual when it comes to platformers.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: This game has that old school charm that died out after the PS1 and N64 era.That is a good and bad thing, tbh. It has a cartoon style that is low poly cute and very clean. It's a pleasant game to look at. It also has very good level design, as in each stage has layers, it has depth and some stages feature light puzzle elements to be able to find all of the collectibles. It's a bit like Captain Toad's Diaper Adventure on Wii U/Switch, except it isn't polished to death and devoid of any challenge.There are many issues, however. For one, the aiming of your frog's tongue is a wonky thing. I imagine it was meant to be a bit like 3D Yoshi but without a lock-on mechanic, it sucks. There are these race levels with a poser bro and I don't like the fact that once you beat him and finish the level, he isn't gone. If you want to go back into the level to find more collectibles, well you have to race him again. The game has built in means to continue to play the level once you make it to the end but it often leaves you unable to get all collectibles. So then you have to race the guy again and pray to Miyamoto that you don't mess up.Still, I really enjoyed my time with this game. It is a nostalgic experience and I can see this game leading to perhaps a fleshed out sequel with better control mechanics and such. Give it a try if you at all liked games like Croc, back in the day.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: Frogun has a great accessibility, it's not impossible but neither too easy to complete, it has a great balanced experience. Reminding us of classics like Crash or Super Mario, the game offers a great feeling on the gameplay and some good to have extras. I recommend it, it's a great game to complete or play for fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: A faithful throwback to the 5th console generation platformers, for better and for worse. Graphics are colorful and designs are fun, but the draw distance is purposefully very short. Music is MIDI or MIDI-like. You can (and will) fully rotate the camera, but it sometimes gets stuck behind a corner of a nearby setpiece, etc. I don't know if I should mock or admire the author's dedication to reproducing the bad parts of that era along with the good.I wouldn't exactly recommend it to people who didn't cut their teeth on pre-2000 platformers, but if you don't mind occasional pad-throw-inducing rage after failing to chain grappling hook jumps for the 30th time, go ahead. At the end of the day, it _is_ quite fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: This game goes to show that a charming presentation, setting and premise can make a game great despite a lack of immersive atmosphere and deep narrative. It looks really adorable, has a simple but charming story, and still looks pretty good when you lower the resolution to 800x600, thanks to its graphical simplicity.In the shoes of adorable little archeologist apprentice Renata, you go on a quest to find your archeologist parents in some dangerous ruins. Before you go, you take the titular Frogun, a wise sentient frog gun that shoots its tongue and gives advice, to help you on your journey.Right from the outset, I was enamored by Renata's cute design and cheerful attitude. I really need this kind of wholesome vibe in my life right now, and her always smiling face fit the bill perfectly. It also helps that the game is quite fun and light-hearted overall, it just makes me smile.The gameplay consists of exploring simple 3D platforming levels in search of collectibles and the level exit, pretty basic stuff. The levels are usually pretty short and abstract, in contrast to games like Yooka-Laylee or A Hat in Time with sprawling themed levels and large landmarks. That may dissuade some 3D platformer fans right from the outset, but one must understand that Frogun is not trying to be like those larger-scale games, instead choosing a more straight-forward, snacky approach.The closest thing I can compare Frogun to are games like the Bomberman platformers on the N64, that Pacman platformer for the PS1 or, more recently, Super Mario 3D Land, but even those games do not match the exact vibe Frogun goes for. Despite the simple, short levels, Frogun is very much a collectathon at heart, albeit one that comes in bite-sized portions.Personally, I really like the smaller level size this game goes for. I love collectathons, but I'm often overwhelmed when I have an entire new world to explore with upwards of a thousand different collectibles to obtain, so having a collecting experience divided into tinier levels is exactly what I need to keep me from feeling fatigued.The levels are quite fun to explore, and the controls are pretty good too... mostly. Renata's slow walking speed, combined with the lack of a run button, makes it a bit annoying to backtrack, but not enough to ruin the fun. Also, I like that the levels reward attentive eyes with hidden collectibles, while still being streamlined enough that finding everything is never overwhelming.Furthermore, in an era where every major videogame release is trying to de-gamify, focusing on atmosphere and immersion, it's a breath of fresh air to see a game like Frogun, content with being, well, a videogame. Every aspect of it, including the visuals, the enemy behavior, and the level design, reflect this "videogamey" philosophy, which I appreciate. Now, I'm not saying that an immersive de-gamified experience can't be good, but sometimes all you want is to play a gosh-darned videogame for a change, and Frogun is exactly that.I do have some complaints, but they're not huge issues. The levels near the end of the game become quite hard, some boarding on unfair, considering how fast we need to aim while jumping in order to avoid certain obstacles. For the later levels, it's way more fun to just run through them instead of trying to get every little thing, because otherwise, the search for the last coin might make you pull your hair off.Also, according to what I've read from some completionists here, getting all the cosmetics will require a ton of repetitive grinding. The latter really doesn't bother me, since I hardly ever go for completion, but still, might be good to know if you're into that stuff.All in all, Frogun's lack of pretension to grandiose storytelling, coupled with an adorable aesthetic and its intuitive, enjoyable, simple gameplay, made a fan out of me really freaking quick. I recommend Frogun to anyone that just wants to play, you know, videogames.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: I would have given this game a glowing review if I stopped playing before the Dragonfly boss, but I'm astounded how fast I came to hate nearly every aspect of this game from that point forward. The controls have their weird quirks, but nothing I couldn't get past until the game decided every challenge would be bouncing over pits. The targeting, even with the so called "Smart Targeting", is horrendous and I can't remember the last time a platformer character had such a weak jump. You only get two chances to shoot your target mid air to pull yourself forward, but I've had the game shoot to both sides of a target multiple times, despite it being two feet in front of me, sending me falling to my death. None of the control options made any of this better.  I went from 0 to 1 death each level, usually from goofing around, to 20 to 30 deaths every level, killing any fun I was having and making every attempt at time trials and no death runs miserable. I would suggest if you get this game to stop immediately once you finish the volcano area and save yourself the aggravation.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: god i love this game. i only heard about it a few days before release. i bought it on release. and i just finished the main game and am definitely coming back for the post game levels and 100%. theres some frustrating mechanics. and the frogun doesnt always work exactly how i want it to. but other than those small issues its clear that a high level of care has been put into making this game. and the diorama like level design is something really unique. i cant think of another game with this feel. good game
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: If you like 3D platfomer collectathons then I believe you'd like this game. It is a delight and very pleasant for the first 2/3rds or so then becomes tedious at times when spots require precise aim, which the game isn't equipped for. I stopped going for everything once it started to feel more like a chore than fun and it led to me being much happier as I wrapped it up. Overall I had a great time!
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: I love every single thing about this game. The gameplay is challenging enough to be engrossing but not to the point where it's discouraging. The MUSIC, and I cannot stress this enough, is SO CATCHY and every track is an whole MOOD. The controls are easy to get a hang of. I personally prefer playing on controller, but playing KNB is also easy and intuitive. Seriously, this game is perfect.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: All in all, I think Frogun is a fun game. I had to take much of the back half in bite sized pieces though because I got frustrated quickly (not the game's fault). I almost finished beating the levels (just start to finish, not 100%), and as I've seen others comment, the game has two speeds: 1. "Oh, okay. That was fun." and 2. "COME ONN!!!" I think at the time of posting there are QoL improvements that the devs are working on to blunt the edges on some of the more frustrating elements of the game. Overall, it's a fun indie platformer.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: Where to begin. If you're looking for a game that scratches that classic PS1 Croc/Crash itch then look no further than Frogun. The game's controls and mechanics are simple. Not in a way that takes from the player's experience, but in a way that allows the player to quickly become familiar and then be thrown into new and fun ways to use them. The restrictive low-poly approach embraced by classic games turned to aesthetic is the foundation of this game. Built on top of that is a very fun soundtrack, perplexing puzzles, crunchy SFX, and a personality that I find lacking in many recent games. I bought this game on steam and plan on buying the special edition through Limited Run Games for my Switch. Buy this game. You won't regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a blast, Love the aesthetic, love the music, the worlds just look beautiful and the gameplay is fantastic. I enjoy all the different collectibles in the game and think that overall this game is easily worth the price. There are some issues I do have with the game: When having to grapple midair it's very difficult to make some necessary right angle turns to the point where it feels borderline unfair, there are some mixing issues with the audio for example the Freezy fight and a few nitpicks on aiming as well as coin collecting. THE GOOD NEWS: everything that I have issues with for the game has been told to the Dev already and they're already planning on making major changes to fix it. With these changes the game will go from a game I recommend with some caveats to becoming my game of the year and a must have for anyone that even remotely thinks they'll enjoy it from looking at the trailer. It really is an incredible game and for the amount of hours of content it's honestly a steal!
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: Couldn't get it to work with my Ps5 Controller.Tried with or without Steam Input.Tried with DSX. Tried with DSX emulating it as an XBOX controller.It never saw my controller input.Note: Steam input seems to think my wireless keyboard is worth noting as a controller so maybe frogun also sees that and always takes the first. This might be a very niche issue.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: Platformer junkies should absolutely add this to their collections. For as much inspiration as it draws from the aesthetics of retro 3D platformers, the gameplay truly puts it in a league of its own. The grappling skills you have with the Frogun may seem simple,  but the nuances of each level and the multiple objectives you can aim for have kept it from feeling stale so far.  My one big nitpick is that I wish I could remap controller inputs to make LT aim and RT shoot, but when the core of the game is this fun, it's absolutely worth it anyway you slice it.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: Was gifted to me, as it was on my wishlist.It's an awesome piece of work where I feel the love in the design and the execution. I had a blast and the way the challenge ramped up was pleasant and surprising. By the end of the game I was very impressed. I hope these devs get to make more in the future.Plus, frog themed.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: So, I just finished Frogun tonight and I got to say, I recommend it. The story is releatively simple, you're just saving your parents; although the lore you can find is pretty deep. Now as for the platforming, the game starts off pretty easy but gets harder as you progress. Although the Crystal Skull segments are really challenging if you want an extra challenge. The combat is pretty simple as it isn't too complex for normal enemies, although you will have to think in order to beat the bosses. The rival races are pretty fun as you are trying to race against your rival and get through the level as fast as you can. There are plenty collectables, which you can use to buy health upgrades and hats. Now, the frogun is a bit hard to aim when you first use it, but you'll learn the ins and out of the frogun as you play the game. Overall, I had a fun time with Frogun and I recommend you give it a shot. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: No vertical aiming, what?Joke at the start of the review aside... well. I like the game I just have a good chunk of frustration with the game as is as well.Going to state this now: I like the game. A good chunk of the stages are well designed, and so are most of the boss fights. I like going out of my way to find the hidden secrets, and the collectables as such are quite fun to find and collect. However, this review is going to mostly talk of the negatives I have experienced.The ones I want to note in particular: - Sometimes, things feel very hard to dodge and overall feel somewhat unfair (Looking at you, Scorchy). - I find the delay between a missed Frogun shot and being able to shoot again is a bit too long, which is especially notable when in the air: Multiple spots in the game require you to shoot multiple times mid-air, esp. in Worlds 4 and 5, so for the delay between them to be as long as it is sometimes makes it feel as if you are more or less cheated out of a potential recovery from a mistake.- I feel the Frogun shot length is just... off in some way. Really not sure what it is.- Some of the death planes are too high up. I know a lot of these planes are for things where you can't really recover anyways, but it doesn't feel good to be right on the cusp of a platform, miss, and then immediately begin the falling death animation when you have barely even missed the platform.One thing I'd suggest for this game, outside of some fixes to my personal gripes, would be a zoom option for the Camera. Being able to zoom the camera in and out closer into and further from Renata would help with visibility a whole lot. May also be worthwhile to have a dither effect to show where Renata is if she is behind a wall?Overall, nice game, but currently in need of a little more polish.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: This game is cutesy and has a neat sega-saturn/PS1 inspired visual style, but rides those two positive traits for all they're worth.The movement sucks, it's sluggish and slow and aiming and using the frogun isn't great either.The levels in the first 3 worlds weren't too bad but takes an insane nosedive from world 4 onwards, with level designs and environments that mimic each other for 3 worlds straight.The race levels are absolutely horrendous and the bosses are ungodly boring.Other aspects of this game such as the story, sound design, and such feel so cheap as well. They really just went all in on the graphic design and that's it. Too bad when this game finally released there were already a ton of games in this style!
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: I'm having an awesome time with Frogun - I'm not super good at 3D platformers but this definitely has a great range of difficulty. You can play at your own pace or take on some really fun fast paced challenges, including racing another character across entire stages. The camera controls are majorly helpful and smooth which are essential to a game like this, and also helps you enjoy the awesome art. The enemies and platform puzzles are constantly surprising in a great way. Completionists will absolutely love this.A goofy critique: I need Ranata to say a fun encouraging phrase when you choose a stage! It would be such a perfect additional hit of nostalgia :P
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: Frogun is incredibly frustrating due to the extremely difficult platforming. You have to be super precise on where you land or you fall to your death. Racing stages are stupidly hard (I've given up on the very last one). This wouldn't be such a hassle if it gave you a couple of save points. Instead it sends you back all the way to the beginning for you to repeat it over and over again until you perfect it or somehow get lucky.As a pro it has a charming art style but I'd say that's it.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: I'm updating this review to reflect current thoughts on the game as someone who was majorly interested in speedruns and continued play beyond just beating it. The design of this game leaves so much lacking, and the poor quality control from the developers leads me to believe much of it isn't going to improve, at least not for a while. When such a large update comes out with a mile long list of patch notes, I get excited, but when a good chunk of them, especially ones including sound effects not being tied to any channel and blowing my ears out, didn't even actually change I become less so.The greatest thing I can say about this game is that the base movement is more than serviceable, and the Frogun itself is a great idea. It's used to pretty decent effect in a few places. Sadly, it's not nearly enough places, as many levels simply use the Frogun to cross gaps, throw some objects, and chain grab certain objects. This is the entire extent of the Frogun's utility. It's a simple enough set of tools that allows for some fun level design here and there, but across 15 hours of play it gets stale very fast. Many levels opt to repeat the same patterns and gimmicks with a new coat of paint, the largest shakeup being blocks that only appear when you are close to them. These blocks are my second most hated feature of the game. There are more than a couple times where I'm shown a long gap between two platforms with a few things I COULD grapple to, allowing me to chain grab, only to figure out part way through the pull that there were invisible blocks. Not a problem on a repeated attempt, but often times they necessitate a repeat attempt, and being forced to fail isn't fun.Meanwhile, my MOST hated thing in this game, the boss fights. They are time wasters that make no use of the Frogun at any point. They all consist of dodging attacks for a set amount of time, and then throwing an object at the boss. I like to follow this line of thought when it comes to game design: "If I were to replace this mechanic with something simpler and less engaging, would it functionally change?". In this case, if the frogun were replaced with a simple attack button, or maybe the main character picking up a box and throwing it herself, would the outcome of the experience change? My answer is, no, it wouldn't. Mechanically it would work exactly the same, you simply just don't have a certain model in your hand that looks like a frog. The few exclusions to this are noteworthy, as they almost have a good idea going, the main two being ones where you must pull blocks around using the frogun to harm the boss, rather than throwing an item at them. This could be a great foundation, but again, what does the Frogun add to this fight that pushing or pulling them with your hands doesn't? The Frogun's main sell, in my eyes, is the mobility it offers, and the boss fights never make use of this unique feature, instead opting to do boss fights in a way other games do, but worse.So how do we rectify this? It's simple, movement. The most enjoyable part of the game is finding fast and creative ways to traverse maps and avoid obstacles with what's essentially a glorified grappling hook. To this end, why is this idea never used in boss fights? The best case you could make for it being there is the final boss fight, where some of the damaging blocks randomly can't be moved so you use them to pull yourself to a block that can be moved. Never is it explorered further than this, and by that fact alone the boss fights kill any sort of replayability and longevity this game has.As it stands, most of the enjoyable movement comes from glitches anyways, such as being able to pull yourself onto a ledge by grabbing a surface directly at it's ledge and holding forward, but that's not to the game or the developers credit, it's unintended as far as I'm aware. Pile on some missing QoL features such as no rebindable keys, a wonky camera that's been known to induce motion sickness, sound effects not being tied to any channel so they're just horribly loud, and arbitrary death planes set around levels preventing any sort of player creativity, and you're left with a pretty hollow experience. It's possible that some of these things will be fixed with future updates, but I think the core of the game itself is just poorly designed, and a waste of a good idea that tries to sell you on cute art and copious amounts of collectibles before it worries about what it's main mechanic can or should even do.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: Very charming platformer, but grows boring fast.Theres a lot of level design variety, the bosses are fun and I like collecting stuff, but that wasnt enough to keep me interested.You start the game with a basic jump, and the frogun that can snatch enemies or latch onto things, there are no upgrades, no level based power-ups, or environmental mechanics that keep it fresh, none of that, a basic jump is all your getting. Frogun has such a nice concept, but keeps it as simple as possible, its pretty disappointing.If you feel nostalgic and the simplicity is no issue for you, then I recommend buying it, otherwise no.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: As a PS1 style platformer it hits all the right buttons BUT I think it also brought too much of the PS1 style control scheme. Accurately aiming the Frogun on a jump where you are landing on a platform that is going to fall away is too clunky and hard to get precise at all so you're often dying just desperately pointing in the direction of the platform you want to hit as you die. I like the aesthetic and idea, I just think modern versions of it should have tighter controls.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: Its a mediocre platformer from PS1 era but has too many issues. Basically no story. The camera and aiming are truly awful. You cant judge distance or verticality, and in a game where you have to aim and shoot and latch on to things its even worse. The icon for a target lock will appear but then your shot will be too high or something which is poorly implemented. Your girl runs slowly, and her jump is too low and falls too fast. Most of the game is instant death pits. They never add new powers or change much up and it gets pretty repetitive. Apparently you can get more hitpoints but I never saw how and it was never explained to me. But it still has the foundation of an alright game. 6/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: Bought this game thinking it'd be a lot of fun and at first I was right I was really having a lot of fun. Then a few hours later i began to realize that this wasn't fun anymore. So first things first, lets talk about the best part of the game- the platforming. I think this was amazing, it was super fun. Many of the levels felt like they were designed to be explored so that you could find new shortcuts to beat the level faster and faster. Definitely a game meant for speedrunning. Since I'm done explaining the good lets move onto the mediocre. The music for the game is forgettable. I played the game yesterday and the only theme i can remember is the racing theme. While its not bad, its just not on a level of good. Another thing I strongly dislike is the collectibles. Each level has several goals to to achieve that create a dragonfly stone? gem? (idk what to call it). Thankfully frogun's devs made it so that progress towards those goals through several attempts (i.e. meaning you dont have to do all the goals in one run.) One of my issues with those goals is finding all the coins within a level. There have been multiple stages where I have scoured the entire level and I end up missing a few coins and I just don't know where they are. Either it means I missed an area or they're in one of  the jars I thought I broke, but I can't tell which I've broken or not because they all respawn when you die. Another issue for me was aiming your frogun. There were multiple times in a stage where I was unable to properly aim the frogun which lead me to some deaths. While i did find this to be very annoying, I do feel like playing on the steam deck was also part of me not being able to aim to well (that or I'm just being too nice). Race levels were also a thing but most were super exploitable that it kinda doesn't really matter, in the end it just felt like another normal level. Thou cheers to them for getting the player to be able to explore the level after the race. Also theres a story in the game but it just kinda happens. Nothing really too interesting overall about it.Finally, the bad part(s) of the game. Lets start with the bosses. I think these were the worst parts of the game. Many of the bosses had attacks that felt too unpredictable and would end up damaging you. Not all bosses had these but most of them did. The bosses felt as if they were design to be a boss where you have to keep dying over and over until you understand their attacks, which i think is dumb for a platformer. Another thing that actually pisses me off about bosses is that you can grab onto them with your frogun which drags you towards them. The only ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ purpose this serves is to damage you except for one boss. Why even ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ add it for all of the bosses, just add it for the one. The other issue I have with this game is the glitches/bugs. Some of them are relatively harmless. Others were just plain ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ annoying. One of those bugs is enemies being able to hit you if you are next to them one block below or above them. Nothing indicates where they're touching you but it ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ annoying. Lost too many stage and boss attempts to that ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Overall for a developer's first attempt at a platformer its ok (not game they have made two other games before this), but its flaws caught up to me and I couldn't find it fun anymore. I myself cannot recommend this game to anyone. But hey, maybe you're different then me and can find a way to make these faults fun. 5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: Frogun is one of the best 3D platformers I've played in recent years. The art style is fantastic. The soundtrack is catchy and gets you in the mood. The gameplay is simple and addicting. Especially the first hour of the game is pure magic. Your frogun is your main source of travel. You can latch on to walls, activate switches from a distance, and pull enemies toward yourself. It's a multi-functional tool, and once you get used to the controls and master the frogun, the game becomes a joy to play. I really enjoyed my time with it. I finished the game %100 and got all the achievements. There are also a couple of things that annoyed me while playing Frogun, and I want to share them. One of the major problems the game has is boss fights. The boss fights in this game are so bad that they ruin all the enjoyment. I am a huge Crash Bandicoot fan, and I thought boss fights in Crash were bad. It really shows that Frogun didn't need boss fights. They kill the entire flow of the game. One minute you are jumping, sliding, and collecting coins, and a few minutes later you are locked in an arena dodging randomized attacks and waiting for your turn to attack the boss. Another problem I had with the game was the quantity of collectibles. It's a 3D platformer game; of course, I want collectibles and I want to collect them all, but finishing some of the levels felt like a chore. Especially at later levels, this situation gets worse. You have to collect 500, 600, or even 700 coins in order to fully complete a level. I think this amount is absurd and unnecessary. The other collectibles are great; I didn't have a problem with them, but the coins caused lots of frustration on some levels. Overall, Frogun is a fantastic game. Yes, the game has flaws, but I still love it, and if you are a 3D platformer fan, I am sure you are going to like it too.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: Will get boring before you finish a quarter of the game.Lots of pointless padding, including 2 almost identical "boss rush" levels at the very end of the game.Bosses are barely working, extremely boring. Their attacks are extremely poorly telegraphed and sometimes can only be described as BS. There is no challenge there except to not get randomly hit one too many times.To get all achievements you WILL have to buy everything from in-game shop but you will lack ~30000 coins even after you finish the game will all medals, meaning ~3 more hours just grinding for coins.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: The game has a lot of charm, with fun mechanics that have potential to create a fluid platformer. I have 3 problems that deterred me from completing the game:1- Stiff Gameplay: At times it feels like I'm playing a puzzle traversal game from how stiff it feels to control the heroine. Aiming your Frogun, jumping, running, all feel stiff. and the animation kinda emphasizes the stiffness sometimes.2- Bad controls: The controls are bad. And there is a lack of ability to fully customize them to your liking. After ~6 hours of gameplay, I still had issues with them.3- Lack of Polish: I avoid this making this criticism for indie games, but this one got compounded enough to ruin the experience. I'm not gonna mention everything, but some of the things include: lack of meaningful custom control options, lack of ability to push down on the last item in a menu to go up to the first, being able to control the camera / character through loading screens, bad camera positions at start of levels, and other stuff that makes the stiff gameplay and bad controls a worse experience.I will play the sequel eventually, and I can see the gameplay has been sped up. I hope my other issues will get fixed soon because I really wanted to recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has been SO fun. I'm a massive fan of this era of platformers, and it's been a joy to play from start to finish. I've heard some people lodge complaints regarding auto aiming or the general difficulty of the game. I... have experienced none of those issues. There's a handful of times where auto aim gets in the way, but a bit of micro spacing stops that from being an issue. I believe there's also an option in the settings for disabling auto aiming entirely too. The platforming controls are tight enough where I always feel in control. _childDocuments_.review: While the graphics are charming and the concept is great, the game has a critical issue that makes it difficult to enjoy. The main issue is that there's a discordance between how difficult it is to aim and how quickly the game expects you to be able to do so. The titular gun is aimed in two ways: 1, moving the character such that she faces the direction you're about to shoot, and 2, holding down the aim button to have more precise control. The normal mode is imprecise and risky in situations where a misstep could cause your death. The precise control mode is not available in midair, and is also quite slow. The level design frequently thrusts you into situations where you are midair or in an otherwise precarious situation (a crumbling platform, for example) where you simply do not have the time to aim before you shoot, which can make the game feel unnecessarily frustrating. There are various other nitpicks, but they all fall under this type of complaint where it feels like there is a significant and unintentional gap between the thing you are trying to do and your character's capability to do so.

_childDocuments_.review: ...and in February I'm still playing .If you're looking for a game that scratches the collectathon itch, Frogun is a gold-standard option. One things I'd like to address before starting this review: while this game appeals to the completionist types (myself included) you are in no way obligated or required to 100% this game. To those who took the time to write negative reviews, claiming that the developers had  by making saving up for art gallery pieces take too long, here's a reality check for you: the developers aren't wasting your time, you are. The additional collectibles are optional, and if you don't want to "waste" your time, you have the autonomy to choose not to go for 100%.Sorry, it felt necessary to touch upon the critique of others, since the core gameplay of Frogun is so polished and addictive, and the negative reception in the reviews felt rather unwarrented.Frogun harkens back to the 3D platformers of the 90s, with hundreds of collectibles, colourful settings all the while utilising a satisfying original movement mechanic.Our protagonist  undertakes a quest to save her parents, with little more than a sentient, talking gun (beating  to the proverbial punch by several months). This "", for lack of a better term, is a speedrunning machine, and part of the metagame is figuring out how to beat levels as fast as possible by jumping off ledges and aiming for distant, grabbable surfaces. Indeed, the game actively encourages you to beat levels as fast as possible, with developer time trials for each level (frustratingly often without the actual par time listed, though most expert time trial goals are quite generous).Style-wise, Frogun pigeonholes itself firmly as a 'retro revival' title, graphically reminiscent of an N64 or PS1 release at the dawn of the new millenium, but beyond a couple of glitches and exploits, Frogun is a very polished game, with diverse environments and addictive gameplay, so don't let its humble fashioning fool you.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Exploring the Potential Realism of "Little Nicky""Little Nicky," a comedic film released in 2000, directed by Steven Brill and starring Adam Sandler, presents a fantastical world where the son of Satan embarks on a mission to save both his father and Earth from impending doom. At first glance, the premise seems entirely rooted in fantasy and absurdity, but upon closer examination, there are intriguing elements that suggest it could be based, at least in part, on reality. This essay delves into various aspects of the film to explore its potential realism.One avenue to consider is the exploration of mythology and religious beliefs. "Little Nicky" draws heavily from Christian theology, particularly the concept of Heaven, Hell, and the battle between good and evil. While the film takes significant liberties with these religious concepts, the core ideas of a divine hierarchy, the struggle for power, and the existence of supernatural beings are deeply ingrained in various religious traditions. Across cultures, there are numerous tales of gods, demons, and otherworldly entities interacting with humanity, suggesting a shared human fascination with these themes.Moreover, the portrayal of Hell in "Little Nicky" raises intriguing parallels with real-world interpretations of the afterlife. The film depicts Hell as a chaotic realm filled with eccentric characters and surreal landscapes, where punishment takes various bizarre forms. While this portrayal is exaggerated for comedic effect, it echoes certain philosophical and theological interpretations of Hell as a place of torment and suffering. Throughout history, artists, writers, and theologians have depicted Hell in diverse ways, reflecting cultural attitudes and beliefs about sin, punishment, and redemption.Furthermore, the character of Nicky himself offers insights into human nature and the complexities of identity. As the son of Satan, Nicky grapples with his dual heritage and struggles to reconcile his demonic lineage with his inherent goodness. This internal conflict mirrors the age-old philosophical debate about the nature of good and evil within individuals. While most people may not be the literal offspring of Satan, many wrestle with their darker impulses and strive to lead moral lives despite external pressures or influences.Additionally, "Little Nicky" touches on themes of family dynamics and the challenges of living up to parental expectations. Despite being the heir to the throne of Hell, Nicky's relationship with his father is fraught with tension and disappointment. This portrayal reflects universal themes of familial conflict and the desire for parental approval, which resonate with audiences regardless of the fantastical setting.Furthermore, the film's humor and absurdity serve as a lens through which to examine deeper existential questions. Comedy has long been used as a tool to explore complex themes and provoke thought, and "Little Nicky" is no exception. Beneath its slapstick antics and over-the-top characters lie reflections on the nature of good and evil, the power of redemption, and the importance of friendship and love.In conclusion, while "Little Nicky" may seem like a purely fantastical romp on the surface, it contains elements that resonate with real-world themes and experiences. By drawing from religious mythology, exploring universal human emotions, and using humor to probe deeper questions, the film offers a whimsical yet thought-provoking take on the nature of existence. Whether or not one believes in the literal existence of demons or heavenly realms, "Little Nicky" invites audiences to ponder the complexities of morality, identity, and the human condition.

_childDocuments_.review: Frogun is a fun little 3D platformer focused on condensed, single level experiences. The main focus as the game's namesake implies is the frogun that allows you to grab onto things from a distance to either bring them towards you or bring you to them! This naturally plays heavily into the levels as the deeper into the ruins you travel the more precise and quick shooting you need to be with it to cross some gaps as jumps just simply won't cut it.The levels are very well-designed with speed in mind and some minor exploration in order to be able to get all emblems. Some are trickery than others but I can't say any of them gave an impossible feeling, if anything the most that it's done for me personally was taking a longer run of a level just to see how and where I could cut corners to save on time which was quite fun! If you're looking for a little platforming adventure to enjoy casually, then this game might fit your interests easily! For those like me who like to 100%, or in this case 150%, their games then this game gives you some extra challenges to face with that added difficulty that any completionist would look forward to so I'd recommend giving this game a try!I only have a couple of complaints:-the auto lock aim would sometimes lock onto something but when I fired it wouldn't go remotely where it was saying it would, which in the later levels would end up with a fall to death.-The winter area boss has a sound effect that is not affected by any of the volume sliders in the game's options, meaning it was extremely loud every time I fought that boss in all instances the boss shows up, not just in the winter area boss fight.

_childDocuments_.review: Frogun is a cute platformer that revolves around the use of the “Frogun”, which lets you grapple to walls and enemies alike. Every level in Frogun is relatively short, but they are packed with many optional objectives such as coins to collect, gems to find, time trial, etc. which will make you spend more time in the levels. So while the levels are short, going for the optional collectables is worth your time and makes up the majority of the game. For most levels I only needed to play them twice, once for the main collectables and then once more for the time trial, and this formula worked well. My favorite part of the game was definitely the time trial portions. Experimenting with the Frogun to figure out how to cut as much time as possible throughout each level was a treat, there was nothing more satisfying than finding a way to clear a level in 14 seconds because you found a way to grapple around.I peeked at some other reviews and a few of them were either about the camera or the controls being bad, and I disagree with them. Using an Xbox One controller, you press B to shoot, and A to jump, and if necessary you can hold down RT to aim the Frogun which locks you in place. As for the camera I think it also works fine, it’s a rotating 3rd person camera that is a set distance away from the player so you're able to spin it around as much as you need to to help you adjust for any jump or Frogun shot, on top of this you’re able to see so much of the level with the camera and using it to look for secrets within the level is incentivized (which I personally love). Both of these feel fine and natural to use so I'm confused why so many people found difficulties with them. (Also the game has an indicator for where you’re about to land much like Crash Bandicoot 4 has, and it makes jumps that much easier, just for this addition alone the game is fantastic.) I won't pretend like the game is perfect however, the bosses of the game are a bit lackluster, they have very few attacks in a set pattern that are simple to dodge, and the use of the Frogun in them is mostly just using it to attack, I think bosses where you had to rely on platforming would’ve been a nice addition. On top of this the end of the game features a boss rush level, which wasn’t the most fun thing to do. Another major complaint (which will only apply to those who decide to go for every achievement on Steam) there are two achievements which rely on you purchasing every hat and gallery art from the in game shop, but the amount of coins in every level assuming you perfected every level, does not come close to the mountain of coins you need to make every purchase, they should have been made cheaper.Other than those two complaints, the rest of the game was incredibly enjoyable, an easy recommendation if you enjoy platforming collectathons.

_childDocuments_.review: Frogun is not a long game, running through just the campaign will take around about 6 hours but the real fun to be had here is that every level gives you various side-goals to complete and that can rack you up a lot more time and a lot more fun.Of course to talk about the game itself, as you have probably surmised it's a retro style 3D platformer and it's great! This game called Frogun gives you a frog that is also a grappling gun, and it really does make the most of it. Easing you in through the first world, it starts ramping up complexity until you're swinging through the air not touching the ground for entire platforming sections at a time, and thought any one section might take you a couple of tries, every level has more than enough checkpoints to cash in a successful jump. I do recommend a controller for this game as it's easier to make precise inputs than with a keyboard and mouse. Especially if you want to get the camera to look at the optimum angle to make the jumps easiest to intuit.In short, if you like 3D platformers it's absolutely worth your while, and the developers really did make the most out of their frogun gimmick. As a result I'm looking forward to playing their next game Frogun Encore when it releases.

_childDocuments_.review: I am writing this review after receiving 100% Completion/Achievements (just over 11 hours playtime).It's decent. I found it very cute and enjoyable, with some minor complaints.The controls feel nice (depth perception is a pain, but that could just be me, they do try their best). And the game is really forgiving. I went for all of the Collectables and Achievements, and it wasn't bad at all. The speed times are really fun to pull off. If you're good, you are likely to complete each level 2-3 times, and there are 42 in total. I never felt punished for dying (except when going for the Deathless Medals), which is a good thing in my opinion.The main reason I wouldn't recommend this more, was because I just found myself getting bored relatively quickly. About halfway in, I was ready to be done. I'm excited to see what they do with the sequel that was announced, though.I found some of the hit-boxes to be very misleading, and the death zones off stage to be all over the place. I died multiple times from "falling off the stage" when there was a moving platform that went even further down than I did.The bosses were pretty nice. The Final Boss I found was a tad too fast for my liking. There were many attacks that just felt unavoidable due to Renata's slow movement speed. And the Winter level Boss has a TERRIBLE sound bug, so much so that every time I had to fight it, I would completely remove my headphones. This still hasn't been fixed and I have had the game for over a month, so I doubt it ever will.Other than that, if you like cute 3D Platformers, give it a shot, maybe you will like it and be able to play the sequel on release one day!
