_childDocuments_.review: Frogun is a pretty casual, and rather short PS1 styled puzzle platformer, where you use your gun to latch on to walls, enemies and objects to navigate each level.It's fun, but flawed in a lot of aspects. The main problems being the Frogun itself, some of the platforming, and, despite being completely free to move, the camera.Most levels you can invalidate a lot of puzzles simply by using the small amount of height you gain from latching on to a wall repeatedly and essentially jump over walls or across chasms with tight platforming. Some of these shortcuts seem to be intended, but one example I have is from the later levels, where you have 4 gated off areas, with the intention to run through each, press a button and go to the next, unlocking the 4th to continue. However you can simply jump to one side of the 4th gate, latch on to the wall, slowly move across and then latch on to the other side, cutting down the level time to under a minute.The second big issue with the gun navigation is that you often get a short hop over certain interactables which is usually helpful, but the moment you have to chain together shots to navigate over a chasm, it can throw you off, as many balloons or blocks are below the height you end up at, meaning your first attempt at a shot will miss (and if you miss twice without hitting anything, you drop like a rock and can't fire your gun again). So you have to wait just a split second, which wouldn't be a huge deal, if the void out zone wasn't so close below you in these chasm sections. Meaning you run the risk of ruining your deathless run through a level if you time it wrong, and it's so easy to get wrong.With the platforming, two things come into play. The camera and general movement. Your character moves pretty slowly, and as a result, doesn't have much momentum when you jump. Which is fine since it's not often that tricky, but you will come across platforming sections where you have to jump from moving, crumbling platforms and then latch on to a wall or balloon to safety, and need to be able to move and jump quickly. Can be a pain but ultimately you can overcome this.However, the camera often requires you to "set up" beforehand. Meaning some Frogun and platforming sections are made easier (by way of vision or being able to move your aiming reticle to the right direction quickly) if you have a side view or top down view before hand, so you're not trying to jump and adjust your camera at the same time.Those are some of the major issues I saw that might prevent someone from enjoying the game.On a personal gripes note, I didn't like a lot of the underground or cave levels, and thought the volcano and snow zones were a lot more interesting and fun but were unfortunately way too short.Outside of all of this, the bosses were fun, the level design was generally good, visually it's quite charming, and the music doesn't get distracting and pretty well fits each level. I just wish some zones had a few more levels to them, and the platforming was a bit better.Overall I'd recommend it, if you need a quick distraction, and love retro inspired video games.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: Some great ideas, but some ideas were executed poorly. The Frogun the main mechanic of the game, the hitbox could need a fixer upper. Hitting walls that are too close to you even if you aim away from the wall will get you killed. A lot. However the game itself is a fun around 3 hours experience. 100%ing it will require you to play some stages close to perfect, but that's kind of expected if you find a game to be fun enough that you want to 100% it so no complaint, just an observation. It's pretty cheap so you won't lose much if you end up not liking it. I personally had a good time albeit some complaints. 7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed Frogun for the first 4 worlds, as it mostly relied on fun pathing, inventive platforming and had absolutely stellar music. Sadly, the only thing that it carries over into the second half of the game is the music, as the jumps get finicky, requiring precise aim, which isn't really feasible in this game. This results in a lot of deaths that don't feel like the player's fault, especially on later levels with gimmicks like blocks that don't spawn in unless you're close to them. The bosses, which were somewhat tedious from the start, only get worse and I might have liked the game overall had it not had these janky, drawn out fights.Jank, in fact, is the main problem for the second half of the game. I decided to quit when the final boss glitched out on his last wave and just placed himself outside the arena, where I couldn't damage him. Things like that and the frogun not latching onto the right targets made the latter half of the game a really frustrating experience that eventually just stopped being fun. I'm still going to try out the sequel, because the initial stages were quite promising and the graphics and music are both amazingly stylized. It's just a shame that level design takes a nosedive and bossfights bring out the worst in this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: Very cute platformer! A friend gave me this, as these aren't the kinds of games I usually buy for myself but I was hooked on the cute gameplay and rather satisfying collect-a-thon mechanic. Also, beating the Brutal Boss Rush without dying left me with shaking hands and one heck of a buzz (and it didn't take many attempts either). It's one of those games you start out struggling with, but after a while you become really rather good at it! If you like these sorts of games, then it's definitely for you :)
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: It's a really enjoyable 3D platformer with collect-a-thon elements. Its retro look is also a plus. If I had to compare it to anything, I'd probably say it's like an easier Crash Bandicoot with coins being crates and collectables for achieving stuff in the levels (such as time trials or not dying in the level). It's really adorable, but has a fair amount of challenge. I think my only gripe is sometimes it is hard to aim the Frogun while in the air and I really hate those skulls that are introduced in the spooky world. If you are going for 100%, you will have to grind coins too for achievements where you buy everything from the shop.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: Fun retro style platforming collecting game.Only real issue I have with this game is how it's very satisfying to collect and complete but then at the end if you want to buy all the hats/art you would need to grind for multiple hours to be able to afford everything. I feel that 100%ing the game should be just enough to buy everything. Other that that bit of un-satisfaction everything else is very satisfying and fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: A real delight to play! Charming in its aesthetics and characters. Levels are fun to complete multiple times as you change up what you're trying to hunt down. Mostly on the easy side but the final level had me going back to find additional health upgrades. Some of the sound effects are way louder than the rest though so you may need to turn the sfx way down. The in game option to adjust your analog stick's dead zone was greatly appreciated.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: this game is SO CUTE and so good omg I absolutely love it so far! the art style is quirky and and adorable, the controls make sense, the music is spectacular, and the gameplay is really addicting. It kind of feels like Croc for PS1 to me, but with a way better camera and controls setup. I'm really, really enjoying it and can't wait to play some more!
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: To the point=====================This PS1 era platformer provides a great challenge in a fun settingGood Stuff=====================- The game gets the absolute most out of its simple control scheme and as the game continues you'll be expected to utilize these tricks to continually improve your skills- There is a surprising amount of challenge in this game. One look at the style and you might think otherwise but I promise you that around the halfway point, the levels will become intense- The bosses, again starting off simple, keep building up until you have some impressive and challenging boss fights- The world and the presentation are very charming, especially when paired with a great OST.- Renata is cute. CUTE!Bad Stuff=================- Some of the later levels feel just a touch too long due to the kind of maneuvers you're expected to pull off- Pulling off precise wall bounces sometimes feels like hit-or-miss, which can stink if you die right before a check point- I really wish, for the coin collecting medal, that once you picked they stayed collected. I cannot tell you the amount of times I got to the end of a level with 559/560 coins and basically gave up since I knew I'd have to start from scratch on my next run.- The race maps.... I mean at least let us skip the race part after beating Jake the first time.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: A fun old school style 3D collectathon platformer. The main attraction of this game is the grappling hook style gameplay, the Frogun. You can use it to pull pots and enemies towards you to throw at other objects/enemies. You can grapple walls and heavier objects/bigger enemies to pull yourself towards them. You can also bounce on objects and enemies like Mario  games. It is fun to find out what portion of the stages you can skip with the grappling.Each level have a fair number of goals to aim for: Collecting all the coins, the note, the two gems, the black skull, beating the level deathless, and beating the level under target time. Luckily you don't have to aim for all of these in one attempt so you can do multiple stage clears to get all the goals cleared. Deaths aren't too punishing, it puts you back to the previous checkpoint with all the coins/note/gems collected before hitting the checkpoint again. The pots/enemies/black skull only saves after you hit the checkpoint. There is a silver and gold target time but they aren't necessary for 100%. Silver is very doable if you know what you can skip in a stage where as gold leaves almost zero room for error.You have total control over the camera, it isn't static or fix at all. Think of the camera similar to Toad's Treasure Tracker where you pan it around to look for hidden objects and secrets.The levels have a fairly balances and increasing difficulty curve where it slowly introduces different mechanics and gimmicks and slowly starts combining them all towards the end of the game. It does become a fairly difficult platformer but not to the extent of a precision platformer like Celeste or Super Meat Boy.The boss fights you either like or dislike. It's a standard wait until the boss does all it's attacks and becomes vulnerable to hit and repeat. From the time I've been playing, I don't know if there is a way to speed up this process so the bosses fights can end up being long. You spend quite a bit learning and dodging attacks. It is hard to make a platforming bosses fight engaging/entertaining.Other things:-you can buy new hats to wear for your character-you can buy gallery images that contains various artworks-the music is good-there are a variety of screen filters to mess with if you're into that-there is a 2 player versus mode, I haven't tried itSome problems:-there are a few stages where you race a guy. not terribly difficult of a race and some of the racing stages can be cheesed really easily, the problem is that you can't leisurely explore the stages until after the race which at that point you're might be backtracking. you can't explore during the race because if you lose the race, it counts as a death. this by default makes for a longer level than usual-being a 3d platformer with various amount of skips, there are some jank-a lot of people complained that during a casual 100% playthrough of all the levels you still need to grind anywhere between 1-3 hours for coins to buy out the shop, which is required for some achievementsI had a good time, worth checking it out.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: I like Frogun!I was recommended to try Frogun courtesy of AntDude's YouTube video, "9 MORE Switch Games You Should Play And Probably Haven't Yet". And he recommended a good one here.I love this game's old-style, low-poly graphics, and it's cartoony style and characters (AH THE CHARACTERS. The characters in this game are very cute and well-designed. They are very iconic in my mind). The music is actually pretty good, and while the story is simple, it's precious and really fun-loving. It gives off major Mario and Banjo Kazooie vibes, with a heavy dash of "cute". It's really just my style of game.My only major criticism would be the gameplay.Don't get me wrong, I quite like the gameplay! The idea of the grapple mechanic is fun, and *does* work... but I think it could be much better. It works great in some situations (particularly ones where you can take your time or don't have to be perfectly accurate with your grappling) and absolutely awful in others (in this case it would apply to levels that require you to grapple fast AND accurately).To be extra clear, I particularly am critiquing how the gameplay doesn't quite fit with the level design at times. For example: imagine you're playing with the camera at a top-down, birds-eye view. You need to make a grapple-jump maneuvering combo like the following sequence to get to your goal: up, right, left, and up again. You successfully land the first move with accuracy, but when you attempt to turn and grapple the next object, you're not aligned perfectly enough, and miss the object. Maybe you grappled too early and went above the target-- maybe you went too late and are below-- maybe you just grappled too much to the left or right. Whatever happened, you then fall into the void and are returned to your last checkpoint, which is either pretty conveniently placed or pretty inconveniently placed near to where you died.You keep trying, and you find that you fail that sequence multiple times-- and not even at the same point every time. You just keep missing your targets by so little every time.This is what I've encountered quite a bit while playing. The grapple mechanic is good, but it's bound to one plane-- that being the horizontal X plane. And it leads to many situations where I juuuust miss my goal and have to try over... and over... and over... again.That's my biggest critique, but I have one more critique-- the 100% completion requirements.There is absolutely no way I will ever 100% complete this game. I wanted to, but I just don't think I have it in me. There's so many things you must achieve to reach 100% completion-- and it's a back-tracking GRIND. You'll most likely have to return to a large portion of the levels you've visited just to recollect collectibles you've missed while playing. Pair that with gameplay issues, and it's gonna be one wild ride.Let me finish this review on a positive high note though.All these issues didn't keep me from casually enjoying the game (except for some glaring gameplay issues/design choices that just didn't work well for the game itself). It was SUCH a fun game. I really liked playing it, and I'm excited for the sequel and how it will improve upon the original.My favorite levels had to be the racing levels with Jack. Despite them being some of the "fastest" levels in the game, in terms of how fast you have to move to stay ahead of Jack, they were just... so well-designed. Surprisingly, these were the levels that really felt the best to play, given the design of the game and it's few issues.All in all, I really do think this game is worth a playthrough, just not a 100% completion playthrough. It definitely needs some polish, but I really did love playing it.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: 100% Completion. This game plays a lot like if Crash 4 was good. Although there's only two movement types (grappling, and jump), the game really shines with its enemies platforms and environments. The platforming was extremely well thought out and I had a wonderful time going for the time trials. There are moments you can see that cheeky vases and just out of reach platforms were placed for the explicit purpose of tricky skips. My favourite levels were ones in which you had to carefully jump off vases and make precarious grapples just to shave a few seconds. The only true complaint I can make is hats and gallery images are way too expensive. By the time I had beaten the game after playing each level 2-3 times, I was in a deficit of Tens of Thousands. For reference, most levels only have 100-300 coins, with some of the longer levels touching 400-500. This would require hundreds of run of grinding the most efficient levels just to get all the unlockables for the achievements. Definitely should be toned down by a lot.8.5/12

_childDocuments_.review: v difficult to fully formulate thoughts on, as its not especially inviting to play, and im not sure how how much the jank surrounding things like multiple grapples in a mid air row is rly Justifiable or whatever...but i did become very enamored very fast, it rly feels something special in my hands, something that demands constant intentionality and engagement, while not being so rough that its not also responsive and pleasureable. u Can get good at it and i think im p good at this point ! i got whole whole bunch of the medals. man this is a weird one lmao, its a nice cute aesthetic in service of a probably imperfect but vivid and extremely compelling set of often brutal (but never insurmountable-feeling) challenges. rly wonderful level design on the whole, discovering time saves for the time trial medals is always a pleasure, a good mix between focused and open. this review is a mess and i need to go to work soon lmao but yea frogun !!! a fun video game

_childDocuments_.review: A really good Platformer similar to classics like Spyro and Crash Bandicoot. _childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: Very cute. Very frog.A solid gem of a game all around. Catchy tunes, unique graphics, interesting gameplay... and believe it or not, it gets genuinely pretty challenging later on. I highly recommend, though 100% completionists beware, you will have to grind a TON of coins if you want all the achievements.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: It started out as a cute little platformer, but it gradually upgraded to a really enjoyable challenge to complete as the levels progressed. The time trials for every level were what really made this game fun for me. Trying to find all the different skips and shortcuts to save time was a blast! Even better still, all of these challenging aspects had a lot of care taken to minimize frustration that would normally come out of them like plentiful checkpoints and keeping coins after death.There's even some clever design on the optional challenges that turns tasks that'd normally be frustrating into a blast to play. Take for instance getting a death-less run through a level... in most games I'd find trying to complete a level deathless repeatedly frustrating. However, Frogun ALSO rewards you for getting a really fast time. So instead of getting angry at any deaths, I simply start the level over so I can challenge myself to get the fastest possible full run of a level. (I did later discover that dying didn't actually add to the total time spent in a level, however, I still like resetting to get the perfect run :P).The other challenges like grabbing the Eyemeralds, all the coins, and the skull also prevent frustration in their design by being extremely forgiving. Eyemeralds and coins are kept after death, and although the skull is not, the challenge room it is placed in always has a checkpoint by the entrance so that you can save right after you manage to complete the challenge room with it.Overall, I'd say this is a great game for anyone that enjoys a challenging platforming experience, or people that enjoy platforming and don't mind having a bit of difficulty full clearing everything. If you're on the fence about this game, the controls are great, the levels and challenges are fun, and there is a cute frog hat to buy in game.I would say my only regret with this game is that there's no more levels for me to complete... however, Frogun Encore should change that once it comes out!
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun platformer inspired by early 3D graphics. you can use a "frogun" to latch to walls and pick up/throw enemies and objects. music and atmosphere are decent! definitely would recommend to anyone interested.august edit: late game is VERY unforgiving. but i still love this game. just wouldn't reccomend finishing it or 100%ing it. play what you can until it gets really hard.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: I justThe more I've played this, and the further I've gotten, the less and less I want to recommend this gameThere's so many examples of just a confusing amount of a lack of polish that it just makes me saddened by how much I've grown to dislike the experienceThe game looks good - the art style is charming and hearkens back to much, much better 3D platformers, but that's really where my praise kind of stopsEach level is essentially the same, besides some surface level environmental palette changes. There are very, very few examples of unique challenges inspired by the world you're currently in, and each setpiece is essentially just a mishmash of blocky outcrops and floating platforms connecting them, which loses its charm by world 3. The camera and general movement is really sluggish, which just rubs off on everything as time goes on. I feel like a lot of the applications for the titular Frogun are surface level, which really sucks because conceptually it could lead to some really engaging scenarios, but it usually just boils down to just grappling, pulling switches, and throwing objects. Overall, if you're looking for a cheap 3D platformer to put a few hours into, go for it. It's pretty cheap and you can probably get some enjoyment from it, and that's what I'm really basing my recommendation off of. If you're looking to 100% every level and go for as many achievements as possible, however, the lack of polish will just show more and more, and you'll probably end up growing frustrated with the game, like I have. Will I still beat it? Absolutely, but only because I'm so close to the end. I'm really, really hoping that Encore fixes a lot of the issues people have had with this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: 100% completed the game. I love the retro art style but what made me love the game was the platforming. When you start to get the mechanics the game shines.Speed running levels in this game is easily my favorite part of the game. Solid title I would recommend to anyone.My main complaint. The final levels in the game should have rewarded a LOT more coins considering the difficulty jump. It was a bit annoying to finish the game and have to grind coins to get all the hats/gallery images.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not usually a big fan of platformers, but I thought this game was pretty cool. A lot of the platforming is based around using the titular Frogun to fling yourself around and pull objects. Like a grappling hook, but a gun that is a frog. This works for most of the game, but towards the end there is a massive difficulty spike and then it becomes a bit frustrating. Aiming the Frogun is janky and it feels inconsistent with what angle you can hit a wall. Sometimes you have to be straight on, sometimes it will accept a bit of an angle, sometimes it rejects everything but a perfect shot. It isn't a problem for most of the game, but once the Frogun becomes the main way you move around, it feels rough. You can shoot again in the air after a missed shot to try and save yourself, which did help sometimes, but if your angle is already bad, it doesn't make much of a difference. Either way, the game is still fun for most of the runtime though. I liked finding shortcuts for the time trials in the levels. The bosses were okay, but I felt like none of them really took advantage of the Frogun.The presentation is alright. The art is very appealing with the chunky retro look, at least in gameplay. The main character is very expressive and the environments are nice. The music is pretty mixed though. Some tracks are great, some are a bit annoying.In spite of some of its flaws, this is a very charming game and I think it is definitely worth a chance. You can definitely see the heart in it. Just be aware after about the midway point, the game gets surprisingly hard.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun 3D platformer. Great controls, music, art-style.The only thing I didn't really like was going for 100%, as I needed to do a ton of grinding in order to buy everything from the shop.Before starting the grind, it had taken me about 12 hrs to beat the game. Could've been done earlier, but I was spending a lot of time trying to get the speedrunning challenges done. Getting enough coins to buy everything took about 4.5hrs, although if I hadn't bought a few things beforehand, it may have been closer to 5.If you don't care about going for full completion, then you'll still have a blast w/ the game. Can't wait to try out the sequel! I think I give this game like an 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: Fun collectathon platformer with some jank. Decent but often forgettable levels.Boss fights are ok, but the last two are great.Collecting is fun for the most part, but if you miss a coin it can be a chore (you need to either backtrack all the way or re-do the level). Controller aiming is terrible though some options can improve it; you basically need to use mouse and keyboard to play this properly.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely lovely throwback platformer, highly recommended!I have never played the "original" release, but as I understand it, some aspects of the game design have been completely retooled.The gameplay is simple but I found mastering it very satisfying, games have compelled me so in years.I can understand some people complaining about "jankiness" but I never experienced it like that. There were very few instances where the Frogun indicator was red but it still couldn't reach the full distance for example.The only 2 downsides I definitely have to mention are-Hitboxes can be pretty wonky, especially the spiked skulls you'll be platforming on. You'll notice you're bouncing off of platforming elements that you've barely touched, or hurt by enemies even though you're supposed to kill them by jumping on top of them.-You have to buy all cosmetics and unlockable art with coins you collect. This wouldn't be a problem if you hit that total sum by collecting every coin in the game at least once, but I have already completed 99% of all gameplay challenges yet I'm at sub-90% total game completion.It's a very lovely game, but it's not fun to grind for coins when I've already experienced everything the game has to offer gameplaywise.I hope these 2 downsides will be fixed in the future, or at least in Frogun Encore.I'm very much looking forward to the sequel and would like to especially thank the devs for providing a Linux build!
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: Great game that instantly reminded me of PS1/N64 era action adventure platformers. It has a cute aesthetic, a photo mode, and collectathon aspects a la old RARE titles. I see a lot of criticisms on the janky controls but to be fair, this is what  the genre was like literally 25 years ago (To me it's more endearing and actually useful more than anything). I also played it on controller so take that with a grain of salt. This review would probably be different if I played it solely on KB+M. The only criticisms I have is if you're 100% trying to complete everything in the game it'll leave a bad taste in your mouth. I found trying to perfect the  levels too hard. Also if you're trying to 100% everything, you need to buy all the artwork in the shop, which in total is some ridiculous number like 42,000 or something? Mind you, the fastest I was able to complete a level was like 1:30-2 min, while collecting around 150-200 coins. And while this is a fun game, there's no way I'm going to mindlessly play a level almost 300 times for an achievement. All that being said, great game would definitely recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: Frogun as a whole is a good game but it has some issues that need to be discussed,On the one hand, it is a game that has an aesthetically attractive retro look for those who grew up in the 32-64 bits console era, similarly to titles such as Mega Man Legends and Banjo-Kazooie in both character expressiveness, textures and sprite models. It is clear from the different sections, the gallery and the concept art that an effort was put into this aspect as well as the soundtrack, where I was able to find a few favorites, including the Fire Temple one and the final boss one. They go from low to high tempo, mixing a variety of instruments and immersing you into a higher quality product of the era.On the other hand, the main attraction of this game comes with its features mechanic: a frog that acts as a gun which can suck some enemies in order to throw them away as well as pull Renata (the main character) towards a wall in a similar vein to a hookshot. Conceptually not only does this open a range of puzzles to be traversed in a 3D space, but allows for certain tricks to be performed. Say, shoot a wall and shoot another one mid air in order to perform a "corner shot". Well, this was implemented, as well as a trick based on constantly shooting the same wall over and over in order to slowly climb it and stay in the air for a bit. I personally got a lot of mileage out of that even if it wasn't intended for the normal playthrough.Unfortunately, the gameplay praises are cut short by the fact that the controls and their execution aren't the best suited for some of the given tasks. For starters, third person 3D platformers are notorious for having camera controlling issues and this is not the exception, as it can be controlled by the right stick but sometimes it's either too slow or inaccurate. This can become particularly troublesome at the time of aiming when you deal with how the game snaps the gun onto targets, which may or may not go your way.But to me the biggest offender to the gameplay is the input delay which I've noticed all throughout my playthrough. Many jumps that I've missed or hits I've taken have come from a delayed command that came just some frames too slow. Combine that with the fact that Renata can't run, so at the time of dodging boss attacks if you haven’t reacted fast enough sometimes you may get close but no cigar. Another criticism I'd like to make has to do with the game completion. To be fair, this can be a non-issue for casual players or those who are satisfied with beating it in a couple of hours, which is what it lasts even if you're not that skilled. In this matter, completing a level consists of earning parts of an emblem which can be done by either collectibles, finishing it under a certain time or without dying. This provides rewarding challenges and takes advantage of the level design. And that it would be all good and well if the completion percentage was limited to that.However, there’s a shop with concept art and accessories which you can equip, and they cost coins. But their prices are certainly very high for the maximum number you can get per stage. On average, most levels don’t have more than 400 coins and each piece in the gallery or a hat costs 500 coins. As a result, given the sheer number on display, this can amount hours and hours off padded out gameplay from replaying each level at least 4 times in order to afford them all, and that is if each run is good enough. Locking the 100% completion percentage behind something like this is mind-boggling considering the alternatives: lowering the prices, increasing the rewarded coins once you get past a certain part of the game or just leaving them for free as art to be marveled at instead of worked towards.All in all, the game is certainly one of last year's indie darlings in terms of its characterization, presentation and concept, but it has a lot of problems at the time of executing them, particularly targeted towards completionists and speedrunners. I'm looking forward to its recently announced sequel with the hope these could be addressed properly.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually write a review for a game I haven't finished yet, but Frogun is such a solid game that I needed to give it a positive review RIGHT NOW. It's a solid treasure hunting collectathon 3d platformer that feells like a combination of Crash Bandicoot, FEZ, Captain Toad: Treasure Tracker and the "Frogger's Adventures" games (no, not because of the frogs) with that lovely N64 era look. It's not a "traditional" 3d platformer, but that is certainly not a bad thing. It knows what it is and it executes its gameplay perfectly. This feels like a game that anyone can enjoy, so I recommend that everyone give this a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely feels like a PS2-era platformer. Loved the art style. The dynamic between Renata and the Frogun reminded me a little of Banjo and Kazooie, one being the straight man and the other being the snarky sidekick. I had the most fun trying to break the levels with the frogun, jumping quickly across obstacles and gaps. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: Love this game. It just oozes charm and cuteness, and it's really polished and tight. The physics are very exploitable and it's fun to speedrun. I don't usually go for time trials in non-racing games (especially hard ones), but this game is an exception. Casual players can beat the game without too much fuss, and experimental players like me who like to push games to the breaking point can have fun finding new and creative ways to skip obstacles. My only regret is that as the game came out recently (like within the past 6 months), there is hardly any community content. I hope an achievement guide comes out soon. cause I have a feeling that it's gonna be hard to figure out some of these. The only negative I can think of is that coin hunting can get maddening. You'll understand when you reach the end of a level after tearing it apart only to still be missing 1 or 2 coins. I almost feel like the levels should have MORE than the number of coins required so that you can miss a few and still get the all coins medal for the level. Just change the wording from "all coins" to "coin collector" or something. Then the coin requirement can be rounded to numbers like 350 instead of 361. Maybe getting more than the requirement adds bonus score
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: I liked this game. A lot, actually. It has the vibes of an eary PS1 era platformer, or even a classic PC platformer. Moving so slow means the level design feels more compact and cosy, which lends to the charm. Also grappling with a frog tongue is just plain fun!The game is also a lesson in frustration. There are simply WAY too many collectibles and side-goals in each level to complete, requiring you to go through them multiple times. Get ready to reach the end of a level, only to realize you're ONE coin short, forcing you to go through the ENTIRE thing again. And while you keep the coins when you die, this is not the case for the obsidian skull. Now, these ARE optional, but the way the score is presented at the end of each level makes you feel bad for not going the extra mile. And even if you do get all the emblems, the progress bar stops at 75%, nudging you to play the boss rush, grind for coins so you can buy all the hats and artworks, etc.And the bosses are some of the worst I've ever seen. They follow the "dodge until you get the chance to strike" pattern, which I've never been fond of, and all of them overstay their welcome (especially that last boss; banger music, but dang was it an annoying fight!).That all sounded super negative, but like I said, I liked this game a lot! I just wished I hadn't spent so much time trying fully complete all the level; my patience ran out when I realized I had to beat the final boss again for the speedrun emblem, and as far as I know, you don't get more than an achievement for it. I would recommend playing this game as a normal platformer, ignoring the collectibles, but you also need to complete SOME of it to unlock more health. Just don't be like me and spend 16 hours on it.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: The game truly shines when you are trying to "break" the levels to blitz through them. Unfortunately, I was doing most of the playthrough in a completionist fashion and once you hit the point of needing multiple playthroughs of a level to find all the collectibles then perfect your speedruns, it started to drain on me. Especially during the moments when your Frogun doesn't grapple to a spot because it hit at just the wrong angle.I played through the last two areas just trying to play briskly and it helped make the game more enjoyable. Don't think I'll go back for what I missed, but 7.5 hrs for a charming indie game I got on sale is worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: A moderately engaging but simplistic platformer, which presents a solid gauntlet of levels to play through.There's nothing about the game that is especially unique apart from the basic grappling hook mechanic. Otherwise the story, the world, the level design and boss design are each quite ordinary. The dialogue is distinctly translated and the story is relatively uninteresting, but the core gameplay system of running through each level is engaging enough. There are a decent amount of different side-objectives across each level that encourage players to replay and optimize their performance. This comprising a significant amount of the substance here. Unfortunately the game eventually requires players to grind for several final achievements, which unnecessarily hinders full completion. But up until then, the process of fully unlocking all the different trophies on each level is decently compelling.The game does a good job of producing obstacles that require a fair amount of attention to surmount yet never become too frustrating for the most part. There is also a variety of moments where obstacles can be bypassed or approached in a more efficient way to reward players that are going for the time trial achievements. The only significant problem with the game mechanically is that there are many moments where players have to worry about platforming and grappling at the same time. This requires players to simultaneously pay attention to the height and depth of their current position which is often not intuitive or even physically possible, resulting in trial and error guesswork on certain grappling maneuvers. Which can be frustrating but fortunately it does not become a significant problem very often.The experience is not particularly unique or memorable per se but it is engaging enough to be reasonably satisfying. Especially if the player is really looking for an okay platformer.If you're interested in finding more games like this I've probably reviewed quite a few on my curator page .
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: Was debating whether I should recommend this game or not, but I will recommend this game if you like cute PS1-inspired platformer game. This game gave me Captain Toad Treasure Tracker vibe as well which I love. The game start off slow, which is great, but get very difficult and precise at the halfway point. The issue is the grappling Frogun is difficult to aim quickly, and with the latter stages requiring quick grappling on tiny platform, over the void, this get frustrating. I wont recommend to 100% the game because of this, but to pay casually through the end will still be fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: This is a wonderful game, casually and as a speedrun. The controls are tight and just wonky enough to allow for great platforming and speed gaming. The asthetics are charming, the soundtrack is chill and catchy, and there's plenty to collect and unlock to keep you going. If you look at the trailer and are even mildly interested, you should just go get it.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: This is a neat indie 3D platformer. It is simple and there are only two action buttons besides the basic movement: a jump and the frogun that shoots a short ranged grapling hook. But later on there are some difficult jumps and movements required so there will also be complexity for those who want it.Still while the game is decent, it doesn't compare to the classics like Mario 64. Also, given how this is an indie game there are a lot of small issues that can be annoying sometimes.The overall audio design is rudimentary, and specially the songs leave a lot to be desired. The music for the first area of the game is painful tough. Also, the frogun behaves erraticaly on diagonal angles; 50% of the time shots are able to graple on diagonal surfaces/angles, and 50% of the time they do not. It would be nice if the game designers made up their mind if they woud allow this type of shot to land and fix the level design accordingly. Related to the above, some of the end levels have many sections where you have to change direction mid-air and keep shooting the graple on sequential floating objects to progress, which is fine by itself but the problem is either the hitbox of those things as I lost count of how many times I shoot the graple right through the thing but it didn't connect (without auto-aim), or maybe it is related to the angle/diagonal approach I mentioned above which is annoyingly inconsistent in the game.Still, I had fun with the game and can recommend it, specially on a sale. just be mindful that this is a small indie game and with it comes a little bit of jank, or in other words, it won't have the level of pure game design polish like more professional titles.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: Reminds me of playing Spyro, with Mega-man Legends graphics. Until about the half-way point. Then the difficulty ramps up to a point where its just frustrating to play.The later game has a sharp difficulty spike, and with that, the cracks in this game begin to show. The imperfect hit detection really starts to sting. Still worth playing the first half if you really dig the art style. Grab it half-off.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: Is it okay to recommend MOST of a game?From an aesthetic standpoint, this game is perfect. It's charming, it's cute, and every enemy/asset is clear to the eye even at a distance. Sound design is workmanlike and does its job.From a gameplay standpoint, the controls are responsive, but Renata falls like a lead weight and your frogun grappling hook occasionally has a mind of its own with auto-aim. This isn't a huge deal until World 5 when you are required to pull off precise platforming challenges while fighting both the camera and your finicky frogun. If I bought this before the quality-of-life patch that let you fire the frogun a second time in mid-air I would have refunded it. It would have been frustrating and borderline impossible to beat.There are also too many collectibles. Every level has over 150 coins to collect as well as enemies/pots to smash, and later levels can go up to 500 coin objects ("700" accounting for their value). Levels can take 2 minutes each, or 30 depending on how much of a completionist you hope to be. Again, there was a patch that let you keep coins on death, so while this doesn't address the late-game issue of not enough checkpoints it does demonstrate that the dev is willing to listen to player feedback and improve.I would love to see more from this developer, just not two conflicting styles at the same time. I hope the sequel to this is either a cozy collect-a-thon, or a white-knuckle grapple-fest with improved controls and camera. But not both.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: A fun throwback to collectathons of the 64 bit era, mostly great, some things not as good. It's a really fun game with a fun story and no shortage of well designed levels. The difficulty scales pretty well the further you get in the game. Nothing ever felt impossible, just challenging (The final boss felt somewhat unfair at times though). Some of the game's main mechanics, such as chain grappling, do not work very well a lot of the time. Sometimes you'll find yourself dying or taking damage from things that could be easily prevented with a properly working grapple.There are some glitches, such as a time glitch that happens sometimes where the timer stays frozen at 0:00, which will basically allow you to take as long as you want in a level and still get diamond awards for the time trials. There are also times when grappling a wall will bring Renata to the wall, but other times when grappling the same spot doesn't work, seemingly at random, causing you to fall to your death.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: It is a very fun and cute game, very reminiscent of late 90s platformers like Super Mario 64 and Sonic Adventure. If there's one big criticism I could give on this game, it's that it's a bit... clunky? The collision can be very weird sometimes and Renata feels pretty slippery to control, and this is especially evident in platforming sections with small and/or rising platforms (mind I'm using a controller to play, others who play with a keyboard may or may not have a different experience). The camera is also a bit janky, and it can be fairly distracting sometimes.I love this game so far, though! I hope to see a few patches in the future that maybe fix or address some of the problems I mentioned here. Looking forward to other games from the developer!
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: It seems the developer had a list of games they loved from their childhood and wanted to cram everything they liked from those different games into one product with no understanding or consideration for how they interact with each other. It hurts me to say that because the demo fooled me into thinking it was a charming platformer. For the price I paid, it's not the end of the world, just another disappointing indie game from someone technically proficient, but needs to study game design for at least another decade first.It's not fun. It's not the worst thing I've ever played, it's just bland because the game design is non-existent. Game design is more than a character, mechanics, levels, and objectives. It is the understanding and deliberate choice to create interesting dynamics with the rules and interplay.Frogun is a . It wants to be a platformer, adventure game, collect-a-thon, time attack, no death run, racing game all in one. Playing a level is overwhelming. The levels are short if you run through them, but very long if you collect everything. There is no cohesion or flow.At the time of this review, this game is on patch 1.92 and it feels like it should still be in Early Access. Massive changes have taken place from community feedback since the game was released, but It wants you to collect all the coins in a single run. Originally dying meant all the coins would respawn. The game was patched with bandages to just let you keep every collectible except the challenge item. It doesn't solve the fact that all these collectibles are fatiguing. There can be 500 to 600 coins in a single level. These coins should have been passive collectibles like the coins in Super Mario Bros. Not needed to be collected, but encouraging jumping, exploration, and giving a bonus when enough are collected. All the collectibles look the same, and many of them are in random jars all over the level.Problem is the levels are linear with some branching loops. You can't tell which routes are optional sometimes. You can see other parts of the level in the background being poorly culled out from fog, only adding to the confusion, instead of, what I guess is, the developer trying to make the level feel expansive and seamless. All it does it create noise. The level should have had warp points that separated parts to be easily digestible.Yet, the lengthy objectives would require a more open world type level design.The levels and collectibles in them have no intentional design to their layout. They are just strewn about the map. The simplest analogy I can give, is good game design is like good music that interweaves new instruments, melodies, and arcs into a complimentary harmony as a whole. This game is like a 2 second rap beat played for 5 minutes.The game levels are made up of abstract islands of platforms. The main mechanics of jumping and the frogun are at odds with the level design.The frogun is underutilized and mostly just annoying. It lets you grapple to objects and drag objects to you. Probably the biggest failing of the game is that there is 360 degree movement and verticality. You are left with a camera and aiming that is incredibly raw and lacking discreteness. Even though 45 degree aiming and camera options were added, it doesn't matter because of the level design and poor registration of aiming.Even if the frogun's tongue is in range of something one of many frustrating things will happen. It won't latch on even if the reticle shows up, probably sending you to your death. You get no visual feedback that you can latch onto something until you point in the direction of something and a reticle shows up that is either grey or red, and it's inconsistent, often showing you can grapple but then not. You have no depth perception in any direction in your range or height. Since most of the game is over bottomless pits, there's no tolerance for mistakes, and no shadow for the character or other critical information to judge your position in 3D space. Even being right next to jars off the ledge and aiming in the general direction will result in you whiffing. The frogun is probably something the developer wanted to be highly flexible because they were thinking of speed runners and attempts to create emergent possibilities, but failed to even make consistent, fun, and useful core mechanic. The problem of understanding shows its ugly head when you can repeatedly jump and mash the tongue and slowly scale up walls. It's sloppy.The levels where you race a rival are daft because the game forces two differing objectives on you: racing and the other objectives. You have to win the race or you are forced back to the start to restart race at the beginning of the level. During the race, you will traverse a lot of collectibles, platforms, and level elements, but it means nothing if you don't win the race. Only after you haphazardly "win" the race at an unmarked point on the map, can you finally loop back and collect everything in the level. Remember, you can't just exit the level and then do the other objectives. You will always be prompted to race, and you are always required to win the race. This means you're looping through the level 2 to 3 times. Even with the changes to how collectibles work, this is a lot to ask of the player. Nothing should have been in the level until you finished the race, then you're forced to exit the level. Once you go back in you can choose to re-race, or ignore the rival and continue on to collecting. Alternatively, lower the amount of collectibles to be manageable to get while racing to add a layer of challenge.In general levels really could have stood to have you pick an objective before you entered and then had the objectives focused in the level one at a time, and some of them should just not have been required for 100%. There is no need to make everything be required. Unlock it after you beat the game as an optional challenge to beat times and not die. If one's response is don't do them all at once, then what are you suppose to do? The game is pulling itself apart with all these incompatible objectives and is placing the burden on the player to figure out what they want to do instead of focusing a fun experience for them.The interface is really not useful. Each of the objectives is a piece of a jewel symbol that makes a firefly emblem. But neither it, nor the high resolution out of place menus with a bizarre font choice give you any indication of what objectives you did or didn't complete unless you memorize what each of those abstract symbols means.Do you know how you can tell an indie game mentality? Everything is strict and meta. Strict jumps. Collect everything perfectly the first time or start over from the start. Obsessions with speed running, collectibles, time attacks, and old poorly designed video games that they have fond memories off because they were young and had nothing better to do than be at the mercy of lives, continues, and replay value that were all fronts to extrude quarters and perceived value out of their expensive game, and not because they were well designed.The bosses are really poor. They all involve you waiting around for a long time dodging poorly telegraphed attacks until their weakness is revealed. There is little to no feedback as to when some bosses are vulnerable or how and when you can hit them. Can you jump on them? Can you latch on to them? Do you have to shoot at it with an enemy? It's inconsistent, contextual, and confusing.I don't know if I can force myself to beat the game. I don't even think I can force myself to finish this review. Everything about this game makes me feel gross and upset. That's a strange reaction for a game with well executed and appealing PlayStation inspired visuals.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: Fun little patformer that grows a lot more then I was expecting the further you go in. Really charming, old fashion game where you get a simple and amusing story with a lot of cute characters, with familiar level themes. The thing that makes it stick out is the Frogun and how unique it is as a method of traversal.It's essentially a grapple hook, but you have free aim of it by just holding a button down. A lot of the fun and challenge doesn't just come from weaving past obstacles if you're trying to beat a level quickly, but thinking outside the box, observing your surroundings, and making use of the tool to get to places you wouldn't think possible to reach. It's rewarding to replay levels to try and finish every objective, and the game proper oozes style and charm.Just be warned the game is harder then it first appears. The most difficult moments are only for those trying to 100% it, but there are some odd spikes. It's perfectly doable, just don't go in expecting something breezy because of the art style.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: an absolute treat to play, and a cute aesthetic to boot! if there's one thing i could criticize, some of the requirements for getting 100% are a bit ridiculous (like needing to purchase all of the in-game artwork, much of which costs quite a *lot* of coins), but other than that it's a wonderful lil game!!
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: Frogun is a decent game with a lot of potential. It’s rough around the edges in some areas that end up being its main sources of frustration, but it’s still an enjoyable enough experience for some players to want to persevere. The game does a great job at being a love letter to games from the era that inspired it. Frogun’s story is nothing to write home about, but is somewhat reminiscent of console platformers from the 32 bit era. The Hoppses, a family of archeologists, decide to explore some ancient ruins. After Tod and Lilly Hopps disappear for a few days after deciding to explore on their own, their child Renata sets off on a quest to find them deep in the ruins, and possibly rescue them from whatever dangers they’re facing.The ruins are filled with expedition notes that serve to provide exposition and more knowledge of the game’s backstory for the players. These are, for the most part, very well written and have a certain charm to them.The presentation is wonderful. The art style is really cute and fits the lighthearted nature of the game, with even the enemies (including spiders, a creature I’m often deadly afraid of) benefiting from the cutesy aesthetics. Even the game’s overworld is brimming with little details that foreshadow what the player will find in certain levels.The soundtrack deserves special mention, with most of it just being really catchy and in some cases, relaxing. The tunes used in the game complement most stages greatly; giving off a sense of adventure, calm, peril, and even a sense of hurry when needed.As it is to be expected of this kind of game, gameplay is the main focus of it. And how does it fare? Relatively well, as it is the only area that’s really missing some polish.Frogun’s main gimmick is the titular weapon used by Renata. Said weapon is a hook pistol in the shape of a frog (so, a frog gun, or “Frogun” for short) that can be used to grab items, throw said items, launch yourself towards walls or platforms, or even enemies. It is a mostly well designed mechanic, but aiming it midair is difficult and frustrating at times, especially towards the end of the game.Stages are divided into three different types: Regular stages, race stages, and boss stages. All of them have multiple collectibles and objectives in them, as well as a secret area; all of which serve to fill different parts of the level finish medal, and are also required to unlock health upgrades and hats. The level design is fine, and most levels make great use of the frogun-related mechanics. That said, the platforming is very clunky and inconsistent at times. For example, there were a few occasions where somehow I couldn’t reach platforms that I had no trouble reaching before, even when repeating the same steps and jumping from the same position. This is especially noticeable when using the frogun, since sometimes it won’t latch itself onto whatever specific part of the scenario you were targeting.There are 36 stages in total, so going for 100% completion in every single one of them might take a while, but I found most of them to be fun enough to have some replay value.Camera angles can make certain traps and obstacles hard to tackle, making some of them outright invisible. Thankfully, the player can control the camera, and proper mastery of it is pretty much required to beat some of the hardest levels.Boss battles are the highlight of the game, giving the player a fair challenge in most cases, although dodging some attacks may seem hard at first due to how slowly Renata moves. The bosses’ patterns are pretty simple, so they don’t take long to learn and memorize.While the game has plenty of checkpoints and unlimited lives, having to repeat certain parts due to the lack of refinement in both aiming and platforming can be really frustrating. One of the post-release patches made it so you don’t have to pick up coins again after death, so that relieves some of the tedium of aiming for 100% completion in levels where checkpoints are scarce.All that said, when the game's mechanics work well, the platforming is very satisfying. The devs are still releasing patches for the game and listen to community feedback, so there's a chance that with a little more work the game ends up being overall great. The game also features a 2 player duel mode, where you compete against someone else locally. The goal is to pick up more coins than your opponent on a timer. I didn’t have anyone to test it with, so all I can say about it is it’s very simple.So, would I recommend Frogun? Only if you’re a big fan of 3D platformers and/or you’re craving one. The difficulty is pretty low, and most of it might feel artificial due to the aforementioned factors. It took me around six and a half hours to beat with only 4 perfect medals, so it’s the perfect length if you’re in the mood for something on the shorter side. I still managed to enjoy the game despite its shortcomings.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: Game is an instant classic. It feels very much like a new buckle on the belt of the old traditional 3d platformers. Every level seems to have been painstakingly put together. The boss fights are a little simplistic, but they do well by adding fun dialogue and a nice little break from the main bulk of the platforming. The levels are well put together and ramp up in difficulty at a really good pace. The frog gun mechanic is fun and feels like a modified version of the chameleon's tongue and Chameleon Twist. Main character isn't annoying and in many instances has fun interactions with the enemies of the game. This game has studied well what made 3d platformers great and adds its own unique angle to a genre and style that hasn't seen too much love in quite some time.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: First off, the game is fantastic. From level design, to enemy and area variety, to the music, most of the aspects of this game are nothing short of amazing! If you're a fan of older platformers, such as Spyro, Croc, Crash Bandicoot, Banjo-Kazooie, etc. you'll probably at least enjoy this game. That being said, I don't think it relies on nostalgia for those games... too heavily. It is definitely its own game, and the heavy usage of the grapple (Frogun) mechanic sets it apart.However, the game isn't perfect. Some late game mechanics can be nothing short of frustrating. Not because it's particularly difficult- the game does have difficult sections which are NOT frustrating- but rather because it feels as though the mechanic isn't working properly. This mostly concerns the Time Trials, so if you aren't going for 100% completion it shouldn't be that big of a deal.Now for specifics:Speaking of the Time Trials, though, they feel wonderfully executed, as if the level and its timings were designed around the "ideal" or "fastest" route. Only a few levels feel like an exception to this, mostly the later, more complex levels. On the other hand, some time trial runs are endlessly frustrating because of the grapple targeting system. It can feel inconsistent in high-pressure moments. Hitting a wall at an angle and not getting the grapple on one attempt, but getting it on another. Also, the targeting system prioritizing pots directly next to a wall, trying to make a long jump and grappling to the wall, only to grab the pot and falling to your death is one of the most irritating parts of the game. It's a small section of it, so it doesn't  the game, but it definitely doesn't help it. Rant:TL;DR This is a fantastic, retro-esque platformer with fairly unique and interesting mechanics, which unfortunately fall short in some small sections of the game. Not perfect, but if you're playing casually, it's a great experience. If you're playing for 100% completion. Don't. At least not right now, in the game's current state. Either way, the game is well worth the $15 it is listed at, and a steal at anything less than that.P.S. My rant may have been long, but that's only because I felt a lot of detail was needed. The pros of the game absolutely outweigh the cons.Edit: I also played the game with keyboard and mouse for most of the game, but also tried it with controller. The jankiness of some areas is not fixed by the controller, and I vastly prefer the keyboard and mouse set up, personally.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: Great game thats super charming that is kind of bogged down in the late game by its own design.for the most part its really fun to explore being able to find nooks and crannys between each level but later worlds demand more precise platforming and aiming which doesnt really match the game and because of that you will probably stumble into unfair deaths. There were also moments when i was playing when the game felt sometimes buggy but that was a minor issue. It was very enjoyable with obvious hiccups but the world design and incentive to collect gives the game replayability and a want to look for everything in a level. The colours and characters are also very charming which made any area very fun to be in and explore I love this game a lot despite the glaring flaws.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: Frogun says it the soul of the PS1/N64 era, and that is one hundred percent true, the only thing Frogun does different is having good controls.Unfortunately if you want all of the achievements, you'll have to start grinding for gold at the end.You need to buy all hats and all gallery artwork, which cost a considerable amount of money, adding at least another a few hours to your play time.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: I think I finally figured out why I don't like this game.  It's a combination of controls.- You have a laser pointer but it's button placement is so that you can't aim and shoot.  Unless you want to hold the controller weird.- The targeting reticle doesn't always work.  It might point to a distant surface, but the frog's tongue might stick to something closer.  It's like with FPS games where you're aiming down sights and your bullet ends up hitting the wall you're peaking around.- You only have the one attack.  It either pulls the item to you or pulls you toward it.  It's not always clear which is going to happen.  And then you run into the problem of missing (which is easy because of the points above), so you might end up being pulled off the level.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: Frogun is a fun and charming 3D platformer, in which your skill will be put to the test!With loving graphics echoing to the days of the PS1 (but with higher definition!) and a great soundtrack, the game will take you through various environments and challenges on your way to save your parents. Collect coins and diamonds with your trusty Frogun in hand to grab or grapple things near you!Overall, the game is really nice, even if it gets tough at the end, where the camera and handling can often trick you to fall into deadly pits, though I seem to understand a patch is underway to ease certain advanced moves.Otherwise, it took me 11 hours to finish all the stages, and I haven't collected every emblem in the game.If you like 3D platformers, chances are Frogun will be right up your alley!Congrats to the devs for this really fun game!
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't finished the game yet, but after playing it for 4 hours, I can say it is just OK, nothing incredible.The main character is charismatic.The sounds, although very simple, do their job well.A joystick is a must and your worst enemy in it is the camera. Simply horrible. A fixed camera would be much better.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful love letter to the PS/NS4 era of gaming. This game was clearly made with a lot of love and care and it is refreshingly cute and innocent. As other comments have mentioned, I was also a little frustrated by the sudden ramp-up in difficulty, although perhaps trying to get every single collectable in every level on a first run is a bit unrealistic!
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: This is a must-have for 3D platformers fans. Tight level designs, gorgeous artstyle, and kickin' music. The only thing I'm not a fan of is the damage your rival deals during races. Other than that, I'm having a great time. As the game progresses, levels get full of so much to collect, yet are short enough that replaying/dying mostly comes as a small hindrance. PLus, Renata is simply adorable.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: Fun, challenging, and a good callback, but with it's own identity. With this genre of game, bosses are usually half baked and not very challenging, but with Frogun, work was put into the bosses to make each one of them unique and challenging (Especially the final one).Not to mention the sheer amount of content in this game. Took me 7.2 hours to beat the game, not including the post game content, which is pretty impressive for an indie game.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: I 100% recommend this game. The gooides in each stage made exploring each small stages very enjoyable and satisfying trying to collect all the items in all the 42 levels. I like the concept of the grappling system used to hook to walls or drag boxes at times It gives its own identity within the 3d platforming genre. My complaints are time running in dialogue and grappling sometimes not sticking all the time as it seems to stick within every 45 degree angles and also the grappling auto aim can ruin my chain grappling which i use the square button to fix aim but it did cause frustrating deaths at times.Overall not perfect but still very good and a lot of heart was put into it made by a small team and for fans of the 3d platformer genre I heavily recommend it
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: Really well made classic collectathon with a lot of style and heart. Lots of QOL stuff like an obvious shadow and auto aim make this one of the least frustrating collectathons I've ever played. The levels are dense and fun to explore in a Captain Toad sort of way while also being made for speedrunning. All this plus an interesting core mechanic and an excellent soundtrack make this a must buy if you're a fan of the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: An adorable old-school platform where you play as Renata, who is in the mission of finding her parents. Your partner in crime is an adorable frog-shaped gun (or gun-shaped frog?) that let's you grab/throw stuff with the frog's tounge, as well as zipline to otherwise unreachable regions. It's such a creative mechanic that adds a new twist to the genre. Huge recommend!Here's my first impressions:
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing a lot of 2D games recently, so my review might be exaggerated but so far the game is amazing at launch and with the first patch already in beta, any small issues will be fixed soon. The controls of the game are easy to learn, however there is no re-mapping of controls at the moment. The visuals are charming and nostalgic, and they don't take away from the experience. The mechanics and animations are very smooth and unique, and they slowly introduce new mechanics with every few levels to keep the game interesting and challenging. I really like how this game tried to mimic the old days of 3d platformers, and it did so very well. The soundtrack is not great but it's not annoying, although i wish they would at least have different boss music. The game is challenging if you want to get all the collectibles in each level. Otherwise its relatively easy. This is a game worth 100%ing
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: Frogun NAILS that "extremely tight controls, but one wrong movement could hurl me off a cliff" feel of an N64 platformer—I haven't had this much fun with a platformer in ages. The visuals are stellar, reminiscent of the N64/PS1 era but not artificially held back by their limitations. Did I mention the soundtrack? Incredible.I want to add that this game is a perfect Steam Deck game. The low-poly visuals don't lose detail on the smaller screen, support for a 16:10 aspect ratio allows you to make full use of the Steam Deck's display, and being able to put the Steam Deck to sleep makes stepping away from some of the more challenging Obsidian Skulls a bit easier to do (oh yes, this game gets challenging in the best way).One thing that would make Steam Deck support even better is Steam Cloud support. I'm someone who likes to switch between playing on my Steam Deck on the go and my primary desktop while I'm at home, but without Steam Cloud support, transferring the save file between computers is a bit of a pain and so I've stuck to my Steam Deck for this one. The Steam Deck is a great way to experience the game, but I'd love to be able to switch between computers more easily.EDIT: As of August 10, an update has been released to enable Steam Cloud support, and it's great!
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: She has a frog and it is a gunThis game is...really fun!Only real complaints I had in my main story playthrough were sound glitches and steep difficulty spike in the 2nd half where multiple frograpples in different directions were really hard to pull off. However, it appears that these issues have already been acknowledged where some will be addressed shortly after launch and others will be addressed at a later time (including an auto-aim tightness option, which I'm personally really excited for).As for the positives, Frogun really nails that retro 3D aesthetic in a pretty solid 3D platformer experience. Customization options, multiple game modes, great soundtrack, quirky dialog, animated cutscenes...the list goes on. Fantastic work, Molegato and team!
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: Frogun is a cute throwback platformer bringing something new to the table. The Grappling hook mechanic is fun, and the level design is terrific, giving you some challenges, secrets, and different ways to approach problems.If you are looking for a sweet casual platformer, Frogun might be just for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: Just started the game and it's been wonderful so far. Love the retro graphics and the whole Frog Gun mechanic, it's a lot of fun.If I could compare it to something, it's like Captain Toad: Treasure Tracker but with more platforming and freedom of movement. There's also extra settings for you to change the look of the game, and my favorite is the retro filter.It really feels like something I'd like to play until I get everything, Seems like a Completionist/Speedrunner friendly game.I hope you folks enjoy it as much as me right now!

_childDocuments_.review: Early review to help visibility.I have played a few levels of Frogun and, so far, I'm having a lot of fun. It's a classic platformer, very much in the line of those launched for PSX and N64, and it plays and feels exactly like you imagine when thinking about that time. Why am I saying this? Because I've read a couple bad reviews talking about the controls and sound design, and, while they're not superb, they work perfectly. They're just... classic. Vintage. Old-fashioned. And, in this kind of game, I think that's a feature, not a bug! To highlight something, the game has some collectibles per level that require exploration, but it also rewards you for completing the levels as fast as possible and without dying. That offers replayability, or at least different approaches depending on what playstyle you prefer. The frogun/grappling hook mechanic works really well if you master it to speedrun the levels; I just tried that.In summary, I recommend the game if you like 90s platformers or want a similar experience. I do not recommend it, however, if playing Crash/Spyro/Banjo makes you angry.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fun and makes me want to play more! Oozes charm, you can see the dev(s) put all their heart, time and soul into this game. Very tight platforming mechanics, fun level design, lots to collect and find out! Just passed a fun boss fight.If you like games like Captain Toad - Treasure Tracker or any collectathon then buy this game!It's refreshing to play a game that is simple, satisfying and wholesome, no sad story, just fun.Only bit of feedback to players: if the coin collection sound is driving you mad, you can set its volume separately in the audio menu, helped me.Amazing work devs, it's a labour of love, thanks for making this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic game that is well designed and while serving to give a nice taste of nostalgia for N64 era 3D platformers, it is its own unique thing and experience.It has collection challenges, it has speed running challenges, and it has some clever puzzles and hidden paths and collectables. I've only played the first six levels, but I enjoyed each one enough to play until I got all the challenges for the levels done. Fully recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: Frogun has a great platforming concept that is implemented well and has great level design. The levels are short with plenty of checkpoints (so far only one level has a section that feels too long), plenty to collect, and very cute aesthetics. Each level has a challenge room that presents quite a tough challenge, and each level can be time attacked as well. With cute outfits, a bestiary to fill, bosses to beat and more, it's definitely a game that is worth your attention.
_childDocuments_.name: Frogun

Full 1280 x 800, gamepad works brilliantly, although the prompts (which you don't need once you understand the basic controls) are a little "old indie game"-y, i.e. it'll list "Hold X/right shoulder button" as plain text instead of icons. _childDocuments_.name: Frogun

_childDocuments_.review: I have only had a little bit of time with the game but the core gameplay loop is solid. The game has me wanting to get all the collectibles and find all the secret areas. Thank goodness for the checkpoints which come in handy for sure. The controls are really smooth. I have been playing on my steam deck which is great for short gameplay sessions.
