_childDocuments_.review: The following summarizes my Sins of a Solar Empire 2 gameplay experience so far. My rig: I5-12400F, 32 gb DDR4 ram, RTX 4070 TI Super. The game is installed on an ssd and all the drivers are up to date.Positives:- The game is a decent sequel to the original.- It has partially washed away the sorrow and bitterness i had with HW3 release.- Graphics are so good that sometimes i find myself watching my capitals dishing out and forget to manage the rest of my empire. - Wonderful art piece level sky boxes.- The music is very good. - I wish someone made a full movie like the intro. - Stable game performance, i experienced no crashes or frame drops even during 2000 point fleets engaging each other. - Some new innovative mechanics such as shifting orbits require careful planning and spice things a lot.- Unfair and above difficuilty provides a challenging AI which has a passive income and maphack. Hard to defeat.Negatives:- The campaign is pay-walled behind the premium edition of the game. This is a bad move by the designers.- The UI is hideous and outdated. It has to be redesigned completely.- Sounds require rework. Female voices are too loud and very annoying, some ship guns do not have the audible weight they deserve.- Ship balance is all over the place. Missile spam defeats everything, carrier spam decimates all. A new mechanic has to be develoepd to encourage mixed fleet compositions. At the moment, everyone is spamming either carriers or missile ships. - I found the capitals very fragile and sacrificeable. It should be the opposite.- There are a lot of ships and features missing from the original.- Tooltips are mostly absent.- Research tree is complicated and the representing icons rarely tell what the research is about. _childDocuments_.review: It's rough around some edges, but overall I think Sins 2 has a very strong foundation to being a fantastic sequel to the original game.So some context to my history with this franchise. I bought this game back when you bought PC games inside physical stores. Back in 2008, I took my allowance money to the store and bought this game and it was a mesmerizing and beautiful time in my childhood. Several expansions came out which I wasn't able to play because I was too young to have a credit card and there were no physical copies. Several years later in February 2012, I managed to convince my parents to pre-order Rebellion on Stardock's website before it released and paid them back in cash. I remember downloading and playing the beta as the loyalist and rebel factions were released and was astounded with this. It was one of the first multiplayer games I played with my friends along with Minecraft. Anyways, I'll talk about what I see as the pros and cons of the game: - Honestly, I was worried about the game requirements being too heavy for my 8 year old laptop, but it still runs pretty darn smooth. It's awe-inspiring to see the evolution in the models and texturing from the advancements between 2008 to now.  - The music in Sins 1 was fantastic, and it follows it up in sins 2. I will say I wish the main menu music was a little more iconic like in Rebellion, but it's by no means bad. - This may seem like a weird pro, but I assure you it's very important. By Rebellion v1.9, the devs set the engine to be large address space aware which got it to a maximum of 4 GB of RAM. Due to age, Sins 1 got more unstable and could crash. The new engine should last for a long, long time. - The fact that planets orbit now and create new phase lane connections over time is incredibly cool. The new additions of planet building slots and capital ship item slots adds a neat tactical touch and lets you specialize those. The new exotic resources and species unique economic mechanic (Trade for TEC, Unity for Advent, and Phase Manipulation for Vasari) helps reinforces the differences between each playable faction. - Many ships such as the 2nd faction corvettes, anti-structure ships, space mines, diplomatic ships and capital ships are not present from Sins: Rebellion. They may add this in the ship pack DLC, but I'm not sure how I'd feel about getting ships that used to be in the first game in a DLC instead of part of the base game. - Auto-building space structures is weaker than it was in Sins 1. It used to build in a spread pattern which required enemies to spend time navigating around an orbital well to blow up structures. In sins 2 it builds in a clustered formation and will easily go down since they're all next to each other. This seems to be done to reinforce a new orbital structures mechanic (which itself is actually cool). While it can be useful to rotate all these away from phase lanes, I would still prefer the choice to switch between a clustered and spread auto-build function. Also, just being able to click into auto-build mode is no longer a thing  (or at least I couldn't easily find it). Holding ctrl to auto-build is somewhat clunky to me. - The settings are incredibly sparse. There's no way to change 3D model details or particles in case your computer is very old to make it run more smoothly (or want reduced particle effects). There's no ability to adjust resolution other than virtual fullscreen and resizable window which while neat, feels incredibly unconventional and difficult to get exact resolutions in situations that require them (e.g. streamers using OBS that want the game to run windowed at a specific resolution so they can use a standard layout while having screen space for other things). There's also no accessibility options (such as colorblind mode or the ability to turn off skyboxes and other visual elements which may be distracting to some) which feels behind the times and out of touch for a franchise of this size in 2024. To be honest, there's less options than Sins 1 so it's been especially noticeable. - By far the weakest part of the game. When it comes to strategy games especially RTS games, the UI design is incredibly important because the design needs to be efficient, clean and not be artistically dull. The good news is it's not artistically dull. The bad news is it's not always efficient or clean. Let me break this down. Take the planet interface in Sins 2. This is a UI widget I would describe as well put together. It has icons so once you've read the tooltip to what the icons mean, you can quickly associate them to what you need to do when you're rapidly trying to build an economy. Ships there, specializations there, slots over there. Bam, bam, bam. Quick and snappy. Good UI design.The research tree is what I would call a very mixed bag for UI design. Sometimes it's clear without using the tooltips to enlarge the picture what it is you're researching (e.g. crystal, shields, ships). Other times it's not clear. A lot of the icons have too much backgrounds in it, some of the art is reused in multiple places (which make it hard to quickly associate it to a specific research, since 1 art = multiple research choices, it's not memorable for it.) The design language is also all over the place. It feel very unfocused and some things have a lot going on in them and other things don't. Compared with Sins 1, where the research art was very clean and immediate at a glance to tell which research was what without expanding a full icon art, this one is quite frankly kind of a mess. Like the laser upgrades were easy to tell because it was a laser that got progressively bigger and changed colors as you went up in tiers. This one has a laser, a different laser, multiple different laser guns, and a laser gun firing a laser all in a prerequisite chain. Especially when it's at icon size, it can be very hard to tell what you're looking at. I won't argue about AI ethics here because there are a million other forums for that, but regardless of it being AI-generated or not, it simply isn't working to make the UI easier to navigate.Ship items and planet buildings art also suffer from this problem. I think simpler and more stylized icons would have sufficed for all of these.I hope that the devs will try to polish up on some of the rough edges as content is being released. I think this game will truly shine as a sequel once that happens. Looking forward to getting a campaign (something originally planned for sins 1 but cut) and the mysterious fourth faction answering 16 years of questions finally!

_childDocuments_.review: I was a big fan of the first Sins game, many moons ago. I am glad to report that the devs at Stardock have created a newer, better, shinier version of the original game. This is a great implementation of space battles and conquest, with a lots of levers to pull and 3 different races with quite a lot of depth and varied play styles. This game does not try to change things much, so if you are looking for revolutionary mechanics, this is not it. What this is, is a very polished version of a good space strategy game. The new game runs very smoothly and I am very much enjoying it. I recommend it if you like space battles and no nonsense good games.Right now the game only has single player scenarios (quite a bunch of them) and multiplayer lobby for scenarios ranging from 1 to 1 to crazy 10 faction all against all. There is no campaign, which is something I would like to see one day. I still recommend the game as is today. I mostly play single player  and I have a lot of fun building my empire and managing space battles., I do not need much else.  One additional note, the modding community for this game is absolutely amazing. They are a main factor in keeping the original game live for so many years. I cannot wait to see what they come up with now that this new, better game has come out. My thanks to them, and looking forward to things to come!
_childDocuments_.name: Sins of a Solar Empire II

_childDocuments_.review: Positives The game runs smoothly no matter the speed, galaxy size or number of players.The graphics are decent and the fleet combat can be enjoyable to watch, given that the weapons fire smoothlyEach faction has somewhat of a different strategyThe minor factions add some variety to the game, which can make for different strategies each run.NegativesThe game becomes a bore fast.The planets rotating and unlocking new lanes of travel seems like it would be important but it ends up being a very dull gimmick, which rarely brings excitement.The supply cap effectively creates a one fleet system, where you end up just having long battles where reinforcements are needed to flood in to turn in the tide of battle.Early game defences are expensive and mostly ineffective, late game they become good but the one fleet system means that whoever attacks first normally is going to lose as the defences delay long enough for a full power fleet to reinforce. The tech tree has AI art, which may make it look nice but rarely makes for understanding what you will be unlocking. Furthermore, the tech tree is a lot of boredom, much of it is merely increase this, increase this, decrease that, creating a dull and repetitive move.No campaign yet.No steam achievements.No map editor.Overall, the game has promise but for a game that has been on epic for 2 years, should have a lot more content, not just be a smooth game. For what we currently have, it is a smooth running, overpriced, repetitive but promising game.I would wait to see if they can make the game better in the coming months, and ideally pick it up on a large discount. For now just hope the game gets better, because the way it runs is amazing, the lack of content is the main disappointment.

_childDocuments_.review: The amount of love this game is getting I understand as there is a ton of Sins 1 and Rebellion fans out there. However, it is quite barebones. If you are new do not expect this to be a strategy game beyond the scope of what old school Red Alert was - Starcraft 2 has more strategy to it than this. This is more of a standard RTS in space. I've had some fun with it but  for me it comes with lots of annoyances: in wormhole tiles it is very hard to select your ships, my ships often will move on their own even while placed on hold position, and their version of balance seems to be some sort of goofy rock, paper, scissors thing (TEC vs Advent becomes so tiringly annoying - to me at least). The moving map is both good and bad as on paper it is interesting but in reality it can add up to be annoying. There is a lot here that, in 2024, just makes me scratch my head... Why no true 3D movement (Homeworld did this in 2003)? Why is the map full of sectors that contain only a planet and a few rocks or an asteroid - and not solar systems? Why does this have its own launcher? Why are mods listed within the game and not utilizing the Steam workshop - or why not allow both? Why is there zero motion to the "world" - no weather, no gas clouds moving, nothing - just a pretty jpeg background? This game, if you look at it and its mechanics, is a game that could have legit come out in 2008. Again, I am getting some entertainment out of this but it leaves much to be desired. Then you have the unit chatter: it's horrid - it's like Command & Conquer kind of chatter. It feels lazy.

_childDocuments_.review: I would encourage people to avoid this game. The development team has been very resistant to changes needed for PvP-related balance. Many veteran players have confirmed that it’s the lowest of their priorities. The community is toxic, with PvE players who have mod powers abusing them to prevent PvP-related changes. The community is in decline, and the original game had a history of having a very limited population. From all we can foresee, the game will return to that limited population. The gameplay itself is unbalanced and not intuitive, and is limited to just one or two combinations of ships per race.

As minor complaints voice lines can repeat non-stop. A good example is when trade ships or your insurgents pop up in an enemy system with a phase inhibitor. God almighty the game reminds you nonstop. I once had it repeating for 5 minutes straight and I am not exaggerating. Another issue is fleet movement. They should really bring back a button that locks a fleet to move as one because right now ships just jump one by one as they see fit.
_childDocuments_.name: Sins of a Solar Empire II

_childDocuments_.review: This is my 'Red Alert' in space. I've never heard of this franchise before tonight and picked it up on a whim after getting bored of my other titles. What a gem! I like the no nonsense approach to building your empire and taking on the enemy. You can also play defensive and form blockades  in intersecting systems. I enjoy the build up of making massive fleets and then rolling head on into huge battles and planet bombardments. Pausing the game mid battle and flying around and past the ships is great and gives you a sense of scale when you are close up and right in the thick of it. I find it simple yet deep enough to keep me glued to the screen. If you want big fleet battles without the tedious micromanagement, then this is it. I'm looking forward to this getting better and better.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who's never played Sins 1, I am pleasantly surprised by this. I'm a huge fan of Stellaris having put 100s of hours into that game so the initial look appeared similar and drew me in but they are quite different games. Sins is truly more of an RTS than Stellaris where I can complete a game in 1-3 hours or so where most paradox campaigns could last me a week plus.If you're into that faster pace while still managing the intricacies of an economy/culture to keep your empire expanding, then you will enjoy this game. Also, graphics are amazing and the UI is clean and easy to manage. It did not take me long to feel comfortable with the game at normal difficulty.

_childDocuments_.review: Sins of a Solar Empire II is very much a return to form, as it is basically Sins 1 but with a lot of quality of life improvements to the UI and management of technologies and fleets. It's still the same very enjoyable RTS with 4x elements with some new added wrinkles, such as the orbits of planets and star systems slowly changing which actually transforms the battlefield over time. It's also very technically polished (no crashes, looks great, runs great at ultra settings). So why I am not recommending it? Because this game launched at full price while being unfinished: at the moment there are tutorials, about a dozen custom maps to fight on against the AI or humans in multiplayer, and zero single-player campaign. Instead, the single-player campaign is locked away behind a season pass and is promised to be released a year from now. Look, if you know your game is lacking major components, just release it into Early Access and signal to us that it's unfinished, rather than releasing it as a finished product for a finished product price. I'm sure I'll be playing a lot more of Sins II when the campaign and fourth faction are out, but for now it's a somewhat bare bones - albeit very polished, experience.

From the same copy-paste planets and asteroids to Clunky camera movement, cluttered, confusing old-fashioned UI on top of that the voice acting get's old real quick and becomes more annoying than anything else. Most of the time you don't even know what's going on, and the painfully unclear researchtree feels like it has little impact on the game. Comparing this to Stellaris or Endless Space is a complete joke.This game would've been nice if it came out in 2004.

_childDocuments_.review: Caveats first: I love games with spaceships. Always have, always will. I've also been a big fan of SoaSE since the original launch back in the early 2000s. This game ticks all my bias boxes and then some. Feel free to take a pinch or two of salt with this review.Right, now onto the game.Gameplay:The game is an incredibly robust re-imagining of Sins1. The ship combat identities have been stripped of hidden stats and modifiers, what you see is what you get; capships have been made the stars of the show; planets R O T A T E now(!); planet development and construction have been greatly streamlined; faction identities have been dialled all the way up to 11.In short, the game plays like sins but better.Most of the iconic ships and abilities from the first game are still present. Javelis swarms are still a nightmare, Advent still have strikecraft for days, the Coronata titan still hasn't learnt to chill out, and ships still jump between planets a lot.Put simply: in gameplay terms Sins2 is a direct and meaningful upgrade to Sins1.There are several new aspects to the game. The most notable of which are the staged HP states of capital ships, and the new interactions of Point Defence and missiles. Capships now have their HP split into shields, armour, hull, and "crippled hull". Shields is what it says on the tin, a bubble around the ship which only starts to regenerate after a moderate delay. Armour, much like shields is an extra hp bar, it however also offers damage reduction to the ship, and is likewise depleted as the ship takes damage; as with shields, when it no longer takes damage it starts to regenerate, but after a much longer delay. Hull is what it says on the tin: it's those squishy fragile bits under the armour plating. This leaves us with Crippled Hull. When a ship has no Hull remaining it goes into a Crippled state where it can no longer fire or use abilities, but can still use its engines to attempt an escape. This adds an interesting tactical decision-making aspect to larger fights, as its easy to eject capships from fights, but not so easy to finish them off decisively.The new Point Defence interaction is really quite simple: missiles can now be shot. As compensation, missiles are now a fair bit punchier, and my god do you REALLY need to bring PD along to survive.Art, Music, Sound, Visuals:Visually the backgrounds and planets and other assorted decorations of the game are superior to Sins1. Stars glitter a bit more, the backdrops have godrays sometimes. Transitions when zooming in are gorgeous. There's no doubt about it, the backdrop is picture-perfect.Now for the ship visuals. In short, TEC look gritter and more armour-clad than ever; Vasari look like the ancient scions of a long-forgotten empire lost to the depths of space, and advent decided that their ships should also have togas and crystal spires too. The capships of the first game have all had an incredible makeover, making them shinier, pointier, or heavier as the faction identity demands. Ships were already very distinct, but now they also ooze character too. That visual upgrade is not solely limited to the capships though. Even frigates and cruisers got a makeover, and the new characters to the factional lineups are just as good. This visual display is not just limite to static ships however. Turrets turn and track, lasers, kinetics, beams and missiles all contribute to a fantastic lightshow which makes even tiny skirmishes a visual delight. Have no doubt, the game is a visual spectacle without compare, contesting Homeworld 3 directly for the title of "prettiest space game".The game's soundscape is similarly well crafted. Ships do not only have single barks and shouts when commanded and selected. They now react to the situation of the battlescape. A capship losing its shields while heavily outnumbered will sound scared while a capship on the verge of destruction in a battle you're winning will happily make its sacrifice for the empire. This alone is an excellent development, making the battlescape alive in a way which few games have done previously.I would be remiss at this point if I didn't mention the UI. It's a good UI. Nothing revolutionary, it's clean, direct, and reflects the faction's aesthetic in a pleasingly traditional way.Finally we come to the art. A lot has been made of the usage of AI in the art of the game. Let me be clear, this is not random art ripped from artists online. Speaking with the devs reveals that they used an AI framework and fed it a diet of exclusively in-house SoaSE art before generating anything. There is no question of art theft here, nor of a lack of originality. The art was always going to be derivative on the second game, but in this way at least there's some certainty that the art identity has remained purely Sins.So, what is there left to say about the game?Well, it keeps the spirit of the previous game, loses a few of the more awkward and inhibiting aspects, and adds in a whole lot of new ones; then it also makes the stuff it kept better. It's Sins1 but better. This is basically how HW3 was hoping to be compared to HW2, only Sins2 succeeded.

It is a direct upgrade to Sins 1, and this is probably the first time I've ever seen a sequel to a classic game that actually makes it hard to play the original because of how much better it is.

_childDocuments_.review: Mechanically and Graphically, this game is amazing. I enjoyed the improvements to colony and fleet management, as well as the fleshed out minor faction and diplomacy interactions were a nice change. But quite frankly, the prolific use of AI art, from the leader portraits, backgrounds of all the UI, every research tree icon, ship ability icon, and planet art. Once I noticed it with the human portraits I realized it was everywhere, genuinely flew under the radar which is kinda crazy. I would rather have paid the full $60 than see this kind of low-quality AI slop.

_childDocuments_.review: With the recent releases in the strategy genre being utter flops *cough* HW3 *cough* it’s genuinely gratifying there’s a great game now released. SINs 2 imo is everything that a SINs long term fan could have dreamed of. I love the graphics updates, the deepening of the combat models with positional turrets, projectiles being physical objects and missiles being finally counter-able. There’s also a ton of QoL things throughout the gameplay and the interface is much improved.The only complaints I have about the game are very minor, things like how certain sounds are WAY too loud, namely missile explosions, SINs 1 deffo had that issue as well. The music is also a bit… bland? Compared to SINs 1. Also where are the steam achievements?? Hopefully they can be added later down the line.

_childDocuments_.review: We're so back. I was worried, because early access looked rough, and IGN was strangely harsh on it, reviewing the early access as if it were a full release. But now that we're at full release, I'm so relieved to see how much polish and attention that has gone into the game.It's not without its faults. There are unfinished UI bits were things are just weirdly obtuse or blank. No more market graph either, which makes the market feel very non participatory.But the rest is great, and I'm looking forward to figuring out more of its new systems.

_childDocuments_.review: I liked Sins of the Solar Empire 1 a lot. I am a big fan of sci-fi games, loved Homeworld, Starcraft, Deus Ex, Cyberpunk etc, you get the idea from these titles.When they announced the "sequel" I was super excited. Disappointed by the Epic exclusive, but still looking forward to play it.It turns out that aside from the graphics, this is not a huge development on the first one, but I am happy with that because I can find myself starting a game and then three hours have passed without me noticing it.I like this game for what it is, RTS in space with spaceships destroying each other in a beautiful spectacle, from seeker vessels to titans you name it. There are no game breaking bugs, far from it, in fact it is being finely tuned as we speak with feedback from the fan base.The developers are actively working on fixing bugs and adding new features so there's something you don't see much these days.If you think you could enjoy space battles then this is for you, buy it.

I especially love being able to zoom in on all ship battles, the intuitive actions of the AI. This game is nearly perfect. Buy it, you don't need to wait until it's on sale. Do wish there were achievements though, and an American faction would've made my little heart sing.

_childDocuments_.review: Its like Eve Online but about 12 GBs and somehow runs itself like a chrome tab... Idk this engine is something else. 10/10 would be 6hrs in with an AI companion set to deity. And we still have not even won the game. Against neutral npcs and two singular normal difficulty AI. The endgame defense curve is real in this game. Which I believe is a positive. Also pro-tip. Have your AI buddy take planets for you. Then simple wait 15min~ to diplomatically ask for any random planet. That they control, exclusively, and ask for nothing else. _childDocuments_.review: Great successor to the original Sins. IT's basically the same thing, but better. If you liked that, you'll like this. If you didn't like that, you probably won't like this. If you generally like strategy, you should give it a shot. I like it because they manage to balance depth, action, and thoughtfulness really well, resulting a in game that rewards caution, but punishes timidness.My only real complaint is that I would have liked a campaign. I enjoy those. I understand one is coming in the enhanced version of the game, but that's quite a premium to get what seems like it should a standard feature.
_childDocuments_.name: Sins of a Solar Empire II

_childDocuments_.review: Sins of a Solar Empire was always one of my favorite real time strategy games, combining my love of the RTS genre, 4X genre, and space games (not everything I love about space games, but nothing can be perfect). This sequel is everything I loved about the original, with massive QOL improvements that sixteen years of insight can and should lead to. I have not finished my first play through of the game as of writing this review, but I can say with confidence that if you enjoyed the first game, you will enjoy this one. If you never played the original, but you like real time strategy or 4x games and don't mind games running in real time, there's a good chance you would enjoy this.

_childDocuments_.review: Having over 3000 hours in original Sins (over 1500 here on Steam) and less than an hour on this new Sins II... why? FYI: I'm also  programmer. You would think Sins II would get high marks from me but no and this game was most anticipated. I'm even disappointed to have requested a refund.What is amazing about this game:[1] Graphics and shaders are well done[2] The various races are familiar and have become even more twisted which is awesome[3] Tactically there are countless variations and permutations that rivals any previous Sins (impressive)[4] More advanced diplomacy and diverse economic sub-systems[5] Did not get far enough in to a game cycle to provide more (sorry).Game stopper for me:[1] non aesthetic  ship and building mesh outlines (yes all lines can be turned off - but why so course to begin with?)[2] Outlines around planets and systems not proportional and lines are way too thick (not what one should be focused on in game play - in my opinion)[3A] menus seem slapped together without much coherence and some menus contain partial content with tabs to single or empty menus (menu should not open if "content unavailable"[3B] why use drop down menu format types... should use panel or tiled menu so one can easily flip or TAB thru [3C] menu contrasting ratio is out to lunch (out of perspective) - I personally do not see this style easy to "get used to"I love Sins, but, I have to say the layout here seems to be rushed and too over simplified - in my opinion.  This game has so much potential though, I look forward to a future version when it feels more like the realistic game play I've come to expect.

_childDocuments_.review: While I can recognize many people may enjoy this game, and might like how hands off the colony management is, I honestly could not get into it. I found the game almost clunky in a way, and the UI was horribly unhelpful. Sometimes UI buttons were for upgrading (clicking once) or building stations (clicking and then selecting a location in your gravity well), with no discernible difference. It felt like they were trying to keep things simple, but ultimately made it more complicated as the UI lacked direction and clarity. There was very little customization available, and everything felt very copy paste or standardized.This is also coming from someone who has played many hours of Stellaris and other strategy games like Sins of a Solar Empire 1, Galactic Civilizations, Civ, the lot.Ultimately it just felt off to me and I just didn't enjoy myself.

_childDocuments_.review: Out of all the games that have dropped the ball on their successors, Sins Of A Solar Empire II have not. The game has more depth than the first trilogy without over loading you as you learn the game. There are so many small quality of life changes that feel good. There are also some lore changes that affect the game. The Vasari "Loyalists" ships are summoned rather than built to fit within their nomad culture, they also don't start with a planet and instead start with a small fleet and coloniser capital ship to take the home-world.
_childDocuments_.name: Sins of a Solar Empire II

_childDocuments_.review: The best RTS game I've played. When you first start off, it seems like it's going to be really complicated. But if you play the first couple tutorials and then jump in, it's really easy to get the hang of. The Fleet battles are extremely satisfying to watch, especially late game (3-5 hours in) when you just have masses of capital ships and titans brawling it out. highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Sins of a Solar Empire II

_childDocuments_.review: As a star trek fan this game is amazing. As a casual fan of rts and 4X games this game is great. It removes a lot of micro managing aspects which really lets you focus on the macro play of war and expanding. You still need to build up planets but that's it, not too much to micro in that front. As a nerd who loves space, this game is stunning visually. I highly recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Sins of a Solar Empire II

_childDocuments_.review: This game has brought me back to playing the first Sins of a Solar Empire. However, the new features are AMAZING. It is incredible how technological advances reflect so much of the gameplay. Now, fleets can have a vast and immersive amount of ships that can blob on any star or planet. Shootout to the rework on the missiles and guns as well! Every bit of the game feels like the original, only better. I do have one thing to say: The advents have much less work than the other factions. TEC and Vasari have different starbases when selecting their origin, but the advents are just the same. I want more content for these factions. Also, it would be interesting to see some new races or even just ships, as the current content is almost the same as the original entry.Overall, it is a hell of a good game! It is an impressive Sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is excellent.  8/10.  The Fleet battles are incredible to set up and play out.  Ill purposely delay a game just to get max 2k vs 2k supply fleets going at it,  A great improvement on the first without losing the feel.I have one significant issue.  The Diplomacy seems completely random and arbitrary.   For example.  I am about to wipe out an enemy at their Home World.  So, I offer them 50,000 credits, 25000 Metal and Crystal for a 30 minute ceasefire and they decline.  They sure know how to negotiate in their best interest...10 Player game.  I have an AI ally.  There are two other AI who allied. so its a 2 v 2.  We are barely holding on.  Suddenly, my ally drops the alliance and attacks me.  5 minutes later he gets wiped out.  I soon follow.  Knowing the AI behaves like this, I started preferring to play team AI games so that Diplomacy is preset.   AI should be much more nuanced and complex in their choices and what is best for their alliance.  If you can afford it, you should be able to bribe opposing factions.As for minor issues there are quite a few buggy things, but I am confident they will be fixed.  Finally, not a fan of the advent voice over.  Sometimes sounds screechy sometimes off tone for the ethereal feel you are supposed to get with the Advent.  That said TEC with old guy who smokes too much and the V are awesome.TLDR.  Fantastic.  Minor annoyances.

name: The Quarry
detailed_description: The Quarry - Deluxe Edition Enjoy some extra teen horror flair with The Quarry - Deluxe Edition! This Edition includes: The Quarry Full Game Deluxe Bonus Content Pack: ‘80s-themed character outfits (available post-launch, see below), instant access to the Death Rewind system, Gorefest Movie Mode option, and Horror History Visual Filter Pack Note: The ‘80s-themed character outfits will be automatically delivered in-game on or by 7/8/2022 ‘80s THROWBACK CHARACTER OUTFITS Horror History Visual Filter Pack Tailor the aesthetic of The Quarry to your liking by choosing from three cinematic visual filters, each replicating a different era and style of iconic horror filmmaking! Choose from an 8mm-style film grain (Indie Horror), a retro VHS aesthetic ('80s Horror), or the classic black-and-white cinematic filter (Classic Horror). The Quarry - Official Trial Version Experience the thrilling Prologue chapter of The Quarry in this free trial! Trial Version players can also be invited to play online multiplayer by friends who own the full version of The Quarry on Steam via Wolf Pack Mode, and vote on key decisions to create a story shaped by the whole group. Plus, story progress will carry over if you choose to get in on the fun and purchase the full game using the same Steam account! And remember – what doesn’t kill you will make you stronger. About the Game As the sun sets on the last day of summer camp, the teenage counselors of Hackett’s Quarry throw a party to celebrate. No kids. No adults. No rules. Things quickly take a turn for the worse. Hunted by blood-drenched locals and something far more sinister, the teens' party plans unravel into an unpredictable night of horror. Friendly banter and flirtations give way to life-or-death decisions, as relationships build or break under the strain of unimaginable choices. Play as each of the nine camp counselors in a thrilling cinematic tale, where every decision shapes your unique story from a tangled web of possibilities. Any character can be the star of the show—or die before daylight comes. How will your story unfold? YOUR STORY, THEIR FATE Will you dare to check what's behind that trap door? Will you investigate the screams echoing from within the forest? Will you save your friends or desperately run for your life? Every choice, big or small, shapes your story and determines who lives to tell the tale. A STUNNING CINEMATIC EXPERIENCE Cutting edge facial capture and filmic lighting techniques, combined with incredible performances from an iconic ensemble cast of Hollywood talent, bring the horrors of Hackett’s Quarry to life in a pulse-pounding, cinematic thrill ride. ENJOY THE FRIGHT WITH FRIENDS Place your faith in up to 7 friends in online play*, where invited players watch along and vote on key decisions, creating a story shaped by the whole group! Or, play together in a party horror couch co-op experience where each player picks a counselor and controls their actions. CUSTOMIZE YOUR EXPERIENCE Adjustable difficulty for all gameplay elements let players of any skill level enjoy the horror. And if you prefer to watch rather than play, Movie Mode lets you enjoy The Quarry as a binge-worthy cinematic thriller. Select how you want the story to unfold, kick back, and munch on some popcorn in between all the screams! STARRING: David Arquette as Chris Ariel Winter as Abigail Brenda Song as Kaitlyn Evan Evagora as Nick Halston Sage as Emma Justice Smith as Ryan Miles Robbins as Dylan Siobhan Williams as Laura Skyler Gisondo as Max Zach Tinker as Jacob Ethan Suplee as Bobby Grace Zabriskie as Eliza Lance Henriksen as Jedediah Lin Shaye as Constance Ted Raimi as Travis *Online multiplayer functionality will be available post-launch on or by July 8, 2022.

_childDocuments_.review: Non Spoiler Review: Fun game with great suspense. Extremely underwhelming ending with characters whose quality of writing is consistently downhill. Some lower quality rigging and animation takes you out of the immersion and is borderline creepy at times. Borrow it from a friend, not worth 80 bucks. *Spoilers Now* The beginning of the game is a tad cringy which will always happen when you have adults write young people and the temporary nature of youth language/memes. Kaitlyn is written really poorly and is just a vehicle for sarcasm the writers refused to trim down. Jacob is not redeemable, he's not awful but simply boring and aggressive. Emma seems... crazy? The way they rigged her mouth like it's so swollen she can't smile properly always made me shudder and if she evades death with a werewolf she hardly mentions it and expresses no fear or character growth. Ryan has a chance of being really interesting but even in extreme situations doesn't display anguish. Ryan gets over his issue with killing Chris Hackett pretty fast and when he does, he just says "I guess that's Chris Hackett" like bro wasn't Chris your uncle figure for years?? Laura is the only interesting character. Overall character rigging is pretty off, Abigail's hair constantly clips into her face, women walk with their arms wide out like they are tight-rope walking and Jacob's bare traps stretch in uncanny ways.Despite this, the beginning is still overall entertaining and made me really excited to keep playing. So many character arcs were set up, motivations and relationships, unfortunately, they result in nothing. Characters undergo amnesia about their fellow counsellors. There could have been an epic reunite, but no matter what ending you get, you will be underwhelmed. On my first playthrough, I easily kept every person alive, and the ending didn't honour that accomplishment. The ending of the game neglects any character's personality and prioritizes QT events. The UX for the quick-time events is also extremely confusing until you've failed a few times, luckily that doesn't actually kill you most of the time, it's very easy gameplay-wise. I would recommend the game just for the thrill and fun at the beginning but the ending will leave you let down.

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't expecting the game format. Just looked interesting from the Steam promo page and a dev playthrough of the prologue prior to release. Decided to buy it and I am  glad I did!It has the familiar feel of a classic cheesy horror movie (the impulse to shout at the screen as you wait for the character to make a cliche bad decision around each corner) but instead  get to be in the driver's seat to make the decisions. In many cases, saving them from peril, but in some situations seeing that you can't know what would have been needed without a seemingly innocuous choice earlier on in the gameplay. Plus, for better or worse, there are  to your choices. So, The Quarry actually delivers on the promises made so that, unlike the Mass Effect series, you can  the destiny of the characters rather than all roads converging to the same end no matter what color road you took. Add to that the on point score, hyper-realistic face work and near-perfect realism of character movement drawing you in to the story, and I have to say without reservation I am supremely impressed. I've only played through once, but I can say that dozens more playthroughs are on deck. Plus with co-op and movie modes as as yet unexplored, I expect this will also be a game that I'll be able to easily share with others and I fully intend to do so. Bravo and brava to everyone involved in the development of this game, and thank you for your work. It paid off, and I hope to see more in this theme and this style of gameplay, even if it's just a sequel to find out more about the world of North Kill, but... a different setting and set of characters would be a step to set things up for one hell of a series.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely amazing. Just as good and as much fun as Until Dawn, but it's not without flaws. Firstly, the main issue is the lack of online co-op at launch, and the fact that the online co-op is only going to be a movie mode essentially. It's not going to be like the Dark Picture online co-op mode where everyone can control their own characters and make their own choices, no, in this, the host player controls everything and up 7 other people can join and merely vote on choices and actions, that's all. If you were wanting this game for the online co-op then pass, it's not going to be what you want. However, if you like these kinds of games for their branching story and replayability then this is definitely worth playing. So many characters to love or hate, so many on the spot choices you have to make and live with, so many twists and turns, it's absolutely engrossing when playing solo. Graphics are incredible, on par, if not slightly better than Until Dawn, with the exception of the water. For some reason, the water in this game is hot garbage on all settings and is really jarring when you're immersed in everything. Motion blur is also a bummer since you can't turn it off for some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ reason. I had no crashes, bugs, glitches, etc, and I'm definitely going to be doing more runs of this to uncover more of the story. I will say I bought this for $35 which felt like a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ steal after my first play so look around for cheaper options or wait for a sale if you're on the fence.

_childDocuments_.review: The Quarry started off pretty strong, maybe a little cringe, but the writing and the actors were pretty good. They do a decent job of fleshing out the characters, for a bit. Somewhere around chapter 5 or 6 they throw it out the window and you no longer care about most of the characters.They setup some characters to make you think they will be a helpful or useful character. For example, Ryan; the first time we meet him, he talks about a podcast about the Hag of Hackett's Quarry. They make you think this is gonna be a character that will have knowledge of the spooky shenanigans and will want to believe what he is seeing. Yet every chance they give him, he acts like the 'monsters' are just bears or something and nothing crazy is happening. He also starts off as a nice-ish person that you want to root for, but somehow just acts like a ♥♥♥♥ to the other characters. The same goes for Katelyn(sp?). She's shown as being hunting/forest smart and just a smart character but refuses to do anything at points that would make great use of her skill and has to stay back with other characters to 'help' them and makes another character with no gun experience go off with the gun to check out who attacked them.All the romances are pointless and in hindsight were just there to fill time.That could all be looked past except for the fact the gameplay and the QTEs (if you can call them that) were absolute garbage. The QTEs were 1 of 4 things. They show you a circle a full 2 seconds before a prompt so you're 100% ready, and then you match the single thumb-stick direction and thats it. Or you just smash the 'A' button. Or you hold the 'A' button for a few seconds. Or you press the right trigger to shoot something. All of these give you tons of time to do them, a couple times we had the controller set down and had time to pick it up and still succeed. The entire play through we failed 1 QTE, and that's because I touched the thumb-stick before it showed the prompt.All the action was crammed into the last couple chapters where it felt like the devs forgot they were making a horror game and had to rush everything. The ending was absolutely trash and abrupt, and was so stupid we honestly thought it was going to be a "gotcha!" moment and then throw 2 more chapters at us to make us figure out the real ending. But nope, we stumble upon the BBEG and 2 seconds later its over. You don't confront the Hag, you don't confront the family, you don't even have all the characters meet back up at the end to tie it all together. It just ♥♥♥♥♥ the bed and ends. I could give the story and loose ends a pass if the game were difficult. If the QTEs were hard and I messed up I could see why I should miss info or story lines and get characters killed, but I didn't. I found mostly every collectible/clue/tarot card/whatever and really expected more at the end. If you're really interested, skip buying the game, watch someone play though it and you will have the exact same experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid 9 hours for a first run. There were a variety of scenes to play through and a lot of the character interactions had me laughing, the cast did a great job. _childDocuments_.review: This game is very dreadful to play and only part of it is the story. The other part is the constant freezing and lag. It was fine near the start but after chapter 2 it became a huge issue. It is very frustrating to play when the game freezes every single scene. The screen will go black for long periods of time during scene transitions, the audio is way faster than the visuals on screen, some characters will repeat the same lines twice in a row, and sometimes there will be no audio at all, especially during the scenes with the old lady. The story itself is defiantly a huge step down from Until Dawn. The game scary factor is almost non existent. Some of the characters, along with the acting, is incredibly cringe at some points and makes me care less about them during my play. Even later on some actions (ones not controlled by the player) just become strange, confusing, and even laughable at points. Minus the dialogue sections, the gameplay feels like it happens less often. You can go through entire scene and character section with little to no gameplay. Yes I understand that's how this game is and how it was made, but I feel I can't even understand the characters more or enjoy them when their scenes end in 2 minutes. Until Dawn felt way more vibrant and defiantly had more gameplay than this.The few good things I will say is the atmosphere feels alive and cool. Some of the mechanics, such as the hold breath, makes those moments feel super tense. Besides that, this game is really lacking and horribly buggy. If you really want to play I would recommend waiting till the freezing and lag is fixed and till the game goes on sale. The game is not worth $60, and I regret paying that much.

_childDocuments_.review: I left a review for this game after my first playthrough, but now I've played it four more times and have a few more things to say, so I'm rewriting this.First of all, this game is fantastic. It does a spectacular job of recreating the stereotypes and cliches of a classic horror film while also cleverly updating them to create a modern story. Each of the characters are also very well-written. Most of them felt very one-dimensional at first, but over the course of the game I learned that many of them actually have quite a bit of depth. The ways that the characters were developed were very smart in the context of the game. For instance, one character in particular seemed to echo a lot of stereotypes at first, but over the course of the game it was revealed that they used those stereotypes as a facade to hide their insecurities.The plot is pretty great too, with good pacing and never a dull moment. There are an insane amount of different dialogue options to see depending on the choices you make. I've played this game five times and still haven't seen a lot of them. Also, I know that a lot of people were disappointed by the ending (or lack thereof), but it honestly didn't bother me much.Overall, I love this game. The characters are compelling and the story is almost perfect, aside from a few conveniences. I can absolutely recommend this to everyone.

Who do i need to kiss? Seriously. I love you.The ending itself can feel very abrupt, but I've come to expect that with Supermassive Games, it's basically their thing, wrap up a massive story with a few lines of dialogue (or in this case, a paragraph).The podcast was a nice touch, especially with the evidence collection, that made the abrupt ending feel less of an issue.

_childDocuments_.review: Ending is pretty anticlimactic, but everything leading up to it is pretty entertaining. _childDocuments_.review: Bought it 80% off and even so I feel this is not worth it for a game released in 2022. The full price is obviously an absurd for what is in the package. Let's see.- Gameplay is very lame and basic in all aspects.- QTE's are not fun nor challenging and most of the time don't even make any sense, like many of the "hold your breath" ones.- Every time you are in control of a character you have to cover all the area in that specific scene walking around to find clues/cards/trigger an action/make the character say something relevant to the progress of the story even if there is nothing in that specific spot calling your attention to go there, sometimes no objects, no posters on walls, nothing, you just have to step there and a light saber will protude from the ground as you approach so you know there is something to trigger there. Lame. Not to mention those tarot cards that many times are in locations you can't reach and even so you collect them anyway. The whole mechanics and points of interest feel just thrown together after the scenes were made and not made as part of the same level design.- Graphics are ok in regards of textures and lights, BUT characters models, movement, facial expressions are flawed for the most part, again for a VERY expensive game released in 2022. Lip syncing feels like an early 2000s game most of the time, though the voice acting is very good. Characters movement are VERY rudimentary, robotic, e at many times all wrong and roughly worked on. Disappointing for an expensive recently released game.- The story is uninteresting most of the time, the "horror" in this is very weak, and almost all the characters are boring, annoying, and not likeable at all. The jokes and sarcasm are unintelligent and not even close to make you smile. It's all very irritating actually. I think maybe for 13 year-olds or people who think Twilight is horror the writing in this might be relevant, but if your are an adult and a serious horror fan this is gonna be a big waste of time. Childish and annoying. Not to mention the many scenes that don't make any sense, e.g. among many others the one where a girl is sitting on the driver's seat of a car, doors closed, and the 3 characters outside the car can't see her for whatever reason and she can't also see who is outside the vehicle. There is a whole suspense in this scene for something dumb that is more of a design/writing flaw than anything else. The last chapter is as weak as any other and doesn't look like the end of a 10hs story. Too expensive to just let this kind of s**t go with it.I'm just glad I finished this, so I can uninstall and never play it again.Also, if you ended up here looking for Friday 13th vibes, like me, this has absolutely nothing to do with any 80's slasher as they tried marketing this.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a prologue and 10 chapters. The prologue and first nine chapters are fantastic. Interesting character dynamics, an intriguing mystery, a terrifying monster, real and impactful choices, and more.Then you get to chapter ten, and it just... Ends. There are so many things that get set up in previous chapters that you get absolutely no closure on, especially if you do a playthrough where everyone lives. Will Laura and Max reunite? Will Ryan get with either of the people who are into him? Will Jacob and Emma reunite? What exactly is the fortune teller going to do? How does the Hackett family deal with so many of their own being killed? What will the cops think of all this? The game answers all of these questions with "I dunno"You shoot the big bad (Or die to him), get a quick montage that tells you who lived and died, and the game just ends.Oh, there's also an annoying 30 minute podcast after the credits roll talking loosely about the events that happened. They don't talk about the characters though, just that some people got arrested. Or they talk about the massacre, if you kill every character.Again, everything up to the ending was fantastic. But I just can't feel good recommending a game with such a cheap, hollow ending.

_childDocuments_.review: The game looks good and the story is okay. I have few problems with the game. First of all the game is poorly made for coop, especially 2 people coop. Basically the other people in ''wolf pack'' don't get achievements. They can't control character movements nor menus (except settings). They can vote on how to people react or what stuff they do. And the game also counts if majority passes QTE's. The real problem is when there are 2 people. The invited player has no power. In choices, if owner chose something, it goes. But it does end there. If second player fails QTE, but owner succeeds, then it passes. BUT, if the invited player succeeds and the owner fails, then it fails. So basically, second player has 0 input on the outcome. My second problem with the game is the choices are sometimes fake. For example, you choose to save someone. The character runs to save, then gets scared and runs off, abandoning the other character. Also, the characters are incredibly dumb. Like there are basically 4 characters in the game with a somewhat of a brain. Others are just dumb. For example (doesn't exactly happen in a game, but gives the point): You find yourself in a minefield. You are lucky not to step on any, but you are surrounded. What do you do? Of course, without any control, your character just starts backing off without looking where he is stepping and steps on one of them.... like... why??? And for the last, some deaths are very random, like you make 1 mistake and done, i don't speak like major one like shoot something or not. Some deaths are like, you didn't inspect that one thing befor opening this, instant death. Anyway, i cannot recommend this game alone and the coop is complete sh*t.TL:DRGood graphics, okay story, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ coop, idiot characters, some very random deaths.

_childDocuments_.review: The Quarry, like most of Supermassive's horror catalog, is an incredibly enjoyable experience if played with friends.  Much like Until Dawn, the extended length gives the story better pacing in contrast to the Dark Picture's games.  However, I feel that much of this game's potential was squandered on poorly developed characters and a less realized mythos found in other titles from the developer.  The "teen drama", commonly found across many of their games, was far too indulgent in the Quarry and was ultimately detrimental to the experience as a whole.  Some characters felt entirely underutilized; which stands in contrast to Until Dawn which had a similar sized cast.  Despite the negative points I've mentioned above, Supermassive Games makes a couch co-op sub-genre of games that is not replicated anywhere else.  Even their most middling titles have enraptured my group of friends to leave us anticipating the next in the series.  If, like me, you love watching horror movies with friends and are a sucker for "choose your own adventure" games, don't skip out on this title.  Even though rankings rarely mean anything; I'll post mine below:1: Until Dawn2: House of Ashes3: Little Hope4: The Quarry5: Devil in Me6: Man of Medan

_childDocuments_.review: In Until Dawn, your character has a “walk faster” button which smoothly switches to a new animation where the character takes longer and more purposeful strides.   In The Quarry, the same button simply speeds up the walking animation, making your character look like they’re in a 1920’s silent comedy.   And this rather sums up The Quarry as a mere shadow of Until Dawn.  It feels rushed, underfunded, and without the attention to detail that made Until Dawn a standout horror title.Facial animations are largely abysmal, particularly the mouths.   It’s as if they had to go back and re-record a load of dialogue after doing the original facial capture, and attempted to fix the animation to match.  I say this because sometimes it’s ok, almost Until Dawn quality; other times it looks like an acid trip.   It mostly affects Emma, so I wonder if she had the most re-recorded dialogue.The water in the lake… look like black oil; the graphics here are a particular low-point, particularly when the characters start splashing each other.The “werewolves” are clearly wendigoes, the decision to make them werewolves coming very late in production (this game started off production as a sequel to Until Dawn).  They don’t look in the least bit dog-like… you know, like wolves?And the decision to allow a completely free 3rd person camera in many scenes was, I believe a mistake.   A horror movie is scariest when the director has control over what you can and can’t see.   Being able to move the camera in that way destroys the “movie look” and destroys any sense of tension.It’s a real shame because I had far less of a problem with the characters and narrative than most reviewers.  I mean, the characters are all unlikeable and the writing/dialogue is poor, but not so much it would have ruined the game if the technical stuff was up to scratch.  For me, this game’s technical failures completely break the immersion, to the extent it ranks bottom of all the Dark Pictures games.EDIT:  And it’s one of the rare games I couldn’t get to run on Steam Deck at all… I just got a pop-up error message, despite following many different solutions from ProtonDB.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly was very impressed with this one. Jump scares were nice and provided nice experience.But why the Downvote ? 1. Despite atmosphere being amazing, at core it is still a game which we need to play. And this is where this game collapses extremely. It's 2022 and we are seeing a linear world with "fixed camera angles". Yes, you read it correct - "fixed camera angles". This is so annoying and makes exploration and navigation such a pain in the ass. It feels as if devs deliberately did this so as to make clues and collectibles harder to see.2. The facial detection was so poor. Girl smiling in a tensed situation and keeping a straight face after seeing her friend die in front of her eyes. Characters looking at weird angles in cutscenes. For eg - The opening scene where 2 friends are driving in middle of a forest, they seem to be looking at roof of the car while talking to each other.3. After every conversation or any crucial event, the characters mindlessly keep staring at same place even in a cutscene for a few seconds. Script looked so weak and dumb. Girl clearly sees a dead body in bunker and calls her friend to check it out, but her friend just sitting in a far corner for no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ reason.I had so much expectations from this game but now it's going out of my wishlist. _childDocuments_.review: Initially I couldn't play the game because the cut scenes and the audio were lagging. After i went through and upgraded my memory and graphics i was able to finally get the game into a playable form. It was still crazy laggy, but it was bearable because i had waited so long to play the game.Overall the game is nice. The environment was cool, but it was a little hard to maneuver around due to the suggested brightness levels. I played with a D-Pad and I found it very difficult to operate the shooting functions because I couldn't get it to stay on one point. I tried the mouse, but it wasn't much better. There's not much game play. I spent a lot of time putting down the controller and just waiting for a QTE or just watching the ridiculously long cut scenes. When there is payable time you're wandering around looking for cards that only show up if you walk in the right direction, or you're looking for the little lights for findables. There's points in the game where the 3rd person perspective got laterally in the way and it made it incredibly difficult to maneuver around and using stairs.I'm disappointed with this game. I had refrained from watching play through of it since it came out, because i wanted to play it fresh. Honestly it seems more like an interactive show on Netflix than a video game. The story was cool, but by the end all the characters were like "Oh My Gosh!! All the pieces are coming together!!" it was pretty cheesy and the ending seemed like the writers were just like "Ehh, lets stop."

_childDocuments_.review: Good: the game encompasses all the good things about teen horror flicks, and it's a genius move to cast Ted Raimi as the creepy copBad: it's a choices-matter branching game but the choices do not necessarily make any sense (e.g. take/don't take a teddy bear with you -> someone else dies/doesn't die hours later, but only in certain circumstances, and in all other cases the teddy bear choice is irrelevant)Also it's going to force you to complete each run uninterrupted from start to end, and there is , meaning if you want to experiment or get the achievements (which have mutually exclusive goals and thus require multiple playthroughs), you are going to spend  of your life - time you will  - watching the same cutscenes again and again. Again and again. Again and again. So you can change one little thing, .That's why this game is getting a negative review: no NG+ skipping cutscenes you've seen. This is a standard feature on most choose-your-own-adventure games, just not this series, and it's all the worse because of it.

_childDocuments_.review: This genuinely hurts to put a negative review for this game, as a huge fan of Supermassive Games, however this game is just downright awful.I was so hyped for this game but unfortunately it just had to be a complete mess. The story is predictable and clearly not optimized for character deaths. And more on character deaths, most of my deaths happened in the final chapter because of decisions made in the first one... and normally this wouldn't piss me off but the fact that literally 3 of my characters died SIMULTANEOUSLY because I didn't pick up a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ teddy bear in the first chapter just is inexcusable and terrible game design. _childDocuments_.review: I really, really, really liked The Quarry up until the end of the game where unfortunately enough - the conclusion to the story is ridiculously unsatisfying and lazy. Not going to spoil anything, obviously but... Damn, what a way to ruin a great game.There's a lot of interesting characters here, each of them feeling fleshed out and likeable, very good facial animations and some of the best, if not THE best dialogues I've seen to date in a game like this. Superb job in that department!The music wasn't very memorable but neither was it bad, it sort of was just there, you know? Perhaps that's a good thing, they say "When you do things right, people won't be sure you've done anything at all". Though I do remember really liking two particular tracks.Graphically, the game looks good for the most part. There's some DOF issues going on at the start when you play during the day, but as soon as it gets dark(er) the game starts to look the way it should. Nothing too crazy in this department, looks good - nothing crazy. The faces do be looking good though.Playing through this felt great for the most part, I felt like my decisions had influence and it was fun comparing my own outcomes with other people's on YouTube.Sadly, there's a few instances here where the outcome of the situation feels too punishing because you made the wrong decision with no right of knowing that it would just reward you with an insta-death for no reason. No indications, no way to see it coming or a chance to stop it from happening, just *BAM* insta-kill hehe!Those who played it - you know what I'm talking about.Lastly, like I said before - this f*****g ending, man... So unsatisfying, so lazy, uninteresting it actually annoyed me. I have no idea who came up with this idea, but I'd like that person to know they have single-handedly ruined the game. It's like the game tripped over it's own feet right at the finish line and tumbled down the hill for a couple of miles, lost it's shoes on the way down, stood up and immediately stepped in dog sh*t. I will not forgive this.

_childDocuments_.review: The good:- Whilst the writing starts off cringe, it gets better as the game progresses. And to be fair, its meant to be a gamified teen slasher movie, and the writing for those is often pretty cringe too.- Graphics are great. The facial animations are a mixed bag, some characters look really good, some look like a mannequin with skin pulled over it, but overall the game is graphically competent.- Good camera work in cutscenes. Some of the angles and shots in the game are just *chefs kiss* - The soundtrack slaps super hard.The bad:- Emma- Okay no, now serious. Controlling your character sucks ass a lot of the time. Especially in tighter spaces, I couldn’t see ♥♥♥♥ half the time not because it was dark, but because half of my screen was covered by the character. The sudden camera changes don’t help.- Even tho I praised the writing for getting better as the game goes on, there are still some really dumb moments throughout the experience. Characters don’t ask questions an actual person would in that situation, characters dont make decisions that make sense outside of being a crutch to move the plot forward. Also the scene where  - The game also borrows a lot from Until Dawn, especially with the whole - A large amount of the choices are a complete guess. This is both bad and good. Bad because the player is basically just tossing a coin, very few scenes offer options for proper decision making, instead you’re just picking between equally confusing options. At the same time, due to the limited impact of these choices, it only matters in a couple specific scenes. So whilst you are guessing, at least the game doesn’t punish you for your guess all the time (I will expand on this in the next section.)- EmmaThe ugly:To preface this section, it’s mainly stuff that I don’t like but don’t think belongs into the outright bad category for specific reasons- Most decisions don’t matter. I read through a thorough guide after my playthrough through and it was surprising by how many choices just don’t affect anything at all. Even worse, some of them are followed by a popup saying smth like "this character didn’t like that" yet it’s never brought up again. Dialogue choices in general are the biggest culprit here. Aside from that, many choices are just a choice between not having a QTE and having one, or even just between different types/amounts of QTEs. The following scene/s are technically different, but lead to the same exact outcome. Sometimes even messing up a QTE doesn’t change anything going forward. I understand that taking into account every single choice the player can make is unfeasible, but considering how much the game screams at you that choices matter, I was surprised by how many of them don’t make any tangible difference.- This ties to the previous point. Outside of which character lives or dies, there are very few scenarios which change based on your choice. Now obviously a character dying is a big deal, but it’s a shame that you cannot for instance explore different areas, or meet people in different circumstances. Most scenes have a very defined outcome, with only slight changes like an extra line of dialogue. This is the biggest culprit in why so many people call the game a “movie with gameplay”.- To not just ♥♥♥♥ on the devs, I will point out that a couple choices, especially towards the end of the game, can lead to some pretty different scenarios. Whilst I would definitely enjoy more consequences for more options, I have very much enjoyed watching the couple key moments from previous chapters all come together.- This one is more of a pet peeve, but my goblin brain can’t deal with the fact that you can’t collect all clues and all tarot cards in a single playthrough. One of the very few exclusive paths (meaning you can only get one or the other, not just a scene not happening because of a character death) is in chapter 2 and it literally exists only to stop you from getting all collectibles in one run. Outside of the collectibles, the decision is meaningless, you end up in the same exact spot after. And this is the only time in the entire game that it happens. There are no other split paths that would stop you from getting a clue or a tarot card or evidence. The only way to miss them is to literally just miss them. It’s not even like this was necessary to do to make people do multiple playthroughs for achievements. There are other exclusive achievements that require starting the game over at least partially.Conclusion:There is fun to be had with the game, especially if you have some friends over and you can all discuss what decisions to make, who you like, what you think is going on, etc. The characters are (mostly) fun to watch and by the end you want to keep at least some of them alive, and not just to get an achievement. If you're a fan of other Supermassive games, the Telltale games, or just B movie horror in general, this game is for you.However, I personally don’t think it’s worth 60 bucks. The game takes roughly 10-15 hours to beat, and outside of character deaths, replayability is limited in that about 90% of the content will stay the same. I would recommend waiting for the game to go on sale, or getting it through the Humble Bundle monthly subscription collection during October.

_childDocuments_.review: Have you always dreamt of starring in your very own kinda trashy slasher movie? Then this is the game for you! You've probably seen this story done over and over as part of the horror genre--and let's be real, it's fairly predictable. But being able to steer the story, the many decisions you can make in order to save (or not ;) ) the protagonists still makes playing The Quarry absolutely worthwhile, and the characters all are interesting and sometimes surprising in their own way.I really enjoyed the voice acting and actor choice (Lin Shaye has become one of my favourite faces for the horror genre!), as well as gimmicks like adding a filter to the game, selecting a different style of outfits, or choosing the alternate soundtrack. The developers appear to have put a lot of effort into the characters and less into the surroundings, which results in somewhat flat textures for the backgrounds, judging against today's standards, but impressively detailed and realistic faces.I know that this game is getting judged against Until Dawn. Does it hold up story-wise? Probably not, from what I've seen of Until Dawn. But if you love the slasher genre, I absolutely suggest you give The Quarry a chance.

_childDocuments_.review: Thank goodness I bought this on sale, because at full price it would be a rip off. It feels like the dialogue was written by an AI it's so generic and bland. It feels like it was set in 2012 instead of 2022 the dialogue and slang are so dated. The graphics and animation have problems too. The only meaningful change you can make to the graphics is brightness, but the contrast is just awful. It's like they somehow managed to clip the whites and blacks. It's really annoying because it makes it hard to navigate in darker places. Anything in a shadow is invisible, creating a lot of invisible walls in annoying places.The animation looks like the animators were forced to turn in their first  drafts. Mouths extremely desynchronised from mouths at times. People's heads turn a creepy amount, like they don't have vertebrae in their necks. The mouths and faces look weird when people talk. They all look like they've got marbles stuffed in their cheeks. Their  blinks and eye movements are also poorly timed and animated. Instead of relating to how people talk, as if expressing an emotion, it's like the eyes have their own agenda. It creates a really uncanny valley experience. The walk animations also suck and are really stiff. Let's put it this way, it feels like if it had been released for the PS3, you would assume it was a cheap knock off of a better game. In 2024, this is unacceptable, especially for an $80 game.

_childDocuments_.review: Long story short the game was poorly optimized and has several QoL issues that I'd love to see fixed-- No way to skip dialogue or chapters: it's embarrasing the game doesn't have a way to just skip to whatever chapter you want; you need to use a save file with more progress than the chapter you are on which on paper sounds fine, but when it's a nine hour game with no way to skip, it just becomes a slog. A shame because it does have some replay value but not enough to justify sitting through another playthrough.- No way to customize in game: similarly, there's no way to switch cosmetics during a game - once again, you need to start a new game to try using the 80's pack if you preordered it (which was also delayed by over a month for some reason)- Preorder bonuses in general: I've already mentioned the 80's clothing pack being delayed for some reason, but the "movie mode" is laughably bad and had almost no description prior to preordering. You can choose to watch everyone survive, or the goriest deaths - but there's no way to skip or rewind, meaning you sit for over 3 hours with no way to even slightly interact with it apart from stopping.- Multiplayer mode: an awful feature that lets people vote along with you what choices you want to make, but requires people to own the game themselves for some reason. Why would this ever be a feature? You might as well just stream the game on Twitch and let your audience decide with you.- Story: there's much of the story I feel disappointment for but to summarize - choices have little impact since the game is less "choices matter" as it claims and more linear, characters have one (or two if you're lucky) ways to die and are either protected by plot armor until that time comes around, or they all but disappear from the story. Deciding to make the endings for each character a freeze frame with a couple sentences and calling it good just reeks of rushed production. The vast majority of the playable characters are alone by the end of the game and there's no big finale like Until Dawn where the characters reconvene for one last struggle.- Music: "streamer mode" was a joke. All of the music (except for the intro and ending) is copyrighted - the exact thing it claimed not to be. This is super amateur and embarrasing for a AAA studio to do.- Refunding: after waiting over a month for the cosmetics and "multiplayer mode" to be added, Supermassive dropped the ball and left them extremely lackluster. There's no way they can't know that you can only refund a Steam game if less than 2 hours have been played, and made the game at least nine for a single playthrough. It feels scummy to leave out preorder bonuses on the day of launch, but it feels unforgivable to drop the ball so hard towards the ending of the game, knowing it's impossible for players to refund it.TL;DR don't buy the game. I'm disappointed in Supermassive for making such an underbaked flop especially when they have Until Dawn and multiple Dark Pictures games on their resume. To get the good ending you need two monitors, one for the game and one for the IGN articles to guide you. For RPGs that's fine, but this is to be an immersive horror game. Kind of hard to be invested in the story when you're stuck looking at the wiki half the time. I found all 10 evidence and kept all the campers alive, but it didn't matter. Would be a fun 7/10, but for all the reasons above it is a 4/10. I hope their next project will be better.
