_childDocuments_.review: The Quarry is a visually stunning game with movie-like graphics and thrilling horror sequences that will keep you on the edge of your seat. The characters keep things consistently interesting throughout the course of the game with their funny, sad, annoying, and downright mean moments and interactions with one another. One gripe I have for the characters is that there is really no character development for any of the camp counselors. For the most part, they are still pretty much the same characters at the end of the game (provided they survive) as they are at the beginning when they are first introduced. The monsters, or werewolves, if you will, are a bit unique in The Quarry as they do not take on the traditional werewolf appearance like we are accustomed to seeing in movies and tv shows. They still follow the traditional rules of lycanthropy such as only turning once a month during the full moon, their weakness being silver bullets, and being bitten by a werewolf will turn the victim into another werewolf. The werewolves of Hackett's Quarry are intense and downright terrifying in most scenes which I love. The only con about the werewolves for me is their process of transformation. When someone transforms into a werewolf, their skin quite literally explodes off of them and suddenly they are a fully fledged werewolf in a matter of seconds. In my opinion, a more drawn out werewolf transformation where we see a character slip away from human and into werewolf would definitely add to the scariness and horror that the werewolves can instill in players and would provide a good opportunity to show the other characters reactions to seeing their friends become blood thirsty beasts. Other than that though, I thought they were portrayed rather well. One last critique is the numerous bugs and glitches that can interrupt or downright hinder gameplay. In some cutscenes, mainly in the middle of the game for me, the audio will not match with the character's lips and the cutscene will freeze for a moment to catch up (like buffering on a YouTube video). When these can get patched and/or fixed, the game will be that much better.Overall, I really do recommend The Quarry to anyone who loves the choice making and the horror that comes with it. If you have played Until Dawn, you will already have a good idea on how to play The Quarry. If you are new to this particular genre, don't worry! The game has detailed tutorials that you can come back to anytime you need a refresher! What doesn't kill you will make you stronger!

_childDocuments_.review: I love this kind of games. If you've played Until Dawn or The Dark Pictures Anthology series you definitely know what to expect. Playing The Quarry I had a pleasant horror experience, with few exceptions. First of all, the graphics are amazing and the actors are well chosen. Due to the length of the cutscenes it almost felt like I was watching a movie, which I didn't mind at all. The interventions you have as a player from time to time give you the opportunity to change the course of the story according to your own choices. Some choices are insignificant and do not affect the course of the action, and others are crucial and can decide the fate of a character. One good thing is that the game has replay value. After completing the game for the first time, you can either go back to a certain chapter to change something, or you can restart the game from the beginning by making other decisions. In case you want to do this but think you'll get bored (the game doesn't have an option to skip cutscenes), I recommend you also buy the cinematic filters in the DLC for a more refreshing experience.The biggest minus of the game, for me, is the ending. I understood the point of it and the direction it went, but I expected a lot more from it. Other downsides would be the small bugs that I won't go into much detail about since they will probably be fixed in a later patch.That said, I recommend the game to everyone, especially if you're familiar with the genre and want something new. However, I don't recommend buying it at full price.

The first several hours (and the price tag) set us up to anticipate this sort of depth, but it doesn't really deliver, down the road.So, at $60, the game is overpriced, but if you can get it on sale (I got it half-off), it is absolutely a worthy experience for fans of innovative, character-driven storytelling.

_childDocuments_.review: The Quarry is Supermassive's perfect sequel to Until Dawn.  It's a "choose your path" path selection horror title with a great blend of scares and comedy relief.  The plot is both familiar and new and the characters/protagonists are quite likable.  The game has not one, but two different supernatural elements (no hallucinating gas here!) and it's easily one of the top five most beautiful games I've ever seen.  The Quarry is easily more beautiful than 99.9% of the fare out there, in fact, with  stunning lighting, great shadows and excellent facial motion scans/captures.  The game is technically demanding since it produces nigh-photorealistic graphics.  At 4K, ultra, my Radeon VII could only manage a meager 40 fps, consequently, I reduced the resolution to 2K on the second playthrough, where I netted 55 fps.  The game is stable and didn't crash for me at all.  I also did not experience any severe glitches or bugs.  The actor/actress likenesses are absolutely uncanny and each performer produces fantastic voice over work.  The soundtrack is great and the sound effects add to the excellent atmosphere.Good character exchanges are peppered throughout a fairly good story.  Choices are often relevant and impactful.  The game is short, lasting about 8 hours, on average.  Replayability is limited and there is obviously no real online multiplayer to speak of.  I doubt there'll be any DLC for the game.  The game's high cost might put off some players when presented with the prospect of a 20 hour game.  People need to understand that this game is less of a recurring product and more of a special experience.  Sure, I may only net 18-22 hours out of this game but that's kind of the point with a game like this one.  This isn't L4D 2 multiplayer.  This isn't a pachinko machine like Apex.  This isn't pay to win slots like Vindictus.  This is a story, presented in state of the art graphics/sound/cinematography and if you're ok with staring at 7 Days to Die for days and days, that's ok, but they're not the same kind of game.You can't compare a game with buildings that look like card board boxes to something like this that looks like something out of the future.  If you have the disposable income, this game is a worthy pickup.  If not, wait for a sale and pick it up immediately.  The game is totally worth it.Recommended.8.5/10.

The cringe turns into some really bold and strong personalities, although, since it's a horror game first, they still make some dumb decisions which you don't really have any word in. The walking speed is only slow when climbing or going down stairs and the AI sometimes blocks your path or just moves in ridiculous ways.Overall, I liked it a lot. _childDocuments_.review: Will Supermassive ever reach the heights of Until Dawn? I mean, they haven't yet. They've now made 4 games in the same vein, but none can capture the urgency and genuine surprise of that game. I beat this in just under 8 hours, and while it's being clearly held as a bigger game than the Dark Pictures anthology (because it costs $20 more), it has about the same emotional impact of those (not much). I don't know, has a few memorable performances, with Laura and Ted Raimi, but it never builds to a real big climax. It kinda just sputters out until it ends abruptly, giving no closure to the stories established in the previous hours. It's like if a tv season finale cut out the last twenty minutes. I don't know, I miss Until Dawn.

Literally having to open chrome on the first 30 seconds of gameplay is not a good thing. I feel bad for playstation playersWhy is the "prologue" so unintuitive and weird compared to the rest of the game. i guess in the first playable section of the game your decisions should be respected otherwise it just totally destroys the idea this is a game where choices matter but yeah this is what happens in this game which made me not take it seriously most of the time and killed the whole vibeWhy do i need a short filter animation whenever i "take a decision" to tell me that yeah i chose a path. i wouldn't have any problem with it but sometimes it will happen even when the game just only started a new narration string. Is it horror related? no sometimes the game just wants you to catch the phone a character just threw at you (this one is unironically a great tutorial to get the hang of QTEs though fortunately they kept it at the start of the game i just found it kinda stupid to have it 3-4 different times it's genuinely a running gag at this point)Sometimes the characters like Dylan can be fun to play with but let's be real all of them are plain stupid at multiple parts of the story and you don't even have a say in it. lowkey makes it seem like the devs want us to go on a route where we kill all of them which is stupid but fun to try out (i watched a gameplay, cba playing this game again)Why is dramatic irony so poorly used throughout the whole game especially when it slows down the rhythm for nothing which is annoying and the opposite of what players typically wantSome examples of what i said above: Sometimes the characters just don't act like they just got out of 2 months surviving in the wild or whatever Hackett's camp is for which is not related to the story. also most of them act like they never even explored the place to start with.Why does this one female character (laura) always act like a huge ♥♥♥♥♥ to others no matter the dialogue or choices made when you play as her? Just proves how meaningless the dialogues are in the game to be fairCollectibles are mostly completely useless in the game. why? clues are just lore for the player but why can't it be used in the story, that would make it so much more fun and interesting. evidence does nothing but change  which makes no sense at all as it just isn't what the tutorial says, evidence should instead alter different types of endings for sure, that's not even to be debated.The cards can be collected to see stuff but 90% of the time you can't figure out ♥♥♥♥ so just a dumb feature since you get the cards going to random places. this is even worse because the game 90% of the time NEVER rewards exploration whatsoever which is stupid. the moment you figure out clues and evidence don't change ♥♥♥♥ you just stop exploring and it ruins the fun.Why is the dialogue so cringe-inducing just for the "charm" of the game? that's just unbearable, the jokes in this game simply aren't funny a lot of the time.Again why is combat so rare in the game, it's so much better than "interrupts" encounters where you just click a button, and you don't even know what's gonna happen making it a ♥♥♥♥ feature. Gameplay in this game is terrible not because it just is but because it's just so unpredictable, most of the time you'll think you're watching a cutscene and then a QTE plays out, and if you miss it, too bad you'll have to replay the same chapter again and waste half an hour if you wanted to keep this character alive.Why did the ending have to be so frustrating? _childDocuments_.review: If you've played any of Supermassive's games before then you know what to expect in terms of gameplay. A combination of quicktime events (PAY ATTENTION IN CUTSCENES) and controlling different characters around smaller, pretty linear areas.I don't have much to say about the gameplay itself. I will say that the camera can sometimes be atrocious and change angles unexpectedly so that you start walking a different direction. Not super frequent but I did find myself annoyed by it a couple times.The graphics are, for the most part, very good. A few effects don't look quite right, aka WATER effects. Sometimes facial animations look a little off, but overall I think the game looks pretty good and most animations are pretty good.Sound is good for the most part, but the music tracks they play and the timing of them can feel misplaced. My main issue with this game is the characters and the story. Without going heavy into spoilers, A LOT of confusion and miscommunications could be completely avoided if people actually just used their damn voice and talked like normal people. Some people are overly cryptic and by the end I realize that there really was no great reason for this. Just a layer of conflicts that felt unnatural because I would imagine actual people in these situations would talk and use their words to communicate.Many of the characters were completely unlikeable in my opinion. Possibly because they take stupid and cringe to a level you have to see to believe. I can let some stupidity slide, and I really try to ask myself if I was in that persons shoes how clearly would I be thinking? And honestly most of these instances of stupidity I just couldn't understand how any individual could be that stupid. This was probably the most frustrating aspect of the game for me. A game about CHOICES where a lot of the choices that are out of your control are not just dumb, but actually insane. A lot of the dialogue options in the game have, at least in my opinion, pretty clear cut correct choices. I like to have to try to think and weigh my options and many of them consisted of one decent option and one completely moronic option. Not all of them were like this, and I don't expect every choice to be super impactful, but damn the ones that were actually tough choices were an extreme minority. This game would 100% be worth it to my even at full price if it had intelligent characters, and if it respected the intelligence of it's players. Don't railroad me into terrible decisions, people being silent or cryptic for literally no reason, and put the characters into the story as intelligent people who just can't catch a break and need to navigate out of bad situations. Not complete morons who make me wonder how they even made it this far in life with their abysmal social skills and problem solving skills. When you play the game you'll surely realize what I'm talking about.I get it, it's a game. It doesn't need to be hyper-realistic, or have every choice be perfectly crafted. But I would definitely like to think that at least MOST of the decisions should be thoughtful, and that the characters wouldn't constantly make awful decisions completely out of my control to keep the story flowing. Just ends up frustrating when you try to make good decisions and then they make a horrible one right after that's out of your control.I would still likely recommend this game, even as it is, if it were $30-40. At $60 I have to recommend waiting for a sale. So I would have recommended this game if not for the high price. Expect around 7-8.5 hrs for a playthrough. This assumes you look around a little bit, take a minute to think sometimes, and aren't running to exactly where you need to go as soon as you're able to.

_childDocuments_.review: Hacketts Quarry has a generic Werewolf problem, a long time ago a bunch of backwards rednecks burned down a freakshow because of their hatred of circus folks; which let their pet werewolf free and it bit a few people in the process. So for the last six years they have been hunting this thing and never found it until now when it suddenly does show up for no discernible reason. Because if you kill the original vamp- I mean werewolf, it magically cures everybody further down the line. Rather than just kill the infected and prevent this whole problem, they act aggressive and pretend the problem is somehow hard to explain or complicated. This is a an 11 hour movie with the illusion of choice, of which the choice is typically "Live" or "Die Instantly" and the game typically won't tell you which is which. While the game pretends there are choices or alternate outcomes, it's 100% linear and always happens the same way; the "choices" relate to choosing whether or not a character survives to the end of the linear, prebuilt story. And even then, the game tends to kill you with cheap tactics like having a combat mode where the gun is purposefuly hard to control. There's a "combat" mechanic where the character will drunkenly sway with the gun, forcing you to aim with the flashlight. The problem is that the things you need to shoot are ALWAYS MOVING and even when you aim directly at them; YOU MISS AND LOSE A CHARACTER. What's funny is that this garbage mechanic just exists for you to get frustrated at and turn off, because the achievements will unlock even if you set everything to easy mode. There's no real replay value here, it's the same thing every time with no real room for change.

_childDocuments_.review: I tried playing it by making coercive choices that in my mind simulate the written characters personalities. Gameplay is more like a beautifully animated motion-capture mini-series of interactive cutscenes, in most cases when you get the option to explore it makes little to no sense in doing so, even if there was something to find, it kind of ruins the pace of the story. I like to consider myself logical and rational, and with that in mind I found the majority of the post decision dialogue and the overall forced outcomes somewhat infuriating (atleast the first half of the story). The choices you make don't seem to change anything unless it's a life or death scenario which you can't really predict as you have no power over the story. And the way some of these characters are written makes them seem so dense as if they don't have any base intelligence or survival instincts at all (again first half, maybe the story is meant to display some character development or perhaps that was my decision making. At this point I'm not even sure anymore). Still, I guess it's supposed to mimic a classic American teen horror flick so good job in that regard. Overall plot was aight'. If you watch movies you can clearly see the characters are portrayed off and played by real life actors/actresses. The graphics and cinematography are astonishing. Sound production did an amazing job. The credits are well done, I think this might be the first time I actually sit through one. The podcast was fun to listen to. Got it from HB, would not recommend at full price as there's practically no gameplay but if you're aware of that and looking to watch a movie of sorts, I'd still say get it at like 50% off. I'm sort of stuck in between as you just have to give praise to the visuals and sound but the gameplay and choice matters aspect is really lacking.Edit: Changed the review to negative as I am a pessimist. 2+(-2)=0, neutral status is a drawback in my book.

_childDocuments_.review: The Quarry is a horror mov... uh sorry game, with an quite entertaining story I have to say, I honestly had some doubts at the beginning that it could be full of ass, and to be clear the story is not great but fortunately not bad at all. As far as movies of this kind are concerned, I know almost all of them: Nightmare On Elm Street, Halloween, Texas Chainsaw Massacre, IT, House Of 1000 Corpses, Monster Man, Scream, Dead Snow, President Evil, Children Of The Corn, Jeepers Creepers, Friday The 13th, Carrie, Urban Legend, Sleepaway Camp, See No Evil, Girls Nite Out, Unhinged, Flashback, Fright Night, Brainscan...I'd have to break it down into percentages, but don't feel like doing the math right now, but in general the mov... uh sorry the game, looks pretty good, there are some parts that don't work though. Most of the characters' facial expressions look good, but some characters' mouths look really weird. Sometimes the game also creates errors in the characters, they have scars, then they don't, then they do, all within a few seconds. You also have to overlook the fact that all the characters seem to be constantly smearing themselves with lubricant, they're all a bit too shiny for me. And there are also a lot of unnecessary sequences, or in other words, they could have shortened it a bit more and had more playable moments, because that's where the real strength of the mov... uh game lies. Unfortunately there were also some very illogical moments, but some of them are so stupid that it was kinda funny again.I don't want to spoil anything, but I have to say at this point that for me the design or representation of the "monsters/creatures" failed almost completely, throughout the whole game I asked myself how this was waved through, they don't look like... and not even looking some kind of cool.At some point the money must have run out or some idiot was too impatient and wanted to release instead of doing a few last things nicely, then maybe it would have been an absolutely great mov... uh sorry again game, because if there are scenes with water splashing, whew it's not a treat for your eyes. Despite all of this, I really enjoyed The Quarry and I will play it again, the quick time events fit in well, soundtrack and sound design is almost flawless and convinced me very much, almost everything was done right so great job there!Diverse dialogue options, different endings, good voive acting. Moreover, when playing on a PC, the Quick Time Events (QTEs) rely on mouse movements, and they tend to be clunky and unresponsive, particularly the "downward" motion, which can lead to frustrating moments. _childDocuments_.review: A great return for Supermassive! So I was a big fan of Until Dawn (don’t take a shot everytime I say the name in this review) back in the day, as I am a huge horror fan, and that game was a cool twist on the genre, as well as point and click games, giving even Telltale a run for their money. After Until Dawn though, Supermassive just made a lot of games that didn’t interest me like Hidden Agenda which felt too gimmicky and the Dark Picture games that I have not played but all I heard was that they were too short and not worth the asking price. But The Quarry seemed like a return to form and a spiritual sequel to Until Dawn. That’s what I expected and that’s what I got. The cast of characters are pretty solid as like in Until Dawn, they come off as very annoying stereotypes of horror movie teenagers, but as you play, you get to know them more and see the depths of their character. Overall, I still like the Until Dawn cast more, but these characters are still pretty good with some notable actors that I recognized playing them. Though David Arquette is barely used in the game which sucked. It makes sense in terms of the story why he isn’t present as much, but you only see him in like 2 chapters (at least in my playthrough) and as a massive Scream fan like myself, I wanted to see more of him. Gameplay wise, this title brings over much of the mechanics from Until Dawn. You're usual QTE prompts and choices. They do provide accessibility options so you can increase the time for QTEs which I appreciated. And thankfully they only really come up during appropriate times and not like you have to do a prompt every time your character does anything physical, like in other games. They also bring back the don’t breathe mechanic when your character hides from an enemy, but instead of using the dual sense controller like Until Dawn, you simply just hold down a button which I liked. Tarot cards are used in place of Totems, as they can give you a hint about a future choice, however you can only see these in between the chapters by speaking to an old woman, who basically acts like the psychologist from Until Dawn. I liked this mechanic overall and your interactions with the old woman. Though I did get really annoyed since she got angry at me for a choice I made in chapter 9, but I didn’t have the context behind that choice until after the chapter, but then when I fixed my mistake in the last chapter so to speak, she was still angry at me for what I did in chapter 9. I’m a terrible person apparently lol The story really is the best part for me though. I was honestly hooked from start to finish and I beat the game in 2 sittings. They keep an interesting mystery going for most of the game until the details are revealed and I thought they did some cool things with the monsters and the lore attached to them. I did try my hardest to have every character survive by the end and I got pretty far too but I slipped and lost 3 characters in the last chapter which sucked. They do have a lives mechanic where if you die you can spend 1 of 3 lives to get a do over, however if you spend the second life you have to go back to chapter 1 and basically replay the entire game, which I’m like what’s the point then?But overall, this game scratched my itch for a new Until Dawn game, and I enjoyed my time with it. Recommended to any horror game fan.

_childDocuments_.review: I never played Until Dawn, (the game was never on PC) but i've seen countless videos on it and know its fame and how good it is. The last couple of years i played the new series by the same devs: The Dark Pictures anthology and i liked it a lot, specially Man of Medan and House of Ashes.  The Quarry is a standalone game, longer than the Dark Pictures games, similar to Until Dawn and has much better dialogue, better motion capture for the faces (it was done in collaboration with digital domain) and also has great actors across all cast. Not saying the Dark Pictures games didn't have good actors on them, but after playing all of them and playing The Quarry now, you can see how a good combo of great actors and good dialogue can make many scenes much more enjoyable.It is also strange to say this, since this is a horror game (and it has scary things on it) but some of the dialogue on it , and the way it is delivered by the cast, its just plain funny (in a good way). That's what it has that it probably makes this last game by Supermassive more close to Until Dawn than any of the Dark Pictures games.The game is not perfect regardless, as much as i liked it more than all the Dark Pictures games, i have to say that one thing i found lacking on The Quarry was the ending. Without telling any spoilers, i would say that it missed having a post ending scene (or scenes) in which you could see your characters after the ending. Since this is a long game and you spend so much time with them, its a little anticlimactic to just have them on a "screenshot" in the end.This of course also has to do with the fact that i end up caring a lot about some of my characters. If i play the game again and make different decisions, and something different happens to them , (they end up in a different place or just plain dead) i will just have to dismiss it as some alternative version of the game that never came to be! Lastly (but not least) this game has some good music on it (at least on licensed mode) The overall ambient music is good, but it has some outstanding themes in certain scenes wich just plays excellent. The gameplay is mostly like The Dark Pictures and plays ok, but in terms of replayability there are some cuestionable decisions, like for example the "Chapter select" feature, which lets you jump to any chapter on the game (After finishing it once) which is great, so you may look for any missing collectibles without playing the whole game again, but then erases all your progress after the jumping point (and your collectibles) so you still have to play the whole game again... also the fact that you are never able to skip a scene or a dialogue (while replaying) is nonsense, since the game will not be shorter because of this (if you already played a scene , there still plenty of alternative variants and dialogues to look out for) meaning: this game has tons of alternative content , dialogues even full scenes that will probably never 'll be seen because it just too much time to replay scenes without being able to skip.Aside from this caveats The Quarry, ends up being the best Supermassive game (so far) on PC and a good spiritual sucesor to Until Dawn.This review is ©2022 Pablo Costa.

Even during the day it's good on the sun but in the shadows it's totally dark and you can see nothing. It was very annoying. I hated some parts, like where you need to free your friend from the cage, but you're given just a quick view on doors number and then you need to choose what doors to open without possibility to look again, and you had no idea that you had to remember numbers! Or in the last fight you have a timer to aim and shoot, but for some reason in the middle of that time it stops like you didn't shoot and character is dead. Wtf? And yeah, you can't reload and replay immediately. There were also several super stupid parts where you had to walk, just walk without any possible actions. _childDocuments_.review: I am now convinced Supermassive Games were a one-hit wonder devs and have no idea what they're doing and are just milking and riding on the success of Until Dawn. Unlike that game, The Quarry has one of the dumbest characters and plot I've ever seen, along with the fact that the gameplay is an absolute waste of time. To make matters worse it seems horror fans are so deprived of good horror games and movies that they just feel forced to enjoy any trash that is released. I won't be as forgiving. 👍 -Nothing👎-Acting is abysmally cringe and nonsensical-The main story wastes your time-Gameplay is practically nonexistentIt's not difficult to make a decent horror movie around fantastical beasts such as werewolves or similar creatures, yet somehow the writers managed to make the dumbest plot on the planet that somehow without any logic involves a ghost? maybe? and not actual werewolves but the skinny hairless version of them. So the gist is, that you play as various dumb teenagers that have absolutely no logic in them whatsoever, which is the norm with horror media, but in this particular case, they are the dumbest I've seen. Anyway, you are at Hackett's Quarry, which is a summer camp for kids that is run by the Hacketts. Yes, you may be thinking now, wait, why is there a summer camp for kids in a horror environment? Well, dear reader, it gets worse, they run the camp for kids knowingly that there are werewolves being hunted in the area, but it's cool because there's no full moon until the plot of the game starts so the kids are safe lmao and luckily the camp ends A DAY before the full moon starts. Anyway, one of the douchebag characters you play as sabotages the car that you and the other main characters were supposed to return home, and now you're stuck there, BUT get this, the summer camp leader also has a car and he just leaves the characters there when he could've literally saved them all. The game is marketed as all choices matter and let me tell you right away, they do not. Almost all choices while they initially seem different will ultimately lead to the same exact path. The characters only die if you're absolutely bad at the game or under absolute BS circumstances which I'll talk in the gameplay part. Every decision the game wants you to make story-wise is absolutely baffling and no way any human being capable of having normal thoughts would do any of those actions. "oh no you got jumped by a humanoid hairless creature, I think it was a bear!!! let's walk alone in the forest!!"Every single character seems to have double personalities, like this skinny-ass dude tells the guy to do something, the guy does it and then HE STILL GETS ANNOYED. Who wrote this? Find a better job. Story rating: 4/10There is no gameplay. You just walk forward, wait for a cutscene, then walk forward again for 1 minute and then another cutscene and sometimes you have to select dialogue choices that most of the time do not matter or impact the story at all although the game tries really hard to make you believe they do.  Oh right, you also maybe shoot the shotgun 2 or 3 times without making much of an impact anyway. There was also a specific puzzle that will impact whether a character dies or not and it was the dumbest puzzle of all time. There are 3 choices for that puzzle, one in which you can retry twice, and if it fails, the guy you play as just says, "eh I won't bother saving you" and leaves the other guy to sit there, another choice in which the same thing happens but it's automatic the first time you do it and the I'm assuming good solution which I could not get because the puzzle had no logical solution other than just randomly picking. Even if it was my fault for failing the puzzle, the fact that any human being just sorta shrugs and leaves his friend in there without doing his best, is absolutely moronic. I didn't talk about this in the story, but every single character in the game has the exact same mentality, the shrugger, horrific events happen around them and they are just kinda "eh, whatever"Gameplay rating: 3/10Voice acting is not very good, they're all bad actors, they seem bored and passive, there is 0 charm in any of them, randomly yelling when they shouldn't, not acting scared when they should, etc. The music is almost non-existent and the sound effects are just pale. Audio rating: 3/10The game runs nice, for me at least, on my high end system, but that ain't saying much as there's not much to look at. Environments are dry and devoid of detail, just a cabin here, a forest there and that's about it. Character models look weird, especially their mouth movements and the monsters looked badly designed. As for bugs, I have not encountered anything so I guess thats a plus.Graphics, performance and tech analysis score: 6/10Avoid this trash at all costs. Yes, I get it, you're bored and you need your dose of horror and there's barely anything good, but stop giving these people your money. They haven't learned and improved a single thing since Until Dawn.

_childDocuments_.review: The Quarry was good fun for one playthrough. However, this is a major shortcoming for Supermassive. With titles like Until Dawn, and The Dark Pictures Anthology, under their belt... The Quarry was decently enjoyable -yet  I cannot recommend this game for full price. It leans into a comedic/cheese role which is perfectly fitting. Yet dialogue is unnatural, and choices seem to not matter anywhere near as much as they have in previous games by Supermassive.There were no real reasons for choosing one thing over the other, as the game would hardly change in most scenarios. I've found myself revisiting Until Dawn after playing this, and probably won't return to The Quarry. This is exactly why I cannot recommend this game. For a game sold under "choices matter," they really didn't change much in the overarching story. Replaying the last chapter, and watching the entire game through again on movie mode, I saw very little difference. Let's not forget that there are no longer relationship stats and personality traits.The Quarry is a dumbed down gorefest, with very little gore.

_childDocuments_.review: Though as much as I enjoy these type of horror games from time to time, the execution is really, at this point, what stands between a memorable horror game, and one that floats in the water (Inside Game Joke). _childDocuments_.review: I bought this game under the impression that it was gonna be a fun summer slasher game. I am a long time fan of Until Dawn and the Dark Anthology series but this was not it. This game was buggy af. There are so many problems I made a list:- Audio issues throughout the game- Textures and models delayed load-in- Blood and wounds not loading in at all- Settings/environment wouldn't load in- There were times where choices wouldn't change the outcome- Characters could be pushed to do the opposite of a choice- The characters reacted in ways opposite of what we chose (There are two major events where this happen)- Character deaths are glossed over- Epilogue feels hollow and condescending- Felt like there were scenes that were just missed or never implemented into the game based on our choices- The game felt unfinished- The game progressively fell apart as we neared the end- The ending was anti-climatic - There were times the game felt stitched together and ridiculous- Felt like devs gave up on the game- Tarots were supposed to give perspective of future choices but were no help- The game description is straight up deceitful and made people think that an entire group had to buy the game to play wolf-pack mode when they could just use the trial- Payed $60 CAN on sale for an unfinished game original price $80 CANOnly upsides:- Dylan- Peanut butter butter pops- Brenda Song (but her character was barely played)Overall I was frustrated and I would've rather had a remaster of Until Dawn than this game. _childDocuments_.review: Sadly, although I did enjoy my playthrough of this game I just can't recommend it for a few reasons.- The graphics seem to be very poorly optimised. Hair flopping around everywhere, lips out of sync with sound, extremely dark areas and unreadable notes, faces distorting. All forgivable if the game wasn't a full price £55 (or £65 deluxe) game. If you are asking for top price then I expect a fully polished product.- it is SUPER annoying that in order to read any notes or letters you need to pick it up, wait, then pick it up a second time in order to read the text. Why not let us read it on first interaction?- The music was jarring and brought me out of the moment. I didn't feel like it added to the game, it just felt like it was shoehorned in and I don't understand why.- the game feels very "clickbaity", with its supposed 186 endings, how different are they really? I haven't had time to try get different endings yet but from what I've heard they aren't really that different. I think there are in reality at most 2 endings with variations of who lived and who died along with what evidence you found changing the god-awful way too long podcast. Let's not ignore the "free to play" thing they are doing here too. Perhaps it is an honest mistake and they'll fix this soon but it appears to be that they made it free to play to attract more people into playing the demo under false pretences that they can play the game for free. Very scummy if this is true, but maybe it's a mistake and I'll edit this if it turns out that way.SPOILERS from this point of review onward:- The ending. What a shame. I felt like I was leading up to a kind of secret ending since I found a card that triggered a cutscene and hinted that I might want to do some things differently but then after doing this it just felt kind of like I'd made a mistake. Maybe I did make a mistake somewhere but the point is it made me feel stupid, like the game was either tricking me or there is in fact no hidden path to take. Eliza acts angry and bitter towards me even though I did exactly what she wanted.All of this being said, I did enjoy the game and its various twists and turns. I just can't recommend this for the price that they are asking with all of the above issues that I mention. Good game with a lot of problems.

_childDocuments_.review: In theory, I love Supermassive Games' work.My introduction to them (like for many, many people) was Until Dawn. I quite enjoyed that game. Man of Medan was alright - acceptable and worth the price but not much more than that. The only game adjacent to this genre worse than Little Hope is Indigo Prophecy, House of Ashes is FANTASTIC and I didn't play Devil Inside yet because I have other things to do.But this game was a gift to me from a friend, and it's one I'm extremely grateful for.The Quarry is an odd game. Most games from Supermassive have a bit of a loose formula to them (one that thankfully varies more than, for contrast, Telltale's formula through those four dozen copy/pastes). The Quarry does a lot that's fresh and interesting I won't be mentioning because of spoilers. There are a few complaints I have about the game, however.-This game could have chopped off about 25% of its total duration and it would've been fine.-Several characters could have been condensed down if they chopped the game down like I think they ought have; alternatively, there are several who /really/ needed more to do in the plot.-The end credits sequence is T E R R I B L E. Past games were especially noteworthy here - the endings of Until Dawn and House of Ashes are possibly the best parts of those excellent games, but this one was so bad I found myself wanting it to be over pretty much immediately, and it is /by far/ the longest sequence. My biggest gripe is a spoiler that's relatively minor I think but I'm marking anyway: It's all subjective, but to me Until Dawn did this thing where almost every single character was made unlikable out the gate and you either grow to like them with time as they develop or they're Chris and you wish you'd killed them when you had a chance. House of Ashes' cast is fantastic from the first minute and this never changes. The Quarry has the most extremes of any of these casts. With a multitude of named characters, they range from "LOVE this character any time they're on screen" to "why are you even in this game?"Unfortunately, several of the game's more appealing characters have very little to actually /do/ in the story. There are several decisions that are not nearly as impactful as they feel like they should be. There are twists and turns the story takes and while one in particular COMPLETELY blew me away, most of them are so obvious I literally didn't realize they were supposed to /be/ a twist at first.Listen. This game's good. I want Supermassive to succeed because I want them to keep making games. This is a decent game. I enjoyed it. I even recommend it. But I can't recommend it as heartily as I do House of Ashes, and that game is half the price of The Quarry.I really can't emphasize enough how much my enthusiasm for the game went from "I want to replay this IMMEDIATELY" to "Maybe I'll reinstall this again someday" /just/ because of the credits sequence ending. It's really THAT bad.

_childDocuments_.review: Title: The Quarry: A Masterpiece of Narrative and ExplorationThe Quarry stands as a beacon of excellence in the gaming landscape, offering a captivating blend of storytelling, exploration, and emotional depth. Developed by a team of visionaries, this game transcends the boundaries of traditional gaming experiences to deliver a truly immersive journey that leaves a lasting impact.Set in a remote quarry town nestled amidst the rugged beauty of nature, the game invites players to step into the shoes of a young protagonist grappling with the complexities of life, loss, and self-discovery. From the moment you embark on this adventure, you're enveloped in a rich tapestry of narrative intricacies that unfold with every step you take.One of the most striking aspects of The Quarry is its masterful storytelling. Every character you encounter feels like a fully realized individual with their own hopes, fears, and dreams. The dialogue is impeccably crafted, drawing you into the lives of these characters and forging genuine connections that tug at your heartstrings. Whether you're sharing heartfelt conversations around a campfire or unraveling the mysteries of the town's past, each interaction is imbued with a sense of authenticity that is truly rare in gaming.However, where The Quarry truly shines is in its commitment to exploration and discovery. The world is vast and teeming with secrets waiting to be unearthed. From hidden caves to towering cliffs, every corner of the quarry town is filled with wonder and intrigue. The sense of freedom you feel as you traverse the landscape is exhilarating, with each new discovery fueling your curiosity and driving you to delve deeper into the world around you.Visually, The Quarry is a feast for the senses. The attention to detail is staggering, with lush environments that are brimming with life. From the gentle sway of the trees to the soft glow of the moonlight, every element of the game is rendered with breathtaking beauty. Combined with a hauntingly beautiful soundtrack that perfectly complements the atmosphere, the result is an experience that is as visually stunning as it is emotionally resonant.Beyond its technical prowess, The Quarry is also a triumph of emotional storytelling. As you navigate the trials and tribulations of the protagonist's journey, you can't help but become emotionally invested in their struggles and triumphs. The game tackles themes of grief, identity, and acceptance with a deft hand, exploring complex emotions in a way that feels both poignant and cathartic.In conclusion, The Quarry is nothing short of a masterpiece. With its gripping narrative, immersive exploration, and emotional depth, it sets a new standard for storytelling in gaming. For anyone seeking an unforgettable gaming experience that will stay with them long after the credits roll, The Quarry is an absolute must-play. This is not just a game – it's a work of art. 10/10 stars.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a "yes" review, but with some heavy caveats. First off, the game isn't worth $60 for only around 9-10 hours of gameplay, so wait for a >= 50% off sale before buying. Secondly, the game is more of an interactive movie rather than a typical horror game because 80% of the game consists of various cutscenes, so keep that in mind.That said, I personally loved the game and it fit with what I was looking for very well. The soundtrack is great, the voice acting and *most* dialogue is fantastic if a bit cringey sometimes, and the animation doesn't disappoint. If you can suspend your disbelief just a little bit, the atmosphere and story are also quite engaging, and keeping your favorite characters alive quickly becomes a personal mission.If you're like me, you can probably eke out two playthroughs of the game. On my initial run, most of the characters died and I got a bad ending, but after studying some of the paths and events that transpired, it was extremely satisfying to fix many of my mistakes and get a much better ending the second time around. Unfortunately, much of the core story remains the same between playthoughs and there is no option to skip cutscenes, so I don't think there is much replayability beyond that. Still, overall a great experience that I would highly recommend when there is a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: OK I'm saving the original review at the bottom for posterity but TL;DR on that bit - I assumed after they patched out the issue where the game freezes on scene transitions that I'd be able to recommend this game but upon reaching the end I have decided instead not to. Turns out that terrible QTEs and choices designed to trip you up are enough of a reason for me to say, "don't buy this!" at least not at full price. If you played Until Dawn, you know it had some uhh, irritating QTEs and some choices with ambiguous outcomes where it wasn't clear that choosing wrong will immediately get someone killed, so be warned - the QTEs are worse now. First off, everything was reduced to either a button mash (A if you used a gamepad, I assume enter for Keyboard) or a Joystick tilt. When you got the button mash, things were okay, you mash the button, so long as you press the button enough times you succeed. But the joystick tilt was designed to trip you up. It took me a full chapter to realize that if you wait a few seconds, it will TELL you what direction you're supposed to tilt. Up to that point I assumed I had to act fast because QTE, and so I would guess. The first couple times it came up I assumed it was referencing a button until I checked the controls. They were intentionally vague about what it was supposed to be, and as far as I could tell, keyboard was no better about labeling directional buttons. The idea was simply to make you mess up while you didn't know any better. Guess they didn't think that having multiple endings would be motivation enough for people to play more than once? Idk. And that would be bad enough except choice events will also try and screw you up, especially at the end. For example, I lost 2 people because the game made a huge deal out of this stuffed rabbit. It had its own butterfly effect path and everything. So I assumed, because of where it ended up, that if I went for it, something good would happen. There was an event where I thought I'd get the opportunity. Instead the rabbit ended up being entirely irrelevant. Idk maybe it would have mattered under different circumstances? But it seemed like the perfect point for it to come up and it just... didn't. And again, if it was ONE instance of the game falsely setting expectations or me misreading the scene, it'd be one thing. But that's just the most egregious example, there are plenty of others. Unrelated, but after playing these and the Dark Pictures games, it's clear to me that Supermassive just... doesn't know how to write a good ending. At least in this ending you don't kill everyone at once with one wrong move. [Original Review about the bug issue - if you're reading this and it's like, the end of July, you probably can ignore this bit]If you liked Until Dawn you'll enjoy this just fine, but give it a few weeks/months. I'm playing on the recommended hardware (almost exactly) and I'm not exaggerating when I say it freezes every 2 scenes. Sometimes it comes back, sometimes it just crashes. Turning Graphics settings down doesn't help, tried a BUNCH of fixes that also didn't help, but hey, I can take comfort in knowing that because there's already a help page for trying to fix the issue that I'm not alone and it's probably not my PC's fault. I'll probably come back and update this to a positive review after it's had a few patches and that issue's dealt with. But if they never fix it and you have a Playstation, chances are good Supermassive made it with the PS4/5 in mind anyway. Also probably more convenient to do the couch co-op mode from a console anyway

_childDocuments_.review: First play through is insanely good. Story twists a few times. Rare visual bugs/desync but no crashes. Collectables and evidence do not matter (I liked the narrator better in the dark anthology anyway). Podcast/news mechanic is an afterthought and not very entertaining. Endings are not very good and very few loose ends get tied up including main characters. Replays are very meh once you realize a majority of the story events and paths are set in stone and your decisions tend to cause only minor variations. Character (and specific enemy) deaths are locked into specific paths so you cant have a truly unique path that you create where a random mix of people die or survive. For example, a specific enemy can only ever die if you make a decision to sacrifice three other main characters in trade and that action locks you into a specific story ending. All of the major decisions are like that and must happen only one of maybe two ways. Its not awful its just way less complex especially compared to house of ashes or until dawn. I finished my second play through and was getting majorly bored midway through and probably am done for a bit. Overall, recommend. Not sure its worth 60 bucks but technically at 24 hours I got my moneys worth.

_childDocuments_.review: A solid, fun and interesting horror game suitable for couch co-op. The story is around 9 hours long and it's pretty fun to go through. Taking into consideration that you could replay the game and choose different outcomes and get different endings helps content wise. The characters are well done, and written in an interesting way. Plus, the '80s' artstyle and horror inspirations fit the game perfectly. When it comes to the visual and technical side of it, the game looks amazing, in and out of cutscenes. The movement is decent, but the camera can feel a bit odd at first. The quicktime events are much easier than in other 'Until Dawn' type games, personally. The only thing in the game I can without a doubt say I dislike is not being able to skip the cutscenes. I understand the decision to not let the player skip certain cutscenes, but the cutscenes being essentially 50% of the game and not being able to skip any of them makes replaying it a bit exhausting. But that aside, I definitely recommend it, ideally when it's on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is game is probably worth 20$ in terms of an experience. The production value in terms of animation and sound design are amazing, but unfortunately the game falls apart in the major categories of gameplay and story, which are far more important.Don't bother buying this game, go watch your favourite content creator go through it.I don't enjoy this game, so instead of a pro's and cons I'll just break down the problems I have with it.The story is drenched in bad tropes and cliches from start to finish. While tropes are not inherently bad, they are terribly used here to make a bland, boring and predictable story.The characters are all one note, one line smarmy ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. They are far more caricature than characters. There is little to no growth in any of them, and all of them carry pretty much one specific identifying trait. If the cast was smaller or focused on better then this may have been alleviated somewhat.The story is constantly jumping around due to the large cast, but also comes to a full stop at terrible times to deal with a badly executed card collecting mechanic. The pacing is already very bad, but becomes a literal showstopper with this event.The moment to moment gameplay is basically non-existent, and where it does exist I kind of wish it didn't. The walking around searching for clues bit is long drawn out and incredibly un-engaging. There is very little reward for exploring around, and you're locked into such a specific set of requirements its a wonder that you're allowed to explore at all. It is literally move to x and press y with no depth or real interest.The QTE's are the only other major mechanic, and they are as basic as they sound.Overall the game is an animated choose you're own adventure book, but the story sucks, the characters suck, the gameplay is tedious and un-enjoyable and there isn't really a single new idea expressed anywhere in the game. Its all so route and by the books there's a literal movie mode so you don't even have to play the game.Even the greatly praised animation dips into the uncanny valley well over half the time, with terrible idle animations, only one active character per interactive walking scene, unnatural facial animations, weird proportions, and janky visuals on occasion due to bugs.Easily the best part of this is the detailed animation and wonderful sound design.To their credit, the music is on point for 90% of the game, the SFX is decently done and the voice actors really do sell their characters. I'd love to see more of their work in a well written game.

_childDocuments_.review: The Quarry does have some replay-ability in a sense that every choice you make can potentially create a different outcome, which there are around 168 of- and unfortunately, I don't think that it makes any difference at all, since  thing at the end of the game, which shows a slide of each character one by one and what happened to them. It's up to your imagination, I guess.However, during the epilogue, there is a computer monitor displaying the front page from the local , and if I'm not mistaken, the headline can change depending on how much evidence you collect throughout the evening.Nevertheless, I still enjoyed The Quarry quite a bit- I never experienced any issues, it ran like butter and looked gorgeous. _childDocuments_.review: In the past, Supermassive Games have already shown us who is the King of horror games with an emphasis on player choices, but how is their best title since the release of Until Dawn doing ? In my opinion, it is perhaps even a better gaming experience than Until Dawn.In short, as I'm guessing some of you haven't played or seen the game yet, we are at Camp Hackett's Quarry where we have several characters to play as, make decisions and improve or worsen relationships between them. Specifically, we are talking about Ryan (Ryan is quite serious and pessimistic, the type I like) then Kaitlyn (A girl who has quite a lot of sass but also a charming sense of humor) Jacob (A typical dumb who you would rather kill on the spot because his IQ is maybe only double digits) Emma (Typical conceited, egotistical and arrogant blonde who hasn't picked up much sense either) Abby (Shy goth girl who tries to keep everything under control) Nick (Who tries to be calm and somehow fit into society, because this character has a Script about halfway through the game, so I don't know much about him) and then there is Dylan (Dylan is my favorite character, he is an Optimist with a large portion of humor and can make light of any situation, even if the circumstances do not really require it). However, the game starts with the last day at Hackett's Quarry Camp and our camp leaders are going home, however MR JACOB can't stand that the girl flirted with him but didn't mean it, so he breaks down the car so he can spend one more night with her and he thinks it will make a difference  So because of one Teenager's cockiness and horniness, he put a group of people in great danger that emerges as soon as the moon rises (Respective full moon) As there are certain creatures in the forest that only appear in the full moon, and our leaders are in great danger because of JACOB, honestly at the first playthrough (I play the game for the second time), Jacob died and I cheered, but my Achievement, which said that everyone must survive, was not so Optimistic.If you have played a game from this Studio, either Until Dawn, or a game from The Dark Pictures Anthology, then you certainly know how the game plays, although the word "plays" is very strong, their games seem more like a Movie that you control and you decide the plot. And speaking of that, this game is really governed by your decisions, you have Key decisions that will affect the plot of the game and various events, but there are also decisions in dialogues that affect your relationships with others and accordingly to you approach for the rest of the game, in short, if you act like an arrogant jerk or egoistically or somehow do not understand the group it will have a big impact in that others will not trust you and their willingness to help you will also be very low. However, according to what I noticed during my playing, the longest sequence when you have your hands on the keyboard and really move is about 15 minutes if you explore everything, however, the classic length of the game with a simple passage and no exploration will take you a maximum of 5-7 minutes. However, as is often the case with these developers, you can find Tarot Cards in the game, which if you collect, at the end of each chapter you will reach a fortune teller, who can show you a small snippet of what may (but may not) happen in the next chapter, it works on the principle of our favorite The Curator from Dark Pictures Anthology.Here is something that can ruin your gaming experience, if you don't have a good enough PC that can run the game in Ultra settings, then your eyes will definitely see the big details that are between Ultra settings and Normal settings, that is, I play the game on Normal for every graphic setting (Except for AA, I have it on Ultra, otherwise the game looks absolutely horrible). However, yes, the graphics side of the game is quite cleverly done and the developers played around, but there are things that I need to clarify and these are necessary: Close-up shots (Please note that I am comparing the game now from my perspective, not from Ultra settings) When the game brings you some detail, the textures what the camera is currently aiming at are out of focus and not scailed, it totally detracts from the realism that the game sets with its graphics in a different way. Another thing is the shadows, when you have Shadows on Normal, the Shadows are not even a little soft and are mostly pixelated, so I'll tell you, I have not seen the pixelated shadow of the tree yet, again, since the shadows are made in this way on Normal, the lighting of individual scenes (during the day) looks absolutely terrible, almost as if there was a shadow by 20%, which again reduces the game experience, the only settings that work on Normal are Effects and SSAO these settings are perfect. However, as far as game optimization is concerned, it's different here, but I have to admit that the developers have really taken care, because with the game on the highest settings I don't meet the CPU nor GPU, so I have to say that when I play the game on Normal, the frame rate does not change from 60 which I have to admit is really cool and I'm glad that the developers at least really cared about this.​So let's be clear, we have a game here from a Studio that makes absolutely top notch Horror games that are controlled by the player's decisions, so how could this game be a flop? Honestly I have to say that this game is really great and I can't wait to play the game on Ultra graphics settings in 2K resolution because this game has so much energy and most importantly so much potential that is squeezed to the maximum, however for me I think that if you have already played some games from Supermassive studio you should give this game a chance, if you enjoy games like Telltale Walking Dead or Life is Strange, I have the impression that this game will be perfect for you, however, if you are not afraid of horror, the game also has uniqe sound and I recommend you to play with headphones, because then you will enjoy the whole game in a completely different perspective, however, for me the game takes away ... quite a pleasant score, I just hope that the next game from this studio will turn out even better or, at worst, on same level as this game.Played on:AMD Ryzen 5 2600 (6-Core)GeForce GTX 1660 Super (GDDR6 | 6GB VRAM)Corsair Kit 2x8GB 2666MHzWindows 11Pros and cons✔ Amazing story✔ Great audio✔ Decisions have a powerful impact✔ Great optimization✘ Game details on Normal are really bad✘ Character bugs during animations✘ Occasionally shifted Audio from Animations​━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━PLAYED WITH: ⌨️ 🖱 🎧━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

_childDocuments_.review: Completed the game and am now on my second play through. I want to leave this review in the hope that the developers see or hear what I think should be improved upon for the games replay-ability and game play experience.Before I start if you want to bypass using the silly 2K Launcher and play the game only via steam, go into your games properties and enter this as a launch option (include the speech marks and change the drive accordingly): "C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\The Quarry\TheQuarry.exe" %command%My main issues are the QTE's, they are pretty easy (being the arrow keys) and can only be changed to be slower. They are also pretty predictable, you know when they are coming they won't catch you off guard. There should be toggle-able options in the games menu for faster QTE's and different variation of keys (like A,S,W,D in Man of Medan).Action sequences like aiming a gun at an enemy takes too long as well with the opponent pretty much standing still while you line up the perfect shot. There should be a difficulty option that encompasses this and the fact that you have all the time in the world to make dialog decisions.These additions of what is essentially a customisable difficulty setting would really add the game. There are small problems like audio desynchronisation in certain isolated cut scenes but I am sure issues like this will be patched soon.

_childDocuments_.review: First off this game is immensely overpriced, no excuse for how much this game costs for its runtime or what you're getting. This isn't to say this is a bad game but its not worth the price tag its at, if you're ever going to buy and play this buy it on sale or don't at all even if you're a fan of Supermassive games, and if you're not already a fan be cautious doing so, these games are generally a overpriced for their length.Overall I really liked The Quarry I think it showcases the cause and effect of your decisions extremely well compared to most of Supermassives works and I found myself actually reflecting on my choices because I could directly see and understand what they caused. There are a few characters I think that have way to punishing and specific issues in their respective route to the end that feel like its so specific that most people will have no say in it before its way to late, 1-2 characters in particular probably come to most peoples minds.This game is also essentially an immersive movie there is not much gameplay and I think that's partially what makes some things feel so punishing, a lot of this game is pretty hands off.I think this game is definitely worth playing if you like its style and like Until Dawn, or a lot of the Dark Pictures games, but only on a massive sale so I recommend it for the game itself but with that large caveat to doing so.

_childDocuments_.review: The characters are really stereotypical and sometimes bland, we got the popular girl, the loner, the jock and so on. There is nothing unique about the story, some teenagers are partying in a forest and then a killer ends up hunting them. The biggest problem however is the lack of deaths, out of all 9 playable characters, 6 have their first poissble death in chapter 8-10 and later, one even got his first poissble death in the last chapter. Many characters never get enough time to shine while others get way too much playtime, the game has failed to even out everyone's own story. The gameplay is also really easy and the quick- and the don't breath events isn't a challenge for most players and ruins any chance of the game being intensive.Even though the game has many flaws, this is still one of Supermassive's better games, I enjoyed this more than any of the 3 games from The Dark Pictures Anthology. This feels more like a sequel to the fantastic Until Dawn (please release it on steam) than any other game. This is probably the longest game with the most hours of gameplay out of any Supermassive game aswell.I mostly enjoyed my time with the game and the only thing that really bugged me was the horrible ways my characters ended up dying that didn't have to do with consequences but instead out of pure luck. The game isn't worth 60 dollars and I think something closer to 40 dollars would be a better price for a game like this. This game is simply decent, better than most horror decision making games. Big credits to some of the actors like Justice Smith, Siobhan Williams and especially the one and only, Ted Raimi.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of horror or suspense movies and like games that have multiple storylines that are influenced by your choices then you'll love this game.First off it's an incredibly good looking game with character models and environments so well done that it's easy to get immersed in the world which is exactly what you want in a game like this where you need to build emotional attachment to the characters to really care about their survival....or deaths.The action from chapter to chapter is so good and the jump scares are all fantastic. There were a lot of moments where my I found my jaw literally open wide due to a reveal of a story beat or death of a character in a way I hadn't expected.The acting was great, there are characters you're going to love and some that you will absolutely hate - but that's just a testament to how good the acting is.I really can't think of any complaints that wouldn't be nitpicky, this is a must play for fans of the horror or pick your own adventure genre. I don't have the time to go through another playthrough, but there has to be hundreds of hours of replayability based off how many branching choices you go through in the game.

Mistakes were made, some things happened, and well, death, destruction etc etc ensues..  Lots of Death, and Lots of Destruction... or not really that much, the choice is yours.(Technical issues were fixed Along time ago, but I never got around to playing the game,, I blame my backlog, and working too much, but I finally did it,, just in time for Supermassive's next game The Casting of Frank Stone... Even if Dead by Daylight moderators, unfairly banned me from the steam forums for making a stupid joke)  Gameplay - If you've played one Supermassive game you've played them all.. Some choices unlock Fluff dialogue, other choices mean someone is about to die..  Be careful out there.. _childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Looks great, great acting, and great for fans of cinematic choice games and horror. It still has to be said that it's not as good as it could be and the moralizing of past SM games is still here. Spoiler free review below.The Quarry by Supermassive Games is a step up from two of their three (I haven't played one of them) Dark Pictures Anthology titles. One thing about those Dark Pictures entries I'm not a big fan of is that the story foundations tend to be more thriller-like than straight up horror. There is a difference! But I'll stop there by saying The Quarry provides a legit horror story. The presentation is solid with great graphics and appropriate moody lighting changes as you enter into the final few chapters of the game. Writing is good with very few off moments but when they happen they really stand out and feel odd. The characters are good. Some of them are fleshed out in a way that, depending on who you are, you could either love or hate the character. There's one character in particular that I imagine a lot of people would dislike, but I totally appreciated and respected. That's a good accomplishment for characters and valuable for a choice-based game.Inevitably for this type of game, there is going to be disappointment with how the choices are handled. I found when I made a choice I didn't like the outcome of, the writing stages a defense through the in-game characters in the next scene with characters saying things that highlight how choices the player just made in a different scene were not thought out. Kind of weird, but makes sense for the player who will be salty or confused about how they made a wrong choice. I did have that happen and had to be like, 'yeah, I didn't think about that.' It is unfortunate that a couple scenes are not clear on what your choices are about--with one in particular being fatal. To Supermassive's credit, I do like that dialog choices here don't just say the type of response 'friendly/mean' but also give a snippet of the actual dialog you're choosing. This is great as in other Supermassive Games I've felt like some of the dialog types I would choose didn't end up being at all like I imagined. If the player is going to make a choice in game, it's good for the outcome to feel like it represents the choice that was made. So, good improvement even though there are a few moments that aren't done so well.I've only done one play through at the time of this review and that may be all I do. That said, I can't really speak to how much choices impact the game. I imagine most of the life or death decisions happen in the last three of ten chapters, while there are some things that definitely set the stage for life or death early in the game. I can still say there's an obvious moralizing I strongly dislike that's involved in the narrative design and choices offered to players. Yeah, yeah, it's kind of artsy, and, yes, I believe empathy is very important. I do wish they would hold off on the artsy moralizing until they've mastered making this kind of game. Give me a well-paced and consistently great experience before you bust out the moral high horse. Horror is about many things but some of the core elements are scares and excitement. I'd rather my choices as a player be decisions that result in different kinds of scares and thrilling moments rather than earning a morality badge from a set of developers. It kind of screws with the point of why a cinematic horror game is being played. Leave the life lessons to Bluey or be more subtle about it.Pacing is surprisingly good considering that I believe The Quarry is twice as long as some of the Dark Pictures games? I'd have to go back over my time with those to be sure. I still have to say the pacing could be better. Chapter 7 would be better off removed from the game. Wow, does that chapter just slow things down! It's not bad story wise, but it's backstory and there's a reason you don't see those kinds of segments in extended fashion in movies. They kill the pacing. Just let the player/audience catch up. At the very least, it's a problem that chapter 7 felt longer than any other chapter. If you're going to make an extra long chapter, don't have it be your backstory exposition!Back to some positives! I only lost two main protagonists in my run, so I didn't see a lot of gore, but there's still plenty of blood! The cast is really solid across the board. Brenda Song has a cool about her here that feels well suited for horror and I am disappointed that most of her roles are for kids' shows. With upcoming titles from Song that include Chibiverse, Blue Eye Samurai, and Operation Taco Gary's, it doesn't look like that's changing anytime soon. Not really a surprise but still worth saying, Ted Raimi outshines here and I think progressively gets better in the later parts of the game. I am interested in another play through potentially. I tend to be a one and done on these kinds of games because you usually can't speed up repeat playthroughs. However, features like Movie Mode and unlocking a death rewind ability for new games does hold some appeal.
