_childDocuments_.review: + Visually, this game seriously impresses at times. Very beautiful environments and characters that, often times, look almost photo real. Supermassive has proven time and time again they have a solid understanding of how to make human beings look good, and this game is no outlier.+ The Quarry embraces the 80s-90s slasher vibe with colorful interface decisions (such as detailing "Paths" as VHS tapes with creative covers), music choices, and environment details that often times feel nostalgic. + Compared to other story games, The Quarry does a fantastic job of getting you invested in these characters (for the most part). While they have an awkward start, each and every character (and their many concerns and interests) starts to grow on you and stand out from one another, without falling entirely into established tropes. One particular example is the romance between Ryan and Dylan, which is extremely cute (even if it doesn't go anywhere). Even side characters and ''evil'' characters pull you in with wonderful voice acting by an extremely talented cast of real actors. The performances are downright flawless.- Ending/Resolution: The ending is absolutely disappointing. All you get for beating the game is a quick summary of who survived and who didn't, and a crappy podcast voiceover during the credits that attempts to justify the existence of the clue system. The quick snippets telling you some minor details of who survived pales in comparison to resolutions in other story games -- Until Dawn, for example, at least at the character interviews where I learn how everyone felt about the events of the night. I was left with so many questions... What did Ryan decide to do about his family, and his sister? Did Ryan and Dylan get together (because they were very cute together and they had INSANE chemistry, and the game does nothing with it)? Did Jacob's gambit to get Emma to reconsider him work? How did Abigail and Nick feel after the events of the game? What did Laura and Max do with their new freedom from the curse? How did the Hackett family grieve, and were they truly the bad people in the story? Also, biggest question: Did anyone believe the characters at all if you have enough evidence, and if they did, how was the situation treated? Is there a government organization that stepped in?- Your Choices Matter: Yet another story game where the phrase "your choices matter" is a gross exaggeration. A majority of the game's paths are fixed -- Decisions are often forced upon you, situations arise that you couldn't have possibly foreseen, and you will inevitably end up second guessing decisions that should be easy. Worse, the game actively attempts to steer you into bad decisions because it implies that you don't see the full picture. For example, a 'big' decision the game puts forward to you is that you shouldn't kill an ancient evil because of the innocence tied to it. HOWEVER, doing so will ♥♥♥♥ you over - there is no purist ending, people will die because of your inaction, and you don't even get any sort of redemption reason for making that decision, because the Hacketts arguably haven't done anything wrong in regards to Silas. There are also characters that, despite the game pretending like you may be able to save, cannot be saved, and attempts to save them will kill far more people. Even though there are certainly ways you could come up with where everyone lives.- Hints (Part 1): The hint system is absolutely terrible, and resulted in a character getting killed for me. It often times serves no actual purpose because the hint is unclear, and sometimes will outright mislead you into doing something you wouldn't normally do. This happened to me: Emma, at a certain point, ends up alone on an isolated area. The Tarot card "The Star" implies that Ema looks up at a hatch, something falls out of the hatch, and you take a photo and get out unscathed. So, when I reached this hatch, which was bumping, I assumed that I was supposed to open it to get a better look. I would have NEVER done this had the hint not implied to me, the player, that my expectations were wrong. But not only was I wrong, there is literally no way to prevent dying if you do open the hatch. You die IMMEDIATELY.- Hints (Part 2): "The Hint System is intentionally misleading because the narrator wants the Hacketts to pay". I can admit that the idea sounds compelling, because it can be interesting to lie to the player and mess with expectations. However, this sort of method does not work in a game like The Quarry. There is no real benefit to replaying the game because there is only the one "right path", and everything else are just mistakes for you to make. Nobody is going to replay this game after getting a disappointing ending. In fact, very few story games can actually get the player to do this (maybe Detroit: Become Human?), because you essentially watched a movie with some minor impact on the ending. Doing this only leads to breeding dissatisfaction with the player, and ruins the one (and likely only) playthrough of the game. - Story - Lack of Explanaton: There are a lot of loose threads that... go nowhere. We have no idea why Silas is the way he is, why we have these ghostly apparitions of the "Hag". or why the Hikers had to die at all (what possible motivation do they have to kill them? Even if you suppose they wanted to keep the situation a secret until they fix it, killing them brings just as much potential media attention as letting them go with no evidence. Why even have this as a plot thread?). There are also more severe loose ends, like, why does Abigail act like she has some of the wolf powers twice? Twice she pushes Nick away and acts horrified like she doesn't know her own strength. How many werewolves have been killed? Why did Silas return now of all times? - Story - Bad Decisions: So often, characters do absolutely dumb things to make the plot happen. Jacob falls in front of bear traps and backwalks into one, the cast decides to split up and do meaningless things (why find a car part when you'll be fine when the morning comes anyway??). Also, the family clearly has electrified cages -- why were the family members who are infected not in those cages? Also also, if the camp site is a significant place for Silas, and they know that it is, why not use cameras in that area?While this game initially pulls you in with compelling atmosphere, intriguing characters, and highly detailed environments and character models, it soon starts to turn sour as you dive into the story, which is mishandled in the worst of ways. The illusion of choice becomes more and more obvious as your character make dumb decisions that you have no control over. If you made the mistake of following the hint system, you might've misunderstood what happens and ruined your one playthrough -- and if you didn't, you'll find yourself disappointed that the ending does not reward you adequately for your success. I spent $60 for a 7 hour playthrough - but I did not list this as a negative, because I do believe that a low playtime doesn't necessarily mean the money was wasted. However, the entire experience was very disappointing, which is a crying shame because the game had SO MUCH potential.I would recommend avoiding The Quarry unless:1. The devs rework the ending and hint system to fix these glaring issues.2. The game is deeply discounted and you're desperate to scratch the narrative game itch.3. You really like Supermassive Games and want to support them.

_childDocuments_.review: Refunded after one hour so this review can only be counted as a first impression.Black bars at the top & bottom of the screen that can't be turned off, motion blur from hell that can't be turned off, stiff and outdated facial expressions of the characters make many situations seem unintentionally funny and often destroy the whole atmosphere. The writing fluctuates, but often suffers from the fact that certain things don't make much sense, because the story has to work as a video game. So for example you can't talk to the person who just did something insanely stupid five seconds before and confront him about it because whoops, it's a videogame and the devs didn't think of that. So everybody just acts like nothing happened.As the player, you are often given trivial tasks to complete while all the other characters stand around and wait for you to do these chores. _childDocuments_.review: My review of The Quarry after a first play through run!Just finished my first play through, have to say it was downright amazing! The realism is uncanny awesomeness on a whole different level, like playing real life people, or controlling a movie! It's a one of a kind experience everyone should take a try at, I mean unless you absolutely hate the horror genre in which case no hope for you. LOL To be honest whilst this has lots of horror elements to it for sure, it is also a thriller, action packed, strong story driven, a mystery to solve, & choices actually matter, and changes pathways each time. The choices also make for great replay-ability for multiple attempts at different outcomes, and overall endings! The best part of this entire experience for me are the different main characters that you get to really like over the course of the game story, and even fall in love with for their personalities! Everyone will have their favorites, or least favorites but they are all decently written characters overall. I'd also like to say the background music, and actual songs used in this game were fantastic too! The timed events, quick action choices, and dialog choices I felt were top notch overall. I never felt too rushed with the default settings for those actions, & with the settings for replays you can also tweak just about everything to your liking. So as example on a replay if you wanted to play more hardcore, and harder experience next round, you can easily set it to be like that if you desired. I also own all the DLC content, I feel it was well worth it, especially the 1980's outfits pack, as it's fun to play again seeing everyone in classic 80's fashion next round of play. I also love the filter options DLC content allowing the reply to be classic 80's style filter horror theme!I highly recommend picking this amazing game up to experience for yourself, though as I usually suggest for games of this type of price, try to pick it up when on a Steam sale if you want to save a bit of cash on the purchase. I score this 9.5 out of 10 for one hell of a ride! Buy it, you'll be glad you did! XD

_childDocuments_.review: As far as choose your own adventure games go, this is probably one of the best. The horror entertainment genre is a relatively new experience for myself, chalk it up to being a resident of weenie hut jr., but I'm glad I took a chance on this one. The Good:- Great writing, voice acting and motion capture.- The initial playthrough is thrilling and engrossing. I've lost many an hour of sleep in favor of finding out what happens next in the storyline.- "Calm down, son. It's just a drawing," was something that I had to say to myself a few times. So great character modeling.- Good mix of brevity and serious moments.- You get a pretty good idea of how the character that you're playing is going to speak/respond based on the conversation options provided to you.- I also blame everything on bears when I go camping.The Not So Good:- I experienced a few audio bugs and rending problems.- There are a fair amount of opportunities to explore, but if you happen to take a wrong turn you miss out on doing so sometimes. So be sure to explore when you can. _childDocuments_.review: *No spoilers*Generally:This game is pretty damn good. I think I can say I'm a fan. If you played until dawn, its pretty similar. A pretty balanced amount of interactive quick time event cut scenes as well as little moments in the game that allow you to explore a find things like clues and tarot cards and other interact-able things. The only frustrating thing though is that sometimes its impossible to tell if the next thing you press A on will send you to the next scene, or if it will allow you to keep exploring. The other thing is that you really gotta be careful about which moves you make at times because you might make a decision that just straight up gets a character killed and there is nothing you can do about it. However, a majority of the time its pretty controllable. You really have to play this game multiple times through to truly understand what happens after which move you make. I think this game is more for people who want a good story (and be able to manipulate it!).The story:The general story sounds pretty stereotypical and generic, but I was anxious and genuinely surprised the entire playthrough of this story.  Most if not all of this story is pretty exciting and unpredictable. The rest of the game is trying to put the pieces together and understanding what is going on. There really is a lot of parts to the story that kept me on the edge of my seat. The way they conveyed this story in the way that they did, made it so good. The mischievousness of the chronology of this game was amazing, and it wasn't confusing to follow along with. It was also really satisfying to find clues and figure out details of the story, to be later confirmed by a character explaining what is happening. Quick time Events (QTE's)There is a whole bunch of these. In action packed points, and even in calmer moments of the game. Its a cool idea, and it keeps the player's attention when watching long unskippable cutscenes. I honestly thought this game would be boring and more like a movie, but its really not. QTE's are placed generously and I think that there is not too much and not too little. Im probably gonna play this multiple times through. One last thing for the developers and I guess anyone else:PLEASE PLEASE do something about the credits. It was insatiably excruciating to have to sit on the UNSKIPPABLE credits screen for 25+ minutes. This is such a heinous way to end this game. I liked the little updates after the game ended on every character, which was fine, but maybe instead of making us sit through the entire ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ credits to get a stupid achievement and have the game actually count as finished, why don't you have a sanctimonious cutscene at the end of the game with all of the survived characters meeting up in the front of the lodge? or SOMETHING?? The podcast was a cool added touch, but the podcast only plays for about half the time you have to watch the credits. You have to watch the rest of the credits with some added music. Like literally who in the entire universe wants to watch a credits scene with one singular visual of a computer screen and the same newspaper heading for 25 minutes. Even with the podcast in the background, I wanted to blow my brains out having to sit through those credits. It's worse than going to a marvel movie and having to wait for the post-credit scenes. Because those credits are shorter. Somehow.Another thing that is annoying is that no matter what every single individual cutscene within this game does not have a native method to skip or speed up. I guess it is the whole point of the game, but it would be nice to at least be able to skip early scenes like the prologue which have no affect on the rest of the story and only have a few different scenes to branch from. The prologue and epilogue of this game get pretty repetitive and a little annoying, to be honest. Im not sure if it is just my system, but EVERY SINGLE TIME I boot the game, and exit a game and return to the main menu, it asks if i want to turn on , even though I already said yes the first time I beat the game. At this point, reguardless if i say yes or no, the option remains turned on. So it gives me a dead prompt every single time I return to the main menu essentially. This is a really annoying bug that should have been fixed a while ago, honestly. Something else you should know: This game runs so much better and smoother when you bypass the 2K launcher. Click properties on The Quarry and find the "Launch Options" space. If your file path is the EXACT same as mine, copy and paste this: "C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\The Quarry\TheQuarry.exe" %command%If not, copy and paste your file path to the Quarry.exe file and add %command% on the end. Make sure that the file path is in quotations. The game does not require the additional launcher to function properly. Its funny actually, the game runs BETTER without it.Stability:This game seems to have pretty good optimization, with occasional stuttering. Seemed to run smooth 90-150 FPS at high-ultra settings, on a GTX 3060 and Intel 13600KF and 16GB memory.This game is probably one of the least glitch filled games I have played as of recently that is a new game. In fact I didn't experience a single game breaking bug, or anything that was bad enough to remember. There is a very slight visual thing when models are set before the camera switches angles, and you can sometimes see hair or clothes falling from items spawning. Other than that, this game is essentially perfect, for my standards. Respect to Supermassive Games for actually testing and bug fixing the game before releasing it, unlike every AAA developer these days. I highly recommend this game, especially for anyone who wants a good story and doesn't care to be doing something the entire playthrough.

_childDocuments_.review: *Spoiler-free review*TLDR: If you're looking for the successor to Until Dawn, which a fair amount of people will argue is the best "experience" to ever release on the PS4, this is it. Same developer, same high quality but completely different story. Much longer than the Dark Pictures mini-series they have (I enjoyed all of those; I thought House of Ashes was the best but Little Hope had the better story). Somewhat same interface, though "traits" seem to be non-existent in this. Like how in their other games you would have relationship meters and adjectives that developed over time; those do not exist here. QTE's are way easier than in other titles, mainly just pushing the keys or controller in a certain direction. You can turn these off in the settings if you want. Hell, you can turn off just about anything you want in the settings.  People complaining about "2k launcher," give me a break. Play the game in Big Picture mode and you won't have to do that additional one click of "play" which seems to be just way too much for some people.I've played through it twice, first time as best I could and the second time trying to get everyone killed for the achievement. Was actually unable to get everyone killed off, so that's something. The first play through where I tried to do and see everything took just over 15 hours. The game is not an 80's slasher as some have pegged it before release, simply because it takes place at a summer camp. It's in a modern setting, with cellphones, internet, streaming, podcasts, etc. I will play through it again just because there is so much material here and you literally can miss out on an entire part of the game if someone dies or if you choose one path over the other.My only gripe about the game is that if you miss something early on, you will very likely miss it completely. In chapter 2 I didn't get to explore an area completely because I interacted with an object that moved me to the next area and I never had a chance to go back. That sucks, a lot. Especially because in other chapters you will actually get a "warning" about moving on to the next scene about "are you finished here?" / "keep looking around". And that's not a sign that you necessarily missed something, it's just a warning that you are going to the next scene and probably won't be back to this area. I'm not sure why this exists in some chapters but not others. Other minor grip is when you are interacting with the "storyteller" in between chapters they do not say nuanced things about decisions you made like in other Supermassive games. In other titles they might say something like "it looks like so-and-so met an unfortunate end, and you have to wonder who else will join them throughout the night" or "things are getting dangerous, if only you had found a weapon to protect yourself." None of that exists here, which again, kind of sucks. But it's not game breaking.Anyway, The Quarry is a game that did not disappoint and I found myself thinking about it at work and being excited to go and play it. I haven't had that feeling in a long, long time. The characters all had distinguished personalities, though no one was really super annoying. There's no "4.0 ♥♥♥♥♥, honor roll" but Kaitlin's workout pants more than make up for it. I'd say I probably actually liked the vast majority of the characters. Supermassive has been my favorite game developer for quite some time because they have a modern take on the adventure game/ CYOA style of experience. As I grow older my reflexes aren't what they used to be, so sometimes it's nice to just enjoy a story and make decisions along the way. Highly recommended for fans of the genre or people looking for a different gaming  experience. Also, Supermassive, if you read this can you guys release some merch? I want to buy a shirt so badly and I ain't going the redbubble knockoff route. Thanks.

_childDocuments_.review: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐Masterpiece of the  genre, The Quarry has jawdropping graphics (on par with RDR2) and a great story that could have been written by Stephen King. The majority of negative reviews come from people that didn't know what kind of game they were buying. in some parts of the game, you'll hide and hold your breath, represented by a red bar. You'd think the right thing to do is to wait until the bar is almost empty to move, and sometimes it is, but not always. If you do that, you may miss the only opportunity to escape. _childDocuments_.review: Just as great as their other games, I defiantly think this is better then the Dark Pictures Anthology games, with the story being better in Little Hope. I spent about 12 hours on my first play though, making sure I got as many clues and collectibles as possible, and still missed stuff. I was able to save the main crew of people just wish their were more options and I could of saved more. I think this game did a better job at hiding what the correct response was. In previous games I find it to easy to keep everyone alive, this time it was a bit of a struggle. I even had to use the death rewind just to save someone. I enjoyed the options for accessibility, along with the option to use OpenDyslexic font. This helped make my time playing easier. I was able to auto do the breathing OTEs something I have struggled with in most of their games (ie dont move heatbeat) Having extra time to make choices was also helpful. I think a lot of these new features help make the game better for not only myself but other people who might need them.Spoilers I think their are better choice your adventure games out their with more endings Heavy Rain and Detroit doing an excellent job of making your choice feel more important then in this game, their endings also feel more unique because their are more of them. This game only has a few true endings with most the endings feeling the same. I think that along with lack of choices are the downfalls of this game. Overall I think this is an great game, especially if you are looking for some replay value. Having the movie option from the start is also nice so you can just sit back and watch. I don't think this game is as good as Until Dawn, but I do not regret paying full price either.If you like their other games you would like this one, if you want a game with more choices and better story I would wait till this is on sale, I am not saying don't buy this game cause it is defiantly worthy of playing but if you are questioning it just wait.

_childDocuments_.review: By far I'd say the most controversial entry Supermassive has done! And by that I don't mean it's like, uooooooh super terrifying, it's just a very... dividing game, some people hate it, some people love it.Me personally? I love this game! It's the first Supermassive game I have finished since Until Dawn because the Dark Pictures Anthology was super boring for me.I see this game as a... modernization of the cheesy 80s horror movies, it has those stupid tropes, counselors being stupid but overall it just had a really 80s vibe despite the game being set in modern times. Now how do you see that? As a pro or a con, depends on the person you're asking that to, I love this kind of stuff personally, It makes up some really goofy moments that personally made me laugh.The characters are... the most controversial part of the game i'd say since, you can hate them or love them, I loved most of the cast to be honest! Except for Emma who was a manipulative POS and Jacob who you can't just unsimp. The dynamic between Dylan, Ryan and Kaitlyn is so lovely too!Now, onto the meat and potatoes (that's a thing people say, right?), the story.albeit predictable at times, I thoroughly enjoyed this game's story and how much my decisions affected the outcome of my characters, where they ended up, if they're alive or dead, etc. Granted, it's nowhere near Supermassive's best work Until Dawn and its really fun Butterfly Effect mechanic, but that shouldn't discredit The Quarry's handling of these decisions! The only part I was like "that's it?" is the "epilogue", I wish they handled that but I'm not gonna go into details because we're getting in spoilery territory, something I wish to avoid.Overall I'd give it a 8/10, fun game, but please if you plan to play it, disable 2K's horrendous launcher, there are guides out there that can help you with that. It degrades performance massively and it's overall a really predatory launcher.

_childDocuments_.review: Small note: I beat this entire game on PS5. I only downloaded the demo to write this review, which is why my playtime is really lowFor Steam Deck users: Don't waste your time. It barely runs on Steam Deck no matter what settings you use. Poor optimizationCompared to the other Choices Matter games by Supermassive games (Dark Pictures Anthology, Until Dawn), this game is very underwhelming. Despite that, this game is still really enjoyable. Easily the best part of the game is the music. It's drastically less challenging in a few ways. QTEs are very trivial and very hard to fail. The "Don't Breathe" segments are as simple as holding a button until the red goes away. Compared to how stressful and challenging these things were in House of Ashes, it's really disappointing. In House of Ashes, nearly all deaths were from failing these. In The Quarry, majority of deaths are just a simple option that you're given no clues about. Straight up instant death for picking what seems reasonable.This isn't to say I don't recommend the game, it just deserves to be much cheaper. It looks great, sounds great, and runs great. The story is very interesting (despite some parts in the story that're never answered and the disgusting end credits scene) and engaging. The main "antagonist" of the game definitely makes up for a lot. It's way better than Man of Medan and Little Hope, that's for sure.Long story short, the game is good. For your wallet, wait for a sale. It's not worth full price.Until Dawn is essentially just a better version of this game. Cheaper, better antagonist, better characters. The characters in this are awful compared to Until Dawn and House of Ashes. I really didn't care if a single one died. In fact, the best characters are the two you first meet right at the start. Best part, you barely even get to see them the whole game. They aren't directly awful, they're just very typical teenage counselors. That's the idea though, right? Unlike Until Dawn, these characters never progress. They're all the same miserable characters at the start as they are at the end. For how much they put into this game, it's disappointing. In general, it's good for what it is. Still some fun outcomes in the game and definitely worth it if you love games of a similar genre

_childDocuments_.review: Look, I really like this game.It has an intriguing story, with genuinely compelling characters.I like the setting, and just can't get over the fact that there are over 160 endings.My only problem with this game is that Supermassive 100% needs to somehow add incentive to playing this game more. I would love a feature like Until Dawn, where we have a personality meter for each of the characters. If they wanted, Supermassive could add a DLC where there are a broader range of decisions, but the ones offered to you are solely based off of the personality that you have grown that specific character to have. Something like that would definitely spiral me down to many hours into this game.To re-iterate what I was trying to say before, there is simply no replay-ability. And this is really the only thing that makes me not want to recommend this. I love the game, which is why I overall am giving a thumbs up, but I think a 12 hour campaign can sometimes just not be worth 60 bucks. I think I will continue to replay the game several times, but I really believe that if there can be some type of incentive to make us CONTINUE to play the game even after the first playthrough, I can truly, genuinely tell people that they should buy it, not just if it's their type of game.

There is no way to skip or fast-forward cut scenes without using cheat software and no way to go back if you make a mistake or miss collecting an item. You have to start all over which is ridiculous. The game is so long and many parts are painfully boring. _childDocuments_.review: We've recently started playing The Quarry, and I have to say, it's been an absolute hit with my family. We're about halfway through, and every session has been filled with excitement, suspense, and a good dose of laughter.The best way to experience this game is definitely through couch co-op. The decision-making process becomes a communal event, with everyone chiming in on what to do next, leading to some heated debates and hilarious moments. The game's narrative-driven approach and branching storylines keep everyone engaged, making it feel more like an interactive movie night than a traditional gaming session.The graphics and atmosphere are top-notch, drawing us into the eerie setting of Hackett's Quarry. The characters are well-developed, and we've grown quite attached to some of them (while others... well, let's just say we're not too upset if they meet a grisly end).Overall, The Quarry has become a beloved game in our household. If you're looking for a game that brings people together and provides an unforgettable shared experience, this is it. We can't wait to see how the story unfolds and what other surprises are in store! Looking forward to try Dark Pictures Anthology, since it has couch co-op too!

_childDocuments_.review: Perfect interactive spooky game for spooky season. Play with a friend (or 4) and buckle up for a fun mystery horror experience. My only neg on this game is that - like other Supermassive joints - this game really amplifies the "oh woops that was a mistake my bad, well they're dead" feel in the latter half of the game.It's a slow burn and I take the good with the bad, but at some points it does feel like the game is intentionally withholding camera angles or other dialog info to set you up to have a character die. If you've played some of The Dark Pictures Anthology games, you'll probably know what I mean - the stakes just get really high towards the end.For that reason and pretty much only that reason, I give this game a very solid 9/10. I will be revisiting this next year to try and get a different outcome - the replayability is certainly here!

_childDocuments_.review: The Good - I'm a huge Friday the 13th fan so the "teens stuck at summer camp" is right up my alley. The characters are the usual mix of ones you will love and ones you can't wait for a reason to find to kill off. There is an actual threat here (unlike Man of Medan) so the stakes are high. The game is beautiful and definitely Supermassive's best looking yet. The soundtrack is also fantastic and sets a good mood. Voice acting is top notch despite some cringey comebacks from a particular character but otherwise watching excellent voicelines match up with probably the best facial expressions you've seen in a game is amazing. The game seems to grab an 80's vibe despite the current day setting. The tutorial videos are also a real treat. Scene selection is back once you complete the game once.The Bad - Supermassive seems to keep trying to revolutionize things from previous games that simply just aren't broken. These games are all designed to be played through multiple times, so why on earth they removed the ability to skip scenes is well beyond me. Chapter 7 in particular is painful to replay multiple times. On this note there are at times VERY long times between when players actually make inputs in the game. This game more than all the others is more of an interactive movie than a game. QTE events have been dumbed down to mainly simple directional presses, but this may be a plus for many people. The biggest offender for me though was the removal of a collectable tracker from the main menu. This has existed in every other game. So, if you are a completionist and want to collect everything, you are gonna have to do it in one run, as collectables don't carry between runs either. In closing I'll give The Quarry 7/10. It's definitely fun and tense to play at least once and some of my complaints may not matter to many people. To this date Until Dawn remains my favorite from this dev but why they try so hard to deviate from it is something I just don't understand. I'd rank Supermassive's games as follows.Until DawnHouse of AshesThe QuarryMan of MedanLittle Hope

_childDocuments_.review: Title: The Quarry: A Compelling Single-Player Adventure with Disappointing Co-opRating: ★★★☆☆ (3/5)Review:The Quarry is an intriguing game that combines a compelling single-player story with an unfortunate lackluster co-op experience. With its engaging narrative and immersive gameplay, the single-player mode offers an enjoyable adventure. However, the co-op mode falls short, limiting the second player's involvement and failing to deliver a satisfying cooperative experience.In the single-player mode, The Quarry shines with its captivating story. Players embark on a personal journey, exploring the mysteries of a quarry and unraveling its secrets. The narrative is thoughtfully crafted, drawing players into a world filled with intriguing characters and thought-provoking scenarios. The game successfully immerses players in its atmospheric environments, creating a sense of discovery and immersion throughout the experience.Gameplay mechanics in the single-player mode are well-executed, providing a mix of exploration, puzzle-solving, and decision-making. The Quarry presents players with choices that shape the outcome of the story, allowing for a sense of agency and personal investment. The puzzles are cleverly designed, offering satisfying challenges that keep players engaged and motivated to progress further. The gameplay mechanics are intuitive, making it accessible to a wide range of players.However, the co-op mode of The Quarry fails to live up to expectations. While having a second player in co-op can enhance the experience in certain games, here it feels limited and underutilized. The second player's role is reduced to simply assisting the primary player in selecting options and making decisions. They have no direct control over characters or significant impact on the gameplay. This lack of meaningful interaction diminishes the potential enjoyment and cooperative aspect of the game, leaving co-op players feeling disconnected and unfulfilled.On the technical side, The Quarry presents visually pleasing graphics that enhance the overall atmosphere of the game. The art style and environmental design create a distinct and immersive world. The sound design complements the visuals, effectively setting the tone and adding depth to the player's experience.Despite its shortcomings in co-op, The Quarry's strengths lie in its single-player mode and engaging narrative. The well-crafted story, immersive gameplay, and intriguing puzzles make it a worthwhile experience for players who enjoy story-driven adventures. However, for those seeking a robust and satisfying co-op experience, The Quarry may not meet expectations, earning it a rating of 3/5.In conclusion, The Quarry offers a compelling single-player adventure with a captivating story and immersive gameplay. While the co-op mode falls short in providing meaningful player engagement, the game still manages to deliver an enjoyable experience for those who appreciate narrative-driven gameplay. It's worth exploring The Quarry for its solo experience, but players should be aware of the limitations of its co-op mode.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for October 2023, and this is part of my coverage of the bundle. If you are interested in the game and it's before November 7th, 2023, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.A Slasher movie which is also a game. The Quarry is a spiritual successor to their biggest game, Until Dawn.  This screams slasher movie, and while I always say I’m a scaredy cat for horror, this is great.  There’s so much atmospheric pressure here, amazing use of lighting, and a few moments where the game had me on edge, but I was enthralled with it rather than scared or bored.That being said.  This is still a Supermassive Game, by that I mean it’s a game where players are going to be making choices rather than directly playing the game.  QTEs rear their ugly head, and passing or failing them can change the story.  Some of the writing is a little cornball, it’s a slasher-type movie after all, and there’s a mode that doesn’t require any input, called movie mode, where you can choose the outcome before you start the game.  You don’t even have to play the game the first time to watch it.  Odd. Though this is a game where choices matter, at least enough choices that you’ll be able to potentially replay it if you want to.  Everything appears to be well done, with great acting so far, and one thing I always forget to mention on their games is you can play this multiplayer, at least local multiplayer this time, or just watch someone else play it. Though this is more intended to be a movie with minimal interaction, than a game with a movie presentation.Pick this up if you like slasher movies, horror movies, Supermassive games, or just want a unique story-driven experience.  There are a lot of intense moments with this title, but there hasn’t been too much pure terror yet, to the point that I’m honestly going to play through this one, and I don’t play any horror titles.  Maybe a bad sign for the game, but good for me. Though who knows what will happen after a little more runtime.If you enjoyed this review or want to know what I think of other games in the bundle, check out the full review on or subscribe to my Youtube channel:

For example the QTE's are entirely used with the analog stick if you're on controller, and frankly unless I was distracted the QTE's were extremely easy in comparison to past games.Characters are deep and most of them are likeable but of course that also has to do on how you play them, this game iv very true to that. I've only played through once though so I am excited to play again to see other small outcomes.The setting is very nice, it's full of chessy horror vibes and tropes and has plenty of references to other horror material. t's pretty aware of the cliches and tropes on purpose as you would expect from these games, and they play into them in a fun way and the characters do a lot of fun things to surprise you.I'm not super great at this kind of thing but if you're thinking about buying the game and want a worthy successor to Until Dawn, in my opinion, look no further. _childDocuments_.review: I streamed The Quarry  on my Twitch channel, and I think it's a great game to stream. I would similarly recommend it for friends and family who want to spend time together watching and interacting with a movie-like game as a shared experience. Take turns each chapter for who controls the Quick-Time events, and make decisions together when there's not a timed choice (or come up with your own way to play).In either case, treat it like a watch party, and be mindful of Quick-Time Events - on my first playthough, i often missed choices and chances as i fixated too much on my community chat !!As for the story, the characters are delightful - 'trope'-y in all the right ways, with unique and human details. If you like campy horror, this is for you - fans of American Horror Story's blend of comedy and horror will feel at-home here. The voice acting is top-notch, and the plot turns feel very good. There is a small dip about 2/3rds of the way through as we go into a flashback sequence, but other than that, the game is rock-solid for the majority of its reach, and very replayable. You will enjoy it more to make mistakes and see where your own decisions lead you, I promise !!Personally, I'll give this game a 92/100. It has an excellent story, delicious voice acting, good twists, a fair dose of tension, and is enjoyable right out of the box. I'm knocking points for the post-game evidence score system, an unintuitive puzzle  and sluggish walkaround sections. Highly recommended, and I'll look forward to more by this developer if they keep this style of play.

_childDocuments_.review: The Quarry splits into ten chapters lasting about an hour each, totaling 10 hours of playtime for a single playthrough. Considering the game's structure, all its game modes, and collectibles, it's required but not necessary to complete it several times unless you want to experience everything the game offers. Depending on the circumstances, you're looking at up to 40 hours of playtime to go through everything the game offers.I'd describe the gameplay of The Quarry as an interactive feature film, which it does brilliantly. You control nine teenagers, each different from one another. The game presents you with meaningful quick time events either limited by time or presented by choice, and each of them shapes up the destiny of characters, with brief world explorations on the side to set up what follows in the story. Outside the QTEs, there's not much on offer besides a few interactive collectibles here and there that go along with the story itself. So, roaming around and interacting with infinite useless things is out of the question. The stuff you interact with outside of the main 'do or die' and 'this or that' events isn't overwhelming and adds meaningful detail to the story piece by piece as a puzzle.What matters the most is the interaction between the characters and their relationships, but not to the extent you might think. I wish the interactive object markers were more prominent, as they're weirdly rising from the ground the closer you get, meaning that you'll miss them unless you're looking at the floor to spot them at times due to the game's viewport cut-off by black bars at the top and bottom. The letterboxed perspective adds to the immersion, but the cut-off only makes sense during cutscenes. During gameplay, it's more of a distraction and a pain to deal with in some chapters. The user interface is nicely designed and fits together with the rest.Let's first start with the bad. The motion blur in this game is horrendous, but there's a mod to force it off. The temporal anti-aliasing the game uses doesn't fare any better, and it leads to the constant shimmering of small objects and certain things like tree leaves disappearing as the camera moves away due to softening. The characters' hair breaks up constantly during close-ups, even at 4K resolution. Water splashes and fire effects run at bizarrely low framerate compared to the rest of the presentation. Certain characters look high at times, exhibiting weird eyelids and eye movements. Some textures are low in resolution, and generally, the high-quality characters look out of place at times as the rest of the presentation doesn't match in quality. For example, the clouds and the moon look like a flat texture glued to the sky, and the rocky terrain and some other environment pieces generally look out of place and unfitting with the rest. The indoor scenes are much better.Thankfully, depth of field and the darkness mask this very well, so the lack of detail is evident only when the camera pans around the world. As for the rest of the presentation, the lighting is generally okay, and the atmosphere matches what the director had in mind and wanted to get across. The soundtrack's few licensed tracks fit the narrative, and the sound design, in general, is more than decent. Considering this is an interactive movie, it plays like it and delivers on the premise of a feature film, both visually and auditory speaking. The voice acting and motion capture are great, though, as mentioned, there are some questionable animations. In the end, it's a very dark game, so it's hard to make out all these details but they're worth mentioning.Set in the remote summer camp of Hackett's Quarry, the story revolves around a group of teenage counselors who decide to throw a final party on their last night at camp. However, their celebration quickly turns into a night of horror as they find themselves hunted by bloodthirsty locals and something far more sinister. The game blends traditional horror elements with modern storytelling, where every decision matters, and this pretty much sums it up. I thoroughly enjoyed the story, mostly because I love these stupid horror movies where the characters spit cringe dialogue and get picked off one by one in the most outlandish ways possible. That's not exactly the case here, as you're in control and ultimately decide the fate and the conversation between the characters, but you get the point. The characters you play with can make both stupid and good choices based on your input, meaning that you're the one deciding the faith of each of them, and it's what makes it so enjoyable for me. The podcast thing is also a great idea. The ending felt satisfying, and the whole story is tied up neatly outside of a few loose ends.The game is powered by Unreal Engine 4, alright? As expected, the game suffers heavily from stutters and inconsistent frame times, the same issues many other UE4 games do, including The Dark Pictures Anthology series, developed by Supermassive Games. Each scene cut introduces a stutter, and each new thing loading in introduces a stutter. Basically, whatever the game does introduces a brief stutter. It's much less noticeable playing with a gamepad as opposed to a keyboard and a mouse, and certain display technologies help with this, but it's a constant stutter-fest. As with many UE4-powered games, the graphics settings are bare bones, meaning you don't have much control over anything the game does visually besides the generic UE4 options. At least the loading times are fast, but for the visuals it outputs, it doesn't justify the hardware demand.The Quarry is a less ambitious version of Until Dawn that anyone who likes an interactive narrative experience will enjoy and appreciate regardless. Outside a few performance and technical issues, it's a decent horror experience that gets more interesting with each chapter.

_childDocuments_.review: This is by far my favorite game from this company! Until Dawn was incredible when it was released (not a perfect game, but definitely deserved it's time in the sun- and in my opinion, still holds up) so they had some large shoes to fill when they released The Quarry- and I definitely think they succeeded.I'll be honest, I'm not a huge fan of the Dark Pictures Anthology games. I think most of them feel half hearted, and the majority of the characters are either so unlikable I'm relieved when they die, or just fall flat in a way that leaves me extremely detached from the plot. The Quarry, however, is rich with a lovable, diverse cast of characters that, while playing on classic horror movie tropes, still manage to feel like whole people with complexities of their own. As a fan of the era of 80's slasher horror movies, this game hits the nail right on the head. The perfect blend of cliches while still managing to incorporate effective jump-scares and a building feeling of suspense and dread that makes the high stakes really feel like high stakes. They really captured the "bunch of young adults working at a summer camp having on last fun fling" that the 80s slasher genre perfected. The music is excellent, the camera angles (though some can be a bit frustrating to navigate at times) really make it feel like the counselors are being watched, and the lighting and ambiance fully complete the atmosphere of horror surrounding the story. Most importantly, the choices feel like choices. There are clear consequences throughout the entire story that call back to choices you made earlier on. While some might find it frustrating that choices you make earlier in the story can screw you over in the end, I find that stays really true to the nature of the "butterfly effect" style of story telling these games aim to capture. Even better, if you make a wrong choice, there are opportunities in the future to rectify the wrong choice and put you back on the better path. All in all, I love this game. It's not perfect, sure, but it's effective and entertaining, and I will be replaying it again and again. Fans of 80s slasher horror and fans of supernatural horror alike will adore this game. Bonus shout out to Murph and Emily for being the podcasters in this game, I've never been more delighted by a cameo in a video game. Great game with replay value and a truly cinematic experience!

_childDocuments_.review: Unsatisfying story, more movie than game, lame decisions, replayability, control input and the ending...Positive things: the actors, voices and setting. (Though the setting does have a lot of similarities to Until Dawn)There was so much wasted potential here. So first, unsatisfying story: the game is making fun of itself from the beginning, which was a good thing. Tackling cliches makes it ok this way. Even the characters make jokes about being in a horror piece in the first part.. but then they go and make the weirdest choices: running around a forest half naked, splitting up, not grabbing weapons or letting themselves get caught. It's frustrating in movies already but in a game it gets unbearable. More movie than game: they should have just made a movie with this cast. I think 3/4 of the experience is watching cutscenes. You get some choices (always a or b, live or die (now or later)) but I never felt like the choices played out as I hoped they would. Which just gets frustrating in a game. In a movie you don't give any input but this happening in a game just makes it feel lame. They add a limited rewind option after the first playthrough.. why not in the original game. I noticed it even saves directly after making a choice, this isn't Dark Souls you know?When you finally do get a playable part, it's a very bland walking simulator where you move from a to b and hope to get some clues before accidentally triggering the next cutscene making the previous part inaccessible.Replayability: yes, you can replay it but small things like not being able to skip or speed up cutscenes make me do not want to replay it. Sure, I'd like to see how some choices played out if I picked b instead of a but I don't want to redo entire chapters for that. And even then I'm not sure how some decisions affected others. The paths are some help but if you look to a game like Detroit, well there's just no comparison here.They tarot card system was also just clunky. I explored everything and still I ended up missing a lot but they also felt really worthless. Who doesn't pick show more in the cabin? Why can you only see one card? Why is the text more helpfull than the cutscene..Control input: there have been so many games already with cool quick time events but this game, seriously wtf? Hold A until the red light is gone, mash A a few times, flick joystick in a (most of the time random) direction.. They've done games before with better input, how did this get through? The interrupts were a nice addition but most of the time you knew they were negative. Adding more of these could add some cool different paths but I think they'd probably just add more negative ones.Ending: trying to stay away from spoilers here but it was very abrupt, felt like once again an A or B choice, some characters start showing trust issues toward each other at random points, forgetting someone just murdered everyone you love, almost everyone is scattered and the epilogue.. that's not a story round up, a kill cam would have been better than this. They should have put more time in this instead of adding overlay filters.I liked Until Dawn but upon seeing this ending I remembered why I only played it once. This will also remain just a single playthrough. I really hope I read this review again before ever buying another of their games.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game overall, less of a successor to Until Dawn and more of a loose reinterpretation of the story in a different format (this time at a summer camp). As mentioned before, the game definitely fizzles out in the last couple of chapters, but after having a few days to process the entirety of the game I'm still very glad I played it.One piece of advice - plan to have two playthroughs of the game, one where you blindly make decisions that seem entertaining or fit your personality, and a second where you use a walkthrough to discover all Clues/Evidence and to chart out the path to the "ideal" ending. Note that there is not really a "true ending" in the sense of winning the game, there is just a secret cutscene towards the end that gives some closure to the full story. I unlocked the "true" ending my first playthrough and was pretty frustrated to learn that was indeed the "secret ending". As I mentioned earlier, the ending is somewhat unrewarding, but I think the journey up to the end still makes this game worth playing.A few pros and cons:Pros:-Worthwhile story that doesn't leave too many loose ends or introduce too many plot holes-Characters have enough moments (either solo or in groups) that make them endearing and makes you want to save them-Some good plot twists that kept me wanting to see the next chapter-Clues & evidence are very fun to track down - there is also a system where some clues have hidden info that are unlocked later in the game as other clues are found. Loved that system.-The music and audio in general is phenomenal. Team clearly had a big budget for music, and it really enhances the whole idea of "playing a movie". The Ariana Grande song that plays in the trailer still gets stuck in my head from time to time.-The end credits scene is actually very fun, and encourages you to collect as much evidence as possible. I absolutely agree that the ending was unfulfilling, but this specific part of the ending was pretty fun (though even this part feels somewhat rushed)-There are quite a few hidden scenes and paths that mean your decisions truly do matter - and not just in the "make the right decision or get a Game Over" vein of punishing players, but in a way that truly sets up a branching narrative. There is an achievement for having all of the counselors die in a single playthrough, and it is fun that the game actually gives you new pieces of dialogue or scenes rather than just removing the parts that dead characters would have been in.-I did not play couch co-op, but have heard it is a fantastic experience if you have a group of close friends or a significant other with whom you can commit 10 or so hours within the span of a week or a weekend. This game thrives on plot twists, character development, and corny humor that is best appreciated in a social setting. Some of the horror movie tropes they play on are pretty great - worth mentioning this game is pretty hilarious at some points, which is always a great complement to a horror game. (Though I would almost call this a thriller more than a horror game, especially in the second half once the premise has been fully revealed)Cons:-First playthrough was 8.5 hours, and to be honest I would have been fine without a second playthrough (I thought there was a "true ending" I hadn't unlocked, assuming that is why the ending was so barren). Don't get me wrong, I don't need every game to take 50 hours, but it wasn't just that I beat the game quickly, it was an experience that felt cut short. Feels like they were missing two or three chapters towards the end.-On a similar note, there are some pretty rough edges to this game. I get the impression they had to rush a lot of the ending of this game, and it shows narratively as well as some of the dialogue throughout the game. The graphics are pretty poor in some parts as well; for instance water splashing looks god awful despite me running the game on pretty high graphical quality.-While I do appreciate how well this story sets up a cohesive branching narrative, there are definitely some times where the outcome of your decisions feels unfair and a little bit railroaded. And as I've mentioned before, this is only exacerbated down the end of the game.Overall, I enjoyed the vibes, the characters, and the journey on which the story took me, even if I was a little let down by the ending. As other reviewers have mentioned, this is probably a game worth buying at $30 or lower, so keep an eye out for a sale. If you haven't already played Until Dawn, buy it first and see if you enjoy this style of game - if you enjoy Until Dawn, I guarantee you'll enjoy The Quarry.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me just start off by saying that I absolutely loved this game (I'm already on my third playthrough), along with pretty much every game supermassive has put out. I adore the concept of games where your choices matter, specifically in horror/thriller genres and I do wish there were more games out there like this.The Quarry was absolutely genius. Although a lot want to compare it to Until Dawn, saying that Until Dawn is better, I completely disagree. However, I can see why the comparisons are made. Many of the mechanics, along with scenes in the early chapters of the game are extremely reminiscent of Until Dawn. I'm assuming that most of these were intentional, seeing as how the developers decided to flip everything you thought you knew on its head.What I like about this game is how unpredictable it is at time. The game seems to heavily focus on the concept of "Not everything is what it seems". Sure, the game may have its moments where you can see coming, but the other moments I was genuinely surprised once the story starts to come together. I really do love the fact that the game plays off of something seeming so obvious in the developer's intentions, only for it to be flipped completely on its head later on in the game. It genuinely did keep me on my toes.The characters:Compared to Until Dawn, I genuinely found myself liking a lot more of the characters, whereas many of them in Until Dawn felt bland, thrown aside (Jessica), or simply unlikable. Although there are certain characters many find unlikable in this, all have their charm. They each have enough personality to where the exposition dialogues and cut scenes are entertaining just by how humorous the dialogue is. Many of them, however, are based off of cliche stereotypes, which I find fits perfectly for the setting of the game, especially since it has the theme of being an 80s slasher styled horror movie. The Quarry played off of these cliches, giving them their own little special twist to keep the player engaged.The choices:Another main portion of this game is the choices. Although, a lot are saying that choices matter far less than Until Dawn (Especially the deaths), I completely disagree with this. However, a lot of the choices in this game are by far a lot more unforgiving than the ones in other games, like dark pictures. Many of the choices can end up being fatal, which makes the game very intense, especially on the first play through. Although there are some choices that seemingly have less of an impact than others, overall the outcome of pretty much everything is based on the choices you make.The mechanics:The mechanics of this game weren't anything groundbreaking, they were all simple but utilized well. Of course, the QTEs came back, which I do like that you're able to change the length of them (Although I wish you could make them a lot shorter than the shortest option). The rest of the mechanics, such as the don't breath and combat mechanics are simple yet have a lot of versatility and impact on the game despite their simplicity. At first I thought the don't breath mechanic was repetitive and all the same, however, it starts to change leading to the end of the game, which was a pleasant surprise.The story:Personally, I found the backstory of the game to be far more consistent than Until Dawn. Sure, the second half of the Quarry has a lot more impact on the status of your characters than the first half, however, there's a nice connection between all points of the game where the story is progressed to make an engaging progression of events for the player. The story, although seemingly predictable, is filled with twists and engaging plot points. However, to understand a variety of the backstory, including how all of the events are connected, the player has to collect clues around the map, making exploring worthwhile. (Also, I personally like these monsters better than Until Dawn, they're a lot more threatening) My only problem with this game was a lack of a ending sequence like Until Dawn had.As for the price. Can't we agree that most games are too expensive at this point? I'd recommend waiting for a sale unless you're a feral supermassive game fans like I am.

There seemed to be little point in finding and collecting the cards and evidence. There was never any clear tie back to the story or outcome. _childDocuments_.review: I’m not sure if The Quarry is a very good game since it is so cutscene heavy and has very basic gameplay, but it is a fun experience, so I’m still going to go ahead and recommend it. Much of your time in this game is sitting back and watching a cutscene play out. Occasionally you will get a dialog choice or a very easy quick time event that supposedly changes the way the story plays out, but there have been a number of times where it felt like my choice didn’t actually matter, so I do wonder how differently this game can really play out. In addition to this, there are times when you get to control a character, walking them around, searching for clues, evidence, and tarot cards, which are like this games version of collectibles.While there are enough of these interactive segments to keep me engaged, there were many times when I wondered if this would have been better as a mini series on a streaming platform. You would lose the interactivity, but seeing how little there is and how much of the interactivity is just basic button presses, I’m not sure how much would be lost other than the dialog choices. The story is good enough to stand on its own. Don’t get me wrong, I really like games with dialog choices that matter and change the narrative, I’m just not sure how much the choices actually matter in this game since several of mine really felt like they did not matter.Something that has to be said is that on a technical level, this game is a mess. While I can’t say I have any major performance issues and the game does look pretty good, the game also renders with thick black bars on all 4 sides of my screen, so It’s only using maybe 75% of my screen. The segments where you control a character often have awkward controls and always have a heavy motion blur and mouse acceleration that both seem to be forced on. Furthermore, I tried remapping some of the controls and it just doesn't do anything. The button prompts still show me the default inputs and my newly mapped buttons do not work. The game also does not support Steam Cloud, so you’ll need to manually back up your saves if you want to use multiple devices or protect against your computer’s drive dying.

_childDocuments_.review: Well... I finished the game. I've gone back and looked at the negative reviews and have to say I agree with most of them. This is my first foray into movie-like horror genre (as opposed to like, first person where it's all jump scares), so for me the game was "OK". But after reading comparisons to some other titles, I suspect it's the novelty that worked for me. The "low points" I concur with in the other bad reviews:1. the mouth / dialogue sync-up is. truly. *awful*. The characters look like grotesque meat puppets and their mouth animations (especially Emma's) are just terrible. 2. there's not a lot of "choice" going on. it's mostly cinematics, which was OK for me but others may be looking for more actual "gameplay". What gameplay there was could be a bit janky. I had to blow a couple of my 3 "free lives" just because aiming and firing a shotgun is so horribad.3. The story is pretty bad, character development and relationship development is completely missing. Another reviewer talked about how so many things are left unresolved in the end (do the "star crossed lovers" end up reuniting, etc.) - none of it. There's no "closure" to anything.4. The spyware/malware 2k launcher and ToA. Capitalism at its worst. Stop selling me.So, yeah, I'm ok that I paid $15 to watch a bad, 4-movie series (let's be honest, most camp/slasher movies are pretty bad to begin with). As a game? Not so great. Other reviews here call out other games you might want to look at first, as I said this is my first foray into this specific genre, so I can't comment there. I do know that if I'd paid full price I'd probably be kicking myself.Edit: I find myself now watching movie mode. I changed my review from negative to positive, because, honestly, it was entertaining enough at a really basic level to get me all the way through it without bailing out. So, yeah. Just be aware of the limitations and then decide for yourself. Again, $15 yes. $60 helllllll no. I'll prolly go through it just to see how horribly and quickly I can kill everyone off. So yeah. replayability. lol.BTW, there was one strong point to the whole mess: Siobhan Williams. Whoever is out there, she needs more work.

_childDocuments_.review: Spoilers to followThe quarry has a somewhat strong start, it introduces a cliched cast of characters but they are just interesting enough to make the tense moments in the first half of the game pretty engaging. The initial run-ins with the monsters give you some choices that 'feel' meaningful, but I suppose I'd have to play the game twice to truly know if they were or not.Then the issues start showing up. Character inconsistencies become glaringly bad. The nerdy guy who is into cryptid podcasts at the beginning of the game is suddenly a skeptic who refuses to believe even when confronted by actual monsters for example. A character gets his hand amputated by a chainsaw and people tease him about it fifteen minutes later. The tone is absolutely bizarre. Then the game goes to ♥♥♥♥. Just as the pacing is ramping up and the game is getting intense at the halfway point, we are re-introduced to a character from the prologue, and dragged into a 2+ hour flashback sequence that builds backstory we already could have inferred from the main plot. This character, who we really had no reason to care about for the first half of the game, then takes center stage and becomes the main protagonist. She's also inexplicably a badass. She shoes up acting like sarah connor, and you assume she has been a monster hunter for months now or something, but the flashback reveals, no she actually has less experience dealing with the monsters than the main cast. The pacing remains wildly inconsistent until the game abruptly ends, right after the narrator injects herself into the story, further shattering 4th wall, and the game tries to make you feel bad for the original monster, who has had no character development anyway. All of the character subplots developed in the first half are left completely unexplored and unresolved. They clearly just ran out of time or money and pushed the game out the door without wrapping it up. By the end, my girlfriend was recommending we just read a wikipedia to see how it ends rather than suffer through any more tedium.

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked Supermassive's previous games or games from developers like Telltale, Quantic Dream, Don't Nod/Deck Nine(Life is Strange), you will probably like this game depending on what you want out of the experience, primarily the narrative and storytelling. The Quarry takes a lot of things from one of Supermassive's previous games, Until Dawn. The use of certain tropes and themes, the general tone and setup, several story beats and character relationships, etc. This is clearly a spiritual successor in some sense. Personally, I thought Supermassive did a much better job giving most if not all of the characters opportunities to become appealing to the player in comparison to Until Dawn thus making their well-being more of a priority for players. One or two characters main characters don't seem to get much attention in the scheme of the overall story, but more of an attempt was made to give them some compelling character traits in comparison to several characters from Until Dawn from my experience. Given it is a spiritual successor to Until Dawn and that approach to storytelling, don't expect a very deep story or anything where characters will truly develop beyond their general archetype or personality. That isn't to say there aren't good character moments though. I felt myself become pretty invested early on in several characters and character relationships. One thing Until Dawn did better was the handling of endings. Given the nature of games like this, there are lots of different outcomes for each character and how their relationships unfold with others. It can be difficult to craft entire cutscenes to account for all the different permutations. In Until Dawn, the credit sequence had any of the surviving characters in the playthrough talking about the events of the game and it was framed as a police interrogation after the events of the game. The characters would mention certain choices based on player's decisions, various clues the player found to unmask the mystery, their relationships with other characters whether positive or negative based on the player's choices, etc. The Quarry makes no attempt to do any of this. The ending sequence just has the camera pan to the characters and denote if they survived and a short description of their status, but nothing beyond that. The game doesn't make an attempt to address character relationships or anything like Until Dawn. You can have a character kiss another character, the game will pop up text saying, "X is starting to like you" and nothing becomes of it. The credit sequence doesn't feature any of the characters. Instead, an in-universe podcast referenced throughout the game recalls the events of the game as they are anonymously sent clues depending on which clues the player finds throughout the playthrough. I really wish the credit sequence actually featured the characters and gave better insight into what happens to the characters following the events of the game, at least copying exactly what Until Dawn did would've been a major improvement. On a slightly related note, the last few chapters feel a bit rushed towards the conclusion, the game could've used maybe 2 more chapters to really flesh out a few things and give a few characters more things to do during the climax and conclusion. Also, one chapter is almost entirely a flashback which slows the pacing to a halt. It is framed as a character telling other characters a story and is handled in an interesting way since they do sometimes return to the characters in present day hearing the story. But, I wish they added other events outside the flashback during that chapter to help balance the pacing. The game isn't perfect by any means, but I enjoyed it and it felt like it was a few steps short of being incredible.

_childDocuments_.review:
As the sun sets on the last day of summer camp, the teenage counselors of Hackett's Quarry throw a party to celebrate. No kids. No adults. No rules. Things quickly take a turn for the worse. Hunted by blood-drenched locals and something far more sinister, the teens' party plans unravel into an unpredictable night of horror. Friendly banter and flirtations give way to life-or-death decisions, as relationships build or break under the strain of unimaginable choices.

Play as each of the nine camp counselors in a thrilling cinematic tale, where every decision shapes your unique story from a tangled web of possibilities. Any character can be the star of the showor die before daylight comes.

How will your story unfold?

YOUR STORY, THEIR FATE
Will you dare to check what's behind that trap door? Will you investigate the screams echoing from within the forest? Will you save your friends or desperately run for your life? Every choice, big or small, shapes your story and determines who lives to tell the tale.

A STUNNING CINEMATIC EXPERIENCE
Cutting edge facial capture and filmic lighting techniques, combined with incredible performances from an iconic ensemble cast of Hollywood talent, bring the horrors of Hackett's Quarry to life in a pulse-pounding, cinematic thrill ride.

ENJOY THE FRIGHT WITH FRIENDS
Place your faith in up to 7 friends in online play, where invited players watch along and vote on key decisions, creating a story shaped by the whole group! Or, play together in a party horror couch co-op experience where each player picks a counselor and controls their actions.

CUSTOMIZE YOUR EXPERIENCE
Adjustable difficulty for all gameplay elements let players of any skill level enjoy the horror. And if you prefer to watch rather than play, Movie Mode lets you enjoy The Quarry as a binge-worthy cinematic thriller. Select how you want the story to unfold, kick back, and munch on some popcorn in between all the screams!

name: The Chant
detailed_description: A SPIRITUAL NIGHTMARE A single-player, third person horror action-adventure game set on a remote island spiritual retreat. A peaceful weekend soon turns to dread after a group chant opens The Gloom, a psychedelic dimension of terror that feeds off negative energy. Interact with a recurring cast of characters, untangle the complex history of the island, and witness terrifying revelations about the cosmos. Only you can fight off the creatures, reason with the survivors, and unravel the legacy of a cult from the 1970s to reverse the ritual. EXPLORE AN ISLAND FILLED WITH COSMIC DREAD Interact with the other members of the retreat as they slowly become consumed by their own negative energy. Survive against an array of prismatic creatures and cultists released from The Gloom as you piece together the weird history of the island. FIGHT OR FLIGHT You must choose your fights and battle for survival with spiritual weapons and abilities. Collect, craft, and manage your resources to take your chances in close combat - or succumb to panic and flee. MIND BODY SPIRIT Balance is everything. Steel your mind against horror and panic; Protect your body against physical threats; Elevate your spirit to meditate and access supernatural abilities. MODERN PSYCHEDELIC HORROR Inspired by the psychedelic horror of the 1970s, experience a landscape of colored lighting and an electronic rock soundtrack, composed by the award-winning Paul Ruskay. STARRING • Siobhan Williams, starring as Jess • Kira Clavell, Starring as Kim • Nicole Anthony, starring as Maya • Praneet Akilla, starring as Sonny • Emily Tennant, starring as Hannah • Adam Millard starring as Tyler
