Survive against an array of prismatic creatures and cultists released from The Gloom as you piece together the weird history of the island. FIGHT OR FLIGHT You must choose your fights and battle for survival with spiritual weapons and abilities. Collect, craft, and manage your resources to take your chances in close combat - or succumb to panic and flee. MIND BODY SPIRIT Balance is everything. Steel your mind against horror and panic; Protect your body against physical threats; Elevate your spirit to meditate and access supernatural abilities. MODERN PSYCHEDELIC HORROR Inspired by the psychedelic horror of the 1970s, experience a landscape of colored lighting and an electronic rock soundtrack, composed by the award-winning Paul Ruskay. STARRING • Siobhan Williams, starring as Jess • Kira Clavell, Starring as Kim • Nicole Anthony, starring as Maya • Praneet Akilla, starring as Sonny • Emily Tennant, starring as Hannah • Adam Millard starring as Tyler
short_description: A single-player, third person horror action-adventure game set on a remote spiritual island retreat. To survive you must craft, fight, and escape the psychedelic horrors set loose when a spiritual ritual goes wrong and awakens a dimension of cosmic terror.

_childDocuments_.review: Protagonist Jess is invited to a spiritual retreat by her friend Kim, in the hopes of recovering from a severe trauma of her past and finding clarity. What initially looks like a new-age, hippie shenanigan soon turns much darker, as ancient and obscure rituals make their way in the commune’s everyday life. Unsurprisingly, fiddling with poorly-understood spirit-channeling crystals isn’t the safest outdoor activity, someone loses composure and everything goes to absolute crap. The idyllic island is transformed into a Stranger Things-esque mish-mash of clashing dimensions, and Jess will have to survive through it.Generally each environment is crafted with care and looks good, however the quality isn’t always consistent. A highlight are the dimensional rifts, each inspired to one of the ritual members’ emotions and past experiences, that truly feel like walking in someone else’s nightmare - while Jess’ own traumas also make their way in. The creatures that roam the island range from quasi-human to completely otherworldly, as the inhabitants of a yet-unknown dimension should be; great job in portraying this difference. Expect a terrifying and mysterious world that changes at every turn.The island is divided in several areas, most of which are locked-out initially, and accessible only when you’ll obtain the correct pendants to cross the color-coded dimensional rifts, or find key items to unlock doors and passages or shortcuts in the “real” world. The layout is semi-open but generally linear, with a main path dotted with small secondary areas that contain lore, additional resources but also more threats at times - there’s no map, some orienteering is needed. Later on fast travel is unlocked but this mechanic feels redundant, as the world isn’t so big and backtracking on foot may lead to additional resources you’d skip with fast travel. In a light survival-horror fashion, inventory is heavily limited in how many resources you’re able to carry, be them crafting implements, weapons or consumables. You may very well have to leave something behind due to the lack of space, but in most cases you’ll be able to go back for it later. Each item has its own category so there’s no need to drop anything to pick something else up, and critical items occupy no space at all either. These items may be combined to solve puzzles, like making an alchemical solution following a recipe or crafting a metal shape to unlock doors, to name a few. There are several puzzles, most of which are unique and well-designed.Jess will have three main attributes: Mind, Body and Spirit that each level up in different ways, and also are drained by diverse factors. For instance, reading lore files will grant Mind points and will be drained inside the alternate dimension, while defeating physical enemies like Cultists will give Body XP as a reward, which is drained by physical pain and leads to death if exhausted. Dialogues also grant small amounts of XP based on your choices. These points are useless on their own, and need Crystals, found in the world, that act as skill points to level-up useful passive skills like damage resistance, stunning enemies on a perfect parry, carrying more consumables and so on. This encourages exploration as the majority of Crystals are hidden out of the main path.Crafting materials, mostly in the form of herbs and solutions, are found all over the world and can be used to craft weapons and consumables. Since all weapons degrade with use, constantly crafting new ones is paramount. There may be a scenario where you’d have to reload a previous save because you simply ran out of everything, but this is only a worst-case scenario unlikely to happen.Combat plays out in third person with mechanics like dodge, pushing and light / heavy attacks as foundations, plus different damage types depending on what weapon or skill you’re using at the moment. All enemies have different attack patterns you’d be wise to learn, and while all attacks stagger them, they’ll retaliate with powerful charged moves if hit repeatedly. All foes are more vulnerable to specific damage types, for instance using a Fire Lash (weapon) on physical foes will inflict bonus damage - but there are also combinations like using Oil + Fire to boost damage even more. Finding and reading the Bestiary entries in the world can give insight on an enemy’s skills and weaknesses to specific combos, further encouraging exploration.Jess may also use her Spirit stat to fuel six different skills, from offensive to defensive ones, that have powerful effects but also a cooldown, like a scream that pushes enemies away for example. Consumables are an important part of combat and they can be set down as traps on the ground or thrown, mostly with utility effects like slow, stun, stagger and such. It’s a pity that most enemies, while damaging, are too slow and that Jess has no stamina or cooldown on dodging, which allows spamming with impunity, making avoiding attacks rather simple.

_childDocuments_.review: is a third-person survival “horror” game where you participate in a ritual that goes horribly wrong, and it is up to you to fix the mess. ✔️ For an indie game, the voice-acting, lip-sync and facial expressions are top notch.✔️ Good visuals and a massive island to explore.✔️ Fun bosses that rely on using your surrounding. ❌ Forgettable storyline and not scary at all.❌ Average gameplay; it’s neither interesting or bad, just “meh”.❌ Spongy final boss.❌ Awful soundtrack. You play as Jess, and you decided to attend a retreat with your friend, Kim, after the death of your sister in order to find closure. You visit a "peaceful" island that is owned by a spiritual leader named Jared Let... I mean Tyler. You will meet other characters on the island who are also trying to cope after experiencing a past traumatic event/loss. Cutting to the chase, you participate in a ritual that goes horribly wrong, and it is up to you to fix the mess (as the owner/leader chickened out, typical). There are three different endings, which depend on the dialogue choices that you pick (they are tied to the three core stats; Mind, Body and Spirit), as well as killing/avoiding specific enemies, picking up lore notes/reels, and meditation. Also no, there are no branching paths and the dialogue choices do not affect the story, just the last 1-2 minutes.The story overall was average, I guess; although the voice-acting is pretty good, as well as the lip sync and facial expressions, the story is not memorable and the game is not at all frightening, thanks to the cheap and sometimes predictable jumpscares. After the failed ritual, a new parasitic dimension is unleashed on the island, known as the Gloom. There are 6 different dimension rifts, and each one can be accessed using a crystal that corresponds to the rift’s color. With the crystals, you can also go back, or fast travel, to previous locations at any time, although I see no use doing that other than finding missed documents. Some of those dimensions can be closed by killing the parasitic flower-looking monster that controls it.You have three stats that you can upgrade as you progress; .  is Jess's mental state, and it slowly decreases inside the gloom and from certain enemy attacks; you'll start to panic when it goes to zero and you won’t be able to fight back.  is your health, and  is used to perform special abilities or meditation (regain mind points when out of the Gloom or not in danger).The combat is similar to , another $40 game that I do not recommend in the slightest. That being said, it is slightly improved here; you can’t stunlock the enemy with multiple attacks, as now they can perform uninterrupted attacks, so you have to dodge to avoid them. The game automatically locks you onto the nearest enemy, making encounters frustrating and infuriating if you are faced with more than one monster.There are three types of melee weapons that you'll unlock, and they can depend on the enemy type and if you are in or out of the Gloom. In addition, throwables and traps can damage enemies over time or temporarily stun them. All weapons and throwables can be crafted using different plants and materials that you can find scattered on the island. There are also types of plants that can be used as consumables to regain Mind, Body (health) and Spirit points.You will fight 6 story bosses, and I liked most of them since they depend on you using your surroundings instead of just spamming the attack button. That being said, the final boss fight was a nuisance; it was spongy and took too damn long (to a point that I was questioning myself whether I was doing it wrong).Other than that, most of the enemies and monsters that you’ll encounter look generic and uninteresting (you’ll fight a giant toad and a massive salamander, how quaint). There are some puzzles in the game, but they are pretty mundane and not at all challenging. Dodging makes you invincible as well, which is pretty useful since I played the game on the hardest difficulty and had to avoid most enemies.The visuals are fine, but not what you would expect in this day and age (looks similar to Dead By Daylight’s visuals), yet the system requirements are quite high (according to them, you need an RTX 3080 to run the game at Epic graphic setting), and there’s no ray-tracing to justify it. Thankfully, DLSS and FSR 2.0 can be enabled. The island is pretty big, filled with documents and film reels that are littered everywhere that tell more about the island and its former and current inhabitants, monsters that want to tear you to shreds (or jumpscare you), and various plants and materials that you can use to craft weapons and throwables.The game worked okay most of the time, but later in the story I experienced major FPS drops and high GPU usage spikes every time I entered the Gloom, and when I looked at certain doors and windows. I encountered a few bugs as well, but nothing game-breaking. It’s bad. I only remember two songs from the intro and first chapter and they were awful; one of which was too bombastic and a total mess (trying to be like Silent Hill's soundtrack, but it just doesn't work at all here), while the other had a weird vibration sound effect that, for a second, I thought came from my phone. I don't know what type of music genre they used and I don’t care; there are 25 other songs and I don’t remember any of them, not even boss fights themes. The game is bland; good voice-acting, fun bosses and okay visuals, but they are accompanied with a forgettable story, mediocre gameplay and an awful soundtrack. It’s one of those games that you’ll completely forget about after the credits roll. Adding insult to injury, this $40 game took me 5 hours to complete. my advice is to save that money and wait for the other six survival horror games that will come out in the following six months.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is way better than it has any right to be. It clearly had a small budget but was made by a team that also clearly had a passion for the project. Play it on the hardest difficulty for a slightly "souls-like" experience which actually requires you to manage your limited resources and choose your fights wisely. Is it a AAA horror game no? Is it a unique horror with aspects rarely covered in horror? Yes.  Is it terrifying? No. But neither are the AAA horrors are they? Does it get you with a few well timed jump scares? Of course! Overall this is a great game to pick up on sale and can be beaten in one or two sittings. Perfect for those of us with less time to play than we'd like.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a bit too short and it kinda suffers for it. Going through the story felt a little rushed and never really gave you time to get to know any of the other characters other than through notes or film reels you find laying around. The game has dialogue choices but there are very few of them and feels like it barely impacts anything including the ending. The endings were abrupt and didn't really make sense based on whatever route you chose.(Mind, Body, Spirit)The combat is very basic with a 3-hit combo attack, dodging and special abilities that use spirit energy. I'm not really counting it as a negative since it's pretty responsive at least, just nothing outstanding is all. My main issue was that I did run out of weapons to fight enemies with sometimes so I ended up running around until they gave up the chase which ruined the tension a lot. The one thing I was impressed by was the very detailed graphics and animations(the dodging animation is really good given the setting of this game) despite this being the developers first game. Personally I thought the game was okay but wished the game gave a little more setup with the main characters and ways to keep the tension high if you happen to run out supplies. I give it a 6/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Cosmic horror, spirituality and new age philosophy meet in the new survival horror / action adventure game  from fledgling studio Brass Token that sees a young woman attend a spiritual retreat in the hopes it will help her deal with her tormented past. This peaceful weekend soon turns to dread after a group chant opens up a portal to a psychedelic dimension of terror known as "The Gloom" that feeds on negative energy. Are you ready to balance your chakras in order to save yourself and the retreats inhabitants? is an enjoyable but flawed experience. Dated graphics and some subpar writing are matched by a pulpy and enjoyable plot that moves at brisk and thrilling pace combined with some truly unique and grotesque enemy designs. Combat is serviceable, if a little clunky, but  has promise thanks to 3 different weapon types with different attacks each matching a particular enemy health bar so you will need to switch in and out depending on the different enemies on the screen at once which adds a nice dynamic feel to the combat. As a first game from Brass Token, it's most certainly a step in the right direction.I had an enjoyable time with the game. In the end I found that despite the many rough edges, it delivered a solid survival horror/action adventure romp and is definitely something I would recommend be played by aficionados of the genre. It exudes great atmosphere, despite the AA level graphics, it has a moody and engaging soundtrack, and while I would be hesitant to call it scary, the various enemies the player must face off with are mostly fun to engage with.

Issues of motion sickness really need additional attention by devs as this will greatly impact sales and reviews.

_childDocuments_.review: Now that I've had some time away and the Dev responded asking for clarification, I wanted to flesh out the review.The game had potential. It feels like a Mass Effect 3 fix could work patching in a "complete" story. But at 40$, even then it wouldn't pass the threshold for recommended due to the shallowness of world the length imposes and I can't base my recommendation on sale prices as those fluctuate and are not always available. I would say this game feels right for 20$ as-is or 25$ with a satisfying story.First, clarification on the endings.So, to work through with Jess to a resolution only to have a rug pulled is what sours the whole the experience retrospectively.Second, the length that even with a fixed ending can't quite justify the full price. I position this game as a more combat-heavy walking simulator. There really aren't puzzles and the combat is more of an obstacle than a feature which makes the story, world, and characters much more paramount to the quality of the game. I love how Jess and the other characters are  as normal characters but we never get a chance to develop any connection to the cast beyond Jess. They have their superficial traits and personalities and that's it. There needs to be 1 or 2 chapters simply dedicated to getting to know them and setting up interpersonal conflicts while getting embedded in Glory Island as a member of the cult. There needed to be more lore items, more backstory, more grounded events.Third, the combat. 80% of the time I didn't care what I had in my hand, it all worked to roughly the same degree. I honestly believe the combat could have been dropped with a focus on environmental play. The possession, candles and mirror encounter was way more interesting than anything that came later. The monsters could have been puzzles rather than enemies.I want to end on what was positive.Most importantly, the Gloom is probably one of the most interesting supernatural ecosystems in any form of media I've seen in a while. I would advise, if possible, to stick with this and expand on it with future developments. .The cast were designed well. They come across as real people, believable in the setting. There was a lot of potential there for an interesting ensemble.Glory Island is fine, and the settings around the island are well designed to feel lived in.

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly have mixed feelings about this. While I enjoyed the journey at the end I was also kind of relieved it was over.First of all I really like the cult setting and the atmosphere this game gives off. Graphics look great too and performance is not an issue at all. Characters are honestly quite forgettable and the story has some weird parts, but is overall enjoyable.My biggest grime with this game is actually the combat. _childDocuments_.review: The Chant is one of those games that sits on the border of whether to recommend or not and since Steam has a binary review system, I will give the game a positive review with the caveat that I would ONLY recommend this game on a deep sale and highly suggest playing the DLC (thankfully free) after the main game. The Chant's premise has promise as psychedelic/cosmic horror is a genre that is slightly underused in my opinion. Unfortunately, poorly thought out systems and lackluster storyline hold the game back from realizing this premise. It's difficult to separate what the game does well from the bad, because so often they are intertwined. Let me explain.The Chant has a story and characters that could be diverse and interesting and at moments it is, but it doesn't spend enough time fleshing out these characters to make you care about them. There are 3 endings based on your highest stat and they are all abrupt and unsatisfying. This is only remedied by the free DLC that expands on what I suppose is the canon ending. Additionally, the voice acting can range anywhere from serviceable to stiff and emotionless. A surprising fact given the talent they brought in for roles making me question if this was an issue with direction. Graphics and animation are also a mixed bag as there are moment where the game looks fairly pretty but others where it looks quite hideous for 2022 title. Animations share the same problem, though they are generally pretty good in thanks to the use of mo-cap. The facial animations are strange at times, however, with characters often staring at each other, mouth agape, as the other speaks. The music and sound design are probably the only part of the game I can give complete appraisal for. Monsters sound quite menacing and the attacks and abilities have a weighty/satisfying sound to them, The music being a blend of psychedelic rock and dark synths perfectly fits the atmosphere they game is trying to set.The Chant leans more heavily on action rather than horror with any scares being mostly cheap jump scares rather than genuine dread or terror. There are moments where a stalker enemy pursues the player while they are meant to resolve a roadblock preventing progress but it is so easily dispatched that it serves as even less of a threat than the normal enemies. Enemies consist of cultists and gloom entities found exclusively in either the real world or the gloom dimension respectively. They are surprisingly varied in their attacks though  some of the enemy types are vastly underutilized. Combat itself is probably the strongest part of the game, though it still has issues. You have 3 types of melee weapons, 3 types of thrown weapons, and 6 different spiritual abilities at your disposal that you earn over the course of the game. Weapons have durability and must be crafted as there are not enough found in the world itself to get you through the game. You additionally have 3 stats: Mind, Body, and Spirit that must be managed and are "leveled" by defeating certain enemies and through dialogue options. These function as your sanity, health, and ability power respectively. Prismatic crystals can be found throughout the game and are used to purchase perks assuming you have met the stat requirement to do so. The stat requirements are far too high for many of the more interesting perks, meaning you won't be unlocking them until the last 20% of the game and unless you save your points until that point, won't be upgrading them to their final tier.Are you noticing an issue here? For a game that can be completed in around 5 to 6 hours if you take your time and speed ran in 2 hours, there are too many systems. The dialogue options and crafting system don't lead to any meaningful choices or difference in outcome. The perk system should have been design with the short game length in mind. Abilities are varied, but there's not a real clear use for a number of them and with the heavy focus on combat, there isn't much reason to use anything other than the overpowered swarm ability. Boss fights are actually not bad for a horror game with different mechanics in each. Enemies are represented by a colored health bar based on which of the 3 stats they align with and using the correct weapons in dealing with them is key to not wasting weapon durability. Melee combat doesn't get that much more interesting beyond that, however, as you otherwise just spam light or heavy attacks while dodging out of enemy attacks. It's good enough that I didn't find myself bored of it by the end of the game, but I won't give it any further praise than that.The Chant has quite a few problems, though despite that, I didn't hate my time with it and don't regret playing it. While this is not a review for the DLC, I will mention that it was the high point of my time with the game and really should have been a final chapter in the main story that satisfyingly ties up the plot while fleshing out the gloom. If these problems I've laid out don't sound like enough to offset what the game does decently, then give it a try next time it is on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: 'The Chant' provides a brief yet immersive horror experience, clocking in at about 8 hours of gameplay (not including the free dlc). The game brilliantly weaves cosmic horror and Cthulhu themes, opting for genuine unease over cheap jump scares. An engaging storyline paired with striking visuals, commendable art design, and atmospheric music truly elevates the experience. However, it falls short with rigid facial animations and lacks depth in its supporting characters, making it challenging to feel a genuine connection or investment in their fates. Overall, it's a captivating journey for horror enthusiasts looking for substance over shock.

_childDocuments_.review: "The Chant" is a short (ca. 9h) but intense survival horror action-adventure with a fresh cosmic horror setting, room for exploration, engaging puzzles, somewhat clunky but functional combat, and mild RPG elements.You play as Jess, a young woman who feels responsible for the death of her teenage sister. A friend invites you to a spiritual retreat on a tropical island to clear your mind. While you observe that the group feels "culty", you talk to the members and participate in an event. However, things go south very fast, and you have to fight for your life while also trying to save your friend.The game generally does a good job of capturing the fundamental elements of cosmic horror - the idea that you're up against an immensely powerful enemy that is beyond human understanding. At the same time, the setting feels fresh due to the unusual elements of the tropical island and the spiritual group, as well as the at least partially plant-based nature of the enemy. Unfortunately, there is no subtlety to it - once the first enemies appear, the story is very in-your-face, there is barely any psychological horror present, and while there are many open questions, I never had the feeling that I was unraveling any sort of exciting mystery.Each of the game's 5 chapters focuses on one character, and chapters 2 to 5 are all structured in the same way, which makes the story a bit formulaic, repetitive, and predictable. I still enjoyed it and I don't think it's a bad story for a video game, I just wish the story had been more varied and imaginative, and not quite so black-and-white.Notes that are scattered across the game reveal background information about the characters, which was nicely done, and also some research on the creatures you're fighting. The latter reveals some very interesting ideas about their biology that I would have liked to see expanded upon in the story as well as the visuals. While the game doesn't really do either, it would be nice to see that in a possible sequel. With puzzles, crafting, combat, and an RPG-like progression system, the game offers a pretty varied set of mechanics, which were all well-designed, but a bit undercooked due to the limited amount of content.The game encourages you to explore and rewards doing so with resources that you need to craft gear and to level up. While the playable area isn't extremely large, there is enough room to leave the beaten track and find loot in optional areas. Locked doors, the labyrinthine design of some interiors, and the fact that many areas are dangerous to traverse until you (optionally) destroy their beachhead, further contribute to making navigation an engaging challenge.The first half of the game doesn't have any puzzles unless you count the hunt for door keys which have been broken into several parts and need to be assembled. Later chapters involve multi-stage puzzles that span the entire local area. I would have liked to see more of the latter, but appreciated what was already there. The puzzles are very straightforward, but can still feel challenging because of the traveling involved.Combat is fairly elaborate - you can attack, dodge, shove enemies, and cast various "powers". I found it a bit too difficult for my taste, possibly because I never got the hang of dodging properly, and often got hit despite seeing the attack coming and trying to evade it. I think that was more a "me" issue than a problem of the game.The game has a crafting mechanic, which I enjoyed, but it is very basic. There are 5 different crafting resources, and you can craft 5 different items, each of them requiring 2 resources. The available items consist of 3 plant-based melee weapons and 3 close-range throwables, the latter of which can also be placed as traps. The melee weapons have different strengths, but it is very straightforward which one is best for any given situation. Melee weapons degrade when you use them, and thrown weapons deplete. Since your carrying capacity is limited and resources are scarce in certain areas, you can't just attack every enemy or you risk facing a boss without any remaining weapons - but if you keep a good balance between evading and attacking enemies, you'll prevail. This mechanic conveys a proper feeling of vulnerability.The game also includes some RPG elements - namely, you have 3 meters (body, mind, spirit), and each stat can be "healed" with a specific resource. Depleting your "mind" means that you'll have a panic attack and won't be able to fight. Depleting your "body" means that you die. There are also 12 skills available, each with 3 levels of power, and learning them requires a special resource that you find by exploring. Skills range from increasing your 3 base stats to making your use of healing resources more efficient, to giving you new combat abilities like stun attacks. I think that this was a fresh way of implementing the body/mind/soul trinity in the form of RPG mechanics, and it was working pretty well, but once again, the limited amount of content made it feel a little undercooked.Graphics and sound are phenomenally good for a game that was produced by a self-proclaimed "single A" studio. The environment and the characters are brought to life by high-definition textures that remain crisp even when you get very close. Areas and creatures under the enemy's control feel properly eerie and surreal. Animations are smooth and realistic. The art direction and the artists themselves did a stellar job here.Sound effects and music are on the same high level of quality. From haunting percussion tracks while exploring, to pulse-pounding metal tracks during combat, the sounds always enhanced the atmosphere and never felt out of place.The game is fully voice-acted, and the actors also did a very good job, though the voice direction could have done better - sometimes the voice actors stress the wrong word and/or don't seem aware of the context of the conversation.The game offers detailed 4-step quality settings for textures, shadows, foliage, AA quality, and post-processing. It supports FSR 2.0 resolution scaling. Advanced features like bloom, motion blur, ambient occlusion, etc. can be toggled individually. An FOV slider, FPS lock, brightness slider, vsync toggle, fullscreen/windowed selector, and resolution selector are all present. Four audio sliders let you finetune your acoustic experience. Subtitles can be toggled on or off and can use any of the available languages, independent from the audio.The game's difficulty can be changed between 3 settings at any point in time, even in the middle of a fight. Control options include 2 separate sensitivity sliders for the X and Y axes, as well as 2 separate "invert" toggles. Keyboard controls can be fully rebound except for some within the menu system, such as tab switching. There's nothing serious missing from the options, it's really nice to see a self-proclaimed "single A" developer take so much care to provide an all-around smooth user experience.Unfortunately you cannot save the game manually, but it autosaves fairly frequently. There is only one save state per playthrough, and starting a new game erases it. This could have been done better, though an argument could be made that having only one save state contributes to the feelings of vulnerability and immediacy. There is also an option to restart the current chapter, in case you feel that you wasted too many resources.I did not run into any bugs."The Chant" is a well-rounded, fresh-feeling horror game that I really enjoyed playing. While many of its parts feel like they could have used some more elaboration, I found the whole package enjoyable and interesting. I'm curious what these developers might do with a bigger budget, and I wouldn't mind revisiting this world.

_childDocuments_.review: Looking for solace in all the wrong places. Charismatic cult leaders taking advantage of gullible individuals as a gaming theme has been covered extensively in recent years. "The Church in the Darkness" and "Far Cry 5" come to mind. Yet this title I'm writing about today has taken it a step further by fusing elements of the supernatural, still ambiguous enough to allow room for interpretation.The path towards that form of enlightment is not straightforward. I am glad that it managed to subvert my expectations in a positive manner. Was it a fever dream, a hallucination after all? Only one way to find out. The Chant is the Steam debut for developer Brass Token, while being published by industry veterans Prime Matter. A successful combination which proved there's still some novelty left in the aforementioned topics. Take nothing at face value here. Given the player choices which can steer the outcome in three different ways, being unpredictable is an inherent trait for the majority of characters.Jonestown without a massacre of that scale, The Chant's fictional island is still exhibiting lush forests prowling with dangers, ethereal or not. You'll find lovecraftian elements in almost any horror story, if you look close enough. True, we do have a lighthouse which plays a central role for the narrative, as well as the even more obvious cult mingled with bouts of insanity. I won't discount The Chant's tale as anything short of original. It's more than just "a  colourful Evil Within" as some players have called it. You need to appreciate a cult-centric story that eschews clichees and tropes akin to those topics. No nudity or gratuitous violence in The Chant. You can even avoid most fights by being nimble enough and fleeing the subsequent pursuit. Most foes cannot follow you for very long, thanks to the island's barriers and protective wards. Meditation and non-violence pay-off in the form of specific Steam Achievements. However, the exploration may suffer, as several lore-rich documents and film reels are well guarded by enemy entities you will have to vanquish.All the more reason to make early choices and stick with them. Replay value is obvious and planning ahead with save you a lot of time. Without spoiling anything, the center stage is taken by traumatised female protagonist which must overcome her own fears as she faces otherworldly challenges that will change her perception and initial skepticism.  Unreal Engine 4 is being pushed to its limits in The Chant. Showing its age, but it gave me no cause for complaint. It's a stable experience which can still be maxed out in 1080p on my 2016 system. What I really appreciated about The Chant's visuals, are the many colors & shades it adopts depending on circumstance. Tied very well to the in-game crystal mechanics that in turn control what powers and areas of the map you can access. You won't get bored if you just stop and admire your surroundings, that's for certain. Hidden crafting components are just around the corner.Minimal HUD design by default, the User Interface can be entirely disabled from the Options menu, so I wasn't hindered at any point during my never ending hunt for proper screenshots. Took 33 for the spoiler-free cut here on Steam and thrice as many for my personal archive.Finding and reading as much auxiliary material across Glory Island as you can, will also reward with stat-boosting experience. No time constraints, so be thorough in your search. Plenty to read or watch while you're dodging physical and mental attacks.Not the most enthusiastic voice acting from what I could deduce, but it's passable. At least it's not involuntarily humorous. The Chant's serious tone leaves room for the occasional element of comic relief, but for the most part you'll find the Gloom foes to be quite...gloomy. Nothing wrong with that and the soundtrack was on point during both combat and moments of respite.While there's even a Steam Achievement for speedrunning The Chant is less than four hours, I strongly recommend you take in the sights during your first playthrough. Explore every nook and cranny, interact with NPCs and carefully examine those maps and bestiary drawings. There's a lot of foreshadowing hidden in plain sight. All you have to do is flip those documents more often. I managed to complete the story on the default difficulty in ten hours and I enjoyed every last bit. The save system has so many checkpoints, that you don't have to worry about losing any progress if you pause or exit a lot. You might wanna do that, just for the loading screen artwork.Mind, Body and Spirit are your main resource pools and they can be enhanced by simply consuming the adequate items you shall craft. Dialogue choices further shape those stats as well as the interactions with fellow survivors. I'm still torn between the lables of survival or psychological horror. It's probably a mix of both, depending on how you approach it. Hippie commune turned into something truly sinister which feeds on raw emotions and false hopes. The key element is knowing when to stay on the move and when to cut yourself some slack in order to access all those documents. No matter how thorough I was, there were still two pieces of intel I somehow missed from the total of 61. There's always a next time and I will take the fight to those cultists instead of showing mercy. Changing tactics will offer sufficient incentive for a second playthrough at a later date. Signs hinting at a potential sequel are also present. You can't expect clear cut results when your perception is being altered to that extent. An eye-opening ride even if you're not really into occult themes.Far from being an expert in cults or meditation, I was still intrigued by what The Chant has achieved with a story that could have easily been just an afterthought for the gameplay. As it stands now, they complement each other while ensuring that players have something new to examine alongside adding new challenges as the game progresses towards its open-ended conclusions. I do not consider it overpriced or overrated. Unfair comparisons with other series or singular titles should also be shown restraint. The Chant deserves your attention. Especially if you're looking for cult stories that transcend caricatures. Open your mind, unleash your spirit and wholeheartedly embrace change!+ Steam Achievements.+ Beautiful graphics and soundtrack.+ Replay value through story & gameplay choices.- No Steam Trading Cards.- Bland voice acting.

_childDocuments_.review: I've always liked Cult and supernatural stories so I do like  as well as the time I had with it, but this isn't for everyone. Recommended for those who want to become involved in a bizarre story surrounding a Cult. The game's biggest flaw is in fact poor balance between the game's various mechanics as you will see in the flaws section.I will say that the composer for the music absolutely nailed the overall tone of the game, I was really drawn in by the atmosphere that the music provided which paired up with the content of the game very well.Instead of writing an overly long review with a detailed analysis I'm goings to list this game's shortcomings and give my thoughts on them. :- . Swinging around twined together burning branches or a burning sage stick at enemies just isn't interesting enough in a combat setting. There needs to be more variety in the weapons and attack animations. This is a supernatural game about a cult, I can think of a million and one different attacks and occult weapons which would work.- . If you're playing the game for the first time figuring out the mechanics then you're not going to do well because you haven't learned the resources, their effects or when to use a specific resource for a particular scenario. Scarce resources when implemented properly can work in a game, but it just isn't fun in have  type of resource management in a game that isn't . It's almost as if you have to have played the game multiple times with a really strong resource management skill in order to do well in the game which is indicative of poor game design.- . This really detracts from the game because it's bringing a Souls-like experience to a game that isn't in the Souls franchise. This isn't meant to be a souls like game which begs to ask why try to emulate a combat experience from a different genre and a different type of game? - . There is one bad guy whom is a cookie cutter villain and a completely unnecessary part of the game which makes me question why he was even included as a boss battle. He's not the focus of the story, he's a secondary side character and he isn't even the final boss of the game.- . There is a specific term that I heard while playing which made me erupt in unexpected laughter and the writers didn't need to get so goofy with the lore. There was a guy in the '70s - a time when cults and psychedelic spirituality were at their peak - whom created a commune and is the founder of "". Yes, you read that ridiculous crap right. We're talking about 3D geometric shapes - prisms - and crystals that hippies like to collect. Now, prisms are an important of math and geometry, but we're not talking about legitimate science instead it's a pseudo-intellectual "science" based upon the study for the flow of cosmic energy as it relates to prisms. I don't think anyone even in the '70s would have taken such a term seriously. Now usually when a game has spongey bosses or scarce resources there is some type of counterbalance meaning for every mechanic implemented there is another mechanic of a different kind to balance it out. So, if a boss is spongey there might be a wealth of a specific resource you might need for that particular battle or your character might learn a new skill you will need for that boss battle. Not The Chant. They went all in on scarce resources, limited weapon types, the same basic attack animation, spongey bosses and a hardcore RE styled emphasis on resource management which doesn't work out too well in the end and can make the combat setting more frustrating than enjoyable. It doesn't "kill" the game and I was intrigued enough to stick with it, but there will be a lot of mixed reactions and I don't think they're going to see those big audience numbers for this game because it desperately needs proper balance.The Chant is an admirable effort with a lot of potential and I'm genuinely curious to see if Brass Token learns from this to give us an even better sequel which is properly balanced. There are some good ideas here, but they don't work well together in this context and The Chant really just needs some fine tuning of its mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow this was a good game, I was looking for more survival horror games and after tons of walking simulators I got this gem of a horror experience. Well, I mean gem like compared to everything that came after Evil Within 1. It is no Silent Hill, but it earned its place among the new survival horror classics. Now, for a survival horror experience it lacked one thing very important to me: A MAP. No map in a new age retirement center?. I hope it gets implemented even if it is not as detailed as a Resident Evil one (that paints blue or red depending if there are items left to collect in the room) a nice one that can tell us where we are and which doors are locked by which key. PROS:Interesting characters.Fun and challenging combatNew kind of weapons for a survival horror (Don't expect a handgun or a knife)Good music (Although there's a track with a garage sounding drum that in my opinion could be improved)As original as any "we go to a cult and bad stuff happen" can go. It actually subverted a bit my expectation.The voice work is fine too.The length is ok too, specially since you have to replay it to get a different ending.CONS:I got a weird bug that painted the main character's face brown or sometimes white. (a reload will fix it until it happens again probably not in the same sitting)Some stuttering, maybe some optimization could be implemented on a next patch.The ending sequence felt a bit too rushed, maybe some pacing could make it more impactful.NO MAP! (I hope this urgently gets implemented in a further update)No BACKPACK (I know you can carry items and increase it in the ability tree but 2 backpacks with extra space distributed in the mid and last chapter could be very rewarding for the player)I'll give it another play and probably update this review but as of now I totally recommend this game, I give it  a 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Short Review & Impressions here for The Chant:It was a pretty good game overall, despite not everything coming together in a cohesive package. There's one aspect of this game I thoroughly disliked but other than that, pretty solid horror survival game akin to the PS3 era of Silent Hill games. Despite the above mentioned, the game wasn't all that scary but the exploratory aspects and seeing what happened in the past was very neat. Combat is a bit wonky but once you get the hang of it, you can combo strikes into stuns into prism powers which made most combat encounters a joke. Your weapons are craftable sticks (?) with differing attack powers depending on when they where they were used but I didn't really find them to be all that different from one another. That said, having to explore for materials to build your weapons ended up being a pretty fun aspect despite my initial reservations to it, mainly because it heavily rewards exploration, even minor, and how efficient you are at using your Prism powers and tools or just knowing when not to fight and bolt outta there.That said, the one aspect about this game I heavily, heavily disliked was a stalker enemy introduced early on that goes by the name of Angie, a manifestation that follows you around in the form of a bunch of bugs. Angie broke up the pace whenever she would appear and would often force you to rush through an environment or else you'd have to deal with two annoying mechanics, one is the rapidly diminishing Mind meter, which induces a Panic Attack state that just makes you unable to fight back for a time and the other is the fact that this enemy is a constant thorn on your side as then the lower Mind makes exploring inside the Gloom zones much harder to boot.I also have to give glowing praise for the game's use of environmental storytelling, it's excellent models and pretty neat enemy designs and the absolutely haunting sound design they went with for the title. All in all though, the game does get a recommendation from me, but I would advise waiting for a sale if you're like me and are already sick to death of Mr. X stalker archetypes as Angie can and will ruin a good bit of the game's pacing, on top of that, the combat being kinda janky may not be for everyone. If you're looking for a pretty decent horror experience built by what I definitely consider to be a hella hardworking team, I think this is a good one to keep an eye out. PS - Thank you Mike for having a small chat with me over Steam, I'm glad to see a lot of the stuttering issues were cleaned up to a tee, made post update a stutter free experience and a joy to play at 4K.

_childDocuments_.review: I saw the trailer and I was hooked. I really loved this premise the game has, a horror story within a cult on a remote island. Sounds amazing already. What could go wrong? It's just that I though that it would be more of a choice-based game like Dark Pictures Anthology for instance. I was wrong, there are not much choices to be had, but I like the fact that in this game you can fight. It's a decent action horror game, but it's not amazing in my opinion. Though it could be if the story was better and felt less generic. It feels like bad writing. And not only the story, the whole gameplay felt too generic. The characters felt bland and uninteresting. The dialogue was kinda poor, and the voice acting pretty mediocre. The fighting very basic and you are in constant need of resources.The natural environments are pretty for the most part, but I really did not like how the gloom areas were portrayed. At first they are locked areas with a fog-like specific color. Once you unlock them, you wander within those areas seeing no other colors than the specific color set for that "supernatural" area, until you clear it of the gloom entities, and not all gloom areas can be cleared.This game would be so much more enjoyable without any of the colored areas, in my opinion. That just makes it look bad and cheap, and there are many of such areas throughout the game. Maybe you'll think I'm exaggerating, but to me dwelling in those colored areas was annoying as hell.Then after the locked areas there come the locked doors. There are many locked doors you must unlock by collecting 3 metal pieces and combine them together. But for me this was kinda annoying, and then there are also some doors with symbol on them and you must find the right key to unlock their padlocks.I'm just not a fan of such puzzly obstacles in horror games. Also aligning the green ray crystals, that was another pretty annoying puzzle section followed by an annoying "boss" fight. But ok, at least later fighting the guy with the pink ray crystals was kinda fun to beat. Some enemies can be pretty annoying tho, like the entity made of fireflies, that keeps forming back to shape and never dies. However the dodge mechanic is king in this game, I'm not joking, it's just great! One of the best I have seen in any game.Other than that the game has a basic character upgrade system which is ok. it seems like there are different endings, I got the mind ending...It would be unfair for me to give it a negative rating, but if I could rate it more specifically I would rate it a 5.5 out of 10.Would I recommend this game? Yeah I would, for one playthrough is fine, also since it's not too long.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I didn't get very far in this game, but I was quickly disappointed (and bored out of my mind) by it and couldn't see myself playing any more. The promise sounded so exciting, but honestly resulted in boring game play and story. For the mechanics, I was excited by the idea of choosing when to run, managing my sanity and spirituality, and story choices, but I in the first hour and a bit, it was clear that this wasn't what I was getting. The first run sequence was fun, but didn't offer any challenge or choice. Then the main game started and the story choices were minimal and didn't feel like they affected the story at all. Managing your sanity, health and spirituality is a matter of having the right resources and clicking on them, it felt like any other generic game. Then the combat was painfully awful. See badie, click the mouse button until they die, or sometimes use a power to give you a bonus. Honestly, it's supposed to be a psychological horror, fighting should feel like a last resort, not the key to progressing the story (as it was in every case I encountered it). The puzzles boiled down to, search every nook and cranny until you find thing, put thing in obvious spot. Maybe it gets better, but I don't have the time to slog through to find out.Honestly, I can overlook bad mechanics if a story and characters are interesting. The Chant had a really solid start and even the intro premise was neat; a cult performing dark rituals, toying with things they don't really understand, something goes wrong... all the pieces are there, but the execution was poorly done. The main character is clearly a skeptic, yet when things go wrong, she 100% believes someone is possess and starts doing a horrific ritual to save them. I guess the writers just wanted to get to the main game play, but it really hurts the story for this disjointed character. Also there isn't much of a transition between here's the cult get comfortable, to, running around killing creatures and saving your possessed friend. For a big budget game like this, I would have expected better writing. Finally, this is a minor gripe, but the character models all looked really uncanny, and not in the good spooky way but in a, maybe do a couple more passes on the design phase. I never return games, I'm content to let my library will up with stuff that I'll probably never touch again, but even on sale, I wanted my money back. Maybe if you're just getting into the horror genre and want to ease in with something bland and generic, this could be fun, otherwise, there are so many more interesting and fun games you could be playing!

_childDocuments_.review: The Chant has an intriguing premise and setting that set it apart from its cousins in the horror/action adventure sphere. _childDocuments_.review: The Chant is a single-player, third-person horror action-adventure game set on a remote spiritual island retreat. You play as a female protagonist called Jessica and you have to survive by crafting, fighting, and escaping the psychedelic horrors set loose when a spiritual ritual goes wrong and awakens a dimension of cosmic terror. Rate: ★★★★☆ The game follows a rather linear quest line, where you learn how to craft, fight and go through simple puzzles that unlock new areas of the map.You have in-the-game perks that you can unlock which help you hold more resources, helping you to become stronger and make the use of items more viable. Rate: ★★★★☆  I honestly enjoyed the game despite the issues I had with the frame rate. The game becomes more stable after a while and despite that, I thought the story was the main thing that would hook me, it was actually the combat and the gameplay. It was an enjoyable game overall.  Rate: ★★★★☆ I’ve had some weird visual bugs here and there, but overall, this game looks good. The characters are well-animated and the cinematics looks good. The world is well-built too and the creatures and monsters are strange, but beautifully designed. Rate: ★★★★☆ When I first started the game, I didn’t expect this game to be much of a horror. It has nice voice-acting and scary music that creep me in some areas. The music was punchy and trilling and the soundtrack sounds great.  Rate: ★★☆☆☆ I was expecting a much more compelling story to be honest. It wasn’t bad but was rather difficult to feel any kind of attachment to the characters and their stories. The decision-based aspects are poorly executed and it’s difficult to determine what’s the outcome. It doesn’t feel like much effort was put into them and I feel that they should have just taken them out as the story doesn’t feel to change much except a few dialogues.  ☑️  Short ☑️ Average 🔲 Long  🔲 Unlimited  The game took me about 10 hours to complete without putting much time in exploring everything or chasing achievements.   🔲 Easy ☑️ Normal ☑️ Hard 🔲 Brutally Hard 🔲 Impossible  I’ve played this game on medium difficulty. The game feels rather difficult at the beginning of the game and gradually gets easier as you upgrade your perks and discover new things in the game. The end boss felt difficult and kinda struggles to prepare you for it. The Chant has been a good game for me, with a few flaws that I believe the developers will eventually find a fix. Although I wanted more from this game, I really enjoyed my time with it and I’m curious to see what the developers have else to offer.

_childDocuments_.review: All the laughable writing and slapdash 'psychological horror' mechanics like being scared of the dark unless you've got some lavender to munch on would be forgivable, and maybe even be charming, if it wasn't for the total hate crime that is the combat system.It's not even that it's particularly hard, it's just bad. _childDocuments_.review: The Chant ReviewSTORY - 7/10A lot of the story about what happened on the island before the main character arrives is told via collectible notes/pages. If you don't mind that/reading in general, you'll find some interest and enjoyment. Unfortunately, the story being told with character actions and dialog is lacking. Expect many instances of "Why doesn't Jess tell them what they found/know about the gloom??" GAMEPLAY - 8/10Very solid and easy to learn gameplay. If you've played and liked Remedy's Alan Wake or Control, you'll enjoy this game's core mechanics. Dodging is extremely easy and forgiving and most enemy attacks are simple enough avoid completely by either side stepping or dodging. You are constantly finding resources to refill your weapons (melee sticks or throwable oils).  GRAPHICS & PERFORMANCE - 8/10 (on a 6800XT)Character models and environments are highly detailed and textures look great. Great use of lighting and fog like visuals within the gloom segments. Recommend turning off Screen Space Reflections, as they exhibit a weird ghosting/trailing like effect when panning the character around (most notable on the dock at the beginning of Jess's arrival). FSR2 and DLSS available. Didn't visually notice too many (maybe 3?) #stutterstruggle that most UE engine based games have, and I believe that's because they implemented a new shader caching method post-launch that's much appreciated!!FINAL VERDICT - 8/10I quick (first playthrough runs in at about ~6 hours) and enjoyable game that has a decent cast of characters and nice visuals. Story is a little lacking and if you're looking for deep gameplay mechanics, you'll be disappointed. But if you like simplified controls and a bite-sized story about a group of cultists trying to bring 'Gloom to Glory', you'll have a fun playing 'The Chant'.

I wish it were longer. also people saying the game doesnt look finished due to stiff characters and graphics i just dont see the same thing.
