_childDocuments_.name: The Chant

_childDocuments_.review: So, it may be this isn't for me, but as someone who enjoys horror games I feel the need to weigh in. This is a case of "I wish Steam had a middle of the road option" or something a little more in depth than yay or nay. The game has an interesting premise, with some interesting ideas. Immediately with the three bars for your Mind, Body and Spirit I was reminded of Eternal Darkness, which I loved, but it felt like I never had any issue with mind, while I was constantly starved for spirit, and other than making you run from a fight, mind never really seems to be an issue when drained, which I feel they could have learned from Eternal Darkness, assuming they took any inspiration, and made more scary psychadellic hallucinations when you have low mind, as opposed to the screen just draining of colour. The other thing is that I noticed on the Steam page it encourages you to pick your battles, because your resources are limited, which rings totally hollow for me because you are never really sure what rooms are important, if a room has resources you need, if you're going to be coming back to an area later so it may be worth battling enemies within the moment, because more than once I spot other doors that I can't do anything with now, which I assume I'll be coming back for later. Without any of this knowledge, 'picking your battles' is a frustrating task. The combat is passable, light attack, strong attack, different weapons for different enemies, but your weapons break constantly and you need to craft new ones using limited resources. The "magic" is interesting, but I found myself constantly out of spirit because the things to replenish it seem to be more rare than the resources to heal your mind or body. The whole package is pretty alright. The story and writing I can't comment on, it seems very cheesey and the voice acting can be a little weird, but I can enjoy that. If there is ever a second game or if the team makes another horror game, I hope this game made for a great learning experience, and that things could be tightened up and improved. Get the game on sale, and give it a try, maybe you'll vibe with it more than I did.
_childDocuments_.name: The Chant

_childDocuments_.review: Jess' voice actress deserves an award for her screams in this game. They're some of the most grueling, believable sounds of anguish I've heard. Good on her.  The rest of the game is really good too. Its a survival horror game where you use crystals and sage to beat the ♥♥♥♥ out of extra-dimensional plant monsters. A for originality. Gameplay balance is great as it forces you to adapt and get the most out of your resources. I had alot of fun with this game. Devs also get kudos for releasing free and engaging DLC.  They're a small team which makes their final product that much more impressive
_childDocuments_.name: The Chant

_childDocuments_.review: The Chant has a boring story with poorly written characters and repetitive combat. The story deals with heavy themes like grief and guilt but lacks focus and never comes to any meaningful conclusion for it's characters. Every story beat is predictable and uninteresting. The combat is extremely repetitive and enemies take a long time to kill. They give you three melee weapons and three thrown weapons that all work the same mechanically so there's no reason to use one over another aside from one breaking and forcing you to switch. Very little enemy variety but they may as well all be the same enemy because you fight them all the same - LMB spam, space to dodge, throw in a RMB to keep yourself from falling asleep, repeat. There are magic attacks in the game as well that you can use to help if you find yourself outnumbered but despite having five or six in the game (I can't remember) there's never a good reason to switch and I found myself using the same one for almost the entire game. It borrows the crafting system from Resident Evil which forces you to decide if you want to use Plant-X to make a weapon or a throwable but because the weapons all feel the same it never feels like a meaningful choice. The Puzzles in the game are very simple which is to be expected from a game trying to be Resident Evil but its even more offensive in The Chant because the devs don't trust the players to figure out the extremely obvious puzzles on their own and have the characters direct you every time. I liked the 80s inspired soundtrack but nothing else in the game added to that vibe imo. The game borrows a lot of good ideas from other games but doesn't execute any of it properly. 3/10 would not recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: The Chant

_childDocuments_.review: Over all 7.9/10 Combat is simple but fun to master. The Talent system is one of the coolest systems out there, very unique. Make sure to backtrack!! Look around they hide stuff from you, but its not a hard search so have fun. Graphics are fairly ok, feels like premium indie quality. The Story is fine quality. If you play a lot of spooky games you will feel right at home here. and the DLC is free( DLC- The combat is much harder with a shake up on powers ) Over all 7.9/10 game. Awesome game to get this on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Chant

_childDocuments_.review: "The Chant" is like if "Resident Evil" had a child with "The Stranger Things". And maybe if that child was a bit sickly.The basics of the gameplay is walking around collecting stuff in order to open some door (mostly literal, but sometimes metaphorical) while also protecting yourself from weird creatures, which seem somewhat plant-based, but nonetheless evil. Unlike "Resident Evil" you have not guns at all, but you can collect different good plants to craft various types of besoms, that you use to ward of those evil plants by literally wiping them to death. In addition you can collect some salts and oils, that you can through, and another type of salt, that you use to improve your stats and learn passive skills.The skills do make surviving quite a bit easier, especially considering limited amount of resources: both throwables and melee weapons "break" or otherwise expire, and most monsters are relatively tough, with some being really tough (although in case of bosses you normally do have way to replenish your resources). On the other hand most enemies are quite stupid, so in most cases you just dodge (which can feel weird at times, but maybe that's for the sake of realism, since you are not playing as a real fighter), hit a couple of times, dodge again.So while gameplay does not really introduce anything new, it is quite solid, especially paired with quite good level design, which provides just the right amount of freedom and nooks and crannies to explore, while maintaining your progression pace. The story, though...It's not bad per say. The beginning is especially good, it really hooks you in, but when the failed ritual happens... A lot of things feel rushed. It does make some sense considering the circumstances, but it feels like everyone becomes kind of ok (even if a bit insane) with all of the crazy plants roaming around. That does not make any sense, because technically only one person is supposed to be somewhat knowledgeable, but even that person behaves worse than a child with his character overall being very poorly developed.I think the main problem was that the first chapter was very short and it pushed you into the craziness too fast and did not really allow you to get to know the people around you. Yes, you can gather various notes afterwards, that do expand on the characters somewhat, but it's not enough. It would have been better if 1st ritual worked fine and only thing that changed was Jess (protagonist) started seeing things, that she would consider hallucinations or something like that. And then 2nd ritual fails and you get everything else. Although this would not have saved us from DLC ending, which does not fit the established rules of this world in any way.Another complaint from my side is voice acting: in a lot of cases actors are underplaying, and the low quality of some voice lines does not help. In fact, to my ears all women in the game sound almost Identical to Jess, even when they are talking with each other and you actually see who is talking. That is worsened by the fact that facial animations, on the contrary, overplay the emotions, which sometimes ruins the atmosphere entirely: so much that even really good soundtrack did not help in those moments.But despite the bad things, I still did enjoy my time with the game. From what I understand this is the first game from "Brass Token", and if that's the case - this is a very good introduction, and I really wish them success with future releases. I think if you do like "Resident Evil" like games or worlds with "evil plants" - you will probably enjoy it, too, even if you buy it at full price.
_childDocuments_.name: The Chant

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:   - Good Story   - Good Graphics   - Not taking cults too seriouslyCons:   - Combat system was a bit frustrating          -buttons not intuitive on keyboard        - Getting animation locked for too long dodging during combat.        - Not enough materials to craft the weapons you need to effectively target creature types           (certain crafting ingredients too scarce)   - Would have preferred a playthrough path where "drinking the koolaid wore off"   -Choosing an ending based on 'which type of creatures you killed more and which items you used' seemed odd when you don't give players the right items at the right times to do that effectively
_childDocuments_.name: The Chant

_childDocuments_.review: This game was really cool. Definitely an interesting take on the survival horror genre. The main story is pretty short, only about 7 hours and that's with a lot of exploring. I would avoid paying full price but if its on sale its pretty good. It is a small budget indie title and it certainly felt that way at times, but this is overshadowed by the amount of love you can tell went into the game. There were only about 12 devs for this game so its pretty impressive what they were able to acomplish. The Story and atmosphere are really great, the highlights of the game for sure. The combat is janky but there is enough of a skill curve and rhythm too it that it remains entertaining for the full length of the game. If I had to pick a game to compare it too I would say the sinking city is a good comparison. Overall I would give it a solid 7/10 Not the most amazing game in the world but still really cool. I have not played the DLC yet so I cannot comment on that but I liked the main game enough that I will make sure I get to it soon
_childDocuments_.name: The Chant

_childDocuments_.review: This is a pretty linear action-adventure game with horror themes and material scarcity (which is where the "survival" bits come from, I guess). You have to juggle your 3 attributes (health, mana, sanity), as you explore the island that was supposed to be a spiritual retreat, but cosmic horrors happened. You gain psi powers as you collect various prisms-these are also your colour-coded keys to access bits of the island blocked off by the various flavours of "The Gloom"- local version of the Shadow World where the evil things live. To fight them, you get to craft 3 kinds of weapons, or throw 3 types of projectiles (which can also be laid down as traps). you can craft these using plants and oil you find, and you also use 3 different plants to boost your meters. The combat is fairly basic, but you have a dodge, ability to shove enemies away, plus light/heavy and ranged. The game loop is, follow a character as they gradually descend into madness, solve some puzzles, collect some lore, kill some things, get new prism, repeat. There's some optional areas that contain more lore pieces and the crystals you need to upgrade your skills, and one optional boss area. Overall, I found the story to be pretty formulaic, but the combat and exploration loop to be generally fun. The puzzles aren't difficult, and the game streamlines the key item hunting and combining mechanics compared to the classic titles like Resident Evil, but it's not bad. As much as it can, it tries to add variety to the puzzles and the boss fights have some puzzle elements as well. Game ran well, no bugs. Environments can be quite pretty, character models are so-so. English voiceovers were well-done, the actors played out the B-movie script quite well, so noo complaints there. There's a lot of options to remap controls (though I couldn't switch run from L Shift to R shift, and had to use NumZero instead to play with arrow keys instead of WASD.) Running animation could be a bit faster, I guess, but then it wouldn't work as well with the  script if you could run away from things quicker. Overall, a very competently made action-horror game. There's 3 endings based on which of the 3 main stats you work the most, and there's a speed run and a "don't kill humans" achievements, so I guess there's some replayability potential there. Definitely a good pickup if you just want a simple story for a few evenings.
_childDocuments_.name: The Chant

_childDocuments_.review: Great game inspired by the classics of the genre but at least tries to offer something new in its setting and mechanics.The best survival horror I've played this year just behind Resident Evil 8 Gold.Mix the exploration mechanics of a resident evil with melee combat like those of dark souls. It seems to me a very successful combination because that is how someone who does not know how to fight would defend himself and dodge.The lore, the music and the story have seemed a little more superficial than I expected but it complies in all aspects.The endings could be better but at last it have different ones that depends on your gameplay. Thumbs up.
_childDocuments_.name: The Chant

_childDocuments_.review: Imperfect, but very good.The pros: Great action, interesting story, creepy atmosphere, deep game mechanics. All around a well thoughtout and well executed game. Fun to play and a great addition to the Survival Horror family, especially for an indie game.The cons: sometimes the level design did not play well with the camera. I understand that claustrophobia is part of the DNA of SH games, but it got a little annoying at times when there were too many plants, or shelves, etc, in the way of the camera. The facial animation is not great. Reminds me of 2005 games, but for an indie game, I'm willing to let it slide.You're asked to make decisions that are important to the story many  times throughout the game, but it feels like we don't know enough about the characters or the situation to make a good guess. It's completely random, and then you have to just live with the results.
_childDocuments_.name: The Chant

_childDocuments_.review: It's a interesting game. Are there better combat games? Yes, Better Story driven games? Yes. But not one game lets you beat a monster with a lite sage or a burning bush. Its really silly game, the combat is decent, and the story, while... it's typical, the locations and powers are unique and interesting. Plus the DLC is really cool.I think this game has a lot of potential but doesn't reach that level. It's still fun and interesting to play and I would recommend, but I can see where with more work it could have been a top tier game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Chant

_childDocuments_.review: Glad I took the gamble on this. An enjoyable game that plays not dissimilar to how I imagine a cosmic Resident Evil would. It has some good attempts at mixed damage types and crafting weapons based around those damage types as well as a three-type 'health' system that has meaningful interactions with one another as well as playing into the XP/upgrade system.The game is not perfect (although very well polished and crafted given the small dev team) but worth a pick up on sale if your looking for some horror fun with some decently engaging gameplay mechanics and B-movie narrative.Free rogue-lite DLC is also available!
_childDocuments_.name: The Chant

_childDocuments_.review: I was super enjoying boshing flies and ghouls with my sage sticks, until I got to the first boss and my sage stick broke. Could only shoulder it from there on out and the area I was in did not allow to go gather further resources, so I've locked myself into failure and need to start 3 chapters over to hopefully move past, successful sage stick management dependent. I don't want to run past enemies, I want to kill everything and there should be an option for this.Other than resource management, I enjoyed the rest of this game up to Chapter 3. Quit from getting stuck as didn't want to start over and worry about sage sticks.
_childDocuments_.name: The Chant

_childDocuments_.review: I liked it. I finished it. But... oh my god. Early on, this game is *extremely* stingy with consumable resources, so much so that by the end of the first chapter it looked like I was going to get trapped between a checkpoint and a fight that would be impossible to beat going in half-dead with insufficient consumables available to prep or heal, unless I restarted the chapter and played more conservatively. I don't have the time or patience to re-play large swathes of content, so after a few failures I decided to lower the difficulty level. I never regretted it: even on "Neophyte," the game was still hand-to-mouth with consumables until the very last fight, when they were (luxury of luxuries!) actually available on the battlefield. I loved the short length of the game and the intensity of the story, in contrast to the increasingly common 100+ hour extravaganzas with innumerable side quests. A nice tight story like this has little chance to lose momentum. And I loved that I could set the spoken language to German but with English subtitles, since (is it just me?) all games are more enjoyable when you can play them in a language you're trying to learn.
_childDocuments_.name: The Chant

_childDocuments_.review: The Chant reminds me of a "crunchy cousin" to games like Silent Hill and The Evil Within. It's a great game for die hard fans of survival horror with a cosmic horror twist.  It has all the ingredients for great survival horror: a beautiful isolated island with a creepy 70's cult history that opens a gateway to cosmic monsters. With that being said, I felt the whole base game was weighed down by some terrible characters. There are literally six characters in the main story and only two of them didn't make me want to stab them to death with a crystal dagger.  These particular characters made the worst choices possible and did not seem to be too bothered by the fact they were being hunted and murdered by otherworldly monsters. Tyler (the man-baby leader) was the worst and literally yells and whines at you through a screen door/window(?) for a majority of the game. Another particular character appears to have her s*** together and then at the last minutes decides to make the worst possible choice and puts the rest of all mankind BACK into danger. WHY?!?! Because she wants to be loved?!? These characters made the game nerve-racking. Anyway, there is new and free DLC called The Gloom Below. It does a great job of wrapping up some of the convoluted endings from the base game and makes a great improvement on the remaining characters and story.  It does a great job of giving the main protagonist and antagonist more personality and  back story.
_childDocuments_.name: The Chant

_childDocuments_.review: A really good game; interesting storyline and gameplay - if you like Call of Cthulhu, Dead Space or The Sinking City, you'll feel fine with this game. I do feel the story was too short and some threads remained unsettled; but otherwise the controls, graphics, gameplay all are good! I highly recommend this game for fans of third person horror/survival games!
_childDocuments_.name: The Chant

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game, but I can't totally recommend it to everyone. I don't want to overhype it, but if you're curious, may grab it on sale. That said, I’m stll giving it a thumbs up because I enjoyed it. The game blends cosmic horror with a mix of exploration and combat. Its visual gives me vibes of Stranger Things and '70s horror mysteries. I'm sure play it again to chase some achievements.The main story and The Gloom DLC present interesting lore, explaining the purpose & existence. But to be honest, Tyler (the cult leader) doesn't feel like a 'real' cult leader. The combat mechanics feel realistic—Jess even stumbles when dodging (double spacebar). The items are mostly plants fits the remote island setting full of nature. and the inclusion of supernatural powers are cool concepts for a cult-themed game. The supernatural powers are a great fit in this game, makes the combat more interesting.You’ve got 3 stats to manage: Mind, Body, and Spirit. If you stay in The Gloom or dark areas too long, your Mind drains, and you’ll start to panic. You can convert Spirit into Mind to regain sanity, and the upgrade system lets you boost all 3 stats. The Gloom DLC is free to claim, it continues the story from the main game, adds some new items, and expands the supernatural power upgrades.Took 16 hours to obtain all achievements for me.
_childDocuments_.name: The Chant

_childDocuments_.review: The game is really well put together for a small development team and the visuals and sound took me by surprise with how good they are. The combat system is pretty inventive and enemy encounters are satisfying. It's good to have a new survival horror game where you can fight back as so many these days descend into games of hide and seek with forced instant fail stealth sections.I've experienced a little of the dreaded UE4 stutter, but the developer assures a patch to pre-compile shaders is coming so this may not apply at the time of your reading this (I'm writing this the day after release).
_childDocuments_.name: The Chant

_childDocuments_.review: The debut game of a small studio. Not a bad comfortable game. On the plus side pretty good graphics, but unfortunately poorly optimized. The plot is not bad, but I would like to go a little deeper into it. I liked the mechanics of combat, especially pleased that the heroine falls while dodging, such a thing I have not seen anywhere else. The weapons as herbs look interesting too. It was a pleasure to come back to this game and go further in the story.So if you're looking for a good and comfortable game for an evening or two and don't expect anything supernatural from the Chant this is a great choice. I wish the studio success and growth, I will be happy to play the next projects.
_childDocuments_.name: The Chant

_childDocuments_.review: Despite the performance issues here and there I think this is a nice game.I had some trouble getting used to the combat mechanics, but eventually got the hang of it. I just found the swarm of bees that come to you annoying (plus the panick attack). The rest is all a learning curve. The story itself is very simple, and you eventually know what is going to happen, but I find it very fun how they implemented it with the different crystals, characters and monsters.I give it a 7/10!
_childDocuments_.name: The Chant

_childDocuments_.review: I will say, when i picked up the Chant I was not really sure what to expect.  It was kind of a surprise recommendation i got which looked neat so I grabbed it.  So far, I would definitely recommend this game for anyone who likes storybuilding horror.While not really on the same level, the best game i can compare this to is "Control", sans all the telekinetic powers and Flying around.  The characters in some cases fall a bit bland, but fit the typical trope of horror movies and expected actions of such. Overall, I really enjoyed it and look forward to more games from this studio.
_childDocuments_.name: The Chant

_childDocuments_.review: doesn't give you time to care about any of the characters, which is a shame. I would've loved to get to know the others and maybe actually feel upset about getting betrayed or losing any of them. They all have very monotone personalities, and it was easy to predict who was going to be the first victim.  is extremely simplified, janky at times, response time can be slow, too. was great! It helped setting the tone for each situation. are very good. _childDocuments_.name: The Chant

_childDocuments_.review: A worthy entry to the survival horror genre that (at least on the hardest difficulty) definitely takes limited resources seriously. I know survival horror games emphasize limited resources but this will have you pondering the age old question of fight or flight and I respect it for making you ask just that. In the game you will use those limited resources to craft weapons & throw-able items and you will use them to keep (Jess) alive through the implementation of upgrading Skills that include Mind (Sanity), Body (Health) & Spirit (Special Abilities). Now based off of those three things (Mind, Body, & Spirit) there are three endings however no matter what ending you get I would recommend just looking them up as there isn't really any replay value. In the end I thoroughly enjoyed it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Chant

_childDocuments_.review: Aloha, this is my review for the Chant, a survival horror game where you play as Jess, a girl with a troubled past who goes to a spiritual retreat to heal her battered soul; obviously since there is a game, things don't go as planned. The game follows the standard collect items, combine and craft weapons, kill monsters, run out of items, run, level up skill tree, unlock psychic abilities. I bought the game on sale, and found it delightful. The game also features three different endings, determined by your play style [fighting, exploring, what you eat] and answers given for the dialogue options.The Good: the game design is incredibly creative, the psychedelic setting and story is unlike anything I've played and I enjoyed the aesthetics of the entities from outer spheres. The sound design is great, with all manner of weird drippy and creepy moans. The main character, Jess, was enjoyable to play, good voice acting but her co-stars were a feast of large Hams, which in other settings would have been unrealistic, but as a person who has spent quite a bit of time in the spiritual/healing/guru communities, this is entirely accurate. The game has good controls and interesting ability designs, and generous hotboxes for dodging. Also, honestly, Jess was and just a really well-written character that I wished I could have spent more time inside of. The crowning achievement of this game is how it presents cosmic horror better than other "actual" cosmic horror games, that the eldritch horrors that lay slumbering outside and beyond our plane of reality cannot be defeated or killed in any meaningful way, you can lull them to sleep, or temporarily sate their hunger, however, it is we who exist to serve them. The Bad: the music was lacking and given the wild setting some weird psychadelic rock would have been more fitting than the soundtrack. The game was quite short [6 hours, even with my faffing about and dying] and left me wanting more. The crafting and combat can be unforgiving, and clumsy play may lead you to be weaponless, so be careful!The Ugly: How criminally underrated this wildly creative game is!
_childDocuments_.name: The Chant

_childDocuments_.review: game-play makes this very intriguing to play. however , the story line lacks, not enough backstory on characters or plot and combat mechanics aren't the best. very annoying at times when character is having panic attacks while fighting monsters. game had a lot of potential, it was just hard to keep interest in the game. if you have been eyeing it like i have , would only recommend if its on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Chant

_childDocuments_.review: The Chant is a modern day classic.Evoking memories of Alan Wake, Oxenfree and a smudge of Resident Evil. The Chant offers a great overall experience and is without a doubt double AA horror that punches well above it's budget.At the start I felt the combat was a bit weird but after a few hours it really clicked with me and I had so much fun smacking away at cultists and the horrors from the beyond without much difficulty, which introduces one of my biggest issues.The game isn't very difficult, even on the hardest difficulty I never had much trouble and it made the resource management a lot less tense knowing I would never run out or even get close to it with how easily I could dispatch enemies.I was very quickly drawn in by the story and characters and I really enjoyed the acting, but I think the story should have had more of a slow burn at the start. Being part of a cult is such a unique setting for a game and it's a shame it so quickly get's into the horror and I wish we could have had more time spent learning about the cult and getting to know the other characters.Some of the characters also have too little screen time which is a huge shame since there are so few of them.When I beat the game I had some issues with the way it ended and though the game could have done a better end game and the story really fell flat in some areas.However with the free dlc The Gloom Below, pretty much every issue I had with the original game is fixed and gives an incredible ending to neatly tie the whole game together.Overall as a whole package I had an absolute blast and enjoyed this game immensely and it really brought back memories of playing Alan Wake back on the 360.In some areas the budget shows and at full price you are getting a fairly short game, so take that as you will.But I will sing The Chant's praises to people for a long time and I can't wait to see what the developers have cooking up next!
_childDocuments_.name: The Chant

_childDocuments_.review: I picked this game up because I really like the lead actress, Siobhan Williams, that also played Laura Kearney in The Quarry. Overall, I liked it, not the best game I've played but also definitely not the worst. It's a short game and there is not a lot of buildup so I personally didn't really care for any of the characters that got hurt. I also felt like some items were a bit too scarce, which led to me running around kinda improvising to take out some enemies mostly later on in the game. I wouldn't buy it for 25 euros but it's definitely worth to pick it up when it's on sale!
_childDocuments_.name: The Chant

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I really enjoy the premise of this game. It's a bit rough around the edges, but for being made by such a small and new developer the creativity really shines. Pros:-good graphics-detailed monsters and lore, they all feel very creepy, well thought out, and a bit different when in combat-interesting confrontation choices, there were many times where I could choose to run instead of fight-can be very creepy when characters are being developed, hearing them go mad in the gloom is interesting-combat itself is fun without being too difficult or easy-exploring different areas is intriguing -History and lore is well fleshed out, and reading notes is worth it-Intelligent access to materials, not too much so it's meaningless but also sparingly enough to allow for tension in combat-Useful level up systemCons:-Pacing can feel a bit rushed and off, would have liked to spend more time in the beginning getting to know the other cult members before diving into the ritual-Can feel a bit less scary due to the abundance of enemies, again pacing would be a bit better if there were more creepy and quiet moments without enemies to build tension (might just be a personal opinion though)-Lack of character development at times-dialogue choices can feel a bit unclear and inconsequential, kind of like the game is in a weird limbo between being a singular narrative experience and a choice-driven one. -Puzzles aren't very memorableOverall, the Chant is a great concept and a good game with a few rough edges. 7.5/10 would recommend to anyone who's into witchy stuff, cults, or action-packed horror like the resident evil 4.
_childDocuments_.name: The Chant

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing already. The atmosphere and biomes are some of my favorite of any games (the designers really understand their color pallete). Music is hit or miss in areas but sounds are always keeping you on edge. Unique combat play, good enemy variety, intriguing story, good exploration, and it plays very well like a triple A game! Only exception being the face animations and voice overs aren't great. Highly recommended survival horror! It's breath of fresh air that it's a good survival horror without Zombies.Update: the survival horror elements are well balanced through the game, especially for the after main game free dlc which is a roguelite style.
_childDocuments_.name: The Chant

_childDocuments_.review: Sorry but ... 40€ is really not worth it. I like visuals of game, but really cant figure out what this game want to be. Story is know from start how end, enemies are, how to say it, weak or avoidable. Boss fights i rather not bother to spoil but they are, waste of time. Really Liked visuals and graphics. But thats all. As i like Horror and RPG games, this game realy dont know what want to be and if u want to try it.. wait for Sale 10-15€ is worth. Sorry devs, but ... NO
_childDocuments_.name: The Chant

_childDocuments_.review: This game is rough around the edges, especially in its presentation with the great music sometimes coming to a complete stop, and a claustrophobic camera during combat. But despite the flaws, it's very well-designed overall. Lot of nice touches here. I like how the mind, body, and spirit are turned into simple yet engaging gameplay systems. Exploration is always rewarded--not just with survival resources, but also skill upgrade resources. Collecting lore documents grants a bit of experience for skill upgrades too. Even fast travel, which to be honest was barely needed, isn't just a menu. New enemies and abilities are consistently introduced, so the game rarely feels repetitive. My ideal mix of story, exploration, and combat. It ends on a wet fart, perhaps because the inclusion of multiple endings meant that none of them could be fleshed out. All in all I still enjoyed the game, and I'm excited to see this developer grow.

_childDocuments_.review: The Chant is a fun game. Although I've not completed it; if people are claiming it to be short, then I would add: "but sweet".When I first saw it announced I wanted it to be like Until Dawn, or the Dark Pictures Anthology, as The Chant leans heavily into a mysterious story-driven narrative. Not to say that the action-related elements feel 'tacked on' - because they don't. In my opinion the shallow crafting/combat systems actually help round-out the game, as the items you find, and the items you craft from them, fit within the theme presented. With that said, the story, interactions between characters, and overall horror theme would have fit perfectly as an Until Dawn/Dark Pictures title - and it feels like a missed opportunity there.With that in mind it's almost as if The Chant needed to hone in on one particular archetype. It's hard to sell yourself as a horror game when I'm capable of fighting off all threats presented to me, and it's not going to be sold as an action game when the relative mechanics are few.Look into what this game offers before you buy, make sure you'll be able to appreciate what it does well, whilst not letting what it falls short on affect you - because there's something to be had here. It may be short, and have uninspiring combat, but that's okay when it's length and mechanics only exist to serve the narrative goal they're aiming for. I can't help but genuinely say I'm enjoying it - even if I can critically pick it apart. It looks nice, runs well, and keeps me entertained. Not every fun game has to be a masterpiece.

_childDocuments_.review: Have you ever wished your MLM, crystal-obsessed, super spiritual friend was actually right? Well this is the game for you. Its a nice and tight survival-horror game with some melee-action focused combat. There's 3 weapons, but they all play the same but can do more damage depending on which enemies you use them on. There's also 3 throwables/traps  and 6 actionable skills. This seems simple, but for what is a 4.5-6hr story, it gets the job done. By half way through the game I had gotten the hang of things and was able to chain together all the tools to effectively beat the ever loving ♥♥♥♥ out of enemies.I can't make this up: Your first weapon is a Sage Smudge. So yea, you spend a lot of the game "cleansing" eldritch cultists by beating them over the head then throwing acid in their face, before using a force push to make them kneel before your next MLM barrage.The story is well told. A lot of indie survival horror games can not stick the story, dialogue, acting, but I was pleasantly surprised by everyone's performance. VA's and writing team. I expected to just riff on the story and make fun of it as I played, but no, its a good horror story and by the end I was really rooting for a couple of characters to survive.The Chant is a great purchase if you're a fan of survival horror games, eldritch horror, souls-like combat, chances are you'll like the game.I only really have two gripes:1. There should be a lock-on button. It would've made combat a lot better and taken out most of the jank from encounters. Especially the combat encounters where you can have 3 or so enemies crowding you,2.   there are some parts in the 1st section that are 1-hit kills, which is fine, but they should be telegraphed a bit better for the player's first run through.

_childDocuments_.review: I totally dig this game. The soundtrack rocks, the premise is simple and strong, the acting is excellent across the board, and the whole portrayal of the cult is spot-on, right down to its dirtbag charismatic leader. The monster designs were all pretty cool, with special mention for some truly alien-looking flora. I played on the standard difficulty setting and found the difficulty to be immaculately balanced; each combat encounter was dangerous and I was constantly aware of my limited resources, but never so dire that I felt unable to utilize the full range of my toolkit.Items are precisely scarce enough to keep constant tension throughout the game, and I found myself scrambling for supplies right up to the final encounter, which felt enjoyably desperate. Your character is clearly not an adept combatant, which is generally the case with survival horror games, so genre enthusiasts will feel right at home.The Chant also enjoys the considerable benefit of some fantastic classic horror game map design, with the island partitioned into character-themed segments that, while somewhat linear, feature various branching paths and locked doors, turning each area into just enough of a labyrinth that untangling it proves deeply satisfying. The lighthouse area deserve special mention here for some really tight design, and a brief puzzle which involved  felt like a warm nod to Resident Evil fans.A big shoutout as well for the final boss, which went for the kind of grotesque and bombastic weirdness that a lot of modern horror games seem reluctant to embrace. It might not be appropriate in other franchises, but given this title's ever-so-slightly retro tone, I thought it made for a perfect curtain call. The actual ending is weak, but the rest of the story moves along at a good clip and more than balances things out.In the end, Brass Token has crafted a great entry that speaks to the AAA-grade talent they've assembled, and I'm really excited to see what they put out next. The Chant is a definite recommendation for any fan of the survival horror genre.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a first release from a new studio so there are a few hiccups and ideas that won't be appreciated by all. Finished it three times to get every achievement and endings; first with perfect run, second speedrun and third on the highest difficulty. If you're not into achievements, the game is perfectly fine for a single playthrough. However, there are a few questionable design choices that might require some tweaking in future games:First is that teleporters and semi-open world are pointless. You include this feature to let players collect missing things and access previously inaccessible places. However, this game locks a lot of collectibles behind sections that can never be reached again. The only reason to go back now would be resources, but that’s a waste of time because you can only carry a limited amount. The fact that I’m missing exactly one piece of lore and one special enemy makes this even more frustrating.The second is saving. The game has a single autosave slot that only saves when you reach a point that’s relevant to the story. So if you spend 30 minutes running back to pick up resources and die before reaching the next story point, all those resources and time are gone.And finally, the fly lady. She shows up at certain spots on the island and can’t be killed. I’m now in the endgame and she’s the only enemy left. I was exploring previous areas, collecting resources and she killed me just as I was returning back. This felt cheap. Unless there’s a hidden area to save her from this curse, she’s a very sad character.Update: encountered a bug at the end. After the final boss, the screen goes black. You can still select your inventory wheel. You need to fight the boss again and skip cutscenes to prevent this from happening.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to recommend this game, purely based on it's visuals and concept. But a game can't stand on a small leg like that, so if the premise intrigues you, get it on sale (like right now). Otherwise, maybe skip out on it.It starts off perfectly. As someone who has a great interest in cults and cult-type groups, it ticks all the boxes. It all is super promising, until the failed ritual, and everything falls apart around it.The cult leader goes from an uneasy presence to an idiot, only relevant at the very end. Why didn't he interfere with Jess more? Why was his potential wasted by not having him at least be a bit of an annoyance throughout the game, to give us a bit more flavour? In the end, you genuinely don't care.Speaking of not caring, the other cult members aren't treated any better. You can describe most of them in a single sentence. The in-game cult applications you find give them more character than any of the dialogue. You don't get any reason to care about them, besides some dialogue in the Gloom. You speak to them each once for one in-game morning, and suddenly you're supposed to be invested in them? There's no moments of personality or candid dialogue. And it feels weird for Jess to care about them as well, as they're practically strangers (besides Kim.)The Gloom is a great concept and looks fantastic, but because you don't care about the game's characters and the memories you get from them through the Gloom, it doesn't feel like anything more than a game mechanic to bar you from certain places for a certain amount of time.The Gloom's monsters are many, but they don't get enough encounters to really matter. By the time you've seen two or three, a new enemy is already thrown at you. Only the plant returns in every area, as a sort of cleanser, but any of the regular monsters are very one-and-done.The combat mechanics are alright. I like the weapons, the throwables. My only gripes are that you have to hit the enemy before being able to see what type they are, and you don't nearly get enough materials by the end for a full arsenal. Especially Twine is something the game seems very stingy on. The double dodge making you fall over is understandable, since Jess isnt exactly a combat expert, even if it's a little annoying at times.!!!SPOILER ZONE!!!!The ending was what made me audibly laugh with my friends. The big boss being all the faces of the cult members and Jess' sister, with Hannah sacrificing herself to summon it, was... A little stupid! I would get if the big boss held the face of Jess' sister, as that seems to be her personal fear, but to add the rest of the cult members despite not knowing anything about them, really fumbled the whole thing for me.I got the Mind ending. I've seen the other endings on youtube, because after getting the Mind ending, there was zero reason for me to replay it. It's objectively the worst ending out of the three, leaving on a very weird cliffhanger for no reason. Compared to the others, who have at least some semblance of a cosmic horror with enough closure, it's just disappointing.!!!!SPOILER ZONE END!!!!I would rate this an overall 5/10. Great start, great premise, great concept. Lack of care for the characters, disjointed and nonsensical story, no real depth and a feeling of it being very rushed by the end.

_childDocuments_.review: “The Chant” is a no-brainer purchase for fans of spooky, story-driven games. It’s a sweet adventure that doesn’t overstay its welcome and is best consumed in one sitting during a rainy afternoon. Now, let’s get the obvious out of the way: this isn’t an AAA release. But given that this is the devs’ first project and that it is a budget-friendly release, what is on showcase is bordering masterful. It has all of the makings of a great game, but you can kind of feel that it isn’t quite there yet. Mostly, the spotty gloss on the polish and the fine-tuning of some gameplay elements give away its budgetary constraints. No comment on creativity though: it is fully unleashed here. So, what didn’t I like about the game? Well, it’s got 3 types of XP based on matching different enemy types with the right weapons, which I found to be overengineered for no real reason. The good news? It doesn’t bog down combat in any cumbersome way. There are a few instances of forced writing that left a bad taste in my mouth, but that is only because the rest of the game is really well presented. In this release, atmosphere is king and it is very effective for the most part. That being said, the mix between folk horror and psychedelic imagery didn’t feel as natural as intended, but I do appreciate the creative effort for sure. There are a few elements of confusing game design, such as countering, which works just like in any other game, but the way some enemy attacks work are intentionally odd. This is also why I’d argue that having euclidean-inspired enemy designs isn’t a good idea, as these monstrosities would have a difficult time clearly telegraphing their intentions. All in all: minor gripe. The game is kind enough to present players with a fast travel system, but the moment in which I attempted to use it, I got a headache. I have no clue how one is expected to utilize this thing and I urge the devs to keep up being this considerate, but in more clear ways. My biggest gripe in this game is one specific puzzle towards the end of the campaign. I hated it, because it puts the entire story into a grinding halt, which is exactly the opposite of what I’d want to happen in an action-adventure game. If guides were not available online, I admit that this would’ve been the point at which I quit the game and uninstall it forever. Listen, because this is important: you can’t have memory puzzles involving menial tasks in games such as this. They are intended for an entirely different type of audience and when uncalled for, they will be hated. Lastly, at the start of the final chapter of the game, there is one absolutely absurd narrative moment, which makes no sense. I was tempted to attempt and break the game, but I didn’t do so. A bit after that, I found out why most people hate the last chapter itself. Truth be told: it’s not that bad; it just pales in comparison to everything that precedes it. TL;DR: If you are going to force me to go a certain way, don’t let me do a 180 and just leave the area. Then there’s the DLC. I appreciate that it offers more content at no cost to those who fell in love with this world. Personally, I was immediately put off by its implied roguelike structure. Oh, and by the fact that all of my progress from the main story — which the DLC is a direct continuation of, mind you — including inventory and skill unlocks was completely nullified. I mean, I spent extra time working on those upgrades, so losing them for no given reason felt like a sting. That was a total bummer, so I watched the “final ending” on YouTube instead. Now, I know that all of that may have sounded like I didn’t like “The Chant” as much, but I just wanted to make sure that I’m being honest with anyone truly debating whether to get the game. So let me spell it out here: trust me, none of the above is a deal breaker. The game’s world is inviting. The enemy designs are creative and worldbuilding is at a very high level. The writing is consistently great and the voice acting elevates it further. The soundtrack is fantastic: it has a unique and fitting flavor, so I purchased it separately too. By the way: the fact that the OST isn’t available on Spotify is borderline criminal. My favorite part of “The Chant” was undoubtedly the combat. Not because it was fun — I mean, not that it wasn’t, but hear me out — but because it showcases a variant of “fighting” malevolent entities through spiritual means, which is both satisfying and accurate. Instead of walking around and chanting, you fling smoke and salt, which is exactly how exorcisms in action games should work. Really imaginative stuff, felt very proper.I had only one technical issue during my time with the game: an enemy glitched out, remaining submerged and invulnerable until some mystical number of cycles passed, after which I was able to defeat it. Weird stuff. Other than the title needing a bit more optimization, though, it runs great, especially considering its graphical fidelity. “The Chant” is a really impressive game. It has clearly been put together by a team that knew exactly what they were aiming at. I hope that teaser at the end of the game comes true, because I’d love to play a more streamlined, better designed sequel that gives me more of this brilliant atmosphere.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, this game is a technical disaster: a stuttering, juddering mess. I played on an NVIDIA RTX 4090, so the issue is not power but poor quality assurance. And ... it doesn't really look so great for its 2022 release date, with low-resolution textures and janky animations.If you persevere beyond the bad performance you will experience an eminently mediocre game. It's a linear action adventure with some minimal exploration and puzzles, all wrapped around an unoriginal, predictable "horror" story, which is actually not scary at all.Combat is ... OK. It's all about timing and resource management. Annoyingly, resources you need for basic combat are scant, and if you run out you will have a very unpleasant time because there is no manual save: your only option would be to restart the level and make better choices. I managed to avoid that by the skin of my teeth, but you'll find many people in the forums who got stuck.To be clear, mediocre does not mean terrible. If you enjoy this genre and have played everything else on your todo list,  might prove satisfying enough, assuming the stuttering isn't too distracting for you.There are 3 endings, but you would have to play the game 3 times to get them all. It's definitely not good enough to warrant that.Finally  DLC: it's a "rogue-like"-like experience that is 99% combat. Unless you really love the combat in the main game, skip this.

_childDocuments_.review: The Chant is a brand new psychedelic survival horror game set on a remote island in which a spiritual group is preparing a special ritual to remove all the negativity accumulated from past traumas. Something goes wrong and the communion opens The Gloom, an alternate dimension that feeds off negative energy and creates rifts around the island, unleashing frightening monsters. You play as Jess, a girl who’s trying to forget the death of her sister by joining the retreat for the weekend. Soon after reaching Glory Island, you are quickly introduced to an interesting cast of characters, each one dealing with their own trauma. The narrative feels a bit rushed at the beginning, with some cutscenes ending abruptly and characters that could have used some more dialogues instead of instantly coming out with their negative thoughts. There are few graphical artifacts (especially on the protagonist’s hairs) and the facial animations are subpar for a story-driven game, but once you have accepted these problems the story gets more enjoyable and the gameplay becomes really engaging. Jess has three main attributes that constantly need to be checked: Mind, Body and Spirit. Haunted by her past, Jess suffers from panic attacks that are caused by the gradual depletion of the Mind bar, which often occurs when being inside the dimensional rifts or during certain jumpscares. If this bar is completely empty, Jess will panic, meaning she won’t be able to defend herself and will need to run away to a safe area where she can meditate. Meditating consists in trading Spirit points, which are generally used for Jess’ psychic powers, while the Body attribute simply consists in her health. These attributes can also be replenished by consuming different herbs and they can even be upgraded by spending crystals on the skill tree; these are hidden around the island, so exploring the entirety of it is greatly encouraged. There are also other ways to increase your stats, such as defeating enemies, reading lore documents and choosing certain options during dialogues. Additionally, there are three different endings based on the attribute you have developed the most.Following the classic survival horror scheme, gameplay features melee combat, abilities, resource management and puzzle solving. Fighting mainly consists in dodging, pushing and using three types of chanting sticks to deal light or heavy damages. Psychic powers can be offensive or defensive and they are obtained by progressing through the story. Resource management also plays a very important roll. The inventory is limited, thus everything you find must be either consumed, preserved or used to craft sticks (which deteriorate over use) or throwables, such as salt and essential oils. There is enough variety of enemies, from masked cultists to deadly flowers, and finding bestiaries around the island will help you to better understand their weakness. There are also some predictable boss fights, but nothing really memorable. Unfortunately, the combat difficulty is generally low and thanks to the lack of a stamina bar you can continuously dodge the enemies’ slow attacks. When not forced by the story, you can even avoid most of the enemies by simply running to a different area, and they won’t follow you. There is only one exception, which is a more recurring enemy that will chase you around the island no matter what, but there are still some areas they can’t access which are marked by a special sign. Despite the low difficulty and some predictable moments, gameplay successfully manages to build tension through the whole story. Few jumpscares also hit me unprepared and some enemies were somehow able to insta-kill me with a single deadly attack.Glory Island is divided into different areas connected through blocked doors that can be unlocked after finding certain keys. Some areas will also be inaccessible due to the colored dimensional rifts and can only be entered by wearing the crystal of the corresponding color (obtained throughout the story). There is no map, so orientating can be confusing at first, but the island has signs everywhere to ensure you are following the correct direction. Later on, you can even unlock a fast travel option, which I think is rather useless once you have unlocked every path and the island is easily traversable.While I never got bored of the setting, I couldn’t stop noticing multiple flat textures and dated graphics, along with the mentioned subpar facial animations of the characters. Fortunately voice overs are really great and keep you immersed in the dialogues, but at this price I was expecting a more polished game. As a survival horror, the experience feels close to ’s one, moving through the island, completing puzzles, fighting enemies (or running from them) and learning more about the lore by reading documents and watching films. There is something about  too, like the constant need to check your Mind sanity to avoid panicking, and other narrative references can be found from movies/shows like ,  and .It took me around 7 hours to complete The Chant on its standard difficulty, exploring every location accurately (even multiple times) and finding almost all the lore documents. You can definitely finish the game in less time and there is even an achievement for beating it under 4 hours. Overall, I was expecting at least three more hours of content, as the setting and its characters clearly have the potential to offer more, while the endings feel very disjointed from the rest of the story, as they don’t make much sense (particularly the Mind ending).The Chant is clearly rough around the edges, but it’s one of those games that I wish had a higher budget, more time and developers, ‘cause all the ideas are in the right place. The narrative keeps you hooked until the end, the gameplay delivers a great survival experience and the island is a pleasure to explore. While still an enjoyable experience, I can’t entirely recommend the game at full price, but it’s certainly something you should try once discounted, especially if you like classic survival horrors.

_childDocuments_.review: At first, I was invested in the premise for "The Chant". It has a quiet start, with moody scenes and an ominous setting. You are "Jess" an athletic and "no nonsense" kind of person who tries to live her life as best as she can, but has to carry a terrible burden from her past. Following the invitation from her friend Kim to join her in a remote island as part of a healing   sorry group, I meant healing group, yeah...  she arrives there, and well... not long after 5 minutes she doesn't even have time to finish her herbal tea and all hell breaks loose.That's a problem with The Chant, while it has many good elements in place: Good voice actors, good enough graphics (a very psychedelic color palette) suggestive music (a 70s rock acid trip you’ll soon forget), unreal engine, and possibly too much game mechanisms for its own good, it ultimately fails in putting all these elements together in a manner that doesn’t overwhelm the player.Shortly after the game intro, your main character Jess is going around the island looking for everyone to save them (partially understandable of course) which by the way, the few people that they are, they all go as far away from each other as possible.... why? Because of the story? No, because it’s a game and we have to make it who knows? But also, you (Jess) really don’t know this people. You barely talked with them and yet there you are, helping everyone…At the same time, when we reach each one of this illustrious characters, we are faced with them talking about their personal story, traumas and a possible descend into madness but wait... who are these people again? We barely know them, as in, NOTHING. That's possibly the biggest problem with The Chant, it has all these story aspirational points, characters, game mechanics but it’s all hanging there without introductions or transitions, it is almost like everyone working on this game had a different part of it to work on, and at the last minute just before launch they tried to put everything together to ship the game and... did it work? The game lacks direction basically. Because since you begin you are jumping from one part of the game to the next without giving the characters time to do or say something to even care about them (and having some documents telling stories is not exactly the same, it can complement but does not replace having some proper dialogue or narrative to get to know them) Same thing happened with the game itself. The Chant has a lot of mechanisms, like crafting hand weapons, explosive weapons, defensive fluids (?), each weapon specifically suited for this world or "The Gloom" and then also a skill tree with mind powers, body and spirit...All this is very interesting but really very heavily throwed at you, the player, almost all at the beginning of the game and then you have to work it out... in my case at one point I had to stop crying and switch to baby difficulty and only by half of the game I started to get a hold of myself... really it could've have used a more organic and extended learning curve...In any case, after all is said and done, I did get to enjoy playing some of the levels and story segments of The Chant, because the elements are there, but same as the game, it all came too little too late.

_childDocuments_.review: First, I should say that I love horror games, but I never feel scared.  If you scare easily, you might find something for you in this game.  While I don't think it's terrible, it isn't memorable either except for the setting.  I like the whole 60's psychedelic cult thing.  Although it was initially interesting, the story kind of felt flat for me.  You pick up notes and film reels that allow you to uncover more information about the island, but it just wasn't that exciting and I didn't get have the feeling of wanting to explore and discover more that I have had with more open games like Prey.  Even if I wasn't inspired to explore, there could have been other draws to the game.  I love games that make me feel invested in the characters, but I really  didn't feel invested in any of them.  The final thing that killed it for me was the combat.  It just wasn't very fun.  It's a short game, but I found myself wishing it were over about halfway through.  I know this sounds negative, but I really don't hate it.  I like that they made a story about something a little different, and I hope in the future they are able to execute it a little better.  The Chant is like a B horror movie, but not in  a complimentary Evil Dead sort of way.

_childDocuments_.review: Before playing  I had some gradual exposure to it through the Steam store page, and I wasn’t very compelled to play it because the trailers on the Steam store page the only exposure I got, and the trailers on the store page seemed to be hyping the game up a lot. While I appreciated the polish on the trailers, it didn’t seem to compel me enough to buy the game. With the obvious cosmetic microtransactions that are on the store page ($1.99 Spiritual Retreat Outfit, and $1.99 70s VFX Filter Mode), it further disincentivizes me to buy the game. But I’ve played it now and have some thoughts. ✅ – As this is Brass Token’s (the developer) first foray into a commercial game collectively, the mastery over animation sequences and cutscenes with the main character and tertiary characters is impressive. The seamlessness with which we walk through the world of  is wonderful, and feels good. Seeing as this is a story heavy game, I appreciated these sequences of ordinary cutscenes and interactive cutscenes. ✅ – This is legitimately the most organic part of the entire game. I won’t give an overview of every boss in the game, but I will review the first two. For me, every time I have been engaged in a boss fight, I understand what I am meant to do, and, despite further criticisms of other systems I will have below, it has made the game’s existent systems more enjoyable. The first boss fight seems misplaced and a bit random, but very enjoyable, as the mechanics seem to be fresh. The boss is not nonthreatening and gives just enough pressure to feel anxiety inducing. To be able to interact with the horror in the game gives it an additional sharpness to the feeling of horror.The second boss fight is a little less straightforward, as it does involve one of the game’s systems of damage that I will speak of later. Despite this system that is a little bit confusing in the first place, it felt good in this boss fight to be able to pick up resources around an arena, not be punished for crafting weapons, and to fight back against something horrific. ✅  – I really enjoyed the sketches of what the enemies looked like and the explanations of what they were, as this was great worldbuilding for the game. It made the enemies have a bit more depth, and the illustrations were interesting, too. 🟡  An observation I made from the very first parts of the story is the setup of the story seems somewhat awkward as we aren’t given a lot of context as to what the trauma the main character is enduring. Additionally, everything seems to hinge on the cult aesthetic and the two dimensions of this as well. For me, it didn’t need to have this element of what may be perceived as realism. It could break over these edges and be ambitious. 🟡  I feel totally unsure about the decisions that you can make in the conversations you can have with characters. I understand that maybe these conversational decisions have an outcome or impact at the end of the game, but trying to force the conversational decisions tie into the overcomplicated experience system seems a bit frustrating and seems to make people want to behave in a very particular way when they are making conversational decisions in this game.  ❌ – I understand that one of the objectives of making a video game and putting it out there is to make money and to help people make a living. I understand that. But whenever there are $1.99 outfits and $1.99 VFX filters on the dlc for the first game that you put out as an indie studio, it is entirely frustrating to observe the strong possibility that in the future there will be games that the studio will produce with the same cosmetic microtransactions. Now, I realize the studio has also put out a free DLC. That’s great! But there are still cosmetic microtransactions. ❌ – In the first few hours of the game I have unlocked what I can only describe as a red weapon ability, a blue weapon ability, and a yellow weapon ability. Additionally, I have had a corresponding yellow spiritual ability, blue spiritual ability, and red spiritual ability be unlocked. Now… With this as a foundation for the game, there are also corresponding red health bar enemies, blue health bar enemies, and yellow health bar enemies. Having a new type of enemy introduced in every section seems to be a bit much. Currently, I am still confused as to whether I need to use each corresponding color with the corresponding enemy. I understand this may be an accessibility feature, and having the colors is understandable in this case. But overall, I don’t think that we need different colored health bars for different enemies. It felt like it was trying to do too much. And I felt like every time I had to switch to the exact weapon that corresponded with the health bar of the enemy…❌ – There is an idea that I would like to enjoy playing the game and have fun. Fun for this game for me was to be able to experience a great, and memorable horror game that was an indie studio’s foray into commercial video games. This was not my experience I had, sadly. It felt like it could have been an adventure horror game with light survival horror/combat elements. The real point here with this criticism is that I didn’t feel as though I was playing the game. I felt as though I was merely responding to what the game had to give me rather than having a good time or experiencing something horrifying. That and the writing was also mediocre, but the setup and idea for the story are great.  I am somewhat disappointed with this as I had looked forward to playing this horror game for a long time. What I have ended up is not what I was expecting, as I was hopeful. On its face, the microtransactions immediately gives a sour taste, and as the game sputters along, it feels as though the scope of the game in total could have been reduced, and it could have been a great game. Light to a medium 4 out of 10. ❌❌❌✅✅
