_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game after watching the game stream of the game author going through the initial few steps and thought for 10 EUR i should give it a try. In the beginning it was fun to play a more text based narrative story with a rather well made sound stage. And the world building worked really well for me. But after about some time this initial experience starts to fall apart. Some of them are minor user experience flaws (too many clicks to move, not knowing where the story continues and blocks the 'next cycle'), and me realizing that I would have preferred a game with voice acting to connect better with the story.The point where this game really fell apart for me was the rather limited game mechanic that got boring quickly and the feeling that the offered choices were having little to no meaning to the process of the story. Yes you can choose which of the endings you want. Yes you can choose to help other characters or not, which then gives you a few more story elements (a good number are meaningless). But all in all the story felt linear, overly scripted, choices did not matter for survival (looking at you bounty hunter and the fate of the other sleepers). The oinly point where it felt meaning full was the Briar mission.For me the combination of rogue-like savegame mechanic with the story procession not ending up with so few meaningful choices and no real character development makes this game uninspiring. Good enough for a very rainy day. But in terms of world building and characters, i'd guess i would rather read the sifi novel instead of playing the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Citizen Sleeper is a fairly straightforward game with turns and dice and a bunch of choose-your-own-adventure  storylines to complete. Of course I don't know how different the outcomes are based on each decision, it's all hidden to the player but it's a sad universe, a dystopian future where greed and selfishness ruin everything (so it's a commentary on 2022). The fun of the game comes from inhabiting a different body/person in a far off place and meeting other characters and seeing which decisions pay off in unexpected ways. I love the sci-fi theming but, even for a socialist like myself, this game sort of preaches too much. I think a more subtle, less overt anti-capitalist message might make it more fun. I felt desperate for connection and kindness in this story so I chose to do anything to help Lem and Mina but it felt very bittersweet in the end.

_childDocuments_.review: If I had to summarise this game, it would be "cyberpunk Disco Elysium with a smaller budget". Unlike Elysium's fully realised open world, this time the space you navigate (no pun intended) is pretty much just a map screen. But really, that doesn't matter, because you're still going to be reading a lot of text, and when you're not doing that, you're rolling dice.Waking up on a space station on the run from the megacorp who wants back the artificial body they loaned to you, you're going to have to avoid starving, patch up your constantly decaying body, and ultimately choose a future for yourself.I mentioned dice rolling, but it's a bit different here than what you might expect in an RPG like this. You preroll a certain number of dice at the start of each day (called "cycle" here, because we're in space, get it), and then whenever there's a check, you assign the value of the die of your choosing plus any bonus given by the skill used for the check, and that determines your odds of getting a bad, neutral, or good outcome. Hacking instead requires specific results to succeed, and this is a good way to use your low rolls, keeping your good rolls for the more difficult checks. The system is very elegant and it makes going through checks a breeze, which is good, because you'll be doing a lot of them as you go through your daily routine. A lot of events are linked to timers, so you'll often have to juggle things around in your calendar to sync up various tasks.Ultimately, the point of the game is meeting and helping people. A lot of people. Citizen Sleeper has a lot of characters, with complicated backstories, motivations and value systems. You assist them in whatever endeavour they're on, and in return you get things that help you live another day. Those characters are all interesting and I had a blast spending time with them, figuring out what they want, and trying to help them achieve their goals. It's overall a very humanist story, which plenty of touching moments.It's somewhat short, for an RPG, but I think it's a good thing. Any longer and it would probably have felt a bit bloated. And anyway, considering how hard it was for me to put it down, it wouldn't have been healthy. We all need to sleep, sometimes. Yes, even game developers.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: This game unleashed something within me. An understanding. A revelation.Many people play video games to escape. Break free from the monotony of their lives and become someone else. Something else. And I do too, for the most part. For years now I've had a worry in the back of my mind about being forgotten. That eventually, down the line, no one will remember me. Every action I've made, every mistake I've learnt from, will have been for nothing. This game, to me, embodies that thought, and the breaking away of it. You are just a sleeper. Sure, you have abilities and attributes that normal humans don't have, but at the end of the day, you're replaceable. Frankly, in this game, you're a mistake. A fluke. You managed to break free of the chains of enslavement and slipped through the cracks. From there, You're free to make a name for yourself, help or hinder those around you and become more then you should've been.I think that's why this game resonates with me. I  to matter. Maybe everyone else feels this way too. This is why gaming is such a big part of my life. It allows me to feel like I do matter. That, despite these stories being entirely fictional, I can still make a difference to someone,  We all aren't born with the power or means to change the world. Some people are and will, but for self gain. And that doesn't sit well with me. Gaming allows me to express these frustrations by being someone more than me. Please. Experience this game. This game has, by far, some of the best writing and story I've ever had the pleasure of experiencing. Maybe I will make a difference. Maybe I don't matter in the slightest. But my sleeper does. And that's enough comfort for me, at least for now.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. People compare this game to Disco Elysium which has some merit considering the dialogue is delivered in almost the exact same way. However, the writing is far easier to comprehend and far less cryptic than Disco Elysium, while still maintaining the same level of depth. The gameplay aspects of this game are surprisingly addictive for a while, but get a bit repetitive towards the end. But by that stage you will be so immersed in the story that you wont care. 10/10

The game's structure is much more akin to the social side of the newer Persona games rather than the number-driven RPG mechanics behind Disco Elysium, but it definitely scratches that same itch.

_childDocuments_.review: This game rules! Be prepared for a ton of reading but if you give it a chance you will not be disappointed. It is a dense sci-fi story so take your time getting to know the setting. This game makes you feel like your actions have real consequences. It makes you think about what your next move should be. Feels like a traditional rpg like DND but innovates and does it's own thing at the same time. Would recommend to anyone who loves a deep narrative based game!!
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Probably one of my favorite games I've ever played. The audio/visual flair in the game is great and how the game blends in it's tabletop-like mechanics is fun (though I will admit that actual die values seem to matter less and less after you get enough skill points to get advantage on every roll), but the writing is what transcends this game. Nearly every NPC encountered in the game has so much heart that I couldn't help but complete all of them because hearing everyone's stories on this hunk of metal in the middle of the galaxy is an absolute treat.And in an interesting twist that I didn't quite expect, I wouldn't really consider any of the (currently) 7 endings of the game to be objectively "good" or "bad". It feels like the choices you make really matter towards the end of the game and how you handle the situations given to you and how you feel about them is truly up to you. Fully recommended, can't wait for the new content and I will likely start fresh with a new character sometime soon. Love this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: A narrative game about trying to survive just one more cycle on a space station.  Everything is a race against the clock as you struggle to make sense of a world, and to try to have just a little more control over where this story takes you.  There never is enough control or time and the very real question of what is most important; curiosity, family, or your freedom has to be decided.  In this cyberpunk world there isn't hope to get everything, and there will be doubts wondering if you made the right decision.  Just like real life there will be moments where there is never an ability to have it all, to travel down all paths of life.  Some times there will be forks in the road.I am happy with the paths I chose, and unlike life where we only can go down these roads once.  I will play this game again, unspoiled and find out what is down that second path.  But I still will be sad about who or what I have to leave behind.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of my favorite games to come out in a long time. I built rituals in the game because it felt so important to reflect on how far my character had come. Something as simple as finding ways to budget my money to make sure I had enough to feed my cat and afford my medications every day was a sign of how long and hard I had fought to make my life on the station better. One of the endings I didn't choose left me sobbing. Multiple quest lines had me in tears, both for choices I made and choices I didn't. This is a beautiful game with a wonderful system that I thought would be overwhelming at first but it is amazing at how it engrosses you into the stakes your character is living through. I cannot recommend it enough.

_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: This game got me so good, I loved it. Amazing story that felt so.. fragile. If you want an amazing interactive story that ebbs and flows with your decisions and tugs at your heart strings look no further. The game-play mechanics help balance the text heavy story but they're fairly straight forward and nothing revolutionary, it's just placing probabilities into clocks that count upward until you do or don't unlock the next thing. This was like reading a good book before bed, but if that's not your thing then I think it's okay to pass on this. Though, if you are okay with text heavy games or at least a little curious then I say give it a shot. Hope you find what you're looking for Sleeper.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Brilliant narrative. Effectively a choose-your-own-adventure story, with a light UI slapped on top. The visuals are deliberately minimal, but just enough to give you the feeling of really "being there". But you should buy this game is made brilliant by its writing. Some of the best writing I've seen in a game in years. Every character you meet feels so unique and authentic. And the tension! You are perpetually spinning just slightly more plates than you can handle. You find yourself forced to neglect things that matter... not because you stop caring about them, but because you simply don't have the capacity to do everything... and in those neglectful acts the game finds its central tragedy. The tragedy of being unable to fix a broken world, when you are just one small broken part of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: A well-crafted, gripping science fiction story with plenty of characters to meet and situations to resolve.I went in expecting to be bored, but instead ended up gripped by the game's writing and atmosphere.The art style won't be for everyone's cup of tea.The characters' portraits could have been more plentiful and emotive.Some of the tension fades over time, as you come to grips with what to prioritize most. However, making the survival aspect more difficult may have made the game frustrating.With that said, tension never completely goes away, as stabilizers are expensive. Engineer upgrades help a ton, though.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: This game more than pleasantly surprised me. The unique gamestyle threw me off at first, but I quickly fell in love with the immersive sound design and atmosphere, and was absolutely blown away by the character art (it's truly amazing). The tales, or 'drives', were all extremely heart-wrenching and really brought me into the complex world. I recommend this game to everyone who has an afternoon or two to spare; really sit down and just play it, and you're sure to fall in love. I am waiting excitedly for more expansions!

IT's sad and human and optimistic and I love it.But again if you are looking for a crazy action game this is not it. This is a slow branching story with some dice management mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: Nice snack. Entertaining story, manages to be well written and have just enough words to be deep yet not boring.The game aspect of it does it job for a couple of hours, then it gets old - it feels like an exciting survival race at the beginning, but then it gets a bit too predictable after.Choice is mostly an illusion, but it doesn't detract much from the experience. 6 out of 10.

_childDocuments_.review: As a longtime sci-fi fan I enjoyed it very much. I played it in one sitting. It doesn't really do anything overtly original with the story beats or the endings but the characters and the small stories are extremely well crafted. It gave me a similar feeling as reading the wayfarer series by Becky Chambers ( I think there was at least a shout-out in one of the achievements). it's true the universe is slightly more grim here but between the art-style and the upbeat narrative it left me with an optimistic aftertaste. It feels like home, it's comforting and satisfying.10/10 P.S: It has gameplay, sorta, but its not the main focus so I won't mention it much, I didn't feel any strong constrains or anguish over it. The challenge posed by the resources, money, energy, etc. is very mild.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very cool sci-fi story game that is a lot like playing a solo tabletop role-playing game. It's all immersive story and tough decisions, although I must admit it was not as difficult of a survival game as I expected. The writing and art direction is terrific, I was hooked right away. The only downside, as is common with this type of game, is that certain storylines seemed to vanish and I was never able to find a way to continue them. Sometimes this seemed like a case of where I was spending too much time on a different storyline and needed to expand the overall game world but in some cases those storylines just vanished altogether. Overall I did enjoy this game and I think I will play through at least once more just to see how the experience changes.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: I hated it. Important disclaimer: I am not the biggest fan of Play by Apocalypse games, and Citizen Sleeper was clearly doing its best to emulate that game experience - congratulations, it's quite close to the non-digital thing.That being said, the game also tries really hard to emulate Disco Elysium's writing style and eerie vibe, and here it fails. The intro is quite generic and tries to re-hash a tired amnesia trope into a deep sensual experience - yeah, all it did was force me to compare the writing between the games. Characters are not really interesting, usually hiding behind a veneer of implied zaniness, implied drama, implied depth. Everything implied and never delivered, as dialogues manage to be on the most trite aspects of what should be an interesting setting, characters being basically lore-givers with a a crust of personality or complexity. I'm pretty forgiving when it comes to games, so I was really really surprised when I couldn't find a single plot line or character that sparked a minimum amount of interest.So I focused on the gameplay, cause maybe that's where it's at. Spoilers: it wasn't. The gameplay is basically assigning different tasks a set of success odds you receive at the start of a turn. Sure, you can influence things here and there, but every turn also narrows the opportunity window to partake in different questlines - intriguing ♥♥♥♥ like "fix the ship", "work with scrap for money", "eat". Riveting. Problem is, nothing interesting happens if you fail a task. You get punished and that's it. Since you don't get much control on the activities, this is also one of those games that accidentally ends up inviting constant save scumming: you either advance the story or get punished after participating on a dull activity. The rewards tend to be resources needed to survive or advance other quests, aside from the occasional perk point that helps put the odds in your favor.The problem is that the game design doesn't invite exploration (as each choice for an activity means reducing time available to try and fail at other activities), doesn't offer a unique setting (basically a bunch of new weird tropes stitched together with classic sci-fi; the Hunter's shape in itself was a huge letdown, as was learning how little it mattered to get "caught"), doesn't foster strategizing (thus making me less connected to the gamplay), doesn't make good use of the music (great tracks that don't really resonate with the game and are barely noticed while playing), doesn't offer an interesting story.The art was amazing - it literally carried the game on its back and is probably the reason for so much praise: people are incredibly tolerant of games that look good.If you require something beyond pretty static sprites, don't buy this game. Not even during a sale. Go find the artist's patreon or pixiv and support him directly, support the sound designer and/or band who worked on the music, cause the rest of the experience is just soulless space disco elysium.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Overwhelmingly positive? Try criminally overrated.I cannot understand, for the life of me, how this game is getting the praise it's getting. Reviews praise it for its "well-written" and "realistic" characters, when in reality they are ALL extremely one-dimensional stereotypes. The player character is the blandest of all, and for a "role playing game," the very small amount of dialogue you actually get to choose seems to make absolutely no difference. Like, they're all just two or three ways to say the same thing, and the other characters' responses don't seem to change whatsoever. I understand it's an indie game, but good god. "One of the best games of the year?" "The finest video game sci-fi writing out there?" "A deep and well-crafted narrative experience?" No. Not even close. It's an extremely skippable and forgettable experience. If you must try it, wait for a sale, no way I'd spend $20 on this again or advise anyone else to.

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy sci-fi books, especially ones that touch on what it means to be human, this game is for you. It asks all the right questions and provides a plethora of questions. Both haunting and exhilarating, the writing, music and game play create a specific mood for your time on the Eye that brings the story home. I, of course, cried at more than one ending, and one in particular. So yeah. It's really good.

I was captivated the whole ride, having fun managing dice and meeting people, as well as seeing how they remain part of the story later on as well! love it!!!

_childDocuments_.review: This review may be a bit biased considering I love most media in the cyberpunk genre, but hear me when I say this: I often struggle with narrative games (given my potentially undiagnosed/untreated ADHD and a tendency to completely zone TF out whenever I have to read more than three paragraphs at a time), and I BINGED this game. _childDocuments_.review: If it's on sale and you enjoy other character's stories over yours, it's a good, maybe great game. Dialogue and character development is often heartfelt. Gameplay-wise, it's light on the RPG-stat aspects and very heavy on grinding. Despite getting through much of the main branch of the story in ~5 hours so much of that is padded juggling quests that need 4-8 turns (cycles) of wait time and grinding for dice rolls (actions) and the two constantly dwindling resources that impact how many dice rolls you get per cycle. It does a good job of putting you always on your back foot, but in a way that punishes decent and good players almost equally. Even in the almost end game I find myself navigating across annoying map segments trying to optimize actions per cycle because if I don't I won't have enough credits or item X. If I don't have enough of Item X, I'll need to gather precursor Y (1-2 turns), plant Y, wait 4 turns to harvest, and maybe need to repeat for yet another stage. In between grind for basic resources almost as annoyingly at level 30 as I did at level 1, all while dealing with 1-2 second delays on basic inventory actions because of an unnecessary timing bar.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR, this game is an excellent story teller, but it feels as though it needs more story.To begin with, I found this game by chance on steam. I picked it because the thumbnail caught my attention. I had heard nothing of this game developer, or game, and just bought it on a whim. It downloaded quickly enough, and I pressed play. I had no expectationd either way.What I discovered is a dystopia of galactic proportions where you are LITERALLY property, and probably sapient, but not considered Human. This is a factor that is hardly played into in the game, as pretty much every other major power considers the location you end up to be a rogue state, so you have just as many rights as everyone else, more or less.I'm a fan of dystopias, in writing anyhow, and this game proposed an interesting one, so the scenery is there. You get screwed by corporations as a daily happening, and you're lucky if someone doesn't mention your manufacturer in casual conversation.The game plays easily, and is pretty easy to understand. The tutorial could be better, but the game has very few mechanics, so it isn't too bad. The game is a story game first and foremost, and the story itself pushed me forwards... to a point. Overall this game is competently made, with a small handful of exceptions.The biggest problem is that the game is, when I went for every ending in two playthroughs, about 12 hours long. I could have done a fresh playthrough for each ending, but every mission plays out the exact same every time, besides whichever way you choose to fight the BBEG with a big ol' gun. Once you finish with someone's quest, you're done with them. You will never see them again in any real manner. You learn someone's entire story in moments. In game this is representative of what one might consider a couple of days, but when all you're doing is slotting dice into spaces, the time scale is lost. I will regularly complete entire missions is one "Cycle", and then have the guys I'm doing it for wiping their brow and telling me that I've served them loyally for a while now. Congrats.Essentially, for a story game, I feel it lacks story. I would love to hear more in this vein, and to meet these characters again, but I will have to content myself with finding another story game to quench my thirst for lore.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: A decent little story game about a little robot guy doing his best to survive away from the evil corporation that used to control them. While the gameplay is simple, watching the story unravel while you build yourself up from nothing is a really satisfying experience. Going from nearly dying to being fabulously wealthy with stabilizers to spare really does make you feel like you're growing alongside the narrative. And there are tons of interesting characters to meet and choices to make with them to dictate your personal story on the Eye.Give it a chance if the trailers seem interesting to you. It's a lot of reading and a lot of rng, but even without a guide an oaf like me made it through to the end of the expansion story just fine, albeit missing some achievements based on a few stupid choices. But that's just how the world works sometimes.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Don't get me wrong, the game is good, and its a marvel when you consider it was made by a single developer, but I can't give this a broad thumbs up recommendation.The game is most interesting during the first ~4 hours. There are many ticking clocks that you have to manage, which gives the game tension which makes you feel more invested in the stories the game is trying to tell. Once the problems causing those clocks to tick are dealt with, and you "solve" the economy, the game is riding entirely on the strength of its story, which I don't think is strong enough to hold the game afloat on its own, without the threat of mechanical failures.I reached my first ending ~6 hours in, but kept playing to try and get another, but gave up after 7 hours. I simply didn't feel compelled to play any longer.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic experience. This game is a joy to play through with writing that is engaging and cathartic. The overall gameplay loop keeps things bite-sized and interesting throughout. Maybe a little bit too easy - both resources and timers are quite generous. I would be interested in a hard mode where more of the quests had less-than-happy endings. Will definitely play through multiple times to see different outcomes.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this experience, and I say experience because this "game" is pretty much an interactive graphic novel, one in which it's impossible to lose or deviate from the predetermined story. It's very well written, and combined with the visuals and especially the music, it makes for a really immersive setting. Ok, the evil future corporate dystopia is pretty much a trope at this point, but there's nothing wrong with that. Now in terms of the gameplay itself, it does fall a bit flat. For about the first half of the game, your character is struggling to survive and save up enough money for the medicine that keeps you alive, all while you're being pursued by a bounty hunter who wants to kill you. It makes for a good setting. At this stage, the game mechanics of dice and clocks are still fun and interesting. But you reach a point about half way into the game where you aren't struggling to survive anymore and you have plenty of resources. From then on, I found the gameplay just kind of got in the way of reading the story dialog. I did enjoy the characters, although I think they were too nice overall. Pretty much every character had a "heart of gold", and in general, the characters were too sweet and sappy. There were exceptions but I think there should have been more nuance and conflict. My other criticism is that every class is exactly the same except for their artwork and whether a certain skill starts with a +1 or a -1 modifier. So class doesn't matter, neither does dialog choice until the very end of the game (when you have to pick an ending), and you can't die or lose the game in any way. Knowing these things, I still recommend it for the experience, and I'm looking forward to playing the three new episodes that will be coming out in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't hear anything about that game before, and honestly I was going to ignore it when it was included in this month's Humble Choice bundle, but it caught my attention when I started reading its description, about it being an RPG that's taking inspiration of traditional TTRPGs, of resolving outcomes thanks to dice rolls.So I decided to give it a try.And now, after finishing all the stories and last three episodes, I can safely say that I do not regret that decision. This game's a hidden gem. Try it.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: CITIZEN SLEEPER is nothing short of a masterpiece.Boiling it down to its absolute basics, it's a choose-your-own-text-adventure with simple diceroll mechanics you'd expect from a tabletop rpg, against a background of beautiful scifi cellshading and a dash of classic anime cyberpunk.But CITIZEN SLEEPER is so much more than that. The choices you make have consequences, some good, some bad, and most somewhere in between. With every decision, with every action you take (or don't take), you craft a narrative unique to your playstyle, and you become wrapped up in the story in a way most other games fail to achieve. You aren't playing as a Sleeper, you ARE the Sleeper.And at every oppurtunity, the game allows you to make your choices without pressure. With a couple of exceptions, at no point are you ever really forced to do anything. The ending you reach is up to you, however you want it, and each one leaves an impact.CITIZEN SLEEPER is a 10/10 game sits with you long after you've stopped playing (and it's just so dang pretty to look at and listen to).
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely beautiful game! The Eye is such an interesting and also sometimes terrifying location and I adore it! I love the story we follow and the choices we can make with it, the dice rolls and the many events really immerse you into the world, and even after you finish the main game there is still so much to do in the episodes! This game has hours of content and so many endings to explore, and amazing writing too! I love it so much and recommend to anyone looking for a strategy game with a beautiful story that will leave a lasting impact on them!
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Its essentially Disco Elysium and Persona in space. Its got that really good dialogue and atmosphere from Disco Elysium, except in space. Similar to The Expanse book / TV series in how it depicts humanities forays into interplanetary colonization. And its gameplay loop is based on a limited number of daily actions you can perform, similar to Persona, through dice rolls. Its a captivating system of micromanaging what you want/need to do to stay alive and advance the story. Buy this game PLEASE. It's such a well crafted game that it deserves a Disco Elysium style expanded edition with full voice acting.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: The themes around the struggle to survive, finding meaning in each other, and the shackles of society all feel honest and real. There are some bugs with tooltips and the BGM not pausing when a new track starts playing for major events, but those don’t matter. The writing is excellent, the characters heart-wrenching, and the atmosphere intoxicating. This isn’t a hard game once you figure out how to manage your resources, but it tells a better story than so many others. If you’re dealing with grief, an existential crisis, loneliness, or just like rich stories, give this game a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a beautiful game, in all aspects. It all turns into one mystical experience that keeps you so engaged, working to different story lines. Getting to know the characters, the bond and friendship you can physically feel because of how well they are written. This game is a must experience and I would recommend this to absolutely everyone, and their stray cats <3
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: i really adored citizen sleeper - came here looking for games like disco elysium and while they are not actually very alike, it, like disco, does a wonderful job of world building. i really loved the sound design and music and i really enjoyed the gameplay. the world was filled with interesting things and the text was easy to read. highly recommend for those who enjoy a bit of social sci fi !
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: This game nails it on every front. Gorgeous art, beautiful music, incredible story, interesting gameplay and outstanding characters. It's rare for a game to have every character be likeable, but Citizen Sleeper absolutely pulled it off. And I don't mean everyone's a good person; some people are horrible but damn I love to hate them.I constantly found myself thinking "just one more cycle" only to find a new story line and pulling yet another "one more" cycle to see where it goes.It's not too long, 7-10 hours depending on how much you do but it's impact is well worth the price. This is a game that will stick with me for a long time and has easily landed a spot in my top 5 games.10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Its a fun adventure game but in the end it felt a little tedious as the game uses 'dice' to do actions and a lot of the later quests felt like it was just tossing a lot of dice at a problem simply to extend the game.Also the they/them quota was a little high for my taste but as theres no romancing and stuff but just a lot of text it wasn't enough to turn me away. But being an old conservative the wording kept feeling wrong. All in all a fine game that had the vibe of thos old wall of text rpg's so a thumbs up.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like this game would be considerably better with Voice Over instead of just a novel's worth of reading.That being said, its kind of just really depressing and existential. Everyone's lives are sad and terrible and it really just bummed me out.The gameplay was fine I guess, but overall I found the experience rather boring and found myself starting to just skip over all the text near the end, which is basically the entire game.I'm sure loads of people will like this game, but its basically like picking up a book.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic narrative-centered RPG.-Interesting sci-fi worldbuilding and setting.-Great cast of characters, which are the main focus of the game, with their own desires, ambitions, agendas, beliefs, morals; with unique and engrossing backgrounds and diverse relationships with the player and their envoironment.-Excellent writing, characters and situations are charged with emotion and purpose, it varies from being relatable and relaxed to thrilling and heartwrenching; without ever being melodramatic or over the top. It is also capable of depicting some sci-fi scenarios in creative and immersive ways.-Functional and non-invasive gameplay loop: the choice-skillcheck based gameplay is very straightforward, it doesen't waste the player's time and attention with minigames or tasks, keeping the focus on the narrative. it's still important being the main way to pass time and gain resources or money, so it affects progression and the outcome of quests, especially timed ones, and therefore the narrative as a whole.-Very nice character artwork, stile, and interface.-Terrific, spot-on soundtrack.An enthralling and often moving experience, with a simple and neat "less is more" design.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Citizen Sleeper is a very somber and fulfilling experience outlined with hope. Can't recommend it enough for the story, but the gameplay slaps too if you're into resource / time management systems. It's flexible enough that bad uses of time won't sink a playthrough, but harsh enough to make you really want to squeeze all you can out of every action and decision.Can't wait to start a second playthrough... after I play some other games.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely wonderful and unique game mechanics. Excellent critique of neoliberal capitalism. Just enough insight into the future of neofeudalism. Not far along just yet to assess late-game balance, but it is very promising. EDIT (June 3 '22): most grammatical errors have since been fixed.Few other visible bugs so far. The developers put a lot of love into Citizen Sleeper and I anticipate there will be updates to further improve the game. Highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Short but sweet. Real human(?) drama informed by a deep and relatable sadness at the inevitability of systems failure.Far future rustpunk (laborpunk?) With themes of depersonalization, exploitation, cycles/revolutions, and identity/community. This is corporate utopia after the plastic has yellowed, the flashy neon has burned out, and software is no longer supported or updated.In terms of game mechanics there are some routine but clever gameplay loops that can be monotonous after 10hours of clicking but are in keeping with the theme of cycles and provide a simple but effective way to gameify what is essentially a collection of short stories on a decaying space station.The art style is very 80s/90s mecha anime in the best possible way. I was always excited when a new character was introduced just to see the portraits.Overall 9/10. Would be 10/10 if it was a little more closure on a few of the storylines but I can't really complain for $20. I hope this developer continues to have the freedom to make games of this caliber
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Great game with a brilliant narrative.Thoroughly enjoyed every minute of it, love the art style.Gameplay is basically resource management and after a playthrough were I maxed out the money you can have and completed all the missions I left feeling content.Not sure I'll replay it but there's the option to if I wanted to chase all of the achievements.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: By the time I was finished with Citizen Sleeper I had a few attachments in the ringed world of Erlin's Eye. I had grown close to a rough-looking cook, sharing stories as I helped him try new recipes. I had dived into a system-spanning conspiracy to "relocate" the people living on the Eye, hacking my way through trying and fix it, while imprisoning a murdering rogue AI in the process. I had momentarily melded my mind with a centuries old sentient being, and was invited to join it, though I elected no to so that I could stay gardening with my friend. And I finished my playthrough watching a family I'd grown close to drift away into space aboard a grand ship. I could have gone with them, but decided not to. After all, the Eye was my home now.I believe a good way to refer to Citizen Sleeper is as a melancholic space-cyberpunk game. It is close in vibe to VA-11 Hall-A and Shadowrun, and to Sunless Sea/Skies in structure, providing an open-ish world with dense nuggets of story to be found as you explore. As far as mechanics go, the game is quite bare-bones, but in a good way; you are here for the stories and the dialogue, the daily action-points based exploration merely serving as a means to space out the story beats. Though the game is still pretty clever in how it handles your daily actions. Citizen Sleeper lacks an overarching plot, but presents several mostly independent short-stories that explore concepts found in cyberpunk and sci-fi, while focusing  primarily on characters. The game has maybe 10 or so of these short-stories, some of which tie into the games endings, and it is likely that at least a couple of them will resonate with any given player while giving plenty of roleplaying opportunities along the way. A couple of these stories were a bit of a dud (I found Feng's arc a bit tedious), but I'd imagine that varies a lot from player to player. So bottom-line, this is a big recommend from me. Citizen Sleeper is a great experience for anyone that enjoys text-heavy games. Here's to hoping you're doing good Mina, wherever you are.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not usually into these kinds of DnD style of roll-dice-to-perform actions types of games, but this game captivated me in a way no game ever has. To put it simply, this game has the best writing that I've ever seen in a game in my life, period. And the game mechanics are simple and unobtrusive so as to let the language/narration take center stage. It has been truly an incredible experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: it's NOT for everyone.It's a game for those who enjoy reading and following the story set in this pretty dystopian sci-fi universe. It's not packed with action, it's one of those games that let you follow a pretty well written story. Treat this game as an interactive book with a few endings. It's great tale for a few evenings (or a couple of whole nights in my case) that you immerse yourself into, accompanied by a really good soundrtack.As other mentioned in, the mechanics is pretty basic, not all choices really matter and it isn't a Dark Souls difficulty level game - as I said, it's a story, tale to follow and enjoy.I finished it along with the first episode, done all "drives" etc in 16h total. I regret nothing, great tale and I crave more.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful visuals and soundtrack. The story is phenomenally dense, and the characters are incredibly memorable and worth getting to know. The idea of "the cloud" as a tangible concept is incredibly cool and compelling; this game does such a great job of bringing life into the modern world of technology and the corporate ruling class. One of the most memorable stories I've played through, I doubt I will encounter one as unique in a long time.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Play this game, immediately.The first time I played it I didn't stop until I suddenly was done. The next day I did the same thing. And then the day after that. Then I forced myself to wait until the last DLC to play it again, and did two more playthrus, and I'll be back into it soon.No game has so firmly entrenched itself into my heart so quickly, maybe since OoT as a child. Pure and heartfelt and heartbreaking and joyful and bittersweet, it's difficult to put into words the magic of this game.Citizen Sleeper is a triumph, and one of the most rewarding gaming experiences I've ever had. Immediately an all-timer.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: It's a really simple game, great for if you're just looking to kill some time with, the storytelling is quite good, moving even. In fact, one of the story lines was both my favorite and the most heartbreaking to fully thresh out. You can easily blast through the whole game in 8-10 hours if you skim through the story, but if you want to read EVERYTHING probably about a full 24, super short, super simple, super fun. 9/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: This game made me cry so often. It's exactly what I wanted from a cyberpunk/death-under-capitalism-hell sci-fi story. I was so enamored by the people and the city and the life I'd built by the end of my play through that I'd willingly fallen into a mechanically useless routine of feeding a stray cat and eating breakfast at the same shop every single day before setting off on the other tasks still left to do. I absolutely recommend this game anyone who's a sucker for these kinds of deeply human sci-fi stories about community and mutual aid.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: ✔️ Excellent narration with loads of interesting characters, high personal involvement, and a lot of hope despite all the hardships.✔️ Cool cyberpunk worldbuilding.✔️ Love to see deep damages caused by capitalism and corporate greed.✔️ Incredible synergy between the narration and gameplay.✔️ Wonderful musical ambience.✔️ Minimalist but beautiful graphics.💭 In the case of some endings, the rhythm of the game broke off a little bit because the task that triggers an ending "waits" for the player while in the narration it shouldn't. While I understand why it has been done - they didn't want to pressurise the players to make final choices with stuff still going on - I can't help but think that those tasks would have been more impactful with a timer.Overall, an incredible narrative game. Feels a little bit like how you could do a Disco Elysium on a lesser budget in the smartest way possible. I recommend it to anyone!
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing this game for just a short time so far.I like the mechanics and the UI, and the premise is interesting.I'm afraid I might be a little too ADHD for all of the quests (drives) I've got open, and with so few dice per day, it's starting to become a bit overwhelming and I'm feeling lost in it, almost paralyzed.  Me more than the game, for sure.  But it would be nice if there was some gameplay option for broken brains like mine, like some kind of a "story mode" where the dice rolls weren't important, and a little more could be accomplished without constantly worry about finding food, running out of money, etc...
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: In general I don't play RPGs. But this one is different. It pulled me in with the story and with the soothing game mechanics. Making decisions in two ways: choosing "text options" and choosing where to spend "resources". I am playing it without much thinking. The story and mechanics move themselves, somehow. When not playing I am thinking sometimes about the story, does not happen often. Try it out. For some it might be to abstract as there is only little animation. Occurrences and back stories and history which would be big cinematics in AAA games are told by text. It is a text adventure with a nice shell around it with a very nice "world", good characters, great drawings. Try it.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Imaginative, evocative, deep, and full of character. The gameplay is clever and moreish, the UI is absolutely superb, the characters nuanced and interesting, the setting compelling, and the player's decisions meaningful. You have a lot of freedom to express yourself through the choices you make.The presentation is stunning, the worldbuilding is fascinating without being overly expository, and the writing is not just excellent, but thoughtful, and the characters (whether ordinary, heroic, villainous or anything in between) are treated with subtlety and a warm undercurrent of empathy.This was obviously made with *a lot* of skill and passion. It also has a brilliant free DLC which expands the story. Kudos to the devs.This is great sci-fi with heart, set in a universe that feels alive. I can't wait for the sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Brilliant story interwoven with good player agency and choices. Tying player upgrades to quest completion is a great way of encouraging players to explore and discover all the questlines. If you're smart you can do almost everything in a single run in 5-7 hours depending on your reading speed. Can't wait for the sequel!
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: [9/10] If you want to read why I gave this score:Citizen Sleeper offers a rich, narrative-lead experience that can be completed within 10-20 hours (depending on how much of a completionist you are). If you like dice games, resource management, engaging sci-fi settings or just want to enjoy a story with a lot of heart and engaging characters, give it a try- you won’t be disappointed! [7/10] The game presents a tight set of systems that culminates in a neat balance of resource management and rpg-lite character progression. The dice, resource management and light RPG systems are likely not going to be everyone’s cup of tea, but I very much enjoyed them personally. If you’re on the fence like I once was, I encourage you to give them a shot!Incredibly fun and juicy in the beginning, these systems do well to support the story you’re thrust into, as well as the Sleeper’s growth over their journey on The Eye. Near the late game, however, the majority of challenges are trivialised as you overcome the resource systems. This lead the endgame to feel a little less challenging than you may feel it should be given the narrative weight of what’s happening. [9/10]Aesthetically, the game does a lot with very little. A combination of a well-detailed 3D model of the space station you call home, as well as beautifully rendered illustrations of the majority of characters make up the bulk of what you see in the game, but they do a fantastic job of adding life to the world and its people between the text.The interface, overall, is clean and easy to follow. At times I found myself wishing that some information was communicated more clearly, but this was rarely the case. [9/10] Citizen Sleeper’s use of sound and music are absolutely a carrying force for the game. Spacey, synthy beats drum idly in the background as you go through each cycle, evoking a strong sense of isolation and, in strange ways, hope. Hearing the soundtrack was what convinced me to take the plunge and buy the game, and I was proven right in that call. The music makes the best moments in the game.Ambient audio, like environmental machine sounds, are sometimes present, albeit it rather scarce overall. I feel that more ambient sounds and voiced characters would have really enhanced the text-based narrative that encompases the game. Given the size of the team behind the game, they did a remarkable job nonetheless  [10/10] No weird technical faults or crashes in my playthrough. 0 complaints!  [10/10] Absolutely the crown jewel of the game is its story. Citizen Sleeper presents us with a dystopian scifi drama about finding home, freedom and friendship in an otherwise lonely and unforgiving world. The flow of the overall story, as well as its characters, are fed at a healthy pace that keeps things engaging throughout and, thanks to the quality of the writing itself, holds up from the very first moments to the last. My first full playthrough was done over only 2 days because, like with the best books, I just couldn’t put it down until I reached the end.  [10/10] You can tell a lot of love went into this project- the characters, world, music and all the connective tissue come together to tell a beautiful story that I personally really connected with it. The game takes a lot of care into how it presents itself to you, and ends up quite an intimate experience as a result.Personally, this is a big hit, and something I’ll eagerly revisit in future as I clear out those last pesky achievements.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: This game made me rediscover emotions I didn't know I forgot.The writing is phenomenal, all endings are filled with so much feels, and you can tell great care has been put into the crafting of this game. To be honest, it jumped into my top 10 of all time favorite games in the first three hours of playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Citizen sleeper is short, however getting through the story is worth the cost. All the characters feel fleshed out and motivated and the story is worth the time to sink your teeth into.Even the shorter questlines are worth their time to read. The storytelling is amazing. Without spoiling any of the questlines each is well written, character driven and at times can tug at your heartstrings. All of the endings feel fulfilling.Buy. This. Game.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed the setting and RPG elements. It felt really rewarding to watch the world aboard the Eye unfold in front of my very eyes and to see a difference in the world, which I had caused. As someone who played Disco Elysium, this feels similar to some degree, so if you played that game, I absolutely recommend this one as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Great take on the visual novel genre, with good writing, characters and stories that resonate. Really makes you feel like you are living in a late-stage capitalism sci-fi dystopia, but manages to retain a hopeful message. Fully recommend for anyone who likes story-driven games.The one complaint I would maybe have about it is that the game seems a bit too easy mechanically, but then again, that's not the main selling pointAlthough I do have to give a disclaimer - there's a lot of reading involved.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine the gameplay as an interactive novel where your choices matters and takes you to different places in the story. Put in randomness in dice and voila you have Citizen Sleeper. That sounds crude, but its really elegant really. The story is way beyond what you normally got fed gamewise. It is interesting and compelling. The gameplay actually quit deep. Top game!
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Just an excellent little roleplaying game with inspiration from the Forged in the Dark tabletop system. Lots of possible endings but best played through just a single time. Despite how mechanical the interaction with the game is a lot of heart comes from where you choose to put your time and energy. Making sacrifices between taking care of yourself and advancing different story threads.I think the game could be improved by having more story threads but not incorporating them all into a single run. Randomizing some and sprinkling them in to give it a bit more replayability as there are 3 classes to play but no driving reason to play again.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Great text based rpg that has a very strong first half that keeps the tension high. The 2nd half is way easier though but that helps you have time to build relationships with the characters. The 3 bonus episode I'll say are not very entertaining though and brought the game down. Still for the most part I enjoyed this quite a bit
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an example of good story telling on a beautiful background. The only thing that would make this game any better is if they had it professionally narrated. I'll be recommending this game to anyone that expresses interest in story rich, attention vacuum games such as this. If this game had paid DLC I'd buy it, even if it was overpriced. That being said, the game is reasonably priced and I'll be paying attention to all future content from this publisher.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: An incredibly well written story supported by surprisingly engaging game play. By relying on evocative situations and the player's own foresight, Citizen Sleeper maintains a constant clip of both intriguing choices and risky situations that despite the outcome, always left me unable to put it down. Runs great on the Steam Deck.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: An interesting interactive fiction game. If you enjoyed the gameplay of Disco Elysium - dialogue with skill checks - you may also enjoy this.Update after more time: Playing through more of this, there is some great writing here. The gameplay is relatively simplistic, but don't be fooled by that - you will come up against choices that are going to be hard, and that will shape your character (even if only in your head).The Eye is a very human place, even if all of its inhabitants are not. You will meet people you bounce off, and people you want to work for/with. Don't be fooled into 100%-ing and finding every path. Be purposeful in your actions and decisions; mourn the missed opportunities; cherish the experiences. This is a game that will take up residence in your head if you let it, and although I will need to take a break before a second run, I'm glad I left paths unexplored for the next playthrough.Cyberpunk and science fiction at its finest - exploring what it means to be human through subtlety, and by showing humanity across its infinite diversity. Heartily recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: I usually dont like games with lots of text and tend to skip dialogues alot. But this game made me play it all time to the end holding my breath. It is a magnificent mixture of interactive novel, quest and management, all together experienced in my perception as interactive sci-fi tv-show. Many character whos story arcs naturally bind into solid storytelling... and also lots of "one more turn" moments. Incredible experience!
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: "Wake up sleeper"Citizen Sleeper is a cyberpunk narrative-centric visual novel dream.Backed by an amazing ost this narrative adventure game is one of the best of it's genre I've ever played,With table-top elements thrown into the mix the story of sleeper feels tense at times and impactful throughout your play through.If this game gets the Disco Elysium treatment and has all characters dubbed then i'm sure this will go on to be a classic for many. 9.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent game. Beautifully written, evocative characters, simple but often heart-wrenching music, and functional, fluid game design. Having played through twice now, I'm left feeling quite sad, because I would like to have stayed in that world longer. Luckily, the creator is releasing free expansions over the course of the next several months. The quality of the base product makes me certain that the new chapters will be great. It's important to note that Citizen Sleeper is short. Very short. Having played through twice at a pretty leisurely pace, I've racked up only 13 hours. But you'll be surprised how much this game can get to you in so short a time. I kinda wanna cry now. <3
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: HIGHLY RECOMMEND! It's a great resource management, point-and-click story game. I immediately got sucked into the story and kept wanting to play it. Learning all the characters and their stories was super interesting and captivating. There are multiple ways the game could end, so its really up to you how you want to spend your time in the game. I also really loved the overall look of the game.If you like story driven games, I'd give it a shot! Only took me like 3-4 days to 100% it. Got all but two achievements in one playthrough. If you wanna go the 100% route to see all the endings, I'd make sure to look at a guide!Only thing I hated was there was no overall sound setting so the game would always be blasting. Can easily just turn down your headset but if you're doing something else or talking in discord, its kinda annoying.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing.Is it mechanically complex? no.But what it excels at writing and tension.The game play loop at the beginning absolutely nails the atmosphere it wants you to feel. The desperation, the limited time. The feeling of just getting by. When this starts to ease, it feels thematically relevant.Some people say that this isn't a role playing game, just a digital comic book.While I understand where they are coming from, I don't agree. Sure it isn't Disco Elysium, or Baldurs Gate, Or pathfinder.But it doesn't need to be to be a role playing game. The more I engaged with the different options the game provided, the more I felt a personal connection to some of those places.[LIGHT SPOILERS]For example Talas Bar. It is not mathematically the most efficient way to make money in the late game. But I felt like my sleeper liked to go back there and work shifts with her. That's how I role played. Another example was the Commune in the Greenway.  Once you have completed a lot of the story there, there isn't a reason to stay there over anywhere else. But I like the idea that my sleeper was treeted as an equal there. Not exploited. And had found friendship with a really interetesting character. So they continued to stay there, and the Greenway largely contributed to the decision I made a the end of the game.My point is. its not a crunchy RPG and thats fine. If you want something crunchy, go play something crunchy.This is a unique experience and dare I say it, closer to interesting art than some games are willing to go.Its not expensive.Give it a chance and it will captivate you and make you feel emotions.10/10I can't wait for the next one or whatever else this team creates.

_childDocuments_.review: The best part of the game by far is the well-written dialogue, the main character’s dissociation and introspection, and the situation and world. I can’t say how much of that is my imagination, but I can at least say it hit me where it needed to for what it is. And then there’s the theme of you escaping from your past life and trying to pull yourself out of your situation by your bootstraps and by making new friends and connections, which is always a great theme. I think, overall, its narrative and setting hits a more relatable tone in the dystopian sci-fi genre, which seems more rare and difficult to pull off. By extension, I think it hits what Mike Pondsmith said, “Cyberpunk isn’t about saving humanity, it’s about saving yourself.”So I can certainly understand why it received as much praise as it did; though that naturally lessens the chance for the dev to hear constructive feedback. I suppose we’ll see when the sequel releases.Citizen Sleeper is basically a visual novel with just enough TRPG elements for it to make sense as a game. It was enough for me to want to pursue multiple story threads at once while trying to survive, and that’s really where the game shines. As we survive, we explore more areas to unlock more locations to meet more people and uncover more possible survival options or ways to get certain materials or make money, etc, and this expansion occurs across multiple story threads and areas at once (thanks to the dice allocation system) which is really neat.And yeah, I admit, some of the story beats and endings hit me pretty hard. Again, though, I don’t know how much of that was my own imagination or projection, because despite the fantastic setting and the MC’s situation, the game starts to fall apart mid-late game.There are some storylines that feel like they jump a little, like we’re supposed to have a deeper connection to a character before that storyline’s ending. There are a couple moments where I would force restart the application if I felt an option I chose didn’t make sense or I wasn’t informed enough or some such. Typical narrative issues in games. But honestly, the vast majority of the game didn’t suffer from these issues, which is impressive. There are a couple bigger issues that I have with a couple narrative beats, but that’s spoiler territory so it won’t be mentioned here.It’s worth noting that I don’t know how much player choice actually affects story beats or events or dialogue. All I can really comment on in that regard is that the dialogue options pretty much always had the choice that I wanted within the selection, and I think that’s a crucial factor when implementing dialogue options. Though that’s a whole range of topics for another day.The dice allocation system works because it seems to be there to encourage (or force?) players to go through multiple story threads at once. But it’s not that simple, because yes, there are cooldown timers on storylines when waiting for their next event to trigger. But what the dice system does is give you high values that are great for riskier events/actions, and low values which are useful in the  or otherwise can be dumped in safer events/actions. As you can tell, this also pairs very well with how each task or action has a Risk associated with it, so the higher the Risk, the more you’re punished for failing. So it seems like the dice system exists to try and get the player to interact between the game’s systems simultaneously, which is great. This also means it more consistently maintains the player’s feeling that the main character is different from everyone else as a Sleeper (regarding specifically the  tasks) and helps to push the game’s themes.The dice system was also integrated into the survival management, so the less Condition you have, the less dice you have per cycle (day). This creates a cascading failure system that you have to take seriously and becomes crucial to the game. Cascading failure can easily backfire in game design but I feel that it works well here. You also have to manage Energy via food. So basically, the survival management (Condition + Food) while making connections with characters and learning more about each location and faction, was quite interesting and worked as a system. You’re splitting your gameplay between exploration, story / character progression, and survival because of the dice system (and survival system), so it didn’t just feel like a book, and the dice system wasn’t just a means to an end (until mid-late game).So, when does the game fall apart? When the gameplay stops working. Mid-late game (or even earlier, from what I’ve seen most people say about their experience), the survival aspects are gone, and the dice allocation system becomes more of a chore and routine that slows down the game’s pacing without any meaningful choices or tension, so the dice system (which is the core gameplay loop) becomes a means to an end.You no longer need to struggle to survive — which could be a great, meaningful story beat if your situation changes based on the friends you make — but instead, the game throws a string of people at you who need things from you and that’s pretty much it. They’re well-written, but there’s this very strange feeling of loneliness and emptiness at the end of the game as you complete each individual character’s storyline. This isn’t an expected loneliness/emptiness that fits the theme or story. Even though there are many introspective moments, the game’s goal is to establish close friendships across factions with people of differing goals and motives — finding a place of belonging despite your dissociative situation, which, again, the game does well to maintain that theme of you being a Sleeper. These are definitely not disparate goals or themes at play here. This is more of a matter of an unfinished or unsatisfying conclusion or a lack of narrative consequences.Because, ultimately, nothing comes out of the experience within the game itself, whether through the gameplay or even the narrative. Heck, even unlocking new  is never an upgrade from these friendships. It also doesn’t feel like the survival aspects were assisted by the completion of the storylines (with rare exceptions). Instead, these people who we’re supposed to make connections with just completely vanish once their story is over. We’re not really friends with these people, even though we’re supposed to be. I wish there were more permanent changes or that the character relationships were more permanently established in some way, especially since some of the characters don’t have endings associated with them, so it can feel quite abrupt once you realize their story thread is over and there’s no other way to interact with them and the friendship has basically ended entirely.So both from a narrative and gameplay perspective, by the end of the game, it falls quite flat, despite starting off strong and nailing certain aspects of its theme, setting, and story beats that still stick with me. Again, despite these quite major issues, I can understand why it received so much praise because of the certain aspects that stuck to me. That just means the upcoming sequel has the chance to be a real gem.

_childDocuments_.review: While this game isn't horrible, it is really disingenuous and especially since most reviews are overwhelmingly positive I feel like I have to leave a critical review to balance that. Essentially, this isn't even a game- It is a novel that you click through. And not even a choose your own adventure story like it promises, but one where you are railroaded along with little say and no real ability to make meaningful choices. And constantly the game  you how to feel. If it was well written, you would feel something genuine. But the writing is mediocre at best and so the devs have to tell you that you should be angry or sad or whatever. At one point there is even a line essentially saying 'you had never realized other people have their own problems to deal with too' and it comes across like a condemnation on the player. IDK if this was a revelation for the developers but I think anyone with more than 2 brain cells already gets this concept... So even as a novel this is not a great experience. As for the gameplay you slot dice rolls into various actions to try to get successful outcomes. There is a little challenge at the very beginning since you don't have a lot of resources and are still figuring out how exactly everything works. But pretty soon it becomes routine. I actually didn't find things too tedious since I pretty much 'solved' the system by  Finally there is the setting, the real reason I bought this after being thoroughly disappointed by Cyberpunk 2077. But despite leaning heavily on the evils of late-stage capitalism and corporatism the overall effect is not any better here. Going back to that line above, yes obviously everyone has their own problems. And greedy corporations don't make things any better. Yet there is not really much else being said here and that is a shame. Great stories, and especially science fictions stories, hold a mirror up to life and reflect it back. But there has to be some distortion too, amplifying something or bringing small details into focus. Think of how Blade Runner used the Turing test to question humanity. Or how Brazil used satire to study free will. They all had something to say, this game unfortunately does not. Despite this so far pretty negative review, there were some highlights along the way. I thought the sequence with NOVOVEND, while not super original, was at least interesting. Feng's questline was also decent despite the obvious cliches. There was definitely some suspense with the countdowns for the hunter, the merc chasing you, fixing the ships for Bliss, etc as well. I also liked that you could get to see all of the endings on one playthrough if you  Ultimately I probably wouldn't recommend this game unless it went on sale for like $5 or less. However, there is a great sci-fi game you can already buy for that price. It's called . Pick that up instead.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a pretty good character story driven game, although i want able to completely finish it as i cant end the day to regen my rolls. The system uses dice generated at the beginning of each day/"Cycle" that you can spend on events, allowing you to prioritize where your good rolls go. even then though, you can get a "neutral" result on a 5, some upgrades seem way more powerful than others, especially when you get to a point where money isn't much of an issue, it really seems only like a beginning rush to specific upgrades to get even more cash saved for the end.The game does have some current day politics in it, which you can expect in any cyberpunk setting, such as "corporation bad" without any real nuance as you might see in other stories. There is also a commune that works on space magic if your worried about that sort of thing, but its not forced, and it more of a way to help you avoid a game over from health loss. By the point you get there, health loss is not much of a problem as its end game, kinda like how some upgrades become irrelevant.While it's nothing you haven't seen before if your into the cyberpunk genre, aside from it being in space, i'd give it a 7/10, being held up by the character writing and pace until about the end, where you can end up waiting for events to fire, and your not strapped for cash, so doing odd jobs isnt all that interesting. However, i should note that the developer is still releasing new content for you to play, so for 20 dollars or less during a deal, it can be a pretty solid game to beat during your time off on the weekend when you have nothing else to do or are waiting for other games to release/dowload.

_childDocuments_.review: i think citizen sleeper is by far my favorite cyberpunk game. it hits aesthetically and thematically and also somehow manages to completely avoid slapping on any of the things that feel genuinely bad about cyberpunk as a genre. typically, i'll have to wade through some uncomfortable things such as the rampant fetishization of asian people or ableism regarding people getting mechanical prosthetics. i don't have to suffer through any of that in this game. the game also doesn’t sell you this idea that playing to capitalism's whims makes your lifestyle admirable or more worthwhile in some way compared to someone like the Sleeper or anyone else on the Eye. being wealthy in the game doesn’t make your character’s world better necessarily. the ideology presented with the game feels significantly better than the ideology presented in other cyberpunk games that i’ve played, making it one of the kindest and most thoughtful games i’ve had the pleasure of playing. the soundtrack's also really good and meditative, and i'm really glad that i decided to buy the full bundle. the fact we keep getting free updates also makes this game one of the single best purchases i think i've made on steam. on a technical level, the poetic writing moved me to tears on a couple occasions. i'm a huge fan of the philosophical explorations in this game. highly recommend it. 10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: 4.5 ☆Great cyberpunk RPG with very strong narrative. The writing is top-notch, with great world-building, that you understand more and more as you speak with the different characters, and it doesn't do too much exposition at once, which would get boring. The characters are also very well-written, deep and flawed. The overall setting is cyberpunk, so it has that bleak nature, but the overall vibe of the characters and plot progression is positive and not bleak (and very progressive).I liked the gameplay loop, where you get some random dice everyday and distribute them how you want among the options. I also enjoyed that there are several time-constrained missions that make you feel the urgency of what's going on, and makes the universe feel more real instead of just reacting when you touch it. You're never too overwhelmed with missions, though, and can do most of them.

_childDocuments_.review: Citizen Sleeper is hard to discuss without getting into spoilers, as is the nature of a heavily story-based game. What I can start with is that it has a relatively slow start. There isn't a lot to do right away as it introduces mechanics and your character's situation is laid before you. In fact, the Sleeper's health (or condition) can feel very intimidating or overwhelming at first. My advice would be to prioritize exploring Bright Market between helping Dragos, the first person you meet. This will both get you money and eventually access to a stabilizing drugs for the Sleeper. During different playthroughs, I've discovered that the doctor  of their supply until you fully complete their quest line. Feel free to take advantage of this, because by and large most quests are not on strict timers, meaning you can relax and take your time. Any quest that  have an actual time limit will tell you so.The gameplay switches between the Sleeper's tasks and survival on the Eye, a dilapidated space wheel they've escaped to, and the ghostly data cloud they learn to tap into over the first few cycles (time periods). Almost all actions require the use of dice which are generated every morning, and the amount you get is based on your condition. Each "bracket" lasts about 3-4 cycles and the fewer notches left the fewer dice you get. Hunger decreases every day but is relatively easy to gain back by buying food or later methods as they become available. All of this will, of course, be explained in the game but it's nice to know about beforehand, right?There's around seven endings, though two of them require making very specific choices early on so you'll almost certainly miss them and, in any case, are probably best left to replays. The rest of the endings can be obtained during regular gameplay. If your ending results in the Sleeper leaving the Eye, the game will continue at the choice so you can opt to stay behind and keep going. There is rather a lot to do in the game as you follow peoples' storylines to their conclusions, so unless you're racing to the finish you can probably expect to go over 60 cycles before you've seen everything. I believe my original save exceeded 78 cycles and there's nothing really stopping you from playing for as long as you like. As you complete drives, and quests will sometimes consist of several, you'll earn upgrade points which can unlock perks or bonus modifiers to your dice. I think there's around 27 points you can currently earn, which is enough to get  of the skills unlocked.At the end, I think this is an amazing game and I'm very glad I played it. I was hooked from beginning to end. However, one caveat I do have is that Episode Flux, the first of the DLC story segments, has a very strict time limit and requires you do quite a lot in that period of time. It warns you that this is late-game content, but further warning should include having enough resources beforehand because it's going to take up a lot of your focus. It's certainly an  story, albeit only one chapter, but I do feel somewhat frustrated by how its handled.It is, of course, up to the player to decide how they feel, so take my feelings with a grain of salt.
