_childDocuments_.review: I'm not quite sure what to think about this game, there are a lot of good things to say about it so I suppose we can start there.First and foremost, the artwork is fantastic, the same goes for the atmosphere and Citizen Sleeper really excels at the world building aspect. It's pretty steeped in that grimy, on the edge of nowhere sci-fi setting and does a good job in this regard.The music also does a lot of heavy lifting, it's very atmospheric, sets the tone perfectly and pretty much every single track is an absolute banger.However, there are a few things that annoyed me personally... I don't know if it has something to do with me doing a lot of writing over the years but a lot of the introductions to different characters felt rushed. There were points where I can't remember them introducing themselves and then the Sleeper knowing their names. Almost every interaction felt like they were jumping in with both feet first, it could just be that some characters got a lot more love than others and if that's the case then... it shows.It's a real shame too that there are no branching paths to a lot of the minor stories, there's basically one big "main" story and that's it. The others don't really matter, like the one with the mercenary and her old friend or the bounty hunter. Like with the Telltale games, no matter what you pick, some of these character paths will not diverge in the slightest.Also, the gameplay loop of doing jobs, earning chits and buying the things you need is too easily exploited. I only ever had an issue with keeping my condition up in the first hour or two, once I realized what paid out most and what I could work with I never had an issue and was topped-up pretty much the entire game.Not to mention that being able to upgrade everything no matter what type of Sleeper you choose to start as... makes the choice feel hollow.Now, I don't point these things out to rag on the game, because I enjoyed my time with it and I do recommend it.However, I would love to see these things taken to heart for the next game. Improve the gameplay loop, make it a little more challenging and fun and either remove the choice of Sleeper or improve on the concept to make it matter. Give all the characters the same amount of love and attention as Lem and Mina, tighten up the writing a bit and give it a slower burn and add some more side-stuff and variables.The reason why I am disappointed in the things that I mentioned towards the end is because I wanted to spend more time in the universe of Citizen Sleeper. I wish the experience was longer and more polished but I do not regret the time I spent in the game and I am really looking forward to the sequel.Thanks for reading.

_childDocuments_.review: Stunning. Truly stunning. To paraphrase the game, I feel both a little bit more empty and more full after experiencing this story. Citizen Sleeper is a beautiful, bittersweet narrative about survival, hope, and finding meaning; and it touched me more deeply than anything since Life Is Strange. If you think you'll enjoy this game, take the chance on it; you will. I can't wait for the DLC.   - Hand-drawn character art that's both charming and expressive   - Relaxing, entrancing, atmospheric, and supremely vibey soundtrack   - Excellent worldbuilding and character writing. Erlin's Eye feels like a real place inhabited by real people   - Compelling plotlines that know when to apply pressure and when to let you breathe and take in what's happening   - "Inspired by the flexibility and freedom of TTRPGs" is an overstatement. It's more like a choose-your-own-adventure with dice rolling, time, and an open map. Not a problem for me, but some may expect more mechanical depth than there is here   - Grammatical & punctuation errors—not a ton, but too many for a mostly text-based game   - Gamepad controls (wired XB1 Elite) can be finnicky, with some dropped inputs   - Some odd UI bugs (the Drives menu frequently bugged out and refused to close unless I mashed the button)
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy Ghost in the Shell, Blade Runner, and other forms of cyberpunk media you will enjoy this game. The story during the first half of the game is very captivating with enough mystery and tension to keep you invested. However, when you reach the last few hours of the game the tabletop dice mechanic gets a little tiring (I am personally not a huge fan of tabletop mechanics) and by the last hour I was begging for the story to end. There are multiple endings and branching stories which means you can replay this game multiple times. Overall, this is a great game if you enjoy the cyberpunk genre and I recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: A really wonderfully written experience. While I would enjoy having full VO à la Disco Elysium, the script is so lively and immersive that I was right there time after time. The characters are wildly different and have believable personalities that makes them all really stand out. The character art is also so very detailed and a joy to look at.Gameplay-wise it does what it set out to do, integrate tabletop-style dice rolls in the actions in a lightweight way, but sometimes I did find myself wanting for a bit more variety. Thankfully the sequel seems to be doing something about that. Additionally there's sometimes a tad too much waiting on things and the game seems to suffer a bit from the main character doing everything, though I like how some events happen regularly that you have no control over, it gives the world more life.All in all be aware that this game is 85% reading and you really have to like reading to enjoy it. But if you do, boy are you in for a treat. I'm eagerly awaiting the sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy choices matter/cyberpunk aesthetic games give this a try. There is a solid 12-20 hours of content that is well worth exploring. I approached this game role-playing the main character with a specific set of values and ethics in mind and some of the choices I had to make were agonising. I highly recommend this game if the style of game appeals to you. Definitely a best-in-class contender.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is truly incredible, its writing and mechanics wrapping me in a story that makes me feel seen by a piece of media in a long long time. While I ususally struggle with text-heavy games, the writing and powerful character choices always left me wanting more. The straightforward mechanics directly produce the feelings of scarcity and urgency that games like Pathologic also aim for, even with the turn-based text intensive play. For every moment I spend in game, I spend three times that much thinking about this game in my day to day life, it's characters, where the threads might be going, and how the threads interweave. Also, if you are looking at my playtime, I'm long from reaching the end, I just needed to write this review because more folks need to play this.One of the best mechanical representations of the experience of chronic illness I've seen in a game.Game of the year, and it keeps updating with more.

_childDocuments_.review: Genuinely one of the best narrative games I've played in recent years. Amazing writing, great art, and a killer soundtrack! While the text-heavy, gameplay-light experience won't be for everyone, if you don't mind that then this is definitely worth a try!The survival mechanics of just trying to get to the next day at the start, slowly learning your way across the space station, until eventually you can get involved in slightly bigger things is implemented fantastically well. But despite this, the story knows well enough that it will never fully revolve around you, it knows you are merely one of many people in this place, and what matters not is changing all of that, but the individual relationships you build, and how you affect them, and they you. The fact that when I thought I was approaching an ending, and took the time to go around the space station visiting all these people I started caring about one more time, for no other reason than I felt like I had to before I might be gone, is a testament to how well written the game is.On that note I love this game's approach to endings. Where you can be following a questline, and suddenly be presented with an ending, a way off the station, a way towards a new, different life. And you can choose to follow that, but you can also always choose to say no. Decide that the life you've build on the station is worth more than whatever's out there for you. And the game never judges you for that, it's not a fail state, it's simply a choice and it will never force you to leave if you don't want to.And I didn't want to, I felt that all the people I met across the station were worth staying for, even as some of them decided to leave on their own. The fact that it accomplishes this in a bunch of hours of gameplay is absolutely magical to me. The fact that even between all the bigger events I got involved in, I found so much joy in simply having a job in a bar, and that's what helped me decide to stay over and over again, I think is what makes this game so special.So yeah, I truly love this game, and if it seems anything like something you might enjoy, I can definitely recommend you give it a try!
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Citizen Sleeper is in essence a virtual novel with board game mechanics included to give the player agency. They are a combination of worker placement and press your luck. Dice are rolled on each turn and they are the "workers" and the numbers indicate how likely an action is to succeed.  There are some light roleplaying and simulation elements but these are kept fairly simplified. Occasionally there are time limits but they are typically generous and did cause undue stress. The story is interesting enough and has elements of space sci fi and cyberpunk. While not completely amazing I found the experience enjoyable and want to see more games from this developer in this series.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: So, I've done my first playthrough of the game, and all I can say is, It is incredible as a story. If you've enjoyed Disco elysium, or any other narrative-heavy games with some TTRPG elements thrown in for some extra opportunity for immersion and suspense, then I whole-hearted recommend this game. I found myself utterly enthralled by nearly every set of characters, and while I'll try to avoid spoilers, I have to admit that the ending I got left me tearing up from melancholic joy, while also ready to jump right back in and play through again, as I still had so many open-ended mysteries to uncover and stories to complete. It's perhaps not a perfectly polished game as I noticed a couple small hiccups in the grammar and in the menus interacting, but every issue I encountered were completely avoidable and fixable bugs that most likely won't exist within a month, and if they do, it'll only mean one extra click with the mouse to keep playing uninterrupted.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: The perfect balance of optimism and pessimism. A cruel universe of heartless capitalism, while communism grows in its ashes. The systems of power would incentive people to kill you, use you, or simply ignore you, and some do. Yet, most people you encounter are kind and decent, just trying to make something of their circumstances.A must-play.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Remember the Citadel from Mass Effect? Imagine you have to build a life there, from nothing. You are a nameless android, needing repairs and food to survive. You have to manage your time and opportunities to keep yourself alive and find your place on this station.There is no combat. The challenge lies in managing your choices and resources to find a way forward.I was intimidated first by the stats and numbers, but the game is not that complicated. It helps you to get comfortable fast and being curious about this world and the story of the different characters you meet.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: As far as I can tell, none of the choices you make matter.The writing has some incredible sentences that are downright poetic and worthy of placement in an art museum. But as a cohesive story it... isn't. The story isn't good. This novel (that's what this is - much more so than a game) just isn't honestly a good story - in both plot AND WRITING.The few sparkling features this game has aren't gems - even turds can reflect light.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: A nice experience if you can get it for cheap. People do feel real although there is only so much to do and survival is not much of issue except for the bounty hunter/tracker problem you need to solve. I'm probably not going to play this game again as I've experienced almost everything in 8 hours and read the other endings on the wiki.Loading screens for each action means the game takes far longer than it should and you can't make any manual saves. Overall, I did like this game for its atmosphere and everyone's stories but it doesn't have much more than that. Your choice of starting stats don't even have much effect on your gameplay as once you get rolling, you quickly start getting and completing your quests and getting upgrade points which means it doesn't matter who you pick to start. The only difference it would make would be if you decide to keep your drawback to use the one point needed to negate it elsewhere.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Got this game last night and just spent almost the entire night playing it. The game is a wonderful narrative driven game. I will say the game is easy but that's not really a problem as you're playing it more for the story than just the game play.  Going into the game blind and picking choices without knowing the end result is best. There have been several times where I've made a choice that I thought was about to end my story only to find out that I picked the "more interesting" option and the game continued in a direction I didn't expect. I think my only real complaint is the fact that map movement seems to be controlled only by the scroll wheel on the mouse making it tedious to go through the nodes eventually. Though admittedly this could just be because I haven't looked too hard for another option... far too interested in playing the game. Excellent work to the developer and look forward to playing the sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Its a great transposition of Table Top dice mechanics from games like Blades in the Dark, and it conveys the sense of working against yourself along with your circumstances.  So well designed gameplay wise, sleek visual design, and a spot on sound design.  A great game to pick up for a few hours at a time then comeback to months later.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Skillfully written storythreads conveyed in a condensed and compact way.Gameplay immerses the player deep into the daily struggle of the protagonist.Pride yourself on every little achievement, and move on from your mistakes you will make.Find your place, purpose, meaning in life; and prepare your heartstrings for they will be tugged.This is a gem.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Outstanding. Incredibly well written, characters with depth and personality, under pinned by solid resource management system.  I found this game incredibly thought provoking, upon finishing the first ending I sat there processing the journey of my character, the sleeper. 9/10  Delighted to see a sequel on the horizon. Played through on the steamdeck, no issues at all.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Simply put, this is a very excellent game *if* you like the story. If you can enjoy a good cyberpunk story that is very loosely reminiscent of Blade Runner (mostly in regards to theme and tone), just play it blind, you're going to enjoy far more that way. Don't read any more of this review, or any others for that matter, if you're just trying to validate the purchase to yourself by scrolling through the reviews, you're just putting yourself at risk of spoilers, just buy it and refund it if you don't like the tone, it's pretty transparent in what it actually is. Storyline wise, *if* you can fall in love with the characters, it feels crazy immersive. On my playthrough, there were multiple points where I would sit there looking at my screen, thinking about whether I can trust someone, whether I think they could survive without my help, whether *I* will survive if I sacrifice some of the time I could be using to make an income to help them. It's at those moments that the game really shines. It punishes you emotionally, and it never stops feeling like there is a degree of hopelessness to it all. Every little success you get feels like one fought for, and yet, still ultimately meaningless in the face of those who control you. In an industry of superheroes and warriors, this is one of the best games I've played that truly makes you feel like dirt, just the absolute bottom rung of society. If you're more interested in the actual mechanics, you should know that everything comes back to the story, and whilst this isn't a bad thing (since gameplay elements and story should work in tandem for a game like this), it means that if you can't stand the storyline, you'll be left with a husk of a game. The actual tone of it is really really amazing, and if you're like me and stress over deadlines with an active counter each day, you'll find it really well builds up that sense of urgency and hopelessness. Still, it feels like the game is simulatenously too short and too long. By the time I finished, I didn't have time to finish up half a dozen quests, and at the same time, it got so trivial by the end of the game that there just wasn't any challenge at all, just a series of waiting around for the next quest hook to hit. It's a game that's very very good at making you think it's much harder than it actually is. This is not a game where Mechanics and Story share equal focus, it's more like the mechanics are a means to get to the story and most of the major "stakes" are held within the storyline, not the gameplay itself. Once you get to the point where you find a daily routine, it doesn't take long to realise that since the start, you've never actually been in any threat, and really, you've just been slowly getting more and more lee-way to pursue side quests. TL;DR: Whilst the gameplay is pretty fun, it is completely built around serving the plot. If you like the story, you'll like the game, if you don't (or are neutral/uninterested on it) you will probably just be bored by it. Play it for an hour, see if you like the tone, style and narrative, if you don't, refund it. This isn't a game that takes very long to get up and going.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: my god what a wonderful game. from the art & character art, the soundrack, the writing and the simple but meaningful resource management, this game is oozing from its pores with heart. it has multiple endings that you can go through. its not terribly long to play through, but man what a stellar sci fi game this is. i found myself at points being engrossed; visualizing the words being transported there.citizen sleeper 2 is soon - wake up, sleeper
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: I love just how immersive this text adventure game is, especially how easily you get the hang of the dice roll system. The artwork is beautiful, the story and sidequests have me hooked, definitely worth the money alongside the free DLC episodes for late-game content. Very much a cyberpunk game that I highly recommend playing if you enjoy strategic text adventure games in a dystopian setting
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: I started this game, then a year later decided to jump back in. Three hours later I'm thinking "Ok just one more cycle. I gotta do some engineering jobs then...oh wait how is it so late??". It's a beautifully written and crafted, deceptively simple game. The story is engaging, as are the various characters you meet, and you find yourself lost in The Eye, the space station that youre stuck on as you scrape by and try to avoid expiring as a corporate replicant with a killswitch that's slowly killing you. I love this game, it's extremely relaxing. Something about pressing "End cycle" then waiting to see what dice you roll for the next day.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good game. The gameplay is excellent. The stories are well-written and engaging. The character advancement is fun and customizable. The art is limited but well executed.I hate it, unfairly, for two reasons.First, I hate time pressures, and time pressures are a core element of this game. In any round you will have one to three red timers counting down to some catastrophic event. If you focus on solving the problem or finishing resource-gathering for any one of the timers you'll be able to finish most of them off before things go wrong. Compounding this is the fact that you can trigger new countdowns while others are still active, and be faced with multiple timers with Bad End written all over them. Learning to manage all of this happens in your first playthrough, and by your second playthrough you should be able to navigate the countdown timers. But to be honest, I found the process of repeated bad endings so unpleasant I stopped my first playthrough despite the game being worth my attention. This game punishes you for being bad at it- but also for not knowing what it expects. It's like a weird combination of Contra and old Sierra RPGs.Second, I play games to relax. I wanted to play a space RPG to have fun. In this game you play a character living through unspeakable oppression and making bad decisions because they didn't have enough information, being forced to choose between equally bad outcomes, causing pain and chaos despite best intentions because of a couple ♥♥♥♥♥♥ rolls, accidentally triggering a countdown, and a system built to pressure the player. It's 2022, fascists are multiplying, the world's on fire, inflation is double digits, and toxic chemicals are in everyone's bloodstreams. The last thing I need in my games is to watch end-stage capitalism crush interesting and sympathetic characters while I either stand by helplessly or make things worse. If I wanted to see that, I could walk downtown.Basically, all the parts I loved best about the game- the characters and the story- were stuck behind the parts I hated worst- time pressure, lose-lose decisions, and end-stage capitalism. There are games set in corporate hellscapes that manage to be not stressful and depressing. I really enjoy CP2077 and Shipbreaker, because those games involve screwing with corporations and fighting the system. This game's story- as far as I played it, poorly, before giving up- is much more about being crushed by the system along with other people you also get to watch suffer.This is a good game that deserves recognition and fanfare. I hate it and will never play it again for reasons that have nothing to do with the excellence of the production and writing and art and gameplay. There are some people who enjoy lose-lose decisions made in high-pressure contexts. Those people will love this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just beautiful. Simple, elegant, poetic.It straddles the lines between graphic novel and RPG. The storylines are gripping and suck you in. The characters are endearing (mostly) and really help to shape and inform your choices in game. More than once I got a lump in my throat as a story arc came to its conclusion - a testament to the incredible writing involved in this game.The play time is quite short (I exhausted every option available to me in my playthrough), and I can't see any reason for a repeat playthrough. But every minute spent in game is pure pleasure - it is well worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: I bought it thinking of just trying it out and refunding it before the 2 hours but by the time I remembered I was gonna do that 5 hours had passes, I love the music and I love the people in it the only thing I hate about it is that I won't "talk" to those people again, so here I am with a sad/happy feeling after finishing it in 1 sitting. Cant wait for episode 1!
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: I can't describe how good the writing is. The characters have so much depth, more than you would expect from a limited visual-novel style medium. There are so many great storylines, a few that made me want to cry. Plus it has great replay value, several different endings. I highly recommending playing through the main storylinee first, then trying out alternate endings on future runs. Good luck!
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: A quick game but fun. Good story telling. Simple interface. Easy progression chart for the character. Have played through one time and I liked that I could continue on even after finishing a story line. By 'quick' I mean that i finished it in under 9 hours so, keep that in mind if you like to consider your cost per entertainment hour.  From what I read, the story doesn't change much if you select different character types so may be the replay value after the 2nd play might not be that high. I'm not there yet though and the overall experience was positive.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Citzen sleeper is a visual novel in the style of a TTRPG. if you are here looking for mechanics and interesting tasks. I suggest that you wait for a sale. I say this mainly because, the turn system in this game has somewhat guaranteed outcomes making most of the actions that require actual dice inputs kind of trivial. The story though is were this games strength is at, the characters are well written and each ending is emotionally compelling. 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic story game that plays like a Roll-and-Write with some indie TTRPG flavor (that is to say, Clocks).There are a few more rough edges here near launch than I'd like, but typos and scene/character mistakes could easily be fixed soon.I do wish there were some more feminine choices in the art for the starting classes/frames and one or two more "endings" that might appeal to me more than the ones I passed over, but what's here is still very interesting.I'm not sure I can say I "enjoyed" my time on The Eye given... you know, but it  incredibly riveting and I'm already thinking about what my character for another playthrough might be like.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely setting and interesting stories and characters. Graphics are fine as well, as is the pacing; it's a pretty good game, moreso because it disguises it's nature very well. Citizen Sleeper is, like many games of this genre, more a visual novel that pretends to have gameplay when in actuality there is basically no failstate. Sure, you can try to deliberately fail, but there is no need to really think that much about how to ration money or you actions. The mechanics still manage to instill a certain sense of urgency, and that is great. And with 12h, the game isn't even as short as you might think. Sure, getting all/most of the endings is a bit boring, but you don't need to do that.What I liked less was how there were certain paths or character arcs that are unavoidable. Why again do I need to be in a fight with a bounty hunter that randomly kills a sleeper for a reason? Because the game tells me that was a badwrong action.Why is the most negative reaction I can give someone that wastes the sleepers precious time and money REPEATEDLY due to incompetence that I ignore them and apologize for not helping afterwards? Well, that's just the path the game lets me take. All in all that is fine for telling a story, but I wish the game wasn't that railroaded at times. What additionally annoyed me is the amount of nowadays seemingly obligatory identity politics in games; "they/them"s amass because apparently, in space noone is in a regular relationship anymore. But that's a minor annoyance and I suppose you've got to include these things if you want to be nominated for awards these days.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed the storytelling and writing in this game.  Throughout the main stories, everything is very well-woven, from the dream reality, to the 'soul' of the station, to the practical needs of the survivor, on a station full of survivors.  There also quite a bit of strategy involved.  Can't wait to see the conclusion of the DLC.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I think it was worth the money. The setting is quite well realized, the story has some interesting characters and overall interesting choices. The music is pretty good and the art is really gorgeous.The gameplay is shallow, which becomes apparent towards the end it was more about just ticking the boxes off than actually strategizing my next move. Yet, with that being said, I am looking forward to Citizen Sleeper 2, which should say a lot about how much I enjoyed the experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Citizen Sleeper is extremely fine. The dice system is somewhat innovative if a little repetitive, the writing is mostly decent, the overall narrative arc is an uncommon blend of hopeful and somber, and the save system is forgiving so getting all endings and 100% achievements was relatively painless. Unfortunately, for the most part neither the characters nor the setting really feel "alive", and somewhere around ~two thirds of the way through my play through I'd lost interest in the game beyond the desire to actually finish it. This is a case where it would be great if Steam offered a Mixed option. On the balance I'd give the game a 6/10, but if someone asked whether I recommend it my answer would be "not really".As a big fan of narrative-focused games, I've seen several comments that are both favorable and unfavorable comparisons between this game and Disco Elysium. I fall squarely in the camp that Disco Elysium is a masterpiece, and this game is not. For anyone who enjoys the genre and is looking for a similar experience to Citizen Sleeper (albeit with a different genre, and more plot-focused than character-driven), I'd give also give a strong recommendation to Roadwarden.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: I binge played this game over the course of a couple of days. My complaints? I have mixed feelings on the waiting element (i.e., when you complete a task but have to wait several in-game days to continue to the next stage) and there's clearly some balancing issues with the game's skills. So much so that many core, innovative mechanics become irrelevant deeper into the game.Outside of those two notes? This was a beautiful, evocative game with compelling mechanics, intriguing story, and a strong premise. I loved it. Even more than enjoying the experience, though, I find myself thinking about the game at random, even now that I've finished it off. As such, I can happily recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: join a commune and subsist on home grown magic mushrooms gifted to you by a benevolent ai gardener/god. ascend to a higher (digital) plane of being. screw a single father out of his only shot at leaving a crippled space station. or don't and join him and his adorable daughter on their way to an off-the-grid colony world. make friends with a vending machine. be adopted by a stray cat.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game with an original, effective and enjoyable mechanics, that smoothly works as a pace-giving engine for the unrolling of the story.The developer made it absolutely sure that anyone can play this game, enjoy it and reach some ending, giving a genuine sense to “inclusivity” through gameplay design. The game is very well paced, keeping an ever-present tension due to Damocles’s swords kept above the player (no spoilers). The characters are varied, consistent and you always get to see another side of them, even of the “worse” and “best” characters.I loved the mushroom and vegetable gardens part, and for me these are clear references and elaborations to the contemporary micoecological thought from “The Mushroom at the End of the World: On the Possibility of Life in Capitalist Ruins”. Overall the game is an exceptional achievement for a micro indie team.The game’s length sets an example, like in books did the birth of the paperback: yes, a game can be played in two sittings and be very good. Get used to it.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: What can I say more than this is an easily overlooked masterpiece. No for real. Though it might not be a whole lot more than a novel with a little ressource management added, Citizen Sleeper is almost perfectly executed and with no margin left hits my taste fully.We got a somewhat dystopic society with barely hope left but then such interestingly written characters which all have their agendas, problems and dreams. And that is all paired with choices of struggling either for your own life or for the characters you meet. At the beginning I thought it was a little difficult to really bond with the characters since you often spend relatively little time and dialog with them. However, the actual existing dialog paired with the felt intensity when a character helps you directly, promisses to help you or right out threatens you is balanced really well.I can not stress enough how much I want to recommend to give this a try. Even more so, since it is not bloated with text or places and factions. It's simple enough to get the big picture, well balanced in your typical cyberpunkish phylosophy questions and also engaging and intense to keep you pushing forward for your (ingame) survival.I love this game 100% for what it is.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not sure how many endings there are to this game, but if they are all as wonderfully written as the first one I just experienced, then I've got a lot to look forward to.  It reminded me a bit of Disco Elysium from early on, which remains one of my favorite games.  So if a heavy focus on narrative story telling is your thing, you'll probably like this.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really good game about what it means to be human. The gameplay loop is enjoyable, but it has the "just one more turn" issue. The character designs are gorgeous, and the writing is good. Ultimately very satisfying, but quite short. Highly recommend it if you're looking for a cyberpunk meditation on humanity.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing! I absolutely loved my first play-through and I am thrilled to hear there are more chapters coming so I can play more! My one complaint is that I cannot manually save so there is no way to quickly see the outcomes  and you need to play all the way through again to change something. A minor thing that I noticed near the end of my second play-through is that there is less urgency near the end of the game and it kind of trails off by the time you are trying to raise some mushrooms (which takes FOREVER to grow). This will probably change once they add more chapters, however. Overall, I love it and pray they keep adding content!
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: I don't traditionally leave reviews on Steam for a game. This game is absolutely wonderful. It has a really enjoyable difficulty curve that will leave you making tough decisions with out derailing your experience. The characters so thoughtful, and different.I try to call balls and strikes so the one criticism I'll level is that the UI can be a bit much. Busy, at best but downright confusing at worse. By the time I reached the end of the game (have not yet played episode 2 (free) DLC) I fully comprehended the UI but that is a long time for it to come around.The one feature I would add would be to allow you to click and drag (instead of scroll) to navigate the map. My hand tired quickly of that scrollwheel. It would also be helpful to have a key or some kind of sidebox in the open world, showing how many (or what) time-sensitive tasks were ongoing.I criticize because I love, however. I want no one to be intimidated or scared from a game that is so pure and loving and challenging, emotionally, tactically. I stayed up far too late playing this. It was a joy to look at, a journey reading through, and one I'm eagerly looking forward to jumping right back into tomorrow. I cannot wait to both replay it to make some different decisions, and also play the DLC. Looking forward to that third episode.Lovely game, tremendous soul. Left a lasting impact on me on par with Mirror's Edge, Gris, and other indie games. AAA Corporations would never.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, a really great game!I can't say enough about the atmosphere - both the music and the art come together to create a beautiful, melancholy world. The characters are unique and complex, each with stories that draw you in and leave you wanting to learn more about them. And I was pleasantly surprised at the amount of different outcomes in the plots, and how much your choices affect them.My one issue with it is that there's a rather large amount of grammatical errors. I found it difficult to continue reading after a time, which seems like a rather critical flaw for a game that's so text-heavy. I'm surprised that so many mistakes slipped through the cracks. It's not enough to make me dislike the game - I still love it. It just bogs things down a bit.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Citizen Sleeper is an exquisitely written video game that tackles a lot of topics in a very few words. The art is amazing, the soundtrack is haunting, and each character is unique.While you survive and make your way through the game, you quickly understand the game system, obscure at first but increasingly conveninent as you progress. If you like deep and well written narrative game, sci-fi atmosphere, and slightly light RPG elements, you should enjoy the world of Citizen Sleeper. Get ready to meet endearing characters, all confronted with harsh reality of future capitalism, face hard choices, and to make your own way in a unique depiction of transhumanism and society.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished it for the first time and I loved it. I bet I will give it a couple of more play through because there are a ton of quest that I didn't start yet and many different endings. An interesting mix of narrative game with "one more turn" mechanics. If you like story driven games, especially Sci-Fi/Cyberpunk you should not skip this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a tough sell at a pricepoint of 15 pounds. The gameplay is barebones, it's closest to adventure books where you flip to the page to see the result you got, maybe break out some dice now-and-then.The art is decent. The writing ranges from serviceable to engrossing, but it demands that the reader be introspective. Otherwise, you'll feel nothing for the writing, most people who play videogames are looking for pure external stimulation and are not looking to be alone with their thoughts. Just look at the screenshots on this store page. If you like the setting and introspective writing, it will appeal to you. But the gameplay can be mind-numbing busy work. Which I suppose is the entire point.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATED REVIEWBelow is the original review before the DLCs came out, if you're interested to see the development of my thoughts. Currently, I've played all the free DLC up to Purge, and here are my thoughts.Citizen Sleeper is a game that crept up on me and took hold pretty fast. I got lost in the world-building of it and felt it incredibly immersive. Part resource management and part visual novel, the game has an incredible writing style that hooked me from the start and I wanted to spend much more time in the game.Every DLC that came out had me running out the gate to slip myself back into the world, excitedly exploring the new story and revisiting old haunts and characters. It's rare for me to be so invested in a game's story as I have with this game and with the final free DLC finally over - I'm quite certain that it'll sit comfortably in my heart for a long time.-Original Review (Pre-DLCs)The game's fun and with great writing and atmosphere - which makes me wish the game was slightly meatier.Without spoiling, with a single playthrough, I think I managed to cover nearly every story out to their endpoints, with the only replay value being if I'd be interested to actually go down a more permanent route for some of the storylines.It speaks to the quality of the game that I just want to spend so much more time in this world with these characters, so I'm definitely hoping for more content in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely great stuff. What a fascinating game.The core mechanics are exceptionally fun. Simplifying decisions to a randomly generated set of dice is just smart game design. And because there are so many options, I never felt limited by the dice I had. Obviously you usually benefit from having a nice, fat 6 available to ace a check; however, some actions necessitate a 1 or a 2, so having a low die available never felt painful or annoying. And even then, if you were stuck with a low die, failing a check was rarely so impactful.But this is a narrative RPG, so hopefully these unique mechanics balance with unique stories. And they do! As a sci-fi and a cyberpunk story, this is a homerun. Everything always feels bleak, capitalist, sleazy, and gross. And yet there is just so much warmth in this game. All the characters do their best to look out for each other. Everyone is interesting, or has passions you want to learn more about, and the only frustration was that there never felt like enough time to help everyone. By the time you wrap up the game, you have so many friends, so many memories shared, and the space station changes so much (and yet not at all). It's all about everyone eking out a living, doing their best to scrape by, just like you.The writing is also generally great. Despite a few typos here and there (inevitable with a script this large), everything was solid and immersive. Everyone felt unique and I was engaged with everyone's stories and arcs throughout. The dialogue choices felt a bit limiting at times, but as they're basically just tools to advance the script, it wasn't a big deal. There were also a few times where I felt like my character was way more invested in a situation or plot than I was. On the same note, at least one of the arcs was... a bit much. But for what it was worth, the story remained immersive throughout. It also did a particular good job of exploring the digital world (something I feel many sci-fi stories struggle with). Not to mention the commentary on "entities," sentience, and what makes a life. All good stuff that was ruminated over from a unique perspective.There are some minor flaws. Firstly, the UI leaves something to be desired. The quest log is just bad. It does the bare minimum of tracking quests. But I really wish that it gave a summary of quests that was longer than 10 words, as sometimes between sessions I forgot what the main task was. The hacking mechanic also feels hidden away, and I felt annoyed that I hadn't seen the system for a long time in the early game. Finally, as much as I like scrolling my middle-mouse to move around the space station (a nice choice), by the end of the game, it can feel exhausting moving up and down the space station over and over. And with several sections of the space station separated by cutscenes, it just took a lot of extra button clicks that weren't necessary. It would have been nice if there were fast travel buttons once you unlocked new sections of the station, so you could get to where you wanted to go without scrolling and clicking around everywhere.But these are nitpicking at an otherwise tremendously well made game. The game feels dense, and there seem to be quite a number of endings. I'm only upset I can't experience them all in one playthrough.This game expertly scratches an itch that is so niche and unique that I can't even appropriately express what that niche is, something that only a very few games have been able to do effectively. Dystopic cyberpunk slice-of-life in space? Sign me up. Lem and Mina are the best, and I got a big tearjerker in the finale. Also The Stray is best boy/girl and my head-cannon is I took them with us when the game ended.

_childDocuments_.review: Really wanted to like this one given the setting, but it's at best mediocre.The mechanics are simple and uninteresting and the gameplay loop is simple and uninspired. The writing and characters are thoroughly "indie" which is never a good thing, and in this case really clashes with the dystopian setting. _childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: I'm giving this a lukewarm recommend. I don't think this game is going to convert anyone who isn't into Visual Novels or Text-Heavy Narrative games, but it's a decent effort in this genre.TLDR That had us in the first half, not gonna lieThe narrative starts off strong. The first few hours into Citizen Sleeper introduce a number of themes, characters and narrative threads that all compete for your attention and resources. Story beats are time-gated and initially there are some looming existential threats. Then by mid-game, you realize that none of this is real. The existential threats are hollow and carry no real consequence. The time-gated events are easily balanced and you are able to mostly complete every quest. The tension disappears and the game becomes a dice-powered grind to activate the next story beat. One specific gripe I have is that a number of quests are gated behind obtaining mushrooms, and as far as I can tell the only way to get mushrooms is through a long and tedious process that you are likely to encounter towards the end of your journey. I was unfortunate enough to have to spend quite a few real life hours doing the mushroom grind while I wrapped up some other quests I didn't care for, all so I could use the mushrooms to complete the quest I was actually interested in.The story is alright. Initially there are some exciting plot beats surrounding our main character, but those taper off by mid-game. After that you're mostly running errands for other characters. While some of these characters are interesting, it's very disappointing that there isn't more content surrounding the main character. I have so many questions about Sleepers, and I would have loved to have the game focus more on that aspect of the story.Hacking is another mechanic that falls off after early game. There's not much to it besides doing your dice rolls on the same map with a nice filter overlay, but the mechanic is mostly thrown away in the game's third act (with a tidy lore explanation, but still).Resource investments also really ramp up near the end of the game, generally making things take longer. I understand the desire to increase the stakes as the game progresses, but I think that could have been better served with harsher punishments for failure rather than longer time investments. This is a bit exasperated by the lack or "real" endings in the game. For the most part, when you "beat" the game, you get some dialogue that is identical to other dialogue in the game, the credits roll, then you're thrown right back into the game either immediately before or after your game-ending decision. I think the game could be vastly improved if:- There were real consequences for failure (death, game over)- The mid and especially late game had their difficulty tuned to be less about time investment and more about actual challenege- Force the player to actually make decisions that matter (Help X or Y character but not both)- Have real endings that reset the game into NG+ (with the above implemented 3 points implemented to encourage replayability)All this being said, the game was still enjoyable for the most part, especially the first couple of hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot recommend this game enoughIf you like good writing. Hell, even if you don't you should play this gameA lot of people talk about other CRPGS etc famous for their writing such as Disco Elysium, and if you're curious how they compare, this game is at the exact same level of quality. The only difference is D.E. is a game written by people that understand politics, whereas Citizen Sleeper is a game written by people who understand people. The messy emotional piles that humans are, and the tangled webs of drives, needs, and wants that is life. Fawning aside, if you just want some bullet points:+ the writing of course. I think I took about a hundreds screenshots just of absolute crazy-good lines. The entire game is still good, but the writing alone is worth the price of admission. Some of these lines here, and especially some of the artful descriptions of scenes, will stay with me for a while+ wonderful music, very chill, fits it perfectly+ despite the look this is not a dice-roller like a TTRPG etc. You won't be at the mercy of RNG, just your own ability to manage time and keep "plates spinning"+ survival mechanics done super well. Your character is constantly needing to eat and repair. Yet both hit a good balance between forgettable and overbearing while still nailing the presenation+ phenomenal art style, the whole UI and the big floating station never tire the eyes no matter how long you stare at it. All the overlays, effects, and SFX are well fitting, immersive, and elevate the scenes. Characters as well are near perfect in representing whats shown in the text. I mention a hangup in the negatives section but that's only a minor one with the faces mainly.+ phenomenal UI. Eveything is clean, lean, and tons of fun. Allowing players to juggle multiple tasks with ease while also making every single interaction still tactile and engagingThe bads (had to really strech for some, there's barely any)- character art style took a bit to get used to. The art is great, but the sometimes cutesy characters jarred with the otherwise bleak and realistic world. In time, I found it endearing and a helpful way to feel compassion for the cast. So don't take this as a true negative- Not much SFX, as it stands, there's only about three special effect noises. Not an issue at first, but it would be nice if there was just a bit more special effects for interactions. Maybe even just more sounds. For an example (that doesn't happen in the game) you could be tapped on the shoulder by the grim reaper or hugged by your long-lost brother and both would cause the same little ui effect and sound- Drive log. Its quite good, but sometimes mid-quest the log wouldn't update while the objective changed. While usually not an issue, would be nice if the text direction did. Especially for some longer, over-arching drives that players may come back to after long periods of timeSummary: I already said it at the top. This game rules. Its easily one of my favorites of all time and I will be pestering everyone I can to play it. Including you, readerGo play it!
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Not a bad game, I like it quite a bit. But it has to be said : the game is short, has almost no replayability value if you don't rush your playthroughs, and has no real difficulty unless, I guess, you blindly rush everywhere and randomly puts your dices without any plan or thinking.What I like in this game is both its dice system - that I find quite fun - and the overall melancholic ambience that emanates from everything. The stories of each character you meet, help and confront aren't groundbreaking, but they are done well enough that you keep getting that melancholic vibe. Anyone who helps you is probably doing it for their own good, even if they smile at you, and nothing free on the Eye remains unexploited - your good will included. Thumbs up to the moments of self-reflections across the game, that allows us, players, to emphasize with what a "sleeper" is going through in that world : the disconnection with its own body, the loss of the self, the fear and anger in other's eyes...The real good point, in my eyes, is that it's not cyberpunk about corporations dominating the universe, but cyberpunk about the aftermath of the fall of such corporation. Probably not that original, but refreshing enough to my taste.The sad part is that the gameplay itself, while at first pushing forth that feeling of disempowerement and need to choose one way to survive, ends up too easy and lacking real effects from player's inputs - thus trampling this weighted ambience : it's hard to get into the "maybe today's my last day" feel when I have enough money and items stocked to last me 2 other playthroughs and a half.There's also a small but interesting Stats points system that allows you to get better as you complete stories, but even that ends up making everything even easier than it already was. To be blunt, stats quickly become irrelevant due to the perks you unlock from them and how easy it is to specialize in everything at the same time.Moreover, for a world where sleepers are hated and treated like slaves, you actually don't really meet many obstacles due to your nature - only due to your working class status.When all's said and done, Citizen Sleeper isn't a bad game, quite the opposite. Just don't expect a revolutionary title or to spend dozens of hours in it : it's halfway between a light novel and a small RPG. But the universe is interesting, if you're willing to let yourself slip inside its rusted frame.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: absolutely phenomenal game, well worth the money and the time to immerse yourself in it. if you liked Jump Over The Age's first release, In Other Waters, you'll adore Citizen Sleeper: the depth of character, the themes of scifi corporate greed and the tact with which they're handled, the methodical UI that slows you down just enough to immerse yourself in the atmosphere that extra bit—if these are the hallmarks of the JOTA brand, then call me their number one fan.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was very good, but also on the short side (the time I have on record is how long it took me to finish all main story threads and side quests). The story aspects pull you into the game and there are a lot of characters who its easy to get invested in, and theres also a layer of resource management and scraping by to survive that adds to the tension. My one issue with the resource management part is that it ends up being too forgiving by the midgame, and can be ignored pretty easily, which takes away some of the urgency of the plot. _childDocuments_.review: Base game is really short (we're talking about like ~6-7 hours worth of game here—haven't played the other episodes yet and I'm not sure if I'm motivated enough to do that), I guess a computerized TTRPG just isn't really for me? I guess the mechanics are kinda neat but there's only so much fun staring at a space station and imagining your character is there running around and interacting with people and absorbing the unfamiliar world of the Erlin's Eye... Eh.Aside from the lackluster gameplay and presentation I honestly feel like this game lacks a dramatic conflict in its story. Sure, there's the whole gang business and the struggle to survive and the whole father-and-daughter plot, but I felt emotionally unengaged throughout the plotline because all I do is go between points A, B and C and do random quests that help me the heck outta here. _childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Cyberpunk, as a genre, tends to forget its roots in anti-corporatism and anti-capitalism. It forgets that it is stories about communities persisting and learning to thrive in the face of systems that seek to crush them into a fine powder, to better extract what scraps of value they can take. Citizen Sleeper knows its history, and the kinds of stories the genre was made to tell. It is hearbreaking, and heartening. It is, above all, a game about people, the communities they build, and how those bonds of community provide a strength that no one person can muster on their own. It is, in short, the perfect encapsulation of the 'punk' part of cyberpunk.It stands peer with, if not a bit ahead of, Disco Elysium in what it does for story-driven roleplaying games. The gameplay loop it solid, if a bit easy past the first few hours. But that's part of the story too--as you enmesh yourself in the community, you're not one person against the world. You have friends who will help you get what you need to survive. Of course it will get easier. In that community, you and everyone else can thrive if you rely on each other.If you liked Disco Elysium, or like the cyberpunk genre beyond the "wow cool chrome" meme, or just have an appreciation for well thought out stories and RPGs, there's no reason to sleep on this game. Even at full price, the 12 hours of story had more impact on me than any triple A game produced in the last decade.

_childDocuments_.review: there isn't much in the way of gameplay, it's mostly slotting dice into roll checks and hoping you get the good roll. however, for me personally the story of a struggle for survival among the decaying struts of the station and   systems piled on top of age old systems grabbed me immediately. it's basically a visual novel with dice rolling but it kept me entertained like a scifi book might. if you like that kind of thing, maybe check this out.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Citizen Sleeper is a game that I wanted to buy for a while now, but never got around to actually do it, because the game was one of those games where I wasn’t sure if it's actually *interesting* - I am someone who can get really annoyed with too much text and completely text-based-games are usually a bit hit-or-miss for me, so I really wasn’t sure about buying it. That being said: I can recommend that you buy this game SO much. Citizen Sleeper is an incredibly well-written, thought-provoking, very thematically coherent game that has an intriguing narrative, an engaging set of mechanics, a beautiful art style, clever and creative worldbuilding and a wonderful soundtrack. This game will be in my mind for quite a while, I think, and I had a wonderful time playing it.In Citizen Sleeper, you play the copied consciousness of a human person that was transferred into a robot, so that you can work as an indentured worker to pay off your debts. You escape the company you belong to and strand on an off-the-beaten-path located space colony that has tons of stories to tell. You have to struggle with keeping your robot-body alive, escaping and hiding from hunters and not starving to death while you try to figure out what kind of life you envision for yourself. The game does not follow one overarching narrative, but rather many small stories that all develop during your time in the colony. The story is very well-thought-out and filled with lovable characters and intriguing pieces of world building, as well as genuine, nuanced and developed overarching themes that don’t over-explain their whole morality to you – at its core Citizen Sleeper discusses the question of “what makes us human?”, but not in a cheesy or chewed-up way, but rather with genuine empathy and thought behind it. I especially loved that the game isn’t afraid to antagonize the player or create situations where the player has no real chance of winning because while you could argue that you sometimes get a bit Deus-Ex-Machina-d in the story, I loved how the story and mechanics really conveyed that it’s tough to survive on your own and your newfound freedom might be over any second. The story isn't afraid to put you in situations where you actually think you will die any second, and I really enjoyed that.I also think that Citizen Sleeper does a great job at encapsulating what a cyberpunk story should be about – the story isn’t just a cardboard-cutout tour to show how much injustice, corruption and oppression there is in the city – while there of course is corporatism, exploitation and blatant abuse of human rights in Citizen Sleeper, the story still tries to find hope in this world and explore how people are living under and fighting against systemic injustice and the story takes its time to actually look at systems of power that are active in the city and examine how they came to be – so to me the game felt like it was actually taking a very reflective look at our current society and offered both insight into how we might be able to prevent structures like this from forming, but it also argued that there is still hope to be found, even in a city like this and that this city very much can be redeemed, and I found that a lot more insightful than e.g. cp2077’s approach to the genre, which was more like “What if a city was like that? Wouldn’t that be f*cked up?”The game is so incredibly well-written and combined with the sound design the developers create a fully immersive experience – I was already stunned how well In Other Waters, another game by the studio, pulled it off to make you feel visually present in a world that you cannot actually see by using nothing but sound and description, but Citizen Sleeper really perfected that storytelling style. Visually you see nothing but the UI, some character sprites and a miniature version of the space colony in the background - but when playing the game, you can visualize the city and all of its districts SO well, the colony really starts to feel like home after a while. Coming back to the writing I also want to say that I took the transcript of the epilogue of the ending I had gotten and sent it to someone I know and *just* the transcript, with zero context to the bigger plot of the story, made them cry, so I can assure you that this game is very well-written.Citizen Sleeper’s mechanics perfectly underline the plot and tone of the game – it is a resource management game where you are constantly running out of time, money or food, as you try to follow the plot while trying not to die. Slowly, as you get to know the colony better and form an own kind of “community”, you start to slowly manage – it’s still not super easy, but it starts to feel less like you could die any second. What I personally loved the most was the aspect of “rolling” which actions you have at your disposal for the day. This heavily encouraged me to switch between tasks and I never fell into a “grinding-mindset”, where I wanted to invest all of my actions into making money on that day. The game in general makes sure nothing gets too grind-y, even things where I thought the game would expect me to do them regularly were often at least slightly changed over each iteration as the surrounding plot progressed, so it never felt like you were stuck in some daily routine.The map never got overwhelming, and you really get to know all the spots in the colony and start to get attached to the city. I found the game to have a pretty good length, where it wasn’t too short, and I did (I assume) about 90% of the content in the game without it ever starting to feel repetitive. My only real criticism would be that for the ending I choose, the game starts - with very little warning - to count down a timer and once the timer is over the ending cannot be achieved anymore. There were 2 or so storylines that I didn’t see the end of because they would have been done 1-3 rounds after the “deadline”, which felt a bit dissatisfying, since one of them was a pretty long storyline. So here is a cryptic hint you might want to keep in mind if you don't want to set off the timer on accident:  The other thing I found a bit complicated was that the game actually has very little linearity, which is a fascinating concept, but once or twice in the game I found something way too late (for example after the aforementioned timer was already ticking) or it sometimes messed with the pacing of the story a bit, but nothing that felt too off-putting - still, I can imagine that some people may actually have pretty badly-paced playthroughs.  Tl;dr: I loved the game and if you like cyberpunk and story-based games, definitely check out this game, it’s exceptionally good. It’s beautiful, well-written, and I was ugly crying during multiple plot moments.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: The game is great, very storydriven to the point is more of a novel than a game. The RPG elements are there mostly for some inmersion and after the early game they won't matter much, you can complete the game and see most of the endings in a single playthrough. The story is what carries the game; "The Eye" and the people that live in it.I loved the story: is very idealistic, rather than focusing on the darkness of it's cyberpunk setting it focuses on the people surviving and living in spite of it, in defiance of it, people just trying to build and make a future for themselves on a dilapidated station left free from the control of corporations mostly by apathy. Because of that the game will be spent less on interstellar conspiracies, futuristic politics, and rebels against the system and more on talking and building relations with the people of the station, helping with their troubles, and eventually choosing whether the life you build for yourself in this station is worth staying or you want to leave for another possible future.Ultimately is a game about people managing to be people in spite of a system that wants them to be property.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: The ultimate chose your own adventure book, Citizen Sleeper, is a roller coaster of emotion both heart-warming and deeply melancholic. Resource management game-play mechanics are simple and engaging, but this is all about the story. The game is set in a futuristic, intergalactic, late stage capitalistic society controlled by large scale corporations. Your only objective is simply to survive. Follow your drives to day-by-day discover more and more about who and what you are, and what is truly means to be human. Wrestle with themes of freedom, consciousness, friendship and ideology to make your story truly your own.10/10 - Get some snacks and maybe a box of tissues
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: I finished this in two sittings over the course of 24 hours a few weeks ago, if you want some idea of how gripping this game is. (10 hours for the base game at time of posting, +4 hours after all DLC played)There's not much I can say about it that others haven't said, the story, atmosphere, art, and characters are exceptional. While a bit of a cliche, "cyberpunk done right" is a decent descriptor. There's no wasted or superfluous story threads, choices are emotionally impactful and interesting. The only caveat I can provide without saying too much is that this game does lean more towards interactive fiction than an RPG, the RPG elements are more of a surface level way of interacting with the world and choosing your actions as opposed to more fine tuned end game "build" progression, multiple fail states, etc.; this game is telling a story, not trying to kick you ass, so this might leave some folks expecting the mechanics to drive the experience wanting. That said, I thoroughly enjoyed my time with this game. For folks who like story driven stuff this comes highly recommended, no further elaboration - play it now! For folks expecting a more serious hardcore mechanics driven RPG that gets increasingly difficult, this isn't it, but I would still suggest keeping an open mind if every other aspect seems appealing to you! Just be aware what type of game this ultimately is.EDIT: I've since finished the DLC and have little to add except that I thoroughly enjoyed it and its conclusion(s). While not particularly tough, (it's very easy if you're moderately prepared, especially so if all other story threads are wrapped up before engaging with it) I've already explained my feelings on that above so won't elaborate; it's not an issue. This final bit adds roughly another ~33% to play through, in a necessarily slightly more linear fashion (also not an issue). This is done to great effect with the introduction of new and interesting characters, revisiting a few others, and well structured/ paced narrative stakes that help flesh out this game just that much more. Looking forward to the sequel!
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: It's surprisingly difficult to describe Citizen Sleeper in complete sentences. It's a game that embraces its own wonderful kind of meaningful brevity. A short and sweet light RPG with one of the most innovative dice-based systems in video games. A story more interested in how you spend your limited time than wasting it on endless XP grinding. Ruthlessly effective character-driven sci-fi wonder. In short, one of the best games of the last few years.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: It's the easy comparison and while they both play very different, it's disco elysium but a lot less reading, and the ending I got with Lem and Mina was really beautifully done. overall 9/10, the actual gameplay left a lot to be desired but the characters and writing was compelling enough I didn't find myself too bothered.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: An engaging narrative RPG experience with good writing and cohesive art design. The story delves into several philosophical topics that are somewhat expected from a science-fiction story in a cyberpunk universe, but manages to present multiple compelling characters and quests that kept me interested. The time management and slight RNG of the daily dice mechanic never felt unfair and provided additional suspense. In my experience the game has slight balancing issues that lead to a feeling of being a bit under-powered and under pressure at the start at the game and overpowered by the time the endgame hits, but I think this will definitely vary from play-through to play-through and the order in which you do the quests. I am also not sure whether I liked the auto-save mechanic or whether I would've preferred to have multiple saves. I imagine this might be a downside for people who want to 100% the game, but don't want to do multiple play-throughs. I think a mode in which you can go back to re-do individual quests after completing the game would've been a nice middle-ground.Overall I absolutely recommend this game for the story, the atmosphere and the wonderful art. The devs focused on what was important for this type of project and did exceptionally well for such a small team.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: This game resonated with me on so many levels. From it's incredible science fiction brain tickling concepts (an AI in a 3D printer that speaks through the precisely-controlled movements of the print head's stepper motors), to the deep and meaningful connections between characters, to the simple routine of carving out a life for yourself in a hostile universe, this game weaves you into its narratives and immerses you in its world. I cannot possibly recommend this highly enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Like a good book, I couldn't put this down. The mechanics and narrative blend almost seamlessly to simulate the experience of being an android in post-collapse capitalism just trying to make it one more day. Like any good cyberpunk drama there are plenty of fascinating decisions to make - not all of them great but all of them with something interesting to say about identity and family and work. There are some cracks in the foundation: the third act takes too long to wind down, the game rewards generalists over specialists (undermining the character class system) and the narrative ultimately removes any resource accumulation stress, which takes the edge off. But the writing is great!
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: what to say. Citizen Sleeper is definitely an incredible game, though it does have its shortcomings.the story and characters are fantastic and well thought out. the atmosphere is palpable, and the places and people you see and meet feel securely placed in the world's day-to-day. The pacing is tight, the mechanics are innovative. however, most of this begins to unravel towards the end of the game, the systems easily perfected, and the number of quests low. anyways i wont spoil it. the game is 100% worth playing and will solidify a place in your mind with its characters and immersive world. oh also the writing is wayyyy too flowery and there are typos >.<
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Recommend... but gently. There are other, better games out there with a similar format. Disco Elysium is one that will be a lot more engaging in terms of character building/world building. The overall idea, though, is fun - and I am excited to see where they go with the new episodic additions. I would love to see more character interactions long term in this game, but alas; the story must flow on without them once you have completed a mission. But the few characters you do get to see repeatedly in different scenarios are sweet, and this game has a lot of good points about society if you read carefully. It's a chill game, enjoyable, good storyline, and has lots of potential, but I would say wait until it is on sale (unless the upcoming episodes really blow the game out of the water). The space theme of this is cool too - and I do like the dice system, as it adds a level of randomness to the game as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing experience, a great balance between unraveling a story and interactivity. At first I was skeptical of the Dice system it was going to have, but the more I played, the more I learnt how to adapt. Majority of the stories kept me on the edge of my seat.
