_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy science fiction and games that focus on weaving a narrative thread throughout your playthrough, chances are you will enjoy Citizen Sleeper.  If you enjoy tabletop RPG's, you will DEFINITELY enjoy Citizen Sleeper.  The writing in the main campaign are so descriptive and fascinating that I never felt as if the game needed more art than it had.  The art that is there is gorgeous, however.  I also wanted to mention just how much the game's music adds to Citizen Sleeper.  It adds a lot of poignancy that might not have been there otherwise.  The game's ambient, calming, relaxed music is something that gripped me right from the brilliant title screen track.  The game's dice system also works really well and is surprisingly exciting!  You can have easy days when you roll well, but you also might find yourself trying to deal with days in which your rolls are not as good...measuring each move and strategizing  how to keep yourself alive and fed, while deciding whether to focus on quests or self-care depending on your character's stats and the skills required for each task in the game.  However, as one progresses through the DLC material, your character will get so powerful that these decisions unavoidably get much easier...and whatever path you chose in the beginning will not really matter in the end.  In fact, by the time I was playing the third DLC, all my stats were maxed but one.  There should have been some sort of consideration of this IMHO.  Also, as much as I enjoyed the system in the main campaign, if one was so inclined, one could very easily save scum through the game and have no challenge.  Now, as this is up to the player, I don't feel it is fair to count off much for this...but I feel it is worth noting.As enjoyable as I found Citizen Sleeper, I found the most exasperating element of this game to be the length of the DLC content.   During my own campaign, I ended up finishing DLC Episode 1 and 2 while still thinking that I was playing the first episode (without feeling suspicious that I was reaching the end)!!  Now, if there wasn't such a protracted wait in between each episode, that wouldn't have been TOO annoying, but unfortunately, I get a feeling that the dev's did not have a lot of incentive to invest their efforts into lengthening the DLC's because they were free content.  This is so unfortunate, because I would have much preferred to pay and see something of decent length and of equal quality as the core game, because I was already invested in the story.  The third DLC is the biggest offender here.  Parts of it are wonderful, but there's just too little of everything.  The quests are predictable, and I was done with all the quests WELL before the game tasked me with the last event.  I felt that I waited half a year for a DLC that I beat in a day!! That is unacceptable and quite frustrating.However, all in all, even with the pacing issues, Citizen Sleeper is -absolutely- worth your time.  It is an unpolished gem that, with a little more thought, could have been something TRULY special.  But as it is, it is still special....and a very memorable and fun game.  And in the end, I am glad I took some time out of my day to visit "The Eye".  I would recommend Citizen Sleeper with the caveat that the player know ahead of time that the experience is short.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: A friend gifted me this game because I like Disco Elysium and The Expanse. Turns out he was spot on - Citizen Sleeper is great! It has a melancholic vibe, mysterious lore, political elements and LOTS of text.Citizen Sleeper is a bit more gamey and mechanical than Disco Elysium in that it urges you to manage your resources more. The characters also feel a bit flatter because there is overall much more harmony going around. A character who is truly bitter, cynical, or disillusioned is hard to come by, which makes for a suprisingly happy playable story given the bleak look of this game.My boyfriend eventually started calling Citizen Sleeper "the mushroom farming game", and even though it does not reach Disco Elysium's greatness, it is still more than worthwhile for fans of melancholic playable books with a scifi story about transhumanism.Oh, and it also has great LGBTQ representation. Always love to see my crowd in a story.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games I was on the fence on, for buying/not buying it.It got it on sale and was pretty much stuck to it for a couple of afternoons. Even though you are quite literally playing a faceless protagonist, it still felt like I could shape this character in a way that made me really care about them. There are different story arcs with their corresponding endings and the ending I got made me so emotional, I never want to see the other ones.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: Finished the game. Short but sweet. The quality continued at the same level and one of the songs has been stuck in my head for a few days now. I really want this developer to make a larger game with more content in this same style or universe. My main complaint is I wish there was more of it.I have limited time with the game currently but I am very much enjoying it and would highly recommend to fans of science fiction and cyberpunk. Worth the asking price and then some. I might come back and update when I get further along.+++Amazing characters and writing+++Great story and setting++Good simple gameplay loop+Visuals, art, UI, sound design, and music are all excellent-Gameplay elements/RPG mechanics are on the lighter side-Text heavy-Visuals are mostly static and character portraits, much is left to the imagination-For a cyberpunk game its lighter on the action side of things-Might be too easy for some, the survival mechanics are fairly basic and mostly there to show passage of timeI bought this game on a whim and could not put it down the first time I played it.I grew up on cyberpunk novels and games and Citizen Sleeper reminds me of the best parts of William Gibson short stories, playing tabletop Shadowrun, and countless others. If you're a cyberpunk or sci-fi fan I would highly recommend this for the story alone. I was pleasantly surprised at the connections in the writing, meaning that there aren't any ridiculous point-and-click-logic puzzles (this isn't Mystery of the Druids!). The narrative seems to progress naturally and you feel like the station/setting is  alive enough that you feel confident to figure out plot elements on your own. There is also a good degree of choice, partly through dialog but mostly through the actions you choose to take.The character writing is also excellent - I found myself so invested in them to the point where I was rushing to complete quests, hoping for a good outcome for them.Keep in mind this game is very much based on text with minimal visuals. I normally don't like this in my games (I had a hard time playing Pillars of Eternity to give you an example) but the brevity and minimal nature of the descriptions really helps keep me interested.The core gameplay loop is simple, easily explained and mostly a way to invest you in the story. That being said, this is definitely not a visual novel or walking simulator, there is more to do - think of it like a light RPG with no combat. I had some moments in the beginning where it genuinely felt like I had a lot at stake and was worried about every choice I made.The skills progression is fairly light. Despite there being multiple classes with starting debuffs and bonuses, you can pursue every thread evenly.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: This is a Cyberpunk Space Dystopia CRPG Linear Visual Novel - it has a story to tell, and that story is brilliant. Gameplay centers on the placement of rolled dice in order to accomplish tasks which serve to further the plot. Each day, or 'cycle', the player is granted a number of already rolled dice equal to their current health status, and 'spend' the dice to hack computers, work at jobs, and many other activities. Progress is rewarded with character interactions and plot events as the player character, an escaped synthetic humanoid with a living copy of an enslaved human mind inside, struggles to survive and find freedom on a vast space station. Compelling and fun, the game plays like an RPG despite essentially being a book. Genius!
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: This game is about the illusion of choice. For example, here is one objective near the beginning with a tight time limit.  If you ignore other tasks to beat the time limit on this one, the game just adds another task on so you can't succeed. There are I beat the game and the ending I got was basically "you succeed..but haha, you don't actually."
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: The main draw of the game is its story, which isn't good enough. Each character you meet has its own story, which is isolated from the rest of the game, exists for 30 minutes, and is then gone and forgotten, never to be seen again. The stories don't manage to pack enough of a punch in the short time-frame they are given.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Finished the game elsewhere before I purchased it on Steam. A surprisingly emotional experience with one of the greatest soundtracks ever. The only flaw I can think of is the fact that the dice rolls became less meaningful as I progressed further into the story. But that is a very minor flaw given how wonderful the rest of it is.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely amazing story, hands down worth the money for the experience. It's something that will stick with you for a long time. No notes, play it for yourself. You can reload after every/ any ending so don't be afraid of locking yourself out cause you can always go back. As for the gameplay, I have a few notes. Nothing that stopped me from enjoying the game, merely just a few pinch points. For one, the biggest one imo, the re-roll ability is busted OP. If you had to re-roll all your dice (before using any of them) it would be a really interesting ability, but instead you can use all your high rolls (Or low rolls if you're hacking) and then re-roll your less useful dice. It takes away from the challenge and randomness of the game. Considering that by the end game you've most likely got +1's and +2's in pretty much everything. It does make sense to go from barely surviving to thriving but with that ability you're just absolutely OP by the games end. The only time I felt genuinely challenged after about mid way through the game was the first episode of the free extension. The race to prepare for the supply run was amazing, although considering the events that happen after it does feel kind of meaningless in retrospect. But perhaps by re-playing the game and failing that event chain I would see more of the impact it had. All up just some pretty minor grips that I hope the devs will iron out for the second game. But boy. Oh boy. I will be there for that second game, you can count on that.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: It's alright, if you're fond of similar titles. Jump Over the Age clearly understands the ethos of cyberpunk, but Citizen Sleeper's world and the characters that live in it are a lot softer and easier to navigate than one might expect. I get what they were going for - most people are basically good, and just trying to get by while taking others into consideration as much as they can - and that's a sentiment I can agree with. Still, I found the characters a little TOO trustworthy, and I wish decisions in this game were more consequential.The game's core conflict (trying to get by while helping out others where you can) would have been more compelling if the game were more difficult, or at least had some kind of higher difficulty setting. I played the game sub-optimally, but was still easily able to reach a decent ending while helping out almost everyone I wanted to help out.It's passable, and I'm looking forward to JOtA doing better in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: This game is ... beautiful.Simple as that.I enjoyed the resource management. It made the playthrough a bit challenging, but really rewarding with each goal achieved. The music works wonders for immersion and atmosphere without being too intrusive. All the stories and characters are beautifully written and make the whole game an experience that I couldn't put down even for a moment.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic telling of a dystopian, cyberpunk-esque story. The characters are well fleshed out, the world has lots of mystery too it and doesn't give away all of it's secrets by the end letting your imagination fill in the details. And the soundtrack is phenomenal, always seeming to change the tone as you're reading at the exact right moment.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Citizen Sleeper is a visual novel about constantly looming deadlines, and the choice to push on even when things seem grim. The game is split into cycles, and at the beginning of each the player must prioritize the dice the game rolls to solve the constant list of problems everyday life on The Eye throws at them. For me Citizen Sleeper was at its strongest when I was finding new ways to solve these problems, often because of the people I chose to help. The game's characters all come to life as you spend the cycles helping them, and they in turn help you. The writing, artwork, and music all breathe so much life into the world of the game, and makes the small moments of triumph shine all the brighter. There are light RPG elements, and the dice management does provide some gameplay, but I stayed with this game because of the story. The mechanical parts of the game work to reinforce the themes of helplessness and inevitability in the story, and reviewing them in a vacuum would to me be like reviewing the font choice of a book. If you want a capital G game, then Citizen Sleeper might not be for you. But the story this game tells, and how its gameplay helps tell it, is some of the best I have ever gotten from a game.I wholeheartedly recommend this game to anyone who has even just a passing interest in it. I loved it from start to finish, and will have to play it again once I recover from the ending. In a sense I knew what my choices were leading to, but the bittersweetness stung all the same.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't know living a story vicariously through the main character was possible to this degree. Never before have I played a game and felt like I really, truly wanted to help the characters I met and connected with them. Like dying was out of the question because it would mean losing everything you built. The desperation to survive. The joy of barely making it out on time. The gravity of the seemingly small choices. The attachement to this strange cosmic spinning wheel you feel like you could truly call your home. The absolute devastation at the failed  that took a good few days away from the game to get over emotionally. The tears I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ shed at the DLC ending. And the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ character writing man. How was every single character unique and interesting to the point you couldn't get enough of any of them . I want a whole movie/book about the adventures of Peake and the Sleeper, please and thank you.This is the best DnD session-ish game I ever played and I'll definitely be here for the sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: i was surprised by how much i liked the game. It's not voiced, a whole lot of reading, few artworks, even the gameplay is minimal. But it's strangely relaxing and a nice story.If you like reading books, this is effectively a visual novel.It plays out a bit like the social part of the persona games. Choose who to spend your time and progress their story while planning the optimal schedule. problems:It was a little hard at first, but towards the later half of the mid-game it becomes extremely easy. I had 1000 money, (Food costs 15 every 3 days, so 1000 is a lot) 20 scraps, 5 stabilisers, all kinds of mushrooms... It effectively killed any strategy or gameplay, since by that point all you're doing is managing your time. Also you can rig the game pretty easily. You never lose heath unless you go to sleep starving, so you only need one energy block. (Could be a bug). With the engineer perk you get scrap by doing missions and you can use that scrap to heal yourself, which means I never had to buy a stabiliser which was a big part of the game. And the operator perk made the hacking missions super easy, since you had 2/6 chance and 6 rolls to have the dice you need, it's pretty much a guaranteed win. It's not bad, it's just a bit unbalanced.Some missions can be easily failed if you don't pay attention the description. And the game auto-saves, so no save scumming. Also, I'll add the endings are a little underwhelming. No artwork or big closing statement. It's kinda like:"You did the thing, you are happy you did the thing.""You did the thing, you're unsure about the thing."It's definitely about the journey, not the ending.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Sleeper is a fun story-driven adventure. There is no combat. Just you doing jobs earn money, food, and medical supplies to survive another day. The individual stories within the game have multiple paths and are engaging. Several stories end towards one of several multiple endings. However, you can easily reload your last save and keep working to finish the other stories that end with a credit roll. You don't have to restart the entire game unless you want to try different choices and outcomes. Overall, a nice visual novel.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Amazingly written visual novel pretending to be an RPG. There are very few choices in the game but the characters and their stories just suck you in. The dice and resource management is kinda interesting, it incentivizes taking it slow and living one day at a time but it can be frustrating once or twice. The soundtrack is also sublime. Solid 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Citizen Sleeper had a great story to follow along with. I found myself feeling attached to each of the characters as I went along. I made the mistake of pursuing all the story threads throughout the game, so it wound up feeling like a bit of a completion exercise, requiring a bit of sleeping to progress timers at the end rather than having made impactful choices throughout the story and discovering my fate. You can get multiple endings per run.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: if you like worldbuilding, scifi, and the daily struggles of a kind-of-robot in a society that really does not like them, then you would like this game.great storylines and satisfying (if occasionally repetitive by the endgame) gameplay, but the best part is the developed narrative that comes by the choices you make and the order you do things in. i loved seeing my sleeper go about their daily life, and you start to really feel in character as them as you play. you will have a lot of fun with this game if you like emergent narrative as a concept!
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Citizen Sleeper is a visual novel, and nothing more.  If that's what you're looking for, this might be your game.  If you want meaningful gameplay, choices that actually matter, and some degree of player skill influencing outcomes, look elsewhere.There was a moment or two in the early game where I was concerned that a bad decision might end my game early - that I could actually lose because I wasn't careful or got bad rolls.  (Game actions are based on a random dice system.)  After that, it was smooth sailing.  I strongly suspect the game won't actually let you lose before it's time, and I'm positive that, with very minimal exceptions, dialogue choices don't matter one bit.Most of the game is just going through the motions.  As long as you keep your condition up (which I had no difficulty with), you just do all the tasks as they become available.  If you CAN'T keep your condition up, I imagine the game could get very frustrating, as you have very few actions to take each day and no great way to catch up.Citizen Sleeper is long-winded, a little predictable, and preachier than I'd like, but maybe this sort of game isn't for me.  That said, because it's not for me, I also have difficulty recommending this game to others.  For six hours of gameplay, there are likely better ways to spend your money, especially if you're not getting it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: If you are into space opera, transhumanism, cyperpunk-esque narratives, you're going to have a great time with this one. Even with my rampant ADHD, this game has kept my focus for a lot longer than most games. The music is banging and the story is rich and diverse with a lot of awesome twists and turns. Go and grab your chits and buy some drugs.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: I finished just about every ending in this game. 22/27 achievements will do for now because this game makes me feel mildly depressed and I found it hard to get through as a follow up recommended to me after Disco Elysium, which is a rather hopeful game. The writing was decent, but the empty and lonely feelings of the games - of everyone leaving you or hurting you or betraying you or trying to kill you or discriminating against you or even just the feeling of "this place is ♥♥♥♥♥♥, do you wanna stay on a doomed station or leave" was rough. I really loved the art style, I liked the gameplay mechanics, it was easy enough to get the hang of and understand what's going on. I think most people will probably know just looking at the images, description, and genre whether they would like this game, but I would be selective about recommending this game, unlike The Cat Lady or DE. Despite the fact that I don't love games that feel hopeless to me, I still wishlisted Citizen Sleeper 2...
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an incredibly humbling and human experience. It's absolutely a great game to finish the night with for an hour or two. I've seen some comparisons to Disco Elysium and I would hang that hat at the door because this game isn't really like DE that much. Yes its a table top style rpg with contextual dice rolls, but it's not about being a walking disaster like DE so failing isn't really fun or funny, it's a horrible strain on your resources. It's about optimism when there really shouldn't be any, it's about being in a foreign, but semi welcoming place while being dogged by your past both mentally and physically. If you have the patience to just recline and read and enjoy some pretty character art reminiscent of Moebius or DethBerger but with a kinder, softer edge, than definitely pick this game up. There is more than enough content here for the asking price and I believe there is more to come. TL:DR simply lovely, choom.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Fun little game.  I'm not sure if you can die beyond possibly resource mismanagement.  (I didn't).  The game seemed to bail me out of some tough situations where it looked like I flipped the wrong page on a choose your own adventure.The game doesn't seem to have a definitive end unless you take certain actions.  I got the "end" credits 3 times, but was able to keep playing.  With the last time, i do not think there was anything left to do.I will agree to a degree with some that by mid game, resources become quite trivial.  Money, and the ability to repair and sustain yourself become quite accessible.  (possibly the intention of the game.)The game has a lot of charm and a degree of emotional investment similar to Disco Elysium, (just a much more sober version.)  I would like to see them pump a bit more meat into the middle of the game, though.Regardless, as it stands, easily well worth under $20 bucks.  100% satisfied with my purchase.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: A surprisingly hopeful story, filled with endearing and well-written characters. May not be for everyone, as it quickly devolves into ping-ponging between storylines or waiting around to be able to progress said storylines, but for what it's worth, I found every second of gameplay gripping and myself itching to see the stories unfold.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Played on a Steam Deck - no problems encountered.This is an interesting game and I'm enjoying it. It is a proper hard sci-fi exploration of what it means to be sentient, alive and free as you play a Sleeper who is a copy of a human consciousness loaded into a corporate-owned body, much like a replicant in Blade Runner. You are on the run and the corporation that made your body is going to hunt you down, and in the meantime you have to struggle against built in obsolescence that is slowly killing you.So the setting is great, but what about the game? It uses a dice mechanic where you get a bunch of dice rolled at the beginning of each day and can assign them and their rolls to your choice of tasks. It works nicely, though as your body fades you get less dice which can be a bit annoying, but thankfully doesn't become a death spiral (at least in my case).Overall -- and I've not finished it yet -- I really like the game and it has left me thinking about it after each play session is over, which is always a good sign. Played on Steam Deck with zero issues. Recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: The ambiance this game provides is truly magnificent. You'll be on edge for a good portion of the story, feeling the weight of choices you make, marvelling at a world to discover. Outstanding soundtrack and worldbuilding accompained by a minimalistic gameplay and simple yet beautiful artwork. I must say, this is a heavily story-driven experience. If you onto reading good old space-sci-fi novels, anime, or other pieces of media, you will fall in love with this story.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: This is a neat game. This is a visual novel driven by dice mechanics, which is fast becoming a whole thing I love (not sure if that's from Disco Elysium or the TTRPG boom at the moment.) The story writing here is solid, beautiful in moments, and how it all adds up to a solidly-realized world is why I finished it.I found the way it works with endings kind of interesting, in that it was hard for me to figure out how to resolve all threads at the end, and it felt like my final decision sort of left some other things hanging in a way. Specifically, I wish the game had let me go close out other plot threads narratively when I was at the point of choosing my ending. Still, a game I happily finished, and a great example of using budget wisely to create a product that feels constrained but yet also very beautiful - reminds me almost of Bithell's games in that sense.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Citizen Sleeper is a relatively short, narrative oriented game. Game mechanics are simple and easy to understand. Characters are nice and interesting to get to know. The ambience and atmosphere of being stuck on a cyberpunk space station is done extremely good.However, when buying this game, keep in mind, that:- Game is not that hard- It takes 6 hours (2-3 evenings) to beat the game, while completing almost all of the questlines- There is no voiceover for the dialogues, so be prepared to read quite a lot
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: This is a weird one. The setting is interesting, as are the characters; the game mechanics are strangely fun (yay gambling without consequences~). Yet most all decisions you are given to make are completely inconsequential. I wanted to try and role-play as a cold and self-centred moneymaker, but apparently, who you are is already determined for you: a selfless naïve robot, out to help anyone and everyone. The different starting classes don't actually have an impact either after the first couple cycles.I'm still going to recommend the game because, despite all the negatives, I really enjoyed my first playthrough of it. But I won't lie that I was a little let down after having my expectations set by all the praise it's received. (Also, the game ran quite laggy for me, even on a higher-end PC — I'm not counting this into my personal rating, but maybe it's worth saying.)I'll make sure to keep a lookout for the upcoming instalment.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting Characters and easy enough to understand storyline with plenty of branching paths that you get to see play out at your leisure. Youree not forced to help any particular person outside of yourself which is nice. There's a handful of endings to see which is nice and even the characters i didn't really care for did have some amusement factor to them. Idk if its a spoiler to say there is no fail game state which is well implemented and while it does take some tension out of it the game does make it a point to remind you that you're not immune to the actions of other people and i like that. Its a nice read ina well developed and easy to understand world. Nice stuff and I'm ready to play the next game
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: An exceptionally strong first half of a game. Tense, borrows some of the best mechanical ideas from TTRPGs in recent years, and oozing style.The back half leaves something to be desired, for the following reasons:* As many report, it becomes 'too easy'. Having few real ambitions beyond survival, once you manage to thwart the various oppressive forces making your life a drag, there's not really any challenge, just waiting around to see how various NPC arcs close out.* The plot arcs with various characters end up feeling too isolated. You make friends, dig in with them and help them thwart their own crisis, and then they just... disappear, all actions pertaining to them resolved and removed. The arcs almost never interact (with a single exception that I found), and it just ends up making these stories of other characters feel oddly siloed from everything else, including one another.At a discount, at least, this is definitely a must try. Just go in with managed expectations.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: This game wasn't bad, but it also wasn't good. In the early bits, there's a lot of stakes and tension, but your quickly progress past any real sense of urgency. From that point onwards, you just act out as a 'some person who does things' for the majority of the story beats, and it's... Quite boring. A lot of the storylines have endings at the end of them, but the endings don't really feel that special. And, you can just do stuff like leave the ship, see the credits roll, boot the game back up and then choose another ending. It quite quickly becomes a matter of just trawling through the endings to read them all. Which is kind of understandable, because getting to the endings is a bit of a chore, but still, narratively it's uninteresting.I think the best term to describe what's wrong with most of the plot beats is that, even though on paper they should be exciting, they end up feeling inconsequential. Overthrow X? Okay, doneso. But that doesn't really affect the other storylines that much, so there's no real sense of consequence. Your own character also seems kind of devoid of characterization, and I don't think this game is branching enough to justify that blank slate-like personality of the MC.So yeah, I don't now, it was... A very okay-ish game. Though definitely not one I'd go around and recommend to people.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Once in a while there's a game like Citizen Sleeper that comes off and when that time comes I'm so glad I found out about it. From the beginning until the end the story is absolutly touching deep and philosophical with a smart gameplay that serves the storyline as its best. I highly recommand this jewel of a game/experience!!
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly a great game: a well written story, cool character design and a lot of good music and sound effects. Doesn't do anything too radical, it's a small game but it's cut above a lot of small games in my opinion. Different to In Other Waters (dev's previous game) but with a few similar details, they put a lot of love into this. More free content coming, so I'll be playing it once again for that.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely story and execution on a fairly simple-seeming mechanic to move the narrative along. Quite a few time I had to pause (which the game allows) and think over what choices I was about to make and the potential consequences that could follow. In the end, I got what I aimed for, but in a bittersweet kind of way I'm not sure it's what I still wanted. I can't wait for enough time to pass so that I can forget most of this and play it again.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: I know this game looks like a very basic TTRPG cyberpunk story, but trust me in that it is much more. The game manages to captivate you with a basic UI and simple dice mechanics through its storyline alone. As a major fan of SF, I have seen a dime a dozen cyberpunk stories that fail to meet the mark or try something new, but Citizen Sleeper has the perfect tone and story to keep playing. At the time of this writing, I've only played the game for four and a half hours and I already consider this one of my favorite games on Steam. Heavily recommend for those looking to be immersed in a narrative about survival in space.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: With the right expectation this is a very enjoyable game, you should treat this game more like an excellently written visual novel with multiple non-linear storylines and an engaging resource management system. However it might start to become a bit grindy and lose it's survival elements late-game, but that only happens if you choose to continue the game after reaching its ending so that's just the curse of 100%ing games
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: I want so badly to like it, but it's a let down on a few critical points that lead me to feeling it's the most solid 5/10 I've ever played. Art direction, character designs, and music are all on point. A rugged sort of futurism that reminds me a lot of the ttrpg LANCER. The mechanics are interesting at first glance, and in the first hour or two genuinely are engaging. Same with the writing, but beyond that holes start to pop up everywhere. Eventually I got bored and went with the first ending available as the writing and gameplay became stale. I suspect it would take me about 3-4 more hours to see everything I chose not to do at 6~ hours of playtime. To be specific, the game clearly wants to be about the building of a community, your relations within, and the development of a character with questionable existential implications. Sadly, much of the character writing itself and your relationships are hampered by the limited engagement you have with them, progression locked by the mechanics with little to no punishment or difficulty, making it mostly time-padding in-between the written segments. So in the instances where you do interact with the cast, it's for a predetermined end that you don't have a say, with the assumed closeness your character has gotten to them in the time between while you're rolling dice and moving to the next cycle. Which leads me to my personal problem with the writing. Why is there no naming for your character? We're called "Sleeper" a title given to the type of machine we are. But you're telling me that after all the time and work the Sleeper does for the cast not a single one cares to humanize a machine that was once human with a name? A minor nitpick, but to me a damning flaw that took me out of good faith in the writing and the characters that the MC is supposed to form connections too. The gameplay is not particularly fun, the setting is shallow and made lesser by the mechanics not matching the struggle of the place we're in, the writing is self-serving and cares more about making the reader read than having anything to say or be engaged with, but I'll admit the game's best quality. It has damn good title screen music.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely beautiful game. The artistic direction and emotional and in depth characters and character development is absolutely wonderful.The world is incredibly complete and from the first day you "wake up" you will have tough choices to make and friends and enemies abound. Seeing the complex web that ties the refugees, wanderers, dreamers, and hard workers in this station that was run into the ground by capitilistic greed. Seeing this station that is only kept afloat by working together and finding solutions, even if they are sometimes bloody is a incredible and moving journey.The play-style is very much point and click and narrative reading with interactions and choices. I will say however as someone who loves action RPGs and  first person shooters for the most part that i was never bored, you have to work each cycle in game to push what narratives you want and help who you can, it leaves some very tough choices and some very satisfying story elements.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: It's like a "choose your own adventure" book.   Nice and soothing.   I haven't played a text based game since "Adventure" back in the 8080 days.  I like the fact I appear to have more control over my interface with the story.    Not finished, so I really don't know how much control I have over my story until a second playthrough.  I have some suspicions though.Oh, I also like the characters I'm working with even if they are unsavory.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: A high quality narrative focused game. The world and story are both of an exceptional standard, and the art style is charming. However, the fact that the success of actions taken by the player are determined by literal dice does make it feel a bit too gamey, breaking the immersion a bit. Still, it's an excellent experience overall.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Should you play Citizen Sleeper? Yes. It's not like any game I've played before. I really enjoy the strong roots it has in the RPG style and the setting of the game is brilliant. This Game is rich with story, however, it is a story you read, so as much as the reading is part of Citizen Sleeper's charm, be prepared for that, it's not like a lot of other video games. Trying to survive and make friends and find your way and your place in the grim city that is the Eye space station, is very fun. Its a cold, harsh environment that at times warms your heart. When I crank this game up I don't want to put it down. I haven't reached the end of the game yet but...Solid 4/5Voice acting, if done right, could be a nice touch. But absolutely not necessary.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Starts of very strong, lots of existential fears (how will i feed myself?, where can I hide?, what happens when I lose control over my body?).. But then the curtain falls. The game mechanics lose their mystery and uncertainty and it becomes predictable, avoidable and the Eye transform into a very safe space. Although it is satisfying to be able to roleplay a rags to riches story. It removes what I thought was the point of the game. If the game had more hidden mechanics/twists that reveal themselves later in the game, i would've been more immersed.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: I finished this game on Gamepass and loved it so much I bought the Deluxe edition on Steam.This game is one of the most compelling experience's I've had in a video game. The game play is fun and interesting enough to see you through the credits with a few wrinkles thrown in at key points; but where it shines is in it's dense atmosphere, loving character writing, intriguing scenarios, incredible art, and frankly all time contender soundtrack.Please play this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: It's rly well written, the narrative is the full focus of the game and it manages to make u imagine how it is to live in The Eye by just pure descriptions and texts. The soundtrack is great too, fitting rly well with all the atmosphere.i recommend it, a lot, but have in mind that is like reading a book, a rly good book.So go on, wake up sleeper.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a masterpiece. Don't listen to the people saying this is a surface level "capitalism bad" story. While those critiques are there, the writing is far deeper than that. Few games have had such an emotional impact on me. The character writing is phenomenal, even for those you don't see too often. _childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

Great story telling and interesting game cycle that i've never seen before, BUT, it's basically walls of text that you have to read to care. I don't think most people will put enough energy into really enjoying this game, but it is a great game.Friggin sad though. No matter what you do, expect the results to end bad for someone. Play your favorite emo songs when you play because it's going to pull you apart emotionally.

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10.The game is intentionally minimalistic and doesn't actually feature any real "gameplay." It plays more like a visual novel with a bit of RNG added in. If this is the type of game you can enjoy, then this one is really incredible. I haven't fully finished the game but I've gotten far enough to see the conclusion of multiple plot points and get into the "endgame."The Gameplay - The gameplay usually boils down to reading character dialogue or your own inner monologue and selecting between two or three different ways to react/respond to it. When you aren't in a text sequence, you can spend your days (or "cycles") doing various objectives around the station to get money, advance certain stories, or unlock other points of interest. The way you do this is through the Action Dice that the game gives you (between 1 and 5) based on your character's physical condition. These are standard 6-sided die that give you different chances to succeed depending on which number it is, with 6 obviously having the highest chance of a positive outcome. You are given your dice at the beginning of the day and you have the opportunity to choose where you want to spend which die, which allows you to prioritize the objectives you find important by using your best dice on them. Depending on which activity you are doing, the negative and positive outcomes can change drastically. There are a few other gameplay mechanics like "clocks" but this is the only part you really need to worry about for now.The Story - Without spoiling anything, the story is very unique and I found it pretty engaging even though I usually don't like these sorts of games. I found there to be a bit of a weird focus on gender pronouns, but other than that the story felt very realistic and cynical. There are certain storylines which clearly have good and bad endings which drastically change your relationships with important characters. My only real complaint is that it can be quite hard to tell what the implications of your choices are. For example, If two characters are having an altercation and you decide to stay out of it, that could potentially end with one of those characters getting ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up and you really had no way to see that coming.The Music - is really ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ good. I actually felt no need to put on music during the game even during some less-than-exciting moments because the soundtrack is awesome and it doesn't overstay it's welcome. Certain tracks are chosen for certain important moments in the story and it fits really well.Overall - If you don't enjoy reading, you're not going to enjoy this game. However, if you can play it as a visual novel with a little bit of economy/decision making then it's great.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: If you like good stories with choices, then I'd wholeheartedly recommend this game. The Soundtrack is amazing, the writing hits home, the setting is a beautiful mess of a space station, and the art hits the aesthetics just right for this genre. You play a Sleeper: a consciousness in an artificial body, who learns not just to survive but to truly find a life. The game play is dice rolling, and simple leveling mechanics, but the count down clocks give urgency to your choices. The game explores themes of survival, life, death, home, identity, connection, and freedom. With the DLC, different starting stats and different endings, there is quite a bit of replay in this game, but nothing that is extremely long and out of reach of the casual player. It's a good little game and a wonderful piece of art frankly.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: really well written, great setting. at the beginning where you are scrabbling to survive is very compelling. the alternate way of spending your low dice rolls via hacking is a great way to get around bad rng. practically every character's story is worth reading. each of the three ending escape options are very well done, especially . great music.It is a little too easy to be swimming in money though by the midway point, which means you can have a ton of dice and can avoid all bad outcomes, and become good at all the skills. the overhanging threat of being hunted starts good but ended disappointingly  too neat, too much "thats it?" after the excellent ratcheting pressure of being an escapee.overall didnt stop me loving this and i really want to return to the setting.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: A short but heartfelt story of a Sleeper - a corporate-owned bio-mechanical frame imprinted with a human mind - who escapes his/her owners to make a life of their own. This game is well written and explores many mature themes of identity, building a life from scratch, and finding your purpose in life that often come with bittersweet or hopeful conclusions. There is a limited degree of player freedom, but there are no "wrong" choices. What little choices you are allowed to make are extremely meaningful to the ending(s) you'll see, and you'll want to see them all. All in all, Citizen Sleeper took me about 8-9 hours to read most of the endings, and I'm a slow reader. Don't "sleep" on this!
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Finished this game on Game Pass but just had to buy it on Steam as well to support the devs and because of how much I enjoyed it. The writing and world-building in this game is amazing and really sucks you in. The gameplay is simple but satisfying. The art and music are great as well. Definitely one of the best games I've played this year.But now it's time to follow the thread back home.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: I do not recommend this game, as it lacks a number of features it advertises. The survival aspect is trivially easy, which would be fine if the entire narrative didn't revolve around "You're dying very, VERY quickly. Try to survive.", and the story only progresses when you want it to, which again, doesn't work with their "The Eye is changing.". Finally, the story and roleplaying aspect are entirely lies; there is zero difference in the outcomes of different choices you can pick, and most of the time your choices mean the same things even at face value, for example "I didn't have a choice." and "She just wants to help!". There is very rarely a solid "No." or "I disagree with (x) sentiment." that actually matters, the only occasions those options have existed for me being laughed off.  What this game really is isn't a roleplay game, but a medium for sharing a sentiment hiding behind a stale story and an illusion of choice. If you want to see someone else's incredibly interesting world-building, this is a good game for that, but you'll have to wade through a sea of average story. If you want a roleplay, choices-matter kind of game, this isn't the one for you. Thank you for reading this far, have a good day.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: A short and sweet game bustling with love, care, and lore that takes at most 10 hours to complete in a single run with most of the endings if you're thorough.Played at native 4K 120 fps with HDR via Special K.----------------------------------Gameplay: 9/10 - I went into this game with somewhat low expectations for the dice roll system but came to enjoy it quite a bit! The system is simple but encourages taking the occasional risk, especially earlier in the game first starting out. It felt like the class specialization doesn't have much of an effect once you reach the mid- and late-game drives where you're mostly upgraded.Story: 9.5/10 - Every drive (gameplay objective) in this game is emotionally and thoughtfully investing and really immerses you into the world. Hours will go by without even knowing. "Just one more cycle". I loved and cared about every single character I met in the game, although it does kind of suck that once you finish some drives, some of those characters just disappear into the void with no further interactions. I do wish I could see what they were up to or with some recurring dialogue.Graphics: 9.5/10 - The ship is beautifully rendered in 3D along with the vast emptiness of space. HDR really takes it up a notch with better highlights and colors, but it still looks good in the normal SDR presentation as well. All the characters are beautifully hand drawn and I wish we could see some sort of animated work with them sometime. I loved seeing a character's sprite pop up for dialogue; it's honestly my favorite part about this game.Music and sound design: 10/10 - A masterpiece of melancholic, electronic ambient music. The way the score times itself in conversations to certain gameplay events, hearing a new motif every cycle you wake up, it's all gorgeously choreographed and strongly evoking. I can't describe the shivers of finally reaching the end and hearing the last song, immediately thinking, "I don't want this to be over yet." The sound effects for the gameplay loop are equally satisfying for the dice roller.Replayability: 7.5/10 - I definitely would want to go back in to redo some drives and see what I missed along the way. In fact, I did and was as equally satisfied with it as I was my first playthrough. I am eagerly looking forward to the episodic DLC content, but would also love to see other characters' storylines get extended depending on certain gameplay decisions.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic little game! Very well written and full of heart. I know some people say that there doesn't seem to be any follow-through and were disappointed. I guess I can see where they're coming from considering there isn't a grand overarching narrative. But I don't think that was what the team intended to make here. Instead the focus is on the daily lives and struggles of yourself and those you meet, and the relationships that blossom or whither along the way. And with that in mind I think they did a stellar job!Some advice though: as far as I can tell, each of the endings has a choice right before it to do A or B. After choosing one you can go right back in and continue your save, which will place you in the same cycle right before the choice so you can go with the other option if you like.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: A game never heard of until a video I watched a few months back. A man who had recently become a father was reflecting on the games he's played through 2023. He'd found his new parental life allowed him little time for games. Though he did not begrudge this, for he was filled with love for his bawling daughter, he recognised that he would not be able to play the several hundred hour epics he'd enjoyed previously. And so it was that he looked for shorter games. Ones that reflected his deep love of stories and of characters. Ones that provoked him to think about the themes raised well beyond his time with the game. I bought one of these games on impulse. Something about the visuals in the brief shots in his videos grabbed me. It was on sale on Steam at the time and so I snapped it up. It sat in my library for a few months until today. I opened it and consumed it's main story in one sitting. 'Citizen Sleeper' manages to convey warmth in it's bleak setting with both it's writing, as well as it's soundtrack which is as comforting as it is unobtrusive. It's characters charm away the protagonist's seemingly inexorable loneliness. The story's themes have a core of what it means to be human, to be free, and to find one's place in an ever changing world. It's charming, simple to understand and engaging. Quite simply - it's lovely. I think you'd really enjoy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Played this all in one sitting and it took 6-7 hours, but it might be a few hours longer for you as I am a quick reader.Citizen Sleeper is a light CRPG that has a presentation quite similar to Disco Elysium. You have to manage your time in each cycle whilst making enough money to be able to sustain yourself and react to changing circumstances. The Eye is full of an array of characters to meet with their own interesting stories and motivations to meet as you strive towards various goals.In terms of gameplay, there isn't too much to speak of. This is where the comparison to Disco Elysium is apt as the game is presented in the form of utilising your skills and making choices through dialogue and having the story delivered to you through text. It's not nearly as complicated as Disco Elysium and this game is much smaller in scope, but that is not a bad thing.Outside of that, I found the writing to be engaging, complimented with good visuals and some great music/sound design that compliments the immersive experience of the game. Yeah, I like the game. You should buy it. It's good.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: It is a wonderful game with an amazing story to tell, and the pacing is great. It's simultaneously slow-paced and calm, but also manages to give a sense of urgency without stressing the actual game play. The art is lovely, the mechanisms are fun, and there are lots of things to find and explore, even though the map/world seems rather small at first. Lots of small decisions, but also a few hard ones.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: When you wake up realizing all the games you have been playing are dead inside.  Like some of the best science fiction novels of my youth, CS forces you to think about your existence, your motivations, and what you want out of life.  Simple and easy to follow story lines that somehow tug at the most fundamental of emotions.  Companionship, family, loyalty, desire to live, sadness, loss, forgiveness....  Too many times I found myself listening to the soundtrack as the credits played and contemplating things I haven't had time to think about in a long while.  A deep sigh as though you needed it and never really knew.  Let it grow on you.  And be open to it.  It will remind you of places within yourself that you thought you lost a long time ago.  Thank you.  Thank you for making this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: tl:dr - This... isn't really worth the price point, or at least, it wasn't for me.  It's an interesting experience, but it's brief, and (as a game) lacks depth.We'll start with the positives* (positive): It's very pretty.  The music is nice (though it does eventually get a little old).  The artwork is pretty cool.  The world-map is well-presented.  As an aesthetic experience, it's well done.* (positive): The narratives are interesting and well-written.  Real effort has been put into creating the characters that you interact with, and their stories, and into leaving some negative space for you to fill with your own story.* (positive): *As long as you don't spoil yourself*, there's some interesting/engagng discovery-based gameplay there that can be pretty cool... at first.* (positive/neutral): There is a significant bias towards the liberal/diverse.  I don't know exactly how to describe it, but there's a certain political ethos baked deep into its bones, that colors... I link it literally colors every character in the piece.  If your own political leanings are towards that side, you'll probably count this as a positive.  I note it as positive/neutral rather than positive/negative, though, because of how refreshingly *non-hostile* it is about the whole thing.  Like, there's a clear bias, running in threads all through it, but it doesn't go toxic or belabor the point too badly, or lay it on super-thick in the way that you see elsewhere.  I have to give respect for that.* (negative) That discovery-based gameplay enjoyment I was talking about before?  It doesn't last.  The best part of the actual game of it is in discovering how it all works, and once you've exhausted that, there's just not a lot of fun left in it.  The gameplay itself, once you fully understand it, isn't a lot of fun.  It degenerates into just something you have to get through to read the stories that are left.* (negative) It's short.  It just is.  Eventually, you just run out of game to play.  There's a *bit* of replayability, if you want to go back and scrub out all of the corners and make sure you get all of the achievements, but that runs right into the wall of "the gameplay is super-thin, when you know how it works" - in order to actually get to those corners, you're going to have to be doing a bunch of stuff that's... just not all that interesting, anymore.* (negative) It says "decisions matter", and some of them do, but a lot of them don't.* (negative) Very little actual challenge.  There's the illusion of challenge, but once you realize how the game actually runs under the hood, that falls away just like the rest of the gameplay enjoyment... and it's not like it's all that hard to figure out.Conclusion: to my mind?  If I'd picked this up for $7-something, I would have been fully satisfied with my purchase.  The enjoyment I got out of the art of it and out of exploring the world was worth $7.  For a price point north of $20?  There's just not enough there.  Admittedly, that's in part because I was interested in this as a game, first.  It's pretty clear that the people who created it are artists first, and if you're more interested in the art than the game, you might be happier with it than I was.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay itself isn't that captivating. You sleep, use your dice, repeat. At the beginning you have different choices which make the game interesting, you explore different possibilities, but later it just becomes less engaging and more tedious. I'd say the writing and the story are the best parts of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game. I don't have much to say piece by piece. It's all good. I just had a very palpable experience in learning, forming attachments, becoming truly, truly desperate, and feeling genuinely grateful for being alive that was really meaningful. A near-death experience after which I could almost weep just being able to forage fungus for another day.The "one more day" grind of working a job is painfully acute - the sickening joy of being able to work several long cycles for the "reward" of maintaining your body. The system hates you more than any individual. It often asks you to forego your work for personal relationships, pressing hard to get it across without being cruel as a videogame. Deftly done.Communist mushroom farms, earnestly and earthily written. Wondrous.There were some onboarding issues; it's difficult to retain a lot of the tutorial information, so opening a menu to see them would be nice, and I'd also like more detailed Drive notes and symbols for clock progress vs. item rewards from a check. Also some way to hold and drag the middle mouse to scroll the station, or use number to progress the conversations and go places. Sometimes the immediate empathy of the characters straddles the line between working-class and meaningful vs. confusingly out of nowhere, but it always pays off and smoothes over with time.Great job on the game! I would recommend it to anyone.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: This game was an absolute delight. I got most of the "good" endings on the first run though but it was an enjoyable run. Only one noteable glitch, items in my inventory would not reappear to be used. Had to reload the game and it fixed itself.Honestly I am going to play this again, and again. great way to spend an afternoon.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Although the actual gameplay takes a backseat about a quarter of the way through, the quality story and worldbuilding carries Citizen Sleeper to the end (or rather, ends). Fantastic character writing, supported by subtle, melancholic music, had me in an emotional grip, as final choices were made and a few difficult goodbyes were had.Only criticism is that you can't advance text by anything but a mouseclick. Being able to press spacebar instead of 'Continue' and/or pressing e.g. 1-4 to select dialogue options seems an obvious thing to implement, but it's a pretty insignificant nitpick compared all the game has to offer.Great interactive experience. Looking forward to the sequel once I've recovered emotionally :')
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Citizen sleeper is exceptional- the art, writing and design are all interwoven so well, and form a incredible, immersive story.Quite simply, you have to play this once.Don't play it much more than once, though. It's a great story, but it gives you the illusion of agency- not real agency. Every story contained within is brilliantly realised- the longer ones, and especially the DLC, being real standouts. You'll want to see every nook and cranny of the eye. But it achieves this through being a highly curated experience. It is telling you a story. You are not telling it.This shouldn't put you off playing it- it's just a warning. This isn't a 'Choices matter' kind of game- but what it is is a series of well rounded characters in well-crafted stories in a well-developed world. And when you approach it that way, you'll have a great time.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game as part of a humble bundle and didn't really think much of it at the time, but decided to play it on a whim recently. Man, what a good decision that was. On a surface level, it has really beautiful character art, a really sleek and polished UI, and an evocative OST, but more importantly, all of those elements come together harmoniously to aid the telling of a really heartfelt and contemplative story of hope and survival. It almost makes more sense to think of it as an episodic story where each subplot is focused on a small cast of characters, slowly revealing their background, motivations, and relationship with the world around them. This format seems like a pretty good fit for a game which wants to explore a multitude of themes with some depth, and without any of them feeling forced or tacked-on. The writing is engaging, and treats the player like an adult, abstaining from preaching or moralizing—just laying out events as they happen and letting you make up your own mind. The speed with which I found myself attached to certain characters took me by surprise, but in a pleasant way, and made the conclusions of their respective character arcs that more emotionally impactful. I don't think I have a single bad thing to say about the game; the gameplay feels fair and balanced, the difficulty curve isn't too steep, the atmosphere set by the music and visuals is awesome, and the gripping plot is backed by solid writing. Get it, it's awesome.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Great game!It's easy to lose oneself in the wonderfully written narrative and stories. And you really must deal with your choices. Sometimes, you'll be lucky with the dices, others you'll wish you had a better roll, but it all adds up to a great adventure. Even though you have limited art pieces, the writing really make you visualize it in your head.Just try it.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: First off don't read any of the negative reviews as they have holes in their heads and have no idea what they are talking about. Citizen Sleeper is probably one of the, if not the, most beautifully written games I've ever had the pleasure of playing. Every single character in this game you're able to empathize with and feel so human. The stories that they tell are amazingly beautiful and tragic at the same time. While the game is set in the ruins of interplanetary capitalism the game is about the characters that live in this world and how they interact with those around them. How they try to overcome with the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ cards that they've been dealt in life. Experiencing the writing of Citizen Sleeper is like trying to describe a miracle to someone who has never witnessed one.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Like others posting reviews my only complaint with the game is that there isn't more to play. The story of this game is amazing, characters with amazing art design in a world that is wonderful to explore. The story of Sleeper can be whatever you want it to be, anything from a cynical escapee that is out for themselves and no one else to a story about someone trying to make a place to call home and finding friends and family along the way. The endings are touching and this game was very good at making me love characters in such a short time. This game is great and deserves to be seen by more people.There is also a cat and you can pet it (Sometimes, when it allows you to. 10/10)
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Starting off was a bit counter intuitive, for me at least, but once you understand the game ethos, it's a solid game.It's also not obvious whether or how it is possible to save the game at key decision points so you don't have to work through each path from the beginning.It doesn't need zillions of saves like a RenPy game, but a handful of voluntary saves in addition to the Auto-saves would be good.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Better the first time round and blind than on repeat playthroughs, but ohhhh that first run through the story.Erlin's Eye and its people have a special place in my heart now.Art and music, excellent.Gameplay, interesting as a ttrpg analogue.Story, aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa.Yeah.Play it.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Played this once through on Game pass, enjoyed it so much thought I'd buy a copy to check out the DLC when it comes out. Don't normally replay story-based games, goes to show how much I enjoyed the game!Simple gameplay, not too challenging but enough to keep the brain going, engaging story, memorable characters and chilled music.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: This review is just for the base content that was at launch, I have not done the extra missionsThis game is fairly simple but damn its engaging, and has some strategy to its core elements, but that is not why you play citizen sleeper. You play this game for the wonderful art style, lovely writing, and interesting characters. Also all the additional content added to the game was done so for free which is goated. _childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: If you like sci-fi with a touch of transhumanism and you like visual novel type story driven games, you will like this game.A very well written game. I accidentally did everything in the right sequence to be able to get almost all of the endings by reloading my save(which is intended, since it's not deleted after). The run took around 10 hours, which I thoroughly enjoyed to the point where I didn't even get distracted by anything outside the game. The characters are all interesting, it is plain that they are people with their own drives and desires. I got seriously attached to Lem and Mina, to the point where I almost didn't do one of the endings.The gameplay system is pretty straightforward too, not really complicated, which I liked. I didn't really come to this game for a challenge, rather I came for a good story, which this game definitely has.The endings, at least the ones I got, all felt good, but one stood out to me as the most emotionally impactful. Overall, highly recommend for anyone who likes these kinds of games.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: A must read/play for all systemic narrative enthusiasts (and for all for like reading in general). Beautifully evocative and atmospheric, with a tightly written and edited script, a tone that masterfully balances between melancholy and hope, and play systems that take excellent cues from modern tabletop experiences to provide a non-linear progression that's deeply player driven while remaining cohesive and well paced. The visuals are mainly menu driven with a clean and clear UI that's plenty legible on Steam Deck thanks to a bigger text option. The character illustrations are fantastic with masterful lineart and coloring, and serve to guide the imagination while it fills in the world the rest of the text creates.The main issue so far is navigation using gamepad and UI responsiveness (for upgrades, or when selecting event hotspots), but this doesn't detract from the core of the experience too much.It's some of the best cyberpunk reading (and playing) I've had the pleasure to discover in recent memory, highly recommended for all who previously liked/enjoyed titles such as The Yahwg, Monster Prom, Neo Cab, Gnosia or similar approaches to systems-driven storytelling.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Few games leave me sitting quietly for a while after the credits roll, fewer still cause me to stop and think only about the game months after I finished them, but Citizen Sleeper did both. If after looking at the screenshots and trailer you are on the fence about this game, I cannot recommend this game enough to people into this sort of narrative focused RPG.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: come for the beautiful sci fi aesthetics, stay for the incredible character pieces and narrative. the gameplay is less of a game and more of a book with rpg type mechanics but it works so well. replayability is definitely not this game's forte, but as a story goes it mixes elements of heartwarming, scifi action, and tearjerking moments. would definitely recommend, at its price you won't find a better visual novel. 9/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: Citizen Sleeper is a Cyberpunk TableTop RPG-Like? combined with a Visual Novel. You are a "Sleeper", a human mind inserted in a artificial body property of a corporation named "Essen-Arp". You have no rights or freedom so you escape of your captors and you arrive to the "Erlins Eye", a ruined space station with zero memories of how you ended here, with Essen-Arp pursuing you & for more problems all the Sleepers has something called "planned obsolescence". Basically it is you don't get injected with a medicine that only essen-arp produces you die. So you have a mission escape from the claws of Essen-Arp. Find answer about your past & and escape or build a life in the eye but the more important is survive.I remember view this game a few times in the past, one I the most remember is when the sequel was annunced and I say "hey, this really looks good" this added that much people reccomend me the first I decide to give a try and wow what a huge surprice! Citizen Sleeper is one of the best games I played in a large time, the reason? Well almost everything.How I was saying the game is two genres combined a TTRPG & Visual Novel. The TTRPG element It's different from what we're used to, in the game the board is the spaceship in there you has missions where you use your dices but you don't roll the dices, the game every day gives you your rolls and you used in the missions you wanna do. Also you have two bars condition & hunger every day this two bars decrease, your condition it's the most important because this determines the number of dices actions you can do in your fully conditions you can do 5 dices actions you always wanna have 5 - 3 dices actions beware. The food bar is more manageable but be careful of not get starving because you loss condition faster, the mode to fill the bars is buying items with money obviously you get money working in some parts of the ship so find a balance between survive day to day & complete the missions that assure you a future. And the Visual Novel stuff? Well, how I say you have missions like disable your tracker or find a doctor in this travel you gonna find several characters with many things to tell, trust me. Play this game for me was like play a solo RPG campain but without having a master who controls your game but rather a narrator who tells you the story of the charactes, the life in the eye, the difficulties, the little hope that remains in every character for a good life in this galaxy destroyed & dominated by corporations. It's a story with a really huge sentimental charge, I fall in love with every character (well almost all), they makes me feel happy, sad, angry and even helpless simple & minimal but insanely effective."Simple & Minimal" this is something that can be view on others aspect of the game like the interface, it's just beautiful you can understand everything easily and directly without losing any of the cyberpunk tone and the identity of the game, is a flawless job even in the visual novel parts, they really understand that all the time you are reading & thinking. The soundtrack is other aspect where this comes to shine really setting you in the galaxy without forgetting to be relaxing and dramatic. This aspects of the game serve to enhance the characters and their design every one fully detailed and beautiful, it really helps to put all your attention in them and their story. There is only one thing that I don't like, it is the relations with the characters once their history (so their mission) is finished they go to nothing. You can't interact with them once their mission is finished doesn't matter if the result is good or bad. It really feels like a punch in the face get involved the life of this characters when the mission ended, like we are super friends continue with the game and no view this characters again, no talk with them again, nothing abosolutely, nothing this can even be seen in the ending of the three dlc campains (The true ending at least for me). I can't convice or almost talk properly with my friends of the past missions and the final ending (the two ones) they are so insubstantial and lacking in information that I think: "Well, there is a sequel confirmed, maybe the final is so open because of the sequel" but the sequel is with another sleeper in another history, it's hard for me to understand this because I don't think that the story of my sleeper and the other characters finishes here, it's a little sad. Even with this Citizen Sleeper is a Game that yo need to play, is easily go to the top of my favorites games, I can only recommend you to play this game. I Hope you enjoy it like I did.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: This is  an rpg. This is a text adventure/visual novel, with a simple time management system built on top. The narrative is linear and choices amount barely to decisions at the end of each npc story that give you one ending or another. You won't be roleplaying your own character, nor the world around you will change depending on your actions. This is an on-rails narrative, a short storybook with minor interactivity.That is perfectly fine, and the developers should not try to sell this game as something else. Now, if the description avobe is something that sounds interesting to you, you're in for a treat. The worldbuilding is really good, the characters interesting and the stories are engaging. The art, of course, is superb, although it left me wanting for more. Citizen Sleeper is that short sci-fi novel that you read in an afternoon and you thought was cool. As such, I recommend it only as long as you get it on sale. Its full price is too high for what it is. Which is just cool.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10Amazing RPG, amazing story with a really nice pacing. The game balances the "survival" mechanics with story progression really well. The difficulty level is really nice as well, not too punishing but you definitely still have to keep on top of your "health" bars while you try to progress the story.
_childDocuments_.name: Citizen Sleeper

_childDocuments_.review: I am a huge tabletop roleplaying game (TTRPG) fan. Like, a  big fan. This game takes inspiration from many TTRPGs to create a compelling narrative with simple yet effective mechanics.An evocative story with TTRPG-esque mechanics. If you are a fan of roleplaying games and (maybe, tangentially) visual novels, I would recommend this game. While not very difficult, it provides an engaging emotional experience throughout its respectably short runtime.
