_childDocuments_.review: Devolver Digital surprises me time and time again with the developers and titles it takes under its wing, and that's how Gunbrella has been put on our sights since it was announced, and even more so now with its launch trailer. With expectations formed by its previews and the quality that this publisher usually shows us, it’s kinda obvious that I was looking forward to what the game would bring, and I can say with satisfaction that it was what I expected and even more, even with some details that I will mention in the course of the review.Gunbrella is an action-adventure game that places us in a Noir-Punk world, where we’ll take the role of a tough vigilante in search of revenge; something classic but that when well executed is very cool, and that is the case in this instance. It should be noted that the title also encapsulates several themes such as climate disaster, and corporate greed, among others more and less subtle. But making use of a weapon that is a product of the wonders of science, the Gunbrella (a shotgun disguised as an umbrella), we will shoot, jump and glide our way through this melancholic universe and those who get in our way.Me being me, the first thing that caught my attention was the pixel art, and I can say that the game is perfectly captured in this style, with a super retro feel. The gloomy color palette matches well with the locations and the atmosphere that is maintained throughout the adventure, from ruined villages to fortresses inhabited among the trash and debris of a junkyard. The character sprites are not neglected in the least, they are simple but detailed, and this is also seen in the bosses and animations both in combat and in general. The soundtrack is excellent, very consistent with the style and atmosphere, with melancholic melodies and a neat arrangement. Every scene has its accompaniment and various sound effects, and there is a perfect harmony with the visual section, and this always makes me enjoy the game much more.The story is the next point I want to address!	 It's pretty simple at first, we've all seen the typical hero or anti-hero out for revenge, but the devs have employed unique twists and touches that separates and distinguishes it from other stories. On this journey, we’ll accompany our character through different situations, meet other cast members and be able to establish friendships or show indifference to those around us.In turn, we face a cult and their aberrant creations, a company that seeks to extract as much as possible from the world with selfishness and delusions of grandeur, and a special force of agents who also carry Gunbrellas; all in pursuit of reaching our task, to find who has put us on this lonely path, and we have a bullet ready with their name on it.It is a story that mostly conveys a sad and desolate feeling, but the developers have managed to add some comedy along these serious issues, and you can tell that they had a lot of fun creating the game. Nothing is out of place, no moment overstays its stay, and the plot flows very satisfyingly. I was thoroughly entertained, and it does feel like a rough and hard-boiled Noir tale. As for the gameplay, I must admit that it was my favorite section; not to detract from the rest, far from it, but because it's super fun to play. In essence, the character's movement is simple: we can move sideways and jump, aim the gun in the direction we want and eventually we can climb the walls by bouncing on them (the classic wall-jump!); but what gives it a real kick is the Gunbrella, since besides being a firearm, it is also a shield, a parachute, and we can even use it to propel ourselves and maneuver between platforms and enemies, with controls that feel tight and responsive.The Gunbrella is the centerpiece and only weapon (ours that is) of the game, clearly obvious from its title, and being able to take cover, lunge, return bullets and glide, makes it feel like a very interactive object. The mobility it gives us is fantastic, and I had a lot of fun with it! It's an all-in-one, and when it comes to combat it's super practical and even has different ammo variants, like rifle-like bullets that reach farther or sticky bombs to, well, stick to enemies. I admit I didn’t find myself using them much, ‘cause I’m a damn hoarder, but it’s a nice thing to have.I also want to mention that the Gunbrella can be upgraded, for damage and charge speed, and we, as a character, will also have life boosts, both in the form of extra temporary hearts by eating food, and permanent ones by collecting two heart halves (usually rewarded by secondary missions). To finish this section, I want to add that boss fights are cool and add a little more challenge compared to the rest of the enemies, and feel very fitting and grounded.In conclusion, Gunbrella is a game that fits very well in its genre, with a gameplay that I loved and kept me absorbed in the game, and tells us a story that touches on various themes and situations that made me feel from hopeless or happy, to depressed and angry; and the latter both for the story itself (sharing the protagonist fiery revenge), and for a bug that I found at some point. I can’t avoid mentioning that one bug because it almost cut my adventure short, but it resolved itself, luckily; however, the devs addressed and fixed the bug pretty quickly, so leaving that aside, my experience with the game was extremely pleasant.It's a game that really amused me, after all, who hasn't picked up an umbrella and started playing as if it were a gun or a sword? Eh, just me? Well... anyway. The Noir-Punk theme is something I haven't experienced a lot so I’m glad I could, and beyond my encounters with the aforementioned bugs, I think it's an excellent title with a really cool and badass atmosphere. I invite you to give it a try, I feel it's a game that will appeal to both hard-boiled story fans and side-scrollers lovers, and it lends itself to a good time of fun thanks to its concoction of ideas and creativity.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunbrella

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game, but there are a couple of caveats that might turn off certain players.Firstly, this has a simply told, but fairly meaningful and surprisingly dark story that ends in a way I did not see coming. It does a good job at conveying a lot of meaning without needing a ton of words to do it. The titular Gunbrella is also an awesome combination of multiweapon and traversal tool, giving your character a way to move around that I've never seen in another game, but which also feels fantastic and is easy to master.You will travel around the world, unraveling the story and completing optional quests for people you'll meet along the way. Don't sit on them too long though as there are several you can miss if you progress too far before completing them. At certain points, you can go back and forth between areas, but this is pretty linear overall.The two things that I didn't mind, but that I think some might is that Gunbrella is both very short and VERY easy. My playthrough where I did most of the side quests, but missed a couple only took me about 5 hours, though How Long to Beat says 100%-ing it can take up to 10. I also died maybe a half dozen times in the entire game and half of those were on the final boss, who I thought might be a challenge until I discovered something quickly that made him trivial. Unless you have bad aim or bad reflexes, you won't find this challenging at all. I didn't mind either of these things as I prefer shorter games these days and sometimes, I just enjoy a fun adventure that isn't a skill test, but some players will find the lack of challenge boring. That's fair if you're that type of player, so you should know that.I had a good time with this and I hope Doinksoft makes more stuff like it.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunbrella

_childDocuments_.review: On one hand, there's a lot to like in Gunbrella. The atmosphere is fantastic and the gameplay mechanics and traversal are well done. I loved using the umbrella all the time. Also, it felt nice that instead of going through levels you do quests and side quests back and forth in different areas while getting some minor upgrades.On the other hand, the game is a bit lacking. Bosses are extremely easy. There were one or two in particular in which I didn't have to do anything other than stay still and shoot in the same direction. You get a ton of weapons but hardly a reason to use them. I used the base shotgun 99% of the game except in the parts the game forced me to use another gun to kill the wraiths. There are like 5 other weapons that I didn't even try 'cause there was no reason. The shotgun is that good. I also played this with a joystick and it took me a long while before I got used to what each trigger does. The game has a lot of buildup that feels good but then it doesn't deliver. It doesn't feel satisfying to do anything because the rewards are meh. I still had fun in my 5 hour run and I was intrigued by the lore of this world. I do recommend this but it's not GOTY material.3.5/5 - Good, not great.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunbrella

_childDocuments_.review: It's a solid game but I had much higher hopes. The clean pixel art graphics, moody music, and dark story all create a great aesthetic that kept me engaged. The gameplay is tight, however it hardly evolves throughout the 9 hour run time. The mechanics you start with are essentially the same as what you end with. The final level kicked up the difficulty, making it necessary to get creative to get through its sections but this was too late. Gunbrella almost feels like a demo of what the traversal and action should be with the titular weapon. I expected an indie game-of-the-year contender but this probably won't crack 2023's top 10. I enjoyed this game but was left wanting more.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunbrella

_childDocuments_.review: the protagonist is out doing x when he sees a column of smoke rising from his home. He rushes back, but we know it’s too late.  unfortunate hero finds his wife murdered and his newborn missing, with only a single clue at the scene of the crime: the murder weapon. It’s a strange device; a gun doubling as an umbrella. Our hero takes it, and sets off on a fugitive’s journey to uncover the weapon’s history, in the hope that it will lead him to his child.I liked , but I didn’t like it enough. It’s a game that feels like it’s so close to being that much better but never quite gets there. No single element really sings, feeling untapped, under-served. It’s true of its weapon upgrade system, the currency you collect, and the world you’re introduced to. They all feel like they need to be given more breathing room, because as it is, in a game as brief and cursory as this one, it's difficult to invest in them.Taking place in an intriguing steampunk world, you use a railway to journey between towns, slowly uncovering a conspiracy involving death cults, dwindling resources, political corruption, and the end of the world. A pretty tasty set of ingredients for a decent neo-noir, but like most other aspects of , it never coheres into something truly satisfying.Exploration is stymied by the fact that you’re moved on so swiftly, and there’s never much reason to return to previous areas unless the plot demands it. Sure, you could go around collecting currency to upgrade your weapon, and sure, you could complete the odd quest. Problem is, there's little incentive to do so. You always sense that the game is moving too quickly to its final destination for any of these to be rewarding. Is there any real benefit to maxing out the titular gunbrella if I'm only going to spend a few hours with it?Probably not.Which is a shame, because  is fun. Really! The side-scrolling combat is meaty and engaging, with some clever quirks, and the game has a commendably irreverent sense of humour. The world’s bleak, the protagonist’s journey bloody, but  never takes itself too seriously. It also has its heart in the right place, and there's a real ecological anxiety cutting through that feels current and authentic.In a way, the game might’ve worked better without the bells and whistles—if it just focused on a linear, narrative experience, instead of indulging a series of diversions that only ever feel half-baked. As it is,  is a fun, well-made little outing, but it’s too watered-down and unfocused to really stick the landing.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunbrella

_childDocuments_.review: I was inspired to write my first review in years because of this game.I wish I could give it a neutral rating, but I'm leaning more toward negative. I wanted to love it, but I was just disappointed with the story, characters and gameplay. I love the idea and can see why people like this game, but the controls never clicked for me despite my best effort. I was also expecting harder boss fights. If I didn't kill a boss first try, I took them out on the second one. And since I wasn't using the movement to its full potential, all of the fights felt the same. _childDocuments_.review: TL;DR buy at promo.Gunbrella is a good game for shoot-em-up fans. This is what the game is at it's core, a shoot-em-up with limited roaming and some side-quests to do for extra loot and upgrades.The sad part is that Gunbrella is just underdeveloped.Underdeveloped characters, mechanics, combat and movement.Everything is really solid but at the same time lacking in depth, the strangest part is that you have the foundations to give everything depth but you just don't because the game is way too short.Heck, the combat and plataforming both get repetitive by the end of the game and it's not because these mechanics are bad or the game drags itself for too long, it's because it never gets imaginative and creative about how it can use the quirks of movement and combat.It's just dull, lacking in depth. And when you think they'll do something different it ends, it cuts it short.That happens for mechanics, story beats and characters.There are like 5 factions and 3 main villains in the game and of these 3 main villains one of them gets killed in a gag moment and their entire subplot gets sideline really quickly. And of these 5 factions you get to know the bare minimum.At the same time there's this light of passion behind Gunbrella that makes it so I can't help but like the game despite it's flaws.I just wish the team at doinksoft had more time to cook with GunbrellaThere is a wonderfull story and a crazy good gameplay somewhere here but we only saw a glimpse of it all.

_childDocuments_.review: I genuinely really wanted to love this game, the music is bloody fantastic, and the art style is so so so cool and interesting ( at least to me ) the gunplay felt nice and simple but easy for my brain to understand, but that's kinda all I can say about this game.the story and world building was just so underwhelming and sad story: It felt like it happened, there is no good conclusion to it or really any weight either it's like they wanted us to feel invested but what was there to be invested in? , everything just kind of happens within such a small frame which could've worked if the game was well longer, but it has no time to develop or grip you ( don't get me started on some big lore things being hidden behind a bunch of comics that can only be bought with the deluxe edition ) but I can't say much without massive spoilersthe world-building: the ♥♥♥♥ is this world building it was the thing that annoyed me the most, I WANT to know more about this weird world, whats with all the weird animals and monsters? why are there demons and magic, what's with all this tech but nothing to really tell us what this world is like????I'm very conflicted with this game, its trying to do so many things but not knowing what it's trying to go for.I am excited to see what the devs will make in the future because they seem VERY competent and know what they are doing but, maybe they need to stick with like a a few very well-put-together things instead of just trying to do everything to a good level but not going past that.

_childDocuments_.review: Fairly fun game, but it's really specific for people who like narratives.The trailers give the impression that this is a more action-oriented game, but what you see in the trailer is actually all there is to the game for combat. Because of that, I made the mistake of starting this game at hard difficulty. The hard difficulty is almost unplayable because the game's combat can feel very clunky.The best way to deal with mob enemies is to kill them before being spotted. The devs know this too, as they made the first mobs a one-shot kill on normal, but it takes two shots on hard. On hard, once spotted and you failed to kill them first, you're honestly ♥♥♥♥♥♥. Even the most basic enemies fire too quickly for you to find the chance to position yourself right and get a shot.The combat can still be fun if you're just going along with the narrative, but it quickly falls apart when it tries to be a more dynamic game where it expects you to do more than just move and shoot. To heal, you need to hold the button, which makes your character stand still for a good 2 seconds. Go figure that you shouldn't even use this while in combat.There's also just some general clunkiness, like it sometimes gets visually messy and you don't see what's actually happening. Or your gunbrella actually doesn't block a turret's bullets from point-blank. Also, the game resets the film grain option every time you exit to menu.Narrative games like this can honestly feel pretentious. It forces the story on players by making dialogue and cutscenes unskippable. This should be optional, as not all players will take your game the same way. Some only want gameplay. This severely limits the game's potential, as it also dooms replayability once you finish the game. They at least could have made cutscenes skippable once you finished the game and could do a new game+. The way the game ended, I honestly felt like all my game time was for nothing. I don't get to explore the game again with all the upgrades I unlocked or get the chance to unlock them all.The game does have a good world that could make you want to explore it. Sadly, the game doesn't fully realize its potential. I would have wanted to stay in the towns longer if there was actually something to do. What makes it worse is they later just get used for backtracking and making you walk long distances to advance the story.From this angle, this game is similar to Eastward. Eastward, however, does a better job utilizing its world and making you care for it. If you're looking for a simple narrative game you can just go along with, this is still a good experience. If you're looking for more gameplay, I recommend playing something else.

_childDocuments_.review: It has a great core mechanic that doesn't get to shine as bright as it should because both platforming sections and combat encounters stay very basic throughout the game. The sound, the visuals, and the overall vibe are all great tho.Hope they'll make a second one. _childDocuments_.review: (Will update as game gets updated)There's a lot to love here in Gunbrella, and although I cannot say that it's a perfect game, perhaps even far from it, it's absolutely an exceptional one that I do believe is worth your time. Instead of writing a super lengthy review, I'd much rather just write the pros and cons for this one.  Presentation - I believe that everything from the visuals, to the music, to the sound effects, to the designs have ALL been nothing short of fantastic. The different regions are memorable and beautiful, the music is fitting and fun, and the sound effects are chunky and crisp. Narrative - I do not think the narrative was perfect, but it was still far more interesting and engaging than several games I have played in a very long while. I was hooked, and the writing, for the most part, is either entertaining, or captivating. Narrative direction aside, even the characters were always fun and interesting to talk to! I don't believe every part of the narrative made sense, and sometimes there could have been better dialogue in some parts, but overall, I had an EXCELLENT time with this game's story and characters. The Gunbrella - The Gunbrella feels amazing to use. The platforming, the shooting, ooooh boy, it's amazing! It DOES take some getting used to though. Although I wish the game utilized the Gunbrella more with harder combat segments and more platforming ones, I was still very much satisfied with this marvel of a tool. Ammo System - The Gunbrella's default shotgun is a blast to use. It has infinite ammo, and is always reliable through and through... The other ammo types however... fall into several issues.                       1) They're in short supply. They're kiiind of expensive to buy, especially for the small amount that you get from purchasing them, and some of the ammo types are a little rarer to find naturally, either through enemy drops or through chests.                        2) You can only keep so little of them. This leads to a problem where you're always hording them because it almost never feels worth wasting them on enemies.                        3) Imbalance. Some SHRED and TRIVIALIZE bosses and some aren't even worth your inventory space.                       4) Swapping between weapons on controller... feels awful. More options please. Healing - Ehhh... Similar to Hollow Knight, when the player wishes to heal, they have to hold down the heal button to eat/use a consumable from their inventory. For some reason though, even after they fully complete the little gauge, some healing items have an animation afterwards that leaves you completely vulnerable??? I already finished the gauge, why is there a healing animation afterwards??? Makes it soooo easy for bosses to punish you and makes the healing feel god awful and awkward on some healing items. Bugs / Sometimes bad polish - These are currently being addressed, but they DO exist. Enemies - Enemies can kind of be dumb sometimes. It's really easy to enter a room and pick enemies off one at a time. Even in combat encounter rooms, for some reason? I feel like enemies were underutilized too sometimes. Would have been cool to fight off multiple enemies at a time, with some mixing and matching of different enemies. Despite these flaws, their actually not all that bad! In Hard mode, they're actually sometimes pretty menacing and although I wish enemy AI was better, and more was done with them, I actually still had a pretty fun time fighting them, especially, again, in hard mode where they're at their absolute best, and it can be tough to fight 'em!Bosses - There are a TON of bosses. I think because of this, there's a quantity over quality approach to them, where there's lots of them, but a ton of them can be cheesed or demolished. I enjoyed mostly every boss in the game but I truly feel like had some ammo types been more balanced, boss health was raised a bit more, and some bosses got a bit more time or polish, they ALL could have been AMAZING. There's tons of potential with these bosses, but none of them, not one boss in the game, has reached their utmost potential. Despite this, they're still fun, but they live a liiiittle bit to be desired. No cutscene and dialogue skips - Now, as I mentioned before, I actually love the characters, story, and cutscenes, but upon starting my SECOND play-through, I realized that they could not be skipped. That can be a deal breaker for some, and it makes replaying the game sooooo much more of a hassle. There's a lot to love here, there really is, but this game feels like it came out a little bit too early. A few more months, a bit more care, and I think we would have received one of the very best metroidvanias to date. What's here is great, and what's here is worth playing, but it isn't as good as it COULD'VE been and that leaves a sour taste in your mouth. If this game is to receive any updates that work on any of the aforementioned things, I'll be sure to edit this review. Until then, I would still highly recommend this game, but not to everyone.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm giving a negative only because of the communication and support of the developers. The game got 3 hotfix patches around launch for softlocks with no patch notes. The game still has enough bugs and I've read reports of more softlocks in their discord channel. The developers either ignore those reports, say cool, nice or thank you and that's it. At one point I asked when they were going to release a patch to fix the settings from resetting (film effect and someone else mentioned screen shake) and my question was completely dodged. I was told to do something with the ini files that has been confirmed to not work. They never said anything about releasing more patches in their entire discord. They're a core team of 3 developers but I've seen plenty of one man or a bigger team doing far better at releasing patches and informing the audience when to expect them. I'm talking patches to fix bugs and softlocks, nothing extra. It doesn't sit right with me despite enjoying and completing the game.  I will gladly change my review to positive and talk more about the game itself if it gets patches that are needed. And ideally, communicate better. The game deserves better than this.

_childDocuments_.review: A delightful, short metroidvania. The titular "Gunbrella" gives you your full range of movement from the start and it's fun with interesting depth when you try to integrate it into combat. The combat is fun, though you will encounter small bee enemies that are from hell.The highlight to me was, to my surprise, the story. It was simple on the surface, but cinematic and quite touching. I just finished it and still tearing up a bit. Also -!- a lot of choices that have consequences in late character interaction and (be careful what you say) sometimes character death. Quick personal preferences that might be useful to you - I'm not super hardcore but I play a lot of these games and was glad I chose 'hard' difficulty from the start. I didn't need more than a few tries on most bosses. Also, you can turn the film grain effect off and to my eye it looks better.Great stuff!

_childDocuments_.review: *NOTE: Beat the game, time played inaccurate due to playing offline*Gunbrella looks and plays like a passion project and for me that's enough of a reason to enjoy it. It's a simple, arcady game that is just fun to play. It's not audacious, brutal, surreal, and while I often like those characteristics in a game, Gunbrella reminds me above all what matters is: was it fun? Gunbrella was tight, simple platforming fun. _childDocuments_.review: One of the best recent 2d metroidvanias to hit the scene. Gameplay loop is perfect, controls feel excellent, story was surprisingly decent, lovecraftian elements, unique way of doing traditional platformer/metroidvania controls so instead of dash you open your gunbrella, open while jumping for "double jump", just a damn good, and I mean damn good, game. 5/5
_childDocuments_.name: Gunbrella

_childDocuments_.review: In short, the game looks great and polished, but the gameplay is critically unfulfilling it's potential and for that I wouldn't recommend the game at full price.The game's art-style, animations and audio is great. The gunbrella is a really fun mechanic for both fighting and platforming. The characters were interesting and the story was alright.HOWEVER, the game has extremely easy boss fights and nearly no platforming.I would argue that the first boss fight is the hardest due to the limited health points we have, but that quickly changes after like the third boss because the game suddenly starts handing out health upgrades like candy and you can then mostly tank and spam the ensuing bosses. I was playing on the hard difficulty and never needed to use any consumable during fights. This is a spoiler, but . Also, the second to last boss is by far the easiest in the game. He does one single move on repeat that is incredibly easy to evade.As for the platforming, I can only recall two sections that really made use of the platforming. This is mostly disappointing because the gunbrella is a great mechanic for platforming and it was barely utilized. I would have expected more platforming challenges and also more secrets reachable through platforming. There were so few secrets and so many opportunities for secret rooms.Small final note that the setting to adjust the film grain doesn't save for some reason. I have to readjust it everytime I open the game. It also reset itself after I beat the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunbrella

_childDocuments_.review: Checked this game out after seeing the trailer and the comparison to Celeste for the platform type movement.Whilie I thought it was a really cool concept, and I thought the art style/music were really well done, I felt like this game was really bare bones and lacking in secrets/exploration/challenges. It felt like you were on a rail, following along a noir story, and any puzzles you had to solve were basically talking to the NPCs in the correct order and going through every dialouge choice available. While the mechanics of the gunbrella are really cool (walljumps, mid air dashes, floating down from the sky) and the weapons also offered variety (long distance quick shots, short shotguns, high impact grenades, sitcky bombs) they felt really underutilized. The only time I struggled were the 5-6 boss fights. Otherwise, you could just race from place to place.It seems like this game was made by a small and dedicated team that had a very strong story and art direction in mind with a really cool mechanic in place. This is a solid start- but it just feels like they could have done so much more to make the movement of this game actually worthwhile (it's almost never worthwhile to jump around and explore the edges of screens). As both a shooter and a platformer this felt really underwhelming to me and I feel like it could be so much more.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunbrella

_childDocuments_.review: While I enjoyed Gunbrella, the game is weird.  It kind of just confuses me.For one, the gunbrella is inherently kind of goofy, but most of the game is played up as completely serious with blood, gore, and some hard swearing.  This contrast is present throughout the game's story, and it felt like a bizarre twilight zone experience for me.I played on hard using keyboard and mouse controls, and the game play was really enjoyable.  However, it felt like the game's difficulty curve was backwards for me.  While playing through the game, the most challenging part was the very first area, and the difficulty gradually lowered from there.  Maybe I just got really good with the controls as I progressed, but later areas and bosses felt trivial.  You could also say I shouldn't have upgraded the gunbrella and my health, but games with these things can still have a fair challenge after upgrading.Finally, performance was fine and I never had the game crash, but the game generally feels like it's missing an update that fixes just a handful of minor bugs or annoyances.  For example, the film grain setting resets to its default value every time a save is loaded or when going to the title screen.  It's just strange that this kind of thing slipped through and isn't patched yet.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunbrella

_childDocuments_.review: Very good game. Although it might be a bit cruel and kinda "depressing". _childDocuments_.review: The short of it:Absolutely and utterly NO, unless you like arcade action run and guns with an analog stick, AND 3/4 of the stick's movement each way (left/right) being a dead zone (no exaggeration), AND no user configurable controller options at all in game.In a nutshell, horrid controls ruin a potentially brilliant game.I didn't even make 10 minutes and it was already a chore rather than any kind of fun. That said, I can't comment on the music as I didn't go deep into the game, I was only practising the controls on the first stage, but I CAN say I liked the pixel art style quite a bit!Now, the uber long version:"Another potentially awesome game, RUINED, due to terrible controls".Once again, someone has done that rare but ridiculously short sighted thing of releasing a run and gun action game and disabling the d-pad (I mean, seriously)?.. but of course, the character movement is NOT analogue, in fact there is a massive dead zone, AND he only moves at the one, DIGITAL, speed. We are losing SO much response time just moving the analogue stick from left to right, instead of an instant reaction d-pad. The mind boggles with these ridiculous developer decisions.Strike one.You can almost work around it by playing it as a twin stick - almost -  but the aiming on the right stick is infinitely variable and very precise, i.e. not always suited for heat of the moment action, whereas aiming with the left stick is a few quick preset directions like diagonal, straight up, down etc. The way most will play, IMO.Really, the game is designed primarily as a single control stick run and gun (and the tutorial instructions say as much), yet without d-pad support, and designed as such that it fights the player every step of the way, instead of giving crisp, insta reactive and low lag controls. AND THEN:-If playing in twin stick configuration, there is no "hold the analog trigger down to continuously discharge weapon" function, you need to pump the right analogue trigger for each and every shot. So fatiguing. Do you know, only about a single percent of twin stick shooters and run and guns behave this way? Most don't do it, cause it outright sucks. Combined with the unbelievably important umbrella dash/fly move being on the right bumper, this game is downright horrible to play as a twin stick shooter.Strike 2.Not a single input option in game, in fact an input options section doesn't even exist.It's an exercise in a finger decathlon, *incredibly* poorly thought out, and makes me wonder if the developers have ever even played this type of arcade action game before. I am still surprised. I mean, seriously, devs?Strike three.I already returned it before I wrote this review, as it was not fun to me at all, rather in just a few minutes I KNEW I'd be fighting the controls the entire time, and to me, that's zero actual fun.Instead of making it organic and natural for the player, it's as if they have purposely coded it to feel frustrating and downright compromised no matter whether you play it as a single stick or twin stick -  artificial tacked on difficulty due to horrible controls, is *never* a good kind of difficulty. In other words, each control scheme is severely hampered by not having any adjustability, nor rapid fire in the case of the twin stick configuration (as well as the horrid analog stick dead zone), and no d-pad support in single control stick operation. You could use an arcade stick, as most good sticks have a toggle to chooser whether they transmit as the d-pad or analog stick,  but the button mapping for everything but movement is then wrong, hence, it NEEDS an easy to use in game remapping option if they are going to stubbornly stick to the idea of no d-pad support. So there's literally no way to make this game good, unless you are comfy with Steam control setup (I am not, at all) and deep dive to create a Steam custom control scheme.I always say, if a dev can't be bothered to code their own game properly, I don't spend my time doing their job for them. I already paid for the game at that point, and that's all I should have to do to play it and enjoy it, other than change some IN GAME options. But they aren't there in this case.I was really looking forward to this one, truly, and snapped it up at the first sale.What a shame. For me, this has the worst control scheme of any run and gun I have played since I first used Steam in 2020. Period. It sucks.How they can fix it:1) Allow d-pad for movement, so we can play with A for jump and X to shoot like a regular run and gun, and therefore completely ignore the right stick.2) Allow some input changes in game, so we can say put direction lock on left bumper and dash on right bumper (OK, dash is already on right bumper), but this way, by not playing it as a twin stick but rather as a regular run and gun, it will feel totally natural as two fingers will be permanently sitting on the bumpers and not interfering with shooting or jumping on the X and A buttons in any way shape or form.3) Allow an auto fire of some kind, especially for those playing as a twin stick and using the right trigger. Less important if using the X button to shoot.So really, what it boils down to is, by locking out the d-pad, they created a ricochet effect that ruined the rest of the game, as every single control setup suffers from it.Never in my lifetime will I understand why a developer locks out the d-pad on an action game with digital character movement. Make it make sense.And it's not as if they aren't aware of the d-pad, as it can be used for options and journal/inventory browsing in game.. it's as if they purposely locked it out for movement, to make the character feel sluggish with a massive dead zone on an analogue stick. It really feels like, "we have ruined the controls on purpose, muuuuuuuhahahahha".They sabotaged their own game.Sigh. Sigh. and sigh again.Of course, one could play it with the left analogue stick and ignore the right, and use A to jump and X to shoot, just as the game instructs, but due to the ridiculously large dead zone, it's a no go for me (and anyone else who likes responsive main character control).This one is not hard to fix, but will they? That remains to be seen. I will indeed bother to re-buy it and spend my money on it again -  if the dev bothers to fix it;)I have decided to add a final rating to all my reviews from now on.As it stands, this is a 3/10 at best, as the current control scheme is truly horrid. 'Nuff said.

_childDocuments_.review: Gunbrella is a good one!  Solid pixel art, solid combat, and fantastic traversal methods combine to form an enjoyable little 2D side scrolling action game.  Your gunbrella not only blasts enemies, but can give you a dash in any direction and then help you glide to your destination.  In addition, you can wall jump up vertical planes, and this all combines to give you an excellent sense of freedom as you move through the world.  The action is par for the course, but the ability to use the gunbrella for defense, and the aforementioned traversal options give the combat that extra, unique spice, that every good game needs.  It's a cliche story of revenge, and a world on the brink, but the characters have a lot of charm and the story serves its purpose.  I enjoyed Gunbrella and I am glad I played through it.7/10Note - Currently Steam says I have only 2 hours played of this game.  There must have been some issue with the timer and the Steam Deck, it feels like it certainly took a few more hours than that.

_childDocuments_.review: Take an umbrella and slap a gun on it and you get a pretty fun little fast-paced indie side scroller.Gunbrella is a side scroller that emphasizes fast combat and fluid movement. Most enemies die in one or two shots and this leads to some faster paced gameplay, only helped by how quick the movement is here. Your gunbrella allows you to slide, jump, hover, and otherwise dash around very quickly and it makes for some really fun gameplay. It is never not satisfying to enter a room and dispatch all of the enemies while flying through the air and exiting without even touching the ground. The devs really did a good job making the movement fun and intuitive to use.The combat is also quite fun, but not without its issues. Your gunbrella can make use of multiple ammo types, but I found the other ammo types so scarce that I only ever ended up using them for bosses and that just felt like wasted potential. The game could use more of those enemies too. It got a bit old fighting the same types over and over and while new ones were occasionally introduced, they lacked the variety to really get rid of that monotony.That and the game has a bad habit of sticking these enemies with the simplest of attack patterns. Which unfortunately also extends to the bosses - probably the most hit or miss element of the entire experience. You get some really cool ones that have a bunch of cool moves and then other ones that seem like they should be this big and difficult thing, but end up having just a single move that they repeat the entire fight. Very disappointing there.The level design is cool and leaves room for secrets and even full blown sidequests, the game world is incredibly detailed and I really liked the grungy pixel art aesthetic, the music has some standout tracks and matches that aesthetic, and the story actually is not that bad. I did not go into this game expecting the story to be such a large element, so I was pleasantly surprised to find a somewhat well thought out plot complete with characters that are genuinely interesting to talk to, dark humor that matches the setting, and even the ability to make decisions throughout the story that change certain outcomes. It is not something super complex, but it is engaging enough.It took me just under five hours to complete the game and that is with doing some side quests along the way. The experience is rather linear and I cannot say that it is really that replayable as a result. That said, there are some sizeable side quests to clear if you are looking to squeeze additional time out of it, along with some achievements that could possibly require a second playthrough.A bit disappointing that it appears to be locked to 60 fps, but otherwise, I had no issues with performance and no bugs to speak of. It is a very polished experience and plays well on both controller and keyboard and mouse. Gunbrella is fast, fun, and violent - mixing a dark and grungy aesthetic with some very fluid and satisfying gameplay. It may be lacking in some areas - namely enemy variety, the boss fights, and the ammo types, but the rest of the experience makes up for it. I enjoyed my time with it and it’s a great way to kill five hours or so.Follow my  for more reviews + videos!

_childDocuments_.review: What an excellent game this was!  The gameplay was fluid and fast.  I love the hybrid genre mix of a metroidvania with something like an open sandbox game with resources to buy and quests to accomplish.  All the characters are unique and memorable.  The enemies (particularly the bosses) look -fantastic-!! One of the things I really appreciated about this game was that there was a bare minimum of backtracking and that even without a map I never felt lost.  That is quite hard to do I imagine.  I only wish the game could go on for longer...not that it is that short of a game for this particular genre....its just that I was enjoying the game so much and did not want it to end!  To that end, I would say that if I had to find a fault SOMEWHERE with Gunbrella, it is that I don't feel there are enough quests.  I feel the potential to go back and check up on old friends is there but not capitalized on...but in the future, perhaps there will be DLC content to grant my wishes! :)  Regardless, I fully recommend Gunbrella for fans of the genre, and for gamers who just like great games (because I don't particularly seek out metroidvanias myself but I LOVED this title).  Give the demo a try and if you like it, def give this one a purchase!

_childDocuments_.review: I actually refunded this game today, and it's a pretty big shame. I do like the developer, do like the controls A LOT, but this really fell flat for me for multiple reasons. I originally bought it, as movement-heavy games like this are fun (I speedrun stuff on Twitch sometimes) and this looked like a great game. Both from a casual experience, and a potential speedrun perspective, this game really just wasn't fun. The things I can give it:- Controls for sure, very fluid, very responsive, very good mechanics. Very Celeste-like, just not as complex, but still very deep. The legitimately bad:- I love narrative, but I honestly didn't care about this world and its characters even right from the start. There's a lot of dialogue, but dialogue that must be interacted with to progress, which honestly halts the platforming very often. - The problem, piggybacking on the first point, is there's an extreme lack of direction as to where you're supposed to go, both in general and for side quests. At least, in the beginning, I was wandering around aimlessly trying to figure out where to even proceed, and in talking to everyone, solved quests in reverse. I basically explored sewers, killed rats, picked up rats, then talked to a NPC I didn't talk to the first time/missed who suddenly needed rats for a train ticket that I needed to progress.- The biggest problem: the controls and mechanics are very good, but there's nothing in the game that I experienced in about ~2 hours that really makes use of them on a complex level. You could strip the game of every mechanic outside of jump and wall jump and probably beat up until I did using just those 2. The mechanics are extremely underutilised. Overall, maybe I could of pushed myself to enjoy this and maybe it would have been a good game, but it's just very slow, not at all what I expected. I rarely request refunds and leave negative reviews. I was really let down by this one, as I don't often buy newer games close to release either (primarily just play retro stuff.) I don't think it delivered in any way and didn't enjoy my time with it at all. I'm glad others seemed to like it, but yeah, everything above made it not for me.

_childDocuments_.review: I wouldn't say this is a bad game, it's definitely possible to have fun with it. It just really felt like something was missing with it, like it was just a hair away from being really memorable. The movement options are really solid, but the level design almost never lets it live up to its full potential. There are a lot of screens that forcibly slow you down, either through long empty spaces you have to trek through or obnoxiously cramped quarters that you can't schmoove in. The combat is decent, but none of the enemies or encounters are interesting enough to make it thrilling. The whole inventory/consumables system feels entirely unnecessary. I likely would have interacted with it more if using/switching items and ammo types wasn't as slow or finnicky, or if it was more convenient to obtain them. Enemies don't respawn, so you have a finite amount of money and therefore finite items, not to mention extremely low item caps and having to bring various items you pick up (which are limited) to a vendor somewhere to convert them into usable items (which are also limited). It seems like the low item cap was meant to encourage players to use items more, but when your ability to obtain them is so unreliable it doesn't work.The writing is, well, flimsy. This is sad because it tries to tackle some interesting themes and has lots of potential for exploring the world and the characters within, but it never fleshes them out properly. This ties in to my biggest complaint of the game: THE PACING. This is a short game, and while that is by no means a bad thing, for this particular game it throws a huge wrench in the works. The story premise is an investigative noir in a melancholy setting, all of which begs for time to stew and ponder, uncovering things slowly and starting to put the pieces together. There's even hints at this being considered during development, with your multiple dialogue choices when questioning some characters. There are a bunch of characters who could be charming if your conversations with them didn't happen at mach 2. There are characters that treat you like they've known you all their life when they have had a total of like 5 minutes of screen time. I was able to complete all of the optional content and fully upgrade my character and the game still felt kind of hollow, just because nothing was given time to develop naturally. No locations stick in your mind, the boss fights are forgettable, I can remember the names of only a couple characters, all because everything was just crammed into such a tight timespan.Ultimately, I respect this game and what it was trying to accomplish, I just think it didn't know its own strengths and weaknesses and subsequently fell short. It isn't at all an unpleasant experience, but I can't say it's a memorable or engaging one either.

_childDocuments_.review: I think its fitting that my 100th Steam review is not only an indie game, but a Devolver published indie game, because Enter the Gungeon was my FIRST indie game, and the one that made me fall in love with indies in general. The first thing I said when I booted up Gunbrella on stream and shot the gun for the first time was, "Hey thats kinda like Gungeon". Most of this game is nothing like Gungeon, but as with most games that Devolver chooses to publish, there's a certain something about them that exudes this consistent feeling that the game knows what it wants to be and reaches for it. Gunbrella is great, lets get that out of the way. For 15 bucks you can't really complain about much. Its stylish, the sound design is going to be one of those that goes under the radar come GOTY time, but damn if this game doesn't sound f*cking amazing. Every little bleep and bloop, sound effects, trills to let you know things are happening like saves and quests popping up, it all fits so well with the theme here. The music is also fantastic, but as an aside, there were some portions of the endgame that I think lacked music not for atmosphere, but because the script wasn't working properly and the music just wasn't playing. Audio bugs were the only thing I encountered the whole game though, so props for releasing a game thats... well, finished? lolI saw a review call this game "Celeste with guns" and honestly, thats not a bad description. The movement is very clean, with great precision but just the right amount of floatiness to balance between too stiff and too floaty. Its the third bowl of porridge, just right.The combat overall feels pretty great, especially when you really get a good clear of a room going and pop the shotgun at the perfect time to get full damage and one hit kills all the way through, but as far as the combat goes, I do have a few criticisms. First and foremost, I did not feel the need or even incentive to use other ammunition types until quite literally the very end of the game. There were opportunities that it could have been fine, but it never felt like I'd be gaining a huge advantage over the base shotgun. More often than not, too, I opted to just keep the shotgun out for familiarity's sake. Why switch up the rhythm of how I play when its still working?Enemies were fun to engage with mostly, but they did feel fairly sparse until the very end of the game. The level design was fun (especially some platforming gauntlets) but on the normal difficulty, which is typically the best balanced in most games, I felt as though the difficulty curve never really had that uptick. There were parts that I died, but it was mostly due to my own impatience, and some of the later bosses and just bosses in general were pretty lackluster. Thats not to say they arent visually engaging, they all look great, but mechanically speaking the second to last boss even was just kinda underwhelming. Thankfully, that doesn't matter all that much, because the other elements of Gunbrella really tie everything together very solidly despite the noteable dip in quality in the last hour or two.The sound design is phenomenal like I mentioned, graphically speaking the pixel art is great and its very stylistically cohesive which is tough to pull off. I wasn't expecting as much eldritch theming as there was, but it didn't feel out of place. The story is basic and predictable, but held together by a charming cast of characters. The dialogue was pretty genuinely funny sometimes and that goes a long way for keeping players moving along. There were definitely some lull points where the dialogue was a bit too wordy at points, and frankly the ending of the game made f*ckall sense. I think I got the bad ending and I have an idea as to how to get the good ending but regardless of the very final moment of the game, there was a lot of "I guess that's how that worked out" moments that left myself and the people watching me scratching our heads a little bit.Again, this game is great though. I realize that I'm criticizing it a lot in this review, but thats mostly because there's an almost intangible joy to playing something like this. I really liked how zipping around the levels at 100mph shotgun at the ready was a valid playstyle, and I enjoyed the second half twist. I thought I was nearing the end of the game about 3 hours in, but there's a fun realization that you are going to see the very direct future consequences of your prior actions in game and that was great. Despite the lack of a real difficulty bump or mechanical test of skill towards the end of the game, the most important takeaway for Gunbrella is that from opening to closing credits, it was very *fun*. I think that gets missed in a lot of reviews, because I can nitpick and put every game under a microscope until there's nothing left, but at the end of the day all that really matters is if a game delivers on the fun factor, and Gunbrella's whole deal is ensuring that your gun/umbrella stays entertaining from start to finish. Thanks for reading, follow my curator page for more indie reviews like this one (a little more coherent usually lol its very late for me).

_childDocuments_.review: No.I've experienced a lot of bad controller setups. Gunbrella is yet another that just isn't and can't be planned out well. It is a twin stick shooter, but suffers from what could be considered two jump buttons....except one of them isn't always jump. Yep, the umbrella button. Its horrible.Add in the "lets pause your ability to react while you consume a item that takes a couple seconds to use, yet everything else is going on around you" button too. Ugh.Being a twin stick shooter, the game plays best when focusing on the bumpers and triggers, but that gets confusing. LT is jump, RT is fire, and RB is umbrella. But to get the full umbrella effect...you jump first, then open the umbrella. However, when fighting baddies...this becomes a mess of me having to stop and think what order I do things, rather than naturally reacting.it does also let you use the X,Y, A, and B buttons....but that doesn't last too long since it takes away the ability to twin stick this. And that is fine and dandy until you get to the first boss. Then you will need to two stick it.Sadly there really isn't a good layout for the way this works. But I just got too sick of:"Here comes the boss. Jump and....oh crap that was umbrella button. Gotta shoot quick to push him away. Oh crap...now I hit the jump button instead of fire. Better hit umbr....ugh...just hit the item button trying to get the umbrella open."Maybe it just isn't working for me...but I have been playing games since  Atari 2600. Controls should just become intuitive quickly. This one just doesn't. Also I got sick of sharing a space with the guns, having the umbrella open to block shots, but because we were overlapping, all I do is register hits and lose 1/2 health. There are too many good games out there. Go towards one of those instead.

_childDocuments_.review: "Gunbrella" is a fun game where you play as a cowboy with a cool tool: a mix of a shotgun and an umbrella. This special item lets you shoot enemies, block attacks, fly in the air, and zip along lines. The game is all about action and using this umbrella-gun in clever ways.The setting is like a cowboy movie mixed with a fantasy world, full of steam-powered machines and quirky towns filled with people who give you missions, sell stuff, or challenge you to battles.In the game, you can move around in all sorts of ways, like dashing, jumping higher by opening the umbrella mid-jump, and gliding on wind. Fights are exciting too. You can use the umbrella to bounce back enemy fire and use the shotgun part to take down the bad guys in a big way.Playing with the gun-umbrella is the best part. As you move forward, you get different types of bullets that change how you can fight. But even with these cool features, the game sticks to simple controls and fun action, not getting too complicated.There are ways to make your gun-umbrella better and to heal up or get stronger, but the game is set up so you're not too worried about losing. If you're having trouble, it's usually more fun to just try again rather than going back to get ready.It's a short but super fun game that keeps you entertained with its unique weapon and the action-packed adventures in a steam-powered cowboy world. It's easy to get into and keeps things exciting from start to finish.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to give this game a fair try but the pacing was so off putting to me. There are moments where the action turns up and combat feel rewarding, but later screeches to a halt after passing a few screens (or the frequency of save benches, which also heal you). The number of mechanics they introduce to you at first is overwhelming, such as different ammo types, various foods, shops that can cook food, and beds that give you extra health (not to mention the pills that give various buffs). Another thing that's all over the place is its difficulty: from two enemies on the screen who die in a few shots to three enemies that can wreck your health. This feels like a super ambitious project that had a lot of idea wanted to get crammed in at once, and that's not always a good thing. I'm sorry, but I won't be getting on the next train to see how this story ends.

_childDocuments_.review: I think that Gunbrella is a really well made game. Overall rating:7.5/10Gameplay:5/10Story:9/10Difficulty:3/10Here's why:The animations and style of the entire game are absolutely wonderful to look at and experience. however, I don't think that it's the best game for everyone. There isn't much of a challenge and it feels like a lot of the focus of the developers went more to the story rather than polishing the gameplay. _childDocuments_.review: As a huge metroidvania fan, I was drawn to  during the 2024 Steam Summer Sale. The demo showcased the titular gunbrella as a unique and fun way to navigate the world, with an intriguing combat/blocking loop and potential for interesting upgrades. However, if you're expecting significant growth and evolution, you'll be disappointed.If you seek frustrating combat mired with unwieldy controls and leftist subtexts against capitalism and individualism,  is for you.The story is simple: you're a father seeking revenge after your wife is killed and daughter stolen. It's a standard trope, lacking the sophistication of games like . Many other games have handled this story with greater nuance.The gritty, grim aesthetic is appealing, though I turned down the film grain as it was distracting. Kudos to the artists for conceptualizing the setting.Controlling the gunbrella during firefights is cumbersome. There's no control mapping option, and you can be holding the block button, facing the right direction, and still get hit. This is especially frustrating in gunfights with multiple opponents, where blocking often fails inexplicably.Checkpoints range from overly generous to frustratingly sparse, compounded by unskippable animations and cutscenes. While some cutscenes can be shortened, others cannot, making repeated attempts a slog. The end credits, for example, can't be skipped, only fast-forwarded.The ending is unsatisfying, likely intentionally. The "good" ending requires acquiring a random, unremarkable item early in the game. This item is never explained, and two NPCs try to convince you to give it up. Despite the game's political themes, it lacks depth in its lore.Spoiler Alert: Ending and SymbolismWhile political discourse through art and media can be nuanced,  opts for a stark, inelegant approach, which only serves to highlight the game's flaws. Even without the developers' slant, it's biggest issue is that it just isn't a good game. The gunbrella mechanic never evolves beyond what you see in the demo, with no exploration upgrades. The results are unrealized possibilities for what should have been a unique navigation mechanic.Overall, the game doesn't outstay its welcome, but its poor controls and unfulfilled potential make it a mediocre metroidvania. The politics are really just the cherry on top of an underwhelming sundae of a game. It's not worth the price of admission, and I wouldn't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Gunbrella is OK. I feel like it could've done with about 10% of the text in exchange for more encounters and platforming level design. Ultimately I feel like the game has really tight controls and fun idea for combat and platforming, but it's not taken advantage of as much as it could've been. I felt like I spent half the game reading text, in a game that's clearly an action combat platformer with some original ideas for mobility.Other than lacking a quantity of interesting combat encounters, and more variety in enemy behavior (most enemies can be countered by stun-locking them with the Gunbrella and shooting the base shotgun rounds), the inventory menus (ammo type and consumables) are not well suited to the action gameplay.The pixel art is wonderful, the world is a diesel-punk dystopia that's well fleshed out with some fairly memorable locations, and there's tons of potential in the action. I think most people will get some enjoyment out of it. But it I was quite bored of the story by the end, and wished the team had leaned more into what made Gunbrella unique - the action mechanics.I'm leaving a positive review because it's not a bad game. It nonetheless failed to deliver on its potential.

_childDocuments_.review: Celeste with a gun was how this game was sold  to me.  While that is accurate, I was surprised to find how story focused the game was. For what its worth the story is engaging and the noir aesthetic carries the game well, but if you want pure platforming the game might leave you wanting. Especially considering the game is fairly short even with the story beats.The game play itself is engaging. the fights feel fairly frenetic and the platforming while finicky at first felt rewarding to master.  With that said the hard mode just increases enemy health and rate of fire, which I didn't find to change my playstyle very much since most of the enemies have rather dumb A.I. and can be cheesed. Similarly several of the bosses can be stun locked. It's a game that feels intense without being overly demanding.An extra thing to point out is that rather than the achievements focusing on challenges, they focus on different choices you can make during the story. While this encourages repeat playthroughs, it doesn't do much for the platforming.Try the game out if its around $10.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those rare cases where I'd like to recommend it, but simply can't. Gunbrella's artstyle and music are beautiful but the game just feels half baked. The gimmick of the Gunbrella is fun at first but it never really adds depth to the mechanic, nor really challenges you with it. Overall, Gunbrella is quite easy with save/heal benches in every couple rooms, and bosses with 3-5 attack patterns, most of which can be nearly stunlocked with just the Gunbrella's dash and spamming the shotgun.Gunbrella also cant seem to decide if it wants to be an intense gameplay focused game like celeste or a more active story game. The frequent backtracking, especially in the middle third of the game, also come across as padding in an already short (4.5hr for me) game.I think Gunbrella could've used another year in development, but i can appreciate the final product for what it is. That being said, if you're interested in Gunbrella, watch a lets play of it, then decide if it looks like something you'd like to spend you're time and money on.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really fun little game.  It's a very personal story about revenge set in a sad, failed Lovecraftian world.  Along the way you're confronted with decisions that can have a noticeable impact on that world, making it a bit better or worse than when you set off on your journey.  The gameplay is sublime.  It has your standard run-and-gun combat, but the introduction of the umbrella as a tool does a lot to elevate the game.  The umbrella acts like a shield/parry system, repelling projectiles back at your enemies.  It also lets you slingshot into the air, which makes the platforming feel like something more at home in an (easier) version of Super Meat Boy or Celeste. Combat aside, half the game is exploring, talking to people and taking on random but short-and-satisfying side-quests.  The whole story is a very fun, creative ride, and I was happy to strap in for it.  Just go in with the right expectations, knowing there's some dialogue heavy scenes at points as well as town exploring, and I think you'll end up really enjoying this game.  Immersing your self in the game's dark, horrifying world, with its Lovecraftian themes and black comedy, is half the fun.+Exceptional combat+Fun roller-coaster of a revenge story+Small but dense world to explore+Fun antagonists+Side quests with real consequences (and rewards)+Great visual style -It's short . . . that's my only real criticismSo yeah, this is very sold recommend.   I hope Devolver Digital keeps publishing games like this, and that we see more games from Doinksoft in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: I was so pumped for this game on release, but waited until a sale to pick it up because of average review scores. Those reviews were generally accurate, but I will add my own thoughts. This is a worthwhile game for a first-publishing attempt!! I think this game had a ton of great mechanical ideas. The umbrella combat felt fun, I liked the dashing, jumping and reflecting combat tricks that had a mild amount of depth before dropping off in difficulty near the end of the game. The story was absolute dribble, not worth paying attention and the tone couldn't decide if it wanted to lean seriously into noir drama or 5-year old comedy chops. This game didn't need a story IMO, but the amount of dialogue we got did not motivate me. Overall, grab it on sale and crunch in an afternoon! Some experiences don't need to be perfect, this is one of those that was worth my time and I want to see this kind of game in the future addressing it's weak spots!!![+] Mild depth in game play mechanics, umbrella combat is cool[+] pixel graphics and lighting were well produced[-] Only about 5 hours of story, and side missions were an underdeveloped afterthought[-] story and writing are not well developed
