_childDocuments_.review: A fun little game that lasts about 6-7 hours. Pretty straight forward with good violence, some humor and manageable platforming. I must admit that until the end I never really got a 100% how the umbrella works. I got along but never felt fully in control. Also, I think the game would have benefited from improved weapon handling, especially when changing ammunition which is rather cumbersome and imprecise. What I liked was that there are no respawning enemies, so you can really clean out the levels which feels appropriate for a revenge driven story. The ending could have been more ambiguous, after all they first present a rather big and relatable moral dilemma - only to wash over it seconds later. Good, but not brilliant 6.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Gunbrella

_childDocuments_.review: The  game is not too long but packs a punch in terms of its story and its plethora of interesting and relatable characters. It's very fun to play and rarely for games of this type, makes me want to play it again after the first play-through. Both platforming and fighting are incredibly fun. I played it on the Steam Deck and it worked great.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunbrella

_childDocuments_.review: Like it? buy the game!So Gunbrella is fast and satisfying gunplay mixed with unique movement mixed with intriguing storytelling.Outstanding for me were all the unique characters you meet, the challenging level design, the (often grim) jokes and the coal coated steampunk there was to explore.Small advice (No spoilers):At first this game has a heavier focus on the murder mystery story and world exploring and feels a bit slow-paced. This  changes after you beat the first boss, things escalate and combat gets tough, leading you one step further on your journey. If there are items to buy, don't save money, buy them now. You'll need them later. -Core Gunbrella gameplay is really easy to learn, but hard to master -> good movement is as important as  precise aim-Special ammo types are neat although standard buckshot works best against most enemies (also WHY are rifle rounds burst ARGH)-Good balance between character dialogue and combat, fighting against large enemy groups is really fun I wish there was more of it-Bosses are exceptionally well made, some could even use more HP (played on medium difficulty, hard mode should be different)-Pixel backgrounds and people look vibrant and lively despite the sun-blocking coal clouds (though I recommend turning down the film grain slider a bit)-Talking with Scarlett, Sewert, the Scapyard Gang or everyone else feels real. Some really great dialogue.-As mentioned, after the introduction the story progresses slowly for a bit. This however isn't the case afterwards, now you got a decent clue where you need to head to, you make new friends and foes while travelling to foreign places with just enough time to appreciate them but never enough to get too familiar. When the time comes you'll know what to do, but after that uncertainty waits.Gunbrella is really good.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunbrella

_childDocuments_.review: Very good game. achievement hunt is pretty quick but also inspires replay-ability.  The bosses are pretty lacking and i feel they could have done more complex things with the platforming. story is extremely well crafted and interesting and each replay seems faster each time. overall 8.5/10 would buy on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunbrella

_childDocuments_.review: Gunbrella is a short and sweet experience that definitely scratches that classic Metroid-Vania itch with a hint of Celeste thrown in for good measure. It's not without it's minor faults, but it's outweighed by it's overall engaging gameplay and punchy combat mechanics. BIggest downsides would be it's overall length, lack of grander map/exploration, and it's replayability. Overall, a good sale purchase and a solid game.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunbrella

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic action platformer with a ton of heart. The story follows a man on a quest through a dystopian world to save his daughter. Along the journey you'll meet all sorts of interesting characters to help or harm on your quest. From cultists, to wild animals, mercenaries, and even demons there's no shortage of interesting enemies to take on either. Game is an absolute gem start to finish.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunbrella

_childDocuments_.review: narrative focused metroidvania with sick gunplay, fun movement, lots of interesting side content and choices that have a palpable effect on the world and story.there were a few hiccups with umbrella controls in sections where i wanted to float but instead got a mid air dash, but they were relatively rare. short, sweet, and the aforementioned choices give you a fresh experience on a second playthrough if you're into that
_childDocuments_.name: Gunbrella

_childDocuments_.review: I came because the concept of a gunbrella is pretty cool, and it's cool, mostly a shotgunbrella, the game is at it's peak when You're dashing from to enemy to enemy, since if You are close enough to land the three dispersing shots is mainly an instakill, and if it's not You can always dash at them to stun them and finish them for good.So the core of the gunbrella is excellent, but that's all You'll get, there arent any new abilities, only some limited ammo types that are too akward to use, I only used them in some bosses. This is fine if a little disappointing, but it's a game of a little more of five hours, and maybe You can master the Gunbrella movement in an hour or two. And for the rest of the runtime they add some really needed hazards to the levels, like unclimable walls, chains for swinging, conveyor belts, and some more. So in the end gameplay wise it doesnt get boring, I mean it would be hard since the base movement is so fun, dont expect hard platforming, is overall pretty easy.Easy are also the enemies, since You can parry all of their bullets, or ram into them with the dash, they feel pretty helpless and You wont need to adapt Your strategy of closing the gap and shooting.The bosses are mostly on the easy side too, they have a little too much health for my taste, but it was over once I learned when to land my shots and when to evade, even if in some cases I died a couple times.Gameplay aside the story and characters are my favorite part, it starts slow, but it's worth it, except for the end that doesn't have almost any dialogue, and I would like to know what the charismatic characters think about the ending, not just some mude scenes.The pixel art, and overall lock of the game its pretty good, also the sound too, they combine to make a perfect ambience. The music its allright too, nothing too crazy, but it gets the job well done.Overall my congratulation to the developers, I'm looking forward for whatever they do next, they nailed this game vibes, so I have in faith in their next games.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunbrella

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely worth a buy. I really liked the art style and the story. Might go for a second run and do things a bit differently.If you like a happy ending, then . Mechanics could be a bit less clunky, at least that's my impression. Murray doesn't always get the umbrella out in time, when you expect it. But I still enjoyed it. 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Gunbrella

_childDocuments_.review: You could simplify the description of the game as "a revenge story" but that wouldn't be giving it enough credit. Gunbrella is stylish, smooth, crazy, fun, intuitive, exciting, cute, disgusting, and insidious, all in one package. I won't say much else except that you absolutely must play it, because it is so damn good.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunbrella

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, I just played through and finished. I thought overall the gameplay was really good but seeing other people play it with mouse and keyboard made me think I shouldn't have used my controller because GOOD GOD the freaking BEES are so hard to hit when you can only aim in 45 degree increments and you move where you aim which made this so much harder. Still doable but final boss took like 5 tries. I thought the game was fun, story was ok. A decent bite sized platformer. The gunbrella was the most fun and interesting thing in terms of gameplay/movement, felt good man.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunbrella

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very hard review to write, because I enjoyed the game, I really did but.......It isn't what I thought it was. The screenshots and trailer frame it as an action shooter adventure... sadly the game is 60% pressing "E" reading speech bubbles and full with very easy boss fights. Like really easy... With no heavy spoilers, one fight (that I was really reaaaaaaaaally looking forward to) literally defeated the boss by closing my eyes and doing nothing.. I was in shock!Had no reason to use any other weapons in the game (main gun is OP), and the enemy types are less than a dozen... So why am I giving it a recommendation? I liked the story and the way your choices can impact the story. Really liked the humour and characters, the gunbrella mechanics are so much fun and the art style is so good. I highly recommend people to read the reviews first before buying to see if the game style is what you are signing up for. I just wish it was advertised differently thats all
_childDocuments_.name: Gunbrella

_childDocuments_.review: Yes I'd recommend it with the caveat that you probably want to wait until its around 20-30% off.Story wise its strong the entire way through, no complaints about it or the dialogue.Gameplay wise, its quite frontloaded - most of the fun parts happen at the start and the later parts suffer tedium wise - with the final 3 bosses being quite a letdown compared to some of the initial fights (spongey with either 0 strategy required, a specific cheese bait required, or just plain rng based in order leading up to the final boss).Overall I'd definitely recommend it, and its a solid game, just needs a bit more polish at the end to be truly great.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunbrella

_childDocuments_.review: It's pretty dreadful on controller, the controls work fine but it just never felt good and I think that's due to the twin-stick being designed with a mouse in mind. After like four hours I was still trying to aim my gun and umbrella with the same stick (since its the same ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ thing in his hand) and it just made me nauseous to try and master. I know that's a niche issue but I also don't like the game. The characters are less interesting than my hotel wall and the story is earthbound-derivative-derived millenial mush, the tiles look bad and you can't tell what's a wall, the enemies are boring and irritating, I hated this game. I hope the developers don't take this to heart if they see it though. Thank you for all your hard work I just hated it
_childDocuments_.name: Gunbrella

_childDocuments_.review: Great game i had a lot of fun with the combat although being somewhat basic, you only get essentially different ammo types the farther you go through the story. i started to feel the lack of real options late in the game(like 7 hours in) since you usually just spam all the new ammo at bosses since its limited and the shotgun is just so strong that you don't need any other ammo type for the non bosses except for specific things it cant reach. The story for the most part was surprisingly good and did things i like. (i cant go into detail without spoilers)7.5/10 i had a lot of fun.Things i wish they added/improved on would be more upgrades like shotgun range or parasol attachment (part you jump around with) upgrades like increasing stun , speed of dash, added damage on hits and reflected bullets for example. i think that would give the player more options on how they would like to play the game, instead of being stuck using just the different ammo types the game gives you and would keep the game fresh on multiple playthroughs.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunbrella

_childDocuments_.review: 100% worth, the schmoovement is off the charts and overall the game rocks. Dialogue, combat leaves a smidge to be desired (alt ammo felt underpowered) its still really fun and satisfying. i actually felt the need to 100% achievements cuz its just fun to play. but yea like solid 8.5/10 at the very least like bare minimum 8.5
_childDocuments_.name: Gunbrella

_childDocuments_.review: It's impressive that by the end of this adventure the actual gunbrella weapon feels as iconic and memorable as it does. With its unique movement mechanics I had a blast making my way through this steampunk x occult setting.Visually I would honestly call the game a looker. it's a lot of muted colors but the art team was able to provide a real unique style to a game that at a glance looks rather familiar. I was really impressed every time I entered a new area.The narrative unfortunately while super compelling at times, is a little mixed overall. I really liked the amount of character work and lore that went into the setting, but parts of its supernatural plotline kind of fall flat. Its main villain also kind of drops the ball in the end with a final boss that felt like kind of a let down.Even with its woes I really do think Devolver Digital showcased another winner here. I hope Studio Doinksoft bring us back to this world in a sequel. I only see room for improvement if there is one.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunbrella

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10 game, get it on sale.This game wants to be a metroidvania LITE, but it borders between lite and almost hard.Has everything going for it, from the really neat mechanics, ideas, weapons and such, but dosent use almost ANY of its potential, until its way too late, which is a shame!When the game shines, it shines HARD, but when it dosent, you just see sparkles aaand its gone.The best thing I can say about it, it is unique and I hope there will be a sequel, which should just be a straight up metroidvania or a completely linear platformer, cause this sits in the middle of both, but very uncomfortably.Im recommending it because its not bad, I just wish it it knew what it was

_childDocuments_.name: Gunbrella

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic. That's the best word to describe Gunbrella. Engaging character writing, satisfying gameplay in all aspects; movement, combat, platforming, and level design, and a genuinely intriguing world and story. Play the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game. Absolute ♥♥♥♥ ton of content, insane levels of polish, and a beautiful art style (once you turn off the horrible film grain). The vision for this game is excellent, yet the execution of it is truly exceptional. This is an S-tier indie game, possessing the passion and creativity of the indie scene and the technical skill, experience, and budget of game studios to elevate the experience to a level that only publishers like Devolver, Supergiant, and Deck13 create. This is in the same eschelon of quality as arguably masterpieces like Hollow Knight, Celeste, Hades, Dead Cells, and Cultic. If you told me this was your favorite game of all time, I would immediately know that you have good taste.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunbrella

_childDocuments_.review: Not a bad game but the main story wasn't fleshed out enough for me. The mechanics are decent but I found the controls for movement a little clunky. The art style I can appreciate but just not my personal taste. The boss fights were a bit disappointing as once you'd upgraded the gun then you could just tank the bosses even on hard mode. The devs should still be proud of the game its just a bit forgetful for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunbrella

_childDocuments_.review: Fun, enjoy the movement of character a lot. Although, there could be more enemies to make the fight more hectic. Usually, I just leisurely walked past many maps in this game after I killed two enemies in one screen. A lot of choices and sidequests that affect which characters will appear and influence the flow of the story. However, seems like the story still ended up at the same place which is fine by me.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunbrella

_childDocuments_.review: 6.5/10I played the demo and was super excited to pick up the full game. Just rolled credits. There's plenty to love here. The audio and visual design is great. Pixel art is fun and pretty. Looks way better once you turn film grain off (barf). Great mechanics, but it was way more text and RPG heavy than I expected or wanted. It was like 30% cool platforming and shooting and 70% mashing through walls of super uninteresting text. If that ratio was reversed, could've been a way higher rated game for me. Great ending though. I recommend the game still, but if you hate RPG's and are looking for a more just shoot and go type game, look elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.name: Gunbrella

_childDocuments_.review: Loved every minute of this game, characters felt really good, the platforming and combat felt really nice, story was interesting and fun to see where it went, but I just can't shake this constant feeling of just questioning what was missing from it, this game does so much right and I can't praise it enough for that, but I have been just stumped on what is specifically missing from this to be a 10/10, my entire playthrough I had this same thought in the back of my head like something was just missing but I couldn't pin it down for the life of me. _childDocuments_.name: Gunbrella

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game from a small dev team. The art style and soundtrack create a great atmosphere. The gameplay and movement are satisfying. Level design is pretty straightforward but there are plenty of items scattered across the levels. There are some health and weapon upgrades that aren't hard to get as well. The only issue is no new game+ and boss fight difficulty. While enemies' attack rate is increased on the higher difficulty, most of the bosses have easy attack patterns and often can be stunlocked. The final boss can be easily killed by stacking multiple sticky bombs and activating all the mines at once. The game is really enjoyable and it's worth buying if You're not looking for challenging boss fights.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunbrella

_childDocuments_.review: This game first caught my eye at PAX 2022, i saw a big sign with "Gunbrella" at the Devolver stall. I waited 20-30mins in line just to give it a try, I even got a pin.SInce then i had been counting down the day till the release, every time i looked at the pin i'd go and check the steam page.Now over a year later I've finished it and boy what a fun time!To be fair and critique the game, perhaps this being my own fault, but with some of the weaponry types available it was rather easy to defeat some bosses. Those stickymines particularly. Otherwise, with the basic shotgun ammo it was so fun. It felt powerful blasting some enemies down in one shot. The manoeuvrability offered by the Brella makes combat exciting!TL;DR I waited so long for this release and it did not dissapoint, i could barely pull myself away from it. Fun Combat, interesting setting. Only complaint is that it wasn't longer!
_childDocuments_.name: Gunbrella

_childDocuments_.review: The closest comparison i can make to this game is hollow knightThe major exceptions being that you start with all of your movement abilities, it's game-play and story is way more linear, and they say "♥♥♥♥".Having all the movement abilities at the start felt awesome to just ♥♥♥♥ around with. The games setting, story, characters, occurrences, and enemies felt grounded in its world with nothing feeling really out there(in a good way). I think the one part of the game that could have been better is the bosses. Most feel like just another bad guy of the week type guys that don't feel that memorable.8/10, game good, maybe not for all, but i like.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunbrella

_childDocuments_.review: A solid platformer with satisfying gunplay and a fun way to fly around and deflect bullets. The setting is an eldrich steampunk world that's strongly atmospheric. The dialogue and story have real heart and lots of personality with some great characters and really clever humor. The game feels, looks and sounds fantastic, with lots of polish and detail. I beat the game on Hard on my first playthrough and found it pretty challenging while learning the ropes.Do yourself a favor and ditch the controller's face buttons for jumping and shooting once you get the hang of playing. These are training wheels for the sake of convention, I think. You can play much better with your right thumb always on the right stick, using the (already mapped) shoulder buttons and triggers to jump and shoot, along with opening the gunbrella to block directionally.You can really steamroll bosses especially in the mid-late game just by laying in with the DPS-- it'd be great if they got the bosses to force you out of your attack patterns more. The train boss was my favorite though :)
_childDocuments_.name: Gunbrella

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like this game needs more attention. It's not very challenging, but honestly it feels refreshing and just wants you to have fun. I think it does that very well. It has a hard mode if you feel like it's too easy (I played on normal).Game length is a little on the shorter side, but I think it's just right for me.I'd say give it a try. I've been getting bored with similar 2D exploration games and this hooked me.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunbrella

_childDocuments_.review: YOU are sleeping on this game! It's amazing! Tight movement, engaging combat, actually fun side quests, challenging bosses, excellent atmosphere and world building, deep and intricate story, this game has it ALL! My only complaint is that it's so short! I would totally be up for a sequel or DLC campaign! 10/10 worth your money and time!
_childDocuments_.name: Gunbrella

_childDocuments_.review: Great game with engaging (albeit easy) combat loop, and fantastic movement. Could use some better sound design, especially during boss fights, and some voice acting would be cool, but overall doesn't hinder the game by too much.Weapon balancing could be important, as a number of bosses can be defeated quite easily, even with the base weapon. The flamethrower makes fighting bosses even more of a breeze, but I understand I could use less powerful weaponry to increase the difficulty.Also, the auto-save could be seen as a bit intrusive due to the nature of some of these achievements, but since it appears not too many rely on the late-game, I imagine it wouldn't be to much of a hassle to get them.Regardless, overall great art direction and design, killer soundtrack, fun movement, and a good story. Could use improvements regarding sound enhancements, mainly during boss fights, as well as some tweaks regarding weapon balance and auto-saving. Would recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Gunbrella

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, a great game, but it could use it's potential in much bigger ways. The umbrella platforming and gunplay felt soooo smooth I really wished there were some challenging levels, but alas sadly game never really pushed them hard. Which is also at the same time a plus I suppose? It feels pretty relaxing to play it and very nice overall, but there's just little to no challenge time to time. That isn't to say however that I didn't enjoy, in fact I really enjoyed it and I hope to see a DLC of sorts.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunbrella

_childDocuments_.review: This game rules. The graphic style is fantastic, the audio is great, the writing is really well done (especially the humor), and it is all bundled up in an intriguing and fleshed-out world. There are several different choices you can make, and each decision has almost immediate consequences - none of that "illusion of choice" ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that AAA studios are notorious for.The controls are tight, and while the umbrella mechanics might seem a little unwieldy at first, you will be wall-jumping and performing ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥' kills in no time. Despite the cutesy graphics, this game is unapologetic in it's brutality. That said, it isn't gratuitous. Like, it's not hardcore just for hardcore's sake. It's real enough in it's tragedy to convincingly depict a world in dire straits.I'm not sure how far along I am, but I think I'm almost done, and based on what I've seen I would recommend this game to anyone who enjoys action platformers.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunbrella

_childDocuments_.review: I was really looking forward to this game, ever since playing the demo late last year. I'd played Gato Roboto (the deb's previous metroidvania masterpiece) and absolutely loved it. I'm so happy that, so far, Gunbrella has not disappointed one bit.• Tight controls.• Traversal feels great and fluid, especially since you have access to wall climbing / jumping as well as both your gunbrella™ dash and float/glide.• Beautiful presentation and music.• Crisp audio design.• FUN gameplay loop of exploring, shooting, looting, gunbrella™-tooting action and exploration.• Gunplay feels good and there's enough variety in ammo types / movement options to keep it fast paced and fluid.• Plot (which I don't normally care about in games like these) is actually decent.• Characters are funny and well-written. World actually feels lived in.Seriously, this game just oozes style and atmosphere in every frame - everything from the menus down to the minor environmental background details. It is so incredibly fun to play and control, and it doesn't have that overly 'videogame-y' feel a lot of games have nowadays.If you are in any way a fan of metroidvania style games or just 2D action-adventure games in general, please do not sleep on this gem.You can really see all the love, care, and effort the devs have put into this game. I've had my game paused just so I could write this review as I really don't think this game is getting the attention it deserves (yet).To doinksoft: thank you. Seriously.P. S. works great on Steam Deck - even smoother with Steam Input disabled and using a controller.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunbrella

_childDocuments_.review: The game was alright, the movement was smooth, the combat was enjoyable and the story wasn't bad I enjoyed it. The bosses attacks were very easy to predict and you could kill them all with just the shotty rounds if you really wanted to (I really had no need to use any other type of ammo). Last thing I'll add is that the art was pretty cool!
_childDocuments_.name: Gunbrella

_childDocuments_.review: The story is really good, the combat is easy but satisfying same with the movement system. My main problem is the bosses every boss has somewhat of an easy learning curve when it comes to learning their attacks and some even had exploitive learning curves, also the ammo types should definitely be more effective the sticky bomb and grenade are good but I find myself just using the normal shells when fighting I dont ever find a need to use anything else, other then that it was a really fun game and again the story was really good I enjoyed it.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunbrella

_childDocuments_.review: Get out your Gunbrella because it's gonna be raining blood!! pros:gameplay, movement, controlsthe story, the world, the characters, and their quirky gibberish voicesthe soundtrack that feels at times inspired by my personal favourite video game soundtrack, LISAmuch of the game feels very inspired by Celestealthough also has much of its own individuality and originallittle things, like the way you bleed when you have 1 heart left or the gato roboto referencescons:not populated with enough enemies,takes awhile to get started (become challenging, ex; enemies are often looking away from where I'm headed)no brightness control setting combustibles are very cool, but tend to have little practical use in most situationsbarter system has no way of selecting multiple items to sell or buy making it a hassle to pawn each individual itemits on the short side I've been following this game since its announcement and I really think they delivered. A lot of people say Celeste with guns, but I think this gives the false impression that you'll be faced with Celeste's gameplay of timed obstacles or puzzles - you won't. It's Celeste with combat in lieu of these things, while wearing a similar coat of stylization, but also shares its fluid dynamic controls. When you have a game where the movement flows the exact way you want it to, where you can use force to propel yourself towards precisely the action you aim for, that is exceptional design and what made Celeste so fun, and the developers deserve credit for capturing that feeling with Gunbrella. It is a LOT of fun to play. However, it would have been nice to see more creative ways to use the unique idea of the gunbrella's mechanics and sense of acceleration with more interesting level design to make the most of that feeling. But overall, there's a lot to love about this one and I do strongly recommend it.8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Gunbrella

_childDocuments_.review: Gunbrella is a really great action platformer. It has a cool world, the mechanics are smooth and satisfying, and the story has me intrigued so far. Some difficulty balance feels a bit off here and there though. I had a boss that I stun-locked, completely trivializing the encounter while other areas had checkpoints so spread out I thought I was missing one. Overall though the game is excellent and I definitely recommend it at the current price point but if you're at all interested and it is on sale its an easy rec for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunbrella

_childDocuments_.review: The core mechanic is a really good one–the gunbrella is unique, fun to use, and created very well. However it could have been greatly expanded upon with some more in-depth level design. With how floaty yet precise the gunbrella is, I wish there were more open, tougher platforming sections. I think that where this game really excels is in its atmosphere. The art is beautifully executed. As for the music, there were no real standout tracks that I can remember, but it did do a great job of enhancing the atmosphere which is what it’s supposed to do so there’s really nothing to complain about there. The story is very solid, although the ending felt a bit abrupt or anti-climactic. Overall, it was fun to watch the plot unfold and witness all the twists and turns, because there are a couple that I just wasn’t expecting.	One of this game’s biggest shortcomings is that there is too much content. There are so many ammo types, but I rarely found myself using them aside from the time when you’re forced to at the start of the game and in the very final boss. The main reasons for this, I think, are that it is way too inconvenient to switch mid-combat, the maximum amount of ammo is very small, and the base shotgun weapon is just better in all situations. When switching ammo types, you have to move your thumb off of the left-stick to the d-pad, which is just not a great idea when there are enemies jumping you from all directions (Keep in mind that I played on controller, this might be a non-issue on keyboard but I’m not sure). A possible, and simple, solution to this problem is just to pause the gameplay when you’re scrolling through your ammo. Since the amount of ammo you have is limited, there is a feeling of scarcity and wanting to save it until you really need it, leading to the player just… never using it. There is also the fact that the default shotgun is just a very good weapon and better than the others in many ways, especially when upgraded. 	Speaking of upgrades, the final ones are way too expensive and are just unrealistic to achieve in a normal playthrough. It takes so much of the specific currency, to the point where it is not feasible to fully upgrade the gunbrella. By the time you’ve finished grinding out cogs to fully upgrade the gunbrella, you could have just beaten the game. To mitigate this issue, I think a possible solution is to significantly decrease the cost of upgrading, but make the enemies have more health. As it stands, the only reason to fully upgrade the gunbrella is to get the achievement. (I recognize that the devs probably aren’t going to implement my “solutions”, but I still want to put them here just ‘cause.)As someone who loves speedrunning, I wish it capitalized on the true potential this game has for it by adding things like an in-game timer, the option to skip cutscenes or speed up dialogue, etc.	Overall, this is a well-crafted game with many cool ideas, but ultimately falls short on using them to their full potential. I know this review focuses primarily on what I wish was different, but this was a fun and unforgettable experience of a game. I would heavily recommend this game to anyone, especially if you’re into games like Celeste and Katana ZERO.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game with well designed pixel art, funny dialog, fun movement, and a soundtrack fitting a noir mood.Pixel art visuals are a dime a dozen today, and not every release is artistically of the same caliber as another. Gunbrella’s art style is certainly in the higher-quality camp. The color palette is deliberate in presenting a somber setting. Everything is broken and dimly lit, water is a puke-like green, and grey metals and machinery are scattered throughout a junkyard serving as a home to NPCs.Some characters the player encounters are written with funny dialog, not just in the writing itself, but also the moments of silence between one text bubble to the next (regardless of how the player advances the dialog) — or the moments of the opposite. For instance, there are two NPCs in a particular conversation where one is interrupting the other. Considering the game's voiceovers are brief grunts of gibberish, the exchange and delivery between those characters are done in a charming manner.Gunbrella’s locomotion is forgiving and meant to provide fun before any challenge. The gunbrella itself is integral to combat as well as traversing through the game world and platforming segments — in such a way that, whenever it is taken away from the player, the game’s pace noticeably slows down.The gunbrella serves as a dash, double-jump, shield, and projectile parry in combat. Players have the ability to move and aim independently with an arsenal of ammo types of various uses. Switching between each type during battle is not intuitive. There is no weapon wheel to pause or slow down time while switching. Rather, the different ammo types can be scrolled through in a predetermined order. The second option is to pause and go into the inventory menu, which completely halts the game’s momentum. Furthermore, even on hard difficulty, most of the ammo types are not essential to the combat or any other gameplay, and it is in this sense that Gunbrella’s economy is superfluous.

_childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly more deep and well-crafted than what I was originally expecting.The story was a lot more engaging than I was originally expecting it to be. There are lots of fun and lovable characters as well.In my opinion, the bosses fell short towards the later half of the game, but their overall visual design made up for it.I wish there were more areas to explore as well, but the ones that were presented were very well done in terms of lore, and each locale felt very unique to traverse. _childDocuments_.name: Gunbrella

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, Gunbrella is a good game. 100%'ing the game took three playthroughs for me, although I think I could've technically done it in two and a half. The first playtrough was by far the most enjoyable. I liked exploring the different areas, doing the sidequests and upgrading various things. The second and third playthrough were much faster however, because I just focused on doing the main quest. All things considered, if you just focus on the story, this game can be beaten pretty easily in like 2 - 3  hours. I would not necessarily say that it is worth it to 100% the game, as I didn't really feel that I got much of an award, and it became a little bit of a drag at the end.The best thing about Gunbrella is, you guessed it, the Gunbrella. It allows for very fun, fast and satisfying movement and I can see this game becoming quite popular as a speed-game. If you get the movement down you can blast through areas really quickly,If I were to critique something it would be some of the character models. Although I am a fan of pixel art I found some of the characters grotesque, and quite ugly.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunbrella

_childDocuments_.review: Short and Sweet! The game feels great to play until the end and Gliding, dashing with your gunbrella never gets old. The game is not a metroidvania, so probably not for people who love exploration as it is fairly linear and straightforward.However the ending left be a bit unsatisfied, as it felt all the build up let to very anti climatic ending.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunbrella

_childDocuments_.review: The key positive for this game is that the movement is sick and lets you schmove around the levels and enemies in really fun ways. You have so much aerial mobility that you get to have a lot of moments where the game gives you a helping hand to the next platform and you just zoom right by it, which feels good.The downsides for this game are that it's short, there are enough bugs that you'll likely see a handful in your own playthrough, and the the story is just fine. The jokes are pretty funny, but the main plot is meh. The upside to the downsides is that the game is aware of its small scope and it works well as a tightly designed package to play over a couple sittings. Despite the flaws I'd still recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Played without issues on 512 steam deck. It’s a lukewarm recommendation. Gameplay is good, has difficulty options, nice sound effects. I appreciate stories in games like god of war, the last of us etc but this bite size gem is lackluster because of it. _childDocuments_.review: No doubt one of the best-feeling 2D platformers ever made. The movement is fluid and extremely rewarding to master, and the way it works into the combat makes it somehow even more satisfying than normal to blast enemies in the face with a shotgun. The story hooks you fast and turns out to be an absolute roller coaster, with very heavy themes and story beats that had me genuinely in tears after all was said and done. And all that isn't even to mention the fantastic visuals, immaculate music and sound design, and everything else that went into this unforgettable experience.Doinksoft's best work by a mile, and one of the best games Devolver has ever published. Even when 2023 has been stacked full of incredible games, Gunbrella still manages to stick out to me as one of the year's best.

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10, solid action platformer with a few flaws.Throughout, the gameplay is great. Controls are tight and work just fine on a mouse and keyboard, easy to learn and tough to master. The game's difficulty curve is overall solid, but can waver at points. A few bosses are a little *too* vulnerable to being burst down to 0 health with an all-out attack. Still, with regards to the gameplay I have no complaints.I do have some points of criticism with the story. The game takes itself very seriously, and also wants to have replayability value. In service of this, at several points in the story you are offered choices which can influence the fate of certain characters. But, oftentimes there's a right and a wrong choice, and its easy to make the "wrong" choice by accident, presumably to encourage replaying the game. This culminates in the ending - the game has a "good" ending which rotates on a decision you make less than a third of the way through the game. The decision seems perfectly calibrated so that a player who's paying attention would never ever get it without using a guide, while a careless player might manage it accidentally. This is my biggest complaint against the game. Replayability value just doesn't hit the same when it feels forced, and it does here.Overall, however, this game is a perfectly good way to burn 6-10 hours on a weekend. If you're looking for a solid action platformer, this is an excellent pick.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good. The game part is fun. The art is gorgeous. The atmosphere, sound and music are great. It's an overall job well done and in the end I would still recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun game! Movement is great, there's a good mix between gameplay moments and story moments (though I would have liked longer/deeper exploration/dungeons). Lots of cool ideas!I had to switch my keyboard to qwerty since I couldn't change the keybinds, and there are a few small questionnable level design choices. I still had a blast playing this game though.Probably a bit short for its price (I finished the game in 5 hours), but there seem to be different routes depending on the choices you make, so replayability is there.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunbrella

_childDocuments_.review: Gunbrella is great! It has interesting characters, visceral combat, a solid visual aesthetic... but to be honest. That's not really the reason to play it. Ya see, the umbrella part of the portmanteau does most of the heavy lifting here. The movement just rules! Gracefully jetting around corners to stun lizard dogs, floating down long corridors to flip a switch, and flinging yourself off a zip line into a cultist so you can watch them explode with a single KO shot - beautiful. I love it. There's also plenty of moments where the title is lacking. For example, why would you even give me alternate ammo types when shotgun shells always work best? Character's stories can be weirdly paced (Oli seemed to pop up at the most random moments), out of character for the protagonist (why did we have to kill that endangered dog?!), and sometimes don't resolve at all! (The Mayor just leaves town I guess?) And towards the very end game, if you've upgraded everything like I did, things just get SOOOOOOO easy. Like too easy.  But all in all, I really enjoyed my time with Gunbrella. And if you're looking for a fast paced action platformer with style - go for it!

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible game. Some of the most fun movement and combat mechanics I've ever experienced in a 2d platformer - which I expected after Gato Roboto. _childDocuments_.review:
Gunbrella is a noir-punk action-adventure set in a world dependent on a rapidly diminishing natural resource.

Players take the role of a gruff woodsman on a quest for revenge, armed with the mysterious Gunbrella: a firearm that doubles as an umbrella. His investigation becomes entangled with the inner workings of ghouls and gangsters, cops and cutlists, and the fallout of corporate exploitation.

name: Lost Eidolons
detailed_description: The land of Benerio was once a shining kingdom by the sea. Then an iron-fisted conqueror, Ludivictus, set the world on fire and redrew the maps. Now Benerio is one downtrodden province in a crumbling Empire where the only true master is corruption. Enter Eden, a charming mercenary captain forced to become a rebel commander when his village is thrust headfirst into war. Now Eden must rally his allies and stand tall against an imperial army, fearsome monsters, and enemies within. MASTER THE GRID Strategically station your soldiers in every battle to take advantage of their class and magic skills. Master the battlefield and seize victory in challenging grid-based combat scenarios. WIELD THE ELEMENTS Lay siege to towering castles, overtake cunning bosses with unique abilities and take on hulking monsters that will force you to change up your tactics, or become their next meal. BOND WITH ALLIES Leading a rebellion isn't just about winning battles. You'll also have to build your camp, convince people to join, get to know their stories, and help them navigate the highs and lows of revolution. CUSTOMIZE YOUR SQUAD Recruit and train the perfect fighting force, with over 20 playable characters and 10 classes to choose from. Equip and train your allies to unlock new skills, spells, and passive abilities. Pit your mighty squad against entire armies and rise triumphant. RELIVE YOUR GREATEST BATTLES Win the war all over again, with a rich NEW GAME+ mode. Carry over your choice of stats and items, then recruit new allies, try new strategies, and experiment with different difficulty levels.

Its a good enough experience gameplay wise to make you a bit invested in the characters, which only amplifies how bad the story is.I love tactics games and this hits alot of good notes, but then it just sort of ends. _childDocuments_.review: I want to like this game. I really, really do. The parts of the game where you're on the battlefield is great. It runs real well, the tactics are good, the animations for the combat are nice, and i even like how when you zoom in on the combat that there are more people fighting in the background behind the characters that are fighting each other.If this game was mostly focused around that part of the game then i wouldn't be leaving this negative review. But as it is, i can't recommend it because about 75% of the gameplay revolves around running around camp and doing boring, mundane, stupid crap.Look, I DO want to manage my people's equipment, have conversations and character banter and set up their training for certain classes. What i don't want to do however, is help someone find their lost book, or run over to the vendors and buy "supplies" that are only there specifically for a quest to just take them to some other random person so that they can be distributed to "the local people" and try to build rapport with random people that are just kinda hanging out at my MILITARY camp before i can recruit them. Seriously, what the hell are these people doing in my camp? They shouldn't be allowed in unless they are with us, how do we know they aren't imperial spies?I tried to power through the horrible and mundane camp quest stuff to get to the good part of the game but even then you're still getting halted at every turn. Like i said before, i like character banter and will even stick around games i hate the gameplay for if it's got a good enough story. But boy oh boy does this game like to talk about nothing! You get on the battlefield and characters will bring up something that should be obvious and they will sit there and talk, and talk, and talk some more, not really saying anything at all. Then it'll say your turn starts but NOPE! We need to talk some MORE! The characters will do a pointless swing animation and say one line, then go back to the battlefield only to show them do ANOTHER pointless swing animation to say one MORE line and they'll do this like 4-5 times in a ROW. OMG Shut up and let me play the freaking game already!Once i get to actually play the battlefield i genuinely have a good deal of fun but the moment i show back up in my tent at the camp, all of my enthusiasm just DRAINS. Great, how many pointless tasks do i gotta go do now?I'm not sad feeling like i wasted money on this game. I really like how the developers seem enthusiastic and willing to take feedback and improve and i want to support them. I look forward to seeing what they make next and if they learned from their mistakes they made in this game. There is some really awesome stuff in here, it's just too much trouble to dig and get to it right now and if the developers truly learn and grow and take the feedback to heart like i think and feel like they are, then i've no doubt that their next game will be great.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Eidolons

_childDocuments_.review: I dont typically like turn based games but this one is pretty good.Likes-turn based combat doesnt take forever to get engaged-plenty of character interaction outside of combat-story is easy to follow and engaging-fights are visually appealingDislikes-Some cut scenes tend to drag on a little too long-camera movement in turn based mode is a little clunky but not too much of a concern-not too much variety in attack methods, its the same every timeMiddle ground-not a graphic masterpiece overall, but i think that adds to its charm in keeping things simple.All in all, these are just my own opinions and i think its a good game.

_childDocuments_.review: This one was tough for me. This game has an awful lot going for it, but the few glaring things I don't like make me wish I had gone with a different game instead. Overall I will give the studio another shot on their next title because for a first game it is very polished, bug free and had some great ideas. I just can't recommend THIS one at it's price. Pros-The Voice Acting is fantastic. There are some recognizable VAs in there. Nobody felt very out of place or lacking.-SOME Characters are generally likable-The Story had SOME interesting moments-The Combat system for the most part passes as engaging, though it is pretty simple. Cons- Your Main Character is some sort of chosen one (because of course he is), but is not really explained why unless it is buried in non-voice acted conversations. The "Ultimate" Ability he gets is very rarely impactful, except in cutscenes when the story needs it to be. He murders entire armies with this ability in a cutscene just to have it do less damage than a normal spell in a battle. - The Chapters are just BLOATED with monotony. You do the same fetch quests in the camp between missions, and the exact same optional battles. I wish the game had honestly been about 5 battles shorter because it just gets repetitive. -There are maybe half a dozen battles where the idea is to just escape the main antagonist, and this is after you easily murder his Army several times but just more troops keep spawning. There is no real sense of danger...just your party running away which gets very repetitive.-You fight and defeat the SAME named enemies MANY times. I don't like the trope in this type of game where your units surround the boss, beat him to 0 HP just to have them somehow get away MULTIPLE times. It gets very stale, and loses all tension and immersion when fighting them because you know you'll just have to beat them again. - ****SEMI SPOILER**** The last fight.....God I hate this fight. It is ANOTHER fight where you spend most of it either chasing or running. You easily smash the antagonists Army yet again....but then when you get to him *****SPOILER*****....He just keeps respawning and healing, and doing BS one-shot mechanics and becomes immune. He takes like 5 damage from your same characters that have felt OP the entire game. Then he heals for 10 while your party takes 50 damage. I don't mind a hard fight, at all, but to just drop a bunch of random BS mechanics unlike ANYTHING else you've faced in the game up to that point just feels cheesy. Certain "Master" Classes are just not good in the fight whatsoever and its better to just cheese him down with 4 range sharpshooters. It wasn't fun, felt forced, nothing in the game prepares you for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Eidolons

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly mediocre. Game mechanics are shallow and not fleshed out. For every strength this game has it has a comparable weakness and then some. The quality of dialogue is not good enough for a game that features so much of it. The voice acting is actually passable however. The game also wears out its welcome. I completed it at about 51 hours but it would've been best if it ended at 30, most of the missions are just the same thing, different location on the map. What really sealed my negative opinion was the final battle. The final battle has a game breaking boss that requires ridiculous strategy and goes against what the game was leading up to it. I thought this game was passable at first, but all things considered there are much better turn-based strategy games, or just games in general, that more worth your time and money.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Eidolons

_childDocuments_.review: This... might be one of my favourite games this year.It's quite endearing, really. Indeed, they fall into the shortcomings of, say, Fire Emblem Three Houses. Time skips and character motivations that feels rushed, and personally, I can understand why. It is very impressive what they could do with just $50 000~ as their budget. This game has heart, and the devs are clearly passionate about it. Sure, it lacks the depth of those AAA games, but man, if this is what they made with just $50 000(!), I couldn't possibly imagine what they could do with the budget of Solasta. Or, Divinity. Story :Quite simple. You play as Eden, a mercenary before falling down the rabbit hole and fights for a rebellion against the tyrannical rulers of Artemesia. That's it.As said above, I have gripes with time skips and the lack of certain major characters' motivations. And many other... recruitables lack characterisation as well, which I can let slide. However, some of these major characters are very endearing in their own rights, and honestly they were one of the main reasons I stuck with the game.Faults aside, the main story is also... pretty neat. Of course, if you're not a fan of theses kinds of narrative and gameplay then, I guess it is what it is. Animation & Artstyle :It's understandable for them to use basic, clunky animations during conversations. However, I think it came to the game presentation's detriment. It would've perhaps benefited with something akin to Hades' sprites. It's clear to me that they aren't exactly short in those kinds of things, given how the painted narrated slides look dang good.Combat :This part is also simple, at least, in face value. Now, I've just recently finished the game on the hardest difficulty, Maniac, and managed to do not lose any allies(The Unvanquished achievement). It felt as if these fights were meticulously crafted, which to my understanding were about 27 main fights, and it isn't quite as many, of course, given their budget.But as such, the fights felt compelling, enemies' strategies and surprises often hinted at by characters. I've seen a couple of reviewers calling the dialogue boring and enemies popping out of nowhere, but I guess they just have a relatively short attention span. And having played it in the most ballbusting manner, I'll say that all fights are winnable unless you whine like a brat.Another layer of depth they have are the class systems. God I wish they had more. More skills, more things to kill. Speaking of.Gameplay Loop :I wish there were more side-battles. I mean, it would definitely defeat the purpose and allow us to farm exp, but hey, more content wouldn't hurt. Regardless, it's a simple loop. Chapter starts, you roam the camp, talk to people, fight ensues, post-fight camp roam again. If it were simply just fights, it would be shallow, and the 'free-roam' part actually gives the game a bit more depth.Voice Acting :It's pretty good at some parts. It varies high-highs and low-lows. Main characters sound great, you might've heard of them if you've played Fire Emblem. Again, I'll use this card repeatedly: $50 000 budget. And these stuff feels and are presented better than those with 5x the budget(cough Solasta)Music :No comment. Conclusion :What can I say? I'm just surprised. It's not the best or whatever. But for what it is, it's dang great. I enjoyed this much more than Elden Ring, or any huge recent games that came out this year. I've gotten my ahh handed to me here, but I enjoyed every moment of it.Also, its Balastar, not Baltastar :)--Edit : Hey devs, Sky's Edge's weapon skill can be refreshed by swapping the weapon. Might want to look into that.That, and Sera's achievement is bugged, where it gives you Marchelle's instead.--Edit 2 : I might be the only one to think this way, but I'd prefer a more conclusive and defined ending than a vague slideshow... but regardless! I'll be keeping an eye on what y'all make!

_childDocuments_.review: This game has been a ton of fun that I would highly recommend except for a single point of contention that ruins my ability to suggest this game to my friends.I love the interactions with the npc's and the camp followers: it really makes the experience very immersive. There are a bunch of class options that you spec into though i wish there were slightly more efficient ways of raising talents that would allow me to raise the various skills so I could try the other ones for the various characters; but this is a minor nit pick. There's a good variety of main mission types and unique ways of fighting monsters that really help differentiate gameplay; the "bonus" missions are usually very generic but they're just extra content for grinding so i'm not too miffed. The ability to redo turns is a wonderful option as the, while you can see the anticipated enemy attack vectors, the  enemy can suddenly gang up on units or suddenly spawn a huge enemy force led by a hero.... further explanation of why this is redo worthy below.Now, the negative that stops me from recommending this game: enemy hero buffs. A major mechanic for the game is when an enemy hero has an allied non-hero soldier within 5-6 tiles next to it, the E hero takes roughly 90% less damage from attacks. In order to get rid of this buff, all non-hero soldiers must be eliminated. Now the issue with this mechanic is that this ability doesn't just affect the commander of the army but ALL characters in the enemy's forces. There are battles with 6+ enemy heroes with dozens of troops scatter between and behind the enemy lines protecting them from damage. Being forced to "ignore" or  skirt around the powerful enemy heroes to kill a single generic soldier can take turns to accomplish, especially if the hero is a choke-point and blocking off easy access to enemy soldier. This problem is worsened by the fact the enemy heroes aren't passive, they will aggressively hunt down your soldiers and make good use of their screening soldiers to render them near immortal. While this isn't necessarily game changing, some missions (especially later on) will force you to preform this dance while weathering blows from half a dozen heroes while you spend a handful of turns trying to skirt around them while ensuring your own units aren't being torn apart. this is especially frustrating with enemy mages and archers who will pick off your vulnerable back lines units with impunity since you can't interrupt them without special abilities; though, this means your delaying your troops from hunting down the generic soldiers. I love tactical rpgs like fire emblem and this has really scratched that itch in an extremely pleasing way! However, the enemy hero - protection mechanic has soured my opinion on recommending this to any of my friends, I wouldn't wish for them to experience the frustration I have while playing this game as it seems to just be designed to waste your time.

_childDocuments_.review: Lost Eidolons is a double-A attempt at a more traditional fantasy version of Fire Emblem: Three Houses. If you've played that game, many of the mechanics both in and outside of battle will be familiar to you.What I liked: - gameplay is strategic, fun, and the undo function makes it quite forgiving.- In game models are high quality and cutscenes occasionally utilize paintings which are beautifully done. - Voice acting is full of well-known talent who elevate the material. - Writing itself is a bit shaky at times but serviceable and engaging if you're willing to meet it on its own terms.- A unique take on the weapon triangle where it matches weapon types against armor typesWhat I disliked: - Animations often feel stiff, voice acting is not lip synced, and most cutscenes feature static posed models which pop awkwardly in and out. This is clearly a budgetary limitation, but it gives the impression of one of those bottom of the barrel steam greenlight projects and isn't on the level of the rest of the game.- Assets are re-used a lot. There are very few unique body models (tho plenty of unique heads), and you'll see the same costumes with no variation over and over on your own characters and NPCs for most of the game.Overall:I like this game more than I thought I would. It's nice to see someone else attempt the modern Fire Emblem style of game, and this is a competent attempt at it. Worth playing if you enjoy turn-based Strategy RPGs and are able to look past the places where budget limitations are more obvious.

_childDocuments_.review: *sigh* So....starting this game will give you completely the wrong opinion of what is truly a quality piece of gaming. It's unfortunate that silly errors at the start have this effect because many will be missing out on a great experience. In fact, the first time I bought Lost Eidolons I instantly refunded it because having an xbox controller connected made the cursor disappear and even setup menus glitched beyond usability. I bought it again and discovered that unplugging it stopped this but this silly issue really doesn't set the stage for what is to come.In addition, the early sections of the game are lacking voice-overs that are more prominent in the rest of the game thus giving the initial opinion that the whole thing is janky - which it is not. Given just a little more forethought and polish would have turned a very good game into a truly great one and it is a real pity that this wasn't the case.If you can force yourself to not throw the baby out with the bathwater you will find an excellent and storied turn based strategy underneath. It has a ton of beautiful cut scenes mid and late game that are all fully voiced and a heck of a lot of voice work throughout the game to the extent that it is completely understandable that they had to resort to text only for many conversations. But it's impossible to feel that much of this is "arse backward" with some important things being unvoiced and many far less important things being voiced. They just got the balance wrong.Gameplay is varied and interesting particularly character progression. The downside is that despite the camp sections appearing to be open world the game remains completely linear but this is not enough of an issue to detract from what, in the end, is an epic journey in an interesting world.I will 100% be buying the forthcoming sequel game.

_childDocuments_.review: [Game dropped after 30h of playtime, shortly before reaching the end. Might pick it up merely for the sake of finishing it.]Update: After trying to beat the 3rd last mission endlessly on Normal, I switched to Story Mode and beat the last 3 missions of the game. The difficulty got laughably easy and there was practically no way any of your units can die in this mode (or toss them one potion and they'll be fine).Granted, the last mission was a major headache, and I wouldn’t wanna try playing that on Normal Mode at all. Kinda glad I saved my time.The storytelling of the game was such a strong selling point, but the ending was quite....hm. It did wrap up the main story, but for some reason it wasn’t really a very satisfying ending, as you get one short cutscene and then it jumps right to 3 power point slides and the character stories' endings. Needless to say, it didn't feel like a roughly 40-50h campagin should end that "abruptly" (again, the story got wrapped up, but it just left me thinking "Wait, that's it?" as there's barely any lead up. And you may get to know the character's endings, but for a game this long, I feel like more dialogue or interactions would’ve been necessary. You're kind of left guessing what happened in the gap between the story ending and the character endings, as those 3 power point slides merely make you "guess" what happened. It may be obvious, but why not write it out???)Honestly, I still wouldn’t recommend the game because of the major difficulty spikes on Normal. The NG+ feature seems somewhat interesting, but I wouldn’t want to play the game again, unless I really want that classical Fire Emblem gameplay itch sated. So granted, the game isn't horrible, nor is it bad, but...well, I wouldn’t rec paying full price either way. Or necessarily playing it.Let me start off by saying I really liked the game until roughly 20h in. I played on Normal with No Permadeath on. I play the game as though permadeath is on, though. I didn't mind the limited turns (you can turn that option off entirely which I didn’t as I do enjoy some difficulty). At first, I also didn't mind the fact that there's this stupidly hard fight against  that takes way too long+ . But there was also another fight where  Whatever. That was still tolerable and not a deal breaker for me. But then there was this other bad design choice of having to (vague spoilers alert, fyi) "disregard" a tactic the game/character tells you to follow because if you try following the advice, you end up losing whatever unit you sent out to follow said advice and possibly lose the fight as well because of BAD DIFFICULTY SPIKES and that's when things started getting less fun for me. And even worse:  You only have a limited amount of rapport time. You focus on building up relationships with some of the characters, but if you want to recruit new people, you nearly don't have any rapport time left. The story was really good up until a certain point, then it just tried too hard to include twists instead of sticking to a solid, "predictable" plot. Imo a predictable plot with no fantasy elements (that kind of come out of nowhere) is better than one where you're just left wondering why or how . A shame, because at first, it stuck to a rather good premise and a solid plot before (points at spoilers). A normal, classical "war sucks" plot would've done it for me just fine tbh??? It's such a shame. I haven't even finished the game yet completely as there are even more bad difficulty spikes as I've heard (I only have so little time and so many games on my backlog), and I really thought the incredible voice acting would save the game for me. The graphics are okay, as static pictures look great, but when it comes to having characters move/talk/interact, it doesn’t look that great anymore. But for me, that's not what makes or breaks a game. Not even MCDs or having to push through some bad difficulty spikes.But if too many cons accumulate at once, and you're not someone who has an incredible amount of free time, you'll find yourself INCREDIBLY more and more frustrated as the game goes on. I was looking extremely forward to the spin off that's been announced as I played through the game. Now, I feel like I've sadly wasted enough money and don't feel like trying my luck out again.All in all, if you stop before you reach the mid point of the story, you might not be left as unsatisfied as I am. And I don't want to disregard the hard work that's flown into this indie game- despite the high price tag, I don't mind getting "mediocre" indie games in general, and I don't dare compare limited budgets to AAA games. There's an incredible amount of work and dedication that was put into this game, and it certainly shows!Sadly, this game fell flat for me as time went on in too many areas (I could list even more things tbh). If it goes on a deep sale (I wouldn’t spend more than $20 tho), maybe give it a try if you want that Fire emblem itch. If not, go finish your backlog first...or play some bad AAA games instead.

_childDocuments_.review: Lost Eidolons (LE) is a solid and enjoyable tactics game with lite RPG & social mechanics. There's a lot here to love, and the elements that fall short for me are quickly being looked at by the developers, who are at the top of their game with addressing and implementing community feedback. When I say I no-lifed this when it came out, I mean it.LE takes inspiration from older tactics games while implementing downtime social activities akin to what we saw in Fire Emblem: Three Houses. There's a lot to love here, and if you're a fan of turn-based tactics games, then this is a no-brainer to pick up. If you're on the fence, please read the notes below about "Downtime activities & Characters", as there is a sizeable amount of downtime in this game, and if that's not your thing, you may be disappointed.  Around 60 hours. I did everything available to me though multiple options, some challenging missions that require more thought. Based on "normal" difficulty. Carry on reading for my completely spoiler-free review:While I gravitate to turn-based grid-style tactics games for the gameplay, having a great story also benefits keeping you griped on the world and characters. LE's story is hit-or-miss. I enjoyed it for what it is. There are some great plot points, great character moments and some threads that they can leverage for some highly engaging DLC in the future. However, as seen in their discord, some users aren't happy with the direction the story takes, the omission of some key plot pieces, and how the characters seem to ignore their existence. This wasn't as big of an issue and didn't detract from the overall experience for me, but if you need everything to be tied up neatly, you may feel a bit let down.The ending to the game may leave a sour taste, as it did with me. It ends rather abruptly; however, I believe the devs are looking into this, so that may change. It wasn't an annoying finish, but rather an "oh, that's it" ending.Combat is what we come for, and it takes centre stage here, with us getting multiple options to take down our foes and support our troops. We field our personal squad on the field, often having our max unit number capped at 10 - which gives sizeable flexibility with how we want to tackle each fight. Unit progression follows a similar suit, again, to Fire Emblem, in that units can progress to the next stage of class. A unit's class progression will depend on their character and "position" in the story. I.e., if you hire someone really into magic, it's likely their stat spread will follow suit. While the game doesn't lock your characters into one particular path (props to the devs), this focus on the "cannon" path is firm. It can be challenging to divert a unit to a completely different path. With these classes come skills to use on the field. LE doesn't limit a weapon's use via durability, but you will have a set number of uses for your skills and magic, forcing you to consider how best to use them during combat. The same can be said about unique skills - skills only available to a particular character - which can create dynamic moments or strategies. At no point during this game did I feel that things were unfair, nor were there any "true" scummy moments where enemies would appear behind you and wipe you in one turn. LE does feature turn rewind, and quite a generous limit at that, so there is always the opportunity to re-do a harsh turn and try again should something unexpected happen. Oh, there is no hit % on attacks. You will hit your attacks if you target someone; however, depending on RNG and their stat spread, they may guard it. Similarly, where magic is focused, you can create elemental effects by combining magic with certain tiles. AEO shocks by using lightning on water, burning forests by using fire on a grass tile etc. Similarly to FE: Three Houses, LE features monster combat. Fighting monsters involves targeting their weak points with the right weapon to deal damage and avoid counterattacks. Design-wise, these monsters look fantastic, but unfortunately, they aren't used that often, aside from some side quests. I like the inclusion of monsters, but not in the same way as this. Some monsters are overpowered in terms of what they can do, while others are more of a nuisance. The attackable parts of the monster change at the start of each round, meaning you can move swordsmen over to them only to find that next turn, you don't have the characters there to hit it. Characters can have two weapons, but you can't use magic as a sword user (aside from specialised classes), meaning, if RNG isn't in your favour, you could be forced to rewind a turn or not attack out of fear for a counter. If RNG is on your side, killing them off is relatively simple, as you are granted a stacking damage bonus for each consecutive "correct" hit. LE did well with the map design. Maps are manageable and full of things to do - holding a choke point, using elements to CC foes and block others or interacting with walls to open another path. All story maps felt well designed and, at points, challenging - but in a good way. As mentioned before, there weren't any maps where I felt the AI had a "scummy" advantage, that being random appearances or extra units that felt unfair. Don't get me wrong, units do appear like that in some areas, but I think it's in a fair or expected way, given the map layout and story at that time. So, a big one. In-between combat maps, you'll engage in downtime activities in the camp. These typically include completing quests for characters, interacting with other characters to build rapport or completing side quests - a set of combat maps with the same units. The rapport feature is nice; you get to learn about the other characters in your squad and some unique rewards if the character has them. This is heavily character dialogue centric, and while not every dialogue is voiced, the writers have done an excellent job of making each character feel unique. But if you aren't a fan of downtime activities or investing in a wide range of characters (there are a lot), then you may feel like your progress is being throttled. You can skip this stuff, but you will miss out on a large percentage of the game. Building rapport with these characters requires you to use leadership - a separate currency you can use on camp activities. This is finite, meaning you can't build rapport with everyone. You'll have to pick your fav characters, meaning 100% is locked behind additional playthroughs. Again, this will feel like most of the game. All in all, one of the better tactics games I've played and you can tell it was made with love from a dedicated team. You won't be sorry for picking it up and giving it your time

_childDocuments_.review: So I really wanted to finish this game before leaving a review, and here we are, several months after release for reasons.I am a big fan of strategy games, FF Tactics, Fire Emblem, Ogre Battle, Mario v. Rabbids, you name it.  1) I recommend this game, 2) I give it 7/10.Graphics:  The game is very well rendered, the art style is nice, gritty when it needs to be.  The cinematic scenes lend an almost painted style artwork to the realistic vibe, which is also very nice.  I ran into very few clipping issues with clothing and hair, in fact, only really one issue of someones face going through heavy armor late game.  That said, I will note a few things.  The scenery never changes, its castle, some trees, maybe some dirt, but its all very bleak and boring.  Just because realism is the goal, doesn't mean there can be nice, or beautiful backdrops in some fights or areas.  They also re-use the talking backdrops quite often.The character models are nicely rendered.  They do not, unfortunately, have any unique movements, they sometimes feel a little dead, and show no real emotion.  I would have almost rather still images during conversations, as opposed to the 3d models, just because of the lack of emotion.  I often simply listened to the conversations and did something else on my phone because I couldn't really watch them.  No engagement there.Combat: I found the combat engaging, but similar to other games like this.  There was a learning curve for mages range, as it sometimes seemed a bit overpowered, especially early game.  Enemies were not as "smart" as I would like them to be, you could sometimes bait them into attacking multiple enemies to avoid them killing off others, while keeping the low hp ally in battle (e.g. by simply raising their def one stage, so it would require two attacks to kill them, the enemy will automatically shift their target to a weak magic defense ally, even if that ally is full hp).  The "big enemy" mechanic was neat, changing what weapons they were weak against - it did remind me a bit of Fire Emblem Three Houses / Three Hopes.Spells: Magic was visually appealing, not enough variety.  Too many re-used animations in different colours.Camp: Running around camp is so unnecessary - they did this in FE: Three Houses, and it just seems like a waste of time.  They gave no new "mechanics" or reasons for this choice.Story: I enjoyed the story, and even (almost) cried during it.  I think, had they had perhaps a larger budget, they could have made some really emotional scenes that would have made it more immersive.  It was; however, similar to stories I have heard in the past.There is a part of the story where it isn't really fully explained, and I get its sort of a ciff hanger to learn more about the protagonist in a future game, but alas, it felt a bit incomplete.Characters:  Good.  They all seemed interesting with their own backstories.Voice acting: Good.  Although, not enough of it - specifically, allies "friendships" should have been voiced, at a minimum.  Regular chat in camp was fine without.Side missions:  Honestly, the worst part of this game.  There were three side missions, enemies at a river, enemies in a forest, some beast enemies in the plains.  They recycled these SAME THREE MISSIONS THE ENTIRE GAME!  Sorry for the caps - it was frustrating, even for quests relating to ally's stories, it was the same maps.  C'mon guys, throw a few trees or rocks around to create new maps.  This was extremely lazy.Overall, I enjoy the atmosphere, the story, and the art.  I loved seeing a dark, realistic strategy game.  This is my style, and honestly, given how small the studio is, the polish and lack of glitches (we are seeing more and more in AAA games), I am impressed.  Well done, and I look forward to the next game.

_childDocuments_.review: Holy cow, initial impressions are not great. It feels clunky, amateurish and clumsy, Yet, I somehow find myself engaged and want to continue. It's like your kid in high school made a game and you pretend to like it at first, but then you actually do. Weird. The cut-scenes are way too long and kinda stop-motion, but the voice acting is very good, making it tolerable. Combat is great and intuitive and I absolutely love the fact that I don't have to spend hours creating a character. Plus it supports a gamepad. Nice!! Still, it is growing on me and in time I may even give it a higher score. Let's see
