_childDocuments_.review: I've been deceived by online reviews that I can only suspect have been financed by this game. The game is NOT strategically deep in any sense whatsoever, it's painfully average, and even an average turn based game has more depth than this game does. All units get two shot for the most part. The only thing that adds " depth "  is the rock paper scissors weapon type vs armor bonus but even taking this into account, more than 50% of the time, units get equally 2 shot, so then what's the point? You'd think items or skills might help? No, they do not, there are no level up choices, characters give the impression that they level up but I've never seen a more useless level up system where you do not get to chose what stats to level up, nor does it make any difference since the enemies are two shotting you at lvl 1,3, or 7 equally so. Be it a mage, a warrior with an axe or a sword user. There is the option to " Defend "  which seems to skip your turn ( mostly used when you f'd up your turn and couldn't reach someone and hit them ) and this defend option simply gives you +1 defence, which should in theory reduce damage by 1, which doesn't matter, because you'll get 2 shot more than 70% of the cases anyway. The only depth in strategy this game has, is movement tiles and how far a unit can reach, it's all about how well can you 2 shot everything that's in range, so that the enemy can't 2 shot you back. The game does have other aspects that are nice, but this game should sell under story, graphics adventure click game, not a strategy game, which it's not. It's also one of those games that the moment you start it, you can see that it was designed for console and you're sat there struggling to figure out how to do simple things with the use of keyboard and mouse. I've tried to like this game but I can't. I was hoping it gets better as time goes on but that doesn't appear to be the case either in game progression sense, or in real time ( the game was released a year ago and it doesn't look like it's getting any meaningful updates or polish/care )
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Eidolons

_childDocuments_.review: Tried hard to like it, but the game starts trying to add unique elements to the turn based tactical genre which kind of diminish what it has going for it. The bad:- Monster fights are unique to start but quickly become annoying. - Gimmicks to certain levels (such as the patrol level in chapter 18) are convoluted and annoying- Your AI ally is usually really stupid and gets into trouble more often than not- Difficulty spike about halfway through is quite substantial. Feel like you are extremely under tuned but don't have many opportunities to level up outside of main combat encounters.The Meh:- Story has it's moments but feels awkward at times- The camp between campaign quests is kind of boring and quickly starts to feel like a chore. It does help with story pieces though.- Leadership points are kind of underwhelming and really just used to build rapport, which is also kind of underwhelming.The Good: - Characters are certainly likeable and interesting enough if you invest the time into speaking with them between battles.- Combat is still fun when it doesn't have a weird gimmick to it.- Weapon swapping is useful and adds to your strategy- Class advancement is a fun way to change up your playstyle. - Armour aesthetics are awesome when you advance your class.I wish there was a better rating than a thumbs up or thumbs down, but ultimately I feel that I wouldn't recommend this one to people as I felt myself starting to wear out as I got closer to the end. I would give it a 6.5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR A good game, with a story that will hold your interest and combat that is good enough to carry the run time. Its worth the money at least. Certainly worth looking at if you like Fire Emblem etcThat said, it has a fair amount of room for improvement. - Having played on Hard, the class balance isnt great. You will require Warlocks and Sharpshooter. Melee classes don't have the longevity to survive many rounds of combat, which they would need to compete with Sharpshooters and wizards don't have the spell count or CC to compete with Warlocks. You will use one or two priest/bishops for healing. But tanks/melee don't have the ability to mass taunt etc to make use of buffs.- Class customisation is pretty much non existent, characters can really be anything, and mastering classes doesn't give you any meaningful skills to use on another class. As such you will just end up using one class tree. Especially with new game + on the horizon this is defiantly and area for improvement.- Cheap tactics on both side. The tactics can be very cheap at times. Either its enemy butt rush.. for which you need Warlocks to cc them. Get to an objective, for which the enemy will teleport units to your objective thus removing the scope for cleaver tactics, and meaning you need to buy yourself time with... Warlocks, and move slowly. Or kill the enemy at your own pace, which you can do with warlocks. Also, as interesting as it is in the start, the mechanic where the enemy bosses take less damage till you clear out the normal units usually means latter on you will require cc to delay them until you can hurt them. Delaying them can only really be be achieved using Warlocks.-Which leads to lastly, a far bigger range of cc and taunting (tactics skills) for all the other classes not called Warlock. This is basically a repeat of my first point, but all the other classes need, more diverse spells and skill, or enough spell/skill uses to make them work for a whole mission in their assigned role. As an example, sorcerer big AOE spells have 1 use, as an aoe dps class this really hamstrings them. Same goes for tanks with 2/3 taunt uses, or assassins/berserkers who need a way to bypass guard and have a way to get way, or not die on the enemy turn to bring anything a sharpshooter wouldn't do better.Dont get me wrong though, i had fun with the game, just has room for improvement.

_childDocuments_.review: Good strategy game with interesting story. Though with critical flaws.Story has depth, obviously based on Chinese history, but the presentation is lacking and fragmented. Interactions with your companions feel messy, confusing, and unrewarding. Ended up skipping through most of it and only watching the cut scenes, which is pretty good. Love how many interesting characters there are and how some of them can have meaningful deaths in the story.Gameplay is pretty standard for a strategy game, positioning and trading blows seem more important here as it's not easy to one shot enemies like other games, which is nice. But the boss mechanic where you need to kill all mobs first is straight up annoying, serves little purpose and unfun to see all the bosses whacking on your guys but you need to chase down the mobs in the backline first. Final boss is just BS, no strategy at all and keeps reviving when you kill him. Feels like a waste of time.

_childDocuments_.review: I changed my review to a Yes.It's incredibly nerve-wracking to play at first because like most Asian games, it is all menus.  Takes a while to get acclimated to it.  Everything takes so bleeding long to do.  Combat is clunky at first, but works pretty well, again after a lot of practice.  I bought it on 60% discount.  I would have complained at full price, but after giving the game a 2nd and 3rd chance, I can see it justified.  It's very linear (no choices), and there are a LOT of cutscenes, but overall the game holds up.  Once you have a handle on the frustrating mechanics of the game, you can have some fun with character progression.  Battles can be fun in a '90's style Panzer General' kind of way.  Note that the mouse/cursor control in combat is VERY janky.  If it could be slowed down it would help. Another plus, there isn't a launch screen (bonus).  The game ending is underwhelming.  But getting to it is fun.  Also, this game relentlessly prompts the player to spend 'leadership points' (a kind of in-game currency) developing relationships with npc companions.  And then the game arbitrarily murders them.  And there's nothing at all you can do about it. (Lists of the npc's that get murdered this way are available on lots of online forums).    The developer support for the game is excellent.  They're ready and willing to help you and support their product.  It's a good concept. Could do with more polish and a ton less menus.I like it. Thumbs up after giving it a few chances.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Eidolons

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: Classic, addictive JRPG style tactical turn based combat.Divinity: OS2 style elemental/terrain interactions are done well and add a great dynamic to tactical planning.Monster fights are extremely fun, should be more of them though.Solid story and well-written characters, some definitely better than others.Fully and competently voice acted.Dragon Age style in-camp fed-ex quests may not be for everyone, but I like it for breaking up the monotony of constant battles, plus adds a lot of immersion.Cons: Annoying boss mechanic where you have to kill all the underlings before you can do any appreciable damage to the bosses/minibosses.Some levels are overtuned, especially the ones where reinforcements show up all over the place.Story ending could do with a little more fleshing out.Too many cutscenes in the middle of battle ruin the flow of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Eidolons

_childDocuments_.review: You know what the best part of a turn based tactics game is??That's right, handing out food at a camp while running from one side to the other to have the most banal conversations over and over again.Look, video game writing in 99% of games is absolute trash. So for a game to force so many cut scenes and awful banter between the most insufferable characters is a total slog and making my brain weep.I think I like the actual turn based fighting, but I feel like I have to go through an hour of god awful cut scenes to get to it. Unfortunately im past the two hour mark. I figured the game was just taking a bit to get up to steam. But after the first camp section -- im dreading where this is going.If they made a sequel, and cut all this useless time waster; I bet it would be great.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Eidolons

_childDocuments_.review: Now THIS is some fresh air!IDK why some people can't read the game description and understand in 3 sentences what this game is trying to deliver.I am an avid player of story rich games (Telltales, Dontnod, Quanticdream), and since more than 20 years playing RPGs Turn-Based games. TBS games (Turn Based over a Grid) being my favourites, after for long time such games were mostly jRPGs available only on consolles (or if you are old enough - X-COM, the original one, 1994) - where the golden age of such games was during SNES-Genesis / PS1 (Tactics Ogre, Shining Force, Final Fantasy Tactics, Vandal Hearts 1/2), after the "reboot" of X-COM and Divinity Original Sin, finally on Steam we saw a proper invasions of cRPGs TBS as well several jRPGs.Lost Eidolons is brining a totally innovative concept, or better said, merging Story-Rich game, without going in the typical "huge open world RPGs" where you end up loosing the hype of the main plot, and with FULLY VOICED characters, spectacular FMV, gifting again the somewhat dark-ish Fantasy theme, with a proper plot, unique characters personality traits (if you played Vandal Hearts of FFT, you know for sure what I mean), and adding some other classic RPGs elements, offering a great challange of TBS battles scripted (no random encounters), to properly enjoy either the story, if you don't want to play hard more or if you are new to TBS games - or as veteran of such genre, enjoying with both environment, weapons and skills very challenging battles!Props to the studio and the devs, you really don't see such kind of games, especially from a Korean Studio - they did a fantastic job, put a lot of dedication, and the live stream they are doing is amazing, where you see the enthusiasm and passion for their release and I am sure they will certainly fix any possible bug (so far I didn't enounter any problem and it's running fluid). The battle system could not be the most complex ever seen, but with the various other elements (and the shining force / fire emblem animations on each battle engagement), it makes overall a pure breath of fresh air merging two of my fav. games genre.Thank you a lot for this gem!
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Eidolons

_childDocuments_.review: A mediocre and tiresome main story, a plethora of bland and generic characters that look the same and act the same, a lot of stupid game mechanics that are there just to annoy you and a bunch of repetetive battles against the same generic enemies makes me regret the time i spend playing this awful game.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm loving this! Fire Emblem will be mentioned a lot as an influence of this game, but that's an excellent series to use as an influence. I love the smooth turn based game play, the graphics are stellar, the voice acting bombastic but setting the tone well. The music is spectacular. I've heard this called a 'western' RPG, but you can only say that as far as the medieval European aesthetic. The rest of it feels right out of an anime, from the plucky heroes making bold proclamations of virtue to the villains practically chortling in wickedness to the aria song that opens the game making it feel like the intro to a Netflix series. I love the details like the army that materializes when the combat zooms in so you can keep track of your units but also get the impression of larger wars and military actions. I love the animations special to units when they get critical hits and the unique subtle magical effect that looks like tendrils of lightning. Entirely enjoyable! I needed to drop some graphical bells and whistles to get a steady framerate but that hardly made a difference to the excellent art direction.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an absolute gem of a game which quite frankly still surprises me. It falls in the category of a standard top-down tactical RPG consisting of familiar elements. The story is ok-ish so far, a bit too slow paced with an inconsistent script. Tactical gameplay is fun but no revolution and the camp mechanic is nice and functional. The underlying systems of gear, skills and levling are nice but no wow-factor.But somehow, the developers have managed to put these parts together in a way that just WORKS. I'm amazed at how fun it is. This truly is an example of how the game is much greater then the sum of all it'sparts. I can absolutely recommend it at full price, just get it and be amazed :)

_childDocuments_.review: While I do plan to try and get through more of this game, at which point my opinion might change, currently, I cannot recommend this game. It is surprisingly bad. I was looking forward to getting this for a couple years now, and discovered it was part of the Humble Choice monthly membership this month, so I figured I would sign up for this game and a couple others. I regret my purchase and the fact you cannot refund Humble Choice except in rare circumstances unlike my own.I'm not sure if the worst part is the mouse and keyboard fighting each other when navigating the battlefield resulting in you only being able to use one or the other at a time. You cannot pan with WASD while moving the mouse into position or the view window moves sporadically around as the mouse mysteriously starts controlling the camera as it focuses on each square it moves over, even though it doesn't do this when not using WASD to pan.Or maybe the wort part is the cringe-worthy lack of any animation whatsoever in the spaces where the story scenes between battles play out even as one character at a time appears on screen with full animation behind the chat box—which is really weird because there is full animation in the battles for large numbers of invisible soldiers who suddenly appear out of thin air to fight each other while your character and an enemy character attack each other (after which, said soldiers again cease to exist after the two characters are done attacking each other). In the story scenes, everyone is literally still as a statue like some kind of visual novel—it is really unnerving. There is more life in such scenes in games from the SNES days—and just about every other game I've ever played.Or maybe it is the fact that archers, by default, can only attack exactly 2 squares away, no more, no less. And to make even less sense, they can attack through solid objects in the process, including floors and walls.Another annoying factor that (probably) isn't the most annoying is: after single attacks, the game pops up a menu screen showing multiple experience point gains for different things, like you might expect at the end of an entire battle—except this game does this after individual attacks, making the pacing extremely slow and disjointed.I'm really not trying to be overly critical, because I like the concept of the game, and the art style is good—and I'm sure a lot of effort was put into this game by the developers. However, the game being as it is, I would not spend my own money on it had I known the quality and issues (which videos just didn't properly display), so I cannot recommend others to spend their money, nor time, on it.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Eidolons

_childDocuments_.review: After 80 hours I have finally finished this game.The game is very linear and normally for me that's a big turn off...  However even thought this is not even close to a sandbox I still enjoyed the game because they took the linear on rails game and did a great job with the story....  The Graphic's are nice, the interaction and play with developing your rapport with the many possible characters that will join you on your adventure is solid.  The story has a lot of up and down your really feel a whole range of emotions and the game does a great job of sucking you in and allowing you to experience it with a well done music track (Music I actually didn't turn off in the options?!?)  The Combat is good enough...  its got some interesting mechanics that cause the player to have to think from time to time but for the majority of game it doesn't take that much thought....  However the final battle is stupidly different from the rest of the game.  If your the type of person that enjoys games like Elden Ring where your willing to fail for hours to figure out mechanics then the last battle will be your cup of tea....  Certainly is not mine....  However other then the final battle this game is solid, the story is nothing amazing but the execution of the story is really done well....  As for replayability I don't see this as being an RPG your going to play a second time.  One time is enough...I do recommend this game and I am pretty picky about games I recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a tough review to write because overall I really liked playing this game, but the ending was so non-existent that it felt insulting. Without spoilers, you fight an epic final battle and are rewarded with basically nothing. Your romance may or may not work, no explanation and you'll have no idea. No detail on what happens to any of your companions. Two largely meaningless paragraphs about you, and a single graphic...that's it.The underlying game mechanics...exist but are not well explained. What do stats do? Basic explanations exist but good luck calculating them. Classes are fairly unbalanced, for example there's almost no reason to run any non-ranged character from the fighter line, assassins are nifty but their damage is incredibly disappointing given how squishy they are, berserkers are worse. Sharpshooters in plate easily outscale and outdamage rangers. Dark magic wielders become meh in late game compared to light and elemental.Graphics are amazing and the gameplay is really fun. The lack of polish in game mechanics is a minor pain point. The fact that the ending is so terrible though feels like the developers just gave up on the story and put the least possible effort in, essentially creating a single graphic of "You won."

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished this game on normal difficulty, curious about the story and gameplay for the most part. For gameplay, its fairly straightforward for the genre. There are base classes that go into intermediate than advanced. Certain classes and certain armor sets travel the map a certain distance. Standard stuff. At normal difficulty, I think the game gives more than a fair challenge which I respect, I didn't feel like I was that overpowered and I did have to put in effort to think before moving. The UNDO feature was a nice add. At first, I thought it was a bit soft, but with the way the game plays it is actually nice to have especially for people like me who are not playing for the challenge.The map interface is good, smooth, I didn't have any issues mid-battle at all. However, the preparation (pre-fight stuff) I felt could have been done better. I spent a ton of time back tracking who I assigned aides to and trying to figure out which match is best fit. Then I would get lost because of having to scroll and find a name I was looking at previously. I just feel there's room for improvement there in terms of...organization? Not sure how to explain my query.I also felt the abilities were repetitive but there is some logic in that, considering the perma-death mode. I think on higher difficulty, some of those abilities should be buffed just to encourage people to try it out. Just my thoughts on the matter.Smaller critiques. The optional battles were repetitive. In the future, it would have been good to re-use old story maps for these but that was not the case. These optional maps were one of what, three? Maybe four? In the future, consider re-using story maps or even shuffling them, if possible. Some story maps were one and done and that just feels wasteful. Just giving feedback here.As for the story/character stuff, I will try to be non-spoiler here. I really like the world and story, and I can tell that a ton of thought and care went into it all. It's a fusion of Eastern and Western high fantasy, more so the latter of course. There are knights, wizards, a feudal like society with lords, ladies, kings and of course, and evil empire. But the more magical side, at least to me, felt very eastern. The eidolons and that aspect of the story. Liviyu reminds me of classic wuxia setting of a lawless land run by bandits, monsters and all sorts of trouble that main characters go to for a training arc.The characters are engaging, I really like how you get to interact with all of them at some point in the story. The interactions CAN be a bit shallow, but I respect the attempt. The uh, social leveling part of the game was okay. It is better than some, not quite as good as say, a Fire Emblem game. There isn't that much incentive to level up everyone, something I feel can be improved upon. Games like Persona, Fire Emblem, they give a ton of incentive to level relationships (extra maps, battlefield buffs, etc). This game, there is less, and its not like the conversations were particularly interesting. Some were better than others, there is clearly a...bias...among the romance options I think (*coughMarchelle). Also, I've heard that there is a bug with the romancing part of the game and I hope that is fixed. I, personally, only saw two conversations lol.Despite the weaknesses I've mentioned, I think how characters were used made it feel more exciting seeing them on the map. Instead of killing randos that come and go, you actually know these characters and it makes the story battles more engaging. ALSO, I have to give HIGH praise to the people who drew and narrated the scenes for when events happen between chapters. The art for those were superb, the music was very well-fitting and gave a historical feel to the game. I especially like the one for CH26. Outstanding work. That was hype. I really have to give that particular team credit.Moving on from that, I really liked how the story is written. The main character is not perfect, he makes mistakes, and this causes internal conflict that I feel is understandable enough. Although, I did see his point of view and understand why he did what he did, it just means the characters felt alive here and I appreciated that. So motivations were well done, for SOME characters at least, I felt some villains were rather shallow. Especially at the beginning xD come on guys, not all bad guys have those annoying villain voices. Do better.There were a couple anti-climatic moments but not that much. The story kept me interested and was my favorite part of the game. The gameplay was standard, the social leveling was fine, but the story and lore I can tell the team put a ton of effort into it.Do I recommend this game? Yes. But I do not think I will replay until NG+ feature is added and some bugs are fixed. The story team, you guys did great. I hope if you improve upon this game, make it a point to focus on the social leveling aspect, which I felt was quite weak. Not terrible, but it can be better. Just need more interactions, more reasons to level them up, its content that can make this game more special.Thanks for the game! Good job overall. Please accept this review as constructive criticism.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just good enough to barely recommend. It's not bad, but I didn't enjoy it much near the end and I just wanted to finish, but struggled. Between Chapter 24-27 I gave up and pursued other games that interested me. The story is interesting enough to hold me, I like building relationships with characters and the realistic art style as well as the leveling up. Occasionally, I found the battles fun enough. There's a little space you can maneuver in-between battles that's a little camp and it's fun to watch it develop.My issues were initially only cosmetic. It's a gorgeous game - but outside the active cut scenes which there are few of, the models just stand around with a well detailed backdrop as their conversation goes on. It was a little disappointing, but I adjusted. I appreciated there was some challenge to the game, but minimal as I'm not a hardcore strategy gamer. I'm here to play and enjoy the story, not spend 100+ hours in an alright game. Early on I did pay attention and was able to plan out some characters' progression, because you need to. If you mess up and don't teach someone in lower levels both magic and physical abilities then it's nearly impossible to do so later in game when you notice, as I did for some side characters. Also, suddenly midway in the game the difficulty jumps outrageously, I can't recall which chapter although I've seen others mention it. The first half I'd mess up a few times and retry with success. Suddenly I'm failing at least 5+ times with no idea how to progress despite having invested heavily in items and character skills. Honestly, after failing one of the last escape cart battles at least 15 ten times I uninstalled the game. I took a break, lost 8 more times, looked up guides for suggestions and decided not to waste anymore time on it. Particularly, because as a casual gamer I just played with the same characters and trained the others I recruited 'just in case'. The biggest annoyance to me besides everything else - SO many main characters permanently disappear/temporarily disappear later in the game, when it gets HARDER. My main archer, my main barbarian, my main healer, my main warlock - not all at once, but over time. I was just shocked with WHO ELSE WILL I LOSE? For example, the battle I gave up the characters unavailable to me were (my secondary archer, my main attacker, my main warlock) and I'd somewhat adapted to the loss of my main barbarian. If not for my earlier plays, where I flew through the chapters and stayed up late at night I'd probably NOT recommend this. But I won't deny I had fun at first. Perhaps a real strategist player would enjoy this, but I got fed up. My shining star in this whole thing was honestly the archer Karin, perhaps I molded her right, I'm not sure - but she was a beast archer at the end. May have been a sharpshooter, but she took out things left and right and was a nice constant to have for performance considering all the other variables. I truly loved her character in battle.

_childDocuments_.review: I only played for a bit but I think honestly this game is not bad, not sure why the review is so bad. _childDocuments_.review: Fire emblem meets western-medieval-dark-fantasy setting? That is how I would describe Lost Eidolons in short. It has a "slow" start, but once the story and more gameplay elements are set up, it starts showing its unique charme. The game borrows some well known gameplay mechanics from genre greats like Fire Emblem and combines them with micromanagement systems from older RPG classics like Dragon Age: Origins. There is one main battle per chapter, each followed up by a camp phase where you can talk and interact with your allies and manage your ressources like weapons, skills and buying new stuff at the merchant by adding some minor tweaks here and there to still make it feel like a unique experience. The story kicks off with a usual theme: a mercenary-band that knows each other since childhood, that gets involved in political intrigues. The story gets more and more interesting the further you progress. (Awesome voice acting by the way)It is a more than solid game for genre fans and considering the price of 34,99€ you get a lot of content for your money. One of the downsights: Sidequests in the camp are only interesting if you care for the characters, which may not be the case at the beginning of the game. Optional battles are mostly repetitive and have no unique map designs or unique goals. Your goal is most of the time the same: rout some bandits or monsters. Graphics are awesome and it runs smooth on the steam deck, no issues so far. (Savegame shows 32h playtime so far, reached the last third of the story). If you like SRPG's you should give this a try, you get a quality game that may have a slow start but gets more fun the further you advance the story. Leveling your units and see them become more powerful with additional class and skill progressions will give you more variety in your tactical decisions. I would give this an 8/10 and considering that this game was created by a small studio we can only imagine what they could have created with AA/AAA game budget.

_childDocuments_.review: A really impressive, if maybe a bit overly ambitious first game from this dev team. It's fire emblem without the anime, and without some of the polish. The tactics gameplay is solid and fun. Combat skills and the magic system provide a bit more depth than I remember FE having. Camp management breaks up combat and exposition with maybe a little too much distraction from the core gameplay -- basically boils down to fetch quests and running around/teleporting between characters to talk. In this vein, some of the dialogue feels slightly unnecessary. Your mileage will vary here based on how invested you are in the characters and story. Graphically I think this game is especially impressive coming from such a small team, it's basically punching at AAA weight in this category imo. There is no real need for such high quality textures and reflective surfaces on wet ground and armor in a tactics game, but it's there and it's a neat touch.The limited turns are basically a mechanic to reward faster completion of battles rather than a tight clock that you're running up against, but if you're the type of person who hates even the existence of such a mechanic, then this game isn't for you YET, but they are working on implementing a no turn limit that you can select when starting a new game, and even seem to be keeping the xp rewards for faster completion of missions, so hey, win-win for you.Overall I'm having a good time with it. My one pet peeve that I just have to get out there is how often characters do weapon swinging/poses in between lines of dialogue during battles. At first it seemed like it's an effective punctuation for what's being said, but it's absolutely overused and really starts to feel like it's just wasted time, which results in me being taken a little out of the experience.

_childDocuments_.review: This game makes some horrendous mistakes, it wants to be story rich and driven but the writing is not fantastic and full of logic problems, the whole thing with the noble at the start wanting to kill everyone and not doing it drove me mad and then this idea he could frame an inquisitor felt poorly thought out, it feels like it has some good plot ideas but the way it executes them seems unrealistic and ridiculous.Example one, the woman who hires you in first mission is told to kill you by the noble, she doesn't want to so you break free from two guards holding you on your knees grab the dagger hold it to the nobles throat then surrender... all of the sudden the noble rather lock you up when moments ago he was keen on your death for doing nothing to him, the whole scene left me checking out.Example two, He has an inquisitor he has locked up with her men, he comes into the dungeon and talks about how he's going to kill them all and frame them as rebels as the inquisitor has evidence of him robbing merchants... why is he keeping them alive in his dungeon when his whole idea is murder them!? it would have been better if the reason he was keeping the inquisitor alive is to have her communicate to her superiors that everything is fine and that he's innocent of his crimes and that she's refusing to play ball so he's going to kill her men one by one until she cooperates, this gives actual reason as to why they're all currently alive, he's going to use them to clear his name, that makes logical sense, not he's going to murder them all and he just seems horrendous at following his words...I feel if the noble told me he was going to kill another person I'd be like sure bub, I believe you, just like the last three times you've said you want people dead... or maybe he thinks kill and murder are words that describe his f'ing dungeon.  This game needs a better writing team that keeps each other in check, the other problem I had is with the camp, the camp for what they're using it for is really dull... it's massive and it's a place to talk to NPC's, it doesn't need to be huge... and it has map markers for people you can talk to who have nothing to say like someone forgot to clear the markers... it's all tedious mechanics other games have realised are not fun and ditched.Other than that the game play so far seems fun and I look forward to seeing the class system, game play seems fairly fine, it's just marred with too much cut scenes and conversations that are just not gripping or engaging and make the game feel so much more budgeted.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty darn good. It reminds me of fire emblem, but it focuses more on positioning and creating bottlenecks as well as utilizing terrain and environment.It's mixed in some areas - for example, the voice acting is great and draws you into caring for the characters, but each time they talk, they pause for like an hour before speaking. The intro cutscenes at the start of the game could probably be cut up to the parade scene and imo it would improve the game greatly.Unless you know everything from the get go, you will probably have to restart your playthrough if you intend to beat the game. I had to - some things (like skills and classes) don't have any decisive impact for 80% of the game and then become necessary. In order to obtain the needed options, you have to train, and the final battle is not the kind of battle that can be won with any old team. That said, I feel like it speaks to how much I enjoyed my time in the game that I was eager to restart - they earned my interest and I felt like I was learning quite a lot about the mechanics of the game just from doing so (and it was rewarding af - battles are entirely different when you focus on different tactics)

_childDocuments_.review: I thought I'd update this review because of the huge number of people that found it helpful (3). I played another 3 or 4 hours after my initial review and....just lost interest. I realized I was grumbling more about the shortcomings than finding enjoyable/novel/interesting things to prompt my interest. Here's more cr*p wrong with this game.... things that I think could be fixed, but only because I'm an optimist;1) Someone armed with a sword can attack an opponent in an adjacent space, roughly 5' away. Someone with a bow can attack an opponent 2 spaces away, roughly 10' away. WTF is that about? There are improvements later, but what aspiring archer even starts shooting at 10'? Answer: none.2) Why can't I attack and move? If moving and attacking requires a certain amount of time, certainly attacking and then moving requires the same. The are zones of control and those should apply, but WTF?3) Why is there no cover? Oh... right! Because I can only shoot a bow from 10' away so an opponent can step around my cover. WTF?4) Why do merchants even bother selling things in my camp? Their items suck! WTF?5) Combat sucks. It took a few battles to realize the limitations in combat. The strategic options are so painfully limited that large-scale battles are just staged mini-battles. On a battlefield, I might see 20 opponents, but they are kind enough to wait until I am within a certain range before they move or attack. The worst AI ever. There is no need for a class of character with any crowd control because the enemy is always kind enough to wait until I am ready to kill them. WTF?There are more petty issues that lead to a collective vurp, leaving a bad taste in my mouth. Usually, if I have gotten $1 per hour play time from a game, I'll rate a game a thumbs-up. Not here. In this case, the game was a sultry ho0ker, just leading me on until she showed me she sucked. Poorly.---Original--A heck of a lot good about this game, but the lead-up was so slow I nearly gave up.Notably, this game has perhaps the best facial animations of *any* game I've ever played - that's a lot of games, whipper snappers.While I'm still (roughly 15 hours) not a huge fan of the combat, it has improved enough to keep my interest. The tactical options in the (very) early game were plain boring. They're tolerable now. Looking at the skill trees has convinced me there are good things to come.If you're not one of my sons, you'll be shocked to hear me report on the egregious dialog here. Wait! Hold up. Voice acting is superb. No complaint there. The writing, as I'm wont to report in the games I review, gives me heart burn. The sheer douche-baggery of the main character, the scum I have to play as and listen to, is the most  inane, pitiful, dialog ever. The basket case dork that I've been forced to play in this video game gives me bladder stones. I blame this on the Japanese. JRPGs glorify adolescents in combat and the result is a terrible conflict between character innocence and the maturity required for processing combat/war. Japan aside, this dialog hurts my heart.I like what I've seen. I'm not too keen on the menial tasks at camp in between combat missions, but it hasn't worn out its welcome yet. The characters are interesting and many have perky b0Obs. I expect I'll play another 20 - 30 hours before I'm too sick of the main character and move on. That's well worth my money.

_childDocuments_.review: I am surprised, I only  bought this game as was not sure what to play and I am enjoying this game much more than I thought I would. The game reminds me a bit of Dragon Age Origins, Black Desert Online and Game of Thrones. I've seen people say it's like Fire Emblem, I've heard of that game but have never played it.The combat is fun and the battle animations are great though too repetitive.The story was a bit iffy at first but it gets a lot better and I like it mostly.Sometimes I prefer games that are more simplistic as I don't like games that have too much strategy or are too complex.I really like the characters and I enjoy chatting to them in camp. I like how the characters interact with each other. I find them all quite unique and interesting.I like both the combat in the field as well as all the activities in camp and following the story.It seems like a lot of the negative reviews are from people not knowing what the game is and expecting the game to be something it's not. I watched reviews on Youtube as well as gameplay which helped me decide that I possibly might like this game so bought it even though I was not 100% sure I'd like this game. If you are interested in this game and aren't sure maybe watch some you tube videos.Only things I dislike is that facial animations are just the mouth moving and eyes blinking and no other expressions, I understand it's not AAA and they have a budget but the voice acting  makes up for it as it is very good  at conveying the emotions and expressions the face lack.I also dislike how outnumbered you are. _childDocuments_.review: Pretty standard strategy game but definitely scratched a strategy itch. The great: I felt the story was pretty good overall. The overall depth was good, though the plot twist in the middle could've used some polish to make it more palatable. The "Eidolon" things seemed very much an....unnecessary addition to the actual story (game's name...I know). Maybe a future game/DLC or backstory from this developer would be good IMO. I thought the voice acting was really good considering their resources. Just the main/side quests were voiced, the small sidebar convos weren't, which is fine. Definitely a long game if you do everything and listen to the voiced conversations. I quick-read a lot of the generic comments, but still clicked through every optional side-quest and conversation and came in just over 70 hours.The good: Combat and strategy were fairly run-of-the-mill rock/paper/scissors with some environmental effects thrown in. Not a lot of variety in map types and most of the battles outside of a few specific ones were just about baiting the enemy to advance and then killing off the dangerous ones quickly. Still, there was a good amount of customization, spell options, weaponry, and classes to give the strategy enthusiast something to chew on.Graphics were pretty good. Not exactly a selling point in a heavy strategy game but the fight scenes were fine.Sound other than the voices was fine. Music got a little repetitive but whatever. Good sound effects.The bad: The rapport system needed a lot of work. You can easily max out most of the people that give you rewards and have leftover gifts/leadership points to spare for the last 3-5 chapters. This definitely needed more variety and choice as a replayability issue. More characters needed more rewards to provide choice and options.The merchants were....sort of useless? Ended the game with a boatload of gold and never needed it outside of some potions, gifts, and a few pieces of gear. They definitely needed more variety of things they sold and increased prices of those things.Itemization: While there was a decent weapon and magic variety, there was very little variety within each category. Outside of 1 epic per weapon type (sword/spear/axe [that you can't even use] and magic books), there was really nothing beyond that. At every level you had like 3 types with very minimal statistical difference to differentiate them (+5 accuracy vs. like +3 crit vs. whatever). Needed more options and variability.

_childDocuments_.review: 1. Personally, I see no issues with a turn limit. At least, in the early gameplay, it has never been an issue. However, I also understand players who disliked it. The way I see it, is in future it will force me to take risks. High risks, high rewards in terms of execution of the right strategy. Otherwise, I can cover myself in the corner in defense position with ranged warriors and healers, and that would take away all the fun.Nevertheless, to satisfy all users, as developers have mentioned, turn limit might be optional. At the same time, there could be few additional layers. Such as, finish battle within 20 turns, get extra rewards; within 25 turns, just a little bit of extra exp; anything above those, no premiums.2. I absolutely love animation of defending units. Instead of waiting for a blow to come, which might lead to death, they try to deflect and counterattack. Super immersive. Great job on that idea.3. I`m not sure what the future holds for the game, but I would love seeing my team settling somewhere permanent. Instead of pushing the story, and going through endless dialogues all the time, I`d simply would love to log in to the game, take some random missions. From missions, I`d get some materials to upgrade my camp. Walls, archer towers etc. Then, some missions would be to defend my city against a massive army. Archer towers would be assisting me every turn (Heroes of Might and Magic siege vibe).I also believe, this concept would bring more longevity to the game.4. I`m a bit annoyed when 2 persons are having a conversation, and there is like a second delay before the second person portrait pops up, and the speech will sound. Perhaps, transition time can be much shorter.Edited. 5. I also would suggest to improve sensitivity of WASD movement. It is way too slow comparing to mouse movement. Some users shooter users are used to play with WASD, so it could be of big help to them. EQ could be rotations to left and right.Apart from that, thanks for a good game. Good job.

_childDocuments_.review: This is another time where a middle button or 'indifferent' option would be great. Come on Steam.I purchased Lost Eidolons hoping to scratch that Fire Emblem Awakening itch I've had since beating it so many years ago. I felt connected to those characters, the intense 20 unit fights, the changing terrain, the romance options. Even my custom character felt part of the universe. Lost Eidolons is about you starting a rebellion over a woman being captured. A group of sellswords go full-scale anarchy over a lack of human rights which, in the era this is set in, was commonplace so I wasn't drawn in. I felt my characters were also over powered, one hit of mine equals two of theirs which didn't shake out right. I also was disappointed I couldn't recruit a custom character. I generally do not care much about graphics if the gameplay is there but the characters look strange, as if they are missing a final render or a texture pack. Lastly, the lip synching was bad. Like old school ninja move bad. What Lost Eidolons does well however is that it has good, fluid combat, A decent amount of characters involved in the story with well-mixed emotions and personality types. There is a system in place, though underdeveloped, that shows which weapons work against which armor type so a little extra consideration between turns is necessary which is nice. The mechanics of the game are also well explained without being presented all at once to bog the player down with a learning curve which I also liked. I feel like this game could have really been a home run for me if there was some sort of character creation, the textures were a tad more developed, a romance system was in place, and I had a reason to care about the characters but really the first two are what matter to me personally. I want to feel like I am in the game, not that I am pretending to be Eden. Try though I might, I am not a sexy Italian man with chiseled abs and a charismatic personality. Thank you for reading.

Most enemies are two hits, so it's doing one ranged hit and one melee hit and then healing through the damage on the enemies turn.The XP system is very confusing. You level up three separate bars but I can't figure out what they do or what the benefit is as you level up. The enemies have been two hits since the beginning of the game and still are.The dialogue/plot is translated exceptionally well, but sounds strange occasionally and some plot details don't make sense. _childDocuments_.review: I'm gonna tell you something you don't want to hear. Fire Emblem lacks depth. It's a very simple series mechanically. It is the entry level tactics game. This game is just a clone of FE but worse. If you like FE, you will probably like this, and you should probably buy it, at least on sale. If you have played a lot of other tactics games, this really doesn't cut it anymore, at least for me.Hard difficulty with Permadeath on MANIAC mode (their names, not mine) is admittedly pretty brutal because everything, including your units, dies in essentially 2 hits. That is why it has no depth. It doesn't matter what class you are. You don't need any tactics. Bait the enemy by stepping into a purple square. Have them chase you. Use a ranged attack to soften the enemies up and a melee to finish them off so they don't get counterattacked. Repeat for every map so you don't lose anyone. Failing to do this properly results in basically a guaranteed death. Also, they got a lucky crit? Depending on who they are attacking, you might just lose your unit in one hit. At least you have 5 undos. Graphics are overall better than I thought, but animations are terrible and characters are dolls. There's a good amount of unique faces and I think some of them have good designs.The voice acting is okay, I feel some of the actors are good but poorly directed? Or maybe the writing and dialog are kind of terrible. Or maybe translated badly? It's not good.It feels like these people really wanted to create a narrative-driven game but didn't have the resources, but said "♥♥♥♥ it" and did it anyway. I gotta give some respect to that, but I still also have to say that the presentation can be so bad because of it that it seems like it wasn't worth it. I also just started to tune out of the story because the dialog is pretty bad. Despite looking more western, it is just full of anime dialog and weird tone/emoting that almost makes it verge on cringe.There is SOOOO much time wasted on dialog and talking to people in your camp. It's too much, and the conversations are so banal most of the time. I tried my best to stay invested in the story, but I eventually just started resorting to skipping all dialog. And it would still take forever to get through all the conversations. They tried. And if you like FE, you will like this, because it's pretty much the same. If you were looking for a tactics game but have played a lot of them already, I personally feel this game is on the lower end of the overall totem pole.

_childDocuments_.review: yeah, it's western Fire Emblembut it's actualy goodyou would be shocked looking at the quality of polish and presentation this rather low priced game offersbeeing it (fully voiced) ingame cutscene, mini cutscenes, ingame lore-books, charcter and world designthis feels much more like a AAA game then an AA game, in all the right ways mind you.the voice over is spot, the writing is okay; it's not Monkey Island, but it's also not Xenogears3-esque teletubby niveau.the grafics (everything maxed) are detailed, and look pretty impressive in many places.but the most important part is the gameplay: it's brilliant.like you would expect your roster of charactes gain exp (in different categories), are fully equippable, got classes and spells to play around with. it's all rock solid, even getting some of those "bondig"-elements into the core combat (charcters that like each other offer more boni to each other, etc.).  as a new elemt monsters come into play each monster got weaknesses to certain attack types (like axe, sword, magic, bow, etc.), hitting em with said weakness inflicts more damage and shuffles their position, hitting em 2 with the same type of weakness breaks their guard to this specific damage type, which means the next of the attack will inflict massive damage. it's a great system, fitting the turnbased Fire Emblem like combat. as whole i often got the Dragon's Dogma vibes, in presentation, general flow and yes: when fighting the monsters.there are turn limits, but you a) got the chance to turn em straigh off and b) they offer exp boni.amazing game, punching way way above it's weight and hitting nearly all of it's punches.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing!  There are a lot of similarities, game-play-wise to other games, like Fire Emblem: Three Houses, but these are all the good aspects of that game.  The story is similar, with a bit of game-of-thrones, and another 'chosen-one' vibe, though the emphasis on your character doesn't feel as quite so center-stage as FE:3H.  Gameplay is smooth, solid, and I love the more 'realism' styled armor, weapons, and characters.Cinematic scenes are a mix of movie style rendered, and "still-frame" backdrop with animated characters for whomever is speaking.   Lots of voice-overs, even during camp-scenes, although some just have a few minor utterances instead of full voice-over, but that's okay.  It doesn't hurt any of the story-telling at all!The game feels very well paced!  The pattern tends to go cutscene -> story battle -> camp (optional side battle) -> cutscene -> rinse/repeat.  This gives you a good mix of "action" whilst giving you plenty of time in between to manage your troops, talk to your friends, do the things, etc.  I haven't felt either rushed, nor bored with the pacing.  I think it's a great balance!  Although for any sequels or future installments, I hope there will be more options for training and doing mock battles to unlock all the jobs for every single character, and be able to max relations for all the friendship dialogues.  But I still love this game as-is!!The class options are surprisingly well balanced and despite the fact that all the enemies have the same classes as you, each encounter was well designed to be interesting.  With maybe the exception to that being some of the bandit optional fights.  But those are still fun as I tend to use that to get some exp over to the less/under used people from my story fights.Story is interesting, and the characters all feel like they're  well written.  The visuals are great, and voice acting is all very well done!  All-in-all, this was a total sleeper for me!  I hadn't seen any marketing, but I'm so glad this game was recommended to me because I love it!  I've definitely enjoyed it, and have played WAY too much of it on a daily basis, lolz.  If anyone is a fan of Fire Emblem: Three Houses on switch, or the FF: Tactics, or Tactics Ogre: Reborn, I'd highly recommend this game!

_childDocuments_.review: I've got mixed feelings about Lost Eidolons but I think the good outweighs the bad. I came in expecting gritty Fire Emblem and got what I wanted plus some more. The bad is mostly on the technical parts of the game: side quest and optional battles design are repetitive, the missables seems a bit mean-spirited, and realistic models contrasted with zero facial expressions is definitely a choice.Gameplay is also up to fun TRPG standard and also follows the FE direction of classes being the deciding factor between variety for units. Otherwise there isn't going to be much variety between units if they're using the same class even though there are minor differences from single use "unique"(some actually have the same ones) skills if you follow their intended classes. Weapon “triangle” is here as well with different weapons dealing more damage to different armor sets. Reinforcements out of thin air are also a thing in this game but you always have a fresh full turn to react to them before they act so they're pretty fair. People seems to complain about the difficulty in later chapters but unless you're braindead or playing on masochist permadeath, some basic aggro+range management and CC on key enemies make it pretty easy for your godlike units to mop anything up. Also this game even has built-in save scum so I didn't even need to restart any map ever on hard difficulty. I played with turn limits off but I don’t think I ever exceeded 20 turns and the limit is like 30-40 turns.On the other hand, the plot and character development is a big strong point. The plot setup is pretty standard with it being a huge war that we kinda stumble on but it progresses well with no absurdly long-winded exposition. The core side characters that form up your council is also pretty good and they feel pretty tight as a group at the end. The other side characters that make up your army is also fine if you're used to the one-note traits common to these games. And yeah just like FE you can build up relationships with them through various means to reach checkpoints for special dialogue and occasionally very good rewards. Also quite a lot of voice acting with main story being fully voiced and even the side quests are fully voiced but the objectives itself are mostly just go from point A to B and talk to some people.Now, what I think stands out most about the story in this game is that it actually manages to develop the MC and the Antagonist quite successfully. They have clear arcs and I actually like the both of them throughout the story. Overall, the game is pretty gud methinks.

_childDocuments_.review: The game's fun, but it does have a couple of issues, so I'll start with those.Normally I hate ragging on a game for graphical issues, especially because this game does look really nice most of the time. The combat animations are really well done. I just don't think there was enough time put in to things like cutscenes or facial animation to work well with the good character models. In-game cutscenes have characters just teleport in and out of the scene, as well as into new poses. I think the game would've done better with a simpler art style that they could work with more smoothly, or handling cutscenes with more still images.Secondly, I think there's some major skill-creep that makes it hard to tell what your allies and enemies can do. When you check on a unit, from the midpoint on you'll see like 15 skills on them and most do pretty minor things. Except there's one really important skill in the list that you might've missed, like they're immune to certain status effects. Having multiple of these small skills be rolled into one that upgrades gradually would've made things a lot clearer.Thirdly, I think the game has some mechanics that look minor at first but aren't explained very well and turn out to be pretty big. The random conversations with allies in camp seem like they're just fluff text, but then occasionally they're super important and let you get sidequests, recruit characters or get items. Or how there's very little indication on how an enemy's special abilities will activate. Where their AoE is going to hit for example, or if it's a charged attack or not.Otherwise though, this is a surprisingly rock-solid tactics game that I really recommend. The lack of a true dodge means that combat is very fast-paced, and what you do on your turn is super important. Gimmicks in maps are telegraphed without feeling incredibly hand-holding, large enemies are super fun to take down with good positioning and unit variety, and bosses are threatening while still having ways to outplay them. For what it's worth, I'm playing on hard, permadeath and no turn count limit. It's not a perfect game, but it's a fantastic first tile from a small studio.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a fire emblem with decent graphics but very basic story and progression this is for you.Having been spoiled by Langrisser 1+2 I can't recommend this game.Things I didn't like about this:The story is on rails, nothing you do changes anything, which means zero replay valueGame interface is really hard to understand, and important things like gear levels are almost hiddenThe cursor is battle is hard to control, since this is something you'll be using a LOT it makes no sense at allEnemy type icons are hard to distinguishThere's a TON of management between battles, a lot of it involves trying to min max thingsThe story is linear and completely lacking of any novelty or common senseThe characters are not likable and most lack personalityThe friendship system makes zero sense, you're traveling together with people you grow up with and according to the friendship system you're not even acquaintances, it's a huge wtf momentAll camp activities are limited by the amount of points you haveEquipment and classes are very limited if what they can doMovement and ability range are completely off, most of the time your team can't attack or do anythingAll classes even mages can use platemail, why wouldn't you XDHow can they fix the game to make it more appealing?Let us move on the map and have control over which battles we want to doStreamline the user interfaceFix the battle cursorGive us the responsibility to find resources to upgrade camp in the way we want itMake monster hunting and boss activities on the mapLet everyone able to use a grimoire and use the magic they are proficient inImprove all ability ranges and movement ranges, to streamline combatAllow us to recruit monsters

Yeah it's what fire emblem does but since they refuse to bring that series over to steam to take my money, It's a nice feature to see in a game2.The voice acting is overall good but it is hurt by them not animating the faces3.The soundtrack is light but overall is good.4.The armor looks pretty good detail wise(expect for bals armor,we are sitting down for a drink & his leg guards are all f*cked up),I would of preferred it to come with capes but it's fine. 5.The game holds onto player retention fairly well & makes me wanting to come back.6.The music overall has been fairly decent.7.The cast is enjoyable & they are written fairly well,Even with the dead faces of characters i still find myself being invested & they even get a chuckle out of me.8.Never got bored with this games combat,It helps that they switch it up fairly often.9.The nice combinations of effects example my go to is poison flask+night veil=Massacre.Both do dot damage which are both around 8 damage plus the added effect of veil that slows movement makes this combo one of the best if need to thin the herd or hold a location/buy time. Another good combo is rain+lighting=For nice aoe damage or rain+blizzard=damaged frozen enemies. If possible for bigger group you want to do rain,lighting then blizzard.10.A almost perfect last level,They did everything right outside of con#3 & there should of been more than one tiny boat.11.The game does a great job making you care about the named foes due to the limited times you get to talk to them & how often they recurred in fights & they grow alongside you're group.12.The art pieces for stylized cut scenes were well drawn.Minor pros 1.Being able to fast travel to the person you want to talk to.Minor feature but there are other games that make you teleport to a way point & then make you waste time traveling to that person.2.It's nice to actually have allied npcs that are actually worth a sh*t in a fight,Doesn't happen enough in turned based war games. It's a bit sparse though i think i only had it happen like 5-8 times through my hours.Cons1.The tutorial being from a scene in the future. I have no idea why devs think it is a good idea to spoil events in their own games. It ruins the story telling aspect,If possible i would like them to remove it for new players. Like i'm still fairly early in the game but thanks to them showing me the future for no reason i now know who not to care about.2.The constant loadings,Finish a battle then load into the world map,to then load into a cut scene then after that section is done loading get ready to load back into another cut scene. It breaks all fluidity to the story telling.Speaking of ruining the fluidity.3.Forcing me to watch my units gain exp after each hit they land/take,Ruins the whole flow of combat & that's saying something due it being a turned based game(yes you can skip it but it overall shouldn't needed & the exp can be allocated at the end of the battle the same way). It would of been much better to allocate the exp after the battle.4.The background armies are using the same armor,So i have no idea who i'm rooting for. Yeah they are just background art but it does matter for immersion. Simple fix would be to main their coats white & black. Black for the empire & white for the rebels or some simple color differential. Yeah it so jarring, like i'm invested but when i see two sides fight in a mosh pit in a cut scene again i have no idea who i'm rooting for.5.The faces do not express emotion which hurts the voice acting. Example someone delivering their lines with passionate rage with but the face of the speaker is emotionless,Like that could work in a less serious title but this game wants you to take it seriously with it's story telling.They should of made helmets or face wear toggle able for people who don't want to see their faces.6.I hate partial voice acting,Either do one or the other. It is always an annoyance.7.The cost of leadership to talk to someone(15pts) feels off due to the amount of rapport you are rewarded with compared to giving a gift(5pts) which talking gives out the same as a basic gift even though it cost more.8.Has bugs,Granted i'm over 20hrs in on this game & now i'm starting to run into some bugs,Worse one being after loading into camp after taking the shield of empire i was unable to move or use any feature.I had to forcefully close it.9.There was a scene that made no dam sense,ok so your original group have been friends since childhood right(doesn't make sense that they start off as peers but not the point)so  with that content how tf are they just going to stand there & do nothing when one of their life long friends might be killed.10.Trying excuse the girl for leaving us to "die" by saying she's strong willed. Idk why they are trying to excuse her behavior "T_T daddy said i was a bad girl, i'll let him die" So far this has been one of the two writing points i've had issues with in this story. No what she did because she was in her ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ feelings is insubordination & borderline treasonous, the BARE minimum would of been to strip her of rank & have her on a tight leash.11.No helmets for your units,I did have it minor con section but after thinking about it more i decided to move it to the con section.Due to the fact that helmets & face wear would of offset the dead faces the characters have.I understand that not having helmets for your characters make them more recognizable but as i said in cases like this were the faces express no emotions helmets & face wear should be a default feature with them coming off during cs or at camp.12.The world detail for the most part looks nice but it can be ruined during cut scenes where it takes place next to barely polished terrain that can sticks out.Minor Cons1.The character models in the in game cut scenes are pretty basic,Reminds me of kings bounty 2 models.2.Your mercenary group starting off as peers for rapport but most of them have been friends you with since childhood, i'm just saying they should start off at close ally.3.Game catfishing  a cut scene it showed the mc riding a white horse with armor,awhile ago & i still have not got that horse : l gimmie the horse & it's armor. Scams,deceitful heresy.Also a cape was shown in the cut scene so naturally i want that for my character. Thoughts I would like these devs to go more of a fantasy route for their next game, Orcs,dwarves,elves,ogres & w/e else they want to toss in. This game is the foundation & i'm curios to see where they go next.If they didn't feel like doing another turned base game i would be more than fine with something like ninety nine nights 1 or a smaller scale of kingdom under fire crusade/heroes.Honestly if this games devs & the dev team of spellforce conquest were to do a colab,It would probably be one of the better turned based games in years due to losts story direction & combat animations while conquests would bring unit race diversity that look pretty good.(not just humans with different skin tones,I'm talking about real diversity) & world detail. Lost world detail isn't bad but it can be during cut scenes with it looking pretty bad.

_childDocuments_.review: I finished the game, which is saying something. Unlike a lot of games, it did manage to hold my attention until the end. I was enjoying the story, but expected more to be revealed. There is quite a lot that is never explained. The end was disappointing, and was possibly the result of a bug? The rapport system is a major part of the game, but the ending I got seemed to have nothing at all to do with my relationships? I feel like I spent all that time building rapport for absolutely nothing. The voice acting was great, but the game is NOT fully voiced and the parts where it's missing is just awkward as all hell. The first time I saw it I thought the game was bugging out. The graphics are nice, but the animation was pretty bad, especially the mouths when people are talking.Overall I feel like this game could have been great, but they ran out of time and money and shipped it before it was ready.

_childDocuments_.review: For a first project, this is almost insane. Reminds me of old Fire Emblem where you can't just run in with your brain off. Doesn't have that sort of budget behind it but the reach to go beyond a basic game is there, you can really tell they cared about making this through gameplay and I'd love to see what they can do for a sequel. There's also a very generous rewind system if you overlook something. Rewinding two turns with knowledge and then perfecting them is insanely satisfying.Dev team is also very active and addressing almost every complaint (turn limit hasn't bothered me like others, each map has been completed with half the turns still remaining). If you like Fire Emblem support this team. We need more of this and less soulless cash grabs.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Eidolons

_childDocuments_.review: Don't expect a Fire Emblem game and you will enjoy the game much much more. Good voice acting with pretty nice aesthetic. The writing is a bit weird though. The story as a whole has potential but the execution is unfortunately quite a mess. New locations keep getting introduced into the game every battle with little to no real world building. Characters's writing is decent but I wish there were more to them. Soundtracks are quite forgettable except for a few. The combat can be very challenging but also very doable. I managed to finish the game on hard + maniac mode with everyone alive at the end despite not playing optimally. The escape maps are some of my favorites. Character progression is okay but I do wish there were more variety. Give it a try. Can't hurt to support small indie devs with clear passion and love for the game while also being brave enough to try out new things to elevate the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Eidolons

_childDocuments_.review: The games OK. Its a decent all be-it halfbaked fire emblem experience. you get camp sequences where you build bonds with allies, and subsequently recruit new ones. Several menu screens worth of information from equipment, to spell book, stat sheet and etc.The story is still images with 3D representations of the characters speak overtop it, dialogue in English is okay, characters feel and represent themselves like youd imagine know nothing farmers would. Combat has some unique mechanics for large enemy's, skills you can trigger per character and with they're attached "army" as well. Thats about where it stops scratching the fire emblem itch.The overall story is pretty lackluster and i skip every cut-scene most of the time if not to get some context about my missions. Playing on harder difficulty settings at least "maniac" or "ironman" mode is a NO-GO! Id suggest normal is the "correct" way to play the game without ripping out your hair and still enjoying the game. Even then the game has a RE-WIND feature per every level that allows you to turn back the clock and try out new variables so that helps.Im on chapter 11 or so now, and you slowly and steadily unlock new features around camp and etc. But to this point i have been behind the curve for every enemy ive faced in any mission. Every enemy is either on par with any unit of the same type from your own OR BETTER than what you have access to (hard mode). There is no meaningful equipment ive been able to buy or get access to yet that really feels like it made any difference. Sure you get some rares here and there from chests but they do all of maybe +1 attack in x scenario. Point and case, if you want a decently fire-emblem like experience you can try this if all you want is the camp stuff and turn based combat. Beyond that nothing about this game is exceptional, or even stands out amidst this genre overall. Id only say, playing on normal will more than likely lead to better appreciation of the game.
