_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game as a Fire Emblem inspired tactics. My Initial impressions of the game were on the whole positive, but gradually soured as the game progressed through the second half. Ultimately, I would say pass on this game and hope the experiences learned in development/post launch  makes a superior future product.To briefly explain what bothered my about the combat, it essentially boiled down to how they tried to improve or iterate on the Fire Emblem, but then proceeded to abuse the advantages they gave the AI to punish you. Basically, playing Lost Eidolons is like a game of Chess where your opponent's Queen and King can't be captured until all the pawns are dead and your opponent is allowed to replace the Rooks, Bishops and Knights once per battle, placing them wherever they want on the board. The Invincible commanders as a solution to stop you just rushing them was a neat idea in the early game, but in Part II the level designers abused this. Invincible commanders will regularly spawn within 5 tiles of you, be immune to many crowd control effects, and attack you with a vengeance. Combine this with a lack of mobility owning to limited horse availability (1 or 2 for most of the game with 4 in the last couple chapters), and I felt the only way to play the game was to spam the (overpowered compared to the rest of the army) Sharpshooter archers. They were the only way to peg the aoe magic attacking pawns with healing spells hiding behind the invincible commander ripping you to shreds. As for the story, I will say it was a C+. As for how these games go, I liked the characters/units  but the plot was so-so. It felt like the story writer had the first 3 seasons of Game of Thrones explained to them by their younger brother. There was some compelling intrigue in Part I, but it's quickly dropped and forgotten about. The main open questions towards the end were still hanging out there for me. I could infer answers but that felt unsatisfying. That said, in terms of story, better than Fire Emblem: Engage, but also more forgettable. Finally, if you do purchase the game I recommend some sort of guide or warning for miss-able items as the game hides a fair bit of the good equipment behind performing actions that only make sense in hindsight.

_childDocuments_.review: Only a little bit in  (waiting on customization on class upgrades) but so far its pretty good. The combat zoom in attack is VERY reminiscent of Fire emblem.  Everyone gets a backup bow a couple missions in for ranged, and spells work well.  And you get a turn return option too to help with errors. EDIT -- more a middle thumb after more playing.That extra turn return is essential, because you will need it with incorrect indicators.  Enemy 'prediction attacks' where it tells you who will hit who, shows moreso who the enemy thinks it will hit for the most, prefering a killing blow.  It is also updated after every attack.  So, when its deciding predictions, archer will say I cant kill anyone, ill hurt the mage the most, and does the line indicator.  Turn begins his ally hits someone and suddenly the archer can kill your hurt unit now, changes and kills him.  The turn prediction IS BAD.  Straight up bugged for archers ontop of ramparts as it doesnt show movement when they get down.  Clicked one, shows my unit is safe.  start next round, he climbs down and shoots him.  Clicking on the unit to see his movement did not show any available movement below.A few sticklers for me, defend doesnt seem to do much.  I think I defended and took 1 dmg less (still 9-11?) which is still getting 2 shot (hard difficulty).  Its kinda weird both units try to attack both times in melee combat,  I land first blow, we both swing, they land second.  Its just odd that we both try both times.I felt I had to leave a review because of 'mixed' on account of combat turns... The first couple at least (i think im on mission 4) the turn limit is seriously 20 turns... I beat them in less than 10.  So no, the turn limit isnt some X-com bomb in 5 turns crap, no you have plenty of time to do it and the timer is viewed more as incentive (more exp bonus) than a hindrance for me.That aside the writing is iffy.  The bantering feels off, the plot points dont quit follow for me.  Examples of missions 3 and below ahead. After some more playing I got to the beasts which in a review was praised.  This game seems to have hard ripped from FE 3 houses.  The monsters a are similar to those, use a wep on a specific monster for good dmg and no counterattack, except it has a combo.  Combo resets with non-critical wep hit.  Except the enemy turns to face whoever hit it last and the special hit tiles are 2/4 not all of them.  Sooo depending on position it can be  a pain.  The turn rewind, also ripped straight from FE3 houses.

_childDocuments_.review: Hello!I essentially never do reviews but this game is great so here we are. Let's start with the team at Ocean Drive studios. They hosted several community live streams during development of this game and each and every one of them was informative, interactive, and very helpful in showing what would be on offer at release. They have been passionate and driven towards the success of this game and supporting the community with a product we can all enjoy, quite frankly it has been very impressive.Now to address common negatives. Essentially every negative review I've seen has been misaligned expectations and people who struggle with turn based tactics games. I do agree that there shouldn't be "hard" turn limits on battles where speed isn't required, at the same time the amount of turns they give you are FAR MORE than enough. Also they are just that, a turn. You choose when and how to take it, also when to end it, and you even get an undo option. If you find yourself struggling, i suggest taking more time to think about your next move. (They have also said the current turn limits will be adjusted in the short term and eventually removed in a dev post).This is not a AAA game studio, this is a small team of dedicated people making games in a style they love for a community interested in those games. Do not expect a 90 hour Square Enix title here (SE's more recent titles could use some work anyway). There is a deep story, a cast of characters you get to learn about and grow with, lore sprinkled in books and findables throughout the game if you're looking for extra, surprising encounters and some nifty twists. Come into this with the right expectations. If you're a fan of tactics titles then you'll feel right at home with this. There is a lot to love about this game, it's a wonderful entry in the genre and I'm very excited to see more from this studio. Thanks for all the hard work, Ocean Drive! Good luck to everyone in their journey through Artemesia!

_childDocuments_.review: I was hoping this would be something like Fire Emblem for PC or maybe FF Tactics with modern graphics.  This game seems to have a decent enough foundation, but needed LOTS more time to be polished up, and refined.I barely got out of the tutorial section of the campaign before the issues became apparent. I requested a refund, but got denied because I made the mistake of trying to tough through the issues past the 2 hour mark, to see if the game would pick up steam...I first tried the campaign on HARD mode, but didn't manage to get past the second combat scenario. Even using the game's UNDO mechanic to rewind out of bad positioning and sub-optimal turns, I wasn't able to finish it without losing a character. Just a skill issue? Maybe. Maybe if I had spent a few more hours, I would have found the perfect series of turns that resulted in killing the enemy commander without losing a unit, but then that doesn't fill me with any hope that the game would improve.When the game punishes you THIS HARD, and THIS EARLY, without giving you the various tools to plan an attack, things like classes, equipment, formations, synergies, etc. I have no reason to believe it would somehow become easier when I'm able to tweak all these things to get the most out of my team.Part of why combat is so difficult, even on normal difficulty, is that your character can't move past an enemy character, which they call zone of control or "ZOC". In theory, this is good because it's more realistic, and makes positioning of units even more important. In practice, this is a terrible idea, especially when coupled with the maps in this game that have multiple obstacles and thickets everywhere, traversing the battlefield becomes such a chore that you feel exhausted just closing the gap to engage the enemy.Points 1 & 2 are terrible design choices, in isolation, HOWEVER, consider this. Monsters in this game, just as in other similar games, are multi-tile units where a couple of the tiles are considered "weak points". That's fine enough, except that the weakness tiles are determined at random, AND the weakness (sword, axe, bow, magic) is also randomized. On top of this, you need to hit the same tile multiple times in a single round in order to break it and get a guaranteed crit, which is nearly impossible due to the positioning and movement issues mentioned above.Example: you need to kill a monster with about 4x HP of a typical enemy. It has two weakness tiles, front left (sword) and front right (spell). So you approach the monster, hit him with a spell on the spell tile, hit him with a sword on the sword tile. Then you try to position another sword unit on the side to chain attack the sword tile, it works, AND THE MONSTER ROTATES, ruining all your attempts to position units to take advantage of the tiles. No problem, eventually, after attacking with a bunch of units, you end your turn... AND THE TILES SHUFFLE so you can start moving units again to match the right weapons with the right tiles. Except, all the units that are in melee range can't move because of the zone of control of the enemy. Oh yeah, and the tile types shuffle as well, so if you had a bunch of swords and spellcasters up close, too bad, you now need axes and archers to attack the new weaknesses.

_childDocuments_.review: I played ~12 hours during the beta test and I'm caught back up to where I got up to then. I'm still really enjoying the game and all the new things I hadn't seen during the test. I'm a fan of turn-based tactical games like Final Fantasy Tactics and the Fire Emblem series and this feels like it takes the best of the genre but also makes it its own. I like how I can use the environment to alter my strategy and change weapons without a turn penalty. It took a little bit for the story to take off, but now I'm invested in the main characters. And honestly I would do anything for Francisco.I'm impressed with the changes the developers made since the beta AND since launch to really take player feedback into account. The cutscenes are a welcome addition plus some other nice qualify of life fixes like the undo system for when I'm not paying attention and accidentally leave someone squishy in the line of fire. The devs are very transparent about the work they're doing and I would love to see what they could do with more resources. I would never have guessed this was their first game if I hadn't been following the progress. If you like turn-based strategy games, you should give this one a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Very entertaining SRPG. The obvious comparison is Fire Emblem and the game manages to have a similar level of addiction kicking in, based around the "FE Formula": Dialogues, base and troop management and combat. The start is a bit janky, especially during dialogues, when characters fade in and out and during the VN style scenes, plus some of the line transitions are a bit abrupt, but it improves once the game opens up with your own base and a wider story focus and more characters.Combat also gains a lot more complexity after the first few chapters, where the game is VERY easy and might even seem flat to the player. The ramp up could have probably been a bit faster for difficulty and mechanics, but once you unlock them it becomes pretty fun.On top of that character models are fairly impressive and better looking than in many higher budget titles and the map design/artstyle also keeps improving the further you get into the game.its a very solid first game for a small studio and a nice addition for SRPG fans. Can definately recomment it to people who enjoy games based on this style. 2022 has been a great year for these games.

_childDocuments_.review: When I first saw and got this game, I really wanted to like it. For a brief period, I did. It looked like a refreshing change to every other tactics game that saw Fire Emblem's success and copied it down to the pixel, changing location and character names to call their own title. The refined CG style was a real breath of fresh air. Character development and story seem solid so far. I really like the camp mechanic as a middle ground to improve character relations and get new units between battles. Now the combat that made and soon broke the game for me....Initially, I liked it. Loved the rewind factor, anyone who has played permadeath tactics games will appreciate rewinding a turn over restarting the battle on an oversight error. It especially felt like the creators like magic users with how well thought out magic was. Really like how they did the elemental magic mechanics between setting up the grimoires and environmental effects. Unfortunately, it did not take long to realize the makers HATE melee glass cannons from the one mechanic (or lack there of) that slowly, single-handedly ruined the game for me. To even have a stat called "Accuracy" is a sick joke since everyone has 100% accuracy. "Penetrating potential" would be more accurate since all it does is lower the chances that the enemy will block for mitigated damage. I understand that some games make broken crit/dodge swordmaster classes and I am assuming they were trying to avoid glass cannon sweeps with no damage. Rather than tweak balances, they lazily just took away dodging mechanic entirely, making the berzerker class worthless and turning the assassin class into a glorified errand boy that can collect treasures since they at least have decent mobility. It just felt like a tease to even have those classes on the tree. This turd mechanic essentially makes attack and defense by far the most useful stats and strong arms you into range/tank teams if you don't want to rage. On a side note, they do have a second game in the works so hopefully whoever made the awful "accuracy" call will get overruled and the next game will let you incorporate more variety into your teams.TLDR: If you like range and tanks with a fresh twist on magic and base mechanics, you are in for a blast like some other reviews have stated. If you prefer quick crit hitters that can dodge, keep looking because dodging doesn't exist so non tank melee units have no business in this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Prepare for a thorough review after having played through most of the game. *Keep in mind, I made this back in Feb.24th when I gave up on playing it due to a specific chapter so perhaps some updates were done since then, I just forgot to post it back then.I've played many tactics games such as advance wars, the legend of runersia, fire emblem, and even many obscure indie titles.  This game comes across as a fire emblem game using 3d models similar to the tellius games.Now for the major points:GAMEPLAY:After the initial tutorial you have your party of characters with various equipment.You have a "battle" taking turns(there is no turn order based on speed), you choose whoever to move on your turn.  There is an "undo" mechanic with a maximum of 10 uses if you want to back several turns(possibly more; explained later).Afterwards the enemy has their turn and does the same thing.You get increased rewards(usually just bonus experience awarded to allies for weapon types, and levels ), so the game seems to reward more aggressive play vs turtles.You go to your "base"(once unlocked) and this is where you can talk to party members, do side quests(once unlocked like many things in the base), purchase supplies, weapons, etc.And it just loops from there.Story-->fight-->base-->story-->fight-->base--->etc.MORE GAMEPLAY INFO:Characters: There is permadeath, there is even permadeath for story reasons on specific characters if you play on "normal" with no permadeath(if you want to know who see spoilers at the end)Weapons info: Melee weapons are Sword, axe, and lanceranged weapons are bows and tomes(elemental magic, dark magic, and light magic)^--You want to have at least 1 of your maximum of 8 characters with at least one of each. The reason for this is because occasionally you run into "large monsters" and they have weaknesses from specific directions based on a specific weapon type. So a monster may only be weak to bows and tomes one turn, then the next turn it swaps to all melee only.Weapons also break down into "tiers". common, rare, and I believe legendary(but this has 2 categories itself with "unique" being orange/gold text color acquired through special means).As far as I know, only "three" unique legendary weapons are obtainable just playing the story and that is a lance, sword, and dark tome(in that order).Armor info: It's really just the base type for your class such as leather for berserkers/archer, plate for knights, and cloth for wizards.  These also separate into "tiers", but I've yet to see a "unique" legendary armor(not sure if it exists).There are also "trinkets/accessories", but these are extremely rare and somewhat underwhelming providing extremely minor bonuses. At ch.19 only have 5.I believe only one seems valuable providing defense and bonus guard(chance to reduce damage in combat), but I got it late into the game. If you had to put one someone, I recommend those engaged in combat more.Items info: Each character carries a max of 3. Consumables that give stat boosts never seemed worth it as they last 2 turns and healing is extremely limited(explained after mounts). The last thing you want to do is have to avoid using a strong character stuck at 20hp because you ran out of potions and healing.**And no you can't trade items while in a map unfortunately, so filling up with healing potions is even more recommended.When trading any item/equipment between allies in a base, however, you automatically unequip the 2nd party member(the game doesn't autofill it with what you traded for theirs), so be sure to reequip them...Mounts info:Talk regularly and be close with Robin the archer who starts in your party. I did it by chance, but apparently he will give you I believe a max of 4 mounts while in your base, use them well. I had 2 for most of the game, 1 for a healer and 1 for the main tank. Got 3rd somewhat late into the game.Healing in this game: (In its own category due to how it works.)For magic you have a limited number of spells you can choose to use combining crowd control, buffs, debuffs, damage, and healing(light magic only).For healing each "spell" such as healing touch has a limited number of uses. Once you run out that's it! I'm surprised there's no item to restore these or a mechanic such as a crit(can healing even crit? I don't think it can. Never did for me.) that prevents one charge from being consumed.Crowd control: Dark mages are the only ones who can put bosses to sleep or silence their pocket healers. I recommend at least one. 2 makes boss fights significantly easier *as bosses when surrounded by allies take much less damage.Recruiting characters: Recruited in base only by talking reaching "acquaintance" tier 2 bond level. If you fail to reach that point in 2 chapters they usually leave the base and return much later(possibly making them essentially unusuable if they keep the same level).Raise the bond by using somewhat rare "consumable items to give "bond points".**most bonus recruit characters just became "unusuable partners" for combat map characters, so you may wanna try to recruit them for bonuses in combat.*only 2? so far can be "missed if killed in combat" which is why the 2 dark mages I had were so useful.My party that got me through every map was essentially the following:Main character(melee sword/bow), 2 other melee(one sword/axe other spear/axe), 1 archer, 2 dark mages(both with silence/sleep), 2 elemental mages, and 2 healers.STORY:	 It is text heavy, there were times where it felt excessive or unnecessarily long; at one point I had to go to the restroom after completing a fight and when I got back(forgot to pause) it was still showing more cutscenes/story after 8+ minutes had passed?). 	Personally I feel you will either find it interesting or not. The story itself is based on a group of mercenaries that are caught into something much bigger involving the entire nation they reside in and you take control of their "leader" who is the protagonist (no you cannot edit him at all other than giving him a specific class change to unlock unique "outfits" as long as you remain that class).MUSIC:It simply exists. I think only one song was somewhat enjoyable one of the base songs after something happened story wise, but I can't remember when. Other than that, you will probably barely notice it.SPOILERS:Only boss that made me use all undos was the snakes/behemoth in ch.15Main reason is unlike previous chapters the game doesn't teach you anything about how to combat them. You're just expected to figure it out which is what I did with the undos. The behemoth in particular had significantly high hitpoints.  And use your special on the behemoth before it dies for a unique legendary weapon.The snakes basically target an ally and once they're targeted they will guaranteed be removed from the fight next turn as they are "eaten" and released when the snake dies.They also can remove multiple party members adjacent to their original target. They all take damage while inside the "snake".Both the snake and the behemoth heal hitpoints as well(when behemoth is on grass?) and after eating someone(snake)/someone inside them?You also take massive damage from the snake eating someone or the behemoth ramming into you.**allies that die story wise-unavoidable-->Leon; if you wanna know more check the guides as I played blind have fun!I recommend this game after they fix with most if not all of the changes I suggest/explain. See below.*THE BAD*I created a topic in the feedback/discussion of this game where I layout every flaw of thisgame I could possibly think of that should change.I just ran out of space on this review!  Go check it out if you're interested!

_childDocuments_.review: One of the better indie strategy turn based RPGs I've played. Having been a backer since the beginning, I'm glad to see that the game has come this far.Combat is a mix between a few tactics games (Fire Emblem being the main inspiration of course, though this game pays more tribute to Shadows of Valentia than to the more recent Three Houses). Unlike in Fire emblem, however, there's no dodge stat as far as I can tell, and there isn't any sign of doubling, at least at the point in the game I'm currently at, so the combat is less RNG and more strategy, which is quite welcoming (though you can still get crit, wouldn't be a tactics game without the AI critting you while your units can't crit lol). As for the turn limit currently in place, I haven't had issues yet, and I prefer to clear the map as efficiently and quickly as possible (I'm doing Hard/Maniac and it seems fine still). 9.5/10I've seen some people say the voice acting/writing is below average. Personally, I've never heard any of these VAs, but they do fit the characters they're voicing. Writing isn't all that bad either (serviceable as of my current playtime, definitely has potential to be better). The one real gripe that some people have when they watch me play is how conversations are carried out at times (you would see one person talking, then they'd disappear and then the next person shows up. 8/10.In terms of the graphics/animations: graphically, the game looks good. Some of the animations can be a bit funny, kinda reminds me of Remnant: From the Ashes mouth movement sometimes, but not as bad. 7.5/10.As for the developers themselves: they have a discord, and they frequently discuss topics with the community, as well as listen to the user feedback, as shown in their most recent letter after the day 1 launch. Communication is something that I wish game companies did more of, despite it being a good standard to go by; props to Ocean Drive Studios for that. Overall, a solid buy.

_childDocuments_.review: Lost Eidolons is a turn-based tactical RPG, with a heavy dosis of dialogues and a bit of inventory management. It's reminiscent of games like the Shining Force and the Fire Emblem franchises, with a touch of Dragon Age. It's clearly designed as a hard game with permadeath, though both hard difficulty and permadeath can be shut off to have a more casual feel.It's not a bad game, it delivers what it pretends and there are enough people who like it for what it is, but I just happen to hate it. For me it's just a horrendously tedious... ah... not-a-game. Too many things reminded me right from the beginning of what I don't like in most japanese whateverRPG: - characters from a class do just look the same, they wear some kind of "uniform" equipment, giving the feeling that the characters are some fussing schoolboys and girls or cadets;- no hero does wear an helmet (they probably don't want to damage their haircut I guess), although the head is usually one of the easiest spot to hit. Ok I know, it's like that in most fiction stuff, whatever the origin, still can't bear it;- the plot seemed right away and by far too manicheist, and the nice people are overly and artificially nice, like it was some educational piece of work. And it keeps being so, though the main character can go toward a less tamed direction;- the introduction is ridiculously... ah... naive? Childish? Spineless? Fortunately it gets better afterward, which is why I continued to play after the first hour. But still... it proved spineless in another way. You can't be a leader if your goal is to be both nosy and everybody's best friend.Then, there was a tremendous lot of dialogues. I never was much interested in too much text in video games. I read enough books for fun. But it was ok. Until after 20 or 30 hours of game. Then I was fed up. And hit either space or esc almost constantly until near the end. Except with one or two characters who seemed a bit less to come directly out of a kindergarten.The combats themselves seemed a bit void at first. And unfortunately didn't come much more interesting. Monster hunting is fun, but else... It's Fire Emblem, except the levels aren't pleasing to look at. You cannot advance without being constantly on the defensive. I loved that kind of play when I was a kid. I hated it after teenagehood, when I began to play more on the offensive. You cannot really create opportunities in combats, you must simply mitigate the damage you receive. And most fights are for this reason, or the level design, simply tedious.The very last fight is the worst. It makes sense regarding the plot, but it's just uselessly tedious. I might have beaten the game, understanding what a team I should have put on the field to defeat the final boss, but I just didn't want to lose more time reaching him: no challenge until him and artificially too long. And that's the whole problem with this game: it was rendered long by forcing the player to play in a very specific way. It's not a game for me, it's a chore. But yes, it's partly at least a matter of taste.Ah, I almost forgot... I tried from the very beginning to have a romance with a somewhat obnoxious female character by default, as all the other female characters seemed either to wanting to be my mom or to having some monomaniac issue. After completing the peerness scale to max with her and giving her a specific item to get the last dialogue with her... I happened to propose romancing another character in the final flirting scene. One the few bugs I met, but a very frustrating one, since it was my last objective (well, except finishing the game).

_childDocuments_.review: Lost Eidolons is very heavily inspired by Fire Emblem. If you've played any of the recent FE titles, you'll be familiar with how this game plays. _childDocuments_.review: I found the writing extremly boring. Have you ever gone back to your cherished childhood books, like the Hardy Boys, and realized it was grossly simplified dialogue and (as an older reader) you read all 200 pages, every single word, in less than an hour? This story feels similar, like it is targeting a 3rd-grade reading level. And there's nothing wrong with games made for youth, i just wish there had been a warning label.While I couldn't quit the game fast enough, i have a few more scamples: 1) After single 1 minute encounter, which came after 5 minutes of bad dialogue, and that was the end of chapter 1. That does not bode well for game length or complexity. 2) the voice actors are awkwardly over the top, the intro done by an edgelord describing a budding empire. 3) during the dialogue, the speaker flashes on the screen, and then there's brief pause before the next speaker flashes on screen and says their bit. So not only are you mentally 10 sentences ahead of the characters waiting for it to end, it feels like 2 or more AI trying to have a conversation with each other  (you know those chat programs). Frankly, if the conversation WAS procedurally generated and voiced, I'd be extremely impressed. I still wouldn't play the game though, and I didn't even get the point of dealing with the combat turn limits other comments refer to.If you have someone in the household under the age of 10 and you want to introduce them to RPGs, then this could potentially be a good buy. But i'll be seeking a refund.

_childDocuments_.review: The time spent playing within the refund window made a lot of bad impressions. I usually give a game around 2 hours to really "sell" me on it, and LE had a couple things that I consider red flags in this kind of game.The biggest is reinforcements. The third, or fourth mission already has enemies spawn in within threat range of your partially spent troops. When the game is balanced around the idea that there is permadeath, this sort of thing is terrible. It's one of my biggest pet peeves about the Fire Emblem series as well. You either play on Casual, which makes the game too easy since unit death matters profoundly less, or you play on permadeath, and have to deal with random reinforcements, crits or guards leading to a restart.Speaking of which, random crits on attack or defense are another big problem that tactical games should do away with, doubly so if they want you to play with characters permanently dying if they go down. This too has been solved by other games already, like making criticals only happen during specific conditions so that the player has a modicum of control over it.My other core issue is the story, and pacing. This is more of a personal topic and might not at all apply to you. The writing is neither bad nor good, just sort of there. The intro drags too much and does the thing where they show you a flash forward that doesn't really add anything to proceedings except being confusing. The whole "Good guy rebellion versus generically evil empire" thing has been done to death and there needs to be something more for me to care about it at all.Pacing wise, LE does the thing that games like this usually do, where gameplay and story are seperate things happening in bursts. As I said, the writing isn't nearly good enough to make me want to run around a campsite for half an hour between every mission, to exhaust all the dialogue.If you want your tactics fix, I think somewhat recent release Symphony of War does a much better job of frontloading its strengths and is a lot less boring in the in between mission parts. The writing isn't much better, but it insists less on you spending time with it.

_childDocuments_.review: I REALLY wanted to like this game. I love Fire Emblem, I loved Triangle Strategy...but there are SO MANY design decisions that waste my time. I ultimately gave up on Chapter 23 because of the most stupid, slap-in-the-face design I have ever encountered in a strategy game. But let me do a broader overview first:Bad:1) The skill trees have ZERO effect on gameplay. Okay, archers can shoot one square further. Big whoop. Still takes 4 turns to kill an enemy, even playing on easy.2) I notice NO difference based on what weapons I have equipped. Magic is the only place where stronger skills have any impact.3) The Boss design. OMFG, the boss design is so ridiculous. You can't deal any meaningful damage until all the ADs are killed. But in some maps there are like 6 bosses coming at you. You end up surrounded by bosses, unable to harm them, because all of their ADs are behind them.4) Chapter 23 - this is what broke me - I love the idea of escorting a unit. it's tricky, play carefully, sure. But then at the LAST MOMENT, the escape zone gets blocked by 6, SIX, enemies. That's like another 8 turns, just to clear the escape zone. No, no no no, that is the last bit of time I give to this game. I have other things I want to play. I did my best to get to the end, already knowing that the final boss has 3 health bars. I wanted to give it a far chance, but I'd much rather go play Fire Emblem than give any more of my time to this. Sorry, Ocean Drive, it turned into a letdown through really dumb design. I never felt powerful, I didn't feel like the game honored my time. It devolved into menus, tedium, and terribly written dialogue. I don't care about the characters, their plight, and, in my case, Eden's story ends with him dead in a baby carriage--which frankly, he deserves. He's a wiener.I regret Kickstarting this. I should have waited to see what the result was before giving away my money.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to like this game but it does everything to make you not like it.It has potential. It has interesting ideas. The problem is imagine someone made a game and presented it to you but they cut holes in the middle of every cutscene or plot idea so you play through the cutscene or plot but a big chunk is clearly missing. Animations are awkward in cutscenes. Character dialogue is awkward and forced in some segments, some characters feel poorly developed and just remain the same. The Protagonists and their crew are very one note and barely change nor are they challenged much beyond a very predictable struggle.Combat is a Slog. Turn system is fine but often your able to easily clang your units into the enemy formation. The In between of moving everyone around can feel dull, and I do wish there was more meaningful dialogue mid battle and between the character cast in the cutscenes their in. The Intro is very poor right before chapter 1, your dumped into a no context battle that just spoils a later part of the game lol for no reason theres no dream no vision nothing your just there.The Class system I liked, I wanted to like this game but its just so uninteresting. You get punished for playing it. You try to like the characters and theres holes upon holes in the cutscenes or awkward janky dialogue that someone really should have trimmed through and fleshed out. I'd much rather a long character developing cutscene than short awkward ones that I question why their even there. This game tries to be fire emblem also, and if it just stopped trying to be Fire Emblem I think it would have been vastly superior. The game greatly takes inspiration from Fire Emblem 3 Houses, and imitates as many of its mechanics as it can. Resulting in a very poor imitation of each one.  If Lost Eidolons defined its own mechanics more strongly and ignored imitating Fire Emblem more I think this would be a solid 8/10 game if it had much more polish too.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to like this game. Die hard Fire Emblem fan and without Fire Emblem on PC, I'm taking whatever I can get.So why the bad review?Well I would say this game has cripplingly poor optimization that just bricks my GPU even though I'm well over spec for it. Not to mention how dated the graphics are (early PS3 to late PS2 era) you would think running it will be no problems.From memory leak to GPU crashes, idk how it's so poorly optimized.Other than that my biggest complaint with the story atm (getting into the mid game) is how on top of being generic JRPG tropes most characters are, the problem is their personality don't pop and thus are forgettable.This compounds the issue when most story beats outside of cutscenes are largely talking heads animation. And they decide to add camp dialogue like Dragonage / recent fire emblem games but because of that the problem really shows and the story really drags that they add fast travel to each character in the map. It's like they're aware of the problem later on well into end stage development2nd biggest gripe is the customization for classes imo isn't deep enough and there are only a couple of really standout classes: Light / White mage, Knight Tanks, and Archers. Knights and White mages being core of any team and Archers being close 3rd. You can skip Mages and Fighters/Melee DPS.This is sad and egregious and really show when you do some of the "siege" battles where you stand around to break a gate/object only to be smacked repeatedly by enemy archers with no other strategic depth. which only to highly how important your Tanks and Archers are.Other than that, the game is challenging reminiscence of old fire emblem except it's due to in large part because of ramp up enemy stat and lack of player tools imo.This is a first game from an indie studio so i'll be more lenient on them but I hope they take this as valuable feedback on how they should go forward game design wise. I'll change the review to positive when they go about fixing the optimization issue

_childDocuments_.review: The TL;DR is if you like Tactical RPGs and you like Fire Emblem style TRPGs, then you will very likely enjoy this game, even at full cost.Lost Eidolons is essentially a FE game with trace elements from FFT. The FFT elements are limited to what actions you can take in battle, and the ability to take parts of one class, and combine them with other classes. Each class will have base abilities or passives, but you have 5 slots to work with when assigning abilities and passives from other classes. This helps give each unit a specific play style to work with. Almost every other aspect of the game is taken straight out of FE. Combat is done in turns. All of your units take action then all of the enemy units. There is somewhat of a Triangle approach with strengths and weaknesses, but with a slight twist that pits weapons vs armor types. The healing spells are basically identical to the FE repertoire, whereas the elemental and dark spells have a little more variety. The biggest change to magic here is that you select which spells are in your grimoire instead of using a consumable staff that eventually breaks down. You are still limited to how many times you can cast each spells (typically 2-5 times) but that limit is reset for each battle. Your gear is not consumable like in FE but upgrades can be found. These upgrades are typically slight, but meaningful. The truly impactful upgrades seem to be rare, but honestly even the base gear is serviceable when applied correctly. Healing items are very useful but in relatively short supply, so use them carefully. Your gold income is also very limited, as there is a limited amount of optional battles that you can partake in. Items found at the rare merchant will not stay there when she reappears.There is a support system (they call it rapport) that is ripped straight out of FE though it is significantly less cringe IMO. Again the bonuses are slight but meaningful. You are very limited in how many people you can build support with, and how high you can get with those people. Between battles there is a camp section in which allows you to build rapport with your selected allies. Rapport can be built by spending time or giving gifts. The biggest issue here is that it can be very difficult to figure out who likes what gifts best to make sure you don't waste them. This system is also used to recruit new allies. I'll be honest, recruiting this way feels very bad, as it takes some units a considerable amount of effort to recruit, which limits your ability to build rapport with your other units. You also do not even know if the new recruit will be better than someone you already have.The battles are well done with a steady increase in difficulty. Though I will say even playing on the hardest difficulty settings, the game is on the easier side of things. I am only at chapter 12 though, so this may change. The AI is pretty good, but it suffers from 2 things (or rather it is made easier because of 2 things). The first is it has the same problem that most FE games have. The enemy comes at you in waves. Provided you don't move too far ahead, you will only aggro a portion of the enemy forces. The game compensates for this by the last pull being almost twice the size of the earlier pulls. The second issue is that the game will tell you exactly which units will be attacked by whom. Or rather, it tells you what each enemy unit wants to do on their turn as the board currently lies. It does not take a genius to figure out what will actually happen with this information, and makes taking risks much less punishing, as you can essentially game the enemy AI. I really feel like there should be a difficulty option to turn this off as its nice for people new to the genre or those looking for a relaxed playthrough, but kind of puts a dampener on those looking for a challenge. There is also a rewind function. It works exactly the same as what can be found in Ogre Tactics: Let Us Cling Together.In regards to the gameplay loop, the game is pretty solid. The starting classes are a little lackluster, but they improve over time. The game has an adequate challenge rating. The AI is competent enough and works together. The map scenery is a little repetitive in looks, but the layouts present new challenges and strategies. The gear and rapport upgrades feel impactful. I'd give it a 7/10.The writing, however, is a little more shaky. It is definitely not the worst writing I've seen in a game. but I would say about half of it falls kinda flat, while that other half varies from acceptable to decent. But if you are a FE fan, then you are probably already use to this. I'd say its better than the average FE game in terms of writing and story. The story is fairly generic, but I will admit that the very generic elements are a bit deceiving when it comes to plot twists. The game definitely makes you think, "Ok, I've seen this a 100 times, X is definitely going to happen here." but Y happens instead. It is kinda like they know they used some very generic tropes, and use it to bait and switch, which is honestly refreshing. I can't say much more with out putting in huge spoilers. Most of the characters are at least fun, but there are a few that just come off as very obnoxious. This is made worse by the game wanting you to from a relationship with said obnoxious characters via side quests at camp time. Most of the dialogue is over the top with "default good guy speak" and brotherly love. It can be a bit much sometimes. Some of the dialogue is pretty good though, and there are characters worth getting to know. All in all, I'd give the story a 6/10 so far, the characters an average of 7/10, and the writing an average of 5/10.The thing I like most about this game is Francisco. The thing i hate most about this game is that Shift (the default go faster button in basically every computer game ever) makes you walk in camp. I really would love to know why anyone ever thought that was a good idea. Thankfully there is a quick travel system when in the camp.

_childDocuments_.review: Three days ago I recommend this if you enjoy strategy/turn-based games in the vein of Fire EmblemHowever... Chapter 20 on Hard/Maniac and I'm quite done. I quit.The developers tried and clearly put alot of heart into this, but I would not recommend this game to fans of the genre.It's by no means a terrible or bad game, it just is so average and has such a time commitment to it I'm burnt out.Funny enough, the turn limit people were angry about is the least of this games issue. It's pointless I agree, but I managed to finish every map with almost half my turns remaining.List of grievances:- Story length far exceeds what it needed too. 40 hours in and I have no clue how close I am to finishing.- Aiming for realistic characters and personalities means that none grab your attention, hovering between "acceptable" and boring.They needed a different artstyle all together for their characters, as facial expressions are practically non-existant and you are stuck with wooden dolls.- Camp interactions/relationships have no gameplay reward or substantial character growth.- Equipment lacks diversity. The difference between common, rare, and legendary is a few stat points and minor perks attached. The equipment mechanic should've been scraped.- Customizing, Formation setting, and Setting spells takes far longer than it needs as the UI is clunky and sometimes unresponsive.- Classes are in no way properly balanced and on harder difficulties you will be punished for using melee characters late game. Use primarily casters/range or you will suffer on higher difficulties.- Class progression is also terribly handled. There is a 20 level gap between intermediate and expert classes, over 11 chapters. During this, your growth caps and there is no substantial reward for having your characters master other classes.There is no way to unlock the last set of classes apart from reaching the chapter.- Cheese difficulty mechanics: Bosses are nearly impervious to damage if any common enemies are around and charge you alongside them. Monsters need to be chained attack by specific weapon types on specific portions of their body in order to be defeated. Their resistance resets every turn, with a different weapon type required.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me preface this by saying that, if you like Fire Emblem, the game is still worth a buy if you find it for 50% off or more. That said, this game has some glaring problems. The gameplay concepts are actually unique in theory especially as a way to separate itself from Fire Emblem, but the weapon/armor interactions that are meant to replace Fire Emblem's weapon triangle largely carry a superfluous effect on combat (At most you might be able to squeeze like 4 points of damage out of exploiting these interactions if you're lucky and even then that's usually not enough to make a big difference). However, as a Fire Emblem clone, I can usually overlook something like that but what I CAN'T overlook is the story. Simply put, the story is so enamored with the relationship between its main hero and villain that it leaves enough holes with the story and worldbuilding to make swiss cheese jealous. To name just a few:And those are just the three biggest ones I can think of. There are other ones like  that MIGHT be explored in a potential sequel, but the narrative seems to make no indication that there will be a sequel. Even if there is a sequel, though, there's a very unfortunate chance that it will end up like Fire Emblem: Radiant Dawn and be a meandering mess that does little more than resolve remaining plot threads in a very dissatisfactory way.

_childDocuments_.review: This game looks like a good game - but in the end it plays terribly. It's not a "RPG" it's a VN with flat, turn-based combat sprinkled over it. All the conversations are just so tedious. The story is nothing to write home about, at least the first 4-5 hours. I couldn't bring myself to play longer. Character progression is close to non existant. There are 3 base-classes: Squire, Fighter and Mage. And that's it. But you don't get to choose the sub-classes - the game does it for you. So "Eden" the main Character has NO option but to become a Squire. How is this a RPG?Then the combat itself is super flat. The battlefield is squares, like you know from XCOM - but there is NO elevation. Everything is flat. NO highground advantage for ranged Attackers, no defense increase against range-attacks when being in cover. Yeah there is the "element" angle, like if you make it rain, the ground gets wet, if you cast an icespell you get frozen. But it's all so shallow. There is absolutely no depth to it whatsoever.The "cutscenes" are animated decently and the game looks good. But it doesn't take away from the sloggish flow of the game from the beginning and still going on 4.5 hours deep. No choices for the character to take, no way to customize your characters, no RPG. This is a VN with a flat turn-based combat system on top. Stay away if you want a RPG with deep TBC.

_childDocuments_.review: I find it hard to believe anyone is okay with the insane loading times on this game. There's all these tedious conversations that could do double-duty as loading time, but instead you have to endure (or skip) the tedious conversation *then* the incredible obnoxious loading time. I apparently have "played" the game for 1.9 hours, and I think maybe 5 minutes of that was getting to play the actual game, perhaps as much as 10 minutes if you include wandering around camp for mandatory conversations as playing. The first time one of the long loading times occurred I almost exited the game thinking it had got stuck (the loading spinner was spinning, but it didn't seem like it was ever going to stop).If you like this genre of game and aren't for some reason in love with "realistic" graphics, Dark Deity is so much better that I wouldn't even recommend playing it before this one, I would recommend playing it instead and not bothering with this one. I guess if you really aggressively hate anime-style graphics then that could be a justification for preferring Lost Eidolons, but honestly I'd rather play a game of this genre with original Nethack-style ASCII "graphics" than endure the endless waiting for the promise of maybe someday getting to do a battle that Lost Eidolons offers.As far as I can tell (from 3 battles) the gameplay doesn't even really have anything interesting to offer, and it didn't seem like it was going to get significantly more interesting. Dark Deity does the leveling/progression aspect better too.

_childDocuments_.review: (h1)This is recommended on the basis you purchase this game on SALE(/h1)Overall Score 7/10Lost Eidolons is a game that you will enjoy if you are a fan of turn based RPGs, after over 60 hours I can say i'm glad I picked it up but its not one that will leave a lasting imprint on my memory.The Good:- Excellent value for money (in sale) with a lengthy campaign to sink your teeth into- The turn based battles, animation and choices for party development are very good- The difficulty spike shortly after the mid-point of the game is a welcome shift of dynamic and certainly helps with retaining engagement though this does level out again toward the end- Medieval aesthetic is awesome and the game can run without issue even on a very basic buildThe Neutral:- Good sound track which helps with the longer battles and voice acting is okay though hamstrung by the poor script- Mission variety is decent but of the 27 chapters too many are similar/repetitive and it becomes tiresome defeating the same enemy generals over and again- Spoilers exist in the trailer...- Camp features are good though a little too limitedThe Bad:- The shoehorned dialogue and story is something you just need to accept as a budget issue, it doesn't really make any sense - Non existant tutorials which is a problem for any players not used to the genre- Story 'choices' have no correlation with the end 'results,' this seems to be a common theme with player feedback and it devalues the investment of putting time into progressing character relationships- Opening chapters will put a lot of people off as its very clear this is a game made on a shoestring budget, that said if you can see past it and stick with it, it does get betterSummary:A great find if you're looking to scratch an itch for a Turn-Based strategy game and for fans of the genre but still one to pick up on sale.  You'll not be remotely interested in the story they are trying to tell here but there is a gem underneath the rough edges.  The game could have been excellent, however it sits just at the range of 'above average'.Decent, hopefully future games are better.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: This cheap imitation of 3 Houses quickly becomes a terrible slog of nearly identical battles with nothing to look forward to. Don't make my mistake of thinking the game might get better - it doesn't. Do not buy.Pros:- Good voice acting- Undo feature is very nice to have- Many difficulty options, more than most turn based strategy games allowCons:- Camp quickly becomes tedious with busywork and fetch quests. This is the #1 issue right now that's absolutely ruining the game for me. I don't want to skip all the optional recruited characters, dialogue and rewards, but it literally takes almost an hour of busywork between chapters now and I dread it so much I don't want to play anymore.- #2 issue is that your characters begin to max out their combat skills around chapter 8-9 with no incentive to swap classes (they'll be weaker and therefore ineffective in combat). But you can't access better classes until chapter 17. So you have nothing to work towards.- Too many early/mid game battles are too similar: ram the gates and attack humans that take 2 hits to kill, over and over and over...- Sound is EXTREMELY quiet even with game volume and speakers turned up all the way. This problem is unique to this game only.- Uninspired sound design- It's difficult to distinguish between all the similar-looking white male characters in combat and it's very hard to distinguish between similar-looking icons (heavy/leather especially). I wish a different style or approach had been taken here.- Related to previous point, the game uses a very limited color palette which creates a drab look, especially in camp where it's so dark. Yet another reason to go with another art style.- Subtitle size can be increased, but not unit information, text, menus, etc... why?? There's massive amounts of room for it and the most important information in the game is difficult to read.- Cutscenes look silly because characters are looking in the wrong place or have inappropriate facial expressions or something. They also often feel rushed or unnecessarily drawn out; there's not much consistency here.- Combat animations often show the 2 characters fighting amid dozens of other noisy characters, even when there are no other characters around. It looks, sounds, and feels ridiculous, especially because it's suddenly quiet again when the animation ends.- While you can customize what spells you take into battle, there's not much effective difference between most of them. Kind of disappointing.

_childDocuments_.review: Finished it, I would recommend watching a bit of gameplay and if you like it, buy it on discount. The bad outweighs the good too much to recommend it on full price.The game does have potential and I hope the devs will learn from it and create better product in the future.I finished the game on hard with permadeath and turn limits, the game was not easy and not too hard, although some difficult parts felt cheap. Did not have any issues with turn limit, seems to only not allow endless stalling / exp farm.The Story starts out ok, but runs out of steam quickly. Eden is generic as protagonists come, his counterpart got charisma of a brick. It's like they forgot to write plot for the second half and just filled the biggest gaps to ship the game. You don't get any meaningful choices to make, and the game fails to explain motives behind most of the biggest events in the game (of which you never have any control of). I think it would be a great improvement to make certain characters speak out with something meaningful during a mission for a line or two, instead of having a million mundane non-voiced conversation in camp, torturing players with boredom.Combat is rock paper scissors with weapons and armors, weirdly it feels like a step-down from fire emblem as there is no magic triangle, and you can use any armor type on anyone you just need to grind levels on a class that can max it out. Armors don't differ in stats much. Really didn't like how the game makes you move your units as a big clump in a lot of the missions, takes away from tactics aspect of the game. There isn't much to look forward to and the path for each character is mostly predetermined as there isn't enough time to unlock all necessary stuff and max out another class on most characters. Monster combat is fun, wish they made more missions that have both monsters and human enemies in them, I remember only one of these.The class system is shallow as well, there is not much benefit in mastering classes outside the ones needed to unlock hero skills, unless you're going to keep using it. Yes, you get to use one passive on other classes, but they are mostly useless anyway. You could at least get some stats from mastering or better passives, now it seems like class exp is irrelevant until you get to last class tier. Feels like they over tuned archers and berserkers a bit.Rapport system and in general camp interactions are not great, a ton of mundane non-voiced dialogues, you give your lads gifts to get random rewards, you never know if you get something completely useless (like a couple pots or rare accessory) or unique weapons that are the best in their category in the entire game, or nothing at all (you get conversation topic, but there is nowhere enough time to use them on everyone anyway). Again, something like stats for getting to the next tier like in fire emblem, or at least leveled rewards for every character would improve this a lot. Also voiced dialogue for reaching max tier at least? There is way too much mundane non-voiced dialogue to click through, and the game makes you click through it, since you unlock some quest doing these random mundane conversations, not great.The Optional Missions start out decent, sadly later on they just copy and paste same exact missions over and over just upscaled to higher level, sad.Overall, could have been a much better game with a bit more work put into it.

_childDocuments_.review: Only up to about Chapter 7 or so, but here are my thoughts so far.Good:Nice graphicsTurn based combat is entertainingCharacters are mostly decent, more on that later.Voice acting is pretty good.Female characters are actually attractive, and characters in general are nicely presented.Haven't run into any annoyances on the battlefield.Time limits can be disabled.Game seems stable and runs well on my PC.Average:Writing and dialog are pretty decent.Not a lot of "woke" stuff that I've seen so far. As far as modern games go, this is pretty good.  A bit more on that below.Bad:I'd say at least half of the female characters have horrible attitudes, and are very unlikable, seemingly just to make them "strong".  You don't have to be an ass all of the time to be "strong". They routinely take a massive dump on your lead male character who is supposed to be the leader, but he just takes it like a shy high school kid. On the opposite side, the male characters are generally friendly, and the ones who aren't as friendly are still reasonably likeable. I think my last complaint is that the ranged weapons and spells don't have enough range, and can only hit in a certain pattern of squares. The bows and spells only reach out maybe 2-3 squares. Out of place diversity.  Nearly everyone in the game so far is white, which makes sense for the medieval European style setting. A lot of names sound Italian or Spanish.  But every once in awhile, this random African person shows up, with no explanation for why they might be there, and no character ever seems to notice. I haven't heard any mention of other nations with different Afro-centric cultures etc, that these people could be from.  At least give a reason for why your DEI characters are there, even if they're just traveling adventurers, merchants, nobles etc. Overall I like the game, and I do recommend it if you like turn based strategy RPGs like Fire Emblem, XCOM etc.  I would likely buy a true sequel to the game. Not at all convinced yet by the Veil of the Witch game coming out later though.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a poor clone of a fire emblem game. Probably the two most frustrating things for me were: 1. There are levels where a failure condition is letting an AI controlled character withdraw. The AI is hellbent on charging these characters forward and getting them killed. The player can't do anything about it other than rush to keep up with the suicidal AI (getting people killed). 2. Enemy leaders take very little damage when friendly units are near them. The enemies often act in large groups so the leader is rarely in a state to take down unless everyone else is taken down first. This means the leader can act with impunity a lot of time. Combine that with the suicidal AI and you get a lot of cheap deaths and level failures. If you're looking for a strategy RPG I'd recommend Expeditions: Rome over this.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be honest: not gonna spend any more time on this.In 1 hour I've completed the "intro", in which you get 4 "heroes", complete with 3 unique skills and probably their best equipment, and then the first 2 chapters or so ... and let me tell you, this game is utterly boring, and mid.The graphics are pretty bad for a 2022 game. They've invested quite a bit into faces and everything, so the cutscenes (apart from the insultingly low poly hands) look decent, but the combat just looks bad.While we're at cutscenes... this IS the game. You actually watch more cutscenes with terribly bland dialogue than fight. Something about an emperor at first, but then you kinda go back in time (not literally), and start off at level 1, fighting some douche-bag Lord, who is the epitome of cartoon villain, while you're of course the goody two shoes mercenaries who go around helping people, often for no payment. Your group consists of several planks of wood, your way too nice leader and his meathead brother. There's a conspiracy afoot, a rebellion, etc. blabla, you know ... the usual.The voice acting in itself (in English anyway) is ... okay-ish, but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ if I wanted to play cutscene simulator the game I'd have bought a visual novel. It's loading screen, cutscene with slow, meandering, meaningless dialogue, loading screen, more cutscenes, loading screen, more cutscenes, loading screen, battle, dialogue during battle, loading screen, cutscenes, etc.Combat itself is also the most basic version of tactical round based combat you've ever seen. Your troup of misfits can (supposedly) be outfitted with various weapons and armor. I know this, because the wiki lists different rarities of these, so I'm guessing you probably get these upgrades automatically specific chapters (of which there are like 27), and from what I could gather online it seems you can switch classes, gear and magic around a bit more freely later on.To get to this point though you'd have to suffer through the insufferable cutscenes (or skip them and not know what's going on) and the lengthy battles, which are just too uninteresting to grab my attention, at least. Every attack is also either displayed in a lengthy animation (the camera zooms in and the characters attack each other), or you can disable those animations and you'll just see numbers above health bars ... which is equally terrible. Attacks can also in most cases only be carried out to directly adjacent fields, not diagonal ones. Movement is limited, and ranged units only have ONE more range than melee units (but can attack diagonally, but not directly adjacent targets, ugh). It's just not ... interesting, to be honest.Everything about this game screams mediocrity. And the story didn't grip me. Neither the "end game" you start at, nor the humble beginnings of your heroes. Couple that with a rather bland combat system and I'd not recommend buying this. Ever. You'd have to be ultra desperate for a turn based combat game. There are dozens of better ones.

_childDocuments_.review: So... let's begin with the positives. It looks lovely. A lot of effort has obviously gone into the character art especially and the 3D models and lighting all look good. That's about as much good as I can say for it though. At heart, the problem with this game is that the developers seem to have forgotten the player almost entirely. As a player, you have almost zero agency at all - you just click through dialogue scene after dialogue scene (no dialogue options at all, btw, just following the - pretty badly written - script one click of the sapcebar at a time) until you get to 'battles' which, as other reviews have said, are definitely more puzzle-like than turn-based tactics (and also pretty easy). In between battles you hang out at your (again, very nicely rendered) camp which, at the beginning of the game, it seems like you might get to make some decisions about the evolution of... alas, no. Instead, after every battle your camp has grown automatically - cue more cut-scene dialogues to learn about the new stuff that's appeared and more pointless wandering around to reach those dialogues but, still, no actual CHOICE about anything. There are some VERY light RPG elements but don't begin to think you're going to be poring over skill trees or comparing equipment options to make your unique personalised build... there are only four weapon types in the game and each character's skill development follows a fixed course. Basically, this is an extended animated story the developers want to tell, interspersed with a few mildly engaging puzzle stages. That might be OK if, firstly, it was advertised as such and not as a turn-based tactics RPG and, secondly, if the characters, script and story were good enough to sit through however many hours there are (after 11 hours, they are not). Finally, 11 hours in and we've only met one person of colour at all (extremely brief appearance - baddie, obs) while one of the three rather bosomey female characters you meet early on (who comes sobbing to the main, male, character to save her) is now working as the camp cook (for real?!), one is a 'noble healer' and the other the 'spiky' one. To be fair, the lazy stereotypes are equally mirrored in the male characters too (there's the - overly wooden - 'reluctant hero', the 'big dumb strong one', the 'sensible boring one', etc, etc). Ah well, at least the characters' models are three dimensional.  I don't like flaming indie studios but this title really does seem to have missed the mark on some of the very basic fundamentals of what makes for a good game experience - and be quite misleadingly advertised - so, soz, flame on :/

_childDocuments_.review: This is an unpolished, but decent Fire Emblem-like game that scratches that itch for those waiting between releases.Pros: Gameplay makes some improvements on the Fire Emblem formula, and is tactical, with a wide variety of map-types that make you think about strategy. Parts of the story are surprisingly poignant, as are some of the character 'supports.' Magic system is simple, but more interesting than its Fire Emblem counterpart.Cons: Outstays its welcome--could've condensed several early-game chapters into one, and probably the same for the late-game. Uninspired character models, most non-quest dialogue is unvoiced, and the first hour feels like someone outside of the studio meddled with it. The world-building is limited, and mostly consigned to 'read this glossary entry' oblivion.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: definitely worth it on a discount. Had great fun and was engaged in the story, last time I was this deadset on completing a game was yakuza 0, which, imo is one of the highest compliments. It has some problems though, more down below.I have read some of the negative comments and it seems a lot of them expected the game to be more like another game and were disappointed it isn't. I was very apprehensive to buy the game for a long time because steam reads "mostly positive" on reviews, but I am glad i did purchase it at a very nice 70% discount too.The story is actually rather good, enough to keep me engaged despite it being predictable, the game does start off heavy on cutscenes and a whole lot of "what is going on?" but things click as the story progresses and none of the twists, that you see coming, are making you wait on them to happen to a point of irritation.The voice acting is more than adequate, I've seen people complain about the voice acting, either I need new ears or their standard is too high. While nothing spectacular and one or two actors globally missing the mark on every line, nothing reached the point of being irksome.The writing, overall, is at the level of "acceptable". It never goes below "acceptable" but sometimes it does rise above and beyond good, making those moments very memorable. A simple exchange to help prove my point is when you ask the old man "speaking from experience are we?" and he replies "kid, i'm old. whenever i open my mouth i speak from experience. whether i like it or not."The TBS combat is actually pretty fun and engaging, though, after a while, I did skip through the attack animations and even enemy turns as those can become quite lengthy, especially when an ally is involved in the battle.I played on normal difficulty and I have to say that it challenged my brain more than adequately, I have no ambition to play on anything harder than normal as I do not wish to pull my hairs out. The only mission I had to restart is the final mission, though the fact you can get redos at any given point in the battle (a limited amount) helped greatly in me not having to start battles from scratch.The main reason I used so many redos and had to do the final battle again is just a lack of preparation to the battle's start. Preparing properly for the battle is 80% of the work, as I proved to myself theorising a battle for 1hr and 20 minutes only to steamroll that mission completely. If you're not lazy in preparation, you won't run into the similar frustrations I ran into having to constantly think on my feet.The animations are a bit stiff and there's a few funny bugs, the text speed goes too fast for me, so I switched off the auto move to next, so I could read in peace, clicking through voicelines sometimes resulted in a character's head growing in size, which is hilarious. The end credits, first few names, are bugged as hell, it litterally says "role" -"name" rather than the actual role and actual name.There's a new game + and I enjoyed the game enough to engage with that at a future time, not right now, right now I'm proud I finished this game.Bottom line, definitely worth it on a sale and if you don't have the highest of expectations or another game in mind to reference this by, definitely not a disappointment.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a mixed review, the thumb is UP, but I will report mostly what hasn't worked for me:While this game shamelessly copies a few good traits from Fire Emblem and overall has some good strong points (the voice acting is very good, congratulations! And I liked how the classe system works), it's balanced quite poorly.In fact, once you get to the second part of the game, everything gets relevantly harder, and no amount of tactic/preparation can save you from re-starting a chapter.The Developers added a number of "surprises" that pick the player off-guard, and while this is intriguing by a plot-perspective, it completely damages the player's experience, as it basically forces you to lose and re-start the same chapter a few times.While I normally thought I could ignore that, once I got to the last chapter I realised the developers wanted to make this extra hard on purpose, since the amount of sh*t that hits you there is impressive.Dear Developers, as I can see you underestimated BALANCING your game: adding two thousand traps and put the player in a constant outnumbered situation, give the bosses 100000 armor unless you kill all the common soldiers, etc... is FAR from funny or even CHALLENGING. It's just frustrating.Likewise, the battle menu is overly complicated when it could have been much easier to navigate (and since you're so inspired by Fire Emblem then why not get inspired by its overly simple Battle Menu?).And the sub-quests are ok, don't get me wrong, but in the end it's always you being somebody's errand boy.Finally, there are a few annoying bugs:1) When changing the class of a mage, sometimes it's not possible to select some grimories (the icon disappears, it's not there anymore).2) Once or twice the game stopped for no reason.3) The most hilarious bug was during this fight where Eden killed an enemy BEFORE the fight started: once the battle kicked off, Eden kept running forward and through houses and lakes INDEFINITELY. XDI still believe this is a good game, but the difficulty spikes are simply excessive by the end: do you want players to have fun or to feel frustrated?

_childDocuments_.review: A solid, straight forward tactics RPG. Lost Eidolons knows what it wants to be and is very straight forward in its presentation. The story is simple, normal guys get involved in a revolution, forced to take the front lines, chaos ensues. Character develope and grow as they learn about the dark aspects of war while trying to keep their ideals as pure as possible all while trying to survive. Its very basic and we've all seen it plenty of times.Combat has a very straight forward rock, paper, scissors weakness triangle we see in lots of other tactics games while offering some decent progressive challenge as it goes. While the game loses no points for failure to be what it says it is, it is honestly straight forward. Combined with the low magic/fantasy world and the only thing that really holds this game back is just how mundane and boring it looks and feels. Its a.... safe game that does not take huge risks with its story telling or presentation. A bit of a paint by numbers game and while some my not like that, there is no denying paint by numbers works to some extend as it gives you a clear and honest view of what the  developers where trying to make. If picked up at a slight discount, Lost Eidolons will provide some hours of entertainment for the average tactics fan, but the simple classes and lack of combat complexity will leave you wishing there were more to the game and may have you leaving early to play something more thought out. There is sadly no denying there are lots of other tactics games that are the same price or cheaper with much deeper and fun mechanics that will keep your attention longer. While there is charm that comes with Lost Eidolons simplicity I'd be lying to you if i said it should be on the top of your to play lists. Its mid at best but I don't think its bad. You can be playing something worse for sure, but you can also be playing something better.

_childDocuments_.review: I finished this game (well it bugged during the last step of the final battle so I declare it complete as I was about to win). There's a lot to like in this game, that it actually does better than Fire Emblem: a) the story is considerably better with some very good twists b) you actually care about the characters c) the classes do play a lot different - a dark mage's role is quite different from an elemental mage or a priest d) main missions have some variety and you can use multiple strategies to win e) everything is skipable and you really need it because some armies are just that large f) world building is quite goodNow about what is not so great: a) artificially long, side missions are boring b) character leveling up isn't linear and if you're not planning in the middle the classes for your characters, you won't be able to fulfill their pre-requirements in time c) some main characters become unavailable after you've invested A LOT into them and that felt cheap, but at the same time great as you actually felt the loss d) a lot of the mythology is spoken of, but there is no actual explanation of how things are the way they are e) tsunderes work in anime, not in an european medieval scenario... some characters are just insufferable.Overall an excellent experience, and it feels like if the studio had been given a bigger budget and more time to tweak the experience to the best, this would be an all time classic! Still recommend it, was a lot of fun!

_childDocuments_.review: A good game. Not a milestone in the genre, but worth your time and money. Simple but working mechanics, quite realistic, with small splashes of fantasy graphic style (I was especially pleased with the clothes and armor of ordinary soldiers). A pleasant plot, without unnecessary pathos and hysterics in dialogues, often typical of modern games. The characters behave plausibly, it is interesting to talk to them. Actually, this is the point of the game - immersion. If you expect to quickly run through all the battles and see the final credits - the game will seem quite empty, this is not Baldur's Gate 3 with its endless tactical possibilities. But if you calmly wander around the camp, talk to allies, meditate on inventory and classes, and then entertain yourself with another test of your abilities in battle - the game is addictive. In terms of the feeling of the game, Eidolons most closely resembles Dragon Age: Origins. Of course, the characters don't have many lines here, but the game's budget is also significantly smaller. So for its money, it's a very decent game. The only downside is the game's rather uneven difficulty. On normal difficulty, most fights are fought with one hand behind your back, and then suddenly at some points, the unprepared team runs into an impenetrable wall. I wouldn't say the difficulty is prohibitive, thoughtful planning solves everything, but such difficulty peaks are somewhat stressful. For those who want to avoid this, I've put together a short guide on how to get through such difficult moments. Overall conclusion - I highly recommend it.
