_childDocuments_.review: I did an early review and now that I've completed the game (on Hard/Maniac) this will be my full review of the game with parts about adjustments that can be made. This will likely be a very long review for those who will be reading as a word of warning.The core of the game is very good from mission design, classes, difficulty, voice acting, story is very solid while rough around some edges (described in more detail in the relevant sections). Examples such as certain parts being great in intent of mission (chapter 18) but the balancing wasn't quite there The last boss being generally just unfair from all standpoints which should have either been a separate encounter or having a full redesign of the fight since by time you got there you were just exhausted after all the other fights. Really loved the mission design in the games which only got better the further I got into the game.l I loved the different objectives (something I have been asking for Fire Emblem to return to ever since Radiant Dawn to no success). You have multiple ways to solve these missions regarding the classes you use. For example, during the first defence mission where you had to last 15 turns, I failed on the 11th turn first by just trying to defend so on the second attempt I used one of my mages to put down water on the enemies, then another with Blizzard and then finally Eden with his lighting which destroyed 90% of that portion of troops which then turned the defence mission into me just killing all the troops. Stuff like this is what I really love. Make levels that can be conquered in multiple ways which encourages experimentation. Overall, I liked the different classes with each having their own niche to do on the battlefield but the issue I have with them is that there is just not enough between the advanced and master class (needs a whole set of classes added between that dull period) while there is no encouragement to experiment with different skills since you’re limited to 5 skills which you can’t really put them out since most are essential.  On the armour of classes, for each character they are the same with the only difference being their gender. I would have liked if there were differences between each armour set depending on the character who was wearing it bringing out that character.I would say combine things such as sword power, axe power etc into passives and increase it to 10 while allowing you to put on skills from other classes which allows you to create units unique to you. Something such as the Tactics Ogre system is what I have in mind while also putting in a training option that the original Tactics Ogre + Reborn has since you can’t do that with the limited battles you have right now.I can’t put input on normal but on hard most of the time it was very fair and when I died it pretty much was my own fault or just required for me to take a step back to think about how I would tackle the mission. The only part that was bad was the final boss with on Hard being worn out to the brink when you finally reached it. Refer to the discussion about it which I agree with everything there. Needs to be redesigned or a separate encounter.This part can be pretty subjective but for me, I think they mostly did a good job although there were some parts that didn’t line up with me such as Eden’s first speech which is probably to do with not enough communication between the voice director, the staff and the VA since I think it was remote.Really enjoyed the story. It was a simple premise with not being unique but it knew what it wanted to be and did it well. It shows you don’t need some brand new idea to be good but be confident in what you are doing. Most people will say that it reminds you of Game of Thrones which is true but for me it reminds me more of War of the Roses (English Civil War) which Game of Thrones is based on but less complicated which is a plus for me. The only parts that felt weak to me are the parts where they speak of something such as Klara actions but you don’t see it, I imagine DLC will cover this later on. The weakest part would be the ending which was just some pictures. This needs fleshing out in a free update let me know what happens to everyone.If you ever played a Fire Emblem game you’ll feel almost right at home with the only real difference is weapon triangle is not weapons but armour and Zone of Control. Zone of Control is a neat addition and really adds to the strategy with not just being able to rush healer or mages that are at the back. The weapon triangle didn’t really largely matter on my end since I mostly just always killed them in two shots no matter what I did. The leader units work in a way you can’t really fight them until you take around everyone around them to remove their buff so you’ll largely have to rely on debuffs or provoke them with tanks till you do that.Magic was by far the most engaging combat element for me with how it all worked together and it being limited in use so you have to pick the targets cleverly with AoE spells if used right can turn the battle over in one turn. Melee combat was by far pretty basic if you played any other TRPG it won’t surprise you. It was fine but could use changes to make it more engaging to use.It wasn’t terrible nor did it stand out. It did its job without getting in the way. The only problem I really had with it was that the game didn’t use Voices of Lost and Broken Promises to their full potential. There are two chapters in the game with chapters called this when a drop of these ones would have been perfect but it never happened. Listening to Broken Promises while writing this review made me see how much it matches with the events. It would be great to have these start playing when you face the main boss unit of these chapters.I will be pretty blunt about the Leadership system, it is no good at all. It reminds me of the Trails of Cold Steel bonding system which is not good. You lock behind character points for your characters behind a limited resource which makes you not seeing a lot of it or save scrumming. It really needs to give you unlimited resources or a way to see all of it within a single playthrough. This also ties into some of the characters that die within the game. Great addition of not making it that obvious of who dies but the fact that they are on this resource as well makes the player mad that they just wasted their time spending the leadership points on them.Short note on the romance part, it was fine with not getting in the way but it needs to be part of an epilogue where you see what happened with your partner since for the one I did it with nothing happened at the end with no reference to it. This links back to the story section with the ending needed to be expanded on.The combat animations are just pretty basic. If you are coming into this thinking you will get high end animations you might want to pick a different game. They are pretty much one note animations doing their job but nothing more.The facial animations are not good. They don't express in any way what the character is feeling or their individual personality. If it wasn’t for the voice acting I wouldn’t be able to tell what they felt during emotional scenes.Overall, I really loved the game despite the rough endings and the rare bad part in it. With addressing the tweaks and feedback that they have been receiving I believe it will be a very great game that will end up as an underrated gem and look forward to what they will be able to do in the future (give me that Klara DLC!). Congrats Ocean Drive Studios on a great first game. I am very pleased to have backed this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Eidolons

_childDocuments_.review:
The land of Benerio was once a shining kingdom by the sea. Then an iron-fisted conqueror, Ludivictus, set the world on fire and redrew the maps. Now Benerio is one downtrodden province in a crumbling Empire where the only true master is corruption.

Enter Eden, a charming mercenary captain forced to become a rebel commander when his village is thrust headfirst into war. Now Eden must rally his allies and stand tall against an imperial army, fearsome monsters, and enemies within.

Lost Eidolons is a turn-based tactical RPG with a gripping cinematic narrative, set in a waning empire riven by civil war. Take on the role of a charming mercenary captain, Eden, and lead his band of allies through epic encounters on a classic turn-based battlefield.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Eidolons

name: HUMANITY
detailed_description: WORK LIKE A DOG HUMANITY is a third-person puzzle-action game where you become a dog to command massive, marching crowds of people to jump, turn, push, float, shoot, and climb their way to salvation across 90 story-mode stages. READY, AND…ACTION! Devious puzzles and strategic thinking is broken up with more action-focused elements and platformer-like levels, even some epic boss battles! UGC = USER GENERATED CONTENT, UNLIMITED GRATIFYING CHALLENGES Browse an ever-growing library of stages created by other players. Play, rate, and discover new types of puzzles in this limitless vault. CREATE AND SHARE LEVELS Bring your ideas to life using the intuitive Stage Creator, be it a straightforward puzzle, action stage, or heck, even an artful sculpture! (OPTIONAL) VR Compatible Immerse yourself like never before as you tower over the teeming, ant-like people! Mu ha ha ha ha! Whether on your standard display or in the optional VR Mode, watch as breathtaking swarms of people follow your commands to the exit, all in HUMANITY’s stark iconic style, courtesy of director and celebrated visual designer Yugo Nakamura and famed game creator Tetsuya Mizuguchi (Rez Infinite, Tetris Effect: Connected).

_childDocuments_.review: The re-birth of Lemmings. Humanity yields a Lemmings-like 3D experience with some great mechanics, amazing soundtrack, and apparently endless amounts of levels with the amazing user created levels already. The level creator and playthrough reminds me of the latest Super Mario Maker 2 in regards to the ease of making and playing user created levels. Highly recommended at retail of $30 with VR as well I can only imagine how amazing it would look (Gets vintage VR set out of box and blows off dust)
_childDocuments_.name: HUMANITY

_childDocuments_.review: Finished the first major arc of the game and yeah, this game is cool as hell. It's a excellently designed puzzle game that rides the fine line between clever but fair. Puzzles require a surprising amount of execution in order to clear them + get all the goldys, which gives a lot of spice to the game's simple mechanics. There's something about its art design and music that also really strikes me in the right way too - everything about this is gonna be strong enough to keep me away from finishing the new Zelda. For managing to accomplish that with no trouble? It definitely deserves a recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: HUMANITY

_childDocuments_.review: This starts as a clever and cute puzzle game and near the end loses sight of what its original goal was. It pivots multiple times into different genres in the final act of the game. From puzzle to tower defense to bullet hell to stealth to RTS. And all of those pivots feel under-baked and at the expense of the core game.The first two thirds of the game were genuinely joyous, but the rate at which the game devolves into a frustrating mess of questionable design, poorly telegraphed mechanics, and unreliable unit behavior makes the joy and satisfaction vanish. In fact, at times it feels as if it was never there.I loved this game and wanted more of it. Until I got more of it. This was a heartbreaking experience and I mean that in the worst way possible.
_childDocuments_.name: HUMANITY

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a difficult ask for $30.  It starts out AMAZING, but later mechanics can be very frustrating and too trial-and-error.  The game is lacking a lot of QoL features, and the soundtrack is super hit or miss too.EDIT:  Completed the game, changed my thoughts a little bit.  It hurts to say, but I still wouldn't recommend the game without a sale.The big advertised aspects that made me buy the game, leading infinite streams of people through fun puzzle platforming challenges in real-time, get sidelined in later chapters, and I didn't find a lot of the new stuff as enjoyable.  There's far less platforming, which was my favorite aspect of the game.The game starts out with puzzles, but later on, it often turns into trial-and-error when combat starts to be involved.  Sometimes, enemy movements even happen during the middle of the stage, and there's not enough warning when it happens.  Other times, it feels like RNG whether or not you win a combat, and some missions are extremely unforgiving, making you fail the level or lose access to Goldies if you lose even one human.In many levels, time is stopped while you place commands, then you start time and see if it works out.  These stages become more tedious than hard when enemies are involved.  Instead of discovering the solution to a tricky puzzle, you're retrying over and over, adjusting your commands tile by tile until you find the exact setting that either avoids or defeats the enemy, and then reaches the exit.EDIT:  In some time stop stages, you can position some humans before starting time.  However, these starting positions of humans are NOT saved, so you have to re-do them each time you retry.Goldies start out as bonus humans that you have to safely guide to the exit without letting them fall.  This mechanic starts out super fun, and you're often sending something so valuable flying through the sky and hoping they make it.  Some of them are very challenging to collect and bring to the exit, especially in real-time, and it was great fun in early chapters.But later on, Goldies become required to unlock the exit to complete many stages, defeating the purpose.  It's not bonus anymore.  Some required story stages only have 1 Goldy, and you must get it to clear the stage.Some later stages have extremely trivial Goldies, directly on your path or right next to it.  I've even found one that was placed a couple tiles in front of the exit.  It was just... free.  You CAN see how the enemy humans will move.  They have arrows and stuff just like the ones you place, but in black.  HOWEVER, you cannot see these arrows unless time is moving.  You need to , and then you must enter .  Otherwise, you can't see the enemy arrows.  I went through the entire game not realizing that this information was available because of this issue.During time stop stages, the start button is a physical location you have to run to.  When you retry, you get teleported back to the starting position and then have to walk back to where your error was, fix your error... and then walk back to the start button.  This should've been streamlined somehow.Soundtrack is very hit or miss, and the music selector is bugged; when you retry a stage, the music resets back to default.  The chapter 4 song is terrible, and I had to mute the music completely because of this bug.Some combat or physics RNG can cause you to randomly win or fail a stage without changing anything.  If a Goldy enters an intersection between two streams of humans, it might get diverted into the other path.  It might not.  It's random which way it goes, and I've had to restart stages until I get the desired outcome.-HUMANITY is not a BAD game, but it's just very rough around the edges.
_childDocuments_.name: HUMANITY

_childDocuments_.review: Puzzle games come in all shapes and sizes but how many let you (inadvertently) kill hundreds of thousands of people? This puzzle game lets you direct the flow of hordes of humans to get to an the level exit and in doing so you will end up losing many, many people. Some will fall off the edge of the map, others will be tossed to their doom. It's like a highly advanced Lemmings game. And it's an absolute blast. The puzzles are thought provoking and clever. I was impressed by the quality of the levels and their design. The graphics are crisp and animations are smooth. I marveled at the number of people on the screen without any hint of slowdown. This is really a great game and deserves more attention.
_childDocuments_.name: HUMANITY

_childDocuments_.review: In life, failure is as inevitable as success – this is the underlying principle of great puzzle games. You're equipped with all the tools you need to succeed and it's your responsibility to utilize them effectively to achieve the goals set before you.HUMANITY places you in control of a luminous Shiba Inu, tasked with guiding hordes of people towards a light that transports them into the unknown. The game unfolds like a series of puzzle boxes, each with a fundamental set of rules: shepherd your humans to the light, prevent them from falling from great heights, and use the provided tools to avert their untimely demise. If navigating the crowds from point A to point B wasn't challenging enough, the game rewards your efforts to collect Goldys – the epitome of human accomplishment – which in turn unlock progress and assistive tools for easier puzzle-solving.Initially, the toolset is simple, with arrows for direction and commands to jump. These rudimentary tools soon amalgamate into a complex web of commands, making the gameplay increasingly intricate. It would be easy to liken HUMANITY to Lemmings, but doing so would disregard the platform challenges that uniquely define this game. As a player, you'll find yourself questioning how to access certain areas of a level to place commands and realizing that the stream of people you're guiding are also instrumental in your own journey.The tranquil aesthetics of HUMANITY are a signature of the team behind Tetris Effect, Child of Eden, Lumines, and REZ. Coupled with the pseudo-futuristic techno music, these visuals create an immersive and cohesive experience, reminiscent of an interactive design studio’s portfolio. The game's sleek aesthetics provide a calming backdrop for the perplexing trials that await you.The crafting of a good puzzle game demands talented designers capable of devising some of the most challenging levels. HUMANITY embraces this notion by enabling anyone to create and share their levels, ensuring a constant influx of new challenges from the community.Fans of games like Portal, Baba is You, The Witness, or The Talos Principle will find HUMANITY an easy recommendation. As with those games, failure is not a dead end; instead, it forms part of the learning process propelling you towards success.HUMANITY is a true Goldy of puzzle games. Underneath its engaging gameplay, it communicates a deeper message – one that resonates with its players, and, much like its puzzles, equips you with enough tools to reach your own conclusions.
_childDocuments_.name: HUMANITY

_childDocuments_.review: So reminiscent of Lemmings, Humanity is a delightful and rewarding puzzle game, with just the right level of challenge.  At least it was until near the end of the game where it turns into a quick-twitch action platformer.  I'm unable to play that genre of games due to health conditions and it brought my enjoyment (and my game) to a screeching halt, leaving me with only a tremendous feeling of disappointment.  What a shame that the devs took that path, completely ruining what had been an enjoyable experience for me.I post this simply to warn others that struggle with or don't enjoy quick twitch games.  Kudos to the devs on the puzzles in the first 2/3rds of the game.  So very well done.
_childDocuments_.name: HUMANITY

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really just... so wonderful. A Lemmings-style game where you, as a little glowing dog, lead a (sometimes) never-ending army of humans as they march to your commands (often to their doom). Solve puzzles, which sometimes involve fighting, sometimes involve blocks, and sometimes involve giant glowy gold people.There's also a level editor with a ton of user-created levels that can be accessed in-game, so that's a plus.
_childDocuments_.name: HUMANITY

_childDocuments_.review: Haven't played that much yet but i'm loving what i'm seeing so far. this totally feels like a surreal style puzzle game from the PS2 and DS era. if your like me and have been trying to find something to crave the odd itch for the past few years, then this is it! and the fact theres a level editor with online sharing will give this game plenty of replay value, im sure of it
_childDocuments_.name: HUMANITY

_childDocuments_.review: This game went criminally underrated in the mad rush that was 2023 but it is my favorite game of the year (I played most of the big ones but this one really scratched an itch). Humanity is one of the most incredibly polished puzzle games I've ever played. The difficulty is almost perfect to constantly give you the ah ha moment with exceedingly few points of frustration. It is super relaxing, performs amazingly, has an interesting story and to top it off, has one of the best boss fights of the year. Easily joins the puzzle greats like portal imo. A must play.
_childDocuments_.name: HUMANITY

_childDocuments_.review: Humanity is a really fun puzzle game with some unique mechanics. The game reminds me of Lemmings, but Humanity has its own mechanics that make it feel new and fresh. You control a small dog that can run around a 3d environment made up of blocks. Your dog can create commands on each square that tell the humans which way to go, or which way to jump. The goal is to lead an ever flowing parade of humans into one or more lighted end points. The humans are unlimited, so you don't have to worry about some (or hundreds of them) falling off the edge. I'm still early on and I'm sure there are many different other commands that I will eventually be able to choose from.On each level (at least so far), there are special golden humans that you can try to collect. It becomes more difficult when there is more than one on the map, but it's a fun puzzle trying to figure out how to collect all of them, without them falling off the stage.One thing that is genius is that if you retry the level, you can choose to keep all of the commands that you had on the map in your previous try. You don't have to start from scratch every time. You can just tweak your previous attempt little by little, until you solve the puzzle. This is a really smart thing and I hope future puzzle games steal this idea. I'm only an hour in, but overall this has been a very enjoyable puzzle game with an amazing soundtrack. It's starting to get difficult, but not too difficult to where it is frustrating. A definite recommend for anyone who enjoys puzzle games.
_childDocuments_.name: HUMANITY

_childDocuments_.review: The puzzles aren't mind blowing, but they do the job. It's fun to play and the plot is also a welcome one. The game has huge potential in terms of community levels, I have to admit. I believe the game was designed in such a minimalistic style exactly because of this. It also looks cool as hell in VR, sadly my old HTC Vive didn't work (also didn't put any effort in trying to fix it, so maybe it's possible to use them).But the game has some big cons if you ask me:  If I could, I would give this a horizontal thumb, but overall, it's too good of a game to give it a thumb down.
_childDocuments_.name: HUMANITY

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible game. The concept is well executed with an artistic direction that add so much ! The level are diverse with a really good progression of mechanics. The story might be a bit short, but it's really cool to follow. I finished the game 100% plus achievements in 15 hours but there is so much more playtime thanks to the community editor with already many fun levels.
_childDocuments_.name: HUMANITY

_childDocuments_.review: Humanity is truly a work of art.Humanity (the game) much like humanity (the biological species) exhibits vast diversity, endless creativity, and is at times beautifully arresting. This gem of a puzzle game is a joy to play, each trial thoughtfully constructed to push users to think in a non-lineral manner.The visuals, and accompanying soundtrack, are appropriately trippy and trance-like. My favorite levels are the ones which have water features - watching a never-ending stream of humanoid bodies swim by like a school of fish is mesmerizing. The game does a great job of gradually revealing new tricks and mechanics to meet the ever increasing challenges of the next trials.Anyone who thinks that video games can't be art needs to see Humanty's throngs of low-poly crowds throwing elongated shadows cast by a low light source, or unending waves of bodies hurling themselves into oblivion... Then take some time to examine that obviously incorrect belief they hold.Humanity is a "must play" for anyone who loves great puzzle and/or trippy & psychedelic games.
_childDocuments_.name: HUMANITY

_childDocuments_.review: I don't typically play puzzle games, don't have the patience or the care to learn their intricacies and I'll at most play some tetris because I find it more engaging. Comically enough, this is from the same publisher of Tetris Effect, a game I love to death and this is no different. Whatever they're doing to render these enormous crowds of people is extremely impressive, and it leads to the most satisfying puzzle game I've ever played. The puzzles themselves are extremely well designed to the point that when you solve them you feel like an absolute genius. The puzzle elements are very clear, the puzzles themselves are well designed and their solutions make you feel like a genius (and aren't annoyingly obscured to make the puzzle maker feel smart, unlike many puzzle games I've tried), and it's very fun to watch your conga line of humans reach the end, sometimes creating a work of surrealist art in the process. Highly recommend for the asking price, you will not regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: HUMANITY

_childDocuments_.review: Positives:- Having this many people walk along paths or float though the air is awesome. It's like watching an ant colony but way way cooler.- The puzzles are varied in their mechanics, and overall they have a nice progression that is not just "the same but more difficult".- The skins which can be unlocked from optional tasks (Goldies) are actually quite fun. This also makes the Goldies a bit more valuable rather than just being the more difficult task that makes the game enjoyable.Neutral:- Replaying a stage can take quite a while, even with keeping the commands and at 2x speed.- Every person is sort of doing their own thing and there are hidden forces that keep a group together. This can make the game rather imprecise. Sometimes 1 person gets pushed off their path by the group, changes direction and you have to restart the stage.Negatives:- Depending on your artistic preferences, you may either call this "music" or "incomprehensible noises".- The platforming is a bit unnecessary. You might as well put in the commands by just clicking on a tile with the mouse. Moving around with the dog makes the game even more imprecise because you can fall off the stage and the placement of commands depends on the direction you are facing.
_childDocuments_.name: HUMANITY

_childDocuments_.review: Underrated action puzzler that gradually introduces and deviates on mechanics that shift the gameplay into creative and unexpected genre fusions. What starts as grid automation puzzles slowly morphs into combinations of puzzle platforming, physics puzzles, real time strategy, stealth, and shoot em ups. 2/3 of the way through the game it felt like I was playing a completely different game than a few hours before. There’s definitely some depth sacrificed here and I felt the game was overall a bit easy, but that’s understandable when the result feels like 6 different games smoothly packaged into 15 hours of gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: HUMANITY

_childDocuments_.review: This is a puzzle game where you play as a dog and must (most of the time) help humans find the path to the end of the course (light square).This game is good looking, there are different kinds of puzzles that should please everyone. One complaint: it's strange but the first four "worlds" were definitely the best as it was focused on a puzzle solving aspect. Starting with the fifth world, it gets way easier and replaces the puzzle aspect by fighting you opponents/overwhelming them. You also have a level editor and play other people's levels, that's awesome! Probably the best puzzle game I've played this year.
_childDocuments_.name: HUMANITY

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely fantastic puzzle game. If you liked old smaller Playstation JapanStudio titles like Echochrome/Echochrome 2, Lemmings, Star Wars Pit Droids absolutely worth checking this out. What the media and marketing does a kinda poor job of marketing for the game is just how packed the game is with mechanics. You'll never really feel like you're stuck doing the same stuff over and over because every few levels stuff gets flipped on its head with new tools, new victory criteria, new ways to play the game, so on and so forth. It's more like a toolbox for making lots of different-feeling puzzle games. One stage might feel like planning every move out like chess, another might feel closer to an old school Zelda block pushing puzzle, etc.It scratches the same itch I had when playing Neon White, where there was an emphasis on finding unconventional routes to solve almost puzzle like stages, except here it's a bit more meditative.At $30 its honestly a pretty easy recommend. For the very money-sensitive $20 or 25 might be more worth it, but at the same time we don't really get games like this all that frequently. The creation mode is also extremely robust and so you'll have a ton of playtime there as well if you want.Difficulty wise it feels good -- you only need to obtain a certain number of sub objectives in levels to progress and the main path of levels is usually pretty straightforward feeling, but some optional levels can be pretty darn tough.
_childDocuments_.name: HUMANITY

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I'd say that this is an incredibly good game. The game frequently throws in new mechanics and updates to the game, so the levels never get to a point where they feel stale. The overall aesthetic and storyline is also a huge bonus.If there was any ~minor~ gripe, I wish I knew that the game wasn't purely a puzzle game. It certainly starts off more puzzle based, but then it shifts into more real-time strategic as you get to later layers. I'm struggling a bit towards the end, but I think that says much more about me than it does the game. Still super fun despite my lack of skill.
_childDocuments_.name: HUMANITY

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic, the music is super chill, puzzle are satisfying to complete, I get a fantastic feeling of polish with this game. Its super rare that a game comes out that feels bug free and complete from day one so I've got to commend the game on this! I've not tried the community maps and the creator yet but the fact it exists is awesome! Super relaxing and rewarding feeling puzzle game 10/10 and at a fair price!
_childDocuments_.name: HUMANITY

_childDocuments_.review: Humanity is a game unlike almost any other.  It starts out a bit similar to classic games like Lemmings but advances quickly to becoming something entirely unique.  A puzzle platformer at its core, the game has you lead humans into the light while battling obstacles, others, machines and four increasingly challenging bosses across 90 story levels.  It took me around 14 hours to reach the final boss battle and I haven't yet completed all of the optional levels in the 90 included with the story mode.  What really stands out though in the game is the brilliant level design, the fantastic soundtrack and the added bonus of an extensive level creator that allows for some fantastic user generated content.User levels thus far available include works of art like a PC building simulator, a round the bases simulation of a baseball diamond complete with batter, pitcher, base runners and cheering onlookers in the stands, and a giant pyramid level.  There are tons of options to extend your time in the game and I'm looking forward to seeing what others build and explore in this one.
_childDocuments_.name: HUMANITY

_childDocuments_.review: I've just scratched the surface but I can already tell this is an outstanding puzzle game. It's Lemmings 3D for the new generation. I love the bouncy feel of jumping all around like an excited dog, laying down commands for my people and figuring out how to get them through. Then I love gazing at the surreal, bizarre scene of thousands of humans flopping through the air, knowing I did this.If you played Lemmings when you were a kid, you'll want to check this out. Woof.
_childDocuments_.name: HUMANITY

_childDocuments_.review: Satisfying puzzler with futuristic design. For me, Humanity is standing out mainly because of some extent of automation, which saves lots of time (and brain power). But couple of last chapters are based entirely on "follow" mechanic which IMO doesn't work well enough to focus on it as an isolated element. Storywise, there is some philosophical takes on humanity (surprise) and its future, which works good enough as a background.BTW Whats up with Lemmings?)
_childDocuments_.name: HUMANITY

_childDocuments_.review: A fun game, intriguing story.However, game very quickly starts to depend on you making quick alterations to to achieve bonus objectives. Neither the control scheme, nor the way people move in this game, is conducive to this.Only recommend if you don't really care about 100% maps and struggling with a slightly awkward control scheme.
_childDocuments_.name: HUMANITY

_childDocuments_.review: Good puzzling game, played this in non-VR mode.You should be aware that the later levels essentially change the genre of the game and have little to do with the "lemmings experience" that is presented initially. I liked (most) the combat or stealth sections, but it's not actually what you expect when playing a puzzle game and I understand everyone that is disappointed about this.The music is atrocious though, it's really novel in the beginning of the game when you are still introduced to mechanics and every level is like 3 minutes. But these repetitive noises become so annoying in the later levels that take longer to solve. This is the first game where I actually had to turn off the music because it was bothering me so much in some of the levels.
_childDocuments_.name: HUMANITY

_childDocuments_.review: A brilliant puzzle game overall, and a game that puts a lot of effort into design in the conventional sense. The visual style, the modeling, the typography, the music... all came together to make the experience a piece of pleasant visual art.While we have already reached a stage where we consider video games a new form of contemporary art, maybe it is equally important to take a step back to think of how this new form of art can interact with and interrelate to the "old" forms of art.
_childDocuments_.name: HUMANITY

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely one of the more captivating puzzle games as of late. Every new chapter introduces new mechanics so the game never ends up feeling like you are playing the same puzzles over and over. Story is nice and intriguing enough to make you want to progress further.Also always fun to watch your humans fall into the abyss.
_childDocuments_.name: HUMANITY

_childDocuments_.review: This game offers an equally enjoyable and relaxing experience. The puzzles increase in difficulty in a satisfying manner, striking the perfect balance between progress and ease. The art direction, coupled with the sound and music, contribute to a serene, enjoyable gameplay experience. It evokes fond memories of playing Lemmings during my middle school years. Thus far, I've only delved into the main campaign, but the availability of customizable features and user-created levels suggests that this game will maintain its spot in my roster of installed games.
_childDocuments_.name: HUMANITY

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an absolute blast.  Another rock solid puzzle game that is amazing.  I can't wait to go back and do all the challenges.  This game has some trial and error and some tedium but overall the new mechanics each challenge phase brings as well as the satisfaction when you finally win is always worth it. I just never got sick of the beautiful imagery of thousands of humans walking at the same time too.  A really clever game that takes the best of lots of previous puzzle games and makes them all its own.  A must buy.  So much content.
_childDocuments_.name: HUMANITY

_childDocuments_.review: Please play it, or at least buy it to support its development. It’s one of those games that comes around once every twenty years. It’s leaving a mark on me just as Outer Wilds did back in the day—two different games but extremely similar at the same time. They both masterfully exploit the sense of wonder, both in gameplay and visually. It’s a concentrate of ideas, sounds, and U-turns. It’s my Game of the Year (or rather, among my top games of the generation).I’m truly grateful to Mizuguchi, who, besides being my favorite game designer along with Kojima, is also an incredible teacher. Even though Humanity isn’t directly his creation, it’s clearly inspired by his work; his influence is evident, and he has shaped a fantastic team.I think the press has underestimated it. Perhaps due to the rush to finish it, they didn’t spend much time collecting all the Goldy, which are crucial to fully appreciating the design of this title. For me, it deserves the highest rating, at least on my scale where a 10 is reserved for those titles that I know won’t age, not even in 60 years. Music, art direction, ideas—it’s all perfect in its imperfections, just like humanity.
_childDocuments_.name: HUMANITY

_childDocuments_.review: Made me depressed about Humanity. On the other hand, it’s one of the more creatively imagined games I’ve played. The mechanics take a bit of getting used to. Adjusting your view from a holistic standpoint can get confusing, since some movements inevitably move the dog at the same time. I frequently don’t even notice I’m moving the dog, only to realise it after the dog falls off the side somewhere. I wish I could freely rotate my view once a puzzle is completed, just to marvel on my solution. You might be able to, but I haven’t been able to do so. Aside from being a neat puzzle game, the themes behind exactly what is happening on the screen makes you think about bigger things beyond the realities of wasting your life staring  at a monitor.
_childDocuments_.name: HUMANITY

_childDocuments_.review: I'm becoming part of some weird Cult. 👿We... Need... People!! 👿You can read my other reviews Video review: Puzzle-solving has always fascinated me in video games. Finally having that super satisfying click of lucidity to solve the presented problem puts a smile on everyone's face. After a couple of hours of taking the form of a Shiba and guiding people into the light, I feel like my problem-solving is sharper than ever, at least at the puzzle level.Humanity is a modern take on the puzzle-strategy genre in the style of Lemmings, presented by the producers of Tetris Effect, where the objective will be to lead individuals to the main goal. Of course, not everything is as linear as this explanation, but even so, it is possible to solve the problem in a few minutes. What's fascinating about this title is that there isn't just one solution to solving the puzzle. It is interesting to revisit previous levels and with all the baggage collected from the experience during the adventure in Humanity and discover new paths that previously seemed impossible, making sure that there is no monotony and increasing its replayability.The preparation of flows and mechanics that each level presents is all done by the player. At your disposal will be the tireless Shiba in the form of a ghost that can move around the entire game board. Even though it's not an action title, there's a good deal of jumps to platforms and dexterity in using mechanics at the right time. It's tremendously easy to move the little character around the map, there's even a skill that lets you move faster on top of people. This is all associated with the very smooth camera movement, where it is even possible to zoom in and out and which helps a lot in perceiving all the points of interest. Unfortunately, I don't have any VR device to test Humanity in this mode, but I believe that it can be quite immersive. Regarding the mechanics, they can go through the simple redirection of the flow of people by means of arrows, the inclusion of jump skills, jumping further, or even shooting at targets, always with the intention of shaping the path to the light.In addition to the main objective of bringing the flow of people to a specific point, there are secondary objectives that essentially involve taking one or more figures, which are distinguished by their height and gold color, even resembling a golden globe, to a specific point. It is not necessary at all levels to make them cross the objective, however, the chapters will be closed and instead of having keys to open them, it will be necessary to collect X number of these figures to open them. I never felt the need to repeat a level due to the lack of units to open the next chapter.There is also a progression system that will evolve as secondary objectives are achieved and unlock rewards that are essentially related to different aspects for humans and even gameplay features such as changing the level's music, stopping or accelerating time, etc.The story doesn't make any sense, but uses interesting metaphors about human nature that somehow explain to the player what the heck he is seeing on his screen. Moments where the "voice" that guides the player, builds a human head with the people present in the vast universe created in the chapter's selection lobby, and that declaims its lines of text. These are undoubtedly bizarre moments that mark the fun experience.Another interesting aspect of this title, in addition to the story mode, is the implementation of the Stage Creator mode, which allows you to play levels created and shared by other players, or the construction and subsequent sharing of levels created by the players themselves. This means that after finishing the story mode there is always something new to be tested, levels of all shapes for all tastes. In addition, the more custom maps that you play and/or the more upvotes you received on your creations, the more XP you receive and thus the possibility of unlocking elements for the player's avatar.Humanity is the vibe, literally. Modern, simple but with enough mechanics that make the most meticulous players interested in their creations. It is possible to spend hours on end trying to discover a path to the goal. Extremely recommended for everyone who enjoys a good puzzle and also for those who like to create problems for their opponents. All this makes me wonder how a player who loves creating levels in Mario Maker will feel.

_childDocuments_.review: My rig: Valve Index & Rift CV1, Asus Strix OC RTX 3090, i9 10900K (10 cores, 20threads, 5.3GHz), 32GB 3200MHz, 8TB, Win10. Note that Humanity supports both native SteamVR drivers and native Meta/Oculus drivers for optimal performance. This could be my game of the year - it's that polished and amazing. I tried the demo with my PSVR2, but got very bad 60 fps and reprojections, especially reprojections with the white dog were constantly easy to see. So I did worry about the PCVR experience. With Index and a RTX 3090 I get solid 90 fps using Index res 300% (about 27 million pixel per frame combining both eyes), and that's using highest possible in-game graphics settings (including ambient occlusion) - and that game looks night and day better than PSVR2. Blacks are awesome with the Index, but I think devs have tweaked the game for lcd hmd, as Quest seems to be their primary target. That said, Index controllers are fully supported - controls are easy to learn, but take time to master. I also tested the game with the Rift CV1, the game still looked great and I got solid 90 fps with ss 2.5 (also 27 mill pixels per frame). The game does seem designed more for Touch than Index controllers, as just the slightest touch of Index grip will accelerate the time in the game - and it's easy to touch the grip by an error. This does not happen with Rift Touch, as you need to press a button for grip to work with these controllers. This really is Lemmings 3D VR anno 2023. Using humans instead of lemmings is brilliant, as you instantly react more emotionally when seeing many humans fall to their death. The game has awesome dynamic shadows, and you can control the camera in every way you can possilbly think of. For those worrying about the price - you're really getting a $59.99 game for half the price, it's that good. IGN rated the game 9/10, and Shacknews said 90% - with the Index res 300% you really can see the most tiny details, and I'd rate this gem 95% for now - but I need to play it more. Btw, sound is great too - as said, this is one of the most polished VR games I've ever tried - from the makers of Rez Infinite. Note, this game does not feel like a 2D port, it feels like made ground-up for VR, because you really need VR to experience the grandiose design of this game!

_childDocuments_.review: Humanity is a puzzle game that doesn't play fair.The general goal - guide "the people" to beams of light, collecting golden idols along the way - is interesting. Many levels feature fun and thoughtful puzzle design, and were the exact deterministic gameplay I'm looking for in the puzzle games I play. The theme of the game is artistic mumbo-jumbo, but the core mechanic of spatial programming is well-designed and fun.Unfortunately, this game relies on the player understanding detailed functionality that isn't spelled out anywhere. It's easy enough to learn that "the people" can fall 2 blocks safely, but much more difficult to figure out the exact jumping arcs when Float is combines with High Jump vs. Long Jump vs. Regular Jump, or how those jumps are changed (or NOT changed) by water. The game does a pretty good job telling you what each of the switches in the world does, but mostly requires you to commit to extensive trial and error when combining the mechanics together.I stopped after reaching world 4 (after fully completing every prior stage), only to find the new mechanic was "others" that move along the board in ways it's impossible for you to predict. Once again, you can't possibly understand how the stage works in advance - it's up to you to commit trial and error and learn how the "others" act on every stage where they appear.Additionally, the fast forward speed of "the people" is not very fast at all. Many tougher levels involved watching "the people" walk around for 60 seconds or more before reaching the goal. That's not great if your level solution is correct, but becomes painfully slow whenever your level solution has a single error in it.All in all, there's a decent game here but the thorns in the game's design are quite painful to fans of the genre. Worth checking out on a sale, but I wouldn't recommend this over other puzzle games.

_childDocuments_.review: I've seen many comparisons of this game to Lemmings, which yes, it does share some gameplay elements with. Now imagine you took Lemmings and mashed it with Intelligent Qube. Then you added some light shooter elements, a little bit of Metal Gear Solid VR Missions, existential story droplets, and a dash of 3D action. Humanity is the amalgamation of many different ideas but it still feels cohesive as a puzzle game.That said, there were a couple of levels near the end that felt like they relied too heavily on a combination of luck and precision, and the frame rate on the final level slowed to a crawl on my Steam Deck.Overall though, Humanity is a great puzzle game and I couldn't put it down.

_childDocuments_.review: A unique puzzle game which I can recommend in parts, and an under baked frustrating mishmash of genres that undermines the core strengths of the game at others.- This isn't a game where you can plan, set the puzzle into motion and watch your efforts come to fruition; some puzzles require active modifications as they progress (particularly puzzles with belts and boss battles) and this can become a source of frustration.- The goldy start off as an interesting side objective with some QOL features attached as rewards, but later they become mandatory to complete some levels, and therefore a significant portion of the latter half just abandons any form of optional content and often times the Goldy are placed in borderline unmissable locations which trivializes the already reduced side content. - As the game progresses it strips away both the difficulty and the puzzle mechanics which brings me to... the trial and error combat (because every video game needs guns and action), and the escort stealth sections which are undoubtedly the worst sections in the game.- The player character (dog) needs to move onto a tile to place commands and can jump 2 tiles high; Functionally this limits your ability to traverse the map ahead of time, however you can attach yourself to a human and travel with them to previously inaccessible heights. This is a good concept and limiting when certain sections can be accessed allows for some unique puzzle opportunities (like how instructions can only be placed inside glass after the barrier is removed by a pressure plate), but it's rarely used as such, and you just end up with more tedious platforming and maybe restarting the level an additional time to keep placed commands.- A few QOL features are lacking, most notably is the inability to see enemy paths until you start the level and then pause. Sometimes the dog blends in with the crowd. For some reason the final boss caused massive FPS drops although those were brief.- The soundtrack is generally okay but a few tracks almost forced me to mute the game.

_childDocuments_.review: UGH! This COULD'VE been good.... it was so close! TRAGIC!1. Having to use that dumb dog as a cursor on each board was a VERY bad developer choice. Requiring it to run to locations on the board so you can leave your directional commands there is time-consuming and unnecessary. It also prevents you from immediately assigning commands on higher elevations that the dog can't jump up to; you have to wait until someone in your stream of people climbs there so the dog can warp up to him.2. The dog is all white with no detail and is quite difficult to find in a crowd of people. I don't understand why the developers didn't make the dog a distinct color or have it flash so that you can see it easier.3. Poor camera angles will occasionally fool you into thinking that the dog is elsewhere on the board, which can prevent you from timing your actions appropriately. It also makes it easy to walk off of an edge.4. In addition to the dog issues, sometimes random people in the stream will veer off on their own (for no reason) causing you to forfeit achievements or invoke some other terrible consequence. This makes some stages totally unplayable.5. My last complaint is the difficulty level; about world four or so, Humanity becomes borderline impossible since they introduce "bad humans" wandering the board that will actively hunt and kill your "good humans". They can freely move wherever they want to, whenever they want to, and are MUCH faster than your slower-paced people confined to walking a set path. There's no way to avoid them. The game ceases to be fun at this point.I feel like the game can be saved with a little bit of developer work, but for now, I'm going with the thumbs down.

_childDocuments_.review: Humanity is a refreshing puzzle game with amazing Lemmings-esque gameplay, where you play as a Shiba Inu who has the job of guiding humans to the goal of each level while avoiding Others and collecting the sometimes optional Goldy by placing turns, jumps, and other commands. Sound like a lot? Don't worry! The game starts off nice and easy with a hint of challenge - but don't worry, you won't get stumped. New commands and features are added throughout the game's many levels and boss fights. Plus a story that although it may not move you, will push your desire to carry on.And if the ninety story stages aren't enough to draw you in, well, there's more. A level editor and constantly expanding selection of thousands of incredible levels is also included within Humanity, which means that the player can continue the fun even after completing the game, or you can get a breath of fresh air if you're stumped on a level. Express your creativity with a level editor that's the perfect blend of restrictive and open, then share your stage online! They offer Stage Jams too, meaning even those with mental block can get involved. And they also stream user levels on a weekly basis, every Wednesday, with the great Austin and CJ.You get all that for just £25, plus a free demo to feel the game out. And if that's not a good enough deal already? Humanity is also available on PS4, PS5, Xbox One and Xbox Series X|S, and on each of those systems' respective premium deals; Xbox Game Pass and PlayStation Plus. So, why not buy Humanity? You  regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommend for lovers' of Portal, Lemmings. etc.  A pretty much perfect game for that kind of puzzling.  My only gripe with the game is the controlling the dog is sometimes a bit fiddly, or at least figuring where the dog will land.  It's especially tricky where water is concerned.  Also, sometimes your view (the dog's view) slips off the map.   I'm only on the 3rd level so far, so take what I say with a grain of salt.  If you do like logical problems and being given the time to fix them, this will scratch that itch.  I'm loving it so far.  Also, I actually paid for the soundtrack too - very Steve Reichian.  Wonderful stuff.  To sum up; if you enjoy the satisfaction of seeing a problem that looks nigh on impossible until your brain clicks, you'll appreciate the inventiveness on display here.  The levelling up/bonuses for collecting goldies is/are clever too; very meta re basically adding functions you just wish you had, just before you get them.  One major tip - you're going to lose humans (unless you're one of those savants out there) - I've lost thousands - to the extent I got an achievement for it.  Also, this game for us ordinary mortals I think expects you to work on the fly, i.e, keep testing commands in game and work the solution out as you go.  All in all, but for the odd fiddly controls re the dog, this is a brilliant puzzler.  Highly highly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: What if "Journey" was a puzzle game?In "Humanity", you play as a dog made of light. Your goal is to make humans achieve things. Your obstacles to that? Unsurprisingly, humans.The gameplay usually consists of setting up commands for a flow of humans to direct them into completing objectives. Sometimes the setup happens in real time, sometimes it has to be preprogrammed. The puzzles can require automation, platforming, or even be metroidvanias.In the story mode, the dog (the player) receives a goal to help humans. That 15-hour journey is a very unpredictable campaign and truly a wild ride. Combined with the abstract graphics and experimental soundtrack, the experience is one of a kind.The game has two extra modes. While I can't comment on the VR component, custom levels I've played have been hit-or-miss: there are some interesting ideas, but the content is mostly linear or simple. At the very least, the community is active and the discovery of new levels is straightforward.For me, it's an interesting concept in an unusual wrapper of visuals and sounds. It's really a fulfilling piece of art, and I hope you give this game a chance.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very clever game, with interesting, mind-bending puzzles which force you to think and plan. A lot of the puzzles aren't "set it and forget it", but rather require you to have a degree of real-time interaction while the level is flowing in order to solve them. I haven't had to think "outside the box" like this since Portal II. If problem-solving puzzle games are your thing, this is a solid entry in the genre. There's no pressure, there's no dying, there's only the binary status of you either solve the level or you don't. The game is aesthetically pleasing, with relatively simple graphics being all that's needed for a super entertaining gameplay loop. Kudos to the devs for a genuinely creative experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Humanity is a puzzle game that challenges you to guide masses of humans through various obstacles and scenarios using simple commands. The game is developed by Enhance Games, the creators of Tetris Effect and Rez, and it shows in the stunning visuals and music that accompany each level. It is not just a game, but an experience that explores the themes of human nature, cooperation, conflict, and creativity. The game offers over 100 levels that range from easy to hard, and each one introduces new mechanics and twists that keep you on your toes. You will encounter enemies, allies, traps, switches, portals, weapons, vehicles, and more as you manipulate time and physics to reach your goal. The puzzles are clever and satisfying to solve, and sometimes require you to think outside the box. This is a game that I highly recommend to anyone who enjoys puzzle games or wants to try something different. It is a game that will make you think and feel as you move on.
_childDocuments_.name: HUMANITY

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent puzzle game. Starts off fairly simple and straight forward but becomes increasingly complicated with each stage, with the later stages throwing quite a few game play twists your way. Watching your crowds of humans reach their goal is so fulfilling and cathartic, knowing that it was your creativity and forethought that lead them there.Full of charm and philosophical whimsy; HUMANITY is a must play for fans of the puzzle genre.
_childDocuments_.name: HUMANITY

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. Story mode introduces new mechanics at a nice pace but doesn't drag or overstay its welcome. If you want more maps, there's always user-created levels to choose from. There are a few frustrating levels/achievements here and there, but that's to be expected.(Playtime's a bit inflated because I was afk for a bit, real playtime is probably closer to 10-15 hours, depending on achievements/completion)I did't try the VR yet but the game looks and sounds very good so it might be a neat addition to the experience.
_childDocuments_.name: HUMANITY

_childDocuments_.review: Very interesting and engaging (mostly) puzzle game! I really enjoyed the change of pace that comes with the new mechanics for every new level. And at the end, the game actually becomes something quite different compared to the beginning.Most puzzles are nice difficulty, some are pretty easy and some are quite hard, and a few can feel pretty tedious, especially if you want to go for 100%. But, overall, very pleasant experience!
_childDocuments_.name: HUMANITY

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, this game is very well done. The puzzles and mechanics are interesting and it is generally satisfying to work out the solution. The only complaint I had was that there are several sections where the game ceases being about the puzzle and instead forces the player to rely on player dexterity rather than puzzle solving. But overall, those few stages don't detract from the overall game, even if I found those segments unsatisfying. All in all, recommended as a fun and enjoyable puzzle game with a few bumps.
_childDocuments_.name: HUMANITY

_childDocuments_.review: I've enjoyed this game, though too many puzzles feel like there's really only one solution. I'd prefer a looser approach with many tools and paths available. This would lead to a coarse solutions more easily and early but then eggs you on into a loop of finding a better way until you're satisfied with your solution. This game isn't that.I still recommend the game though. Even with the constraints the puzzles are fun and varied and I haven't played "Lemmings" in 30 years. That's been overdue for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: HUMANITY

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a truly excellent puzzle game. The story mode continues to add new mechanics/twists through to the end which help to make the game feel fresh through the full playthrough. While not all of the later level mechanics are quite to my taste, I was happy to see the developers take some big swings and overall I enjoyed the entire experience quite a bit.The addition of the level creator/sharing adds some great replay value with quality user levels finding their way to the front of the offerings.
_childDocuments_.name: HUMANITY

_childDocuments_.review: my brain hasn't really had to think like this before. its a similar feeling to the first time i played portal.  There's a chill ambiance. Definitely a game to take a break from and come back to when your mind is fresh.  Really cool.  A tad overpriced on release though. Unless youre making your own courses and getting really into it, i could see the initial price point. i really just wanted to play the story mode. (at least at the time of writing)
_childDocuments_.name: HUMANITY

_childDocuments_.review: Humanity is a fantastic puzzle game from newcomer developers tha ltd and veteran publisher/co-developer Enhance. As one would expect from a game that boasts Tetsuya Mizuguchi's involvement, Humanity is a visual and audio treat. The puzzle difficulty is finely tuned; not so difficult that you'll be frustrated, but just challenging enough that you'll feel like a genius when the solution comes to you. Plus, you get to play as a cute dog!
_childDocuments_.name: HUMANITY

_childDocuments_.review: Maybe pick it up on sale?For the first two thirds of the game it feels like a good spiritual successor to the old game Lemmings. For the last third it feels like a showcase for their level editor and not much else.For instance, after knocking out some satisfying puzzle levels, the game shifts to just pointing troops in a war of attrition. Then all of a sudden you're playing follow the leader through Metal Gear Solid style stealth missions.  As the tone skips all over towards the latter part of the game it really is just a transparent show and tell on what sort of experiences their level editor can deliver.
_childDocuments_.name: HUMANITY

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a relaxing puzzle game that doesn't create difficulty by arbitrarily limiting you, this is the game for you. The tools you can use from level to level change, but you can let your streams of humans fall to their deaths all you like, place and replace as many instructions as you like. The only thing the game wants you to do is solve the puzzle.Some goldies are very difficult for me so far, but I haven't made it very far and I'm still fairly new with the tool set.
_childDocuments_.name: HUMANITY

_childDocuments_.review: It's a nice spacial-cognitive-reasoning/logic puzzle - and I do think the VR adds to he experience and can help figure out the solutions (PC, HP Reverb G2, 4090)......interestingly (and I'm only on the Green Orb so far), some of the solutions require more than a) simple chess-piece moves and b) timing moves....;oP
_childDocuments_.name: HUMANITY

_childDocuments_.review: This is a surprisingly good puzzle game, it was consistently challenging, but the difficulty curve was steady and never felt unfair.  It changes the style of puzzles consistently from start to finish meaning you never get too used to anything (and probably gives a lot of fodder for user created maps.)  Was fairly long for a puzzle game, even if I was smarter I imagine there was at least 10 hours of puzzles in it.
_childDocuments_.name: HUMANITY

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a well designed, unique puzzle game. It takes what was great about the old school classic, lemmings, and transposed it 30 years later. While also adding it's own unique ideas and twists to the formula. I'm only on chapter 5 right now, but from what I seen, it starts to borrow a bit from the old indie hit "darwinia" as well .
_childDocuments_.name: HUMANITY

_childDocuments_.review: Humanity is probably the best puzzle game to come out this year. Especially in VR, the experience is awesome; gameplay is very unique from any other puzzle game--moving humans with a dog that collects powers along the story mode, and challenges the player with amazing courses that depend on quick changes and good path-finding.Enhance once again making a great, and beautiful game in the puzzle series.(also, before Enhance was founded, Q Entertainment was their main studio. why do I mention this? because that studio made my #1 favorite puzzle game -- Meteos; a game for the DS you should check out too)
_childDocuments_.name: HUMANITY

_childDocuments_.review: Humanity is an enchantingly peculiar game that combines an adorable canine, mind-bending puzzles, and a dash of strategy. I couldn't resist diving into this canine-filled adventure. If you enjoyed Lemmings back in the day, prepare to fall head over paws for this one.Visually, Humanity is a treat for the eyes. The art style is delightful, showcasing vibrant environments that feel straight out of a dream. Each level presents a unique and increasingly complex challenge, requiring you to utilise the different canine abilities at your disposal. The puzzle-solving possibilities are endless. It's incredibly satisfying to witness endless loops of humans falling and re-spawning over and over again.The level of creativity in Humanity is commendable. The developers have managed to strike a perfect balance between accessibility and depth. The early stages gently introduce you to the game mechanics, while later levels will put your strategic thinking to the test. It's a joy to tackle each puzzle and witness the "aha!" moments as you find the optimal solution.Additionally, the inclusion of a robust level editor provides endless replayability, so you can create and share your own mind-bending challenges.However, it's worth noting that Humanity may not appeal to everyone. Its whimsical nature and peculiar concept might not resonate with those seeking more traditional gaming experiences. Nevertheless, for those open to an enchanting and unconventional adventure, Humanity is a hidden gem waiting to be discovered.In conclusion, Humanity is a beautifully odd and captivating game that combines puzzle-solving, doggos, and humans in a way that will leave you thoroughly entertained. With its charming visuals, clever level design, and addictive gameplay, this title shares a spiritual kinship with the beloved Lemmings franchise while adding its own unique twists. Rating: 4.5/5
_childDocuments_.name: HUMANITY

_childDocuments_.review:
SAVE HUMANITY, FIND YOURSELF. 

The year is 2156 and Earth has been decimated. All that remains of the once great planet is desert and human life is dwindling due to water and food scarcity. You play as Landon, one of the last surviving humans, who stumbles upon a wormhole. The wormhole you accidentally find transports you light years across the universe to a strange and beautiful planet where you meet a new alien friend named Zip. 

With Zip as your guide, you will hunt for a new planet for you and your wife Jessie to inhabit and carry on human existence.

Created by a single developer over two years, this story rich and atmospheric game poses many questions about what makes life worth living and how we as humans can save our planet before climate change destroys it.

Will you be the one to save humanity before it obliterates itself?
_childDocuments_.name: HUMANITY

name: SpellForce: Conquest of Eo
detailed_description: In this turn-based strategy game set in the fantastic world of SpellForce, take up the mantle of your master as the heir to his mysterious wizard’s tower. Study a multitude of spells to cast over the lands around you, summon fantastical minions and train mighty warriors to roam the world. Fight in fast-paced but tactical turn-based battles. Explore the Realm of Eo Win over mighty heroes to go on adventures for you, find useful artefacts and ingredients or bring back riches. Seek out talented apprentices to expand your domain and workers to gather a wealth of resources for you. Unearth the secrets inherited from your master and follow his quest to tap and unleash the ultimate source of magical power – the Allfire! Face powerful foes Among the other mages, there are those who would oppose your rise to power. You will have to face great armies and even greater ambitions of your rival Mages. Can you survive the struggle for domination? To expand your domain, you will need to control sources of Allfire, so you can fill your grimoire with new magical spells, craft mighty artefacts, and expand and improve your tower. Choose wisely Become a Necromancer creating dozens of powerful undead, an Alchemist concocting potions and explosive vials for use in battle or an Artificer crafting glyphs and magical items to furnish your troops with. Bolster your might with over 60 spells and more than 100 different troops from lowly goblins to majestic griffons. Leave your mark Befriend cities, harvest resources, and expand your domain. Fill your grimoire with arcane knowledge to best your rivals as you vie for sources of power. Hunt arcane artefacts and unearth the long-hidden secrets of the Shapers or take control of mythical locations to absorb their power. Improve your tower and furnish it with new rooms to grow your dominion, with upgrades ranging from a necromancer’s crypt to the mystical crystal chamber. Tower on the fly Your immense magical sophistication allows your tower to levitate from the ground and travel the lands. On your path to exploit the sources of magical power on Eo, you will face New Purity fanatics, hostile granite dwarves, and bloodthirsty orcs. Encounter undead, demons, and monsters as you explore forgotten ruins or help a village haunted by ghosts. You might even need to face the other wizards’ armies of minions and best them in battle so you can march on your competitors’ towers and reduce them to rubble. Or perhaps you might find a way for you to appease them and profit from their knowledge? SpellForce: Conquest of Eo lets you dive into a rich world, filled to the brim with magic and adventure. Will you succeed or perish in the struggle to become the greatest mage the world has ever seen? Expand and improve your tower and construct new rooms to forge your wizard’s path Choose from one of three archetypes and six spell lists, all allowing different styles of play Recruit individual heroes and apprentices to lead your troops Make the living interactive grimoire reveal new secrets and spells to you Craft anything from magical glyphs and artefacts to undead minions Explore over 600 adventures different with each procedurally generated campaign
