short_description: On a journey to great magical might, explore and control the lands of Eo in this ever-changing turn-based strategy role-playing game. Field armies and heroes in tactical combat, finish hundreds of quests, and gather spells and artefacts to become the most powerful mage of all.

_childDocuments_.review: A caveat: I beta tested this game. However, even with me beta testing the game, there was nothing that *made* me play it for over 300 hours. What made me play the game over 300 hours was its deep, fun gameplay, incredible variety and how much it pushes turn-based strategy games in a direction they needed to be pushed.The game basically takes the earliest, most fun parts of a 4X game and extend them over the entire game. From my perspective, this pushes the game out of what is conventionally accepted as being a 4X game out of it, but it actually improves the overall enjoyability of the game. The combinatorial possibilities of different starts is pretty large, and the replayability is immense as a result of that. The static map may turn some people off, but frankly with everything else that changes between runs I honestly appreciate the stability. This is already getting long so I will say that on the whole the game is a lot of fun, really good, and I highly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: SpellForce: Conquest of Eo

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a mixture of the best aspects of turn based strategy and RPG. Every hour the game becomes deeper: new mechanics, units, artifacts, spells and so on become available to the player.For the entire playthrough (about 35 hours), I met only a couple of small bugs, what is pretty rare in our time. Just a week after the release of the game, the developers released a patch dedicated to player offers and complaints about the game. Cause they read and responce in discussions. Yes, it is possible.
_childDocuments_.name: SpellForce: Conquest of Eo

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not well designed. I started a new campaign and the game never explained how to level up my tower, so I spent most of the first 50 turns figuring that out. Once I worked it out it told me I had to recruit a second apprentice. I did so and she was immediately killed by a massive stack of monsters. The game told me that the only way to get her back was with a spell, and to learn the spell I had to do a quest. I completed the quest and it resurrected my apprentice on an island where she can't get off, and my next quest needs her to travel somewhere else. This seems to be fairly common with the game - it randomly generates some aspects and makes no attempt to ensure that the game is actually completable on any particular play through. The assumption is that if it generates an impossible situation you just start again, which is not how games should work in 2023.
_childDocuments_.name: SpellForce: Conquest of Eo

_childDocuments_.review: It is a fun and innovative take blending traditional Fantasy 4X with RPG and Rogue-like Elements, there is a lot to be desired, namely a lack of a detailed quest journal can be particularly frustrating. It also has a lot of room for improvement, the upgrade chains for units, and perhaps some way of upgrading units to move from tier 1 to 2 and beyond. However it is very challenging and fun, I highly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: SpellForce: Conquest of Eo

_childDocuments_.review: Pirated the game at first and then decided to buy it to support the creators. Love the spellforce universe and the mechanics and randomness of the game. Has a ton of replay-ability to it too and gives you a very old timey feel like Heroes of might and magic. They really dont make games like this anymore. Really hoping that they add a demonologist that summons demons as a starting class at one point since of the enemies is exactly that and I'm anxiously looking to any new content they release.
_childDocuments_.name: SpellForce: Conquest of Eo

_childDocuments_.review: I like a lot about this game: the art, the design, the Crafting mechanics etc. One thing that hasn’t been said as much, though, is the excellent controller support, which is much appreciated!I’m not too sure yet about the replayability, but even if it might not lend itself to countless playthroughs, I’m sure getting my money’s worth out of this game.
_childDocuments_.name: SpellForce: Conquest of Eo

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great on so many levels, challenging, engaging and beautifully presented. Not a sandbox style game but heaps of customisation to make each play feel unique. Clocked about 100 hours on it and have completed almost everything in the game. Very resonantly priced for the content and hoping there is a new dlc map in the future, with this the only thing holding back the replay ability of this fantastic game. Highly recommend
_childDocuments_.name: SpellForce: Conquest of Eo

_childDocuments_.review: Unlike other conquer-the-world games, you start playing S:CoE as an upstart; standing against 4 mages responsible for killing your old teacher, who got too curious for his own good. Many new players get overwhelmed because no other wizards start off at the early levels like most games -- and they are out to get you.The game has three schools of magic, and you are not restricted in your spell choices. A necromancer can create a vampire, and cast a life spell on it (like Invulnerability). Only down side to this game is the map is set. You can start in different places but the world map never changes. Not a game breaker but can make multiple playthroughs a little vanilla.
_childDocuments_.name: SpellForce: Conquest of Eo

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun game and a supportive dev team that listen and interact with their player base often.If you liked genres like Age Of Wonders and Planet fall there are good chances you will like this.This game is unique however in the way they approach your rise to power with many side quests. Also it's not expensive for what it offers.After having played AOW 4, imho SpellForce Conquest of EO offers way more fun but it costs around 70$ cad less for now.
_childDocuments_.name: SpellForce: Conquest of Eo

_childDocuments_.review: Such a gem of a game! So happy to see another dlc is coming out! If you're into turn base tactical combat and likes a bit of stories and rpg elements, definitely try this out! There is a lot of flavor and themes into the map design, so much so that I think it's much better for me than aoe4. Both're great games, for some reason, I love this one a bit more!
_childDocuments_.name: SpellForce: Conquest of Eo

_childDocuments_.review: No. Not worth your time when despite updated difficulty settings they are mostly ignored by the game and all enemies dive your tower/lodge constantly, early game and non stop every 5-7 turns. A tedious game where you are always on your backfoot having to play defensively the whole time just to adapt to what the 4 mages throw at your constantly. No quest log and broken quests (eg. being sent to the same 3 battlefields to search for something taking around 10-12 turns to finally find the item in one that was of course already searched over and over) so good luck trying to keep track of what is most important for each stack to do in every turn. The game doesn't feel finished and this is highlighted by "changes" that were patched days after release. This game doesn't really know what it wants to be and suffers because of it and a toxic community to top it all off.
_childDocuments_.name: SpellForce: Conquest of Eo

_childDocuments_.review: Crazy addictive! I just started Spellforce: Conquest og Eo and it's unlike anything i've ever played. Resource management like Age of Empires meets the sandbox of mount and blade meets classic tactical turn-based rpg battles in my first run with the game Iwent from not knowing what I was in for to 4 hours later receiving my first ominous warning from a member of the Circle as I chased down a baron's lost ring and encroached on another mages land in the process . I've been playing on my Steamdeck seamlessly and having a great time!
_childDocuments_.name: SpellForce: Conquest of Eo

_childDocuments_.review: Having beaten the game now (atleast on the lowest difficulty so I could go through at what seemed a more reasonable pace), I'm ready to give a more indepth review! Overview:This is a wonderful hybrid of RPG mechanics, turn-based tactics and 4x gameplay. However, by trying to have all of these elements in one game, each one does fall a little bit short of greatness.  The RPG mechanics allow for a lot of variety in how you customize your tower, abilities and gameplay, but it can feel very constricted with a semi-randomized path and most "cool" options being somewhat suboptimal or wholly unnecessary after a certain point.  The turn-based tactics are solid, and the AI can give a fun fight here and there, but it lacks in depth and felt repetitive after a while. For the 4x gameplay, it's very fun at the start and keeping you mobile means you can't just turtle to success, however, it does not really scale well.  Progression:In the game, the player can progress in a myriad of ways, you can upgrade troops with runes, get new spells, customize the rooms in your tower, etc.  It's good! Though it's held back from greatness by random spell unlocks (For example, really needed the basic heal spell, but it just kept picking other spells for me to research first.) and from units having limited level-up/glyph options.  Additionally, you will find that trying to spam units with a certain resistance, or adding 3 +2 range glyphs to a spellcaster makes victory assured. Pacing: Pacing is vital for any good strategy game.  Here it does well pretty much throughout the game.  The early game exploration is fun and exciting, the mid-game rush to get enough resources and hold back the Circle is fantastic, but the end-game is where the whole thing stumbles a bit.  The reason being is the map becomes so completely full of quest markers, ore markers, enemy and bandit stacks, allfire spots, etc.  It becomes too busy, and by the time you reach the endgame, it's going to be going through the motions to victory, and this busy interface kept distracting and detracting from that final yard of gameplay. Presentation:Honestly, all high marks here.  The world has character, the various lands do have specific unit/element/tactics that do differentiate them enough to keep a new region being of interest.  The map itself is beautifully detailed, though it is all on one map, so the replay value might leave something to be desired.  (Some elements are random each campaign, but really it's just camp/allfire/resource node locations, the cities and enemy types are static.)
_childDocuments_.name: SpellForce: Conquest of Eo

_childDocuments_.review: Instantly liked the game the moment I started playing. It seems to do a lot of things well such as story telling and immersion. The combat is a bit basic but still interesting enough. The overall campaign is good from what I have played so far. However, there are some things I would love to see improved. I would love if there was some customisation elements to the game, like if you were able to customise how your mage looked. Even if it was just cosmetic at first and only showed in still images, currently there are only three stills that depict your character and they are dependent upon whether you chose alchemy, necromancy or glyph magic and I'm not in love with any of them. It can take you out of the game a little to never see your mage and then suddenly they are represented by a dwarf still image just because you went down the artificer root.  Would then be great if you could use your mage in battle, like if you were able to use a astral projection spell or something (in order to explain why you are still in the tower but also leading an army). Lastly, it would be great if there were more crossovers between the three arch types of magic, like rather then choosing alchemy at the start, you are able to do all three and need to devote research to one in order to make it more powerful. But even as is, the game so far seems to be worth playing.
_childDocuments_.name: SpellForce: Conquest of Eo

_childDocuments_.review: Not a winner for me.Why do stacks of units, even when they are down to 1hp, still deal full damage on retaliation/attack? It only makes sense if it is a large single unit, like a dragon/giant/etc.This is something HOMM got right decades ago.For example, a unit that appears to be 5 goblins deals the exact same amount of damage with its abilities/attacks when it is 100% hp and when it is on 1%hp.The magic is very basic and not involved in combat.Hero upgrades, when they level up, are rubbish. Unit's can't become cooler units. Army sizes are really small. Hardly any spells in the game.I think it needs a lot of work to become something deep.It feels like a boardgame that's been made into a computer game, like for like.
_childDocuments_.name: SpellForce: Conquest of Eo

_childDocuments_.review: Even with 100 hours in this game, I still do not recommend it. At least not in the current state. Cons:Auto-Resolve is very broken. Units that are literally invulnerable to the enemies in the opposing stack will be defeated or destroyed. An army with a strength of 900 will be destroyed by a stack with a strength of 400... etc. This means that you will need to manually do almost every battle.Map Control: You get resources by having your mages create a lodge, in order for that lodge to extract all the resources it will usually take 12 turns. But if you want your stack to keep moving, then the lodge gets attacked and you need to backtrack to save it, because you cannot build a new one while it's being attacked. Also, your "Hero" cannot build a lodge.Terrain is Pointless: with the exception of the bridge maps, there is basically no difference between any battle map other than aesthetic, and everything moves so fast that it doesn't really matter. You will have a mosh pit around your melee often before you've even had a turn.Unit Xp: It takes a long, long time to level units up. As a result, any loses are extremely punishing, as the difference between a level 15 goblin with runes and a level 3 without them is night and day. No reason for multiple stacks: Only your stacks with a hero or mage will have any chance to perform well, so having back up stacks running around and draining your resources is pointless, since they cannot claim resources on their own and will almost certainly be killed in a battle or two.Crafting: Curve is bad, early and mid game you won't have the resources to do what you want, late game you will probably have more than enough.Quests: There is no log for what to do, but that doesn't matter because the specifics of the quests are basically meaningless 90% of the time. Larger, more complex quests would be far superior to the hundred you just hit next on.Pros:The spells are generally interesting and you will use many of them.It can be fun to select a new ability for a unit on level up.The map is large and generally fine to traverse. The game really just needs a ton of quality of life improvements and a shortening of the time to beat the game.
_childDocuments_.name: SpellForce: Conquest of Eo

_childDocuments_.review: This game is sort of something new in the tactical combat / 4X genre. It has really rich fabular plot and MANY, MANY RPG elements. It is NOT typical 4X game. It takes everything what is absolutely the best from 4X games ands the best part of some RPGs and compiles it with success.I dont remember when last time I spent so much time with the game within few sessions. I start at 7pm and in a second its 5am!If you like tactical combat and you like discovering, evolving things, experimenting, etc. this game is for you. Graphics is really good, music is really good, the whole concept of the game is fresh and really engaging.Game is a bit hard at the begining. It is recommended to play it 3-4 times to consume whole content. I am fascinated with this game, the main concept of the game and the level of entertainment when playing it.Big recommendation after 40h of gameplay.For this price it is just MUST HAVE for any one who likes game like Age of Wonders but with muuuch deeper RPG element.
_childDocuments_.name: SpellForce: Conquest of Eo

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game but it feels incomplete. There's basically a single map for the entire game and the same units, stories and progression for every gameplay (which happens on the same map) with simply a different starting point. Character creation is exceeding limited with only 3 options and 5 branches and the spells are shared amongst characters. There's no feeling of accomplishment or progression, just feels so bland it's not worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: SpellForce: Conquest of Eo

_childDocuments_.review: Somewhat similar to Might and Magic of old.  Good mechanics, fun combat, fairly deep crafting system for a game of this type. _childDocuments_.review: I hear a lot of Age of Wonders references, which is fair, but if this reminds me of anything, it's probably Sorcerer King, because you do not start as one wizard among equals, but rather in a much lower, underdog position. In Sorcerer King you played as a sort of renegade in a battle that was already lost, here you join as a newcomer in a race that seems almost over.Another thing that the two have in common is that at the start, your power is so pathetic that the forces-that-be barely even want to seem to be bothered to deal with you at all.There are 3 classes that you can choose from, each drive a rather diffent focus. One lets you focus on crafting consumables such as Bombs that can make any unit useful, as any unit can use items, you can create mighty armies as a necromancer, or as an artifcer deck out your armies with enhancing glyphs and artifacts that can make your army really powerful.Many compare this to 4X which I feel is not quite accurate. There is a base yes, it can be expanded, it can even be moved around later, but there is no conquering 30 cities and be forever trapped setting up building queues. There is one base, and factions that you can ally with, for better units, equipments and more.I think the idea behind that was to remove tedium, and it's working for me. I often get the urge to just abandon a (4X) session and start from scratch once a certain management effort level treshold has been exceeded.I also like the pacing. You get to choose to some extent how fast it is. The harder you push the game, the harder it pushes back. But if you just feel like chilling for a few rounds and create items or artifacts, the game will usually let you do that.If I recommend this game depends on whether you came for the RPG/RTS Hybrid you already know, or whether you appreciate RPG and Strategy games in general, and also fresh ideas, because this game has a fair number of them. In a genre that has grown a little bit stale to me, I really appreciate this one!

_childDocuments_.review: SpellForce: Conquest of EO is a turn-based strategy game with RPG elements, I would say it is as if Age of Wonders and Kings Bounty have a baby. The game focuses mainly on single player experience, with no multiplayer options available.The game boasts impressive artwork, but the limited number of unique pictures and images is a disappointment with quests often sharing the same picture again and again. Despite its recent release, the game still needs further polishing, with various bugs, like some skills and abilities not working as they are supposed to do. Some of these issues have been addressed in recent updates, while others remain unresolved.One of the strengths of SpellForce: Conquest of EO is its vast and expansive map, allowing players to fly their base tower across the game world.One of the controversial features is random leveling of units and heroes. When leveled, the unit gets a choice of two new abilities or upgrades and it seems to be completely random. This is nice from an RPG point of view, because it adds some variety to the game. It is a nightmare from a strategy perspective, because enemies have the same mechanics so you can sometimes check a unit one by one for its upgrades.In conclusion, SpellForce: Conquest of EO is a solid attempt at combining RPG and strategy gameplay, with a lot of potential. While it may not be perfect, it still offers an enjoyable and engaging single player experience for fans of the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: I've very mixed feelings about this game. On the one hand, it has some rather interesting ideas and game machanics clearly inspired by beloved classic Master of Magic. On the other hand, they unfortunately chose to make this more like a turn based RPG on an insanely large map. And while I wouldn't say that this can't work out, there's a bunch of problems with how it's implemented here.First, the game is extremely random. It's barely possible to plan anything ahead, since you're getting stuff like spell formulas or building blue prints just randomly by quests or special events. You can't even choose what units to build or heros to recruit, since you depend on what you can find. Not to mention that you can't look up pretty much anything. And yeah, be prepared to loose an important hero randomly by a special event anytime.Secondly, the game is extremely grindy. Since resources run out, you constantly have to rebuild your hero lodges, move your tower and swarm the map with harvesters. And to a certain degree, this could still work to keep you on your toes. But it's just never ending and turns more and more to annoying busy work the longer it goes. And this gets even more problematic with another major flaw, that being...Thirdly, the game is slow. Both in terms of pacing and unit movement. It took me about 15 hours just to get through the early game to the point where I'm getting the circle tasks. And now I'm expected to conquer the whole map and hunt down and kill all circle mages (amongst other tasks - it's quite the ToDo list, even if you don't have to do them all ). On a map that rivals the size of the Immortal Empires map in TW Warhammer 3, just with units so slow that they barely reach a quarter of the speed there. That probably beats every 4X endgame or MMO in terms of grinding and tedium. I'd estimate at least an additional 30 hours to just finish the game. And thanks, I pass! Even Master of Magic had the spell of Mastery to avoid endgame tedium like this.And fourth, the battles don't have auto-fight. And sorry, auto-resolve is no replacement for this. Speed is also too slow there, even if I'm not sure if that can be changed in the options.On a side note, while I did like the alchemy system in principle, most of its recipes felt pretty much useless. In a game with so many fights, the effects have to be permanent and not just temporary for one battle to make a difference. And using it for room extensions made no sense. Like none at all. Just imagine, that in order to get paladins you have to brew the most deadly poisons you can think of. WTF!!!On a more positive note, I think the game does a surprisingly good job for its presentation. The map art in particular is amongst the best I've seen so far and can easily compete with the likes of Humankind. Can't say the same for the 2D art though. Battles are still decent, but don't reach the quality of AoW.Overall, I think for a game about exploration, questing with tactical combat, the King's Bounty games did a way better job. And for a small turn based 4X fantasy rogue like, Conquest of Elysium has more classes with more unique play styles, better pacing and more customization options if you can live with the simplistic art.That said, I still think this game could excel as a real 4X game, if its somewhat tagged on systems would be taken and refined into a new reimagination of Master of Magic. Unfortunately, this game ain't it yet.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm 20 hours in and I am very sad to have to NOT recommend this game. I bought this thinking it was like Heroes of Might and magic, or Age of Wonders. And while it has some similarities it has some things that are very much its own.You cannot get higher tier units by yourself. You have to go to prioritize going to random villages and grind quests to get them to like you enough to give you a schematic for a better barracks, or to hire a unit from them, or to possibly learn how to include a 6th zombie in your army (what?). Because of this behavior, after 2 losses I had to give up on playing spoiler free and google where to go to increase army stack sizes, because my size 5 army full of tier 2 units was getting hammer by size 7 armies of tier 4 and 3 units by the enemy AI.The story encourages you to build lodges to harvest materials, and capture allfire nodes, but this hyper-aggravates the AI so they hunt you down mercilessly.  Units take a long time to build, so losing an army feels catastrophic and hard to come back from. If you only have one training slot it can take 20+ days to rebuild an army, which encourages you to reload when you get wrecked.  This feels cheesy but necessary, and is further complicated by the fact that there is no quicksave or quickload buttons, forcing constant menu navigation and loading screens.You don't realize it at first but you have a timer. Your growth triggers the enemy to attack you, so even if you keep to yourself and try to build up, once you are strong enough the hammer falls.  I really enjoyed the gameplay up until that moment. Once they lock on to you it doesnt matter if you try to lift off your flying wizard tower and relocate. They will hunt you down and do not stop.And after 3 runs, and 20 hours, I don't have the energy to try this balancing act a 4th time.

_childDocuments_.review: On the surface, this might seem like your run-of-the-mill assymetrical 4X game, where you start of as a weak mage and try to rise to the top, facing off various enemies, from wild beasts, to anti magic fanatics, and even powerful demons and elementals, all the while trying to avoid or appease already established rival mages, who are much, much more powerful than you. Indeed the game is all that, but also so much more. I find this a rough gem. As an experienced 4X player, my biggest gripe with this type of games has been poor scaling. Take any 4X, fantasy/sci-fi/historical and I've always felt overburdened in late game, which limited my enjoyment. Too many cities or castles, too many units or armies, too many things to defend and pay attention to, to the point that it often felt like a chore.Here, devs had the guts to go for something different - even in very late game, you will only ever use a few armies. You start with one "city" (your magic tower) and you end with only one as well. What's the strategy then? Glad you asked! Depending on your class, your play style and RNG you will end up building your tower in a very different way to suit very different purposes. What happens if one of those circle magi takes an unhealthy interest in you too soon, or you need different resources not found in your current regions? Simple, just levitate your tower and move elsewhere. There is truly an immense amount of possibilities to rise to the top. You need to raise your relations with a neutral settlement, to be able to upgrade your tower and buy/build better units? You can bribe the city. Or you can use magic to influence it. Or you can take control of their taverns and slowly build your reputation over time. Or finish their quests. New players might feel overwhelmed at start, but I promise it doesn't take long to figure it out.Even though there are some balance issues, and very rarely you can get in problems due to bad RNG, there are always options. It is certainly a very strong recommendation from me. The foundations the game is built on are very strong. It only needs balance tweaks and more content at this point. Hopefully, devs will continue to support it for a long time and hopefully some of its innovations will carry over to other 4X games.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is rich, and quite unique in the genre. At a glance, it looks like a fantasy 4x game (ala Master of Magic). Well, you can destroy your rivals... but doing that alone won't see you to victory.There's a lot to this game. Much more elegant than a mere 4x. It's quite a challenge and will frustrate you with the learning curve - but suffering loss often isn't a game-ender like many similar games. In my first win, I almost quit half a dozen times thinking I had lost. But perseverance pays and things aren't as bad as they seem - because this isn't a 4x game where losing a valuable city can be a game-ender. You take your losses, replace them and experiment with glyphs, buffs and unit combos to come back stronger and win the game, like I did.Surprisingly deep and sophisticated, elegantly put together, frustrating and rewarding, fun challenge.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Just one of the best 4x games around, terrific turn-based hex tactics, "node"-based mechanisms for research/mana that harken back to Master Of Magic and do so in a way that is ultimately satisfying.  The best thing about this game is that the difficulty settings are pretty modular, so you can have a very challenging AI setup or a very RPG-ish storymode, your choice.  The game is also one of the best balanced games for 1p that I've ever played, serious thought went in to every mechanic and possible combo, and while there are still some exploitable "broken" combinations, that's part of the fun of this sort of game IMO.  The AI/environment can very easily kick your a** if you play on hard difficulties.Just one word about replayability, if you are a fan of the eXplore function of the 4x, you may be frustrated by the lack of a procedural random map choice; You are essentially playing the game on a single fantasy continent, and while resources are randomized for location, the major cities are always in the same place and act more as resources than places to conquer.  With several starting locations, magic schools, and crafting systems (you pick one at game start and that's a permanent and unchanging part of your "civ") the game has a huge amount of replay value, but less than Civ and their ilk.  I got a couple hundred hours out of the title and still enjoy dropping in to a game now and again.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit 2024-10-2The latest expansion actually added Randomised worlds. So along with my hours put into this, it is now changing to recommended. It is still NOT a 4x strategy game. Its more of a RPG strategy game. And with that understanding it is probably worth playing.Edit 2024-02-28While I still can't recommend the game, my view is now more more Neutral. Come at this game like its a 4X and it is lacking. Approach it more as an RPG with Strategy Elements and its easier to take. With that view I was able to play through the game finally.The game feels unfinished, as it is seriously lacking things that give others it is genre staying power.  Their does not seem to be any RNG for a Random Map, you only have a select few maps simply based on difficulty.You always start with Goblin units, with no real explanation of why you start with Goblins, other than they being the basic starter units.The same script plays out time and time again.Their is no Player Character unit, unlike other Spell Force games, that can level up and own the battlefield as a powerful Mage. Player character exists only in the Narrative. No early obvious way of increasing Army size.Maybe I need to play longer to see some of this, but can't really recommend this game.Edit: Played a bit more. And basically agree with my earlier review.The game really needs a few more RNG features for world generation.  Always start out with the same army of goblins and then whatever familar based on my Crafting Choices. Always get the same Apprentice multiple turns in, always have the exact same fights to reclaim the reserarch. The map might change if I pick a different map out of the choices of 5, but beyond that way to much is static.The AI is also just wierd. They move on the map, and claim sources that you have already claimed. Even while some of them say they are willing to give you a chance. Then they get angry that your inside their border. I get that they are not suppose to be treating you as an equal. But the AI interactions, seem incredibly limit, and one sided. You can initate doing favours for them. You can give them all-fire sources out of a desire to appears them. I get your suppose to be insignificate, but some of them do have small amount of quests, and are willing to ask you to do things, but that only seems to slightly delays the inevitable fact that you have to go to war with them. As their are far more ways to lower your Rep including the static message that lowers it by a set amount of a number of turns.  Even though some of them say they are willing to wait and see...Edit - December 27.Game is not bad, but it it just feels limited.  5 Goblin units in the army.... the Rng only ever has one of them learn pack tactics... neither of my three wolves learned it that game either. _childDocuments_.review: An excellent turn based strategy game. They took the combat system from their Fantasy General 2 game, added elements from Age of Wonders / Master of Magic and created a story driven strategy game with its own twist. _childDocuments_.review: An interesting and engaging game. Easiest way to think about it is like if you could build mega tall in a 4x game. You only have one city (your mage tower) which houses your infrastructure with outposts (your mage lodges) which give you spots of influence around the map. You can move your Tower around which gives an interesting combination of nomadic and tall play style. If you enjoy 4x games or strategy games this game is worth a try.There are some issues however, first being lack of a quest journal. It makes tracking the info for quests miserable which sucks since quests are a common and otherwise interesting part of the game. The second issue is that alot of info about how different systems work is non existent or hidden from what I have seen. This will likely get solved as the game matures and a third party wiki gets established but a more expansive in game encyclopedia would be useful.Overall I like the game and I see alot of potential going for it, the positives outweigh the negatives heavily but I am far to lazy to list all of the positives.

_childDocuments_.review: Other reviews tell the story : good game, beautiful map, excellent ideas.To answer some badly placed critics about replay, yes, the map is unique. But it is big, and you are mostly stuck around your start point for a long time ; so you can change the start point. In addition, lots of things are random on that map which means that even when you take the same starting point, you get drawn in different directions, depending on where the events send you or where the resources are.If I have one bad thing to say it is that the game is waaayyy too difficult. I played at "balanced" and got ripped big time twice. Well, first game is first game, so that was OK. But second time was a bad surprise. The game is difficult enough when you're just battling quests/random encounters or the occasionnal stack sent against you by one of your opponent. Problem begins when one opponent declares war on you (I don't know how to prevent that). Unless you're ready (meaning you have a full stack ot well upgraded and magically enhanced tier 3 units led by a competent leader), you're toast when said opponent sends you THE army that destroys your tower (you lose that battle : game over). Your opponents will resent your presence, and most of time their patience will run thinner and thinner as time passes. I still have to understand how to keep them at least somewhat happy.

_childDocuments_.review: Mmm, interesting game, really not bad, though not at all what I was expecting. This is quite a different experience from previous Spellforce titles. Previous Spellforce titles were a combo of RPG and RTS, mostly driven by developing your main character and taking them across a number of different maps, each of which presented new challenges. There was a strong element of tower-defence, and it felt more RPG-like.  This game is more like an advanced version of Lords of Magic, with some Heroes III elements thrown in. You do have some quests - or Adventures as it calls them - but this is less RPG/RTS and more turn based strategy. It's not bad, but you don't have the fun of developing and fighting with your main character, and the biggest element taken from previous Spellforce titles is purely the worldbuilding. It's interesting, but I would recommend it to players of CIV-like or strategy games more than to players of RPG titles. Don't expect to enjoy it just from enjoying previous Spellforce games, this is not the same type of game at all.

_childDocuments_.review: Steam Deck controls are really weird, until you get used to them. Then, you will find the control scheme is quite decent, but not great, but your hands will probably start to hurt after a few hours of play. It definitely takes some getting used to, buttons will do different things in every screen you come across. It works, it almost sometimes makes perfect sense, but it just could be so much more copacetic.For instance, when you cast a buff spell on your stack, you use L1/R1 buttons to select a unit in a stack, but you would generally expect d-pad or joystick. When on a screen that uses an on-screen cursor, which is controlled by joystick, and not trackpads for some reason, the cursor is just not visible on certain screens, I had to use the touch screen to select how much mana to spend on a mentalist spell to improve relations with a city.When selecting which abilities to make use of during combat, or on the overworld map, you use the d-pad when making those selections. The trigger buttons are set to be radial menus for some reason, for which the trackpads would be far superior. When using the trigger for radials you need to also input from the joystick to make a radial menu selection. The two radial menus should be on the trackpads. Instead, all you really do with trackpads is zoom in/out. I find that games that use triggers and touchpads heavily are the most ergonomic. This game barely uses either. Instead the vast majority of the time you do everything with with ABYX.Games good tho, I'm gonna keep playing. Im 39 hours in and finally took down my first great mage last night. The writing of the game is surprising decent. More variety in quests would be cool. Very often I find that there is no crafting recipe for a combination of essences and materials.Overall, I would say that there is very little I do not like about this game, and plenty that I do.

_childDocuments_.review: Best blend between AOW-ish and D&D type game play. Things I like better on this game than AOW..1. You can modify individual units within your stacks. 2. Stack size will grow as you gain experience/levels.3. Less resources spread across the map so much more intentional how you move around the map (more strategy)4. Resource depletion.. unlike AOW, most resources are finite.. so you need to move your area of influence around the map.. adding to the strategy of game play... unlike AOW where you can spam Outposts.5. You can retreat from battles.. if  your stack is attacked, you have the option to retreat. Depending on the difficulty level you play, you may or may not survive the retreat.. but units will definitely be very low health afterwards.. Typically two retreat attempts will kill you stack (being attacked from two different AI stacks back to back).6.. there is a ton more.. it just feels more configurable which adds a ton of strategy areas where AOW doesn't have.CONS..1. Nearby stacks don't participate in battles.. I wouldn't call this a big CON, since you can retreat or cancel a battle if the game shows you will lose.. and then move in with a more powerful stack.2. I haven't figured a way to do auto battle once you select to do Manual first.. (so you enter the battle field, but want AI to run the battle.. I do this on AOW so I can better organize my army prior to letting the AI run the game.. which seems to be a big factor on AOW AI Battle outcome). This may exist but haven't found it yet (I play a lot on Steam Deck)3. Variety in classes and races.. AOW definitely has more choices when setting up your faction at the beginning.. 4. No Vassals which I enjoy as part of my game play.. but your Heros can move their area of influence around the map and be able to draft new fighters based on the buildings that are in your area of influence.. I see this as a PRO when wanting to mix your army with Orcs, Humans, Wizards, Slavers, etc5. Graphics.. AOW is a beautiful game both at the MAP level and within battles.. SpellForce is also a great looking game, but you can tell they just didn't spend as much time with the polish.. However, where it lacks in this area it more than makes up with a more strategic gaming experience.6. No Multiplayer.. this is my biggest dislike of the game, but if you have played AOW with friends via multiplayer.. you know late game waiting for friends to finish their turn can definitely take a while and instead of getting 10-15 turns in for an evening.. you might only get 5-6.Overall I like this game AS much as I like AOW. If I am playing solo.. I tend to play this. If I want to play with my buddies, I play AOW.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- Decent 4X game but unlike other games on this genre, you only have 1 "city", your Mage Tower. I kinda liked this mechanic as micro-managing multiple cities in other 4X games gets really tedious and I almost always lose interest mid-game. - Turn based combat is also decent. Gameplay reminded me of the "Heroes of Might and Magic" games. - Story was decent but nothing to write home about. - Game is hard at the start but gets much more manageable once you figure out the mechanics. Cons:- 3D models for your units don't look that great and mostly, look very different from the 2D portraits.- You are locked out of the other 2 crafting mechanics (Necromancer and Alchemist for my case) after picking your desired crafting profession, Artificer in my case. IMO, the crafting tower rooms for the other 2 should be unlockable mid game when you really need it.   - Some of your spells are way too overpowered and potentially game breaking, especially the mind-control/tame beast spells. These spells don't seem to have a failure chance or expiry duration and in my experience, takes control of enemy units 100% of the time for the whole combat. You can enter an impossible combat and slowly take control of the opponents and let them kill each other and achieve a heroic victory. - There is only one map and you only get to change your starting locations in future games. Kinda kills the replayability as I had already explored almost everything in my first game. Overall, 7/10. A decent 4X game.

_childDocuments_.review: There are a bunch of choices that were made in implementation that make this interesting, but also not something I want to do again. Not being able to just choose what race you want your character to lead, or have it as part of the archetype is a really weird decision, given how common that has been for decades in these games. Quests block your ability to progress way too much. This is made worse by the fact that many quests provide no significant information to complete them, and it really locks in a playstyle/approach to needing to unlock that, instead of letting you learn and explore on your own. I'm not a fan of the spellforce series, compared to other magic 4x series, and this did nothing to change my opinion, in spite of the presented material making it appear as though I'd like this one. It's early, but there needs to be several significant changes to the game to make me want to play it any longer than I did.

_childDocuments_.review: Sadly I can give only a negative review at this point.The game crashed on me at the end of a mandatory, main story fight.I then realized I am at 118 minutes play time, so I jumped in, beat the fight a second time and it crashed again at the end. With playtime around 2 hours I was able to refund.I send in the bug report, but sadly I don`t want to wait 2 weeks on the chance that the game might work for me after patches.Don`t get me wrong, for the majority of players it seems to work with nor crashes or major bugs. But some have save game issues, some crash issues at various game states. I read the german test on Gamestar, which at least in the comment section the tester confirmed no major bugs or crashes, only 4 crash to desktops in 30 hours. But no game stopping ones like I encountered.So I suggest to wait a few patches to see if the reports of crash issues get less freguent.To the game itself, what I could play in 2 hours seems like a focussed, albeit not grand take on the 4X genre. Which I really like, focussed games with a clear vision and some new takes on established gameplay is interesting. For example that you only have one "city", your mage tower. Yon can later build expansions which add to your realm and move the mage tower around. This intrigued me, because it cuts on the tedious city building aspects and filling of build queues.Also the battles were interesting and at the staart of the game challenging. You really have to think about positioning and attack order and buffs/debuffs. So a debuff on the world map on an enemy stack is not only a nice buff, but essential to win early fights. The experience with Fantasy General 2 really shines here.The Artwork is great.Can`t say much to the story.

_childDocuments_.review: SpellForce: Conquest of Eo is a solid addition to the SpellForce franchise, offering players an enjoyable mix of turn-based strategy and role-playing elements. The combat system is engaging and entertaining, though it may not pose a significant challenge to more seasoned gamers.The exploration and story aspects of the game draw heavily from the popular Heroes of Might and Magic series, which may be a plus or a minus depending on the individual player's preferences. Regardless, the game's immersive world and engaging characters make for an enjoyable gaming experience.While it may not reinvent the wheel, SpellForce: Conquest of Eo provides a satisfying gameplay experience for fans of both turn-based strategy and role-playing games. With a decent combat system and well-executed exploration, crafting, and storytelling elements - it's definitely worth a look.Overall, I would give SpellForce: Conquest of Eo a 7.5 out of 10 and recommend it to fans of the genre who are looking for an entertaining and engaging gaming experience.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun, small scaled 4X game.Beautiful splash screens welcome you to the game alongside a pretty, functional, and immersive UI. The world itself is gorgeously rendered as well: snow-capped mountains, golden plains, dark swamps, and much more are waiting to be explored.The combat is fun, although I found the AI to be rather predictable in its engagements despite the variety of enemy units that you could fight. Do they have more ranged? They will camp. Do they have less ranged? They will charge for you.The game really shines with its spell system. Casting enchantments on your armies, summoning units, or changing the landscape of the map itself is fun. You can also pick up your tower and float it across the map. Those type of overworld spells are amazing in any 4X fantasy game and Spellforce handles them wonderfully.My biggest criticism of the game is that it doesn't really have that much diversity. There are three archetypes of wizards to choose from, although you can make your own custom wizard. You also can't change your starting army. No matter what you are starting out with goblins and with a summoned creature reflective of your primary school of magic. I love goblins, but I also love being able to choose my starting army composition to add variety to the game.I think the lack of variety is my biggest issue. While in the late game you will have a variety of units to draw from, in my experience the early game is typically the most enjoyable and hard-fought part of these types of games. So this hurts the game overall.However, I think that this game is still worth picking up to play. If you absolutely love 4X games it is worth picking it up. If you are interested in the game, I'd wait to pick it up on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I played Civilization 4, 5 and 6. I have played endless legend, endless space and age of wonders 3. I have also played Dominions 4 & 5. And even Fallen Heroes...So you could say that I like 4X games. If you like 4X games, you will most probably like this game as well. I am still in the early game, but here is why i think this game is very good so far.In this game you are building a dominion with tons of exploration in the early, mid and late game. This means that you will never get bored of the world during mid game, where in other 4X games, only war makes the game fun. What I really like about this game is that your resources are depleting and therefore you are a wizard that is always exploring and trying to get new resources (e.g. gold, mana, ore, soldiers, reputation, herbs) to become stronger. Because of this feature, you have to make hard decisions to explore North, South, West or East from your starting location (which you can change when you start the game). So the whole game is not about conquering the whole map as a race (like in AoW 3/4), but instead managing your influence in the Eos world where ever you want to, whatever your play style/objective is.In the mean time, random quests are popping up, which you can follow or ignore. This also could impact the direction you want to explore.I do not know what the end game exactly looks like, but I could imagine 4-5 mages that fight with each other for influence in the world of Eos. Pretty unique compared to other 4X games if you ask me.Edit: After now playing through the mid game (over 30 hours) I can confirm that this game is very good and unique in the 4X world. Based on the price and value of content, I give it a 8,5/10, because I can still play other type of mages and starting locations, which would mean I will play around 100 hours in the end. There are still many improvements possible so I really hope they will continue to release (free) DLCs of new mages, new starting locations, new maps, new units, new heroes, new apprentices, new spells. Happy to buy these DLCs if it expands the content.

_childDocuments_.review: Rather than writing a lengthy preamble I’ll simply do this review as a list of pros and cons with a TLDR at the end.Pros•	The story is engaging and well written, as are the events that occur.•	There are a lot of different elements to the game – crafting, base building (adding rooms to your tower then kitting them out with “mods” that impact their usage), army management, research, quests, casting spells, etc.•	There are plenty of different units to play around with.  I’ve only played as the Necromancer so far but creating undead units is pretty unique and well done (its part of the crafting system).•	Exploration is rewarding and varied.•	The spell and research system is well done and interesting, the “living grimoire” is good although it does seem to feed you one spell at a time.  However from what I can tell the pages you get in each play through are random (bar the couple you select as part of your character).  That said I may be wrong given I’m still on my first game.•	Most resource nodes only last for around 10 turns so you’re constantly on the lookout for good locations to move your tower to/build your apprentices lodges.Cons•	Combat is good but not massively tactical.  There is some strategy involved but it mostly just boils down to having the larger/better army.  Personally I still enjoy it but it’s nowhere near as good as something like AoW: Planetfall.•	The auto resolve option for combat often results in a much worse outcome than if you’d fought the battle yourself.Misc•	The game doesn’t make a great first impression – stick with it and it gets much better!•	I’ve seen this called a 4X game…it’s not, or not really anyway.  It’s got elements of it (like exploration) but not the “normal” amounts of expansion or exploitation.  I guess it’s across between turn-based strategy and an RPG.  Either way it works and I’m enjoying but if you go in thinking it’s a pure 4X game like Civ or Endless Legend you’ll be disappointed.•	The map is handcrafted (so the same every game) – the resource nodes etc are randomised as are quests etc. so there is still replayability but it’s worth being aware of.•	As far as I can tell there is no sandbox mode – only the campaign.  Still on my first so I don’t know if the start of subsequent games will be as slow and “handholdy” as the first one.TLDR:I’m enjoying myself with the game so far and recommend it provided you go in with an understanding of what it is.  It’s not a 4X game, it’s a turn-based RPG with tactical combat and 4X elements.  In terms of whether or not it’s true to the Spellforce universe – I honestly don’t know but it wasn’t important to me anyway as I was more interested in this game for it’s own merits.Also – if you’re going to play it you’ll need to give it more than the 15 minutes I’ve seen some reviewers play for as it’s only once you’ve been playing for a while that it really gets going.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR:This game is my current favorite example of the genre, staying true to its roots with a few interesting departures that worked well. I was totally sucked into it for two weekends. Compared to similar games I rank it much better than Master of Magic, which just came out. I also liked it much better than Age of Wonders 3 and Fallen Enchantress, which were previously my favorite takes on the genre.More Detail:What sets it apart is the three different "classes" (which operate VERY differently) and the more story-centric single campaign map. You can start in different parts, but you probably aren't going to be playing this more than 2-3 times. There is still quite a bit of randomization and the game seems mostly balanced around soft caps, which results in some interesting emergent game play. There are lots of factions and the CYOA aspect is extremely well done and interwoven with the story. Your spell-book is interactive and objectives line up with new powers and the story line while allowing you multiple ways to achieve your goals. Your tower and each of your apprentices enclaves are also nomadic, with most resources on the map only lasting a certain number of turns before disappearing, and the ones with permanent yields offer a much lower rate with the exception of certain world landmarks.

_childDocuments_.review: I like the Spellforce series and I expected to enjoy this but it's even better than I had hoped for. It plays more like the Heroes of Might and Magic series than it does, say, Civilisation and that is a good thing.With only 1 central tower as your base you do not get bogged down in city micromanagement hell late game and can instead focus on what your heroes and armies are doing - Exploring, completing quests and fighting. You can casts spells, learn new spells and the spells you start with are determined by your starting choice of mage. All units can level up (up to lvl 15) and you can choose a new upgrade each time which is from a randomised pool based on the unit. All units can use items in combat and can equip glyphs. Apprentices and Heroes (special units) can also equip artefacts making them very powerful.Did I mention you can customise your tower? Or craft potions and glyphs? Well you can!I want to do everything and then do it all again with a different mage!

_childDocuments_.review: 100% achievments hereA beautiful throwback to TBS with an added roguelike elementTACTICS (in battle): Age of Wonders 1-3 mechanics where you actually use tactics like range kiting, tanking bottle-necks, flanking, swarming a stronger enemy with expendable weak units, enriched with an Elements mechanics (white, death, elemental, mental and physical resistances and damage types in play), battles are finished in 3-5 roundsHowever the AI (autoresolve option) is bad, and completely missing when you manually do the first 2 rounds of troop positioning and preparations (buffs debuffs).  the auto-combat that helps you is bad EDIT: not anymore since a couple of weeks ago! it's been revamped, so much so that it takes less damage than me early game. which i love, cause that's the painful part. see belowthe AI you manually fight against is A CHESS BEAST. had to reload up to 5 times some fights. Which makes it more rewarding when you start winning against bad oddsSTRATEGY (on the map): somewhat story driven development, only 1 huge map is available (you just pick your starting location when starting game) and you have to slowly grind your way forward with low tier troops, keeping you busy for tens of hours. The roguelike element is having balanced armies able to endure and advance until you get more efficient reinforcements.very little city building and management, buildings unlock with time at the same pace as the rest of the playthrough and most are pretty impactful aswell.the start is very slow so don't panick. it's part of the curve. you might need to restart a couple of times, like for example when the Circle tower spawns over your recruitment building :).

_childDocuments_.review: "SpellForce: Conquest of Eo" is a game I had high hopes for when i read "procedurally generated campaign", sadly that is just PR, the map is exactly the same with resources being moved, after first play-thru you already know where all resources and city's are.To not waste your time: > Visuals: 8/10 - a very appealing design and animation in my book, nothing flashy and for sure nothing bad;> Sound: 8/10 - nothing special or memorable for sure , but at the same time nothing bad;> Design: 4/10 - nothing new and many issues (if interested more data in "Con's";> Game mechanics: 5/10 - absolutely nothing new you would not expect to be here, but much much much more missing that you would expect to be here;> Difficulty: 4/10 - Bad game design makes difficulty spike mainly due to poor designed events, more data in "Con's;> Replay-ability: 3/10 - adding a 3 out of respect for developer , 3 because you have 3 archetypes by default, after the first 2 i was bored...Total Rating: 5.3/10Pro's:- I had no bug or crash so far, big praise to developer, big big round of applause, this usually never happens- Good game responses, no delay and fast scene processing- Story-line is interesting, but badly executedPro and Con- Tower migration is a Pro and Con at same time... it is nice to pack up your junk and move after resources are used up, but technically you are a nomad , you can never own anything as there is no permanent base, apprentice lodges do not satisfy my need to close choke points on map, and yes i know you can use spells to create mini-forts but that has a mana cost...Con's:- I was not expecting to NOT be able to design a leader or the apprentices- I was not expecting to NOT have a research tree for the tower, needing to buy reputation locked rooms...- Gear in general is lacking , non-impact full, and fairy sparse to come by (not considering crafting, you should not be able to have the ability to print artifact level gear)- Enemy faction interaction is sh**, no pacifist route possible, by breathing you are losing reputation, they invade my base , i defend , i lose reputation and so on and so on......- No diplomacy actions...... You can cheese with spells neutral city reputation, but that is bad design...- Enemy army composition is dreadful, i could not tell at what progression level they are if any, and in key moments they pop out incredible level of power on some stacks with certain immunity's or damage types that ravage you army's- EVENTS, THE DA** EVENTS, who balanced and approved them should be changed. Imagine having FULL control over a corner of a map , you upset an enemy faction leader, and OVER YOUR DOMAIN , MAGICALLY, from THIN AIR, 2-3 towers that overwrite your control zone appear, with 1-2 full stacks of OP enemy army's next to them, in general you will not be rocking more than 5-6 decent stacks spread all over..... - Army composition seemed to me a bit lacking, I am still trying to figure what combo works best due to troops being very very similar, in most cases the 15 updates you get do not alter the units enough to make them specialAll in all, i will come back to the game sometimes, I am interested if any major changes are going to come to the game , as it is now in a few months it will go in the generic RPG pile of games, for sure not memorable or iconic. Thank you for the time if you read so far, I wish you many fun hours adventurer!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is decent but lacking really basic features. I will play through it once but at the time being it's just a worse Age of Wonders 2 that is lacking basic UI/UX settings that have been in games for 20 years.- No way to change hotkeys- No way to even VIEW the default hotkeys- No quest log. You might have 10 or more active objectives going and it's really hard to keep them straight and remember which location is for which thing- No diplomacy. All you have is a meter per AI which is how much they like you- No way to adjust tooltip delay- No way to adjust camera scroll speed or zoom speed- On the steam deck, no way to change the super annoying "hold to confirm" on many buttons- No multiplayer- Only 1 map- Only 1 "city" per faction, you win 1 fight and it eliminates the entire AI playerIt is also extremely annoying how bad the autoresolve is for the player. I had a fight with 3 goblin brawlers and 1 goblin archer, all level 3 or 4, against 3 goblin brawlers. The autoresolve says this is a DEFEAT even though I have more units and they are higher level. When manually fighting it, it's really easy to win without even losing a unit. So you need to manually resolve like EVERY single fight.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is great, however! the start has been very badly implemented and can be extremely confusing. Which can lead to the game seeming impossible/stupid in the beginningThere are so many things the game doesn't explain to you until much later, that it def. should. Here is a small list of things you absolutely need to know:* You start with a very limited spell book with only few pages (2 primary 1 secondary), however, after researching spells you open up new spells to research. However, the game doesn't clearly explain that you can find ADDITIONAL EMPTY spell pages in ANY school of magic that will then gradually fill in by researching- The circle mages are like enemy factions in Civilization games and can be driven away from the map- The map is one huge set map that is the same on each game, your starting location is just that, just a starting location on that map. You can reach the exact same locations eventually no matter your selected starting location.- After you get your first apprentice, there will be an aggressive circle mage fort summoned next to your domain, and will periodically spawn enemies to attack your tower. Defend 1-2 waves and take out that fort as fast as possible to be free to start the real game- most importantly, there are independent towns you NEED to interact as fast as possible. These towns are never aggressive to you, nor can you attack them, but you need to complete quests to unlock rewards from them. And these towns are your only way to access T2 and T3 troops early game (apart from lucking out from quests)- your tower troop training is only for the first few turns, but after that, getting troops from towns and quests is the main way to get them until late in to the middle game.- you will get apprentices and be able to move your tower very soon in the game, and should be doing it all the time. most resources on the map deplete almost instantly, and your income/research/mana will stagnate instantly if you don't constantly relocate from depleted areas- Allfire nodes require a summoned willow wisp or a summoned guardian spirit (T2 wisp with +2 range to domain) claim. These will give you domain, and will stay as long as enemy doesn't claim them with their wisp.- There are a lot of quest locations which seem bugged/inaccessible at first, but require you to move your TOWER domain there to unlock the structure/quests, but you also need to move in with a hero/wisp as well- summons are insanely powerful in the early game, and are the best way to survive the first 20 turns. They also use mana instead of gold for upkeep, making them much easier to upkeep in the beginning as well- units with FOLLOWER have no upkeep costs, so try not to let them die early. T1 units will however become useless after the very beginning, so best use for these is to teach them mining/harvesting and use them as no upkeep harvesters. Dwarven workers can also get +2 gold/day ability so they will generate money instead of costing it- You will get a LOT of spells and items later on that will help you recall/teleport/move armies over the map much easier, but this requires you to unlock them via main quests and research. But you will eventually get them, so don't despair- Armor is a flat damage reduction to physical damage, and willpower is your flat damage reduction to magical damage. This differs from the % based physical/magical resistance- Speed is by far the most important attribute to raise on level ups, especially if under 9. Your army speed is directly tied to the slowest unit in your army stack, so try to raise their speed with level ups/items/runes asapHopefully some of this info/tips will make the game more enjoyable

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game a masterpiece? Yes, kind of, but you should know that it has nothing in common (gameplaywise) with Spellforce 1-3. It is a turn-based fantasy 4X game. At its core, it consists of a single-player campaign whose quests are always randomly thrown together. You play an apprentice whose master has been driven out of his magic tower. You take over the abandoned and looted tower and turn it into your new headquarters as you build up your magical skills, recruit troops and explore the land. You also control the surrounding land - but only within a certain radius of the tower. Foreign cities in the realm can be visited, but not permanently taken over. This is a major difference from the usual 4X games. Your heroes (you can recruit a few of them) can build a camp that also controls the surrounding area, but basically you are nomands. The heroes dismantle their camp and build a new one in a new place. And you take your tower and float with it to a new place! That's really funny and above all unusual. Why do you have to move the tower or the heroes' camps regularly? Mainly because you have completely cleared the surrounding land of resources. Mines or forests only last a few turns until they are exhausted, so you have to look for new resources and build your tower nearby. And of course you need resources - for your armies (around 100 different unit types), and for your magical shenanigans.At the beginning of the game you have the choice between three completely different classes. The three play quite differently and it is fun to play through the campaign at least three times. On the one hand, you can choose a Necromancer, who creates new life like Dr. Frankenstein. Or an alchemist who doesn't make gold but does make highly explosive devices. The Artificer strengthens his troops with spells and thus helps them to victory. Moves and battles are turn-based. When a battle takes place, the game switches to a detailed map where you can move your units. This works quite quickly and the battles do not usually last forever. Battles can also be calculated automatically if you don't like this part of the game at all. Most of the game takes place on the overview map. Here you move your armies, recruit new troops or research new things in your tower. You can also build new rooms in your tower or craft powerful artefacts. You can sell things you don't need. New things happen regularly in your realm, which are presented to you in small text boxes, and you make your decisions in multiple choice. For example, you come to a town whose water has been poisoned and are asked to bring remedies from further afield. Or you find a bunch of deserters who you can either recruit or slaughter. Some of the quests are very short, others can take a long time and many turns. This part of the game plays much like the old gamebooks, or newer choose-your-own-story games.Overall, I enjoyed the game quite a bit. A 4X fantasy game that not only offers the usual resource management and empire administration, but also includes detailed turn-based combat and puts a lot of emphasis on a story. After about 5 months on the market, the game has become a little insider tip for fans of the genre. If you don't fancy multiplayer and are looking for a story-heavy fantasy 4X game, I can only highly recommend it.Overall, I enjoyed the game quite a bit. _childDocuments_.review: I highly recommend this fantastic game.I rarely review a game before 150 hours of gameplay unless it is total garbage or a masterpiece. This one is a true masterpiece from a small company based in Austria named "Owned by gravity". I really hope they will achieve commercial success and expand this game with additional maps, randomized maps or make other wonderful games.You start as an apprentice who inherits what is left of his master's tower and grimoire after an attack by the Circle of mages who came to resent his growing mastery of magic. There is much exploration, expansion, exploitation and extermination to do. (It is a 4X game) And much learning. The game doesn't hold your hand very much. You are expected to put in some effort.But the rewards are amazing.It is difficult and challenging. The AI is very competent.Steam achievements show less than 47% of players successfully made their mage tower fly and less than 3.9% won the game as alchemist. ( I have not played artificer, necromancer, demonologist yet.) There  are 6 victory conditions. It is not necessary to defeat all the rival circle mages for victory. There is an immersive story, beautiful graphics for the world map and combat areas and appropriate epic music as a background to your adventures.Which kind of player is most likely to enjoy this game?If you enjoyed  any of these games: Master of Magic, Warlock 1 or 2, Age of Wonders, Endless Space, Endless Legend, Heroes of might and magic (Heroes3 complete) XCom, there is a strong probability of enjoyment. This game expects you to discover things by yourself. You will not be spoon-fed like a toddler. It's all about thinking and planning strategically. The map is huge. I could not explore it completely before victory.There is a lot of replayability with 4 mage types, different quests and multiples choices and multiple outcomes, different starting areas, several difficulty levels, mage customization. I would recommend new players start as Alchemist, Explorer difficulty, Easiest starting area.I recommend playing every battle manually especially for new players for several reasons: the graphics are great, the heroic uplifting music  ambience is great, and you can learn so much about all the different units, their abilities, what works against certain enemies and not on others, how and when to use items in your backpack. I never tire of watching the troops fight each other. Please do not use auto-resolve. Personally, I think it removes 50% of the game enjoyment. I don't feel the game is meant to be experienced that way.The Demonology DLC has gotten very positive reviews but for new players it causes an event that will be hard to deal with so you should disable it in the Steam DLC options until you become a more competent mage.Technically the game has been bug-free for me on W10. It runs on Linux and is rated Platinum on Proton DB so you will still be able to play it when W11 forces itself into your computer and messes things up.It is also free of the toxic game features that poison the current gaming environment: Datamining, account creation, denuvo, anti-cheat, microtransactions, pay to win, lootboxes, multiplayer.

_childDocuments_.review: SpellForce: Conquest of Eo reminds me of playing Heroes of Might and Magic 3 back in the day. It is the best TBS-RPG game I've played in a long time.- The world and lore are detailed. It feels like a real place.- There are all manner of fantasy units with different damage types and abilities.- The map is enormous and great to explore, with many interesting locations.- The grimoire is thematically amazing, with a huge number of spells.- There's a multitude of well-written quests.- The combat system is extremely tactical and consumables add even more options.- The starting class and map location options result in very different playthroughs.- It has an interesting levelling system; units won't be perfect so you need to mix and match between stacks.- You build up a single tower, so you don't get overloaded with management late in the game.- The game is extremely stable and polished.Minor gripes:- There are heaps of things to craft which is good, but sorting through all the recipes, glyphs and ingredients is a bit annoying.- The auto-resolve is better than at launch, but it is still necessary to fight most late-game battles manually.

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent blend of Age of Wonders, Heroes of Might and Magic and King's Bounty.It brings the magic of those legendary days back.I absolutely adored Age of Wonders 1. I felt that the sequels had lost its original charm somehow. This game does scratch that itch.Pluses:* great crafting system,* good tactical combat* focus on few units and heroes with great customization, no hassle with unit spamming like in AoW* faction reputation system* beautiful, atmospheric graphics* yet clean and unobtrusive* sleek, responsive design* engaging progression without the hassle of taking care of many cities* your tower flies!* you can roleplay Sauron if you'd likeNegatives:* the tier list of units is somewhat limited* there are some interface issues, e.g. you can't remove ingredients by dragging them with mouse* no custom keybinds* there is a map, but sometimes you'd wish there was a minimap to help navigate* the campaign map has static layout* when equipping artifacts you have to click every slot for upgrades, as there isn't "inventory" accessible at this point

_childDocuments_.review: A brilliant game. Its a bit of a blend between an RPG and Age of Wonders, and the whole thing is really polished and clean.It is a 4x game mixed with a Roguelike.You build a base and have a central town, but instead of slowly expanding across the map, your main city and its heroes harvest resource and quest areas, and travel around the map exploring. The Base game is full of interesting factions and scenarios that makes each area feel very unique. The magic part of the game is brilliant, its like Master of Magic with more of a focus on the base units, and collecting reagents and dungeon matter to build your spells and items. Each faction and area in the game has different items and bonuses, making each playthrough feel very Roguelike, you can radically change your game depending on where you go. Combat is simple yet deep. There is a lot of variety in the gameplay and outmaneuvering the enemy. It has strong Xcomm Vibes. I've played a lot of AOE and AOE Planetfall and this game feels like the units are much more clear and the combat more deep in what you do to win. I found the other two games suffered from too much stuff going on with units, this game nails the complexity balance.The Art is painted and gorgeous. The models are fantastic and characteristic. The Music is good. Items and Icons are both clear and very cool looking.Overall this is just a great game with wonderful design. It doesn't radically break any rules but it does what it does very well and has a niche is fills with skill and thoughtful design that keeps me coming back.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really enjoying the gameplay, presentation, and lore. It's a solid blend of the 4x genre with RPG elements that I would recommend checking out at this price tag to any fan of AoW or HoMM. Honestly, I have a lot of good feelings towards the game so far......but it's really clunky with a laundry-list of neglect for some really basic UX elements that keep this from being a 5/5 great review:1. No key remapping2. No hotkeys for the separate research/crafting/recruitment tabs3. No quick save or quick load that I've found4. There is no surrender option in battles5. No saving mid-battle6. Even worse, no loading mid-battle - especially irritating because there is no surrender option. You have to quit to main menu and load from there7. There's a ton of lore and great text... but no encyclopedia or unit descriptions anywhere.8. Putting a unit in guard mode requires two separate clicks - one to select, the second in a pop-up to confirm9. Scrolling in and out of the global vs local map has a confirmation delay to make sure you *really* want to do it, rather than being an organic transition

_childDocuments_.review: More Spellforce? Sign me up.Biggest strength of this game is a clear gameplay vision. Systems are easy to understand, which means crafting, tech research and base building is mostly intuitive (not a fan of spellcasting yet, you have one specified slot, and need several turns for a spell to be active). Combat system is solid, has a rock paper scissors feel to it, and units have some cool abilities (albeit simple). One thing I'm not a fan of in early levels - focus on damage, and less on CC.Finally, map exploration and art style are enjoyable and true to the new iteration of Spellforce. I personally loved Spellforce 3, so that seamless continuation is a major plus.
