_childDocuments_.review: A decent turn based strategy / tactic game, but with substantial shortcomings. I'd only recommend it to those who  like this genre.The game mixes together a few different elements. There's the large scale strategic map spanning a continent, where you build movable outposts and explore with armies. There's aspect-based crafting where you turn the resources you find in this world into powerful tools. There's the base building where you upgrade and customise your mage's tower. There are the RPG-esque plot lines where you help out different communities to gain various advantages. And finally there are the turn-based battles where you control individual units within an army when those clash. This is a good mix, diverse enough to feel fresh for a long time, while still being well enough integrated to feel cohesive.There are some flaws however. The balance isn't great, and it's easy to abuse synergies to the point where battles become boring as early as the middle game. There is no quest log so the map quickly becomes full of quest markers that mean little. The game only keeps track of crafting recipes you've used, not one's you've discovered. This all adds to a little bit of friction.The real problem, however, is that it suffers from the same bloat as many 4X games do in the latter stages of a play through. There's so much of everything (crafting resources, armies, units, heroes, outposts, etc...) that simply keeping track of who's doing what where becomes tedious. Each battle and even each unit promotion is exciting in the early game, but there's quickly so many of them that I just stopped caring. Expansion goes from being a daring push in a new direction, to endless whack-a-mole all around a disjointed territory.The game swamps itself from the endless quantity of stuff the player has to manage, which is all repetitions of what the player has already done. If I do finish my first play through, it will be because of my completionist streak; at the moment reaching the end feels like a chore. Which is a shame, because the start was great and there seems to be a decent amount of replayability with the choice of starting archetype.
_childDocuments_.name: SpellForce: Conquest of Eo

_childDocuments_.review: It seems to be a combination of Civilization (camera perspective, map, terrain, hexes, army movement, resource gathering, interaction with other races or towns), Heroes III (unit stacks, retaliation) and a classic RPG title (character personalization, gear upgrade, abilities upgrade, story, positioning, flank, spells, status effects), but for me was unappealing, seemed nothing special after having played those kind of games. Tries to do many things, but doesn't excel at any of them in particular. Graphics aren't as good as I expected. Sound or music aren't too good; there isn't any voice acting, not even at game start to introduce you to the story, and soundtrack is quite generic. The general purpose of the game seems very good (have a city builder with tactical combat and RPG character progression), but the result wasn't what I expected.
_childDocuments_.name: SpellForce: Conquest of Eo

_childDocuments_.review: I don't normally write reviews but I will say, this game is amazing for it's price tag. There are some things that could be better, yes.. But I think what you get is more than fair for the price. Some of the negative reviews are treating this as if it is asking twice the amount you can buy it for, which I think its unfair. Game is good, if it looks fun to you I strongly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: SpellForce: Conquest of Eo

_childDocuments_.review: I finished spellforce 2 and it was great. This is one of the best turn based RPG I played. I really like that you have a tower to develop, however I would like to see an update or dlc that expands the playtime of the normal path of the circle scenario. I would personally like to see Tower going to level 200 with units leveling up to 30, way bigger map that I can actually fight against 7 8 AIs and obviously more units, items and runes. It is a great game very pleased with it so far.
_childDocuments_.name: SpellForce: Conquest of Eo

_childDocuments_.review: 30 hour, first rune, very additive!a lot of curiosity and a lot of desire to play yet another round. Not since HOMM III or the first AOW have I been this into a fantasy tactical game.There are many good things but also many others to improve.Better tutorials, more intuitive interfaces, some form of story introduction, random maps and skirmis matches. Maybe even more customization and content, but the game just came out and I'm hoping for lots of DLCs that will bring the game to its full potential in three years' time. Hopeful and enthusiastic.
_childDocuments_.name: SpellForce: Conquest of Eo

_childDocuments_.review: 2 hours played review...Quite a charming little game so far... Nothing groundbreaking mechanically - like an amalgamation of AoW, HoMM, Fallen Enchantress and Master of Magic... but within a scope of 5 maps/campaigns each with multiple missions per map and three 'race' types.The Alchemist - Healer, Nature typesArtificier - Dwarven earthy typesNecromancer - Well duh... undead sorceror typeYou can play about with a custom mage, but really seems a bit pointless having a a tree hugging necromancer but not tried it yet...The graphics are quite nice, sound effects a bit dull, but decent music I'll probably turn off in another hour (its a loop).Overall at this stage seems very stable (no bugs or crashes), runs pretty well with an occasional stutter on the AI turn...The UI is acceptable, but I think certain stuff - like the tower upgrades etc really should be more than blank boxes that get filled in with some artwork.I think the game is decent but not exceptional and will probably lack replay-ability since a lot of the start of the game is scripted event chains etc...There are no random maps/sandbox content.I'd give the game a 6/10 so far a marginal thumbs up for the 20 quid price point. If I find a lot more content lategame or some other fun new mechanics I'll re-visit my review. For now though hope this helps.Cheers.34 Hours played review:--------------------------I can now confirm the game is a decent product. Not outstanding, but decent, well made with some really nice touches (such as the moving tower/home base), the surprising variety of monsters/units and the tactical combat (which is almost identical to Age of Wonders combat).The main issues are (1) replayability - the 5 starting scenarios all take place on the same map. Once you've discovered the map, well every play through you will know where all the cities are etc. Some POI do spawn differently each time, but one map and no random mapmaker is poor.(2) The scripted event chains are an issue because they are like hoops you have to jump through every game. They occur in the same order and are restrictive to proper 4x style gameplay. there should be a more advanced game mode that drop you in later after you've got the basics of your tower done.(3) The balancing of certain units is way off... I mean physical resistance immunity on lategame units is one thing (a bit OTT at 100%), but your starting casting spawn of wisps also has 50% physical resist - it is decent ranged and basically puts most other units to shame, with the only drawback being they dont level up. Some of the resistances need altering, or the base damages of units need a bit more of multi-damage types.(4) Agency for the player:- because so many events are scripted you feel railroaded by choices.... often simplistic ones like 'be nice' or 'nasty'. There is so little input from the player other than picking necromancer or tree-hugging alchemist, that the game does a poor job of allowing you to control your path. You essentially become an all-rounder wizard, using what troops are local.... which is always goblins and humans etc.. It would be nice if you could 'custom build' more because the 3 starting archetypes are not mechanically different enough.On the whole though this is a fun and well made game. Lots of really postivie things here too like resource gathering, variety, crafting/learning spells, the unit animations, levelling up, the artwork/graphics. I think if they could add more depth to the gameplay with more maps, deeper customisation, and giving players more agency to control more of each game, then I feel this game could be a really good one.As it stands though 6/10 is still about right. If you're a fan of the genre you'll like it, but otherwise it may be a bit shallow. Hope there is much more to come post-release - I guess time will tell. Cheers.
_childDocuments_.name: SpellForce: Conquest of Eo

_childDocuments_.review: One brilliant idea: the moving domainExcellent ArtworkOne novel idea that fails to take off: The Crafting SystemA solid foundation: Fantasy Turn-Based Tactics and Campaign Map MechanicsSome unfortunate tedium: Too little enemy/battle variety, Crafting lacks depth, Soundtrack is just passableA good price for a good product.7/10I'll remember Spellforce for the twist on the 4X formula that it introduces: your base moves and resources are finite, making you a nomad on the worldmap. The game comes out of the gates strong, with a well-presented world and lots of mechanics to dive into, creating a lot of initial excitement. Unfortunately, as the game develops a lot of tedium creeps in. There was enough good stuff to make me want to see it through, but it destroys the replay-value of the game in my view. That said, a couple tries and a single playthrough racked me up almost 70hrs of entertainment, which is a great deal for the friendly price of 30euros. Good value for money. Some QoL tweaks could improve the game further (in particular, making cancellation of active spells from the unit page possible, mass casting of unit-enchantments, and maybe something to speed up your stacks movement).
_childDocuments_.name: SpellForce: Conquest of Eo

_childDocuments_.review: This game is somewhat simple (as far as i can tell) but entertaining. I could not really sink into Age of Wonders, spent many hours in HoMM and Civilization and i must say, this is nicely done combination. It is definitely worth current price. In 6 hours i encountered one crash near the begining but nothing more.
_childDocuments_.name: SpellForce: Conquest of Eo

_childDocuments_.review: It is actually a very good game. Not your average 4X but more of a rpg and your character is leveling with the total power of your combined army. It is almost unique as what it is trying to do and it does a good job. That said, it is not for everyone as a whole play through takes a lot of hours and many people will only do 1 play through and the first one's experience isn't that great as you only learn things bit by bit and would be very beneficial in future runs. If you got a lot of time it is definitely worth it. If you can only spare few hours of a day to play you will probably hate it cause it demands time investment to get consistency. Overall it is surprising good especially after more than 10 hours and you get a good picture of what's going on. But definitely not for everyone.
_childDocuments_.name: SpellForce: Conquest of Eo

_childDocuments_.review: Besides all the other bugs and glitches, I now run into a gamebreaking blank page bug :CThe idea is nice, but I am 2,7h in... and it is still not epic for me.The tutorial was confusing, I am glad I know such games.And some artwork had strange noise and texture, like very tiny JPGs scaled up. It didn't fit the rest of the artstyles.
_childDocuments_.name: SpellForce: Conquest of Eo

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. Usually, I hate Civilization type of games, but I really love this one.Piece of advice : start as necromancer as they seem the strongest in early game and let you get high tier units much more easily.Alchemist and artificer are a lot stronger, but they only start to shine in mid-late game when you have abundance of resources.
_childDocuments_.name: SpellForce: Conquest of Eo

_childDocuments_.review: Having a game that you really enjoy and play hundreds of hours is worth more than just getting a cheap deal. So when deciding between a game that costs €25 or +€50, the lower price tag is for me no real argument. Enjoying the game is essential.So I can't say yet wether this game keeps me playing for hundreds of hours, but so far I like what I've seen. The battle system is good. I like the graphics. The story telling, lore and game mechanic are all quite good. When you think that my text is a bit too long, then the game is probably not so good for you. It creates a very dense and nice story, which is told by texts you need to read (no voice over). I personally like it so far and can recommend SpellForce.
_childDocuments_.name: SpellForce: Conquest of Eo

_childDocuments_.review: Surprising deep strategy and turn based combat game reminiscent of Heroes of Might and Magic.  The expiring resources, and the flying tower (main base), are an interesting twist.  The crafting is also interesting and with the four different character / crafting types, has good replay value.My only real complaint is that it is always the same map.
_childDocuments_.name: SpellForce: Conquest of Eo

_childDocuments_.review: I have changed my review of this game to a thumbs up. Even though I stopped playing originally, I still bought the DLC because I just couldn't stay away from the game. I started a new campaign as a Demonologist and was happily surprised to find a bunch of QoL and UI improvements to the main game since I last played. If you're looking for a great 4X single player adventure, this fits the bill.
_childDocuments_.name: SpellForce: Conquest of Eo

_childDocuments_.review: First of all this is not spellforce. This is something of a completely different genre. Anyone coming here to play an rpg/rts run away quickly.Next the actual game. Holy hell the is extremely difficult to master. My first game was a complete dumsterfire with the neighbouring enemy being 50% resistant to my damage. I havent won a single manual combat. The AI is completely murderous. No chill at all. Only way to win a combat is auto resolve.Very AOW 3 kind of game. If your a fan of that you could get something out of this. I recommend setting everything to as easy as you can and pray... hard.
_childDocuments_.name: SpellForce: Conquest of Eo

_childDocuments_.review: This is a weird genre-defying game that takes a lot of risks. Not all of them pay off. It's unbalanced and weird, and the beginning of the game feels dull and lethargic, but once you find your footing and you have a magic flying mage tower following you around and can set up multiple bases, there's nothing else quite like it. It's not quite Civ, not quite Heroes, and not quite Gloomhaven. It's not quite great at anything, really, but it pretty decently does a whole lot of things. It's its own strange experience that takes a while to get used to but lets you find your own way to play.
_childDocuments_.name: SpellForce: Conquest of Eo

_childDocuments_.review: Simply brilliant.I never write reviews for games, but this one has captured me. It is a combination of all the best parts of Sorcerer King and the exploration and discovery of Planetfall blended together and I am here for it. I'm always pushing back the frontier, finding more to learn and discover, and dodging the gaze of those Circle bastards, patiently biding my time for revenge. Totally smitten with this game, guys. I will absolutely devour any DLC on day one!
_childDocuments_.name: SpellForce: Conquest of Eo

_childDocuments_.review: Everyone was skeptical at first because of the change of direction of the series. None knew that it was going to be one hell of a 4X game. The devs are listening and actively improving the game, which is another big plus as well. Amazing, probably the biggest surprise hit of 2023 in strategy genre! Too bad it's released too close to Age of Wonders 4, which is probably gonna be amazing as well.
_childDocuments_.name: SpellForce: Conquest of Eo

_childDocuments_.review: A great 4X game for the Price.  The map is static but just about everything else gets randomized each game aside from major towns and events.  Unique Mages Grimoire research system that really  helps to immerse you into feeling like a Magus in training.  Combat is decent with quite a bit of unit, Hero and mage apprentices each featuring randomization each game Really scratches that 1 more Turn itch.  Can only recommend and I fully Intend to support these devs as they've done something really cool here.  Will be gifting this to a friend or two for sure!.
_childDocuments_.name: SpellForce: Conquest of Eo

_childDocuments_.review: This is an amazing game well worth the price.The gameplay loop is satisfying. Fights are fun and tactical. Discovering and using the abilities of your mage, like crafting undead, runes or potions feels satisfying. Doing the quests, which have nice flavor text and great artworks, is immersive.In general the vibe and feel of the game is amazing, especially because of the flavorful writing and the astonishing visualization.I would love for the game to have deeper 4x mechanics, especially considering factions and the cold war with the circle mages and to have more stats be number based and complicated, giving me more of a mastermind, subversive and hidden influence feel.Then again, it would be a totally different game to what it is now (and probably a lot of work, too). And what it is right now - a fun roleplay adventure game with little 4x elements - is a lot of fun how it is.8.5/10 would buy again
_childDocuments_.name: SpellForce: Conquest of Eo

_childDocuments_.review: Quite solid. Kind of a cross between Masters of Magic and maybe Mage Knight (board game). There is a lot to keep you busy on the map, that's for sure. I can definitely see myself spending many hours on it. The play is slower paced, but I rarely have turns where I'm waiting for things to happen, since there are so many little side quests to complete, roving monsters to deal with (and loot), etc. Much more depth than I was expecting, here.
_childDocuments_.name: SpellForce: Conquest of Eo

_childDocuments_.review: This game has started off great. Each wizard plays completely differently, lots of diverse builds and strategies, and just tons of edge of seat fun. It’s also very different from the other 4x mom/Aow types out there. I expect that it will continue to get better over time and I will be following closely.
_childDocuments_.name: SpellForce: Conquest of Eo

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really fun to play. I love turn based strategy games and spent hours in games like Battletech or Xcom. A friend of mine gifted me this game. I had some experience with the past Spellforce games, but was never a big fan (because of the RTS aspect), but I really love this one. THe setting mixed with the turn based structure, the exploration and the combat are funI only played one mage type so far, so I cannot say how the different classed change the game, but I look forward to do try out. Graphics are nice, music is amazing and the text show that the team likes good storytelling games and RPGs. Overall a recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: SpellForce: Conquest of Eo

_childDocuments_.review: It's great game, especially if you like Spellforce universe. Factions, units, Mana imbued items and POI, all these will be pretty familiar to you. It has slow start and it takes time to understand how system works. There are tutorial messages and hints, but it still took me few restarts where I did a mistake I would avoid knowing how all works (mana upkeep consequences - you can loose really good unit unexpectedly if you do not pay attention as I did). Timers of army abilities on the strategic map are not very visible, so after getting flying you may end up in the middle of a lake with your best army waiting for a spell to be researched. Anyway, beside few hiccups I have a pleasant experience in diverse scenarios experiencing not a total, but decently significant randomisation with every start.I easily recommend this game, if you are looking for something enjoyably repayable with good customisation of your troops and heroes.
_childDocuments_.name: SpellForce: Conquest of Eo

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game for a great price. I am a big fan of turn-based strategy games, especially the fantasy sub-genre, I probably played and loved them all (HMM, AoW, Disciples, Eador, Fantasy General...).  EO is a great addition to the "club". It has the same addictive characteristics (one more turn...) together with enough new features to keep it fresh and interesting. I played for just over 10 hours, and I am already hooked. This game will keep me busy for hundred of hours. I thank the devs and the publisher to give us such a quality game for a very reasonable cost.
_childDocuments_.name: SpellForce: Conquest of Eo

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game, I like what it tries to accomplish. The all powerfull circle, an authority in magic, against you, a small apprentice of you own master. Trying to raise against the mighty. Quite frankly, it does feel like that, all elements of the game work well with one another. But none of them are fully fleshed out. In about sixteen hours, I finished a campaign. I did not rush it. Thing is, I do not really see any replayability. Does it need one ? No, even in our modern times, not all games need replayability. But this one could have used a bit of it. I played as a necromancer, and I'm honestly glad I started with this archetype which is quite fun, creating your own units. The theory is good. The execution ? A bit lazy. I see icons used in other games. I see models reused again and again. The worse part is that anything that is unique about the game is of stellar quality, the artworks are beautiful, the map is really great, the locations on it give it some sort of life. At first it feels absolutely ginormous. The tower mechanics are interesting. But as much personality that everything has, it fails to create a great game. Do I recommend the game ? Not in this state. It's been out since early febrary, and at the time of writing this we are in early april of the same year. But this game did do something great for me. It reminded me how much Heroes of Might and Magic 5 was a great game, and made me play it again. I guess that's a win.
_childDocuments_.name: SpellForce: Conquest of Eo

_childDocuments_.review: On a journey to great magical might, explore and control the lands of Eo in this ever-changing turn-based strategy role-playing game. Field armies and heroes in tactical combat, finish hundreds of quests, and gather spells and artefacts to become the most powerful mage of all.
_childDocuments_.name: SpellForce: Conquest of Eo

name: Caravan SandWitch
detailed_description: In Caravan SandWitch, embark on a journey across a Sci-Fi Provence-like world, driven by a mystery through your missing sister that unfolds with each step you take. Interact with the communities on Cigalo, help them with their tasks and meet new people along the way. Take your time to explore the world, whether in your van or on foot. Life is simple: no combat, no death, no timer, just you, your van, and the world. Explore a Provence-like World Equipped with your van and an array of essential tools, you set out on a quest to find your missing sister. Upgrade your van throughout your adventure and explorations to open up new passages and ruins. From navigating treacherous terrain to uncovering ancient ruins, every step of your journey brings you closer to unraveling the truth behind your sister's disappearance. A hopeful Post-Apocalypse From a green planet to a desertic one due to human activities and sur-exploitation; discover on Cigalo the impact of humans and its population through your road trip. Meet the Reinetos, an old aboriginal species, the Robots left behind after the planet exploitation, the humans who stayed after everyone left for another planet, and the mysterious SandWitch. All of them live peacefully in Cigalo and help each other in this unwelcome environment. Meet a diverse cast of characters As you interact with the diverse characters you meet along the way, you'll come to understand that your community is your home. Help everyone and contribute your piece to the edifice, enabling everyone to live in harmony in an environment hostile to all civilizations due to over-exploitation. A Game developed for All Plane Toast made huge importance to create a game in which everyone can feel included, representing their vision of a world where communities help each other to overcome the environmental consequences of our world. Caravan SandWitch is written with an inclusive script, that represents a real community with its people and representation. Accessibility options are available.

short_description: Embark on a journey across vast landscapes in Caravan SandWitch, a captivating narrative-driven exploration adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: Another game where the real rating is "middle thumb".There's a lot to like about Caravan Sandwitch.  It's a great open-world that's big enough, but not too big.  It's got great art design, the music is complimentary without being overpowering.It has two major flaws though:1) It's  janky.  The movement system fails to work sometimes - Sauge will just refuse to clamber up onto ledges that should automatically clamber onto to.  And then sometimes she'll clip through the ground in the process.  When driving the van, I found that it would sometimes activate the boost all by itself.  Then there are a couple of platforming puzzles which suck not because they're terribly designed, but because the movement system just isn't built for it.  It's not fluid enough, it's not responsive enough.2) The English localization is .  It borders on Engrish.  There are two English localizers listed in the credits for this game, but I'm pretty sure they just ran the script though a machine translator and laughed all the way to the bank.  The localization is full of broken grammar and incorrect or unnatural words (like calling teleporters and transmission towers "receptacles").  It genuinely hindered my ability to be invested in the storyline, so for most of the game I was simply continuing because I found the world itself compelling enough to do so.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games I find hard to truly recommend to the average gamer, but for a specific few this is one of those rare little treats. At the time of this review, I have 99%'d the game. With the exception of a few achievements, one of which is simply jumping the truck off every ramp in the game, there is isn't a single drop of content left to do. Personally, 7 hours for 20~ dollars isn't the worst value, but I am left feeling unfulfilled. I am left wondering if another year in the oven would have worked wonders for this game, or if it's reached the limits of the creator's vision and that vision is simply incomplete.There is no challenge here, as in no combat and no genuine puzzle solving. You drive a van from point to point, pick up shiny objects and maybe read a little dialogue as part of whatever quest you're on, maybe sometimes you climb a bit... and... that's it. Everything is spelled out fairly clearly (barring the definitely rushed localization) and you are put under absolutely no pressure to do anything. The entire game is 'This place is sorta interesting, I wonder what's over there', held together by so-so platforming and a fairly interesting story that gives you enough crumbs to give you a desire to keep going. As the progression is casual enough that it never feels tedious, even when there isn't much to do but drive from one landmark to the next, the 'drive' (haha) must come entirely from within or your desire to get more story beats.I enjoyed my time with this game, it was a great 'shut-your-brain-off' for a lazy Sunday kinda experience. However, the ending felt crazy rushed, the build up and pay off is almost insulting and it ends so abruptly I'm simply left confused. When you reach the end and uncover the big reveal, it really just felt like 'uh...okay i guess' and then the credits roll and there's nothing after them. No little teaser, no final to-do, just some cute pictures and the names and roles of the people involved. Quite literally boiling down to a binary choice. Pick A or B, here's the credits.I think this game is a spot on 6/10. It's definitely a step above the standard jank that's released by the gorillions these days, but it's far from perfect. If you could pick this game up on a decent sale, it's well worth a few hours of your time, doubly so if you're more of a casual gamer that just wants to chill and shut your brain off.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: Caravan SandWitch is exactly what it markets itself to be — a stress-free, relaxing 10-hour romp through a beautiful wasteland filled with heartfelt stories and colorful characters. While its repetitive quest design, iffy PC performance (better now compared to the review build), and technical issues prevent the game from achieving its full potential, Caravan SandWitch offers a pleasant experience that all demographics will be able to pick up and enjoy.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful adventure game without fighting but still so much fun and interesting. One of the best games of 2024! The game will take around 12 hours to complete and will warn you if you are approaching a point where you can miss out on stuff.  Around 12 hours 2/10 1 I wrote  No Yes, however, the game warns you if you want to continue when you have side quests left that will stop working after that point.  No No No No No No difficulty option, but there also is no fighting within the game NoI'm so impressed with Caravan Sandwitch. I wasn't sure what to expect before starting this gem but loved the esthetics. I played through the entire game as quickly as possible as I just couldn't stop playing! I instantly fell in love with this game and just wanted to keep playing every free hour I had. The story starts right off the bat, the intro will tell you you got a distress signal from your sister's spaceship... but she went missing 6 years ago and you all mourned and moved on at some point. However, you can't let this go... you travel back to your old hometown to search for where the missing signal is coming from. You'll meet up with the people that still live there and help them out as well along the way. While learning more and more about the past you didn't know back then because you were only 12 when she went missing.What I love about Caravan Sandwitch is the music (I added the music from the main menu to my Spotify list) but even more the exploration. There are so many little details to explore. You'll find components (the things you collect in this game) everywhere, so it is always worth it to just explore every nook and cranny and be rewarded for it. Every place in the game tells you a story about what is going on or what happened there in the past. It is just amazing how much of the story is told in such a natural way. Just by the environment or by what is brought up by the characters, but it never felt like it was forced into a conversation. Did I already mention that I love this game? I was surprised to see the details your truck has. If someone is riding with you, you'll literally see them in your car. And if you receive a trinket from a sidequest, you'll also see that appear on your car. It is also great how smooth the movement with your character as well as with your car feels. And having the option to teleport back to your car and/or teleport back to the main town are such welcome Quality of Life features every game should have!Another thing that impressed me is how responsive the dev team is. They are so active on social media and on Discord, but also when I brought up through private chat a small bug I found they instantly replied and updated the game. Having tiny bugs in your game can happen, what is important is the response, and if it gets fixed. For both questions, the answer is definitely YES, they listen and they fix. They ask follow-up questions if it isn't clear. That was just wonderful to see. It takes around 12 hours to unlock all the achievements. Pick up every component (and those very cute stuffed animals) you see and use every springboard you see, to get those achievements out of the way. Some achievements might be missable but if you read the warning about continuing with the storyline and which sidequests will become unavailable you won't miss anything. All the other quests will be for the main quests, side quests, and exploring everything on the map. I really love Caravan Sandwitch so much and I hope so many others will too. In my book, this game is a gem and I hope it will not end up being a hidden gem.I give Caravan Sandwitch 4,5 out of 5 stars.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: Cozy Death StrandingRelaxed open world exploration game. Gameplay itself is solid with some metroidvania elements such as getting upgrades and unlocking places to progress further. Music and sound was good and navigating with car and protagonist was fluid. Performance on Steamdeck was also solid and didn't run into bugs. The story was very light and maybe a little too stretched. Still felt that the length 7-8h wasn't too long. Overall would recommend 7.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: The art is great and the world call only for one thing: To be explored. That's where the issue lies, there is nothing to explore. After 4 and half hours of playing I couldn't tell how far I am in the game but it does not make me want to continue. The character is heavy, controls and world interactions are clunky. There is no real fun game play elements that make the solo journey interesting. Some of the dialogues at the start of the game are interesting and make you want to find out more but they are cut short and most of the time you never speak with any of the characters again. Lastly the game starts off by showing you a message you get from your sister who's disappeared so you go to the planet where the signal came from to try and find her. There is a sense of urgency. However within 10 min of being there you're sent on a mission to find cheese and bread to organise a picnic... it just pulled me out of the experience Get it on sale if it drops to 10 bucks,

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very rough game, not bad per se, but it has a bunch of small issues that in aggregate annoy me more than i'd like.First up I want to say i did have a mostly good time with this. its very pretty, while not a technical marvel it has very good art direction and there is character in the design. driving the truck is mostly fun, i like that it kinda sucks to drive  combined wit the crappy terrain you have to traverse, tho it did randomly gain huge amounts of speed and become hard to control for no reason. And i appreciate the story it is telling even if i find it lacking.The biggest issue i have, that while not a real problem, was that the translation, or writing (it's certainly some amount of bot) is very stiff. I cant speak to how it reads in french, but in english the dialogue never felt natural or smooth, it made it pretty hard to get into it because i always felt at arms length from the roughness of it. This somewhat leads into the story/setting/plot as well, i appreciate the message here and what s going on, but it both feels pretty simple and vague enough but also at points really hits you over the head with its themes and maybe that's what some people need i guess, but it was a bit eye rolly in how bald faced it is.I also enjoyed the side quests more than the primary narrative, i liked learning a little bit about the world. Oh and I quite enjoy the main theme.Something that also seemed neat at the start but I quickly grew to dislike was the components and crafting, tho calling it crafting is a stretch. what seems to be the main incentive to explore the ares and do the puzzles is that you need components of varying rarity to craft stuff for your car, but you will quickly realise that the crafting is linear and based on if you have finished the next main story quest. It really feels like padding, every time after finished the story quest, they'd mention we need to build the new upgrade for the car so you can progress and do the next quest, but i often dint have enough components so id have to just go do all the side quests and explore so i'd have enough, and that is the main loop of the story and game play. I understand you need to come up with a reason to motivate people to explore but it really feels tacked on and i think it would have led to a much smoother experience if it wasn't in the game at all.It also can get a little buggy, not in a way that was game breaking for me, but in small ways that were either amusing or a little irritating.While the within the final hour or so i was feeling fatigue and wanted to finish up, it mostly doesn't overstay its welcome and its certainly feels like a lot of passion and effort went into making this and i do think that's worth supporting.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: It's giving me Outer Wilds vibes so far, which is extremely high praise.There's no combat, just exploration and discovery. You go around learning more about the characters and world, slowly gaining new abilities that help you reach places you couldn't get to before, which help you collect items you can use to help out the people you meet.In most AAA games I am sick of everything having boring, forced, parkour sections- meanwhile this game is nothing BUT parkour and environment navigation and yet I am absolutely in love with it. In this case, the fact that the focus is on the movement and climbing, instead of it simply being an interlude to get you to the next combat set-piece, is probably what makes all of the difference!

_childDocuments_.review: Completion Edit: Yeah, this game isn't it.It WANTS to be an amazing, cozy, memorable adventure, but the devs needed another year to cook to get it there. A severe lack of polish isn't the only issue - the story goes from intriguing to just plain boring near the end, and the ending itself is unsatisfying as it could possibly be. The characters have a hint of being interesting, but they fall flat on their two-dimensional faces pretty quickly. It's really a shame - this has the look of a winner, but what's inside doesn't match up at all. Original review:A beautiful game held back by a lot of polish issues.Caravan SandWitch is, without a doubt, one of the best looking games I've seen this year. The art design is sublime and the environments are enough to make you want to sit and just stare as you trundle around in the yellow van.This, unfortunately, is overshadowed by a BIG lack of polish. To wit:- Dialogue is clunky, and really needed a localization expert to smooth it out so that it helps the story instead of distracting from it.- Some of the character's animations are jerky, like they were 90% complete and then work was paused and never resumed- Dialogue choices will sometimes elicit a response from who you're talking to that reads like it would if you chose the *opposite* dialogue choice- Things that you interact with and pick up are finicky in places- The van's interaction with the environment is... not good. Driving it is enjoyable, but it stops *instantly* upon contact with any objectIt's gorgeous, relaxing and enjoyable in spite of the issues, but this doesn't feel like a game that's finished. Early access, or beta? Yes. Finished? No. It needs a couple more months of polishing out the rough edges.

_childDocuments_.review: I was really enjoying this game, it looks great and the exploration was fun. But it just did not stick the landing, I found both endings incredibly disappointing. The story just comes to a grinding halt and then the credits roll, showing pictures that are not specific to the end you chose. There are underground buried creatures and a trail you can only see with the radar that doesn't do anything or mean anything. The collectibles were frustrating and I'm annoyed how tedious it was to 100% the game. Adding the food and locations to the map would be ideal for this type of game where the scenery is a simple style.Design wise, my 2 cents is the vehicle needs softer suspension and less traction. Rather than swapping the tools when I select them it would be more satisfying if the tools always showed on the vehicle and activated on selection without magically disappearing from the roof. I paid around 28$ but I would value this game at 10$ for the experience. I still think the creators should be proud of what they made and it was a charming and freshly non-violent game.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could put a neutral review. There's nothing wrong with this game exactly it's just not exceptional either. It's pretty much just fine.The gameplay is fine, it's exploration/collect stuff with some small puzzles. The driving mechanics functionally work but aren't anything special. I was sort of hoping for more functionality around having to customise and repair the van, there's is no damage mechanic in this. There's also no health mechanics so you can just inexplicably fall from great heights and be fine. There's not really a whole lot to the gameplay beyond this which again is fine it's just not that memorable.The plot is meh, it seemed kind of interesting to start with but doesn't really feel like it goes anywhere beyond "Collect things and press buttons" and the climax of the plot felt very quick and disappointing. Dialogue is also fine albeit a bit stiff at times. There is also LGBT stuff in this game but it literally doesn't matter, anyone complaining the game is "too woke" is, in their own terms, a snowflake.Music and sound design are very good. The sounds in this game are very satisfying and scratch an itch in my brain.Art design is pretty cool.Not sure what else to say really, the game is fine just nothing that special.

_childDocuments_.review: is a relaxing open-world adventure whose peaceful gameplay is focused mainly on exploration, solving light puzzles and interacting with the characters of the game world through dialogues and various quests. You take the role of a young girl called Sauge, who receives a distress signal from her sister's ship, six years after she mysteriously vanished from their home planet Cigalo. Sauge then decides to travel back to Cigalo to find the source of the signal and further investigate the circumstances of her sister's disappearance. Upon arrival, she finds the planet in a semi-apocalyptic state, with her family and friends being among the last survivors.’s gameplay consists mainly of exploring the wasteland of Cigalo in a cozy, rusty car-a-van and visiting every ruin to collect old computer parts or items needed for quests. The map is fairly small, and after a couple of hours of gameplay, you will have already become familiar with it like the back of your hand. However, the progression is heavily gated by the upgrades you can buy for your van, which obviously require a certain amount / type of computer parts to craft. Thus the gameplay loop boils down to visiting the major locations more or less every time you get a new upgrade (which happens 3-4 times in the game) that allows you to go one level further into the ruins. They’re designed in a linear way, making it very easy for the player to know where to go or what floors are blocked by not having unlocked a certain upgrade yet. The computer parts to collect are very abundant and found everywhere on the map, even outside ruined locations too (thus there will be no grinding for those), yet scattered in a way that motivates you to progressively visit new places. There’s some light puzzling involved in some locations, where you will need to press a button to activate doors and open new paths, but there’s nothing complicated about it, nor anything requiring deep logic.The gadgets you can unlock for your van are very fun to use. Aside from a radar that will highlight all collectible components, doors, generators and other essential game elements within an area around the player, you will further unlock a grappling hook that can be attached to poles located on higher platforms, thus creating a zip line for you to slide up there. This will also be used to uncover hidden containers in the sand or to pull down doors, Mad Max style. With further van upgrades, you will be able to hack platforms and communication terminals, allowing you to read the secret messages that Sauge’s sister tried to send to Cigalo.The story slowly unravels as you explore the planet and its abandoned compounds. It’s a sci-fi story that has an environmentalism theme at its core, as Cigalo’s now-arid habitat proves to be the result of human resource exploitation. The “SandWitch” in the title refers to the fact that Sauge’s every step is monitored from afar by an enigmatic creature presumed to belong to the controversial Sand Witches faction.The peaceful vibe of  is given not only by the lack of combat but also by the interactions with the NPCs and their own stories filled with nostalgia. Aside from humans, two races live on the planet in harmony with the nomads, and their own narratives, shared as they prepare to soon become extinct, will also tug at your heartstrings. Everything here is topped up with an outstanding soundtrack, bound to stir up even more emotions inside you.To fully complete  will take you around 12h-15h. While there is no requirement to collect all computer parts available, some of the achievements are extremely missable. The game offers a few very nice QoL features, such as returning to the van or the garage with a button press from any location, however, there’s nothing that can help players with these missable achievements. The hardest to obtain are the ones requiring you to use all the springboards and to visit all locations. These are indicated on the map, but not highlighted in any way when you visit them. More so, some locations are quite hidden even if they’re visible on the map (or reachable only by foot) and the game doesn’t naturally send you there through its storylines. It’s quite difficult to track these without any outside help, some of them also being very small. Having a check mark applied on the map whenever you use a springboard or visit a location would be a tremendous improvement. Without it, I ended up spending an extra 3 hours aimlessly roaming around, revisiting every visible spot on the map and while the game was a very pleasant experience for me, this last bit was quite infuriating.I would compare  either to  (although  is mainly about driving your van to deliver packages) or to , although the latter is much more complex. It's certainly a very chill and easy game, that I would warmly recommend to fans of cozy games and wholesome stories.

_childDocuments_.review: Caravan SandWitch is a delightful indie game that takes you on a unique adventure through a beautifully crafted world. You play as Sauge, a character on a mission to find her missing sister in a post-apocalyptic setting inspired by the picturesque landscapes of Provence.The game shines with its emphasis on exploration and storytelling. There’s no combat, so you can fully immerse yourself in uncovering the mysteries of the world and helping out the various communities you come across. The blend of retro and modern visuals gives the game a charming and nostalgic feel.Navigating the world in your trusty van is a joy. The van isn’t just for getting around; it’s also essential for solving puzzles and accessing new areas. Upgrading your van adds a fun layer of progression, keeping the gameplay fresh and engaging.While there are a few minor visual glitches and some limitations in movement options, these don’t take away from the overall experience. The characters are well-developed, and the narrative is compelling, making it easy to get lost in Sauge’s journey.Overall, Caravan SandWitch is a cozy and relaxing game that’s perfect for anyone who loves exploration and a good story. It’s a refreshing break from action-packed titles and offers a wonderfully immersive experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Caravan Sand Witch is the literal definition of "A Walk in the Park". --> Niché Recommendation.What to expect:- Easy Mode on steroids: No combat, no death, no penalty. Very basic puzzles designs.- Beautiful scenery worth exploring. Post-Apocalyptic and Sci-Fi-Elements. A dying planet trying to florish anew. I adore this world, with many climbs rewarding you with great scenery.- An endless collectathon that attempts to reward your curiosity and exploration, but becomes quite repetitive at times.- Polished gameplay with nice animation. Glitches are rare and can be overcome by teleporting back to base.- A forgettable story with charming characters that save the liveliness of the game. Woke elements weren't neccesary but they don't hurt either.- A missed opportunity to become a full fledged challenging game in gameplay means, but is still highly enjoyable if you accept the first list entry.I believe after personal judgement of the above list you'll find yourself in a state of either total dislike or curiosity. Personally I enjoyed the game for exploring a mildly large beautiful world while switching between walking, climbing and driving around. It's a very similar experience to exploring the world of Shadow of the Colossus. The post-apocalyptic world drags you in its desert with the enormous everlasting storm in the background. While the industrial zones invite for parkouring and seeking every nook and cranny, the forests are unfortunately left behind in that manner. There's still plenty mountians and plateaus to be climbed for wonderful views.Caravan Sand Witch will have an audience that will enjoy the game for what it is. I can only recommend it to those who are keen on exploration and flling collections. As a personal member of that group I could get 12 hours of enjoyment before I lost interest in that and let the credits roll.

_childDocuments_.review: "Cozy post-apocalypse" has almost become a whole genre. I guess that says something about the times we live in, but let's not think too hard about that now. While the choice of title may be a bit questionable (the person occasionally looking over my shoulder only learnt today that it's not about some kind of food truck), I found Caravan SandWitch a pretty good adventure. It was compelling enough to draw me in and make me want to continue, but I never felt like I  to . I really enjoyed the freedom to explore, the impressive visuals, the atmospheric sound design with chill music. The story centers a mystery, a sibling relationship, but also a group of people who didn't really find their place in mainstream society (so it shouldn't surprise that they are much queerer than a random sample) and are trying to build up a sustainable community. Let's blame the laid-back game logic on the Mediterranean influence that doesn't only show in the landscape and architecture: Your big mission is tracing an emergency signal, but it can't be too urgent to sit down with some good food and music, and if you're going to drive around looking for tech bits then you might as well give rides to people and do all kinds of side quests on the way. The result is a good balance of nice (although littered) landscapes, social stuff, breaking into industrial ruins and a bit of sci-fi. Gameplay is platformy enough for some frustrating falls if you're as clumsy as *cough* some people, but not too bad. I'm also pretty sure if the local traffic police saw me play, they'd want my driver's licence. There's a mostly helpful quest log neatly integrated into the game world (and maybe we ARE developing towards texting while standing right next to each other). Sometimes I was left with no idea what to do for a quest though, especially a few of the main quests when I wasn't paying very close attention. Which wasn't too bad, because there were always other things to do until I figured it out by chance, epiphany, or once or twice consulting the forum. The writing isn't mind blowing (at least not in English), but it doesn't have to be. Suggestion for a hardcore drinking game: every time the word "receptacle" is used for something that's definitely not a receptacle. I honestly can't tell how coherent the story is, because you can find out a LOT about what's going on and none of it is documented in a place where you could look it up (there's not even a dialogue log). I still managed to follow roughly, but both for story and quest purposes I wouldn't recommend taking a longer break from playing. The game's strength, in my opinion, lies in the satisfying exploration with your "caravan"'s gimmicks and the whole atmosphere. My favourite experience was (spoiler for a location) . Also the fact that you don't take fall damage and there are LOTS of high places to jump from :D You can't die or fail at all, there's no stamina bar, no time pressure, it's all really chill. The various places to sit down and gradually get a bird's eye view are a nice touch as well. A little heads up, then, that the ending is not of the "and they lived happily ever after" type. Other people have criticised it, I'm not sure I'd go that far. It didn't leave me warm and fuzzy, but it wasn't really a downer either. There were hopeful notes, and nice postcard-like epilogue bits during the credits to watch out for. You have to make a choice at the end, but you can explore the other option by loading your save later. All in all I really enjoyed this game, and I might come back for the question marks left on the map in places that I haven't fully explored. * * * If you like chill and story-driven games, check out my curator . You're also welcome to join the .

_childDocuments_.review: I don’t think I have any desire to go into the “van life” world, but I do love seeing a cool van. Especially when that van does some cool stuff in addition to being a rolling box. Caravan SandWitch gives you a van almost straight away and, while you don’t spend a ton of time in it and it doesn’t quite do as much cool stuff as I had hoped, it still opened the door to me to check out a good game I might not have otherwise played.Abbreviated Review: The premise of Caravan SandWitch is straightforward, at least in the beginning. You’re dropped into the role of a girl on a mission to find her missing sister after a distress signal mysteriously pops up six years after her disappearance. It takes only a moment for you to navigate the intro and make your way from a space station to the planet you grew up on to begin your journey. Of course, like most games, your important mission almost immediately takes a back seat to the dozens of random tasks the handful of residents lay upon your shoulders.In general, everything that you do in this game involves platforming to and through various locations and solving basic puzzles to make your way in this manner. Your character doesn’t have any elaborate move sets, just walking, running, and jumping, so the puzzle element is the core of the gameplay experience. Not long after you start, you get a scanning function for your van that will allow you to highlight the various items you’ll need to collect. Most of these are different rarities of circuit board pieces that serve as the currency that you use to upgrade your van with new parts. However, you’ll also need to keep an eye out for several different quest items as well as the handful of jammer towers that provide a Ubisoft-style map unlock functionality.This puzzle platforming and gadget unlocking cycle is pretty compelling, especially when you’re first venturing into some of the points of interest on the map and exploring the ruins of abandoned industry. However, this design also forces you to do a lot of backtracking – where you’ll visit a location and get as many resources as you can only to hit a progression wall. Then when you upgrade with a new feature like a grappling hook that can open doors and crates, you must return to explore what you’re now able to unlock. At least until you hit the next wall.Despite being more noticeable as you get deeper into the game, the progression gating doesn’t really break the experience. That’s partially because many of the events have a solid chunk of the narrative woven into them. It’s a bit strange that seemingly most of the side quests are optional. Not just because they’re especially exciting, but because so many of them have a noteworthy piece of the story within them. However, the game does prompt you to do the more ‘tertiary’ quests as you approach the chapter end – which happens every time you upgrade/add to your van loadout. Yet, it seems like it would be such a waste to miss out on learning about the characters in the game and the environment that you explore.The stories told aren’t exceptionally deep or complex, and I don’t think there’s space for them to be that way within a ten-hour game, but I found that half of the fun was exploring the nuances of the characters they created in their limited moments in the spotlight. There’s a surprising amount to uncover with the indigenous species, nomads, and the history of the Consortium that previously ran the planet. All of that ties into who they were, why they left, and what remains in the locations you explore. It makes what would otherwise be a basic puzzle platformer into something that’s far more engrossing and a bit more meaningful than I expected.Aside from the eventual frustration of backtracking, there’s only one other part of Caravan SandWitch that I thought brought the experience down a bit. It’s always inherently a little difficult to tell a cohesive story in an open-world game. There were parts that felt significant that I completed relatively early and parts that seemed redundant that I finished much later just because of the way I chose to do the quests. The gating does allow for some control over that, but it still seemed like when I reached the end, the majority of the twists were dumped on me in the last 30 minutes, and some of it seemed like reiterations from optional bits of the game I discovered. That took some weight away from the revelations and made it feel like the game needed to be longer to accommodate more. Also, the ending itself even seemed to be set up for a sequel or just more of the game, which felt a little awkward.Yet, what is here is thoroughly enjoyable even if it doesn’t present a great deal of challenge and has no real failure state. It’s “cozy,” even as much as I don’t like that descriptive term for a game. Caravan SandWitch even manages to look cozy with its lovely environments, soft colors, and numerous lofty areas you can climb to for a cinematic view of the world. And while all of the platforming, visuals, and even the (occasional) music make it worth playing, the part that takes it over the top for me is the excellent world crafting established through exploration and narrative.

_childDocuments_.review: A first look:Caravan Sandwich truly is a breath of fresh air by being an open-world exploration with no action, deaths or violence. Just carefree roaming around, helping other people by doing little (sometimes time-bound) quests while working on the overall bigger (story) quest.It was a delightful experience with a story that will linger with me for a while. I must start by saying it is a visual and auditory masterpiece. The soft, vibrant colours set against a post-apocalyptic backdrop, combined with an enchanting audio track, create an immersive experience that's hard to resist. It's a peaceful, inviting world that you'll want to explore. There are sitting places where you can take a breather, and I have often thought about how I want to be there and sit there… That's when you know you truly got sucked into the game. The gameplay in Caravan Sandwich is a smooth, enjoyable experience, even for those with limited driving skills—like myself. The game's mechanics are intuitive and easy to grasp, allowing you to focus on exploration and questing without being hindered by complex controls. And it's impressive how the caravan always landed on its wheels just as Sauge always landed on their feet, given there was a one—maybe two-second impact shock, and very understandably so, given some hights, I leapt off to take shortcuts.Most of the time, when I did manage to get my Caravan stuck, I could get it unstuck by wiggling around enough, but when all things fail, there is always a trustworthy back-to-garage button to help you out. Of course, the collector in me was happy too that we had a few things to collect without it being too much or too rigid. At some point, it felt like there was a point of no return, making me scared for a few seconds, wondering, 'But what with the things I haven't finished yet, like some of my achievements?'. But fear not; you can jump right back in after the credits and pick up where you left off. This game is worth picking up, and when you do, I genuinely hope you love and enjoy it as much as I did. For me, it was worth binge-playing the living frekklesticks out of it—who needs sleep anyway, huh?A beautiful sitting scene VS a whoopsie... It just happened ok! Don't judge me!

_childDocuments_.review: It's a nice exploration game, with an interesting world, no bugs (that I found anyway) and fun graphics. I think the exploration could have been fleshed out a bit more, but I believe the gameplay is actually pretty good. I'd give it a firm thumbs up, except for two things.  One: The ending. The final quest just feels rushed and unsatisfying, not to mention abrupt. When the credits started up I was like,  That's it?!"  Two: The writing. It's bad. Very, very bad. Massive plot holes, logical fallacies, and some of the dumbest people (and robots) in existence. I tried to shut my brain off and enjoy it, but a couple stubborn cells refused to go offline and kept me wondering, "Were the writers drunk? Was there even a proofreader?"  In a story-driven game, the story actually needs to be solid. The ending has to be something other than a rushed, and rather depressing, semi-cliffhanger. The developers can't just rely on pictures during the credits to tie up loose ends, especially when said pictures tie up nothing because some of them contradict the story, (and common sense).  Sad to say it, but if you have critical thinking skills, avoid.

_childDocuments_.review: The good:- Graphics and art style- Soundtrack and sound design- Traversal and movement (running, climbing, driving)- Solving puzzles (though nothing too hard)- Exploring the map and structures- General calm vibe- Basically anything you might consider “design”The bad:- Characterization is flat- Plot is convoluted- Worldbuilding is nonsensical- Dialogue is cringeworthy- Simplistic ideology- Basically anything you might consider “writing”Summary:I enjoyed playing this game from start to finish. I found it both relaxing and stimulating. It’s a beautiful game and really fun. It sounds good, it looks good, it feels good. I would have spent many more hours doing the same gameplay. I thought it was a beautifully and intricately built world. But boy, the world building, dialogue, plot, characterization — anything writing related — is frustratingly childish. I’d really like to give this 3/5 stars.My complaints- Every time a character spoke, I groaned. I found everyone to be basically the same annoying person. The planetary natives (frog people), “awakened” robots, and human villagers all speak and behave the same way, and they all believe the same things. The dialogue all has the voice of Archie comics. Even the slice of life character writing felt flat. “Ha ha I’m the gruff guy who bakes bread but really I’m actually nice.” That’s about as complex as anyone gets.- I disliked the villagers most of all. The nomads, frog-people, and robots are fine. But the villagers verge on parody of failed 70s communes. They just… can’t be serious. They aren’t self-sufficient and they’re trying to live in a difficult environment, but they just want to play the banjo and open a cafe. It’s bizarre bourgeoise bohemian larping. It’s all alternative haircuts and straight white teeth for these folks. These are not salty survivalists on the frontier, they’re unserious people who think we wouldn’t need any laws if everyone would just be cool, man.- A witch is trying to stop two teenagers from doing something she believes in catastrophic and her tactic is to… appear mysteriously. She doesn’t explain herself, she doesn’t attack the main characters. She just stands there and looks menacing then disappears. - The plot, generally, is nonsensical. A disaster drove the evil Consortium from this planet, BUT a lone teenager can fix it in a week. There’s no reason to come back and exploit this planet BUT they absolutely would come back if the disaster-causing machine was turned off.- The game is a bit moralizing. As I’ve said, everyone believes the same things, and if anyone ever disagrees, it is only so that they can be shot down and subsequently see the ideological light. This feels less like a simplification for a younger audience and more like adults being intolerant of complexity.

(For example, you are wanting to find your sister, but you have time to collect cuddly toys around the wasteland for a kid? Also, who would give cuddly toys to their kids that have been out there in nature for ages? Ew? The father maintains a cafe in a town of 6-7 people where nobody ever visits?) It feels like the writing was done by committee.What kept me playing here was the overall atmosphere of the game. Great art style and sound design, very nice music.TL;DR: get it on at least 50% discount, unless you absolutely cannot handle love stories that involve characters other than a male and a female.

_childDocuments_.review: I will update this review with a video review sometime next week, so keep an eye out for that!I don’t usually post reviews to Steam pages for various reasons, but I had to do one for Caravan Sandwitch. I started to follow this game several months before release because I found the game's aesthetics appealing. I completed my first playthrough, with 100% of all achievements and everything found, in under 13 hours. The first thing I noticed when I started the game was the clean title screen, the game’s beautiful soundtrack and I was immediately on board with the game’s world and storytelling. After finishing my first playthrough, I can wholeheartedly recommend this game. Some people might not like the game because it lacks combat, voice acting, and the so-called “Wokeness” (I feel gross even writing out that word) that some people are up in arms about, but if you give this game a chance, maybe you’ll fall in love with it as much as I did.--Standouts with this game:* Open world exploration* Responsive driving controls in the van* Wonderfully written scenario, character development, and realistic feeling dialog between the main character and the others you meet.* Runs beautifully on Steam DeckMy personal negatives about this game* Very minor graphic glitches* Some of the platforming on ledges and ziplines doesn’t always work right the first timeNo VSYNC options - I had a lot of screen tearing on my PC* A little on the easy sideThat being said, I love this game. So far, at the time of writing this on Sept 16 2024, it is my favorite game of the year. Not just my favorite indie game, but my favorite game by any studio released this year. Thank you to everyone from Studio Plane Toast that worked on this game, I can’t wait to see what you do next!Like this review? Check out my Steam Curator Page “Ten’s Indie Seeker” here:

_childDocuments_.review: The game is gorgeous. Art direction is fantastic. The gameplay and controls are extremely satisfying. I felt like I got a really solid gaming experience time and money wise. Absolutely worth it. However, the story and the dialogue (at least the english dialogue) is clunky.The narrative and story is the weakest part of the game, which is a real shame. There are hints of a good story in there, tidbits of good world building, but in the end it was not successfully or coherently pieced together. The poor english localization really hinders the immersion as a lot of the dialogue just does not flow or sometimes it flat out doesn’t make sense. It makes the story a little confusing and uninteresting. However, I’m not convinced it’s all because of the poor english localization, although that is a major component of the story feeling like it falls flat. A lot of the story itself felt rushed and not fully fleshed out, thus a good bit just didn’t make sense, and this of course was compounded by the clunky english dialogue. Usually this is caused by the art coming first in development and the story coming last; “building the tracks in front of the train”, but who’s to say.Despite this, I thoroughly enjoyed the game due to its strong art direction, level design, game mechanics, and satisfying game loop. Just long enough to make you feel satisfied and not over extend its welcome. I was able to, for the most part, overlook the lacking story/dialogue because I simply enjoyed driving around and exploring.

_childDocuments_.review: Caravan SandWitch so clearly has heart behind it. The developers obviously put everything they had into what I think was a poor design document from the start, and I think this idea of an open world to explore without combat can and has been done. I get the intent. It’s also a love letter to their home of Provence in France, which I think is very lovely, and I see the drive to celebrate their culture here. Other than the visuals, however, I can’t really praise anything about Caravan SandWitch. It doesn’t really even work as a game to play while listening to podcasts or watching TV because the driving mechanics are so bad and moving around the world just doesn’t feel good. I love how inclusive the character roster is for LGBTQ+ folks of all kinds, but every single one of them is just so freaking boring. I want to believe there is something for someone here, but I have found not an ounce of fun in Caravan SandWitch, and I’m not sure anyone else will either.

_childDocuments_.review: is a casual narrative-focused exploratory sci-fi adventure through varied post-apocalyptic landscapes on the planet of Cigalo.It is a wonderfully gripping adventure game that effectively omits any pressure-inducing factors to create a relaxing experience that is enjoyable and satisfying. The gameplay is varied and fun, mixing driving, platforming, exploration, and adventure in a casual way. The sci-fi narrative is intriguing and delivered at an effective pace, keeping the player engaged and interested.Aesthetically, the game has originality, mixing vibrant characters and elements with some more subdued scenery components such as storage crates and abandoned sites. The soundtrack is mesmerising and a real stand-out feature of the game, emphasising the more emotive moments and generally connecting the player to the experience as a whole.Caravan SandWitch will take around 6-9 hours to complete, depending on how thorough the player is being, and offers a great experience for its price. It offers something unique with its accessible and casual gameplay and has something to offer a variety of player types. I thoroughly enjoyed playing this game and I’d happily recommend it to anyone looking for an immersive narrative adventure.My full review where I go into detail about gameplay, narrative, and styling is available on .

_childDocuments_.review: Caravan SandWitch came out of nowhere for me as the quintessential indie experience. A short but meaningful adventure, filled with love and passion in its detail. The world and the music ooze with chill vibes and play into the relaxing environment that has you running around completing errands for a colorful cast of characters, while enveloping yourself in the mysterious story of a world that lies mostly in ruins.There is no combat and the focus is on platforming, puzzle-solving and progressing through the story to improve your titular Caravan's abilities, to help you help others. It is truly a game everyone can enjoy over a relaxing weekend, the type that will have you indoors on a rainy afternoon potato'd in your couch, controller in hand and will make you both laugh, surprise you and even tear up every once in a while, as you discover the people that inhabit the land of Cigalo.Clocking in at around 10 hours, slightly less if you're just rushing through, it doesn't overstay its welcome nor feel tedious, giving you just the right amount of content to feel satisfied, just like a perfect meal.I'm very happy I had the opportunity to both play and support this game and hope to see more from the developer in the future, and that they stay true to the spirit and vision that encouraged them to gift us with this little indie gem. We need more games like Caravan SandWitch: straight up fun and uncompromising exploration-oriented experiences that let you just stop and take a moment to let the sights and sounds sink in, that anyone, no matter their age, background or beliefs can just pick up and share with their friends and loved ones.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish steam had a MEH rating cause this game is not bad but it's defs not that good.for me, the music and art is beautiful easily an 8/10, the story and the game tho... I'd give it a 5.5/10 on a good day. It's playable but nothing remarkable and it gets really tedious.The whole game is only 7 chapters. The first 2 chapters were great, fun cause you're still learning the mechanics but by chapter 3 you realize that oh, this is it?The character doesn't do anything outside of the standard  walk, run, jump and interacting with things. The van tho, does everything else: Scan, Grapple, Hack, Zipline, Power cord, each and every one of those upgrades is locked behind the end/start of a chapter.The tedious part is that there's only like 7(?) major locations in the game if you ignore the NPC areas and each one has an area locked behind the next van upgrade so you're going back to these same locations over and over again for the rest of the game. Doesn't help that the NPCs also have quests in these locations so you're going back to the same place A LOT. It makes the world feel so small especially since you have a vehicle to drive around in. Really felt like this is a demo+ of the game cause it was so promising at the start then just took a nose dive once the whole map was unlocked.Warning I'm gonna mention spoilers from this point on.The story... oh boy the story... The whole premise is that MC goes back to her home planet cause you received a distress signal from your sister that went missing 6 years ago and you meet up with the people from the village you came from and you collaborate with your sister's ex to help find her.It becomes very obvious early on that they're not being honest and you find out that the reason your sister disappeared 6 years ago was because they tried to stop the magnetic storm happening on the planet to try to get the consortium (Which I'll call MEGA CORPORATION  from here on out) back to the planet to give people jobs and ♥♥♥♥ and they're trying to do it again with your help by also using it as a reason to maybe find your missing sister.and that doesn't make sense to me ????? like very early on it's obvious that MEGA CORPORATION is bad??? there's a local race of frog people that are very open about how the planet was ♥♥♥♥♥♥ over by MEGA CORPORATION and they changed whole planet for the worse. There's also an old woman who is basically everyone's grandma who openly regrets her time working for MEGA CORPORATION and HAD ADVISED your sister and her partner not to do this cause MEGA CORPORATION is bad. This character, your sister's ex, had 6 years to reflect on their failure causing them to loose their loved one and also talk to the frog people who are regular visitors of the town and the granny but no?? they're gonna try their failed plan again??And the Sand Witch... ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ what a disappointment...They were such an intriguing figure at the start of the story and seemed almost mystical. You know the trope, they would appear in the distance watching the MC and when you try to approach them, they walk behind an object and disappears. (They do this a metric ♥♥♥♥ ton) As the game progresses they make a more frequent appearance and becomes less mysterious and almost annoying cause the most that they'd do is taunt you guys like "It was so easy to get rid of your sister, Good thing she was a bad pilot, I didn't have to do anything". Things like that, like what are you, a teenager?And the reveal is that she was one of the saboteurs 40 years ago that caused the magnetic storm to happen and that everything she said and did was to dissuade MC and friend from stopping the magnetic storm.MAM. YOU COULD HAVE SPOKEN TO THEM. 6 years ago when they were getting close, why didn't you just give up the mysterious witch gig and told them what your goal is and that you're trying to protect the planet from MEGA CORPORATION. Instead you play dress up and taunt these 2 kids until one of them PILOTS A SHIP INTO THE STORM AND DIES. You didn't even do the courtesy to return her body to her family and show regret on your failure to stop the 2 of them. Instead you continue your dumb act for 6 years until a new person fills in the duo of idiots for you to play charades with AND THEN YOU DO THE SAME THING AGAIN. There is no lesson learned.These characters are caricature of themselves. I feel bad wasting my time on this game, I lost brain cells trying to understand this story.Again, beautiful game, convoluted and terrible plot.Do not recommend unless you just wanna take in the sights.

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game a lot! Its charming, and visually gorgeous, and the music is a delight. It operates at a scale that works perfectly: just big enough to meaningfully explore, not so big that it becomes a chore. Being able to teleport back to your van at any time is such a genius idea that more games should implement. The games biggest weakness though is the English localisation, which is in a word: bad. I think its serviceable, the story still makes sense but its really sloppy in a lot of places, pretty much every other line either uses a wonky synonym for the word they should have used, or comes across like a really formal first translation. Tbh it reads like it was only translated and not localised at all. E.g: characters never use contractions in their dialogue they always say "I am" "I have not" etc in a way that comes across very stilted. In practice the dialogue is still very readable, but every few lines will just suddenly have no character to them, or require a second pass by you reading it to make full sense. In before they patch out "Insert it into my receptacle"  Ultimately, I don't think its bad enough to be a dealbreaker, definitely give it a go! But it means you're pretty consistently being gently tugged out of what is otherwise a very immersive, peaceful experience by dialogue thats just *slightly* wonky. Hopefully they see how many people have noted being distracted by this and go back in and edit it a bit.
