_childDocuments_.review: I really wished I enjoyed it more!The game looks like art wherever you place the camera. The mc and van have a nice feel to them, which I consider very important for enjoying moment-to-moment gameplay.But,I was not invested in any of the story's characters (minus maybe Saffran, since he is at least a very minor foil to Sauge), so every quest and sidequest felt very unrewarding. A lot of "vibey" games have missions that are objectively chores, but they are fun to complete because I am doing them for characters that I connect with, either through insight, entertainment, or friendship. Every character in Caravan SandWitch is milquetoast, share the same goals, and opinions. There doesn't have to be any conflict in a story to make it interesting, so I'm wondering what's missing here. The cinematics after the prologue felt student-level. Voice acting would have been great in a game that's mostly dialogue. The ending is especially harsh. It ends too abruptly, and cements my feelings that none of the characters mattered because there was no epilogue for these milquetoast, same-y characters to re-evaluate their situation after the ending's revelations.It's very pretty and that's it. I'm very confident that the development team's next project will be a lot better with this game's launch under their belt.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start off by saying that this game is exactly what it looks like and nothing more. If all you really want out of this game is to get in your van and drive around the desert and do some simple puzzles then this will be a great time for you! I am recommending it based solely on this feeling and this feeling alone.If you want anything MORE than that.. I would suggest waiting for an update, a sale, or skipping entirely. Let me try to explain why:It is will an extremely heavy heart that I type the list of problems I had with the game, because I was really looking forward to it and there's a lot good with it. Before I, perhaps "lay into it" I want to talk about what the game does well!The movement and 'gamefeel' are key to this being a fun experience! The jumping feels great, the zipline is fun to use and you can jump on and off it at different points, as well as the ladders, the climbing feels really nice and responsive, the car handles really well, and there's no fall/car damage so you can move around the map without fear. I really do want this game to do well, get updates and maybe a DLC, because it really is fun to run around in. I wish more games had movement that felt this good.The music is also gorgeous! There are a lot of "places of interest" on the map where there's just a radio and you get to hear a new track from the OST and it's really nice. They're also usually accompanied by a vantage point, so you can look at the next great thing about the game: the scenery! Somehow this game has an extremely muted color palette but it's still so beautiful. The art style is truly wonderful and helps make the entire experience better. Running around and exploring the map was, unfortunately, where this joy ended though. Perhaps if the game were pure sandbox and less plot I may have had an easy time recommending. As it stands though, this is where the issues come in and I HAVE to talk about them.First off, the localization is bad. It just is, I'm sorry. There are so many emotional moments with characters where responses just fall completely flat and ruin the immersion and mood. I don't know how to describe it as anything other than disjointed. A will say something to B and B will respond as if they are having a completely different conversation; it's strange. Truly the worst thing about the game right now.Then there's the car upgrades and the way they work with the map. For some reason you're upgrading your car throughout the entire game, but you've also been to basically every single part of the map by the halfway point of the game, if not sooner. So, what this means is that you're going back to ruins over and over again to complete a single part of a puzzle you have yet to do because you didn't have the right car upgrade at the time to do it. It's a clear attempt to stretch out the run time and I was getting very tired of it by the end of the game.In addition to this: the main reward for traversing the map, doing ruin puzzles, AND completing NPC questlines are components. These components have only 1 function - to upgrade your car. However, there's tons of them in game and, by the end of the game, you literally have no use for them at all. I genuinely ended the game with hundreds of unused components because there was nothing else to do with them. I was so frustrated realizing this, because it was hours of work to get those and for *literally* no reason. What were the devs thinking? I am truly baffled by it and this fact *alone* made me want to click "Not Recommended", but I know I got some fun out of it so I'm just STRESSING that the devs fix this and that you, the player, don't worry about getting every single component. By the time you have the grapple hook that can also charge things, forget about the components and just bum rush the ending.The game also runs SO poorly. I don't have the best machine on the planet, but I just played through all of Ghost of Tsushima *with* an active memory leak in it and it ran better than this, which I also suspect has a memory leak. Not only would the game stutter *a lot* every single time I would close my map/menu, it also made my OBS run like complete dog water. On top of those issues, once I finished the game I went back to my save to load and play through the second ending (not worth it btw, why is the save where it is?!) my game had completely broken. Somehow, through watching the ending credits, my language in the settings was automatically changed to Spanish and then (once I fixed that and loaded my save) the audio was completely broken. I even attempted to do a full reload and it didn't fix it -- completing the game literally broke my save. How does you game ship with these issues? It was so much more frustrating than it ever should have been to complete this game.And finally, let's talk endings. I'm getting into spoilers now, so be warned.The ending felt rushed. I had my last car upgrade for like 1 or 2 hours before the game ended, and I think I only used the said upgrade like 3 or 4 times across the entire map. It felt pointless. Like I said, I still had a lot of upgrade materials by the end so I thought there would be a bit of a post game? But nope, it just ends. Abruptly.By the end of the game you are given 2 choices for endings. Basically you either  Issue is, both endings are exactly the same, and not because the outcome is literally the same, but because the devs just couldn't be bothered to change anything between the endings. Like... 1 small cutscene is replaced by another but it is literally less than 1 minute of screen time and it gives ZERO closure at all. The ending where  Pictures of life back at home play through the credits to give some closure. However, when you do the second ending  Which is great and all, yay happy ending! But none of the pictures in the credits change? And both ending cut scenes are so short. So you're never really given an ending that actually wraps up the story or feels complete.And I'm not sure if all of this is just lack of funding or perhaps they thought the game was taking too long to make and just said f it? It could be a really great game, there's some amazing bones here, but a lot needs to be updated imo. I mean, even the NPC questlines lack proper cutscenes to cap off each quest. Every questline simply ends with a black screen and some text to *say* what they're doing, not show you. I assume rigging cutscenes was maybe hard but it's so important for a video game to have cutscenes to give payoff for the world you're in and the characters you interact with and, as of now, this game just fails on that front at every possible turn.There's more I could say, especially about the car getting stuck and having to forcibly return to the garage because they thought to put every button on X and then not let you switch actions, but I only have so many characters and this is long winded enough...All that said, I still am clicking recommend. Maybe I'm too soft for this biz, but I can't look at all this hard work and then say the game has no value. There *is* fun to be had here, just don't expect the world and, maybe, give it some time to iron out it's issues. Absolutely a solid 6 or 7 out of 10 if they can at least fix some of these issues. As it stands, solid 5 and I'm being nice I swear.

_childDocuments_.review: After finishing Chapter 1 which seemed framed as the intro chapter, I have to say the game is very good with a few small buts. I love the environment, the characters, the music, oh man the music; I haven't heard a game OST that so easily throws me back to my days of playing and enjoying 'Life is Strange' in a long time. The world it builds is interesting, the platforming is relaxing and fun, the driving is quick and snappy (which is a personal point of contention because it makes the vehicle you drive a little flighty and flimsy feeling but I understand its a personal pet peeve and doesn't much effect the rating of this review). Can't rate it on a numerical scale but if you're looking for a chill platformer with a good visual direction, you'll find it here. However, if you have more severe cases of motion sickness while playing video games, I can't say I'd recommend it. I have the motion sickness accessibility option on and at max(?) but I still got sick after playing for an hour and a half. I'm not a pro at motion sickness accessibility options but something tells me the dot that exists right now might not be enough. Few small gripes that I hope will be fixed is that there is no advanced graphics options, in the sense that I can't go and tweak specific qualities and settings, instead I have to use a preset system, which is fine but a little primitive. The camera can be tough to deal with. The dialogue is not properly translated(?) at times which can break the flow of conversations that are otherwise perfectly servicable and cute; I just found myself losing immersion when the flow of conversation breaks when something from French is translated so-and-so into English. I *think* some of the idioms and sayings and meanings are not coming across exactly right but I'm only at the beginning of Chapter 2. All in all, a game I do not regret buying and one that I might have to chip away at in pieces if the motion sickness continues, but even despite the few flaws it has, it is a game I was excited to try and do not regret buying.edit (and I really hate having to say this): but having a pride flag on a wall is not political in a game about a settlement surviving on a planet abused and abandoned by a mega-corporation; anyone calling a pride flag 'political' is exactly the type of person that pride flag is there for.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a chill, low-stakes game focusing on exploration, then this is for you. The closest comparison I can think of is Sable. While Sable has a larger open world with no way points and no real story, Caravan Sandwitch has a much smaller world (about 10 locations) that you'll revisit after unlocking abilities, has a linear story and side missions, and does have scanning and some way points. The game play is solving very simple puzzles on how to reach different parts of each point of interest buy climbing and opening doors. You won't find any climbing/stamina mechanic like Sable here. Overall, Caravan Sandwitch is a a smaller, easier, and linear version of Sable.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: I am really enjoying this game. The exploration is fun, I'm not the best at platforming, but it's not too challenging here. I love the fact that there's no fall damage for the player or the van, and there's an easy "unstuck" mechanism if you do something dumb with the van. Much appreciated. The camera can be a little wonky at times when it snaps to the wrong direction, so I may try the manual camera option and see how that works, but it's not a huge issue. After spending months in Cyberpunk ripping people to shreds with mantis blades and monowire, it's nice to take a break with a game that's all good vibes. Soundtrack is beautiful as well. If you enjoyed Rime, The First Tree, Firewatch and other chill games, you'll definitely enjoy this one. PS Don't stress about locked doors, they'll sort themselves out later in the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: Sometimes you just know a game is made for you. This one took me out with its inviting sense of exploration, both in its charming world and the inner lives of its characters. Never too overblown, the story enriched the atmosphere of this abandoned planet. Like the storm, forebodingly present through everything you do, rescuing your lost sister as a goal gives a sense of urgency and melancholy to go with the happy reunions and heartwarming encounters elsewhere. I loved the day by day progression, the traversal, collecting, everything. A genuine pleasure.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: Caravan SandWitch is a game about navigation: thru the environment and thru the emotional landscape of the people in its world. Like most science fiction, it tells the story of the present thru a thinly-veiled metaphor called "the future;" in this case something most-comparable to Cowboy Bebop's gutted-out, post-late-stage capitalist apocalypse in space, but with that usually-Japanese feeling of Mono no Aware best captured in Yokohama Shopping Log (where cute lesbian robots do nothing while humanity peacefully goes extinct).What really pulled me to Caravan Sandwitch, besides that I wanted to know what a Sand Witch might be, is that it has a van, and doesn't have any combat whatsoever. It's a game about driving around a small open world and stopping to platform and gather collectibles in the effort of helping your friends to re-establish connection between their community and a growingly disparate and untamed inter-spacial mainland. I'm reminded in a way of another manga story, Wandering Island, about a girl who delivers mail via bi-plane to some of the most-obscure islands of the Japanese archipelago. Dialog choices aside, the openness of the game's world gives it a kind of simple Rorschach test quality, in that your personality and proclivities will play heavily into how you approach this fairly small and self-contained adventure. You can stay focused on the tasks provided by in-game characters and take a fairly linear path thru the game's story, or you can do like I did and immediately perimeter-scan the world to find its boundaries and then slowly work your way inward. Everything great about this game is great about other games, but Caravan Sandwitch is as defined by what it doesn't have compared to other games as by what it does. It's innovative not for breaking new ground, but for boiling all the bloatwater out of its genre to give you a more concentrated flavor. If combat is more core to your enjoyment of adventure games than traversal is then this game will mean nothing to you at all; but if you're like me and think you would've enjoyed Breath of the Wild more without having to fight or avoid any Moblins, this game is perfect for you just like it was for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: 6.5/10, a couple of bugs here and there but nothing game breaking, enough content for roughly 10 hours, story and endings could be improved as they feel gutted probably due to deadline crunching, the puzzles and exploration although quite simple are enjoyable. A lot of these issues could be explained by it being their first game so it's fine, i don't think it's worth the 25€ it asks for but i recommend playing it if you can get it on sale for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: The narrative introduces a ton, brings up a lot of questions, builds an interesting world but doesnt resolve much (really anything). It is the post-boom plight of every coal town when the company moves out, writhing in the slow death of a way of life but too stubborn to give up and change. There is no happy ending, just wasting away as entropy descends. Sure, it's cozy feeling because of the art, but the only reason the narrative isn't rain drenched sadness is because the setting is on the edge of an endless desert. It starts melancholic and just proceeds downhill from there.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: It has everything a high tier indie game needs. Beams of light going across the map. It's a 8/10 for me for this one and worth the money. The experience is fun and relaxing. The world is fun to explore. Yet it does come with its bugs. Audio errors, buttons not functioning, duplicate actors in a shot, and small bugs here and there. However, it does not remove or break the experience. The story is solid and has meaning. If you are looking for discovery, exploration, and tons of lore, this is the game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: I have a bit of bias for this game as it aligns with some of my favorite types of games, but I can say confidently that this game was amazing.  It is exactly what it set out to be and was executed perfectly.  To start the story was captivating enough for me to be consistently intrigued by it and its characters,  While it wasn't the driving force of my enjoyment of the game it damn well was a plus.  The characters were also very well written and had me genuinely wondering about some character's motivations and the backstory of others.   What really captivated me about this game however was Cigalo itself and the intractability of its environment.  I am a total sucker for exploring dead, desolate, and otherwise abandoned worlds and environments, and this game displays that vibe in an incredible and unique way.  Most dead and dying worlds feel dreadful and weary, while this game makes it feel like the exact opposite; relaxed and sort of hopeful.  I spent so much time just exploring all the different nooks and crannies the planet had with my caravan and I don't regret a single moment of that exploration.  SPOILER ALERT (although not really): my only gripe with the game is with the story of the sand witch, which felt off or not really in the best place within the story. If you love:Chill games with Open WorldsExploring said worldsUnique Gameplay MechanicsAnd a decent amount of game timePLEASE check this game out I promise you won't regret it
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an absolute gem.The art direction, music and overall design is superb. If you enjoy light-hearted open world adventure games with puzzles and a totally chill vibe, this one is for you. I am absolutely in love with the world they have created with such style. The dialog design makes sense for a small dev company, it is reminiscent of Animal Crossing or comic books and well done. With so much dialog, hiring voice actors would have murdered the budget. The storyline is interesting and keeps you curious as well as understandable so it is accessible to kids and they can keep up. The world rewards exploration and climbing on everything.Is 'cozy sci-fi' a genre? If so, this is it. I've only run into a little bit of glitching on the collision model and edge detection, but pretty impressive overall. Just remember three things while playing:1. Hit R to warp back to the van if by chance you physically get stuck or glitch.2. If something isn't working or you are confused, you may have arrived at a section or interaction too early in the story, wait and comeback later.3. Relax and enjoy it. My only request to the dev team is,  for this game. It is fantastic. Bravo!
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: I had this on my wish list for a long time and boy did it not disappoint at the start. Already 5 hours in in the first play session because I couldn't stop playing. The visuals, art and character designs are adorable. The story is intriguing and will keep you hooked trying to explore as much as you can. In my opinion worth every penny!
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: While I recommend Caravan SandWitch, I don't think it is for everyone and while I enjoyed aspects of the game I didn't love it as much as I had hoped I would. Although Caravan SandWitch primarily takes place in a desert wasteland, the game is gorgeous. The color palette, character designs, and overall landscape pull you with cohesive design choices. The art direction is top-notch and stands out in the indie genre. The sound design is also well done. The opening soundtrack for the game, which is also used in the trailer, is by far my favorite. I also found myself listening to the soundtrack outside of playing the game. My issues with the game are in the core gameplay. I knew Caravan SandWitch had no combat before playing, which I didn't mind. However, I felt that the game was too cozy. Many reviews compared the gameplay style to Death Stranding, which was part of my draw to this game. However, I think what Death Stranding did well that made me struggle through Caravan Sandwitch was the lack of tension. You occasionally see a mysterious character throughout your gameplay, but you quickly realize that the character is doing nothing but watching you so the intensity and tension wears off quickly. I got to a point where I felt like I was aimlessly trying to find components to upgrade my vehicle to explore the next thing. This leads me to my next issue with the game.Exploration was a lot of fun and I was always curious to see what was next. However, not having the right upgrade created blockers in many different areas that made it feel more like a chore than enjoyable. From my perspective, it may have been nice to have a new tool lead you into a new area as opposed to being blocked 2-3 times in the same area because you didn't have the next upgrade. Lastly, the side characters were quite cute. I never felt attached to any of them though besides Néfle. The player has the most interaction with Néfle which would make sense why I grew the most fond of them. I was also interested in the main character, Sauge, and who they were. I with the characters had played a more dominant role in the game and didn't feel like they were just people to get components from. They were all quite nice but my interest in them was lacking. The time it takes you to complete this game will vary greatly on how fast you find things and what side quest you complete. I'd say the game is roughly 7-10 hours. While my playtime is around 8ish I took a while to do a few things because I missed something small and I skipped a handful of sidequests. Despite these issues, I still recommend Caravan Sandwitch because there is a lot to love in this game. The game is targeted toward those who want a cozy experience, with little tension, and while I don't think that's bad, it was the reason I didn't love it.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent exploration based game with good worldbuilding and decent writing.  Strikes a good balance on length and not too bad for achievement hunting.  Frog lifecycle is probably the most interesting idea in the game, followed closely by a manmade natural disaster protecting the planet by making it less profitable to exploitation for building a dyson sphere.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: The past week has been rough for me; constant stress from work, friends too busy with their own lives. This game came at the right time and made it a bit easier to get through. Something cozy that kept me curious till the end. Nothing groundbreaking but a fantastic game nonetheless. Take your time and enjoy the little things it does well.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: A tightly wound collectathon in a small open world, Caravan Sandwitch uses its space intently to give you a progressive sense of enrapture and confidence in its spaces. The exploration loop is punctuated with colourful characters, many of which are queer, and this brings me joy in equal measure it brings self-identifying Gamers ire. The dialogue can be a little shallow due to a reliance on short exchanges, but the more I played, the more comfortable I was with the pace of their narrative. The full cast of characters features some quirky jokes that made me smile. My only real gripes are minor: I felt much of the music was a little too ambient, and the ability to sit and drink in the landscape in the manner of a screensaver is for a different player than I. The linearity of upgrades makes the collectathon aspect feel hollow at the end, I would've liked some optional cosmetics to 'craft' (but I suppose that might make it feel less tightly wound, which again is a strength). The core story builds nicely to a rule-of-threes crescendo and a sequence that manages a tense tone despite the safety blanket your character is swaddled in. In sum, the core loop is fun, inviting and moreish, and in its efforts to be a serene, relaxing yet still stimulating casual time, I think Caravan Sandwitch succeeds marvellously. The price point is very reasonable for a couple of afternoons worth of indie play, and it has flamingos. Give the French your money and have some fun :)
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: The game has a beautifull art style and chill music. The gameplay is very relaxing, solving easy puzzles, exploring and helping NPCs with some easygoing quests. Find some teaddybears for a kid, get some seeds to plant in the garden, bake a cake etc. A very nice time if you want to relax a bit. There is a main narrative/mystery that pushes everything forward.Fair warning this game has a lot of woke language and there is barely any strait couples in it, and if they are they have a they/them child. (No wonder there are so little people on this planed if everyone is gay who makes the babies?). So if it triggers you stay away I guess. Lastly the ending is completely out of left field and completely misses the tone of the game, makes little sense and gives no closure to the relationships that the main character built with all the NPCs.To sum it up, a good looking, chill, short game with an unsatisfying ending and some woke stuff put in.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: Just played the baby tutorial, the opening experience was smooth as butter, it gives you tons of gentle reminders what you're supposed to be up to and the writing so far is rock solid. Also with FSR and frame generation on, I am able to play on epic quality, at 1440p with a 780m iGPU around 30-60fps depending on the scene. I love treasure hunting and gather materials so the whole game is going to be a treat. Finally, the color scheme is so dang good!
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommended if you’re in need of a tranquil, relaxing gaming experience.If you're looking for a game that feels like a peaceful retreat from the chaos of life, this is it. Playing this game is like sitting in a quiet park or taking your pet out for a calm stroll—completely soothing and refreshing. The atmosphere is incredibly calming, with gentle soundscapes and a beautifully minimalist design that transports you to a place of peace.The gameplay isn't demanding at all; instead, it encourages you to explore at your own pace, savor the environment, and just *be*. It’s the kind of experience that allows you to unwind and take a mental break. Whether you’ve had a stressful day or just want to escape for a bit, this game is the perfect place to recharge.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: A cute exploration-focused game that's not too long (or difficult) to fully complete. Some of the translations from French-to-English may come off a bit stilted, but overall it delivers it's narrative succinctly.I enjoyed my time with it, and think it's a nice palette cleanser and good addition to someone's library.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: I DEVOURED this game. It is so much fun to play. I love exploration, puzzling and platforming games and this game is the perfect combination of all these wrapped up in an engaging narrative that is delightful. The progression is easy to get through and the game is good at letting you know if you have missed something before moving forward. I never once felt so stuck that I couldn't figure out something on my own, even if it took me awhile. My only gripe is I wish there was more game to play XD. I'm about to play it again just to make sure i have all the achievments.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: A charming and relaxing action-adventure (without fighting gameplay). Deep worldbuilding and lore for a dystopian sci-fi setting located on a mediterranean coastline of a far away planet. Heartwarming dialogue-interactions with the planet-dwellers. Artstyle akin to contemporary French/Belgian comic books. A small open-world with dilapitated brutalist concrete ruins and environment in Used Future/Zeerust aesthetics to explore. Backtracking required since you upgrade the capabilities of your van and thereby open new pathways in the world. Collectathons for fetch quests don't overstay their welcome
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game so much!! if you are a fiend for exploration and good world building like I am, this will be right up your alley. no combat, but plenty of places to find and things to scavenge. oh, and NO FALL DAMAGE or stamina limitations! it’s been hella fun to just sprint around, collect components, complete quests, talk to the npcs, and drive your van like a maniac through the desert without worrying about hitting things/falling off cliffs (it can take a seriously beating with no consequences) or running out of fuel. so far there is lots of lore that makes the world feel very well-thought out! my one small complaint is some of the dialogue feels a little clunky, but overall this is the perfect game for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: It's a charming, cozy, lovingly crafted exploration game. Not much more to say about it. If you watch a trailer and think "This seems like something I would enjoy," you will, indeed, probably enjoy it.If I had two complaints, and they're small:- For a game that orients around driving a van, the van isn't particularly fun to drive. It's functional, but it doesn't make me go "WOO!"- The English script is a bit stiff, and I encountered a few bugged lines that still included French. It feels like the sort of game where the writer is a fluent-but-not-native English writer. Unfortunately, it's felt pretty much constantly, and this is a game where the core hook is dialogue-driven fetch quests with charming NPC's. The game would benefit from an editing pass by a native English writer.Those little ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ aside, it's lovely and deserving of your time and money. The developers should be proud of what they've created here.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: You feeling down? want a comfy adventure? Then this is the game for you.Edit: Almost done with the game now and still having a great time, I am feeling super relaxed while playing this game, so much so that I fell asleep not out of bordom but because I was so extremely relaxed as I sat the MC down on a pillow overlooking the map on a mountain. In that moment I felt a great amount of peace as the the combination of the ambience and music made me relax so much that I past out for a few moments.That is of course not to say that you will keep passing out while playing this game, overall it is super exiting and all the stories keep you exited to find out their conclusions.In summery, if you are tired of shooting of orc heads and chopping of limbs with blades and just looking for a short comfy adventure to relax too, then this game is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: Leaving this review to debunk a previous negative SteamDeck review I saw someone leave, as it runs beautifully on my LCD SteamDeck. You of course can’t run ultra settings, but on high I get a steady 35-45fps, and a fairly steady 60fps on Medium settings. No other issues whatsoever, and I’m enjoying every second of playing this joy of a game so far!
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: Caravan SandWitch is a beautifully crafted adventure exploration game.The story sets you on a track where you interact with a multitude of interesting characters.This game features light platforming and asks you to collect parts for devices to upgrade your van.These upgrades help you in a similar vane as to how 'Metroidvania' games play.You get teased impassable progression to backtrack later on in the game.And on top of all that it features a great art direction with a captivating story.Ps. The music is a 10/10 for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: great adventure game without fighting but still a lot too do, love the art style. also plays great on deck.  you wont be disappointed with this one as you drive around the wasteland searching. Couple things I think that need attention is the terminals when you hack them I didn't know you had to do something else with it after the hack so I literally hacked them all and once you hack them it goes away off your map even though there's more to do. Now I'm not sure if what you need to do with them is relevant or if its just getting to know the game on a better level. Also, a navigation would be helpful when you mark something on your map just like how they have in the story when you need to go somewhere with the blue line that you follow I just think it would be easier to navigate with that still as an option on your own marks. The springboards even though jumping them all is an achievement there's no way I know which ones I've jumped and where they all are this is a little frustrating they should be marked on the map and then once you jump it then it either has a check next to it or it tells you how many are in the area that you have left while still being shown on map. But as I'm more hours in I really don't have anything negative to say I'd still recommend playing this.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely stunning game. The characters have real depth and meaningful connections with each other. The story flows well and with a positive solarpunk vibe about it.      On the planet Cigalo, a solarpunk world is depicted with a focus on inclusivity, upcycling or recycling old tech, and a strong message about the importance of community and self reliance.       A great story for only a couple hours if you're not a completionist low-key like me.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: A lovely explore game with driving mechanics. Great soundtrack with one solid main song by Antynomy‬, but expect dialog translations to your language to a bit stilted. Functional but bare bones menu, sound, and video options. Has key bindings,  accessibility, and motion sickness reduction. Three game save slots. There is a Return to Garage in menu, and you can hold down R to return to the van. Inclusive language, references to violence, social issues, and puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: This game is FANTASTIC! From the music, to the cozy atmosphere and adorable, unique atmosphere: This is one of the first games I've played without any active combat element, and the fact that there's no timer, an no death... That I get to explore the world at my own pace, bar any quests to unlock new gadgets, is a major selling point for me! The cozy, low stress nature of the game and the inclusive nature of the characters really warms me inside and makes me happy <3 You can bet that I'll see everything there is to see in this game!! ...At my own pace, of course~I find the abundance of plant names on a desert world a little disheartening, admittedly. The subtle environmental storytelling was really nice, too!! Overall, this is a 5/5 from me <3
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: A calm and cozy exploration game with slow pacing, and strikingly rich environment. I'm enamoured by the aesthetics of the rough and rugged land, and the simple living, interspersed with chunks of rusting machinery, communication systems and power generators. If you enjoy taking your time exploring a landscape, finding a moment or two to stop and appreciate your surroundings, then I'd recommend considering Caravan Sandwitch.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: This game rocks, I wanted to play a cool exploring game, and now I'm playing a great exploring game with beautiful world, interesting story, satisfyingly designed map and super concentrated gameplay loop. Just finished two hours and I can see tons of content waiting for me to unlock and to explore. Can't wait to play more^^
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: This is really not my type of game but the zelda-like careless and relaxing exploration got ahold of me.The visual design is insane and the game is beautiful. Just came back from the south of france and it's undeniable their art team were very inspired by where they live. It's insanely pretty and smart, feels good after a stressful day where I just don't want to play any sweaty competitive game.Bravo les gars pour cette release ;) !
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: if you just want a cozy exploration game then SandWitch gets a thumbs up and I recommend it.But if you care about getting the "exploration" achievement then sadly it's another cozy game ruined by hardcore achievements, not all of them: the achievement for resource gathering is capped at 500 and you should get it just by playing. The problem is that you have to do every last side-quest and visit every last named location and interact with every last vantage point to get their achievements. After 10 hours of an 8 hours game I really didn't like being forced to look up a guide to find my last snack bar and my last named location (thankfully I found both at the first place I checked). The two different achievements for the "different" endings were also a chore, basically forcing the player to skip the credits, reload the last save and then play through the whole dialogue-heavy end sequence with all the heavy emotional beats just to make a different choice right at the very end and see one different brief cut scene. I know only a small number of people care about achievements, but I think they are the majority of the players who will finish the game and might be almost all the players who 100% it and yet dev's still clearly have no idea how to make satisfying achievements that doesn't turn a cozy game into chore. This game is not as bad as TinyKin (an 8-hour game that I still failed to 100% it after 11 hours) but still it was just the same old silly misuse of achievements and I have decided to thumb-down games that do from now on.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: If you are looking for a twitch fest...this isn't it. What this game is, is a mix of role playing and puzzle solving. The world you play in is both beautiful and desolate. A distress call from your sister's ship starts this tale of discovery. Although your sister disappeared six years ago, this message compels you to return to your home planet Cigalo where the adventure begins. Reacquaint yourself with the folk of your hometown. What is the deal with the signal jammers? What and who are the Sand Witches anyway? Uncover the truth behind your sister's disappearance. Will you be able to find out what happened to her, and why? I very much liked the art, story, and game mechanics! I could have done without the politically correct family sexual dynamics. The inclusion did nothing to enhance the story. I found what was there wasn't odious enough to spoil my enjoyment. I found the game quite interesting and fun and recommend it! My hat's off to Plane Toast Studio!
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: A light, dreamy, pleasant adventure in a beautiful world healing up from past scars. The depth of the storyline, the rich character design, the simple elegance of a rocky alien world with solarpunk and post-industrial esthetics, and the well thought out mechanics of the game make for a relaxing gameplay to let your mind wander off in a peaceful place.The game provides about 10 hours of content. It would be great to see a bit more coming :)
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: A nice little free world adventure with a very beautiful art style and cool game mechanics. I really enjoyed that. Can be completed in about 15 hours (including all side quests). Considering that it is that short, the characters and the story are pretty good. It's also suitable for the whole family, if that's important for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very stylish - with a pretty great art style and really nice and relaxing music. The story is so/so and the whole gameplay loop is definitely repetitive. I would like to think this is a good game, but being softlocked by stupid fetch quests where I have to find 50 of these random components for no reason is sort of frustrating and takes a lot of the fun away from the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: I was so excited ever since I first heard about this game and am happy that I got to play it now!It took me almost 18 hours over the course of 3 days to finish the game and I never felt bored during my playthrough. After just a couple of hours I was so excited that I had to actually force myself to stop playing, because I got headaches from my intense concentration, from my motion sickness as well as the bright colors of the in-game desert. If you are sensitive to brightness, flickering textures/lights and motion sickness, you might not be able to play for long stretches, but to me personally it was still manageable. :) The motion sickness setting helped a lot, but everytime I was in a small room or had to look around a lot in search for things like a ladder, I got really nauseous from turning the camera.A lot of these 18 hours have actually been spent very stressed. :D  the large facilities and  areas had me tense up a lot. After the first 4 hours I felt like watching a thriller unfold and the paranoia really got to me. Which is not necessarily a bad thing (I like thrillers!). But it is something to consider, if you are rather looking for something more cozy and are also quite receptive to an oppressive atmoshpere.Regarding the size of the map, I was really relieved! When I first played the demo I had concerns that it would be too small and that the game would be over after 3-4 hours. Luckily, I was totally satisfied with it.My favorite part about Caravan SandWitch was its exploration progression. I loved the fact that I got to see every location multiple times, because in most cases I had to come back with the next tool upgrade to progress even further. This backtracing can probably be frustrating to some, but I had a blast. There is a certain hidden secret which also kept me very engaged. To sum it up: There's lots to explore and I turned around every pixel to get the most out of it. I liked the little surprise moments, for example: At the beginning I was wondering, why on Earth the game had the physical Toaster terminals. Those getting a deeper/second meaning  later in the game was perfect.As others have already said: The visuals are great, the soundtrack and sound design are great and my favorite sound was definitely the crunchy plants in the forest. A fair share of my playtime has probably been spent on repeatedly walking through these plants and experiencing childlike wonder. I also liked the amount of quests, characters and locations. It was enough to keep me engaged and not overwhelmed.After all, I didn't love the game as much as I had wished for. It didn't manage to touch my heart in the way I hoped it would. There are some negatives that I'd quickly like to mention (just from my subjective experience):The worldbuilding felt incomplete sometimes. There were some logic errors that repeatedly threw me out of the immersion. Right at the beginning we start the journey by travelling on a space train that hasn't been operated in... years? In an empty space station? Does everybody just know how to drive a train in this universe? It seemed odd to do interstellar travel just like that, but it's fine, I guess. Other aspects also seemed to lack some logic, especially Nothing major that would have kept me from playing it, but it felt a little unpolished here and there. :) On a positive note: It kept me constantly thinking about this futuristic world, that has been crafted with a lot of love, I'm sure!One thing I simply couldn't get behind and am still frustrated about just thinking about it was the one-way exits of the  areas. I could enter and leave through the entrance to each , but driving through what appeared to be the exit always led me to some completely different spot on the map. This is great for shortcuts and exploring, I guess. What really bugs me with this though: You can't go back in. In order to access the area again, I had to drive across the entire map. From my personal perspective there was simply no reason for making it hard on the player by not letting them get back to the  through the same door they used to exit. It's an immense pet peeve I have with games when they "punish" you for literally just playing the game and trying out different routes.To make it short: Gathering the components will most likely not be enough of a motivation in itself for a lot of people to explore and collect them. There could be a lot said about the way the game design of this "currency" leads to it losing its value in the grand scheme of things. At the end of the game I had probably about 300-400 components left in total. It is extremely easy to gather them and you don't need a lot of components to get to the next update of your van. To me, that was rather disappointing. After the last upgrade, I was convinced, that there would be some final main quest related item that I would need my 300 components for. Or that I would find someone or something that would reward me for all this exploring that I did. Because why else would the game give me so many of them? Realizing that this was in fact not the case and that my excitement had been for nothing was honestly a little devastating. After a while the plot got very predictable. Which, again, did not stop me from enjoying the game. It simply led to me being quite frustrated at the end of the game. Even if the last scene would have lasted a minute longer instead of showing just for a few seconds, that would have improved it immensely.  I definitely appreciate it, for what it is though!Being able to develop such an amazing game from start to finish is an incredible achievement! Even though some aspects about the dialogues and worldbuilding can appear a little unpolished, it is a lovely game with wholesome characters, great exploration opportunities and a stunning aesthetic. I would and probably will play it again at some point in the future. :)

_childDocuments_.review: Gorgeous stylized game, featuring no combat, environmental puzzles, and some amazingly good writing and story. Highly recommend, would buy again.How do you review, or provide feedback on a game like Caravan Sandwitch? Do you talk about the absolutely gorgeous stylized presentation, the audio and music that is just sublime, or the story that has some pretty good depth at times?Or do you tell about how it affected you? Parts of the story will resonate with you. Stories of loss, distancing friendships and family, misunderstandings, lack of communication and ultimately healing?Or bring out the amazingly low-stress gameplay, that has you driving, running and jumping around in a world with no combat (at least that I've seen so far) and some really fun environmental puzzles?I've "only" played 8 hours so far at the time of writing this. And I can honestly say, without a shadow of any doubt that this game is worth every penny. From the driving around the map that is surprisingly fun ( Press spacebar to honk. It doesn't do or affect anything, but who doesn't love honking aimlessly?) To the little points of interest where you can take a seat and just take in the view and the world. As someone having dealt with personal loss recently, it's precisely those moments that really cemented this game for me.If you're looking for a game that is fun, cozy, yet doesn't shy away from some of the deeper nuances of what connection means (and if you do, just click through the story - but you'll be missing out)

_childDocuments_.review: At its core this is a nice, gentle game that tells a nice story with fun little interactive elements. The story starts to show coherence problems early (is that a VR rig or a teleporter? Both?) and worse, quest text is often unrelated to the goal. The latter is made worse by bad writing - it feels more like lack of getting an independent editor than just non-native translation, but could be both. Also, as you progress through the story the later areas seem to have been implemented in a rush, with the clever puzzle-like elements replaced by boring tedious back-and-forth movement.Personally, I'm also disappointed that there's so much linearity  - quests are gated behind points of no return when you develop each new tool, and the linearity is grows clumsy -  some doors are just inexplicably locked without any UI or clue until you reach the right chapter and then unlock without requiring the new tool.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game. The careful attention to detail is astonishing--the puzzles of the relays, the way the tasks unfold with each new equipment earned, the resting spots with the spinning panoramas that reflect the storm itself. It's lovely. The music immediately hooked me, and I went and listened to the whole album on Bandcamp (I'll be buying it). The complexity of the problems the people have and how it relates to the land itself and the Consortium were engaging and heartfelt. The end choice! I loved that there's no fall or van damage so in between the seriousness of it all, you could play and goof around with the environments. The ability to jump back to the van with a timed abort, and the option to go back to the garage in the settings added a huge ease of game play for me that I truly appreciated. The Nomads and the frog people were fascinating, and I loved the line where one of the characters told the dad that she didn't like him acting like he was in charge--that idea of community decisions and communal responsibility versus individual actions were a thread throughout. Such a great story! I'm putting this game on the Nebula writing recommendations. I hope more people play and enjoy it!

_childDocuments_.review: Full Gameplay Walkthrough - Caravan Sandwich is an immersive adventure game that stands out for its extensive exploration of the various game areas, which is essential to progressing through the adventure and immersing yourself in its atmosphere. Exploration is not just a secondary aspect, but represents the heart of the entire gaming experience. Each area visited offers new discoveries, hidden secrets and essential objects that allow us to advance in the main story. The game map is divided into different areas, each with its own unique visual style.In addition to following the main storyline, in Caravan Sandwich we can dedicate ourselves to a series of secondary tasks that enrich the overall experience. These tasks not only add depth to the game universe, but often offer unique rewards, such as resources useful for progressing in the game. However, you should know that some of these tasks are timed, which adds a dose of tension and requires careful planning: they must be completed within the current chapter, otherwise you risk losing them.The gameplay of Caravan Sandwich is designed to be simple and intuitive, making it accessible to players of all levels. The ease of control and user-friendly interface allow you to focus on exploration and solving environmental puzzles, without unnecessary distractions. These puzzles are never too complex, but still require a pinch of ingenuity to be solved. Usually, we find ourselves having to manipulate elements of the environment to open secret passages or activate mechanisms that allow us to proceed.In conclusion, Caravan Sandwich has some great ideas regarding the plot, which manages to entertain and keep the player involved. However, at times it can be a bit obvious or inconclusive, leaving the feeling that some parts of the story could have been developed with greater depth.The cartoon style, on the other hand, is one of the game's strong points, making the visual experience captivating and suitable for the light atmosphere of the title. However, the lack of spoken dialogues could represent a negative aspect for some players, especially those who prefer a more direct narrative involvement.In terms of duration, Caravan Sandwich aligns well with the standards of games of the same genre, offering an adequate amount of hours of gameplay. The exploration of the areas adds value and stimulates curiosity, even if these could have contained more elements or secrets to discover. _childDocuments_.review: I tend to be cautious about games that position themselves as 'cozy' - I need something with a bit of bite, and I tend to find that cozy games often sacrifice narrative or theme in the pursuit of atmosphere. Not the case here. It's a beautiful world, calming to inhabit and explore, but the setting and vibe is immaculate. There's a sense of narrative pressure keeping things moving forward, and the core pitch, salvaging a world abandoned by corporate interest to survive, absolutely speaks to me while being rich for storytelling opportunity without undermining the game's uplifting ambitions.My only real complaint is that I wish the van was a bit more characterful to drive - it's convenient the way it has a tight turn radius and stops on a dime but it makes it feel more like a tool and less like a character, if that makes sense. There's no real learning curve, it doesn't really ask anything of you, and it's great for jumping right in, but I personally feel like it's a bit of a missed opportunity. Very small issue in the grand scheme, though.This is definitely worth checking out, I'm having a great time with it so far.

_childDocuments_.review: I became aware of this game in the weeks leading up to its release. It looked too good to be true, but it was clearly such a labor of love, I had to have it! I bought it the hour it released. The only reason I waited so long to review it is because I wanted to give an honest review after playing a decent amount, and I have been savoring it.I think I'm past the halfway point now, so i can safely say this a 10/10. 100%! This game feels like the trailer makes it look.  Everything is beautiful, and the spaces are just the right size: Big enough to explore, but not so big that they are a chore to traverse. Movement feels great, and the puzzles are fun. Nothing too complicated, fun to engage with. The story and characters strike a really good balance of real, relatable emotion, without getting too heavy. I think that's one of the things I like the most about it: it acknowledges and talks about fears and regrets but frames them in a context of people doing their best to move forward and heal. The lack of things like combat and fall damage frees you up to just drink in the sunny possibilities and listen to what the game is telling you. If you look at the trailer for this game and thing "aww that looks cute, I want to play that!" DO IT. You won't be disappointed. It's worth every penny.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed the demo when I played it, so I purchased and played the full game on release. Tl;dr: If you don’t let the propaganda bother you, you’ll enjoy it. Get it at $15 or less. 8-10 hours. ——At its core, Caravan Sandwitch is simple: a no stress, casual exploration game. There’s no health bar, no enemies to speak of, and no timer pushing you to do things RIGHT NOW.The Positive:The story is light but interesting enough, with a bunch of simple puzzles and fetch quests giving you purpose as you wander across the world. Progression is paced well, gated by tools needed to further explore locations. This isn’t a big game, and the world is equally small, but you never feel that way, as the devs manage to make the setting feel vast and open so you never feel cramped.And did I mention the game is beautiful? The models, colors, and atmosphere really make it the most beautiful game I’ve played this year. And it could potentially have kept the title if Neva wasn’t releasing next month. If Cigalo was a real place, I’d definitely give it a visit, much like I would visit Death Valley (also very beautiful IRL, but don’t go in the summertime, your car will melt, no joke). Not-So-Positive, but Tolerable:Movement on foot is great, but movement in the van could use some polish. It’s a bit strange that hitting anything brings the van to a complete stop immediately. This includes small bushes one assumes you can crush with your van. Also there’s no fall damage, which is fine, but you can literally drive off a cliff 50 meters high with zero consequence and that’s not at all immersive. (The van is cute though. I’d prob print a model of it and paint it up.)There is still some polishing to be done. I had to restart the game a couple times when the camera decided it wanted to continuously shake even when I was standing still. Also Rose’s shawl/cape turns into a jagged epileptic mess during cut scenes. The Not-Positive-But-Deal-With-It-I-Guess:On the other hand, I can’t help but notice that there’s something very strange going on in Cigalo. It’s definitely a very inclusive game and the devs are very open about that fact. But when basically EVERY guy is into other guys, and EVERY girl is into other girls, and straight people are the rare exception(so rare even now I had to go back and check if they were the gender I thought they were(and I’m honestly still not sure)), you really wonder if something is in the water. There’s also gotta be an inside joke about the frogs being more straight than the humans are in a queer world.I also can’t help but think that maybe Cigalo’s depopulation has more to do with reproduction more than anything else, though given the main character has siblings it’s clear that children are being produced somehow in an unexplained manner. Other games do inclusivity a lot better and more subtly, eg. Coral Island. The agenda is just too obvious here. I just want to play a game, not get beat over the head with the devs inclusivity. Remember, the best propaganda is the stuff you don’t notice. Conclusion:Overall, the game is still worth your time, but not at $25USD The most direct comparison I have got for this game is Sable, another indie exploration game set in a desert planet with puzzles, fetch quests, and also worth a play. Art and sound design are great, the narrative and gameplay are passable, the music is great(dreamy, chill, ambient, French, already in my playlist). A short, beautiful game, get it at a discount at around $15USD or whatever your equivalent is to a Big Mac Meal. Just don’t let the agenda hit you on the way out.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR - Generally, the game is a delight, showcasing both great aesthetic style and solid game play. A few drier moments in the narrative/game play towards the end can be overlooked in favor of the powerful final act. A game well-worth its price tag, especially if on sale.__Full Review__Good lord. What a game! This project is ambitious, thoughtful, thought-provoking, and perhaps most importantly - fun to play!Background:Caravan Sandwitch tells the story of a young person named Sauge who makes her way back to her home planet of Cigalo to investigate a cryptic star ship crash message from her sister Garance, who went missing many years before...As she unravels the mystery of what happened to Garance, she also connects the dots in a deeper mystery, to understand her own home world and the efforts taken by its inhabitants to hold their lives together in the wake of a complete planetary stripping of resources, led by "The Consortium," an ominous, omnipresent yet never seen corporate entity that has bled Cigalo and countless other planets dry. I'll leave it there and let the story do the rest...Graphics:For any indie project, this is nothing less than stunning. And even if you aren't a fan of indie games, there's so much in the artistic style that deserves recognition! I couldn't stop taking screenshots of the beautiful scenes throughout the game.Gameplay:Caravan Sandwitch's gameplay is such a fascinating blend! Have you ever played a game that is:1) Open-world2) Non-violent (also, no dying!)3) Cute4) FUN4) Sad and surprisingly mature? Well, if you this game then your answer is yes. The game provides numerous quests, mysteries and even vehicle upgrades that keep the game moving forward with interesting progress. The open world environment evokes comparisons to other "cute" games in the genre, particularly BOTW on the AAA production-side, and A Short Hike on the indie side. Sites may be discovered, and likely you will need to revisit them in order to solve the total sum of mysteries each location offers.While there are no serious issues, two complaints are worth mentioning. First, in the last third of the game progress can feel a bit tedious. If you have already unlocked all upgrades, old technological parts - the most common of discoveries at each location in the game - are no longer relevant, and serve as an unnecessary distraction to completing the story. Second, while the controls of the game are by and large excellent, there are periodic and minor disruptions to movement, particularly when climbing up ledges or riding the grappling hook. The result is, in worst case scenarios, a need to repeat the action. In a game where time is not of the essence and dying is impossible, this is not a huge issue at all. However, it can be frustrating in the late-game, when there is nothing else to do but finish the story.Music/Sound:Am I an expert at music or sound? NO! Those things are so hard to do well in a game, but Caravan Sandwitch pulls them both off excellently. Great music, and fascinating sounds that provide perfect environment feel and make character actions really pop (I want to hear some huffing and puffing when I run!). The soundtrack is understated and thoughtful. In its best moments it truly embodies and accentuates the atmosphere in an emotionally powerful way.Narrative:The game's narrative is probably its weakest aspect. This doesn't mean the story is bad! It's just a testament to the excellent artwork, amazing music and sound, and great game play. If we compared this game to a five act play, I'd say the third and fourth acts felt a bit uneven. There were many stories wrapping up at once, and while they were technically all connected by the larger narrative, they felt distant, or separate. I believe this is because critical aspects of these tangential narratives were relayed exclusively through dialogue after each "mission," rather than in the midst of the game play itself. This game is not exactly designed to reveal such insights in the middle of game play, so its "tell, don't show" method is not surprising. Still, I couldn't help but feel I was forcibly wading through moments in the story, when it naturally should have carried me downstream. That said, the end of the game wraps things up nicely enough that I was not especially bothered by this, and would absolutely recommend this game to anyone who is a fan of the genre.Thank you, game makers! You've put together something really excellent and I'm happy to have played it :)

Story progression is adequate albeit a little slow, but I never felt like the game was dragging its feet. Gameplay is quite linear except for one decision you make at the end. However, that decision didn't really feel that impactful to me. IMO it would've been far more interesting if the decision had been about  and the moral dilemma arising from that conflict of interests.The worst thing about the game is probably the platforming. It's passable with mouse and keyboard, but with a controller it's downright bad, because the camera angle (and thus your trajectory) keeps changing at the most inopportune times. I fell off a ledge because of this on several occasions. And I have a suspicion the developers are aware of how bad it is, because the game has no fall damage at all.At the end of the day I think this is an average game, but still worth checking out if you're looking for a nice, casual open world adventure.Rating: ★★★☆☆

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun game about a young adult and the community she returns to to navigate grief, hope, and uncertainty in the wake of capitalist exploitation. The main character is super naive in a refreshing way, and the other characters you meet along the way are pretty joyful. The gameplay is more exploration than puzzle-based, which feels like a bit of a missed opportunity considering how much I visited the same parts of the map many times. Very pretty, with fun musical choices. Everyone is gay also, and it's handled really well... except for Baie. How dare he hit on me only to find the love of his life halfway through our date! I do recommend it - get it on sale :)

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game. No combat, no fall damage, excellent driving. Just exploration...what's that...go have a look...how do i get up there...figure it out. Do little tasks for people, un jam the map. Get upgrades for the van that help you scan the area and later get a grapple to yank doors off their hinges or pull boxes half buried in the sand.Played 11 hours so far and the time just whizzed by. There are still some cables I need a pulley for to use and some doors I am not able to open so, I need to work out how as the game has almost no hand holding at all. It is just very chilled relaxing exploration with driving that is better than some AAA games I've played. (I'm looking at you Ghost Recon Wildlands!!!)It's also very easy on the eye, really pretty graphics and excellent sound.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of games are filled with action, and a lot of games throw you into stories that pull you around. The artistic style and tone of which pair so nicely to create a world that makes you want to explore because of some primal curiosity. _childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: Chill game with a lot of interesting places to explore, and the art is absolutely gorgeous. The environments look spectacular, which makes it a joy just to roam around. As with most games of this genre, there are a lot of quests ranging from engaging and story-advancing to mundane and boring. At a certain point, the narrative gets very heavy-handed and gets in the way of exploration, but it settles down a bit before it picks up again in the end. The overarching story is interesting enough, but the dialog is pretty painful and overly wordy. I ended up skipping most of it. The endings were rather underwhelming, but for me, it was more about the journey. It’s also the wokeiest wokester of a woke game that ever woked. I’d give the game itself a 7/10 with a DEI score of 100 bazillion out of 10. They/them stuff all over the place, which makes the somewhat poorly translated dialog just that much more confusing. Ignorable, however, especially if you skip most of the dialog, which I was doing anyway. Overall, recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: A cozy and heartwarming game.Journeying through this game is quite relaxing, to quote the game's description "no combat, no death, no timer, just you, your van, and the world."The style, ambiance and music made for a very pleasant and cozy experience, I enjoyed my stay in Estello Village and was delighted by the sense of community within Cigalo!
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished Caravan Sandwitch, a gorgeous cozy game with a great soundtrack. Gameplay was perfectly serviceable for its short length, but I struggle to recommend it because I found the writing really boring. There’s the seeds of a great game here, but the game struggles to get you to care with its incredibly simplistic narrative and dialog that reads like it was written for a 4th grade reading level. Wasted potential in my opinion, maybe it reads better in the original French. Once you’ve seen the trailer you’ve seen about all this game has to offer.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: I've loved each character I've met in this game. You start out on your way back home to investigate your estranged sister's distress call and are soon entangled with the last remaining residents of your old home planet. Think scifi Night in the Woods kinda. The game's story does a great job of drawing you in. The main character can reminisce but also has a good reason for needing a recap from everyone (she's been gone for years). It's a story about a group of people struggling to make a home out of a place that space capitalism has destroyed. It's heartwarming in all the best ways without being cloying.It's also, of course, beautiful. one of the few games where I find myself savouring the lookout points and panning the camera around to get a feel for the world through the environmental design. Great work all around.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: Caravan SandWitch is a small-scale open world adventure that delivers a tale that’s as heart warming as it is sombre; it’s filled with nuanced relationships and impressively deep lore, and I found it a joy to experience. There’s little to fault about the cosy, risk free gameplay except that it simply may not be to everybody’s taste, but for me, it makes a nice change of pace to a landscape that’s currently bubbling over with ultra-tough soulslike adventures. Pottering around in your beat up old van and doing good deeds for people feels genuinely rewarding, and exploring the final abandoned outposts of civilisation on Cigalo offers a sense of adventure that’s so much bigger than its 10-15 hour runtime. Full Review:
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: I became utterly obsessed after playing the demo. The worldbuilding is gorgeous and the characters all feel so real, even the giant frogs! As someone from a small island currently living in a big city, the planet Cigalo and Estello Village give me this feeling of almost being home again. So if you're feeling homesick, this is definitely the game for you.The storytelling is beautiful and I enjoy the diversity of the characters and their identities. It feels very natural and normalized rather than divergent and preach-y. The gameplay is relatively simple but in a way that doesn't make the game boring and actually allows for more people to play. There are many accessibility features, like motion sickness reduction, that I've not seen before in other games.Overall, I'm in love with Caravan Sandwitch and cannot wait for more developers to put out games like this.

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful little exploration game not without flaw, but a commendable and satisfying one made by a small team. Successfully emulating larger titles by dramatically reducing its scope, the game offers a tight, bloat-free experience that does not overstay its welcome.The game engages the player by offering a limited amount of tools to work with in a dilapidated world to great effect. Unlocking necessary tools is achieved by driving and meeting characters to assist them with their problems. Think Kiki's Delivery Service meets vehicle exploration. There is no combat in this game.I did encounter minor issues playing on Steam Deck using the medium graphics setting, including a particle effect that played at a higher speed than intended, a couple minor collision issues with the pulley and wench system. I also was not able to properly unlock the Community Service achievement due to a bug. These are all negligible when the game as a whole was polished and enjoyable from beginning to end.The game is a heartfelt story of grief and connection in a post-colonial world where the abandonment of critical commercial infrastructure affects regular people. If exploring that landscape and having a few surprises along the way sounds interesting to you, Caravan SandWitch offers a terrific bite-sized open world experience that has the ambition of a triple-A studio at a smaller level. I recommend this title, particularly when on sale. It is a wonderful world to immerse yourself in, if only for a short while.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: I arrive at my hometown to be invited back to an old ladies place for tea and a place to rest, luckily my friends, family and literally everyone here is a socialist and were kind enough to lend me the only vehicle on the entire planet, give me food and upgrade my vehicle as repayment for poking a stick into some signal jammers. I find some of the early ability blocks a bit frustrating, sometimes im not sure if I should or shouldn't be able to solve an area, and even the spaces just outside of the first town seem beyond my current understanding and abilities in game. It would have been nice to have the environment progress in difficulty the further you move away from the first town, but within scope I believe there is opportunity to convey when something is not accessible yet. Some areas feel artificially locked out too, some spots look like I should be able to use my van or some parts of the environment to find my own paths through puzzles but the environments are meticulously crafted against that. I feel like that is a missed opportunity for player creativity and instead of encouraging that freedom of exploration its punished as a waste of time.I also think the map UI desperately needs some attention, just a little arrow up or down to show if a target is above or below you would help tremendously especially given the amount of verticality this game has.Great game otherwise and a must play. It's especially fun on the steamdeck
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: I had wishlisted this game on a whim when it showed up as a recommendation on Steam and after finishing it quickly became one of my favorite games of all time.I was entranced by the story and characters to the point I quickly found myself wanting to do every side quest possible that when I realized I missed some tasks and immediately wanted to play another file, which I'm about to make my after work cool down.The map is filled with many landmarks and points of interest, I found myself wishing I had more markers though you will easily be able to remember scenery in this game. The map is the perfect size that backtracking doesn't feel like a chore. Matter of fact, it's hard to backtrack after a certain point cause you would have unlocked the whole map and would loop around.And the art style! It's a perfect fit and it's so lovely. I found myself taking screenshots at every viewpoint, cutscenes, or even when just traversing through Cigalo.I definitely recommend this game, especially for fans of cozy games that want something different. Now if you'll excuse me, it's time for file number 2!

_childDocuments_.review: Caravan SandWitch is, to me, a perfect game. There is no shortage of beauty to discover, a haunting mystery tied with an equally haunting atmosphere. I've always wanted a game about a nomadic desert life, and even though this is a peaceful game it scratches many of the same itches as Borderlands, Mad Max, Half-Life 2 and even Assassin's Creed. I cannot recommend this game enough.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are looking for a slower paced open world exploration experience that does not feel either overwhelming with sheer size or too mechanically challenging, Caravan Sandwitch is a game that might be worth your attention.In this game you will be chatting up a few NPCs, doing side quests with bits and pieces of exploration puzzles that involve a vehicle. The gameplay loop is quite robust and boiled down to the basics - as you explore (either during quests or freely), you'll be picking up components to simply advance towards a new ability for your van which will enable you to access more of the gorgeously presented world that's just pleasant to look at and cruise through, There are no combat systems, and even as far as platforming puzzles go there is no fall damage either. It is a safe sandbox, and outside of a few minor glitches  at the time of writing this review there are no real friction points within the game itself.I would say Caravan Sandwitch does not try to be more than what it appears to offer, and it's its honest strength. You can expect to finish the game in under 10 hours, or slightly more if you're a completionist. I approached the game during a time when I was looking for a slower paced, pleasant experience I could "vibe" in, and Caravan Sandwitch let me accomplish exactly that.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: Caravan SandWitch is warm and comfy like a soft fleece blanket. And it's filled with absolutly adorable people, and Sauge (the main character) is so kind, honest, real, I simply love her.It's filled with love, kindness, friendship, and filled my heart joy and serenity!I'm eager to see the next project from Studio Plane Toast!

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful story led game with memorable graphics and engaging characters. Puzzles never become frustrating and most (not all) of the side missions advance the story as much as the main missions.It's an enjoyable hybrid of Jusant and Sable. The story advancing through missions rather than self led discovery.Main advancement and game is towards the discovery of where you sister went/crashed/disappeared, on a planet drilled out to provide material for a Dyson sphere. It has some side quests that advance this story and other quests that are essentially filler (I'm desperate to find my sister, why are you asking me to return a mixer?) - but that's life. Hindering and helping is a mysterious antagonist and a cast of characters that are enjoyably diverse.Good and inventive game mechanics, well implemented vehicle physics, exquisite scenery and mysterious, explorable abandoned ruins driven by a plot and sub-plot that is engaging with a message make this a highlight of the year in gaming.
