_childDocuments_.review: Lovely game, perfect for chilling for a few hours. If you enjoy exploring nooks and crannies with your van and on foot, and solving quite simple puzzles where you have to figure out how to get from point A to point B, don't mind backtracking once you've unlocked some new mechanics, go for it. I enjoyed the main story as well as all the side quests and chats that let each character shines and echoed some of the issues we are facing too in a thoughtful way. We only get to explore a very small part of this world and learn about some of its lore but it was the perfect length for me. Longer and I would have found it repetitive, shorter and I would have been left wanting more. The art is great, the OST and sound design too. It was lovely to stop and admire the guarrigue and calanques, and listen to the wind and animals. You may get stuck a few times and driving the van on a controller can get a little tricky (you can't do tight turns) but you can TP to your van or TP to the village if that happens. There's no death or fall damage mechanic, which is awesome. The only tiny issue I've had is missing a quest at the very beginning and not knowing how I did that. Also be aware that when you're on a van mission, you can't deviate from the set course -not going off road like you can otherwise- nor get out of your van so do your exploring outside these. Merci, Plane Toast! I won't forget Cigalo and its inhabitants.Some content warnings if you need them (spoilers): .

Same with ladders. It just seems a bit off teleporting in and out of the van or on to ladders. Other than that, pretty good game.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: Caravan SandWitch is reminiscent of older Nintendo titles in the best possible way. It's a peaceful, charming, low stakes, character driven narrative that lets the player progress and explore at their own pace. Its vibe and stylised presentation are in the same vein as Jusant, Wavetale, and Sable. The fact that I eagerly 100% completed this game while leaving bigger and bolder AAA games in my library untouched says a lot about how engaging it is.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: Small independent developed gem. The enviroment is unique, technological ruins you're able to explore with creative ways involving your handly big metal friend on 4 wheels. Driving around your caravan feels just right. But being able to just perform the abilities of your caravan freely, makes the gameplay very smooth. If you're looking for relaxation with semi-open world gameplay and puzzle solving where you climb stuff, or drive around, this might be for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: Has a really well put together world and story that unravel slowly in a really nicely paced way with some fun calm exploration mechanics. Manages to get the big exploring the world feel while not feeling overwhelming quite well. Also art direction and effects really take advantage of Lumen well to just look really nice. Really recommend for anyone who likes exploration and story driven games.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: A fun game and great if you enjoyed titles like Sable and Journey.The art style is a huge standout for this game, the amount of screenshot potential is very high throughout! Without spoilers: I thought the end would be quite predictable but ended up being pleasantly surprised. I would have liked to see it expanded on a bit though cutscene wise.The Rientos were a main attraction for me, I really hope we see their story expanded on in a sequel.A few suggestions Id have: The Van itself lacked a bit of personality in the handling, it felt too snappy driving forward and in reverse and the physics of the van didnt feel quite right for me. Id love it to have a bit more weight and have a bit more challenge driving through the environment. Spinning tires, sliding around, taking time to stop. Right now it feels a bit like driving an RC car. This contrasts the main character Sauge who feels really good to control and feels like a lot of love was pt into the character controller of.The desert itself was also made to sound like this big dangerous thing from the characters in the story, so its weird that you can run around (and across it) without the van with basically no ramifications! I doubt anyone would really try, but it would be cool if there was some kind of heat bar and maybe your clothes or packing water would allow you to spend longer away from the shade or your van. Survival elements! Just an idea.Its also kind strange that there is no fall damage, it felt super weird being able to (and it being the quickest way) jump from the top of the refuge all the way back to my van without any negative effect.If a sequel was to come around, id also love to see the characters expanded upon a little bit. In a game without combat the cast is a pivotal point, yet I feel ive only just scratched the surface of many of these people. So to conclude, if a sequel is made and a few of the points I made above are considered, Id buy it in a heart beat. Im looking forward to seeing what the team does next
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: So, I've finished this game. And I can say: this is a good game! Its very calm for me. It's just pure, calm exploration. But story is also very good. But I mostly love art style and atmosphere. There is no death, no HP, no stamina - and its great. If you love to spend few evenings in some cozy game, if you love calm exploration (oh, whats here on the horizon? what if I climb to this tower?) - this game for you!
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: Shorter game, but just about the right length for the wonderful story and fun exploration. Side quests were numerous and really built out the world, and the main story had checkpoints that let you know you should finish side quests before moving on. Overall very pleased, and I encourage people to try the demo. Isn't it great that demos are a thing again?
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: Finished this game. Good story and good graphics with pretty art style that personally i like it. Gameplay is simple puzzle platforming with open world. Soundtrack is good to and bring cozy feel. Worth it for the price and the game length is qood. Make me remember about Beyond Good and Evil. Hopefully in next game the developer made, add more fauna or flora to make the world more life.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed the art style. The music, although I don't speak French, was very beautiful. I enjoyed the story and the game play. It was relaxing and engaging, I look forward to more from the creators. I also like the inclusive story. I haven't played many games that embrace or are excepting of all lifestyles like same sex marriage/relationships. 5/5 Bravo
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: An honestly incredible game. Was so excited when it released, just beat it today and I have to say it was worth the purchase! The game's got a captivating story with a great pace of gameplay with plenty of mystery to reveal! The puzzles were just complex enough to stay enjoyable without requiring a guide or anything crazy.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: After playing the demo I was very much looking forward to this exploration, puzzle game and I will say it didn't disappoint. I enjoyed collecting all the components while exploring the map and figuring out the puzzles. It was a very chill game which I appreciated and loved. I usually play exploration games with combat so it was nice having a break from that especially with no fall damage for once. I liked how the tasks were given so you didn't miss any of them and the game let you know you should finish tasks before moving on. The art style and music were amazing. So beautiful. I'm also new to playing with a keyboard and mouse and this game is a good intro.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: Super chill and casual game. The environment is beautifully crafted and the climbing is satisfying. The characters are lovely too (Abricot is my favorite!). The background score and music is fantastic, there were moments where eyes watered listening to them. Overall game direction is amazing!Finally, some nitpicking:- Keep pressing (X) to continue with a conversation is kinda annoying- When in scan mode, can't see the amazing environment 😟- The pacing of the game feels slightly slower than I personally would have liked- Camera glitches and clipping, although not frequent, when it happens, is annoying
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: Cozy vibes, fun urban-exploration-based environmental puzzles, beautiful art direction, and an interesting story that doesn't overstay its welcome, featuring positive themes like human decency, respect, and generosity. That description either IS your jam, or it isn't. I finished the game feeling inspired, rather than drained. Ten hours well spent.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: Caravan SandWitch has a great atmosphere and world for you to explore, with an engaging narrative to go alongside it. I enjoyed exploring the planet, searching for components and points of interest, and taking in all that Cigalo had to offer. If you enjoyed titles like Sable, I think you'd also enjoy Caravan SandWitch.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: Caravan Sandwitch is an absolute blast! I've always gravitated towards games that give me a sense of exploration and puzzle solving and this game gave that to me in spades. The open world didn't feel too compact or needlessly stretched out. This is especially helpful in that there isn't much of a "fast travel" system in place.The game's art and lighting is gorgeous. The quasi-cell shaded look of the characters didn't feel out of place in the world at all! The score and soundtrack are spot-on as well, comfortable and not invasive, but I do feel the background music had a bit more variety. The twangy guitar and soft vocals fit well but seemed too repetitious after a few hours of play.Gameplay controls were consistent and responsive once I got used to not oversteering the van around tight corners. I  particularly liked how snappy Sauge was to play. Her movement was fluid and jumping was tight and controllable. I never felt like the devs took any shortcuts with movement in this game.Now as for the story, Sauge is simply trying to find out what happened to her sister. The various characters she come sin contact with during the game offer clues and insights as to what happened, usually by asking you to do a quest for them. Now there were a few times where the quest information or map locations seemed in consistent or somewhat vague, so I hope the devs take a look at that. Now as far as the ending goes... well I don't want to spoil anything for anyone, but the ending needs some work. It was a bit abrupt and I didn't feel like it offered a proper emotional payoff.Finally, there were a few buggy moments in Caravan Sandwitch. A flight of stairs and a door threshold I found seemed poorly aligned with the floor they were on or next to. Easy to get around though with a quick jump. There was also an issue with am activation button disappearing later in the story, but a quick exit and restart of the game helped fix that. There were also a few occasions where the van had to be parked in just the right spot or else Sauge would fall off the tether when she got close to the ledge of the buildings.Overall, I'd say this was a fantastic game. It kept me entertained to the point where I even managed to get all the achievements for it. That said, I did have to use a guide two find the last two I was missing. There's a hidden fetch quest in which you have to find 6 stuffed toys in game. Completing it will net you Community Service and New Look provided you've done all the other content in the game.I do hope that there's more to this universe than we've seen before. It would be great to see Plane Toast revisit Caravan Sandwitch again in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: a really beautiful looking game and enjoyable exploration experience, the game is not super long, but for the price I would recommend people give this game a shot! throughout the game you unlock new tools to go back to past areas to explore more, this could be a positive or negative for some people. the game has been completely bug free for me, and feels like a pretty well polished experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: I thoroughly enjoyed this game from start to finish. It has a lovely art style and relaxing but rewarding gameplay. Although I can imagine it is not for everybody, but you will no right away from playing the demo if it is your cup of tea. I found it very addictive and completed it in a handful of sittings. It was the perfect length and didn't outstay its welcome.I would also like to praise it on a technical level, as it was a very smooth experience on my machine. No stutters or bugs of any kind. I was particularly impressed with the AMD frame generation, as it allowed me to get a locked 120fps at 4K, using the quality preset. I played the game on a machine equipped with a 5800X3D and an RTX 3090. I used RTX HDR with great results, as the game doesn't include native HDR. I was initially concerned about the lack of DLSS, but the FSR looked really great in this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: This was a beautiful, atmospheric exploration game with compelling characters and a mysterious central narrative. I wouldn't say it breaks any boundaries in terms of gameplay, but the whole experience feels really solid and intentional. The art direction is the clear highlight here, as well as the music. I wish the van had a more advanced handling model or felt a bit more responsive. You spend a lot of time driving between locations and it doesn't quite compare to a dedicated racing/driving game.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: Felt like a mix between an interactive storybook and a Metroid style puzzle game, with large sections of open world exploration where you are looking for the next spot you can unlock to be rewarded with more cutscenes and story.  There were moments of pure joy and excitement and parts that fell more flat and felt a touch unpolished, but overall the length of the game means you won't be sitting in one place too long and the overall game is rewarding.  I missed some achievements, but completed all the in-game missions I found in about 10 hours and enjoyed the game!
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: SOME SPOILERS BELOW (I try to keep it vague)Such a great little gem I hope more people come across! I enjoyed exploring the planet of Cigalo and the van controls were easy to use and super responsive. The art and little sounds characters make when speaking really gave the game a comforting vibe that was easy to dive back into in-between play sessions. Great game to 100% and felt nice getting that badge at the end! Really can't wait to see what else the team gets up to.I did feel a disconnect with the world meant to be this barren, dangerous place (hence why you need the van to avoid 'heatstroke') and the lack of death mechanics. It was hard to be as invested in the story and its characters due to a lack of stakes affecting anything I really interacted with in the game.LIGHT SPOILERS:I felt that the two endings could have been combined into one as it only really changed where your player character ends up rather than the entire fate of Cigalo. Also, the reveal of the antagonist's identity wasn't the strongest in my mind. Maybe with less characters and more frequent visits back to the village, I could've felt a deeper connection to the people I hadn't seen in six years. Additionally, it felt like people forgave or moved on a little too quickly and any NPC's that would push back on coming with you for a particular quest, quickly caved after a line or two.Overall, I'd recommend the game to someone looking for a light, pick up and play experience with a great soundtrack and cute art!
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: I don't often do this, since I don't usually play games in the 'cozy' genre, but these are small indie devs and I saw them getting some unpleasant hate on Twitter, so I decided to buy this at full price and leave a positive review to show them my support. I might get into gamedev myself someday so I wanna give a hand to the little guys where I can.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game. An instant indie classic. I love how the hard sci-fi elements are blended and grounded in the folksy ascetic. The driving mechanics are good, but dark-souls this is not. There is no real way to lose, just the joy of exploration and the occasional mild puzzle to solve. The writing and narrative is excellent.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: this was a nice romp. small open world with some characters and quests and collectionables.a bit for most people, its a nice cozy game.no action or combat of any sort, and no stress either.its very much a take-your-time game, and anything that needs to be done before you move on will usually give you a notification along the lines of "maybe you wanna do this before you do the next thing", so no FOMO either.itll give you a few hours of fun, and if you only want the story, thatll take some hours too.definitely worth the price i paid in full.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: Such a charming and cozy little adventure, even if it drags some the end, if you do everything and the ending itself could have been more fleshed out. Will need to go low settings, with resolution scaling at 80 or 90% to get a mostly stable 60fps on Steam Deck. Still looks good like that due to the artstyle, except the shadows and having things pop in quite close to the main character.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: Likes:- An adventure featuring a world brimming with character & mystery- Freedom to explore as you please (some places you cant until you progress story)- Quest that involves every NPC in the game- A good ending but could have been betterDislikes- Having to go back to garage everytime the van gets stuckNeutral- Mild woke elements purely for inclusivity and not pushing any agenda- A good ending but could have been better
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a lot longer than expected, and that's definitely not a bad thing! This game was a lot of fun to explore and interact with, I loved most of the characters you meet throughout. The game was very fun and very silly, nice vibrant colors, and a H U G E map to explore.The only thing i didn't like about the game is how 99.9% is locked behind upgrade advancement. That's not necessarily a bad thing, just not my personal cup of tea. Otherwise a very very cool experience and 100% worth the money and 13 hours I put into exploring every corner of the world
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: A few days ago, there was a post on a social media site asking "If you lived for a week in a game you last played, how screwed up would you be?” My game was Caravan SandWitch and living in it for a week would be a joy. To be able to drive around in a van around the deserted areas, having a cup of coffee with friends in a local coffee shop, hanging around a garden with grandma and doing all that in a place as beautiful as Cigalo would be a blast. I'm biased towards deserted areas, but still, for me, an interesting setting can hide a lot of gameplay flaws. I'm not saying there are many, but it's definitely an interesting game in many ways.Although I like games with no fail option I must say that I missed some kind of fall damage, because being able to jump down from any height while climbing is such a prominent gameplay feature, I felt a bit like I was cheating. I must also say that I fully support micro open worlds like this one and Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip.Overall, I very much enjoyed my time in Cigalo.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: A hidden gem with cozy music to keep you occupied for a good 8-10 hours. This game kept me hooked from start to finish! This game is aimed at exploration and rewards your curious nature all the while taking you along on a journey with a great story. Thank you to the dev team for this hidden gem because you can feel the love put into the development of this game the entire time when playing it.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: Cozy adventure game that’s easily beaten in under 10 hours but I ended up exploring a bunch more because the game looks that good and I wanted to make sure I saw it all, did it all. Good music and sound, the van is actually fun to drive, some dialog seems a but unpolished but the story is not bad at all. Glad I purchased it.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: Looks pretty, has a dope soundtrack, compelling world and narrative on top of being fun to explore. The upgrades have good synergy together and allow you to explore further and easier, making them feel like a real improvement and giving a sense of progression. Exploration and quests were a ton of fun, not just to get parts for upgrades, but because you learned so much about this intriguing world through dialog or seeing Sauge comment on the environment they're exploring. Reaching a cool spot and getting a few words from Sauge is the best reward in my book. Can't get enough of Cigalo and it's people!
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a sucker for games that reward exploration, and in that regard Caravan SandWitch seems tailor made for me. No combat, no chance of death and puzzles are deceptively simple, but everything works in favor of exploring a surprisingly vast world and feeling an immense sense of satisfaction when you finally get to reach a place you spotted from far away and you weren't sure it was even possible to get to.As the game progresses you unlock a few more tools that help you reach previously closed areas, but also the game is designed in a way where you can simply use ingenuity to reach certain places without those tools, which feels incredibly rewarding, especially when there's some collectible item to find. It's a relaxing experience in general, but you can still find a few tense moments by trying to pull off some tricky platforming.There are a bunch of items to collect, and the majority of them have some sort of purpose so you don't feel you're collecting just for the sake of it.From a technical perspective the game is fantastic. It looks gorgeous with a cartoonish, somewhat cel-shaded art style and colorful environments. Music is calm and relaxing, and fits the world very well.The story is simple and I'm only a few hours in but so far not particularly original, but works well enough to setup the main gameplay loop, and the worldbuilding gets more interesting as you progress. Characters fare a bit better, since they're varied and colorful and their sidequests tend to help build up and deepen the world more than the main story does.While I'm still not finished with the game so far the experience hasn't gotten old and since the purpose of the game is to be relaxing I'd say it does its job perfectly. It's a full recommendation from me, particularly if you're into exploration and you don't mind games with no combat.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: A charming little platforming/exploration game with a quiet atmosphere. I like that this game often invites you to take in the world's scenery, listen to music on the radio, and that quests culminate in trinkets decorating your caravan to make it feel more lived-in. The driving *feels* good, it's enjoyable to zoom around the world especially once it opens up. Also, the lack of fall damage is fun both in driving and platforming; it's fun to jump from a roof, cliff, or zipline and land next to your objective.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice game, with a strong nostalgic vibe. You catch glimpses of a much larger world that are sufficient to understand the setting, and the adventure itself is focused on a small cast of lovable characters. If you want to enjoy the worldbuilding to its full extent, remember to talk to everyone until they start responding with a picture. I would welcome a deeper exploration of the universe, be it in video-game form or as something else.The core gameplay loop is about exploration, dialogs and deliveries. I appreciated the lack of fall damage, and the controls while on foot, which made it all about the exploration and not focused too much on precision. The length is right for this type of game, and it comes to a satisfying conclusion before the (somewhat) repetitive gameplay loop becomes tiring.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr : ahah lil gay trucker go wheeemore seriously, caravan sandwitch is a game that should be played more like an interactive story in a world that should be explored as it contain context about the story and overall the world, go explore, enjoy the sights, the ambiance, music while progressing through the main story.+ it got a friend shaped sentient robot
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: This game is beautiful, I love its simple but very colorful and evocative art. Overall there is very cool vibe and it very much reminds of the South of France. Just wandering in the various environments is a pleasure by itself.The gameplay is simple but polished. Driving and exploration are the core of the game and are nice. I like the overall progression based on improving the van in order to get access to new parts of the ruins. However, I felt that visiting the same ruins for the fourth or fifth time takes away some of the initial appeal of the exploration.My main complain would be about the writing which is too simple for a game that obviously wants to tell a good story. The whole material (planet wrecked and abandoned by a greedy corporation) is cool but the story just scratchs the surface, characters just share some very simple thoughs and nothing goes deeper than "Not everything is fine but it's okay". I understand that the game want to tell a lighter story than something like Citizen Sleeper but I would have liked more developped characters and situations.But overall I really had a good time exploring this beautifully crafted world. For a first game, that's a very damn good one!
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: PC specs in profile. No optimization issues. Ran into a bug where the screen would not stop shaking. Happened twice and both times it persisted until relaunch. Not a big deal but worth mentioning.  Game is chill and relaxing, only ever so slightly more engaging than a pure walking simulator. Very light puzzle/platfoorming elements, but again, there are no stakes so it's all very laid back. The world is kinda interesting, but I found the characters to be mostly extremely boring, so I wasn't very engaged by much outside of the core mystery. I think I 100%'ed the game in about 11 hours. Come to think of it, I may have missed one or two collectibles (stuffed animals) but I did clear out all the sidequests from the log. Light recommendation here. Played it as palate-cleanser and it's fine at that.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: A really cozy open world adventure. The story was a bit underwhelming at times & a tad short, the driving mechanics can lead to you speed boosting in reverse gear occasionally & the absence of any combat can lead to some tedious moments; especially with the amount of back-tracking required for resource collection for van upgrades. But the world, characters & soundtrack are fantastic and I can highly recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: Overall good, relaxing chill game+Enjoyed the world design, especially the starting coastal area and the village+Easy exploration, colored paths and rocks literally indicates "climb here"+A little bit of eerie feel in the ruins (and the witch) gives me chills, which really adds the excitement~idc about LGBT+ or woke stuff, as long as it doesn't affect the game/ gameplay itselfalso enjoyed the character designs (at least good looking/ attractive)who cares about colored races when there's frog people in it, loved them-Driving is a bit funky, especially when 30% of time is spent on driving and travelling, though it's acceptable as it's not a racing game-The "stuck? reset" button is the same as action button, making it impossible to give up the van and continue exploration on foot-Some npc interaction actions are a bit repetitive, i'd prefer more variations or the action only appear during the 1st and last dialogue, with the rest having no action at all. I don't want npcs to wave their hand like crazy everytime when they speaks a sentence.-some bugs, though not game-breaking and devs are fixing it
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: Really loved the aesthetics and graphics of this, and the music fit perfectly with the style and the emotion of the game. The world building felt just right, it explained where you were and what events had taken place, but still left enough mystery to want to go out and explore. The map was more diverse than I thought it was going to be, for a desert planet, and each area felt unique and different to the last. Doing the side quests and talking with characters really helped set each of them apart and give each of them their own individuality and stories that you could follow along. And getting the cosmetic items on the van for helping them helped give a feeling of progression and that you were really part of the world.Some negatives early on for me were more quality of life things. I really wanted to have my scan of the area persist a bit. Being able to only mark one item felt a little frustrating at times, when I knew there was more items to collect in an area, but couldn't quite find where they were. I had to keep going back to the van to scan again and mark a new objective. At first I thought it was annoying to get to an area and realise I couldn't complete exploring without a certain mechanic unlocked, and that I would be tired of re-visiting locations. The way the game directed you back to some locations in later chapters anyway really helped with that, and it happened kind of organically anyway.I feel accomplished for finishing the main story, and relieved that I can jump straight back into my save before the final chapter, and go complete outstanding achievements without doing a full new play through.I highly recommend this to anyone wanting a relaxed evening or two or exploring and storytelling.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: Cool open world game without any fighting or combat whatsoever which is refreshing. The world is small enough so that it's not boring and big enough so it's cool to explore and  makes you wanna explore. The van is fun to drive around, at some point I used more the vehicle rather than the quick travel system.Cast of characters is colorful and nice, sound design and art direction is great. Takes around 10 hours if you're a completionist and the game doesn't overstay its welcome. I'd like more games like this.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: Was a interesting game. The art was perfect for this style of game. Puzzles were a good old classic "Can't get through right now. Have to come back with another bit". Story rang pretty good, and made you feel like this is exactly what you would do. Not huge or bloated with a few side quest sprinkled in with the main story. Pretty short. Only negative I would have to poke at is "Fetch questing" I get there are those moments where you need to get the thing to do the other thing. But that is pretty much all the game had you doing. But as I said on the hole it was a great game. Congrats to the Dev team
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: Nice and beautiful.  A quiet pleasure to play.  Will do a second play-through, just to re-experience the game play and the story.  I appreciate the understanding from the game developer that the van and the player will get stuck in geometry, which led to a simple way to get out of that predicament by returning to the garage, or just exiting and coming back.  When a dialog is exhausted, a lovely emoji is shown instead of dialog.  Overall a straightforward uncomplicated game, easy to play and get into the story.  I struggle with the van reverse speed, but I am sure that I could get better with more time.  Sometimes having a reasonable low ambition is all that is needed for a good game.  As a software engineer myself I always cringe in games when "hackers" and "hacking" are depicted, but I guess that is is more a modern meme and lore, rather than an accurate representation of my profession, so I will let it go :-)    Thanks for the love that obviously went into making this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: I have 35 years of gaming under my belt, so im coming from playing ALOT of games and Caravan SandWich jumped up my "best off" ladder instantly. What a abolute treasure of a game this is. I instantly was currious about the world, its tech, the story, the characters, the lore. The open world is beautiful, calm and tranquil. I INSTANTLY fell in love with this game world. I highly reccomend this game if you want a light puzzple platformer that takes you on a journey in your Van as you cruise the sand dunes. This game really shows that games is art
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: Fun little open world third-person platformer. Unique setting and characters, beautiful visuals. Keywords: relaxing, calm, casual, exploration.Has a number of thoughtful 'quality of life' controls and designs to reduce repetition and tedium.Flawless controls on Steam Deck and runs well, but wide open setting make the fan run at full. Battery drains in about 70 minutes (25 W pull seems to be typical).
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: I do not typically write reviews, because I don't think I care about the same things other gamers tend to, but I did want to write that I was delighted with this game. I was looking for something beautiful to look at, some exploration, some world building and clever little puzzles and navigational challenges. I got exactly that and many more pleasant game play experiences that I hadn't expected. The sound design was lovely, and the ongoing activities (components, challenges and collectables) never once felt like a grind. The characters were very chic and naturalistic, and I was honestly impressed with the final choices in the narrative, because I had a made a few guesses and didn't feel at all disappointed when they proved to be wrong. Everything was a little french, a little chic, and interactions of environment, sound, and allowance for the visuals to be highlighted and the pace to slow down were all really quite special. I think they also nicely captured the vibe of a young adult returning home and developing a new perspective on the people and environment they grew up in. Last, I noticed a lot of complaints regarding the LGBTQ2* characters in the game in the discussion threads. Many of the people I love most in the world are, and I was very happy to see characters like them represented in the game as I know them in life - just existing, the same as any one else. I'm not LGBTQ2*, and my experience wasn't diminished nor impacted in any way as I played.To focus on that alone is to live a deeply insecure and reactionary life, and those folks who have that kind of problem with inclusive content should move on to other titles. I'll keep an eye out for new games from this studio. Thank you for a wonderful 20 hours. :)

_childDocuments_.review: CS is a good solid, game marred by a poorly implemented objective system and some annoying bugs. It is very difficult to know exactly what one should be doing at an given moment, and where to go to do it.The game revolves around Sauge, a once-native of a planet abandoned by a mining corporation. Only a handful of people are left on the planet, living a peaceful life and scavenging what they need. Sauge retuirns to her home  after some time away when she receives an automated distress call from her sister's ship. Her sister vanished several years ago and is presumed dead. It's a compelling premise.The open-world playspace is large, but not so large that trvaersing it becomes a chore. There are sections where it is very easy to get turned around and lose one's way, and some of the terrain that is supposed to be driven on can be very vehicle unfriendly - often one will collide with a low-profile rock that wasn't visible on what otherwise looks like a flat piece of ground. That said, trundling around the world in Sauge's van is a pleasant enough experience. In the later part of the game one can unlock a fast-travel-style system that allows Sauge to quickly move between certain places. In fact, the system becomes an important part of the plot.There are several infuriating bugs - the camera and movement system will occasionally clash, especially in smaller or cramped spaces, resulting in Sauge inadvertently leaping off a narrow suspended plank. Some game objects have overlapping use volumes, and the game has difficulty knowing which object to prioritise, resulting in wasted time as Sauge ziplines away from the control panel she actually wanted to interact with. Sauge qill automatically clamber up onto smaller obstacles which is a nice touch, except when one simply want to interact with them; for example, Sauge will climb on top of a crate one is trying to open. After upgrading her van Sauge can use a grapplehook to create a kind of reverse zipline, but if the angle of the line is too steep Sauge will fall off at the top, and there's no way to know without trying.The French-to-English translation leaves something to be desired, and it's especially obvious with idiomatic phrases. I encountered more than one line that hadn't been translated at all, but thankfully I could understand what was said via context.All of these issues are minor compared to the canker sore of an objective system. Sauge receives texts from other characters with vague instructions on what to do. There's very little tracking of objectives, and virtually no front-loading. There are no up-front reminders of what Sauge should be doing moment-to-moment. I had to refer to a walkthrough to solve a critical quest.The music attempts to be unobtrusive and ambient, but merely becomes bland, uninteresting and repetitive. Too many areas of the map use the same music and after a while it becomes a kind of annoying background noise. For such an interesting setting a more dynamic, though restrained style might have worked better.Don't take my criticisms too harshly - if you enjoy narrative-driven relaxploration games then this one is definitely worth your time. The aesthetic is lovely, the characters are fun and the setting is interesting. I hope that the issues will be addressed in a future update.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: This is why I like indie games. A short self-contained single player experience with good ideas, something to say, and piles of charm. Gameplay is mainly exploration and meeting new characters. Exploration is allowed through gadgets, and by adding new gadgets, new areas are unlocked as the story progresses. I was impressed how the game can have such well though through mechanics with relatively limited production values. All the gadgets and puzzles feels logical, polished and fun!Unfortunately it's not as plain sailing in the technical department. The game is not spared an occasional switch-gone-bad bug or the "quantum door effect" where the door is open and closed at the same time. However, nothing a game reload wouldn't fix. The auto-saves are frequent and well made so it's not a problem. The only thing that could still use some attention are the optimizations. Frame rate dips in the larger areas are something you need to get used to and distracted me a bit from the immersion. Luckily, since there's not combat or any real danger, the technical issues won't spoil your progress.In fact I found it remarkable that a game that doesn't allow you to fire a single shot from a gun and where nobody dies - except for where story demands it - can be so much fun. Chapeau to the designers.This brings me to the last point I would like to make. Since there is no combat and since most of the interactions in the game are very positive, one could expect a wholesome stress-free experience. Be warned, this is not 100% the case here. The story takes a more serious turn and tells a grand finale which quite honestly felt a bit out of place, given both the production values of the game as well as the tone set in the first phase. Usually such a change of pace is a good thing, but in this case it left me a little disappointed. However, it should be said that this is purely subjective! In the end the authors stick the landing and manage to tell the story they wanted to. Far be it from me to tell them otherwise.By all means this game is recommended!

_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: as of writing I am not yet finished with the game but I'm decently close and feel confident in my opinions. overall I think this game is very good and well worth playing but it's also clear that they ran out of budget at a certain point and had to cut corners to get it out the door.starting off with the good I love the world and the characters, for the most part. I'm so glad to have a game that is just about helping people even when things seem bleak. there is no combat or real danger, its just drive around and do your best to help. what a lovely thematic exploration especially when most games seem to focus on combat as the main means of expression.I love a game about driving but not racing. Don't get me wrong I love racing games too but cars in games don't need to be used for that power fantasy. here the van is all about freedom of exploration and as a tool for helping others. you are only able to achieve what you can because of this van. it was gifted to you for free out of kindness and its your job to pay that kindness forward.exploration is fun and satisfying. the world is well designed and the game gives you the tools to make getting around and finding what you need to intuitive and easy. the gameplay is solid.problems start to arise with the previously mentioned cut corners though. the game has very limited animations and cutscenes amount to characters in their idle animations talking at eachother and cutting the camera abruptly to not ever show anyone moving. that itself is not inherently a problem and is a clever way to get around budget constraints. it can make cutscenes sometimes jarring and confusing though.the real problem is that the deeper you get into the game the more the english translation becomes stilted and at times near incomprensible. at least I assume its a translation since I'm not quite sure where Plane Toast is based at. while the story and writing initially hooked me eventually the dialogue starts feeling poorly machine translated with awkward phrasing, grammar mistakes, and sometimes complete nonsense sentences. it keeps getting worse the longer I play and it's really making me bounce out of the story since often I can't tell what is meant to be conveyed in a scene. the story seems to dissolve into the abstract when I really don't think that was the intention. I really hope Plane Toast is able to release a re-translation patch at some point because as it stands I'm really disappointed I'm not able to comprehend the story at its best.still, this game is worth playing and recommending. its got its flaws but those flaws don't come from lack of talent or passion, simply lack of budget.

_childDocuments_.review: Playing the demo: "oh, this is cute and chill and easy to enjoy"Completing the full game: "oh my god this is "Definitely a contender for the "games as art" crowd. It's chill, yeah. The gameplay mechanics are shallow, dialogue is pretty simple, there's no danger or challenge, the story has some weaknesses, and there is still quite a bit of roughness around the edges. Why does it still get an unquestioning thumbs-up?The "budget" here is spent in making the game immersive and genuine-feeling, and this is where the game shines. What's the worst example of a human-caused environmental disaster that you know of, and the level of neglect or immorality that was responsible for it? Can you picture what it would be like if it was ten times bigger? A hundred times? A million?. Can you imagine <whatever awful mess>, but scaled up to a sci-fi setting where humans and technology are powerful and advanced enough to span the galaxy? the meat of this game: it goes through every effort and painstaking detail to sell you the feeling that you are living in and exploring a wasteland that is man-made. The ravaged environment, the abandoned corporate facilities, the last survivors dotting the land, trying to cling to life any way they can... The game holds a mirror up to some of humanity's ugliest behaviors, and shows what it might be like if today's failures are carried out with tomorrow's tools. Cyberpunk? Solarpunk? Doomerism? Silent Spring in space? I dunno what's the proper label, but this game delivers on it for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: Caravan SandWitch: it's a delight.  Stunningly beautiful world straight from french comics, cute characters, chill, but intriguing story and killer soundtrack (honestly, probably the best one in 2024). I also like how despite low stakes and no fail states it feels like full blown game, instead of just narrative experience. The platformers like exploration is just so joyful. They also very smartly designed the campaign. At the very start you need to collect a lot of resources, which forces you to explore the whole map. While doing so you see where you can't go in yet until you obtain new stuff and then return those places multiple times to unlock new portions. This gives the world a feeling of actual physical space instead of just a scenography. You really get to know this world like a back of your hand.I just wish it had some dubbing. Full one was probably to expensive for devs so small. But just short shout or "hi" at beginning of convo, the way Yakuza handles side stories, would be huge improvement. This is a minor complain though. Overall, it's a triumph and if you want to chill in a game looking at breathtaking vistas, while still having plenty of gameplay to play around with, Caravan SandWitch is for you.

_childDocuments_.review: A pleasant ride through the desert! The first thing to really hit you about this game is the vibes. Having all these spots to sit around and take in the atmosphere while listening to the lowkey (and really good) soundtrack was great (I have plenty of screenshots), and I found getting around the planet pretty fun to start off with - you get used to the layout of the roads and know exactly how to get from point A to point B without checking the map by the end. I also found the setting to be quite compelling - a borderland planet wrecked by corporate greed where the people remaining are trying to do the best they can with what the have. Unfortunately, the rest of the writing is where the weak points of the game lie.There are some highlights, in particular a funeral mission which I thought was very pleasant. But that's really it, everyone in this game is pleasant to the point of it being grating within a few hours. There's not a lot of differences between them, there's not many jokes, there's no-one really going against the grain, everyone's just... there. The designs of the characters are a lot more striking than anything they actually say. The plot is functional but doesn't really go through any twists and turns apart from a final act that sorta just... exists. And in a game like this where there aren't any real puzzles and you're traveling around just to hear more dialogue, I think that's a rather strong negative.I did have a good time with this one and I think it deserves a gold star for running as perfectly as it did on my old machine while still being visually striking, but the game itself didn't really hit the highs that it could have.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: Caravan SandWitch is an exploration-focused game without combat, set in an open-world with incremental upgrades allowing to access to new zones.You search for your lost sister six years after her disappearance after receiving a distress signal. Set on your desert home planet Cigalo, you encounter colorful characters reconnecting and learning about a deeper mystery. The game excels in exploration, whether on foot or driving an upgradeable van, providing a cozy atmosphere to enjoy the stunning landscapes.I'll recommend it if you love mystery, thorough exploration, and heartfelt narratives with diverse characters.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: It's like a hybrid of Death Stranding and Little Kitty Big City. A serene little world to explore full of delightful characters. It just feels good to drive around or climb to a high point and look around. A must play if you like frogs.

_childDocuments_.review: I put this game into the same basket as Omno, Gris, Jusant and maybe Chants of S.its a short and cute, chill experience without much attachments or circumstance.its cute. its relax. characters are cute. gameplay is cute. story is short.game is short. map is way smaller than I thought it would be.the biggest flaw of this game is how small it is. because the concept of open world exploration somewhat promises a vast land but its a handcrafted yet tiny map.I adore this game but i fully understand why some people just dont vibe with it.that said i think its a bit expensive.it really should be under 15€

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful relaxing and intruiging gaming experience. 10/10. Will be replaying this game.  A world that is perfectly populated for a mostly deserted planet, with colour and characters that I doubt I will ever forget. If you like games with similar artstyles or tags you will enjoy this game. (coming from someone who has played a couple similar indie-lower poly games)First playthrough took me about 10 hours with most achievements and a lot of wandering around. Worth every minute.A game that shows the creators cared for it. Everything feels in its place and like it should be there, neither cluttered nor sparse. Beautiful design and gameplay that is well thought out and controls and movement that feel right and in their place. The characters and their respective backstories are fleshed out and interesting (especially loved the frog-like reinestos*-people race and its backstory) The world feels huge initially as you begin to open the map for the first time, but about after the 1/3 of the game you realise how great the size of the map is. Allowing you to travel to your objective (even on the other side of the world) in an amount of time that will not have you largely complaining and wishing there was a more convieneint skyrim esque system in place while also giving you heaps of places to explore (or finish exploring after unlocks) and tons of components to find.I really enjoyed the character talking dialog box style and think it really adds to the game and its simple, low animation aesthetic. If youre not a fan of this style, give this one a try (and give pronouncing the names a try) its really well worked and super easy to get through with conversatinos not taking too long and most of the time giving you clues and adding to the playthrough experience in the game.I have had almost no issues with bugs, the game is good at righting itself in odd places and keeping you from obviously being where you shouldnt and i appreciate the subtle ways it will tell you you shouldnt be there.I really enjoyed the open world aspect of this game that didnt railroad you nor overburden you with menial quests to do for every single character at every stage of the game. Length of game was perfect and left me only wanting more. Devs, if in the future you release anything else of this standard you will have my excitement and my support. 10/10 you guys crafted a beautiful game with a beautiful world and story. Well done!
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful small indie game, made by a French Team. It is really sweet, beautiful, and with a great OST. The story is also interesting, speaking a lot about ecology and humanity as a whole. The characters are interesting and diverse. The game as a whole is sweet, while also being ultimately pretty sad.The mood of the game, for me, feels like a mix between Outer Wilds and Celeste, I recommend it, and you shouldn't really hesitate to buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: Caravan SandWitch is a small game with a big heart. Cigalo is a beautiful landscape, with many hidden gems. _childDocuments_.review: On the whole, I'd recommend this game - it's worth playing as a fun, chill exploration game.The good:MusicVibesExploration - it's fun to spend time exploring nooks and crannies and, fully explore the mapFrog people are coolThe bad:The van handles like ass. I'm not sure what it feels like, but it's not a vehicleVery buggy - you'll encounter places where you get stuck, visual bugs, and in one location I encountered a progression-blocking bug that I had to quit and reopen the game to resolve, for some reason the game also reverted to French once I finished it.EDIT: I've just spotted fixes for two of the big bugs I encountered in the latest patch notes, so it seems like the game will get more and more polished if given a bit of time.

_childDocuments_.review: Short, but sweet open world game. No combat to speak of. _childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: A delightfully cozy exploration game with light puzzles and platforming mechanics thrown in. I'm not normally a fan of games with a tone of driving (skill issue I'm afraid), but the driving in this game is super beginner-friendly (bonus points for both stick and traditional steering options). If you're having issues with the driving I recommend adjusting your graphic settings and camera sensitivity. (My best driving experience was with the camera sensitivity at 70.) The story makes you think about the price we pay for aggressive corporate progress and the inherent loss of community that comes with it.10.8 hours is how long it took me to complete my first full playthrough, but I would play this game again for the other ending, and to see what happens when you take a more corporate-friendly approach to gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: I've found out about this game from a twitter screenshot about the protagonist being in an exact color scheme of Lois Griffin.Very chill platformer with simple low poly art style and -to my taste- a bit odd soundtrack choice.it may feel a bit grindy from time to time, but it didn't really annoy me that much.The plot is simple, characters are well written most of the time, I really liked Reinetos folk.There are some minor bugs (mostly with sound) and somewhat questionable mechanics (e.g. restart of the ride if you decided to take a shortcut over a dune), but they are not deal breakers.I would say that strong sides of this game are scenery, van riding and world exploration.It's fairly good, give it a try if you want to play some casual platformer
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely art style, it was super chill just driving around collecting stuff and using the different gadgets you get.I encountered a few bugs which were mostly getting the player/van stuck in the environment. I don't remember getting anything that couldn't be fixed by using the 'return to van/garage' options though, so it didn't really bother me.Definitely recommend checking this out, was a pretty enjoyable experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: Caravan SandWitch is an extremely charming little game, with some gorgeous art and a world that I loved exploring. It's so lovely to have an indie open world game that really encourages exploration and discovery on your own terms in an order that suits you (once you're out of the tutorial zone). It has some really simple but smart game design that meant that when returning to areas you've been before there's always something new to find using the metroidvania traversal unlock system. The world is really fascinating as well, strangely it reminds me most of the post-industrial landscapes of the Borderlands series, but obviously far more relaxing. A very enjoyable and tight experience that doesn't outstay its welcome. My only caveat is to go in with the right mindset: there's basically no challenge to the gameplay, so if you're looking for something more than a relaxing drive in a pretty environment this is unlikely to be for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: Such a wonderful game. The environment and music are lovely. While some may take the lack of "challenge" as a negative, I think it greatly added to the game. It allowed the devs to focus on puzzles and story building. That said, I personally feel the ending could have been paced better. Highly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Caravan SandWitch is so lovely. Whenever I thought I had seen everything and could tell where the game was going, I was wrong. _childDocuments_.review: Very enjoyable little exploration game with a focus on driving your van and exploring not just the enviroment/worldbuilding detailing how it became like this, but also the different characters and their stories.Gameplay is mostly scavenging for parts to upgrade your van, doing quests for npc's and uncovering the mysteries behind your sisters disappearance and what happened on the planet Cigalo 6 years ago. It's very casual and easy to sit down with, but with a lot of hidden depth and thoughtful commentary about corporations exploiting the enviroment and the way that can effect different niche cultures. Some small gripes i had with the game: - Some weird audio issues where all the ambient sounds and effects would cut out so i only had music and dialogue?- A bit to railroaded at times like for example it teleporting you all the way back to the beginning if you don't follow the line exactly in the "drive a character to specific location" parts of the game.- No way to customize you or your van which feels like a wasted opportunity to me personally. Like i just really want to be able to change the color of my bag and put on different outfits, and spray paint my van with fun colors and patterns ヽ(ﾟДﾟ)ﾉLastly a very big wasted opportunity is there isn't any tracks on the van's radio you can shift through since you will be spending a lot of time in there driving around. Why have random radios in the middle of nowhere have all the music instead of the van? I'm gonna leave that place after like 10 sec.  Sad it's not longer but that's the curse of enjoying things i just want more. Definitely recommend you try this if you like these types of games o(*>ω<*)o
_childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: 100% the game. Was fantastic from start to finish. The love and hard work that was poured into the game is very visible. _childDocuments_.name: Caravan SandWitch

_childDocuments_.review: I love everything about this game! It is relaxing yet engaging. I love the exploration element with platforming and puzzles. _childDocuments_.review: Enjoying this a lot, love a game where you talk to people and drive around doing tasks for them. Reminds me of 'Lake' in that regard, which I really liked. There's more 'game' here, with nice puzzles and platforming. Movement feels nice and there's a good sense of progression with upgrades and unlocks. Really dig the visual style - the game looks stunning and stylized, and nails the feel of an abandoned and decaying world. But it isn't all gloom, you get the hopefulness of the people making the best of a bad situation. The sound and music adds to the feel, and the menus have great blip sounds. The characters are varied, and I've enjoyed learning more about them as the game unfolds. They feel realized, and being dropped into the middle and piecing all the different relationships and histories together has been engaging. Plus there are frog guys, big plus there.Was impressed by the quality of life features. Always having the option to return to the van or return to the garage is really nice, and I was pleasantly surprised when I got stuck and the game detected it and offered a recall. Marking which quests are time-limited is appreciated, and you get a warning if you might lock yourself out of any. There are a couple of fiddly things, but nothing that's detracted from the experience too much. The biggest negative I've noticed is not being able to track a quest when you get a new message and open it - you have to go to a different message and back before it will work.

_childDocuments_.review: A great and relaxing game to play on the couch in an afternoon or over a weekend. The environment is beautiful and the music as well as artstyle only serve to complement it. For me I felt the overall narrative felt a bit on the weaker side, but the character dialogue and interactions were definitely charming.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, this is a game worth playing. While I'm normally pretty lukewarm on walking/driving simulators, the art and music were enough to lure me in, then the world and characters developed in a way that kept me playing to the end.Pros:-beautiful art-soothing, smooth music-interesting world-collect-athon (that's my jam, finished with 383 excess components)-well-developed characters who start out feeling shallow and are later fleshed out with optional missionsCons:-stiff platforming-some bizarre reactions from your vehicle when it hits angular terrain-awkward translations at certain points in the story, sometimes with characters saying things that feel like they're from an earlier version of the script-a few vague questlines that have you meandering across the wasteland figuring out where to go nextThe game could definitely use a few minor tweaks, like having the run/speed button be a toggle rather than a hold function (my arthritic hands need accessibility too!), maybe check marks next to the ruins when you clean out the last collectible, and it's probably a good idea to remove those hatches on the ground in certain areas that never actually come into play. They show up on my radar, but they don't do anything or have labels, so that's odd.If you notice I don't really touch on the LGBTQ+ aspects of the game, that's because they don't really bear mentioning. The sexuality of queer folk and their relationships is all very low-key and inoffensive to anyone but the most rabid troll, and their identities or orientations aren't what the story is about. They're people with struggles and goals, most of whom happen to be queer, which is pretty much the best way to handle it. There are lots of queer folk, there are some heteronormative folk, and they all manage to coexist in peace without worrying who's attracted to whom.Which, maybe, is the most sci-fi aspect of the game in the end. Ba-dum tish.Overall, it's an 8 hour game to get 100% completion. Some people are saying 12 hours, but I did plenty of meandering and still clocked in at 7.6 hours. Two endings, and as much inclusivity and diversity as you can shake a pride flag at. Finally, the developer handled their game being pirated almost immediately with both grace and humour, which I can respect.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for an Open World RPG that's going to feel fresh even 6 hours in due to having a fantastic van upgrade system, then this is one we can definitely recommend. You'll start off annoyed that you can't reach the tippy top of the ruin systems with pully ropes and power circuits just out of reach, but as you progress, the world is your oyster and if you want to spend a lifetime sitting and admiring the gorgeous views from the cliffside, you can do that. Plenty of side quests that feel entirely relevant to the world and story, and some fun easter egg collectibles to pick up along your journey as well. I particularly enjoyed the hardcore parkour we could do, not only as Sauge, but in our van too. Don't worry, there's a built-in reset system should you find yourself upside down in a ditch (literally), and you'll have a good laugh waiting for the short time it takes to pop up. Our only complaints were with a quest towards the end of the game not doing a great job of guiding you to where you needed to be, which felt odd given how fantastic the game had been about every other quest except this one, and occasionally you might find yourself staring at a rock wall face due to camera clipping when driving up a steep cliff, or talking to an NPC at a weird angle. I also wish there was more context to the end of the story, but great possibility for DLC or a future game, so maybe that was planned <3Our Honest Thoughts:

In Caravan SandWitch, embark on a journey across a Sci-Fi Provence-like world, driven by a mystery through your missing sister that unfolds with each step you take.

Interact with the communities on Cigalo, help them with their tasks and meet new people along the way. Take your time to explore the world, whether in your van or on foot.

name: Trolley Problem, Inc.
detailed_description: There is a runaway trolley careering down the railway tracks. On the tracks are five people unable to move. You are next to a lever. If you pull this lever the trolley will switch to a different set of tracks. However, you notice that there is a person on the other track. Watch the situation play out and five people die. Choose to pull the lever and only one person gets killed - but by you. What will you do? And that’s just for starters. Trolley Problem, Inc. is a darkly comedic narrative game based on real world philosophical papers, in which you are asked to make a series of impossible choices from two awful answers. Wrestle with your moral compass, decide the fate of millions – and then see how your choices compare to the rest of the world. * A tightly-wound, two-hour narrative experience. * Questions are based on genuine philosophical papers, complete with references. * It’s you vs The Narrator as every decision you make is challenged. * Compare your choices with other players. * Full Twitch integration - let your audience help guide your decisions Trolley Problem, Inc. is a brilliant, challenging, uncomfortable, comedic game from Samuel Read-Graves, the executive producer of Gang Beasts. What will you do?

_childDocuments_.review: I thought this game would be fun and seemed like it would have multiple routes, but your choices actually dont matter at all. _childDocuments_.review: Some people disliked the game for not having your choices provide any meaningful impact, that doesn't seem to be a fair assessment because this game presents itself not as such a game where your choices define your ending. Rather, the game's purpose seems to be to provide a list of different philosophical/psychological scenarios with immediate pressure to choose the 'correct' option, then step back and analyze your actions. Then compare and contrast the hows and whys behind your answer as an exercise in philosophical thinking and to possibly provide some introspective into some ways you may not have been aware that you were thinking...This game fails in that too, It attempts to string together a narrative into these scenarios resulting in you losing the suspension of disbelief needed for the trolley question to be effective in the first place (It's rather hard to take my position as "President" seriously when I just escaped from an AI controlled, robot terrorist organization after getting drafted from a failing company) resulting in the later questions not being answered in any meaningful way because the player's thinking and response becoming "Well there's no way in hell this could be happening or it seems just silly, so whatever"This also meshes terribly with the Narrator's constant berating of the player, their choices begin to seem pointless because there's no benefit or good reasoning for either choice because the narrator will elaborate just how unreasonable the player is being before and after each question. If this was done for the purposes of introspective, it fails as it leads to most players feeling frustration rather than any thinking, because the narrator only ever acknowledges the downsides in ways that are communicated at surface level reasons (Example: The first trolley problem never calls into question the fact that, by pulling the lever you are actively killing someone and the ramifications that may or may not hold in one's mind, rather the narrator just says "Oh my god you killed someone(some people), try to not do that mkay?" which fails to elaborate on the details of this example before jetting off to "what if the one person was a child").Due to the constant berating by the narrator for situations that get incredibly unbelievable within seconds, most players don't engage in any levels of thinking the game seemed to want to cultivate, rather most players just begin to express frustration at what appears to be a 2 hour slideshow saying "You're wrong" that costed them $10. Overall, this game seems to be a *really good* concept, but requires a decent sum of rewriting so that it is delivered in such a manner where it does what it intended to do. Currently it just makes a fair number of players frustrated and feeling like they wasted their money. Thus the Mixed Review score it possesses at the time of writing this review.

_childDocuments_.review: I think this is a game that had far greater potential than it actually realised, but it's still enjoyable and reasonably thought-provoking. I see that some people feel it would be improve if choices had meaning, but I disagree. I think the value of the moral hypotheticals is diminished if you 'game-ify' them too much. But I do think it would be improved by a deeper analysis of your choices as you play - evaluating what moral philosophy your choices align to, whether you're consistently adhering to that philosophy, giving you an opportunity to explain your choices (and why they might be inconsistent), and so on.But still, despite having potential to be far greater - in my opinion at least - the writing, voice acting, and music are well done and make the game a worthwhile, if short, experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Trolley Problem, Inc.

_childDocuments_.review: Warning: I highly recommend reading reviews before buying this game. While I did enjoy it, I think I only did because I read reviews. It helped me get a better understanding of what to expect (and I don't mean spoilers)- There is no right answer and this game will "shame" you for whichever one you choose. Imagine a little devil's advocate making little quips each time. So don't take the comments too seriously. They do later make the point that sometime both choices are bad and there's no good way out.This game definitely make you think. There's a scene where someone  in response to that, you have the choice to either  I remember feeling "I avoided doing further harm and got punished for it", but hey, real people probably felt that exact feeling when they were being shunned. People complained that it dragged on, but I liked the range of questions that covered different topics and different comparisons. I just wish they had some type of possible "contradiction list" at the end where they show you when it looked like you held a certain stance (eg: never pull lever/push someone, but did so if it was to save someone important, etc) so we can get a better sense of when our internal rules show inconsistencies. Suggestions for improvement: Maybe at the end of the game, you can go through a list of questions and filter them by "type" and see your answers? (eg: a question filter called "saving the majority" where it shows if you were consistently or inconsistently choosing the option that saved more people, or "level of involvement" whether you consistently or not stay "hands-off" and let nature run its course. or even "legality" about whether you always made legal decisions or not). I felt the game simply ended, when there could've been an interesting analysis portion to it, aside from comparing scores worldwide and with dev.Also how do we know if worldwide scores are sincere? People may be trying to see different outcomes/responses or going for the funny answer if they're a streamer. I think having a "are your answers going to be sincere?" question at the beginning of the game (with some text explaining that a "yes" or "no" doesn't affect the game, but that it's so the game knows which series of answers to add to the "worldwide score".
