_childDocuments_.review: Edit: I have heard there are actually 4 full movies in the game, but i am kind of confused by "human tv" I decided to try to watch the movies with gene on the couch this time, and i had a possible bug where after going to commercial break, the screen just went black. I've heard this may be due to that i was not sitting on the couch as i crouched closer to the tv, or possibly that i may need progress further to watch the whole thing, but i can not confirm as the movie starts from the beginning each time i come back. If i have one real complaint about this game so far, it is this, as there is an achievement for watching a specific commercial that i believe only comes on the house tv, as well as an Elvira type parody that i would like to fully watch, but you cant control the tv in the house, so it is somewhat frustrating. Overall i do love this game though. Most of the people saying it's too short and doesn't have enough content probably just rushed through every mission without exploring the world. There are collectibles and also achievements, and it is sort of like Trover saves the universe, in that, if you want to experience it fully, you need to take it slow, listen to dialogue play out, talk to characters multiple times, watch all the parody commercials. There are even 3 full feature length movies in the game, and Demon Wind in the movie theater was hilarious because there are 3 guys in the front row talking through the entire movie about the movie, and actually made it more entertaining than just watching the movie alone. I have not watched the other 2 movies on the couch with gene just cause he doesn't comment on them as far as i can tell. The combat is ok for having sentient guns with faces, the graphics are actually beautiful, the plot is interesting, but the commentary is one of the best parts of this game, why rush through all of it? I've seen people with like 7 hours of playtime saying that the game is too short. I as of writing this review have 14.6 hours of playtime and have not even beaten the game yet, so i fully recommend that if you're a fan of Justin Roiland's humor, that you take the time to actually slow down your playthrough and listen to it instead of bypassing it and then complaining that it's too short. You'll miss many funny parts if you just run from mission to mission firing your gun constantly, relax a little and explore the Rick and Morty interdimensional cable type world they created. I may add more to this review once i finish the game, but i bought this full price to show support to squanch games and Justin Roiland, and i don't regret that decision at all so far.
_childDocuments_.name: High On Life

_childDocuments_.review: Ok so they made a hit, AGAIN. Aside from some occasional glitching, probably due to the files, it’s the funniest Rick and morty ish ♥♥♥♥ I’ve played since their last game.Favorite part, is the movie theater. The call back to the best Sci Fi  show that was made. I sat in game to watch the entire movie, and to listen to the commentary. This is classic comedy.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is VERY fun, especially if you enjoy childish/immature sense of humour things. However it is filled with bugs that require you to google solutions to the problems of, MOST of which are reloading a checkpoint/restarting the entire game to solve, including losing -all- of your guns farmed upgrades, which, you might miss and therefore end up playing the game for quite a while without noticing you just lost a 3rd of all of your bullets in all of your guns.. This is somewhat of a big freaking deal, and while the game lends itself quite easily to playing for a 100% run, problems like these can quickly ruin the entire thing for you.Unless you like the satire/humour of rick & morty, like bright flashy colours, and can withstand being presented with game-breaking bugs you have to forcibly reload the game yourself to solve, Don't buy this game. Somebody badly needs to patch this thing.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was not well designed, the only reason I spent quite a bit of time on the game was becausethe game mechanics had no sprint and the objective locator in game was not functioning properlyand would reset to previous objectives, causing me to become lost and waste time looking for my original objective.Another issue with the game was the NPC interaction, the dialog was good but the gamewould have the some obnoxious characters constantly talk to you to a point where youcan not enjoy the game because the voices were constantly pestering you with randomvoice lines that made no sense and had no relation to the main story.I really looked forward to this game because I'm a big rick and morty fan but this game was a let down and coulduse more bug fixes and removal of certain NPC interactions. This game was not worth $60.
_childDocuments_.name: High On Life

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: If it's on sale, go for it. It's funny, but the gameplay is mediocre. Not worth the full price.I'm going to be honest here. The gameplay itself isn't particularly fun. It's a mediocre shooter where you fight the same handful of enemies over and over. I suppose you could say that about most FPS games, but in this one it really stands out. Even on the hardest difficulty the game isn't remotely hard. I didn't even bother buying all the upgrades as they just aren't needed. The game drags on and in the end I had to force myself to finish the game.The comedy style is basically Rick and Morty (as one would expect). A lot of fourth wall breaking, improvising, and voice actors laughing at their own lines occasionally. I really enjoyed the humour and it's definitely the best part of the game. However, if the Rick and Morty style of humour isn't for you you'll likely not get much out of this game. And I can't justify paying full price for it on the comedy alone.It's not worth full price (£46.49 as of writing). £20, maybe. Wait for a sale. It'll be interesting to see what happens with this game, if anything, with whats happening with Justin Roiland.
_childDocuments_.name: High On Life

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyed a lot the game, a bit short in my opinion but the humor, as well as landscapes made up for it. i loved the interactions between the character, funny choices of dialogues. Thought, the learning curve is quite weird, it felt really easy for the first three bosses. But the one following one was a nightmare to beat and then it went back to easy mode. Especially the final boss, probably easy because of lezduit but still, could have been more interesting. Overall i'm glad that i bought it, even with those flaws it was a good experience. side note; if you enjoyed the game, i recommend journey to the savage planet which is pretty similar.

_childDocuments_.review: a refreshing way to experience TOBACCO's Skids and Angels album as some layers/synths either are removed, combined or even mastered exquisitely different while maneuvering a vivid universe with excellent movement and decent gun play with their own quirks and a Metroidvania approach as some optional content for the 100% can be accessed from unlocks later on. Having heard Joel Haver only added more to the charm despite the jokes ranging from hits to misses. Albeit the raw story without spending more time looking for everything to 100% the areas/game is a little short for the price (waiting for a sale is the best option if you still want to give it a shot). Regardless of that you most likely find something enjoyable, or not; I don't know your sense of humor and neither will I judge. If the enemies or your own weapons start to bother you with dialogue, try the audio settings as both can be reduced and/or turned off entirely.For people still wondering what the trailer tracks are, Gods in Heat from Sweatbox Dynasty (2016) and Lamborghini Meltdown from Exorcise Tape (2013 / DEMON QUEEN).

_childDocuments_.review: Fun, a little buggy, more or less exactly what you would expect from this game.Lots of neat mechanics, with a nice easy learning curve introducing one or two at a time - in essence, it's a 3D shooter / platformer.The designers put a tremendous amount of work into dialogue, including tons of background stuff playing on TVs in the primary city (as well as licensing a few entire movies to play in-game). There are numerous lines of dialogue that are only triggered under specific circumstances.The inability to make multiple saves removes a vital failsafe, as the game has no "get me unstuck" feature; I nearly lost all my progress by getting stuck, and after nearly ten minutes of wiggling around and using every possible combination of movement available, I finally freed myself. Level design is very good, aside from an overreliance on invisible walls. Oddly, in a few places they used universe-appropriate textured translucent forcefields - in most places, they were immersion-breaking design elements.For all the depth of dialogue, the breadth of the game is somewhat less than I would have liked. I hope they add more content in the future, even in the form of paid DLC. Nothing in this game appears to have been procedurally generated - it seems to have been entirely handcrafted, and a tremendous amount of labor must have gone into it.For what amounts to a comedy game, the basic mechanics are very strong - it has better shooting mechanics than some of the early Fallout games, and the platforming and general in-game movement and physics are very good. My only kvetch regarding the shooting mechanics is a total lack of any sort of sniper-class Gatlian.The most annoying bug I encountered was that near the end of the game, just before the second-to-last boss, all of my magazine capacity improvements simply disappeared.Overall, I strongly recommend it. If you're fond of Justin Roiland's style of comedy, you'll enjoy High On Life.
_childDocuments_.name: High On Life

_childDocuments_.review: High on Life is a refreshing take on the shooter genre, which has been stale for a while now. Going into it, i knew the game would be funny, as it was created by Justin Roiland (Rick and Morty), but did not imagine me having as much fun as i did. The game kept bringing me back with the interesting gun play, exploration and extremely funny dialogue. The game is stunning to look at and runs really good, better than most of the triple A games I've played recently, there was some serious love put into this game and am looking forward to future projects from this studio. 100% would recommend to anyone that wants a goofy game, with very polished fun gun play and fluid movement systems.

_childDocuments_.review: Like others said, it's way too short for $60. If you were interested because of all the videos on youtube and facebook, sad to say, you've probably already seen the best the game has to offer. The devs like the number three; three mods for each gun, three (real) levels to explore, three locations in two of the levels, three bosses in one boss, three phases/attacks to most bosses, three textures fighting over the same surface at the same time...Bugs everywhere, and not the kind you shoot at. Easy to get stuck outside the map as there's many unfinished and glitched areas, and no real way to revert your save to a previous checkpoint (as the "previous checkpoint" when free exploring is the last place you touched the ground), meaning if you get stuck, you'll probably have to start *the whole game over again* which is really bogus. For a game that encourages going out of the way to explore and find lugloxes, it's obvious the devs don't *actually* want you to explore, as there are invisible walls everywhere. They want you to have the illusion of exploration while still staying on their designed path.Sometimes your ability to ads (right click/left trigger on gamepad) is just completely taken away and you have to reload to fix it. You'll randomly lose the ability to knife sometimes, and the only way to fix is to reload from checkpoints. Enemies and especially bosses fall through the map and make it impossible to finish the level without reloading. Enemies are dumb, like really dumb, even on the hardest difficulty. Not enough upgrades and what's there doesn't make much of a noticeable difference as everything is basically an incremental 10% upgrade (+10 heath, +10% ammo cap, -10% reload time, -10% special reload time +10% jetpack height, etc) save for the gun mods, and there's only three of those per gun. I didn't find myself switching up my tactics or my loadout much at all the entire game, in fact I rarely used any gun other than the 1st one you get unless i needed their trick shot, the others are just...not good. The shotgun works better at shredding off chunks of armor than it does at doing the type of damage and knockback youd expect from a shotgun, needler knockoff's mods are underwhelming and don't work the way you'd expect from the description, the grenade launcher is underpowered until fully upgraded, then it's overpowered, and knifey, arguably one of the funnier characters and premises, is completely under-utilized as a character and his only upgrade doesn't seem to actually do anything. There are many areas that serve no purpose but to return to once you have the proper equipment, and the payoff is usually lackluster (100 pesos, 200 pesos or a card, or 300 pesos or a mod or card) and is not randomized, meaning the same mod/card will always be in the same luglox. The cards don't matter, another useless collectible, they could have been useful by providing stat buffs or something but nope, even finishing sets gives you nothing, and as of this update, even getting every single one does not guarantee an achievement as the achievement tracking is bugged. A lot of half-baked ideas went into the game, and it shows even from the Bounty 5000's broken tab; they introduce a mechanic only for it to have little to no relevance to the rest of the game. Sure, you can save the humans you find, but there's no real incentive to do so; no bonuses or perks, no reward whatsoever besides some mildly entertaining banter if you go talk to them in the human habitat, so I didn't bother. Sure, you can collect the trading cards, but besides the 100% completion achievement there's no point. Sure, you could use the shotguns special to get up there, but after one or two jetpack upgrades you don't need it anymore, basically at all. Sure, you can buy special warp discs, but there's only like 5 or 6 and they are one-time use easter eggs, so again, save for two of them that give you a reward, no reason to buy the others on another playthrough. Finally, a lot of the dialogue (arguably the focal point of the game) is easily missed or skipped. The characters often talk over one another, enemies will talk over one another, and location-based dialogue can be cut short by moving too fast and bumping into another trigger/moving into another zone. Proximity based events are usually one-off, so if you move too fast, you'll miss it and won't get it again unless you start a new save. It's obvious that this is a studio's first slug at a game, because it doesn't seem to want to *be* a game; the funniest comments and moments happen when you *stop* playing the game and either idle long enough for your gun to talk or for the scene to play out. A few moments like this in particular come to mind, first with knifey and then later on once you get creature, where if you're playing this like a typical run n gun shooter, you'll miss most of the humorous bits in the game. Is it worth playing? IF you like rick and morty style humor, then yes absolutely. Even worth a try if you're not sure. Is it worth *paying*? As it is right now, with all the bugs and lack of content (the devs even joked about adding DLC in-game through one of Kenny's dialogues), I can't say that it is. Wait until it goes on sale for $30 or preferably $15, its not worth full price as is. Unless they add a lot of free content and fix a bunch of bugs and patch a lot of literal holes in their game later on (which I don't see them doing minus the bughunt), it's not worth $60.

_childDocuments_.review: Big open areas full of pretty basic lock & key metroidvania treasure hunting, but the great dialogue elevates the experience. It feels good to zip around and explore, especially after getting the jetpack. I feel like I'm about 40% through at my current playtime of 8.2 hours with 3 bounties done, although I've been going through very casually and really exploring the maps.Definitely could've used a big polish pass - I casually fell through level geometry a few times just looking for more treasure chests, and the state tracking has some issues where I think the game was trying to display two different stages of a scene at the same time (the highway warp in the paradise zone). The motion blur combined with low fov also made for a mildly nauseating experience before I turned off the former (truly no excuse for missing a fov slider in a modern pc game).All that said, the game is full of great humor and breaks my expectations a lot. It's obvious that Justin Roiland & the team at Squanch play games and know when to lean into tropes to make understanding what's going on easy, but also exactly how to surprise us. For all the million gripes you could give, there's enough here that's really interesting and funny to forgive everything else.[Post completion notes:]"100%" completion took about 20 hours, which is great for a game that's very heavily reliant on its writing. 1hr 36mins of that was spent watching Demon Wind. I had a good time screwing around hunting for missing treasure chests, although I really wish there were a few more tools that helped track them down.Frustratingly, either the game's achievements for treasures are broken or the in-game location selector doesn't tell you about all the chests. I got all the ones that were tracked but apparently there's something like 30 left, but since I have no idea where to even start looking I'm invoking my ancestors' warcry of "♥♥♥♥ that". You also don't actually get the listed 10k bounty for the final boss, which is super ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ annoying since without any more treasure I can't clear the shops and try out the last few gun mods I hadn't gotten. This is some annoying ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.I stand by my pre-completion point that there's more than enough great comedy to enthusiastically recommend the game, but I do hope these issues get ironed out.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright Morty, strap in, 'cause we're diving into "High on Life," a game that’s like if Rick Sanchez himself decided to create a psychedelic shooter in a lab filled with sentient, talking guns. First off, let's talk about the humor – it's got that classic, in-your-face, irreverent style you'd expect from the creators of "Rick and Morty." It’s like they took every weird, inappropriate thought and crammed it into this game. So if you're into that, you're in for a wild ride.Graphically, it’s a trip, Morty! The visuals are like a kaleidoscope of vibrant colors and bizarre alien worlds. It looks so good you might even forget you’re playing a game and not just hallucinating on some interdimensional cable.Now, for the bad news. Bugs. And no, not the fun, squishy kind you’d expect to blast with your talking guns. I’m talking about the kind of bugs that make you want to throw your controller into the next dimension. There’s nothing quite like getting sucked into a game-breaking glitch just when you’re about to save the universe. It’s the kind of frustration that’d make even Jerry lose his cool.But hey, here’s a silver lining: the game runs surprisingly smooth on the Steam Deck. So if you're looking for a portable trip through this chaotic universe, you're covered. And here’s the real kicker, Morty: you can snag this wacky, glitchy adventure for dirt cheap on Humble Bundle Choice right now. It’s like getting a Plumbus for the price of a butter robot!So, if you’re up for some insane, bug-ridden fun, and you’ve got a twisted sense of humor, "High on Life" is worth the ride. Just, y'know, keep a portal gun handy for when you get stuck.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid game, a bit overrated in my opinion.Pros:Lots of great comedy.The combat is top notch really fun.Story is basic but nothing horrible which is all you need for a game like this.Cons:8 hour campaign which is kinda the minimum required for a FPS. Which wouldn't be a big deal if it was all great gameplay. But there are a considerable amount of scenes that drag on with no way to skip or speed up. Like the detective mode parts, or Lizzie and Gene arguing. Or other unsinkable dialogue scenes. Not sure how much these drag out but all together I would estimate around 30-45 mins which is a lot of downtime in a 8 hour campaign. Some of the gaming meta jokes kinda get old after a while.The last boss fight was was very anti-climatic. Honestly one of the worst boss fights because Lezduit makes it insanely easy. In general the boss fights seem to go down in quality with each one. 9-Torg was very interesting with a lot of environment hazards as well as different attacks forcing you to keep moving and using Knifey to stay airborne. Then one of them dies before the fight so you just deal with waves generic enemies for some jokes.Bugs: Softlocked the game at least 3 times, not even doing anything special each time just moving around during dialogue scenes in the house. Reloading last checkpoint fixed them all but still kinda annoying but rather minor.The ending:Overall for the shooting mechanics, good comedy and some fun platform elements the game is a worthy pickup. I wouldn't pay $40 for it however, I picked it up a key for around $13, but otherwise I think $30 or less is worth the grab.

_childDocuments_.review: The sophomore title from Squanch games is a hit in both humour and gameplay. The game's story revolves around aliens that have found humans to be a fantastical new drug. An interstellar gang called the G3, invades Earth and rounds up humanity to serve as major bong hits for high-end clientele. You and your sister get caught in the middle of all of this as you encounter a different alien, a gatlian named Kenny, who helps you escape. From here, you and Kenny quickly turn to a vengeful life of G3 bounty hunting. As with their seminal title, Trover Saves the Universe, the enjoyment of Squanch games latest outing will depend a lot on how much you enjoy the comedy stylings of Justin Roiland's other works (Rick and Morty, Solar Opposites, Koala Man). As a fan of this style, I really enjoyed my time with the game. Each gatlian has their own personality and will say witty quips and offer observations on the environment. The verbosity of your arsenal can be controlled in the options menu, in the event that you find their interruptions to be too much. As with Trover, I found myself just standing around for long periods of time just listening to the (often improvised) dialogue happening in the world around you. This is taken to the extreme when watching interstellar television (equivalent to an episode of Interdimensional Cable from Rick and Morty), or when attending the MST3K-style movie theatre, which plays three different B-movies at their full length. Humour aside, the actual gameplay in this title is a vast improvement over Trover. Part of this comes from eschewing the limitations of Virtual Reality, and using a more comfortable first person shooter format. The developers did a great job of balancing the power and limitations of each gatlian. Your character is given great traversal options, and each of the three main worlds is peppered with collectibles, characters, and other interesting things to do. Boss fights are pretty straightforward, but many do rely / encourage you to swap gatlians throughout the fight, adding a nice puzzle-solving aspect to these battles. As an Indie title, there are still some rough points in the game that I would like to see the developer fix in their next outing. As with Trover, High on Life has many moments in the game where a character's dialogue will abruptly cut off in a conversation. These moments make it sound like someone is reading a telegram instead of having a natural conversation. Similarly, there are dialogue triggers that occur when fighting some enemies, and will happen regardless of whether those enemies are still alive. It can throw you for a loop when a ghost starts just talking as you walk along. The game has some mixed messaging with the inventory system. You can pick up a lot of random things, but some of these random things can be used for achievements, or to give to other characters. Thankfully, your inventory is limitless, but it would still have bee nice to have key items separated from random bits. There are also "forum posts" in the game that you can read, They double as achievement goals. Unfortunately, aside from one thread, these posts are really only meant to be read for the humour. Most don't offer any hints on where to look for some of these achievements. Overall, I found this game to be a blast to play, watch, and listen to. I recommend picking it up at full price or on sale. You will get a decent play time and an entertaining experience. Lastly, there is an unexpected bonus for Farscape fans. Both Gigi Edgley (Chiana) and Wayne Pygrim (Scorpius) play characters in High on Life. Pygrim in particular is worth seeking out as his character (Dr. Gurgula) even feels like a version of Scorpius. I'm not sure why Squanch games has this relationship with Australian actors, but I'm glad that they do.

_childDocuments_.review: High On Life : By Triple F"High on Life", developed by Squanch Games and released in late 2022, is a first-person shooter that combines vibrant, sci-fi action with a heavy dose of absurd humor. The brainchild of Justin Roiland, co-creator of Rick and Morty, the game presents a chaotic and comedic romp through an alien-infested universe. Known for its irreverent humor, talking guns, and unpredictable storytelling, "High on Life" delivers a distinctive experience that sets it apart from more traditional FPS titles, though it does come with some noticeable flaws.At its core, "High on Life" throws players into the role of an ordinary human who is thrust into an extraordinary situation: the Earth has been invaded by an alien cartel called the G3, who seeks to harvest humans as drugs. The protagonist, armed with sentient talking guns (called Gatlians), must navigate a series of hostile alien worlds to take down the cartel’s leaders and save humanity. The game's premise is refreshingly original, merging dark themes of drug trafficking with the absurdity of the living weapons constantly chatting, offering commentary, and breaking the fourth wall. This bizarre setup establishes the foundation for High on Life’s irreverent tone and comedic narrative.The humor in "High on Life" is very much in line with Justin Roiland’s style, with its combination of surreal scenarios, rapid-fire dialogue, and crude jokes. Each of the Gatlians has a distinct personality, with their dialogue providing constant banter throughout the game. From Kenny, the default pistol voiced by Roiland, who has a nervous but enthusiastic personality, to the more aggressive and sarcastic creatures like Knifey, the homicidal knife, the game ensures that there’s always a layer of humor accompanying the action. While the humor can be hit-or-miss depending on personal tastes, it undeniably provides a unique flavor that gives the game personality. Fans of Roiland’s previous work will find this tone familiar and engaging, though those who aren’t fans of his comedic style may find the constant jokes grating over time.From a gameplay perspective, "High on Life" offers standard FPS mechanics with a few twists. Players traverse colorful, often bizarre alien environments while engaging in firefights with a variety of enemies. The talking weapons aren’t just for laughs—they each offer distinct abilities and play-styles, which help diversify the combat experience. Kenny, for example, functions as a basic blaster with the ability to shoot glob shots, while other Gatlians provide more specialized abilities, like time-bending or crowd control mechanics. These weapon abilities also tie into exploration, as they can be used to solve environmental puzzles or access new areas. This synergy between combat and exploration keeps gameplay fresh, though it’s not as deep or polished as some of its genre peers.The game’s world-building and art design are definite highlights. The alien worlds players explore are filled with vibrant colors, bizarre flora and fauna, and absurdly detailed environments that feel like they’ve been pulled straight from an animated sci-fi comedy. Each location is brimming with strange characters and quirky side missions, making the universe feel lived-in and distinct. While the game doesn’t offer the sprawling open-world design of modern FPS titles, the levels are large enough to allow for some exploration, with hidden chests and collectibles scattered throughout. These encourage players to engage with the world beyond the main questline, though the exploration can feel somewhat shallow as the game lacks meaningful rewards for thorough exploration.On the downside, "High on Life" does suffer from some technical and design issues that detract from the experience. Enemy variety is somewhat limited, and the combat, while fun, can feel repetitive over time. The AI of enemies isn’t particularly challenging, and combat often boils down to basic run-and-gun mechanics with occasional use of special abilities. Additionally, while the game’s humor is one of its defining features, it can sometimes be overbearing, with non-stop chatter from the weapons that doesn’t always land. Players may find the constant jokes and dialogue interruptions during action sequences to be distracting, especially when trying to focus on more intense combat moments.Another area where the game stumbles is in its pacing. "High on Life" struggles with balancing its fast-paced combat with its narrative and exploration elements. Some sections feel too drawn out, with lengthy dialogue-heavy moments that break the flow of the action. While the game is undoubtedly committed to its comedic storytelling, the pacing can feel uneven, particularly when players are eager to jump back into the action but are instead met with extended cutscenes or dialogue exchanges. The result is a game that sometimes feels like it’s unsure whether it wants to be an action-packed shooter or a comedy-driven adventure, leading to moments of tonal dissonance.In short, "High on Life" stands out as a bold and original entry in the FPS genre thanks to its offbeat humor, colorful world design, and innovative concept of talking weapons. While it has its share of flaws—ranging from repetitive combat to uneven pacing—the game’s unique tone and sense of humor make it a memorable experience for those who can appreciate its brand of comedy. It may not reach the heights of more mechanically polished shooters, but its charm lies in its unpredictability and willingness to embrace absurdity. For fans of Justin Roiland’s work, "High on Life" offers a chaotic and entertaining adventure through a bizarre, drug-fueled universe that’s unlike anything else in the FPS landscape.

_childDocuments_.review: High on life is a welcome surprise to vidya. Being the type of person that favors the gameplay and mechanics over story, I haven't liked many games lately for their "interactive-movie" nature and same old boring mechanics and settings.This game not only is a breath of fresh air regarding those aspects (to an oversupplied genre (shooters/FPS)), it also makes a case for its uniqueness in how guns are developed, with player interaction and fitting every part of the game in harmony. Movement is swift and somewhat fastpaced, although grab windows are strange and short. This helps maneuvering and exploring different worlds. Comedy is fitting and not over the top as I was expecting.Talking guns with backstory are not only a innovative mechanic, but also makes the story incredibly interesting - a first for me in games. Voice acting is superb, with huge dialog options with different lines, just don't expect much of an impact in your choices, just play as you like.Overall this game could be just a little longer, but that doesn't take any of its merits. Enjoy a fun ride.

_childDocuments_.review: Good game. Clean art style, looks nice. Plays well and runs well (5800X3D, 3080 12 GB) @ 3440x1440. I enjoyed the story and I enjoyed the pace. I think the game could use a little TLC in terms of bugs, there are many places soft locks exist, and some things are difficult to trigger. In most cases though, dying, or reloading can help. You'll always be able to back track in the game, so enjoy moving forward knowing you'll have plenty of chances to explore later on. Now, for what's amazing about this game is the voice acting. There's SO MUCH of it from so many talented people. It's decently written and then absurdly improved and riffed on from there. It's endless. I'm not sure i'd ever be able to see all the lines of dialogue this game has. Quite impressive. I know there's some concern over Justin's work after other events in his life, but Joel Haver is on fine display, and Squanch Games deserves kudos for their efforts despite the obvious attachment to Justin. Enjoy!

_childDocuments_.review: As a note, i've never watched an episode of Rick&Morty and couldn't care less about their creator's involvement in this game so that wasn't a selling point for me. So, is this "talking guns zany space-soapy-opera" any good? Yes, it is but your enjoyment of it will heavily depend on your brand of humor as on one side you have a fairly competent and enjoyable FPS while on the other you'll have non-stop absurd obscenities chatter, situations and scenarios with pretty much every step taken. I enjoyed it but beware, this ain't the type of easily digestible humor...quite the contrary, it's on the edge of annoying as profane stupidity veering into extreme absurdity are its main selling points and while there are genuine snippets of comedy gold sprinkled in it, they are usually stretched very close to tipping over their "it's hilarious" boiling point.  Leaving this aside, there's a lot of love and attention to detail put into crafting this game and it looks and plays great. So that's that - about 20h max on the hardest difficulty and hunting every secret.(PS: i wouldn't say "No" to some DLC expanding the training level as damn, that was hilarious as hell)

_childDocuments_.review: My name is Walter Hartwell White. I live at 308 Negra Arroyo Lane, Albuquerque, New Mexico, 87104. This is my confession. If you're watching this tape, I'm probably dead, murdered by my brother-in-law Hank Schrader. Hank has been building a Virtual Youtuber empire for over a year now and using me as his recruiter. Shortly after my 50th birthday, Hank came to me with a rather, shocking proposition. He asked that I use my Live2D knowledge to recruit talents, which he would then hire using his connections in the Japanese utaite world. Connections that he made through his career with Niconico. I was... astounded, I... I always thought that Hank was a very moral man and I was... thrown, confused, but I was also particularly vulnerable at the time, something he knew and took advantage of. I was reeling from a cancer diagnosis that was poised to bankrupt my family. Hank took me on a ride along, and showed me just how much money even a small indie channel could make. And I was weak. I didn't want my family to go into financial ruin so I agreed. Every day, I think back at that moment with regret. I quickly realized that I was in way over my head, and Hank had a partner, a man named Motoaki "Yagoo" Tanigo, a businessman. Hank essentially sold me into servitude to this man, and when I tried to quit, Yagoo threatened my family. I didn't know where to turn. Eventually, Hank and Yagoo had a falling out. From what I can gather, Hank was always pushing for a greater share of the business, to which Yagoo flatly refused to give him, and things escalated. Yagoo was able to arrange, uh I guess I guess you call it a "hit" on my brother-in-law, and failed, but Hank was seriously injured, and I wound up paying his medical bills which amounted to a little over $177,000. Upon recovery, Hank was bent on revenge, working with a man named Riku Tazumi , he plotted to kill Yagoo, and did so. In fact, the bomb that he used was built by me, and he gave me no option in it. I have often contemplated suicide, but I'm a coward. I wanted to go to the police, but I was frightened. Hank had risen in the ranks to become the head of the Cover Corp, and about that time, to keep me in line, he took my children from me. For 3 months he kept them. My wife, who up until that point, had no idea of my vtubing activities, was horrified to learn what I had done, why Hank had taken our children. We were scared. I was in Hell, I hated myself for what I had brought upon my family. Recently, I tried once again to quit, to end this nightmare, and in response, he gave me this. I can't take this anymore. I live in fear every day that Hank will kill me, or worse, hurt my family. I... All I could think to do was to make this video in hope that the world will finally see this man, for what he really is.

_childDocuments_.review: Before getting canceled by the twitter mob, Justin Roiland and the company that he started made two games including High on Life. If you watched Rick and Morty, you should know his comedy is absolutely stupid and random at times which makes it fantastic. High on Life is a hilarious game that features fun combat, good exploration, and an ok'ish story. 👍 +4 feature films can be watched in their entirety in the game+The humor is fantastic+Pretty well done level design👎-The main story is a bit lackluster towards the end-Weak soundtrackYou play as some random person who finds himself caught in an alien invasion. As you try to avoid being killed you find a talking gun that helps you defeat the alien invasion. You then get teleported to an alien world to find help in hopes of saving your planet. That is the gist of it. The comedic timing, the overall humor, the punchlines, and every single written dialogue in the game are bonkers and extremely funny. It's a type of humor that isn't exactly for everyone, but I appreciated it quite a lot. The main story won't blow your mind, it's a pretty casual sci-fi trope mixed with random comedy and the ending is pretty much boringly generic which kinda ruined the whole experience a bit. Comedy games, just like movies or shows can be a huge hit or miss, because not everyone can appreciate humor, especially nowadays when most people get offended. So if you're one of the latter, fk off and play something else. If you're a normal person with an open mind, this game will most likely make you laugh at the very least. Story rating: 8/10It's a first-person shooter, that heavily focuses on exploration more so than combat. The combat is pretty decent and gets more fun towards the end when you unlock all the guns and skills. It's not a very difficult game or mechanically advanced, as it takes inspiration from other games, but never truly does anything unique to separate itself from the crowd. The guns talking is the only thing that it has going for it, aside from the humor of course. Each gun has its own voice and each gun you find is mechanically different from one another. When you're not in combat, there are a lot of open-ended areas to explore and find upgrades for your weapons and whatnot. Not much else can be said about the gameplay, it's as simple as it can be, but still enjoyable for the most part. I only wish it had more difficult and varied encounters and far more/better boss fights. Gameplay rating: 7.5/10This is where things start to shine. A good comedy game must have good voice acting, and suffice it to say, High on Life excels at voice acting. There are a lot of hilarious voice actors, Justin included, that elevate the experience and I can't think of a single character, except maybe your sister, that didn't do a great job at making you laugh or smile. Sadly there's also a negative aspect in regards to audio design and that is the music. It's pretty weak in my opinion and at times it felt like just random sounds mashed together which was a huge shame considering it could've improved the simple combat a lot more. As for the sound effects, they're pretty good, unique at times, and specifically designed for comedy purposes. Audio rating: 8/10The game ran absolutely perfect, had no issues whatsoever, no bugs, no crashes, nothing, and more importantly stutter-free considering its engine. Visually the game looks pretty damn good at times, the neon lights, the cities, the whole sci-fi design, and especially the gun designs. The levels are really well done which was quite a surprise considering the type of game, there are a lot of areas to explore, secrets to find, and shortcuts to open, and if you know me, I love great level designs. Graphics, performance and tech analysis score: 8.5/10As I've said, if you're an open-minded person, High on Life will make you laugh and while its general gameplay isn't something to write home about, it's still decent enough to recommend. Fantastic humor carries the entire game. Recommended at any price, but also ♥♥♥♥ the devs for canceling Justin for no valid reasons.

_childDocuments_.review: If you love the humour behind the TV-series Rick & Morty, you'll love this game. It might not be sophisticated or have a lot of "variety" in enemies like some people claim, but it's just so much fun. Awesome voice acting, a lot of talking... I mean, its just absurdly funny. And some people might think it's all toilet humour, but its just so much worse lol. And you just got to love it. Definitely worth the money in my opinion and I only played like 2hours at this point. Even the commercials, and the tv-shows (even full length old B movies are there to find) are just plain fun to watch and listen to. There are some "bugs" that hopefully will be fixed, such as "being stuck in a map" and I had to glitch my way back to the exit lol. Or reloading checkpoints doesn't save the things you actived on the map, so you either are stuck again or you need to find a workaround. But so far, im having a blast, worth it in my opinion. _childDocuments_.review: After finishing High On Life, I can't help but want more. Whilst I enjoyed the story of the game a lot and found the combat fun and exciting, the game does feel a bit on the shorter side with roughly only 15-20 hours of content. I particularly like the soundtrack of the game, which I feel suits the Sci-Fi futuristic atmosphere very accurately. The game looks stunning as expected and played smoothly on my PC with only a few stutters when entering new busy areas. The 3 different difficulties of 'story mode, normal mode and hunter mode' offer a good balance of story and combat, with some of the later boss fights proving to be quite challenging. Apart from the lack of content that I mentioned earlier, I think High On Life is a good pick if you want to have a nice laugh and relax while playing a 'run-and-gun' shooter game. 6.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; The game is a buggy, overpriced, mess. DO NOT BUY THIS GAME UNLESS IT IS ON A VERY LARGE SALE!This game is occasionally funny, which seems to be it's main selling point. Unfortunately I can't recommend the game. As much as I want to, if you are looking for a GAME to play, this is not it for a few main reasons. Price, bugs, and game play.The bugs in the game are very frequent, to an inexcusable degree. In a large portion of the combat encounters that I have done, the enemy AI just breaks. Animations and voice lines replay for seemingly no reason. I could go on, and I haven't been paying that much attention to all the bugs, because they are so numerous. I can forgive most bugs, and even think some of them are funny, but in a game that relies heavily on it's jokes, hearing/seeing the same one on a loop, doesn't do it many favors. Think a comedian that repeated every 4th joke 4-5 times. You laugh at some of them, but even the funniest ones get old after the 3rd time they have been repeated. I haven't played a game this buggy since Cyberpunk 2077 at release.Moving away from the topic of bugs, the game play is honestly, not good. The game doesn't for lack of a better term "feel good" to play. If you are looking for a game that is fun as a player, move on. The game lacks the same energy as DOOM Eternal, and the story isn't good enough to warrant playing for that. In all honesty, the story feels like it was written merely as a way to get from one mediocre punch line from the next, and the choices of the player do not matter in the story as much as you would expect in a game with the only real selling point being the "story." IF you still want to see the story, watch a play through of it.As negative as I have been to the game, that has been with the knowledge that they are charging $60 for the game right now. If the game was $15-$20 that would be an entirely fair price. If you passed 4th grade math, you likely noticed that the fair price and the actual price are off by a multiple of 3. Needless to say, if you care about your money don't buy this game unless it goes on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Ah, what a delight! High On Life is overflowing with ridiculousness, self-awareness and heart. It achieves a uniquely obnoxious and outlandish tone that remains consistent from beginning to end. It is hard to think of a game that has enthralled me with its humour and made me chuckle as often as this one. My play-through was a gateway to unfiltered, ubiquitous and utterly refreshing fun. Four components of this game really worked for me: I found the movement satisfying, the gun-play familiar yet liberating, the boss fights engaging, and the characters endearing. It is short, lacks enemy variety, and can undoubtedly overstay its welcome for some - yet it is easy to recommend during a 50%+ sale. High On Life is simply a blast!
_childDocuments_.name: High On Life

_childDocuments_.review: A humorous, wacky departure from the generic linear FPS. High on Life is worth playing, especially when you consider the reasonable price-point.Pros:1) The comedy - I was a little sceptical about how I would enjoy the comedy, but it was great. As long as you have not problems with toilet humour, you are going to have an enjoyable experience.2) The visuals - This game may not be at the forefront of modern graphics, but the unique character and world design sets it apart. It is such a breath of fresh air to be in scifi game where you are the only human around for the most part.3) The gun concept - The sapient guns with different personalities is such a fun and unique idea that I have never seen get fleshed out to this extent before!Cons:1) The protagonist is completely mute. In a game where comedy is one of the primary attractions, a mute protagonist feels a bit lacking. I feel like we have missed out on potentially hilarious conversations between the Gatlings and the player.2) While weapon customisation exists, the Gatlings remain about the same to look at. It would have been great to see more advanced visual changes happen the more we upgraded our guns.3) It would have been cool if Lizzie had a bigger role in the game. She seems like a cool character, who would be ready co go on adventures too, but she just sits around in the house for the most part.

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, I refunded this game, but that's only because I found out it's on game pass after I bought it. Very fun game. It's not for all people, which is completely understandable, but for me it was a blast. The combat in the later stages of the game was especially fun and a lot more fast pace than the start. Being able to slide around, tether off of ledges and use the jet pack to get above your enemies, creates a fun shooter which can suit to all play styles. The colourfulness of the game is just amazing, with every location having their own style with the music to match. The dialogue from the enemies and guns is also great whilst in the middle of a fight. The game is a little too easy, even on the hardest difficulty, with the ability to pick up shield from enemy corpses and also the cheap prices of the health boosts and weapon upgrades. I ended up forcing myself to play even more aggressive and careless so that the fights would actually be a challenge for some points. Also, after running through the game and not worrying about collecting all the loot boxes in each location, they become a pain in the late gain to collect them all because they become scarce and spread apart, and the radar has a small range. So if there was a map or something you unlock at the end of the game then it would make it much easier. But overall, this game is amazing if you're fine with excessive dialogue and potty humour.P.S. The red guy is hotter

_childDocuments_.review: Fun unique combat full of quirky characters. If you like the rick and morty style humour you will love the game. If that kind of humor is not for you I can imagine it will get grating after a while as the visual and verbal jokes are constant (you do have the ability to reduce the amount of chatter you hear in the settings but this takes away a lot of the charm and fun from the game IMO). The story/characters are the real star here but beyond that the varied locations, gun and suit skills and boss mechanics make it fun to play regardless. TLDR; Funny linear FPS with some unique mechanics that you will either love or hate depending your sense of humour.

_childDocuments_.review: High on life is like a B movie, it's not trying to be more then it is on the surface and it don't  have to either. I had fun with this game, the combat was fresh, the weapon creatures were fun and diverse in usage and easy to mix and mash, the humor....I'll be honest that was kinda one note, Justin Roland seems to have trouble with finding a good punch line his jokes don't really pay off despite  a lot of built up. It comes to show that he needs a creative partner as he had for Rick and Morty. Likewise the story was ok, but I did not really care for the whole sidestory with the sister. One other thing I did not like, was how quickly we stopt going to new planets and just added zones to the existing planet. That really was a shame and needlessly so. You could have to second to last boss have his spa on a space station you warp to. Despite that, I was reminded off ratchet and clank with the whole going to planets, shooting everything, light puzzlework and back tracking with new weapons to uncover new boxes of loot. I do recommend the game but I do say to get in on sale. It was fun but not at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't remember the last time I laughed so much at a videogame from start to finish. The runtime is short but the segments of worlds to explore are relatively large, with more and more paths opening as you form your team. There's only four talking guns but they're all multifunctional and each a great character.  The bounties are all fun characters, too, some of them having way too little to say but they are voiced by A-list talent so they got what they could afford. There are tons of hidden collectibles and the threadbare economy sort of forces you to find as many as you can to buy upgrades, which seamlessly pads out the time between the bounties. Meanwhile the original soundtrack by Tobacco is fantastic; chill while exploring and more upbeat noise whenever combat erupts. The gunplay is the real star, though. On Normal difficulty I died an awful lot until I realized you have to keep moving, jumping and switching up your attacks like the Slayer in Doom Eternal, which I was not expecting from the goofy comedy game about aliens getting high on humans. If you were a fan of Channel 101 back in the day you are going to love every stupid moment.

_childDocuments_.review: Short Review: High on Life is a great game that is well written, hilarious with great combat controls, diversity in equipment, and just all around a great experience. However, it's a 10 hour experience that I just don't think is worth the $70 without any additional DLC or end-game content. Instead, I'd put this on your wishlist and wait for a sale, but if you have the money to burn go for it.Long Review: It really pains me to give a negative review for this game because it was so much fun, but I really don't think the 10 hours of fun I had was worth $70. You've probably searched this game because you're either a Rick and Morty fan that has been following it since its announcement, or you stumbled across this game to see if it was real after seeing it on TikTok. In either case, you've been drawn to the promise of being immersed in the shenanigans of Justin Roiland yelling at you in various voices with Rick and Morty style writing all the way; and you'd be right.The game is made with great detail, there's entire movies you can just watch, there's commercials clearly recorded in the same animated improvised content (filled with character breaks and actor laughs) as the inter-dimensional television episodes of Rick and Morty, and there's an in-game interaction with player actions that is near genius. The combat is smooth, simple, yet satisfying, and mastering switching between your Gatlian weapons for their unique abilities created one of the most satisfying FPS RPG experiences I've had in a long time.I enjoyed every moment, from getting gooped to freeing the "Prince Chosen One" to shoving that bomb up that alien's a**, and I'll be talking about this game with people for a while. So, why the negative review? Well, this great experience lasts about 10 hours, and that ultra-satisfying moment when you have all your unique guns and get the groove of mastering them is really only in the last level; which lasts about 20 minutes. If your gaming mantra is like mine that I want 1 hour of gameplay out of each dollar spent on the game, then I am missing about 60 hours of gameplay to make this game worth it. Sure you could try to find every lugloc, which could possibly add 5-10 hours of gameplay, but I don't really think surveying every inch of every map in some walking simulator is a great selling point for 'fun and satisfying gameplay'. Hopefully they release some DLC, but if it's not free it hardly makes up for the lack of game time.In all, I give my experience a 9/10, but if I had to be honest with myself in terms of cost to fun, then I have to give this game 1.4/10, which is the same ratio that I got in (gameplay/cost). Wait for a sale, but be sure to have it at #1 in your wishlist!

_childDocuments_.review: I have to give this Shooter a big thumbs up.  A big part of Shooters are the Guns, and in this game they take a unique approach to making them central to the action. This is a colorful entertaining shooter that dares to be different. But don't let the appearance fool you, it's a shooter, a seriously fast paced shooter. This game is all about movement and rapid in-game command utilization. At my age it was beyond my capabilities, it is best played with a game controller, this is no mouse and keyboard shooter (at least for me). But even with that said I have to give the creators their due. I tip my hat to them.I highly recommend giving this game a try.You will know if it's something you will be able to master well within the STEAM 2 hour refund limit when you take on the first "easy" Boss Battle. It may look like a kind of silly colorful game, but it is not, it is a shooter to its core it tries to be nothing else. Players throw around the term "skill" when talking about games, this game requires them. The commands are few, the action is simple but it's in your face from start to finish and it's a real work out for a real gamer.Another big plus for the game is how slick it runs. I ran it on an off the shelf plain-Jane gamer with an 3060RTX@8g, 16g RAM, and an AMD@3.7 and it looked great and ran smooth as butter.A few years ago I'd a beat this thing.It beat me, and won my respect along the way.I'd give it two thumps up if I could ... and it handed me my hat.

_childDocuments_.review: The trailers look interesting. It looks pretty unique and the aspect of a.... talking gun just seems like tons of fun.Unfortunately the humour is just as unique and definitely a matter of taste. If you're unsure of what kind of humour expects you, have a look at the "Rick & Morty" TV series. Same creator, same humour. If you don't like R&M you might not like this.While this is all subjective, the game also has gameplay issues that made me click the "Don't recommend" button.Overall the game-play feels "rubbery" and slow. Especially for a shooter. It just doesn't feel "crisp" and that really detracts from the fun. Secondly, the UI is pretty bad. The way they solved waypoints is annoying: To see the waypoint to the next objective you "ping" with a scanner, and then the waypoint is only on screen for a few seconds. Another ping is required to display it again. This in itself is not an issue. The issue is that the point that is shown after the ping is not the  waypoint. It's not the . So you are  to re-ping all the time. This gets annoying  fast.The weapons also feel pretty underwhelming.  Even thought they talk.Luckily the frequency of the gun chatter can be reduced. The default is pretty annoying again. Another issue with the chatter is that the devs didn't bother muting the chatter when another plot-dialog is starting. I had the issue several times that the gun started to blabber a longer sentence just before a plot-dialog started. I ended up with two dialogs at full volume. Final annoyance: Control rebinding.Some buttons don't rebind properly (or rather, they do no bind when bound to something else). For me this was the ping button. It is by default on "T" and I re-bound by reload to "T". Now every time I re-load, the ping is executed. There are certainly other bindings that have similar issues as well.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend it, but not for the €49,99. I bought it on sale and that's about what I would have found acceptable as a price, after playing this game. As some people stated, you can finish the game in about 8 hours. Then everything else you do is just for achievements. The achievements aren't hard to get, but you need to kill quite a few enemies and some of them are missable.If you like Rick & Morty humor then this is the game for you. In fact, the same voice actor also voices the gun (Kenny), you get at the start, and a lot of side dialogues too (like commercials you seen on tv's in-game). The game is fun for a first playthrough, and a bit buggy at times. Though I did not find any game breaking bugs. The game has a decent combination of platforming and shooting sequences, I found it quite enjoyable. However, there is no re-playability. After playing once, you pretty much have seen it all and a second playthrough can be a but tedious since there is no way to skip the dialogues. If you are a completionist, check for the achievements that are missable and make sure you get those at the first playthrough.

Why do I have to sort out their feelings?- bugs: dying right after opening the loklox box on Gatlus permanently removed all of the upgrades I had acquired for all guns; that sucked.- enemy variety: there is some at the start with the ants, but after that it is mostly just the gooped up Merks; they do get an Elite toward the end, but over all, it was a bit boring; I would have liked to fight the ants more; I was also expecting to see 8-Borg (?) after the first boss fight, but that didn't happen (or maybe it is a secret thing?)- customizing: while the suit automatically gets cooler skins with certain upgrades in-game, it would have been nice to change the colors and appearance of the suit with in-game purchases or unlocksThe music is dope, too. I am excited for a sequel and hope they improve on the few things that weren't great. Solid recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Bare in mind that I am a firm believer in death of the artist - I played this game and I am reviewing as it stands alone, not in association with the recently unearthed, unpleasant actions that Justin committed. If I was being totally honest, High on Life is less than the sum of its parts - its a mid game all around. The gun-play is not particularly exciting, the enemy design is uninspired and repetitive, and the movement is unsatisfying despite the freedom it gives you. As a game, High on Life really misses the mark. That said, I enjoyed every second that I spent playing it. The world design is straight out of a kid's imagination - its a fully-imagined, immaculately designed sci-fi playscape that is fully realized and enjoyable to the eyes and ears from start to finish. From the Tomorrowland-esque cityscapes of Blim City to the gorgeous nature scenes of Zephyr Paradise, High on Life really stretches the boundless wonder of what sci-fi worlds are capable of. I deeply, truly loved the absurdist humor of the game, from the absolutely asinine inclusion of Space Applebees to the humorous quips of the Gatlians and even the bickering of Gene and the player's sister, High on Life had me laughing out loud on a number of occasions. The music and sound design of the game was top notch. The music loops grew old eventually, but generally speaking, the OST SLAPS, and slaps hard. As an RTX 4090 user, the graphical fidelity and performance were top notch, and I only soft-locked requiring a "restart from last checkpoint" once, but I can imagine the game being difficult to play on weaker machines, especially given that the beauty of the game is really all it has going for it. High on Life represents what you can do with video games when you only care about making something fun to play and enjoy one's time with rather than fitting the game into a specific mold. The world of the game was fun, colorful, and wholly unique from anything else available right now. Name any other game with a futuristic city and society that isn't seedy, grimy, and dirty and is actually not depressing to explore and play in. The game is an easy recommend (especially on sale) for people who enjoy the humor of Rick and Morty or Solar Opposites OR had an active imagination as a child who would enjoy playing around in an adult-sized version of Disney's Tomorrowland.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I think this is an 8/10 game. Gameplay:This is one of the rare occasions where I have purchased a game released after 2018 that felt like the developers had at least gotten close to finishing their job. The combat gets repetitive early on, although I have yet to run into any bugs or have the game crash. I think that is something that can reasonably contribute to a $60 price tag. The FOV is not adjustable without the use of cheat engine at this point. Trying to play the game the same way that many play Call of Duty makes me dizzy, but being a little more methodical is a simple fix that prevented any motion sickness. However, I do sincerely hope that the game is soon updated with the option to adjust the FOV. I give the "feel" a 6/10. Graphics:What you see is cartoonish on purpose, as the game wouldn't work under any other style. There are a lot of vibrant colors. It does come off as a 3D animated Rick and Morty. The game takes you a bit on a color palette journey that is really quite pretty. To the game's credit, I have only had a frame rate drop once. The graphics are a 9/10 for me.Story:This is definitely a project involving Justin Roiland. You're likely to be satisfied with what you get if you liked what you saw in the trailers for High On Life or in Rick and Morty or Solar Opposites. The humor is very much on brand as is the preposterous premise. It should be said that I am far from Justin Roiland's biggest fan, but there is no false advertising here. While nothing in the writing surprised me, there was nothing there to disappoint me either. That is why this story gets a 10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: High on Life (main game) is a fast-paced FPS in somewhat of an extremely colourful “Rick and Morty” alien worlds setting. The plot explained in short is that Earth is attacked and taken over by aliens (the G3 Cartel) who want to use humans as drugs. The player picks up the fight against them and is trying to free his species. On his journey, he’ll get help by a variety of sentient, talking guns. You’ll probably spend 12-15 hours on the main story and a bit of exploration. For a completionist approach play time is going to be around 22+ hours. Here is my pros and cons list: Pros:+ crazy colour scheme+ comic style but adult plot+ fresh setting+ hilarious start of the game+ some equally hilarious small encounters during the game+ alien worlds and cities+ fast-paced, well-working combat+ parkour elements+ great alien models+ funny dialogues and characters+ details of the environment+ good graphics and lighting (although not outstanding)+ talking weapons+ unusual music style+ lips sync well done+ goofy + small puzzles+ alien TV & commercials+ some good “side quests”+ change of scenery+ good amount of looting+ after game exploration possibleCons- Clipping errors (fall through textures)- Quite frequent level and asset recycling- Combat mechanics can sometimes be a bit sluggish- Some game crashes and freezes- Bugged achievements- Bugged bounty hunter forum posts- Repetitive colour pattern in levels- Colour overload in some levels- Variety of worlds could have been more- Some remains of bad console control portation because of unnecessary elements- Music is very repetitive and can get on your nerves quickly- Low quality level backgrounds (2D pictures)- Strong start in plot and conversations, but also strong decrease after first 10-20% of the story in interesting engagements and new ideas- Only minimal ray tracing effects- Missing face animations- First half of the game is super satirical and comical, black humour, second half shifts to pretty serious storytelling. That’s a strange break with the general character of the game. Seems like the developers found it hard to decide on which focus to put on it.- Some of the quests and conversations are over-exaggerated and can be a bit too much after a while- More conversations with citizens would have been nice- Some dialogues stretch on and on…Conclusion: High on Life is a super colourful, quirky, comical, quite over-exaggerated, kind of “Rick & Morty” Sci-Fi alien shooter with small riddles, lots of looting and fast-paced combat will be happy playing this game. It’s a fresh setting and fun to follow the main story. It does have quite a few technical errors and inconsistencies though which lead to a lower rating in my opinion. Otherwise recommended. Rating: 6/10 points

_childDocuments_.review: It's a pretty enjoyable game. Not perfect, but worth it if you enjoy Justin Roiland's brand of silliness. Some minor gripes (Don't let this detract too much from the game, it's a fun game, but complaining is also fun): - Even with going after most of the collectibles, it's a fairly short game. It's an understandable tradeoff given all of the quality that's gone into the voice acting, art, etc, but if you were looking for a lot more game for the money it might feel a bit disappointing. - While the world is visually quite enjoyable to look at, the level design isn't the best for the kind of game it is. As a metroidvania style game you will do a lot of backtracking to go to new areas and find collectibles you couldn't access before. While first treks through the areas for story are straightforward thanks to a daisy chain of story events and waypoints, revisiting the areas leaves you without those navigational crutches and I frequently felt lost in areas that weren't built in a way to help me develop a strong mental map. Nor is there any in game map. - On the subject of backtracking, the mobility tools you unlock are often not even needed in places in a way that seems unintentional. You unlock a jetpack relatively early in the game and I found that with a little finesse I was able to bypass platforming challenges which were clearly supposed to be locked behind a later tool. By the time I got that tool, there were few places left that even made use of it, and confusingly a lot of random spots where you COULD use it, but for no discernible reason. - Personal preference, but I felt like the combat encounters often went on for longer than was fun. There were a lot of points where I felt done with a combat bit and then more would show up and I'd just feel like "Really? Even more?"- Lastly, I did encounter a few relatively minor bugs. Nothing that wasn't fixable with a quit to menu, and the check-pointing is generous enough that it didn't majorly disrupt my gameplay. I had a bug during a boss fight that literally stopped me from continuing and when I reloaded I was right back at the same scripted bit and it worked fine. It'd be nice to get these fixed, but overall nothing that bad.

_childDocuments_.review: It's pretty good, but not for me.Plays sort of like a ps2 era platformer with light metroidvania elements - the gameplay loop is fighting themed bosses and their goons, and unlocking mobility powers that allow you go back to previous areas to hunt for treasure to fund more mobility / combat upgrades.Graphics are good, soundtrack is great, and it's a really well imagined coming of age science fiction story from what I played of it, and the controls and level design are pretty on point (although even with the AR markers to show you where to go, it is still easy to get lost - the mines level could have used some better hinting for where the exit to the area was).Overall, it's fairly solid but the character dialog and humor put me off - it's not that they're bad, and some of the jokes were good, but given that it's a Justin Roiland thing you're basically required to enjoy the kind of humor presented in his works to really enjoy it.Give it a shot, especially if you like his work.

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly didn't know what to expect of this game other than it's developed by the same people that did 'Accounting+' and 'Trover saves the Universe'. I went in blind and I enjoyed every second of this sci-fi comedy FPS title. The writing had me in stitches and I loved every secret and weapon that I discovered. The environment and overall art design are top notch and sparked my imagination like few games today have. The combat is robust and responsive, I'm actually impressed with how good it felt. The upgrades for each gun as well as the collectibles in each world are worth exploring for and obtaining. If you are interested in a fun sci-fi adventure with funny writing and unique guns then look no further than 'High on Life'. I recommend this to everyone.

_childDocuments_.review: I can appreciate a game that is silly, full of nonsense, and awkward humor. I admit, some parts of the comedy grew tiresome due to excessive repetition, but I think the game was just the right length for this not to be a significant problem.I also found myself enjoying the gameplay, which even improved over time as I played. You unlock new features at a relatively fast pace. The last half of the game, where you have most of your upgrades, ends up being a great deal of fun. There are many different ways to fight, and as they say, variety is the spice of life.The one thing I don't agree with is the game's claim that it is "story rich." Sure, there's a lot of dialogue, but it's mostly nonsense, and the story is about as simple as a story can be—similar to a popcorn movie with Jason Statham. I am not saying that this game should have tried to have a stronger story; it was the right kind of storytelling for this format. But it isn't "story rich."

I've ran into zero issues so far and enjoyed every second of it.   If you pick up this game I recommend you take your time for it, don't rush through the missions, instead try to observe the scenery and interract with npc's.  Remember you're in this crazy universe where nothing makes sense so when you start taking actions with that in mind you'll find yourself unlocking quite a few interesting achievements. _childDocuments_.review: Absolutely incredible. This is one of the rare few games that does a certain set of things well, and doesn't try to extend beyond it's original scope - which makes for a very focused and polished experience that I cannot fault.Story - The main meat of the game is experienced through the story, and to avoid dropping spoilers I'll just say that it's a simple, linear narrative that's interesting enough to hold attention without the cliche twists and turns that make more complex stories feel predictable. What you see is exactly what you get, and it's greatly enhanced by the rest of what the game has to offer.Core Gameplay - My favourite part of the game is by far the shooting & movement. Again, without spoilers I'll just say it's very fluid and natural. The combat itself feels very 'Doom' inspired, although I wish the 'shotgun' was more impactful; Rage 2 is where the bar is set for me personally, and this game didn't quite get there in terms of feedback & power. World Design - The various levels, worlds & sequences are very well made, and it's obvious a lot of love went into designing/creating them. Every environment is unique, and on max settings the game looks amazing. There are heaps of easter eggs and references scattered everywhere, and there's a lot of NPC's that really add to the world building.Overall - I think the crux of this game comes down to whether someone can tolerate or appreciate Justin Roiland's humour; the super satirical, self aware side of Rick and Morty. This both makes and breaks this game, because there's no way to avoid it. Personally, I love it, and the fact the developers leaned into this made it a huge strength. As the saying goes, 'there is no perfect game, only many perfect games' - for me, High On Life is one of them.

_childDocuments_.review: Cyberpunk if it was goodSeriously though, story is surprisingly deep for what initially appears to be a rick and morty episode. Your choices seem to matter and each of for "supporting characters" has a unique dialogue for every story beat. The world of the game, despite being absurd is actually quite believable and consistent. There's a TON of side content not critical to the story: npcs react to your actions, weird alien shows are on tvs everywhere you go, References to previous events and in-universe culture are commonplace. Combat is fun and I find myself using the entire arsenal when fighting which is rare for me. Bosses were a highlight, introducing new mechanics and toying with your expectations every time. Enemies feel alive, reacting to your actions in combat in a unique manner. Snipers give up when you come close, tiny dudes run away in fear when their friends are killed and elite guys teleport away from your charged attacks.Upgrades are significant and game changing, so looking for secrets is really rewarding. That ties into metroidvania aspect of the game where you revisit previous areas, using combat upgrades for traversal and puzzle solving. Platforming is surprisingly fluid which meshes well with the frantic pace of the shootouts and lets you cheese some puzzles.TL;DR If you can tolerate rick and morty humor there is a solid 15 hour action adventure waiting for you here

_childDocuments_.review: An epic story of alien space travel and incredible dialogue. There’s not one second of this game that feels “the same”. Every level is full of commentary, unique to each weapon, characters, or npc’s. Each world feels fresh and makes you want to explore. Combat = 8/10 - You’re ability to slide, dash, jump, &  jet pack makes it manageable fighting large swarms of enemies. Each weapon allows you to fight with a different style and speed. Visuals = 9.5/10 - This game is every bit of “bright and vibrant”. Each location is well detailed, a mix of alien skylines and space jungles. Story - 8/10: You eventually get used to the long dialogue cuts and become genuinely invested into the story. At times it feels a bit rushed, repeating bounty after bounty, occasionally straying away for a side mission. Dialogue - 10/10 = Never have I burst out laughing at a video game before. This game I absolutely did…nearly every few minutes. Every alien/weapon has a bold personality that pairs well with their part of the story & or skills. This game felt like it broke a few rules (in a good way) and got away with it. Great play for those looking for a fairly easy and laid back FPS alien experience.

There are strong vertical slices of gameplay, scenes that play out which get a laugh, but the constant dismissive undercuts leave you not really invested in anything. This is especially not helped by the guns.There are four to unlock (not counting Lezduit who is only used on the final mission), and the first two you unlock (the ones you'll be stuck with for half the game) are pretty grating. There's Kenny, the Morty-voiced blue gun who complains constantly, and Sweezy, who's a one-note aggressive character. The later unlocks, Gus and Creature, have a  better performances, they don't carry the bland and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ plot.

_childDocuments_.review: There is about a handful of positives, a multitude of "meh" and some glaring negatives. Sure, the game itself is not "bad" in a way it's poorly made or doesn't play well. Game wise, it's solid, but i just cannot recommend it. If i didn't got it from humble choice, i would refund it after an hour, but since it was here until deleted, i decided i might as well see if it gets better.It doesn't. From 1st hour to the last, it's just mediocre shooter-platformer with everything and everyone yapping. Just constant yapping. Even if you turn them down during combat, there is a lot of dialogs with more yapping that cannot be skipped. At times it was amusing, but for the most of the time it was just toilet humor. So much jokes and gags in this category it was just irritating at some point. For better or worst at least game isn't too long, so i didn't feel completely awful about it.For a more listed annoyances of mine, here is a handful of positives, mehs and negatives.+ Weapon abilities were neat, and combining it during traversal segments with jetpack and dashes was pretty fun+ The story premise. Pretty dumb, but they stick to it and it worked, somewhat.+ Artstyle. The whole vibrant albeit "goopy" alien world of High on Life is something that should be given a positive for. = Combat. The whole combat just felt... Dull. Feedback on receiving hits or shooting and hitting is nearly non existant. = Traversal. While combining abilities and jetpack was neat, as a whole package, it was jarring to deal with. It didn't flow well. I played games that are over 10 years older than this and did that better.= Dialogs. Sometimes they were aight, but for the 3 aight dialogs or quips, there was about 5 that made me get a headache.-  Talking. So much talking. Unskippable dialogs of talking. Guns talking with no way to skip them. Suit talking. Everything talks, almost all the time there is something that talks.- Enemy variety. There is about 5 enemy types (7 if you count reskins between ants and the yellow dudes).- Boss fights are not engaging at all. The only good one is the one before final boss, due to having some story moments. All remaining ones can be done by unloading special abilities and juggling boss in the air/time bubble/stun
