_childDocuments_.review: The game has its peaks but overall it feels underdeveloped. The game tries to make it seem like bad things will happen if you fail, but it's constantly undercut by jokes to the point where you no longer care and it feels like you're fighting the same 3-4 enemy types (with the same quips) over and over and over again. The lack of variety becomes abundantly apparent. The level design feels lazy since you end up revisiting the same 3 areas for most of the game, and yet it's still very linear when a free-roam approach would have worked well. You get back home after killing a boss to find out the next boss was just around the corner from where you were, but linear progression stopped you from doing both back to back.Normally I love story-driven games, I never skip cut scenes and typically get very engaged in the game's story. The story in this game isn't engaging at all, I couldn't have cared less when story characters were talking, I just wanted to get to the next mission, not settle a petty argument between 2 characters. The game tries to be modern in it's dialogue and game play elements, but turns around and forces you to listen to characters go on and on. None of the side stories are interesting and much of the development happens off camera or through texts you can't reply to or read for more than a few seconds, if you're not checking text popups while fighting 3 dozen enemies, you'll miss half the side plots.The talking guns are the best part, it seems that's where they put the most time and effort, so I actually enjoyed the dialogue from them. That said, your character appears to be a mute and Kenny does the talking for you, but also has one-sided conversations with you throughout the game. There was lots of opportunity to have genuine conversation options with Kenny or the other weapons and have that impact future dialogue or your relationship with them.It only took 10 hours to beat the story, I can't recall the last game I've played that was that short. Even Call of Duty has longer campaigns! In many ways it really does feel like a demo of a game, even till the end the game tells you what to buy and when, there's barely any choice when it comes to gear or weapons. It feels like you're riding a train, it'll get you from point A to B, but you can't steer or change the speed along the way. Disappointed overall for such a hyped up game.

But for the rest of humanity, this game gets old... fast. It has some smaller fresh concepts and the art is goofy & interesting, but it really feels like a game from the 2010's... from the massive invisible walls to the hidden loot chests everywhere without any real meaningful rewards and the running to cover and waiting for a shield recharge, there is a feeling that High on Life is just outdated. The puzzles are also super super basic platforming and are pretty mindless. True to the theme, everything about this game is pretty mindless. The guns are fun and interesting, and the game ends before the combat gets super repetitive, but unfortunately the enemy variety is extremely lacking. Overall I give it a 6/10. _childDocuments_.review: As someone who has not watched Rick and Morty even for an episode, I can easily say that I had a blast playing this game. At its core, High On Life is a decent linear story, semi-open area FPS game with some Metroidvania elements. It has decent gameplay, graphics, and level design. But where High on Life shines is the writing. Interact with everything you can, and listen to every dialogue there is. If you do those things, you will see that the attention to detail in this game is crazy. Throughout my playthrough, I found myself wondering about what was going to happen next and what the characters had to say. That's something I haven't experienced in a long time and care about in a video game's design. Great voice acting, janky but fun gameplay and a colorful world. High on Life is another example of why we never should let critics impose opinions on us. Even though High on Life is not a great game, making a game that relies on humor is a brave attempt and seems like it's just what I needed.Follow My Curator Page:

_childDocuments_.review: The amount of enjoyment you get out of this game will be determined from how much you enjoy Rick and Morty; specifically, the humour of the show and Justin Roiland's delivery of that humour. High on Life is basically the video game version of Rick and Morty. The game was a lot of fun. Very vibrant and colourful with lots of interesting locations. The dialogue between the weapons and the NPC's and characters were all hilarious, and the end of the game had some more heartfelt moments. Overall I really enjoyed all aspects of the game, and I found it to have a unique aura. Special mention to the "drug trip" - you'll know what I mean.I finished it in about 14 hours, so the game isn't too long which could be a sticking point for some people when considering the price. I also ran into some technical bugs, where scripts weren't triggered and it forced me to restart at my previous checkpoint. One of them I thought was game-breaking but the next part of the level finally opened up. There were only a handful of these and they all appeared in the second half of the game. Nothing that forced me to quit and I was able to continue each time.I'd definitely recommend this game. I think Justin Roiland/Squanch Games have come up with a gem here. You have to like his particular brand of humour to enjoy this game. If you do, I say forget the price tag and dive in.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: I added some screenshots of some map glitches. Repetitive: From the dialogue to the gun play the games charm ends rather quickly. After the first hour you find yourself wanting to skip dialogue and just progress the missions. It's not going to happen. You have about two hours of the 10 hour campaign of forced dialogue. Boring, filler, dialogue. The gun upgrades look as if they added random words into a hat and made a mod out of it. Like kenny's magnum mod. Does increased damage with less ammo. Cool! Everyone would take that... but only while aiming down sights. It's now useless as we already have long distance damage on the team. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ stupid. The boss fights. You can beat every single boss with just kenny. The only difficult fight is the last and its just bullet hell. Each gun has a cool feature, but not once does it matter in a boss fight. Glitches/Incomplete Game:♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥! I lost my first save entirely due to falling through the ground into a later checkpoint and no way out. 2 hours gone. By just simply playing the game I've falling through the map several times. Those are just the accidents. You can get out of the map intentionally on almost every single map. Pop ups getting stuck on the screen. The grade from being a detective, just never went away until i restarted the game. The prompt to get rid of pop ups stayed when the pop ups were gone. My hand being fully visible because the gun is behind my hand. Crashes. The game won't even start now without crashing which is why i'm here writing this now. Enemies spawn or telelporting inside of the environment. The frame rate in general is poor. General grievances: (Spoilers)You don't actually get to eat your food at applebees. Gene lives being stabbed. Your gun lives being a butt plug. The entire sister tweeb arc. The sisters existence. Not being able to skip a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cutscene or dialogue. Not being able to play the husband shooter again after the beginning. No leaderboard for the secretary and skateboarding mini game. I got over 1 million points skateboarding and no one will ever believe me. The teleport disks just being able to be put anywhere. It's kind of boring for them to not have a place where they fit perfect. Nearly every mod sucks. Knifey upgrades? Why cant he grapple enemies like he ziplines? Why doesn't gus's suck grapple an enemy when its close instead of dropping it to the side of his hit box? Also why is his accuracy 0 and 1 foot? Yeah he's a shotgun but he's a high tech alien one. Even if he is sawed off size he should have some sort of accuracy and a lot more damage than he currently has. Creature also feels boring. Cool concept but the damage isnt worth the wait. Squeezy while not aiming down sights is 1000% the worst damage in the game. The height limit on the jet pack is dumb. That's not how those work. There is no real resolution to the story. It's left open ended without returning home. Rescuing humans doesn't grant an achievement. Wether it's 0 or 100 the same number of humans rescued are in human haven. No way to warp back to home when you do and will get stuck at some point playing this game. All the slow ballsack monsters leave the spa faster than they should be able to move and you don't get to kill them. There's no onslaught mode. You don't get enough pesos from luglox to get every upgrade in the game. It doesnt matter what character model you pick because you will literally never see your face after you pick it. There is no option to actually take the drugs. Squeezy can't shoot the bomb at the end of the game even though her shots go through people. There's no achievement for playing the hardest difficulty. There's no option to redo bosses at the end of the game. Everyone and their mom already mentiond FOV. There's zero replay value aside from achievements. You never find your parents. You can't buy everything in the pawn shop. Every part where you're locked in with waves of the same enemies you started the game fighting. You can't destroy or stop time with the trolley. Not once do you drink or eat alien food. The fact that squeezy's secondary charge shot is her best part and not her only part. Just make her a sniper RIFLE and not another pistol. _childDocuments_.review: It feels like Metroid Prime was written by Rick and Morty with a dabbling of Robot Chicken... it's dumb crude humor that dips into a bit of dark humor.You unlock suit upgrades, weapons, weapon upgrades and mods, and more through chests you can open and a pawn shop where you can purchase items. You traverse three different worlds that are interesting looking, but the npcs are pretty dull... very much deadpan and dull personalities that are very reminiscent of Rick and Morty scenes that felt very ad libbed and mostly unscripted... which in smaller amounts is amusing, but its consistent through the entire game.Although the game lacks some depth and features in certain areas, it is a pretty consistent shooter and something new in a world of sequels. I'd pick it up on sale, it's a quick play... I finished in about 15 hours and then spent a few more hours hunting for some achievements and collectibles. $20 at most.

_childDocuments_.review: Such an awesome game. Funny as ♥♥♥♥, well-crafted and functional (an achievement, something to truly behold in today's era of games), no microtransactions (another thing to praise in today's era of pure greed and exploitation within the gaming industry), and quite the ride from beginning to end story-wise. Glad i also picked up the DLC cause it ended way before i was done with it. Also something interesting about this game is you'll spend much of your time simply listening to the dialogue of the characters. I'd argue it's more than half of the value within this game. I've never had a game make me laugh and smile so much before. The Rick and Morty style of humor is right up my alley, though some people find it kind of cringe. So that is something to note for both camps.I also really liked the talking guns, or the Gatlians. If this game comes back for a sequel or prequel, they need to make a return. It's such a bizarre experience shooting at enemies and then having my gun ♥♥♥♥ talk them, but I'm all for it lmao. Gus is probably my favorite out of the bunch, but they are all great and it's a bit difficult to pick a favorite since they each add a unique take to various situations and happenings within the game. overall this was probably one of the best single-player games I've played, and one of the best games to come out in the past couple of years. in an ocean full of ♥♥♥♥, the diamonds shine through, and this is one of them.

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably the first game I have ever felt physically sick from playing. While the game is stylistically interesting and the humor can get a chuckle from time to time (you’ll know whether or not you’ll like the style of humor before buying the game) but the technical aspects of this game hold it back and refuse to let go. The game defaults to an atrociously low field of view that makes The act of just looking around feel nauseating and it cannot be changed without third party tools. The visuals, while interesting, are very fuzzy and blurry and take fiddling with to make it look like how it should look by default. And the movement is so hard to explain. On keyboard it feels like you continue to move if you let go of W while moving your mouse. It can feel like having the back end of your car sliding on an icy road. I can’t explain it but if you play you’ll notice it and that is not something you should have in s movement like shooter. If the movement were tweaked and settings were added for FOV I would say the game is worth how many laughs you’ll get out of it. The gameplay is fine and the setting is neat but the humor will be what carries your play through. If you like Rick and morty style humor then you’ll enjoy the game. If not just stay clear.
_childDocuments_.name: High On Life

_childDocuments_.review: High On Life is a humoristic, narrative-driven first person shooter game with a colourful art style and creative design aesthetic. For me, it got close to 9/10, but I will settle for 8/10 as there are some flaws.Pros:- I had some good laughs in this game XD- Great characters, each with their own unique personality- Surprisingly fluid shooter mechanics. Shooting feels fun and several arenas have interactibles, such as grappling hook... hooks, which make combat feel more energetic and exciting- Decent plot and villian- Great and colourful environments- The game had the perfect amount of challenge when I played on normal difficulty. The difficulty is well balanced.- (Mutual point) Game is not too long and I managed to complete it in 12 hours. This might be a bad point as some might expect it to be a bit longer and it would be fair for them to assume so. I felt that it was long enough, but some more content would definitely also have been welcomeCons:- Some guns, although they have great personalities, were very underpowered and borderline useless.- The ending was a bit... abrupt and sudden. There was not enough buildup in my opinion.- Hearkening back to what I previously said about the game's completion time, some might feel it to be a bit too short.- I felt that some characters were underused and kind of forgotten about (looking at you Knifey)- This game gave me some rather embarrassing Steam achievements; therefore, the real score is now 1/10 as part of my vengeance XD Joking
_childDocuments_.name: High On Life

_childDocuments_.review: This game is too damn short for the price. The humor is OK, nothing we haven't seen before and done way better elsewhere.Gun play is kinda like Serious Sam take your pick 1- 4 . You don't have to aim directly at the enemies to hit them. _childDocuments_.review: This is a good and enjoyable game. The game setting is great, the graphics are great, the music is just so on-point too. Dialogue is enjoyable and humorous (though definitely for mature audiences). This is incredibly on-par for a Justin Roiland game. I've had a lot of fun playing it...until I got about 2/3 the way through.You spend a lot of time trying to find and unlock chests that give you gun upgrades & pesos (in-game currency), and spend it on additional upgrades for your guns. Finding and unlocking the chests is pretty enjoyable in itself honestly, as you are rewarded heavily for exploring the maps.But all this is pretty much for naught, as toward the end of the game, you set your guns down (twice, in fact) for a conversation. Upon picking the guns back up, you will find one or more of them have lost all their upgrades (not the mods, just the upgrades). Upon the 2nd time putting your guns down and picking them back up, you will have lost all upgrades on a least a 2nd gun or the remainder of them.Quitting and restarting the game did not fix this problem, even after I knew it was likely going to happen when picking guns up a 2nd time.I searched to find if anyone else was experiencing this issue, and come to find out, people have been experiencing this bug since the game launched and nothing has been done to fix it.So no, don't get this game, they won't even fix a known issue that's been ongoing for over a year that completely undoes the hours of time you put in hunting down chests to upgrade your guns.

_childDocuments_.review: Since this is a weird and fairly short game I'll try to keep my review the same way. High on Life is a classic story focused shooter made by Squanch Games. A studio founded by Justin Roiland who is also one of the founders and previous voice actor for the TV Show Rick & Morty. You play as... someone. You dont have a name or anything. You are just a nerd in your room playing games all day. Earth get's invaded by an alien drug cartel who wants to capture humans and use them as drugs. Now it is on you and your arsenal of talking guns to take them down.Of course this pitch sounds very weird. And it does sound like something from an "Interdimensional Cable" episode from Rick & Morty. And this  how the game feels! It's weird, it's funny, full of meta commentary and often times completely off the rails. If this style of humor is yours, you will have an absolute field day! If not then there might be nothing here for you.Because this is the main draw of the game. The charakters and the humor.Don't get me wrong the gameplay is decent. It feels like a solid AA shooter. It has this 2010's shooter era vibe to it. Mostly linear levels with a few small areas to explore, weapons to upgrade and loads of combat areas with the same types of enemies and a few bossfights sprinkled in. Nothing groundbreaking. But servicable. However, it is very clear that you play this more for the charakters and humor rather than the gameplay.The voiceacting is stellar of course. Well done all around. Sounddesign is also fine. The only thing that I found to be grating was the music. There is not very much of it. And it is going by the theme of being very weird. But it kinda wears you down after the first couple hours.The game is also fairly short especially considering the price. I did a little bit of exploring here and there and it took me 12h to finish. If you wanna go for all the collectables and upgrades I can see you spending around 15-18 hours. But if you just wanna blitz through the main story that will probably take you less than 10 hours.At first I was irritated by the little playtime but overall I dont think that is bad. Yes, the price for what you get is way too high. But at least the game doesnt overstay it's welcome that way.For me, this game is a good "in between" kinda game. You know, when you've just finished a big 50+ hour game and you need something light and short to digest before the next big game? A little breather of a game. That's this game!It's a fun, sweet and short 10h ride.But again, beware if you do not enjoy the Rick & Morty kind of humor (dont know how to phrase it otherwise) you should probably skip this one. If this sounds like something for you then this is an easy recommend. Just dont buy it at full price and wait for a good sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Rick and Morty theme game with great jokes, secrets and references, but terrible combat. The jokes go a long way, it's funny and enjoyable, like if you are in a R&M episode (if you're into that). But the whole gameplay feels like a bunch of jokes layered with a bunch of random shootings to extend game-time. Exploration with various moves you get is good. But the combat in between just breaks the fun. Guns variety is nice, but it's a few types of enemies thrown at you and that's it, nothing special. There is no risk, no challenge => dying doesn't lose any currency, or XP, or even reset the enemy waves, you might as well not even be killable, it's the same. So why even try and not just run into them... The only place where the combat is good are boss fights. The bosses have nice moves and attacks, some take it on a whole new level (hint: Nipulon). *Graphics = Nice to look around, unique atmosphere *Gameplay = Outside of combat fun, in combat "meh"*Audio = Few amazing tracks (like the forest map)*PC requirements = Weaker PCs might run it on low*Difficulty = easy peasy, like too easy*Grind = reachable 100%, just no motivation why, finding chest is just for gold*Story = Average, could be better - the jokes are what you're here for*Game Time = Could be more for the prize, just enough in length, but wait for sale*Bugs = Minor to none*Audience = If you like Rick and Morty, you will have a blast. If not, probably dodge this one. --{ 6 / 10 }--

_childDocuments_.review: After finishing this game, I can say that this was not worth the 60 bucks. I'm sure most of the folks that enjoy this game are only here for the High IQ comedy and really nothing else. The gameplay was serviceable, the dialogue was grating at most times, but if you're into a joke being hammered into you for 30 seconds straight then go off king. I can say that the scripted stuff was a lot more palatable, and the VAs for all of the guns save for kenny are pretty sweet. The incredibly drawn out improv parts of the game just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ suck. i wish i could skip them. I also wish i could choose a single gun to configure the amount of chatter for, not just for all of them. The other guns were all completely fine save for a few lines.Getting past my own opinion of the comedy used in this game, there's still a major problem with how expensive this game is. Despite it taking me 8 hours to complete this game it felt like most of it was filler. Some missions felt like they had importance to the overarching storyline while others felt like I was walking through a side quest (this was 3 of the only 7 jobs in the game). The ending was anticlimatic and just ends with "welp i guess we won" and roll credits. Overall, I think this game would be fine being in the 40 dollar range. If you really like Justin's type of comedy you probably will like this, but those of you who really don't, don't play it.

_childDocuments_.review: To be fair, you have to have a very high IQ to understand High on Life. The humour is extremely subtle, and without a solid grasp of theoretical physics most of the jokes will go over a typical viewer's head. There's also the gun's nihilistic outlook, which is deftly woven into his characterisation- his personal philosophy draws heavily from Narodnaya Volya literature, for instance. The fans understand this stuff; they have the intellectual capacity to truly appreciate the depths of these jokes, to realise that they're not just funny- they say something deep about LIFE. As a consequence people who dislike High on Life truly ARE idiots- of course they wouldn't appreciate, for instance, the humour in the main character's existential catchphrase of whatever that Morty gun says, which itself is a cryptic reference to Turgenev's Russian epic Fathers and Sons. I'm smirking right now just imagining one of those addlepated simpletons scratching their heads in confusion as Dan Harmon's genius wit unfolds itself on their pc monitors. What fools.. how I pity them. 😂And yes, by the way, i DO have a High as Life tattoo. And no, you cannot see it. It's for the ladies' eyes only- and even then they have to demonstrate that they're within 5 IQ points of my own (preferably lower) beforehand. Nothin personnel kid 😎 I wrote this from the heart and by no way copied and pasted a meme and edited a few parts.

_childDocuments_.review: The most fun I've had in a shooter in a while. It will make you laugh the entire way through and even has some touching moments. Can't attest to hard mode. There are plenty of rewarding things to find if you explore outside the set quest path too. It's not meant for hardcore FPS fans, but it's extremely entertaining and worth a try if you're a fan of Roiland-style humor. I really took my time in exploring/talking to people and it took 15 hours to beat, but HLTB shows 9 hours or so for the main story if you rush through.

_childDocuments_.review: Best way I can summarize this game, Justin Roiland took some drugs and made his own version of DOOM. I came into this game expecting a semi-open world shooter with funny and interesting dialogue, fairly solid combat, and a decent variety of tools to play with. I'm happy to say, this game has delivered on most of my fundamental expectations. However; to say it did much more than that would be an understatement. High on life delivers with the classic Justin Roiland/ Rick And Morty style of humor. So if you aren't a fan of his deadpan delivery of jokes, or vulgar and offensive style of comedy it may get annoying fast rather than humorous.  However even if you aren't quite a fan of his form of comedy, there are some situations in the game where it works. I feel like i'm dwelling too much on the comedic aspect of the game, but if you like Rick And Morty style humor it will certainly work for you. Many of the dialogue scenes and characters will drag on for quite some time if you hang around, and can be pretty entertaining if you spend the extra moments. All in all I enjoy the humor, and appreciate the extra content for staying around with otherwise one off appearance characters. As much hate as the jokes in this game get, I find the topic subjective as is most comedy. Moving past that to the meat and potatoes, let's start off with the combat. Frankly my expectations for this game in terms of combat game play were fairly low, and after the first hour or so it would seem that way. Thankfully, I was mistaken in my assumption. High on Life has a total of 5 unlock-able weapons, each of which has several different modifications and improvements you can add to them. Which both improve their effectiveness in combat, and even change up how their special abilities work for extra utility. The weapon sandbox isn't too vast in terms of sheer numbers, but the improvements you can give your weapons are quite numerous and often require extra exploration or credits to attain; rewarding exploration.The combat is also fairly fast paced, similar to the doom franchise. Complimenting that, throughout your progress in the game you unlock several other methods of mobility for moving around the battlefield as well as the open world. Which flow quite well with the mainly projectile based combat as most if not all attacks in the game are dodge-able in some manner. Even during boss battles where the boss surprises you with a new attack, after a second or third attempt you will learn how to counter said move. It feels very rewarding to watch and witness yourself progress, taking on larger rooms of enemies that will continually increase in difficulty. It also is quite satisfying to hit enemies, the game doesn't shy away from gore. The hit registration feels solid, and all of the weapons have their uses both in combat and in the open world with their utilities that promote exploration; and even returning to prior areas where you can now access areas you were previously unable to without your new gear. Attempting to tie everything in a neat bow here, I'm going to circle back to my DOOM comparisons. Specifically DOOM 2016 and DOOM ETERNAL. This game has many components and mechanics that feel heavily inspired. You have a dash/dodge ability to strafe side to side. You can execute low health enemies with a melee attack for temporary invulnerability. There's a jet pack and wall climb mechanics (mostly for exploration but also a few boss and enemy encounters). However if you enjoy how the modern doom games play, this one is fairly comparable. Dashing from shield units enemies dropped to barely stay alive, jet-packing over a dangerously close melee enemy, finishing off a tough foe with just enough health to spare with a melee execution, AOE attacking a cluster of baddies, or exploding a barrel sending them flying. Also you can combo attack enemies in the air which is INCREDIBLY satisfying. The combat is one portion of this game that over-delivered compared to my expectations. It is very satisfying and they give you more than enough to play with where it doesn't get old. Enemy variety isn't spectacular but it offers enough where it doesn't wear itself out. Flying enemies, tanky enemies, grunts, fast enemies, all coming in various forms shapes and sizes. The boss encounters are probably one of this game's best strengths. Each one feels unique to the character you're trying to find and take down. They all have their own abilities which thankfully aren't too similar to other bosses you will face, so it doesn't get repetitive. They're challenging enough, however I did play this game on Hard mode my first play through. I didn't die more than a handful of times on most boss encounters. So perhaps there could be some bit of a difficulty tweak needed there, or maybe a new game plus mode. Although, I did die at least once on nearly every boss. That's part of the reward is learning their move set and figuring the best way to take them down; which this game accomplishes in spades. Many boss arenas have several platforms, grapple locations, zip lines, climb walls, that you can utilize for their fights. Which also tie in with the exploratory aspect of the weapons you will utilize, coming full circle there. It also keeps in mind the form of movement based combat this game adopts from shooters much like the modern DOOM games. If you enjoy Justin Roiland's style of humor, and the fast paced movement based shooter combat of DOOM. You won't be disappointed by this title. There's plenty of exploration, secrets, unlockables, spicy dialogue, and goodies for you even after you finish the campaign. 8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, I'd like to say that this game is short and sweet, so don't expect to get 500 hours in this game.So let's get into my review.Like I just said, the game is short, I'm writing this review at 7.3 hours into the game and I've beaten it at normal difficulty.So if you don't like short games, this one might not be for you.However, the game may be short in length it doesn't lack in originality.For the first time in a while I felt like I was playing an actual new game instead of some recycled garbage.The game cracks LOTS of jokes, if you don't pay attention for 15 seconds it'll be likely that you've already missed a joke.All the characters/guns feel original and fun, they all have their own voice lines and characteristics.I know that "Morty's" voice was a great thing for marketing, it's hard for me to not listen to Kenny as if he isn't Morty. Every other gun feels awesome to talk to, even if you don't use them often, I mostly stuck with Kenny but I heard the other guns talk every once in a while in the background.The game has a decent plot, but it's silly, at least the game is self-aware about it and doesn't hesitate to get a little "meta" sometimes.About the bugs, the game isn't very buggy at all (at least in my experience), I only ran into 2 bugs, 1 where I got stuck and another where the visual of my gun got displaced.These bugs weren't game breaking, the only crash I had was after I beat the game so the game seems incredibly stable.To finish of this review I'd like to say:I recommend this game if you're looking for a fun and wacky shooter with a fun cast of characters and mechanics, don't expect this to be a dark souls type game, it isn't!

_childDocuments_.review: I was really excited for High on Life when I bought it, thinking it was an interesting concept for a shooter game and believing it would be one of the funniest games I'll ever play (it was), but I was actually left a little disappointed. When I say I "recommend this game", I only recommend it  for a multitude of reasons. To make it absolutely clear, my thoughts have nothing to do with the drama around Justin Roiland shortly after this game came out and are 100% based on the merits of the game itself. The case has long been closed and his charges were dropped. Like my other reviews, this one will be split into five subsections: Graphics, Audio, Gameplay, Story, and Conclusion/Final thoughts. Without further ado, let's begin.This game's graphics are very impressive for a cartoon game. The different worlds are highly detailed and sprawling with alien life, especially the MASSIVE hub world, Blim City. The guns you obtain throughout are all very different looking to each other, giving them a lot of character with just their designs and also making it obvious what guns you're using with just your peripheral in stressful combat situations. Most aliens you come across in this game look straight out of Rick and Morty, which is great for the large amount of people who got the game because Justin Roiland was behind it.Audio was similarly well-handled. Because the guns themselves are aliens, I like the touch of not making them sound like guns, but instead giving them strange or sometimes gross noises when shooting or reloading. I think it's funny that they all have different personalities and talk to you while you're fighting or exploring, and they're all pretty likeable.This game is unbelievably fun, despite how horrifically short it is. The multitude of guns you collect all have a fully unique gameplay style you can learn to balance during combat to dominate enemies. A minor complaint I have is that there aren't very many regular enemy types, which is unusual mostly because the game is a boss-rush style experience with lots of unique bosses, but the very small amount of content in this game is also a factor in this. Shooting off the goo armor on enemies is satisfying, and the sheer amount of silliness around every corner, even in combat, makes the gameplay experience one of the most hilariously enjoyable I've had in a while. Also a spoiler-heavy, very minor, and very petty other complaint I have is that  In all seriousness, however, another big issue is the complete lack of post-game content. You pretty much just grab achievements, find all of the lugloxes, get all of the upgrades for the guns, and do the very short easter egg side quest. That's the game. I did almost all of this in ~11 hours, rounded up, and I don't think it would be higher than 13 hours if I 100 percented the game. From what I've heard from others, the game has a substantial amount of major, unpatched glitches, but I can't confirm this myself. If you have a gaming setup that can run bigger games at least decently, you probably don't have anything to worry about.The shortness of this game is in part due to it being entirely story-driven. I think the story is  nothing spectacular. If you like Rick and Morty, you'll like this story because it's quite similar thematically. There weren't any characters I hated particularly, though the game being short makes the characters a little two-dimensional and basic. Overall, this game is most definitely the funniest game I've played, and I think the big focus on humor sets this title apart from so many other shooters. As a spoiler-free TL;DR, in a sudden alien attack on earth, you're roped into becoming a bounty hunter against an alien drug cartel after picking up a sentient alien gun. You slowly pick off each big wig in the operation, and collect other guns along the way. Kenny, the main blue gun, has a great deal of character development throughout the story, which on one hand is great, but also leaves a lot of development to be desired from the other guns. The last two guns you get in the game actually have interesting backstories, but never get the chance to build on that backstory, which is understandable but still disappointing. Overall, pretty good but heavily suppressed by the length of the game.Overall, the game is absolutely hilarious and extremely fun start to finish, but it's WAY too short for the price. The fact that there's games out there you can get hundreds of hours out of, for equal or less price than this game, makes it very hard for me to fully recommend this game. On sale it's a decent deal; at full price it absolutely is not. Please don't spend 60 dollars on it.All in all, I give High on Life a final rating of:

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyable shooter, with some great jokes here and there, excellent voice acting throughout, and TOO MUCH Justin Roiland. Requires a sense of humor to enjoy. You can assume that the vast majority of those negative reviews you've been reading come from essentially one place. The game's world building is largely excellent, done with a lot of care, and it shows everywhere. Each of the planets you explore are large, have a ton of content to see and do, and reward exploration. Gunplay is for the most part excellent and had yet to get old by the time I was done with it. The weapons are weird and varied, with excellent voice acting from the entire cast, but they DO talk a bit too much. If they didn't repeat the same lines it would be less annoying, but...they do. An example: If you want to move through the game quickly, you'll sprint a lot, and the game notices when you're sprinting a lot, and whichever gun you're using at the time will say something along the lines of "WOAH SLOW DOWN THERE BUDDY HOLY ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ♥♥♥♥ WHY NOT TAKE A LOOK AT THE WORLD AROUND YOU HUH?" and there's about 2-3 of those lines per gun, and they repeat them frequently. It gets old, fast. Copy and paste that scenario for situations like "you're almost dead", "you're doing really well in this fight", "you've been in the air for more than 3 seconds", "you've activated the jetpack", etc. Despite all that, you CAN turn off those lines of dialogue. This way the guns will only speak story-related lines, and you won't have to hear their incessant ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ every minute or two. I should add, also, that that annoying "feature" is very much the worst part of the game. Other than that, it's great. I had a legitimately fun time with it, and I hope it does well enough to warrant a sequel, although that's looking less likely as time goes on. Also, Justin Roiland is simply no longer involved at Squanch, in television, or in any other large-scale multimedia industry, so even if they do make a sequel, it *probably* won't be as good...unless they get Dan Harmon to write it. Anyway, if you can get it on sale, do. It's good. Assuming you have a sense of humor.

_childDocuments_.review: High on Life is an adventure-FPS that throws you, your sister, and your entire house onto an alien planet. To get back to Earth and save humanity from bizzare fate, you become a galactic bounty hunter, meeting quirky locals and acquiring sentient alien weapons along the way. The story is delightfully bizarre, with moments of charm, but it can sometimes feel a bit forced, with long unskippable dialogues.The real standout of High on Life is the weapons. Each gun has its own distinct personality and actively comments on the action, adding a fun layer to combat. While the weapon variety is limited (only 5), each one serves a unique purpose in both battles and exploration. The world is packed with cleverly hidden secrets, but only a few reward you with rare and useful weapon mods.Unfortunately, the shooting mechanics are pretty basic and clunky, though they improve slightly as you gather more weapons and mods. If you're not a fan of the Rick & Morty-style humor — crude, grotesque, and often hit-or-miss — this game might not be for you, as the gameplay itself is pretty barebones.Oddly, there's no manual save system, which is a frustrating oversight. Overall, High on Life is a parody of FPS games with plenty of dialogue, but unless you're in for the wackiness, the gameplay won’t hold up on its own.I recommend it, but only at a heavy discount.

Most of the time in "difficult" areas it is more spam of moves and gunfire. If you just hide behind a wall every 5 seconds to regenerate your health it is a push over. There are some areas that are enemy spam to increase the damage. You can also just knife enemies when you break off some of their Goo Armor, you get armor back. Most of the upgrades and guns are pretty useless. I primarily used Kenny and Creature. Sweezy is good for some more mobile enemies and Gus is good for small Mites. Kenny and Creature alone will carry you through the game. There are health upgrades through the game and there are some jet pack upgrades. The upgrades are basically useless with what they do mostly, you can be fine they are there to make the game even easier. Jet Pack duration, Armor Capacity, Gatteral Capacity, and general upgrades for weapons. A great upside is the actual mods that the weapons have.  I would recommend this as a passive humor game but do not expect a difficult shooter, the game does not have that much playtime. I am missing 10 achievements after 22 hours of playing the game. _childDocuments_.review: I didn't hate High On Life and found it very funny at times, but I can't recommend it.I like FPS games, so I enjoyed the gameplay more than Trover Saves the Universe, but it's so-so compared to other shooters.  Some of the guns are good like Sweezy the rapid fire Gatlian, but others are very weak like Gus, which is one of the worst shotguns I've used in an FPS.  Others like Creature are interesting but situationally useful.  You do get a BFG-type gun but not until the very end.  There is also platforming and backtracking to open new areas like Metroid Prime.  I usually don't like platforming in an FPS most of the time, but it was fairly painless in this game.  Most of the backtracking feels optional because the game isn't that difficult and you don't need to find every powerup, so this aspect is more for achievement hunters.  Speaking of achievements, the game is still very buggy and I couldn't complete the last and most grindy one because it bugged out on me.  The game isn't unplayable but I think there has been only one patch that fixes stuff.The story is straightforward, so most of my enjoyment came from the characters.  A lot of them are pretty funny but some are annoying.  Sometimes the Gatlians (especially Kenny) talk too much but this can be adjusted in the options.  There is a lot of ad-libbed "let's throw poop at the wall until it sticks" humor that often fails, but there are also plenty of genuinely funny moments so I liked this aspect of the game.  The game is too short for the price.  You can finish the main game in about 10 hours and the rest is padded with collectible hunting, so it could have used another zone with more bounties.  One thing I did really like were the warp discs that create little interactive areas like a movie theater that plays full (and very cheesy) movies and a tiny world that is at your mercy.  All of these were very amusing.  Overall, High On Life is a mostly funny, but so-so FPS that is too short and has too many bugs to be worth its current price.

In my opinion $60 is a little much for this game, i believe $40 would be a better price but I still got my play value out of it.

Thankfully, you can lessen the frequency or mute them all together in the options menu if you find it "too much". I had the enemy and gun talk to "occasional" and it was the perfect for me. Overall, the game was memorable with a few jokes that landed well. There were some scenarios that were hilarious like . Would recommend this game especially if you can get it on sale - it's a pretty good way to spend 10-15 hours if you just want to shoot talkative aliens.+ Decent time to finish. Around 10 to 12 hours so it doesn't become tedious+ Good selection of the main guns - all have their own personality and charm+ Some of the location designs are breathtaking and screenshot-worthy!+ Some decent Easter eggs like 4 full old movies you can watch in the game (TV or theater)- The voice actor for the MC's sister was just annoying. _childDocuments_.review: SPOILER FREE REVIEW!!!In 13 hrs I've beaten the made game and the DLC so decided to make a review about my experience.First thing first, the game itself is incredible and has so many good moments, to where you will at least laugh (and/or chuckle) a solid 10 times. The gameplay is honestly not that bad and the movement you can pull of is quite satisfying. The worlds you travel to all have a unique look and the NPC's actually have different dialog depending on where you are and what part of that world your in. If you like Rick and Morty, you will love this game without a doubt. Pros:.You can play anyway you want that being fast or more slow and chill.Every NPC feels unique so the game doesn't feel boring or repetitive when it comes to NPCs.Different weapons have different personalities With the player and other beings .Big world for you to explore.Game never feels like its against you and feels balancedCons:.If your an achievement hunter then good luck as there are like 400 collectables (no joke).Dialog can be annoying as there is A LOT of talking but you might not mind it like myself (also you can change it in the settings!).Some quest require you to constantly go back and fourth (specifically the DLC) Which can be very annoying and tedious.Some items in the store cant be bought which kind of feels like a slap in the face.This game gets you completely immersed leading to you probably forgetting the time of day ( I'm serious, its a issue!!)That's pretty much it, If i had to rate this game it would be a very solid 8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Haha look at this guy making fart noises, isn't that funny? Please listen to him make fart noises for another 5 minutes. Our game is funny and quirky, I swear!Most of the humor in this game is extremely stale and unfunny. Whenever the game tells a good joke, they repeat it over and over and over again and I can't decipher why the devs thought that was a good idea. It's almost as if they think their audience is too stupid to understand the joke the first time so they repeat it an extra 10 times in a slightly different way just to make sure you got it. And I'm saying this as someone who enjoyed most Rick and Morty episodes, so it's not like I went into the game expecting to hate it.The gameplay is okay I guess, the movement isn't great and the last few guns completely ruin the game by either being way too good despite requiring zero effort to use or by being terrible. The first two guns are well balanced and actually fun to use though, especially with mods equipped.I am thoroughly disappointed with how small this game is. A shooter with only 4 guns (I'm excluding the last one for obvious reasons) is kinda lame. And there are only like what, 4 planets to explore? And it's not like you're exploring much on those planets, you explore a few notable locations and that's basically it. I don't want this to sound like whining, but I expect more content from a full-priced AAA game nowadays. Even Outer Worlds, another space game that I believe is way too short, has much more to explore than this game.I don't recommend buying High On Life unless you enjoy the humor, but even then, I'd wait for a sale. This game just doesn't offer enough content for the price.

However, the game duration is also pretty short, which makes this less an issue.

_childDocuments_.review: Whether it's on Steam, Google, YouTube or Facebook, phrases like this can be found everywhere:“A must have for any Rick and Morty fan! Anyone who likes Rick and Morty will love this game!”But that is just phrase-mongering and I simply can't confirm this statement, and it goes even further because I have to give the game a very special award at this point, namely the one for the biggest disappointment in recent years.I could have gone into great detail about what's good and bad, but I have something else in mind, and the game is only recommended when it's on sale, when you have nothing else to play and without considering getting the DLC! So this review is dedicated to all Rick and Morty fans, especially to those who share Jerry's mind.Once upon a time there was this production venture called: Comic Sacrifice, and one of the things they did back then was a Back to the Future parody called: The Real Animated Adventures of Doc and Mharti. And I still remember that time very well, even if it was a while ago. It was 2006 and I had decided to move to Berlin and was preparing everything for it. That same year we had the Soccer World Cup Series here in Germany, which I gave a damn about, the term “caricature controversy” came third in the Word of the Year poll, which was interesting for someone who was also politically involved.That year saw the release of new and groundbreaking music by Stone Sour, Slayer, Pearl Jam, J Dilla, Puplic Enemy, Busta Rhymes, Cut Chemist and DJ Shadow. Some very interesting movies were also released that year like: A Scanner Darkly, Tenacious D, Borat, Silent Hill and Idiocracy. And not to forget to mention my video game highlights of 2006: Marc Ecko's Getting Up, Black, Me & My Katamari, Worms Open Warfare, Dead Rising, Def Jam Fight for NY and Gears of War.The Real Animated Adventures of Doc and Mharti came out in October, but I saw it in December on New Year's Eve. A friend of mine that I knew from a skatepark was at his aunt's house in California and yelled to me that his cousin showed him something funky and wanted my opinion on it. This friend knew that I had a wide range of interests and that I was into serious things but also had a fable for crude humor. So at the end of 2006, when the tenth season of South Park had just ended, I watched this strange stuff and didn't really know what to say at first. The friend said, just give me 2 words, the first two you can think of, so I said: mindless diarrhea. We laughed a lot and changed the topic, because it just wasn't worth talking about it anymore. Rick and Morty could only become so successful and popular because almost everything was changed and very likely a few people were involved who could bring a certain mix of professionalism and experience to the table. And this gave a rise to the following features:1. The series combines black humor, satire and absurd situations that are often unexpected and surprising,which mixture is particularly appealing to an adult audience.2. The main characters especially Rick Sanchez, are multi-layered and show both ingenious and destructive sides. This depth makes the characters interesting and comprehensible.3. Each episode offers new, often crazy adventures in different dimensions. This variety keeps the series fresh and exciting.4. It also deals with existential questions and philosophical themes, often in a humorous and accessible way. This gives the series an additional depth that appeals to many viewers.5. Rick and Morty contains numerous references to pop culture, science and classic science fiction, which makes it attractive to a wide audience.6. The eye-catching and unmistakable animation style also contributes to the appeal of the series. To be completely honest, High On Life is closer to The Real Animated Adventures of Doc and Mharti than to Rick and Morty and that's what bothered me the most. There's hardly any humor in it, 90% of it is just stupid, pointless and annoying nonsense. The gameplay is repetitive and not very innovative and the game suffers from many bugs and performance problems.The story falls short of the potential the game could have had and as a result the game feels unfinished. The soundtrack isn't bad, but it doesn't really match the atmosphere of the game, there's no gripping story and the controls are often imprecise and clunky, this also makes the price an absolute outrage.

_childDocuments_.review: Looking at  in my library, I was thinking to myself: "Hey, I haven't played a AA/AAA shooter for a while now, and this one looks like a weird take on that, with the talking guns and everything. That should be fun, right?"About 4 hours into it, I guess I was wrong.It's definitely not because of the graphics. The art direction is interesting, blending a sci-fi setting, the trademark Rick & Morty goofy and weird aliens, and stylized, cartoonish models. The environments are rich in detail and colorful. So detailed, in fact, that you get a dedicated button you can press to see where you need to go due to all the visual clutter.The gameplay could be a part of it. High on Life seems to be trying to emulate the more recent Doom titles with a combination of fast-paced shooting and platforming. Unfortunately, the shooting part feels really lightweight and "floaty", for lack of a better term. This may improve later on in the game, but there's just no feeling of heft or kick when using the default gun.The platforming is also a little off, due to that same feeling of weightlessness, and the visual clutter I mentioned above. There's not really much of a point to it either - outside a few story-driven moments, the only platforming you'll be doing is trying to reach loot chests, and the loot simply isn't worth the hassle.I feel like the writing is the main culprit here. Like my friend said when we were talking about the game, it's as if you're waiting for a punchline that never actually comes. The humor boils down to the game trying to shock you in lame and predictable ways, or the characters pointing out how weird the situation is.As for the characters, they're never not talking. So much so, there's a slider in the settings that lets you adjust the amount of gun and enemy chatter. Pro tip: The default amount is pretty annoying.If you're a die-hard fan of Rick & Morty, this one will probably be right up your alley. As for me, I dipped out somewhere between seasons 2 and 3, so High on Life isn't really doing anything for me. If the gameplay was a bit more satisfying, I could probably sit through it, but as it is, it's just not worth my time.

_childDocuments_.review: You can tell this game developers have never gamed in their entire life, the "game" is not actually a game, it's just a movie where you are the one to choose when to end the scene and go to the next one.Game is super linear, there is an illusion that it's an open world at the start by showing you a shop and currency but the more you play you discover every side exploration is only a chest containing +100g if you're lucky, sometimes you find nothing.You might think the jokes are funny at start but really gets dull after a while, gun screaming at your face over and over with the same voice pitch, no character development or personality change... you get different gun after while but they won't shut up either. All the characters are written so shallow you can be described them in their entirety in one sentence.Your character being silent 24/7 and giving all the dialogue to your gun is so boring, why did they even bother letting us understand aliens if we're literally never gonna interact?Gameplay is so easy even on highest difficulty, the aliens aim worse than stormtroopers, they rarely hit! and then each alien you kill drops you fat health pack to keep you alive... I know this game is supposed to be not-serious-funny type of game, but I thought I might as well mention it since it failed in the 'funny' department for me.So overall we have poor combat, same jokes repeated 10 times an hour, and 0 characters depth, linear story,  nvm, refunded. I would only buy this on 80-90% sale, and only for a child to play.

_childDocuments_.review: Upon first wanting this game I thought it would be worth playing mainly for the comedy aspects of the game, and whilst that still is the big selling point, the game-play is actually pretty good too.Combat is smooth and you can engage with fights however you want and with whichever guns you want (each of the guns allows for a very different play style). If you even want to switch styles during fights you can simply just switch to one of your other guns. The freedom in combat and how fluid it feels is really good, and on top of this the jet-pack, magnet boots and rope/grapple swinging system makes movement in general (and during combat) really fun to use.I found myself pulling off some crazy stunts in midair and killing the same enemy with different shots from different guns.The game is not too difficult, I think my only death in my entire campaign was accidentally jumping off the map.The game is kind of an open zone game, if you have played the EA single player Star Wars games, it is similar to that. But there is loads to do in each of the planets that you can travel to.After finishing the game there is still loads of really interesting (and funny) stuff to do and I will for sure be going back soon and getting all the warp discs.The warp discs are the highlight of the game in my opinion, but I'm not going to explain what they are in this review as I think it's best for it to be a surprise for players!8.5/10

name: Melatonin
detailed_description: Melatonin is a rhythm game about dreams and reality merging together. It uses animations and sound cues to keep you on beat without any intimidating overlays or interfaces. Harmonize through a variety of dreamy levels containing surprising challenges, hand-drawn art, and vibrant music. Melatonin explores the relationship between the dreams we have when we’re asleep and the experiences we go through when we’re awake, through unique rhythm game levels. Hand-drawn in a colorful and detailed visual style, with music produced to flow hand-in-hand with the gameplay and visuals, you will piece together elements about the main character’s life as you dive deeper and deeper into their dreams at night. Features Discover over 20 dreamy levels spread across 5 chapters, with every level introducing a new song. Unlock a Hard Mode that will truly test your rhythm. Experience Melatonin from a new perspective by unlocking fun level Mashups. Make the rhythm game level of your dreams with an easy to use Level Editor. Use Practice Mode to guide you through each level. Try out plenty of assist features if you’re feeling lost.

_childDocuments_.review: I think this game's amazing, but it's not for everyone, so here's a rundown of things you'll want to consider: Sets of 4 minigames that lead into a remix which combines them all into a single song.  It's arguably not as hard as Rhythm Heaven (definitely not as hard as the challenge train, thank god), and it doesn't have as much visual variety, but it's basically the same otherwise. I'm not usually one for comparing games, but it's pretty clear to me that this is what they were going for. That's because they've cut all the fat: every minigame is fun, every song is a bop and there's nothing else that gets in the way of enjoying those two things. That also means that, if you beat all the levels first try (which isn't too hard, even without accessibility options), the game's about an hour long. You can perfect all the levels and their hard mode versions, which'll tack on a couple more hours (wildly varying by skill level), but the main content is the game is short and sweet. There are plans for "fun new twists on existing levels" in future updates, but it's unclear what these are or how much they'll add. There would be custom levels to add more content, but... It only allows for editing the vanilla tracks, has no way to preview the song or start from halfway through, has no way to export created levels and has limited/finnicky cues. For example, the cues in Desires have a set time between picking up and dropping (either 1 beat or 5 beats), and cannot be manually adjusted. However, there are plans to update the game to add custom music support and to allow for making remixes: I can only hope that these updates will also flesh out the editor to make it more user-friendly. Most of the story/conflict is implied through the subject of every minigame, as well as short intro and outro sequences between each chapter/remix. What's there is pretty good, but don't go in expecting a story-heavy game: it's a rhythm game first and foremost, and it's better for it.Otherwise, the game's basically perfect! It has a clear focus and vision and succeeds with flying (pastel) colours; the dev team should be proud of how well it turned out.oh and add V-Sync please, it's driving me nuts not having it

_childDocuments_.review: After fully completing the game 3 ring and starring all levels I have a quite a few things to say. Overall the game is probably the best rhythm game I have ever played (over 20+ rhythm games played: thumper, osu, beatsaber, rockband, rhythm heaven, just dance, necromancer etc). With a previous gaming background of more competitive scene games like league of legends, CSGO, Valorant, and old call of duty (MW, BO era), this brought back those feelings of joy where I could play for hours at a time. Unfortunately the new games do not provide that for me anymore (new mario games, pokemon, call of duty, etc)The music and animations work perfectly with the music, and you can tell the developer took their time to choose sound effects, music, and animations that would match the overall vibe of Melatonin. The levels are well made, and satisfying to play, I found myself never really frustrated (when calibrated properly which I will get into), and just found myself fully immersed in the game. I have been phasing out of gaming, but this game brought back those good memories and feelings of wanting to fully complete a map or a game no matter how long it takes.TLDR: The art is wonderful, music chosen well, everything was done with a purpose, and I haven't enjoyed a game this much since Covid-19 (last one was probably Celeste) 9.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Melatonin is a simple rhythm game, with a focus on ease of gameplay and calmer sounds.If you're expecting something on the tougher or more upbeat side, this ain't it.  Ironically, I had more fun as I stopped focusing on scoring well, and more fun when I was just feeling the music and half-asleep.  The sounds and songs are quite relaxing lol.On the shorter side of games, it still delivers an enjoyable experience in what it offers. The timing is a *little* on the forgiving side, and there are even accessibility options if you need a little more help, such as timing circles, metronome, and a bigger Perfect window.  If you'd rather go for a challenge, a Perfect only option is also available.Controls are quite simple, using  3 directional keys and an action key (Space by default). In each tutorial, you're told whether you'll need to hit directional keys or the action key, and whether they're held or not, as well as general timing.  For some stages, the instructions don't give you as good an idea as the tutorial itself/timing circles do (Work and Time levels for me).  All good, but in some levels you get tempo changes in the middle of the song that can throw you a bit off, especially if you're just grooving to the audio cues... when you can hear and distinguish them.  Unfortunately, there are a few levels where the audio cues are either far too similar to each other, or happen too quickly to react to.  This can be a bit of a bummer, as I prefer working off audio for rhythm games, as their focus should be lol.  While Melatonin doesn't bring a whole lot to the table, it doesn't need to.  Less is more here, and the art and sound direction definitely hit their target.Relax.

Some requires you to remember patterns, listen/see for clues, actively pressing keys or, waiting for rare actions.+ Practice mode for each level that explains level mechanics.+ Normal and hard difficulty for each level — with more tricky patterns and fast tempo.+ Pleasant graphics and music.+ Accessibility options.= Note, that completing whole game (normal+hard) is taken only ~.= The game has a very : perfect actions gives a score multiplayer, but each an early/late action breaks it, and misses removes scores. _childDocuments_.review: Have you ever played Rhythm Heaven? I haven’t, so you won’t hear too many comparisons to it here, but if you do know the game then I suppose it’s my obligation to tell you that lots of people are saying  But what does that mean, exactly? Well, read on and you’ll find out!In Melatonin, you play through the unnamed main character’s dreams. Most of the gameplay is divided into 4 nights. Each night is divided into 4 levels that can be accessed via a mini overworld of sorts, and a 5th level that combines all 4 prior and switches between their gameplay. Speaking of  You have three buttons you can press: left, right and center (which is the one you’ll be using the most). Sometimes you’ll be prompted to press left/right together, or long press any combination of those three. That’s it. You need to accumulate 8 stars to unlock the 5th level each night, and the rings are just for bragging rights.  If you hit a note in time with the beat/visual cue, you get the perfect rating, which awards you the most points. Late/early award you less points, and missing actually LOSES you points. Score is your standard game mode, and hard is pretty much the same stage/melody as score, but harder and with variations in the patterns. These are the gamemodes that award you the star/ring rewards, and in fact, you need two stars in any given level to unlock its hard mode. Tutorial is basically what you would expect: it teaches you how to play the level. See, each level boils down to a rhythm game, sure, but they have different melodies and patterns coming at you, and the tutorial aims to teach exactly that. On the standard accessibility settings, once you play on the “real” gameplay modes, which are score and hard, you don’t really get help. You don’t get an indicator on your screen telling you to press A at the right moment, no no no. You HAVE to recognize audiovisual cues and react to them at the right time, which is precisely why the tutorial is so important. And at the same time, it’s also why the game can be so hard. You can easily see examples of this in what are likely to be your very first levels played: dream about food and dream about shopping.In dream about food, you have boxes of different types of food throwing, well, food at you. They have three attack patterns, all of which are, in fact, timed with different beats of the song, but you can also just as easily click A when you see the food pretty much on top of your character. That’s how I got through both score and hard mode with pretty good ratings. In dreams about shopping, however, you have objects falling in a specific order with specific timing between each object. Once the full collection has fallen, you have to then swipe your credit card following the same timing in which they fell. Unlike the food dream, that shows the food reaching the character, here you have to rely on your feeling and on the beat of the song. This made things a lot harder for me.Some levels also have obstacles such as clouds that show up and cover part of the screen or visual cues that randomly leave the screen for a while, which makes things even harder depending on the level. I fully acknowledge that this is a me issue, so I’m not complaining. I’m just saying all this to illustrate that  There are 5 different assists. All of them can be individually turned on and off, allowing you to fully customize your difficulty. The options are: visual assist with the timing circle, audio assist with a metronome, increasing the window of time you can hit the button to get a perfect, less penalty for early/late hits and controller rumble, on by default. There’s honestly no shame in turning any of these on: at the end of the day, what matters is that you, as the player, enjoy yourself, especially with a game that looks and sounds this cozy. and fully fits the dream aesthetic they were going for. The game looks amazing, and I can not stress this enough.  The tracks are vibrant, and they mostly work really well with the levels. I won’t lie that there were a few moments in which I felt like beats didn’t align with when I had to press the buttons, but I’m pretty sure that’s on me and my apparent inability to properly perceive sounds sometimes. Seriously though, words do this soundtrack no justice, so go watch the trailer! You can infer a lot about the main character via his dreams and the little cutscenes you get between nights of him and his room, but that’s about it. While it IS really cool to learn about him via his worries and desires and the environmental storytelling of his room, the fact is that the story is mostly there to introduce the gameplay, which is absolutely the focus here.  I did, however, feel a bit of a disconnect between the mood of the game and its difficulty. I was absolutely expecting a comfy and cozy experience by the beats and the visuals, but instead I was massacred by a lot of the levels. This isn’t an issue, mind you, as you can adjust difficulty via the accessibility options I mentioned, but it was still quite a shock for me. And if you have epilepsy, beware, as the game does contain flashing lights and an epilepsy warning. There’s no effective tutorial for it, it doesn’t allow you to switch songs, you can only use the set pieces and obstacles that are within that specific level, and you can’t even export your levels. There is a chance they will update the editor to make it more universal, though, so check back in a few weeks! It’s a joy to play through, provided the difficulty doesn’t frustrate you and you’re not too proud to turn on the accessibility options. If you’re curious about the length, the game took me about 3 hours to beat to the end of the “story”. I did not get 3 stars/rings on every level, and I turned on the help for some levels. If you do end up getting the game, let me know how you like it!

_childDocuments_.review: My only complaint with this game is that there seems to be a bit of input lag which I think unfortunately comes down to slightly inconsistent frame timings. This means that even if you adjust the latency offset in settings you still end up missing hits because sometimes they're early and other times they're late. It's incredibly difficult to get perfect hits on just about every level without turning on the increased time windows, and even then it can still be tricky. I wanted to make sure I wasn't just out of practice with rhythm games so I booted up Rhythm Heaven Fever and tried some osu and didn't have this problem.This is really just an unfortunate issue with using Unity's default input and audio systems, if the game instead played the audio itself and received input events from the OS then piped that info over to the engine for rendering then this likely wouldn't be an issue.I think it would likely be worth looking into that as a solution if there's ever to be a sequel or DLC pack, it's some engineering work but there's definitely resources out there on how to use natives within Unity.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game as a massive fan if the Rhythm Heaven series, which I believe made have partly inspired this game. I find the minigames here  to be in-and-of themselves quite enjoyable, and would recommend them for their replayability.However, on the first playthrough of many minigames, I found the Practice mode to be rather lacking in ways that the Rhythm Heaven series did somewhat better. I'm currently on Night 3 and have encountered issues numerous with the Practice stages for a large number of the minigames so far, which can be summed up as follows:1. Practices fail to explain all cues: In this game, the tutorials only explain the mechanics in text form at the beginning of the Practice, giving only a vague sense of how the minigame works. While "learning by doing" is hypothetically a good thing, the problem comes from the fact that in the Practice, not all cues are explored. For example: in "Space", the practice session introduces only the regular speed and slow cues, not the fast cue, resulting in the player being incredibly likely to completely miss the input when they first see it in the actual game. This is a flaw in my eyes, as I feel that player should be able to understand what the inputs and cues actually are when they have completed the tutorial and not be surprised by this element in the actual game.2. Practices are too long: The tutorials in this game are rather long and feature repetitive gameplay. The intention of the developers is clear, give the player time to get used to a minigame's simplest cue, then move on to the next cue and give them time to practice that and so on until the end of the practice session. My problem with this is that, as mentioned above, not every cue is given time at all, in which case why bother going on this long, but second, the practices don't take feedback from the player input whatsoever. They give you a certain number of attempts at one cue dictated by a timer before moving onto the next, whether you are ready or not. In Rhythm Heaven, each cue is given its own allotted time as in Melatonin, but the game does not advance to the next cue until you have demonstrated understanding of the previous one. Thus, when the player reaches the real game, they are well prepared to play it well, as the game ensures that player of any skill level will have had the time that they in particular need understand the controls. I am well aware that this tutorial design I am advocating for can be frustrating in-and-of itself for some players. I've seen RTGame's Monkey Watch tutorial gameplay and have myself gotten stuck on Lockstep's tutorial in Rhythm Heaven Megamix for a time. However, I feel that letting player get their frustrations about the controls out in a space designated for the purpose is better than making it occur in the actual minigame. I personally wish to be challenged on my actual ability to follow the rhythm and cues and not on my conscious ability to know what the controls actually are during the game. On the flipside is the case where the player is skilled enough to understand a cue and its inputs very quickly. The amount of time Melatonin spends on a single cue can be a bit excessive for me personally. I got the first cue for the very first minigame, "Food" down almost instantly, and grew bored of repeating it over-and-over, and so skipped the remainder of the tutorial, not realizing there was another cue in it I had yet to learn (which I concede was not a wise decision). By not taking the player's skill level into account, and moving to the next cue once a player has demostrated understanding of the previous one, you risk boring them, as happened with me here. In summary: I would like to see tutorials that adapt to the player's skill level rather than just putting them on a timer as was done here.3. Forced accessibility features during the Practice: The forced usage of both the visual and auditory guides during the tutorials can at times interfere with observing the actual cues of the minigame. Take for example "Mind" in this level the visual guide is placed directly on top of the visual cue in the center of the screen and the metronome makes it hard to hear the actual audio cue for the real game. Which I absolutely appreciate the inclusion of these accessibility features, I find them quite distracting for learning the actual cues of a minigame and wish there were an option to disable their appearance during Practice in the settings.These last two are absolutely my subjective option, and can largely be considered just my personal taste, but I would like to mention them anyway.4. Repetitive music: Melatonin does not use a dedicated piece of background music for the Practice session nor does it use a re-instrumentation of the minigame's actual theme. Instead, it typically uses the music for the intro section of the actual minigame or a slightly sparser version of it. I personally find the this makes the beginning of most minigames to be somewhat boring, and they sound and play exactly like the Practice, which I already think are too long. 5. Occasional required use of visual cues: One element of Rhythm Heaven that I personally really enjoy is the ability to play the game without even looking at it, as all of the cues are (most of the time anyway) entirely based on sounds, either in the BGM or sound effects. This makes for a very smooth and fun experience that I can play without needing to keep my eyes glued to the monitor. Not every minigame in Melatonin can be played this way, (though most can). Take, for example, "Time". this level has three different cues, and two of them sound completely identical to me (though this may just be due to my lack of a headset).All in all, Melatonin is project quite clearly made with passion and is a great new entry in the recent resurgence of rhythm minigame collections, however I personally was dissatisfied with the tutorials, and as a result did not have as much fun as I could have on my first playthroughs of most minigames.

_childDocuments_.review: My feelings towards Melatonin are ambivalent. On one hand, it is very well presented, showcasing a lot of love and care in its development. However, the gameplay itself felt somewhat uninspired and overall too easy.When comparing this game to the Rhythm Tengoku/Rhythm Heaven series, the gameplay feels somewhat lacking. The player-actions lack variety and, more importantly, hindered my ability to achieve a flow state. While some levels, like "Dream about Desires" and "Dream about Stress" came close to achieving that state for me, the majority of levels required me to actively pay attention to audio-visual signals, which disrupted my flow. Contrasting "Dream about Nature" with Rhythm Heaven Gold's level "Crop Stomp" highlights this difference clearly. In the Hard-Mode of "Dream about Nature", my attention was solely focused on listening for audio cues instead of feeling the rhythm, which left me unsatisfied.Another aspect where Rhythm Heaven excels is in its Remix levels. In Melatonin, the different segments feel disconnected, lacking the seamless transitions found in Rhythm Heaven. Rhythm Heaven often introduces a new mechanic in one segment and follows it up with the next segment building upon it. This kind of connection is absent in Melatonin.Additionally, I found the content of Melatonin to be a bit lacking. It took me just over 2 hours to beat every level on Hard, even with collecting at least two Saturn Rings (?). Considering the game's price of 15€, this feels a bit steep.Another minor nitpick is that I was not able to rebind my controller buttons. This might not sound necessary on first look, however I played this game with an Arcade layout controller, where due to the button-layout of fighting games the R button is to the left of the L button. I did some custom rebinding with Steam Input, this feature should be in the main game however.I believe Melatonin has the potential to be a great game. Its visuals and sound design are fabulous, and I appreciate the story that players can interpret from the character's life. It effectively represents the anxieties of modern life. However, it falters in its gameplay, which is unfortunate.With reservation, I recommend Melatonin. It certainly has its strengths, but the gameplay sadly did not meet my expectations.
