_childDocuments_.review: Rating          9/10Gameplay     8/10The game being a rhythm game only has 3 buttons to press in different ways, yet from the 20+ levels none of them play similarly at all. Each single level feels like a unique experience, coming from the art and the songs. As I write this, I listen to the game's soundtrack which I refuse to pause. Most levels in the game managed to captivate me, all of them focusing on a specific aspect of our modern lives. Some are about dating apps while others are about meditating, which are things our protagonist dreams about. While I liked most of the levels and I did get my favorites ones there is a few I did not enjoy as much. The game knows this and does not expect you to master all your dreams. To progress through the game, you must receive a specific number of stars from the levels, but getting them only requires you to maybe do ok in all the levels or master one or two so the one that you might not have enjoyed as much can stay on the side. Aside from the basic ranking to progress through the game there is the master difficulty option for all the levels, in case you enjoyed specific songs more you can decide to attempt this difficulty. I appreciated how the game needs you to play all the songs correctly it does not want you to hit your head against the wall with parts you might not enjoy as much, which is great as so many other games force mechanics or parts of a game you might not enjoy as much down your throat. I do love how you need to play all the stages of the game since the final level of each night (chapter) are a combination of all the levels of that night. So being proficient on all the levels do comes around to test your skills, which is great. In general, the game trusts you to be skillful and stay on your toes but does not push you to your limits unless you want to.  The only reason I’m not giving the game 10/10 is simply the length, now I know how picky that might be especially since what we get is almost perfect. I say this due to the price point since I would have liked to have some more content. I also believe the game is not attempting to revolutionaze any type of gameplay since it’s mostly trying to explore some different ideas. It does something simple extremely well and that’s also ok. Art 10/10I would be doing a dishonor to the game if I didn’t mention the art. The game has obviously a dreamy-like feeling, beautifully hand-drawn illustrations, and animations are present in every corner of your eye. The game has a beautiful purple hue that makes you feel as if you are floating, which is obviously the goal. Each night has a specific change and theme that our protagonist has for the week. The changes may be small or if you are playing quickly you might not notice, which is why I believe playing the game slowly is a requirement to fully immerse yourself on the game. When I first started a level the first thing I would notice was the art and the new dream the protagonist was having, that says a lot since I usually look forward a lot more towards the gameplay rather than the art itself. The positioning of objects around the levels, the bedroom of the protagonist feels perfectly positioned. I could easily imagine a person with those exact items surrounding their room. Which is a perfect segment for story segment of my review.Story 10/10Although at first the game might not seem to contain any story later on the game I started realizing how the themes of the levels were intentionally chosen. I do believe each person might hold very different interpretations of the game since there is nothing clearly stated one can be left to create their own story. I believe that is where the beauty is coming from the story how personal it is, probably from the designers and how personal it hits home, especially if you are a young adult in this modern world of ours. This is at least my interpretation of the story. Our protagonist is a young adult apparently living on his own, he seems to be facing some sort of mental health issues. For me, those mental issues are clearly anxiety, depression, stress, and perhaps a broken heart. The game never directly states any of this topics but it subtly hints what our main character is thinking, and is obsessed during the week which leads him to dream about specific things. Money, working out, the future and ambitions, the past etc. I also noticed how the dreams I enjoyed the most are the ones I identified the most with, and I think that works great since some people might have different favorite levels and obviously interpretations.X factor 10/10Some small spoilers in hereI think the most notable aspect of the game is how strong the message is for adults on their 20s with how much going on is so easy to be thinking about the future and the past. Buying a house, getting a car, dating, grieving. We simply have so much to keep ourselves busy with but how little time we are given for it. The X factor of this game is how incredibly deep it was for me by just simply presenting ideas that I even myself have without realizing. This game tells you how much your thoughts affect your dreams and vice versa. The ending of the game to keep it as spoiler-free as possible, plays with your expectations of the game design and it makes you wait that waiting time it makes you reflect on your thoughts, as we see the many dreams flashing across our eyes, many dreams we’ve all have it just lets you think about them, and it almost makes you think “what are you waiting for”.The game doesn’t have a fantastical ending where the world changes but neither does the start of the game, and I think that works in the favor of the experience. We can truly connect to the protagonist, we simply dream today and we will dream tomorrow….Final thoughtsWhile I believe this game won’t be for everyone, if you are into chill vibes, reflecting, dreams, and meditating you will love this game. I cannot wait to see what next games the developers might create.

_childDocuments_.review: Step into a world of beats, rhythms, dreams, and pastel colors as Melatonin invites you to groove to its game, where chill meets the quirky charm of lo-fi vibes. If you're into rhythm games like Osu! and Rhythm Heaven, this new entry might just be for you! On a side note, my sister and I spent seven hours playing and exploring each and every level of the game. Join me as I share our thoughts and impressions, inviting you to chill and groove along in this spoiler-free review!Released on December 16, 2022, Melatonin is an indie rhythm game developed by David Huynh, with “Half Asleep” as his game developer alias. In this genre, players press or hold buttons to match the beat of a song while enjoying unique visuals and soundtracks. Just like Nintendo’s Rhythm Heaven, Melatonin incorporates a similar style, yet distinguishes itself with a variety of levels, surprising challenges, captivating hand-drawn art, and vibrant music.As a fun tidbit, a game that was created by independent developers is known as an indie game!LO-FI SOUNDS AND PLEASING GRAPHICSAs we step into the pastel world of Melatonin, the game immerses you in a captivating audio and visual experience, especially for rhythm game lovers. The game welcomes you with a pastel aesthetic, featuring hand-drawn animations and a dreamy soundtrack that sets the perfect tone right from the start (I’ll leave that to you!). The consistent color palette throughout the game complements each visual element harmoniously. The cartoony and minimalistic art style adds a perfect touch of cuteness, matching the overall mood of the game. Moreover, the game introduces visual cues only for tutorial purposes. This approach allows players to immerse themselves in the visuals without the distraction of sudden circles and buttons popping up on their screens. Overall, the graphics are not only smooth but also well-designed, providing a satisfying experience for players.In line with the game's dream-focused theme, the lofi beats in the soundtrack not only enhance the gaming experience but also create a relaxing atmosphere, ideal for unwinding and even falling asleep in real life. Also, the soundtrack features a mix of original compositions and licensed tracks, which truly deserves its own Spotify playlist!SIMPLE, YET RELAXING STORYSadly, there isn't much of a plot in the game, but thankfully, the presentation is wonderful!In addition to the captivating visual and audio experience, the game's story unfolds with a soothing and relaxing presentation. Picture this: in reality, you're living your everyday life, but as you drift off to sleep on your couch, a world of fantastical moments unfolds in your dreams. These moments seamlessly blend your dreams and reality into a harmonious experience.In Melatonin, each night's dream becomes a game level, featuring different music and a unique mini-game. To complete the game, players must navigate through various stages across four nights and a grand finale. Also, at the last stage, there is a surprise awaiting!RELATABLE CHARACTERSurprisingly, the game features no other characters; instead, you take on the role of a hoodie-wearing guy who keeps falling asleep on his sofa, probably something we can all relate to when trying to sleep! Afterward, you jump into his dreams, each featuring distinctive mini-games. These mini-games reflect his likes or, perhaps, offer a glimpse into his life – covering everything from food, shopping, technology, desires, and more. As you have noticed, the main character appears lazy. However, the art style and pastel-color combinations truly bring out the cute and chill environment of the guy.PERSONAL OPINION AND RATINGIn addition to my previous review of the game, here are some pros and cons based on my observations and opinions.Pros:1. Addicting Soundtrack:Again, the game's soundtrack is fantastic, especially the calming lofi beats. It's so comforting that you'll want to play it on repeat, and the replay button deserves to get broken with this one!2. Replayability:The game offers a variety of levels and difficulties, which encourages the player to challenge themselves.3. Satisfying to nail a perfect timing:Once you master the perfect timing and get used to it, the gameplay and audio experience become truly satisfying. It immerses you in the soundtrack, allowing you to feel every beat.Cons:1. Some visual cues are offbeat:Throughout my playthrough, the tutorial was clear and easy to understand. However, in the actual game, hitting a perfect timing seems tricky. Even when you get the beat right, it is sometimes early or late. Paying extra attention to the animation timing is crucial, as some cues are offbeat, making it more challenging to achieve perfect timing.2. Story is short:I hope the game offers DLC or updates featuring different life situations or moments to explore more dreams. It would be great to see some storytelling or progression for the main character as well.Despite its pros and cons, Melatonin is undeniably an enjoyable game that brings a unique approach and experience to the rhythm game genre. It’s a game that can be enjoyed by people of all ages, thanks to its lofi sounds, pleasing graphics, simple yet relaxing story, and a relatable main character. Lastly, melatonin offers an unmissable experience for rhythm game lovers, casual gamers, or newcomers alike making it worth a try. With everything that has been laid out, I give it a well-deserved, once in a blue moon final verdict of 9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't go into this thinking it'll sate your Rhythm Heaven hunger, but it is a neat little game. That's not to say it's without fault, though. The call-and-response minigames, however, were usually the most fun to play.As for the difficulty, my perspective is a bit skewed since I went for a got Perfects on all songs/difficulties, but let me just say that there is a wide gap between the difficulty in beating some songs and getting all Perfects on them. Some of the levels, like "Followers" and "Time" are unfun because the inputs feel wrong, while levels like "Money (hard)" are ridiculously react-heavy, and are almost stress inducing when going for Perfect.I also felt the need to adjust the calibration between almost all of the levels, but particularly between ones with different inputs, i.e. arrow key inputs would feel fine, but then with the same calibration, press-and-hold space would feel floaty and bad.Overall, it's a fine little game, but in my opinion, outside of the "remix" levels at the end of each Night, none of the songs were particularly engaging, but if you're looking for a light game with a charming aesthetic, this should work.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good game! Not bad, not okay, not perfect, just... good :)The mechanics are interesting, and the aesthetic is adorable and cozy. The game does a great job of creating a motif, and then riffing on it just enough to keep it from getting stale, but not so much that it becomes too hard.The core gameplay is pretty formulaic: every chapter has 4 levels, and then a final level which combines them all, a la Rhythm Heaven remixes. Actually, quite a bit of the game draws inspiration from rhythm heaven, from the simple controls, level design, and overall structure. It's definitely a love letter to the series, and definitely scratches that itch.Unfortunately, such a strict adherence to the formula starts to feel very repetitive after a few chapters. The main place where this can be felt is the hard levels. Every level has 2 main modes: "scored" and "hard", pretty standard for the genre. I would have *loved* to see the hard levels take the mechanics that we learned in the scored mode, and put a new spin on them, or use them in more and interesting ways. Unfortunately, most if not all of the hard modes are faster versions of the scored mode, with slightly more complex rhythms, or taking away visual cues. Even the backing tracks are the same as the scored mode.I don't want it to seem like I'm dogging on the game at all. What's there is great! However, it still feels like it's missing a little something - something to bring everything together. I like the philosophy and the aesthetics of the game enough that it's motivation enough to play the game, but if you're looking for something to chew on, this probably isn't the game for you. If you'd rather have something small that you can play to wind down from the day, and not really think about? Melatonin does that pefectly.

_childDocuments_.review: Melatonin is a game inspired heavily by the Rhythm Heaven series. It's a rhythm game which fills a gap for those wanting another in that beloved series. But it also does a good enough job to stand out on it's own, really helping to make an identity from the shadow it's under. However, that isn't to say the game is perfect, but it's quite enjoyable where it needs to be.Visually speaking: stunning. While the game that it's working off of has a much more cartoony-style to it, the visuals in Melatonin have a more dreamy aesthetic to them. And, working with the music of each individual mini-game, crafts a truly wonderful playthrough that had me engaged from beginning to end.The music, obviously, is a key component to your one's ability to enjoy this title. For me, I found the short tracks to be rather charming and fitting the mood set in the game. There's a dreamlike quality to them, and the harder tracks knowing when to increase or decrease the tempo where it makes sense.The gameplay is, overall, fairly solid. There were a couple of the mini-games which left me questioning the beat it wants the played to work with. In addition, there aren't all-too-many to work with. However, with the quality that is present, and community that could craft something with the bones that are there, leaves a delightful product.For the price listed, it can be steep for some people. I have finished the game at a little over two hours. If I worked to perfect everything, I could squeeze a couple more out, but I don't think the average person would be looking to do that. If you're interested at all, I guarantee you will certainly get your money's worth, especially since you'll probably have an itch to come back or get better at that is there. However, if the price is a bit too steep, I would say keep an eye on it and grab it on sale. Finding a good rhythm game always puts a smile on my face and this is no different. A thumbs-up for fans of the genre!

_childDocuments_.review: In a nutshell: lo-fi Rhythm Heaven.Melatonin did an excellent job on accomplishing what it set out to do - being an approachable yet still challenging rhythm game. You start with playing each mini-game in isolation so you can learn its patterns, and by themselves they are fairly straightforward. And then the "boss" of each stage is a rapid-fire mix of all the mini-games you just played which really puts your reaction times and your understanding of each game to the test.Very fun experience with pleasant beats and cute visuals.
_childDocuments_.name: Melatonin

_childDocuments_.review: If you like rhythm heaven you'll probably like this game.The differences (not bad or good, just different):~I feel like Melatonin has less complex beats but puts more emphasis on accuracy. You have a combo meter on the side that breaks with an "early" or "late". They don't punish you too hard for it, but it's certainly not good. Thankfully they have a lot of options in the accessibility settings that can help with this.~ ACCESSIBILITY SETTINGS: honestly something I sincerely wish rhythm heaven had. Like optional visuals (moving circles like in practice mode), an audible metronome, and a button that gives you leniency on early/late. Also allows you to change input keys (extremely helpful).~Some audio cues feel extremely subtle or blend in with the song a little too well. I had a few stages where I couldn't tell if it was a cue or part of the song. I ended up relying on some visual cues for those levels even though I have a feeling that's not what they were going for. BUT, with practice it's something that you can detect better and again, they have really accommodating accessibility settings. ~Shorter game but puts effort into quality and hints at a story. While the money level was the most painful level for me (you're catching coins left and right, but when there's lightening, you need to press the opposite button ...and that melted my brain), I was impressed that I could hear the cue coming from the left or from the right side of my headphones depending on where the coin is falling. Did it help me clear the level? Not really, but I was impressed and excited nonetheless.Conclusion: If you like music games, definitely pick it up. There were some levels I couldn't stop replaying because I liked the music or gameplay of that level. You'll probably find your favorite in here too. (I found the faster pace of the hardmode levels to be easier at times, so always give it a shot!)

_childDocuments_.review: I don't actually like this game as a whole.Context: I play a lot of rhythm games from stuff like rhythm heaven, muse dash, and mobile idol games like bang dream and proseka so I like to think I'm pretty good at rhythm games but something about Melatonin just wasn't fun the entire time.I enjoyed certain levels and the music was great but to me a lot of the design elements didn't really work with the beat or rhythm and I genuinely couldn't tell where I was going wrong without turning on the visual circle guide and even then I couldn't tell if it was actually to the beat or not. Also this game is just really unforgiving which isn't always a bad thing but I didn't know this chill rhythm game was gonna soft lock me during the app level and I'd have to furiously tap my space bar to figure out the beat again cause I can't hear the actual music over the fact I'm suddenly missing every single note. It took me out of the experience and just made me frustrated.Another thing I was kind of iffy on was sometimes the accessibility aid wasn't very helpful at all. During the claw machine level the visual aid pops up out of nowhere and you have to have fast reactions in order to catch it even though all other visual aids have shown up at the bottom or near the bottom of the screen and made its way to the circle with time for you to prepare. I understand that it's supposed to be quick but why change your accessibility aid for that at all. I didn't struggle with that level but it threw me off guard.All in all I do recommend this game. I got it during the sale and honestly knowing now I'm glad I got it on sale but that's also just my opinion. I still do love all the music it's just the somewhat janky level design on certain levels that keeps me from fully loving this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a great fan of rhythm games such as Elite Beat Agents, Friday Night Funkin, and Rhythm Heaven, and Melatonin is a wonderful rhythm game as a lofi-cozy version of the latter. Levels feature different mechanics, whether you have to repeat rhythmic notes like in PaRappa the Rapper or tap to the incoming beat. Practice modes are like mini levels in themselves, to help you learn how to go through the level, with visual and audio cues that would really help you in figuring it out. -- On a personal level, I wish that Practice mode was nonstop, so that you could truly  to get the beats right before deciding to move on to scored/hard mode. There were a few levels where I finished the practice mode but was still unsure how to perfectly time my key presses. I wish I had more practice time, because I can say that I only got through some levels relying on the visual cues because I couldn't figure out the audio ones. The visuals are crazy aesthetic and yet wild as it captures how weird dreams can be. It looks great, and the music is top notch. It's hard to not bob your head to the beat while playing. The levels themselves are really fun to go through, and I love how lengthy these songs are as well, as it really lets you get into the groove of the song as you play. Some levels, as mentioned, miight have you rely on the visual cues more than others. Shame as I'd like to play this game blindfolded sometime.It's rather easy to get through the entire game in one sitting, but , it's gonna take you a good while to not only get 3 stars/rings on every level, and longer to get all of them perfect. For most players, I'd recommend to just finish the game, but for those that want to grind away to perfect these levels, I can say that Melatonin has a great replay value and it's really satisfying to perfect them (and very frustrating when you almost do heh)Had Melatonin on my wishlist for the longest time, and I'm glad to own it now. I'm excited to see what Half Asleep has to offer us, such as DLC or similar games. This is a definite recommend in my book.

_childDocuments_.review: 7.5/10When I first saw Melatonin on YouTube, I was immediately lured in by the art style. I love the color palette this game uses, and the overall "aesthetic" of this game is very satisfying. However, as a rhythm game, it is frustrating, to say the least. The first two nights are pretty good, with the first night being my favorite. However, once I got to the third night, things started to get very... "experimental"? The mechanics for a rhythm game, in my VERY inexperienced opinion, should be simple, on beat and consistent in its pattern. There should also be distinct audio queues to clue you in on when to strike the keys, NOT visual queues. A rhythm game should not have you rely on visual queues to strike the keys, lest the timing be off by a wide margin. I will say that the Exercise game was very enjoyable and quite challenging, however the Money game was not, the difference between the two eluding me at the moment. Once you got to the third night, it just became impossible to play. Mind is unrelenting in its unpredictability and its nonsensical mechanics. Time is alright, but the fact that there is no auditory difference between a fake out and a real trigger is very upsetting and makes it unnecessarily difficult. I have not progressed past those points because I cannot physically play Mind without rage quitting (whether that's because of my short temper or lack of experience with these games is up for debate). Overall, I've enjoyed it so far and will definitely try to advance, blood sweat and tears be damned. I think this game has incredible potential, and that future games this studio puts out will only continue to impress in style and improve in mechanics. For now, however, I give this game a solid 7.5/10.

name: They Always Run
detailed_description: The galaxy's inhabitants have been swamped by crime since the fall of the empire. Being able to find anyone, anywhere has become a highly prized skill. Aiden is a three-armed bounty hunter who must hunt down the most dangerous and elusive cutthroats in the galaxy. Some bounties are rewarded with money, others with valuable information that Aidan can use to find the people who set him on this path – all while getting embroiled in a galaxy-wide conspiracy. Having three arms lets you deal with more enemies at once and makes for a persuasive argument in any scuffle. Use your third arm to perform targeted attacks and throws, manipulate the environment, destroy obstacles, and wreck enemies. Hunt criminals across the fringes of the galaxy, the core worlds, and the ruins of long-gone civilizations. Upgrade your equipment, gain new abilities, grow stronger and destroy anything that stands in your way. Enjoy a complex story interwoven with high-octane gameplay and full of twists and turns that hit as hard as a bounty hunter's third arm!

_childDocuments_.review: I want to start out by saying that this game is beautiful, and that the things it does well, it does really, really well. Those things being painting an interesting world, establishing a cool character, and *when everything is going right*, making me feel like a badass space ninja. That being said, the two main components of the game, the platforming and the combat, are both plagued by glaring problems that fundamentally disrupt the flow of either segment, and therefor fundamentally kill the fun of the game.The platforming suffers from bad hitboxes on platforms/climbable terrain, and frequent and confusing killboxes. -Multiple times I've fallen to my death after having my model visually intersect with the monkeybars I was supposed to grab onto.-Any of the numerous "careful you might get crushed" primarily function by simply attaching a killbox to the bottom of them. This means that even if you jump against the bottom of large piston as it raises, you will instantly die.-In general, all of the moving platform segments leave *MUCH* to be desired. There is a lot of rapid switching between falling/standing as some of them tilt/lower, and momentum/movement doesn't seem to be preserved properly sometimes.-Killboxes are frequent, punishing, and sometimes non-obvious enough, that I actually just stopped exploring/looking for goodies because as often as not I would drop down a small ledge, die, and have to reload. Special mention to that one time I got an assassination prompt indicating there was an enemy I could drop down and assassinate, and upon pressing the button, my character jumped down, assassinated an invisible enemy (who I guess had falled onto the killbox and not despawned?), and then died.-Not really platforming, but certainly has to do with the unpleasant feeling movement: You can't run on your ship? You walk at like a snails pace. Unless that is, you are carrying a bounty over your shoulder, in which case you do the half-run that you do in the field when you are carrying a bounty. This means that you move through your ship *faster* if you are carrying a bounty. ???? what???The combat LOOKS great. I just wish it FELT great.-Despite the visuals, combat is actually very sluggish if you aren't countering everyone to death. This is due to the fact that it takes 6-9 sword strikes to kill a standard enemy, but after a 3 sword combo you will send them flying across the stage. Meaning you spend a lot of time chasing ragdolled enemies around.-For the above reason, and because you are often fighting 6 guys at a time, combat is heavily counter based. Most attacks are counterable, but some aren't, and to indicate this the devs have cleverly made every attack have either a blue or red glint that happens near the end of the "wind up" for the attack. Insanely, when this glint occurs is *not* when you actually need to counter the attack. The counter window is slightly later, when the attack is closer to hitting you, and varies from attack to attack. This makes countering feel like *garbage*, and combined with the relatively unforgiving unsuccessful counter-delay, and the occasionally-uninteruptable enemy attack animations makes combat really frustrating.All in all, They Always Run wants you to feel like a badass space ninja, and when it succeeds its great, because you feel like a badass space ninja. But my take away was that there was often too much friction for it to make me feel like anything but a frustrated consumer who had plenty of better platformers with better combat in his steam library.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game- and I was mostly enjoying it despite a bit of jank. It's probably the most weirdly abrupt ending I've ever seen in a video game, something that left me completely unsatisfied in a way that actually tainted the fun I'd had up until that point.There's ways to tease a sequel that don't involve completely blue balling anyone who was actually enjoying your game up until that point.With all that said, if the gameplay looks fun to you- you'll probably get your moneys worth as long as it's on a heavily discounted sale. Just don't get invested in the story.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE:I have come back to change my thoughts.  The Devs have shown vigilance and been updating especially the controls! It's still far from perfect seeming at times like the Devs played every plat-former with bad mechanics and decided "that's for our game!"  But having gotten the latest update I can say this a recommend now.  The games beauty is now matched by more solid controls. Kudos to the Devs.  If they get it completely polished you may have spawned yourself an actual franchise level IP.  Original Review below:Sadly I cannot recommend this game.  I was really excited after playing the demo as the look and style grabbed me right away.  Unfortunately after getting my hands on the full release the janky controls and lack of polish are very apparent.  Don't expect tight controls like Dead Cells, Blasphemous and other modern games in this genre.  The game feels at time like playing a bad platformers from the late 90's and early 00's where you clearly land on a platform but die anyways cuz the game doesn't register that you moved even though the position of where you die on screen is a safe position (It's weird).  Be prepared to miss a ton of easy jumps because of the animations.  There is no cancel animations at all.  So getting close to the edge of something the run animation triggers even though you barley move your joystick.  There is no fine movement animations either.  There's one part on the second level where you have to avoid the pistons and even if you jump off in time you will die even if you are nowhere near being crushed.  The game doesn't register it.  I don't even know what is going on with that.  The demo seems so polished but they really needed to work on the gameplay meshing with the animations more.  It gets frustrating and like I said I was really looking forward to this and am sorely disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: They Always Run does not quality for a good platformer in my opinion, there are some famous and popular games out there you don't need me to name any. However, what kept me playing and finally finished it was the art design, the music and to the end I even got emotional knowing the truth of the story.More specifically, as a platformer I can hardly give it positive - there are some good action part like smart jump/dash combo, but the battles feels dull and not fun, there are not enough enemies types and devs could really use more test since enemy stuck in wall often, and I reload several times to skip glitches.However, what saves this game is the art. While not in the battlefield, the player stays in either spaceship or in the city, just looking at the light/shadow from the flames is joy, I assume most of the budget goes to the art department. It's really fascinating. The overall cyberpunk feeling with neon light suits the game, and while in the battle field the scientific/planet background is satisfying. Sometimes player would go for a ropeway ride and it's fab the way it is executed: first from the closer view than the camera goes farther and farther, until player become a single dot to let player appreciate the rich background view, upon seeing how small a human could be and the magnificent of the view is breathtaking.I wasn't paying much attention to the story, especially when I read 3 arms I was constantly thinking of thieves. As a platformer it does not require a rich story but this game is special as it has pretty long dialogues. However, the color in lines should be limited into fewer colors, putting a rainbow color does not make the content stand out but in the country, I find it is hard to concentrate. The last 10 mins is the highlight of the entire game, I won't give out much but it was definitely stunning and congrats to the devs. The music goes well with the story and that moment seeing the credit roll reminds me of the latest James Bond movie No Time To Die, in the movie from the very beginning it constantly gives hints to the audience that 007 is just a code name rather than a real person, which lives on. They Always Run also plays with names in a good way, for the ending alone I'd give it a positive.

_childDocuments_.review: They Always Run~~~~~~~~~~~~~~They Always Run is a fun new side-scroll, platformer with bold hack and slash gameplay elements in a rusty cyberpunky space-western setting. You play as a three-armed bounty hunter Aiden who is in pursuit of some of the most notorious criminals that this side of the galaxy has to offer, all while being pursued by other criminals himself. They Always Run is one of those hidden indie gems that you can’t really appreciate until you’ve experienced it yourself. From high jumping parkour elements to intense multilevel hand-to-hand combat, this game has it all. Plot: After the fall of the great empire, the galaxy went haywire and soon became flooded with criminals. In an intergalactic society like this, being able to find anyone, anywhere has become a highly prized skill. Here’s where our protagonist Aiden comes into play; a three-armed bounty hunter who must hunt down the most dangerous and elusive cutthroats in the galaxy.You start off drinking in a bar, when a bunch of no-goods approaches you and starts questioning you about who you are after. One thing leads to another and you find yourself in a bar brawl. Taking advantage of the chaos, your person of interest takes off and you now go after him and the journey follows.Gameplay: As the plot goes, you start off with a bar brawl, and here is where the game’s tutorial takes place. The game presents its button layout in a simple and meaningful way. Anyone can catch up to it with just a little bit of attention. The movement is your basic WASD and space for jump, with combat consisting of the left mouse for sword attack, right for third arm control, and Q for counterattack. This whole control system works almost flawlessly. Almost*, I wish the control sensitivity was much higher than what is currently in play. And the third arm is mighty powerful when it's used right but the control is still a bit rusty; this needs to be polished. As a bounty hunter, your main goal is to take criminals into custody and take down criminals for information, which plays out great throughout Aiden’s adventures. Another feature which to me is super unique to this game, and I had a lot of fun with, is Aiden’s ultrasound scanner ability. By hitting C, Aiden can send out a sound pulse that will reveal high-value criminals and hidden buttons nearby. This feature is particularly useful in locating hidden buttons throughout the game, which can later be accessed by breaking the button with his third arm. Combat: Aiden will mostly encounter more than one goon at a time, so it gets really tricky at times. Luckily the parkour and platformer element in this game is pretty on point and you can roll, jump and swing your way out of incoming blows and attack another enemy before heading back to the first one.Boss fights can get a bit tedious at times but it’s all good. For the most part, the utility of the third arm in combat got into question, as it takes a bit of getting used to and it’s a bit rusty. For the most part, I forgot to use it and relied heavily on the other elements. But overall, a genuinely fun experience with They Always Run’s combat.World Design: They Always Run’s design felt heavily inspired by retro art, blade runner, and cyberpunk. The world looks empty but lived in, and artistically I see the point of it.Although I wish there were more areas crowded with both hostiles and non-hostiles. Music and sound effects: Pretty lite-hearted Arcady music, with some good beats. The same goes for the sound effects; they went for some lite intense music and sound effects for Aiden’s adventure and when he gets into fights. Positive: + Fun plot+ Smooth platformer + Intense combat with many elements + Good music and sound effects+ Loved the art style+ On-point world theme relevant to the plot+ Good controller support Negative: - Controls can be improved- Combat environment can be improved and experimented uponAn absolutely fun experience with many star indie gameplay elements, and the character is an absolute badass. 8/10Key provided by the developer/publisher for review purposes. Any opinions expressed are entirely my own!

_childDocuments_.review: Wowowowowow... I'm at a loss for words! This gem, this shining piece of entertainment software is why I LOVE games! _childDocuments_.review: 8/10Summary:  It's a story-oriented game, with unique, fantastic visuals and animations. Gameplay mechanics are flawed but have some interesting stuff to play around with. The plot is good, it starts as "meh" but only gets better the more you play and has a nice juicy reveal in the end where it shines. It has it's flaws in many areas, especially in combat. Enemy types a few to find and they get just boring and annoying at the end. They throw a bunch of them at you and it becomes a mess, where you are trying to play cool to look good but in the end just shoot them all as fast as you can most of the time so you can move forward to see the plot unravel. Ultimatly combat is fine. All this just starts to get boring near the end. The only thing that never annoyed me was the selling feature of this game - your 3rd hand. I can't say much about it - it just works and it's fun. (lol) Platforming is a much less of a mess. You get this fluidity, feels good, but some places annoyed me a bit. Still it's forgiving, lots of checkpoints so no big deal here. I would say this game needs some changes in combat to become more fun, but what's done is done. The good part is, of course, the artstyle. Fantastic. Just fantastic. Pleasure to look at, all this animations, the lighting, the textures and the backgrounds with a touch of paint brush. Magnificent. Finally the story. It's quite short ( and it's a good thing cause all the bad stuff I've said earlier wont hit you that hard.) and it's quite good. Yeah, maybe in the beginning it was kinda slow and not that interesting, but in the middle of my playthrough I was wholly invested in it. Then was the final reveal and that ending sequence hit me hard right in the feels. I instantly remembered all those bits and hooks writers put all over the story so now they actually started to ring in my head all at once. And that song ... Yeah... Very satisfing experience. In that sequence it even shows in protagonist animations, all those things we were told about. This is a great detail that enhances this last experience. I myself absolutely love this kind of things in games. Gets you you to an emotional peak with all the other stuff that happens on the screen. Hats off to developers. It's that thing that made me go there to write this right now and add +1 point in the final score of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a good try by the devs. Maybe if they make a sequel, they'll make a good game. The good:- The combat, while a bit janky at times, is fast, exciting, and pretty fun.- When you're in the groove, the platforming is pretty smooth.The bad:- This is a game that's unfair. There's no way to replay missions so if you missed something important, too bad, you have to restart the whole game. You also can't freely buy upgrades whenever you want, only between some missions.- This game is overflowing with instant death pits, many of which shouldn't be there. You'll be climbing a tower and fall, but instead of landing on a lower platform, you just die.- While fun, the combat is also unforgiving. Enemies can generally take you out in 2 or 3 hits, and while there are healing items, you have a limited supply, and the only way to get more is from random enemy drops (or if it's not random, I can't tell). You read that right. An important resource is only available randomly, and you can't grind for it.- This might be the fault of the publishers or steam, but the tone for the art is inconsistent. Look at the image on the store page. It looks like a kind of goofy game. Well in game it's trying to be rather serious and grim. Just the game's title screen is a totally different art style and theme. To echo some other reviews, the final (I think it's the final) boss fight is basically impossible. Maybe it's possible with enough practice, max HP, a full stock of healing items, and the ability to save-state right before the boss fight so you can retry with full gear, but... basically impossible. I quit the game after this and will not return. I cannot recommend the game like this.

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend grabbing this when it's on sale. Despite how beautiful this game looks, it doesn't match in playability, I'll explain,Combat can be very fun but there's an ability called the third arm that is used as sort of a heavy attack that gets recharged every time you deflect a shot from an enemy. This is great and all, but in order to activate it, you have to hold down the RB on your controller while moving your right analog stick in the direction you wish to use it. With fast paced action games, the less button pressing the better, and holding down the RB to be able to use this ability takes away from the fluidity of combat.The animation and art is similar to Sundered or a mid 90s/late 90s Image comic, I love it. The backgrounds and parallax scrolling is a triumph. What is not a triumph is the HUD, menus, and fonts. They do not match the artistic beauty of this game, they seem thrown together very fast. You'll notice in your menu that some of the text doesn't even fit on the menu buttons, it looks flimsy. On the shopkeepers screen any items that you already possess have in large text underneath them: YOU ALREADY OWN THIS ITEM. Their are 15-20 something items you can get in-game and YOU ALREADY OWN THIS ITEM is written on almost all of them when in possession. It's kind of hilarious but an eyesore.The in-game dialog is all text paired with a timer that runs out when the text is ready to move on. You are presented with the option of pressing a button to get to the next speech dialogue, however, if you press the button before the text has presented itself, it completely disappears, instead of just displaying the text that you wish to read instead of waiting for it to completely present itself. I read fast and not being able to control the speed of text made me lose a lot of the story forgetting that the way text is presented in this game and how the player controls it is COMPLETELY unlike any other game, ever, of all time.The first boss of the game has a fire attack that doesn't start or finish animations. You have this beautifully detailed boss and it drops fire and the fire doesn't douse itself out when it leaves the screen, it just instantly vanishes. It's a very strange detail that did not get addressed.Enemies do not have death animations when falling into death pits, they just vanish. It's very strange looking considering how much work was put into the animation overall. It's as if they just forgot to do it.Checkpoint system is a little wonky. Depending on where you die, sometimes it will start you off in the perfect spot, other times it starts you off in very inconvenient positions, as an example, if you die at the first boss, it spawns you in the boss room with the boss and you have about a second to react before you get hit.Later in the game you get an ability that lets you deflect bullets from enemies. Instead of it being mapped to your parry button, it's mapped to your attack button instead, which doesn't seem to be characteristic of the action.Some of the music seems out of place at certain points and at times lacks dynamics. Songs that play during boss battles or intense moments start abruptly and tend to not match the level of intensity that the moment is trying to display emotionally. Some of the music even seems phoned in, as if it was made before the game was even made. Some of the ambiance tracks are INCREDIBLE. I'm very conflicted.Despite my gripes, this game was obviously created with passion from the devs and from what I've read, the game ends on the setup to a sequel. I hope they're working on part 2 and correcting any issues that might have been in this game. I look forward to the next game from this team!

_childDocuments_.review: A short (6ish hours to 100% minus the annoying buy ammo achievement, protip reloading your game /restarting checkpoint to rebuy ammo will still move the counter) side-scrolling beat-em-up in the style of guacamelee. I found the middle a bit draggy but the ending run and flashbacks was quite the experience. No need to explore things thoroughly as there's no achievements tied to 100% exploration. There's no hidden chests off the edges of ledges too, so save yourself some unnecessary curiosity killed the cat moments. Some platforming moments are a bit janky, but nothing overly annoying. Generous checkpoints help too. The combat is smooth and quite fun.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is definitely trying to do some spectacle gameplay. It's just not very good at it. The camera always feels a little off, and it zooms in and out in order to show you things and to make you feel like you're missing something when it goes in for extreme closeup of... you running through a very small empty corridor between platforming and combat.The game wants you to know the devs understand that triple-countering is very cool, and it doesn't really work in practice because the shield guys don't have moves you can counter, but do confuse the AI slightly by blocking their own teammates from setting up a double or triple. Shield guys are very common and definitely are there to ensure combat is neither a complete breeze nor fun. Some, you can roll behind and attack, others have 2 shields and your only option is to use the 3rd hand to punch first. All of the shield guys need a good 2-3 full combos to put down, which isn't a challenge, it's just a chore. And very hard to do while in the middle of a pack because you can't see cues to counter or dodge very well when 6+ guys are stacked up.And then there was that first boss. Mechanically very simple, it's only got ~3 moves. Tail swipe, shoot, or ground flame. Roll behind for the first two, jump on something for the 3rd... but get off it QUICK because it will do a very fast little uppercut to punish you for using the Y axis. This boss, the first one, very mechanically simple... is a chore to fight, because the rolls are a bit floaty and you can go too far to just start attacking from behind without pushing the stick back. Which might make your combo take you on top of the boss sprite while he's shooting, so you take a bit of cannon fire point blank because you can't trust your controls.The combat system is just not fun. Definitely made to look good, but never made to feel good. It is clever when it does the ranged fire and just hits whatever can be hit, the times I didn't use that properly were very much my fault.Oh, and sometimes, especially on your ship, the game switches to RP-Walk. _childDocuments_.review: They Always Run is a narrative driven cinematic platformer sadly held back from true greatness by some frustrating design choices and clunky gameplay elements.With an instantly striking visual style, you will be drawn in to this space-western by the appealing designs of the characters and locations. Drawing influences from a galaxy far far away, expect desert planets with dusty settlements, gleaming space ports and cyberpunk cities, outposts filled with scum and villainy, hidden rebel bases and enemy strongholds. Everything has a nice painterly touch which gives vibrancy to the universe and fluidity to the characters. When everything is working as it should, this is a fairly entertaining romp through a believeabliy hostile universe.The tonal identity of the game is really enhanced by an incredibly strong soundtrack composed by Deallry. The tracks are largely electro, house and techno pieces that suit the hard science fiction setting, while occasional flourishes of acoustic guitars, strings and harmonicas really sell the space western vibes. Stand out pieces are Evening in Gigapolis, Last Bet and Other Culture which all help set a very specific mood; whether that be for one of the many locations, or for important narrative beats. The briefest search for the composer shows their work also features in Wall World and Necrosmith, two games which  I own and will definitely check out simply for the music alone.The main character is well animated, and when you are in the heat of combat or parkour, you really feel like an intergalactic action hero. Unfortunately there are occasional animation glitches which can result in the break of flow, and this often leads to unfair deaths. For instance, jumping to a higher platform during combat often results in the protagonist locking into a jump animation, failing to grab onto a ledge, and being left open to attacks. This is a real pity, because the combat can often look beautifully balletic in motion. This becomes even more unforgiving during some of the faster paced parkour sections where you are chasing a foe, or outrunning some kind of instant kill aggressor. It is important to maintain momentum to succeed in some leaps of faith, but often the animation comes to a stop and the character makes a feeble jump to certain death. This always felt undeserved, and really detracted from the kinetic flow.Combat looks great, but there is little variety in most of the encounters. Light enemies will telegraph attacks which must be countered, while heavy enemies will telegraph attacks which must be dodged. Countering light enemies will instantly kill them, while heavier enemies must have their guards broken with the protagonist's third arm. This is controlled independently with RB and the right analogue stick, and while initially novel, it soon becomes monotonously rote. Even with a variety of moves and weapons available, the combat never evolves much beyond simple patience and timing. A three armed mutant cyborg bounty hunter should have multiple tactics at his disposal, but things will mostly play out the same every single time. There are a few boss encounters which will require a mastery of the complete move set, but most are easily dispatched once you have observed their attack patterns. When the combat is flowing well, it really is something to behold but most players will likely find it all too simplistic and shallow.While the story is reasonably entertaining, the way the narrative is presented is both limiting and frustrating. The plot is entirely conveyed through conversation, but as there is no voice acting in the game, these are all displayed as box outs on screen. Most of these come during active play, and as a result they break the flow of the game and often result in the player missing important story beats. While the story is being conveyed, the player is slowed to a walk, and this just horribly breaks the pacing of the action. There are frequent grammatical errors, and the script is often clunky and wooden. It can be difficult to become truly invested in the narrative when it comes at the detriment of gameplay. While not particularly original, the characters are mostly likeable and well defined with understandable motivations and goals. If the story had just played out between levels rather than during, I think it would have greatly helped the overall feel.Most of these issues are entirely subjective and for the most part, the game and story are perfectly serviceable. When everything coalesces as it should, They Always Run is a fun yarn spun through a beautiful science fiction universe. If you can overlook the bugs and questionable design choices, there is much to enjoy and hopefully the studio are given an opportunity to revisit this world with a lessons learned and a bigger budget at their disposal.

_childDocuments_.review: As much as it hurts to say it, this game was not ready for a public release.  I love everything about this game, from the basic Space Western aesthetic and playing as a bounty hunter, to the parkour, chase concepts, the fluid and interesting combat. The music, lighting, graphics... it all adds up to a great package. But when it comes to the controls/platforming, that's where the whole thing falls apart. I had to request a refund for this game, because I ran into a complete progression blocker early on in the campaign. On The Anvil, the military base, there is a moving platform section, and one of the obstacles that you SHOULD be able to remove using your recently found upgrade, does not work at all. And instead of progressing, your player simply falls to his death over and over again. I'm sorry, but that is the kind of progression blocker that should have been fixed long before making this a full priced release.

_childDocuments_.review: Neat little action platformer. Has a short and interesting story, a decent combat system and good platforming. The problems that generally arise with the game are the visual contrasts.Cons:Text Boxes are generally black on black backgrounds, kind of makes it hard to tell who is talking in certain conversations when the background is black, have a white outline might fix that issue. Having left mouse be your skip button as well, it not working to skip dialogue sometimes is a pain and having a timer on dialogue, might make it harder for people who read slower to read and follow your story, removing the timer and changing the button prompt will solve the issue.Secondly insta-kill traps, I'm personally ok with instant death platforming, if it's smooth and gives me opportunities and prompts which are clear, here is a 50/50 case. If I jump off in the wrong direction I die of fall damage, that's fine, but then I touch the edge of 1 spike or my toe on an icicle and it's instant death. The loading screen and death screen become a common sight and not having tips to remind you of things you might have forgotten kind of takes away from the game's flow as do the instant traps and very little time for jumping from area to area in certain sections.The combat is serviceable but more often the not I end up spamming dodge rather than parrying since I never had an opportunity to parry multiple people at once, having ranged enemies also made it a priority to chase or shoot them and then do melee combat. The final few levels of the game are really fun but the boss fights are anticlimactic. Bosses generally were not designed with the parry mechanic in mind or the third arm to be used frequently, which is disappointing as the game has a solid foundation but does not work with it's own system frequently enough.Pros:The game lets you be a bounty hunter, often you will scan around the enemies to beat up, meaning you can potentially find a bounty which will pay you a measly fee, but it's better than what a chest, 100 per chest and around 500-900 for bounties which are not part of the main story.You get to make minor choices about what you say and how you handle some of your bounties, taking them Dead or Alive, which is a neat way to do choices in a game, but it does not affect the story much.The platforming and combat are solid and fun to do, makes you feel like a 3 handed samurai/gunslinger at times with the amount of enemies thrown your way.Verdict:I really like the game's concept, visual, story and foundation, but It needed more time in the oven for refinement of it's mechanics and ironing out it's rougher platforming sections. It's still a good game, which I recommend you get on sale, like I did. I hope they make a sequel and keep the bounty hunter aspects, as they were the most appealing.6/10 Not great, not terrible.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: 7-/10, do recommend at full price.This is a tentative recommendation. I really like this game but there are a few elements that are incredibly frustrating.The good:It looks incredible. You see the screenshots, it looks like that all the time. It feels amazing in both combat and in horizontal movement. You feel like an acrobatic space hunter in the best possible way. The animations and controls are very smooth.Really good character and environment design. The feel of a space western is perfectly captured. Same with the Characters and the writing.The bad:Vertical movement has its issues. There is a good reason the chases and pretty much all portions of the game are lacking vertical movement. There is however one level that is nearly entirely based around vertical movement and it frankly sucks. The boss fights are an insane diffculty spike for no reason. And not because they have intricate attack patterns or can dodge stuff. They are just tanky as hell and do literally a third of your health as damage per hit. They also are immune to your ranged atacks and are not affected by most of your abilities. This makes them frustrating and frankly boring.There are a few places in the game which are incredibly unclear. To the point where  I had to look up a guide.The best and most intersting parts of the game (The chases and taking people in alive) are just not used in the second half which is an absolute shame.Conclusion:All in all, a decent game with cool aspects but glaring flaws. A sequel is hopefully in the works as I believe that all of the issues can be rectified by the Dev team.

_childDocuments_.review: There's quite a few interesting bits in there, but they're surrounded by a lot of rough. The combat is just not very good. Tough, imprecise, and the saving grace is that checkpoints are very common. The traversal has a similar problem - sometimes the game just decided to be a jerk. Then there's the technical problems. I really struggled to keep the game running at a stable pace. It's really good at ignoring vsync and even dedicated GPU overrides. The only way I could get it to run at a mostly stable framerate was to run in a window (not the borderless kind), and then I still had some frame stutter to deal with.But outside of that it is a lovely are style and the story actually grew on me. The level design is not half bad either. But then the ending dropped and I have mixed feelings.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright let me get my two gripes out of the way for this game, because this is a hearty recommend from me.1) The movement is fairly janky. It just isn't as tight as it should be. Most of the frustration in this game is due to how the movement can make you feel really  incompetent when you maybe aren't.2) The checkpoint system.... ho-boy.... You will (unless you are really  good or really lucky) have to repeat a lot of puzzles and obstacles and bosses. And the game just arbitrarily decides to put you in strange checkpoints often WELL before a puzzle. And (aside from the last boss) it always puts you AHEAD of all the dialogue, so if you die in a boss fight, you have to go through and mash Y (on a controller) over and over to get through the dialogue every time you die.But once you get past the weirdness of the controls and get used to the combat, the fighting is generally a lot of fun, the upgrades are cool, and it's very entertaining seeing how many ways you can defeat a group of enemies. The bosses were all pretty fun too. Hard-ish, but fair once you learned the patterns. It reminded me a bit of Dark Souls 2, in that you have to just learn how the game wants you to play to succeed, and that means for a lot of the game, it won't be easy if you aren't really good at sidescrollers. But it's overall worth the struggle in the end.The music is superb. I would have preferred they stick with the western-in-space theme, but the direction they went with it nonetheless was great.The art is 95% amazing, and about 5% "why did they use the paint tool on the background?" which means most of the game is gorgeous to look at.But what got me most, and why I will be keeping an eye out for their next game, is how good the story was, how great the writing was, and how it all sucked me in right up till the end. (Watch till after the credits for a bit of an after credits scene.)My only real disappointment with this game is that it's over and I'd like to play more. That's a great problem to have though. I dug it. I'm glad I bought it. And the ending (especially the song) is perfect.

_childDocuments_.review: Played entirely on the Steam Deck at the default settings with no issues. Playing this game on the deck was a very enjoyable experience. They Always Run is a linear action platformer with great style and combat. This a simple game compared to others out there, but it is very focused. The game knows what it is and what it is trying to do. It's not overly ambitious outside of the art style but it gets all the important stuff right. This was a fun game to play and not overly difficult.  There isn't much exploration in this game and you can't decide which level to do next. But the game has a fantastic flow to it. It is very satisfying once you get going with the running, jumping, grappling, and shooting. The excellent combat and story kept me going until the end. If there is ever a sequel, I will happily purchase it.

_childDocuments_.review: They Always Run looked like a fun game and I was sucked into it for the first stage of the game. Then I kept playing.I enjoy the music and the art style of this game. However that's where my likes for it end.I kept trying to play this game, I spent $6 on it and at least wanted to try to finish it. I lasted 5.9 hours and I cannot stand to play anymore. The platforming isn't really platforming, you follow a painfully linear path that requires pixel perfect positioning or you will not make the cut. Or if you're like me and kept forgetting to lower yourself to the lowest corner of a wall climb so you don't bump your head on whatever's above you due to the strange arc of the jump animation. The devs must have thought adding random and unnecessary instant death hazards to multiple parts of the missions would somehow equate to good game play. If only! Every level is designed similarly with the same set pieces cobbled together to make different maps. Combat is decent at first. Then you notice you'll be fighting the same 3 1/2 enemy types: A melee guy, a ranged guy, and a shield guy. You have the double shield variant, and eventually come across a grenadier type. They get tiresome to fight after hours of gameplay and the boss fights aren't much more interesting either. My issue with combat is obviously the tedium, and there's no reliable way to obtain healing items. The many chests you open throughout your time will contain the credits to upgrade yourself. It's easier to simply gun everyone down with your pistols.I got to some energy boss that was taking forever to defeat and I quit the game. I stopped having interest in the game and no longer wanted to further waste my time. I had no investment in the characters, or the story, or experiencing it anymore. I am someone who's easily amused I own such games as Saints Row The Third and Magicka. I found the humor they attempted to inject into the dialogue to be eye-rolling bad.I can't really recommend this game to anyone, but if you still want to give it a try wait for it to be on sale for >$10. Or just watch someone play it on Youtube/Twitch

_childDocuments_.review: Now thats a hidden indie gem! This game flew completely under the radar, but you would be doing yourself a disservice by not checking it out.Graphics and animations are way above a level of small indie game. Many interesting designs and locations, very cool main character. Combat is slick with counters and third arm mechanics implemented nearly perfectly. At first I thought third arm would be awkward to control, but it feels great to use and is a crucial part of the gameplay. Platforming segments are also top notch with fluid movement and clever puzzles. You constantly unlock new moves, gadgets and weapon upgrades, keeping things varied throughout.Story is pretty decent and the plot got me interested by the end. Writing is passable if a bit awkward. I didn't really care for the characters, but gameplay more than makes up for it. Unfortunately game ends on the cliffhanger just when things were starting to get interesting.Overall I recommend playing They Always Run and keep my fingers crossed for the sequel. Its a fun, fresh action platformer that is sure to keep you entertained for at least 6-7 hours. Alawar Premium proved to be quite a talented bunch and I'm curious as to what they do next.

_childDocuments_.review: A mediocre action platformer.Pros:- premise is interesting- aesthetics are nice, most of the planets are really nice to look at- music is nice, especially the ending song- interesting gimmick with the manual control of your third armCons:- platforming can be touchy at times- animations are nice when they get going but the transitions are stilted and awkward- some of the dialogue is kinda awkward, probably due to translation issues- health isn't easy to come by- combat is quite repetitive- upgrades are mostly boring +x to stat type things. Better pistols, better melee damage, more energy bars, that kind of thing.- awkward boss fights, Mueller in particular has zero windups to his attacks and is a pain to fight- absolutely nonsensical endings, feels like 2/3 of the story. You find an information broker who tells you three targets you're after. You get to the second, then there's a twist in the plot, then... roll credits? It doesn't make any sense.I think with the platforming not being as good as it could be, the repetitive combat, and a good chunk of the story missing, there isn't enough here to justify the cost. Maybe get it on sale or in a bundle, as it's not a  game, just not a very good one.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of two things: cool ideas and jank. For most it's probably a 6/10 but for me it's 8/10, I find all the little imperfections absolutely adorable. Gameplay is the strongest part, Batman Arkham like combat mixed in with platforming that's meant to be cool rather than challenging. Story is servicable but poorly executed. _childDocuments_.review: The storytelling is completely weak.  The "cut scene" dialog reads like it was put together by one of those AI that are programmed to read/learn a script, then write a new story based on it.  It reads terribly, it's presented terribly, and it barely qualifies as english.The combat is diverse in terms of what the player can do, but overall movement is sluggish as all ♥♥♥♥ to the point of being aggravating.  Just turning around feels like the character has a load in his pants.  Countless times I've died trying to do an action that is prompted on screen (grappling to a hook while falling, for example) just for it to never work no matter how much I spam the button.  And with plenty of "act fast" moments in the game, the load-in-your-pants movement is awful.After spending so much time building up your character's arsenal, some fights are designed to just be tedious.  One particular battle towards the end of the game where if you try to complete it by non-lethal means it just turns into a 5 minute dodge fest (which only works half the time), where you are doing minimal conscience damage due to no way to replenish arm energy during the fight.  On top of that, the boss is 100% immune to firearm damage, so you're literally gimped to either grind down the conscience meter for 5 minutes or use swords only.Overall the concept of the game is great and if not for the abysmal controls and storytelling, would've gotten a positive review from me.  But the fact that I've had to  myself to finish the game rather than  to finish it says it all for me.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm writing this after the post-2021 patches, so many of the bugs previously described have been patched and have allowed for a mostly-smooth ride along the story. Although I agree the options needs tweaking to improve graphics and allow for windowed play among others, I don't think it ruined the experience. And what an experience it was. Many players describe this game as "too short" but I believe that this was a breath of fresh air from other games that expect tens or hundreds of hours of your time to even beat the story (and that's without "fun" mechanics like collectibles and fetch quests.) They Always Run is very quick. Beat a level, upgrade, next level. There's no fiddling with menus and having to deal with annoying lengthy chores. In my playthrough it only took me 10 hours to beat, but when the entire time was spent playing through level after level without many breaks on a double digit number of long levels, I wouldn't exactly call it "short." The hand-brushed backgrounds and multitude of different landscapes for planets, cities, and slums all made for a beautiful game that came alive. Not to mention through the destruction of environments and interactive objects like barrels and shelves that went flying with enemies on your attacks. Not only does the combat feel real with the weight of enemies affecting their distance, but also with how punishing it is to fail a counter or reflect a sniper's shot back at them. The game isn't impossible per se, but it challenges the player to come up with combos that are fast yet also accurate as hordes of enemies surround you from all sides and the game  begins. Dives, kicks, grappling, countering, shooting, blasting, slamming, and slicing are just a few of the many different ways to get yourself out of a sticky situation. The pure creativity in allowing for any combo of moves to be chained together in weird ways to devastate anything that crosses your path. And after the butchering is finished, simply teleporting up some of the more infamous goons for extra pocket cash old-west-style isn't too bad either.There are some negatives, however, as in some of the bolder platforming sections jankiness and a few retries can be found (looking at you icicles.) Some parts of the game are still buggy like how boss fights can sometimes break and a retry is needed, but it only happened once on my run so I couldn't call it an important problem. Like the aforementioned graphics settings of which there are none, I believe that most of the game's problems are under the hood and could be fixed easier than some of the buggier games I've come across.All in all, They Always Run is a beautiful game that has just the right amount of length for it's nonstop action, beautiful art direction, and amazing storytelling that's unlike any other. It has its technical problems but ultimately this game is a solid 8/10. It is definitely worth the $20 price tag and has shown me yet again the creativity and bombastic nature of solid indie devs.

_childDocuments_.review: Review originally published at Murphy's Multiverse: Right from the get-go, you’ll feel a serious lack of QoL features. From the game “feel” to the way the sound design/score comes and goes, it just feels off. The walk animation of the protagonist is so slow and for some reason, the game limits you to walking anytime you’re in the spaceship. The transitions between each story beat and level are so jarring; the game literally just jumps to a new level without oftentimes no segue.I’m a huge sucker for games and apps with good UI design. Having it good is evidence of cohesive vision and having it cohesive makes for a more immersive experience. When your UI looks haphazardly put together with fundamentally bad layouting and poor choice of fonts, it cheapens the experience. Sadly, They Always Run has it looking generic. The game’s interface looks straight out of a cheap 90’s sci-fi bargain bin novel. Texts are overlayed where they shouldn’t be. The menus look so dull and unimaginative. For a sci-fi bounty hunting game with a quirky world, having your UI look pedestrian and mundane is a huge blunder.A lot of the game’s more palatable qualities can be found within the game’s actual combat mechanics. Playing a three-armed assassin, the game somewhat gets the job done and delivers a serviceable combat system that gets fun to play as you progress up the awful-looking skill tree. There’s a depth to the mechanics at play here; having a third appendage allows players to creatively get out of rushdown scenarios when enemies gang up on you. On top of that, you also have options to use guns mid-combo. And then when you start unlocking the Spider-Man grappling hook abilities? Every skirmish becomes a challenge to do the craziest combos yet.But then the jank starts creeping in and poops on the party. The fight animations are so rigidly done that it underlines the lack of flow with the combat system. It’s a total shame since a game like this would benefit from a system that allowed seamless movement and transitions. Cancel animations don’t exist in this game; I can’t count the times I died because I couldn’t roll out from an animation frame. Modern action-heavy platformers need that feature. It also doesn’t help that the hitboxes are so all over the place that your attacks don’t always register.They Always Run could have been a decent game as it has promising aspects. The art style is great. The characters look interesting. The bounty hunter premise is fun (though it could’ve been done without the linearity. Imagine being able to simply pick which bounty to chase) Sadly, the lack of polish prevents it from reaching its potential. So I do not recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was a better way to put this, but this game has some serious flaws. Not saying it's bad. It's actually quite enjoyable until the very end. I rushed the game and had to quit because I couldn't keep up with the last Arcturus-7 boss (on this later). I'm thumbing up, because it has potential. But before you buy it keep this in mind: General* Aesthetically the game is beautiful. There are some very cool details all over.* Story-wise the game feels like a rushed patchwork space opera, but it is somehow catchy. * Level design is good. It varies a lot although you can see repetitions all over.* Combat is cool, but it's repetitive.* Characters are cool.* This should be a mix of side scrolling action and platformer, but it has so many extra weird mechanics that it ends being none of those. For good or bad though.* The game is extremely short. Most of the time is actually wasted on chit-chat.* Jesus, allow me to jump, crawl, run, etc inside my ship! Yes, you have a ship.* At some point you'll fight a shark. Glub-glub?* You can't change display sizes (you have to play full screen). Seriously?Mechanics* Controls are weird. The game does not respect input so nicely to a point that you will be mashing buttons to activate the grappling hook and you'll die.* What a horrible collision detection this game has. It's worse than the hit boxes in MH X. I was dying to hits that we're visibly not happening by 1 or 2 cm.* The control response is also weird when on the very edge of a platform. You'll get stuck as if trying to jump, but still on the platform.* Some of the physics are weird specially when carrying objects and running. The game has a sliding effect when you're stopping or changing directions, but it feels slightly more acute when carrying objects. This got me off guard when trying to stop at the very edge of a platform. Just to slip and fall to my death.* There are some auto actions that can be annoying like getting close to a cable and automatically climbing up.* The auto saving mechanics needs to be streamlined. I had a couple auto saved states where I was in mid jump between two platforms. Took me 2 deaths to realize I had to use the grapple hook and not continue the jump.* The game has a gear progressing aspect where you buy better equipment. This is the sole reason why I quit the game. As I rushed it I wasn't really into making money to upgrade gear. Neither should it be a major requirement. Until Arcturus-7 boss where each hit felt like I was ♥♥♥♥♥ slapping it for 1s. With 2 health bars and a combat pattern that required near perfect dodge that is a no. Resetting the level also does not gives you much option as you won't be able to buy anything once you're in the level and making money seems now impossible. I'm stuck in a extremely annoying fight. Second best option is to start over. Third option is to mess up with game files.* The menu UI follows the same control problems. Sometimes its not responsive.* This might not be a problem with the game, but I had it stuck consuming computer resources after politely quitting it through the menu. Had to quit steam client to kill the process properly.

Except being like a wish come true for an Assassin's Creed mainline games fan in a 2D cyberpunk style, I really liked that I finally found a game with this kind of particular graphic that is used for a game where you can really fight, not just games where you can only run away from things, resolve enigmas or having a bad platforming experience for the whole or you're playing a graphic adventure game.
