_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I'm quite mixed about this game. On one hand I'm disappointed by most of the game, and on the other hand I'm quite impressed by some things.Let's start of with the thing that reels most people in, the art style. The art here is great and always manages to look great. Not only is the art great, but the animation is also really good. I especially like the multiple counter animations. The music is also pretty good, with one song standing out from the rest.Unfortunately, I can't say that many positive things about the gameplay. The combat is fine, just fine. I think the biggest problem with the combat is the lack of enemy variety. There are only three enemy types, which vary slightly based of which faction they are from. This leads to combat becoming very repetitive after a while. Individual enemies are not that strong and some of them die instantly from a counter, so in order to make the game more difficult, the developers throw huge hordes at you which just creates a lot of visual clutter and hurts the fluidity of combat. The bosses are also very bad with the final boss being the worst, like what is it with games and always messing up the final boss. The final boss is literally three waves of a huge horde of enemies, like come on man.  The main mechanic of this game is the third arm that your character has and it's very underutilised. The tutorial pays a lot of attention to the third arm, but then the rest of the game barely does anything with it. A positive of the gameplay for me was the parkour set pieces that happen during chase sequences during the game which is pretty fun.The thing is, I would be more forgiving of the gameplay flaws if the story was good, but this is also a mixed bag. The story throughout the game is very boring, most of the characters are extremely boring and some of the dialogue is also a bit off, but there is one thing that elevates the story for me from being bad to okay and that is the twist at the end. It's a very good twist and I definitely was not expecting it, and you probably won't either. It then just upsets me that the game's ending is unfortunately just a set up for a sequel.A few bonus points, there's one really good joke at the middle of the game that is pretty good, and I encountered one glitch that caused me to repeat a level in the game because my game kept freezing when my character tried to climb a ladder.In conclusion, I don't think this is a bad game, but it's not even close to a great game. If you really want to play this, I would recommend that you buy this on a deep, deep sale. If you are looking for a good action platformer then I would rather recommend that you play Katana Zero instead.

_childDocuments_.review: Not going to lie, I was super excited about this game when I first saw the trailer. I thought, "Holy crap, it's a space bounty hunter game! Awesome!" Unfortunately when I started playing it, I was disappointed. The story is alright, but the game is extremely linear. You don't really feel too much like a bounty hunter, because you can't go to a bounty board and pick up missions. You do the missions that the game tells you to do. I also wish the combat was a bit faster, but to be honest I came to this game from Dead Cells, so I was used to fast-paced sidescrolling action. It is a pretty cool concept, but I don't think they executed it very well. Also, the way you heal is by using these little health packs, and these give you back about half your health. The problem is, they're pretty hard to find, so I find myself dying a lot. Not sure if I'm just bad, but that was my experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I have not beaten this game yet but I feel like I've got a lot to say about it already.I guess the summary would be that it's a good game filled with bad design decisions, like how you cannot run in many parts of the game, yet you can shoot and deflect. How you are forced to walk in many parts of the game. How dialogue text moves super slow and stays there for a very long time until it moves on to the next line. How the controls don't feel natural both using a joystick and a mouse and keyboard. How the ship sometimes faces the right side and some others the left side, confusing the player. How the camera moves too fast in some areas and how in some it doesn't let you see further than you need to. How some animations clip in parkour sections. And I could go on and on and on about this. But despite all of this, I'm having fun. And that's no understatement. The game is fast paced and the combat is innovative enough for me to keep wanting to push forward. Levels are rather long and the lack of a good story make them a bit more tedious than they should be, especially the interludes between missions. But I love the platforming sections and how the character controls. More bosses would have been nice. And of course, way more polishing. ---Update: in the end, the issues with the game design ended up ruining it for me. The gameplay couldn't stand by itself and finishing the levels was starting to be a chore more than a fun activity.Final score: 7/10 - Meh.

_childDocuments_.review: This game isn't good enough to be as hard as it is. It's the difference between challenging, like Dark Souls, and just cruel and not fun. I like the setting, themes, art, style, everything, but I'm refunding it after not even beating the first level because this game is trying to be "challenging" without know what that means, it doesn't mean getting stun locked and having stim packs that barely heals anything and drops as frequently as a Kanye album. _childDocuments_.review: Spoilers sortaThis game didn't work for me, I enjoyed parts of it, the plot was interesting especially near the end (though I personally think the "final boss" was a waste of potential for an actually interesting boss fight) where there is story points that re-frames the way you see the game, followed up by a redemption arc for one of the characters that got me excited... but then was immediately cut off with abrupt credits and a post-credits scene that made no sense to me.Story aside the art is beautiful, the entire game is gorgeous, the moments with nothing but running and the backgrounds scrolling were actually very satisfying to have a break from the constant combat. Speaking of which, combat is fun but insanely repetitive, any chances you have to deviate and explore for a second or two left me disappointed, as it was either a small health related upgrade or a measly amount of ammo for one of the two guns you have which just left me discouraged from trying to explore. Combat on it's own was fine, the lack of enemy variation was a bit annoying late game  but each combat sequence can happen so quick that I found myself not caring until the final half hour of game play. Also the shield generator thingies were really annoying later on when you have to rush past a flock of enemies hoping they don't get a cheap hit off only to try and destroy the shield generator and accidentally hit an enemy shield causing me to take damage i couldn't avoid.My least favorite part by far was the Mueller boss fight which took way too long to do. On one hand it was a bit of a skill issue for getting hit by the same attack over and over, but on the other hand this is a fifteen minute long boss of the same two attacks where, as far as I'm aware, you can't use ranged weapons at all. I dislike that fight with a passion and I honestly was planning to leave a negative review for him alone.I'm glad people enjoyed it and maybe Mueller made me a bit too salty but this was not fun, achievements weren't that hard at least but that doesn't change anything

_childDocuments_.review: Mostly it's a good game! _childDocuments_.review: They always Run is a solid pixel-art 2D action combat/platformer game for people who have never played such games before. It is basic, it has class, it is bug-free but it lacks the oof factor many other games in this genre have. The developers hint at a sequel towrds the end, so if they wanna invest more in this IP there are a lot of improvements they have to make here. Here are some of my suggestions:1) Justify the existence of alternate playstyles if you are gonna include them. The game has a shotgun & pistols. They are not well realised at all. They are just insta "I win" buttons. They  do not flow well with the sword playstyle, especially in late game when grapple moves are unlocked.2) If you are gonna use early game bosses as late game mob enemies make sure to include the entire kit of the boss when they are a mob. For example  only uses 2 of its move when it becomes a mob enemy in late game. The principle of showing player progression by having them face multiple boss enemies of the early game boss only works if that boss is at full power and nor nerfed.3) Some boss fights need way more work. . There was another boss who you can beat but just dodging around him. That was not play-tested at all, Such an obvious oversight. I don't even remember his name because it was that forgettable. The 2nd to last boss uses the same model and is a way better fight.Those are my recommendations. There are a lot of things to work on if there ever is a sequel but if you guys stick to it I wholeheartedly believe you can make a great game in this genre. You have the fundamentals nailed down. All you need is more hard work and a bit of innovation.

_childDocuments_.review: They Always run is quite the fun action side scroller game.  Both the visuals and music are quite stunning.  Controls are tight and it is easy to move and fight throughout the levels.  Combat can and does keep you on your toes, but it is not what I'd call overly challenging.  The only criticism that I can come up with at the moment is the lack of voice overs.  In my opinion this game needs voice overs to help with the immersion.  I don't know why but I can imagine Simon Templeman (voice of Kain from Blood Omen) being a fitting voice for the protagonist Aidan.  But who knows, maybe they'll add voice overs in future patch/ updates.If you like action side scrollers, then I think that this game is for you.I give They Always Run 4 out 5 stars.Edit:  Above is what I wrote when I've played the game for a couple of hours.  After seven hours of gameplay I have finished the game and can now say that I do NOT recommend this game.  Here in Australia the game cost around $28.95 which is very steep considering that the game does not have much content at all.  But that is not the worst part.  The worst part is that this game isn't even finished as it ended on a major cliffhanger.  I suspect that the developer intends to sell the rest of the content with DLCs.  Now I do not fault gaming companies trying to make as much money as possible, after all it is a business at the end of the day.  However when the desire to make money compromises the quality of a product, we now have problems.  And as far as I am concerned a seven hour game does NOT warrant an excuse to finish the story with DLC.  Like I said before it is a very short game with little content and as such there is NO reason why the player can't experience the full story right now.  This feels like a cash grab.If by chance that the developer does release the rest of the story via DLC and FREE OF CHARGE then I may (I say may) change my review.  Until then I cannot in good conscious recommend this game.  DO NOT BUY.

_childDocuments_.review: They Always Run is a console ported 2D retro platformer/brawler with QTE combat (because combat should be like Dance Dance Revolution, right?) and a bizarre theme as you're some kind of post apocalyptic three armed mutant... whatever. You can tweak the controls and there's 4K support, but the art assets are reasonably static and not all that high resolution, so the game isn't going to look great on top end rigs (but at least it's not 2D retro pixel "art"). While the game isn't broken and it works, has decent stylised art and a rich story, I think at absolutely no point in time when designing the game did any of the zoomers involved ask "Is this fun?".  Because it isn't.  It's awkward and unrewarding to blip through the Dance Dance Revolution combat.  Ultimately, games need to be enjoyable as well as have a solid technical execution, and I can't say that of "They Always Run".   If you want a good 2D platformer, try Hollow Knight.

He only has two attacks and you have a very small window to attack. Both attacks are easy to avoid so you're just waiting for your window to attack, get a couple hits in, and run away. _childDocuments_.review: The hunt is on!Where They Always Run shines the most is during its running sections. The game has a good way of giving you a feeling of speed, smooth traversal and the rush of the chase. Sadly the rest of the game does not shine as brightly but that does not mean there is nothing positive to be had.Another strength is in the presentation. Even if the story is at times kind of jumbled it still presents an interesting and fun sci-fi world with quirky characters and fun dialogue. The environments are not exactly high-def but still have their painted and drawn charme when it comes to the backgrounds and character designs.Cimbat is not exactly complicated or deep but still satisfying. It lives for a large part from parrying attacks but smaller mechanics like sneak assassinations and ranged weapons do make sure that you never feel under equipped for the challenge at hand. Combine that with the third arm that the main character possesses for non-lethal melee and object manipulation and you get a punchy combat system that carries you over the short playtime.Sadly the game does have a couple of issues when it comes to bugs and glitches including falling through the floor or things just not happening that you need to progress. Also oddities with the animation required me to restart an entire level because I could not progress otherwise.They Always Run was one of my favourite demos during Next Fest a couple of years ago and it feels like they did deliver on a short but sweet indy game that can be picked up pretty easily during a Sale.6.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: I was close to abandoning this game within the first hour or two, but I'm glad I didn't. The gameplay itself took some getting used to, but was pretty fun overall. After that, dealing with regular enemies felt like just a chore to finish in order to progress the story.Speaking of the story, it was alright. _childDocuments_.review: The Good As mentioned in another review, it does kind of feel a bit like an off brand Mandalorian game collecting bounties, upgrading gear, making allies along the way. I liked the story, and the ending twist was a surprise to me. It really needs a sequel for a better resolution to the story Aiden.  I had a bit of a chuckle at the Keanu Reeves Johnny Mnemonic reference to one of your allies you meet. It has a great art style and fluid animations along with the combat that flows OK most of the time.  Double swords, dual pistols, shotguns, reflecting laser shots Jedi style, countering attacks and third arm punching added to the wide range of combat abilities.  Unlocking new abilities and weapons in the skill tree was easy.   I didn't experience any game breaking bugs as mentioned in some other reviews. I did have to restart Colonel level because I didn't have enough health when I got to him but after learning patterns, he is beatable. Sometimes I would panic a bit in combat and in some intense platform stages and unintentionally push in the left thumb stick which actually helps identify bounty targets.  ------------------------------------------------------ Issues/Annoyances Sometimes Aiden's actions are not as responsive as they could have been, especially when using grapple line. A lot of Metroidvaina games and other platformers have done it better.  Sometimes the game seemed to not register button presses at all and Aiden would just stand there for a second, even occasionally in the middle of combat.  While chaining grapple shots in some stages the left bumper button press would just not register for me. At first, I was unsure if this was my wired Xbox 360 controller or just the game. Other reviews have confirmed for me that it is the game.  Combat or counter animations can leave you open to laser rifle shots. You can deflect them but not if you're stuck in an attack, roll or counter animation cycle. When carrying an item/bounty to the escape point, Aiden will slide around on the ground like Mario in an ice stage in Super Mario 3.  This can be pretty frustrating and lead to unintentionally falling of a ledge or platform. There was a section in a train stage where the character was constantly going up and down a zip line cable, stuck on a ladder climbing animation all in the middle of trying to fight 4 enemies in a really small area which was very annoying. The upgrade/ skill tree is below average really. It could have been organised or designed a lot better and it also felt like some upgrades didn't really have a significant impact on combat game-play.  Will I replay it again at a later date?  Probably not.

_childDocuments_.review: They Always Run is an extremely stylish 2D side-scroller action platformer with a really cool sapce-western setting and a story that starts out feeling silly but ends up being surprisingly compelling.I think the main draw of the game is the style and atmosphere. The art is gorgeous, the animations are great, the writing is fun and witty, the fact that you can scan enemies for bounties and then collect on them is a really great thematic gameplay mechanic, and combat really makes you feel like a badass. Well, when you win, anyway. Because you're probably gonna die a lot.It's not an easy game. I wouldn't put it up there with the hardest games I've ever played, but it can be pretty challenging at times, and not always for the right reasons. The right reasons, in this game's case, are that you don't have a lot of health so fast reaction times to keep dodging and countering are a must, and enemies will attack you all at once forcing you to keep track of them all and position yourself carefully. You also have a limited number of healing items in a level, so being careful and smart is necessary. That's all really great and makes the combat as satisfying as it is challenging.The wrong reasons are the controls. This may have been a thematic choice to fit the game's cartoon-themed low framerate animations, but the controls just feel very rigid. I don't know how else to describe it, really, it's just a lack of flow that gets in the way of the fast paced combat and platforming. It wasn't a deal-breaker for me, but it sure was annoying - especially in the later stages of the game where platforming started requiring speed and precision, which is not really great level design when your controls are so rigid. It's far from unbeatable, but it can be a little frustrating.The story, as I've mentioned, is pretty good. The setting is interesting and pretty well fleshed out (but not too fleshed out - leaving quite a lot of mystery and "space magic" in it), and can pretty much be described as... Star Wars but not. Not the Jedi stuff, the scum & villainy stuff - bounty hunters, smugglers, backwater desert planets, etc. You play as a three-armed bounty hunter on a quest to avenge his friend, and during this journey you hunt down targets, collect bounties, build up your weaponry, and assemble a team for your spaceship. I think this game could have really benefited from more player agency in the story - some ability to make choices, even small ones like which bounty to go after first, would have really elevated it and added replay value imo. Sadly it's completely linear.Dialogue is all done through text, as there is no voice acting whatsoever, but it's pretty fun, well-written campy text that I enjoyed reading for the most part.The story ends on a cliffhanger. A pretty good cliffhanger after a twist that I absolutely didn't see coming, but I really don't like cliffhanger endings. Finish your stories, people. You don't know if you're ever going to get to make a sequel.Overall, I had a good time with this game. Would recommend to fans of fast-paced combat and platformers, if you can handle sub-optimal controls.

_childDocuments_.review: I finished the first tutorial mission but was more annoyed than entertained. The tutorial is obtrusive—telling you things that would be easier to figure out yourself—and also doesn't give you much space to practice the things you need to keep yourself alive. I died about 20 times before I even got to the boss, but not in a fun "I'll figure this out" way. It felt like the game was getting in my way.I think one issue is it dumps too many mechanics on you at once. The game would be significantly improved by giving you only one mechanic at a time—maybe even introducing one mechanic per level or something—and letting you practice and get used to it before introducing the next. As it was, I couldn't figure out (and didn't have time to figure out) when to use each of the various moves I had, and I kept getting tackled by a huge number of enemies, making it even more difficult to track what was happening or what I should do.The story bits I got didn't grab me enough to make me want to push past my initial annoyance, and the mechanics felt like they got in my way more than they made me feel like a badass. I can see the potential fun in it, but it's not for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Aesthetically it's nice. Does an overall good job of capturing the space western feel. There are only 3 enemies types - melee, ranged, and shield. Combat feels very samey because you're fighting the same guys over and over.Some boss fights are prohibitively difficult to do if you don't come into them with full health or extra stimpaks, so if you've reached the checkpoint before the boss and keep losing there's nothing for it but to restart the level or cheat.The third arm is really only good for two things. One is clearing space around you when you're surrounded. But since you'll do the most damage in melee anyway, there's not much use in flinging enemies away from you.  The other thing is breaking an enemy's guard, but you don't use energy when you do that so that energy bar will stay full most of the time. Guns are questionable. Pistols auto-aim but you can't control where they point. Your shotgun one-hit kills enemies but only if they're point-blank and not shielded. The game's story itself is not too long to tell or too complex, but it you only get exposition a few sentences at a time because everyone in the whole game insists on being coy.   Without spoiling anything - the classic structure for videogame stories is that in the last or second-to-last act, mysteries are revealed and your character gains some new power to overcome the final obstacle. "They Always Run" instead just *stops* when you've gained your new power and drops a weak sequel hook. I feel like the game's whole plot could have been wrapped up with another hour of play, two at most.

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly, I know the store page says it's a platformer, but I really think it's more of a 2D beat-em-up. By this, I mean combat is the main focus, not the platforming (which isn't great but I don't think it's a problem). And you should also expect some level of repetition that is standard in beat-em-ups.With that said, I really liked the game! For a beat-em-up to be good, you need to get 2 things right, it needs to feel satisfying to beat people up, and give the user a bunch of cool moves. This game got both right. The combat animation is so good (the game in general looks gorgeous). And you get so many moves (I LOVE how you keep getting new moves through out the entire game).What really sets this game apart is that it’s a beat-em-up that knows how to keep things fresh. You are not just beating people up for 6-8h. Fights are ALWAYS spaced out with light platforming bits (platforming is quite automated, but feels pretty cool cuz the animation), story progression/character interaction, getting new moves, or boss fights. It means the action doesn’t get old/tiring and I just want to keep playing. The story and characters are ok, too. There is a very well-done twist I won't spoil. What I really liked is how it’s integrated. I love how every bit og action has story reasons for why you are there, and there is a great mix of high-stake and low-stake missions.

_childDocuments_.review: We'll break this down piece by pieceVisuals and Art 5/5The game looks fantastic, the art style and design is likewise very aesthetically pleasing and good looking. The visuals are a call back to more retro games  from the 90s onward, similar to say Tree of Mana, Chrono Trigger, Metroid.Sound and Art Design 5/5The soundtrack is full of bangers, tis but a fact. The track 'Invisible' is fantastic beyond words. There isn't much to say here, if you've seen the official trailer and listened to the music in that, you have a good idea of what the quality is going to be.The sound effects all sound good, they're crisp and clean.Gameplay 4/5The gameplay is a blast, it's so very fun and makes you feel like a total badass when you play well. At first playing the game is very difficult, but once you start to get into the groove it gets easier and easier. The game rarely ever feels like it's unfair and generally when you die it's your fault. The flow of gameplay is smooth and quick(mostly, more on that later), and combat is solid given the price tag(if the asking price was higher for the game I'd be more critical of this).The difficulty curve is pretty solid, the game can be difficult at times but in a way that gets easier as you improve at the game, however there are issues. Stimpacks either need to heal more, or need to be more common, there were many times I fought a boss and had to play it perfectly to get through because I had no stims and no way to get more. This would be like playing Dark Souls but being stuck with 1-2 Estus charges and they very rarely replenished themselves, meaning in many fights you would have to play absolutely perfectly to get through.This problem was a big one for me, it was to the point I scoffed at having more room for more stimpacks because 90% of the time I was lucky to even have 2 of them at any given time.This is only made worse by the fact that you are only somewhat more durable than your enemies, enemy hits, especially ones from guns, can do a lot of damage very quickly. So generally because of the drought of stims your play has to be 100% on point.Another major issue with the gameplay is the flow, if you do die, and most likely you will a lot, unfortunately the game kills the pace of the gameplay by bringing up a menu, and asking you if you want to reload to last checkpoint, restart the level, or quit the game.This is not ideal, if a player wants to restart or quit, they are perfectly capable of doing it themselves by merely pressing ESC. So what the game should do instead is just immediately pop you back to the last checkpoint on its own without forcing the player to manually click a button whenever they die, which would not be so bad if you were not likely to die a lot.Ideally there would be no loading screen and like ULTRAKILL would allow you to press a button and immediately get back into the action.The final set of issues are mostly ones that could be solved with some polish. Many environmental hazards in the game are a 1HKO. The problems with this are that sometimes its not clear that something is a hazard(or even if it is, you might think it won't instantly kill you because there are hazards that only hurt you instead of kill you). Then there are hazards that...frankly I struggled to figure out how they are an instant kill, like an icicle embedded into the floor in front of you, it might hurt to run into it but I fail to see how it could kill you immediately.There are issues with hitboxes as well, while the hitboxes in the game are overall pretty tight, there was one boss that actually hit me while I was behind  him and his attack was not aimed at me, and some environmental hazards will kill you even when you do not appear to be physically touching them.Story 3/5The story is going to take some hard knocks on the score, not because it's bad, but because of something I will discuss down below, though there will be a spoiler warning.I love the story of this game, it's characters, it's world, I got very invested in it even if it is cliche in a number of ways. Even though the story is often cliche in a lot of ways, it presents itself in a way that still feels enjoyable and is just overall an adventure and an entertaining to the extreme. There are fun twists and turns with the story, the characters fun, and overall I got invested in the protagonists story.Now we'll discuss why the story gets such a hard knock, since there will be spoilers down below I am going to first give my overall score to the game.I'd rate this game with a 4 out of 5! A very hidden, underrated gem, I encourage people who enjoy games like castlevania, metroid, things like that to buy it!SPOILERS BELOW, DO NOT READ IF YOU DO NOT WANT SPOILERS!!!I am going to talk about why the story got knocked so bad for score, and why the game did not get a 5/5 from me, there is a very large problem with the story that was very upsetting for me. If you have already beat the game or do not care about spoilers, perhaps you're not very into narratives.If so then carry on reading.The main problem with the story? It ends on a bloody cliffhanger for God's sake, right when the story starts getting really good, when everything is coming together for a final boss/climax of the story. The fireworks are about to go off and they end the game right there.Right after we discover big plot reveals about what's going on with the main character, with the overarching plot, we find out Aiden is not actually a Three Arm, we find out that he was actually a guy named Dan whose friend was a three arm named Aiden who got killed and he trained to get revenge.We find out what the big bad evil guy's main plot is, he's got half the galaxy brought to it's knees so he can become the new Emperor, we want to see how Aiden(Dan) is going to come back getting beaten to get his ultimate revenge and stop the big bad evil guy.We get new questions when despite Dan's cyber third arm being ripped off, he gets this new cool technomagic arm thaat does super punching!Do we  get any resolution to any of this? Not a bit, Aiden(dan) gets his super cool magic arm, he fights off some guys...collapses.And the game ends, that's it, credits roll.To me, this is not only terrible from a story telling perspective, but it also means from my point of view, that the game is not even finished! This is not a finished product! You can't end the story and game right there when things are really getting good! That's terrible! We all know why, the ending to things is paramount in a narrative based game, the perfect proof of this is Mass Effect 3, the rage that was inspired by the ending to that game is legendary at this point, I am not equating this game to that fiasco, but I am using it as an example that endings are important

_childDocuments_.review: Summary: It would have been a classic if it were a PS1 release. Released now, it is a good-looking and well-executed cliche. I enjoyed my 5hr play-through, but as a someone on a budget I would recommend getting it on sale. I might revisit this again after a few months, it was enough fun to deserve it. Good platforming, simple but satisfying combat, a beautiful art style, and a slow-burn story that really makes it the well-executed cliche. It left me wanting more, so I'll be checking in with this developer.Gameplay: As stated above, the platforming is good and the combat is passable. That is the majority of what you will do, jump/climb/grapple around the 2D levels looking for extra loot while bashing through enemies. Some people have complained about the "QTE" combat, but it's not. It's a standard "react when you see the thing" setup like the Insomniac Spiderman game or Batman Arkham games. It's not revolutionary, but the stylized takedowns when you time it right are always satisfying.Art: Definitely a highlight. Both the visual art and the soundtrack are really nice. It won't stress your system unless you use a literal potato, but it still stands out and I like it. The locations don't throw it in your face or overstay their welcome and the music is nostalgic and fitting to the scene. It gets energetic for combat and chase scenes but wow did that ending strike me in the gut. Performance: Never had any issues. The combat and platforming didn't have input lag or weird responses. I include this because some people seem to have that in other reviews. I don't know, maybe they use potato computers.Characters and Story: I'll avoid spoilers. You're a 3-armed cyborg and galactic bounty hunter. The game begins with you taking down a bounty, who of course runs. As you take them in the story begins to hint at your past, but you shake it off and move onward. You gain allies and abilities that change how you move and fight. The characters themselves are all pretty simple. Like I said in the summary, a well-executed cliche. They do pretty well at making most characters, especially minor side characters, stand out visually. As with the overall game, they don't overstay their welcome.

_childDocuments_.review: They Always Run is a sci-fi sidescroller action-adventure game (NOT a metroidvania, in case you were wondering). You play as Aiden, a mutant cyborg bounty hunter with 3 arms. The third arm plays into the games mechanics as well as the story, which the game focuses on a lot more than I expected. It's a great game with a few flaws I'll address.First of all the pros: The graphics and music. This game nails it's art style, animation, and music that really sets the tone of the game. I always found myself being pulled in by its visuals and sound. Definitely top notch here.The gameplay is a side scroller action game with some platforming thrown in. For the most part, the game nails these elements. You have upgrades you can buy as you gain more credits by taking bounties which the game linearly throws at you, as well as killing regular enemies and such. That third arm I mentioned works a few different ways. It can break certain walls, stun enemies, or do other contextual actions. Certain bosses will have a health meter and a stamina meter. You have the option to either kill the boss by traditional means, or you can use your arm to knock that stamina meter down to knock them out and take them in alive. It's a cool idea that I liked, making you feel like a bounty hunter in a sci-fi wild west of sorts. The mechanics are very fun, if a bit basic.Now for the not-so good. The controls can be frustrating at times. I played with an Xbox controller, and the problem comes from the buttons being pressure sensitive. The game doesn't inform you of this though. So for example, if have to use your grappling hook, you can either use it to pull down a wall, or launch yourself towards a point of interest. The problem comes from certain life or death sequences. Need to pull down a wall? You have to hold down LB. Need to launch yourself? It's the same button, but you better tap it. It doesn't sound bad, but there were way too many cheap deaths because of this. I was hitting the button, but just not in the right way (and again, the game never tells you this. It just tells you what button to press). Not sure how it is on KB and M, but this was my experience.Lastly is the story. For a side scroller action game, this has a LOT of dialogue, and none of it is voiced. It has speech bubbles that you can skip, but sometimes they come up at inopportune times, like when fighting something. It's hard to read something when I have something else more pressing happening. But the story itself is entertaining and I enjoyed it for the most part. However, the ending is abrupt and ends on a cliffhanger that felt like the devs just didn't have enough time to finish, so it might continue in a possible sequel or DLC. The ending sequence I LOVED, but was shocked that it just stopped when it did and the credits rolled. Which is unfortunate, because most of the rest of the game was pretty awesome.I definitely recommend it if it looks cool to you. It just has some obvious flaws that are hard to ignore. Some cheap deaths with partially flimsy controls and an unfinished story, but a really cool and fun atmosphere that was great to play.

_childDocuments_.review: This game just oozes style. As a 90s kid who grew up with a Sega Mega Drive (Genesis), They Always Run reminded me of several games from that generation, but with some gorgeous artwork and lighting made possible by virtue of modern technology. Seriously, the way that light plays across Aiden’s poncho is gorgeous when stepping in and out of lit sections.I actually played a demo of this game last summer during the Steam indie event; It’s interesting to see that the developers ditched the non-lethal vs lethal upgrade system. In general, it feels like the premise of being a bounty hunter with a choice of targets and modus operandi was scaled back to get the game out. The full game ended up being more linear (in terms of planets/targets) and more story driven than I expected. To the somewhat negative extent that scenes can change abruptly and new characters are introduced in a flash. It’s not bad, but it felt rushed to me.The game is short enough that the gameplay doesn’t overstay its welcome. I would have liked a few extra melee options, such as a power attack or pause combos, but generally the combat works well. The platforming is similar enough with upgrades adding variety as you progress through the game. A particular frustration was with platforming during a later level set in an ice cave, where twitch-like reflexes are required to pass a couple of sections. This sudden difficulty spike is gone almost as soon as it appears, but I felt it was worth mentioning here as it feels overturned by omission.Small complaint, but why is 'Buy Ammo in the Store 25 Times' an achievement? Why not something that can be completed in a single playthrough, like get the majority of upgrades? Otherwise it's a fair list that you can get in one run by being thorough.Overall, I was left wanting more! I get the feeling that the original scope I gleaned in the demo might (hopefully) be realised in a sequel!

_childDocuments_.review: At the time I am writing this I just finished watching the end credits roll over my screen. According to Steam I spent almost 9 hours playing this game; that is with me having to replay an entire level due to a progress-stopping game breaking bug at the end of one level (though it was partly my fault for getting stuck in that situation), and having died a fair amount of times - particularly during some frustrating jumping sequences that leave no margin for error. Moreover, despite the game being pretty linear I tried to find most of the secrets in the levels, so someone who is better at platforming and rushes straight through the levels can easily subtract two or even three hours from my playtime.So, what *is* They Always Run?In essence, a mostly linear sidescroller with tight combat and a few annoying platforming sequences set in a sci-fi setting. You are playing as Aiden, a three-armed bounty hunter on a personal quest for revenge.I won't cover any of the story details here to avoid spoilers, but I can honestly say that I enjoyed it, and it was one of the reasons I kept playing despite ragequitting the game once or twice.What sets the game apart is its art style - characters and backgrounds are made up of detailed 2D graphics, and the lighting (rim lighting in particular) is really well done here, giving an illusion of depth to the scene. The animations are mostly good and very stylized, although I remember a few coming across as a little janky-looking.Speaking of jank, the controls are... a mixed bag. For the most part, combat feels really good and satisfying, and despite the overall limited number of enemy (arche)types it rarely gets boring. However, with some enemies, including bosses, you end up fighting the controls more than the enemies, often leading to Aiden's untimely death. Most bosses require running, jumping and dashing around most of the time with short intervalls inbetween where you get to pummel them. The issue is that the player character often doesn't stop movent in time and starts a combo (or interrupts it) by lurching forward instead of remaining in place during the attack. This is particularly annoying when you are attacking an enemy from behind and end up dashing right into their attack. It should also be mentioned that Aiden can't take too many hits, and healing items are rare in each level (and you can't buy them, only find them as drops from enemies or in chests). So often made me restart from a checkpoint if I took too much damage during a fight, which isn't exactly great game design, IMHO.Additionally, there are also a few bugs left in the game. One particularly nasty one required me to replay an entire level from start to finish including the boss. At the end of the level you are usually required to carry the bounty back to the ship, and this requires you to traverse the level back to the beginning or to a different location - either way, it's usually a trip that is filled with traps and enemies. To deal with those, Aiden has to let go of the bounty and pick it up after taking care of them.On one such occasion I didn't realize I could actually climb down a ladder with the bounty because the controls were so unresponsive - no kidding! - that I thought I could only climb UP with a bounty. As a result I ended up leaving the bounty on the ground, thinking I would need to unlock a shortcut first... Well, turns out there is a certain point on the way back to the ship were you can't turn back, and the game decided to autosave right after, so I was screwed.On the upside, replaying the level wasn't as tough as the first time because I already had the patterns for most enemies encounters, traps and jumping sequences down. Same goes for the boss.Speaking of bosses, they are real damage sponges, and some of their attack patterns can be nasty and hard to avoid. They are also highly damaging so you can't take too many hits. Moreover, if you happen to run out of healing items just before a boss you're ♥♥♥♥ out of luck.The balance when it comes to bosses is generally weird. Some bosses can either be brought in dead or alive. In order to kill them you just need to keep hitting them with your swords and guns; to stun and bring them in alive you need to hit them with your arm, preferably with powered attacks (think of it as ammo for your third arm, which only replenish one by one upon countering enemy attacks). Unfortunately it looks like some bosses have been tweaked post release to take much, much more stun damage than they used to, which makes them nigh impossible to bring in alive (Colonel Mueller is one such case).That being said, the bosses for the most part aren't as hard as they appear at first once you learn their patterns. In the end it most often boils down to a marathon where you try to wear them down bit by bit... Annoying, but doable.Does They Always Run have it's share of problems? For sure. It's janky at times, and some parts of the game are infuriating. But overall it isn't too hard or frustating, and I found the experience rewarding. Plus I liked the characters, story, setting and art style (so, so MUCH!)... And I'm probably alone in this but I actually liked the ending, even if it felt slightly anticlimactic and sudden. Either way, I want, nay, demand a sequel!Purchase or no purchase? I'd say play the demo and buy the game if you liked it... and have some tolerance towards frustration. It's still a good game with its own unique character, despite the flaws.

_childDocuments_.review: Although I recommend this game, it leans on a maybe, I understand it was made by a small team, but there are a lot of obvious cut corners and a lot of spots in the game that just doesn't feel right, to cut to the chase.TLDR: 6.5/10Story: Overall good, no overt cliches or tropes other than ones that would be obvious for a setting like this. The game does excellently on getting you to feel immersed and it builds up the world pretty well, however, and this is a problem I will be mentioning often, due to cut corners there are a bunch of reused models everywhere, and when you see the same 5 faces everywhere it starts to break the immersion. The story made me smile, and there are good jokes here and there, but I wouldn't put it anywhere near a top 10 it's just good, and that is fine in my books. One last thing I will note in this section is during dialogue it will always skip to the next piece of text after a couple of seconds I wish there was a way to turn this off, as sometimes im comprehending information and then realize it skipped several pieces of dialogue.Gameplay:Feels good, for being a three armed badass machine it does great in making you feel that way, and there is a bunch of attention to detail that helps, from hitting behind you with your third arm, to pulling a third gun to help you mow down multiple enemies at a time. There are a multitude of gameplay elements that rely on your third arm and I love it, however, there are times when the game feels clunky, pieces of combat or platforming that just doesn't mesh with the rest. For combat I would tie this to how there isn't a set time when enemies will start blocking its just random, for platforming the chainlink walls feel much slower than the rest of the platforming making it seem like you are spending twice as long on those sections than any other part of the platforming, definitly gives off the feeling of cut corners. Difficulty:I am having this separate from gameplay because the difficulty is weird, for a majority of this game you breeze through it, however, there are small details that make the game harder at times, for one healing. You heal from stimpacks or in the rare ocassion of increasing your health bar, stimpacks however, are completly random to find, it does seem that they are more common when you are at low health, but despite this you can go on for a large portion of a level without finding a single one. This makes things difficult for lets say a boss fight, where the game often does not give you any healing before the fight, so you are forced to fight at a disadvantage against the boss due to a lack of healing items. I will mention there are abilities and powers that just never get used, and for some of those they get completly reset upon death which makes it so fighting a boss gets exponentially harder after the first try. Going back to the stimpacks, I'm not sure why they didn't make it so that you can buy stimpacks with credits, there are very few consumables you can buy and that would help if someone wanted to be overly prepared for a level, I should add, you can increase your cap for stimpacks, however at the rate you get them you won't ever be capped, I was maxed on stimpacks once in the entire game. So basically, the game is easy, until you land in a bad spot not knowing the boss was just coming up and are forced to fight the boss on effectively hard mode.Art/Music:Fantastic, however, the cut corners make it so that their are sections of the game where you will just see a pretty obvious slowly moving stagnant png, which, can be quite jarring at times. Not a whole lot else to say for this section, the art is great, lots of tiny objects that didn't need a bunch of effort that definitly seems like they got every piece of effort and more, same to the music which fits perfectly for the game's genre.Overall good games but would have been MUCH better if they spent another 2-3 months fixing some of the rough edges and cut corners.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun platformer with a nice bounty hunter story to it. Cool timed combat with ability progress system, advance as you gain more money from your bounties. You have the choice to kill your bounties or capture them alive, after what I understand this impacts the story line.Can recommend if you love old school platformers like me. If you played and loved games like Katana Zero, The Messenger, Mark of the Ninja, Dust: An Elysian Tail ect ect, you probably love to have this in the your collection too. _childDocuments_.review: Such a great little game.If you want some tight action combined with some light platforming this is definitely recommended. It's not a difficult game, I'm just decent at platformers and I finished it without problems. The games has some AMAZING artstyle and music in it and coupled with the really nice animations it makes for some really nice combat moments. The combat is focused on dodging and parrying and also has a ranged element (which is very overpowered) and it's quite good, but lacks in enemy variety. The story was also a stand out, I was just expecting it to be a "hunt targets all game" thing, but it keeps you engaged all the time, just shining enough light on the mystery each mission to keep you wanting to see more.Now for the bad parts: the character has momentum during jumps, meaning he doesn't stop immediately when landing, which is really bad in a platformer, but since the platforming isn't that hard I got over it. The game also has really few bosses, if you can even call them that; and the last boss especially disappoints. It also ends on a cliffhanger which is a bummer since the story is actually really nice. Also, like I said, the enemy variety is low.For the price or especially on sale, I think it's worth it, if you just want to look like a badass mandalorian-type bounty hunter just speeding through levels and slaying enemies with style. Just don't expect any challenging content.Hope to see improvements in the next one form the devs. They definitely have potential.
_childDocuments_.name: They Always Run

_childDocuments_.review: Flow of combat is really good once you get used to the controls. Characters and character banter are not unlikable, which is rare in modern gaming space. Story is also interesting and plot twist is really well done. However, platforming is janky and most importantly only 4 stages of 6 stage plot structure exist. Game ends in a heavy sequel bait cliffhanger without resolving pretty much anything.
_childDocuments_.name: They Always Run

_childDocuments_.review: The game have it flaws. You can see that team was pretty small, but in the other hand they tried to make a decent project. Ye animations are cluncky, not that much secrets/upgrades, crates have usually only money/ammo which reduces your desire to hunt them, plot is linear and there is not much happening(exept ending). But in the other hand design/OST manages to create awesome atmosphere, and thats why I love indie games like that. They usually strive more towards gameplay and immersion(like old games did — chrono trigger/metroid etc). Gameplay looks hard but is actually pretty simple and after you pass the tutorial you are set to kick some ass like a cool looking 3handed bounty hunter.In the end i must say that i've completed the game and very happy about it. I had my 10+ hours of fun and the ending brought a tear to my eye. I know that DEVs see their flaws and I hope that there will be "they always run 2" at some point with better animations/gameplay mechanics, because the concept is pretty cool and engaging which is the main thing.
_childDocuments_.name: They Always Run

_childDocuments_.review: Good: Beautiful art/animation, fun space bounty hunter concept, & when it's clicking, the combat is fun and stylish. I LOVE the cool 3rd Arm concept and gameplay (sometimes it reminds me of the free form controls of the whips in Castlevania games). It's cool to be incentivized to capture bounties alive for more money. Something subtle that I really like is the variety of animations during melee combat. It is not just a basic looking 3 hit combo. Aidan does backflips, dropkicks, sweeps, etc. It looks great even though I'm just spamming the x button. Last but not least the soundtrack is really good and fits well with the space western vibes.  Bad: The controls could be tighter. This really shows itself in the platforming sequences (which is half the game). It just feels a bit off at times. Like the controls are at odds with the animation at times. There are escape or chase sections where there were plenty of times I missed a jump during the controls not being more precise. Fortunately the checkpointing is very forgiving.Also the transitions from location to location is a bit jarring since there are few non-engine cuts scenes outside the same ship enter orbit animation. Many times I was just talking to someone and then BOOM jump cut to Aidan on his ship on another planet. Perhaps this was a budget issue.   Overall It's not perfect, and it could use an update or two, it's greater than the sum of its parts. I'm enjoying the game and for $20 I can recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: They Always Run

_childDocuments_.review: A solid bounty hunter game with a decent story and bunch of great world building both subtle and obvious.  Only real criticisms are that there are some platforming spots which are glaringly tighter than the rest of the game which really throws you off, and it looks like certain things were scaled back from the demo, such as the blackmarket having less than 1/4 of the number of available items/upgrades.  It is worth noting, that the game is under 6hrs long, I just took a bit longer because I got a progression stopping bug and spent far too long trying to get around it.
_childDocuments_.name: They Always Run

_childDocuments_.review:
The galaxy's inhabitants have been swamped by crime since the fall of the empire. Being able to find anyone, anywhere has become a highly prized skill.

Aidan is a three-armed bounty hunter who must hunt down the most dangerous and elusive cutthroats in the galaxy.

Some bounties are rewarded with money, others with valuable information that Aidan can use to find the people who set him on this path all while getting embroiled in a galaxy-wide conspiracy.

Hunt criminals across the fringes of the galaxy, the core worlds, and the ruins of long-gone civilizations. Upgrade your equipment, gain new abilities, grow stronger and destroy anything that stands in your way.

Enjoy a complex story interwoven with high-octane gameplay and full of twists and turns that hit as hard as a bounty hunter's third arm!
_childDocuments_.name: They Always Run

name: Lil Gator Game
detailed_description: More from Playtonic Friends About the Game There’s a buddy atop every hill in this open-world, movement-focused adventure and they all seem to need help! Bop cardboard baddies, brave serene hills and forests, and scale sheer rocks that only a kid would dare! Explore a lovingly crafted island full to the brim with areas to discover, friends to make and joy to be had. Each area of the island brings unique quests and characters to meet. Glide through the mountain tops and drop in on the Theatre Troupe kids, swing your stick sword through the forest with the Prep schoolers or find the ‘Cool Kids’ down in the Creaklands. With plenty more areas to discover, there's no knowing who you might run into! The world is big when you’re a lil gator... Good thing it’s also full of friends! Make new friends and invite them to play in the islands playground. Each new friend you make will add to your adventure, but making new friends isn’t always easy, You might have to complete a quest or two! Collect arts & crafts supplies all over the island! Use them to make yourself all kinds of goodies and bring the playground to life! Craft new abilities - use your ragdoll teddy to ragdoll lil gator from mountain top to the valleys below! Skim pebbles into hard to reach cardboard baddies! A no-pressure adventure game! Lil Gator game focuses on adventure and play, don't let a health bar hold you back from reaching your goal!

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine your six years old again and it's fall break. You just found the coolest looking stick on the ground you have ever seen, and you feel ready to take on the world. But then...ALL your friends show up too! That is Lil Gator Game. In the span of eight hours I cried, laughed loudly enough it startled my cat on accident (oops), and buried my face in my hands from puns. Don't let the cartoony graphics fool you, this game has plenty for all ages, and I'd even argue gets better with age. Embark on a epic adventure, grow personally, explore, problem solve, parkour, and most importantly, vanquish evil only as a lil gator can.
_childDocuments_.name: Lil Gator Game

_childDocuments_.review: This game and its characters really show how strong friendships are and how much of an impact life makes for us as we grow older.It's a cute and yet powerful exchange with very-notable references of adventure and courage, as well as a really soothing soundtrack to swing, waddle around or even ragdoll and tumble down hills in. The game's gimmicks of skills, weapons and other equipment are very unique and seem to attract an audience that admires a carefree trip into nostalgia.As of writing this review, I'm only two hours in and I just love it!Five hours in: I may have spent at least one genuine hour ragdolling around and tickling myself pink.Eight hours in + final summary: Make that two hours of ragdolling, but also reiterating the powerful motive with this game. This game has had me shed some tears and be reminded the importance of family and friends. Sometimes you just need a break and hang out with them, after all. Fantastic game, perfected it and will play again.Nine+ hours and however many more that may follow: Ragdolling and listening to the soundtrack to soothe my stresses away. Also, I really have to say:I wish this game was out before the voting period ended for this year's Steam Awards, because this game really deserves one.Eleven+ hours in: voting this game as Best Soundtrack and Sit Back and Relax. Vote for this game!!

_childDocuments_.review: My experience in this game felt like a mashup of *Breath of the Wild* and *Animal Crossing*, but without the building or organizing of things in either. You do a little bit of exploring, a good bit of chuckling, a lot of laughing, a surprising amount of frowning, and a dash of crying. All in all, it was a wonderful experience, and one that was full of memorable dialogue. I'd love to play this game again, but, just, like, more of it. Bigger. _childDocuments_.review: A delightfully charming game. I was cracking a smile in every-other conversation and laughing heartily frequently. The challenges are minimal, so you're really here for the dialog and maybe the 100%-ing. The latter is made easier by two post-game items that allow you to find quests you haven't completed and "monsters" you haven't defeated.It took me about 3 hours to complete the story, with occasional distractions. I'm probably not going to 100% this one, despite my usual inclinations, because I feel like it would sully the "playing for fun" spirit of the game. I might come back later for some more romps, though.This is a 5/7 on my rating scale. Excellent example of its genre, but maybe not for everyone. Well worth the 20$ asking price if you want some charm, some laughs, and some low-stress platforming/questing.
_childDocuments_.name: Lil Gator Game

_childDocuments_.review: This game looks like it's meant for preschoolers. And a preschooler could play it--it's a supersimple platformer, like Mario 64 or Crash Bandicoot. You run around an island, doing small collect quests for people to get them to join your imagination game. There's no death, no fighting, just exploration and a little-puzzle solving and searching. There's nothing hard about this game. And yet I was compelled to play, to find all the goodies. Something about the story--that you were a little kid and you were playing while your sister is nearby, but distracted by her college work. The game is simple, yet elegant, with a relatable theme.
_childDocuments_.name: Lil Gator Game

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games I've ever played. Perfectly captures what it was like to be a child and lets you relive it in vivid detail. Sharp, clever humour mixed with charming music and aesthetics. Regardless of what any reviews or critics say, this is an immersive masterpiece. Would highly recommend to anyone and everyone, regardless of their prior experience in other games.One of the few games I'd give a 10/10, right next to Okami HD and Outer Wilds. I can't imagine why it hasn't gotten much attention apart from its short length. I got it on sale, but if you ask me it'd be worth it even if its list price was $5 more.

_childDocuments_.review: When I first purchased this game my husband said, "looks like a nice game for a 7 year old." Two hours later he was having a blast watching me skateboard around with a bucket on my head while chopping down cardboard monsters.There were two things that I didn't like about the game though, and they were one; that there was no mini-map. I feel like this was done intentionally to pad the game play time a bit, because I know I spent quite a bit of time running around trying to find areas/people again after wandering off, and this could have easily been solved by having access to a map. Second, there is no quest journal. It got a little bit annoying trying to remember or figure out who or where I was supposed to go after I finished a quest or got sidetracked. Eventually after wandering around mindlessly for a bit I ran into the people/places I need to be, but it sometimes got frustrating.It's a great game though, really. No pressure or stressful situations to deal with. Just good ol' wholesome fun for players of any age.

_childDocuments_.review: Loved this little title. Definitely one I had a lot of fun with and didn't expect the ending to come. Gotta appreciate how nice short and sweet games are. _childDocuments_.review: Game was very fun and emotional. If you are a fan of sincere storytelling this game is great for you, the ending had me tearing up. Even though the story was emotional near the end, there were many moments of levity through the humor which never failed to make me chuckle. This game is on the shorter side but it is still well worth your money for the experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I preface this by saying that i rarely write reviews.Finished in one sitting on stream, and it was some of the most fun i've had in a long time. Lots of fun ideas (theres literally a ragdoll button and a sticky hand you can use as a grappling hook) and i really hope to see these devs continue making great games like this.While yes, it is a short game (about 3-4 hours to beat the main story) there are still things for the completionists out there, and even items after the main story to make completing the game easier.Buy this game, play this game, and for those like me that cry easily, prepare yourselves.

_childDocuments_.review: Reminds me a bit of A Short Hike, and tbh, i liked ASH a bit more...ASH had some more varied puzzles and secret things to find.However, this game oozes feels and cutemess...the joy in wearing a bucket on my head or making my character naruto run around this gorgeous island was well worth the price. _childDocuments_.review: Gator Game is a wholesome platformer where you play a lil Gator. The controls are solid and tight being able to platform similar to Mario Odyssey and LoZ: BotW. The game is very cute and has the innocence of playing make believe and enjoying the adventures that we create when we are young.You will get lost and act on your instincts to be just a lil silly Gator.Great game and great experience. Perfect amount of content that doesn't get annoying or repetitive.

_childDocuments_.review: So this, this was a fantastic little experience that I thoroughly recommend. It had fun, drama, twists and adventure but from all the things in this cute little game about being a smol gator pal and having mischief with your friends, I didn't expect to cry. Not that it's a bad thing, not in any way. Sometimes, something comes along which reminds us that it's okay to cry, or okay to play, or relish in our childish side. Other times, we have to be grown ups, even if we - or others - don't want us to.This really was enjoyable, and whole heartedly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Cute & Wholesome game, where the world if your playground. World is a joy to explore and quests aren't a chore and are different from each other. Only minus that I do have for this game is that one of the achievements is a bit annoying (destroy every breakable object), thankfully game does give you radar for them. Overall game is really similar to one of my favorites "A short hike", if you enjoyed that game you will most likely enjoy this game too.
_childDocuments_.name: Lil Gator Game

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked playing A Short Hike, Lil Gator Game would be right up your alley. It is a game full of charm and adorable characters.It's not a hard game, nor a long game (I actually played through twice and purposely took my time exploring the second playthrough just to see if I could get everything before finishing out the game). Actually now that I think about it, this game has the sort of relaxing zen charm that allows for re-playability like Short Hike or Unpacking even though nothing changes. It's the kind of game you play when you really want to chill.I recommend the game if you want something relaxing and heartwarming to play in between longer more intensive games.

_childDocuments_.review: A short -- but very sweet -- game that continually left me grinning and chuckling. It's fun exploring the island discovering what zany quests the other kids have for you to accomplish, and with a multitude of fun gadgets and gizmos -- some of which are huge movement-boosters. There are also a huge assortment of cosmetic items you earn from completed quests, which remind you of missions accomplished and friends made. The premise is heart-warming, the writing is light-hearted and optimistic -- the polar opposite of the often-jaded writing styles of modern indie games. The whole experience left me with a smile on my face and hope in my heart that more games take this approach to open-world adventures with twists-and-turns around every corner!A fantastic game, I would absolutely recommend it!

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah, I cried at the end.There's so much I want to say about this game to explain why I love it so much, but words are failing me. It's one of those things where it's difficult to describe your feelings. While the "physical" stuff of the game is awesome, I think what makes this game extra special is that evokes such emotion in the player.It's much more than just a cute game. Well... it IS adorable, which is one of its main charms, of course. When I first saw the trailer I pretty much screamed internally because it was so damn cute.But there's something so heartfelt about the story and characters. The gameplay itself is comforting and it's hard not to feel happy when running around the island as a small alligator. The controls add to this experience and there are very little limitations. It's pleasant and easy-going.Interacting with more and more characters solidified my love for the game. They join the playground when you befriend them! It's so endearing.There are items to collect too, and I think the number is just right at 48 total. It enhances the personality of the game, especially the descriptions in the inventory.The developers did a really good job of making you so involved in the story that the ending part hits hard. The writing is wonderful; the music is sweet; the visuals are lovely. In particular, I love the autumnal theme and every time I played I wanted to go to a park and sit amongst the trees. It just feels like genuine, pure fun to play this game. If you like cosy games you'll surely like this one too.Lil Gator Game, I will see you again.

As a good friend of mine put it This games achievements aren't hard to get and there isn't any miss-able ones on a first play-through. _childDocuments_.review: Lil Gator Game is a wholesome, charming, cute embodiment of childhood. It encapsulates all the wonder and magic within a childs mind, a perfect way to relive and experience those youthful days, the game feels as though it's for kids by kids while simultaneously having dialogue and humour that can be appreciated by adults, it felt like a huge nostalgia trip for me and I'm sure anyone older would agree that while playing this cute lil gator you are reminded of the wonders of childhood, the game is so well crafted to tug at our heart strings: there is so much relatablity whether you are a kid playing through this cute little adventure game, a teen in the midst of life, or an adult going through it all, this game has a way of speaking to you and just filling you with such good vibes, I couldn't wipe the smile off my face as I kept playing and reading all these lil animal friends talking with one another and playing together. It's such a great feeling to feel this joy from something so simple (and so adorable). Just as a personal note, this game is even more special to me since my boyfriend so graciously gifted it to me, so if you are thinking of getting this gem for yourself or anyone else I'd highly recommend. Now some of the actual "gameplay" review: you might feel like some of the quests become repetitive, since it is alot of "kill these monsters" "race" or "find this thing" but I honestly did not find it an issue, since all the interactions with the characters are so unique and different each time, there is also deviation with the Raccoon and the Monkey, I felt excited to help them and have them apart of my playground town. All the designs of the characters are so cute, of course having animal characters in a game isn't the most original concept, but it doesn't matter since it's executed so well here: having a shark lose his retainers or a whale that is so much bigger then everyone else really adds to the immersion of this wholesome atmosphere. The design of the game is wonderful, all the monster designs and equipment is so charming, even though you do see a lot of the same creatures it was nice seeing certain ones pop up in specific areas, and with all the goofy equipment that your lil gator could wear would always give me a chuckle. The mechanics of the game are not complicated at all so literally anyone could pick it up and it's nice that the more you do, the more you unlock. The artstyle, like the design, really suits the vibe they were going for and the music and sound design further compliments that. The whole gaming experience was a pleasure and I'm so glad I played it. As a side note, the end game feels so rewarding and as a person who loves achievement hunting and going for the 100% it was so nice to see the game actually think of that and assist me with that once I had finished the game. This game, as most indie games, is such a breath of fresh air and a lovely break from other games that steam has to offer. So go play Lil Gator Game! A lovely way to experience childhood again while having a good laugh, wholesome fun for anyone^^

_childDocuments_.review: Open-world games have a difficult and often impossible line to balance: On one hand, there's creating large, expansive sandboxes to make it look like the game will be a colossal experience, while on the other, ensuring that there are enough activities and content to keep said sandbox from feeling like one big hiking trip. Lil Gator Game forgoes that first point to make instead a delightful adventure that can be finished in a few play sessions that's up to its ears in charm, comedy and charming comedy. When my only 'major' criticism is that the script can sometimes be a little too silly, this game is a delight and then some.Lil Gator Game's premise is creating a grand adventure and play session for Lil Gator's (the playable character) Big Sis, who's visiting from college but is stuck doing academic work. While creating this game for her to play, Lil Gator themselves goes on a grand adventure to recruit others to assist in the project. There won't be personnel or base management, as recruiting friends involves finding them and completing a quest, be it locating something, smashing cardboard monsters or conducting a time trial. Excluding the major quests that lead to the game's finale and use these recruited friends, these smaller tasks take only a few minutes and often will point you toward other characters to talk to, or cardboard entities to bop for more loot (the in-game currency).Rewards are regular in the game, as some quests award new equipment that is often just aesthetic in terms of their use but can have additional effects, like a headband that lets you run faster or a trampoline shield that's unruly to handle but lets you get great air. Lil Gator isn't the swiftest reptile on foot (though their waddling is adorable), but when combining movement options like gliding, shield surfing and hovering, getting around feels satisfying, doubly so when chaining these movement techniques together. They're seldom-needed save for cases of needing to get somewhere high or doing a time trial, but goofing around still feels fun and can lead to new discoveries.This isn't the most challenging game out there, as most of the challenge comes from getting around or finding the right angle/height to hit cardboard enemies or pots. Aside from the presentation and satisfying (if simple) movement, the main appeal comes from its writing and charm. Being a story about a younger sibling trying to help their older one have fun from 'adult stuff', the kids (and occasional adults) you'll meet around the island all have simple and kid-like problems to solve: One wants to help revive a sapling, while another wants to fit in with 'cool kids' by using the most rad pose possible. One kid wants a tea party with their busy parent, while another wants to make amends with their friends. It's all so endearingly wholesome and frequently funny, to boot. Some gags and jokes caught me off-guard and made me laugh out loud. The script did dip into randomly silly dialogue that felt like it was trying too hard to elicit a laugh, but it always stayed within its welcome and avoided detracting from the other, better jokes. Other than the finale turning me into an absolute wreck of an emotional mess, I had a big ol' smile while playing Lil Gator Game from start to end.Excluding some anti-aliasing and lightning bugs here and there, Lil Gator Game is not the most technical game in terms of its visuals, but they're a dream to look at. Even with its bright colors, the art style keeps the world grounded and realistic with its autumnal weather when hoofing it around in the lowlands or higher up in the hills, with vibrant orange, yellow and green leaves both fallen and on trees. Added to this is the dynamic soundtrack with a folksy arrangement that only adds to the childlike glee about this 'little big' adventure, making exploring for loot and quests have the added benefit of giving you regularly changing music to mellow out with.I finished Lil Gator Game in about 4.8 hours, and with some apparent secrets and 100% to strive for, the replay value is only the best if you're interested in the speedrunning tools. With a price tag of $25.99 (CAD), I was also hoping for a bit more in terms of content, namely with minigames or mobility options - There is a piece of equipment that lets you ragdoll on command so that alone had sold me once I found it. Lil Gator Game is mainly about exploring, its story and experiencing the delightful comedy it has to offer. You won't be hard-pressed for challenging inputs or much decision-making outside of your equipment for style points, so if you're the type who wants more agency in their gameplay outside of which direction to go next, you may not enjoy yourself fully. Past that caveat? I absolutely recommend Lil Gator Game as a short but wonderfully sweet joy.

_childDocuments_.review: when discussing sable, jacob geller proposed it as the perfect Mid-Sized Breath Of The Wild, a comfortably sprawling point between the massiveness of BOTW proper and the bite-sized single-setting take on many of its aspects in a short hike. lil gator game sits between a short hike and sable on this imaginary scale and as much as i appreciate all these games (especially sable) this may very well be my fave of them all!! its kind of incredibly how expressively each game's runtime informs its overall feel but lil gator game is the absolute perfect Exhaustingly Joyful Afternoon, it somehow doesnt feel like a micro-anything it just feels like a real time day spent in exhilarating childhood antics. even more then breath of the wild or a short hike it reminds me of other works that concern themselves with Imaginative Play: the lessons in empathy across age gaps from spike jonze's where the wild things are, the whisperingly quiet melancholy of what drives reality into fantasy from calvin and hobbes, and the quiet radicalism re: the emotional and spiritual *necessity* of imaginative play from bluey. it is very humble and warm, mostly lacking the overt quirkiness that characterizes a lot of the modern flavor of Indie Game Twee (which is something im fond of, if not entirely enamored with) in favor of calmer colors, both literal and emotional. when these types of games fold into an emotional crescendo my response is usually nice enough (i am quite open to these things) but i swear this one even tho its not insistent at all just hit me with tons of Inexplicable Feelings out of nowhere. i feel like someday i have to take a real hard crack at writing ab Imaginative Play and art about it, prob turn it into something political and spiritual. but at the heart of any such thesis no matter how many big words i lay on top will be a relatively simple texture, an almost mundane ecstasy, and this game perhaps more then any other work ive encountered is essentially nothing but that texture and that ecstasy in its most potent, concentrated formit's a lot of work to make a game. there are lots of better things our work could be used for then the things we do now. we must re-learn how to imagine things being different
