_childDocuments_.review: I have so much I could say about this charming little game, though I will keep it short for the sake of convenience.First off, I would like to say that I LOVE the story behind this game. Short and simple, yet is capable of taking you on an adventure all it's own. A story truly unique to itself, as I have yet to see a tale quite like this in my decades of gaming. Plus, it delves into emotional problems we've all been through: acceptance of loss, change and moving on. All while keeping a childhood vibe 100% of the way.Second, I would like the address the overall quality of this game. Absolutely fantastic. This game is like a quilt made by your grandma with love in every stitch. No two NPCs are alike at all. The dialogue fits the theme like a glove and doesn't feel generic. For example, quests in this game don't give me a skyrim-like "kill 10 bears" vibe, which I find not only super-lazy, but increasingly common these days. The quests in this game may be short, but they aren't lazily made.Lastly, I would like to comment on the SIZE of this game. Dear devs, how on earth did you pack all that...into just 500MB??? What sorcery is this? And everything looks fantastic (for the game's size). Honestly the graphics fit the theme so well, you can't tell that the game is so small.Overall, this game is fantastic. And it's also priced perfectly. It's nice to see a small group care so much about the quality of the games they make. We got WAAAY too many of 'em out here just puking up cash-grabs. In fact, the only gripe I can even conjure up is that, sadly, I can never experience this wonderful little game for the first time again.Rating: 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Game received as a gift from my spouse during the winter sale.Good, cute, fun and wholesome game where you are a kid gator on a pretend adventure and trying to reconnect with your college-age older sister.  You jump, glide, climb, and skateboard your way around 2 islands while swinging a wooden sword (or other objects) at cardboard cutouts of monsters, then use the broken cardboard to craft new items.  You help other animals along the way to build a playground into a town to impress your "Big Sis," and both Lil Gator and Big Sis learn something by the end.  Not too long (100%'d it in just under 5 hours in a single afternoon between managing loads of laundry), did not overstay its welcome for what the gameplay offers, and definitely accomplishes what it set out to do without trying to do too much.  You can tell the devs put a lot of heart and care into this.  Played the whole thing on my Steam Deck, and it definitely deserves the Verified compatibility rating.I only have one real criticism, and it's that I would have found some kind of map screen helpful, to just orient where you are and where you're facing to landmarks to make finding your way around a bit easier.  I found myself getting turned around and wandering aimlessly a fair bit before getting back on track to finding what I was looking for.  Since Lil Gator carries around a phone, some kind of in game Google or Apple Maps seems like it could fit in seamlessly.I will also admit part me thinks 20 USD as base price might be a bit steep for what the game is - I wouldn't blame anyone who finds 20 USD for a 4-5 hour game a little too much.  I'd still recommend this to someone looking for a chill, shorter adventure game, and definitely recommend to nearly anyone once it starts to go on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: When I bought this game, I expected a cute simple 3D platformer game with elements from breath of the wild, and like most cutesy 3D platformers, I expected the story to be an afterthought and quite frankly the last thing I cared about.This game's story struck me in a way that not many others have. No game has captured the feeling of being a child quite like the sense of nostalgia this game has. When i say nostalgia, I mean real nostalgia. I don't mean "wow! this game is like games from back in the day! #retro so cool!!" I mean it brings me back to how childhood was for me. I was the youngest of four siblings, and vividly remember the creativity my siblings would bring to the table when we would play together. Specifically my older sisters. And of course as I got older, they didn't have time to play anymore. But playing is all that ever really made sense to me. I didn't do well in school, even today the concept of working a full time job horrifies me. What is the point of having a promising career if you feel emotionally and socially unfulfilled? It can be a lot harder to balance that kind of thing for neurodivergent people like myself. I actually started this game after my first day at an office job that quite frankly made me miserable. I had no time to myself even when my shift was over. And I kept thinking, what is the point of living if i can't play games? It is so important to prioritize your own happiness, and this game came at such an important moment for me. That isn't to say you should just neglect any responsibilities you have, but every person needs to find their own balanceAs i type this minutes after beating the game, wiping tears from my face, I just want to thank the great team from MegaWobble for bringing Lil Gator Game into the world. You made my days a whole lot brighter :)Oh and also, the game is a lot of fun. Really fun movement, fun items to unlock, hilarious writing, tons of unique scenarios, just such a pleasant lil gator game that i would recommend to anyone who needs some more unbridled joy in their life

_childDocuments_.name: Lil Gator Game

_childDocuments_.review: Lil Gator Game is an adorable adventure game where you play as a little gator playing a game of make believe with all your friends. This game is super cute, from the cutesy art style to the quirky dialogue and the funny characters. It's very simple, and I imagine it would great for kids just learning how to play video games. The story is sweet and oddly heartfelt, and it was a lot of fun going around collecting everything around the world. I did think there were just too many collectibles in the forms of things to slay, but otherwise this was a quick and fun adventure that is perfect for young audiences or anyone who wants to feel like a kid again.
_childDocuments_.name: Lil Gator Game

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very fun, cute and wholesome! Very relaxing experience and had me smiling the whole time. _childDocuments_.name: Lil Gator Game

_childDocuments_.review: I know I might not have played it for very long at this point, but this is a fantastic game. It's very cute and sweet and fun! It also focuses on some topics that many people might have overlooked. It talks about how deep down inside, we are all the same, and all just want to be happy and loved. It talks about teamwork, and how it can really make everyone's lives so much better. And it talks about continuing to focus on your studies as you enjoy life: still getting older. The thing that made such an impact on me was the entire: "we won't be long forever, so enjoy it while it lasts" point and even when we get older we need to have fun sometimes, and not just always be an "adult" (as an adult, I can say this). This game is one of the greatest I have ever played and it genuinely made me cry lol. Show your love to the creators and never forget to be yourself and enjoy what you have. Never take any of it for granted.

_childDocuments_.review: So glad to see a more recent take on a mascot platformer, although short; this game packs a punch in its small story.  is an adventure of a kid who uses his imagination and friends creativity to try to bring back an old childhood game he played with his big sister back to life. The story uses this to put you into the perspective of a younger sibling and what they may face as everyone around them starts to grow up. I would say it was worth every penny and Lil Gator is such a unique and charming character. The achievements were not hard, as you naturally progress through them as you progress the story with very minimal clean up needed. 8/10, great game!

_childDocuments_.review: This is how you make an open world game with lots of fun things to do.  It is not how you make an engaging story. _childDocuments_.name: Lil Gator Game

_childDocuments_.review: I dont think ive seen any other game thats as tightly designed as this one. Im not normally into "endgame" stuff, i dont like looking in every nook and cranny to find the last x, but this games core gameplay loop is so fun that I spent about an hour after finishing this game just finding everything I didnt during the main campaign. It also had a system which was not just giving you a map and pinning everything you missed which was really refreshing to see and very clever.The visuals are really nice too, it was very clearly inspired by A Short Hike but I think it does make an identity for itself! I loved how there were a wide variety of enemies, kept things interesting as you went into different areas. I also loved how enemies in the water had little boats or lifesavers, thinking about it this game has lots of tiny details that add up!The story is really impressive as well, its very simple but also extremely present in a way that I havent seen before. everything and i do mean EVERYTHING plays towards it a very natural way which i dont think ive seen in any other game before. It also gets a bit emotional towards the end which i really appreciated, i may be biased but it made it way more memorable!oh right it also REALLY funny sometimes i absolutely loved thatOverall i would give this game a big ol 10/10. It has a very solid concept, explores it to its fullest and does so in a very fun way. Its really fun to just move around, explore the island and kill enemies and i could do it for hours if i could. As a game developer, this is the kind of game I want to make one day, and I cant wait to see what this studio does next!

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty sure this is the first game I've maxed achievements for on Steam. So um, yeah, I liked it quite a bit. Also helped that I could knock out the game and all its achievements in under six hours.Plays like Breath of the Wild (including gliding and shield surfing, but no weapon breaking, thankfully), but with a more youthful and exhuberant main character (Lil Gator is a kid trying to relive his glory days playing with his big sis after all). Kind of funny that the only enemies are static cardboard cutouts but still satisfying to take out and satisfying hunting down all of them scattered about the island (there's hundreds of them).Lots of humorous dialog done very well. I especially like how some of the quests are just 'go pick up that thing two feet away from you' just to kind of play with the idea of making quests. In general I like how most of the quests are pretty localized to the immediate region you're in, you don't have to go running for minutes to get to the place where you need to do the thing.Sometimes I did get a little confused on where I had to go, though, as the instructions are somewhat vague and there's very few landmarks or signs or even names of areas within the game to lead you to where you need to go. I did have to consult Google a couple of times to get some clarity on what I was even looking for a couple times. Also the handful of times that things weren't in the immediate area for a quest threw me a bit, as I'd been conditioned with all the other quests to look just super nearby that I assumed I shouldn't be traveling any further than a certain radius to find what I was looking for.Story is an interesting one as well, about how adults tend to lose their sense of play and fun as they get caught up in what they want to accomplish in the adult world, and why it might still be a good idea to embrace the imagination and fun of our childhood, which I can only relate to all too well now that I'm well into my adult years.Great short playthrough. Check it out if you liked Breath of the Wild and want something a bit different, funny, and quick to 100%.

_childDocuments_.review: In a world of embarrassing shovelware thrown at kids, here is a RARE masterpiece. I remember as a kid top quality games aimed at my age range were few and far between.  I also remember being burned countless times by garbage which were released on expensive cartridges.  AVGN made an entire living off reviewing such games.  Here is an example of developers who truly respect the consumer and have a passion for game development.  Though there is no way to "lose" the gameplay is polished and fun.  The writing is witty and for all ages.  I experienced ZERO audio, graphical, or gameplay glitches.  I can't recommend this one enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Lil Gator Game

_childDocuments_.review: This game deeply resonated with me in more ways than I can possibly describe, every facet of its story, style, characters and overall message could have been lifted from my head and my past. It would be spoilers to explain, and besides, you aren't reading the reviews for that.I played the game and completed the main story in just under 8 hours, you could do it in less, but that isn't the point of this game. For the first time in so long, Lil Gator made me feel like I could do things for fun, for no other reason than it was fun to do. I jumped on seesaws, climbed jungle gyms, painted the world with the brush and pallette shield.I climbed the tallest tree I could find, jumped as high as I could on the branches and used abilities to go higher still into the sky. Not because there was an achievement, not because an objective box would be filled, or a collectable was there.But because much like the lil gator, my inner child said "Lets try, it'll be fun!", and I listened. And of course he was right, it was so much fun!There are heartfelt moments that you stumble upon, and I encourage you to stop for a moment to take them in, instead of rushing to the next thing. Pause and un-pause the game, and lil gator will sit down with you while you do, or use the ragdoll to lay and chill. In these moments it feels like there is nowhere else you need to be, and nothing that needs to be done.Suffice to say, I found the game meditative, healing, and I couldn't be happier with it. There is some more to do beyond the end of the story and this will probably be the first game I 100%, but only by accident while I'm having fun along the way.
_childDocuments_.name: Lil Gator Game

_childDocuments_.review: I am a slave to many nostalgic games in my life (Zelda, Final Fantasy, Castlevania, Metroid and etc.), as I am sure many can empathize, but this is a game that I randomly discovered on twitter in my late twenties and it has reminded me of the significance in retaining your childhood memories more than any game I actually played in my childhood. It is a game that brilliantly convinced me that even though I am an adult, I can still be that little hero I imagined I was with my friends back when things seemed so simple.That is how the game impacted me upon completing the story.While actually playing the game, I was just having a genuinely good time. It's fun engaging with all the friends you can meet, no character in this game lacks personality or charm.Little to no bugs, I think at most I had a few frame drops and that could just be due to my own setup so it runs great. Physics in the game are genuinely fun to play with and silly on purpose.Gameplay is great and the controls are so solid, it is designed to be a relaxing, non-linear time and still rewards you simply for talking to NPCs and exploring anywhere at your own pace. Focuses on more of an fun story experience rather than a speedrunner's field day of a 3D platformer (they have a speedrun mode in the settings so that's actually really cool and kinda funny)I got this game while it was on sale but I can safely say that this game is definitely worth giving a try even if it's not on sale.Overall, heartwarming and very therapeutic, especially for a younger and/or older sibling. Perfect 10/10 and by far my most favorite game I've played this year.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is sickeningly adorable. It heavily reminds me of A Short Hike and is filled to the brim with Zelda references, but manages to set itself apart with its clever writing, heart-warming story, and lackadaisical presentation. The game presents multiple mental health and relationship issues through a child's lens, and manages to make it all seem realistic and satisfying to resolve without sounding trivial and childish. A multitude of movement mechanics makes getting around quickly a fun challenge in itself. Getting around can even be quite hilarious at times! A ton of attention to  detail and passion was obviously put into the game. Minor spoiler regarding progression: The dialogue may be a bit too discord-y/reddit-y/social-media-y for some peoples' taste, but I did not mind it at all, and the dialogue and story are very well written regardless.I can see anyone of literally any age enjoying this game, it's funny, charming, and an absolute joy. I'm gonna gush about it to all my friends until they get fed up with me.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you want to commit mass murder on a small population of cute monsters? Do you want to slowly induct others to join you on your cause? Do you want to please the Elder Sister so she might find amusement in the slaughter of such innocent things? Then this game is for you.Lil Gator is a game about adventure, where you slowly purge the land of cardboard monsters and make allies with visitors on an island. Break your helpless foes and use their parts to create new items for your character. Make new comrades as you build up your base so you can finally please the Elder Sister. Do not worry. Such cardboard creatures are no match for you, Lil Gator. There is no trial that can't be beaten, and no monster who stands a chance against your overwhelming power!But be wary, for this adventure can be incredibly short. Like, I seriously got all the achievements in 3.9 Hours. Still a fun game though.

_childDocuments_.name: Lil Gator Game

_childDocuments_.review: Lil Gator Game is about a little alligator kid whose older sister is visiting during her break from university. Big Sis (as she's called in the game) is still busy with a school project, so your character wants to surprise her and distract her from her schoolwork by creating a game for you to play together. So you get all your friends together (and make some new ones!) in order to make it the best game possible.The game consists of exploring the two islands, breaking cardboard structures ("monsters") and ceramic pots to get crafting materials, crafting items, going on quests for both new and old friends, completing races, and collecting bracelets to get more climbing stamina. Despite the gameplay being fairly simple and easy, it doesn't ever feel slow or boring. It's rewarding, and overall really fun. And there's something about climbing the mountains and gliding, sliding, and swimming to your heart's content that just feels incredibly freeing.(Also, getting all the achievements took about 11 hours overall. So if you're an achievement hunter like me, this is a fairly easy one to 100%)The story is usually cheery, but will definitely hit you in the heart at several points. Especially if you're a youngest sibling, you'll feel for the protagonist when As for the characters, they're all lovable in their own ways. I won't say too much here, as I think it's more fun to meet those characters yourself. But I will say my favorite is Avery. Partly because they're a frog (one of the best animals), partly because their name is spelled "avery!" (exclamation point included!) in their dialogue boxes, and of course their personality.This is honestly one of the best games I've played in awhile. I originally bought it because it looked cute, and reminded me of A Short Hike (and I was right). It's adorable, cozy, has absolutely lovely music, and will probably make you very nostalgic for your childhood.
_childDocuments_.name: Lil Gator Game

_childDocuments_.review: Lil Gator Game is an adorable adventure game with a low barrier to entry (If you don't really play games you'll still have a good time) but with enough depth to its moment-to-moment gameplay and its overall story that it's worth playing for even seasoned gaming veterans. Will the immobile cardboard enemies challenge veterans like me? No, but they're not supposed to, and the variety of movement options (most "borrowed" from breath of the wild, and  all done about as well) makes the world truly fun to explore.It has a few minor issues, the camera doesn't always behave itself in tight quarters, and the climbing animation plays at times it shouldn't, but it runs well, and none of the minor technical issues took me out of the experience.Easily the highlight of the game visually is the orange effect it applies to far-off objects, that give the game a sense of depth and scale, and also tie it into the autumnal feel it's going for, both in the time it literally takes place, and thematically.I wish they'd make a DLC where you got to use the shield surfing to its full potential. I'd happily pay full price again for a racing? game that expands on the short downhill racing segments near where you first get the shield. I think "I wish there was more of it" is the best thing you can say of most media. Play Lil Gator Game, it's maybe 15 hours to do everything - and its short length is a feature, not a criticism, it goes out of its way not to waste your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Lil Gator Game

_childDocuments_.review: It feels weird to not recommend a game that I actually really liked, but for the price it just falls flat in too many areas. The game is extremely one-note; pretty much every friend quest is either breaking a few targets, sometimes timed, or just finding some characters and clicking through some cute dialogue. The environments follow suit, where the only locales are Forest, Mountain, and Slightly Dry Forest. Most items you get are reskins of the default equipment, with some fun exceptions but nothing mind-blowing. The default stamina wheel is quite small, but upgradeable - as it turns out, I didn't find any of the 3 upgrades until after finishing it, so they weren't really all that valuable anyway. Movement feels good and the art, dialogue, and story are cute. There's no post-game guidance like a map or anything to help you 100% the friend quests, so after about 85% of them I called it quits rather than exploring the samey island looking for characters telling me to do the same chores. $20 for a lukewarm 3 hour experience isn't the best value in my opinion, but for a heavy discount I think this game is worth picking up. Definitely play this game's inspiration A Short Hike though, I thought the pacing and advancement of A Short Hike was done better.

It definitely hits home for me because I can relate to it on a more personal level. with everything that's going on in my life.The game is easy to play with simple controls, and the environment has a lot of bright colors and fun items to collect. The characters are really funny and a a lot of fun to interact with too. The story and objectives are easy to understand, which makes the game relaxing and fun to play. The sound effects and music are really nice too.I think 20$ for this game is a little high, so I would recommend buying it when it goes on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Go on a cute little charming adventure as a lil gator.No game has quite managed to make me feel like a kid again like Lil Gator Game has. Really nice, charming graphics. LGG has some genuinely great writing that feels surprisingly real and relatable. This is a game for the family, but in the way that Super Mario Odyssey is for the family. Obviously, the polish isn't quite the same level as Super Mario Odyssey. It doesn't even try to do the same thing. But what I mean by that comparison is, anyone and everyone should be able to pick up and enjoy  about this little adventure. Takes clear inspiration from A Short Hike, but in the best way. It's not ripping anything off. This is full of creativity, passion, heart, soul, and imagination. Relive those days of imagination and finding creative ways to play on the playground when you were a kid. Lil Gator Game is wholesome, cozy, heartwarming, heartbreaking, grown-up, and mature, but at the same time full of "childlike wonder" all at once.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're wondering whether the 99% positive reviews are correct, they definitely are.Lil Gator Game is cute, charming, and super fun. _childDocuments_.review: This is among the best games I played.It's both short and simple and easy, but engaging and fun and full.  It's a goofy platformer that never stops becoming more satisfying. The progression gotten through exploration is perfect on its own, but not necessary either. I spent a lot of time just riding around  and various other items.There aren't any absolutely unique items, so it's still simple, but the little quirks of each item makes them feel simply special. Doubly so since you associate it with the stories you went through.It's a wonderfully charming, funny, and heart-warming adventure. There are so many nice little characters. Finding each new quest was not just a good excuse to explore the area and kill time, but a short story or a gag to be invested in. And the main quests had that same great humor and charming simplicity. And they were surprisingly hard-hitting stories. Because of its focus on childhood escapism and mending hurt between friends, and because it was unabashedly wholesome and childishly honest, the game is great at disarming the player. You know exactly what will happen. You will probably guess how it will happen, too. But the humor keeps you engaged, and the story warms your heart. No twists needed, no grand ideas need to be hinted at, and no complexities need to be attached. Just a whole lot of humans being humans (well, animals being humans), and children being children. A low-stake conflict that means the world to everybody. A Coming-Of-Age story written for adults to appeal to our childhood. Only, this coming of age is about children becoming children.

_childDocuments_.review: Lil Gator Game is one of those games that you play through with a smile on your face from start to finish. _childDocuments_.review: This is without a doubt the single cutest game I've ever played. I'm not an expert, of course. At the time of writing, I've only played through Animal Crossing and A Short Hike, so I'm not exactly well versed in the area of cozy games. Play at least one Zelda game before buying, though, preferably a traditional one. Not playing The Legend of Zelda won't hurt you too much, but some of the best jokes in this game are all making fun of Zelda or games like Zelda.I doubt I need to say this, but this is an unapologetically easy game. Like, five year old could beat it easy. I'm not complaining. This game really isn't about difficulty, or pressure, or stress. It's not about the dopamine rush that comes from a perfect parry, or the looming satisfaction of a well built system, or the pain of failing again and again. This is a game about finding joy in humor, about the sort of casual comedy that comes with childhood, and, of course, the feeling of exploration. It's the best kind of nostalgia, both as an avid Zelda player and an inner child. You talk to a lot of people in this game, and do not under any circumstances skip the dialogue, for the dialogue was what for me truly cemented this game as one of my all time favorites.Sure, the movement's a bit wonky. In my opinion, the snap is a bit overzealous, and the camera can sometimes be messy. But seeing as this is not a precision platformer, or action rpg, I don't really see why I should care. The baseline is, if you want to relive some of that childhood magic, explore a small little world, and make a lot friends (a lot of friends), this is the game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Though I played this as an adult, this game is perfect for kids who are unfamiliar with 3d adventure games. It is like playing a modern Legend Of Zelda game, but with no violence, pain, or punishment of any kind. Navigating the world was very easy, and I never ran into a spot that felt frustrating to traverse. My one complaint is that I thought the draw distance was too small, even at max settings, since it was easy to get lost and I wished I could view the entire map without fog.To be specific about this game’s strengths though, you begin the game with a stamina meter, and the way that it was implemented was absolutely brilliant. Like every aspect of this game, it introduced difficulty in a way that you could casually confront, without frustration. Then, right when those stamina based challenges started to seem tedious, I unlocked the ability to remove stamina completely, which opened up the door for me to become a completionist and easily explore every part of the world that I missed. Additionally, if you’re worried about missing some of the beautiful cardboard monsters and treasure, you’ll also eventually unlock an ability that will guide you to each and every one. The devs really thought of everything when it came to what people would want to do and how much time it would take to do it.I also love that the characters don't have obvious genders, and I love the variety of animals. I thought that the character art was perfect; just expressive enough, without forsaking the game’s casual, conflict-free tone. It was a breeze to play, completable in under 4 hours. It is the perfect game to spend a day off with, whether you’re a kid who’s new to video games, or an adult who wants a break from the constant pressure of adulthood. Lil Gator Game’s sense of progression, whimsy, and imagination throughout the entire experience made it one of the most enjoyable games I’ve ever played, so I have to highly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: In a world full of political conflicts, wars, global warming, social media drama, miscommunication, among other sources of mental instability it's good to know that there are ways of escapism other than drugs and addictions. This is certainly one of them.Indeed, this short narrative delves into how as we grow up we start to pay more attention to our responsibilities, leaving aside cherished moments we could make with our special someone. Be it family, friends, tutors or just about anyone that we look up to, sometimes it is good to take a pause from the everyday routine, look up from your workstation and seize the present as it is. This doesn't mean you shouldn't prioritize your studies nor your projects, but just don't overdo it to the point that once you realize it those who were calling out to you are no longer there.In any case, this 3D platformer in nature bases its other main engaging aspects on its various side quests and exploratory aspects. The island is vast with lots of collectibles to be found, heights to be reached and characters to be met, each with their own concerns that may sound childish but always leave us with a warm feeling of satisfaction upon solution. Not only that but sometimes the reward involves artifacts that change our gameplay in minor yet exciting ways, expanding our experimentation horizons in the process. This is all accompanied by a soothing and relaxing soundtrack and a simple yet colorful aesthetics that perfectly captures the essence of the adventure.Still, this doesn't mean it's perfect. Some of the dialogue may come off as a bit repetitive in some places and the hitbox detection isn't the most accurate in a few specific locations. Nonetheless, these nitpicks shouldn't really be a bother for its target audience who'll most feel at home with its premise. If you have a few hours at your disposal, this one's a given for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: I had the very good fortune to be able to experience this game. I saw Playtonic advertising it on Twitter, signed up for a chance to get a key because I thought it looked cute, and was lucky enough to get a key. I knew the game looked cute on the surface, but I could not imagine just how adorable the presentation really was. The art style, the text font, the character movements, absolutely everything has love and attention put into it. The big-headed anthropomorphic animals are all cute, and are made cuter by a full range of motion! They pose, they waddle, they sway, they do so many things that make the character models feel dynamic! The text font is large and comical, with each character having a different text color to make it easy to identify who's talking, although there are other visual cues to make it clear who's talking for accessibility. And of course, the island you explore is bright, colorful, and expansive! The game makes very obvious parody references to the Zelda series, but does so in a way that's endearing throughout the game. The gameplay is primarily rooted in exploration, and it does a fantastic job of it. The game starts out simple, with only being able to move and jump at the onset. But within mere minutes, it expands your options to include sliding, climbing, gliding, and so many more. You gain a lot of secondary items that allow you to do optional actions that are still a lot of fun... After playing this game, I am convinced that having the ability to rag doll on command is something that every game needs, because it is hilarious even if it doesn't have any functional use! And of course, you can interact with objects in on the island as well; you can sit on benches, chairs, swings, seesaws go up and down, and you can slide down slides as well. The exploration feels organic because of the way you can interact with the setting. The only downside with the exploration is that with no map, it can be confusing to keep track of your location until you get a feel for the island, but it does at least remedy this somewhat by using four tall structures as a means of reference to figure out which direction to go. Exploration wouldn't be meaningful though if there weren't things to discover, and this game has two main objectives to seek out in your exploration: Cardboard Enemies and Friends. There aren't any true "enemies" so there isn't really any combat, but cardboard enemies/obstacles are placed throughout the island, While they offer no resistance as you hack them apart with your sword (or other bludgeoning tools), they do satisfy the collection itch as you seek out each and every one, and collecting their confetti remains is your means of currency to purchase items for both aesthetics and usage. The other main aspect of the game is seeking out characters throughout the island to "recruit" them by doing simple quests, most of which range to picking the right dialogue option, doing fetch quests, or breaking some cardboard enemies. Each character is unique, and despite the short interactions with them, most were endearing to the point where seeking them out felt enjoyable rather than just being an objective. The writing in this game was also a highlight. The game does not take itself too seriously most of the time; the characters are written accurately like children of varying ages, and as a result the dialogue tends to be light-hearted and silly, especially through the lens of the young protagonist. Yet despite the silliness, the game's narrative ended up being very moving, and gave me a lot of feelings by the end of it. This game isn't long, and it isn't challenging. Collecting everything can be a little tedious, but even then the game gives you means to circumvent that and make 100% easily attainable for everyone. It took me about 7 hours to completely 100% the game, including all achievements. But the game had plenty to see and plenty to do throughout those 7 hours, so I never once felt bored. This game really feels like a mix of Breath of the Wild and A Short Hike, and the result is something truly special. I 100% recommend this game to absolutely everyone; it's silly, it's fun, and it'll put a smile on your face, guaranteed.

_childDocuments_.review: is a heartfelt, charming little title that perfectly captures the spirit of childhood play in the best possible ways.Stepping into the role of the eponymous little gator, you find yourself trying to make the most of a fleeting fall break with your sister who's back in town from college and weighed down by no small amount of over-the-break work. Lil Gator hatches a scheme to organize and orchestrate the grandest high-fantasy make-believe game possible to snap her out of her funk and recapture those memories from early childhood. What follows is a joyous romp that synthesizes a small catalog of influences and design concepts that culminate to something far greater than the sum of its parts.Aesthetically,  owes a lot to  though I can't say for sure if that's intentional or incidental - either way, it's welcome and a surprising intertext. It's a welcome and stylish choice, and the goofy, big-eyed animal characters doing floppy animations combined with the relaxed synth and acoustic music totally nails the vibe. As one might hope, it threads the needle between "nostalgic memories of a beloved video game" and "making up adventures in the neighborhood woods" mood that it aims at, while setting up larger themes about growing up that the game will return to time and time again in its side-stories.Mechanically,  borrows heavily from the  school of design, openly referencing that game, its mechanics, and its UI. It works well, though, due in no small part to the emphasis on exploration over combat. There's not really "combat" in the game as much as there are cardboard targets you can whack periodically with collected swords. Instead, most of the game is spent climbing over and navigating obstacles. From learning how to surf on your shield to slowly improving your stamina in climbing rocks and hills, just navigating the world is itself effortlessly engaging, and it's shockingly well-tuned to boot.But I feel like I'm doing the game a disservice breaking it down by such obvious categories, because it's the way its systems and design all interconnect and overlap that make it work. The cartoon-ish presentation lowers your defenses for a surprisingly heartfelt narrative about valuing loved ones and making the most of your time together, while the seemingly simplistic core loop hides a shockingly robust movement system that makes exploring the space a true delight... all of which make the simple mission designs and exploration slot seamlessly into the experience, allowing the overarching design of building out a small "town" of characters in the playground surprisingly engaging. I'm sure I could press some quibbles if I wanted to - the camera can sometimes be fiddly, and tracking down narrative quests isn't always intuitive - but they're so minor that it feels contrary to the playful attitude and tight design of the experience. The developers at Megawobble have done a really impressive job tying the whole thing together, and frankly, I'm hard-pressed to really think of any drawbacks to what is such a thoughtfully considered game.  feels good to play and knows just how to hit the right emotional beats to stick with you after finishing. It's a true delight, and I can't recommend setting off on this particular adventure enough.

_childDocuments_.review: I smiled, I laughed, I got immersed, and I cried. This game feels deeply personal and I'd love to shake the developers hand just to thank them for what they've created. I needed something like this in my current stage of life: just graduated with a Bachelor's Degree... have no idea where to go from here. I didn't expect this game to elicit a wide array of emotions and memories from me, but it did. Overall though, I wasn't expecting to cry. This game isn't sad, it's very cute and it has a powerful message. It's also extremely enjoyable and frustration free. Lil Gator feels so satisfying to control--I didn't expect movement to be this fluid--and there's enough guidance for the player so that they can explore as they please without feeling lost. Gathering collectibles and unlocking items is such a joy, and each item is distinct enough to not just feel like a reskin. There's different effects, some items are varied in usage, and there's even a set of items that I feel transform the way the game is played entirely! Such an amazing bit of detail and care that didn't need to be there at all. And that level of detail is seen throughout the game.I managed to get 95% completion and accumulated all of my playtime for this review in one sitting, so this game's not a major time commitment. Though I do think it's well worth the asking price, which makes it an absolute steal on sale. And surprisingly, this is one of the only platforming games I'd recommend based on the story alone. That's not to say the gameplay isn't as excellent--it is--but I feel this game as an entire package is something special. The entire game is framed around this story, which is ultimately just cute characters having fun and role-playing like we did on the playground, picking up sticks and saying they're swords. But there's a lot of strong, adult themes that I wasn't expecting the game to touch on. Mostly about childhood, togetherness, and belonging. And it's all done with a gameplay style that really immerses you in the narrative. I'm serious when I say this game is something special for fans of platforming games.All that to say, this is a game kids will love, but adults might get choked up over. I know I did. Honestly the easiest recommendation I've given a game in years.Thank you for reading.

_childDocuments_.review: 6h 2/10 1 not sure how good or helpful it is, but  No No No No No No No No difficulty settings NoLil Gator Game is such an awesome game. You play as this kid, which wants to play a video game but then in real life. He did this all the time with his big sister, but then she got busy and they didn't do this anymore. He misses that and wants to try to convince his sister to join in again. Will he succeed? You really feel like a kid in a playground! Extra adorable is that you can use the things in the playground like the slides or the seesaw. The game looks adorable and cute, it is just amazing. It mocks video games from time to time but in a good way and not all the time gladly. This game reminds me so much of , which is a good thing. there aren't enough games like this on the market. You'll go on so many short quests in this game and will make so many friends on your way, which is cool as they all will come to hang out in the playground when you finished their quest. _childDocuments_.review: A lovely, brief, elaborately indie mix of well-established open-world adventure elements wrapped up in a cozy and playful island-investigating package.To draw some cheap comparisons: it's another low-poly animal-friend experience akin to Frog Detective, in terms of goofy writing, and A Short Hike, in terms of open-ended island-roaming. Although, I'm not sure whether the premise of a protagonist being obsessed with a nonspecific green-hatted adventure game is a superb excuse for borrowing so heavily from its inspiration. But perhaps it’s to the benefit of the game’s message that the gameplay feels so familiar. Plus, the creativity that Lil Gator Game does bring to the formula is admirably distinct.For as enjoyable as Lil Gator Game is and in spite of how its self-aware attitude approaches gameplay, the not-so-lil scale of the main island often reminded me of how open games tend to fall apart. I occasionally felt like a map might be nice, or map markers, or a quest log, or fast travel, or HUD waypoints, and then all the fun would be gone. Point is, Lil Gator Game teeters on an edge where a lot of that typical organizational fluff starts to feel self-destructively appealing. Perhaps the sense of exploration could have been even stronger had the island been slightly more condensed or had the overall foliage been reduced (for better terrain visibility).

_childDocuments_.review: I went into this game already knowing that I was going to enjoy it as laid back platform adventure games have been pretty big for myself these last couple of years. After having combed through the entire islands and getting everything I can say with full confidence that I love this little game. To be clear this game can easily be completed 100% in like 3-4 hours at a casual pace, the only reason I have more hours is just because I enjoyed jumping around the islands and ragdolling my poor Gator buddy across the land that much. Ontop of that the game does a fantastic job at recapturing the child wonder of getting to explore while also touching on topics of social anxiety, the difficulties of communication, and consideration of other people's side of things.There's no time sensitive objective, there's a handful of gadgets that you can get along the way, and a fair few cosmetic options so you can look stylish as you have your own little romp. _childDocuments_.review: Lil' Gator Game is masterful. From its easy and engaging gameplay, relatable and effective storytelling and the plethora of options it gives, Lil' Gator Game has continued to impress me through and through. I have spent a lot of my childhood playing video games, do make-believe and go on grand (self-made) adventures. Although the game is short (give or take, you can beat it in 2 hours if you know what to do), Lil' Gator Game has been able to capture that magical feeling one once had when they went out to play during the weekends, after school and or during breaks. It does so through an open world with tons of collectibles and epic quests for you to complete. And then there is the story. Not spoiling anything here, but I do have to share this about the story of Lil´ Gator Game; As of writing this review, I am slowly tearing up from its premise, its well-timed beats and overall execution. Digesting all of it after having finished it, I am glad that although I have finished the game this quickly, I could've been part of this Gator's grand adventure. Knowing this, I may do a new playthrough of it next summer, just to recapture those moments and enjoy what this magical game has to offer once more.I'd highly recommend you to give this game a go or even give this as a gift to a friend for the holidays if they are a person who likes to collect stuff or likes stories of video games. This has been the best 20 euro's I have ever spent on a game. My only regret is that I had not stopped to smell the roses and spaced out my play sessions. But that does not matter, because I'd do it all over again.

_childDocuments_.review: Lil Gator Game is one of the most heartfelt, adorable, and downright fun games I've ever played. Every second of it is filled with charm and humor and wonderful messages that even as an adult I think I needed reminders of. On top of the story, which made me cry btw, the gameplay itself is tight, responsive, and feels so so SO good to control. This lil gator has some strong movement tech, ngl. The game is a bit short but honestly I feel like it's the perfect length for the story it's trying to tell and of course the story isn't all there is. Exploration is fun and I'm sure there's a ton I still missed.  All in All, a truly wonderful experience that I didn't want to end.

_childDocuments_.review: Lil" Gator game is a relaxing game to play and just pass the time to remember when you were a kid if you are old as me, playing outside, making up games to play because either you couldn't afford a lot of digital entertainment or the only kids you could talk to were at the local park. It also shows the childlike wonder of what the world could be like. The story can hit home for a lot of people with older siblings or parents when you loved having fun together but they can’t due to things out of their control which in turn makes the kid think it’s their fault when it’s not but also a lesson for the older folk that its OK to take a break sometimes and reconnect with your inner child to remember your hobbies or things you loved to do. That you don’t have to give them up but do it in moderation and you’ll be fine, plus you can share the things that make you happy with the people you care about, don’t forget to check on them. You can finish Lil" Gator game in one sitting which is about three hours but if you want to 100 percent the game then you are looking at five to six hours and for 10-20 dollars depending on the sale is fine but with that said I’ll give Lil Gator game an 8 out 10 for reminding everyone to take a breather and spend time doing the things you love with the people you care about.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an amazing game. It's very fun; it's the type of game that makes you want to explore every nook and cranny because there is so much fun stuff to find. It's also not huge, so exploring everything feels very possible. Despite not being huge, the game world is dense! All sorts of cool biomes, geography, activities.The game is also extremely touching and emotional. The finale is such a wonderful ode to change and the inevitable loss that comes with change. This isn't cheesy "someone important suddenly dies" emotion, this is the real stuff we all feel as we go through life. This game is so grounded in reality while being about a bunch of animals making an impossibly cool game!There's so much other cool stuff: everything is player friendly from the movement mechanics to wrapping up loose ends post-game, the focus on how talking helps solve problems, new items that make end-game traversal a blast. Literally, Zelda could take tips from mechanics in this game, such as how the stamina works and the fluidity of movement.If I had to say a "negative" thing it would be that this game is very low stakes. There's no real combat or way to lose. To many that's a positive, but I know some would view this game as a glorified walking simulator. I'm fine with it since it's such an amazing game. There is room for both low stakes games and high stakes games and this is a wonderful example of the former.

_childDocuments_.review: Lil Gator Game is such a wonderful short experience. Lil Gator is about a lil' dude who loves to play and enjoy life with all of his buds. The game consists of doing little various quests to sucker in Big Sis to join the festivities. Big Sis is Lil Gator's older sister who used to join in on the festivities, but now she's swamped with work and school, and doesn't really have the time to play with her Lil Bro anymore. So what ensues is Lil Gator's elaborate plan to pull Big Sis back into the fold. The game feels really cozy, and nostalgic. I feel as if the player could imagine themselves doing the same antics that Lil Gator does. This review doesn't really have much form, and my thoughts are pretty unorganized but I loved this game. There's so much heart, and spirit in this game. I 100%ed everything in about 7 hours, and even then I wasn't really ready for this game to end. It definitely gives Night in the Woods vibes. I absolutely love the relationship of all the characters, especially Tom and Gunther. I would recommend this game if you have a few hours to kill, and you want to tackle a game with childlike wonder again. Such a chilled little nostalgia-fest and I'd recommend this game to anyone who loves a high quality cutesy game with exploring and a shocking amount of depth in its gameplay and story. Definitely pick this game up!

_childDocuments_.review: It's rare that I have nothing bad to say about a game. I struggle to even find anything to nitpick.This game is just a charming, fun little adventure, with just enough variety to keep it interesting, and the perfect length to not outstay its welcome.Often times when games go with these stylised cartoony visuals, it can come off as just an excuse to be lazy with making graphics, or arty. But while it looks cartoony and simple, this game has a lot more variety than I expected, especially with the cosmetics and effects. The world is beautifully detailed and colourful, and, while many pieces of equipment serve the same purpose, the devs went all out and gave many of them different animations, visual effects on the world, and more. Most other games would just reskin or palette-swap, and call it a day.The sound effects are cute and serve their purpose, and each piece of music for each area is catchy and playful. Some of them have come to mind randomly even a few weeks later.The controls are responsive, and you have plenty of freedom of control, as well as a bunch of gadgets for different ways of getting around, keeping it fun to wander about the open world at your leisure, climbing, jumping, gliding, in search more cute childlike adventures with friends, and treasure.If anything, people might take issue with the amount of dialogue in the game. There's a LOT of it. But I found almost all of it to be wonderful and amusing to read. I'm very hard to make laugh out loud, or even chuckle (I'm a very internal laughter kind of person), but this game got me a few times. The story even made me feel emotions, almost making me cry towards the end.I never expected this to be such a special experience. Thought it would just be a cute little play-and-forget deal. But I love this silly game.Helps that I love reptiles, especially crocs/gators, and this is the most adorable gator I've ever had the pleasure of playing as!

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game over the entire duration of a seven hour flight to LA. After about 30 minutes when all blood flow ceases in my body, i hate the plane. ♥♥♥♥. Playing this game, I wish the plane ride was seven hours longer. I wanted to be kept in the lil gator world this game built around me. It takes you back to a time as a kid when you made up adventures with your friends and played outside. I am an adult now and I don't remember how to get outside anymore. The game isn't just about being a kid though, it is about retaining that child-like wonder whilst growing up and oftentimes growing out of that feeling. I didn't realize the game would get even a little heavy, but it tackled stuff that had me crying by the end. I got to name my character Cunka Poots. He looks like his name is Cunka Poots. If you get the game, you should name him Cunka Poots. The art style is divine. The colors are so bold and the landscape is so pretty that it makes you want to explore every tiny piece of it. The designs of the friends you meet along the way are similarly endearing, each one has their personality written out for you to see. The soundtrack changes depending on which area you enter, which speaks to how small this little world is for the characters. They make a mountain out of their little ant hill. This game will probably make you laugh, it definitely made me cry, and the monkey character is funny. It checks off all the boxes. There is also a ragdoll button which has about 0% utility. Every game should have that probably. This game is amazing.Side note: the people next to me on the plane ride watched about half of The Good Wife season 1 translated into korean. My enjoyment of the game was possibly positively impacted by watching half of The Good Wife season 1 translated into korean. You can do this as well, but don't tell anyone.

_childDocuments_.review: I first heard of this game last year during a Steam Next Fest. They had a demo out for this game and I went to try it and absolutely fell in love with it. Now after waiting a long time for the game to come out and after a while of playing other games, I finally decided to kick this off my backlog and my god, Lil Gator Game is by far one of the best 3D Platformers you can play at the moment. I have literally nothing negative to say about the game in general. I loved it all the way through and have nothing but praise for it. Not only that, but this is a LANDMARK Title for Video Games. What DUSK did to Boomer Shooters, Lil Gator Game creates a new type of Sub Genre that many games coming out are being influenced from. These games range from the upcoming Smushi Come Home and newly released Mail Time.  That being the  which is a new unique sub genre of it's own. It involves non violent gameplay, open world exploration, simplified mechanics from more deeper, bigger games, wholesome and adorable characters and a lightweight story with hilarious humor. Lil Gator Game single handedly creates all the elements of this sub genre and I feel this game will be a HUGE influence on 3D Platformers to come. The game is heavily inspired by Nintendo's Zelda Games and is a loving and original homage to games like The Wind Waker and Breath of the Wild. It copies mechanics like crafting, combat, gliders and climbing while simplifying it for a smooth, smaller and responsive experience. The controls are insanely responsive and smooth and never stilted or overactive. You have so much room for experimenting with movement and early into the game you can craft a rag doll mode which can allow you to roll around in the air or on the ground which can often be incredibly funny. The simplified mechanics make this game a joy to play as crafting only takes a press of a button and nothing more and nothing less. But in general, the controls and gameplay are only a part of what makes this a masterpiece. The graphics are full of life and very bright and the character designs are all so adorable and cutesy that you want to hug literally every single person in this game. The music is super relaxing and gave me tons of comfort and it never got redundant despite how much the same songs play throughout areas.But to me, the story and characters and humor are what make this game work. The humor is often if not all the time hilarious. No joke falls flat and every single time a character spoke or did something funny I was on board the entire way through. But what makes Lil Gator Game so great is the fact that there's so much subtext behind the game. It's about growing up, learning to love your youth and most importantly, being kind to others. The messages are fantastic and the game will be a HUGE influence on not just kids but every single person who touches it. The ending of the game is also fantastic, feeling like talking with a counselor and being a great dive into the psyche of a kid. The twist at the end about the main character's older sister was also a delight. I was grinning during the final moments. And the story works because you absolutely care about the characters. Not just Lil Gator, Avery, Martin and Jill, but everyone on the island. They're so unique and full of life and personality that it's impossible to not love them. This game is impossible to hate. How can anyone hate something as wholesome, loving and wonderful as this? The game has a near perfect 99% Rating on Steam which is unsurprising. Everything about Lil Gator Game is wonderful and outstanding. It's a contender for one of the best games I'll play all year. It's a masterpiece and a new landmark for 3D Platforming. It created the Cozy Platformer and will be an influence for years to come on the genre. I loved it. It's full of life and exuberance and never fails to set out what it wants to do. A full 10/10 Experience which is something I rarely give games nowadays. A MUST PLAY.

_childDocuments_.review: The spectrum of Video Games can span as far as the imagination can go.  It captivates so many people across so many loves and interests.  Whether you use video games to be a fearless warrior taking on thousands or a daring protagonist taking on a brave new world, or maybe a big brave shooty man taking on a buncha big bads.  OR OR OR a galavanting knight treading day and night to find their imprisoned princess!  OR, OOH, why not find a magical sword that can beat anything it faces?!Games let you take those childlike ideas and flesh them out as vividly or intricately as you can.  Where Lil Gator Game shines is that that is its whole premise: taking those adolescent dreams of grandeur and making the coolest day ever with your friends!  You play as the little brother, nickname pending to your choosing, as your sister is back in town and it's time to catch up and play all the games with her!  …but she’s stuck on her computer and won’t get off it.  So now lets get ALL the townsfolk together to make the bestest game ever so she’ll have to get off her computer and play with us!The gameplay is as simple as its premise, your lil’ gator can perform all your old school platformer bits: run, jump, climb (with the help of some magical bracelets), float, slide, ragdoll at ludicrous speeds.  These combined with hacking and slashing cardboard foes will help gather paper bits that can be used in numerous ways.  Use bits to craft weapons and shields and a fully functioning digital camera, or trade them in to barter with the island residents and fulfill an aging (16 year old) raccoon’s dream of gathering enough trash to make it big in the world.  Buy the paint gun.  Do it for him.To build the bestest castle fantasy town thing ever, you’re going to need help.  Strewn about the island are various goers of different animal variety.  Embark on a quest to retrieve a shark’s retainer, or get a blood black cherry sorbet with a bat, or roll explosive bowling balls with a mole rat: kid stuff!  Helping these friends in whichever way they’re needed will add them to your friends list and will help in building even bigger pieces of the castle puzzle.Everything about this game puts a smile on your face.  The light and fluffy color palette to the goofy characters and their chuckle-inducing dialogue to the freedom to do some stupidly funny things (ever cannonball ragdoll off the side of a cliff and have one of your buddies be super stoked about it?) makes playing the game just a treat throughout its 4-6 hour runtime.  Collecting different pieces of clothing change the way you rummage around the island as well: using mini-trampolines to bounce instead of slide, or donning the Ninja Headband to, and these are MegaWobble’s words, “run like a weirdo.”  It’s all a nicely put together package.Though there are some problems within the island, none are enough to push me away.  The quests, while elementary in nature because these are kids just making stuff up, tend to all be solved in the same fashion (find a thing, break a thing, do a thing) and get a little same-y as you reach the later half of the game.  I also found myself getting lost sometimes due to a lack of a map.  This could entirely be on me being directionally challenged at times, but thankfully if you’re trying to 100% the game, Lil Gator Game provides some helpful cues to use to aid you on your journey.This little nugget of joy and passion was a great start to my new year.  There’s so much to love in Lil Gator Game and you can feel that love built into every portion of MegaWobble’s foray into the pre-teen age of wonder and freedom while quietly supplying a potentially auto-biographical slice of retrospective nostalgia.  This Lil’ Dude’s quest to be the Legend of Hero is a love letter to the soft and charming platformers of our youth, and worth every goofy gator step you can take around the island.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely iconic. Went straight onto my favorites tab.Movement is great with complex variety, no actions become monotonous.Beautiful art direction, comes with a chonky setting so you can pixelate your resolution. If you want some pro gamer moves, turn all the graphics to low, set to chonky, and put the resolution to 320 x 200.This definitely scratches the "A Short Hike" itch. I'll also recommend Sable if anyone is out there looking for more chill open world games.Shout out to the little things. No map or fast travel (there is a position reset but like come on.) I like that crafting is simplified. You spend so little time in menus, there's little to no distraction in immersing your experience.A couple of things I didn't like, I don't like how much text there is, and I can't say I resonated with the story. If you were to speed run the game I'd argue there's more time mashing through dialogue than playing the game. It is charming just not my cup of tea. I recommend having it so that if you hold down A then it will speed through text, then when it comes to choices it'll stop auto advancing. This is a practice I see in a lot of VN's.I wish there was a way to re spawn enemies after you cleared them all. There's so many means of traversal that go under utilized because by the time you would acquire them, you've already explored everything. The sticky hand for instance you can only get after purchasing a lot of items, and by the time you get it you've probably cleared out most enemies. Perhaps an item randomization? I just wanna bop cardboard so bad!! It would be great for post game activities. It be nice to have an active file open that is completed, and I can jump in any time to  just goof around.Thanks again for making such a wonderful game!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an absolute paragon. is the prime example of why you should never judge a book by its cover. This game can be easily overlooked because of its graphic style, but honestly, it was unlike any game I've ever played; every aspect of it was absolutely precious and pleasant to play through. This game has so much to offer: charming dialogue, countless costumes to dress your lil gator self up in, collectibles, and exploration to your heart's content. This game has it all and is perfect for any kind of gamer. Uncover a beautiful story (and maybe even shed a tear or two, if you're like me) between two siblings and embark on a journey of friendship, teamwork, and maturity.Explore an island that is entirely open-world, destroy cardboard baddies, and climb the tallest mountains for only the bravest of souls. There is very simple "combat", where you will have to destroy cardboard cutouts of monsters, and it is unbelievably satisfying to destroy these 'monsters'. You will receive numerous quests from characters you meet through exploration; you must complete these quests in order to gain new friends who will help you create a huge town for you and all your other friends to play in. Through these quests, you will also unlock cutesy little costumes, new weapons, and objects to use for sliding (it's similar to skateboarding and it's super fun!).There is an  in this game, but if you're not super dialogue-heavy, you can skip through it all. I found it rather lovely to read through it, and there are some funny little moments in the dialogue with some of the characters that I found to be one of my favorite quirks of the game. I would recommend taking your time and reading through it!If you are looking for a game that you can take your time in, never feel pressured or rushed, and never have to worry about dying, this is the perfect game for you. Also, the developers are very interactive with their community and actually listen to their players, which is such a wonderful thing! If you're someone who likes to speedrun, they even added a speedrun mode! I highly recommend this game to everyone; it is a beautiful play.Thanks for reading my review and have a fantastic day!Rating: 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Lil gator game is exactly what I was looking for.I love open world games with fun movement mechanics (crackdown, saints row, hat in time etc) but wanted something more casual to relax to and not say so many gamer words when I fail another jump in Hat in time. And this game delivers, so many fun movement options. It has climbing, gliding, floating, sliding, skating, hopping and using a sticky hand as a grappling hook.The premise of the game is that you and your sister used to play a fantasy make believe game out in the woods, but that was before she went to college. She's back on her break but is too busy with an assignment to play with you like she used to. In order to try to draw her in you get all the other kids to participate in the game and act as NPCs and quest givers for the mighty hero (you) until the fantasy town you're working is impressive enough to pry her away from her school project.The world is large but thanks to several large landmarks you eventually figure out how to navigate. The main loop of the game involves exploring the island and finding new friends to add to your fantasy village, once you meet them they give you a quest to solve (usually something very silly) and you're rewarded with scraps (the in game currency used to craft and buy items) or items. Every NPC is unique and has their own personality quirk. Even by the end of the game I was still looking forward to every quest.The story is cute and well written. It starts out very simply but near the end of the game it gains some good depth through a level which reminded me of psychonauts in how it blended storytelling and gameplay. Nothing unexpectedly dark and tragic, just the sort of stresses and problems anyone goes through growing up. Very importantly: after the main quest is done you are given items to help find every person and cardboard monster you missed so you can satisfy your inner completionist. I managed to 100% after 6 hours which took me about 2 good sessions. I think it's the perfect length and being able to 100% it is the cherry on top.An excellent game and one that IMO gets better the longer you play it and unlock more movement options. If you are a fan of open world exploration and cozy games it's worth a buy.

_childDocuments_.review: What an adorable pick-me-up this game was. All I wanted was a short, cute, casual game to play on my Steam Deck, and Lil Gator delivered hard. You'll probably finish the game in about 3 hours (4 if you're like me and want to explore EVERYTHING). It delivers perfectly at its $20 price point, and I feel lucky to have gotten it on sale. I think anyone can enjoy this game, so if you're reading this - give it a shot!===  General Vibe === The game borrows from the conceptual cuteness of Animal Crossing, but still has its own unique identity in terms of art, design, and music. It also feels like a short love-letter to the Zelda games without there even being any threats of enemies. Just exploration, fun 'weapons' to gather, and a set of '3 Quests' that must be accomplished in order to activate the end-game sequence. Just beneath the cutesy surface, there's a shallow (yet touching) story about youth and the reality of becoming a grown up.=== More Details ===The gameplay is super simple but executed pristinely. You adorably waddle around, jump, sheild-surf, climb, and swing a stick. You'll collect items that more uniquely modify your traversal or 'combat' mechanics. Lil Gator has so perfectly made these simple mechanics feel so silly and enjoyable through its map design, fun item selection, and physics system.'No work during play time' is a theme that underlines the game's storyline, and I really appreciated how they tied it in with the gameplay. There were so many times I ended up goofing off and meandering around without paying a second thought to the larger 'quests' at hand. I just felt so 'present' playing this game... It made me feel like there was nowhere else to be, and nothing else to do but listen to the voice in my head that made me feel like a kid going to a new playground with my friends.The map design also compliments this exceptionally. The open map is large enough to get curious and feel the urge to explore, but not so large that you end up feeling lost or confused. Once I traveled off in any direction I'd lose myself in the exploration. I'd interact with NPCS or side-quests, and continue on until I encountered a familiar landmark from earlier which reminded me to get back on 'task' when I felt like it. I'm not the kind of gamer to 100% a game - but just by virtue of how fun it was to play and explore, I found almost nearly every NPC and found 85% of the game's findable 'currency'.=== Final ===If you want a casual, cute, mindlessly fun game, Lil Gator bravely earns its price-tag. And that says a lot for a game so short. Give it a try :)

_childDocuments_.review: Lil Gator Game is an addictive, cozy and exceptionally cute exploration-adventure game. Whilst it is reminiscent of  or the  series, it stands out from the rest with its quirky style, varied gameplay, customisation and gadgets.Lil Gator is determined to get his big sister to join him in his playful shenanigans, and is willing to do whatever it takes to try and capture her attention. Recently, his sister (only named Big Sis) has had less time to play with him. She has grown up and now has other commitments, like college. She is forever typing away, talking about deadlines and other priorities. Lil Gator does not understand, how can someone spend all day at school and then come home to do, more work?! “Blasphemy!” He thinks. The protagonist then takes it upon himself to make things right, making their island home into a game, befriending everyone and getting them all to collaborate and build a castle. A castle that will surely impress Big Sis and make her spend time with him, away from all of the “adult stuff”, just like she used to. Or is it all for nought?Gameplay is simple, but extremely addictive. Based on a rather large island, Lil Gator and his friends’ plan is in motion. The entire island is a playground, filled with baddies made from scraps, ready to be smashed into pieces. The pieces of scraps are then used as currency. This currency is used in customisation upgrades, either for cosmetics or gadget crafting, to build the castle itself and in the purchase of “bracelets.” There are four bracelets to collect and each bracelet grants Lil Gator more climbing time. This is vital as majority of your time is spent gliding through the air, surfing the ocean and climbing mountains. Having more stamina to climb makes it easier to reach tricky places, but collect all 4 bracelets and you have earned infinite stamina. Making it a breeze to clean up the island and 100% the game after completing the main story. The main goal of the game is to impress Big Sis by completing construction on the castle. To do this, Lil Gator has to scour the island to recruit- I mean befriend, fellow youngsters. This can be as easy as just talking to them, or sometimes they may ask a simple quest, such as to beat a race, retrieve an item and so forth. There are ample characters to meet and all of their interactions are inherently unique and memorable. Collect trash for the raccoon, flip someones chess game,  help make a mum hang up her annoying business call so she can have a tea party and so much more.There are hundreds of cardboard baddies to hit, rewarding you with scrap currency and allowing you to customise your gator! It can be purely cosmetic, or some items do have a function. Items are sometimes also rewarded from completing quests (meeting characters), but usually they will still have to be crafted using the scrap material. Choose a princess theme with a pink wand (sword), pink hat and pink serving plate (shield). Or change it up with a leaf shield and space hat. All shields allow Lil Gator to surf the water, but other items have more useful functions such as allowing you to shoot targets long distance, or to more efficiently glide on the water.There is no mini-map or real direction. The island is vast, but there are tall landmarks in the distance which you can try and judge your location on, such as an antenna or windmill. These were helpful, but my sense of direction is far from great, and I became lost extremely often. Trying to circle back to a character to complete a quest, but having no idea where this area of the island was.. became frustrating. The characters are there to be discovered through exploration, there is no interface or map marker guiding the way, and I liked this freedom, but trying to find the key sections such as the treehouse felt harder than it should have been. Thankfully, upon completing the story, players are granted two useful gadgets that mark where a character is that has not been befriended, or where a breakable item is. Allowing for a fulfilling and non-frustrating 100%.The visuals in Lil Gator are similar to the  series, with their blocky and colourful child-like characters and lack of detail. The text is in a playful font, bouncing along the screen and capital letters are missing in the text. This all adds to the atmosphere, drawing players into Lil Gator’s whimsical imagination.The characters are not voiced, but the joyful upbeat soundtrack was pleasant and definitely had me smiling as I am waddling around every corner of the island. It took me 2.5 hours for the story and almost 5 hours for 100% completion (finding all characters, destroying all breakables etc) Player choice, whilst I did not play with controller, this type of game would match it well. No. However, I do highly recommend completing the game to 100% as there are some final scenes that properly conclude the game. These will only play if the island is cleared.Lil Gator Game is an utterly adorable adventure game with a focus on exploration. Its relaxing, cozy gameplay provides for an entertaining and heart-warming experience. The game is short, and navigation can be confusing, but time absolutely flew by while I was playing, showcasing its great quality. If you like games such as  or  you will more than likely, love this charming little game. This is a must play for all wholesome/cozy game fans, and it has become one of my favourites.

_childDocuments_.review: What I expected was a cute little relaxing game to fool around with for a couple of hours. What I got was a cute little relaxing game that led me on quite an emotional journey with a little gator who reminded me of myself when I was younger. Various points throughout the game hit very close to my own childhood and felt way more relatable than I would have expected. And there were more than a couple of times where I had to stop for a minute and reminisce.All in all it took me about 4 hours to finish the storyline, and about another to round up missed collectables and achievements. And while this might seem a bit short, I can say that every single minute of this adventure was filled to the brim with well written dialogues, lovable characters, and humorous situations that had me in stitches. All of it packed into a wonderfully crafted, cozy world which invites you to explore every nook and cranny, climb every mountain you can find, and turn over every rock in search for those evil cardboard monsters. All while listening to the wonderfully idyllic tunes that accompany you on your adventure.I can't recommend this game enough to people who are looking for a cozy platforming adventure, as this is the perfect game to sit down with on the couch, enjoy the evening with a cup of hot chocolate and just have some relaxing fun with a widdle-waddling gator who couldn't be more adorable.With this I want to thank the developers, not only for crafting a game which clearly has soul and heart poured into it, but also for allowing me to take a trip down memory-lane.
