_childDocuments_.review: Do I think this is a good game? My Recommendation: - The game's art style looks fantastic. The characters are very expressive and emotive, despite having very simplified models.- Most of the controls were intuitive.- I genuinely enjoyed playing the game while I was playing it.- Most of the dialogue is entertaining and well-written.- Super-optimized. I played 95% of the game on a Steam Deck and it ran flawlessly.- The game captures adventure and exploration so well, the transitions between dialogue to cut scene are so smooth.- Once you load your save game, you will never see a single loading screen the entire time you're playing.- There are a lot of cosmetics and toys to mess around with to help your traversal. Some of them are more useful than others, but you can freely wear anything and with the exception of one quest (where you're forced to wear a certain item), it will prominently display in every cutscene. Some of them even have fun details, eg a certain hat will change your running animation entirely.- The story wasn't anything groundbreaking, but it kept you motivated to keep pushing toward the end. The ending had way more of an emotional punch than I was expecting.- When you finish the main story, you unlock some items that point you in the direction of any missed quests and collectibles, making it super easy to get 100% completion.- The game is SHORT. I completed the main story and saw the ending in less than 4 hours, then spent another 40 minutes grabbing all the missed sidequests and collectibles to unlock the "100% completion" ending. You could probably speedrun the whole game in less than 30 minutes if you know where everything is. Even the devs seemed to realize this and recently patched in a "speedrun" mode that encourages you to rush through it.- Not all the quests made it clear what the goal was. There was a specific quest involving finding an insect that I spent over an hour on, mostly because the hints the game gave me were too vague, and I only found it by accidentally stumbling on the right area. There was another quest asking me to do a specific trick (that was tied to an animation the gator plays during a certain move), which I completed entirely by accident.- Some parts of the map are suspiciously empty until you hit certain triggers in other areas, and it's not clear where these triggers are until you hit them.It's a good game. A very short but good game to be specific. I 100% recommend this game, but I don't think $20 US is worth it for only 4 hours of playtime. Wait until it goes on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Lil Gator Game is a shockingly great game that has largely flown under the radar. I'm a huge fan of A Short Hike and that game, and Lil Gator Game manages to capture the same magic that made that game special, while exceeding the size, scope, and design of A Short Hike.Watching my six year old kid play this game reveals the mastery in game design that the folks at MegaWobble were able to pull off. My kiddo has struggled to learn how to use right analog stick to control the camera in all other 3D games. This was the game that finally taught her how to do it. And it's because of the accessible and inviting game design as well as the engaging world that is full of intriguing locations and characters. This game invites her to experiment and learn while also giving her excellent dialogue to read full of great lessons. I hope the folks at Outright Games are taking notes...That said, this isn't just a kids game as I also loved exploring the world the developers have crafted and finding all sorts of interesting secrets along the way. Absolutely worth playing if you are looking for a game with chill vibes.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an absolutely incredible experience that respects the players as much as it respects itself. This game knows its audience, its limitations, and that it does not need to take itself too seriously to be a great time. I found the polish and feel of the gameplay to be the strongest elements, while the music/characters are a great benefit to the experience. Some mechanics felt underutilized, but that came down to my own preference of how to play the game, so it never bothered me too much.The story was solid for me and made me tear up a tiny bit at the end, which is impressive for me since that has only happened two or three other times in a video game. I also really liked how the game let you play at your own pace, though I feel it may have let go of your hand a little too much at times, since it could become difficult to remember where I needed to go and what to do. The island is not large enough to get easily lost in, however, and the solid level geometry and visuals meant going to a hilltop or tree could easily re-orient myself for the most part.Absolutely recommend to anyone who has dry spell for short-yet-sweet exploration games that never overstay their welcome and let you leave comfortably whenever you like.(Also, I played this on Steam Deck. _childDocuments_.review: Charming, conflict free open-world exploration game about being a carefree child but because it's an indie game turns into an existential treatise on leisurely activities and the societal pressure of adulthood. Because it's an indie game, of course.Lil Gator Game shares a lot of spirit (and aesthetics) with A Short Hike. It's an open world game with lots of hidden collectibles and charming characters. It absolutely nails the movement; you're able to climb any surface Breath of the Wild style but the controls are tight and snappy. You have a "shield" that lets you surf, a "sword" that you use to smash cardboard monsters, and two item slots for goofy gadgets like a sticky-hand that lets you swing like Spider-Man and ninja stars for long range enemies. You can 100% the game on a lazy Saturday and that's in keeping the spirit of the game. Booting it at sunrise and going home at sunset in one sitting is the perfect way to tap into your inner child or play the game with a child, it's all good.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is nostalgic, but not pandering. Heck, I'm sure somebody without their own sibling stories about exploring old adventure games together could enjoy this game thoroughly. It made me think a lot about how my relationship with my sister has grown and changed, and I think I appreciate the things we did together more now.Playing this made me cry! This like, only the 5th game to do that so good job!For my 6th Birthday I recieved the Zelda Collector's Edition, and for the next two years I explored Hyrule and Termina with my big sister. Every time there was something too scary for me, I knew I could hand the controller to my sister and she'd beat it for sure. Though even together we couldn't beat the games, so the real hero of this story is my Grandma who let us copy her save data! This one's for you, Tufstuff, I'd never have seen Ganon's defeat without you.

_childDocuments_.review: It really does manage to capture that feeling of playing pretend when you're a kid, of the forest you grew up next to (or even just your yard or neighborhood) being that truly endless space of imagination. Of picking up a stick and being a sword wielding hero, fighting invisible monsters and chasing a quest only you know about.It is short as expected, but it doesn't *feel* short, and I think that's the important part.Price might feel a little high, but I think on sale it's perfect.
_childDocuments_.name: Lil Gator Game

_childDocuments_.review: Remember when you were a little kid and the biggest drama in your life was "which ninja turtle is the best ninja turtle?" That's this game. It's your childhood. From nerf guns to sticky-slap hands, from playing zelda with your big sister to dressing up as a space-man--- it'll unlock a lot of core memories for a lot of people.Lil Gator is sad that his big sister won't play with him, so he decides to involve the entire island in a Zelda-esque LARP-ing game, complete with quests, cardboard monsters and building their own cardboard TOWN on the playground.With tons of costumes, unlockables, easy achievements and a meaningful ending, Lil Gator is the perfect way to relive your childhood, and the wonder and majesty of climbing on things you're not supposed to but you're gonna do it anyway because you're ten and it's gonna happen. Hahaha.A must-play!
_childDocuments_.name: Lil Gator Game

_childDocuments_.name: Lil Gator Game

_childDocuments_.review: Such a delightful little game. Also quite relatable for those with younger siblings.I'm not a completionist, but I really wanted to 100% this game (the fourth time I've ever done so), I loved it so much. Side note: mad respect for the completionists out there, that takes persistence.Loved the art style, it's quite simple while showing the personality of the characters amazingly. The feeling of destroying items on the island was so satisfying, during my playthrough I didn't tire of it despite how much in game currency I had. The dialogue as well, it's hard to make a kid talk like a kid (I hope that makes sense), but this game does an amazing job of it. Also, how the music changes were handled was really satisfying. Sorry, I'm jumping between disconnected good points. In short, the team behind this game got so much right.The one thing I felt this game lacked was a map. Though I am the kind of person to get lost frequently, so it could just be a me thing.Overall, a very charming game that players can take at their own pace, making it a nice chill option to wind down with at the end of the day.Lastly, obligatory mention that this game clearly takes a lot of inspiration from a certain game series with a green hat wearing protagonist with a focus on triangles.
_childDocuments_.name: Lil Gator Game

_childDocuments_.name: Lil Gator Game

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty short (I completed it 100% in 5.2 hours) but it's obvious that it was made with a LOT of love and passion. The dialogue is full of personality and very wholesome, the island is very well designed (despite there being no map, I rarely got lost and the objectives and placement of quests felt very intuitive to follow) and it's probably the least stressful game I've ever played. I highly recommend it if you're in a dark place in your life, as it will do a good job of brightening your day.Only nitpick is that the game is short, but that might be kind of a good thing; the gameplay doesn't overstay its welcome, the story is paced nicely, the hours you get are very enjoyable, and I could see myself occasionally replaying it.

_childDocuments_.name: Lil Gator Game

_childDocuments_.review: This game did something spectacular in that it made me feel like a kid again! It brought back so many memories of experiences younger me had and plays really well off of the emotions that evokes. Every feature in this game feels like they're designed purely to add onto the ability of the player to make their own fun. Wanna go speeding around endlessly on one of those hand scooters you'd mess up your fingers with in elementary school gym class? Go for it! You can ride around forever on land or on water! In fact, different shields have different fun boosts - I won't spoil what kind of stuff you can do with each one, because almost every single one is unique!Wanna use a balloon to fly as high into the air above the entire map as you want? In time, you can do that too! The game even has a dedicated RAGDOLL BUTTON! What more could you want? Comedy gold has never been more attainable - and all of these things create an unrivaled whimsical childlike wonder experience that brings a smile to anyone's face. I also really enjoyed the writing, each character and scenario had goofy jokes that I felt were clever for the most part. Some got a bit meta, but in a good way that didn't overstay their welcome! This might be in my top 3 favorite games from 2022, it felt like such a breath of fresh air :)

_childDocuments_.review: ★★★★★I was in tears during the game's epilogue. Beautiful and simple game about growing up. I loved the music, cute art style and animations. Gameplay is imaginative and fun. _childDocuments_.review: Yikes.  Really disappointed with this game based on the overwhelmingly positive reviews flying around.  You start on a small island and run around smashing cardboard and doing a couple of random fetch quests, and then when you're done that, you do it all over again, only on a much, much larger island. With no maps or quest markers, no real directions as to where to go, just... "hey all these people just took off across the island, go find them, and then come find me. I also will be somewhere else by that time."  Fetch quests, "hey go find this bug, look for a fallen log."  Where?  Pfft, find it yourself!  Have fun traversing the island.  And much, much, much, much, much more cardboard smashing.Additionally, the characters have no character.  They're all very alike.  Additionally additionally, even after you 'gather' them and send them to the playground, they do not move.  They will appear at the playground if you go there, but they're also still hanging around in their original spot.  So, you know, good luck figuring out who you have and haven't gathered after awhile.  And worst of all, the playe character just comes off as... a pest.  Everybody has to play their game, the way they want to play it, at the time they want to play it.  Who cares if other people have plans?  YOU'RE here now, it's time to play YOUR game!I'm frankly baffled because I don't really know who this game is aimed at.  It's far too simplistic for adults, but also, what kid is going to take in the idea of older kids/young adults needing to focus on schoolwork enough to take in the lesson to... not overly focus on schoolwork? (At least that's the lesson I presume comes at the end, for all I know it's an outright "**** homework, kids!" or like, rocks fall, all the kids die, "should have focused on your homework, kids!")So I played this for about 2 hours and then went back to look at the reviews, baffled, and saw one that mentioned it's 6 hours of playtime or so, and... there's no way in heck I'm going to spend twice the amount of time I've already spent doing THE EXACT SAME THING.

_childDocuments_.review: Spectacularly made game. Fantastic character controller, great graphics and models, exceptional performance and zero bugs. I love the way the enemies are inanimate but still fun to destroy. It's obvious a lot of thought went into getting the fundamentals right, nothing has been ignored or half-baked. _childDocuments_.review: Lil Gator Game is the perfect romp around game mixed with nostalgia. I played this with a preschooler who had an absolute blast just watching me play, and the story was so much more touching than I thought it would be.I highly recommend for anyone who just wants a game that is purely a good time with almost no difficulty (unless you choose to make it a fun challenge), and for anyone who wants a game with a taste of a BotW parkour.I think the only drawback is if you're looking for a challenge, or for a longer game this isn't for you. _childDocuments_.review: While the game COULD be played in one sitting, this IS a very casual and chill game.  The point is to just beat up "monsters" to collect paper scraps, and try to make friends while growing a little fantasy town just to convince your big sister to play along with your hero game.  There -is- a little more to it if you look into the story as you conclude it, but it's a nice little message for people (especially game devs starting off with their own game in mind/are in the middle of making one).The aesthetic of the game is cute, and the characters have a nice design to 'em.  They all have their own little personality to them too (and there's quite a lot of characters to befriend).  The movement is SUPER satisfying though!  You're able to pick up speed/verticality if you know what you're doing and you can really schmove.  And second time around in a new save file, when you know where the stamina bracelet monkey is at, you can hit him up first and uncap your stamina and try for a speedrun and go nuts climbing/flying everywhere~  They have an option for "unstick character", but I can only imagine it's for a rare time you pick up super speed and ragdoll into something too hard....I never got stuck anywhere just from climbing/sliding around at all.If I were to really give an idea on if someone would like this or not, I guess I'd have to ask if you played and liked 'A Short Hike'.  Basically very similar as that game, but just....bigger.  But still being cozy and simple~  If you liked 'A Short Hike', then you'll REALLY like this game too.  Man....I remember when this was just something someone did to show off a 3d gator.  Then it became GIFs/vids of them doing game stuff as they liked 'Breath of the Wild''s movement options.  Eventually, it became a game, and it's a really fun and great one at that.  Dunno if the folks that did this game plan to make anything else in the future, but if they do, they already got a good track record with this one ^^
_childDocuments_.name: Lil Gator Game

_childDocuments_.review: I went into this not sure what to expect other than I had been told "oh my god it's so cute".  And I can for one say "BOY HOWDY IS IT!"   Aside from that though it also tickled my nostalgia buttons in a big way from several different angles... playing pretend, growing up (and others with you), interacting with any random stranger without a care in the world as opposed to fearing what could happen.  There's this beautiful carefree-ness to the world that I miss feeling could be real.All that aside it's really just entertaining and 100%ing it was a delight.
_childDocuments_.name: Lil Gator Game

_childDocuments_.review: As a lil' gator trying to persuade his busy big sis into playing with him, our titular protagonist has his work cut out trying to prove that his kickass game is fun and that his big sis is missing out by being all busy with adult stuff. The best way to do that is OF COURSE to play the game that he's set up with his friends with all sorts of wicked adventures all spread out throughout the island. His cool friends have built cardboard enemy cutouts and pots all over the island that are ripe for the breaking and seems like there's also a bunch of potential pals all over with their own short quests to do! Finishing their quests will potentially also give you cool new weapons and gear which, as we all know, MORE gear equals MORE fun! There's also this mysterious monkey who appears in the most unexpected spots to give you these bracelets that let you climb higher and higher! To get to more spots to break more stuff! What fun!The gameplay loop is essentially exploring every nook and cranny of the island to finish small one-off quests but also to gather the core party to build up a base on the center to get the sister to play with the Lil Gator. While being simple, the game is short enough where it does not wear its welcome out though by the very end of it I was most definitely ready for it to be done. You start off with a melee attack, a slide with your "shield" and two items though these expand as you finish quests for people scattered all over and adds a little bit of flavor as you swing your paintbrush wearing a beret and sporting a massive easel shield that you use to slide down mountains. The bracelets that you get fro the monkey that you can find give you stamina that you use to climb up sheer cliffs though you could pretty much finish the game on a single one considering I had barely any difficulty scaling anything but the highest points on the map.While the gameplay is simple, what makes this game so enjoyable for me is the MASSIVE dose of charm, earnestness and pure joy injected directly into everything. It reminds me of my own time as a kid being a little scamp, making imaginary games with my friends and making my own fun with the areas around my house. Our troupe of daring ne'er-do-wells would play out all sorts of adventures on various fantasy lands and this taps directly into my nostalgia for that time. The presentation adds so much with its goofy yet lovely character models, a pretty well rendered and pretty landscape and some soothing music that lilts through most of your time.I'm not sure if A Short Hike was an inspiration for this game but it is extremely similar to that in a lot of ways but definitely does its own thing that's clearly more inspired by Zelda. The game brings a TON of charm and heart into a fairly simple exploration based game in a small island making it far more than the sum of its parts and I thoroughly recommend this for anyone looking for a short jaunt through one's childhood adventures.
_childDocuments_.name: Lil Gator Game

But all in all a very cute and ejoyable game. I'd more than love to see a sequel with further adventures.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a lot of fun. It invokes a child-like sense of wonder and exploration. There's a lot of similarities to A Short Hike that Lil Gator Game has. Aesthetically they feel very close, minus the pixel filter that A Short Hike has. The humor is really tongue in cheek and has some really good points. Getting all the achievements was very easy, and there's tools built in that make getting everything very easy after you complete the main story. It took me 4.5 hours to 100% all the achievements.If you enjoyed this game, try out A Short Hike. If you've played A Short Hike, try this game. _childDocuments_.review: What a fun little game, mostly played with my son who is currently in elementary school.  We had a blast together running around the island, completing quests, leveling up and getting through the cute little story.  It blows my mind what some creative developers can come up with.  This game has:- [x] Story - cute characters, full of emotion, easy to digest dialog that is well written along with some choices that matter and make a difference in the world.  Fun scenarios that help provide young ones with some moral choices to make.- [x] Visuals - simple enough yet pleasant to look at.  The world is colorful and animated.  Character animations are also solid.- [x] Gameplay - simple mechanics that are a little forgiving but fun and get slightly more complex as you progress through the story as you unlock new tools and abilities.- [x] Music and sound effects - decent original soundtrack that contributes to making the world feel alive.All around a very fun and wholesome little game.  Highly recommended as a relaxing family friendly game to play, especially with young kids who are early readers.  There is a lot of dialog and not a lot of voice acting.

_childDocuments_.name: Lil Gator Game

_childDocuments_.name: Lil Gator Game

_childDocuments_.review: This game is my GOTY. I don't think anything else can surpass it in terms of sheer joy to video game drudgery ratio, because this game is 100% joy without the faff. I don't think it cribs from A Short Hike too much at all, because you can't just copy funny, heartfelt dialogue like this, and this game is genuinely hilarious. _childDocuments_.name: Lil Gator Game

_childDocuments_.review: So, big downside right off the bat is its length. I finished it in a little over 4 hours.But those four hours were full of charm and happiness. The atmosphere of this game is amazing. You're just a lil' gator who wants to play, and pretty much everyone wants to play with them.Run around, climbing hills and trees, swimming in lakes and rivers, imagining yourself as the hero, saving the world from boredom as you tear through hordes of monsters (which are just cardboard cuttouts).Fantastic for those who are young, young at heart, and miss being young. _childDocuments_.name: Lil Gator Game

_childDocuments_.review: Any game in which you can play as a little alligator, who I can name "Agent 49", who can rag doll out of the sky, at blistering speeds, having just been foiled by a piece of bubblegum popping, sending me towards the ground, and in most other games, to my inevitable death, only for me to fall on to a wolf called Lucas, who I then talk to, with him wanting to overcome his fear of talking to Martin (a horse), before spending the entire conversation trying to persuade him to watch "Power Fighters on DVD", is a pretty decent game.I just wish they would add the ability to punch in the face and/or groin to really test the player's discipline.+rep cool guy easy fair trade.

_childDocuments_.name: Lil Gator Game

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a grown ass man and this game almost made me cry several times.It's just a little platformer with no stakes centered around the brother-sister relationship between two little gators and all the friends you meet along the way, but it absolutely oozes charm and wholesome energy.This is a game I'd recommend for basically anyone, though if you just like feel good games this is especially for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Lil Gator Game

_childDocuments_.review: This game is, to put it simply, pure joy. It's incredibly cute, the story is a timeless, touching tale and the characters are so godamn adorable. It's a relax adventure on a lovely island packed with adventure only a kid could dream up, and it's extremely endearing. I'm a sensitive guy, and I'm not lying when I say a couple of places made me crack a wide smile with childish glee or shed a tear of emotional bliss. If you want a relax game that takes about 5 hours to get through if you're going through nooks and crannies, please pick this game up! It's absolutely wonderful.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good non-violent game with good controls.It's peaceful, don't have to rush anything, though you could try to excel at challenges.Currently there are no leaderboards, but there are activities in game that are time challenges. These challenges are quite well made and are fun.About 7 hours of gameplay. Quite text/dialogue heavy (they are good quality dialogues though). General activities/quests could use more depth, they felt very shallow, in a sense of what you, as a player actually do. There is some variety in activities. Open world could be tighter, both in regard to movement speed, and to ability usage. For example, broader venues to go on shield bounce streaks, meshed with tighter npc and climbing spaces, where you just walk around. By the end of the game you do get unlimited prancing around.So the pacing of the game and activities depth could be better. Visually the game is fine, though for my taste I'd have greater shadow fidelity to make plane separation easier on the eyes.Sound is very, very well made.Overall, the game is not about the result, but about the journey, and I like that.

_childDocuments_.review: I LOVED this game! Very cute, chill, fun to just relax and have a good time with. The characters are charming, the music is great; Esme's cave area has the best song in my opinion, but they're all good and don't get old, the style is CUTE and colourful, plus there's not only a certain level of customization for your lil gator, but a photo mode as well! The game gets deep when it matters, but it's mostly just a funny, quirky little game. Nothing TOO serious and deep, which I enjoy now and again!There's a lot of places to go and friends to make, and my only real complaint is that I wish there was a map to figure out where I am sometimes. There's a map here and there in-game, but it becomes somewhat easy to get lost if you're trying to get back somewhere specific. That said though, it's really not a deal-breaker, and in terms of in-game reasons, I even understand why there isn't a map.As someone who like to get achievements, I do enjoy that once you finish the main story, you get items to help you find some stuff you might've missed. name: Essays on Empathy
detailed_description: Essays on Empathy is a curated compilation of Deconstructeam 's best efforts in seeking new narrative experiences in games. Inhabit the lives of a diverse cast of characters from all walks of life in bite-sized, innovative, interactive stories; from a hitman working at a flower shop, to a schoolgirl who is convinced her skeleton isn't hers. Explore 10 unique, offbeat tales including ' De Tres al Cuarto ,' a brand new short experience exclusive to the compilation about a couple of two-bit comedians trying to make it big. Ten Short Games About Life: Step into the shoes of a richly imagined cast of characters over 5 hours of vivid and varied gameplay. Premium Collector's Bonus Content: Soak up Deconstructeam's acclaimed artistry through sketches, design insights and a new mini documentary created specially for this collection. Sounds Of Sympathy: Features more than 2 hours of original music by Paula Ruiz, aka fingerspit.

_childDocuments_.review: So what exactly are the games on offer in this captivating collection?Let me break it down into its ten components:Underground Hangovers (Genre: Metroidvania/Platformer)If you had to leave a mysterious planet tomorrow would you: a) go to sleep at a reasonable time to ensure you don't miss the only rocket off the planet, or b) have a massive party, wake up with a throbbing hangover, and miss the only rocket off the planet? Well in this case, the unfortunate party from Underground Hangovers chose the latter.In what feels like the odd game out in the collection (as it's far more focused on gameplay), you're tasked with collecting enough ore to rebuild a rocket to make your way off this desolate planet. Though a simple game initially made for a Game Jam in 2015, it features some creative platforming puzzles that feel right at home in the genre. Supercontinent Ltd (Genre: Cyberpunk/Narrative)Bold, atmospheric, gripping and clever. Supercontinent Ltd is a narrative-heavy cyberpunk experience that will leave you thirsty for more. Playing as Brandeis (a character who also appears in The Red Strings Club), this game revolves around the use of ancient technology: a landline phone. Through use of a voice modulator (VOMOD), Brandeis makes phone calls to unravel the plot behind a mysterious organisation on the evening of their plan to overthrow the police force.With its engaging dialogue, gloomy pixel-art aesthetic, and ambient synth soundtrack, this game oozes style from every pixel. Impressively, Supercontinent somehow manages to achieve more character development and world-building in thirty minutes than games like Cyberpunk 2077 do in their entire narrative. Thirty minutes well spent.Behind Every Great One  (Genre: Drama/Narrative)Riding on a high from Supercontinent, I jumped straight into the next game. I was not prepared for what I was about to feel. This game is, at times, mentally and emotionally difficult to play. Interestingly, the developers too discuss how difficult this game was to create. If you're not in a good headspace, I would approach Behind Every Great One with caution. It will make you feel like absolute ♥♥♥♥.You play as Victorine, the housewife to Gabriel, who is a renowned and celebrated artist. Living in his shadow, life has become a monotonous repetition of household chores and meaningless attempts at activity devoid of passion, interspersed with frequent anxiety attacks. The story becomes progressively more depressing as you delve deeper into the characters' broken relationship and expectations of Victorine. It's a highly emotive and confronting game that is not for the faint of heart.Eternal Home Floristry  (Genre: Narrative/Flower Arrangement)An injured hitman loses his arm in an attack and is forced to seek refuge in the house of a florist called Sebastian, with whom he builds a relationship during their short time together. Learning the art of flower arrangement and the messages the blooms convey, Gordon is able to delve deeper into his own emotions and relationships. A highly emotive narrative that explores raw human emotion and the fragile elements that reside within even the most harsh exteriors.My favourite in the collection. Several times it even had me on the verge of tears. An impressive feat for a game that can easily be completed in half an hour. Though the game may be short, choices based on your flower arrangements will dramatically affect the outcome.The Bookshelf Limbo (Genre: Point-and-Click)Simplistic and charming; more of a minigame than a proper standalone title. Pick a comic book from the shelf at a bookstore to purchase as a birthday present for your father! This game was created as a birthday gift alongside a friend of the developers and features amusing cover art, genre stereotypes, and mocking of internet trolls.Zen and the Art of Transhumanism (Genre: Sci-Fi/Narrative)Pottery meets Cyberpunk in a genre mash-up I never thought I'd encounter. As a new member of a human improvement workshop, you're tasked with creating body modifications to fulfil your client's needs. By handcrafting differently-shaped mods, you'll be able to enhance certain physical traits and oblige the wishes of the often-selfish humans. Engolasters January 2021 (Genre: Sci-Fi/Adventure)In my opinion the least-enjoyable game in the entire collection. Set in the real life small mountain town of Engolasters, the protagonist (whose son has just run away from home) stumbles across extra-terrestrial life which offers to bestow great power. She must make a choice to save her son, herself, or unravel the secrets that lure her into the unknown. Afflicted by a wound and slowly losing blood, players must manage their life, phone battery, and car fuel while exploring the frosty overworld. The overworld is vast, empty, and lacking in direction, which led me to become easily frustrated.11:45 A Vivid Life (Genre: Point-and-Click)The most interesting concept out of all the games: what if your skeleton didn't belong to you? This simple point-and-click game explores the topic of body image and acceptance. By stealing an x-ray machine and fleeing to the country, the protagonist discovers more about herself by looking inside. Literally. X-rays reveal implants, evidence of past trauma, and pieces that seem mismatched and out of place. Once located, any foreign body parts must be forcibly removed through the use of pliers or scalpels. Not for the squeamish! Players can choose dialogue that will vary the consequences of the story, weaving an entertaining, introspective narrative with a stylish visual aesthetic.Dear Substance of Kin (Genre: Horror/Adventure)For a moment I could have sworn I was playing something straight out of Bloodborne! This title is melancholy, chilling, and is dripping with disturbing atmosphere like a blood-soaked cloth. Exploring a decrepit and dilapidated town, you are the Coppersmith, an immortal artisan who harvests the organs of townspeople in exchange for fulfilling their requests through blood magic. By interrogating the residents, you can perceive their selfish desires and choose to either fulfil or sabotage them.Des Tres al Cuatro (Genre: Comedy/Narrative)The main feature of this collection, a game that translates to "Three for a Quarter" (e.g. something of such poor quality that you can buy three of them for a single quarter), also the name of the comedy duo that you play as during this game. Garza and Bonachera are two halves of a failing comedy act, two lovers, and two grown men struggling for success, stumbling over the hurdles of their passions and their relationship. The story here is particularly personal to the developers, as it emphasises the harsh reality of making a living off of a creative pastime. Conversations between the characters are deeply intimate and allow the player to dive beneath the surface by revealing the characters' inner thoughts on a separate area of the screen.Gameplay is incredibly creative and unlike anything I've played, combining aspects of deckbuilding games with comedy dialogue, allowing you to attempt to earn coins to improve your deck. Cards will either build upon a joke, execute a hilarious punchline, or fail miserably and embarrass yourself in front of an entire crowd. Not only is it fun to play, but many of the jokes are legitimately amusing and it's quite satisfying to be able to slowly improve your confidence with each show.ConclusionA vast amount of passion has been poured into crafting these short but powerful games, which becomes even more apparent while watching the developers discuss each title in their respective documentaries. Thoughtfully reflective, introspective and emotive, Essays on Empathy is 50% videogame, 50% documentary, and 100% heart. If you're the kind of person who plays videogames not only for enjoyment, but for deep narratives, important messages, or artistic expression, then this is an essential experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Essays on Empathy

_childDocuments_.review: This is like touring a vineyard or a craft brewery.For $13, you get not only several samples of their wares (some progenitors to games like Red Strings Club, some completely unique), but you also get wonderful commentary for each and every one of these by the artisans that made them, as well as the history of the studio and the people within over the past few years.These commentaries are completely optional, and can be taken before or after or never at all in relation to the games, although I highly recommend you do. Regardless, if you're only interested in the games themselves, $1.30 per game with concept art AND soundtracks is a steal in and of itself. Each game is different and unique, and it has a lot of variety to be had. You are near guaranteed to like at least one of these games, if not all.I bought this because I am a big fan of the studio's previous works Gods Will Be Watching and The Red Strings Club. If you like either, you will love this. If you haven't tried either, perhaps this will interest you in their further works.
_childDocuments_.name: Essays on Empathy

_childDocuments_.review: - Short Review -Essentially a collection of short stories that cover a wide range of topics. I will say there are strong themes in most, if not all, of the games present in Essays on Empathy. There are warnings before you play each one so you will not be blindsided. A lot of these games hit close to home, so please play with care. - Toasty -11.45 A Vivid Life Eternal Home Floristry Behind Every Great One A Bookshelf Limbo De Tres al CuartoDear Substance of Kin Supercontinent Ltd - Burnt -Zen and the Art of Transhumanism Engolasters 2021 Underground Hangovers I would get this game just for the toasty short stories, but everyone has their flavour so the ones I didn’t enjoy might just be your cup of tea. - Long review -Underground Hangovers went a tad bit over my head with the mechanics, but the idea of the game was very neat. Some bugs soft locked the game so I was unable to fully enjoy it (aka complete it) but it’s worth a shot to see if you can finish it! Supercontinent Ltd was a short but fascinating game, letting you play detective while unravelling corporate antics. Loved the gameplay for this one (may have gotten a little stuck in the beginning but I blame my poor detective skills) Behind Every Great One is a game that needs to be played in order to fully grasp how strong and emotional it is. Definitely not a game you play because it is fun, the messages it portrays are very important. Eternal Home Floristry is a melancholic game about floral arrangements and coming to terms with past events. This was a beautiful game to play and a joy to replay. 10/10 bouquet names. A Bookshelf Limbo is one of those games that people might not see the point of, but my goodness was it lovely. If you enjoy browsing at the bookstore then A Bookshelf Limbo is definitely your game. It’s sweet, thought provoking, and tells a lot with very little context. Zen and the Art of Transhumanism had a cool gameplay concept but my god the controls were just not something I was a fan of. As someone with a 60% keyboard, I had a very difficult time with this game. Don’t let this hold you back though, the game was still very unique. Engolasters 2021 has a slow burn, oh no what is happening, feel to it. I like the idea but it feels like something is missing. If you like exploration with little payoff then this might appeal to you more. (SPOILER) I was stuck wandering endlessly for over 10 mins on the lake trying to find the aliens but alas I made no progress. I don’t blame the game for this, just my tiny brain. 11.45 A Vivid Life, man words escape me for this game. Just like Behind Every Great One, this is a haunting game that doesn’t make you feel very good. It puts that pit in your tummy, the genre of this game really depends on you and how you interpret it. Dear Substance of Kin is a bloody cool concept of a game (no pun intended.) This dark, fantasy theme would be perfect as a full game. I mean, I got goosebumps playing this! This one was a one of a kind in the collection for sure. Last but not least, De Tres al Cuarto. This was the longest of the games, ranging around 60 minutes. Some parts can feel a little repetitive but overall it’s enjoyable enough to keep you going (can be addicting if you like deck building games.) There’s a sad reality to this game, not the whole comedian shtick, but I imagine everyone can relate to at least one thing in this game. The pandemic was a hard hit for all and De Tres al Cuarto goes deep into the daily struggles of life that everyone faces at some point in time. Lovely little game to end off the collection. If you have the time and thoroughly enjoyed the games, I do recommend watching the documentaries that go along with them. They provide a little extra context behind the meaning of each game. - Verdict -These games are not perfect but overall, they’re pretty fun and worth the price in my personal opinion. I’d give it 8 loaves out of a dozen.
_childDocuments_.name: Essays on Empathy

_childDocuments_.review: First: Everyone who rates this negative didn't get the point. Let me explain why.This is not a game, it is a collection. Regard it as a sketch book with some more, some less polished prototypes that are presented in a very nice basket. Decontructeam decided to put together a brief overview over their work of more than six years and selected ten games to go into this basket. They did not pick the best fruits, but the ones representing their development as a studio. If you know The Red Strings Club, their most famous title, you will recognize two of the prototypes.But what makes this selection truly special is the video commentary accompanying every game. It gives us players insight in a process we never get to see that closely, the ups and downs of development, the struggles of being creative. I was touched by the open-heartness I encountered in these videos. The three developers from Decontructeam talk about their personal issues and why that influences their games. Play them to watch the videos afterwards.And you get the soundtrack on top. Paula "fingerspit" is one of the most talented artists I know and her work is outstanding. Just listen to the soundtrack, even if you did not like the games. They are not what this is about. But if you are not satisfied yet, have a look at the concept art and be inspired by true artists.If you are not interested in getting insights on an outstanding studio, consider buying The Red Strings Club instead. Or just buy it to support the artists that are visionaries in the game industry. They deserve every cent. But please have a second thought before rating this negative.Liked this? Visit me .
_childDocuments_.name: Essays on Empathy

_childDocuments_.review: The title really suits the game. As a (most likely) a mentally healthy person, I could experience a chunk of how people with mental struggles live. Especially the one in Behind Every Great One. I came in a condition where I didn't want to continue to the next day in the game because I didn't want to face the all the same (or even worse) struggles over and over again. Then I came into realisation that perhaps that's how people with mental struggles live. And it's terrifying just to imagine to experience it alone without a support system every time.Really loved how each 10 bite-sized games come with behind the scene talks from the developer. Still hard to believe most of the games were created during game jam / hackathon such as Ludum Dare. Each of it has solid concept and able to touches our heart or tickles our brain even with minimal gameplay, artwork, and sound design. Some of my favourites are Behind Every Great One, Eternal Home Floristry, and Zen and the Art of Transhumanism.That being said, I wouldn't recommend this game to people who already experience mental struggles IRL as it'll probably be triggering things we wouldn't want to happen. But would really love if more people who never get exposed to these sensitive topics to play. It'll really be an eye-opening experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Essays on Empathy

_childDocuments_.review: A collection of game-jam quality gamemaker studio games. Don't get me wrong, they would certainly be above average for most game jams, but overall? The game's are lacking a lot of substance. They have good ideas, writing that ranges from a bit boring to kinda good (so never outright terrible), art that's pretty consistently impressive, game mechanics that are not the greatest, and programming that just sucks (but that's also just gamemaker for you). The title of "essays on empathy" made me think this would be a series of vignettes into grounded or morally complex stories, and unfortunately it's not really there. Honestly I would've given these 3-4 stars on itch.io if they were released for free, but as a paid product? I could just see three as the number of games in this collection that are worth your time and money. is an extremely amateurish metroidvania. The game functions but it's super buggy and it's easy to get stuck in a wall or the floor. The game's design overall isn't great either, I get what they were going for but the gameplay just isn't there. is a "morally complex" (debatably) hacking game about social-engineering your way through an organization. It's got some issues of not really making it clear what information counts as "new information". Overall one of the better games in the collection. is a narrative game about a woman dealing with an egotistical husband and his disrespectful family. Out of all the games this one feels the most like it has something concrete to say, so even while I think it's a bit surface-level in terms of the mechanics and narrative, I think this is the sort of game which, given some more development, could have really shined. Either way, it kind of feels like a proof-of-concept more than a finished game at this point. Still, the way the game judges your choices and you're always playing catch up is a good way of integrating what little gameplay this has with its narrative. is a flower-building game about a hitman. It's pretty slow, but honestly it's innovative and one of the best games in the collection. It wasn't too long, even if the opening is a little slow, and the flower-building mechanic is simple enough for them to build around and complex enough to allow some creativity. It's nice.  is barely a game. Even sofar as other ones are barely games. It lampshades the fact that the whole "Essays on Empathy" title is pretentious but that's pretty hollow considering... well, they still called it that. Anyway, the game is basically a browsing storefront and you can never choose a book. That's the gimmick.  is a pottery game where you make various pottery designs to help people with their problems. As cool and innovative as that sounds on its surface, the mechanics are kinda boring, and the game overall feels like it's lacking a lot. I have a feeling most of the work went into the core mechanic, but it's a hard one to make into a game. is a top-down game where you can choose to love your son or ♥♥♥♥ off and become space witches. Honestly I don't think there's anything more I can say about it, mechanics are janky and feel bad to control, narrative is compelling enough but missing a lot.  probably the most experimental and interesting story of the bunch. I'm not sure there's a bunch of critique I could give without super getting into the weeds, so I'll just say it's interesting. Much like the rest, it can be a bit slow in some places, and maybe some variety for multiple playthroughs, but overall good. The premise is pretty much immediately gripping, and the story is left pretty ambiguous to fill in. a painfully slowly paced top-down game with the most interesting premise and worldbuilding of the bunch. You are the coppersmith, a mysterious man(?) who goes around essentially doing the opposite of palm-reading. Back-writing? In any case, it's got a very dark-souls vibe to it I just wish that the game didn't take so long, but part of that is probably because the game is part of a collection and so I was playing them in order. is a game about two gay comedians struggling to get by in the Spanish comedy circuit. The characters are pretty decent, the gameplay does a really nice job of making you feel like you're struggling to keep up, sort of like Behind Every Great One. The jokes range from alright to god-awful, but I think that's partially by design. Either way, didn't super satisfy me as a narrative goes, but not super disappointing either. It's fine.Overall meh. Even at 50% off, I'd say $6.50 is more than it's worth. I'd say $5 would be a reasonable price for it, if not a little less.
_childDocuments_.name: Essays on Empathy

_childDocuments_.review: This is not just a game, it's a manifesto about what are games right now and about what they can achieve as an artistic medium. You can feel the "empathy" of the title in the ten works, but it's specially in Behind Every Great One and De Tres al Cuarto where this amazing experiment shines and shows us how videogames are capable of dealing with human relationships and emotions.
_childDocuments_.name: Essays on Empathy

_childDocuments_.review: Although some of the games are tedious and/or lack substance, most of them are great. The art is amazing in all of them; Deoconstructeam never fails on that. Standout games are: Behind Every Great One, A Vivid Life, Eternal Home Floristry, The Bookshelf Limbo, and my favourite: De Tres al Cuarto. Those are the ones I think have the best story, and De Tres al Cuarto and A Vivid life were the most innovative ones, in my opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: Essays on Empathy

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely easy to recommend, there's so much here to appreciate. Compelling narratives, consistently great music, beautiful art, relatable and believable characters. Always love when a game's mechanics tie in with its themes. Basically everything in here made me feel something real. Just buy it. With 10 unique experiences it's a safe bet you're gonna find something you like. The interviews are such a cool bonus too! I love hearing artists talk about their creative process but it's especially fun learning things as a long-term fan.
_childDocuments_.name: Essays on Empathy

_childDocuments_.review: Essays of Empathy is a collection of little, short games which are all full of soul.The games themselves shift between a variety of genres and different moods quite effortlessly and what's very interesting in this package is also the developers' commentary about each game's creative process. I didn't know much about them except the fact that I loved Gods Will Be Watching, so this was really nice to see.Some of the games aren't exactly the most polished games ever, but (particularly considering that most of them are developed on very tight deadlines for game jams) they don't need to be. In the end, it's a very enjoyable experience and one you'll very likely be into if you enjoyed some of Deconstructeam's other works. Otherwise, check it out if you're into this newer school of more mindful and thought-provoking videogames that touch upon real life issues and social/emotional/sensitive topics.
_childDocuments_.name: Essays on Empathy

_childDocuments_.review: A collection of ten short games from Deconstructeam. It's really cool seeing how a game team develops a style.I see this like a short story collection - short and sweet, with thoughts from the creators at the end on how each game came together.There's a few bugs and typos, but overall this is really cool.
_childDocuments_.name: Essays on Empathy

_childDocuments_.review: Overall this anthology is a pleasant experience, my only gripe is I wish there was more content in individual games. However, having watched the documentaries after playing each game, I understand why there wasn’t. I’m going to delve into each of the different games. I’ll be ordering them from least liked to most liked in my personal opinion. Spoilers ahead of course. Zen and the Art of Transhumanism: Right off the bat it’s difficult to play, the action button on the keyboard is x or space. I feel like this default would be more acceptable if the movement keys were wasd, but they aren’t, they are the arrow keys. The button mashing required for the game to proceed is repetitive enough that it becomes painful to play for too long. The concept is interesting and the art is intriguing but I simply can’t play it properly. The Bookshelf Limbo:Not a whole lot to say, it’s about finding a book for your father as a present. There’s some story and the gameplay is short, requiring you only to look through the options and pick one. It’s akin to a very short visual novel. Simple but sweet. Engolasters January 2021:A slightly corny game about someone in the mountains with a telescope. They get lost on their way home and run into aliens. Funny thing is I really did get lost in the game, I don’t think I ever found the aliens, it’s been a little bit since I played this one but it’s not something I’m super into.Underground Hangovers:I would rate this one higher on the list, but the others after it appeal to me more. This game is about spe scientist left on a planet after blacking out, you have to collect and build the materials they need to escape back to home. It’s a platformer metroidvania that is quite enjoyable. I may not have been able to figure out how to beat it, but I implore you to tryEternal Home Floristry:A game about accepting the past. I love the story and the gameplay of building bouquets, the flowers you pick completely determine the meaning of each bouquet and it influences how the story goes a little. I find this one very relaxing.  Supercontinent LtD: I really enjoy this kind of gameplay, however the directions can be a little hard to find/follow at times. The concept of making calls and investigating isn’t new but its a fun take on the trope11.45 A Vivid Life: A story that can be interpreted in three different directions, each one a chilling visual in its own right. The themes and art strike a cord with me an I appreciate them, though the game itself could be triggering to some. I recommend heading the warnings before playing it. Dear Substance of Kin: Similar to Engolasters January 2021 this is an open world game. However the visuals, story and themes are much better developed in my opinion. I enjoyed this sandbox game a lot more than the last one in this collection.Des Tres al Cuarto: Deckbuilder, cheesy comedy and a compelling relationship driving the story. What’s not to love about this? It’s fun and challenging while keeping me interested in the characters and the gameplay at the same time.Behind Every Great One:This is the game I enjoyed most of all, it’s monotonous and is emotionally draining as a story/game experience. I recommend just playing this one and hopefully you’ll agree with me just how good it is.
_childDocuments_.name: Essays on Empathy

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful collection of short games, each with something interesting, but more importantly, telling the story of this tiny studio developing their craft. The mini documentary is the real star here (and it seems a shame that, according to the achievements, a lot of people are skipping the videos and just playing the games). It explores what each game meant to the creators, what new ideas it brought that they carried forward, and some of their personal struggles.The games themselves are raw. They are mostly game jam prototypes, "finished" but not polished. They are short, often janky, and it often feels like another week of work on each of these would have polished them into a beautiful perfect gem. But that would tarnish the historical value of each: that they are records of where the studio was at at a certain time. So no, these games aren't perfect, but they each have something wonderful to discover. I played this in the lead-up to the Cosmic Wheel Sisterhood release, something which they clearly hint at in the videos but were unable to discuss publicly at the time. I like that some of the later games have elements that would make it into Cosmic Wheel (like the creativity in Eternal Home Floristry, or the deckbuilding for narrative choices of De Tres al Cuarto).The one thing that feels missing from this collection is a specific game: I would have loved if the collection started with the original prototype of Gods Will Be Watching. Since the story of this package is the trajectory of the studio from "space sci-fi is cool" to "let's talk about our feelings", it would have been neat to open with the prototype for their first big game, and have a video where they talked about that experience and how they grew from there. Instead, Underground Hangovers functionally serves that role as the "this is how we used to make games" game.I'm really glad for this curated collection. You can play all of these games (now even the previously exclusive De Tres al Cuarto) for free on their website, but buying this package gives you a neat curated set with concept art and the documentary. If you're a fan of Gods Will Be Watching, The Red Strings Club or The Cosmic Wheel Sisterhood, you should check out this behind-the-scenes tour of their smaller "in between" games.

_childDocuments_.review: Unintuitive, is the first thing that came to my mind. I really wish Steam had a "mixed opinion" option but it doesn't, and so I can't recommend it. The games are indeed from many game james and as such suffer from quite a few bugs, as i've suffered during play.Many of them have odd or old control scheme, much older than the year they were being made in, and some suffer from questionable design choices that impact the pacing and feel of the game overall. Some games simply have no help or indication at all which can lead to quite a few confusions. There is also no save system.As i assume that all games from a game jams are a free, i cannot recommend such a price for what amounts to gallery pictures and short interviews. Some interesting ideas came of it all, but the Deconstructeam strikes me as quite excentric and their games sometimes suffer from it.If you are interested in game jams and their results as well as playing with some interesting interactive stories, i'd recommend it during sales.

_childDocuments_.review: I played The Red Strings Club and it's one of my most favorite interactive point and click games of all time.  I just recently bought and am currently playing The Cosmic Wheel Sisterhood.  I really enjoy the graphics, the music, and the storytelling in both games.Essays on empathy is a very well done compilation of the developer's earlier mini-games and with their added documentary clips, gives very detailed insight into how this studio evolved from one game to the next.  The entire package is fun and engaging to sift through, and I wish other indie developers did something like this.  I'd buy them all!If you love any of the games by Deconstructeam (Red Strings Club, Cosmic Wheel Sisterhood, Gods Will Be Watching) then you really should experience 'essays on empathy'.As a bonus, the entire 2-hour soundtrack for this compilation comes with it.  A folder of MP3s.  The album is called 'Sounds Of Sympathy' and it's free! it will install with the game.This game is such a value.  Really recommend this!Note:  My Xbox game controller works in a few of the mini-games I've played.  So have a controller ready when you go through this!

_childDocuments_.review: From the little I was able to play, Essays on Empathy was really good. Whether it’s picking a gift for your father or picking possibly the last flowers on earth for a memorial, every story packed a punch emotionally. The issue I had with the game was that only 3 of the 10 stories worked on Steam Deck despite being marked as playable. Sometimes the screen will start to flicker violently before crashing. Other times directional button inputs wouldn’t register at all before the controlled character runs and gets stuck at the edge of the level. Even on a traditional PC there two very annoying design flaws. All the in game developer’s commentaries will not load and there is a 90 minute game here that doesn’t have a save feature. At the end of the day Essays on Empathy biggest failure is its accessibility.
_childDocuments_.name: Essays on Empathy

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good collection of some really nice game jam games- and an invaluable look at the work of Deconstructeam. It's the whole journey from before The Red Strings Club to working on The Cosmic Wheel Sisterhood, and I'd highly recommend playing both those and this for the fullest picture.The real gem, however, is the videos. It's an absolutely incredible chance to look behind the curtain, of how they develop games and why they make the ones they do. For that alone, this is worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: Essays on Empathy stands out as an anthological game series, a product of the unique collaboration between Deconstructeam’s trio of creatives: Jordi, Marina, and Paula. This team has crafted ten short games encapsulated on an 8-bit isometric landscape, each resulting from their various experimentations, 'happy accidents,' and Lurem Dure themes. While some may wonder about the creative writer’s decision to mix literary devices as part of the game’s title—it provides a cohesive direction on what to expect from these curations of games. Indeed, every game is an essay, the creative’s narratology on several themes—and how these narratives intertwined in the gaming landscape.  While the gaming industry thrives in the proliferation of what seems to be consumed as ‘easy entertainment,’ several games step beyond the line by breaking the fourth wall. It takes more than just some thought-provoking dialogues inserted into characters—it also allows the player base to see these characters (despite being animated) as vessels of empathy. Visual novels, due to their nature of narrating within the game, are perfect experimentation grounds for creative writers to instill ideals, their vision of the world, their mores, and all. As Theodor Lipps perfectly describes, the “emphatic encounters” we indulge in allow us to “appreciate art and all the truths it creates.” To have a vessel for gaming creatives is to instill Charles Bukowski’s ideal of “burning and destroying” concepts to give birth to “new truths.” The integration of artwork and music reconstructed these essays into a Homunculus of possibly a radical turn of creating visual novels—and hopefully—gaming in the future. As mentioned, this multi-game is enclosed in isometric capsules, allowing players to choose up to ten games.In this point-and-click game, you will play the life of Laynie, a confused lady who truly believes that her skeleton doesn’t belong to hers. After stealing an X-ray machine and scanning several parts of her body, she dissects every material to infer her intrusive thoughts. The different dialogues provide a lot of replayability, with six possible endings you can come up with. While some graphic scenes of self-mutilation and PTSD were shown, the 8-bit pixel sprites reduce the grotesque factor.This point-and-click game provides a dramatic narrative of impending anxiety within several spaces. Gabriel and Victorine are having a rift between their passion, parental pressure, and romance. As a growing artist, Gabriel feels the pressure of widening his space in the art scene—climbing the ladders of creation to outweigh his previous art pieces. Meanwhile, Victorine feels strangled and tightened on several expectations to be more than just a doting homemaker. While this offers only a linear depiction, this game conceives how internal pressure and anxiety could affect someone’s depiction of themselves and their loved ones. If you were given a chance to give a book as a present to your father, what would it be? The male MC has several books to choose from on the bookshelf via point-and-click, albeit limited to what the game developers only produced. Despite being the least relatable game in this series, it is still fun to see how to introduce reading literature in a gaming way. It piques interest and could get someone who doesn’t read much to skim a few books or two—and start reading.“Three for a quarter” is self-deprecating humor about how Garzo and Bonachera see their comedic duo. Living as homosexuals, these two small-time comedians reflect life by the beach of Menorca. While the deck-building doesn’t affect the character’s decision, it adds an element to the gaming experience—a metaphor for how their lives are shuffled and arranged in such a manner—for the quest for contentment in the ever-greedy world we currently live in. I’m also impressed with how they introduced relationships beyond the ‘conventional’ monogamous setup—a radical attempt to introduce interpersonal dynamics and what romance could be made of.In this horror point-and-click game, you will play as The Coppersmith, withdrawing life for those whose innermost carnal desires still crave more. Using life as a vessel of currency adds a dreadful atmosphere to the game as you watch these characters barter even with their kin to gratify their wishes. This game from the Deconstructeam’s suite is the only one with voice acting, which added much-needed chills to the spine. The sandbox approach to this game also gives additional leeway for the players to get involved in the narrative process—by creating a non-linear course to the Coppersmith’s path.Gordon, a wounded hitman, decided to tend his wounds in a flower shop owned by Sebastian. In the hitman’s short stay at the older man’s flower shop, the two develop a mentor-mentee dynamic—as Sebastian teaches Gordon life through flower arrangement. Depending on how Gordon arranged the flowers, the outcomes for the flower’s recipient would also vary. This allows the player to create a deterministic outcome on the subjects—and while it wouldn’t affect the overall narrative—the switching of dialogues creates a diverse dimension in the visual novel itself. In this sci-fi game, Meritxell is torn between solidifying the possibility of having aliens in Engolasters while keeping her hands with her breaking family. As she explores the areas of Engolasters Lake, she will also encounter ancient witchcraft, potential alchemy, and other oddities that could explain the supernatural. The game is similar to survival modes with items under scarcity. Time-constrained equipment that could be repowered once you get the suitable materials—added another tension to Meritxell’s decision-making process.The game is bugged, so I had to rely on gameplay available on the in-game community via Steam, and it's an exciting watch. Integrating ancient technology with the futuristic cyberpunk atmosphere creates a deep contrast between the freelancer’s intent of unveiling mysteries—and the thrill of scheming via futuristic manipulation methods such as voice changing, quick information hacking, and more. Like Supercontinent Ltd, I had to watch the gameplay via YouTube since the keyboard binding wasn’t working as intended. Brandeis, the assistant, provides Akara with several client profiles from people from different walks of life. Depending on what Akara molds, the client’s response will also vary. They could be the human molded to do the “greater good,” or the pottery vessels would ignite their humanistic desires to take on what they believed was predetermined to their path. After the dazed hangover, these underground miners realized that they had to create their spaceship back to Earth using the minerals available from the undergrounds of Urult. As a Metroidvania game lover, seeing Underground Hangovers on the list is interesting. While the premise is silly, the actual gameplay is tricky—analogous to Super Mario and Castlevania’s setting.- FATAL ERROR, Eternal Home Floristry. This occurs whenever I add more than five leaves of the same variety. - CONTROL BUG, Zen and the Art of Transhumanism. I tried restarting, but I cannot operate the machine—which is a total bummer because I’ve wanted to try making pots.- ROAD GLITCH, Engolasters January 2021. It's hard to navigate the car because it gets randomly stuck in areas despite no barricades to hinder driving.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't say enough positive things about this collection. The games themselves, although short, are jam packed with emotion and show how Deconstructeam has evolved their game design over the years. Each game is unique and deal with a variety of difficult themes, some which may hit harder than others depending on your own life experiences. They play on your emotions, but in a tactful way, rooted in reality rather than skirting the issue, which creates an incredibly impactful experience, particularly if you have dealt with similar issues.One of my favorite things about this collection are the mini documentary style videos attached to each game that explain their game design philosophy and creative process. The Deconstructeam devs seem like wonderful people and I'm truly  glad to hear how Devolver has been so supportive of them through some rough times. Really looking forward to their next big project, whenever that may be, I'll be here for it.

It's barely even playable, there are no settings, so the blaringly loud sound was only adjustable through the windows sound mixer, the controls were very finnicky (In Zen and the Art of Transhumanism sometimes the controller input just didn't work at all)This can barely be called game and i don't understand why someone would bent themselves backwards just to be able to "play" this any longer than a few minutes.I really tried to work to get anything done here, but it's severely not worth my time.Writing this negative review was a more user friendly experience than what i have seen from this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Essays on Empathy

_childDocuments_.review: An incredibly powerful set of short narrative experiences with accompanying interviews discussing the nuances of narrative development, being LGBTQ in the Spanish game development scene, crunch, inspiration, and a whole range of topics important to the Deconstructeam. Standout games for me are Behind Every Great One, 11:45: A Vivid Life, Eternal Home Floristry, and De Tres Al Cuarto - all of them explore the collection's central concept of empathy in unique and often deeply effecting ways. BEGO and DTAC incredibly elegantly balance their game mechanics (BEGO inspired by a Ludum Dare about running out of space, and DTAC being an example of the now ubiquitous deckbuilder genre) with a closely observed characterisation which shines in its small, apparently insignificant, nuances. EHF, with the story of a mob hitman in hiding at its core, is less immediately relatable, but building the story around the process of crafting flower arrangements brings an emphasis on craft and materiality to the digital, procedural medium of digital games, which supremely elevates the experience, and is a concept Deconstructeam also explores in The Red Strings Club.11:45 A Vivid Life is the strongest game in the collection, for similar reasons. The narrative evolving out of the process of brutal self-examination works as an incredibly powerful metaphor for any number of mental health issues and traumas, and really highlights the degree to which a single, very well-written, mechanic can lead to an incredibly powerful narrative experience.Two of the games here, Zen and the Art of Transhumanism and Supercontinent Ltd, are prototypes for episodes in Deconstructeam's earlier masterpiece, The Red Strings Club - while it is interesting to consider the ways these both evolved into their equivalents in RSC, they are both woven so wonderfully into that game's larger narrative, that they have somewhat less impact here taken in isolation - I'd recommend picking up RSC immediately if either look interesting to you.
_childDocuments_.name: Essays on Empathy

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible. I wholeheartedly recommend this release. If you enjoyed The Red Strings Club, you will definitely love these as well.They're so much more than just games (maybe apart from Underground Hangovers, it's the odd one out), they depict real, relevant issues, the characters feel so genuine and relatable; and the graphics together with the music and the sound design work together perfectly with the narratives.Quoting the developers in reference to their style in one of the notes, you can expect "thought provoking concepts and stimulating questions and decisions".I have played four of the games so far, and had an amazing time with each one of them. The devs also went out of their way to include a video for *every single game* sharing their thoughts about the creative process and so much more (even their own personal growth), AND you get the KILLER soundtrack (16 tracks) as part of the release too. I will update this review after I've played through all of it, but really, get this anthology, and tell your friends, cause it deserves to be known and appreciated. It's definitely not for everyone, but there is so much valuable content in there, if you are open for it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is such an amazing set up for a collection! The insight from the developers and how convenient it is to have all these games in one screen really makes it worth the purchase, but sadly not for the complete price listed. Coupled with the fact that most of these are Ludum Dares and Game Jam games that are all listed for free on itch.io (Even De Tres al Cuarto can be downloaded for free and it was supposedly made specifically for the collection.), some of these games have gamebreaking glitches and just some very unneeded mechanics. While this is only a problem for the first 4 games (last 6 are probably the ones you're gonna enjoy the most anyways lmao), it's still a very prominent issue. I can respect keeping the games the same to establish the growth of the dev team throughout their career, it's actually one of the best aspects of the collection! But Super Continent LTD. wouldn't be any less fun if it didn't have that glitch that literally traps you in the call menu, and it definitely wouldn't have suffered from having that phone number on the wall made readable. I'd also like to make it clear that you have no option to save in games  (which didn't really give me that much of an issue except while playing Underground Hangovers) or in the documentaries (which did give me an issue multiple times). Overall, I do wholly recommend it! It's an amazing experience and kept me busy for quite a while. But maybe with a few dollars knocked off the price. (Just a few though, because Paula's music ESPECIALLY in De Tres al Cuarto is gorgeous.)
