_childDocuments_.review: Essays On Empathy is a collection of 10 short experimental narrative-based Game Jam games, Each has a short commentary video from the three developers, along with some concept art and the banging soundtrack as external .mp3s. If you are interested in game development or using games as a means to tell stories about human experiences or relationships, then you absolutely need to play this now, because it's honestly phenomonal. It's not perfect, and not every game I personally enjoyed, but the occasional clunkiness is part of its charm - because this is more about experimentation. There's also a ron of really great diversity and representation through out, which I loved a lotTo give an individual short review of each game: The first game on the list and as the devs mention, this is a demo from before they shifted towards more narrative games. It's a platformer, a bit clunky and it can softlock but I beg players not to judge this collection on this one alone  A detective style game about trying to find information by looking through phone numbers. Searching the environment for clues is a lot of fun. I don't have a whole lot to say on this one but it's super good and feels very fleshed out - will definitely leave you wanting a full game based on it! A life sim about being stuck in an abusive relationship and the emotional strains that come with it. You have tasks to do around the house, or you can relax, but not enough time to do them. At the end of the day, your partner will passive aggressively comment on what you missed and try to coerce you into sex. This one is incredibly tough to get through, it's not fun per say but overall, it was my favourite - even though I played through most of it in tears. It really hit home, especially since there's a lot of stuff I've been told personally This one involves a hitman hiding out in a florist shop and creating boques, with your choices slightly affecting the outcome. A really great premise that's excecuted very very well and will absolutely leave you wanting more A really short game about visiting a bookshop to find a book to buy your father as a birthday present. Gameplay involves looking at book covers and reading the reviews or quotes. The gameplay is extremely simple and the game is very short but this was another favourite of mine. It really gets you thinking and provides a great atmosphere  This one didn't click with me but I definitely plan to revisit it at some point! I don't want to judge this one too harshly but I personally didn't get it, since there's not many instructrions on what to do and you can accidentally get in a situation where you're spending 5-10 minutes walking across an empty map. Again, maybe I'll revisit this one again some day since I think my issues were more on me than the game itself This is a game about a girl who thinks her skeleton is not her own and digs through her own body to find the truth. There's hints of memories of a previous life, alien lifeforms and processing your personal childhood trauma. The body harm, such as eye and teeth removal, made me a bit squimish but a fantastic concept none the less I don't know how to describe this one but it's a fantastic little horror game. You are Coppersmith and you go through a town demanding human sacrifice, but the method is up to you. It's grim and the soundtrack is absolutely fantastic. The only fault of this one is that it's short and unclear when the game is over  This is a game created exlusively for this collection and it shows, lasting about an hour to play through. It's as deck building game about two comedians and using those cards to make sure your stage show doesn't burn. After the show, you explore the relationship between the two characters. I wish I could explain how much I loved this one and how fantastic it was without spoiling it but man...it's so good. I love the way how as the characters talk, we're given further insight with another text box that explains their thoughts. Listen, if you aren't sold already, there's dudes ♥♥♥♥♥♥ and that's awesome
_childDocuments_.name: Essays on Empathy

_childDocuments_.review: A great collection of an array of different game ideas, all accomplished very well in every aspect.These are all story driven games (except for the oldest one) and the whole collection feels like a collection of short stories. As opposed to a novel, you get to jump into a new world with new mechanics every 30-60 minutes, but also break off the connection, you had built to characters as well as to the world you're presented. All of this is thrilling and a bit sad at the same time. Although I had played all of them, except the newest and oldest game, I couldn't just run through them in a go. It felt, like they need space to breathe and be able to resonate inside me a bit.Deconstructeam has grown to be on the very top of my list of game developers and it was also very interesting to watch the enclosed intervews and see them elaborate on the creative stages they've passed in order to develop their tone and style, which I personally find very unique.My favourites are Dear Substance of Kin and Behind Every Great One, closely followed by the standout game of this eddition - De Tres al Cuarto, which by the way has probably longest play time.
_childDocuments_.name: Essays on Empathy

_childDocuments_.review: is not one game but a collection of ten rather short games. It comes with a video for each game in which the developers talk about the creation and struggles of said games and their experience developing games in general. While the pixel-graphics is phantastic and the atmosphere in most of the games terrific I still cannot recommend getting it.  First the technical reason: While all games start, most of them do so in a very tiny window. This after the menu of the game is perfectly full screen. I did only manage to enlarge two or three of those, the rest stayed small. Maybe there is a way but I did not find it.Second the gaming reason: Most of the games are games in a very abstract way. There some great ideas and mechanics there but they are not enough to make the full games. They are more like small vignettes. Neet ideas that could have been part of a larger game but are ‘sold’ as a full game.And thirdly: The politics. Every game has a content or trigger warning listing the potential “problematic” aspects. And most for most of them are, well, the content is more than mild. While I see a sense in some warnings for example if there is talk or depiction of suicide - since there is solid data that this can “inspire” people – I believe you should treat people like adults. Also, a several of the stories center around elements, themes and aspects of ‘social justice’. While this can be interesting and fine, here also – at least for my taste – it was to on the nose and like the game mechanics was not great to carry the story.  While I did not watch all the videos actively, I heard in one that the developers do not see these things as politics but simply their identity. Which is their right and does not diminish their work, but while I do not have an issue with having thought provoking elements and turns in game, I do not so much like it if I am under the impression the game is preaching to me. And that was the impression I got…

_childDocuments_.review: The game that caught my attention and made me buy Essays on Empathy is Behind Every Great One.Initially I thought that each game would be along the same lines as Behind Every Great One, only changing the setting and characters, but I was surprised to see a variety in game genres, design and gameplay.Of course, due to the time limitation imposed by game jams, you shouldn't expect games with a completed and enjoyable  gameplay. _childDocuments_.review: A great collection and examination into video games that feels like much more than the sum of its parts. The two individual games that impressed me most were 'Behind Every Great One' and 'De Tres Al Cuarto', but every game had combined innovative video game concepts with complex emotional storytelling in some way (even if not every result was 'fun' in the traditional sense). The galleries and videos were quite valuable and have secured this team as one I will always want to go back to.Those interested in the artistry in the creation of games and the types of stories they can tell shouldn't hesitate to give this a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely recommend it. I think it should be approached more as a documentary / retrospective on Deconstructeam's work and the genesis of their identity as developers through those works, rather then a series of games. Well, that would be the case if some of the titles in there weren't so powerful and gut wrenching. With Essays on Empathy I got to experience more of Deconstructeam's unique and visceral game design of introspection and empathy, but in different flavours from what I was used to. Some of those will stick with me for a long time. As I'm writing this, I only played 6 out of the 10 games, but I can already say it's worth it. Behind Every Great One and 11.45 A Vivid Life are really memorable. Also, as a gamedev, it made me want to do more small projects, to experiment more. Essays on Empathy is not only valuable to me as a player, but also as a designer.Edit: I also absolutely love Eternal Home Floristry. And some of the comments Deconstructeam makes about the process of making games were really touching and made a lot sense for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Essays on Empathy

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, what a journey! A compilation of short, contemplative games that showcase the evolution of Deconstructeam over the years. While, yes, I did immensely enjoy pretty much all of the games (those monkeys in Underground Hangovers will never let me see to the end of it...), the real highlight was the documentary starring the trio behind Deconstructeam, Paula, Marina, and Jordi! Their philosophy behind game-making is fascinating to learn about, especially as we watch the growth from game to game. I love the exploration between different concepts in each game, a lot of which were very satisfying to mess around with and leave room for replayability. My biggest gripes would be the inability to fullscreen most of the games and not being able to go backwards or forwards in any of the documentary videos (which, granted, the latter is fairly common for in-game cutscenes)With this being my introduction to Deconstructeam's work, I'm excited to see how these concepts are applied in a more polished environment like their full-scale games, which I know I will absolutely be checking out!!
_childDocuments_.name: Essays on Empathy

_childDocuments_.review: It would be easy to look at  as a collection of games all delivered to you at a cheap, reasonable price in a nicely packaged bundle. What this  is is a wonderful interactive documentary from an indie studio about the nonlinear process of game development where the interactive element is getting to play all these games they made along the way. All of the games provided in this collection are beautiful, even if some of the themes and topics they focus on are not. It is a testament to the talent of these artists, which is what they all are. Rarely, even with indie studios, do we as players get to see a face behind the works and hear their thoughts on the games they make. In scanning through all of the neatly bundled behind the scenes artbooks and in watching the mini documentaries, you can get a real commentary not just on how each game was made, but how it influenced the next game or some other title from the studio. Most importantly, though, these videos and these games offered a window into what these games meant to these developers through the ever changing, nonlinear act of creation.These insights are really fascinating, but from a purely entertainment, gameplay perspective, there is a lot on offer in each of these games. The "final" game, if you're moving across the collection from the left to the right, is exclusive to this bundle. The rest have seen releases previously as part of various "game jam" type events or as side projects or stepping stones in making other titles. They all play differently, but there are certainly some shared themes. I liken the experience of going through all of these to evolution. It is not a linear process. Some things branch off and go nowhere, even if it was a really successful design. Other things, things you might not expect to be successful, take flight and become the foundation to entire new branches on the tree. Notably, I haven't described the actual gameplay much, but I do really feel that is something for you to experience on your own. There are warnings provided whenever a game does touch on a sensitive topic, so you shouldn't be taken off guard. There was one game in this collection that really got to me,  and it is arguably one of the most simple out of all the games, gameplay-wise. Its presentation actually really benefited the story it was telling, I would argue.All in all, I do very much believe this is a collection worth your while whether you're an established fan of this studio or not; and, if you are anyone who has any interest in game development either as a personal passion or curiosity regarding how things actually work, then I'm sure you will get a lot out of this collection as well. Getting this on sale and/or as part of a bundle is always going to be the best way to go from a consumer perspective, but $12.99 is a really good, fair price to me.
_childDocuments_.name: Essays on Empathy

_childDocuments_.review: Truly such a beautiful collection of game. I've loved all the games I've played from Deconstructeam and as a still growing young gamedev it was really cool to see the concepts + reflection videos on each of these games! Would definitely recommend this to people who love narrative based games that experiment with how mechanics can work for them. Also would definitely look at the trigger warnings before playing each game because these games *do* get dark.
_childDocuments_.name: Essays on Empathy

_childDocuments_.review: Pros -Games are generally short with generally diverse stories so for the most part it's really fun to discover what each story is gonna be about.-The music never fails.-Features documentaries where the developers describe their developing processes, inspiration, and struggles.Cons-they desperately needed a proofreader, there aren't just typos but also common mistakes with indirect questions for example, if you're a grammar nazi like me this can get a bit annoying :D-documentaries were fun but some were a bit too long and I personally wasn't interested in all of the things they said. I get they were optional but I wish we had an option to fast forward/skip a bit.-speaking of fast-forwarding/skipping, in some of the game jams there were repetitive scenes (especially in De Tres Al Cuatro) and you just have to wait for the words in each dialogue line to be typed before you move on, I wish they'd made that easier to navigate, as in have the whole dialogue line typed/showed in one-go rather than wait for each letter to be typed.Now for the games themselves,Underground Hangovers - I didn't really play this one, I tried but the mechanics were very fuzzy and un-intuitive to the point it was frustrating.Supercontinent Ltd - pretty fun though the final puzzle could have used some polishing so don't worry if you can't figure it out perfectly.Behind Every Great One - interesting attempt at showcasing emotional abuse, anxiety, etc. Eternal Home Floristry - poetic, creative, and uniqueThe Bookshelf Limbo - interesting and chill, not a lot happeningZen and the Art of Transhumanism - a chapter of The Red Strings ClubEngolasters - the premise is interesting as you play as an ufologist who has very limited time till they die to get some things done11.45 A Vivid Life - the highlight here is that you have multiple choices and  you get different endingsDear Substance of Kin - by far my personal favorite and maybe also my favorite of all the games I've played by Deconstructeam. It's basically a Grimm fairytale but in their own style, it's poetic, macabre, and metaphorical. Also multiple choices to choose from and the music is top-notch for this particular atmosphere.De tres al cuarto - interesting mechanics for playing comedy-punchline cards to get points, coupled with a unique storytelling way that shows the characters' relationship and feelings.Bottom line, I recommend this for fans of Deconstructeam or fans of short stories that usually employ poetic storytelling amd/or one-of-a-kind premises.
_childDocuments_.name: Essays on Empathy

_childDocuments_.review: A collection of Deconstructeam short games, mainly narrative driven but with some tool mechanics, platforming and RPG elements. Behind Every Great One, about a destructive relationship, and De Tres al Cuarto, a deck based game about an unsuccessful but loving comedy duo performing and chilling in between gigs on a tropical island, stands out to me. This collection includes seperate interview videos about each game, as well as concept art & music tracks. If you're a fan on The Red Strings Club I recommend it, partly to see where some of the ideas evolved from. The games are all fairly different and so you will likely find something to your liking, if you like mood, artistic value, great story telling, and is openminded.

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't played through all of the games in this bundle yet and may update my review once i did, but I really can recommend buying Essays On Empaythy if you want to play a collection of weird, unconventional stories that deal with equally weird and complicated people. I only played three of the games yet, but each of them is incredibly unique both in game mechanics and in telling a story that really makes you care about the characters. I especially liked De Tres Al Cuarto, the latest game in the collection just for the absolutely crazy premise of a standup-comedy deck building game about a gay standup duo. The games have such a weird, lovely charm to them and I really love their honesty and the willingness to portray human conections as messy and far from the clean-cut sterotypes you often see on tv. Most of the games are game jam games, so I really cannot be mad about encountering bugs or having some jank in the games, but be aware that you sometimes might have to re-start a game, but since most of them aren't super long, it's not really that bad, and I personally really didn't mind. I really don't want to go into too much detail about the collection, but I think less than 12 € is complete fair to pay for these, specifically since these are fun enough that you already have you money's worth if you liked 2-3 of them. I also really liked the more conceptual approach these games have to them - there's an interesting mechanic that could be explored further and it's very inspiring to play through these titles and see what the developers came up with.I'd say, if you are looking for one longer, polished expierience, this may not be the game you are looking for and even if you do, you may not like every game in the bundle, but if you are interested in playing through some short games with a focus on interpersonal narratives, I can really recommend you check it out!
_childDocuments_.name: Essays on Empathy

_childDocuments_.review: I'm glad I bought this, what a nice discovery! Didn't realise they were the people behind The Red Strings Club (which I loved), and now I just appreciate them more. The games themselves are very interesting and presented in a nice format, but they really get all their flavor and depth when you watch the interviews and understand the reasons behind design decisions and the people taking those decisions. It has been a true pleasure to follow their thought and creative process, which are very inspiring for my own work and anyone leading a creative life in this sad world. Their struggles and realisations are meaningful, and I can't say if I enjoyed the games or the videos more. And this comes from someone who never, ever watches or listens to any dev commentary.I hope the path to the release of Deconstructeam's next big game stays free of major obstacles, and I will be at the front of the line to buy it. Thank you for your dedication to creating meaningful interactive works of art. You folks are amazing and inspiring!
_childDocuments_.name: Essays on Empathy

_childDocuments_.review: A really cool set of Itch.io-esque games dealing with subjects from standup comedy to the abusive relationship of a spouse to an egotistical creator. But more than that, the documentary for each game in this collection is SUCH a cool and beautiful insight into three creators and human beings. If you're interested in the insight behind games and want some context on some really interesting works, this is a recommendation. (I wish I'd known about how cool pairing a documentary short with each of these games was before I picked it up.)Keep up the awesome work - I hadn't heard of the other two bigger Devolver-published games Deconstructeam has made, but I'm super interested now and will be picking those up! The sound design is great, the art is great, and the game design is interesting - I really liked The Hidden & The Unknown, interesting to connect the dots that it was Disco Elysium-inspired. Also, it's interesting to hear the perspectives of creators for whom English is not the first language. I obviously love that these games get made in the language I speak, but to Jordi's point about fears of expression - while I can't erase the frustration of being forever at a remove from the language and thus more prone to make cultural 'errors', y'all express yourself quite well and were plenty entertaining to watch!
_childDocuments_.name: Essays on Empathy

_childDocuments_.review: Essays on empathy is a series of small game experiences that flood your senses with incredible art direction, atmosphere, music and distilled curiosities. It also comes with hours of music and well-put-together interviews documenting the thoughts behind the development of each title.This is not something I would recommend to most people, but if you view games as an art form, there are very few purchases you can make that will satisfy your need to explore the minds of game developers quite like this. It comes highly recommended for those interested in game development on any level and if you pick it up, be sure to try "dear substance of kin" which is my favorite game jam game of all time.
_childDocuments_.name: Essays on Empathy

_childDocuments_.review: This collection is the reason why I love indie games so much and tend to get as much as I can.Having a game collection like that with videos explaining the process and the intend of the game was a real enjoyment for me and I wish more games or collection would do something like that.The games were very unique in styles and story and were a total blast to play through them all and experiencing so many different emotions in them all.I will surely look closely to their upcoming games.Good job on this collection and I really hope more peoples will get to enjoy the process of Indie Development.
_childDocuments_.name: Essays on Empathy

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic little journey to go through. I love their games, and this just made me appreciate them all a lot more. Long story short, this is a collection of a lot of their smaller, free games (as well as one larger game exclusive to this) with added optional commentary and concept art if you're interested. The games themselves are worth the purchase, but if you've ever wanted to see the devs' perspectives on their creative process, I'd suggest giving the videos a watch as well. It's incredible to me how such a small teamhas been capable of making some of my favorite games, everything from the art, writing, and music is just astounding on them. I'm glad I purchased this collection, it's given me an even greater appreciation for the games I love from them, and I cannot wait for more to come from them!
_childDocuments_.name: Essays on Empathy

_childDocuments_.review: its amazing how every game from these guys bring me to tears I LOVE THE DIALOGUES AND THE CHARACTERS ITS ALL SO PERFECT AND THE GRAPHICS i love you deconstructeam i love you (except that i hate you for destroying me like that w eternal home floristry, i swear)i really absolutely ADORE every chosen themes and discussions they bring, and this is one of my fav game studios of all time & a huge inspirationstill havent played all the collection [my favs so far are eternal home, de tres al cuarto & behind every great one (OH BOY WAS THIS ONE HARD TO PLAY)] but i love it all already so uhhhh cmon if you're still unsure just give this game a try

_childDocuments_.review: 'Essays on empathy' attracted me just with its title. Those mini-games are different perpectives from reality to fiction with a lot of emotions to deal with. I love this concept and the way it is done. Everything is on edge. I need to do the first two games from this studio 'The Red Strings Club', and ' Gods Will Be Watching' ! _childDocuments_.name: Essays on Empathy

_childDocuments_.review: Essays on Empathy is a game developed by Deconstructeam and published by Devolver DigitalAlthough nothing to write home about, it's an interesting set of games created by Deconstructeam for Ludum Dare and equally interesting is the behind-the-scenes of how each game was createdEssays of Empathy is a cute collection of games and for the cheap-ish price it offers, it's an interesting collection of little games to play
_childDocuments_.name: Essays on Empathy

_childDocuments_.review: It's a nice mix of games that were made available on itch.io by the team, a first game which I believe was never released and a new one, "De Tres al Cuarto"; all glued together with original art galleries and short documentaries talking about their creative process. I loved playing the games, thinking about how they made me feel and then going through the video to see if I got what they were trying to express.Because that's what this collection is about: feeling. And you have many different moods to explore: anxiousness, creepy, plain weird, despair, love, freedom...If I have to pick, I just love "Behind Every Great One". It just felt so true to me. So powerful.And about "De Tres al Cuarto", I loved the theme and the mechanics (I'm a fan of deck building games), and I think they really combined them perfectly on this last game. Also, sound and music got to a new higher level on this one. And what did the game make me feel? That not being successful is not such a big deal, if you have fun while trying. And that's something that all this studio's games expect the player to realise: that it can be fun just to play and experience and not caring about if you are actually winning or loosing the game. Just... enjoy the trip.
_childDocuments_.name: Essays on Empathy

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great compilation. The games are small, but just in scope or length, because all of them are games of high quality, and the themes and thoughts they talk abut in them are very interesting and profound. But also the documentaries about their creative process are very inspiring. If you have a creative spirit, you like games with meaning or just enjoy listening and playing stuff of very creative people I strongly reccomend this compilation.
_childDocuments_.name: Essays on Empathy

_childDocuments_.review: A curated compilation of Deconstructeam's best efforts in seeking new narrative experiences in games. Explore 10 unique, offbeat tales including "De Tres al Cuarto," a brand new short experience exclusive to the compilation about a couple of two-bit comedians trying to make it big.

name: Blood West
detailed_description: Weird West legends meet eldritch horror in BLOOD WEST , an immersive stealth FPS. Become the Undead Gunslinger, doomed to roam the barren lands until he finds the means to purge their curse and free his soul. No, this isn’t your typical Wild West desperado redemption arc. This is a damnation arc. The Canyons, the Swamp, and the Mountains. Each swarming with abominable monsters and unholy demons, these are open-ended worlds for you to explore freely at your own pace. It will take the player over 20 hours on average to complete all three scenarios, and over 35 if they want to see everything the barren lands have to offer. Blood West is a stealth FPS inspired by the genre classics such as the Thief series (whose fans will be happy to hear the voice of Stephen Russell, the actor voicing the master-thief Garrett, returning here as the protagonist), S.T.A.L.K.E.R. games, or - from the contemporary catalog - Hunt: Showdown. The gameplay rewards the careful approach: scouting the area, stalking your enemies, and striking from the shadows. Can you figure out a way to clear a fort full of ghouls and monsters without raising an alarm? The Barren Lands present the player with a nightmarish, twisted vision of the Wild West legends. The curse that has befallen the realm has corrupted every living thing, defiled the land itself, while summoning restless spirits and dark entities. In this mixture of gunslinger pulp and Lovecraftian horror, dark occult magick presents just as much of a threat as sudden lead poisoning. In Blood West you will meet many colorful, yet strangely twisted, fully-voiced NPCs. Just as much prisoners of the Barren Lands as you are, they will sometimes share their unusual stories and send you on various missions. Play nice and they might reward you or become your allies. Cross them and risk their wrath. The game won’t hold your hand. You’ll have to explore the land for yourself (buying a map from a vendor might prove useful!), and figure out your own way to approach quests. As you poke around the three expansive maps, keep an eye out for hidden places and secret stashes. There’s gold in the mountains! Fair warning - it’s probably cursed. If sneaking around isn’t exactly your thing, or you feel that you have a power advantage over your enemies, you can always take the head-on approach and meet your enemies guns blazing. Blood West comes from the creators of the fan-favorite boomer shooter POSTAL: Brain Damaged , so much gratuitous fantasy violence and pixelated blood splatter is to be expected! One man’s hell might be another hoarder’s paradise! From simple one-use items like bandages, through medical tinctures, explosives and incendiaries, straight to arcane artifacts that - once slotted - can change the way you play the game, the Barren Lands are just filled with STUFF. There are tons of useful items to discover, and there’s a special player’s stash crate for all those super-rare potions that you’ll hoard and never use. A gunslinger without a gun would be just a regular slinger. Where’s the fun in that? Blood West makes sure you’ll have plenty of weapons to choose from. Revolvers, rifles, shotguns, carabines - a great variety of firearms, from standard army-issue to those infused with powerful magic, or straight-up possessed. And if you prefer not to cause a ruckus, there’s a wide selection of hand-to-hand combat weapons and archery weapons to pick your favorites from. The RPG-like perk-based progression system in Blood West will allow you to highly customize the gameplay experience to your liking. Become a stealthy hunter, a revolver-fanning gunman or a relentless berserker. You will gain experience and progress through the skill tree, while discovering new artifacts in each of the scenarios that will bestow on you additional abilities. Combining skills and load-out creates more possible playstyles than you’d normally be able to explore in one playthrough. Are you ready to take back the frontier from the dark forces of demonic corruption and earn the right to move on to a better world? The Barren Lands call you, Gunslinger!

_childDocuments_.review: So I'm gonna describe what Blood West feels like for me. Here goes, Blood West feels like the old school Turok games on the N64, that is what this game brings me back to, with stealth mechanics, western themed and challenging game play. It doesn't force you to do the story right away; the moment you complete what is the tutorial level they let you go where you want. I am excited for the future of it and even now I think it is a must play.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great if you like carrying a big iron on your hip. or screaming ITS HIGH NOON SOMEWHERE IN THE WORLD at the top of your lungs. or a game like thief that needs a little more finesse and thought on your actions than most modern games demand. add to that a lot of undead blood gore and a character who respectfully nods to my man Caleb and you have something really good. the feel of the gunfights of running for cover or counting the enemy shots to take a safer shot yourself is amazing. i will give it 10 yeehaws out of 10 and then subtract 3 of them and hold them hostage until we get more maps weapons an things to shot/hack/stab at. I recommend this game a lotEdited: SPOILERS AHEAD.The new enemies are hot garbage. bonus points my saves just disappeared. Suddenly everyone detects you from insanely far away, enemies with long range weapons who attack in groups said long range weapon is a winchester with 15 bullets and 3 put you in a shallow grave 2 guys shoot you you wake up dead and cursed. (i had the perk to dodge ranged and the ectoplasm relic still was reliably 3 shoot every time 12 times in a row)  everything else bleeds you super hard and is not alone and the map design is not suitable for such enemies no cover when ♥♥♥♥ hit the fan and it hits it way too fast. the leech trowing midgets are the worse shoot one 3 times with silver bullets from my orb of night in the face to no effect, got leeched to death by his 5 other friends for my trouble. The new items are way too expensive to the point i had to use a save before fighting the first boss just to farm money to test at least one of the new weapons just to use it 5 minutes and have my saves erased.... Over all the new map has been thoroughly disappointing and frustrating.

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game, reminded me of fallout a bunch with all the constant looting of dead bodies and scavenging for supplies to survive. as long as you are patient the game isn't too hard. just save up ammo and go for headshots :) I was playing through a chapter at a time per session so it is very addictive. took me 16 hours to beat the entire thing so it's a very long game. Thumbs up!

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game! Played it way longer than required b/c it was such a blast. Tons of heart and soul clearly went into this game and it shows. Core gameplay loop is very solid. Great art and enemy design. Excellent use of pixel type graphics.For fans of any and all of the following:stealth, fps, slightly difficult game, different combat styles, inventory management, light RPG level-up skill tree, inventory management.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't recommend this game in it's current state.Clocking in at around 4 hours for full 100% of the content currently available I went through several different phases of enjoyment during my playtime.Phase 1: Challenge (the first hour)At first I found myself enjoying the challenge, it felt like if I didn't get the sneak attack head shot on enemies then I was in for a rough time. I found myself scrounging for ammo and picking my fights a little more carefully, I felt poor constantly.Phase 2: Equality (2nd and 3rd hour)I picked up a few perks and by about level 3 I felt like I was on equal footing with the enemies, I had a steady stream of ammunition and felt like i had learned how to use ADS effectively so that even if I whiffed a shot, I felt comfortable landing the follow up hits, I was starting to pile up my gold and my storage was starting to fill.Phase 3: Overpowered and bored (3rd and final hour)it was when I hit either level 4 or 5 that I realised how limited the skill tree was for ranged characters, I hypothesised that you could make an overpowered ranged character by level 3 by just picking the right perks (Slow down time, ammo on kill, and no drop off dmg for headshots being the major ones). I started to tire of exploration, realising that the only real benefit of exploring was to get experience, but then what would I do with the skill points that are awarded to me? It dawned on me how "casual" the stealth system is, with enemies 5 feet away not hearing me shotgun blast another enemy in the face. Once I had the unique revolver, the game just got far too easy. I felt like the reward you get for finding all the cursed gold items was not substantial enough for collecting them all.I've not played as a melee character and assume it would provide quite the challenge as there are no damage resistance perks and limited healing items, and that you would have to rely on sneak attack as well as hit and run tactics to get by (or using the bone knife).Misc issues:There are quite a few grammar and spelling issues scattered throughout the game.For a "horror" game (check game description), there is a real lack of scares, I would have appreciated a jump scare or 2 to break the monotony of head shotting every zombie on the horizon.I did enjoy 3/4 of the time I spent with this game, and I hope that the developers work on and improve the issues that I've personally had with the game, as I would hate to go from "episode 1" to "episode 2" with an overpowered character that I feel isn't worth the time exploring and investing in to skill progression.//Post Chapter 2 and full release//Chapter 2 (at time of release):I don't really remember much of my time in chapter 2 as I played it at release during early access, I enjoyed the exploration but felt it was very much more of the same head shotting every enemy in sight.My only real issue I remember is that the final boss is some kind of puzzle boss, which constantly regenerating health, and I being dumb skipped through the dialogue before the boss in which how to deal with the boss is (I assume) explained. As I was playing it at time of release, there weren't any updated guides, so i ended up cheesing the boss with the bow that scales with health lost, and out damaged the regen. At the time there was no way to ask npcs to repeat anything about the boss, I'm unsure if that has been changed.Chapter 3.Chapter 3 was the most challenging part of the game for me, I died a lot more than I would've liked, not a fan of the invisible enemies or the large bear enemiesThe final boss another source of frustration, in my original review I said that playing a melee character would be a challenge, well I have no idea how you would deal with the boss as it flies around the arena and deals constant damage when landed.In terms of a ranged character, I once again took advantage of the bow that scales damage with lost health, but this brings up another frustration with the game, merchants only restock items on death, so in order to stock up on arrows, ammo and consumables to defeat the final boss, I had to repeatedly kill myself, this combined with the soul flaw mechanic (debuffs on death) would have caused even more annoyance, but every few deaths the merchant would restock on the cure for said debuffs, and considering I had 10k gold by then, it just became an annoying time sink.I have changed my review from not recommended to recommended as I did enjoy a lot of the skulking around, exploration and scavenging. Fans of more "hardcore" games will likely enjoy their time spent here, but more casual gamers might find frustration.

_childDocuments_.review: How sneaky! Developer Hyperstrange snuck out Blood West on December 5th of last year to rave reviews, meaning I'd have something else I needed to try before settling on my favorite games of the year. I thought the setting of the game was cool, and liked the similar setting of 2015's  (which I'm currently playing) and 2022's . It seems like the "[adjective] West" genre is going strong. I also liked the game's graphical style, which reminded me of games like LucasArts' . I have some solid nostalgia for 90s FPS graphics.I liked exploring the world well enough, buying and finding new equipment/items and further tailoring my character with perks and skills. It  satisfying to sneak up behind some fleshy ghoul and blast him in the back of the head with my pistol. It also "hit the spot" to sneak attack some beastly monstrosity with my axe and see the special animation and massive damage that resulted.But unfortunately, much like Steam user  (who wrote Steam's currently featured most helpful review), I don't feel like this stealth system is very good. Steam users have been brutal to her, giving her seven "jester" awards (which typically means that the user thinks your opinion makes you a clown rather than thinking your writing is funny). They've called her problems with the game "skill issues," as though someone who's played and beaten , , , , , and  (I went and took a look at her profile) is turned off by a little difficulty. However, I have to admit that there are multiple schools of thought when it comes to stealth. Some players prefer hyper-realistic stealth - games like  and PS2-era  games, and those are likely to be the players that enjoy  the most. However, there are other stealth enthusiasts (like myself) who, although they don't mind difficulty, prefer to be given as much information as possible. Some of my favorite stealth games include , , , , , the XBOX 360-era  games, and the 2011 & 2016  games.  gives you much less clear information than any of the games I mentioned, in terms of enemy sightlines and noise made by the player and their distractions. I spent too much time just crouching and staring at monsters.Once you're detected it can be difficult to hit enemies, as a lot of your weapons (at least in the time that I played) are quite slow to swing, fire, or reload. If an enemy reaches you and gets a few hits in, your character will take a tremendous amount of damage. I made progress slowly but surely as I played, even killing a Wendigo, but I had to return back to the safe havens more often than I would've preferred. If the stealth system gave the player more information  if the game had manual saving (or even checkpointing of some sort), I might've continued. But eventually, I just got tired of playing and decided to do something that was less tedious and more fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Hell yeah, this scratches my weird west itches. The pixel style is cool and clever. The curvy monsters and NPCs are amazing to gander at, and finding your groove and playstyle is fun to do. Can be a super ninja or a clever gunfighter. Make it yours. The unique weapons are fun, cool, and can change how you fight. Which makes finidng your favorite weapons a fun puzzle to fit together.
_childDocuments_.name: Blood West

_childDocuments_.review: I'm so done with this game. The theme was interesting at first, I liked sneak killing with an axe and a bow in the first chapter (which turned all to naught in the next chapter, when you have to have somehow better gear right of the bat to deal with these abominations); yet the gunplay is atrocious—for those that want to aim with precision in order to line those perfect headshots to no effect. When you aim at the head and shoot at it, it makes no contact. Even when you get a chance at hitting a basic enemy in the head from the right distance, it won't kill it. Well... at least Witchfire respects aiming.When I'm out of sight, or more accurately: out of line of sight, enemies can still see me (almost like they have eyes on their left and right sides also), which started to vex me greatly. And they can somehow see me when I'm at a considerable distance.No way to manually save to experiment with things. Which makes it impossible to reload a previous save when you made a mistake by accident.And since experimentation is not allowed, there is no point even using those tomahawks. Because there is no arc when throwing those, and you have no way of knowing where it lands before you throw it.Also: no way to stack health potions. Begs the question: how is it then possible to stack bandages? Anyway. Made it frustrating to get back to the camp and restock when I happened to use one.There seems to be a clear disconnect between the Gunslinger character's voicelines and dialog options. Mainly when you first come across Anabelle—or Annabelle, whatever (Ivy Wilde:  if you know you know). Oh, right! I'm fairly certain - indicated by the previous cutscene, that he would be by that time just tired of it all. Either let him be the grim type of a gunslinger with no-nonsense that even death cannot stop, or in the worst case scenario: make him act so that the woman in question can easily (with no effort on her part) come on top. None of those three dialog options is even remotely what that character would say - one of them sounded so out of place that I couldn't take any of this seriously any longer, and yet none of those choices makes a difference in the long run because Anabelle answers with the same exclamation. There is a correct way uplifting a female character, but not at the cost of tearing down a male character by doing so. It would've been better if there was at first an uneasy alliance between them, with no promises from the Gunslinger whatsoever and only reluctantly helping her (and the Totem in the grand scheme of things); made apparent with dialog options, or by pure chance in his travels.If I should say one positive thing about this game, it's the eye-candy from the Prodigal Daughters (to some extent), and of course from Anabelle (to a much greater degree).
_childDocuments_.name: Blood West

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game in early release during the Steam Summer Sale and feel like I stole it.I expected a run and gun shooter, but this game is all about stealth- and it is done really well. The graphics remind me of an 90s FPS, but I have always thought gameplay is so much more important than eye candy. There isn't much variety in weapons, but what they have are really fun to master- then most of the undead become 1 shot head shots.I have played for 19 hours so far and am having a lot of fun. When I am done- I will replay.I don't know how much more the developers will work on this, it runs pretty flawless right now- but there is a lot that can be added in atmosphere, sun light, animals, and NPCs.Thanks for a great game.
_childDocuments_.name: Blood West

_childDocuments_.review: The game is good , I personally enjoy playing it so far ... buuuuut it may not be for everyone..The good : Really nice visuals , I'm a fan of games that look like Blood west very appealing to the eye , combat can be challenging but so far has been fun due to the variety of things you can do for example , my gameplay is based around stealth so far,  for anyone who likes exploring and collecting things , the maps are really nicely designed and there's a lot of places to explore (I'm at chapter 2 )The bad : Shooting is honestly a bit weird and sometimes it feels like your shots magically miss (I do know how to play fps , so yeah..) stealth all though enjoyable kinda sucky cause it's pretty much impossible to do stealth with melee when a lot of enemies are grouped together , melee-killing an enemy triggers every enemy nearby to look towards you ( the enemy you killed ).Edit : I forgot to mention inventory , can be a bit frustrating when you want to hoard items , but as our boy says , we all do have hoarding problems...My conclusion... The game is fun simple and enjoyable ,has variety for playstyles , it can be quite challenging and you can explore the cool maps to your hearts content , enemies are fun , art style is great and very appealing .Of course let's not forget about booba-shotgun-thicc-lady.Overall score would be 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly I thought this would get some updates and nothing has happened, so definitely not worth the price right now. It's just extremely basic FPS stuff with high health enemies and darker environments to make it horror. With more updates I might change my review but after a couple hours there's no point in playing further
_childDocuments_.name: Blood West

_childDocuments_.review: Blood west is good. It's not great, it's not bad, and it's not alright. It's good. The game play and stealth mechanics are great for what it's going for, the art direction is phenomenal as I'm a big fan of the 90s early 2000s 3D aesthetic, the monsters designs are inspired, and the voice acting is stellar. The first map is fairly run of the mill but the second and third map is where the game really shines in my opinion. However, the game suffers from pacing issues in several places, the first boss can be a breeze or a frustrating challenge depending on how you approach it, yet every boss after can be beaten without any thought. But most disappointingly for me, is that the story is all over the place. Spoilers after this point but the totem of souls, the thing that revives you originally, turns out to be the big bad. A character in the second chapter hints at this, but then suddenly your at the mountain top and the totem is your big bad? You kill them in three shots and it's a 'you won, but didn't win' situation. Perhaps teasing a possible sequel or maybe there wasn't any real narrative to begin with and it was shoehorned in for a conclusive ending. I'm not sure which but at that point just have an ending. Why eliminate the bosses in every chapter when they're the totems thralls? It doesn't add up. That said, Blood West is a fun, western horror immersive sim, one of my favorite genres and even if it isn't one of the best out there, the attempt alone and the effort that went into its creation are commendable and worth your time. Again, it's not a great game, it's a good game, and there's nothing wrong with that.

_childDocuments_.review: The pistol ADS feels awful. it obscures so much of my screen that I dread getting in gunfights with the birdmen who not only have a ranged attack like mine,but my pistol obscures their tiny head, before they hop after every shot they take, they without a doubt are the worst enemy to fight and their attack pattern combined with their dodge without alternating make encounters a massive pain in the ass. that aside, most everything else is fun, but the revolver and its iron sights and its scale needs work.Edit: after getting to chapter 3 and using some more weapons, I will say the problem is literally just the revolver's iron sights' tone and coloration against the already dark and drab backdrop and the enemies. it blends in too easily and makes shooting it a pain in the ass, that along with the hit box for heads on the Birdmen a tedious chore. that said, the Orb of Night revolver which is shiny and silver and not dark gunmetal grey is very easy to use contrasting the dark characters quite well. once you get other weapons the game really opens up and is mostly a good time. _childDocuments_.review: So first things first, this isn't a game where you can run around like a lunatic and kill everything right out the gate because of how clunky the aiming is and how slow the reloads are. It also, unfortunately, is not a dating sim where you use your cowboy rizz to try and pick up some amalgam waifus, so don't even bother. Once you get a feel for it, however, this game is incredibly enjoyable even if you don't get to bone the Boo Hag who asks you to find her skin for her. At a glance this game might seem like a run and gun sort of game where you just do whatever and kill by any means necessary in a bunked up world full of demons and amalgamations. You might hate this game if you try playing like that because while it is possible to play very aggressively later in the game, the game itself heavily rewards you way more with stealth based gameplay. This means sneaking around like an undead cowboy gremlin and finding the right moment to pop a head and move on. With a headshot multiplier of 5x in this game, why wouldn't you want to be stealthy and just delete heads? At some point when you've gotten more ammo, better guns, more perks, and good accessories, you can easily make the switch to a heavily aggressive build or strengthen your sneaking even further. The stealth in this game, its most powerful mechanic in your favor, is actually quite lenient and enjoyable. Because it is an open world and each chapter has its own specific layout you can really take your time with it, unlike other stealth games where you're in an enclosed space and are constantly getting caught because of how fast you can be seen. If you're within range of an enemy (the range of which depends on the perception of each type of enemy) then you'll get a bar at the bottom of the screen to indicate their alertness to you and how. An ear to signify that they hear you and eyes to warn you that someone can see you. With no time constraints or random spawns you can essentially take all the time you need to sneak around and find the optimal spot and time to take out enemies one by one while trying to not alert any others. Piece by piece you tear through the enemies and loot everything along the way until the entire area is cleared out and you move on. To balance this out, especially at the beginning, a lot of enemies can hit pretty hard and kill you really fast if you find yourself underestimating the enemy and fall asleep mid fight. This is combined with the fact that there is no natural health regeneration so you'll have to manage your health through bandages and potions until you can get an accessory that will give you health over time starting at 1 every 8 seconds. Until then you might find yourself at 80 health, mess up a singular engagement and get hit like twice, and suddenly you're less than 10 health or something. You are a glass cannon late game, and until you get the power to back it up then you are just glass in the early game. Once you do get the ball rolling and you find some unique weapons with special effects and the ammo to use them sparingly (chapter 2 will give you a TON of short ammo to make use of) then you'll start to really feel how powerful you can get in the game. One shot nearly everything in the game with the right weapons and positions, or just equip a shotgun and alert everything and introduce them to all mannerisms of buckshot. Heck with the right movement and weapon you can even go for a melee build where you just run in and wreck house or sneak around and go for a stealth bonus. If you're not a fan of stealth at all then you might hate this game for the first couple hours as you won't have the tools to do otherwise. You could in theory just kite enemies the whole time and mow them down but with the headshots counting as 5x damage, and ammo being very limited at the start, you'll find that this isn't very effective until much later, taking easily 5 to 10 times the ammo to kill one enemy. However the leniency of the stealth in this game might be more enjoyable if you just give it a chance and really take in the satisfaction of popping heads and watching the bodies drop and taking all their sick nasty loot.

If you like stealth gameplay mixed with intense gun play and deadly monsters and a well done soundscape and ambiance, give Blood West a try.

_childDocuments_.review: (JULY 2024 Review)Game can be really fun but also really aggravating so beware. Lack of a middle way review on Steam leads me to leave a negative one unfortunately. Good aspects of game:- Game exploration is great and slowly learning the map and eliminating enemies by precise head shots is fun. - Gaining and selling loot gives a satisfying feeling allowing you to upgrade to better weapons, buy ammo, buy potions to increase, health and stamina etc. amongst other things.- Upgrades to your character although underwhelming can help in shaping your build either by allowing aim down sight slow down speed, stronger melee etc. etc. You get the gist. - Enemy design is eerie and very well done as is the overall atmosphere of the game.Not so good aspects of the game:- Souls like mechanics that have no place in a stealth fps. You die you get negative traits. This is not fun for me personally, especially as you are learning the game and experimenting. These gained traits earned by death impact XP gain, melee damage, damage taken etc. its random in what you can get and to remove these traits you need to do very repetitive Simon says tasks aka stealth kill 3 monsters, head shot 4 monsters and so on. - Expanding on the souls inspired mechanics, enemies re-spawn after death, lack of loading previous saves and enemies that can just about 2 shot you. If you love these souls type mechanics great but again for me this is not fun. - Boss fights. Yep this game has boss fights. *sigh* These just feel out of place and not very well designed. At least not the 1st boss which spams you waves of enemies and also attacks you whilst you 'shoot the red glowy thingy' of the boss to kill it. Completely kills the pace of the game and again dying from the boss will net you negative traits, re-spawn enemies before you try to get back to the boss fight. Not fun. - Finally the stealth system is kinda borked. Most of the time it works fine however in certain scenarios the flaws are evident. For example, I hid behind a corner in a cavern and identified several enemies in the distance all grouped up. thought this was a good opportunity for some tnt time. I threw the tnt, still BEHIND COVER mind you and OUT OF SIGHT , and upon detonation the enemies nearby somehow knew my exact location, rather than just being on alert, and came Forrest gump running my way jamming their claws up my arse. Sounds fun? Me dont think so. To sum up.These are a quick summary of my experience and its evident that a souls like design was inspired here which is unfitting for a game like this quite frankly. Why must every game be a souls like ? It kills the experimental immersive sim elements because even if you dare to get a bit creative and die in the process, well, all the points mentioned above occur and sour the experience. You may love the game which fair enough, but still try get it on a sale. However personally I cant recommend it due to the many aggravating down sides.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, great atmosphere, great monster designs and sounds, hearing the Prodigal Daughter for the first time through a wall was horrifying and the sounds of the Human-Pedes always digusted and creeped me out an keep me on my toes the entire time even when I had a ton of ammo and could gun anything down and I can't wait for the other episodes or whatever they will be called. A couple things about it though, sneak shooting with a ranged weapon doesn't give the critical hit a sneak melee hit, so a headshot is necessary, sneak killing even with gun doesn't alert anyone to your location unless the target doesn't die, and you cannot continue the save file when you complete the game and click "Save and Exit", nothing that I would mark against the game when recommending to someone though

_childDocuments_.review: This game falsely markets itself as an immersive sim, but it's just a boring stealth game with a retro, Gothic horror Old West coat of paint slapped on. Sneak up, melee, sneak up, melee, sneak up, melee, repeat ad nauseam. The guns are all completely useless unless you manage to land a headshot, which the game actively prevents you from doing with an excessive amount of weapon sway. All these big, slow cowboy guns ought to pack some punch, but they're about as powerful as a timid fart. The enemies are brainless bullet sponges that kill you in a few hits. The controls suck, the UI sucks, everything sucks. You also get punished for dying in the form of permanent debuffs, which makes the entire experience even more frustrating and unrewarding. The only thing this game has going for it is the aesthetic, which is admittedly pretty cool. Do not waste your money on this game, no matter the sale price and no matter how many idiots gave it a positive review- seriously, is everyone on crack? Did they really just get hypnotized by the "spooky wild west" premise? Games shouldn't be able to use being cheap or having old-school graphics as an excuse for not being any good, but apparently everyone seems to give it a pass. Anyways, don't believe the hype. Words cannot express how much I hate this pile of garbage.

_childDocuments_.review: [JANUARY 19th, 2024 EDIT: This is an old review that I plan to update once I get around to beating the now-complete game. It's only gotten better since then, though. They fixed a lot of text errors and added cardinal directions to the compass, too.]Blood West is an extremely fun game that already feels mostly complete in terms of mechanics. The devs have promised an additional 2 scenarios that I honestly can't wait for. The current scenario isn't terribly long (it took me about 4 hours to complete), but because of how much fun the game was, it still felt like a fulfilling experience and I personally already feel like I got my money's worth. (If you're wondering why I have so many hours in the game, know that I speedrun it.) If you're willing to listen to the largely positive reviews for this game and jump in early, you won't be disappointed.Some pros, mids, and cons to consider:PROS1. Shooting feels good, especially if you invest in perks that deal with aim sway, and ESPECIALLY if you nab a Winchester. (Yes, there is aim sway. This isn't DOOM. Think about your shots before you take them.)2. The gameplay cycle of carefully taking out enemies, looting, selling what you don't need and buying new items and gaining new perks may seem simple, but it's rewarding as all hell. Finding a health potion is wonderful. Finding an artifact that goes well with your build is more wonderful. Finding a unique weapon that's perfect for your playstyle? Priceless.3. It's extremely hard to go gung-ho in this game. It's not impossible, but you're going to have to earn that guns-blazing glory. The game rewards methodical play, and in my opinion, that suits it perfectly.4. The perks you earn upon leveling up and the artifacts you find on enemies and hidden in certain places feel substantial. Even though they're generally stat increases as opposed to new abilities or anything, you *will* feel those stat increases. (Usually.)5. The atmosphere and storytelling is really nice. Walking through the fort and hearing the calls and footsteps of ghostly soldiers was such a neat touch. I also liked the little stories the Totem of Souls told you when you brought it cursed items.6. This is by no means a movement shooter—your movement options are limited to crouch-walking, walking, running, and jumping, and you can't run and shoot—but that doesn't really stop the movement itself from feeling great. Running jumps allow you a nice freedom of movement, and you can pull off some fun parkour here and there, if you're so inclined, since there's not much in the way of invisible or simplified geometry. If it looks like you could stand on it, you probably can. (If a speedrunner is saying this, you know it means something.)7. There's a fun variety of enemies for you to fight, and they all act in unique ways. They'll all pursue you, but humanpedes avoid close-quarters combat in favor of spitting at you from a distance, while prodigal daughters will move faster if you shoot off their masks. Even the "standard" zombie has a lunge attack up its sleeve to mix things up. I never felt bored with the enemies throughout my playthrough (although I'm not sure this would extend for two more scenarios; here's hoping they add more enemies for them!)8. The ranged attack enemies are VERY good at leading their target (AKA you). You will not get away with simply strafing in one direction to avoid taking shots, which makes defeating them more difficult and more gratifying.9. Some have considered the soul flaw and curse system to be something they don't like about the game, but I think it's an effective way to make you care about death. Deaths actually have an impact beyond sending you to a checkpoint, and the game gives you tools to prevent or cure these effects. The system is a pro, not a con, in my opinion.10. The scenario ends right around when you'd get overpowered. Realistically, the monsters are ALWAYS capable of mauling you if you get too comfortable. But by the time I felt my power was reaching its peak, it was time to face the boss. It felt right.MIDS1. I won't spoil much about the boss, but it felt a bit underwhelming to me. It wasn't bad, and I kinda like what they went for, but I feel it could have been better.2. The map/compass is not great. With regards to the map, it's really not supposed to be, which is why this isn't a con (you're supposed to explore the mines for yourself; the map just tells you where to find the mines, not their whole layout). But a glaring omission is the lack of cardinal directions on the compass; it just points you towards objectives and enemies who are aware or becoming aware of you, which is nice, but finding out which direction you're facing is weirdly difficult.3. I said before that enemy behavior is nice and varied, but enemies whose attack plan consists of chasing you can be gamed if you're above them or past something they can't move through (the latter is especially true about the hulking Vendigo). This is also not a con because the tutorial makes it clear that this is sort of supposed to be the case, but it feels a bit cheap to defeat enemies because they have no way to climb ladders.CONS1. Lots of mistakes in the text in this game. As an aspiring editor, this hurts me; not because I personally care that much, but more because I know it takes away from the professionalism of the game's presentation. Trust me when I say this is a very well-made game in almost every regard; the text is just messily written in a lot of places. (Side note: I love this game so much that I'd be willing to proofread all the text in the game for free. I mean, I doubt they'll take me up on that, but I'm serious.)2. The depiction of natives is not great. It's far from the worst I've seen, and I'd like to think it keeps from being outright disrespectful, but the way the Shaman is depicted is at the very least pretty lazy. This kind of thing is a bit prevalent in Westerns, so I'm just glad it's not worse, even if that doesn't really excuse it. But if you're socially conscious in that sense, it's worth being informed of.You may notice I haven't listed any cons pertaining to actual gameplay. That's because I couldn't think of any. Make of that what you will. I think you should buy this game!

_childDocuments_.review: God this is such a mixed bag for me, concept gets a 10/10 for me, execution is more like a 5. This game is hard, and there is no difficulty setting, it's a stealth shooter, but doesn't have the environment to be a stealth shooter, I feel like I'm trying to sneak up on people who are standing in an open field. They do give you a distraction method to disrupt AI pathing, it doesn't work half the time. The combat in this game is incredibly unforgiving, if you mess up you die. The enemies feel uninteresting, the environment is empty and these pixels would look better if I played it on my PlayStation 2. The playloop feels like I'm playing a classic dungeon Crawl game, but frankly I'd rather play one of those games. Don't let the great Ghoultown song in the trailer the music in this game is practically non existentThe guns Feel great, and the smoothness of the stealth kills you can get is really satisfying. The voice acting is passable.  The Concept for this game is great and it feels like the developers may have sat down to play Deadlands classic at a few points in their lives. I like the progression system, the perks you get are a bit generic but serviceable. This game is not worth $25, buy it when it's on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Blood West

_childDocuments_.review: It's a decent immersive sim with awesome visual aesthetics and atmosphere. The enemy designs are probably some of the best I've seen and the side characters are all pretty fleshed out and enjoyable. The stealth system is pretty bare-bones, but the combat is fun and fairly challenging. The final confrontation is the lowest point of the game, unfortunately, which is a shame because the story was decent up-until then. It wasn't enough to ruin the game for me, though.Honestly, I recommend it for it's premise (which is really cool) and the enjoyable gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Blood West

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of people compare this game to Hunt: Showdown but it feels far more akin to a boomer-fied STALKER with central hub areas and a semi-open world peppered with a few NPC-given quests for direction. The game has a great sense of exploration combined with old-school inventory management, RPG-lite mechanics, fantastic art direction, incredibly immersive sound design and is just dripping in a weird west atmosphere. Blood West is well worth the price of admission in its current early access state.
_childDocuments_.name: Blood West

_childDocuments_.review: It's a solid game, just not for me.So the game is one giant map as far as I know, but with a huge emphasis on stealth, meaning you're waiting a lot for enemy patrols to walk by or face their back to you. Very basic and a bit too slow for me. There are skills you unlock as you level up which I assume alleviate these issues by making your character function more properly, but at the beginning I felt very under-powered and could only take a few hits before death.Speaking of which, the game has a sort of "you die you lose your buffs, but also get debuffs" system, which I'm just not into.. I'd prefer being able to quicksave.Overall is the game bad? NO! Far from it, this game is amazing at what it wants to do, it's just that it wasn't for me, I prefer the stealth from recent titles like Gloomwood where it's fast and to the point.I'm sure if I put enough time into Blood West, I could get some perks that allow me to go in guns blazing, but I just don't have the patience, so I'll be refunding sorry.
_childDocuments_.name: Blood West

_childDocuments_.review: Finished the game, tried to do everything in every chapter.Enemies are interesting, and felt like I was always cautious heading into a new area.Weapons are nice, didn't do much melee aside for sneaky backstabbing.You are sure to find some combination that you enjoy.I played sneaky archer for the first part of the game before going full on guns.Would have loved a chapter 4, focused around that one part we saw in the epilogue (keeping it vague to avoid spoilers, but you'll know what I'm referencing).Maybe in Blood West 2? :)Either way, easy recommend if you enjoy Western setting, FPS, Survival horror, skill/perks, and scrounging for bullets.
_childDocuments_.name: Blood West

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a fairly competent stealth shooter rpg. Initially I called it an immersive sim, and while i still think it qualifies, it's rather limited in what approaches it can offer you beyond rpg character builds.Ultimately, I got bored and dropped it. I think the culprits for me were the uninspired environments and the disengaging story.
_childDocuments_.name: Blood West

_childDocuments_.review: At 13 hours in, I see where I need to go but I don't think I want to do it. The aesthetic choices are good. The game play itself is fun. The first episode is pretty fun and the game eventually feels good as you get into the swing of it. But the punishment in episode two is where the harsh punishment really turned me off. While I don't mind a challenge, I started to feel the life minutes flowing away on the 10th time running from the underground bunker trying to scrape coins together to buy better equipment. Or, slowly walk through every house to make sure I'm not missing something. I like what this game does but I think I've seen enough/ 24 bucks is probably fair price to take a punt on this game. But, if you can get it on sale, I think it's 100% worth trying out.
_childDocuments_.name: Blood West

_childDocuments_.review: At first the game makes a mid impression but I recommend sticking to it for a few hours. After you start discovering unique items with interesting effects, and difficulty starts picking up it becomes very engaging. It's a soft 'immersive sim'. It has inventory management, some rpg elements with an emphasis on clever use of your equipment. The levels are open-ended and a stealthy approach is encouraged but not forced. The thing that is missing the most is environmental interactivity. I hope that if they ever decide to make Blood West 2, they follow this path and add some physics and objects to play around with.
_childDocuments_.name: Blood West

_childDocuments_.review: In my opinion, game is on strong 9/10. See there inspirations from System Shock, little roge-like. Graphic design is simple but pleasing for the eye. And this atmosphere, is so good, horror + wild west is turned out brilliant. Game encourages exploration of every corner of the chapter. But it is worth remembering thats game is not easy, it is damn difficult. Of course, I dont consider this a minus of the production, but a plus. You never know whats waiting for you around the corner.

_childDocuments_.review: Fairly simple gameplay (in a good way), fun weapons, and great vibes from the combination of setting and graphics. _childDocuments_.review: First of all, this game is a fine ass comeback for immersive sims. It has satisfying combat, progression, exploration, everything. And you don't even have to worry about saving. This game also takes world designing inspiration from dark souls and manages to be f@%king scary at times. I truly enjoyed my time with chapter 1, and was a bit worried for chapter 2 as I nearly breezed past the first boss (most likely due to a lot of exploration and grinding, this game is fun). But this game managed to prove me wrong, it still managed to be tense and fun even in chapter 2 and now I am truly content with my purchase. Not many games manage to be tense and difficult after the intial few hours, but this game is different. And there is something nice waiting for you just at the beginning of chapter 2 ;)

_childDocuments_.review: Blood West.Hunt: Showdown meets classic Arkane Studios gameplay (Dishonored, Deathloop, etc.), all wrapped in a rather pleasant retro-style aesthetic, though for a /very/ short singleplayer game.In Blood West's current state, you've got roughly five-ish hours of content, with somewhat limited replayability. Admittedly, those five hours are /very/ well-made, and /very/ tightly put-together. You'll be sneaking, stabbing, and shooting your way through a vaguely horror-y vibe Western. The actual horror and spookiness is, admittedly, minimal, more-or-less just stuck to spooky and grotesque-looking enemies, and one of the four voice actors having a rather spooky overlay for their voice.The game, for the most part, seems decently feature-complete. Every feature is there that you'd expect. A little polishing here or there is needed, but otherwise- you've got a /very/ solid stealth system, marred only by lean mechanics that don't really seem helpful. You've got VERY crisp guns, that feel EXCELLENT to shoot, even if there are only four different gun types, a revolver, a lever-action rifle, a sawed-off shotgun, and a full-size double barrel. They all handle well, and feel good to shoot, with enemy feedback feeling excellent, especially on headshots, when enemy heads explode into mists and spurts of air. You've also access to a bow, but I hadn't tried it out, as bows tend to be rather uninteresting for me.My complaint about guns, though, is that instead of giving most of the better weapons interesting mechanics, or notable differences, and the general lack of /other/ guns, the better variants simply deal more damage, and the unique variants usually just deal even more damage if you fulfill a specific condition (IE, extra damage while drunk, or extra damage to a specific enemy type). I'd rather have preferred if the worse weapon variants had negative mechanics, like jamming, or something to actually make them feel worse, beyond looking rusty and dealing less damage, and better guns would be better not just by dealing extra damage, but also, perhaps, having an extra ability, or not jamming as often.There are a few enemy types, for the most part, they all feel generally different-y, my only real annoyance is that there's basically no difference between the standard undead, and miner zombies, aside from miner zombies just dealing some more damage, and having slightly better loot? Other than that, they all feel interesting to fight, if a touch overwhelming at times.My complaint with the enemies is that there aren't any sub-types, even visual sub-types. All the standard undead look identical, all the birdmen look identical, all the prodigal daughters look identical, etc. Just a little visual variety would've been nice.The game as it stands right now, takes place on one fairly small-sized open world map, in which you'll likely explore every location, provided you aren't speedrunning. Each place is generally unique-y, and the game does a good job of slowly introducing new enemy types as you progress further into the map, though I found myself getting a bit tired of caves by the fifth hour in, though overuse of caves to the point of exhaustion is a fairly common problem with many open-world games.My absolute biggest complaint for the game? There just isn't enough CONTENT, which- the developers have claimed they're planning on adding, and judging by the interactions I've witnessed in their steam discussion forums? They seem quite dedicated to it. I remember seeing a discussion post asking for toggleable aim-down-sight (Right click once just to scope in, right click again to unscope, rather than hold right click the entire time.), said if there was demand for they'd consider it- some demand showed, and about three-odd days later, lo-and-behold, toggleable ADS was added to the game.But the game really does need content. Not just a bigger map, but more enemy types, new guns that aren't simply "The revolver, but more damage", more quests, and- in my opinion, a better selection of perks. Most of the perks I've seen are generally uninteresting in design, most of them being "Number Goes Up" types, where a stat just gets a boost. A few, though, were good. In particular, you can get a perk that gives you a temporary matrix-style bullet-time when you aim down your gun's sights for some easier headshots, but most of them were just "Stat gets a +20%", which, IMHO, isn't particularly inspiring. Replacing them with various magic powers/abilities, given that this /is/ a sort of semi-magical/cursed land, would've been cooler.But! Despite all the complaints I've levied, it's still a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ FUN five-odd hours. And the Devs do seem dedicated from my own observation so far.
