_childDocuments_.review: This is the first single-player game that has caught my attention in YEARS. From the moment you start playing the game, the art style really caught my attention. You're quickly introduced to stealth mechanics which is a big plus for me as I love sneaking around quietly dispatching enemies although if you prefer you can always just run in guns blazing if that's your preferred playstyle. There is loot to find around the world which you can also get from enemies you've killed to then sell and buy better weapons or health, ammo, etc. This game also has inventory management sort of like RE4 which I thought was pretty satisfying debating fitting as much as could heading even deeper into unknown territory or turning around selling all my loot. All in all I think this game is great and I look forward to the other 2 parts.

_childDocuments_.review: I really, really enjoyed this game. Congratulations to Piotr and the Dev team. A super tense, creepy and atmospheric game reminiscent of STALKER or Resident Evil. I really appreciate the Souls style autosave as it prevents save scumming (my worst habit in stealth games). The weapons (particularly the guns) are just fantastic. My only suggestion would be to lean into immersive sim elements a little more; things like throwable bait to attract creatures, riggable TNT with a remote detonator, things like that. It feels like most of the groundwork is there already and it would add a bit more variety to a fairly lengthy campaign.Very good game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good game, truly, but it does have a few "short comings" that could use some refinement.Mainly the sneaking element. I find enemies to "telegraph" less that they see "something" instead of just a progress bar increasing.I find that relying on the hud to know their observational state to be immersion breaking. So much so I did what the devs most likely hate people do to their game; Cheat.The bizarre huge damage the enemies do, feels also weirdly out of place, and the revival mechanic is also not fun for me.But once i used something like Cheat Engine to make my character Regen health at 3hp/s regardless of combat, and double stamina and triple stamina regen, I started to have a LOT of fun. I still died a ton, but I felt less punished for being a bit reckless.The one thing i guess i could really complain about is the weapons. There is something about them that just feels "Meh".I could never really find a weapon i really enjoyed, although the Bone Knife was clearly my favorite until made useless in Act 2, which i hated. No way to upgrade it or the like. I REALLY enjoyed the knife, and the enemies bloated health pool just meant i had to stash my lovely knife. It's clear where the Devs was trying to go fore, but i felt punished for enjoying a weapon in act 2.The bloated health pools nearly always feels lazy in any game, and it was the same here.Instead of thinking of new ways to mess with the player, they would rather just bloat HP of enemies.I'll still play through BW act 2, but if enemies health a bloated even more in act 3, then i don't really have must confidence in the creativity of the devs.I enjoy mostly everything else. Love the enemy designs, although they could use a minor variety. Different colored dresses or pants, different kinds of pants, etc... Not a lot, just something to add a little variety. The game had a dry feeling to it due to lack of variety.The upside, it allowed my potato computer to run this game just fine.Oh, and had to kill the music in act 1, haven't heard if act 2 is any better... But holy heck... the short looping music track in act 1 is annoying!When i get back in the game, i'll give act 2 a chance, but i do not have any hopes it's any better. Some weird design choices throughout this game, nothing bad, just weird.Would love to play a NG+ with some kind of OP Rapid firing gun and just mow down anything and everything in my way, no ammo limit or the like. just a fast gun, little thought, true American way; Spray and Play.

_childDocuments_.review: Will update as I keep playing this, having spent 4 additional hours in the huge demo released for the Steam Next Festival.I loved the games demo and I love the game here! Instantly became one of my most anticipated games following the festival, and it seems to (mostly) live up to expectations.Blood West fills the hole in your heart S.T.A.L.K.E.R left. An exploration based, treasure-hunting immersive sim/RPG with horror elements that really hasn't been explored since. Blood West does an excellent job of significantly furthering the style of game by introducing new ideas and mechanics heavily inspired by newer games and game genres (Souls-like, roguelike, modern survival horror).It is definitely still fairly sparse and early access feeling. The sudden drop into the world, the limited play area, some of its more "video-gamey" feeling elements like enemies just sort of meandering about the world with no real rhyme or reason as well as limited NPC's; all of these things make the game feel a long ways away from finished. But if you're like me and you just can't wait for this to be finished or hope that the new S.T.A.L.K.E.R ends up being what we all hope it'll be, Blood West's Early Access will still satisfy and excite you.

_childDocuments_.review: Having now finished the first scenario, I can safely say this was a thoroughly enjoyable experience. The core gameplay loop is satisfying, and you can really feel the passionate, focused approach the developers took to the game. The graphics are wonderfully nostalgic, sound design is crisp and the voice acting is that right mix of corny and quality. I'm also a big fan of how natural the progression feels, both with levelling up and collecting new gear. If you like games like Hunt: Showdown, this is a game for you. I do have some criticisms, however, which should be taken into consideration. If you focus on melee throughout the game (as I did), you will have WAY too much ammo. Seriously, more than I knew what to do with. I had to force myself to use guns because melee is just far too effective for most situations. This goes for items like healing potions, gold coins, special ammo and bandages as well. Also, the winchester (and its variant Drunk Master) are basically useless compared to the revolver. The revolvers do more damage and even though they don't have as much effective range, this can be easily offset with skills. The AI in this game is incredibly easy to cheese. There were a couple of times where  enemies caught me off guard and made me adapt to the situation. The first time I encountered a Vendigo I just about ♥♥♥♥ my pants. However, the 3rd, 4th, 5th, 6th, etc., the tension was basically lost. I had learned how to trick the AI by jumping over a fence and forcing them to go around, or jumping up on a ledge where their pathfinding would get stuck and I could easily headshot them. I'm not sure how this could be solved, but if you want to have the best experience with this game, try not to take advantage of the occasionally clunky AI. My last criticism concerns the final boss of Scenario 1, so don't read if you don't want it spoiled. I only criticise the game so much because I really love it and care about the direction it takes through Early Access. This has the potential to be a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ outstanding 1.0 release and I would love to see it make it there.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR it’s a grindy crouchfest with interesting beginningGame starts fun and interesting, you’re an undead cowboy fighting ghouls and zombies, simple but classic stealth mechanics make you think this might be fun. But the game doesn’t introduce anything except these basic classic mechanics and there’s nothing new after the first chapter. The only viable way to play is to crouch, get as close to the enemy as you can and either slap it with melee weapon on the back or land a headshot. If you weren’t able to land a headshot – you run away because it’s almost impossible to deal with enemies in face-to-face combat. In chapter three even this stops working as enemies become so tanky that can take multiple headshots unless you’re maximizing damage with trinkets or special ammo. So, after chapter one there are no new mechanics, no new interesting weapons or skills, no interesting story, you just crouch and try to headshot stuff. You can’t stack artifacts with desirable effects as you have same three slots as in the beginning of the game and enemy placement only becomes more dense and clearing the area or attempts to just quietly pass through become more and more like a chore. Unless some new ideas or mechanics are introduced, there’s nothing to see or do after chapter one.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those times I wish there was a thing between positive and negative reviews but oh well. Blood West is a western themed horror game with focus on stealth and being cautious in the choices you make because getting swarmed by enemies and dying is very easy. The game is open world set in 3 different maps, you get an arsenal of weapons and different ways to approach the enemies, whether you want to play a melee focused build or be like me and just play with a bow throughout the game. Gameplay feels very similar to that of S.T.A.L.K.E.R and I really enjoyed running around killing monsters and hoarding loot like the loot goblin I am, to sell it for big profits.There is lots of monster variety and it's definitely not a game you can just rush through because these guys will never stop chasing you. Some monsters prove to be an actual challenge and it feels rewarding when you are able to actually slay these beasts.The story... was there. And I am saying 'was' because the story fell off quit a lot in Chapter 3 and it just didn't make any sense. The first two chapters you are helping this totem of souls cleansing the lands of evil, but in chapter 3 suddenly the totem is evil because reasons and when you defeat it, it doesn't matter, your world is doomed anyway and there is nothing you can do about it. Everyone dies. Look, I'm not saying that every game should have a happy ending. But with Chapter 3 it feels like the developer just got bored and just wanted to finish the game and get it out of early access as soon as possible and be done with it. All the characters you meet don't matter. Any lore tied to them, doesn't matter. Any choices you make throughout the game and all the 'evil' that you cleanse, that doesn't matter either.A very dissapointing final chapter and ending to a game that had a really good thing going for it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game came as a total surprise to me. I stumbled upon it and it sparked interest with its inspiration drawn from the excellent Hunt:Showdown by Crytek. Ive poured many hours into that game and can say that the devs of this game have nailed it. They managed to be inspired and not copy and paste like nearly all other devs. I can see the inspiration, but I dont feel like im playing another game...its just so incredibly well done and I love to see this amount of detail and care put into a seemingly little game. Whats here, is polished, and while I have really only one issue with the game, it is something so tiny compared to the greatness the rest of it is. Guns feel heavy, punchy, and damn strong. Stealth is highly suggested, but as you get better gear and knowledge of the enemies, you can more or less "run and gun" for the lack of a better word, bottom line is you have a choice of how to play this game and you're never punished regardless of said choice. The issue I mentioned earlier is that some monsters don't have footstep sounds, especially the big dudes. Again, not a big deal, but just something that does need to be addressed. 9/10 rating by me...feels far more polished than 90% of the AAA titles released lately. Its dev teams like this that give me hope <3

_childDocuments_.name: Blood West

_childDocuments_.review: Blood West is a first person game where you, as an undead, explore a cursed land with all manners of monsters roaming it and many secrets and quests to find. Death isn't final and there are many playstyles and a level up system to take advantage of.Overall, I liked blood west. It got a bit repetitive towards the end despite them changing up and adding new enemies with the new maps, but it still always felt cool and fun to explore these dangerous areas and slowly make my way through the monsters guarding them. The game also gives you the ability to get deceptively powerful but also not, enemies can kill you fast in this but you can also do the same if you're aiming good.Good stuff : -Weapon variety is decent, there isn't that many weapon TYPES but what is there is a good mix for what the game offers, in addition most if not every weapon type has some amount of special versions of it that have unique stats and effects tied to them. For example a bow that doesn't need arrows, instead it uses small bits of HP per fire.-There's also a equipment system in the form of these 'artifact' items you can find, just like those special weapons you'll find strange items that range from a bark heart to a playing card to literal human skin with writing on it, all of them give unique effects and there's a lot of synergies in the game for extra build variety.-Enemy designs are great and I love that we get progressively more freaky stuff as we go from act to act. First time seeing some of the more monstrous enemies provoked a "woah what the hell" type response consistently.-Maps are great as well, each act gives you a new map to explore with their own themes and the environment of all 3 of them are so varied and with so much to explore that unless I was wall hugging THAT HARD it never felt like I was really exploring into nothing too much and hell sometimes when it did feel like that I still found something. The fact you're also unrestricted and can go almost anywhere is a massive boon, you can end up completing objectives early and be able to tell npcs "oh yeah I already have that", its a nice feeling.MEH Stuff : -Looting is simultaneously fun and tedious. I like finding new areas and combing them down, but some stuff just blends in too much and some item placements are annoying. It would've been nice if items had a glow or occasional sheen to them when they were in view, I ended up having to regularly open my inventory to check the GROUND section and see what's near me and it became the regular thing to do by act 3.-Level up skills are a varied list of "That's just too good" to "this is basically useless.", some of it depending on your build, but its scattered everywhere. Especially if you know the game already (either doing another run or you were in early access), there's some skills that are just plain useless to you and I'm not talking about the ones that aren't of your build specs. Instant 3 I can point to are : the 2 "enemy can miss" perks, ranged enemies can have their aim baited and melee enemies can be ran from or just taken head on. And the Thick Skinned perk, not a lot of enemies do those damage types and most of them barely do damage or are easy to kill, meaning it's not worth dumping points in it.-End boss fights for each act in general were rather easy in my opinion, first one was cool, second one was walking sim and third one was cool but just didn't do damage to me. All of them suffer from a lack of attack variety as well.Disliked stuff : -I did not like the ending or the story reasons for the final boss fight. Not gonna spoil anything just do not like it.-It gets repetitive, despite the new enemies and environments as you go to each act, your gameplay will remain largely unchanged. You skulk around, maybe headsmash some people with whatever weapon and do that place to place. Very rarely is there an enemy that makes you mix it up and even then you can often brute force em, even act 3 tried to have an enemy that requires fire but they die just as fast as any and by that point you'll have the ability to get plenty of fire to deal with them. I managed to not mind this repetition too much due to the game's style keeping me interested but it is still a disliked thing.-Death mechanic is very iffy. On death a good number of the enemies killed will respawn, but not all of them, you also get a 'soul flaw' unless you were wearing a coin to prevent it, you wont be though because artifact stats are stupid good. Your first flaw is a random stat decrease, the next 2 flaws will be the same one, stacking on. At 3 flaws it turns into a curse with the max effect, you can NOW get a quest to purge it by playing fetch for a specific group of items OR you can find a special purple potion to just cleanse all curses/flaws, this potion however is notably rare especially in the earlier acts and if you die often you'll likely be using them more often. This punishes new and less experienced players massively, some of the effects gut the experience like -xp gain preventing a proper level up amount to trickle in or -maxhp which just means you'll die more often and you can get MULTIPLE CURSES, letting you get every flavor of "sorry shouldn't of died lol." on you. The actual quest to purge the curse now also distracts you as you must either hope your next objective location happens to have the enemy you need the parts of or you must go and search an area for them, potentially one you've already went through. Not fun.-To my knowledge there is no NG+, I beat the game and no options or anything has shown up so unless I bugged or missed something, it appears to not be a thing. Games like this are great with NG+, being able to go back to older areas with a later game special weapon and blast fun is always a nice time.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd recommend it with a caveat. Blood West is a brilliant core of a game with some frustrating flaws, How you feel about said flaws will determine whether or not you'll stick with this one. Blood West pretty brilliantly understands things like level design and exploration. Layouts are often branching and nonlinear, but still sensible and fairly easy to navigate while not so straightforward they're without secrets. Enemy placements and patrols are also well thought out, giving the player just enough space to get a kill and reposition without giving you so much breathing room that it becomes trivial. Loot is well hidden, and rewards you for being thorough. It's satisfying and meaningful, and on the rare occasion you pick up something you'll never use, traders have enough good stuff that selling it is worthwhileThe stealth combat is overall mostly fantastic. You know when you're being seen and heard, and have enough time to make a snap decision based on the situation. Having a strategic approach will almost always be rewarded, whereas charging in will usually be punished. The effect of combat is really sold by the sound design, coupled with the VA's excellent performance. Gun sounds especially stick out to me as great, really selling their power and impact. Edit: I've seen some backlash over the protag VA changeover, so I feel it's worth noting that Stephen Russell does a phenomenal job as the protag. The voice work in Blood West overall is far above the cut. Alvaro especially is a voice that just oozes personality and brought joy to me to hear.Non stealth combat and sniping are where the game fall short for me personally. Sniping struggles due to the aesthetic of the game. A muddy, fairly grey-and-beige color palate means it can be hard to tell where a distant enemy ends and the environment begins. The game gives you a lot of great vantage points for sniping, but I very rarely found myself using them, as failed attempts led to substantial wastes of ammo, or in the case of not being protected by a latter, getting swarmed.Non stealth combat is my biggest gripe with the game, and it entirely hinges on the fact that the game feels incredibly inconsistent on a few fronts. Foremost is damage. An enemy may take wildly different amounts of time to kill with a melee weapon outside of stealth, even when you're using the same weapon, same build, same level against the same enemy. It's not clear why this is, as it occurs even when factoring for headshots. Hitstun is the same way, sometimes you can stunlock an enemy to death, sometimes they'll completely ignore you and attack anyway. Once again, the same type of enemy may exhibit both behaviors. Lastly is inconsistent hit detection. Frustratingly often a shot that ostensibly should be a headshot won't be, or I'll miss completely at point blank. This I think comes down to the precise hitboxes and the fact enemies bob up and down a ton.Ultimately that inconsistency has really brought down my enjoyment of the game, because I feel like I'm always punished for taking a risk instead of the safe, slow route of sniping and abusing ladders/crawlspaces. Occasionally I'll be playing perfectly, make one mistake, try and correct only to be killed by these inconsistencies and be left with frustration.To conclude, Blood West is a challenging and satisfying game that suffers from being frustrating at times. If you enjoy the exploration aspect of Bethesda games or need some first person stealth and don't mind the flaws, you'll most likely enjoy this one even at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: I just started, but boy - do get this game.It starts so strong, I highly doubt it'll let go by the end. It takes Clive Barker's Undying as a clear inspiration (beginning monsters look a lot like Howlers!), but modifies the first person shooter formula with a healthy addition of - soulsborne mechanic!You can't save whenever you want, but only when you exit the game. Meanwhile, if you die - you respawn at the checkpoint totem. You can sleep to restore HP, but it respawns mobs. And mobs - they hit hard. VERY hard. You're encouraged to go stealth and make every shot count. It also encourages exploration because there's some trading to be done, and you will really, really need those extra bullets, arrows, healing kits, etc.There's simple leveling/perk based system - you gain level, you get skill points, and you pay to unlock a perk - stuff like, faster reloading, harder to detect when sneaking, etc.There's even some questing!Graphics are simple and style is dated - but imo, its top notch. Back in 200x this would be an AAA title, graphics wise. Sound is great, and it has really good oomph on weapons. Voice acting is also pretty good, even if its exaggerated for effect and style.All in all - I stumbled upon this by chance, and I'm really hoping it'll keep on the way it started, because its effin' awesome and you should totally buy it, if you dig games like Clive Barker's Undying, Thief series, Blood and such.

_childDocuments_.review: So, who should play Blood West? Well, preferably a lot of people, because it really is a fun, well-crafted little game. With its dark, tense atmosphere, retro-style visuals and pleasant fusion of FPS and RPG elements, it’s clearly been made with fans of oldschool immersive sims in mind – if you’re into mildly challenging, methodical gameplay that focuses on discovery and exploration in the vein of Thief, S.T.A.L.K.E.R. and Deus Ex, you’ll want to give it a shot. Fans of Soulslikes will also find a lot to enjoy here, with various different enemies that all require different strategies to defeat, a “bonfire” system that revives certain monsters when you rest or die, as well as a curse system where every death makes you progressively weaker, thus incentivizing you to get better at the game and weigh your options in terms of how much danger you're willing to take on at once – otherwise, you’ll have to deal with nasty (albeit removable) debuffs and some respawned enemies. All in all, Blood West has been a very pleasant surprise for me that managed to tick off a lot of my favorite checkboxes, so if what I’ve described above sounds exciting to you, I highly recommend you check it out.For more honest indie game reviews, check out our Curator page:

_childDocuments_.review: So I'll start of by saying that I recommend this game  cautiously. What you're getting up-front is a roughly 15~ hour singleplayer experience with very limited replayability. The best way to describe the gameplay is something of a immersive-sim-esque stealth-action FPS RPG. If that sounds like a mouthful, that's because this game is wearing many hats at once. Overall I think it suffers from this in the end. On to the game as a whole each chapter features what I would describe as a miniature 'open world' for the player to muck around in and explore. Though, they are largely bereft of meaningful content aside from the main-quest "dungeons". Each dungeon largely amounts to a meandering maze with a smattering of enemies strewn about to serve as obstacles, but sadly being quite lacking as far as loot or interesting combat encounters go. The gameplay loop likewise suffers from pulling itself in multiple directions. There are incentives for stealth, but the game has boss fights where you more likely than not  the extra health and damage they provide. At the same time "going loud" is also a poor idea as ammunition is scarce to the point that your only 'sustainable' option is melee. With guns being very restricted in use up until mid-late act 3 (the last chapter).And then all of this stacked on top of itself, the perks themselves are mislabeled and do not properly report what sort of statistical increases they provide. Meaning the player will likely invest poorly and be forced to restart if they make a poor build due to this bad phrasing.If you can put up with all of the above for some pretty nice atmosphere, a few neat guns, neat aesthetic and trifling story, then go ahead. Pick up blood west. But consider this my fair warning to those interested in picking it up, it's got issues, just as much as it has untapped potential.

_childDocuments_.review: Blood West has to be one of those indie games that I love but I also have gripes with. Blood West is a type of game that I love, a weird west setting that has open maps and allows you to proceed through it your own way, whether that is stealthing through the abandoned towns, backstabbing zombies or blasting them away with a double barrel shotgun. With unique weapons, trinkets and perks that allow you to refine your preferred play style the game has options on how to play through it.  My only gripe is that the game is sold as a stealth shooter but I found myself easily running around guns blazing without much care for stealth at all as long as I made sure to aim for the head. You are quite vulnerable as most creatures can knock you out in a few hits but they also drop before they even become an issue. I would say that if you managed your bullets and other resources carefully you can easily get through the game with a much more aggressive playstyle. There are a few monsters that can drain your resources or kill you easily if you aren't careful so you might need to use stealth but after encountering them a few times you can easily deal with them. Your experience may differ as you can go with a much more stealth and melee oriented build so you may have a completely different view of the game.Monster variety was pretty good, I liked all of the designs and they all caught me off guard when I first ran into them. Finding notes in the world to learn more was an actual joy as I not only got lore on them, I also given info on how to deal with them. You do have your basic zombies and some expected creatures in a weird west setting, but there were quite a few at the end that genuinely surprised me. The story was fun, but shallow in a way as it set up all this evil and torment plaguing the world but you never really delved deeper into it. Surprisingly Act 1 had the most story as you learned about the places of interest and what caused the downfall of the region. I wish there was more of it in Act 2, but Act 3 brought that back. I wish I could get more into the story but I don't want to spoil anything for those who might be interested in playing through it. Generally I loved my experience with Blood West, my first playthrough clocked around 15 hours but how I played the game may have allowed me to breeze through the experience so take that as you will. Sorry for any grammatical or spelling mistakes in the review. Thank you for reading

_childDocuments_.review: The easiest way for me to summarise Blood West: A Single-player Hunt Showdown experience with a nostalgic touch. My first playthrough ran me about 18 hours and Blood West delivered on exactly what's on the tin. This is a stealth focused FPS RPG with a weird west aesthetic, and I couldn't put it down until I completed that first playthrough. As an RPG Blood West offers a small variety of builds for your character to follow, focused around your level based perks and the equipment available to you as your progress. Build diversity starts off small in your first playthrough, as you are limited to the equipment available and a smaller perk list, but by time you've reached Act 3 you'll really have a wide variety of choice. Thankfully any subsequent playthrough will give you the full perk list from level one, and most of the later unlocked perks are broader additions to your character like inventory size rather that combat focused anyways. For my first playthrough I followed what I imagine is the most common build path, a stealthy gunman focusing on revolvers and rifles, which served me very well for majority of the game. Separated into 3 acts, each act has a unique local and set of objectives that helps keep each act fresh as you progress. Each act performs well as a standalone experience. Act 1 made for a great starting experience, both gameplay and aesthetically. Act 2 was a big jump from Act 1 with a significant increase in difficulty as the variety of the enemies widens drastically, but felt great once you learned the ropes. Act 3 took a smaller jump in difficulty, but changed up the formula to deliver another fresh experience as you explore. I really enjoyed how each act changed from the prior to keep it fun and exciting.Each act is inaccessible after defeating the act boss, which means you have to make sure you've explored every nook and cranny to make sure you've found all of the unique equipment you can before taking on the bosses. A change I'd like to see in the future is a New Game+ feature that lets you cycle back to Act 1 after you defeat Act 3's boss, as currently the credits roll and your save file is simply left in a limbo saved at the final boss arena (you can get out and return to exploring Act 3 but that is all). Outside of headshots and backstabs with melee weapons, enemies feel very spongy, and when 2-5 are rushing you down you'll very rapidly have to switch to a run and gun approach of emptying your guns and reloading as they chase you. If you do not land those headshots some enemies will easily take 3 to as many as 10 or maybe even 15 bullets to down. My limited experience with shotguns felt just as bad outside of headshots, the only difference being I was basically in melee range when they discovered me. Stealth and precision is king. The boss fights in Blood West do unfortunately fall short for me as individual experiences, as none of them reward the stealth based gameplay the overworld basically requires. That being said, I can't as a player think of ways to make FPS bosses that would reward stealth gameplay, so I would call that a consequence of the genre rather than a failing of any developer. Boss 1 was my most difficult fight, but that was likely due to a lack of tools in the early game. Boss 2 was easily the weakest experience (and very loud). Boss 3 could have been more impressive as a final boss, but worked overall.The final comment I have is that there is a feature that lets you turn down the rate of the player character's commentary, and I personally needed to make use of that and almost considered turning off the commentary entirely. No hate to any of  the voice actors, they all did incredible work! But by default the player character makes out of pocket one liners about just about every single action you take. Killing enemies, picking up items, healing, suffering from bleeding I really do mean almost everything. Even with reduced voice lines turned on it was still near constant commentary about picking up ammo, treasure and killing enemies. It just didn't work for me personally, but this didn't effect my actual gameplay experience at all.All in all, I heartily recommend giving Blood West a playthrough! I personally hope to see an Act 4 in the future, or (given the proper tools to support it) a community driven custom Act maker.
_childDocuments_.name: Blood West

_childDocuments_.review: A Thief-Inspired Horror Trip Into The Bloody WestIt took me a little over 50 hours to beat this game, and I must say that I thoroughly enjoyed it - here is why.GENERAL INFORMATION AND (SOME OF) THE GOODBlood West feels like a more forgiving, more action-oriented Thief. There are three massive maps to explore which all offer their own unique peculiarities, locations and monsters. Most importantly, they are all filled to the brim with loot, and the main attraction of the game is undoubtedly to pick up absolutely everything in sight while either going full stealth or shooting your way through enemy hordes, the latter of which does not always work. But regardless of how stealthy you try to be, sooner or later there will be that moment where enemies do spot you, requiring a quick escape or the aforementioned ballistic response. Both means of combat function without issues and can be plenty fun. Knifing a monster from behind, shooting them with a rifle to make their heads explode, or even using bows and crossbows from afar - there is plenty of variety to get violent.Initially, travelling around will feel somewhat slow, and whatever you encounter can be a threat. But as you grow stronger by unlocking skills and looting better equipment, the world begins to just invite you in. Personally, I did not care much about the story, which thankfully isn't that important and mostly exists for the sake of having a story. By the third map, I was playing Blood West solely in order to stumble upon more creepy places and loot them dry. The atmosphere is really quite something, and I never tired of traversing dusty canyons, old mines, abandoned towns, nasty swamps and foreboding woods, Some moments even provided really subtle visual story-telling, which enhanced the spooky mood even more. But if you are looking for a deep narrative to push you forward, you will not find it here. Once again, it is about the journey, not the destination.As for the main gameplay loop, well, one has to be a fan of it. You will be looting, a lot. You will be fighting tons of enemies, a lot. You will be sneaking around, a lot. Blood West is definitely designed for patient people, as plunging yourself into combat can be quite punishing. Since the maps are so vast, dying can result in long hikes back to were you perished, and some monsters do respawn. This never bothered me that much, though; after all, you are meant to sneak around and get punished accordingly if you make mistakes. Sometimes, I would get tired of it and turn off the game, only to return to it again an hour later. It just keeps pulling you back in, even after such moments, and that is the sign of a good game in my opinion.(SOME OF) THE BAD AND THE UGLYNow, all of this sounds really positive, but I would like to point out some specific flaws. Firstly, the game's difficulty and overall balancing can be deceptive. The first map is easy enough to handle, especially once you get stronger - however, the boss at the very end of it is a massive difficulty spike and might cause people to just quit entirely. While there are ways to weaken it beforehand, the boss ultimately cannot be dealt with in a stealthy manner, meaning that you have to start blasting, which can feel a little sudden if you have been avoiding gunfights and just been sneaking up to that point. If you die, you will not get any of your spent resources back and need to potentially endure another long hike back on top of it - only to perhaps die and get punished again, thus losing even more resources. The balancing really felt weird with that one, and none of the future bosses were nearly as difficult. Additionally, the game would occasionally start stuttering and lagging after a certain amount of time spent in a map. This wasn't so bad in the first one; however, the second and especially the third gave me issues towards the end of each area and made fighting the more action-oriented bosses a chore. I still won against them, so it wasn't impossible by any means - still, I feel that some better optimisation could have helped in those cases. According to the developers, having to many items in your stash can potentially cause the game to slow down, and such a flaw in a game all about hoarding items is truly unfortunate and baffles the mind.Lastly, I felt a little disappointed by the many unique artefacts one can find in the game. All of them have their own unique quirks, but the majority of them felt somewhat insignificant and worthless. Once you have found some really powerful ones that are obviously the best around, you will never eye another one and just collect them for the sake of filling up your inventory and selling them later. I just wish that there could have been more variety with them to create some more unique builds, rather than just focusing on what provides the most health, stamina and stealth increases. By the time I did find some silly ones, there was no longer any point because, well, I wanted to survive and thus needed the overpowered stuff.FINAL THOUGHTSGive this game a go if you love Thief and are patient; also, if you love Wild West-themed horror shenanigans. Blood West has great enemy design, very much enjoyable combat, a vast world featuring countless locations to explore, and it just scratches that itch if you are like me and want to explore and loot, all of it while spooky atmosphere washes over you. I certainly took my time playing, and 50 hours later I can say that it was all worth it. Not so much for the conclusion, but definitely for the blood we spilled along the way.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is good, it just overstays it's welcome by a long shot.The main problem is a lack of strategy, from beginning to end every single fight goes like this:Stab in the back (or the head from the second map onward since the enemies are more tanky) in stealth.Shoot in the head from distance.Open up with dynamite (for the nasty ones) and finish off with a gun.Except for a handful of skills there is no reason to level up.Monsters are interesting with their own vibe, but it doesn't mean a lot when every single fight goes as i said, the main difference is if they're going to shoot or chase or both.There is no concept of "trap" in this game so you can't plan ahead and make up a strategy to take out the baddies, at best you can pick and choose who to kill first and from where start shooting (if you're not in a cave), in the end the ultimate strategy is "they saw me, better run and reset aggro and repeat until it's over".Repeat this for 3 maps and thousand of enemies, by the time i explored 20% of the second map i was already tired.Stopped playing at 25% of the third map.I still recommend this game, maybe wait for a discount or for a dlc that adds some mechanics to spice up the repetitiveness of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: 1.0 UPDATEGame is still hard. Game is still fair. Game is still fun. Game is still rocks! Also Stephen L. Russell!CHAPTER 2 UPDATE:What I said in my previous review has only been strengthened. Again, it was hard to get into, but as soon as the game clicked with me again, I was swept away by the extremely satisfying gameplay loop that I loved so much in the previous chapter.Make no mistake, Blood West remains difficult as hell, but it is also always fair, which I feel a great sense of deliberateness behind. You can fool the game quite a few times (especially the AI), but it somehow adds to the immsim nature of the experience. The new location could be a bit more lush, a bit more green, but otherwise the swampy jungle environment is a perfect match to the overall tone of the game, as are the new enemy types. The NPCs are imaginative and pretty likeable too.What can I say. See you in the next chapter, Cowboy!ORIGINAL REVIEW:It is a "clicker" type of game. In the first half-ish hour it is janky, confusing, hard and unforgiving, and kind of a ♥♥♥♥♥, but as soon as it "clicks" with you, it suddenly becomes an addictive, highly entertaining, uniquely weird romp.It highly encourages and rewards exploration and stealthy, tactical gameplay. Okay, the blurb already says that this is a stealth horror game, but I cannot emphasize this enough! This is a hardcore stealth game, which becomes a shooter-RPG after several hours of play, grind, and looting. Don't expect the blood-pumping, explosive and frantic shooting of games like... Blood for example. This is a slow-paced game, where the blood-pumping part comes from the fact that your ammo is scarce, your health is small, your chances are always low and you are outnumbered and outmatched all the time. But this is the main hook of the game, because when you start to overcome the challenges with - relative - ease, the game becomes a true "soulsbornian" experience. For the devs: Just a few comments. The open-world design is fantastic and it works well, but the basic movement speed is very slow and the stamina - without special abilities of course - drains very quickly, which makes traveling long distances quite frustrating. The game doesn't communicate or make it in any way clear what the respawning of the opponents is based on. Okay, I only managed to die once, but I slept several times, and sometimes 1-2 enemies spawned again and others didn't and it wasn't clear what this was based on, making it a little difficult to plan ahead.I almost forgot: the two-weapon system is a terrible mistake. Even in real life, a man can carry two rifles and a pistol or an axe, a rifle and a pistol on him at the same time. In other words, it doesn't make the game immersive, it makes it seem like our protagonist is just clumsy... A 3 weapon system would override this nicely, then you could develop sets like axe, shotgun, pistol or rifle, shotgun, pistol, etc... That way you don't have to dig through your inventory during combat, which I've done several times while playing. Not a big addition, but it can alter the gameplay experience pretty significantly. Other than that fantastic work, keep it up!

_childDocuments_.review: This is easily one of the very best games of the year and one of the best indie games in recent memory.  Blood West is extremely punishing early on as you're learning how things work, but as you learn enemies and their weaknesses and engage with a surprisingly robust loot and progression system the game becomes a true masterpiece.Stealth is tense.  A great stealth game is all about careful, meticulous design.  Enemy placement needs to be just so.  Patrols need to be just so.  Enemy behavior has to be punishing enough to keep you nervous, but forgiving enough to not make the game a tedious slog.Blood West is one of the very best stealth games of the last 20 years.  Atmosphere, music, sound design are top notch.  Combat is fantastic.  Progression is fantastic.  Enemy design, encounter design, it's  all meticulously crafted to make every moment of sneaking feel tense and high risk.The economy is perfectly balanced, loot and artifacts and weapons require real, meaningful choices and trade offs.I struggle to think of how this game could be any better.  Some people are going to bounce off this game hard in the first 3 hours because it's highly punishing early as you scrounge for ammo and money but once you clear that hurdle you're treated to a masterful design.I hope this thing sells a bajillion copies and this developer gets to keep making games just like this one.A triumph of a game.
_childDocuments_.name: Blood West

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome and unique experience. Great value for the $$$.It took me about an hour of somewhat frustrating play to get into it, since I'm normally more into standard FPS shooters, but it's a ton of fun after you get the learning curve and feel for it. This isn't a run-and-gun game. Patience and stealth is essential.I found the save system quite unusual. You can't just hit F6 for a quick save. You can manually "save and quit", or it auto-saves when you die. There is no "save, make a mistake / die and then re-load to a previous point" possible, all gameplay is permanent. BUT, they make it enjoyable and fairly easy to make up for your deaths and mistakes so you can carry-on.The inventory system is well-designed and the items/weapons and artifacts are well balanced so far. Good work devs, I can't wait to play more.

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy Weird West aesthetics and atmosphere, and at the same time crave that "Skyrim Stealth Archer" experience, you'll find Blood West to be immensely satisfying. All-out fights are brutal and you'll find the reliance on stealth and resource management to be your key weapons.In terms of aesthetics, the game utilises its limited graphical fidelity in a precise and efficient way; the monsters are unique with interesting designs, the weapons satisfying to use, and the world surrounding you appropriately distressed and depressing.

_childDocuments_.review: The game seems to be cool, but the 2nd act does not work for me, well, more precisely, there are no enemies or characters, just a "free" (invisible walls) world with loot. After switching to the 2nd location, it was saved and exited, after loading it was written that your save was corrupted, we loaded the current save from somewhere ....Very interesting of course, but this is the maximum stupidity not to give a choice of a save cell, even when moving to the next location. Basically game broken for me, thanks for the beta test.At least they would ask after defeating the boss of act 1: "Do you want to stay in this location or move on to the next one?", hardcore and broken saves are all included.I got stuck in textures a couple of times, once I fell under the map near some cactus or stone, who will play, carry 1-2 sticks of dynamite with you, they really help to get out.In a single player game with 1 locked save, yeah..., in case of such bug, no thanks, it's better to play Tarkov.Yes, yes, I know, start a new game again, next time nothing will break, thanks, but no, the whole act 1 of replaying it is ridiculous.By the way, about the boss, I won't say that it was difficult to crawl through the tunnels, but where is any incentive to win, a trophy, a weapon, anything? In general, no satisfaction from victory, the boss died and died, we go to the next location ...Conditional game map restrictions: In the desert mountains and cliffs are okay; in the swamp, there should be an abyss and mountains, at least as a limitation or depth of immersion. The game is very raw, and move away from invisible walls, it ruins the atmosphere.In total.Of the minuses: Invisible walls; lack of screensavers after the events; the inability to choose a save cell in a single game (I'm not asking for a free save, there are enough saves at totems, in case of bugs, crashes and other breakdowns to another cell, and not to save and exit on one); the plot and lore of the game; perks repeat each other in value and more than half are absolutely useless; few useful potions, for the whole game I used only healing ones, everything else was not useful.From the good: Juicy headshots; jumping and running mechanics; weapon reload mechanics; mechanics of healing and bleeding; shooting; different types of cartridges; garbage collection (I would classify this as a minus, but since it is already in every game, so it's all the same); Infinite stash inventory (thank you for that, it's rare in some games, but why doesn't the first totem in the game have it?).While the game is not recommended, maybe after patches and near release version.

_childDocuments_.review: Giving this game a thumbs down should be a criminal offense. If you're a fan of horror, S.T.A.L.K.E.R., a little bit of immersive sim, and retro style, this game is a fantastic romp.EDIT: I feel the need to address some people in the reviews here that are giving some pure misinformation and haven't made it past the first area. Respawning enemies aren't unending. When you die, some enemies respawn, mostly smaller easy to kill mobs. I won't say it doesn't happen, but I personally only went up against harder enemies again a couple times after dying, and those were in "secret" or bonus areas you don't normally frequent. If the enemies didn't respawn at all on your death, the game would have zero difficulty, and turn empty.Combat requires you to learn how the enemies and weapons work. If you're a brain dead idiot that wants to run n gun, or if you think you should be able to just hack away at enemies blindly without getting hit back, that's on you. You start out weak, but stealth isn't mandatory. You also find artifacts, and get experience to upgrade your stats and abilities as you play, so you definitely don't stay weak, either.Maybe if they made a baby mode for people with no penalties for dying you stupid dipwads would enjoy it more? Yes I'm being edgy, you people are playing a game clearly not for you and whining about it, while blatantly lying about what's in it because you barely played the f***ing game.

_childDocuments_.review: Desperado Zombie FPS with a small amount of souls-like. Every death is punishing in that some slain enemies return and you get a piece of a curse. While dying can be avoided with the correct supplies, dying and receiving a curse can also be avoided by equipping a coin that blocks the negative effects (and these coins are everywhere). So the people complaining that the game is too challenging/punishing with death mechanics need to spend more than a minute learning about the items/planning out their strategies. (After all ammo, dynamite, molotovs, and even rocks can be used to your advantage) After you get a specific headshot perk and the repeater rifle, the game becomes far more fun and manageable. But the first hour or so of gameplay is dependent on how well you can assess a situation and sneak around threats that need more than a simple axe wound to bring them down.Absolutely loved my time in this one though, so if you are looking for a decent challenge or just love FPS/souls games I think this one is worth it. Especially with the additional maps coming soon.I cannot wait for the new maps to release personally because this game kept me very hooked.If interested my playthrough is here: Edit: (11/3/22) I have just completed the Swamp map, a terrifying new addition to Blood West. All enemies are tougher than their canyon brothers. The evils of the Swamp are far more cunning as well, with much deadly tricks up their disgusting sleeves. I loved this map, although it does take some getting used too. The swamp is far bigger than the canyon map, more densely populated with bullet sponge enemies, and almost any encounter has the potential to go wrong quickly. To my desperado friends I'd suggest the golden rule of the undead, two shots to the head. Also known as the double tap.I had a considerable amount of glitches while running through this map (although I did play through it in the 4 days or so that it was updated), Several enemies did not spawn until they were within 15 meters of me, The end boss of this area got stuck in a tree and I couldn't shoot or damage it in any way, some enemies appeared seemingly out of nowhere even in cleared areas, and although this isn't a bad glitch at one point the game allowed me to infinitely shoot flame short ammo out of my revolver for some reason. These issues broke my immersion hard for awhile, but Blood West is still one of my favorite games to come out of 2022 and I continue to look forward to the last map coming soon, The Mountains, especially since the Swamp leaves you on a cliffhanger ending....

_childDocuments_.review: The stealth mechanic is a meter that fills up the closer you get to enemies, even if they're not looking at you (why???). To sneak up on someone, you crouch and slow walk up to them while the meter fills, and then you must completely stop moving to make the meter go down. So, it's slowly creep up, then stop and wait, and then slowly creep up, and then stop and wait...until you get close enough to attack. And you better get a headshot because you're screwed otherwise. Sound like fun to you? I've played Deus Ex MD, all the DIshonored games, Prey, most of the MGS games, and Hitman WOA. Blood West wants to be a stealth game but its stealth system doesn't reflect any of the refinements developers have made over the years in stealth mechanics. I have no problem with an alternative take on a stealth game but I do have a problem if the alternative take is much worse than what I've already experienced. If you like how stealth was done in the other games I mentioned, then the stealth mechanics of this game may be so problematic for you that all the other things the game has to offer won't even matter. That's how it was for me.You're punished with ability debuffs when you die, there's no quicksave, you can only save and quit, there's only one save file, and you can't save scum. These things don't pair well with stealth mechanics and they inhibit experimentation if you're not a masochist.My brain works very differently than the brains of people who like this game, and that's okay. There's plenty of room for games like Blood West and I'm glad that the people who like games like this have the opportunity to enjoy it. However, if you're anything like me, save yourself some money and frustration, and look elsewhere for that itch you thought you might scratch by playing this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Short version - if you like STALKER games, than Blood West is the best STALKER-like you can play and in many ways much better than its inspiration. Obviously Blood West doesn't inherit the setting of STALKER, but it does an amazing job with bringing its own version of Weird Western to life.The strongest element of Blood West is its immersive gameplay. Its a mix of stealth and FPS, with plenty of RPG elements, including inventory management, leveling up and perk selection. Stealth is encouraged but not mandatory, as there are many viable playstyles, thanks to well balanced perks and itemization. You want to play as bow and tomahawk wielding warrior - go ahead! Want to use cursed artifacts to take advantage of some crazy synergies and one shot most enemies - knock yourself out! Personally I prefer a good old gunslinger with a touch of stealth-sniping using crossbow, with a Buffalo rifle stowed in one of my backpacks for taking down bigger monsters.There are three chapters to play through, each set in a different region. You start in desert Canyons, your classic Western setting, filled with ruined churches, abandoned farms and mines. After that you move to the Swamps, which are even larger and more varied than the Canyons. You will encounter completely different structures and enemies in each chapter, which took me completely by surprise when starting Chapter 2. When I finished Chapter 1 I was feeling pretty confident and felt I had a good grasp of the mechanics of Blood West. Boy, was I wrong! Chapter 2 is when gloves come off. You will be facing much stronger foes, with very different behaviours, which will require you use every tool at your disposal to win. Chapter 3 will take you to the Mountains, for the finale of your adventure. This is the greatest challenge in the game and another shake up in the enemy roster (screw those Hellish Clots!). Enemies in Chapter 3 are TOUGH, one-shotting enemies from hiding won't work so well anymore. Demons and Hellbears will be a bane of your existence if you don't adapt.The sheer variety between each chapter is putting your usual triple-A game to shame. It feels perfectly balanced, each chapter offering something completely different and constantly challenging the player. Blood West is a pretty challenging game, that punishes recklesness and requires you consider your approach.When you die in Blood West you are returned to your base camp, some enemies respawn, and you receive a random debuff to one of your abilities, dying three times in a row will result in a stronger debuff - the curse. There are ways of removing those debuffs, so you are not punished too severely and can improve your chances with good resource management. Its a well designed system, where death is punishing, but doesn't bring you back to square one.One of my favorite aspects of Blood West are the uniquely placed items. As far as I know there is no random loot, outside of drops from enemies, that means you won't be getting some crappy, luck dependent loot at the end of tough area. There are many unique weapon variants that posess special abilities to enhance your playstyle and these can be real game changers. Some of the strongest weapons and artifacts can be purchased from merchants you encounter in each chapter. Their selection of goods is not randomised as well, so when you see some amazing rifle in shop, you can focus on gathering enough money to buy it. There are some ways to farm gold and greatly improve prices at shop, adding yet another layer of depth to the mechanics. It reminds me a lot of old Infinity Engine games, like Baldurs Gate or Icewind Dale, these also had hand-placed loot that felt so much more satisfying to find than the random crap games like Cyberpunk 2077 are showering you with.Only complaints I have are about the story and the lack of polish when it comes to quests in Chapter 3. Story is forgettable, with rather basic dialogues and characters. Its not offensive, but I started to ignore it by the end of Chapter 2. There are some good stories to be found on notes scattered around the world, like murderous chickens or the story of 'flying' locomotive. My problem with Chapter 3 is the inconvenient placement of your main camp and the storage chest. Its placed at the western edge of the map, unlike the camps in previous chapters that were placed in the center. This makes for a very out of the way base and considering all the looting you'll be doing, it makes for a tedious trip.I really like the visuals of Blood West, it has a pixelated look, but you don't really notice it from afar and things appear more detailed than they are. Overall vibe is perfect for this setting, thanks to great ambience and music. Areas could be a bit brighter or have a touch more vibrant colors, but I guess that would ruin the aesthetic. Enemy models are perfect, there is a ton of enemy types, each of the appropriately creepy and/or scary. Trust me, when you see a Hellbear charging at you, you'll get it.Overall I cannot recommend Blood West highly enough. It takes all the thing I loved about STALKER games and does them better and in a fantastically unique setting. I almost forgot about this game, as I didn't play it in early access, but now it has easily become one of my favorite games. You owe it to yourself to play Blood West, you get a lot of game at this price, it took me 31 hours to finish it once and I feel like I got way more than I paid for. I really hope Hyperstrange will continue with this type of games, as experiences like this are few and far between in barren wasteland of modern gaming.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't call this a "boomer shooter". It is something else entirely. It's a very unforgiving stealth shooter with a great atmosphere.You can find and buy items to give yourself an edge and customize build according to how you wish to play it.For instance, when you die some but not all monsters will respawn, if that bothers you there is an artifact you can carry that stops them from respawning, though farming monsters for EXP and loot is a viable strategy in the beginning, Some monsters will seem unfairly strong until you discover their weakness. But make no mistake, if you do these creatures will have you down in the dirt in no time. Head shots matter a great deal. I am really enjoying this game, it's not what I thought it would be and I couldn't be happier! This is an easy recommend if you like stealth and tough shooters.EDIT: After finishing the game I am actually sad that it's over. I really enjoyed this game. It felt like King's Field in the wild west. There is definitely a Fromsoft vibe here. Any complaint I've read in the negative reviews is actually addressable in the game. There are artifacts to counteract almost everything. Getting curses when dying? Pay a coin to the totem and get a status that will not curse you when you die. Also there are plenty of potions lying around that will cure cursed status as well. Coins are common as dirt and you wont run out. Tired of creatures respawning when you die? There is a very early game artifact that prevents that. The game does require skill and strategy and it is way more slow paced than some would like but in all honesty I loved this game and enjoyed every second in it. Progress felt so satisfying and getting to be more and more of a bad-ass as the game progressed felt earned.My only gripe is that my vision is not as good as it used to be and the game is pretty dark, but not dark enough to actually impact my play much.I want more!

_childDocuments_.review: Blood West is a gift that keeps on givin' - imho one of the more successful Early Access stories, and a game that can proudly stand shoulder-to-shoulder with Thief (to which it pays homage in abundance, both with its methodical gameplay and meticulously crafted levels). The theme is also flawlessly executed - I've heard a bunch of people saying that this game is not horror, but for us folks who try to beat the entire game without dying it surely is! Be it passing over (subjectively thin) rail with deadly precipice beneath, or dealing with a menacing enemy for the first time, or simply being caught off guard by the enemy due to inattention and subsequently running for the hills like a true yellowbelly - there have been MANY situations in my 6 hours of gameplay so far that made me sweat more than any 6-star HUNT: Showdown lobby, and I ain't even done with the Chapter I at that!The sounds are really well-done, especially the sounds of weaponry and enemies (both in their idle and alerted state), while the atmospheric music raises tension with each new area I explore. The VO is also stellar, with one-and-only Stephen Russell in the protagonist role (channeling this sort of an amalgamation of his snarky Garret and true-grit, grim-sounding Spaghetti Western gunslinger). The rest of the cast (while unknown to me) also gave their top performance, and judging from the trailers and snippets of gameplay from subsequent chapters, I gotta hand it to the rising star VA behind the skeletal Undead NPC - seldom can you hear a performance befitting of a character shown on the screen, and this guy nails it!As a whole package, Blood West (despite its somber, unsettling atmosphere) is quite clearly a labour of love, made by the devs which live and breathe the Thief Trilogy of games, and masterfully merged with a weird western theme that I simply adore beyond measure! I can't recommend this game enough, and I urge anybody who is into hardcore, brutal & methodical gameplay, Deus Ex RPG-level of character progression, and immersing themselves into the dark and foreboding atmosphere of wicked Wild West, to give this game a fair shake - I guarantee you that you won't be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: Very cool game. It reminds me somewhat of old school shooters like Blood in atmosphere and style, but with a heavy emphasis on stealth. I recommend it if you like survival horror, resource and inventory management, and exploration. If you are terrible at aiming then it might be a lot more difficult for you because the weapons  are not inherently powerful, you have to use them effectively.It took me about 7-8 hours to explore and do everything that I could and finish the main questline. A good amount of content for early access and the price point, and it seems like there's more zones and such to come. Looking forward to that.My biggest complaint was there wasn't much in the way of weapon variety, but it didn't necessarily take too much away from the core gameplay. A minor "issue" I had was that I pretty much had everything I needed about halfway through my playthrough and anything new I got was extra. I didn't have to think about ammo much at all besides deciding how much to carry so I had room to loot. I was also extremely efficient with my ammo and did a lot of melee stealth killing though, so that's going to vary a lot for people.Lastly, I'd like to add that I encountered ZERO BUGS, which is a very welcome change from most early access games. It's a very solid base and I hope that continues onward.8.5/10 - So far

_childDocuments_.review: This is without a doubt one of the best games I have played in recent memory, The two things Blood West does best is the Gunplay and the creepy atmosphere. The sounds for the Shotgun and Winchester are so satisfying, and the stealth mechanics are very polished. Blood West also features a Diablo-style tetris inventory which I've personally enjoyed. Blood West also has some light RPG mechanics like a leveling system with skill points to spend on perks to make you either more stealth focused or guns blazing. The only gripe I could even think of with this game is that the ladders can sometimes feel a bit janky when you're trying to hop off of them. Other than that this is a game I would recommend to just about any of my friends, this game is definitely worth the modest price as well as your time.Also, to whoever did this soundtrack. I want to kiss you on the mouth.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really awesome and I had a blast playing it. It's a solid blend of an FPS game with stealth set in the west. It's definitely more of an FPS at the end of the day though seeing as you can't avoid boss fights at the end of each chapter, but I went into it expecting something like that and was happy as I prefer to blast more than slink in the shadows. The game is largely regarded as "difficult" but in reality if you're smart and use all the different weapons, relics and consumables you get along the way there's usually a solution to anything you run into. Hell, even running is a solution if you have enough stamina.My only gripe really was with the voice acting of the main character. I heard his voice lines three times and set their frequency to "never" lol. It's truly very poor voice acting and sounds genuinely bad. That aside though, the weapons all feel great to use and I legitimately only will stop playing because I've done all there is to do. I just wish there were more!

_childDocuments_.review: Very well done. Pretty much everything you do feels rewarding, good environment and high difficulty. You should absolutely buy this game.We're in EA now--two things I would change/add. First: Our character yells a lot when they do things like jump/attack/kill something--which is fine most of the time, but it breaks the immersion quite a bit when you're stealth killing a baddie; especially if it's right next to another baddie that doesn't notice us yelling. I would add a new set of whisper/stealth sounds to use when the character is sneaking. I think it will improve the game dramatically more than you'd expect.Second: The AI behavior is a little weird sometimes. Enemies chain pull sometimes when you don't expect them to, and don't when you would--like if you just shot someone next to them for example. They don't seem react to loud gunshots that you would expect them to notice. I think maybe the issue is the way the enemies react to sound. It seems like the sound detection system is only based on the character's movement/ jumps--and gunshots don't seem to add enough to that soundbar. Changes to that could make an already difficult game much harder--so we should keep in mind some balance. Maybe some guns that have some kind of silencer or similar magic effect could be added.Thanks for reading :)

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best immersive stealth shooter I've ever played. If you don't read the rest of my review, get this game if you want a game to replace S.T.A.L.K.E.R. or if you're looking for a first-person souls-like. The game completely draws you in with an impressive audio and soundtrack, mysterious story and difficult-but-rewarding gameplay. There are even interesting characters in each chapter, though the land is mostly populated by hostile creatures. The weapon variety is adequate, and the level-up system is interesting. I loved the survival and inventory management aspects as well. You start the game with almost nothing, and if you're careful you can be pretty set by the end of the first chapter, or completely out of ammo and healing if you're not. I enjoyed every single session I played of this game, and explored nearly every inch of the map in all 3 levels/chapters. I wish I had something to scratch the itch that this game left me with, but I'll try my best by trying out Gloomwood. I doubt that it'll be as awesome as this.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent first person stealthy game with full player agency. Be as stealthy or loud as you want, attack from the main door or find an alternate path to pick enemies one by one from behind, lots of weapons to play with (don't worry, enemies in this game seem to have terrible hearing capabilities when it comes to extremely loud gunpowder weaponry so you can be stealthy AND have fun with guns at the same time believe it or not).The horror wild west mixture is fascinating and works beautifully as a setting. The music is very eerie, but it still has a classic spaghetti western guitar riffs every now and then, in the distance. The world seems to be apocalyptic and filled with monsters, and yet there's still friendly NPCs that offer you respite and sell you items and all that good stuff. It's all very surreal and intriguing. Can't recommend it enough. I wish more games like this were made more often. There really is nothing quite like taking a moment to plan your next raid to the next location you'll head to.

_childDocuments_.review: If you want an action horror game with a focus on stealth then you'll probably like this. It's kind of a little bit like System Shock in the Wild West, with a low-res pixellated aesthetic like Valheim. It's definitely not a run and gun FPS though, and you'll die very quickly if you try to play it like a straight up action game. If you want to stay alive you'll need planning, recon, and quick reflexes, because each enemy is capable of killing you with 2 or 3 hits. Buy it if you appreciate difficulty and don't mind a slower paced FPS with more of a stealth focus.

_childDocuments_.review: I can decidedly, positively recommend this game, but you should  still wait for a < 20€ sale.I'm always a sucker for first person 'immersion sims' and this is kinda the "sort of singleplayer Hunt Showdown" I was craving. The enemy design - both visual and functional - really makes this game pop, as does the art style.Enemies have certain weaknesses and traits. Not as expansive as I could wish for, but it's there in principle.Low poly, unfiltered pixel texture has been done to death for some people, but when it's done this well and cohesive, I can eat it up any day. The sound design is pretty well done as well - guns sound powerful, enemies give unique & identifiable sound cues and interaction sounds are nice. Sadly the ingame music is a bit barren - what's there is okay, but it's not much of it to begin with, and no ambience background tracks to speak of...You should probably also turn the player character quips down to "infrequent" at most - they occur way too often, and aren't thematically queued - it's just a general pool of one liners that wears you out pretty early on.The progression & death system with it's perks and penalties is a bit low on the ground, but the legendary and cursed weapons and trinkets, the different ammo types and overall consumbale & resource management more than make up for it.Collecting Loot and satisfying my grid-inventory OCD. Guns feel weighty, clunky and .Meele is a desperate last resort or a daring head on assault. A basic stealth system without canned takedown animations. Yeah, it can devolve into "skyrim stealth archer" gameplay if you're basing your build on that, but it doesn't  to - it's efficient though.One can still dream what a game with more budget and time would've made out of this principle - more complex enemy traits and behaviors, deeper environmental interaction, etc etc.But what's here is still really really cool.

_childDocuments_.review: Very good and polished game, its short mind you but i expect once the full launch is out you will get more than enough for the asking price.The campaign is around 6-12 hours based on your experience,patience and if you want to complete all the zones and go search in all the nooks and crannies for the unique weapons.I experienced no crashes or major bugs, there are some frame drops and minor text glitches as to be expected in any game but nothing that breaks the experience.In case the devs are reading these i suggest that: you put an FOV slider in the game, put some brightness settings because sometimes its hard to see items or highlight them more and in the darker insides you may seem lost at times and finally i for one feel that the game needs a more hardcore mode because once you know and have enough levels you start just mowing everything down.These are my opinions of course but i feel these are the only nitpicks i can have with the game, overall a solid experience and if you like these kind of old style/retro shooters you def need to give this a shot and even for those not into retro experiences like myself i feel you should still give it a try, this is a 9+/10 game so have fun with it.Update 1: The devs have listened and added an FOV slider and Brightness, waiting for the more hardcore mode maybe one death and you are out or you must fight in the spirit world to get back in the real one.This is on the road to becoming a must buy so il start nitpicking everything i can on this next play so we can make this game even better.BTW: An actual Roadmap would not hurt at all keep up the good work!Update:Roadmap was shows ,tons up updates reworks, buggs solved and im sure many more to come.This is a must buy for all those you like these styles of games!

_childDocuments_.review: Blood West is broken up into 3 chapters, each has different theme/characters and enemies. As you are giving missions its very easy to get distracted exploring caves or cabins and being rewarded by finding special items with interesting properties to change how you play.One of the things I really appreciate is that 90% enemies that can be killed with one shot, which makes the slow firing guns feel impactful and adds tension to each shot, especially when panicking The difficulty curve starts off harsh, but you can game the system with the correct choice of talents at the start of the game. You feel very powerful clearing big groups of enemies with ease until you miss that one shot and realize how fragile the player character is.The inventory management is a grid based system like RE4 attache case, but it gets a bit cumbersome when you find extra bags and you effectively have several inventories within your main inventory. I hope they'd redo this system entirely.I can't say I'd replay this game, but I'd be buying a sequel without much thought.
