_childDocuments_.review: This game has some nice ideas packaged in some really old western paper and wrapped with barbed wire. Here are the problems:--- The devs present the game as a stealth game and compare it to Thief but there is barely a well done stealthsystem there. Enemies wont investigate or sniff you out, they will just know where you are and pinpoint the perfect path to you no matter where you are. Really not fun to play with.All enemies act in the same way, they will run to corpses when they see them, this is weird as some enemies are clearly mindless and others even use guns and are clearly still intelligent... what is going on with that, should there not be a difference? On the other hand: A nice detail is that dogmonsters will feed on their fallen comrades but this get soured because they will just know that there is a corpse nearby and rush to it. This will surprise you the first few times and ruin the stealth with them just showing up.The detection in this game works as follows:> when you are visible it will raise a, on screen, detection bar> when you are being heard it will use the same shared bar> When you stand still and the enemy cant hear  see you then the bar will go down.So far so good, right? Well then, walls dont obstruct enemy hearing so your meter goes up at all times in some areas because there are enemies all around you. This does not make sense. Enemyvision is also always the same, there is a lean mechanic but if they see a fraction of your body guess what the meter goes up! In the same speed as just openly standing there by the way in case that was not clear. What kind of system is that??There are also no hiding spots or anything. Not that those would help they will know where you are and get you as soon as you are detected... It is  bare bones. When you shoot, depending on your postiion, no one will react to it as long as the targeted enemy dies. They wont react and investigate. If you are visible to an enemy while shooting another they will detect you thou.--- Weapon handling is at best okay, ranged weapons are a little weird when aiming where they glitch a little before you properly go into aiming down sights, the guns move to the side of the screen first instead of moving up and going into the aiming position. Very weird, did seriously no one notice that? Seems to happen mostly when pulling a gun out.The sway of the weapons is horrible and you literally have to use skillpoints to counteract that only somewhat (or find legendary / cursed weapons that have a bonus to that). There is no breathing mechanic where you breathe out (use stamina) to aim much more calmly and maybe even zoom in a little. This will make you miss many vital shots.A fair amount of enemies have their head in slightly lower / awkward postions as they are not human or once were human. This makes shooting them even harder without any zoom. Not to mention that enemies, when transitioning animations, will do some really sudden and jerky movements. Making accurate shots impossible when you need them. Just imagine aiming at an enemy that approaches a corpse of a fallen comrade and you take aim only for the enemy to switch tracks and switch positions because a new animation has started. Frustrating.Melee weapons cant be swung continuously, this would be somewhat alright if it only was the heavy attack but the light one cant be queued and therefore you cant stunlock weaker enemies. It is really frustrating. They also will eat attacks like bacon & eggs for breakfast once you are out of stealth. They are soooo tanky. No blocking or dodging in the game either, so yeah open combat is not welcome here but the stealth is trash...Once you are out of stealth you are screwed except if you have lots of ammo and a shotgun and even then when there is big enemies or lots of ranged ones they will just slaughter you. Why devs? You also need your ammo for the really healthy bosses by the way.The enemies also have no leash, they will follow you to the end of the world and they will know every shortcut to take in order to get to you faster. Have fun, running is  an option, you are the only one with limited stamina.I just now have engaged what is essentially a miniboss and I hopped on a wall because I was spotted through a crack in the surrounding area and I was not prepared to take it on. And well that thing was able to hit me in melee even thou I was 3 maybe 4m above it. The phantomrange on the enemies does not only go in front of them it also goes above. The devs needs to seriously step up their game. This is bad.Oh and there is a glitch which makes the doublebarrel fire only one shot and then you are out even when you are fully reloaded... How is this game sitting at 80% positive. So many problems.--- Enemies have pinpoint accuracy when shooting and never seem to run out of ammo or need to reload... not fair. They play by different rules.- Level design is okay, dont expect amazing encounter design like in soulsgames, this game is very open in its world building and you can approach completely freely. But there is a lot of empty space in most areas. If they had hiding places and perhaps things that could be used as traps or distractions against enemies this would be more fun and dynamic. Oh and there is a distinct lack of cover in lots of areas but tons of enemies in it, not that it matters once you are detected that would get in the way of you running or attempting to run.I think adding a crafting system and filling the void with materials to harvest would be smart. Let us create bait to fling in an enemycamp and watch as dogs or werewolves tear them apart as an example, let me trap an area to ensure that the enemy that will see me take out its brethren will die or get immoblized, please!!A weathersystem to add to the stealth would be nice and also dynamic enemy encounters depending on the weather. Have some enemies only appear when it is raining for example.+ Enemydesigns are mostly fine, a little repetetive so far maybe. Overall there are some great ideas here, for example blind enemies and some other spoilery things. Spiritenemies need a tight leash and despawn after they do their attackmove, this would make encounters with enemies that spawn them in in unlimited amounts bearable. They are also very hard to hit.++ There are bosses and they are okay, the second one was okay and the first one is my favorite so far.++ The skillsystem is okay and could perhaps be expanded, overall it gives you some freedom with how to approach the stealthsystem, now if only that system would also work well... the legendary weapons and other items will add to that. For some reason there are clothing items but no clothing slots, only artifactslots. 3 at that. So you have to choose carfully.+/- Weapons and artifacts that can be bought from vendors are very expensive, on the third map it costs 18.000 for a legendary rifle that barely drops ammo when looted from enemies. No sniping for you I guess. has amazing damage thou. I did a fair amount of farming in the other levels for these items as well and it drags soo much, this will raise your playtime to over 20h as well.+/- Your storagechest is unlimited but that was not clear for me, if you reach "capacity" you can still doubleclick items into it and then sort the mess. Good to know, I sadly have sold some of items thinking that I needed to pick and choose... You also cant go back to old maps, boooo!

_childDocuments_.review: You can tell this game was made with a lot of love. It is a mix between Stalker, Bioshock, and a little scent of Dark Souls, with a Dark Fantasy Western Setting. What's not to like?The gameplay loop is basically to grab a quest and jump to explore the open world. The best approach is usually stealth, but later on, you can still go guns blazing.The music is really good, and even if the graphics aren't realistic at all, have a really nice charm to swallow you into the atmosphere of the game.  I consider this game a hidden gem. totally recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: I've completed chapter 1, so please take my comments with that caveat.Like other games that have earned many hours of play, there was a difficult beginning to our courtship, but like XCOM and Thief classic series, I am glad I persisted. Like Thief, this is not a guns blazing fps, it's a slow, deliberate and stealthy game that will result in you holding your breath as you crouch in the dark as a toothy fiend inches closer to you. Criticisms? I think the enemies ability to find you once alerted is a little too prescient, and it is possible to trick their pathfinding with careful vertical placement. Not a dealbreaker by any means.Particular kudos to the ending of chapter 1. No spoilers, but it does show some thoughtful design. On to Chapter 2

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game. It really scratched the stealth itch and was very atmospheric and fun. The environments were detailed and interesting, the horror-themed enemies were quirky and cool, and just generally I am a fan of the western theme. My favourite scenario was the original canyons, which I've been playing since early access. I was so happy when a tumbleweed went spinning by as I was creeping through the moonlit town.I suppose it is a difficult game which punishes you for dying, thus rewarding a more cautious/conservative gameplay style, but, once you figure out how the enemies work and level up a few times, then the stealth gameplay does get a little bit easy and stale. On the other hand, if you try to go in all guns blazing you'll probably get rapidly destroyed as the enemies often do a lot of damage very quickly. Fighting more than one enemy at a time, for instance, can be very difficult especially if the space is confined. I think this is just the unavoidable trade-off for a game like this. The story is interesting, though not always clearly told. The voice-acting is cheesy but great. I really enjoyed listening to the dialogue of the totem, the priest, the doctor and the shaman in particular. There has been a lot of attention put into the world-building which I appreciate, while at the same time maintaining a nice sense of mystery throughout.Probably the biggest weakness were the boss fights for me. Quite a lot of build-up, but then culminating in a big clumsy sort of monster, but ultimately a fairly easy fight. Because I stockpiled so much ammo, the last boss went down very quickly. The journey up to the boss fight is really what makes the game fun for me. Overall, a great game!

_childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly good game, I was initially judging it by screenshots and realized my mistake only after playing it. Pros: Amazing sound design. Visuals look great. Enemy designs are quite creative and most of the enemies feel different. Great big maps with a lot of little holes and caves to explore. My favorite thing was that no matter where I went, I always found *something*, in every tiny room and every cave. Exploration really feels great here.Cons:Pretty uncomplicated stealth system and enemy AI, can be cheesed somewhat easily. Story is basically "Cleanse the evil, don't ask questions". Got plenty of different weapons and "loud" perks, but because of sheer enemy amounts and their damage, you're expected to sneak and kill silently. Maybe will add more after completion.UPD: Yeah, finished it in 15 hrs. Great game, absolutely recommend getting it, especially if its on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Short version: Buy this game.  It's fun, easy to learn and provides a challenge.Long version:This game is a lot of fun.  It's not a fast paced shooter, and requires a bit trial-by-fire to get used to it.  It's not an unfair game - most of the time when you die, it's because you messed up.  Running away can be part of your strategy to lure enemies to their deaths!- Visually spectacular (I LOVE the texel pixel density consistency *chefs kiss*).- Difficulty can vary, .- Relatively easy to learn monsters, environments, items, and controls.- Audio/sound is pretty good and hints at what's around (and locale specific sounds are a nice touch).- Audio/music is there and you don't even notice it (ie. perfect).- Cool monster designs and features, x1000 for the sexy monsters.- , but some very minor changes?- I'd like a little more generic ambient noise, like wind, a creak in the wood, a scuttle of a bug.  The tumbleweed doesn't seem to have any noise either :(  Unless it's there and my tinnitus and partially deaf left ear aren't registering it?- Environments are detailed "just enough" to be interesting but not overwhelming, which makes you look for items.  Locations are spaced out enough not to be too far which I appreciate.  It can look/feel a little empty at a distance though.- It's hard to tell where to go sometimes - if you like exploring the entire world before continuing with the main quest, then I guess this is perfect.- Auto-sorting inventory is based on size, and there's no way to change it, but adding multiple ways might make it more complicated and Blood West is a nice level of "simple".  Sure you can re-arrange it manually, but when you are trying to quickly swap weapons in combat with a full inventory, auto-sort by size is probably the only way you won't die.- It would be nice if you could use the - Some areas I've explored don't have anything in them except some enemies - not sure if they are quest related or not - and considering they weren't easy to get into, I was expecting at least some ammo to pick up.- It's hard when you start out, but easy once you learn everything (which is pretty easy).- 1 hour in, I'm dying constantly.- 2 hours in, I'm (carefully) slaughtering baddies because I'm using items and the environment properly with run-hide-stealth-sneakattack/headshot tactics.- 3 hours in I die cause I got greedy and made some stupid mistakes (full inventory, missed a sneak attack, climbed up high forgetting enemy had ranged attack, lost $100 from an item ability).- There are various item effects and curses that "punish" you - but they are either temporary or can be removed.- Exploring the open world is great, and there are some awesome challenges with  a nice item at the end, but for me this early in the game it's hard to tell if these places are there just challenge seekers to get through.  I'm not sure on the value of pushing through these areas for non-committed players though.  I guess you can just explore to find more stuff to sell to buy better gear!- Everything is designed with a purpose, and they all work together nicely to create a "realistic" but playable challenge.- People compare Blood West to Dark Souls.  I despise Dark Souls - as a player, I don't want to memorise where to stand and time enemy animations.  If you want to make that comparison, then consider Blood West an easy "lite" version of Dark Souls (but actually fun).- Hint for easier kills: - Hint for instant kills:   It would be nice to know if the sneak-heavy-attack is supposed to be instant kill or not, and whether or not different melee weapons change instant kill (I don't want to find out the hard way).

_childDocuments_.review: As I had a lot of fun with this game, I would like to share my impressions of Bloodwest. I personally classify Bloodwest as a "souls-like" stealth shooter. If the player dies, he wakes up at a fixed spawn point and with him some already defeated enemies, but he keeps his equipment. Unless you had a protective coin or similar equipped, the player receives a temporary stackable penalty on death in the form of negative skills, e.g. reduced stamina. The always fair gameplay is designed to move slowly and tactically through the game world and complete small missions. Most of the time, this missions involve retrieving a special quest item. There's a bit of a lack of inspiration here. The game comprises a total of  extensive maps/chapters with plenty of incentive to explore. It is important to mention that after defeating one of the level bosses, you immediately move on to the next chapter, so weapons, items etc. should be collected/purchased beforehand, as there is no return journey.In my opinion, the enemy design is very creative and it was exciting to discover the weaknesses and strengths of the individual enemies in each chapter, even if some enemy types merely represent an iterative development of known ones as the game progresses. In my playthrough, I skilled the protagonist for stealthy close combat and targeted revolver handling. However, the skill tree also allows for other play styles, which I did not try out. The moderately demanding, very good gameplay and a carefully crafted game world give Bloodwest an unmistakable uniqueness in my opinion. I also praise the audio presentation, the atmospheric background music and the specific sound effects of the enemy types reinforce the situational depth of the game and contribute significantly to the creation of an atmospheric density. In particular, the band performance in the epilogue after the third act felt like an additional reward.Bloodwest is undoubtedly a little gem that will hopefully get the attention it deserves thanks to its stylish and timeless design. As an Early Access buyer, I'm pleased to see that the finalization has produced such a well-rounded result. Good work!

_childDocuments_.review: Very rarely, if ever, do you come across a game that feels like it was made for you specifically.A western survival horror/stealth shooter/treasure looty game, as if Hunt: Showdown was made into a singleplayer game.It's hard to describe how much I adore this game. It's a masterpiece that is a little rough around the edges, just like the old westerns.Now that I've sung it's praises, it does have a few cons:1:The inventory system could use a little more polish, like letting you swap item positions without needing to have more open space in the pack and auto rotate items to make them fit. Needing to make room horizontally when it could fit vertically is annoying.2:A few more guns of each type wouldn't hurt, as weapons just get outclassed by in further acts. Also having some guns be cursed just makes you not want to use them because the un-cursed alternatives can be just as good. It's just more of a nuisance than anything else.3:I want more. I love the gameplay and atmosphere so much, I just want more of it. Expansions, DLC, whatever please just make more. I want it.Also more Gianni Matragrano please. I love my funny little totem man.

_childDocuments_.review: I had a great time with this game. Pros:1. Guns and headshots feel excellent and are incredibly visceral, in turn, dealing with each enemy appropriately feels rewarding. The answer is usually a headshot, but you'll get caught in many situations where you need to carefully headshot and be very mobile while headshotting.2. The atmosphere and environment are great and look excellent with the art design and graphics. I've been on a bit of a retro kick and the graphics really are delightful as you move through this world.3. Enemy variety is pretty good, we see some reskins, but they're coded a little different.4. Exploration is pretty satisfying as you come across more and more things to sell and equip. There is a con associated with this below.Cons1. SPOILERS -- From a narrative standpoint, the final chapter is a little silly. We're a bad ass reanimated undead who can take down all kinds of evil. Yet we keep falling/messing up and need to be reconstructed by our homie? Also, I think I got a little lost with why our Soul dude wanted us to kill the evil he was apart of? Maybe he wanted to absorb the souls for himself and needed us to do it?2. The skill tree feels really lackluster after your first 4 decent skills, which in turn makes leveling feel less and less valuable. After you get those initial perks you don't really need anything else.3. Money is in a weird spot, you kind of need a tremendous amount of it initially for your good stuff and then suddenly you have infinite money and need none of it. I finished the game with around 35k after buying ammo and a couple of things from the stores that mattered.4. Exploration outside of it for explorations sake gets less relevant when you realize you need no more money, you don't need any more XP, and your guns are perfectly good for what you need.Additional note: AI is fine. We have to remember we're mostly fighting monsters, undead, and people have given up their souls. They don't need to be geniuses, they react to sound and will swarm you given the chance. It feels very satisfying to play against it for the most part.

_childDocuments_.review: Slow paced stealth gaming. The stealth system is fun, but not realistic. The enemy can either hear or see you. If they see you, you're basically caught unless u break LOS, and if they can hear you, you just crouch and stop moving to get the bar to go back to zero. You don't need a silencer for some reason. You can blast a shotgun right next to an enemy that isn't far, and so long as you kill the enemy you shot at, no one hears it. It's a fun little system that isn't overly complicated, and I enjoy it.You build your character and choose your weapons, so there is potential for multiple playthroughs. However, if you pick a weaker build, you might have trouble with that character at the start of chapter 2. I do believe there are balance issues, depending on what weapons you choose to go for.You can get easily frustrated with this game if you aren't slow and deliberate. If you want to play faster, it is possible, but you need to aim for the head. Don't miss, get gud, rip n tear.

_childDocuments_.review: Great atmosphere, the combat is really meaty and the resource management doesn't get annoying.The game has kinda weird difficulty curve right now.You can easily oneshot 90% of the enemies while sneaking for most of the game making it a breeze, but when the game introduces the end game enemies you gotta finally start thinking. Blood West could really use some enemies that are in between insta killable weaklings and unkillable tanks.Edit: After playing the second episode, I can safely say that the difficulty, enemy toughness and enemy numbers have risen considerably. makes the game more interesting IMO, since you can't always rely on sneak + headshot insta kill combo anymore.You also get to do some proper exploring and investigation, no stick skull just telling you what to do the instant you start up. NPCs have gotten more intresting, too.All in all, very happy with this update.

_childDocuments_.review: This game requires an odd bit of grinding early on to get an item or two that make life significantly easier. I also think it might be too easy to get screwed if you die too much and are no longer able to lift curses. The item needed is too infrequent, at least at first. That said, I've found the difficult game loop pretty addictive and played a good four hours before taking a break. The general vibe and look is pretty cool, too, and I think I'll keep plugging away at it some more (tomorrow). I think if world items respawned even randomly, the game would be a lot more compelling for more casual players.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok. Final release. What we got here.... ah nice artwork style, sounds and music, what else? Tarkov inventory with a lot of Tetris gameplay, some of you will like it. We got gore, we got 50% useful skills, others don't needed ever. And most importantly - we got gameplay - it's average, really, I spent 14 hours and it's always stealthy gameplay. Only headshots, or you waste all your ammo in 1–2 monsters. What a garbage idea. I really don't like it. Full gameplay depending only on stealth or you will be punished badly! Oh, and - all maps are dark, like in a coal mine. No lantern or anything - you can only turn Gamma high.MAP 1 - Classic western type. Pretty pleasant map.  I understand that in early stages like Map 1 (I will call them Maps) we got apocalyptic situation with only 2 survivors, and that's OK. Low on ammo, adrenaline, horrors everywhere, and you're completely inexperienced with rusty guns. After 3 hours, you will get better equipment and Skills. You already know how to kill every type of monster on these Map 1. Ok, I'm ready to roll. Next Map....MAP 2 ♥♥♥ Swamps. "We hate this place" Totem (Our Ally who bring us back into these Apocalypse) hate this place. I'm totally understood you, buddy.We got the couple of new monsters here. And the most horrible and ♥♥♥ broken - Skin collector. Fat bastard that can outrun you. Broken - you can shoot in him, but hitboxes become broken while he's running on you. I died because of this 4 times. I shoot exactly in the center of his body - no splashes of blood. Nothing.Other fiends are ok.Last boss, not even a challenge. Stupid walking sponge that you can kill with 7 shots with nitro.... Boring.Positive side: I'm glad that they add some characters. That's all.MAP 3 Mountains. The worst design. The worst monsters, the worst..... I'm really tired of "bring that item and come back"New monsters (Bat dudes) - are the most disgusting among them. After their death, they spawn ♥♥♥ leech that flies toward your face, and eating  around 30 hp. That's a lot. And even if you kill them with STEALTH - they know where to fly. Disgusting.  Kojima stop with your stealth ♥♥♥♥ please.Final boss... and ending.SPOILERSSo. I'm very disappointed. When it was EA only 1 Map that was enough. And that ending, and f up characters. I really don't know how to react. 5 Out of 10.I'm not recommend. Waste your time somewhere else.

_childDocuments_.review: A game that takes all the good aspects of a bethesda game and scraps the garbage. Carry weight? nope. Crafting? god no. Picking up EVERYTHING? only the shiny stuff. It basically makes a game out of being a stealth archer but instead you use guns and melee.Keep in mind I've only played the first act.Pros:-Excellent stealth system with visible indicator feedback.-Economy that scales well offering a challenging start without making it grindy later.-Ambiance creates a very spooky experience, i play with goosebumps whenever i'm in a new area.-Many "will that kill me" moments. (often the answer is yes, i recommend dynamite.)-A Diablo style inventory system that suits the game very well, providing limited but expandable on-person inventory to promote a survival feel, and an infinite (i think) stash at camp that lets you hoard all the things.Cons:-Graphics are dated, and while they have grown on me and i actually think they suit the game perfectly, they can be off-putting to others.-Its very hard to see the path of my projectiles, especially while ADS, making me miss shots way more than i prefer, and it becomes hard to judge the spread of the shotgun.-I have no clue how the enemy respawn system works, because sometimes a whole area will be respawned when i return after just a few minutes, while some enemies seem to take forever to respawn, or it will only half respawn an area. seriously what's the deal with it.-No indicators of where special weapons or accessories are. they can be in VERY obscure places, and a subtle hint to them in conversation with one of the NPCs or a note that says something about them would go a long way.-Very few side quests, after the first couple side quests in act 1 you just stop getting any more, there's almost no direction given to non plot-progressive content.Overall a great game so far. I'll see after act 2 if i need to make changes to this.
_childDocuments_.name: Blood West

_childDocuments_.review: This is a sluggish nightmare of an experience to play because it is an extremely punishing game with no proper saving system. It autosaves upon death and you can save and quit. While I understand this is done to prevent save scumming and that death has attached mechanics which add incredibly pungent debuffs, it becomes infuriating to constantly have to alt+f4 because you walked 10 feet, died, and don't want to become cursed or lose progress due to your death - which then makes the game even more difficult. If you even miss a single headshot in this game, it generally means certain death. And guess what, your character has Parkinson's! It is the saving reason alone that this game becomes incredibly tedious and irritating to play around %90 of the time. If the devs fix this by adding saving and loading, then this fixes the one big issue with this game and many others it has. Slow pacing, extremely punishing deaths, odd learning curve - all can be fixed through adding manual saving. But until this is added or a mod is made, Blood West is more tedious than enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: Blood West

_childDocuments_.review: Blood West is a spooky western RPG-like game. A FUN one to be clear. The game paces you along to appreciate the items you get and slowly build you up. Sure you can use a rusty weapon, but what about a unique one you found in the bottom of a mine in a corpse pile that makes you sneak better? The game features a leveling system with a skill tree that actually has some good variety to it. There isn't any filler trash skills xp isn't a pain to get. Stealth is big here and ammo is limited but after an hour or two, you'll have more than enough to run and gun. USUALLY, I'm more than confident enough to run in guns blazing, but the enemies in this game are JUST scary enough and JUST deadly enough for me to actually use my brain and avoid some conflict. If this first chapter of the game says ANYTHING about how the other two are going to turn out, I HIGHLY suggest you try it out. The game is genuinely fun and rewards you well for snooping around.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the first games I've played that felt like a chore. There's probably something good later on in the game, but the first hour is just tedious. I wanted to like it, been searching for an FPS that switches up the genre, but this ain't it. Really cool art and atmosphere.Pros:- Awesome art- Diablo like inventory system was cool to see in a shooter- Very interesting stealth mechanicCons:-  Hard to tell when an enemy is going to turn in your direction, there's no tell as there are no set paths. They could take a couple steps looking 180 degrees from you then turn around fully after a short resting phase- Gunplay is a joke. I get that you're able to upgrade your gun skill but there's no way a gun should feel as useless as they do even at the start of a game. Can't even tell where the bullet has gone most times.- Enemy bullets have insane tracking- Dark Souls curse like mechanic adds to the game feeling like a chore, and I love the Souls games. Feels so out of place and unnecessary as you are pretty much guaranteed to get killed if there are 2 enemies with guns on your tailArt: 9/10Story: 8/10Sound: 8/10Gameplay: 4/10
_childDocuments_.name: Blood West

_childDocuments_.review: It's okay, but it's extremely rough around the edges and has a long way to go. The first hour or so of the game, starting out blind and all is very fun. But once you've encountered every enemy type the game very quickly becomes stale. Enemy ai is extremely simple to the point that there is no real punishment for not going stealth so long as you've gained enough gear and don't run past every enemy, gunshots alert enemies 15 feet away at best. The sole objective of the game is go to a place, find a cursed piece of gold, return it to a checkpoint, repeat. You do this until the boss of the scenario which is your extremely generic "shoot it until it dies" boss. The horror aspects lose charm once you realize the repetition of the game play and find the guns that are just objectively better than most others. Inventory management is redundant, curses can be easily bypassed if you know what you're doing, giving death less of an impact. Blood West has a lot of potential to be a great horror fps with hints of survival horror and Thief like open ended-ness. But as it stands it's too easy to get over-geared for extremely simplistic ai to the level where the game just becomes a point and click fetch quest.
_childDocuments_.name: Blood West

_childDocuments_.review: Chapter 1 is awesome Chapter 2 is awesome but the economy is way too grindy if you don't get the right items and honestly you can just stop there really. Chapter 3 sucks. Game's atmosphere and creativity with enemies is a huge breath of fresh. Those two are really the highlights of the game. The combat is honestly stupidly deadly and punishing if you don't stack hp and/or damage reduction like crazy. The stealth however is very rewarding if perhaps far too easy and forgiving if you've built your character around it. Overall a solid 7/10 in my opinion. Not super long but I could see myself replaying this in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Safe-houses are strategically placed to provide quest gathering, respite, item trading, player stashes, quick travel and revival pointsItems hidden throughout the map encourage explorationThe map is an adequate size for the limited number of quests and makes travelling from A to B less dauntingNot enough locations, but those there are, are built with depth, being above and below ground, some having multiple floorsNeeds more quests as these are few and sequentialFlaws (debuffs) are stacked on the player's soul when revived, a nice incentive to stay alive. Removable by itemsA handful of potions to heal, buff or cleanse are useful for keeping the player aliveHealth recovered by bandages for light injuries, potions for more or resting at a safehouse fully, which respawns enemies28x perks allow for playstyle specialisation across four branches of abilities/mechanicsCharacter progression is well balanced with current content with XP providing up level 6As well as melee or ranged combat, vitality, endurance, resistances, carry capacity and loot finding can all be enhancedPerk upgrades feel one dimension due to the compact nature of content currently availableStealth and patience is required to close distances and silently takedown enemies with melee weaponsA stealth gauge is the perfect tool for sneaking around, tracking sound, vision and alert statusesStealth is encouraged through design where levels hold alcoves and other LoS blocking sceneryLoud noises (even explosives) don't always attract hostile attention of every critterA small cadre of shotguns, revolvers, Winchester rifles, a bow, 2h axe and knives allow for a good mix of take-downsWeapons have their own distinct behaviour and use. Perks make them more efficientMost quest location layouts provide good sources of tactical positioning to engage enemiesQuick, primary and secondary weapon slots limit play-style to the weapons and items heldLook down sights give better aim when using ranged weapons. The player can also lean around corners and aim in coverGood mix of Lovecraftian inspired enemies from bipedal to the exoticEnemy behaviour is predictable, but show direct purpose when alerted, closing distance at speedPatrolling enemies do not have their alert levels raised if they see other dead enemiesFour types of ammo inflict more general damage or are for use against certain enemiesPerks or additional equipment can expand inventory capacityDynamite and molotovs can be obtained to take out groups of creaturesA combination of creature body parts and equipment provide bonuses to abilities when equippedEasy to forget uncollected loot as map markers are not generated► Game world design, its locations and the choice of perks and inventory, afford a choice of playstyles or a mix if the player is so inclined to be adaptable.► Despite its open world design, quests are given in a very linear manner until towards the current finale.► There are too few quests and a minimal number of sub-quests. ► The majority of the experience is exploring, stealthily taking out lone enemies, before taking on set-piece situations to get quest items.Will suit players who are patient and meticulous.► FPS combat is a toss up between easy and challenging. Enemies can get alerted very quickly and track down the player relentlessly. Its easy to die due to slow reactions, running out of ammo, take damage to quickly or needing to reload.► Melee and ranged combat kills are not 100% guaranteed in the beginning, especially when up against more than one enemy. Investment in skills, better weapons and equipping certain items changes this.► Returning to previously cleared areas will be boring unless a significant amount of time has elapsed or the player has fully rested a safehouse, to respawn some enemies.► Not all creatures are alerted when using firearms in their vicinity, allowing the player to cheese past some encounters.► The ability to alternate between between using melee, shooting targets using or explosives on fly really adds to the enjoyment of combat.► Loot and inventory border on being somewhat shallow.► No game game-breaking issues where experienced during this playthrough.► A few minor issues with item stacking on the same spot and firearms that do not fire exiting the safehouse while reloading, which were overcome quickly.► Gameplay stacked to be everything one would expect from a 1990s game of this type. Gunplay was excellent. Being able to mix-up stealth and going loud - great. It was a lot of fun and mistakes were not costly with the auto-revival and the items to remove curses.Blood West is well-made, well-balanced and everything expected of a 1990s inspired FPS. While not the best looking, its playable and full of considered features that provide the sort of  experience one would hope for. Complimenting mechanics deliver viable stealth and gung-ho playstyles. Though perks and loot feel shallow by the end of the game.Given nothing game breaking was found, its incompleteness and few issues currently rates as a  experience.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is about the early access version of the game and will be changed when the game gets a full release. Even in early access this game is very polished. The voice acting feels very fitting to the general mood of the game and makes me think about the game Blood, which also had excellent voice acting. As soon as you get a hand of the combat mechanics you will feel right at home if you have played games like Dusk, Blood, Hedon, Hrot and other stylish retro shooters.The western setting and all that implies on the visuals and more importantly on the weapons and combat gameplay makes this game stand out from the crowd though. You need to have room in your inventory for extra bullets and your sixshooter only has a six bullet drum, so you need to count your shots and reloading takes time. So you really need to plan your battles.The perk system is a nice addition that allows you to customize the player character to your style of play, be it stealthy scavenging or head on gunslinger. However, I suspect the perk system might need some balancing as some perks are way more useful than others but cost the same to aquire. There is also special so called artifacts that you can find ingame that have perk like qualities, that you keep equiped on you to gain their bonuses. Now you can just find them when roaming the land but I think it could just as easy have been side quests to find those, or that you find newspaper clippings that hint to their existence.The only things I can say something negative about is that the UI isn't as polished as it could be. Mainly the inventory handling. You loot containers and bodies and that brings up your inventory alongside the looted objects inventory side to side. As of right now you can not drag an object ontop of another object to make them switch places. That makes "tetrising" your inventory hard as you can not drag things around if there aren't enough free space. You can drag ontop to switch, but only from your weapon hand, not within the inventory itself. This is but a minor annoyance and I am sure it will be fixed in time.All in all I greatly enjoyed this game because it fills a hole in the genre matrix that isn't often explored. Horror western is a very underreprecented genre in games. This game is well worth the money you spend on it.
_childDocuments_.name: Blood West

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly a really great start for a game that's fresh on Early Access.Blood West I'd say fits the bill of being an FPS horror title. Not for those who are expecting speed and explosions, but rather you want to take your time, take your shots and creep your way around enemies instead of having your face torn off.Having played, already beaten the first boss (the only boss as of the writing of this review) the map is surprisingly complex even for not looking so large, having more vertical depth as you clamber through the mines or climbing through the forts towers. As for combat you're free to do as you like in the sense of either leaning on the guns or your melee for a more quiet approach if you want to get the jump on enemies, as well as the various trinkets you can equip to alter your stats some.There are a few cons but overall I would say its too early to judge but I can safely say if you want to throw a few bucks to the devs you're in for a fun time and only  bound to get better as development moves on. I'll come back to this review when the full release happens.

_childDocuments_.review: Blood West is a really cool if occasionally frustrating stealth shooter.You can try and play it like it's doom, but it's obvious that the developers meant for the combat to be slow paced: guns are long to reload, hip firing is wildly inaccurate and the difference in damage between headshots and bodyshots is immense. Unless you're fighting a single, weak enemy, every encounter will require you to stealthily pick off enemies one by one until they're all dead or you're spotted.Sadly, the stealth is very basic: creatures don't investigate explosions, gunshots and other suspicious activites and can't handle the player being on higher ground: i think many fights could have been made much more interesting by giving enemies more vertical mobility as well as attacks that don't require line of sight (grenades / mortars...). As it is right now, it's likely you'll die a lot when you start but once you start figuring out how the AI works the game's challenge mostly crumbles.Despite this, the game feels great to control, there's a great sense of progression and the playing area is vast and offers a good variety of combat arenas.I Beat the campaign with all quests done in a little under 5 hours; little of that time was spent doing anything except exploring new locations and fighting enemies. According to the current "ending", there's two more areas to come, which is an alluring offer considering the game's low price. Definitely recommended !

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fun until you fight a boss, the boss fights are atrocius.After having played through the entire game and all 3 episodes, im gonna fill in some details.Episode 1, 93%This episode, grips you, takes you in and stabs you in the eye, this episode is fantastic, until you get to the boss... A vast landscape canyon like western classic setting, it has mines and caves and even a fort, it might seem small, but its the kind of packed small that makes it big, something that few games have done before, but when it happens it just feels right, Risen from 07 did this really well with its small island and harbour town. So you walk around not quite knowing where to go at first (you know the feeling), but then you start clearing areas from the evil that lurks there and you find things, sell things, level up etc. etc. This is good stuff.Boss score: 5%Episode 2, 45%At first i wasnt sure why i didnt like this episode as much as the first, but i think i know now, its flat.Just simply put, it's flat, first episode has fantastic verticality, this episode, not so much, i think the best part of the episode is when the boss awakens and you hear its roar in the distance as you sneak around the area, other than that, theres quite a few new weapons to be found here, even though i probably used the XP revolver from the first episode pretty much all the way to the end of the game.Boss score: 15%Episode 3, 87%As you can see my score is way higher on this one, thats because verticality is back!, with a vengeance!, cause now you fight some really strong enemies, the only tip i can give is to save up 18k gold and buy that gun, youll need it and food for it is plentyfull, but save the nitro for when you REALLY need them.Boss score: 15%The enjoyment score as a whole im gonna put at 75%The bosses drags it down, but also the swamp episode, its just so uninteresting compared to the other two.

_childDocuments_.review: Blood WestA very well-thought-out and fun game. With a few tweaks and as time goes on, this could turn into something even greater. This is a resource management, stealth, FPS/rogue-like type game. There is an exploration and leveling side as well and feels good for the setting. With more content to come, I hope it holds up and even improves on what is already here. The aesthetics, item models, music, and environment all feel good and look great.  The voice acting and dialogue so far fit well and sound good. The protagonist explores a western-style map with monsters on the loose. You are out for blood.It's not overly punishing but there are a few penalties in place for certain situations, including death. It requires you to think or plan from time to time and depending on how well you explore and conserve supplies it can start to feel like every encounter is a big deal. Also, the opposite is true, if you spend your resources wisely and explore as much as possible you will have more than enough at your disposal.You have your main quest as well as side quests that seem to be optional. They do tie into the story and the main objective so I went ahead and completed them all if nothing more than to experience all the game offers.Enemy variety is fair and I could only assume future scenarios will add more. The same goes for the supplies. For early access, this game delivers an awesome experience so far. I explored all possible areas and experienced all there was to offer and I took my time doing so. This ran me around 11 hours for the first scenario. Depending on your play style and experience you can very well finish this in half that time, especially if you do not go to every corner of the map exploring. The price is worth paying in my opinion, I got this during the sale but the full price would be fine. Consider there will be updates and more content to come. The developers seem to be fairly active and I can tell there is an excellent amount of work put into this. Pick this game up!

_childDocuments_.review: VISUALS: Great pixelated 3D style, that reminded me of Quake/THOT kind of feel games. The dark and sinister vibe is done really right. The balance of being somewhere without sources of light at night and being able to see is spot on. (I would be very interested in finding out how devs did this trickery)SOUND: My favorite part. Ambiance and music is just perfect. It would immerse me really into the mood and often made the hairs on the back of my neck stand up, even when there was no action. Props to sound design team!CONTROLS: Very easy to understand and straightforward, with ability to change various settings that I needed.PERFORMANCE: The game ran smoothly on my system with 2GB memory graphics card.STORY: This part is quite lacking polish and content. Any bit of information just raises more questions. I think more needs to be done to elaborate the backstory and involve the player in the tasks. I didn't quite understand why I was involved in this mess to begin with. A lot more should be done here by the devs to make this title more compelling and engaging.GAMEPLAY: Is SHORT. The mechanics that are in place are great and work really well, but due to lack of content and short play time make this feel more like a demo. I felt disappointed it all ended so soon, as the potential here is great. Having different ammo types is cool, but what is the point when most of the enemies can be killed with one headshot with any type of ammo? Whats the point of the stealth system, if it doesn't really add anything, only saves you few rounds of ammo (which of is plenty in the game world to find or buy)? I would really love higher difficulty settings and more meaningful variations of weapons to fight harder enemies. Also would love to see new enemy types in the future. I really hope devs will continue to put effort into this title to make a more polished and balanced experience with some replay value, as there is great potential here for sure.SUMMARY: Pixelated Western feel horror FPS with great potential to become a full game sometime. If you are prepared to pay for a demo (but a very action packed one) with opportunity to play a full game sometime down the line, then this is for you. If you prefer to put your time into more complete/full experience, then this is not for you YET. But my suggestion is to give it a go to find out if it is worth the wait for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome little first person shooter with some light RPG and loot mechanics. Really a blast to play. Blood West drips with atmosphere and you can tell the devs put a lot of care and work into the game. It has tight combat and gameplay, great atmosphere, awesome art, moody and well fleshed out levels, and creative enemies. Supernatural westerns seem to be hit or miss, but Blood West really nails it. It feels like it drops you into a Spaghetti Western directed by George Romero. If you're a fan of titles like STALKER, or enjoyed the vibe and atmosphere of games like Diablo 2, I highly recommend checking Blood West out! Most fun I had playing a shooter in a while!
_childDocuments_.name: Blood West

_childDocuments_.review: First impressions make this game feel like Stalker and Dark souls had a child and then left that child to be raised by their uncle The Hunt: Showdown.The basic vibe is heavy Urban fantasy with western themes. The music is simple but hits all the right notes you'd want in a setting with foreboding atmosphere.The visuals while obviously styled on classic low poly models still manage to be creepy, they hit that source that Silent hill and Nightmare creatures took from and it comes together really well.The UI is great, giving you all the information you need while not taking up space, it makes the stealth gameplay reliable and while some enemies certainly have faster reaction times it gives you plenty of time to plan your attack usually.As for the dark souls element it shows mostly in just a handful of ways. You can "rest" and gain back HP but some monsters will also respawn, when you die you keep anything you've found and respawn at the nearest totem (which is usually in a safe zone with a bed to rest) unless you have a certain item on you you'll gain a penalty for dying, while at first this seems like a problem there are ways to remove said penalty and its refreshing to see a punishment for dying thats not either overkill or a slap on the wrist.Theres a healthy dose of RPG mechanics involved too. Between inventory management (which really could use a sorting mechanic) you can level up as you go and gain different perks, many are straightforward but a few give some neat stuff. Theres also a large amount of artifacts, status effect items and alternate ammo types to give you plenty of options to play.Enemies tend to hit hard and so ambush and stealth will serve you well early on but its not a mandatory thing from what i've seen so far. if you have a steady enough hand and enough ammo you can handle most encounters without sneaking, though the surprise attack and melee mechanics are solid enough that stealth doesn't feel like a chore.As for flaws there arent many, a few of the hit boxes can feel unforgiving to the point of jank and enemy pathfinding can sometimes be really weird. The common zombie also has a lunge attack that lets them 180 and still hit you even if you dodged the actual animation itself. These are mostly nitpicks and don't really hurt the experience.A solid fun title that feels like a good call back.

_childDocuments_.review: Updated 1.0 reviewI really thought I wouldn't like it but gave it a try, it ended up being the best game I played in years. Enemies are brain dead, that's on purpose, they can't see or hear far, that's on purpose. They will forget they saw you seconds ago, that's on purpose.This game is very easy... until you miss a shot, then you'll run for your life or pull off some of the best headshots of your life while your heart is pumping like crazy.Things can go South quick. This game is a balancing act of cautious risk taking. You will go "fµck it, I'm doing it" and it might pay off, or be your doom. You will feel like you're toying around with a carefully crafted challenge, you'll get the same feeling as when you're wondering if you can jump over a fence in one jump. You'll feel cheeky for trying some stuff, you might get punished for it, that's the fun part.Each new chapter will make you want to give up, the previous one made you feel comfy after a while, you'll have to re-learn a new set of enemies and get comfy with them... It will come. The large enemies you were avoiding for hours on end will soon go down in 1 or 2 hits and you will get comfy again... Until the next chapter.I was an early access player, each new chapter felt like a let down, they weren't, I just had to give them a chance and they were as good as what I'd loved up until that point.Replayability is great, at least in my eyes. It's extremely satisfying to restart from scratch, knowing exactly what to expect, where to expect it, and toy around with a new, different build.

_childDocuments_.review: Full game is out and done. How did it fare? Very well.For starters, I love blood west. If you can stomach the graphics then it offers a fantastic sneak-shooter game in a very grim western horror setting with good voice acting and fantastic environmental story telling. You are an undead, resurrected to combat ancient evil present in the locale you are set to roam. Search for items of importance, hear the story behind each of them and seek for the next one. Simple. On the way you quickly realize the whole map is loaded with secret goodies, artifacts, unique weapons and soon you are sniffing through the entire map like a loot horny packrat. Somehow it all just melds together.Enemies are plentiful and you can die very quickly but that goes to enemies aswell, even the strongest ones. Angle of attack, good preparation, good aim and enough ammo surplus guarantee you come on top in every encounter. Some enemies are resistant, even immune to certain damage types so choose your approach appropriately. Silver for ghosts and spooks, fire for anything which seems like it would suffer from some light torching and gold when you just dont give a damn and want to blast through your foes.Its nice that both melee and ranged combat are viable options, though I definitely lean towards latter. Some enemy types are brutally efficient in close combat and without potions and artifacts to nulify damage taken you would be down before you get your 3rd hit out. Overall, I enjoyed my time with the game. Its not too short and you can definitely sink some hours into it if you are inclined to sniff through every corner in search for unique weapons.

_childDocuments_.review: Was excited about this one. Loved the concept behind it. Loved the fact that Stephen Russell was in it. But I just could not get anywhere with this thing. The difficulty is absolutely crazy. What baffles me is all the people complaining that it's too easy. Are we playing the same game? I must have died 500 times in 30 minutes. I was filled up with penalty curses for dying which meant I now had basically no stamina or health and would bleed out super fast. So this game says "Hey I see you're having a hard time playing this. So basically I'm gonna make things even worse as punishment for you sucking at this game." What kind of logic is that? Some people say "I bet you're trying to play it like a boomer shooter and that's not what it is. It's like Thief. You have to play it that way."  I absolutely LOVE Thief. The first 3 Thief games are some of the best games ever made. But I don't recall many places in a Thief game where massive hoards of guards were all in the same place so that sneaking around them was near impossible. "Ok, but if you trigger the enemies just run away. They can't catch you."  Yes they can because the game has levied massive penalties against me for not being good enough. I can't run anymore. "Well just start over so you don't have the penalties." Sounds like a great game! Just keep starting all over again and wading through the tutorial again.  "Look. The stealth in this game actually sucks anyway. Don't play it like Thief. Just run up on enemies and bash them in the head."  So, play it like an FPS then? Which it isn't. And that gets me killed quickly. This is a cool idea for a game but the gameplay mechanics do not actually remind me of Thief at all. This game reminds me of Pathalogic. Another game that seems cool but is actually mad f'n frustrating and borderline unplayable unless you're into torturing yourself. I wanted to like this. I really did. But this isn't fun. This is for people that like Dark Souls and Rougelike BS.

_childDocuments_.review: BUY THIS GAME, BUT-Honestly, this game is dope. The exploration is amazing, the looting is vast, and the enemies are varied, however, there is a huge caveat....This game is beyond Dark Souls levels of difficulty.I played this game for over two months. Here's my routine:New game - Okay sick, lots of loot, there's XP on kills, a skill tree, buffs and perks, and even artifacts you can carry that help you along the way! Loving it so far!However... Saving basically isn't an option, it's like an NES game where you technically can save, but if you venture too far from the save point, and die, you've just wasted like 2 hours of your life.Reader: "But DankWestern, you can die and lose hours of progress if you kill 41 enemies, and turn left instead of right around one corner and die instantly from an enemy you had no clue was there, but you can just play again for another month to get back to the starting point with the things you lost. You're just a casual."Well, you're not wrong, however, the learning curve is brutal. One mistake, and you've just wasted your free time after work. If you're younger, and can commit 4 or so hours to carefully assessing enemy movements patterns and attack patterns, it's doable, but some of us are adults, and we work every day so we can live indoors and eat every day.This game is fun, but balancing is a major issue.I adore the stealth play too, that's my preferred method of play, but crawling around for a couple hours, dominating every monster, only to turn a corner, and find a monster off guard, and heavy attacking it, expecting a kill just doesn't happen. Some enemies are armored, so your entire playstyle is just worthless.You'll think you've got the drop, only to find that your stealth attack just stripped the armor, and a full health enemy lurks within who is instantly ready to kill you in under 2 seconds if your reaction speed, and ability to swiftly uncrouch, and change your entire loadout from stealth to commando can't happen in 2 seconds results in your instant death just... leaves you wondering what the point was.I made a discussion asking what I was missing, and the replies just told me I was a scrub, and that I sucked, and the dev took their side and encouraged me to network amongst their Discord server for enemy patterns and behavior since the game doesn't allow the player a chance to observe these things firsthand.Maybe I am a scrub, but why not give the player some kind of a buffer? Why not ease the player into the game by offering one or two encounters that let you study the enemy patterns and behaviors at least once before being brutally murdered and setting you back to a point where you'd just sat down as if you'd never played in the first place?I will admit that I adore the difficulty, and even though I've bashed my skull against this brick wall of a game, I am a glutton for punishment, but I simply do not see myself among equals that I would confidently be able to recommend this game to.I hope this rambling review helps you. Know the punishment you're paying for before you get this game, and use my torture to formulate your own choice before buying.

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting immersive sim built around a Wild West with Eldritch Horror.Even if the game encourages stealth, one can make character builds that allow the player to fight toe to toe against the various horrors. For instance, my first run was a stealth character that relied on light melee weapons and bows/crossbows, and it worked excelent when exploring any new area, however it may prove difficult to face the tougher and big enemies. Later on I tried another character but this time he relied on firepower from any ranged weapon, after gaining some perks and some gear this character started blasting his way through the game in brutal fashion (But still could die easily), facing multiple enemies in a single showdown and even the tougher mobs proved a decent challenge, but nowhere as difficult as they were for the stealth character.Does that mean that combat based characters are better than stealth ones? Not necessarily, they are only different approaches to the same problems. As I said earlier, the gunslinger can still die easily in two hits against big enemies, and it's prone to die more often depending on the player's skills to aim, take cover and improvise. The stealth character rewards being aware of the enviroment, in a methodical way, for those who don't want to be pressured in real time. And I haven't tried too much melee builds, but I figured out those could rely on the player's ability to exploit whiffs from the enemies, timing the hits right, and not crumbling under pressure when in low HP because there are many perks that benefit melee when the HP is lower.Overall, I enjoy the ideas this game let the player experiment upon. Maybe in the mid game the quests might be a bit grindy (There are fetch quests basically) and the story is just and excuse to move on to the next area, but I still like Blood West for what it is: "A System Shock 2 but in the Eldritch Wild West"
_childDocuments_.name: Blood West

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, so!Blood West: Thief meets Duke (and, if you're an RE: Village fan, you'll get a similar vibe here too).The Stealth mechanic in this game is well-executed without being overly precious - sneaking about is simple and enemies are reasonably forgiving with their lines of sight, but that doesn't remove any of the suspense; if you get caught, enemies hit HARD and healing isn't instant. STRONGLY recommend the fox buff from the totems - could even be a little overtuned, actually.Combat is intense, headshots connect properly and are satisfying, the guns feel good in a wild west clunky way; the combat 'feel' suits the game's aesthetic and is all the more enhanced by our undead protagonist muttering to himself.The monsters are varied and fulfil the roster of expected enemies in a 90s shooter... looking forward to seeing more!That being said - the ADS is a little clunky and can make combat more difficult that it needs to be. Aiming in and out isn't as responsive as I feel it should be, and there's not even a perk to rectify this.The weapons on the whole are well designed and are different enough from one another for your set up (1 large weapon + 1 small weapon) to actually matter - tailor this to how you want to play; I run the axe and pistol combo at the moment. It'll be interesting to see if we get more weapons. I could even see RE4-style weapon mods having a place in this game.The only weapon I am not sold on is the bow - I just... can't make it work. I feel like it could do with a big damage buff to compensate for its long draw time. Level design is brilliant - a sandbox-style world where areas connect with one another. Early on, whilst on the Shaman's quest, it is possible to enter the fort; I suggest you don't do that straight away! The night sky above you is both haunting and desolate - seeing the silhouettes of broken buildings ahead of you really adds to the immersion. The landscape rises and falls, so there's a real sense of vertical combat. You can find vantage points to plot out a path to what you want to do. There's a bridge early on that really gives a great sense of height! Vertigo is hard to achieve in games and the developers have done a great job here. What would I add/my thoughts? - I think sand storms to obscure vision could be interesting - perhaps forcing the player to find a place to hide- A torch mechanic or beacon lighting mechanic- A 'quick use' button and some items to use in conjunction with your one-handed weapon slot. The ability to use dynamite and molotovs with speed could be interesting- A smoke bomb of sorts. You will get caught out eventually, and certain enemies are very punishing, particularly in groups- I feel the alcohol could use a tweak in general... it sells for so much and getting the stronger weapons (I assume they'll be elsewhere in the full release) at this point is just far more important- Not entirely sure how to remove a curse at this point - I have no doubt missed something- The merchant shop (Jim) doesn't seem to empty of the things I sold him (I have to keep running back to the Shaman!) - again, I may have missed somethingSo. For an early access, Blood West is brilliant. I can't wait to see what else is to come. I'll add to this as I find out more.P.s., Don't underestimate the Q-bound rock throwing.P.p.s., BUY THE MAP

_childDocuments_.review: First off I was experiencing bad frame-rates by the end of Chapter 2 and into the beginning of Chapter 3. What solved it was turning off V-Sync and replacing it with a max set FPS that matched the refresh rate of my monitor. This issue almost killed all the motivation for me to finish Blood West until I fixed it. One more tip don't use the auto-sort for your inventory because it doesn't do a good job sorting your items to make room for more. You're better off doing it yourself. Besides those things Blood West is great and the closest thing to the single-player Hunt: Showdown experience we all want. If you like your more stealth oriented action games this delivers. Last tip always keep a gold coin equipped in an artifact slot.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is continuing to exceed everything I expected from it. I was intrigued, but waited to buy it on sale with a pack but I would pay full price for this game. Where I feel the game lacks are areas I do not want to complain about or note because it could sour others opinions and these areas could very well be deliberate, creative choices and if that is the case then I applaud the developers for sticking to their guns, no pun intended. Some might not be interested due to its graphics and the choice to capture the era of gaming they did. I hope those players can look past and give it a chance because it excels in every other area: sound design, level design, inventory  and inventory management, gun play, game play, I could go on.I am very big into how a gun feels in games. For example - I think the Shotgun from Duke Nukem 3D is to this day a very rewarding gun both for how it looks and feels when used. During my current play through of B-Dubya  (3rd restart after figuring out my character build) I am using a 6-shooter, and two-handed axe. Both of these weapons are rewarding with every single head shot. I may edit this in the future or add more, but for now, I am continuing to love and enjoy and be captivated by Blood West. f

_childDocuments_.review: Terrific game, delivers on all fronts...til the boss. Seldom have I had the pleasure of playing a game that delivers such intuitive options for stealth, while also allowing the guns blazin' approach to be entirely viable. First though, this game is HARD in the best tradition of rewarding, challenging games. You will die, you will accumulate curses and you will be duckin' behind the nearest tumbleweed once the freakish monsters get you in the sights of their big irons! This game will test you and the first few hours are particularly brutal until you level up enough to purchase the better loot perks. These are absolutely essential, to the point they should be the FIRST ones you get. Yes, the ammo/supply starvation early game is that bad. Even once you get the perks, limited shopkeeper inventory prevents you from carrying too much of anything too long, but ultimately it feels well balanced....Until you get to the boss.This boss is horrible and it was like the brick wall that my enthusiasm for this game hit at high speed.  The boss is completely different than anything you've practiced before in the game. Good area bosses build upon the mechanics you've learned before and puts them to the test, leaving you with a climatic set piece of a battle. Not so in Blood West; instead I found myself running in circles, constantly out of stamina, fumbling with the inventory system. It's a battle that requires you to go into inventory..the only problem being the inventory is designed to only be opened when you're not in battle. When you're forced to go into inventory when under attack, you can probably figure out what happens. This boss fight will consume ALL of your supplies so you better hope you've been stockpiling before this. Otherwise get ready to farm enemies for the gold to buy more health potions, ammo and throwables. This boss was so bad that I sadly put the game away and haven't touched it since, so brutally did it crush any sense of fun I had with this otherwise amazing concept. I still recommend this game in the hopes that the devs fix the boss or alter the mechanics/economy to make the first boss a little less miserable to fight. Even if you also get stuck at the boss, i would recommend it still. Why??Well because the gunplay is satisfying, the enemies are varied and require different techniques to eliminate. The stealth mechanics actually work and reward the careful player with some of the most satisfying sneak attacks. (I was shouting taunts at my enemies as I peered over the roof of a barn, and fired my lever action rifle into a birdman's skull mask!) And, like I said at the start, melee players can have fun with this too AND they can enjoy a stealthy attack as well. It's just as satisfying to swing your axe into an enemies back as it is to blast them with a shotgun, perhaps even more so! Bottom line: fun stuff, mechanically solid normal gameplay, sadly undercut by poorly thought out 1st boss.

_childDocuments_.review: I've had a blast with this game over the course of a 25 hour playthrough, definitely worth checking out.Pros:- Ammunition types, Standard, Silver, Gold and Flammable; Standard is most common but has no benefits, Silver is especially effective against Spirits, Gold deals double damage but is hard to come by and Flammable sets things on fire making them take damage over time.- Artifacts are a great way to really change up how a player decides to approach a situation or play the game in general, if you're just wanting to farm XP and level up then you can equip artifacts which increase your XP rates, same thing goes for most play styles.- Multiple ways to approach areas, you could go through the front or sneak in via a tunnel system etc. - Open-ended level design with plenty of areas to explore.- Sound design of the game, what echoes throughout the area when you fire a shotgun or revolver really makes the guns feel like they have weight.- Visual Style gives the game a very unique retro-styled aesthetic.- Wide variety of enemies to overcome, each with unique characteristics, usually exclusive to the Chapter they're introduced in, though there is some overlap with a couple enemies making appearances in later Chapter.Cons:- Alerting enemies when firing a gun is very inconsistent, often times I'll be a decent distance away and it'll alert them but then other times I'm much closer and a gunshot doesn't alert them.- Curse system isn't all that detrimental, the moment you actually receive a curse you can just talk to an NPC who will give you an easy quest to do to remove it, this quest is usually as simple as "Kill 5 of X enemy".- Detection meter for Spirits makes little sense, sometimes it depletes as fast as it does for anything else and other times it depletes at a snails pace, no indication as per why.- Very easy to get lost in a couple areas due to how labyrinthine the layout of the cave systems can be as well as the fact everything looks very similar.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright how can I put how I feel about this game? The graphics are a nice blend of oldschool and modern HD ports of the old style games. The environment textures are nice in catching the old pixelated look, same with the monster textures. The models are low poly models that wouldn't be to far from quake 2 or unreal. As it stands, there is not a a lot of weapons in the game; but the weapons that are in the game are fairly nice and balanced. Combining the RPG leveling to improve how you use weapons is nice, as well as the ability to do only the direct story missions or do both story and side missions to improve your weapons and abilities is very nice.Only having 2 shops in the current version is a bit difficult though, as if you use all your ammo and have already explored the map, you then have to go from one shop to the other to get ammo and healing items (as they do not respawn like the monsters do) is a major pain, given that you will have to use ammo or health to get between them at times. The aiming seems a bit broken; but that might be just part of the RPG elements as one of the perks improves aim. This is a personal gripe, as when I am aiming directly at something the shot should go straight to where I aim. The variety of ammo is nice, using the right ammo for the right enemies and watching them die instantly is fun. The sound design is also fairly nice with an awesome sound track and every sound being identifiable. The map that is released, as the others are still being developed, is fairly barren with large spans of empty. It does feel like an old west environment like that so it captures to feeling; but for a game that seems to be high action and sneaking based this leaves large areas where you have to just run/walk with nothing happening. Overall I give this game as it stands a 3/5 Potatoes. This is only based on what is here so far and I will edit my review with future map updates.
