_childDocuments_.review: By no means is Blood West a bad game, but it does have some glaring flaws.Blood West is a retro-styled RPG shooter with stealth elements that reminds me of a combination of Diablo 2, Red Dead Redemption, and even Metal Gear or Last of Us. While it does these things individually on paper very well, having all three in rotation at the same time is clunky and awkward at best, and downright frustrating at worst.RPG Elements involve basic equipment upgrades, inventory, and exp opening up 3 talent points to spend on upgrading yourself upon leveling up. Some of these skills are well thought out, like +25% stealth or faster reload speed, however others are redundant and placed twice (two HP upgrades, for example) and some feel like options that should have been implemented in the game from the beginning to make gameplay feel better, mostly revolving (mind the pun) around combat mechanics, particularly aiming/shooting, which leads me to the most glaring flaws of Blood West, the combat mechanics.Combat in this game is where it's flaws come to the forefront... Melee attacks involve an axe which is brute power, and a knife, which is fast and agile. Both weapons have a light attack and a heavy attack, with heavy taking more energy to use than light but dealing more damage, in addition to bonus damage by sneaking up on opponents. However, this almost doesn't matter because if you actually want to kill anything you MUST sneak up on them for bonus damage, then attack them with your melee weapon at the head, and that's your best bet for combat. If the accuracy mechanic decides to not let you get a headshot you will more than likely get thrashed and be infected with status defects (which happen upon death, similar to Dark Souls) to make your already lackluster stats even worse, whether it be less % health, stamina, experience, and can only be cured after obtaining the maximum defect of that particular stat (stacked to 3, so 3 deaths) and doing a special side-quest for the skull totem that you respawn at. The skull offers upgrades for gold coins, which are absolutely necessary if you want to win. They tell you what they do, although sometimes not specifically... I went with Luck of the Bear (more power) and an axe/sawed off shotgun to make it through chapter one.This is made worse by the shooting mechanics, where even though the weapons have a recommended/preferred range, seem to be all over the place in terms of accuracy. There's an upgrade called "Steady Aim" to assist the 'sway' your character has when looking down the sights but I'm not sure this helps accuracy, as sometimes even when an enemy is in sights, you just happen to miss anyway. There's also another upgrade that makes looking down the sights slow down time for 2.5 seconds, a la Red Dead or even Zelda Breath of the Wild, but it's almost completely ineffective because the timer starts when you right click, meaning the drag your character takes to raise his firearm to his sights is ALSO slowed down. If you're using this ability with the rifle, it seems to work as intended... If you're using it with the revolver, however? It's broken to the point of being useless--The drag it takes to raise his revolver or even his sawed-off shotgun takes up almost all the slow-down time... Not that this really matters, because aiming down the sights still has a change to miss, and just like the melee combat above, if you're not getting the bonus damage from headshots, you are going to get rushed down and thrashed. Come to think of it, I did the entirety of the first map (there are at least 3) and don't recall getting ANY kills with a firearm that weren't based on headshots. If you whiffed the headshot you could either use all your shotgun ammo killing the enemy or get out the knife/axe and aim for the head as your best bet. This works for chapter one, but as you get to the later maps, enemies get stronger and need two or three headshots to kill them, which with these wack combat mechanics makes the game incredibly frustrating. There are other ammo types as well which add a nice variety such as bonus damage with silver and gold bullets, but some of this feels like the talent system before--Your firearm should be strong enough initially that if you put 4-6 rounds of your .45 ammo through your revolver in the body of your average enemy it would lie down.Stealth is stealth--You crouch and move slowly to sneak on your enemies and get bonus damage or avoid them completely. You regain energy at a slower pace while crouching rather than walking or standing but while stealth is strong, it's not overpowered by any means and often involves you having to stop mid-way through the pursuit of an enemy in order to not be noticed. The only way to make this "Stealth-detect meter" go down is to be completely still and out of sight of the enemy, which usually means you'll be almost in melee range of your enemy from behind and have to stop for a few seconds to make the meter go back down then continue your pursuit, hoping that he doesn't just turn around and you have to bum rush him with an axe to the head lest you die and have 5% worse stats. There is a useful mechanic however, that if you press X while stealthed you can throw a rock to either distract an enemy from you or to even pull them in alone from a group of others. However, enemies do respond to sound and if you kill one and there is another nearby they follow the screams of their dying friend. They will also follow the sound of gunshots so aim for the head and pray the accuracy RNG is on your side and you don't miss and die immediately.Jokes and harsh criticism aside, I understand the logic of "preferred range RNG" for firearms as it relates closely to real life. In real life the longer the barrel of a weapon the more accurate it will be. Firing a pistol with a 6 inch barrel will have more accuracy than that of a 3 inch barrel, and firing a rifle with an 18 inch barrel will be more accurate than the 6 inch barrel, etc. I understand the logistics, but I also understand that the closer an enemy gets, the more accurate your shots should be... My biggest beef is with the revolver and the rifle as I feel their accuracy is all over the place, even when enemies nearing point blank.I purchased this game in a combination pack with New Blood's Gloomwood and by no means do I regret it. This game has a great atmosphere in the way it incorporates elements from various genres combined with it's retro visuals, making it unique, and while frustrating at times, far from boring.

_childDocuments_.review: WHEW! That was a nice surprise!Blood West is, in spite of the misguided presumptions gained with Realms Deep, a rather interesting stealth focused, open world kind of im-sim light set in a “weird west” scenario. While it will certainly not set the world on fire, it is a really fun chunk of game that contains far more than it first appears to.First let us be clear so everyone can understand: this is not, I REPEAT NOT, a boomershooter despite the somewhat low-res look and Realms Deep announcement heritage. For all the anticipation of this to play like the game Blood due to the wisecracking (and slightly evil) gruff sounding gunslinger, this plays distinctly differently. In Blood West ammo is in short supply, enemies will kill you fast, your character moves like a pregnant yak and his aim is wobbly as all heck. You are not expected to circle strafe and bound around enemies firing off round after round of munition at them. Indeed, the expectation seems to be primarily focused on moving about crouch sneaking before you stop and take in the surroundings and then either creep up and melee enemies from behind or attempt to take them out from a distance with a clean headshot. Its less about the moment to moment “fun” and more about the satisfaction of clearing out an area and looting as much as you can carry with you without dying.The moment to moment gameplay is less Dusk and far more like the criminally under-rated title Betrayer, set in a supernatural historic environment based on quick, lethal combat using slow loading and clumsy weapons. While describing the guns as clumsy may sound offputting, it adds to the satisfaction of pulling off one hit kills. Using the revolvers or the Winchester to pop an enemy head before they spot you is damn nice, enhanced further via the rather meaty headshots. This game rewards caution and patience, and once a plan fully comes together, its damn nice!Enhancing this is the unsignposted open world. A character will tell you a rough direction to go in and, following that path, you will eventually get to your destination. Early on in the game you go from the first safe zone towards the main town and, to get there you head towards the burned church in the centre of the map. While en-route I noticed a mineshaft just off the beaten track and proceeded to check out the area, finding a route through that eventually led to town. Similarly I went and fulfilled a quest for a shaman near the beginning and, through exploring, found a back entrance to a fort which had a key item in it. I found it out of the order the game wanted me to do it in, but that was not an issue, plus I got a nice leaver action rifle from it.These factors; the slow paced play, open ended nature and the resource management, all combine to make a game that reminds of playing the Bethesda Fallout titles when I ignore the plot and just run about doing what I want. It absolutely does not pester you or push you into various busywork XP grinds like a modern FarCry or Just Cause game and just lets you be yourself, curiously poking about wherever and whatever when and how you want, and since that style of game is not becoming rarer, I have to appreciate what is happening here.Are there weak points? Yes, some because of the design and some because it is early access. First there is the factor of this being a, shall we say, im-sim light. Once you start dipping in I can imagine people hoping to start doing actions like pouring oil on the ground to slip up enemies or set them alight, or picking up objects to stack and climb over walls. This is, despite the im-sim tag, quite a static world where most interactions are done via shooting enemies in the head. Also the early access nature makes it feel slightly unpolished. The UI in spots feels a little placeholder, as well as a lot of the text is riddled with typos and errors. This factor hopefully will be sorted eventually and provided the devs don’t soil the bed with it, everything is on track to become rather great.To conclude, Blood West is a really nice little title thus far. While it is not the most feature packed title out there and it has some rough edges, it most certainly is something for folks who feel the need to play something that could be described as a Stalker lite, or something to fill the gap left by the sadly forgotten Betrayer. Just don’t go in expecting Blood III or Deus Ex: Cowboy Revolution.

_childDocuments_.review: Oof, this is a "hard" recommend. Maybe more a meh. The game started off strong. Now go track them all down across this map and remember where you dropped them or know what drops them." That killed it for me. Chapter 3 was a lot better. It was an absolutely difficult drudge. Just no matter what you do, you take damage. It's a fun game that is a pretty hardcore stealth fps game with leveling mechanics. There are things related to the story that never triggered despite finding "the cure". I have a Ryzen 9 and a RTX 2080. Why does this ps2 looking game get sluggish to 40fps with the latest graphics drives? I had fun, but I am darn glad it's over and I'm never turning it on again.In short, the game is a lot of fun, but it has some severe and unacceptable flaws.I don't know, maybe I'm peeved at the ending? The ending cinematic is really awesome, but it had me googling "the good ending" for the past 15 minutes and apparently what I got is just the ending. Lol, maybe I'm just cranky >_<

_childDocuments_.review: I hope the game gets the fixes and additions that could make it a great experience, but it's not there yet and the current issues make it a pretty frustrating experience. I love the setting, visuals, monsters, intricate level design and careful approach to combat reminiscent of STALKER. My gripes boil down to a few major issues.1. Inventory - The game has terrible inventory management that can easily get you killed. Old school grid inventories can work just fine, but Blood West makes it as obtuse and unintuitive as humanly possible. You can't switch one item for another. Autosort after taking an item can't turn it sideways even when there's enough space. Switching equipped items works one way, but not the other. One type of backpack can be opened at a trader, another can't. Basically, be ready to spend 1/4 of your playtime staring at the inventory for reasons that could be solved with a few minor QOL tweaks which were standard since the 90's.2. Balancing - The difference in difficulty between Canyons and Swamps is night and day, and both chapters suffer for it. Canyons become a walk in the park as soon as you get your hands on a rifle. The game quickly turns into a point'n'click shooter where you have to really screw up to be in any kind of danger. Swamps, on the other hand, turn difficulty up to 11 and stay there. Rather than adding tension and excitement to the combat, it only turns it into a different kind of tedium. Enemies come in big crowds, they all have ranged attacks with virtually no limits to their rate of fire and range, yet all turn out to be bullet sponges with more health than you. Until you find the strongest guns, it feels like your previously fine weapons got accidentally switched for BB guns. Did I mention that trader's items cost thousands while your average enemy drops 10-30$ worth of loot?3. Interactivity - Blood West takes its stylization, difficulty and certain design choices from old school FPS games, but one retro aspect it severely lacks, which could add complexity and variety to its gameplay, are interactive environments. The second I got my hands on an axe, I couldn't wait to cut open some wooden boxes and clear boarded up paths to open alternate routes, but the game wouldn't let me, just as it wouldn't let me throw oil lanterns to set enemies on fire, open beautifully modelled wardrobes to find hidden monsters or destroy ceramic vases in hope of hidden trinkets. It might sound like a nitpick, but this interactivity is what truly sells the world's believability and makes the player's throught process more complex than just "click thing until thing dead".4. Enemy spawns - When it comes to monster types and designs, Blood West offers enough variety and many are fun to fight. But subsequent encounters quickly become dull because all enemies spawn at the exact same spot after you rest. The game is only unpredictable the first time, after that you're just going through the motions. Some variation could go a long way in improving replayability and making combat more tense. Certainly a better solution than just flooding every location with dozen invincible enemies who can take a headshot without losing their smile.Overall, I really hope Blood West gets the improvements it deserves. There's real potential here for a great open world stealth shooter. But as of right now, I wouldn't recommend it because of issues which make it equal parts dull and frustrating.

_childDocuments_.review: I do want to recommend this game, but I'm disappointed by it in the end.My big gripe is that it took me 3 hours to complete, even after doing the optional stuff. After 3 hours, I had all the ammo, the best weapons, too much money, etc. The only thing I was missing was unlocking all the perks, but half of those didn't seem worth it anyway.I enjoyed the gameplay in general. The guns are a challenge to shoot, and I like  the crunchy splatter of hitting something with an axe. The stealth is fine, though sometimes enemies with do a 180 spin, standing in place, which is very annoying and reminds me of stealth games from the 2000s. That said, it does keep the tension up.I'm also a fan of collecting things, going through nooks and crannies, scavenging and hoarding items and all that. I should love this game, because it has all that. Unfortunately, you're pretty limited in what you can find compared to similar games like STALKER. There just isn't enough, and what you do find is not significantly better than what you start with.Finally, I don't really like that this game ends in a big boss fight. For 99% of the game, you are taught stealth, caution, conservation of items and ammo, and to generally play "smart". But the finale is a big arena with an oversized boss in the middle. You have no choices but to run around and shoot it in the soft and red bits, while it spawns more monsters. This really feels like it is totally at odds with the rest of the gameplay. It's a bad design decision, but since it obviously took a lot of work to put it, I doubt it will be going anywhere before full release. In fact, it seems like MORE bosses are planned, if any content is added.There was so much potential with the game. The skeleton for something great is there. But as of this review, it doesn't have enough meat to really call a game. It's more of a proof of concept still.

Starting new chapters has a bit of a difficulty spike that levels out as you get the newer gear.If you're like me and Thief was a huge part of your formative years it's also great  to hear Stephen Russell back in the saddle.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm quite split on thisGame runs well, art style looks great, and creature design is cool, there's quite a bit i have a problem with.For one the stamina system, why on earth would you make stamina drain so brutally when your OPEN WORLD is huge, yes there's fast travel but its limited to item usage, why not just do what Elden Ring did and only drain our stamina when engaged in combat and not when roaming around?Secondly is the gunplay, hip fire is just straight up unreliable and the iron sights on the revolver is super hard to use due to the pixel artstyle, i can barely see the front sight at all. Although the guns are balanced as best they can, once you get enough ammo, melee weapons become useless.Thirdly is the enemy damage, I know this is supposed to be a challenging STEALTH game but when getting hit means spending about 2 bandages and 1 health potion just to get into a comfortable amount of health, it becomes tedious and a chore to micromanage your resources all the time.Fourth is just the miscellaneous bugs, one in particular is the Black Raven Skull item that doesn't spawn in CH.2 meaning you are locked out of getting one of the best items in the game

_childDocuments_.review: It's a pretty good game for the money. Starting off, it's pretty difficult and you will probably die a lot until you learn how the enemies work. The open world and artstyle is nice and there is a lot to explore. I would definitely recommend the game, especially on sale. With that being said, this game does suffer from some weird design choices involving the combat gameplay.  Pros:- Rewards exploration, lots of hidden items and unique weapons- Runs well, no technical issues so far and has ultrawide monitor support (I'm running 3440x1440)- Characters are voice acted including the player character (with the option to turn it off if you don't like it) - Dungeons and points of interest are generally well designed and I had fun navigating the world. Could use improvement:- Needs more varied gameplay. Missing shots is very punishing and melee weapons have long pauses between swings. This basically makes sneaking+headshot the only viable way to play. I would like the option to be able to dodge enemy melee attacks, block with my weapons, or at least have a fighting chance if I miss a shot. - There isn't a way to make more than 1 save file or manually save without exiting the session. This is probably to prevent save scumming, but I could see this being really annoying if the game crashes and your last save was an hour ago. Either way, this game needs a much better save system. Autosave would be nice too. - The game is way too dark. I had to mess with the gamma and brightness settings a lot just to be able to see and not squint. - This one isn't a huge deal but I would like to see unique cosmetic clothing items or something for your character that gives buffs or effects so that you don't have to fully rely on the perk/skills system.

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10 - Extremely fun & very promising! This game feels very different from a vast majority of shooters for me personally. It's nice to see a horror themed western shooter, definitely something new and refreshing! You do quests & side missions whilst trying to upgrade your skill traits, overall weapons & find loot. There's plenty of exploring to do & there's a ton of fun and creepy enemies that you'll soon witness amongst the world of Blood West. You can choose to be stealthy and logical about things or go in guns blazing and freak out when you get chased, the choice is all yours! I was lucky enough to have a chat with the developers and it seems they've definitely got a future road map of ideas & content to come. From a wild guess I'd say this game in the future with full release will definitely net you at least 10-12 hours of content. That's damn good for an indie game these days that's story-based.Highly, highly recommend this one. Absolute pleasure to have played and experienced. Thank you Devs. <3

If you like cowboys with guns and a bit of stealth fighting all kind of monsters, go and try it! Well worth the price.

_childDocuments_.review: It was fun, but I wish some features were more polished or different. Visually I loved it, variety of environment and enemies were also very nice!Difficulty would need some balancing. It was very difficult at some points and then a cakewalk at others (it was mostly the latter) including bosses, which were all way too easy. Design wise I liked them and attack patterns were fun, but it was over in under a minute, even the final boss (without issues). Enemy awareness is also a joke, with shooting guns will only trigger few meters close enemies and rest will remain idle. Killing enemy in plain sight from stealth will only make them come closer, without giving away your position. This should be more punishing for sure.I also wish there was a way to actually specialize. You can kinda get some perks first and use specific weapons that focus on something, but it is very limited. Before buying the game, I was hoping for more, focus on stealth or fighting all out, being melee or ranged focus or even builds for bleeding and such, because there are some small pushes to create a build, but it goes nowhere, which is a huge shame. You will in the end kinda play jack of all trades whether you like it or not. A bit more variety in weapons would also be nice, but it is enough for one playthrough. Timewise it took me almost 22 hours to fully play through the game, which is nice! And I did miss a few little things here and there, so I could play for 2 more hours still.I also do not see myself playing the game anymore, unless there is a new DLC with new chapter. Replaying the game with the way progression and perks work here is also a no-no. I still recommend it, because I had fun in those 22 hours, but I get that this could be a let down to some, so check it out a bit more before playing!

_childDocuments_.review: Blood West! the ol' west (quasi) Immersive Sim I've never knew I needed!There is little to said here: amazing non-linear FPS game based on survival, stealth (but way less than you may think) and good ol'gunplay, with tons of secrets to find (secrets that are actually useful, like finding unique items and weapons) and locations to explore, with a nice little pieces of story telling... although the game doesn't have that much of a story.Still, the settings are good (western and Lovecraftian, while not a unique mix, are certainly a welcome one) and the gameplay, especially for Immersive Sime players (...although in that department I expected something more), is amazing.Really recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is like a mashup of Hunt: The Showdown and Stalker. Both games which can be very difficult to get into and extremely frustrating. Like those two, this game is difficult and frustrating at times, but unlike those games, I got the hang of it within a couple hours instead of days.If you can stick it out past the first half hour, this game just opens up and really sells itself. The atmosphere, sound design, enemy design, inventory management, and gun play are all great and a well thought out combination. The death mechanic is unique to my knowledge and adds a bit of spice to play better while not being outright destructive to the experience.I heavily recommend this game to anyone who likes looter shooters.

_childDocuments_.review: I completed the game and even then i wouldn't recommend it.1.THE GRAPHICS ARE DISGUSTING. The game is so dark that i set gamma to a fairly high level, and even than i'm supposed to melt my eyes in order to search for collectables among this dirty mess which pretty the whole game visuals are. There are no any flashlights or things like that. Also, the visual bugs like white dots over textures are very common.2.LOOTING / ITEM MANAGEMENT IS POINTLESS. You are spending half of the game time to gather all the crap from monsters and sell it. But in spite of that, there are a heck lot of empty places, and you just waste your time checking them. That all gives me those stinky Stalker vibes, which is very disappointing for a souls-like game.3.THE COOLEST ITEMS ARE HIDDEN IN THE ASS OF A SQUIRELL. For example, i found an item that makes the protagonist invisible almost just before the final boss. But, the most of boost items are just ridiculously useless and you stash them for nothing.4.ENEMIES ARE SPLENDIDLY STUPID. The whole figthing concept is just hit'n'run - enemies are just not able to withstand it. But if you rush them - they are damn imbalanced and even can deal damage through mashes. The melee weapon are straightforwardly garbage, exept of throwable ones. _childDocuments_.review: I bought this as the other half of a Gloomwood bundle. I regret buying the bundle.Visuals======Blood West does display some basic competency presenting a decent atmosphere and simple but pleasing aesthetics. Unfortunately the palette they've used results in everything looking like a pixelated Disney movie poster which grates on the eyes after a while. Stealth======Oh man. The 'stealth' in this game is pretty tragic. This may be a little unfair coming of the back of my 1000th playthrough of Thief 1&2, but the stealth system in this game is two things - Rudimentary and Immersion Breaking. A good stealth system should feel organic - it should be conveyed by AI behaviour cues and sound design. If I'm sneaking up on someone so I can terminally pat them on the head with an axe, I'm going to be focused on what the enemy is doing. Are they suspicious? Are they searching? Has their vocalisation changed? Who knows, I'm busy staring at an ATB gauge. Being instead forced to watch a meter fill up kills that focus, and subsequently kills the tension. It makes engaging the enemy a binary system which to me feels extremely limited considering it's one of the main selling points for Blood West.Combat======So you weren't paying attention and the ATB gauge has filled up and now it's signor Cadaver's turn. The AI's cunning strategy is going to be run at you whilst sliding slightly clockwise around you. You tried to get a few shots of your revolver off but alas, you forgot that you've got Parkison's and your epilepsy has just kicked off so while the first shot wings them, the other shot lands on the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ moon. Time to break out the axe. Landing a good blow in melee at least feels fairly visceral, at least when the hit detection works. The rest of the time you feel cheated with what feels like should have been a solid hit. Unfortunately follow-up swings have all the urgency of a palsied grandmother attempting minigolf and you will invariably cop a hit or two, which is about all it takes to re-kill you. It seems a bit odd that you're some supposed bad-ass undead-hunting undead when you're clearly the least powerful entity roaming the wastes (which is fine, just don't have him talked up so much at the start. Expectations =/= reality.)Exploration=========The game appears to be reasonably non-linear, but it's a choice between exploring an empty environment vs a bland environment. There's little in the way of environmental story telling with most areas being some rocks garnished thoughtlessly with enemy placements. Sound=====It's ok. Weapons and monsters sound...fine. Nothing amazing. The droning soundtrack serves its atmospheric purpose. Voice acting ranges from good (totem spirits) to hilariously bad and borderline racist (Shaman Squatting Dog) to the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ protagonist. The player character really needs to shut the ♥♥♥♥ up. His emphysemic, clattering one-liners get stale very quickly, and there's something indecently aggravating about him spouting off for the 100th time about how chuffed he is to pick up bullets when he's just picked up a single arrow. There isn't much promise of better things to come with updates being few and far between, and seemingly a thing of the past. Blood West is starting to look as dead as its inhabitants.

_childDocuments_.review: Just what I needed while I wait for Elden Ring & Updates for Dota 2.Really good!EDIT.The game received many quality of life updates after my initial playthrough along with some difficulty + balancing changes.I restarted from the first chapter again before going to the new second scenario, and found the nerfs & rebalances way too harsh, ammo, healing items and alcoholic buffs seem much rarer now, also backpacks were introduced that can be duplicated for infinite amounts by just dying after buying one and revisiting that same shop, you lose inventory space for larger items than the backpacks can hold, but gain more grid slots anyway.In my first run, I never died and was always running with a full inventory and running back & forth to sell unwanted loot, so the game was pretty easy and I thought could use a bit of a buff for monsters & reduce a bit of the loot found which the devs did, but it was a bit too much IMO.Now during my second run i noticed the difficulty increase fairly early due to some items missing where i had found them the first time, so i opted my build a bit more on the melee side so I could stack some ammo for harder encounters. Turns out that the reduced healing items made melee build much harder as well, I've died over 10 times atm in my first 1,5hrs due to ranged enemies like birdmen. It feels like the difficulty bump was a bit too much. Any other players who played the game pre-nerfs that think this too?
_childDocuments_.name: Blood West

_childDocuments_.review: Wild west monster hunter with stealth elements.Weapons consist of dagger, axe, bow, revolver, winchester, long shotgun and sawn-off shotgun.You get various "artifacts" to adjust your character's stats such as HP, reload speed and more.It does have "survival" elements with limited health at the start and having to use bandages/healing to stay alive.There is also inventory and resource management as you sell monster bits and valuables to traders to keep supplied and buy new gear. (Limited inventory space)Decent amount of different monsters with completely different attacks and models. (No reskins)Music and sound is fitting.Length of game is limited but it is early access and more is to come, but is likely worth the current price if the developers deliver more content.tldr; Good game would recommend at current price for what you get (£11.49)

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game about a year ago while it was still in early access and recently came back to it once I saw that the full release came out. That being said, I just hit the 3rd act and had a good amount of fun while playing.  The gameplay is relatively simple, sneak around, get headshots, or stab an enemy in the back of the head and hope the other enemies don't see you. The enemies ai is pretty simple, and albeit- dumb; but it still feels nice skillfully sneaking around and taking out a large group of enemies without being seen or heard. The guns feel nice (especially the DB shotguns with flammable ammo), there are tons of different relics to equip to give you passive buffs which is always neat, and has a Tetris like inventory system. This game also benefits people who explore around every area and look around every nook and cranny to find hidden relics, weapons, ammo etc. I do wish some things were different about the game though, I wish the enemies AI was a bit smarter and the environment had more interactions with it, to keep the gameplay a bit more fresh and less repetitive. Overall, I still find this game pretty enjoyable and thinks the devs did a damn good job with it- overall 8/10 in my book, pretty fun game for the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Blood West

_childDocuments_.review: Blood West is a challenging but rewarding I-sim. It keeps you on your toes, even when you think you're unstoppable. Starting out, your character is very weak and isn't particularly good at anything. Guns aren't very accurate, ammo is scarce, melee is dangerous in a stand up fight, and even stealth isn't as OP as it is in other games, as you are slow and enemies can detect you easily if they're in a group. Your inventory is also pretty small, meaning you have to either be choosy about what you take or be ready to make the trek back to grab loot. Dying is the only thing you're good at doing, and even that has drastic consequences if you do it too much.Then you start finding artifacts, rare weapons and cash to improve your chances, as well as slowly gaining XP to level up into various perks, and you start to come out on top more. And then once you hit a point where you think the game is getting too easy, you make it to chapter 2 and are put right back on the bottom of the food chain, quite literally.I personally love the games monster design, which has a great wild west horror vibe. The voice acting is surprisingly good, with Gianni Matragrano and Stephen Russel being highlights. The level design is surprisingly intricate, especially in later chapters, and the more elaborate set pieces can take some time to fully explore. The shooting feels great, with the game having an emphasis on head shots which are always satisfying to pull off. Melee can also be quite fun if you specialize your build for it, and stealth gets a lot easier while still feeling risky in high population areas.If I have any complaints, it's that the first chapter can feel a bit bland. Your arsenal is pretty limited and you'll see all the enemy types within the first hour or two. It definitely shows that it was the first map iteration in the development cycle. The game gets significantly more fun in the later chapters, with more interesting enemies, weapons and artifacts that allow for some very unique ability combinations.This isn't a game for everyone but if you are looking for a challenging game that gets more rewarding as you go, this game might be right up your alley.
_childDocuments_.name: Blood West

_childDocuments_.review: Love this game so much honestly don't know what else to say. Seriously this game hits and I honestly can't recommend this game enough. TBH I really think they are undercharging for this game.My only bugbear is that I can't change around some options for accessibility.  Honestly just a Dyslexic font and being able to change the item shine to another color tho for that one I feel as if it was an intentional design choice. Also about the item shine when you know what your looking for it becomes less difficult to pick stuff out of the background.
_childDocuments_.name: Blood West

_childDocuments_.review: Imsims that run on less than godlike hardware are few and far between. This one is exemplary at combat balance, level design, and sound engineering. The storytelling is also pretty solid, but I wish there was more immersive lore and consideration for things like enemy placement and the purpose of designs. Voice acting and what lore exists is really good, and I cant complain about it given this is maybe a third of the 1.0 game. Worth the money given at the initial release, I recommend you get on the ship early if possible. Unless something in the future changes, this is a solid 8.5/10 and is worth your time as is right now.
_childDocuments_.name: Blood West

_childDocuments_.review: blood west is made looking like the old school shooters, and is a stealth-horror action FPS about carefully navigating and dealing with foes, all while trying to stay alive. It entered Early Access today, and is set to spend another half a year or so in development, as well as receive two large content updates. The game’s first section is already in place, which should last most players a few hours or so. But the question stands: is Blood West worth it in Early Access? Or are you better off stalking prey elsewhere?Blood West places you in the undead shoes of an undead man who has been recently resurrected by the Totem of Souls. This ‘being’ brought you back to supply it with energy from cursed items, or something. It’s your job to find these by carefully sneaking around this Western-themed hellscape lorded over by shambling monsters and winged gunslingers. Unlike the dev’s previous game, Elderborn, this one has a pixelated art style, which works well. And while this isn’t a Souls-like, it still has some mechanics that have been borrowed from them.As for what you do in the game, it’s quite a bit like STALKER in a lot of ways. You carefully sneak around while exploring and scavenging. Your tools consist of melee weapons and guns, which are carried in a grid-based inventory. Moving while crouched makes less noise, but enemies can still hear you. As you move, your detection level increases, so you’ll need to stop and wait for it to go back down before moving in for the kill. Hitting an unaware enemy does extra damage, plus you have both light and heavy attacks with which to dispatch them. Blood West is effectively tense in that capacity. hope you enjoy..:)
_childDocuments_.name: Blood West

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of potential, I'm excited for updates! The story is ok, I do think you can enjoy the plot, but I also don't feel like it's where the game shines most. I really enjoyed the resourse management and skill progression, and the combat is pretty good.Come on, it's a spooky western shooter with a (good) stealth system; it's everything I ever wanted. The unique guns add cool effects to your playstyle, and the death system is rather harsh (and I take that as a good thing). The enemy diversity is neat, each one feels very different from the other. Hope to see more of this good stuff in the future!
_childDocuments_.name: Blood West

_childDocuments_.review: Really solid, especially for an indie Early Access title. Some things are still a bit janky -- the writing is clearly by non-native English speakers so some of it reads or sounds off, enemies don't really react to sounds like you'd thinnk (namely they can hear you sneaking about, but don't hear you firing a gun or another creature screeching as it dies), enemies also feel a bit too spongy if you don't hit them in the head, even with really powerful weapons, and it could use a gamma option in the menu, but other than that it's quite good. Gunplay feels pretty decent and appropriately weighty and slow, enemy detection and hunting behaviors are pretty good, it looks very nice with its art style, and there's clearly a lot more yet to come. I look forward to playing more, expecially when the new regions are released.

_childDocuments_.name: Blood West

_childDocuments_.review: If you wanted the atmosphere/art style of DUSK, but with the slower methodical pacing & exploration of Thief or Dishonored (even got the voice actor of Garrett/Corvo which is great), and set in The Old West, then this is an easy recommendation. After 4 hours straight I can say I'm fully immersed and on-board for everything that this game has going on. The only negative I can think of right now is if you've played a stealth archer in any Elder Scrolls games you might become a bit OP pretty early, since while you do go down in a couple hits in open combat, you can pretty reliably one-shot 99% of enemies (in Act 1). Bullets are very limited, but they can almost seem useless since you can buy a bow and and plenty of arrows right from the start, which are silent, have better range, and are (mostly) retrievable. Also I will admit that the gameplay loop doesn't exactly seem "revolutionary," and I think a lot of this game is carried by its atmosphere, which is fine for me, but I can see being not enough for others. Outside of that though I have no real complaints; I love games that reward exploration with unique artifacts, weapons, and loot, so even if everything past Act 1 is "more of the same" this is still one of the best times I've had gaming in a while. Tense combat, rewarding exploration, Old West eldritch horrors, and Garrett audibly chastising himself for being a hoarder. This truly has it all.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly a super fun game where stealth is important its kinda easy to cheese but resource management is a must. _childDocuments_.review: Saddle up, amigos.  It's time for some Weird West hybrid souls like + stealth shooter pixel blastin'.  The three stages are well designed and allow for plenty of RPG-lite exploring and gathering to enhance your Deader's survivability.  Enemy variety is better than I expected and secrets abound.  I'm a huge fan of the Weird West genre and this indy shooter checks just about all the boxes.  It's challenging but fair and rewards careful planning, scouting and resource management.  Good solid stuff from start to finish.  If you enjoy stealth shooters, this one's an easy buy, cowpokes.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun little game, not a lot of meat right now.The game has a nice low-poly style, has an engaging inventory system, and does weapons well, with most feeling very weighty and fun to shoot around with. They handle especially well when switching between them which is fun. I like the looting aspect and the traders, but the inventory UI needs some work done on it. It uses a Resident Evil style limited space box to store items, but to my annoyance you can't swap items of the same dimensions which makes everything take longer. Ammo stacks are very small, although you wont have many bullets at any time, which is also obnoxious.Cool enemy designs and environments - a good world has been set up in this first episode.Voice acting is passable - I liked the cowboy trader, the totem was neutral, and I don't know how to feel about the shaman. Game has minor grammatical errors and probably a stereotypical view of Native Americans, which is negative, and befalls most Western videogames.Very very little to do right now, but it was a fun little game that shows competence in level and creature design, gameplay mechanics, and atmosphere. Even if it seems a little scared to do too much with it's plot, Blood West was a fun one-sitting game and I'd recommend it for the price point - as well as the promise of future content.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a pleasant surprise that I was not expecting. Cool FPS where you are a revived gunslinger back from the dead to restore balance in the barren wasteland. Some enemies can create a different chance of pace on how to approach them, be wary when facing off against a Vendigo.If there is anything to be critical of, and it's nothing major, but when selling items other traders inventory becomes full and you have to exit to the main menu and load back in again to sell items since inventory resets when loading back in, unless i missed something where there's another page/layer to sell more items when the main inventory gets full. There's a decent amount of weapons, but seeing a little bit more variety of top tier weapon choices would be welcomed as well.Other than that I look forward to seeing what new implementations happen with Blood West.

_childDocuments_.review: This is easily one of the best games I've played so far this year. There's more depth in this small open world than most AAA games. The environment is as fun and rewarding to explore as it is oppressive and terrifying. It can be tough to find your rhythm in combat at first, but it's extremely satisfying and rewarding once you do. Blood West is more than just an homage to immersive sims of the past, it feels authentic and true to the era. I saved the best for last... this game has a grid based inventory system in the same vein as S.T.A.L.K.E.R! More games need user interfaces like this that are meant to aid in immersion as opposed to the streamlined, loot-box filled messes we're so often used to these days.

_childDocuments_.name: Blood West

_childDocuments_.review: The thumbs down here is partly due to my own preference of playstyle but with some genuine issues as well, I really wish I could have got into this more.TLDR: Slow paced stealth shooter is good ONLY if you like those kind of games, I don't reallyThe Weird West setting is always a fun place to dive into (and not used enough imo) and this game certainly dives deep with gross monsters, magic, curses and more. The retro ps1-ish era look is really nice too, definitely suits this games vibe but sadly that's where the positives end for me personally.I know it's a stealth game but it's so slow it becomes painful, there's no real direction per se and I found myself wandering into an area I was woefully underprepped for and being punished because of it. The guns seem pathetic, when an axe swing can kill an enemy in one hit but a bullet can't? That seems a bit wonky. There are RPG mechanics but no way of keeping track? Does killing foes reward XP? I have no clue. The enemies are a little too punishing early on and the curse mechanic means once you've run out of curse coins it becomes even more of a difficult slog. The music isn't bad but there are long periods of time where there is little to no sound at all which is just a bit dull.If it had an easier mode or some sort of difficulty adjusting for impatient people like me that don't want to sneak around at a snails pace and have to back and forth constantly to stock up on consumables this game would probably rate a lot higher for me but as it currently stands I'd give it maybe a 6/10
_childDocuments_.name: Blood West

_childDocuments_.review: I don't normally recommend games, though considering how underground this game is, I reckoned it deserves one. One of the most immersive games I've played in recent years. Gameplay has a learning curve to keep things interesting, inventory-management and growth in your equipment (and skills) keeps things fresh, and the world is wonderfully crafted. Wish there was more, and I wish there were achievements. Everything else is great. Can't wait for chapter 3!

_childDocuments_.review: Great game - FPS RPG, imagine Bioshock in the Wild West with some horror and supernatural elements. Embraces immersive sim elements  (Prey 2017, Deus Ex, Dishonored) but boiled down to a simple premise, a good map and very satisfying mechanics.You are given a basic tutorial and allowed to go where you please. The more you explore the better loot you'll find but if you get cocky or underestimate an encounter you will be punished for it. The world is interesting with some great sound and visual design making you want to explore.It's all about sneaking, picking your battles and learning the map to best utilise the scarce resources available to you.
_childDocuments_.name: Blood West

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, one of the best games I have played in a while, Blood West is a game that mixes FPS, horror and stealth in such a great way that you can go with different playstyles and enjoy it anyways. I want to be clear about something though, and start saying that I am not a stealth gamer, but I had a lot of fun playing stealthy in this game. Reason why might be that stealth is not forced to you (yes, you need it a lot when you start, but you can just go all guns blazing after a bit, or just continue being stealthy) and it might be because of the same, but I think this game is NOT for "pro" stealth players, because they will think it is too easy to stealth their way through.In Blood West you play as an undead gunslinger and your main purpose is to purge the curse that is haunting these cursed western lands. For that, you have at your disposal an arsenal of weapons, consumables and artifacts to clear your way through hordes of horrifying enemies by shooting, burning, stabbing, throwing, blowing them up or whatever way suits you better. As I mentioned before, the game might be too easy for stealth players, but you will also find people who think this game is too hard, and the main reason is that the balance is great. Yes, you can clear your way through by stealth; yes you have an arsenal of cool weapons to blast your way through, but don't forget this is supposed to also be survival horor... So, if you mess up, you will have to be prepared, because these enemies are relentless and deal a lot of damage, making you go from a chill stealth experience to a nightmare.Atmosphere is as eerie as it should be and the retro graphics are great; don't think the enemies will lose creepyness by looking old (it might even be worse). Voice acting is also really cool and feels nice to talk to every NPC.Weapons feel great, with different types if you like to take the combats closed-range (axes and shotguns), if you like faster-paced shooting (no smg or AR though... remember, this is a western) or if you want to take on the enemies as far as you can (some really cool rifles) and you also count with different types of ammunition, to hit harder depending on the enemy.The game experience is long, divided into 3 chapters, and you will need around 20-40 hours to clear the full game, depending on the way you play it and how much you want to clear on each map, but probably the only bad aspect about the game (at least for me) is that by the end of the last chapter the game doesn't keep the pace. Don't get me wrong, each episode will include a new area, with new weapons and new enemies, being this last aspect the most interesting part, but after 30 hours you are quite acquainted about how to deal with almost everything, so you will most likely just try to rush your way to the end. Still, that doesn't mean it is bad at all, considering how much of an awesome experience this is most of the time.I would keep talking and praising this game, but it would take me too long. I mostly recommend this game to people who likes horror with shooting, or people who are into slower-paced fps and don't mind the retro graphics (like playing a retro pve version of Hunt: Showdown). You can still go for it boomer shooter style, but the first enemies might be a bit hard for that.I would rate this 9,5/10, only because, like I mentioned, I felt like just going for the end during the last hours. And if you are not convinced and are interested in some gameplay for a clearer perspective, you can watch some here
_childDocuments_.name: Blood West

_childDocuments_.review: Blood West is amazing, i'm not a huge fan of hard games, as i am extremely casual, but this game is just geniunely amazing, the slow-paced gunplay of western firearms, slowly loading your revolver as the unwashed masses approach is something that i've seen very few games accomplish, while Blood West IS unforgiving and can at times often be difficult, many of the complaints i see are extremely superficial and could be fixed with adapting to the game and its mechanics which by the way, are WAY easier than most other difficult games, i geniunely think anyone could pick this up as baby's first hard game - The biggest problem with this game is it's bossfights, they're not entirely challenging and all use addsI'm not trying to attack anyone with this review, but this is a really easy game once you get the hang of it, it's an extremely fun game and even if you have to slow down and be more cautious at times, the gameplay is extremely satisfying once you level yourself and find the right artifacts, you'll have ALOT of fun. Explore this Bloody West and find artifacts, items, even weapons to aid you in your fight.
_childDocuments_.name: Blood West

_childDocuments_.review: Great stealth - fps shooter with a neat perk system and great weapons. The looting and hording of gold reminds me of the first 2 Thief Games. The Graphics are good enough - nothing special but i like the retro charme it offers. Lighting / Shadows could be better though. The atmosphere is dark and the music ambience is awesome. The story is nothing to serious or special but it serves the purpose. Level Design is outstanding... everything seems to be placed with care and there are a lot of different ways to achieve your goal. I hope for a sequel!
_childDocuments_.name: Blood West

_childDocuments_.review: This game does exactly what it aims to do. The graphics are ugly but clear enough to give a visual cue of when to dodge. The sound design is basic but carried by decent voice acting. The stealth system is fluid, the stone throws allow diversions, and sneak attacks almost always kill. Combat is possible but you need to do a running battle. The loot system is fun and rewarding. Exploration is rewarding. The level design understands what made Dark Soul so fun: nook and crannies, connected areas, verticality. I've already played ten hours and finished the first area and I'd say I already got my money's worth of fun. This is what an indie game should be.
_childDocuments_.name: Blood West

_childDocuments_.review: Blood West is about a resurrected cowboy thief, wrecking a local economy (Jim) by killing, and re-killing, the undead inhabitants of a town that succumbed to its own endless greed. Only the first scenario of three planned ones is currently available, but there is plenty to do and multiple ways to do it. I managed to squeeze 7 hours out of my first playthrough, and I barely messed around with some of the available weapons and artifacts, so I could definitely see myself doing a second playthrough of it at some point.The game has some sense of "Dark Souls" mechanics, in that dying (or resting) causes some of the enemies you've killed to come back, and death comes with negative side effects you'll have to manage before they get out of hand. Sadly, however, I found the game way too easy in this current build, only dying once, so I can't actually say much about what these negative side effects actually entail, but if they're anything like they were in the demo, then I know some of them can be particularly nasty (FX lowering maximum health or stamina).Other than the game being too easy my only real issue with it would be there being a ton of grammatical errors, lack of graphics options (had some bothersome screen-tearing at points), and the UI being kinda ugly, though that third point is definitely not a major concern for an Early Access build.Overall, highly recommended, look forward to future updates and other stuff from Hyperstrange, and hope development goes smoothly!

_childDocuments_.review: I didnt enjoy it. Every mechanic is deliberately constructed to be against player, and character feels very slow and weak. After dying you get a debuff like - few % of health or stamina, and 3 of them make more powerful curse (like -20% total hp) which is annoying as hell.Inventory is like tetris (old Diablo-like games come to mind), but newer h'n's at least have auto-sorting enabled so you can clean this quite fast. Here you have to drag and drop every damn item every few minutes you find something useful to sell. _childDocuments_.review: Spoilers ahead.If Clint Eastwood and Ash Williams had a bastard child this would be it. Start to finish I was engaged and enjoyed every second. I didn't want to test my luck against enemies at first, so stealth was my only viable option.. and it did have tense moments. By the time I had rat ♥♥♥♥♥♥ my way to the Orb of Night and Bone Knife the rest just fell into place, I was so confident that nothing was threatening. The gameplay loop is fun, but I have small pieces of constructive criticism. 1. More variation in enemies would make the already good gameplay loop exponentially better.2. More weapon variety, even if just changing the skin of a pre-exisiting weapon. I went in with zero spoilers and was bummed when I found the Hermit Stick 2 minutes before game over.3. In a game that rewards exploration, which it did to me numerous times, there is so much in the world that feels barren or overlooked. Don't get me wrong, finding the Decapitator or a random nugget made me extremely happy, but there were other times where I felt as if I was looking in vain.4. Maybe this is intentional, but once I figured out what worked where, nothing phased me. My last 30 minutes was at the Burial Grounds then the Boss Chamber. I walked through the 4-5 Vendigos like it was nothing, had it down to a science. And the boss was painfully disappointing, especially considering there was no fan service at the end. It just was. I smoked the boss in under a minute while the lone Vendigo between Tower and Farm took an hour and a half to work around.Now for the good-1. The NPCs are perfect, every piece of dialogue feels great. From the first time I talked to the Bone Shaman, I was hooked.2. The risk vs reward factor never left, even when I was seconds away from the boss chamber. Should I go on a quest now for a better tomorrow? I genuinely had to think about my actions.3. Inventory management is executed perfectly, should I carry 30 extra rounds of short ammo or do I need to pack extra molotovs? ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ genius implementation.4. The style and feel is lovely, if not a bit empty at times.5. The interior environments had so much life, and each location told a silent story. I love that you didn't jam everything down my throat, all was ambiguous. Finding notes on monsters was one of my favorite experiences, and I loved that sometimes I just had to figure it out. The story is communicated well enough through the totems but tenfold through context clues and notes. So well done.All in all I'm excited for the next two scenarios and I can't wait to see what you bring to the table. 9/10 all day for me.

_childDocuments_.review: The stealth isn't good enough to make it a stealth game. The shooting isn't good enough to make it a boomer shooter. This game fails really badly at making its fundamentals actually FUN. Stealth is bare bones and un-immersive. Something so simple as the iconic stealth game "Sneak up behind them and GET them" is made an agonizing process, of crouching behind them, walking slowly towards them, stopping.... waiting for the audio detection meter to go down... then creeping again. rinse and repeat till you're close enough to stab them and whoops! someone else saw you, or they turned around, or your infinite stash of rocks turned out to not be distracting enough, or you biffed your shot, and now what was supposed to be a silent kill ends up with everyone knowing exactly where you are, and ripping you to pieces. The stealth is a complete simplification and actual downgrade of stealth in games like Theif or Deus Ex. Enemies AI is stupid and ridiculous. with how they all know exactly where you are and beeline for you, how they all approach a corpse to get a good gawk at it, how they un-immersively snap to aggression and make it so clear that they are poorly programmed enemy ai and not scary monsters. Games like these often have a means of risk control. Allowing you to be really slow and undetectable visually  and audibly, or to move faster and be more conspicuous. You play the game of risk and reward, trading speed and betting you can close the gap quicker than they can notice you. However this game has only the 3 speeds. Sprinting, which gets you noticed instantly so it is not a factor in stealth gameplay, Walking, which is almost just as loud and conspicuous, and crouching, which, even with max sneaking stats, buffs, and items, still hardly allows you to step around without needing to stop every few seconds for the enemies to forget they heard anything i guess, which is also ridiculous because... they can hear me... or at least are hearing SOMEthing, but i guess it doesn't exist to them yet until it makes an arbitrary amount of noise for long enough. Yeah, i can hear footsteps trailing behind me for about 5 feet, but if i hear a SIXTH footstep, so help me god i'll whip around and roar and them really loudly and let all my friends know telepathically where they are.And now once the enemy notices you, detection propagation makes it a big big problem, and the punishments for failure are severe. There is no immersion in the stealth. There are few ways to go about stealth. Your stealth tools are minimal, and throwing rocks does NOT a stealth game make. In total the whole experience feels really bad, for something that is supposedly the main draw for the game. In a perfect world, this game would be a survival horror that put the power back in the bullet. Ammunition as a limited, but intensely powerful resource used to get you out of a jam when caught, as a tool for picking off enemies from afar, and watching them scramble as you snipe them, and as a means of giving value to putting a gun in one of your weapon slots. Melee weapons or other ammunition like arrows, throwing knives, bolts and so on being the typical stealth tools, requiring precision, risk of proximity or clever thinking, but of course being essentially infinite given methodical play. Bullets could be so much cooler, if using them put down enemies in one or two shots. Making silver bullets put down enemies in one. Gold bullets could be given some other use like increasing loot drops, or just being cool loot items to sell that function the same as silver bullets, but ask the player if they'd rather save their gold, or burn the bullets. The player would care so much more about every round they shoot. Every bullet a gun could hold. Make sure that every time their bare the shotgun, those precious shells are put to good use. Instead, Enemies are tanky. Take a bunch of bullets to put down if shot anywhere but close and to the head. and eat shotgun shells for breakfast unless the barrels are in their mouth. bullets become meaningless after a while. I am really disappointed by the stealth in this "Stealth Game". Stealth is among my favorite types of gameplay, and this game makes a mockery of stealth gameplay. There's a reason metal gear, or splinter cell, or even thief didn't need to give you infinite rocks to throw. But hey. Toss a rock, and go crouch walk your way right by. That sounds like fun right? That sounds like it asked you to think cleverly about how to avoid an enemies line of sight, or area of detection. Hopefully this games mechanics get better on a fundemental scale. It has enough atmosphere and aesthetic and one liners to make me replay it every now and then. But every single time i am disappointed by terrible stealth gameplay, and an un-immersive experience. This game is so close to being everything i want it to be. everything i know it can be. I hope that maybe with some NEW-BLOOD (See what i did there), hopefully someone takes a look at this game, and gloomwood, and considers a thing or two. Till then... maybe go replay deus ex again.

_childDocuments_.review: Its a pretty wild little game. I'd describe this as a FPS rogue-like with a few RPG elements. It does have a bit of a horror/scare bend to it and death comes quicklyCombat isn't easy, exploration is interesting and varied. It probably took me a few hours to figure out how to sneak around more and fight straight up less - fights costs you resources and health which are challenging to get back. Its better to sneak attack as much as possible or headshot if you get caught. Even run away if there are multiple enemies.Graphics are Quake1/Quake2 like - but it doesn't mean it doesn't play well. Enemies are annoying and vary their attack until you learn how to approach them. Still not entirely sure how to deal with the screaming heads for example. There is a skill tree, but it doesn't super overpower your character, just small improvements. I dunno, its quite an interesting concept and I can see where they add lots here and make it awesome.I like games which are an uphill battle and this is definately one of them!I should add - this game does rely on you sneaking and using head shots often. Straight up shooting enemies wastes a lot of ammo and leaves you in a bad spot. Using a close combat weapon to sneak attack enemies is also very important. You will die, but you will learn how to do it. Recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like reloading, stranger?8 seconds to load 6 rounds into a revolver, 14 seconds to load 10 rounds into a rifle.No hyperbole - I love every painstaking second I spend crouched behind a crate, feverishly shoving round after round into my weapons, listening for the creak of floorboards coming closer and the ethereal whisper of some wretched undead thing, wondering if they'll pop 'round the corner before I get the last round in.8 seconds to reload my revolver, 14 seconds to reload my rifle.I probably spend far too much time unloading the weapons I'm holding (they added a shortcut so you can take enemy ammunition, but it works on your equipped guns, too!) and watching in mesmerized silence as my gravel-gargling cowboy plonks a bullet into the cylinder, slowly spins it, grabs another round, thumbs that one in, and on...8 seconds for my revolver, 14 seconds for my rifle.I experience the purest joy whenever I buy or discover a new weapon because I get to learn exactly how long it takes to reload from empty. Step outside, take a few practice shots, hit R, and watch the show all over again.8 seconds, 14 seconds.And, hey, every weapon reloads one round at a time, so I can always interrupt it in a firefight! With how much noise I'm making firing a .45 willy-nilly into the dead silent night air, I will, assuredly, be interrupted.8, 14.So I'll ask again, stranger: do you like reloading?

_childDocuments_.review: What a cool "little" game! I bought it thinking I would complete it rather quickly, but instead I've taken more than 25 hours just to complete the first chapter and get into the second chapter.This is definitely not a run and gun shooter. You need to be very careful and utilize your stealth skills to gain the upper hand on mobs. If you try to rush in and take them head on, you can easily find yourself overwhelmed in a hurry and the game is unforgiving of that. Plan your exit strategies before engaging for when you miss an important shot, or when you get bum rushed by more mobs than you counted on. I was concerned that the game would be too hard, but the devs made sure you have more than one way to remove curses after death, and the overall balance is just fine. Some things I like: The stash is apparently infinite in size, so you can hoard all that you want for those special fights if you so choose. I like the weapon types, the unique weapons and artifacts that accommodate different play styles. I like the skills that I get to level up. The ambiance and atmosphere is excellent. You can close your eyes and know whether you're outdoors in a desert, or swamp, or inside of a cave - the sound keeps you locked in and immersed. I thought maybe the pixelated graphics would bother me but I got over it in the first couple of minutes. Easily love this game more than some prettier triple A titles I've played. Some tips for new players in no particular order are as follows: 1. There is a type of potion that you can buy to remove flaws. 2. There are multiple cursed gold tokens which you can use to bless yourself at the soul totem to prevent being cursed upon death. 3. Max out points in 'Gold Prospector', this will cause mobs to have a much higher drop rate, which means more money items but also more cursed gold coin chance as well. I'm less than 50% into the game and I already have 23 spare coins in my stash so they aren't that rare. 4. When you get your first Wendigo heart, keep it, and use it to passively get your health back up to 100% before your next fight, then switch it out for something else, this way you save on all other health recovery items. 5. Don't be afraid to buy consumables like arrows, ammo, etc. because the shops replenish their items. 6. Take your time to explore and look on top of, behind, and underneath objects in the game world, you will sometimes be rewarded for your keen eye. I've found many an item carefully tucked between vis-block game objects. I hope the developers hear me when I ask them to continue development, bring us Chapter 4 and beyond. I'm only in Chapter 2 but I'm dreading completing the game. This game may not have gone truly viral yet (I don't know if it has at least), but it's a sleeper game. Give it time, don't try to cater to any and all complaints, don't make it too easy, stay on the course you guys have already set and people will keep buying your game and future work you guys ship out.

_childDocuments_.review: Blood West would best be described as a semi-open world immersive sim. The game is split into three acts, each of which is a large, open ended map with plenty to find. A blind play through will provide a fulfilling exploration experience. On the other hand, knowing where items are means you can get some good gear early, providing you can reach it without being torn to shreds by monsters. This pairs well with the degree of build variety on offer for plenty of replay value.Stealth is present in the style of the Thief games with the ability to lean around corners and enemy line of sight that is extremely consistent. Melee combat is very competent and, as someone who has spent thousands of hours between Vermintide and Darktide, I definitely appreciated how tight the hitboxes felt on enemy heads.While stealth is generally encouraged, direct combat is still viable and enjoyable. The western setting somewhat limits the available arsenal (revolvers, lever actions, double barrel shotguns, bows, crossbows, breech loading rifles) but it's more than adequate with good aim. The enemies are varied, creative in their designs and challenging to fight.Light souls-like elements are present in the form of beds that will act as a checkpoint, fully heal you and revive some enemies. Dying also causes "soul flaws" that will merge into a strong curse after multiple deaths. These can be removed with a limited item or by completing a challenge provided by an NPC.My only minor issues with the game would be the voice acting and the overall level of difficulty. The voice work is unfortunately somewhat inconsistent. The main character is voiced by the legendary Stephen Russell and the most prominent NPC is played by Gianni Matragrano. Some of the other voice work sounds amateurish, especially by comparison. I found that the difficulty dropped off dramatically by late game and I had so much ammo and other items in my stash that the game was chugging every time I opened it. That said, the good aspects heavily outweigh the bad and I would definitely recommend this game if what I've mentioned appeals to you.

_childDocuments_.review: Sooo, it kinda is a 6.5 out of 10 / 7 out of 10.The low poly-style reminded me of the times when I played Outlaws on my old PC.But this game is the Dark Souls of Western-games.Pros:- cool looking environement- a vast array of weapons (bows, different six-shots, rifles, shotguns, dynamite etc.)- a vast array of enemies (normal zombie / ghoul, gold-digger, bird-guys, former saloon-dancers...)- an open world to explore (towns, outposts, an abandon train-wreck, and much more) - slight RPG-mechanics (guns have different stats, you can increase the stats of your char)Cons: - dying-mali (I died three times due to the bird-guys being so hard to hit and got a malus in stealth - which is kinda essential in dispatching of the enemies easily; died again and my health was lowered) - no real tutorial (reading each item-description is mandatory to understand the games mechanics) - ammo can be rather scarce (looted a few revolvers, but didn't know that you could unload them and sold the ammo in them too)- guns not really accurate against enemies (I kinda had the issue, that when I tried to aim, my char would begin to wiggle with his hand like in CoD, when you hold your breath as a sniper too long and the ironsight bounces around)Neutral:- Don't sell the coins!!! Gold YES, Coins NO! Those Coins can save you at least from getting one Malus each, when you have one equiped when you die. Conclusion: It has a nice premisse, but it isn't for western-fans who expect Red Dead Undead or Outlaws.  Buy it in a 50 % sale.

_childDocuments_.review: What a game! It has been a while I haven't felt so immersed in a video game world as I was during my playtime with Blood West!Great game design with a beautifully implemented mix of stealth, survival, and exploration. The story is simple but intriguing, combat is responsive and complex, and power progression is satisfying with xp gains and skill point trees; which gives the player several build options on how to approach the game. However, what makes this exceptional is the resulting ambience that all these game components create to suck you in, and make you care about your every-single step!My first few hours were a slog though, this game is WAY HARDER than I expected, even reading reviews of how hard it was, I wasn't prepared. I haven't played other stealth games like this one before (review's point to STALKER which is next on the list), but it took me a while during Chapter 1 to understand how I was supposed to approach the game. I ended up going with a full stealth + crossbow + cursed shotgun build as that is what worked the best with my play-style.Amazing experience that I definitely won't forget anytime soon. If you are at all interested in this game I highly recommend you give it a try!

_childDocuments_.review: Time to flip this review from negative to positive, wahey! Feels good being able to do that.As a quick note:My previous review was negative but focused largely on two main issues (despite the game being pretty damn good) - the first being a small fuss regarding save deletion, as the game would not prompt you if you clicked "Delete Save" by mistake, thus instantly obliterating your save file with no warning. The second was more severe, whereas the game would sometimes CTD when looting enemy corpses which would corrupt the game save, deleting all entities and interactables from the map you were on, thus rendering the game impossible to complete. I lost three playthroughs to that CTD issue and then when the fourth got deleted instantly without warning through a misclick I decided to make a negative review.Well, I can happily say those issues are taken care of now! A recent patch has added a slew of fixes, including multiple back up saves, a prompt on save deletion AND somehow massive performance increases up to +30FPS and +70% performance overall, which is basically something you never hear of these days...a finely optimised game? Whoa! Solid gold! While admittedly I can't say for sure 100% that the CTD issue is fixed (there's older patch notes about an issue concerning ALT+F4ing out of the game causing maps to have enemies / objects deleted being fixed, but my issue was a CTD issue and I still experienced enemy / entity deletion from a CTD after that patch + people have been reporting the glitch happening to them recently so perhaps the bug has resurface) I haven't had any crashes or hitches like my first few playthroughs, so it seems alright to me, anyway.So, onwards with the proper review:The game itself is really fun and innovative to play, it's one of those nice "free" games that doesn't hold your hand and hurries you along, you can take your time, explore, go where you want when you want to and handle things in whatever order you desire and how you like, which is instantly a fantastic thing. It's also responsive without feeling floaty, granting you a range of movement without the clunk behind it. There are limited RPG elements as well, with you earning XP and then choosing perks to define your character / playstyle, but without a rigid structure involved. Each map has a few quests you can complete as well.It's also not fond of babysitting the player. You don't regenerate health, and enemies don't respawn unless you die (and even then, only a handful at a time, not the whole lot) - you have to manage limited resources and loot the world for supplies, which also don't respawn. Vendors exist with limited restocking inventories however and melee weapons exist and don't require ammo or have durability, so you can't softlock yourself somehow if you put yourself in a bad corner with no gear to get out. Very good! It has a retro style of graphics but it's not ultra low poly - texturing looks like something out of a PS1 game perhaps, but the poly count feels more modern - it's no AAA game that sells on graphical quality alone (and thank God for that, eh?) but the graphical quality isn't ugly, either. It's pretty neat, in my opinion. Retro stuff done right, not hamfisted and in your face about it, you can tell what everything is as soon as you see it. It also helps performance, the game isn't going to tax your system or need a high end PC to play.Devs are pretty friendly and responsive in the discussions and are quite open to suggestions and new ideas, at least reading them if not actually implementing them! They're steadily working on new content for the game, we've already seen a bunch of patches since release including a big content update that added Part 2 (out of a planned 3 parts) which added a brand new big map with lots of new weapons, artifacts, enemies and places to explore. The game definitely doesn't seem in danger of being abandoned - devs themselves have hinted that Part 3 won't be the end of the games life cycle and instead will receive some more quality updates after the fact as well. Great!It's a very fun game to play, survival horror in its own Western style, with perfect sized open maps to explore without falling into the "open world but nothing in it" trap that you might expect with this kind of thing. The maps offer some good verticality as well, plus has areas you can see from one location and then eventually reach later as you explore, which is always fun. You start out with nothing and through your own hand become a force to be reckoned with. If you like first person games that aren't all about running and gunning, having room for stealth and benefitting from applying your noggin' before joggin' headfirst into problems, then I can absolutely fully recommend this game to you!Also, there's an extremely voluptuous enemy / character in the game! You should buy it for that reason alone! It makes a nice change when devs allow women to be women and not ironing boards, wahey!DLC soon, yay!
