_childDocuments_.review: OK, now longer version. is a great, stealth based game based in supernatural world filled with ghosts, zombies and other monsters during the western era. So already 10/10 for the setting.Now, you're the guy raised from the dead and sent to banish the evil spirits that made that world into the hell on earth. To your arsenal you have what you would expect from a typical western setting - revolvers, lever action rifles, double barrel shotguns, bows, knives, axes, sticks of TNT and molotovs. With some artifacts to improve your fight, elixirs and alcohols. Ammo is in small amounts so going in guns blazing is rarely an option. As you are pretty squishy yourself, you are highly encouraged to avoid direct encounters and stealth your way around enemies, taking them out one by one with melee or bows. is that it's fairly short, with me being able to get all there was on the map in around 6 hours and buggy in some places, but it's an early access game, so I hope the game is gonna get fixed and expanded as the ending shows that there's more coming for us.Well, good luck cowboys, you're gonna need that.

_childDocuments_.review: Tl;DR: it's a fun, semi-open world game with a grid-based inventory and light RPG elements. Slightly flawed, but worth your time with great atmosphere and fun world to explore.The RPG elements are standard skilltree stuff, nothing special. You get to go about exploring the world and tackling the quests in any manner you see fit, with plenty of optional areas to find trinkets that help you form builds and unique weapons that add quirks to your build in fun ways. You got your Re4-styled inventory system and dying is built in to the gameplay as an anti-savescum feature. When you die, you start in a safe zone with a level 1 curse that acts as a minor debuff, and if you die 3 times in a row you get a full blown curse that is a major debuff. This sounds scary but you have multiple ways of getting rid of the curses that are all easy and accessible to do. It's a game in three acts and all acts are fine with a nice sense of escalation, but the bosses certainly leaves something to be desired, the same situation is present with the ending itself. But for the price-tag, you get a fun if not slightly flawed game that hints at a sequel of some form. I still recommend it, even if i personally felt the ending was unsatisfying.

_childDocuments_.review: This one is a really tough review, mostly because I loved the first act of this game immensely. It is genuinely an incredibly fun and well made game, and I think the first six-eight hours of immersive sim-lite old west stealth horror gameplay that constitute a full run of Act 1 justify the price.My problem is that the second act, which was released well after this game got most of its positive reviews, fails to capture the magic of the first, and wasn't fun enough to keep me playing. Below are some comparisons of how the systems work well in the first act, and fail in the second.Inventory Management and Cash:-In Act 1 The inventory management starts off as a series of interesting decisions about what you keep and what you leave behind. You have limited slots, and are forced to use basically every weapon type to make your ammo go far enough for the first half of Act 1. Enemies are dangerous, healing items aren't plentiful. By the end of Act 1, you will have two bags that give you expandable sub-inventories (which are very annoying to use, but necessary) and you will likely have dozens of extra rounds of most ammo types, and more healing items than you can use. Not to worry though, you can sell most of this stuff so that you can earn enough money to buy the special weapons that the merchants have, which are cool carrots to motivate the player. A healing potion sells for $40, the rare gold nugget drop off a mob gives $70, and a rusty revolver taken off a dead cultist sells for like $7. For reference the unique items the merchants have cost anywhere from $300 to $1000. In pursuit of these cool weapons and accessories, you get in the habit of just picking up everything, and when you don't have enough room, you just run back and sell, and then resume your adventure where you stopped. Its equal parts tedious and satisfying, and I ended up taking the +inventory space, and +drop chance perks to boost my income. But as I played through Act 1, I eventually gained enough money to buy the cool unique weapons I wanted, and I felt like the cash progression was rewarding. -In Act 2, you are instantly introduced to the only merchant you will be meeting for a long time. She has new unique items! How Fun! Sadly, they cost $3000-$7000, and while the body parts you find on mobs in Act 2 sell for more, they don't sell for that much more (also, the average drop takes up more space compared to Act 1). This really pushes the tedious packmuling back and forth to merchant to its limit, and after 2+ hours running back and forth like a ♥♥♥♥♥, still unable to afford the items I wanted, I decided I was done and stopped playing.Stealth and combat:  -Combat is tense, and stealth is fun in Act 1. The two work together to form a satisfying balance, rewarding the player for untangling enemy patrols and enemy formations, with the ever present threat of high risk melee combat always looming. The level design is well suited to a variety of gameplay options, and I left Act 1 very impressed with the map design, and the combat feel in general. -Combat in Act 2 is much slower and cheesier, and stealth sucks. The enemies are beefy, taking many shots to kill and having too much health to safely backstab most of the time (unless you get the elusive sneak attack melee headshot, which is hard when everyone is hunched like Pudge from Dota). They also tend to be grouped in large enough packs that engaging in melee is suicide unless you pick off all other members of a group first, and at that point why not just pick the last member off as well? This was when the failing of the AI become very apparent. Upon seeing their friends get shot in the head, enemies will run over, stand where their friend stood, and look bewildered, ready to get shot in the head themselves. The problem of annoying encounter design is exacerbated by the fact that the beautiful canyon map of the first act had its interesting geography, differentiated areas, and cool building layouts replaced with a drab swamp full of large open areas, with only the expansive recessed swamp pools and trees to break them apart. Progression:-By the end of Act 1, you will have every perk relevant to your preferred playstyle. There just aren't that many perks, and many of them are quality of life perks. I was fine with this though, since the set of perks you are picking from in the Canyons map is clearly labeled "Canyons", implying there would be a new set of perks for the next zone. And there are new perks. Four of them (down from Act 1's 32 perks). They are fairly strong perks, each offering a significant upgrade to the various playstyles, but also I bought every perk that I wanted from that list with the leftover points I had stored up from Act 1 upon entering the map, and was then left with no character growth to look forward to. The other metric by which you progress is item progression, but I've already detailed why that is tedious as hell in Act 2. All in all, I think the first Act of this game is brilliant, and worth the price. I think the second is hard to get through, and frustrating. I hope for the fans' sake, they refocus the game in the third act, but I don't think I'll bother finishing the second act to ever see it.

_childDocuments_.review: A surprisingly well made game, I was a bit hesitant as a psx style game with gunplay is a gamble in itself; However, I have nothing but praise for this game, combat 8/10, world 7/10, and story is interesting as well. _childDocuments_.review: I understand that a lot of people like this game, however it is just not for me. You character dies in a couple of hits from most standard enemies, if you don't get a head shot on an enemy you might as well have breathed on them for how effective it is and if you do anything aside from stealth you are going to have your butt handed to you. _childDocuments_.review: Fantastic indie open world game, held back from perfection only by a few minor gripes.TL;DR: I wasn't expecting to like this game very much but it hooked me quickly and I wasn't able to put it down until the credits rolled; the moment-to-moment gameplay is fantastic and if you're a fan of the thief/dishonored style of open level stealth/combat exploration you'll likely enjoy this as wellPros:- Great gunplay and moment-to-moment gameplay- Well designed world to explore- Tons (maybe too many) of unique named weapons and trinkets to collect each with their own modifiers that vary from minor stat adjustments to stuff that will totally change how you approach the game- Awesome atmosphere and a pretty great variety of enemies to fight (many of which require unique approaches to defeat)- Great voice acting for an indie title+/-:- Very stealth-heavy gameplay (at least until you get the tools and traits unlocked that let you be more aggressive)- Not a strong focus on an overarching narrativeCons:- Enemy AI isn't fantastic and this can be exploited fairly easily (although I found this didn't take as much away from the game as I expected it to)- The writing/English localization is not great, and this applies to both the dialogue in the game and item descriptions- The inventory management systems are serviceable but not fantastic (particularly when it comes to handling items stored in the sub-inventory compartments you can acquire ); this becomes a pretty big problem if you, like myself, feel compelled to loot everything that's not nailed to the floor
_childDocuments_.name: Blood West

_childDocuments_.review: Oh well... I had a real problem about whether I should recommend this game or not. From one perspective it is a very well done game, with a lot of work put into this but on the other side it is just a simple game with rather primitive game-play loop... . Until the end of the game I could not decide but the ending sealed the decision for me...Pros:- Interesting and satisfactory weapons. Game has quite a lot of weapons with different stats and abilities. In general it is fun to use those weapons.- Nice design of the enemies. It has a feel of the wild west and some American folklore.- Good map design. Each of the places are believable and could pass as a real place where NPC could live their lives.- Exploration rewards you with a lot of items that help through the game.- NPC are in general nicely written and fun to interact with.Cons:- Simple game-play loop. You have a quest, you go to the location, get what you need and then go back to the NPC quest giver... and it is like that for the whole game. It would be nice to have some more quest variety. Maybe doing something together with other NPC etc.- AI of the enemies. Enemies are... just wandering around in various places. Just like some old MMO enemy spawn point. When you play stealthy you are almost always guaranteed that the enemy will place itself in a direction that allows you to stealthy take them down either it is a close range weapon or long one. There is even a mechanic that allows you to throw rocks in order to distract the enemy but it is never needed because enemies are brain dead. If you have stealth stat high enough it becomes very comical because you can just get to the front of the enemy and stealthily take him down even though you are clearly visible to him. When you take an enemy down with other enemies in the vicinity the other enemy just goes to see his dead buddy and then goes back to wandering around... and it applies to all enemies. Enemies should have some more AI states that for example are looking for you etc. Instead of that it is very boring, especially since you will be going to do that through the whole game... . Maybe have different types of AI for various enemies, make them do something instead of just wandering around aimlessly. Lastly you can always run away, it is quite easy to do, just give your enemy some obstacles that you can jump over but enemy has to make a detour. - Game is fairly easy because of the simple game-play loop and simple enemy AI. The only difficulty that this game has is that the player is not aware of some things in the game. After getting familiar with the game it is fairly simple... and boring. I only died once in Chapter 1, I fell from the bridge because I had to pick up the phone.- Ending. - Skill tree. After Chapter 1 I had every skill that I needed. Rest of them were just useless or very situational. It also made exploration and gaining experience less exacting.Chapter 1 was cool, I had fun. In chapter 2 I started to see the crack in the game reality and in chapter 3 I lost all the immersion. The worst thing that a game can do to you is to remind you that you are playing a game and this game did for me exactly that. I wanted to drop it but I have dropped or not finished a lot of games recently. I thought that maybe at least it would give me a bad ass ending but no... . I cannot recommend this game, even though it has quite a lot of cool and nice things in it but the core game-play loop of the game is just bad.

_childDocuments_.review: The best "boomer sneaker"!This was a very nice surprise. It's been long since I've played a really good "immersion" sim, the last one was probably Prey. Though in theory, you can go guns blazing, this game is about stealth and careful approach... and dying. No save scumming for you. When you die, unless you protected yourself (and used either a blessing slot or one of 3 artifact slots for this), you gain a soul flaw, which can with additional deaths turn into a bad curse. You can remove those of course, but it takes time, money or patience, so fearing the death is constant (and upon your respawn, a lot of enemies respawn too - though that means more money for trophies from respawned enemies).The game has "only" 3 levels, but each will take you maybe a day of play or more, taking you on a journey of undead (and possibly drunk) cowboy through weird west ravaged by undead curse. Every level is a small open world, up to you what you do and how. You carefully sneak upon enemies, snipe them, charge them (and die), you look for cursed artifacts, level up your character, constantly battle too small inventory, rearrange your artifacts... and have fun, if you're like me and love stealth immersion sims.It took me about 40 hours to finish first playthrough and I'm definitely going for another one, when I'll find time. And now I demand more "boomer sneakers"The negatives:There are some, of course, though it's mostly nitpicking. The inventory management is incredible pain in the ass. Sort doesn't work much, new items are not placed in the backpacks, you spend a lot of time rearranging stuff here and there. Annoying and time consuming.For some, it will be too difficult. For me it was about perfect, though there were moments were I wanted to rage quit.The story and writing is... Ok. It fits the game and mood, on the other hand, the handful of talking characters are more like decoration. It feels like a wasted potential.I really hope that the team behind this will make more games like this :)
_childDocuments_.name: Blood West

_childDocuments_.review: FPS immersive sim lite set in a horror western setting. Clearly a labor of love and made by a Hunt Showdown fan.The good:- Maps are very open, lots of secrets, side paths to explore.- Good VA- Setting and visuals if you are into horror, western and retro (at least you don't recoil at the sound of those words)- The mechanics all works very well together sticking closely to the im-sim formula. Some may say uninspiring, but other may call it "if it ain't broke don't fix it".- Some rudimentary form of choices and consequences in Chapter 2 to 3.- Interesting enemies each with different behaviorsThe could be better:- You only have one save per run. I have not managed to make saves in previous chapters.- The skills are uninspiring. They are just there to make you slightly better than before in your core stats.- Weapons from new chapters clearly outclasses previous ones: You are just in an arms race with AI health- AIs are very simple. They have limited detection radius, forget about you quickly and don't work together- Weapon balance are iffy: Anything other than headshots don't do very much and is effectively a waste of ammo, coupled with high AI damage you either hit your hs or die trying. - Your stash size affect your fps. I started the game with 160+ and ended it with 40+ in Chapter 3 because I have too many items in my stash. This is a known issue.

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed Blood West!Up to now, the EA offers around 10 hours of gameplay, if you don't rush, which is not advised unless you like to make things harder than it should be. It's almost 1.5$ per hour, so skip one meal at a cheap restaurant and get this game!At the moment, there's one big level out of the 3 planned in total. The first level is in the night desert, plagued with monsters of the West American folklores. There is enough variety in them but a few of them more wouldn't have hurt!You can level up you character and invest points in passive skills like "find 10% more gold items" or "sneaking is 25% easier", etc. II found the game challenging enough either with gun blazing or sneaking, although the skills for the latter makes the game easier.The voice acting puts you in the mood of the game.The graphics, in old pixel style like the PS1 era, is a matter of taste. Personally, I found it gave something special to the atmosphere and you're not overloaded with stuff on screen. It goes straight to the point, as much of the rest of the game with no half-assed features.Let's see the future updates & levels (swamp), but for the price I higly recommand it :)

_childDocuments_.review: I am in love with this game. Bought it on a whim and didn't know exactly what to expect, but ended up loving it from start to finish.It started a bit difficult and confusing and I kept dying until I understood the stealth system well enough. Stealth might be the cause of issues for most people not liking the game. It is not Thief, it is not deep or too smart, but it does its job and keeps the game fun. It is pretty arcady and enemies are sometimes stupid and unpredictable. Some playstyles are probably not as viable as they would seem in the beginning (most melee options seemed inferior to me).But once the gameplay clicks with you, the levels become your playground of stealth and headshots. Exploration is encouraged and the new weapons/loot are often unique and rewarding. Gunplay is satisfying and gory. Atmosphere is great. Enemy design is cool and it stayed varied throughout the game, and they kept introducing new and interesting foes far after I thought they would run out of steam.The game is such a joy to play and I wish it immediately rolled me into NewGame+ or something, because i just wanted it to keep going. More of this, please.

_childDocuments_.review: Splattercat was right, after seeing his video recommendation and having spent several hours into the game myself i must agree: this game is Good & Fun. There's just something that this game does that just makes it work, is enjoyable and the nice art style makes it pretty timeless as well, especially the swamp is a big step up. is it perfect? NO, for example you can cheese some enemies with doorways that will mess up their AI pathing (due to size constraints and their targeting) and there are some other minor annoyances like enemies respawning when they shouldn't after using an item, enemy shotgun pellets going near everywhere but hit you (which can be considered a good thing haha) and other small things alike. similarly the canyons map could use a touchup on a few things after rummaging through the swamp map and seeing the various QoL improvements made there which didn't trickle back down (like information note names for one)But hey, all things considered it's great. So grab your shotgun, six shooter, bow, axe or whatever else you fancy to chase after "Evil" and be careful not to die. Revolver and shotgun headshot simulator, 10/10 would want to play with the Vendigo's again.

_childDocuments_.review: I am recommending the game, but I really wish steam reviews offered something between "recommend" and "don't recommend".The game's trailer on steam implies that you will have some kind of action-packed experience. 90% of the time, you will not. It also implies that you will have some kind of control over what you focus your build on. You won't. You can make certain things you do easier/more effective, but you will need to use all the tools and options given to you about equally in the first act. In the other two acts, you have to use stealth weapons like the crossbow or melees, and you have to get headshots. The main cause for the issues described above is this: Enemies are extremely tanky unless you hit them in the head, and once they've spotted you, most of them move around too much to reliably hit in the head, and kill you extremely quickly. The most effective way to play this game is to be stealthy and to get headshots, and every other approach is so much riskier and more wasteful that it isn't worth doing. That said, I found it fun to explore the maps and get good at the stealth mechanics. I'm just annoyed that it's not the action-packed experience the trailer made me expect.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: - A Stealth Immersive Sim with elements of Survival-Horror and STALKER set in the Weird West sub-genre; Blood West is a thrilling yet intense experience from start to finish with a retro aesthetic and challenging yet satisfying combat; rewarding players for exploration and staying in the shadows. -*Update: Chapter 2 essentially improves upon Chapter 1 in almost every way imaginable and more or less sets the standard for upcoming chapters along with giving you a taste of the game's true potential.*The first couple hours or so is admittedly slow and punishing where stealth is essentially your ONLY option due to the fact that you're (intentionally) under powered. However, getting over this hump is where Blood West really starts to open up and shine. Stealth is by far the best way to go but you can at least get by with one on one combat as it's no longer an instant death sentence should you blow your cover. Each enemy pose a legitimate threat and shouldn't be underestimated regardless of your gear, blessing and/or abilities and pray you don't get swarmed by a mob.The visuals are akin to the Quake/BLOOD era as it gives Blood West a grim, foreboding and unsettling atmosphere along with the eerie western soundscape. You truly feel like your walking on cursed land corrupted by greed and power. Performance wise, I did experience the occasional hitching and frame drops but apart from that, the game ran rather smoothly on a GTX 1060 Max-Q with an Intel i7 8750H and 16gb DDR4.Needless to say, stealth is HEAVILY emphasized in Blood West. You can *technically* go in guns blazing but unless you're packing some SERIOUS firepower, it's ill-advised to do so. You're given just enough to get by as your ultimate goal (aside from vanquishing evil) is to just simply survive and uncover the mystery of the accursed land in which these creatures now inhabit. Mysticism also plays a heavy role in Blood West. Collect gold, valuables, trinkets and unique weapon while traversing an interconnected sandbox environment.There's simply not enough Weird/Fantasy West games and I'll take whatever I can get.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly this is one of the first immersive sims I have played in a long time that really captured my attention. _childDocuments_.review: Gameplay-☐Very good☑ Good☐ Nothing special☐ Okay☐ BadGraphics-☐ Masterpiece☐ Beautiful☑ Good (Low Poly Stylized)☐ Will do☐ Bad☐ AwfulAudio☐ Amazing☑ Very good☐ Good☐ Decent☐ Not too bad☐ BadAudience☐ Kids☑ Teens☑ Adults☐ EveryoneStory-☐ Lovely☐ Good☑ Average☐ Not great☐ NoneDifficult-☐ Just press a bunch of buttons☐ Easy☐ Significant brain usage☐ Easy to learn / Hard to master☐ Not so easy☑ Difficult☐ Dark SoulsGrind-☐ Nothing☐ Only if you care about leaderboards/ranks☐ Isnt necessary to progress☑ A bit grindy sometimes☐ Average grind level☐ Too much grind☐ InsanityGame Time-☐ Short☑ Average☐ Long☐ Depends on you☐ EndlessPrice☐ Just buy it☑ Worth the price☑ Wait for sale (If no rush)☐ Maybe if you have some spare money left☐ Not recommendedBlood West is a great little indie looter shooter with a interesting story to boot. The game very much heavily relies on stealth and passively rewards players that attempt to surgically dispatch enemies one at a time with head shot. If you opt to go guns blazing you will find yourself always low on health, potions and ammo because most opponents absorb far more damage from the neck down. The game is almost reminiscent of a souls-like with guns... it does not hold your hand with checkpoints or re-spawns, but permanently punishes death with de-buffs that you have work to dispel. So in short, the game rewards stealth and patience. As for the story, its okay. It has a interesting narrative arch, but the ending felt rushed and sort of dissatisfying. Luckily, the game play makes up for this shortcoming. Lastly the graphics... it is intentionally low poly and retro. I personally love the graphics and find they compliment the western aesthetic nicely. Graphics in this situation are subjective as to whether they are good or not: you decide.  Definitely worth a play. I would wait for a sale, but if you have to have it, its price point is fair enough.

_childDocuments_.review: Welcome to find a different flavor. It scratches that stealth FPS/RPG itch. Yes, it's hard, but not in an unfair, stupid way. It demands you put effort into learning its unique flow and mastering combat; leveling up your character and getting some valuable perks helps a lot, too. Once you're powerful enough, the game becomes very rewarding, but you'll never get that annoying feeling that you're overpowered and just going through the motions to finish the game. No, the challenge remains no matter how good you become. Pair all that with a very imaginative and colorful vision of horror/fantasy Wild West, and what you get is a game to remember! Finally, I liked the game quite a lot in the 8 hours I experienced it. Those interested in the genre should check it out.

_childDocuments_.review: /!\ MIXED /!\Loved the visual work, the atmosphere, the scattered secret loot, and RPG elements.But the gameplay loop is quickly repetitive and boring. That is not helped by the fact the game is about trial and errors, and doing the same areas over and over again with safer approach is getting redundant and slowing the exploration, respawn after respawn. It is simply tiring and unappealing after a while.On top of that the AI is too random : you can litteraly bait them to do what you want, OR they can suddenly go rogue outta script for no reason at all.Also I admit I never managed to kill the "vulture pistol guys", not one. I used 3 firearms, even tried melee. They were a wall to me, I couldn't go any further in the map as long as I came passed them.Then the first map is rather empty and creatively limited. I know it's the desert, and it seems like the game's prologue, but it's not much engaging after 2 or 3 caves/mines, climbing some dusty slopes, and walking around flat spaces, coming across the same props etc.The permanent night time is also drowning the overall, otherwise well tuned, ambience.In all honesty, I think 2 hours felt enough to see what the game has to offer as it stands. All that being said I really think the devs got something interesting here.

_childDocuments_.review: I knew I stumbled onto something special the moment I saw this game.This game is excellent so far, very fun to play and spend several hours scouring the map for goodies and loot.The guns feel smooth and fun to use, and the various melee you can find are fun to use and some of them feel rather meaty to swing.The accessories(artifacts) you may find around the map and on various enemies are unique and most have effects worth using at least once.The various locations you can explore feel pretty realistic layout wise and fun to explore through.There are multiple enemies with their own way to fight back, creative designs for each of them and usually multiple ways to deal with each of them.I've enjoyed this game so much, I've written my own guide on how to find the various Artifacts around the map ingame. Enjoy!

_childDocuments_.review: +++ Fantastic maps with tons to discover++ Great atmosphere++ Awesome gameplay+ Cool music video+ Unique visuals+ Cool enemies and bosses+ Good soundtrack+ Interersting world/premise* Meh story* Experimental stealth gameplay- Combat is a bit too unforgiving, forcing stealth- Too many enemies at times, making stealth impossible- Inconsistent enemy awarenessAlthough the beginning of the game is pretty hard, once you get used to the mechanics and intricacies, this game is a BLAST to play. Exploring the maps is very fun and the world/premise is quite interesting. Overall gameplay is great too, focusing on a slow, methodical approach. The atmosphere is fantastic, which is further enhanced by the unique visuals and the cool enemies.Things I was mixed about, was that the story was only OK, and that the stealth system feels pretty experimental, as you need to use the compass a lot.Negative points for me concern the combat balance: it is a bit too unforgiving, which forces you into a stealth playstyle, which can be pretty wonky, as there are at times too many enemies with inconsistent awareness.All in all this game is a mix of STALKER and Thief, which is very fun to play around in. _childDocuments_.review: A cute choice of words: Blood west is a bloody fine, stylish stealth/action horror hybrid adventure that will leave you stranded in bleak world of undead cowboys and eldritch abominations, rewarding accuracy, patience, vigilance and an attitude of an explorer, whilst simultaneously punishing recklessness, overconfidence and short sighted approach. The non-linear progression allows you, the player to go out into the wild and explore at your own pace. With 2 out of three episodes being finished, you can easily sink upwards of 20 hours into them combined, exploring every nook and cranny, following every lead and just having fun. *The crunchy, pixelated artstyle is amazing, able to effortlessly sell that grunge, grime, blood and rot of this bizarre world. Apart from a few outliers all of the monsters are well designed, twisted and interesting to look at. *The audio is really well made, from the sound of your footsteps mixing with clangs of your gear, to the inhumane wails, screeches and whispers of the abominations that roam the area, with solid gunshots and the wet squelches of popped skulls in between.*Incredibly satisfying core gameplay loop. *While stealth is definitely the safer, and more viable option when compared to combat, especially considering that the protagonist is generally squishy and suffers from debufs upon death, going guns blazing can still be used as a fun change of pace.  *The voice acting is damn solid across the board, with the protagonist and the supporting cast being unique, interesting to listen to, albeit the game is indeed stingy when it comes to dialogue, where, perhaps delving into the psyche of the characters much deeper would help flesh out them and the world they inhabit. It isn't perfect, has a few hiccups with the inventory management. The first episode is admittedly more rougher in comparison to the second one:*Enemy variety is a tad slim (addressed in chapter 2)*Weapon diversity could use a little expansion (note, there are many reskins and such that can be found around in the world, but all of them still are some variety of bow, lever gun, a double barrel, pistol or a rifle)*Fiddling with the inventory is bothersome especially when in a rush, or under stress, a way for the game to automatically rearrange some inventory items when equipping and unequipping certain weapons would be nice, as right now you have to manually do some rearrangements every time you want to swap a bow out for a shotgun, when the inventory is full (and it will fill rapidly.)*Later in the second chapter, a very black and white choice will be presented to a player, an absolute no brainer for those who pay even a modicum of attention. *Chapter 2's final boss does not properly communicate its state of vulnerability, which lead to a few minutes lost in head scratches. *The protag does tire a tad too quickly, but it can be taken as a deliberate way to up the tension a few notches. *As a personal pet peeve, there is rarely an incentive to vary up the artifacts (capable of giving you passive abilities, like increased stamina, speed, health regen, etc).*The chapters do outstay their welcome a tad bit, but in all honesty having thoroughly sunk so much time into each chapter, I think this is personal.*The music does get a little stale and somewhat grating.All in all, even at this stage, you owe it to yourself to get this game, that is if you like blood, west, cowboys, revolvers, monsters, a solid and addictive gameplay loops, old school graphics and such. Solid 8/10, and getting it on this steam summer sail of 2023 would be a steal. Take care, and thank you for reading this far.Sebastian Agner.

_childDocuments_.review: Level Design - Hand crafted map is titties. Neat shortcuts and hidden things thru-outVoice Acting - Protagonist sounds perfect Weapons - I love the slow reloading and feel of the weapons, both melee and ranged. Devs nailed it.The Sweet 15 - If you play this game til the end, there will be 15 minutes in which this game is perfect. Before and after that sweet, the balance is a little wonk. Balance - At the start, it may feel overwhelming with your cowboy stacked against the odds. The most scrub enemy will kill you if you're lazy. After just a few levels up though, you're OP and have probably figured the game out.Voice Lines - As great as the protagonists voice is, his lines aren't always so great or make sense. Whenever you pick up an arrow "ooohhhh, bullets." Pick up a random item "Whatever gets the jobs done." Too repetitive and too frequent and not always appropriate. Minor nit pickAI - This could be a neutral comment. AI is not horrible. The enemies are deaf so for a stealth game you will not be overly concerned about the sound of your shotgun blast. Lack of immersion - Not sure exactly what is missing from the feel of the map, but it never got me immersed satisfactorily. It always felt like I was playing a video game, never got fully sucked in. Something about the sterility of the map, not quite sure .... More map detail may remedy this.  Overall, this is a safe bet for an EA pick up. It is fleshed and not buggy. May pick up again when the next chapters drop.

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly, the overall atmosphere and setting of Blood West is fantastic. There isn't enough "Weird West" games so when it's done the well it's worth championing.Many of the reviews I see mention the enemy AI and I'd agree it's pretty easy to manipulate, but I think if you meet it on it's own terms there's a lot to love about the gameplay and interactions with enemies. I'm currently on my first play-through and I'm going for the no-death's in each chapter achievement. It's created a real sense of tension and danger in each encounter and it's bringing me back to playing the S.T.A.L.K.E.R series for the first time.One of my personal critiques is the lead characters voice lines. Although I'm a big fan of Stephen Russell's work (Mercer Fray, Nick Valentine, Garrett) I find he's overused in the actual moment to moment gameplay. You hear a voice line every time you pick up an item and kill an enemy and this can get grating after literally hundreds of times.Despite this, this game is really worth your time especially if you like stealth action shooters and especially if you're interested in horror-western as a sub-genre. I've played for almost thirty hours and the gameplay loop of killing enemies, searching for loot and returning to camp still hasn't gotten stale.Looking forward to the expansion and curious what changes they will make, as it is now I feel the base game is great/on the verge of greatness.

_childDocuments_.review: Played (and streamed) this for four hours today and I really had a lot of fun with it! _childDocuments_.review: Blood west is a very intriguing game with some good mechanics and a great atmosphere. however while I like the game I do feel that there area few things that game could improve on.-Better detection system: I've noticed even though I'm a good distance away from enemies I can still be detected by enemies and have even been seen through walls. There needs to be some kind of balance with the detection system to where it can benefit the player and feel like they aren't being cheated out.-Less enemy placement: I understand that the developers want to create a sense of difficulty for the player. However I feel that in certain areas there needs to be less enemies. Right out of the gate by the crashed train I feel that there are way too many enemies. This too needs some kind of balance.-Combat: right now the combat is not good. The game, at least for me not sure about others, lags when certain attacks are being done by the enemies. especially that lunge attack. I also think that the enemies shouldn't be able to execute attacks so fast as that can really make or break a player from playing. Yes stealth is an option but certain points combat is where you need to get by.-Way point marker(?): Maybe have some kind of guidance to the player on where they should go. I've gotten lost quite a few times and I haven't even been bale to complete any objectives other than the starting one.-Gun play rework: The guns are fine but there is a problem with aiming them where the gun slightly waves around when aiming down. It makes it really hard for you to aim for head shots if yo want to avoid combat.All in all the game is great probably the best game ive seen. There just needs to be a bit of fine tuning for it.

_childDocuments_.review: The game feels like a mix of some nostalgic gaming for me.Thief's style of sneaking, Blood 3D combat, Daggerfall's RPG elements.. all wrapped up in a Jonah Hex themed game world. I picked games that have similar pixel old feel, but there's more than that, the gameplay feels like those old game.The stealth doesn't rely on more modern tropes  like needing a specific location to hide, etc, it's based on a more systemic "awareness". Sound and sight. It's hard to explain how that difference feels, but if you've played the old Thief or Tenchu games, you know what I mean. If you can run up and surprise an enemy even from the front, you can get a stealth kill.The RPG elements are quite light, and you don't need to max your level as there is absolutely a skill element to the game. However, each perk you select feels like you actually gain something impactful. Equipment too. It's more "+200% damage" here, or "+50% stamina regen" there, or entirely new abilities even (for the more expensive perks). If usually feels like you've gained something by using new perks or new equipment. Many change the way you can play.The combat itself is pretty good as well. Definitely unforgiving if you mess around. You can only take a few hits back to back, so you will likely be stealth killing a lot, until you find a group and then start tossing out the molotovs and blast away at groups from a distance. Or switching to your sawed-off and blasting a big vendigo in the face twice before booking it to reload before he rips your head off. Headshots matter. Distance matters. Timing your shots to the creature's movements, and knowing their various unique defenses. Each new "room" having different monsters with different attacks, defense, positioning, etc, makes it feel like the old Doom/Blood 3d games.I can definitely appreciate the care put into making this game, and the attention to gameplay details. It hits just the right spot for me of metagaming mechanics, skilled play, and nostalgia.

_childDocuments_.review: The combat is simple and it's rewarding either you run with melee or ranged build, it never miss.Although you could play as solely melee only throughout the campaign, you still need a gun or bow for bosses or for quick XP farm as all of the enemies deals insane damage even if you had 500 HP and it pretty much also occurs for gun builds too.The game never escape from only one weapon type only run as I previously stated, this game is hard like very difficult and you'll get punished for executing actions recklessly without consideration.I do really like this game and we do need additional long chapters as DLCs or just an update or New Game+ because when you enter the last chapter your character's basically OP once you find the correct artifacts that will keep you alive in steep duration and it is unfortunately the only things to happens we could enjoy momentarily. The game's actually pretty average in terms of how story goes but explorations makes the game felt long to complete (which is the main goal for this game).My first playthrough finished after 25 hours of playtime and with the absence of new chapters or New Game+ there's nothing to do unless if you want to start over again with different builds but this also spawn another problem, once you farm like hell and obtain almost all of the skills, the build you play initially at the starts of chapter becomes redundant and fighting through hordes basically felt like nothing but parts of obstacles that try to kills you. You don't need to advance to another chapter to farm like crazy but usually you'll get bored for fighting the same types of foes and kind of forced to finally beating the boss and play the next chapter and farm and get bored again after farms and farms and so on.The game is fun like the amounts of fun is everywhere.Another mode or chapters is really needed to amp all of the above or basically any experience in this game.For the developer, thank you for creating amazing game, I do hope future updates is still given and attract all player to play this sublime experience new or returning does not matter as long this game delivers, it's always a blast to play.9.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: I truly don't mind Stealth FPS, but I can't in good faith recommend this game. Combat feels rewarding, yes, but the pacing is at a snail's crawl. You get punished for any small mistake that alerts nearby enemies. Progression feels rewarding, but its at such a slow pace that it's a struggle to stay engaged/motivated to continue. For stealth to be the main game mechanic here, it is not fleshed out well. You assume the enemies would not be able to see you if you're in a reasonable line of sight. I found that even if I'm one frame within the enemy's peripherals or a hair behind and to the side of them, the game still counts it as the enemies being able to see you. I've died multiple times because I assumed I would be able to get a surprise attack off to get face checked, which feels horrible given how scarce health items are. If there were more health drops scattered about, it wouldn't feel nearly as demotivating to die.Not that it's a massive downside to the game, but the lack of explanation on if you should visit other areas before the main objective (spoiler: you shouldn't) makes pathing a little confusing. If you're willing to put up with the progression slog and a lot of backtracking to return to safety/buy items/etc. then I'd say give it a try. If not, I wouldn't put yourself through the frustration. 6.5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic little shooter. The story is fairly straightforward and short, but still enjoyable and the whole game can be completed within 4-6 hours with the current content as this review is written. Gunplay feels good and the enemies are satisfying and diverse enough to make the gameplay loop fun throughout the entirety of the game. There are a good number of skills available and a few artifacts to give you a decent selection as far as how you decide to play the game. Exploration is well rewarded in finding both supplies and extra artifacts/lore pieces in both notes regarding the enemy types, and cursed items which when turned in give you an extra bit of story/exp. All in all for $15 I'd say it's well worth the buy, despite being short it's entirely enjoyable and I'm very excited for the next scenarios to be released.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think I can recommend Blood West, though I wish I had a thumbs-middle option for it because I do enjoy some aspects of it. I like the concept, I like the aesthetics. The gameplay can be fun for a few hours. I feel bad about being negative on what is a passion project by a smaller studio. Here are my key problems with Blood West:1: The Artifact SystemIn Blood West, you can have up to 3 artifacts equipped at any time. The vast majority of these artifacts are very situational, such as only being useful against specific enemies, only being useful in certain environments, etc.The problem that having limited slots and situational artifacts is that you must do one of the following:* Leave less useful artifacts equipped when you don't need to (less effective)* Swap artifacts constantly (very tedious)* Use very general artifacts that are useful most of the time (boring)I chose #3, and I suspect many other players do the same. This is unfortunate because Blood West has MANY artifacts. I never used almost any of them because the basic +loot +headshot damage +revolver stats artifacts were always relevant and swapping artifacts constantly was tedious.2: The AIBlood West's AI is really bad. They cannot climb ladders or terrain, allowing you to manipulate them easily. They can't navigate terrain well in general. If they see an enemy die, they walk right up to where it died, letting you chain kills. Poor AI means the player has less decisions to make and makes the gameplay more boring. 3: Punishment on Death doesn't result in the gameplay you expect as a developer...In Blood West, if you die some enemies respawn and you gain a 'soul flaw' that acts as some form of debuff, such as lower XP gained. Punishing the player in some way on their death seems like a good idea on paper. It adds tension and makes them care about dying. The problem is what this causes many players to *DO* about it. Many will simply choose to play as slowly and tediously as possible. Stealth all the time. Headshots all the time. No risky plays. No running in guns ablaze. Never trying a new idea because they have something that works. Always keeping one artifact slot filled with the coin in case you get jumped. That is frankly not a fun way to play the game. It's very boring and personally it started to really grate on me in the middle of the second chapter and was unbearable in C3. I wanted to go play something else instead and frequently put the game down after realizing how long clearing an area would take.And respawning enemies is never fun. If you just cleared half of the chapter's map and then died to an invisible enemy - now you have to kill dozens of those enemies all over. That feeling alone made me not want to play once or twice.4: Repetitive GameplayBlood West is not an immersive sim, despite any surface similarities.  Unlike games like Prey 2017 or Deus Ex, your interaction with the environment is very limited and your options for dealing with most situations are very few. In an ImSim, those two are the key components.I mainly bring it up because ImSims by their nature tend to have a lot more variety and replayability. One time you may reach an objective by killing everything. Another by hacking. Another by bribing someone to tell you about a secret route. Another by stacking boxes until you get there. Another by creating a distraction  and using stealth. Etc. Blood West does not play like this at all.BW does not 'need' to be an immersive sim, but that language shows up on the Steam page and in the reviews - and it's definitely not the case.Also: Because you can't simply re-spec at any time for free (it costs a potion that there are few of in the game), most players will stick with one build for the whole game, which is a bit of a bummer.5: Other issues* Most of the skills are very boring, unfortunately. +X% XP is not a fun skill, even if it's objectively good in the long run. Neither is 15% more stamina.  Towards the end I was just taking whatever because nothing sounded that appealing or interesting to me for my build. * Even with all the storage upgrades and the largest backpack, your inventory will constantly fill up with mostly useless junk. Dragging all of it back to the stash is not all that fun, and gets egregiously tedious in Chapter 3 when the chest is so far from the rest of the map. * The lesson about consumables still hasn't been learned. If you provide consumables that are even semi-rare, players will hoard them and never use them for the entire game. Many games have developed systems to keep players using similar abilities without this problem. Maybe the + accuracy alcohol is great, but I kept 'saving' it until I realized I had beaten the game. Same with the Keen Bolts, exploding bolts, etc. If I've only found <10 in my playthrough I'm never going to use them.* Notes as physical objects may be immersive, but it's frustrating. You have limited space and can't afford to carry dozens of these notes around with you. Which enemy is which again? I think a "Bestiary" with a picture and gets filled in as you find pages for each enemy would have gone MILES to making it a better system. The rest of the notes and journal entries you find could be added to some kind of book to keep track of it all.* More added later once I think of them6: There's not a lot else hereI'm willing to forgive the gameplay and mechanical flaws if there's something else here...but there's not. The story is fairly threadbare, there's few characters with few lines of dialog, there's no real big moments to notice. It has good style but not a lot of substance.I think I counted maybe 3 side quests? Each of which was "go to a place and bring something back" which is about as barebones as it gets. A game like this can work, but the gameplay has to be rock-solid in order to make up for the rest being thin. And IMO, Blood West does not have that foundation.

_childDocuments_.review: This game satisfies my need for rewarding mouse precision, stealth, inventory management, AND scavenging all while having a desolate, open world. It is without a doubt the surprise of the last 5 years for me game-wise. I wish I could wipe my memory of this game so I could rediscover it. To my knowledge, and without checking before writing this, I have never played a game by this dev before and they have my support for future retro titles of this "sort." There are unique weapons in the fallout style as well as different types of ammunition for meaningful and situational application. If you're new to mouse and keyboard, this would be a great tool to help you dial your sensitivity and make you better. There's a reason they're bundling it with kovaak's right now, I'd wager. It's a short game, keep that in mind (even though there's a 3rd episode coming out). One gripe I have is that if you are a good shot, you can accumulate ammo quickly and it feels like you are unstoppable with that much extra. HOWEVER, if you are caught by surprise, that ammo can disappear very quickly. It's a 9.5 out of 10 for what it is, in my humble opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: What's cool? Cowboys. What's cooler than a cowboy? An UNDEAD cowboy. What's cooler than an undead cowboy? An undead cowboy fighting monsters in an old west horror stealth RPG shooter, which is what this is (well, RPG is debatable, although there is XP and a perk system).Blood West has an undeniably cool aesthetic and comforting, slightly boomer-shooter-esque gameplay (I can make that joke, I'm over 30). What it ALSO has is a fun emphasis on stealth and making ammunition count that ratchets up the tension in a pleasant way and forces you to make fun little decisions such as "do I use my last molotov cocktail to burn these leech-throwing cannibal cultists to death or try to land slightly difficult headshots on them & save the molotov for the giant cleaver-and-axe-wielding bucket-headed skin-flaying maniac in the shack?"Seriously. It's a very fun game. It never feels TOO hard, not in the miserable, just-started-playing-counter-strike-in-2023 way, but you WILL probably die a few times (and be raised again, possibly with a mild case of occult curse) in pursuit of your goals. Enemies never stop being a threat; you can die in a RELATIVELY few hits if you're not careful, even with a few survivability upgrades. The game doesn't have a METRIC ton of branching paths, but the choices you are called to make feel reasonably weighty when you make them, which is better than a lot of games manage. Chapters 1 and 2 feel very distinct in a way that manages to keep the game feeling pretty fresh. All in all, very enjoyable. I'd highly recommend and I'm waiting with bated breath for chapter 3.

_childDocuments_.review: Blood West is a stealth-oriented FPS with RPG elemenst (inventory, XP, skills, character improvements, quests, money, permanent and unlimited stash, etc.), almost a "metroidvania FPS", set in a "weird west" setting (post-1866, judging by some weapons), where revolvers and bows meet undeads and spirits.The game encourages careful gameplay, backstabbing, diversion by throwing rocks, use of cover and timely reloads, as unless you're able to score headshot after headshot, tackling more than one or two enemies at a time is a recipe for disaster.If, like me, you're bad at precise shooting, get ready to die a lot, as most enemies have a lot of HP and/or are fast(-shooting) and/or hit hard. They have unlimited ammo, though they still have to reload like you do. Also, being the late 19th century, most weapons only hold a handfull of rounds, which are reloaded one by one. Of course, more powerful weapons have low ammo capacity, and vice-versa.All wrapped-up together, this makes for slow and careful approches, followed by short and brutal skirmishes… and panicked retreats while frantically trying to dodge enemies projectiles/lunges and reloading at the same time! Because for some reason (gameplay balance/rythm, I guess), enemies react to missed shots, but not to shots that kill a nearby enemy in one go.Dying applies increasing debuffs (unless you sacrifice a rather common item), that you can get rid of by drinking a potion, or doing a small side-quest for an NPC.The game is divided into chapters (it's currently impossible to go back to a previous one), and though the maps may seem empty at first glance, the level design is brilliantly intricate, with almost at least 3 ways to approach/explore/infiltrate any point of interest, and lots of items to reward exploration!Most of these items are consummables (ammo, health items, gold, etc.), but the most hidden/remotely placed are artifacts or unique upgraded weapons with special powers.The graphic style is reminiscent of the late 1990s/early 2000s FPSs and may not appeal to everyone, but as one of my friend noted, it's crisp and clear, with almost no clutter/distraction caused by reflection, bloom, or any other eye-candy effect: if something moves, it's definitely an enemy looking to kill you, and not some random trick of light!Overall, Blood West is a great game with a lot of potential (patches and improvements are still coming up, and the devs are friendly and pretty quick to reply), but make sure to take it slow and careful, as rushing and dying will only make things worse and worse. Although, if you're a headshot expert, you can try and speedrun it!

_childDocuments_.review: (Devs shame anyone who wants the game to be fun and not a chore.)This game can be fun, but was ruined with the latest patch. The game was already nearly too tough to be fun, if frustration is fun for you, great it is not fun for me. Stress and tension are not why I play games, I get enough of that in life, I play games for fun. This elitist gaming movement making everything so hard, so unforgiving and so stress-inducing is why people give up on games. Gaming was not like this 10 years ago, games were made for the most part, that everyone could play and have fun with. Now I see this gatekeeping crap and I have had enough of it, this is a really cool game that ruins it for players by forcing everyone to play on the hard mode... This is the only thing I would ever see as a reasonable complaint, I get it is a stealth game, I understand that, but lack of forgiveness and quickness to failure, is not fun for everyone! Why does it matter to others, if there is a difficulty option that allows zen gamers a chance to have some blissful fun? I think it is because the world hates fun, and wants us to love frustration and stress.  In short, this is the first game I will refund due to an update focused on making the game nigh unplayably difficult.

_childDocuments_.review: So I just finished this game and honestly, it has a lot of promise though it does have some issues that hold it back.The first is the difficulty curve which starts off hard when you have no artifacts, skills or gold coins with only an axe and a rusty revolver with little ammo at the start. By the end however I have so many gold coins I can wear for protection or turn them over to the totem for a luck blessing, making the death mechanic entirely redudant, loaded with standard and special ammo due to looking around every corner for loot, flush with health potions and bandages to heal myself. The threats were hardly a problem once you get the skill that eliminates the range penalty on headshots, I could just pop any baddies head with a winchester from any range. The only real issues were when dealing with vendigos since they require several headshots with the standard ammo. Other then that, the game became pretty easy up to the end, the boss not even being much of a bother since I got all the gold cursed items and had plenty of gold shotgun ammo.I'm not sure how it'll continue in the next maps but I feel the game will end up being monotonous if I still have the same inventory, skills and weapons brought over from the previous map. Maybe if the challenge gets ramped up in the next maps with different enemies or enviromental hazards? I wouldn't condone removing all the stuff i accumulated since that would suck.Again, it has a lot of promise but I feel the challenge needs to restructured so that I don't become such a powerhouse by the time I get to the boss, especially since there's so much ammo even in the cave leading up to the boss (I mean its sealed, why is there so much gold,silver,flame ammo in there?).Definatly worth keeping an eye in the future though and I do hope the game keeps it challenge in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: So, just finished the game, with tons of hundreds ammo, items, etc, even with 30k+ gold in my storage LOL. I liked to use a lot the crossbow (you can get ammo back). Anyway, my first solid review in a long time:TLDR- Great game about hording/gathering and fighting enemies with different approach;- You can die easily, but if you manage how combat works, it really becomes easy;- The first boss was the hardest one. Second and third one were very easy -.-'- Story is simple, enjoyable and quests are also easy to follow. No real highlight here;- I loved the combat, loved the concepts and art style;Pros:- You can easily lose track of time when you are exploring and getting items. The game has much more items than you need if you are the exploring player type;- The tons of different items and "artifacts" gives you different combat approach, but this is also a "Con" - explained below;- Chapters are different enough for you to enjoy exploring, but the last one just felt a bit more "grinding" than fun;- Different types of weapons for you to "feel" and select your play style. All of them, for me, enjoyable enough to clear the areas;- I did have that feel about "one more run, one more search" you know, and this is great for me in a shooter game with open quests to solve on your own;- Great fun trying to balance between your best souls/advantage items (I don't remember the name, but it is those ones that you keep activated);Cons:- Many items that you collect is really not needed to move on, feeling like waste of time and design here (like many potions that I never used, I did not really even care, because it made no sense to me);- Map levels are big enough to have fun, but could have a bit more "traps", hidden spots with real treasures. You do have special items to collect, but some if just better to get with vendors;- I did not have a real big challenge with "strong" enemies, it is the same approach to kill any other (you can also take advantage of some level design here and use exploits);- No real replay value, it would be great if I could use my so "hard-earned" loot (I collected all great weapons, but at the end of the boss, just used one - I was so strong that, with a few shots, I killed the boss LOL). So all that feeling where you feel you were saving items, time, etc, is lost at the end. Shame on this part;- I finished the entire Chapter 3 without dying - I was a bit disappointed.But all in all - I highly recommend the game for the ones that enjoy a good shooter with freedom to explore and some different types of mechanics into their own lore and art style.===== ORIGINAL REVIEW =====One of the best "different" games I found out there. Classic FPS, but with deeper exploration and item collection. Good graphics for the style, lot's of fun while you explore and fighting. After you get used to it, it becomes easy, but depending on where you make a mistake, it will become a challenge again. Highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Rating 9/10Summary:Pros:+Great Price+Gameplay+No bugs+Filled small Open WorldCons:-Weird stealthThis game is a great western "Survival" game.And all of the weapons can be categorized as Western going from Knives, Axes, etcto revolvers, bows, and rifles.In this small "Open World" (more like one area) you can find many buildings, caves, etc filled with different monsters (with an acceptable AI), weapons, consumables, and ammo (even different types like Golden Bullets for extra dmg, silver bullets, fire bullets, etc).It's very rewarding to explore those caves and houses, but it's also really fun and sometimes scary due to the enemy's Grunts and environment.You will need to manage your  weapons damage, ammo, health, stamina and inventory.Inventory managment is similar to resident evils one.This game has also a Skill system where you can spend your 3 Skill Points that you will get every level up.Due to the different weapons and skills, it's possible to play different kinds of playstyles like stealth and "I shoot everything I see".Now stealth is kinda broken right now.You can shoot enemies with a revolver or rifle and you will not get spotted by any other enemies that should technically hear your loud shot.But if you walk for too long in an enemy's hearing area you can get spotted by multiple.So it does not make any sense to use a bow because a revolver is basically the same thing.If they would nerf the guns to a point that shooting reveals your position to everyone nearby a bow or knife would be more essential to use.All items you can find can be stored in a chest within a secure area. In that secure area is an NPC where you can sell your stuff and buy new weapons, ammo, etc.Also, they will give you small side quests that will grand you some items or money.If you die you will respawn at the last camp you visited the skull (Main quest "NPC") and you will get a negative trait (3 times stackable), but you won't lose any items

_childDocuments_.review: Let me preface my review with a few things:I do not regret my purchase and I advise no one against buying the game. My review is set to not recommended because the game has mostly positive reviews and mine will be less drowned out if I do this. I have enjoyed my time with it, however I have issues with it, which I hope to make clear in my review.I will not start every sentence with "In my opinion". Take everything I say as my opinion unless I eplicitly state it as fact.I have not finished the game as of writing. I have played until what I think is the halfway point of chapter 3.There are many things I like about the game:The sound design is excellent across the board, be it monster sounds, music, gun sounds or anything else really.I really like the artstyle and the enemy designs in general. The voice acting is also phenomenal,and the gunplay is great.My problems with the game are in found in the game design and can't be changed now. But maybe they could be different in Blood West 2.May main problem with Blood West is this:Enemies just run straight at me until they can punch me or are in range to shoot. They appear to be unaware of each others presence, and make no attempt to flank me, or use cover for their approach. (Intentionally I mean. Running behind a house because that's the shortest route to me doesn't count :) )If one of their number dies without them being alerted by me, they run over to the body, look at it for a moment and then walk away again.They don't search for me, they don't alert their friends and they don't become more careful. They are either coming at me or not aware of me at all.They are also very easy to kite. Most enemies can easily be escaped from, simply by pressing shift+w and booking it. They will loose interest quite quickly.The mighty Wendigo's full speed sprint looks so imposing that it almost triggered a fight or flight reaction in me. It looks like a mighty beast that could easily run me over. And what does it do? It comes to a standstill and swipes at the empty air in front of it.This is made worse by the fact that all enemies are less dangerous the further away you are. Melee enemies can't hit you and ranged enemies projectiles are easier to dodge. Indoors and spotted by enemies? Shift+W outside because that's the objectively correct response, as they will always follow you outside and are easier to keep at a distance that way.Most of my deaths were caused by being spotted indoors and forgetting where the exit is.The game want's the player to feel like a cool badass. But that requires cool enemies: They look cool, they sound cool, and their animations are cool. But what they are actually doing often isn't that cool at all.The game want's the player to be scared of the enemy. Having them run at me is certainly scary in a very direct way, but wouldn't it also be scary if they weren't always so gung-ho? If they would patiently lie in wait to get me instead of following me outside, when that would put me at an advantage? If they shot at me from the cover of windows instead of standing in the open, making themselves an easy target?(I really like the birdmen though, because they at least try to dodge my attacks. It gives me the feeling when playing that they want to kill me and don't want me to kill them)I'm not a programmer, I don't know how hard it is to make a computer opponent that is more intelligent than what's in the game. And I also realise that more dangerous and more intelligent enemies would make the game more difficult, which could be a problem in combination with the game's death system. But then perhaps it would be a good idea to do away with it and allow the player to quicksave in order to be able to have stronger enemies without making the game a chore to play. Or include difficulty options. Allow the players to change many variables. Normal enemies without Quicksaves. Strong enemies with quicksaves. Low rescources for the Survival game lovers. Everything dialed up in difficulty for the masochists.(Maybe a permadeath mode? I'm sure someone would want to play it)If none of that is possible, I would appreciate it if Blood West 2 featured battles that see the player fighting against large hordes of enemies. That would work well with enemies that always act in a very direct way.Fighting a group of five very smart enemies is cool, so is fighting a large group of very blunt enemies.Fighting a group of five idiots isn't. Even if the gunplay is great.I rarely write a review, especially a long one. Your game motivated me to do that, because it made a big impression on me. I am very much looking forward to Blood West 2 (if you're planning on making a sequel of course) and hope that you can improve on the formula.I wish you all the best and good luck in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: I really like the setting and performance was great - no real technical issues. It seems a tad one-dimensional in a couple places but I feel it's on a decent path. Perhaps it's less important later in the game as you get more skills, but early game I was feeling this quite a lot.Given the amount of stealthing it requires (as the character is quite weak against direct damage) I find the enemies hard to mind-read, which I think is a crucial aspect of... stealth. Knowing what your enemy is thinking and reacting/adjusting to it. It feels like the player is required to stare at the HUD elements a LOT, such as the detection bar at the bottom of the screen, which throws the immersion off.Could be bugs, but it's hard to tell on certain things whether they're intended or not. For example, the enemies will sometimes run at you without making a screech/roar first, and sometimes they will.Anyway, it's still a recommend. I think there's a good bunch of fun to be had here and the setting is unique and cool. Needs a bit longer in the oven, and I think it'll get it, as long as the developers focus on the right parts.

_childDocuments_.review: Where do I start with Blood West? I picked it up about a year or less back and started to play it, I was jumping at my own shadow in some parts early on and got frustrated by the stealth mechanics, so I often started fights with a single head shot and ran away after that unless it was a Melee Kill. I originally felt like I had to take this REALLY slow. That was... until I learned a bit more about HOW it all works.Pros:-Difficulty Curve isn't forgiving but it isn't impossibly hard.-Vast array of weapons and skills to customize yourself to YOUR playstyle.-Game Economy isn't terrible, enemies do respawn so makes you have to take a step back and think 'Do I farm with Melee to make money? Or kill what is in my way to progress and gain XP and Money to make my progress easier?'-Inventory is actually fairly decent. Most games with an inventory people often complain you never have enough. I make SURE I have more than enough space and you should too! (You'll understand when you progress in Chapter 1)-Story is very nice, it ties things together and paints a picture of the world. How it became the way it was and so on.-Graphics make it feel like a retro game. It feels like an old Playstation title, polygons and all!Cons:-AI does sometimes have a little fit and you need to either reload the area or 'sleep' to reload. It doesn't happen often but very minor problem.-Not very punishing if you die. Why is this a con? Well, yes you get a curse if you die and curses are negative perks that hinder your gameplay. HOWEVER if you're smart you'll collect the item you can use to 'buy off' that curse and wipe it from yourself.-Directions aren't 100% clear. Sometimes you just have to explore to find what you're looking for and it doesn't really 'Stand Out' sometimes. So if you want to get all the secrets too you'll have to look VERY hard.-Descriptions need some updates, more legible and coherent. Otherwise the perks/weapons/items descriptions are fine as is.Overall I give this game a solid 9/10 because there are STILL some things that can be improved and they are working on that. Perfect scoring this would be dishonest just like most games or anything really. Nothing is truly perfect, but it's also those little flaws that sometimes bring some character to something!

_childDocuments_.review: I found the initial learning curve a little steep, but once you get your bearings it's a super fun supernatural western stealth action romp that is one of my favourite games of the year!Blood West does a great job of making you start out as a scared little lamb, confused by the big mean creatures around you before you get some upgrades, some knowledge on how to kill each demon and you buy some new bombastic weapons to pack in your resident evil style inventory.By this point it is YOU who feels like the demon to be feared! _childDocuments_.review: I'm only 2/3 way through the game, at the end of Act 2 of 3, and I gotta' say, this game has been great for the price. I bought it based on the big butts and breasts I saw on the Steam page, as I'm not afraid to say that I'm a male, and I've been consistently impressed by what I've seen so far. Great atmosphere, the game really just throws you to the wolves at the start (in a completely good way, I already understood the basics and was just given a problem, then told "Figure out how to get into this monster-infested town your own way"), and, for the price of $25 base, even lower if you grab it on sale, this is a great little game that has given me my money's worth, which is rare for a game these days.Only cons I really have about the game as a whole are: the soundtrack, which is underwhelming, as most of the time you'll hear scary ambient background noise, which is good, but it's not really music and can get old after a couple of hours; the constant "witty" quips and comments from the player character as you loot random things in the world, which were immediately a red flag and made me think that this game was going to be terrible, but it was one of the only bad things about the game, as it doesn't even reach a good level of "camp," instead of just borders on Marvel-esque cringe; the fact that vendors don't sell more than a handful of bullets at a time. Yes, I get that it's trying to be a horror game, but if I already have a giga-tier stealth modifier and $6k money in the pocket, I feel as if I should be able to just dump my money into an NPC and be able to go rambo without having to go the strenuous route of knifing every enemy, loading one or two shotgun shells at a time (pistols usually drop 2-3, rarely 5 unless you have an item that increases loot drop rate), and THEN finally being able to mess around without a nagging fear of running out of bullets. Besides that, fun little game, I'll be watching this Dev for future products, especially if they include more hot chicks (sex sells, baybay, and my purchase proves that).Edit: after finishing the game, I can say that the last chapter is the weakest link, and the game should've probably ended at the end of Chapter 2. The third one just felt a lot more... narrow? Not as free to explore as the previous two maps you were given? A lot of tight areas, a lot of tall mountains that block you on either side, and the twist ending was just not very fun to see. The story could definitely use some work, but I will say that the voice acting for pretty much all characters (especially the two females, they were absolutely amazing) was a true treat in this day-and-age of hacks. Would still thoroughly recommend this game, but I did find myself just rushing past the last chapter, not really exploring the entire map in depth like I did the rest of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: A solid immersive sim that's got plenty of replay value. The game takes a minute to learn, because despite it's appearance, it's not a fast paced movement shooter. Hip-fire is extremely unreliable, especially while moving. Enemies can easily gang up on you and quickly end your game. Running away from a conflict can attract more enemies, making stealth important, and direct conflict riskier. However, there are a lot of small things I want to mention.Tomahawks are easily the worst weapon in the game. Not because of their damage out put, but because they're just a nuisance to use. They're the only throw-able item in the game that doesn't have a trajectory arc, and the hit box of the blade is very unreliable/predictable. I don't know how many times a throw looks like a headshot and it ends up in the enemy's shoulder. The decision the player needs to make in Chapter 2 is utterly in consequential and not entirely difficult to make. It is if you believe there consequences, but there aren't. Whoever gets saved makes a brief cameo in Chapter 3 and that's it. There is little to no environment interaction. In Chapter 1, you can find hanging corpses on the big bridge near the beginning of the area. I was a little disappointed when I couldn't cut them down and loot them. There's hiding in the bushes, and rarely shooting down an oil lamp on top of an enemy. That's it for the environment.The story is meh at best. What starts off as intriguing in Chapter 1 almost completely loses me by the end of Chapter 2, and to me, the ending of Chapter 3 seems very disconnected.Despite these flaws, they did not stop me from getting all of the achievements. I would definitely recommend this for fans of the immersive sim genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Really solid open-world survival FPS deeply soaked in atmosphere. The gameplay loop is comparable to the S.T.A.L.K.E.R. games in a lot of ways, making you delve deep into monster-infested, abandoned sites to scavenge for loot and artefacts.Visuals are amazing. The low-res textures, reminiscent of Quake, add a special flair to the overall dirty Wild West looks and are near perfectly executed. Monster designs are positively disgusting and have a strong identity.Audio is incredible as well. All guns (so far) sound rich and powerful and the noises monsters give off are the stuff of nightmares. The soundtrack reminds me of a mix between Borderland's desert ambient themes and Thief's droning background noises. However the music is very much in the background and the game mostly lives off ambient noises and your own footsteps, creating a beautifully desolate ambience.
