_childDocuments_.review: This is difficult for me, but I ultimately have to not recommend this game. Please understand, this is a really good game, and I hope the Dev continues his work on it. There will be plenty of people happy with this game. In fact, I hope the entire WORLD is happy with this game. It's just not for me. But hey, if literally everyone else on the planet EXCEPT me likes it, that's still a 99% recommendation, right?The problem is that when I first bought this game, I thought it was going in a different direction. I have been STARVING for a horror western game ever since I first played RDR: Undead Nightmare. It was a side, fantasy horror DLC that had me greatly intrigued. And this game does intrigue me; especially the atmosphere and the enemies. However, it's the gameplay that has me lost.Stealth is boring to me. This is a game where you slowly walk up to enemies and whack the ever-loving !@#$ out of them with a melee weapon.  Yes, but they suck. This isn't a shoot'em up game. It's a "Holy !@#$ there are monsters all around me that can easily kill me in seconds and I need to be extremely precise or sneaky in my attacks or else I'm screwed" kind of game. In my opinion, whatever that's worth, guns don't belong in stealth games like this. I know, there are guns in good stealth games, like Metal Gear games, but those games allow you to use guns loud and proud, if you should so choose. There is no option to go loud and proud in this game. This isn't a stealth-hybrid, it's only stealth. And that's where you will be disappointed if you are expecting a hybrid. I was looking for something different. I know I originally gave this a positive review, but that was only because I was hopeful that things would change. I wanted a genre like this to succeed. And maybe it has? But in the end, this game isn't for me. I had no business buying this game, and I'm sorry for that. But let my review be a lesson to those who have a similar mindset: this game is very good for what you pay, but it may not be exactly what you're looking for. Give it a chance, maybe? But understand that though this game has guns, you are not a gunslinger in this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun time. Clocked 22 hrs for all three acts (got 6hrs during early access, after beating Chapter 1).Performance is not really good. Chapter 1 runs well, where Ch.2 and Ch.3 can chug even on high end PCs.I wouldn't call this game an immersive sim, as some people do. It's a stealthy shooter where you either go with headshots build (since body shots are pointless), melee hit-the-back build or "throw rock to distract enemies so you can sneak past" build. The game expects you to take your time, plan your approach, line up shots to make them count or suffer the consequences. Which is burning through somewhat scarce resources and/or death.Enemies respawn if you die. This can be either a major PITA or a life saver, depending on how far you are in the game. Early on, dying means that the area you probably struggled to clear will now be partially repopulated. This contributes to a feeling that the game is punishing you by undoing your progress. As you learn how the game works, this mechanic changes into a minor inconvenience or a resource farm.One thing I really like is how enemies never stop being a threat. Even the very first enemy you meet in Ch.1 or at the end of Chapter 3, where you have a decent arsenal of weapons and trinkets, it's very easy to die if you're not careful.Chapter 1 is in my opinion, a lenghty tutorial. Ch. 2 is where the game cranks the difficulty quite a bit and initially you might struggle before you find new weapons. If you equip yourself well in Ch.2, Ch.3 won't be too much of an issue, assuming you figured out the way you want to play and got good at it.Story is mostly there to move things forward. Don't expect award-winning writing. You can do main missions at your own pace.Gunplay is satisfying but clunky, most likely for a reason. Lining up a follow up shot can be challenging if you need to chamber the next bullet when aiming. The animations themselves combined with sway make it hard to pinpoint where you're actually aiming. On top of that, aggro'd enemies move sporadically to make headshots even more difficult. After shot animation blending from hipfire to ADS and vice versa isn't as smooth as you'd expect if you play a lot of modern shooters. So, again, line up your shots and make them count, or at least have a safe "exit strategy".The game features a grid inventory, or "tetris" inventory, however you wanna call it. You can manually rotate items to fit or press a button to automatically sort, but the entire inventory management experience is underbaked. Moving items between containers can be time consuming and there's always this small thing that doesn't work the way you expect it to.

_childDocuments_.review: I was hooked the instant I started playing!Pros: Good story, great scenery, fluid combat, excellent portrayal of darker themes, monsters are numerous, and are scary and fun to fight, monsters range in difficulty every area, the boss fights are all distinctly unique in their own way, lots of collectibles/weapons to be found, numerous RPG perks when leveling up, rewarding for the exploring type, difficulty is based on your patience as a gamer, but MOST importantly this game has serious replay value; you will play through it once, and again, and again... and again!Cons: Looting/Inventory management can be a slight pain at times if you don't mind leaving valuables or loot behind for later. The game leaves you (me) wanting more! Seriously, a DLC or sequel would be welcome with open arms.Overall Critique: Blood West is a solid game that will challenge the common gamer and captivate gamer veterans. Better than most triple A games being released today. An easy 8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Good. This game asks the player to engage with its mechanics more than some may like, but it's an easy recommend if you enjoy a stealth archer build in other RPGs. Plays much more like an imsim than a boomer shooter though enemy design tends to be closer to shooter.Enemies have specific behaviors that can be exploited and memorized. Whichever weapon or solution you decide on won't work in every situation. This game definitely rewards experimentation -- so much so that it may be your only choice to progress. Your reaction to that statement should tell you whether this game is for you or not. Overall a really solid RPG horror fusion. Unique, inspired, and pretty darn fun. Just be aware that it expects you to use all the tools at your disposal to progress.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is pretty decent for its price range as a exploration type of game. But as a action game its falling short for several reasons. The only viable strategy in the early portion of the game is the shank everything with the bone knife once you get enough money as well as bow and arrow landing headshots on each and every zombie. My talents tells me that I'm good at a variety of weaponry, but the ammo runs out dry after a few tries or a few deaths. Just seems to be a poor man's dirty and hard version of any immersive sim that I've played so far. It doesn't do a good job at telling you how to take out the coffin enemies either or birdmen without sneaking up on them, until you stumble on a note at the cursed fort and a note far off into the distance from the starting area. But I guessed how to do it. Just use the axe or bone knife with a secondary swipe up close. The other issues are that the game is just really boring to play because it lacks things to do besides explore. There are no ways to help the player out in a bind except the very very rare item of the bird stones to teleport you to your bone totem "check points". Theres hardly any reason to play this any longer until the following is done; unless there is options for difficulty modes, remove the flaws affliction from the character every time you die, decrease the damage enemies do, save anywhere mechanic and make the ammo more plentiful to either find or buy aslong as you got the money to buy some of course. The game is too difficult because of the ease in which the player bites the dust whenever getting meleed or shotgunned by the nasty female courtisans. These enemies are far too numerous and deadly for the player to have to deal with regularly. You can't even just shoot them after 15-30 minutes of gameplay because of the loss of ammo. So what else can I say but steer clear of this unless you love hard games. Its fun as a exploration game but then you have the combat to try to avoid somehow.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazingly fun game! This is basically Hunt: Showdown meets Stalker gameplay. I love this game and it's basically what I wanted from a dark west occult adventure. _childDocuments_.review: Finished the game in ~13 hours, it's a decent game but has a lot of weird design choices, feels like it wants to be a stealth game but stealth just doesn't feel that good in this game, as a lot of the levels are not designed for stealth at all and completely depends on your "stealth stat", speaking of stats this game tries to be an RPG but also not an RPG, you either completely commit to something or just don't.Also a lot of people say this game is difficult or whatever, I finished the entire game while only dying about 6 times, this game rewards being prepared and knowing the weakness of enemies which is something amazing and rewards being attentive and reading the notes on enemies, kinda reminds me of Pathologic 2 where being prepared makes that game trivial.All in all a decent game and I highly recommend it, but if you are looking for a stealth game this is not it.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't recommend this game enough. I've loved and adored the Weird West and undead gunslingers in particular since I played Blood in my teens. Blood West scratches that itch with a vengeance. The pace is slow and tense - the world will kick your ass if you don't take things methodically. The sound, the atmosphere all top notch - the enemy design is horrific. The way its set up - that you die and resurrect with a debuff (and some enemies respawn) mean that death always has a cost. Sometimes this can be frustrating, but not too often. By the end of the game, you feel like a badass. not only because of the character build, but because you've learned how the game works. This game is excellent.

_childDocuments_.review: If an enemy is 10 feet away staring directly at you with while you're both completely out in the open with no obstructions at all, he will not see or hear you shoot your shotgun. What he will notice is the rocks you can throw. The infinite rocks, with no cooldown, and a trajectory guide so you'll never miss. _childDocuments_.review: It is a dark, cold night in the desert. I leave my camp, fully stocked up on ammunition, carrying my trusty revolver on my hip, and my battle axe and lever rifle on the back. There is a mysterious trinket that has to be recovered from the nearby mines, so I head there, avoiding a ghost town now populated by feathery assassins and ghastly spirits. The entrance to the mines is at the bottom of a cliff, so I slowly make my way down by carefully sliding from rock to rock, losing a bit of my health as I miscalculate the final landing.Finally underground, I stealthily backstab undead miners as they mindlessly hit the walls in search of golden nuggets. An ominous wind catches my attention, leading me to a hidden, massive cave: at the centre of the room is the trinket. As the greedy cowboy that I am, I sprint for it without checking my corners first. A booming roar makes me realize that I have been detected: a tall, imposing Vendigo has found my presence and rushes to the cave, ready to tear my head off.I quickly grab the trinket, equip the rifle, and start unloading the bullets into the beast as I make my way back to the exterior of the mines. I finish my ammunition and the beast shows no signs of stopping. Right outside the mines, there is a small village with a handful of buildings populated by the undead. With no more ammo and very little health, I climb the first stairs I find to the top of the first building. The Vendigo, thankfully, cannot reach me at this height, so it starts pacing back and forth, waiting for me to leave the roof.However, I find a hole in the ceiling, so I drop inside the house. A distracted undead receives the tip of my axe in its neck as I look for any weapon possible. Finally, I obtain just what I was looking for: a molotov. Everything else happens in quick succession: I jump out of a window, the Vendigo ready to start the chase again, and I throw the flammable bottle at it. The explosion illuminates the area, and the creature lets out a horrifying screech as it burns to death. The violent inhabitants of the village are now aware of my presence, but before they can spot me I have already escaped back to my camp, barely alive.No, this is not a chapter from a Dark Tower novel by Stephen King. This is what an average play session of Blood West looks like. Currently in Early Access on Steam, this first-person action horror by Hyperstrange is an outstanding title, as challenging as it is rewarding. Thanks to its Weird West setting and high learning curve, patience becomes the best tactic to survive in this brutal world. Exploration is encouraged to get as much ammo and loot to later sell to friendly vendors in exchange for resources and talismans, but it is the thrill of the experience that is ultimately the main hook of the game: knowing that the protagonist is not invincible, learning which battles are worth fighting, mastering the stealth system to hide in the shadows and avoid combat… It all adds up to a refreshingly tense and nail-biting video game that feels old-school in the best of ways.

_childDocuments_.review: A very fun simplified immersive sim. It has those elements but minus the story choices. You can't play this like a boomer shooter or you'll have a bad time. You're meant to take it slow and utilize stealth, even when using guns.+The gameplay is simple but very fun. Stealth and shooting action.+I like that shooting is quieter than it sounds, so that you can still stay in stealth if you position right and are aware of the enemy and the surroundings.+Headshots are mandatory and they result in a very satisfying head explosion and sound. Bodyshots do very little damage.+3 chapters where each one is a giant map that lets you go anywhere at any time.+Long game, took me 25 hours to beat my first time, and I didn't explore all of chapter 3 (I did for the other two chapters).+The layouts are fun and hide many secrets.+Good variety of enemies where all of them behave differently and are distinctive.+Artifacts are a lot fun, giving a wide variety of unique abilities and effects. I only wish we could hold 4 instead of 3.+A variety of viable builds. You can do the tried and true gunslinger, a bleed build where you take no damage from bleed but do more damage while under its effects (which you can extend), a drunk build which reduces the negative effects and makes you even more powerful, and a pure melee build using either of the two previous builds.+A good variety of weapons. Pistols, long guns, bows, crossbows, shotguns, and melee weapons.+-The curse system is a little unbalanced. Whenever you die you get a soul flaw; die 2 more times and it becomes a far more powerful curse. Some of them are inconsequential like reduced sneak or chance to bleed from enemy melee attacks. Others are very harsh like reduced exp and reduced health. If you're bad at the game the death penalties could send you in a terrible decline. But there are ways to avoid it and you can buy/find purple curse removers.+-The game is perpetually dark given that the sun is blocked due to the curse. You can still see, but it can be a little annoying, although you do get used to it.+-Throwing rocks to get an enemy's attention and move them around has the potential to be overpowered. But if you don't want to "cheat" then don't use it, and I rarely did.-Ending is divisive at best. But the story is extremely simple anyway, so I wasn't really upset by it. Play for the gameplay not the story. The devs are working on an expansion now, so we will see how that goes.-I wish we had 3 weapon slots, where one was dedicated solely to melee weapons.-The bandage skill needs to be buffed as it's pretty useless.1. You will want to max the bonus exp skill asap. 95% of your kills will be headshots so the bonus exp is huge. Then get the lower shop prices and greater monster loot. Eventually you will want to max inventory space. The stealth skill is useful for every build. After that get what you want, gun stuff most likely on your first playthrough. Chapter 3 gives skill point reset potions if you mess up.2. The stash (first found next to Jim) is infinite. To place more when it is "full" you double click the item.3. Buy the bags asap as they give you more space. Chapter 2 I found 2 more small and 2 more large bags. Then buy the traveler's bag from the priest.4. Chapter 1 you will want to focus on melee stealth kills with the bone knife from the shaman, using guns for harder enemies or when it's easier. Hoard as much ammo and supplies as you can, because you'll need them. Chapter 2 and onwards I stopped using melee almost entirely and went pure guns. A melee build you'd obviously keep using it.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a breath of fresh air in the stealth genre, IMO. Gunplay seems a little floaty at times, but it matches with the overall aesthetic of the game, and it took me back to the Golden Eye days. Exploring actually rewards you with great loot, sometimes different weapons or an equipable item like the Occult Mask. Made the rest of the encounters cake. A variety of enemies that require different tactics, and sometimes different ammo, like Boo Hags. Enemy design is a thing I could write a review on by itself, as they all, through the acts, have something about them that's either new all together or a little modifier with a smooth difficulty curve. I really only have two complaints about the game. Fetch Quest City, and no New Game +. I passed up some of the side missions in all the acts thinking on my second playthrough on the same character, I'd fly through it all and finish the game in its entirety. I beat the last boss, cutscene, back to the main menu. No New Game + option or even to select different acts to go back to. But maybe I'm missing something and just overlooked something somewhere?Overall, 9.5/10 for me. I only wish I didn't have to make a new save just to get the side missions done.

_childDocuments_.review: This game lists Hunt:Showdown and STALKER as inspirations. From where I'm standing, that's pretty much on point. I'd say give it a chance if you like either of those two or if you absolutely hate that Hunt:Showdown is a multiplayer only pvp battle-♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥-royale and there is nothing like it in singleplayer (now there is, though, thanks to Blood West).Your main guy handles rather clunky, which means you're not gonna just run in and gun everything down willy-nilly and stay alive, most of the time. Instead, Blood West encourages a methodical and planned approach to combat, which may not be everyone's cup of tea (aka you may be bored out of your butt by this), but thankfully it works veeeery good with the rest of game mechanics, like a good oiled mechanism.This is one of those 'hoarder paradise' kind of games. Your inventory space is pretty much your 'how soon should I go back to base' timer (so I suggest buying both of the bag items in the first location) and you'll be stuffing it with loot, ammo, artefacts and weapons, even more so if you level up the right perks. As for me - I live for this shizz. I'm one of those guys who will make several trips to haul all of the armour sets from the battlefield back to the trader because they sell for insane buck, so this is my cup of tea perfectly.Stealth and sneaking are done adequately. In fact, they are done so adequately I can't even find much to criticise. You can be spotted by sound and sight, there are skills and items and bushes to modify all that, and it works as you would expect. The only weird thing is that shooting a firearm doesn't really reveal your presence as much as it logically should, so there's no need to stick with bows and arrows if you really don't want to (although you'll have to consider doing that for other reasons). So in general, you sneak around various compounds, headshotting some real nasty fellas and collecting a bunch of stuff that will help you get out of a pinch when stealth fails. Most of the time a direct confrontation would either be a waste of ammo or... well... life. Between murdering and looting everything on the map you're doing simple quests and finding more ways to turn yourself into a badass, be it through skills, artefacts or unique weapons. It's surprisingly addicting because level design is pretty good with lots of secrets, looping pathways and points of interests to explore.If I was advising the dev I would've suggested adding a bunch of environmental hazards, traps, exploding barrels, sound traps, useful contraptions and etcetera etcetera. It could've made wonders for the overall world feel, but it's kinda too late for all that now, oh well.In the end, I'll say that I scoffed at this game some time during its development, but seeing some gameplay from the second location piqued my interest so here we are.

_childDocuments_.review: Protip: Equip a rock whenever you aren't in open combat. Rocks can be used to distract enemies. But they are best used to herd enemies into groups, where you can molotov or dynamite them, saving precious ammo. They also let you manipulate the enemies search patterns, allowing you to sneak by unseen. Anyways, onto the review! This game is the Thief meets S.T.A.L.K.E.R. meets Outlaws (Lucasarts 90s Western FPS.. look it up, it was awesome), meets Hunt: Showdown experience, I have been waiting my whole life for. As a huge fan of Westerns, Horror and slow-paced immersive/tactical single player shooters, Blood West definitely delivers! Don't let the three chapters fool you into thinking this is a short game. Because it really isn't. I've been playing the same file since early access last year and I'm currently only about 25% through Act 3 with 55 hours clocked. I can't stress how important it is, that you don't fire this game up expecting some high-octane action-packed Boomer Shooter. The best way to proceed is to use stealth to navigate into enemy territory, where you can pick out the locations of as many enemies as you can find, then slowly snipe them from cover and out of sight, with head shots, or sneak up behind them for stealth kills (which aren't always fatal, so I rarely use them). Your Revenant Gunslinger dude is not a bullet sponge. So you really do want to stay in cover and back away or straight up run away from encroaching enemies. Thankfully most enemy units will lose interest in you after you run a decent amount and they lose sight of you. But there are some enemy types who will hound you clear across the map. So beware!Each time you die in-game you gain a flaw (some negative trait to your abilities). And dying two more times exacerbates the flaw into a curse! Thankfully curses are pretty easy to deal with (you do a short quest for an NPC), but they do stack and can get worse. This is all of course to encourage you to play more carefully. The sound FX and Music are all really on-point. And despite every map feeling like it has the same ambient music, I never really got bored of it. The SFX are really the standout for me. You can hear monsters shuffling around and groaning through walls, when you are in close proximity. Guns have a nice hefty punch, head shots give a nice satisfactory Splurt effect. Sound is also really important for navigating past enemies unseen. The Voice Acting is imho a solid B+ across the board. No one character really stands out, other than the Totem of Souls, (and I swear I recognize his voice from a hundred other things). But none of them are bad.The graphics are almost like Quake 2 Engine, with 3d enemy models. The enemy designs are all very gruesome and creative for the most part. Drawing heavily from North American folklore. Also for some reason every female character (save a small child in Ch 2) have comically large chests. It wasn't immersion breaking or anything, just makes me laugh whenever I see a female enemy or NPC.When I picked this game up in Early Access, with only a demo available, I knew that Hyperstrange was onto something really special here! And I'm glad to say that the 1.0 version is certainly everything I was hoping for! Really hope they keep this IP alive with either DLC or a sequel. While I still haven't found that mythical single-player extraction/FPS, Blood West comes pretty close.

_childDocuments_.review: Initially, I gave this game a tentative positive review partway through act 2 as it has many positive factors that I think many people would enjoy. It has a fantastic atmosphere, great art design and a lot of unique ideas. Many of the gameplay ideas are good too, but this gameplay is also where the game completely flounders.I really wanted to like this game, but it genuinely feels like a stealth immersive sim and a high-action FPS are fighting at the core of this gameBoth sides of this identity work will in a vacuum, I found the stealth satisfying and there's a lot of unique items and weapons. However when put together, it becomes a constant tug-of-war between a smooth, satisfying flow and some incredibly frustrating gameplay.Much of my time playing this game falls into the category of getting killed by something, respawning, trying to run back to the objective and getting killed again before I can reach it. So many enemies in the game are just so powerful that failing to kill them in one stealthy hit is basically guaranteed death and act 3 has a lot of them. I really wanted to finish this game as when it all fits together, it plays really well- But the fact of the matter is that I ended up simply finding it far too frustrating and every time I picture going back to it, I just imagine the slog of endlessly throwing myself at enemies in the hopes I get lucky enough to get around them.

_childDocuments_.review: Blood West, at face value, looks like it'd be a good time as a weird west stealth-action game with some horror elements mixed in. There's hints of it being an immersive sim in there but overall I'd say it falls short in that regard, though there is some character customization via levels and a perk system.But if I had to use a single word to describe Blood West it would be this: .The main reason for this is the incredibly restrictive save system, where progress is only saved at checkpoints whenever you visit a safe zone. Now, if the stealth mechanics were actually  and the weapons didn't feel awful to use,  the checkpoint system wouldn't be so bad.However, I strongly dislike this system for two reasons:1) it discourages experimentation, which is a huge component of immersive sims. If a plan goes wrong you can either risk losing a huge chunk of progress by restoring a backup save or get punished for dying because .2) the penalty for death is severe and wastes the player's time.Not only can you get hit with a debuff that makes your character's stamina drain  than it already does (more on that later) or a debuff that reduces the amount of experience you get, dying also causes a percentage of enemies to respawn. (You can also intentionally cause enemies to respawn by sleeping, but I honestly didn't see the point in doing that).Now, as a Souls player, the idea of death being punishing and having to do corpse runs through groups of respawned mobs is nothing new to me (although there are no corpse runs, thankfully).My main issue with this is that the curse system requires you to die  before you can remove it  you buy a fairly expensive potion or restore a backup save. So while you're better off yeeting yourself off the nearest cliff to get fully cursed, you also respawn almost the entire map in the process.And despite this being a weird west game,  of the guns feel awful to use, especially when you get spotted and it takes 3-5 headshots to take down a single enemy followed by an agonizingly slow reload animation. Even if you manage to headshot one mob from stealth, nearby enemies will notice and run over to the corpse, which sometimes results in you getting spotted immediately because the buffs to stealth seem to do nothing for line of sight, only sound. As others have mentioned, even the Thief trilogy had a better stealth system.In the first chapter this isn't a big deal because the enemy density is low enough that it allows you to pick off one mob at a time and there's plenty of hiding and sniper spots to cheese encounters if you need to (despite guns being largely ineffectual at range because that makes sense).But the second chapter ramps up the enemy density a la Dark Souls 2 because "mOrE eNeMiEs MaKeS iT hArDeR, rIgHt?" which is  true but also another layer of tedium on top of the already tedious gameplay while also being a really cheap and lazy way to make your game harder.You could also try and run away from the enemies to lose aggro, except your character absolutely  at running. With how fast your stamina drains you can run for maybe 3-5 seconds before your character obnoxiously and loudly starts panting, which can happen repeatedly if you forget to disable the toggle because the game doesn't do that automatically for some reason. The only way to prevent this is to slow down, which is bad when you're being followed, or stop moving entirely, which is . You  throw a molotov to try and distract the enemies temporarily, but they're so weak it's not worth keeping them in a quickslot and the game only pauses in-menu with a certain artifact equipped.And while there are upgrades to the amount of stamina you get and how fast it recovers, there is nothing to reduce how quickly your stamina is consumed. About four hours in I got so frustrated with the stamina system that I opened up Cheat Engine and locked my stamina at max so it could never drain regardless of how much I ran or jumped. It detracts from the gameplay so severely that I question why it's even in the game in the first place.Speaking of obnoxious, managing your inventory with a controller is incredibly frustrating. The 'cursor' will randomly snap to other items in your inventory, pressing any of the directions on the d-pad often causes it to jump multiple spaces, and there's no way to rotate items unless you use the mouse. There's also no way to use items directly from the inventory, so every time you want to use something you have to equip it to one of your three quickslots first. And heaven forbid you try to take something out of your bag manually instead of double-tapping 'A', because if it can go in a quickslot the cursor will get stuck on the first two quickslots and refuse to go into your main inventory.I should probably praise the game for something at this point, huh? Let's see... *checks notes*One thing the game  do well is the environments, I really like how this game looks and the atmosphere of the different areas. The enemies could use a little more variety as all of the enemies of that type look identical, but I also know that's a lot of extra work so I understand why they didn't go that route. When it comes to the soundtrack there's only a few tracks in each area unfortunately, but the tracks that play do a good job of adding to the tense atmosphere (except the weird recording of the one guy shouting, which felt out of place and played in both chapter 1 and 2). The silence can also be pretty tense because you can often hear enemies mumbling or groaning nearby, even through walls..Overall I really wanted to like Blood West because it seemed like it had a lot of potential and it does have some good things going for it, but after almost 12 hours of bashing my head against the wall I think I've had my fill of this game.If it looks interesting pick it up on sale, but definitely not for full price.And before anyone says "git gud," I'm not going to waste the time needed to "git gud" if I'm not having fun doing so.

_childDocuments_.review: Stealth gameplay has an unspoken scale when it comes to tuning it to be challenging - how difficult the stealth is to execute, and how punishing it is to fail. These are not tied to how rewarding it feels to manage the system successfully, or how fun the game is in general, it's just an encapsulation of what sort of stealth game you're playing.Ideally your game should be straight down the middle - a hefty helping of both so the stealth feels engaging and challenging, and the stakes for failure feel appropriately high. For games that are truly 'stealth games' this balance is their lifeblood, it's what allows a game to be almost 100% stealth yet function fantastically because the only mechanic you're engaging with feels fleshed-out, complete.Blood West, sadly, is waaay off to the side - the punishing side. It's not the most punishing stealth game ever by any stretch, but if you look at how the stealth feels to use and how punishing it is to fail on-balance, it's so far into punishment territory it's not even funny.In terms of where the game IS, failing to stealth properly is brutal. You'll be chucked into fights with fast-moving enemies, often swarmed, and must use limited resources (ammo/consumables) to stand a fighting chance. Then not only did you use those resources, but you'll often get chunked or even outright die as part of the punishment, especially if you fail more than once in a life.This leads to the death punishment, which is a stacking random curse that may affect your stamina generation, XP gain, or hilariously even your stealth effectiveness, with a sidequest to clear it along the lines of "collect 5 non-guaranteed drops from dead enemies" or "do this many stealth kills".So to recap: not only are you cursed with a penalty which is removed by a time-sink chore, you ALSO used resources trying to avoid death which you no longer have, AND the enemies RESPAWN meaning you've been robbed of any progress from using resources and need to complete the same situation again in a much worse off state.Every death this compounds, every failure makes the game feel more chore-like and like a huge step back. So then on the flipside, the stealth would need to feel really engaging and fleshed-out to match this brutal punishment.And yet it doesn't. Stealth is literally walk behind something crouched until the detection bar is nearly full, then sit still for a few seconds until the bar goes down. Rinse and repeat for the entire game. Enemies are often walking away, meaning you're doing a sort of "two steps forward one step back" approach to reach them. They also often just pivot and look at you because they've reached the end of their patrolling route; this is a common occurrence in other stealth games, but in those games which do it well it makes sense because the stealth is the engaging/fun part and you're being encouraged to be methodical and scope the situation before approaching. There is no method here, just going through the motions.This is all a shame because the game itself is SUPER cool. I love the enemy design, the world's visuals, music, sound effect design, voice acting, and general combat feel. But it feels like I'm playing an awesome wild-west-demon-hunting-revengathon that's been dunked into a muddy pool of boring-and-incredibly-frustrating-stealth-nonsese.My request to the devs: please at least add an option to disable curses. This would not be in the spirit of your game, but the spirit of your game is exactly what's making it horribly unfun for some players, myself included. If this change is added I'll revisit and give it a more thorough run to see more of the game and revise my opinion - but I'm not slogging through this as it currently sits.

_childDocuments_.review: -Kurt Russel as Wyatt Earp in Tombstone (1993)Howdy, feller! Have you ever wanted to sneak around various desolate landscapes of the Wild West riddled with unimaginable horrors, while you send hellspawn monstrosities back to the abyss that spawned them? Well, look no further! Blood West is an immersive first-person stealth shooter. You play as an undead gunslinger with an unknown past, who got thrust into a cursed, nightmarish world when he was ressurected after his untimely demise... . Not entirely sure as to who really brought him back from the dead, the gunslinger is soon given the reason why: find the source of the curse that plagues the land and destroy it. Like Hunt: Showdown, Blood West caters to a niche audience, fascinated by a decaying Western themed world filled with death, gore and horrors beyond the wildest imagination, perhaps even tapping into the Lovecraftian realm of cosmic horror. The romanticized alure of the Wild West is combined with demons, ghouls and ghosts. Blood West consists of three episodes, each one taking place in a different biome. There is a desert, a bayou and lastly a mountainous area. The game's lore is explained in various notes discarded throught the land, item descriptions and of course by talking with NPCs. Sin's repercussions and subsequently damnation are thematically prevalent, especially for greed. There are no difficulties to set in-game; it's permanently hard and punishing. Blood West requires a lot of patience, otherwise frustration is unavoidable. Especially in the 1st episode, if you refuse to play steathily, you will suffer. It gets easier as you progress and that becomes apparent in the 2nd and 3rd episodes, where roleplaying as a spaghetti western's pistolero, gunning down everything that moves, is really easy. Val Kilmer (Doc Holiday) proclaimed, followed by a sneaky cough casting doubts upon the statement. Well, the gunslinger in Blood West enjoys his newfound prime.... Every death is countered by ressurection, albeit at a cost. Various debuffs are applied each time the player dies and although they may begin small, they will stack up upon your every subsequent demise thus potentially having disastrous effects on the playthrough. Luckily there is a panacea for all them pesky debuffs/curses and it's in the form of a potion -fret not partner, not the kind snake oil peddlers deal in, for this one actually works! Another penalty that the gunslinger has to face every time he resumes his corporeal existence is that some enemies will inevitably respawn. The enemies come in many shapes and sizes and they are all equally disturbing and . As I mentioned before, your first death won't be your last. The gunslinger is the definition of a glass canon: you can one-shot/melee hit most enemies with a proper build and suitable weapon, but you get a punishment too and rather swiftly. Now, hold on there, partner. Best make them spurs go quiet real fast.... Blood West's stealth components are nothing extraordinary but what they lack in complexity, they make up in immersion: There is a sneaking bar, triggered by enemies hearing or seeing you. This way you can gauge how stealthy you remain, as the bar levels flactuate. Such simplicity was personally welcome, also the UI on screen is generally minimal. And when that stealth meter fills entirely.. oh boy, . There are guns, bows and a plethora of melee weapons.The inventory is organised in a primary and secondary slot weapon slot, with also three slots for necessary consumables such as health and stamina potions and another three for artifacts, i.e. tastefully designed trinkets. There is also an RPG element, with experience gained and skill points unlocking by leveling up, but personally I found the skills themselves somewhat trivial. That doesn't mean that there aren't some vital choices to make when it comes to building towards a stealth-based or guns-blazing playstyle, it's that the effects of most skills are inconsequential in the long run. The gore is delightful, despite the graphical limitations of the game. Blood squirts and splatters all over the place and watching the body motion of enemies dropping dead is simply put, . The guns feels amazing with a satisfying kickback and cool sound. The ambience is subtle yet so effective. The PS1 aesthetics and the low-res graphics help create a disturbing atmosphere. The pixelated textures take away some of the punch that Blood West's gore carries but certainly succeed in building up creepiness and conveying dread. "The eternal tranquility of smoldering ruins" is often disturbed by monsters growling and revolvers going off... Ok, I'm not gonna lie. Gunslinger's grunts of agony as he is getting slashed, pierced and shot are also there. Don't hesitate for a second to skedaddle outta danger, partner and by all means: don't be ashamed. I've run for my life in Blood West more times than I have glanced at Annabelle's bazookas and that's a lot of times . To sum up, Blood West is amazing, I never thought I'd fall in love with a (primarily) stealth game since I rarely approach games with a stealth mentality. Oh well, it was more than worth it and I highly recommend it~

_childDocuments_.review: Recommendation: Buy it. Gameplay summary spoiler based on my Early Access experience as of 3/21/2022 You play in a fully open map without any instancing or restrictions.  Why you should buy it:- Phenomenal game. I don't say this lightly. I am very excited to see the finished product. - EARLY ACCESS: Only one chapter is available out of three. However, the chapter appears to be, quite surprisingly, polished, full, and complete and it seems to have taken a few hours for me to complete it. I didn't even notice. That being said, and since there are no other chapters yet, I recommend you complete all your missions before taking on the boss since you cannot resume your pre-boss progression once you kill the boss. You just get an Early Access "Soon (TM)" end screen.- The graphics sold me the game. Oddly enough, the graphics remind me of the old Outlaws game if it were faithfully moved to 3D. Even the random items like the tin cans littered around look great and fit. I can't say it's PSX graphics for sure because it's somehow better but still has that same feel to it. - The gun mechanics are fun and feel just right, but they incorporated gun sway, bullet travel, and bullet drop. - The level design is very well thought-out. Whoever worked on this deserves a pat on the back. Good job. Exploration is rewarded and there are lots of hidden secrets, items, and side routes that do not waste your time.- The sound effects, the music, and the voice acting are exceptionally really good. My recommended improvement and/or issues with it: - The AI can be easily overcome in some instances when playing vertically (jumping on a ledge or looping around a ladder-based platform). If there is a route that does not involve jumping or ladders, the AI will use it to get to you, but if you jump down the platform then the AI loses you and starts walking back. Needs to be improved. - Noticeable amount of spelling and grammar mistakes. It does not affect the game, but it does annoy me especially because their English is otherwise great and not at a novice level.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to say, this is not a bad game by any means, it's pretty solid for what it is, and a good start into early access, and if I could give this a neutral review, then I would, but ultimately the lack of gameplay depth has made me decide to give this a negative review.It only took about 30min of playing, and simply selling all my starting gear, and I was already able to get the best knife (Bone knife) from the first trader in the game. I'm currently about halfway through the first (and thus far only) Canyons map, I could beat the boss right now, but I still have things to explore, and I'm already at the point where I don't even bother picking up any loot anymore, because I have more money than I could ever spend, and I have not even explored the entire map yet, as I've said, so the potential to get more loot to make money is still huge. I have two large bags in my inventory, and bought all the special guns, and still have over 3k money.Same thing goes for the skills, I'm halfway through this first map, and there will be more maps coming to this game, and I already have all skills that I care about. (I'm level 7, and there are more skills, but I don't really have much incentive to get them, because they are mediocre)Absolutely zero environmental interaction.I've come across so many areas where I thought to myself that so much more could be done with this game. An example is the bridge that goes over the Canyon, where the cropses are hanging, why can you not hit the rope and make them fall down, and then later loot them? Or why aren't there instances where you see a rope hanging off a cliff, and you get a prompt to pull when looking at it, and it pulls up a small chest or so? There's just nothing to interact with, no shortcuts to unlock, or anything else.Few enemies.There are like 7 different enemies on this first map (boss not included), most of the time you just fight the same 3-4 enemies over and over, the common ones are all present in every area you go to, there aren't really any areas that only house a specific enemy type, and you just (mostly) fight the same group everywhere.The enemy variety is also lackluster. It's no secret that this game is inspired by Dark Souls, and a big thing that DS has, is that it features unique enemies and you may only ever encounter one single time, and it makes you think "what the hell is that?", because it just stands out so much, and it's not even a boss, or may not even be hard to kill, but it may drop something nice, and just adds to breaking up the repetitiveness. Like, why isn't there a group of small spiders in one of the caves, that can only be found in this one cave, and nowhere else. Even if you simply re-color and re-size an existing enemy, and just put it somewhere at the edge of the map guarding a chest, just anything that breaks up the monotonous nature of the game.Dire need for a hardcore mode.This game is too easy. I've already mentioned the easy economy, and that money is not an issue, and even the curses upon death are no real challenge to get rid of again, they don't really make you play more cautious, you can still fairly casually run around and just knife (almost) everything after you got the hang of the game. (Because it can be difficult in the begining).And so I think there just needs to be a mode where, when you die, you lose all the loot you picked up, and lose all the XP you gained since your last level-up, which then, in classic Dark Souls fashion, you can try to pick up again, but if you die again, it will be gone.I've already read in a topic in the forums here, that one of the devs said that he'd like to revise the current map, but he's not sure if it will happen. So this makes me very doubtful that those issues will be adressed, or that gameplay will be given more depth. Sadly, because I think this game could be so much more.

_childDocuments_.review: Blood West lets people play as a Revenant of sorts, an undead soul bent on some measure of vengeance for the other undead souls that summoned him. It is a first-person shooter with light rpg experience progression, taking place in an open old west world. It is the original Thief games, but with a glorious sub-text of carefully procured firearms. Sneak around and make stealthy kills of western demons, and when you are in the right spot and amongst good cover, pull out your revolver or shotgun and blow them away. Combat mechanics are solid and reward discipline (!) and precision. Exploration opportunities are ample and rewarded. Enemies are vicious and not to be underestimated. This is one Hell of a great bit of sneaky violence... the sort of game any Thief fan had wished would have evolved from the ground-breaking series. My own skulking around, patiently waiting for the right moment, is going to cause me to spend a great deal of time hunting demons in this old west world. The developer did right here. Very very worthy.1.0 UPDATE:An improved Skill tree, additional weapons & items, new enemies. The dev knows how to strike a balance between difficulty and fairness, challenge and playability - for example, the benefit of the doubt is given to the player when calculating LOS for stealth purposes, making it easier to sneak, rather than impossible. Remains very very worthy. DLC, sequels, and entirely new settings please... keep developing!

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely Brilliant, easily one of the best experiences I've ever played. To preface, I'm a huge sucker for wild west meets supernatural and this game absolutely nails the premise. The story is very straightforward with very little need to explain itself, and yet throughout the games   I found an rich environmentally told story of towns and locals torn apart by the very westward expansion that was so dominate at its time. The voice acting was absolutely ear-porn as there was not a single actor not positively nailing their role (Gianni was great and all, but Holy ♥♥♥♥ Stephen Russell knocked it straight out of the park with his performance) The sound track was also simply perfect, with its ability to slowly capture the tension of stealth in one section, and the titillating chase of enemies hunting you down in another. The combat felt absolutely fantastic, with the game feeling straight up punishing and cruel at the beginning, almost forcing you to learn how to navigate the locations around you in stealth. I had so many moments especially in the first chapter seeing new enemy types and going "Wow, that sure looks like a place I will not go now, but cannot wait to get geared up to go there!" And every time it felt more and more enjoyable getting stronger and stronger. (Minor note but the fact that every enemy wielding a firearm not only drops its firearm, but also its ammo depending on how fast or clean you killed them is fantastic and made me feel so much more inclined to kill them in stealth. I appreciate that game decision so much) The games Enemy variety kept me constantly having to adjust my play style and work with the different types of weapons and firearms the game gives you. Finally, the games bosses were not only actively challenging, but genuinely fun to fight. die, and fight again.Easily one of the best games I've played in recent years, and cannot recommend trying this out out enough. Don't be fooled by its rough difficulty in the early stages, you'll feel like a walking Texas Ranger by the end.In regards to the ending  Whatever the case, I've been made a fan and am now eager for whatever Piotr Szekalski does next.

_childDocuments_.review: Full disclosure: I actually reviewed this game for an outlet.I don't write Steam reviews too frequently, but Blood West is a really special game and I'd want to make sure that the people who pick it up know what they're getting into. Expectations for this experience are key:-Immersive Sim? That's a bit of a stretch. To the dev's credit, they haven't bandied this term about too much. Don't expect a zillion ways to approach each encounter; instead, this game is a weird west horror-themed action RPG, and is combat-focused and stealth-prioritized. Which leads to my second point.-Unique combat mechanics? Definitely. Shooting feels a little weird and goofy and first, so early hours are gonna be backstab city. Luckily, backstabs feel fantastic, the environmental audio is excellent - both in terms of beasties groaning and muttering creepy dialogue - and taking apart an encampment of ghouls is terrifying and often challenging. The randomized enemy placement and resurrections between death keep things jumpy. I love how not EVERY monster respawns on death, just enough to make you feel paranoid when returning to locations. Note: you WILL get better at the shooting. Partially with a couple of good buffs and items, and partially just as you grow more comfortable with the feel of the game, so more aggressive play styles are certainly available when ready.-Gear? HECK YEAH. Can't think of a recent indie with a more satisfying range of weapons and equipment. There's tons of cool stuff to find and purchase in each chapter, and a lot of it is lost forever if you move on to the next chapter without discovering it in the last. There's plenty of space to buildcraft and spec what's important and select only the loadout kit you want. Use a guide if you must, but most items aren't locked behind some esoteric gating; it's there for the picking if you're thorough. ALSO: I think that a lot of the items swap locations, so you won't always find a specific piece of gear in the same spot every playthrough.-Exploration? If you love exploration, chances are you'll love this game. While it's not packed with NPCs or side quests, searching high and low through Blood West's maps almost always leads you to something cool or valuable (see previous point). It's a pleasure to figure out the shortcuts, alternate routes, dangerous enemy patrols, and hidden stash locations. While the environments aren't completely unique on their own, the weird west setting adds to the eeriness and novelty.I think that those averse to stealth will not take too well to Blood West, as they'll never reach the aptitude needed for more aggressive play styles. And, for those purely interested in stealth, they'll find much of chapter 3 to be a beatdown, as the front-facing action picks up significantly by then. However, if you love BOTH forms of play and dig the vibe, I think you'll love what Blood West achieves in its design. It's a high-quality and finely-detailed experience that truly feels one-of-a-kind, even while tipping its hat to its core inspirations.

_childDocuments_.review: Played in early access between 07.13.2023 and 07.15.2023I picked this up because after playing the System Shock remake I've been on an immersive sim kick. The game was designed to be an intentionally clunky old school immersive sim, right down to needing to reload your weapon manually when you are out of ammo, along with having limited slots in your quick access bar, and limited inventory so be prepared to stockpile your loot somewhere near a trader. You're only allowed two weapon slots; the first can fit all weapons, the second allows only the knife, pistol, and weapons of similar sizes. You also have three accessory slots for healing items along with Molotovs and drinks that give you specific bonuses.The aggro system is odd. Enemies are able to hear your footsteps and see you if you are in their line of sight. They cannot however hear your gunshots. Once you aggro one enemy, every single one within several meters of it will be aggroed as well, so you will be ambushed the moment you are spotted. The enemies will chase you until they can no longer see or hear you, and they are able to follow you eons away from their placements. The gunners will always lead their shots, so you have to be mindful to change direction after you hear them fire or you will run into the bullet's path.The basic ammo have almost no punch aside from getting headshots. The enemies in the second map are spongy as all hell, able to soak up to about four bullets from the upgraded revolver I got from the first map, and about three non-headshots from the double barrel shotgun. Headshots are pretty much mandatory to kill. I don't know if the guns' ironsights don't line up to the center of the screen or I'm just bad at aiming, but I've had an easier time getting headshots from the crossbow than any other weapon since the aiming reticle doesn't disappear when I ADS. I've had better luck with the knife in the first map which has a surprisingly long reach and has even the headshot function if you knife the opposition in the head.Keep in mind you'll be facing more than three enemies at a time if you aggro any one of them in the crowd so it's absolutely not advisable to start a firefight, which is odd since the steam page advertised that it is an option for progression. The game throws a lot of different enemies at you when you aggro them, and you are left to basically shimmy through a maze of lead on bullet fire while trying to headshot the running melee rushers. With the limited HP you have, you are brought down in about a total of four hits from enemy fire unless you upgrade your HP, then it's maybe five.Death in the game is incredibly punishing. When you die, you will suffer a penalty towards one of your attributes unless you have a trinket that protects you. Die three times and the penalty becomes a curse that penalizes you further. You could have less max HP or make more noise when you sneak, or various other things. You are able to heal the curses through drinking a specific potion, or by doing a task that the totem in the respawn point gives you if your penalty becomes a curse after three deaths.I would have been fine with how the curses worked, but the game punishes you further with how far some of the respawn points are. In the second map, there are very strong and spongy enemies that ambush you if you aren't stealthy, and I was only able to find one respawn point, which is the one you start at when starting the map. So not only will you suffer curses, but you will have to traverse back all the way from your respawn point to where you wanted to go with all of the enemies you've killed along the way respawned. You are put at a further disadvantage each time because you are spending money to keep yourself stocked with ammo along with the trinket to protect you from the curses. Eventually you may run out of those resources effectively making the game needlessly more difficult and tedious to get through, forcing you to grind to kill the respawned enemies to gather up the money needed to remove the curses and keep you healthy.Mechanically the immersive sim portions work pretty well and the game has an interesting world to explore, especially the second map. The issue is that the game is brutal and expects you to take a lot of punishment. However instead of designing it in a way where you learn from your mistakes, it punishes you further with a very questionable enemy design where you are effectively playing a lead on bullet hell with far away spawn points. It tested my patience so much that I essentially save scummed to circumvent its mechanics rather than to use them as intended, because after awhile, trying to get through an area's long slouches of walking from point A to B without dying to bulletfire had stopped being fun.Another point I should make is that the game has no real way to save either. You're only given two options to save your progress; either at a respawn point or you can quit the game through the pause menu and it will save at the exact location you're standing at. Your progress will be overwritten the moment you respawn, so the way to circumvent its long and tedious grinding is to force quit the game between the time you die and the moment you respawn. That way you are able to resume the game without losing progress if you've saved through quitting the game through the pause menu.With the way the save system is designed, it's very likely that the devs do not want you to create your own checkpoints and quicksaves, hence why I'm a lot harsher with my criticism of the game. However the choice is your's. Either you waste time to manually save the game then resume, then alt+f4 and resume the game quickly after dying, or waste likely more time to grind to get back what you've lost and find your way back to where you've died.As this game is still in early access, I'm hoping the devs will iron out and balance some of the shortcomings to make this game worthwhile to return to when chapter 3 rolls around in December.

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels like a supernatural wild west version of Deus Ex - with a good touch of the old game Blood as well. Fairly open level, you can shoot your way through but shouldn't, skill progression, artifact augments... I'm not usually good at stealth games, but something clicked for me with this and I spent a good eight to ten hours trying to explore every location. Four stars.

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't expect this to be anywhere near as good as it was. It handles like a solid stealth shooter, with generous hitboxes, fluid movement and mostly gun handling (old west guns are by their nature somewhat clunky). It's not a super fast twitchy sort of shooter like DUSK, games like Hunt Showdown, STALKER, and Dishonored feel similar. Combat starts out DIFFICULT. Enemies are punishing and melee forces you into harms way more than you'll be comfortable with, you'll be starved for ammunition, and unless you can get headshots, you'll feel outmatched. As you learn and get more confident in fights, they start to feel REALLY satisfying, especially at the end of each stage where you'll be fully equipped and can easily make your way across the map without dying. My only advice is to USE the tools you're given. Don't stockpile away dynamite, purple remedies, and ammunition for a rainy day. The world and shops provide most ammo and consumables as you go. The weapon variety is great, (more would be nice, but the selection is pretty good as is) and the legendary weapons look good and aren't hidden away behind secret walls, they're all accessible if you explore a bit. Look for ramped boards, holes in walls, and other obvious nooks and crannies. The RPG mechanics aren't too in-depth, but they provide a good sense of progression and the upgrades are all useful, depending on your build. There are TONS of items in the world that give you buffs/debuffs to your stats. Some are a safe bet, some are risky, but they can all be sold for decent money. The Hunt Showdown inspiration is pretty apparent and it really works. The "retro" graphics are done so well that it's easy to forget about given how great the lighting is. The models are high(ish) poly but the textures are pixellated, giving the weapons and enemies a really refined but still stylish look. Enemies have a creepy, unnatural sort of look to them that sells the "eldritch horror" theme. Environments look great and make sense, with different compounds having a spread of enemies that make you never really feel safe, but it's hard to get totally overwhelmed if you're planning ahead and using stealth. I went into this with no expectations but it's honestly my favorite game of 2023. Can't wait to see more, would love to make some mods down the road. Easy 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good game, graphics are nice and gameplay is satisfying. It's kinda hard until you learn the basics and one or two tricks, then if you die you probably dun-goofed. There's one huge map per chapter which takes a few hours to fully explore, especially if you're like me and hoard everything. My only complaint is that a bunch of times i miss and i don't know if i whiffed or the hitbox was not where it should've been, which is why you'll probably want to shoot still enemies until you get some slow-down effects while aiming. Also the ending didn't make sense but whatever i didn't buy this for the story. Anyways here's a few tips for new players: - Stack raven skulls and chicken heads to avoid having to run everywhere (stealth game so character is slow af) - Exploration is usually rewarded with unique weapons or artifacts if you carefully search areas away from "the main path" - The player's stash has INFINITE space, double click what you want to store if you can't drag and drop, you can use shotguns and coins to make it bigger and then order everything however you want - Items in the stash carry to the other chapters - So far you CAN'T go back to a previous area after the chapter's boss so be sure to grab everything on the map before moving onGiev dlc pls

_childDocuments_.review: UghIt's like Turok, Thief, and maybe even Call of Juarez had a baby and they made it blood(THAT blood) difficult.It feels like unfair ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ half of the time but something keeps me coming back. It wasn't until unlocking the final boss in map 1 that I got anything CLOSE to being able to contend with enemies and that's because I began to understand their strengths, health pools, and planned out how to fight them. You will always be low on ammo, you will regularly accidentally get your ♥♥♥♥ ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up, and you will probably spend more time than you'd like scrounging for ammo or taking pot shots at the big enemies to whittle their health down and swinging from feeling like an arrow headshot assassin to wonder why one birdman has 7 arrows sticking out of him and ISN'T DEAD YET.If they could at least introduce difficulty levels I could see this having a casual play-style, but right now this is a VERY hardcore retro fps rpg that demands a lot of attention, focus, and strategy.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ fun. The sound design is FANTASTIC. Every weapon is fun to use. A lot of the enemies stand out in my mind. Almost every aspect of the gameplay is perfectly done. Its perfectly does stealth game play and fast pace combat at the same time which is very impressive. It has plenty of builds and items I find myself trying out regularly that really spice up the game play a lot. Of course at the end of the game I had a overpowered set up I used most of the time that suited me, but even then I had a lot of items that I switched from. This game was really addicting to play since almost every encounter feels meaningful. At any moment a simple enemy could change the tide of battle really quick.This game at first when you don't know anything is TOUGH. It really feels like your trapped in a apocalyptic wild west world where every enemy can kill you with their supernatural strength/abilities. Over time through acquired knowledge and skill I over came these intimidating obsolesces. Even after my OP build, stupid enemies I've killed over 100 still killed me at times because I was careless.This one of the few game that gave me that same power struggle I overcame over sheer will like Dark Souls. Speaking of Dark Souls, besides some very slight similarities in it's story, the fact that almost all the mechanics of the game are tied with the world of Blood West itself is really great. It really immerses you in the game's world where it doesn't feel like a game at moments. I gotta say the level design of the three main stages are great. I find myself wondering to every corner of the map just to experience more of it.If there's one thing I could complain about is that the story itself is pretty lack luster. With out getting into spoilers, it doesn't really go anywhere interesting besides it's base premise. All the NPCs are just cliche archetypes with no characterization besides what that character archetype brings. The only character stand out in my mind which is Annabelle but that's just because she gave a little of her backstory so she has a little bit of depth but ultimately a fairly cliche character. I like the undead cowboy too but my interest in him is purely surface level. They also don't stick around in my mind since most of them barley do anything in the game besides help you progress in the main quest. Most of the main quest is not interesting since they're mostly just fetch quest. The places they lead to are cool but the quests themselves are boring. In fact I accidentally completed the final quest before starting it because I picked up all the quest items by just wondering around the map.If they are working on an expansion DLC, I would focus on making weird to fight enemies with beefy varrients of main game enemies to recapture that initial struggle of the main game where you overcome seemingly great odds. Of course place it in a interesting new location to spice it up. Maybe a snowy place to do that classic western movie troupe. Otherwise I have full confidence they will make a really fun/interesting DLC gameplay wise. Story wise they need to take a whole different angle to it. Keep it edgy and badass, but explore the possibilities of a haunted wild west. Make unique characters where they could only exist in this game's weird world. Also have the main missions of the DLC that are more then fetch quests. Have them more involved with the game world itself.I might've crapped on the story a lot but it's not bad at all. It's just serviceable. It stands out to me since the game itself is amazing. I definitely recommend buying this game if you like stealth combat/challenging shooters.

_childDocuments_.review: Skin is the prison of the soul!Blood West is a survival horror immersive sim in a weird west setting that never leans too hard into either game genre. This can be disappointing to some, but despite that the game honks.Set across 3 chapters and maps, Blood West is a bigger game than first glance. Once you get the first map you might be a bit disappointed at the size of the level, but as you explore you quickly learn it is deceptively big, with lots of tunnels, caves, towns, and more to explore. The level design is reminiscent of the best in the immersive sim genre, however it ultimately falls a bit flat with the intricate level design being meaningless. Yes, there are multiple paths through a level, but it is never guided by the skills I choose or how I play the game like the best immersive sims. Despite that I enjoyed thoroughly exploring all 3 maps and every zone within the maps. Finding new weapons, ammo, potions, and talismans kept it rewarding. The combat is quite intense at first and things can quickly get out of hand throughout the entire game, but the enemy AI is easily gamed. Regardless, sneaking around to stab someone in the head or landing headshots with a punchy revolve always felt incredibly good. If you aren't scouring every inch of the map ammo might become scarce and you're forced to sneak and stab. There is a good variety of enemies, a good number of them being re-skins/modified enemies from the first chapter, but I never got bored fighting them even with the AI issues.The inventory system could be handled better. The survival horror inspiration is evident, but things like windows not being on a consistent side, having to run back to your stash, and auto sort only working in the main backpack was frustrating. The inventory management/ammo scarcity is a good idea, but there's so much ammo in each map it doesn't reach it's full potential. This is where the game falls flat in terms of its survival horror inspiration. On the subject of survival horror, the game isn't scary!Blood West is obviously horror themed with ghouls, monsters, and demons, but the game lacks scares. I don't necessarily think the developer was going for scares, but I think the game would have benefited from some more tension.While this review is full of criticism, I really enjoyed Blood West. The gunplay felt good, the gameplay loop was satisfying, and the art style was great. Don't go into this game expecting a super deep or well written story. If you're into horror themed westerns and maybe are a bit intimidated by survival horror or immersive sims, Blood West is a great starting place.

_childDocuments_.review: In my ~25 hours with horror western FPS Blood West, I endured what can only be described as a bell curve of fun. My first hour as the game's nameless undead gunslinger of a protagonist was about as much fun as being born: I had zero context, zero skill, and was perpetually screaming—at the game’s spooky pixel monstrosities, sure, but also at its clunky, cumbersome UI and frustrating mechanics. At least, I thought they were frustrating (and justifiably so) because on death the game would slap me with a random debuff, like reduced max health or stamina, that would inevitably lead to another death and another debuff. After a couple hours of experimenting and a dozen or so deaths, my now super-nerfed stats made it impossible to kill anything, meaning I couldn’t gather the requisite materials needed to pay to remove my now mile-long list of debuffs, meaning I had to completely restart the game. In hindsight, this self-propelled death spiral was mostly my fault, because when I first booted up Blood West, I saw pixels, demons, and guns, figured it was like any other fast-paced retro boomer shooter to come out in the last five years, so I Leeroy Jenkins’d face first into every enemy I saw. Only problem with that plan is the fact that non-headshots do next to nothing in Blood West, and having to reload mid-fight is a guaranteed death sentence.  Like I said, I started this game like I started life: zero skill and zero context. You see, Blood West is decidedly not a new school, fast-paced pixel art boomer shooter but rather an old school “immersive sim” – a genre term I had little appreciation for before Blood West, despite having played and enjoyed games like Deus Ex HR/MKD and Dishonored 1 & 2. For the uninitiated, the term “immersive sim” broadly refers to games that prioritize immersion and player choice via environmental interactivity and realistic simulated systems... which is all nerdspeak for, say, having an easier time sneaking past a guard after you extinguish a lantern or blow out a streetlight.  Now, Blood West doesn’t have a high level of environmental interactivity—wooden fences and lanterns aren’t destructible, for example—and its simulated systems, like basic AI behavior and stealth, aren’t all that immersive, in part because the AI in Blood West is as figuratively braindead as it is literally, and stealth in this game is visualized with a boring proximity-based UI meter that spoils scares before they happen. Thus, from a mechanical standpoint, Blood West isn’t particularly good as immersive sims go... in fact, it’s pretty bad. But where Blood West fails to create immersion through its mechanics, it succeeds with a dark, atmospheric soundtrack, intricate level design, and above-average voice acting. Welcome to our strong climb toward the zenith of Blood West’s bell curve of fun: mid-game, particularly around the end of the game’s first chapter, of which there are three. By this point, I had more or less figured out how the game wanted to be played: stealth and headshots, headshots and stealth. If I was feeling desperate, I’d even kite big groups far enough to reset their aggro and then pick ‘em off one by one with their backs turned. Gradually, I started leveling up, unlocking helpful traits, buying buff-bestowing artifacts, and upgrading my personal arsenal. I was starting to feel pretty unstoppable... just in time to get punched in the gallbladder by Blood West’s first boss: an evil tree that will pull down its pants to receive punishment if you pop its little plant root pimples (assuming you can dodge its wave of wooden spikes and cull its incessant adds). While I wasn’t exactly impressed by this or Blood West’s other boss fights, what I faced was challenging with interesting narrative relevance.  Speaking of narrative, let’s talk story. Upon resurrection, a talking totem directs you to every corner of all three maps to gather cursed artifacts for the totem to neutralize in the hopes of restoring the land. There’s a nice twist to this dynamic at the end of Chapter Two that I won’t spoil, but then the plot pretty much goes right back to making you “go there” to “get that thing.” And it’s right about now you’re probably realizing that we’re on the Blood West bell curve’s downward slope. After realizing that there was little more to this game than repetitive fetch quests, through interesting biomes and well-constructed levels, admittedly, I started to have progressively less and less fun with Blood West. The characters themselves aren’t particularly engaging, and while a variety of new and interesting enemies—like the Predator-esque super Wendigo and two-headed Nightbear—helped inject some dangerous novelty into Chapter Three, they ultimately didn’t change the fact that I felt like I was doing exactly what I did in Chapters One and Two. Still, for $25 ($17 on sale!) and about 20 hours of content, I do think Blood West presents above average value. This said, don’t go in expecting a highly polished or replayable experience. In the end and after averaging up our micrometrics, Blood West earns an okay aggregate MEGA score of 3.14/5 (full scoring breakdown, from “Plot” to “Sound” available in the video review), and I’m happy to answer any questions you have about the game or my review. Thanks for reading!

_childDocuments_.review: Blast the heads of some undead, search around for ammo and hidden "legendary" items with special effects. Exploration is rewarding, combat is decent enough and sneaking around smashing in skulls with an axe is exciting. The game lacks a bit of variety in both weapon types, enemies and locations, and the gameplay isn't all too deep, but for the time it took to complete i enjoyed it very much! Love the gridbased inventory, the whole system around death-penalties, graphics and satisfying headshots. There's also a good bit of environmental storytelling and details around the world and items. It's a pretty fun game and it was well worth the 10€, although it's still a little bit thin at this stage. Took 11 hours to get through (what I assume is most of the content) the game has to offer so far, having explored most locations and thoroughly re-murdered the undead. From being scared and sneaking around in the beginning, to blasting through the west guns blazing by the end, I had a lot of fun! Very much recommended to all fans from Doom to Skyrim's stealth archers!  A small dissapointment was that after you complete the scenario in the game (this version has the first of three, which will all be released later on) your save is locked at the victory screen, and your gun-blazing comes to a screetching halt :(

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent, very challenging, but consistently engaging work in progress game. It brings to mind games like Stranger's Wrath and Darkwatch. Some ghost town of the west, trapped in time. Shooting mechanics are very slow paced and reliant on patience, timing and skill/mastery of said mechanics. The enemy variety may be the only thing lacking, aside from some noticeable spelling issues -presumably due to the creator(s) native language being something other than English. Overall, a fantastic experience. I finished it in one sitting. Sun up, to sundown. I absolutely recommend this gem of a game. It can only get better from here.
