_childDocuments_.review: While I typically abhor checklists, I believe there's value in using one here. For a series long dormant like Metal Slug (Other than the brief belch of caustic dust that was Awakening), much of this game's appeal is how effectively it evokes its subject matter.Thus, I've composed an objective list of criteria to measure this game against, after which it will receive an official Metal Slug rating.☑ Has a Metal Slug☑ Highly expressive, comedic pixel art and animation.☑ War machines that look as if their engineering schematics were written in Comic Sans.☐ Arcade hard difficulty.☑ Military jazz soundtrack.☑ Move-or-die gameplay.☐ The guy says "Heavy Machine Gun"☐ Discoverable power-ups mid level.☑ Mummies!☐ Zombies!☑ Your guy screams "Noooooooooo" on death. ☑ Your girl screams shrilly on death.☑ "See you in Hell"[...]Oh, you're still here? Did you want an actual review? Why would you come to the Steam review section for that?Fiiiinnnnnnnne. First some quibbles. As a tactics game, it's a little lacking on content, with only four levels and a handful of enemies types. Characters offer different playstyles, but there's a lot of ability overlap to muddy those distinctions. I also wish the harder difficulties were unlockable right away, as you might need them to feel challenged. It's got some bugs (an overlapping music bug might force a restart on occasion), but patches have been squashing them so far.All that aside, the emphasis on sync kills and moving as much as possible each round encourages tactical creativity. The game excels at presenting you with a seemingly hopeless starting situation, then making you feel like a genius when you scramble out a victory.If you're the type who would play Metal Slug until you could 1CC it, I suspect you'll love this game. Alternatively, if you're the type who noted the FAT transformation was missing from my checklist, you may feel the content mass of this Slug is too light, and could use some more plating.If you're not a Metal Slug fan, I'm not sure how you got here, but Into the Breach is three klicks west (stick around though if you've already conquered that warfront.)Do you align with how I look at games? I might have more titles to recommend to you.

_childDocuments_.review: MST is a very interesting take on the genre. Since you can only aim in 4 cardinal directions, positioning becomes not only super important, but also extremely rewarding. Chaining synchronized attacks can often feel better than crack, and I love how much it emphasizes run and gun gameplay over hunkering down and slowly advancing like in XCOM. The visuals are brimming with charm and personality, and I really enjoy the core gameplay loop. I can't not recommend the game. But at the same time, I have to ask myself, "Is it good enough to justify 3 years of waiting?".There are a lot of underlying balance problems. For example, there's no penalty for dying unless there's a secondary objective requiring everyone to survive. It feels like the game could've benefitted a lot from what Slice and Dice has, where a unit that gets knocked out starts with half health in the next encounter. Revives are way too abundant, which makes the game even less punishing. It also seems like there's no scaling based on how many regions you've done, meaning doing all the regions makes the run super easy, while doing as few regions as possible is ♥♥♥♥ and ball torture on higher difficulties. Another big issue is that the game seems to lack content and variety. It feels like you've seen everything there is to see on your first few runs. While there's a nice amount of variety in regards to loadouts and playable characters, enemy and mission variety is rather poor.I really enjoy the game for what it is. But more than anything, I look forward to what the future holds in store. There's an excellent foundation here, and I think a few updates or expansions could make a world of difference.

_childDocuments_.review: The first misstep for Dotemu. But that's salvageable. From a business perspective Tile Tactical Turn Base is the opposite deal of Rogue Like games: it's a niche genre in wich there's few contestants, and they're all champions (Tactics Ogre, Symphony of War, Into the Breach). Competition is ruthless, it takes the sharpest of mechanics, thorough balance and tempo. And Metal Slug Tactics is not there yet.Don't get me wrong, it's still a pretty entertaining game. Animation and graphics are still top notch, Metal Slug franchise theme is well rendered. Pushing movement to get dodge and mock up the run and gun style is smart. But it's just not crisp enough. Boss fight is a piece of cake. Positioning is not crisp, elevation is messy, templates are unclear. Adrenaline mechanic is convoluted and wording is confusing. Half the extra abilities and weapon mods won't see any use.  Moreover you can pretty much "Marco'n'Grenades" the game through and through without really put brains in it. And, fellas, we just need more tanks, more 'copters, more moving parts.More metal, more slugs, less rough edges. You chose a complicated matter with TTTB Dotemu, be up to it, I'll still be supporting you.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite the game launching with all the bugs, both small and big, as well as it being structured like a rogue-lite, it's a nice take on the SRPG/TRPG genre. The creative way they took the philosophy of the 2D games to "run and gun" with Tactics' Adrenaline and Dodge system is a creative way to encourage aggressive positioning, especially for early parts of the run to maximize your point economy for actions, since the later parts of the run you can potentially earn those points effortlessly from passives and active skills. I get the complaints about the game being "short", not just from the rogue-lite structure of short amount of stages to complete a run, but if anyone doesn't know any better, there is a true ending, which requires a minimal of 3 separate runs to unlock the path. But honestly, it makes it to where, even in a longer, fixed story structure, they definitely encourage experimentation of different character combinations and their loadouts to see how they can potentially synergize. The devs themselves have said that the structure is directly inspired from "Into The Breach", so any complaints about the structure is contested with how Into The Breach worked, and a lot of players loved the game.I'm also in the camp of "I'm not quite sure if 3 characters is a good number of characters to take at a time, but sure, whatever you guys say lol". I personally I would've like to see a team of 4 like how some games can let you play up to 4 players at a time, but woulda, coulda, shoulda, we got the product now and it still works out. I'm hopeful of seeing further support for this game, not just to patch bugs and such, but more scenarios, more characters, more loadouts, maybe custom loadouts, or a combination of these ideas. I like what we have so far, but it's understandable how some people might say it feels bare bones in content.Full price is not bad, but it would most likely more convincing as a sale game, and definitely as a gift. Overall, 8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: A Worthy Breach-LikeGonna start by saying what this isn't: This is not a number tactical rpg, this is an Into the Breach-inspired game, it's more of a puzzle game than beeg numbers get beeger. The ''TACTICS'' do mean tactics here.This take on Metal Slug and the choice to be inspired by games like Into the Breach was a good choice. It translates that fast pace perfectly into a Tactical game. You're always expected to think of the best way to take down enemies on your way to something, be it the end of a level, deal damage to a boss, or defeat enemies themselves.The lives system is also interesting since, much like the OGs, you're expected to die, or even make sacrifices here, so you have 1ups to make up for it, and you're going to need it on higher difficulties.Each difficulty unlocks different units you fight against, on the initial one things are quite easygoing, even on ''normal'' but after that, you're gonna start to have a few close ones or just get obliterated if you don't actually think or understand the mechanics properly.It's a great ''I have 40 minutes to waste'' game.For people disappointed with it being a puzzle game and not a tactical RPG may I recommend ''VALKYRIA CHRONICLES''? it always reminded me of Metal Slug a bit, down to a very marketable tank, check it out, it's great.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun, if pretty simple tactics game. With the potential for good strategies making you think and figure out the best solutions. It has a procedural generation campaign with a few options and unlocks to keep it different alongside a myriad of upgrades, weapons and loadout choices. Its design is very similar to Into The Breach. While I might say its a smidge more complex, its a little less like a board game (or chess which i compared it to at the time) but the general control and idea is the same as is the campaign setup, you have zones you can clear, each zone you do a few missions and then you fight a boss before you can do them all, the more zones you do the greater the challenge but the greater reward. Meaning the medals at the end of the campaign count for how many zones before doing the boss zone. which is pretty much exactly how into the breach's system works. but into the breach is pretty good so its not an issue. if you like metal slug designs, youll like how this looks even if in some cases its a little more pixelated (a stylistic choice) and if you liked into the breach but wanted just a smidge more depth and persistent upgrades then the gameplay should suit you aswell. This as of launch has a fair few texture glitches. overlapping and sometimes misleading positions as a result. i hope they fix them but its early days and they seem like small glitches even if some cause real annoying problems

_childDocuments_.review: The big thing to know here is that this is very self aware entry into the grid-based tactics/puzzler space.  It's riffing heavily on what's gone before and is very playful with rules and expectations found elsewhere in the genre. Units can go completely wild and generate enormous action economy depending on exactly how the perks and upgrades fall out. This is paired with really strong objective focus- comboing out is fine, but it needs to get you across the map (or whatever you're being asked to do.)Because the game is like this, it puts a bad foot forward. The first map or two of a given run is really flat, as you basically just rotate units around and proc synchronized attacks, unable to really go flying. Initial perk selection is really crucial...and without having seen any combos go off, it's not always obvious what you're going to want. This connects to the big issue(s) which are consistency and documentation (sooort of in that order). The first thing is that the game just isn't very consistent in how it rules actions. There are a fair share of bugs, but even beyond the bugs, the rules just bring up a lot of situations in which it's not clear what will happen- does this trigger that? is this 'an attack' for synchronization purposes? does this consume flurry? (etc etc) and the game is really very inconsistent in handling these. This means you're always crossing your fingers- this looks right, but does it actually work like that? This is compounded by abilities jamming a lot of text into little boxes and often just...not doing what they say they do. Characters often do stuff that just isn't apparent from perusing their card (a good example of this is an early unlock who moves farther than everyone else...and thus builds more resources...which they really aren't very interested in telling you). A lot of abilities are combo pieces with two open ends- they need to connect between two other things, but since the perks are just random they can flat be dead draws- and the description text isn't clear enough to work out what they do in many cases until you find the parts that plug in at one end or the other (causing you to go 'aha, this actually does...') Assuming the bugs get fixed (the boss respawns in spot A but isn't targetable there + if you reload the map it reveals that he really respawned in spot B but the sprite was placed incorrectly) this will still feel really weird playing maps 1-3, and the first few runs to boot. The reward for putting up with it? Really toothsome tactical puzzling with the eventual promise of flying off the handle and clearing off whole maps (though given the objective focus, you'll usually just knock out your goal and be gone).

Might seem a bit confusing to explain like this but this mechanic is kinda different and enjoyable.I have only a couple of complains:- Protect missions: it is not helpful for the friendly NPCs to protect to be stationary, without any interaction to make them move. For example there are Special Actions that move other units (alies and enemies) , but these are unable to be used on them protect NPCs. Of course using them might make the game feel easier, but who likes to protect NPCs? This could at very least be an option that we could toggle before each game session, so it could be enabled so it doesn't feel stressfull having to defend the NPCs; hardcore players can keep them stationary.- Undo button: I feel that this button doesn't do much... yes it is good to redo the move command, but it is all it does. If for any instance we attack or use a Special Actions that we don't like the outcome, it doesn't undo that action... there is a Turn Refresh, but it has only 2 usages, and have to redo all actions is a pain... Again I know this in place to keep the game challenging, but I have misclicked some commands and shot my team when I only wanted to check their skills and stats...  having a complete undo action would be great - maybe have it has as option toggle!So far I am enjoying it very much.And the mummify part... such nostalgic seeing this! :')

_childDocuments_.review: No tactics game has gripped me like this since The Last Spell and this one might be even better. I’m expecting to easily sink over 40 hours into it, and it's one of those rare titles that’s worth every penny, even at full price. The only downside is the occasional bug in certain levels, but I’m confident those will get ironed out over time.Positives:Fresh, innovative gameplay: Damage reduction depends on constant movement around the map, with a heavy focus on combos and synchronized attacks to bring down even smaller enemies.Beautiful, nostalgic art style: Both the character designs and pixel art are stunning.Concise story: It’s short and to the point, with no lengthy exposition, and no need for prior knowledge of the Metal Slug series.Roguelike structure: Each run feels unique, and characters can adapt to different roles depending on how you build them.Negatives:Bug fixes needed: Nothing game breaking, but annoying nonetheless. The game should not have been released like this and needs polish.More content wanted: While the game’s content is fair for the price, it feels like it’s just begging for DLC. Additional characters, enemies, and areas would elevate it even more.

_childDocuments_.review: It is probably a good game, but I decided to refund it. Here is why:1. My problem is that this game encourages constant movement and "synchronization" with other characters (plus the neverending reinforcements). Which not only goes against the traditional way of how most of the tactical RPGs work, but it is big limitation in itself. So yeah, the positioning is a key here, but in a way that the game forces you to be in certain positions to get the results. It effectively nullifies strategies like tanking, shooting from afar, slow and careful advance, blocking the bottleneck aso.2. You are overwhelmed by active and passive skills from the very beginning. Yeah, having variety in available skills is great and is the reason why I enjoy good tactical game, but you have to build your char from the bottom up to get used to char's abilities and to use them effectively. And especially in game like this where non-traditional behaviour is a must it is very difficult also to watch and constantly remind yourself what the actives and passives of your companions are.Perhaps I am just an old dog, too conservative for the playestyles of this game, but bottom line I couldnt enjoy playing this game, even though there is hardly bigger fan of pixel art tactical RPGs than me. BUt I am sure this game find its audience, it just wont be me.

_childDocuments_.review: I thought this was going to be more of a traditional TRPG, like Final Fantasy Tactics or even Fire Emblem. Or maybe even more of a puzzle-like TRPG, akin to Wargroove or Advance Wars.It's definitely in the direction of Wargroove, but even the puzzle aspect seems weak. Most of the time I can just bruteforce the match, with little consideration of consequences. The game really does want you to run and gun. It tells you that in the tutorial! Additionally, the battles don't have that length that I was expecting. Most of the battles are quick and dirty. A battle might be like 5min. No more than 10min for sure. Also seems like there's little depth to the fights, aside from the synchronizations (combos). And the systems that exist, such as weapon upgrades and ammo management, just serve to complicate without any real benefit. Metal Slug Tactics reminds me a lot of a game called "Pathway." And I liked "Pathway." I guess when I see the word "Tactics" in the name of a game, I'm expecting something like FFT. My expectations were a bit subverted.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not bad, but.... ugh.Maybe after they fix some of the bugs, make some of the gameplay elements more user friendly, and it's on sale.  As is, it just wasn't fun.  Normally a strategy game can suck me in and I'll play for hours without realizing it.  With MST it felt like I had played for a few hours and it was only 1.  That's a bad sign.This is just going to end up as a list of little issues that add up to a blah experience:- If you like turn based strategy games, you'll probably hate this.  It's unusual in that the game tries to force you to move as much as you can (because run-n-gun).  That's very different from most strategy games, and you'll get used to it, but then they start randomly teleporting enemies in and all strategy is out the window.- Varying pixel size in a pixel art game / ugly UI.- Trying to scroll with the mouse is canceled out if your mouse is over a UI element.  And most corners are UI elements.- Clicking on a characters portrait doesn't scroll to that character.- LOTS of bugs.- Confusing dodge / cover / shield system that's only made more confusing when a bug changes the rules.- Only having two undos, and no way to restart the mission (other than dying).- The map height levels suck!  You use the scroll wheel to select levels so you can see things that would otherwise be covered.  However, when you scroll to a new level it selects the tile above or below the currently highlighted tile.  Which means the tile you're selecting is no longer under your mouse cursor.  If you move your mouse cursor, it then highlights the tile you're actually over instead of the tile you scrolled to.  If that was confusing, THAT'S BECAUSE IT IS.  I thought tile based games were pretty much figured out in Roller Coaster Tycoon.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been a fan of metal slug, tactical rpgs, and roguelikes for my entire life, so this game felt like it was tailor-made for me, and ended up buying it on day one. And initially, it delivers. There is an incredibly solid gameplay foundation, depth, and variety, all of this paired with some amazing pixel art that metal slug has always been known for.But... that's gonna be the extent of my praise for this game, at least for now, because there are a ton of visual and interface bugs. Now, regardless of your personal tolerance for these kind of issues, a deep tactical rpg with roguelike elements is probably the worst possible genre for such bugs, since these games must deliver every relevant bit of information before taking decisions in a clear and intuitive way (the golden standard for this is, in my opinion, into the breach). If resetting a turn in a tactical rpg not only breaks the way  all of this information is delivered to you, but also breaks interactable items' and enemy sprites, then this is a game I cannot recommend, especially given the amount of things going on (lining up your troops for chain attacks, keeping passive procs and environmental interactions in mind, etc). You can probably imagine it is not fun to keep track of all of this in an inconsistent and buggy interface.I really wanted to like this game and praise its gameplay elements to hell and back... but I guess that's gonna have to wait.

_childDocuments_.review: There is a reason for the negative vote. This is a fun game, but there are more bugs than I have ever seen in my lifetime of gaming. I wish I was joking. This thing is RIDDLED with bugs. Every character, every mechanic, EVERYTHING has a bug associated with it. Not only that, but there are only 4 maps and a handful of missions and enemies. The store page claims there are 110 hand crafted maps, 20 different mission types, 36 different weapons, 176 weapon mods, and 36 loadouts. This. Is. A. Lie. You will only play the same 4-5 mission types over and over again. The vast majority of weapon mods are useless, you won't even want to unlock 90% of the unlockable ones because they will just muddy the pool when rolling for the ones you want. Not only that, but the majority of the weapon mods have 3 tiers to them, meaning that number is actually 176/3= 58. And 36 loadouts? More like 27 useless loadouts you will never touch because each unit has a clearly superior loadout when comparing their respective kits. Upgrades aren't all that great aside from a few of them, so you will end up with a massive stack of cash with nothing to spend it on pretty quickly. I see a lot of people crying about the the cover mechanic in the reviews and the discussion board. The cover mechanic is not an issue at all. People that have a problem with it are stuck in the Xcom mindset - to them I say branch out kiddo. This is a good tactics game, even if it is likely the easiest one you have ever experienced. Due to how easy it is even at the highest difficulty, you barely feel the roguelite aspect once you get a better understanding of your characters and enemies mechanics.Like I said, this is a good game. But for the reasons I mentioned, I would suggest waiting for it to go on sale. I bought it at a 10% discount, but 20 dollars is still a bit much for what you actually get - especially when there are more bugs than you can count. Wait till it's about 15$, or buy it if they add more content for free.

_childDocuments_.review: I've never played Metal Slug, so I'm not familiar with the characters or the connections to past games. It is a turn-based tactical RPG that requires you achieve particular objectives of a variety of difficulty, such as killing foes and reaching a destination. It has a classic arcade vibe to its presentation, the music is wonderful, and the sound effects are good. The main issue, in my opinion, is that the difficulty can be a little too high at times. When you have to save units from mummies or chase down a target, and mummies will kill them in one turn while spawning right next to them at the very start, usually while you are on high ground and cannot reach them down below or vice versa, ending your whole run right then and there. But then other times you'll have the same mission, but it doesn't matter if the units you're protecting get killed, it bugs out and lets you succeed. But it's still a bit weird to have one objective being "Kill 4 enemies in 1 turn" and then "Protect all these units for 5 turns, or it's game over!" and not even work properly.The bugs in this game are game breaking. Your units that downed and you revived? Now they are stuck in their downed state or their downed transformed mummy state with no normal skills, unable to move or attack. Save and Quit, those units are now somewhere random, out of bounds, in a much dangerous location and also their turn is over? These become more and more common the longer you play, wouldn't be so much of a big deal if not for the fact that it will ruin your run. I didn't enjoy having limited ammo since it prevented you from using your special weapons when you truly needed them while you were attempting to salvage all you could before entering the final fights against the bosses. Since you can't just spam your strongest weapon, you have to focus on setting up synchronized combo effects (being in sight of the enemy when engaging) to really fully utilize your ability to win each stage, which felt boring. Especially since it's limited to once per turn against bosses, add on top of that the layers and layers of bugs, glitches and other issues and it's just a disaster. It had the potential to be entertaining, but it lost its appeal after about an hour of reaching stage 4 and losing since there was no hope of preventing the units from bugging out, units being killed on the first turn and sometimes ending the run and sometimes not, the softlocks, the reloads, the teleporting units and multi-layered boss fights are really cool with awesome designs, but just like the Steam Next Fest demo they provided a while back, unpolished and needing a lot of fixes.

_childDocuments_.review: I really hate to leave a negative review for this one because I love the IP, it is incredibly polished in some areas, and what it does it does well. Unfortunately though, it's lacking a real "hook" to keep you playing. At about 5 hours in I've unlocked all the areas, more than half the cast, and completed a run on the base difficulty. According to achievement stats, that puts me in the (currently) ~20% of players that have even completed a run and that's understandable.Metal Slug Tactics is an incredible looking pixel art dream (something we rarely see nowadays) that plays somewhere between a roguelike character builder and a puzzlish-strategy tactics game. A lot of reviewers compare it to Enter the Breach (which I haven't played) but from what I know that comparison seems right. One look at this and you can tell that the Metal Slug IP is perfect for this kind of gameplay and at a foundational level this works well. Moreover, this does enough to innovate on the tactics formula to separate it from the bog standard move, attack, end turn formula. By incentivizing you to move each character as far as possible to increase damage reduction, interact with environments, and align characters to synergistically increase damage output, this creates a tight and fast paced feeling experience. It's surprisingly thinky, with difficult enemy design and passive abilities requiring correct ordering of plays to succeed. There is also the typical roguelike/lite in-run and meta progression of resource management and looking for the best skills or weapons to develop. Add to that a host of unique characters, each with separate loadouts, which can make play incredibly diverse. Overall, here is a lot to enjoy here in the underpinnings as long as you don't mind a little grind.But that's where MST starts to falter. I wouldn't go so far as to call MST repetitive, but realistically there's not much actually happening at any given time to create real gameplay variety. It very quickly boils down to doing what's most optimal at any given moment, and that's usually the same handful of things. The incentive to move far on turns often conflicts with environment limitations and requires you to choose between damage reduction or damage output, which gets stale as characters are low HP and enemies are spongy AF. Boss fights are absolute slogs and pre-decided attack patterns on map spaces or enemies boxing you in often force you into death, artificially inflating an already inflated experience. There are also some weird decisions here with regard to height in that it doesn't offer you any defensive advantages and most of the time you can't hit anything below you or across a gap. Some enemies create defensive zones that make groups of enemies completely invulnerable or wall off areas with damage, while other enemies afflict you with status effects that outright destroy your options. What I'm getting at is that while there some cool ideas at work here in regards to tactics, most of the time you feel limited in what you can actually do and that drains engagement. Die hard strategy fans might really love this, but I'd wager it's not satisfying enough for the average player.The main positives I have for MST revolve around how beautiful the game looks, the uniqueness of play, and potential variety in methods of play. I also have to admit they do have some really cool QoL stuff like a clear interface (despite the small text issues) giving you all the information to make the best plays and ability to cancel moves or replay turns. For sure, this is a solid experience... despite some game breaking bugs. It's worth mentioning that my winning run was almost completely soft-locked on the final phase of the last boss, which definitely soured my desire to keep playing even though I was able to finagle it into completing.Another major issue I have is that I feel like the IP isn't as well handled as it should be. While the pixel art is fantastic, and there are a ton of nuanced in-world references, all the characters look slightly "off" from typical SNK Metal Slug art. This is understandable of course as it's made by a 3rd party company, but it lacks a lot of the cartoonish flair that MS is known for. Adding mummies is cool, but what about fat soldiers? And maybe I simply haven't seen them in my time played, but where are the Martians? Even more egregious, where are the Metal Slugs? From what I can tell, they are only available in particular locations, missions, or usable with particular skills. I haven't seen one in my ~5 hours of play.You could argue that I haven't seen all of what the game offers or that I don't completely understand all of the nuance and I'd agree with you. The consistent conclusion I come to is that while MST looks appealing to play, actually playing it just doesn't click for me. If does click for you, I can totally get that. I certainly can't be mad at the asking price, which, even if I don't like the game, is worth putting forward in support of more SNK IP experiments in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Metal Slug Tactics is a fun and unexpected game in the series. It's nice to see the metal slug crew escape the mobile slop tie-in pits that SNK has submerged them in. This game does have a few bugs but it is otherwise an extremely polished and well-tuned turn-based tactics rogue-lite. While the latter part might turn off some people there is enough variation in builds, team composition, and level up rewards to keep you going for hours. Plus the game encourages you to try out different combinations by offering story vignettes as a reward. This helps keep the game play fresh even if you are playing the same maps over and over again. The Music and graphics are excellent and the sprite work is so well animated you will constantly be looking for little details, plus its so colorful. They really captured the Metal Slug Aesthetic. As for gameplay its a a solid turn-based tactics game that reminds me of Disgaea with the emphasis on lining up your characters to perform synchronized attacks. Mastering positioning is the key to success and setting up disgusting combos that can wipe out the enemy. Each of the character has a unique play-style and you can take up to three for many combinations and each character has four load-outs as well leading to many permutations. If you are a fan of SRPGs I highly recommend giving this one a try.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fine addition to both the Tactical Turn Based genera of games and also to the Metal Slug Franchise. Each character has their main specialty and weapon setup along with several alternate setups that they can swap to as well. You will almost always find yourself outnumber as usual but feeling similar to it's run and gun roots most enemies don't take major effort and can be taken out in one or two attacks.For me one of the more interesting shakeups is the dodge and adrenaline systems. Adrenaline is your MP or Skill Points. It’s what you use to activate your active skills. And you gain it from movement. The other thing gathered from movement is Dodge. Which acts as temporary(unless effected by a specific status) armor higher dodge the more damage that ends up being ignored. In some way making this a run and tactics. I haven’t played a massive number of TTB style of games so I can’t say how new of a system this is but it felt very unique to me and caused an interesting mix of having to decide on getting the most dodge for more suitability or the perfect positioning for group attacks or skill usage.I was worried when I first heard about this game. It’s not the first time I’ve seen a beloved series try jumping into a new genera and while I felt that R-Type Tactics was solid this game feels like it stuck the landing much better.If you’re a fan of Metal Slug, or a fan of Turn-Based Tactics games I’d recommend giving this game a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Super charming and well thought out tactics game. The constant-motion of your troops that is required captures the essence of classic Metal Slug in a turn-based format, which is laudable in itself, not to mention the delightful pixel art you'd expect from the series.There were a modest number of minor initial bugs, but the devs have been prompt to quash those so far. _childDocuments_.review: I've heard about some bugs, but I haven't ran into any so my experience has been nothing short of positive. Now as someone who’s obsessed with Fire Emblem and a bunch of other tactical games, I have to say, Metal Slug Tactics is high on the list. It’s not your usual “sit and strategize” kind of tactical game—has its own vibe, and honestly, it’s one of the most fun I’ve ever played. What makes this game so unique is how much it pushes you to keep moving. In most tactical games, you’re setting up defenses, splitting your squad into groups, and carefully plotting every move. Here, it’s the opposite. You want to keep moving around, steadily advancing across the map. And here’s why: movement builds two key resources—Dodge Points and Adrenaline Points:Dodge Points make your characters harder to hit. Adrenaline Points charge up your special attacks. So, instead of camping out and playing it safe, this game thrives, on constantly moving every turn. It’s such a cool shift in gameplay that makes every turn feel intensePre-Battle Prep: Upgrades, Abilities, and the TankBefore you even hit the battlefield, there’s a lot you can do to get ready, and it’s just as fun as the combat itself. For starters, you can upgrade your squad’s weapons and abilities. Each upgrade lets you tweak your team to fit your playstyle—whether you want more firepower, better defense, or faster ability cooldowns. It’s a satisfying layer of customization that lets you feel like you’re really building a team that’s yours.Now about the Metal Slug tank, because what a treat for longtime fans. It’s  a powerhouse on the map. Using the tank strategically can make or break a fight, especially when you’re up against tougher enemies or bosses. It’s a blast to deploy it at just the right moment and watch it tear through everything in its path.Weapons in Metal Slug Tactics are another layer of strategy. Everyone gets two types: Your standard weapon, which you can use forever without worrying about ammo.Your heavy hitter, which burns through limited ammo but packs a punch when you need it most.And trust me, you’ll want to save those big guns for the boss fights. There’s nothing worse than running out of ammo when you’re face-to-face with a beast of a boss.Friendly Fire: Off, and That’s a Good Thing In Some CasesNow, here’s something interesting: friendly fire is turned off. You may think it's weird but it actually works in the game’s favor IF you do NOT abuse it. With friendly fire off, you can position your team in ways you wouldn’t dare in other games. It opens up a ton of options for aggressive tactics. Plus, it lets you focus more on wrecking the enemies without worrying about hurting your squad granted it's not abusedSync Attacks Are Game-ChangersAnother mechanic that’s a total game-changer is Sync Attacks. If you can line up your team with an enemy along the same path of fire, you can trigger these powerful combo attacks. They’re not just flashy—they’re super effective and can completely turn the tide of a fight. Sync Attacks force you to think ahead and position your team carefully, which is a lot of fun when you pull it off.Vastly different charactersEvery character feels unique, and their abilities really drive home the idea that no two play the same. Some have passive abilities—like boosting the team’s defense or dodging more often—while others have active skills that let you dish out extra damage or provide support. It’s a blast experimenting with different squads and figuring out which combos work best for your style.If you’re into tactical games but want something that keeps you on your toes, Metal Slug Tactics is one of them. The way it leans into movement, sync attacks, and resource management gives it a fresh feel that’s so different from the usual tactical grind. Whether you’re a Metal Slug fan or just someone looking for a unique spin on strategy games, this one’s worth checking out.

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely a worthy title in the Metal Slug line. tl;dr, lots of little weird bugs they need to fix, but the wombo combos you can set up after a few levels up is a good time. The roguelite aspect means a lot of variety for replay, but it could do with more regions and more bosses... which should be pretty easy for them to implement. I'm really hoping we get plenty of expansion packs here.  The Sync system is fantastic, and creates some awesome setup opportunity that makes you feel very clever. I don't think I would wholeheartedly recommend a full price purchase, but I don't regret throwing 25 bucks at these devs at all. Basically, you start off with three out of nine characters unlocked. Each character has an easy unlock method, with Leona's being the hardest; beat the game with each of the other eight characters. Trevor can be trickier because you need to beat the game with just two regions, which means no power leveling. Nadia needs all four regions. Each of those characters has four possible loadouts, though only one is available at the beginning; one more is unlocked by beating Morden with a character, and you buy the other two with in-game currency, earned by saving coins or picking gold coin missions in the game. The harder the difficulty the more money you can get. These loadouts change a character's playstyle pretty significantly because they decide your weapons. The skills are less significant, though confirming you have a certain one can make setups pretty neat. For example, I had a very underwhelming run with default Clark at first, though he does bump damage a little. With the Gale machine gun loadout I was running into an enemy at map start, launching them into Trevor, who was positioned to use his AOE sword; by the end of the run it was 10 points of damage on a dude, giving Clark extra move to bump Gale's damage up to 6 per shot, then throwing Marco's default skill to shoot three shots. This positively shreds bosses. Trevor could position enemies where he needed them with Flying Knife, them teleport into the middle with Shinobi, and slice them all up with a basic attack (which might be aided by an Instigator mod from some weapon). There are definitely bugs as of 28 November 2024. I don't think I really noticed anything that messed with the game much - my worst was when the game seemed to lose 4 momentum from a move that was intended to throw an enemy into a Sync kill to finish an objective. Most of these are graphical, like a character dying as a mummy reverting to the character but appearing alive. Sometimes they're confusing; an objective where you need 5 killed with Eri, but the progress tracking says "6 remaining", and did get claimed at 5. Characters appearing to fall down chasms versus leaping them, but zipping back up to the other side. It definitely feels like a beta release at the moment. Polished enough to play through, a lot of fun, but hopefully they'll knock out all these weird issues. The devs are engaged in the discussion boards and there's a dedicated bug board as well.

_childDocuments_.review: MS Tactics is a fantastic answer to the "how do you make a new Metal Slug game when arcade games aren't a thing anymore?". The rogue-like tactics and fast arcade style pace of the game fits in great with the franchise. Pros:1. Great new art and spritework (the inclusion of classic sprites is also welcome)2. Great soundtrack3. Challenging levels4. Developers and writers clearly know the actual story of Metal Slug and it's characters. 5. Game is fun and has replayability. Cons: 1. Game released pretty buggy (it's improving, but I'm still finding new problems till now). 2. The scope of the game is pretty small. In retrospect, this makes sense when you realize most metal slug games can be played in 20 minutes, but this also leads to not much variety in mission types or zones/bosses. 3. Figuring out the roguelike elements and what's needed to push the story along isn't very clear, nor are they always very rewarding. 4. Some characters are too situational for use in all playthroughs. 5. You might never see some fan favorite enemies until you bump up the difficulty. Overall, if you love Metal Slug, you should get this no matter what. But the game and it's concept are going through some growing pains on launch. Nonetheless, I've been feeling happy to finally be playing a new Metal Slug game again.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like Metal Slug? Do you like rouge-lite stuff? Do you like tactic games? Are you not missing a part of your brain? Well, you may like this game. Devs did a fine job translating the 2D run-n-gun nature of the classics into a TRPG format. If you understand what the game teaches you and not hunker down like any other TRPG, then you will find your characters using their specials very often, take much more abuse than you think, and you will be fragging so hard, you would run out of mooks.The sprite work is great, fluid and charming as ever. Though it will take some time to get used with the new perspective. Coming from the classics, it felt a bit weird to see your characters talking with dialogue. Weirder still, to see brand new characters. But they are not too out of place unlike the ones in MSD/MSA/Awakening. The characters you know from the originals are still the same dorks with the same specials adapted to this game and then some. And the gang's all here too! Downsides.At the moment, the game is riddled with bugs. Most of them are minor and can be ignored. But sometimes the boss breaks and require you to go back to the main menu. Few bugs may crash the game or chop up the FPS. One may require you to restart the game unless you don't mind having white noise playing as long as the game is up. But these are temporary problems that can be fixed.There are only 4 big bosses in the game. There are mini-bosses to add to the mix, but dang do I wish there are alternate bosses at the end of a region just to break the monotony. I understand that we are dealing exclusively with Rebel Army so we can't have Aliens, Amadeus or Ptolemaic stuff. But, it gets a bit boring without some change of pace. You can put original bosses in if you must but please include alternate bosses.Also, minor stuff. Morden is like a father to his men, that's why they are all loyal to him after he defected from Regular Army. Morden wouldn't have a tendency of shooting them up. They took away Dragon Nosuke's wheels and Big Shiee doesn't actually use its BIG ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ CANNON at you. Shame, I know, but I am guessing it's a hard limitation on how the bosses are handled.Suggestions.It'd be nice if we get a ranking board in-game so we can see and compare our runs; with other players or ourselves. Just to flex who has the sickest fragfests.The hardest difficulty level gives you the most credits. By this point, you probably have no need for more credits. I would like it if we could use credits to buy weapons and skills then use them to customise our starting loadout (within the same limitations as vanilla loudouts) just so we can have the freedom of fragging with style or maybe as an assistance on General difficulty.Lastly, I wish I could choose to shut Margaret up. Yes, I know my character is being targeted and I have to step out of the fire. All that's available has been great but I want MORE.

_childDocuments_.review: A great tactics game, with its own identity compared with your typical fire emblems, and Final Fantasy tactics-es. This definitely has some huge potential. That's why it also disappointed me, when I first finished it and said "is that it". The game is criminally short, because the idea is, that you are supposed to play the same couple of stages over, and over again.Trying out different characters, weapon/skills build, and difficulty modes, in your typical rougelike fashion. I was first unsure if I should rate it positive, but ended up playing so much, that I realized that I was enjoying it quite a bit.  Still, I feel this was a lost opportunity to tell a proper story featuring the Metal Slug character and show off their world. Is it not supposed to be somewhat of a rpg, right? No interesting story, no voice-overs, and not that much variety in tactics as it should have been. I have played every single one of the original Metal Slug games since I was a kid, and there should be a LOT more of everything, if you are claiming to be making a rpg tactics game. The trailer said "110 hand-crafted maps" it definitely does not feel like it, maybe 40-50 at most, maybe the maps change at the highest difficulty, I haven't tried it yet. Maybe I just missed something. My final criticism is that all the bosses are all from the old games, there is literary nothing new, and the music, while defiantly passable, should have been much better than what we got, since the soundtrack from the old games is supremely amazing. I mean, how do you miss adding the mission complete music when you clear a stage, that is almost inexcusable, it is the most recognisable piece of music in all the Slug games. I am giving a lot of rough love to this one, by criticizing it as much as I am. Still despite my complaints, I am still giving it a solid thumps up, nothing is actually bad, it just should have been better. The game is still very fun, but I expected more, and the price is also fair. The game is worth 25 bucks, and definitely worth getting it on a sale if you are unsure, as long as you feel you enjoy turn based combat. I feel that a lot of the negative reviews are not completely fair to this one, but that is just me.

_childDocuments_.review: Even though I'm SNK fanboy I can say that this game is objectivly fun game. The most similar game to this is Into the Breach (also a great game), but after playing this game I think I can hardly go back to the Into the Breach. There are 3 main reasons:- Game forces you to move like a maniac. In other TBS games you want to take your ground slowly, to minimize the risk. In this game you will usually want to move as far as possible. Reason being that the further you move, the more armor you gain for that round (armor reduces the damage by flat number, and doesn't go down till the end of round. So if you have 4 armor, and are attacked by 100 enemies each dealing 4 or less damage, you wouldn't take any damage) and builds more adrenaline (used to cast special skills, think of mana). This chaotic movement really sets this game apart from other in this genre.- Sync attacks. So basically if your ally is in required space, he will also attack when your character attacks. (bad explanation, but just see some dude on yt for better one). Basically it is similar to the over-watch mechanic of xcom, but instead of it being defensively, it us used offensively. This is THE KEY for achieving absurd damage, which later becomes required. Also I find it way more fun to combo with my teammates, then with mountains/water- Skills. You will unlock some passive skills, some active skills, and some modifications to your weapons in every run. This is not unique to this game, but I think it is really well done here. The funny things is that you can make some completely broken combos, but I think those are fun and I think that game even encourages it.While I really liked Into the Breach, I think that with this game existence, Into the Breach is now obsolete. This game is not perfect, since there are some bugs (I only had visual so far, but some other users reported more serious ones), and the variety of bosses is not good (5 bosses in total, counting the secret boss).There are also other aspectes like comfy hub, charming victory animations and generally nice music. Worth noting is that one run will probably take somewhere between 2 and 5 hours.TLDR: If you like TBS or rouglikes this game is the must.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the hell out of the original coinmuncher back in the days of the 90s arcade, so I was a bit sceptical about this studio taking a classic arcadey action title and condensing it down into a roguelite grid-based strategy game along the lines of Enter the Breach or XCom, but I'm still really enjoying it! I do have a few gripes here and there, but they are pretty nit-picky.- I have been playing this for 24 hours now and I haven't seen one single RAWKIT LAWNCHAIR- The pixel art and animation is nowhere near as smooth and fluid as the original games, but those titles were INSANELY detailed in terms of pixel and sub-pixel work. What's here is perfectly acceptable and mimics the style of the originals very well.- It's not as gory. The original had all the horrors of war, as well as cartoonish zombies that made arcs of projectile blood vomit. However, I can understand why this one went a bit more PG to appeal to a wider audience!- There are still plenty of bugs. There have been several times where I've seen the visuals, sound and music glitch out, but nothing gamebreaking, yet.- The characters feel a bit 'waifu-ized'. They looked like a bunch of dorks in the original pixel art and part of me misses that, but I'd imagine the vast majority of players would prefer the massive tits (on both the men and women characters!)- The boss fights are cool, but might start to feel a bit stale, after a while. However, the game is constantly throwing new mini-bosses at you as part of optional objectives.- This is one of those games where each run seems to get easier as you progress. The hardest part is the early levels where you start out with very few abilities and can't do much damage. But by the end of each run, every character is extremely tanky and can take out entire squads of badguys with very little thought or planning. Maybe that's part of the fun though!Overall, the look and feel of Metal Slug has been captured brilliantly and applied to an extremely pick-up-and-play game style. Plus, there are tons of unlockables to keep things feeling fresh. Really loving this one and I look forward to playing more.

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't expecting *too* much from Metal Slug Tactics but I was very surprised by how much effort and love was put into it (I can't put the game down), and how they adapted the run-n-gun gameplay of Metal Slug into a tactics game. It had some bugs on release but they are actively fixing them (a patch just came out around a day ago from writing this). I think most important of all the bug where people lost their saves is fixed now (I never had that issue fortunately).I feel some people might misunderstand the mechanics; I find they have incredible strategic depth and are very fun. The game highly encourages , not turtling behind cover (you'll need to give up the habits you developed from playing games like XCom, lol). Move characters far and over as many gaps in the terrain as possible to acquire Dodge and Adrenaline to utilize more powerful moves to kill as many enemies as you can before they have their turn. You can also figure out the perfect setup to ensure  even if they are attacked by every enemy on the planet. Every turn feels like a puzzle you're trying to solve to figure out how to ; the satisfaction upon realizing the perfect synergy of your characters and moves doesn't get old.I also think the roguelite power progression and build-making is done very well and unlocks so many unique strategic options for your team composition. I can't tell you how many times I've found a new character ability or a weapon upgrade and went "OH that could be used for so many cool things". Also, there are 3 starting characters and 6 more unlockable ones with very different playstyles, each with 4 unique loadouts to choose from when beginning a run that change their weapons and starting abilities (loadouts are unlocked after you end your first run). Characters keep their weapons the whole run, but can upgrade/modify them as you progress.The upgrades are also very versatile. For example, Tarma starts with a knife in his default build that can only target 1 space adjacent to him but does high damage. I once acquired a mod that changes the targeting of his knife to attack 3 spaces in a straight line like a spear, rather than just 1. There are a lot of different attack pattern mods you can get like this. Another example is "Side Mirror" for handguns, which makes your character additionally shoot to their left and right after they shoot once with their handgun.There's so much more I could talk about, but that would require a more extensive review.Please give this game a try!

_childDocuments_.review: Metal Slug tactics is a game that feels like its undergone several major changes during development, trying to capture the essence of the franchise while functioning as a top down tactics and rogue-like. The game isn't bad, it's a bit confused, and personally I'm not a huge fan of the overall amalgamation. The game is built on three core concepts:-The first move you make in a turn determines a defensive stat that reduces damage, usually to 1-2 damage per enemy. Bonus movement does nothing for defense and only allows you to reposition for sync attacks or move out of range.  -Your squad of 3 will make a bonus sync attacks with their primary weapon when another squad member attacks an enemy thats also within their attack range.-You can buy from a random selection of upgrades after each boss and get drops via missions. If this sounds good to you, you'll probably enjoy the game. So why am I complaining:It's not what I was expecting and something feels off. The movement mechanics are supposed to represent the constant moving and dodging that occurs during the mainline games. That sounds great but it means you're running your group together in circles for sync attacks each turn and then eating enemy attacks for reduced or no damage (which looks kinda stupid). Once you get some items that generate additional actions this damage reduction mechanic falls off in favor of simply killing all the enemies that can reach you that turn. You also generally cant shoot or get shot up or down elevations creating odd situations where the enemy AI can do almost nothing (intentionally or otherwise). Bosses don't really have unique puzzles or requirements, they kinda all do the same 3 attacks (big aoe, multi small aoes, tracking aoe) and I see it as a gear/ammo check as you'll be worn down by adds if you don't just pump all your damage into them immediately. For a better word it feels a bit awkward to play as intended.Outside of clicking on the green squares your entire tactical focus until you reach better damage breakpoints and extra actions is setting up sync attacks. The game lets you undo moves and redo entire turns which you can abuse to figure out your optimal sync triggers for higher difficulties. It's less of a puzzle and more of a maths exercise as 99% of sync attacks are a single extra pistol shot for 2-3 damage that you want to use efficiently to finish off enemies. The game needs you to focus on this too much while a lot of tactical abilities struggle to be relevant outside of the ones that are just damage + bonus action. Into the Breach is a common comparison but that worked so well  for me because it feels like you're reacting and outplaying the opponents based on their broadcast moves and you have numerous very different options and debuff mechanics. MSTactics just doesnt have most of those options or gives them to you unreliably or towards the end of the run.Mission variety feels small and some carry high risk of ending your run with an instant loss condition (bad RNG on escort, destroy truck too early without enough DPS) while others are difficult to lose unless the run is going absolutely dreadfully (kill targets/survive). You'll often play the same missions over and over for the sake of certain rewards offered on that tile, but also because you'll want to avoid the more tedious missions. There's 3 missions before each boss, and up to 3 bosses before the final boss. There's always a pressing need to get upgrade drops and coins, with the alternatives being ammo drops and reinforcement rewards that are only relevant when the run isn't going so good. I think a branching pathway would have been far better (It's also a feature of the mainline series) with the story having some integration or actual structure. Having 4 loadouts per character is great and I like that teams can be kinda built or specialised. However there's a tiny pool of upgrades that persist between runs that form almost the entirety of the unlock progression system. It adds some new weapon upgrade options, shop rerolls and loadouts for squad members. Id have preferred to see these unlocks tied to gameplay exploits or removed entirely with how sparse they are. After you buy all the reroll charges and some character loadouts, thats basically everything done.

_childDocuments_.review: Metal Slug Tactics put a spin on the iconic franchise with a blend of turn-base tactics with rogue-lite elements. The pixel style is vibrant and charming, with humor sprinkled throughout the game. There is an epic spin put on the classic sounds and music.Lead a squad of three characters through grid maps, using tactics and positioning to pull off combos. The strategic elements are fun with several mission objectives types which offers a satisfying challenge. Each character has different weapons and special abilities. Unlock more permanent features, loadouts, and characters with each run. A great time for the tactics lovers.

_childDocuments_.review: Positives:Back to form: If I was given the choice of playing Metal Slug Awakening (a free but soulless cash grab) and Metal Slug Tactics (a paid but passionate work). The choice is obvious. It goes back to the old sprite based artwork, and it is beautiful to look at. The animations are well done and fluid. Even the Rebel soldiers got a makeover such as grenadiers carrying a backpack of grenades, Shield soldiers wearing a riot helmet and sporting shoulder armor and the elite (Black uniform/colored varieties) have a face mask similar to the Ptolemy army.A different take: Compared to the standard Run n Gun where the only part of your brain required is reflexes, memorisation, and luck. Here, it requires more brain power AND luck. Being a Tactical Roguelike, you need to stop and plan ahead and check your options. Take stock of both your unit's abilities and adrenaline system along with when is it worth a risky gamble to kill the enemy target or preserve your units' HP or go for the occasional POW that grants you bonus 5 coins and exp (may not sound like much but every bit helps). This mentality also applies on the stage select, do you go for extra exp, reinforcements tokens (The lives/Revives) or weapon mods. There is a lot to consider on how you tackle the challenges ahead of you.More fleshed out characterisations: Unless you read the bio, played Metal Slug 3D, that God awful mobile game (Metal Slug Attack and Defend) or KOF, you can only guess what each characters' personalities are. Completing achievements will unlock miniature dialouges where the characters interact with each other, like Tarma's distrust for Clark, Fio and Eri making a vow to not turn on each other if the whole team turns on itself. Idle animations while awaiting your deployment shows the team doing casual activities such as Fio playing the Run n Gun version of Metal Slug on the arcade or Ralf playing KOF on a game console (Guess they got time to play with themselves lol.) There are even some hints and dialogues that shows that despite finally getting it's act together, the Regular Army's top brass is STILL corrupt and Morden's Insurrection will always come back to haunt the heroes.Bosses got a redesign or expanded: In the old Run n Gun games, we never really got a good look at the bosses full appearances (unless you read the supplementary material). Now we have a good look at some of them no longer being obscured by limited hardware. I used to think the Aeshi Nero was a giant cat back in the day (cats are highly revered in Ancient Egypt, after all). It wasn't until Tactics that I see it I'm it's full form and thought; "IT'S A COBRA THIS WHOLE TIME?". The Dragon Nosuke is another example. We never really see how it travels when fighting on the train, though artwork shows it has train wheels. Tactics further expanded upon it by making it a spider tank like unit, allowing it to no longer be stuck to the tracks of the train.Cameos and references everywhere: There are cameos and references to past games like in Soursop jungle, you can see a Regular army soldier fishing and almost getting his face bitten off by the flying piranhas in MS3. Spotting them puts a big smile on my face as it leads to a "THERE IT IS!" moment.Negatives:Bugs, bugs everywhere: Given that this is the modern video game industry, it's bound to have bugs on release. These can range from characters still being able to use the mummy's abilities after being revived to the infamous Dragon Nosuke's hit box going off the rails requiring you to reset a turn to fix the issue or else it will crash the game. Achievements not triggering (such as Spy, Leaving the Army, and Commitment are the three primary bugged achievements that I've run into). Level events not triggering properly (Paqar's event didn't show up after completing the Argun desert mission where you take out the mosque artillery.) Using Alice sometimes causes a persisting high-pitched ringing sound that continues well after the run is completed. I do hope these issues are resolved soon.Lack of enemy variety: Aside from the Morden Rebel soldiers, you fight against Abul Abass' Middle Eastern Swordsmen (MS2/X), Egyptian mummies (MS2/X), Mutated Supersoldier experiments that only appear in the final mission (Mission 5 in MS2/X) and Soursop Jungle Tribes (MS5). Even the bosses are the same enemies you fight over and over, which leads to boredom and nothing interesting happening. I hope future updates/DLC adds the Martians, Venusian Invaders, giant mutated insects and wildlife, yetis, zombies along with the Amadeus Syndicate and the Ptolemy Army to fight against.Poor wording for achievements: One of the most frustrating things is the wording used for completing certain tasks and achievements. Most of them are seen to stem or be related to Clark Still's achievements. It either makes you think it's bugged or you're doing something wrong. ESPECIALLY if you want to go for 100% completion.Missing playable characters: As much as I hate the mobile games that are Metal Slug Attack and Defence, they did a good job with the Sprite work. Hence I wished they add Nathalie Neo, Roberto Nicola, Walter Ryan, Tyra Elson, Gimlet, Red Eye, Tequila and Hyakutaro Ichimonji (As playable units) and Rumi's sister, Madoka Aikawa (As an NPC) as either free updates or future DLC.(Personal opinion incoming) Subpar soundtrack and questionable sound design: The music feels rather.... Subdued, which is fine on its own but.... It lacks blood pumping energy like Assault when you fight Allen or a final attack when fighting Morden or Steel Beast when fighting the usual giant vehicle bosses. While it does fit the slower paced nature of a tactical RPG game, it feels like something is missing from it. The only tracks that give that blood pumping action is the menu screen and character select theme. Another thing I miss are the classic death sounds you hear when you kill enemy soldiers in Metal Slug 1-5 and 7 (6 and XX uses a different death sound which is good but not as iconic as the classic sounds). The CLOSEST we got are the mummies and mummified dogs when you kill them and they make a more updated version of their Run n Gun counterparts' death cries. The new playable characters death sounds are good and I will leave it as it is.Overall: I am VERY HAPPY that Metal Slug is back to its sprite based roots. Seeing the cast again is like revisiting an old friend. I just hope we get a classic Run n Gun Metal Slug 8 complete with all the current playable cast. I mean, if you need a classic Run n Gun to scratch your itch, I suggest checking out SuperBlinky's Metal Slug Fanthology. Metal Slug is like Megaman if you ask me, both their parent companies aren't doing jack with them and it's up to the fans to pick up the slack, and the fans are doing a FAR better job that whatever SNK Playmore or Capcom has been doing so far.Edit: Some bugs may have been fixed but there is still some cleaning up to do. Like Fixing the Spy Achievement.

_childDocuments_.review: Metal Slug Tactics is a fun game that does a great job at adapting it's source material in style and gameplay. It attempts to keep the rounds as run and gun as possible while still allowing for tactical strategy and honestly, it works really well. The game reminds me a little bit of Into the Breach with its rogue like elements and small fields with a slight puzzle element, but there's enough here to keep it's identity as a metal slug game rather than a straight up ripoff. this is probably the best tactical adaptation of a popular game in a different genera that i played since Metal Gear Acid 2 (yeah i said it!, Metal gear acid 2 kicks ASS!)Also i want to echo what another said in a different review; there's a disturbing lack of "ROCK-IT LAWN-CHAIR" but i'll live.It should be mentioned that as of this review (11/11/2024) there are glitches and issues that do cause some trouble, but it seems the devs have full intentions on fixing them so i will update this review when that time comes. im personally not one too be bothered too much by such things and still enjoyed my time so far with the game, but if that's something that bothers you you should take it into account.

_childDocuments_.review: It's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ difficult, and it's buggy on release, but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ the love put into this title is something else.If you're a fan of the Metal Slug Run and Gun franchise this title is full of pretty much every single bit of fan-service you could possibly ask for, as well as dedication to the evolving artstyle over the years. Did I mention it was difficult? Yeah I could barely squeak through a couple of runs on the easiest difficulty. That said, the gameplay is vastly different from games like 'into the breach' and evolves around keeping your characters moving as much as humanly possible and focusing down the bosses - much like the original game!Overall I think it's well worth the price given that Dotemu and Leikir are already working on the bugfixes and they have a proven track record of releasing polished titles. Long Live Metal Slug

_childDocuments_.review: A very unique rougelike turn based game that i haven't seen before.In short, the game rewards you for being extremely aggressive, pushing forward and shooting everyone. You will have to break the "bad habits" of hiding behind covers and just keep moving forward. The more you move, the more you can maximized your character potential in both offense and defense.The other main gimmick is synchronization, where any ally is in a line of sight, they will follow up with an attack. Tho be careful since there is friendly fire in this game, so positioning is key.In short, I think they did a splendid job combining both turn based and run and gun of one of my favorite series that hasn't got a new game in the past 15 years. (if you don't count the mobile games)
_childDocuments_.name: Metal Slug Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: It is a different type of tactical game. Its fun and the rougelite elements keep it interesting, but if you are going to have to unlearn some TRPG tropes (can't hit on different levels of height except with certain weapons, hitting from behind does nothing, always want to move if possible, and the use of cover is simplified). But once you get used to how this game works, nothing is better than pulling off a big multikill round using smart placements and synchronization attacks. As far as graphics, they are great if you are a fan of the Metal Slug series in general and the story is...theres no story really, that is not the focus as it has never been with Metal Slug.There are a few bugs, but they have already recognized they exist and are working on a fix, but they haven't really broken the game for me anyways so I'm in no rush.Its great fun but hard to describe, give it a try if you like solving puzzles and such.

_childDocuments_.review: Even with all the current bugs and glitches in the game I've been having a lot of fun with this game. The bugs are very bad don't get me wrong, I've had crashes, graphical errors and gameplay glitches, but runs are non-committal so it doesn't feel that bad, regardless it's still a mark against the game. It captures the feeling of running and gunning in metal slug with fun tactics gameplay. The game isn't too challenging to complete, most of the challenge comes from completing side objectives or refrain from using specific resources. I enjoy that pretty much any combination of characters can be used to complete a campaign, you'll find synergies everywhere and there's tons of room for experimentation. My favourite right now is a squad of deputy commanders and Leona who spawns copies, generating tons of synchro attacks.The music and pixel art is obviously gorgeous, nothing needs to be said there, the traditional hand drawn art is also very nice although more limited in quantity. Really, it's only the bugs on launch that are what I find disappointing about the game, and lack of zombies which I'm sure will be addressed in future updates. Despite those issues I'd still gladly recommend Metal Slug Tactics if you're a fan of the genre or want to dip your feet in.

_childDocuments_.review: Metal Slug Tactics, is a turn-based strategy game that reimagines the classic run-and-gun series in a tactical format. The game successfully blends the franchise's signature pixel art and fast-paced action with strategic depth.Pros:- Faithful Visuals and Sound: The game retains the iconic pixel art and energetic soundtrack of the original series, providing a nostalgic experience for longtime fans. - Engaging Tactical Gameplay: The transition to a turn-based format introduces strategic elements, such as character positioning and resource management, adding depth to the gameplay. - Diverse Character Abilities: Each character offers unique skills and weapons, encouraging varied team compositions and strategies. Cons:- Steep Learning Curve: New players may find the game's mechanics challenging to master, potentially leading to initial frustration. - Repetitive Mission Objectives: Some missions may feel repetitive over time, which could affect long-term engagement. - Limited Enemy Variety: The game features a limited range of enemy types, which may reduce the challenge and excitement in later stages. In conclusion, Metal Slug Tactics offers a refreshing take on the classic series, combining nostalgic elements with strategic gameplay. While it presents a learning curve and some repetitive aspects, it stands as a commendable addition to the franchise.Score: 9 out of 10 Metal Slugs—A strategic triumph that honors its roots while forging a new path.

_childDocuments_.review: A really fun spin on the old Metal Slug formula. The art and pixel art is absolutely gorgeous and really gives you that old Metal Slug feeling. Sound design is great, with familiar sound bytes that you've heard a million times when playing the old SNK games. Even Morden's evil laugh is back. The only thing it's missing is Allen Jr.'s "C'mon boy!", but maybe I just haven't run into it yet.I don't play too many rougelikes, but I've completed three runs so far and have unlocked some interesting weapons and abilities. There are a few characters left to unlock, but I'm having a lot of fun with Clark and Ralph. It's especially hilarious to have them use wrestling moves to toss enemies back and forth between each other to trigger a sync attack to get rid of that enemy.Gameplay wise, you are pressured to always be as mobile as possible, so planning out your moves and trying to set up sync attacks to get rid of enemies is really the name of the game. If enemies are near you, it's dangerous to try and camp unless you have certain abilities and adrenaline points stored up.The game isn't overly difficult,  but I've only played 2 runs on normal difficulty and 1 on the hard. I will be trying out max difficulty tonight. The main thing that cuts down the difficulty is that in later stages you can build some very powerful set ups and combinations.  Obviously it's a bit more difficult at the start of a run.I'm having a lot of fun with the game and would definitely recommend it to any tactical fan, and especially any Metal Slug fan.
_childDocuments_.name: Metal Slug Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, great tactics game that does a decent job of making runs feel variedPros:- The sync and adrenaline systems are absolutely fantastic and turn normally slow turn-based combat into a much faster paced game (completely changes the normal way of thinking of a tactics game, which I enjoyed something new)- Visuals look great- Upgrades and progressions felt good within a run - Great enemy variety- Works perfectly on steam deck (controls may take time to get used to).  - Can save and quit at any point making it easy to pick up for quick or long sessionsCons:- Just one nitpicky one, undoing moves can only be done in the order you took them which can reset your entire turn if you need to undo your first move.  Truly nothing terrible, just a minor annoyance.- Biome bosses are always the same from what I've seen so far, would be nice if there were variations.  Even if it's just after beating them the first time.Great game for any tactics fan!
_childDocuments_.name: Metal Slug Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: I'm writing this review pre-patch, as the day 1 experience has been a little buggy here and there. There are workarounds thankfully but it is unfortunate that they exist still. A few hiccups aside, those are my only gripes with the game so far. I very much enjoyed the demo and have been excited about this game for years now. I've always been a big fan of Metal Slug and a bigger fan of tactics games, so this itch being doubly scratched was wonderful. I love all the characters, the writing, the music, the art. It all oozes good ol' Metal Slug while having fresh new gameplay for the series from a genre I hold dear.I really am impressed with the end product and, after a patch or two for performance and bugs, I think this will genuinely be my GOTY. Can't wait to play more, and hope to see more for this game/franchise in the future!

_childDocuments_.review: Metal Slug X for the PS1 was a brilliant, arcadey action game with excellent gameplay and pixelart graphics. It's still one of my all time favourite classic action games. And it seems like Metal Slug Tactics has been adapted perfectly for another highly addictive genre: tactical turn-based strategy! So far the art is just as amazing as in the original Metal Slug series, challenge is spot on, and tactical gameplay offers near endless possibilities for different strategical approaches. If you've ever played Civilization-series, you know how addicting this kind turn based games can get. Highly recommended! +++++

_childDocuments_.review: Turn-based tactics with just enough originality to make it fresh and engaging.The importance placed on ensuring your characters are constantly moving sets it apart from some of the genres mainstays when caution reigns supreme.Co-ordinating your characters'  skills and abilities to ensure they compliment each other and synergize can be really rewarding.Super enjoying it so far.
_childDocuments_.name: Metal Slug Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: My experience with Metal Slug was mostly dying on the 1st stage but loving the pixel art - a painful lesson in how fast 50 cents can vanish. Strategy games are more my speed.I was surprised and delighted by how much this game shares with Into the Breach. I haven’t tried the harder difficulties yet since I wanted to unlock characters first, so it hasn't been challenging so far. I spend way more time planning turns than in ItB, though.There are combos that break the action economy wide open. Between Marco’s bonus actions and ADR generation, plus passives that add bonus actions/moves on kills, a well-built team can rampage across the map in a single turn. These combos are satisfying but lead to long, mentally taxing turns - probably why you get two turn resets here vs only one in ItB. It's a bit much to try to complete a run in a single sitting, so I've been taking breaks mid run.The adrenaline and cover/dodge mechanics are so, so smart. Credit to whoever came up with those. They make the game feel more run and gun and heavily incentivise you to be aggressive. A lot of tactics games encourage you to be super conservative which can make those games drag.Unfortunately, it's missing polish. Playing on Steam Deck, I’ve seen visual glitches and weirdness especially when resetting turns. Performance has been fine.Overall I really like it, but I’m unsure how long it’ll stay fresh. Higher difficulty adds enemies/encounters, but I’m not sure there will be enough variety especially when it comes to bosses. In ItB and FTL: Faster than Light, unlocks tied to the achievement system increased replay value. There's some of that here, but maybe not enough.For me, it’s an easy purchase - no regrets. Hopefully, they fix the technical issues but they would've noticed these in testing, so who knows.
