_childDocuments_.review: Metal Gear Tactics is a fun take on an amazing franchise.  The gameplay focuses on movement, aligning your team to attack enemies together, and using your environment to block enemy attacks.  The weapons, upgrades, and different classes are neat and offer a variety of gameplay styles. It's a little rough around the edges that I expect will get patched out (missing enemy tag descriptions for example).  I'd like to have the ability to completely clear areas or go to the shop between missions. Overall, great if you like Metal Gear and/or Tactics games!

_childDocuments_.review: Took a little bit for the game to click but it's a lot of fun when it does. Much faster paced tactical game than what I've been used to previously. Somewhere between Into the Breach and X-Com 2. Rogue-like elements with each game consisting a "run" with modifiers and boosts you can earn for each character
_childDocuments_.name: Metal Slug Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: Love Metal Slug. Love Run and Gun Games. This is the first tactics game I have played in a long time. Not too hard to pull your hair out in frustration but also not too easy that you end up falling asleep. This is the kind of the game that you cannot breeze through. You have to think. You need a game plan if you want to play defensively or aggressively. You also need to take into account character shortcomings and put them into your gameplans like Eri sucks being alone but she's better when grouped up for synchronized attacks. Marco is well balanced but is more effective in a group. etc, etc. once you click the "How to play [Character]" ine one of the menus in the barracks or in between stages, You'll slowly realize how you are meant to play the game.My only dislike for the game right now is how you lose your XP levels whenever you get a game over (all 3 members of your team is dead). I would like to keep what I got and earned during the stage so that I can come back stronger (and not just wiser too!) whenever I try again.Overall, this is a great game and a strange, yet welcome departure from Metal Slug's arcade roots as a Run and Gun game. I like to believe that this game will, hopefully, get more people unaware (or have forgotten of) Metal Slug to check out this fantastic franchise and hopefully get enough demand for SNK to go back to the Run and Gun Roots and make Metal Slug 8!And lastly, the one thing I miss having in this game is the voice calling out weapon names like HEAVY MACHINE GUN! ROCKET LAUNCHER! ENEMY CHASER! LASER GUN! and so much more. I hope that the devs can add this franchise staple later in the game's lifecycle as an option because I would like to always hear the name of the weapon I switch to. It ain't Metal Slug without it!
_childDocuments_.name: Metal Slug Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: + Sprites and animations are fun and look good+ Lots of variety in how you play with multiple characters who each have multiple starting loadouts+ VERY unique gameplay which highly encourages you to run around almost recklessly and set up combos while avoiding turtling defensively+ Solidly challenging but fair. The only RNG elements are reinforcing enemy spawns, map extensions, and boss attack patterns. + Character upgrades are frequent and satisfying and can significantly alter how a character plays, and what they do- Pretty buggy all across the board.    - Reset turns have deleted incoming delayed strikes and removed a character's movement, some keywords have broken descriptions, glitches with visual effects, etc.   - There is a semi-frequent stutter that lasts 7~ seconds that gets annoying. There is also an immense slowdown if there are too many enemies on screen.- Lack of content   - As is, there are 4 regions each with only one boss. Enemies seem to have a good variety however and higher difficulties have more enemy variants.    *Edit; there also appear to be miniboss quests after your first run, which is really nice.Some minor nitpicks: There are some clashes with the overall style like the character art cut-in for abilities and some fonts not being pixelated, the reused character art stands out with the codec calls (why does Ralf look like he wants to kill Margaret?) Overall a great addition to a starving genre. It scratches my itch for more advance wars.
_childDocuments_.name: Metal Slug Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: Metal Slug Tactics is actually a solid entry in the turn-based strategy genre. People who are surprised by Metal Slug incorporating both tactical RPG and roguelike elements probably didn't pay close enough attention to what the game is all about. However, don't expect these elements to define the game's genre—it’s still primarily a turn-based strategy game. So don’t be surprised to find something different from an action roguelike, a tactical RPG, or even the classic run-and-gun style of the original Metal Slug games, because that’s not what this game is. If you enjoy games like Into the Breach, you’ll likely have a great time with this one too. The game has its own mechanics, like using cover to block attacks and setting up combos, which work well and feel satisfying.
_childDocuments_.name: Metal Slug Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: You like Metal Slug's artstyle and all the visual details? You like turn based RGPs? Then I'd certainly recommend it. For the most part the game is solid. At first feels a bit basic, simple, but it certainly has some depth to it. And minus a couple of odd gameplay choices and maybe one mission type - seems to be be pretty solid! Interesting take on the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Metal Slug Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing! Instead of being a traditional tactics game, this game heavily prioritises movement of a small three person squad and combos performed by multiple characters attacking the same enemy all at once. Allied characters will almost always join an attack, even if they already performed actions during their turn, meaning that with only three characters on the field you can perform up to a dozen attacks per turn. This turns the game into something much closer to a puzzle game, where you have to figure out how to inflict as much damage.As well as being a very cleverly designed game, Metal Slug Tactics is an undeniable love letter to the Metal Slug universe, as well as Neo Geo and SNK in general. Pixel art is brimming with personality, numerous weapons from the original games are present and each character feels like a fully fleshed unique personality instead of simple sprite swaps. Bosses are as large as expected and landscapes are filled with details.I fell in love with this game almost instantly. Can't wait to dig into it deeper in the future to unlock all available options!
_childDocuments_.name: Metal Slug Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: Damn this was better than I expected. I like tactic style games and they really shook it up with the combo attacks and also bringing in the whole “move farther for damage nullification” to represent dodge.It feels a lot like chess when Im playing because of that. As I said i love games like these but most of the time even on harder difficulties you dont have to think too much about future turns. However since you are heavily incentivized to move, and having sync shots pop off is essential, its a lot more engaging.I do feel that its a bit easy right now, so far ive defeated one boss and am about to fight the next one. But I did see there is at least one higher difficulty so I hope theres a good amount of progression. Also I tried it for a bit on the steam deck. I dont think the text is too small. Seems to play fine but sometimes I notice some stutters when selecting whete to use different abilities. For example eri has a explosive jump that deals damage to both nearby and wherever you land units. If you move the cursor around and enemies are target/no longer targeted, theres a slight drop of frames. Not the biggest of deals but might as well mention.Ill probably update my review later, but after my first session I already put it in favorites.
_childDocuments_.name: Metal Slug Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: This game will find most of its value for nostalgia-driven fans. It's chock full of references and all the things we loved about the old games: the sound effects, music, humor, characters and more importantly, the difficulty.The game itself plays in a roguelike fashion with different kinds of missions that are quite short and simple, although not braindead easy in any way. You will find several props, like cranes you can sabotage, metal slugs and more during the maps that will aid you in completing the objective and side objectives; do so and you'll be rewarded with extra experience to level up your characters so you can choose extra skills, coins to spend in the base for permanent upgrades or assets to use in the current, ongoing campaign.The player can only choose and control 3 characters in their campaign, while the enemy will have more models in play with reinforcements coming every turn. so making use of all tools available to beeline to the objectives in the most efficient way and setting up sync attacks will be key to winning the tougher scenarios.I'm amazed that the game didn't garner as much attention the day of its release and almost launched silently, without making any waves. This is definitely a hidden little gem that I hope is the precursor to more Metal Slug games to come.
_childDocuments_.name: Metal Slug Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: Without a doubt the best pixel art of this style in the last decade.The game is already worth it even if I brought it just to look at the animation.However, that's not all, this is actually a very creative X-Com game with their own unique mechanic that I believe a lot of X-Com game should take note and implement in their future game. Because the mechanic is that unique. And very useful to stop player from "optimize the fun out of the game"-Making moving your character at max range and gain 'dodge HP' is a genius idea. It stop player from hugging cover that a lot of X-Com game kind of force player to do to avoid risk.
_childDocuments_.name: Metal Slug Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely in love with this game. Fun tac rpg, I enjoy the roguelike element, arts amazing and people finally remember Metal Slug. I will say the rogue like elements are definitely gonna be a turn off for some wanting a dedicated tac rpg from this. Plus some of the character unlock criteria is a bit rough but honestly it's all worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Metal Slug Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: This WAS not recommended, but after the latest patch I'm correcting it to a recommend.I actually really like this game. It feels a lot like a sequel to Into the Breach, except Metal Slug with a great emphasis on character movement and Disgaea-like combos, combined with fairly good pixel art and a decent soundtrack reminiscent of the classics.The developers seem to be on top of the debug game, while I wish more games would just release already in a fairly playable state, this is enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: Metal Slug Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: well the game is really nice. with the few hours i've played the game is quality. It's kind of rogue like in which- every operation you do (win or lose) will give you some money at the end to improve your characters either by getting new load-outs or upgrades you find along missions. "beating" the game doesn't yield you a true ending, apparently this is one of those where you should play multiple times if you wish to see the games real ending.---------------------------now an overall pros/cons deal---------------------------Pros-good dynamic gameplaygood music- BIG SHIE boss theme is amazinginteresting boss fights (each one differs in some way)leveling enemies (the longer you play the harder they get)Vehicles- while they are present they aren't relied on heavily, but when you do get them they are VERY strong.decent controls- my only issue with controls is when selecting a target there is no "intuitive" deselect attack button which when i first started did cause me to friendly fire a few times.. BUT this mechanic is useful in some situationsSmooth combat- the games focus is based on 2 things, moving *alot*, and your SYNC attacks, not to mention many abilities are strong. -------------------Cons-Some minor bugs with animations currently (nothing game breaking, just looks weird)if you don't try out other characters or load-out when they unlock, expect this to get repetitive doesn't seem like there's much mission variety unless you run special missions (rebel army marker).certain missions, especially early on, seem obscenely difficult compared to later missions (may have to do with the true ending i believe)actually that's it... overall a really great game for 25+$
_childDocuments_.name: Metal Slug Tactics

_childDocuments_.review:
Donald Morden is back! After a long time being hidden in a country opposed to the World Government, he patiently staged a coup d'etat and is finally ready to take revenge upon the World with the army he gathered throughout the years.

The Peregrine Falcons will have to do everything in their power to make it through the enemy lines and take down Morden before we get further into the war! 

METAL SLUG is back with a brand new entry in the METAL SLUG universe. Discover a new side of the emblematic run'n'gun and jump into a dynamic tactical RPG with roguelike elements!

Super fun and lighthearted, Metal Slug Tactics takes what makes METAL SLUG so special and unique and brings it to the tactical genre!

name: Forgive Me Father
detailed_description: Sequel available now in Early Access About the Game As the only one left with full senses, you embark on a journey in search of answers and relief in this FPS game that is created in a distinctive retro horror comic book style and feels as if it came straight out of Lovecraft's books. Be aware of your madness level which dynamically changes during gameplay and gives you additional power. Choose your active skills depending on your play style and use them to fight against the eternal evil. Explore this Lovecraft-inspired world that is full of hidden and hard to reach areas, and uncover the entire story to solve the mystery of this crazy place. Feeling of a classic FPS from the 90s Timelapse animations, opponents and elements of 2D in a 3D environment; first aid kits and life points, non-reloading weapons, powerups during dynamic combat with numerous opponents. Custom combat experience With scripture in one hand and weapons powered by an unknown substance in the other, the player will face the challenge of maintaining their humanity. It is up to the player to decide how their equipment evolves, and to find ways of defeating hordes of unpredictable opponents. Dynamic level of madness Directly influencing not only the audio-visual experience, but the gameplay itself, its effect varies depending on the current level of player’s madness. The gameplay is presented in a comic book style Hand-drawn graphics designed to maintain a distinctive comic book look, where any screenshot from the game could be a part of a new comic book. Mood straight from Lovecraft's dark novels All throughout the game, the player will feel the atmosphere of dread and horror that the works of H.P. Lovecraft are renowned for. Surrounded by the occult and forces of eternal evil, experience the feelings of hopelessness, madness and confusion, and the burning need to find answers and bring back some semblance of reason and sanity to the world. Many climatic levels and varied bestiary A diverse world entirely made by hand, full of interesting enemies ranging from possessed inhabitants to monsters straight out of your worst nightmares. Two heroes to choose from Each with their own, unique development tree. Experience the story from the perspective of either a priest or a journalist.

_childDocuments_.review: I guess it's good. The Journalist character is supposed to be the aggressive character but her abilities are kinda trash. The sword isn't good enough to out-heal the damage taken from getting into melee range, the camera's range is ridiculously short to the point of being useless. Voodoo doll's range is also equally short and therefore pointless. Her only decent ability is the cigarettes for the enemy slowdown effect. I wish I had picked Priest for my playthrough but oh well.
_childDocuments_.name: Forgive Me Father

_childDocuments_.review: I played through the game twice on Expert difficulty, Priest and Journalist.Pros: Guns and movement handle well (though the movement feels pretty floaty because of the speed you move at), most guns are fun to use and the skill tree offers a bit* of customization to your build as well as offering the chance to play around with different gun paths to see what you like best. The 3rd and last bossfights are fun and challenging.** The game looks amazing, the art-style has a "hand-made" feel and everything from the enemies to the environments to guns and even pickups look phenomenal. Enemy variety is large and every new world introduces about 3-5 new enemy types, all varied and none copy pasted, though some have similar ideas. Soundtrack slaps. The cutscenes look nice.Cons: I will address the *s I've marked in the Pros section. *: By "a bit" I really do mean "a bit". There isn't too much to change beyond some gun-changing upgrades and increasing stat values (HP, Ammo, skill stats, damage and fire rate increase). Barely any of the gun upgrades made me play any differently than I would've before. **: The other three bossfights were extremely easy to the point where I was surprised it took this little effort. I was wondering whether to put this next one on the "All that's in between" section but I feel it's way to egregious to be overlooked. The voice acting for the MCs was so extremely hit or miss for me. The large majority of one-liners and dialogue from both protagonists is either very cliché or just poorly written/poorly voiced. I remember a specific voiceline from the Priest I kept hearing, it was obviously meant to be a shout/warcry but the way it was voiced sounded like someone trying to feign constipation... I'm not sure if this was done on purpose but this and most other voicelines (save for probably less than 10% of them) are unbearable.All that's in between (Not necessarily issues but not pros either, decide for yourselves): Feels like a less special version of DOOM (2016). Yes, there are different abilities, weapon upgrades and a skill tree but the charm of the art-style and the setting doesn't carry over to the gameplay and for me that makes it feels a bit bland and repetitive, especially in the final stretch and even with all the new enemy types introduced. The story is also kind of a nothingburger 'all in le head' type of story that was expected but not so bad. I have a mid-range PC but had to go from Epic settings to Low on one of the last levels because it was so hardware intensive. I'm pretty sure there's no real use-cases for specific weapons over other. Enemies aren't specifically weak to specific weapons and I think that it could really add alot more depth to the game and make combat more interesting and engaging as well as giving more incentive for replays and NG+.Overall: It was a fun experience for the first few hours and turned a bit sour in the last stretch. Overall I give the game a personal overall rating of 5 out of 10 exploding barrels though I can still recommend it for boomer-shooter lovers.
_childDocuments_.name: Forgive Me Father

_childDocuments_.review: Forgive Me Father, but I have to give this one a negative review in its current state. This fact really saddens me because the Art and Music and overall gameplay are really cool .First let me say, I really like Retro-Shooters but I know that I'm not that good at them AND prefer to play with controller. This is the reason why I always choose the lowest difficulty setting in this kind of games. And here is where my main issue drops in: even on the very easy setting the game is sometimes ridiculously hard. The main reason for this seems to be the only thing that is adjusted by difficulty setting is the damage enemies deal, but not health drops, ammo pickups or enemy health. If you are in an arena, where tons of enemies spawn you also get screwed if the enemies deal less damage but your out of ammo and there are tens of them left to shoot you with homing projectiles and exploding stuff. Also some of the bosses are really hard in easy mode though, especially the second one where the moving walls deal way too much damage. There is a balancing patch upcoming that maybe fixes some of the problems. Another issue is the lack of controller support like auto aim etc. This should be standard for FPS that support controllers, because without them they are almost unplayable on higher difficulties and in the case of Forgive Me Father even on lowest difficulty setting, because for example Headshots are almost impossible but still necessary even on "Very Easy" to stand a chance in some situations.I really hope the devs adress this issues because then the game would be absolutely awesome.
_childDocuments_.name: Forgive Me Father

_childDocuments_.review: Forgive me Father up to this point is a well rounded game. If you enjoy what a classic Boomer Shooter has to offer you gonna have a great time with it.To go into further Detail lets break down a view things:Enemy AI:The enemy Ai is simple but functional every enemy has 1 simple Pattern he follows, which makes it really easy to learn. While there are some that feel simmilar to one another most of the time they have a twist two them. The basic Zombie for example sometimes holds a second Head, so if you Headshot them he just puts on the second head. It's small spins like this that really create fun highlight moments. As Feedback to the Developer: I think the Barrel Ai needs some sound or windup, it's the only part that was unreasonable frustrating to me while playing through, since it does to much dmg to quick.Level Design:The level design warries a lot which is good, it feels like the Developers put an emphisis on switching up styles of Gameplay. But I have to say if you are looking for a more Doom2016/Eternal Arena style this might not be for you. SkillTree:The Skill-Tree is wierd to me, while beeing a awesome add to the game it also feels just like that. To be fair thou, I haven't taken the time to really try out builts. For a player that plays through a the game once and then leaves it behind, it might just be a gimmick in the end. Which is sad since there is a lot of love in that thing.Spells:The spells are awesome but clunky. I feel like the whole cast time on the spells makes them really wierd to use. While they are amazing tools, it feels more like a pacebreaker. I think it has to do with how they are implement. While you have to press one button and they activate they usually take 1-3 Seconds to wind up. In thoes 3 Seconds as a player you just run arround. I think they should either be a switch two and then hold and click to cast, to make the player physicly feel what he's doing or be a quick VFX and then move on. Art:Just perfect. It oozes with style and feels fresh and unique while using oldschool 2D Sprites as enemies. In the end it feels fresh, while not forgetting where the Genre started.Sound:Sound Design is nice. Enemies are clearly communicated. Weapons feels nice and punchy. And diffrent movement sounds depending on the ground the player is on create a nice sense of location.Music:The music slaps. It can be nice and ambient or right in your face. The first time some metal track started in level 1 it instantly got me hooked. If there is something I forgot - It's not working against you so I think its good :D Keep up the good work! Looking forward to more.If anyone read through this this far thank you for your time! I hope you have a nice day.

_childDocuments_.review: Everything about this game is great: horror story and dark humour, action, monsters (tentacles), gore, fun weapons and their upgrades (sometimes mutations?),  RPG skill trees, imaginative boss fights, fresh visuals and metal music. There are no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ achievements like "beat the game on ultra hard permadeath difficulty" or "find all secrets in the whole effin game". Simply put Forgive Me Father is a perfect game!

_childDocuments_.review: A good boomer shooter busting at the seams with Lovecraftian vibes. It isnt much for content but the atmosphere if highly immersive and has 2 classes with different abilities, and a short but branching upgrade tree that changes how you play the game and adds a lot to its replay value. Worth the money.
_childDocuments_.name: Forgive Me Father

_childDocuments_.review: I received this game through the Humble Bundle monthly choice bundle. This game has an awesome atmosphere. Graphics work for what it is and look great. The sound effects are good as well. The music is just excellent and is really fitting from the atmospheric parts to the large battle heavy metal parts. Controller support is decent enough but this is definitely a PC game and I had to use my keyboard and mouse to get past some parts. The difficultly does ramp up pretty quickly as others have said and the boss fights range from pretty dang hard to extremely easy. The final boss is extremely easy and I was surprised by that considering the rest of the game. The special abilities are nice and the skill tree works as well. The game feels somewhat old school with some modern touches which is actually quite nice. Overall, I would recommend this game as it's presentation is great and it is a lot of fun.I am going to add to my review after giving this game a second play through. My first play through was with the priest who makes the game a bit easier because of the healing ability. The second play through was tougher with the journalist as her healing ability requires you to attack enemies with a sword. Overall, I enjoyed my second play through as much as the first and believe this is a excellent game and would like to see more games like this with such a good presentation.
_childDocuments_.name: Forgive Me Father

_childDocuments_.review: The best thing about this game is its music, which truly is awesome.Gameplaywise the game couldn't be more underwhelming: Imagine shooting cardboard cutouts with pea shooters that barely hit their mark. Or try to blow 'em up with a rocket launcher that shoots projectiles that move almost as fast as a turtle on valium.If you're looking for a good "boomer shooter" (as they call 'em these days) that uses 2D sprites instead of polygons for enemies, you should look somewhere else. CULTIC, SUPPLICE, ION FURY, PRODEUS just to name a few examples...Stay away from this one or wait at least until it's on sale...
_childDocuments_.name: Forgive Me Father

_childDocuments_.review: Out of the recent crop of retro FPS games, this is without a doubt the worst one I've played. Its not all bad.  The animations on your organic weaponry writhing in your hands is pretty cool. Some of the enemy designs are pretty cool. But the enemies don't have any sprites for looking at them from different directions, which makes them feel like paper cutouts. The 4-frame blood animation that plays when you damage them is huge, and actually makes it hard to tell when their dead. The sound effects on the weapons are also weak.There is some decent, mindless catharsis to be had here, but the ending soured me on this game so much it turned my rec from a maybe to a no. Now I didn't care about the story AT ALL for 99% of my playthrough. It's feels like it had one pass through google translate and is barely comprehensible. Your character's endless quips are also stilted, awkward and obnoxious. But right at the end, you drop the final boss and they hit you the lamest twist of all.  It's like the ending to an edgy fanfiction. Made the whole game stupider in retrospect.
_childDocuments_.name: Forgive Me Father

_childDocuments_.review: This game has everything that would make it awesome if they would finish it. The artstyle really got me, the whole theme is very cool. It seems to be a real loveletter to old-school shooters, even with it's Lovecraftian theme. The music is really great, all of the fight tracks are huge bangers. the gunplay is fun, shooting feels good, the sound design is pretty decent too. The idea of the skill tree was weird for me the first time, but I have grown to like it like I did with the special abilities. This could very well be one of my favourite FPS games, if some issues would be resolved. I understand that this is an early access game, but ther are several levels that felt almost incomplete. That is one thing, but the first levels, and some later ones were really linear and boring. The greatest issue with this game is with the levels. Some are too short, too mazelike, too simple, too plain, too narrow for the fights. There were ones that actually felt so bad that I think it should be completely redesigned from scratch. Otherwise, great game, I hope the developers will put much more effort into the level-design in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Forgive Me Father

_childDocuments_.review: I had a blast with this game. It's mostly just a good boomer shooter with a cool art style, but some of the boss fights feel like dark souls boss fights, with patterned attacks and different stages. Those bosses are hard as hell (on the highest difficulty. I didn't play any other difficulty so I can't speak on them). It's not a very long game, but I enjoyed it quite a bit and it's very reasonably priced
_childDocuments_.name: Forgive Me Father

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:-Fantastic gameplayThis game just feels good.  You can headshot most enemies, which is highly effective, though there are enemies who have clever work-arounds with it; such as a zombie that carries an extra head it puts on after you shoot off the first, or an armored enemy with exposed fuel tanks you can shoot to partially melt him.  There are also a lot of enemy varieties, which helps keep gameplay feeling fresh.  Even a guy who throws exploding fish!-Good level designLots of secrets, great looking environments, and many unique encounters make each moment enjoyable, and re-enjoyable.  A great example is an early map in the second episode, in a graveyard.  There are mostly low-tier zombie enemies, but lots of tall grass.  You can hear them, so you know they are present, but finding them before they get close takes effort, and you have to watch your back.-Solid weapons (all of which are useful)I find myself using every single weapon I've gotten so far.  Even the melee!  The starting pistol is weak but accurate and great for headshotting low-tier enemies to save ammo.  The only downside I'd have to say is some sound a bit weak, but not every gun can be the Super Shotgun from Doom 2.-A lot of levelsTwenty-five maps?  Feels like an old 90s shooter!  Loving the amount of levels.-Amazing Boss FightsI've faced two so far, and they break the stereotype of FPS games having lame or weak bosses.  These are masterclasses in good game design, IMO.-Great priceGame is a third the price of a AAA title and feels far more polished than one.Cons:-Some guns sound weakJust as it says.  I wish they had a bit more heft to their sound, though it's not a dealbreaker.-The Voice acting is badPerhaps they were going for old-school over the top, but it leaves a bit to be desired.  Fortunately, you can skip most of it save for the one-liners during gameplay which are tolerable.Neutral:-There's an upgrade system.Feels a bit out of place in an old-school FPS, but it's reasonably implemented, I suppose.  Even with the "get more XP" talents, leveling seems very slow.  I wouldn't say you even get one per level.-The story is just . . . there.Lots of "story" prompts around maps and beforehand exist.  I like Lovecraftian horror, but I've not been too interested in them.  It exists, is all I can really say about it.-There are two classes with recharging abilities.Another thing that seems more modern, there are two classes, one more based on offense and the other more defensive.  They have abilities that recharge as you kill enemies.  These powers are generally good and borderline essential on higher difficulties - I'd say they're well done.
_childDocuments_.name: Forgive Me Father

_childDocuments_.review: + Great comic book art style+ Varied range of weapons, including some really interesting 'alien' versions of standard weapons+ Super shotgun feels and sounds great, very satisfying+ Huge enemy variety + Good level design and mixing arena battles into it keeps things fresh (for the first half of the game)+ Great voice acting - Not enough experience points gained throughout the game to make full use of the skill tree - Irritating flying enemies that make the laser beam weapon basically mandatory to get - Boring boss fights (except Glitch)- Lazy and/or rushed levels in the last half of the game, mostly arena battles and annoying platforming- Poorly written dialogue, needs proofreading from a native English speaker More positives than negatives, so it gets a thumbs up from me... but it probably could've used another couple of months in development. Still a fun game.

_childDocuments_.review: This one came out of nowhere, I love this game. It reminds me kind of like Project Warlock in some ways, because it does have a leveling system, but I like this style more. Every time you finish a level they give you a new skill that you can use to help you in combat, and you can level it up, like being invincible for a short amount of time, or freezing enemies in place.The comic book art style is done well, and the satisfaction of killing zombies and monsters feels satisfying.

_childDocuments_.name: Forgive Me Father

_childDocuments_.review: All style, no substanceOut of all the so called  new Boomer Shooters that have come out in the last 10 years,  this one is one of the most overrated offerings I've played.  The visuals are solid but that's about it. The gunplay is atrocious. There isn't a single weapon in the game that feels like it has any impact. Everything feels like you're shooting cardboard because there's no knock back. The level design is barebones and enemy AI is nonexistent regardless of the difficulty settings. The games idea of ramping up the difficulty is nonsense fun house spawning.  The original vanilla Doom feels better to play than this.
_childDocuments_.name: Forgive Me Father

_childDocuments_.review: A shotgun enthusiasts wet dream. The sound design for the shotgun is *chefs kiss* superb. Fantastic visuals, tight controls (and forgiving hitboxes) with a heavy metal OST you'd come to expect from the genre. I really like how the weapons change visually as well to match their upgrade path, truly making them feel unique - and sometimes changing their function entirely. The upgrade system, and the lore/aesthetic are enough to set Forgive Me Father apart from the sea of retro/boomer shooters and make for an easy recommendation. 8/10 based on mechanic and visual design, 15/10 for shotgun cause based.
_childDocuments_.name: Forgive Me Father

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good boomer shooter, although it does get repetitive after a while. The music is good too, and the artstyle looks wonderful, but the gameplay never feels amazing. The weapons are cool, but the shotgun is ridiculously overpowered if you upgrade it a lot. Makes all other weapons sort of redundant by comparison. The levels aren't anything great either, but they get the job done. Not a bad little shooter.
_childDocuments_.name: Forgive Me Father

_childDocuments_.review: The first 3 acts have been great, but the further i get into it the more bullet spongey enemies get, and from the other reviews I've read I'm not the only one who feels this way. The art style and weapons are all great but some guns just lose all viability because they don't hit hard enough and fights are never "hard" they just take foreverUpdate: The last act is really, really not well done at all, it is just all the problems I previously mentioned turned up to 11. couldn't even bring myself to finish it
_childDocuments_.name: Forgive Me Father

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty solid boomer/twitch shooter.  At the start...  But late game...?Pros- Cool artwork.  The overall Lovecraftian theme is on point.  The comic book-y art style and animation takes some time to really acclimate to, but goes well w/ the theme.- Amazing music pieces.  Some set pieces just hit amazingly well.- RPG type system to level up and gain passives (can't farm, so there is a limit to exp).- 2 characters w/ different skills to change up the playstyle (each has its own save file tho).- Bosses have some interesting mechanics and I'd say are well-designed.- The fact you can only use a lamp/flashlight by itself w/o a weapon adds to the dread of the game, great for the theme and homage to Doom 3 (other games, too?).  However, I do feel you should at least have been able to hold the lamp/flashlight and pistol together.- Still better than Doom Eternal.Cons- Same monsters seem to get stronger (more HP) for some reason later in the game.  "Some reason" being rhetorical, of course.  I know why they're stronger - it's late game.  But the same trash mobs shouldn't just have more HP b/c it's later in the game.  It throws off ammo usage and overall balance.  I am not 100% certain of this, but it sure as heck felt that way.- Lots of cheap deaths.  Enemy swarms are cool and all, I love them.  But not when you can't see half the time due to low lighting or madness mechanic (again, I know by design.  But it's bad design).  - Plenty of enemies late game have "unreactable" projectiles.  See above about cheap deaths.  The game becomes a tactical shooter at times, just corner peaking to time projectile dodging.- Some gauntlets in the end game can't be treated like gauntlets?  A couple gauntlets in last stage that just...makes 0 sense in design sensibility - do i run&gun to the end or just slowly pace myself and waste all my ammo on the countless mobs?  These massive platforming challenges that have too many floating and moving and tanky enemies to take either approach realistically.- Art style leads to sometimes not knowing wtf is going on.  Enemies layered over other enemies (i.e. blocking your vision to see those already annoying projectiles), enemies blending in w/ the environment, not seeing gaps in the wall to progress, etc.  - Endgame area's save points become a burden to manage due to their sparsity and increased difficulty of encounters between them (autosaves appear to not really do anything, death = reload last save checkpoint).- Madness mechanic seems inconsistent, if not poorly implemented.  It seems to have random degrees of spiking.  Regardless if it's a 2-mob encounter in a hallway or a big arena full of a horde, the Madness increase doesn't seem to function consistently.  And there's no way to reduce it besides letting it cooldown.  Worst part is, while it is a buff, it makes the things hard to see (see above w/ already poor lighting in some areas).  A nice thematic fit, but...we should be able to reduce or control it somehow.   - BFG equivalent sucks.- Plasma Rifle equivalent sucks.- To summarize the above 2 points, the game doesn't seem to realize the risk/reward of projectile weapons vs hitscan.  Projectile weapons are not good for the most part in this game, save for the harpoon (still flawed fundamentally by having low range for being the defacto sniper) and the plasma rifle vs some monsters.  The damage is just too low.  WAY too low.  Some basic monsters take 2-3 BFG shots to kill...  And plasma rifle isn't TOO bad, but late game there are too many tanky, speedy, and flying enemies for it to be useful.  There is almost no point in using projectile guns mid-late game, except to snipe w/ the harpoon or to corner peak spam w/ the plasma rifle vs slow enemies.- But ALL guns have limited range.  Bullets, projectile or hitscan, just disappear after a certain, unreasonable distance. - Endgame platforming challenges (in the dark of all thing) are completely unnecessary and frustrating.- Despite bosses being well-designed, the execution on some are just terrible.  Looking at you,  boss.Overall, it's a good boomer/twitch shooter.  First couple acts are good.  Kinda gets frustrating towards the end.  I honestly do recommend it.  Just last act gets really cheap and frustrating and there's enough wrong w/ the game to warrant a thumbs down just to get more eyes on it.  I'd still recommend Dusk, Amid Evil (kinda), Hedon, etc over this for indie boomer/twitch shooters.  But if you love the genre, this is a definite must-play.

_childDocuments_.review: Forgive me Father is a FPS game like none other. It pits the player against hordes of eldritch monstrosities in a Lovecraftian/Edgar Alan Poe-inspired world, sending the nightmarish beasts into oblivion with the use of a ranged foray of upgradeable, yet strange and outlandish weapons.One of the game's most prominent features is it's presentation that blends pixel shaded 3d environments with unique, dark comic-like hand drawn artstyle of monsters and weapons which works surprisingly well and evokes a feeling of being plunged into a bygone era of the 1920s. The gameplay is fast paced and the endless hordes of monstrosities will keep you on your toes at all times with save point locations spread far and thin to test your grit. As mentioned, locations are three dimnentional and the enemies are hand drawn. Both come in a lot of varieties, from swamps, big city rooftops, decrepit asylums and foul stenching crypts. Each location is very detailed and sprinkled with tidbits of story trivia that we discover along the way. There are also Easter eggs aplenty for the keen eyed. It is also worth mentioning that although there are only a handful of enemy types, the developers took care to provide different sprites, depending on mission setting, so as we i.e. fight a squid soldier in the fields, thst same enemy type will look like nurse Rathlchett in the asylum levels which enforces immersion and is an attention to minute details that is worthy of mentioning. As the game progresses, dispatching monsters provides experience points that can be spent on upgrading weapons and abilities. There are also several artifacts the player will utilize to enhance  their game experience which are eflssentially buffs, but have been blended well into the story in the form of i.e. A cross to regain life points, an arcane book of knowledge that grants immunity to damage for a short while etc. All these elements, along with retro style vibes and a dark metal soundtrack blend well with the game's theme and provide for an exhilarating experience that will keep you in front of the computer screen for hours.

_childDocuments_.review: I did enjoy it to begin with but it soon became quite the boring game. Very empty after the first hour of playing...nothing special, worth it in a sale if you want something new to play but once you've played it through you won't be coming back. Only took it 3 hours to completely put me off even wanting to complete it...just felt like a complete waste of time.The thing with these wanna be boomer shooters is they just lack the intelligent design that was present in almost every FPS made in the 90's and early 00's. The level design in Forgive Me Father is bad...especially the open/larger levels. The enemy AI is OK but not great. And as always...carried by an unnecessary soundtrack that attempts to big up moments that really don't deserve it. Having this guy make a sound track for every boomer shooter is really getting boring...they all sound the same. There's just no point to anything. Original boomer shooters were new and offered an exciting/fresh experience. If you're gonna re-imagine that era then at least learn from the classics and build on what's already there. Every single one of these modern shooters have the same "I'm gonna rush you" AI and the "I'm gonna hide an enemy around the corner!" and for one level that's cool BUT this is all they have...for the entire game. The guns have no purpose or placement...there's a pistol 'cos you've got to have one. There's a shotgun...'cos you need a good shotgun. But when you're game is a lot worse than what came out 30 years ago well...you've missed the point. If you're just chucking things at your game 'cos every other game has them it's going to be really boring!!!Overall, nice visuals, nice sound, boring enemies, crappy guns and a pointless skill tree...oh, and invisible walls!! Just a complete lack of originality and creativity. The more I played the less I wanted to carry on...big shame. Just play Doom and Doom 2...play some free mods...they're all 1000% better than this and they're free!!5/10

_childDocuments_.review: First off, let's get to the positives: the game looks incredible. The artstyle and 2d animations are absolutely stunning, this is what darkest dungeon would look like if it was a shooter.the first two acts of the game are amazing. And then there's the rest of the game. I don't think I have ever seen a game fall off this hard. The level design in particular becomes atrocious. Do you like mazes? I don't. And no, I don't mean "the levels are maze like", I mean there are actual mazes in the game, tight corridors with 90 degrees turns filled with dead ends that you navigate via trial and error. Then the game alternates between sprawling nonsensical sequences of doors after doors after crammed corridors where every sense of exploration goes out the window to just... rooms with enemies. The first two acts had arenas too, but now, you just get small rooms with bullet sponges that you cannot headshot nor lure into barrels. so much of the later half is also fighting in pitch black darkness. And again, I mean this literally. you have to hold up your torch, see where the enemy is, and then shoot in that direction blindly. Again, the first two acts had this, but they handled it intelligently, with a level set in an open space (no risk of an instakill fall) and enemy eyes glowing in the dark, which is so good it tricks you into thinking the rest of the game will be good. It's like the second half was designed by completely different people.

_childDocuments_.review: Forgive Me Father is another in the recent boom in retro shooters, adding a slight spin with an eldritch horror theme and somewhat unique upgrade tree. I'm currently not done with what the early access offers, but an hour in and around 6 or so levels down, i've come to a decent enough point to make a decent enough review. Although not adding much new or innovative to the table, its a fun enough time if you're still on that retro FPS vibe.A couple of criticisms so far: The borders are not needed, its 2021, they don't add to the atmosphere or to the horror, they are just annoying. Music is awesome, but doesnt mix well with the theme this games going for. The best fitting music IMO, was in world 1: harbor, the slower paced twang of the guitar mixed with the faster background music really fit better than the metal/rock we've heard alot lately in the genre. Enemies could afford to be louder, the amount of times ive been hit from behind by a sneaking zombie is in the dozens for just an hour long play time so far. The madness meter turning everything black and white is fine, but atleast highlight enemies in red or something so you can actually see what your shooting at, happens mostly in dark sections, same goes for invulnerability mode, but its a little better with seemingly more emphasis on enemy outlines during that mode. Just a note, i tend to be more critical of games i enjoy, and only want to see them improve, especially in early access where changes are more acceptable. Im enjoying the game and look forward to more in the coming months, and will most likely stop here as to not get burnt out before full release. $15 is very fair, its not a broken or unplayable game, the foundation is here, but could use some work to be a better rounded experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Forgive me father is a fun oldschool fps that finds a nice balance between deliberate hand picked enemy placement and locking you into arenas until everything is dead. Levels are well designed with a classic find the coloured keys progression, but its a testament to the design that even without a map, I rarely, if ever got lost. The game starts out very slow paced compared to the average boomer shooter, with limited ammo, encouraging you to take the time to line up headshots, but as the game goes on it becomes more fast paced, and ammo more plentiful, but it still has a slower more deliberate feel when compared to its contemporaries. This isn't a bad thing mind you, it gives it its own style and personality.The story is your by the numbers Lovecraftian tale, but considering its not really been done for this kind of shooter, it feels like a very unique setting. (despite many games such as Quake having lovecraft inspired enemies and architecture, its not been this overtly set in a Lovecraftian setting). The levels play out in about 15 minutes which feels like the perfect length to both squeeze in a quick level during my lunch break, or spend a couple of hours "just one more level"-ing in the evening. The levels offer a great variety with each one having it's own theme and aesthetic. I was always excited to see what sort of location the next level took place in.Weapons are also really fun and can be upgraded to either improve them (improve damage and/or firerate) or completely change them (submachinegun can become a grenade launcher) which can add a nice bit of variety for future playthroughs. Speaking of which there are 2 characters to choose from who have different abilities, a priest with a self heal and other defensive abilities, and the journalist with more aggressive abilities. Another excuse to play the game again.Overall I highly recommend the game. I love the current popularity of oldschool shooters but many of them are arena focused (Doom Eternal, Serious Sam style), and as much as I love them, its nice to see a more oldschool level design (even with the odd arena battle thrown in).

_childDocuments_.review: Forgive Me Father is a “Punch out your throat and s h i t down your neck” simulator/Retraux First Person Shooter developed by Byte Barrel and published by Fulqrum (who's taken to publishing other FPS throwbacks like Hyperviolent and Dread Templar). The origins of this game are unknown, like most Lovecraftian creatures (for those not in the know, Lovecraft’s schtick is the unnameable horrors that when you see them, you go mad. Look him up, really fun stuff.) but what I am able to find on the origins of this game involve the actual animation stuff (which I’ll put in graphics and art direction later) so I’m kind of unsure at the moment. What I can tell you is that anyone who knows me, knows I’m a HUGE sucker for H.P. Lovecraft and his horror, the idea that anything can drive you mad just by looking at it to me is the most visceral form that one could really deal with. While I appreciate the ideas behind it, sometimes I just wanna shoot s h i t as well, and this game was advertised…somewhere and it somehow got my attention enough to wishlist the hell out of it. If I were to make a guess, I’d say it would be AlphaBetaGamer again, because they usually find the good stuff that makes me wanna snort it up my nose and into my veins to get my video game indie fix. I had gotten this game myself from a buddy of mine, Bad Ghosts (link down below) for my birthday I believe during Early Access and so I went about giving it a try before waiting to finish the final game around April of 2022? I had recently just gave it a shot again with a buddy of mine to wrap up the achievements for Halloween and this is my review.The graphics/Art direction for this game is astounding with its comic book inspired design along with the 2.5D perspective the actual gameplay takes place in. Most objects will do the thing where it rotates depending on the direction you look at it from while the actual environments in the background stay static where it is. I love it, but according to the developers it came with certain challenges like hand drawing the animations to fluidity (while lowering the amount of frames) and matching the lighting to fit the perspective while also keeping it 3D around the model (at least I think, I suck at Dev lingo sometimes). What I can say is by god, it’s amazing how many screenshots I could have and have taken in the time that I’ve played this game. The game looks beautiful from its artistic gothic streets all the way to the non-euclidianesque design of the final chapter. The lighting and color scheme of everything is different and varied from bright purple to murky light blue to even going black and white during the final boss. Speaking of, the creature and boss designs in the actual game itself (especially the Liquidators oooooh boy they look phenomenal) are freaky and intimidating and I love it. I love everything about this, they pulled these designs either straight from Lovecraft or mixed and matched their own vibes and while it’s ominous, with you and your weapons in your hand you it reeks of a good action horror experience. Speaking of the weapons, going to gameplay next but I’ll say that the weapon animations are also great for what they’re working with and the extra flair of the upgrades once you buy them add a sort of different aesthetic design that while is over the top and extra, doesn’t feel out of place for this game’s world. You’ll find your fair share of easter eggs out in the wild as well from references to The Shining, to Witcher 3: Wild Hunt, amongst others that you’ll experience. To finish off with audio stuff, The voice acting is pretty decent, you’ll only really hear voice lines from the Preacher and Journalist as well as the narrator and everyone does a solid job for the most part in the delivery of their lines. The environment sounds are amazing (the guns especially) and the soundtrack consists of banging metal riffs that get the job done in making you feel hyped.The gameplay for the most part is simple fare: it’s a first person shooter. You’ll get guns that range from pistols, to Tommy Guns to Shotguns to whatever while ripping and tearing through enemies and collecting different colored keys for different colored doors. HOWEVER, it does SOME things that are different: mostly this has to do with the upgrade system as well as the two different characters in relation to their classes. As said before, you can upgrade your weapons in different ways that have different abilities (like having the Tommy Gun turn into a straight up laser cannon if I remember correctly as an example) and it allows for different variations and class choices in your run through the game. Either way, the weapons feel punchy as hell and amazing; so it doesn’t feel JUST like you're shooting a pea shooter even if it’s a weak weapon. The game also gives you reset skills as well after each act if you ever want to reset some of these skill trees to something different. You can also choose between the Priest and the Journalist, both of whom apparently have different skills according to the game? I can’t tell you about the Journalist except some guides say that she’s more of a crowd control person, I didn’t notice as my buddy played through it on Very Easy with cheats on for New Game Plus (which there is one if you want to play again with stuff unlocked) so I’ll post a guide but what I can say is that for the most part I didn’t really use the abilities? Half the time I even forgot what they did, but then again I played as the Priest like a year or two ago so I’m not too surprised in the slightest to be honest. The only other thing I can mention is that while I got confused sometimes, most of the levels were intuitive while the bosses can be a difficult HELL to get through and all require different strategies (I’m talking to you King in Yellow, and “Big Ugly Fish” you f u c kers) but feel satisfying to get through once it’s done.The story is a simple one, either as the Priest or the Journalist you  That’s the most part of the story I could catch, there are documents scattered around that give flavor text but other than some references and vague stuff you don’t get much to go on. Between the boss battles you find  Who knows but the ending fits the Lovecraftian tropes and I’m all for it and even though it's minimalist it does a good job conveying atmosphere.So what’s the verdict? Do you need a small four to five hour retro FPS game to shoot s h i t for Halloween? My answer is yes, the game is worth your time and your money, if you want to get it on sale then that would probably be smart? My 10 ½ hours or so came from time in Early Access as well as my playthroughs with it but If I didn’t get it for my birthday, I would’ve gotten it on sale most likely. Either way, it’s a solid fun time and it’s sequel just got released on Early Access either today or yesterday so I’m a bit late but yeah, play the game it’s good!Links:

_childDocuments_.review: Forgive Me Father is a highly enjoyable retro fps with some RPG elements tacked onto it. For the story, it's a very run-of-the-mill Lovecraft feature; probably the most polished attempt at the niche genre itself which doesn't say much. The art style reminds me of Darkest Dungeon with the enemies and the protagonist's very gritty and dark designs. Weapons sound great aside from the explosive weapons that tend to fall flat for me. Level Designs are fantastic whether running across rooftops of derelict buildings or diving into a deep-sea temple forgotten by time. The difficulty was set to hard for me, and I can say it got hard going into the fourth and fifth acts, but they have easy, so if you're more into the story, feel free to try on those. I give Forgive Me Father a 7 out of 10

_childDocuments_.review: Forgive Me Father is a decent retro FPS. It wears its inspirations on its sleeves proudly and should, but it's a bit rough around the edges.FMF is set in rural Massachusetts in the 1920s- the classic backdrop of many stories of H.P. Lovecraft. As in other titles inspired by the Cthulhu Mythos like Lovecraft's Untold Stories, Tesla Force and Darkest Dungeon, death and madness already reign and the protagonists' only way out is through.You can play the available 13 levels in this Early Access build as a Priest character, who is to eventually be joined by a Journalist. FMF has an experience and level system with branching upgrade paths, and the two characters are to have separate trees in the release build.FMF features a familiar array of weapons so far- knife, pistol, double-barreled shotgun, two flavors of submachinegun including the ubiquitious Tommy Gun, a precision harpoon launcher and one that is quite a bit stranger in appearance but not so in function.The game has varied locales if not the most creative level design- city streets, gardens, docks, a hospital, graveyards and catacombs, caverns, ruins, swamps, forests, cornfields and likely more to come. The cornfield level in particular had a more interesting layout then most and I think is indication that the game is maturing over the course of its development.I mentioned some roughness. FMF's aiming is a bit jerky, enemy attacks can be difficult to avoid given the prevalence of toe traps and obstacles, and most of all, the game's lighting is... difficult to appreciate. While stark contrasts between black shadows and brightlights CAN be interesting, FMF's light sources are absolutely eye-stabbingly glaring and the effect is more painful next to the very deep shadows. To wit, the last retro FPS I played before FMF, Severed Steel, has very bright visuals throughout but consistently so, and not at all difficult to adjust to. FMF's lightning varies drastically and its just hard to look at.While not on par with games like DUSK, HROT or Project Warlock, FMF is far from mediocre. It just has a long way to go.

_childDocuments_.review: Fast paced, fun, and super challenging. Like the latest Doom games, player is required to move and shoot all the time facing the monstrous creatures, and always stay focused, otherwise  ammo could go short fast and one mistake may lead to an easy game over even for a veteran player (yeah by veteran I mean me lol).Before I clicked New Game I went to the setting, saw the default difficulty was "Easy" (5 in total) and I thought it was an insult (lol). I begin the game in Normal difficulty and it fit for the first 20 mins, until 20 mins later monsters start to come in waves and surprising corners. After dying at the same place a couple of times I compromise to Easy. Then at last, after 1.5 hours I start thinking: would it hurt my pride to be Very Easy? Thanks to the devs allowing player to adjust difficulty at any time. Just keep in mind this game is more like made for hardcore player who loves challenges and can't wait to polish and test their skills. If not for my lack of proficiency I'd finish the game, during my 3 hours of gameplay it is satisfying, yet a shame I stopped half way knowing I wasn't looking for a hard one, but the game is decent and fun.I am not that into horror games, but can't say no to a surreal, dark and full of mysteries world setting. The first impression is gore, blood covers the screen and when losing too much health everything turns b/w except the scarlet blood. It certainly adds a lot of panic, besides the monsters are really well built, not only vary in skins, rather, devs put good effort making each a good style and an unique way of attacking, which constantly brings new excitement, good work! As for the weapons, some are given directly but others are hidden for curious and careful players willing to explore the map, well worth the time to find the secrets (The slaughterhouse, corn maze are my favorites, with secrets like walking on the wires to get to the second floor, a mill wing can take player to the roof are both well made), though occasionally I am unsure where to go - adding a mini map would be favored.Character movement is smooth, shooting feels good and the map ranges from simple to complicated, player can jump and use special skills to hit or regenerate. Boss battle at the end of each level is exciting, and again, challenging. The only thing that might be improved is probably the story pieces, but it is a minor problem for most old-school FPS games. I'd put this game with Doom, Turbo Overkill, HROT, DUSK etc., love to pick it up again sometime later.I'd love to have a physical copy of the game, and imagine it would be more fun to play with friends. If any dev actually read this review - Would you Please consider making a Super Easy difficulty for 5 years old so I could probably beat it in the future? LOL. Good work, I recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: ---{Grind}---☐ Nothing to grind☐ Only if u care about leader-boards☑ Isn't necessary to progress☐ Average grind level☐ You‘ll need a second live for grinding---{Story}---☐ No Story☐ Text or Audio floating around☑ Average☐ Good☐ It‘ll replace your life---{Game Time}---☐ Long enough for a cup of coffee☐ Short☑ Average☐ Long☐ To infinity and beyond---{Price}---☐ It’s free!☑ Worth the price☐ Get it on sale☐ Not recommended☐ You could also just burn your money---{Bugs}---☑ Never heard of☐ Minor bugs☐ Can get annoying☐ Game-breaking bugs☐ The game itself is a big terrarium for bugsForgive me Father is a first-person-shooter with horror elements (lovecraft) where you clear 12 levels and a few boss fights. There are two playable characters (each with a few different skills) along with a variety of weaponry/upgrades for the player to choose from but you do end up unlocking all the good ones by the last few levels which reduces replay-ability.Monster variety is decent and the soundtrack is solid. Game-play is fast and weapons are satisfying to use. Items are very powerful but kept in check with cooldowns.The weakest aspects of the game are map design, graphics and the saving system. While most maps are fairly linear, certain maps are designed poorly and often involve back-tracking which can confuse the player having them running in circles. The graphics while decent, could have been better (enemy corpses are two dimensional like paper dolls). The saving system is like a souls game where you find an npc at various parts of the game and interact with them to save. They do appear fairly frequently so it is a minor annoyance at best.

_childDocuments_.review: To this day, I don't know how Forgive Me Father avoided my notice for so long. The weapons bite hard and feel fun to use, and the enemies put up a real challenge before exploding spectacularly and colorfully. The music has you feeling powerful and motivated (and doubles as good workout music).The pacing feels a bit rushed, like we're being ushered along too quickly to make sure we take in ALL the sights, and the story exposition is just a BIT too spaced-out and brief to feel truly coherent. The voice acting is also..... patchy, to say the least.But that's not why we're here. We're here to lay low abominations and Great Old Ones, and this game makes it fun. Fish and Tear!

_childDocuments_.review: Forgive me father is a so-called “boomer-shooter”, which means it is inspired by titles like doom, quake or blood. The setting is based on a lovecraftian lore - not very original these days, but welcome nonetheless.The thing that distinguished the game from the titles mentioned above are mostly visuals and the existence of weapon upgrades. Quite an original idea - add 2D models in the 3D world. Stylish!There are 2 main protagonists to choose from, with different sets of combat abilities, like a temporary rage mod, or a camera that freezes enemies in place. The abilities and weapons can be upgraded after acquiring experience from killing enemies.The main problem of the game is the gameplay. It is not very smooth, the game runs unexpectedly bad for how it looks. I expected more encounters with hordes of enemies, but the majority of time it’s just you and several enemies in a small room. Probably the devs just couldn’t have optimized the engine to be able to support so many enemies presented at one time.*For the record, I've completed the game as a journalist, on a hard difficulty.The level design is too plain, there are almost no memorable areas. You mostly encounter single enemies or little groups of ‘em. Also, some enemies are very annoying to fight. It’s not a skill issue, there's no challenge in that.And the voice acting, oh boy. In fact, the sound design as a whole is pretty bad.I mean, the game isn’t terrible, it’s just that there are a ton of better alternatives. It’s not as dynamic and fun as painkiller or serious sam. The level design is not even close to original DOOMs.Forgive me, father, but I cannot recommend the game. I hope the devs take into account all of the weak points and make the sequel a better experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not done with the game yet, but I am really enjoying it. I just want to write this review because there are some things that really stand out to me.This game is clearly not made by a native english staff. That's not a bad thing; but the english translation is... clunky. It's not ever really  (except for a time they spelled "peace" as "piece", but I will address that later...), just not written or delivered in a way that ever feels natural. If that's what the writers were going for, that's fine; artistic license and all that. But the lack of contractions - like "it's" - is kind of jarring. I am playing as the priest, so the journalist may be a different experience, but I have no real reason to believe so. If the actor isn't american, his accent is great, but his delivery gives it away. Unless the clunk was truly intended, any (good) native actor would have pointed this out and asked if they should make it feel more natural. The voice acting, otherwise, is serviceable.There are often lines that I'm not sure whether they're meant to be played straight or are meant as a joke. The game's tone is deadly serious (which is fine), but some lines peek in and make me wonder "was this meant to be funny?" The delivery is often stone cold, but the lines are written in ways that could be interpreted as purposefully humorous - without any indication they're meant to be. For example, the "peace" line earlier was part of "Rest in piece." Was this meant to be "rest in pieces?" If so, that's a pretty big error to make, as the pronunciation is identical (it's a homophone). Another line which could be construed as potentially humorous is "Knowing is half the battle." It was delivered seriously, and without any real context. Was this meant to be humorous or serious? To American audiences, this is a rather absurd line to have in the game- a reference to the war on drugs is kind of weird.I really hope the devs read this, as these issues could be (hopefully easily) addressed and make the experience significantly better. Other than that, the game is great!

_childDocuments_.review: The slightly more expanded version of the mini review on . With the current state of the game being in Early Access, must say, overall it's been a fairly solid experience. Good music (at this point it feels to be a common thing for these games), consistent action. The skill points and abilities add some variety to the traditional/old-school shooter experience. Graphics are appealing and a combination of 2d and 3d experience certainly play along nicely. Levels, for the most part, combine that old and newer style of design. What with you having to go through labyrinths as well as more complex moments now and then. The weapons, while mostly 'standard' for this genre, feel pretty nice (even if the accuracy can feel a bit 'wat' now and then. Bite me.) Out of downsides, so far can probably point out that the "surprise enemy wave rooms" get a little bit too repetitive at the times. Making you want to have an extra mini-boss of some kind instead. And of course, with it being an Early Access the bugs and unstable moments can happen, for example - in the cemetery level, when you walk into the small house to pick some ammo right before another action segment. The music kind of just cuts out. Or a couple of times, I managed to get stuck in a wall. But those are minor issues that don't ruin the experience! All in all - I'd say its worth looking into if you're a fan of old-school shooters or simply have a bit of that "craving" all of a sudden.

_childDocuments_.review: Forgive Me Father is probably my favorite "boomer shooter" of this year (so far) over Prodeus, Metal: Hellsinger, Shadow Warrior 3, and Turbo Overkill (still in EA). It has issues for sure which I'll go over, but it's provided nearly everything I look for in this type of game. Pros:-Mazelike level design with a plethora of secrets-High difficulty-Very challenging boss fights-Unique aesthetic mix of Lovecraft and graphic novels-Impactful gunplay-Great weapon variety with branching customization options that visually alter the weapons-HEAVY soundtrack and punchy audio mix-Two playable characters with their own unique features-Sanity system (Rewarding constant aggression in combat with increased damage)Cons:-Voice acting is very wooden-Act 3 boss fight has some awful platforming-Random performance dips (this has been addressed recently)-World 5 is genuinely awful. Way too many encounters and overlong levels.I don't have a lot of complaints. It's definitely a high recommendation to fans of Blood. I'd give it a 9/10.EDIT: This game is harder than Chinese algebra. World 4 onward is BRUTAL.

_childDocuments_.review: 9.5/10Forgive Me Father is a combination of Doom and classic LucasArts games, especially Outlaws (1997), with a Lovecraftian theme. _childDocuments_.review: This is a fun little game that has a great art style and enjoyable fluid game play. It's a classic fps in the style of doom with a lovecraftian setting and period and setting appropriate enemies and armaments. The devs did a great job with the art direction and really convey that setting through it. It also has a hint of sort of pulpy comics/fiction as well with nods to Mike Mignola's work in a lot of the presentation. The action is simple and smooth with appropriately punchy guns and effects that help you feel their impact. Combat is typical for this genre: very fast and rewards constant movement, situational awarness, and precision. It's well done and I definitely recommend it on both these point. Unfortunately I had to refund it due to a larger main issue that was also helped along by a minor one. The most significant being that it was starting to cause noticeable motion sickness for me over time which often makes games unplayable for me personally despite their good qualities. So if if motion sickness is an issue for you be aware that it might be a problem. The second minor issue that honestly on it's own I'd probably have just ignored is that the writing and voice acting for the characters is pretty rough. For both the Priest and Journalist the line delivery is stiff and often gives the impression of something that's been inexpertly translated. It's not the worst I've ever heard and you can always turn off the voice lines in the options, but they can be a bit jarring and as an aspect of the setting which is a big selling point of the game they let the production down just a bit. On their own not enough to be a dealbreaker at all especially for the price of the game, but definitely a rough spot in an otherwise very polished production. If it weren't for the motion sickness issue I'd probably still be playing.So overall I'd say check it out as long as motion sickness isn't a big issue for you. It's a cool little indie title that I wish i'd gotten to play more of. It's especially worth it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Forgive Me Father

_childDocuments_.review: Forgive Me Father is a cool retro fps that might benefit from a bit more design iteration.Essentially, it's a fast-paced high damage precision shooter in cluttered environments. Enemy projectiles rip out at one billion miles per hour, it's easy to get jammed on pieces of the environment, and everything hits like a truck. HP recovery is pickup-based, and feels scant, and theoretically you have some tools for recovering it (a chargeable special melee mode,) but these tools are cumbersome and unreliable.All of this rewards careful play. Peeking corners. Mentally counting down to when enemies are likely to fire so that you can pre-dodge, which gives you a hope of avoiding their shots. Conserving ammunition and aiming for weaknesses.But Forgive Me Father desperately does not want you to do that. It's forever dumping you into cramped, cluttered arenas and blaring rock music at you while you face tank a dozen light-speed projectiles at once.I think if the game leaned further in either design direction, it would be on more solid footing.Slower, more precise, more rpg elements, great.Faster, more open arenas, recover health from gun kills, great.As is, splitting the difference sort of tears up some of the playability too.I'll play a bit more in hopes that I'm wrong, but otherwise I'd check this out if you want to try something a little different and you don't mind hitting a frustration wall at the end of act II.Edit: Yeah, nah. I tried giving it a second shot to see if maybe the other character had a better play experience, and no.

_childDocuments_.review: I can believe not everybody can enjoy this game, but for those who enjoy atmospheric shooter games, this is really worth giving it a "shot". The game can be challenging at times, but you can always adjust the difficulty at any time and even activate a bit of an aim bot.The weapons, the monsters and the story are not extraordinary. But the true strength of Forgive me Father lays in it's dark atmosphere accomplished by the awesome soundtracks and a quite unique art style. Extra bonus points for the level creator(s) who managed to design original settings that I had not seen before.
