_childDocuments_.review: Duke 3D/Quake/Doom throwback shooters are currently a hot trend, and frankly this is a pretty mediocre outing compared to it's peers. For context, I played up until the sewer section in the third chapter on hard.The Good: The unique art-style is pretty charming and some of the levels, particularly the early ones taking place in the town are pretty nice to look at. Enemies take extra damage for headshots which means even the pistols stay relevant later on in the game as they can mean huge damage in exchange for spending "cheap" ammo. The shotgun is great for the genre in both sound and functionality. The upgrade system is a little flawed in execution, but an interesting idea and upgrading the weapons provides enormous, noticeable benefits. Upgrading the pistols, shotgun, sten, and tommy gun were very rewarding choices, if a bit limited.Negatives: Incredibly frustrating "gotcha!" level design, combined with poor visibility, combined with non-existent sound cues for some attacks, combined with awful bloom on every single light source, combined with the genuinely awful "madness" screen discoloration makes this game painful to try and look at sometimes and even more frustrating to follow along with. It's incredibly difficult to tell why you didn't hit something with finicky hitboxes on enemies, but your character will take damage from anything within 6 feet of you. You know how in Quake you can hear the grenades bounce on the ground? In Doom you can hear the fireballs from the imps fly by? That does not exist here. The gas mask enemies will blow your ears out, but little did you know there are 3 fisherman far above you, blending in with the walls, throwing grenades quietly atop your head. Visually and audibly, the game is kind of a mess. The voice acting for the female character is atrocious, and expect to hear the same 5 lines for your entire playthrough.The ability and madness system, what should be game-changers for the larger firefights, are straight up liabilities. First off, go to the options and turn off that awful, abysmal black and white setting for high madness. It's already hard enough to see what you're doing, the fact they're trying to somehow artificially make it harder is insane to me. Dealing damage raises your madness, worsening your vision but making you take less damage and giving you access to abilities. Here's the kicker though: Every single ability is near-useless. You will get some mileage out of the bullet-time slow-mo and maybe the AOE damage voodoo doll, but the sword that dampens incoming damage relies entirely on melee combat: something incredibly janky and inconsistent in this game. Melee hitboxes are one pixel big so pray you're the perfect distance and aiming at the perfect angle while running around at high speeds. The camera ability stuns enemies who are point blank with you and you have to be aiming at them for it to work. Know what kills enemies point blank instead of stunning them? The shotgun, the harpoon gun, the tommy gun, etc. Why even bother stunning anyone? Enemies die so fast, and the range on the move is so short that it ends up being redundant. I don't even really notice the damage reduction from going insane, at least on the hard difficulty. The whole game is just frustrating for me. It has it's heart in the right place, and there's almost something really cool here, but man every gunfight feels like I'm bleeding ammo and can't find anymore, praying that some enemy who's attack cues aren't loud or distinct enough doesn't teleport behind me and one shot me. I'm not staying mobile to dodge projectiles, I'm staying mobile because who knows what I can't hear or see. So close yet so far to being solid.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun little retro FPS. Nice variety of interesting weapons and abilities that you can upgrade at your discretion in a small skill web with experience gained from kills. Overall length is comparable to most retro FPS games and IMO is neither too short nor too long; it tells the story that it wants to without dragging on too long.Great game overall, would certainly recommend if you enjoy retro FPS games.

_childDocuments_.review: i'm honestly confused by most of these negative reviews. i'm guessing they haven't been updated since pre-release. i've played through the game 3 times now and haven't had any hit box issues. or any of the other issues that i've seen listed. i think people might just be misunderstanding some of the more unique weak spots. which is definitely a thing. you don't want to just go around holding down the trigger in this game.- there are a (very) few platforming areas. most are not hard, but in the last level there are two that require a lot of patience. overall they're not that bad on contiguous playthroughs. - i'm very pleased with the amount of skill the game demands of you. it is definitely it's own game though. so don't expect DOOM 2016, or assume anything really, and you'll have a great time. :)- the boss fights are incredible. it requires you to be mindful of everything that's going on during the fight. which i love. MMO players will feel right at home with the mechanics.- this is a refreshing take on the "standard" FPS. i hope the devs stick to their guns with the difficulty and playstyle. because it's great.- art is phenomenal. as well as the sound and enemy design (there are twists on some classic enemies that really refreshed them for me!) and the music, oh the music!- 99% of the game is super-tight. the only things worth mentioning would be; the last boss fight on the highest difficulty is very hard to get right with all the variables and is extremely unforgiving. (it can be rough for the A.D.D. crowd for sure, as there is a lot to pay attention to. focus is a must.)- and sometimes the slow time mechanic of the Journalist's ability can get weird results on attacks going through at the beginning and at the end of the effect. and to a lesser degree on the Priest's invulnerability skill.- ngl, voice acting is very out of place and poor most of the time. although there are a handful of decent lines for each character and the narrator's voice is fine. (a little over-dramatic, but it fits the theme perfectly) and if it bothers you, you can always drop the voice acting volume to zero. (doesn't mute the narrator) although the words still pop up at the bottom of your screen)- there is a story there, but not much. and does feel a little weak. i'm certainly not playing it for the story, but more lore would be nice to draw people in to that aspect more.so far, this game is my game of the year. and overall i'm excited to keep playing and to see what the future holds for Forgive Me Father! :D

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10I think this game excels aesthetically but falls a bit short on the core gameplay aspects to call it a great game. I'll just go over the positives and then the negatives. Also I need to mention that even though I've played a lot of modern shooters, I've not played many old-school arena shooter type games, so my criticisms will come from this perspective.So, I liked the levels, although sometimes it did feel a bit claustrophobic and maze-like - not sure if that's intentional but it was a bit hard to see where you have to go in some parts.  Great variety though, both scenery wise and for mixing up gameplay. I didn't pay much attention to the story, so I can't comment too much - it did seem more of an afterthought - just a backdrop to give some meaning to your slaughter and to create an atmosphere which I have no problem with. Perhaps if you read the notes there's something worthwhile there but I don't care about the story too much in these type of games so I didn't bother after the first level if I'm being honest. The story that was presented through cutscenes I thought was passable. The enemies and the guns all looked quite cool, especially when upgraded. The shotgun and the raygun in particular were both quite awesome. The boss battles also were generally quite enjoyable with interesting mechanics.As for what I didn't like..The gunplay, the guns felt somewhat weightless maybe apart from the shotgun. There just wasn't enough feedback when you shoot enemies for that satisfying feel, maybe that's due to the 2d models so not much the devs could do but regardless I found it lacking when compared to other fps games. Some guns like the spear gun in particular just felt really meh to me for this reason. The movement and aiming also felt somewhat floaty, I can't really articulate it beyond that but it just didn't feel quite right - like my character had no model. I also didn't like the 2 inch vertical jump - feels off when your character moves at like 100mp Makes it pointless to bhop as well which I feel like normally is a major component with games like this. But yeah some platforming parts in particular were quite annoying because of this.  So to summarise, I think it's a worthwhile experience mainly for the style, worth purchasing on a sale. But nothing particularly groundbreaking or super fun when you consider that the gameplay portion is not that great.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid classic Blood inspired FPS game, but unbalanced and lacks polishGood:+ excellent graphics+ great, great OST that has a lot of punch to it+ simple, but good gunplay+ weapons sound good+ most of the weapons are useful+ upgrade system is interesting+ simplistic plot that doesn't get in the way of gameplay+ lenght is not that badBad:- upgrade system is half-baked, with some of the abilities being completely useless (like additional experience, which actually doesn't give you anything)- lamp/flashlight are useless. Instead of that, there should be alt fire for guns, which would make some of the guns more interesting and upgrade path better, because some of the upgrades can be duds (like changing machinegun for explosives or energy, when you get pretty good energy weapon later). Since there is no way to reset skills, you either go back to previous save before upgrade or just deal with weapon you will be unhappy with- taking away half a second from power-up time for animation to hide gem/book sucks- uneven difficulty with merciless difficulty spikes. I played the game on expert and I had barely any trouble (except invisible enemies in chapter 3 - which got fixed), but some encounters in chapter 4 are complete mess. Also difficulty is sadly about how much damage enemies do to you (on expert, as priest, you can be dead with full armor in like 4 hits).- damage calculation is all over the place, sometimes you can survive more hits, other times, you might die from 2- glitch, chapter 4 boss, is one of the worst bosses in video game history. It's fast, it teleports, it disappears, it's like chasing a chicken that doesn't want to get caught. It's God awful and shows game wasn't playtested enough.- some of the sound mixing is terrible, like automatic doors in factory in chapter 3, it's incredibly loud, loudest thing in the game. Shotgun was loud (but it got fixed), but this is whole other level.- bugs, ranging from elevators being stuck to save point putting you in the beginning of the stage instead of save point. I also had a feeling sometimes alcohol doesn't give EXP so you won't get to lvl 16- some of the enemies suck (like abyss hunter)I've got it in EA for around 10 bucks and for that price I can recommend it and say it's worth it. It's perfect 7/10 game - good, but unpolished, unbalanced and has potential to be a lot more.

_childDocuments_.review: Forgive Me Father is a good one of those. One of those being a retro-inspired FPS. It's good, not great.The Good: The gameplay is pretty solid. The guns feel pretty good to shoot and, for the most part, feel unique. Some of the upgrade paths for weapons leave a couple of them feeling kind of the same. The enemy variety is bountiful and the designs are great. You're never fighting the same types of dudes for too long, a problem I've found with other games of this ilk, like Ion Fury. The level design is linear, but well done. There is a good variety in the aesthetics of the levels, so you never get tired of the same environments repeating. The levels are a perfect length for me, too. You're never gonna be stuck in a 30+ minute level -- on average you're looking at about 10 minutes per level. It always keeps you on the hook that way.The Bad: There are a few problems I have with the game. The Doom (2016) soundtrack is good, but it's given too much credit by people that don't already listen to heavy music. That soundtrack definitely influenced the soundtrack in Forgive Me Father. The music is fine, but it feels out of place with the rest of the game's aesthetic. Djenty chugs over a cartoony comic book 1920's Lovecraft world just feels weird. The story is also pretty weak. The developer is obviously inspired by Lovecraft and has a cool visual representation of Lovecraftian horrors, but the writing isn't quite up to par with the visuals They tried going for a show don't tell approach, like a Souls game, but you're never shown much, and what you're told is poorly written. There isn't the same level of writing or attention that a souls game gives, so its just kinda there. Don't get me wrong, I don't play a lot of FPS games for the story, but it could have been better, because the opening is definitely interesting from a narrative perspective, but it goes nowhere interesting and has a generic/predictable end. The upgrade tree starts off interesting, but ultimately isn't. It isn't necessarily bad, and it's cool to have choice, but it was a letdown. The voice acting is objectively bad. It's so bad I can't tell if it was intentional or not. The madness mechanic is interesting, and for the most part I like it, but when your madness gets high the screen goes black and white, which makes screen readability tough. I'm not sure if that was intentional, either. The last couple of levels have some platforming, which isn't great. The worst part about this  This sudden change to a mechanic you're introduced to earlier with no warning is annoying. There are some other times where you can fall and instead of dying, you just start back at the ledge and repeat. It serves no narrative purpose, it isn't fun, and it's just frustrating when you have to repeat this bad platforming in a FPS that never made platforming a core aspect of the game until the end. Finally, some of the geometry is pretty basic. Lots of hard angles and boxes.  It's quite the contrast compared to the rest of the game's aesthetics, which I really like.Overall I like the game. It's good, but not great. I know I wrote a lot more negative stuff than positive stuff, but it's easier to be negative than positive. If you like boomer shooters you'll probably like this game. If you like the look of it and kind of like boomer shooters, you'll probably like this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game takes pretty heavily after Doom 1, being that it starts really high, ends low. Feels like it could have had the last 2 chapter compressed into the first 3 rather than dragging on for so long, by chapter 4 I was just thinking 'my god this game's long" and completely losing my enjoyment because it just starts to get tedious, a lot of the later enemies take a fair bit of gunfire to drop and only some of the weapons being actually useful, I blame the upgrade system for this since it just feels like it gives you a 50/50 choice of picking the good weapon and picking the ♥♥♥♥ one, you'll learn that quick when you take the dual pistols and notice that your once reliable, headshotting revolver has been turned into an ammo eating miss machine that should be dumpsterred immediately.The levels are ok, nothing truly shined, only a handful had interconnected secrets with goodies to collect, where as most of the others were just a straight shot from beginning to end with only a secret placed behind a building or on top of a roof.The abilities were neato, bullet time is always a favourite for a shooter and from my experience turned most of bosses into a straight up joke, same with the larger encounters and while I'm on this train of thought, I'm gunna recall the levels again, earlier levels; chapter 1-3 feels like playing a Doom game, then Chapter 4-5 feels almost like playing Painkiller or Serious Sam with how often it's arena fight then health+ammo then arena fight.Art style is incredible, things look fantastic, but gameplay wise it can be difficult to spot enemies which is a problem and the madness turning your vision B&W is nice, but my god it makes things impossible to see, which is probably the point? but you have 0 control of it, you sometimes get pickups which raise it, but you deal damage to raise it too and you have to deal damage, unless you picked up this fps to just do a friendly meet and greet with the fishy abominations, you can turn the B&W off though, which is nice.Overall, it is enjoyable for the first bit, but I wouldn't blame you for feeling a bit burnt out as you got in the final stretch.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall the foundation here is great. Phenomenal artstyle with the Lovecraft aesthetic that was mixed with a comic-book style artwork, it's amazing and I love it, thank you for the idea alone.If I should give any feedback to the devs as to what to improve going forward: The enemy variety is there aesthetically, but not gameplay wise. Most of the time you'll just be gunning down simple walking ghouls, or projectile shooting enemies, though there is some spicing up for sure, the further I got the more interesting and polished it seemed to be. At first I was a bit disappointed that there aren't any very "eldritch" creatures to fight, but as I progressed the game showed more enemy variety and with it more strange creatures. In the beginning few levels you'll just be shooting simple ghouls, later some undead officers who shoot projectiles, but towards the end of the early access, things will get a bit more crazy and strange, with teleporting cultists, cursed altars that spawn enemies and fishermen who throw bombs at you. Also there's a certain spooky surprise involving a barrel, but I won't quite spoil that here.Arsenal is about what you'd expect. You have your melee weapon, handgun, shotgun, machine-gun, rifle and later on you'll also get a harpoon, which acts as the piercing, high-damage type weapon. Overall the weapons are fine, shotgun was pretty satisfying to use. Only gun I absolutely don't like is the Thompson machine-gun unfortunately. That thing is just stupidly innaccurate and I have no idea where the bullets go when I'm shooting, so I don't know how to adjust. Later on I just started using it as the last resort, I'd always just step into the monster's face and spam it. The more accurate counter-part rifle, when upgraded to fully automatic, totally fixed the issue of not having an automatic weapon and I didn't need the Tommy gun at all.There are also abilities in the game, they're pretty useful, since pickups are quite scarce. I'm not a big fan of this "huge nests of pickups" philosophy, where for most of the level there is nothing at all, but then there are certain areas stacked with loot. I think it's better to scatter the pickups around more, to incentivize exploration. The later levels seemed to do this more, but not enough. Your abilities are tied to a Madness meter which fills when in active combat. I found some use to pretty much all of them, but one thing that I don't like about them is how slow they're to cast. Especially the medailon and the cross. You need to use these a lot mid-combat and it just doesn't feel right to wait so long to be able to fire after executing them, a swift animation but with a longer cooldown on the ability would be better.Controls are a bit clunky. Namely the gun switching. Sometimes you click the number to switch, but nothing happens, then you do the same and it switches, and it's very hard to control mid-combat, as it gets intense fast. You need to have very responsive and smooth control of your character in a heavy combat focused game.Speaking of combat, the first levels are a mess. They feel very unbalanced, there are swarms of ghouls in random corners all the time, and since the enemies make no ambient noises (which is also a big issue), you just get swarmed all the time and hold the trigger, praying it will work. It got a lot better and more interesting in the later levels, so I suggest just checking back on the first 2 or 3 levels and polish them a bit.Big problem with the monsters is they make no ambient noises. They make an alert sound, hurt sound, attack sound and a death sound, but no walk/ambient noises. So if there's one behind you, you'll not know a lot of the time. Monsters need more sounds. Also the damage feedback mid-combat is quite weak. Often times I just kinda "died", not really realizing I was getting hit by projectiles flying at my back. The priest makes some damage noises sometimes, but it's very hard to catch and "feel" when mid-combat, needs crunchier damage feedback for the player.The "crypt" level with the big arena room that connects all the other rooms is stupid. The little window with a bridge is pretty strange, it is not hard to find once you realize it's there, but it's just so out of place and strange that I was wandering around for minutes, and when I checked on a guide to see where I'm supposed to go, the guy was stuck there aswell, so clearly I'm not alone in this.There's also a levelling system with upgrades, which is good. The upgrades were handy. I haven't explored all of them by far during my first playthrough, but the ones I've got were useful and worked.Music is good and fitting, didn't make the experience worse. Menus are fine. Interface is mostly fine, I'd probably cut the blackbars, they feel a bit unecessary. Environment variety is great, you are already able to explore tons of different Lovecraftian spaces in the early access - forests, bogs, cemeteries, cities and even a hospital/asylum of sorts.Overall I've enjoyed it. So far so good, I'm hyped to see what will you guys come up with for future chapters, as the game only gets better the more you progress. Good luck!
_childDocuments_.name: Forgive Me Father

_childDocuments_.review: Forgive Me Father isn't a terrible game by any means, but it's really not for me. The art style is great, but the actual gameplay tends to be a mixed bag, in my opinion, with a lot of small things that make the experience worse, and not enough good things to make up for them.To start off, the story is weak. That's not a huge deal of course, (nobody plays boomer shooters for the story,) but the way it's presented feels wrong, with the narration being presented in second person (i.e. they say *you* do this, *you* feel this,) even though the two playable characters have distinct identities from the player and are making story decisions outside of my control in those moments.To get to the actual gameplay, it's mostly fine. It starts off slow, with nothing but a pistol and a knife, but you slowly unlock more weapons as you progress, and can upgrade your current weapons with the skill tree. Some small issues arise with the weapons, such as the double pistols constantly being out of sync and worse than the basic pistol. There's no reloading, so it's very easy to never check your ammo count and then be surprised when you're out of ammo, because you'll attempt to shoot and instead your gun will switch to a different one, possibly even switching to another gun that's empty. The throwing knives are aimed above the reticle, so you have to aim below the enemies. The shotgun has a relatively small area that it hits, so it's not actually good against groups like in most games. There's also other small things, like destructible objects in the environment that never drop any items, thus only ever getting in the way. A swamp level where all health and ammo dropped by enemies is beneath the water so you can't see them. An elevator segment where the drops stay where they are while you descend. Small hitboxes on drops. Only being able to see enemy health if you're aiming directly at them, even if they're within your reticle. Feeling like I'm being punished for headshots as an enemy just slaps a second head on. Small stuff like that just adds up as you play.The main thing that cause me to drop the game was the underwater stage. For an entire level, your vision is obscured by a diving helmet, your movement is slowed, you can't use any skills (such as the ability to heal), and you can't use any weapons other than the unupgraded harpoon gun. The slowest weapon in the game.  I attempted to upgrade my harpoon gun during the level, using one of my limited skill tree resets, but I didn't receive the upgraded harpoon gun until the next stage, which is a boss battle that you can't really prepare for, as the only ammo dropped in the underwater stage is for the harpoon gun. I still made it through the boss without much issue, but it didn't make up for the underwater stage being so bad.

_childDocuments_.review: Since you're here, you're clearly on the hunt for a unique shooter experience - and you'll definitely get that and then some! _childDocuments_.review: A pretty good boomer shooter.It has 2 classes and some light RPG elements (kills get you experience that you can use to upgrade weapons and class specific abilities. Good variety of weapons and skills. The art style is comic booky and feels unique, and the Lovecraft style plot and enemies are good enough.Definitely recommend if you want a solid old school shooter. There are better out there, but fans of the genre will enjoy at least one playthrough. There is a New Game Plus that lets you tweak a lot of options for subsequent runs, which is a nice addition.Also for completionists, this game is fairly easy achievement wise- no achievements for 100% kills/secrets/items like many of this genre.Only downsides I have are the game is fairly short- probably 5-6 hours on normal difficulty  for your first run and even shorter once you know where you are going.The skills system is interesting and can change the game up significantly, but EXP gain is super slow and you have fairly limited skill resets. Would be nice to see both increased to allow for more dynamic gameplay.Excited for the sequel!

_childDocuments_.review: Forgive me Father is another great retro FPS. The graphical style reminded me a lot of Lucas Art’s forgotten classic Outlaws, but with tons of blood and gore added. The atmosphere is moody and dark while the music ranges from eerie during exploration to DOOM-like heavy metal during combat. The gunplay is fast and precise. There is a good variety of enemy types, and several big boss monsters and the level design is both creative and fun with lots of variation in the surroundings. There are also a few jumping challenges, but nothing too difficult. You can choose between two characters, a priest or a journalist, which both come with different skill trees. Yes, you can level up and skill your character. But don’t fear that this is another wannabe RPG game - it’s not. The upgrade system is well thought out and nicely scales with the growing challenge the game throws at you over its eight hours campaign. There are upgrades for your character like getting more experience points during combat, more health or more ammo reserves. There are also upgrades for your weapons which actually change their appearance and how they function. And then there are several skills like for example stunning enemies, temporary invulnerability or endless ammo which can also be upgraded. One aspect of the game certainly will divide the player-base is the absence of a no quicksave option. Instead, you need to rely on save points inside the level. Which can be quite irregular. So no save-scumming in this one, but I didn’t mind that. It only added to the tension in firefights. The only part of the game that didn’t convince me was the story. The game starts interestingly enough with lots of clues you can find in the levels that give fragments of a backstory. But these story bits become less and less the further you go and everything is thrown out of the window in the cliché ending scene.
_childDocuments_.name: Forgive Me Father

_childDocuments_.review: Forgive Me Father has something of an identity crisis.  It can't decide if it wants to be retro, modern, or an indie title and does a bad job of trying to be all three.Localized damage never works in games like these that try to be fast paced FPSs, and the incentivization for headshots felt odd and out of place.  Add in poor level design and awkward feeling fight arenas, and Forgive Me Father ends up feeling very lukewarm.  While the art style was charming at first, seeing enough minimal animations on enemies who pop in and out of cover makes the already middling gameplay feel like little more than a goofy shooting gallery.The soundtrack is ♥♥♥♥♥♥' good though, too bad it can't carry the gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Forgive Me Father

_childDocuments_.review: If you love the art style, or its on sale for $5 then get it. Otherwise the game is just shy of being worth it. Strong start, but soon you will realize the art is really all that it has going for it. The weapons are severally unbalanced and your starting pistol is better then nearly all the mid to late game weapons which takes a lot of wind out the old sails. You get all sorts of cool looking weapons, but you'll mostly be looking at the pistol(s) and shotgun. That said the shotgun looks sick and packs a punch. The levels lack focus and it starts feeling like a grind later when the game begins to lean to heavily on key cards. Also the story is extremely bare bones, which is fine, but they went through the trouble of having voice acted cut scenes when it feels like that energy could have been better spent elsewhere polishing up levels.  There a few power ups, but their efficiency is tied to the leveling system which I found strange. You earn points to spend on  upgrades that range form the aforementioned power-ups, but also your weapon upgrades, shield/health pool, flashlight strength and a few other things. Would benefit from being broken up into separate systems/menus.That said, it has it's upsides. Obviously the overall aesthetic, the combat is very fast and the movement, despite being slightly slippery, is fine. However, an unfortunate side effect of the speed of the game is you are often blowing past enemies and level dressing.Looking forward to the sequel and hope they polish this up, but for $20 it isn't quite there yet.
_childDocuments_.name: Forgive Me Father

_childDocuments_.review: The gunplay feels "Meh..." _childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this a bunch. About 13 hours of game play to beat the game and I have another toon to play if I wanted a second time. _childDocuments_.review: Look, I actually picked this up due to a $2.00 pricing error from a 3rd party vendor. Ultimately the pricing error was corrected and key revoked. No big deal, because it at least gave me a chance to check things out. Recently having picked up a half dozen "retro" shooters this really wasn't on my radar. With so many popping out of the woodwork, I've found that a lot of them don't really bring anything new to the table. This isn't the case with Forgive Me Father. In the very short period of time that I had to kick the tires on this, I was drawn in the by the stunning artwork as well a legitimate underlying story. Aside from the typical "Save the World", "Escape from Hell", or "Kill Everything that Moves" themes, there seems to be a well thought out story line here. In the end, while I was disappointed that my key was unceremoniously revoked, I was happy for the time I did spend playing. As the price of Forgive me Father seems more than fair, I'll definitely be picking this back up at whatever price I need to.

_childDocuments_.review: Having played now for about 10+ hours, and finishing the game i can finally set my verdict. This game sucks. 1) The length of the levels are not really consistent, the first few were short and then they just suddenly got super long. 2) The level design in chapter 3 to  5 is the absolute worst. You have to constantly mind your hp because you might not get enough going forward. you walk in places where the floor just isn't shown to you, so you guess where you can / can not walk. wow. amazing3) The game feels hard just for the sake of being hard. Even Normal difficulty feels hard because the save points are so few and far between. I end up saving at the first save point i see, run ahead, shoot 2 or 3 enemies and quickly run back and save because i don't know when next i will get one. Peek around a corner, let the enemies follow you, retreat back and take them out 1 by 1. it kinda gets too repetitive   Save points are waaaay too few and far between in the later stages.  I have to constantly reload and do an area 3 to 4 times because i lost 50 hp and probably not going to get it back.5) if you finish a level while having too low hp, well too bad you are not guaranteed hp at the beginning of the next level. so you have to think "ok do i do this level over or can i manage into the next level".6) The chapter select screen absolutely sucks. _childDocuments_.review: I find it very hard to rate this game, because there's a lot of good, a lot of mixed, and a bit of bad. There's definitely enough good that you're likely to enjoy the majority of the game, even if there's areas where it falls short. I commend the effort and so I think a thumbs up is still fair, with caveats.The good:-great art design - that's a no brainer, just looking at the screenshots-satisfying guns - though actual combat can sometimes be another story, the guns themselves feel good to use-expansive skill tree - the skill tree is really great, and what helped keep this game fresh for me was resetting the tree halfway through and changing up my entire arsenal. The mixed:-level design - some levels are good, some levels are fine, and some are labyrinthine back-track-o-ramas which aren't particularly fun to navigate. Every chapter of the game has its ups and downs in this regard so it's not clear cut-combat - enemies range from generally okay to fight, to annoying enemies you can barely hit, to bullet sponges that don't pose a threat but just delay the gameplay for ten seconds at a time. this is what drags down the gunplay a littleThe bad:-bosses - no boss in this game is anything more than a bullet sponge. they're not very fun and the giant fish monster boss in particular had an unacceptable checkpoint placement that meant retrying the fight was just painful.-the writing - character dialogue, story writing, and narrative flavour is all very baseline, and the delivery of most lines for the journalist was pretty bad. it unfortunately is bad enough to take you out of the story altogether-overall story - the story is a jumbled mess even if you're reading all the mini lore snippets, and then the game ends with a total "gotcha" ending that wasn't deserved and just left a bad taste in my mouth, after probably the best boss in the game (which still wasn't great, but was fine).A lot of these are learning points I see in other reviews here, positive or no, and I hope Byte Barrel designed the sequel with some of these in mind. I liked the potential here enough to maybe pick up the sequel on sale, and I genuinely think this is a talented group of folks who just had teething issues with this concept.
_childDocuments_.name: Forgive Me Father

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, the short answer is: yes, it's a promising game. Nice atmosphere, refreshing graphics, fun gameplay.I like how the game is designed to make savescumming impossible, though some enemy placement and spawns behind your back do end up forcing you to memorize some positions so you don't take any free hits. I'd like some more sound cues to know when I am supposed to turn around. Once I clear a room, I don't expect enemies to show up behind my back anymore.The skills are where the game needs a lot of work. Not only because of the many, many "WIP" nodes, but because some choices are downright stupid. The most glaring one is the noob trap: you're obviously supposed to spend your first skill point on the skill that increases EXP gain. There is no reason not to start with that one. You'd only not pick that skill if you somehow failed to realize it's there, which is why I consider this to be a noob trap. It also forces you to spend your first skill point on something boring rather than cool, simply for long term gains. I think this skill should be removed entirely, and the exp required for the next level should be scaled appropriately. I also found some choices to be clearly better than others. Would you rather have an SMG that fires a little faster while also draining your pistol ammo, or an SMG that's actually a grenade launcher, utilizing its own unique ammo type?One final comment: please consider buffing the knife upgrade that says it "massively" increases its damage. It's still not enough to make it effective against the enemies that tend to get in your face, especially in that fishing town level. I thought the upgraded knife would be great against the enemies that emerge from the water, but it disappointed me hard.

_childDocuments_.review: I was initially on the fence about whether to recommend this game or not. The opening first Act is really weak, with small tight corridors that feel the opposite of what the gameplay really requires. The actual gameplay itself is about as basic as any this genre offers, and the voice acting (for both characters) is absolutely dreadful. I really wasn't enjoying myself at all.Then I got into Act 2. The levels opened up, upgrades started fundamentally changing how weapons worked, and it started throwing some more interesting enemies at me. Even the boss of Act 2 was a significant improvement. I was actually beginning to enjoy myself! I thought "yeah, I'll recommend this and tell people to stick with it as things get better".So what happened?Well, after playing the game over three sessions and getting through half of Act 3, I sat down to play the game today only to be met by a black screen. "That's weird" I thought, as I opened task manager to kill the task (that was listed as Not Responding). Sadly, repeated attempts to launch the game result in the same thing. Verifying game files, reinstalling the game, trying older graphics drivers etc. None of it made a difference.Digging into the discussions on the Steam forum (I know, always a risky proposition) I was met with countless threads of people all having the same problem, as far back as 2 years ago. Many saying they've had the problem for months without a fix. So I suppose this is the end of my time with Forgive Me Father. Of course, it had to happen just after I'm out of my refund period as well!So let this review be a warning to others that consider picking the game up. It might just stop working, for no reason, after some inexplicable period of time.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not the biggest fps-player anymore, but this game is like an incantation commin true.the soundtrack is already a contender for best OST 2021, beeing hit more electronic beats, hard metal riffs, or more Lovecraft-esque classical scores (accompanied by strange voices whispering) it's perfect...yes perfect.than there's the visual style, design and quality of presentation. it's not an uber realistic pixel perfect U5 game, but it's one of the best comic-style iterations i've yet seen. it's also the first game where i let all the effects active, even the grain (which is normaly the first thing you need to turn off). beeing it the level-design, the enemy-design, the guns you wield or the skybox: the game was made by people that understand the appeal of the source-material.when it comes the gameplay it's thankfully not a new-age-rpg-looter-shooter-open-world-copy'n-paste-bore-fest, but a more oldschool Quakeish/Doomish approach. Fast pace, lots of strafin, jumping, headshot-galore mixed with enough space to dodge incomming fire-salvos and lots of hidden secrets. the whole thing gets rounded up by a) a skill tree, offering not just flat boni like more bullets-carried, but also variations on the guns you are carrin (get an eldritch shotgun with riccpchet-effetc for example b) perfect implementation of the source-material. your priest can take out his cross to reg health, madness makes you more durable and dps-heavy while building up the more you fight (visual effects inclusive)enemies are not just grotesque but also got hitboxes, leading to wholy different hit-effects. get a headshot for more dps, or shoot the acid-container of an eldricht monster to disable it's ranged abilities. zombified enemies might start robbin across the floor after you "disable" their legs, etc.c) beeing a PC game. yes: there are actual menues with audio, display, grafics and gameplay-settings, rebindable keys, etc. difficulty can be kinda brutal, but the difficulty-settings do have quite an effect. so even you suck at fps (like myself) it's absolutly mangable.the only negatives i can think of is a) the OST not beeing available to purchase yet b) no voice-over. if the priest had a voice-actor in the veins of Darkest Dungeon it would be perfect, but tbh. this would probably strain their budgetand most important c) it's to easy to get boxed in and to get stuck in the enviroment or on enemies. this is partly due to the level-design itself. while large encounters often take place in bigger arenas, during the levels nearly all my deaths were due to me hanging on some standout wall, rock or a corner blocked by a wall of the living dead. more than pleased with this one. this is how a Lovecraft-fps should feel, look and sound like.

_childDocuments_.review: honestly, this is probably a game you will quit halfway through. the art style is fantastic and the gameplay is fairly tight with satisfying guns. but, the combat and level design is fairly boring, on top of poor AI for the enemies. this isn't too bad in the first few levels where there is plenty of space and enemies are easy to dodge, but it becomes an absolute chore somewhere in Act 3 of 5.the worst component is definitely the level design. Starting in Act 3 you end up in literal mazes, some of which you'll have to backtrack through. also, they throw so many enemies at you that you run out of firepower. the amount of ranged enemies in late Act 4 and Act 5 is just ridiculous to the point that i had to turn down the difficulty just so my ammo wouldn't run out.it's fun enough to try, so check it out if you're interested. but, i didn't think fun enough to complete or recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: I was only on level 3 when the game crashed out on me.  It was my fault, I had a few other things open while I was trying the game out so no fault to the game for that. _childDocuments_.review: Recommended with very large caveats - and out of respect to the "small indie developer from Poland".On the Steam page: maybe it's the comic book art style that grabs you. Perhaps it's the Mick Gordon-ish metal infused with spooky ambient soundtrack that gets you to add to cart. The appearance of non-stop action that makes you push buy. Or perhaps -- you're a big ole fan of Lovecraftian stuff.You're in. Let's DO THIS.The first hour or so... not bad. The story is in the way, but you can pretty much ignore that if you want. I found the attempt to sprinkle story items to read half-thought through in terms of placement and execution. Throughout there's a bit of things lost in translation which only gets worse as the game progresses. It's fine, just... other games do this much better and with more immersion. It could've benefited from a more seasoned translator/English speaker, I feel.The main flow/parts of the story are lackluster. Boilerplate Lovecraft, even. Without spoiling too much: You've seen this all before, you've been here before. You can safely ignore it. You're here to rip and tear, anyhow.Speaking of rip and tear - I am fine with the enemy variety. I am less fine with the arena shootouts where you battle waves and waves of Cthulhu chum. It's tiring and the level design? Well.The level design could've used a few more iterations. Environments are rather sparse by themselves. There's five worlds, each with a boss level so 6+1, 6+1, 8+1, 4+1, 3+1 = 32 levels! That's impressive for a $20 game, right?! Yeah, well... the levels tend to feel a bit on the long side. They needed "editing". More play-testing? Enemy placement quickly becomes predictable: alcove sneak ups, "mob storage" with triggered rapid-open doors, bit of teleporting. Keys to find, doors to open. Mostly linear, semi-hub-style esp. in later levels.I encountered a few instances where it wasn't clear what to do next (esp. around a particular boss that drowned me a few times before I realized what the game wanted me to do). I don't quite want to call them bugs but design issues?Guns/sounds are varied enough. The music is a high point. Well done and fade in/out nicely.Bottom line: I got halfway through World 4 of 5 and was bored. Turned difficulty down to causal just to plow through the end... and it still felt like a chore. It all was too much of the same thing. Run, shoot, kill, repeat. Sure, there were a few nice touches here and there, but overall? The game needed a editor, a producer, a stream-liner, someone to tell the game devs "Hey. Quality over quantity here. You don't have the AAA team budget." but I also get the point that then people would probably complain "$20 for 10 levels? I've been robbed!"You never can win. Maybe you'll like that feeling.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll give you a few things I enjoyed about this game:1. PerformanceThe game ran flawlessly with no bugs (I was shocked as well). Frame rate was steady even in heightened activity.2. Game playGame play was engaging with the exception of a few tedious points. Weapons sound and feel great and I enjoyed the extra customization that came with the leveling system. Special abilities felt well tailored to each character. I appreciated the amount of enemies and the clever placement of the more "troublesome" enemy types. Puzzles were fairly simple without being trivial. The Bosses were challenging and fun to trounce. 3. Art and SoundI enjoyed the sprites and the amount of detail each one had. Enemies felt distinct with small differences between them. The environments were detailed and atmospheric, giving you this sense of a crumbling reality. The soundtrack is a good blend of mood setting motifs and enjoyable combat music. The voice actors for the narrator and the priest were good, however, The Journalist was not quite as good. I found her execution of the lines to be "off" from what I would expect a chain-smoking, ball-stomping heroine but all things considered she did a decent job and was a solid entry to the "Strong Female Lead" category.4. Lovecraftian settingWorking within this universe is difficult to pull off in a way that is fresh and engaging. Though this story is simple in comparison to other works by H.P. Lovecraft it is intriguing. It is more of an "Icing" than the main course but this provides a good flavor to the game.I hope you found this helpful. Happy Hunting!

_childDocuments_.review: This is frustratingly good. I wanna enjoy the Lovecraftian atmosphere and the Darkest Dungeon style art and story. These elements are nice. I wanna know what the ♥♥♥♥ is going in this world and where the characters came from and where they're going. The music is dope, reminds me of Dusk or other really good frenetic FPS.Now for the bad things...Least of all, the voice acting is a bit wooden. I feel like the VAs are either overacting or phoning it in and reading the sheet in front of their face. Minor complaint, but it's there.Secondly, what on EARTH is the deal with the fish boss, dudes? I can't see the water's surface from underneath it, and the water hurts WAY too much and too fast, like, the nanosecond your head goes under. It's kinda bad design, and feels really over-refined, like it was supposed to be epic and frenetic, but it's just frustrating because of the limitations of the game.Third, the hitboxes. I step too close to an enemy and I'm instantly damaged. There seems to be no skill involved in avoiding enemy attacks like there is in much simpler games like Doom or Doom 2, I just have to kind of guess where the radius is around them that I can't step to, and it means that if I get surrounded, there's nothing I can do besides spam voodoo doll and hope the enemies all die. (They won't.)These things, and other irritations like them are really obstructing my enjoyment of what this game could be.Lemme reiterate, I don't hate this game. But the pieces of it that frustrate me are worryingly close to obstructing the parts I like.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, I played through what is available, and I gotta say I like it so far. The horror-comic aesthetic is distinct, beautiful and striking, especially the environments and atmosphere. The grass and flowers look especially cool. The gameplay is very reminiscent of OG Doom, which I love because I love OG Doom, with some Build Engine (like Shadow Warior) flavor thrown in. The big ambushes and arena battles especially get my blood pumping and are some of the most fun I've had in a long time. I really love the level variety too, there's so many unique locations, it reminds me of old retro horror games I used to love. The soundtrack is totally awesome as well, really thrilling and always ramping up at the most intense moments. As a Doom mod and boomer-shooter connoisseur (Hedon, Ion Fury, DUSK, Nightmare Reaper, Project Warlock just to name a few favorites) I think I have a few crucial suggestions that really push Forgive Me, Father to its full potential. ___Really Important Tweaks:___ - Show a timer or a bar for how long I have left on my invincibility or unlimited ammo powerups. Losing invincibility at a crucial moment is extremely inconvenient. Also, maybe shorten the "casting" animation. When I want my invincibility I want it quickly. - Show more feedback when getting hit by enemy attacks. Right now, the red screen edge flash is barely noticeable, especially in the heat of combat. I find myself ignoring it, which results in my getting attacked by enemies on high up platforms. Add a directional indicator by the crosshair, a grunt of pain, and a very dim flash of red on the screen (all things seen in OG Doom). - The Revolver gunshot sound is absolutely pathetic. I get that the first gun should feel weaker than later ones, but this thing has no kick, no punch and almost no feedback. The way it splatters enemies (like all weapons do) is great, but a little more bass and a little more recoil would do wonders. (I love revolvers, throw me a bone!) ___Less Important, More Subjective Tweaks:___- Add an alt fire or quick melee to the right mouse button. The lantern is not particularly useful, almost ever. Like in Duke Nukem 3D, the ability to swing my machete while still holding a firearm would be very good for fast moving melee enemies like zombies or tentacle things. Make the lantern an alternate melee weapon, or activated with the z key or something. - Add more variety to the zombie enemies. I must have killed a thousand of the girl-zombie-carrying-a-head enemies. The fact that you have to headshot them twice, or shoot them twice in the stomach is just irritating more than fun. I really love the artstyle of this game, and adding a few more flavorful zombie types wouldn't be out of place, would they? I especially like the unique glowing-eyed guys in that evil-dead type forest. Those guys gave me the creeps! The rest of the enemy variety is fine, but seeing flavored variants (like the Nurse-liquidators in the hospital) and types would always be welcome. - I don't like the Double Barreled Shotgun, even after I upgraded it. It feels pretty weak compared to the Super Shotgun from Doom 2, or the Riot Gun from Shadow Warrior. It often can't one-shot a Liquidator from close range, although that might be my terrible aim, or its spread. Its slow rate of fire should be made up for with power, but it feels pretty useless. - I stuck with the upgraded Tommygun and the other submachinegun for most of my run because they absolutely destroy even the toughest enemies with focused fire. It feels kind of OP, and the other weapons feel pathetic by comparison. The upgraded Tommygun liquidated the first boss, Ca-tharsis, in like 30 seconds. Buff the other guns so they feel comparable, and maaaaaaybe nerf the Tommygun's damage a little. I did like how the Harpoon gun (railgun) could one-shot every normal enemy, that was pretty neat. - There were some strange grammatical errors in the priest's dialog and some of the perk descriptions. For instance, the Eldritch Shotgun should "excrete" pain, not "excrements" it. Some of the priest's dialog felt very clunky, too. It's not a big deal, especially if English is not the developers' first language, but having an editor or proofreader go over it could help fix all the mistakes. - The "Headshot" text is a little immersion-breaking and hangs around a little too long. I think replacing it with a "SPLAT" or just making it disappear a little faster would improve it, but that's entirely personal. I know it exists to help improve readability during combat, but personally I'd like an option to remove sound effects. There are only two, "Headshot" and "Boom", one of which is not a sound effect. The great sound design can stand on its own. The game Void Bastards has tons of comic-book sound effect popups, perhaps adding more text would make it feel less strange. I know this seemed like a long list of complaints, but overall I really, really like this game, and I feel like it has the potential to become a superstar. If you read my suggestions this far, I salute you! Thank you for listening, I'm looking forward to the game's completion, and wish you all the best!

_childDocuments_.review: Don't let Borderland-esque art style fool you. This is a good old-school shooter. Emphasis on "good", not other more positive adjectives. It does what it does pretty well(when it does, that is), but... there might be some things that needs more polishing.First half of the game was extremely satisfying: it scratched that old school itch nicely.  However, starting from a certain stage, the difficulty noticeably spikes. I guess there might be many factors contributing to this, but the major problem to me was the skill tree system and scarcity of ammo. (As for the latter, the developers patched the game later and it became somewhat manageable. Still, prior to the patch, dearth of pew pews turned me really off. A shooter where you cannot shoot stuff. How nice is that?) As for the skill tree system, - The XP boost perks apparently are meaningless, as per some shrewd fellow gamer reported on the steam forum with detailed calculations. (Not knowing this, I wasted my precious time and perk upgrades) - 'Is this really an upgrade, or have I been had?' sort of situation. Some weapons upgrade perks were downright useless (I'm looking hard at you, full auto-upgraded Sterling SMG). - Resetting the skill system is currently nonexistent(although the devs promised there will be one in the future), so the safest bet was to quicksave first, and then try out the perks.Still, the core of blam blam is pretty solid. Give it a go when all those issues get ironed out.

_childDocuments_.review: Forgive Me Father is a really solid boomer shooter with great progression.  The game starts out as a bit of a slog, as this kind of shooter typically relies on movement and bullet spam.  Here, you all too often finds yourself in tight corridors and your starting weapons are under powered.  However, if you can stick it out until you get a few upgrades, the pacing really opens up and you dont feel so outgunned.  The Lovecraftian them and graphics work really well for me in an old school cartoony kind of way.  Plus, all of the Lovecraft Easter Egg's and story elements are a real treat if you enjoy that universe.  I've only played one character, but apparently the second option has different abilities and would make a second play threw at least somewhat interesting.  I am enjoying my time with Forgive me Father, and after every death I actively want to try again.  If you are a fan of boomer shooters and enjoy Lovecraft, Forgive Me Father is a really solid option.  What is on offer here is really good, but if your not a fan of boomer shooters, it's likely not going to be so good as to convert you.  My in genera ratting is B+ and my general Indie gamer ratting is C+.   So take that as a recommendation with some cavorts.

_childDocuments_.review: Ehhh... 30 minutes into this, I was absolutely loving it. The art style is beautiful, and the gunplay is reasonably fast and satisfying. Unfortunately, that's about the extent of the positives. As mentioned elsewhere, the animation on the enemies is extremely limited, the script is terrible ("Do you know about war safety?") and the voice acting ranks as bad as anything I've ever heard. The simplistic level design and aforementioned lack of animation means that after a while you just feel like you're running around a warehouse shooting at targets. For all the carnage in the arena sections, it just feels kinda dull.If you're into boomer shooters and get it for a reasonable discount, you'll probably be pleased enough with the addition to your collection, but there are far better retro shooters out there.

I have to upgrade a certain gun before I can get the extra health perk? Same with extra armour, you have to upgrade a gun before getting to it. Why? _childDocuments_.review: The game is a Lovecraftian First person shooter with a nice comic book look to it. Also reminds me of Doom.Story for the game was interesting, but it's a shame there wasn't anything different when playing it a second time as a different character. Sure, the dialogue would change for the character you chose, but that was all that would change.The Levels; in terms of their looks and designs were fine, but it's the platforming however that was what made playing the game rather irritating  at times. Especially in later Acts where the platforming was the pivotal point in finishing the levels!Combat is a mixed bag if i'm being honest. It's good don't get me wrong, but after a certain point it  becomes a slog fest just to finish the level when the game just tirelessly throws the same enemies into a room and calls it a day. Rinse and repeat till the end of the act and you fight the boss. Just got to a point where it felt boring at times which sucks because it was fun for the first part of the game.Going to add this in here as well; the final boss is a bit of a let down for all the build up it got for the entire story, I won't go into full detail, but i was pretty disappointed with how it all ended since most of the other bosses in this game were way harder to fight than them.Sometimes I wish i could leave a "Maybe" option for these reviews. I won't say it's a terrible game and still give it a thumbs up, however I would highly recommend getting this game on a sale if you can.

_childDocuments_.review: The first few maps were pretty raw and kind of bare bones. I felt starved of ammo so I wasn't having fun and put the game aside for a bit. I came back and pushed through to give it one more try and I'm very glad I did because this is a great game and perfect for the Halloween season. It's a classic-style FPS mixed with some pseudo-RPG elements and a quality Lovecraft atmosphere. Any of my complaints from the first handful of levels were washed away playing the rest of this game which is balanced and mapped out wonderfully (get the ammo capacity upgrade first then faster XP gain second on the skill "tree" and you'll be golden).Slow to get started but once it does get rolling it's one hell of a fun ride. A hearty recommendation all around especially for boomer shooter fans.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid 8/10 arena shooter. Played through on normal difficulty as an experienced shooter player and found the combat reasonably tough, even if I never actually died specifically to the monsters themselves.  The game does kind of drag in the later hours as levels get longer, more maze-like and tend to rely more on platforming and traps than enemy design for encounters.I do have a handful of criticisms, though:1. If you want to take the story seriously and get into the moody lovecraftian vibes, play the priest. I don't generally criticize indie games for their voice work, but nothing takes you out of the cosmic horror vibes quite like the reporter refusing to take any of this seriously, with "well that just happened" tier lines like "I don't have any strong feelings one way or the other" and "I've always wanted to wear TWO bulletproof vests"... especially since the story is trying very hard to push how horrified the character is outside of gameplay.2. The boss fights are... kind of not great for a first person shooter, with many of the threats the boss throws at you not telegraphing from the boss themselves. This leads to situations where the boss is high up in the air but the damage telegraphs are being displayed on the ground, making most first time encounters with the bosses a test of memorizing when you should be looking at the boss and when you should be looking at the ground.3. The game has an "insanity" mechanic, which boosts your damage based on how much damage you're doing in a given encounter, and the higher the insanity gauge the more greyscale the game becomes. I'm not sure if this was intentional by the developers, but when you're at maximum insanity it can be extremely difficult to parse the environments as many enemy varieties tend to blend into the background without their colors to help them stand out. Fortunately you can turn this greyscale off if it's a problem for you. Apart from those three things (two of which are optional), I still say it's a solid retro shooter experience, well worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: A BUGGY MESS!Art style grabbed me like I'm sure it did most of you. Started out strong with amazing art, fun guns, and decent level design and music. Unfortunately that's where all the issues start cropping up. The cod style health hud damage system is super broken, guns do not scale after level 2 and cannot be further upgraded, broken textures or objects missing textures completely. Dont even get my started that 1/3 of the levels barely run at 15 FPS. I thought maybe this issue was on steam deck only but was easily able to replicate on both of my pc's. To make matters worse you are having to deal with probably the worst voice acting and story ive seen in a game bar none. Leaving out these elements would have easily improved this mess. I have no idea how they were able to put out a second game. Nor do I understand how people gave this a good review. Maybe they didnt get past level 2? Overall there is a huge lack of oversight on this game. If the team was 1-3 people you could make the argument this is excusable, but since this was a full indie team I really have to put my foot down to this kind of behavior.TLDR: LVL1: Good stuffLVL2: Some weirdness but ok lets continueLVL3: this is def broken how could this shipLVL4: barf

_childDocuments_.review: has a wonderfully executed and very unique aesthetic that I appreciated more and more as the game went on. That goes for everything from the level design to the enemy design to the lighting and to the sound effects. It all meshes together well. The bossfights are always a treat and visually the game mixes it up a lot which is nice. The one sore spot in all that is the writing and voice acting which are both not worth your time. What little story there is doesn't propel the gameplay at all and if I ever replay this game I'll probably skip the cutscenes and story collectibles entirely. That being said, I'm a bit torn on if I ever would replay the game. On the one hand, I think it has great autumn vibes and would fit October well, on the other, it's fun for a first playthrough but I feel wouldn't hold up for a second as the gameplay is a little too simple and wears out its welcome by the time the credits roll. In the end, I recommend  but it's nothing groundbreaking, in fact it wears its influences on its sleeve, for better or worse.

_childDocuments_.review: After beating ACT I, I'm probably going to refund this game...Gameplay is decent and it looks gorgeous, but bad voice acting, subpar writing and broken achievements don't make for an overall fun experience. On top of that, the game doesn't really do anything interesting with the Lovecraftian premise. This isn't the first FPS-game with Lovecraftian or cosmic horror elements, but Forgive Me Father is the only one I know that tells a Lovecraftian story and honestly, it kind of feels like it misunderstands Lovecraft.Now, the store page does say the game is only inspired by Lovecraft, but (spoilers, I guess) using an Elder God like Cthulhu kind of automatically makes it seem like an extension to Lovecraft's stories, not just a game in the cosmic horror genre or one with cosmic horror elements. Now, keeping that in mind, having a character like the Journalist joking around and seeming oblivious to her surroundings kind of breaks the immersion of the game telling a Lovecraftian story. H.P. Lovecraft never really was interested in telling human stories and so his characters never really had any personality, only told stories of horrors they had witnessed. That and the game just drops the name of Cthulhu out of the blue. In the story Call of Cthulhu which worked as the debut for the God, when an Idol of Cthulhu is introduced, no one knows what it is. Here though, the main characters instantly recognize an Idol when they're presented with one and right after, the character that gave the Idol gets killed by something, as though Cthulhu and his minions somehow took it personally. I get that it's a minor thing to get bummed over, but even the idea of creating a Doom like shooter set in the Lovecraft Mythos defeats the idea of cosmic horrors being undefeatable, much less unknowable. If I could, I'd give it the game a decent rating but seeing as I can't, I'll give a dumbs down since this game wasn't really for me. I understand my nitpicks are kind of my own and others might not see it as I have, but this is why I didn't like the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Forgive Me Father

_childDocuments_.review: About five or six levels in or so, and I've been enjoying the game quite a bitArtstyle is great, there are some very interesting ideas at play with the enemies, and secret hunting is fun but not overly ridiculous like some games make itThe pistol and the burst rifle are the two best weapons for most situations. Accurate and powerful, great for landing headshots. The shotgun is great for taking out one single enemy, maybe two if you're lucky, at close range, but between the reload animation and the pellets not piercing at all, it can't handle hoards of weak enemies like I was expecting. But, if in the middle of a fight you need to take out a liquidator quickly, but you can't land a shot on their tank with the pistol or rifle, the shotgun is a perfect solution. (Also it sounds like an absolute cannon, which I love)The machine gun baffles me. I have not been able to find a useful situation for it. The recoil is crazy, even with the upgrade, and the damage just does not keep up with the recoil. Better off using the burst rifle. All in all though, the game is a ton of fun, music, art, and sound are all excellent, and gameplay is really good. Not every game lets you be a priest dual wielding revolvers as you leap across rooftops doming eldritch horrors

_childDocuments_.review: Very solid FPS retro shooter with a graphical style that works so well with the Lovecraftian aesthetic. _childDocuments_.review: The game starts off fairly basic; boomer-shooter, cool art style, some lovcraftian-inspired enemies. But as the game goes on, it changes from being lovcraftian inspired to full blown cosmic horror. The final few levels are very reminiscent of the final levels of DUSK, where everything goes off the rails, ant its awesome.Some of the voice acting is awful (Particularly the journalist), and the skill tree sucks when it forces you to upgrade things to get upgrades for unrelated things. Also the final boss was OK at best. But the gunplay is great, the weapon variety is really good (especially when you spec into the weird stuff), the level design is good and has some incredible art in the latter half of the game.I adore this game, and I honestly believe it is the best boomer-shooters, up there with the likes of DUSK and CULTIC. Well worth your money.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game with an interesting art style, awesome soundtrack, and very fun gameplay. _childDocuments_.review: tldr: Grab sequel, it's just so much better.This game is reall very close to being a great fps. Graphics are amazing, nothing else to say here. Movement is rather fluid and most of the arsenal feels good to use. Music and sound (exept for awful journalist voice acting) complement the gameplay well.The biggest shortcoming of he game is level-design. Levels are mostly very cramped and difficult to maneuvre in, which is especially bad for a retro-fps game. Some levels feel outright redundant. Game has no save feature, just checkpoints. And god these are placed bad. Difficulty spikes are a thing in this game, too. Sometimes you are running through a level wondering if your difficulty slider accidently slipped from max difficulty, and sometimes you feel infuriated after replaying a several minutes worth of gameplay ten times. That all being said, this is a fun game, but it overstays it's welcome and may be very irritating at times. Get it on sale.Or just get a sequel, it addresses most of problems this game has, making for a really uncompromized enjoyful fps experience.

_childDocuments_.review: In all my time of gaming, no game has ever given me a more convoluted, muddled gathering of thoughts regarding it's quality as Forgive Me Father. When the game is running on all cylinders, when everything comes together just right, it is truly great, Yet, that "when" in the previous sentence is a very important qualifier, as the game deteriorates into a slog in by the middle. What confounds me is that there's no singular glaring flaw to point at, nor even a consistent notion as for why the game begins to feel off. It's an intertwining web of mechanical quirks and slightly out-of-tune design ideas that grind together into an amalgamation of boredom. First though, I should get the basics of the way. The gunplay is great, the artstyle is fantastic, the sound is pretty damn good, and the game is generally well-polished. Forgive Me Father nails all of the fundamentals, which is rare for an indie game. The devs did an amazing job on that front, and it's extremely impressive. The story here is faithful to Lovecraft's books, telling a story through a collage of tiny pieces. If you like that style then you would probably find great enjoyment from piecing this all together, but the entire thing is skippable if that doesn't rock your boat. There are two playable characters that have different playstyles, the journalist and the priest. I have played with both, and I strongly, strongly recommend the priest. More useful abilities and the voice lines aren't actively annoying, like the Journalist. She reminds me of the protagonist from Ion Fury but unironically, and I have a feeling that the Dev team was not going for that when making her. There's much, much more I want to say, but that's irrelevant for those who want an actual review. To those contemplating purchase, let me put it like this. The game is worth exactly it's price. If it's on sale, I would very much recommend it. If you have 20$ free and just want a good shooter, this is a good choice. But if you have to choose between this game at full price or another game on sale, get the other game. Forgive Me Father relatively short, and the middle section seriously drags, but it is definitely fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Really into my cosmic horror atm so, coming from 22.7 hrs of "DREDGE", for a bargain price "Forgive Me Father" gave me some more amazing Lovecraftian goodness (evilness?) but in a totally different genre. 19.4 hrs for completion for me, the main issue for the longer playtime was that at a couple of quick save points I was low on health and resources and hit a difficult section of gameplay which then actually became a bloody nice challenge to overcome! Plus, I'm old and scared of tentacles going into my butt...Starts off slow and a bit underwhelming but then really warms into things. The gem is the fast pace and the lovely crafted 2D art style ('Lovecraft' LOLZ!). I'd describe it as Mike Mignola meets "The Wolf Among Us". The weapon design is stunning (I want more options and cool artwork please!).Overall, super keen to support the next addition, Part Deux. More weapon modifications, build respec availability and boss battles would be my humble request. Oh, and perhaps some spicy mayo with sriracha to go along with the squid rings x

_childDocuments_.review: Well darn....I really wanted to like this game. Seeing it last year on Realms Deep shivered me timbers.Alas, at about the 4th act, this game becomes a nasty slog to play so much that I quit. Like others have said, the enemies turn into bullet sponges and some fly around the air super fast and launch well-placed projectiles. It becomes a pain to dodge all that crap while trying to have enough ammo to take anything down when they can take so many hits (even on normal). It just isn't fun for me after a while.There are definitely some cool parts to it. The style is unique. Lovecraft elements are always a plus. But crummy dialogue and the awful levels combined with bullet spongey enemies turn this game from decently fun to a chore quite abruptly.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm typically a big fan of old-school shooters, but Forgive Me Father just never clicked for me.The stylised visuals are a treat and there is some fun to be had, but I found the core gameplay far too repetitive, with largely uninteresting encounter design and an arsenal of weapons lacking in unique identity and utility (although some of that that may have been down to the specific upgrade paths I followed). Some of the levels are quite intricate and feature some fun areas, but those bright spots fail to make up for the sea of bland mazes and corridors in between.The narrative is also bizarrely over-complicated. There are dozens of lovingly-made story collectables and cutscenes, so it's clear they were going for... SOMETHING. But it almost immediately tangles itself up in confusing details, made worse by poor localisation and voice acting throughout.Overall, Forgive Me Father is a competent FPS and the comic book visuals give it a fantastic sense of style, but there's very little substance underneath. It doesn't do anything special and by the halfway point I was more than ready for it to be over.
_childDocuments_.name: Forgive Me Father

_childDocuments_.review: The first three episodes are good, but it starts to lag as it reaches towards the finish line, with enemies becoming increasingly more annoying, and the combat becoming more and more repetitive.The guns themselves feel good to use, though the rocket launcher feels weak with how slow its projectiles move and the little impact they do. Enemy designs all feel pretty identifiable and unique from each other. The maps, although linear, do offer a variety of settings and circumstances, but are overall a step back from the complex worlds of games like Duke Nukem 3D and Blood.The biggest problems are with the maps being so linear, and following a simple hallway -> arena -> hallway design; the upgrade system which feels tacked on and doesn't really assist the gameplay in any way, instead it can sometimes cause weapons to become ineffective if you choose the wrong upgrade; the way that the visual cue for being hit isn't consistent with the amount of damage being taken; the flurry of visual effects can make it a bit hard to tell what's going on - i.e., when the screen goes grayscale, or when there's too much blood to identify where enemies are - and there's very little immediate distinguishable audio cues to alert the player.The game is at its strongest in the first three episodes, when upgrades don't matter as much, and when it is able to be more atmospheric. Overall it's a good game, but the final two episodes are where it plummets in quality and the kernel of problems found in episodes 1-3 are expanded.

_childDocuments_.review: There are a lot of retro shooters on Steam, I would skip this one. I feel bad ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ on it because a lot of love went into certain aspects of it, but they forgot the dang fun. IMO there's not much fun about how slidey everyone is, how quickly they lock onto you to attack, weapon design, or how no gun has any alt fires or ADS modes. For instance, you get an AMAZING looking gun midway through that pulses and you're like whoa what's it do? It shoots a slow floating ball that blows up. I was excited for eldritch weapons but they're just skins that behave like regular guns, or worse. Most of the damage you take is because they tucked a guy behind you when you went into a room and they immediately triple shot you when you came in. It's not too difficult, because there are generous heals in the game and on your person, but it's frustrating to play. Games like this need to set up fun scenarios for you and give you tools to take those scenarios on in fun ways but this game forgot that bit. They just tucked enemies into all the corners and called it.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game, but it's just not that good:-The story is nothing to write home about, the ending twist is laughably uninspired and the priest and journalist campaigns are the exact same except they switch the protagonist's sprite in the cutscenes.-Even when I upgraded my weapons to their max level I was still unsatisfied with most of them.-The tree skill could've been better.-Some secret areas can only be discovered by sheer luck but I guess that's just a nod to the first Doom era and they're not mandatory anyway so I'll give it a pass.-Aiming doesn't feel right and the same goes for a couple platforming phases (you can feel the capsule shape of your character sliding on some edges)-Most of the levels' design is pretty uninspired and doesn't present any kind of challenge whan it comes down to the "puzzles" you've got to solve.-Music is not bad I guess but it's just not my cup of tea.That being said:-The sprites are good-The kills are satisfying-There's a lot of variety when it comes down to ennemies and their attacksBasically, it's a very average shooter that I think is worth its price but is just not good enough to be recommended.
