_childDocuments_.review: The game was great - up until the last act where the dev(s) made a bunch of incredibly poor decisions that made the game more annoying than anything to the point I didn't want to finish it. It made it seem like they did little to no playtesting and just threw ♥♥♥♥ at you to annoy you. Having to switch between light/lantern and a weapon is awful - there is a reason in Doom 3 a mod was made to be able to have both at the same time. Having platforming sections in a game meant for running and gunning is also a piss-poor decision, especially when you're running full speed you don't jump at all and just fall flat. Finally placing pits that you fall to your death if you're not playing close attention DOES NOT BELONG IN A FAST PACED SHOOTER.While this did have a complete 90s feel I loved, I just couldn't get over the decisions made in the last act that just absolutely killed it for me.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a big fan of lovecraftian aesthetic, and boy howdy does this game deliver.The game starts out a bit technical, demanding you score headshots to survive. Then it gets a little easier as you gain more weapons and abilities, and you're able to bullethose enemies down. But, then the game gets hard again as the enemies start piling on; rooms and layouts become increasingly insidious, and managing the appropriate weapons and making optimal use of your special abilities becomes integral to survival.Overall the game does well in scaling the difficulty. If you're not good at or inexperienced at shooters you may want to start at an easier difficulty level than Normal. To my knowledge there are no achievements tied to difficulty level, so choose whatever difficulty feels most rewarding.

_childDocuments_.review: Really liked the art style but the level design is so bland that it makes the game feel longer than it is. The middle part in particular was exhausting to get through. A lot of the gameplay loop for some levels is find red, yellow, and blue key to progress while killing enemies. That is boring as hell.Gunplay was serviceable but there were clearly weapons that were better to use and others that were straight up hot garbage. Hint: energy weapons are godlike. Next, some encounters in the game are way more hectic than others without any sort of ramp up. Some other reviews touch upon this but its like one minute you blow through a group and then get into another encounter where you're easily decimated. There's no natural progression in those instances to play more effectively until a wall comes up. Another thing, the game is also not very good on cluing you in how it wants you to progress sometimes despite my previous comment of a lot of levels being simply a unlock gates until you finish level type thing. I know there were some parts in the mid section where I was confused as to where said key was because the game doesn't do a good job of naturally leading you to where you need to go. I don't really play this genre very often so I may not know what makes a good retro shooter but I know i've played games with a more interesting narrative and better gunplay than this.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of the difficulty appears to stem from two things:The enemies have collisionI can't see anythingI feel that I'm forced to memorize the level layouts to avoid being punished at times, some of the jumps are a little cheap. There also isn't a lot of indication where I'm getting hit from, so if something spawns behind me while I'm fighting something else, a lot of the time I just won't notice it's attacking me.Enemies, being 2 dimensional, sometimes group in a way where I can't at all tell how many there are, as in they tend to perfectly silhouette one another when extremely close.All in all, this game looks great, feels pretty decent. It's in early access so it gets a pass.

_childDocuments_.review: Forgive Me Father is an awesome boomer shooter with a distinct Hellboy/Mignola-inspired art style that really stands out. The dark, comic-book visuals and Lovecraftian atmosphere set the perfect tone for a fast-paced and intense shooter experience.Most of the weapons feel great to use, and the upgrade and skill systems offer meaningful customization, letting you play the game your way. I played as the priest on hard, and the difficulty felt just right — challenging but fair, and very satisfying when you get into the flow. The game's length is also solid, providing a good amount of content without dragging on.One of the standout elements is the energetic soundtrack, which really amps up the intensity of battles. The music keeps your adrenaline pumping and perfectly complements the fast-paced gameplay.There are a couple of downsides, though. The story is decent, but it could have been more engaging, and a few weapons end up feeling pretty useless compared to others. Overall, though, these are minor issues in what is otherwise a fantastic shooter that fans of the genre shouldn't miss.
_childDocuments_.name: Forgive Me Father

_childDocuments_.review: Forgive Me Father puts its best foot forward in its first two episodes, introducing the player to both new weapons, skills, and enemies, then declines in its last three with poor game design resulting in arena rooms, labyrinths, and overly annoying enemies. Both the ability and skill systems fail to hold up in the endgame as less options become viable due to the fast, health-sponge enemies of the latter episodes.The beginning of the game is enjoyable with well designed levels that feel old-school yet with some unique visual flair, but it gives way for poorly lit, visually basic ruins by the end that go on for way too long that it spoils the earlier experience. Early enemies can be critically hit by aiming for the head or for the fluid tank which is fun, but by the end, the enemies have too much health, fire very quickly, and are thrown together in large empty rooms resulting in the same combat arenas repeating for room after room. I appreciate that Forgive Me Father attempted to push some modern features into the boomer shooter genre, but it's sadly a failure. Abilities are wildly unbalanced between the two characters, with the Journalist being practically useless other than her time stop ability, as getting in melee range of enemies on the hardest difficulty most certainly means death. Contrast that with the priest, who can activate infinite ammo, invincibility, and health regeneration, and it makes me question whether there ever needed to be a second character. The writing is... subpar, but if the gameplay is good, I can normally look past it.Leveling up allows you to spend skill points to upgrade weapons and abilities, which sounds nice, but don't really offer that much choice in how they feel to play. Changing a gun to use another type of ammo is usually pointless because then you have to weapons that use explosive ammo and perform the same function. Upgrades normally just increase weapon or character stats which don't feel too different. The experience bonus skills are terrible and should never be included in any game as they are always the go-to skills to increase for higher profits (not to mention I was able to unlock all three in the first few missions). Skills can upgrade abilities, but they just increase duration. It sadly feels like a pointless addition.Bosses are interesting, but not all of them are designed very well as they require you to look up at the boss to hit them while the boss shoots projectiles on the ground level, meaning you must look up at the boss and look down at the floor to see where to dodge. It's fine for third-person games, but it isn't great for first-person. Overall, the bosses are a cool spectacle and break from the normal missions.Forgive Me Father sadly falls apart the further you play it, which is disappointing because it has a very strong opening.

Well ♥♥♥♥ you, you dont get to use them for random reason. All of your skills (as journalist) are completely useless: Your "berserk rage joint" is useless cause you cannot reach him, meaning you can neither hurt him nor heal yourself, you cant stun him with camera, you cant hurt him with voodoo doll. Very cool, give us these abilities, let us enhance them with points and learn to effectively use them so you can do nothing with them against literally the only really hard boss in the game. He has a variety of attacks, whether you can evade them usually depends on the planet constellation and whether or not you sacrificed a goat this morning: He does a groudn pound which is so fast i didnt even register it until i went flying, he spams projectiles as well as massive fireballs you have to dance through and pillars of fire from the ground. When the fireballs hit they blind you so you just get stunlocked to death, meaning instakill usually. Pillars, Fireballs come from the ground, which you cant see cause you are looking up, great game design here, either you can see the boss or you can survive, very cool. But the worst thing is "the blob": A shallow but big mass of flesh that follows you around, damages and stunlocks you. it cant be killed, it persists throughout the entire fight and YOU CANT ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ SEE IT CAUSE YOU HAVE TO KEEP LOOKING UP. So 50% of this boss fight is just luck, whether the blob hits you or not since you cant evade it since you cant see the ground. Also it can just randomly block the way through the fireballs so yeah, this boss depends on sheer luck. Another great game ruined by perhaps the worst boss in gaming history, abilities are useless, half the guns are useless, he just has 5 billion hp and spams always the same AOE attack and you cant even see him and the ground. Great boss design, im honestly too frustrated to give it a good review, so yeah, first half good, second massive disappointment

_childDocuments_.review: Wish steam had a meh ratingwhats great:Soundtrackart directionwhats bad:level design and pacing you can basically blitz through the first 2-3 chapters in 90 minutes then they probably realised the game is gonna be too short so they just filled the last 2 chapters to the brim with bullet spongey enemies where a very common enemy takes 3 shots from point blank from your double barreled shotgunlast chapter have needles platforming to pad out the levelsthe scariest thing about this game was the journalists voice actingOverall a meh game if you like the art direction you'll probably enjoy it but there are a lot better boomer shooters out there but you could also certainly find worse out  there
_childDocuments_.name: Forgive Me Father

_childDocuments_.review: For anyone looking into the game and wondering how it actually plays compared to others in the "retro shooter" lineup its overall solid for it still being developed. I played it on hard mode and its a nice challenge with a first boss fight that was fun.Its a mix of tight corridors and square box areas that feel along the same lines of Project Warlock however with a bigger horror aspect with the various dark corners and ammo shortages.Things to improve: All upgrades are non refundable and for the weapons change how they function quite a lot. While this would give more repeatability in theory, the slow progression makes each change matter that much more. This creates an issue since some weapons are functionally the same with how their used. The holy water doesn't seem to have a use in large crowds or against bosses where a damage grenade effect would have been more useful and functional. Lastly all madness points gained during combat goes away after about 4 second cool down, this makes it really hard to use it other then long drawn out moments where when it finally kicks in only to give the damage boost to killing the last enemy in an encounter. A possible easy change is to let it be an at will buff like Amid Evil does allowing for split second use to help keep the player alive.Still, I'm excited to see what the final product will be.
_childDocuments_.name: Forgive Me Father

_childDocuments_.review: PROS+ Art style is amazing+ Nice boomer shooter gameplay, is not Doom but is pretty good anyways.+ Cool and inventive boss fights.+ Decent variety of enemies.+ Plenty of levels  so it has enough content to justify full price CONS- The story is pretty bad.- Story bits you can find on the levels are cryptic making it hard to piece together what is goin on.- Sometimes I got lost and didn't knew how to advance so it can be a little frustrating trying to find how to progress.Overall the game is pretty good, Is a shame the story is so barebones and the levels felt connected with super glue. But the most important thing (the atmosphere and the gameplay) is there so is an easy recommend for any boomer shooter fan.
_childDocuments_.name: Forgive Me Father

_childDocuments_.review: If you want good sprite work, tight gunplay, and decent writing, go play one of the hundreds of DooM mods out there that do it way better than this barely-more-than-Wolfenstein-3D knock-off.The gunplay is good, but only because it is basically the gunplay from DooM with headshots (which DooM mods have been able to do for a decade).The writing is subpar and switches between the third and second person narration just in the first few minutes. Most of the 'lore' is crudely adapted from existing lovecraft lore and does nothing new or interesting with the material.No sprite rotations. When a monster is walking away from you, its sprite continues to face you. They figured this ♥♥♥♥ out in 1996 and could get full rotational sprites from clay models. Now-a-days we have so may more tools to streamline this process, which DooM modders already do, to emulate a 90s 2.5D art style. Just lazy.All in all, not worth the time and definitely not worth $20.

_childDocuments_.review: While i don't regret buying this game and playing it i do feel a bit tricked since the devs put so much work in the first 3 chapters then rushed the last 2 for when the early access ended and 1.0 released with all 5 chapters. Playing the game you can clearly feel the drop in quality and map design.The gun play was nice, the upgraded eldritch weapons looked really cool but and there is a big but the whole talent tree was pointless, plus the 'powers' you can use. Finished the game with level 20 with all weapons upgraded, all 3 points of extra exp from monsters, some points into the ammo packs then the last 3 points used them randomly. They could have done something different with the powers, maybe have more impact in the game? Idk, but i didn't use them at all. Maybe once or twice pressed R to reload (habit from playing other fps games) and used whatever power was on R.The presentation of the game with the eldritch monstrosities is hands down the best i have seen from an indie developer, that being the factor that made me buy this game.Buy the game at a discount if you liked the visuals, for a bit of fun gun play with some decently cool guns but don't expect the quality of the first 3 chapters to continue with the last 2.PS: After the dev comment. _childDocuments_.review: Not quite soup yet. The design is great. The guns, for the most part, feel good. Revolver could use more oopmh. My issue is with the balancing of difficulty settings and the madness meter. I played on the hardest difficulty off the bat, and while I don't think the game is too hard, the lack of ammo was frustrating. And I get it "well it's the hardest difficulty- duh" but that isn't the point- I don't think ammo, at least for lower-tier guns, should be incredibly scarce even on the highest difficulty. It just isn't fun to switch to your knife and strafe circles around mobs because there just isn't ammo left. The problem is probably mitigated by certain skill selections as you go through the game, but it was frustrating in the time I spent playing. The madness meter was very underwhelming. It runs out incredibly quickly even if you are playing aggressively. Doesn't seem to reward aggression and playing well as I hoped it would. Lastly, pretty big issue- the voice acting for the journalist is terrible. I didn't play the priest so I can't speak on that, but the VO for the journalist is grating and very cheese. But not in a good cheese way. Just feels a bit amateur. I'd buy the game again once it gets some patches and quality of life fixes.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a first person arena shooter. So the gameplay is in on itself fairly simple and straight forward.You get to chose 1 of 2 charakters at the start. They both get access to the same weapons and skilltrees but have different active skills at their disposal. You get 4 different skills per charakter and the game states that the Priest is suited for a more methodical/defensive approach and the Journalist for a more aggresive approach  Looking at the skillsets I can see why. However, after chapter 2 there are no more possibilities for "slower thought out gameplay" because thats when the difficulty starts to spike. The game tricks you at start into thinking that it is a smooth and at parts almost relaxing game. And the first 2 chapters certainly feel that way. However, as other reviews have already mentioned: After chapter 3 the difficulty starts to spike. And around chapter 4 and 5 you will be fighting the spongiest and most hard hitting enemies the game has to offer. Unfortunately at this point you will very likely have most of the relevant upgrades if you chose the "More XP Skill" at the start. So while the difficulty ramps up, your damage wont. The game could have benefited from a slighty bigger skilltree in my opinion.  Sound is another mixed bag. The ambient sounds and music tracks individually are absolutely amazing. I genuienly enjoyed those. However, the game took clear inspiration from the 2016 DooM game. So whenever there are wave sections the game will hit you with a sick metal soundtrack. Again, these are great. But they kinda put this game in an awkward position where you are not sure if it tries to be a horror game or just a kick ass arena shooter.The voiceacting is also a mixed bag. While it is not top of the line it is mostly serviceable for that kind of game. Well, and then there is the Journalist... and I am really not sure what happened here. But unfortunately her voiceacting is just completely off. I can only assume that the direction was something like "Badass Action Hero" which in on itself would already be a bad fit for this game. But unfortunately even that direction is poorly executed and awkward at best. This will be a clear preference kinda thing. I really enjoyed them. I think this comic look works well  and looks really nice and fresh. And it also allows for a clear distinction of what type of enemy you are fighting. But I can definitely see why some people may not enjoy these types of visuals. Again, I genuienly enjoyed them. But I am aware that this is just a question of personal taste.The one exception in terms of visual design are the Children of Ygolak. They are another testiment as to how the game doesnt really know what it wants to be. All enemies look great visually. But these are smaller variants of the Ygolak... but with shorts with a pink heart print on them? Now, don't get me wrong. I am a "shorts kinda person" and this would definitely be my kind of  a different kind of game... However in this game it just feels off. But to be fair this is just a small exception to the otherwise great visual design. Especially the designs of the levels is something to praise here. You will have all sorts of bioms that change suprisingly ofter but still stay mostly coherent. I am sure there is one. And you get bits and pieces told either by cutscenes or story snippets you can find throughout the levels. But in all honesty I very quickly lost track. Especially since . The game currently costs 19,99€. A full run with a charakter might take you anything between 6-9h

_childDocuments_.review: Forgive me Father is one of my favorite shooters. The art style is phenomenal, the soundtrack slick, and most importantly of all, it's just a fun game to play. The controls are tight and the shooting is just plain phenomenal. And that's just scratching the surface. There's an upgrade path for your weapons, letting you have a degree of customization to how you play. Nothing too major, honestly, but it's enough to spice things up. And the power-ups are just a treat. Slow down time with cigarettes, become invincible for a short time, all the kinds of buffs you'd want in a hectic firefight. The story is practically paper-thin, and the voice acting is what you'd see in a B-movie, but at the same time, that feels like the vibe the game is going for so it's hard to knock the game for it. It's cheesy, it's over the top, and it's ridiculous, and I could not recommend it enough. If you like these types of games, Forgive me Father is an immediate buy, plain and simple.

_childDocuments_.review: great game, but what happened to the dev's minds in the last world? Overcomplicated level design for the sake of nothing, tons of enemies, enemies respawning, new enemies that deal tons of damage, that are fast and have thousands of HP each, all of that in almost complete darkness, visually generic setting with completely unnecessary platforming sequences that were not present through the whole game. Last but not least, a final boss that requires you to shot high but almost all his attacks are low, making so if you shot him you necessary take damage, if you avoid his attack you can't really shot him.As I said, the game is great, but the last world is literally a mess and I didn't quit only because it was close to the end of the game itself.Also the story is totally unclear and explained (I believe) using the old "notes and objects" scattered around the world, which is the worst type of narration human species ever invented. Stop doing that, it's literally better if the story isn't there at all than making such distractions around maps, which almost always contain useless information to begin with.
_childDocuments_.name: Forgive Me Father

_childDocuments_.review: The game starts out SO great. Chapter 1 is filled with mystery, enemy balance is just right, and levels are short enough that they don't overstay their welcome.Unfortunately, every chapter after the first one just gets worse. There are more enemies and they have so, so much health. We are talking multiple point blank shotgun blasts to down an enemy here. New enemies are introduced but they are all so..annoying. Every enemy has homing projectiles or is tiny and explodes. And due to the blood animation that plays out when you shoot them, it is difficult to see what the enemy is actually doing to avoid it. Nevermind the fact that each enemy also has 2 or 3 frames of animation at most, they are basically cardboard cutouts.You also stop gaining levels almost since XP becomes so stingy, thus making the level up rewards almost not matter.The levels themselves get longer and longer, and at the same time blander and blander. I swear the game never ends. There is a 40 minute section of a dumpster and a sewer..jesus. And the story just...dissapears. There is literally no story. I am on CH4 currently and just forcing myself to finish it.The game shows incredible promise in the beginning but really falls flat on its face. It is clearly obvious that it was rushed in order to deliver a ""finished"" product. Keep in mind that, even though the game has 86% positive rating, around 5% of the people who bought it have actually finished it. And the game is less than 10 hours long. That should tell you something.It makes me very sad to say this but at the end of the day, I don't recommend Forgive Me Father.

_childDocuments_.review: Forgive Me FatherReviewA new Early Access Gritty FPS set in 20's/30's i believe, the graphics are really well done and the later levels really show this best, the frame rate is tight and everything runs smooth.. except one thing i will discuss further down.I have played probably around 10 levels or so, i havent seen all the weapons but so far the upgrade system is pretty great.. except when i re-entered the game and it did not keep my Stats.. _childDocuments_.review: If you are in the mood to blast through hordes of monstrous entities with holy fervor, "Forgive Me Father" might just be the salvation you seek in the boomer-shooter genre. This game offers a delightful journey through a beautifully twisted world that perfectly marries a fresh art style with classic run-and-gun mechanics, creating an experience that feels both nostalgic and innovative.Artistically Blessed GameplayOne of the most striking features of "Forgive Me Father" is its unique art style. Instead of the typical retro pixel look that many shooters in this category opt for, it presents a more modern but equally artistic vision. The comic book-inspired visuals are not only a breath of fresh air but also enhance the game's eerie atmosphere perfectly. Although I have a personal preference for retro pixel aesthetics and would have loved to see this game pay homage to that style, the chosen graphics undoubtedly add a distinctive charm that sets it apart.Sinfully Fun to PlayAt its heart, "Forgive Me Father" is incredibly fun to play. The action is intense and gratifying, featuring a variety of enemies that keep you on your toes and weapons that feel satisfying to use. The game excels at keeping the adrenaline pumping from start to finish, which makes it hard to put down once you've started. It's the type of game that invites you to lean into its chaos, encouraging you to revel in the mayhem that unfolds.A Descent into MadnessAs the story progresses, the game takes a dark turn into ever more psychotic scenarios, reflecting the protagonist's descent into madness. This progression adds a thrilling psychological depth to the gameplay that escalates the chaos in a mesmerizing way. It's fascinating to see how the narrative and gameplay interweave, pulling you deeper into a madcap world that grows increasingly unhinged.A Labyrinthine ConcernHowever, the game is not without its sins. The maze-like maps can be a significant source of frustration. I often found myself getting lost in the elaborate labyrinths that make up the levels, which can detract from the otherwise immersive experience. The absence of a map feature is a puzzling oversight in design. Including a simple navigational aid could greatly enhance gameplay, helping players maintain their bearings without sacrificing the complexity and explorative allure of the environments.Verdict: A Blessing for Shooter FansDespite its navigational challenges, "Forgive Me Father" stands out as a stellar addition to the boomer-shooter genre. Its fantastic art style and exhilarating gameplay are more than enough to forgive its few shortcomings. Whether you're a fan of old-school shooters or looking to try something new, this game promises heaps of fun and a visually striking journey through a nightmarish landscape that grows increasingly psychotic. So load up your holy shotgun, and prepare to deliver some divine retribution to the monstrous hordes that await!

_childDocuments_.review: is a great oldschool FPS with a graphic novel artstyle that fits its pulpy lovecraftian setting very well. The soundtrack also enhances this vibe and is the cherry on top of the frenetic action and helps getting into the flow of it.The games' story is suitably simple and told through story clues found in the levels, as well as motion comic cutscenes, that are executed pretty well. The story can be experienced with two playable characters, although the character you choose does not impact the story at all. I chose the Priest on my first playthrough and unknowingly picked the far easier option (due to his abilities), but I also picked the hard difficulty option and it turned out to be a fun but challenging experience for me (not being the best FPS player).The gameplay feels very fluid and while running through the eery rooms and dark corridors or facing a horde of enemies in an arena, you really get into its speedy flow. The games' weapon arsenal seems pretty basic at first, but the simple skilltree comes with the option of upgrading weapons, making them more interesting and introducing some amount of strategy with chosing the ammo some of the weapons use or weighing accuracy against speed. Skill points are gained relatively fast (especially with the EP-boost perks) and respec points are supplied regularly enough to warrant some experimentation. During a normal playthrough, all levels you have already reached can be selected from the main menu individually, which is great for secret-hunting. After completing the game once, you unlock an the  (an arena survival mode with different maps) and , which has a ton of modifiers to play around with. I was also determined to hunt for all the achievements in this game and it took a second playthrough with the Journalist character (much shorter, because I knew my way around) and some time playing the Endless Mode as well as a handful of select levels with NG+ modifiers to make my life easier.All in all I can wholeheartedly recommend  if you like FPS games, especially of the classic/retro variety and/or enjoy the aesthetics of this wonderful Lovecraft + graphic novel combination.

_childDocuments_.review: Review by Unam God, Forgive Me Father is great.Let me start by saying that I love the Doomer Shooter genre, it's one that constantly innovates with games like Doom Eternal, Ultrakill, DUSK, and the list goes on. However, it is important to note that games that don't innovate are usually forgotten or not appreciated as much as those that do. That being said, Forgive Me Father joins the ranks of the list of games that deserve all the appreciation for it. By far the most unique aspect is the art style. The game oozes a cartoonish aesthetic that fits the tone of the story. Everything looks so detailed and energetic like you're a comic book from a first-person perspective, and it does it amazingly. The enemies are also super varied in their design. They all have different weaknesses, but hitting the head usually does the trick. There is also an insanity meter, which fills up when you kill enemies and makes you stronger/faster. That is incredibly cool, and it creates a risk/reward system that is not commonly seen in the genre. For the price, the game is also lengthy, so trust me when I say you're definitely getting your money's worth out of this one. Where it gets a bit messy is with the skill tree. Your character can gain specific stats and abilities, which is a cool concept, but the problem is that most of these abilities feel gimmicky or useless. The other issue with the game is that the weapons are generally uninteresting and generic. There isn't one weapon where it is iconic and emblematic of the game like the BFG from Doom or the Revolver (that shoots coins) from Ultrakill. That is a shame, but these mistakes can be fixed with a content update and some small tweaks. Overall, the game is a great buy for those who enjoy fast-paced action shooters. It probably won't impress you much if you've played other games from the genre and there are some annoying issues, but for what it is, it's a great game.I give a Forgive Me Father...

_childDocuments_.review: "I shall send ye back to hell!"Forgive Me Father, a dark depressing foundation of an shooter. Set in an eldritch world that descended into madness. Everyone is either under a cosmic horror spell or is dead. Except for a pastor, which is you. Guided by the hand of God you will eradicate the hell ridden spawns!We can't expect God to do all the work however, that's where the guns come in. (Note this is not all the weapons/their upgrades. This is also taken on the hard difficulty)Knife - Surprisingly usable. I mostly used it at the start, because I hate melee weapons. It takes out groups of low life enemies. It has a big boy upgrade and a throwing knife upgrade I however did not use, because I was too far in to give them a chance. Will update when I get around to using them.Revolver - The workhorse weapon. I found myself using these so much, as there is an upgrade that gives you t w o. I love this gun, make sure to keep on using it near the end also. Also quick tip, double tap to the chest for the regular zombies with a skull in their hands. Trust me, it's quite useful.Shotgun - I love this design for a weapon. It is lovely and a damn fine shotgun also. With the upgrade for the power shotgun makes it a killing machine for groups or a single mid tier enemy. I also heard that there is an upgrade that makes it bounce pellets off of walls. Sounds fun and more fun.Tommy Gun! - I love tommy guns, this one is fun. It makes a fun noise when firing and mows down mid tier and low end enemies. Lovely I love it and the upgrade kit for it makes it shoot faster and is also pretty.MP18 - I like this weapon also, It reminds me of a Sten SMG, but more "Modern" for the time. Problem with the weapon is I did not use it like an SMG for long as there is an upgrade for it that makes it a FRICKEN GRENADE LAUNCHER! Which dispatches hordes of hell spawn so quickly, I love it!Lastly, from the weapon list I can remember the Harpoon Launcher - Oh my god this slays too bad I got it right at the end of the Demo. I am sad for that, but it's good for how I upgraded. Most of my upgrades were close range oriented, having range was nice for a change. One shots most mid tier and DEGENERATE low life enemies.Now for abilities, we got a few. The cross on activation gives health. The mop of holy water "Which is just fricken funny by the way" stuns enemies, the bible makes you invincible, Amulet makes that current weapon have unlimited ammo for a short while.How do you gain these abilities? BY GOING MAD of course! By killing things with extreme prejudice, you will gain madness which makes your attacks hurt more and you take less damage. When the meter is charged, you will gain one of each of these abilities. Overall, this pastor is not to be trifled with. Because while God forgives, he does not. With two chapters already out, several different enemy types (only a few are annoying as they are wack a mole enemy types), two different bosses with different styles of fighting. This was a fun time waster. One that I will happily come back to when more content comes out.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR;Pros-Short and sweet (~5 hours playthrough)-Great gunplay-Good class customization-Great level design-Decent story (Great characters)Cons-Most bosses are boring-somewhat bullet spongey enemiesActual Review              This game is seriously underrated compared to other boomer shooters out right now. It's not as flashy as some of it's competition but a lot of it's arenas, and the abilities made for a super fun experience. I played as the priest in my first playthrough, and halfway through a journalist playthrough as of writing this. Priest's abilities give you exponential spikes in power such as immortality for a little bit, or giving you infinite ammo; the tradeoff is that the abilities have to be charged by killing enemies. Journalist on the other hand is a more linear combat, with cooldown based abilities that complement the gunplay such as bullet time or wide aoe damage or crowd control. They both are really fun to play and down to players to choose who they want to use.            All the guns feel good to use, and you when you level up you can upgrade the gun, most have branching trees, which lets you change your loadout to fit with how you wanna play better. Where the game shines is its madness effect though, madness is a meter that gets built up during fights, and as it goes up you do more damage, this lets you start a fight off taking cover and playing slower, but ramp up to a run n gun as the fight progresses. My only issue is that for a lot of fights in the game, it feels like madness only hits after the fight is almost over, ruining the point of the effect.            The only issue with the combat in my opinion is enemies can be a little bullet spongey, especially on the higher difficulties, this also turns ammo management into a real hassle, forcing you to always use the right weapons for the right enemies. In my opinion it makes the game feel like less of a shooter and more of a puzzle game, not too big of a fan of how it was done, but it's not bad enough to turn me off the game. Bosses though, bosses are way worse. Every boss, with the exception of the final boss (who was a really good fight), has a massive health pool that isn't fun to wittle down, especially with most of them having super easy to dodge attacks, it makes for a super tedious fight all around. Again, this isn't a big enough negative to keep me from recommending the game, but it's still worth bringing up.            The story is passable, I didn't come to the game looking for a great story, but both playable characters have a good sense of development while you play the game. No spoilers but the ending was boring, it does a twist, and feels kind of overdone. The cutscenes in between levels are super cool, and the characters dialogue during fights and as they react to the story is pretty good for the most part. With both characters having a similar development of becoming less timid and more of a badass as the story goes on.             That's everything I want to talk about in the game, you really should play it for yourself. It's a little short for it's asking price, but the multiple playthroughs, and an endless mode make up for it in my eyes. Highly Recommended

_childDocuments_.review: Pros+Great atmosphere complimented by the comic book style graphics+Guns feel great to shoot and the feedback is punchy and satisfying+Combat can get hectic and requires quick thinking and constant movement in order to survive+The sound design is fantastic and can go from dark and foreboding to rocking your nuts off with chunky metal riffs whenever you get into a fight.Cons-While the graphics can look great, it's hard to discern some things as all the sprites kinds of "pop" and it can lead to everything kind of meshing together. Exploration is encouraged to get secrets, but a lot of the time you're just kind of humping around the perimeter of outdoor area looking at foliage taking up 80% of your screen, while you wade through tall grass.-Glitches. The game just came out so I expect the devs to fix these issues as users report them. Most notably is the issue with the auto/quick saves not loading automatically on death. I'll die then sometimes get kicked to the beginning of the stage. The solution is simply to go into your options and manually load the save, but it's annoying nonetheless.The other glitch is invisible enemies sometimes appearing in particularly chaotic fights. They can be any enemy since the issue appears to be that the game simply didn't load the sprite but the AI is active. I've only run into this glitch in about three fights, but it was still jarring to take damage and not know where you got hit from, which leads me to...-Damage feedback. I can't tell when I took 5 damage vs when I took 150. You have to constantly check your HP in fights to ensure you can continue playing aggressively, or if it's wiser to fall back and take cover and/or look for health and armor. A damage direction indicator would be great as well since you're surrounded in almost all engagements and it's easier to tell where the immediate threat is. (I should mention that my first full playthrough of this game was on Hard, so I'm not sure if that's something that could affect this)-Boss Fights are fun and challenging, but require a bit of trial and error. The first boss killed me a few times because he was  spawning something behind me, but I couldn't tell because neither the audio nor the boss really made it obvious. I'd just be running into explosions while strafing around. Some bosses have "tells" but others don't, and even then you kind of need to just be aware that you're going to wind up in "hey, you got the boss into phase 2, but you're not standing in the correct place and you're gonna take some damage now while you get to the spot where you SHOULD have got the bosses HP down to the threshold required for the next script" situation.Overall it's a fun game and I definitely recommend you give it a try

_childDocuments_.review: FMF is an interesting attempt at making a Lovecraft styled FPS and the developers appear to have put significant time and effort into the art style, aesthetic and sound track, however shortcomings in the game play, level design and late game enemy/boss design hamper the overall experience. If you love FPS games styled after doom/quake and your a fan of HP Lovecraft then FMF will likely be worth buying on sale, otherwise probably pass on it.The good:-As mentioned above the visual style of FMF is very good with interesting areas and enemies.-Enemy design. During the first half of the game enemy design is good. Enemies are balanced, non-spongy and often have quirky interactions (like zombies replacing their heads after headshots).-For the most part level layout are fun and balanced for exploration and combat, this does change slightly towards the end game.-FMF also has a character leveling system, which (to the best of my knowledge) is not common these types of games. This system is very basic and offers some rudimentary variety to the your play through, however props to the devs for trying to implement a unique system into a well established genre. The bad: -The skill tree is very limited in verity and some weapon upgrade options are worse than the base version. -Weapon balance is inconsistent. The two SMGs are very powerful once they have their damage/accuracy upgrades, additionally the shotgun always stays relevant at point bank range even in late game. However weapons like the harpoon gun and the rocket launcher are mostly underwhelming, the knife becomes almost useless late game because of high number of enemies and lackluster damage and the pistol uses the same ammo type as one of the SMGs, meaning your better off just using that instead. Overall you will likely forget the harpoon gun exists until your out of SMG ammo.-Many late game enemies are fasting moving with high hit points and often hard to dodge attacks. Having powerful enemies is a good thing, but their design should hopefully feel fair and be engaging to encounter, unfortunately FMF uses a old school approach to increasing game difficulty and just replaces most of the early game enemies with many tougher ones. Furthermore, the weapon imbalances become more pronounced with these faster tanker enemies because the only weapons that can reliably hit them are the hit scan SMGs and the shotgun, meaning the remaining weapons are almost pointless after the halfway point of the game. -Finally boss design. There are four or five bosses in the game, most of them are ok at best and none of them are exceptionally good. this is mainly due to their simplistic design or sadistic design. For example, the first two bosses are pretty easy and do not introduce any new gameplay ideas or mechanics to the genre. additionally, the execution of the boss fights is not groundbreaking in any meaningful way, in short most of the bosses are just bland mechanically. The final boss is actively not very fun to fight, not because he is super hard, just mechanically frustrating and towards the end cheesy.Regardless of how this game turned out, I wish the devs good fortune with their future projects and i am glad they tried to make this game, even if the execution was slightly off.

_childDocuments_.review: Quick Description:-Forgive Me Father is a throwback boomer shooter w/ a lovecraftian comic book style.  This game throws a whole bunch of different things against a wall similar to a Jackson Pollack piece and spits out a fast, chaotic, and brutal fps w/ a soundtrack that slaps.  This game has so much potential, but unfortunately misses the mark when it comes to weapon balance, fundamental fps mechanics, and a frustrating progression system.*Notes:-I played on the standard difficulty and found it to be pretty good.  I found it on the easier side early game, but found it quite challenging late game.  I would say that Forgive Me Father is harder than the average game in the genre, but not substantially.  What's Good:-Forgive Me Father has a really cool and unique visual style.  You will not likely find a single game that looks like this.  They opted for a comic book style w/ big and bold colors, hand drawn art, and it takes place in a lovecraftian wasteland.  The animations are great, guns look badass and bizarre, and the bosses can cover the entire screen.  This game should win plenty of visual presentation awards.-There are tons of unique guns to keep you busy.  You have your standard pistol, shotgun, submachine, but you also have some extremely unique mutant-like guns.  The shotgun can be upgraded to a powerhouse that blasts enemies to pieces, the submachine gun can be upgraded to spray energy bolts across the screen, and the harpoon gun can be upgraded to impale even the most abominable beast.-If you are going to make a throwback shooter in 2022, than you had better have a banging soundtrack and this game does not fail.  It's not Andrew Hulshult, but it's still pretty awesome.  It's lots of fast metal music that blasts your eardrums in just the right way.-There is a skill tree, which I was really happy to see.  You don't see enough skill trees in the fps genre.  Every gun has a couple of different upgrade paths, which gives players choices.  I love when games allow players to have options and customize the game to their liking.Could Use Some Changes:-As much as I loved the idea of the skill tree, it ultimately failed due to a few key factors.  Firstly, multiple guns share ammo.  You probably shouldn't have guns that share ammo b/c it tends to make one gun not worth using.  You can accidentally end up w/ three different guns that share explosive ammo, and this ammo is very hard to find, especially early game.  The next major problem is that it becomes harder to get a skill point, the deeper you get into the game.  I used my first 3 skill points on skills that maximized my ability to collect xp.  This was a massive waste and shouldn't be offered.  You are way better off upgrading your guns and max health right away b/c you will eventually get to a point where the XP grind hits a dead wall, making it extremely difficult to get another point.-There is a massive issue w/ the amount of ammo that is available.  I played it very safe, using my knife on all cannon fodder and being extremely selective on when to use stronger weapons, and still ran out of ammo continuously.  To make matters even more frustrating, when you run out of ammo, you won't automatically switch weapons.  You can even switch to a weapon that has no bullets.  I lost track of the amount of times I switched to 3 weapons w/o bullets in a row while running in circles trying not to die.  It's brutally defeating when this happens.-I think the Save Spots could use quite a bit of work.  There really should be a Save Spot at the beginning of every level.  I found it very tedious to feel the need to have to travel all the way back to a previous Save Spot b/c I was worried about dying.  I would survive a really intense gauntlet of monsters, but then die a few moments later to a random cannon fodder b/c I was out of ammo, lost too much health, and was searching for a Save Spot.  This doesn't feel like a fun way to challenge the player.-There are some issues w/ the color scheme and a few of the enemies really blend in w/ the surroundings.  This was an unintended consequence of the visual choice.  A few of the early levels that have lots of tall grass were the most noticeable moments where this affected my vision of enemies.  This is a fairly simple fix w/ a bit of editing.Consensus:-Bottom Shelf Game (Tier 5 and makes up 10% of my reviews).  I found Forgive Me Father to be a difficult game to review.  There were moments where I could really see the potential of this game.  I loved the art style and am a huge fan of anything lovecraftian.  I thought that the guns were really cool looking visually and I was really intrigued by the skill tree.  Unfortunately, I found myself more and more frustrated as I got further into the game.  The devs have already put out a patch that address some of the issues w/ the skill tree and the lack of ammo.  I will wait a few months and give this game one more full playthrough, just in case some of the problems are fixed.  Unfortunately, as of now, I can't recommend this.  The fps genre is incredibly crowded, and there are some amazing boomer shooters that Forgive Me Father has to compete w/.

_childDocuments_.review: Forgive Me Father (2022)A beautiful looking game playing off in the Lovecraftian universe. You get to shoot monsters beyond your comprehension with a wide variety of guns such as the revolver or shotgun. As you kill enemies you gain experience to choose upgrades for your guns, abilities, health or shields. You get to choose between the Priest character or the Journalist character. I played the priest so I can't say too much about the journalist, but the priest plays extremely fun. He can stun enemies, you have invulnerability, you can have infinite ammo for a short while and he can heal himself.The game is fairly long if you take your time to explore each level. There are secrets to be found, in the form of armour or ammo as a reward for finding them. You need to search for the story clues so you can stitch them together to learn the story of the game. Each of the five chapters are unique with more and more, stronger enemies coming at you the further you progress, Each chapter has an end boss to kill. If you love the works of H.P. Lovecraft. this is a real fun game to play. There is an endless mode, see how long you can survive. There is also a new game + mode where you get to choose how you play. You can give yourself all the weapons in the game, you can give yourself as many skill points as you want and you can tweak almost any setting in the game to craft the perfect run for yourself.You have the adrenaline fuel of oldschool shooters such as Doom (1993) and you get to save the world from eldritch horrors. Really fun, great game. Give it a go.9/10“The most merciful thing in the world, I think, is the inability of the human mind to correlate all its contents. We live on a placid island of ignorance in the midst of black seas of the infinity, and it was not meant that we should voyage far.”― H. P. Lovercraft

_childDocuments_.review: Great retro style FPS. Love the comic book art direction on this one. There's lots and lots of blood too. Gameplay mechanics feel good. The game is very difficult, especially once you get to acts 4 and 5 when flying enemies start spawning. Ammo can be a bit of an issue at times, so make sure you're locking in on your targets and not wasting too much ammo because you can run out pretty easily if you're not careful. Classic red key, blue key, yellow key in order to progress in the levels. Shotgun is king, especially upgraded. Upgrade the cross healing skill all the way for reupping on health in between save points. Final boss battle with Cthulhu really drives home the HP Lovecraft inspiration. It's epic. All in all, a difficult, yet very satisfying FPS. Highly recommended if you don't mind dying a lot and are thirsty for blood. Use cover whenever you can to mitigate damage taken. A+ would recommend and will play through the game again at some point because it's that much fun. This is an example of an early access game done right and developed into a full blown cosmic blood bath. Definitely worth the price.

_childDocuments_.review: So I've just finished the game as the Journalist and oh god what a horrible ride.The game starts of strong, it looks beautiful, the melee weapon is useful and aside of the voice acting being straight up horrendous, it seems okay.A little later, after more terrible voice acting you get faced with stupid choices like those ennemies that when killed just continue chasing you while crawling or those zombies carrying another head which they use to revive themselves when you shoot their main head.The weapons feel punchy but most of them are useless due to recoil so you'll mostly use the shotgun and the pistols.Easy difficulty is way too hard btw, wtf is this ?The skills are unimpactful and aside of the weed sword to regain health with kills they seem fairly useless for the most part.You're given a skill tree which doesn't make sense as some weapon upgrades lead to more health or shields (yes, somehow)The story doesn't seem to make any sense and concludes on a very unsatisfactory end, and most of the bossfights are totally awful except one of them (big ugly fish)So in the end, what's good you may ask ?The designs, the artstyle and the music are all this game has going for itself.It also oddly reminded me of Dusk during a lot of the playtime and I like to call it "Dusk if it was bad"So yeah.. _childDocuments_.review: I have to say, its really good, but tough.  No offense to anyone, but I played on easiest difficulty.  I am sorry.  Anyway, it is like Doom and Lovecraft combined together to make an exciting FPS, lovely, a match made in heaven.  It's also as tough as Blood, just like an old school FPS toughness.  Something to push yourself to complete the game. Even though this is an early access, I am pretty sure it will carry anything you earned over the main game when its released. Now for the meat and potatoes, the story is just about ta priest (a reporter will be added later) to fight against enemies and kill evil, that's all for now, but its game-play action make up for its light story telling.  The guns you use to fight evil is responsive and can be upgraded which is lots of fun since you can use different types of upgrade points to make your weapons stronger and some have a few negative points.  But the fights also make up for it.  Enemies blast you from a distance and hurt you when they close, my favorite are the wretch's who have two head, head shot one, they put the next one on.  So enemies have ways to kill you in fast pace and interesting ways, so keep your guard up.All in all this a fun one, and worth your time, when the game is complete and is released play it to the end.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr Great interpretation of a doom type shooter. Soundtrack seriously slaps. Art is awesome. Lighting on point. Weapons are fun as hell.  Definitely looking forward to seeing this game finish its development.More in depth reviewI played this game on the hardest difficulty and i never felt cheated or some arbitrary challenge was placed in order to fill the settings' stereotype; ie, monsters being bullet sponges or damage being over the top. There is one particular enemy you'll encounter that will absolutely nuke you into oblivion if you get caught off guard but i think that's by design in order to keep you from being able to speed through the entire level for free. From what i could tell it was implemented with increased damage received and sparser ammo drops, which tbh in a game where you're holding 7 at a time it just encourages weapon swapping which is A-Ok by me.  The music is so incredibly good. If you were into the Doom 2016 and onward soundtracks, this game will scratch that itch. They have a mechanic in this game where chaining kills in quick succession builds up a meter where upon reaching a threshold your damage is increased for a duration. I never really felt the power spike if im being honest, but when you do meet the conditions the music and screen change to further increase the intensity of your gameplay. 10/10Boss fights. There's a few of them in this bad boy, way more than what i was expecting in an early access copy. Each one is unique and introduces more challenging and demanding mechanics. They took me a couple tries and i never felt like the game was being unfair. It's very VERY apparent that everyone who participated in this game cares about the quality of their contributions. This is a GOOD game, in a market saturated by half assed garbage. its 10$, you'll enjoy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: The gunplay is decent, weapons are satisfying so the essential point for an fps game is already here.It's fast paced and the fights are entertaining, solid run and gun classic blow up everything formula.Forgive Me Father art style and graphics are nice, good cell shading and 3D/sprites effects.Unfortunately the level design sucks in the first levels, they are very linear and uninspired.Later levels are a bit better and opens up a bit more, still linear but not as bad as the first levels.In this game it's really easy to get swarmed and cornered by enemies and some spawns are kinda cheap to be honest.I suggest removing collisions between enemies and the players so we don't end up dying gang banged by enemies.Would also be nice if we could remove the black bars and increase the fov to higher values.Forgive Me Father is a promising indie fps, I enjoyed playing this early access sneak peekRight now there is not much content, should take around two hours to complete for most players.Now let's hope the developers listen to the community feedback to improve the game.

_childDocuments_.review: You like old school shooters? You like Cthulhu? Go ahead. Give this game a go.It doesn't offer an absurd amount of game time, I completed it on normal or easy, I forgot, in about 6.5 hours.BUT the fact that every level is different in structure and art direction helps immensely to a) make the game feel longer than it actually is, and b) to not get fatigued easily.I'd even say that this is the game's strongest suit.Gameplay is a mix of "♥♥♥♥, what's around the corner" exploring in the dark, shooting single enemies with precision, and going all Doom 2016 with the glorious soundtrack in several arena battles, some of which take place on precarious platforms as well.Guns handle mostly fine and can be upgraded throughout the campaign by simply killing stuff and levelling up your character. However, a BIG flaw of the upgrade system and the game in general are the ammo types. If you're not careful you will end up with 2 or maybe even more weapons that share the same ammo types after being upgraded, and that could be a serious problem, as the game gets very stingy later on with some ammo types. That being said, even your starting revolver is pretty good, even in the final levels. Changing guns though was a big annoyance. There is neither a weapon wheel nor a hotbar where you can actually permanently see which weapon is associated with each keyboard shortcut. Scrolling through the weapons with your mouse wheel is almost suicidally slow. Faster weapon switching would really help the game out.Furthermore your character has certain skills that can also be upgraded, from healing to stunning, invulnerability or limitless ammo for a time. These abilities get charged by simply being bad-ass and killing stuff. Brutally. There is a second character you can use as well, but the gameplay is basically the same. She does get other abilities, but they all sound way worse than those of the initial character. Maybe if you want a more hardcore experience? I don't know.The art style is what ties this game together in the end. You're reminded of a more modern interpretation of the older Doom games. From the level design to the hand drawn art assets and the way enemies "move", since they're basically 2D animated images in a 3D world. Quite unique I'd say.Forget the story though ... it just serves as a vehicle to get you from chapter to chapter.I'd normally say 20 bucks is a bit on the expensive side for a rather short game, but this one is a gem and it's just unique and interesting enough that I think it's more than worth it if you're into classic 90s/early 2000s shooters like Quake or Unreal. Plus, there's an endless mode and you can test yourself with harder difficulties, play through on the 2nd character, etc. etc. If you want to. So, those 6 to 7 hours can easily turn into 20+.

_childDocuments_.review: Just beat the early access content.  Pretty good game. Had a lot of fun.  This is Doom meets Lovecraft.Despite the cartoonish, comic book graphic style the game looks pleasant. It still manages to keep a dark atmosphere. I actually had a few moments of uneasiness and some jump scares here and there.Sound design ranges from very good to very meh. Some of the monsters sound like a little kid trying to make a scary voice.  There's a good variety of enemies.  And the bosses are awesome to fight. (only 2 bosses at the momment)  The weapons are satisfying and there's a bunch of them.  You can also upgrade your character. I haven't check out all of the upgrades avaiable, but from what I have experienced, its pretty cool to use them.  For example you can upgrade your knife to a throwing knife. Incredibly useful when you have no ammo.But I do highly recommend to get this on sale only. Also, as a christian I have to mention something... you play as what I assume to be a christian character hence the title of the game  ''forgive me father''.  And through out the game you gain abilities to use. Such as a cross (regens a portion of your health) and a bible (makes you invincible for a while). I absolutely loved that. This is probably the only video game I've played that showed some respect to christians, while nearly everything else in the market is so quick to mock and defile christianity in the most teenage edgy way possible.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has me conflicted. On one hand, the 2D art is impressive and creative with interesting visual designs for enemies and weapons. The sound design for weapons is very strong, the skill tree is interesting and I welcome the respecs you get after boss fights. After finishing the game though I found the experience honestly tedious. Combat with enemies doesn't really change throughout the game, enemies get faster, shoot more projectiles and have more health. There are very few interesting enemies outside of their art once you've fought a few. Additionally the story is not good, which can be fine if it's downplayed for the gameplay, but it feels like someone trying to complete a checklist for Lovecraftian tropes, the ending of which being the worst offender. The level design and combat is simply tedious after a time. Some areas have really nice ambience and spooky enemy ideas. However, instead of letting these areas and new enemies breath, they are turned into key hunt mazes with every room being filled with ever enemy you've ever seen. I'm not going to talk about the platforming because it's just not good.I did also find it strange that the VFX seem to throw away the art style, but not entirely. Blood is animated in the same method, but magic and projectiles are all these bright generic Unreal engine particle effects. There are a few things that also break cohesion in the environment, like some buttons for elevators being default Unreal red cylinders.Lastly it is a minor issue, but levels are strange in that you kind of just appear in them as if you were King Crimsoned into a new location. Some levels don't even feel connected to the previous location.Overall, it's an okay game, with cool visuals, good sound design, a fun skill tree, and somewhat tedious everything else.
_childDocuments_.name: Forgive Me Father

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun! I can tell the developers spent a lot of time on this, lots of detailed texture work and well thought out levels. Upgrades keep things fresh and exciting through the campaign, which was longer than anticipated! This game has some meat on its bones, I was surprised at the quantity of levels considering the quality.Definitely an experience worth your time and money.

_childDocuments_.review: With its beautiful visuals, this game serves as a decent throwback to the Doom and Duke Nukem style of '90s games. While I enjoyed it, I will say this is far from a perfect game. The story is very superficial, with the narrative devices and objects you find along the way serving more of a general thematic purpose rather than a storytelling purpose. Also, as some others have noted in some more negative reviews the level design (while pretty) is often not functionally fun later on, and the difficulty is somewhat all over the place.That being said, I enjoyed my time with it enough to spend a few extra hours grinding all the achievements and would recommend this if you can find it at a slight discount and are already a fan of the genre / game type.

_childDocuments_.review: Another one to add to the pile of "didnt finish because it got so bad I just had to stop". You can check my reviews, I very rarely never finish a game, no matter how frustrating or bad it is, hell I even play some bad games twice like Dying Light 2. I can't make a proper review as per usual to games I dont finish. Anyway Forgive Me Father is one of those boomer shooters or retro shooters that are generally hit or miss with the fans such as myself. Sadly Forgive Me Father is a huge miss more than half the game. Actually the last half from like World 3'ish or so, becomes so bad that I could barely play more than an hour or so per day.The design of the game, specifically the weapon designs are meant for close quarters, short to medium range enemies and the first zones are perfect, they are balanced, not too maze'ish nor too simple either. I enjoyed it a bit but not rly much as the game did nothing to stand itself apart from the retro market but I was willing to finish it. But then these dumb devs or perhaps they changed the people designing the levels, decided, to enlarge the maps in a shooter with weapons designed for close quarters. I am not even kidding. Whoever thought that was a good idea, should rethink his/her lifes decisions. Not only that, they start throwing huge amounts of HP sponged enemies at you. The upgrade system is terrible, good idea, I like the diversity but the upgrades were bad especially with so many weapons sharing the same ammo. Speaking of ammo, its very scarse, and you're gonna have to run around like an idiot towards enemies with your useless small ranged weapons in large open areas that were designed by a child. Bosses are the worst offender, whoever made the World 4 boss should find a different job. No point raging about it, I played it on the hardest difficulty which was a perfect challenge the first few zones but then it becomes dog sht. Lowering difficulty makes the game baby-mode which I refused to do. I had no issues dying, I love suffering but when the level design screws you so bad, bores you so much, and the game decides to crash more than a few times, you kinda get tired. The best thing about a boomer shooter is the level design and the weapons. No one cares about the story or everything else. If you dont get those two right, you've ruined your game. And Forgive Me Father failed at those two spectacularly, less so at the start and more so towards the middle/end-game. Don't bother with this. Even the thumbs up reviews call it a mediocre experience, which says a lot.

_childDocuments_.review: 85/100 TLDR: Solid boomer shooter with flaws but the art style, story and game mechanics make up for the shortcomings. If you’re a fan of the boomer shooter genre then this is a must-play. The art style is unique and the Lovecraftian story and characters are well done. Some really creepy and creative enemies to fight. There are two different playable characters, each with their own special moves that add replay value to the game. The skill tree is a cool feature that allows you to tailor the guns and gameplay to your style. There are difficulty modifiers right from the start, so you can make the game as easy or difficult as you please. Once you beat the game it unlocks NG+ which opens up even more game modifiers. Each level has numerous quick save points, so if you die you don’t have to waste time redoing the same parts over and over. The story and setting were well done and it kept me engaged until the ending credits rolled. It’s clear the gameplay design choices were made to enhance the “fun” level for however you want to play the game. Its an under-rated aspect since you can basically setup the game to play anyway you want, it doesn’t force you into any obnoxious or annoying gameplay. There are a few shortcomings. -The levels in the first couple of acts feel a bit similar and uninspired. The later levels are much better.-Steam Deck verified, except there is some serious stuttering beginning in act iv forward. No amount of changing settings fixed this, I ended up playing the rest of the game from my PC-The voice acting for the journalist character is pretty bad. The priest VA is very good, so it’s a stark contract if you play as the journalist second.-The difficulty spike for the level bosses was significant. I rage quit on most the bosses at least once.-The sound the grenade launcher makes is the most underwhelming weapon sound of all time. All that being said, even if you have a cursory interest in boomers shooters you should pick this one up.

_childDocuments_.review: I feel that act 5 is the weakest of all partially because one of the new enemies that it adds are small, fast, multi-pellet shooting and have a decently large health pool so they get annoying fast when rooms spawn around 3 or 4 of them at a time but the biggest issue for me was that act 5 levels felt darker than the rest of the game to the point of it feeling unintentional where there could be enemies literally in front of me and I just couldn't see them, thus the levels became me just holding right click to equip the lantern bumping into the enemy pulling out my shotgun or crossbow and blasting them on repeat, I actually wound up using the invincibility book here the most and not for survival but just because the filter that it applies helps you see much better. Personally feel that adding small glowie bits to all enemies would fit aesthetically and help identify enemies in the darker rooms not necessarily all of them if you want things like ambush or "jumpscare" mobs but stuff like Troopers, Mobsters, Zombies, the purple teleporting guy and especially the Slither could have used some glow in the dark effects. Apart from my complaints for act 5 this is a pretty cool game think I will come back to it after a break to finish it as the reporter.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for September 2022, this is part of my coverage of the bundle. If you are interested in the game and it's before October 4th, 2022, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.Spooky scary monsters, and the guns to kill themForgive Me Father is a retro horror FPS but with a great graphical style and a lot of interesting enemies. At first, it seems like a typical zombie shooter but after headshoting one of the zombies, they took the head they were carrying and placed it on them, and kept coming. There are a lot of fresh ideas throughout this game. Even something as weak as a “Foggy area” works well here, and gets the blood pumping. On the other hand, After seeing four different enemies, the game just kept throwing them at me over and over. There’s probably more but it was often similar. The story is there to have some collectibles to find, but this is much more on the combat. There’s also not much horror here, though it does have a horror aesthetic, you should have enough ammo to just tear through enemies rather than being afraid of some terror. Pick this up if you like retro FPSes. This is well-designed, and the music is awesome. The gameplay is fast-paced, and I had a blast. There is even leveling with skill points which aren’t needed but also didn’t upset me as much as I expected. However, it’s not that scary, to the point where I could easily come back and plunk down even more hours into the game. _childDocuments_.review: Playing as either a Journalist or Priest, players will be called to a remote town in order to investigate a series of strange events, which culminated with the disappearance of the entire city's population. This gives an incipit for our protagonist of choice to go through increasingly maddening locales, in what soon becomes a struggle for survival. In an Old School FPS, expecting an elaborate story is out of the question; regardless, there are actually a good number of documents and indirect narration elements that give out clues, tidbits about the events that went down - inspired to the Cthulhu Mythos and other supernatural cults. Despite being an unimportant requirement for this genre, the writing itself is of good quality; the same can be said for voice acting and narration - even if the voice-lines do get rather repetitive in the midst of battle, after several hours. Overall, a solid mark in this department.The prime activity in FMF will be, of course, shooting heaps of cultists, mutants, abominations and everything in-between. To do so properly, you'll progressively unlock new weapons found every couple of levels, each of them using different types of ammo and having a distinct purpose on the field - although there are some redundancies. Expect an old-school feel and pacing to the gunplay, as circle-strafing and kiting enemies around while vomiting lead are the peak strategies during combat... but not always! FMF does have several levels that encourage or even force a more considerate playstyle, as they hide enemies or other hindrances behind corners, walls and such obstacles, so you can't just rush and run as you'd think. It's a nice change of pace that forces you to reconsider your approach.Both characters have four different skills; on paper, the Priest's are more defensive while the Journo's encourage aggressiveness, and this is true to an extent. Especially later on, however, the former's skills will simply prove better, as you can't really compare powerful statuses like total invincibility or infinite ammo, with a relatively miserable AoE damage or slow motion that, while useful, just don't feel as good as the holy man's feats. Such skills can be used via Madness, a mana-like stat charged by either taking or dealing damage, granting permanent charges for each ability as it increases. All feats can be upgraded to enhance their effectiveness or duration significantly, but never their core functioning. Weapons may as well be upgraded with the skill points gained by slaying enemies, with mutually-excluding patterns that transform them into significantly better - or different - murder tools. In the end there's a choice to be made between favoring better weapons or better skills, as there're not enough skill points for everything in the long run.Enemies prove varied and interesting, with each act sporting many unique variations. Some of them have weak-spots that, when hit, cause them to mutate (generally becoming weaker) and change their behavior. This rewards accuracy and know-how, but isn't really a core mechanic, as it can be done only on a handful of foes compared to the total. All enemies, on higher settings, hit like trucks while healing and ammo are sparingly found; an issue that becomes overwhelming in the last act and makes it a frustrating, unbalanced mess of bullet sponges and ill-conceived layouts.Aside from the general slaughter, you'll want to take your time in finding secrets and lore files, present in almost every level. The bounties of supplies present in hidden areas can really make the difference between a resource-starved fighter and a ready-for-anything one. With how little ammo and health there is around, especially later on, you'll soon want to become a treasure hunter, no doubt. FMF uses fixed save points in the shape of a drunken hobo, appearing once in a while to retain your progress unlimited times, but only at fixed locations. You'll also want to find color-coded keys to open doors, as it's customary in the genre.Each act has one boss, and all of them, except maybe one (Act 4) prove decently designed, challenging and feel unique. These powerful foes feature evolving attack patterns as they lose HP, and often spawn additional minions you gotta deal with, or soon get overwhelmed by the crossfire. It feels like latter ones are a bit too much on the bullet-spongy side, but nothing too bad in this regard. Even if multi-phased, arena-swapping in some cases, all bosses must be restarted from the start without checkpoints in case of death, which is fine.After the main story, for those who really can't get enough, endless mode is present with five unique arenas where you have to survive as long as you can with either the Journalist or Priest, against increasingly powerful foes, on a difficulty setting of your choice - while upgrading yourself and your arsenal. Completionists and achievement hunters will get into this surely, but in the end it's just "more of the same" without significant variations.

_childDocuments_.review: Forgive Me Father is was one of the most unique spins on the retro shooter norm that I have played. The main place that it shines is in the art style.The gameplay is very similar to that of a retro shooter with most of the weapons being upgradable, and the design of the weapon changing with every upgrade. Enemy types are fairly unique, my only complaint is the air born enemies were pretty annoying to shoot down on controller. The level design was in line with most normal retro shooters, grab (enter primary color here) key and open door. The puzzles were not often the thing which hampered my progress during levels. The story was perfect, well narrated, and easily skip able for those who did not care. Finally the art style (my favorite part about the game). Byte Barrel did a fantastic job of taking the 2D style gameplay and making it part of the aesthetic of the game. This game looks, plays, and feels like a comic book even with explosions being animated with a big "BOOM" in an air cloud. All the weapons and enemies are absolutely beautiful and horrifying at the same time. Overall, this game is a beautiful, horrifying, fun adventure which is definitely worth one play through. PS: There is also a jump scare that legit almost made me have to grab a new pair of undies, fantastically well done.
