_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr This game is okay. Occasionally janky, but it's fine. That's how I would describe my entire experience with this game. The enemies are ok. The bosses are fine. The weapons are alright. And the combat is there.So yes, this game is okay. Too okay, in fact.First couple of hours were fine, really. Standard stuff, nothing exceptional, and that was what I was expecting for early-game and was along for the ride. But that was only because I was also expecting the game to get more... exciting?The formula is the same as other retro shooters. Go somewhere for objective, do some platforming, walk into arena, fight enemies, do objective, get out, get new objective, repeat. And that's not inherently a problem. What IS a problem to me is the fact that, nothing really happens other than that. Nothing that keeps you interested.DUSK had amazing set pieces, devious traps and unique tongue-in-cheek tone.CULTIC, among other things, had PHENOMENAL atmosphere/style, punchy and impactful weapons that feel good to use (especially the dynamite), and varied combat scenarios that you can take multiple approaches for.In comparison, this game feels very... bland. Even boring in some parts.Two major complaints, and one of them is that the combat feels very same-y. It's mostly just, walk into an open, flat arena, monster closet opens or they just spawn in, you kill them and you move on.The other, the levels are pretty uninteresting. A lot of them, especially the open ones, progress in a very linear manner, and your surroundings aren't much to look at. Also, this is a fairly minor complaint, but the secrets aren't very rewarding. Maybe if it was, say, extra experience points for your skill tree, or powerful weapons that you normally get 2 levels later, it would've felt more rewarding.The most excitement I've received from this game was the part where hundreds of villagers swarmed me from all directions. It felt dire, it felt intense. And when I opened the gate, thinking it's my way out, only to see even more of them waiting for me on the other side... I must say, I was pretty excited.But before and after that, nothing of that degree really happened, as far as I remember. And as a result, after about 4 hours of gameplay, the game lost its grip on me. Which is a shame, because the game has unique style to it, and I've also bought the sequel in a bundle deal and now I'm not sure if I want to play the sequel. (That's only how I feel about it, I will check it out when it is released in full regardless.)So to wrap it all up, this game is fine when you start, but pretty boring after a while. It's very standard and doesn't really do much to keep you invested. I wouldn't recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Forgive Me Father

_childDocuments_.review: This is a tentative recommendation for an interesting but very divisive experience with some real bright spots and some baffling areas in need of improvement. The sound design is generally superb - weapon sounds and music are absolutely top-tier, and they get the enemy sounds right in that you can identify most of them just by hearing them. The art direction is also fantastic - an incredible amount of detail in the models and weapons, and a very evocative world. The colour choices are beautiful and in general the game is extremely vivid and interesting to look at. The progression system is well-implemented - every weapon can either be improved or modified (a binary choice that locks out the option you didn't choose) and at the end of each act you're given 1 point that will allow you to respec, offering the opportunity to test out all the different weapon types and decide on your favourite combination. A few inevitably end up sharing ammo, but there are small differences between them that make it viable to use both in certain situations. I also appreciate that the action-oriented character is the female option - it just feels like a nice change of pace.The gameplay is generally okay - it draws a lot off of Doom in terms of its movement and gunplay, but other design choices enforce a slower pace that only detracts (in my opinion). The levels are hit-and-miss: generally very short, cramped, and often dark, so you're just as likely to get boxed in by enemies as you are to avoid them when trying to manoeuvre. A feeling of 'flow' eluded me for the majority of the game. At best it plays well, and at worst it just doesn't do FPS mechanics better than a bunch of other games in a flooded market.The areas in which the game properly falls down are story, script, and voice acting - all of which feed off the quality of the writing which, at least in the English version, feels like it was fed through Google Translate. The problem with adapting something for a Lovecraftian style is that the mystery of the strange goings-on is key to the atmosphere of the cosmic horror genre. Any pretence of an intriguing mystery goes out the window within the first few levels as the cutscenes and scraps of in-game text reveal themselves as insubstantial to the point that I quickly forgot what my character was supposed to be doing and why, and the game fails to make use of strong archetypal playable characters with its weak, and poorly-translated quippy dialogue. The last few levels is where the game really feels like it's becoming something interesting, and but then it gives you whiffs of its tired trope of an ending. I was begging the game not to go there but I was proven right. The spoken words have a 'no-one speaks like that' feel of literal translations not adequately adapted to fit the natural cadence of a language. Many spoken lines include grammatical errors or outright make no sense. The voice actors - American English speakers by the sound of it - occasionally mispronounce certain English words (says = 'say-z' instead of 'sezz') which is coupled with strange line reads that put emphasis on the wrong words and make statements sound like questions, leaving almost all the dialogue feeling terrible. I feel like I could have personally polished the entire script within the span of a single day, so I find it curious that within such a costly process as developing a game a step so crucial to the perception of quality is left behind. The one circumstance in which the captions said the awkward "what is happening to me" and the actor contracted it to a more natural "what's happening to me" was the only thing stopping me from believing that it was read by text-to-speech, and so it seems the actors either didn't suggest more natural versions of the line, or they did and were rejected. Either way, odd, and it really hampers the game's credibility.In all I'd say this is a game with a broad spectrum of quality that seats it in the middle of the pack. The art style is the immediate draw and the sound design a surprise success, but much of the rest is derivative or lackluster, and it ends with a fart instead of a bang. It sounds like the sequel doesn't fare a lot better. Worth a look for cheap if you're hurting for another FPS though.

While some are stronger than others, it's hard to pick a favourite gun even after playing through the game twice.The game utterly falls flat in other fields, the quality of the voice over and the writing of the lines have me recommend you turn off the voice over all together. _childDocuments_.review: Boomer shooter set in a Lovecraftian world. I don't usually play DOOM boomer shooters, but this was a fun experience. The graphics are interesting and works very well. Enemies and bosses are varied enough so they don't get boring. There are many grotesque and weird stuff to look at here, but I never felt any horror or dread when playing. The movement is good and weapons satisfying to use. One thing to note is that it isn't really a hard game, except maybe on expert. Took me about 7 hours to beat the game on hard. You can play as either a priest or a journalist, which have slightly different playstyles and encourages a second playthrough. The music is fitting and the voice acting is good for the most part. TLDR; Lovecraft boomer shooter with a great visual style. I think even non-shooter players will enjoy this game, though it might not be for everybody even with a great discount.

_childDocuments_.review: As of this review I have completed all of the available content for Forgive Me Father on Normal, this game has a really great atmosphere, gunplay, and art style. The only department that left me wanting was the music, there was 1 track that stood out to me and the rest felt pretty boilerplate as far as boomer shooters go these days (if you have played DUSK you have heard this games battle music) and if I had a suggestion I wouldnt mind hearing more sea shanty style sombre tunes ala Dishonored or perhaps some southern style Bayou hymns. _childDocuments_.review: Beautiful, unique art style that looks almost like a comic book/graphic novel. I really think it looks so different from the average retro-shooter. There has been something of a renaissance of 'Boomer Shooters" in the last few years, these are modern games designed to look (and play) like first person shooter games from the 1990s. I would kind of classify this as that style of game, but it does very much have it's own unique visual identity. The game is a little bit on the difficult side, in a good way. You really have to be careful or you can die quite often. It's mostly a linear, action game where you traverse the levels and survive and get new, more powerful weapons. There is a skill tree, which is something that you usually don't see in this type of game, but it can offer some useful upgrades to your weapons (and player character).There is a significant amount of story and lore, scattered about the world but it's very much optional to engage with it. You can just skip past it if you want to, and most of it is text-based information in the form of documents and posters and various things that you find along the way. Some of the enemies have a lovecraft-inspired design, they look creepy. All of the enemies are not quite human, I honestly am not even sure what the narrative reason for this is, I just have been having a blast shooting them all. 😂
_childDocuments_.name: Forgive Me Father

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those hard games to review. On the one hand, you have an excellent Lovecraftian atmosphere in every level plus a decent retro fps. In addition, the sound design is excellent and really gives you the creeps in many situations, it really adds a dark layer to each level. On the other hand, I have found the game to be dull and inconsistent. The most glaring element is the level design, you often find yourself looking for keys and walking through long corridors and backtracking. Sometimes it is a welcome rest after an intense combat section, however, the need to go back and forth again happens too often. Something similar can be said about the enemies, there are quite a few but some are just different versions of the same type of shooting foe.Overall Forgive Me Father is not a bad game, of course not. The fps revival has produced some amazing masterpieces in the genre but this one is not at the top of the list, at least on mine.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing this game since its early access days on my partner's account, but I decided to get it myself at 1.0 and start fresh. I'm really loving this game, and honestly surprised to see it sitting at ~75% for recent reviews. I would probably rank this one in the top five when it comes to the new retro shooter revival (maybe below Dusk and Amid Evil, but above Dread Templar, Ion Fury, Hrot, and others). The aesthetic is fantastic and the weapons all feel great to use, with an upgrade system that really helps keep things fresh. I love how each enemy type tends to have a single, easily identifiable "gimmick" that structures how you engage with them - some have weak points, others have different stages they go through as they're damaged, etc. The story is... not cheesy, really, but definitely hard to take too seriously because the writing is so clunky. But the result is a very pulpy 1920's feel that I actually thought worked very well for it. My only complaint would be that the upgrades aren't reversible, which means you can be locked into a new gun mod that you don't actually want once you get it. The developers may have made this decision to extend replay value, but I don't think you have quite enough information to decide for many of them, so it feels like a roll of the dice. I didn't end up picking any upgrades that really messed me up, but I can see how that could happen. Hopefully the option to respec is something they can patch in later.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're reading this, you're looking for a no nonsense shooter and Forgive Me Father is just that. Variety of hordes of enemies, some really awesome looking, to dispatch with a few neat weapon. Who would have thought a harpoon shooter can be so OP? Cool things about the weapons is also that when you unlock new skills you can alter their attributes and appearances.The game is mostly fast-paced as the arenas often force you to move around to avoid damage. You get a surprising selection of areas to explore though. First encounter with Patients in the psychiatric ward can be menacing and some later stage arenas get really creepy, however, there's also an underwater level, which is a waste of time. Good it's so short. There are also some truly annoying platforming parts that are unnecessary.You get to chose between 2 characters with some slight differences to the gameplay. I picked the journalist looking for her lost brother. The story is pretty generic and won't be your main bother.Bosses are generally hit or miss. The second one was definitely my favourite. They did try to make them unique though. The last boss is just ridiculous though for a fairly easy game like this.The visual direction is definitely a standaout even though we've had a few shooters in this style in the past. It's extremely gory and actually mostly 2D. It's quite a brilliant trick to make 2D object rotate to create 3D illusion and save on resources. Enemies also feel a bit cardboard, I find it neat.I came for a bit of mindless fun and that's what I received minus some frustrations and lacklustre levels.P.S. Is it just me or the narrator is lifeless in his delivery?

_childDocuments_.review: Developers Takes notes, not all games need to look sexy with graphics to be good. Forgive Me Father Has the Right amount of Love Craft Story telling, Guns Selections, and kick ass music to tie it all together. _childDocuments_.review: The writing can be a bit hit or miss and the character quips (at least on Priest) are grating. The gun variety is neat, with branching upgrade paths based on what you like. The enemy variety isn't over complicated, but the mix of types in some of the later areas can feel almost unfair to manage. The art style is solid (if sometimes too dark on default settings) The boss designs are pretty rad, though the only one with a meaningful mechanic to prolong it isn't even the final boss. For the type of shooter it is, I'd actually wished it was a little shorter? It kinda drags in the third act, but the final act feels almost too short, so it's kind of at odds with its own buildup. At the end of the day, I had fun with it, and can still squeeze out more time hunting secrets and trying the journalist or endless mode, but it isn't my favorite thing from this genre. 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: A decent start, but not quite there. Maybe some of these problems have been solved in the sequel, I don't know. It seems to me like a game developed too quickly by ticking off a checklist, perhaps due to the market and not strictly due to the developers (example: the lines the characters say seem bland and unjustified compared to the well-known examples of Duke Nukem 3D or Blood).What I don't like:- checkpoint saves, one of the worst plagues that afflict the world of modern video games- the environments are extremely bare but above all unrealistic (example: the hospital does not look like a hospital at all, but looks like a series of generic rooms with objects placed randomly). The rooms all seem identical to the others, the floors are reached by climbs or stairs, sometimes without handrails and without any detail. They do not keep up with the environments of many FPS released in the 90s with much less resources and examples- the movement is too fast (apparently this is a problem solved in the sequel). In the corridors and small environments you cannot see or understand anythingI just can't find the motivation to play it. The whole setting and lore seem decorative rather than substantial. It's about looking for yet another set of colored keys, each placed in a generic room, while the enemies are not interesting and are more of an annoyance.

_childDocuments_.review: I’m not too sure how to go about reviewing this game - for every thing I loved about it there was something I hated. I’m going to go with “not recommended” simply because I think the “very positive” status it has now is too good for what it is currently. I actually WOULD recommend it for people who are into 90s shooters - I just hate Steam’s binary review system! This is a “positive” or “mostly positive” to me. A strong 6 / light 7 out of 10.Things that I liked:- The art style is great!- The sound and enemy design is also impeccable. Each enemy looks and behaves fairly differently, and they have great sound effects. Some of the electrical enemies are especially terrifying.- The guns feel great to shoot, and there are some cool upgrades as well (there is a downside to this that I’ll get to, though)Things that I didn’t like:- The skill tree is a really cool idea in theory, but not so much in practice. The biggest example of this are the upgrades for health, armor, and ammo. The issue with these is that it doesn’t ever really end up being all that useful because the game is incredibly stingy with it’s pickups.- Many of the gun upgrades looked like they would be super cool, but I felt discouraged from getting them because many of them use a special type of explosive ammo. The game is barely giving you enough ammo as it is, so there wasn’t much motivation for me to change the gun to use an even rarer ammo type. Maybe I’ll replay it on an easier mode so I can use all the weird guns.- There are too many power-ups and not enough of them are useful. The cigarettes were the best, in my experience. I didn’t use the camera or the voodoo doll once.- There is no weapon wheel, which was frequently very annoying. I get that FMF is a retro shooter, but it’s still 2022 and weapon wheels are an absolute improvement over the mouse wheel days of old.- A lot of the environments were boring! A lot of bland and repetitive corridors. There were never any locations that really stood out or made my jaw drop the way certain places in games like Dusk, Doom, or Quake did.Overall, despite my many complaints, I WOULD recommend this game to folks that like boomer shooters and want something new to play. For almost anyone else, maybe not, though. Thankfully,  almost all the biggest issues for me are things that could easily be fixed by the devs, and it seems like they are very active and committed to making changes and balancing things, so we’ll see what happens.

_childDocuments_.review: Effectively OG Doom, but with cool lighting and fog.  The gunplay/movement  will feel very familiar and fluid.Smooth framerate, great soundtrack.  The Lovecraftian backdrop is just a theme, although it's a fun sidestep from the classic hellscape/base-on-mars.  The art style is... not my favorite, but it goes well with the old tech level / new tech lighting combo.  They could have done a lot more with improving the billboard/spritecard rendering of stuff to make it cooler without ruining the retro feel of it (e.g. normal maps, parallax... maybe double the frames of the animated sprites).  Amazing what a difference modern lighting makes.If you're looking for a good, fast-paced retro shooter, with lots of gore, look no further -- this one is well done. _childDocuments_.review: Full disclosure. While I think this game is good, my recommendation is to those seeking more retro shooters that aren't aware of this one. For the average gamer, there are better FPS games out there. is a tricky game to pinpoint my exact thoughts. It feels like a game directly tailored to me. A boomer shooter rooted firmly in Lovecraftian lore and atmosphere? Sign me up!  promise fulfills itself rather well for the first couple of hours. The art direction is outstanding, perfectly capturing the look of an old Weird Tales pulp magazine combined with the look of a Locke & Key style comic book. The level design for the first chapter is quite strong, and the leveling system leaves plenty of room to fit your playstyle. The enemy design is also fantastic, and the designs for enemies and levels have plenty of variety for much of the game! All of these aspects lead to a fantastic experience right from the beginning but start to unravel and fall apart as the game progresses.For reference, by the way, I played as Journalist on Normal difficulty. Many of the problems later in the game are the same, if not worse, no matter what settings you pick, though.The first two acts of  are solid retro shooter action. The encounters are fun and well-placed, even if many of the early enemies are machete fodder. The leveling system is involved and syncs itself well to picking up new items. It also balances action and horror rather well; the second act steals the show by blending the two together. The third act starts with a clever nod to Blood, and while there are some fun levels here and there in the third act, the problems start to arise. The most obvious problem is the stagnant leveling up combined with the increased numbers of enemies, many of them being spongier. Many shooters with a leveling system,  as an example, succeed by never slowing the progression down in the first place. Enemies get tougher and grow in numbers, so keeping the progression consistent helps the player feel rewarded.  severely drops the ball here, especially by the fourth and fifth acts.(Worth noting: recently, the devs have mentioned that they hope to fix the level system issues in an upcoming patch. We'll see if this stays a problem in the future!)Speaking of the fourth and fifth acts, all of the game's problems amplify to absurd degrees here. Not only are the newer enemies bullet sponges, but most of them also aren't fun to fight either. Whether they behave the same as previous enemies but with more health or just have annoying placement,  combat becomes stale real quick. The level design takes a nosedive near the end, too: when the levels aren't grindy or a slog of enemy spam, they're unbelievably frustrating. Act 5's dips into Xen levels of frustration, with platforming littering levels in a game never intended to involve platform jumping. While many retro-style shooters at this point take an  style approach with movement and can get away with platforming aspects,  is a lot more sluggish. It's not a problem for most of the game, but in Act 5, it gets infuriating. Not to mention, the bosses get worse near the end too. Despite Act 3's boss being my favorite, Act 4's boss and the final boss are insufferable.So, where does that leave us? Ultimately, a mixed bag. I'm more on the side of wanting to defend this game than to attack it, but I'll definitely say there are numerous problems. From a visual-audio standpoint,  is a treat. Sink into the gameplay past the first two acts, and its faults become way too hard to ignore. There's no denying that there's a great game here, but it fumbles mixing these ingredients a bit too much to make it there. It's a reasonably fair entry into the retro shooter genre, but I don't see myself coming back to it even after some fixes.

_childDocuments_.review: First-person horror shooter, with Lovecraftian aesthetics.Similar to old school shooters like Doom or DukeNukem3D. You search the levels for colored keys to unlock doors. And a lot of pop culture references (anime, movies, tv shows,etc)There are stuff you can interact with to get a bit of extra plot and story.You play as either a priest or a journalist going from level to level. Location to location. Trying to solve the mystery of whats going on.Retro inspired pixelated FPSs are very common now. And to be honest I personally find most of them to be crap. Banking mostly on nostalgia but not really doing anything interesting. Trying so hard to be edgy and bad*ss I find them cringy.Forgive Me Father on the other is actually doing something cool with its premise. Gameplay is neither too fast or too slow. _childDocuments_.review: ^TLDR^There's 2 characters to choose from at the start of the game. There's the priest, and the journalist. I started with the priest, which I believe is the default character you're supposed to play the first time with. Each has 4 special abilities that are similar but different. For instance Priest has a cross which when you press the button he holds up for a set period of time and it heals an amount of HP. Journalist, on the other hand, has a special sword and goes into a mode where she supposedly takes less damage and each strike of the sword on an enemy is supposed to heal you.There's also a good weapon variety. There's 8-ish base weapons.There's an upgrade screen as well. Both the characters abilities and the weapons can be upgraded here when you level up and gain a point. The characters abilities are just a line that make them last longer and make any other aspects better as well. The priest has an ability to make himself invincible for a few seconds, and another for infinite ammo for a few seconds. You can only use 1 ability at a time, so don't expect to be able to become invincible and heal yourself simultaneously.The upgrade screen gives you even MORE weapon variety depending on how you upgrade the weapons. A melee knife can become an even bigger knife or an infinitely useable throwing knives. Revolver can either be dual wielded which fires faster but less accurate or become a Mauser C96 which fires faster accurately but does a little less damage. Double barrel shotgun can be upgraded to put out more shot per shell or it can have shot that bounces off walls. Thompson can fire faster plus more damage or it become a friggin' laser beam rifle. There's another SMG "rusted stuck" on 3 round burst that can become full auto or become a grenade launcher. There might be other weapons I'm forgetting. IIRC the harpoon gun's choice is between upgrading it or giving your character higher max armor. (might be HP I forget which)Maps/levels are finely crafted and interesting to explore the first time, for the most part.The enemy variety is just right. Some are melee, some shoot. A few are annoying AF... Sometimes the controls to switch weapons simply stop functioning for a few seconds. I thought this was a controller issue, but I also saw a forum post from someone using KB/M who complained the number keys sometimes stop working to switch weapons.It seems like the stick for looking around goes at different speeds. Sometimes it's lightning quick up/down/left/right movement, other times it feels sluggish. It might be tied depending on the frames per second or something from my observation.Like I said in the good section; some of the enemies are annoying AF. Your mileage may vary depending on if you think those ones are BS or challenging.Another issue i have is that there's sometimes rooms that are deathroom arenas... that are the size of my living my room. Okay... I'll be fair... they're more like  the size of my living room. Point is; they're entirely too small. I wouldn't mind the BS monsters if the areas they spawn into repeatedly were bigger. But they're often not.They're horrible. They're always horrible. In pretty much every game ever made with them they suck.Not only does it prevent you from seeing the area around you, it also makes it impossible to see enemies in some places. Some of which fly while shooting at you.You have a lantern as the priest which lights everything around you in a short radius, or a flashlight as journalist which lights a small circle in front of you to a distance. They're on the left trigger and while you're holding up the light you can't use any weapons. The lantern has a handle, and I've never seen a priest/minister/pastor in my entire life who didn't wear a belt... I feel like that's a problem solved right there. I got nothing for the journalist. You can upgrade the lights 2 or 3 times, but IMO they're kinda worthless compared to more powerful weapons. If the final upgrade was being able to toggle on/off the light while being able to use weapons I'd go for it, but alas...

_childDocuments_.review: First off: Forgive me father is a gorgeous game. No doubt there. There are interesting gameplay elements to it that redeem some of the stuff I am about to groan about, but in general I found myself quite disappointed.For starters, this is not a lovecraftian game in the slightest, tiniest bit. This is a doom style shooter set against the backdrop of purely visual lovecraftian themes, with a slathering of pop-gamning-culture references to games that really don't have much to do with the genre at all. There is effectively no story outside of little tidbits you can gather from papers in the environment. The music is BLARING heavy metal, like a proper doom clone. In effect, this game could palette-swapped with almost any theme and you'd never have known it was meant to be lovecraftian.The gameplay then goes in the exact opposite direction of a doom shooter with enemies that constantly punish aggression, even though a core element of the game is a "Rage" meter your character can build up to use abilities. This meter is nearly impossible to charge outside of massacre rooms because you play against high damage enemies that often do things like poke out of cover or viciously punish you for moving forward at a fast rate. Even if you overcame the foes behavior, you will nearly always be low on ammo and have to be extremely careful with what little you get, and there is no "Chainsaw" method to get it back, only environmental finds. These traits give the game a sort of identity crisis, it feels like a doom shooter, the guns shoot like a doom shooter, the music screeches like a doom shooter, the story is absent and the levels are structured like a doom shooter, but then the actual gameplay punishes you for trying to play it like one. It makes most of it quite unfun, especially on harder difficulties.Equipment wise, your preisty boy has access to a number of guns and tools. Most of the tools rely on the rage system, which makes it a bit of a crapshoot as to if youll get to use them or not. Additionally most are just not that useful, a little douser that can stun a single enemy if you hit it point blank for very little time? Yea, use cases for the tools are slim. The guns are better off, and can be fairly satisfying, but the diversity is lacking (Why two smgs?) and the upgrade paths are quite the doozy. The starter revolver is actually a fine weapon, and the constant ammo crisis makes you use it quite often. Possible upgrade path: Broomhandle mauser. Shoots faster, sounds good... and cant headshot anymore. Yea, the normal revolver can OHK a majority of trash enemies, the upgrade cannot. That is an utterly massive nerf to the weapon that essentially renders it useless since it doubles your ammo consumption. Upgrades as a whole feel odd, out of place, or just plain unimpressive. The enemies really are cool, but the gimmicks behind each one are minor and the feedback from smacking them with weapons isn't very satisfying. Normal zombies can come in weapon variants or a variant that holds a second head, which it will replace the first with if headshot. This is grim and creepy initially, but quickly gets overused and just serves to make the enemy more annoying and a bigger time sink to deal with. Riflemen with acid packs can have the pack get shot to force them into becoming melee foes, and this gimmick is often essential in dealing with them effectively given how strong these guys are at range. If they weren't such a breaker of the doom-style gameplay i'd actually rate them highly for the cool design and the acid gimmick. Environments are pretty, and are a highlight of the game. Not a lot of interest outside that, first level had some cool creepy tricks and traps, but after that they just become mazes for you to blast and shoot through. Forgive me father is not really a bad game on its own, but when a buyer is expecting a lovecraftian FPS and gets a somewhat poorly designed doom shooter with a cool skin, it's going to leave a bad taste in the mouth. Good lovecraftian games are hard to come by, and an FPS one complete with hand drawn foes and such brings images of some deep tale with twists and turns and horror and sanity. This has not a single hallmark of the lovecraftian genre, it merely is a pretty FPS set against the backdrop of places, foes, and themes that may evoke a lovecraftian thought.Which is unlikely with heavy doom metal blasting at all times..

_childDocuments_.review: To summarize: "Pass this one up, there are better Doom Clones" I think the enemy types are too similar, everything is basically just a run at you and melee variety enemy. _childDocuments_.review: I've played countless FPS games, as well as a large amount of boomer shooters, so I feel like my expectations are pretty reasonable. This game doesn't really reach my expectations, or at least what I'd want from a game. Some people see the US$20 price tag and give it some leniency, but that's just purchasing the game to play. You still need time investment to complete it, and this game doesn't REALLY offer a justification for said time investment.Every time I open the achievements, I'm reminded of the fact there are 4 acts, and I audibly groan. At the moment I'm working my way through Act 3, and man is it a chore. There just feels like there's no soul in the game to speak of. You'd think the type of game Forgive Me Father should be similar to would be something like Duke Nukem, HROT, Blake Stone, Ion Fury, Doom. Really, the closest are Chex Quest and Void Bastard. The first 10 minutes is essentially exactly the same as the next 8 hours. Sure, you get upgrades and more abilities as you play, but it FEELS the same. The gun-play is intensely similar throughout, the tactics are effectively the same, the story is incredibly boring and the voice acting is almost comedic (is it deliberately that bad? Is it a joke I'm not in on?). There's praise for the visuals, but even then I'm not a MASSIVE fan. The "story" pick-ups are essentially a total waste of time. The secrets can be fun once in a while, but most aren't interesting. Maybe pick it up for a tenner? There's just no reason in my mind why someone wouldn't just buy a better game at a similar price and genre like HROT or Ion Fury or Postal: Brain Damaged or Amid Evil or any other number of excellent faux-retro FPS games? I appreciate the work and effort put in, don't get me wrong, but it just isn't that fun unfortunately. If I gould give anything other than a total binary yes/no, I'd offer a 5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: so, like, naturally this is a competently constructed and well-paced boomer shooter, with a strong art style and a presentation method that's reminiscent of games like Void B******s, but I want to point out the fact that this game is also incredibly goofy, and it knows it. I believe this is fully intentional, but the internal monologue from the characters, particularly the Journalist, is so funny that it transforms the tone into a B movie type of experience. You'll be walking along the DUSK-adjacent corn maize level and, approaching the end, she'll say "I just realized that... I don't even like corn." delivered with some of the most deliciously cheesy acting that i've heard in a game like this. I absolutely love every single line that comes out of her mouth as you progress, like when getting a headshot and she will say "Pop! There it goes..." I cannot stress enough the fact that these jokes work entirely because of how the actor sells them. her delivery is so irreverent and silly that it surpasses the "Well that just happened" nature of the joke and wraps back around to being absolutely brilliant.This game isn't going to win you over on boomer shooters if you're not a fan. It's a fun time blasting through the levels and playing with the unique skills, but if you're curious about the aesthetic and love the tone of more B movie style games like House of the Dead: Overkill or Lollipop Chainsaw, I highly recommend going in as the Journalist and kicking back as she whispers sweet nothings in your ear, like "What's so special about this rock?" and "What!? These monsters are barrels too?"

_childDocuments_.review: The pacing and combat are amazing ... until you hit the water level and the boss with the disappearing islands. At that point, the game takes a sharp nosedive, and starts to feel like it is just wasting your time and they ran out of cool ideas. _childDocuments_.review: Forgive Me Father is a first person shooter in the same vein as Doom or Quake, but a little more fleshed out, plus it has an incredible artstyle.Since we’re discussing an Early Access game here some things might be changed or added into the future, or even removed. So please keep in mind that this review might not be up-to-date by the time version 1.0 releases, hopefully in 2022.When you start the game you are quickly dropped into your first level. I wasn’t sure if this was maybe still some sort of tutorial at first, but it quickly became clear that this was the game’s actual first level. So you pick up your first gun, a pistol, and get on your way through the dimly lit mansion. A few minutes into the game you’ll come into contact with your first enemy and once you get over how great the art looks you might even want to (read: have to) shoot him. This enemy in particular only deals melee damage so he’s easy to take down. Enemies have a health bar, but most of the times a (few) headshot(s) will suffice to take them down. Or explosive red barrels to take down more at the same time. Later on more enemies will arrive - and sometimes they will spawn – that will also shoot (multiple) projectiles and do area-of-effect damage, making it a bit harder. The more difficult parts, however, are the parts where enemies suddenly spawn or come at you in bigger numbers. On occasion it gets a little overwhelming and once you get cornered it’s hard to get out of the situation. It either means you might get away with little health (unless you know beforehand what you’re running into) or you’ll die, in which case you have to restart from the latest checkpoint. Fortunately, since this is a game similar to Quake and Doom there are also health pick-ups that can be run into in order to heal up. Later on you’ll acquire a skill that heals you depending on how much Madness you have obtained. Madness is obtained by killing enemies and drinking liquor and the more Madness you have the more damage you will inflict, but it will also make your screen black and white which means things can still get hard to see. I’m personally not a fan of this effect as it makes the game even harder where in reality it’s supposed to make you more powerful and the game more easy (I’d say, right?). These effects cancel each other out this way.Killing enemies will also reward you with skill points. Currently there are four skills to choose from; the others that are there are acquired by going through the story. Most of these skills are related to your set of weapons and skills, and there’s also a skill that lets you earn more experience. More will be added later on during the Early Access period and for now these skills are enough, even if they’re a little plain and unimaginative.Besides health there’s naturally also ammo to find, as well as armor and colored keys to unlock same colored doors. Story pieces can also be found scattered throughout the level and these are very easily marked with the word ‘Story’ (hence my confusion at the beginning of the game where you’re just dropped into the level; I thought Story would begin a level, or at least the story). Anyway, a nice piece of art will then show on screen that tells you more about the (back)story.In your first level you’ll also acquire a lantern that will play an important part during some segments. If it’s dark (because it *is* dark, but also because of the shade) you can take out your lantern to light the way, but this also means you won’t be able to use your weapons. It’s either one of the two. So you have to light the way to see where the enemy is then quickly switch to your gun (by that time you’ll also have acquired a shotgun) and aim at where they’re still hopefully located. It’s a fun twist, that adds a bit of tension to the situation, especially if your health is running low.In the levels you can also find secrets. These are usually fun to find (either by accident of by actively searching for them). Once you’ve finished a level, which can take anywhere between a few minutes to up around 10-15 minutes maybe, you’ll get a ‘percentage complete’ score to see what you might have missed or how you can do things differently the next time. The score is based on story pieces found, red barrels blown up, secrets found, kills made and time, although I think the latter doesn’t influence the score in any way.The current set of levels will take you through the mansion, a backyard and through a church/chapel area, among other locations. Currently there are 12 levels and more will be added later (25 in total).As I already mentioned more skills, more weapons, more bosses (yes, there are boss fights), and more enemies will also be added later on (and there are already more than what I just described). It’s just been released last week so things are still early days.Visually this game is great. It has an amazing artstyle, but some of the animations are a bit lacking. Hopefully more frames will be added to them, because right now they move a little – just a tiny bit - awkwardly, but I guess that’s also done on purpose. Besides being very dark, the game also has some colorful elements. Everything looks nice and sharp, with detailed textures. The environments, especially outdoors, also look terrific. Nothing with this game visually, let’s hope they can add to it and make the necessary improvements.Sound-wise the guns sound realistically, but maybe not as clean as they should. The music, when it kicks in, is not my cup of tea, but fans of the heavier music styles out there will enjoy it… probably.Forgive Me Father is a visually stunning game that fans of Quake, Doom and similar-styled games will definitely like. It’s fast paced, has some nice secrets and references and so far also has enough variety in its enemies, locations and weapons. More will be added, and has to be added, later in order to keep things interesting, but for now you can get several hours of gameplay out of it for sure. It’s a cool game, with a fun, but still kind of basic, gameplay loop; just don’t expect anything revolutionary.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really tough one to review. The first 2/3rds of the game were great - fast paced, FPS combat reminiscent of Doom 2016.  These levels were a joy to play.Then there's the final levels of the game, where the transitions between levels grow increasingly disjointed (you could make a case this is plot-related). At this point, combat becomes a chore - enemies are too tough to be satisfying - flying enemies that can easily avoid most weapons, or hordes of overly-tough enemies, but minimal ways to deal AoE damage. Then it keeps on going and going and going. Pre-determined save statues meant that to be competitive, I had to wander back to old save locations (if they existed at all) and back to the action. The progression system of skill points has all but dried up by this point, requiring thousands of kills to improve the character. I was a fool to invest in the 'quicker xp gain' powers, because it turns out there is a soft cap in obtaining more.At this point I was no longer having fun. I had a choice - stop playing or crank the difficulty all the way down. This did not help too much. It does not make enemies less tough, just less damaging. There was barely enough ammo to kill everything, and it was certainly excruciating to progress. I decided to run past every single non-essential enemy. It worked and I eventually found my way, level by level, to the final two bosses. The bosses were fun. All of the bosses are fun and reasonably challenging on normal. Shame about those final levels - they could be fixed with some tweaking.

_childDocuments_.review: Pro:+ Beautiful comic book like artstyle + Some of the weapons are very fun to use+ Good Level Design for most of the game+ Some Good BossesCons- Enemies in the final chapter of the game are boring bullet sponges- Redundant padding via boring platforming sequences- The upgrade system is completely broken it dies halfway of your playtrough when you need millions of exp for 1 point- Some of the weapons upgrade are underwhelming and borderline useless- Ditto for some of the character powersIt pains me to give a negative review to 'Forgive me Father' since this game starts on all cilinders, the lovecraft inspired atmosphere is great, the initial battles with your enemies are amazing and the map design flows pleasantly.And then you reach the end of Act 4 and the entire game devolves into garbage, hordes of enemies with far too much HP and annoying unfun mechanic (constantly sliding on the floor, flying far too fast for any non hitscan weapon to hit..etc etc) far too many arenas and annoying platforming session in the dark and cherry on the ♥♥♥♥ cake one of the most boringly annoying final bosses i've ever defeated (you know whats fun? a tiny microspic arena, a bunch of high damage AOE attacks from the boss and AN IMMORTAL ADD THAT KEEPS FOLLOWING YOU) which results in one of the most insultingly bad ending i've experienced in decades of gaming. Clearly this game was made with love and i know an upcoming patch is trying to fix most of the cons but i do not plan to play 'Forgive me Father' ever again: 5.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Forgive Me Father : By Triple F"Forgive Me Father" is a bold experiment in the first-person shooter genre, blending the frenetic pace of classic arena shooters with the atmospheric horror of H.P. Lovecraft's cosmic horrors. The result is a game that is both exhilarating and unsettling, a rollercoaster ride through a grotesque and nightmarish world.From the moment the game begins, players are immersed in a visually striking world that is both familiar and alien. The game's comic book-inspired art style is a bold choice, but one that pays off handsomely. It lends the game a unique aesthetic, while also allowing for some truly grotesque and disturbing imagery. The environments are varied, from the claustrophobic interiors of the monastery to the open, desolate landscapes beyond.The audio design is equally impressive. The game's soundtrack is a haunting blend of industrial and ambient soundscapes that perfectly complements the game's atmosphere. The sound effects are crisp and impactful, and the voice acting, while limited, is suitably creepy.At its core, "Forgive Me Father" is a fast-paced shooter. Players are armed with a variety of weapons, from shotguns and machine guns to more exotic options like laser rifles and energy blasters. The combat is intense and chaotic, requiring quick reflexes and strategic thinking. The game's "madness meter" adds an extra layer of challenge, as players must balance the need to unleash their fury with the risk of losing control.However, what sets "Forgive Me Father" apart from other shooters is its Lovecraftian influence. The enemies are grotesque and otherworldly, and the game's atmosphere is filled with a sense of cosmic dread. The game does an excellent job of balancing the fast-paced action with moments of eerie quiet, creating a truly unsettling experience."Forgive Me Father's" narrative however is a mixed bag. On the one hand, the Lovecraftian themes are well-executed, and the game's central mystery is intriguing. On the other hand, the story is often overshadowed by the game's intense action. The characters are somewhat underdeveloped, and the plot twists are predictable.While "Forgive Me Father" is a visually impressive game, it does suffer from some technical issues. Frame rate drops can occur in particularly intense moments, and the game can be prone to crashing. These issues are somewhat mitigated by the game's overall charm, but they can be frustrating nonetheless.In summary, "Forgive Me Father" is a game that defies easy categorization. It is a fast-paced shooter, a horror game, and a Lovecraftian experience all rolled into one. While it may not be perfect, it is undeniably unique and memorable. If you're a fan of either shooters or horror games, "Forgive Me Father" is definitely worth checking out. Just be prepared for a wild ride.

_childDocuments_.review: Forgive Me Father is a doom-like FPS set in a world inspired by the works of HP Lovecraft. In its current early access state, it will take you about 2 hours to finish. And 2 hours is all it took to leave me craving more.Within the first 5 minutes, Forgive Me Father put a big smile on my face with the unique enemy mechanics. After killing the first enemy with a headshot, you headshot the second just for them to put a head they were holding on their shoulders and continue towards you. What a simple but genius idea. And then in the very next level, they introduce an enemy which you need to headshot or they'll turn into a crawler! The game has a 3D environment with 2D sprites that always face the player. Every design in this game, whether it be a weapon, enemy, or just part of the environment, looks amazing. The art style is very satisfying to look at, and the animations, despite usually being only a few frames, add to the overall feel of the game.You also get skill points as you defeat enemies, which you can use to upgrade your weapons, gadgets, and just general upgrade like a larger ammo capacity. Most weapons also have different upgrade paths, for example, you can upgrade the revolver into a pistol (less damage, higher accuracy and fire rate) or dual revolvers (lower accuracy, get dual revolvers).I can't wait to play more

_childDocuments_.review: So right off the bat I will say this game was awesome. For anyone who enjoys the Lovecraftian universe, this game pays homage to that literary universe with its aesthetic, lore and even bosses. Think kthulu, giant elder ones and squid like alien beings. The art style in this game is fantastic. The music is also banger after banger, think DOOM mixed with The Shining. Be warned though, this game is punishingly difficult, and can be challenging at times even on normal, you will die but you learn the maps and how to deal with each enemy type. This game was finished on normal in about 8hrs in its early access form. I highly recommend this game to anyone who enjoys the art style of Lovecraft horror and the fast paced action of DOOM. 8.5/10 is my score, with the .5 deducted for the lack of content at this stage, and the weird way how your gun wont shoot sometimes while moving, not sure if this is intentional or a bug.

_childDocuments_.review: First 4 Acts are great, but Act 5 ruined both the story and has questionable map design. The final boss is great but the ending that comes after that just seems thrown together and makes everything bad ass that happened throughout the game feel stupid... unlike  Putting that aside, the game play is pretty serviceable for a boomer shooter fan. I played through as the Journalist and the abilities of that character, especially the camera and sword, felt right at place alongside the combat. The enemies are fairly basic, so don't expect Doom Eternal levels of complexity in the combat loop, it's mostly dodging sphere projectiles at a range and melee attacks up close, but the strength of combat has to be the weapons. The skill tree in the game allows you to upgrade your weapons through the course of your play though, and fitting in with the Lovecraftian theme, turns some of them into eldritch monsters. In particular, the shotgun goes from being a typical boomer shooter shotgun to a lovecraftian sea creature thing that shoots bouncy pellets at your enemies and shreds most of the enemy cast. This approach to the arsenal was a fantastic way to use the setting to create something innovative in the boomer shooter genre. The main issue I have with the combat is the map design; outside of combat, enemies will frequently be hiding right behind corners or approach from behind, which can feel cheap paired with the fact that many enemies in the game have little to no distinguishable audio queues apart from their attacks. In fact this is something I especially noticed with the Act 3  It doesn't affect the game enough to be a serious concern during arena encounters, but outside of arena encounters, it became frustrating especially with the barrel enemy.Overall, if you like boomer shooters and lovecraftian horror, Forgive Me Father is a decent experience that will scratch that itch. Being entirely honest, it doesn't compete with the greats of the boomer shooter genre, and I'd argue that DUSK is probably . If I could give this game a mixed review I would, however, there will be plenty of people who will enjoy this game regardless.

_childDocuments_.review: Forgive me Father is a very fast paced first person shooter with a cel-shaded comic book art style. I honestly did not get too far before frustration set in. I still have to give it another chance because even as frustrating as it may be to get annihilated by a horde of Lovecraftian zombie-like insane and infected humans, it was fun up until my demise.  The game gives out such a thrilling and exciting vibe while you play that you can't help but get hooked. Being a Lovecraftian game, it has the commonly found "sanity" levels. The less sane you are, well - things happen. In this case you can also get perks or abilities to help you out or just make you more badass.  If you like H.P. Lovecraft's stories and monsters, give the game a chance. If you also like retro games like Doom or fast paced action, even better.Go fight some baddies already!

_childDocuments_.review: Forgive Me Father is a retro fps that sets place in a lovecraftian universe. What sold me first is the incredible art style it has but what kept me going was its solid gameplay. You play as one of two characters with different abilities through the story mode. I played as the journalist and from the other people i heard that this was not such a wise choice. Her skills are much less powerful compared to the priest so keep that in mind in your first playthrough. There are tons of weapons you unlock throughout the game and you also have a skill tree in which you can evolve your weapons, enhance your skills and upgrade your health etc. All the guns feel different and the upgrades they get are really interesting and almost entirely changes the guns. In a retro fps what matters the most to me is how it feels to kill enemies and Forgive Me Father nails it. It feels super satisfying to kill enemies especially with the shotgun .The atmosphere this game has is insane.Level designs are really well made and exploration is rewarded by having secrets you can find. The soundtracks are also really fitting and makes you feel like a badass while you kill bunch of enemies. Although most of my views on this game are positive, there are also some bad things about this game such as the hilariously bad voice acting and writing. The story is also not so easy to follow and takes a backseat in this game. So if you are looking for a compelling story, look elsewhere. However if you are in search for a really solid retro shooting gameplay, this game will satisfy you.

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this game on a deal if it looks cool to you or if you are a huge fan of the genre. Otherwise, skip it and get Doom 2016 or one of the other "boomer shooters." It's another game I wish I could give a "mixed" review.Pros:- The 2D art is so good I actually forgot it was 2D art most of the time- Music is amazing- Guns are all unique, fun to shoot, and feel really good- Fun secrets hidden on each level- Each level is fairly short- Plenty of content- Cool weapon upgrade paths that are reset-able a few times if you want to shake things upCons:- Combat areas often have a bunch of clutter. Cannot count the number of times I died because I strafed into a barrel.- Very few save points, so you have to repeat large chunks of content- You have very little health, so you die easily and have to repeat large chunks of content.- There is no way to dynamically heal, so you die easily and have to repeat large chunks of content.- Did I mention you have to repeat large chunks of content? Because you do. A lot. Lots of times. Many times. So many times. To the point the repetition becomes annoying.- As difficulty increases, this turns into a game of "memorize every enemy location and practice how you are going to deal with each one so you don't die". Have I mentioned anything about having to repeat chunks of content a lot of times?I think this game needs dynamic ways to heal and restore ammo, and maybe to clean up some of the large combat areas, and then it would be amazing.As is, I eventually stopped having fun. I know I could probably push through, and at least part of it is my lack of skill at FPS games, but I think I'm fine without playing each of the remaining levels a few dozen times in order to get through it.

_childDocuments_.review: This could be something that you like, I just think that there are better boomer shooters out there and that this game has multiple questionable design choices.my likes:-aesthetic-the shotgun-upgrade tree is something you don't often see in boomer shooters so it's cool to see it heremy dislikes:-Level design seems mostly bland, there are good, distinct levels, just very few of them. The games length makes this point worse as levels go by.-few of the enemies get stun locked and have very fast, hard to dodge attacks which is problematic when a good amount of the game takes place in cramped quarters-While there are a good amount of guns, a lot of them don't really justify their existence. it basically boils down to basic damage dealers, guns with shotgun bullet spread, and explosives.-While the upgrade tree is a nice addition, if you decide to restart and redistribute points, it will give you a small fraction of the points you've spent meaning there isn't really any room for experimentation.-unlike other boomer shooters, hit boxes are unforgiving which means you have to slowly, precisely, aim at your target which not only interrupts flow, but also, most likely causes you to get hit.-While boomer shooters don't aren't really known for being to lore heavy, this games story feels bland. I know that it is literally about fighting a lovecraftian cult but we've already had so many boomer shooters about fighting cults. Not to mention the environmental story telling feels very disjointed, confusing, and most of the time it doesn't feel relevant.-the save system..... why. In boomer shooters you have a few different save systems: autocheckpoints, quicksaveing, limited/collectible quicksaves, but this game uses stationary checkpoint like quicksaves like a soulslike. Not only do they feel infrequent, but it's just annoying to complete a really annoying section, go all the way back to the checkpoint, save, then go all the way back to where you were.-Also, while key and switch hunting is a staple of this genre, instead of feeling like finding more keys to kill more enemies, it feels like I'm slogging through enemies just to find keys to get out of there.It isn't a terrible boomer shooter, just one with a lot of flaws that you should really only get if you like the aesthetic a ton.

_childDocuments_.review: It was a solid game, but not particularly amazing. I love the lovecraftian setting. The art, weapon design and monster design are all fantastic. Also all versions of the shotgun in this game are some of my favorite shotguns in any game. The level design is also pretty good, with some annoying parts at the middle to end. I really didn't like how dark some of the areas were. There was a particularly annoying level at the end that held up my playthrough because I couldn't find the next area. Also the ammo drops near the end are way too rare. This game is meant to be aggressive but I couldn't really do that when I was constantly worrying if I had any ammo in any of my guns. The upgrade tree was fun but I would say it needs some work. Also the madness mechanic was a good way to keep players aggressive, but I think it was poorly implemented. I rarely ever looked at my madness meter, and was not encouraged to use it because of the limited ammo. Overall the game was fun, but it started to drag on a bit. I was ready for the game to end like 5-10 levels before it did.

_childDocuments_.review: Great retro shooter with insane variety and fantastic visual style. First few levels are a bit boring, but game picks up the pace once we reach the rooftops and doesn't slow down until the credits roll. Its decently lengthy shooter too with good replayability thanks to two playable characters with different skills and voices (journalist voice actor is bad tho).Gunplay itself is very reminiscent of old Doom and Blood games, its simple but very fun. As is tradition there are also multitude of secrets to find on each level and plenty of easter eggs, referencing horror classics and retro games. Game uses a blend of manual save system and Dark Souls bonfires. You can only save your game when you find a friendly drunkard with a statue of Cthulhu and there are no checkpoints in between. Not everyone is going to like it, but I think it helps build the tension.Character progression is quite good, skill trees are pretty big and require you to think carefully about your build as you will not be able to get even half of available skills and there is no way to respec. My favorite skills are the ones that completely transform weapons, turning them into either nightmarish armaments or just tuned up versions of the base weapon. Typically the lovecraftian weapons require more points to reach their full potential, but offer amazing firepower (I highly recommend transforming shotgun and Tommy gun).Each character can also use four different skills that can stun enemies, slow down time, heal you or make you invulnerable for a short time. This really helps the replayability as each character plays differently and can use different skills.Best thing about Forgive Me Father are the visuals. Everything looks as if it was taken straight from the pages of comic book. This is where this game's variety really shines, there is a huge amount of enemy types, each of them drawn and animated perfectly. Weapons get the same treatment, there are 8 base weapons, each of them can be transformed into two different variants. That is 24 weapons! And they all look and sound fantastic! These are not some slight cosmetic changes, they are completely different. Huge kudos to the devs for such attention to detail, whoever drew these - you are incredibly talented.Locations we explore are a bit less detailed, but they blend with the visual style very well. Also they get progressively more insane the further you go. And I mean INSANE. These devs really know how to unsettle the player using darkness and enemy placement. Story is your typical lovecraftian trope, nothing to write home about, but it helps build the atmosphere decently. Same goes for the music, its an enjoyable mix of rock and metal, but gets a bit repetitive after a while. Its not disruptive, just a bit bland.Overall I strongly recommend Forgive Me Father to any FPS fan, whether you like retro or not. Its one of the best Early Access Games I have ever played, quality and variety of it are through the roof for such a small studio. It took me around 9 hours to finish the game and I'm already starting the 2nd playthrough with another character and different build in mind. After disappointment that was Shadow Warrior 3 this was a nice surprise.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best boomer shooters I have ever played. Great level design and enemy variety meet spectacular art direction and soundtrack. Boss fights were simply amazing and reminded me a lot of Returnal from Housemarque. It feels challenging in all the right ways and does not shy away from making the player feel powerful and like a total badass, as the boomer shooter sub-genre should. As an extra, the horror side of the game is also surprisingly well made. Well earned jump scares and excellent use of darkness in and out of combat keep you on your toes. Lastly, the audio is just superb. The enemy sound effects, weapon and environmental sounds are all integral parts of what make the horror part of the game work.

_childDocuments_.review: On paper, this looks interesting - an oldschool-inspired shooter with the world revolving around the Cthulhu Mythos. However, the gameplay has its share of issues, which prevent the player from enjoying the game. The movement is fairly clunky, the skill system along with the whole skill tree and the weapon roster is lackluster, while the game itself starts slow, gets better over time, and after a while becomes tedious and on the brink of being boring. Overall, it has some good elements, some bad elements, which eventually makes it hard to recommend to everyone. If you’re willing to accept some of the design and gameplay choices, then you’ll have a great time here. Otherwise look elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: <This is a revamp of my original review.  I originally didn't recommend it, but have now changed my mind.>A fun shooter with a memorable art style, and solid music.  Because it's a boomer shooter, there's not much variety in the gameplay outside of moving and shooting, aside from a few platforming sections.  Fortunately, the mechanics are well-made and require strategy as you encounter enemies.  To go through dark areas, you have a lantern but prevents you from shooting at the same time.  There are powerups to unlock and level up.  And a variety of weapons you can upgrade.  The skill tree doesn't let you unlock everything on your first playthrough, rather you have to choose between two paths on some of them.  After an update following the 1.0 release, you are able to respec if you find your choices don't work, however they can only be unlocked after completing each act, so you use them wisely.  You also increase a madness levels the more kills you get, which increases damage dealt and decreases damage received, but is also is required to use your abilities.There are two playable characters: The Priest and the Journalist.  I found that the Journalist is less powerful and more frustrating.  While she is made for players on the offensive, a few of her perks either don't work against bosses or are ineffective against flying enemies.  This is where you need to rely on ammo, which I found can be lacking at times, especially when tougher enemies can be bullet sponges.  The Journalist could use some balance tweaking to make the game more fair.  Personally, I had more fun playing as the Priest as it feels like the game was made with his character in mind.Finally, the game has a bit of a grind issue the longer you play. The number of experience points increases the more you level up, and it becomes a chore to level up. By the time I reached Act 5, I had the majority of upgrades that I needed, but it required maxing out an XP perk very early on.  If you miss that, it's going to hurt you later.It doesn't reinvent the wheel or set a new standard for boomer shooters, but if you like these kinds of games I recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good fun, shooter mechanics work fine. The art is great, though having everything facing you all the time is weird, some angle might be good like Prodeus. Secret and trophy hunting was fun, wish there were some skill point pick ups or something though.Skill and weapon progression is great, but the upgrades on Pistol are all downgrades.. leave the pistol as it is ;) Invest in the skills and learn to use them early, they restock (i dunno when/where/how, but they do) so you might as well use them!Got a lot of play time out of it, a lot of levels to get through though some are shorter than others. The Last world uses a lot of annoying platform mechanics though, some parts you can walk on air but others you can't? You will need to find a good "what the game doesn't tell you" video for this one.Penultimate level is a bit buggy, thought I'd a game breaker before the final boss, but turned out I could just skip a whole section of the level instead :shrugs: Final boss not as exciting as others, little anticlimactic.

As the only one left with full senses, you embark on a journey in search of answers and relief in this FPS game that is created in a distinctive retro horror comic book style and feels as if it came straight out of Lovecraft's books.

Be aware of your madness level which dynamically changes during gameplay and gives you additional power. Choose your active skills depending on your play style and use them to fight against the eternal evil.

Explore this Lovecraft-inspired world that is full of hidden and hard to reach areas, and uncover the entire story to solve the mystery of this crazy place.
